name: Of Bird and Cage
detailed_description: Copyright information About the Game FIRST OF ITS KIND STORY-DRIVEN MUSIC GAME Experience the overwhelming power of metal music like never before. Featuring artists from (ex) Guns N' Roses, Epica, Within Temptation, and many others! Music by Arnold Nesis. Dive into a dark, twisted game specifically tailored to its music. Let symphonic metal lead you through a two-hour-long story of trauma, violence, and madness based lightly on ‘Beauty and the Beast’. Play as Gitta Barbot, a 25 year-old drug addict, who tries to escape the physical and mental prison of her captor—Bres Lupus. Make quick choices that will have dire consequences and watch how your actions reveal new paths while struggling to keep your sanity. You’re surrounded by violence at home and at work, engulfing every aspect of your life—what will you do? Will you take revenge or grant forgiveness? Ultimately, the choice is yours. Follow the twisted relationship between two characters, portrayed in a gut-wrenching way. Happy endings don't come easily here. In this first-person hybrid of a concept album and a game, your choices and actions will shape the narrative. Kobra Paige (Kobra and the Lotus) Davidavi 'Vidi' Dolev (Subterranean Masquerade) Ron 'Bumblefoot' Thal (ex-Guns N’ Roses) Rob van der Loo (Epica) Ruud Jolie (Within Temptation) Danny Worsnop (Asking Alexandria) Casey Grillo (ex-Kamelot) Rocky Gray (ex-Evanescence) Mike Lepond (Symphony X) Tina Guo Snowy Shaw (ex-King Diamond, ex-Therion) Act: Solve puzzles, reveal the story, and fight to survive Decide: Shape the narrative by making quick decisions to reach one of multiple endings. Listen: A haunting two-hour-long symphonic metal concept album fully synced with the game’s world. Look: Experience an insanely dark reality through single-player FPP. Disclaimer: This story is a work of fiction. Any resemblance to actual events, locales, or persons, living or dead, is entirely coincidental. Warning: The game includes themes such as alcohol, drugs, violence, abuse, and harassment.

_childDocuments_.review: Games can be an art form, but what makes them unique from other forms of art is that the outside player’s interactions are an integral part of the work. The gameplay experience may be different for each individual player, yet it is essential to bring any game to the status of masterpiece.  is an interesting example of how the traditional art form of music seeks to use the medium of games to bring itself to a new level. The question remains whether it succeeded in creating a game or little more than a glorified music video. builds its world and tells its story through music, with much of the dialogue being sung rather than spoken. The story is presented in three acts with four possible endings depending on choices made during the game, and the player mostly acts from the perspective of Gitta, a 25-year-old woman whose tragic and violent childhood is probably what led to her adult drug addiction. However, as is sometimes the case with music videos, the story often feels like it doesn’t make sense. Part of this may be because Gitta’s addiction makes her an unreliable narrator, but there is also a lot of jumping around between past and present as well as between reality and memory or nightmare sequences.In addition to being inspired by symphonic metal, the story is a macabre retelling of . The tone is dark, and the themes explored feel like the game needs more robust content warnings. For example, a scene of domestic violence is the first of the game and recurs throughout, and that isn’t the only scene of violence to play out on screen. While this can be a powerful jumping-off point to explore deep and complex subjects,  seems to miss the mark in drawing essential connections to prevent the violence from coming off as gratuitous and meaningless.True to its marketing of a metal album presented as a game, the gameplay experience is essentially an interactive music video. QTEs make frequent appearances, and the vast majority of scenes run on timers. This can be stressful due to insufficient cues on what the player is supposed to be doing or how they are supposed to accomplish it. Gitta’s addiction affects gameplay by blurring and graying the visuals if she can’t get access to drugs (although imagery of birds can also help her focus), which adds an additional layer of challenge in a way that feels more frustrating than fun. Some players may feel like they’re more along for the ride than actively influencing the outcome. There were many times where the clock ran out, and I was left wondering how my action (or inaction) could have possibly led to what was happening now. I played with mouse and keyboard and found that the controls weren’t always intuitive or responsive.The graphics quality is perhaps not as high as it could have been for such an artistic endeavor in 2021, especially when considering the artistry frequently present in symphonic metal music videos. This includes the fonts, which seem childish and out of place. The menu interface design certainly conveys the music album theme since the player chooses which level or part of the story they would like to play by selecting a song in the soundtrack. The game does use a gothic color palette, but when Gitta is in the throes of her addiction the blurry vision and grayed colors get so extreme as to render the player taking actions impossible. The game does open with an epilepsy warning due to the visual design choices.’s name-dropping of artists from several of my favorite symphonic metal bands immediately piqued my interest in the game, so it’s not surprising that the soundtrack is one of its strongest elements. The majority of the dialogue is sung rather than spoken, although where there is spoken voice acting it tends to be mediocre, particularly when compared to the singing. However, as much as it pains me to say, the music isn’t as emotionally gripping or compelling as I would have anticipated for the primary driver of the story’s throughline, and the songs won’t be ones I’ll be adding to my personal playlist.At the time of review,  is $14.99 with an as-advertised playthrough time of approximately 2 hours. However, there are four possible endings, 57 possible Steam achievements (many of which are missable), and in-game collectibles such as CDs, story items, and visions to give the game plenty of value in content. Fans of symphonic metal may find this an interesting and interactive musical experience. However, if you prefer a more player-involved experience or aren’t a fan of dark and violent themes, this game may not be for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh my this a hard one to judge. On one hand it's a wonderful game with amazing idea, on the other hand this game is beyond terrible. I would like to say it's an unpolished gem but I can't even say that.This game is a metal album presented as a game and it's a great idea, it is original and unique and I love that. But why developers took such a complicated route? This isn't one of those narrative games like Quantic Dream, DontNod or Telltale makes. It might seem like one but it isn't, it actually has a lot of gameplay and it sucks, it sucks so badly that when it comes to gameplay I could only compare it to shovelware. I know it isn't shovelware but it feels like it and i know developers have tried but it's not enough.So the gameplay is pretty basic. Music starts playing and it never stops, all the sections are timed and last until the song ends. So far sounds great huh? But instead of standard narrative gameplay we have overcomplicated mechanics which ruin the game. First you'll need to explore the surroundings, controls are very clunky but exploring isn't the bad part. There's no clear goal, you don't know what to do, or maybe I should say you know what to do but don't know where to start and with time running out quickly you just run out of it. It works similarly to first person point&click game where you explore the surroundings, pick up items and find the use for them. Many items are very hard to find and due to clunky controls and strict time limit it's even harder to do something in time. Why couldn't they just give us similar controls to the games I mentioned? Go there, pick it up, use it. Just make it so that you couldn't do everything in one playthrough.There's also driving. Why, just why? The driving is terrible, worst i've seen. Why not make it as a quick time event series? Or something on rails like Beyond Two Souls?There's shooting too. It feels like the worst fps game. Again why? Why shooting isn't a qte or decision? It's just clunky, buggy, glitchy mess.Not enough? Well, say hello to some platforming sections and carrying various boxes and objects. What in the world is that? Why? It just doesn't work as intended. And opening doors and drawers when each second counts? Nope.Wait there's more. Fistfighting. The most stupid feature which doesn't make any sense at all. First like everything else gameplay related it's a glitchy, buggy, clunky mess. You don't know when the punches connect, you lose the sight of your enemy because you can't lock him, you slide back 5 meters for some reason. And why on earth fistfighting is there? You play as a drug addicted girl and you fight big men with your fists. No wait it gets even more ridiculous. Sometimes these men have bottles in their hands, you just raise your hands to block the hit then hit back few times and he gives up. What the...?But of course there are qte's and even these are done poorly. You need to do them extremely quickly and it's hard to tell what you need to do – hold the button, click it repeatedly or click it once, the icons aren't clear enough and very similar to each other so when you need to react in a split of a second it's too hard. Why not use colored button icons?I think that's all about gameplay.The story is dark and very violent. It seems nice, I love it, there's domestic violence, torture, mass shootings, drug abuse, sexual abuse and so on. I love this stuff in games. But the plot doesn't make sense towards the end. I'll put spoiler tag now so don't read if you intend to play it.  obviously I love violence in games but I want it to make sense or just be stupid over the top like Yakuza games. This one is neither because the game presents itself as realistic.But the story in general is pretty nice, it tells a sad tale of drug addicted girl and a man she meets. Gitta is a waitress who strives to become a musician but she's addicted to drugs and her life was crap since childhood, it was traumatizing. Kids often blame themselves for parents fighting. She constantly fight the addiction and if Gitta doesn't use drugs it's getting harder to see the world and it becomes surreal.There are also various text messages appearing on the screen which are very hard to read but it think it's a good thing because it shows the thoughts of a mentally unstable person.Such story with such idea, I thought it's a guaranteed success, worst case scenario a slightly above average game so it's still beyond my comprehension how they messed it up so badly.It also has great replayability value since it has few endings and you can make completely different choices throughout the game. One playthrough is roughly 2 hours.Graphics. I...i...i...don't know what to say. What is this, a PS2 game? I'm not exaggerating. The graphics, 3D modeling, texturing is so terrible that asset flips look better. What... why... how? Only the surrounding areas are nice looking so 9/10 for that, but characters and animations are laughably bad. It's like Skyrim running on a 480p.At least the artistic style is decent.Performance is great, game runs on max settings fine along with native ultrawide support. Played on 5800x, 2070s, 32gb @3440x1440.Controls are terrible, sometimes you get wrong button prompts (X instead of RT) and it's just clunky. Often it's hard to click on items. Why not make it third person and use button prompts when you approach something?So we came to sound finally. First, there's no voice acting and this game doesn't need it. There's only music playing all the time and the story is told through combinations of cut-scenes, gameplay, lyrics and music. Sometimes characters sing some lines along. It's a brilliant idea and the whole album is wonderful. It fits into the mood of the game and every single scene so well that I can't even describe it. It's just wonderful. You say: why not just listen to soundtrack then if the game is so terrible? Without seeing the scenes and characters, their struggle, you won't understand what is going on, it's like an opera/musical, you need to see it.The symphonic metal album is absolutely great. Probably 99% of the budget went to the artists.This game needed few more months in the oven, maybe even a year or more, such a shame, such potential, a lot of people won't play it because of controls, gameplay or graphics and I don't blame them. The idea and atmosphere is brilliant but idea is not enough. If you make a game with such diverse gameplay mechanics you need to make them work decently at least. If it had the gameplay like traditional narrative games it could be a wonderful game. Definitely not worth the asking price. I'd say it's still worth playing but only if you get this from a bundle so give it a chance in that case.I obviously gonna play it because I still find it somewhat enjoyable due to the soundtrack and replayability and i'm still looking forward to the next game (hopefully) but you'll need to decide for yourself if the idea and soundtrack alone are worth your money.

_childDocuments_.review: Of Bird and Cage is a 2-hour metal album under the guise of a narrative game. The gameplay is bizarre and sometimes frustrating, but as expected, the soundtrack is the titles saving grace. The collaboration of many infamous artists is by far, the strong point of the game. The story itself is exceptionally grim, centring around various traumatic themes that are thrown in all at once and it is certainly not for the faint hearted.+ Amazing metal soundtrack that matches and compliments the scenes in the game brilliantly, featuring many prominent artists, known from  and many more.+ At least 4 different endings and varying choices throughout the game, providing excellent replay value.+ Easy chapter select options to replay certain levels.+ Collectables + Steam achievements.- Everything is timed, no time for exploration and some tasks are unclear with a short timeframe to complete them.- The overblown amount of trauma and violence in the game was overbearing and confusing (until later acts)Playing as Gitta, a 25-year-old with an exceptionally troubled past, players are thrust into her chaotic world. Gitta is a drug addict, reliant on feeding her addiction to see the world clearer (or so she thinks...). Beginning with scenes from her traumatic childhood and abusive father to quickly venturing to drugs was a lot already, but it gets worse. After giving up her dignity with a dealer to obtain more drugs, Gitta gets into physical fights, is taken advantage of by her boss, is beaten by her abusive boyfriend and father whilst being witness to graphic murders by her abductor, Brees (yes, she gets chased and kidnapped as well). If this all was not enough for her, she also uncovers an awful death in the family and a long-forgotten connection with Brees that further spirals her downwards. After my first hour playing Of Bird and Cage, I was thinking, what on Earth am I playing? I am all for a dark story, covering intense topics but this game really takes it to the next level. When you think that is it, the developers curve the story more to make it even more twisted. In the first Act, I did find it a bit overwhelming, with no real background story or understanding to the protagonist, all of her ordeals began to swirl into one and was a bit difficult to keep up, also lessening the emotional impact.  Thankfully, it does begin to take a better shape in later Acts but by no means does the game ever become "pleasant". It is a gruelling experience and truly demonstrates the realistic spiralling nature of someone in Gitta's position.Unfortunately, as I envisioned, the gameplay is NOT the best element of the game, but it also is not terrible. Using typical WSAD keys to control Gitta, explore the areas and pick up collectables and items, that aspect is all pretty straight forward. Where it does a complete 360 is that every scene is timed, predetermined by the length of the song playing. This made it impossible to take in my surroundings and explore, or in parts where the tasks were a bit obscure, I simply did not have the time to be able to figure it out. Once the timer ends, it does not result in death, but just acts as if you did not complete it so the story branches down a different path which is slightly annoying. I lost count of how many times Gitta finds herself in physical fights with multiple men. I found each and every one of these scenes to be god-awful, simply painful. Using easy right click to block and left click to strike, it was utterly janky, and I have no idea if some of my hits connected with the target, or if my blocks worked. If my hits connected, it was merely serendipitous. Not to mention that I am playing as a tiny 25-year-old female drug addict (who is shown to be physically weak), against multiple men at once, including my large, fit, and older abductor, and I can win, just using my fists? I am all for female empowerment, but this was just bizarre and the actual combat, an embarrassment. The movement was also quite clanky and simple tasks like using a broom to reach a box was a real challenge. On a more positive note, there were many story items to be found throughout the areas, as well as little extra choices, typically connected to achievements. This made the world seem richer, but it was once again severely impaired by the time limits imposed on players. Even finding the actual "task items" before time ran out, could be tricky. The game is also riddled with QTE's, which are not my favourite, but I found majority to be more forgiving in this title, thankfully. Graphics are quite average, with most characters featuring similar facial expressions from start to finish. The world is constantly flashing and words popping up everywhere, emulating the perspectives of a drug addicts. This did get a bit taxing on my eyes and I was constantly choosing to take more drugs just for clearer visuals, but I suppose this is the intended purpose. Understandably, the developers from  are a small company of musicians and fellow gamers, with little actual background experience in large game development projects. Their passion to convey music through games is both unique and inspiring. In my opinion, not having top tier graphics in this style of game is not necessary. Depending on your expectations, Of Bird and Cage does not look awful, its decent and it is enjoyable, especially when paired with the wonderful soundtrack.Although I have laced my review with plenty of constructive criticism, one element which I cannot fault, the actual premise of the title - the music. Everything plays brilliantly in sync, sometimes as if the characters are in a metal musical. The melodramatic riffs and theatrical rhythmic beats are impeccable. The songs themselves are also catchy and it is clear that this is where the game shines the most. Running away from enemies through burning, hazy streets with the clashes of an orchestral symphony in the background that perfectly matches the flashes of lightning across the screen, really fuels the heartrate!  Despite other elements of the game being a bit haphazard, the soundtrack and unique music focus in a game is enough for me to recommend the experience to metal fans. Featuring  and many more, the collaboration of these artists make for an impressive album. Of Bird and Cage differs from other titles, solely focusing on its musical incorporation and composition. Despite its lacklustre gameplay and overwhelmingly traumatic story, it still manages to be a captivating, yet distressing experience, one I will not forget too quickly. With differing branching paths and an easy method to replay chapters, the option for replayability is high. The developer’s passion for displaying an impressive metal soundtrack through a game is both clear and unique. I recommend this title to those interested in the featured artists and musical genre as a whole. For those looking for a darker story, not too fussed with the application of music, I'd recommend looking towards more narrative-focused games.  This review copy was provided to the Devils in the Detail curator.

_childDocuments_.review: This title falls under the "wish there was a neutral button". I played only via Steam Deck, so feed back here for the review is based on my experience playing it this way. First off, the game is labeled as being a verified deck game. This is more or less true, the prologue worked fine with no settings changes. However, getting the actual game to run required forcing it to Proton 5.13-6 compatibility. Some video did not display properly and navigating back to main menu from ends of chapters hung the game requiring forced shut down.The Music score was stellar and fit the themes of the game well as was certainly intended. The game play for me was less than stellar. QTE events run the show here and are quite confusing in some places or out right impossible to get right as you are on a time elapse to complete objectives and use QTE. There isn't much room for exploring an area because of this and you will often fail to accomplish a lot of things. Although failing to do things doesn't lead to any game over or repeat of the chapter to continue, it left me feeling like I missed a large part of the narrative going on. I'm aware that there are multiple endings which I assume I could reach by completing QTE better or managing to beat the clock in some scenes to alter the outcome in the ending. I don't think I'll be doing another play through to be honest as the pressure of beating the clock to find things in overly large areas coupled with QTE system that had a lot of moving parts puts me off from giving it another try.I found the story was adequate for my time spent with it and it is certainly a different type of interactive game that is worth a try. In closing I would say cautiously recommended with the expectation that there will be much trial and error to see all thats on offer here.

_childDocuments_.review: This is quite a crazy game.Watch your alcoholic father kill your beloved mother and become a sanity-losing and seriously drug-addicted woman sleeping with her drug dealer and dreaming to become a rock star.Flee hallucinating through dark passages while brawling (and constantly losing) during QTEs. All this while there is no speech or sound, but only a metal soundtrack (with different songs, not so bad) blasting through your speakers.Don't take drugs.

_childDocuments_.review: Video Review:  Music 9/10 Story 7.5/10 Gameplay 5/10 Of Bird and Cage from Capricia Productions is a unique one. A 2hour long story driven metal album. Playing as Gitta a drug addict who goes on one hell of a bad decision train and ends up kidnapped by Bres Lupus. The team was going for the strange and ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up realities of drugs and trauma, and if beauty and the beast stock holm syndrome was in real life. It’s a roller coaster of game or should I say album because this is the main focus of bird and cage. It sets itself up like a musical with characters singing.  Graphically its lacking but it gets the message across well and doesn’t hinder the music in any way. Mechanics are slightly strange, with you needing to preform actions with in a set duration of the song. Actions like driving, collecting money, setting traps or trying to escape. Failing to do so will not fail the game you will just be sent down the branching paths of the story to either redemption or destruction. Of bird and cage has many branching paths and multiple endings at least 4 that I know it has.  I would say the gameplay, if not for the music, would be mediocre at best, if the music was not driving the story and all you had was the game play, you would not wanna play. With objectives that are confusing or level design and some controls lacking. It's truly going to be one you play for the story and in this case the music. So technically this is an album review for of bird and cage because this is where all the money was sunk into.  With Ron Thal (ex Guns N’ Roses) Rob van der loo (Epica) Ruude Jolie (Within Temptations) Kobra Paige (Kobra and the Lotus) and others. With symphony style music scores, heavy rifts and drums it’s a heavy metal fans wet dream. Now there are some sections of the album that are strange with talking portions to drive the story, but overall, the tempo the structure of the music is beautifully done, but this may hinder the album itself, a portion of the songs really only connect in context with the game it’s a unique median to portray music especial in a musical essk style, and I could be wrong. I’m not the one who listens to heavy metal all the time so this huge story driven linier album you be a thing.  Overall, of bird and cage is an experience. With a story that can get extremely dark, music made by a wide variety of Artist coming together, and I Enjoyed it. It’s also a game that can be streamed with no copyrights on it so now you can have music on twitch again and that’s a positive. With a Price tag of 15 dollars, you are getting a deal with either an album with a game, or a game with an album. So, if you are a fan of branching stories and heavy metal pick this game up, I don’t think you will be disappointed and have multiple playthrough giving you hours of playtime.

_childDocuments_.review: First I have to say, the idea behind it, that the story is told through the music in the genre of metal I find ingenious and was accordingly, also by all the positive reviews really curious what to expect. Unfortunately, the game has disappointed me very much. It's not the music, which is most of the time really very very good, but everything else was really not so successful. The controls are really crappy in places, the fights just don't feel right, and everything in general is a bit weird. The story is poor to okay at most. The animations to the spoken & sung are subterranean and the voice actors at the beginning of the game really didn't speak convincingly and seemed very posed.The gameplay itself was, because it was adapted to the music often very stressful and I have often not even managed what was required by the game. I can honestly not quite understand the positive reviews, that is except for the music just really badly done. In any case, no recommendation on my part, sorry.

_childDocuments_.review: Of Birds and Cage is a story focused interactive game with music elements. Play as a young drug addict named Gitta as you journey through a part of her life in a small town.The gameplay is a first-person interactive fiction story as you go through the harsh reality and world. There are numerous people to meet, puzzles to solve, and areas to encounter. It does have some Life is Strange vibes with the game being in a small town, starting off in a dive bar and playing as a young woman. The story itself is interesting with multiple endings so of course there is some replayability in unlocking and viewing them all. Though not everything ends with happy endings as such in life, it does come with consequence to your choices and actions. There are some interesting components to the game, like what relates to her drug addiction. With it, it can affect the colouring and blurring of the visuals depending on if she is able to get drugs or not. All in all, the gameplay and story are quite enjoyable to progress and go through.The visuals and graphics are pretty good, which again reminds me of Life is Strange. There are several locations to progress through with an array of characters, some friendly and some not so and are also well voice acted for the most part. With music being a focus in the game, having some quality music to listen to is an important factor. There are some maybe recognizable artists that are featured depending on if you listen to the band or genre. I do recognize Guns N’ Roses and Evanescence, but not the featured artists themselves. Though I don’t personally listen to much metal and rock, the music in the game have been enjoyable and accompanies well with the story and theme. Not all the songs and music are limited to metal and rock, as there are some more melancholic and emotional ones in there as well which adds to the somber tone of the game.Controls aren’t anything complex with the game being pretty much just moving your characters around, interacting with what is in the area and with people, and various buttons to press for certain events. It is controller support so can be played with whatever is most comfortable. Overall, the game is a noteworthy story-based game with an interesting, dark themes and some quality music.
_childDocuments_.name: Of Bird and Cage

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an absolute dumpster fire with a beautiful soundtrack. I really, really wanted to like it, because I like the work of many of the musicians involved. But it's awful. Think Superman 64 levels of bad.-The physics frequently don't work. For example, at multiple points during scenes of running or driving, my character or their vehicle would get stuck and be unable to move/climb/drive.-The game mechanics are a mess. Fights can be easily won by pushing someone into a corner and spamming the punch button. The QTEs aren't telegraphed at all, and the visual difference between indicators [hold vs press once] isn't easily discernible when you need to react quickly.-Basic words in both the subtitles and lyrics are frequently misspelled, and some sentences are worded like they are poor translations. And some of the writing is laughably bad - for instance, a drug dealer who has a list of customers titled something like "drug money from drug buyers". The kind of stuff you'd expect in a parody. -Glitches abound. Be careful checking your collectibles on the menu, for instance - you might crash the game, or end up with a collectible covering the screen even after you've exited the collectibles menu.-The storytelling is horrifically bad. It's really unclear why in the world a guy who got into a car wreck to avoid hitting you then went to jail for it. And it seems like he comes after you years later for revenge, but then has a change of heart for... no clear reason? And then he kills your drug dealer - which, fine, ok. But then you're expected to shoot the police to keep this guy - who kidnapped you - from going to jail. And then the third act does stuff like drop you in the diner where you used to work with a gun and hostages, acting like there needs to be no explanation for why you'd do that. That's not to say these plot bits couldn't work with good explanations, fleshing out the characters, giving everyone motivation... but the game doesn't do this. ...there's so much more. Honestly, I'm really sad about it, because I had been looking forward to this game, and hoping that it could show of some great new possibilities for how to experience an album. Instead, it just made me jump back and forth between laughing, screaming at the ridiculous decisions, cringing at the dialogue, and wanting to throw my computer across the room because of shonky controls.Do not buy. Stay far away.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not easy for me to give this game a bad review, because I genuinely think the idea is wonderful and the devs seem like lovely people. However, I want to be honest when giving reviews, as this serves both other people as well as the devs to improve their game.The idea of this game, a metal album presented as a game is pretty neat. In practice this basically plays as 1 level = 1 song. Sometimes the music is just in the background, sometimes it's the characters themselves singing. Each song is roughly 10-15 minutes long so the game isn't super long, but it doesn't need to be to tell it's story.The reason I'm giving this game a bad review is the gameplay. There is too much going on in this game. You can tell the devs had lots of ideas they wanted to implement into the game, but sometimes less is better.You have a drug meter in this game, you can find drugs and take them which changes the vision of your character. It doesn't do much else aside distorting your vision if you don't find any drugs. The gameplay itself feels clunky..What bothered me most where the objectives in the game. Very often you're tasked to explore and find certain items in order to progress, but since the game constantly runs on a timer, the song, you always end up not being able to find everything in time. The game does not wait for you and depending on how you do the story slightly changes. You can't really lose or mess up, which is good cause half the time I felt myself not finding an item I needed. It does feel like the type of game that wants you replaying it multiple times in order to get everything perfect. Further shown by the fact that there are multiple endings.I don't want to say too much about the story, since it's most likely what you will get the game for. I liked how it started out, but later on there were some things that didn't make a lot of sense. But again, it was an interessting story.If you want this game, I'd suggest waiting for a sale. The devs had great ideas, the execution just lacks. But for an experiment worth about 3 hours, it can certainly be a fun time.

_childDocuments_.review: Before you read this, I'll say this: If you like the music, buy Karmaflow The Rock opera Videogame on Steam. Much better game, much better music. HOWEVER, STILL SUPPORT THIS GAME.This game basically commands you for multiple playthroughs to completely understand the plot. That's not terrible, but very annoying. Your first playthrough will be VERY confusing, jarring, and ultimately leave you unsatisfied. You'll feel frustrated by the end of the first act, but the second act is where the story really becomes understandable. That's where you feel the game as what it truly is, and connect with the characters in the story. This game is not for the faint at heart. There are VERY dark themes. Uncomfortable themes. But, don't let that take away from the unique style and concept of this game.There are things to understand and things to improve upon this game, as any. Biggest would be captions for the vocals. The plot of the game is barred deep in the vocals of Kobra Page and Davidavi Dolev. The downside is that it can sometimes be hard to listen in to their story while solving puzzles. Having something to read would have been nice to help with while playing the game. I also would have enjoyed a bit more "guidance" rather than just simply assuming I know what I'm doing. Some times, that concept can work very well for a game. With this, and the whole game being timer driven, it can be viewed as anxious, and feel like your first playthrough will leave you with a bad ending. Also, it may be worth not streaming this game the first time you play it. Doing commentary while listening to the music while trying to figure out what's going on can be super jarring. Honestly, I wish I played this by myself before I decided to stream it.Understand, I still am telling people to play this game. There IS a good game in there. The story is engaging when it happens, and is a very unique style albeit not new. Like I said before, Karmaflow: The Rock Opera Videogame is also available and shares the same concept as an interactive music game, but that has a deeper platformer vibe. I'd love to see DLC from this, or even a sequel from this game with a deeper storyline or another storyline with the same concept. I applaud Capricia Productions for this concept and hope they continue with this in the future. This is their first game, and I'm glad there's room to improve in the future for them. It's a solid first release from a new indie studio with some issues that can improved upon. That's 100% acceptable and fine. I will follow this company and eagerly await what they have in store for the future.Buy the game, but be honest and sincere in your criticisms. Doing so means this concept can thrive, and that's something I truly want in the gaming industry.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game, because the concept behind it is suuuper cool. Like, an interactive metal album? Sign me the ♥♥♥♥ up! Reality, however, is harsher. You can have style over substance in video games, but there's very little substance in this, and it's all very bad.Of Bird and Cage tells the story of a young woman who can't seem to escape bad decisions, even when you're telling her to stop ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ up, y'know, in the INTERACTIVE part of the game? The game part plays as a sort of point and click adventure, where you have to find stuff to interact with in order to advance the plot. Again, cool concept, but poorly executed. The story is bad, and told ass-backwards - as in, something happens, then the game goes "five hours before", then something else happens and it's "two hours before". ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ just tell me the story the way it happened. I know this was probably created this way in an attempt to hide the fact that the player has very little agency, but it just makes the plot unnecessarily hard to follow.Getting stuck in this game is very easy, which is a problem when you have a set time to make the story advance. It's hard to stay inside my 5min time limit when I can't find a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ pair of shoes anywhere and that's all I'm looking for during the entirety of those five minutes.Finally, the music is awesome, but it takes you too long to reach it. In fact, I never did during my playthrough. That, and the bad game design and poorly told story made me give up on the game. The idea has potential, and I feel like it'd be awesome if the devs came up with a patch to fix all these issues, maybe make a definitive edition of sorts. As it stands though, it's hard to enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, so it pains me to have to say this, but I wouldn't recommend this game.It has absolutely wonderful and great concepts applied, but it falls apart in the dev side.  Best way to describe it is it feels like an amazing game concept, but slapped together with all the cheapest or free assets possible to make it come together when you don't have the budget to do the programming yourself.  So S-Tier concept, absolute failure in terms of gameplay.Controls are trash, mini game fights are trash, quick time events are somehow 1000% more trash than most quick time events, and I say this as a software developer that for funsies has made basic games whose controls functioned identically to this game.  Know how I did it, purchased or installed free assets that other people made and then tweaked it a bit to try smoothing it out.  It came out just as bad as this.Should pull out the dumb fights, turn it into more timed choices, basic puzzles, etc.  Play to the games and devs strengths here.  Sure you won't have as many features to the game, but I would greatly prefer a fully functional simpler game than this buggy crap (bug in this case meaning not ship-able quality).  I legit want to see the other story possibilities, but getting through to one ending was a huge trial in patience that I uninstalled it after one play through and will not ever attempt to play it again, not will I watch someone else play it just to see the other endings because that in itself would be painful to watch.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a metal musical PC game! What more could a metal-head gamer ask for? :)The play time is between 2 and 2.5 hours for the first run, and looks like it doesn't depend a lot on the player's choices. Most of the gameplay is timed and it's almost impossible to complete all tasks in the given time, but, luckily, it's not needed. Although some outcomes depend on the player's actions, the game will reach an ending regardless. It's worth replaying several times to see the different endings, complete quests and collect story items.The style reminds me a bit of Life is Strange, if it was a lot darker, with a heavier soundtrack. There are a few fist fights and shootouts too. I like the way the characters start singing along to the background song. It's as if I was watching a musical. It's a unique game. Heavily recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most unique and surreal experiences you will ever play. Beauty and the Beast meets Sin City on a modern story covering multiple real adult issues.Story 10/10Naturally this is where it shines. It focuses on your character(Gitta) who suffers from having a traumatic childhood and ends up having the same traits as her parents. As she is now grown up she naturally falls into the wrong crowd and becomes addicted to drugs and is at the mercy of her dealer BF and has a rather rough and unplesent life. This abruptly changes once she meets (Brees) who takes her captive and she really falls through down the rabbit hole and spirals into insanity and the dark places that come with it. Her drug addiction alters her perspective as it shows the affect having withdrawal has on the body and mind. Without your fix the world looks dramatically different. What I really like is how this game covers multiple difficult to talk about subjects, Drug Addiction, Domestic Violence, Abusive relationships and highlights them into an artful story that makes you really feel the physical and mental struggle she is going through.You are looking at a Whirlwind 2 hours with a lot of incentive to replay for 4 endings and collectables.Audio 10/10Fantastic music soundtrack throughout the game. Heavy metal sequences in action moments and an even a duet in one of the captive sequences, The songs really highlight the impact Stockholm syndrome has had on Gitta and through the music it shows how her perspective of Brees changes throughout the experience. In a game like this it would have to deliver and it does oh so marvellously.Graphics 8/10 - Ran very well and didnt have any FPS issues. Locations all looked crisp and set the atmosphere needed to progress throughout the game. The addiction fire looked an impressive visual.Gameplay 7/10Probably the one area it is a little bit weak in places. Most of the story based interactions plays very well and the chase sequences are smooth. I just found the fighting sequences to be a tad weak especially the hand to hand combat sequences. They just didn't deliver the theatrics the rest of the game delivered. I would also argue you have to think fast in a lot of the sequences and why I would encourage everyone to at least play this 2-3 times as for some of the endings you will need to have a firm knowledge of where key objects are to alter your scenario as time really is your enemy a lot of the times.But I loved how some of the sequences you are set up to fail. It highlights the struggle and the mental hopelessness Gitta is trying to push through with no clear. path in sight.Overall 9/10 - Going to say this is a new and must play experience. It tastefully and Artfully covers several difficult subjects and highlights how no life is perfect but you could be in a far darker place and what is needed to overcome it.My Full YT review is below

_childDocuments_.review: I had high hopes for this one because the marriage of progressive metal and interactive story-telling would be right up my ally, but  completely underwhelmed me.The music is good, that's all I can say on a positive note. _childDocuments_.review: Really liked the music in this game and kudos for daring to try something different - using a series of songs to tell the story is a very cool premise. However, like many players have pointed out, the game seems to want you to do too many things within a fairly short time limit. That's not including the fact that many of the stuff that needs doing can only be uncovered if you explore the place and that there are plenty of collectibles to find and collect, and yet the time limit doesn't allow any of this. Wasn't able to really complete all the objectives in any one scene either, and probably have had the game force the story to go the way I would have preferred it NOT to go.I'm guessing the devs designed the game this way in order to fit the game to the length of the song and to get the player to replay levels just to get everything perfectly. Of course, there's also the fact that there are multiple endings to uncover. Still, every scene felt rushed to me and I wasn't able to take my time to really explore and figure out what needs doing and how to do it. Many of the Quick-Time Events also caught me by surprise and there were plenty of times when I wasn't able to respond quickly enough (probably no thanks to feeling nauseous; reason at the end of this review), which skewed certain events towards outcomes that I would love to avoid. Personally, the story is alright - a tale of vengeance or forgiveness, depending on your decisions; and it's a very tragic tale at that. In this game, you play as a 25-y/o drug addict with some major childhood trauma to unpack, who has her dealer as her BF; works at a diner as a waitress for meager pay and have a total creep for a boss; lives in a crappy RV; and has an alcoholic, abusive father whom she suspect killed her mum back when she's just a kid. That's not including the other main character, Bres Lupus, and his own story which was intertwined with yours, no thanks to a tragic event. There are some parts that I think don't really make any logical sense, like , or that I agreed with, but it is what it is I guess.The controls here aren't the best, but I'd say they are serviceable. The only major qualm I have is the way you have to drag objects and open drawers or doors. It's a bit frustrating especially with the time limit hanging over your head, despite being more realistic. In addition to driving, I'm not a huge fan of the many brawls Gitta managed to get herself into either. It took me awhile to figure out how to really land a hit - aim for the head - and that you can't just constantly block attacks. There's also the little drug addiction thing that you'll have to contend with. Drug withdrawals are typically tough to deal with. In this game, it will cause Gitta to hallucinate, but it doesn't really affect the gameplay too much. For instance, ven with blurry vision, I was still able to headshot "enemies", who were just doing their jobs and were coming after Bres and Gitta, because... well, they did assault and kill someone . Last but most importantly, despite the indicator at the middle of the screen, the game still gave me some pretty severe motion sickness which forced me to take lengthy breaks in between Acts - sometimes even in between scenes. Not sure if there's something more in the settings that could have alleviated this, but I'm glad to say I made it to the end of the game.For me, I'd give a hesitant recommendation. The game has some good and unique ideas, which IMHO warrants at least a playthrough if you love a solid tragic story and excellent metal music, but it fails at properly executing these ideas, at least in a way that allows the player to comfortably do all the things the developers want and expect the player to do. Personally, I think it would have been better if time limits are removed entirely, but considering how the "levels" are designed, this might not be possible. It could use a lot more polish as well, namely the controls.

_childDocuments_.review: Of Bird and Cage doesn’t really start until you approach the sound guy and ask to have your demo CD played.  It is this very CD that provides the non-stop musical engine that drives the rest of this two-hour experience divided across three multi-part Acts and a summary credit sequence and epilogue.  Once the music starts to play each and every scene in the game will unfold at the pace and length of each song, as displayed by the track progression meter at the bottom.  When the music stops, the level ends regardless of what you have or haven’t done.  You could simply stand there and do nothing for the duration of the song and the story will continue, albeit taking the failure path vs. a potentially different path if you were to accomplish the listed objectives.  A list of tasks and sometimes collectibles will tell you what needs done before the music stops.For those playing the game the first time, expect plenty of failure, as the song times are quite restrictive.  Sometimes it would take me the entire song length to simply explore my surrounding, thus the game demands multiple replays to win, let alone accomplish extra objectives like finding hidden CD’s stashed around the game.  For this very reason it is best, at least for your first playthrough, to just not care about “winning”.  Just experience the game, owning all your bad decisions, accepting all your failed QTE’s, and living with those impossible musical time limits.  There are three possible endings to this bizarre story that is so twisted and depressing I won’t even begin to describe it.Of Bird and Cage is a tough game to recommend because your enjoyment is totally reliant on several things, many of which defy the very concept of gaming.  First, you must enjoy heavy-metal music.  There is some amazing music from amazing artists included in this game; check out the videos on Steam to get a taste and even see a live performance.  For gamers, you’ll need to put aside everything you have ever learned about adventure gaming and approach this as more of an objective based speed-run.  Even the most basic objectives are on timers with only seconds to spare.  Accept the fact that if you want to see and do everything this game has to offer you are going to be playing some chapters multiple times.  Of Bird and Cage is also painfully depressing to play, and even when you are allowed to take Gitta on a Kill Bill-style, choice-driven revenge trip it’s hard to find satisfaction.Read full review at

_childDocuments_.review: Welcome to my Ted Talk:OBAC is a "Life is Strange" -esque deep dive into the life of one young woman with a ton of real life problems. She grew up in an abusive home, still lives with an abusive parent, and has fallen into a life of drug abuse and so much more. She is so sad and compelling leading us to empathize with her and hopefully guide her to a better outcome through it all.Honesty up front: I have played only the first act (songs 1-5) of the game, but I have played them numerous times over about 6 hours. Is it a perfect game? Absolutely not, but let's cover the important stuff.The story of the game is as immersive as it is heart wrenching. It makes us want to succeed, and the more I learn about Gitta and her past, the more I want to help her through this turmoil.The key division among reviewers... this game has many coding flaws and glitches, but that's part of the charm. It is blatantly obvious where the developers wanted to focus their coding. For example, as the music plays, some things in the environment illuminate or pulse in time with the music. This is very enjoyable. Gitta's thoughts randomly appear as words you walk in/through/around, and that feels true to how thoughts enter and exit our minds as things happen around us. And the singing scenes are beautifully created while some of the lesser non-plot based conversations are not as thoroughly polished.Every act is one song in length, each with their own missions and "story changing actions". You have the length of one song to find the correct things to interact with and/or people to talk to. IMHO, this increases my desire to replay the game (and why I have 6 hours in only 5 songs). Either I enjoy the song itself, I enjoy trying to figure out what to accomplish during the song, or many times BOTH. It is absolutely possible to accomplish every listed mission within each song. Some songs give plenty of time to do this, while others do not. In the end, whatever missions you accomplish or story changing actions you end with is up to you, and you can replay each song to get the results you desire, ultimately developing Gitta exactly the way you want her to be by the time she reaches the end of her journey.Interactions happen in the form of mini-games where you have to click or hold buttons to accomplish a task. Some reviewers say these QTEs are needlessly complex, but I say that adds to the tension of the moment. For example, a drinking mini-game requires you to hold one button while clicking another repeatedly, simple enough. But a couple of songs later, you have to hold a button and click another repeatedly in a frantically shorter amount of time to escape a pursuing kidnapper. My only negative comment about the gameplay is in the form of the combat system, but this game isn't a fighting game! It's a song-based story. Not only that, our character is a drug-using 25 year old waitress. She shouldn't be good at combat anyway, making the fight scenes quite realistic.Let's get this out of the way: as much as the game says it is "metal", it is not. This is symphonic rock. Some of the songs are purely instrumental while others are fully vocalized with in-game characters singing. The music sounds like Evanescence and Within Temptation because that's what the developers wanted it to sound like. It is obvious that the music is where they spent the majority of their budget (as you can tell by some of the game's coded scenes).Ok, so the voice acting isn't all that great, but again, that's NOT the point! The conversations that do occur verbally are merely filler to get to the music. It's the plot that matters, and many of the best interactions in the game are not voiced at all. Instead, they are Gitta's thoughts written around the person talking explaining what they are saying in fewer words "I'm late for work" or "He wants privacy", etc. Another example of just how smart the developers were is how realistic Gitta's thoughts actually are. As a 5-year-old Gitta plays with her mommy, she is an innocent little child. This makes the abuse her father causes to her mother all that much more heartbreaking when observant little Gitta thinks "Mommy and Daddy are dancing" before he hits her and "Is it because of me" after the fight ends.  There are many other thoughts Gitta has that clearly outline how her mind is working as the events unfold around her, showing the developers had a strong understanding of how her mind would work in reality. And if I'm being honest, I like Gitta's voice.Play it from start to finish in one go, and take what you get in regards to what happens to Gitta in each song, and yeah, the game is only 2 hours long. It's the replayability where this game makes its mark. As I said above, you WANT to play again because you WANT to do better. I find myself replaying songs wondering what happens if Gitta doesn't make it to the elevator, or what if Gitta doesn't take any drugs? (BTW, the game actually doesn't let you enter certain areas if she is halucinating! That changes the story!)There are 4 endings.  I have seen none of them, but I can't wait to see them all!tl;dr:Do I recommend this game?  Do I recommend this game to gamers?  This game is for people who love music (symphonic rock fans), story (Life is Strange and Detroit: Become Human fans), casual games (5-15 minute game fans), and walking simulator games (Gris, Journey, and Dear Esther fans).Thanks for reading!

_childDocuments_.review: Proper review pending once I actually finish the game. I've played through two acts so far, trying to keep it at one a day.I love this game for its sheer audacity, and I highly recommend it. I had been pondering whether a game could also be a musical (as I'm a fan of both) when it popped up on my recommendations. So of course I bought it, and then sat on it for a month before playing it.Neither the music nor the gameplay are impressive on their own. The latter consists of unreasonably difficult, timed object hunts; intrusive, Telltale-style quicktime events; and clunky, unresponsive combat against NPCs with completely unrealistic behaviour. The former sounds like the cheesiest power metal concept album you've ever heard, complete with bad synth, almost stupidly on-the-nose lyrics, and incredibly simple chord progressions. (Credit to the musicians for at least playing and/or singing it very well.)Somehow the combination of the two is utterly engrossing.The Telltale-style quicktime events are disruptive and distract you from the music, which is  the lyrics are stupidly simplistic: they let you pick up on what's going on even while you're scrambling to accomplish the tasks you've been given. Meanwhile the music, while certainly not impressive, is in no way bad, and the operatic and disturbing plot adds a huge amount of weight to its metal cred. Even when I find myself laughing at janky animations or ridiculous minigames, I am still thoroughly immersed in what might not have been a good metal album if it were a traditional release, but is an excellent metal album taken as a whole package.Some of this game is even broken, and I just don't care, because none of what's broken actually matters. If anything it adds to the charm. I salute the devs and musicians for taking this risk, and I even hope there'll be a follow-up that surpasses the original.An afterword regarding difficulty: as I said, a lot of the sections are unreasonably difficult. I don't think I've won a single object hunt yet, and it took me until the middle of act 2 to finally win my first fight. Part of that seems to be purely for immersion -- fights that your player character just isn't equipped to win -- but I think part of it also is replayability. The music actually seems to change based on what you do or fail to do, and at the end of the day, a metal album is something you listen to again and again, not just once. I think it actually fits the artistic vision very well.

_childDocuments_.review: After waiting patiently for this game to release, I can firmly say the end product being so much more than I expected. The game plays on some very intense situations as you join Gitta on her downward spiral into addiction. You're placed in scenarios where bad decisions can cost you your sanity and really throws out the question of how far are you willing to go for your next fix. One thing I absolutely loved about this game is that you can choose to not partake in Gitta's vices, but will equally struggle with getting by. Indulging in her addiction will lead you down a broken path, but choosing to stay sober will give you a chance to experience the mind-numbing struggle of *needing* to take one more hit, but refusing to do so. That is really well done in this game. The game itself plays along to a metal/goth rock album that steals the show more times than not, especially when the characters in the scene not only acknowledge the music and lyrics, but actively respond and take part in performing them. This can start to dull out a little bit if you intend on replaying the game multiple times, but even after listening to the same songs 6-7+ times, they're still a welcomed change to the normal ambient music you find in most story-driven games like this. As far the gameplay and decision making goes, I gotta say it's really well done. The game is full of quick moving QTEs that you'll need to perform, but unlike other games, if you fail these QTEs, the story will change. You have the opportunity to visit new cutscenes and areas depending on how well (or not well) you do with the QTEs (save for any "minigame" related ones). All of these areas are related to some form of collectible, be it a story item or a CD, so you really want to take your time and visit every branching path available in the game if you're going for all of the achievements. Be warned about those achievements, though, as some of those CDs are quite hard to find. The voice acting in this game is absolutely phenomenal and really sets the tone for the ever-changing plot line that dips and dives through intermingling character stories. The more you learn about Gitta, the more questionable her situation becomes, but you can either let it get to you and cower away, or stand up and fight your demons. The game itself is not too long (looking about an hour/hour and a half depending on how well you do on the QTEs), but it offers a lot of replayability if you're willing to take some chances with your decisions. Overall, this game is very much recommended. It's intense, it's easy to play, it forces to you make quick and sometimes brash decisions, and is all delivered in a well put together musical package that you'll be thinking about well after you're done playing.

_childDocuments_.review: Let's get one thing straight. I love nu metal and still will pay to see Korn in concert because I refuse to grow up, but there's nostalgia in that. Furthermore I love me a good rock opera and I would gladly pay to see Kilroy was Here if the real Styx ever decides to get back together and tour. (Dennis, you're too good for them.) That said, this rock, nu metal opera with some mixed in soulful ballads was a mixed bag of problematic storylines that didn't feel resolved, a weird dive into trauma and sexual themes, and a story that continued to make me question my own gameplay. I've achieved 2 of the 4 endings, neither of which were satisfying (perhaps I got the bad ones?) and instead left me feeling ways I can't express for fear of ruining the story. I've been in enough abusive relationships that maybe that interferes with the way I see the story. That said - the idea is dope. I want to see more of this style. I like the idea of an album that you can play. I love the idea that your protagonist is literally writing the song of their life. It's unique and this game is full of cool ideas that in themselves could have been individual games. Too many mechanics, too many themes, too many ideas. Reminded me of a school project where your group just keeps adding layers even though the basic plot is already there. No, Kevin, it isn't a better project just because we add more costumes and a narrator. The music instrumentation itself sounded pretty good and I was vibin with it, but the lyrics were a bit - well - comical at times. ********SPOILER ALERT *Please don't be discouraged from this idea. I love it. I just don't think this was it. Y'all took a risk and this time it didn't work, but that doesn't mean there isn't a gem in here. <3

_childDocuments_.review: Review contains spoilers.This game makes me angry. There are glaring bugs, such as trying to go back to the menu from the prologue screen freezing the game (a terrible first impression) or the controls not updating when you unplug the controller. There is head bobbing, plus the camera swings wildly all the time. This can't be turned off. Combined that with the "drug" visual effects and the blurry text you're supposed to read to learn the protagonist's thoughts, and soon I had a massive headache (I still have it as I write this).The protagonist is implied to be making terrible decisions. If you attempt not to make them, the game will ostensively let you, but the bad decisions will happen off camera anyway. Why pretend, then?Often the gameplay seems to want you to find objects on the scene, but you have to do so within very tight time limits. You have no idea where these objects might be, so soon the game will tell you you failed. I'm not sure this matters either. Whoever's nearest will then turn violent and beat up the protagonist. Ugh. Other pointless minigames include key mashing QTEs and escape sequences with really janky physics.Finally frickin DJ Billy Butcher from The Boys will show up to kidnap you and lock you in a trunk (singing all the while), and that's when things turn full blown psychadelic. If you thought you were as frustrated as  you could be, think again. Whatever the game telegraphs as the objective you're supposed to accomplish is a lie. You will teleport from scene to scene, platforms will disappear from under you, barriers will block your path, basically you're doomed to lose, I think.  The whole game is outrage and frustration porn. I quit at this point in disgust, confusion and with one more migraine than I had when I started.The music is pretty good. I don't know if it's possible to buy the soundtrack separately, but if it is, I would recommend doing so. I'd rather just watch this as a non-interactive youtube music video playlist really. I would probably have a good time.

_childDocuments_.review: I started playing the game at the time of this review, despite getting it a while back. It's an interesting concept. If you love symphonic metal, you're going to love this journey. The "game" itself is more of an interactive movie than a game. It's still within the boundaries of PG-13...esque. I mean, sure there are some mature themes, but nothing ever explicit aside from the occasional strong language. Visually, it feels like watching a twisted children fantasy. The character models although recycled have their own styles and flair to it. But only one costume throughout, hence my comparison.Now, onto gameplay: If you are familiar with QTE games, it is basically that. You have sets where you can explore and "investigate", sometimes with "minigames". The controls...can use some work on. But, I haven't played the game with a controller yet, so I don't know if plugging in a controller plays better than sticking to keyboard and mouse combo.Do I recommend this game? In short, yes. Do it for the music. The musical cast is great. The voice cast...YMMV. Visually? Tolerable. But you didn't come here for the visuals. Gameplay: relatively simple, if you are used to playing various games. Control-wise? Could be better.

_childDocuments_.review: My review, originally published on .These days we rarely get to see innovative and new ideas in video games. It's a huge risk for AAA companies, and it takes a lot of effort from indie developers. But the developers of Of Bird And Cage took on this task, and they delivered a truly new experience. Developed by Capricia Productions and published by All In! Games, Of Bird And Cage is a story driven game designed as a platform for the players to experience a metal album in an engaging and interactive way.The game starts with protagonist, Gitta, as a small child, living through a traumatic event. We go forward in time to see her as a young adult, dealing with the aftermath of this trauma. The story deals with topics such as loss, abuse, drug addiction, and kidnapping. Gitta's choices and actions eventually lead to her being kidnapped by someone from her past, and as she learns about her kidnapper and how their paths had crossed in the past, she falls in love with him. The inspiration from classics such as Beauty and The Beast is apparent in the way this Stockholm syndrome is played out.The story is very grim and dark. The character goes through traumatic experiences, and our choices can lead to even darker paths. Finishing the game takes two hours, but playing the whole game from start to finish was too overwhelming for one sitting. These types of dark and sad themes are common in video games, but Of Bird and Cage takes it to a new level, especially with the symphonic metal soundtrack that compliments the emotionally intense scenes of the game.Our choices and actions from the beginning of the game has heavy implications on how the story will progress and eventually, what ending we will get. There are multiple ways the story can end based on how we make decisions, and after we finish the game, we are kept wondering, 'what if?' This is a great motivation for the us to start over and experience different decisions and endings, and in turn listen to the music album over and over again.Other than the choices that we make during the Of Bird and Cage, the gameplay and our success and failure also influences the story. The gameplay is a combination of quick time events and interacting with the environment, and in each chapter of the game, we have a certain amount of time to act. The time limit is the length of the song playing on each chapter, which gives the game a very natural and smooth flow.Succeeding every task is very hard, especially in the first playthrough. It takes a while to get used to the quick time events and the physics of the environment to do everything we need to do in time. On top of that, the addiction element of Gitta's personality adds a layer of difficulty by introducing hallucinations whenever she hasn't taken drugs in a long time. These hallucinations make interacting with environment even harder, as we need to figure out what we need to do as the entire world is in flames and mystical birds are flying all around us. But failure is not a bad thing. We never get a do over if we fail at a task. Rather, we see the consequences and move forward.The way the gameplay is designed, adds another layer to motivate replaying the game. At the end of each chapter we are kept wondering what would happen if we managed to do what was needed in time. Everything in Of Bird and Cage is designed to keep us coming back to the game, to experience every detail and every way the story could go. This is of course the core idea for representing a music album in the form of a video game. The way we get hooked on the music is if we get to listen to it multiple times, and experience deep and emotional scenes.While the story is a motivational tool based purely on curiosity, the gameplay's way of motivation might feel forced, and even frustrating at times. Gamers love challenge, but some elements of the game's difficulty seem to stem from poor design rather than challenging design. Interacting with the environment and moving object is hard and glitchy at times, and with a miss timed jump to get to our destination faster, we might get stuck in a piece of environment and lose tens of seconds of precious time and watch as the song comes to a close before we get the chance to reach our goal.Physics of the Of Bird and Cage's world is another aspect that comes short. While in a story driven game we don't expect the world to feel completely realistic, there are moments when the way the world works takes away from the emotional depth of the scene we are in. There is a scene when Gitta confronts her alcoholic and abusive father, and we might end up in a fight with him. In this fight, after each punch, the father pushes Gitta back, and the way we are thrown in the air is so weird and cartoonish that it ruins the intensity and the importance of the encounter.These frustrating moments are rare enough to keep us coming back for more, and we eventually can get used to them and look past them to discover every detail of the story, and enjoy the epic music that comes with it.It's not surprising for a game that is advertised as a metal album, to have amazing music. The tracks are symphonic metal songs featuring artists from popular bands such as Epica, Within Temptation, Evanescence, and Guns N' Roses. In many scenes of the game we see the characters singing the lines of the song, which makes the game feel like an immersive and interactive music video. Of Bird and Cage seems like the next step in the evolution of music videos. The media that started decades ago with just the bands playing music in front of a camera, in recent years reached a point where music videos emerged as new form of art, combining the best of both worlds of music and cinema. And now, Of Bird And Cage took a leap forward by bringing in the interactive element of video games.Of Bird and Cage is not a perfect game. There is a lot of unpolished elements in the gameplay and the world design. But the idea is unique and innovative enough to make it a worthwhile experience. We are used to music being a supportive element for video games, to add atmosphere and rhythm to the game, but with Of Bird and Cage the roles have changed. It's designed for us to enjoy the music in a new way. I'd like to imagine a future where this way of presenting music becomes as common as music videos, and maybe at that point we can look back and see Of Bird and Cage as a breakthrough.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most unique games out there today. The album/soundtrack is fabulous, and the story, even though - or probably because - it is so tragic, is addictive.It's absurd - even though I have only 3.2 hours of gameplay so far, I've spent so much time watching walkthrough videos and the game store's pre-recorded stream of act I over and over again, listening to the music and learning how to complete the objectives.So in fact I have spent dozens of hours watching those videos and listening to the music, and obviously the music and the story kept filling my mind throughout the ~12 days since the game release.I do agree the gameplay mechanics (fighting and QTEs) need to be improved, but in my opinion it doesn't affect the overall experience, which is a blast.I would give this game 9.9/10.

_childDocuments_.review: For me, this is the first experience of playing in such an unusual genre. The game is cool!Their pluses:- graphics- musical accompaniment bomb- plot (there is something to think about, for this many thanks to the authors and developers)As such, I didnt see the minuses, but for beginners, especially those with mediocre knowledge of the languages ​​in which the game is now available, it can be difficult. _childDocuments_.review: Just finished a run with the game! The music is top-notch and level design really conveys the atmosphere of each song. I especially liked levels that were more abstract, that shows Gitta's subconscious and past memories. It was a very unique way to experience a music album, and I believe I'll return to it for a replay to try and catch things I've missed in my first run, now that I know the context behind it.
_childDocuments_.name: Of Bird and Cage

_childDocuments_.review: There's no denying that the music is great and in my honest opinion actually makes the game shine for that specifically.I've played through the first two acts and it's been a bit of an emotional roller coaster while trying to guess everything that's gonna happen and think about how everything I do will be affected.That being said, it felt like I didn't have a lot of control as I would've preferred... QTE within a timed environment is interesting, but I guess maybe it works better with the music?I found it pretty difficult to control things properly at times and adjusting wasn't that easy, but that might be just me.I also personally found it a bit more difficult to track what's happening at times through the story because as soon as I learned something, something else happens and changes my perspective but I believe I need to play more to understand it even better.Also, it might be worth to making the seizure warning stand out a bit more early when you load the game.For the music specifically, I do recommend it or if you're a completionist and really want to go through the game multiple times ^_^
_childDocuments_.name: Of Bird and Cage

_childDocuments_.review: After 30-40 minutes of playing this game I thought it would be sufficient enough time to leave a review. The concept of the story is interesting especially with the main character being a drug addict because the hallucinations add another layer of detail. Of Bird and Cage utilizes the old school concept of suspense and suggestion for the danger/scare aspect. This is similar to how old school horror movies or the horror short stories of Edgar Allen Poe, think Pit & The Pendulum, work to draw audiences in. Overall I find this to be a solid concept and look forward to playing more in the future. Considering this is far outside my genre of normal games (JRPGs, Mario, Zelda, etc.) I think a follow up review would be appropriate after additional play time but didn't want to let my initial impression of the game slip through my fingers
_childDocuments_.name: Of Bird and Cage

_childDocuments_.review: So yeah, I've played through this game once as of now, missed about every possible quick time events available, but still had a blast with this game. Incredibly engaging, squeezes the soul and never quite let go. I'll try to do better next time, because there WILL be another time through this game. Yes, I bought the soundtrack as well, but it's not the same experience (still a great OST, I highly recommend getting the whole package).
_childDocuments_.name: Of Bird and Cage

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, This game is so rocking, from the start all the way to the end...The music sucks you in and then the story sucks you in even more. I can't praise Capricia Productions enough for your 6 years of work. This game is for sure a game that will be replayed until all possibilities are found. I have never seen a game like this before. I don't think there will ever be a game like it again....unless they make another one. Seriously if you haven't done so already go buy this game. You will love it.
_childDocuments_.name: Of Bird and Cage

_childDocuments_.review: Good story progression, For you crazy gamers that like to 100% everything there are collectables and puzzles and things to keep you busy :)For sure the music is good in this game and integrates with the story very well.I went through the first run of this game and reached one ending and would love to play it more soon and change choices and see what other mischief and results I can get from doing things differently.I caught myself staring at the monitor to see what happens in silence, I caught myself headbanging to the music while listening to the lyrics to understand who is who and what's going on!Overall I would recommend this game and I have enjoyed my first run and I'm sure I will enjoy the following ones as well to see what other endings I can get :D
