_childDocuments_.review: A good introduction to factory builder genre, although personally I prefer Factorio/Dyson Sphere Program.Starting from the good and interesting, Satisfactory does have a fairly unique approach to exploration and rewards it.There's plenty of rewards that can only be acquired through exploring and they're very useful.The creative aspect is better than in many, many games. Very few competitors in the genre or even beyond it offer as many possibilities when it comes to building in general. Overall quality and polish are outstanding.Design is intuitive and most things make logical sense.Now on to the problems: Building and scaling up production in satisfactory can get very, very tedious. Whereas in many similar games you're able to construct multiple buildings at a time and connect them with conveyors with relative ease, in Satisfactory all you get is very restrictive blueprint system that doesn't fully unlock until basically the finale and even then offers significantly less than ones in similar games.Vehicles are fairly ineffective and there's little reason not to just build long conveyor tracks, especially given how in many areas you have to build elevated highways for the vehicles anyway, Having to record their paths manually adds another layer of tedium. Trains/drones are somewhat better but still very restrictive and not a major advantage over conveyors.While exploration is one of the positives, the combat is not. It feels more like a distraction all things considered. Would've preferred more puzzle style challenges rather than very repetitive enemies.

_childDocuments_.review: The game has a lot of potential and originally I enjoyed it, but after so many hours it got very grindy and boring.  Additionally, having to constantly manage parts and machines to make said parts drove me nuts.The graphics, sound, and music are all very beautiful.  The planets are large to explore and there is pretty scenery.  With the exception of some toxic gases and a few creatures (a couple of which are VERY aggressive towards you) there is nothing else to encounter but minerals and other things to mine or otherwise exploit for your factory.  Further into the game you will be exploring into the nether regions of the planet looking for harder to find minerals, water, oil, etc. Doing this on foot is a tiresome chore, and using the first of available vehicles is only slightly better.  Needless to say, I never even got to the point of making a train.The game mechanics are a little strange to get used to at first, and more in-depth tutorials could have helped a lot in this regard.  It takes some doing, but once you understand how it all works, you'll get to the point where you start assembling a factory to actually make and research items, only to build more advanced machinery to make and research even more items, etc.  If you have OCD like me, this will drive you up a wall in no time.  I found myself constantly counting and estimating how many pieces of part X it takes to make part Y, and after while it drove me absolutely nuts.The problem is, the further you go along, you are constantly moving things, reorganizing your factory layout, running out of power, etc and eventually it all becomes a logistical nightmare. At first, it's kind of exciting to advance to better machinery, but after awhile you are basically just doing that over and over.What especially bothers me here is that later machines should be able to build EVERYTHING that earlier versions of those same machines could in addition to newer items.  For example, if a first level machine can build a Doohicky, then the second level should be able to make that and also a Gizmo by routing the same raw materials into it. The third variant of it should able to make the Doohicky, Gizmo, and Thingamabob all in one fell swoop.  This would improve line efficiency a lot and save time, power, and resources.  As it is now, you have to make machines for all 3 items, route parts via conveyors into each, and then still manually collect the items and do something else with them.Additionally, there is really nothing to do when you finally have automated lines all working for you and building things.  You literally have to sit and wait in real time for it all to get done, which is boring as sh!t.  A minigame, letting your player sleep or wait, or even letting it progress when you shut the game off and come back to it later would have solved a lot of this.  It's not fun, it's a horrid grind.I played the game for many hours earlier this year, then got bored with it and waited until several updates happened.  Today I tried it again, and it just doesn't appeal to me.  I can't recommend it unless you have a lot of patience or the above points won't irritate you.  Guess I will never get to see that train.12/25/2022 UPDATE - Spent the past 2-3 weeks trying again.  Slightly better game play but core issues still exist.  Still never made the f*cking train either.  I'm done.

_childDocuments_.review: Satisfactory is a decent game for an early release. It is more polished than I expected. The game play is fairly straight forward. There are few surprises. The game logic goes something like this: Land on uninhabited planet; collect resources; build things; collect more resources; build more things; so on and so forth. What sets this game apart from other survival-build'em-ups is its focus on automation and factory building. In essence, the player builds buildings to connect to other buildings which turn resources into usable parts which are used to build new buildings and to build more complex parts. There is a nifty in-game upgrade and achievement system which represents the main plot of the game. By collecting and creating the required parts and pieces, the player unlocks new building schematics, equipment, and access to a wider range of resource types. All of these game elements are well designed and feel like they belong in the game. Constructing buildings is fairly easy and is surprisingly less glitchy then most early release games. Combat with hostile creatures on the planet is a bit clunky and can be frustrating to effectively target the critters for a shock-prod induced death. One small thing stuck out to me early in the game. The voice of the FICSIT helper program, which is more or less your only tutorial and guide through the game, explained, as I was descending to the surface of a foreign planet, that I should be wary of "hostile extra-terrestrial life-forms." This statement struck me as somewhat perplexing. I was the extra-terrestrial on this planet. I was the armed interloper who had just taken up a company issued shock weapon. I mulled this over in my head while exiting the drop pod. It was then I had a troubling realization: was this a design error in the AI helper program or had this AI accurately reflected the ways in which humans generally experience their surrounds - as theirs to conquer and freely abuse? Perhaps the FICSIT company AI determined we humans believe that everything in the world, or in this case the galaxy, belongs to us. Had this AI realized the arduous and ethically ambiguous task of surviving to ultimately exploit and ravage an untainted planet would place considerable psychological strain upon me and that I would be more effective if I believed my actions were justified. After all, this was an extra-terrestrial, terrestrial planet - at least to me. I pondered this small question for only a few moments, for within seconds of finding a large iron deposit I was attacked by said hostile creatures and died immediately. I suppose the answer will be left to my replacement.Update: This game needs in-line overflow valves and mechanisms for tubes and conveyor belts to automatically siphon excess materials away from backed up lines!

_childDocuments_.review: Picture this: You're dropped on an alien planet with nothing but your wits, a multi-tool, and a mission to build the biggest, baddest factory the universe has ever seen. Welcome to Satisfactory, a game that takes the phrase "go big or go home" to a whole new level. If you’ve ever dreamt of being a mad scientist crossed with an over-caffeinated LEGO enthusiast, this game is your jam.From the moment you hit the ground in Satisfactory, the game hits you with a sense of scale that’s both awe-inspiring and slightly terrifying. Your goal? To build a factory so efficient, so sprawling, that it makes Amazon look like a mom-and-pop shop. And let me tell you, once you start, it's like potato chips—you can’t stop at just one conveyor belt.Speaking of conveyor belts, they are the lifeblood of your factory empire. Imagine miles and miles of conveyor belts, snaking through lush alien landscapes, transporting everything from iron ore to space elevator components. If Willy Wonka and Henry Ford had a love child, it would look a lot like Satisfactory's factory designs. The game's mantra might as well be: "Why walk somewhere when you can build a conveyor belt?"But it’s not all about the belts. Oh no, dear reader. You also get to play with tractors, trucks, and even trains. Ever wanted to drive a semi-truck through a forest of giant alien mushrooms? Well, now you can. And nothing says "productivity" like hopping into a train you've painstakingly designed to transport goods across your meticulously planned outposts. It’s the kind of chaos that makes you wonder if your degree should actually be in logistics.One of the most delightful aspects of Satisfactory is its co-op mode. Because if there’s anything better than one person obsessing over conveyor belts, it’s a group of friends doing it together. The camaraderie of working together to build a factory, yelling at each other about misaligned conveyor belts, and collectively groaning when someone accidentally deletes the main power line is a unique form of bonding. It's like the IKEA effect, but with a lot more swearing and much less furniture.The graphics are stunning, and the alien world is a pleasure to explore (when you're not obsessively managing your production lines). The flora and fauna are beautifully rendered, and occasionally dangerous, reminding you that this planet isn’t just a sandbox for your factory dreams. It's also home to some rather grumpy locals. Keep an eye out for those angry spitters and charging hogs—because nothing says "productivity loss" like being ambushed while you're trying to optimise your copper smelting.Satisfactory isn't just a game; it's a lifestyle. It's a perfect blend of exploration, creativity, and management that will keep you up at night, planning your next expansion. Whether you’re a seasoned engineer or someone who just likes to see things go brrr, Satisfactory will have you hooked. So gear up, get building, and remember: In Satisfactory, there’s no such thing as too many conveyor belts.

_childDocuments_.review: i love this game.  once i have advanced combat, enemies are no issue.  i am always trying to learn better ways to build and organize my stuff.  i haven't mastered the art of the 100 (insert building type here) like some others, but i have no problem completing the space needle projects and all research items. still working on completing all the ticket items and have yet to master clean nuclear power. looking forward to new things still yet to come from this game as well as the hinted story line.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: Well this game is as the name implies. You will be satisfied as u build your factory. How can u be satisfied from building a factory? Than just try it, You would not even know where did the time flew off while playing. If you start playing there will be 2 outcome either, you are having sleepless nights playing or dreaming about conveyor belts good luck.p.s. Let me know which one you are on the comments
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: good game if you play alone.  not at all fun to play with friends.  can only have 1 hub so other players stuck in one base  or having to travel to said base to build item that can only be built at hub (mainly a start up problem) .another problem is resource nodes can be harvested by  another player. stilling resources  of other player become the norm  and that becomes a huge fight . other  than that i loved the game solo all the way :)mod game then multiplayer is fun you need the fixit.app follow instruction an install ( hub)
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy shooting zombies, driving fast cars, leveling up your character, and a deep rich story... this is not the game for you.If you enjoy tedious logistics, math, exploration, and resource gathering... this IS the game for you!Tedious makes it sound un-enjoyable, but the tedium is part of the fun. Constantly adjusting conveyor lines to improve productivity. Calculating efficiency rates to manage faster factory lines. Implementing transportation routes including trains and aerial drones. TONS of unlockable research and new buildings. At 285 hours, my crew and I have finally completed the final phase of the space elevator. Can't wait for update 6!!!Excellent chill game with great multiplayer. Dedicated servers made the online experience so much better!
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: Satisfactory is a Brain hacking game that turns chore like tasks into a fun hobby from designing factorys to the nity griddy math hoops for the OCD. Effincincy is the name of the game. A tip for new players is that the moment you unlock foundations rebuild all the machines youve already built on a foundation and if you do you will have a much better time progressing through Phase 2 and 3 when you get to them.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: Single player review.This game is an absolute blessing to play.It's lightweight and smooth. I have never dipped below 130fps in 15 hours of gameplay. (1080ti)The quality of the game is overwhelming, my hat goes off to the developers.The first 30 mins of the game is a bit hard to get into. I feel like there's improvement to be made there.Personally I think holding the hand of the player for that duration would be helpful. It would help not feeling like you've never done this before.I can't wait to see what this game will become. If the devs keeps working hard and keeps this high quality standard, it will definitely be one of the best factory games out there, once it comes out of early access.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: The game is quite immersive and satisfying as the title suggest, even if personally I've encountered multiple crashes when tried to start the game (black screen after splash screen and blue screen of death (BSOD)).Nevertheless, it is worth the while and I'm praying for the dev team@satisfactory to fix these issues.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: I have currently surrendered my life to this game. I eat and think about how to optimize output. I try to sleep, and think about optimizing output. I play, and fail to optimize output.You can feed pet doggos berries and they will fetch you powerslugs 10/10 goodboys.You can slingshot yourself into air with the hypertoobs 10/10You can make trampolines so that you bounce 100 ft in the air while dropping explosives onto the local wildlife from above 10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: found a work around in windows firewall to make multiplayer work would be nice if the game FAQ talked about this issue with windows. can recommend Just be aware that you will need to allow "facortygame" to have both in and out bound connections on both private and public networks for multiplayer to work
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: I have played this game for 3 hours. Playing Satisfactory reminds me of when I played Minecraft for the first time. It was a magical experience that brings back memories of simpler days. The gentle music in the grassy world is really nice. Learning how things work together is rewarding and growing my base is so much fun. Truly a unique experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: Got this game on a whim after a friend suggested it to me, and I gotta say I think it was one of the best impulse purchases I've made. Very good pacing, shed loads of content, well thought out GUI, and a lot of attention do detail in the graphics. It's very impressive how much can be happening on screen at one time, and yet how fluid the game still runs. Honestly my only gripe with this game is that bugs are not uncommon, particularly in regards to movement, however this can be overlooked easily as the game is still in beta. 100% worth every penny of the cost
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: Satisfactory is incredibly addictive. I have spent countless hours designing and perfecting my factory. From making iron plates and screws to eventually plutonium fuel rods and supercomputers, Satisfactory keeps its grip on you the entire time you're playing and even when you're not playing. The ever expanding tree of items you need to automate to progress through the game, each more complex than the last constantly keeps your brain moving and planning for whats coming next. Easily one of, if not the best factory building game of all time. 10/10 would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: Satisfactory combines the joy of old school video games with the beauty and complexity of modern video games.  Nintendo games were all about doing the same thing over and over to develop a perfect way of playing through them.  Satisfactory captures that same feel while allowing the freedom to do whatever I want at whatever pace I want.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: I love Factorio and this game gives mi similar feeling to build more and optimize. Plus the environment is beautiful! I love to explore the world and new biomes always surprise me. I also like more peacefulness - the creatures only attack you when you expand, they don't attack already created factories etc. Which gives me peace to focus on building/optimizing while keeping the combat element.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: This may be the greatest game of all time. The satisfying  of things being constructed, the lovingly hand crafted world, the hard but not  hard logistics. (optimising those logistics is another story). The co-op shenanigans that organically develop as you try and line up two different production bases and say screw it and shoot your friend in the face with a rebar gun. If you like the thought of Factorio or Dyson Sphere but the perspective throws you off, or you want to design things that are aesthetically pleasing with no practical purpose, or you want to pretend that you are playing a horror game (try exploring a cave with the audio up and the lights off), then you are gonna like this game.And thats not even getting into the mods, which easily double the fun you can have. You know the scene in Marvel Civil War, where Ant-Man gets all big and moves slowly? You can do that. (use the infinite scale mod, create a vehicle that is super small or super big... get in and out). Think the base game is too easy and for children, install the Satisfactory Plus mod, add a few things like Refined Power and Fiscit Farming and say goodbye to your family for the next decade.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: Satisfactory is a game that is excellent, and it's hard to describe exactly why. The engine of the game runs smooth, a tremendous amount of care has been given to the design, and the environments are quite beautiful.But the main gameplay loop, on paper, shouldn't be fun--and yet it is. Extremely fun. Addictively so.tl;dr:Get this game, the devs clearly adore it, and it's easily the smoothest and best designed building system I've ever seen.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: We making it out of Massage-2(AB)b with this one. Coffee Stain really knocked it out of the park with Satifactory, truly a satisfying game to play. The whole map is hand made and not procedurally generated, the level of detail in the factory mechanics is perfect, and the whole game looks beautiful. The game is a mix of building, resource management, and exploration with a little combat and portal-like humor. The amount of playtime you get for the price is remarkable, if you are on the fence just get it.10/10 would turn nature into a amazon warehouse again
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: Fatally flawed.They never did get the fluids working just right, I still have to go back and destroy various bits of the fluid system to get components working.  Not ideal.If i have to get back into the half functional hyper tube again to go 2000m away to fix my broken fluid system while I tab out and do something else because it takes too long...I was going to lose it, enough.The game wants so hard to be a 3d factorio, but I feel like they emphasized the 3d over the factorio, they should have approached this with a different set of priorities.  The basic mechanics of creating a factory feel disjointed, bland and utlimately boring.  I suppose it looks pretty good, but otherwise clunky and not much fun.Also, force people to play a female to satisfy your thinly veiled politics?  No thanks.  Adios.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: I will re-review my previous negative score for the 1.0 release:Tedious.Extremely tedious. This is by far one of the worst factory/construction games I have played, and I have played quite a few. The pacing is atrocious. - Unlocks are tedious, bring little value and everything takes eons with it's worst in class interface. I feel like you are supposed to explore while things in your factory "bake" and this is a terrible mechanic because the exploration is fairly joyless jump puzzle and barely acceptable combat. Not to mention that often there isn't really enough downtime to warrant any large excursion.- Unlocks from the things you find exploring seem to range from limp to boring, especially in the early game they have nearly 0 impact.- The factory building is an afterthought. You'd be better off and get things done faster just slapping a mess on the ground. Eventually you'll want to clean that up I guess just for eyesore reasons, and you will be introduced to one of the most tedious construction interfaces imaginable. Footprints are huge on constructors. Even 2 of the tallest walls won't give you enough clearance. Perspective is awful for what you are trying to do and there is no real tools to make it better. Every game I have experience from Ark to Valheim seems to do a better job of snapping than this game.Honestly this game feels like it is 90% marketing and kids watching Youtube videos for the spectacle of what you could build, but the QoL enhancements necessary to not make this essentially a job or a mental illness are non-existent.Enjoy the "We don't need GLADOS we've got one at home" Ada and here mild dystopian humor. There is no real story.I am honestly angry writing this review at the lack of effort that went into these games and the lack of polish that happened in EA. It really feels like they programmed a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ building in 3d and then EA was just level designers ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ around (since there is no world gen, likely because of the choice to make it 3d).It's a great game to fall asleep to while playing though, especially why considering whether you want to manually pick up your entire base just to slightly improve some throughput that you would probably just get leaving the game running for an hour. All while managing your inventory because it can't be bothered to QoL literally anything.Factorio had pacing, QoL and careful design. Same with Planet Builder. Dyson Sphere Program is far more impressive visually.This has first person, verticality that adds nothing and budget GLADOS.Also I have to reset my graphics every time I play or face a screen of static in the 1.0 release.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: This is the second copy of this game I've purchased. I have over 600 hours on epic and love it. Coffee stain listens to their payer base and the updates are always full of fun new things to explore. I've restarted my play-through multiple times and the game feels different on every go. Play at your own pace, and make your experience as complex or as simple as you want. The freedom to play however you like is why this game will never get old for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: 235.4 hours played and many to come this game is amazing in any regard I can think of .Coffee Stain Studios did an amazing job at idealizing and creating the game, took their time listening to the community and all of the critics to make the game better and better  brilliant design and amazing optimization even with everything happening on the screen it still runs beautifully. Haven't played many other factory games but this one struck me and made me wanna play and made me stick to it.Everything is perfect in this game accept maybe the story which is a bit lackluster and vague but considering the type of game it's the least of your worries.If you are in to this type of game you 100% percent will enjoy every moment of it and sick countless hours into it. BEWARE OF SPIDERS OR CATS that's all
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game. I had been itching to play it for years, waiting for the full release, and it really met all my expectations and more. The game is HUGE, big maps, lots of items, lots of machines, on top of a really nice complexity given by the alternate recipes that let you make the same object using diferent components. My only grip, although small, is that its strongest point, the scale of things, is also its weakness. Going from one side of the map to the other is long and even with better transportation methods, it still gets tiresome. On that aspect, I think it probably gets a lot better playing in multiplayer, although still an excellent game in singleplayer.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: A factory/resource automation game with nice graphics~I love this game~Being efficient with your builds will definitely help you out in this game in the long run. But even my inefficient builds still manage to get things done. Just takes longer.My only criticisms would be about the customizer, where you can dye/paint things. When upgrading/replacing things, it always goes back to the default color swatch. (or possibly what swatch is set as the default for that type of thing) I'd love for it to keep the color swatch of what is being replaced instead. The other thing is that there seems to be a limited number of swatches and I haven't found any options for adding more custom swatches. I could also be overlooking these options, however.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: My first review of this game after 740 hours of play from Update 3-4 to update 8.Update 8 has a lot of bugs and sadly the snapping is it harder to get right, so it requires more fitness to get a design right in the correct grid. But that only a minor issue from update 8.I am totally amazed that this game is so beautiful and still running at 60 ftp on my 1050, then all other games out there, are much poor in graphics and runs in 12 ftp. Like KSP or City Skylines 2.This game is simply one of the best experiences for me.I am a bit scared to see if the final game will be like ARK, you played it all in Early Access and after release there is not much more in the final release. I dont care for the story mode, but i like to see a better tech tree and more stages or making it harder with more material requirements, Since you can unlock must of tiers in a day.I can only recommend this game, you will spend TOO MANY hours drinking coffee and just look at your automations run flawless. Thank you Coffee Stain Studio! What a masterpiece!
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game of math, planning and precision - all neatly bundled in one package. While it does offer and action, adventure and exploration, it is the factory building that will take up the most of your time. Will you build sprawling industrial complexes? Minimalistic, perfectly placed manufacuring clusters? Chaotic tangles of factories and conveyor belts? Hypertube rollercoasters? Water pipe art? You can do all that and more - the only limit is your imagination. And if you find that the base content is not enough to quench you construction frenzy, then there's plenty of user-created mods to keep you working 24/7.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: The map, weather, resources, mobs, etc. do not change. There is also currently no story, lore, and only trivial survival elements. Since everything is static the game is basically about using math to create a flowchart (or use one already available online) to create items that allow you to check off the boxes... and if it's your thing you can make it all look pretty. If this is your idea of fun this game does an amazing job of visualizing it.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: love it aside from the fona doesnt grow back if you let it and mobs spawns spawning weirdly aka like how ever the radius is determined when a mob wont respawn as you are now classified as "occupying" that space and thus it wont respawn there anymore and a few game breaking bugs like not being able to pick up a dead animals drop every now and then but its early access so its to be expected at this point :P
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: Too many problems compared to other factory games, if you want a new factory game but do not like factorio for some reason get Dyson Sphere program and not this game. tedium is the name of the game here. it never stops. moving forward with the game is extremely easy there is nothing complicated that rattles your brain. What keeps me stuck sometimes is realizing have to again cross way too much of a distance to get anywhere. They realize this and give you so many new movement options on each upgrade, but its not enough.placing each object gets ridiculously tedious placing each object is also extremely annoying with the first person prospective also a basic thing that kinda made me just ?? was when you get to build a space elevator right away but you dont get anything that improves item transportation until you build a space elevator which is just a big ?? why can I not build a train but I can build a space elevator just make it make sense.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fun.Really.Really not sure, this game has consumed my soul. I can not recall the last time that I have seen the sun since I started playing this game. I must optimize every factory to the maximum. Whether the factory is a few square meters large or takes up the entire biome. I NEED to completely maximize every bit of output. I do not care about how much I have to build. I do not care about how much space I need. I will finish that factory. Whether it takes me 5 minutes or 5 months. The factory has to be finished. I shall not leave any factories unoptimized. There is just no way for anyone to leave a factory with a little bit of overflow on materials. And don't get me started on manifolding vs load-balancing, because I will load balance all my conveyors, even if I need to place over 100 splitters and mergers. I will do whatever it takes, just for this damned factory to be optimized to the maximum. The lore behind this game? I do not know. There's a weird woman who told me that I'm ugly, stupid and I should defenestrate myself. Also some other woman, which keeps telling me to consume. I think they have consumed my soul, for I have been building temples which rhyme into effigies which flow into the current of blood.The game's fun. Buy it. Love it and then make it your life.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this game a lot.  I have not played it long enough to give a fair review.  I am hoping to share with the devs to possibly make it an option to choose to have timed crafting.  I feel while I am crafting resources I am looking at whatever is playing on my off monitor while holding down the mouse button to finish the large amounts of resources I have to break down. and it'd be nice to have the option not to just hold down the mouse button while not paying any attention to whats going on anyway.  The game is fantastic and I am enjoying playing it.  A game one in of itself, it's a very fun and exciting experience overall.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: I've been watching this game for ages, waiting for the Steam release...It starting as an Epic exclusive was frustrating, and I'm not gonna lie I downloaded it illegitimately prior to the Steam release and fell in love. I watched the release livestream and bought it the moment it was available.It's a wonderful game, full of exploration and problem solving. The game looks gorgeous, and has tons of little bits of character that really make some of the elements feel alive.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty early to review a game. That having been said, this has been fun to this point. A good story line, decent layout and planning that while could be improved has been good overall. I will post more to this but for now given the price I paid I think it has been fair. I seems to have a lot of content so far.So, now at 225 hours or so, I've done a few restarts along the way due to updates and continue to enjoy the game play. I have tested a few mods to see what can be done and this is one of a few games I can actually still recommend. The updates have been frequent and seem well tested although there are always a few issues once they are released. Issues are identified and resolved in a timely manner which to me is important. One thing I am going to try to add to my reviews although I only do a few here and there is my "cost per hour" calculation. So far, the cost per hour for this game is about 0.088495 cents. This will change as time passes but it helps me keep track of the more valuable games in a more tangible fashion. As a comparison, I have played Insurgency for 1,979 hours. This works out to around 0.015159 cents per hour and actually less since I paid lower for the game than originally advertised.As another comparison, the game ECO I purchased was and is a disappointment. So far that game works out to about $5.555555 per hour of play. Sadly this was a poor investment on my part. Buy Satisfactory if you are on the fence as its been well worth it and I expect it will only get better. If it goes on sale thats even better yet.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

I've put over 100hrs into the game so far and feel like I'm just scratching the surface (in a good way).The possibilities are endless in this game and you'll always log off thinking about your next big build project in game!
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: Even though this game is still in early access this is one of the best games I have ever played, there are still some bugs but that is to be expected for a early access game, if it was released today at a full 60 dollar price tag I would still say its worth the price but its only 30 dollars and is constantly getting updates to fix bugs and add content, the only reason you should not buy it is that you can not become completely addicted to a game because that will happen with this game, if i could chose 1 new game that i would consider perfect it would be this one,
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: I make a thing to optimise another thing to be able to build another thing which I build while waiting for another thing, and then I unlock a new thing and all the things can now be renovated, but only after I finish making this thing so that i can have a full network of things and-why was I doing this again?
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: I really love the calm pacing of this game and the ability to make as messy, see Let's Game It Out on youtube, or as clean a build(s) as you want. The versatility behind such open ended mechanics is great. Even at an early access stage this game has run very well for me with only minor glitches, such as game crashes, and I look forward to future updates. To the Dev's I offer the idea of perhaps more eco-friendly methods of power generation such as solar, wind, or even a way of harvesting hydrogen to be burned as fuel. I can't wait to see where this goes in the future and look forward to version 1.0
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: Love this game. Beautiful and fun. The developers constantly add things and improve it in ways that make it clear they have actually played and understand their own game / playerbase. The convenience features and fluidity that come with each version are just insane compared to what I'm used too from other games. Also they have an alien species called "Lizard Doggo".  I'll somehow find a way to make my review even more enthusiastic when they implement some form of alien kitten.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: I have only played this game for 20 odd hours, but I can already tell I can and will easily sink hundreds of hours into it. My recommendation, Do you have ADHD of any type? You will love this game.Similarly, are you slightly autistic with a need for everything to be one way and for that way to be the most efficient? You will  love this game.If you're unsure about buying this I recommend checking out this video by camwing.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: The game is pretty amazing despite it being on early access. There's so much to do and so much to explore. I personally find the things you send up to space (like the HUB or the space elevator) so fun to watch. My S/O makes those tube transportation thingies for me to explore the different areas and thats fun although half the time I'd get motion sickness from it. Worth it!
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely wonderful mix between Factorio and Subnautica, with incredible fun to be had between friends as well as solo. Factorio does a wonderful job of doling out tools when you need them (giving you drones when it becomes too tedious to build by hand, etc.) and Satisfactory could do a better job of smoothing out the higher tiers. Factorio has you dealing with units of items in terms of belts, but this game has much more various needs, so it would benefit from a way to read how many items per second are being produced on a belt at a single time. Another great change to keep the player thinking at the higher level would be to add drones or something similar (understandably way more difficult in 3d space). Overall I really enjoyed my time with it but I think it overstays its welcome in the later phases, probably as a result of the staggered release early access, rather than people playtesting the entire game as a single experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: Witness the deep and sing for us.We composed a resonant-song to curve the effigy, tapping into the inner currents.We sacrificed our blood and our temples and let the metal in from the void to eat our flesh.Consume our blood. Worship at our altars. Curve the melody.Be appropriate.Harvest.Consume.Witness.Play. Play. Play.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: This was longer than I expected it to end up, but in short its a great game with tons of hours of gameplay and tons of potential.Well I've had this game for a week and it has taken over my life. I would not recommend if you are prone to being addicted to addictive things like meth, heroin or anime titties. The game is very in depth and has a lot of content for being an early access game. The game does a great job of teaching you how it works without overwhelming you and slowly builds and gets very complex. I haven't even reached all the content that the game has to offer yet after almost 70 hours, which was very surprising. One of the reasons I waited so long to get this game was because I was afraid there wouldn't be enough content to make it worth the cost, like other early access games. Mainly raft is the first one that comes to mind, which is very fun, but doesn't have enough content currently to make it worth the cost in my opinion (less than 20 hours). I was glad to find out just how much there is to do in this game. The only negatives I can think of are fairly small and don't affect core gameplay, except vehicle, which could be better. But playing with friends in my experience has been laggy, where only who is the host can actually see other people all the time and everyone who joins the host sees people running straight for awhile and can only see people every once in awhile, I'm sure it will be fixed later, but if you are playing with friends, in my experience vehicles are laggy/buggy as well. I heard they are going to add dedicated servers which would fix this (I think). The game currently also has mod support which is great for keeping the game fresh. My only other slight complaints are the lack of decoration options, angled walls and some sort of lighting (unless i haven't found that yet) since it can get dark inside at night, which most likely will all be added at a further date. The movement in this game is very fun and it has a lot of potential with custom maps (if they add some way to easily make and share maps, like some creative mode) which excites me since it reminds of a lot of custom maps from halo 3.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this approximately 6 months before it fully launched (left Early Access), and the first time I tried playing it, I didn't get very far, just past the starting objectives, referred to as Onboarding. _childDocuments_.review: Incredibly fun game, so glad I got this as part of a Humble Bundle. What's really cool is that half of the problems the game presents you with are not the typical "fill out this grid as efficiently as possible" problems these types of games throw at you. Although that's definitely a factor too! After the earliest tech trees your biggest challenge becomes navigating the terrain. At the first spawn point, resources spawn really far away from your home base and the sheer distance leaves you scratching your head, scouting the terrain, clearing brush, laying conveyors and so on. This process is as interesting as making sure your factory is running smoothly. My favorite moment so far is wandering off into the jungle chasing the oil icon on my compass, assuming that the oil must be at the top of this mountain I'm climbing, eventually getting totally lost and depleting all my resources making various bridges and towers, only to reach the peak and see my oil on a beach hundreds of feet below me. The sense of scale and the hilarity of the moment both made me fall in love with this game even more.

_childDocuments_.review: A friend once said 'Coffee Stain, they are a good studio and they know what they are doing', This was in reference to Valhiem - A game which I thought was a bit naff. So, if your up for landing on a distant planet and you only have yourself to rely on.  This game can apparently handle multiplayer but why bother share this world when you can have it all to yourself.  I picked this up as I was looking for a replacement for Astroneer & it doesn't disappoint. 146 hours played at time of writing and I have yet to look at another game, coming from a hardcore gamer with 100's of games to call on that's not bad.

_childDocuments_.review: I started SATISFACTORY not having seen any videos of other people's builds. My first attempt was a disaster. I built my hub too close to a cliff wall, my buildings were at all sorts of weird angles. I wanted to start fresh. My second attempt was better, but still too close to a cliff wall (despite my planning) and I wasted resources on unlocks I didn't need/want until later. So I decided to scrap my build again. Third build, I am finally getting the hang of things. My factory is still a mess, but I'm using foundations and vertical space better. I'm sure I'll come to a point where I want to scrap this base and start over based on the newer things I learn with this attempt. Or maybe I'll try to salvage it and keep making it better. Regardless, I'm loving the game and I know I'll be playing it for some time to come.Thank you, Coffee Stain Studios, for out-of-the-box ULTRAWIDE support. The game looks fantastic.

_childDocuments_.review: So the reason I am not recommending this is only due to performance and lack of options to improve it. It's really disappointing to me because the game is a ton of fun, but I've tried 2 new games now, and by the time I get to mid-game, even on all low settings, I am getting massive frame stutter every few seconds. I tried a few different things to improve performance, but nothing worked.There are also no options to help. You can't display your FPS in game, nor show network traffic or dropped frames. You can take the game offline, but it then creates a new copy of you with no inventory, and you have to be offline (which is just not great).Once they work out the performance issues (hopefully before the end of early access) I think I will give this another try.EDIT: I can't say I haven't gotten my enjoyment out of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty obviously inspired by other popular games like Factorio and Subnautica.However, it tries to do too much and ends up as a shallow experience when compared to either of these games.Let's compare this game to the titans of the genres, shall we?Compared to Factorio,  the factories you build end up feeling, ironically, much more two-dimensional. The recipes are simple and straightforward and don't require much thought. Maybe this is a good thing, because making complicated factories is actually frustrating thanks to the building controls. Building a factory in first-person view isn't easy, and the interface doesn't do much to help. I can't count how many times had to re-connect thole bulky belt splitters and mergers because they didn't connect *just* right.And then there's the question of why even bother? Whereas Factorio provides you with several incentives to grow and expand, such as the threat of depleting resources and ever-encroaching native life, Satisfactory just says "unlock more stuff." There are no threats of any kind to worry about and for resources, you simply plop down a mine on top of a node that never runs dry.So you sit around and wait for your factory to pump out enough products to unlock the next upgrade. Build a few more constructors, hook up a few new nodes, rinse and repeat. So while you sit around and wait for the next upgrade, what do you do?Explore the world! This falls flat, too, unfortunately. The worlds are somewhat interesting, not poorly designed, but not spectacular either. The problem is that there is little reward for exploration. As an early access game, I can understand if the exploration aspect of the game isn't complete now, but as of right now, there is little reason to explore.The Subnautica vibes are strong - you're on a strange planet owned by a hyper-capitalist super-corporation and you are a pawn sent there to collect resources and build stuff. There are alien creatures to fight and collect resources from - but it's all biomass in the end. You can collect power slugs that can be used to upgrade your factory buildings, which is currently the only real reward for explorations. There a few "alternate" recipes you can unlock along the way that will improve your factory, but it seems pointless - remember, there are no threats to your factory, no depleting resources. The hostile creatures don't even respawn. You can rework your factory to accommodate the new recipe...or just go grab another node.So in the end the game lets you build (not without unnecessary pain) a factory that works. It works little too well, and demands little thought or planning - just build more instead - and there will never be a snag in the line that you need to react to. Then you sit around and let it pump out components for the next upgrade, maybe wander around a little bit and pick up a couple slugs. Then do it all over again.For a game so highly praised and recommended, I was quite disappointed. I absolutely love both games that I have used for the comparison, and they are both natural comparisons for this game. Satisfactory doesn't currently offer me any reason to play this game over the others.

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot recommend Satisfactory 1.0 as someone who's put thousands of hours into alternative automation games. I have found playing the game to be boring, the build mechanics tedious, and the "story" to be wholly unimpressive, if not actively hostile to my experience. It is truly sad that this is the state of things after the game spent several years in early access.A major mar on my opinion of 1.0 is that the developers use the narrator as a self-insert to voice petty, unprofessional remarks about past player questions and concerns about the game. This is not okay. It's not funny. I'm not here to feel berated while trying to play your game. The comments make trying to experience the game's "story" wholly unenjoyable.The build mechanics are just plain tedious, and the absurdly huge size of the buildings doesn't help matters. While 1.0 introduced some quality-of-life features, they in no way solve the fundamental issue that the process of building simply is not fun. This is primarily driven by the sheer slowness of recipes in most buildings more advanced than a constructor while ALSO requiring absurd volumes of inputs to push out tiny amounts of outputs. The required scale to get any reasonable amount of even early-game products is simply insane, especially when you have to place every single building, splitter, and merger individually down a line. There is a mechanic for placing multiple foundations, yet the devs in their INFINTE wisdom decided against developing that mechanic for factory buildings. They're out of their minds. MODS have added this functionality and made the game less tedious, but with 1.0 including a game engine update, ALL mods are broken and need to be updated to work with 1.0.The blueprint system also has its issues. Blueprints are PER SAVE, not global, so you have to manually go into your appdata folder to copy your blueprints between playthroughs. There's no method of exporting or importing blueprints in-game, either. It's all manually done out-of-game. The whole process is pure tedium.I could keep going, but I'm frankly too tired to keep writing. I think you get the idea by now. There are far better and cheaper automation games out there than this.

_childDocuments_.review: It looks nice, it's well executed in many ways (and cheesy in a few others, but it's a beta), but at the very core, it's an idle game. There are, like in any idle game, a few superficial choices you can do to be more efficient, and it keeps you busy so you don't get bored in between the craftly intervalled drops of dopamine the game design is centered on delivering. Reward/unlock are spaced so that you can nearly access the next upgrade, just play 5 more minutes etc. But can you lose? No you can't. Can you embrace a variety of approaches? Absolutely not. Just build, farm, build, farm, connect, connect, connect. It's not a game as much as it is a toy.It's a reasonably cool toy though. You can chill building what is indeed a satisfying factory. Not a clever one, not a challenging one, but yours truly, and there's joy in that.Still, the game take an awful lot of time to make you on the whole dumber. If you have any self estem, or don't fancy to be a dopamine junky, skip.

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't played since covid, back when this game was called fps Factorio by fans of the genre. So many things have changed and improved! It's definitely a great game, you should buy it. But if I have a small nitpick or two, is that a lot of things got "cartoonified" in 1.0, so to say. Merser Sphere's and Sloops look way less ominious. And ADA has too much tongue and cheek in my opinion. As well as the dimensional depo. Insanely useful addition to the game, so I don't have to run to my storage for items every time... actually, I don't even have to build a storage location because of the depo... Isn't this kind of game breaking?Long power lines, same thing. Insanely useful. I can have my factories be powered way before I unlock trains and build them. But at the same time I now can explore the entire map in seconds by building power lines and sliding from one to another. I can be in all 4 spawn points and tens of artifacts in one hour of building all of them. This kind of destroys the need for the small car vehicle. Great game, great update. But I'm left kind of conflicted with some features. Which is fine.

_childDocuments_.review: Exploration game 7/10Builder game 9/10The combination of both of those things in a multiplayer server? 420/69If you are a math/engineer type, PLAY THIS GAME. If you aren't then play with your friends who are and watch them FREAK out about the minor inefficiencies of your base... hilarious fun times await!Now go get those radioactive slugs!
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: It is pretty fun, but once you get to the point where you have to venture off for other resources you realize that the stupid zapper weapon isn't very effective and you just die repeatedly. There needs to be some kind of protection sooner in the game so that you can defend yourself. Other than that it is pretty fun to try and balance machines to craft complex pieces.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, recommended for anyone who enjoys automation and exploration. Beautiful graphics, relaxing music. The game offers combat, but since it isn't the main focus of the game, it doesn't have much depth. Factory building, on the other hand, feels amazing. Satisfactory also offers multiplayer, but I haven't had the chance to test it.Edit: Multiplayer is awesome, lol.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good game; I do actually prefer Factorio, but this game is kind of cool. Some of the mechanics are annoying, and some of the glitches even more so. The space-dookie is hella annoying, especially because sometimes you'll clip through the floor near it, or you'll die and your inventory box will. It's a bit cheesy and a bit annoying that assembler upgrade tiers aren't really speed-based, but instead a function of how many (and what types) of ingredients machines can process. Factorio just has a better system for this. Biggest QoL feature they're missing is ability to limit storage warehouse slot counts. Being able to set which slots load and unload from the conveyor would be a good start. Other missing feature is that splitters and mergers don't have input or output priority. So the only way to regulate that is to use more splitters, which can only approach the right behavior, not achieve it. Still, I enjoyed researching the tech and completing the tiers and MAM trees. Good work on a cool game.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: The pros:I love playing with a friend on this game, cooperation is well in place. There is always something to do, no really need to stay still while waiting for resources to be made.The scenery is beautiful, the atmosphere changes a lot depending on the areas. The difficulty is there and the number of equipment/machines/vehicles is considerable.The cons:When you die, I cross my fingers every time because the loot is sometimes found in places that are impossible to access.Too bad there are not two places in the vehicles, to move with your friend.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game with a well-designed system for a new player to settle into playing at their own pace. The game has been very engaging with at least 9 hours poured into today. For someone like me who prefers to avoid fighting monsters I really appreciate that those creatures won't respawn near areas you build at. I was also about to smoothly figure out the factory/conveyor belt system and I feel the storage system is a lot nicer than many other similar games. I definitely recommend this and look forward to playing further (at 12 hours so far and about to unlock tier 3 I believe).Edit: 254 hours logged now... this game only gets more fun as you progress. The map has a bunch of different "biomes" each with beautiful, alien plant life, some additional life forms (monsters) as well as variations of the stronger life forms I've seen. This is a seriously addictive game and I can't recommend it enough to those who like to build, especially if you like playing with formulas to make the amounts of inputs and outputs line up juuuust right!
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: As the name says, you play for the satisfaction for the automated system in the game. Few down sides is that the game is too chill to play not too much challenges on combat but rather more challenges in collecting resources. There are some bugs in this game but is not too much of a big deal to it.I would recommend this game if you just wanted to chill, farming resources, building factories and automation.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: What can be said about Satisfactory and Coffee Stain Studios? This has to be the absolute gold standard for an Early Access format, with an amazing development studio, community interaction and a fantastic, well developed game. Even if building games are not for you, I would still recommend giving Satisfactory a go. Its surprisingly addictive, well developed and balanced, surprisingly bug free compared to other modern AAA games. I have played this game since 2019, on both steam and epic, and followed its development since shortly entering EA, and have watched the game grow from pre- conveyor lifts to pipes through to 1.0.Congratulations to Coffee Stain on what the have made and I'm looking forward to countless hours in this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: Me and my friends have played Satisfactory, since 2021. 12. 25 Christmas. We've played for 170 hours, and really enjoyed the game whenever we have free times at holidays and weekends. By the end now, we made 50 'nuclear power plant' and it was really challenging. Most of the game was satisfied, but i've found that pipe deliver so little amount of liquids (Max 600 per mins), and liquid mechanics was too confusing- so that we need to fix the pipes for bunch of times. I really want some more advanced pipes and more simple liquid  delivering.After all these, this game gave me lots of funs and pretty satisfied.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a masterclass on how to do early access right. Started off a little rocky with epic exclusive, but hey they used that Fortnite money to fuel up their development budget and create this absolute gem, so in retrospect the "controversy" was really overblown. The communication between the community managers and the player base has been phenomenal. It really shows that they developers care about feedback and want to include our voices in development decisions. I have never felt as invested in a games development as I have with Satisfactory. I have been following development since the game came to Steam. The videos created hype for each new update while still having personality and not feeling forced. Other studios should take notes on how Coffee Stain runs their community management.As for the gameplay, I have never been more addicted to math homework in my life. Balancing inputs and output sounds like a boring excel sheet on the surface, but getting to actually walk around in these MASSIVE factories that you created really gives a sense of scale and importance to your hard work. 3D first person was such a good choice for this reason. The animation and sound direction is so, for lack of a better word, CRISPY. Its hard to describe but flipping the breaker after a power outage is just so cathartic. Something about the weight of the animation and the clean sound design scratches an itch for me. All the animation is like that, so heavy and impactful. This all combines to make a... ahem... *satisfying* experience.I have to say, the updated ADA might just be my favorite thing about 1.0; they really cranked up the GLaDOS vibes and I'm totally here for it. Also straight belt mode is a godsend.TLDR;Overall, I don't normally write reviews for games but this one is so good that I felt I needed to, so here it is... 10/10. Like crack the video game. I cannot recommend this game enough. Coffee Stain enjoy this huge boost in players for 1.0, you've earned it. If you are thinking about getting this game you should. Now I have to get back to work digging my hub out of a mountain of spaghetti.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: Satisfactory is a great game for people that like grinding and putting real effort into building well-thought-out infrastructure. What soured it for me was the incessant voice lines trying to get you to "comply" with a storyline that isn't finished yet. I played the game as a way to unwind, and get my mind off of studying at the end of the day, but being jumpscared every 15 minutes defeats the purpose of the game for my use case. I genuinely hope that the team behind this game can make a game mode that allows you to progress without creepy voice lines and jumpscares in the otherwise -mostly- tranquil environment.

_childDocuments_.review: Satisfactory Review: Crafting Paradise with Room for ImprovementRating: ★★★★½(4.5/5)Visuals and Design:"Satisfactory" boasts stunning visuals and immersive design that bring its alien world to life. From lush forests to rugged mountains, each biome is beautifully rendered with attention to detail. The industrial machinery and structures are intricately designed, creating a sense of scale and grandeur as players construct their factories. The day-night cycle and dynamic weather effects further enhance the immersive experience, making players feel truly immersed in their alien surroundings.Gameplay and Mechanics:At its core, "Satisfactory" is a factory-building game that challenges players to optimize production chains, automate processes, and expand their operations. The game's mechanics are intuitive and easy to grasp, allowing players to dive into the world of industrial automation with ease. The satisfaction of seeing a well-oiled production line humming along smoothly is unparalleled, and the game offers ample opportunities for creative problem-solving and optimization.However, some players may find the learning curve steep, especially when it comes to more advanced concepts like logistics and resource management. Additionally, while the game offers a vast array of building options and production chains, some players may find themselves wishing for even more variety and complexity to keep things interesting in the later stages of the game.Community and Support:"Satisfactory" benefits from a passionate and engaged community of players who share tips, tricks, and creative builds with one another. The developer, Coffee Stain Studios, has demonstrated a strong commitment to supporting the game with regular updates, bug fixes, and new content releases. Community feedback is valued and often incorporated into the game's ongoing development, ensuring that "Satisfactory" remains a vibrant and evolving experience.Value and Pricing:Priced at $29.99, Satisfactory offers excellent value for players seeking a deep and immersive factory-building experience. With its expansive world, satisfying gameplay mechanics, and ongoing support from the developer, the game provides countless hours of enjoyment and replayability for fans of the genre

_childDocuments_.review: Played it in EA four years ago, now fired it up with 1.0. It was and is a good and polished game.However, I got my enjoyment out of it back then and now, I don't feel like "working" in this game again. It's a me issue mostly. I lost interest in the genre over the years as I grew older. On a pro-side, buying into EA contributed into finishing the game for sure. _childDocuments_.review: The game is okay right now, but it's clearly Early Access.  It's not nearly as far along as would be implied given the overwhelmingly positive feedback.  The company also has a very slow update cycle for now.  That said, this game shows a lot of promise.  But how many games have you bought based on promises?  I'd recommend waiting till Q4 2021 or sometime 2022 and then assess how the game is coming along.Detailed opinions:1. People are comparing this to Factorio meets No Man's Sky.  It's a pretty good description at first glance.  2. Resource management vs space management.  Factorio, imo, was about both.  This game is reasonably competent with the resource management stuff, and likely will have more content and crafting balance stuff to adjust along the way, but when it comes to space management, Satisfactory has barely scratched the surface.  You can see hints that they are planning to implement clipping/overlapping checks, but right now, I was often able to overlay conveyor belts and pipes so that any reason to grow vertically was negated.  Once again, there is potential here, but not there yet.3. Research.  Factorio's research was in one place.  Press T and deal with the labs.  Now getting stuff there, that's a different matter.  In Satisfactory, however, research is split across 3 different devices, each with their own tier system.  Thematically, it makes sense why they did it, but it gives the illusion of there being more than there is.  Additionally, Factorio would let you approach some research non-linearly.  There's little of that in this game, except maybe with the MAM which is very underwhelming, I've wondered once or twice why the MAM was in the game yet.4. Exploration and combat.  Well... the exploration is pretty great, but as a rule, I don't buy exploration games.  I buy games about other stuff, and then enjoy if there's exploration in said game.  I think Satisfactory has a great handle on this.  I wouldn't be surprised if they have more exploration stuff planned, but that's not a selling point, imo.  However, while exploring, you should be ready for some FPS combat (without guns... unless you've build the really weak rebar shooter).  Thematically, you work for a corporation that's sent you to a planet to collect resources and ship them back to space via a space elevator.  But all they give you is a little weak baton and expect that'll be enough.  It's a little silly and more than cliche.  On the other hand, the few creatures that do attack are so amazing predictable that I found the stun baton was more than adequate if I had some local flora available to chomp on afterwards.  Factorio's combat is hardly stellar, but even that pistol was more fun than this stuff.  And for this being an alien world, there seemed to be too few creatures and of those, too many hostile ones.  Definitely room for improvement, but once again, has potential.So yeah... potentially a great game, but it's not there yet and is still a couple years out.  I expect to update this review in a couple years sometime around release with a more favorable opinion.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually write reviews, but this game deserves it: everything about it is just perfect! There are so many aspects of it to keep you fully engaged: resource hunting, creating new production lines and improving old ones and unlocking new materials and recipes through the tiers, space elevator and research. This game is masterfully crafted, there is never a moment of boredom because there is always something new to do: improving the power grid because you put down new machines that build new components, meaning you need to tweak your old production line to make it more efficient and maybe hunt down some resource nodes to upgrade your raw material input.The progression is also very well engineered: you start from zero, having to do everything manually until you can automate the process and then, as you unlock more things, the production lines get more and more complex, requiring some clever thinking and planning to make it as efficient as possible.There is also a multiplayer aspect, so you can build your factories with friends, even though I personally don't care for that.And the game isn't even finished yet! But it is already so great! I very highly recommend this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: If Factorio is 'Factory Crack', Satisfactory is 'Factory Weed'. It's a relaxed and beautiful trip of a factory builder with a lot of freedom in how you go about constructing factories, exploiting resources, and exploring the world. While not as fast-paced of a game as something like Factorio, Satisfactory takes a fundamentally different approach to its gameplay that focuses on exploration, customization, and enjoying the ride. There's always something to do, or something to optimize. The game is also incredibly beautiful, with both the natural environments and incredibly pleasing building designs and animations being equally stunning. The building system is also incredibly intuitive and customizable, with just about anything being possible if you're willing to get tricky with the parts and systems available. I would heavily recommend grabbing Satisfactory with a friend if you want a more active time, as having multiple hands working at once both speeds up some of the slower parts of the game (especially pre-coal), but also opens up more room for activity and shenanigans.

_childDocuments_.review: Satisfactory was a game that was a lot of fun in the short term, but the burnout crept up fast. It felt like that meme of "boys' two week Minecraft server", but instead it ended up only being a few play sessions for me and friends.There's not really much notable about the progression. It just follows a system of exponential growth making each new tier feel more or less the same, but with the caveat of taking 3x+ the time invested as the previous one. The actual enjoyment comes from each tier's new perks, but the enjoyment is very short-lived as you're constantly lead to continue grinding for the next upgrade. Which... would be fine, but I found that it didn't feel all too rewarding. Past oil production, the game really hits a decline in terms of gameplay.I am also salty about no retro-active achievement handouts. Especially given that a few would require going through the entire process of a world over again. Overall, I'm a bit disappointed by the game, and I'm mostly just using this to vent and also serve as a warning to people looking for something with good longevity.

_childDocuments_.review: After 8 years of development, and 5 of early access, Satisfactory by Coffee Stain is releasing version 1.0 tomorrow. After 600 hours of gameplay, I guess I should post a review, but there's really just too much to say, so I'll be brief: this is my favorite video game. I've spent countless hours in this game as a way to exercise my brain with logistical puzzles, express my creativity through building fashionable factories, or to relax and forget my troubles, using the in-game chainsaw to fell foliage for future factory expansion.After hundreds of hours playing modded Minecraft, the transition to this first person factory builder was easy. Explore and find resources, work out the logistics of getting them to the right place, and build efficient production chains for maximum advantage.To progress, satisfy increasing material demands at the hub and the space elevator. Unlock new technology in tiers to add complexity to the gameplay. Increase your base's footprint, and expand your production chains.I still haven't beaten the game, or experienced all it has to offer (thanks in no small part to my tendency to start a new save once every few months.) - But if it's your cup of tea, you are guaranteed many hours of fun.

_childDocuments_.review: So, so, so, Satisfactory. Where do I begin? And where do I end? Much like a new players first attempt at a factory which lead to spaghetti, let's start at the beginning. Yknow. As any place should, I suppose!I first learned of Satisfactory when I'd been followin' coffee stain on twitter. Big fan of sanctum and all that. Got sad it was an EGS thing, waited for it to hit steam and so it did. Bought it when I found out. So, how do I feel about it?All in all, I think it's quite good. The music feels chill, I absolutely adore the designs in this game. They've crafted such a pretty world that is rather quite large, too. And packed it full of things to find or just nice places ot look at. And the designs of the buildings and vehicles and just.. stuff like that? It's all boxy, orange,I love it. It's great.The actual main part, the building + factory stuff, is.. about what you'd expect I suppose! You get introduced to the basics, figure out how some things work, and things get more complicated. You find, handcraft, automate, unlock, and kinda repeat, and so it goes. Though, I think Satisfactory is a bit more easy to.. grasp? So long as you're willing to do some maths. Yknow, stuff like "Oh hey, this uses 15. I make 30 currently. I have 120 of this, so 120 divided by 30" and so on. You can make some spaghetti with your conveyors or power lines but.. the game don't mind too much. Things like conveyors and pipes can clip through eachother most of the time and.. Yknow hwat? I'm okay with that. There are other factory games (which I shall not mention for many reasons) which don't let me do that. And sometimes it hurts my brain when I can't. We aren't all experts, and some of us don't wanna watch a 3 hour long video guide on how to set up the most efficient factory and take out the fun of figuring it out. I appreciate that I can break physics every now and then.Anyway, that's the building part. So how about the rest?It goes simple enough. You got your irons, your iron products, your copper and copper products early game, iron becomes more complicated when you need 3 things to make 3 other things that require 2 of the before mentioned thing, yknow. Stuff like that.Then you get your coals and your irons and your steels, and your slowly but surely increasingly complicated products from it.Other liquids get added, and byproducts from those liquids you need to plan for andadd into your increasingly complicated layouts, all that stuff. Mind, I don't think the early/mid game is that hard to work your brain around? It's when you get oils and long ra nge transport things get.. weird, to me at least.(addendum: I forgot to add this, but to make a quick edit: Exploration is rewarded with a lot, but keep a keen eye. You find Freighters dotted about the place. Fix them up, get their harddives. Scan them at the M.A.M. and you'll be rewarded with some alt-recipes. Some of these are amazing and game changers. Love; a confused lizard)Another thing I think benefits this,  I get the feeling the people making the map were actually kinda smart. I've found several locations that are just wonderfully perfect for certain things. Find a nice lil place to make steel in the rocky desert. I got something that needs steel pipes and copper, and then I got hit by it"Oh, ♥♥♥♥! RIGHT, MY STEEL PLACE HAS COPPER NEXT TO IT."I feel this game is kinda slow a lot of the time. There's a lot of periods where.. nothing is really going on? You're just kinda waiting for your machines to do the heavy lifting before you unlock the new stuff. Use those down times to explore your surroundings. Figure out where you'll source new materials, pathways to take, find slugs, find delicious carapace or organs, get terrified by the local fauna when you realise there's creepy ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ spiders that spit acidic spikes at you (or, in my case, pictures of floating cat faces that drool green slime because I have arachnophobia mode on. Yes, there is "I'm scared of spiders" mode that replaces them with floating cat faces. And the cats meow, instead of make the horrid skittering sound those Stingers make.)The game gives you some movement options relatively early on if you can find them. Here's some advice, if you want it: Oh, I forgot to mention. So you can "Overclock" things in this game. You unlock it early on, and they very much want you to use it. It lets you simplify, or complicate, your designs. You can find these slugs all over the place, I call them "Friends", and you can use them to make power shards. Plug power shards into something, and it starts working faster. Something like a screw constructor uses 10 iron rods, and a single iron rod constructor makes 15. Soo.. rather than building 2 of those and building 3 of the others, you could just make 1, overlock the other to 150% and make things less of a headache.EDIT: I learnt that Overclocking drastically increases power usage of a building. So much so that a single refinery will use about 150 MW at 250% overclock. So careful with that! underclocking has the opposite effect. In terms of energy use, underclocking buildings uses a lot less power but requires you to use more space when building. I think the only thing I /don't/ like about this game is the early game power. It's all handcrafted or hand found. I don't really enjoy running around, picking up leaves and wood, turning it into biomass, into solid biofuel, dumping it into biofuel burners and then getting to work and praying I work fast enough to "out-run" the situation where i run out of fuel and I have to spend another age cutting down trees and foliage to power the generators.The moment you unlock coal and coal burners, this problem goes away. So my advice? Get Coal Power ASAP.I love the movement options in this game. Anywhere from "ride on my power line" to "Jump pads, baby!" to "I'm going to make this tube so long I will afk for 5 minutes as I get flung towards my oil by a transparent tube."Unfortunately, I can't tell you what I think of mid/late game, because I never made it that far. I always end up feeling terrible that I can't build right, or i just don't have the energy to figure it out. But just because I get sad about it, doesn't mean you shouldn't check Satisfactory out if it catches your fancy.Just remember, if you're struggling to figure it out.. just take a step back. Take a few breaths, and just go "Alright, let me break this down in my head."And remember, if you need space, platforms are your friend. No room? Build up. FICSIT encourages verticality to streamline short range transportation. But they also defy physics, and if you want you could just make a floating sky factory on platforms.... Okay, one more thing. The space elevator is one of the coolest ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ things ever. I never get tired of seeing that animation. Or watching my constructors work.. or listening to the sound of machinery chug and hum. It's great.
