_childDocuments_.review: Satisfactory, for me, is able to immerse you into an alien world but also promote a sense of self accomplishment with everything you do. I typically don't go for many tycoon games, but Satisfactory immediately caught my eye when it came to gameplay. From the typical beginning from relatively nothing to work with, I was able to enjoy the game as I started my factory. The biggest thing I love is how accomplishing it is to automate the production of resources, especially when they require extensive processes to make. The tier and phase system is a really creative way to keep you invested as it gives you an incentive to play and unlock things as you progress in the order you chose within each phase. I like this because it helps tailor the experience to whatever you want to focus on. The multiplayer I think is one of the minor things aside from certain bugs that should be improved because even though it makes the factory building process much faster, it lacks some type of sandbox element that I think would go well with the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I've logged a lot of hours on this game, so it kinda goes without saying that I recommend it. Satisfactory has a great mix of factory optimization and exploration and I really liked the fact that each is sort of separated. It was relaxing to be able to let things run without worrying about some "big bad" coming in to rip down your stuff; at the same time if you wanted to look for a fight all you had to do was venture out in any direction. I spent most of my time just trying to maximize production and didn't really worry about how "pretty" anything was. Later section of my factory were much better laid out but I appreciated that that was sort of optional. I really liked the nuclear age because it had some interesting trade-offs. Resource nodes are infinite, which I appreciated (even if my "suspension of disbelief" had some issues) because chasing or worrying about running out wasn't the focus. Perhaps the developers might consider different "challenge" modes in the future where there's a goal to reach but nodes have fixed resources that run out as this would force the player to have a reason to utilize less expensive technologyI can summarize what I wish was different pretty quickly:-There needs to be a few more lairs/dungeons with a new "big bad" monster you don't find elsewhere. There's a cave system with a mix of required resources inside that was a lot of fun and I'd like to see this expanded a bit. The swamps were a great end game section with a high concentration of challenging foes but it seemed a bit anti-climactic. -The artifact messages can drive you crazy running around. It was a motivation to collect them, but until they're wrapped into the final game build as something you need it's just an obnoxious component. If there's a setting to just turn them off at some point that would be good. -Clipping frames would be a good addition in my opinion; sure you can carefully align factory components but being able to lay a frame down as an architectural guide that had set measurements for each building side (with each dimension) would make it easier to organize layout.

_childDocuments_.review: Very polished for an early access game, with loads of content to explore and mess around with and frequent updates and content from a lovely developer team.This game isn't for everyone though- if you like the idea of building factories to automate increasingly complex tasks, you'll like this game. If that sounds tedious and confusing, this game probably isn't for you. This game does have open world survival crafting elements, but they're secondary to base building and automation.Personally, I've had a blast and I highly recommend this game to any fans of the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Game was kind of hard to get into at first, it took me about 5 attempts of having nothing better to do and booting up the game before I finally got into it.During the periods of time I didn't know what I was doing, the game didn't seem like it had enough direction and I was lost and bored and wound up quitting the game.Fast forward to me and a buddy finally sitting down one day and saying "F*ck it, lets force ourselves to learn the game, we almost wound up quitting but we finally learned it and have been hooked since.I'm currently at Tier 6 level hub with plenty left to do, the game has a very enjoyable gameplay loop of making factories and automating every single little task you can, game has me hooked beyond belief, and it's even more enjoyable when you finally automate everything so you can just let the game run overnight while you are sleeping and be stacked on materials when you wake up in the morning.The graphics, sound, music and gameplay all feel on par with a AAA game. Best of all, the game is OPTIMIZED BEYOND BELIEF. I have no clue how this game runs above 60FPS on ULTRA with the factories I have built but game runs amazingly some how. Great job Devs.Devs are also constantly updating the game with major content patches.For the great low price of $29.99, I couldn't recommend this game more. If you are having trouble getting into the game, try focusing on automating as much as you can and you'll be hooked in no time.

_childDocuments_.review: Prior to Update 5, I tried this a few times, kept getting killed by the aliens, but I didn't do any research online, nor did I actually put any effort into it, it was then, just 'another game in my library'I decided to go back to it, and I'm so glad I did. Once you get the hang of things, and follow the tiers (which are like a tutorial in themselves) it is way fun, and I keep going back for more. I've always tried to get into 7d2d, Rust, etc. But there is always that element of 'Food' 'Water' 'Warmth' etc, which I appreciate is for someone, but for me, the tedious part of that puts me off those games.I realized, I have so many things in my life that are automated, from Alexa to Excel VBA to .bat scripts on my PCs and that is why I feel I like this game so much. I love automation.It's a chill game, if you put yourself in a safe spot, you can move from your PC and get on with IRL for a while, and then come back to the section you need to pick up your items to go off and build.I'm running this on a dedicated linux server, so I can't use any mods at the moment and I'm really happy with my progression through the game. I'm currently at Phase 3 and working on Tier 5 and 6 and I have enough items being produced that I can put a hold on that for now and start on 'Base 2' using all the stuff I have learnt from Base 1 to make it optimized, etcSuch a fun game, although one thing puzzles me, my only Hypertube I'm using at the moment from Base 1 to Base 2, takes over a minute to get up their, yet 15 seconds to get down, and if there was a wall in front of me on exit, I think I'd go 'Splat'at the moment it's still on Early Access and their are various streams from the creators to keep you in the loop and I believe it has lots more to come.Get it while it's on sale, get it in a bundle, get it full price, if your like me, I'd recommend you buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game, big time sink though. If I could change anything it'd be the sheer volume of items you need to produce late-game, which makes even making one new item feel like a chore if you're not in the right mindset at the time (think 9 uranium fuel rods/min needing 3k quickwire/min 900 copper/min etc etc). Alternatively add higher belt tiers to make higher throughput possible without using multiple Mk.5 belts (I am aware they said this is an engine limitation, however I'd imagine it's possible for them to add higher tier belts as long as they are covered in some way so they don't have to render 1000/min or whatever items moving on the conveyor).
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: Would be perfect but it is missing one thing. Creative mode in vanilla! It could be used to test out new updates and test theories and just do what ever you want (like build art). Examples: The basics: flying, and unlimited materials. More difficult ones but fun ones could be: no fuel usage no items consumed (like parachutes), and no damage whatsoever (be that from beasts or radiation. AND FALL DAMAGE) Thank you. _childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: Man. Actually a game with a dev, who plays their own game. Everything works, had no bugs yet, super stable frames. I have nothing to complain about. _childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: its a good game but its easy to get burnout when there isn't anything to push you forward. another game that is very similar to this is factorio and it features a direct threat to your expansion, with alien nests that attack you when your pollution reaches them. if this game were to add that it would be complete
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: I want to be fair and say that if you like farming resources, crafting, and engineering, then this game is fantastic and perfect for you. A new/space-age, engineering-based Minecraft is how I would identify it. The newer trailers for the game give you a pretty good idea what you're getting into, but when I tried it, I thought it was  going to be a base-building game with a similar game/instance length of Deep Rock Galactic. I was so wrong. This game will devour hours of your time if you are into this genre. I am not.While I personally would not recommend this game, I DO recommend this game for people that are into the genre. I do not, I do not see the point.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: This is the ultimate game for anyone who finds joy in straight lines and perfectly optimized workflows. The planet is beyond stunning, but let’s be real: it’s just the backdrop for a conveyor belt empire. And yes, I did rebuild my entire base twice because "dat one pipe" wasn’t symmetrical.If you love turning OCD tendencies into an art form, this game is dangerously fun. Just don’t forget to eat... or sleep... or socialize.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: Me...Oh idk if I'll like this type of game...184 hrs in, haven't passed phase 3 yet, having a blast.Co-op has been fun to have someone else have those eureka moments or both having them.If you like this game you probably already have it.If you aren't sure you like this game, it scratches an itch so good.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: Satisfactory is my favorite factory-type game, absolutely exceeding all my expectations. The core gameplay loop is engaging and there's always something to do, build, or achieve. This constant sense of progress keeps the experience fresh and rewarding.I consider Satisfactory to be nearly perfect and would absolutely recommend it to others. If you enjoy games like Oxygen Not Included, Factorio, or Dyson Sphere Program, you'll likely find Satisfactory to be a great addition to your collection.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: Caution - You will definitely lose track of time with this game. Tiers are getting more and more balanced and it's extremely satisfying to see all your items being produced after hours of building and calculating. Stunning graphics, though the storyline hasn't been released yet. Lizard doggos are very cute, and I like the fact you're not constantly suffering from ongoing threats like in factorio.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: All grind and no game. It's just a sandbox builder.If that's your thing, then great, but DO NOT buy this expecting a 3D factorio. Factorio is a game, this is a sandbox, they're not the same thing.Graphics and mechanics are nice though.I wanted to like this so badly, but just can't bring myself to bother continuing. If they ever make a DLC with enemies/challenge, I'd definitely buy it.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: I have decided to post a negative review on steam due to recent bad decisions on developers behalf. This applies to multiplayer (MP) which is how I want to play the game and also a marketed feature. If you like single player much of the below may not apply. Hopefully this will be fixed and I'll post a good review.Looking at this from a *consumer* perspective Update 7 has fallen below expectations. Multiplayer is completely broken with the update. Encountering creatures crashes server and clients. Deleting objects sometimes causes crashes. Performance is bad. Clients often desyncs. Vehicles don't work. Vulkan, directx, dedicated host/client host doesn't matter. Its unplayable in multiplayer more so than it was a year or two ago with other updates. There is a point where stability is so bad it no longer is worth playing the game. It is very disappointing many of these  game stopping  bugs are things that existed in experimental. I'd suggest developers looking through crash reports and starting fixing some of the worst bugs. Stability doesn't need to be perfect but its bad then game is not playable in multiplayer this means less MP  players. less MP people testing the game.  Also pro-tip: Don't launch new versions before festive season! That was really, really a bad move.Update: Developers have released experimental 8 which is unplayable in MP on my worlds and even more broken. They are now on vacation for one month.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: Northern Forest is my favorite map although I played the grass lands several times before hand so I had the feel of the game. New and old players alike will love the exploration and I am glad my family talked me into coming back and playing again, excellent work on game creation ! Highly recommended !
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: Some games have been "ready" for years, but are still full of bugs that ruin the gaming experience. And then there is an "early access" game that I have never, not once, experienced the slightest problem with. Early access here probably just means "hey, try it out, but don't overdo it, there's a bunch of new game elements coming soon".That's exactly why, after nearly 300 hours of 'trial play', I put aside my time to wait for the 1.0 launch, which I'm delighted to say is coming this year. Oh, and in that time, while I've developed essentially everything but the nuclear age, I've "filled" a fraction of the playing field. It's simply immeasurable how much potential there is, and it's breathtaking the buildings and factories that some people are able to build. It's not a game, it's an alternate reality in which one's real life temporarily ceases to exist - and all that remains is thousands of kilometres of conveyor belts (Mk5)...
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: Played this last when it was freshly released on EPIC games, bought it on steam since its been released (prefer all my games in one place) i have to say i really enjoy this game, its hard to fathom scale and the first few tries will be hard and slow if you havn't played the likes of factorio or mindustry, it is beautifully made and the community is really strong, the updates have depth and thought behind them in line with what the players want, playing every iteration after a major update feels like playing a new game with the anticipation for the new content, 5/7 would recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Current major problem with this game is a poorly done multiplayer synchronization. 1-5 minutes lag is always present and it makes it completely impossible to build smth together. Fot the record, buildings are synchronized decently, but anything moving does so with considerable lag. You can never be certain, where exactly your friend is right now, or where the rhinoceros dog is charging you from at this moment.Due to sync problems many cool things in the game, like vehicles or trains, become effectively unusable for clients. For example, you place a train wagon, but have no idea if it is attached or not. Then the wagon disappears, but it is still there - you can jump on it, wait for 30 sec and it will reappear again, etc.The second major issue is a complete lack of blueprints. For example, you came up with a factory, that produces 20 heavy modular frames per minute and it needs hundreds of constructors, foundries and assemblers, carefully interconnected with belts and power poles. There is no way to batch build it and little to no visual guidance at least to make the building process consistent. You will have to place each power pole yourself and if you want to keep the offsets or splitter/merger orientations the same you will only suffer.The last thing is that building is always done from 1st person view, and buildings are only becoming bigger and bigger. 3rd person top-down view for building placement purpose would've made the game far more convenient to play, but there's no such thing - the closest is a lookout tower, but that is not the same.

_childDocuments_.review: I was expecting this to be a combination of Factorio, and No Man's Sky, both games I love. But this honestly feels like the worst of both worlds.It doesn't have an early hook, some form of accomplishment in the first five minutes where I could go "yeah, my game-life is tangibly better" or a sense of curiosity of "ohhhhh, what's that". I went from click and hold to produce resource, to click and hold to produce different resource, but in a different building. Trying to figure out which building to go to was also a pretty big barrier.Overall I spent close to an hour of slogging around, I didn't feel like I had accomplished anything that would remotely accelerate my future slogging, and that was with the help of two experienced friends.Performance and graphics look very polished. Might come back when there's a better tutorial.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, having a lot of fun, but there are plenty of issues that don't make this a true 1.0 release for me.Getting used to the first-person view didn't take as long as I expected.The world is beautiful, fun and rewarding to explore.I'm having issues with building, mostly repetitive building. I tried using blueprints to make things quicker, but it's not because the thing looks connected visually that they are.If you place one rail blueprint next the the other, they are not actually connected... so you actually have to build stuff manually most of the time.Talking about trains, intersections are a mess. You build it manually, add signals, and everything looks fine, but the train doesn't path. After messing a bunch with the signals, you redo a part of the rail and the train starts to path. Again, It's not because things look connected that they are.I had some crashes here and there, it's annoying but you don't lose any progress, including a repeated one when trying to add a subcategory to blueprints while making a new blueprint. I had to clear the blueprint MK1 and start again for it not to crash.All in all the game is super fun and I want to play more, but I wish everything worked a bit better

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game for people who can get sucked into a single game. ATTENTION, do not play if you are easily addicted, because you will be. It is a bit on the grindy side if you do not know what is going on, expect your first save file to easily exceed 100hours trying to figure things out. (I am still not at the final tier and have 105hours in that save file, whoopsie) It also requires your brain to actually function, you have to think about the most effective ways to get everything you need with minimal loss in between. And you have to calculate how many power sources you need for your factory, if you do it wrong or neglect power... yeah that takes a while to solve. If you have a phobia of spiders, this game covers that! Well, kinda. You have a setting to turn the spiders into pictures of cats, but you can still hear them crawling. But no worries! The game is easily modded, and yes, there is a mod to remove the spawns of satan. Anyways, a great game, I foresee many more hours added to my timer soon.10/10 would receive again!

_childDocuments_.review: Very much like Factorio in 3D as anyone can tell from looking at a screenshot or two. Lots of fun though, especially with multiplayer. I can see myself sinking lots of hours into this game. Satisfactory does have quite a few noticeable bugs (especially where ragdoll physics are involved) and a few unfinished items that don't do anything but that is to be expected from an early access title. It definitely lacks some of the polish and feature-completeness of Factorio, but it has a lot of content already and it will only get better with time. Its pretty cool to see your factory expand over time and the verticality of a 3rd dimension presents lots of new opportunities.I'll update my review if I have more to say in the future but I'd recommend it to fans of Factorio and other factory-builder games.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: Satisfactory is still in the early access, but it's definitely a game, that worth your time.If you ever played Factorio or similar games, then you should feel right at home. There's none. The game ask you to pick one of the available biomes and start your adventure.  And now the juicy part. This game is named "Satisfactory" for a reason.Manual farming, transporting and resource crafting get old pretty fast and in order to be efficient, you need to build a large net of factories, platforms, power supply and transport systems.For example, you found an Copper Ore node, then your actions can be like this:- Build a Miner MK1 in order to start automatic extraction- Connect Miner MK1 to the Smelter, so that Copper Ore will convert into Copper Bar.- Connect Smelter to a Constructor, so that Copper Bar will convert into Wire- All that left is to connect it to a Storage near your base. At the early game, the power supply is rather limited, so you can't go ham with your buildings, pay attention to how much energy supply your Burner can produce and gather Wood and Leaves, when you run around. Those are your early game Fuel supply.The Fauna can be agressive here, but it's not that dangerous, just pay attention to rare spawns, like Slimes. They can provide various boosts. If you need to recover health, gather some local fruits or mushrooms.Aaaaaaaaaand, that's pretty much it.At your main base you can advance tiers in possible unlocks/upgrades and that's your main goal aka in-game progression. Enjoy this great game in your own pace. Satisfactory also support crossplay between Epic Games Store and Steam, which is always nice to have. Currently, there's some bugs, but the devs are actively working on resolving & fixing known issues.Gonna list the most important one: you can stuck in the trees. If you found yourself stuck like that, the only option there is to "Respawn" (which is a suicide, so you need to get back to this spot again and pick your dropped stuff). I tried various methods, but none of it worked, so in the end i was forced to suicide. Just be cautious when you try to jump on a rock and there's a tree near it.The optimization is pretty good, considering all what happens in your world in realtime. 8/10There's some small issues in multiplayer, but the game is great both in single and co-op modes and recommended to all, who enjoy this type of games.- This review was presented to you by "Casual Game Reviews" Steam Curator.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: A highly entertaining explore-and-exploit type of game with few survival elements and little combat. The fun lies in producing ever more in ever more complex ways. In this, the game is similar to Factorio, but it's not as complex in it's production chain - instead offering verticality and inexhaustible resource nodes instead of an ever expanding 2D map.Drawbacks are that it's a single, static world, so on replay you'll know what's where. But this barely diminishes the fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazingly fun game. It's a balance of factory automation, exploration, building, and watching the sunset. I'll probably have another 1000 hours before long of which at least 982.5 will be great fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: This game is much more then I bargained for. It starts so simple and straight forward and as you progress and expand it never loses the simple but just becomes more grand in it's scale. Soon your one little production line on the grass becomes a tangled web of conveyors in a multi leveled, unplanned  and mashed together factory that still somehow works. You will find yourself doing maths... because if you don't watch your efficiencies then before you know it you are all out of the one thing you needed to finish that last build and the train just left the station and the only stack of that item is on the other side of the map.The world is beautiful, and immersive. I can't help but think it can only be an enviromentalist's nightmare to go and despoil the pristine alien landscape with pollution, oil, and cold steel. As you deforest the landscape and destroy the indiginous species. When you get bored of building, or just waiting for items to complete, you can go explore the vast open world fighting alien creatures and discovering alien artifacts (they are still a work in progress) Just be careful as you play, it is amazing how fast the time fly's as you are trying to build a new efficient layout for your iron mills or trying to just make your dang rail track straight. So far it has been a truely enjoyable experience. I look forward to what the game is coming up with in the future. I'm sure it will be a nightmare of planning and sub-processes but will make me keep coming back for more and more.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: This game is still early access but....There is already so much to explore and so much to build that its totally worth it! I play it in multiplayer and the worst bug is that i cant really drive the cars. But thats it. Its already so good and so amazingly beatufiul! Im so excited what the future will bring. I think this game really fits the description overwhelmingly positive!
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: After almost 1000 hours in this game, I can say it's one of my favorite games of all time. For starters, there are a lot of things to do, between factory building, exploring, and upgrading. These are all still connected, as factories let you upgrade your exploration gear, and exploring gets you incredibly useful things to build your factory with. A full play-through of the game can take hundreds of hours, and the alternate recipes, abundant resources, and different styles and ways to build factories mean that no two play-throughs are the same. The multiplayer feature also feels really well implemented, and I find it fun to explore together and build racetracks and skate parks for the Ficsit factory cart. Altogether, I's a really well made and interesting game.

_childDocuments_.review: Was never a factory builder game player, and still not sure if I am, but this game definitely set the bar for me. I actually find it almost as engaging as the exploration. I would definitely give this a try if you're on the fence. I've "only" put in about 60hrs. and I'm hooked.

_childDocuments_.review: I have played many games. Some are good. Some are great. But Satisfactory... Satisfactory is perfect. The world and music are breathtakingly well done. The building UI and factory function are as smooth as butter. Rewards come just as quickly for an explorer as a math brained factory focused worker. Make bombs. Build cool guns. Make a little electric car that can do backflips. Drink some coffee while your character drinks coffee. Paint your machines hot pink or fluorescent green. Make parachutes. Shoot yourself across the map with a hypertube cannon. Listen to relaxing music and make conveyor belt systems in perfect symmetrical polygons. Accidentally irradiate yourself with nuclear waste. Get attacked by spiders. Shoot those same spiders with a feggin' rebar gun. You can do whatever the heck you want.In short, buy this game. Right now. Get a friend, and make a factory, because this game...This game is the best game I have ever played.

_childDocuments_.review: Phenomenal game, and one of my favourite games of all time, and I say this as a person who plays all genres of games. First of all, the most important checkbox to tick in any game in my book is: [Is it fun?] YES!Satisfactory is in every sense of its name, very satisfying to play. Everything you do is worth your time, every process in the journey lacks any frustration. The tools you are given to achieve your goals are wonderfully thought out, so that the quality of your work and implementing your processes is purely down to the player; because the game gives you everything you need. The QOL in this game is actually insane, i feel like they have thought about everything. These guys and girls clearly play their own gameCoffee stain studios have truly build a masterpiece here, and to do so they have carefully listened to player feedback, and proven time and time again that what we say matters, as demonstrated by the many simple and complex things they implemented into the game over the years. Whilst listening, they have also been communicating the whole way through, not with just written word, or weird scripted 'campfire chats' like other insincere games companies have, but made funny, relatable, honest and sincere videos about the progress of the game and the challenges/obstacles in doing so. I have been following the development of this game closely for several years, and i'm always blown away with the quality of everything they do, inside and outside the game.Do yourself a massive favour, even if you do not think you enjoy this kind of genre of game; give it a go at the least, you may find yourself utterly absorbed in the pure joy that is watching your factory grow.

_childDocuments_.review: Version 1.0 has a number of new and useful features which have made it more fun to play than Early Access Update 8. It has cloud storage, teleportation, and various forms of power augmentation, Of course, all of the new technology must be unlocked, but the additional content leads to more play time before there is nothing left to accomplish. The look and feel, as well as the basic game play are similar to Update 8, but there have been changes to various parts of the game world that I think are very interesting in terms of what can now be done in places that had been useless in Update 8.  Some things, such as Mercer Spheres, SAM ore and Somersloops, now have important uses. There are still anomalies, such as boulders that can be removed with explosives, and others that can't be removed at all. Vehicle operation is still problematic. Version 1.0 is still a big step in the right direction.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm very mixed on this game, but overall I do think it's a good game. I just find myself not wanting to play for a long time, and there are other factory games that I prefer.I enjoy factory games, but not fps games, so this game is both a positive and a negative. I could do without the combat, but thankfully it doesn't happen very often. I wish we could switch to a third person view and zoom way out so I can actually see where I'm building things. I find myself having to place, destroy, place, destroy buildings until I get them in the right spot. This is all very early on in the game, though, so maybe it gets better.The buildings are HUGE compared to the player, which is kinda nice when walking around admiring what you've built, but not great for trying to place things just right, and you have to keep in mind that you will need lots and lots and lots of space to do any amount of automation, so don't place buildings too close to each other.As of this writing I have 23 hours of game play, but that's across multiple saves with a long time in between. I end up playing other games and then coming back and starting over because I don't remember what I was doing, so I've only really experienced early game stuff. I haven't even made any vehicles yet, though the first time I played, quite a while ago, I did get to that point and found it confusing.One thing that annoys me early on is the lack of power generation. You basically can only power your factory with leaves and wood (and you don't get much wood at first) and that's not really enough to power much, so the whole thing is constantly shutting down. In one game I unlocked a power plant that uses coal and water, scanned for coal and spent an hour trying to figure out how to get up on some big thing that apparently it was on top of. I ended up just giving up on it. The terrain is a big challenge in this game, especially with how large the buildings are.I've run across several bugs recently. Scanning for quartz and it not finding some that I can see off in the distance. Placing a splitter on an existing conveyor belt and it ending up just off a bit to where the conveyor belt ignores it. The game also gets super annoying if you are near an artifact. It basically tells you to go get it and won't stop until you do, even if it's something named "WIP" that you can't do anything with yet.I also wish we could take only some items out of a smelter, constructor, etc. If I need 8 of something for some reason, I don't want to have to take all 500. Once in your inventory you can right-click to split a stack in half, so I find myself taking the items, then right-click and put half back over and over until I get down to about how many I need. Part of the reason I don't want all of it is because I want that building to be full so it doesn't use power since I struggle to keep everything running.

_childDocuments_.review: I purchased this game on sale right after the 1.0 release because a bunch of reviews were saying this game was like cocaine for those on the spectrum.  I happen to be one of such people and have been needing a game that provides that kind of kick for ages, and I honestly didn't believe you suckers, so I kinda purchased the game just to prove y'all wrong.I got proved wrong instead.  Big time.  Thanks, Steam review bros.That being said, there are just a few suggestions for the gameplay that have come up in my 150-ish hours playing so far that I'd love to see happen:- A later-game secondary back slot so you can wear two different back-techs at once: Jetpack+parachute = controlled falls at all times (just press spacebar when out of fuel to activate secondary tech).  Hell, even Hoverpack+Jetpack would be nice to conveniently switch to fuel when out of electricity.  Either way, having two back slots would be killer.  Perhaps unlockable through the MAM or in a tier unlock for tier 8/9- An easier-access delete button for blueprints when you enter category edit mode in the blueprint maker (like a little trash can in the corner of each blueprint when edit mode is enabled).  Maybe I'm just an idiot, but I can't find the dang delete button for the blueprints lol.- A dismantle-only repository that you can build with Mercer Spheres (thus unlocked in the MAM probably) that can hold a ton of crap from dismantling stuff so that when you inevitably need to delete an entire massive factory because it fails you, you don't have to go around like a monkey picking up all of the dismantle crates and shoving the materials into piles of temporary industrial storages for later use...  Had to do this twice now, and it's actually the most tedious part of the game right now.  I want to feel freedom with deletion as much as I feel with creation.- On a similar note to the last one: let me set how many things I can delete at once in the settings menu up to 500 items (if possible, 50 can remain the default).  I'm willing to sacrifice a lag spike for a quick-delete of a lot of crap.- A couple more basic wall textures would be lovely at minimum.  I'd love to see some brick styles for that old industrial-age look.  Even better if we could also get some weathered overlays that go on top of textures like that so I could make my brick near my coal plant look sooty or make the steel bridge near the ocean look rusty...  In general more cosmetic stuff for factory-ing my factory for different industrial ages would be pretty neato.  Just don't turn into the Sims 4 and make me pay 15 bucks for each pack of crapola lol.- Official mod support should probably be a priority for this game.  It has an incredible community that I didn't even know existed, and official mod support would inject a longevity into this game that would be unmatched.  I can only imagine the Tekkit-like packs that would emerge over time with ever expanding tech trees and upgrades out the wazoo...  Those would be the glory days frfr.- The Zip-line tool needs tinkering IMO; I'd love it if I would actually go in the direction I was looking at and holding W towards when coming to an intersection in power-lines (which only seems to work when there is a designed even split), and you should be able to wrap around tighter corners than what is currently allowed.  This is the least of my complaints but still makes it on the list.  It would be sick as well if you could upgrade it for SPEED and LONG-DISTANCE ATTACHMENT later in the game to give it relevancy after you get the Hoverpack.  Perhaps you add zipline attachment upgrades to our legs to skate on top of power lines lol...- Please reduce the hard-drive completion time; that s**t is TEDIOUS for no apparent reason.  2-3 mins MAX.-

_childDocuments_.review: This is not an “Exciting” game, but more of a mind game.  Think Ark without so many things trying to kill you.  It’s a crafting game with exploration and a little combat thrown in to break things up.  It’s very pretty and kind of hard on a computer.I run a custom water loop (i9-9900k and RTX 2070) and this puts more strain on my system than MSFS 2020.  I run it at Ultra settings and expect it to scale down some for lighter built systems.  I think it has to do with the number of objects it can have in motion at any one time.  It’s still in development, so, I expect them to clean that up as it gets closer to final publication.  For me, this plays like solitaire.  I can easily waste hours wandering around my factories, developing new production strategies or exploring the wilds.  I’ve got 36 yours in in 4 days of play… that proves I'm complying with the Stay At Home Orders…  I just made it to the 3rd tier of the beginner’s map.  I feel that there is a lot of content, yet, I think the developers are still adding more.Exploring caves was interesting.  I wonder what kinds of biomes I have to play in and how big the maps are.  It does feel rather large.The biggest issue I have is that it is not a contiguous world, as I have found it.  Unless I’m on a huge mountain, there seems to be a world boundary that is simply a cliff.  These are Flat planets.  I truly hate that.

_childDocuments_.review: Warning: May Induce motion sickness  I wanted to like Satisfactory, so much.  It's been on my wish-list for ages, I was waiting for release.  Yet with all the updates I thought it must be at least playable.  Boy was I in for a shock.  Now, it's not all bad for about twenty minuets I loved it, but then the nausea settled in.  This was bizarre, I don't get motion sickness or sea sick or anything like that.  What sort of catastrophe have you created Coffee Stain Studios? This game is supper pre-alpha in terms of it's camera.  Heck most late 90s 3D games have smoother action then this.  Anytime I moved the mouse the screen would jitter horribly.  I tried adjusting the settings but nothing worked and after a few more minuets I was down right queasy.  I tried playing it without moving the mouse outside of menus but that got pointless real fast.   It's also sad that a game that's been in early assess for this long is so nonfunctional on such a basic level.Edit:  if you fuss with the settings a piece the camera does restrain itself better.  Will no chance or persistent pain the game is quite fun.  Though I do hope the finished version has a stable camera.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is amazing for the right player. If you can and like building your own story, you'll find it hard to close the game. Otherwise, do note that there's very little in terms of story or progression. There are tons of unlocks, but none of them feel essential or linear too much, which can be good if you like the freedom to do your own path of progression. Main gameplay loop is automating and optimizing your production to accumulate materials so that you could unlock better buildings to speed up the production even more. Think minecraft with  conveyer belts. For me it was 10/10, but I can see how it could be a complete miss for some people.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great. It's beyond great - it's borderline crack levels of addictive.Let me start by saying that multiplayer isn't a perfect experience. If you aren't the host then expect lag on enemies and driving amongst other gripes. I'm fairly confident that will be fixed before release though and it's not so gamebreaking that you wont still be able to have a great time building factories alongside your friends.Now that the bad stuff is out of the way let me get on to the positives of this game - namely, everything else. The world is extremely pretty and very diverse from end to end. Sometimes whilst exploring you'll find yourself just stopping to take in some of the staggering views around the world. The gameplay is inexplicably additive. This should be work.. you're a corporate slave to a giant company, tasked with setting up their pipeline of parts on this planet and yet the experience of doing so is so very relaxing you'll find yourself gladly doing it time and time again whenever a new part is needed. The process of building your factory then tearing it down and starting again because of a new ore, part, tool etc. and the thought process required to figure out how to best piece it all together is so addictive you'll find yourself thinking about it even when you finally exit the game about 2 hours before you need to be up for work.This is an exemplary game with a lot of potential for its full release. Even as an early access game I strongly recommend picking it up.Edit: A few more hours in now, still agree with the above.Edit 2: Yeah.. it's still great.

_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: Ever played a game and felt like "darn it, I just spent the price of a full release for what plays like an open beta"? Well, Satisfactory is here to make up for it, because this is quite the opposite case! It is allegedly early access, but it doesn't feel incomplete in the slightest. It's tons of fun to play, the mechanics feel well rounded and you are constantly given goals to work towards, but you can always choose to do your own thing and play around with the game mechanics, or just build beautiful stuff. And so far I've not encountered any significant bugs or performance issues.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: If you like building factories, whether it's mom's spaghetti or some contemporary art, this game is for you.If you like Factorio and thought "How difficult could it be in 3D anyway ?", this game is for you.If you need a heater during winter, this game is for you.If you love community mods, this game is for you.It's fun, it's addictive, and before you know it, you're b-deep in a multi-story building of interlinked production lines.So you decide to clean it up, make everything properly aligned, going minimalistic even.Then you realise you haven't slept in three days but it's alright, watching your perfectly aligned conveyers gives you some zen-like energy.But then, there's a power outage. Because who tf builds an entire factory with coal generators as their energy source anyway ?You devote your next days to building a perfect fuel generator setup that yields over 5GW with a single source of crude oil.You just keep doubling your factory size and adjusting your energy production accordingly.You finally get to the endgame after hundreds of hours of sweat and tears, most of it used to clean your sh*t.You feel proud of yourself. Right until you see your reflection in the mirror and ask yourself "At what cost ?"
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: The goal of the game is "only" about building a factory which was not really a selling point for me. At least in Space Engineers or Dual Universe it's about what you can build with the factory. The fun thing about Satisfactory is that you have to solve logistical issues and you have to explore a lot to find resources. Exploring is fun in this game and a huge selling point. Beautiful biomes! Scary critters! Lots of interesting things to find. Everything from wreckages with Tech to Alien artifacts. I'm super pleased with the progression and level of grind. Some things, like Tier Upgrades, take a lot of time. But you also have tier-independent upgrades which relies on you finding things out in the wild to unlock tech trees and that is adds a level of excitement and curiousity to the world. I miss having more statistical overview and better logistical control, but at the same time the game is more challenging without it. There are multiple scenarios with different challenges. Little/No water - well how do you power your stuff? Etc. I'm gonna try those out as well, but all in all. It's good for about 80 hours (includes a couple of real time nights of idling production)
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: Satisfactory is a highly engaging PC game that excels in both the small details and the grand scale. From the very beginning, the process of mining ores and setting up your first small production chains is incredibly satisfying. The gameplay loop is both addictive and rewarding, as you gradually expand from simple setups to massive megafactories that dominate the landscape.One of the game’s greatest strengths is how it perfectly balances complexity with accessibility. The intuitive design of the building and automation systems allows players to feel like engineering geniuses as they optimize their production lines. The progression feels natural, with each new milestone offering exciting new possibilities.The game’s open-world environment is also a highlight, offering vast, beautiful landscapes to explore and conquer. As you expand, the challenge of managing logistics and efficiency across sprawling factory networks keeps the gameplay fresh and interesting.In short, Satisfactory is a masterclass in sandbox game design, providing endless hours of fun as you build, optimize, and perfect your industrial empire. Everything in this game just clicks, making it a must-play for fans of resource management and factory-building games.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: 77 hours in and I’ve got to say... this game is tremendous. My spaghetti factory? It’s a masterpiece. I’ve got Iron Ingots, Steel Beams, Motors, and more flying out of the place 24/7. I’m even sending Smart Plating and Automated Wiring straight to space with my Space Elevator. It’s an intergalactic trade operation like no one’s ever seen.I’m automating production while I sleep—who knew building factories could be so addictive? Honestly, if you’re not playing Satisfactory yet, what are you even doing? Absolutely tremendous game. 10/10, would automate again.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: At first I didn't think this is a game for me personally but gave it a go after seeing positive reviews. You know the games you see dreams of and it keeps amazing you every day you play. You play and constantly forget what you were doing in the game and time passes by so fast. This is it.  Its superb! The guys who has made this map needs a raise. It just so beautiful to look at and roam around. Main boss has been so far that sound that informs your power is out and it nails your coffin with the breaker sound you desperately try to turn it on again aaaaand no! ffffkkk, once more... no! No power. I love it. Game is stable, crashed once and needed to google how to unstuck(just crouch), Hope they add way more monster variety and would love to see them adding bosses between tier upgrades. Not all the fps types, one who to race against, one to defeat by building, ones to shoot at?  Even at this stage its awesome and you should give it a go. Gl with keeping power up and water in pipes.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game. And I tried, repeatedly. Satisfactory gives you a HUGE and gorgeous landscape to play in, with mushroom-trees and cute little lizard-foxes, and tells you to produce goods with it. Mine, smelt, assemble, deliver. Improve production lines and maximise energy production ad infinitum.And for a while that was fun. Arranging my open-air factory, working out how to get my coal generators working, moving coal and iron from one base to another. And exploring! It felt really good to run off into the unknown, following a compass ping for undiscovered minerals and oil, then working out how to best use or transport them to get to the next tech tier. Travelling by foot starts slow but eventually you unlock a basic vehicle, and the 'blade runners' let you run across the world in what I can only call a less unreasonable pace. Still, I had fun cave diving and finding rare prizes to make my factory back at home base work faster, better, harder.But at one point, 25 hours in (and oh so slowly progressing towards developing oil-based power generation) it just... wasn't fun anymore. All the advice I found in the game and online about how to progress involved building big boxy factories, everything tightly regimented and as closely placed together as possible. Well fine, I COULD do the maths or follow a diagram but that's not a game. That's work! And it's not creative or beautiful anymore.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: I really love this game!  I love how it gives some direction and goals, but there is so much freedom on how to achieve those goals.  As I learn new technologies and techniques, I have found myself rebuilding sections of my  factory over and over, just to "do it better this time".   Because there is no loss in resources to do this, I only find that to be a positive experience.   This may be an early access game, but the quality is very high.  There are some bugs yes, but nothing I've found has been game breaking.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing love just sinking a few hours in every week it gets more and more complex as you go in and yet somehow easier, if you do end up getting this game understand the first phase of the game is a hill you have to cross and once power can be automated the game opens up a lot more. The changes in 1.0 hugely improve the game for new players and with the story being so in the background its really hard to have it spoiled for you. If your a fan of factory management and a game that is gonna somewhat test your planing ability its a must buy.

_childDocuments_.review: I hardly write reviews but this time I feel like I should contribute. This game is great. I hardly play other factory games, but this one is addictive. _childDocuments_.review: I still remember the first time I descended upon this planet. This alien place, ripe for exploitation. It's recources available for me to aquire and send off planet as the Company commanded. It was overwhelming at first, even the few recources and few machines that I had to manage seemed too much, but I got used to them, I designed the production lines necessary to complete my orders. I explored the area around me, felt home in its once alien valleys. The spark of progress within me grew brighter as I started constructing more complex parts, one goal in my mind controlled all thought. To complete the orders of the Company. And I did. I expanded, forged what was asked, turned the area I lived in into a large mass of belts and machines.As I sent the latest order upon the sky, I felt proud with my achievements. But that feeling soon vanished. As I received more orders, more materials, more complexity. It was at that time that I explored beyond the valley that had housed me, and saw the horrific size of the areas that surrounded me. What I had conquered was but a tiny part of a thing I did not comprehend. I was lost for days, unable to get back to what I considered home in this alien place. I faced terrors and hardships I thought this planet could not harbour, and my body could not survive.As I finally returned back to the familiar valley I realised something. The reason why I was here. It was not the Company or the orders, the materials that were constantly required of me. It was the spark of progress that had ignited the flames of domination within me. I see now that I crave the endless expansion, the conquering of the natural world around me. To see the green fields turn to metal...And suddenly the Factory spoke to me.There is only one thing to do now.I shall strip this planet bare, I will construct all that is possible, I will dominate the cliffs, the deserts, the seas. I will drain its recources and forge upon its rotten corpse a technological wonder. I shall feed this planet to the Factory, I shall help It grow, until It touches every corner of this place. Until Its sweet voice is echoed endlessly.I am the Factory, the Factory is me.I shall grow.The factory shall grow.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely an amazing game. Bugs out after 2 players and have had one crash from a player joining BUT amazing game.Cons:0. You can't remove nuclear waste... if only you had some kind of space type elevator device that could take the stuff into space... HHHHMMMMM1. Crafting appears to be well thought out, however they let you make a bunch of items that you no longer need in the game after finishing all the unlockable items.2. They have collectibles in a game with a map that has edges that instadeath you and make the items unobtainable.3. Easy to grief players by going and obtaining hard-drives and suiciding off of cliffs permanently disabling alternative recipes.4. The Space Elevator hit box is WELL above its cage that shoots up so if you go to land on it, you die by landing on nothing.5. The sky is a static PoS and the moon doesn't rotate its a static image... Need to use a "Boundless" approach when the rest of the game is this pretty.6. The default graphics at max are crap... to make the game pretty, you must hit "Ctrl+Shift+L" and hit ~ and type the commands for grass/stones and up it to 20 so it doesn't look like poop.7. When developing the world, they didn't create any predefined roads for vehicles, rendering them useless for travel.8. Vehicles are unlocked too late and literally aren't useful compared to conveyor belts, and they move SLOWER than the player... -_- what???9. Trains again unlocked too late and useless compared to conveyor belts... Highly recommend the developers follow the Big O methodology when developing the game.A good way to nerf conveyors is to simply make them cost energy and the longer they run the more diminishing returns they give on speed when long running conveyors with the ability to give them upgrade slugs to speed them up a little.After that, they need to give vehicles a rocket league type flight mechanic to make it over this crazy terrain 10. The guns are too weak... I have unlimited craftable ammo with 10 round clips and its too little. I would recommend upping the stacks from 10 to 100 and the ammo clips from 10 to 100. Ironic that this is problem number 10. The power is weak and its easily fixed by just letting it spam a little more with A LOT less reloads and maybe introducing it sooner as it feels kind of crap that the blade is FAR better in every aspect and is cheaper, and introduced sooner.11. No massive bosses to fight and the massive animals are passive or in the flying guys case, literally unkillable killed which breaks the immersion.12. No survival mode where enemies build bases and attack you the bigger you get like Factorio. Could be added after alpha.13. The space station is introduced too soon.14. Parts of map has zero development which takes 20 seconds to add even in an alpha so players can and want to build anywhere.15. Liquids which can really be worked on by a 4th player is introduced kind of late making the structure kind of messed up. One player works on unlocks and energy, one player hunts for slugs, one players works on factory and building, and one player works on water/oil production.16. Summersloop/Alien Orb, when picked up mutes audio in the area it was in as if its still there. 17. Multiplayer is pretty broken for anyone outside of a host even on the best network such as myself. Anyone outside of the host can equip and unequip jetpack for infinite fuel. Players other than host can't drive vehicles.18. No enclosed conveyor option to reduce frame cost by reducing item movement load on cpu's. 19. Can't swim under water... -_- what??? This is 2020... get on this.20. No weather. Should at least be an option for such a pretty map.21. Crafting doesn't lead up to anything good for progression in the world serving no purpose unlike satisfactory which is to fight to expand later on.22. Can't do the naruto jutsu on demand... :/ Its amazing when it happens to you but if nobody believes you did it... then it sucks for multiplayer... have some emote code that does it on command.23. Nerf the man cannon glitch... -_- its broken that I can send myself across the entire game in less than a minute by stacking tube entrances... the fix for this is pretty simple, drop the speed of the player to nothing once exiting the tube to remove all momentum.24. Bombs don't cause A.I to rag doll and do almost no damage making it feel like they do nothing and it takes 6 bombs to kill a big enemy... I mean it looks amazing to place it on rocks and watch them explode all over... but it looks like crap when you throw it on an enemy or person and it explodes and does nothing... breaks immersion very badly.25. Node scanner is TOO SHORT... it's frustrating to PING see it, go for 15 seconds in the direction and PING again... and again... and again... and again....... and again......... up that to 5 minutes up from 15 seconds. 26. No second clothing slot for exo-suit and jetpack or exo-suit and radiation suit. Makes kind of no sense as the EXO-suit is EXO as in OUTSIDE of the clothing on the body... and the jetpack is also OUTSIDE the clothing of the body and has no interaction with the exo suit... in a game of LOGIC... please use some... add this in the next patch... 27. You should start with a chainsaw and it should run on leaves... -_- my entire group got stuck in a tree glitch which forced us to suicide, as the rag doll console command doesn't work forcing us to lose all progress until we got everything back after an hour of travel with no exo-suit and 3 health. Dumbest crap I have EVER seen in a game... I almost didn't recommend the game because of this game breaking glitch... Death should also start you back at half health up from 3... regen at 3 is fine. Nobody is going to suicide at base to get 2 health back health and if they did... who cares... they are at base... 2 health won't make or break the game but it will make travel with nothing a little less punishing.28. Launch pads need a buff and landing pads need to be larger in diameter.29. Need to allow players whom aren't host save the game locally so they can continue it while you are offline as to not hold everybody up when the host can't play. Just throw a warning when joining the same save seed, that hey your time stamp is a little older, save their save over yours and continue?PROS that need little tweaks:1. THICK crafting almost to the point where you get sick of it, but no reason for doing it outside of building. (Good for builders, bad for explorers) Have an occasional alian invasion that comes down from space and introduce some factory weaponry that can help with waves to protect the base. We need more from the thick crafting.2. Pretty game (with options upped manually through console)3. Enemies that currently exist are well developed, have smart A.I most times and will make you work to survive. (Just not enough big boys and weapons to make it eventful)4. Machines work as intended and base building works as intended.5. Where nodes are currently placed are perfect (Just needs the world a little more flushed out for bare spots)6. Vehicles drive well for main host (just not other players) just need temporary flying capabilities like the tank from Starfox 647. The flow of progression of crafting is very well done. They only have a few mistakes like unlocking silica early on at tier 4 when you don't use it until tier 7/8 and the ticket system which causes players to blow tickets on trash items for progression not noticing it increases in cost each time making it harder to get tickets later on when you need it for cosmetics.8. The art style of items is crazy well done and optimized.9. The fuel progression is really well done but a A.I in our head that warns us when we are approaching the max energy load would be nice. Kind of sucks when you walk away to explore and come back with everything stopped because you didn't know it was going to blow... :/8/10 Would pay $30 again.

_childDocuments_.review: I have played this game since very early on in development. The amount of improvements and implemented feedback these developers have done is impressive. Building up after each milestone, expanding upon your existing infrastructure, attempting to improve your lasting infrastructure to keep up with the needs of higher tiers of construction, starting in one of the starting zones and slowing expanding outward until finally you have a network of trains and drones expanding the entirety of the map. Its just lovely. I give this bad mo f'er a highly recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: Progression can be addictive.  I especially like that the resource nodes do not diminish.  There have been some occasional frustrations with devices not working as intended.  The problem with this is that it can become time consuming trying to determine whether something is glitched or if I built something incorrectly.  Overall, for being early access it feels completely finished to me.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. Took a little time and some youtube to really get going when I started playing in update 8 because this is different from other games I have played. Once I got the hang of it, I was hooked. This game has endless playability because there are so many ways to accomplish a single task. It really allows you to be creative within factory building, base building, or both. Exploration of the world is amazing. I was initially concerned about the map being limited, but after over 200 hours I still haven't explored it all or ran out of projects to complete. I'm sure there are still some bugs here and there, but overall it seems to perform exactly as intended and expected. I haven't encountered anything worthy of note on that front since updating to 1.0.

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible value proposition - a reasonably priced game that ensures hundreds of hours of playability. The graphics / biomes are nicely crafted and make this game very relaxing, yet challenging. The entire set of production chains is very well thought-out. How rather satisfying it can be to harvest and store huge amounts of infinite resources - only to have later game stages deplete such stock in a heart beat.  It's a game you can come back to multiple times, complete the entire technology tree yet again while getting consumed by building structures of any kind. I personally spent over 200 hrs constructing a renovated soccer stadium " Camp Nou".........just because I could.......... In my next run through I might just build the Great Wall of China. It is just fun!

_childDocuments_.review: Did you like factorio, but wish you could get TRULY deep into making a factory in layers? look no further, satisfactory is factorio, but for people you aren't train geniuses. no sir-y, no complicated network of train stops, crossings, intersections and so, so so many deaths at the hands of a train that sped by so fast it was on screen for all of 10 framesinstead, welcome to the hell of optimizing everything, as you work within the confines of a limited number of unlimited resources (it makes sense, trust me). embark on a journey, as you scour the lands for enough iron ore to feed your factories growing demand for plates, rods and screws... by god the screws.however, when you have completed the journey you understand that you have completed a task, a monumental one.

_childDocuments_.review: I have reccomended it already. My 10 year old son insisted we buy Satisfactory and he now has to kick me off of the computer, I thought my gaming days were over. What I like about this game is that it has influences of all the great classic and modern games. While there's plenty of fps action, what's engaging about this game is the thought that has to go into design of your factories and there's plenty of room for different approaches, so there's a creative aspect to balance out the classic shooting scenario. I have it turned off for now because it gets repetitive like listening to telephone hold music in the states. _childDocuments_.review: I hit the 40 years of age mark, and I've thought a lot about how games used to be more immersive and enjoyable in my younger years.It's not unusual for me to try a highly praised game and get bored after an hour or two. Bought this, tried it out. The first night I stayed up to 6am and went to bed only so my girlfriend wouldn't realize how long I had stayed up. I dreamt of factories.Then the next day I pretty much ignored her and continued to optimize and build factories. Then I stayed up and continued playing until 6am again. At some point I'll install the game again and lie to her about working long hours, but until then all I have to say is that it got more out of me in a week than almost any other game has in years. For the cost to entertainment factor it's already passed it, and it's early access. Crazy.

_childDocuments_.review: Picture this: You're happily exploring the map to pick up items you need for your factory to be more efficient and streamlined. Hopping and parachuting your way around, snatching up items while avoiding the pesky enemies trying to stop you. You spot a mercer sphere guarded by a couple of big hogs you land directly on top of it and snatch it before they can do anything, over the hill is a slug with a few hatchers, you fly right in the middle and boombox blast the annoying fly's away, grab the slug and bounce off into the distance.Suckers!Then you hear it... The noise. Your throat tightens a little, your skins starts crawling, your body involuntarily shudders and without looking you RUN! You hear a thump right behind you but you don't dare turn back to look, it's on you and you know it, the noises continue, a guttural shriek and then the sound of its legs skittering along the floor. You find a small hill and scale it. Whipping out your trusty rebar gun, you slot a rebar in the hole, pull back the hammer, grit your teeth... and you turn. There it is, in all its unholy glory, an 8 legging green monstrosity twice as tall as you and 10x as mean, dripping poison from its gigantic fangs and moving at an unnatural speed for its size. It's disgusting, angry... And terrifying. It's readying itself to jump, you have 2 or 3 seconds before its on top of you, so you fire you rebar and it thuds home. It launches at you and you gracefully sidestep it as you reload, the next rebar slams into it chitinous hide, it moves so fast you barely have time to react and its huge front legs smash into you throwing you backwards. One more hit and it'll be feasting on your corpse so you scramble away as it keeps... making... the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥... NOISE! You can't shake it, it's too quick and it can jump too high you're peppering it with rebars when you can but you're mostly just running for your life.Then you see it, your saviour, the most beautiful thing you've ever seen in your life, a gigantic green grey rock with tusks sticking out, stink lines of radiation streaming off it like some transcendent angel emerging from a sewer... A nuclear hog. You launch yourself in its direction and pull your parachute string gliding slowly... too slowly towards your new best friend, the stinger senses your mistake and launches itself gleefully into the air to claim its meal. It's flying straight at you, its fangs glistening, your death in green techno colour, its millimetres away... and you drop the chute. As you plummet to the ground below the stinger flies straight over your head in the space you just occupied and finds itself staring directly at its death. The nuclear hog really dislikes anything being in its personal space, let alone its natural enemy the stinger, it turns its massive frame slowly and carefully, faces the stinger and then charges. It's so fast you can barely track it, the stinger who mere seconds ago seemed like an unkillable death machine, it makes the noise which seems kind of sad and pathetic now that you both realise its true place on the food chain, the real king of the ring has shown up, the true alpha predator. In a last ditch attempt to save itself it releases a cloud of noxious gas, that inadvertently leaves it a sitting duck for the 10 tonne slab of meat muscle and tusks to turn it into stinger paste. The stinger dead the hog goes back to doing what it did before, sitting around looking real menacing and minding it's own ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ business.You snatch up the stinger remains and give its corpse another rebar for good measure and off you go back to peacefully  collecting more stuff.This is a great horror game and it ads a few interesting things to the genre, namely a weird factory building portion that seems a bit out of place but is super engaging and fun. Would recommend any horror game fans to give it a go.♥♥♥♥ that noise though, seriously.

_childDocuments_.review: 9 hrs - Multiplayer can be a little rough, just be sure to set the network quality to "ultra". Other than that, the gameplay is great, and progression is nearly constant. Performance is solid.33 hrs - Performance:I've progressed through most of the game and have a substantially large factory. Starting out, as well as being away from the main factory, the framerate is a solid 144 (vsynced to the monitor's refresh rate). As the factory got bigger, the game performance slowed down roughly 50%, leaving an average fps of 70 - 90. I've also seen frame drops below 30 fps. I am not GPU bound with my rx 5700 xt, with its usage is around 60%. As far as RAM goes, I'm on 2 x 8 GB 2000 MHz DDR3, and as long as you have at least 8 you should be fine. This leads me to believe that the game is very CPU intensive later on into the game's progression. I have a i7 4770K OCed to 4.8 GHz. Looking at the usage, it seems that the game hits all cores at times. Having a higher core count CPU would help the experience. That said, the game remains responsive even when frames drop. Placing long belt runs or resetting the fuse on the power grid doesn't lag the game. The lower fps only happens when large amounts of resources are on the screen, so covering all the belts with platforms or just walking away from the factory boosts fps by quite a bit. This is also with quality maxed out, and the screenspace reflections and lighting are very pleasing. More games should look this good.Multiplayer:As far as multiplayer implementations go, Satisfactory is pretty good. The "Network Quality" option should be set on by default, as any other setting leads to frequent "rubber banding" and death to invisible enemies. It pissed me off actually. But once you apply the change and restart the game session, non-hosting players can actually see where other players are and the term "here" actually means something. Multiplayer still isn't glitch-free. One such example is the ability for non-hosts to reset their jetpack full by switching off the jetpack and then switching back. The host has to unlock the ability to refuel the jetpack. Vehicles are completely unusable to non-hosts as well, and hypertubes can exaggerate the multiplayer effects. Another thing is that hazards like enemies, radiation, and poison can not be visible to some players, causing them to take damage unexpectedly. This only killed me twice. The latency makes fighting enemies quite difficult, so I stuck to building the factory and fixing the power grid. Here the latency doesn't matter that much so I really enjoyed myself. And factory building is the core mechanic of the game, so that is what makes the multiplayer good. How can I describe the multiplayer quality? It's better than Space Engineers in terms of latency, and way better than Scrap Mechanic in terms of glitchyness. It is about equal to Astroneer and Trove, but it could be improved still.Gameplay:It's 3D Factorio. You collect both infinite and finite resources throughout a large but limited world. Raw infinite resources are smelted, constructed, assembled, and/or manufactured into components that are used either to build or meet milestones / send into the space elevator. Finite resources include the remains of aliens, various foods, and other special items found throughout the world (no spoilers). You build a big factory (or a couple) and progress to make every item in the game. You can make vehicles, hunt for interesting items, and construct weapons. Although food exists, it only is used to heal you and not as a requirement for survival (currently). Water is only used in the factory to create things. You can die from the following: fall damage, aliens attacking, poison gas, radiation, going too high (space), and leaving the map, falling into the abyss. Swimming underwater doesn't and can't kill you. Vehicles are pretty useless because the terrain is too rough. Trains come too late in the game and are less efficient than just straight mile long conveyor belts because they use power and conveyor belts don't. If conveyor belts used exponentially more power as they got longer, trains and vehicles would make sense. As far as wheeled vehicles, they should be given the ability to jump up off the ground and maybe be able to ram enemies to death. Currently, they vehicles are outclassed by using a jetpack or bladerunners. The game is still being fleshed out, but nevertheless the game is addicting af. Like playing it for 6 hours straight addicting. And then dreaming about it.Some problems include (most of which are caused by multiplayer):Falling through the map (rare)Getting stuck in a hypertube (moderate)Getting surprised by teleporting aliens and poison gas (common)Not being able to place a building in a specific spot for no apparent reason (rare)Not seeing the correct position of another player (rare w/ network on ultra, common w/ out)Being able to place conveyors and that travel through the ground (on purpose)Vehicles misbehaving, like jumping and being unresponsive (only happens with non-host)Host crashing on player connect (rare)Client crashes in general (rare)rare being that problem happened once or twicemoderate being that problem happened a few timescommon being that problem happened oftenVerdict:For the thirty bucks I purchased the game for, I'm very happy with the game. It is early access, but I am seeing regular updates from the devs and pretty nice improvements. If you plan on playing by yourself, the game doesn't feel like it is an early access game. However, in multiplayer, the game can feel inconsistent. The performance is better than expected on the GPU side, however a strong CPU may be necessary. The gameplay is addicting and the visuals are what more games in 2020 should strive to be.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DRSatisfactory is a decent very casual factory game, but focuses more on the building aspect whereas the complexity/depth of automation/factory management is incredibly shallow/basic. If not for mods adding a bit more complexity, this would get boring for me very quickly. If you are looking for relaxing factory-flavored sandbox, this is it. If you are looking for a nice, in depth complex factory game, this is definitely not it.Satisfactory is a very good game that scratches that automation puzzle itch. Beautiful graphics, non-complexity make it a very chill game. As a base platform it has potential, and if it weren't for mods/the modding community, I'm not sure I'd be giving it a thumbs up. While it is very satisfying to build large factories and the logistics of them, the game is really, really simple/shallow. 90% of it is spamming the same 4-5 machines over, and over, and over again. If you are really into building pretty, you'll get that here for sure. But complexity and depth? Not really. It's more of a puzzle than a challenge and I think that's the aim of CSS, to make the game as casual as possible to appeal to a wider audience and generate more revenue as expected.If you are craving a bit more, mods like Satisfactory Plus really amplify the basic base game a lot more. The simple core remains, but at least it becomes convoluted enough to actually challenge your brain a bit.The building aspect is where it truly shines. Building is mostly painless, with many QoL features to your advantage to create large builds in mere minutes. Deconstructing refunds all materials which makes early game building completely forgiving. The blueprint system, while not perfect, helps too.Honestly, the pros outweigh the cons. But I won't lie if I'm not just a bit disappointed that certain things didn't make it to 1.0, and that the core of the game remained simplistic for something that stayed 5 years in Early Access. But I suppose they aren't a big experienced dev team either and they did do Early Access the right way so, all in all, thumbs up.
