_childDocuments_.review: [1h]Starting out[/h1]So this will be a guide, and as you can figure out, it will be some what of a spoiler, so you are forewarned!Starting out can be confusing. The first thing you'd want to do is increase your motor skills, which can be done by picking up various items and examining them, which also levels up your sense. The starting point will be different for different people, specifically me, I was attacked by a large tiger-ancestor, and due to me waiting for the load, I was not able to do the dodge rolls.Surviving through sleeping, eating, and drinking water all allow for you to build up your neural pathways, because it refines your abilities. Among basic needs, you also may need to stay warm, and no wet. Its pretty easy, our ancestors have fur unlike us, which protects them from the mild cases, however if you become severely cold kath, a medicinal plant found in the world, allows for upkeep in warmth, and some for protection against getting wounded, it does not cure being wounded!From fall, to getting hit. Wounds happen, to cure them fairly annoying and easy. First, you lose health from your wounds, so its suggested not to wait on it, or switch to a clanmate who isn't wounded, and get the medicine through them. Its best to climb to a high place so you can search through the trees, and you'll find fibers in the trees, which your ancestors use to bind up their wounds. You should carry them to your home for your hurt clansmate to seal their wound, and hell it could help in the future, so stock up! The game is something of a survival rpg, in my opinion. You level your individuals by most successfully carrying your baby generation as you complete various tasks. You pick up an item, and sniff it, baby gives you neurons to use for leveling. You eat, drink, or scream at your family, your little chimping baby cradled against you has learned something, and grants you more leveling essence. Now when you finally do get this neuron capacity to level up a certain task, you find a sleeping spot, which you can make, unless your starting point already has one set up. The level screen is called evolution. In this screen you can choose to level, go to the next generation, or the whole damn species ladder. The more individual level is what we want to start with. Leveling the motor skills will allow for the most success.This is largely the backbone of the game, which you can actually use a bone as a weapon. I killed my first warthog ancestor and started using its tusk to bash other animals' heads in. It is exciting! Though we need to start at the beginning, which until you level your motor skill, you wont be able to do. Your most easiest to craft item is sharpened sticks, rocks broken down to make certain tools, beds, walls, and messing with coconuts when you find em. : First you must locate these gathering locations, go in and open your intelligence sensory. You'll focus on a dead tree, which tells you a quick tooltip about the focus. You then approach that focus, and analyze it. This begins the crafting process. You can now pluck dead tree sticks off of a dead tree. from there when you activate the motor function, switch the stick to the other hand and can start interaction with it. I find it easiest to strip the stick without a rock, but you can strip dead sticks with rocks and your bare hand. After that you gain a regular stick. This point you need a rock, which will sharpen the stick. You can choose this as a weapon, gathering tool, and the such.Rocks are useful, especially the basalt. They all have their own practicality. Basalt, changes how quickly you sharpen a stick or item. Granite Grinders allow for medicinal items to be made. The rocks can also be used to defend yourself.So the construction system is truly lackluster. You may become disappointed quite easily late game when you want to have some mighty fortress of sticks, or something. Anyhow, Its pretty simple to make a construction. You place enough of the same item into a stack, and when you place enough the construct tooltip comes up for available options. Now, if I remember right, the original amounts for these constructions are as followed:  = 4 Cycads bushes  = 4 dead tree stick, that has not been turned into a regular stick. So when you make a decent bed and area you want to live at, you will have the option to make that area your settlement. Take your clan to the new settlement by using the unlocked communication neuron, and then to get them to stop following you, end the exploration, which is found at the sleeping spot you newly made. This will make your clan settle at the new location.So you made a settlement and find it boring to see your clan standing around. Well, time to introduce the bonding system, real easy to grasp, no motor skill needed. You begin by grooming a chosen member of the opposite sex, and after that you become bonded to that clanmate. You can groom others of the same sex, but it doesn't really offer much towards the grand scheme of things. I guess you make a friend from it. When you obtain your mate, go back to your sleeping spot and do the action to call for your mate, and pregnant them, or become pregnant. Then after a cut scene you will have a giving birth option with no respectable time span. You can choose to immediately give birth, the time frame will skip the months ahead, and time passes as well. After sometime the scenes become repetitive. I would recommend skipping them, or watch em if you really enjoy the whole scenery. I got tired of the cut scenes of the discoveries of new areas.So I mentioned new areas, so lets hit up that beckon of joy. You of course have the starting area. Though you can expand past that, of course. These areas function as their own ecosystem. There will be birds, snakes, hogs, felines, and the such trying to kill you! So be ready for that when you come across a new place. Each of these places give you the action to face your fear, which is what happens when you turn and scream at the evil trying to stalk and kill you. Facing your fear expands your home space, which allows you to make the settlements.So after two days of dodging and get mad. I didn't understand how the combat worked at all. I had to actually watch a video on it. You can choose to avoid, dodge, or counter attack your predators. Boy once you get it down though, its fun as hell beat the creatures that made you so annoyed. I chased down a huge snake till my man knock the brains out. In the beginning though, what can you do against any of those things, avoiding. Its a powerful strategy. You can actually make these creatures fight themselves! I led a panther into a snake, and watched the thing kill it in two strokes. Made me feel like a giddy ol' master mind. So you're probably wondering, how do I counter attack and dodge. Real easy, depending on your gaming set up. The computer has visual and a musical que on when you do your action. So when a predator tries to attack you, you have about two seconds to react. You hold down the action button, and then choose which way you want to react. Depending on where you react towards, you will dodge, or counter attack. If you react any way, but towards the attacking party you dodge. When you react towards your predator, you counter attack. To put this into perspective though, I have a software that slows my game down to half-time, and I perfectly hit the que for the counter attack priming visual and musical que. I still became wounded. Its chance related, which can be in your favor the more you develop it, in the neural pathing leveling system.That is all I can think of right now, but if I can find anything else I'll be sure to add it.

_childDocuments_.review: The behavior that you exhibited was ape-like, the ape jumped out.This game unlocks the primitive little goblin instincts from the deep recesses of your brain in the most pleasant of ways. Some of the monkey moments I've had so far, in order:- Accidental lesbianism. Ended up losing most of my clan and was trying to repopulate, couldn't get my mate pregnant. Finally paused and saw on the menu that the ape I was controlling was also female. Love that for them.- Said "Oh my god, did you steal my stick?" aloud at a fellow clan member, genuinely felt rising anger, then found my stick on the ground nearby. Realised I needed to take a break.- Spent a lot of time collecting rocks and putting them in piles.- The rush of power once you successfully start countering predators and shedding serious blood is The Human ExperienceTo those who think the games mechanics ruin it or get in the way, I'd simply say... it's okay to not like a game. I think this kind of gameplay and control scheme tickles a very specific part of the brain that some people adore and some people don't get at all. I think that the controls (using a PS4 controller) are perfect for the intention. Once you learn it, it's second nature. That's why you can turn the interface off. Imo, if it still feels janky you haven't learnt it. I'd also like to say that a game not rewarding you for playing your own way is not the same thing as a game punishing you for doing so. There is definitely a chain of events the game wants you to follow, but you can do your own thing. Take your time. Get attached to your hominid (and hurt about it later), explore, fail, start over. You can have fun and not make progress, and not making progress isn't a game having a vendetta out against your playstyle. ((((But rushing / misunderstanding game mechanics is not a playstyle.))))ps. My first playthrough of this game was not on Steam, but it sure wasn't on Epic either. Glad to have somewhere to finally support the game. Down with this new trend of games being paid off and held for ransom, I have enough game launchers on my PC.

_childDocuments_.review: When only 80% of players have achieved the basic milestone of playing the game, it raises concerns about the overall experience. This title was gifted to me, prompting reflections on the appropriateness of maintaining a wishlist for games I am skeptical about, given the disappointment that followed.Initial impressions within the first 30 minutes of gameplay were marked by several issues:    The startup features full-blast music, a common but significant pet peeve among players. Prioritizing sound options as the first menu upon startup could alleviate this concern.    The inability to skip the intro, coupled with the controller becoming unresponsive after alt-tabbing, presented an unnecessary hindrance to the overall experience.    Despite being touted as best experienced with a controller, inconsistent functionality raised questions about the game's programming in comparison to other controller-supported titles.    Attempting to explore the supposedly "free world" resulted in random deaths due to unclear starting locations and insufficient guidance on initial objectives.    Completing the full tutorial proved to be an exercise in frustration, as the tutorials were both unhelpful and persistent, obstructing a significant portion of the screen and hindering visibility of objectives.In summary, the game has left me confused and dissatisfied. While a refund may be warranted, the absence of this option for gifted games raises questions about the overall customer experience. With improvements and input from competent game designers, the potential for a great game is evident, but the current execution falls short of expectations.

_childDocuments_.review: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey is a game about 10 million years evolution of humans where you'd start with discovering basic interactions and exploration. It's an interesting and unique concept with lots of cool features and ideas. Then you'd be able to kill a sabertooth tiger with a stick and chop him with a meteorite stone at some point. Cool stuff. It's a great game if you're into crafting/survival and trial and error gameplay doesn't scare you. However, there's 2 major gameplay issues that could be more or less obvious depending on your playstyle and luck. Freedom of what to do and where to go is an illusion here. I had to abandon my 6 hours playthrough because I became  the last monkey in the jungle and new ones didn't spawn (I've checked almost the whole map). This was reported a year ago (one year beta-test wasn't enough) as I've checked forums and many people had this issue but it happened. When I encountered the same problem for a second time then I decided to only follow "the orders" (there's something like a super weird quest order tab but only to some point). So I don't really believe that any playthrough here will be unique.Even if you'd be lucky enough to not end up in a situation when you'd have to abandon your 6 hours save - you'd still experience a lot of annoying/frustrating mechanics with clunky controls. I'm not talking about things that are here for immersion, only about poor adaptation to mouse + keyboard and non-intuitive mechanics. There's nothing challenging in this game. I've never had this feeling during 70 hours in Death Stranding on max difficulty while I was constantly annoyed in Ancestors and wasn't able to get used to some things even after 10 hours in the game. All in all, Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey is a fun and unique game - I'm mostly enjoying it so far. At the same time this game may heavily disappoint you if you're not ready to google what to do in a certain situation and if you're not ready to follow in-game instructions to a certain point, because as a "sandbox" experience it doesn't work too well while "trial and error" method may end up in a completely lost progression. This is a first game where I had to backup saves and it's definitely not adding up any fun. 8/10 for the game itself and 3/10 for poorly implemented mechanics.
_childDocuments_.name: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a conventional game with combat and experience points and a static hero or party, this is not that. Instead, this is a much deeper and more meaningful experience, a journey that spans generations.As your homonid clan learns and evolves, you'll be quite pleased with how even the simplest change in your abilities, such as holding an item in each hand, can dramatically alter the flow of the game and your clan's survival. The rocks you once used to bash in the skulls of snakes can be made into tools for improving food and medicine, or sharpening sticks as weapons. Your advancements in language will allow you to give commands to the whole tribe, allowing you to stockpile resources or treat individual wounds.The game is, by design, not going to hold your hand. It's up to you to learn how to navigate the jungle with all its dangers and resources. You WILL lose clan members, at least a few from falling accidents as you avoid the forest floor jumping between trees. You'll also learn the value of safety in numbers and ingenuity.And after a few discoveries, you'll appreciate what it means to be human, with all of our intelligence and complexity.

_childDocuments_.review: After reading the reviews, I bought this game suspecting it would be a glorified meme at best, expecting to lose interest after the first ten minutes. Instead I have developed a mild addiction.The game is not easy at a first glance, but it does have a comprehensive tutorial and yes, you should switch on both it and the full HUD the first time you play. With both enabled, it doesn't take long to get a basic grasp on the controls and general gameplay, to the point where you won't get slaughtered by everything that moves and the occasional poisonous shrubbery. While there are a few things which can remain frustrating, particularly the AI of your fellow clan members, they are only mild inconveniences, and serve the game's overall aim of giving that sense of discovery and evolution in keeping with its theme. I did occasionally resort to a guide when I needed just a slight nudge in the right direction, but hey, we evolved through communicating our ideas and discoveries, so why not?Once settled in, the addiction comes from the balance of tense exploration into the unknown and peaceful, almost therapeutic moments recovering at your settlement. Some people may find this loop repetitive, especially in the mid-sections, but personally I found it rewarding and relaxing in equal parts. The hominids you play as are oddly engaging - when I lost an adult ape to a bird and the two babies accompanying her promptly got themselves stuck in the middle of a stampede, not only was it a solid recreation of The Lion King, but it was a genuinely stressful moment.The game promises not to hold your hand and occasionally becomes a little too obtuse as a result, but ultimately it rewards those who stick with it and is well worth a shot if the premise appeals to you.

_childDocuments_.review: Let's start by saying that Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey really, really doesn't try to be likeable when you launch it for the first time. As the devs say in the intro, they won't help you much, and it's quite likely that your first few hours of playing are gonna be... tedious. Heck, the tutorial section is absolutely (and probably willingly) confusing, and the controls aren't really easy to understand at first.But the magic of it all is that, in this very case, it all makes absolute sense thematically. You're here to explore, try new things, learn and, ultimately, die after passing on your knowledge to your child. If you manage to get past the initial confusion, you'll find yourself in a weird mix or roguelite/survival/exploration game, where you play as a small tribe of monkeys (or, more precisely, homininians), who are weak, scared of the unknown, and pretty much at the bottom of the food chain.Pretty much everything you do will make your monkeys improve. First by unlocking new neurons (ie. skills) in a pretty huge skill tree. For example, crafting a lot of tools will unlock a neuron to make crafting easier and faster. To activate this neuron, you'll need neuronal energy (ie. XP), which is gathered by carrying children on your back while you do stuff.Long story short: you'll quickly learn ways to make survival a bit easier, and to handle the various threats nature will throw at you. By exploring and just playing the game, you'll unlock evolution feats, which in turns will let you advance time, and replace your monkeys with other (more capable and more recent) subspecies of homoninae. The game, which include various biomes, ends when you make the jump to the Ho-mo (gg Steam for censoring this word...) genus.I personnally enjoyed every bit of Ancestors, which is filled with interesting things to discover and explore, in a trully amazing and beautiful world. And I think the game did a great job of linking its theme and its gameplay. I hope there's a sequel in the work.That being said, the game was sometimes a bit repetitive, as it goes through many gameplay loops that aren't necessarily interesting (but can be automated later on, as you unlock more neurons). For example, you gotta reproduce everytime you jump to a new generation, and that can take up to a few minutes. You gotta craft always the same stuff before you start an expedition, etc. You gotta feed your monkeys because they sometimes won't do it by themselves...I also think the difficulty balance was a bit odd. The game can be quite daunting early on, but the difficulty quickly drops. It's part of the theme, I know, but the fact that you can learn how to craft the best weapon really early on doesn't help. Once you've found it, you immediately find yourself at the top of the food chain and only ever get really threatened when you overextend or play recklessly.

_childDocuments_.review: A real shame, I was looking forward to this game, but it's really not fun to play and I honestly have no clue what I'm meant to be doing!There is a 'tutorial' but it is negligible, and the controls are far to complex for the game its trying to be.  You need to use your 'senses' to look at, listen to or even smell(!) a thing; be that thing another ape, a stone or a blade of grass before you can even interact with it.  Its way too complex for the game it's trying to be. It DOES work with a controller or mouse and keyboard, but it is very unintuitive.(one example of this would be “jumping”.  You “jump” by releasing the same button you hold to “run”! So, to stop “running”, you need let go of the Dpad (or W key) first, and then the run button or you’ll fling your generic, identikit-ape, off a cliff or into a tree! Or into the path of terribly modelled and animated sabre tooth tiger).Considering this game came out in august 2020, it looks at least ten years older!  Sure the lighting looks nice but models, animation and textures are very under par.It gives a whole cheep feel and look to the over all experience. Sure graphics aren’t everything, but they are a big part of it.Nice idea, poorly executed. It sort of feels like a proof of concept, or a tech demo, rather than a game costing £33 / $44 / €37I tell you, at that rate it’s a wonder we even evolved at all!I'm sure some will like it, but it’s really not for me. I’ve asked for a refund.Buy it if you want but buy it on sale for %50 or less.

_childDocuments_.review: The Industrial Revolution and its consequences have been a disaster for the human race. They have greatly increased the life-expectancy of those of us who live in “advanced” countries, but they have destabilized society, have made life unfulfilling, have subjected human beings to indignities, have led to widespread psychological suffering (in the Third World to physical suffering as well) and have inflicted severe damage on the natural world. The continued development of technology will worsen the situation. It will certainly subject human being to greater indignities and inflict greater damage on the natural world, it will probably lead to greater social disruption and psychological suffering, and it may lead to increased physical suffering even in “advanced” countries. The industrial-technological system may survive or it may break down. If it survives, it MAY eventually achieve a low level of physical and psychological suffering, but only after passing through a long and very painful period of adjustment and only at the cost of permanently reducing human beings and many other living organisms to engineered products and mere cogs in the social machine. Furthermore, if the system survives, the consequences will be inevitable: There is no way of reforming or modifying the system so as to prevent it from depriving people of dignity and autonomy. If the system breaks down the consequences will still be very painful. But the bigger the system grows the more disastrous the results of its breakdown will be, so if it is to break down it had best break down sooner rather than later. We therefore advocate a revolution against the industrial system. This revolution may or may not make use of violence; it may be sudden or it may be a relatively gradual process spanning a few decades. We can’t predict any of that. But we do outline in a very general way the measures that those who hate the industrial system should take in order to prepare the way for a revolution against that form of society. This is not to be a POLITICAL revolution. Its object will be to overthrow not governments but the economic and technological basis of the present society. In this article we give attention to only some of the negative developments that have grown out of the industrial-technological system. Other such developments we mention only briefly or ignore altogether. This does not mean that we regard these other developments as unimportant. For practical reasons we have to confine our discussion to areas that have received insufficient public attention or in which we have something new to say. For example, since there are well-developed environmental and wilderness movements, we have written very little about environmental degradation or the destruction of wild nature, even though we consider these to be highly important.Reject society, return to Monke.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really disappointed by this game's mechanics, not only is it tedious but the controls are also clunky and jumping from branch to branch is beyond frustrating for something that should be as easy as breathing for an ape. The controls themselves wouldn't be as much of a deal-breaker if only the tutorial system was at least somewhat decent. _childDocuments_.review: I was waiting so long for this to be released on PC and it is finally here. Where do I start?Positives:This game is truly a good game, it's hard but really fun and you can just immerse yourself in the dangerous world our ancestors lived in and truly feel to some extent the harshness and dangers of what it was like. You start off as prey and work your way to the top being the apex predator just like our ancestors. You discover new technologies, mutations, neurological improvements along the way until your walking upright and dominating the landscapes of Africa. The game doesn't give you much guidance which truly immerses you in the mind of a developing Hominid; if you do however get stuck you can always refer to trusty old google unlike our Hominid ancestors. The graphics are nice and the landscapes are beautiful with varying biomes, terrains with benefits/negatives for each one. The game takes a lot of time to finish and complete all the achievements, I spent about 60 hrs for my playthrough and you really feel a sense of accomplishment on finishing each one. I truly hope they make a 2nd game exploring into the next stages of our evolution. It does truly well to make sure the game is very factually correct to the best it can and makes a lot of effort in making it realistic to that period of time.Negatives:To delve into the negatives this game, which it has unfortunately, I'd start off by saying some of the mechanics for fighting and dodging are a bit confusing at first and it took me a while to figure it out even with a guide. That may be my own incompetence though. Since it doesn't give you much guidance you could also consider it a negative if you're one of those people who requires babysitting throughout an entire game. Something that bothered me to some extent was that a lot of the tools, medicine, weapons and food are all very repetitive and a bit lackluster once you discover everything, it just gets repetitive seeing the same gathering spots for various objects and when you do find something new it is basically the same. The food variation is also kinda pointless as most food doesn't really give any outlying benefit to other food other than maybe quenching your hunger better, would've been cool to see meat give benefits to your brain power like it was in our development or fruits which quench thirst. The game does run on a kinda linear system and I'm not sure how much re-playability there is for it as of yet since every playthrough from now on will be about the same just way easier.However to end on a good note, I really hope they continue this saga and continue the humankind odyssey all the way to our recent ancestors. Thanks to all the guys at the development team, this was a great break from the world into our past!

_childDocuments_.review: a lot of the bad reviews this game gets are from people who failed to understand the reasons behind certain design choices. You're expected to learn to survive as our first ancestors once did: trial, error, and painful death. You're also expected to learn about yourself and your abilities. You're meant to start off weak, afraid and prey for anything, and gain confidence as you understand everything better, and become more accustomed to your enviroment. There are ways to do things that are bettter than others, but sometimes you won't realize you can improve the effects of an item by preparing it differently.If you liked climbing in BOTW as much as i did, you'll likely love this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Play the game... and find out the real monkey is YOU!A good game is not defined by graphics, sound, innovation or even story. What makes a game great, is how it makes you feel. The immersion. When the game becomes you, when you become part of the game.This game does exactly that.You start out as a confused monkey, who barely knows how to move around or how to grab something. By trying over and over again, experimenting with different materials and styles, you learn. And just like the in-game monkey learns, you the player learn. You learn how to quickly find a weapon, be it a stick, a rock, or a bone. You learn to always carry a weapon. You learn to eat & drink in time, when & where to sleep safely. You learn to identify a coconut tree, whose fruits can satisfy both thirst and hunger and can heal an upset stomach. You start wielding power over not just one ape, but an entire clan. The secrets of generation switching or an entire evolution unfold. That feeling when you can make what once was mystery then work for you in the way you want it - that is the feeling a video game should give you. And ancestors does.The game does a great job not holding your hand too much, and letting you explore, discover and learn, while still avoiding you get stuck or bored. It's forgiving enough to allow mistakes, while being brutal enough to keep you on your toes and let you realise that the danger is real. One killed monkey does not mean the end, but when you're at your last monkey, you'll quickly learn to sleep in trees or use your sense of smell and hearing before jumping into the unknown - which will turn out to be a crocodile. As you get further in the game, the threats get more varied, but you'll also conquer more. The feeling when that panther who's been stalking and killing your clan for ages finally ends up dead on the ground after a brutal battle - that's amazing. That is why we play. And that is why you should play this game! And offcourse, your monkey will not just kill the panther. It'll also bang its fists on the dead head of the fallen foe, go totally bananas in the victory rush as all clan members join in the wild screaming and chanting... and then you find a rock, buther the corpse, and eat the meat. Woops, not carnivorous yet? No worries, your upset stomach now means your offspring will be... one day.Does the game have downsides? Off course. It's a game about evolution, so you'll spend quite some time managing your traits and passing generations. And that means ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ other monkeys. A lot of them. And everybody knows: doing the same thing too often can feel repetitive - even ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Oh well. You learn a quickie is good enough to generate a baby monkey and you'll be enjoying the new traits fast enough to reap the benefits. After a while, you unlock a trait that auto-couples and auto-reproduces, and the grind lessens. Soon, you will dominate the world.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, yes, I absolutely recommend this game. It's hard to put into words what this game actually is, but it's really nothing like other conventional games out there. I guess I'll just address some of the possible negatives about the game.1: The first obvious thing is the tutorial. The game tells you what you need to do, but not how to do it. I actually really like this. In this game, you are NOT a human. You don't know what is what in this world, and you are learning at the same pace as your tribe. I recommend you go in completely blind, and learn slowly what "hit rock with other rock do," but if you don't I understand. :P2: The game is pretty repetitive. Unfortunately, for the game the devs were going for, that was kind of unavoidable. The gameplay loop revolves around learning a new skill, and maybe you can pass it on the the babies in your clan, or you will have to relearn the skill. There are 3 stages, the first is your personal skills, the second is next generations skills, which allows you to make some skills permanent, and the third evolves your species as a whole.3: Controls for me are kinda weird, using a controller like the game recommends works pretty well, but some things can be mapped weird, for example, the button for run (Hold A) is the same for jump (Release A while moving). So you have to release the A button while moving to jump, this can make climbing high up dangerous as you can easily fall to your death.4: Some of the "Quicktime" events are hard to understand. They all have an audio cue and a visual effect, but I've notice that the visual effect is less important than the audio clues. For a while I could not figure out how to counter attack, even though the tip for it was that same as the dodge's tip. Turns out you have to wait for that audio cue, and then you can attack.Overall the game is great, and these issues are very minor. The exploration is fun, and making connecting neurons is my heroin at this point.TL;DR- Kinda grindy/repetitive. Overall great. 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly don't understand why this game doesn't have more positive reviews. Sure it has some minor bugs and some things that could have been implemented better like the mimic function but the game is solid. Also this game is mostly a survival game so if you have certain expectations then you may be disappointed. I would say that most of the time it's a very relaxing game except when it's not. You get attacked by a predator and it's literally a run for your life. Also you don't get to attack directly, it's always a counterattack so don't expect going hunting with your tribe buddies, you can however have them defend themselves.Beautiful scenery, a huge map and rewarding gameplay as long as you don't go straight to Google to ask where to go or how to achieve something. The game rewards you for trying things and exploring, looking stuff up on the internet will definitely spoil the game. The world is big and beautiful making exploring and finding new locations and landmarks a lot of fun. The exploration is not only limited to the map but you also have to explore new ways of finding food, healing/curing yourself, making tools, surviving attacks, etc. even finding new tribe members so there is a lot of experimenting. It may be a little frustrating when you start the game because you have no skills so everything takes what would seem too much time or too many hits to make something, everything you eat makes you sick, etc. but as you acquire new skills it will get better. You can survive at first with the basic stuff and as long as you are curious you should have no problem finding all this other stuff on your own little by little, give the game a chance!The skill upgrade tree is a little tricky at first but you really don't need to pay too much attention to it in the beginning, you will figure out later how to maximize your upgrade points. You start out very weak and slow but you will gain skills that make you move or climb faster or jump further and it will become easier so again give the game a chance!Now for some things I think they could have improved. As I mentioned above, the mimic function. I wish there were less steps in between ordering your followers to mimic an action, it's a little convoluted. Also one of the more annoying bugs was when I was trying to have someone mimic an action and getting whatever they had in their hand stuck and not able to make them drop it. The only workaround I could find was to switch over to control that ape, drop what he was holding then switch back otherwise it would not eat or sleep and if it was hurt eventually die. That is the only bug I remember because it was annoying when it happened but it was rare but honestly this is a very minor issue in a very well made game.I hope they make a new one with UE5 it would look sick and I would buy it in a heartbeat.TL;DRGame is beautiful and fun to explore just don't look stuff up in the wiki, it will spoil it. Game starts slow but it picks up quickly just give it a chance.

Controls are a cluster F, I've died multiple times just because my ape didn't grab a branch, tree, or wall on the way down. There's a difference between fun/challenging and downright bad design. You can't throw totally random mechanics at people with zero input or information and EXPECT them to know what to do.

_childDocuments_.review: At first I was like huh?, then Oh!, and now this game has me hopping in my chair saying o-o-o-e-e-e-e. This game is very unique and unlike anything else I have played. I have not played a game that you actually need to use ALL your senses to find things and to navigate the world around you. I do not recommend getting emotionally attached to your monkeys as you will cry when they get wrapped up by a Python, munched on by an alligator, or picked off 1 by 1 by the big kitties. _childDocuments_.name: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey

_childDocuments_.review: A smartly crafted game and map design where the audio and environment keeps you immersed. Also sick that they implemented a ♥♥♥♥ ton of cool evolutionary theories as apart of the game play, since most of our past beyond 10 Million years is still uncertain (the missing link). From this, we know the human brain somehow doubled in size in a relatively short period of time, so as apart of the game play with becoming omnivorous, they kind of implement the "stoned ape theory." The more mushrooms you eat, the more neurons you gain and can eat more of. The birth of religion and mysticism also comes into play with seeing "snakes in the sky" (Meteors) that our past selves carved at say Gobekli Tepe and other sites, and also finding precious gems and minerals to worship and help you be less afraid. Such a fascinating and thought provoking game, especially if you love learning about ancient humans and how humanity somehow became the best species there is on this planet. Also, monkeys are absolutely hilarious
_childDocuments_.name: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey

_childDocuments_.review: Whoa... This was different in a way I wasn't expecting.The actual game play is just okay, with it feeling a little fiddly when I first started. Also it gives the option of no HUD when starting a game, I tried this but I personally found it less immersive, so I quickly turned the HUD back on. Once you get used to the controls and moving through the canopies, oh man, what a thrill!Where this game really shines is in the level design and character progression. You can tell there is no procedural generation here, with each "level" encouraging you to develop and evolve to deal with new challenges in a way accurate to our current understanding of human history.  The progression feels good, especially if you're not worried about maximizing gains quickly. If you'd like to power level, I'd suggest reading a guide as the game is rather coy about the mechanics.I also would like to call out the enemy AI. I love that the enemies are not overly aggressive like you'd find in other games. You hit a predator in the face with a rock, and you can bet (until the next generation) that they'll think twice when you yell at them, haha! (As a general pacifist in games, and a vegetarian in real life, I've never felt like it was my duty to eat other animals as much as in this game. Take that antelope!)I played relatively slowly, and it took me about 65 hours to hit credits. (My play time is higher, because I wanted to check out survival mode. Pretty much the same, but still a good time!)
_childDocuments_.name: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey

_childDocuments_.review: Great game! Tough to learn even with the tutorial, but once you get the hang of it the depth is profound. You're not just running around being an ape, you are solidifying information for the next generation and evolving your species with nearly everything you do. From eating and learning how to forage to walking on two legs you are always teaching your clan members. The environment is beautiful and it sounds just as I imagine a jungle before humans would sound... Great work!
_childDocuments_.name: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey

_childDocuments_.review: It's crazy good. Yes, I want to play arcane monkey life simulator. I want to press Y to use my obtuse Intelligence UI and identify rock, and I want to develop the neuron that lets me eat eggs. Incredibly funny game for how deadpan and self-serious it gets when the subject matter is "monkey find mushroom." Made by ex-Assassin's Creed people so the movement tech when you're climbing those trees is crazy. High-minded 1990s ecological sim merged with 21st century triple A Unreal Engine physics and particles and ♥♥♥♥. It just rules. I don't care if it's repetitive sometimes, or if encounters with predators can be chaotic to the point of incoherence... I am monkey.
_childDocuments_.name: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey

I played it a lot once I figure things out.  Definitely something different compared to other survival games, well worth the time and money.
_childDocuments_.name: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey

The apes that you don't control are literal braindead, i mean i know they are apes but when im perfectly dodging every tiger lunge, this ♥♥♥♥♥ still linger around for the tiger to pounce on them again so that i have go and seduce the tiger again. Maybe i haven't unlock it yet, but a button to tell everyone "DANGER! GET THE ♥♥♥♥ OUT" would be nice. Things like this makes you wonder, why even be mechanically good and not take any damage when you still end up having to clean everyone's wound after every expedition. Another thing is i settled on Cascading Clifts thinking it would turn that into my base and have a protected area, NOPE an anaconda just slithers through like it is new york time square, next thing i know 2 of my apes got broken bones and if that wasnt enough, they spawn a tiger right into my base, and it is the whole ♥♥♥♥ fest again. _childDocuments_.review: Im sorry I really love this game but I cant find it in me to recommend it.Its very fun at first finding new thing increasing neurons,swinging from trees and seeing different animals and exploring new places.But that only lasts so long.The combat system goes from very hard because the game gives basically no indication of what you doing to extremely easy because once you understand its a quicktime event you can kill basically anything.You will find out you have discovered everything there is to craft and all the animals in basically the first 5 hours of gameplay . _childDocuments_.review: Love the exploration and evolution systems. The world feels alive and full of things to do, places to find, and animals to kill. The combat system is admittedly, a bit repetitive, but with all the different enemies and animations it still feel epic when you engage in a fight with something. The crafting system is pretty cool, and small things like all the different pastes you can use to buff yourself allow you to confidently walk through even the most dangerous of areas. The animations when you kill something are super epic, giving extra motivation to look for fights with other animals. I would pay the full price for it, but if you're feeling unsure, you can always wait for the sale, which brings the price down to $10. Overall great game would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey

_childDocuments_.review: A truly unique and captivating experience that will hold your attention tightly till the end and then stay strong in your memories thereafter. With a growing interest in survival games and a very long-standing interest in human evolution, the concept of this game grabbed me from the start and continued to keep a hold of me. I'd spend time outside it, carefully planning my next play session's expedition, keeping in mind what I'd learned along the way to make it smoother and safer for my ape-people. Now almost 150 hours in and doing regular skirmishes into the final biome, I don't want the experience to end! I've stopped playing as much to try and keep this unique and compelling experience going as long as I can. Now all me and my fellow devoted Ancestors fans can hope for is news of a sequel. We need to continue the path to ♥♥♥♥ sapiens and beyond into the stone age!

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game cause I was looking for a open-world survival game and saw this game in my search for such a game, I watched some videos like the trailer of the game, brief game-play to see how mechanics are, and reviews on the game. I only played for 37 mins my first play-through and got real bored because I didn't know particularly what to do and never really left the waterfall because I was scared XD. Now I think a couple of months have passed and I have returned to the game because I was watching "OwlTime", mostly "The Isle" Youtuber but I saw he has videos on "Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey", not even part 2 of his series and I immediately downloaded the game again and tried my hardest to learn everything and tried new things. _childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game but despite it being recommended for controller use there are some controls that just make this game hard to handle.  I wanted to keep my HUD up but some controller controls change that.  Having to go into my settings to fix that because it doesn't make it easy to fix is also annoying.The concept is kind of cool, but after a certain point it just feels over clunky and not quite the sort of game you'd want to play if you like colony survival sims.  I've put 20+ hours into this game, and realize every time I play it just how clunky the game can be.  There are some instances where trying to dodge creatures becomes annoying as heck, or trying to just groom.  There's no real clear concise way of getting things to work.  If you hold a button for too long you break things you don't necessarily want to break.  You mess up grooming if you don't have an idea of how it's supposed to work (and tank a grooming session that way).  All in all, the concept is great but the the game itself is very clunky and overwhelming.That said, it's not a bad game, but it's definitely not a game I can say that's enjoyable unless you have way too much time on your hands and you've got literally nothing better to do.

_childDocuments_.review: This game DOES NOT hold your hand!It can be a bit slow starting out but holy Christ is it a gem once you start to get your ♥♥♥♥ figured out! I normally hate survival/crafting type games but this one is done really well. You basically get tossed into the jungle afraid and alone and have to find your tribe and get yourself situated in such a way that you can survive properly in the wild. This game truly portrays the struggle to survive as a wild beast. Sometimes you are a predator and sometimes you are prey and you have to think and act fast to avoid being eaten by a jungle cat or a python. In other situations maybe you kill the Saber Cat or the python, it's up to you. To gain experience and expand your neural network to learn new cognitive functions, you must use your 5 senses. Gain xp with these:Visualize your surroundings.Hear what's around you.Smell whats around you.Attack new beasts to gain new understanding (which is like gaining xp)Lure beasts to get attacked by other beasts for a similar outcome.    For example the rock python can kill off 5 other beasts and vice versa. This gives lineage experience. Fruit in the world could be ripe or it could be rotten. You need to visualize or smell it to determine if it is good to eat. The area you start in is quite vast but if you move on to farther areas you will truly see how vast the world is. I have traveled so far from my settlement that I couldn't even fathom the idea of trying to make it back there again and it seems like I can go that far many more times over. The world is gigantic! There are a few animals in the jungle when you start out, but there are many more to be discovered as you venture onward.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game because of how unique the concept is but the fact is that I hated the entire time I spent playing it. Granted, I could have given it more time but in the end it wasn't the lack of tutorials or getting killed by things without understanding why or how to avoid it (both of which are annoying in itself) but the fact that the controls are completely counter-intuitive if you're playing on a keyboard. _childDocuments_.review: This is one of the only games, possibly the first, that I have ever requested a refund for on steam. The controls are pretty terrible on keyboard and mouse. The game says it's best played on controller, but that doesn't really justify the awful controls if you are going to release it on PC. The tutorial is just awful. Most games you can figure out what you are doing pretty easily even without the tutorial, but this game is supposed to be about experimenting and discovery, but they do a really poor job telling you how to get started. I chose the immersive start (Full tutorial, minimal HUD) and didn't even realize I had a HUD at all because the game doesn't tell you how to bring it up (it's one of the arrow keys). Maybe that's just me, but there are a lot of unexplained mechanics that are essential to the game.The game has a lot of points of interests when you go into the intelligence mode, but you have to be perfectly still to view them and you can't highlight ones behind you. Once you discover something, lets say a plant for example, you will unlock some features and information about the plant. The problem is that all the other plants of that type don't become discovered as a POI in intelligence mode. They remain a gray square until you focus in on it. I would have to compare it to scanning something in No Man's Sky, but instead of scanning the plant once you have to scan every single plant on the planet.Lastly I have to talk about the climbing/jumping mechanics. Imagine every time you've played Assassins Creed and your character didn't go the way you wanted him to or he jumped and didn't grab onto anything causing you to fall to your death. Now imagine that x10 in the jungle. What really makes it bad is as you watch all the branches fly by that you're not grabbing you realize that when you hit the ground your clan will lose another valuable member to poor game mechanics. Then you get to stare into the eyes of your lifeless corpse while the game autosaves.Overall I think this game could have a lot of potential and it's an interesting concept, but the execution of it is very poor and not worth the $20 I spent let alone $40 at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: Monkey see, Monkey doYou see the monkey and the monkey see you.To be serious for a minute,this " " " Experience " " " as they announce it it's just a grindfest of the same 4 thingsGet to WaypointKill StuffEat stuffCraft stuff to eat and killGot this on humble bundle as i was interested in the concept,which is interesting and cool... for the first 1 hour, after that, i found myself literally grinding trought sticks to kill stuff, don't you dare travel with companions as the AI is beyond retarded (as well as the NPCs) you'll do it just to unlock neural nodes/change biome.The point is. there could be some much more to this game but instead it's Assassin's Creed 1 without weapons and objectives ,Made for people who get easly excited over little things done over and over , feels more of a tech demo,which is not bad itself as we can see in games like Death Stranding (overhyped too but still it has content) they lost track of what they where doing half way trought or just ran out of ideas, which is a shame.Sure the in game world feels and looks cool, but you'll get stressed and notice every single flaw of it since you don't have much to do apart from exploring to gain nothing. wait. you get POINTS! for... EVOLVING! which is basically ... 2 more unlock and in total i guess 4 features more for a grindfest not worth it,but if you like the feel of points added just play any old Atari game; the features you want to have are behind an rng system called "mutations" , as i was so close to finish all the achievements i tried to get the last two which to me where Omnivorous and obviously launch the last evolution, i spat out 162 sons and none of them had the required mutation. _childDocuments_.review: I had this game wish listed for a long time because I thought the idea and concept behind it were interesting. I actually had forgotten about it until the recent seasonal sale and I grabbed it for roughly 15 bucks and I am so glad that I did because I knew I wish listed this game for a reason. This game is definitely not for the faint of heart or might not be what you expect - which was my case, but in a great way. Long Story Short = This game is about our early ancestors roughly 10 million years ago before we evolved into ♥♥♥♥ sapiens, the game is about not only surviving in the wild but thriving and evolving which is definitely harder said than done. This game is very unforgiving in certain terms, they let you know from the beginning that they wont offer much help and you have to figure it out, which to some gamers would be extremely frustrating and that's why this game isn't for everyone. But for me its a lot of fun to figure things out and actually use your brain to determine how to survive in the wild. Long Story Long (potential spoilers) = Even though the game is very unforgiving in some regards it is forgiving in other ways, mistakes WILL happen, but you'll learn from them. You probably will die or come close but you'll learn from it. it wont be end game as you are not just "one character" but you are the tribe in itself. you can switch to any member(to play) and through evolution unlock more possibilities. the game focuses very hard on a slower pace play style to focus on learning about different food sources & food types, learning the surroundings as well as inspecting and figuring out how to change or alter your surroundings or resources with tools and other resources. you'll have to take care of your clan and its members, which is done semi-automatically. heal injuries, make sure the clan is eating and getting water etc. you might think you'd need to switch to every member and eat/drink etc that's not true that's just tedious and boring. if you are playing as a member and are in the settlement, whether others are following you or not, if you start drinking or eating the tribe generally starts drinking and eating too. however injuries and other ailments like poisoning etc will require a more manual approach, you'll need to get specific items to the injured tribe member and either use it on yourself as the injured member or give the item to them and hope they use it on themselves which doesn't seem to work 100% of the time i believe its because when or what in their hands when you give it to them etc. or what they are in the middle of doing.If you like survival/crafting/settlement management/thinking outside the box/tree climbing/jumping/hardcore parkour/evolving/exploring/discovering/learning and aren't afraid to brave the wild.. this game might be for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey

_childDocuments_.review: I am absolutely loving this survival sim. The controls and camera took some getting used to, but I'm far beyond point where navigating my environment and combat/dodging are no longer overwhelming. Timing (marked by audio/visual cues) is key to every aspect of the game.If you're into diligent resource management and environmental exploration, this game is fantastic. There's nothing you can't get past by planning ahead. The game won't hold your hand, though, and trial and error are everything. It's somewhat niche, but if it's your niche you'll be thrilled.Not-Pro Tip: Even with the controller, I didn't commit myself to mastering the early game possibility of swinging from tree to tree. If you're going to practice that one, spare a thought for how far your ape has to fall. I felt like I'd committed a homicide, man.ETA:  Pro-Tip: Now that I have 11/13 achievements (one I'm going to take my time on before ending the game, it requires some extra ranging) I've gotta say that I've become really good at jumping around in all directions. Believe in yourself! Me and my biological anthropology degree give this one a 10/10.

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of reviews complain about the lack of hand holding and tutorial quality but I bought the game anyways. And then I returned it. After three hours of gameplay that was honestly not fun at all but mostly frustrating. And it wasn't the lack of tutorial or missing support but the fact that so many things in this game are so tedious and unnecessarily slow and infuriating. Some examples:While in "intelligence" mode, which means that time seems to stop and you can look around to discover new things, dozens of unknown squares show up. Once you focus on one the item behind it is revealed. But it takes a few seconds for each square, and there must be several hundred of them just in the starting jungle.Climbing and moving on trees is incredibly slow and tedious. There really isn't a good parkour system like in Mirror's edge or AC. For example, once on a branch, you can't turn around (or I didn't figure out how), which means that if you want to go back you have to walk backwards. Also, jumping to other trees is difficult, so I relied on walking on the ground more, but there are other dangers there...Days are so short that you barely have time to explore between eating, drinking, and sleeping. You get the feeling that as soon as you leave your home turf it's already time to get back.The list goes on and on. The graphics aren't that amazing either. Not bad, but not outstanding either.I'm very disappointed. This would have been exactly my thing, but the grindy, frustrating mess this game is, I really tried, but I can't. It's too bad.
_childDocuments_.name: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey

_childDocuments_.review: Could not get over the poor control scheme. They had an entire controller's worth of buttons to map functions to, and for some reason decided to map every single movement-related behavior to a single button:- want to run? hold the A button- want to stop sprinting? Release A button... while not moving the control stick- jump? Release A button... while moving the control stick- pick up an item? Release A button while near it. Hope you didn't also want to jump.- catch vines while jumping? Hold the A button.- jump off of those vines? release the A button. Hope you didn't want to go down, or just hang there, or climb.the rest of the face buttons are mapped to various vision modes, and could very easily have been a selector instead, considering the fact that there's never any urgency to use them because you can't use them while moving...Definitely not worth the asking price, and up to you whether it's worth a deep discount (for me it's still a no).
_childDocuments_.name: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to set this as a yes because it is good fun activating some monkey neurons.But the more I play, the more the cons out-weigh the pros.But one of the biggest turn-offs in video games for me is when the devs try to boost the difficulty by spawning enemies behind you on a regular basis. You can put your back to a clear dead end, start crafting something, and within a minute you'll have a tiger spawned behind you and already locked on.There are just so many annoyances. The camera is constantly zooming in and out or spinning around for whatever "cinematic" effect they're going for. Climbing is incredibly clunky and at times frustrating. If you're tired, the screen starts to have a "eye closing" effect. Getting a stomach ache for some reason makes your vision blurry (Whoever designed that, please see a doctor about your stomach issues. That is not normal). And while I understand they wanted to go with a "minimal hand-holding" experience, I feel that much more context is needed for certain mechanics of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Terrible ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ game. Don't waste your money. It's cool for the first few hours until you realize the game is just the same ♥♥♥♥ over and over. Even the way the game walked me through the mechanics and controls in the game was difficult for me to follow. I had to start a new game like three or more times just because I couldn't figure out what the hell was going on. Obviously, I'm not the brightest crayon in the box by far, but ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, dude. I'm of the opinion that if the game was actually good, the instructions would be far more straightforward. I can't remember the last time I played a game and was unable to nail the controls within a couple of minutes, maybe a little more depending on the game. The gameplay mechanics for dodging predator attacks is beyond -100000 IQ. The Machairodus does not walk up to you. It quite literally teleports in from ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ nowhere and you only know when you're being attacked after you see the dodge skillcheck screen. Specifically the Golden Machairodus, because it's never roaming the jungle floor like I've seen a black Machairodus doing before. It just appears from nowhere. My entire clan was intimidating it and would not do anything besides switch its attention from the clan member it was already attacking onto me. I figured that it might be because I have no sharpened stick in my hand, but the only reason my clan members did not have a sharpened stick equipped is because if they did, they would be unable to dodge a predator on their own. I did not have one because I had something else in my hands. But as I kept trying to get to the stacks of my stripped sticks and sharpened sticks, the Machairodus would pounce on me before I could even hover over the item to pick it up. I kept trying to ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ press A to pick up the stick, but it wouldn't hover over the item, so my monkey I was just playing jumps and I continue to be pounced on by the sole Machairodus. It's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ atrocious.Thank god I got this game on sale. Otherwise I'd be seriously irate. Complete waste of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ time and money. I bought this game because, yeah, I did want to play as monkeys, but it's also heavily implied that your clan can evolve over time and actually turn into a more "modern" version of the Hominids. I was excited that such a game exists, that I could actually choose which genes to lock in and how to play the game to evolve slowly into a more human-like monkey over time, to breed in strong traits to make your hominid clan as strong as possible. _childDocuments_.review: The game is difficult but very good. As other comments mention, there is a unique learning curve. It took me about 8 hours of game-play to really understand the controls and abilities. You're a monkey. And as a monkey, you have to learn the simplest of things. Such as switching items to your other hand, walking upright for a bit, and carrying things. You use your sense of smell and hearing to learn more about the environment around you and overcome your fear when you venture into unknown territories. The world around you is trying to kill you, either run or find a way to kill the predators first. As you evolve through time and pass through generations, you'll unlock more neuron pathways to learn more skills. Use Google as a guide, some of the tools combinations can be tricky to discover especially since you don't always succeed when creating or using the tools.The game recommends using a controller but I use a keyboard without any issues. I think it would all depend on your preference. Enjoy and return to monke.

"omg this game suuuuucks", "worst tutorial eveeerrrr.." As the game concept says, the timeline in this game is year 0, before the humans being appeared. So there is no definition of "weapon" or "spear" "bed" etc.. because it never been made! , because your species spending most the time to collect food and sleep anywhere they think it safe, Basically eat - sleep - bang - repeat. And then somehow you, a monkey have some curious mind, start inspect everything and try to create something that even you don't know what it is but you know it gonna be useful when it done. , like you pick up a leaf, smell it and thinking "dam, this leaf is so smooth like the baby(monkey) ass! _childDocuments_.review: A great concept. The game is immersive, and there is much to discover. There is a real sense of accomplishment and progress when you get your specie to evolve. Group behaviour improves in interesting ways, and automation through immitation works more or less. Movement is fluid. Play this if you like to explore a well crafted world and discover how you can interact with it. You will need to be curious, and be prepared to miss some important elements of the game at first as it gives very minimal instructions.The goal of the game is to advance through time to evolve, and this happens by doing feats, like discovering new places, doging attacks and many other things. Every time you validate your progress, the game makes you start fresh with a new clan, that inherits your previous clan neurons and mutations. You are also expected to reproduce, and pass one or two generations per clan to "lock" newly acquired skills.As this is a "humanity ancestors simulator", there is some repetitive actions to do, like drink, eat, sleep, make tools, reproduce (maybe the most repetitive and less interesting action), prepare camps, and so on. There are evolutions that reduce how much time it takes, but it won't go away. I actually find it not that taxing on the game time, while creating enough pressure so that you have to organize your expeditions a bit. As long as you actally . Indeed, I lost a lot of time grinding on my 5-7 first hours because of this. This time could have been reduced a lot, and my enjoyment multiplied if I followed instructions. But I am not this kind of Hominid, it would seem.I would advise to play with the UI on at first, and maybe de-activate it later, to learn the many contextual actions and the idea behind the control scheme.  and read carefully, so you can enjoy really playing with each generation, and advance at a good pace.

_childDocuments_.review: Good presentation (graphics, sound, music), and a big world to explore.  However, the mechanics really let it down, and very quickly become incredibly tedious.  (And that's once you understand them, which the game does nothing to help with.)Firstly, this isn't a game where you just control a single monkey and go off exploring on your own.  You're managing a whole tribe, and you need to develop their skills and help them evolve.  You do this via unlocking nodes using "neuronal energy" (i.e. XP) on the "neuronal tree" (i.e. a skill tree).There's a huge problem with this system: Eventually, you'll need to pass a generation.  When you do, you only get to "lock in" a handful of skills.  Everything else will be wiped out, and you'll have to spend XP on them again.Eventually, yes, you can lock in everything and finally stop losing skills every time you gen-up.   But it's needless grind that seems to exist solely to pad the game's length.  (Plus, advancing a generation is tedious: You need to pair up all your monkeys again, make them mate and have kids, etc.  This takes about 5-10 minutes or so, and it's just needless busy work.)Each kid has a chance of having a helpful mutation, and once you're satisfied with the mutations in your tribe, you can "evolve".  This is like a super-generation-up.  These mutations become a permanent part of your skill tree, and any feats you've completed — like "discover {location}", or "dodge an attack from a giant warthog two times", or "apply the healing properties of honey two times", etc — advance you by a certain number of years, typically 20,000 to 40,000.  (You need to have completed at least one of these to evolve.)At first, it's easy to evolve.  Everything you do is new!  But late in the game, I ran out of locations to explore and had done all the spontaneous feats I was going to do.  I had to start treating it like a tedious achievement checklist, and doing things I would never have done otherwise.  (Dodge a warthog?  Why?  I've killed dozens of them for their meat already.)There's a ton of other problems, too.  Early on, before you've learned weapons or how to intimidate as a group, your only realistic option is to stick to the trees, away from the dangerous predators on the ground.  But the jumping system is  — no preview of where you'll land, and the game uses the same button for both "jump" and "grab onto surface", meaning you'll probably just end up immediately letting go again.  Be ready for tons of "broken bone" injuries, and learn what plants heal them.Speaking of which, the game pretty much  a controller — I tried KB+M and it was awful — and even then, the button overloading is .  I know that console games in general have this problem, but this takes it to a whole new level.  The same button is used for• sprinting• swimming• jumping• grabbing onto something while falling• standing up• laying down• sleeping• picking things up• taking things from other people• trading your item for theirs• butchering• constructing stuff• probably several other things I've forgottenMeanwhile, there's a whole button pretty much just dedicated to smelling things, and two whole triggers dedicated to adjusting your "mood".  It's the most bonkers control scheme I've ever seen, and there were probably hundreds of times where I did the wrong thing as a direct result of this awful system.But, back to the game.  One key part of the game is leading your tribe around the map, either to change settlements (which you will do a lot, there's rarely any reason to stay in a location very long) or just so you can keep an eye on them / intimidate animals better.You can also have your tribe do things, like sharpen sticks to turn them into spears, or grind herbs to turn them into medication — pretty useful if you want to arm your entire tribe , treat wounds, or apply preventive medication.  You do this via a mimickry system, which involves doing an action and then pressing a button that makes them mimic what you just did.To understand why, you need to understand the equally awful inventory system.  You only have two hands, and you always do things with your right hand, while your left one is used for holding things while you "alter" them.Let's say one of your monkeys is injured.  You've got a grinder in your hand, so you could grind them some medicine to help.  You see the plant you need on the ground.  What do you have to do?• You'll need  your hands.  If the grinder is in your left hand, move it to your right hand by pressing L1 (swap hands).• Drop the grinder by pressing R1.• Press A to pick up the herb.  (Don't hold A or you'll automatically start eating it.)• Press L1 to move it to your left hand.• Hold L1 to enter alter mode.• Hold R1 to begin altering it.  (Don't start holding R1 before L1, or you'll throw it away as far as you can.)• Let go  you hear the audio cue, or you'll destroy it.  (Can't hear the cue?  That's your problem, go play another game.)• Go find your grinder and pick it up by pressing A.• Hold L1 to enter alter mode.• Hold R1 to begin grinding it.• Let go when you hear the audio cue.Congrats, you've got medicine.  Now you need to give it to the injured monkey, which means juggling  inventory, too.  (Are you having fun yet?)Now imagine if you want to have your entire tribe do this, so you can "mass vaccinate" everyone against injuries.  You're looking at doing all of the steps above  pressing "mimic me" between every step  making sure there's enough grinders that everyone can do it  making sure there's enough plants that everyone has one.  And all the while, your food and water and sleep timers are all counting down, and you're at risk of being attacked by predators.A lot of the game's systems would be great in a single-monkey exploration game, but utterly fall down when you try to apply them on a tribal scale.  Even with something simple like "grab a dead tree branch and strip it with your bare hands to make a basic stick weapon", I would find some of them carrying an un-stripped branch, and some of them carrying nothing at all.  And there's a bunch of activities that can't be mimicked at all, like fishing, or fetching coconuts from trees.  It's unreliable and frustrating as all hell.  Oh, and did I mention that , and they need to eat and drink ?Ultimately, it's simply not worth trying to get your monkeys to mimic anything complex.  They never evolve to the point that they understand how to do these things efficiently.  If you really want to arm your entire tribe, you're better off making a pile of weapons yourself and then telling them to pick those up.  (And don't forget to have your tribe put their weapons in a pile before you gen-up or evolve, because the game  taking your stuff away from you whenever possible.)All in all, of the 50 regrettable hours I spent playing this game, about 5 of them were spent coming to grips with the horribly explained mechanics (the tutorials are ), 10 were spent actually having some fun exploring, and the remaining 35 were just me hate-playing the game to completion because I'm stubborn like that.  (And because I wanted to see if it ever addressed my problems with the game, which it didn't.)  The ending actually came as a surprise — I thought I had 2 million years left to go, but it's just "NOPE you're done roll credits".  But it was a very welcome surprise, and I wish it had come much sooner.

_childDocuments_.review: As a gamer whose education is in anthropology, I was really looking forward to this game. Unfortunately it seems like it was designed by an inexperienced team. The graphics, sound, programming, and concepts are great. The main problems are in design and can be summed up with three things: bad controls, bad interfacing, more frustrating than fun.①　Whether using mouse & keyboard or a controller, the controls are non-intuitive for either a newbie or experienced gamer. Too many conflicting actions are assigned to the same key/button. For example, moving quickly, dodging, jumping, and grabbing onto foliage (but not branches) are all the same button. This means your apes fall to death more way more frequently than non-human hominins would—but more importantly, it kills the fun. The content was as accurate as current understanding of the period permits, but the design makes brachiation harder than believable for 10 MYA, ruining any immersion. I didn't mind starting with a small tribe that had no previous knowledge of what foods had helped them survive before I entered the story (even though that too makes no sense), but missing the foliage I was aiming for happened so often that I started over 3 times. In the end I just stayed low to the ground (again, killing the immersion for this time period).②　It's fine, and I expected that they wouldn't give hints on skill tree / evolutionary progression, what foods do, how to make tools, what threats might exist. This was the experience I was seeking. But, again, it's bad design to make the player guess how they have to interact with the game to do obvious behaviours like putting down a child or mating. Such things should be instinctual for any animal.If you do buy the game, here's some hints:   ・Tap a button to sense perceive things in the environment, but HOLD the button to sense perceive what your holding onto.    ・The blackish swirls around things mean they are unidentified, not poisonous.   ・Picking bugs off of another ape does not satisfy your hunger need. It's a rhythm minigame which leads to making that ape your mate.   ・To mate, tap the button to first lie in your bedding. If you hold it, it will just put you to sleep.    ・If you can't figure out how to do something seemingly obvious, try laying down in bedding first. There's several things there.   ・Don't collect the apes from outside your clan until the game gives you that mission. I had them join up as soon as I saw them, so when the mission came it was impossible to finish and get the next mission.③　Most importantly, the design team seems to have not heard the industry mantra, "follow the fun." They had a very specific vision and they hammered the game until it fit that shape instead of playing the game as it way being programmed and following the fun that the game  revealed on its own. Countless games became unexpected hits because the developers let the game show them "what it wanted to be."The graphics, level design, audio, and general grandeur of the game are of high quality, so it really sucks that the design prevented Ancestors from living up to it's potential. I got the feeling that the lead designer has a big ego and didn't take suggestions from his team. I'm honestly surprised he has headed up multiple games before this. But, I heard he did Assassin's Creed which I also recently played and oof, it doesn't hit its potential either. Cool climbing, but it triggers when you don't want it to (another example of underusing buttons/keys) and so very repetitive.Some of the problems in ancestors are too deeply embedded to fix, but maybe they'll open it up to modding some day and we can make it better as a community. Ancestors could be 10/10—and I rarely rate anything above a 9. As it is, I can't rate it above a 4 because games should make you want to keep playing. But each time I boot it up I just quit in frustration—not even rage quitting. Just disappointment and frustration.I really want to like this game. Please fix it!(Edited for clarity, proper grammar, & spelling.)

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game! If you like open world, puzzles, and survival games this is for you. There are a lot of warnings that this is a very difficult game, and I will have to agree. The fact that it is difficult only makes the game more intriguing. If you struggle with puzzles this game might be less enjoyable, but each thing you learn about the game leads to the next discovery - just like human evolution. The graphics are beautiful, music is great, and controls are easy to learn if you pay attention. At 20 hours into the game this is still so much more to discover and I am looking forward to it.Now for some warnings: 1. Be prepared to dump hours into this game before you feel like you've made any progress.2. Mating your hominids becomes a boring chore pretty quickly (though it doesn't take toooo much game time)3. There can be jump scares when animals attack you4. If you aren't good at 3D platformers with a keyboard and mouse you will struggle

_childDocuments_.review: Pro- Anyone who enjoys exploring a large map and learning things as you go with the least possible hand-holding will enjoy this game. There's a sense of accomplishment as you gradually reach the top of the food chain and find yourself leaving dense forests in favor of having more room to run. The flow is natural with the closest thing to a "story" being following the meteorites to discover new types of scenery.Con- It's more of an RPG than a survival game and while I like the RPG aspect it seems Survival is just too easy. There are certain abilities and items you'll just never use, one of which (slow motion) doesn't seem to serve a purpose at all. Lastly, while you have the option to sneak around you cannot use this offensively as you are only capable of counter-attacking rather than initiating the attack.All in all Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey is a fantastic game of exploration that I do recommend despite the Cons listed above as these Cons make up so little of the overall game that you might not even notice them.
