_childDocuments_.review: Extremely frustrating and grindy, with some of the buggiest climbing mechanics I've ever seen.I keep coming back to this game hoping that somehow after giving it another chance it'll be fun, but it hasn't turned out that way so far.  You progress your hominids by repeating basic chores while carrying a child, and you lock in skill points by completing a generation.  Afterwards, you get to do it all again, because all of the skills you unlocked last generation have been reset.  High levels of RNG with the mutation system gating off skills until you "mature" a child with a particular mutation, and unless something seriously changes in the platforming late-game I really can't see this being a fun game to play long term.  Your character moves at a snail's pace, they let go randomly while climbing, and one fall is all it takes to kill an ape.  Hope that child you were carrying didn't have an important mutation, because they're dead now too.  Apes have a wierd sense of parinoia that I can't figure out and will randomly act like they're being stalked by a predator when there's no threat to be found, which is a major pain since they'll run back to base if they're afraid for too long.While the idea is interesting the assembled game is one of the most frustrating to play survival craft games I've experienced.  I probably won't be giving it another chance.

_childDocuments_.review: The camera's sensitivity will fly 360's around your character multiple times upon the smallest flex of your wrist on the 0 setting. Besides that, the controls are so asinine I can't imagine how even the developers themselves were able to play this. And the whole "no answers will be provided, figure it out yourself" thing would be a cool challenge so long as everything was intuitive... and it's NOT. The way you interact with things makes it insanely difficult for your character to learn anything or obtain mutations let alone craft literally anything. The hyper specific things you have to do with the objects you pick up in order to do anything with them takes an eternity no matter if you're on a keyboard or controller. To the point that I believe this game was originally meant to be in VR, and if it wasn't... I think it would be more playable if it was in VR! Just so it has a more intuitive and ethical control scheme that actually allows you to do the things you're meant to do. Otherwise having to use two of your real life hands to shift/click joysticks, shift/click the mouse, tap/hold several buttons, basically manipulating an entire NASA rocket console of command prompts for the littlest simplest things like looking around and identifying objects as well picking up and crafting with those objects is unplayable on top of the seizure inducing camera sensitivity. Terrible game, I get the immersion of being realistic but this is beyond realistic and needs to be severely simplified along with slowing the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ camera the hell down and turning off the brain dead motion blur so I can actually SEE things.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly the complaints surrounding this game are mostly people who haven't learned to play the game yet. The mechanics of the game are simple when you understand them. When you understand that the game is a blast! This game is intense, but it's not anywhere near dark souls level like some people make it out to be. Simply put this is how you 'beat' the game: When I first wrote this review I was still discovering all sorts of new items, activities, animals, and places, whether it be gemstones, fishing, beaches, breaststroke, etc. I've since 100%-ed the game. Every thing, activity, neuron, location, prey, predator, craftable item, structure, kill animation, location and more I've completed.This game is by no means flawless. Glitches and bugs are very very rare. On occasion animal and ancestor AI can bug out, but never to the point it's game breaking or even immersion breaking. Every location is capable of being explored. Every nook and cranny is reachable.  There's tons of content to enjoy so learn that's what the game is about.This is just another GET GUD KID review. The game won't hold your hand. It's entire premise is exploration. If you're as curious as our ancestors were, and brave enough to venture into unknown territories this game is exactly for you. If you want a more guided experience do not pick up this title.

_childDocuments_.review: Hard to say I would recommend it.The game is fascinating. It is beautiful. It is all about learning how to play. They are some explanations in the menu and pressing the down shift of the cross of the pad will make info stay on the screen. I play with a pad. I had to use the mouse in the neural menu because it is buggy. It is probably done to only play with a pad like said some comments. I am not sure. I have no issue playing with it.In this game you play more a prey than a predator. It is about exploration, discovery and most of all the evolution of your tribe. Till you have tribe members, you can still evolve. You completely lose when you finish alone (I suppose, I never faced that yet). You can make reproduce young fertile females with males. With a limit of 2 babies per female and per generation.It is a mandatory to ensure the continuity of the game.The reason why it is very hard to recommend it: there is no save except when devs decided it. So it seems if you lose, you will have to start everything from scratch. The game is long, slow paced most of the time. If I have to restart again from scratch... Not sure I will do it.I have a thumb up for all the pleasure I have discovering the universe and all its possibilities. Also for the excitement in some situation, especially with some predators and the couple of situations you can face them. If you stay in the trees, you are quite safe and you can continue to explore and grind. Reading the doc in the menu is a mandatory.Saving in a game is a proven efficient concept since probably close to 20 years now. On a platform game, I can understand the checkpoints and it can be enough since the challenge is to achieve one piece of a map in between 2 checkpoints. Other cases, it is just a fail from the devs. Why could I not leave at any time and restart where I left my game? Why should I be forbid to test something and redo if I want by just loading my own save done just before my action.Here I used to have 6 babies. just by trying to have a new settlement for the first time, I loss one, I loss one adult as well...Because of this, all the nice progresses I did till then are crippled. But why while making a game which is by nature supposed to please, devs frustrate people and make their game unpleasant... It's trying to make you feel like you're a monkey with no idea how to ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ do anything trying to figure out what building even is or what plants are or what animals are. The game reminds me a lot of spore in the creature stage where you go around as a primitive thing trying to level up to become less primitive. I can understand why some people really hated this game because it's really unforgiving at some times but I also don't understand why anybody would love this game. The whole thing of this game was it's like marmite you either love it or you hate it but I have no idea how you would love this game. in the end it just turns into a massive collection game where you have to really slowly go through the giant map looking for things that you missed because you really wanted to get out the jungle. It's kinda fun to be a monkey climbing trees and ♥♥♥♥ but all together it just gets really annoying really quickly and you notice that the game does ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ things like every now and then a tiger jumps out of nowhere and attacks you but to dodge the attack you need to hold down A/X and then let go, but if you let go too early it hits you. I always ♥♥♥♥ this up because the fastest way to get about in this game is to halo jump (constantly press A/X) this means every now and then when you're exploring you have to go back to your base because this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cat came out of nowhere. You can't kill it as well it's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ just keeps coming back.Overall I'd give this game a 6/10 not really worth playing but kinda cool. i would've really liked it if I could've progressed as a human and made a small tribe or something but the game cuts off when you reach the first actual human, before that you're just a kinda humanish ape that walks a tiny bit. _childDocuments_.review: I love this game but it is not for everyone. Getting used to the UI/ somewhat janky and unintuitive controls (keys have multiple functions which can lead to some very annoying situations) will take some time and it is definitely a steep learning curve. Combat doesn't really change throughout the game and it isn't hard to master. Personally I found the most enjoyment in the game exploring the map and interacting with Pleistocene fauna which is (most of the time) beautifully animated, especially in the fight cutscenes. Being able to hunt large animals such as hippopotamuses, rhinos and elephants is incredibly satisfying. The stalker cat will also keep you on your toes thtought the game and really make sure you don't ever feel completely safe while playing just as our ancestors did 2million years ago. Overall a great game for lovers of natural history but not without its flaws.

_childDocuments_.review: Great concept, but the controls are awful, mechanics are not intuitive whatsoever, and the game needs some significant effort to be more player-friendly. Controls and mechanics are function terribly and many are not explained whatseoever.Dodging predators is practically impossible - I had to watch a youtube tutorial for more information because the tutorial gives you almost no information, and still I don't know what I'm doing. _childDocuments_.review: Panache Digital Games came up with a game we always desired. Start your journey from scratch and evolve accordingly. There are not many restrictions imposed on the players. If you want to tarry with your group and don’t leave the settlement, you are free to do so, or gather your clan and evolve throughout a journey of exploring new kinds of stuff. Feel the adventure of surviving the world that ages up to 10 million years ago. Monitor the growth of your hominids as you traverse, explore, survive, and evolve through time. Carry on your knowledge and discoveries to the new evolved generation. The game is slow-paced because of its “help yourself” idea and might feel frustrating sometimes. With the numerous possibilities, you can surely grind a good chunk of hours.Ancestors has a slow-paced complex gameplay that might feel frustrating over time. The gameplay might vary according to your playstyle. If you want to stay close to the settlement and increase your domestic skills, then your gameplay might omit danger from wild animals and fear of the unknown. Migrating your settlement to search the unfamiliar lands might inflate tremendous danger and can wipe your entire lineage. The controls feel too complex and are not fun. Climbing and swinging through the trees is frustrating. Most of the time, you will experience difficulty locating the next branch to jump on, as the tree positioning is weird and poorly made. One button can perform multiple operations, which can result badly in certain situations. You are supposed to educate the species about every possible useful kind of stuff, from sticks to rocks to edibles. Establishing communication between the clan is very important, as you will need to switch characters to keep the evolution going. The idea presented is pretty good, but it lacks proper execution.  The graphics are not bad, neither wondrous, but they are quite enjoyable and don’t affect the gameplay. It lacks details in the interaction of characters with the environment. It looks more of an old game instead of a new-gen game. Keeping in mind that this is a new concept game and the development team had limited funds at that time, this is quite promising. The map is enormous with numerous focal points , and also very diverse flora and fauna. Some of the effects like fear of the unknown and infection are pretty good. But somehow, these above-average graphics require good GPU power, which is quite unusual. The cinematics are top-notch with great story portraits and realistic quality graphics. Little things like dream showcases and animal fight cinematics bring an extra level of detail to the game.Don’t rush things, learning is a slow process. Most of the time, you will have to figure out the solution yourself. Turning down the music will help a lot, as most of the actions in-game are executed on a beat. Without spoiling too much, we can say that both hands are useful and can craft wonders. Most of the players neglect to carry a child, but actually, they provide you extra experience, and you can carry up to 2 of them. This is an interesting detail of the game that you will undergo during the exploration of new regions. When you are away from your familiarized territory, your character will feel scared and might enter the state of hysteria. This will result in losing your current clan member, and you will return to your main settlement. To conquer this, focus on your senses and identify the elements nearby. If your hominids recognize them, he will feel confident and will calm itself.The game’s objective is to finish the evolution before the actual time that was taken according to history. So your first objective is to enhance your species and not a sole character. Tarrying on one character will influence your progress and might back-fire. Keeping the clan guarded and prosperous is your foremost goal. This concept certainly raises our expectations and makes us biased towards the game. The story should have been stretched to the start of human civilization, but it ends at a generation switch that feels incomplete. It provides a mesmerizing experience to the gamers. Recommended buying during a sale.Rating: 7/10Reviewer:  Walking on two feet.

_childDocuments_.review: I've binge gamed this specimen of a "game" for a while now and I can definitively recommend against others playing it.This game is not hand holding at all, in fact the game insists you figure out how to do things in a trial and error way, as if you were an early primate working out the wonders of the world for yourself. That is unless you wiki that aspect out of the game like a first timer playing minecraft.This game is tedious. You may want to go ahead and unlock all the "skills" in the "skill tree" first thing as I did only to have your knuckles wrapped when you progress your lineage to the next generation only to find all of your skills are now missing. To keep your abilities you must assign points based on the number children your hominids have before progressing to the next generation. A whole new level of tedium arises when you consider the sheer amount of things to learn in the game. Not only that, but you can learn through mutations that only come from a random chance during birth that you need to see through to death to make permanent. So late game when the only neurons left to fire up are the ones that need to be mutated you'll find yourself spawning hominids just to swiftly send them to their deaths in your efforts to create the super hominid of your dreams. INCREDIBLY BORING.Otherwise the game is pretty, you get to play as a band of monkey-like creatures intimidating anything that comes near, because the fighting is unintuitive and boring anyway. Like press x to not die, or rather hold it and release after the chime, gets boring fast. It's neat to see your hominid brutally shove pointy sticks into the still-living eye sockets of your enemies only so many times.But yeah, survival, with ape like creatures, "real to life" tedium of evolving one aspect at a time over years, and it will feel like years, to get one upgrade that you likely wont notice while playing anyway, doesn't make for a great game. If you do pick it up despite this warning, don't expect to love this. People who play this game likely play simulation games, for the mind numbing, repetitive, grindy, brain-shutting-off, time killing nature of it.Some people may like it, but I doubt many will.In spite of all this, I'm going to finish it, pray for me.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: 9/10. Buy it if you can make the commitment to playing it the way it was meant to be played.Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey is a very unique game on the market. It follows the idea of human evolution. As the player, you are responsible for taking your clan of hominids from something very similar to a chimpanzee to ♥♥♥♥ ergaster, which was supposedly a precursor to ♥♥♥♥ sapiens, and everything in between.I highly encourage you to play this game without looking up any hints online. The idea of this game is that you can use your own human learning to discover new things about this game, which is represented by your evolutionary progress. The process is very immersive, and a great many things can simply be figured out by using your innate ability as a modern human to learn new things.The game very much rewards you for playing in the way that you want to play. If you often try to intimidate predators, you will get better at intimidating predators. If you do so in a group, you will get better at communication. If you often hunt with tools, it will become easier for you to make tools. If you prefer to dodge out of the way of predators rather than attack, you'll become more proficient in that too.The process for evolving is very easy to understand. Doing activities matures neurons and gives you neuronal energy to develop them into new abilities. When passing a generation, you can reinforce a certain number of those abilities so that the neurons don't need to be developed again (this is usually equal to the number of kids in your clan). Finally, an evolutionary leap will allow you to leap many thousands of years and allow you to develop genetic mutations that have come up throughout the generations.There are only a few minor complaints I have with this game. First, the AI of your fellow clan members is abysmal. They don't eat unless you eat around them or give them food directly. Even while you're away from your settlement, your fellow clan members just stand there and don't take care of themselves at all. They don't even sleep at night. In addition, the combat is entirely reactive. There's no ranged combat, either. I would have loved to be able to throw a rock at the crocodile waiting at the bottom of the tree for me, or throw my sharpened stick at the gazelle that was yet unaware of me, but no such ability exists. Perhaps that's intentional. Lastly, I would have loved to be able to play as ♥♥♥♥ ergaster! We do get to see what they look like in the ending cinematic but it's not possible to play as them. I do partially understand this though, because the ability to control fire would radically change the dynamic of the game. My hope is that the developers could make either an expansion or a sequel so we can continue to evolve.Many people have complained about the controls of this game, but I played this game for 72 hours with a keyboard and never found them to be a problem. Some might prefer to use a controller, however.Pros:- Great visuals- A great many opportunities to exercise the innate abilities of your own human brain- You're rewarded for nearly everything you can do- Intuitive evolution system that gives the game a cycle and makes it fun to learn new abilitiesCons:- Horrible AI for clan members, they're basically useless- Combat is totally reactive- Inability to play as the final evolutionOverall, this game easily receives a 9/10 from me. Progression is slow, but it is steady. Making discoveries feels just as rewarding for the player as it does for the character. If you're willing to make the commitment to learning, absolutely buy this game.

_childDocuments_.review: In an industry saturated in sequels, re-releases and bald-faced ripoffs, this game gets my thumb-up just for representing a new IP with a novel premise.And yet, sadly,  isn't something I can recommend to everyone... because it isn't for everyone. Going into this with expectations that you're about to play a typical open-world survival game is a sure road to disappointment.  is willfully, stubbornly esoteric; even the HUD doesn't provide any comforting familiarity and will take some time to understand, playing into the game's overarching theme. That theme is discovery, and as a reflection of it, the gameplay is alien and somewhat impenetrable. The game won't hold your hand much, and you must largely figure things out on your own.What do you get if you manage to overcome 's initial curve? You get about 50-60 hours of pleasant ambient exploration, some lessons in anthropology, surprisingly cathartic kill animations, and the simple joy of hearing baby chimpanzee squeaks wherever you go.Full disclosure: I took a few courses in anthropology during college. The foreknowledge it gave me might count as cheating at this game. It also means I knew what a sahelanthropus was before playing , and if that doesn't earn me nerd cred, I don't know what will. But I swear to all the gods, the next one of you that calls the player characters "monkeys" is getting a lecture!

_childDocuments_.review: So I played like the whole day it came out. This game is pretty good. For me it was mostly trial and error, I was tempted to look up guides but I decided not to. You learn a lot as you play, it takes a while but it's fun for me. You learn strategies on how to do certain stuff, such as fending off attacking enemies. _childDocuments_.review: Whoever commissioned, greenlit, and designed a company splash animation of a jump scare of a moose being run over should never be allowed to touch video games again.Just trying to get into the game requires sitting through so much pretentious nonsense, including credits for all the people involved in the game, probably because they know if they don't assault you with it from the beginning, no one would see them due to lack of caring enough to check them out from the settings.The game tries so hard to sell itself as some sort of 'experience' with an epic monologue intro to set the scene that only accomplishes getting a cringe response at how hard its trying to sell itself as more than a modern ripoff of Tokyo Jungle,After seeing the icon used to depict Left and Right click I almost puked, it is by FAR, the WORST way to depict left and right mouse buttons in any video game ever made, combined with the arts and farts intro monologue, and the opening credits to the 'developers' its obvious no one working on this game has ever  a game before, and that they're not even trying to make a game. This is an art student 'experience', not a game, and not one I want to bother spending more time on than I already have. The controls and gameplay are so clunky and counter-intuitive, it feels less like being a monkey fighting for survival, and more like trying to wrestle a monkey for your own survival. You have to fight almost every instinct learned from any other game, and try not to develop RSI trying to learn how the controls and mechanics are intended to work. I truly cannot stress enough how much this does not play like any other video game, and that is an insult, not a compliment. Prompts will for example tell you to press a button to 'remember' something, however this does not change if you already remember that thing, meaning you instead forget it. The only time the prompt changes is immediately after you 'remember', so if you leave an area and try to follow the 'remember' prompt, you will just forget the things you previously added to your memory, It's gameplay aspects like that that really indicate lack of awareness as to what a game does versus what a game needs to do. If you're trying to innovate and create a new experience, do so with the options in actions in the game NOT through trying to reinvent the wheel by giving them bumps in the form of completely warping controls and core gameplay mechanics anyone who  played a single video game before is familiar with. A completely backwards approach to innovative game design.This will definitely be enjoyable for the kind of steam user who loves games like The Witness, where the game is more about taking in the beautiful graphics and being left alone to explore and enjoy the game without popups and menus, but do not be deceived by the 'hehe monke' reviews thinking you'll play a monkey roleplay survival experience, or an upgrade to the gameplay you would find in Tokyo Jungle. If you want a  that focuses on generational survival where you can play as a monkey, just go emulate Tokyo Jungle, and stay away from this up-its-ass interactive ''retelling of the story of evolution''

_childDocuments_.review: I review most games based on one criterion in particular and the rest is secondary.  That criterion is control.  This game fails in this aspect, ruining access to any and all cool parts that might be beyond.  You play as an ape, at least to start.  Have you ever seen an ape move through familiar territory?  They are parkour masters.  They move from swinging on a branch to hopping across a log to another branch like living water.  Animals are extremely kinesthetic.  The apes in this move like uncomfortable people in gorilla suits.  They fly past obvious holds and plummet to the forest floor, somehow surviving anyway.  I suspect the devs looked at the cost and effort of making a good control/movement system and said, 'Nah, just turn down fall damage.'  The quicktime events are just as dumb in this as they are in everything else (excluding rhythm games) so I won't get into how pointless and lazy they are.When the controls are this bad it ruins the experience of anything else the game might have to offer, so unless you particularly enjoy the sensation of hitting buttons and just hoping it goes well, find something else to play.  Even if you do enjoy that, there are better games, really.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a mix of GTA 5 or RDR2 (where you don't die but get out of a hospital, or "wake up" somewhere near the place you "almost died", and it always cost you some ingame money), and a grinding survival shooter/fighter game like Assassin's Creed or Kingdom Come: Deliverance(you grind to get better, and get perks, and you fight your way through the game, cause you need to fight/kill some people to survive). This game only has autosave, which cannot be disabled. It also has manual saves by sleeping in your bed, but like Ironman in Crusader Kings, you only have 1 save. And there is no normal mode or Hardcore mode, there is only one mode. So you cannot practise, you can only play, and see where you land. It's the ultimate realistic evolution of ape to man. It's so realistic, that you can actually fail the game, or you can fall behind because you "died" or got lost a few times. There is no reload, only doing a new playthrough. This makes the game almost impossible to play, and much less fun to play.Now to make it easy, all reasons why this game is ♥♥♥♥ at this very moment, 6th of August, in the year 2022:- Only one save slot per playthrough.- Only one difficulty setting/level(there are some helpful hints but you still find yourself running to Reddit).- Autosave after making a mistake in your own eyes, so you cannot go back and undo what you did; all you can do is restart or start a new playthrough.- It only feels like a game when you are so injured or hungry or wahtever, that you cannot continue, and are placed in your "village", where you wake up. But it feels more realistic because there are no saves you can load in real life either.Either make this game more dynamic by giving multiple options and saves, so we can reload a previous save, and maybe introduce the so called Ironman mode if people want to get achievements.Or give me and others who thought this would be a fun game our money back.It's a fair choice. It's a good looking game, but the fun gets sucked out if you need/want to redo something because you didn't do it quite as well as you wanted, or your reputation with someone has fallen. The last one is a big reason people reload a save in other games, cause we are softies.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been playing PC games since the early '80s (mostly strategic and RPGs), and as you can figure out I have seen almost everything there is to see. But this is an absolute masterwork, no kidding!Yes, you are not an invincible superhero breaking heads with a mace or burning your enemies alive casting fireballs from level 1.... yes, your tribe will most probably be wiped at least three or four times until you understand the game mechanics... yes, to figure out the properties of everything you can eat or find in the jungle is not easy at first, and you will have to use some ingenuity (a lot, indeed) to find out what to do with a certain material and how to build and use a certain tool... but after living moments of pure terror or deep embarassement you will (probably) figure it out... and you will realize who we are. Starting at a very low level in the food web, you will learn why we were living (ar least at first) on trees. You will understand the value of the team. You will realize that the first way to survive is reproducing at a rate higher than the toll in casualties the jungle will make you pay. And, at last, you will realize who we are: explorers, tool makers, and above all... deadly hunters-killers! I came to a point where my species is developing the capability to defend and attack in a team, and with our pointed sticks now we are rapidly ascending the ladder of the food web. Now are the other animal the ones learning to fear us!To make a long story short, a game that I strongly recommend, even if probably is not a game for everyone.I guess it will not be attractive  to FPS masters, even if once a while I play them too, as its pace is relatively slow (relatively!). And some of you willl hate the idea of grinding, knowing that  all in a sudden a Machairodus (an ancestor of the saber tooth tiger) can jump on you all in a sudden from behind, this is not for you :DMake sure you play with a controller, though. I have an old Logitech Dual and had some problems configuring  it, but solved them installing the X360CE emulator. I haven't played with the keyboard but the fact that the tutorial gives you the commands only referring to the controller is definitely a down. Now, time to get back to the jungle!"Taaar-maan-ganiii"!!!!

_childDocuments_.review: Well this is something you won't find anywhere else, 'monkey simulator 2020'. In saying that, this is a niche game and will appeal to only a select few, so ignore the majority of the negative reviews as they are nit picky. We get to play as monkey people millions of years ago as they start making their way toward human evolution. This is done through exploration of the environment and your monkey's skills with the addition of raising your monkey families. So what does this mean for the game overall? Grindy grindy grindy! It's a constant battle of trial and error, of which the consequences from mistakes can be dire to say the least. That exploration is what makes this game fun. I highly recommend going into this one blind and without walkthroughs, because the discovery aspect is what creates the enjoyment. The satisfaction is real as you discover new ways to survive and move along the evolutionary chain.Most peoples biggest gripe with this game is the controls. I'll say this, if a game opens with “best experienced with a controller”, then don't use a mouse and key board! Playing the actual game does come with a steep learning curve, but the in-game tutorial holds your hand enough to keep the pace moving while not revealing too much. At first it's extremely tense as you are constantly being hunted down by predators, always playing on the back foot, constantly in survival mode. However, after you get into a groove in regards to the overall formula, you can really start to dominate each region you take over. Once you hit that aforementioned groove, the tension dies right down and overall game-play becomes very placid. At this point you really need to be the 'sim enthusiast' type to enjoy the game as there is a lot of rinse and repeat. Even if you're not that type of player, what saves the game is the very nice visuals and expansive environment that is always open to explore.Like I said above, this game does not cater for everyone as it is very particular with what it's trying to achieve. But it hit's the mark with what it tries to achieve, even if it's not for everyone. I did find the novelty wearing off at the end of my run, but that was after 20 odd hours of game-play. Well worth the price if it interests you as you won't find anything else like it.

_childDocuments_.review: imagine hideo kojima wanted to make a game solely about being an ape and this is what you'd get. for better or worse, there truly is no other game like it. i really liked this game but it has one glaring issue - how it ends. i remember wishlisting this before release but didn't actually get it until it was featured in a humble monthly, and i just got around to playing it. you get thrown in with basically zero direction so you have to fend for yourself, which i really liked. though you really don't need any direction, you just play, survive, and evolve. it's been out for over two years and there are plenty of other reviews that can go into better detail than i can, so after repeating that i thoroughly enjoyed every minute i spent playing, i'll tell you what i really hated.. you can't complete it.. or at least i couldn't. maybe with prior knowledge and proper planning someone could, but i didn't have that luxury on my first playthrough. i didn't know the game has a hard stop after you get to a certain point in your evolution, and you need to evolve in order to lock in genetic mutations (basically perks/traits). there aren't any achievements related to this, or any missable achievements for that matter, but i would've kept playing to unlock all the genetic mutations and evolution feats. yet i literally can't. evolving leads to the credits with the only viable option to reload. so, that sucks. i'd love to see a patch or mod to fix this.

_childDocuments_.review: The concept of the game is great, but the gameplay completely falls apart. Simply said, Ancestors is an open world survival game. You eat, drink, procreate, sleep, fight, craft and go out exploring (not essentially in this order). Sounds fun? Maybe in the first 5 hours or so, before you realize those are all the actions the game has to offer. You repeat this set of actions on different parts of the map until you make enough discoveries that make you and your clan evolve through million of years. Most of these actions can be done by simply holding down a button, while some like fighting only include one boring QTE. Sprinting and jumping is tied to the same button and often lead me to some risky moments when I didn't want to jump off the tree but I did and got injured. Overall commands feel really clunky and not intuitive.The tutorial is mostly lacking and doesn't really explain things well, which can result in some confusing moments when the game asks you to do something, but you have no idea where you should start. Even the UI is so minimal that during the first hours you will have an hard time understanding your stats and the useless radar on the corner.The progression system is disappointing and completely defeats the game purpose. After million of years you are supposed to evolve and retain what you learned, instead you are forced to restart with mostly your basic skills and grind all over again. Every time you evolve you respawn on a random location that you previously explored, meaning you can be brought back to any of your first explored areas and will need to move to your latest ones if you want to continue discovering new lands. Having to restart from distant locations not only is time consuming, but it's also quite frustrating. Unfortunately, the world around you stays exactly the same with no variation after million of years and the same goes for animals.Clan growing options are disappointing too. You can make them follow you but they are completely brainless and most of the time they will just stare at a predator coming for them instead of getting on a tree like I do. This means that bringing your clan with you while exploring can be completely annoying as you have to do lot of baby sitting and if they die you will lose "points" when evolving or possibly risk a game over due to extinction. Even after evolving they never really help you in any crafting or fighting activity; you need to put items on their hands so they can replicate what you do. So while you evolve they basically stay the same, unable to do anything on their own without your commands.The open world looks good and has different biomes, but it's maybe too big and there is not enough variety of content. There are only a few animals and hostile predators, some food and a few materials to craft. For some reason they didn't add snakes on trees, which makes them the safest way to move around the map (although not always will be possible).In conclusion, Ancestors is the classic game that looks great from the trailers and probably for the first ten hours too, but just like you learn how to survive and discover new lands, you will also unveil the hidden repetitiveness of the gameplay and the pointless progression system. Fair warning: while I didn't play the game 'til the end and probably never will, I have to admit that the ending I saw online could have gotten me mad, particularly after 40+ hours of gameplay. I don't recommend the game, but if you are still going to play it I strongly suggest to avoid wasting much time on it.
_childDocuments_.name: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey

_childDocuments_.review: Totally unique, a vast land to discover, hunt, gather, build, communicate, have children, befriend outsiders, evolve.I have never played anything quite like this before. You start as an early ape like species with no knowledge of your surroundings or your own abilities. This is really a game of learning how to play the game. There are no tutorials. You have to figure things out for yourself but that is also part of what makes it a really interesting experience. Its also what makes it hard at first.Trying to survive in a hostile environment is no easy task. You are always having to balance risks with potential rewards. Stray too far from clean water or food and you could starve to death. Eat the wrong food and you could end up disorientated and lost. Fall too far or get attacked by a hostile creature and your injuries could be fatal or leave you bleeding to death or with broken bones. Slowing you down. Making you an easier target. You could lose everything you have worked for. That is unless you managed to find a mate and had children with who can pass on your genes and your skills.There are planned sequels to this game as the evolution of the species doesn't take you all the way to modern humans. Hopefully they will be made.This is another highly recommended game.

_childDocuments_.review: To open, I imagine this game is "Australia simulator", where everything wants to kill you. It's not hard to survive, really. However everything wants you dead, and perhaps as a nice snack. The trees are safer but not totally(i won't spoil THAT WTF moment).I love the concept and I even love the majority of the gameplay, it's a unique idea in a field of redundant shooters, platformers, etc. HOWEVER where the concept falls flat is the controls, they're not absolutely horrible but I can't count the number of times my monke has failed to grab  a branch and goes falling to the forest floor, even better when there's a predator below waiting to "wtf pwn me" with a rodeo backflip attack.Literally got eaten by a croc that somehow managed to lunge halfway up my tree from behind itself. While this hasn't been typical I think with a bit more care and attention to detail this could have been a revolutionary game that would have influenced future game concepts and development. The game otherwise runs well, without any major bugs yet. IMO the one thing that brings this game down to being frustrating to deal with isn't the difficulty or lack of hand holding. It's absolutely the controls and dodge mechanics. If they would fix those issues and improve them I would give this game a solid 10/10 for being an innovative and unique MUST PLAY. However the controls mar an otherwise wonderful experience. Which in my opinion still leaves it at a 7-8/10. If the Devs ever improve the controls and tree jumping mechanics on mouse and keyboard, I'll update the review to reflect as such.In conclusion, if you're willing to deal with a few issues with poor controls and the game looks interesting to you as a concept, and the game is on sale. You probably won't regret your purchase but there are times you'll curse the terrible control mechanics and it will cost you a clan members life because of it far too often.

_childDocuments_.review: Bought Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey wanting to scratch my Stone Age survival itch not realizing the game ends once you become ♥♥♥♥-Ergaster meaning you spend the whole game as an Ape/Ape-man and this certainly made me sad but I ended playing the game all the way through and beat it. While it's not a perfect game at all I found myself enjoying swinging from the branches and exploring the MASSIVE game world.The Good stuff: - Fun Ape antics such as swinging on branches and climbing EVERYTHING- Exploration is quite fun and each location is unique or at the very least distinct- Each biome is unique and introduces new creatures and challengesThe Bad stuff:- Survival in the beginning/mid-game is ridiculously easy, animals will hit you once and run off meaning combat is easily survivable.- Combat becomes trivial once you master the timing (and it only gets easier as you evolve). My ape from 10 MYA to 1 MYA was a one man extinction machine with only a rock and a wooden spear. It's the ultimate combo.- Who in God's name thought making your company's visual credit (which plays at full blast when you start the game) a jump scare was a good idea. Yeah I'm docking Good Game Points over this because it's obnoxious.In conclusion I'd recommend this if you love Human Anthropology or expansive exploration games.As a note to the Devs I think this game, despite it's low points, is quite entertaining and I'd love to see either a sequel or DLC which let's you play as ♥♥♥♥-Habilis up to ♥♥♥♥ Sapien; this would be something I think many would be interested in, especially if you're given the choice to play as some of Humanity's cousins such as the Neanderthals or Denisovans.

Early game is tough, every loss is tragic, 10/10 would recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: To the developers, the game is good and it has a lot of potential. I hope you guys don't give up on it. This game has heart. You'll probably get the hang of it a lot faster than any ape. - If you are a fan of the Planet of the Apes movies, you would enjoy this game. But there are elements that I wish the game would have like a clash/union of 2 clans, a coordinated attack on an animal as a group. Or maybe see a few remnants of an old civilization lying around.. I'd love to see an ape scratch their head over an old and rusty AK-47, but yeah, that would be a stretch. - The developers don't need to make the game suuuuper realistic, so why not add a few bits of fun like drawing/scratching on the rock walls with a stone?? It might not be 'historic' but what the hecc do we know?! - More building please and a way to order other apes to build at a specific location. Why can't we use a rock to chip wood off of trees...

_childDocuments_.review: DISCLAIMER: THE ENDING OF THE GAME IS VERY UNSATISFYING: You only get a short animation of neanderthals walking. And then it ends. Very boring ending. Not worth all the effort to get to it.The game is fun and enjoyable for a while, you discover new things and slowly progress, dodging predators, then scaring them off, then killing them. The game at first plays like an adventure/discovery game. The game is all about discovering new things and "progressing". Once you get to the final area of the map though, the beach, the game stagnates. You realise there is no more new content left, and you now have to go back to all the previous areas to unlock every "evolution point" to evolve. These include things like, killing all animal types, dodging all animal types, using all healing plants, intimidating all animal types, etc... This is not fun at all, and even annoying like it was in my case, trying to get a white rhino to spawn for hours so I could kill it to evolve. And after all that work, you're rewarded with a short animation of neanderthals taking a few steps. No gameplay, no big cutscene, no in-game scripted event to end the game with, no playing as a neanderthal, no making fire. Also you never get to make proper tools. The furthest extent tools go is "sharpened stick" and rocks. You don't get to make a spear with a flint head. No fire-making. So the ending of the game is truly unsatisfying. However you will have good fun for 20 hours as you discover the game. So I'd say it's worth it on a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: In this game, you play as a family of monkeys.  Your mission is to keep these monkeys alive through generations lasting millions of years in order to adapt, overcome, and evolve to a higher form.  You gain experience in different areas by simply doing stuff.  Standing up and walking increases your motricity skill allowing you to eventually permanently walk on two legs.  Hitting rocks against sticks increases your dexterity and hand/eye coordination making it easier to hit rocks against sticks.  Sniffing plants will eventually make you better at sniffing plants.  This is a game about learning and exploring by doing.The controls are a little weird and not super intuitive at first but once you get a handle on it, it's not that bad.  The game plays a bit like a mix between a survival game and doodle god where you're bashing different kinds of rocks against other rocks or sticks to see what you get out of it.  Then figure out ways of using said rocks/sticks.There's not a whole lot of tutorialization to this game so the beginning might be a little rough but the core premise of this game is that you're a monkey trying to figure things out.  .  In the beginning you start as a helpless monkey but by the end you're a gang of stick-wielding badasses stabbing elephants, rhinos, and sabretooth tigers to death.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an interesting game. Take your usual Ubisoft fare like Far Cry with its exploration mechanics and revealing points of interest on a map, add a survival system with hunger and injury management, throw in a bit of colony management with leading your clan to nests closer to resources, then link it all together with tech trees that advance as you unlock skills by experimenting with your environment.Don't get too attached to your first ape colony, however. To reach your full potential, you will need to selectively breed beneficial mutations into your bloodline and advance time to allow them to become permanent traits. As time is such a relevant mechanic in this game, your apes will age and die, passing on their knowledge to the next generation.It's definitely not a fast-paced game. You can fight tigers and snakes, swing through the trees at breakneck speed, and reach nearly every corner of the map, but these aren't the core of the game. If you're looking for a game with a unique take on survival, this could scratch that itch. Return to monke.

_childDocuments_.review: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey stands out as a truly unique game, offering an experience unlike any other. Its innovative approach to gameplay, combined with a beautiful and intriguing world, sets it apart in the gaming landscape.The game features an in-depth progression system that is both fascinating and rewarding. However, this complexity is also its biggest drawback. The mechanics are poorly explained, leading to a steep learning curve that can be both confusing and frustrating. This lack of guidance can make the game feel unwelcoming to new players, which is a shame given its potential.Ancestors is brimming with fresh ideas and awe-inspiring moments that can genuinely blow your mind, provided you have the patience to push through its initial challenges. The game’s premise—evolving and surviving as early hominids—is compelling and offers a unique perspective on human history.Despite its flaws, Ancestors could greatly benefit from a complete remake or a sequel that refines its mechanics and offers better guidance. Such improvements would help unlock the game’s full potential and make it more accessible to a wider audience.If you’re intrigued by the concept and are willing to invest time in learning its systems, Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey can be a rewarding experience. It’s worth considering if you find it on sale and don’t mind consulting guides to help you navigate its complexities. With patience and persistence, you might find yourself deeply immersed in this ambitious and thought-provoking game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the second time I've uninstalled this game due to what I can only perceive as a bug where I am hunted and attacked day and night by the same white tiger regardless of my position on the enormous map. I honestly want this to be a bug because if it's a feature, its a HORRIBLE game ruining feature. I really want to love this game because I enjoy the moments when I'm not being hunted (which I almost always am now) but the fact that I can spend 2-3 hours fortifying a rest area with fencing that should keep anything out only to be woken up from EVERY sleep cycle by - again - the SAME white tiger is absolutely inexcusable.  This includes instances where the white tiger SPAWNS INSIDE MY FORTIFIED ENCAMPMENT.Like I love the challenge the predators add, the incentive to stay in a tree to avoid threats while also need to be on the ground to collect a lot of resources but this bug, this mechanic, whatever it is, is the dumbest thing and sucks every last drop of enjoyment this game had to offer me. I should not be under constant threat from the same one predator day in and day out, hindering any actual progress I could ever make with my tribe while simultaneously making any defenses I build or any environmental advantage I attempt to take 100% obsolete. You could make the argument that this is a realistic environment, and I'd agree, hell so much about this game is so realistically immersive- that's a large appeal of the game to me: the very bare bones "figure it out yourself" experience. However realism does not always equal enjoyment, and in this case, it actual destroys any enjoyment I could possibly have. Again, this is considering that this is feature rather than some sort of bug.  I'm inclined to go with the latter because of how this EXACT predator spawns at regular intervals at my exact position out of nowhere with no provocation at all times (if that's not a bug then HOOOOO BOY what were the developers thinking.)Regardless I've no intention of re-installing until I can play the game in a manner where any progress I make matters even slightly rather than losing 1-2 tribe members every 20-30 minutes to the same predator that is seemingly omnipotent and multi-dimensional.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't listen to all the bad reviews, they are just people who don't understand what this game is really about. This game in my short time playing is cool and unique.many people are complaining about the controls being weird, well guess what, it tells you it is best played with a controller, so people complaining about weird controls with keyboard are morons. People complaining about unskippable cutscenes are either blind or lying, since you can skip all cutscenes except for the opening one.This game is meant to be difficult, it tells you it won't hold your hand through out it. You are meant to explore and try out new things in this unknown world, test different things, bang different types of rocks together, munch on the strange new fruit. This is a game of exploration and survival.The reason some things you can't do in the beginning is because you haven't unlocked it yet, you need to learn and reinforce the skills into your tribe of early Human ancestors. your meant to fail and then learn from those failures. I kept getting food poisoning from these berries in the first base area until I learned to look for the brighter pinkish red ones which were better to eat. I learnt bashing obsidian and Granite rocks can create a grinder which makes making a healing plant easier and more effective. A really cool thing I found out is you can throw things in your hand by holding down the button for altering (or dropping, Can't remember since it has been almost a day since I last played at the time of writing this) if you have nothing in the other hand.I give this game a solid 9/10.It looks great.It sounds great.The mechanics are solid.It is a very interesting concept and premise.This game is meant to be unforgiving, we are meant to fail and learn and try again. We are meant to explore and conquer our environment through trail and error. This is a true hardcore survival game, you will die, you will get hurt, you will get poisoned. But that is the point, you are meant to learn from it.Listening to the reviews with less then an hour in the game is pointless, as they have essentially only been in the gameplay section itself for like 10 minutes before giving up and whining about the game being hard and thus the game is garbage, rather then actually exploring and learning.

_childDocuments_.review: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey is a very interesting new approach on exploration, a small part survival and of course evolution of mankind from it's ape-like ancestors. You start as a youngling on the back of your mother, then all of a suddon comes a giant bird out of the air, attacks and kill your mother while you get lost in the dense and unkown jungle. You can walk, you have your senses to search the unknown, but you also feel fear. In fact in this simulation you can see 'fear' by shadows of sharp predator teeth shine out of the dark unkown. So you can try to reach your nest or hide in a hideout and wait for other members of your clan to find you. It is an open world experience and the center of your world is your clan and it's progress. You learn with every new item you encounter, with every tool you learn, with every item you may explore to craft with different tools. You use your natural senses to explore and your two hands to carry and craft. Eating, drinking, sleeping are the only things you have to care of on a regular frequency, but it isn't overwhelming, so you have plenty of playtime for the real core of the game, exploring and learning. In fact there is no real path, nevertheless the goal to become human is fixed. It is up to you, how to path to that goal. Every decission you make can be a step forward or just survival. The graphics are nice and suit that simulation quite well. In parts it reminds a bit on Subnautica, but with a more basic and natural biome, while you don't swim, but climb and jump to reach the interesting places. Advancing is related to your learning process by neurons you could reveal and which you combine with the children of your clan to give them forth to the next generation. A very cute and interesting way that represents how our ancestors may have struggled through the eons of time until they became human. It is (sadly) only singleplayer, but a lot of fun doing things learning-by-doing instead of following a given route. You have to learn every single step...like one quite basic early step is to learn to hand over things from one hand into the other, but also other things like you could poke a processed palm stick in a bee nest to gain new food - honey. It is a journey, a journey of learning and exploring how to do things, to learn for itself and to gain a very new perspective on how humans or in this case to-become-humans might learn. A very neat and interesting new game idea and hopefully there will be other games that take up this very unique gaming experience. Recommended? Yes, if you like open-world and life simulations, if you like to learn how animals or children might prosper in an unkown but very interesting surrounding. The parts of survival are mild and also crafting isn't the core, it is exploring that is the main attraction and the pure fun to climb and jump around in a dense jungle until you find new things to explore. Rumors tell, later you'll get into the savanna with threats like lions, elephants or water buffalo, but I am still only exploring the very start of this great journey. Linux is supported with Steam's Proton support and the game runs like native. If you could grab it on a sale, you can't do wrong. Have fun!

_childDocuments_.review: First impressions - beautiful graphics, loads of promise.But the tutorial is TERRIBLE. Make a bed. How? Google it. Pile up 5 leaves. So I do that. Nothing happens. No cue. Google it again. Stand on the leaves. Still doesn't work. Turns out you can't do this when you are a baby, which is what I've been since the start of the game and at no point has it either said that babies can't craft, or told me that I can actually swap to another character to get this done.  So I Google it (again). Swap characters. Get the bed. Now I have to make a couple How? Google it again. Groom a member of the opposite gender. Try that. They just shake me off constantly. Google it YET AGAIN. Apparently there should be some kind of "snipping" sound cue when you release B. No such sound cue. Either I'm deaf or it's bugged.I shouldn't have to be Googling every single thing I have to do in the first hour of a game. I get they are trying to be immersive here, but I set it on first-time player mode. I'm not an idiot. I've played tons of these types of games before, and most of them give you at least an idea of how to craft and interact other than "Make a couple".I get that this game is pretty new on Steam but my understanding is that it's been out on consoles for a while so they really should have sorted this out by now. I don't expect to be spoon fed, but at least some idea of how to achieve these nebulous goals without having to be constantly searching on the Internet for the wise words of those who have gone before and sworn at the screen going "Yes, I get what I have to do, but how?!"If they made the tutorial actually tutor you, this might be a fun game. Right now it's just frustrating. I shall persevere but it's not fun yet.I'm of a vintage where we had new games and didn't have the Internet to look stuff up all the time. Games had to be designed to teach you everything you needed to know to play them. These days they just get lazy and assume everyone is just going to watch a YouTube walkthrough instead.../edit To sum up - if you want a game to be immersive, making it so that people have to look on forums and walkthroughs every five minutes is not the way to achieve that./edit. Persevered. Turns out to groom you don’t just hold down B. You hold down B BEYOND the circle filling up. I can’t explain better than that. The mini game is not intuitive at all. Again, I get that they are trying to be immersive. The whole “being a monkey” part needs to be just up to you. But the interaction between you and the game needs to be either intuitive or explained. Monkeys don’t need to be taught how long to press a button to pick a flea off a friend; they just see the flea and pick it off. We need to be able to see how to control, and this is very, very lacking. It just feels like they’ve used “we want it to be immersive, no help” as an excuse to not bother writing a decent controls tutorial.It does look really promising and if I could give it a 50/50 review I would. It’s just that the first few hours of this game are a hot mess and it’s jarring. I want to explore the mind of my ancestors, not breaking immersion all the time to find out why pressing the button it’s telling me to press isn’t working and then finding out it’s because I’m a baby and, I’ll say again, the game started with me as a baby and has made no attempt to tell me I don’t have to be a baby and in fact shouldn’t be a baby for this, the very first task.

_childDocuments_.review: For the record, the amount of hours on my steam profile doesn't reflect my total hours of game time, which included 100% the game on a different console. So this is going to be way longer than it should be but TL:DR: This game is niche, but if you like this niche and are willing to give it a try, you'll find a jewel of a game. THERE WILL BE SPOILERS! Now with that out of the way...Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey is a "simulation" of what types of events are believed to have transpired for the formation of humans. You start the game as the mythical "missing link" and evolve your way into animals we recognise today. As the game says to you from its start: there will be no guiding hand. Your linage lives and dies with you/your clan. Gameplay can be broken up into 5 phases -1.Explore2.Discover3.Learn4.Camp5.Evolve Exploring is self explanatory. You, or you and a group of how many other apes you chose from your camp, can venture out into the wilds in the hopes of finding new things. This is the most dangerous part of the game and where I have seen a lot of reviews express frustration with it. But in all honesty - the game is not hard. Exploring is dangerous if you do not approach it carefully or think ahead. If you treat exploring Ancestors like you would Skyrim, you will be seeing the death screen a lot, and eventually a game over. Early game you are a very small mammal at the bottom of the food chain, so think like they would and you'll find yourself much more successful. That doesn't mean you won't die while exploring, but each time you do die should be seen as a lesson. You can explore by swinging through branches, running along the forest floor, swimming, cave diving.... Wait, cave diving?Discovering is also semi self explanatory. As you explore, you use your various senses (such as smell and hearing) to discover new items (indicated by an audio and visual effect). As long as you have a baby with you, each of these new discoveries awards you with experience you can use later at camp. Your ape will make a unique animation based on whether the item can potentially be altered (when first grabbing a coconut and inspecting it, for example the ape has a very noticeable reaction to prompt the player to investigate further), whether its is bad to eat, etc. The game will not TELL you the berry you are about to eat is poisonous, but looking at how your ape reacts when inspecting something can tell you a lot about the potential of the item. The map itself is beautifully hand crafted, full of surprises and biomes I never thought I would see, and key locations offer you points for discovering them. I was repeatedly surprised and excited to find something I had never seen before and the biome evolution also reflects humanity's own evolutionary journey, which I think is a great touch.Learning and discovery go hand in hand as you'll be doing both as you play the game. The more abilities you unlock, the more ways you can discover items and even find novel uses for old ones. Again, the game never guides you on how to make a salve to give you a bonus to stealth, but mess around long enough and you will discover it. At most, if you have the HUD on, scanning an item can show if it has more than one use. With no HUD, you are left entirely in the dark. Learning also comes in the form of making mistakes. There are a lot of things out there bad for you to eat or drink, causing various status effects. Again it will be up to you the player to discover how to fix them, or what might even be causing these issues in the first place. The same can be said when dealing with predators and other animals.After a hard day of running away from giant snakes and tigers, you'll come back to your clan's camp. The "story" mode of the games starts you off at the same camp every time, but you can pick up your camp and move it at any time, to any place.  The starting camp is the most safe place on the map, so while new players are still learning the ropes, the audio for the camp quickly becomes a comforting one. At camp you can do a few things. You can switch between different members of your clan, mate with someone, birth babies, sleep and most importantly, "level up" here. Finally comes the evolution phase. As you play the game, you'll grow new neurons and get points to basically string them together, unlocking new abilities. These can be as simple as learning to use both hands, to something has historic and famous as learning to walk on two feet. Which neurons (abilities) you unlock and when depends on how you play as well as random luck. Once you chose to evolve and time-skip, those choices are locked into place for the rest of the game.  You'll develop your Locomotion faster for example if you try to walk a lot on two feet or swim, however some abilities are hidden behind chance. Each baby born has a chance to have a genetic mutation that, once they reach adulthood, can be permanently added to your species (new generations will share the traits you learned/gained). Because so many skills require unlocks from other skills, there is a chance you could be locked out of an entire branch of evolution just due to bad luck. The first time I beat the game I wasn't even an omnivore or able to walk on two legs because I had not hit the genetic jackpot.This will be your loop. As you evolve, your species will change and your abilities along with it. Because of how levelling works, you will naturally be pushed to explore further and further until maybe one day you'll even get to see the ocean....Moment to moment gameplay varies wildly from sitting at camp peacefully stripping branches to running desperately for your life from a group of lions who have already taken out one of your family. The game really shines as you watch , slowly, how your missing link takes their steps towards becoming a human. It also amazingly highlights why adaptations we have are crucial and maybe even things we take for granted now. Can't see over tall grass? Sure helps if you learn how to stand!The slow pace of the game will definitely be a turn off for a majority of players. It is a game that requires you to throw mud at the wall until something sticks, and then to figure out if that is even useful to you or not. This is not monkey assassin's creed and if you come into it thinking that like a lot of critics did you are going to be sad. The pace is a choice, not a flaw. And neither is the game being "hard". The game is obtuse on purpose and unforgiving, but it definitively is not hard. Especially in the late game where you basically become invisible. Think like a small scared monkey and you'll be okay.That doesn't mean that game doesn't have problems though despite my love for it. The game is full of bugs. And extremely bad ones. I have on several occasions lost clan members because they clipped through geometry and starved, or wouldn't come out of the water and therefor drown and just generally the A.I not being terribly smart. It can lead to a huge amount of frustration when trying to coordinate larger clans. Sometimes my entire clan spawns in invisible. Why? Who knows! Sometimes I grab a branch when I jump, sometimes I miss that exact same jump the next time. It's in those moments when the game becomes actually frustrating. Any time I have quit the game out of annoyance was after a long play session being ruined by some bug or another causing one of my apes to die.As a whole, I think this game is amazing if you are looking for a slow paced, semi-scientific look into human evolution in the form of a video game. It doesn't pretend to be what it's not. So go forth and be monke.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay... I tried.I won't say I tried everything. I barely scratched the surface. But I tried.To be honest, I like this game. It is intelligent and quite beautiful. But it suffers from flaws that makes it difficult to recommend, at least in the actual state.I find the camera very, very disturbing. Too close to the character. I understand there is probably a reason for this : it makes it more intimate, more close to the subjectivity of your character, without being a first person camera. But you lack situational awareness, and you have to fight with the camera just to gather some fruits. more than that : the angle of view is very narrow, it's like trying to shoot a movie with a long focal lens. It moves a lot and it isn't very precise, you spend your time being too much on the left, then on the right, then on the left again.This makes us talking about playability : The jumps when on trees should be automatically directed to an other branch or not jump at all. I don't have the ability to jump from trees to trees. I don't know what  kind of branches I can grasp or not, and since the camera is very clumsy, I really don't see where I am going. So there should be a mechanism that allows your characters to do those things with her own senses. Trees are dangerous, so maybe in a "hurry" mode you can jump freely and pray you find something to grab (and even then this would... (well actually it is already) be a nightmare since again, you don't see where you jump, you have to turn your camera so you can't go fast like a real tree animal would do...), but the default way should be from a safe place to an other safe place.Communications with other members of the herd/tribe is quite difficult to understand too. Actually, most of the interface is difficult. It is a mode style interface, but instead of having a key/button to leave a mode, you have to move to do it. So you spend generally a lot of time trying to understand/remember how to leave a mode, then you hit the button for an other mode, then you come back to the original mode you where in and then at last you understand that all you have to do is to move, you do it and you lost a lot of time just for that.Transitioning to time. The day is measured in hours. That's strange. I would have used sunrise, midday, midnight and other things like that, it would have been more intuitive and less destructive considering the immersive feeling this tries to give you.Time runs very fast too. Eating, drinking and sleeping is supposed to give you a durable satisfaction feeling, but you can't stop thinking about this watch showing time, every minutes going every seconds, and that you now have to hunt/gather and explore again. Most survival games does that, it gives a very "arcade" feeling, bringing you intensity and pushing you to think fast, while in real live, you spend a certain amount of time moving, gathering and hunting (which is an intense phase) and then resting, exploring and socialise for the species that are adapted to it. (a calm phase). Here, the calm phase is reduced to it's minimum.At last, I have a big problem with the introduction. Credits, videos, time-consuming presentation, you can't play directly, you have to watch all those names which are of course important (the team who made this game deserve recognition) but when you just want to play a game, that's an enthusiasm breaker.I would love to recommend this game. Especially since it's base on scientific method, it tries to respect what we know of those eras and our species, and it is very clever, intelligent, intuitive (except those exceptions I developed before) and deserves recognition.It is an important game in the gaming sphere. But it needs a lot of ameliorations before being considered a "good" game. I clearly recommend this game to anyone who is passionate by science, anthropology, palaeontology and biology.  This is a must for them.But as a video game, it needs a lot of work to make it better/more intuitive/more adapted to different styles of gaming (pressuring people to move fast and hunt and gather and move and hunt and start over without any rest isn't for everyone...) I have some suggestions, of course, because constructive criticism is easy but is worthless without trying to fix the problems : 1 : Put your credits to the end. I insist. Really. When you finish the game, the reward is the credits. It works in movies, in video games, it will work here. You have a "credits" button on the menu. It's great, it's enough. Or you could if you wish make the credits roll on the side while on the main menu, that's some name exposition here !2 : Allow skipping the video at the beginning. We get it. To eat ot to be eaten. "Skip". Allow it. It works. Everywhere else it works. It will work for you.3 : Allow a change of the clock's speed. Yeah, I know "gameplay". But you already have different difficulty levels. So just let people explore at their own rhythm, everyone isn't a hard core gamer able to run through thing with a focused mind for 2 hours. It is tiresome for a lot of us. A choice is better than no choice at all. Allow us.4 : allow to have a "safe" button for jumping. For instance, while keeping the jumping button on, the character will jump from branches to branches without hurting herself, direct the jump to the nearest possibility, or will stop if no options are available. And, if someone wants to test the limits and have fun, he/she will simply have to tap on the jump button once and the character will jump regardless of if there is a safe possibility or not, and everyone is happy. Please note that this is inspired from other videogames that found a good way to explore while jumping without making it impossible because of camera and lack of 3D perception and situational awareness.5 : camera should be more adapted to what we want to see. I don't have a specific suggestion here, most of this would be solve by point 6.6 : Allow a change of angle of view of the camera by the player. Either in the options or with a key or a combination of a button. Don't mix up camera distance from the subject and angle of view. One widen the angle, the other keeps the angle narrows but push the subject further away without solving anything. (the opposite is true : if you have a wide angle of view and people complains about it, pulling the subject nearer to the camera will only make things weirder...) You have a very interesting, very important game in this community of gamers, geeks and scientists. It is mainly well executed and only lacks those small things to make it better. I really suggest you do it, you give the option to people to tune it a bit to their own tastes and abilities, so this game is more universally recognised and allows players with different profiles to play it without having to sacrifice too much the difficulty. (when you have more time, you take it, it is still a menace in the long run, it just allows you to have more fun with the features that the game gives you and there are plenty ! Same for cameras !)Take care, this isn't a negative review, it is a "so so". I can't put a thumb up because a lot of people I know may take it as a great game without flaws and I can't honestly say this is it. But this isn't a bad game, it needs tweeks but it isn't bad at all. It is a great game that I can't play for now because it doesn't allows me to do so without being overstressed by time, clumsiness and lack of accessibility features.Still, congratulations. This is one of a kind.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely awesome concept of a game. I'm in the midst of a playthrough several million years in, and I'm having a total blast.Starting out and knowing nothing and just trying stuff out is really cool. Sometimes it works, sometimes it doesn't, and I really see the vision of learning to "become more human". The progression of going from a tree climbing and vine swinging wild animal into the gradual changes that make us humans is really ambitious. Any time I've done a "new thing" I get a huge rewarding feeling - especially killing something for the first time, the kill animation and my ape brothers getting hype made ME hype.I really haven't ever seen a game quite like this before, and it's scratched so many itches from my enjoyment of science and history that I never would have thought I'd see in a video game. If you also find yourself reading up on evolution in general, or what makes us "us", then I recommend this game with my whole chest.

_childDocuments_.review: Since there is not a "Meh" (average) vote option I currently am down-voting it (this could change)It's an interesting concept that is hampered by two VERY annoying an clunky mechanics/featuresThe 1st is the control interface.......O M G, this has to be the 3rd or 4th worst CI I have ever had the misfortune to contend with.  It's rather clunky and delayed.  Actions often present the feeling of lag even when they are actually responsive.   Crisp is not a term one will ever use about the CI as is.  It works poorly with both controllers and mouse/kb. This is compounded by the next barrier to success the game has...The UI.It uses a contextual interface what you are standing near, holding, or interacting with has a lot to do with what you can cannot do.  This is not helped by the same key/button being responsible for vastly different actions based purely on environmental context.  (somewhat understandable with a controller set-up, largely heresy with mouse/KB).  This can be annoying if your innate  understanding of tool use does not match the developers.  As an example; a beehive reqs a certain type of stick while in the real world...not so much.  One may or may not be as effiecient  (or safe) but it'll get er done.  Much like using a screwdriver as a lever, chisel, back-scratcher, or nose picker(care in deploying this technique is advised).  This would be fine if it was more intuitive regarding developer intent/perspective, and if the CI didn't lag behind.  As is it just contributes to annoyance and frustration not challenge or fun.  Also at issue the prompts are somewhat subtle audio and visual cues.  Individuals with certain disabilities (hearing loss, colorblindness ect) will likely struggle.  These are not impossible "features" to improve, only time will tell if they are.Those are the two main gripes I have with one additional minor gripe(also fixable)  If/when you master frustration with the CI & UI and get as comfortable with them as you can, you encounter the next problem.  Content tedium....there is an incredible amount of mindless repetition in advancing your tribe.  This gets worse as the game progresses (not due to added repetition, but due to lowered challenge)  As ones tribe advances, the environment, AI, and biomes become less challenging without becoming less tedious.   Early game everything feels big and dangerous; mid/late game it's boring.
