_childDocuments_.review: I do not recommend this game at full retail price, only when it is on sale for $20 or less. Please read my full review to understand why.A visually stunning adventure game that captures the essence of early human evolution. With a strong emphasis on graphics, gameplay, and atmospheric elements, the game aims to immerse players in a primal world of survival and adaptation. While it boasts several positive aspects, it also falls short in various key areas, leading to a mixed experience for players.Positive Aspects:- Visually stunning graphics that were groundbreaking for its time.- Engaging early gameplay that effectively captures the essence of evolution and adventure.- Diverse evolutionary paths that allow players to choose their playstyle and shape their tribe's destiny.- Impeccable attention to detail in animations and an immersive atmosphere amplified by ambient sounds and weather effects.Negative Aspects:-Dependency on player ignorance can lead to a lack of content for experienced gamers, resulting in a less satisfying experience.-Limited variety in gameplay mechanics, particularly in the number of structures and uses for collected items, diminishing the overall depth of the gameplay.-Inability to utilize critical evolutionary milestones such as fire, leading to missed opportunities and a less immersive experience.-Repetitive animations and environmental elements that detract from the overall immersion, despite attempts at realism.- Imbalanced traits system that incentivizes grinding over exploration, undermining the game's intended adventurous spirit.- Lack of depth in relationships and the absence of engaging quests, resulting in a less compelling narrative and gameplay experience.Conclusion:While Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey provides an engaging initial experience with its vivid world and immersive gameplay, it ultimately falls short in several key areas, hampering the overall enjoyment for seasoned players. Available at a discounted price, it serves as a worthwhile introductory experience, but the lack of content depth and repetitive gameplay elements may deter players from fully completing the game. Therefore, unless purchased on sale, the game may not be worth the full retail price, especially for those seeking a more immersive and dynamic gaming experience.Overall Score: 6/10 (based on its groundbreaking graphics and initial gameplay experience, but deductions for the lack of content depth and repetitive elements)

_childDocuments_.review: Very interesting game. The "mixed" tag is largely about two things: the lack of directions, and the poor controls. In the latter case, yes, this game was designed for consoles and, due to the number of available actions possible in this game, has a lot of context-sensitive actions that can sometimes be a struggle to wield with the "realistic" movement this game models. The port to KB/M unfortunately did little to remedy this, as the number of available buttons was not expanded, just remapped. It's not unplayably bad, and you can fiddle with the controls in the settings if you like.Regarding the first point, though: the game literally tells you that it's not going to help much. The game is a roguelike survival sandbox of sorts, and to better model what life was like for a primitive ape, you're going to have to figure out a lot of stuff yourself. As far as I'm aware, there's no such thing as a "game over" state, or at least it's quite difficult to achieve one, so don't worry about that. But if you aren't the kind of person that's willing to go into this game blind, I don't think I can recommend it for you, because that's where a lot of the fun seems to be. Sure, you can look up some info on how the UI works, since some parts of it are a little confusing, but for the actual game world: I think you should figure it out yourself. That's how I've been enjoying it so far.

_childDocuments_.review: 🌍 Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey – Embrace Your Inner Ape! 🐒Ever wanted to experience evolution first-hand? Well, buckle up because Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey takes you on a 10-million-year journey through the most epic survival story ever told—your own! 🌱🦍Set in the wilds of Neogene Africa, this game is like nature's ultimate throwback, where instead of respawning with better gear, you evolve! 🍃 You start as a humble primate, swinging through the trees, foraging for food, and fending off giant predators with nothing but your wits, opposable thumbs, and the occasional sharp rock. 🪨🦁The game is more than just a survival simulator—it's a life lesson in trial and error. You'll spend your days teaching your clan how to do basic things like not dying, while also unlocking new abilities like walking on two legs and inventing fire (spoiler: it’s pretty useful). 🔥🐾 Every choice you make impacts your lineage, from how you fend off hungry predators to deciding whether or not to eat that suspicious-looking fruit. Pro tip: don’t eat the red ones. 🍎❌Exploration is key, and the open-world environment is vast, lush, and absolutely stunning. It’s not just a jungle gym—it’s a world filled with danger, mystery, and the occasional leap of faith. One wrong move, and you're lunch for a giant snake. But hey, that's evolution for you! 🐍😬The evolution system is brilliant, and the satisfaction of seeing your clan go from timid tree-dwellers to brave tool-makers is next level. Watching your descendants evolve based on your actions is incredibly rewarding. Plus, you get to do it all with an intense, cinematic vibe that makes you feel like the ultimate survivor. 🎥🌿If you've ever wanted to experience the survival of the fittest, Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey is your chance. It’s part survival, part exploration, and all about figuring out how to turn your primate pals into the top of the food chain! 🧠🐵So, get ready to evolve, adapt, and conquer—or get eaten trying!Created with <3

_childDocuments_.review: These first few paragraphs detail some of the struggles you will face and how to deal with some of them so in a way this is a guide AND a review in one. This game definitely isn't for the faint of heart or the average casual gamer. If you're either steer clear. This is kinda like the dark souls of survival games. Its brutal and doesn't hold back. You will receive very little help. Keep the game on full HUD and tutorials on. it doesn't really matter because you're gonna have to learn some mechanics by yourself still. The tutorials will give you the basic knowledge you need but it still doesn't guarantee your survival. One of the biggest threats you'll face is predators. The Saber-toothed cat enemy in particular is quite common and deadly. In addition to that there are also snakes, crocodiles, wild boars, and even giant eagles if you climb too high in the trees.As far as combat goes you have the choice to dodge attacks and get away to climb trees. if you have a stick or sharpened stick you can perform a counter attack and stab the attacker with it dealing damage and causing them to flee. Some predators can also be intimidated. The chance of intimidation is based upon your groups current number, the enemy's size, and what neural perks you've invested in. Large groups can intimidate larger animals. Predators aren't the only danger though. Your apes can die from injuries sustained from falling or getting into scrapes with predators. You can also suffer from poisoning by eating certain foods. And if you haven't evolved ominivorism yet you might as well forget about eating meat, poultry (bird eggs), or mushrooms.Making babies is essential. The more babies you have the more you can secure neuronal development is passed on to the next generation. Babies also help the adults grow faster so taking them on expeditions with you is recommended. occasionally you'll find a lone Homonid in your travels. you can either scare them out of your territory or invite them in with open arms. To invite them in though you need to meet their needs. Their needs can range from injury, hunger, to berry poisoning. Its your job to determine what's wrong with them. Thankfully the body language makes it easier to identify their problem. After you give them the item they need they will join up with your tribe.As for controls, yeah Controller works better but you can use a keyboard and mouse if you must. As some people have stated in other reviews, button prompts are context sensitive and they tried mapping too many actions to one button. A game like this would be better suited to running a keyboard and mouse really but this game was also made for console players as well.The soundtrack is your typical Jungle styled music. you know jungle drums, pan flutes, tribal chants, etc Its not bad but its not exactly anything special either. If you like it its on sale on steam as well if you enjoy it enough *wink* *wink*Finally, in conclusion this is going to be a game that some will love for its difficulty and no holding back against the player while others will hate for the same reasons. It's a rough game but its just that kind of game. Either way don't expect it to be a walk in the park. Hopefully this review/guide was helpful to some players. If not then I apologize.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm enjoying the heck out of this game. I love sandbox games where I can make my own story... Like the time I brought the kids to the swamp so we could get used to the area and not be afraid, but on the way home we got ambushed by a warthog. My dude was bleeding to death, carrying the only 2 children of the clan. We escaped into the trees and right as my guy was about to bleed out, he discovered medicine in the trees can stop bleeding. We also found some fruit to eat. After a brief rest we climbed down, got drunk on fermented berries and crawled back home. It was a fun adventure!!It's the kind of game that some people might not enjoy. There is no objective! It's pure sandbox. Like driving a car or flying a plane, except you're controlling a clan of primates. Pay attention to the available prompts and try stuff. it's fun and not dangerous to you, the player. I mean it sucks when you clan wipe your clan, but life's hard man. I'm also new to the game so it's still very mysterious which adds to the excitement. I can't say how you will feel after a few hours of play time.I think the most off putting thing might be misunderstanding the level up system. The game is not a grind at as I've read in other reviews. To get smarter you have to bring a kid out exploring. It's like teaching them. Doing actions in the world will create new 'skills' based on how you play. Carrying children with you while interacting with the world will gain 'xp' towards those 'skills'. There are 2 ways to 'level up', by generation to lock in skills or by species to carry over genetic mutations. Yes you can lose skills, but xp seems so easy to get that it's no big deal to lose a few skills after advancing a generation. Just go look at stuff, enjoy the scenery. smell it, listen to the sounds. Move to a new location, build a fence, whatever. Just don't get too attached to your first lineage (sigh...save file name...) because they will probably suffer horribly while you learn the controls and game mechanics. You should try and enjoy that part too. Don't go asking the internet for help on your first play. I've just started my third lineage and this is the one man , we gonna make it this time.You will never become a human and drive around in fast cars with guns or even light a fire. You're a primate, you eat food and drink water for a living. Go figure out how to poke something with a stick in your free time.How is that not the most epic fantasy setting ever? I think it's beautiful and I hope the game can get more updates. maybe even a sequal at some point in the future after enough updates and interest.

_childDocuments_.review: The recent reviews had me scared, so I thought Id let everyone thats considering buying it on sale know before the sale is over.The game is built for YOU TO FIGURE IT OUT. If you buy the game and resort to google everything from crafting to how to fight, and then complain this exploration/survival doesnt offer anything. Well please, go play a preset storyline that holds your hand through it. That way you can have your predefined 50 hours of fun.Ive only just started with under 10 hours, but since the "i cheated the game to get to the end, and now I dont have any content" kids flooded with reviews, I thought Id let everyone that actually enjoy these type of games know that is actually quite nice. Play it as its supposed to be played and I'm very confident its 100+ hours of playtime - probably more.Think logically through playing and choose a difficulty your comfortable with (1 to 4) and you'll have a hell of a lot of fun. If pure originality (which is hardly ever seen in new games nowadays) and a bit of brain twisting is something you enjoy, you'll love this.Edit after 30 hours : The game is even more than I thought. One of my all time favorites already.

_childDocuments_.review: The game was sold to me as a monkey-themed Assassin's Creed with deep RPG and bloodline mechanics, but what I bought was some wild mix of Disgaea, Planet of the Apes, The Giver, and The Handmaid's Tale. Allow me to explain:Ancestors is a game with a big hook and primary feature of "learning" about the world you're in with repetitive actions that you then pass down as matured abilities through your lineage and ancestors (hence the name). This is fantastic at first, because the natural exploration of the game in and of itself is very rewarding and then filling out all the little bubbles to make your lineage stronger feels very satisfying. However, it's biggest strength is also it's downfall. Once the honeymoon phase of swinging through trees and making monkey noises wears off (just kidding the monkey noises button somehow never gets old) - you're left with an extremely grindy, clunky, monkey-themed upgrade game that's so sluggish it almost qualifies as a sleep aid.There appears to be little to no flexibility in this growth tree for things that you are not interested in.Scouting with your senses? Absolute grind fest. Walking through water? Multiple upgrades, and the only way to complete it is...by walking through water. Sleeping upgrades? You have to sleep. Healing upgrades? You HAVE to GET INJURED and THEN you can gain XP through healing it. You can't gain XP by witnessing things or figuring out things by doing similar things, it's only like-like.(Final example, there's different trees for both crafting WITH and WITHOUT tools despite there being all of like 10 recipes in the game. You want to level unhanded crafting? Craft about 40 spears, of which a max of 12 can be used at a time between a max-size clan...)Here's a brief example.Hour 1-3: Learning the game, naturally progressing through the skill tree and exploring the world. All is well.Hour 15: "Christ my child didn't randomly get the upgrade I want, better have six more and try again."At the point I'm at, it's literally been gamified and the way I feel I've been forced to play it would make the devs weep. New generation, have six children, pray to RNJesus, grind a little to fill in the bubbles, repeat. Repeat. Repeat. Repeat. I'm not even playing the game anymore, I'm literally waking up, making monkey babies and grinding a tech tree all while in the safety of my oasis because that's all there really "is" to do. If I want to grow my tech tree further I have to venture into the world...and then grind some more.I'm out of motivational factors outside of my own personal interest in some of the late-game techs are (and I swear to god if I get "Remember one more additional item" as an upgrade again I just might change this review to 'Not Recommended'.)If you can get this one for cheap - or like I did got in in a bundle - it's worth swinging from a few trees and having a good time for a few hours, but this one lasts the staying power to play for any long period of time or a revisit for nostalgia or fun unless you're REALLY into grindy upgrade games.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so deeply weird that I don't know where to begin.I'm not sure what I was expecting, but it wasn't quite... this. I was expecting an action-adventure ape game, maybe a good itch-scractcher after watching Planet of the Apes, and I wasn't exactly wrong, but that's not the whole story. Let me just summarize this before I get to the rating part.You're an ape some 10 billion years ago. Your goal is to make the ape human - or at least human adjacent, since it doesn't quite get to the ♥♥♥♥ sapiens stage. You do that by being ape in action-adventure openworldesque setting, by running, climbing, learning to make and use simple tools, so forth, but the real progress happens in the Evolution menu.Which is a little complex.You've got nodes, not unlike skills in a skill tree. They're initially invisible to you, you can only see the ones that you're ready to unlock. How do you unlock them? By being ape. Better running speed is unlocked by running. Walking on two legs better is unlocked by trying to walk on two legs. Senses are reinforced by using them - and so on. But that only unlocks the node.You actually buy the node using "neural energy" which is generated by - apparently - teaching kids. So performing actions with kids present. Conveniently, you can piggyback two and have others nearby, either piggybacked by other apes following you, or following you themselves. Perform enough actions, get the energy, buy the neural node. Which isn't the end.Then you need to reinforce that neuron by passing the generation - which normally allows you to reinforce only 1 node per kid in the clan, so you want to do that often. Kids also get to have random mutations which get revealed when they mature, but only activate upon evolution leap. Which in turn is passing millions, even billions of years (depending on evolution feats) and potentially making your clan into new species.That was a mouthful.It boils down to the gameplay loop of filling in your clan with kids, performing actions to get some evolution feats, unlock new neural nodes and get some neural energy, maybe migrate your clan to a new area, passing the generation, doing that again - and once your elders and adults have mutations available, performing an evolution leap. And that for about 8 billion years.Thing is, it initially does a really good job at showing what it could be like to be ape. You're rather clumsy, and the controls show that. Even if you do things mostly right you'll break your tools, you won't be able to communicate, you'll move slow, it's... a struggle. It gives an impression of bad controls and bad design - which they're not. They're a bit awkward, but not bad.But as you evolve, you realize that this gameplay loop is actually quite engaging. You slowly make the environment yield do you, as you both learn it and as your clan becomes more adept at being ape. The controls slowly become more reasonable, and the game kinda starts to flow. Reaching the end then becomes a fairly relaxing and satisfying experience.So in summary, can I recommend the game? I can. Not to everyone though. It's a deeply weird game that will appeal to players who like unusual games. I find it difficult to put it in the sentence "If you liked X you'll like Ancestors". But I have to admit that once it clicked with me - which required effort - I enjoyed my 30-something hours run very, very much.Try it if you like games that present you with unusual mechanics and provoke some unusual thoughts.

_childDocuments_.review: This is such a unique and wonderful game. I've been so bored with traditional games as of late I'm glad I found this one. The usual quest markers, save reloading, and general boring grind have become more of a chore than something fun with other games. But with this game its a true sandbox. I don't pick something up and go, "well that's dumb, they should have added that feature." Instead I marvel at every carefully crafted detail because I know that everything has a use and purpose and even if I haven't figured out what that is yet I'm excited to figure it out later. As soon as I run away from this prehistoric puma lion... My only complaint is that there isn't multiplayer because I imagine this would be incredibly fun with two people who haven't played the game before figuring it out together. Just one warning, this game can be very scary sometimes. There are no back saves if you die you die if everyone in your clan dies you have to start from scratch with a new game. Which means I find myself genuinely getting scared and having to pause the game. However even though I have anxiety this game didn't make me anxious despite getting scared on multiple occasions. Maybe because it's more of an outlet for adrenaline than a creator of it. I actually found the fact that I'm not constantly reloading saves and trying for a perfect score or perfect collection to be more relieving than anything else.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, I've got mixed opinions about this game.On the one hand, I love the graphics, the open world and the fact that you have to learn as you go much like how our ancestors would have done. All that is great. It's very immersive and interesting, despite the fact that certain aspects might not be entirely realistic, though I suppose some creative licence is necessary to make things more enjoyable.However, the most annoying thing about the game is the manner in which the combat system was designed, especially for a keyboard user. There is no ability to preemptively attack, ONLY the option to either counterattack or dodge, which by the way is about as unrealistic as it gets. Plus the game doesn't offer any definitive means of handling combat. Only a faint audio cue will determine whether you can react accordingly. And given that the key bindings can't even be customized it only makes it harder to use., though it all does get easier later on. At the start however, it's a nightmare trying to either dodge or attack.It also doesn't help matters much that the game doesn't have a map to serve as a guide, or markers with a precise indicator of distance to provide some insight of how far one needs to travel. While it does add a certain degree of mystery, it can leave a lot of people utterly frustrated trying to circumnavigate without a definitive idea of where they're supposed to go and in what direction. In addition, the only way to continue/load the game is to exit the one that's currently being played and that requires waiting for a very redundant loading screen.That's basically my two cents on this. I really hope that the devs could implement an update to fix the combat system. They can even overhaul it, because as it stands, it's probably hell for a keyboard user; I know it is for me. Also if it's all possible, maybe the devs can for the game to be modded so we could implement these changes ourselves, Ancestors has the potential to really be a 10/10 game. As it is, I'd be lying if I rated it higher than a 8.5 because of the sheer headache with attacking and dodging early game; it's really cumbersome, at times it feels like being blindfolded and handcuffed.Please change it a little. I already LOVE this, but would PREFER to love it more.

_childDocuments_.review: Panache Digital Games came up with a game we always desired. Start your journey from scratch and evolve accordingly. There are not many restrictions imposed on the players. If you want to tarry with your group and don’t leave the settlement, you are free to do so, or gather your clan and evolve throughout a journey of exploring new kinds of stuff. Feel the adventure of surviving the world that ages up to 10 million years ago. Monitor the growth of your hominids as you traverse, explore, survive, and evolve through time. Carry on your knowledge and discoveries to the new evolved generation. The game is slow-paced because of its “help yourself” idea and might feel frustrating sometimes. With the numerous possibilities, you can surely grind a good chunk of hours.Ancestors has a slow-paced complex gameplay that might feel frustrating over time. The gameplay might vary according to your playstyle. If you want to stay close to the settlement and increase your domestic skills, then your gameplay might omit danger from wild animals and fear of the unknown. Migrating your settlement to search the unfamiliar lands might inflate tremendous danger and can wipe your entire lineage. The controls feel too complex and are not fun. Climbing and swinging through the trees is frustrating. Most of the time, you will experience difficulty locating the next branch to jump on, as the tree positioning is weird and poorly made. One button can perform multiple operations, which can result badly in certain situations. You are supposed to educate the species about every possible useful kind of stuff, from sticks to rocks to edibles. Establishing communication between the clan is very important, as you will need to switch characters to keep the evolution going. The idea presented is pretty good, but it lacks proper execution.  The graphics are not bad, neither wondrous, but they are quite enjoyable and don’t affect the gameplay. It lacks details in the interaction of characters with the environment. It looks more of an old game instead of a new-gen game. Keeping in mind that this is a new concept game and the development team had limited funds at that time, this is quite promising. The map is enormous with numerous focal points , and also very diverse flora and fauna. Some of the effects like fear of the unknown and infection are pretty good. But somehow, these above-average graphics require good GPU power, which is quite unusual. The cinematics are top-notch with great story portraits and realistic quality graphics. Little things like dream showcases and animal fight cinematics bring an extra level of detail to the game.Don’t rush things, learning is a slow process. Most of the time, you will have to figure out the solution yourself. Turning down the music will help a lot, as most of the actions in-game are executed on a beat. Without spoiling too much, we can say that both hands are useful and can craft wonders. Most of the players neglect to carry a child, but actually, they provide you extra experience, and you can carry up to 2 of them. This is an interesting detail of the game that you will undergo during the exploration of new regions. When you are away from your familiarized territory, your character will feel scared and might enter the state of hysteria. This will result in losing your current clan member, and you will return to your main settlement. To conquer this, focus on your senses and identify the elements nearby. If your hominids recognize them, he will feel confident and will calm itself.The game’s objective is to finish the evolution before the actual time that was taken according to history. So your first objective is to enhance your species and not a sole character. Tarrying on one character will influence your progress and might back-fire. Keeping the clan guarded and prosperous is your foremost goal. This concept certainly raises our expectations and makes us biased towards the game. The story should have been stretched to the start of human civilization, but it ends at a generation switch that feels incomplete. It provides a mesmerizing experience to the gamers. Recommended buying during a sale.Rate: 7/10This game has been played on  platform before tested on .

_childDocuments_.review: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey ReviewA prehistoric adventure like no other! Some key points that this game offers:1.	Unite your species to form a clan2.	Explore Savage Africa3.	Nature is more than unforgiving, behind every gorgeous scenery lies a predator waiting to pounce on you4.	Learn, adapt and overcome every obstacle 5.	Incredibly detailed skill systemSpecial Note:The game has been released on Steam as well now. Even though the game received mixed reviews when it was released initially, the developers have since updated and improved the game immensely. They added new features and altered others. I left my original Review intact so that you can see how the developers took what the gamers said, and improved the game. For a full list of changed and improvements, view the patch notes here.Gameplay & Controls:The controls for the game are rather discomforting, and unfortunately, that has nothing to do with the layout. It is the way the controls are implemented. For example, running and jumping is the same button. You run by holding it down, and when you leave it, you jump. This does not work well with the gameplay itself. There are some movement bugs present in the game, but those will be patched out in the days to come. The game can be played on the keyboard and mouse; however, it is suggested that you use a controller. The game takes place 10 million years ago in the Neogene period in Africa. You take control of hominids, a pre-cursor Ape species. You will have to build a clan, by recruiting outsiders and mating. Your clan needs to eat, live, and survive. It is up to you to teach them. There is a massive world just waiting for you to explore. Everything can be examined to determine its purposes, be it a tool, medicine, or food. As you learn and adapt to your surroundings your species start learning new skills and abilities, such as refining plants for alternative uses. In one instance it’s a food, but ground up, it becomes a paste used to stop bleeding.The same with tools, a branch for example can be stripped clean of the smaller branches increasing its attack power, and later on, a second tool can be used to sharpen the stick. This world is filled to the brim with things to figure out and explore. As you explore and discover things, you trigger neurons which improves the survivability of your species. In the beginning, you are prey to almost every other creature out there, but slow and steady you evolve and adapt becoming better at defending yourself and later on become the predator yourself. This world is truly big and divided up into different biomes, each very realistically tailored to offer an immersive experience. In each of these biomes, there are numerous places for you to discover and even a few that you can move your clan to establish a new home.As it stands, the game is more than fun and sure to offer you a fantastic time. It has some issues and minor bugs. The game lacks some important features too. For example, the lack of a tutorial system makes the game unnecessarily difficult. Figuring stuff out is part of the learning curve for sure, but the lack of basic information makes a game less fun. Then predators seem to constantly attack you when you are out in the open, you barely have any room to breathe or actually just enjoy the game, not sure if this is a bug or deliberate implementation. Graphics:Absolutely beautiful doesn’t begin to cover it. Each biome has been gorgeously created to represent a very realistic environment. There are Jungles, the Savanna and so much more. The day and night cycle along with the weather system doesn’t just add more beauty and depth to the game; every sunrise is a new gorgeous day for you to enjoy.Character models were done just as beautifully. I can’t say for certain what any of these animals looked like back then, but the representation here is done quite remarkably and beautifully as well.All in all, the game is pretty much gorgeous no matter where you are, but there are some spots that you discover that truly offer you beauty like no other.Under the settings menu, we have several options to customize our game.Sounds:Another brilliant add on. The music for the game is astounding! It adds to the realism of the game immensely. The game is best experienced with the volume turned up or with a headset. There are so many background sounds that play vital roles in bringing the game to life. Whether it is you wading through water or the sounds of a massive python hissing at you. The sound brings life to this game in a remarkable way.The animal sounds were marvellously incorporated into the game.Under the settings menu, we have full volume control.Replayability:The game doesn’t really have a new game plus feature. However, the original playthrough will take you a long time to complete, especially if you go for total completion. There is a lot to discover and experience. That alone will keep you busy for quite a while.MGR Gaming’s Conclusions:Spoilers Ahead:More than a brilliant game for sure. There is tons of fun to be had and a very memorable journey to experience. A lot of unique elements went into the game. The Neuron system was incredibly well thought out and implemented. It offered an RPG experience unlike anything else I’ve come across, especially on how you unlock these Neurons. Very well thought out.The Generation and Evolution systems further adds to the unique gameplay mechanics of the game. I must admit that they really went all out here in terms of out of the box thinking and it really paid off well. There are so many discoveries to make and so many memorable experiences to witness.To put it frankly, you are in for the time of your life. This game will offer you an experience unlike anything else you’ve experienced thus far.I do hope they update the lack of a tutorial system for the game, it will make the game a lot friendlier and more fun to get into. The game is an open-world simulation, but the lack of any quest or general direction further adds to the unnecessary difficulty. All things considered, this is still a great game that can be improved.The Official trailer for Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey:Score 7By: MGRzaDate: 4 September 2019Additional Info:Platforms: PC: PlayStation 4: Xbox OneGenre: Action-Adventure: Atmospheric: Choices Matter: Crafting: Exploration: Historical: Hunting: Immersive Sim: Nature: Open World: Open World Survival Craft: PvE: Science: Singleplayer: Survival: Third PersonCensor Rating: Violence: Blood: Partial NudityAge Rating: TeenDeveloper: Panache Digital GamesPublisher: Private DivisionRelease Date: 27 August 2019MGR Gaming Steam Curator:MGR Gaming:

_childDocuments_.review: I want my money back. This game is ambitious and for the right person maybe it's incredible, but in my opinion the controls are incredibly clunky and not optimized for mouse and keyboard at all, and are still poor for a controller.The AI of your clan members is flat out dumb and they're constantly putting themselves in dangerous situations when they are on expeditions with you and getting themselves killed.And for a game that is supposed to be about experimentation, evolution, and learning it sure does like to punish you for trying to do that. Predator attacks are relentless and regularly made mince meat of my lineage as I was trying to learn. It seems everyone else says "well once you get to a certain point-" well I can't get to a certain point because there is a Sabre tooth tiger intent on hunting down and murdering my entire clan! The name of this game should be Buffet Line!And apparently if you survive long enough to jump ahead a few generations... you forget like everything!!!I don't have time to be frustrated like this. This game could have been really good if just for a few key differences. I was looking forward to a challenging experience. I like that the game does not hold your hand. Instead, I found my ape couldn't hold a branch as he fell to his death! Clearly I can't be trusted with the evolution of the species.If grinding out hours of time repeating the same learning process, just to be devoured by predators sounds like a good time, then this game might be for you, and you might be a masochist. Otherwise, stay away.

_childDocuments_.review: Great concept, but a lackluster execution. _childDocuments_.name: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey

_childDocuments_.review: Surprisingly fun, though the game has low replay value due to much of the fun being from the feeling of venturing into the unknown and discovering the mechanics of the game. The progression from a scared and confused ape to a confident and voracious killer of beasts is very satisfying, but once you've really figured out how the game works then much of the challenge is gone. This might have been alleviated if the game worked through dynamic systems, such as in combat, but nearly every interaction with objects and other animals comes through quick-time events. You could have some fun speedrunning evolution after learning the game, but you probably won't be recreating the feel of being a diminutive prey animal from your first time playing. Also be aware that some of the core mechanics of progression like mating your apes is kind of clunky and inconvenient. Luckily, the devs updated the game to make it so this becomes more streamlined as you progress through the game, but it felt like it took way too long to unlock the auto-pairing features which should have atleast been early game unlocks. Much of the game starts to feel grindy towards the end, depending on your luck with filling out the evolutionary skill tree. The game has an excellent ambience, with a great soundtrack and a variety of different environments. At times it can even feel quite relaxing, despite the constant threat of sabertooth attacks.Even if the game is far from perfect, I had a lot of fun with it. Its definitely one of the most unique games I've ever played, and I would definitely recommend anyone interested in evolution, prehistory, or survival games to check it out.
_childDocuments_.name: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey

_childDocuments_.review: This game is difficult for me to review. It is fun for me but I have some serious problems that make me understand why so few share in my enjoyment. Cons: -Game Speed: It is slow in every sense of the word. Whether it be unlocking new abilities, learning key game mechanics, or even just moving from point A to point B, this game drags it's feet. -Movement Speed: Your character is very slow, even after unlocking all the movement speed bonuses and stamina upgrades it can still take a very long time to reach where you want to go. I think if there was a map and fast travel feature then it would fix this problem, but that won't be added to the game. Going to a distant mountain and back is fun, exciting and rewarding. Going to the same mountain and back, again, is draining, annoying and boring. -Save Files: There is only one save file per clan, if that save gets corrupted then you're screwed and cannot get it back. -Re-population: Finding new apes to replace lost ones is annoying and much too slow.Pros: -Rewarding Experience: This game is very rewarding as almost all of the upgrades are earned by you figuring it out or by getting enough experience. When you learn which 2 rocks to bash together to make a specific tool, it's an experience not often felt in games. -Difficulty: The game-play is truly difficult to learn, but it can be mastered given enough time. It's a good difficulty because it is something you have to be good enough to beat, it doesn't just slap a bigger health bar on enemies to make the game "harder".Conclusion: If you are patient and enjoy a very punishing experience with no hand holding then this game is for you. Just save exploring for after you get the movement upgrades.
_childDocuments_.name: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey

_childDocuments_.review: First things first, I did get this on a massive sale, I suggest you look for at sale as well. While it is rather pricey, it's well worth it. I admit, it's not for everyone. It fills a very specific niche, to where only a very specific type of person will like it. But if you like it, you will LOVE it. It has a great game-play loop, with your monkeys adventuring learning, and passing on their genes to the next gen. It is so rewarding to see that silhouette of your next species when you do an evolve jump. the controls are unorthodox, but very rewarding when you one-shot kill any animal. While I kept things vague, I suggest you stop reading reviews now due to spoilers, it's far better blind. The main appeal is discovery. It has a steep learning curve though, so it requires a bit more investment than most games. Also: Spoilers:SPOILERSThere is tumeric, and grinders, but you can't spice with tumeric :_(. I wanted my poisonous hippo meat to be tastier :_(.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is awesome on so many levels. The soundtrack is beautiful as well as the ambiance of the wild... if you're part of the people who made this happen; THANK YOU <3 As a nerd with a bit of science-y interest this game is amazing and fascinating to explore. To the 'review'/helpful hints (SPOILERS)You will need patience for this game and definitely use a controller. I'm not understanding the bad reviews' that, in spite of, I still got this game and it plays fine. I feel it's more of a user issue and maybe they need to get better with it. This is a simulation of our origin; you will have to LEARN EVERYTHING because everything is new to you in game. Take a Dark Souls approach to this game and if you have ever played Conan Exiles you will understand what I mean when I say you have to 'unlock/learn' everything like what is water(legitimately  you don't know what water is. It's ok. Don't panic). To that you need to analyze everything and I mean EVERYTHING('scan'/interact/eat/drink/touch/smell etc). But first and foremost make sure you have a baby on your back when doing/learning anything new. The controls are very basic and no more complicated than you make them. Don't overthink things. The game gives you all kinds of help but only ONCE and then you're on your own. The exception being a very distinctive screen signal and sound for when to let go of the 'charge' button depending on what your doing that's 'charging'. Don't release before this signal! If at first you don't succeed then try again.I'm assuming I'm still in the tutorial area and I'm fine with that. THIS IS NOT A RUSH GAME. The game even tells you to take your time and it's true. As someone in the non-het community I thought it cool that anyone can partner with anyone(mind you this happens in nature all the time so if you got issues with that then i don't know what to tell you). If you want to reproduce a FERTILE Lady and Duder can get together etc but anyone/couple can 'raise' the baby. Speaking of baby they help in many ways. Keep one with you at all times and take care of the group. Yeah this is more of a 'guide' than a review but I didn't feel the need to gush forever about the game that I feel speaks for itself. Maybe not a game for younger minds or those looking for instant gratification. There's so much I love about this game and I've yet to leave the tutorial area( I think? Dunno if it's an area or if I'm in the actual game and the tutorial was the helpful hints that came up at the beginning lol). I can definitely see having to put in LOTS of hours if you want to do it right. Rushing will only leave you with poor evolution which will probably be worse for you in the long run. It's a grind that pays off. Oh yeah did I mention Patience? ^_^ <3

_childDocuments_.review: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey is a rough game. The controls are awkward, the goals aren't clear, the story is minimal. Despite this, I found it fascinating and put almost 100 hours into it. The world is beautiful and surprising, and exploring it reminded me of Zelda: Breath of the Wild, though of course without the Nintendo polish. Without spoiling anything, you begin as a tree-dwelling ape and end up an upright, tool-using hominid, though the mechanics aren't always consistent. Swinging in the treetops was exhilarating and probably one of the better mechanics of the game, but one it explicitly pushed the player away from with the level design and the implication of becoming more human-like.If the premise of this game is appealing to you, you should give it some time, but if you're not having fun by the time you're walking upright and fighting instead of running, you probably shouldn't play further

_childDocuments_.review: Please keep in mind, this game does little hand holding, and the controls are defaulted to explain in terms of controller. You’ll need to switch that in settings if you are on keyboard and mouse like I was. I also have to play on medium graphics, which occasionally can cause the ground to rise higher than the barrier, making objects look like they’ve disappeared under the ground. (Easy fix, change it to high, then change it back to medium graphics)Looking past a few issues I’ve had playing in regards to both of those, I do find this quite fun. There isn’t necessarily much explanation for what you are supposed to do in the game, since it all hinges on what you can actually figure out. The more you know, the greater benefits you’ll get for your generations.The movement and interaction controls are also quite well thought out, in my opinion, if not a bit difficult to master due to the way the game explains itself and it’s mechanics. If you have trouble making progress in a certain area, looking up some guides will make some things that you should do in the game seem obvious and a bit frustrating you didn’t figure it out yourself.I feel that it’s the appeal of the game to figure it all out, to truly get that feeling of accomplishment when you finally figure out how to make a spear, to hunt, to fish. You begin to remember and plan the perfect routes from one place to another as you continue venturing outward. The game’s map is pretty large to explore on foot, too.TL;DR - game doesn’t explain things much, that’s the point of the game. I like it, if you like puzzles or survival games this will fit. Huge map, cool sights, interesting mechanics. ٩(^‿^)۶

_childDocuments_.review: 30 hours into the game and still waiting for the fun to begin.The game could be a lot, but it has, as others extensively stated three main problems; complexity, controls and progression.It is somewhat complex, which is hard to get into without any sort of tutorial. The bad controls don't help, there are just too much actions to have a sensible control scheme, no matter if you play on keyboard or controller. The progression is... slow and the apes can't really do anything. The only reason to travel in a group is the effectiveness of group intimidation, otherwise traveling alone is much more convenient.When you grasp how the game works (most of it is not explained), the game loop becomes very mundane; breed, move to a few new locations while doging/killing new enemies and eating new stuff, settle down, skip to next generation. Do that two times while also looking for meteorites and then you do an evolution, this maximizes the genetic mutation while minimizing time. Nothing of that is explained, you have to figure it out by yourself. If you realize this is how it works, the game becomes vey repetitive.There also isn't really much of a progression, it's basically always "you get better at x" and nothing more. I Expected to evolve, but that isn't really the case. The stuff you can do/make in the beginning is the same stuff you can do/make at the end.I'm mainly giving up because the apes are useless. I'm at a point where the enemy attacks in groups. After each attack you need to gather healing resources and heal your apes because they can't do that on their own. Weapons have to be made and given to them, making them drink/eat is a pain in the a** because if their main hand is occupied, they can't do anything so you have to make them switch hands (which is problematic if some have a weapon in the left, others in the right hand - imho a design flaw, instead of "switch hands" the command should be "ready weapon" because it has no other use). In older versions, apes also got stuck often, luckily they now teleport. Which is good for predators, because if you're next to a cliff they sometimes teleport onto the cliff, getting attacked by a predator and there is nothing you can do because you can't reach them, can't intimidate from this distance and running away won't teleport them because they're in combat. In general, managing your apes is a true nightmare. The game would be a LOT better if predators would avoid a large, armed group of apes.Graphically its nice. The music is ok if you ignore the random wanna-be-african-atmosphere mixed with some scifi-music stuff that pops up seemingly at random.The cutscenes have a big problem. If you inspect or discover something, a cutscene will play, which is nice if the time would stop. So while in the cutscene, your apes get murdered. You can skip the cutscene, but that really shouldn't be necesarry. This creates a sense of urge and insecurity to rush everything and ignore the scenery. I'm pretty sure this is not what the devs wanted to achieve because the terrain is really nice.While i'm at the negative aspects, there is also the very cool concept of unknown territory. If you're in a new area, you will get...lets call it a massive senses debuff, which you have to negate by simply using your senses and doing stuff in the new territory. If cone correctly, you need to "go into the center" to claim the territory. The center of an unknown territory... yeah, that's a nice joke, there is an "indicator" but most of the times that indicator points back to a known territory. So, conquering a new territory is mostly running around in hope the prompt appears. Very good idea but bad execution, which could be the motto of the whole game.The more i write, the more i'm reminded of how bad the game is. You play as a monkey who is able to jump from tree to tree and yet i can't remember the last time i did that. Because it mostly ends in death. Often the apes don't grab to a branch that is clearly in their jump path. Jumping from the end of a branch into their death without you pressing any button is also a random occurance. Oh and if you're not already in climbing animation, there is no way to climb down. So despite being a monkey, the ground is your friend.I'm struggling to say anything positive, so my tldr;- Extremely good ideas but executed rather poorly- Needs better controls, better ape management and more significant progression*EDIT: whwo this became more of a rant than a review. I'm sorry, but i'm not exaggerating, the game really is frustrating
_childDocuments_.name: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey

_childDocuments_.review: It's terrible. I'm sure you had hoped for a vast array of jungle to explore,evolve and amuse yourself within. That is NOT the case here, Yes there is a jungle. How big? You will never know, because your apes simply cannot muster the energy to venture further than a few meters radius outside their camp.Your ape will have to "rest" every few meters it travels,to such an extent that it's a deal breaker.Oh you feed yourself well, sleep regularly and drink plenty of water?Makes no difference. Elder or Youthful, makes no difference.Your apes are slow, boring and dull.Your monkey decided to hang from a branch for 15 seconds real time,15 mins game time. BAM no energy, dying..Wow, so realistic.. amazing.. Yeah. The LACK of energy that your healthy adult apes have. It's only thereso you as a customer take longer to discover, just how little content this game consists of.They spawn tigers out of the blue that will wipe all your progress.The dodge mechanic is awful, the counter attack indictator is non existant.if you are attacked by a tiger it will stalk you forever.Yeah I learned to kill the tiger, shift- and what not on keyboard.Even with the ability to defeat enemies of the jungle, the game is still awful.I spent ages putting up barricades for a no entry base and you have a tiger spawn inside.There are little to NO other apes in the forest to recruit and replace your fallen.So yeah, if one dies-  game over.I'm at the second camp, an entire evolutionary leap forwardwith the status "faster than science". Yet I have met only ONE single ape in the jungle to recruit. ONE.. Just the singular ape and I am not talking about the quest to rescue your own.Are there NO other monkey camps? Are we truly the only apes in existence?Horrendous.It's one giant grind to watch your progress go down the drain, due to faulty mechanics and lazy porting.Oh and make sure your monkey isn't left handed..Oh you got a spear? That's great but will it make a difference? No, because the only thing that occurs is your apes dying.Most of the time you will just be sitting there wonderinghow the hell it is that your apes have SUCH LOW ENERGY?Especially when you diet properly and even stockpile.For a species meant to be stronger than humans,their stamina-span is downright stupid.It's just not worth buying ever. Ever.It's the kind of the game that would make you think ill of the people that made it.

_childDocuments_.review: I tried...I just don't see the appeal or the fun in this game. It's just tedious and boring. And I wanted to like it. I thought the idea of progressing a pre-human "civilization" through time might be fun. And it could be if the game either had a tangible narrative or wouldn't be so obtuse with its gameplay elements. As it stands I'm simply too dumb to even find my way back to my settlement. One would think that even these apes were able to communicate with one another (as the game even states), so why is it that there's not a single of my clan mates answering my calls? The recognize and memorize feature is also extremely user unfriendly. Let's not even speak of combat (or dodging at least). The rest of my complaints could only come from reviews I've read and watched, so they're not valid here, as they're not my personal story.But damn...when you make a game...you should make it fun, no matter the subject. Europa Universalis, Crusader Kings or Mudrunner or Euro Truck Sim are great examples of games that are "different" without an actual narrative, but still fun. This game, however, just throws you right into the mix and expects you to..."do" stuff. Even Dark Souls has a better tutorial. It feels overwhelming and, frankly, just boring. Sorry.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so fun to play! I bought this game ... two days ago? Three? I don't know because I've been practically living in this game for the past thirty hours.  Matter of fact, I may play it once I'm done.  This game is extremely exploration and discovery heavy, but that actually kind of suits me. This doesn't hold your hand and if you are not careful - like me - you will die. A lot. Pros: This game is something that can almost soothe you into a false sense of security and then BAM, hits you with something out of nowhere. Don't know why I like this but I do. It allows for extreme creativity with minimal goals allowing you to make your own story. The world is so varied and gorgeous and dangerous that you WANT to linger... and not be eaten of course. This runs into my next pro, to make this game have a real difficulty curve, they take away any sense of strength or smarts. You have to figure out how to switch Items you are holding in your hands for example. You don't get anything. I like that freedom. Cons: Alright alright, everyone says this - having to breed MORE ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ monkeys after every generation. I wish there was more ways to interact or get attached to your little ape family.  The most I feel when a family member dies is "♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ how'd I ♥♥♥♥ up" and not "OH MY GOD NOOOOOOO".  Sometimes the big cats or enemies LITERALLY spawns out of nowhere. Hard to see in jungle areas but easy to see in the desert and ocean areas. Other than that - not too much. Love it! Would love to play a sequel too!

_childDocuments_.review: Return to monke. A fascinating and some might say also educational game. It's pretty damn brutal quite often and early game is hell until you establish yourself. Think of it more like an rpg game, where you occasionally need to bank skills to advance, leading to some new skills and new options.Music is nice and atmospheric for your actions, visuals are decent, though often you will find that anything and everything tries to kill you, especially the saber cats who seem to exist to hunt you down no matter where you are. Still, you can go from a helpless primate outdone by everything to the new apex predator.
_childDocuments_.name: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to play this game before it existed, really cool concept of walking through human evolution. The gameplay is fun and relaxing simultaneously. I found climbing trees and jumping from branch to branch quite fun. The game doesn't really explain anything which is good and bad at the same time, because you can miss things and get I found myself playing the game "incorrectly" for a long time until I read the wiki. I find the AI a bit annoying and sometimes you have to micromanage your tribe too much. But all in all I enjoyed the game would recommend it for people who enjoy single player games, exploration and figuring things out.
_childDocuments_.name: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey

Movement tutorial (climbing) needs to be a lot better and explicitly tell me what I can and cannot interact with when trying to move around.3. _childDocuments_.name: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey

_childDocuments_.review: Great evolution driven game.  The learning curve is extreme early on but levels out quickly enough.  Despite a complete lack of story there are still emotionally driven moments.  My only real complaint is breeding should be automated/semi-automated after 4-5 generation or should be an unlockable skill/trait as it gets extremely repetitive.  Definitely worth the wait to buy it on Steam.
_childDocuments_.name: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey

_childDocuments_.review: Super interesting for now. The controls are unwieldy though; sometimes they don't make any sense. Why can't I just grab onto a branch like a normal chimp? It's not even implemented. You MUST jump off branches.A warning: It is a closed world, and not procedurally generated.A warning for Linux users: it has extremely bad performance. It leaks too. After 30 minutes it becomes unplayable.
_childDocuments_.name: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey

_childDocuments_.review: There's about 5 hours of content here. You can construct about four structures, craft maybe six items, and get mauled by three kinds of animals (I don't say "fight" because your choice is between running away or trying to scare them away by screaming). Play time is padded by revoking some of the skills you've already unlocked and making you unlock them again (and again, and again, ...).The apes are supposed to be evolving toward being human, but there's nothing more human-like for them to do as they progress. No fire, no stone spearheads, no atlatls, no straw rafts, no bows or arrows, no pottery, no hunting or trapping, no mud huts, no clay figurines (and  no metalworking). You're stuck as a chimp-like hominid that slowly gets better at sharpening sticks and making leaf beds. (Allegedly there's spearfishing, but the fear mechanic is blocking me from exploring widely enough to find a fishing spot to try it out.)It feels like this game's development was cut when it was 20% done, and they're trying to recoup losses by selling what they had anyway.
_childDocuments_.name: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey

_childDocuments_.review: This game has been a total disappointment for me from the start, and I'm also sad that I got it from Humble Bundle; if purchased with my money I would have taken the refund in a record time.FOV. How can a simply setting as that be tied to progress? And I'm not buying any fo that "immersion" bs. Im on ultrawide (3440x1440) and I just can't play the game. The FOV is OBNOXIOUS, HIDEOUS, THE WORSE I've ever had the disgrace to experience in any game after 17 years of gaming. Congrats devs!I've tried to fix it with various mods but they don't seem to work for me. So yeah. I don't recommend this game AT ALL. Glad for those who could bear with this terrible design choice, but I can't.Totally disappointed. This game is a big NO untill FOV is adjustable (which most likely will be never) so the game is PLAYABLE, and I don't end up getting dizzy and feeling the need to throw up after just 10 min of play.Good job on ruining the game with such a dumb decision. _childDocuments_.name: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey

_childDocuments_.review: This game seems really cool in concept. Play through the early stages of what became mankind and live in the dangerous world we evolved from. Pros: the graphics, controls, and sound are all pretty good. There are some minor targeting issues when it comes to cursor placement but I'll chock that up to it being intended to play with controller. When you get a real good combo of swinging vine to vine and you're hurling through the trees it definitely is fun.Cons:There is no real gameplay. There's 4 minutes of content played over and over and over. You inspect this thing, bash it with a rock, get evolution points. Next generation, rinse and repeat. And if something goes wrong you better start all over cuz it death spirals hard. If the game had more variety to it I would excuse its difficulty but there's nothing to warrant the grind, there's no reward for your efforts.
_childDocuments_.name: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game. It's not for everyone. It's tough for a bit at the start of the game and can be a grind trying to complete. The crafting is actually pretty cool. I wish they went a step further with the amount of things you can make. It can feel repetitive at times. Definitely takes patience but if you take your time and play at a chill pace it can be quite enjoyable. I like how the game doesn't hold your hand and things can be challenging to figure out in the beginning stages. I hope they make a sequel and do something interesting with a variety of things to do.
_childDocuments_.name: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey

_childDocuments_.review: Every now and then there's a rare occurrence that pops up of Art imitating Life rather than the reverse, and unfortunately that's all that I can see contained within the immersive setting that is Ancestors: the Humankind Odyssey. The gameplay is ungodly annoying and frustrating at the best of times, such that your attempts at seamlessly traversing through the forest will always be cut short of whether or not you can make a jump or climb on a surface. The social aspect epitomizes these constraints beyond what words can manage, as you're constantly using inputs to determine what items are in what hand, if you're giving, dropping, or tossing an object (all mapped to the same button), and whether or not an interaction particular is long-press, pressed once, or mashed. It feels the whole point of the control system was to reinvent the wheel with bells and whistles attached.The sleep, eat, and drink system is counter intuitive as it conveys the means of similarity to any other simulation game or even survival games, which wouldn't be a bad thing if the game was just more transparent with your needs rather than just surprising you with hunger and thirst notifications. The game itself starts up in right in the middle of the Neogene at 10 Ma, starting you off with primates never given explicit detail, though the in-game system does refer to them as hominids (not hominins) which would make them ancestral by 3 million years of either Graecopithecus or Sahelanthropus just depending on what the fluid definition of hominin currently is. All in all the game is far closer to Life of Black TIger than it is Green Hell.
_childDocuments_.name: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey

_childDocuments_.review: The premise of the game looks interesting, but, so far, playing it has been incredibly frustrating. Let's start with the first interaction of the game: Press A to Continue. Naturally, I have no "A" to press, as that's a controller A not a keyboard A. The game defaults to controller. The game says using a controller is the preferred way to play it. I hate controllers and I won't use them -- if that's not your case, ignore my comments about controls.The mouse/keyboard controls seemed to have been made by someone intent on making them as difficult to use as possible. Trivial things like looking around _with a mouse_ are made incredibly difficult. Let's give an example: I'm close to another member of my tribe and I want to know who that is. If I use E to identify that member, the information will be off my viewscreen because they are close. If I move the mouse to look up, it exits the information mode. I have to move further away to see the information, or next to them to analyse.Shift, control, alt, the standard modifiers we use to change modes like sprinting, aiming, looking around without changing direction, etc, they are not put to use. Left click and right click are used in unnatural ways and in an irregular which results in a constant fight to get what you want done. And some of the key combinations are just mind-boggling, like pressing control and up-arrow (up arrow? that means taking your hand out of the mouse!), then pressing space, then pressing W... In summary you'll get very frustrated if you play with mouse and keyboard.Next, the UI. The UI is full of symbols which are meaningless to me. The tutorial shows some of this stuff from time to time -- usually when it's least convenient and you are concentrating on something else. And you better memorize them right then and there, because I can't find any information about what I'm seeing in the HUD afterwards. And speaking of user interface, there's no apparent way of skipping the introduction, and sound levels do not seem to be respected in it, which leaves the game blaring in my ears, and keeping anyone from hearing what I'm saying on stream.But what finally pushed me over to write this review is that if you inspect one particular spot in your starting area then an event happens that moves you elsewhere, and good luck finding your way back or continuing the tasks you were doing.Oh, and there's no save game. There's no way of getting back from _looking_ at something and having that change the game irrevocably. Or just experimenting with different ways of doing stuff without having to restart.
_childDocuments_.name: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey

_childDocuments_.review: Are there deeper mechanics I didnt get to? Maybe. Is there a whole range of fun to be had the further you get into the game? Probably. But hell if im going to trek through this mess to get to any of it.Straight up the game tells you that it will not be providing help and its basically all up to you to figure things out. Ok, can't say I agree thats ever a good thing to do in any game but it is what it is. I dont need my hand held to go from point A to B, but there are definitely limits. I'm being told my objectives with quite literally no way to do them. You could argue that figuring it out is the challenge. The problem is that NO CONTEXT AT ALL isnt a challenge, its just an F you. I have no idea what this game can offer me, so in what way am I supposed to guess how I'm supposed to do things? Trial and error 30 seconds into the game isnt fun or even challenging, just tiresome.My biggest gripe was almost immediately after leaving the settlement and encountering the unknown zone. New places, hidden dangers basically make your guy freak out and start to have a breakdown if you stay too long. Cool sounding mechanic, except entering these zones almost blacks out your screen and has flashing hallucinations all the time. Scanning stuff around you builds up a meter that will eventually give you the objective to conquer your fear and head to a big ol ball of light to basically map the area and not lose your mind.Issue with that is the ball is BLINDING. MY GOD. SO BRIGHT. Can see it through walls which clearly marks it as the thing you need to go to. After looking it up, apparently you need to walk into it and hold a button to map the zone. At no point was I told that, and at no point did I get a prompt to do so when I walked into it. Turns out its just fickle like that, and with it being so damn bright I couldn't actually tell if I was in it properly to begin with. So right out the gate had I not looked it up I basically wouldn't have been able to leave the starting zone and progress the game.No thanks.

_childDocuments_.name: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey

_childDocuments_.review: In a nutshell: A game with great potential, but wasted by an approach that is what you'd expect from indie games. To start with, the tutorial is useless. It tells you more or less nothing of what you need to do. Also most things in the game are from the beginning totally misleading. Like, "you learnt how to make a bed"! Great, but nothing tells you how to make it, or what you need to make it. You need to keep a balanced diet! How? No indicators. Sleeping is important! Yeah but how much should I sleep?! I found myself going back and forth to websites explaining how things worked in order to play the game. That should not ever happen in a good title! Controls on PC are also pretty poor - some actions seem to require you to lift your mouse button, just to re-press it microseconds later. Microseconds, because otherwise you need to start over. All actions also require you to keep the button pressed for a while, very bothersome. Some actions seem to require you to keep pressing the buttons too. Again, not explained ad all.All in all, a very frustrating game.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is quite confusing when you play it for the first time, but once you get the hang of it, it becomes a very interesting experience. _childDocuments_.name: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey

_childDocuments_.review: I was originally going to just write "monke" for the review, but this game is actually so good that I'd feel like an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ for making a joke out of it.It's definitely not for everyone, but what it sets out to do, it excels in. It's the kind of game that Spore should have wanted to be, but couldn't even have thought of becoming.Of course its scope is much, much more focused - but it still offers the same kind of feeling of progression, while making sure that every step is enjoyable.The main gameplay is very similar to the dozens of crafting survival indies - so don't expect a whole lot on that front - but it feels a helluva lot better.Especially because of its unique UI design and language, and its weird control scheme. It just works wonderfully well.It is hands down the most immersive experience I've ever had. It's so far beyond anything, I legitimately can't compare it to others. No heavily modded Skyrim or Half Life Alyx can stand up to this.One word of caution. If this is your first time playing, DO NOT start in immersive controls mode. The controls are so unique that you will have no idea what you're doing.

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this game.  Yes it is challenging, yes it can be difficult sometimes to figure out the controls and how things work. _childDocuments_.review: This is turning out to be a way more fun experience than I expected.  There's some limitations to address and get out of the way: the graphics are only on the higher end of the indie spectrum with some kind of goofy looking models, it can be easy to sequence break the general objectives that the game gives you which can lead to more confusion than intended, and what tutorial messages the game does offer you tend to show up when don't have a lot of time to stop and read them only for them to vanish forever before you can get to safety and absorb what they try to teach you.  Beyond these problems, I struggle to find anything to nitpick about it.Overall, its a fascinating experience.  With all one's modern human knowledge, there's still a sense of wonder in discovering how to bang two objects together just right to accomplish something so primitively simple as moving a rock, piling up a crude barrier to better protect your cave, or breaking open a new food source.  After almost 8 hours of play I finished my day with eventually figuring out how to create my first sharpened stick, which I found amazing.  Not only does it open up a lot of questions to answer within the context of the game, but thinking about it I realized that I had just created the first manufactured weapon on planet Earth.  The initial spark of all human warfare began at that moment, making for an entirely new experience for me in video games.  You don't get those moments very often.Now I see a lot of negative reviews cropping up for this game, most of which just seem to come from people who lack the patience or cleverness to wrap their head around it, and that's a shame.  I understand if this isn't for everyone, but there's a wealth of entertainment to be had here.  The game is not what I'd call difficult, at least not in the early stages that I've played so far.  You begin with a very safe home to hide in with more than enough resources to get you started, all next to a relatively small area with few active threats.  It isn't a huge ordeal to breed more monkey men to replace those you lose, there are no hard time limits pressuring you to venture out into the risky unknown, and every death comes with a valuable lesson that leaves you much less likely to repeat it.  Could the game benefit from a patch or two? Absolutely, but I still wholeheartedly recommend this game.  Try it out, play with some sticks and rocks like its the first time you've ever seen them before, and take things at your own pace.  I bet you'll have an interesting time.
