_childDocuments_.review: Gameforge provided me a key to this game prior to launch for review. My reactions were streamed live and can be seen here:Tiny Thor is a really great game. My initial experience was actually during the free demo that was originally released on Itch. Since that demo, I've already seen many improvements within the game that have really brought the game up to par.It's main appeal is the retro-style 2D platforming & puzzling that would be fit for the SNES, but a curve ball is thrown in there with Mjolnir, Thor's hammer which can be thrown and bounced off objects for solving puzzles and creating satisfying trick shots.The beautiful pixel art, authentic sound fonts and FM synths really bring the retro package together.My main concern with this game is if there exists a truly captivating spark. The downside with being a 2D retro platformer is that it's a genre we have seen done a lot - so much so, it was the "FPS" game of the day back during that SNES era (back before it was considered "retro"); a genre that dominated the gaming landscape. Since then we've had many different takes on this genre, and as such, it begs the question whether this game can stand out amongst every game of the past. Is the hammer enough to keep the game captivating?While I personally look forward to playing more, I am certain it is a game I will enjoy for a few more sessions before ultimately deciding to put it down and move on. Admittedly my experience with the game is still early, so perhaps a great "hook" is waiting to catch my attention and keep me coming back for more.Regardless, it's a great game that's worth picking up if you've got an itch for this type of game. The trick shots and puzzles with the hammer really make you feel smart.I also want to add an unrelated note; the devs were really kind and cool when they responded to my original review of the demo. As someone who frequently reviews indie games, it's easy for indie devs to feel like critique of their game is a personal attack, so these devs may often take the review poorly. These devs communicated well, and listened to the feedback. So I encourage anyone who has decided to pick up this game to share their thoughts with these devs. They're good guys and they listen!
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Thor

_childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting for this come out for a while, it looked like one of my favorite kinds of games, a "fast platformer". Something like New Super Marios Bros U Deluxe. A fast paced, minimal "figuring stuff out", just sending it kinda game. Not Mario Maker hard, just something fast and fun.In that regard, this game was a disappointment. It's not at all like what it seemed to me at first. It's not nearly as fast as I had hoped for, and there's a lot of mini puzzles to figure out.That said, it is actually a fantastic game, especially if you grew up in the 16 bit era. Everything about this game feels "period correct", with one exception. The graphics, sound, controls, etc all feel like this could have been a long lost Genesis game. The only thing missing is the excessive sprite lag, which is actually a good thing. Some parts of this game would have bogged down any old console. It's actually fun to have to deal with the challenge without the slowdown.I have played my fair share of these "modern retro platformers" and I usually quickly lose interest, but this game has me hooked. The puzzles frequently leave me scratching my head at first, but after thinking about it for a minute, you realize they really aren't that hard. Overall the game has a pretty solid "challenging but not difficult" feel to it.If the devs decide to make a sequel, I hope we get the ability to run/walk. That's the only thing this game is missing.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Thor

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed the first 75% of this game but the last 25% just ended up being incredibly tedious with far too many cheap deaths.  I thoroughly enjoyed the good parts as the game was mainly platforming with a little bit of action sprinkled in. It had nicely placed checkpoints and the secrets were fun and the right level of difficulty in finding them.  That last 25% just has far to many long  stretches of trial and error without checkpoints which makes it extremely tedious to replay over and over and over again.  The challenge level is far to high for an average or even good player.  I felt like the last 5  levels were on the extreme side where it wasn't fun and just a pain in the butt.   At this point the game went from fun to extremely annoying and I didn't even want to continue on.The 2nd last level where a shadow version of you follows you is one of the worst levels I've ever played.  If you die mid level and resume from a check point the shadow is literally on your tail the whole time and at that point I gave up and enabled god mode because it was impossible.   I couldn't even beat the final boss of the game with god mode on because it was just too clunky and cheap and I lost full interest in playing.  Overall a game that mostly is a lot of fun, the last part was a major disappointment and felt like I was doing kaizoo levels for Mario Maker rather then utilizing all the moves and techniques learned and used in the first 75% of the game.    6/10
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Thor

_childDocuments_.review: Gorgeously nostalgic game, bringing me back to the amiga days. The difficulty is becoming steeper as the level progress, there are optional challenges which are much harder than the normal stages; the game is hard, but the good kind where you sigh with relief when you get to the end of a particularly hard stage. Music is pretty groovy and level design is very creative ; I might expand on this review when I finish it(I'm at 30% so far, about 4hrs in), but this is already a warm recommend to anyone who loves classic platforming challenges.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh boy, this one is a Celeste meets Сuphead levels of frustration, but in a bad way.It feels not playtested enough. Instead of fixing obviously NOT FUN difficulty spikes and gameplay quirks, developers just shoved a disclaimer at the start of the game with text like "git gud".Great art and sound though, that's what I liked.

_childDocuments_.review: Tiny Thor is a fantastic game that combines classic platforming with a cool Norse twist. Right from the start, I was hooked by its beautiful graphics, easy controls (mouse+keyboard or controller), and great secrets and puzzles. The levels are cleverly designed, with puzzles to solve and a good amount of hidden things to find. There are also boss fights with unique mechanics. One thing I really like about Tiny Thor is the music and sound effects. The sound track is catchy and fits the action perfectly. The game has a lot of levels to play through, so there's plenty of content. It seems great for both casual and serious gamers. There's a good amount of challenge without being too hard (besides for the challenge levels, which are, well.. challenging).
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Thor

_childDocuments_.review: Well, I went ahead and finished the game, and generally liked it.  It had a few major irritations, but overall was generally pretty fun.  It's a different take on platforming from what I've played; one review called it "Celeste with a hammer" or something similar, and I heavily disagree with that, unfortunately mostly in negative ways.A few segments definitely had the satisfaction of a good Celeste room, but there are a number of things that make this, in my mind, more painful than Celeste in ways that kill some of the fun:- longer breaks between checkpoints: most Celeste rooms are short puzzles, and you save after every one.  A few of the Tiny Thor levels had long gaps between checkpoints.  It worked out with the difficulty most of the time, but sometimes it was tedious to replay a long-ish section dozens of times while trying to puzzle out the next section.- no preview / blind leaps: longer Celeste levels usually gave you a telescope(?) that let you see the level at your leisure.  Here, you don't get to see the next jump until you get to it, and sometimes they require a level of planning that you just can't do blind.  So you get a basically guaranteed death the first time you see them.  This is a way to increase "difficulty", but it always feels cheap.- "race" levels: A number of segments in Tiny Thor have rising water or some other artificial mechanism to make you run.  This is often done will, but combined with the above points, these can be extremely frustrating in a not-fun way.  There's nothing fun about playing an easy 30-second segment a dozen times because you only have 5-10 seconds to try to figure out the next segment before you drown.- slow deaths: This may just be perception, but one reason Celeste works is that the time penalty dying is negligable; by the time you register that you died, you're back at the start of the room.  Tiny Thor has a little death animation that made it feel slow.  And if you get hit and then fall into lava, you don't actually die until the invincibility wears off, which is a couple seconds.  Luckily, the pause menu saves the last selection, so a quick "pause/enter" restarts much faster.- no in-level saving: AFAICT, if you exit a level for any reason, you restart it back at the start of the level.  Some levels took me 40 minutes for the first play through.  I sometimes tried to sneak in a play session in a quick break, but then had to decide between extending the break to finish the level, or having to replay the first part of the level next time I can back.  That is just a waste of my time.- lack of explanations on new moves: as I complained below in older reviews, new moves get minimal introduction without detailed explanation.  Aside from wall jumps, on dash/double jumps, it took me almost to the end of the game to finally establish when you get a second one of each.- hitboxes: Honestly, this was mostly just the final boss, but a good number of my deaths were due to the horn killing me from several pixels away, or falling through the edge of a leaf.Now that I've complained, there are plenty of good bits.  Of course, they need less detail, but they do, for the most part, outweigh the irritations above.- Music: when you're playing a level over and over, music can make it much more bearable.  Overall, it did that here.- There are a lot of good levels.  Many segments were a fun, satisfying run through on the first or second try, and a few were real puzzles to figure out how to get all the secrets.- The secrets are well-done; a good number early on are obvious, but some of the later ones do a good job rewarding "I wonder if I can do that".Previous update:After a week or two I came back to this, and managed to get through the previously annoying part fairly quickly after I figured out my wall-jump issue: you have to wait for the "wall grab" animation before you jump off, and then you have a fairly narrow window to press both away and jump.  I still mess them up occasionally, but by slowing down my wall jump speed, it's dropped to "minor annoyance".  But it would be nice if the game found a way to explain this or had any sort of guidance.I'm now at 52%; most of the game has been fun, with a lot of fun little sections, some parts that took a bit of thought, and a couple that are just gratuitously frustrating.  One in particular was just "you need to jump this far", and much like wall jumps, it's not well explained exactly how to maximize your distance.  After about ten frustrating minutes of trial and error, I finally found the right combination of inputs and timing to make that long jump.Aside from the extremely uneven difficulty and occasional "we didn't explain how to do this well enough" bits, my other major complaint is the inability to restart mid-level.  This didn't come up much in the first part of the game since levels were generally quick, but it's frustrating to be 25 minutes into a level, get stuck on one part, and then have to spend another 5-10 minutes replaying the entire level because I didn't have time to finish it in one sitting.But overall, at this point, there's been enough good that I'll promote my "4-star" review to a thumbs up.Original (thumbs down) review:I wish I could give this four stars, but given the binary yes/no on Steam, I have to go with no.I made it about a third of the way through percentage-wise, and enjoyed the first few levels; they were cute, had a couple neat tricks, and some fun exploring.  Then it got a little tricky; some things took me a couple tries to have the "aha" moment, some just took a few tries to execute perfectly.Then I hit wall jumps; I don't know what it is, but I just can't get them reliably.  The indicator seems to be "go to the wall, then jump away".  So I get on the wall, press the opposite direction and jump, and it sometimes works and sometimes doesn't.  I was especially confused that sometimes I wall-jumped straight up, before eventually realizing that was just double jumping against the wall, I think because I was jumping too soon.This wasn't too terrible; some bits took longer than they should have, but it was a minor irritation for the most part.  Then I got to a rising water section that requires several wall jumps.  After fifteen minutes or so, I got through it, and was about a second too slow figuring out the next (slightly cute puzzly) part and drowned.After a half hour over two sessions trying to get back there, I'm rage quitting.  I'm sure I could get back, but it'`s just not fun.  Most attempts are nearly a minute long, and then a dumb failed jump makes me restart.  There are plenty of other games I can play that I'll probably enjoy moreFor context, I completed Celeste (including C-sides and Farewell) and Getting Over It.  I enjoy hard games, but while Celeste had quick retries in short levels (except when clearly justified) and Getting Over It is its own thing, this feels more to me like a game that's trying to be hard, but missed what makes it fun.  I'd love to see the rest of the game, but it's just not worth my time right now.Also, I agree with some other complaints about the hammer; you can theoretically throw it in any direction, but the control stick is too imprecise and using the arrows too slow, so anytime there's any time pressure (e.g., an enemy on screen) I just jump around until I can do a throw horizontally or vertically.  It contributes to the feeling that this game just didn't quite figure out the controls.

_childDocuments_.review: I adore this game. Is it hard? 100%. But the difficulty is always fair. The upgrades you get to Tiny Thor's hammer & abilities keep the levels fresh.. Beautiful pixel art and a banger soundtrack. If you like the challenge of Celeste, mixed with Shovel Knight style combat, I think this game will be right up your alley. Great, great game.

_childDocuments_.review: A nostalgic retro platformer for passionists.Difficulty ★★★★★★★★☆☆ (there is an assist mode for any kind of player though)The game has very good 16bit graphic. The influence of godlike retro music creator Chris Hülsbeck is cleary hearable and was a very good decision to bring him along. The boss fights, especially the later ones, were cool. And the basic level design is very creative, to be honest. The game does also have very caring devs that listen to their community fan base.* the game only supports 60 FPS, which is just too less for a fast paced game * no safety question if you accidentally choose "return to world map" when you planned to just reload the last checkpoint* if you loose your heart in a platforming part you are most of the times never able to recollect it (assist mode offers an option for this now)* boss lasers of the clock boss have ap physical block (really? is this a salute to Star Wars lightsabers?)The general difficulty is very demanding and tries to give a nostalgic retro platforming feeling. The problem is that some movements or techniques does not offer a too fair balanced behaviour in the later levels or (especially) challenges like Floorless Frivolity, Zany Zigs or Shifty Shafts.Hence it is not easy to balance a game like this, there was now an  added to the game that is accessable during game in the menu. There you can give you advantages like higher jumps, auto-magent of hearts, or even a god-mode to please any kind of players without getting any disadvantage. This kind of solution is not really what I would have favoured as it still feels like cheating at the end, but no one is forced to use it anyway. So it is fine and this change has a bigger impact on my actual review.* if a lost heart is still on screen any hearts of a heart blocks you collect will be just ignored (re-confirmed on new version)* due to some ingame timing mechanics some few peoples might find some stutters although no FPS drop is recognized* cube in Cubic Companion does not get catapulted out of the water onto the brigde like intended sometimes, resulting in a stuck* color scheme explanations in the shop are mixed up in English (re-confirmed on new version)* some mushroom warps in Criss-Cross-Crevice lead to a spike-death if not aimed absolutely in the center* final boss (world serpent) has a bigger non-visible head hitbox than the actual visual sprite which can have a negative effect on your attack* generating ice bridges is sometimes a little bit off. If not placed perfectly, some puzzles won't work out (eg Loki level with the roundabout ice bridge part)* if you dash too hard through a level it might happen that you get teleported to the upper floor through the ceiling* the broken mirror still reflects your character (re-confirmed on new version)Tiny Thor is a pretty good platform game for passionists seeking an old-school retro feeling. It still has some tiny flaws here and there after some patching, but now Tiny Thor is definitely recommandable for all kind of platform players out there. If you like platformers, Tiny Thor is what you are looking for.A special kudos goes out for joemanaco for really caring about his players, and Chris and Fabian for the absolutely awesome music.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Thor

_childDocuments_.review: Tiny Thor started out as a promising retro platformer, with clever gameplay, fun boss battles, gorgeous visuals, and an incredible soundtrack. However, the game's difficulty curve quickly became too steep, with some puzzles bordering on the absurd. As a result, the game may be too frustrating for casual players, but those who crave a stiff challenge may still find it enjoyable.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Thor

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun and simple, straigthforward platformer. It's linear, focuses entirely on platforming mechanics and puzzles. You unlock a few skills and movements along, and subsequent levels explore how these can be used to navigate harder challanges.I think it's biggest strength is it doesn't get boring. Most puzzles require some thinking on how to use your toolkit to solve them, and executing the plan is almost secondary. Figuring things out is very rewarding. The game keeps things fresh by rarely reusing the puzzles, so all the time you encounter new challenges.I also quite liked that it's simple -- doesn't really have quests, progressions, navigation, backtracking. It makes it easy to pick up for 20 minuts, progress a bit and not worry about having to remember what you're supposed to do next time you want to play.The art is beautiful, characters are charming, the story is simple and story segments are short, so they don't break the flow of the game.It does have some weak points too. Some mechanics are a little bit finicky, difficult to get right, for me i.e. wall jumping, or timing of dash-jump. Once you master them it's fine though. Another problem for me was difficulty of challenge levels. They are IMO well designed, but you have to get them in a single try -- usually any mistake means restart, so it gets tedious. I get it's supposed to be a challenge, but it's frustrating. It could be improved by having practice mode for challenges, where you can restart at any point to practice most difficult sections before attempting everything in one go. Another minor nitpick is completing a challenge isn't very rewarding, you don't get anything in-game from that, even completions screen is the same as with regular levels. Having a leaderboard, maybe some cosmetics or custom cutscene would make it more rewarding. I still had fun though, up to challange VII or so.They're optional though, so overall it's not a big deal.Overall if you like platformers focused on mechanics and interesting platforming puzzles, I highly recommend Tiny Thor.

_childDocuments_.review: There's a lot of really creative platforming and puzzle solving in this game. The mechanic of throwing the Hammer is very clever, and I constantly had to think about the best way to defeat enemies, activate switches, and collect items. The game has a ton of clever challenges, whether they be precision platforming gauntlets or small puzzle rooms. The bee themed levels that end the first portion of the game are going to stick with me for being incredibly fantastic and creative.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Thor

_childDocuments_.review: Tiny Thor is an enjoyable, though not particularly amazing, platformer. Though the good outweighs the bad, this is not a game without some issues.To begin with, the art and music are both great and work well alongside the lighthearted tone and often fast-paced action platforming of the game. Unfortunately, the high quality is undercut by just how little variety there is. This is especially true of the third region since, while it has about as many levels as the previous two regions, its levels tend to be much, much longer and by the end I was well and truly tired of listening to the same music alongside the same icy mountains and frozen temples.Platforming generally feels good and Thor has a versatile moveset which allows for some complicated maneuvers. Between walljumping, a double jump, and an air dash, Thor can cover a lot of distance before touching the ground and the later parts of the game will often require you to string these skills together in one way or another while under pressure from enemies or environmental hazards. Thor sometimes spends so much time without touching the ground that it can become easy to lose track of if you still have a jump and/or a dash remaining so it would have been nice to have a visual or auditory cue tied to those, but I otherwise have no issues with the standard platforming in this game.However, one thing I certainly have a few problems with in Tiny Thor is the hammer. The hammer rarely feels good to use, which is a rather large problem when it's one of the game's defining features. Thor is able to aim his hammer before throwing it and the hammer will bounce off of not just physical walls, but also the edge of the screen itself. Many of the more puzzle-focused challenges in the game require you to bounce the hammer at a certain angle or to trap the hammer somehow to make it rapidly bounce in a smaller area. Aiming the hammer can feel finicky, especially if you're on moving or breaking platforms, and this is compounded by the hammer's hitbox being smaller than its sprite implies - even by the end of the game I frequently missed hitting various objects by a handful of pixels. Bouncing the hammer off of the screen itself sounds like an interesting idea, but it mostly ends up feeling weird and needing to make use of the screen's edge rather than static environmental objects often left me wondering if I had actually figured out the intended solution to the various puzzle-platforming challenges or if I had found a significantly more awkward solution the developers didn't plan for. The last issue with the hammer is you'll often want to set it to bounce in a straight vertical or horizontal line, but Thor will immediately catch the hammer if he touches it (often resulting in death for one reason or another), which means you often need to awkwardly make sure you have enough space to throw the hammer and then get completely out of its way before it rebounds. Pressing the hammer button while the hammer is out will make the hammer zoom back to Thor, so making Thor automatically catch the hammer on touch feels completely unnecessary and only gets in the way.There are a few other oddities worth noting as well. For example, blue gems are Tiny Thor's version of currency and, like coins in most platformers, strings of gems are often used to guide the player along platforming paths, especially when the destination is not initially visible. However, gems collected in a run of a level remain gone after dying and respawning, depriving the player of a useful visual indicator, which is an especially odd choice since ghost versions of the gems *do* appear if you replay a level. Tiny Thor has some issues with its visual language too, such as the hitbox on horizontal bounce mushrooms being much smaller than the whole mushroom, the ice covered walls (which you can't jump off of) sometimes blending in a little too closely with the heavily snow-covered walls (which you can jump off of), and the fact that any enemy not covered in spikes is safe to jump on - except for the very round ghosts, which will kill you.Even with its various issues, I think Tiny Thor's level design is quite solid overall. It presents a good challenge and the difficulty curve was pretty stable; Tiny Thor is a hard game without being overly demanding and the only frustration I ever felt was from some particularly awkward hammer-throwing moments. Checkpoints are frequent and generally felt properly distributed. There were a few moments in the later parts of the game where I died because I didn't know what to expect from a new room, but these were also consistently within ~5-10 seconds of a checkpoint and with infinite lives it hardly mattered. Most of the boss fights were also entertaining and level mechanics were generally varied (floating on wind currents got a bit old).Tiny Thor has its share of issues and rough edges, some more severe than others, yet it often provides a solid, enjoyable platforming experience. While this certainly isn't the strongest recommendation I've given to a game, I don't regret my time playing Tiny Thor and I think it's a game worth considering for anyone looking for a challenging platformer.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd love to play this game, but when I reached world 3, the game's controls really felt like a pain to play.The jump to be made just after the kraken was the trigger for me to publish this review.  The dash followed by a jump, whether in this level or in Challenge XII, seems far too imprecise and imperfect, and it's all too easy for the player to miss a jump if he doesn't press the right key in the millisecond.The game is beautiful in terms of design, it's very varied, but the controls of the dash or even the aiming of the hammer got the better of me. Unfortunately, I wouldn't recommend this game, which is more frustrating than difficult.

_childDocuments_.review: Tiny Thor nails the Retro Platformer genre and takes you back to a time when games were fun and challenging. The game allow you to experience the Norse God Mythology from a different perspective and does it with style. Just great fun with a good learning curve . I am only a few levels in and still have a lot of abilities to unlock. To all of you 16 Bit tragics, this will hit your nostalgia button.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Thor

_childDocuments_.review: A fun platformer that knows what it's trying to do an executes it well. The game clearly takes inspiration from Celeste and appears to even offer an Easter egg or two to those who play it. That said, it is very much its own game. Thor's Hammer is a centerpiece of game play and it allows this to feel like the platformer I was hoping for while also offering challenges that felt new and made me think a little bit. For platformer fans who are looking for an actual platformer rather than a metroidvania that has good platforming in it, this game will scratch that itch. The one complaint I have is that the movement felt a tad slow at times. The mechanics involving the hammer would likely be incredibly frustrating if the game operated at the speed of Celeste, but but the speed did take a little getting used to.  All in all an easy recommend from me.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Thor

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful game whose level design impressed me from start to finish.I expected something that wouldn't be very easy, and it's tough yet fair difficulty did not disappoint!If you enjoy a challenge that tries to get everything it can out of the abilities you are given then give it a shot, and don't give up!
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Thor

_childDocuments_.review: I played the demo for Tiny Thor awhile back and I knew it was going to be something very special. I live a busy life and was just now able to get to it. So far I have played stages 1-3 and Tiny Thor has met my expectations and then some. This game is a breath of fresh air and a must own. 10/10PS: Keyboard and mouse friendly, though controller might be best, depends on personal preference (I used keyboard and mouse, and tho tricky at certain points, made it through just fine), and key binding is available.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Thor

_childDocuments_.review: I waited a long time for the game to be released. And the first time I played it, I thought it had colourful graphics, but nothing I hadn't seen before. The gameplay was normal too. Then I gave it another try and found out that the gameplay soon becomes very challenging. Now I love the game. My advice is to play at least the first 4-5 levels to get a complete picture of the game.The story is also cool, I like Hugin and Munin, the two ravens. They have a great sense of humour. It also took me a few runs to get used to Mjoellnir (the hammer). Aiming and shooting is very important, I found out. Some opponents aren't so tough when Mjoellnir hits them in the back :-)I look forward to encountering more of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Thor

_childDocuments_.review: This game is literally all I've played since I got it a few weeks ago. Just beat it 100% and I definitely recommend it! It's not easy, especially the later levels, but I would say it's very fair. There are LOTS of game mechanics, and they push all of them to the extreme. You'll get frustrated, but then once you get past where you're stuck, you'll get excited all over again. Hope we get a sequel!

_childDocuments_.review: I am a 16 bit old-timer and this ticks all the right boxes, while at the same time offering modern platforming based on skill and light-touch puzzle solving. Music is excellent as expected (big fan of Huelsbeck). It gets tough though... not sure I'll have the nerve/patience to actually complete it (I am just past the second boss). The good thing is that you can try as many times as you want thanks to generous checkpointing.

_childDocuments_.review: It's nice to play a game with such polished art. Steam is flooded with so many awful looking indie games with crappy pixel art that it's hard to find games with actual quality pixel art like this among all the garbage.--Graphics--The pixel art is beautiful, the animations are fantastic and this game looks stunning. Henk Nieborg & Nauris Amatnieks are 2 very talent pixel artists and their work here is a pleasure to look at.The title screen and intro cutscene are rendered at an incorrect resolution so they look blurry & awful, which is a shame. (The intro cutscene also has an artstyle that doesn't fit with the rest of the games art)Thankfully everything else in the game is pixel perfect. You can render the game at 1x resolution and view all the crisp pixel art at its intended resolution, which is great and should be the standard, but I can't tell you how many modern pixel art games don't align to pixel grids, mix sprite resolutions, inflate sprites and ruin their pixel art assets in various ways.--Gameplay--The central gimmick of throwing your hammer and bouncing it off of things to kill enemies, collect gems and solve puzzles is a really neat one. Its as solid a base as any of the best puzzle platformers and it's executed here really well. it's always fun and satisfying.you travel a map with levels that are generally just the right length, new gimmicks are introduced at a good pace and you're always interested to see what's in the next level.Boss fights are solid in design and perfecting them is a fun challenge.In addition to major abilities unlocked by killing bosses, There is a shop where you can buy little power ups.Be warned once you buy these they CAN'T BE TURNED OFF. If you decide they make things too easy or you don't like them, you're stuck with them and your save file is sullied. There is no reason why these couldn't have been toggleable like the alternate colours.Collectible placement is mostly good. I've had fun so far collecting everything.. with a few isolate instances of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.level 20 - "Steep Steps" has an absolutely insane single blue gem placed off camera, below and far to the left of a ledge in an area that kills you.there is no way to know the gem is there and dashing down there to be able to see it will almost certainly get you killed by ice winds.luckily you still retain the gems you collected after dying but this collectable placement is not good design.--Design and Execution Problems--There are a few cases of sloppy design and things that don't work well or could have been programmed better.*The wall jump controls suck. In a rather outdated decision the devs require you to flick the control stick away from the wall as you jump.It's manageable but it doesn't feel good and it's not a good way to do wall jumping. there is a timer that allows you to wall jump for a brief period after leaving the wall but you have to be holding away from the last wall you came in contact with.The modern method is better because;1. It doesn't require the player to unnecessarily flick the stick as they jump, since the player always wants to do a wall jump when they press A while clinging to a wall.2. You can let go from pressing towards the wall in plenty of time before wall jumping since the wallslide state is only cancelled by pushing away from the wall for a short period.if they wanted to let you do the double jump off the wall then they should have only had it trigger if you're pressing towards the wall. I don't see why you'd ever want to use it instead of a walljump though because it mostly gets you killed.*There are a bunch of puzzles and places in levels where you can softlock yourself. In my opinion a good puzzle platformer has no softlocks and always has a way to reset the puzzle without having to go back to the last checkpoint.*Your hammer will bounce off the edges of the game camera and there a few places where you have to exploit this to actually move an object upward by jumping to move the camera up. It's weird to see this used in the level design because it doesn't feel right. It feels more like an exploit than an intended mechanic. There's a challenge called "cubical companion" where this is used. The challenge features multiple softlocks and was a distinct point in the game where the design felt clunky to me. *There are small ball platforms that swing on the end of vines. These seem to have pretty awful collision and tend to throw you off arbitrarily. I think it was intended for you to try to walk along them as they rotate but they just don't work well, Your character jitters in a glitchy manner and falls off inconsistently. it's best to continuously jump on them to avoid the janky collision throwing you off.*There are mushrooms at different angles that you slam to launch off of. If you're not absolutely in the center of these, which is hard to see because the sprites are wonky and organic in aesthetic, you can veer off into spikes and die. I would have programmed a subtle repositioning to the correct trajectory.Despite its problems here and there, this is still a very enjoyable, unique and high quality platformer that I would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Thor

_childDocuments_.review: Tiny Thor is a fun and challenging. The game features beautiful pixel art, catchy music and clever level design. The gameplay is centered around using Mjölnir, the hammer of Thor, to bounce off enemies and obstacles. You can also learn special abilities and unlock secrets along the way. The game has a lot of charm and personality, and it will keep you entertained for hours. If you are a fan of retro platformers, you should definitely check out Tiny Thor!
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Thor

_childDocuments_.review: Really good game,  this was a lot of fun and kinda tough in places,  just like old platform games, but the graphics are good and if you played the demo, you'll really have some fun here.The story is pretty basic but if you've played Cuphead and a few others of this genre, it is a familiar kind of fun. There were even a few points that made me chuckle, so that gets it some points too.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Thor

_childDocuments_.review: It's hard to all-out-recommend this game, but I will overall.Under a casual eye, this retro platformer is extremely satisfying to play and very very nostalgic.However, under a completionist eye, this game will be a very distasteful experience.The lack of polish in the movement, controls, and physics really show themselves when you are doing the challenges (especially the last half). Some of the collectibles are hidden a little too out of sight, with no good ingame tracker to unlock later for the blue gems.Overall, I only recommend this if you want a casual laid back experience. If you are looking for another retro-styled 2D platformer to 100% complete, however, I say go somewhere else.

name: Darwin Project
detailed_description: Darwin Project takes place in a dystopian post-apocalyptic landscape in the Northern Canadian Rockies. As preparation for an impending Ice Age, a new project, half science experiment half live-entertainment, is launched. It's called 'Darwin Project' and it challenges 10 participants to survive the cold and fight to the death in a treacherous arena. KEY FEATURES : - SPECTATOR EXPERIENCE: Through the Spectator Experience Extension, viewers can impact each Darwin Project match in several groundbreaking ways: Cast votes to choose the target of a Power activated by the Show Director Place bets on which inmate or team they think will emerge victorious Bid for Powers normally reserved for Show Directors & unleash them in a Private Match - SHOW DIRECTOR: The Show Director is the living bridge between the players and spectators. He/She is the host and master who controls the arena with nuclear bombs, zone closures, gravity storms, and the power of their voice. This could be a real tool of self discovery; the start of your new career as a charming but deadly game show host. - DYNAMIC, TACTICAL GAMEPLAY WITH SURVIVAL ELEMENTS: Gather resources, craft tools, upgrade your gear, track your enemies, engage in both melee and ranged combat, and be the last inmate left alive.

short_description: In Darwin Project, ten inmates must survive the elements, track each other, fight, craft tools, and use their social skills to be the last one standing. It's a unique take on battle royale with a Show Director to influence the match and Spectator Interactions to create a one-of-a-kind game show.

_childDocuments_.review: 9/10 Truly a unique game. It's more than a battle royale due to its entirely unique gameplay. This game doesn't rely on a weapon looting system unlike all other battle royale games. It has a material system that you use to build equipment such as traps and arrows. You only have two weapons which include an axe and a bow. The customizability in this game is insane and picking the right equipment in the lobby is crucial to winning a game. You don't have to play as a inmate, you can play as the game director. As the game director you can: Limit zones, drop nukes, help players etc. Abusing the role of director can get you banned.This game is truly something special and doesn't get the credit it deserves. Please give it a try as soon as you can, it's free!(The game has a battle pass BUT you can use the ingame aquirable currency called ramen to buy it so it is free if you work hard to get it.) Edit: This game despite early access is updated so often you wont even know what the last update looked like because it is already better.

_childDocuments_.review: This game really surprised me with how well it captures the whole "reality show" thing.As a player, armed with a snow shovel/axe hybrid and a bow made of a broken ski, you are placed into a large arena with nine other players, and have to fight to the death. The catch is, you have a one additional player - the Director - flying around with a free-cam and talking to players, throwing events into the game, such as closing down areas of the map, giving players heals, or even dropping a nuke on an entire section of the map. The Director's job is to make the game more interesting for the players, and push it toward a conclusion. The Director also may or may not be streaming their view of the game, which allows their viewers to vote on the details of some events that the Director enacts, such as which section of the map gets closed, or where the nuke drops.As a player, the game is incredibly fun, and trying to entertain the Director/crowd to gain their favor is an extremely interesting social mechanic that can completely change the outcome of the game.I have yet to play as the Director, but I want to wait until I've played a little more and gotten a little bit better at the game, and I want to have some people to stream it to so I can use the voting system (which is totally optional, by the way.)tl;dr this game is basically "appease the director to get buffs", which is unreasonably fun

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually review games but this really does deserve it. For multiple reasons but I feel like I should set the record straight.Darwin used to be 15$ but just became F2P and many of the negative reviews are complaining about this. About how they want a refund or how they got scammed. In no way did you get scammed. This game was most definitely worth the 15 dollars however the playerbase just wasn't big enough to let players meet anyone new. Plus you get compensation for peviously owning the game. You will receive the Founder’s Pack containing 2 Legendary sets, 3 Legendary Axes, 3 Legendary Bows, a full jumpsuit collection, and 5 Fan Gifts on the 24th. So how exactly did you get scammed because that's a lot of items. Not to mention this is an Early Access game and even though it is one of the best Early Access games out there, you knew what you were signing up for.So on to the actual review.The game is honestly amazing. One of the best Early Access games you will ever play. It is a battle royale game similar to Fortnite and PUBG however there are many twists. Such as1: the fact that there are no guns or grenades or anything of the sorts, you have a bow and an axe. 2: you can craft the majority of the things you will need3: there is a survival aspect which is the coldness. you have to stay warm4: there is only 10 players instead of 100 and the map is much smaller5: zones close one by one instead of a storm or gas closing in6: there is a director that can somewhat influence the outcome of the game. and i say somewhat for a reason7: people watching streams of the game can vote for certain director actions8: you can track down other playersAnd those are just the major differences between this and other BRs. So this game immediately stands out from the pack but another reason it greatly stands out from the pack is the dev crew. They are one of the best development teams out PERIOD. They have a discord in which they listen to the community HEAVILY. Your voice will be heard there. They help out people with game issues, support the members and listen for feedback. Even adding new features that are frequently requested or that they like. Not to mention the amazing community in this game. Hospitality is all over the place. There is minimum toxicity which can easily be reported so getting tilted by others isn't something that happens much.All in all I fully recommend this game giving it a 8/10 and thata's only because I think a game can always be improved. In this case the power of the director should be toned down from "somewhat influencing the outcome" to "barely influencing the outcome".

_childDocuments_.review: Brilliant. Absolutely brilliant. I'll do two quick reviews, one for each role in the game.TL;DR: If Fortnite and Hunger Games had a baby, added a simple and tactical survival mechanic, and added in a really, REALLY great community, this would be it.As an Inmate: A game with a very simple premise, just enough depth to allow you to sort out your own playstyle, and an emphasis on tactics and skill over luck... with just enough of a luck factor thrown in to make it very interesting. I don't even know how many battles I've had that were close and intense and came right down to the wire. It's a very well balanced game. The clashes are great - when two people hit each other with their axes at the same time, they'll deflect and bounce off each other instead of just each hitting the other. Axe swings deflect projectiles, too - it makes for seriously good combat. There's only a couple "tricks" and you can do just fine without axe-teleporting anyway...As a Director: THIS IS SO MUCH FUN. I'm a shoutcaster, so this plays to my strengths already, but oooh man. Being Show Director is even more fun than playing as an Inmate, for me. This is where you really get to see the awesome community Darwin Project has - when you're watching two people battling and their zone begins to close, and they stop and help each other escape safely only to continue their battle once they're both safe and ready, it's awesome. Or seeing three players duking it out in a small room, only for a fourth to literally dive in the window and wipe them all out, out of nowhere.And it's FREE. Oh man. Install this right now.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great. It fixes everything that's bad about other battle royale games, namely:- RNG. The outcome of the game is not determined by whether or not you got a good gun 5 seconds earlier than the opponent who spawned right next to you. Because people don't spawn next to each other. Nor can you get an insane advantage over your opponents by getting more lucky with loot, seeing as your main tools are still an axe and a bow, which are available from the beginning of the game, and the loot you are getting will always be very similar to the loot everybody else is getting, because it consists mostly of 2 basic resources which you can use to craft whatever you need at the moment;- Looting. Some people might not see that as a bad thing, but for me, constantly getting new weapons, which might just be slightly better or worse versions of the weapon you already have, bullets of all sorts, other stuff like that, and managing your inventory just isn't fun. It's not a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ rpg. Although in my opinion it's not a fun mechanic even in rpgs, for that matter. In Darwin Project, the process of looting is very simple, because, as I said before, most of the loot is just wood or leather. You get it and craft what you need. Apart from that, it can be one of the three boosting items, an upgrade to your gear, and that's about it. No need to mess with inventory at all. Love it;- Killing from huge distances. There aren't any open spaces on the map. It's all covered in hills, cliffs and big ass trees. And you also can't really snipe from afar with a bow. And one, or even two shots from a bow are not enough to kill you in this game. So you'll always get a fair fight;- Camping. In Darwin Project the problem of sitting in the bushes is solved rather elegantly. The tracking system allows you to learn the player's current position by lookiing at the things they left after crafting or looting something. There are actual tracks in the snow in this game too. And if you get lucky and the area where you did most of crafting and looting gets closed, you still can't hide for long thanks to the heat system. Eventually you gonna have to build a fire to not freeze to death. And that fire will let everyone in a big radius know where you are. And the director can also make you are target of a hunt, which, I believe, lets everyone know where you are.On top of all that, this game also has a very unique setting, cool traps and powers, and the show director system, which I'm yet to learn about. All in all, I'm really impressed with this game. Can't stand other battle royale games, but this one is so much better. Highly recommend it.The only things that bother me are the main menu screen and the loading screen. They look ugly as hell, please change them.

_childDocuments_.review: Besides a few small issues, the Darwin Project is the most unique and best take on the Battle Royale genre since the original ARMA 3 Mod. In This rendition there are only 10 players in a quadrant styled arena. This, by itself, makes the rounds much more "personal" in a way. The game is 'controlled" by a director who goes around talking to players and causing events to happen. Closing "zones" so they can't be re-entered (this game's version of the circle in Fornite and PUBG) and causing little game events like Nukes, Anti-Gravity, and a Manhunt. It makes the games more unpredictable, but in a way that feels fair as opposed to the RNG nature of Fornite and PUBG. Most of the directors are, for the most part, entertaining although occasionally you'll get those directors that attempt to take you down personally if you are racking up many kills by healing people mid battle etc. Although this never felt completely unfair as he could have easily done the same to myself. Its a social game and rewards communication between you and others in the game either banter or asking the director for stuff. The combat is a perfect example of "easy to play hard to master" where you are only given two weapons, the bow and the axe. There are no direct upgrades, and all of the "damage buffs" can be easily obtained by changing which arrows you craft/ which axe buff you have in your Crafting Wheel. I never felt like I was at a major disadvantage in any fight, even if I was outclassed many times by others who had great aim. The combat feels floating and smooth which works (technically) wondrously for the most part. Hits pack a punch and the game informs you when anyone does damage to anyone on the map which makes it fun to strategize where you want to go and who you want to interact with. There, of course, are a few issues with the game's current state. One of the biggest issues is the hitboxes can be downright deceptive at times. Falling from above onto someone, you are much more likely to get a hit then someone looking up swinging at you. There have been also some weirdness with the rage of mele hits that feel random. Sometimes an enemy two feet from me doesn't hit me, but I can hit him. Little issues like that, that do not kill the experience, but are annoying nonetheless. Also it is really easy to "force chain" hits when you corner someone into a house, where unless you stop attacking you will be able to "combo" the enemy to death. This feels unfair as it leaves the defender at a unswayable disadvantage. There are also some oddities, like how wildlife falls from the sky occasionally, it makes it all look a bit cheap. There is also a slight lack of content. Besides playing over and over (Which I don't have an issue with 6.6 hours in) there aren't many things to do past your first few games. There is one map and that is it. I can't call this a total "issue" yet as its still in Early Access (released a week or so ago) and I am sure that they will be beefing up the content. Don't let the low player numbers fool you (555 late at night to 1.8k during midday) it is never an issue getting into a game (partly due to the small game size, only 10 required players makes up to 55.5 active games at the most dead of night) check it out! It is well worth the cheap 15$ price tag!

_childDocuments_.review: So, in this game, you can play as an Inmate or a Director.  As an inmate your goal is to be the last one standing, however many obstacles are in your way. For example, you have to build a fire every once in a while-  because you can freeze to death. The Fire produces smoke which reveals your position to any players that look in the sky. You have 2 weapons, a bow and arrow, and an axe. The Bow and Arrow does 150 damages by default (you have 600 health) and the axe does 150 as well. You can upgrade the damage it gives by sacrificing two woods and two leathers. There are trees and chairs scattered around the map that you can harvest to gain those materials. There are also zones, if you are inside a closed zone (The Forbidden) You will start freezing to death.  As a Director, you are in the game to spice it up. You gain one action point per minute, with those action points you can purchase certain ability's that will spice the game up, those abilities include -Turning off Gravity 5 Action Points, set off a gravity storm in the entire arena, the jump height is increased by 20% for 2 minutes and 21 seconds. -Nukes Costs 5 action points, gain the ability to set off a nuclear bomb in a zone. Once you place the nuke down, inmates have to vacate that zone in 41 seconds or they are instantly knocked out of the game. -The Ability to close a zone There are Seven zones. You have the ability to close 2 of those zones for 3 action points, you can choose what zone you want to close. If an inmate is inside a zone, their cold meter starts going down, so they start freezing to death. Goes handy with nuclear bombs. -Manhunting an inmate You can purchase a manhunt with 5 action points, the manhunt will trigger immediately on the player you choose. What it does is it places a bounty on the man hunted inmates head, and the position of that inmate is shown to all remaining inmates. Manhunt cannot be used if there are only 2 inmates left. -Placing an Electron You gain the ability to place an electron on 1 position out of 8 in the 7 zones, an electron is a rare crafting material which grants the ability to either Teleport, Go Transparent or Go Invisible. You can also craft a turret, which I have not figured out how to yet. -Heal, Speed Buff, Warm Up or invincibility. You can also help the inmates as a director too. If you choose to do this, you can either Heal them (2 AP) Speed Buff them (3 AP) grant them invincibility for 20 seconds (4 AP) or Refill their cold meter (1 AP)  The Directors appearance is a huge freaking drone. The Director can also talk to the inmates, if he is within a 50m range of them. I personally have roleplayed as jigsaw while the director.  because you know, do you want to play a game.  So, do I like this game so far? Absolutely! The Beta ran Extremely smooth for one, I didn't freeze once, and it all around is just a good game! However, the queues for being a director were HORENDUS. I had to wait about 15 minutes to get a game, but as an inmate you instantly got into a game. Also, if you want to play with friends, you have to be in voice coms, but they are planning on adding a custom game system soon, and me and my friends are looking forward to that. Well, one of the only things I found wrong with this game was that in order to really have fun, you have to have a microphone. People who didn't talk ended up dying first, just like in SOS or Friday the 13th, you have to have a microphone.  Nice job Scavenger studios!

_childDocuments_.review: I am 32 years old.My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and we adopted our son together. Both are now 4 years old.When we were going through our separation, I felt lost and unhappy. I was self-destructive. One day, I was so angry with everything spiraling out of control that I punched a concrete wall in a moment of overwhelming emotion. This resulted in breaking my fifth metacarpal in my right hand—the hand I worked with, played games with, and used to carry my children to bed—the hand I desperately needed to ensure I could continue providing.Upon learning the severity of the self-inflicted damage, I became almost suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man, with no history of depression or anxiety. I had never experienced anger outbursts, nor was I the type to break down and cry, but I was in a tough situation that truly prevented me from seeing the light on the other side.With nothing better to do, I looked for a game I could play WITH ONE HAND while recovering. Somehow, I stumbled upon this game and read some of the comments. I decided it was worth a try... I must admit I didn't beat the game, nor did I play as much as some of you. In fact, I may have played this game for only a day or two. That being said, after doing so, I had a new joy and hope for life. I managed to leave behind the pain and suffering that had been thrust upon me. I could experience the joy and happiness of other people. I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥ minutes listening to this music, long enough to realize that I would be okay.After realizing this, I turned off the game and went back to work. My hand hurt a lot, but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so sorry for myself and became the father I needed to be at that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving like.Today, I am close friends with the mother of my children. We don't fight, argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents and friends.Now I have 3 children. My third child is, wait, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my separation, and we just unexpectedly stumbled into each other's lives. We have been dating for a year and are very happy together.Moral of the story: you never know what life has in store for you, and if I had given up when all odds were against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.Thank you.

_childDocuments_.review: Darwin project is a great twist and an amazing concept to the battle royale genre. You got yourself crafting, item managing, fights, looting, perks and unique game elements. The most important thing is that even though it has all this, its fast and action packed.Duo mode is in beta, but its a lot of fun to try and survive with a friend.It's in early access but its way more complete than most of the E-A games. Minor cons: Even though putting a director in the game who controls the battles flow is really awesome in my opinion, it sometimes can get annoying: drops a nuke on you while he can clearly see you can't get out with the equipment and situation youre in.  Preferring players over others, making it unbalanced. Etc. All in all, it's a really fun game, which has its own learning curve. Definitely pick it up while it's this cheap, and you better start practicing with the bow and arrow. :)Cheers.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: typosComing to this game after playing other battle royales such as PUBG or Fortnite, the game feels as smooth as a baby's butt. The graphics are cute, nifty and at higher graphics settings, beautiful. I've been hyped for this game since I found out about the open beta.Playing as a prisoner in this hexagonal post apocalyptic winter arena gives me that Hunger Games vibe, except it's more focused on gameplay than story, of course. Speaking of gameplay, the game runs smooth and the replayability feels endless because every match is different than the previous one. Unlike PUBG, looting, while helpful, isn't crucial to win, you already start with your weapons and those don't change, everything you loot is just variables. The map is well built and always feels fair and random.As a show director, as long as you have a good rating, you get to affect the map, players, and electronic drops (which are basically airdrops that give you a special power). Your job is to be entertaining and fair. I like to help out the players who seem like they would fail without my help, have a nice small talk with the players and overall make sure everyone has a fighting chance.The game has an entertaining announcer that reminds me of GLADoS with its wits and snarky comments such as "You can die tomorrow" when you win.I do have one complaint however, and it's that in the main menu it tells me I'm getting a solid 70 ping, but when I'm in a match, I magically have 200+ ping which is kind of annoying, but still very much playable, I guess.I received this game for free so not many complaints from me, overall, I enjoy 90% of my matches which is more than I can say for other games in my library on which I have pegged over a thousand hours (coughcoughcsgocoughcough).Thank you for the free game, I hope you do well in your sales, this game is definitely worth the price in my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: beta was fun, really enjoyed it. The game is good, and I do recommend it, but NOT right now. I'll explain. Wait for the game to go free-to-play before you get it. I personally don't see the game lasting long unless it goes FTP, but that's my opinion.The game is smooth, runs well, and the overall concept is brilliant and unique.I really like directing, and the overall concept of directing. Directing was the main attraction to me, not to mention I enjoy the BR genre.but as it stands the only people who actually play this game are twitch streamers, and the people who no life it. If you get this game, prepare to get rekt in your face for a few games, as the skill difference will be apparent. If you're going to try to just have a casual experience right off the bat, this game isn't for you. My biggest quarrel is with the knockback system. When you get hit, you go flying, and people can lead another free shot on you if they have any common sense. This is even worse in the low gravity zone (think Flying Scoutsman from CS:GO, because that's EXACTLY what this director-enabled zone effect is. You fly around trying to axe each other or shoot one another. I feel sorry for the poor soul who gets melee'd off the ground and shot with an arrow, because you will be sent flying across the map). You're basically a sitting duck in the air, and it sucks to be in low-gravity. You're better off staying grounded unless you absolutely have to jump.I feel like this game could use a "ground slam" mechanic to counteract the knockback and bouncing in low gravity. I like the fast paced fights, I just hate how there isn't much counterplay to getting knocked back, especially if the director cucks you and buffs your attacker.The female character is very "meh" at the moment as well.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a big fan of the BR style games ever since I got into the Hunger Games series because that whole idea is very intriguing. So after playing games like PUBG, Fortnite BR, H1Z1 King of the Kill, Rust BR, The Culling and so on I found them really fun but still not fully the Hunger Games experience. But Darwin Project is as close an adaption of that model than I have seen so far, the director role when done correctly is super fun and coupled with a director that has a decent viewership it adds that extra Hunger Games dimension of trying to win favor. The gameplay is solid if not just a little lacking in equipment in its current state and I hope the devs add a lot more options for the director to utilize during a match. But as of right now this game is a very solid and super fun experience with plenty of draw to have you saying to yourself “Just one more game”. I do hope they add in something to build towards because you gain levels and fans and such as you play but you don’t get anything in return as of yet. I need some progression in this game because I know they can add a bunch of cool stuff since they already have the ability to customize to an extent currently.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has an incredible potential thanks to a very clever design that get rid of everything I hated about other battleroyale. A lot of good ideas that still need to be fine-tuned for balance though, but overall the game is very well produced. It's very fluid, not a single technical issue in 6 hours (+ as much time watching streams), no freeze, no lag, no frame drop. What's more, I trully love the graphics and the models (lacking diversity right now but the EA is only 6 days old). The private match and spectator mode are truly efficient, better working that most multiplayer games, same for the matchmaking : 10 sec in average to find a game. It might seems silly in 2018 but yet it feels good to have a game that is actually robust, everything is smooth, quick and without that feeling that everything might or might not crash at anytime (even though I have a great PC it happens on lots of game, to stay on BR : PUBG for instance, even on low because it's not just graphic related).The streamer friendly system is really doing some good to the game but it also might make non-streamer players feel like they are "inferior" for not streaming and having a community behind them to use the twitch integration. However it is an absolute pleasure to watch private matches streams among streamers/friends.I really hope this game will have the player base it deserves and that it will keep it until the release and long after, unlike so many before that had their hype moment in EA before disapearing in the abyss of Steam 2 weeks after.Good job Scavengers Studio, keep it that way !

_childDocuments_.review: = as I'm writing this review the game is still EARLY ACCESS =PROS:- The community is vibrant and fun to talk to (most of the people have mics, I suggest you get one as well)- The developers really put their time into the game and their community, with monthly big updates.- The game is still early access so there's plently more to come.- A quick paced battle royale - having up to 10 players each game and a compact map.- Awesome animations, cool fighting, graphics ain't too shabby for a small developer team.- It's free.- No micro-transactions, only cosmetics to buy with in-game currency (which you can also get for free by a small amount daily and they eventually pile up).CONS:- The report system is stupid, getting people warned and later banned if they got a certain amount of reports on them (I could be wrong about this whole section, it's based on people's comments online).- The balance between a good player and a newbie is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ retarded. A newbie will NEVER and I mean NEVER no matter what will be able to kill a pro player (unlike any other game where you atleast get a chance). If you manage to be put in the same lobby as a top 100 player or just a player who has over 100 hours you're ♥♥♥♥♥♥.- The bow and arrow are broken. If someone is even slightly decent with them there is absolutely no way you can win him. Axe parry is stupiditly hard and without a speed drink you basicly have no chance to even get to him.TL;DR:It's a good game, with a broken system of pro players vs new players (who have no chance at winning). Can get on ones nerves but it's still fun.You should get it, it's free anyway.

_childDocuments_.review: Updating this review to add some extra contextI've played this game ever since the alpha stages. It was an extremely impressive Battle Royale/Hunger Games/Game Show style game that immediately peaked my interest, especially when the Show Director mechanic was shown, I was instantly hooked. A major issue with the game though was a massive lack of marketing and promotion. One trailer at E3 and that was pretty much it unless you followed the social media accounts. The playerbase was dying fast because there was nobody new coming in, and the game had a lot of issues at the time that weren't being worked on (Example: There was no tile system before, so the map was completely identical before that was fixed, so almost every game felt the same unless there was a good show director, which even that had it's issues). After MONTHS of players asking for it as well, the devs made the game Free2Play, but at the same time removed a lot of features it had before when the game fully launched (No duos at launch when they've had it for the longest time in early access and a very piss-poor Battle Pass system)A MAJOR issue with this game though is the dev team. This team is being led by the same people who worked on ACE: Arena Cyber Evolution, a 3v3 multiplayer game that, much like this game now, was abandoned due to nearly identical issues with a major lack of marketing and overall the dev team not giving a damn about the game, so they've abandoned Darwin Project to most likely work on another game that will most likely be abandoned after a couple months or a year much like all of their games beforehandDo not play this game or any other games made by this studio. So many amazing games with great potential that gets abandoned before it could ever even get a chance.

_childDocuments_.review: The combat system is simple but flawed.You get an axe, and you get a bow.You can bounce arrows if they hit mid-axe-swingbut the .5 second startup does not allow you to bounce arrows. Those very small moments are what matter, so your best bet you have is to hope you swung at the right time while hoping to make contact with an arrow of which only benefits you by negating damage and giving you another arrow. All while the attacker is far enough away to fire several more without problem.There is very high reward and very little risk for using bows, you slow down slighty and that's about it...  not like slowing down is going to hurt you much when both melee and ranged attacks send opponents flying the same distance.They recently introduced a combat roll, allowing you to quickly roll in any direction. But this takes up 33% of your stamina, something incredibly important if you want to close the distance on that guy chucking pointing sticks in your direction.  Plus, a well-timed combat roll doesn't negate damage, it just makes you change directions. So you can both waste your energy AND get shot.Your health is also incredibly low, with melee only doing *slightly* more damage that can be matched anyway with a headshot from an arrow.You'll deal 200 base melee dmg and 150 base ranged damage. With a health supply of around 600. That means it'll take 3 melee swings or 4 ranged body shots to eliminate someone. A very small difference during any fight, assuming you aren't even wounded from a previous battle or damaged from traps.Even with craftables, the only things that are going to help in a fight is primarily CC (stuns and slows), nothing very interesting and you get to land a free hit each time. Though deploying these have a cast time, but the timer is short enough for anyone to run around a corner and slap down a massive tripwire that'll make you fall flat on your face for a short period. During my gameplay, I have yet to see any traps that are actually visible, so it just leaves you to guesswork to hope you hit something that could've gotten you killed. Again, being able to spot these isnt even beneficial, it's just "ok you don't die this time I guess."The game is fun... Most of the players I've met have good sportsmanship... And I believe that there's potential for the combat. But having the whole thing down to pure luck with axes and basic aim with bows is just incredibly unfun.

_childDocuments_.review: First off I want to iterate that Darwin Project is an Amazing game, well done for an early access project and should be kept in mind if you are looking to purchase. While the Darwin Project still has and needs lots of growth, it is truly a great start into the Battle Royal arena. You need to understand that while the Darwin Project has similarities to Fornite, PUBG and H1Z1 that does not mean it is aimed at being like those Games. This game shares the Battle Royal fun that has hit the gaming seen over the last few years, however it has it own Twist and Turns to figure! The game takes place in the Ice Lands as I call them and the the player count at the moment is way lower. But the concept to be the last man standing and using your surrounding to do so is the same. The maps play out in similar fashion with a collapsing areas and time count downs.  At the moment, I have seen but one map and customization is minimal. However the cost is cheap and the game play is fast. So that is a bonus, but I find its major flaw being that there is no controller support at the moment. On the other hand you gain loads of control through hot keys and a easy to use crafting wheel.   All in all this game is still in development like most others, however I would say do not give it a COLD should, infact try it I am sure it will warn your game loving heart!

_childDocuments_.review: I have leveled up to level 13 by now I think and so far it's very good. There's a lot of people with microphones and I recommend not to play it if you don't have a microphone because most of the fun from this game is through interacting with the other people while fighting them or talking to the game director.  The game is very different from other battle royales right now, and i'll explain now.When you join a lobby before a match begins you can hold "Q" to see your equipment, which you can change with ease. You can change the type of arrows you use, the type of cloak you use, the type of boots you use and choose three abilities from about 9 different ones. When you start in a match you already have your weapons, an axe and a bow. You can farm material by cutting trees for woodand cutting worn down chairs for leather. You can craft arrows, cloaks, boots, and upgrade your axe with those materials. Game directors (which i'll talk about more later) can place down electronics, that you can gather so you can use an ability. As a game director, instead of playing within the match as a survivor you can instead, place down electronis, talk to the survivors, close xones, and much more. I mainly play as director and do quizzes with people so if they get it right i lt them choose what they want me to do.I highly recommend this game for battle royale players and for people who just like conversations with others.

_childDocuments_.review: This review is in this game's early stages still. Darwin Project kinda did like Fornite BR did in regard to PUBG...it offered such a cool take on BR games that was a breath of fresh air to PUBG.So we have crafting, which is great because you can customize what you'd prefer for your matches, but you can always change that up inbetween matches.You're in the cold, so your warmth meter adds a survival element to the game, which is interesting. Don't worry, you can craft stuff to slow your warmth meter from decreasing at a rapid rate or just build a fire to regenerate it!There are only 10 inmates per match so the games almost never go over 15 minutes, at least in my personal experience. The map is still a decent enough size that you can always find materials and chests lying about!Did you ever get annoyed with weapon variety in other BR games due to the overwhelming assortment of armaments to choose from? In Darwin Project, you needn't worry any longer! You have 1 melee and 1 ranged weapon. You can craft a type of arrow that suits your play style, as well as an axe upgrade that could maybe give you a damage boost or even heal yourself when you loot other players!Now, that does sound amazing, doesn't it? Let's add in a Show Director that can change the course of the game by closing zones off, lowering gravity so you can jump super high, or even give you the ability to loot a crafting material that isn't easy to come by...an Electronic! The Show Director probably has a microphone and will likely swing by to say hi to you. Now more often than not, the Show Director is a pretty chill guy/gal that probably won't take sides and won't pick on you for just no reason. However, people can be jerkoffs sometimes, so they might be helping their friend or maybe a streamer. It can happen but that's why after you WIN (or die), you can rate them based on performance! That's the best way to make it so their rating gets low enough that they lose abilities in their future matches. This game is EASILY worth $15! I only play as Show Director (could you tell?) and I'm going to pay $15 for it. If the developers keep working on this game and improving my favorite role, the Show Director, to be a balanced and ever-evolving role then I'll be around for a long time to come!

Go get it and bring a friend or even a whole crowd of twitch viewers for maximum fun.Edit:Now that it got out of Early Access, I must say that it is even more fun. The slow early game, annoying ressource gathering and ressource management have been reduced to a minimum while also introducing three classes that each have their own unique and fun to use trait.Hopefully now that the devs are actually advertising this game, it maybe could take off, but considering that the BR-hype has kinda worn off, it probably won't happen, even though this game really is one of the most unique games of it's genre.Only issue I have with it now is that it no longer has the duo mode, which will hopefully be brought back with the next patch.Also, the game is still free, so just give it a try if you haven't already, it really is fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Darwin Project is a unique game and take on the current battle royale genre. However, there are glaring issues that cause me to not recommend this, at least until the game is further down the road.Optimization is solid, and controls are smooth. Where is falls frusteratingly short is some gameplay decisions made by the devs. Spending a lot of time crafting up armor, cloaks, boots, and sharpening. Getting electronics for strong equipments. All of it is negated by the large amount of fall hazards in the map, accompanied by the arrow and axe knockback distance that is almost impossible to take into consideration when positioning.I cannot say how irritating it is to be one of the last two alive, and the other guy is hiding in a corner near lava who will have a clear shot on knocking you into the lava is. The idea, the core concept of the game, is unique and fun. But the director role is bothersome. Out of the 5 games I played, 3 of them I never saw the director, or the director was placing buffs on one solo person. Making it so directors cannot use powers if their stars are below 2.3 is a smart move, but I don't think it's enough.I'm not even touching how annoying it is to have a director screaming play by plays in your ear. But that's a personal gripe.Personally, I hope this game evolves and works on some of the glaring issues. Maybe players like the knockback. Maybe people like the director yelling play by plays. If that's the case, maybe the game just isn't for me.
