_childDocuments_.review: While technically fitting into the battle royale genre, this game is unlike anything else out right now. I don't normally do reviews on games I've played so little of, but those few rounds I played already were really compelling. The "story" behind the game is a bit convoluted, but it still works, and the basic mechanics are quite simple, but still require both strategy and skill. So how does it differ from other BR games? 1) instead of 50-100 players there are 10, either 10 solo or 5 teams of 22) you aren't air dropped and have no choice over where you spawn3) instead of starting with nothing, you get an axe and a bow, and the only "drops" are small trees, chairs, and electronic boxes that can be harvested for crafting materials.4) you get to customize your crafting menu a bit before entering the game to differentiate a bit from the other players. For instance, you can choose basic arrows and start each game with 5 in your inventory, or choose flaming arrows at the expense of having to craft them all from scratch. Craft boots that make you run faster when you're tracking an enemy or being tracked by one. Switch out the bear trap for a hang glider, etc. I've only played solo so far, but I could see this being especially strong in teams. 5) instead of a procedurally generated circle shrinking every few minutes, there is an 11th player who takes on the roll of director/game master. This person can take pity on you or make your life hell. They can give players invincibility shields, lower gravity, nuke entire zones, etc. My first game I just kind of jumped in without knowing half of what I told you above, including the whole director bit. Out of nowhere a giant robotic eye came floating down to me and spoke to me in a god-like voice (The director was using lots of reverb and pitch shifting on his voice lol) saying "The Woodsman, eh? Interesting name... do you like to chop wood?" I hadn't bothered to look up the push to talk key before jumping in, so I just ran to the nearest tree and started chopping. "No answer... hmmph... typical... I'll take pity on you anyway. Head towards the electronics I just spawned on the map and grab it before the others get there, they're already on their way." he says.I had little to no idea what he was talking about, but I saw the icon on the map and ran as quick as I could. Somebody was already there, so I drew my arrow and missed. I shot a few more times but only hit once and next I know I'm out of arrows. I charge in with my axe and before I reach the enemy he deals the killing blow with his arrow. My next game I actually had my mic working, and a better idea of what I was doing. I even customized my loadout a bit. I started gathering everything I could find until I ran across the first item that had already been harvested and searched it, making the enemy who had gathered it pop up on my screen and I began the chase. I wasn't gonna let anybody get the jump on me this time. Well I got a few shots in before he knew what was even going on. The director mistook me for a good gamer or something and decided to help out the other guy. He gave him an invincibility shield, but he just kept running and shouting over the mic "OMG I'M GONNA DIE I'M GONNA DIE" and as soon as the shield disappeared, he did. Mr Director wasn't happy about that, apparently, because I happened to be right near where 3 different zones meet, center, southern, and eastern. The south was already off limits, and he sets off a nuke in the east where I am, so I run west for the center and he marks that off limits, too, so I turn north and run as fast as I can. With about 30 seconds left to get out of there I giant white light emerges from the east. I knew it was about to get nuked but that was F'ing beautiful. I forgot to mention I was freezing for the entire duration of the run. I was trying to build a campfire when he did all this. I finally make it to safety and set up my fire, with only a few seconds left before I would have froze. As soon as I'm nice and toasty, I'm flanked by another player who noticed my fire. TL;DRdespite fitting into a genre that is the current flavor of the week and rife with cheap, sad knockoffs, this game is utterly original. Easy to learn, difficult to master. Runs smooth and gorgeous for an EA title that just barely came out. F2P and no microtransactions at all at this point, with only cosmetic stuff in the future. definitely worth giving a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: Darwin's Project shows us that you can make a game inspired by someone's else idea, without completely copying it. Yes, it is a battle royale game, but it does so many things differently.Plot of the game is that you are one of the ten prisoners who can win their freedom by winning a battle royale which is watched by huge audience. It goes so far beyond to emulate the real audience feel by having unique twitch integrations and giving people ability to be "show directors", which have complete freedom of watching (show directors control small camera drones). Show directors can also pick which zones will be closed, drop items for players, make player "hunted" so all other players see him and even more stuff! Their job is to make the game as exciting as possible. And greatest thing about it is that anyone can be a director! Its selected as a game mode.Now onto the player's part, game is set in a unique snowy map for a specific reason. Since there are only 10 players in each match, so the game is focused on tracking other people down, and if you pay enough attention, you can even notice the footsteps as a good trail. Each time you gather materials or craft something, red glowing items will appear on your spot, which other players can inspect, and if they do, they will see your location and other stats through wall for few seconds. But even if you arent a good tracker, there are houses around the map which have screen that shows location of all the other players on map.When it comes to fighting, Darwin's Project has a bit of a learning curve. There are only two weapons - axe and bow, which alter the gameplay a lot compared to classic battle royale games with guns. Axe can be upgraded with materials and bow uses limited amount of arrows which you can craft and pick up after you fire them. Since materials are quite scarce you'll usually have 3-4 arrows or less, so if you miss with those, you can either run to gather them first, or resort to axe fighting. Aiming with bow is not that easy and requires good practice to get a hang of especially since player movement is very fast and there is a lot of jumping around in fights. Both axe and bow deal 150 damage (although axe can be upgraded, and bow deal +50 on headshot), which compared the player's hp - 600, leave space for interesting fights where you dont have to worry about getting one shotted from behind.The materials are used for improving your gear (boots, axe, cloak) and crafting gadgets (smoke grenades, traps, etc), arrows and armor (protects you from one hit). There are only two different materials - wood and leather, wood is usually gathered from trees and leather from sofa chairs hanging around the map. Besides them, there is a resource called "electric" which show directors spawn on certain locations shown on minimap. Electrics are used for unlocking special, very powerful abilities. There are multiple different gadgets, upgrade buffs and electric skills, however you can only pick certain number of them to use in match, and they are selected before it starts, in the menu. One more thing to mention is that there is a small survival aspect "cold", which forces you to build fire to warm up and leaves additional trails in process.Not much more to say about it, the Darwin's Project does its own thing, and it does it decently. Pros:- Different from other battle royale games- Play as a player or the show director- Skill based- Duos (5 teams of 2 players)- Crafting and tracking aspects- Character customization- Decent selection of gadgets and different upgrade buffs- Twitch integrations- LeaderboardsNeutral:- Matches can be sometimes too much show director dependant, if someone doesnt like you, you will have harder time playingCons:- Needs more content and game modes, feels too shallow for now- Somewhat high learning curve, noob traps- Female character looks weird - Gets boring quick- A lot of gadgets feel gimmicky and arent used that much- No guns

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know whether or not to recommend it.  It is free, so, worth the price for sure.  It isn't finished, but it is early access, so no surprise, and it may end up being a great game a year from now.  It just isn't yet.The game's main hook, what makes it something other than an already decent mash-up of Fortnite and Hurtworld is the Director: a Game Master who spectates, can talk to all the players, and can hand out bonuses or change game rules while the match is in progress.  Also, people who are watching the match be streamed can vote on many of the same things, meaning popularity can tip the game.  It feels sort of Hunger Games inspired to me.  I think it's a cool feature for sure, but there seems to be some indecision about what the Director's or audience's role should be, how much power they should have, etc.  It has been kind of a mess so far in my experience.  The Directors keep losing power, but the game is really only something special with a good Director.  Not that they are all good.  That is the good reason *why* they keep being controversial and getting power taken away.Which bring me to the next point.  The game is more social than most.  When it is working as designed and not being derailed, the players often doing a lot of talking to each other and the Director as the match goes on.  So the game lives or dies by its community.  Its ftp online shooter community.  Which can be problematic.  Consider yourself warned.It gets old pretty fast and feels a light on content and unfinished, but it is early access.  There is only one map and it has bugs in it.  It only has two weapons, axe and bow, and all players always have both.  You can craft snowballs or a turret, but they very situational, and not part of your standard kit.  The controls and physics for the axe and bow are intenionally cartoony, which I am not a big fan of, but more than that feel really janky.  Timing your axe swings is a required skill, but the axe is an unresponsive beast at best.  Arrows have a fairly slow flight speed, and do drop over distance, but they drop only slightly, and not in anything so logical as a graceful arc.  For TF2 fans out there, they move more like soldier's rocket than sniper's arrows.  Right down to smoke trail, which I assume they added in just to make it easier to tell where you are being shot from.  When hurt, a character doesn't bleed, but does go flying, smash bros style.  A big hit can knock you right across the map.  Or out of the map.  And not in a 'ring-out lose' way, but a 'I'm not sure that was supposed to happen' way.  It seems like they wanted this to look like a cartoon, or a trippy violent grown-up cartoon, but they could have committed a lot more to the aesthetic if that was the idea.  I wonder how many of these decisions are made for game play vs aesthetic reasons vs trying to keep a teen rating in a game about axe murder.Anyway.  The game isn't bad, but it isn't finished.  It will probably be great after a couple more major updates, assuming it gets polished up without accumulating too much toxic community or bad design decisions.  But isn't isn't there yet.  I would suggest checking back on this one in a few months to see where it is.

_childDocuments_.review: A unique Battle Royal game that is more Hunger Games than PUBG. A 10 player free for all where the only weapons at your disposal is an Axe and Bow & Arrow. As like most BR games, you start with nothing, and have to loot to gain power to get an advantage over you opponents. While in other BR games, you usually loot weapons, in the Darwin Project, you need to harvest supplies to craft your ammo, armor, gear, gadgets, and traps. There is also a lite survival mechanic where you have to keep warm by crafting warming cloths, and building fires. All of these items are made with two crafting materials (wood and leather), so it becomes a balancing act of what to craft first and when.The combat is very high flying and arcady. This game is not a realistic shooter. Every hit a person takes, with an arrow or axe hit, knocks the player back and sends them flying. This seems to "reset" the combat almost every hit and makes it more about timing than spamming.The arena is split into 7 zones that will close off over time, similiar to other BR games.  Staying in the zone will drain your warmth making you freeze to death.  So instead of a cricle that gradually gets smaller, different areas of the map become locked out randomly.And lastely, another feature that sets the game apart from others is the role of the "Director". It's essentially an Observer mode were the Observer/Caster can affect the flow of the match. They gain engery over time that is used for "powers" of various types. They can manually close of zones themselves, launch nukes that can temporarly close out a zone, heal or warm up players, etc. The purpose of the Director is to try and make the match more fun and interesting, and keep it competative, but sometimes, they can just make the game a bad time for a few. At the end of the match, you can Rate the Directors performance if you feel they did a great job, or were just trolling. Directors that have bad ratings lose access to powers they can use during a match to discourage bad behavior.I'm personally having a great time with this game, and was lucky enough to get it for free by downloading the Open Beta. The Early Access price is only $15 currently, and I would have defintely paid that price if I didn't get it for free. It's a fresh take on the BR genre and it's great to finally see some games coming out that are really changing up the formula.

Games are quick to get into as an inmate, but I was told there is a longer que for the Director. It's connected to Twitch and Myxer so if u stream your stream can place votes to who they think will win(if you're the Director), or vote for you(if you're the inmate) so they feel more involved.There is a significant skill gap but as the youngins may say you just have to, "gitgud" (play it more). There are no cosmetics atm but I believe that is a good thing as the people playing are just playing to enjoy the game. I have NOT felt as if when I got killed it was due to the other player hacking or cheating in any way nor have I had a truly unfair Director in my game. If you see someone complaining about a Director and they are still playing, chances are they are trolling for some unknown reason. You can rate the director and if/when their rating goes low enough they cannot directly affect a player which is a perk gained through progression.There are craftable and pickup items to make your character faster and armored, but there is no weapon that is weaker than the next (only bow and arrow with dif types of arrows, axe, snowballs, and traps); in saying that, even if another person is armored or a speed boosted, if your aim is better, all that doesn't matter. No lucky shots,  No "where did he shoot me from" if u get killed chances are you got out played. That's coming from someone who hasn't won a SINGLE FREAKIN GAME YET, but yet and still I had fun in EVERY GAME even when I was the first to die.Everyone spawns in to crafting materials but what you do with them is your choice, make arrows or clothing to help you better survive what's to come. You can be the hunter or the hunted and if you are the latter you will know, unless they are just following your foot prints but if they can see you, you know they can see you. If you are the hunter you just may be going into a trap so you always have to be prepared.TL;DR: Game is fun, me likie game, u should try.

_childDocuments_.review: Just won my first game, I have to say, Snowballs are op. For the most part I enjoy the game a lot, the RNG aspect of finding weapons in most BR games isn't here, you start with an axe and a bow; you can change your loadout to reflect how you want to play, whether it means changing what arrow types or craftables you have. The combat is pretty fast paced, you hit someone they go flying mach 10 into another dimension so there's a chance a fight can turn either way. As I mentioned earlier snowballs are op, why? Well there's the cold mechanic which is while you're playing a match your character will start to get colder until the bar reaches zero and you take DOT's (damage over time). Snowballs apply 14 frost damage on hit, and require nothing to craft, so my tactic is at the start of each match craft 10 for a fight, and after each fight recraft the ones you used. Overall this is a very fast paced BR game, with matches lasting about 5-10 minutes, I would reccomend playing this because well... It's free, and fun.

Add to that, the zone system is a lot more interesting, the map is also not that big, which makes things a lot more stressing, faster-paced and funnier.The combat itself might seem pretty simple at first, it's mostly using an axe and a bow, but there's a lot more to it. All of the different techniques you can use during combat is what makes a good player a good player. I've played other famous BR titles before and I usually had no problem getting used to the combat, but the case here is different. I've had my ass kicked by good players numerous times, and I'm still getting used to the system here.The game is still in early access but I think in its current state it is a really good game, I can't imagine how much better it would be after some time. I have great faith in the developers and I can see this game becoming a top title in the BR genre. Surely recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is definitly not a normal Battle Royale game. Darwin Project is a great spin on a BR game with only 10 players, and once you get familiar there is a closely knit community of great, nice players. On the outside it looks as if though everyone is toxic, but most of those people don't stay over time. Once you get a bit of skill, it always feels great to win a game against a biased director. But it feels even better to win with a great un-biased director. Overall, this is a great game, but the devs need to advertise and we need more players. Atleast try this game out because it is free, and it would be great to find some good new players!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing. It is such a breath of fresh air in the oversaturated BR genre, which is flooded with broken, clunky, and/or slow gameplay. The gameplay is fast, smooth, polished, and more importantly it is fun. With 10 players per game, it is less of a paranoid cluster♥♥♥♥ with random unexpected deaths and more of an intense round of balanced gameplay. Rounds typically last 10-15 minutes. Looking forward to the full release.
_childDocuments_.name: Darwin Project

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, great Devs, (sometimes) great community. Title Screen stays on waay too long to be unskippable (really.. it's just a "Darwin Project" screen for 20 seconds, then almost a minute black screen after). Other than that, tons of fun and pretty intense. Quality wise (the one that matters), I give a 9/10, because it's a solid game that the devs put a lot of work into.Opinion wise, I'd have to give it a 7/10, because it takes a bit too long to load for me.. and I've come across too many Show Directors that favorite their friends. Nothing more annoying than being knocked off the same electronic 5 times just so his super buffed friend could take it and hear the director say, "You really wanted that, huh?" :/But yeah, still a great, high quality game. If you liked Hunger Games and ever wanted to play something nearly perfectly representing it, this is for you.Quality: 9/10Opinion: 7/10
_childDocuments_.name: Darwin Project

_childDocuments_.review: In a time where battle royale games are the "thing", Darwin Project just does it right. Its feels familiar enough to jump into, but different and difficult enough to keep you in it. Kudos, devs. Pretty interesting learning curve for the combat mechanics. The game makes you pay for small mistakes and rewards you highly for good timing. I'll be playing this for a long time and truly hoping this won't become another "gimmick-to-die" title.*cough cough* SOS *cough*
_childDocuments_.name: Darwin Project

_childDocuments_.review: I really did enjoy this game quite a bit and loved all of the unique feautures it brings into the scene. I feel that of course it needs more work, it is an early access after all and that is a given. The biggest problem people have is that the whole "director" mechanic is unbalanced and ruins the game, however, as someone who loved playing as the director, I can easily point out 2 reasons why people say the directors are biased. First off I just need to say that directors are there to improve the overall feeling of the game and atmosphere, they are there to spice things up and make what is otherwise a standard battle royale, into an interactive and fun environment. A director isnt going to favor someone who either A. Doesn't have a mic or B. Doesnt do anything interesting (e.g. hides until they can no longer hide, doesn't speak to the Director or other players). Think of a sports announcer having to talk about what a player is doing while they are sitting on the bench. There is nothing there for the announcer to make interesting. The Director isnt going to help you out in a situation unless you make yourself interesting and known to the Director. Bottom line, the Director can just be bad, or are learning, but if you want to be noticed and interacted with, dont hide, speak up when the Director talks, be bold and trust me the director wont seem so negligent of you.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game so much, playing custom games all day long with a bunch of friends. Now the new Update is released and i simply can't recognise the game anymore. Want to customize your loadout? This Option is mostly gone. Liked all the different abilities? You have now to level up to unlock them. You loved the excitement when you found a chest or some leather? Now there is only wood which can be harvested by only one hit (drive by looting). You wanted to battle your enemies so that you get an electronic? Just walk 5 Meter and you will find the new "Darwinium" to unlock your abilities. Trust me: its everywhere... Also the Duo-Online-Mode got removed so you are forced to play Solo or Custom games. At this state i simply dont want to play this game, that i loved even if i didnt play it that much, and i guess i'm gonna deinstall it right now.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR - Amazing game with alot of fun possibilities, tons of fun.Everybody not wanna read gone? okay.When I first got the game was the day it went free, and boy let me tell you I was hooked from the start. There are alot of different aspects of the game that I enjoy, and I'm gonna go through most of the things in detail here.Customizing your loadout:The fact that you can create the loadout that fits your playstyle is something I wish every game like this one has, since it gets more people to enjoy the game their way. I personally go with a loadout thats more of a "Get in their face and hit it until it dies" tactic, that has focus on defencive and movement abilities and some sustain, which works pretty well for me.The outfits:I'm a big fan of the fact that the only way to get clothing is to level up (so far atleast), since it shows that you play this game alot and have some way to show it to others. I wont jugde if they add some way to buy clothing since they went F2P and they could probably need some of the cash.The gameplay:Love it, just absolutely love it. You start off in the lobby which normally is just a mess of people shooting each other and talking to each other on the mic, then when you start you spawn some distance away from the other's which gives you time to loot and craft whatever you need. And the fighting is simple, yet addicting. The electronics ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ is also something i really like the consept of. It's pretty much a must have for late game and it's often contested by other players. However, the game director function is mixed in my opinion. Some games you get an amazing director that makes things happend all around the map and brings action to the table, while some directors just choose a favorite and does everything for their advantage, but then again that just makes it a bit more of an challenge.The verdict:It's F2P, dont take alot of space and is pretty much one of the better battle royales that has come up recently. I beg you to try it out for yourself and have as much fun as i do with it.
_childDocuments_.name: Darwin Project

_childDocuments_.review: So I played this game back when it first launched in some Early Access stuff. I haven't played in probably a year. A HUGE amount of the game has change, but the combat remains consistent. The new classes/equipment they added makes for interesting fights and more customizable playstyles. Seems to be a lot less meta building / rushing X items. Seems to be no more ratings system for the Show Director, or any leaderboards for that matter, which is part of what pushed me away in the first place. It was a feature to this game which I've really enjoyed, but angry players downvoting you just because they lost was the biggest flaw in that system.Happy to be back on here - wish you could still Duo with people, however. My only gripe is that you have to play solo.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game for people who don't really like the Battle Royale genre but might be interested in getting into PVP. I'm one of those people.The game is smooth, beautiful, has interesting gameplay when it comes to the show director, and is honestly just a blast to play. Even though I'm super bad at the game, it has really helped me learn to be aggressive in PVP and to just try and go for the kill instead of running and hiding.Each match lasts around 10 minutes & there is never a dull moment. The game is only $15. Buy it. Enjoy it. Tell your friends.BONUS: The devs are absolutely amazing, truly care about the community, and genuinely seem to love their game.

_childDocuments_.review: Actually VERY fun, theres no unbalance of any weapons since theres 2. your axe and your bow, whats different about this from others is that the weapons may not change but the way you can manipulate them does such as a fire arrow, radar arrow which allows them to be highlighted for 7-8 seconds after hit and many more, the axe as well has different skills, the matches involve 10 people instead of the average 100 in Fortnite and PUBG, this allows players to have a laidback and not have to put all your effort into the game as they usually last less then 10 min, a huge change of pace for other battle royale games and its just very unique my only issues are the amount of materials we need more than leather and wood, incorperate more such as stone metal etc. another is the matchmaking you usually get put with at least one player from last game if not all of them, another is the limited amount of different materials you can wear in game add some others like helmets which allow more damage to be taken before your armor falls off or limit amount of arrows and make a holder that allows you to craft more, there is a huge opportunity with this game and if you get mad easily you wont at this game because of how less tense the games are, if you love fortnite but hate the pacing then this game is for you. a solid 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: I have only played this game for a hour and I can happily say that this, right here, is a good product.THE GOODThe Graphics : To me, they get the job done and it's not too toony with the look of the artstyle. I do gotta say that when ELECTRONIC spawns in, it is a marvel to look at. I am running it on EPIC currently so I think that's the best way to play this. Anything under that seems to make everything look muddy and it's not all that pretty to look at.Gameplay : Gameplay is fun but I do see it being a bit repetitive since there is only the AXE and the BOW. I would suggest to add more abilites somehow in the future but keep the future abilites locked behind a SKILL TREE for the AXE and BOW. Like adding a spin attack for the AXE or perhaps shooting DOUBLE ARROWS for more knockback and a slight attack boost or casually by leveling up to unlock abilites. So currently the fighting part of the gameplay feels bare bones.Managing your resources and warmth however are pretty good though. You gotta THINK what you have to resource so people won't track you and also decide what you gotta make to help you survive. That apect of the gameplay is very fun for me.The BadOnly bad things I think is the combat (Feels bare bones) and the KNOCKBACK. To me, the knockback makes it feel that the MELEE combat of the game is a bit useless since your enemies just go flying. Especially having that force ball ability around you. Using the BOW is king in this game so you have to get better aim with that.(This isn't really a bad but I would suggest to add a higher player count MODE someday to make the gameplay a bit more fast paced. Most of the games I were in I only get a kill or two and so it's mostly just walking around and crafting stuff)(Other comments)So yeah. Overall is it alright for me but totally needs to get worked on with the combat and possibly add that SKILL TREE for more abilities I mentioned to spice up the gameplay. I can also gladly say I enjoy this more than Fornite! Because crafting is more thoughful in this game and you don't see spamming crap all over the place. I hope more and better production will come to this so more players will hop on in.Good luck making the game and for the people that is reading this, give it a try! It's free afterall and it doesn't take that long to download.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: Updating review to reflect my recommendation. Pretty much nothing has changed from alpha/beta to early access and most of what I say remains the same, but due to the EA price, I don't recommend the game. I did update that I received the product for free moving from alpha/beta to EA for whatever reason, though can't say that it changed my mind as I don't give points for developer kindness, sorry.I actually don't like the base game at all, but I like the director thing. The base game is really kinda bland and too simple for my taste. There's one type of combat and it's the bow, though you do have an axe. If you can't aim, then don't bother playing. There is no axe playstyle, it's just that thing you use to deflect incoming axe attacks made by other players. Let me say that once again. THERE IS NO AXE COMBAT PLAYSTYLE. If you use the axe vs anyone with skill, you will eventually lose because every attack you make will be deflected and then they will use the space to shoot you. I don't give a ♥♥♥♥ about 'the bow requires skill'. Going by that logic they could also make 'deflecting arrows requires skill'. Instead it's literally just swing your axe and hope the poor sod is bad at timing shots and you'll make breathing room or run around like an idiot and hope he misses. A good bow player will win EVERY TIME. The axe is LITERALLY just there to deflect other axe attacks and that makes the game inflexible and BORING. If you're gonna do melee, you need to have the possiblity of a melee playstyle. You can't just let them counter each other out and make space. YOU CAN'T DO THAT. Why even HAVE melee? You could also make deflecting arrows a possible thing since arrows are pretty limited. BOTH OF THESE ARE NOT A REAL OPTION. Because you CAN'T predict when someone will loose their arrow and you CAN'T hit a guy with an axe if he knows you're coming because he will just deflect it. In other words the only playstyle is the bow. Hope you like bow and arrow :3.Also the tracking system in this game is trash. It doesn't matter how long ago someone looted something, you always get a 100% view of the player for x amount of time. The lack of depth destroys the trackinig system making it literally just a glorified wallhack. The worst part is that you can use smoke bomb, but hey they just track you using another thing you looted. It's a horrible system with zero depth.I also feel middled by the number of players as there are so few (10). Then again, when I do director mode I struggle to give attention (and annoyance) to everyone equally. I like being able to chat with random people as that's not something I would ever do in a pvp situation. I just don't like conversing with my opponents. But when I get to sit over their shoulder like the annoying brother, that feels fun for me. Though I do still have to get down the part where you don't talk to someone when they're near someone else and ruin the game for them. I do understand that people don't like you chatting at the last part of the game where they're fighitng for the win.I think my biggest complaint is that the director system is totally lame with the 'review' system. Whenever a player dies, they get the option to rate the director (I think it has some limitations?) and it's a 1/5 star system. The biggest thing I realized is that people don't like silent directors. No matter how hard I tried to just make the game fun, no one liked it. Not just that but directors lack the TOOLS to make the game fun directly. But when I started being a nuisance, my rating started to go up. Flashing my lights, telling people to jump in lava there's a secret in there, asking people if they'd like me to close their zone and when they say no I close it anyway. Seems like my rating managed to climb up.And when I say climb, what I mean is that is hung around 3.10. This wouldn't be a problem except that you get some powers taken away if you drop below 2.3 which definitely could happen to someone as mediocre as me who is trying his best to entertain. Realistically that's what you do as the director. And you really have limited interactivity. So if you wanna be a non talking director, there's no options. And because it's so social heavy that means I'd only play this game when feeling social because I don't care for the base game. If I could do more to entertain that didn't require me to put invincibility on one guy, heal the other while shouting 'oh no I ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up! hold on I can fix this!' and then nuking the sector and waste all 10 points, things would be better. I also noticed no one likes some abilities. If I heal someone, people ♥♥♥♥♥ and say 'Oh you're playing favoritism on that guy'. If I throw invulnerability during a fight? People ♥♥♥♥♥. Anti-grav? No one ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ likes it. NO ONE. I asked everyone and the only guy who wanted it didn't know what it did and immediately afterward he said 'wow this is lame'. The worst part is that there are SO MANY BAD DIRECTORS. I didn't realize it the first time I played the game, but now when I had to play 5 matches again and then a few more after that, I realized that there are a ton of bad directors. Not only do they play favoritism for the 'twitch' streamer, but sometimes they'll literally call you out. 'He's undergeared, go fight him over there' or, or, OR you could shut the ♥♥♥♥ up and let me use the 12 wood and 7 leather to put on armor, make a couple traps and upgrade my ♥♥♥♥ you ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. And don't even try to apologize by healing me, the other guy is better with the bow and I'm ♥♥♥♥. Just let me die you ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.Back to the director. The problem is that the abilities being used for what they're supposed to be used for no one likes. If I use them jokingly or throw them away at the start of the game cause some guy said 'just use invincibility on someone as soon as possible' BAM, more points. The system encourages you to be an entertainer cause if you drop below a certain rating, you lose your abilities and then YOU don't have fun. But you can't DO what you're supposed to with the abilities so no matter what you either play as an entertaining director by flying overhead while making car sounds, pulling people over making police sounds and wasting your abilities on NOTHING, or you use your abilities as you see fit and you lose them cause you're trying to actually use the abilities.I mean I'm not complaining that it's that way, but if it's gonna be that way the abilities shouldn't be so geared towards actually helping. Give me the ability to just start vomiting watermelons or spawn random balloons and other cooky ♥♥♥♥. This isn't even mentioning how some of the abilities are actually useless. The nuke can be dodged by walking out of the zone, into even a zone that's closed, and then just walking back in. It's one of the worst abilities and I'd gladly give it up to bombard a zone with exploding rubber duckies.As the director you are an ENTERTAINER. That's your job whether you like it or not. Also there isn't really much incentive to play director beyond the raw enjoyment. You don't gain any levels or unlocks and that's a real downer for me. Let me unlock rubber ducky abilities dammit.Monetization turned out to be a flat 15 bucks which means I can't recommend. The game just isn't worth that amount and I'm prettttty sure it'll go F2P after exiting EA.Oh and one last thing, I'd much rather kill the players than help them and I think they'd enjoy that more. I REALLY think they'd like it more. Not. Even. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Kidding.

_childDocuments_.review: I managed to put a couple of hours into this last beta and I have to say I had some serious fun. I didn't run into any glitches or bugs while playing. Darwin Project brings some really fresh, unique features to the BR genre. My favourite part of the game was playing as the 'Director' where you can effect nearly every aspect of the game from above, closing zones, healing/warming players and even dropping nukes to keep each match completetly different to the last. My only issue with this game as it stands is that each match only allows 10 players + 1 Director, I felt that the map was big enough to allow more players. As a competitive person I did find myself getting frustrated in not being able to hunt and kill enemies before others got to them. I will definately be picking up a copy of this game when it lauches and recommending it to my friends.

_childDocuments_.review: I have to admit that when i first played this game in beta, I was underwhelmed and slightly confused at what was going on.  I had recently come off a period of playing PUBG and had created a standard in my mind for what BR games should be like.  But make no mistake, this game is much more than your standard Battle Royale.  The game is refreshing and quick paced.  You won't spend 30 mins running around finding loot (and being disappointed) like PUBG.  You find what you need and its up to you to choose what you want to craft based on your playstyle.Pros:-Quick paced, easy to learn.-Smooth graphics and gameplay.-Fresh take on Battle Royale.-Directors can be pretty cool.-Optimized for streaming on Mixer.Cons:-Somewhat small game world (could be a Pro to be honest).-Current lack of of variety of weapons (early access)-Sometimes unfair depending on the actions of the Director.Overall this game is very very fun which really should be our main factor when considering games, right?

_childDocuments_.review: This game, is the perfect battle royale.Scavenger Studios first game and they hit the formula right on the head. In this review I'll tell you a bit about the pros and cons. Furthurmore I'll tell you how the pro's outweigh the cons.PROS:-10 PlayersThe whole 100 players in other battle royale proves to be unsatisfying, and makes it demoralizing when you get to top 2 just to die.-No RNG (For the most part)Ever played a game of PUB just to rush into a house, not find a gun, die immediatly, and have about 5 minutes of time wasted out of waiting for that game and getting into it just to die. Well in Darwin there is no rng besides where the zones close. The closing of the zones for better players in easy to ignore aswell.-Fun CombatWhile this is gonna partly be in the cons aswell, but for the most part the combat is really fun. The Axe combat is my favorite personally, but the bow combat people love aswell, The speed and force of the combat makes you feel strong and it is super satisfying to hit someone with an arrow or axe hit. The sound and graphical elements makes the combat feel awesome aswell as preform great.-Custom PlaystylesWanna scavenge and get super OP before fighting anyone, theres a build for that. Wanna be a ninja and sneak around players to get the advantage on them, theres a build for that. Wanna be a speedy boy with an axe that does half their health bar, thers a build for that. No matter how you wanna play, Darwin has fully customizable builds for you to suit your playstyle so you never feel awkward with the game forcing you to play a certain way.-Show DirectorWhile on paper the Director sounds like a terrible idea, in practice it helps the game a lot. Where a game can get stagnant ther is an omnipotent being that can spice up the game and make it more interesting and fast. The Director has a rating which can be used to determine what abilities they can use. So no fear if you see a director teaming with one player, vote him one star and he will no longer have the ability to influence players directly in future games. This also turns the game casual in most games, making the community much less toxic because nobody really gets mad when they lose. Which takes me into my last pro before I keep naming off everything I love about this game-CommunityThis game has, hands down, the best community of a game I have ever played. Everyone is friendly to eveyone else, except for the few asshats you meet but thats to be seen in every community. No one gets overly mad when they die, most of the time when I kill or am killed I say GG and am met with a GG back. Scavenger should be proud of the community they have and work to do everything they can to keep it.Now for the ConsCONS:-OptimizationThe game is pretty poorly optimized, but it being in its early stages that is most likely gonna change. Not really much else to say here. But on lower setting there are graphical glitches ive noticed, mainly in areas where snow should deform but on lower settings it does not so you end up clipping.-Sometimes jank combat.The hitboxes with axes are thicc asf, and when arrow fighting your body hitbox is also a thicc boy with your head being the hardest to hit thing in the game.-Director ratingWhile I said the game is casual and people don't get mad, some people do. And when I play as director I can do great the whole game and be fair but the guy who dies cause I closed a zone trying to push him twords other players is of course gonna vote me as a one. This makes it so I can't use heal, nuke, etc. I can still use other stuff but the values on some of the items need to be scaled down cause it makes them damn near impossible to use them somestimes.The Darwin Project, a Diamond in the rough. Install today and never go back to Fortnite or PUB :D

_childDocuments_.review: A unique, faster-paced take on the battle royale genre. The emphasis on survival through the cold meter mechanic and tracking is interesting, forcing players to focus more on the risk-reward of scavenging to craft better gear versus the flat hunt for better weapons in Fortnite. However, bow and arrow are way too strong, and the massive knockback you get hit with when an arrow shot hits you is just annoying, not fun. When combined with the anti-gravity effect that nearly every MC is going to use once it's down to the final two players, most of your 1v1s for the win come down to whoever getting hit with an arrow first getting knocked clear out of the zone, and dying due to being in a restricted area. This trickles down into the Electronics resource, which the MC spawns on the map and is always visible on everyone's map, forcing players to fight over it. Because of the way matches end, certain power-ups are just far better; invincibility for a few seconds is the difference between winning and losing when knocked out of the zone, meaning that it, along with Radar to find other players and hunt effectively, are almost always going to take up 2 of your 3 slots for tech. Because of the floaty knockback and the strength of ranged over melee, almost every player is going to have more or less the same loadout, with 1-2 slots of the trap category taken up by snowball and tripwire, with the remaining slot filling some kind of rarely-used niche. That said, this could be fixed by reducing or removing the knockback from arrows, because it's excessive at this point. Anti-gravity should also be removed; as a mechanic, it can be fun to see from a spectator's view, but it works against the other mechanics in the game, making arrows far too strong because of their knockback, making melee useless, and ultimately turning every fight where it's turned on (read: probably every single 1v1) into a test to see who can land one arrow first. Replacing it with something else that forces players together would be much better; instead of giant jumps, let the MC permanently reveal and track all players to each other when there's less than 5 competitors left. Spawn animals that attack the remaining survivors. Spawn a blizzard that drastically reduces players' cold meters, forcing more campfires, thus, more confrontations. You want more fights to break out, not have one fight end anticlimactically - especially when that fight is the final duel for the win.Overall, though, the game has a solid base. The survival mechanics in place are great, hunting and tracking is more nuanced and leads to more viable strategy and choice than in Fortnite, the announcer / MC is, barring some of the more questionable events they can spawn, an original and plain fun design choice, and overall, each match plays out in different, interesting ways.

_childDocuments_.review: Darwin Project : By Triple F"Darwin Project", the exhilarating and innovative entry in the battle royale genre, takes survival of the fittest to electrifying new heights. Set in a post-apocalyptic Canadian Rockies arena, this game brilliantly blends the primal instincts of hunting and survival with the strategic complexity of a real-time showstopper. With its unique twist on the genre, "Darwin Project" doesn't just stand out in the crowded battle royale landscape; it ascends to a new tier of gaming excitement.Visually, "Darwin Project" delivers an awe-inspiring spectacle. The frozen wilderness setting is nothing short of breathtaking, with its dynamic weather system and intricately designed landscapes adding depth and challenge to each match. The changing environments are not just eye candy, but strategic elements that players must master to survive. From crafting tools and weapons to tracking opponents, the game artfully integrates its visuals with game-play, creating a seamless and immersive experience.But it's the innovation at the core that truly sets "Darwin Project" apart. A Show Director, an omnipotent being with god-like abilities, can manipulate the battlefield, influencing the flow of the game and shaping the fate of participants. This adds a thrilling layer of unpredictability, as well as a strategic dimension that transforms each match into a dynamic chessboard of survival. The interplay between the Show Director and the contestants is a masterstroke, turning the typical battle royale formula on its head and fostering an ever-evolving ecosystem of tactics.The combat mechanics are a symphony of skill and strategy. The focus on close-quarters melee combat, combined with ranged combat elements, demands players to adapt swiftly to rapidly changing situations. Hunting down opponents requires more than just precision; it requires a keen understanding of the environment, the ability to read tracks, and the dexterity to execute split-second decisions. The result is a pulse-pounding experience where the rush of a successful kill is only matched by the adrenaline of narrowly escaping death.Crafting is the heart of survival, and "Darwin Project" nails it. The resource management system, where players scavenge for materials and craft essential gear, enhances the immersive nature of the game. The race against time to gather resources while evading opponents maintains a constant tension that's hard to shake off, ensuring that complacency is never an option."Darwin Project's" interactive spectator experience is a genius addition. As a spectator, you're not just a passive observer; you can influence the game by voting, casting your opinion, and participating in the overarching narrative of survival. This bridges the gap between players and viewers, making each match a communal experience where everyone is vested in the outcome. The symbiotic relationship between those in the arena and those watching adds layers of entertainment that other battle royales lack.In conclusion, "Darwin Project" isn't just any game; it's a revolution in the battle royale genre. With its stunning visuals, strategic innovations, and immersive mechanics, it creates an experience that's equal parts heart-pounding competition and edge-of-your-seat entertainment. The fusion of survival instincts, resource management, and real-time manipulation creates an intricate tapestry of game-play that's as thrilling to participate in as it is to watch.

_childDocuments_.review: After a rough start with black-screening and lock ups I finally got the game to work and I feel I can give an honest asessment of the game. And I can do this rather fast. It seems like theyve crammed a bit much into this title for the type of game this is. In additon, the controls are clunky, ranged combat is mediocre while playing and while spectating. I appreciate what the devs are trying to do, and I think its a good idea branching out from the BR formula...but it feels a little like the 60 yr old guy who is 5'1" and buys a yellow corvette.*Combat*Heres my biggest gripe. It feels like its made for players with controllers but has way too many options fora controller. 1,2,3,4,5,6 + R, F, G are all weapons, traps, special abilities...things you will likely need in battle. In addition, you have Mouse 1 for melee and HOLD Mouse 2 + Mouse 1 for ranged (bow). Thats 11 options to decide between while in an encounter. Ive used less keybinds in ARMA. Im not being facetious here. ARMA has multiple stances, a hot key for a watch, compass, weapons, etc and it still uses less keys. Its known as one of the most complicated keybinds of all time. This is just took the cake*Class system*I like the class system. But theyve made it obsolete or unneeded by having 11 combat options no matter your class.*Actual Gameplay combat*This is beyond clunky. I turned my mouse down to 400 dpi and accuracy is still a challenge. Landing shots with the arrow is unpredictable. Try it in a lobby to a moving target. You'll see what I mean. If my arrow is going to connect on a moving target without leading it, make it that way. If its going to connect with leading the target, make it that way. For some reason we have what sems to be a mixed bag. Almost as if the shots are slighlty randomized...like BF1. And again, that was done to grab the controller kiddiesAxe swings have a weird and hard to time delay which is absent in the lobby. So if youre trying to time swings in a lobby, just realize it will be totally different in-game. That made sense to someone. But the overall comabt is just pure garbage. I havent seen an encounter that was memorable. its mostly just people missing each other wwith arrows and axes for too long of a time. Srsly, I spectated two players trying to kill each other and I was able to go outside, grab my mail, answer a text, and come back in front of the screen and the battle was still going on. Time to kill in a BR game needs to be shorter. The longer your 1v1 engagement takes the higher the chances of it turing into 2v1. Matter of fact, the best thing is to try and wait for two poeple to fight, observe, and then just attack them both. They'll drain each other and youre good.*Scoring system*Just stay alive and away from everyone. You'll score more points and place higher and you dont have to engage anyone. So stay near a map and away from players. Our last match the #2 high score was a person who encountered no one, did no damage...essentially just sat in one quadrant. Everyone knows that in BR style games your score is (or should be) based on your rank + the damage/kills you rack up for the round. I understand its EA, but still. This is pretty basic. It had to be made this way*How does it Run?*Fine. Its Unreal. It should run fine so long as you dont get too close to realism or overly complicate it. Case in point: Fortnite and Realm Royale both run pretty good (Fortnite better obviously, its their engine)*Is it a god idea?*I think so. It will tell us if players running lobbies can bring this into a broadcasting environment and engage and audience beyond the players themselves. I hope it works and I hope they make necessary changes*So wtf is your problem mate?*My medication hasnt been tweaked in some time and and sick of clunky combat made for controller kiddies realeased into the wild like a badger being let out of a trap. Devs lately say "Holy cow I think we got something...back up, we're going to release this!" Ever had to fight a badger while youre on mushrooms? I do this every Saturday. But it doesnt mean Im going to recommend it to others. I'll give them the same advice...just wait. One day it will morph into a beautiful butterfly. And then you can eat it.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, after investing a fair amount of time into this beauty of a game i feel like i need to defend it and shed some light into it's Pros and Cons, since most of the positive reviews of this site are very vague and coming from people with low playtime and the negatives are critisicing small issues that ain't really that bad or just plain wrong, i'm yet to see any negative review which adresses the actual core issues that this game has (that there really are).WARNING: Long ass review incoming.Part 1: "The Game, is fun, if it's not fun, then why bother?" - Reggie <3So, the game is a Battle Royale, you've heard it millions of times, you loot, explore and kill upstanding members of society in order to become the last man standing. More or less the same, right? Well, you would be kinda right, but this game has some core changes to what i will call the "Royale Formaluae". Namely these are:-Lower playercount: The game's matches are meant for 10 players, 11 if you count the Show Director (we'll get into that later).-No weapon/equipment looting per se, in replacement, the game features a simple and intuitive crafting system which requires you to scavenge resources such as wood, leather and electronic devices in order to craft all the goodies, which include (at the time of writing this review) Four diferent types of arrows (some track, some hurt a bit more, some come in with ammo at the start and some give you stamina boost), three types of axes (More damage, faster looting and crafting times and heals when looting corpses), four cloaks (to resist cold more effectively aswell as to track enemy attackers, have more stamina and lessen enemy track timers), a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ of tools (Bear traps, tripwires, gliders for easy movement, fake chests, tripcages, hooks to get close and personal) and electronic powers (Shrink, teleport, energy shield, ice bolt, power leap, arena and a turret).-Tracking System: One of the best and most unique features of this game is the tracking system. The devs felt like the most boring moment on battle royales such as PUBG and others is the time spent between the exhilarating encounters and shootouts with other players, and felt like just looting wasn't fun enough, so they decided to make it so that every action you perform (crafting, looting, shooting, even your tracks on the snow by walking) can and WILL be tracked in order to find you and probably kill you. This helps increase or decrease the rate of fights depending on the will of the players or their ability to be sneaky.-And last but not least the Show Director: This truly is the most special feature this game has to offer. Each match is issued a Show Director, a player who queues up for that role and is intended to be the director of the match, think Dungeons and Dragons Dungeon Keeper, alright? These Directors have a Power Deck filled with different abilities to use in order to spice up the match, such as closing zones, activating events (Zero gravity, a period where everyone is tracked by everyone, double loot, etc) and many more to come.Besides from all of that, the game also features a Tile-based map which randomly chooses between the available tiles to create an unpredictable and amazing map. The quality of these vary, but i dare say that the last ones are great and very different from any other BR map, really.Part 2: The community.Now, this is a social game, and if you dont mention the community then you can't really talk about it. I've been playing since the very launch of the game and the community has obviosuly had it's ups and downs, but today i am glad to say that it is one of the most welcoming, caring, and competitive communities out there. Everyone strives to be the best, but without being toxic with others or disrespectful in any way, there are some very creative directors out there that really spice up and improve the game for everyone, and the competitive scene is actually quite stable and H A R D (which i love) and since getting gud requires a good amount of time, basically everyone knows each other on the so-called "high ranks".Part 3: But is it really that good?Sadly, the game suffers from quite a bit of issues, some major and some are just some nitpicks of mine, but issues nonetheless. The Devs really try their hardest to deliver good content in schedule, but big content droughts and badly optimized/balanced patches do happen more times than i would want to. There are some core issues related with the way the axe works and its hitbox, some patches it is really inconsistent, some patches it hits really far away or some other ones make it straight up impossible to axe fight without a lot of parries and deflects that make it really hard to make any damage, making it so that people restrain from using it too much and go to the security and consistency of the bow and arrow. The low playercount takes it toll on the matchmaking system, it's not an uncommon ocurrance to see complete newbs go in a lobby against top tier players, making the experience really frustrating and hard for new players, and moreso due to the lack of a proper tutorial which explains it all to them. Some Directors have it quite easy for teaming, and if it weren't for the general strictness of the devs and players towards this attitude it could be easily exploitable, the list could really go on if you count the technical issues and glitches (although that is to expect from a Early Acess game).Part 4: ConclusionI really ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ love this game despite it's evident faults and problems, because it just ticks off some of my most wanted boxes in games, it really scratches an itch that none other game in the market does, and the amount of cool people and friends i've made thanks to this game realy makes it worth the experience, ESPECIALLY since it is free during it's EA period. If you are just remotedly interested on the game, give it a try, join the official discord community for tips, or you can also look for local communities and make some friends (if you're spanish go check out our amazing community :D), and if you think that i got something wrong, please state it on the comments so that i can make this the  U L T I M A T E review.Thank you very much! TL:DRIt's got its ups and downs, but since it is so unique and fun, and free i really dont see it NOT worth playing.

_childDocuments_.review: Darwin Project, a unique entry in the battle royale genre, sets out to revolutionize the formula with its focus on player interaction, environmental manipulation, and a captivating setting. However, while it succeeds in some aspects, it ultimately falls short of its lofty ambitions.One of Darwin Project's standout features is its emphasis on player interaction and strategy. The ability to track opponents, set traps, and engage in intense one-on-one combat adds depth to the gameplay, creating tense and exhilarating moments that set it apart from its competitors.The game's setting, a post-apocalyptic Canadian wilderness, is visually striking and brimming with potential. The inclusion of a Show Director, who oversees the match and can influence its outcome, adds an extra layer of intrigue and unpredictability, making each match feel like a unique and dynamic experience.However, Darwin Project is let down by several key issues that prevent it from reaching its full potential. One of the most glaring issues is its lack of player base, which leads to lengthy matchmaking times and empty lobbies. This not only hampers the overall experience but also makes it difficult to fully appreciate the game's innovative mechanics.Furthermore, Darwin Project suffers from balance issues and a steep learning curve, which can be off-putting to newcomers. The disparity in skill levels between players can make matches feel unfair and frustrating, detracting from the game's potential for strategic depth and meaningful player interaction.Additionally, while the inclusion of a Show Director is a novel concept, it often feels underutilized and poorly implemented. The role lacks meaningful impact on the outcome of matches and can sometimes result in arbitrary interference that disrupts the flow of gameplay.Despite its shortcomings, Darwin Project remains a promising concept with a solid foundation. With continued support and refinement, it has the potential to carve out a niche for itself in the competitive gaming landscape. However, until these issues are addressed, it's difficult to wholeheartedly recommend Darwin Project to all but the most dedicated of players.

_childDocuments_.review: Darwin Project developed by Scavengers Studio is part of the long list of battle royals that have been appearing over the past couple years. Releasing in 2018 the game has gone through many changes such as becoming free to play after their first year, becoming available to Xbox and Playstation, and game changes such as introducing a class system to your character. Darwin project is set in the cold North of Canada where 10 players are dropped into an arena with an axe and bow with one goal, be the last one standing. Apart from gathering resources and battling the cold, Darwin turns this into entertainment by adding the Director who commentates and communicates with the players to make each battle unique.Full Review Here:

_childDocuments_.review: I've tried Fortnite, I've tried PUBG, and I like a lot of things about them, but my brain falls asleep and I never felt the "addictiveness" people talk about. Just feels like "same sh** with different people" and it's boring to me. Well, Darwin Project is the first Battle Royale-inspired game that I actually "get". I see why people like this stuff now.I thought only having 10 players instead of 100 would make it feel stupid and unfair and make matches end too fast, but each player feels like a League of Legends champion. They're powerful, resilient, and have unique ability choices that give each person their own unique signature. Players last beyond the first gunfight, the second, the third, the tenth. Players feel more like heroes instead of defenseless naked children, and that helps it be amazing instead of garbage.Oh and also, the game actually does a lot to remind you that this is a show people are watching! That helps a lot too, including the real-life Twitch and Mixer integration.[]It's a Battle Royale game that doesn't feel cheap and half-baked. It's a "FPS/TPS with one person commanding from above" game that's truly fun.A couple ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ for the developers though, which didn't impact my fun in the end but I think you should address anyway:♥♥♥♥♥♥ 1: I strongly, strongly feel that $14.99 is too high. I think $9.99 would be a better impulse buy, which is what you want. People who say "Oh well, eff it, I'm bored so let's try this" are going to be your long-term target audience. Make it cheaper (fill it with evil cosmetic loot boxes to make up for the lost profit even, I don't care) and I'd be happier about the chances of your game still being packed with people a year from now. I dunno about most people, but for me, $14.99 is teetering on the line where I ask "Hmm, wait, do I really think I'll *love* this?" and $9.99 is more impulse buy territory.♥♥♥♥♥♥ 2: I don't know if it's a bug or a feature, but whenever I listen to voice chat in-game, it sounds scratchy and high-pitched and just plain broken. I don't know if it's my computer or this game, but there's a lot of clipping (the kind of clipping where audio reaches max volume and sounds like your speakers are crackling), please fix it. I play Overwatch, I play Battlefield, I play awful 3D group chat programs - and none of the voice chats sound like they took a trip through the 1950s before reaching my ears.♥♥♥♥♥♥ 3 (this is a big one I think): I tried the Xbox trial just to see how things are over there, and on the Xbox One X at 4K, the framerate is *deplorable*. It's just freaking downright pathetic and unplayable. Please put in some dynamic resolution thing, force 1080p, I don't care, 10fps is not enough to have a chance at winning.Anyway that's all! This game really caught my attention and stood out to me as more than just a cash-in on the BR craze. It's thought-out, lovely, and all-around fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Darwin Project is very good the biggest issue it has is the playerbase size. This game died when it came out of beta almost immediately which is awful. I 100% recommend this game if the playerbase stays in a good condition. i've had some of the best moments i've ever had in gaming because of this game. the combat is very simple but it's very enjoyable and makes for some very intense moments. The new gadgets? not sure what to call them are all very fun to use. I feel like the bird is better then the other two it just lets you loot materials way faster and basically lets you infinitely track an enemy with some speed and damage buffs while tracking them. The jetpack and grapple hook feel very similar to me. The jetpack can make for some really sweaty and intense melee fights if used correctly. The grapple hook can as well but to a lesser extent from what i've experienced if you grapple someone you can lead into a melee very easily and on a bad player it can just kill them but against a good player or even an ok player it feels very useless? The attack is very easily countered I literally just panic left click and counter it 90% of the time so it seems to require a bit more to use well. The director is a very unique and honestly amazing addition. At first I thought his power could be abused but really they balanced it well so the most he could do is give one person a few more resources then the others not really game changing to me. I have the most fun when i'm trying to equally kill everyone :) close a zone then nuke the only option they have left to go into. It rarely kills anyone but it's very fun and the community seems to enjoy it to be honest. Speaking of the community it is absolutely amazing. like I said this game died instantly after beta but a few people still played and still play to this day and man not only are they amazing at the game they're just really cool people. the game is very easy to learn but so enjoyable. I would give it a shot before it dies although I will be crossing my fingers and hoping that it continues with a solid playerbase.

They also took away most of the powers that would get you a higher score such as the ability to heal players or use the Manhunt ability to spice things up (you now need over 4 stars just for gravity storm, an awful ability anyway), now you're going to have to rely on your sparkling personality and giving a couple of players 3 pieces of extra wood...This game has a lot of potential if they can find the balance between stopping bad show directors from ruining games and allowing said directors from having fun themselves and therefore making it fun for the combatants. Right now, that balance has been lost.Playing as a combatant/contestant is still super fun but the game suffers from the "one map problem" most other battle royale games have also suffered from and is in desperate need of a different themed map, maybe a desert map where you need to find water instead of build fires. I'd also love to have a 15 or 20 player map of the same size, so that the game would be even faster paced.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, I would like to clarify something. If you are a very competitive person, or a very casual person, you may love this game. I myself got addicted to this game back in early 2018. I then committed myself to playing the game as it was the only fun game in my library. I got better and better over time, eventually becoming an above average player. I started participating in tournaments and scrims (basically practice tournaments). However, once I got to a certain level of skill, it felt like I was no longer getting any better. So I did what most people would do. Either really try to get better, or look for a new game. Quick side note: If you get competitive in this game and you're generally competitive anyways, you might find yourself getting pretty mad at times. Whether it be that an arrow shot "shouldn't" have hit you, or that axe that you just got hit by was "bs". And sure, these things do happen, but just remember that every game has bugs. Anyways, with that out of the way, I really want to go OVER the game itself. I like the idea of classes in darwin project, however with any huge update like changing the entire combat system, bugs / glitches are bound to happen. I'm not gonna sit here and say that they should revert, but I think they should put a LOT of time into discussing the future of classes if they want to keep the ball rolling with this game. Personally, my favorite part of this game is that you can talk / meet with existing friends, or make new ones. I have probably made 30 or so people on my friends list just from people on Darwin that I just met in game or something like that. But of course the main focus of the game is combat, etc. I like the combat system a lot. (besides all of the dash attacks, etc). The gameplay with just the axe and the bow is so incredibly simple, that it's just so refreshing to see. I haven't seen ONE other battle royale that has used an axe as the main way of combat (besides the bow). Now, the only problem I see with this system however is the fact that since professional players have been using these weapons for over 2 years, they have practically mastered the bow and axe. So when new players come along, sure they'll know "how" to use them, but they won't know things like bow jukes, and how to properly dodge arrows. The main reason this game isn't as popular as it is if you ask me is because when new players come along, they get obliterated by all of the OG / good players, then they stop playing because their rate of improvement is so incredibly slow. As for some suggestions, I recommend adding crossplay. I'm sure you've heard it from a ton of people, but it really would help this game out. For one, the servers on PC as you may know are running pretty low right now. 10 PLAYER LOBBIES are BARELY being filled up. However, with the addition of crossplay, this would no longer be an issue due to their being more players on Xbox. Next up, fix your servers. And once again I'm sure you've been hearing this as well Scavengers Studios. But honestly, FIX  THE  SERVERS. I don't mean to be rude, seriously. But I really do think that people are leaving this game for that reason. Consistent game crashes. Lobby crashes, launch issues, the list goes on. I'm not saying you need to fix everything I say now, but in the future I think this is what the game needs to survive and flourish. As for 2 little personal things that I would like to see added into the game, I think instead of just being able to turn DOWN the Field of view, I think you should be able to turn it UP as well. 2nd thing, and I believe I sent this as a suggestion as well, but make the default crosshair when you boot up the game for the first time the original crosshair from before you could change it. Now I'm not saying to make it to where you can't change it. But I'm saying to just make it the default, and you can change it if you would like. I think that after using that crosshair for so long, and just for it to be taken away and not being able to use it again really threw (SOME) people off like myself. As for small other things, try to optimize your game a lot because I tend to see that I get abnormally high ping / latency only while playing Darwin project. Make the feel of the game better / make the gameplay a lot more smooth. Those last couple of things aren't as big as some of the other suggestions, but they were just things that I personally think would make the game better. I have one last thing to say, and It's the most important thing you must do. This isn't a suggestion, but rather a MUST. And for the third time, you've heard it so many times, but I'm here to remind you and tell you again, They know what they want. Overall I think the game is in an overall limbo. It's not dying like everyone is claiming, but it's not gaining in popularity either. This game has so much potential, and I want to see it come alive. But unfortunately that won't happen if the game company won't listen to their players. Thank you for reading.

_childDocuments_.review: [Edit: Game received for free after playing the open beta. Will update impressions after I play it more]Never played a Battle Royale game before. Played this during Open Beta #1.For a Beta (which should mean "bug/balance testing version of an already complete game, I think), this game had less content than a lot of Early Access games out there. Few customization options, few weapons, few variations on gameplay elements like maps, perks and crafting materials.But the game was actually very fun. The survival, tracking and crafting dynamics are actually very clever, although very simplistic. The loadout system adds a layer of strategy and planning, and having to decide between almost freezing to death or warming yourself with a fire that can be seen for miles is quite a nice touch. This game actually feels like something Blizzard would make nowadays: take a popular genre and make it as simple and casual as possible, but still entertaining to play (at least for some time). As I said, I have no experience with other battle royale games, but this one surely felt very arcadey. Even compared to other survival games like Rust or Minecraft or Don't Starve, there is only so much you can do in this game...I played some rounds, and then left the game with a curiosity on what it will turn out to be when it gets released. I have a fear that it might get repetitive, and lost among many other games that are fine but don't catch on.[Edit: now the game is on Early Access and it is not free. Not sure yet if I would recommend it as a paid product.]I don't know how much this game will cost after release. At the current state, I would only play it as a F2P game, and I recommend it for other people to try it if they can do that for free as well.

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10, VERY addictive and fun game.A lot of people are going to be sceptical "oh, another battle royale game, there's only hundreds out there already", but let me tell you: This is different. And really, really, really good. It is fast paced, intuitive, competitive and a hell lot of fun.I played a couple of rounds, and even won some, and I will certainly play this game a lot more in the future.You join a game, and have to fight against 10 other people, last one to live, wins. Sounds easy, but there are some differences from your standart BR game.There is a show director, which is a moderator who can use specials and buffs for players, nuke certain areas, apply moon-gravity to places, and a lot of other cool stuff. The directors will help you if you are nice to them, and sometimes ask questions to find out if you are worthy of their skills. It makes the battlefield feel a lot more dynamic than in all other BR games I have played. If you stream on twitch, your viewers can actually vote for events in the game!Also there is crafting, which is necessary to get things like arrows, pitfires, traps and some boosts to speed, warmth etc.You can either play solo against 9 oher players, or as a duo against 5 other duos(which I haven't tested out yet)One of the biggest positives for this game is the community. Aside from a few hot-micing russians or infants the people I played with were extremely nice. There is local voice chat, so even though I haven't experienced it once yet, there are certainly going to be a few salty people as well (which you can mute easily), but so far I am amazed by the nice community. At the end of a round you can rate the director 1 to 5 stars, if you feel like he significantly preferred other players, or even teamed up against others, making the game unfair, you can vote him 1 star and he will be restricted in his actions in future matches where he plays as a director.TL:DR:+Beautiful, fitting comic-like graphics+Very good performance+Completely free (no pay2win whatsoever!!!!)+Very generous community+Very easy to learn, hard to master+Combat is very rewarding+Frequent updates+Developers communicate with playerbase, and do a good job at it+Good crafting system-Rarely unfair games because of ♥♥♥♥ directors
