_childDocuments_.review: UPDATED: January 2020.OLD: This game is fun and unique. The push from the devs to encourage fighting from happening more often than in games like PUBG and Fortnite is brilliant, and executed wonderfully. And even with only 10 players, the game still feels tense like the other major BRs. With no weapon RNG, it can easily be more balanced for all the players, and the only way players can get the edge is not being lucky and finding a super powerful weapon, but getting enough crafting materials to upgrade their gear, tools, and powers. Getting the materials, wood and leather, is pretty easy. Getting electronics is a bit more luck based, but still decently fair in the terms of a BR.When I first posted this review, I stated that the director needed work. Originally, the problem was that the director could team and be abused; however, things have changed since then. There is now a rating system which, if the director is a bad director, will eventually get low ratings until he cannot use abilities that cannot affect one person at a time. You can also report people not following the rules, so that will be useful.I recommend it, but you may not like the differences in this game compared to other BRs. I think the game is already good in many aspects, and I hope it continues to grow in a positive direction.P.S: Scavenger Studio gave all alpha and beta testers (yes, even the ones during the beta) a free key for the game. That was amazing, and I am greatly thankful for them doing that. And as of 4/20/18, now the game was made free to play for everyone, so go try it out!UPDATE 1/17/20:Ok, so down below, the general idea is still the same, but they made some big changes for 1.0. First, the customization is constricted (less freedom but more balanced and easier to understand) with classes. Darwinium now exists, and it is used to upgrade your character or earn such powers (Electronic spawns now are just huge deposits of Darwinium). Also, I mention the director. _childDocuments_.review: Darwin Project™, is honestly in a very werid spot, in a year thats honestly very over saturated by battle royale style games, such as PUBG, Fornite, Radical Heights and more to come, this game manages to subvert all of my expectations and be a very unique experience and one of my favorite games of the year.Pros:- The tracking system in this game is one of its greatest draws, when you have to think about all of your resources you use, where you place fires, from where you even walk, makes this game alot more tense than it should be, words don't bring justice to how intense it can be when your getting tracked down by someone, not knowing how far they can be away from you, knowing that they can see PERFECTLY clear where you are.- Combat in this game may be simple, but it keeps you on your toes and makes you constantly think. Having a stamina par, and being equip with a bow and a axe at the instant the game starts, puts everyone at a fair playing field, timing with your axe is key, as well as having a keen eye and a good shot with a bow. What helps as well is that armor in this game can only block one hit, keeping it a high risk high reward of resources.- Unlike other royales, this game likes to keep it small, having a 10 man lobby, this keeps large enough so you don't have to worry about seeing others as you spawn, yet it manages to keep the flow of the game short enough not to feel like your hiding in a building or "in the zone" for 5-10 minutes checking your phone while waiting for some tosser to walk past your door/windowCons:- ♥♥♥♥ off  or however the ♥♥♥♥ you spell your name, you are to good at this game- Some of the items that you can craft need some nerfs, tripwire and turret mostly-Having a bad comentator can ruin a game for you, you could be in the middle of a fight and they could start healing the enemy constantly, having experiences like this constantly can ruin a game for you-Since the game is currently in Alpha, it suffers from a lot of werid issues, I myself have experienced currently, Slow loading, black screens, and the game taking up 80% of my CPU usage for 2 secondsFinal Thoughts:This game is easily one of the best games I have played this year and easily the best battle royale style game I have played, alot more enjoyable than my whole experience on PUBG, Fortnite and Radical Heights. I highly recomend picking it up, even more so if you have some friends willing to try it with you, as you can setup private lobbies.Gameplay: 9/10Graphics: 7/10Singleplayer: 8/10Duos/private matchs: 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: "It looks like Fortnite and will play like any other Battle Royale game probably."That were my thoughts upon seeing this game on Steam today. Oh boy, I was so wrong! 'Darwin Project' definitly is one unique Battle Royale game. It's easy to learn and hard to master. Ten players fight on a map consisting of multiple territories that get's smaller and smaller the longer the game goes on. Last one standing is the winner. Along the way you have to watch your "Coldness Meter" in order to stay warm and not freeze to death. You'll have to hack down trees, take apart leather chairs (to get leather, for some reason you just loot chairs made out of leather lmao), hunt deer and loot chests to craft and upgrade your gear. You can customize your "crafting wheel" in order to suit your playstyle. Wanna go in there and f*ck sh*t up? Take the axe damage buffs, berserker arrows and stamina cloaks. Wanna go sneaky beaky assassin style. The ninja boots and ghost cloak got you covered! Wanna be fast af boi? Yeah there's loads of items that give you a speed boost depending on the situation. You can experiment around a lot! There are also abilities like a teleport, a damage shield, camouflage, a super jump etc. which you can unlock by gathering rare electronic parts in game.The director, a spectator and sort of a gamemaster, views the entire thing and can manipulate it by closing down territories, nuking a territory, speeding/healing/warming up players and so on. You can also talk to other players and the director, which makes for funny situations. Seriously! Right now, upon winning you don't get anything but some EXP. No fancy unlocks, no shiny gear, nothing. And know what? It's completly fine since the actual gameplay is so much more satisfying than pulling a win. You'll laugh or even completly lose it in every match you play. A funny interaction with the director, a hilarious kill, a sudden save by the director or getting completly f*cked over by him/her is always a fun experience if you're light hearted.There are no guns in 'Darwin Project' so far. And I hope they keep it like that. You can of course use your bow, but aiming isn't that easy and you'll run out of arrows if you don't land your shots. Then it's time for the AXE TIME, BABY! You'll not get anywhere with button smashing in this game, so time your attacks properly and you might get out alive. Utilize traps, abilities and your trusty axe properly, while also landing your arrows and you'll definitly come out on top!'Darwin Project' is a nice game. It's got a solid concept and gameplay but what really is the factor that kept me playing the entire day was the amount of social interaction. I can't say this enough, every match is like a huge fun party and you want to be part of it. You almost feel like you're missing out on something when you see people fighting in the combat chat log and you're not part of it.Starting in the pre-game lobby and ending at the defeat or victory screen you'll be talking/screaming/yelling at other people while fighting or talking to the director. It all depends on the director and the other players but generally speaking if you're a fun, light hearted person the others will join in on the fun.Yes! Yes you should absolutely get this game! People who participated in the alpha/beta got the game for free and it is only 15 bucks. It's for the fun and chill guy who just wants to play some casual rounds aswell as for the absolute tryhard that wants to win at all costs.

_childDocuments_.review: SummaryGame feels very boring and uninspired. Controls are loose and slippery, Music is nice, but sfx is loud and annoying. Environment is . Characters... I havent seen characters this ugly since jimmy neutron.GameplayIf you've played any other Battle Royale game then you know what to expect for the most part. Main differences are you only have one weapon, and matches are currently restricted to 11 players. The 11th being the "Show Director"; a disembodied voice actively rigging the match, who can reveal players location, give powerups directly, spawn powerup drops on the map, and restrict area on the map. If this isn't your sort of thing then this game really isn't for you.Also, maps are too large for the small number of players you'll be up against, for most of the game you'll be on your own unless you purposefully spend 6-or-so minutes running accross the map to where you last saw an enemy.ArtEnvironments are nice. If you've played any arcade/anime-inspired MOBA within the last quinquennium then you'll feel right at home.The in-game character designs and animations are awful.  I don't know what planet they came from if they thought it would be appealing in any way... (probably Planet Sheen if i had to guess) but whoever gave the greenlight to these character designs really shouldn't be making those kinds of decisions. Thankfully though you'll be staring at their backs for the most part. SoundMusic is nice though not quite appropriate aesthetically imho. Like "Get Even" some of the music contains breathing percussions, which can be a hit or miss for some.Announcements and Kill sfx are overly loud and alarming when theres really no need, as most of the time the game is quiet and you're just running around the map. Additionally there is one alarm SFX in particular that is ridiculously obnoxious sounding. (You'll know when you hear it)With all that said, the game is currently free to play so try it and see if you like it.

If the person is sh*t, they can make the match really unappealing for anyone but themselves. Not a lot of these, thankfully.Overall, it's a fun game, but...there is not enough players rn. The newbies get crushed by experienced players, more accustomed to the game. That ensures that they'll never play the game again, in most cases, especially if they are f*cked by a mechanic they had no idea was in place.You'll run into the same people (not really a bad thing), but if you can spot a familiar name in the lobby, you might already know you don't have a chance to win.Verdict: Needs a playerbase of any kind. Still a fun passtime if you can bite through few brutal losses and get hang of the game.I honestly love the game. Don't let it die, devs.Edit in 2023: It's dead. _childDocuments_.review: BR games are getting stale as ♥♥♥♥ but this one stands out above the crowd.Higher TTK than PUBG or Fortnite resulting in battles being determined by "who can aim better" and not "who shot first".Show Director and viewer relationship actually feels like the Hunger Games take on the Game Master and Sponsors. Make fans with the crowd or the director and you have a huge advantage on the other 9 players. Match-making makes it hard to queue as a show director in order to boost friends. Hard but not impossible unfortunately.Tracking system is a very, "you can run but you can't hide" sort of deal. Sure you can run for the entire game just zipping across the map but there are so many ways for other players to get your exact location resulting in a very hunter/tracking driven system. Works very nice, camping is utterly useless. Either you run or you fight. There is no hiding in houses.The take on zones closing never once made me feel cheated like in PUBG or Fortnite. There's teleports on the edge of each zone to take you into the opposite zone and the zones close randomly for the most part which allows you to take the route that you imagine is best and not the route that the game just forces upon you. It was your decision to go to the west zone rather than the east so if you get screwed later you know you could have played it differently. The show director has the ability force you into a bad spot but there are always ways to survive as long as you have enough wood for fires or if you have an electronic that allows you access to teleport or superjump abilities.Bows take skill to aim with and shoot. The net-play feels very smooth. Never was I shot with an arrow after I got behind cover. Never have I felt that an arrow should have hit someone when it did not. Axe takes some getting used to since the range is very short but being able to time your swings to deflect other player's arrows or snowballs and then going in for the kill has never felt better.Overall I don't think the BR formula has been perfected because there is always room for improvement but these reasons alone make me feel like it's a massive jump in the right direction. This is the game BR developers need to copy, not PUBG or Fortnite with 100 people and RNG circles and bullets that kill you behind cover.

_childDocuments_.review: This is honestly one of my favourite games ever, and comfortably my favourite multiplayer title (though I also love L4D2) - it's unique take on the Battle Royale gimmick in having a show director to influence games is a fantastic addition and the depth of content stellar - the ability to use things like traps, gliders and turrets for example open up many new strategies of play, which is then further augmented by the ability to customise your characters loadout both in terms of items and stat buffs. This wideness is playstyle also means there is a very high skill ceiling for this kind of game.Of course however this game is not without it's flaws - most of which relate to it's playercount: it's too low. It's not uncommon to start a game with an incomplete lobby (which also means skill based matchmaking doesn't happen) which really slows down the games pace. Furthermore, the few people who have clung on are very often big fans very near the aforementioned high skill ceiling (myself included) which means a VERY high skill floor. Players new to DP (and especially competitive FPS games in general) WILL be killed quickly and ruthlessly by more experienced players. When/if the playerbase expands (hopefully at full launch) this will not be as much of an issue - but right now it's hard to really get involved.I've written a lot about that one issue, but don't let that overshadow it. Put the time in and this game is actually stellar - my over 500 hours played is testament to how sincere I am in that statement. Highly recommended to play and stick at for a while (the bot practice helps with the skill floor) and tell your friends too.

_childDocuments_.review: Note: If you're interested in a shorter review, read the conclusion at the end of this review.It was a really cool game at it's release state. Now since it was abandoned, you could guess why I give it this negative review. There are pretty much no players and you could only play it against bots with no Show-Master which is one of the main features this game can offer.Overall Darwin Project changed since it was released. It received alot of tweaks and balance changes and was treated with care by the developers. It was fun too play aswell since an aggressive was rewarding and experience + skill could make a huge difference. Oh and if the Show-Master didn't like you, you would probably lose anyway because of their really big influence. As Show-Master you can heal players, give them a temporary shield, speed boost them (or drug them), activate Low-Gravity or close specific parts of the map to force encounters between players and much more! While the Show-Master spectates, you are able to use Voicechat to talk to players and give them information, ask them dumb questions or make them hallucinated.  Players could talk to each other too. You were able to trashtalk your opponent mid battle or have a serious argument about your arrows phasing trough the opponent. It really was a fun little mechanic.Players need to collect Wood, Darwinium to craft different abilities, consumables and stat-boosters. There are different abilities, consumables and stat-booster available with other effects supporting all kinds of playstyles. But there is still a best Loadout/Meta in these. Looting from a Tree to get wood, crafting or looting will leave trails behind, which other players can use to track the player down who left them. In Combat you can utilize your axe or bow and arrows + the abilities or use a dodgeroll (it sucks). Landing headshots is difficult but rewarded by dealing extra damage. If you're out of arrows you can still pick up arrows from the ground that missed it's target or deflect an arrow with your axe (really cool stuff).The Game died when they decided to add a battlepass and cosmetics to the game, which was at the same time as the game was made Free-to-play, and when the grapplinghook was introduced. Yes that's right, the game costed 15 euro but as it went free, players who already bought the game, were given 2 Lootboxes which I didn't care about (I'm still mad btw). Moving on to the Grapplinghook, which was a cheap consumable that guarantee's a free hit on your opponent and was not really thought through by the devs and since the game died it never will be balanced.Conclusion: Darwin Project died, because of a too low playerbase and does not receive Developersupport anymore. If you plan on playing this game without friends, you can try to find a lobby (Only if you're not using American servers) but you're likely to not find one. Prepare to play with the ingame Bots that are not really eventful and fun to play against. Or grab about 4-8 friends to play in a private lobby and actually have some fun, as the core mechanics of Darwin Project are fun and enjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: In today's cluttered last-man-standing genre, a lot of BR's look and play the same. Parachute down on a large map, procure weapons (usually firearms), and pick off opponents while pressured into a progressively smaller area. Darwin decided to do something others have not: Fuse a survival game into a king of the hill combat mold. And to a degree, it actually works.Up to 10 players are teleported into a randomly generated map. The map itself is a shuffle of preset "biomes," all mid-winter, but with notable differences: A central frozen lake, scattered treehouses, a futuristic city, a rustic town with a central chapel, a shipping yard, and a molten canyon complete with expansive piping, to name a few. As combatants navigate these, they hunt down chests, chop down trees, harvest darwinium (energy resource), and the occasional robo-deer for special items and healing. Using gathered resources, you can craft arrows, a couple traps, and class-specific upgrades to boost your offensive, defensive, or tactical abilities.It's a lot to take in at first, but with practice, becomes second nature. Darwin is a high skill ceiling game for those who dare to master it, giving you all the tools to pull of incredible trickshots with a bow, intense melee axe fights, or satisfying 4D chess plays of out-maneuvering opponents into hidden, preset traps. There are many montages on youtube that showcase Darwin at its peak, and indeed, it's mesmerizing. Here's just one example: During its early days, Darwin was not built on classes, but rather, customization. You could directly upgrade and build any combination of powers you pleased, limited only by resources and the time to craft them. On launch, they removed this freedom and narrowed your abilities into three classes: Jetpack, Grapple Hook, Seeker Drone. Jetpack focuses on verticality / aerial bow use / speed, Grapple on melee / shields / 1v1, Seeker on tracking / trapping / invisibility. Within your class selection your access to abilities is limited, so you need to make the most of your strengths. Ultimately, though, every class comes down to quick reflexes and good aim.Darwin's survival element has you juggle a constant pressure against cold, which, if ignored, will steadily deplete your HP akin to a poison effect. To combat this, you craft fires that warm you up, but give away your position to the enemy by a stage-wide visible smoke signal. You can put these out early by crafting snowballs, or use them strategically to throw off opponents. Speaking of snowballs, you can lob these at opponents to lower their cold resistance and possibly seal a battle of attrition if they can't warm up.Last but not least, the game had a novel idea of tasking one spectator player as a show director, granting the power to spice things up to their whims. These had access to "cards" (randomly selected events) including things like resource gifts, buffs, zone closure, and even a nuke, forcing players to evacuate or risk KO by countdown. It featured a twitch integration to let the audience vote and grant bonus XP to the most entertaining participants.So why is the game in maintenance mode, then? As per usual, my thoughts: - Before it went F2P, Darwin was a pay to play title, which likely kept potential players at bay (the early access dilemma). Eventually, the game extended to other platforms, but had limitations: It was never available on Switch, and for Xbox players, Live was required. Though it utilized Twitch and picked up some streamers, where else was it advertised? If the intended market was competitive, where were the tournaments and the big prizes? There were some, but I can't recall hearing about them. - Unlike its cartoonish appearance, Darwin is no casual game. If you didn't already, watch the linked video above to get a sense for how fast combat can be... significant precision and foresight are needed to land your shots, deflect attacks, or lure opponents into traps. I'm not sure that Darwin pulled enough of the esports type, which the game seems made for. When streamers picked up the game, some rose to the challenge and improved their skill. But others, soured by continuous losses, became detractors, and their complaints shaped content changes. It's a catch-22 of wanting a competitive audience but catering your game to players who weren't as dedicated, and the end result was alienating both experienced alpha testers (who didn't like the class system) and the newcomers getting stomped by pros in the full release, who may not have stuck around long enough. Speaking of which, some casuals didn't even make it past the survival mechanics to manage their cold meters. They wanted faster games. - Touched on above, not a lot of early adopters appreciated losing the full crafting wheel and being pigeonholed into classes. Battlepass came late in the life cycle, finally giving players something to strive for with tasks to perform. And not to be forgotten, duos - party with a friend - was a defining draw to the game, and it was taken out on release (in favor of ranked free for all). Some people only want to play with pals, and that forced these out altogether.Today, you can still experience vanilla Darwin under custom matches - I suggest you do so - to see what could have been. If you enjoy it, search the forums for discord links to find premades and get a real game going. You can gamble on midweek and weekend randoms but true challengers all go customs.: Typical grind achievements. Very time consuming... there is no consistent way to get XP outside of 1 daily win + top 3 finish. You can farm with a friend or use an idle account. Must be done in public matchmaking, customs don't count. Level 50 is easily a 3 month or so commitment.And caution about the legendary weapon skin. _childDocuments_.review: The Darwin Project is by far the best game in this genre. No guns are in this game, you are equiped only with a Bow and an Axe and several traps and possible powerups. All of these things can be crafted with the correct components. The zone is designed so that specific areas are shut of instead of resucing the whole map down vide a huge ass sphere, This not only makes the game feel new but also if you are the Game Director who essentually controls the game, you can lure your inmates together for a massive free for all mayhem. name: Half-Life: Alyx
detailed_description: Half-Life: Alyx is Valve’s VR return to the Half-Life series. It’s the story of an impossible fight against a vicious alien race known as the Combine, set between the events of Half-Life and Half-Life 2. Playing as Alyx Vance, you are humanity’s only chance for survival. The Combine’s control of the planet since the Black Mesa incident has only strengthened as they corral the remaining population in cities. Among them are some of Earth’s greatest scientists: you and your father, Dr. Eli Vance. As founders of a fledgling resistance, you’ve continued your clandestine scientific activity—performing critical research, and building invaluable tools for the few humans brave enough to defy the Combine. Every day, you learn more about your enemy, and every day you work toward finding a weakness. ABOUT GAMEPLAY IN VR: Valve’s return to the Half-Life universe that started it all was built from the ground up for virtual reality. VR was built to enable the gameplay that sits at the heart of Half-Life. Immerse yourself in deep environmental interactions, puzzle solving, world exploration, and visceral combat. Lean to aim around a broken wall and under a Barnacle to make an impossible shot. Rummage through shelves to find a healing syringe and some shotgun shells. Manipulate tools to hack alien interfaces. Toss a bottle through a window to distract an enemy. Rip a Headcrab off your face and throw it out the window. COMMUNITY-BUILT ENVIRONMENTS A set of Source 2 tools for building new levels is included with the game, enabling any player to build and contribute new environments for the community to enjoy through Half-Life: Alyx's Steam Workshop. Hammer, Valve’s level authoring tool, has been updated with all of the game's virtual reality gameplay tools and components.

_childDocuments_.review: Half Life: Alyx is one of the best VR games ive played. I haven't played tons, but ive played some really good ones. Graphically amazing, sound design is fantastic and the gameplay and controls are simple yet can be complex and interesting. I love the story and how it seems to tie in with Half Life 2. There were a few bugs like sometimes one of your hands would disappear which is very bad if it disappears at the wrong time.....like in the middle of a fire fight or against headcrabs.It can also be very tense and scary, especially against said headcrabs, for the most part, horror games dont really "get" me. But the moment a headcrab latched onto my face? Thought i was gonna have a heart attack. This game is amazing in almost every way and if you love Half Life and VR, pick it up, also ignore those whinging snowflakes annoyed thats its VR only. No one complains when a nintendo game is released on the new nintendo platform, this is no different than that.If i did have complaints it would be the combat. While fun and amazing and tense when it happens, due to VR controls its very limited, like only 3 maybe 4 enemies per encounter. If they could expand on this and make the combat moments more intense and with more enemies without making it annoying and hard then you got yourself the perfect Half Life game. Well done valve, and thank you for making this.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely a Half Life game. It's amazing how much the basic Half Life experience offers totally new challenges simply by doing fewer things for you.No more magic gun expert Gordon to reload for you whenever you go click. Think about your ammo, and how much you have left. Don't drop the mag you were trying to shove into your gun because there's a headcrab on your face. Remember to chamber a round.Feel like a badass with the gravity gloves, snatching anything and everything out of your surroundings. Ammo, health syringes, random debris, the grenade the combine dude just threw at you. Quick, throw that last one back.Honestly the 'Jeff' section goes on a bit too long for my taste, but whatever. Seems like a lot of people liked it.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: I think Alyx was a fantastic game but if I had one thing to complain about it would be that it didn't really feel like the game needed to be VR only. I could see a lot of the puzzles and fights being perfectly translatable to a flat screen. VR adds some depth like being able to shoot around a corner without needing to move your head and the entire stealth section with , but otherwise it didn't feel like it was pushing any boundaries like how Boneworks was. But besides that the game was really good with lots of memorable moments (the club sandwich scene), fun gameplay and a fantastic ending.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I'd recommend the game BUT:To start off I'm not a Half-Life fan. My experience with the series was playing like 5 minutes of HL2 to test my family computer when it came out, and a TON of HL1 deathmatch. So none of my opinion has anything to do with the previous games. Ultimately I don't think this game is worth picking up a VR setup for, nor do I think it was worth Valve making this a VR game in the first place (see my negatives section for why). A lot of what I'm finding engaging is the characters and story. It's not much of a breakthrough VR game from a gameplay standpoint (not nearly as much as I'd consider Boneworks to be). It makes use VR nicely in some areas, but I wouldn't say it was necessary considering that it's not pushing it from a gameplay standpoint with physics, or gunplay, or really any features. It IS a solid VR game, but if it wasn't half-life I don't think it would really be that outstanding. Boneworks has certainly spoiled me overall and I was expecting much more from Valve honestly. I'm only disappointed that this game doesn't push their own hardware in ways that other games haven't or done more with.Positives:The highlight of the game I'd say so far is the characters and story. It's pretty immersive and engaging, and has had enjoyable dialogue between Alyx and Russell.The visuals are also very good and the game runs very well too. I didn't notice many performance dips at all while playing (with a gtx 1080 gpu at max settings). The gunplay is very satisfying, and I'd say it matches up to Boneworks on this purely from the point of aiming and shooting, recoil, etc.Negatives:Doesn't push the hardware from a gameplay standpoint. It just doesn't match up to what Boneworks has done with physics and making you really feel present in a space. Movement is very basic. I use full smooth motion and was really disappointed to see that jumping is just teleporting, as is going through smaller crawlspaces or windows, etc. Even falling from a height is either very slow, or simply teleports you to the bottom. I understand people get motion sick (as do I after a while) but I don't see this as a reason to kneecap a game like this. Either add the option somehow or people play in shorter settings, or have a sit-down mode. There isn't nearly enough to movement in this game imo that warrants it to not be a sit-down type game (maybe I missed this option?).Physics and Freedom. There really isn't much especially compared to Boneworks. Things have physics but you're pretty set in stone as to what you can really do with it. As of right now the only thing I've been able to do is use something as a shield, but it hasn't been useful in any scenario against zombies obviously. You can't switch what hand you have your gun in without using a menu, and there's no real reason to pick up things from the environment to use other than the general ammo and health pickups. I wasn't able to hit a zombie with a bottle or brick and have it do anything to it.Controls and how you interact with the world. It's not that great honestly. I don't like how set in stone you are with your gunhand being either right or left from a menu, and I certainly don't like that changing the dominant shooting hand just flips your controls entirely. I'm left handed but why in gods name would I want to move with the right thumbstick then? This could be fixed by more options or manual remapping (I think?) but in general I just don't like how locked in everything seems.Overall negative is what I stated above really. All of this compounds to making the game less like the "tech demo, yet has a compelling story" that I wanted it to be. I was expecting more use out of the index controllers, more physics and more freedom to tackle obstacles. But really you're left with a game that while it *does* use vr, none of the ways are very original or necessary. I understand *why* they made this game a VR exclusive, but I don't think it was worth it with how the game turned out. If this game had really pushed physics, and interacting with the environment with puzzles and whatnot, I would get it. But as it stands it's a VERY enjoyable story and game, but it would probably be just as enjoyable if it *wasn't* in VR.

_childDocuments_.review: Really lives up to the hype. It's the most polished VR game I've played yet (I've had a headset since 2017).One thing I really appreciate so far is that Valve sets a really eerie tone, but does not take any cheap tricks with jump scares. Jump scares are so easy in VR, and I honestly have a hard time playing some VR games because of it. Thank you, Valve, for letting me just get through the story!Another aspect that makes this game so solid (aside from the expected-and-delivered great story and fantastic voice acting), is the art design. So many locations are expertly crafted: They feel lived in, and real. Not like Fallout debris everywhere (I love you Fallout but sometimes you're a random items generator).I'm also really happy with the gameplay aspect: Combat feels great (and terrifying as I try to load my pistol while a headcrab comes marching at me), the upgrades are rewarding and make me want to keep scouting for resources (which to me, adds to the immersion), and the hacking mini-game puzzles are a unique and interesting take (positioning glowing points in 3D space is neat).The voice acting really needs to be noted again, as it's just so on point. Alyx and Russell feel so natural, and their back and forths are really entertaining (and usually help cut a really tense moment).Sometimes the physics based hand input can be a little tricky to figure out, but I really think it's the best method I've seen yet to give weight to objects in VR (your hand will move but your avatar Alyx hand won't if you're trying to, say, lift an object that can't be lifted one-handed). It's more great immersion. The grip gets a little sticky sometimes, but I think it promotes pushing items, taking advantage of that physics-based interaction that has been lacking in VR (few experiences let you swing a gun at a window and break the shattered glass piece by piece--man that is SUCH a great feeling).My biggest problem is that I just can't play for too long, I mean really, I'm spending between 1-2 hours standing, usually terrified of a headcrab, and very tense. It'll wear you out fast. But I really want to keep progressing with the story. I'd say also that this is very much a linear story, so if you're an open-world fan, this is not it. But it really needs to be, as it plays out like a movie that you're in.

_childDocuments_.review: For the people without time:The physics that made the original Half-Life games so good, BUT ON STEROIDS!!!For the rest:First and foremost, this is not one of the other VR games that feel like an experience, or a demo. It is a FULL Half-Life game, set in VR, shortcuts were not taken. It has some of the usual VR gimmicks but unlike in other games, they feel polished and natural (I know, teleporting is not natural, but you can change it so this review is through the eyes of a player that mainly used normal walking and turning).It's a good game with a nice story.Characters and voice:The characters ,tho they don't seem to change a lot during the game, are believable. Each one is well structured and the chatter between them reflects that. The jokes they tell are also good, serving a much needed comedic relief purpose. The chat between them also helps with game-play, you more or less know when a big fight will begin, or end form the chat either being cut off, personal remarks from the player character or an 'are you okay' check form your "eye in the sky".Enemies:Introduced one by one, they all have weak and strong points, with gun upgrades evens showing them for those of us that are not so eagle-eyed. The tough enemies are generally presented in a controlled environment, so that the player can take all the time she needs. After that they are thrown alongside other enemies, a tactic that makes for some hectic encounters.Environment:In one word... spectacular. Everything just feels right, we have grown from the "oh look a scary pixelated texture". You can get as close to the objects as you want and they will feel realistic, walls doors windows you name it. The game is set in a small area but, it makes good use of all the space it has to work with. Some parts are flat but others take you up, down, and all around, every time you enter a building you are nearly guaranteed to clear it out.One thing that needs to be said is the magic they have done with light. Each light source feels organic, from the underground lights to sunlight, it flows just right through each room you find yourself in, and it certainly makes for some eye candy from time to time.Conclusion:There is much much more to talk about, this review dose not make the game justice but, I just HAD to share my humble opinion. There are bad things as well, along other things clipping through objects and enemies hitting you though walls can and will happen. There are a lot more good things to say, I could not touch on the scavenger feel you get, you somehow get feel immortal, but the game dose a good job into slapping you back in place.Overall it keeps the theme and feel of other Half-Life games alive. I have had great expectations for the next Half-Life title and this game did NOT let me down.

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot begin to explain how great the atmosphere is in this game. Yes, the videos look really good. It's on a whole other level when you're in the middle of it. Although there is a bug where smooth turning isn't working. It has the option to turn off snap turns, but it isn't functioning properly. They're aware of it and working on a fix. Anyway, if you have a VR headset and you even remotely like Half-Life, then you NEED this game in your life. Again, the atmosphere is incredible. There are times when moving through dark tunnels where all you have is your flashlight. It is very creepy. I was sweating, Also, "leave no stone un-turned". There's no telling what you'll find.This game is what VR is all about. You won't be sorry you purchased it.

_childDocuments_.review: [NO SPOILERS - or substance at all, really, just how I felt. I played this on the Oculus Rift S and I really enjoyed it, though I'm sure all VRs on the store page will work wonderfully.]I wasn't sure whether or not to buy a VR early - on one hand, I wanted to make sure I was able to play it on release, so I minimized the risk of being spoiled (and didn't have to continue testing my patience!). On the other hand, there was always the risk that the game might not be very good - and that VR still had time to go before it comes up to the bigger market.I decided, perhaps foolishly, to buy VR prior to release, betting on the fact that it'd probably be at least good. I went into the game extremely critically, and frankly, every problem I had was simply a limitation of VR technology (or in some cases, just a limitation of MY setup). As much as I tried to be in that critical, 'grrr, this is not as good as the old games' muh nostalgia mindset, I simply couldn't help enjoying and loving this game. It's one of the best new releases I've played in the last DECADE, and I was not let down at all. The ending alone makes this game worth every penny, and I look forward to what Valve will do in the future. Let's just hope that optimism ages well, and I don't return to this review in 5 years with no new news about their upcoming projects.If you are in a position in life where you reckon you want VR - or you REALLY want to play more Half-Life - I cannot recommend Half-Life: Alyx enough.

_childDocuments_.review: Declaimer: I got the game kind of free because i bought the index HMD and Controller at release day… so kind of free…However: I played the game for over 6 hour’s straight. I had to stop because my controller power died. First the left one went out of power and I really considered for a moment to play it with one arm.So now I’m back from the virtual reality… And I’m sad! I honestly don’t know how to describe the game property. … A masterpiece… the game of the year in VR for sure and it won’t be the (normal) game of the year just for the reason so please the masses how haven’t gotten a VR-Headset jet.The game is rich of story and absolutely story driven. It has just the right amount of horror to still be playable by the majority of players. It’s the true next Half Life in any way.It’s truly the next step after the source-engine with HL2. It’s a gaming revolution.And I love that there is extra HUD and Layout and movement smoothing for the viewers. It’s really the first game in VR that absolutely and vanilla stream able. That’s the way to go to get the masses so understand and love VR. The ability to share this game-experience natively in this quality is amassing.The game is the next step in VR-gaming. Any other VR game after this will have to adapt to these new standards this game set. Ok… enough of my fan-boy-talk. Here at least a view fact:The movement is absolute perfect. I played with the index controllers but I haven’t found a gameplay-nessesary reason why other controllers should have problems. Rent it, test it, if you like it buy it. It’s that simple… I my opinion it was a shame that index buyers got it for free. _childDocuments_.review: My god this game is absolutely amazing! This is by far my favorite game, even going as far as to beat BONEWORKS. The gun-play is amazing, the enemies are amazing, the environments are amazing, everything is amazing. In my opinion, this is the best looking VR game, in fact, this is the best looking game in general. Valve really took their time with this game and it shows. Using the Index's pressure sensors, you can squeeze shampoo bottles, crush soda cans, and squeeze XEN grenades to prime them. There are 3 guns that you can use, a pistol, a shotgun, and a Combine SMG which looks like a little mini Pulse-Rifle. All of these guns can be upgraded using resin at Combine fabricators. By far my favorite thing in HL:A are the "Russells" or The Gravity Gloves. You can use them to pull objects like resin or ammo towards you, but you can use them on many other items as well, like bottles, buckets, boxes, or supply crates. If it has physics, you can most likely use the gloves on it. I won't spoil it here, but the ending is absolutely amazing, and a shocker too. Make sure that you stay for the after-credits scene, its really important.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the best VR game I have ever played. Easily blew Boneworks out of the water. Control scheme is nice on both the vive controller and Index. The "gravity gloves" work better than most "force" or "telekinesis " item grabs. You feel like a total badass flinging a magazine at yourself, catching it then popping it into the chamber. It handles ammo, loading and guns better than any platform to date.More importantly, this isn't a tech demo or nod from Valve. This is 100% true to form a Half Life game.  Been playing Hl2 and HL2s spawned mods (Garrysmod, CSS. TF2..etc) for over a decade but to see the models lifesize in VR is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ awesome. As a VR user, this is a must have. As a Half Life fan this is a solid must have.10/10 Valve. Good to have ya back.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic, and then some. Best *GAME* I've played in a while - not just "VR Game". _childDocuments_.review: Half Life Alyx not only shows that VR is not a gimmicky trick but also proves how future technologies can truly bring a greater experience. _childDocuments_.review: There's plenty to love about this game. It's very true to its Half-Life roots and has a wide variety of puzzle throughout. The transition to VR was done well, with environments feeling much more alive than previous games. The voice acting is great, including frequent radio chatter voiced by Rhys Darby. I was a little worried it would be overpriced for its content, but I'd guess the campaign is roughly 12-15 hours which feels very fair to me.There are some parts I'm not keen on though. There's collectible "resin" throughout each level which can be used to purchase weapon upgrades. The concept is fine, but gathering the resin can be tedious as it often involves rifling through drawers and cabinets. You could ignore this feature, but the unupgraded weapons are pretty weak, and a good chunk of the available ammo is hidden similarly.The combat is sort of love/hate. All the familiar bullet-sponge enemies are back, including the flying and jumping ones. The shooting mechanics are pretty realistic, which means aiming is difficult and reloading involves multiple steps (e.g. for the pistol: press a button to eject the empty magazine, then use your off-hand to grab a new one and insert it, then pull the slide back). It's fun and immersive but hard. The difficulty butts heads with the VR controls, since to strafe or crouch you need to physically move around while also minding your real-life surroundings. The default controller movement setting is point-and-blink, which also doesn't lend itself well to quick or precise movements. I ended up turning the difficulty down to Easy and found it more enjoyable.For a Half-Life fan who has a VR headset, I'd call this game a must-buy.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Easily the best VR game on the market currently.  It's immersion is incredible, occasionally I would scream when a headcrab jumped out at me from the dark, something not achieved in any past Half-Life games or Valve games in general.  I found almost zero bugs in my playthrough other than the occasional model clipping through the wall.  The only major complaint I have for this game is the way they handle Melee combat, it's nonexistent.  You could hit a headcrab with an entire chair and it wouldn't flinch. _childDocuments_.review: This, in my opinion, is the peak of VR gaming in 2020. Not only is this one of the first VR games developed by a triple A developer, it raises the bar for VR games to be more than tech demos or experiences. Blade and Sorcery, Pavlov, and Beat Saber are all fantastic games, and still premiere VR titles, but Half Life Alyx gives a consistent, fun, and complete game within VR.My first play-through took me 10 hours to complete. I took a lot of time to fully explore the environments  and get as many collectibles as I could to get weapon upgrades. The story was captivating and adds to the existing Half Life universe. There are a few extremely notable set pieces that make this game worth it alone.Overall, if you own a VR headset or are considering getting one, this game is an absolute must have. This is a fantastic return to form for Valve and I am extremely excited to see what they work on next.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Half-Life: Alyx is brilliant, one of the best VR games at the moment. I've had a blast, you should definitely play it, and I'd be utterly blown away if it weren't for Boneworks. It had set the bar high, and in some ways Alyx feels like a step backwards.Alyx is a lot more cinematic, the environments are very detailed and stunningly beautiful, but they feel fake in comparison to Boneworks, where almost every object could be interacted with and climbed. Alyx has its furniture glued to the floor, instead of jumping you have teleporting, and even some narrow passages have you teleport instead of physically crawling through them. You can't spend half an hour playing around in one room. I didn't even realize what a huge impact on immersion being able to topple a shelf had.The lack of melee combat is a major disappointment. When it comes to shooting, fighting enemies that can shoot back is really fun, that's what I'd say the game excels at. Shooting enemies that don't shoot back, however, is a lot less fun. You can't grab a headcrab. You can't even push an enemy back. The zombies move too slowly, you never feel in danger when they stumble in your direction. You also don't feel the impact of your shots. The enemies in Alyx don't stumble back the same way the dummies of Boneworks do. You feel like you're draining their health bar, not devastating them with bullets.Another weird disappointing thing is the fact weapons are stored in a menu, not on your body. And that's with the game only having three weapons and one item. That's another big immersion breaker.

_childDocuments_.review: Played on the original Oculus RIft.The immersion is unbelievable!I've been experimenting with playing the game standing up ( cable is hanging from the ceiling ),  without teleporting too much, but after a while ( ~ 30 mins ) I start to loose balance from time to time, so I've been sitting on a chair and from time to time get up and look around. Teleporting is good at traveling fast between spots ( the stalker scene was done with 0 damage via teleportation ), and helps a lot during combat, as you can sneak behind the combine soldiers.Speaking of combat, the music played during the combat scenes gets you pumped up and ready to fight, and you certainly need that, as they are very intense.The graphics are surreal, it's like the reality has been drawn in front of your eyes ( the chosen colors are clearly not real, but fit great within the game ).The amount of stuff available to do in the world is really at 'Half-Life level", I've tried playing the piano,  but kind of hard with only 1 finger XDThe puzzles are great, sometimes too obvious, but sometimes I got stuck due to bugs making me think that there's more to do.I've encountered several bugs during the gameplay: 1) doors that were stuck and wouldn't let me pass. After reloading the previous save, the issue was fixed.2) I've also been able to fall to the floor on the last level, without dying and being unable to return to the correct path.The bad stuff?There are no melee attacks... like that was one of the biggest things that bothered me. It happened to me to be out of ammo in my gun while a drone kept attacking me, and my first instinct was to wack it at it, doing nothing and taking more damage... I get that we couldn't use any object we can grab to deal melee damage, but not even the weapons ? or are they too fragile ?What happened to the 'grab item with gravity gun and throw it at the enemy' approach ? I think it would have been a great thing to do, throw stuff at the enemy, if not to kill them, at least stagger while you reload or run for cover.Speaking of running for cover ( I've read that you can increase the 'walking' speed via console or start arguments, haven't tried it yet ), there is no running, just teleporting.Still, I ,ist recommend people buy a headset and play this awesome game! After that finish, you will not be disappointed with your choice. The end scenes have given me goosebumps.

_childDocuments_.review: As a long time fan of the Half-Life series, I was understandably hyped when Half-Life: Alyx was announced. With that hype and excitement also came some disappointment that it was exclusively VR based. Knowing that it was VR only I was not too happy because I didn't have the hardware necesarily to play the game, but after over a year saving up to build a new PC and getting an Oculus Quest I finally got to play this VR game that was said to be the first real big hitter for the genre. I was excited, and I have to say the game didn't disappoint. This is the VR game that I went out and bought a VR headset for, and it was well worth the investment in my opinion. This game seamlessly immerses you into the world of Half-Life, and has so many action packed moments that are just a treat to play through. I loved some of the more scary moments too that reminded me of Ravenholm. The story was nothing special throughout the game, though with that said at the end of the game there was a huge twist that left me speechless and teary eyed. I won't spoil what happens but we do get a teaser of the long awaited and almost mythical Half-Life 3!. This game was a blast all the way through and each enemy was extremely fun to fight against, especially the Antlions.

_childDocuments_.review: Impressive visuals and decent audio, but the gameplay and VR issues make it an expensive disappointment. You might be better off watching a YouTube playthrough than shelling out for a VR headset.I got myself a Valve Index for this, which thankfully arrived in time for release, but the trigger on one controller failed. After exchanging a few emails (which took a long time, partly because they ignored half of what I said) they only sent a replacement after receiving the faulty one back (which took a long time) and my order for an extra pair just said "Your order has expired" (after waiting ages). It took so long to get a 2nd controller again that I just tried it singlehanded. It took me 40 minutes to get that controller to accept movement controls.The gameplay can be tiring, as you go around picking up hundreds of objects and try to solve the puzzles. It felt so tedious and tiring that I played it in short stints, losing muscle memory for the controls. My muscle memory was wiped completely when I finally got my 2nd controller - switching control schemes entirely.The reload system is flawed (especially in the dark), relying on good muscle memory and tracking, made awkward by a number of issues. In the process you have to reach over your shoulder, potentially bashing your headset trying to get it to work, then trying not to crash your controllers together. The shoulder system rarely works at all when I crouch, so you can't take cover while reloading. If your hands are sweaty at all then it won't register letting go of a magazine (or releasing an armed grenade!).Enemies chase you, and they can appear at medstations, at the top of ladders, and even at autosave points, so you  to be able to reload quickly. It's fun when it works, but immersion-breaking when it doesn't. It wouldn't be so bad if they added a melee weapon.The enemies are unintuitive, like barnacles instantly grabbing you if you're anywhere near their lines, so you shoot them rather than just walk around them, which feels like a waste of bullets (in a world where ammunition would be very valuable). Many enemies are ridiculously strong, taking several headshots, or have invulnerable parts, or are just completely invulnerable. Soldiers throw grenades so perfectly that you might automatically catch them while trying to reload.Many of the puzzles are out of place, like spending minutes standing there repeatedly failing what feels like a bad mobile game, just for a box to open and give you 2 shotgun shells, or to defuse a mine which you could just shoot instead. Some environmental puzzles are so unintuitive that I often got stuck and resorted to watching a playthrough, and ended up seeing a bunch of spoilers.Other unintuitive problems, like pulling backwards on the thumbstick slightly (to try to move back) - causing you to teleport forwards, launching you into tripmines or barnacles. Sometimes I'm not sure if I died when the screen changes, like when stepping down from something, hitting an autoload point, or getting stuck in a wall. Things that look moveable/breakable are often unmoveable/unbreakable, but later on the way forward is to move or break something that looks unmoveable or unbreakable. Likewise some spaces you can crawl into, some you can't for whatever reason. Some drops are arbitrarily fatal while other similar ones are fine...Other problems include the view getting so wobbly that I felt sick and had to restart VR. You run out of hands, trying to round corners with a gun ready, while holding a torch, and also using the thumbstick movement systems, and sometimes needing to do a 4th thing all at the same time. Sometimes the menu disappears, and the controls aren't readily available, which is bad if you ever forget a button. You'll easily die, and there are long loading times for every death.The game flowed badly for me, taking me 16 hours to complete, and felt like a chore that I only wanted to finish because I spent so much money on it. The parts that were supposed to be scary or exciting just felt frustrating due to the problems that came up. I outright hated it by the second half. Trespasser did a better job of implementing hand puzzles without a HUD back in 1998.The best bits I think were just appreciating the environments - seeing the alien lifeforms taking over a city, complemented by the music. But you can get that from watching a video of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Play HL Alyx, but do not play it as one of your first VR games. Nothing I tried yet came close in terms of immersion and polish. The in-game player presence is the perfect balance possible at the current state of VR technology. Your hands, which you control and are tracked directly, always collide with everything in the game world. The rest of your body that cannot (or only indirectly) be tracked does not collide with anything. In my opinion, this is a much more immersive approach to in-game presence than most that only allow collision when actively grabbing (most games), or try to deduce body movement from headset movement (e.g. Boneworks).
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Half-Life: Alyx is a life changing experience. I have not once in all my years on this earth experienced something quite as powerful as this game. The world in and of itself is easy to get immersed in, but the fact that it's VR amplifies the immersion tenfold. I finished this game in a little over 11 hours and I intend to add another 11 to the play time. And once I'm done playing through a second time, I intend on downloading some workshop content and messing about with some of the player made creations. This game managed to grip me in ways that only a handful of games have. Playing this game FEELS like you're in City 17. It FEELS like you're sneaking into the QZ. It FEELS like a certain someone (if you know, you know) is right there and that at any moment he could reach out and snap you like a twig, and that every noise you make in real life will somehow give you away. The gunfights are INTENSE and encounters with zombies and headcrabs can be genuinely  frightening. There are some annoyances. There is a certain part in the game where I feel the difficulty spikes out of no where, and some of the mechanics could use a bit of polish. The flashlight should have had a dedicated button because being in a dark ass sewer with no flashlight because FOR SOME REASON IT ISN'T DARK ENOUGH YET is admittedly a little frustrating. All around, however, I would say that the mechanics and general game design and game feel are nearly perfect. Valve hit the nail on the head with Half-Life. They drove the nail through the board with HL2 and it's episodes. They atomized the board and the wall they were nailing it to with Half-Life: Alyx. This is the game that will sell VR systems. If you have the necessary components to play this game BUY IT. It is worth every single penny.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Best VR game out now.  Admittedly, I am relatively early on in the game, but its all the little things that just click.  In other VR games throwing a grenade is weird.  Either throwing it super far, or dropping it at your feet.  In Alyx the grenade goes exactly how far I'd expect for how fast I'm moving my arm.The simple fact that the world actually interacts with you, ie, if there is a door your hand doesn't float through it, Alyx's hand will stop  and go flat against it.  This little change I found myself stopping my hands on objects naturally even though I physically could push through them.  That weird divide of reality and VR actually shrinks because of this little touch.Loading guns is soooo satisfying.Graphics are insane (I have an Index and a 2080ti so playing on the max settings)So far best moment for me was when I first started getting into shootouts and realized I was ducking behind barricades, and hiding behind a wall leaning out to shoot that I was like, Whoa....this is it.Great game.

_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Half-Life: Alyx is an experience like no other. Valve has not only managed to cram an entire game into VR, but has exceeded all expectations in doing so. The game keeps that Half-Life magic that we all love and know. The unique, alien visual style. The memorable, mysterious story line. The pacing. Even that little bit of humor. Then, if that wasn't enough, Half-Life: Alyx innovates once more on the classic Half-Life formula and brings an experience only accessible through the immersion of VR.That isn't to say that Half-Life: Alyx is a game for everyone, nor is a perfect game. Like it's predecessor, Half-Life: Alyx is less about the gun-play and more about the experience. There were also a few bugs, most notably one where the game would stop refreshing the image on my Oculus Rift (Although Valve seems to have patched many bugs that I experienced at launch and I'm guessing this one might be fixed by now).Still, I would consider Half-Life: Alyx one of my most highly rated games. It's got that classic Half-Life magic. It's a full length game in VR. It's an experience like no other. That's why I highly encourage you, headset owners, to suck that 60 bucks into the game and play it as soon as possible.Final Rating: Half-Life: Alyx Outta Ten.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

But very happy with it and I look forward to more like it.

_childDocuments_.review: I've kept the following text as spoiler free as possible and it contains no plot points.Immersion. That's the best way to describe my first experiences with the game. The visuals are stunning. The physics are great and the level of interaction high. I've had my first few combat encounters and the combat is solid and easy to pick up, though the experience is so far closer to a survival than an action game. I'm not generally keen on collectibles (in this case, a singular resource) in games as they disrupt the flow, but here it seems tolerable. The familiar creatures are all more life-like (though the headcrabs look a lot... softer?) and the agony that is to be a headcrab zombie becomes quickly apparent.The world feels deep and true to the franchise, with great attention to detail and expansion of the established. A few characters do seem to lean towards the cartoony but it is maintained within reasonable limits. On Index Alyx's voice sounds a little off: quiet, and as if it was around you instead of coming from your mouth. It might also be not knowing what the character is going to say and thus feeling disconnected.Overall the first hours have been thoroughly engaging and enjoyable.P.S. The bread looks so very tasty.

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to love this game, and while I do recommend it, I won't recommend it for the price point of $60. I'd catch it on a sale. My first run of the game took about 9 hours, so on average you're going to spend $6 an hour, which is pretty steep for a something like a Half Life title.The biggest reason I recommend this game is because it succeeds in being entertaining. I can't say anything that you probably don't already know about it--the controls are outstanding, the graphics are amazing, and the sound design is frighteningly good. You can tell that a lot of work has gone into this creation, and it plays like a work of art more than anything else.That being said, I would consider this game to be more of an interactive movie. It gets serious point deductions for the lack of replayability and its duration, however. I am not the sort of pretentious snob that NEEDS intensely detailed graphics and sound. I'm good with playing Minecraft level graphics if the gameplay is engaging and I keep coming back to it. I know this isn't what they set out to do, and it's probably not their target audience, but Half-Life Alyx does not deserve the hype that it gets or the 10/10 score that a lot of reviewers are giving it.I'd say it's more of an 8/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Half-Life: Alyx is not a bad game. Not even remotely. It has seriously stellar-looking graphics, great gameplay mechanics and a world that feels alive. But I have to say, I wish there was more combat. I kept thinking to myself, “Wow, this place is really ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cool”, but I didn’t really have that many moments where I thought to myself “Wow, I am really ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cool” because I did something neat in combat. Fighting 3 guys off is still a big feat, especially for someone with Alyx’s build and no HEV suit or armor, but it made the game feel a lot less like a Half-Life game. Which I guess is fine for a spin-off title, but it still bugged me a little.Ignoring the combat, there’s still a couple other issues I had with the game: There’s no sprint option for continuous movement, meaning that blink movement was a lot faster than just walking places. On top of that, blink movement is just... Too quick. You’ve probably already seen it, but there’s a sub 1-hour speedrun of the game out already that’s made possible entirely by how ridiculously quick you can teleport in Alyx. It feels like a get-out-of-jail free card during combat, and like an ‘’I’m impatient’’ button outside of it. There’s also an AI director placing ammo that refuses to give you any shotgun ammo unless you constantly purposefully run out of it, which is a shame.On the other hand...Wow. This world feels real. Every single building and area felt like a real place. The way the lighting works, the way physics objects collide – I barely ever had a moment where I had the realization ‘’oh right, this isn’t real’’. Some coffee cups have hitboxes that don’t allow for stuff to be stuffed inside of it, but that’s seriously it. I felt like I was there, struggling to keep myself alive in the face of hordes of antlions or horrifying, horrifying headcrabs.The combat – My god, the combat, especially during the latter parts of the game – There’s so many options! This was a real treat. All the guns are very fun to handle, and I found myself ducking behind cover, summoning bottles to throw in combine’s faces to distract them, or trying to get up close and personal to use my shotgun constantly. It’s just sad that the encounters don’t last that long, and are spaced out quite a bit until the end of the game.If I had to be cliché and put a number on it though, I’d still give this game a 9/10. Boneworks is still better gameplay-wise.

_childDocuments_.review: This game demonstrates both the current limitations and promise that VR has to offer. I have had the HTC Vive  for five years, and Half-Life: Alyx easily is the best experience I have had in VR. I can safely say the Valve Knuckles controllers made the experience great, but I did not try the game on the old Vive controllers. In true Valve fashion, the world oozes over with atmosphere, and every segment has good quality. The hacking puzzles are fresh and take full advantage of the VR. In most games, loading screens are a bit of a drag, but here they were a nice chance to take a pause.The story and pacing echo the first full play through with HL2, and the visual story telling does an excellent job of leading the player in the right direction without too much hand holding. Granted if you're looking for more open-ended game play, you won't find it in HL2. Only once did I manage to solve a puzzle by using the physics, which I think allowed me to skip a small section. The world is well developed, and each time you are refreshed by the lengths to which the game devs went to showcase the capacity of the VR.Two recommendations: (1) Don't cheat yourself by trying to play the non-VR version. We waited 12 years for this game. You can get yourself a proper set up. Valve is throwing down the gauntlet to other studios with this title. (2) Play through the Half-Life franchise first, or you will miss out. Make sure you have a good space to play in and have your tracking dialed in. My two greatest frustrations with this game were hitting the walls of my play area, and having my controller's battery die. Occasionally I had minor tracking issues, but I blame my old HTC vive v1 towers and my setup. The tracking only got me killed one time when my hand glitched through a mine, but otherwise the game quickly reset my position and I continued playing virtually uninterrupted.

_childDocuments_.review: Only a couple of hours in, but Alyx has wowed me in pretty much every way. It also doesn't look like it's going to be a particularly short game, which is great.Basically, this is a must get game if you have a VR setup to play it on.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: I admit, after 13 years of waiting, I thought a new Half Life game could go the way of a Duke Nukem Forever, or a Too Human. It easily could have. Instead, we have a game pushed boundaries similar to how Half Life 1 and 2 did previously. Is Half Life Alyx a perfect game? No. Some puzzles are repetitive, and I ran into a weird frustrating bug around chapter 7 that had me scratching my head longer than I'd like. I am willing to forgive all of that for a game that made me actually reconsider VR as the future of videogames after years of me thinking it was a neat fad. I don't think I have ever felt the level of immersion in a game the same way Half Life Alyx immersed me. I wanted to explore every single nook and cranny. I stopped and I looked around the world, finding every little scrap I could find. I found myself laying down on the floor at points with my VR headset to see if there were hidden items underneath objects (and sometimes there were). .This game manages to balance action, horror, and even humor in an entertaining way. This isn't an easy thing to do, but Valve nailed it. In videogames as a whole, I think pacing is extremely important. This game is not paced like the previous Half Life games before it. It is slow, and methodical. Rarely do you get fights of more than 3 enemies at a time, but those fights feel more intensive than fights between 7+ enemies in the older Half Life games. The combat feels really good, and only feels better as you upgrade your weapons throughout the game. This game also has one of the best 3rd acts I have ever seen in a video gameThe future of Valve is exciting again, and I hope we see more games like Alyx in the future. In my eyes, we got our Half Life 3, now we just have to wait for 4.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: So i used to be sceptical about VR and i didn't like the sounds of a Half Life game exclusive to VR.Then one day i randomly thought i really wanted to try VR so i bought the Valve Index Which included this game.I booted the game up expecting it to be meh and short, what i got was instead blew me away.Never have i been so immersed and tense in a video game.Reloading while a zombie is in your face, ducking away to avoid enemies it's all pretty hectic but so much fun.The controls in this game, aiming, shooting, reloading, interacting with objects all work really well.It's not a short game, i finished the game after 23 hours and if you want more you can download stuff from the Workshop.The story is nice but the ending is pretty vague, most likely on purpose to setup for new games later.I wish everyone could play this game but it's also another reason to get VR in my opinion.This game is great and not some small little game to show off what VR can do no, its a full on Half Life game built for VR.So if you ever get a VR headset and you can play this game on it PLAY it you will not regret it!

_childDocuments_.review: This should be the standard for every VR game to come after it, the VR industry was very dry and very niche for the amount of money you'd have to invest into it. However this game sets a standard for what can be done in VR, This game was one of the best single player experiences i have played in a very long time, VR games have always just been glorified tech demos besides a few games out there (Pavlov, Trover saves the universe, ETC.) but this game while showing off innovative ideas for the future of game design, never ceased to amaze me and pull me closer into the story, I've heard a lot of people complain about it being VR exclusive but if anything that makes the sense of immersion that much more intense, this game gives you a sense of really being there like no other flatscreen single-player game could. Whilst expensive to play when it first came out with the valve index being almost $1,000, playing this game on an oculus quest 2 ran like a dream, sure $299 is still rather expensive but now thanks to HL:A we're seeing new and innovative games being made in VR, beating the stigma that most of the games are just "Experiences".Now that valve is back on track making the games we've all been asking for, i cannot wait for another instalment in the Half Life franchise, and i'm sure it won't take as long as this one did (I hope)9.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Maybe my expectations were to high for this game because of all of the praise it got but for me it's a 8/10 game at best. Sure I recommend it but IMO it's far from a masterpiece like most people label it. The VR aspect is done very well and the physics are great when interacting with the environment, some puzzles were interesting but that's about it. I'm still confused with the praise about the great story and writing. What story? Did we play the same game? There are literally 3 and a half characters in the game (including Alyx) and by the end you don't rly know anything about any of them. Sure there technically is a story but it's nothing to write home about and you don't have any choices or possibilities for a different approach in any situation. It took me 15 hours to finish the game and after about 3 hours you pretty much did everything there is to do so the remaining 12 hours were just repeating stuff in a different location and solving some a bit different puzzles. You only have 3 different weapons with no possibility for dual wielding so they cleverly handled the menu navigation problems by not needing to have menus. That's good for immersion which is excellent but your gameplay stile is very limited. There is also no melee combat which is hard to do right in VR so that is another "clever" solution for that particular problem. All in all it's a good game I just feel like it's overrated for what it is. On the side of VR immersion, environment interaction and physics it laid a solid foundation for future VR AAA games and for that it deserves a lot of praise and it will probably be a benchmark for VR  implementation for some time, everything else is nothing special.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: I never realized how biological the whole thing is. Parts of Xen on earth, Vortigaunts as power generators, the healing and control stations. Holy Crap Valve Well Done, tip of the hat to you. Russian elements are epic as well i must have read every single label and sign. Also my grandpa used to have that bottle opener :). Immersion 10/10. Combat is exceptional at times scary and at times pure adrenaline. I played on Hard and running out of bullets and scavenging only added to the thrill. Combat and Mechanics 10/10.  My biggest anticipation was the story line. I replayed all the previous game right before release of Alyx and was worried that since its a prequel we will not know much new. However yet again, Valve came through and delivered a solid end. Make sure you wait after the credits :PStory 10/10.Much Love to all the people that worked on this, I also think you nailed it.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible.The environments feel so natural.The visuals and emotions you feel while walking around city 17 really make you feel like you've stepped into another world. The zen species is pretty and terrifying. Objects are often destroyed, but it all feels believable. Some events don't happen chronologically all the time; sometimes you have you look around, and suddenly the solution will appear, whether it's a literal change in the environment or an idea comes to you. You seem to play with physics like the other valve games, but it's on a whole new level and feels naturally ingrained within the environment.  The story.The ending is completely unpredictable even hours into the game, yet you always have a set goal in mind as you explore. What you are expecting to find at the end of your journey continues to shift to different expectations until you open your last doorway, and . The story links up perfectly with the other games as well.You are rewarded for exploring.You never know what you can interact with and what you cannot, and often you can not only find useful resources but some comical hidden dialogue that could have been easily missed. The environments are just fun to look at as well.Gameplay. VR is significantly more difficult to navigate, interact, and shoot with, but the complexity is what makes VR fun. The amount of enemies has been scaled down significantly with the other half life games to balance out the difficulty of VR. Your character is also feels much more vulnerable and weaker; if you're careless a single enemy can take all of your life down within seconds if you're standing out in the open. It really seems like the enemies you're fighting have just as much health as yourself, therefore you better be shooting a lot of fast, accurate bullets or hiding behind an object to reload your weapons. The need to strategize is a good thing though.

If you are in the market for VR and the games that it has, this game would be an amazing introduction to the bigger world that is the VR community and industry.
