_childDocuments_.review: So couple of days ago I have finished this game and I gotta say its pretty good. I played it personally with NOVR because I don't have vr headset and I dont have a interest in buying it, of course the real and possibly better experience is to play it with vr since you're not gonna have some of those issues that come with NOVR mod. Still its not bad I had some fun with it and couple of annoying parts that slightly bugged me.+ The graphics look really good.+ The sound design is also pretty good.+ The NOVR gameplay is similiar to Half Life 2 except its slower and encourages more exploration if you wanna find scarce ammo, resin and health+ It's suprisingly fun+ Story is alright but....- NOVR mod is still kinda janky, you often get stuck on props, rails and all kinds of junk. Sometimes you get softlocked forcing you to use noclip, aiming with pistol and smg is janky because it can stay zoomed in if you run out of ammo, the range when you throw grenade is short + it's missing some weapon upgrades, puzzles and other ,,vr'' interactions.- There are some weird changes such as: You cant normally kill antlions, you have to shoot off their legs then their abdomen also they are slow compared to Half Life 2, the antlion workers for some reason look different compared to Half Life 2 episode 2. For whatever the f**k reason there are no fast headcrabs, fast zombies and poison zombies, barnacles are not dying when they eat poison headcrab, different voice actress for Alyx.- There are some retconned things in the story such as the infamous Russell which we don't know if he's still alive after Alyx storyline or not, different looking combines except civil protection, combine weapons being only usable with dna or other transhuman modifications, the zoo area kinda confused me since its couple of years since the combine occupied the earth (the blood on the tiger skull looked fresh imo, zombified zoo keepers can be seen in the area somehow surviving the place infested with the combine and antlions)...etc.- The last 2 chapters where I was fighting the combines and especially strider was tough and really frustrating.So do I reccomend this game? Is it a meme or is actually worth? Vr or NOVR? I'd say yes, I belive that its still worth it. I think its still a pretty damn good game and if I was a vr gamer I would consider it a proper vr game and not gloryfied tech demo. While its not the best Half Life game its still better than Blue Shift and maybe better than Half Life 2 episode 1 but Im still not sure about that.

_childDocuments_.review: Ordered the Valve Index and I was extremely impressed by the visuals on some of the free games already available for it. Once I got used to the controls and what it felt like to be in VR,  I decided to try Half-Life Alyx since it came with the Index.  WOW. I didn't think VR could look better but I was wrong. I literally felt like I was there from a visual and audible standpoint. I felt so immersed in the game at times, I had constantly remind myself that I was in fact in a game. I'm not ok with heights in some cases in the real world, and I could feel myself getting a little antsy anytime there was a risk of falling off a structure or building in the game. Luckily, I'm not one to have issues with VR sickness like I've heard some people have so that was a plus.  The storyline definitely pulls you in, and I hadn't played the other Half Life games before this, but I plan to since playing this one.  Controls were fairly easy to master and game is worth playing through multiple times at different difficulty settings. Even though I got it with the Index, I would recommend buying it at some point if you like first person shooters that have a great storyline.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: If you were ever a Half-Life fan, I don't think you will be disappointed.  Even if you never played Half-Life, you will enjoy this game. The control system is easy to get the hang of, easily configurable and well designed. The game is fluid, the story line well done and pulls you in. I haven't even nearly completed the game yet, just enjoying everything I can experience in it so far! Well done!!!

_childDocuments_.review: HL Alyx is one of the best games in VR at the moment so I can recommend it immediately.- The world quite detailed and very nice for a VR title with a good performance (RX5700XT in my case)- atmosphere is awesome, I am plying on hardest difficulty so it has a bit of horror movie feeling :) Now the bad and what really really dissapointed me.- VR approach by Valve does not include the most modern trend established by Boneworks and Blade & Sorcery- you do not see your body and stuff you pick around you can not be used as a weapon. EG if a headcrab jumps at you, the only option you have is to kill it with gun mid air or avoid it. In boneworks or in B&S you could just hit it with anything you have in your hands even the pistol or shotgun would work... I am really surprised that they didnt follow Boneworks way as they clearly had a collaboration with their team as they had access to Valve Index for quite some time.This is the biggest miss Valve did. BUT despite this dissapointment, Alyx is totally worth to play! Havent finished the game yet, but I had a lot of fun in those 4 hours I played so far

_childDocuments_.review: Whoa boy. Okay, hear me out and read what I have to say.Let me start by saying I wanted to love this game. Genuinely, I did. But there are just so many flaws...Spoilers, by the way...TL;DR at the end.Let's do a good, bad, ugly style of review, shall we?The good:1) Graphics, atmosphere, world build. All of that was fantastic. I really liked the settings, despite them mostly being in doors. Overall, very well done in this regard.2) The audio in general was fantastic. I liked the voice acting and the writing of the dialogue. Albeit, the dialogue between Alyx and Russ was cringy at times, overall it felt realistic and I enjoyed listening to it.3) The gravity gloves felt very nice and fun to use. Not much more to say with that.4) The way thing interacted with each other physics wise was very nice as well. It felt good to smash vodka bottles together and push books off of shelves.That's about it.The Bad:1) You only get 3 weapons to choose from and of these weapons they are not very customizable. Yeah, you get a few upgrades but ultimately the guns end up feeling the same and some of the upgrades are even completely useless (I'll get to that in The Ugly).2) You cannot use multiple weapons at a time, which is a shame because why not have the option to even do so? I get not doing it for tactical reasons but... why not just do it for fun? Why can games that are 1/3 the price of this game funded by one of the biggest gaming companies at least not even include the option to do so?3) The ending... okay, now the ending opens a huge can of worms. I almost wanted to put this in The Ugly but there can be a possible fix with updates/DLCs/expansions. So at the end of the game, Eli no longer dies and Gordon is transported to Eli and Alyx is no longer there... Now this would make sense if this happened in HL2:E2 but it doesn't. HL2:E2 happens in the future, 5 or so years from HLA. Because of this, the ending in Alyx essentially retcons the ending of HL2:E2 until they change it back to the original ending of HL2:E2. 4) The puzzles are insultingly easy and boring. Of the puzzles, a vast majority of them are "move thing to other thing" or "turn switch." Not very many physics based puzzles in a game based on the new Source 2.0 engine. Why not really blow our minds with some great physics puzzles? Very odd, and lazy, game design.5) Enemy AI is terrible. More times than not when I threw a grenade at the Combine they would just stand there and let it explode on their feet. Few times they'd go to cover. I understand why this was done. Because throwing things is hard in VR and they wanted to leave you feeling satisfied after you throw a grenade. However, this design choice cripples the enemy and makes them look like a bunch of incompetent morons, which is strange given how they conquered the Earth in 7 hours.6) No vehicles you can use which is strange given HL2 let you use vehicles and there are VR games that are less than half the price of this game which lets you do so as well. Why the step back? Seriously.7) Not only a lack of vehicles, but a lack of enemy variety. Why have less enemies than the last HL games? Why not have fightable metro police? They have models and animations for them in the game... why the step back again?8) There's not enough resources for you to fully upgrade all of your guns in a single playthrough, limiting what you can do in a game. It's just poor design, especially since the game has such a limited armory for you to use.9) The game is very slow paced. You cannot sprint. You cannot jump. You cannot bunnyhop. You can teleport and that's the only way you can move somewhat faster. Half-Life was all about using speed and the physics of the speed to your advantage. Also, because of this, the enemies are slower too. The antlions just walk toward you and the zombies stumble around like a bunch of idiots slowly shambling toward you because you too are slowly shambling away from them. Do the antlions jump toward you? Nope. Are there fast zombies? Nope. It doesn't feel like a HL game.And here we go. The most important part of this review...The Ugly:1) No melee and limited ammo. This is a HUGE issue with the core design of the game because you can essentially soft-lock (possibly hard-lock) yourself in the game due to a simple lack of resources. I get it, you'd have to be bad or whatever to not have enough ammo throughout the game. Here's the problem: it's a critical flaw in game design when your basic resources might not be abundant enough and you possibly need to restart a level or entire game due to the lack of this resource. Let me give you a scenario. Remember the lightning dogs? They take a lot of hits. They also need to die so you can gather their power source to continue with the game. Let's say you didn't kill the dog. Darn. Just needed one more shotgun shell. Now what? You just stand there and you can do absolutely nothing. Can you grab a brick and smash it to death? Nope. Can you maybe pick up a chair and beat it over it's dumb head until it dies? Nope. Can you use the gravity gloves to shoot a barrel at it (like HL2) to kill it? Nope. Can you take a screwdriver and ram it up it's as- NOPE! You can't do anything except reload the game. And, again, when there are games that cost 1/3 the price that this game does that has melee... why the step backwards? This is Valve with a brand new engine! Why take steps backwards?? WHY?! It makes absolutely no sense.2) Poor weapon design. So there are few weapons as is and there are very few upgrades for your few weapons. One of the upgrades is a reflex sight. Another one is a laser sight. Once you unlock the laser sight, the reflex sight becomes completely useless. 100% useless. There is no point in the game where an enemy is so far away that the reflex sight becomes useful. I get that the reflex sight highlights weak points on an enemy, but seriously, who doesn't think about shooting the damn zombie in the head or the antlion in the brightly glowing abdomen when their heads take no damage from shots? It's just crappy design.3) The objects in an environment is not very interactable. For example, they have a spray paint can which you can shake but you can't spray it... why? Again, this is HLA from one of the biggest gaming companies which produced some of the most ground breaking game technology and they limit what you can or can't do in the game so much. No lighting a cigarette, no lighting a match box, no opening a book and writing in it, there's just so much you CAN'T do. Again, games that cost 1/3 as much has much more interactive props. Why the step backwards???4) Probably the biggest issue is that the game is linear. Super linear. Like to the point where you may as well just be dragged along by your hand by an overly paternal nanny. "Nope, you can't go in that door, it's locked. No, sorry, you can't go through that hole in the wall. Come along now, child. Follow me." Very few times do you actually get to explore a bit. Yes, HL series is linear, but not to this extent. In HL2 you could look for G-Man, find the singing Vortigaunt, that kinda stuff. You don't get to explore like that in this game. Overall just poor level design which leaves the world feeling small. Good world, bad levels.I get it. People love Half-Life. HL2 is one of my favorite games of all time. I wanted to love this game too. Unfortunately, I can't lie to myself. I'm not that kind of person. Even if this game was just $20 made by some no-name company, it wouldn't change what the game lacks and what it could have been. The problem now is that other VR software developing companies will look to Alyx as the gold standard when it really isn't and really shouldn't be. Alyx could have been so much more but it ended up being a mediocre VR game and a terrible HL game.TL;DR 4/10. Hugely overrated game which fails as a Half-Life game and barely makes it as a VR game.

_childDocuments_.review: Simply fantastic. This is truly the most beautiful VR game I've yet played. Ground up for VR makes a huge difference in polish and clunkiness that plagues other titles that are mere ports. Alyx did seem to follow about 60% survival horror, 30% action, 10% puzzles that range from slightly annoying connect the dots to actually puzzling. It is really valve polished, and their style of slow crescendo of skill that builds up to a great action climax in a portal kind of way. I don't feel like it overstayed its welcome, it was a good length for me at 10 hours with enough variety that I never felt it too repetitive but some of the minor hacking puzzles did grate a bit.Valve did what VR is best at, and that is spectacle and scale. Environments always felt alive, sometimes literally, and packed with great vistas and dark corridors.  There is absolutely no reason this shouldn't be at the very top of every VR users wish list.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: This... This is an experience like no other. This wasn't my first venture in VR, but it is definitively hand down the best ever I've had. No other game has immersed me in it's world like Half-Life: Alyx has, dragging me into the protagonist's struggle. It's a definitive breathtaking struggle for the survival of humanity amid a positively heavy hearted world, bringing in the innovation the Half-Life series is famous for; pushing the standards for VR above and beyond anything else before it. The controls and interactions quickly second nature for me as it's artistically sculpted environment led me to wondering around ever nook and cranny for more. The masterfully devised hacking puzzles that typically become an annoyance in games were constantly kept fresh, keeping me entertained rather than bored between scavenging and firefights.

_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Half-Life: Alyx is absolutely brilliant, the developers have played to VR's strengths, and utilised them incredibly well. Unfortunately, as it turns out, many of VRs strengths revolve around terrifying you. Bleak, muted colours to avoid eye strain; small confined spaces to maximise performance; high fidelity, spatially accurate, creepy sound effects to heighten immersion; massive, hairy, spidery, head crabs to facilitate the wetting of your under garments. Yes, HL: Alyx has all of that, and more!  It essentially lays the ground work for how VR FPS games should work.  Also, I've been playing for 25 hours and I still haven't completed the story. I strongly suspect that the game can be won in 3 or 4 hours, but if you're like me and have to crawl at a snails pace, peaking around every corner, bracing yourself before entering every room, then you'll probably get really good value out of the game.  I've just met Jeff and its possible I will never be able to complete the game... That guy... just, no. That's my verdict, awesome game, I recommend it up until Jeff.

_childDocuments_.review: I have an Oculus Rift with me for almost two years. The main game that I play is assetto corsa. Apart from that I couldnt find any main stream games. I recently bough PSVR as they released many action genre games and was planning to sell this. On a fine day, I saw this trailer and I was blown away with the possibilities.But the gameplays released later showed teleporting and I kinda lost my interest. Yesterday I read these comments and foud out that they added free locomotion. To verify that, I saw some reviews and videos and without wasting any time, I added the game to my library. For a AAA game with almost 12 to 15 hours of gameplay, they are charging only 1200 INR which is 16 US dollars. Download was happening at 3.8MB/s due to COVID-19. I had to wait for almost 4 to 5 hours. As soon as I launched the game, it blew me away with the way VR introduced the game titles. I am using a 4 year old computer with zotac gtx 1070 amp extreme, 16gb ddr3 and amd fx8360  and the game auto detected to run it in high settings. To be honest, i was skeptical, but as the game launched, it gave me a frame rate between 60 and 90. And the graphics, it looks photo realistic especially the water on the surface. When you stand on top of a building and look far  away, the draw distance is amazing. People look more like humans with less jaggered edges. The main problem that I had with other racing games is that the edges of world objects and electronic advertisement boards use to flicker. I didnt see any such issues with this game. It looks clean even though the resolution was set to 720p. The way the gun works is perfect. Better than any other shooters like Pavlov vr, firewall zero hour, blood and truth or even super hot vr. Physics is amazing. It is the best part of any half life game. What I didnt like is explosion. very less effects and the smoke disappears as soon as it explodes. Glass pieces disappear after breaking.  These things will be fixed by Valve soon i suppose. Character animation is excellent. Watch the official gameplay here.. 21 partsOne thing I can guarantee you is that the game will keep you at the edge of your seats especially when you run out of ammo ;P Happy gaming!!!

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, I mean just wow.  I mean seriously, do I even need to state how good the game is?  I understand some peoples predisposition against the game since it is VR only, but, you have to experience the game to understand why it fits best in VR and it is worth it.  With a flat-screen version, you would not only loose the deep immersion HLA's atmosphere puts you in, but also a lot of features that would be more tedious and annoying on a flat-screen version are instead fun and exciting in VR.  Valve knew they wouldn't get good feedback if they ♥♥♥♥ out some crap, non-physics based VR cash grab, but this is far, FAR from anything even remotely close to that.  You start off in an incredibly detailed area with an astonishing view, interactable objects everywhere and even in the first moments of the game you get to understand why this is belongs in VR.  On a flat screen version, you can't really feel how heavy an item is, but in here, when you pick up something like a watering can, you can tell the weight difference immediately from a can of soda or a box.  The game so far has had a great story line and a great pace of story development.  Almost all dialogue so far has been enjoyable and not at all immersion breaking and really shows off a lot of Alyx and company's characters.  Moving on to level design, where should I even begin?  Every single room looks as if it has been meticulously designed and had hours upon hours that could rack up into multiple days poured into it.  I can't even put into words how good of a job the level designers did on this game, let alone the entire dev team that worked on this.  If you watched any interview with Robin Walker(or any VNN video related to the topic), specifically the interview conducted by Geoff Keighley, then you would know that they analyzed all of the play testers actions, and learned from what they did.  They changed the game according to how they played and reacted, so every level, every room, every single item that was placed and positioned had the player in mind and how are you going to react to it.  This Resulted in the best level design in a VR game I have ever played, and will be so for years to come.  Please, If you have VR, you NEED to get this title, and please, once you realize how great of a game this is leave a good review too because this will help show the dev team that they need to keep creating outstanding, tremendous games like this [no pressure though dev team :) ]  The only thing I would say that is "negative" is that there are a couple of the bugs at the moment.  For a fully physic based game that just released(and compared to the amount of bugs in the V1 version of HL2 and other VR titles), the amount of bugs that I have experienced so far is low, but there are still some.  There have been a couple of janky things that happen, like dropping something in a certain position or the hands messing up when grabbing certain objects, but these are to be expected in a AAA game that just released, mind you it's also in VR, where the player has a lot of more ways to mess with the game and make a situation where things will be wonky.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: This is by far the best VR game and experience to date across the board.  This is what you call a masterpiece and sets the bar for gaming companies to reach for the next decade.  The passion they put into this game is thrown at you in full force.  It's from people who care what content you experience every moment you are playing.  I was Excited, happy, sad, scared, frustrated, and even laughed out loud while playing the game.  Some parts I got stuck at for like 20 minutes because my dumbass didn't see the clue right in front of me, but would I want to forget that experience?  Not at all!  It was worth the suffering of realizing how dumb you are after you figure it out lol.Alot of games like Talos Principle and Boneworks got me taking breaks from motion fatigue and nausea, but this game...Alyx does it so well that it seems second nature for me to play with no issues or feelings of nausea.   The game has a mix of puzzle solving, horror, action, adventure, and nostalgia that needed to be filled since HL2.   So if you are holding back because of the 59.99 price tag, don't.  You are not going to be dissapointed.  You're paying for one of the true AAA titles out there in line with Mario, Final Fantasy, Call of Duty and what made them famous.  This was a life changing game that should set the bar of all VR games and even regular games I want to experience from now on.If there was any negative concern about this game, it would simply be I can't play other VR games now the same way knowing they could've create an experience like this.  Its like eating the most amazing piece of steak(or vegetable if you're vegan) in a faraway land that you can never go back to and you're stuck with subpar steak at home.  It's like being with that 10/10 partner that you could never find in your life again after that one night stand.   Its like loving Game of Thrones till the last season and now you're like wtf Directors why did you ruin that ending and the last 6 years of my life.Anyways.  Is it worth buying a whole VR set?  Yeah if you have expendable income.  If not, go to a friends and use their VR...but remember COrOnaVIRUS its gonna get ya.  Stay at home plz and wash your hands!

_childDocuments_.review: Like any VR game, its hard to truly put into words what Half-Life: Alyx feels like, you just have to try it. I know that VR isn't widely accessible for a lot of people right now, but my God, you have to find some way to experience this. Not only is it the best looking VR game I've played to date, but it's also an incredibly immersive, satisfying adventure in it's own right. The physics are sublime, the firefights are intense, and the horror has been cranked up to a 10. Remember Ravenholm from Half-Life 2? Imagine walking through that. The dripping of pipes, the moans of zombies, and holding your breathe as a hulking mutant passes right by your face. The VR tech on display here is the future, no exaggeration. What Valve has done here is next level stuff, and I can't wait to see what else they have down the line. Half-Life: Alyx is a prequel, and yet somehow manages to STILL keep you on the edge of your seat for the story even after 13 years since Episode 2. If you have the money, upgrade your PC, get a headset, and prepare for something unlike any game you have ever played in your life.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Sometimes I would spend 20 minutes in an abandoned apartment, pulling open cabinets and drawers, picking up books, VHS tapes, computer keyboards, and utensils, and holding glass bottles full of liquid up to the light and spinning them around so I could see the realistic fluid move around the bottle. Other times, I would try on hats and masks, or try to read from clipboards and papers tacked to bulletin boards. If there was a white board or a window and some dry erase markers, I would draw pictures or write notes, and then realistically erase them with an eraser or my hand. In outdoor environments, I would open all of the cars, step into the back of vans, throw bricks through windows, and pick through trash in dumpsters. Oh, and I guess also shoot aliens, explore terrifyingly dark tunnels and caves with only the blue glow of distant machinery and my flashlight to light the way, and progress through the well-paced, interesting story told through the eyes of Alyx and Russel, whose banter was often hilarious. Really, a very good video game in general, but so far the most engrossing and exciting VR game I have played yet. I hope it's not another 13 years until the next one.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: This game quite clearly has high production value; it looks good and is polished.One of my first thoughts were that Valve really did it. The way the original Half-Life game was the first to take a leap in immersion, this really is the first VR game that has made me feel like I'm there.The combat can be a bit awkward since the left hand is used both for reloading and movement. I also frequently switched away from the gun while reloading it, by accidentally touching the touchpad on the index controllers. Not that great in the middle of combat.All in all, by far the most polished VR game I've played.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is BEAUTIFUL!  I was thinking that my computer wouldn't be able to run it, but it runs VERY well on my setup. _childDocuments_.review: EDIT: Thank you for listening to us Valve. After the update I played all night and had a blast. Now I can 100% recommend this game to everyone, even the leftys!If you are a right handed person I can 100% recommend this game, but until the current control scheme is changed I cannot recommend it to my fellow leftys. _childDocuments_.review: This game was amazing to play overall, but there are a few small annoying things that could have been better. The gameplay is solid and well made, interacting with objects is natural and easy, and the story is easily one of the best I've seen in years for Half-Life.My main gripe is one of the types of puzzles in the game (you'll know which one when you find it), as their difficulty becomes increasingly annoying throughout the game, rather than mentally stimulating. I also did not like how the third weapon you find is essentially just the same as the first one, just with more rounds in a clip. Between this and some small personal annoyances in regards to the mechanics of movement, I think my experience was somewhat negatively impacted.By the final chapter of the game however, this was all thrown out the window. I'd say this game is worth it for that chapter alone. It is by far one of the most impressive scenes I have ever seen in a piece of media ever. The storytelling is really what makes this game amazing, and it is most definitely worth your time if you have the hardware to play it.

_childDocuments_.review: After waiting 13 years for a new half-life game, valve came back swinging. The gameplay is really fun and the story had me invested from the very beginning. The story development with this game is phenomenal and has me questioning everything now. Super excited to see where they go with half life next. However, this game tends to have issues running. My pc is very much fully capable of vr but when i play this game it tends to stutter a lot and drop frames frequently. In a regular pc game this would be tolerable but it being vr, your eyes cant really take that too much and its caused me a lot of pain. Not sure if this is on my end or if its a problem with the game. Overall, if you have the chance to play this game PLAY IT. Its so worth it, but only if you really are into the half life story and understand it.

_childDocuments_.review: I personally can say that i had went back, and enjoyed the old half-life games in the series, and let me tell you... this game is highly recommended by me personally.After Episode 2, i felt a huge loss of words, and now, nearly 14 years, it has all come to a close. I felt actually satisfied for purchasing a $60 game from valve after all that they had failed in with me such as artifact. but not to make this too long on someone looking to purchase the games, lets get to the pros and cons/Pros:-it's half-life, and yes, it sticks to things that have happened and there are nods to things in previous games.-the guns... they feel amazing, they have a level of polish that makes them feel weighty and powerful-Source engine 2-- I had my doubts in it after i was disappointed in seeing what it did for CSGO, but it was great this time!-the characters- despite Guillaume passing unfortunately to cancer, and the recasting of Alyx herself to a new voice actor, which was a conscience decision made by the team, it made the game feel full of younger life especially with how it is timed between Half-life and Half-life 2.-can be ran on a semi-budgeted system! it ran perfectly fine on a GTX 960 4gb with 16gb ddr4 and a ryzen 5 processor.-graphics- coming from boneworks to this feels like a whole new step, or as i can say, taking my headset off, it feels like i stepped into the real world with the graphics even on high fidelity!-exploration was nice, graphics gave this a boost on my list because there are so many things you would be able to see in VR over on just the conventional games with only keyboard and mouse.-you get exactly the time played that you'd normally expect out of a valve game, keep in mind, i have only 8.4 hours at the time of writing this, but im only on chapter 7 out of 11 total chapters.Cons-Low end systems STRUGGLE with this game even on lowest settings.-needs more crowbar... or melee weapons.-i personally took it upon myself to play through the entire series again before playing this, but it is a must to play half-life Episode 2 before completing this game-- still, they did a good job on the twist at the end.-no breen (at all) but there are appearances on magazines... and no kleiner sadly.-linear, but open for exploration-- this lead to times where i was super confused on the puzzles, but after a while i found my way because of exploration and all.consensus:was it worth the time waited? was it well made?yes... very worth it, and it's art for me.

_childDocuments_.review: You can view my full review here: + looks absolutely gorgeous, several epic mini-moments+ runs extremely well, even on my 1060 GTX+ animations & VOs+ attention to detail (e.g. being able to draw on the window or feed pet alien bug through jar)+ lots of settings (teleport, full locomotion, crouch, & comfort options)+ guns are accurate & combat & puzzles are generally fun+ you can interact with lots of objects, physics are really good for the most part+ sound-design is top-notch, environmental details as well+ explosive grenade shotgun upgrade+ tagging walls with a marker or breaking windows with just about anything+ generous auto-saves (you can also manual save)+ satisfying ending+ Steam workshop (great community, adding amazing content post-release)- - jumping / mantling is done in an awful way (forced to teleport at times)- holster weapon or tool by pressing down on joystick / it materializes with press on joystick- stowing ammo by putting it over shoulder- easy to grab wrong item with gravity gloves or accidentally teleport- several items you can't interact with (including some drawers you can't open)- seeing your avatar hands move away from door handles of sliding door- melee combat physics is almost non-existant- loading screens- too linear ... several areas blocked off- mini-puzzles got very repetitive & tedious by the second half of the game- no sprinting (so you have to teleport, at least during this one segment of the game)Those are my initial impressions. I know I wrote a lot of negatives, but this game is definitely awesome and worthy of high-praise. However, it's not perfect and some of those negatives are rather disappointing and unexpected. Still, this is one of the best games in VR and a must-buy if you own a VR headset.Anyways, I will update my review if needed.EDIT 11/25/2020 - nominated for GOTY 2020. Steam Workshop is excellent.

_childDocuments_.review: Yes.Only 8 hours in but I dread the end coming, the story is perfectly implemented, the references to older material are spot on, the puzzles, combat, and exploration are on point and the VR is the best I've ever seen. Consider the standard set - bring it on games industry.EDIT: I felt like posting this edit to mention some of the flaws I found - with the understanding that this is one of the best games I've ever played. These are my nitpicks:- The enemy variety is rather lacking, it consists of roughly the same (and less) roster from Half Life 2. With a backlog of bad guys as rich as Half Life I would have liked to see more diverse opponents (creatures namely).- The enemy AI is not the most intelligent, while I think this is good as it warms VR newcomers into the intensity of combat, I'd like to see a very hard or optional AI difficulty slider for those of us that have mastered the combat and are looking for a tense experience.- The lack of any melee combat what so ever is disappointing - while I understand why I would have liked to have seen that for this entry.- NO SPOILERS the final confrontation battle was a little lacking, I wish the player was more involved in the fight than they are.- I would have liked to have seen a few more weapons, while the low number makes it easy to track and the upgrades do help, I can think of several iconic and interesting weapon variations that would make sense in the game, that I am sad didn't make it in.REGARDLESS - it's the most engrossing VR experience money can buy and I highly recommend it to anyone with a headset. I also recommend playing with continuous movement if you can stomach the motion because it grounds you in the world much better than teleporting.

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend for HL fans only, tbh, and on a steep sale. It's one of the best-looking VR games and an evolution of HL's iconic industry-defining physics, but that's kinda where the praise stops. The head crabs are the main enemy and incredibly boring or frustrating to fight and I never find ammo for the guns I actually like. There aren't enough enemies that shoot back, so there's rarely an actual firefight. There are so many small setpieces that feel like they're trying too hard to impress you with the physics and VR-ness, when I already got my fill of "oh wow i can pick up things and wave them around" in the opening level. It feels more like an extended VR Experience™ or an It's A Small World ride that's just throwing every idea they have at you, and while most of them are slam-dunks, it runs out of steam surprisingly quickly.It's a good game, an important game for VR. But other games that cost less and weigh less and lag less have gone on to do everything ALYX did better. Maybe if I actually cared about HL I'd be more upbeat about it.

_childDocuments_.review: 8 hours playtime, amazing puzzles and interesting combat. The scenery was breathtaking, interactions with the world plentiful - and the story delivered!The sense of presence is virtually realized to a higher degree than I have seen before. Contact between your hands or weapons and surfaces feels right, besides the occasional technical hiccups. Reaching into cupboards, using magnetic gloves to pull and grab objects, moving chairs out of your way even though you don't need to, all convey a believable world and my being within that world.How the combat utilizes the environment is fitting for VR, with the obvious explosives placed near your first encounters and grenades lying about for easy use in the heat of a firefight. The enemies require a low enough reaction to avoid confusion and dizziness, but can pressure you in many situations. Headcrabs will spend a small amount of time to line up their jumps, which allows you to get out of the way or line up a shot - but in a pressured situation you may still be taken by surprise. This balance is immensely important in VR, allowing the player to regain some composure and not requiring frantic reactions to every enemy. The enemies are varied enough to keep each encounter interesting despite the obvious optimal strategies for engagement.From Alyx Vances appartment to the collapsing City 17, and the crate filled corridors in between, the scenery contains surprising navigation, use of scale and vertical movement perfect for VR. Moving through Zombie filled territory, Combine controlled city streets and Ant Lion caverns (interspersed by a lovely intimate encounter with Jeff), is a delightful return to the world of Half Life. I was surprised at the detail and variety of environments while the writing kept me pushing through each loading screen with a thirst for more.But the one thing I am most excited about is the ending. True to the Half Life formula, and with some mind boggling consequences for future installments (?), I was giggling through the final battles and was loving the twist to the established mechanics.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; I recommend this game to anyone who has a VR Headset. Even if the price is a sticking point right now and you wait for a sale or for the price to eventually drop, I recommend buying it when you can afford to. I believe that everyone that has a VR Headset should try this game.My experience was with an Oculus Rift S/Touch Controllers, with Sennheiser CX 100 In-Ear Earphones and Room Scale Movement. Graphics Settings were set to the highest option available within the game (No external graphics enhancements applied). I was Playing with Smooth Turning Enabled and Smooth Walking (Coupled to head orientation) as my method of movement and turning with the Right hand as my Weapon Hand.As of version 1.2 which released on 29th March 2020, there was a patch to fix left-hand/right-hand movement control configurations which were a sticking point for some players. A good portion of the negative reviews I was seeing before buying was for the game was about this, I feel it would be good to mention it has been addressed. As I understand it, players can now adjust which hand is used for movement and which is to be used for turning however they wish. Visually it is amazing as VR Games go. The visuals are so smooth and crisp. The headset you are wearing feels like it has a higher resolution when playing this game. It amazes me how just the game that is being played on the headset can swing the visuals so heavily. I imagine it looks stunningly lifelike with the Valve Index.The Audio is excellent. Spacially you get a strong sense of where sounds are coming from, and the weapon audio all feels powerful and authentic. Music throughout the game really helps to set the tone for scenes, including the lack of it in certain instances. The Voice Acting so far has been very well done, with some comical dialogue to ease the tension a little bit as the game progresses.With regards to mechanics and gameplay, I really enjoy the Gravity Gloves. They effectively give you a sort of Telekinesis and can summon objects to your hands. It takes a bit to get used to the motion, but once it's down pat, it comes as second nature. It's enjoyable to just do this to the various pieces of debris that are around as you move through the game, and it is implemented well for progressing the game. Sometimes there is Ammo across the room or through a broken window, and you can't approach it. Or there are Barnacles (Enemies which tether anything passing by and pull them up to eat them) blocking the way, and you pull an object from passed them to distract them.The Hacking tool, or "Alyx Tool" as Alyx calls it, is a neat implementation on puzzles/hacking. I believe I haven't seen all of the possible puzzles that are possible with it yet. Still, it is an elegant and refreshing implementation of puzzles that involve 3D space and positional hand tracking, which some games don't do well.Some scenes offer a decent level of tension. The game introduces you to new challenges and enemies in a way that you can understand how they work before you are then expected to deal with them on the fly. So far, these initial encounters haven't felt forced or felt like tutorials which pull you out of the rest of the game, which I believe has been well executed.The gunplay is nice, but not amazing like in some other games. Given that this game isn't aiming to focus heavily on gunplay, I think the gunplay is decent for the game. The guns feel, look and sound powerful with upgrades that are available to them as the game progresses to make them more practical or more effective. It is also clear that care was taken with their design to make it seem realistic and possible to be using them in just one hand, which I really liked. I've only found the first two guns, and I don't know how many there will be by the end, so this may change as I find more.One criticism I have is that once weapons are equipped, that hand has a gun in it until it is unequipped, it can't be "dropped" or put away without using a button/toggle. I find this a bit annoying because as I am not actively "holding" the gun in my hand at all times when it is equipped, my hand feels free to use. I find that I try to use my right gravity glove instinctively but can't as my hand is occupied with a gun. Unequipping weapons is easy enough, but it takes a moment of thought to do it, which doesn't feel natural at the moment.In terms of the levels, I personally feel they are a bit short, but I am still earlier in the game, and this could change later through it. I imagine this is intentional to offer frequent enough step off points for those players where VR can quickly start getting uncomfortable. I feel like each level so far has taken about 10-15 minutes to complete, maybe 20 if I am spending more time than necessary messing with the environment or investigating. I haven't timed this, and my guess on times could be way off. All I can really say is that when I hit a new loading section, I find myself thinking "already?".I like to consider myself to have strong VR legs, and prefer experiences that have fewer comfort options. This game has a lot that can be changed or disabled which is good. Some are built-in and can't be changed.Falling is artificially slowed down to make it more comfortable for players and less nauseating. For me, this feels unnatural and almost has the opposite effect of making me feel nauseous.Even with smooth walking enabled, there is a teleporting/jumping mechanic which allows you to teleport short distances, which is useful for getting over walls or obstacles in the game. Personally, I would prefer a genuine jumping mechanic, but I can live happily with the teleport implementation.All in all, from my experience, I feel like this game is an example of what a single-player narrative-based game for VR should aim to achieve. What it does, it does well enough in all areas to be a one size fits all experience that almost anybody can pick up and play. The parts that make this uniquely a VR game stand out strongly enough to appreciate that it is a game made for VR. This isn't a game that was designed initially and the ported with some quick VR implementation. I would recommend that everyone who owns a VR Headset or has access to one should at least try this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: HL: Alyx is everything I dreamed a VR game would be.The attention do detail is wonderful and makes the experience so much more immersive. So it's not Episode 3 really, but it's a return to City 17 in all its glory. _childDocuments_.review: I have several thousand hours in VR across the DK1, DK2, Vive, and Index. VR is a new medium and it's very easy to screw up, compared to traditional gaming, by failing to adapt gameplay mechanics and design choices to it. The best VR games to date have learned a lot of lessons from the games that came before, and plenty of games failed for not bothering to learn those lessons. This includes games from AAA developers who ignore best practices from the nascent VR indie scene, thinking they know best, and pump out a game no one bothers to stick with because it feels like a lazy 2D game ported to VR. This is not true for HL: Alyx. Not only did Valve quietly listen and study the burgeoning VR scene, learning what works and what doesn't, they refined and improved upon the very best the pre-Alyx VR community was able to come up with. Every mechanic, map layout, type of interaction, the design direction, the way NPC interactions are handled, the way gunfights are structured, the different options and schemes given to the player... all fit together perfectly to make the most of the medium and elevate it to new heights. Valve took the best the indie scene had to offer and polished the crap out of it. I've never had a better experience in VR, from beginning to end, than HL: Alyx. It will sell you on the viability of VR as an entertainment medium. On top of all of this, as if I couldn't praise the thing enough, Alyx is a solid Half-Life game with sharp writing and brilliant set pieces to boot. It adds depth to the universe and is in no way unnecessary or gimmicky in its use of VR as telling the story from the PoV of a character who isn't a supersoldier with an HEV suit but a nimble survivalist who scavenges and picks her fights wisely. VR necessitates a pacing and style of gameplay that doesn't fit into the established 2D conventions for the franchise and HL: Alyx only benefits from this. I can't wait to see what the modding community cooks up once the Workshop is up and running. Thanks again, Valve, for entertaining me as thoroughly as you did back in '98 with the first Half-Life. This is the company and the franchise that pushes hardware and software boundaries to tell new types of stories and innovate, technologically and artistically.  Compared to pancake games, the minimum system requirements vs maximum system requirements mean something very different. In HL: Alyx, any bottleneck be it CPU, GPU, or memory can make the game unplayable if you don't account for it in the settings. In my case, I was well above the recommended specs (on a Valve Index) but the game was borderline unplayable until I swapped my 1x16GB single channel DDR4 @ 2133MHz for 2x8GB dual channel DDR4 @3200MHz. From all the profiling I've done and observations I've made, performance issues are usually the fault of the hardware rather than the game itself and I suspect in my cases, down to people with beefy rigs cheaping out on RAM. I recommend giving your rig a twice over before running the game, it may not be as powerful as you think!

_childDocuments_.review: If you have a SteamVR compatible headset already, you should purchase this game.If you DON'T have a SteamVR compatible headset, but you live in a country where it's not absurdly expensive, you should get the headset and the game.No matter how long it takes you to play it, you should hold off on spoilers and experience this game for the first time through personally experiencing it. I'm about two and a half playthroughs deep into the game, and I feel like I could still have fun going through it three more times. The arsenal is a little lacking, and I think the game does a bad job at advertising the fact that it SEEMS to use a Left 4 Dead-esque director system to supply you with the ammo you need, so you might end up foregoing the shotgun entirely when you don't have much ammo for it, but they're fun weapons to use and the combat is a blast if you have the space to move around virtual cover.Unfortunately, there's no implementation of melee combat, and thrown props don't seem to deal any damage, which I consider to be a serious missed opportunity, but as long as you go into it expecting it to be more focused on exploration and storytelling as opposed to extremely innovative VR combat, you'll be fine.The environments are a little lacking in color, but Source 2 looks (and runs) fantastic in VR, and its cluttered rooms are a blast even just to explore.

_childDocuments_.review: "This game is a Half-Life." How many times have I repeated this phrase to myself?Wait, Is this game really a Half-Life?Here's my review of the game as a veteran of the Half-Life franchise (I first finished the first installment in 2003, I finished all the games on PC and consoles a lot of times)./!\ Warning, massive spoilers.The 13 long years of waiting for HL2:EP3 or HL3 ends with the release of a so-called prequel in VR that no one asked for.We start with an affront to the fans, how could this end well?Here are the few positive points that I could identify:The game has (kinda) beautiful graphics, thanks to the Source 2 engine and a pleasant physics engine.The puzzles are well thought out although too numerous and redundant.The weapon improvement system via "resin" is nice.The Gravity Gloves as useful and versatile as the Gravity Gun.The characters are charismatic, and can have a serious or humorous tone.The music composed by Mike Morasky is appreciable, very electro and industrial, but is not as great as those of HL1 and HL2.The sounds are very interesting, intriging, engaging and contribute to immersion.City 17's Half-Life Alyx version is very classic, detailed, and great to look at and to explore.But the list of negatives is quite heavy:- Armament:Ammo is too scarce so every bullet counts.The enemies are too resistant compared to the weapons we have.Only 3 weapons! I hadn't seen this since SiN Episodes: Emergence!Some Combine Soldiers have weapons that cannot be picked up (probably because they are two-handed).- ScriptThe story is too vague and has little connection to the rest of the series.It really seems like the devs only had a vague knowledge of the lore.Very few elements of HL2 Beta are recycled when there really is plenty to do.The paranormal / gore side is way too exacerbated...Where is Dog? He is supposed to protect Alyx since her childhood...Where is Breen? Where is all the propaganda?- BestiaryIf the bestiary is quite varied, but how to legitimize its disappearance before the events of Half-Life 2?We had the same problem with the Race-X in Opposing Force long before...The new enemies are not fun to fight for several reasons.The Armored Headcrab is armored on top and only its ventral part is vulnerable.The different Combine Heavy Soldiers are very resistant and their weapons hurt too much, even from afar. Like I said, we can't take their guns. They are similar to the Heavy Replicas from F.E.A.R. ...The Antlion Soldiers are armored, they have to be dismembered so that you can shoot into their abdomen, causing them to explode!Ditto for the Antlion Workers, except they spit a painful blue acid that coats the screen...The worst of the worst from Half-Life Alyx's bestiary:The Lightning Dog (Reviver): A kind of electric Headcrab that, in addition to electrocuting you and being resistant, can take control of corpses like the Remnant from F.E.A.R. 2 and land powerful attacks."Jeff": A unique, blind, but not deaf zombie. I have no words, how to say... Why does such an abomination exist in the Half-Life universe? Who could validate this stuff?- SceneryIf the city, on the surface is pleasant, it is not the same for the undergrounds, moreover too numerous. You will become claustrophobic.The interiors are massively covered with a kind of biomass, dirty as possible, sometimes explosive. There too, we are closer to F.E.A.R. 2 for example.The last chapter is closer to Portal 2. What is the visual affiliation with Half-Life 2?- DubbingThe game is only dubbed in English! Seriously! After dubbing the old Half-Life games in loads of languages!However, it is subtitled in a few languages, even if it's easy to understand in the original version.- Bugs:I found myself several times and easily outside the map not knowing where to go...We regularly find ourselves blocked everywhere for no reason.Sometimes I can't grab ammo because it's stuck in the floor.- ConclusionHalf-Life Alyx is for me a HUGE disappointment, as Half-Life games are legendary.The ending of the game clearly calls for a sequel to HL2 Episode Two.The game being what it is, Half-Life 3 could be ruined.Better for Valve not to make it, and let's keep its legendary aura.In the meantime, I'm going back to Half-Life 2 Beta.

_childDocuments_.review: The wait... The wait was over, and after all the time that passed there was a small glimpse of what's to come, a small blip in a dark void that all of us where looking for.  It was a shocker that after all that a new technology was necessary to play it. Most of us took the leap and OH BOY... was it worth it. The game puts you in the center of it all like never before. Valve staying true to their nature made a big leap in technology but this time it was way beyond mere graphics. A whole new world to interact with, in a way that few of us ever dreamed. The graphics, the tone of the world, the sheer sense of dread and scale like never before. Free to roam, touch, interact with the environment in an organic and natural way. The game while slow paced, makes you feel like you are there a part of it, and It a part of you. The story is polished with a few throwbacks here and there to present day endings of the half life universe, but you are in the past well before any of it happened. Stunning art stile and comic value in the Valve way made the game ever more enjoyable, and the puzzles with the new mechanic where a pleasure to solve. This and many more encounters like Jeff, antlions, Vortigaunts, and Gman where jaw dropping seeing them close to you, almost like you could touch them. Valve in their usual way came and Raise the "Crowbar" again with stunning animations and visuals that will have people talking about them for years to come, Just like the demo the Source engine had, blowing people away with it's features. Was it a long wait? YES... oh god, yes... Was it Worth it? Honestly if I where to have to wait another good chunk of "valve time" for Half life 3 or any other Half life related games, with this kind of quality and polish, I would gladly accept. Thank you Valve for keeping us entertained and ensnared in this universe that you created, let no corner be unchecked, no rock be unlifted, no Gnome be left unlaunched and no Crowbar left behind. Looking forward to Doctor Freeman's return.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: I have been thinking a lot about this game, and after playing through it for about 6 hours, I learned its what VR needs. There are things for you to search for, open up drawers and look inside stuff. I did not grow up as a half life fanboy, but this game makes me want to be one. Its a very well made VR experience, that you should expect from AAA developers. If you are on the fence, I say, give it a shot. The atmosphere itself is worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: It’s absolutely the best VR game I've ever played and it's a real Half-Life game. It doesn't feel like a queue TV spin off for a tech demo or a waste of time. Devs go all in on this and Valve is really here doing great things. If you're extra sensitive the game does have surprises around basically every corner, so be warned! I would say if you can't play it on the VR, You should try to watch a good play through online, maybe like preferably someone not screaming over it. Because it is really good and really immersive even still if you watch it.I think you can play Half-Life: Alyx on most PC based VR headsets and my friend played it via an oculus quest plugged into his PC via the oculus link. It works pretty flawlessly with some dropped frames, but it was fun. He finished the game in less than 5 hours and he was satisfied ;D So, about Half-Life: Alyx: 11/10  I highly recommend it if you have the means. The one thing I didn't expect is like maybe I had way too high of expectations, but Half-Life: Alyx  doesn't really reinvent the wheel, well.. you know.. at least not in some ways. The movement options are all there and each one works pretty great. I chose to move around freely with the joy stick on my touch controller and snap left and right if I need to change directions. That's pretty advanced for the average user, of course!! And I feel great.Once you get used to moving around and you get the magic gravity gloves which allow you to grab stuff from a distance, which is definitely the ace here!!! This is where Valve got really clever because it solves the problem of.. well.. you know, tediously picking stuff up, and it's so much fun. It makes things so much less tedious and thankfully the tracking is really great for everything else.The AI isn't over the top to be honest I think many sequences of the game are a bit on the easy side, but not terribly so and thankfully the game does get harder as it goes. On the second half really picks up.

_childDocuments_.review: FIRST: For me, this is one of the best games ever made and definitely GOTY 2020Why:  - It is technically (almost) flawless and extremely complex at the same time - The graphics are better than anything seen in VR and considering the resolution and frames of the game also one of the best graphics in gaming to date - This game is polished to (almost) perfection. No crashes, and just 1 or 2 Bugs over the entire campaign. It's so refreshing seeing a game that is polished to perfection on release and not a month later  - An amazing story, especially within the HL-Universe  - NO MICROTRANSACTION, on the contrary, we have gotten a few great updates from Valve like amazing "water-physics" (which are actually just textures) and over 3h of great developer-commentary  - The Workshop-Tools for this game allow even someone with no coding-knowledge and 3d-Modelling to use all in-house tools of Valve to create his own Levels and even other addons (although you need to learn some code for addons). For people like me this means that we have amazing freedom to create almost everything while for people just playing the game, content for the game will increase because of the community itselfand so much more...

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start by saying that the game looks fantastic - very well done.  VR controls are fine. I can't comment on the gameplay too much because I keep crashing to desktop during one of the first levels (where you meet Eli Vance / holomap) so I can't continue.  Tried rebooting, reinstalling, set to low settings and CPU crashes every time at that spot. Running 6700k, GTX1080, 32 gig ram, 250 gig SSD - not the best out there but I figured it should run Half Life Alyx ok. There also seems to be a lack of some VR options such as the ability to adjust player height which is not the end of the world but at the price I paid, I'm a little disappointed.  I'll try to Google a fix or workaround to get passed the CTDs and I'm sure I'll eventually figure it out but, for the price of this game, I shouldn't have to do that.I'm very sad to NOT recommend this game based on my experience but as it stands, I simply can't advise anyone to purchase this game based on the CTDs. I would suggest waiting for sale or wait for a few patches to get the game up to par to its price tag.Update: Seems like I'm now able to play for a few hours without the game crashing. What I've done so far to try and remedy the issues is: made sure graphics drivers were up to date, updated .Net Framework, disabled anti-virus (Norton), checked file integrity and of course rebooted after all of that was done. So far so good.Update 2: Welp, although I was able to play a few hours at a time without crashing and managed to get through several levels,  I am once again unable to progress as the game is consistently crashing in the same mission (Jeff mission). Not sure what to do at this point other than wait for a patch. I would definitely wait a few months before purchasing to give the devs some time to iron out all of the problems.Update 3: After the last few updates, the game now crashes constantly after a few minutes of game play regardless of graphic settings or save file. I actually made a clean install of Windows and updated the graphics card drivers and still no go. Very good attempt visually at a VR game but very poor implementation.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd say as a VR game in itself, this is a Middle of the Road experience, but that does NOT make it bad. If you have played Half-Life 2 (or GMod) and know how the physics work in that game, HL:Alyx has the same object properties as HL2 but with added weight in your VR Hands for immersion, In terms of that though just like HL2 throwing objects at enemies will not be effective at all. (aside from stunning 'em for a small bit) They gave Headcrabs some ragdoll physics for when they jump at you, but that's all that comes to VR physics in HL:Alyx. There are no VR Body physics (like BONEWORKS) you pretty much play as a floating head with two hands and you just point and shoot things, pick up and throw objects, teleport or mantle on top of things, and move around in walking pace. (game was originally teleport only) The Upside to playing as a partial body is that it will make the game accessible to many people because there's no things that can knock you down to force you to lay down and there's no slippery movement BS because you have no legs that could put you off-balance. It lessens any potential to make you sick and leaves room to make the game more accessible, Few examples being; an option for one handed mode, the option to change your 'weapon hand', the ability to press a button to adjust your stance position (to crawl, crouch, and stand while sitting down), the option to have barnacles not lift you off the ground, and difficulty settings so you can choose if you want the game to be a bit more simple and *less* stress inducing. (its not going to take it away completely, there's fing headcrabs in the game)Having a partial body instead of a full body though shows you how much more physical the game could've been but the game isn't just shooting things that may or may not shoot back, there's a Story in this game.The Story is pretty captivating and it doesn't try to bore and slow you down too much, when it does it most of the time is trying to show you something new. And if you do like HL:Alyx's gameplay there is Steam Workshop Mods that either slightly modify the existing story or add new maps and entire campaigns. I feel like that alone makes this game worth getting. The only dumb thing about the Workshop though is that half of the mods there are for HL:Alyx or they are assets for S2FM which will make adding mods to the game a bit more harder, however they did recently add some much-needed filters that will help you find the mod(s) you're looking for.VR Game 'Essentials' have been changing a lot and while claiming what games should be a must-play for VR users is subjective, I do think this game is in that category for must-play if you buy a VR Device.

_childDocuments_.review: This has lived up to the hype. This is possibly one of the most polished VR experiences I have ever had. Interestingly, there aren't any singular points that stand out as revolutionary. Where this game truly stands out is as a the fusion of so many things done right. The attention to detail is astounding. Movement, gun play, graphics, sound design, story (good gosh the story is great!), character design/voicing, etc. All of it is top notch. If you have VR already, I highly suggest you get it immediately. Even if you don't have VR yet, this game may shape up to be the turning point in VR. When Valve gets their tools out, I think we could see a golden age of VR content. At any rate, I look forward to what the future of Valve, VR, and Half-Life has in store.

I haven't even finished it yet, as I am trying to savor every moment of it, but it is already one of my favorite games of all time. A MUST-BUY for anyone with a VR headset.

_childDocuments_.review: Finally! A new Half Life story with such a great ending! I may have cried a little, but I ain't no b!7ch! This game hits you right in the nostalgia and doesn't let up. As a Half Life fan, I was very pleased with the narrative and the expansion of the universe. I am very much looking forward to the sequel that hopefully doesn't take another 13 years. That being said, I do not think this is a perfect 10/10 experience. I believe the experience with this game was a little too tame for VR. Personally, I find Boneworks to be superior in the gun-play and "environment interactivity" department. The biggest problem I had with this game is there just was not enough shooty shoot for a Half Life game. I wanted to go ham blasting Combine and this game just doesn't have it. I also had a problem with how the guns worked. Not being able to freely trade my gun between hands was annoying for me. I need to throw a grenade with my right hand, because my left is trash. I also shoot with my right, so I had to stop shooting and put my gun away to pull out a grenade when I'm perfectly capable of shooting with my left and throwing a grenade with my right. I don't want to shoot with my left all the time though, because it doesn't feel right and I know I'm not as accurate. The other issue I had was that all of the guns were too easy to use with one hand. They were all designed like they're pistols that are fully automatic or shoot shotgun shells. I just hate that. Some of you may agree, some may not. It's okay.The Gun inventory was also a little too basic to me. Using this lame menu to switch between 3 guns was a little annoying. This is Half Life! Gordon carried like 10 different weapons in Half Life 2. I hope the sequel doesn't only leave us with 3 main weapons.  I'm sure Valve could be a little more creative with the weapon Inventory. You could seriously have a gun carrying drone follow you around. knowing Valve, it would provide some comedy relief during a shoot-out while it tosses you the guns you requested. Your person could carry 4-5 guns and the drone can carry the extra. Just spit-balling here.Don't get me wrong, I love this game and the Half Life narrative. In spite of my critiques, I very much love this game. It's pretty obvious at this point there will be a sequel, so hopefully they have a more complete experience coming that will address my concerns. Do I think this is worth $60? No, but I'd still buy it anyways. I bought the Valve Index just to play this game and I would do it again.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best gaming experiences I’ve ever had, and by far the best VR game going. Half-Life games have always pushed gaming forward and Alyx is no exception. The level of detail in this game is astonishing, the gameplay too, and the story is sublime. I’m excited for the next Half-Life instalment. I just hope it doesn’t take another 13 years. _childDocuments_.review: Makes you wish for a Rift or Vive if you don't already own one. Makes you wish for a Valve Index if you do.Everything in the trailers is 100% in game and true, just remember that in order to have the scenes reenacted, you yourself have to act it out for you are the actor. The game's level of immersion therefore completely depends on how committed you are, and the game does a very good job on incentifying the player with its storytelling techniques that are unique to video games.Gameplay wise, of course it is a Half-Life game, but there are a few modern touches here and there. Runs marvelously on my Rift CV1 and 2080Ti.This is the next step for VR.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: This is how it's supposed to be done.Best VR game yet.The physics in this game are at the top of the class. There's no jankiness in the physics at all. The developers must have spend  of time tuning the physics engine. Opening doors, moving boxes with your pistol hand, lobbing objects through windows - it's all so effortless and intuitive. I can't recall a single a frustrating moment while playing this, and I'm an easily irritable dude.The graphics and the audio are both atmospheric and imposing. The visual storytelling is so inviting it took me at least fifteen minutes to leave the very first few rooms in the game. It took me a bit over 10 hrs to play through this game and now I feel empty inside. There are no other VR games of this caliber to scratch this itch.

_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Just want to start by saying I didn't get this game because I'm a huge Half-Life fan, I have played the first game early 2019 and enjoyed it, but i got it because it looked like an exciting entry into the VR marketplace. I can only talk about my experience from an hour of playing, and wow... after an hour I've only just received the first weapon. I'm one of those that looks for immersion and world building above all else and I was not disappointed. The physics in this game are way above anything else I've experienced in VR. The walking dead, saints and sinners being the game I've played the most, and I love that game,  but there are so many more way to interact with the world in half life, for example I noticed there were at least three way to hold a mug.this may not sound game-changing but in VR had this extra level of detail in how you interact with the world makes a huge difference when talking about keeping the player immersed.the environments invoke curiosity, and that curiosity is rewarded, whether its seeing a creature in a jar reacting to me trying to feed it, pigeons flying away as hurl a barrage of bottles at them or picking up a newspaper and finding out it's full of interesting information about how the world got to where it is.The attention to detail and graphics are also significantly better than other games I have played and its a comfortable experience. As mentioned before I read a newspaper I found lying about on a bench! again this may not sound incredible but similar tasks in other VR games have been far too hard on the eyes, text often seeming blurry up close, or just hard to read. I'm not saying this was like reading a book in-person, but I'm running this on a laptop through Oculus Link on the Quest and it just looks great.10/10 would recommend, Vr enthusiast will be charmed and I imagine Half-Life fans will not be disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: $60 for a 12 hour AAA experience. It's a great game with great visuals, but it's far from the most replayable game. I got this game from a deal where you get it free with a Valve Index hardware purchase, when I bought my Valve Index controllers. It also has been included in a few other bundle deals, like the Vive Cosmos Elite. Definitely look around for the best offer before buying this.That said, it's a $60 purchase you won't regret. It's a must-have experience based solely on the visuals and the amount of interactables. The Index finger tracking grip is under-utilized to allow you to gradually crush soda cans, but at least it's used. The game has a lot of locomotion options, but teleport is unfortunately necessary to jump gaps and climb some ledges. The gunplay feels good despite the missing player body, and the only real nitpicky thing I have is the way the Alyx character is nice really shown at all aside from her hands and her voice. It would be nice to have some full body awareness going on here, but this game is more focused on being beginner-friendly than being immersive. The overall expierience is great as long as you don't mind the simplicity.There are mods. I haven't touched mods yet. I plan to... someday.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game using the quest 2 with oculus link. While higher end vr headsets would make this game look amazing, i still felt this game looked stunning. In normal games, I wouldn't want to continue, but the game play made we want to keep exploring and go through those moments. The details are incredible in this game. I highly recommend for any vr user.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: I'm gobsmacked...This isn't a game. It's a piece of art. I'll just say it now, Half Life: Alyx is by far the best VR game ever created. Nothing comes close to the level of perfection this game has reached. I think this game is proof that if given enough funding and an amazing team you can make a truly life changing VR game. The game take about 8-12 hours, maybe longer and the cost may put people off but you're not paying for a game. You're paying for an experience. After all these years, playing half life 2 and it being a childhood favourite of mine and finally after so long getting some answers. Not sure what Valve's intentions are but with this game they set up Half Life 3 in what may be a marketing masterpiece. Always imagine half life 3 being the same as half life 2 in controls and style and what not but now I'm not so sure what I want. In all honesty I'd be trilled to see Half life 3 be a VR game. Considering what they did with game I'm sure they could potentially make it the best game of the century. If you have a VR you need to buy this game. You'll fall in love.

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome Game!!One of the best VR experiences yet, and another great game in the Half-Life series.The physics and sounds for the objects you interact with are really well done. From the way they move, to the sounds they make when shaking or throwing them.The detail and textures in the environments is stunning. From the way different things reflect light, to all the micro detail on everything.While this game is amazing in VR, it probably could still work without VR, but it would likely be a bit less interactive.Spoiler for something I didn't like about the game: Great game overall.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Half-Life: Alyx is the new gold standard for VR, and one of the best games I've ever played. But keep in mind, there is a problem with it... for $60 I beat the game in 10 hours. There isn't much replay value unless you like to speed run or try different difficulties. If you just want to know how the story continues in Half-Life, you're paying $60 for 10 hours of game play and story. At $6 per hour of game play and the average theater visit being 2 hours ranging from $15-$30 this can be worth it. But if you're hoping to play this for a long time, understand that you'll be disappointed. It's short, but a golden experience from start to finish.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Alright to start thing off i must say i am one of those people who were not even in their teens when we got our last cliffhanger ending where we had Eli Vance killed,so a long awaited sequel to my favourite game series is something i've been waiting for...well 12 years.And now that the game is out and having played it from end to finish in rougly 13 hours what do i think about it?Well all around....it's amazing.I don't think i will easily forget the way i felt when i first booted up the game and saw city 17 in a way i never had before.I will never forget the way i felt when i saw a train crash or have a tall chimney fall for what feels like 20 meters away from you...it really just goes to show why valve has invested so much in VR,this experience just can't be achieved by any other means.I played on the VIVE and got the hang of the controls pretty quickly,the only thing i had trouble with was the different buttons/triggers for different weapons which was confusing before you get some muscle memory in,but hey they did create it primarily for the knuckles controllers so i am more than impressed with the performance of my hardware.The gameplay itself is fun and immersive.The different multi-tool puzzles are a lot more intuitive and developed than i even expected and with them being randomized each time they don't get old.The graphics along with the long awaited Source 2 engine are phenomenal,at the end of the day they're the reason i took so long to finish the game it was just really difficult to seperate me from looking at russel's highly defined carpet to every other can or crushed water bottle i found on my way.Half-Life: Alyx is for me a 10/10 game again pushing new boundaries for video games as the series has in the past and i can safely say all the people who have spent their last 4 years working on the game have not dissapointed this OG fan.

_childDocuments_.review: Such a fantastic, exciting, and great game all around. The sound design, the details, the combat, the humor.It's such a polished experience, with first-rate interaction. To those wondering if why this was VR only, The things in the game would not be possible with a mouse and keyboard or controller--they really require you to use your hands. Just opening a cabinet to peak inside, or opening a door slowly, or rotating a sphere with your hands just feels so visceral.  The levels are all unique, and very well paced. At no point did I feel bored, or waiting for something to end.The only downside is that it ended. It's everything I wanted again from a Valve game and more. Valve is back--sorry for doubting you!
