_childDocuments_.review: This is the lost hope I once had for a new half life game.   I had resigned myself to the fact that I would die not having played Half Life 3...  This is not hype... it's the real deal.  This is a half life game in a VR world.  Worth every penny.   The mechanics are solid and the game play is fun.   Here's my review:The negatives first1.  Only guns, no clobbering.  If you're cool with not being able to clobber a head crab with a blunt instrument and instead running out of ammo and fleeing like a coward, then this game is for you.  2, Puzzles are rudementary VR mechanics puzzles and are repetitive and small in scale.   They remind me of the sorts of puzzles to be solved in The Gallery.   Still a lot of fun but nothing ground breaking.  I miss the old HL2 physics puzzles that were required to proceed in the path instead of the same repetitive circuit path puzzles to open a chest or boot up the weapon upgrade device.3.  The game basically boils down to collecting resources to upgrade and reload your guns and conserving ammo while killing zombies with the occasional jump scare.  The positives next:1.  This follows the typical HL game format,  Slow introduction to the story and game mechanics followed by immersion into the grizzly horrific zombie stuff, followed by action battles with the aliens.  Familiar and comfortable.2.  The world is unmistakably half life.   The graphics are excellent and exploring in VR is amazing.  3.  If you were scared of HL2,  it's a lot scarier in VR.   The first encounter with a zombie is really fear inducing.4.  Wow this game is a lot of content for a VR title.  I'm used to 5-8 hours,  and this is really an extended game.  I enjoy this a great deal and draw out every moment.5. The dialogue with your companion is fun and entertaining.I look forward to the next half life title,  and since I am now half way through my own life span I hope it won't be another half-life till it arrives.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Literally everything about this game is an absolute ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ yes. The story is what exactly Half-Life needs, it doesn't over reach and try to overhaul so much into the game, it just tells the story the universe and fans need. The controls feel so natural to the point where in years time, I can see Alyx as being to VR what Combat Evolved was to console shooters. The sound design and graphics on display are incredible and is all used perfectly in a pretty flawless feeling game engine.Easily the best VR game released to date and an absolutely brilliant Half-Life game.

Altogether, this game sets a new standard for full-length VR games that will hopefully inspire other developers in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Finished the game in 10 hours. I still have a few achievements to do, so another play-through is going to happen which is fine by me, because it's Just an amazing game. If you are having second thoughts on buying, I would recommend you just buy it. The game sucked me in from the start, I was fully immersed. Some of the elements seemed much more terrifying in VR, especially when being strangled by a barnacle, the tension level goes through the roof, because it feels like you are actually there. Gun-play is good, there isn't a lot of melee, but you can smash up man-hacks with your hands. I would say this has to be the best game I have played in about 2 or 3 years. The only downside is I don't think any VR game will live up to this for a while. The only issue I had was around the last 3 chapters when the game seemed to crash a few times. Apart from that, I don't think I run into any issues. Some of the AI seemed a little stupid, and combine soldiers seem to be incapable of opening doors, which is actually a blessing sometimes. 9/10 - Go and buy it. Best £45 I spent this year.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Came with my Valve Index. A good way to learn VR if you're new, and still, 100% pure Half Life adventure, if you're only in it for the Half Life. But forget the stoic silent protagonist. Unlike the first game, this story is helped forward by periodic back and forth dialog. Cinematically scripted rather than dialog trees, but with enough humor to keep you wanting to move the story forward even when the battle sequences overtax the adrenalin.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: As of the time of writing this review, I believe this to be THE best VR title out there, and one of the best Half-Life games. The story is fantastic, if not a little short as I finished my first playthrough in fifteen hours, the gameplay is excellent, and the visuals are brilliant. I had a few issues with framerate here or there, but I've had framerate issues with most of the VR titles I've played so that could simply be my machine or headset. This is also the first game I've got all achievements on (to be fair, I did use a walkthrough, but some of the achievements are skill- or patience-based so knowing them in advance doesn't change much), so I'm pretty happy with that c:I've currently gone through two playthroughs and am currently planning a third because I enjoy it that much (that, and there's not terribly many other VR titles that are as captivating at this one), so if you have a VR headset or are thinking of getting one, and/or are a fan of the Half-Life series, I cannot recommend this enough.Oh, and the Gravity Gloves. They're brilliant. Really wish I had them irl lol
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: I really don't know how to put all of my thoughts into words here, but I'll try my best.Half-Life: Alyx was the FIRST VR game I played from start to finish, and that might have been the worst choice I could have ever made, because I doubt any VR game I ever play will now be able to match it in quality, enjoyment and immersion. After a what, 13-14 year break(?) from the last Half Life Valve had a lot of pressure to deliver, and they not only created a phenomenal game, but a phenomenal Half-Life game, which is an achievement I cannot give enough praise for.Everything in the game works, the story has no right to be as good as it is and the ending made me feel like I was right back there in 2009.Please, if you have a VR headset, do yourself a favour and buy this thing immediately, I can 100% promise you won't regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely stunning. 13 years since Valve has made their last half life game has led up to this. The beginning of the game before you are in City 17, the title card introducing you to your character and explaining the time gap between the death of Eli Vance and the events of the game. Perfectly illustrated, you start the game in the all known City 17, we get a breathtaking view of the citadel before its final stage in Half life 2. The sound design in the game make it so that you really feel like your in the game as Alyx. The level design did not fail to impress me, with the tricky platforming and brain hurting puzzles. The game has made me not regret buying a VR headset and staying true to the half life franchise. Although it left many more questions than answers, it made me feel as if I was living the moment, the ending almost made me tear up because of how well written it is. I played the games for almost over 13 hours without break because of just how stunning and surreal to me it was. At some points in the game, I thought to myself "There is no way I am playing a Half life game by Valve." Overall, this game was a good way to spark many Half life fans into the fandom again. I wasn't born for the original Half life. I wasnt born for Half life 2. I wasnt old enough for Half life 2: Episode 2 but I was old enough to experience a turning point that could bring a tear to almost any diehard fan(like me). My rating for the game? No lie but like 12/10. I cannot stress how amazingly well written and illustrated this game is.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: This truly is the future of gamingEDIT: Regarding left handed mode. I'm a left handed and I have absolutely no problem with the control scheme. In fact, I prefer Alyx's implementation of left handed controls over other shooters. In games like Pavlov, the mag release and movement are both done on the left controller. This means you'll have to take your thumb off the control stick to drop the mag and reload. By having movement on the right stick, you solve this problem.EDIT: Seriously, make sure you play Episode 1 and Episode 2 before playing this.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Heads up may need to optimize settings for your VR through Steam VR's settings along with the settings on the Oculus app if you are using the Oculus Rift S like me, I'm a new VR user and when first playing this game I experienced weird choppy visuals but after looking around online I found the perfect configuration for my PC setup and now the game runs perfectly smooth, has something to do with Steam VR and the Oculus app running at the same time not the actual game that's causing these issues, The game though is beyond amazing and would recommend to anyone looking for an extremely interactive VR game, the fact you can practically touch and move every item, or something as simple as seeing inside an empty water bottle is amazing, the graphics legitimately make it feel like your actually there, and playing with a fan blowing in the background while standing on the balcony overlooking the city in the beginning of the game made it almost feel too real lol, all in all get the game! This is definitely worth the asking price.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: This is hands down one of the most, if not the single most compelling title available to this day for PCVR and is a pretty good reason to splurge on a VR headset for those that haven't already. What you get from HL: Alyx is an incredibly well-realized, immersive experience set in the dystopian City 17 that is brilliantly fun all the way throughout. Fighting the baddies of Half Life has never been so blood pumping as it is in HL: A where you're physically thrust into the action through the magic that is VR, fumbling your reloads and grenade tosses whilst dodging bullets and crouching down behind cover, lining up those sick headshots and blasting fools away with your shotgun. All of this makes for what can only be described as gaming bliss. As usual with Valve, they really knocked it out of the park. 10/10 Masterpiece
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly good. This game is 100% worth the $60 price tag. If you have a system capable of running it and a headset that works with it, there is no reason not to get it. The gameplay is very good, The story is great, however if you havent played the other half life games you probably should put this off until you have, as there is a major spoiler in the first 20 seconds of gameplay about hl2:e2

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, probably the best VR game out there right now, at least out of those that I've tried. The graphics are superb, even playing on my CV1 OC Rift with touch controllers at GTX1070.  I turned up some of the settings beyond what GeForce experience was recommending and it still ran solid with great visuals.  Curious how it would look on a more powerful VR setup but I have no regrets playing it on mine.  Valve definitely used some secret sauce here because other VR games I own choke with way less visual fidelity.   The weapon handling is great and interacting with the environment feels vary natural.  I love how stressful combat became when I had to reload my weapons manually.  Felt way more realistic than in any FPS game I've played.  I didn't collect enough resin (was about 25 short), so I didn't get a chance to try the grenade launcher upgrade, but all the other upgrades were pretty sweet.  The laser sights were especially helpful, but I did still enjoy aiming using the sights more often than not in order to save my rounds.  Although I never ran out, I always felt like I was running short on ammo.  Not sure how the game allocates this, perhaps it's dynamically.  This is one of those titles where you wish that we also had body tracking, not just the hands.  I found myself trying to kick and elbow things on occasion.  My main gripes are that it was very linear, so I doubt it will have much replay value, even though I do plan on trying it on the harder mode.  The story was OK, nothing extraordinary.  I felt there was a lack of banter compared to the previous Half-life games.  I hope they will allow modding and extra level creation because this is begging for it.  I played the entire campaign room-scale physically standing and squatting down when needed; it was awesome.  Peace!
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: I play this game on in index and it is really amazing! The atmosphere is breathtaking, the sounds  and everything around fells like coming home.As this is one of the visual and gameplay most impressing VR titles I will focus here on the points that I don't like that much but maybe they'll get patched :)There is just one big negative point which I tell everyone who asks me "And how is the new Helf-Life?"The controls are bad for some points:I like to play smooth locomotion and I love that Valve put the possibilities into the game to use teleport or locomotion but the movement speed is very slow and if you try to start running (like in any other vr title) by pressing the left thumbstick you start to crouch instead of run because there is no running and a really bad binding for the crouching function.I tried do change the controls in the menu but it tells me that I have to do this in the Steam VR settings which feeled very overloaded on the first look so i skipped manual bindings and dealt with the default.Valve introduced the game is good to play while standing or seated. In other games if play seated, you can adjust the height of your VR headset so that you dont seem like a really small person. That is not possible atm. so playing this game seated does work yeah but not that well. (Feels awkward to talk to someone while being at the height of his stomach)(Already fixed) smooth turing was not possible only snap turning but this was already fixed with the latest release.This is not a negative point:I had really problems to shoot when I first get the pistol. Most VR games using just the trigger to shoot. In HL:A with index controllers you need to really pull the trigger like you are using a gun. Feeled strange in the beginning but got used to it after about 3 magazines XDI really hope that they will fix the other control "issues" too or give at least setup possibilities for this, but except of the controls this game is totally amazing!

_childDocuments_.review: This game blows my mind how good it is and is exactly why I purchased VR 4 years ago. _childDocuments_.review: Just finished the game. This is the next step for VR and a revolution of gaming for me. I really HOPE now that the next Half Life is in VR. Valve sets the bar for shooters (again) and VR this time. Also they demolished all arguments that VR needs to be restricted much. Yes, there are still SOME restrictions, but it is the whole package, a complete Half Life experience on the level of the old games.The design, pacing, story, dialogue, set-pieces, ... are all very very good. Also the graphics, physics, lightning, animations, sound etc. all are incredibly good, even compared to non VR games.Also, for some who think they might be too anxious because it is mostly a "Horror" game. I can't play normal Horror games (Anmesia, SOMA, etc.), but didn't have any problem in this game. Even some REALLY tense moments are just fun, because you are so into it. The game also never relies on Jump Scares or such things (well... ONE time near the end they got me GOOD).

_childDocuments_.review: Absolute masterpiece, IMO even better than HL2! _childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: A great VR experience, and overall a great game, albeit not without it's issues.I have played all of the previous Half Life games. I'm going to set aside the Half Life aspect of this game for the first part of this review because I want to address the issues properly, without getting my love for Half Life involved.I will say that from a technical standpoint as far as mechanics go, Boneworks is the winner. There is just so much you can do in that game and everything feels wonderful. In particular, the gunplay is flawless. It is not so with Alyx. Your movement is more restricted, sometimes the game requires you to hold forward to advance through a window or other area, and your left arm will feel like more like you've got a gun glued to it than you actually holding one. That is, honestly, the worst part of this game for me - the guns work well but unfortunately they are strapped to your hand and your freedom of movement and interaction becomes limited by this. In Boneworks, you can easily swap guns, weapons and items to your offhand if you need your primary to do something else and vice-versa. I do understand why this is done though. In Boneworks, each weapon and item will disintegrate once you finish the level, forcing you to get new weapons in the next. Alyx might have suffered from that system if it was used. If you haven't played Boneworks, I suggest you play through Alyx first and then play Boneworks.The graphical and audio fidelity of this game is absolutely stunning. It is so clear and every scene had a surprise in store. The particle effects are wonderful and add to the immersion. The way the audio is directed towards the player for individual effects and scenes is fantastic. The immersion level of this game is one of the best that I have experienced.The controls could be better, but they are very far from bad. I am left-handed, so I of course play in leftie mode. Again, Boneworks takes the cake here. In every game ever made in the universe, you use the left joystick to move. In leftie mode, you must use the right joystick to move. It's because whatever hand you choose, that's where the gun will glue to. All of the gun actions are then on that hand, and the other actions are on the opposite. More issues caused by this system...also, there is no crouch button - which, yes, helps the realism, but there's not that much crouching in the game. A crouch button is very nice (Boneworks...need I say more).Finally, I'd like to address the story and world. Again, I've played all of the HL games. The story is very good. There are also many sections of the game where I stood in complete awe and just stared at everything before getting started with the level. The pacing of the story and how worlds and new interactions are introduced to the player is probably my favorite part of this game. The game does not hold your hand, but it will "nudge" (you'll get that once you complete the game) you in the right direction. It will not show up with menus and all that annoying stuff - it will hint at what to do with intelligently placed game objects and it will even give you several paths to the completion of particular sections.The ending gave me goosebumps and got me excited for what's next. If you have a VR kit, pick this game up and play it all the way through. I only wish it was longer.Can't wait to replay once they release this on Linux officially with Vulkan support. Thanks for supporting Linux, Valve!
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: As a very long time fan of Valve and the Half-Life series, I can understand some of the criticisms. But that should not take away from how ground breaking and amazing this game is. From the opening segment that just sends chills down your spine to navigating the terrifying pitch black tunnels of the Quarantine Zone. From the easy to learn weapon and shooting mechanics to the intense enemy encounters. Half-Life: Alyx is without a doubt the highest quality game Valve has blessed us with, and every atmospheric set piece, bit of dialogue and writing, and the sound design/music were obviously created with pure dedication and eye for detail.To hell with Jeff though.

_childDocuments_.review: A great game and a fantastic showcase of what VR is capable of. It's not even necessary to know anything about other Half-Life games to enjoy it.And it's not just a game in VR, it's a game built with VR. The interactions and detailed world is so amazing, I spent half the time drawing on walls and stacking random stuff I found lying around. Still, while it's most likely the game with the best use of VR out there right now, it's probably not ideal as an introduction to VR for most people on account of, you know, the clawed aliens jumping at your face.

_childDocuments_.review: My honest reactionMy name is Walter Hartwell White. I live at 308 Negra Arroyo Lane, Albuquerque, New Mexico, 87104. This is my confession. If you're watching this tape, I'm probably dead, murdered by my brother-in-law Hank Schrader. Hank has been building a Virtual Youtuber empire for over a year now and using me as his recruiter. Shortly after my 50th birthday, Hank came to me with a rather, shocking proposition. He asked that I use my Live2D knowledge to recruit talents, which he would then hire using his connections in the Japanese utaite world. Connections that he made through his career with Niconico. I was... astounded, I... I always thought that Hank was a very moral man and I was... thrown, confused, but I was also particularly vulnerable at the time, something he knew and took advantage of. I was reeling from a cancer diagnosis that was poised to bankrupt my family. Hank took me on a ride along, and showed me just how much money even a small indie channel could make. And I was weak. I didn't want my family to go into financial ruin so I agreed. Every day, I think back at that moment with regret. I quickly realized that I was in way over my head, and Hank had a partner, a man named Motoaki "Yagoo" Tanigo, a businessman. Hank essentially sold me into servitude to this man, and when I tried to quit, Yagoo threatened my family. I didn't know where to turn. Eventually, Hank and Yagoo had a falling out. From what I can gather, Hank was always pushing for a greater share of the business, to which Yagoo flatly refused to give him, and things escalated. Yagoo was able to arrange, uh I guess I guess you call it a "hit" on my brother-in-law, and failed, but Hank was seriously injured, and I wound up paying his medical bills which amounted to a little over $177,000. Upon recovery, Hank was bent on revenge, working with a man named Riku Tazumi , he plotted to kill Yagoo, and did so. In fact, the bomb that he used was built by me, and he gave me no option in it. I have often contemplated suicide, but I'm a coward. I wanted to go to the police, but I was frightened. Hank had risen in the ranks to become the head of the Cover Corp, and about that time, to keep me in line, he took my children from me. For 3 months he kept them. My wife, who up until that point, had no idea of my vtubing activities, was horrified to learn what I had done, why Hank had taken our children. We were scared. I was in Hell, I hated myself for what I had brought upon my family. Recently, I tried once again to quit, to end this nightmare, and in response, he gave me this. I can't take this anymore. I live in fear every day that Hank will kill me, or worse, hurt my family. I... All I could think to do was to make this video in hope that the world will finally see this man, for what he really is.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Now that I have beat the game, I can make a full review. First off, this is one of the first VR experiences that actually felt like a full-length game rather than a tech demo for me. The story is your typical great valve storytelling and you're never pulled out from the perspective of Alyx Vance.The atmosphere is done perfectly and really immerses you into the world and the combat can be pretty fun as well as the puzzles.There is plenty of replayability here as well as the workshop increasingly gets filled with more and more quality mods such as C17: Breakout.This is a spectacular game and I couldn't recommended enough.That being said, and with most of my VR reviews, take this review with a grain of salt as I streamed this game via virtual desktop on the quest as I do not have other standard headsets and link doesn't work for me. Therefore I did not have the "traditional" experience, and many problems I had with the game I attribute to that fact.I was also underneath minimum specs, but this game for the most part still ran smoothly on a 1060 3GB. The optimization is really well done, and if you have an even decent graphics card from the past 4 years then I guarantee you can run this game even smoother than some indie VR games even.Still, take this review with a grain of salt as I did not experience it in the "traditional" way. There are many other reviews that explain why you should buy this game better than I could.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Half-Life: Alyx is, without a shadow of a doubt, a MASTERPIECE! The graphics are stunning, and that alone is enough to get you drawn into this world. Between that, and the realistic and lovable cast of characters should be enough for you to have an amazing experience. But, knowing Valve, they aren't satisfied with "good enough," so they crafted the most realistic and fun physics engine for nearly all of the objects in the game! Most of your time will be spent searching around each and every room, simply playing with all the physics objects and scrounging for ammo and resin, this games currency for gun upgrades. Speaking of the guns, while you only get 3 weapons throughout the game, they are all super satisfying and fun to use, especially once you get some upgrades for each of them. My biggest problem with the guns is that, and this may be just a bit nitpicky, but I never end up using the shotgun because of the fact that I rarely find ammo for it. This is usually the case for most games like this, but it seems way more apparent here. I'm currently sitting at 100+ ammo for the two other guns and just shy of 12 ammo for the shotgun. It isn't really that big of a deal, as I only ever feel the need to use the shotgun when up against the beefier Combine enemies, but still.Anyways, combat with both Xen aliens, zombies, and Combine is way more satisfying and tactical then it ever has been. Oftentimes, I fully embrace my role as Alyx fighting to survive, and when facing the Combine, I genuinely fear them as genetically modified soldiers hell bent on killing me and not as some enemies I just need to kill to progress. That is how real this game becomes to me while playing. No game has ever come close to making me feel this way, at least since when I was a child and everything felt real to me. The genuine sense of presence in the world allows for that kind of immersion. To end this off, I'd like to talk about the whole VR exclusive deal that people seem to be complaining about. This game couldn't be as amazing as it is without VR. VR is this games cornerstone, and would NOT be a fun experience to play outside of VR. This is mainly because it was completely designed for the platform in mind. It just wouldn't work or be nearly as intuitive as it is without VR. You could not have the experiences that I described above without the VR element. If you want to play this game, you need to buy a VR headset. If you can't afford an Index, I recommend the Oculus Rift S. It takes no time to setup, and it is still a high quality experience. Even the tracking system, while it isn't ideal, still works perfectly. Just treat it like you're buying a new part for your computer.Anyways, I highly, HIGHLY recommend this game. I haven't even beaten it yet, but it has already shattered into my #1 favorite game of all time spot. This is, without question, VR's Mario 64 moment. VR's first AAA quality game made for the ground up just for it. It is absolutely a must play!
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: This is without question the best VR game I've ever played.  Not only is it an incredible VR experience, but it's also an incredible game.  How many VR games can you say that about?  It has all of the Half-Life 2 elements, but with the added terror of full immersion in incredible detail.  I hope this is just a taste of what we can expect in the future from Valve (including more Half-Life games)
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: It wasn't Half-Life 3.The protagonist talks too much. Melee combat is completely non-existent. There are a lot of "unfun moments" that are a chore to navigate. (Minor Spoiler; Doesn't Spoil Plot) Explosions pass through walls and around corners generously. The dead bodies are 300 lbs so you can't lift them up or something. The game is too dark (and not in just the total darkness rooms, either)This game would not be fun if it wasn't for VR, but it's not fun  it's in VR. There's way too much scavenging, way too little shooting, and way, way too few shotgun shells.It is one of the best Singleplayer VR Experiences out there, but that's only because VR is a very small market with only indie devs making cool stuff and gaming giants trying to port over their old games to VR in a soulless way. Of course the best company in gaming can make the best SPVR experience there is when there isn't any competition. It has simple controls meant to coddle new VR users. That's fair; this will be many people's first VR title. Could you give us expert controls, though? I hate teleportation mechanics, but you move so slowly with continuous movement that you end up using it anyways, and then, when I want to turn left and right, I might accidentally pull the thumbstick down too far and teleport myself into a tripmine, zombie, barnacle, or just straight-up over the edge into a pit of death.Again, this game would not be fun if it wasn't for VR, Boneworks is the best game I have ever played in my life. It is a linear singleplayer experience and I am on my third playthrough because it is large and fun. It has awesome gameplay, and the gameplay is directly tied into VR.HL:A doesn't have gameplay directly tied in to VR. It's a worse version of the Half-Life 2 formula. The physics that made Half-Life 2 fun evolved throughout the game. The VR expansion that makes this game fun evolves throughout the game. However, your arsenal is smaller, your ammo is never bountiful, the enemies are slow (yet kill you too fast), and the scavenging (almost) never stops. You spend way too long looking for too much resin that you don't get to have fun with because the game ends before you can even fully upgrade all your guns. HL:A takes what HL:2 did with physics and does that with VR, but boring. The story doesn't make up for it, either.I will say one thing though! (LARGE SPOILER! SPOILS PLOT!)
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent.  It's the most immersed I've been in a VR game by far.  Taking the headset off I was sometimes I bit surprised to see the real world.  It feels very Valve, and that's a positive, as the writing is always light and witty, but also a little bit of a negative - the tongue in cheek thing means I was never invested in Alyx's mission, and didn't care what happened to Alyx's dad!    I now need to buy at least a 2070 Super in order to fully appreciate this game. On my RX580 8GB I got slow down every time there was a hologram on the screen.  That choppiness did spoil things a little - and I am above minimum requirements, running on low.  (low still looked great though)
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: After the years of waiting for a new Half Life game Valve found another way to make players speechless. Each Half Life game has something to showcase. Half Life: Alyx was able to show what Source 2 is actually capable of doing. Not only graphics wise but performance wise. Some players may say Valve made a mistake by making this virtual reality only but honestly it is worth buying a virtual reality headset just for this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who hasn't played Half-Life: 2, it was an awesome treat to be spoiled that game at the very start of it's prequel.Valve pls fix.Also the modern Valve intro in VR is here.So basically it's a horror game, a really scary one.Also it's optimized insanely well, looks amazing, and is a new Half-Life game.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Look, If you are looking for a great experience to begin playing VR. This is what you are looking for. Personally? so much of what makes VR amazing to me is lacking here and overall the gameplay is lackluster and rather looks like a tech demo for VR than a proper game. Almost all of the VR games I have played before has done things better. VR interaction with the environment, Inventory management, Gunplay, etc. Half Life Alyx does Vr about as good as Fallout 4 VR with more polish and even then. The movement in Fallout is better. Slow walking and teleporting abusing is just the natural way of moving around in Alyx. Continuous movement is a pain, so slow it makes everything just that bit more boring.This has nothing to do with story, graphics, voice acting, etc. Only has to do with gameplay and I get it. People defend this by stating it's suppose to be a title to initiate people to VR. But It could have been both. By being such a simplistic and lackluster VR title. It ends up aging extremely poorly and being an incredibly unsastifying VR experience for moderate and veteran VR users that have come to expect certain things.If this wasn't Valve and wasn't Half Life. I wouldn't have tried the game and I'm pretty sure most people would also have skipped it and it wouldn't sit at 90+%.Sure I played 1hour. If you think that's not enough, than disregard this review. Environments were amazing, Story was pretty catchy though a bit handheldy, but this is just not the kind of gameplay i'm looking for in VR. It feels like a PC game that was ported to VR.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. Very specific level of physical interaction with the environment, but sometimes there aren't enough logical consequences to messing with things to make it believable (like turning the knobs on a stove to flood the kitchen with gas -- and why is the water shut off everywhere?) Overall, HL:A is a great standard for developers to look at. Only real issue is that SteamVR crashes a lot when I load saves. Sweet Jesus.Excellent, needs more cowbell, needs less crashing.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: By far one of the greatest looking, greatest story telling, greatest interactive games I have ever played. Valved had us waiting for a game for a very long time, and it was well worth it. I managed to make it all the way with the gnome becoming the 2% that have done so, and it was an amazing challenge. _childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. It has the right balance of puzzles, exploration, and combat. It has a level of interactivity with objects in the world beyond what any other VR title has created (of course it's not perfect, but it sure is fun). If you have played the other Half-Life titles, then you also get the benefit of knowing the story, but that's not necessary to enjoy the game for what it is. It's a VR masterpiece.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: This game is SO good, it'll have you thinking about it while you're asleep! I just love the interactivity of the many small objects in the game. It rewards when you're exploring off the main story looking for ammo and resin. After finishing the game, of course it'll have you yearning for more. Thankfully, the game allows for user-creation! The add-ons that the users make are pretty decent!The battle mechanics are great, I enjoy every single encounter against foes. The fact that you have limited inventory space and limited ammo (if you play on hard mode), keeps you ever so resourceful. And the puzzles! I love the puzzles! The fact that you have to pretty much figure out every single puzzle with little to no direction is just so rewarding! After beating this game, I always find myself playing it back up again as it's just that good of a game.I wish more VR games were as legendary as this.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: This game was completely awesome. Really sets the bar high for VR games and although it was short, I thought this to probably be one of the best story games I've ever played. The way it's perceived and how it utilises the many features that VR has, truly combines to make such a great game. It was the first game I played with the Oculus Quest 2 with a semi-decent pc build and it really helped to get me used to VR probably due to its lack of locomotion as the game requires you to teleport (however I believe this option can be changed in the settings) and overall easy controls. Once again Valve, great work.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Half-Life is back!I had a ton of fun playing this game. My only complaints are the lack of melee combat, and the fact that the first half of the game felt like it was meant to be an introduction to VR more than to drive the story. That was an understandable choice, and the game was still fun, I just would've liked to see more story than "go in this direction and occasionally shoot an enemy" up until . The story we do eventually get, though, is totally worth it, .Combat, especially combine combat, felt amazing. It's incredible how much less of an unstoppable tank Alyx is than Gordon. Melee combat would've been nice, but its exclusion is totally understandable given the problems it poses. Interactivity is amazing and the gravity gloves are so intuitive I found myself trying to use them in real life.

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay had to be slowed down for VR, of course, but it still feels like half life.  Definitely worth a play through.  The combat is solid, the aiming works, the lack of a realized physical body does more good than harm.  The writing is good and so is the acting.  Though this is not a horror game, it completely ruined pop scares while playing flat.  I know folks have gripes with how inventory management is handled (i.e., not realistic enough).  But this is a game, it should be fun.   Sure, they could make you take off your virtual backpack, zip it open, look through the contents to find the right clip, slot it, pull the slide, zip up the back pack, and put it back on.  That would be tedious.  Why not make the protagonist have to eat (like with a knife and fork), drink, and go to the bathroom while we're at it?  Reaching over one's shoulder to grab an ammo pack (and occasionally having to pull the slide) is immersive enough and it does not slow you down more than necessary.

_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Words alone cannot coherently describe the amount of emotions and raw immersion into the game I felt while playing this experience...  Especially when for years, VR has been nothing more than a party-trick and a janky gaming experience, loaded with bugs and un-optimized messes of experiences...  This one, was a polished, beautifully crafted, emotional, and overall smooth game to play...  One that was so immersive I forgot many times that I was wearing a big headset on my face...  This game is what VR titles should aspire to be..The physics, the graphics, the dialogue, the characters, the overall fluidity of the motions and animations in the game, the fact that absolutely every single cutscene is not just a cutscene, but seamlessly just animations placed within the game's raw engine makes it all the more wonderful an experience.Most importantly, it balances discomfort perfectly.  Just as you're in the creepiest depths of an infested underground section, you push on in the hopes of seeing sunlight, only to be thrown right back down into the depths of the zombie-infested zones...  Everything is tense, and multiple times I had to physically fight my reflexes to push on.  No game before has EVER drawn so many mixed emotions from meA solid 10/10 in my books..  I can see why they waited so long, and the amount of polish this game shows...  is well worth the wait.Games nowadays are just mindless cashgrabs.  Playing it safe, and not taking risks...  This one took a huge risk being a standalone AAA VR title...  and by god, did it pay off...  I could physically feel the love, and tedious work that went into crafting this game...  If you have VR, you NEED to buy this game
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: this game was the best VR experience ive ever had, and it definitely beat BONEWORKS by a huge mile which was surprising to me as BONEWORKS was already an amazing game. valve really outdid themselves with this game.  it was incredibly immersive (i forgot i was in vr a few times), and incredibly fun. the environment is amazingly detailed and so well optimized that my garbage computer was able to keep high frames throughout the game, even with the amazing graphics. although they definitely had to dumb down ai so people could play in vr, it was still a challenging experience. even on normal i died a few times throughout the game, and im excited for my second playthrough on hard. the story was amazing, especially the ending. the ending gave me goosebumps, especially when i realized how the final chapter's name connected to a specific half life 2 chapter.  i'm very excited for half life 3, and i hope it delivers a similar experience to this incredible game. 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Half-Life Alyx NO-VR review: In 1998 when HL was released, I was already a nearly-40-year-old fanboy. That means here in 2024, I’m an even much older fanboy—who, unfortunately, also has intermittent vertigo problems and suffers from severe motion sickness if I’m not careful. So, if I were ever going to be able to play Half-Life: Alyx, it would never be in its native VR form. Ah, getting old ain’t for sissies, as they say.That’s why I was out-of-my-mind excited to hear about the Alyx NO-VR mod. I would finally be able to jump back into the dystopia that is City 17 and get gunned down by the Combine--before I croak in real life, that is. Now that I’ve made my way through the entire game using the NO-VR mod, I thought I’d write a little…update?I won't extensively review the game. Plenty of other reviews here. But if you are reading this because you are also a longtime HL fan who can’t (or won’t) strap a contraption to your head but want to play the game, here’s my short advice: DO IT! The mod works. You can play the game from beginning to end sitting 12 feet away from a flat screen (or on your couch in front of ye ole’ TV box) and not vomit. Some of the VR-heavy functions in the game have been simplified (or removed) for flat-screen use, but the big, overall narrative experience, high-tension firefights, and creepy locations are still lovingly in place. Sure, it’s not the same innovative experience as it is in VR I guess, but also…you know…no vomit, no having to lay down for an hour to make the room stop spinning. Anyway, the game looks amazing (even now, 4 years after release), and the story and actors are as good as ever. The NO-VR mod has added in workable character models (hands, arms) and reload animations so it plays like a classic HL FPS. Maybe it’s my nostalgia talking, but wow.However since the NO-VR mod is…well…a MOD, my recommendation has caveats. So as of February 2024, here are the hurdles I (quite happily) had to jump as I played through the HL: Alyx NO-VR mod. Since the mod is in active development, I expect many (or all) of these issues will get resolved (if they haven’t been fixed already).GENERAL ADVICE: 1) SPAM THAT QUICKSAVE BUTTON. There are some technical issues with the current build of the NO-VR mod (again, we’re talking Feb. 2024 here…read below) that could be frustrating. Saving often helps soften those problems. There is a decent Steam community controller mod (if you play with controller) which works well, but I personally made one major configuration change to that community controller setup: I assigned the quicksave function to a single button on my controller so I could always have fast access to it. 2) BACK UP YOUR SAVES FOLDER. The way the NO-VR mod works, you only have a limited number of saves (something like 3 autosaves and 3 quicksaves that are continually overwritten, and the NO-VR mod does NOT support saves that were made in the regular VR version of the game—you must use your own NO-VR saves with the mod). The game’s save folder is located within the main install HL: Alyx folder and is clearly labeled SAVES. Take the time to create a copy of that folder and keep multiple copies of it somewhere. Why? It is possible for you to get yourself into a non-reversible situation (again, see specific issues below) and all your saves have been overwritten and you have no way out, other than starting the game from scratch. You do you, but I choose the low-frustration route.SPECIFIC ISSUES I FACED>CONTROLLER PROBLEMS: I play my PC games with a controller (Xbox Series X/S via Bluetooth connected to Windows 11). You might not, and if you use KB+M, then you don’t need to read this. The NO-VR mod supports both KB+M players and players who use controllers, but two issues with my controller happened. First, MOST of the time, after the NO-VR mod booted, it would NOT recognize my controller as being connected even though I had the Steam community controller configuration loaded, applied to the game, and Steam input activated (which you have to do ahead of time). It was super frustrating. BUT I finally figured out what I had to do to fix the issue. I had to boot the game AND Steam in a specific order: 1) With NOTHING running (not Steam, not the mod) and making sure my controller was connected via bluetooth to Windows, I simply had to> 2) Double-click the NO-VR mod launcher.exe itself. 3) This starts the NO-VR mod launcher. (Steam is still NOT running.) 4) In the NO-VR launcher, click play. 5) This auto-starts Steam. 6) Then Steam auto-starts HL: Alyx. If I had anything running ahead of time (like Steam already running, or the NO-VR launcher already running), my controller would not be recognized. This is how I fixed it.CRASHES: When I would die 3 or 4 times in a row (it happens as the Combine firefights get tougher towards the end) and the game would restart from a checkpoint, after the third or fourth checkpoint load, the NO-VR mod would crash to desktop. This is one of the reasons you should spam the quicksave so you don’t lose progress. But outside of this specific situation, I NEVER experienced a crash. It only happened after several quick restarts in a row.STUCK: Due to the nature of the mod, it can happen that you end up stuck on a piece of geometry (usually because you are somewhere you shouldn’t be). Thankfully, the NO-VR mod has auto-enabled the “no clip” cheat to a specific key (V) so it is super-easy to unstick yourself if this happens.FORWARD MOVEMENT STOPS: This one I had to grin and bear it. But Alyx would often simply stop walking forward when she encountered even the smallest object on the ground in some places. A small rock, a tiny cardboard box, a little cable on the ground—these are things she would normally glide right over, but instead she would come to a dead stop. There were some maps where I would have to hop my way through it if there was a lot of debris around. The problem seemed to come and go, but it was especially frustrating in a firefight when I was trying to beat a hasty retreat to reach some cover…and Alyx comes to a complete stop because there was a piece of paper on the ground--and then she’s full of Combine bullets.GUN MODS: The game has Combine machines you can insert your gun into for upgrades. After the upgrade animation ends, the gun is supposed to pop back into your hand. In some chapters though, I found that my gun was still sitting in the upgrade machine after the animation stopped, and I could not retrieve it--all I could do was look at it. I certainly couldn’t go forward without a gun. So this is why I say: Spam that quicksave! Get in the habit of saving BEFORE you do anything major. Most of the time, I would just ignore that non-working upgrade machine and wait until I reached the next one.SCRIPTED EVENTS DON’T TRIGGER: There were two cases where major scripted events would not trigger for me, and the game would not move forward. Again, this is a reason to back up your saves folder so you can revert. One was in the “Jeff” chapter where the monster you are stealthily avoiding is supposed to follow you into an elevator. No matter what I did, Jeff would NOT get into the elevator—he was stuck in an earlier part of the map banging on an invisible door. The second instance was where I deactivated a Combine force field, but it still wouldn't let me go through. In both cases, I used the built-in “no clip” cheat that the NO-VR mod has enabled, and the game moved forward, ignoring the glitched script. Yay.Though the above list might sound like they are all reasons to NOT play the NO-VR mod, that is not the case at all. As with so many mods (and especially one of this magnitude), you have to be prepared for workarounds, restarts, backups…all that good stuff. I was so happy to be able to play this high-quality HL game. I got those old tickly HL vibes all over again after so many years. YAY!! Oh, and that ending! Oh yeah, that ending!

_childDocuments_.review: I played this as someone without any previous experience with the Half-Life franchise, and as someone with the full Index kit.This game isn't the second coming of Christ that everyone seems to think it is. This game is overwhelmingly fine. Using your telekinesis powers to move things towards you is fun, and if you have a big open room and don't mind the physically laborious nature of playing most VR games, this is a fun game. But it's not revolutionary in any way. I was expecting the VR nature of this game to matter significantly more than it did, but it felt underutilized. If you already have a VR kit, go ahead and get it I suppose, so you can judge the hype for yourself.But to be very clear, this game in no way validates the purchasing of an expensive VR kit. I've not yet had an experience that negates my regret of purchasing a 1,100 dollar VR kit, and at this point I'm fairly confident that I never will. I'm definitely a sucker.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Bugs were minimal, but did detract from the experience. A few times I found myself in an area I was not supposed to have accessed yet and had to reload the save/die. Items clipping through surfaces and lost forever, and one specific area that I had to modify the control scheme to cross.Otherwise, this is one of the only games in VR where the devs seem to really understand what makes VR so great. Most VR games are trash, or tech demos, or are good conceptually but lack execution. I wouldn't call Half Life: Alyx perfection, but it's probably the best VR experience on the market right now.It's a bit short, but most FPS games are. The puzzle design is fantastic, and never felt repetitive. The guns start off generic, but they become more unique as the game progresses. It has a satisfying ending, some extremely tense moments, and one hell of a climax.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: The #1 greatest VR game there is, bar none. Just the mods for Half Life Alyx alone are better than most full-scale VR games and it's not even close! _childDocuments_.review: I never knew what happens when a glass bottle gets thrown at a glass window. Half-Life 2's physics were revolutional in their own right, but I don't think the gravity gun provides an exact replica of real-life events. On the other hand, I get to use my own hands to throw stuff around physically correctly. Who'd known that Half-Life 2's physics would provide such a great VR experience?And that's KINDA the gist of it, Alyx is basically HL² in VR.OR IS IT? Not quite. It's not a port, it's a Half-Life game developed from the ground up for VR and it shows. Not that VR-first games were all to rare nowadays, but the polish, the good ol' Half-Life-magic, that's something new.Just like Half-Life back then, Alyx shows that less is more. It's rather low on VR-gimmicks (such as on-body holsters), while offering interesting gunplay (you get to manually fiddle the magazine into the gun, yup) and an overall high environmental interactivity. That reductionism where less is more while offering where it counts has kinda defined Half-Life among other things.Such as going low on the overly-gamey stuff. Half-Life didn't have end-level statistics and even offered an in-universe background for the HUD. Alyx foregoes HUD elements almost completely, offloading most of it into your magic gloves. While I personally consider single-finger tracking more of a gimmick to show off Index controllers' capabilities, the immersion here truly is a thing to feel for yourself.Speaking of the gloves, they do serve as a VR successor to the gravitron. You can't shoot stuff all around (you get to throw everything yourself), you can pull stuff towards you making looting for resources way more bearable. Pulling ammo towards you feels natural since the first moments of doing just that.Scavenging is one part of it (being way more fun than in Fallout 4), puzzles & shooting come next. Similar to the previous titles, there's a healthy mixture. Slow, moody moments mixed up with awe-inspiring vistas mixed up with tenseion and, last but not least, intense shootouts. The pacing is spot-on, as it's always been with Half-Life.As are the combat encounters. They say, the shooting in Half-Life has never been particularly great (I agree that no Half-Life gun comes close to the awesomeness of Doom's coach gun), it's really fun here though. Aiming in VR is awesome by default, but the controls here really got something. There aren't many buttons required, weapon handling requires simple gestures, assuming you understand how the guns work, serving more to increase immersion. The environments the fights take place in are less of, like, places, and more like spots crafted specifically to make for a fun encounter. Speaking of reductionism, there's all of 3 guns in the game, but with their upgrades & firing modes, there's enough choice & variety to be had. All of this feels less like a game, being rather intuitive instead (sez I as a years-long gamer, weird).And then, when you need a breather after that intense shoot-out, a puzzle drops in. As is customary in Half-Life, they're all over the place. Environmental puzzles, including physics-based, have always been a pillar. Now, you get a multitool to do some additional only-VR puzzling. While they don't offer particularly all-too-much depth, they serve to further increase immersion & spice things up (damn, I really am not good at describing puzzles, am I? Please believe me that the puzzles are enjoyable).Ladies, gentlemen and teapots, the hype is real. I'm not sure if Alyx qualifies as a system seller (shelving a kilobuck for a game, no matter how amazing, doesn't seem quite sane), but if you're interested in VR and fancy an FPS which is not about shooting only (or not a "pure FPS", depending on the framing you wanna take), getting Alyx for free with a headset is a boon all right.PS: after months of VR and many other games, I'd like to point out one innovation Alyx got above all the rest: free saving. I don't mind saving on a per-song-basis in Beat Saber. But everywhere else, I don't feel like jumping in because I've no idea when I'll be able to save. With Alyx, I know I can save anytime. Basic 1990's innovation lost in VR space, except this one game. Thank you Valve!

_childDocuments_.review: I played Half-Life and every sequel when they first came out, I went to a brick and mortar store and bought the Orange Box at launch.I have waited the best part of twenty years for the sequel.Earlier this month, I got a Quest 2 and played HL:Alyx in VR, wirelessly and for the first few hours, I made zero progress in the game because I just wandered around City 17 gawping, muttering "ohmy♥♥♥♥ingawd" again and again, thinking "I'm IN City 17."The amount of detail, love and care that has been put into this game is all too clear, the story-telling is expertly crafted.The wait was well worth it and playing the next episode of HalfLife in VR felt like the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Blown away. Hands. Down. The BEST VR game I have EVER played in my life. Buy it. You will not regret it. This is only after an hour, and I cannot wait to complete this game.I'm using the original HTC vive from 2016 and the graphics are just stunning. They have not just considered exactly how, in the real environment, you would interact with everything, they took that and went 10 miles past it. Astonishing.Every minute I have played, it just kept getting better. Another thing that felt human, lifelike. You feel really immersed in this game, it is honestly unbelievable. You just start believing you are there, because your ideas on interacting match with what you would do in the real world. It's not just scale, and some gimmick VR features. This is not like anything you have ever witnessed. I promise you.There is no way Valve have made their money back on this game, it is far too detailed. Even at £50. It is so polished, I would hate to think how much time and money they spent on what is arguable the prettiest, most interactive VR game in existence.When you start the game, they get you familiar with VR on the rooftop of Alyx's apartment. You can pickup and interact with virtually everything. Plant pots, throwing items feels real. Tuning a radio, pulling the Antenna....There is a whiteboard with a board rubber. I cannot explain to you how it felt writing on that white board. What a time to be alive. Opening doors, real, Reloading the gun, real... Accidentally knocking large objects with your hand or gun when you turn around too quick... Picking up buckets full of items with one hand, to sift through it with your other... And then being able to turn the bucket upside down because you can't be bothered anymore. The way this game feels, is incredible.Other game creators need to take a leaf from their book, I honestly don't think any games company will ever come close to the aptitude Valve have applied in this game. It is a masterpiece. This game needs more awards. Incredible.***As a side note, I could never see VR's uses. This, along with steam home has changed my outlook entirely. I feel excited to make things for VR now. I was stood in my Steam home, pulled up my desktop and some other bits. This is going to change our lives forever.***

_childDocuments_.review: Personal Rating: 9/10We've all been waiting for a new half-life game for years. This might not be the HL3 we hoped for, but it is sure has hell a good direction in the half-life universe. I was sceptical at first, worried that this would be just a game that just came out there because VR is new and hot. But BOY was I wrong, and I love it that I was wrong too.This is straight up one of the best AAA VR games out there; You can interact with almost everything - as you could in the previous games. The controls are fantastic - though I've tested it on Oculus Quest with Oculus Link - I cannot imagine how it would be on the valve index. If you are a fan of Half-life or VR, I highly recommend this game as you will have hours of fun by doing small interactive things with objects around - or simply follow the Story which is good. There will be a time when you're stuck in that world that you will be stacking things up just because, or simply juggle things in the air. You'll start to do silly achievements that fits the Half-life franchise, try to finish the game in a different way, just derp around - the options are limitless! And seeing how people have begun modding it... only more playtime will come.

_childDocuments_.review: HL: Alyx - some of the best graphics in a VR game ever. I can't believe what I'm seeing with my super old low resolution Rift CV1. I thought I'd never be satisfied with VR graphics but Alyx proves that VR can have good graphics.The VR mechanics have been polished to near perfection and this will likely dictate the way future VR games will be made.Dropping ammo into your backpack / shoulder is the best ammo management system in VR ever. The sound cues of when your hand is at the right spot is the perfect solution. The ammo stomach pouch done by other games is not perfect because my stomach gets in the way. So every game should do shoulder / backpack ammo from now on.The issue of holstering and switching guns have been solved quite significantly. In other VR games you try to pick up a virtual object stuck to your hips and sometimes you just don't manage to pick it up. No longer a problem with Alyx. Same with grenades. Because weapon selection is a button hold + gesture.Storing small items on your wrist is an excellent way to see what item it is and easily find it when you need it. Instead of storing stuff stuck to a virtual torso.Gunplay of course there's no problems there. VR gun aiming has been pretty much perfect for a while now. Alyx's style of reload is simpler but not arcadey. Its visceral and you need two hands so in a gunfight you need to get good at reloads. This makes gunfights more visceral and pulse pounding. YOU CAN MESS UP YOUR RELOAD AND DROP YOUR AMMO LOL.Alyx chooses to go with single-hand weapons which makes sense. Two hand weapons in VR creates a weird effect because your hands aren't connected in real life and thus won't have realistic feeling 2-hand guns.Picking up objects is solved by magnetic gloves and feels very polished. With a bit of a snap lasso gesture and then snatching the object in the air, it makes for a better object "magnet" effect than Oculus Home where you point at something and press a button to pull it to yourself.The guns have indicators that show ammo count so you can keep track of half-spent guns. Very nice.Your gloves also has a spare ammo count and health meter. Good way to communicate that.You can wear masks, hats, etc.Now, let's talk about the physics engine and why its important for VR. And Half-Life is perfect for this because the gameplay of the flat HL games already use a lot of physics.Your gloves interact with every object in this game. Even walls. You can feel walls. Even though your physical hand goes through them, the in-game hand stays on the wall and you feel vibration feedback. This gives you presence in the world you didn't have before. You can feel doors. You can feel cabinets. You can feel beds. You can feel guardrails. You can feel anything.Having your hands feel things allows you to feel the wall when you're taking cover. Giving you the exact data to process where your hand should be when you need to shoot behind cover.You feel the cabinet when you open it. You feel the door when you open it. You feel the box when you move it. Believe it or not, most VR games don't do this.Physics is amazing too, because you can even use your gun to push objects. I use the muzzle of my gun to pull cabinets open, push doors, etc.The best way to explain physics is you can use ANY object to block a headcrab from jumping onto you. That's physics.Alyx doesn't have melee combat though, because honestly in VR you can't feel what you're hitting except for the small vibrations. So you can technically waggle like the Nintendo Wii and that's just not fun. Guns feel much better in VR.Traversal is quite well thought out, and you get many options of movement and turning. The important ones are here like teleport and smooth movement. And they added smooth turning a day after release - something super important for me. You can even grab ladders to pull yourself up. So yeah basically, well thought out. Jumping is also solved and is sort of like teleporting so its good for when you get stuck in some weird spot between boxes or weird geometry.Other than those, that's mostly it for the VR mechanics done right by Alyx. There's also spatial puzzles you need to solve, sometimes you need to throw a grenade to a vent that needs a bit of basketball skills.Personally I feel like there's a bit too many multitool puzzles especially the orb ones. Its a pain especially once you get to the trip mines. Looking around boxes and every nook and cranny for upgrade ingredients can also get kinda repetitive.I wish there were more physics based puzzles like carry a box here to weigh something down, you know? Instead there's multitool puzzles and switches. 9 out of 10 makes you feel like a tool.Story is pretty simple. HL is never known for its amazing story and Alyx is the same. The plot is basically an excuse for Alyx to go around shooting stuff solving puzzles and whatnot. Of course, this is still Alyx and she's a main HL character so she ties into the entire canon story of HL and HL2 and Gordon Freeman, so its cool to see parts of the story of this world. The ending makes an interesting statement too.Essentially, Half-Life: Alyx is VR mechanics perfected. It takes the best of all VR games' method of presence and picks the best ones, while having the polish of triple A game. Being in VR, the world is much more memorable and tactile. I wish it had more gunfighting, less multitool puzzles, and I wish you could run, but other than that this is the perfect VR game.

_childDocuments_.review: Easily the greatest game I've ever played.  I only have a Ryzen 5 2600 and an NVIDIA 1650 super but it played quite well, over wireless on a Quest 2 using virtual desktop.The only issue that i encountered was if I moved around a lot when a loading screen appeared.  The game would often lock up, then I'd have to re-launch it.  This might be due to me using virtual desktop; I'm not 100% sure.  But as long as I stood still and kept my head still during the loading screen, the game was virtually flawless.  The only other bug I encountered was with one or two health packs (needles...whatever they are called) getting stuck in the floor.  Often several gravity glove pulls would fix the issue, or I'd have to manually bend over and pick them up, but once I did have to load from a save point to retrieve it.

_childDocuments_.review: Right now there are many VR developers out there that don't know what exactly works, and this game shows solutions to that problem that work really well, such as refining controls and physical interactions. Also, the attention they gave to performance, graphics, audio detail, and accessibility is absolutely phenomenal. I started playing this game with high expectations and even that was heavy underestimating of how advanced and fun it is.This may just be the game that refines how things work in VR games, setting the bar high. I'm all for it.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: That has to be the greatest VR game at the moment.The pros:- Visually beautiful- Great face/character animation- Very well rendered atmosphere (music, sounds, light)- Great controls (partly thanks to the continuous turn update)- Only hands and head matter (prevents getting body parts stuck as in Boneworks)- Great challenging shooter: precise aiming needed, nice reloading manipulations, good combat pressureThe cons:- Very linear (as most HL games)- No possibility for getting back to previously visited zones- Not much explanations for people unfamiliar with the franchiseA must have/must play for VR players.Only 3 hours in, and I already dread seeing the credits rolling...
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Looks like valve took back the f***ing reins, despite the long and painfull wait. VR only, only makes sense. I'm really thrilled about this nostalgic comeback! Good job guys! You've managed to make me forget the fury i had for you, for all these years of lies and silence! This is pure immersion in the best possible setting!only con is the lack of variety and less attention to small details like repetative posters and so on
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: I would rate this 3/3 but Valve does not know how to count to 3, so neither do I. This game is revolutionary, unbelievable, amazing, beautiful. Gunplay and handling, throwing, interactions, you name it,  Alyx masters it!. This game defines VR but it has no melee which is a slight dissapointment! Anyhow, this is a game you must have in your VR library.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: While not the most accessible entry in the Half-Life series, Alyx is quite an impressive step into the next generation. Exploring decrepit buildings and combine installations is so much more fun in VR, and the exploration-based rewards are all the sweeter when you can look into every nook and cranny yourself! Puzzles are simple and fun, combat is evenly paced but thrilling, and the voice-work is very well done! It's not perfect, nothing is, but Half Life: Alyx is still a very fun experience that I've played twice over and will continue to play! Plus, workshop integration means you can get all the extra levels and modifications you could want!If you enjoy:Half-life's exploration, puzzles, and combatPhysics based objects to play around withDigging through trash like a little goblinThen Half-Life: Alyx may very well be the game for you!
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: I kind of can't believe I haven't written a review of Alyx yet, considering I've finished it at least 3 times.I'm an old-school Half-Life fan and I've loved them all since release, but Alyx is my favorite. If you love VR and/or you love Half-Life there is no excuse, especially with how affordable the Quest 2 is and how great it works for PC VR in 2023. If you absolutely cannot do VR for whatever reason, you should either watch a let's play, or download the "No VR" mod and play through yourself (though you'll be missing a great deal of what makes the game great). Still worth playing it flat to get the world and story if you're a die-hard Half-Life person.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: The most immersive VR experience i have ever had. Not only is the story a complete mastermind of putting you in sketchy situations you have to solve with some thinking, but also does it with style.The fights are as good as you will get in VR. Making you do everything you can to survive. Be it shooting a canister of gas foran explotion to kill multiple enemies so that you save some ammo or playing it safe in dark places to not get overwhelmed with oversized, nasty spiders.I must say i truly had an insanely fun time playing this game. Reloading as fast as i can as to not get eaten alive and flashing my flashlight in every direction whenever it gets too dark as i personally am not very good with dark spaces :)Amazing game. A must play if you have the hardware required! Would say buy even when not on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Must buy for all VR owners. This game is definitely worthy of the Half-Life title. Gameplay is great, the story is excellent, level design is really cool with small details that are fun to find, and the overall atmosphere is immersive, dark, and amazing. I just love this game and if you take your time and explore each part of the game to look for ammo and equipment then it can easily make it a 13 hour experience on normal difficulty. I wish I had played it through on hard because combat didn't challenge me enough and I only died about 3 times in combat. This is definitely VR game of the year 2020 but I think it is also deserved to be in the top 3 for 2020 game of the year. _childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

The new characters are all great, even if there aren't very many new ones. The graphics are some of the most beautiful I have ever seen. _childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: I gotta admit I was a bit disappointed, though that may be due to having impossible expectations, nothing can really live up to hype of "Half Life" by "Valve" in "VR". Though Valve's classic games were so close to perfectly executed that they are still to this day studied and used as examples and a golden standard of how to properly design games, so I dared to expect near perfection, but instead I merely got the best VR game to date, but not really that much more than that. The finale of Alyx fortunately was amazing and truly felt like what I remember feeling in some of the best moments from Half Life and Portal. Still overall it felt a little bit underwhelming since as a game designer myself, I couldn't help but notice it felt too much like the beginning of Half Life 2 just redone for VR and with story readjusted to be prequel. Environments and progression lacked novelty due to this, which I felt around half the time I was playing, with the other half offering some novelty in the form of new types of environments, level designs and events.I felt the levels involving Jeff were a miss though. The horror aspect of Half Life is something I always because it was predominantly atmospheric, rather than straight up gore. But in VR, everything is so much more up close and having headcrab jump on my head or having big zombie devour my face really just felt unsettling and gross, and actually works against my immersion as I have to remember not to panic and run into a wall or smash my monitor with a controller, but instead remain calm despite being grossed out and startled, wait a few seconds while the game makes sure I finish experiencing dying while being eaten by a zombie or something, so I could push the menu button to load the most recent save. I find myself wishing "best VR game" was more inclusive, something that my wife or grandma could experience as well. So yeah, Jeff part was too frustrating, many times I just didn't know what I was supposed to do and kept dying trying to do wrong things, being unlucky or not reacting fast enough. Having Jeff eat my face once would have been too much. 20 is pushing it a little bit. I played on normal difficulty and am otherwise experienced gamer and VR gamer, but found the difficulty tuning to be a little bit too difficult still. A better autosave system could have helped with that, as I don't particularly mind dying, I mind having to repeat a longer segment due to forgetting to manually save every 20 seconds. Why can't we have "return me 10 seconds into the past" option on the death screen that appears immediately as I die? Or even better, make that the default so that I don't have to press anything in any menu after I die. I think that would have made this game less frustrating for me and more fun. I find the constant need to manually save after I kill every handful of enemies to be immersion breaking and incentivises in me the desire for save scumming due to have wasted a grenade or something. I was able to consciously resist doing that, just wish I didn't have to put in the mental effort.I had some trouble with accidentally dropping things as knuckle controller would think my little finger is uncurled even though it's not. Sure I can squeeze and let go the controller 3 times to recalibrate and fix this for a while, but it still caused some unnecessary deaths. Zen grenades were problematic as well, and I killed myself a dozen times due to accidentally arming it by squeezing too hard. Keybinds on the right hand were a bit imperfect as well, as I found it difficult to reliably catch and throw things with my right hand due to accidentally activating touchpad selecting a weapon and accidentally shooting even which would waste ammo and at the same time I'd like drop armed grenade on the floor and kill myself. I had to gravitate towards trying to throw and catch things with left hand instead just to avoid this issue, even though I'm right handed. And switching handedness wasn't an option as then I would have to fire weapons with left hand which would suck even more.I wish the game was a bit longer, I was hoping for at least 30% more content, ideally 60% more. Having the nearly whole game happen in city environment with no vehicles felt a little bit too abridged when compared to everything we get to experience in HL2.Also minigames are fun at first but get too repetitive as the game goes on.Given this huge rant of a review you'd think I'd give it a negative score lol, but it's still the best VR game to date I guess, and I did enjoy many parts of it a lot, and the overall production and polish is an order of magnitude beyond nearly all other VR games. The final level was like ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ level of amazing, and really finally hooked me got me super excited to play it, I really wanted the game to show "prologue finished" at that point and let me continue playing now that I finally got invested into the story and big things have started happening, instead the games just rolls credits, oh well. In any case, can't wait for continuation or whatever else next thing Valve has in store for us.

_childDocuments_.review: I got a Valve Index about six months ago, and up until now I've been underwhelmed by VR, and frankly regretted spending so much money on a toy I hardly use.HL:Alyx completely changes this. _childDocuments_.review: This is, quite simply, amazing.I can't remember the last time i had such emotional experiences during a video game. In fact video game isn't the correct word for this kind of......I suppose experience is the best word for it now, because that's what Half-Life: Alyx is, an experience.You know logically that it's not real, because you have a VR headset strapped to your head with it's limited field of view, but the level of detail in this world isn't far off. I must have spent hours (in between the action) just simply looking around, and really looking at the environment up close.I was fortunate enough to be able to play through this game using a HP Reverb G2, so the graphics were stellar, and I briefly sampled it with my previous Oculus Rift S, and it was still pretty amazing on that headset too. So, so long as your equipment is up to the heavy task of running a decent VR rig, you will utterly love this. This is the kind of gaming experience that I imagined I would be having when I was a kid in the 70s and 80s, and the story is pure unadulterated Half-Life.Alyx is both an amazing character and an amazing game, and I cannot wait for more.
