_childDocuments_.review: its 5am and i just now figured out why i couldnt open the ♥♥♥ menu for the past hours of my life. IF YOURE LEFTHANDED: GUESS YA FUGGED! Using a pico 4, being left handed and playing this game will result in y, x, b and a no longer working, thus the menu wont even open to switch it back. And guess what, in the main menu: you cant change preferences, so the actual changes i wanted to make are now impossible. GJ valve, 3 years later and ya didnt learn shid.edit: Anyway, I have found one workaround for now, which is to go to Program Files\Streaming Assistant\driver\bin\win64\RVRPlugin.ini and change controllertype=3 to controllertype=1. This makes the Pico software "emulate"/pretend the controllers to be Rift CV1 controllers (as opposed to Pico/Quest 2 controllers by default).I think some SteamVR games can't quite handle newer generic controllers yet, so this fallback is a workaround. credit to  Now that i actually got to play the game: pretty nice. obviously.

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't expecting to jump into VR, and then Alyx came along. I don't even have Half-Life nostalgia, since I barely made progress in the first two games. I could see why people enjoyed them, but my tastes just weren't there to get me to commit to playing through. Portal and Portal 2 were my big Valve turning points. VR wasn't on my radar for the normal reasons: extra expense, cumbersome hardware to wear, no games I was seeing  as must-play. Then Alyx was announced. The trailer got me. I knew I wanted to see where they would take the technology.Since I didn't already have an investment in VR and wanted the full Alyx experience, I took the plunge and put myself on the waiting list for the full Index VR kit after some dragging of my feet. After a couple of months of waiting, I finally received it a week and a half ago, and I just finished the game tonight. Holy crap. Now I know what people are talking about when they say "immersion." Being in such a richly-designed game world, peering around corners, having enemies get right up in your face.... It's an experience I want everyone to have. This being my first VR experience, I'm not familiar with the progression of the technology, but now is the time to embrace it. Yes, the headset display technology can improve some more, but my jaw has dropped with where they are right now. It also seemed wrong not to enjoy it on the sound system I've pumped so much money into, but the slightly off-ear speakers do an incredible job of informing you where you are in the space.The game itself is relentlessly engaging. The characters pulling you through the narrative portions are always entertaining, and the puzzles and enemies filling out the remaining majority of the game are never phoned in. Even when there are variations on a theme, they tweak them enough to keep them fresh. I'm not the most committed game player anymore, but this is one I had to see through to the end. And what can you say about the production value except "OMG"? They took their time giving the world a crazy amount of detail, and I'm going to credit this authenticity with making me almost fall over once because I thought I could lean on an in-game object. The whole game is a blast, with AAA polish ensuring its place as one of the all-time greats.To sum up, even if I don't get too into other VR games, Half-Life: Alyx has single-handedly justified my $1000 Valve Index purchase.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

Summary: It is a good game and with the workshop now open I highly recommend it to any who are considering this purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a 62 y.o. retired male, definitely one of the more mature people who've played this game. It was only two years ago during the pandemic when I had lost a patient I was operating on during ER. She was the first one I've lost. At first I only thought of it as "just another respiratory illness" among the multitude of seniors flooding in. But a child no older than my 7 y.o. niece? I pulled everything out of my bag of tricks but there was only so many treatments for advanced pneumonia-like symptoms. They said hundreds of thousands are dying all around the world, but for me, a child is a child. A life is a life. Did I choose the wrong profession? Am i betraying God's will by trying to save those who shan't be saved? Was my oath taken in pride and vanity. I had to leave, hoping if fate lures me back I'd reconsider it then.Retirement was as expected: someone who's been working his ass off his entire life rarely has time for personal endeavors. And with the pandemic, inability to travel. My friends and colleagues thought I was crazy not to be living it up and doing everything I wanted to do now that I'm out of the grind. My take: I'm such a pathetic wretch, I don't even have one single hobby. A confidant recommended I check out the tech industry, starting with VR (as it was also making the medical rounds). Enter Half-Life: Alyx. Wow, while I was cutting up bodies the nerds were busy cutting up circuits. The visuals in VR are simply stunning. Sure this dystopian sci-fi setting was not mellowing out the lockdown mood but the writing was more intriguing than most Hollywood scripts. Every dead body I passed by reminded me of the collateral casualties of recent times; I proceeded uneasily. But the last straw: I had to jab myself with the medical syringe...the flashback was like someone woke you up from a dream with a pail of cold water. Natalie? Was that her name? I shut off everything right then and there.A few months passed and I tried out a few more hobbies, one more intense than the other: mountain biking, sportsbike track days; yes, things more suited for those 30 years junior but concentration or death kept recent events off my mind. Recently, the FB metaverse in the news reminded me of VR and this game. Although I dreaded having to open drawers and doors like an OCD person, I jumped back into the rabbit hole. Maybe enough time had passed, but I think hearing Alyx's voice helped me push through to completion this time. I can't credit this game enough for helping me through the unknowing guilt, but I felt a tremendous weight lifted off my shoulder and am at peace. This game is a life saver, and will never be uninstalled.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

Other than that, this is the most amazing video game experience I ever had, and I'm a first time VR user. Got my VR headset as an experiment just to see what VR is like. _childDocuments_.review: I presumed this would be a very different experience, more standing around doing puzzles in rooms, but it's still laid out like a normal Half-Life game, there's a lot of moving around, exploring the city, traveling through tunnels. The action may be a little less than normal because everything is so much more intense in VR; a headcrab scuttling out of the shadows is no joke. Reloading it made more into a gameplay mechanic. Although I've played HL Alyx using the non-VR mod - and it's a solid piece of work -  it pales in comparison to playing it at high resolution in VR.  I'm guessing having a 4090 GPU helps but WOW - what a truly immersive experience. I was originally in the camp of "how much difference can it make?", but in reality, it's a totally different game and such an incredible experience. I can't recommend this game highly enough. The developers should be proud of their achievement.For info: =======I played using Steam VR with my PC connected to a router via Ethernet and then 5.1 Wireless to the headset. I chose DirectX11 over Vulkan and also set the priority of OVRServer_64.exe to Real-time in Task Manager.  With the headset plugged in using a 5 metre cable for power, I've enjoyed some lengthy sessions without needing to recharge.I've also played The Room VR - this time in the headset rather than on the PC and used Quest Optimiser to make it crystal clear, fast and sharp. Another great program.

_childDocuments_.review: Half-Life: Alyx is more than just a game - it's an innovative, immersive journey that dramatically reshapes the landscape of virtual reality gaming. As my first serious foray into the VR realm, I found it to be the most refreshing and original gaming experience I've encountered since Half-Life 2 in 2005 and World of Warcraft in 2007.Stepping into City 17 in VR is a breathtaking experience, offering a sense of immersion that truly makes the player feel a part of this dystopian universe. The lovingly detailed environments and the realistic physics interactions make the world come alive like never before.One of the core strengths of Half-Life: Alyx is its seamless marriage of the familiar and the new. The game embraces the beloved elements that have come to define the Half-Life series - the menacing headcrabs, the shambling zombies, the relentless Combine soldiers, and the iconic arsenal of weapons are all faithfully represented in their VR incarnations.However, it's the introduction of new mechanics - specifically designed to take full advantage of the VR platform - that truly propels this game into uncharted territory. Whether it's the intuitive gravity gloves that allow you to manipulate objects with a flick of your wrist or the innovative ways to interact with the environment, these mechanics open up exciting possibilities that evolve and expand all the way to the game's thrilling finale.Alyx also offers a compelling extension to the Half-Life lore. As a prequel to Half-Life 2, the story is richly layered and is sure to pique the interest of series veterans and newcomers alike. It pushes me to revisit the previous episodes to piece together the intricate narrative tapestry that Valve has so masterfully woven.The game also brings a whole new level of physicality to the Half-Life experience. Crouching in your room, using in-game objects for cover while evading Combine fire is a wholly unique experience that no traditional keyboard and mouse setup can replicate. It's both hilarious and intense, as the VR environment drives an unmatched level of player engagement.Half-Life: Alyx is an exceptional addition to the Half-Life series, that utilizes VR to its fullest potential, improving on an already brilliant formula in groundbreaking ways.Lastly, I would like to say that while I managed to snag this game at a 50% discount, it is undeniably worth every penny of the full price. If you're on the fence about making the purchase - don't waste your time on waiting. Valve has once again raised the bar in the realm of gaming, proving that they still possess the magic touch. Half-Life: Alyx is a must-have for any VR gamer.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't normally leave reviews, but this is one of, if not the best game I have ever played out of every genre, and I own over 140 games. It is worth every cent, and every year spent waiting. I will break down what makes this game good.Expectations: I had high expectations, the kind people tell you not to have because you'll get disappointed. Yet somehow, Valve still managed to exceed them. Half-Life Alyx is to 2020 what Half-Life 2 was to 2004.Performance and Graphics:The graphics in this game are so good that they should be impossible. VR headsets are usually in 1440p and have two screens requireing two ingame views, this lowers performance requiring most VR games to sacrifice graphics quality. Alyx does not do this, valve instead used insane levels of optimization.  The only time I had performance issues was when there was a loading screen, or within the first 5 seconds of loading a map.Immersion:Lighting: Most of the lighting appears to be a prerendered ray-tracing, a high quality, easy on performance alternative to real-time ray-tracing. this means that instead of tracing light every frame, it traces light when the map loads. This allows insanely high-quality lighting without melting your pc. Light sources that are not part of the world, such as the flashlight cast shadows as you would expect in real life.Sound: This will vary by headset, but with my Oculus cv1, it sounded great. the sound design is just as great as the previous games but has all the improvements you would expect from new technologyInterface: This will also vary by headset, but the controls are nice and intuitive. Weapons work as they would in real life, and haptic feedback is used perfectly.Environments: The environments are perfect, they are less linear than in Half-Life 2, but it still naturally pushes you in the right direction. The Xen infestations look amazing, they have a perfect mix of beauty, creepynes, and disgust. The game takes full advantage of the animated destruction that you see in other valve games, and it's absolutely amazing in VR.Gameplay:VR combat is far more difficult, so having the combat sequences from Half-Life 2 would be impossible without making the player a bullet sponge. Because of this, the gameplay revolves more around the environment and emotions. This game goes all out on the horror in some places, this game does have a dedicated "horror chapter" like Ravenholm, but it is so much more terrifying. The game does have some good comic relief though, to avoid scaring you away. When you do have real combat sections, of which there are a perfect amount of, it is more fun and exhilarating than combat in any other game. Alyx does not have an HEV suit, and VR makes combat far more difficult. Throwing grenades requires hand-eye coordination, aiming is far more difficult (although there are expensive laser sight upgrades for every weapon), and standing out in the open WILL kill you. Because of this, combat is a lot more tactical and slow, but also intense. Because of this, you can find yourself pinned down by covering fire, peeking around corners, or using sound to aim because it's too dangerous to get out of cover. Crouching behind cover while bullets fly past me is one of the coolest gaming experiences I've ever had.Story:The story is amazing, and VR is an excellent way of triggering the intended emotions. Half-Life has always had surreal moments, such as the G-Man speeches, and Half-Life Alyx would not be complete without similar sequences. I won't go into detail because I don't want to spoil things, but they are absolutely jaw-dropping in VR, even better than the sequence in episode 2.Recommendation:Buy it. If you don't have a VR headset, buy one. If you don't have a good PC, upgrade. It is 100% worth it to buy VR just for this game, you don't necessarily need one of the best headsets of course, but I would recomend something decent (some anti-fog lens cleaner would also be a good investment).

The hard thing about VR is that it's really hard to explain to somebody who doesn't play VR how good a game can feel to play. Gameplay videos on YouTube do the game a disservice and don't give you a proper sense of what this game feels like to play.As Valve said in a recent interview, when people play it, they'll understand why this game was built for VR. This really does feel like a proper HL game, only far more immersive.If Valve were to create HL3 in the future, it would be a big step backwards if it wasn't a VR game after seeing what is possible with HL:A.Played perfectly fine on Oculus Quest with Link on a GTX 1080.Edit: after finishing the game, I'm floored by how amazing the entire experience was to the very end. _childDocuments_.review: It's easily the best VR title out there if you're interested in the HL franchise. Chock full of great set pieces that really ramp up towards the end, fun puzzles that only give you subtle hints on how to approach them, and surprisingly dynamic combat allowing for lots of ways to play out the fights. The gravity gloves work way better than I thought they would and the motion of flicking items towards me got addicting. Its guns are lacking in variety but the weapon upgrades you invest in throughout the story don't make it feel that way, you have all the weapons you really need for the situations the game throws at you.It's also worth mentioning that the game is very comfortable even on continuous movement mode, I was able to play it in big 3-4 hour blocks without feeling any motion sickness (a rarity for me) so kudos to them for putting in the time and effort towards subduing that. I'm playing on a Rift S so I'm missing out on that crisp Index refresh rate and resolution, but the game still looked gorgeous to me and I rarely noticed any jagged pixels or blurry vision. My Rift S controllers worked quite well for everything too and the Knuckles controllers aren't really required unless you want to become a virtuoso that one time a fully playable piano shows up.Valve wasn't kidding when they said to at least play HL2:E2 before this as you'd only glean half of what's going on in the ending otherwise. I don't think  was expecting that twist and I'm so excited to see what they do next!

_childDocuments_.review: Alyx really defines what a AAA VR title should be doing in terms of environment interactions. Reaching out and just pushing buttons, flipping switches, tossing and catching items between hands, brushing aside props to find ammo, and so much more. Its not as "physically" perfect for these smaller interactions, but that's to focus on comfort and immersion. These changes make it more natural and intuitive to just swap items between hands, grab items from the environment (the gravity gloves are amazing), and quickly reload without fumbling to get the magazine in *just right*.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: It is a great re-entry into the Half Life universe. It does a great job of using VR in game and aside from times where it doesn't allow you to use the flashlight (it automatically turns on during darkness) when I wish I could, it is tons of fun with loads of suspense and action. The main downside so far is no crowbar starting weapon (a melee weapon would be awesome but probably cumbersome to use) and sometimes it feels like there's backtracking to do which isn't completely obvious at first (FYI: if you go down a path and you end up where you started, you probably need to backtrack).

_childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting for 14 years for this and bought a VR headset to play it. This was my first VR game and it was totally worth it. If you're a hardcore fan of the series like me, you'll like it. Since it is my first VR game this will not be a comparison-like review. This is just my experience and observation. (played with a Rift S)In Oculus' demo, smooth locomotion was a nightmare for me, it was unnaturally fast. In this game, it felt dizzy at first, but I got used to it fast. I saw some people complaining about the game being so slow, but for my taste it was perfect. I used blink teleportation time to time as well. Moving around in the game was fine for me.Gunplay feels satisfying. Using shotgun and smg one-handed felt weird at first, then I understood that it was the right choice. My only complain is, there might had been a quicker way to change the dominant hand for the weapon;however, it's not something game-breaking anyway. Reloading, shooting feels really good. I don't know if it's just me, but aiming down the sight with the base pistol felt a little bit off. I don't know why. After acquiring the sight upgrade, I could use it with confidence. Shotgun felt a little bit inferior at mid-range. Its range could've been tweaked a bit. SMG is just perfect (especially with laser sight).Alyx used to use multi-tool in previous games, remember? She used to hack stuff. Now we're doing it! What's not to love. Puzzles were neither too easy nor too hard, they were totally enjoyable for me.Dealing with enemies... To be honest, headcrabs were overwhelming for me. Especially  ones. I hated them back then, I still hate them now :). Combines' movements being medium-paced (as the devs stated) was really a sweet spot. If there were fast enemies (combines, fast zombies etc.), it would be way too overwhelming in VR. I also liked having different types of combines. It adds variety to your gunplay as well. You don't shoot the same weapon for a standart combine or a shielded one. It affects the way you play and makes you think. And I'm not even talking about the gloves. I'll be looking for this in other VR games... (or mod them if possible like skyrim).Gameplay is totally 10 for me. (experienced with a medium-quality earphone)As you all know, music and sound was not really the strong suit of previous games. But in this one, music changing according to the situation, sound cues were used right. I liked it. I don't know if it was my earphone simply not being enough (got a brand new), gun sounds were a bit low. I think that especially the shotgun could've been stronger. But still, sound is 9 for me. (played everything on Ultra, fidelity level forced maximum - RTX 3070)At first, looked perfect. Then at some parts, I was heavily disappointed. Then I figured out why its graphics changes on its own. The game has a dynamic system that manipulates it. I looked for it online, and found some launch commands to bypass it. Then it turned to a something magical. These were the commands.I liked everything about it. Textures, particle effects, holograms. At some part () I experienced some performance drops even with a rig like mine. But again, it wasn't game-breaking. Graphics are 10 for me.p.s. edit : cause I literally (14 to 27) finished high school, university, served in the army, and got a job while waiting for it.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: If there is one game a user with VR headset has to play. It's certainly this. At the time I am writing, Alyx is very much way above the VR competition. While some sacrifices had to be made, to make it a VR title, it's the first game I have played, where the number of advantages of using VR and room-scale movement manages to outweigh these sacrifices.It's also great to see Valve's signature environment storytelling together with the environment leading the player be back with full force. I have really missed that... and yeah, sure  - the latter has its flaws, cause you are always risking the player getting stuck, by not telling him precisely what to do in the area, but nevertheless - when done right (like Alyx does it), I am going to prefer getting stuck than being told what to do especially that - with me now being a game developer - it makes me appreciate how much thought was put to make these levels look so well, tell such great small stories and at the same time not be swarmed with detail to the point, where environment hints become invisible as such putting graphics over gameplay. It is really some fantastic level design work and the number of level design iterations had to be crazy to pull it off.But it's not just story, graphics (as for VR standard), and performance where Alyx shines. The gameplay is a Half-Life's signature mix of action setpieces, first-person cutscenes (where Valve once again, outdone themselves with how naturally these facial animations look, while simultaneously having characters react to the player's actual existence in the world - like come on, it's 2021 now and somehow this is still a problem!) and light environment puzzles, and it's the player to world interaction where everything just *clicks*. Half-Life 2 was already going crazy on having a highly interactive physics system and while pretty much nobody in the industry managed to match Valve's physics precision in over 15 years since Half-Life 2 release, Alyx takes it much farther, somehow managing not to be an outright broken mess. Sure, occasional physics glitches happen (as they pretty much have to with such absurd dependence of physics), but the result achieved by the world objects reacting so naturally to the player's actions is well worth the price. If anything, maybe few more things could be even more interactive (as you often find objects that could work as melee weapons), but at this point - it really is scraping the barrel for issues.If I were to have any major complaint - I guess it's the stability issues I've experienced with SteamVR, where my Index would often freeze (especially during loading) forcing a full game restart. Other than that - this is also one of the smoothest, least vomit-inducing VR experiences I have had so far (to a point, where - if the game manages not to crash - I could be playing it for 2+ hours and not for a moment feel sick).So yeah. If you have VR headset capable of running Alyx - get Alyx!
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Came with my Index purchase. Played in continuous motion mode, blink movement when backtracking. Took me 16 hours to look at everything, 4 hour chunks. Motion sick only once. No story spoilers here.The experience was phenomenal, the amount of polish on familiar half life fixtures blew my mind. The fidelity of Alyx’ assets made most of the experience beyond real, human faces are hard to do however and while expertly done I think was the thing that would most often ‘pull me out’ of my immersion. In every other facet of the game I found it wholly believable, just organically interacting with physical objects, puzzle solving, summoning supplies, fluidly managing your weapons and fighting various enemies would suck me right into the universe. I felt like I was there for a little bit, and as a long time fan that was beautiful.Mechanically distinct from the popular ‘Boneworks’ title I found myself comparing the two and asking why I can't do ‘x’ like in Boneworks. Most missed was physical objects hurting enemies and faster continual locomotion. As for Alyx I like the weapon swapping better. By the end I didn’t feel like gameplay suffered in Alyx, distinct designs but equally workable imo. I have little full scale vr experience besides these titles.(04/26/20)Personally I had a lot of bugs. My lit up and otherwise functional controllers not tracking my hand(either or) and dropping vr hands to the floor 4x times through my run. Fingers stuck open or closed, coming and going 10x(usually not game breaking).Run of the mill total game crashes 5x. I accidentally broke sequences 2x, gathering items before I was told to. Lastly a knack for teleporting into holes and bypassing death barriers 6x!Overall, a very fluid and dynamic experience. An alien world that was wholly believable to me while I was in it. Would recommend wholeheartedly. Don’t kill yourself getting an Index, the lovely screen and finger tracking are sprinkles on a delicious frosted cupcake but IMO the polished story telling and realistic world is most of the ride.As for VR vs screen based gamers, you can definitely experience the story on a screen. The experience of HL:Alyx is greater than the sum of its parts however. All the little organic things you do in-world is what makes it next level.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Half-Life: Alyx just set the bar for VR games, and gaming as a whole. Starting off, 'Alyx' is a glorious spectacle. You begin the game somewhere in Eastern Europe, looking over this third or fourth story apartment building balcony, facing the monolithic Citadel in City 17, helicopters flying overhead while giant combine-hoisting striders stomp around. This alone could be stared at and experienced for hours, but the day must be saved. Alyx, Eli Vance's daughter, is apart of a yet-fully-realized resistance crew fighting for humanity against the alien Combine invasion. You quickly meet a friend of your father's named Russell, who gives you a pair of special gloves named, aptly, "Russells." These gloves function essentially as Alyx's gravity gun, albeit much more refined for virtual reality. A quick flick of the wrist sends any item flying across a room to meet your grip. Once you get the hang of it, finding loot is a breeze. Alyx's gun play is bar-none. Early game fights pits you against shambling zombies, armed with a trusty pistol given to you by Russell. Half an hour into the game, you'll have enough of something called 'resin' to start upgrading your armament. Having my eye on a laser sight eventually paid off, although I did have to collect quite a bit of resin before I was capable of upgrading. Walking around with a gun should feel safer, but in Alyx, having your gun out is a sign of fear. You really need to be aware of your positioning and aim, because one wrong advance could get you overwhelmed with enemies. Most of what happens in early fights could only be described as terrifying. Thinking I had any amount of experienced VR chops was a mistake, as I was quickly whimpering in fear once headcrabs started jumping at my face. This game definitely has a way of making you feel very vulnerable at times, a VR development tactic that works wonderfully. Eventually, stumbling over your reloads will be a distant memory, as a mastery of the controls will be required for combat success. This game is extremely detailed. Down to the labels on errant soda cans lying about, (which you can crush by squeezing the Index controllers) the weight of everything you pick up, the soft interface sounds from your Russell's, Valve has created something so sincere that I really feel completely immersed in this world when I play it. Throughout 'Alyx,' you will find yourself stopping to smell the roses, however bloody and disgusting those proverbial 'roses' may be. Valve directed so much attention into the worldbuilding, traversing any one level takes a ridiculous amount of time. Crouching down to really examine that dead zombie's bursting guts, or spending a good while manipulating the corpse of a dead headcrab to get a good idea of what hell awaits those whom they pounce upon, will make you find yourself saying, "oh ♥♥♥♥." Each area you walk in is handcrafted to perform as a highly polished backdrop for overwhelmingly detailed gameplay.The game isn't without it's slower portions - though few and far between, there was a couple moments I felt less tense and more bored by the obvious collect-a-thons for catching up non-explorative players with resin count, as a form of balance. Don't get me wrong, I'm all for collecting the resin, but these moments were a little too apparent for my taste. Having said that, it is hardly a complaint worth mentioning. Collecting anything takes you through gorgeously haunting hallways, sewers and subway trains, so there is always something to enjoy. The story of 'Alyx' has been modernly crafted to fit the bill of today's industry essentials, and then some. It is immediately apparent that Valve is so giddily excited to let players visit the world and lore of Half-Life, and give their fans a sublime return to form. This is the full experience Valve wanted to create after Half-Life 2: Episode 2, they just didn't know it yet, as the technology just wasn't there. Well, it's 2020, and we're closer to the Matrix than we have ever been.'Alyx' is very fun. There is a lot I have yet to do in this game, and a lot I don't want to tell anyone who hasn't played this game yet - I hope that what I have said, however, interests you immensely, because I can confidently say this is the best VR game that has ever been made, and has absolutely created a new precedent for the medium.*MUST PLAY*

_childDocuments_.review: Been playing for about 2 hours. Visually it's spectacular, the physics are good, not great, especially when holding onto handles. The facial capture animations are absolutely insane and you really feel immersed.That being said, weapon handling is atrocious. My absolutely biggest gripe about this game is having to grab over your SHOULDER to get ammo to reload. WHAT?!?!?! Every single FPS in VR has you get ammo from your hip, you know, like you normally would. Having to reach over your should to get ammo is incredibly inconvenient and feels terrible. I lose precious seconds while in combat because I instinctively grab to my hip for ammo to reload, LIKE EVERY OTHER GAME DOES IT!!! I honestly don't know how you can mess something that simple up so horribly. Hip for ammo, shoulder and under arm for storage, IT'S NOT THAT HARD!!!Oh and then there's movement. Walking is so insanely slow it's basically useless. You have to resort to blinking everywhere if you don't want to spend 90% of your time walking around in the game instead of actually playing. Why is there no run option??Also you can't drop your weapons. What's the point of trying to create a fully immersive game when you can't drop your gun when you open your hand? The entire point of the Knuckles controllers is to make it so you can open your hand and still have the controller attached to your hand. The most immersive thing you can do for the game is make weapons droppable so that when you're in combat and you accidentally open your hand you're punished like you would be in real life and have to pick up the gun again. The game treats you like a baby.Edit: 3/25/2020Perhaps my biggest issue with this game is just utter lack of VR exclusive interactions. You want to switch guns? Press a button. That's literally it. What do other games do? They make you physically reach for another weapon because that's the one thing flat games can't do. But what do you do in HL:A? You press a button. That's it. This was supposed to be the crown jewel of VR interactions and they remove the most essential part of VR gameplay.Edit: 1/31/2021 Here's a more detailed writeup.Half Life: Alyx is the most overrated game of all time and people are praising Valve for doing the minimum for a game.Here are the things it does well:Graphics are top of the lineSome physics are goodGood lite-horror gameAnimation is the best availableAAA voice actingWeapon upgrades are cool but stop short.Here are the things it doesn't do well, or just doesn't do at all:MELEE. Seriously? Zero melee in a Half Life game, in ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ VR of all mediums? I'm not asking for a crowbar because that's Gordon's thing but jesus ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ christ how many people played the game thinking they would be able to beat down enemies with anything in the environment? Bricks, planks, other enemies, pipes, literally anything. It's a VR game and there's no melee. It's absolutely insulting.Severe lack of weapons 3 weapons, that's it. You're not forced to choose what weapons to carry so you just go through the game having everything you need and only have to rely on ammo. I get the old games didn't have an inventory max, but in VR you absolutely should have to choose what weapons you're able to carry with you. No crossbow, no RPG, no revolver. You can't grab weapons from enemies like you can in pretty much every other VR game ever made. No 2 handing weapons since they're bolted to your hand.Weapon switching is an absolute joke What was Valve's thinking? "Let's make a game in virtual reality where you can literally reach around your body to grab weapons from different slots except in ours you just press a button, SO IMMERSIVE" Every single other VR game I have ever played has weapon slots on your person. They go on your hips, shoulders and back. Pavlov, Contractors, H3VR, Boneworks, Onward, etc. They all do it because it's the biggest thing you can't do in a pancake game. What does HLA do? They give you a single button to press. This was the biggest immersion break for me by far.Reloading happens from your shoulder for some stupid reason Almost every single other game you get ammo from your hip or a vest. Zero Caliber, Contractors, Onward, Boneworks, H3VR, etc. all do this. HLA makes you grab it from your shoulder. Why? Every game I listed allows you to grab it from your hip or chest even when ducked behind cover. There's no reason for it.The game is basically on rails There's little to no allowance on your movement. You're in a cramped corridor for 90% of the game with no way forward except straight. They give you this amazing city to explore, except you can't explore it. You know what would have been a good game? An open world HLA where you have to avoid patrols, find allies in apartments and would give room for an interesting story.The story I guess there's a story? It's not particularly interesting.Teleporting movement and slow walking speed You have to teleport everywhere unless you want the slowest walking speed in any game I have every played. You can't jump up or down to a lower level, you have to teleport. Valve said it's because new players aren't used to smooth movement, but this is a simple addition for veteran players that should have been included. You should be able to sprint and jump.You can't drop weapons You know what's REALLY scary in a horror game? Losing your weapons. This goes along with the lack of melee and the inability to pick up weapons from enemies. Your guns are literally bolted to your hand, you cannot drop them, they are there whether you want them or not. Why is this an issue? Because you have controllers that sense when you are grabbing things, but when you open your hand you don't drop your weapons and it breaks immersion completely. The thing I was looking forward to most about this game was survival. I wanted to burn through my ammo, drop a weapon and pick up another from a dead enemy. I wanted to have to fight tooth and nail for ammo by beating enemies with anything in the environment like Boneworks but you can't. When you open your hand and expect to drop something and it sticks to your hand, it destroys the immersion. Boneworks does this PERFECTLY where you are in a fight, surrounded by enemies, you panic and drop your weapon and have to fight melee by grabbing enemies and keeping them away from yourself while you try to force grab your dropped weapon. HLA? Nope. You can't do any of that. They introduced perhaps the best grabbing system in a game and it's used entirely to grab ammo and resin, that's it.There's more but that's what I can think of off the top of my head. Every praises it for being the best VR game every made, despite it lacking the most fundamental and basic VR features that are included in every single other game. Just a massive disappointment for veteran players.

_childDocuments_.review: Half-Life: Alyx is nothing short of a triumph in the realm of virtual reality gaming. Developed by Valve Corporation, this installment in the iconic Half-Life series has set a new standard for immersive gameplay and storytelling within the VR landscape.Graphics and Immersion: 5/5The visual fidelity of Half-Life: Alyx is nothing short of breathtaking. From the intricate details of the environment to the lifelike character animations, every aspect of the game is designed to draw players into the dystopian world of City 17. The Source 2 engine truly shines, delivering an unparalleled level of realism that enhances the overall immersion.Gameplay: 4.5/5The gameplay mechanics of Half-Life: Alyx are a testament to the potential of VR gaming. The intuitive controls, precise interactions, and realistic physics create an experience that feels both natural and responsive. The game cleverly integrates VR features, requiring players to physically reach for items, solve puzzles, and engage in combat with a level of tactility that traditional gaming can't match.Story and Atmosphere: 4.5/5True to the legacy of the Half-Life series, Alyx doesn't disappoint in terms of narrative depth and atmosphere. The storytelling is engaging, weaving seamlessly into the existing lore while introducing new characters and plot twists. The oppressive ambiance of City 17 is palpable, and the game succeeds in maintaining a sense of tension throughout the entire experience.Sound Design: 5/5The audio in Half-Life: Alyx is a standout feature, contributing significantly to the overall atmosphere. From the haunting echoes of distant Combine chatter to the subtle creaking of dilapidated buildings, every sound is meticulously crafted. The use of 3D audio technology further enhances the sense of space and directionality, adding another layer to the immersive experience.VR Innovation: 5/5Half-Life: Alyx pushes the boundaries of what VR can achieve. It not only demonstrates the potential for narrative-driven VR games but also serves as a showcase for innovative design and interaction possibilities within the medium. The game sets a new standard for VR titles and has undoubtedly paved the way for future developments in the industry.Half-Life: Alyx is a tour de force in virtual reality gaming. It successfully marries the rich storytelling of the Half-Life universe with the immersive capabilities of VR technology. While the need for VR hardware might limit accessibility for some, those with the means to experience it will find themselves transported into one of the most compelling and memorable gaming experiences of recent years. Valve has not only revived a beloved franchise but has also redefined the expectations for what is possible in the realm of virtual reality gaming.

_childDocuments_.review: Half-Life: Alyx is a great game. It's an awesome VR game too.What you need to understand is that Alyx is not the end-all-be-all of VR. There are other arguably better experiences out there. Alyx is not trying to be the best VR game, it's simply trying to be the best Half-Life game it can be and it happens to be in VR.However, what it does do best are graphics and exploration. And boy are these great. Finding resin in remote corners of each level gives players a reason to grab every little prop to see the amazing detail Valve has put into them. You'll find yourself just looking at your hands in disbelief to see the tiny capacitors and wires that make up the gravity gloves. "How does this look so good and run like this?"(It's a little CPU heavy, though. Just FYI)I have played this all the way through with an Oculus Rift CV1 and the Valve Index. The experiences are pretty much the same. Which might be surprising! The resolution on the Index is insane at first, and the hand presence is incredible. But after you get over the initial wow factor, you just play the game! And it plays great on any headset you can get your hands on.TL;DR-It's got amazing graphics!-Great story.-I have first hand experiences on a low-end headset (CV1) and the Index and can confirm a great experience on both. -This game is a little CPU heavy, so make sure you PC is at least above the minimum.

_childDocuments_.review: Still probably THE title to play if you're curious about the potential of VR in gaming. The sheer quantity of content, and the care that went into preserving the Half Life cannon are staggering.However, the real achievement of this game is in the UX. It took decades of trial and error before 2D interfaces were easy to use. VR resets the clock, and many games are ruined by complex, jarring interfaces. This problem is HARD! And the solutions it invents are why Half-Life Alyx is milestone in virtual reality.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, this is by far the best video game I have ever played in my life, and even if I wasn't a Half-Life fan, it still would be.I can't think of any flaws. Valve has done it again. This literally raises the bar for gaming, and for VR.The combat is very intuitive, has some unique aspects, and offers a good amount of challenge and intensity. The many ways in which you can interact with the world are extremely detailed and well-thought out. The puzzles in this game are rewarding and not as obvious as previous games, which I like.The design of the environments, sound, and ambience is also incredible. Considering that this game takes place in city buildings, what the environments ended up being are actually very stunning.The story and the ending was also very hype in my opinion, and felt very satisfying and exciting.It's been 12 years since I played Episode 2, and all I can say is that the wait was worth it. I really hope this series continues. For a long time, I doubted Valve and felt like they didn't care about Half-Life anymore. But seeing this game, it's clear that they have insane talent and skills after all this time. I'm sorry for doubting them.Overall, this has to be the best video game of all time, and it completely raises the bar for VR gaming and gaming in general.

_childDocuments_.review: It's been 12 long years. 12 full years and a few extra months and Valve decided to release a VR only Half-Life prequel with demanding specs with a voiced protagonist. And somehow, not only is it a fantastic game but it's a worthy addition to the Half-Life series.Pros- The visuals are phenomenal, everything is beautifully crafted. Props from HL2 are recreated with high attention to detail, and new assets fit right in with the series as previous games established.- The best VR gameplay I've experienced. It's a full, real video game with highly polished mechanics and it's clear that lots of thought went into transitioning the Half-Life experience. For example, there are 3 weapons, but they all have a good use and upgrades to keep them important throughout the entire game. Magazines and other important items glow to let you see them easily, health packs are replaced with small items you can keep with you while you play, and they've added real interactivity to things that used to be a single button press, without getting too complicated. It's intuitive and easy to understand.- The writing, especially dialogue, is some of the tightest I've seen in a game in years. I didn't like Portal 2's focus on story and cutscenes and jokes but unlike there, you aren't forced to stop and listen outside of a few very short scenes. The jokes are better, the characters feel natural. For the overarching story, everything fits together and gives the player clear motive and a reason for what they're doing at all times. It straddles the line between being big and feeling like a real accomplishment without making past events in the series seem smaller than it in comparison.- Music is great, it fits the series very well and that's made clear when the game starts playing music from past Half-Life games alongside it. The music fits the encounters and scenarios it's played in, and it's just really well made in general.- Plenty of fangasm moments that reference older games and made me freak out while playing. Cons- I dunno, there aren't many. New voice actors for existing characters are a bit jarring, but not much can really be done about that.If your PC can handle it and you have access to VR, buy this game.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, ♥♥♥♥ yeah, Half-Life game after 12 long years.The game play is very smooth, the weapons are cool, customizing is a real thing, and it's all a ton of fun! The looting from what I can tell influences the exploration of the environment rather than just run through killing everything. My only complaint, is the locomotion. Valve. Guys. You gotta address this issue. Vive locomotion controls are very clunky and uncomfortable. _childDocuments_.review: * * * WARNING * * * This review contains information about the ending of Half Life 2: Episode 2.The most wonderful gaming experience of my life. I've just finished it, and bawled my eyes out at the ending. I think you'd need a heart of stone not to, and I believe that anyone else who, like me, had pretty much given up hope of the story ever continuing will understand and feel the same. Damn, I'm getting sentimental in my old age!I'm pushing 60, and have been playing Half Life games for over 20 years. Shortly before this one was released I replayed HL2: Episode 2 for the first time in several years; I find the sense of triumph and achievement after the final, frantic Strider battle in that game, and the subsequent launch of the rocket that closes the portal, so powerful that I can no longer bring myself to watch Eli's death and Alyx's heartbreak, and have to quit before the end.Thank you for this game, Valve, from the bottom of my heart. It's a masterpiece of game design _and_ story-telling. In technical and gameplay terms you've hit the ball clean out of the ground, just as you did with Half Life and HL2. I spent hundreds of pounds on an Oculus Rift S headset and some major hardware upgrades just to play this game, and it was worth every penny. You've made an old man very, very happy.Side note: the text box into which I've typed this review flags up mis-spelt words, but right-clicking on them doesn't invoke options to correct them, in the way other sites' spellcheckers do. Somehow, that strikes me as _so_ 'Valve'; it's as if they're saying, "We'll point out what you've done wrong, but we won't tell you how to fix it"!

_childDocuments_.review: FOR NEWCOMERS TO THE HALF LIFE SERIES:YOU DO NOT HAVE TO PLAY THE PREVIOUS GAMES TO APPRECIATE EVERYTHING THIS GAME HAS TO OFFER.If you are like me you have no desire to go back and play the original games. I watched the 2 part Gaming bolt video that recaps the story of 1, 2, and episodes 1 & 2 and it filled me in to the point where I was blown away by certain story beats in Alyx just like someone who played the old games would be too. I would say at the very least watch the Gaming Bolt recap, but having played through the game I can say that it isn't 100% necessary. The stories of these games aren't super lore rich like Game of Thrones, and you won't be caught off guard with the different names and places being thrown at you. The Half Life series seems to thrive more off of the characters and how they deal with a world changing event. As for the game itself it is nothing short of a amazing by video game standards, and a masterpiece by VR standards.

_childDocuments_.review: This is my first time playing a Half-Life game. Im currently on chapter 5. From the moment I began playing, I was immersed in a thrilling story and gameplay that felt like I was actually there in the gaming world. The graphics were incredible, further adding to the feeling of being part of the action as I took on the bad guys. It was truly an amazing experience and one that leaves me hopeful for what holds in store for virtual reality gaming when it becomes more mainstream.The level of detail in this game was unparalleled. Every aspect from character design to mission objectives seemed to be meticulously crafted with attention and care. As I explored the various levels, there were little details scattered about that created an atmosphere all its own - from abandoned outposts to hidden secrets made accessible only through solving puzzles or completing mini games within the larger framework of the story arc. Even on my very first playthrough, I noticed something new each time as if my playing experience would be different each time around.The combat mechanics also added to this dynamic experience of exploration - enemies were unique and varied in their abilities while also offering gripping moments of strategy required to survive some intense firefights. This meant that it was never just a mindless run-and-gun type situation; rather, each battle presented an opportunity to hone your tactics against increasingly difficult foes so you could progress further into the game's exciting plotline.Finally, I must praise how well this game utilizes VR technology. After experiencing this title with a VR headset on, it is easy to see why it has gained such acclaim amongst gamers. Being able to look around 360 degrees as if actually inside this world creates a sense of immersion which no other medium can replicate; sure enough, Half-Life: Alyx lives up to its reputation by providing players with an incredibly interactive and realistic environment where everything feels tangible and alive.All these features together make Half-Life: Alyx one of the most compelling titles in virtual reality gaming today - full of engaging experiences, sharp visuals, and tactical combat all wrapped up in one neat package! With its impressive use of VR technology coupled with an excellent narrative structure and entertaining gameplay loop, it's no surprise that this title is setting itself up as a contender for being one of this generation's best games ever released - and if what we've seen here is any indication at all then we are certainly in for some even more amazing experiences once virtual reality becomes more mainstream! _childDocuments_.review: Okay so just a note, before you think about buying this game I have to mention there's a spoiler for the ending of Half-Life 2 Episode 2 right at the get go. If you wish to play Half-Life and keep up with the story, don't start with this one. If you don't care about the story, you probably will after the ending of this game.This is hands down the best VR game I've played in a while. Some say it's about 10-15 hours of total playtime, though I admittedly scoured all I could for while playing it so I ran closer to 18 hours of total playtime.I started playing this game on the Oculus Rift, then swapped to Oculus Quest streamed through Virtual Desktop midway through and without a doubt this game caters to all players, no matter the headset choice. You can even play the game seated, one handed if you need that which is just awesome.The set pieces are beyond stunning, and going through City 17 has never been more enjoyable. You feel very grounded, as just another person doing their routine. A lot of lore will be thrown your way as if you don't know it, with moments where any player can understand why something is done.The trademark Half-Life humor is still here, and while admittedly coming off as dad-jokey from time to time, still feels wholesome. Alyx and Russel's dynamic are second to none, and it feels like Russel is a grandfather lending their knowledge and experience to their young ones, like Alyx. Well, as close as these two can get.The exploration feels natural, and scraping through shelves, digging through cabinets, and checking areas you might not think to pays off in the long run. It rewards you with more ammo, resin, and in some cases, interactions and easter eggs. Running low on ammo and/or health mid-combat and having to scramble for more feels like a genuine panic which got my heart racing from time to time.When combat starts, it feels great. Like every environment is a puzzle to be solved with resource management, enemy placement, and your actions. The moment it stuck with me is when I had to essentially crawl to the ground to get into cover while reloading my shotgun to fend off two combine flanking me from both sides. I shot one, turned around and shot the other while behind a pile of crates. Combat is an absolute rush when it's firing on all cylinders.I did tend to find that ammo was more scarce than health, and I wish the hard difficulty made the syringes less frequent. I always had to end up choosing what to take with me (or finding a milk basket and throwing all my syringes/grenades in it) because it ended up too cumbersome to keep around.It ends up being a fairly straightforward loop until you get to Jeff. I won't spoil that bit either, but Jeff is a nice guy and give him a hug for me when you meet him.And the ending, ooohhh god that ending. I had to go through it twice to make sure there wasn't something I was missing. Without spoilers, it will re-frame the series as a whole when you get there. But you might already have expected that.Do I recommend it? Okay, if you have a VR headset and a computer than can run VR games, then why the hell not? You've probably been waiting for a game to take advantage that the medium of VR offers from a studio with a mostly stellar track record. Or you probably just want more Half-Life. In either case, grab this game. It's the best ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ game I've played this decade so far. And there's plenty on the way to take that throne, but I won't forget this one for a while.

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible VR experience. Less a reinvention of the principles of VR than a refinement learned from the best games of the last 3 years. Albeit one with AAA production values. Having recently replayed some other Half Life titles, I would also rate this as one of the best and most consistently enjoyable of all the Half Life games. If they had replaced the 'Alyx' with a '3' I wouldn't have been disappointed. The game doesn't have the same scope and large areas as previous HL games; instead it's a much more intimate experience. You will spend most your time in courtyards, corridors and rooms. The game is as its most impressive in smaller spaces, so I'm not sure this is necessarily a negative. The game also opens up a lot in the final third.  I played on a first gen Vive with an above average rig, and it looked fantastic and played very well - it wasn't obvious that I wasn't playing on the game's native format. I was also able to run it on a different medium / below average rig and it scaled very nicely - much better than many other, less impressive VR titles. Don't be put off by the intimidating minimum specs. I'm fortunate enough to have a large play area for VR and 'walked' my way through most of the game with room scale in ~30 hours, however, there's a huge number of accessibility options for those with different set ups. I would caution though that I believe the game would have been a lot less fun if I had had a very limited play space or used a locomotive scheme to navigate. In terms of negatives, I think possibly it takes a little long for the game to 'get going'. The environments, enemies and mechanics do not develop very quickly in the first half of the game. But the second half of the game more than makes up for this. An additional negative is the fact that you will definitely end up in conflict with the cable tethering you to the PC. The game encourages you to move around and explore in a way that will twist you in knots and occasionally put you at risk of disconnecting your headset. I was able to solve this to a degree by fixing the cable half way up a wall so that it didn't trip me up, and if I stumbled, I pulled on the wall fixing and not the link box. But you may need to get creative if you plan on walking around and interacting with the game physically!In summary: great game; top tier Half Life entry; unrivalled VR experience; is slightly restricted to the limitations of current VR hardware, but not to the extent that it ruins the experience.

_childDocuments_.review:
Half-Life: Alyx is Valve's VR return to the Half-Life series. It's the story of an impossible fight against a vicious alien race known as the Combine, set between the events of Half-Life and Half-Life 2. Playing as Alyx Vance, you are humanity's only chance for survival. The Combine's control of the planet since the Black Mesa incident has only strengthened as they corral the remaining population in cities. Among them are some of Earth's greatest scientists: you and your father, Dr. Eli Vance. As founders of a fledgling resistance, you've continued your clandestine scientific activityperforming critical research, and building invaluable tools for the few humans brave enough to defy the Combine. Every day, you learn more about your enemy, and every day you work toward finding a weakness.

ABOUT GAMEPLAY IN VR:

Valve's return to the Half-Life universe that started it all was built from the ground up for virtual reality. VR was built to enable the gameplay that sits at the heart of Half-Life.

Immerse yourself in deep environmental interactions, puzzle solving, world exploration, and visceral combat.

Lean to aim around a broken wall and under a Barnacle to make an impossible shot. Rummage through shelves to find a healing syringe and some shotgun shells. Manipulate tools to hack alien interfaces. Toss a bottle through a window to distract an enemy. Rip a Headcrab off your face and throw it at a Combine soldier.

Extra content for Index owners
Customers who have purchased Valve Index hardware by the end of 2019 will have access to unique bonuses starting early next year:

* Explore environments from Half-Life: Alyx in your SteamVR Home space
* Alternate gun skins to embellish Alyx's arsenal

name: Deep Rock Galactic
detailed_description: Roadmap, Publishing, Game Editions and Discord Game Editions STANDARD EDITION The standard edition is simply the base version of Deep Rock Galactic, nothing more, nothing less. DELUXE EDITION Get the DELUXE EDITION to unlock the base game as well as three packs of Cosmetic DLC: The awesome MEGACORP, DARK FUTURE, and DAWN OF THE DREAD Packs! MASTER EDITION Includes ROUGHNECK, RIVAL TECH, and ROBOT REBELLION packs, on top of everything in the DELUXE EDITION. DWARVEN LEGACY The full package - includes the base game, all Cosmetic Packs, the Supporter Pack, and the full game soundtrack split over two volumes. About the Game Deep Rock Galactic is a 1-4 player co-op FPS featuring badass space Dwarves, 100% destructible environments, procedurally-generated caves, and endless hordes of alien monsters. 1-4 PLAYER CO-OP Work together as a team to dig, explore, and fight your way through a massive cave system filled with hordes of deadly enemies and valuable resources. You will need to rely on your teammates if you want to survive the most hostile cave systems in the galaxy! 4 UNIQUE CLASSES Pick the right class for the job. Mow through enemies as the Gunner, scout ahead and light up the caves as the Scout, chew through solid rock as the Driller, or support the team with defensive structures and turrets as the Engineer. FULLY DESTRUCTIBLE ENVIRONMENTS Destroy everything around you to reach your goal. There is no set path so you can complete your mission your way. Drill straight down to your objective or build an intricate network of paths to explore your surroundings -- the choice is yours. But proceed with caution, you don’t want to stumble into an alien swarm unprepared! PROCEDURALLY GENERATED CAVE NETWORK Explore a network of procedurally generated cave systems filled with enemies to fight and riches to collect. There’s always something new to discover and no two playthroughs are alike. HIGH-TECH GADGETS AND WEAPONS Dwarves know what they need to bring to get the job done. This means the most powerful weapons and the most advanced gadgets around - flamethrowers, gatling guns, portable platform launchers, and much, much more. LIGHT YOUR PATH The underground caves are dark and full of terrors. You will need to bring your own lights if you want to illuminate these pitch-black caverns.

_childDocuments_.review: Simply Fantastic. Online co-op hero shooter with objective based missions, rogue-lite progression, and procedurally generated fully-destructable levels. All of this in veneer of playing as space dwarf miners working for their faceless corporate overlords.It's not just a shooter, it's a game which truly treats exploration as a meaningful experience worthy of deep mechanical exploration. Even with the mini-map, it's so easy to get lost. The hero kits really incentivise cooperation. There's variety in the mission types and a number of difficulty settings to adjust to your liking. Ghost Ship Games nailed the landing and you can hardly ask for more.
_childDocuments_.name: Deep Rock Galactic

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just so POLISHED!There is so much attention to minor details, small animations, that just make the game awesome! The atmosphere is top notch, the gameplay is fluid, the weapons feel good, the mining feels good, and you cannot stop shouting "ROCK AND STONE!", it never gets old! 10/10, putting AAA titles to shame, quality and level of polish is that of golden age Blizzard games, which is the biggest praize I can give!
_childDocuments_.name: Deep Rock Galactic

_childDocuments_.review: The progression is completely through hard work. The progression system itself is great, slowly introducing new ways of improvement as you play. The devs actually care about this game, and the voice lines are funny, yet clear on objectives. The music is great. The feeling you get as a swarm comes at you and you start lighting them up is so satisfying. The community is fantastic. I liked this game on Xbox so much, that I bought it on Steam to stop paying for ultimate. Just get it.But you probably won't read this, because no one comes here on their own will. Someone else makes you buy this game. A game which you probably haven't heard of. And yet you will join us in the mines, and eventually recruit someone yourself. And so will they. That is the cycle.None of this probably makes any sense, but it doesn't have to. This game is fun, and you will enjoy yourself. All you have to do, is take the step.Rock and stone, for this will be your motto, and make Karl proud.

I found help from the wonderful deep rock galactic community. Such understanding people. patience for new players is above and beyond, and everyone is so nice. Rock and stone. (Also join the deep rock union).

_childDocuments_.review: honestly just been putting off this review to find the words to say. The game has the perfect balance of repetitive and random to make it replayable as hell. it really gets you familiar with the game and the mechanics while also mixing things up constantly so no new mission is the same. not to mention the awesome community this game has, to go along with everything the game has to offer. I love this game so much. There's a reason my friend bought me this game and ive ended up with over 290 hours.

_childDocuments_.review: We mined deep in those caverns. Real deep. And in our own greed, we realized...we had gone too far. The extraction pod was a long way back and only the fastest legs could get us there. So we ran for our lives, shooting at the swarms of buggas pouring down every wall in what can only be described as a waterfall of death. Run, turn around, shoot. Run, turn around shoot. That was the routine for those final thirty seconds, that final home stretch. Yet swarms upon swarms, they continued. In trying to buy some time for my fellow dwarves, I stayed behind for a short while, killing as many as I could as they zipped across the last zipline to the pod. Now it was my turn. I jumped, clipped on, and looked down at the sea of bugs swirling below me; I had made it. I turned around to jump down onto a small ridge and came face-to-face with an exploding bastard...knocked me right off the line and down into the deadly sea. Five seconds left on the pod, five seconds I'd never make. "It's over lads. I fell," I called out. "It was a pleasure."A bright light exploded from the rocket booster as it lifted away, casting a final ray of gold and white upon me as they swarmed all around, until all that was left was dark.♥♥♥♥ yeah.
_childDocuments_.name: Deep Rock Galactic

_childDocuments_.review: Booting up Deep Rock Galactic for the first time might raise some eyebrows, especially for us jaded gamers who've been burned by overzealous monetization in live-service titles. You'll see a flashy "shop," a bar with buff beers, a "forge," and pickaxe customization, battle-pass?! – all potential red flags. But hold on to your pickaxe, miners, because things are different here.Deep Rock Galactic is refreshingly free of real-money transactions. Everything you see – the shop, the bar, the forge – functions  with in-game currency you earn by playing. No "premium" currency, no endless grinding for basic features.. Not even "premium battle-pass tiers"!Shop is for cosmetics  which asks for in-game currency, Buff beer is in-game currency - and some veteran players can buy the beers for everyone (one price always pours for whole team currently in lobby.The forge, where you unlock weapon overclocks after promoting a Dwarf, offers gameplay-altering modifications, not "endless stat grinds" with "epic drops". It's about changing how your guns perform, not min-maxing in some skinner box.There is ZERO premium currencies. Not even "buy this with in-game currency or premium UwU". None of that. DLC cosmetics is how they "monetize".DRG even embraces the modding community.  While some mods are restricted to dedicated modded lobbies, others, like UI improvements, can be used even in vanilla games. The devs thankfully understand the value of player choice and customization.ROCK AND STONE.If you are wondering about performance;i5-12th gen, 3060 (12gb) = easy 120+ fps My old PCs GTX 960 could do easy 60 fps, probably over - its been a while.Edit: This is mandatory edit to say I voted this for Labor of Love <3

_childDocuments_.review: ROCK & STONE MINERThis one is easily the best co-op game I've ever played, and I'm not the only one that thinks so.There so much to like about this title, from the beautiful and original graphics, art design, colors and so, to the great, and I mean OUTSTANDING gameplay experience. Oh, and also the cult behind the game itself with a pretty passionate community (which I'm part of). Another very positive characteristic are the devs, which make the game fresh, dynamic, bug-free and so much more fun by adding new content all the time and being in touch with what the players want.No much more to say, just sing up and start working miner.FOR KARLFOR THOSE ABOUT TO ROCK & STONE, WE SALUTE YOU

_childDocuments_.review: I got this because procedural destruction is one of my favorite things, but this has gone beyond that to be one the best co-op games ever made.Four classes all work in a synergistic way.Gameplay loop is half zen mode mining, half repelling bug attacks a la Aliens.Highly recommended even if you are playing without any friends, as the community is awesome and I've been having a blast since day 1 playing with randoms.Really hope it wins the "Better with Friends" award this year.2021 Edit: Developers still putting out amazing free updates. Game has more breadth than ever..

_childDocuments_.review: I though about buying this before but decided it looked like it was boring. it wasn't, i really love this game and i am going to buy it. right now it's on sale but it's worth it at full price aswell.i have now played for almost 60 hours and its still fun and i got lots of things to grind for still. i think the beers is one of the best parts of the game because they are all very special and its fun to just go dance with a beer in your hander after a half an hour mission. the game keep getting harder the more you play because of ther deep dives and the hazard variety and it never really gets too easy. every creature in the game is unique and its fun to discover all the different monsters. the big monsters can be really annoying though but in a good way. there is so much more amazing things to say about this game but i don't have the time.this is the best game ive played since witcher 3 and i love how the game never gets boring.i am so happy about the free trial because otherwise i'd never discover how great this is.trust me, you will be dissapointed if you don't buy this game.

_childDocuments_.review: The best co-op experience I have had the pleasure to play. This game very newcomer friendly as all classes have high utility baked into their kits and not locked behind progression, so you can play with your friends who are new at the game even if you are a veteran and vice versa. The progression is relatively short for each dwarf so you'll be done chasing upgrades quickly and off to chasing epic tales of cooperation in no time.Edit: Still holds true after 1600 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Deep Rock Galactic

_childDocuments_.review: Deep Rock Galactic is an excellent cooperative mining game.Even while it was in early access, the developers did an amazing job at updating the game, and even reworking entire sections to improve the gameplay.Procedural levels means there's a lot of replayability, and having to find your way around really makes it feel like you're exploring the unknown. Some classes have a harder time navigating certain biomes, but if you play as a team you can make up for each other's weaknesses.I can't speak to the single-player aspect of the game, as I didn't play much of it at all. As a cooperative experience, it is one of the best. Goofing off is one of the best things in the game, and the design even encourages it.I don't have anything negative to say about DRG other than the performance could be better and more consistent on my older graphics card. Visually it looks great even on the lowest settings.The developers have done a great job, and really know how to focus on making a great experience with good design decisions. They communicate well and always seem to have new ideas and a roadmap for the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Deep Rock Galactic

_childDocuments_.review: Very good coop mining game with really well tuned shooter mechanics. Not too hard, but fun. Have deep progress system, but upgrades are not too strong, so you can play with your newbie friends without any disbalance. It's not open-world, you have missions to complete, but you can do what you want during the mission (even if you don't complete it, you will get some resources and XP). Though completing missions is fun and rewarding.Difficulty is not very hard, though sometimes you can easily fail the mission if you are not careful enough. Game is not stressful, but rewarding on some waves or bosses.You will find some mechanics and familiar features from other games (which is good):- Minecraft / Terraria (you can just mine as long as you want)- Alien Swarm (really familiar setting and bugs, reminds this game in a good way, seems like developers played it a lot)Game is in Early Access for now, but it is really well made (almost no bugs, everything is polished really good).Now don't think, just start playing it with your friends, and after first 1-2 missions you won't be able to stop playing it.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun online with friends and randoms, and fun offline. Just when you think you might get bored of using the same weapon or loadout, the randomly generated caves and missions keep you hooked for long enough to get a new weapon, over clock or upgrade.Literally can't find anything to complain about, because even the grind is exciting.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: LEAVE NO DWARF BEHIND, BUY THIS FOR YOU AND YOUR 4 MATESThis game originally came out Q1 2018 and I decided to buy it on a whim. I thoroughly enjoyed the first 10 hours of the gameplay but decided to put it down for a while and wait for updates. Fast forward barely 11 months(?) later and can only say I am impressed with how far it’s come. Deep Rock Galactic is one of the best fps co-op games I have played in years, evidenced by the smooth controls, fun yet challenging gameplay, easy to understand mechanics; all in conjunction with simple yet pleasing aesthetics. When I look at the game from a designer perspective I can see the pure passion and attention to detail that has been put into this game. Guns are fun to use, classes all have their uses and it’s easy to jump in and just play for a bit. There's no competitive gameplay so I can sit back and relax. That’s all I can say.Pros-Easy and fun gameplay- few different modes to play- lots and lots of cosmetics (no need to sell your soul)- many different ways to customise your dwarf, armour, weapons etc.- still in early access yet incredibly polished - Much more to come- For Carl!Cons- Had a recurring bug since day one where my mouse would get stuck and could move it but could shoot (have to unplug and re-plug it)- $35 AUD hurts my soul as its borderline for friends right now so I am solo (few more updates and I reckon I can convince them)- Very few Australian servers up sometimes during the day or late at night (public servers)- A small community at the moment (huge potential to grow it)Extra note: The developers themselves are extremely translucent with their roadmaps, their forthgoing updates and ideas they are throwing around. Also, from what I have heard they work well with feedback from consumers and take on board what little criticism they have received.

_childDocuments_.review: (This was written while the game was in Early Access, but all of it remains relevant to my review.)There's already a bunch of reviews about how fun the game is, so I'll skip to your biggest question: "Is this another unfinished Early Access game?" The answer: not at all.This game is under the loving care of some amazing developers. Not only is it super fun, but the developers are there every step of the way to make sure things go as smoothly as possible. They listen to player feedback and not ONCE have I seen someone complain about a new update. There's already enough content for an entire game, but Ghost Ship Games continues to add more. Don't let the Early Access tag scare you- this game is here to stay! Thank you, GSG!Post-Early Access Update: my review stands. The game made it through Early Access smooth as butter, and continues to be enjoyable with new content many months later... make that many years later :)

_childDocuments_.review: Deep Rock Galactic is a game about being a few basic things: cool, and being efficient. It's about working your way up through its procedurally generated levels by either dodging hazards, or trying to survive in a world that seems to be perpetually crumbling. Don't mistake it for a platformer or a light puzzle game, either, but it's still a game in which you aren't going to get bored, or things aren't going to feel repetitive.I was quite addicted to Deep Rock Galactic. Part of that is due to how simple the game's objectives are. You start by choosing from one of three characters: a Gungeon-inspired version of Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson as Machete, a colorful dinosaur called Mario, or a suave androgynous "Hobbit" as Batman. There are also eight "procedurally generated variations" of these characters, each with their own unique abilities and stats, unlocked as you progress.

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE 1: I'm at 617 hours and still have more left in me. Seriously.... buy this game.UPDATE 2: I'm at  1,054 hours. I don't play everyday anymore, but I'm sure I'll pick it back up when I have some friends starting their journey and get back in for another 100+ hours. I think this game can safely sit in my all time favorite game. -----Don't keep reading reviews. Just buy this. Super fun. 300 hours in and probably could go another 100 without burning out. That's some serious value. It's constantly updated and great to have a change from PVP.I won't go into a ton of detail on the experience, but here's a few points on what's unique about it:- Regular updates that are just unique enough to not be just skins, but change your gameplay, while maintaining a fair balance.- The art style is really perfect for this game and beautiful with RTX. It grows on me over time.- The mod support breathed a whole new life into the game for long-termers. You can do anything from tame the language if kids are in the room (😄) to enabling user spawns in streamed sessions. A lot of quality of life mods. The stability can be "so so" but they've improved how all this is handled.- Any bugs/quirks in this game are often entertaining as the game isn't so much about "winning" as the experience.Where it might not shine:- I've introduced a few folks to it, but with 35+ updates it can be very overwhelming to new folks and they've not ended up sticking as much as I'd hoped. I don't know that it's the games fault. Variety to appeal to people with 1000+ hours in the game or you have it super simple? I think it's a fair onboarding now, but it does take a little time to not feel overwhelmed.  (Any new folks out there: Leave public coop enabled. It's a good community and the game is so much better with other folks in other than bosco. It makes it much less overwhelming to follow someone).
