_childDocuments_.review: Deep Rock Galactic sets the bar for everything a cooperative shooter should be. It’s a game that pushes teamwork above all else, and its ability to create lasting bonds through this choice is fantastic. It’s a game with a personality so endearing, it’s nigh impossible to resist falling in love, and joining the cult that is the game’s community. Finally, underneath all the goofiness, DRG is just a damn good horde shooter with nigh infinite replayability and wildly customizable builds. It’s even fun solo! If you have the small amount of money this game costs, and either free time, friends, or preferably both, you’ll want to pick this up. DRG has native controller support that is excellent, so the game is certainly playable, especially since the trackpad can emulate mouse well. That said, the game runs surprisingly poorly at the moment, needing to be set to low graphics to run at a decent framerate. The game’s frantic nature also doesn’t lend itself too well to a controller format, with scout in particular becoming much tricker to play without access to a keyboard and mouse. I still play it on mine and can vouch that it works in a pinch. At its heart(stone), DRG is entirely built around the concept of camaraderie. Teamwork is built so fundamentally into the heart of the game that even the community’s memes rely on it (more on that later...). Each of the four classes of deep rock are designed to be powerful, but reliant on others to draw out their true strength: Scout is prone to breaking his own legs without an engineer to build underneath him, while Engineer can’t figure out where to lay his platforms and turrets without scout lighting the room. Gunner can’t cosplay an infantry troop without a driller to dig his trenches, and Driller can’t do his job at all without teammates to kill. Similarly to the class system, but less talked about, is the clever design of DRG’s missions to encourage team play. Missions never have a single objective that needs to be performed by one player, instead, everything is spread out, with enough side objectives and distraction to occupy all players without anyone getting left out. Leadership is optional but not needed, and players tend to fall quickly into their class roles without realizing. Then a swarm happens, and all the players will (hopefully) materialize out of their holes and fight as a group.All the game’s features share this fundamental tenet, and this in turn encourages players to work together. I have never seen another game with average players as friendly as DRG’s. Apart from the occasional grumpy greybeard who treats the game like an actual job, most randoms are a pleasure to play with (something I would never have imagined myself saying). The community is close-knit enough that DRG even has its own unwritten code of practice, with all somewhat experienced players abiding to rules like “No double dipping on ammo resupplies”, or “check everyone is ready before progressing the mission”. Even DRG’s memes need teamwork: Teams of four will spam voicelines such as “We’re rich”, “Mushroom”, “Goo Sack” etc… with a quasi-religious zeal. The community did this so much, in fact, that the devs added voiced responses to this behaviour from the game’s terminally burnt-out manager.Now the burning question you might have in response to the first section is “GentleHoovy... what do I do if I have no friends to play with?” Between the aforementioned friendliness of randoms, and the game’s hyperactive discord community that guarantees other missions and voice-chats to join you shouldn’t have a problem. If you’re still misanthropic enough to want to play this game exclusively alone, you’d be surprised to find that, even then, the game itself is simply just fun!To briefly touch on solo, the game replaces your teammates with a drone that does essentially everything they could do (albeit usually not as efficiently). Solo is fun, but not as fun as multiplayer –my point here is more so that the game itself is fun no matter what.Deep rock has a gem of a progression system, and such a strong focus on replayability that it actually has me worried for the day I finally run out of content. Maps are random, every mission can have random events, different hazards, modifiers, enemy spawns, etc… No two missions will ever be exactly the same. Your builds are highly customizable, and the overclock system reworks your equipment so heavily that they may as well be different weapons (the same gun can shoot homing purple piercing bees of death, or lay mines on the ground – depending on your choice of OC). The game has excellent inbuilt modding support, with mods sorted into categories based around your ability to play with vanilla players and whether balancing is significantly affected. It can also be HARD – at first, even Hazard 3 (out of 5) will feel tough to the average greenbeard. Once you get good enough that even the highest difficulty feels lacking, there are modded difficulties to keep you suffering on, even then. Online games are at their absolute best when you and your team are pushed to your limits over a shared goal, and DRG tends to do this a lot.To use the words of your average IGN journalist: teammates or not, DRG really makes you  like an alcoholic spacefaring dwarf who’s been suckered into high-risk employment. This is due in no small part  to the game’s dedication to its own premise.Probably the first thing that would have stood out to you upon loading up the store page for the game is the ridiculous premise this game has. To say the idea of spacefaring dwarf contractors for an interstellar mining conglomerate is “creative” is a gross understatement. This game feels like an idea cooked up by the mind of a bored literature student during a cannabis-fuelled evening.What makes DRG special, though, is how much the game commits to this unorthodox idea. The dwarves have an ungodly quantity of different voice lines, each as legendary as the next. The game provides you with a selection of different beers, some of which buff you, to drink before each mission, but drinking too many and you may end up drunk on the job. The reason why this is so important to me is that I think this is the last key ingredient to Deep Rock’s fantastic community and the collective brain cell we share. The devs commit so hard to their stupid, goofy, lovable universe, that we have no choice but to follow their lead. It’s such a huge part of what makes a game’s community great, it’s the catalyst behind the inside jokes and memes that form the very glue holding us together, and it’s what makes me keep coming back, even after I’ve squeezed this game of all but the final drops of its content. Screaming ROCK AND STONE in unison to the game’s banging soundtrack while mowing down bugs with three total strangers will always be fun in an age where adults are getting lonelier, and game communities are becoming more and more toxic. It becomes a recourse, a safe place to go where you know your fellow dwarves will have your back no matter what. Leave no dwarf behind is the golden rule, after all.

_childDocuments_.review: Deep Rock Galactic is a great hybrid class-based FPS, Mining game, and waved based survival game. What makes this game stand out is the mining system uses a polygon system instead of a cube voxel based system. These same polygons are used to create a unique and hard-edged art-style that feels properly dwarfy. Teamwork is an important aspect as any dwarf on his own will die a terrible bug ridden death. Sound design is crisp and sounds just like digging a hole in real life with a drill or pickaxe. The game could use a bit more content, but the developers are responsive and are actively developing the game for the better.There are four unique classes in the game to choose from and they are all really enjoyable to play. These classes work best when used in conjunction with one another. While it can be fun to have four gunners, one of each class is the best way to find success in the missions. The Scout has a stereotypical FPS assault rifle, a double barrel shotgun, a really fun grappling hook to traverse the huge caverns, and a flare to light up aforementioned large caverns. The scout pairs really well who has a semi-automatic shotgun, a grenade launcher, sentries, and the platform gun. The platform gun can place yellow, octagonal platforms against any wall. This mean that he can put platforms at high, hard to reach mineral deposits and the scout can grapple to them. The Gunner has a Gatling gun, revolver, zip line gun, and satchel charges. The driller is the most unique class as it directly and greatly effects the digging component of the game. He has a flamethrower, a pistol that is weaker than the gunners, satchel charges, and giant dual wielded power drills. These allow the player to easily shape the world around them to their liking.The mining in the game includes the digging of dirt and the digging of minerals which are found in the dirt. There are few different mineral types such as: gold which gives the player credits, nitra which allows players to call in supply drops to refill ammo, morkite which is the objective of some missions, some specialized ores which work the progression system, and some large gems which require quite a bit of digging. The world is comprised of triangle polygon system of digging. While a dwarf mining will remove a square amount of dirt, explosive enemies can leave oddly shaped craters in the ground which look great. Each cave system is also randomly generated so that each mission never feels the same. The special mineral fuel Deep Rock Galactic’s progression system.Each class has permanent upgrades which can be bought for every part of the class’ equipment. For example, armor can be upgraded so that the player has more shielding or a weapon can have more max ammo. Flares can also be upgraded so that the dwarves have more of them and they last longer. This equipment lights up the darkness that the dwarves find themselves in. These upgrades can be bought with credits, but the more powerful upgrades require the special minerals. This makes sure that the player does not play only the easy biomes. Different biomes have unique obstacles but they also vary in the amount of hits they require to break the dirt blocks. The driller is great because his drill doesn’t care about hardness and will cut through any rock like butter. These upgrades help fend off the monsters in more difficult mission and biomes.Enemies spawn in both small pockets and giant waves. These occur randomly and make the game quite challenging. There are a few different enemy types to challenge the unlucky dwarfs mining a faraway asteroid. One type explodes and does quite a bit of damage and can set off a chain reaction with other explosive bugs. Another type has an armored front but an exposed abdomen and diffuse poison gas into the air upon death. The varied nature of waves and their random compositions help to keep this game mechanic fresh and challenging. A player can predict what kind of enemies will be on a particular mission which makes the darkness all the more frightening.As with any multiplayer game, I must talk about the quality of the community around the game. While this game is great with friends, sometimes they aren’t around and randoms are one’s only option. From my experience, the community is really nice and every player actively revives their teammates and tries to win. The powerful abilities and friendly fire could make grieving prevalent, but it isn’t. I think that this is because a game of Deep Rock Galactic takes on average thirty minutes to complete. No one wants to lose twenty minutes of work so everyone plays nice to get the materials they need.Overall, this is a really fun game with friends and randoms that combines wave based FPS gameplay and mining. Progression feels rewarding and makes the player get out of their mission comfort zone. The developers are also actively adding more content, which is the major gripe that people have with this game. The game’s sound design is excellent. The music is used only for ambiance and never distracts from mining or gunning. The dwarves all have really enjoyable lines that are immediately funny and memorable (ROCK AND STONE BROTHER!!!). Mining sounds are realistic and it really felt like I was a dwarf mining in a cave. Guns have great audio feedback and are satisfying to use on the future squelching bug bits. The graphics have a really unique style. The polygonal mining system’s art style is used on the dwarves and enemies to give the world a harsh, hard edged look. It helps to create the theme of four dwarves stranded on an asteroid while being yelled at by a corporate manager who doesn’t care about their safety. The colors are quite muted and all of the materials are matte to once again create a desolate effect. The graphics are quite crisp and I never became confused when looking at different enemy types as they are all uniquely models. With such a complex mining system I was pleased to find that the game ran excellently on my computer on max settings. The game looks beautiful with these settings and I don’t even have the highest PC specs possible. Great CommunityFun GameplayMemorable Sound DesignResponsive ControlsUnique SettingCould Use Some More Content

_childDocuments_.review: Rock? Stone? It matters not.This game is a gem, both literally and figuratively. You like games where you mess around underground like Minecraft and Metro 2033? You like games that require teamwork in utter chaos like Left 4 Dead and Killing Floor? You enjoy the nutty sometimes dry humor of Team Fortress?Well here's Deep Rock Galactic. A game that delivers all this in one finely tuned, polished package. Four different dwarves, each incredibly well balanced and necessary for smooth gameplay. Each dwarf has different ways to play, unlockable weapons, mods for said weapons, and it all just works. Theres a weapon type for every playstyle amongst the four dwarf classes. If you like precision, its there, if you like colossal explosions, its there, you like bullet hoses, it there.Easy to use waypoint and mark system with the laser pointer also means its quite easy to communicate with your team without needing to type in the chat or use voice chat, although both are available. The biomes are all unique and beautiful in their own way.Each dwarf has their own way of getting around the randomly generated environments, each very different, but when working together you can turn even the biggest clustered mess of topographical nightmares into your own weird jungle gym.And best of all? Low-spec. The game has a very early-playstation-2 look. Everything is designed to be low-poly with simple textures. Its clean. Its consise. You always know what you're looking at from a distance. And this allows the devs to go nuts on the particle effects, of which there are many. Lots of smoke, fire, steam, sparks, fireballs, etc. Enemies are generally color-coded as well so even from far away you can identify critters in the caves based on their hue or the parts of their bodies that glow.Theres a lot of interesting features in the caves as well besides the enemies. Old weird dwarf machinery, strange geological formations that can be interacted with, hazardous plants and fluids.And it just WORKS. Very very few bugs. Almost no crashes.  Even when theres hundreds of bugs onscreen and explosions everywhere. And that WILL happen. Sometimes, often, ♥♥♥♥ just hits the fan in this game and you'll find yourself going toe to toe with craploads of creatures of various types. Theres no healer in this game. Theres no regenerating health. It's all on you to mitigate damage and know when to shoot and when to run.I wish games like this came out more often. No predatory practices. No fomo. No bad balance decisions. The developers actually play their own game and understand how it works and you can feel the difference between this and a lot of other modern games where you wonder if the devs have even played their own software.I'm glad this game is as big of a success as it is. It deserves all the praise and accolades. Its intense, its hard, its silly, and it pokes you right in that wanderlust gland as well. Its the full package. And one nice feature is if you fail a mission (and this will happen sometimes cause the game is random and sometimes chaos is unleashed), you dont lose all progress for death. You don't get nearly as much XP or loot but you never walk away from a mission feeling like you wasted your time.The tagline on the OST says it best:"The richest mine ever discovered just happens to be on the deadliest planet in the galaxy. It's also where you work."- Z

_childDocuments_.review: Deep Rock Galactic ReviewDo you enjoy being chased by alien spiders as you try to crawl your way out to freedom?Deep Rock Galactic puts you in the role of a dwarf miner going planet to planet in order to mine resources for the company, Deep Rock. You play as one of 4 dwarfs available, each one being useful in their own way. You have the engineer, the driller, the scout, and the gunner. Each class will also suit a certain playstyle. For example, you can pick the scout if you prefer quick movements and scouting ahead or the gunner to be the frontline of your team. The driller if you prefer to play strategically and drill holes to funnel the enemies, or the engineer to set up turrets and offer firing support for your team.While Deep Rock Galactic doesn’t have a campaign, there is a story to somewhat follow. The only way to follow the story is the character’s voice lines. Some characters mention the company’s name, Deep Rock, or mention an unknown character named Karl. This seems to be the only story so far and may progress with upcoming updates.	The gameplay is simple to learn, making it easy to jump straight in. You start a mission with your class’s guns, utility, and a trusty pickaxe. The environment around you is completely destructible, allowing you to create a new path with your class’s equipment. The game is also accompanied by a random map generator, making each mission feel unique and challenging. There is also an extra mode called deep dives. This mode features stages and 2 objectives for each stage. Nothing changes drastically with the mode.While there are many different enemies, most are all based on insects. There are normal spiders and flying enemies, but different variants give them unique ways to attack. There are spiders with armor, flying enemies that shoot projectiles, exploding spiders, and a bigger version of the previous enemies that acts as a mini-boss. It’s a big list of enemies, but not much variety as most enemies are different sizes of  bugs with varying amounts of health. Upcoming updates are adding more missions and enemies, further expanding the game.Deep Rock Galactic goes for a polygon type art style, which works great for the destructible environment, though this art style may not please some people. The game’s soundtrack is another aspect I don’t see others talk about as much. The combat music is one the best I've heard in recent games. Some of the soundtracks can be compared to half life’s OST.: 8/10I hope the game further improves on the varieties of enemies and more modes. This game is great, but some may not like the gameplay loop or the lack of variety, making the game feel the same at times.Edit: New updates have added and soon to be released new biomes, enemy types, and weapons. The game is currently releasing new free battlepasses that add to the lore of Deep Rock Galactic. Rock on!New Verdict: 10/10If you liked this review, check out our curator

_childDocuments_.review: You play as space Dwarves, mining gold and other minerals while killing swarms of hostile bugs.There are four classes to choose from: Engineer, Gunner, Driller, and Scout. Each of them can support the mission in their own way, with their unique weapons and tools. The missions are all procedurally generated, which means all of them will be a unique experience. Even though the caves are randomly generated, they still look very interesting, and is always exciting to explore them, since you never know what rare minerals/enemies/events you will find. The type of missions you can play change in real time, every 30 minutes, to keep things fresh. There are also some weekly assigments that gives out good rewards, so there's always something to come back for. Importantly, there are no daily missions, the game doesn't expect you to dedicate all your time to it. I also highly recommend playing with friends over voice chat, cooperating and making strategies is how you will have the most fun, beating higher difficulty missions.Even though it is recommended to play with others, you can still play it solo, if you feel like, and a cool little robot will accompany you, who follows your orders and helps you along the way.So, this is the most fun I have had in any multiplayer games in a long time, I can only recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Good hazard 5 public lobbies are quite rare, but the game is still fun when playing solo. In my opinion, multiplayer is only enjoyable when playing with friends.Now for my rant:An assignment is a list of random missions that you must complete in order to get a reward. Each assignment mission has a specific gamemode that will not change even after the map gets reset. The assignment will select a random mission from the map as the assignment mission.There are two types of assignments: The main assignments, and limited time assignments.Main assignments are unlocked as you reach certain milestones, and you're able to do those whenever you want.Limited time assignments are the seasonal/event/weekly assignments, which become unavailable after a certain time. This is a problem because if you do not do all the missions, you will miss out on whatever rewards the assignment(s) had to offer. Who doesn't love a little FOMO?The weekly core hunts are especially painful to miss out on, as it already takes quite a while to get all the overclocks, even when doing all the weeklies.After you promote your first dwarf and start working on the others, you're bombarded with assignments to do. You will almost never run out of assignments until you get much further in the game, which can be problematic, as assignments are designed in a way that makes it harder for people to find lobbies and play the missions they most enjoy. When playing the game normally, you can simply click on the list of multiplayer lobbies and join any one that you like (and of course, for solo, you can just pick whatever mission you want). When doing an assignment, you are limited to lobbies that are currently playing your assignment mission. Not only do you have a limited choice of lobbies, but you're also forced to play whatever mission your assignment tells you if you wish to progress. Perhaps you don't enjoy that mission type very much, or maybe you just don't feel like playing a Hollow Bough 400 Morkite mission with the Lithophage Outbreak warning. You're still forced to either do the mission, or wait up to 30 minutes for the missions to refresh (though the mission type will remain the same), assuming you want to complete your assignment.One way to deal with this is to speedrun all the missions on hazard 1, skipping everything not necessary for the objective. While this is generally a good way to do assignments, you are often held back by certain missions with time constraints (on-site refining, escort duty, industrial sabotage, and salvage missions). Those missions can be extremely boring when playing like this. For solo, I recommend playing Scout for most missions.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the few games that really deserves the praise it gets. Gameplay, replayability, visual design and music are very well done. But there's one outlier that puts this co-op game ahead of everyone else: . I'll be going through all of this piece by piece, so strap on your seat-belts and prepare for a long ride.TL;DR for those on a tight schedule: Fun game, funny dwarves, best community, no FOMO (Fear of Missing Out) content.Gameplay is pretty straightforward: Shoot bugs, mine minerals, do objectives and get out alive. What you shoot the bugs with is what makes the game fun, so Management sent us a lot of different toys to play with. The characteristics of each weapon is already unique to begin with, but the way you utilize them varies greatly after you obtain "Overclocks" to make them stand out . Each class has their role, and they all benefit from each other. Driller tears through tough terrain with tremendous ease (heh). The engineer creates platforms to safely descend hazardous chasms (or to help out the scout with minerals that're out of reach) while setting up defensive parameters with his turret(s).Gunner provides covering fire, ziplines and safety shields to make sure the team survives a swarm while the scout grapple-hooks himself across the map while providing light to the team with his flare-gun. Of course, that won't stop you from forming a gang of 4 scouts to zip around the caves for the sake of  fun and profit.When it comes to replayability... there's uh, a lot of it. The mission availability changes all the time, which can be which biome, map layout, mission type, secondary objective and even "Modifiers" that comes along the mission itself. The modifiers themselves can be positive or negative, all from mineral-rich caves to having a constant horde of exploding glyphids chasing you. The minerals you mine up are put to good use as well, since you need those to purchase weapon upgrades, cosmetics (more on that later) and unlocking the overclocks you find along the way. You'll always need more of "that one mineral", which will only appear on certain biomes. This way, you'll always find someone in different missions that isn't part of a weekly objective. Seasonal cosmetics aren't going to disappear, as they become available as a random drop in the caves once the season ends!Style over substance, that sums up the visuals this game in more ways than one. The maps themselves may be low-poly, but they make up for it with distinct visual effects (and hazards) that really represents the biome you're in. There's a lot of cosmetics in this game to make your dwarf stand out among your peers, and they even let you modify your trusty pickaxe for a better-looking salute. And a dwarf's beard shall never be covered by the cosmetics, unless specified. Let the beards be free!Sure, there's a few thematic cosmetics are locked behind DLC, but they're mostly a sign of support/appreciation to the devs if you ever think of buying them.There's a few soundtracks in the game, but they all blend in flawlessly with the environment and situation. The mysterious ambiance of the caves, the tense music during swarms and the adventurous fanfare as you march back to the drop-pod for extraction. And then there's the jukebox at the Abyss Bar, for those who wants to party in style.As for the community? It's one of the greatest I've seen in an online game for years.Being a completely new greenbeard of a dwarf makes it difficult to join another lobby, but the fellas you'll meet will always be there to help you out. You're usually in good company as everyone plays for fun, so expect a lot of goofy shenanigans with total strangers.The sheer levels of camaraderie in every mission is also off the charts, if one salutes, the others will follow. Pinging some compressed gold? You can bet that the gang will stop at nothing to do the same. Saving Doretta's head after a successful escort mission, despite not rewarding anything? More like a mandatory rescue ops. Got downed 40 seconds before extraction? Leave no dwarf behind.Sure, there's always going to be some grumpier dwarves hanging around. Probably with good reason, as they're usually found on "end-game" content (Hazard 5 missions, (Elite) Deep dives etc.) that actually needs you do play properly.To summarize, Deep Rock Galactic is absolutely worth getting if you just want a co-op action shooter to play alone or with friends. The absence of FOMO lets you play the game at your own pace without the constant need to grind everyday, and the community is a blast to play with.

_childDocuments_.review: Deep Rock Galactic is the greatest PvE co-op I've ever played. The gameplay is best summed up as a mix of Team Fortress 2's class based system, movement mechanics, humor and combat combined with the hectic fight for survival of Left 4 Dead, set in the fully destructible, resource-filled, randomly generated caves of Minecraft.Each class has their own weapons, support tools and traversal tools. Each weapon has a complex and well-balanced upgrade web, giving the player great creative freedom to build their weapons for different purposes. Each class has a traversal tool that brings unique movement and terrain manipulation mechanics to the game. Each enemy is designed to counter certain builds and to punish players for making mistakes, however, each enemy has counters of its own. Coupled with the random terrain generation, this makes for endless replayability, driven by improvisation and experimentation.Last but certainly not least, GSG's dev team is one of the last of a great, dying breed: a dev team that actually cares about the game itself, first and foremost. They make significant efforts to stay engaged and involved with the playerbase, providing us with constant hotfixes, update progress reports, and even tease us with leaks of upcoming features on their streams. DLCs are purely cosmetic and are just a means to tell them "hey, I like your game, here's some more money to support development, keep at it". This game rightfully earns its spot among my top three favorite games of all time. Get this game, it is really that good. The riches of Hoxxes await, so get out there and make Karl proud. ROCK AND STONE, BROTHER!

_childDocuments_.review: Bought this game to play with some friends, it's only fun when you have someone else to play with. Game runs fantastic, probably best performing game in my library. Lots of fun to be had, worth the price!Update 5/28/22Season 2 dropped, played the beta for a bit and was shocked at how bad things were less than a week from release. The performance was garbage, weapons needed major balancing, and the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ robots are even more stupid.At & after release things got better, performance is still not what it used to be. I used to have super-smooth frame times on DX12 never with any frame drops. Now, in Season 2 I have constant frame drops on either DX12 or DX11 and super inconsistent frame times I can feel. This makes the game feel super rough. I've also unfortunately been crashing quite frequently on DX12 which had overall more frames, but less frame time consistency. DX11 is recommended, but I really want the buttery smooth game play I had on DX12 in Season 1. I noticed some of the lighting has changed, perhaps there's an issue with a new lighting method?The robots have and always will be really ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ annoying. I try to avoid them as much as possible, which being the theme of the season, looks like I'll be mostly avoiding the game all together.I still recommend the game, but know neither the game play or its performance is as smooth as it was, and as it should be.Update 11/15/23Game's performance is great, even on DX12. Very rarely any crashes even while running mods. I have upgraded my graphics card from a GTX 1080 to an RTX 3080, so that's probably part of the performance uplift. Gameplay is a little rough, quite a few significant changes I'd like to see. The robots were nerfed a couple times after my initial reviews, they're better, but still a little over powered. Its not super hard to avoid them, but if we could remove the nemesis from non-rival missions, that'd be great. Rockpox wasn't all that bad in Season 3, there was only a couple of rockpox enemies and clearing the infection was pretty easy even with only one doing it. I would play it frequently for the +50% bonus on mineral manias. Still worth it in Season 4, but its not nearly as easy. In my opinion, the rockpox is too easy to get, if you pop an enemy's blister it'll fill your meter up some 60%, that's only one blister. The infection also lingers in the area you popped it, so significant area denial which is really annoying. I'd like to see the blisters only have that effect when melee'd. I'd also like to be able to foam and vacuum the rockpox enemies, like you can with the Corruptor. The new enemies, the stingtail and septic spreader are pretty broken. They've had multiple nerfs but they still need some nerfing. The stingtail is heavily armored with a lot of health and tiny weakpoints. This is hopefully gonna be addressed in the November Maintenance update.The septic spreader does not need line of sight to absolutely destroy your team, they can hide behind cover with impunity and wipe the team with ease. If there's multiple of them, which there usually is, you're screwed. The area denial potential of this enemy is massive, which makes it super difficult to kite. This guy needs to have line of sight to shoot, probably a longer & louder wind up and probably slower projectiles. We'll see how he is after the update. Also the septic goo looks like red sugar, that's just annoying.It may seem like I'm harping on the issues, which I am. They're pretty minor, and I'd still recommend this game in a heart beat. I'm hyper critical of the games I review in the hopes they'll change to become better.Update 7-29-24:I'm afraid I can't recommend the game any longer, when Season 1 first came out, the robots were really strong, incredibly over powered, especially on higher levels. They had to nerf them several times to make them manageable. Come Season 3 they add enemies with weak spots in the form of blisters, okay - not a big deal. Until they made these weak spots incredibly dangerous, walking near them would dramatically increase your Rockpox which will immobilize you. You can't get up close to those enemies but you need to be close enough to hit the weak points. Like Season 2 was to Season 1, Season 4 is much of the same of Season 3, over powered enemies with little to no play testing (especially on higher levels) and significantly more area denial. Now we're at Season 5, I'll be honest I haven't played much. I tried out the core stone event for the first time, they clearly haven't learned a thing from the last 4 seasons. The enemies are incredibly tanky, taking several breach cutter shots to kill, they are quite fast and have a lunge attack. Probably the worst part is they don't stop coming until you kill the 'Core Stone', which itself is also incredibly tanky, with invulnerability phases. Oh right, this wouldn't be complete without area denial, the enemies occasionally spill goo on the floor which will deal poison damage.I have to say, I'm pretty tired of this. I've already had to install mods to remove the Septic Spreader and the Stingtail, at this point I'd have to remove half the game to balance it properly. This is probably my last time playing this game again.Update 10-23-24:There is now input issues, clicks don't always register.

_childDocuments_.review: Deep Rock Galactic! Ahh, where do I start?This is probably the best coop shooter I ever played and I've been playing shooters back when Doom was basically still a glorified 2D pixelfest.Unfortunately for me my friends preferred to stick with a truck simulation game and a warship simulation game, but this game is perfectly playable in coop when logging in solo (but it's even better with a bunch of friends using VOIP).This game has missions, but you can play them at any difficulty that you want. Also you can join mid-game and still reap full rewards.But the best about this game is definitely the actual gameplay. I'd describe it as a mix of cave exploration/prospecting where you take your time to traverse caves, finding all the minerals that you need, accompanied by a beautiful tranquilizing exploration soundtrack which which sometimes even sounds a bit melancholic or something. Build bridges and ramps to help your team traverse more easily.This exploration bit is regularly swapped out for an incoming wave of enemies where you will frantically try to defend yourselves while traversing this same terrain. You'll get very little time to select a good spot to fight and prepare for engagement of swarms of enemies (and sometimes even very big enemies that can literally dig the dirt from under you if they happen to come from below). It's similar to the movies Aliens and Starship Troopers, but better.You'll sometimes come across an event. Most events can be manually activated so you can decide with your team when (and sometimes if if you're too low on ammo (yes I'm looking at you, OMEN)).This game rewards quick thinking, quick responding, teamplay and playing creatively and this game is excellent at giving a good time for the time I spend in it ingame.DRG is part a better looking minecraft and part a parkour shooter. That's how I'd describe it.The randomness of the cave generation and events and mission modifiers (along with some spacerig shenanigans like wallglitching into outer space and filling up the other pods with barrels and all other kinds of items that aren't nailed down to give joiners an extra warm welcome) resulted in my having stacked 2300+ hours into killing 700000+ bugs. I can just log into this game, play a couple rounds for under an hour and log out and feeling satisfied. No FOMO bs, just quality gameplay.What I don't like is some of the stuff they added ever since they started with the seasons themes. I think the machines and their events (nemesis and prospector) add some nice flavor and variation to the game, but centering entire seasons imo distracted from what I always liked the most about DRG, which is exploring caves filled with loot and bugs and fighting hordes of bugs in a frantic run&gun brawl.The infection stuff I liked even less. The snare that ignored your shield and started eating away at your hp right away and the new stingtail which randomly shoots you into any direction with under a second warningtime before which you may not even have been aware of their presence (especially when playing solo and are somewhere high up, this just makes it more annoying to have bosco uses one of his limited rezzes and you have to climb your way back up there).The new song I also dislike. It doesn't fit the game at all and is too corny and hearing it makes me consider restarting the mission just so I can be rid of it.Also the battlepass stuff. I'm sure many people will like it, but it once again only distracts from what I believe made the game good. A battlepass' only function is to give a sense of FOMO and I think the game would have been better off without it. The rewards being in crates you find is much more immersive, but instead of that I got a battlepass and the "EMPTY..." message.Unfortunately for me, I've reached a point where even hazard 5 doesn't give me a proper challenge anymore but this game can also be fun enjoying it with randoms in hazard 2, teaching them the ropes and the gameplay loop is still very enjoyable despite this lack of sense of challenge. Unfortunately nobody plays using mods except for groups of friends.Also, the future of DRG seems bleak as the game slowly gets abandoned and hackers and trolls slowly take over. Fortunately there aren't many hackers in DRG and there were very few that ruined the immersion.Anyway, all in all there isn't much to complain about. This game is great, especially for what it costs! Compare this to the F2P games which are covertly elaborate P2W 3D advertisements that are build around you getting addicted to flipping your wallet while making you hate it. This game has none of that bs (but the free battlepass was not a step in the right direction), it's about good old fashioned quality gameplay!There's so much more to tell about this game, but it's better to just experience it.Would I recommend this game today? Yes, go grab it and delve as greedily and deep as you can to fully enjoy this treasure of a game! Grab the game, do it! Do it now!

_childDocuments_.review: There are a lot of reviews of DRG that talk about the atmosphere, gameplay and art of the game. I think these are spectacular but not my favorite part of the game. This is probably the only game that I have felt that the sound design is the most stand out feature.You will distinctly hear every enemy before you see them. You'll know what it is, which direction it is, how close it is - all in a single sound. And every sound is so unique and unmistakable. As you learn each unique noise you'll be aware of leeches, grabbers, detonators, all before they actually get near you.Every point of interest makes its own noise, too. Batteries, mules, lost helmets, and more. You will hear all these sounds long before you see where they are coming from. As corny as it sounds, it really puts you inside the game. Many games now are so focused on the gameplay and graphics that all the sound blurs together and you don't notice the subtle things. To me, Deep Rock Galactic captures your ears better than it captures your eyes and that is a unique experience that makes me love the game.

_childDocuments_.review: ---EDITED 05/13/2020---Hats off to Ghost Ship Games for managing to deliver a well-rounded, engaging experience that's rocketed out of Early Access like an escape pod out of Hoxxes. Since my review last year, the developers have managed to add onto the framework they built in a way that compliments and incentivizes the core gameplay loop without sacrificing quality or the expectations of the Deep Rock Galactic community. Updates have been frequent, bugfixes have been efficient, and all throughout the Early Access process Ghost Ship Games were significantly transparent on the status of their project. As a 1.0, the game is as solid as a rock (and stone) with plenty of content for newer players to sink their teeth into while veterans can look forward to earning the newly included prestige tiers. Volume 2 of the soundtrack is also a very welcome addition, adding a multitude of appropriate and engrossing songs to accompany the ever-present senses of wonder and danger within the planet's crust. There are a few features I am surprised to see missing from this release, namely an animation for storing the M.U.L.E. in an escape pod for example. However, GSG has made clear that they plan to continue supporting the game with content updates for the forseeable future and given their track record, such a thing is likely to be implemented eventually along with other goodies for dedicated fans. Overall, I can say with confidence that Deep Rock Galactic has cemented itself as one of the best cooperative multiplayer experiences on Steam, even possibly one of the best in general. If Ghost Ship Games continues on the course they've set, our future in extraterrestrial mining is very, very bright.  ---EARLY ACCESS REVIEW 09/2019---One thing I want to make perfectly clear is that even though this game is in early access it's probably one of the most polished early access games I've ever had the pleasure to experience on this platform. The developers, Ghost Ship Games, already have a very solid and very rewarding gameplay loop that fosters cooperation and friendship and are now working to expand the variety of challenges and rewards you encounter. It is very satisfying to find yourself in a dire situation at the hands of insectoid horrors only to overcome them with a little help from your friends. Each class is fun to play with each of their respective weapons, tools, and abilities while also maintaining a balanced role for maximum synergy with others. Graphically, the game is impressive as well. The art design is charmingly reminiscent of early three-dimensional games where every model has a distinct polygonal appearance to it, yet it also strikes a nice balance with modern textures and shaders to deliver a unique visual appeal. Lighting is also very much fine-tuned as it acts as a key gameplay component given spacious unexplored caverns don't come pre-lit. Keeping flares going to light your way is essential to finding minerals and avoiding obstacles, and the way it is implemented realistically only lights a given radius.The sound design is also of note here as well. Much like one of its inspirations, the Left 4 Dead franchise, each entity has its own clearly discernible cues that both alert players to its nature as well as location. Not to mention a vast majority sound extremely and appropriately alien. Other impressive examples of attention to detail include the varying levels of reverb depending on the size of a cave chamber, the unique firing sound of each weapon, and the robotic whirrings and clankings of the AI-driven drones that and other machinery that accompany you into the depths.Overall, as it is now the game is quite good and as more and more updates are released it looks to keep getting better. I highly recommend this both now, and whenever the full game is released in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: On the surface Deep Rock Galactic is a fast paced survival shooter, but at its core the devs have crafted something much more meaningful: a first person shooter with a genuinely positive community. Every mission I drop into is filled with shouts of "Rock and Stone!" regardless of if we've slain a giant Dreadnought or wiped out of the mission completely, you drop into the caves of Hoxxes as a team and you leave as one. I've put a solid 200 hours into this game and gotten well over a dozen of my friends into playing it as well, and I'm constantly looking for more ways to share my love for this game, so it's about time I finally wrote a review. Deep Rock Galactic is a survival shooter where your mission is to collect various resources for the Deep Rock Galactic mining company, meanwhile gunning down endless hordes of alien bugs to ensure your own survival and your team's. Progress comes slow, but there's easily enough content for hundreds of hours of playtime, and the community has you constantly coming back to complete your weekly assignments and drink a few beers at The Abyss Bar to the tune of some hidden gems from the jukebox. I highly recommend this game if you're looking for something to play with friends or even alone (since the devs put so much effort into making the singleplayer experience just as robust as the multiplayer). Rock and Stone, brothers. May Karl guide you to victory and riches in the caves of Hoxxes.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: DRG is a fantastic game! 100% worth getting!Deep Rock Galactic is a Co-op game with a very enjoyable and rewarding gameplay loop. where you or a squad up to 4 dwarves, either consisting of rando's or friends, go on missions doing various activities.These vary from basic mining of a certain ore and eliminating some dangerous big bugs to on-site refining to name a few (of course, some better than others) with more being added in their version of seasons.You do these missions on whatever difficulty you chose before hand, ranging from hazard 1 all the way up to 5, and happen in different biomes (around 10 at the time of writing), each unique with their own challenges, different layouts, complexity and crafting resources.Also worth mentioning:No predatory MTX or season passes after buying the game, only cosmetic DLC for you to support this studio, truly refreshing and worthy of praise.It's a very fun experience, especially with friends, a kind and welcoming community to new players with most willing to help you out if you ask. And always remember:Rock and Stone!

_childDocuments_.review: The best "mistake" I ever made. I don't buy Early Access games as a rule, but I was compelled to buy this game when it went on sale. I have not regretted it for an instant.  The game feels incredibly unique and the community is possibly the best I've seen in a game.  There's nothing quite like finding a particularly good group to play with, sharing a couple in-game brews, and knocking out a couple missions.  It always feels like there's more to work toward in this game.  Some might consider it grindy, but I feel the pace is pretty good; you get rewarded so often that it never feels like a mission was a waste.  It's also quite clear how much the devs of this game care about it; I've seen two or three major updates in the relatively short amount of time I've had the game, and each update feels huge and pushes the game farther! I'd recommend this game to just about anyone.Detailed Review:The game plays a bit like a mix of Minecraft's cave-exploring and mineral gathering, the gun-play and class system and cosmetics of Team Fortress 2, and the feel of a Starship Troopers movie.  Every mission has you exploring randomly generated cave systems filled with hostile wildlife; a good number of different objective and sub-objective types, levels/biomes with different gimmicks, and various mission mutators keep the game feeling fresh.  The class variety is excellent with the 4 classes playing very differently.  Each brings something unique to the team, but having duplicates on a team still lets you get a mission done with no issues.  Each class a suite of equipment (primary weapon, secondary, mobility tool, and support tool), all of which have traits which can change theThe thing that really sets this game apart is the feel.  Playing a mission can feel incredibly oppressive with darkness all around and hearing the calls of the local fauna through the caves. If you pay attention, you'll begin to know enemies by their calls, being able to figure out what you're up against before you even see them.  Getting out of a mission, the ship feels the proper mix of industrial and cozy, with a small recreational area to kill time while you're waiting for people.  It's pretty fun buying rounds for your squad-mates as you wait for a 4th person, only to end up passing out onto the floor, or maybe dancing to the music in the jukebox.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an absolutely marvelous game! It gives you all the feelings you want in a game. You get satisfaction, triumph, thrill, surprise, despair and a feeling that can only be described as "oh no...." Not to mention the soundtrack is astounding! It compliments the battles and events incredibly well. I do genuinely enjoy this game and its content. It is always best when you play with some of your lads, but the community is amazing and you will always find some other great lads to play with.
_childDocuments_.name: Deep Rock Galactic

_childDocuments_.review: You get to mine, kill bugs, and drink alcohol as a dwarf. What else is there not to love?The last one out alive is a pointy-eared leaf lover.Edit: After 2 years of release, the game still receives a massive amount of love from Ghost Ship Games.Edit #2: They are about to release their biggest update yet, can't wait! You should honestly give this a try with friends or the amazing community.
_childDocuments_.name: Deep Rock Galactic

_childDocuments_.review: I started to love this game, even bought all DLCs a couple days ago but after reading reddit post about unforgiving GSG's modteam behavior I can't recommend supporting these devs. Reddit post if you wanna learn yourself is "The creator of the "Advanced Darkness" mod is stepping away from DRG after being arbitrary censored and excluded from Mod.io modding team, adding another item on the list of account restrictions or full bans with ambiguous motivations from Mod.io and the modding Discord server"TLDR: Modio power hungry mods destroying competing websites, full on banning mod creators with no reason given at all and multiple times trying to remove the evidence of them being corrupt. Modio mods is/are a chosen person from GSG, so this is the "friendly community" everyone's talking about? And the reason why they don't wanna do anything with steam workshop is so they can have "approved" mods so you can't "cheat" in game progression.This post left a sour taste in my mouth, especially after buying all DLC's to support developers and enjoying the game for 66hrs in last week alone.Other than that the game is great. In-game community is awesome, just don't be like me and actually press "Join" instead of going solo in a mission. You won't regret it! I only learnt it on my 60th hour when I was done doing 100th mission Solo. It's so much more fun with other people than wish BOSCO. The only problem is well.... moderators.So far there has been no response from GSG themselves and I highly doubt there will be. Honestly a very fricked up thing to do, especially from a dev team that everyone has been praising as the best team ever. Why not just get normal mods? Or does everyone instantly get corrupted as soon as they taste that sweet sweet red sugar of internet power? Then bring back season 4 and use decontaminator on them.UPD: And if you don't understand what this means. This means that 2 of the best modders (and many more who have been banned with no reason, despite this modder trying to contact GSG and receive close to no communication from them.) in this community just left and are not going to update their mods and dependencies anymore. Custom vanity framework? Gonna be broken, no more custom skins. Build inspector? Bye bye. No ragdolls, better fps, advanced darkness (makes game look better) and custom difficulty + a huge modding tool mint are not gonna be supported for future updates.UPD2: Mods in discord instantly delete messages regarding this situation which makes it even more disgusting.
_childDocuments_.name: Deep Rock Galactic

_childDocuments_.review: What do the dwarves eat? Do they eat the rocks? They drink beer exclusively, so I thought maybe they eat the mugs, like a soup-in-a-breadbowl situation. Turns out they just throw the mugs on the ground.It's easter right now, so the lobby is filled with festive carrot decorations. Do they eat the carrots? But those carrots aren't real, they're just props, right? So that's the same as eating rocks.I'd love to know. I haven't seen any chef-based cosmetics, so I don't know if this dwarven culture has even invented aprons yet. Maybe Ghost Ship Games could add Chef as a fifth class, they cut up bugs and boil them in a soup. That would help me out a lot here.Real good game overall.
_childDocuments_.name: Deep Rock Galactic

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing co-op shooter game from a great developer with a healthy community. Everything felt unique thanks to the procedurally generated maps and the class. Not to mention you can just chill, drink, dance, and many more in the lobby with random people or your friends.Welcome aboard Greenbeards, Rock and Stone!
_childDocuments_.name: Deep Rock Galactic

_childDocuments_.review: That day when Jensen Huang took out his so-called the world's fastest gaming GPU RTX 9090 Ti out the oven, I couldn't help sending him an email showing off that my antique PC with GTX 970 can mine as fast as his latest graphics processor. Jesen believed that I must be out of my "mine" and can't afford to buy the new tech. He came to my place in person to disgrace my rig built decades ago, but apparently I would not let it happen. I run the  and filled my M.U.L.E. with tons of mine in the blank of an eye. That's it. Jensen was totally shocked, crumbbing his RTX 9090 Ti and bought me all the DLCs for this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Best way I can describe this game is, it's what games used to be. Rewarding for the grind, friendly community, great devs, endless/beautiful content and just amazing gameplay all around. Got it on sale for $10, but would def pay the original $30, it honestly should be as much as most of the dogass that are coming out by big developers and those said big developers should take some notes.
_childDocuments_.name: Deep Rock Galactic

_childDocuments_.review: Man, right now, I'm loving this game.4 classes, each with their own advantages, scout can mine or collect stuff that'd be a pain for anyone else to get via personal ziplines.. engie building platforms to help with that, or setting up sentries to take out bugs... soldier who can build ziplines anyone could use... driller who can.. well, I mean it's right there in the name for him.Several different, semi-short missions to choose from (ranging from about 15 minutes to.. depending on faffing about time, think the longest i've done was about an hour and a half) .    Mission types can include escort and protect a large driller to get a super gem, mine out a certain amount of <insert mineral here>  and stash them.... my personal favorite would be the platform, and make rideable rails to various points on the map to collect the mineral (liquid morkite in this case).And their's even fun to be had in the staging area/lobby  what with the bar right next to a jukebox.  Drinking and dancing till you pass out drunk.  Not something I thought that I would need, but surprising how much I'm entertained by that.Plenty of customization, both for the guns, and your dwarves.  This game literally got sold to me on the phrase "you would not believe just how much beard customization this game has".  And he was right. And so many of them are glorious and/or ridiculous.  The fact that it's broken up between 'staches, sideburns, and beards makes the combinations even more entertaining.Have a smart stout, enjoy the revelations and head on out for entertainment.Rock and Stone!!
_childDocuments_.name: Deep Rock Galactic

_childDocuments_.review: It's a game where you have to put in the first 100 hours into playing to actually get itthen everything will be a breeze. Haz 5 is challenging, but it's not as difficult any more.The first 100 hours aren't that bad anyway, playing Haz 3-4 mostly. Players are nice and wouldn't hate you for dragging the team down. It's fine, everyone was there at some point.There are various ways to manipulate your save, so you get the OC you want. check @chanceIIorsother than that, whether its to farm exp or to just guide new players along, DRG will stay fresh for a long time.
_childDocuments_.name: Deep Rock Galactic

_childDocuments_.review: Dwarven space miners digging for ore and fighting aliens, That is my dream game right there, Add some Orc-slaying and it would be literally perfection.For an early access the game is rich with content with the variety of biomes, Gameplay is relatively bug-free and optimized, One of the best co-op games to come out in a long while.
_childDocuments_.name: Deep Rock Galactic

_childDocuments_.review: This game took me by surprise. I was lured in by my friends (we were disappointed with the direction KF2 took after years of playing). At first, I was sceptical. But since starting around March, I was hooked from the get-go.The multiplayer is quite frankly stellar! Coming from KF1 and KF2 my team and I is pretty well attuned, and that's when games like this shine. There's barely something to complain for me.It's definitely not perfect, for example, some mission types don't have the best balancing, but then again, what game gets everything right from the start. The developers are mostly listening to the community and fixing bugs, so I can't complain. Also, they actively develop new mechanisms, game types and so on actually for free, that's something worth mentioning in 2020.It is interesting to point out that the single player mode is actually pretty decent, you get support from a bot which helps you with the objectives and serves as a stand-in for a human. I played a few rounds in SP, but playing in MP is definitely preferred.All in all, a very good game, I can't recommend it too much if you like co-op PvE.
_childDocuments_.name: Deep Rock Galactic

_childDocuments_.review: Easily one of the best online co-op experiences I can think of. I came into the game with minimal, to almost no expectations for this game other than just dumb fun with friends. My friend group and I have become somewhat addicted to just the gameplay loop alone.With 87.9 hours of total game time I can recommend this game to anyone looking for a game to play among close friends. It is also among the few games I would recommend even at full price.Pros:+ Gameplay loop never gets old, as the RNG keeps things fresh while adding its own challenges in traversing difficult environments so threats don't just come in bugs.+ Unlike many games that feature RNG based level design the maps, for the most part anyway, have a defined route to them so you never end up in a situation where you run out of cave, or you run out of items so you can't complete secondary objectives as a result of the random generation. It also helps that if anything is in your way or out of reach, each class has a method of getting there either through digging, setting up a zip line, or building platforms so pathways getting blocked aren't the end of the world.+ Enemy types are wide and varied each posing a threat to your mission in their own way. From grunts grouping up into large swarms to bum rush your position, to Glyphid Menaces sniping you from afar. The enemies don't ever feel like BS when they down you, as that just means you had poor team work. The bugs are just an incentive to speed you along the mission while giving a sense of constant danger, the real make or break is how you provide support to your team using your classes tools.+ Missions come in all sorts of different game modes and length so being prepared and working with your team to ensure you all are doing your part in completing the mission objectives is key. I have never felt bored of any of them, as I feel the moderate random generation as well as having perfectly designed game modes keep things fresh and fun no matter how many times you do them. Honestly, the most boring one I can think of is a Morkite run, but even then on the higher hazard levels the challenge can still make such a mission enjoyable.+ Classes on the surface don't feel too different from each other as they all have their own way of purging bugs, but it's the tools and how you use them that really contributes to the team. Creating zip lines and providing cover fire for players as the gunner, providing recon and light to your team as scout, creating platforms and defensive positions for your team when a big swarm comes in as engineer, to providing easy pathways for your allies as driller. Everyone is helpful, everyone can play in their own way, and the game allows for enough experimentation with weapon combinations and upgrades that it never gets boring.+ My draw dropped as it is the first time I have ever seen a season pass model not only accomplish being satisfying to progress through, but given completely for free. The devs have promised no FOMO will ever be in the game, so any items you miss in a season will be available in random loot crates you can find while playing. If you want to trick out your dwarf, just play the game. Miss out on some cosmetics? Play the game more. This method easily puts every other game that uses this model to shame . Good on Ghost Ship for not jumping on the industry bandwagon of screwing over their players for a little extra cash.+ Game is still supported and will continue to see future updates for the foreseeable future.+ DLC is optional and only features cosmetic skins for your Dwarves and their weapons. Pay for them to support the devs as a tip or don't and enjoy the game with its plethora of free cosmetics.+ It's a game for Squat fans, if that isn't a selling point I don't know what is.+ Games Workshop shamelessly ripped them off with the Votann so you know it's good.+ Mod support, need I say more?Cons:It's honestly very hard to find them. Anything that could be considered a con could either be summed up as nitpicking, personal taste, or will be fixed in the future. I was going to say there aren't enough secondaries, but they have an update on the way that will introduce one new secondary weapon for each class. I was going to say colors are a little sparse, but there are 23 for the four classes to unlock and will likely have more added as time passes. I was also going to bring up the janky physics this game has, but it kinda adds to the fun of it all.I would like to see more biomes, more game modes, more enemy types, the rival mining company expanded upon, but those will probably see updates in the future. I don't dismiss cons entirely, there are probably issues with the game I am overlooking, or may arise at a later point. What I can say for right now is that the game is worth your money, and if you are looking for an online co-op shooter this is as much of a must have as Left 4 Dead 2 in your Steam library.
_childDocuments_.name: Deep Rock Galactic

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazingI must say, everyone just...seems to like this game. There's really not anything bad with it that would push people away so it's always a safe bet if you're looking for a new game to play with a friend, and I will in particular point out the fact that this game's monetising is one of the best I've seen; there's no content whatsoever locked behind paying money, only some cosmetics are there. There's also no FOMO (any cosmetics not unlocked during one season will be available anytime from the randomly spawning packs or lost helmets, while holiday cosmetics are available again next year)I deeply recommend waiting for a sale to get this game... so that you can buy it for friends too ( I got it 50% off, bought it for a friend while it was still 50% off, and bought it for another friend while it was full price just because this game is that worth it in coop. I might have bought it for yet another friend, but that one I'm not sure about anymore)...Holy flip I had completely forgotten how many times I've bought it geez. Worth it though
_childDocuments_.name: Deep Rock Galactic

_childDocuments_.review: The gun action for this game is just amazing, and the weapon variety makes it even better with the amount of different choices, and those choices expand even MORE once you get overclocks which are their own whole thing that can either buff a weapon a bit or change how it works drasticly to allow for different styles for even more customization, and all of these combined with amazing dwarf co-op being able to get drunk and shooting insects on a alien planet, this is certainly a game worth checking out if you wanna play a dwarf mining/shooter game with great co-op it can even work good for solo! (It also has completely procedural caves!)
_childDocuments_.name: Deep Rock Galactic

_childDocuments_.review: These Devs are getting after it when it comes to updates, 22 total and a year on Steam, there is enough here for a full game. Some of THE best 4-player co-op bug killing FPS you will find period. I have purchased it two other times for friends as gifts, so I could share all the awesome dwarf rockin, beard swingin, Morkite mining action! Love this game ROCK N' STONE!
_childDocuments_.name: Deep Rock Galactic

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most complete and engaging games on Steam in terms of both the theme (because who doesn't like Space Dwarves), gameplay and overall presentation. If every early access title on Steam had the level of professionalism and dedication that Deep Rock Galactic released with, the current Steam market would not be as much of a cesspool as it tends to be right now. I highly recommend this game, and encourage you to hop on the DRG Discord, or bring a friend or two for maximum shenanigans.Hope to see you in game and Rock n' Stone!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Deep Rock Galactic

_childDocuments_.review: Rock and stone, miners! This game is pure, unfettered, no-stress fun. It's got an endearingly positive tone and a great community, and it's supported by an attentive, principled developer. If you enjoy feel-good co-op games with good mechanics, look no further. It's worth every penny of the very reasonable full price, and it's often on sale. 9.5/10. It misses out on the full 10/10 solely because I give that rating only to the very rare games that are truly sublime experiences. That DRG doesn't qualify is no criticism.
_childDocuments_.name: Deep Rock Galactic

_childDocuments_.review: Deep Rock is a fun game both single and multiplayer that you can sink hours into or even jump on for a quick mission.  The game has a simple formula that is fun and easily replayable.  Mining, bug killing, and terrain traversing through a variety of biomes using a variety of dwarf classes makes for some enjoyable moments.  The theme of the game really ties everything together.  If you like first person shooter games and the ability to mine or go anywhere you want on a mission, I definitely recommend for both single and multiplayer.  Rock and stone!
_childDocuments_.name: Deep Rock Galactic

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun co-op FPS game. Plays a bit like Left 4 Dead meets Minecraft, you have to kill bugs and mine resources for the most part, with a few other bits thrown in for good measure. The setting is fun and is pretty funny too, there's a lot of character in the dwarves and how they deal with things.The game design is very solid and very much encourages you to work with other players. As a result of this, the game has one of the most chill and non-toxic communities out there, you can very easily join a public game and have a fun time without worrying about anyone being deliberately malicious. There's also a fair amount to do, with the core gameplay loop still being fun to do past the hundred hour mark with things you can work towards. Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Deep Rock Galactic

_childDocuments_.review: This game is good but I cannot trust these devs anymore. A short list of their huge failures:-Botched their modding implementation and then effectively abandoned it in multiple ways. Their modding dev left and they haven't hired a new one, and they chose to hand moderate mods with an arbitrary and convoluted category system but then gave up on doing that and let mod approval requests pile up for weeks at a time. They finally decided to delegate it to five (originally) community members, who essentially ended up with total control of the modding approvals because the devs had minimal to no involvement after that. I would know, I used to be one of those mod approvers.-Their season implementation has been very rushed and unplanned feeling and communication and roadmaps have dissolved into secrecy and sparseness. They really like to pretend they're still really open in communicating but they're way more guarded about the dev process or any plans they may or may not have. Almost a total 180 from how they were when I first started playing.-Their discord mods often act in bizarre in unethical ways. They have one of the biggest discord communities ever and yet GSG drug their feet for a long time hiring new mods to help with the load and times where no mods were awake or home. All of these mods do huge work for GSG and GSG doesn't pay them or anything to my knowledge. Despite my sympathy for their post, some of them act really unethically. I've seen one specific mod mute or ban people for no explanation, or mute people for pinging him in a conversation. One time, a trans woman was being mistreated in chat. She called for a moderator who unhelpfully just said "no politics", which understandably she said was unhelpful and she left the discord. One of the moderators on the discord FOUND HER ON TWITTER and POSTED HER TWEET COMPLAINING ABT THE INCIDENT in a private chat of "regulars" of the discord so he could complain about her. When someone reached out to her, he got mad at them when he was the one who basically invited possible gossip and harassment on her. Another incident was when a harmless Discord troll who made jokes about being the best DRG player ever got banned from the Discord, some moderator pursued him to an unaffiliated Discord and tried to get him banned there too.-When confronted with real issues, the community manager and Discord moderators drop the ball hard. The DRG Modding Discord used to be filled with a lot of blatant misogyny, homophobia/transphobia, and racism. I remember the meme channel was absolutely foul and I once read a user talking about how they wanted a death squad called "The Dreadnoughts" to kill all BLM protestors in the streets extrajudicially. A moderator for the modding discord saw this and basically joked around with them and didn't do anything. When all this stuff got pointed out, all GSG did was say stop or we stop endorsing your server. They swept it all under the rug and no one got punished. The person who called for people to be executed was even made a moderator for the modding Discord server later! The moderator that did nothing and joked around with the person who wanted to kill people in the streets is a beta tester and regular on the main discord. -A culmination of all this is how they handled Unified UI. A central mod a lot of DRG mods rely on is Mod Hub. Earlier this year, Mod Hub received some updates that made it unstable, and the mod author removed previous versions of the mod to prevent people from using them. In frustration with this and the Mod Hub dev's behavior, two modders developed a Mod Hub alternative called Unified UI. Mod Hub's author accused them of stealing code and had the mod taken down and had GSG "investigate". What were the results? Who knows. The investigation took months and nothing ever got said. Unified UI is still gone and one of the devs of Unified UI was straight up banned from adding new mods or commenting on anything on mod.io, forcing him to say his goodbyes in the edits to his mod descriptions. No messages were sent to the accused parties and nothing was made public to anybody in any meaningful way. Around the same time I became aware of this, another user that the Mod Hub dev doesn't like had his privileges on mod.io wordlessly removed. I wasn't active in the community anymore but still had my approver privileges and tried to give him his privileges back. Shortly after, I had my approver powers stripped, also wordlessly. Word on the street is many people who talked about this situation in a way unfavorable to the Mod Hub dev have lost their privs or been banned without reason from the modding discord.The kicker? The Mod Hub dev is a mod approver and an admin on the modding discord, one on record saying homophobia is fine among other things, one who was admin during its foul and racist era.I loved this game. One of the best games ever made. But I expect people to act professionally and ethically in these situations, and GSG and the people they empower and support don't do so in many situations. I don't expect the world moved, but I do expect some effort to be put into creating a healthy community, protecting the vulnerable, and acting in good faith. But it seems that all the effort that will go into the community that made them is sweeping things under the rug, diverting and dodging responsibilities, and twiddling thumbs until Rogue Core drops.
_childDocuments_.name: Deep Rock Galactic

_childDocuments_.review: Had this since early access and a lot has changed. The devs have added tons of quality of life changes and new missions and the game is a lot of fun. All of the missions are easy to understand and the variety in dwarf classes is perfect. Co-op is tons of fun and even if you group with a bunch of randoms, it's perfectly fine because the DeepRock community are unusually friendly. If you're digging together, you're automatically friends. Rock and Stone, Brothers!

_childDocuments_.review: Tons of fun, especially if you have other people to play with. All the classes have their own flavor but none of them are really "bad" I often find myself in the middle of a mission and come across something I know would be easier with one of the other classes. Having a diverse group makes things easier but you can definitely solo play and have a blast too.
_childDocuments_.name: Deep Rock Galactic

_childDocuments_.review: I've followed the development of this game for a good majority of its available release, and since day one, the developers, Ghost Ship, are some of the most consistent and receptive developers for a title, and it shows that they truly care about their game. Every change made to the game has been in a good direction, adding depth and progression to a very satisfying survival shooter. The graphics are a very stylistic low-poly look. They have polished up nicely especially with the 1.0 Launch. The Co-op multiplayer and wholesome community are the core experience of this game. The classes all synergize well with each other to traverse the expanses of the caves, though even on their own, they have enough tools to make it around. After a hard mission's work, you and your new dwarf buddies stop by the bar and have a blast before heading off. On current patch: 1.0, I would rate this game 7.5/10 (6/10 if solo). I am sure with how amazing Ghost Ship is, the game will very likely continue to improve and thrive. I would absolutely recommend this game to anyone who likes Left for Dead, Minecraft, or Vermintide.

_childDocuments_.review: Solid 7/10. Steam doesn't rate games on a point grading system, so despite the glowing reviews, Deep Rock Galactic isn't a masterpiece like Steam makes it out to be. There just isn't much to complain about, hence the overwhelmingly positive reviews.If I had to give a feedback, I wish there were more interesting, whacky weapons and more varieties of monster types.DRG is a game done right, but it isn't going to shake up the industry.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is one of, if not, the BEST game I've ever played. I bought this game way back in April 2018, around a month after its alpha launch release, and that may have been the greatest 24.99$ I've ever spent. The amount of fun I've had playing this game, either with friends or with randoms, is insane. The community is also extremely nice, but of course there are always the rare leaf lovers out there. The amount of FREE content that the devs have, and are adding, to this game is amazing. By free content, I mean new weapons, biomes, missions and monsters. But guess what... there's more! Around nine months ago, the devs added seasons in DRG and with these seasons came a battle pass. Now you might be wondering, "Oh, a battle pass that I'll have to pay to get access to, just like every other game that has one". Well guess what... you're wrong. The battle pass is 100% FREE. Yes you heard right, a free battle pass. Now, I could go on and on about all of the other fantastic things that this game has, but management isn't really pleased that I'm not working. So go buy this game, leave no dwarves behind and most importantly, go make Karl proud!!ROCK AND STONE BROTHERS!!!!Edit: Please vote Deep Rock Galactic for the Labor of Love award. They deserve it :)

_childDocuments_.review: Surprise, surprise! The game turned out pretty damn good even this early!Running with a full dedicated 4 man squad, working together and been having an absolute blast.It's a mission-type kind of game, where you get a set of goals to complete, then you have to escape without dying.Mix a bit of Left for dead, Vermintide but a little calmer with some resource gathering similar in survival games and you'll get this, pretty much!Every class you can pick so far has their own use which helps the group over all in some ways which is handy.I personally wouldn't recommend playing this game alone.
