_childDocuments_.review: I saw this game come by a few times and it looked interesting because im a fan of the whole co-op, 4 player team play style like left4dead, Then again it also looked a bit weird and i am not a big fan of early acces games but it came on sale and thought i would give it a try.And man am i glad i did!First offThe audio in this game for the guns and the impact it makes when you shoot the bugs is really wel done.The overall design of the game and caves are great.You have a level system with skill points pretty cool skills and are able to upgrade your gear and arsenal aswel.You need to grind resources that you get from doing missions to be able to upgrade your gear.4 classes you can play, Gunner, Driller, Scout and Engineer, Each with their own skill set and gear you can upgrade.A lobby list to find people to play with and a good host system with good conectivityi had no problem finding games to play with and when i hosted my own lobby i had people join within 5min.You can see they put a lot of work and love into this game and to think that this game is in alpha state.I'm glad i gave this game a shot and i will enjoy playing it and keeping track of its progression ( hope they keep working on it )- Rock and Stone my Brothers!

_childDocuments_.review: Supports up to 4-player online co-op, but the difficulty scales to keep the game balanced as intended. When playing solo, you're accompanied with a support drone so that you don't miss out on the benefits of working in a team.In addition to automatic difficulty scaling, players can select their own difficulty level for the mission. Each mission is also designed in such a way that some are inherently harder than others, while others can be a casual breeze.Strong replayability because of the diverse mission types, mission modifiers, sub-activities, and playable classes. Small game size because the biomes/caves are procedurally generated. Various progression systems that extend out for some time, but the main progression loops are kept close to the player.The four classes function in distinctly different ways that are still fun and useful, and can be built to play into either more generalized or more niche roles depending on your playstyle.Mission loops are designed well enough that most aspects of the missions are fun to do and come back to.Music and audio design is great. The dialogue is a solid "hot potato" out of 10. Graphics are great, and the art style is consistent throughout the game and its cosmetic DLCs.

Doesn't require lot's of gold to play.+ proves HD-graphics are not needed for AAA fun!+ unique look+ weakpoint system+ funny lobby/ship bar with magical beers that let you do fun stuffSince I bought the game it got (without any dlc cost!):+ 12 more enemy-types+ 2 Mini-Bosses+ 2 "Boss-Fight" eventmaps+ 3 more ingame map events that can happen+ 3 more map bioms+ 6+ more map types (mission types)+ 8 more weapons+ over 20 new mods for weapons+ 3 fun Mini-games on Lobby/Ship+ DLCs are just to support the DEVS. _childDocuments_.review: It's a good game. I had a lot of fun playing it with friends but also with the people who I joined or those who joined me. The 4 classes give a decent amount of variety to keep you interested for a long time and they all take a little bit of time to master. Lots of cosmetic items and most of them are free! (just locked behind a grind wall).The positives: - teamwork oriented game for up to 4 players with a 'matchmaking' system (you can create a lobby (public or friends only) that others will be able to join) - decent variety of content with semi-procedurally generated maps (major caves are usually generated from a predefined list of seeds) - 4 well designed classes with unique tools and different tasks to carry out during missions - high number of active players ensures you will always be able to find a team - weekly content (deep dives and assignments) - lots of free cosmetics to give your dwarves a unique look. If you miss out on any event or assignment cosmetics, they are not gone. You may get them by logging in the next year during the event or from cargo crates in the game. - updates (although not frequently. usually 5-6 months apart) - very friendly community (keep it up, fellow miners!) - lots of grind (if you like it)The downsides of this game: - lots of bugs - I died and teleported to another dimension (800m away from teammates which is way beyond the map), physics randomly decided to yeet me into the air and I died of fall damage, molly stuck (several times), bulk detonator spawning in front of doretta (instant fail), doretta pathing straight down, doretta pathing straight up, doretta pathing through every geyser on the map, doretta flying in the air, mule legs not spawning, core infuser not spawning and a lot more that I've forgotten about - escort tends to be long (30 mins+ for max length escort even if you are a team of 4 dwarves rank 200+ doing everything as efficiently as possible), which has made running deep dives a pain (I spent around 1h 20 mins doing a deep dive elite in a team of 2 while my average time used to be 40 mins before the update) - becomes somewhat boring after a longer playtime (rerunning the same mission types, similar/identical maps, annoying bosses, poorly balanced minerals) - lots of grind (if you dislike it) - the game doesn't care whether you'll be able to complete a mission. Will you have enough time to get to the pod even if you keep running all the time? Will you survive bulk detonator spawning right next to you? Will you have enough oxygen to survive molly going through a tiny hole in the ceiling or clipping through a solid wall? It's your problem

_childDocuments_.review: (Still) One of the best Co-op/PvE games available right now. Every class has worthwhile offensive/support capability but play differently enough to make them interesting. Heaps of equipment upgrades and cosmetics to unlock. And so far, great post launch support. I'm looking forward to seeing what this game is like in a year or two.24/11/22: Since I posted the initial review, DRG has just gotten better and better. They regularly add heaps of new content. They also recently introduced their version of seasons and battle passes, which practically gets rid of the FOMO feeling by adding any unclaimed cosmetics from that season into the overall cosmetic loot pile. I only play with friends, but my understanding is that the community is pretty welcoming and friendly.Out of the all the 4-player co-op games to choose from these days, I would put this one at the very top. It's that good.Rock & Stone! For Karl! Etc.23/11/23: Just updating for badge progression. Game still kicks ass.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot to offer, from beer, dwarves, alien insects to awesome beards for customizing your badass dwarf. I first stumbled upon this game around Update 8 or 9 and I thought to myself "hmm, this game looks like lots of fun". I managed to buy it a little later, around Update 16 or 17. Anyway, I was astonished by this game from the first mission. At some moments it feels a little repetitive, but that's mostly because you're playing alone. I decided to nag some friends into buying it and the game showed it's true potential (just to clarify, the game is tons of fun when you play it solo too, but I can see how it could get a little boring for some people).  Playing this game with friends is easily the best recipe for almost endless hours of fun! The game has 4 classes and a party would consist of 4 people at most. Each character is unique in it's own way. Lastly, I have to add that the things mentioned about the classes, it's just a portion of what the game offers. There are also new guns you get as you progress through the game, upgrades for your weapons, different types of throwable grenades, perks that you can unlock and combine them for different play styles, beer, a shop to customize your character and more beer. All in all, I give this game a solid 9/10. The only thing that I would consider a con, would be some performance issues and not enough beer.Update: this game still slaps and these developers are one of the best!ROCK AND STONE!

_childDocuments_.review: Deep Rock Galactic. Danger. Darkness. Dwarves. This game is a 4 player coop game that forces you to work together to escape this horrific planet's depths with your lives... or die trying.You play as a dwarf working for the Aptly named, Deep Rock Galactic. A mining company that employs underpaid dwarfs to fight whatever alien bugs can be located deep within the bowls of Hoxxes IV. Your goal is simple. Go in, mine, kill bugs, get out with your lives. Simple right? Yes- In theory.There are four classes to choose from, War criminal with a flamethrower and drills (Driller), Spiderman with a double barrel shotgun (Scout), Big man with a big gun (Gunner) and turret man with a nuke (Engineer).Every role is built well enough that if you go a mission without that role you will think "damn, I wish a scout was here to get that gold up high", "i wish there was a driller to let us have a B-line straight back to the droppod", "I wish we had a gunner to take down this REALLY big bug" "I wish there was an engineer here to help me up high." The value of every role can not be understated. As someone who has tried every class, I love the scout, driller, gunner then engineer (in that order).Right- back to the actual review. This game is fantastic. It has everything you want from an FPS. This can be described as "Left 4 dead meets minecraft" and you wouldn't be that far off. Everyone in this game lives by one motto, and a phrase "Leave no dwarf behind" and "Rock and Stone." There is NEVER an inappropriate time to Rock and Stone. Beat a hard boss? Rock and Stone! got your asses beat and sent to the med-bay? Rock and Stone! Engineer placed a platform so you can grapple up to some gold? Rock and Stone! Going back up? Rock and Stone! The dialogue is amazing. One time I pinged a dwarf and my dwarf said "Did you borrow my underwear?", they pinged me right back with "Did you borrow my underwear?" and I almost passed out of laughter. The motto is also one to look at "Leave no dwarf behind" your dwarf has a chance to say this whilst pressing V (the rock and stone button) and it says it on the drop-pod floor. I have had countless missions where someone has gone down deep within the cave. And without a second thought I've grappled out of the drop-pod to go help them up. That person is one of your teammates. A friendly face in the deepest darkest deadilest pit of this planet. You do your damned hardest to make sure everyone comes back alive. Someone should stay in the drop-pod to make sure it's a successful mission. The mission variety is good from an escort mission ending in a boss fight to a simple mining mission to refining liquid minerals to fighting REALLY big bugs. You can get hammered and go on missions (yes you can drink on the job). That's all without even mentioning the music. It's eerie, atmospheric and really caputres the essence of being deep within a hostile enviroment.  This game has it all and you should play it. I'm glad I got to experience this before I died. Danger. Darkness. Dwarves. Rock and stone brother. o7 peace out.

_childDocuments_.review: Rock and Stone Everyone!Do you like  Dwarves and the fantasy themed worlds they come from? You know, they drink a lot, mine a lot, and grow magnificent facial hair?Deep Rock Galactic is basically "Dwarves in space!" Where you (and up to 3 other friends) jump into a space drop pod, and scour deep inside a space asteroid looking for rare minerals.Deep Rock Galactic is a First Person Shooter developed by Ghost Ship Games and released in May 2020.If you don't like reading, or are curious about watching gameplay check out my video here: "Explore the universe" they said, "It'll get you off planet" they said. Well what your character didn't realize is that meant being covered in Bug guts, doing all the grunt labor and repairs on shoddy company equipment at best, and always being on call to do whatever upper management requires of you. Good thing we're not our characters! In Deep Rock Galactic you play as a Dwarf (either individual, or as a member of a up-to-4-person-squad) trying to earn an honest living doing an honest Job.You've joined the Deep Rock Galactic mining company, which has tasked its members to do various missions in space, which range from simple mineral extraction missions, to equipment repair, sometimes the missions get more complex with industrial Sabotage missions......other times you'll be doing a simple mission and stumble across a bonus objective which will completely derail you from the original objective and a quick 15 minute mission will increase to a 40 minute adventure and you'll look at the clock and realize "OH CRAP" it's WAY past your bed time and you need to wake up early tomorrow for work.Well... I guess if my real life supervisor reads this review,  they'll know why i came into work so sleepy. The general idea for Deep Rock Galactic, is Select a Dwarf (class), Select a Mission, Jump in the drop pod, do the thing - to complete the mission, Rock and Stone everybody, Get paid, Do it again.Now everything else coloring the game and world is what really makes it stick for me. You have 4 different classes (you can all play as the same class by the way, want a team of 4 gunners? go for it!), Each class plays differently and has different ways of navigating the map.The driller can burrow his way through the map, by literally creating his own tunnels. The Engineer can create platforms to reach those hard to get places. The Gunner can set down a zip-line that the whole team can use. The Scout has a personal UNLIMITED zip-line and a flare gun which lights up the whole room for the team.Any one of these methods is great. But this is where Deep Rock Galactic really shines; team up with a friend or three... and see how well all these methods complement each other.For one of our groups favorites: A scout will zip-line to the ceiling to get ore, then the engineer will make a platform under him, so he can let go of the ceiling and mine.There's a lot of different missions to do in the game. Mining Expedition, Searching for Eggs, On-site Refining, Repairing Broken Equipment, Escorting "Doretta" the Drilldozer, hunting down particularly nasty bosses and destroying/stealing the competitions property.All these missions have a bonus secondary objective which requires you to collect another mineral/resource (except for Fester Fleas, you just squash them)As you Run around collecting minerals, you'll quickly find out two things: 1) Oh no, I'm full, I can't carry any more!At this point you will either deposit into Molly the M.U.L.E, or you'll deposit into a station or drop pod in a specific location on the map.As you fight to keep the bugs off your back, and on harder difficulties you'll also discover 2) OH NO! I'm out of ammo!This one's a bit more dire. You can call in resupply pods, but that costs Nitra (A red mineral found in levels), if you don't have enough Nitra, you won't get your resupply... you realize what that means don't you? You can no longer shoot your weapons, now you need to smash, every, single, bug, with your pickax melee attack... trust me, that's exhausting, and I'm not even the one swinging the axe.That's probably more then enough information to get started playing Deep Rock Galactic, but upon diving into the game you'll quickly learn just how much stuff there is in Deep Rock Galactic, It's great!You have different gear load outs, you unlock new weapons. After your character gets to level 25 you promote, there are special "Warnings" on maps which add a new Hazard to levels, there's different Anomalies which keep the game fresh, there's lots and LOTS of cosmetics, there's different beers to craft, there's weapon modifications, there's deep dives where you do a series of missions back-to-back and keep the same Ammo and Nitra from level to level, there are are seasonal cosmetics, and holiday cosmetics, Ghost Ship Games keeps on releasing new content and cosmetic DLC you can buy to further support them! It seems like just yesterday I loaded up this game to play with my brothers for the first time. Now I look back and see "Woah, I've already played over a hundred hours already".I have really enjoyed playing Deep Rock Galactic, It's actually tough, because I have so many unplayed games in my steam backlog which I'm trying to chip away at, and then I go and get myself hooked on Deep  Rock Galactic!Deep Rock Galactic keeps bringing me back for more, and I think that's a good sign of a game I'm thoroughly enjoying playing, and if that doesn't speak volumes to my opinion of the game, I don't know what will. If anything at all in my review sounded like something you'd enjoy, you should definitely give Deep Rock a try.If not that's good too! Then you've had some time saved for playing another game. Either way, I hope this review has been helpful, thank you for reading!

_childDocuments_.review: (DRG) is a class based Co-op and Solo first-person shooter with procedurally generated levels and an heavy emphasis on customization, set in a universe where Dwarves have colonized space far and wide. Orbiting the planet Hoxxes, you and your eventual companions will engage in a variety of missions deep under the earth, infested with countless numbers of hostile aliens. Shoot, blast and dig your way to success for glory, promotions and rich rewards..🟩 🟥 🎮 Gameplay is divided into Preparation, Exploration, Objectives and Combat. Is done at your space station, using a variety of terminals to equip yourself, accept assignments and modify your appearance. There also is a bar where you can drink beer for various hilarious effects, while some grant passive bonuses for the next mission. The station also includes a variety of minigames and silly things to do such as kicking barrels around. Each of your classes can be assigned three different sets for diverse occasions, and as you rise through Global and Class ranks you will unlock new weapons and upgrades.Is performed on foot and by using a variety of tools unique to each class. Drillers will employ a powerful excavator to make tunnels, Scouts will use their hook to fly around, Gunners build ziplines to traverse gaps, and Engineers can shoot platforms to build bridges and walkways. Exploring each environment thoroughly is important to find all the required materials such as minerals or parts, to complete the mission objectives and call supplies.  A handy terrain scanner allows to see a 3D map of the caves, while markers and waypoints can also be placed. Illumination is always a concern and flares are for that. Hordes of enemies will keep spawning so being also fast is key. Finding events and hidden loot is time consuming but rewarding.Vary for each mission, and include a Primary target needed to call the Pod and evacuate, while also a secondary one for extra XP and credits. In an Extermination mission you will have to take down multiple Glyphid bosses, while in a Repair mission you need to fix some MULEs and an entire Pod to use to escape, while attacked on all sides. Assignments are global quests that usually require you to complete a series of regular missions, and award cosmetics, weapons or licenses depending on the type. Deep Dives are basically 3-in-1 missions with two Primary targets each and higher difficulty - but also special rewards.Plays out in FPS fashion and focuses on a variety of status effects, weakspots and positioning. Each enemy has certain weak points that if hit inflict massive damage, while also resistance or weakness to certain elements. Many weapons and enemies inflict status effects such as Stun, Burning, Frozen and so on - using such at your advantage while positioning well in the map is fundamental. Taking on a horde of 100 enemies in the open is not a good idea, kiting them in a narrow passage is. There is a good amount of strategizing, synergy between weapon effects to discover and employ. You can never truly die but get incapacitated, a companion can revive you in this case, with 10% HP unless specific perks are used. Deforming terrain to your advantage proves really useful to combat if the conditions are right. Stay together or die alone.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: A satisfying and fun co-op shooter where you can expect a lot of content baked into it. If you've played games like Payday 2 or Left 4 Dead 2, this might be up your alley. You'll be amazed at exploring and learning the many things that this game has to offer. Graphics are very simple, but still beautiful with the lighting effects. Really fun for people who play solo as well!I'm roughly 50 hours in and I've only finished scratching the surface of what this game has to offer, that's how deep this game is. Oh and did I mention that this is only 3 GIGABYTES?? And that this game is REALLY OPTIMIZED?? I first played Deep Rock Galatic during a free weekend, and damn it made me realize that I really should've played sooner. This is a co-op game, but still very playable when going solo. The gameplay loop is very satisfying and addictive. Start the mission in a cave of sorts, collect minerals, collect mission objectives, and then get out, simple as that. There's numerous mission types to keep your busy, with varying biomes and modifiers to change up the the experience quite a bit. While for some this might get repetitive and boring, I don't find it that way. I can just enjoy the game and shut my brain off, at least on the lower Hazards (difficulties). To add to this, the different caves look beautiful. While yes the VERY simplistic look of the textures may throw you off, the colors and the lights make up for that. The visuals are beautiful all things considered, especially since this game is very optimized and is really small in size at only less than 3 gigabytes.I have really yet to explore all the aspects of this game. I've only really focused on one class so far, and currently trying to level up another. There's enough weapons to make each class feel different in terms of their play-style, and the devs are adding even more later down the line. On top of that, each class has its strengths and weaknesses, but none of them stand out to be "the best" class. In fact, I feel like all the classes are fairly balanced when compared against each other, taking into consideration their weapons and gadgets. If you're still deciding whether you should buy this game or not, I urge you to really try it. Words alone can't describe how fun this game is! If you're still on the fence, then wait for a sale, at that point this game is even more worth your money.

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love it.1 The combination of random generation and handcrafted environments makes the same missions never feel old.2 Excellent community never toxic in my experience.3 Weapon modification never simply makes something better, I will find myself grappling over picking between the available options. If I take the faster reload I can spare 1.5 seconds in the middle of battle and I don't need the larger magazine size but if it's upgraded from 6 to 11 I can manage my reloading more so I won't need the fast reload...But increased the fire rate means I can clear all groups quicker and be able to reload in peace...it's all down to how you play and you can go back to any of your old upgrades at any time for free.4 overclocks. Clean overclocks give you small up size with no downsides. Balanced overclocks give you large upsides with larger downsides. Unstable overclocks can completely change weapons characteristics. An example I use a lot would be how the scouts duel SMGs can be unstably overclocks so every shot you miss turns into a tiny cryo mine.5 This you may disagree with but I find the game doesn't encourage me to mane. What I mean is when you jump into a mission it puts the team at a disadvantage to double run a class. The game almost encourages you to be adapt at all classes.6 It's just an excellent game with solid game play that hasn't let me down and it can't run on a cheesecake but has surprisingly low specification.7 good developer morals. I salute you Ghost Ship Games for not having a single paywall, microtransactions or making the grind so steep you need to buy boosters in favour for a balanced progression. There are DLCs with some unique cosmetics But...I argue these are more voluntary donations to the developers.8 Ghost Ship Games has active community ears and keeps the game continuously patched and updated with new content.This is mission control signing off, good luck miners."Rock And Stone."

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR;I'm not sure I can remember the last time I had this much fun. Minecraft cave-diving meets Left 4 Dead/Payday. Get this game.********************************This video game is amazing.You are space dwarves. Mining an alien planet's caves. These caves are full of alien bugs. We just did a mission that had freaking earthquakes that opened freaking magma fissures under our freaking feet as we ran away from a swarm of angry space-bugs, beaten, battered, low on health and ammo. This game throws some truly diabolical situations at you. But by using all the tools we had at our disposal with all 4 classes, we were able to overcome these challenges and still make it back to the pod and escape with our mined riches.The atmosphere is spot on. The narrow spaces feel claustrophobic. The big caves are truly cavernous. Light is an issue. So is finding a a safe spot to fight. Sometimes you have to make a spot safe to fight in.  Each biome feels significantly different. I'm really curious what the game will throw at us next.This game is Early Access. I bought it on sale for 25% off. I would absolutely recommend this game, even at full price, if you enjoyed any of the following games: Minecraft, Killing Floor, Left 4 Dead, or Payday. This game scratches that same itch. And IMO it scratches it better. Don't get discouraged if you get beaten down a few times early on. Every failure is a learning opportunity.In short: Get this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Deep Rock Galactic is one of those rare games that continues to receive loving updates from its developers. To this day, new content is regularly released, including new weapon overclocks, mission types, enemy types, cosmetics, and more. Most cosmetics can be earned through SEASONS, which are completely FREE. It’s a solid co-op shooter that offers four different playable classes: Scout, Driller, Gunner, and Engineer.For the best gameplay experience, it's recommended to form a team with all four classes (the game is best balanced for four players but is still fun with fewer). Each class complements the others with its unique utilities. Here’s a brief overview of each class:Gunner: The least mobile class, but provides the highest sustain damage. The Gunner’s strong suit is the shield, which can be deployed at a chosen location to protect anyone inside from enemy damage.Driller: Offers high mobility for the entire team by drilling through the cave walls to access hard-to-reach areas. Most of Driller’s weapons deal steady damage with fire, acid, or frost, making him effective against smaller enemies and conserving ammo.Scout: The most mobile class, able to quickly grapple to cave walls, making it easy to reach difficult spots. The Scout is typically the main miner of valuable resources that are hard for other classes to access. Provides utility with a flare gun that lights up the cave. The Scout’s weapons focus on single-target damage to weak spots.Engineer: Has weaker primary weapons but incredibly strong secondary ones designed for high burst damage. The Engineer provides utility with deployable platforms, great for helping Scouts reach high places and reducing fall damage. Additionally, the Engineer can set up sentry turrets.A major advantage of the game is the extremely friendly player base, with the lowest number of toxic players compared to other multiplayer games. This low toxicity is partly because it’s a PvE game, where players are more focused on fun than competition.Replayability is high, with endless goals like collecting all the cosmetic items (none of which are pay-to-win). The only purchasable content is available on the Steam store as DLCs, offering visual upgrades for weapons and armor sets. However, the game provides plenty of these upgrades through regular gameplay without needing to buy DLCs. As a regular supporter, I own all available DLCs, but I still use many in-game-earned armor sets and weapon upgrades.Managing ammo effectively is crucial, as you don’t have unlimited supplies. Another key aspect is maintaining good situational awareness, avoiding being surrounded, and always having an escape route.I highly recommend the game. If you don’t have friends to play with, don’t worry. You can join other players, and most communication happens through pings, so there’s no need to worry about social anxiety. The developers respect your time and money, avoiding predatory practices common in many modern games.Rock and Stone!

_childDocuments_.review: I usually don't write reviews, but this game needs to be in as many steam accounts as possible. People need to play this and relearn how game were made before microtransactions ruined the industry.If you don't trust me as you should, play it for 1 hour and decide for yourself. Give it back or keep it. I will almost promise you, you will keep and love it.Ok, now to the game.You play a dwarf and exploit a planet and kill everything that tries to step in your way. At the time of writing this there are four classes (scout, engineer, gunner and miner) each with different main weapons, sidearms, grenades and skills. Each class can work on its own, but excels if matched with the others.The worlds are generated randomly, but never feel fractured or out of place. The "late-game" introduces deep dives, which are a series of multiple handcrafted levels. Each level has a specific objective which you have to achieve, but I don't want to go deeper here, as the fun of discovering new stuff in this game is present, and I don't want to ruin that. Do yourself a favor and don't google any mission types or anything else, at least until you have seen and discovered everything on your own.Deep Rock Galactic is an extremely fun game made how they used to be back in the days before EA and Bethesda haunted our wallets. Yes you pay once for this game. Despise there are probably more cosmetics in this game than there are stars in the Milky Way, and there are no in-game payments in sight. I can't emphasize this enough: This game has absolutely no in-game payments, none. If you want a cosmetic, play the game and earn it. The game is extremely fun, progress does not feel like a grind, the devs actually care for their game, and you can feel and see it in every corner of this game. There are details which maybe get spotted by 1% of the players but still the devs put them there, because they care.Updates are frequently and astonishing in size and content. Modding just works (even somewhat balanced for multiplayer). I highly recommend playing it with friends, but solo or online with randoms is quite fun too.This game is just a giant, planet-sized f-you to "game"-companies that gone down the dark route of microtransactions, whaling and other tactics to squeeze as much money as humanly possible out of a boring game. This one here is exactly the opposite.ps: Please excuse my rather junky English, as I am no native speaker.pps: Buy this game ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, you've read a huge review about it, clearly you want it.

_childDocuments_.review: Deep Rock Galactic is a FPS 1-4 co-op game that takes place on the planet Hoxxes IV. Play as a dwarf and fight endless waves of alien bugs while trying to stay alive and complete your mission. Completing missions for DRG (DRG is the name of the company you work for) is the main objective of the game. These mission can range from manual mining to killing hordes of space bugs.There are four types of dwarf classes, each with their own unique guns and utilities. Each dwarf plays a little different, but they are all balanced. Procedural cave generation. Each cave is procedurally-generated with new environment for a fresh experience on every trip down to Hoxxes IV. Not only is there procedural cave generation, but the entire environment in DRG is destructible.Cosmetics are a big deal in DRG. Every player has the chance to gain free cosmetics by completing assignments, leveling up, or purchasing them from the shop. Hundreds of cosmetics are available to fit every player's style and preferences.DLCs. There are paid DLCs for DRG, but they do not have any impact on gameplay or stats. The DLCs are only extra cosmetics to jazz up your dwarf if you so chose.Season pass. There are seasons in DRG and they are completely free. Each new season comes with approximately 100 levels with free cosmetics, cash, or resources on every level. No need to buy the season pass to get something good. There are NO limited time cosmetics. Each cosmetic from the season pass in repurposed into another aspect of the game, so anyone who missed them can still collect them with some luck.I highly recommend playing with friends, but if you don't have any, do not worry. Deep Rock Galactic is an incredibly indulging game to play solo, with high stakes action to keep you on your toes. Online Co-op is available. Deep Rock Galactic has hundreds of hours of game play and almost infinite replay-ability. I give Deep Rock Galactic a rating of 9.7/10 only because of some of the achievements. A bit of a pricey game, but when it's on sale definitely go pick it up. Other than that, I have nothing bad to say about DRG. Truly a spectacular game, Rock and Stone!

So you can tear down the walls or dig wherever you want to go. But this game can be a lot more if there were a lot of players playing.Optimization for this game is great. I don't suppose you need a beefy computer just to play this game. _childDocuments_.review: I did have fun playing DRG, but I think this game is still incredibly flawed and a little flat, which surprised me given it's overwhelmingly positive reception. After over a hundred hours of playing this game, I can say with absolute confidence that it is lacking content. You are introduced to the game by having to complete one of each mission type, which is a great way to start someone on a journey with proper expectations. The issue is that it doesn't scale into anything more grand, mechanically. There are just buffs and debuffs which make the same 10 missions more chaotic and difficult to handle. At some point, you will unlock Deep-dives, which may indicate that more diverse content and a deeper progression system should be locked behind it. No, this isn't the case either. Deep Dives are just a randomly selected three missions, out of the same 10 missions you've already done over and over, but with random debuffs and more bugs. This was really disappointing because you have to promote your dwarves to even unlock this feature (along with other side missions you can't participate in until you promote), only to do more of the same thing. This is a huge missed opportunity to have unique bosses and map layouts that deviate largely from the core 10 mission types, but could encourage the players to use the skills developed to overcome these weekly challenges.  This part of the game is great, until you get to promotions, then it completely tapers off as there's no incentive to promote other than flexing how long you've been playing the game. All of the major playstyle changes come when you unlock passives on your armor, weapons, Pick-axe, robot helper and grenades. This is where the most fun in the game comes from, because all the features are new, your character is incomplete, and there is something significant to strive for. You feel the power of having 2 passives, and then 4 passives, etc, and start to establish a style for your gameplay. There are weapon alterations which you can make, but you won't have access to those until you've farmed some weeklies and deep dives post promotion. After promoting, there's nothing... Just empty levels, which don't reward you at all. No additional damage reduction, dmg dealt, enhanced passives or party buffs... Nothing that you would expect when you look at a player who has a 3-star gold promoted Dwarf, who then dies just as fast as you and outputs the same as you. This just doesn't make any sense to me. I recognize this is potentially design-space, which could be saved for a future update, but this game has been out almost 4 years at the time of writing and this studio is working a new project in the same world as DRG. This system is mostly good. I don't have a lot to say about the different cosmetics themselves, they are fun and interesting. My main criticism is actually regarding the way they are obtained. Each of the four dwarves have their own independent customization loadouts, but it's the same hairstyles, colors, armors, etc for each dwarf and you have to purchase them all separately. I think this is totally ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and could improved very easily. The full collection should be available to be used by any dwarf, just divide the cosmetic unlockables amongst the classes, so that there's an incentive to change classes. Like a mustache or a particular pair of chops? Well, you gotta play the Driller to get it or maybe the Engineer has a unique armor you want to unlock on your gunner. This facilitates each player spending some amount of time on each character and a proper reward for doing whatever the requirement is. Currently, it's just grind mats, buy hairline 1 on all 4 classes. Grind more mats, buy hairline 2 on all 4 classes, and that's awful.This is where I honestly feel the game's identity is the strongest. The Jokes are funny, the characters are endearing, and the music when you're in the middle of the ♥♥♥♥ is freaking awesome. They've really captured the essence of a 9-5 job, and turned it into a game, which is hilarious and relatable!I had a unique experience with DRG, and there's a lot of things that are done right in this game. There's a lot of charm in this game, and it's clear that this project was loved by the Developers and it's community. Their seasonal pass is very generous and rewards effort over money. Their DLCs are reasonably priced. The game is fast-paced, and while is easy to get lost and very chaotic, it's still fun. But would I recommend it? Personally, no. _childDocuments_.review: TL;DRBest cooperative game since years! It's fun, super polished, full of surprises and never gets old imho. _childDocuments_.review: Deep Rock Galactic is a co-operative first person shooter. Each player plays as a dwarf miner, sent to a planet to extract its resources, fend off its natives, and pet everything and anything that can be petted. There is no real overarcing plot - or if there is, I don’t know that I’ve encountered it - just the story of these dwarves, dropping on to a planet, and coming back up at the end. As an FPS, it has quite a bit to offer. Each dwarf comes equipped with a broad range of weapons, tools, and unique loadouts. Everything from the armour to the perks to the tools is customisable, and customised they will be. Levels themselves are hugely dynamic, with lots of opportunities for customisation to suit each player’s tastes and needs. When I played, for example, my friends were considerate enough to not put the difficulty too high to ensure I was alive at least some of the time. When I did die - as I did, repeatedly - they were also able to come find and resurrect me, meaning I was rarely out of the game for long. Even the structure of the levels themselves are hugely dynamic, with players being able to construct platforms, ziplines, or death pits to their heart’s content. It’s fantastic game design, and it ensures that each level remains unique, even when players have played the game for hundreds or thousands of hours. And, I’ll be honest, it just doesn’t land for me. I will be blunt - this isn’t my game. I’ve spent an unreasonable amount of time trying to figure out why. I have played over a dozen missions with my friends, listening to them explain what the goal of the level is, what’s expected of my, and what all my various bits, bobs, and whizbangs do. I have dutifully flambeed insects with my flamethrower, petted the drill tank, slapped dice, and chucked explosives out of a door, and yet still, this game doesn’t land for me. It’s not even that I don’t enjoy playing it. I do, for a mission or two, enjoy engaging in the memes and the silliness of wandering through a delicately glowing planet to grab large balls. But then, the experience quickly gets overwhelming, and I sour on it. I spent much of the playthrough I recorded for this review reflecting on why that is, and what it is about Deep Rock Galactic that works so well for thousands of people, but so poorly for me. My friends might tell me it’s that I need to try different classes, or to play single player, or with someone other than them, and there might be some truth to that. I enjoy playing driller, though, and I enjoy playing with them, and am just generally leery of multiplayer games with strangers, so I don’t know that any of those will necessarily be the answer.It was at about the point that I sat beside my friend, watching two more friends play Deep Rock Soccer while we all drank beers that I think I figured it out. I figured out not only why the game doesn’t work for me, but why it works so well for everyone else. What Deep Rock Galactic does right that so few other multiplayer games do is foster a genuinely wholesome and cooperative community. This isn’t accidental - the game itself is designed to promote a sense of camaraderie the moment a player joins the lobby. In addition to the level itself and the necessity for players to work together, the lobby is full of opportunities for players to casually interact with each other. From the aforementioned football pitch to a jukebox and dance floor, the game encourages players to not just jump from mission to mission, but to take a moment, have fun and unwind, and enjoy each other’s company before diving in once again. This, in turn, creates a sense of camaraderie between the players that mirrors that between the dwarves. Much like how the dwarves promise not to leave another dwarf behind, as the players climb into the ship and salute each other, they make a similar promise - they are a team, even if one member of the team is me, who struggled to figure out how not to dig a death pit on literally every mission.This sense of camaraderie - and just good game design as an FPS - is what makes the game so successful and work so well. It’s also, I think, why I struggle so much to find my place within it.  I’ve written previously about the depiction of neurodiverse people in games, and about how that feels for me, as an autistic person, to experience. Here, I have almost the opposite experience. Deep Rock Galactic does not depict neurodiverse characters, per se, but rather, a very neurotypical dynamic in a very neurotypical space. This is a team of dwarves. They socialise, they build relationships, they share a common culture, and they work together towards their commonly understood goals. There is an assumption of knowledge and tendencies embedded within the fabric of their society, and it’s one the player is asked to quickly understand and adopt. For my friends, this is easy. They understand this culture, how to move into a space and find commonality with the people in it, and how to participate in that sense of camaraderie. And I…don’t. I struggle enormously with the basics of making connections with people. I don’t pick up on the subtle clues; I learn a group’s norms by chameleoning myself into it, and I memorise the memes and spout them off in the hopes that that’s enough to help me blend in. It is, don’t get me wrong. I blend in just fine, and always have, just not to myself. Engaging with people and building these connections and working together as a team in a shared space is a deeply taxing experience. Within the sheer dynamism of Deep Rock Galactic’s missions, it becomes too much. I get lost and lapse into silence, dutifully following the team, but missing half of what is meant to make the game fun and compelling. I’m lacking that spirit of camaraderie, and no amount of having mission dynamics explained to me will conjure it up. Without it, Deep Rock Galactic becomes just another multiplayer FPS that I’m playing on touchpad. It’s well-designed, but it isn’t the bombastic exploration machine that everyone else seems to be playing. I am an outsider in a culture not designed for me, and I feel every moment of it, even if no one else ever notices that I do.There is an irony to recognising that the thing that makes a game work so well is exactly the dynamic that makes it not click for me. Equally, though, not every game is for every player. I can recognise that Deep Rock Galactic is objectively good, while also understanding that it is not a game I can find a place in. It’s also not to say that my experience is universal; there are many players who struggle with social connections in the outside world for whom games provide a great opportunity for that social connection. Just not me. What I want from a game and what Deep Rock Galactic offers are on opposite ends of the spectrum, and that’s okay. I can still wander along with the group, digging my death pits, petting lootbugs, and accidentally blowing up the rest of the team. For Karl.If you enjoyed this review, please feel free to check out the  and . Thanks for reading!

_childDocuments_.review: Rock and Stone! This review has been a long time coming. Let me start with a hot-button-issue that I often want to know when I come to the reviews:  Coffee Stain Studios is once again showing that picking up good developers and keeping things consumer friendly is a great business model.  Less than 1% of the cosmetics in the game come from DLC (which act as more of a donation than anything), and everything else is unlockable for free in game with original purchase.  There is no FOMO; all event cosmetics are given to you retroactively for logging in during an event (e.g. christmas this year will award new cosmetics + all past christmas cosmetics for free) and all past season pass cosmetics are added to the world loot pool after the season ends so that they can be found in caves.  Did I mention the battle pass is free for everyone, every time?In a greedy AAA-gaming world, DRG is a true beacon of hope for what indie comapanies can accomplish.  Ghost Ship Games, the developer of DRG, remind me of gaming companies and how they used to be: excited, compassionate, gamers who play their own game and make the product they themselves would want to enjoy.  Fun, gameplay, and the consumer come before money to them.You'll *want* to buy the DLC just to support these guys after you get a few dozen hours into the game.  I haven't even begun to talk about the great gameplay.  As far as horde shooters go (e.g. Left 4 Dead and others), DRG is among the top of the pile.  It oozes style and creativity.  The guns and other tools are great, the teamwork is excellent, the communication tools available (context-dependent-ping system, etc.) allow for communication without talking, and it's just a lot of fun even without friends.The game is consistently updated with bug fixes (frequently) and seasonal content with free battle pass (every 6ish months).  The battle pass is 100% free to all players. Each season seems to bring more content than the last and Season 3 is about to begin as of writing this.Get Deep Rock Galactic.  It'll make Karl proud (you'll understand later).  There's a reason it's one of the top 10 most highly praised games on Steam.Can I get a Rock and Stone?

The random generated levels makes it endlessly re-playable, and the completely destructibility of Hoxxes IV tunnels makes it even more fun to play. The classes are well balanced. It is reasonable priced, and regularly updated.I usually do not care about the games Steam recommends based on the games I play or have played. But, boy am I happy that I actually did try this one out.This game combines a few of my favourite things.  (that is Tolkien's fault) and  because it is much more fun to shoot at something (in a video game) with a friend next to you. But seriously, this game offers lots of hours of fun. That means that there is not always every mission type available in every biome. The biomes are (currently) 8 different areas with different conditions. The levels are completely random generated. I did purchase the supporter upgrade because i want to support the Ghost Ship Games team. They're doing a great job providing contend and listening the community. You do not need it to play the game. _childDocuments_.review: I enjoy playing this game with friends. I also enjoy playing it solo. Many might not see this as a solo game, and that's a fair opinion to hold, given anything you do is way more fun with friends. But this isn't your standard FPS. It's more of an exploration game with FPS elements. Every cave is designed via procedural generation, and there is a surprising amount of complexity and environments you'll come across. You'll find yourself saying to yourself (or teammates) "Oh wow, look at this biome" or "Whoa, haven't seen something like this yet!" This happens a lot more than you'd expect. I don't know a ton about their procedural generation techniques, but it seems to me to be quite advanced. Okay, here we go:PROS: Fun to explore w/ or without friendsLovely art style that fits the dark and comical tone of the game Every character class serves a unique purpose, so it's fun to run a full team of four dwarvesLeveling progression, while a little slower than I'd prefer, still feels rewardingThe hub world has some fun activities to occupy your time in between missions with friends CONS:Sound design is great, however when it comes to enemies it's very poorly doneYou cannot tell when enemies are approaching usually due to this sound design flawJust really, really sucks to not know where an enemy is attacking from due to inaccurate soundOther than that, the sound and music are great. It's just agitating at times when you're in the middle of a swarm of critters and you're trying to conserve ammo or shields and cannot hear where enemies are approaching from. All that being said, I still recommend this game since it values cooperation and exploration. The FPS elements, despite their flaws, are good enough for me alongside the rest of the game. IN SHORT: It's fun, slightly flawed, but engaging. The exploration and atmosphere combined with co-op potential make up for any shortcomings.

_childDocuments_.review: Deep Rock Galactic is a dungeon exploration game for up to 4 players in co-op.In a science fiction universe, you play as dwarves in search of minerals and other resources within asteroids, populated by colonies of alien creatures.There are different types of missions and challenges: from simple exploration/ extraction on foot, by mounting a pump with pipelines, through the escort of a drill mounted on tracks.There are 4 different classes with each time firearms and tools that will help you progress in the "dungeon" (Engineer with platforms, Driller with drill, Scout with grapple and Gunner with ziplines).Dungeons are procedurally generated and offer more varied environments than they appear.I appreciate its verticality, its immersive side as well as the ergonomics of the game. A game all the more lively, as the developers have worked well on the "hub" where the players meet; we particularly appreciate the bar in which you can share a beer with the boys. A game that has humour, personality, a special atmosphere and a lot of secrets to discover (like achievements).It's obviously better with friends and synergising the classes' abilities (Engineer can put a platform in a unreachable place and the Scout can land on it thanks to his grapple).For me, it is a very interesting video game, having basic concept and constant attention from their developers.. Meaning, the DLCs are just for cosmetics and optional if you want to support the devs, unlike certain games which add DLCs for "better" or "pay to win" gameplay.It does not demerit in the face of the marks, awards and positive reviews it receives.

_childDocuments_.review: Deep Rock Galactic is a fantastic class based co-op shooter with so many fun ideas.Like for instance the fully destructible terrain that in tandem with the tools at your disposal allows for tons of creativity in how you can approach traversing the hostile environment of the planet Hoxxes, as well as letting you make the environment less hostile therefore making the combat encounters that take place there easier.And then there all the numerous enemies that have been added over the years all with their own unique strengths and weaknesses, And when these monsters combine they naturally cover each others weaknesses creating the fast paced yet thoughtful combat encounters that make many games good if not great. But what about the things you use to shoot said enemies? Well as of now there are 6 weapons per class most of which must be unlocked and all of them can be tinkered with to suit your death dealing preferences especially once you get some overclocks. Want your grenade launcher to fire mini nukes instead of your boring old grenades? With a sizable reduction in ammo Fatboy has you covered. Sick of your gun having recoil? Trade some dps and you can fill a target full 'o lead from miles away.Death and destruction not your style? That's fine you can simply chose a low risk mission and take your time completing the various objectives each mission could have rather than worrying about completing the mission before you run out of ammo.So far i haven't even mentioned the co-op part of the the game which is some if the best co-op ever. It neatly rides the line between co-op that barely even matters and co-op where if one person is is playing just a bit poorly they take everyone else down with them. Its a co-op style that encourages but does not require good teamplay. And when ever someone helps out another dwarf they often get rewarded with a good o'l rock'n'stone.The community is relatively great likely due to the style of co-op (and also the funny dwarves), and so much has been added and is still being added to the game by Ghost ship since the game launched. All of these aspects and more create one of my favorite games, and if any of this sounds fun or even just interests you definitely give it a shot some time.

_childDocuments_.review: I originally played this for eight hours, before the second birthday. I decided to buy this game for my friend this recent Christmas so we could co-op, and my life hasn't been the same. We've been playing this almost non-stop for weeks. The class & weapon variety, upgrades, overclocks, perks, and other systems add a ton of depth (ha, cave joke) to a game with very simple objectives. All the classes feel great to play, and the overclocks I mentioned can do some absolutely wild things to your weapons, practically making them new options entirely. My personal favorite is the Hyper Propellant for Engineer's grenade launcher: it turns your average breach-launcher into a mach-10 missile silo that obliterates single-target. armor and health at the heavy cost of AOE range damage. I'm genuinely shocked @ not only how robust, varied, and dynamic this simple gameplay loop is, but also @ the fact they made the solo mode actually GOOD. When I'm not in co-op, Bosco is broken as hell, and that's on purpose as no one can join in the middle of a solo mission. He's intelligent enough to mine out and carry large items, light areas, and defend objectives, all by holding Ctrl and clicking the material or object of interest. He has upgrades that can make things like his rockets (which you trigger) have various effects, or just improve his mining, damage, etc. The fact that your AI partner isn't a bag of bricks is enough to make me recommend this game even to people who don't have someone to play with -- though, there ARE public lobbies!Overall, yes, best $30 you could spend right now.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic. I have barely gotten into the huge progression system but from what I have I find it to be very satisfying to progress and is quite rewarding and well paced. Perhaps more importantly though, the core game play loop is incredibly addicting and enjoyable which keeps me constantly itching to play. It's basically a beautiful mix of a steampunk dig and doom, the gun-play/combat is great with all of the four classes fighting with vastly different weapons and tools allowing for great co-op between allies during combat. Additionally the mining/exploration part of the game is also quite enjoyable with certain resources to find that progress the objective, some that you keep to upgrade your character later, and some resources that are used to call in additional ammo. Just like the combat while exploring the different classes all have very different movement abilities (all of which are important) that when used in coordination with friends creates a very fun movement system that depends on allies and understanding how different classes work to travese most easily. However, with limited understanding of the classes, or a lack of allies/classes you can still very much complete all of the objectives and have lots of fun.Overall I would say in order to fully enjoy the game you should play with friends (the more the merrier) but even by yourself or with one friend you can experience the full game and have a blast.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty decent solo play, fantastic party play. The game has active devs who work hard and actually pulled the game out of early access! The most recent update added several musical tracks to the game, breathing more life and variety into the atmosphere for every situation. Several voice lines were added as well and the dwarfs will comment on just about everything.Art style looks good, textures look nice and there are some great colors and lighting effects! Game runs pretty smoothly and the particle effects are both visually distinct and practical. I rarely stand there and wonder what a particle means when I see it, and only really suffer frame loss when my friends and I are actively trying to get as many particle effects on screen as possible at once.Hundreds of unlocks and dozens of promotions (the game's version of prestige, restarting at level 1) promise a long grind for anyone into that mechanic! Between equipment upgrades and customization options, many miners look quite distinct!The space rig is a great place! It's a base of operations for your miners, you can change classes, customize your dwarfs, forge upgrades, tweak equipment, play a barrel kicking minigame, reset the gravity, visit the memorial, selects assignments and missions, and most importantly get absolutely hammered at the bar. Oh, there are special unlockable beers with different effects too, have fun discovering them! Blackreach blonde for life.The meta. There sort of is one, I don't pay enough attention to community discussions about builds to know what it is. I just build my equipment in a way that makes playing the game satisfying and fun and I've pulled triple digit hours before full release. I'd say the game is worth it!

_childDocuments_.review: 'bout time I left an employee review, Deep Rock Galactic got me working a few hours.TL;DR: Best job ever.A game that scratches all the right itches. Even though graphics are far from realistic, I immediately feel immersed when I enter the space rig; I'm a dwarf with a job to do, so hurry up and finish your beer ya leaf lovers. On one hand, I spend a lot of times laughing at the shenanigans these dwarves get in to. Whether it's greenbeards getting hit by a supply pod or the driller blowing himself up with c4 (this happens a lot). Even though you can be mixed with inexperienced dwarves, I rarely find myself frustrated about it, the community is generally top notch and wants to learn. The game really drives you to work together too, it's incredibly satisfactory to combine some of those nifty gadgets to traverse the terrain that looks like the seventh layer of hell. It's easy to find each other and point at things with your laser tool, there's no gain in claiming kills/minerals for yourself. Polite dwarves salute their fellow miners when they are granted access to those precious minerals. I think the mechanics are great.On the other hand, when the moment comes you hear Mission Control broadcast "SWARM!" and the ominous soundtrack starts playing, it becomes a serious hardcore FPS, with waves of bugs starting to hit you from all sides. Once again teamwork is key here, true dwarves stand side by side mashing aliens into green paste. No matter how many waves I've made my way through, this still gets my blood pumping. Oh and have I mentioned massive exploding bulk detonators?The four classes are well balanced with each their own pros and cons, two sets of unique primary/secondary weapons, 3 unique grenades, a unique bug control tool (like sentries or the c4) and a unique traversal tool. The devs have been adding awesome "overclocks" to the game as well, which can really change things up, turning the engineer's grenade launcher into a nuke launcher for example. A lot of tweaks and stuff have been added since I start playing, each one better than the previous, keeping things interesting for a veteran like me. And even though this game is great already, I can still see room for great expansions with current mechanics, keep it up devs.All and all, a true work of art, heavily focused on co-op and crazy beards.So what are you waiting for ya whale piper? We've got a job to do.Edit: Nominated for "better with friends" because I have not yet completed a single solo mission in all these hours

_childDocuments_.review: This is an outstanding game in many different ways. First of all the game itself and all the elements are amazing, it looks good. Controls are clean and all of the mechanical stuff is great. The atmosphere within the team, your band of miners, is amazing because of little details that just feel right. The way the dwarfs comment on things, greet each other, are grumpy and greedy as hell. Just to quote my gunner after he killed a Loot-Bug: "I'm sorry little bug, but its your own fault for being so full of goddies." In addition you have a very dedicated dev team, you feel that they really love their game and its theme. These guys and girls could have given up a long time ago and call it quits and people would have considered this to be a complete game, but no they go on and on and improve and enhance what they have. They are very responsive to the community and open about everything. It takes longer then anticipated? They tell us and explain the reasons. You feel respected by them. This, this right here, is the way to build a loyal following of customers and treat them right, EA, Activision and Bethesda please take notes.This is a guaranteed recomendation of mine especially when its on sale, like right now as i write this. Its perfect for 4 players but is still a lot of fun for 1-3 . The community on average is very friendly and surprisingly untoxic. It is great for beginners and can be cranked up to be a nightmare of difficulty for pros.Enough said, need to go back to the tunnels, that Morkite doesn't mine itself.ROCK AND STONE BROTHERS!!

The teamplay opportunities are like no other coop game i've seen, the map generation keeps it fresh, the enemies are so well designed and make the fights very interesting.One of the most expansive and well balanced weapon & gear customization in a coop game. You can literally put hundreds of hours into fine tuning your playstyle, you can feel like a weapon designer, tweaking for your wants & needs.The atmosphere and the artstyle is very strong here. The biomes are beautiful, varied, colorful. The dwarves are a mix of funny, badass and industrious, who do bug genocide and claim riches. It feels like a very manly game, the characters are loud, rough, simple minded and brutally effective. Actually its one of the reasons i decided to try this game - i watched the video demonstrating all guns in this game, and weapon sounds are extremely important in a first person shooter. I think they nailed it for most of the weapons. Also really good sounds for the nature and machinery.Great mod support, and they're one of the most ethical gamedevs on this planet right now. All DLCs are cosmetic (with base game already having insane customization variety). No FOMO, all battlepasses are free & available to switch at your preference.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, DRG runs pretty well. I have encountered no crashes during my current ~56 hours of playtime, nor any gamebreaking bugs or glitches. I have encountered very occasional and brief stutters during hectic gunfights, but those are extremely minuscule and rare enough to hardly be worth mentioning. There is some weirdness to the games’ physics, which seems to be intended by the developer but can lead to some strange interactions with the game environment. For example, any movement seems to carry momentum, meaning that the player may stand still on a rising platform, but jumping off will carry the momentum of the platform regardless of which direction they may be jumping.Being a game that features fully destructible terrain, DRG is not a particularly "good" looking game, but it carries its art style confidently. There is great variety in how to customize any of your four playable dwarves, and where the game lacks in visual fidelity, it makes up for it with charm. For example, the Space Rig, a smallish hub area the player returns to between missions, feels like more than "just" a bit of empty space with a bunch of upgrade terminals. Instead, there are pseudo-minigames, little knickknacks that are scattered around waiting to be found and played with, and copious amounts of things to coax out interactions between players in a multiplayer lobby.Dwarves may not be identifiable at a single glance, but enemies are. Despite there only largely being two categories of foes you may encounter: bugs and robots, sub-types are quite easily recognizable, which enhances the gameplay experience of the faster swarm fights. The same holds true for biomes; while there may not be an immense variety, the simpler but still distinct look and geometry subtly teach the player how to navigate each of the different areas.The music at large is good and features a solid selection of tracks. Guns feel weighty, and the voice acting, even when comedic, never feels grating or otherwise out-of-place, which is something that a lot of more humorous games tend to struggle with. There is some noticeable repetition of voice-lines, and the mission "narrator" can be overly chatty during certain moments, such as constantly and obnoxiously screaming at players during the M.U.L.E. salvage objective if they leave the contested zone.Fundamentally, Deep Rock Galactic is a L4D-esque co-op FPS. The L4D comparison here is incredibly light and is more so to reference the very core principle of the game being co-op-centric and each map featuring occasional enemy swarm mechanics. DRG also sets itself apart by having a class system: gunner, engineer, driller, and scout. Each of which comes with a main- and subweapon; a traversal tool, for example, a zipline; and a grenade weapon. Important to note here is that this means that while every dwarf has a distinct niche that they excel in, they all have tools to engage with the environment and the map objectives.In total, there are eight different map objectives that cycle on a global thirty-minute timer across the eleven different biomes. Additionally, they spawn with three modifiers: cave complexity, cave length, and affixes. This means that a player's favorite objective may not always be available on the map of their choosing and may be further altered by the aforementioned modifiers. Thus, it’s also hard to gauge how long a game of DRG may actually take, as I’ve seen any of those objectives last between ten and fifty minutes, making it hard to view DRG as a game to just hop into on the fly.The only other game mode is Deep Dives, which is merely a kind of hard mode that ties three regular missions together with shared resources across all of them. These also cycle on a regular basis and provide the last tier of progression for the player characters in the form of 'Overclocks'. These are items that can be crafted after randomly obtaining their recipe through those aforementioned Deep Dives, and they strongly tweak the gameplay of any of the weapons they are attached to. Like with the seasonal affixes, these provide a decent incentive to keep playing the game, but fundamentally do not offer a different experience from the basic missions. Deep Rock Galactic does not feature any sort of campaign or story missions. It does, however, hint at its sci-fi setting and has some surface-level worldbuilding. In general, players are part of the titular mining company, Deep Rock Galactic, with the dwarves themselves being somewhat of an elite force that is only sent to the most dangerous digsites, one of which is Hoxxes IV, where the game takes place. The rest is delivered through voicelines during the missions themselves; these, however, never get more detailed than hinting at the ideals of the company or the deadliness of Hoxxes, but more so through the subtext of the assignments given to the player. Assignments are little more than milestones that are unlocked by playing a selection of missions in order to unlock an upgrade, be it a new weapon, cosmetic items, etc. Deep Rock Galactic is a fantastic experience in a quite narrow genre. If you’re willing to adhere to the game’s progression systems, are looking for an almost strictly multiplayer experience, and are willing to overlook the lack of immersive elements in favor of charm and humouristic presentation, then DRG is a pretty safe recommendation, whereas players who are looking for a more flexible gameplay loop, are completionists, or may not have enjoyed games from this genre earlier will probably not find anything groundbreaking here.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't recommend this game enough.  This is an actual coop game where the strengths of all can lead to some truly sublime gameplay.  When every player is using the strengths of their character you actually feel like a team, not a gang of random yahoos competing for individual glory.In essence this is a mining game crossed with Left for Dead.  You and (up to) 3 others get dropped into a dark cave to complete various types of mission, mine resources, defeat a boss, collect eggs, repair stuff.  Each player has a unique role, the gunner has a big gun and a zipline, the engineer can place platforms to help with resource collection and has 2 turrets to help with crowd control, the driller is able to drill through the environment and the scout has a reusable zipline and can light up the environment.  Along the way you collect minerals and gold to fund upgrades to weapons and buy cosmetics.  There are always resources to find and collect.  It's an important point to note that just collecting the minerals feels satisfying and rewarding, they nailed this aspect of the game.But the game really comes alive when it shifts to its other "phase", that is when a swarm of enemies attack, and then you have to defend against a seemingly endless stream of enemies.  In this regard its very like L4D, but there are more enemy types, each with their own weaknesses and you need to learn how to deal with all of them.  The environments are procedurally generated, no two caves are the same but they follow general patterns, the same applies to swarms.  There are special enemy types, the first time you encounter a bulk detonator your first instinct is to run and it's well founded but after a while you learn how to deal with them yourself.A significant difference with L4D however is that you get to pick your own difficulty, every mission has a "hazard level", ranging from 1-5.  If you aren't wanting to change your underpants then maybe go for a level 2-3 mission, or if you wore your official DRG stone panties that morning maybe go for a level 5.  The hazard level changes the amount and difficulty of enemies (your own personal character level also has an impact on this, as does the number of players in a team), so you get to choose what you feel comfortable with but with higher levels comes higher rewards.There is character progression in the game, you can level up each character, their weapons and kit.  Each weapon is well designed and fits with the theme of the character, for example the scout is not designed to take on swarms so his weapons are weak, as a scout your movement is your biggest advantage.  The gunner is designed to take on swarms so his weapons are powerful but his mobility is limited.  There is also a bewildering array of cosmetics that you can buy (with resources you get while playing, no microtransactions here!) so you can customize your character however your like.With update 25 coming up, the replayability of the game will go up although I enjoy the game playing just for its core mechanics of collection and combat.

_childDocuments_.review: I can not give DRG a negative review because of all the fun I had with it during all stages of it and also because overall it still is an amazingly fun game, but I have to say that recent changes and developements make me bother about the future of it. Lets go into detail: + DLC's are purely cosmetic, for 30€ or less you get the full game experience with all weapons, skills and overclocks (farmable weapon tweaks), big thumbs up.+ The space rig (basically where you do all settings and run around before a mission) is lovely made, the bar with different beers is hilarous, kicking barrels around annoys your boss, there is a jukebox to dance to, just all around a lot of detail to make waiting for a full team never boring. + a lot of character, weapon and cosmetic customizations, after 650h I didnt even unlock all cosmetics yet+ usually a very nice and friendly community.+ good optimization, even with mods that massively increase bug spawn rates my frame rate of my ♥♥♥♥♥♥ 1050ti still maintains a good fps+ there is a lot more to tell, basically anything more thats not listed below is positive. - I feel like there is relatively little objective pool for the current state of the game. I know, after 650h everything might get stale, but I am not sure how much work it would be to at least add some more secondary objectives, its usually just picking up blooms or fossils and that for every single map. - I dont like where the Season 1 update is heading to. Dont get me wrong, the update brought 4 new somewhat cool weapons and overclocks, it brought a new additional XP system to unlock more skins and resources, but it also brought this weird "tech rivalry" theme, which just seems wrong. Before it I felt like the games theme was based on russian made barely working vehicles and utitlity thats rusty and falling apart every time you touch it. Now out of sudden the company is facing another high tech company that is trying to mine on the planet and comes with Borderlands-like vault key looking things (ok I admit I am pretty sure thats some sort of easter egg, its too obvious). Also my illiterate alcoholic dwarves are suddenly able to hack high tech drones that were shot down. And the change of theme makes it just weird, a standard shotgun is fighting energy barriers and plasma shooting tentacles now.- It seems they are trying to increase the difficulty of hazard 5 (hardest difficulty), which I was eagerly awaiting, because it was getting a little too easy at times. But it feels like their solution is to increase spawn rates of hardcore enemies. On some maps I just felt like they simply dumped a boatload of the big bugger bulletsponges into the battlefield and called it a day, and I think I speak for the majority of the playerbase when I say that the main fun of the game is spraying lead and explosives into the battlefield and clearing out the hordes in good old fashion and not being thrown around, grabbed or sniped by buggers on the ceiling.I would not even be mad if I lose by being overrun, I just get disappointed when I feel like I had no chance because it went from being thrown around the map by shockwave to being grabbed and then dropped into a hole. And I think exactly that is increasingly happening on haz5 since a few updates.Those 3 negative points are far from ruining the game for me obviously, I also feel like its a very subjective opinion. The games positive rating pretty much reflects what I think of the game as a whole. Rock and Stone brothers

_childDocuments_.review: Early on, this game will seem unfocused, weird and gimmicky. They drop you into missions and you finish it then wonder "is that it?"If you embrace the premise, and view it through the lens of a co-operative game, you will quickly learn why the missions can become so fun. Each dwarf has advantages and weaknesses, and each dwarf can cover eachothers weaknesses. Missions require very active participation from everyone in the cave. The scout needs the engineer to make platforms, the gunner needs the driller to create pathways, etc. The more thorough a team is about collecting resources, the more everyone benefits in terms of currency, materials, xp and so on. These resources serve as the players progression, weapon unlocks, cosmetics, everything that matters is 100% accessible through gameplay- no real money needed. You can unlock everything yourself, in a timely manner, and you can always have something to do, and the game doesnt gouge or entice you into doing it like a second job. there is no FOMO, no predatory daylies or battle passes, there is just gameplay and then rewards for gameplay. But most importantly? it's a FUN game. the dwarves can interact verbally, they can reach insane topspeeds and they can do insane damage to the enemies, environments or their own teammates. It is a game that approves of any playstyle, the objectives are diverse and challenging but not frustrating (mostly- save for korloks and corruptors). Just play it

_childDocuments_.review: I've loved exploration games ever since I played Seven Cities of Gold on the Atari 800XL back in the 80's. These days there are lots of games with "procedural" world generation, but I have a new favorite.Deep Rock Galactic is about a dwarven mining company with a space station orbiting Hoxxes IV; An alien planet complete with multiple underground biomes, several species of alien insectoid monsters, and an unlimited number of procedurally generated dark-cavernous-connecting-cave systems which you get to explore. It's a treasure hunt and a bug hunt which you can either play alone or with a party of four. There are four leveling classes of dwarves with different equipment and purpose and lots of grindy perks - all of which combine  to give you reasons to keep playing (as if gold weren't enough). Almost every outing ends in an exciting run-for-your-life ending sequence that you won't always survive but you'll usually enjoy. If you're a fan of exploration games and shoot 'em ups and co ops this games is for you.
