_childDocuments_.review: Due to the nature of the game receiving so many free content updates, the balance is a tad out of wack in terms of making builds for your dwarves. Some builds are hilarious garbage that can only withstand mid-tier difficulties or specific, uncommon situations, while other builds can absolutely dominate any difficulty, period. One such build that I have discovered to be the game's absolute meta with no other build of no other class being able to adequately match is Gunner's Plasma Burster Missiles 11112 and Coilgun 22222. Should the devs ever actually tally up the pros of this build, they'll almost certainly recognize it as stupid-OP and nerf something about it, but frankly many other builds need huge buffs instead. The gameplay loop is quite strong, though it does get same-y after long enough, which trying out different builds or dipping your toes into crazy chaotic modded servers can usually remedy pretty well. Anyone who plays for more than a few hundred hours will recognize they are doing the same thing over and over, meaning the fun comes from doing it in different ways, hence the value of trying new builds or game mods. The monetization is the most generous and pro-consumer I have seen in a long time. The only paid content is strictly cosmetic, and releases as a single, self-contained package. All gameplay content and the overwhelming majority of cosmetic content is free with the base game, you need only unlock it by playing, and there is no "pay to unlock stuff sooner" functions of any kind. One of the best co-op horde-shooters out there. Devs are talented, humble, dedicated, and I haven't sniffed a hint of the woke mind virus from anything in the game or from Ghost Ship Games directly, which is more than can be said for Helldivers 2.

You get enough credits, materials and xp to get new gear and upgrades just from playing mission to mission.------------------Game Time☐ Short☐ Average☐ Long☐ Depends on you☑ EndlessAt the time of writing I'm well into the end game of collecting all the overclocks, but I still have a ways to go to collect everything there is to collect. You can play this as a casual game to drop into or make it your main game to play for months and you'll still have a fun time! Each mission takes about 15-20mins to complete, though there is a 'Deep Dive' option you unlock about 10-15hrs into the game which consists of 3 challenging missions and can take anywhere from 40mins-2hrs to complete.------------------Price☐ Just buy it☑ Worth the price☑ Wait for sale☐ Maybe if you have some spare money left☐ Not recommendedThis game is incredible value on sale. You'll get tonnes of playtime out of it, and it'll keep you entertained. If you think this'll be a main game for you, I'd say it's worth full price also. I picked this game up a while ago for 50% off, but felt the game was worth more because I love and play it so much, so they offer a 'supporter' DLC which doesn't really include much but throws some extra cash to the cool devs. This game is still actively being updated monthly with new content, and official modding support is in beta, ready to release soon.------------------Performance☐ Can run on a Ouya☐ Integrated Graphics Laptop☐ 60fps Minecraft Machine☑ 144fps Overwatch Machine☐ 2x 3090's requiredThis game is pretty easy to run if you're just looking for 60fps at high/ultra settings, so if you can run something like Overwatch comfortably, you can likely run this well enough. Things get a bit more challenging trying to push for 144fps. My 1080 can run this at 1080p, Medium/High settings at 144fps. My full PC specs are on my profile if you want more info to compare with.------------------

_childDocuments_.review: In light of seeing Ghost Ship getting robbed of the 2023 Labor of Love award for Deep Rock Galactic, losing it to Red Dead Redemption 2, a game that Rockstar stopped updating over a year ago due to not reaching profit targets, i find myself compelled to write a review. Deep Rock Galactic is a PvE shooter that pits you and up to 3 other dwarven brothers up against an endless horde of entomological horrors, whether they crawl, burrow or fly, in 8 different mission variants. 4 classes, each with their own strengths and weaknesses in what they can do both combat and movement wise, be it the lightbringing grapple hook shooting scout, the zipline flinging lead slinging gunner, the platform launching sentry dropping engineer, or the driller who also has bricks of plastic explosive to go with his big drill hands.Progression is dependent on 3 things: your credits, your precious minerals management lets you keep, and your diligence in completing your assignments. Doing mission will give you credits and precious minerals, assignments will allow you to unlock new weapons, their respective upgrades and customization options for your dwarf by completeing a string of missions. Run enough missions and eventually you'll be up for a promotion, in which you cough up some minerals and minerals and you are sent back to level one with not only a shiny star, but a key to the late game content that you can't interact with until you have it and access to the weekly Deep Dives; three missions wearing a trenchcoat that reward you with upgrade cores that you can use credits and minerals to craft and even further upgrade (usually) your weapons to do even more neat stuff.Your Possible Doubts:"Buuuuut Womp I don't have 1-3 friends to play this with and i hate queuing with randoms!!!"In most games like this I would sympathize with your plight, but not here. You are never alone on the Space Rig, you have BOSCO. Thats right, instead of playing with random dwarves or even the other three classes propped up by braindead AI and half function navmeshes you get a little flying robot buddy who will accompany you on your solo endeavors. Not only can he mine or that you can't reach and provide you with some targeted light, but he can also revive you, shoot missiles at targets of your choosing, and carry heavy objective objects or mineral deposits. Your loyal companion will even dig them out of the wall if you tell him to."Buuuuut Womp I bet this game has a battlepass and exploits FOMO and has an in-game currency to leech money out of my wallet like every other game that has come out in the past decade!!!"No in-game currency, no FOMO that i can be bothered with, and a free battlepass that goes with the seasonal event. If you want to support the devs beyond your initial purchase there are bundles of cosmetics that you can pay for."Buuuuuuut Womp that progression system sounds like it will bore me and I'll stop playing it!!!"Yeah maybe, but Hoxxes ain't going anywhere, it hasn't over the years i have been playing and i don't foresee it going anywhere either. I have put the game down a few times before and won't lie and say that I won't in the future. That's the beauty of it, DRG is always there. The Space Rig is always waiting for you to come off your sabbatical and get back to work. As long as you enjoy the game, there is no shame in putting it down and coming back at a later date. In all seriousness, buy the game on sale or not. It is one of the most fun PvE horde shooters to play even solo where most games of this style falter massively like Payday or the Fatshark Warhammer games. Hopefully the spite fueled tirade about a game that should have won Labor of Love 2023 will convince you, the reader wanting a reason to buy the game, to do just that. Buy the game, rock and stone to the bone.

_childDocuments_.review: Sometimes I wonder if mining is all there is to life, then I punch myself in the nose. YOU!Shut up. Take this gun. Keep your head down. Stay on my ass. Don't touch anything but your trigger. Grow a beard. Drink. Tip the bartender. Bring friends. Be excellent to each other.It's Left 4 Dead crossed with Starship Troopers, with Dwarves in space. An OSHA nightmare simulator.My wife says it’s like the movie Aliens meets Snow White plus beer.My wife’s boyfriend says it’s like spelunking in Minecraft, but with guns, more aggressive mobs, everything is polygonal and looks like a PS2 game, and you’re dwarves playing pretend Pest Control. For me it’s just like Left 4 Dead but instead you get to take revenge on the entire spider population of Australia.Just a heads up: The second you download Deep Rock Galactic you become a big manly 37 year old dwarf with a big bushy beard.It’s the saga of 4 space Dwarves that constantly scream "Rock and Stone!", and how they drain a planet of its resources. It's a FPS, but you are a badass Dwarf from space and you fight big ass-spiders and you drink beer and mine for ore that you can trade for money and so you can get cooler guns. Did I mention there is beer? Yup, there’s also an ingame bar you can get sh*t faced in.So… you got an irrational fear and hate of bugs? Well down here at Deep Rock Galactic we give you a chance to exterminate those fu*kers!You're a space dwarf employed by a mining Corporation that sends you on suicidal missions to bug infested planets, missions include: retrieving rare minerals, mining precious metals, exterminating space bugs, building infrastructure, search and rescue of mining equipment, etc. You are put into the caves by management with a job to do, so you always have an objective, the progression is great. Boxes will randomly spawn sometimes with some stuff from old events so you will never lose out on some fashion You go alone or with friends into the surface, and complete various missions as enemies try to kill you. The mix of fighting and mission offers a nice balance.The point of the game is to have fun, kill bugs, die horribly on occasion, and mine minerals.  Not necessarily in that order.  There is no narrative to it, it's a free-form sandbox where each map is randomly generated at the start.  It's a lot like Left 4 Dead crossed with Minecraft - the fun comes from playing, fighting, creating, and those close shave escapes where your team barely survives when things go horribly horribly wrong.  Or, on occasion, those desperate last stands where everyone dies and no one escapes.It's a PVE class shooter where each class plays differently (and is very important to the team). You have 4 main classes, each with various weapons, tools, and traversal options. You can upgrade, collect resources, and improve characters. Every class has 3 primary weapons, 3 secondary weapons, 1 support tool, and 1 traversal tool. You only start with 1 of each and have to unlock the 2nd and 3rd primary and secondary weapons by levelling up and doing missions. Also, the soundtrack, although being the genre synthwave and not my style, is incredible. The neutral music can range from mysterious to very ambient to beautiful (listen to Fathomless Tomb), and the chase music is perfect adrenaline fuel. In addition, every class comes equipped with a pickaxe and some throwable, rechargable flares. Every dwarf can shape the environment how they want, but the driller is exceptional at it.You can play Solo, or with up to 4 Players. It doesn’t matter which class you choose, you can have a team of any combination of the different classes, though having all four classes will get you the most whole experience in the mission, as everyone has an important part in the group. You can invite your friends or join a random lobby or host your own public lobby. You can also invite a friend and then have randoms join during the mission, via drop pod.If you like co-op horde-mode style games such as Left 4 Dead, Vermintide, Killing Floor, etc, then you'll like DRG.  If you don't, well, you won't. Overclocks and new weapons provide different and often quirky or terrifying new options for mining and killing, changing up how each mission plays and allowing for great clutches, tragic mistakes, or the ever-present omnicidal Driller's brutal slaughter of the team.Deep Rock is the epitome of the phrase, "It's not about the destination, it's about the journey." You don't play the game for the material rewards. Unlocking cosmetics and overclocks is fun, but it isn't the point of the game. The point is surviving a detonator encounter or wiping a swarm with a well-placed explosion. It's bringing Doretta's head back and seeing it waiting for you in the space rig. It's getting drunk in the abyss bar during an impromptu game of space kickball. A lot of other games have something you're trying to achieve by playing. In Deep Rock, playing IS the achievement.DRG is honestly my biggest positive surprise in the past several years of gaming. This studio puts many AAA devs to shame and playing made me realize just how distorted and dystopian modern online gaming has become. DRG has no predatory monetization, no exploiting FOMO, no toxic enforcement of competitiveness. The game is designed in a way so that you help your team by most of what you do even if you don't aim to do so, and the benefits of cooperation are massive. This results in the absolute most positive experience with randoms I have had in any online game ever to the point where I had to sit down and think what's wrong with me to be nervous about playing with randoms, because so many online games have conditioned us to loathe the experience. DRG is full of players genuinely just wanting to have a good time goofing off and working together to complete a mission and maybe buy each other beer afterwards (in game and IRL). It is a game anyone would seriously lose a lot on to miss.Amazing game from an incredible developer. The best example I can think of for “hey maybe we can make games without ridiculous amounts of monetization and treat our customers well”. DRG is definitely worth the price.  It is arguably the most beloved co-op game ever, and for good reason. It’s an absolute blast to play with friends.  I wish I had friends that play it, but even with randoms it is a lot of fun. It even surprised me with how good it also plays solo. There is a reason why every gaming suggestion forum is filled with people shouting ROCK AND STONE!! In summary, the game is endless and the content never repeats as long as you enjoy the gameplay cycle. I highly recommend it; it's fun with strangers, friends, or alone. Seriously bro, if you don’t rock and stone you’re not going home. It’s that simple.Finally,For those new brothers about to Rock and Stone, we salute you!10/10

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely exceptional co-op horde shooter!The basic gameplay loop is very simple (Explore cave -> Get loot/kill bugs -> Exit cave) but extremely enjoyable and the wide variety of mission types and procedurally generated maps will keep the game fresh for hours! As you explore the caves each biome has optional resources you can mine to use to buy upgrades for your loadouts or cosmetics for your dwarf.Each of the four roles of dwarf you can play all feel very different from the weapons they use, how they navigate around the cave systems, and how they can support their team mates. No one class feels like "the best" out of all of them; they each excel at their own niche and have their own disadvantages you will need need the help of your team mates to overcome.The shooting in the game feels exceptionally good, every weapon feels very satisfying to use and every single enemy has weak points in their armour to reward good aim, but also almost all of the enemies have deformable armour; you can break though the bugs carapace to make new weak spots to target.  Some weapons can be better than others are breaking off than others and it's very satisfying to shoot at the basic grunt enemies and watch their armoured shells break away before they're killed, or blasting away the shell of a Praetorian making it so much easier for everyone to fire into it's weak spot.Traversing the caves is also very fun and rewarding; while each dwarf has a specific traversal tool like a grappling hook, drills, or deployable platforms and ziplines each biome itself has a wide variety of plants or terrain features that you can use to get around by using the simple parkour in the game. There is no wall running or triangle jumps, but the dwarves will try to climb up the edges of flat surfaces if you collide with the edge of it by doing a little mid air hop; using this you can often find natural staircases, or make them with platforms, to ascend up sheer cliffs or up to the roof of a cave. Or you can just dig a tunnel, that's always an option when you've got a pickaxe.On top of being an absolutely exceptional horde shooter, the devs of this game continue to add amazing new content ton the game; two new mission types were added in early 2020 (maybe have been with the official release of the game, I'm not sure) that are new and interesting gameplay challenges, but they've also just released two whole new biomes that are absolutely beautiful and big bunch of new enemies, including some new boss bugs that completely refresh an older mission type, and they did it COMPLETELY FOR FREE! They could have easily called it a DLC and slapped a price tag on it, but they didn't because they knew splitting the playerbase is that way is a bad thing. This game is run by a competent dev team!Hey, that's a cool shotgun you've got there Scout. How'd you like to use it to send yourself flying across the caves?Oh hey there Engi nice grenade launcher, but let's spice it up a bit; here's some  have fun!Gunner, I noticed that when you fire 5,000 rounds a minute you sometimes don't have time to aim. How about we make it so your bullets ricochet off of walls and into bugs? The downside is that you're less accurate, but really that's an advantage because you get more ricochets that way.Hey Pyro- I mean Driller, have you ever wanted things to be... more on fire? We can make it happen!I didn't mention it in my earlier review because I hadn't fully understood just how much Overclocks change the game. First off, what are Overclocks? Well, they're basically super mods for your guns, each gun has it's own unique set of Overclocks that provide certain advantages and disadvantages that can  how you use a gun.They're introduced to the game once you've reached max level (25) with one of your dwarves and "promote" them (start again at level 1, keeping all other progress/mods/guns/etc, and getting a star above your name in game, after you do it once it's entirely optional to do it more) you gain access to how you earn overclocks; a weekly core hunt assignment and a weekly Deep Dive mission.Both of these give you 3 rewards; 1 random weapon overclock, 1 random unlockable cosmetic (that you can only get from the cores) and 1 blank core.Blank cores are used in random events you will find inside missions, each event has it's own objective and a timer for you to complete it, if you're successful you place a blank core inside a lil' computer and are given 3 random choices; only know which dwarf it's for and if it's a weapon overclock or cosmetic unlock.The game has added a lot of stuff since I posted my original review! Not only have the devs released two new "season passes"  but I missed most of the first season and am  that were added (once again, totally free of charge) to the game so there's not even any FOMO involved!They've added another two new missions types as well as a totally new group of enemies; the Rival Faction, Robots of  origin! Spooky, I know. The two new missions revolve around these factions and involve a little uhhh.... In addition to new missions and enemies, the season passes both came with a round of new weapons; each class now has a new primary weapon and a new secondary weapon! These 8 new weapons also each have their own Overclocks that modify them like the other weapons do.

_childDocuments_.review: I've got somewhere around 200 hours in the game since it was first released in Early Access. Since that time the developers have continuously poured a lot of love and support into it. If you are worried about Early Access don't be - the devs have been very consistent with regular meaty updates, and the full release is right around the corner. I can understand if you want to wait for a full release, but the game is incredibly rock solid now.The game has a server browser and host settings which is notable since those features somehow became optional in a multiplayer PC game some time ago.Up to four players can play together using four unique classes each with multiple weapons and equipment to upgrade via resources gained in-game.DRG had a context-based ping long before games like Fortnite did. The ping system allows anyone to point out important things without something like voice chat (although that is in too), which makes it a lot more accessible to new players and for teamwork. The dwarves will spout voice lines that match what you point at - which is often very amusing.Levels are procedurally generated, and they pull from several "biomes" like your familiar lava, ice, etc. Each biome has its own hazards and unique flora and fauna to deal with, and a huge part of the game is figuring out how to navigate tricky cliffs and canyons using each dwarf's unique equipment while dealing with the Glyphid hordes. I've played the game for a significant amount of time, and can only recognize a couple preset rooms when I see them. The level system is well done, and also scales with the difficulty you choose. This extends to the enemies, as randomly you may have to deal with incredibly dangerous foes such as detonators that require teamwork and your unique movement skills.Since the addition of BOSCO the drone, single player is entirely doable. You can upgrade BOSCO like any other equipment with such things as additional revives, cosmetic skins, mining speed, etc.The addition of Deep Dives and Overclocks give veteran employees of DRG something to collect and master, with the modifications to equipment often significant enough to completely change your playstyle. Cosmetic unlocks like new beard styles and armor add something to shoot for that isn't explicitly tied to shooting itself!  If that makes sense.  Most of all, the game oozes character and community, and the devs are quick with the transparency of updates and fixes. The dwarves are funny and have their own personalities, the game has a dedicated cheer button, and things like a jukebox, craftable beers with fun effects, and social areas have little to do with gameplay but make it that much more fun to play with friends and strangers.I hope to see some new employees! ROCK AND STONE!

_childDocuments_.review: Should you buy it, yes! Deep Rock Galactic (DRG) is a 4 person co-op objective gathering game that takes place deep within Hoxxes IV. Each dwarf has specializations in gun play (usually) and mobility that set them apart from one another.Gunner: Uses high capacity bullet pukers. Sets zip lines to allow passage of ravines or kind of steep tubes.Engineer: Has a shotgun and can place turrets for extra support. Can place platforms, deep pits are now a certified joke!Scout: Has special high powered torches that illuminate rooms. Has a rechargeable grapple hook, great for scouting (duh) and leaving everyone to die. Sometimes.Driller: Uses piercing AoE weapons like the flamethrower. Engi might have bridges and sheer vertical movement covered, you can link caverns, or dig straight to the drop pod because running across chewed up terrain is for leaf lovers.Missions involve you gathering a mineral or some other material in procedurally generated maps, new map layout every time. While you do these missions you'll run into unrelated minerals that are used to buy upgrades and cosmetics in the store. You'll also find plants that let you craft brews for you and your crew to enjoy. All turned in resources increases what is given to each player, so be sure to cash in as much as you can.My experience with other players has always been a positive one. Be it a drop in or a cash n' dash, the game is always best when everyone is doing their part and makes sure every dwarf comes home (within reason). It is an especially euphoric feeling when the party just scrapes out of a mission alive due to some quick thinking and acrobatics at the last possible moments; it is those times where everyone lingers to drink thoughtlessly at the bar as sworn brothers. Even on failed missions, people are more likely than not to stick around and give it another shot.As far as the DLC goes, none of it is mandatory nor does it lock you out of anything super duper awesome (in my general opinion). With everything else that they add to the game, for free, I see them more like little bonuses to continue development. I say that because there are hundreds of cosmetics already available in game, either bough with gold and minerals, or unlock via locating occasional backpacks. I would also like to bring up that they didn't monetize pickax cosmetics, they're gained via the aforementioned backpacks or quests. They COULD'VE monetized them right out of the gate, it would've been easier than breathing, but they didn't. They've added new biomes, missions, creatures, even more base game hats, everything they could've stuck behind a paywall but they didn't.DRG has been a great source of fun for me and my friends. Every mission a gamble and every bug another thoughtless trophy on my wall. Rock and stone brothers!

_childDocuments_.review: My favorite game !So, after almost a 2000 hours of gameplay, I am ready to state what is this game about, and what is special about it.in shortsolo or up to 4 players CO-OP, choose between 4 unique classes of dwarfs, go on a missions underground in a randomly generated caves in a 10 different biomes, more than 50+ different type of enemies (aliens, plants, robots, flying and ground insects, and even bosses) all with their own mechanics, abilities, and weakspots, mine minerals, kill enemies, finish your main objective, and extract to complete the mission.what makes Deep Rock Galactic special:1- No mission is the same ! :  every cave is generated with a lot of different combination, so every mission will be special in terms of atmosphere and exploration, and even spawned enemies and items. you could find gold and many more materials, or some rare items, lost treasures, optional trials that grants rewards, and much more.2- you are free to choose between a scale of difficulty from 1 to 5 before starting any mission, so if you are trying to chill and go on a relaxing mission, you can select hazard 1 or 2, while if you are here for a challenge, select hazard 4 or 5.3-solo player? no worries you have the option to bring with you an AI drone that can be commanded to help you through out the mission.4-not a solo player and no friends? no worries again, host your mission as a public, or join other players that has the same mission you are on. 90% of the time you will find a group5-no micro transactions, no locked missions behind real life money! : everything is obtainable for free, the only paid things are the DLC's which are simply just cosmetics, and does not gain any sort of advantages, besides there are tons of free cosmetics in game already, armors, weapon skins, pickaxe appearance and much more.6- another special thing about this game which shows you how amazing the developers of this game are is that we are now in season 5 and guess what?, every battle pass is free !!, for example if you liked something in season 2 battle pass, a weapon skin, framework, pickaxe part, armor or whatever item you could just activate the season and grind for that item, so you have every battle pass from season 1 to 5 in your POCKET !a little extra details: -unlock many perks that enhance your class, in total if all slots unlocked, you can equip 3 passive perks and 2 active ones. -every class has a total of 6 unique weapons, a total of 24 weapons !-every weapon has a different upgrades which you can combine with overclock to change how the weapon works and damage entirely, but it is not just the weapons, even class equipment can be enhanced.-there is a total of 16 unique throwables.-some missions has modifiers that affects the mission in a positive or a negative way, "anomalies" are on your side, such as extra gold, low gravity, double XP, and much more. while "warnings" on the other side increase the difficulty of the mission, such as an infestation of a creature, a plague, higher spawn rate of projectile or explosion based enemies , low oxygen that limits your movement distance and much more.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a masterpiece, if you're looking for co-op first person shooters.Even if you aren't much of a shooter fan, you might find this to be fun.The gameplay consists of diving into procedurally generated caves either by yourself (optionally accompanied by an armed worker drone), or up to three other players. Once in, you (and anyone else) work to complete whatever objectives Management has assigned you for that mission. As you try to meet your quota, you'll find yourself beset upon by a variety of creatures, most of which could be classified as "an amalgamation of arachnids and ants that could do with a few less moving parts."The bugs aren't your targets, they're your obstacles. To that end, you'll want to scrape whatever resources you can out of each cave as you complete assignments. All resources contribute to experience gain, and some can be kept as currency to upgrade your equipment with. Gold is simply converted to credits, whilst Nitra is used to call down ammo refills, and is also mysteriously confiscated at the end of each mission. As you collect money, experience, and strange looking minerals (see also: not gold/nitra), you can purchase upgrades for your loadout, as well as eventually unlock an additional weapon for each class's primary and secondary slots. Naturally, these are all necessities for reducing the denizens of the planet to a fine paste.I forgot to mention. Classes.Do you enjoy games like Team Fortress 2? If so, you might like this aspect.There are four classes in DRG: , , , and . Each class brings its own form of utility and thrives in varying scenarios when compared to others.Scouts have an unlimited use grapple gun, weapons that excel at removing single targets, and crowd control grenades. Additionally, while all classes may throw flares, Scouts carry their own Flare , which has limited ammo, but fires longer lasting, brighter flares.Gunners bring ziplines and shield dome generators, as well as an assortment of heavy weaponry for optimal pasting of opposition. Their grenades fit well with the theme of the Gunner, i.e., senseless violence.Engineers may deploy up to two turrets (or just one strong turret), as well as platforms to help traverse the absolute hellscape that is Hoxxes IV. Their weapons are also fairly versatile, starting with a shotgun that performs well enough at short-medium range, to a grenade launcher. Their unlaunched grenades, much like the rest of their kit, are versatile. Lures, explosive traps, and a grenade so powerful, you might just kill your own team.Drillers have drills. This might sound unremarkable, but when you consider that working down a wall with a pickaxe might take a while, and drills effortlessly tear holes through the world (but not minerals for some reason), you might change your mind. Drillers are also excellent at removing swarms, as well as the evidence. With thrower-type weapons, whether it be to ignite or freeze, this walking war crime of an industrial power house usually leaves nothing left of the bugs when he's done with them. He also carries powerful area of effect grenades. Or throwing axes. He also carries satchel charges, which you should probably avoid detonating on top of yourself and/or friends.I've rambled on long enough. Give this game a shake. The devs are still active, and cliche as it sounds,  Wild, right?And I mean, hey. If it doesn't scratch your itch for a co-op shooter, refunds exist for that purpose.Show the folks at Ghost Ship Games some love.

_childDocuments_.review: So I played the heck out of this game, and what did I get out of it?From getting it on sale, a lot more than what I paid for! Spent about 130 hours, almost max leveled all 4 characters , and still feels good to keep playing. It almost felt like a robbery.If you feel like you've ever paid too little for this gem of a game and want to support this indie dev team, there is always straight-forward cosmetic DLCs one can buy... and with none of that micro transaction crap.TL:DR The game is well crafted from having a dedicated and focused dev team that also listens to their player base. There is no bloat in it! The graphics are 'simple' but still look great and run smoothly even on an old PCs. There is as much story as there needs to be, and what is there is well done. Much of the game design respects the player by not baiting them into playing too long, or using sleazy micro transaction tricks. On top of that the dev team cultivated a great community that is not just tolerate of new players, but experienced players will help answer questions if they come up, along with having very amusing traditions. I see talent and the fun loving nature of the development team translating through into the game.The story is simple, but very solid and humorous. There are a few written lore things, like the optional briefing for the current season theme, or the bestiary entries, and whatnot, but most everything else is baked into the atmosphere of the game. There is some player character and NPC management banter to add life to things and the environmental story telling is pretty on point. The game mechanics are refined from literal years of constant development and listening to the community (sorry, too new to think of good examples for the latter). Features have been added in, and while it looks overwhelming at first, all-in-all there isn't any awkward feature creep in the game to muddy or overly complicate things. This isn't a F2P game where new crap is rolled out every several months to keep people hooked. Feature unlocks are very well paced through natural progress and at the pace the player dictates; with even a few more fun things unlocking after hitting 'max level' on a character once the player is familiar with the key mechanics.The stylized graphics are just as straight forward as the rest of the game, making it both look great and run every smoothly for most anyone with a PC (even on an old PC like mine!). It has been upgrade from back in the day (see DRG 2018 Legacy Ed. in the Beta branch for a shock!) but again there is no bloat in making things look 'realistic'. For seeing polygons and having no ray-tracing, the environments and lighting mechanics are absolutely great, proving that you don't need 'hyper realistic' graphics to make a so-called 'good game'.After stepping back and looking over this game, comparing it to other PvE team co-op games I've played, there is just no bloat that some of the others have. From the game mechanics, to the story, and to the graphics, there isn't anything there that really shouldn't be there when it comes to fun. It is just a lean mean mining (and bug killing) machine in the form of a no-nonsense beer-loving sci-fi dwarf! There are progress bars for things, but not so much to compel someone that they have to complete them in a certain amount of time or fear missing out on something. If you are the type that gets 'sucked into' doing daily stuff (like me), this game respects your time and doesn't load you down with goals you can't do in a few short sittings at a time (or one long one). So one might ask, what about the community? Is it toxic and/or full of hackers?Out of all the time I played, think I could count the number of gutless mud miners on one hand. Compare that to the countless hundreds of people I ran into that was Rock and Stone, and I'd say that the community is great. Newbies are welcomed and are usually guided through what needs to be done by experienced players if there any questions. Also several amusing in-game traditions have cropped up over the years, and the devs have noticed and humored the players; making the game feel much more like a community.If there are hackers, I have not seen them! If there are any, I'd feel sorry for them trying to cheat themselves out of getting good at the game! There is no high stakes PvP, no hard to get OP RNG dropped items that people 'have to get to win', no real world money on the line, or globe leader board to be a slave to (but there is a leader-board, for ). You Rock and Stone with your pals then you go back home and have a few (too many) cold ones back at the Abyss Bar, before going back out again (or passing out).In short [moved to TL:DR statement]

_childDocuments_.review: I promised to myself to do a review of this game after 1000 h... ok fine.TLDR: yeah it's a pretty good game, go buy it.So, where do I start...  Deep rock galactic is a game. Mmmh. It's a good game. Ok screw it.DRG is a game that I love, for lots of generic reasons: like the music and audio in general are incredible, 100% destructible environment and many missions types, lots of different enemies, it takes little HDD space etc etc.But I could say other things that people often wont tell you.The devs are actually nice people, i really mean it. They stream their game twice a week, have genuine fun and they respond to the questions of the community, they listen to advices, and they follow the game constantly (with patches and balancing).There is a 100% free battle pass, and they won't charge you any other money aside from the base price, the DLCs are only cosmetic, it's just if you want to support them.Also the community is probably one of the best if not the best community out there. The people are so chill and supportive in this game, almost unreal, they only want to have fun, shoot some bugs, gather some minerals and drink some beer in company.Also one of my favourite things is that you can customise your character in LOTS of different ways, from cosmetics to the many different builds for each class. Every modification, every overclock (you'll get it later) feels like you're actually changing your gameplay, there are infinite possibilities, for every playstyle. It's so well balanced (the devs know what they're doing)One last little thing is the modding system; it's easy to use and the community has gone crazy with that, from meme mods, to custom difficulty to QoL mods. In conclusion this game is extremely "random", you can do anything, you could also straight up don't play the mission and drink beers and kick some barrels, the game doesn't take itself too seriously in fact there are lots of funny interactions and they only serve to empathize with the dwarfs.I think this is the charm of the game. It's there, you can do what you want. And if you prefer a real challenge you can simply play the missions at higher difficulty.

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, I do recommend this game.This game feels like an amalgamation (did I spell that right?) of all the games I really wanted to enjoy. It feels like the developers have really sat down and looked at popular games and asked themselves "what makes these games fun?"I think what grabs me with this game is how they have made a vanity shop without money involved. You get the same progression, but it's actually FUN to play it. I don't have to constantly open my wallet, but instead I ponder how to maximize profits. It keeps me in the game and is a genuine escape from my day-to-day life at the moment.Gameplay is pretty straight forward, and I doubt you'll have much issue getting into the game quickly. A great tutorial exists in the game which is repeatable. I enjoy the art style even though it was a bit jarring to get to grips with the way the dwarves look. The caves you explore are varied, and there is enough enemy types to keep you on your toes. All in all this game has a lot going for it.The main pull of the game for me is the community. This game HEAVILY promotes teamwork. It makes people pull together and you will find a very patient community that just enjoys playing the game. Add on that the communication system in the game (VOIP and basic emotes) is enough to make a team communicate well, even without words. If you dwarf sais something, everyone around you hears it. That means "out of ammo" is broadcasted so everyone knows.I love this game. It's great.

_childDocuments_.review: IMO the currently best coop-PvE-experience one can get right now.The game runs incredibly well (mid to high settings, 1440p on GTX 1070 and i7 8700 led to 80+ FPS; is stable at over 130 FPS on my RTX 3080 / Ryzen 9 3900x (max settings)), has very short loading times, is less than 2 GB big in disc space used and most importantly: it's fun as hell.You choose one of 4 classes which you level up individually next to your overall player level. The classes feel different as each has very unique abilities which can be combined to make for an efficient and fun experience. Levelling your dwarfs grants you new equipment; you can unlock new weapons via so-called assignments. Cosmetics are unlocked via increasing your overall player level or finding equipment crates in-game.There are several mission types which include collecting eggs, defeating bigger boss-type enemies or simply gathering resources. The latter pretty much describes the general goal of this game: get into a cave and mine everything you find. Combat is relatively simple but can get hectic and requires a well-coordinated team on higher hazard levels (4 with modifiers, hazard 5 in general). The developers add new things to the game all the time via free updates; all DLCs so far have been cosmetics and purely optional.On a side note, solo is well done as well as you get a little combat / mining drone which helps you reach areas you normally would have trouble getting to while being alone.What makes the game interesting and contributes to eliminating repetitiveness are the procedurally generated levels; each cave feels different as you don't see the same kind of structure twice. Oh and the graphics: beautiful textures, great particle effects, brilliant colors.TL;DR: Great coop-experience with amazing level-design as well as fun progression. Also possible to have fun playing solo.

_childDocuments_.review: As simple as this game might seem at the first glance, it becomes rather complex the closer you get to the higher levels. One thing is roaming the 3rd difficulty, where you can pretty much just speedrun everything, another thing is level 4, which is still a walk in the park if you have any experience in FPS genre. And finally difficulty level 5, where even the smallest enemies may be lethal, and that requires cooperation with your teammates like no other game before.Classes are balanced, each has it's strengths and weaknesses that complement each other and create both a unique strategic and tactical combination for each team of players.Graphics are pretty minimalistic, but OK.Sounds are good, the only pity is there's little dialogue going on between characters, as opposed to, say, Vermintide 2 (and there's pretty much no lore in general, except for their long lost colleague Carl)Gameplay is very nice and responsive. Even though i hate bugs, I had no problem playing this game, the bastards are pictured in a rather cute way.A word for optimization - it's marvelous. An up-to-date game with lots of replayability that takes only 2.5 GBs of space is a gem.As a veteran L4d player (over 200 hrs off steam)and Vermintide 2 (over 900 hrs)I can definitely recommend this to everyone who loves cooperative games!

_childDocuments_.review: Deep Rock is an excellent game. Takes little space on your disk, runnable on potato computers, runs smoothly with good graphics options.In the same vein as other co-op games like Vermintide II or Left 4 Dead, Deep Rock is at is best when played with a group of friends - its core shooting and movement mechanics allow for a high skill ceiling in play and a satisfying feel, yet the random cave generation and wave spawning make for a non-stale loop. Pacing is good, too, with moments of relative peace in-between large hordes of bugs. The classes are balanced, the weapons and upgrades are balanced, enemies feel balanced - it's a masterclass in feeling like a cohesive product. Even the "hub" world between missions has stuff to do, and feels lively.The game isn't without its faults. Some mission types feel repetitive in their setup (i.e. a morkite mission is *always* going to be a roughly winding linear cave, a drilldozer mission will *always* have the same pattern of wave defense), some of the weapons while balanced don't have the proper feel to the hand (the M-1000's recoil is too little for me), and missions can tend to go on for a long time (you can't just "log in for 15 minutes" and play). But those are minor compared to the tight controls, well executed mechanics, and excellent level and game design that Deep Rock contains. Buy it if you don't have it... unless you hate shooters and don't have friends.Rock and Stone.

_childDocuments_.review: Some of you may be thinking what is it like being a miner?  I thought I knew what it was.  I thought I was a hardworking, unionized miner providing for my family.  A job with a good paycheck, benefits, and time off. I was blind.  I thought I landed the dream job.  A job that I can take real pride in. Without us miners, everything grinds to a halt.  A job where you have a true work family.   We are willing to lay down everything for each other, no matter the sacrifice. You certainly cannot get the kind of camaraderie in an office. I was blind. You see, I got the job during the holiday season.  The whole station was decked out in the holiday spirit.  Everyone was merry.  They told me that I came in the best time.  Plenty of holiday food to go around and I got a holiday bonus, even though I was new-thanks to the union.  So much holiday joy.   I was blind.When did my awakening begin?   It was not until my first refinery mission, where we gunned down the vicious elf, as we have always doneIt was not until we had the refinery all hooked up and we began pumping up that liquid morkiteIt was not until the machines whirred with their deafening noiseIt was not until the bugs swarmed us, maddened into an unrelenting fury by the noiseIt was not until I cleansed the bugs with my fire with the pipes bursting all around meIt was then, I realized what I was….It was then, I saw that liquid morkite, which everything our modern society depends onIt was nothing more than blood moneyMy righteous fire,It was nothing more than an imperial tool of oppression The vicious elves and unrelenting bugs,They were natives and we were taking their precious resources away from themI realized what I was, and I was ashamed of it What did I do at that moment?  I lifted my finger from the trigger, my fire coming to an endI shut down the imperial refinery and climbed to the top of it I shouted, “Peace, let there be peace!”All of a sudden, the chaotic fighting ceasedDwarves and bugs alike, turned to look upon meAt that moment, I dreamed of a utopia of dwarves and bugs living side by sideAnd I was here to lead them to itIs this where my story ends?  A happy, fairy tale ending?  Where we all hold hands and sing kumbaya?I wish it was so….To my horror, when my brothers had their backs turned to the bugsThe bugs seized them from behind,Dragging them down to their lairs I stood helpless, watching my brothers scream in abject terrorI have condemned my brothers, my family to a horrible endI knew what I was and I was ashamed of itThen, I heard itA most wicked laugh behind meIt was the elf, covered in liquid morkiteIn a chilling voice, it said to me, “Fool, your brothers you hold dear will now be no more.  Into the depths of Hoxxes they go.  To never be seen again.  However, there is still time to save yourself!”“NOOOOOO,” I roared! Those evil words spoken by the elf awakened within me a true Dwarf spirit  This time I knew what I was and I was not ashamed of it I was no longer blind  I jumped down from the refineryMy finger back on the trigger  This time, holy fire spewed forthThe devilish bugs before me melted awayAnd with that, I roared my battle cry, “Leave No Dwarf Behind!”A cry that echoed throughout the planet, into the station above, and into the hearts of all dwarves     Into the depths of Hoxxes, I goTo the very lair of the bugs, I goI will not return without my brothers-Karl

_childDocuments_.review: This is well made game with a great community. The completely destructible and randomly generated environment allows for a fun and creative experience. Want to play the game as intended? Then proceed to the objective. Want to dig a hole and seal yourself in, leaving all of your teammates out in the open to die? At your will. I think the biggest appeal to this game is not only the well polished missions, balance of difficulty, variety of weapons, perks, enemies, mission types, and small extras that lead to fun experience, but it's focus on cooperative play is, in my opinion, the best part. Playing alone can be fun, but I can only play about two missions before calling it a night. When playing with friends, on the other hand, I find my self wide-eyed when I look at the clock showing 3:00 AM. I've also enjoyed the barrage of posts on Reddit that bring a smile to my face everyday. I find the community very friendly and add to the immersive world that is Deep Rock. Another thing, the developers listen to the community, and have made it their goal to create a game that users love to play. Developer engagement with the community is key to a great release.If I had to give my negatives, it would be that it is hard to play the game alone. It's cooperative focus amplifies the experience when playing with friends, but leaves the solo player suffering from boredom (at least that is how it is for me). However, I would argue that this game is meant to be played with others and not alone.Overall, I'd give the game a 9/10. Note: I don't give games 10/10 unless they wow me, but this game is highly enjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: Deep Rock is a ton of fun. One of the best coop PvE games out there. If you only comparing it to other FPS PvE coop games, then it is the best.Pros: It's great with friends, of course, and the community is pretty friendly, that makes playing with randoms fun too (in a world where so many mulitplayer communities can be very toxic it's rather refreshing). It's also one of the better procedural generation games. No two maps will be the same but their are also interesting and easy enough to navigate. The gametypes are varied and fun which just adds to the replay value. The progression is fun and seems pretty fairly balanced (no egregious micro transactions and, in this day and age, that is a huge bonus). The classes are varied enough to be interesting and have cool synergies between them (even though I think the game would be better without a class system). Cons: There isn't a story but the setting is interesting. There aren't many audio queues so you might find yourself surrounded and overwhelmed without any warning. I wish there were more hud icons to help with navigating things. Not all weapons are created equal, some are fun and effective but others feel useless (like the sniper rifle with the scout class). At the end of the day, these cons feel very minor cause the core game is so well refined.  Strongly recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is what every "Early access game" should aim to be. Content rich, stable, fun and engaging, solo or with friends, online or off. Pros- -Excellent customization-Fun variety in classes, each bringing unique attributes to the group with different weapons, support options, and gear for each job.-Feature rich, full of things to do that will keep you engaged for 40+ hours easily, and more still coming!-engaging "Home base area" with several mini games and a full "Bar" where you can get drunk, and even buy special brews that give you in game buffs! The home base area is even available seemlessly with a group, so you and your 3 buddies each have a pod and you can gear up and drink and dance together while deciding what mission to take.- fun and creative achievements. You will be amazed. There are achievements for ridding on your "M.U.L.E" partner, and other flora and fauna, finding rare enemies and resources. More than a few are very challenging, but very rewarding to get.-Great intuative Co-Op play, or solo play. You can host a public game letting players drop in and out with you, or private with just your friends. The game offers lots of ways to combine your skills and abillities, like using the enigneer's platform gun to shoot a platform high up to reach resources in a hard to reach location, and having a scout repel up with his grapple gun to harvest the resources. Even still, playing solo is no shame, because they give you a tiny adorable little robot named BOSCO who will defend and revive you, and you can even upgrade him to blow your foes to bits with rockets and mine those precious minerals even faster.-Fun and exciting swarms, even on lower difficulties. The beat drops, the games amazing music kicks in and you dig in and defend as a horde of angry critters come scurrying at you with murderous intent. Nothing feels more badass than mowing down hordes of aliens or "tactically retreating" (shut up Karl, I wasn't running away) while the beat drops as you unleash a storm of pain with all the tools at your disposal.Cons-Limited game modes- With only "Point extraction", "Mining", "Egg Hunt" "Salvage" and "Exterminate" missions available, things can get a bit repetitive as time goes on. Most of the time im more excited about maximizing my score and mining the most stuff I can or interesing things that happen in the middle of the game more than what I was actually supposed to do.A pretty small con to be sure, as there is still plenty of stuff to do.Enemy Variety- I think this is where the game suffers the most in my opinion. Most enemies fall into the 2 categories of "Hangs back either flying or hanging off the ceelings and shoots things at you" or "Rushes you like a maniac and sties to maul you". There are some modifications to this, but after about 40-50 hours its pretty rare to see anything that surprises you (the big exception to this is the BET-C. you'll know him when you see him). I was really sad that the Dreadnoughts are mostly just "Big Praetorian's" with an extra health bar and a ranged attack with a further reach, but don't get me wrong, they will bloody chew you up good and proper. Its more than enough variety for the most part, and I hope that maybe i'm just missing some things, but I find myself wishing I would see something new that makes me say "OH SH-T"Tldr- Amazing game that delivers on all its promises. Amazing music, great art style and fun mechanics. I just wish there were a few more mission types and enemies, but its hard to really complain about and early access game of this kind of quality, and I plan to be around when more content comes out for the game!(P.S.- I think I actually convinced my GF to play a video game with me with this game! A+ to Deep Rock galactic! Rock and Stone brother!)

_childDocuments_.review: I only dislike this game because of how quickly it becomes repetitive for gameplay sustinence- and of course I only poured just over 6 hours into it, but I genuinely didn't feel much when it came to my finalized thoughts at that point. I can understand why it's highly Overwhelmingly Positive, because it appeals to that niche of mindless fun. Even as I type this and fully am aware that I kindof played myself for getting into something I wasn't *quite* sure I'd like, I thought it would be my cup of tea since I love games with seemingly endless grind like Destiny. But hey, friends gotta peer pressure one way or another. I don't discourage playing this game, because you quite clearly are either on the bandwagon of love or you're not, and that bandwagon is pretty giant, so most people must love this game. I more or less just might be a rare instance where the gameplay didn't click because of peer pressure, or because it didn't feel similar enough to other games, and I may never be entirely sure what it was. By all means, buy this game if you deep down know that you'll be wanting to grind endlessly for hours upon hours upon hours, essentially being led by how minimal the game's complexity is. Plenty of games in my past have done that exact same thing, just differently, and can be psychologically tailored without the developer knowing or not. So I can fully understand why the game is Overwhelmingly Positive, I'm more or less just an outlier for the crowd.

The main gameplay loop is simple and fun, shoot bugs and mine ores in a wide variety of destructible environments and mission types. Unlike other games that entices you to play with FOMO, Deep Rock Galactic is perfectly enjoyable as a game that you can play once in awhile as well as giving you mini goals to complete, like upgrading your weapons or more importantly dazzling your friends with your impeccable F A S H I O N. This game is playable solo and with randoms through matchmaking, but it is certainly more enjoyable with friends if you have any that is. I definitely recommend picking this up and I hope to see you all at the Abyss Bar.Rock and Stone, brothers!

Rock and Stone!--ORIGINAL REVIEW--Short version: Great game. Highly recommend. Pros: Dwarfs, mining, gold, gems, guns, pickaxes, alien planets, deadly alien bugs, team co-op, special events, weekly challenges, character class advancement, cosmetic customization, silly jokes, and beer... what's not to love? With the seasons bringing free content and the battlepass only containing cosmetics (that will be added to the random loot pool when the season ends), and  the dlc only being cosmetics, you very much get what you pay for. Above all this though is the community, being the single most friendly and anti-toxic game I have seen. despite the ♥♥♥♥ talk you get for ordering leaf lovers (rightfully so), i have only encountered 1 truly toxic people while playing the game, and he was summarily kicked by the host, with a shout of rock and stone. the average experience for greenbeards is having some random level 150+ dropping in to your haz 2 game and depositing useful tips on how to play the game, as well as teaching DRG manners such as typing r in chat when you are ready to proceed with  the objective, pressing v at appropriate times (all the time), and of course, the sacred RICHual. I might not be that grey of a beard, but I have meet my share of greenbeards and it is always a joy to help them and to teach them the ways of ROCK! AND! STONE! PS. _childDocuments_.review: Almost 850 hrs in and it's still a blast. I kinda understand the negative reviews saying it gets stale but let's be honest, they probably either play alone or tryhard on top difficulty which is noticeably less fun than playiing as a party of 3-4 in VC and just goofing around while still doing stuff. You should give it a try. If you look for a game for 2-4 players to have a blast of an experience and lots of fun you've hit the spot. If you don't play with friends it's about 100 hrs before it can get stale which still is a lot of time even for a full price.Basically a certified Australian experience as you find yourself removing eight-leeged buggers and oversized flies from the face of the planet with pretty much any possible way you can think of. Shoot then? Yes. Burn them? Yes. Freeze them to death? Sure! Melt them in acid? Why not! Tactical nukes?! Coming right up! With 4 classes each having 3 primary weapons and 3 secondaries you are bound to find something you like. At first it seemed to me that lack of the ADS mechanic ruins the gunplay experience but you will grow to appreciate it when you fing youself in the middle of the swarm. There are a few mission types and honestly they get progressively more and more cringe with seasons and there are some really questionable decisions made about their usage in assignmemt chains but you still get a luxury of not playing them if you don't enjoy them (unless you are trying to prestige).The game is heavily focused on team cooperation and the best way of playing is in a full lobby of 4 different classes. The laser pointer tool paired up with dwarf voicelines is just a perfect method of communication. There are almost no situations in which you would need to use in-game chat or VC and it's definitely a plus. As for the players DRG is literally the most wholesome community I've ever seen. Of course there are exceptions but most players here are friendly and understanding. Some lobbies do expeсt you to have at least some skill (usually they request some amount of prestige in description) but there are a lot of high-level players that will gladly accept a relatively new player and help them along the way. And on top of that YT has years of video content with gameplay tips, loadouts, obscure trics etc.All gameplay content comes in the base game. All DLCs so far are purely cosmetic. The weapons are not evenly balanced but all weapons are totally viable even in their base state. As you play more with a single class you unlock other weapons and weapon mod tiers that let you fit the gun to your playstyle. Once you get the maximum EXP with one class you can promote it (prestige) and this unlocks the rest of the content, mainly overclocks (an extra weapon mod) and deep dives (gauntlet). Up until player rank 100 (which is like 12 promotions and about 150-200 hrs) you will get progression assignments that boost your unlock speed. It took me about 250 hrs to get all the gameplay unlocks and in 850 hrs I still do not have all of the base game cosmetics. The battle pass is totally free and awesome and all the content you missed from it is added to base game unlocks when it rotates to the next one.As you get stuff and get good at the game you have two ways of playing. You can tryhard and sweat at top difficulty which ins't fun consistently imo but still is an option. On the other hand as you get better you can make your builds progressively dumber and still complete objectives. Suddenly all of the "lackluster" overclocs and weapons are not just ridiculous but ridiculously fun. I've been clearing pre-top difficulty with all kinds of builds and having your friends witness you use up half of you ammo in a second to oneshot some big bugger is a ton of fun. As a bonus you virtually become a millionaire (but the prices of everything except the beer skyrocket as well).As I already mentioned they are purely cosmetic. Don't listen to the reviews saying devs are milking players with them, just read the DLC reviews. Most players buy them out of respect just to support the devs. The skins are really cool yet the base game also has a bunch of fire skins.There are already tons of mods. You can adjust literally anyting from sounds to balance. Cherry on top is that with a little research you can make some basic mods too and it is surprisingly easy even if you don't know any programming languages.Try it. It's amazing. Rock and Stone future miners!

_childDocuments_.review: = Overview / Summary = Deep Rock Galactic is a fast-paced co-op game with a variety of difficulty levels to try out. Each of the classes are unique and useful while at the same time not being required in order for a group to function, though certain classes obviously excel at certain situations/missions/enemies over others. The game could use more game modes and environment types, and the voxel worlds it procedurally generates 90% of the time are great - but sometimes you get some weird layouts (especially if the map complexity rating is high).Also the community is very welcoming and most of the people I run into are cool and don't argue when I play online, making me want to never play solo even when my gaming buddies aren't around. Progression was a bit stale until the seasons patch update, but now I find myself having tons to do when I log in, even if I play a lot.Make sure to pick Driller and C4 your teammates at the end of the game > : ) - and rezz them of course, we aren't that cruel ;) - I also recommend taking the "Friendly" perk if this kind of PvP / team damage fun doesn't amuse you (but most players laugh at it, if it's in jest / good faith - but you better be able to take it too!)= Pros = - Quick games (longest I had was 40 minutes and its usually 15 to 20 minutes for most matches).- Fun and useful classes.- Good progression pacing.- Voxel game that has a lot of features with minimal issues/bugs.- Daily assignments! (This was a previous Con for me of "no daily assignments" but they added some in with the season)= Cons =- The head bob and screen shake stuff was annoying until I learned you can toggle it off.- Some perks feel required to me, like Hover Boots to avoid random pitfalls that can kill you, or Heightened Senses if your teammates don't help you break free. Maybe I'm wrong on this, but prior to having them I died a lot more.- No indication that being capped at level 25 for a class wastes class experience. You're supposed to play another class before promoting the level 25 class or all the exp the level 25 class earns basically goes to waste (since it's capped). Once promoted it resets to level 1 again and the exp isn't wasted.- The Microsoft version and the Steam version are not able to play with each other - which bummed me out for being unable to play with my X-Box buddies unless I forked out money for another copy. At least let use the same copy on both platforms, kinda greedy - don't become like the triple A studios by giving into greed guys. Stick to what makes you good.All in all I love this game and I can see myself putting hundreds of hours on it until I get bored (already over 130 hours played since I got it).

_childDocuments_.review: Deep Rock Galactic stratches an itch that has been around for years, a great fps co-op experience. When originally looking at this game, I actually reinstalled Left 4 Dead just to satisfying that craving. And while L4D is a fantastic game, we needed something more modern. Enter, Deep Rock Galactic.Deep Rock Galactic follows a very similar format to L4D, with drop-in drop-out 4 player co-op bug blasting missions of hilarity. A casual yet challening evironment makes gamers of all skill levels feel comfortable, and the randomly generated caves keep each mission feeling unique. A progression system also helps new players ease into the game while keeping hardcore miners working for pretigious awards.With fantastic use of low poly terrain and gorgeous lighting within the deep rocks, DRG is a treat for the eyes. A repectable assortment of biomes in the game keep your surroundings not only fresh visually, but provide unique obstacles such as sandstorms, blizzards, or even lightning crystals to conquer.On top of the supreme gameplay experience, DRG has a charm to it that many games lack these days. The lobby area on the space station continues to grow and is oozing with personality. The Bar quenches the thirst of any weary dwarf while a lovable barrel tossing mini game gives you something to do while you wait for buddy to get himself another drink.DRG gets this lion's approval for best co-op game of 2018

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: What do you get when you crossbreed "Red Faction" with "Aliens" and throw some dwarves with guns into the mix? I haven't a clue... but it sounds fück!ng awesome!You're a dwarf. A space dwarf, working on an orbital mining station, whose sole task is to get sent to the caverns on the planet below, explore them and mine the quota of rare minerals. Some deposits are hard to reach and present a logistical problem, which can be solved by generous application of grappling hooks or ziplines or by brute force mining. It would be a simple and rewarding job... if not for the local fauna, with teeth and claws straight outta hell, which will interrupt any and all mining attempts.The game comprises randomly generated missions, mainly consisting of a procedurally generated cave, where you have to find, mine and store in a handy four-legged dumpster (think Terry Pratchett's Luggage but with less intelligence and utility) some minerals. Sometimes you'll mount a rescue mission only to find out that everyone is missing and all equipment is damaged. Sometimes you're sent as pest control team, where the pest in question is an order of magnitude larger than what you've encountered so far. But mostly it's about mining. The quotas are generous and the caves are dark and deep...The missions start and finish on the janky, dilapidated Space Rig, which has everything a dwarf needs to thrive and survive - a bunk to sleep, a bar to get sloshed, barrels to kick about and a drop pod to get to the action. You can choose between four distinctive classes, which are designed to complement each other in a 2-4 player coop. Each class has unique weapons and abilities and enough perks and unlocks to choose from to keep the gameplay relevant. If you're an sp gamer at heart you will probably welcome the fact that every mission can be played  and you'll get a companion drone to help with the mining and fighting.The world is fully destructible. I know plenty of games now include this feature, but it's just so fitting in this setting. The egg is stuck behind a rocky pillar? No problem bucko!I think the correct term here is "mine-y" not "grind-y". How else would you expect to get the minerals from the nodes, hmm?And yes, I can envisage it being a bit repetitive and grindy after a while. The content isn't infinite you know and there isn't really a story there. But DRG strikes a perfect balance between living on borrowed time down in the caves and advancing your dwarf of choice through plethora of perks, equipment and unlockable cosmetics. In a way, DRG's main gameplay loop reminds me of the ancient Heavy Gear game and its Career Mode, where all you'd do is go on interconnected string of missions and advance through the ranks. Seemingly pointless, but rewarding in itself.Oh, yessss, it haz bugs! Dozens.  even! More than you can shake your boomstick at!They come in different forms, from small maggots, to leaping youngsters (which are enormously satisfying to take down mid-flight with a well aimed shot) all the way through to lumbering, heavily armed behemoths which make barrels of your trusty minigun glow red with rage.Apart from this there are some weird graphical artefact leftovers here and there, mainly after you've just mined something, and some stuttering when using ground-piercing scanners, but nothing major.Nah. It's at the end of its roadmap anyway and what's there already is worth  you spend on it and more.Remember the hype built around many AAA+ titles these days? How big companies pour annual budget of some "third world" countries worth of dollars into marketing... and all that comes out is an unpolished turd propped with 12GB "day one patch" and pay-to-unlock content?Well, this here game is nothing of the sort. It is, in my most humble opinion, an absolute gem and its reputation is well earned. Spread the word.RÖCK AND STONË TO THË BÖNE!

_childDocuments_.review: Deep Rock is an extremely well designed and crafted game that has been my latest obsession. All 4 classes feel highly rewarding to play with each feeling just as important as the other. Music, while not what I personally would call memorable, is still very well composed and the classic lines of "We're rich!" and "Rock and Stone!" never get old. _childDocuments_.review: Ello G'day, if you're looking for a legit review of this game you've come to the wrong place. But if you're looking for an amazing Lemon Chia cake recipe you've come to the right place.Ingredients: 2 tbs black chia seeds1/3 cup (80ml) milk2 1/2 cups (400g) wholemeal plain flour3 tsp baking powder1/4 tsp bicarbonate of soda125g unsalted butter, softened200g light muscavado sugar2 eggsFinely grated zest and juice of 1 lemon250g Greek yoghurtYOGHURT AND LEMON ICING2 tbs icing sugar, sifted1/2 cup (140g) Greek yoghurtFinely grated zest and juice of 1/2 a lemonMethod:1.Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease base and sides of a 22cm ring mould cake pan and line with baking paper.2.Combine chia seeds and milk in a bowl and set aside for 5 minutes to soften.3.Meanwhile, combine flour, baking powder, bicarb and 1/4 tsp salt flakes in a bowl. In a stand mixer fitted with paddle attachment, beat butter and sugar until pale and fluffy. Add eggs, 1 at a time, beating between each addition. Stir through lemon zest and juice and chia mixture. _childDocuments_.review: A one trick pony that has very little to offer outside of a very basic game loop. If you run a single mission you will have seen everything this game has to offer at this point, outside of how the different classes play. There are very few things to upgrade or purchase at the moment and the crafting materials you need to do so are dolled out very sparingly. There is a good foundation here for a fun co-op game, but it needs a lot of work to get there. I can see why the devs have said they plan to be in early access for a year to two years - there's just not a whole lot here right now. I feel that in my less than 10 hours of game time so far I have seen a lot of the same old in terms of map generation. The random generation is more akin to Warframe's tile system, and while superficially one mission might feel a bit different than the next, overall there's nowhere near as much diversity in map design as you might expect. I feel like eventually DRG might be worth a purchase, but right now it's a rather barebones experience.UPDATE 6/27/18: Decided to revisit DRG and can happily report there is a lot more meat to the game. Maps feel more varied, mostly do to new biome specific hazards. The new perk system adds a bit of variety to builds and gives you more reasons to play and upgrade classes you might otherwise ignore. New enemies add more variety and the game looks and plays even better now. Definitely heading in the right direction, even if development is a bit slower than some EA titles.

Game is well optimised, already contains enough content for many hours of play, you regularly communicate with the playerbase and take/act on feedback given... keep it up.The game itself is a blast, kind of  a mix of minecraft meets Payday2 meets Starship Troopers... all in hectic 4 player coop.The precedural gen cave systems are fantastic, you'll find yourself exploring through tight twisting tunnels which then open up to huge expansive caverns or leading to a sudden drop of hundred of feet that you'll have to try and navigate/create a route down (or up).You can see in places where new content is planned (talking about the orbital mining station here) and the devs are seeking suggestions on new content to add so I have really high hopes for this one.  Normally with early access titles I enjoy whats there and hope more comes, with this I'm seriously confident more will come to turn this into a real gem of a game (pun intended).If you are on the fence about buying this and you enjoy coop based games.... get off the fence, buy it and get your friends to buy it... you won't regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: Another one of what used to be called a "L4D Clone", is now called a "Co-op FPS" and which now might be better named a "Horde Shooter". It's you and up to 3 other blue-collars digging down into a dark, hostile alien world at the behest of a huge space mining corporation. Your objective: strip the world bare of anything valuable. Your opposition: an entire world's worth of swarming space bugs, plus additional hostile flora, fauna, and hazardous environments. This game sets itself apart from other examples of the genre with the focus on resource collection and management, the ability to modify terrain, and a unique premise. You are not just any space miner. You are a space DWARF miner, with the attendant love of gold, drink, and striking things with pickaxes. The dark atmosphere and sense of humor are surprisingly well-balanced.Also available is robust character customization, in weapons, equipment, build and cosmetics. The community is generally quite good, despite the fact that friendly fire is always on- the highest difficulty and the "challenge run" gamemode, Deep Dive, is gated behind your first promotion (prestige), which reduces newbies stumbling into advanced games, and hosts have absolute kick authority, making it difficult to screw up a game and live to tell about it. Alternatively, you can do most missions solo with the assistance of a small do-anything drone.Overall, a definite recommendation. Rock and Stone.

_childDocuments_.review: ok so i decided to refine this review a bit, just for the hell of it. and lemme tell you somethin,this game is absolutely bangin, probably one of my top 3 co-op games of all time.Pros:+ this is the best dwarf game (by default)+ all of the classes feel really good to play, each with their own strengths that they bring to the table for both themselves and their team, while never being absolutely necessary, allowing for a lot of composition flexibility.+ all classes have a high skill ceiling thanks to overclocks and certain upgrades.+ the OST, while not as vibrant as other games i've played, is still top notch.+ the sprinkles of humour are leagues above a lot of games nowadays.+ the visuals are absolutely stunning with its style.+ dwarves as a concept open up a lotta fun things you could include in a game, and the bar and the wacky beer are some of them.+ despite all having the same VA at different pitches, all the classes are entertaining in their own right.+ the devs care, man. this is one of the only games i'll fork money over for the dlcs *just* for the devs.+ "rock and stone" is genius.+ all of the mission types feel fun in their own way, and (most of) the biomes are also a blast.+ the bugs are really satisfying to pump lead into.+ these are battle passes done right. no additional fee for the good stuff, no harsh grind expectations, little to no FOMO, just bliss.+ dwarf burp an fard and it funiCons:- the balance patches can be a bit questionable at times (cough cough ECM mining).- while the idea of the rivals is really cool, the execution is kinda... mostly miss. mainly just cuz the robots are not fun to fight in the slightest. Drilling In The Name Of did a video on this topic, and it covers basically all my issues with them.- Hollow Bough.- perk points kinda need another use. all they're doing is sitting in my point count at like 72 cuz i already maxed out all my perks. it really doesn't take much grinding to get to that point.- speaking of needing a use; error cubes! pleeeease...- the hub is kinda lacking in features (target range, more stuff to do with crew, etc.)- the barrel hoop achievement. good lord.overall, yeah most of the cons are just nitpicks anyway, so imma just say that this game is well worth the money. hell, it might even be worth double that. thank you GSG for this absolute gem of a game. rock and stone!
