_childDocuments_.review: Deep Rock Galactic is a co-op shooter where you mine minerals and shoot bugs.The concept is simple, drop in, complete the objectives, get out. But the combination of classes, weapons, different objectives, fully destructible environment and procedurally generated levels make it fun for many hours. Most of the time you are on the move, exploring the caves, mining ores and kiting bugs, except for some defense objectives.There's a lot of customization to find a playstyle you like with many weapon builds, overclocks (gun mods), perks. With the weapon builds and overclocks you can have bullets that ricochet from enemies, specializing your weapon for primary shooting or charged shots, elemental effects and even shotgun jumping. You can only choose up to 3 passive and 2 active perks that allow you do things like return melee damage, insta revives, shield boosting and the best of all, taming an enemy bug that you can pet!The best combo in the game is the engineer's platform with the scout's grapple to get to any place out of reach. The driller can create a makeshift bunker by drilling the wall or use his drills to directly reach the drop pod. And the gunner has zip lines to help carry teammates and big ores.The main lobby features a Barrel Hoop mini game where you kick barrels into a moving hoop, lots of beer that have plenty of fun effects and some that give buffs during a mission and a jukebox with a dance floor. After you experience the main content of the game, you can level up to get prestige, get dwarf and pickaxe customization, complete the weekly deep dives and get overclocks. Overclocks are sadly dropped randomly, with some choice on machine events, so it might take a while to get an overclock you like.Compared to similar co-op games, DRG provides content updates for free, while paid DLCs are only for soundtracks and cosmetics. It also has an amazing feeling when you join other lobbies, salute with your "Rock and Stone" and get saluted back!For achievement hunters:There are some challenging ones that are easier in co-op and some that require 4 players in the same lobby. You have to complete 100 solo mission and the biggest grind is getting all 4 dwarfs to Gold promotion.

_childDocuments_.review: Rock and Stone.Deep Rock Galactic is surprisingly good for a game in Early Acess. Stable, Performing well and geniunly fun its great to see Early Acess produce quality once in a while. TL;DR on bottom for those who dont like giant walls of text.FEATURES:1. The planet Hoxxes and its many wonders - the game is set on Hoxxes, a planet so deadly you could fit it into Warhammer 40k, imagining youre a squat.  The Caves - your main play area, bristling with ores, crevaces, deadly murder bugs and general unpleasantries. The main thing about levels in DRG (Deep Rock Galactic) is what EVERYTHING (even y o u) is Voxel. You could literally dig your own (albeit empty) caverns if your wish so. Caves feature Length and Difficulty settings. Length determines the complexity, from a simple tunnel zigzaging deeper, to giant (and thats not an exaggeration) caverns, full of native wildlife and ore. Difficulty not only affects how hardy the Nasties of Hoxxes are, but also their numbers. Hordes will most likely deplete your ammunition very quickly on higher difficulty, forcing you to employ strategy and teamplay to survive.  Biomes - for a planet which is completely barren on surface, Hoxxes caves are magnificent. The game features multiple biomes, each nothing like the other, from dry sand pits to literaly fungus jungles. Coupled with random generation, no mission is alike. A prime example is my experience in Fungus Bogs: during mission one, the caves were full of poison mushrooms, giving the slushy hellscape its name, however during mission 2, instead of ample fungus supplies, i found myself in a middle of an Alien nest, with eggs scattered everywhere (which can be destroyed to release the nasties inside) and finally, on third mission sticky, slowing goop was randomly pooling around, making progress difficult. Each Biome has different things for it, giving you an unique experience in each, well worth to see. The Glyphid - your main adversary. Nasty lil ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, Glyphid come in in all shapes and sizes, from tiny nibblers to giant, poison spewing Praetorians. Glyphids, like everything else, are voxel which is a good thing, since you can literally tear their shells apart, making combat quite brutal (as you literally turn that one warrior into a pile of meat). Glyphid themselves are also tricky, while the AI does get silly sometimes, theyre still capable of feats such as sneaking (im looking at you, exploder) or just overwhelming you in sheer numbers, while some species have their unique behavior.  Native Wildlife - while as of now theres not much, alongside Glyphids theres plenty of flora and several fauna you can see in your adventures, most passive with a few either agressive, or defensive. Despite how scarce fauna is, it makes the biomes alive, immersing you in the idea that hoxxes is a truly alien world. Despite just being there, fauna and flora can be useful, platforms, light and so on.  Temperature - newest addition to the game, now you can freeze your dwarven arse if youre not careful in Glacial Strata. Lucky for you, there are ways to keep yourself warm, as long as you dont stick your face in those ice vents.2. The Stout Lads (aka you.) The Classes - DRG features 4 distinct classes, each with their own tools and weaponry. 1) Gunner is the fighter of your team, sporting a nifty minigun to mow down the enemy (just dont let it overheat) alongside a powerful magnum, explosive satchel (essentially C4) and a zipline for Utility.2) Scout is the lightbulb of your party, with his flares allowing you to see whats happening, without tossing your glowstics every 5 seconds while assisting with his full auto rifle and double barrel shotgun. Uses grapling hook to get to places.3) Engineer can be considered your line of defence, his sentry guns packing quite a punch, considering theres 2 of them. Engineer also has a semi auto shotgun and a grenade launcher. Platform gun (literally creates platforms) is the ulitily.4) Driller the hardworking digboy of the crew. Digger allows you to pass into dirt-blocked areas of the caves without it taking ages to dig out (or wasting C4) while providing AoE damage with his flamethrower with a pistol for single targets. Drills serve as Utility. The Upgrades - in DRG, your equipment (even flares) have upgrades to them, damage and ammunition size for weapons, and recharge rates/special bonuses for armor. flares increase brightness and duration while pickaxe give meele damage. Cosmetics - conquer the depths in style. DRG allows you to change the following on your dwarf:1) Armor (includes both body and variety of helmets)2) Skin color3) Mustaches4) Beards5) Hair  Cosmetics are bought with credits and resources you earn through gameplay, no lootboxes.Perks -  DRG features a perk system, from move/carry speed, to jump damage reduction to more resource yields. Perk points are aquired by completing milestones (such as complete X missions in biome B or do secondary objective of type A X times) which give from 2 to 5 perk points. Perks are split into tiers, with the next tier generally consisting of upgrades for previous tier. 3. Gamemodes - Shooting'n'Looting 101 DRG features several gamemodes:1) the Standart Mining operation: you must venture underground to collect X (depends on cave length) amount of morkite. While you dont have to gather anything else, it would be silly to ignore all this gold scattered about. in Addition to Morkite, you have a secondary objective which, while not required to complete the mission, provides with a healthy credit bonus.2) Egg hunt: Collect Alien Eggs hidden throughout the cavern, their location visible on the map and defined by an Organic growth to get the egg itself.3) Point Extraction: youre dropped off in a large chamber, with a mining rig which serves as your main holdout. your mission is to dig out chunks of Aquarq hidden within the walls, and deliver them to the mining rig all while fending off an endless onslaught of Glyphids, eager to chew you up. upon mission finish, you must holdout until the drop pod arrives.4) Elimination: The boss fights of DRG. Your goal is to eliminate Glyphid Dreadnaughts, monstrous boss type enemy with multiple healthbars and attacks. VERY hard to solo and requires quite a bit of team effort to bring the Monsters down.5) Salvage operation: Your objective is to repair several mini M.U.L.Es and then repair the broken Drop Pod, which you will use to escape.  Mutators - added in update 15, Mutators spice up the game even more. Mutators are split in 2 categories, Warnings and Anomalies. Warnings - negative mutators which increase hazard bonus. currently the game has 4:1) Exploder Infestation: Bugs ko kaboom. And theres a LOT of them. +30% hazard pay.2) Shield Disruption: your shields are always down.  +30% hazard pay.3) Mactera Plague: LOTS of flying bugs. +20% hazard pay.4) Cave Leech Clusters: remember half life barnacles? Same thing except more horrifying. +15% hazard pay. Anomalies - postive or neutral mutators which DO NOT increase hazard bonus. currently the game has 7:1) Gold rush: M O R E gold.2) Mineral Mania: Crafting materials (NOT morkite or secondary) spawn in larger amounts.3) Double exp: self explanatory.4) Low Gravity: ditto.5) Critical Weakness: enemy weakspots deal even more damage.6) Golden Bugs: every glyphid killed gives you gold.7) Rich Atmosphere: move faster, have helium voice and spring while carrying heavy rocks. This sums up the game. i hope.TL;DR Game is good and well polished for an EA titles. Devs are transparent about development. Best enjoyed with friends.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the quintessential co-op buddy shooter. Hundreds of hours worth of fun gameplay. Using mic is entirely optional. The classes all feel entirely different and fun. The developers come up with new content regularly and provide it for free. By new content, I mean new maps, new missions, new weapons, and new enemies, not just bug fixing. All this on top of the fact that the devs just (9/14/21) started officially verifying mods and created a built-in mod manager (non steam workshop) that works flawlessly. I paid like 25 dollars for this game over a year ago and that has to be the best $/fun ratio decision that I've made over the past decade.I've regularly spent time playing this while watching movies on another monitor, because there's just something instinctively satisfying about mining shiny stones and scoring head shot after head shot on hordes of enemies.If you like Vermintide, Left 4 Dead, or any other co-op monster killer game, you'll have a blast. 10/10.

_childDocuments_.review: "Deep Rock Galactic is a game that I really like. It offers an excellent balance between the Driller, Gunner, Engineer and Scout classes. Each class complements the others: The Gunner can use his big guns to protect his teammates, while the Driller digs paths to get to the target location faster. The Scout, on the other hand, lights up the caves so that you can see something.The background story of the game is fascinating: a corporation decides to build a space station above a planet with valuable minerals. This corporation, Deep Rock Galactic, was founded by a team of dwarves who are ready to harvest the planet. Anyone who says this isn't a story will be taken 2nd, 3rd, 4th, 5th, 6th, 7th, 8th and 9th by Uncle Yusuf and sat on a chair filled with Lego bricks. That will certainly be painful!

_childDocuments_.review: Here is my insight as an experienced player.The game is fun, really fun. It is the best coop game on the market right now and the spiritual successor of L4D2. As all coop games it's better to play with your friends, but pugs are also very enjoyable. Solo play is also supported. Just a reminder thought : every game mechanic is thought with coop in mind (more on that later). There is no place for selfishness. You will get the best game experience by playing with a full team of each class, you have been warned. Each class and weapon is different with its own strengths and weakness you have to understand and master. There definitely is a playstyle for you, you just have to find it. The game feels extremely different depending on which class you play and its loadout.The procedural generation X mission types X biomes make the game infinitely replayable. The main challenge in Deep Rock is definitely the terrain and how you traverse it to achieve your objectives while trying to stay alive. Each class has its own unique traversal/utility tool so you really want every class in your team to be efficient during mission.Shooting bugs is satisfying. There's enough variety in the bestiary to not feel stale. Shooting/Exploding/Melting bugs in many different ways is always fun. Some classes/weapons are better/worse against different bugs so that's another reason you should have a diverse team. Bugs being able to crawl on walls and ceilings isn't something you see in a lot of games and add to the difficulty. Enemies can and will come from all directions.The gameplay loop and progression is solid. You level up, get credits and minerals to unlock cosmetics, gun modifications and character perks to further customize your playstyle. The "endgame" is doing weekly deeps dives and assignments to get overclocks and cosmetics. This can lead to frustration since unlocks are randoms (not entirely) and weekly capped.The game is challenging. No one play below hazard 3. Casual pugs usually play in hazard 3 while haz 4 is more for experienced players. There is also haz 5, but the way the end of mission bonus is calculated make it too risky to play for the payout vs lower difficulties. High hazard can get unfair at times, but that's just a product of the game's procedural generation and swarm mechanic. You just have to accept that sometimes defeat is inevitable if you get overrun on bad terrain. But that's also part of the challenge, you always need to have a plan.Sound design is on point. I advise you to listen to the OST. The voice actor does an amazing job voicing all 4 dwarves. The game is really atmospheric and downright serene during exploration. The difference between a silent, empty cave and an intense fight during a swarm is always memorable. But never get too complacent when there's silence. There's always something lurking in the shadows.The game just released update 30 as I'm writing this. They balanced many weapons/overclocks that were overused or underused. That's right, the dev team isn't afraid to nerf OP stuff and buff less used alternatives. This means the game won't have powercreep (Payday 2 anyone ?). It can get frustrating when they touch your preferred loadout but it is for the better in the long run. And that's following update 29 that reworked perks. Although understandable, sometimes it feels like they balance solely on popularity and not on actual performance. You can expect the game to stay challenging over its lifetime and not lose its charm, hopefully.Should you buy Deep Rock ? Definitely.EDIT : update 32 released with 2 new missions types and weapon/overclock balancing.These new missions are an escort mission done right (not joking) with a boss battle at the end, and a refining mission with pipe riding. Without going too deep, this is, in my opinion, the new gold standard in game design. The pacing, overall game design and originality is top notch, especially refining. Escort on the other hand is also enjoyable and fixes all the bad preconceptions about the gamemode seen in other games, while also adding its own twists with the refueling phase and the boss battle at the end.The weapon/overclock balance is also welcomed. More playstyles are now viable. An excellent change to the game as always.

_childDocuments_.review: Deep Rock Galactic is an absolute gem of a game, and I don't mean that in a geological sense (though there is plenty of digging involved). The game is beautifully designed, with stunning graphics and an immersive soundtrack that really pulls you into the experience. But what sets Deep Rock Galactic apart is the sheer absurdity of it all. I mean, come on. You're a dwarf in space, armed with a flamethrower and a pickaxe, battling giant spiders and collecting shiny rocks. If that doesn't sound like a recipe for a good time, I don't know what does.Overall, Deep Rock Galactic is a hilarious and action-packed adventure that will have you laughing, screaming, and high-fiving your friends. A game you don't tea-bag others or your own team, but rather, you lift your ax or beer to your other dwarven brethren in reverence and respect. It is a game meant to just, well, be played and have fun doing it. There is this aura of fun and positivity that surrounds this game and is so welcome and breath of fresh air in the current year 2020. And because of this style of game, it attracts such a pleasing player base. All of its ratings are well deserved and genuine due to its gameplay and design, unlike other recent games I can think of. _childDocuments_.review: I think this is one of the best games I've gotten into in a good while, its design nails a lot of things incredibly well into place. The standard weapon upgrades seem to mostly fall somewhere on a line between DPS and survivability, both being valid choices. The dripfeed of content via additional overclocks for your weapons makes it worth to wait for each cycle of weeklies and deep dives. _childDocuments_.review: Dwarves4 player Co-opSynthwave musicAlien bug swarmsIf any of that sparks your interest, then look no further! Deep Rock is a great little co-op game. Its simple, and yet, amazingly fun.  This game doesnt try to be some big, complex game with intricate, detailed systems that you have to learn. Its not an rpg. Its not a moba, or a battle royal. Its not a survival game (unless you could surviving waves of alien bugs). What it IS, however, is fun.I was gonna post a long review about what this game is about. I realized it was pointless, since what you see in the trailers IS basically what the game is all about. Mining, exploring, fighting bugs, and dwarves being dwarves. That it? Pretty much. Why is that special? Easy answer: Its Fun.The game is solidly made. No crashes. Very few bugs in its current state. Devs adding new features and functionality with each frequent patch.PROSSee the list at the top Ive had a total blast playing the game so far.CONSMy only concern is with the progression system. Each item only has 2-3 upgrades for it. After that, there is nothing else to progress towards outside of cosmetic changes. This worries me additionally because if progression stops so soon, then can we really expect the games challenge level to increase beyond a certain point?I really want the devs to be open and let us know what they have planned for this in the game. Will each of the 4 characters be able to buy and equip different items? IE: multiple types of pick axes? Will there be multiple tiers of upgrades per item, so you dont "cap out" 1 week after playing? Etc etc.Overall, for 25 bucks, you can easily get multiple hours of fun. If you are looking for a game with a story, or a large open world, or in depth RPG elements, then look elsewhere. EDIT: My concerns arent really a CON anymore. The devs are doing an amazing job beefing up the progression system, and there is still lots more to come.

_childDocuments_.review: Deep Rock Galactic is the single best co-op shooter game I've ever played, and one of the best co-op games released within the past decade.  I don't make this statement lightly, having put hundreds of hours into Minecraft, Destiny, and other cooperative games, but Deep Rock Galactic has fun cooperative gameplay built into its very bones.  GENERAL GAMEPLAY:In DRG, players take on the roles of dwarves in the employ of a galactic mining company.  They embark on missions in teams of up to four, venturing deep into various underground biomes to complete objectives on procedurally-generated randomized maps.  ALL TERRAIN is fully destructible, and players are equipped with a 3D map that updates as they explore the level.  No two missions are the same, and learning to perform the duties of your class in any environment is just part of the charm.  But beware - the omnipresent darkness hides swarms of insectoid horrors, lethal plant life, unstable geology, cliffs, lava, poison, radiation, and goop.  Lots of goop.  Fortunately, players can be revived by teammates (or by their companion drone when solo) to prevent mission failure.  Stick together, play it safe, get out alive.DARKNESS:You're a dwarf.  You work underground.  It's dark down there.  Like, REALLY DARK.  With the occasional exception of a glowing plant or volcanic vent, you have to provide your own light.  Players have a headlamp that dimly illuminates their immediate surroundings, and have a recharging supply of flares that provide better illumination, but are temporary.  Managing your light and not getting lost in the dark is one of the most important parts of DRG gameplay, and one of the most fun things about it as well.CLASSES:Players can play as four different classes: Driller, Engineer, Gunner, and Scout.  Each class has tools and weapons unique to itself, these dictate the class's role and playstyle.  There are six major slots: main weapon, side weapon, mobility tool, utility tool, grenade/throwable, and armor frame.  Each weapon has two major options, throwables have three options, and every option has a customization tree.  Every player begins with access to a functional basic loadout, and options and customizations are unlocked linearly through playtime.  This design structure leads to each class having a wide variety of possible builds, while remaining solidly rooted in its core gameplay.THE DRILLER:If you enjoy getting your hands dirty up close and personal with the irascible inhabitants of the underground realms, the Driller is for you.  - FLAMETHROWER / CRYOGUN - Your main weapon provides massive crowd control against large hordes of enemies.  You can also unlock a cryo gun that freezes enemies solid for maximum denial.- POWER DRILL - Your mobility tool is a huge drill that lets you tunnel easily through the map, making shortcuts and walkways wherever you need.- SATCHEL CHARGE - Your utility tool is an oversized brick of high-explosive that can be deployed for lethal effect.THE ENGINEER:This class provides creative solutions with its arsenal of weaponized gadgetry.  - SHOTGUN / ARC THROWER - Your main weapons provide potent short-range area denial, with the more advanced Arc Thrower slicing through any number of enemies, with various interesting upgrade effects.- PLATFORM LAUNCHER - Your mobility tool allows you to create platforms, stairs, bridges, towers, bunkers, and more, to cross gaps, reach objectives, and escape from danger.- GUN TURRET - Your utility tool creates an automatic gun turret that provides reasonable damage at extremely long range, and provides a great safety net against unseen threats.THE GUNNER:This class likes guns.  Really, REALLY big guns.  If you sexually identify as an AC-130, this is the class for you.- MINIGUN / AUTOCANNON - The gunner's main weapon provides sustained, effective, armor-piercing, suppressive fire.  The minigun is more flexible, while the autocannon is arguably more powerful.- ZIPLINE LAUNCHER - Your mobility tool allows you to jetpack away from problems by creating permanent, point-to-point ziplines that you and your teammates can ride.  Take to the skies!- SHIELD GENERATOR - This throwable device projects a large shield that protects your team from most threats temporarily.  Comes in clutch ALL the time.THE SCOUT:The most mobile of the four classes, the scout floats through the air with the greatest of ease.  Imagine if the TF2 Scout, Junkrat and Widowmaker from Overwatch, and that chick from Mirror's Edge had a baby.  That's the scout.- BOOMSTICK - The scout's guns are the least impactful as regards damage, but they provide powerful secondary effects such as double-jumping and slow-motion-mode.- GRAPPLING HOOK - Pull yourself at high speed towards a point with this flexible mobility tool.  Great for reaching tough spots, launching yourself in huge arcs, AND it negates fall damage.- FLARE LAUNCHER - In DRG, the darkness is a dwarf's greatest enemy - and you've got the remedy.  This utility tool allows you to set large flares into any surface, brightly illuminating a huge area for a couple of minutes.PROGRESSION:Deep Rock Galactic is a game anybody can jump into and start rockin' and stonin' immediately.  All four classes are available with basic options from the get-go, and players can unlock a huge variety of cosmetic items, gear modifications, and (eventually) powerful augmentations called Overclocks, all through simply playing the game.  There are no microtransactions - the game features an IRL merch store with shirts, mugs, posters, and so on, all created by members of the DRG community.  This seriously is the most wholesome game I've seen in years, and it has captured my heart like the Minecraft days of old.ENDGAME:It's all about the Matrix Cores, baby.  In DRG, you can complete assignments and challenging missions called Deep Dives to earn blank "cores".  You can then complete an optional event inside a normal mission to "infuse" the core, which provides you with three options.  Once a core is infused, you can return to your home base to "forge" it (using resources collected naturally throughout your missions) to craft a usable item.  Gameplay items created this way are called Overclocks, and provide unique modifications to your weaponry.  You can also get the best cosmetics (read: BEARDS) this way.BEER:Your home base has a bar.  The bar has a robot bartender.  The robot bartender serves beer.  Beer is purchased using resources found during missions, and you can unlock interesting beers such as "Smart Stout", which grants any dwarf who drinks it a burst of insight and compels them to babble it out immediately.  Feeling dizzy?  Drink a Leaf-Lover's Special, a namby-pamby drink made by those wimpy elves to avoid being drunk on the job.IN CONCLUSION:Get this mf game.  Seriously, do it.Rock and Stone!Get this game.

_childDocuments_.review: There's no way around it. Deep Rock Galactic Corporation is probably the worst company in the universe.At first you may think the salary + benefits is beyond competitive, but you'll soon realize that practically every equipment upgrade, and even promotions, have to be paid for out of your own pocket.Not only that, but even with the insane profits that Deep Rock Galactic reaps from the hard work of thousands of dwarves, they are too cheapto implement basic safety measures to reduce risk and fatality. For instance, the Drop Pod and M.U.L.E are not even equipped with the most basic version of a defensive turret. We can be lucky they decidedto install some on the Minehead at least. For some reason, the Minehead is even equipped with oxygen tanks for low oxygen environments. How thoughtful!Yet, no effort has been made to actually allow employees to use carryable oxygentanks or breathing masks for these dangerous missions.Deep Rock also has no qualms allowing inexperienced miners to delve into dangerous Hazard 5 areas, yet will refuse non-promoted employees to takepart in their "Deep Dive" operations. Considering you have to pay for your ownpromotions, this essentially means you have to pay to work for them.Finally, I should mention that Deep Rock treats its employees as completely expendable. Upon completion of any mission, Mission Control will give a few minutes for everyone to find their way back to the Drop Pod. If you don'tmake it in time, you WILL be left behind.Let's not forget, by the way, you will be living on a space rig away from friendsand family for the entire duration of your employment. And if you signed thatcontract without reading the fine print, well, that will be forever.

_childDocuments_.review: DRG mixes exploration of procedurally-generated caves with mining minerals, while also fending off alien bug creatures and completing various objectives.You can both start your own mission and have randoms join you, group up with friends, join others' lobbies, and even play Solo, with a lovely robotic companion to assist you.There are 5 difficulties you can play the game on (ranging from very easy to pretty hard, the harshest of which needs to be unlocked via an assignment) and, as you play, you'll be able to improve your performance via upgrading weapons and tools, and by unlocking perks for some extra benefits.The gameplay loop at its core doesn't change much, as you progress: you go in, explore, do the objectives and kill bugs with a bunch of fine dwarven pals. The several biomes and mission types, along with the procedurally generated maps and all the random players you can meet, though, make it so every mission can be an unique, and fun, experience (this has been the case with me, a least!).I personally find the game to be very charming, with all the sights it can provide and the various, lovely aspects one can enjoy (even just the dwarves talking is music to mah ears :D), on top of being easy to pick up to simply play one or two missions, or play for hours on end.Definitely recommend givin' it a shot. _childDocuments_.review: I have nothing but good things to say about this game, the developers, and community.DRG is fun solo. _childDocuments_.review: I have constantly recommended this game and been hopeful for its future until this very moment. As it stands, the developers seem to be making the ABSOLUTE worst decision they could make, which is to say they are attempting to market this game's concept and its universe as a brand of sorts, while simultaneously putting this game on life support to account for split focus. Even when the wait between content updates was already incredibly long in contrast to what they barely delivered in new content, the new "Season" has now been stated to release in the middle of 2024, as they shift their focus to other projects, and they have already stated that it will not deliver to expectations from how long it will take to come out. Even disregarding that this game itself is going to suffer, the projects they are working on instead of this masterpiece also do not in the slightest resemble anything close to the appeal and charm of this game, at least in my opinion. While I gained much enjoyment from this game, I do not believe I, nor any enjoyer of this game, will purchase these "spinoffs" if they lack the gameplay and charm that truly made DRG successful and unique. Though I hope I will be proven wrong upon their release, it makes it even worse to know this game will stall and burn for future prospects that are not even guaranteed to be appealing to me, or frankly even anything close to successful given how, in my opinion, dissimilar they look in comparison to DRG. In conclusion, I cannot recommend this game in good conscience knowing that the developers seem to be all but abandoning it outright, so if you're looking for a fun time and not a long time this game will be 100% worth it, but as it stands it's all downhill now. I urge the developers reconsider their decisions, and I deeply regret not having played more when its future was bright.

_childDocuments_.review: Maybe you're old, maybe you remember Red Faction, or Red Faction 2, where you were shooting people in a mine, and could dig holes in terrain to get anywhere, but it didn't really matter much. It was mostly just a gimmick.Here, digging is the game.There's definitely something satisfying about just breaking things, and that's largely what you're tasked to do in various ways in Deep Rock Galactic, usually just to mine, but sometimes to lay pipe or fuel a vehicle, while waves of bugs descend upon you to harass you. Sometimes there are big bugs that are bosses. But fighting is a side activity to liven things up. Different characters have complementary abilities, helping you get at hard-to-reach ore or to navigate the mine more effectively.Though aspects of the gameplay are similar to crafting and survival games, you're not building a fort or trying to fill your stomach. While gathering stuff is useful for upgrades, once you plateau with those, it quickly becomes another form of currency for cosmetic upgrades and the occasional mug of beer.To some extent, Deep Rock defines a game done as a labor of love, festooned with the technically unnecessary delightful, like a home base with its jukebox, toyetic beers, a barrel-kicking minigame, and more shenanigans to mess around with between rounds. It could be easily passed off as fluff, but part of the appeal of Deep Rock is the obvious fun the developers have been having with the environments and gimmicks.And moreover, it's seen regular, free updates in addition to reasonably-priced cosmetic DLC. I personally find the addition of a Battle Pass to be generally exhausting in its demands, but at the same time it's completely free. In many ways, Deep Rock borrows elements of "live service" games without the strict, predatory money-grubbing. Though it uses some of the tools of larger development, they're put there for those that enjoy that sort of thing rather than to necessarily reach for your wallet. And while it runs repetitive, it's got a fairly satisfying loop that can provide enough memorable experiences from time to time to stay lively.Overall, Deep Rock is probably one of the best team shooters out there right now, but it's an overall strong experience. Mind, it's an experience to be built with friends; there's little meaningful narrative, and the unlocks are modest and drip-fed. But the *game* itself is strong, and that's what keeps me dipping back in. Though I don't obsess over it, it's a fun planet to stop by in from time to time.Put in over a hundred and fifty hours, near universally as engineer, to a silver rank, generally at mid-to-high difficulties with two or three friends, along with various events, mission types, and gimmicks.

_childDocuments_.review: Ladies and Gentlemen, you have just stumbled upon one of the most addicting games, and who better to tell you about it than a random dude on the internet who just started playing the game not even 3 weeks ago and has already logged just under 200 hours. "Rock and Stone Forever!"     Picture this: you and the boys all load the game up for the first time, you all join the host right away (if you skip the tutorial), you select your mission then you and the boys hop on the drill, next thing you know your in a cave 10.000 meters below the surface of an alien planet. You and your fellow dwarfs with pic-axes in hand head deeper into the caves in search of precious rocks and stones. All is calm, then all of a sudden hordes of alien creatures start crawling down the walls and out of the ground. Now its up to you and your fellow dwarfs to use your different strengths and tools to work together as a team, defeat the enemy with your futuristic weapons and make it to extraction with all of your goodies. "ROCK AND STONE!"      There's more to this game than you might think. For starters before each mission you get to chill in this really nice lobby that has a bar, dancefloor, and a minigame. Theres also a massive window that lets you see out into space. They built in a really nice modding system so you can mod your weapons as you level up a character to do more damage and they were also cool enough to include a perking system that shares between all your characters. If your one of those gamers who care more about how they look than how good they are at a game then don't worry cause there's also a shop in the lobby that lets you purchase vanity items to make your dude look like a badass.       All in all its an amazing game, I applaud the developers of this game who are still working hard to update and add new things to the game, as well as listening to what the community says. I highly recommend this game to everyone. Try this game and I can promise you will love it. "COME ON GUYS, ROCK AND STONE!"

_childDocuments_.review: ROCK AND STONETO THE BONEThis extremely well polished game is super fun to play, even moreso with friends (and sometimes randoms), and has what I believe is a very good flexibility for player skill and progression. Squads up to 4 dwarves (players) go cave-spelunking, armed with guns, explosives, and gadgets while they complete various missions. There are 5 difficulty ratings (called Hazard levels), where haz1/2 feels very much like just playing a dwarven version of Minecraft, while haz3+ feel like you're constantly fighting off a swarm of pissed off bugs that you're definitely not invading their homeworld because you want those precious minerals. There's a helluva lot of customization in the game, both cosmetic and equipment modification. Some can be unlocked with in-game credits, others need to be found through more difficult methods. The game feels rewarding to play, engaging, and I haven't seen anything I could consider to be predatory practices by the developers. I love this game, and you should definitely check it out!FOR KARLLLL!

This makes the game feel very tedious as there is no way to do assignments quickly if everyone is at a different level. I still highly recommend the game, but that is my main annoyance with the game right now.

_childDocuments_.review: Deep Rock Galactic is what I would consider a perfect video game. It has everything that I like: Shooting satisfying guns. Grinding for loot. Advanced movement mechanics. Appropriate use of procedural generation to create unique experiences and infinite replayability. Genuinely funny characters with rich personalities. Intense gameplay that requires your full attention, with perfectly paced downtime to get your bearings. Teamwork that is heavily suggested but not required in order to succeed. An uncharacteristically friendly community (I play in open lobbies 99% of the time, and I can count every toxic encounter I've had in six years on one hand.) Loadout variety. Theory-crafting and metagames. Incredible atmosphere. A distinct and unique visual style. And a banger soundtrack that I will never turn down in the audio settings. Always blasting that ♥♥♥♥.I love dropping into a cave on Hazard 5, the doors opening to what I can only describe as "Bug Normandy" and diving headfirst into the chaos. I love single-handedly cutting through an entire swarm with Gemini sentries and a tricked out Breach Cutter. I love sitting on top of Dorretta and chucking grenades behind her into the tunnel filled to the brim with bugs and watching them all explode. I love setting up a Driller bunker and filling the chokepoint with green sludge. I love using the RJ-250 to not only nuke an entire group of Grunts, but to fly away to the other side of the cave and placing a fall-damage-reducing platform under my feet just before I hit the ground. I love when I'm just about to get into the drop pod with 60 seconds left, but the Greenbeard Gunner goes down 150 meters away... and suddenly the objective switches from escaping with my life to a full fledged rescue mission because NO DWARF LEFT BEHIND. There are countless things in DRG that are so incredibly memorable, so exhilarating, and so satisfying... I'm constantly blown away by how much content can be extracted from this game.DRG is the one game that I can always come back to when every other one of my favorite games has some kind of botched update, or fails spectacularly in some way. Over the last 6 years, I've been able to know that if there's nothing good to play tonight, I can always hop on Deep Rock. It's consistently been an S+ tier game for as long as I can remember, and that's an incredible feat in today's gaming landscape. If Team Fortress 2 hadn't already taken my heart and locked it away long ago, Deep Rock Galactic would sit at #1 on my list, no contest. It's just so incredibly good, and the experience never gets old. And they're STILL updating it and adding QoL features that somehow make it even better. Seriously, GSG is quite possibly the most underrated game development team in the history of video games. Deep Rock just stays winning, forever. Rock and Stone!

_childDocuments_.review: It is a great game to play with friends, I never had a coop game with this much teamplay and le epic funny moments, while also giving a lot of variety with every new mission, which starts with the environments. In return most weapons have depth and can have different playstyles. Add random events and different mission types to the mix and every mission has it's own unique moments. The movement might need some getting used to, because when jumping and in the air you have momentum and can't just immediately change directions mid air.Now for the really fun part: the developers continue to support the game and everything is free. The DLCs are just cosmetics for those who want to give more money. Ingame nothing can be paid for with real money, but the weapons you want to play for a certain class can be unlocked pretty easily and the rest is mostly cosmetics. Every 6 months or so a new season comes and brings updates like new biomes, new weapons, new events etc, but also a whole new season pass.There is certainly a lot to unlock and a lot of grind behind it, but you do not need so sink in a lot of hours to have fun. I would say none at all, because the gameplay itself is fun, but you will fail and have stressful moments. You are mining on an unknown planet and bugs keep coming out of every dark corner after all. But there are 5 different difficulties and one of them will be a good point to start.Note for Soloplayers: you absolutely can play this alone and a competent little robot will accompany you, but it is more fun with real people, which I heard there are a lot of friendly ones in the server browser, but I can't say much about that, as I mostly play with friends or the little robot.

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun cooperative gameplay loop.  Community is 99% non-toxic.  Cooperation is rewarded. Biomes are diverse and have character. SFX and graphics are good.  Difficulty can some times spike in fun and unexpected ways creating frantic "save the day" moments, and you don't really lose anything for losing.My biggest issues with the game are: 1) **The U.I. experience.** Its clashing menu layouts hurt the eye to look at and don't communicate their information well to new players.  Additionally the lack of information on certain topics like stats and discrete information about how much of a boost this buff or that debuff is. For example,  I'm 200 hours in and I think I know roughly how much HP bugs have?2) **The cosmetics grind.**  So you unlock cosmetics as you play which then must be bought from an in-game store and purchased for *each* of your character classes if you want to don them.  Leaving the extra purchasing aside, I feel like if devs set free this part of the game; made all the cosmetics available for purchase from the get-go, and unattached them from the core gameplay loops such as the Forge, Lost Equipment, and Assignments, they could focus more energy into the *hard work* of tinkering and polishing  the core game which is, i assume, what we're all really here for.  I hate to put too fine a point on it but I feel disrespected when a game deliberately wastes my time by dangling a silly hat or haircut in front of me on the end of a stick and making it part of core gameplay elements.  It's not entirely mandatory to chase the stick, but its not entirely optional either.  In a broader sense, I don't want to feel like a hamster chasing food pellets so that the time i play the game can be prolonged before I'm SHOWN the cool stuff that was designed.  It smells like bad leftover design psychology from MMOs on a subscription and in DRG I see it as a sort creative procrastination- avoiding some needed polish to an already fun game.

_childDocuments_.review: Very good, 10/10. Lots interesting things to see and do. Between randomly generated maps, 4 character classes, 8 different map environs, 7 different primary mission objectives and half dozen secondary mission objectives, 8 different mission anomaly conditions, and 9 special hazard conditions, (all of which mix and match separately) there is always something new(ish) to do. The game design strongly encourages and rewards well behaved, co-operative play. And the playerbase does seem to get it. Online players are friendly and helpful. I have almost never had to finish a mission solo if I didn't want to. Although, it is possible to play entirely solo if you wish, all of the content is accessable to solo only players.There are cosmetic DLC packs, but no in-game microtransactions, no pay to win of any kind, and a history of numerous (and free) content and support updates. The developers are clearly strongly committed to a do-no-harm business model.My only complaint is that there are no female dwarves. No female character models, and no female voice acting. It ain't 1932 anymore. There should be female dwarves in the company.

_childDocuments_.review: One of my all time favorite games on the PC.  Developers keep adding new stuff.  Not at a break neck speed of big studios mind you, so that's ok.  Slow and steady progress.  No battle passes so far, so that's good, lol. (edit:  now they have battle passes.  but they are the best, it's free.  things you don't get are put in with the other random cosmetics when the season ends, so you can earn things from seasons you missed. honestly the best type of battle passes I've seen.)The game's humor is funny and doesn't take itself too seriously.  If you like dwarfs/squats, and you want to go against good value tyranids, this game is pretty good.  This game is all about team work.  The classes really can compliment each other if people work together.  Grab a copy for yourself and friend and dive in.  I suggest green beards start with the gunner or driller classes as they have some heavier weapons.  But check them all out for yourself.   For new players.  There are 5 different difficulties in the game, and I suggest you do not play at difficulty 4 or above before you get a class to level 25 to unlock perks and get a feel for how the game actually goes.  I've seen many reviews for this game where people say it was too hard, but that's the thing, the levels actually matter.  Also pay attention to the mission moddifers.  Some missions might have more boss bugs, and some might have you die for lack of oxygen.  Which could really make your playing experience frustrating when you're new. Most importantly this is a team game.  At higher difficulties you really have to know how to play as a team and develop some good habits and strategies.  Your teams success or failure will hinge on that at higher difficulties.  So again, if you just start out, don't go full on hardest difficulty.  You won't have a fun time. One of the great things you can do later on is customize your guns with over clocks, which will give you some added boosts to your playstyle to hep take on those hard difficulties  One of my biggest gripes about this game is that it does take a long time to earn these and they are random.  So you have to really grind for them and hope you get the right one.  =[ROCK AND STONE MINERS]=

_childDocuments_.review: Down down underground,Go two Dwarves with rocks to pound.One he heard a shrieking sound,Sounds like a Leech the other found.Spiders biting on our toes,Noxious gasses in our nose,Shoot a bug and up he blows,That's the way our mining goes.Lost my partner to a glitch,Down in caverns black as pitch.He's now laying in a ditch,But I don't care, I'm filthy rich!This pretty much sums up my gameplay of Deep Rock Galactic. While there may not be a lot of content as yet, what there is has a strange addictive quality to it.   The unpredictability of the ever changing procedurally generated landscapes is what gives this game, for me, a terrifying charm. Just when I think I have the hang of it, (which translates as managing to complete a mission without dying once) and I confidently venture forth into another beautifully rendered cavern, a swarm of arachnids swallows me up in a sea of spiky legs and chomping fangs.   Playing with a partner is also no guarantee of success, as my friend will attest to...though to be fair we do seem to spend a lot of time trying to knock each other off cliffs and into fire pits.   In summery, this game while still needing work, is an excellent addition to my collection of fun and rewarding games to play. I look forward to future updates and content, but in the meantime please excuse me while I go pack my pickaxes and bug repellent..theres GOLD in them thar hills!

_childDocuments_.review: Dwarves. Mining. Hordes of alien bugs. Metagame of beers and cosmetics. Unique visual style. That should give you an idea of this game's unique selling proposition. Deep Rock Galactic is a rising star in the co-op shooter genre and boy has my journey with it been fun. Take it from someone who has played co-op games in abundance for a decade, this game holds its own in gameplay and packs an unbelievable amount of charm in every aspect of the game. Be it the grunts and shouts of the dwarves or the descriptions of cosmetics that reference everything from movies to games.Now the gameplay will either make or break this game for you. It's a lot of shooting, running and chopping away at mineral veins. But leaving it at that would do a disservice to what this game has to offer. The missions happen in procedurally generated caves that have varying effects based on a few regions on the planet of Hoxxes IV. Enemies come in all sorts of shapes and sizes, some missions even focus on taking out the biggest and baddest Dreadnoughts. You also have a fun metagame of collecting Matrix Cores, which are gained by doing special  mission chains and later charged in the regular missions with unique mini games, and rare minerals, which you can then use to buy modifications to your gear and pimp your dwarf with some dazzling facial hair respectively. Try the game out and see if you enjoy the core gameplay loop. If you do, there are four classes for you to master and it will take you potentially hundreds of hours to reach the highest promotion tiers with all of them. Each class has a different playstyle, including multiple weapons, and switching between them can keep the gameplay refreshing, should you get bored of playing one way for too long. Playing with friends is always fun, but I've enjoyed Solo missions as well. The feeling of wandering the caves alone, or with your trusty robot helper Bosco, which you can bring along only for Solo runs, is quite different to the usual hubbub caused by multiple dwarves firing relentlessly into enemy swarms while taunting and cursing at the alien bast*rds (and allies).Deep Rock Galactic is a fun game for those that are looking for a new shooter experience and the devs are hard at work improving it with every update. Considering this game is still in Early Access, it's a bloody good purchase. You can always refund it should you find the gameplay unsatisfactory, but I implore you to try out all of the classes before doing that. You might yet find a really fun playstyle that fits you. You will be pleased... and so will Management.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a testament to what every early access game should be. I am honestly blown away that a game of this quality with a dev team this caring has come out in 2020. I have found myself saying "I LOVE THIS DEVELOPER" more times than i can count.For what looks like such a simple game it keeps surprising me with little details that i'm sure i still haven't found all of with "only" 80hours of playtime. This game is truly a masterpiece of the co-op genre created by a developer that clearly loves their game and their community. I highly recommend this game to anyone looking for a fun addictive mining & bug smashing simulator (sorry little loot bug). Now get out there and mine some rocks, but don't forget to have a beer first!

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not one to usually write detailed reviews but for this game...I MUST!Before buying this game (I bought it in early access), I was slightly thrown off by the screenshots and videos of the gameplay and I thought to myself, this is just gonna be one of those brainless run around shoot and repeat kinda game with graphics that looks mediocre by some indie developers. Oh Boi was I wrong...The 4 different classes [Scout-Driller-Gunner-Engineer] each has their own set of weapons, grenades, traversal tool and more. For example, the scout is able to use a grappling hook to navigate hard to reach places, as well as provide flare support to light up the very dark cave while Gunner has a zipline that allows his team to cross high or low areas where you could fall and die and the gunner has a shield that provides a small aoe of (almost) impenetrable defense for a short time.Your role is key and what is your role exactly? Even tho each class has certain playstyles, let's talk about how you have SO MANY WEAPON UPGRADES TO CHOOSE FROM. You would have to pick strategically (or as you personally prefer) the upgrades you would like for your guns, armor, type of grenade, traversal tool and others. You are free to change your upgrades at anytime after you use your resources to unlock it. Maybe the stage involves you killing a huge boss and you need armor breaking, that's the perk to go for! Or maybe you need to clear large amounts of waves, you could get piercing bullets to cut through multiple enemies.The upgrades I mentioned may sound basic but trust me, there is ALOT more to it. Especially once you reach level 25 and unlock the "endgame", you have countless amounts of mods that could turn your gun to something completely different. (I have a mod for my shotgun that makes my scout fly upwards everytime I shoot downwards LOL) I also have a mod for my engineer which makes the laser like gun's projectiles come back to the gun after shooting it out, essentially damaging the enemies twice.There is so much more than just running and shooting and reaching checkpoints. You have many different objectives and secondary objectives that do not feel repetitive. There are many different biomes that each has their unique set of creatures and elemental damages. Every round you play will not feel the same as the system's randomizer changes the way the caves looks and how often the enemy spawns, what type of enemies spawns etc....every time you enter a new round.This game's soundtracks are also great! The synth style really gets you in the moment when a wave spawns or when a certain big bug spawns. This game got me into this genre and that says alot.In terms of the graphics, it has improved alot since i played in early access. The lighting, models, art style, is so beautiful and guess what? Would you believe me if I told you that this entire game uses less than 3GB of your storage size? For mine, it is only 1.88GB specifically. At first I thought there was some error or I am only downloading an update patch or something but nope. That's the total game size.The beginning of the game is probably confusing for many people but do not give up so fast! The game is much simpler than you think and if you put in some time into it, you will see why this game has such a positive rating on steam :DAside from the amazing gameplay and humor in the game, I truly enjoy two things that I find to be rare in other multiplayer communities.1. The community, Deep Rock has one of the most nicest and helpful community I've ever been in. The gamers here wants a good time and that's exactly what they will get! I've learnt alot playing with others and through their official discord, played with one of the discord mods. He was so friendly and taught us many things about the game, talked about few things the devs kept or took out in the past and how the game is going overall.2. THE DEVS! You can just see that there is so much love poured into this game. All the way from the beginning, the devs have not stopped bringing additional content and listens to the interests of the community. This game is not pay to win and all the dlcs you see in this game is a way to support the devs. I bought the supporter upgrade because I feel like the devs deserves it. They deserve the support and I will happily recommend this game to anyone who games.ROCK AND STONE FOR KARL!!!!!(Side note for those who has motion sickness)There is a setting to turn down camera shake and head bobbing. Couple friends of mine including myself has motion sickness. The settings in the game made the game playable for us once we adjusted the settings.

_childDocuments_.review: "There are many ways you can judge a game, but 2 of the most common are looking at a game as art, or as a product" -Joseph Anderson (paraphrased)Deep Rock Galactic, as a product, is perfect. If you play video games, there is no better use of $30 than buying DRG. Unfortunately, the formatting of steam's reviews and how they are presented requires me to approach this as i am to provide this information to the people who may want to hear it.As the game is at this moment in time, it packs more punch and value than the most expensive games money can buy, and in some cases, the hardware they run on as well.Before i say anything else, buy the game. play 100+ hours. go enjoy yourself. these issues will likely not resonate with you until you have 1000 hours or have played for more than a year. I won't explain every issue from the perspective of launching the game for the first time, this is not to be rude to new players, but rather to protect them from coming to negative conclusions about the game in ways that won't affect them for hundreds of hours. Despite all the praise I will sing to get you to experience this game, the game is sick. Not in the good way. Bad practices, minor flaws, and misguided attention have crippled the progression of DRG and left it in the shadow of its potential.Let's start with who this review is written by, the "hundred hour player" The progression of DRG is exponential and linear for around 25 hours, and then becomes fully lateral upon reaching the overclock phase of the game. Once you have your first OC you have effectively reached the end of progression. Yes, you will spend hundreds more hours unlocking EVERY OC, but without taking rng into account, you have an OC slot filled, ergo you are as strong as you will get.And that's where the endgame starts AND ends, 25 hours in, with that first overclock. You've seen it all. Hundreds upon hundreds of cosmetics are out there rattling around, but what the game is asking of you to get them is nothing beyond what you've experienced already.The reason i refer to this as the hundred-hour play is expanding those 25 hours to all 4 classes. even that is probably overestimating, as you will see nothing new by promoting the next 3 classes.All of that progression, OC unlocking, 100 hours amounts to nothing more than playing the same content the same way and honing your skills at playing the same content the same the same way.The fix to this isn't new missions, more OCs, more random events, or more bloat in existing systems. The fix is asking players to interact with the existing game in new ways, ways they wouldn't unless asked.Add 50 new items to cargo crates, nothing has changed. Ask a play to beat a mission under a certain time, without taking damage, without playing in multiplayer, and everything changes. The solution to the lateral endgame isn't more content to engage with or more random events polluting the caves. The solution is asking players to interact with existing content in new and creative ways.This isn't to say the game is drop dead boring at any point, it remains enjoyable far, far beyond the 100 hour mark. My point is the overall content density and at this moment in time, and developer effort, are entirely dislocated from where they need to be.The game was a 10/10 in 2019. but id go so far as to say that massively over saturating the amount of random events in an average mission has tarnished that score. Not to even mention the bloat that is currently in cargo crates, and matrix cosmetics for a player who hasn't even started yet. Bugshehe haha DRG is a bug filled game!!!!Yeah it is, and they're taking longer and longer to fix with every passing year. I think my favorite example is the visible hit box on 1 of the corrupter's 2 attacks. A glaringly obvious bug that was undeniably noticed before season 4 even went live.Would you like to guess how long a highly visible, egregious bug on season 4's flagship event took to fix? 75 days. Two and a half months, to disable a wire frame on a 3d model. Numerous patches were released in those 75 days. Say they had bigger fish to fry, but there's something to be said about the perception players have of the effort that was put into a particular piece of content.The fact the corrupter even shipped with such an inexcusable graphical error is one thing, but taking nearly half of season 4s runtime to be corrected is unfathomable from a QA standpoint. There's plenty of other bugs with a significantly stronger impact on the games course, armor break, Dreads, and hang-fire weapons in DDs to name a few. What concerns me more is how many attempts have to be taken to fix a bug. look at the last 30 patches, the amount of repeat customers is hard to understand as a player. if a patch that presumable took 2 weeks to come out contains 5 items, you would expect all of those fixes to work, but that tends not to be the case.The Client ExperienceIt's hard to explain how bad this feels, but if you've played DRG for any amount of time i promise you know what im referring to. The better you get at the game, the more you take advantage of and rely on split second tricks and inputs to elevate not only your output, but enjoyment of the game play.As a non-host player, many of these skills become inaccessible and extremely frustrating to lose access to. Movement, animation cancels, and at its worst even your aim can be degraded to an instantly perceptible degree that is outright unacceptable for those who are familiar with how the game plays in solo or as the host.I consider the game to be a notably less enjoyable experience as a non host player even when playing with someone who lives less that 10 miles away, this decay of control occurs at even the lowest latency. For a game that is not only marketed, but praised by its community as a co op experience, it blows my mind how much playing with other players damages either your, or their enjoyment of the games while you play.Speaking of the community, we should talk about the Hive Mind.Disclaimer up front, just because you partake in a lil RP or press v doesn't mean you are part of the problem. The point here is that your average member of this games cult like following will jump to the defense of those who ARE the problem.I've been called every slur you can imagine for not saving Doretta, I've seen people who write negative reviews receive death threats, and even a redditor dig through a modded player's post history in order to abuse them with extremely personal traumatic experiences.The overt negativity and accepted hatred of personal attacks against anyone who isn't playing the game the "right" way is mind boggling. Do i go against the grain? Absolutely, I understand that there will be some push back, but "♥♥♥ leaflover" can only get lobbed at me in game chat so many times before I start to notice a pattern.Play our way, or else.I understand the silent majority doesn't do this. but they certainly don't do anything to reprimand the people who are slinging hate against people who don't play like that majority *shrug*  The drop in content quality and tempo since season 1, the ever increasing amount of unfixed bugs, the unfun and unituitive game mechanics like rockpox, the lack of meaningful game change for players with more than 100 hoursThere's a lot more to talk about, but that's all I have the heart to go through for now. I'll reiterate. This game was as close to perfect as any game has ever been, but as time goes on, it is moving further away from that accolade.Buy it if you haven't already, and forget everything you just read until you're sick of it.

_childDocuments_.review: Dwarves.  Dwarves in space.  Space Dwarves...Space Doorves!You work for the Deep Rock Galactic Mineral Trading Company, utilizing the latest and greatest in space excavation mining equipment, with one simple goal in mind:  mine the minerals of the planetoid, Hoxxes IV.  No one else has rights to the planetoid but you and your dwarven brethren and the company you work for.Dive deep into subterranean caverns of various flora and fauna, and combat the natural insectoid inhabitants of Hoxxes IV who want nothing more than to chew on your doorvan keester.  Find the myriad of minerals around these deep, dark caverns, collect them, and extract them...or die trying for the glory of Deep Rock Galactic!Play by yourself with a little robot companion named BOSCO, or bring along up to three other dwarven friends to face off against the worst of your nightmares:  corporate greed.  Equip yourself as up to four classes:*Heavy Gunner, using big guns, ziplines, and explosives.*Engineer, assisting your teammates using a platform-scaling foam gun, shotguns and advanced technology weapons, and maneuverable turrets.*Driller, with drilling arm-cannons to quickly dig tunnels through the depths, and a host of explosives, fire and cryo weaponry.*Scout, with speed and maneuverability as your skill set and survival, using a grappling hook to reach high-or-far spots in a zip, precision-based weaponry, and support-based throwables.As you play, level up your chosen classes, buy perks for various playstyles.  When you reach Level 25, take on a quest to Prestige your chosen Doorve (reset to Level 1, but keep all bought perks and item/weapon upgrades).  Choose from a variety of mission types:  from general mining, drilling station defense, to extractions of specific resources, and even hunting the biggest, baddest baddies on Hoxxes IV.So jump on in, dive deep down...and GET YOUR ROCK ON, DOORVES! \o/

_childDocuments_.review: This co-op FPS offers a nice combination of mining and shooty-shooty, kill-kill gameplay. Basically, you and up to 3 other dwarves vs various sorts of space bugs... crawly and flying things, both big and small, collecting as much resources as you can along the way. Team play is very important, especially on the higher difficulties (Hazard levels). Solo play is also a viable option, should you prefer. You'll then be accompanied by a friendly, efficient and customizable flying robot companion named Bosco, as you head underground on your space adventures. Accepting available missions in the hub area (the space rig), which will set goals like f.e. collecting alien eggs or gathering rare minerals, will take you underground to the mission zones via your drop pod. These zones are randomly generated each time the galactic map updates (every 30 minutes), so the map layout is always a surprise. Most of what you can see in the levels can be destroyed by pickaxe, drills or stuff that goes boom. This means you can do interesting stuff like making shortcuts to objectives or creating tactically advantageous defense spots, in case enemy swarms come for you (spoiler: they will come for you). The difficulty of a mission depends on the chosen Hazard level, yet also scales based on the number of players. Mission attempts grant XP, which will lead to level-ups. Reaching new levels and playing certain mission types gradually unlock new weapons, gear effects and perks for your character of choice. The idea is to complete your mission goal fast, then reach your drop pod to gtfo while being chased by swarms of enemies. There's choices to be made though, as exploring more of the map can lead to finding loot or rare resources. The 4 available dwarves in DRG can be seen as classes, fulfilling specific roles, like supporting your team with tools and gadgets or simply bringing the pain. Installing additional effects on your gear for the first time will cost minerals, but the total amount of your resources will pile up as you complete missions and take stuff home as a team. There's various cosmetics as well, which can be bought by spending some of your gold at the shop on the space rig.The game's graphical style is very charming and will remind you of certain voxel-based games. Graphical effects and colours really add something to the overall atmosphere. The general tone can be described as light-hearted, yet DRG also leaves enough room to make you feel like an absolute badass during big action-heavy fights. The game's humorous quips, banter and yells will surely get a laugh or chuckle out of you. There's also amusing stuff you can do in the hub area, like kicking barrels through hoops, trying to break your high-score and getting drunk (in whichever order you prefer). Sound effects fit perfectly and the synth-heavy music (ambient tracks and seperate ones that will play the moment sh*t hits the fan) is rock solid. There's probably going to be some tunes stuck in your head when you're in bed trying to fall asleep. Things are kept fresh by offering the player weekly missions, which will reward you bonus minerals, cosmetic items and various schematics (the Forge on the space rig can be used to create items from these schematics). There's optional random stuff you can stumble upon as well, f.e. having to collect batteries to power an ammo crate elsewhere on the map, granting you nice unlocks upon completion.The endgame content offered are so-called Deep Dives, which will require you to complete a set of missions consecutively, gradually increasing in difficulty. These are refreshed and unique every week. The fun and interesting thing about these Dives is that your character's end-of-mission state (current health and ammo supply), plus the resources collected as a team, will transfer to the start of the next level of the Dive.The devs are currently still adding stuff to the game, like new mission, enemy and biome types. Plus, there's additional weaponry on the way sometime next year. The best online co-op FPS I've played thus far. You're in for countless hours of mining and bug squashing fun. The excellent random map generation keeps things infinitely interesting. Buy this title if you've enjoyed playing a game like Left 4 Dead and loved the intensity & team play aspect of it.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game!I waited until I got 100 hours of the game until I made a review and completed most of what the game offers. This game will give you more or less 30 hours of gameplay with new things to see and learn. After 30 hours you have seen enough to have seen it all. However this game has great replayability. There is still new things to try and good moments to be had when playing with other people. The caves are generated differently so it never gets super repetative, although the cave generation is not unique enough to after around 60 hours experience something completely different. So basically every mission will start to look the same after you've played it long enough. It's a intense FPS game if you boost up the difficulty. It offers various "warnings" with special things to make things harder (and easier) aswell as complexity, length and hazard levels of the missions.If you want to take it calm and just shoot a few things and mine or if you want swarms upon swarms of enemies to come at you with non-stop action then you can change the settings to have both. That said it is still a fast paced game. It offers various of customizations with gear, accessories, weapons, perks, levels of the character and prestige ranks (promotions). There is absolutely no (buy to win) things in this game, once you bought the game then you will be able to get everything available for you in the game by simply playing and leveling up.It is all in all a pretty addictive game. However all this being said some people might enjoy it for a longer time and others less so. I've got a few friends who loves the game and have played for hundreds of hours and I also have a few friends who played it here and there and gets tired of it. Often clocking between 30-100 hours for those who play less. It makes sense because around those amount of hours you've played enough to have seen it all. Is it worth it? Hell yeah, give it a try. You got my recommendation!

_childDocuments_.review: Me, trying DRG for the first time: ok, I'll play it a bit.Also me, : hang on...Scroll down to whatever interests you most:1) Highly addictive.2) Replay value.3) Graphics4) Achievements and grind.A lot of fun with friends and random players. Gameplay is simple: shoot enemies and collect objective minerals, but...under different circumstances DRG easily gets challenging.Play more and as your characters gain levels, upgrade gear, unlock perks, earn weapon modules. Then test them! Ride zip-lines across a wide cave, shooting flies. Falling in a hole? Active hovering boots! Freeze enemies and whack them with an axe. Throw a powerful c4 and obliterate entire cave (please don't!)So . From casual caves exploration and minerals hunting to complex pipes building and intensive escort duty with strategic defences. Now, . Different weapons and gears! Totally opposed styles. : frozen enemies dies faster, given platform allows to collect minerals in a jiffy, a decoy and shield give breathing room.Then, , each offering individual flora, environment and landscape: icy floor can suddenly shatter and swallow your team, magma streams will burn through armour, while in other areas you can use a flying creature to, ahem, fly around. i.e. low oxygen, low gravity, increased amount of certain bugs, rich minerals, etc,  consider players' factor (experienced and new ones), and you cant even expect what you get in a new mission.Fantastic job done in lights!If you dislike cubic models, I can assure that you'll get used to it real quick. Seriously, you get swarm to shoot! At the moment, a gold rank for every dwarf is required, where each takes roughly 80-100hrs to get there. I spent around 300hrs to make everyone golden.Somehow, there are more achievements with barrels (ride them, kick them, shove in specific areas), than enemies-kills related. Others, purely missions completion count.Overall, it's easily one of the best 4 player coop game with a great welcoming community. Grab it, hook your friends up and mine gold, spamming "For Rock and Stones!"
