_childDocuments_.review: Very fun co-op game with a lot of replayability, 4 classes with (currently) 3 primary and 3 secondary weapons each alongside various class specific tools (grapples, aoe shield, etc.). Weapons are customizable with various mods to build to your playstyle, lots of build variety to experiment with and class synergy is great.Community is generally very accepting of newer players and it is very easy to just join a game with random people if you don't have any friends that play. Devs are very down to earth, battle passes are completely free and get added to the base game after they expire. Everything that impacts gameplay is unlockable for free and cannot be bought, the DLCs are all purely cosmetic. It doesn't feel like this affects the free content however - the base game has a load of free cosmetic options such as weapon and armor skins and paintjobs as well as various hats, beard/hair styles and they also get added every new season with the battle passes.Atmosphere is great and the tense gameplay experience is only heightened by the amazing soundtrack.
_childDocuments_.name: Deep Rock Galactic

_childDocuments_.review: Deep Rock has not only charming low poly graphics and intense swarms of hordes to decimate but also an epic soundtrack that makes gameplay feel epic at the peak of swarming attacks. Absolute chef's kiss!The game gives you 4 class options engineer, gunner scout, and driller. Loads of cosmetics that can be unlocked or bought and even customize your beard, who could've dreamt that? Customizations to your weapons and the hard to find pickaxe upgrades. The game has a lot of varying biome types that you can choose from a varied selection of mission types and even status effects to an entire map, like double XP or exploding swarms. The game is procedurally generated and sometimes this can make completing a mission hard occasionally if something is out of reach. Nitra, a resource you mine to call for ammo refills, can sometimes be lacking adding to the intensity or frustration to the mission. I've played 20 or 30 hours solo, so while it is a coop game the developers have balanced it by including Bosco which is a drone that will help shoot and mine resources for you to pick up. The variety of game modes has certainly kept the game from feeling stale and extend from resource collection to drone rescue missions. Playing online coop with strangers is a gamble and you can get teamed with people who aren't really trying to play the game or hide when the swarms show up. I have 100 hours of making this review and I feel like I'm still discovering new things.
_childDocuments_.name: Deep Rock Galactic

_childDocuments_.review: Deep Rock Galactic is a game I have trouble reviewing. It's the slightly stained shirt that you keep because it's comfortable and you use it for lounging or housework. It's not your favorite shirt, but it's one of the most often worn, and just easy to toss on.I like the graphics and a lot of the gameplay is fun, but it's nothing super groundbreaking or amazingly new. If you've played squad based co-op games (Left for Dead, Killing Floor, etc) you know the basics. Sure, there's different mechanics, and the whole mining thing (which I HIGHLY prefer over the damn gas cans!) but it's not revolutionary.Which isn't a bad thing at all! Sometimes you just want to have something that you and your friends can easily just pick up and play. And it's almost always on my list of 'Sure, I wouldn't mind playing that' when we get to the What Are We Playing Tonight discussion.The main issue with the review is most of the things are 'good, could be better, but nothing really to complain about.' The music is fine, but I wouldn't consider it great. The graphics are interesting, but they like making the game so freakin dark that I don't get to see as much as I'd like.There's a couple things I could complain about, like the fact that they apparently nerfed everyone but scout because no one liked playing scout and that's why the common flares suck, and personally I would have BUFFED the scout, like making their flares be also warning beacons for enemies nearby, or  have nearby minerals glow a bit even when the flare is out, but I always prefer making changes and classes different from each other verses homogenizing everything, but that's also a personal opinion. There's also the fact that Steves only have a small blue highlight, so they often get shot by teammates. A full on slight blue shift (like a sheen overlay) would be much more helpful.But those are fairly nitpicky, and anything else is even smaller nitpicks,  Which really don't detract much from it being a good game.Thinking about it, maybe the shirt analogy is wrong. DRG is like a taco. It might not be an amazing taco, and there's certainly more exciting or exotic foods than a taco. But it's a damn taco, and there's always room for tacos.

If you enjoy digging or being a dwarf, this game is definitely worth it. Rock and Stone Brother. For Karl!!!

_childDocuments_.review: This game has been a joy for years to me, as the hours state. I have bought supporter packs as recently as this spring, and the unique gameplay and community kept me engaged over the past year's slower pace of content drops. That being said, I cannot recommend you buy a game that has openly announced a content drought until June 2024 to work on a Gunfire-Reborn-with-dwarves game titled "Rogue Core". Let me repeat that: there are no current plans for any future major content drops in DRG, despite its player count increasing yearly and popularity near its highest ever. This decision to focus on a new game also follows a string of games from the studio that had limited interest, such as a Vampire Survivors clone and a board game. If you're fine with paying for access to a game maintained by a team that has publicly announced that it's carving the game's tombstone, wait till a significant sale and try the modded servers out! Otherwise you should pass, as the community will likely take a hit from such a significant announcement.

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely fun core cooperative gameplay about mining minerals, carving tunnels, and killing bugs.  Very easy to hop into matches even with people you don't know.  This is because communication is very easy thanks to the laser pointer, telling your teammates what you want help with.  Caves are randomly generated so very few stages feel alike.  The game keeps you busy with all kinds of upgrades to unlock, and goals to try and meet.  Even silly pointless ones like collecting ingredients for new kinds of beer in the space station.  The community is one of the best and most friendly I've seen in coop games, and the developers have been supporting the game even after Early Access... still adding more content with more planned in the future.I cannot recommend this enough.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really what it says on the tin!The game play is simple, but very well done. Because the worlds are generated, it keeps the game size small (2.5 GB when I downloaded it) but the maps are big, diverse and always different! It's a challenging game, but definitely not too difficult, which makes it good for casual gaming. The monsters make it semi-scary (especially when they manage to sneak up onto you) but that jump-factor only adds to the fun. You will never face too many of them, because that also scales with the amount of players in the group.Definitely a recommendation! Do bring a friend or two (or three) because it simply beats playing alone.PS: don't forget to go and explore the home base, there are plenty of things that put a smile to your face ;)

_childDocuments_.review: Short version: Very addicting PVE co-op mining FPS game with dwarfs inside space-caves fighting off alien bugs. Long version: Can be played solo, or up to 4 people together online. There are 4 different classes, namely Gunner, Engineer, Scout and Driller. Each class has a unique way of traversing the various sequentially generated areas in the game, as well as providing different abilities to help out the other miners, and changing up the gunplay. The player can start an assignment that can be finished by completing missions. Once an assignment is complete, the player gets rewarded. There are multiple types of missions, all of them having a main objective, and a secondary objective. It is worth to do both, as it gives more EXP and pays more credits after completion. On top of that, there are occasional random events that can differ between collecting additional loot, or defeating mini-bosses. Always mine out Gold for more credits, and Nitra for ammo resupply, because ammo can run out pretty quickly. It is sometimes beneficial to mine out any unique or extra minerals, as they are needed for purchasing certain weapon and tool abilities, new weapons, and cosmetics. These abilities are locked behind level progression per each class. Enemies usually appear in waves throughout the mission, sometimes they're triggered by certain actions or progression, and there's plenty of different types of alien bugs to make the gameplay challenging and engaging. The more missions you complete, the more new weapons and cosmetics you can unlock. Additionally, you can complete challenges to get perk points to unlock passive and active perks for your characters. Once a class reaches level 25, they won't gain more EXP and levels, and the player has the option to apply to a Promotion Assignment, which when is completed, the class can then be promoted, resetting their level, but gaining a second active perk slot, and maintaining every weapon and tool abilities as well. There is a season pass as well, which is purely cosmetic, and all the DLCs for this game are also cosmetic only, meaning that you don't have to buy them to get the full experience with the game. I tried to make this as short and understandable as possible, there's a lot more to talk about. Rock and Stone brothers.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games ever made by the best devs ever who understand what the real gaming is. Hundreds of hours invested absolutely worth it. Pure fun, adrenaline and joy. I remember my very first dive as a Greenbeard. Even then no Dwarf or gold was left behind. Drilling, mining, exterminating and lighting the path - what else can a Dwarf dream of? Like Someone once said -"This way", and went up where no one couldn't. A Scout, who immediately got grabbed by a leech. What a Bastard. Love him.You want to dig? - You're welcome. You want to shoot? - You're welcome. You want to explore and get leeched somewhere far on the other side of the map? - Yes! You're Welcome! Welcome To Hoxxes IV! Best Planet Ever Found. Caves might call for Adventurers, but Mines call for Dwarves, and we'll make these caves mines. All these resources down there? Yup, those are MINES! The drop pod is ready. I'm coming. Now, grow up and become a real Dwarf. By the Beard and for Rock and Stones! Find your inner Karl. With this game, you'll become RICH in every way possible!Thanks for changing my life, game. Thanks for saving me from becoming a leaf-lover.

_childDocuments_.review: If I had to choose between every co-op game that ever existed and was only allowed to ever play one, it would definitely be Deep Rock Galactic. The gameplay, customization, friendliness of the community, and the atmosphere all come together to make an awesome experience that's hard to find anywhere else.The gameplay loop is simple enough yet extremely fun: Land in a cave, mine resources, and fight swarms all while working towards completing the mission objective you selected. After you completed said objective, you can call in the drop pod and escape. All the mission types give you a huge amount of variety and the gameplay hasn't gotten repetitive since I started playing it. You can choose between collecting alien eggs, salvaging mining equipment, setting up a liquid refinery, and much more. The customization is also super in-depth in terms of both gameplay-affecting choices and cosmetic choices. While the amount of weapons in Deep Rock Galactic is low compared to other shoots, you unlock lots of choices for each weapon you level up, also including special "overclock" upgrades that you can unlock and equip once you promote (prestige) your first dwarf. The cosmetic side of things only has one base model that you can play as, but there's a massive array of beards, hairstyles, hats, helmets, uniforms, and even uncanny things such as turning your skin green. The community in this game is one of the friendliest I've ever been part of, most randoms are a joy to play with, and toxic players are few and far in between. Part of this is due to how naturally Deep Rock Galactic's systems encourage cooperative gameplay. Getting through a mission smoothly involves everyone using their classes' unique weapons to deal with hordes, as well as combining their transversal equipment to be able to effectively mine the resources they need to get enough ammo for the mission and afford that upgrade they needed after they escape. To top it off, the game lets you hit V to give off a cheery "Rock and Stone!" that lots of groups, including randoms, will spam after making it out of a tense situation. The "lobby" that you select missions and customize equipment in also includes bunks for all the Dwarves, a robot-operated bar that'll let your squad get drunk and pass out, and lots of fun things to mess around with. Overall, if you're even mildly interested in co-op games, this is a must have that nobody should miss out on.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun solo - YesFun with randoms - 90% of the timeFun with friends - AbsolutelyThere are 4 classes. They are ALL fun. They work together really really well and are pretty well balanced. They all have their roles and the game is most fun when everyone plays to them. That being said I often get distracted by shiny things and this often makes more fun for everybody else! Right! Yeah pretty sure it does. The community for this Game is solid and probably the least toxic from my experience. There are loads of different guns that can be plenty modified and even overclocked, but the main thing is they are very satisfying to use. There's plenty of humour and it's very atmospheric. What I mean by this is the lighting, sounds and music all work really well to make those moments when you have 30 seconds to get to the drop pod low on ammo with endless bugs behind you feel a bit like your in a movie (That bit in Aliens where the turrets run low on ammo and they start coming through the ceiling always goes through my mind anyway). In summary..... Get this game. Just get it.

_childDocuments_.review: this game has the ability to drag me in for hours after staring at my 200+ games unable to pick what's next. DRG has a wonderful charm that can make you laugh, chuckle maniacally, or  flinch in shock from how quickly it all falls apart.Hazard levels three and below are great for kicking back and mining those sweet minerals with friends, or with the reliably kind community.Hazard levels four and five can be brutal, but still entirely achievable with in-game pings (very fleshed out) as hardly anyone uses voice chat, since the dwarves always seem to phrase it better anyhow...Each of the classes is reasonably well balanced, and has tonnes of customisation room, especially with post-promotion overclocks. The developers LOVE this game and its community, and are constantly advancing to improve the experience.Out of everything this game has to offer, the only criticism I have thus far is the slippery physics system - a blessing and a curse. In the hub it's great for barrel riding and launching objects into the top of the drop pod, but in-game it can cause you to be flung across the map by jumping into sloped terrain :\I've seen many players with 1000+ levels still enjoying the experience of helping out the newbies.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the finest "4 players PVE online Co-op" archetype there is. Excellent and complementary classes. Intuitive teamplay. Crazy good replayability. Loads of unlockables. Frequent and free updates. No microtransaction BS. Blabla, definitely a great pick up !Excellent, fluid and fun. Each of the four classes, namely: scout / engineer / driller / gunner, really plays different and complement themselves perfectly. Every role is really well thought out and fun to dive into... All the weapons and their mods + overclocks also tremendously impact the way you play your class. Definitely some real depth to it. Honestly the procedural generation works incredibly well, you technically will never play the same map twice. After a few dozens of hours you'll start noticing some patterns but will still come across plenty of oddities like crazy monstrous rooms, those hit different the first few times ! At first glance the game seems quite visually unappealing but, it has some charm to it, it even looks pretty good when you put image sharpening to the max. The game definitely isn't a GPU melter but DRG surely has a uniqueness to it.Sounds are good; Music is whatever; And most definitely tired of hearing "For rocks and stones"!!!If you like the game, want to level all 4 dwarves, unlock most of everything etc ... You'll unquestionably get your money's worth ! Great game.

_childDocuments_.review: There's a certain type of magic in role-based cooperative games.  Each player does their part, each player has their strengths and weaknesses, and each player has their fun!  Deep Rock Galactic has captured that magic amazingly.  They took an old trope, (Dwarves mining too deep), and punched it up to 11.  Now we're dwarves, mining on a hostile alien world for as much profit as we can obtain out of it.  You have your Driller, Gunner, Engineer, and Scout.  You can limit the game to one of each, or play with four drillers.  Play the game the way you want to play, have the fun you want to have.Controls are tight, graphics are clean, sound design is impeccable.  Most game modes are enjoyable, the progression system is fun and clear.  There's very little I can hold this game back on.  Even the solo mode is really decent for a cooperative game, (you get a tiny robot Bosco).  There are also some great difficulty curves.  You want relaxing?  Got it.  You want instant death because you decided to mine some gold for 2 seconds?  Got it.There's just nothing funnier to me than everyone screaming bloody murder because two Bulk Detonators spawned and three of the four us just exploded.  You play this game for the wins, the losses.  But most importantly, you play this game for Karl.Rock and Stone

_childDocuments_.review: This game actually makes me go get beer to drink. Those beers are so appealing.Deep Rock Galactic really hits a key note in simple fun gameplay and teamwork. Depending on the hazard level you choose, it can be chill or hectic enough to keep you entertained just how you want. Epic moments, hilarious moments, they're both there.I can only say that it needs a bit more in every aspect, but it's early access after all. Game modes, enemies, weapons, stuff to spend your resources on. More better minigames inside the space ship? Ones you can do with your teammates?The dwarves are depicted as being like some cockney British doofuses, which is often funny. However, each dwarf all has the same voice files, just set to a different pitch. I do wish they were individual, or if there was some proud dwarf voice option maybe. I'd love it if the dwarves were like Bardin from Vermintide 2, or good ol' Lord of the Rings Gimli. You know, those proud type of humbly bumbly dwarves.

This game has it in spades. The taming of a glyphid turning it into a pet that you can Press E to pet. The way you can toast while you have a beer in your hand. The Jukebox that will play songs that your dwarfs will dance to.The effects of the crazy beer, and the little robot that serves you.the silly beards.the crazy hats.The unique progression system that has you hunting down rouge machinery to infuse blanks cores to upgrade your weapons or just give yourself a dope hat. Your choice.The deep dives that are 3 missions in a row with random objectives that get harder the deeper you go. The closest game I can compare to would be Astroneers with caves that want you dead 10x more. with the slow but steady pace of progression like that of borderlands. Devs are great, and the game is great.update from 350 hours in to 2300 hours in. game's still good. update with 3141 hours in, maybe a-little burn out.

_childDocuments_.review: For those who liked L4D2 and Payday, I highly recommend you check this game out.I bought the game on sale for 75% of the original price, but after playing it for around ten hours, I'd recommend it even if it's at full price. Gameplay is simple, mine and shoot. This game does a fantastic job of balancing both elements, you won't feel pressured or rushed during missions, unlike Payday 2 where you sometimes get caught and have to rush getting your money bags. Pros:1. 4 different classes each with its own identity/strength/function.2. Generated maps. 3. Game mechanics fits well with co-op.4. Bug variety. (similar to L4D2, you get boomers, smoker, tank in this game too)Cons: (game still in developement, so this may not be pernament)1. Upgrade choices doesn't feel like enough.2. Solo is hard for higher difficulty missions. (because you'll always have to fight waves of bugs)3. Caves can be a pain to navigate, especially on the way back to your vessel.Overall, this game have some of the best idea/theme in recent FPS/Co-op games, though there's definitely room for improvements, it's already a pretty fun game with lots of potential.

_childDocuments_.review: So let me get this straight. Deep Rock Galactic (DRG) is a game where:- You can get drunk before missions and then spend the entire mission seeing double and falling into chasms as your character staggers around- The community are generally really nice and helpful, will often give you tips to help your play during missions and will ask nicely if they need something from you- You'll enjoy a range of beautiful, procedurally generated biomes with different hazards and structures for each one- Gunplay feels super slick and solid, every gun has a substantial feeling to it and all the animations and handling are really nicely done. For instance, if you tap 'reload' when you're full then your dwarf playfully spins the gun in the air, which is such a cool way to make me forget I tried to reload a full gun by accident- There's an upgrade system that's super simple and lets you tailor your dwarves to how you like to play- There're fun customisation options for your dwarves that don't feel overwhelming- The community are more than happy to have a drink and a dance at the bar after missions- The bar serves "craft" beers with weird effects like setting you on fire and teleporting you around the station- You never really feel short of the in game crafting materials and credits to get the upgrades and cosmetics you want. And even if you are you can either use the mineral exchange or just run like one more mission to get what you need, and that's fun all by itselfWhat more do you want? I  Deep Rock Galactic and I dumped something like 60 hours into it in my first week of owning it. It's so quintessentially cute and fun to play that it's easy entertainment whether with friends or getting matched up with randomers. Left 4 Dead style gameplay brought back in the best possible way.Arguably, you might get a little tired of the gameplay after a point. There're only five mission types and the secondary objectives don't meaningfully alter the main mission feel. The procedural generation of caverns is cool, but after you've played each biome five times then you'll get the gist of how they look and what to expect. I think this is easy to look past if you really enjoy the gameplay and have something to play for, however, that "something to play for" is, unfortunately, DRG's biggest failing.Deep Rock Galactic's one significant con is that the end game content is  poor and leaves you very little reason to keep playing.End game plausibly starts after you've unlocked the vast majority of each dwarf's basic weapon upgrades, which is around 60 hours depending on how many dwarves you do, so you could argue you've already got good value for money out of the game either way. However, if you want to play on then there's actually not much else left to do in the game.The main thrust of end game content is collecting overclocks, which are either special weapon or cosmetic upgrades. You acquire these (largely at random) on a weekly basis where you can obtain a limited number each week and have to wait for the following week to get some more.Now, to be clear, overclocks in general are cool, although I'm not going to touch on the cosmetic ones because they're nice but not essential to gameplay. Weapon overlocks, on the other hand, are funky special upgrades that work like the basic upgrades but with more oomph, so you'll definitely want to get them and I think they're really nicely designed. Many offer interesting trade-offs that boost one part of a weapon at the expense of another (e.g. higher damage but for a smaller ammo clip) and you can use them to really capstone your preferred style of play. There're also some that offer smaller boosts with no drawbacks if you don't like any of the cons to the more powerful ones.However, as mentioned, you're only given two random weapon overclocks a week (assuming you do the weekly assignment and the regular deep dive), plus two blank cores you can choose to make into semi-random weapon overclocks (you can pick from two dwarves when converting the core but the overclock you get will be a random one for any of that dwarf's weapons). So a decent amount of the overclocks you'll get will likely be for a dwarf you use less, or on a weapon you don't like and you only get a handful of chances a week to get something you want. At this point it's important to stress that  so you  get all the overclocks eventually, which is a really nice thing, but it's still frustrating if you don't get any overclocks for your favourite dwarf/weapon for a while.Now, if you're like me and you play several dwarves then you probably won't mind the random aspect of overclock rewards as you simply make do with what you get until you get something you really want. However, my  gripe with this system is that there's very little reason to play the game outside of when the new week begins and overclock rewards reset. There's no other way of getting new overclocks and there's no new content at end game other than continuing to level your dwarves to get a fancier portrait border (which is a huge grind anyway).In short, the issue is thus: I want to actually have a reason to be playing. Maybe if you got one overclock every 15 missions or something I would know I was at least working towards , but right now there's nothing and it doesn't sound like there're any plans to expand end game at the moment.DRG regulars will tell me that Deep Dive missions are technically also end game content, but all a Deep Dive is is a series of three fundamentally regular missions strung together back to back. You can't even encounter special events or gather crafting resources during them, it's all just about how fast you do them, and even that's just for posterity. Maybe if you have a group of friends and you want to do the elite Deep Dive together (as opposed to the non-elite one) to see how fast a time you can get vs the difficulty then you might get some value from the idea, however you have to wait a week for a new set of Deep Dives to generate, so there's still nothing else to do after you've done it once. Overall, compared to standard missions, Deep Dives are just sadly lacklustre as an experience compared to the regular missions.To conclude, end game is an mess in DRG at the moment. The overclocks are great, but they come in really slowly and there's nothing else to play for in the mean time. Like, I absolutely love this game and would happily grind my way through a bunch of missions just knowing I was getting even a little bit closer to unlocking my next overclock... But there's just nothing. There aren't even any cool boss raids or anything. The developers have poured all their time into making the regular missions fun, but I just think there're so many end game content ideas that DRG could expand into that just don't exist at the moment. Who knows. The game's still being developed, though at time of writing I believe it'll be new mission types and biomes next, which, to be fair, will be really good, but I think it's a band-aid for the real issue.To finish, the game's fantastic and you don't need a friend to experience 98% of the content, but you'll stop having a reason to play after 60 hours or so. 60 hours is a long time so maybe that's good enough, but if you finish levelling up your dwarves and can't wait for what's next then you might be a bit disappointed.

name: art of rally
detailed_description: 'To do something dangerous with style is art...' art of rally is a stylized experience inspired by the golden era of rally from the creator of Absolute Drift Race across the world through colorful and stylized environments in top-down view. Compete for first place in the leaderboards with daily and weekly challenges. Will you master the art of rally? Experience the golden era of rally in Career mode, travelling across 78 stages from Finland to Sardinia, Norway, Japan, Germany, Kenya and Indonesia. Get behind the wheel of your favorite vintage cars, ranging from the 60’s to the 80’s, Group B, Group S and Group A. From beginner-friendly options to driving modes that’ll challenge the most expert drivers, all players can tackle the races using their favorite rally driving tricks: Scandinavian flick, counter steering, left foot braking, handbrake turns. Get your name out at the top of the Leaderboard in our daily and weekly challenges. Show off your driving skills, or simply your favourite landscapes, with the integrated Photo and Replay mode.

short_description: Race in the golden era of rally. Drive iconic cars from the 60s to Group B on challenging stages through stylized environments inspired by real worldwide locations. Will you master the art of rally?

_childDocuments_.review: To keep it short; If you enjoy/have enjoyed absolute drift you'll like this. It's in the same vein but much more robust. The graphics are better as are the physics while still being very much funselektor from top to bottom. It's still stylized in all the best ways. Sound design is good even though it's not fancy pants simulation sounds. The whole package is tight and well done. It's a blast.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really fun. It's not just a game for people who are only interested in racing or rally games. This game can be a really great arcade game to get into, also to introduce yourself into the art of rally. I have really enjoyed the event mode of this game and I will definitely be playing more.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game that's easy to play but hard to be good at—strikes a great balance between fun and challenging. The minimalist aesthetic may be deceptive: this game has lots of depth, with career mode, time trials, daily/weekly challenges, and free roam mode. And it doubles as a history lesson. All around, an example of really brilliant game design.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: Great racing game. Really fun game play! The history behind rally, the cars, the car manufactures, the race records, are given though out the career mode, and it is super interesting to read. A great touch to an already great racing experience. One part arcade, one part sim. This is game a little gem with, a kickin synth soundtrack. I bought this as a gift for two other friends...don't miss it.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: This game goes on my highly recommend list. The visuals and art style are excellent, each location has its own real character that distinguishes it from the other. But the cars are where it really shines. The sounds are fantastic, and really help get you in that rally mindset. The dynamics really do differ from car to car as well. I've put a number of hours in so far, and keep coming back for more.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: Easy to play, very difficult to master! Art of rally is a very fun game, but make no mistake, the arcade style doesn't mean you can just "pedal to the metal" and steer right or left, controls are difficult to master, especially on slow tracks. Everythin is attractive, the graphics, the old cars, the lovely tracks and the lighting, but there's also a con, which are the penalties. Sometimes you get penalties even when you're just on the side of the road, and the mechanism that rules them feels whimsical, to say the least. If the devs can fix that, this title would almost be perfect.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: Art of rally is a game with an incredibly high skill ceiling even after 160 hours I still get better with every session and once you master the game you can destroy other people's times just by using the skills you built up. I just recently managed to get into the top 100 across every course in group a and am excited to shoot for top 50. Tldr get this game if you love constant progression and time trials
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: Looks cool, lighting effects in particular are very good. Handling is intuitive and responsive. Good mix of free roam / rally eventsCons: Network issues plague gameplay elements (leaderboard times fail to upload more regularly than they successfully upload) and daily and weekly events are therefore often inaccessible
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: That feeling when it all connects, you carve the perfect line, dropping into second as you glide through a corner like you were born to rally, feathering just enough throttle to maintain perfect traction, pop into 3rd and roar into the straight away like a lioness taking town prey....And then you slam into a boulder at 60 mph because you'll never be that perfect again. It's a drug, and the beauty of that brief moment has you hooked, scrabbling through the dirt until you get your next hit. This is a wonderful game. As frustrating as it is beautiful. Exactly what it should be.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I'm kind of on the fence with this. It just depends on what you want out of a racing game, and for me a lot of that boils down to consistent physics. They're good, but also pretty flawed.As others have stated, this has some great physics traits of a racing sim, but some others that contradict it in ways which don't make sense. It can be frustrating for anyone used to racing sims, as it's inconsistent. That's about its only major pitfall but its enough to put me off. Otherwise its a beautiful game with an amazing car list, and expansive detailed rally locations. If you like challenging arcade racers, or are just a rally fan,  then you'll probably enjoy it a lot. The bad:-It has one of the WORST steering delays I've experienced in any racing game, regardless of how fast the car is moving. Very unrealistic choice there. Raising the steering sensitivity doesn't really help either. -Counter-steering is pretty inconsistent, sometimes it just doesn't react, almost as if the tires are locked up but you're not even braking. -Its also much better with the assists turned off, like the strange counter-steer-multiplier. That assist, paired with the steering delay makes for some infinite fish-tailing from over correction. -Has this weird forced over-steer tendency with most MR/RR vehicles, but its only really like that when you're accelerating. It should only behave like that when you hit the brakes in a corner (i.e. lift off over-steer). Gently accelerating in a slide should give your back wheels a bit more grip via weight shift, not significantly less. It makes said MR cars act like FR drift machines. -It really seems like the assists don't actually switch off in group 4, and it feels wildly different compared to both group 3 and group B (when comparing FR cars for consistency). I might be imagining things or it may be a bug, but group 4 feels like the other two but with the assists maxed out, not sure why. Just a hunch.-The vegetation cut-out is useful but flawed, it just gives you tunnel vision on the top of your car, but nothing ahead of it. This especially affects camera #1. -Brushing against some guardrails will literally stop your car and/or spin it, instead of just slow you down like usual.The good:-Great car list! Many famous rally cars from different classes, including some experimental ones that sadly never got to race. Would love to see a couple of my favorites though, like the infamous Celica GT4 st205, and the '87 Silvia 200sx/s12 seV6. -Beautiful locations, and expansive free-roam maps as well that are excellent to drive around in. They're pretty detailed and the scenery does not disappoint. The mountain roads in Japan are great, and I love the addition of the muddy river in the Sahara. -A banger of a soundtrack in my opinion. Synthwave (w/ a bit of Eurobeat) makes for some fantastic driving music.-For racing games, both this and especially Absolute Drift, have a nice relaxing vibe to them that's pretty unique. -You don't have to compete in the career mode in order to wander around the free-roam maps, and some vehicles from every class are unlocked from the start. -The ability on PC to add custom livery mods is a plus if you're into that.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: this game is completely unapologetic in its hunt for nostalgia. the very best rally cars crammed into a tidy package of an arcade game that quite frankly puts WRC to shame. and maybe even codemasters games. it delivers style and a rewarding drive from the get go. handy assists provide help for those who need it to keep the game fun, but i would recommend you turn off everything to get the best feedback. its difficult to say whether this is the game rally fans were crying out for, but it certainly fills any holes in host of games i own and will be go to rally game from here on. for me its difficult to critique. i love the sythwave OST,  the cars and design, the look and feel. i would like to see the creators drop the camera down to ground level. maybe even in car. the game seems as though it could manage it and still remain tidy. as soon as you drop the camera down for photos and videos you get a true beauty that you can't get high up. i would also like to see some variation on road size in stage, as some of them seem to stay the same width throughout. i thoroughly enjoy this game, the driving is challenging and rewarding. great job funselektor
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: I bought the game one or two months after release and It was great and It still Is. But updates came out really slowly, and they still are. 3 updates in almost 2 years (Only 2, If you don't count liveries/paint options as an update (And only one was a new location, mind I add) I know that the dev team is small like really small. Only one person If I remember correctly, but the content can be played through pretty fast compared to how often content updates come out. The career mode Is lovely and fun when new and Is challenging as novise/experienced. New locations/settings makes you feel like a pro driver just waiting for what's to come.And the way that the groups are unlocked Is good, having to know what came before almost makes you ready for what Is to come.But the thing that made me tired of the game was the leaderboard of the online section. I wasn't bad, I even held multible WR's (although on the same stage between multible groups of cars) It's was still amazing. But now as I've played more hardcore rally/racing sims. The way that you can just cut the track, makes me mad. Well more sad then mad. Because getting a fast time Is about being faster/better and more brave then the opposition. But not here. I've fought with multible people for WR's, but the faster we got the more we had to cut, and at the end I didn't see It as rally'ing but more as "Who can cut more without being caught by the stage borders" It's a bit sad IMO. The online part doesn't take away the fun and satisfactory of the game doe. It's still good and Is still a great game and bridge between arcade and sim for the people who want's more realisme but aren't sure If the are ready for It. 8/10 A great and fun game for at least 50+ hours (Completing the career mode, even later on harder difficulties. Doing online time attacks, aswell as doing daily's/weeky's in online for more knowledge/experience In the different groups of cars)
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an awesome buy for anyone who is a fan of rally / rally cars, or someone who wants a simple game to sit down and chill out with. Overall it is fun, gorgeous, and quite well polished.Pros:- A short but satisfying career mode which allows you to slowly progress through years of rally to see how the cars evolve, along with a sufficient amount of difficulty tuning- A unique free-roam with collectables and unlockable maps and songs- Custom rally and time attack modes- Arcadey and satisfying driving- Broad selection of iconic vehicles from all eras of 20th Century rallying, including some unique add-ins- Simple yet elegant models and eye-popping colors, paired with an incredible soundtrackCons:- A few optimization issues on some of the more cluttered stages- Only five locations currently exist in game (although more will likely be added)
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: lowercasing symbolising the lack of excitement. no co-driver as stages are made up of open flat roads. inconsistent track boundaries. an out of place synthwave soundtrack. crowds are a novelty but they mask obstacles, react too late and make no effort to appear local. assets pop in and forests lag out.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: I like to slide around to rad music. This game is awesome.Edit: I've put more hours into this game. Still love it. Finally switched to manual after 25 hours of automatic transmission and it's a whole new game. You have so much more control (duh) over the car once you get the hang of it. The mechanics of this game are simple but so satisfying. Every car handles differently and provides a unique challenge.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. I've played most of the rally games out there and this is easily as enjoyable and satisfying when you get it right. The principals are the same, and the physics and movement felt very intuitive after I spent about 10 minutes learning the controls. I'm using an xbox controller, and manual shifting.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: Intense gameplay in misleading low polygon world. Having a blast, just running through the levels, without worrying about winning - that will come later. The engine sounds are well done and pretty immersive. There were few micro-stuttering issues, which seem to have resolved after adding  to my launch options.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: This is absolutely incredible! How can it be that a tiny indie developer can make a vastly more compelling arcade racer than massive studios? This cuts through the BS like butter, providing a satisfying and enjoyable driving experience. I have not tried all arcade racers, but most are a turn-off because either the physics are too simplistic, the courses are uninteresting, or the AI are out for blood. This harkens back to the PGR2 days, where it's easy to jump into a race, listen to the soundtrack, and forget about the outside world. Just wish my computer wasn't on fire doing it.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: Good racer. In a time in my life where I really only spend time on games that are the ones that really demand your full attention (read: the real triple-A games that come out each year) it was surprising to me that I kept coming back to this time after time until I finished the career mode. I got really good at it, too.Now, I had bought and overall disliked this developer's previous game, Absolute Drift, years ago. But I gave this one a shot and really enjoyed it. I will say that this game may look pretty plain and simple, but it isn't the lightest when it comes to hardware, really making my five year old 4790K and GTX 980Ti really show their age - it probably has higher demands than even Dirt Rally 2.0, though don't quote me on that.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: The vibrant art style, scenic landscapes mixed together with an amazing soundtrack and challenging, yet enjoyable gameplay. Unforgiving at times but also provides maximum satisfaction when you get it spot on. The game isn't trying to be as realistic like Dirt Rally 2.0 but retains some realism with it's decently complex physics. Every car in each group felt mostly different to one another except for group S where most cars felt understeery and straight to super oversteery when trying to input more turning. Overall, this game is truly a love letter to the rally heritage made with lots of dedication. Definitely would recommend trying it out.Also, turbo go tsutsutsutsu
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: art of rally is a charming indie gem, a distillation of rally into its more core components. No tuning, no pace notes, just car control and loose surfaces. Its simple and incredibly pretty. If you like rally racing, specifically the golden age of group b, you'll love this game. Best played with a controller or wheel.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: This game is awesome. Easy to pickup, hard to master rally game with a focus on retro cars. There are 7 locations that all look stunning and offer different challenges with the various track layouts. The soundtrack is fantastic, and makes the game super chill, whilst still being engaging. This is a great game to keep coming back to for a couple hours at a time. If you like rally games, pick this up :D
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: new innovations in computing such as more memory and lower-case text paved the way for this to be one of the first rally cars to be refined with a computer. it had a top speed of 210km/h which was the largest number the simulation could output before running out of ram. only three prototypes were created, but they were the basis for the future pebble v2.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: A brilliant game that takes you back to the golden age of rally, where the turbos were big, the cars were loud, and the spectators were always in the way! a game with simple graphics but a much welcomed in depth physics model which takes time to master. a must have game to anybody who is a fan of the group B era of rallying.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: For the so inclined this is a satisfying little racing "simulation". The style is just great and you can work on improving your skills. It is very hard though, believe me I've played many racing games over more than 3 decades. Don't make the mistake to play with automatic transmission as the game is just much harder and far less fun that way. MT all the way, believe me (I learned that fact way too long into my playing the game).
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: Really really good. I thought it was too expensive buying it, but there is so much content and polish here. Perfect podcast game. It has a gorgeous art style, and the amount of small details really show how much work the devs put into it. Details like weather effects, crowds huddling dangerously close to car, and messages under your car if you manage to flip it over. They've done so much with a simple concept: Just the way the game starts sets the tone. The game finds the "zen" feeling of driving recklessly fast and drifting around the game world. The descriptions for cars and rally competitions is so smartly written, it makes me like game even more, as if the amazing control and feel of driving wasn't enough. Fantastic game, really glad I bought it. Highly recommended if you like top down racers.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: Much like its predecessor, Absolute Drift, the driving in art of rally takes some getting used to. With no walls to keep you on the track, you'll need a delicate touch on the gas and copious amounts of braking to keep you from flying off into the woods. But it's really satisfying once you get the hang of it. With tons of tracks and cars to unlock, there's a whole lot of game here.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: This game gets a BIG thumbs up! When I launched the game, the volume is set to 50% by default!!! It didn't blow my eardrums out in my headphones! Why don't all games come like this? This is one of the rare games where I actually turned up the volume! Sound track is great, rally mechanics are great, art style is great, the only thing I dislike is my ability to control the cars well :( TLDR; Great game, great sound, great default volume level!
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a lot of fun. It takes a little bit to get used to the feel of rally driving, but once you do, nailing tricky corners becomes immensely satisfying. I've been playing Dirt Rally for a couple of years and, even though I'm by no means very good at it, I was able to pick up and play this game. +controls and physics feel very smooth; just keep in mind it's not quite a sim+wheel and pedal support (I use a Logitech G29 with an arcade stick as my handbrake, lol), sadly without H-shifter support+good electronic soundtrack (even though I mute it and blast eurobeat)+beautiful aesthetic; it even has insane rally fans jumping in front of and dodging your car+good selection of cars (which handle decently differently) and tracks+has Mt. Akina (Haruna) and Myogi from Initial D tho-no pace notes or co-driver; I get that a top-down perspective should mean you don't need one, but blind corners still mess me up, and you'd expect one in a rally game-no adjustable suspension options-I hate the way it controls on tarmac, it feels like you have to throw your car at 20000 mph or yank your handbrake for 17 years to get it sideways-no tutorials (like in Dirt Rally); if you're new to rally driving, be sure to familiarize yourself on the physics of it-no FFB on steering wheelOverall highly recommended, I can tell I'm going to get a lot of fun out of this game.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: Best arcade rally game ever. all the different years including group b and a couple special categories like vans, trucks, and triwheeler. Tons of different tracks and different weather options for each. The top down view might be a little annoying for some people but put it in the lowest view and it works great.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: This game is honestly one of the best driving games I've ever played. I love how every car has it's own description with a bit of history to go with it on the car it's based on (If you know about rally cars of the time you can tell what they are). The simplistic visuals, along with the music and how good the cars sound just works so well. There's also a decent amount of cars to unlock which all feel uniquely different to drive with simplified versions of real liveries and colour options. All at a price that is just too damn good to pass up; even better if it's on sale. If you like racing/driving games...BUY THIS GAME. It takes some getting used to at first, but when you do the game is just so much fun.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: it's just so cute and fun!my favorite racing game i have ever played. physics engine is remarkable and the visuals are great. i personally like to hit F4 and show all the physics and performance variables the game uses. it is so cool. i highly recommend to anyone that likes racing games/sims and is a fan of the more simple, unity-esque style.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: This is the only racing game that's ever put me into a "flow state" similar to Tetris.  In tune with the car, drifting serenely through obviously pretty environments.  I appreciate the campaign mode has no requirements to be a god at the game, anybody can progress and unlock everything it has to offer.  There's no penalty if you have a bad season, unless its the sort of thing you take personally.I also appreciate the story is short, surreal, and most importantly,   If I play one more driving game where I constantly get hassled by an insufferable personality about my internet popularity I might swear the genre off for good.My one gripe is with fade in with certain areas.  Japan is particularly bad.  The plants and shadows are instantly generated (or LOD increased) before your eyes - other areas the draw distance is both much further and the fade in more gradual, making it less noticeable.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10 Great game to just pick up and play. Good physics, fantastic car selection, and amazing graphics that still look good even when playing on a lower end computer. Give it a try if you are burnt out on racing sims and just want a game that you can start up and just have fun without having to worry about championship standing or car setup. There are only two gripes that I have with this game, first is the UI. While a minimalist interface is fine while driving, it is less fine when I am navigating a menu screen and it can be hard to tell what option I am selecting. This is especially prevalent in the repair menu, where the dots to tell you how much each part of the car is damaged can be hard to make out. My second issue with this game is that their isn't much variety in maps. There are only 4 maps and the career mode is not set, it just randomly selects stages from those 4 maps. So, be ready to get sent to the same 2 maps over and over again. Having a random stage selection can also make it difficult when selecting a car, as some cars are better on tarmac stages and some are better in the snow or gravel. Whereas if it was set I can pick a car better suited to the rally. A wider map selection and career mode being set rather than randomized would be greatly improve my experience with the game.Besides those two minor gripes I have with this game, it is a very good racing game with just realistic enough graphics that it is challenging, but not so realistic that it becomes frustrating. Give it a try if you are tired of crashing into trees in Dirt Rally.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: Cute, fun, full of passion for rally and most importantly super satisfying when you get it right. A wonderful pick-up and play style game with plenty of depth and variety, an excellent handling model and a good mix of weather conditions. Really looking forward to more cars and particularly locations becoming available in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: First off I do like this game but it does have serious issues as a "Rally" game. This is more a drifting game in classic rally cars. Some cars will just not go around corners unless you are drifting and if you get the drift wrong you end up sliding off the track. I have driven some of these rally cars and seriously the ones in this game are awful in the handling unless you are drifting, some of the corners I could take faster in a normal road car without having to drift.Some corners it seems that regardless of the speed you are doing you will slide of the road and hit something.Anyway I love the models of the classic rally cars, the "retro" style of the game and the sheer fun factor and simplicity of the game.Simple to play but hard to master.Update:-The more I have played this the better it has or I have got. I have much better control over the cars now and know which I prefer to use. It is still unpredictable sometime in a turn but that is mostly because you are not at the optimum speed for the car and/or surface, learning the tracks certainly helps here. Do time trials and keep doing the same track and same car and see how you improve over time.I continue to play the game, trying to beat my times and see how close I can get to the top of the leader boards.This game to me is truly a fun game and "driving" rally cars from my era as young adult certainly puts a smile on my face.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: At first I was skeptical because of the "top down" view of the race camera, but as I got used to it, I loved this game more and more. The randomly-generated routes give a sense of randomness and keep the game consistently fresh and the car models are on point! Probably my favorite part of this game though is the soundtrack. Huge Synthwave/Retrowave fan and while most games I turn the in-game music off to play what I want, this one is a game where I make it a point not to. Can't wait to see what they bring next to Art of Rally! If you are a fan of old-school Group Rally cars, then this is for you!! Absolutely love it.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: First off. This game features some of the most beloved companies, Exhaust, Oil and Righto.If you enjoy Sim racing as much as I do, don't get upset if you fall in Love and your significant gets jealous Full clutch dumps with proper e-brake and fantastic "borderline Sim" handling. It is just fantastic as long as you turn abs and traction stability stuff completely off, turn up the difficulty.If you enjoy Arcade racing or Relaxing games, this is absolutely for you. The graphic design and art in general is minimalistic and incredible, depth of field is just yummy. Hours of Incredible music by Tatreal, check out his bandcamp. You can buy the entire soundtrack from him for a fraction of the price in HQ formats, Support. Just leave the settings on play on not to difficult and enjoy the ride.This game is theraputic for Casual racers and gamers of any age.And for Hardcore sim racers this game is theraputic for other reasons, you know what I mean.Beautiful Audio. The Vehicle selection is just pure Yes. Courses are amazing and well thought out, Prettiest game of 2020.Hardcore enough for the Pros and Chill enough for the Casual.I cannot recommend this game enough!11/10Ripping down country road Bunch of spectators blocking roadThey disperse, I smash into wallI should have slowed downThey were happily in front of the turn I could not seeThis is awesome!
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: Amazingly fun and realistic rally game with plenty of Easter eggs and delightful surprises for anyone that is a fan of the sport. The game is easy to play but hard to master, keyboard and mouse can be very difficult but do-able as controllable throttle is best. The games graphics are amazing and will stand up to the test of time, as will the soundtrack which I rarely care about in a game but I find myself coming back to listen to more every few days.It can be a relaxing game once you get the hang of it, but your first few rides will be a learning experience.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: Very nice gameplay and aesthetically pleasing. Every car drives differently, for which you need to change your anticipation and angles. Even on the highest difficulty, the rallies, the weather, visibility and random keeps challenging you. The storyline takes you through the different ages of rally, which really makes unlocking newer eras with faster cars an accomplishment. Just when you feel you master your car, a new category unlocks for you to take on. My go to race game to drive relaxed from ten minutes to hours in a go. The music also fits very good. Highly recommended to get this game!
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: After a bit of a struggle to learn how to keep the car on the road, I started to enjoy this gem of a game. When I play, I feel like I am back in a game from my childhood. But be warned: driving is far from easy, only once you understand that you cannot go full throttle all the time will you get the hang of it and start to learn the art. The intro with the Buddha can be a bit strange, but keep playing the game and you will understand it...
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: The most fun I've had in a rally game since ever. The soundtrack and art styles are amazing,But what makes me return to the experience is the gameplay. Every car has a unique feel to it and the stages feel like I'm running them for the first time.The handling and camera view will take some time to adjust to but it's fine once you get the hang of it.If you want a break from the realism based rally games of WRC and Dirt Rally then this is the game for you. And at the best time as well, even amidst the buggy, messy launch that is Dirt 5.Either way this game can be a much more fun alternative to Dirt 5 for about a quarter of the price!I cannot wait for future updates that will add more cars, location and features.10.1/10
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an incredible homage to Rally's Golden Age. It brings back memories of watching summaries of the Championship with my dad in the 80s'. The art direction is magnificent, the soundtrack and Sound FX are awesome and the gameplay is just plain fun. I hope the game is supported with new content/features in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this (I even bought the DLC), the game looks really pretty, the art-style is very unique but its not a good rally game. For me the biggest lack is that there is no information whatsoever throughout a stage. There are no pacenotes, you don't know which corner is coming - because even if this is isometric you very often have no idea - you don't know how a jump will go, there are no timings, etc ... You only know how fast you are going but because of the viewpoint there is no feeling for speed.Secondly, the physics are very floaty and drifty, it might be due to the type of cars and the suggested era but after 4 races it becomes really annoying. The game looks pretty but I think each country only has like 2 or 3 unique stages (and then they also do them in reverse of course) so once you are in group 3 you've seen most of what there is to see.Unfortunately, I would summarise this game as 'not fun'.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a love letter to rally history and chock full of iconic cars from every era, albeit unlicensed and with liveries that are color-correct if anything else.  Make no mistake, the clean, low-poly look of the game undercuts its unforgiving physics engine - this isn't an arcade racer and it  punish poor driving.  While it doesn't quite push the sim side of things, it most certainly leans that way and you'd best be ready to drive smart if you want to make any headway here.This is for those folks who want to run a simcade rally experience from time to time, but can't have a permanent wheel set-up ready to go to run Dirt Rally, or really anyone looking to have fun with a controller and push for fast times.  The top-down view means there's no co-driver here giving you the lay of the land - you can see it for yourself and part of the trick to getting good is learning how to read ahead.  The other, more meaningful side of things is just getting a grasp of the physics engine.  While at times your car can feel floaty and weightless, and while you will likely encounter frustration early on, after some time it will simply click and you will figure out exactly how to make the car do the things you want it to do.  Like its predecessor, , once you get that "aha" moment, you'll be tearing around stages like you gotta take a dump real bad and the bathroom's at the end.It would be grand to have a little more control over your set-up, but with so many cars to go through and each of them feeling incredibly distinct, it's not really that big a deal.  The most powerful cars don't necessarily equate to the fastest stages, so it's all about getting into the car you're most comfortable with and hauling butt as fast as you can.  Like true rally, you're out there on your own and there's idiot crowds waiting at various places to muck up your vision.  The enemy here besides the clock is yourself.The game features quite a few modes that will keep you occupied.  Career mode will have you run the gamut through rally history starting with the 60s.  Time attack mode is here, too, and you will be looking to post times against other players on the leaderboard.  There's also a free roam for each country, allowing you explore and practice while finding random collectibles should you so desire.Overall, I have absolutely nothing negative to say about this game.  It is wonderful, a lot of fun, and while it takes a while to get used to, any racing enthusiast is going to have a good time.  Just don't expect Ridge Racer and you'll be fine.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great little game. It has just enough difficulty to seem impossible at first, but with a bit of patience and a controller one can master the art of rally.I'm far from good, but I have gotten far more fun out of the game than any of the racing games since my teens.Once I finished with the carreer I had a few moments where I just couldn't fathom how I did some of the really fast and technical parts without any mistakes at top speed. Just did it without thinking. Had I thought I would have failed. It made me all giddy with tension. This is very rare in a game.A few hints:- Staying on the road is usually more important than speed. Since road helps you to change both speed and direction of the car faster. Learn the game by staying on the road.- Play through the carreer mode even if frustrating. No need to re-do as the amount of driving will teach you a lot once you conclude with 1995. You can always return and re-do whole seasons once you get grasp of drifts and how breaking will affect the steering and all the tiny micro-skills that exist out there. Trust your brain to learn a lot of it. Experiment.Read the lore; it's fun.- Play with the accellerator by pushing it repeatedly when taking turns. It will help your brain find the balance spot of control.- Try to find cars which have better sideways-grip. Those stabilise better.- Plan ahead. You can't handle some turns by improvising on the go.

_childDocuments_.review: I almost wrote this game off ... because I kept writing the car off. But after a bit of practice, I started to find a groove. When you're actually driving fast in this game, it will feel slow. That is true to life for me. It's very meditative. It forces you to drive on the gears, and after a while you will develop a feel for the weight of the car.Still, I've driven enough fast things fast to know that rally-prepped Minis don't just understeer at < 30mph on dry tarmac for no reason. Some of the car physics just feel ... off (as with more or less every simulator I've ever played). The tyres are made of wood, maybe? Overall though, it's good. There's lift-off oversteer available if you know how to access it - which makes me way too happy - and when you shift, there's a little pause as your dude presses the clutch.I also love the aesthetic (how could you not?), and the focus on the golden eras of rallying. None of your crappy silhouette racers here, but plenty of thoroughbreds like the 6R4, 205 T16, RS200, etc. (although it's a shame they're not licensed). The sponsors are hilarious too - "Oil", "Petrol", etc. It feels like a drivers' driving game, and it's absolutely beautiful. I couldn't vote that down.

_childDocuments_.review: AoR is a first class, top-down racing game. On the surface it might look like a cozy arcade-like that you just play through and forget about, but under the hood these cars don’t have a governor and get wrecked a lot! It pays great homage to a cruel and dangerous era of racing considered to be the golden age of the sport. The first few races to a new player are going to be… interesting, but learning the physics is like riding a bike and something that can be returned to.If you are on the fence about this one I would suggest giving the demo a go. It gives full access to 1 track and 2 vehicle classes and provides sufficient representation to core gameplay dynamics.

_childDocuments_.review: A game created from a passion for rallying, don't let the stylized look trick you into thinking this is just another arcade racer. _childDocuments_.review: is a minimalistic, bird’s eye view racing game. Your goal is to win championships spanning from the 60s and through to the mid-90s.One of the most striking things about  is the presentation: a wonderful, vibrant low-poly visual style, which also includes atmospheric volumetric lighting. Driving towards the setting sun on evening stages is a sight to behold. On top of this, a photo mode is available for your pleasure. It lets you enjoy the lawyer-friendly rally cars blasting through the track, leaving trails of thick smoke in their wake and with their brake discs glowing and sparking. The trackside spectators being cubes may seem odd at first, but they actually complement the game’s aesthetics very nicely.Despite its simple and unassuming looks, this game is quite intensive. I managed to get a consistent 60fps at 1440p on my  system after lowering the “quality” option one step from the maximum. It only seems to affect vegetation density, and the game still looks fantastic with the remaining options at maximum. Otherwise, I’ve not encountered stability issues with this title.For your listening pleasure, please enjoy the  of sensational retrowave soundtrack created by Ukrainian-based composer . It successfully captures the high stakes nature and intense atmosphere of the motorsport and will make you want to drive . Beyond the music, this title nails the sound effects with the same elegance that it wins me over visually. The clusters of spectators whistle and cheer, the Finns shout “oy oy oy!” as they should, the cars sound properly beefy, and later on the backfires sound closer to . Now that’s how you burn fuel in style!This is a racing game entirely devoted to the eponymous motorsport: you must complete point-to-point stages without wrapping yourself around trees or guardrails and try to beat the other opponents vying to do the same. Consistency is king - overdriving can waste valuable time, if not outright ruin your race. Defying tradition, you don’t get a co-driver or pace notes throughout events. The absence of these hallmarks of rallying can appear jarring, but  makes up for it with the camera; it is placed high and far behind your car, letting you see well into the distance and anticipate the changing road conditions. You can even alter its rotation speed, height and field of view, so you’re pretty much guaranteed to find something comfortable. A big challenge that the camera system faces is how to convey elevation and banking changes, and that is also resolved through clever darkening of the track and marking possible jumps with the classic rally gates. From your starting roster of 60s passenger cars all the way to the monstrous prototypes, each vehicle feels satisfying to handle. They have the right balance of accessibility and depth to their handling, and you’re certain to find your favourite rides quickly. You’re going to have great fun tossing these things around hairpins, regardless of using the keyboard, a gamepad or something more exotic. There’s the odd steering re-centre speed when coming out of a slide which may catch you off-guard or indeed send you into a guardrail, but it can be thankfully minimized through the plentiful assist and controller options. There are just so many options! What next, blood type? In the career mode, you will participate in championships spanning over 30 years of rally history. Each race group has five championships that are randomly generated with a sequence of stages; later championships grow longer and more complex. Every region has unique characteristics, both visually and mechanically. As an example, Finland is the classic high-speed dirt roller-coaster with plenty of chances to catch air time, while Germany is top speed asphalt racing on tight roads. Spectators litter each rally stage in large clusters, frequently near opportunities to catch big air time or power-slide through a hairpin. These blocky fellas are absolutely nuts, they try to get close to your car even as it barrels towards them – much like in real life rallying! I’m hesitant to claim these people's ability to occasionally leap onto building rooftops as “realistic”, but it sure is funny. On the other hand, the damage system feels rather undercooked. Moderately fast impacts into trees and rocks have only a chance of degrading your components, while merely scraping against a rail at top speed wrecks your car and can force a restart. The consequences of low part health also seem imbalanced. Suspension understandably makes you pull to one side and worsens your stability, while critical engine condition has you drive an impressive fireball through the stage. That being said, the remaining components could do with better feedback as they sustain wear and tear. Very rarely, you may get a tyre puncture, but in all my time playing I only suffered this twice. At the end of the day, the damage modelling serves as a basic yet functional incentive to not make like Samir and break the car.The stages are open, and the roads are fairly wide, but you must curb your instinct to cut corners too deeply. It’s not just because of dangers like ditches, rocks and trees; instead, there’s an aggressive corner-cutting prevention that resets your car onto the road with a minor time penalty if you try to gain too big of an advantage. It’s understandable why it exists, I just wonder if it could have been done more smoothly, or have that measure removed in its entirety. Your goal through each championship is to finish on the podium without retiring. Complete the five championships in a group to advance to the next one; complete all groups to win the game. Simple and straight to the point. You unlock new vehicles as you progress, and finishing championships without exhausting your restarts also unlocks a bonus skin for each of your cars. It keeps to the spirit of rallying, where just finishing in one piece is commendable, yet at the same time it doesn’t explicitly demand perfection. Do note that the  AI difficulty is rather unbalanced, as they can score seemingly impossible times on early or mid-game stages, then suddenly forget how to drive in rainy weather. At least their mechanical faults are amusing; “bird in cabin” should say enough.You can expect the career mode to last around 20 hours. This may be on the lengthy side for some, given that you only ever race in a single discipline. Players who crave for more, though, can cruise around separate free-roam maps and collect their goodies; these include extra music tracks, beauty spots and the developer’s real-life van, hidden somewhere in each level. The long-term longevity comes from this game being a collection of time-attack courses, and with six tracks per region, reverse layouts plus leaderboards for dry vs. wet for each car class, becoming the best in the world will take a long time.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm around 5 hours into art of rally at the time of writing this review - a point at which it appears I'm around 50% of my way through career and the core of what this game has to offer, having seen enough to feel qualified to offer my opinion.First off, let's clarify what type of game this is: art of rally is an indie game designed to showpiece everything cool about the history of rallying... borrowing from the 90's isometric viewpoint of successful 90s classics, amalgamating with the art style of games such as Abzu and Journey - vibrant, distinct but minimal scenery, and a modern synthwave soundtrack plays seamlessly between rallies and menus. It's stylish for sure... but don't go in expecting Micro Machines. There's a depth to the handling model that puts it somewhere between Forza Horizon and Dirt Rally in terms of handling, with a selection of driving aids for those less confident.It celebrates the history of rally, from the classics such as the esky and the meanie (Escort and Mini), through to Group B, and finally the cozzie, fujin (Impreza) and liftback (Celica) from the 90s. Most of the cars feel different, with the heavier cars such as the turbo brick having substantial weight to them, whilst the 4r6 drives with reckless abandon. There's a definite level of nuance here that you'd not necessarily expect from the screenshots.The sound effects are adequate for what the game offers - tyre squeals and engine noises are distinct but unremarkable. I get the impression the developer may have been torn on how much effort to put into the sound effects, given the stunning soundtrack by Tatreal with his 80's inspired synthwave is a real highlight. It's a must-listen for those who enjoy the likes of the Midnight, or those who adored the much acclaimed sounds of Drive.Visually, the game looks stunning. I can't speak much for performance on lower end PCs, I have it locked at max settings 100fps (9900k/2080Ti) and there's only a handful of visual options, but draw distances are as far as the eye can see and the game sacrifices polygon count for style - delivering a striking visual experience that varies dramatically across the 5 countries you visit. With 40+ vehicles, a free play mode, integrated time trial / leaderboards, there's plenty to offer for those driven to master the game, and it's an absolute joy to play along the way.Thoroughly recommended.
