_childDocuments_.review: Art of Rally is perhaps the one rally game that fans of the genre since ye olde Colin McRae days have been hoping to see come to fruition for quite a long time now. The last good rally game in the arcade-leaning sense was DiRT 3, a title which not only was released over 9 years ago (has it really been that long already?), but isn't even available for easy purchase anymore due to the plague that is expiring licenses. D4 was crippled by its reliance on an under-developed track generator, D5 is still yet to be released as of this review, and V-Rally 4... was terrible.So amidst all this and the much more serious sims that are DR2 and WRC8/9, we now have AoR. And after playing through the game to 100% completion, I can say it's been the kind of rally game I've been waiting forever to play.THE GOOD+ Straight away: the soundtrack. Good lord, this has got to be the OST of 2020. The synthwave music meshes with the game absolutely perfectly, and with just over 50 songs and over 4 hours of playtime across them, you have something truly special that can last across an entire long playsession without feeling even slightly repetitive.+ The entire aesthetic of the game is completely fitting for something with 'Art' in its title. The simple, clean style of AoR looks absolutely beautiful and makes a very welcome change from the ultra-realism that continues to get pushed in the modern era of gaming.+ The gameplay and handling is also almost completely on point. Every vehicle feels subtly different enough from the next to where you don't feel like you're just driving clones of each other while exploring the various wheels of a given Group. The way the cars drive feels incredibly satisfying, especially when you manage to make that one especially long turn while completely sideways, without immediately smacking the car into an errant tree.+ The stages themselves are also mostly excellent and are a massive breath of fresh air from the claustrophobic narrow roads of DR2 and WRC8. The tracks are nicely wide, meaning that you don't have to be especially precise and can enjoy doing those wide slides across every corner. If the stages were as narrow as those two rally sims, AoR wouldn't be anywhere near as good as it is.+ The car variety in AoR is absolutely staggering, with over 40 classic rally cars going from the mid-60s all the way to the mid-90s, and it might even be the only game in existence that allows you to drive the maniacal Group S prototypes that were never given an opportunity to race in real life. And despite there being so many cars, all of them feel different to the next. + The leaderboards are also done incredibly well. Not only are they able to be filled in runs done in Career and Custom Rally (which I feel like it's not a thing in other rally games), but each and every stage has TWENTY separate leaderboards: 10 for each vehicle class and another 10 for when it's raining/snowing.THE BAD- The weakest part of the game's presentation is the engine sounds. Most of them sound quite... synthetic, for lack of a better term, and some of them don't sound anything even remotely close to the cars that they're based on. Normally something like this would be a minor issue at worst but, in a game like this, it's a stand-out problem.- The way the ground of the various maps seems to be put together is via heightmaps. While easy enough to create some proper landscapes with, it also presents problems if said heightmap is not of a sufficient resolution, and this is sadly present in some of AoR's stages. Most notably in Japan, the sides of some steep hillsides is sawtoothed to quite a glaring degree. Not only does this look quite poor, they will also make them feel unrealistic should you end up driving into them, crashing to a complete halt as opposed to tilting the car on the hillside and potentially rolling over. This isn't the only problem with the heightmap either: it's too high in places and causes the ground and grass rendered atop it to clip through the road in several places throughout the game, the most glaring examples being Japan's Free Roam map and Mount Haruna.- Physics-wise, gravity in AoR is almost non-existent. Although a stylistic choice, I feel like it gets in the way of driving the game fast much too hard. For any reasonable jump, you pretty much are forced to back off or even hit the brakes so you don't go off the jump too fast. If you don't, you either hit the ground and immediately lose control, or just sail off the road entirely and either smash into the scenery or fly out of bounds. Either way, it's not a good thing.- Stagewise, although the vast majority of the game is fantastic, the Germany rally drags everything down a notch. Not only is it by far the longest rally in the game on average, it's also the most punishing of mistakes thanks to all the stones lining the edges of the road like bollards in places. And unlike the similarly-long Japan, it's an all-Tarmac rally which makes the stages feel the most samey amongst the five countries. Even the snow represent in Norway has snow, gravel and asphalt to drive on.THE IFFY= Graphically, the puddles that appear on the track when it's raining look very bizarre and pixelated in shape. It's unclear if it's a design choice or not, but it does look especially jarring in contrast to the rest of the game.= The pacing of the Career Mode is a bit inconsistent. Every final event in a given Group is considerably longer than sometimes even the last few events combined, and by the time you reach Group B, the length of the events starts to drag on well beyond their welcome. In more weirdness, the finale of Group S is the same length as the very last event in the game in Group A, and is longer than the entirety of all five events in Group 2.= As of the first patch, the game is not without some glitchiness, the majority of which affects the bonus vehicles. They inexplicably suffer from issues such as specific sections of track in a few stages causing the car to behave like it's driving through grass and not accelerating or, much more glaring, taking specific jumps causing the wheels to clip through the ground, getting the car stuck and forcing a respawn.= Also regarding the bonus cars, none of them are available for use in Custom Rally and are only driveable in Free Roam and Time Trial. It is minor, but it does much to make the Leaderboards for the Bonus categories feel a bit barren since there's less reason for people to drive them.= The performance of the AI drivers was, at least at launch, a bit too easy for those who got used to the handling. Many consider this a problem, although personally it's a much more welcome change to the brutal and wildly inconsident AI of DR2. However the very first patch has changed their performance, so it's not yet clear as to if this is still the case.Overall though, I'd say that Art of Rally has easily been one of my highlight games of 2020, and undoubtedly has the best soundtrack of recent memory. At 20 quid the price is arguably a bit steep though, so do take that into consideration. However the developer did say that there is going to be more content in the pipeline, and if this comes in the form of free updates the value proposition becomes a lot better.In short: if you like rally games, there's no reason to not pick this up.

_childDocuments_.review: Art of Rally is an odd but enjoyable game that does a lot of things right, but also gets a few things wrong. Let’s go over them.First of all, let's go over how it looks. Personally, I think it’s beautiful. It’s gorgeous to look at, doesn’t really matter what car you pick or which track you're driving, it is consistently stunning to look at. In an age where driving games are all about photorealism, this is a breath of fresh air. I know it might not be everyone's cup of tea, but aesthetically I think it’s right up there with some of the most striking games I’ve ever played.Sonically it’s also very well crafted. The cars sound good, the effects from driving on the various surfaces provide feedback as well as sounding great, but the real star here is the soundtrack. It’s nothing short of phenomenal. It’s perfectly pitched to those real life broadcasts where you’d see Subaru’s and Lancia’s diving over crests and kicking up gravel as they sped past. I’d go as far as saying the soundtrack to this game is immaculate. Even if you don’t buy this game, go check it out on youtube or spotify. It’s fantastic.Gameplay is mostly good. You have the general options you would have for rally games, as well as a story mode that sees you rally across stages and rallies that gradually get longer and harder with faster and faster cars over the space of when rallying emerged as a sport right up to the mid to late 90’s when Subaru, Toyota and Mitsubishi vying for podiums.There are several maps of which stages are built from, all of which can be modified so that the races can take place in the rain (or snow), in the fog, at various times of the day and night. It’s what you would expect really.Surfaces include dirt, gravel, snow, ice and asphalt as well as wet versions of all of these. They all drive as you would expect. A personal preference is that I’m not keen on the tarmac based ones, I have the least fun driving these rallies but I can see why they would be someone's favourite.One thing I do not like at all is levels that have rain on them. I think they are a tad difficult and could do with toning down. I groan whenever I see them in legs of a rally I need to complete. They are like driving on skid pans with how slick they are on top of having puddles liberally scattered that make them a complete chore to play. These levels should be a bit harder but should be an exercise in seeing how sideways you can keep the car rather than struggling to keep the car on the road.Another down I’m going to give the game here is that going off the road sees you reset and eat a 5 second time penalty. Rally is about cutting corners wherever you see them and the game feels so inconsistent on where it will nab you for going offroad and will not seem a little harsh. I think if the driver wants to go off road where it looks like they can, they should be able to. If you do not want the driver to cut, prevent them from doing so with obstacles.Speaking of which, there’s very few obstacles in this game. Roads narrow and widen, but it’s not often you see ditches either side, or have to go through gates or anything like that. There are things like hay bales to slalom through but it would be nice if there was more variation to the scenery.Talking of the scenery. Some of it is destroyable and some of it will bring you to a dead stop. This also seems very inconsistent. If a car looks like it should smash through it, it should be able to smash through it. Yes orange plastic netting barricade, I’m talking about you.Also on the track are spectators, which add a well needed bit of texture to driving. It’s very exhilarating to drive through a crowd and watch them narrowly avoid being hit by a 150kph chunk of metal, but there are occasions where they obscure a corner and it can lose you time, especially as this game features no pace notes.I am sort of bewildered why there’s no mud to drive on, sure you have wet dirt, but it’s not the same. Effects for driving over certain terrains are missing as well. It would be lovely if driving in the dirt of the deserts you kicked up a huge dust cloud behind you. I think this may have been cut to maintain performance? Seems a bit odd it’s missing.Car selection is great. All your favourites are here and present. You can even mod in decals for them. I am sad that we don’t go any further than the 90’s as there are some classics that came after that era, but it’s really hard to be disappointed at the vehicles that made it into the game, as well as the cleverly named “off brand” names. Same goes for the real life parodies of the drivers from each era you’ll go up against, a lot of love and care was put into a knowing nod to past legends both vehicles and drivers. It’s clear to see a lot of knowledge about this wonderful sport has been captured with a tongue in its cheek.Finally I want to talk about performance. For some reason this game runs like butter for the first 30 to 60 minutes of you playing it, and then it starts to micro-stutter and get unsustainable to play as it chugs about. I think it has to do with the game loading between rallies or something, but it really shouldn’t be doing this and it can and will hamper your enjoyment, especially in those long play sessions where you start to get into the zone.Overall I give Art of Rally a thumbs up, it’s a nice game to play while you wait for friends to come online or for a quick 20 minute hit of gameplay, but it doesn’t come without its problems and you should consider those when making a purchase.I do hope that Art of Rally makes a sequel and squashes a lot of issues I mentioned, because overall I think it could be a fantastic skill based time waster if it ironed a few of its kinks out.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr: Although arcade-y looking, art of rally is a rather hard-core rally racing game that is at the same time challenging (due to its semi-realistic physics) and relaxing (for the excellent synthwave soundtracks and gorgeous low-poly scenery). I fully recommend it to casual gamers and racing game players alike.Contents of art of rally:Currently, the game has 8 locations: Finland, Italy, Norway, Germany, Japan, Kenya, Indonesia, and Australia, the last being part of a paid DLC. Each location offers 6 stages and a freeroam map.The stages are the staple of the game. The length varies, but a stage typically takes 3–5 minutes to finish. Each of the current 48 stages (from all 8 locations) can be raced:+ in two directions: default and reversed;+ under 6 weathers: morning, afternoon, sunset, night, fog, and rain (or snow in Norway), although only rain/snow change the physics of handling, while night and fog only diminish visibility of the stages, and the other three are purely cosmetic;+ with over 50 cars, each with different handling physics, all based on iconic cars in the history of rally, ranging from group 2 to group A;Therefore, the game has a great deal of replayability.The game has 5 play modes:+ Career mode. This is the mode to play through in order to see the credits roll. You will experience the golden era of rally, from 1967 to 1996, through group 2, 3, 4, B, S, and A, for a total of 200+ stages. The rallies and the stages are semi-randomly chosen from the pool of 42 stages, in order that the difficulty curve is gentle and that you naturally get acquainted with all locations and all weathers. Playing through the career mode will unlock all the playable cars in the game and their bonus livery.There are 5 levels of AI difficulty, the easiest one beatable by even newcomers to racing games, while rivalling the normal one already requires plenty of practice. You can also select from several damage levels, from none to severe, and you will be able to partially repair your car after every other stage. Note that there is no penalty for losing, nor reward for winning. The AIs do not even show when you drive; only their time is displayed at the end of a stage. In other words, the competition with AIs and the damage system are there to provide extra challenge for those who seek it. This makes the game significantly more Zen and relaxing than most racing games, and suitable for casual players.+ Time attack. Choose a stage, a weather, a group, and potentially a ghost car from, for example, your personal best or world record. Then there you go! Try and see if you can improve your record!+ Daily and weekly rallies. Compete for the leaderboard!+ Custom rally. Pick up to 12 stages from one location to form a rally, customise their order and weather, then compete with AIs in the group you want.+ Free roam. There is one freeroam map for each location. In a freeroam map, you can, as you can expect, roam freely and find collectibles. By finding collectibles in one map, you unlock the next free roaming map, a bonus soundtrack, and an achievement.A few caveats:* The game does not have a first-person camera, but a low-down third-person one. You can slightly adjust the altitude of the camera, the FOV, and its rotation speed.* It would be ideal to play it with a controller rather than the keyboard, due to the need of pressure-sensitive buttons for braking, accelerating, and steering.* The handling may not appeal to everyone at the beginning. Some consider the cars uncontrollably slippery, while some others think the physics is wonderfully realistic. Lacking expertise on this matter, I shall not deliver a final verdict on it. Rest assured that the game has tons of controlling settings for tweaking the handling to your likings. Just spend some time getting accustomed to the driving physics, and you will not be disappointed by this gem.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing.The physics are close to real life, yet the game doesn't take itself overly seriously.The driving experience is about as far from "arcade style" as you can get. There are some modest adjustable driver assists in the settings, but in general the game will not help you to smooth out your inputs. To stay on the road and go fast, you have to think about weight transfer, tire slip, timing, and positioning - just like in real life. Surface changes, elevation changes, and sudden dips/ crests, will upset the car's balance and it's up to you to manage all of that. FWD, RWD, AWD, front/ mid/ rear engine all matters in this game for how a car behaves and rotates.The graphics and illustration style are fun and minimalistic. The music is great, too. It's clear that a lot of care and attention went into making this game.The game has great replayability if you are someone who enjoys driving IRL. Since the driving in this game is genuinely challenging, there is always something to improve on and it's very rewarding to find more speed and more control.I have no real gripes with the game. It would be nice to have some sort of navigation or codriver voice to let you know what turns are coming. The overhead view is good enough most of the time, but the night courses and blind corners increase the chances that you're either going to go off the road or slow down too much for corners. But I don't see a way to add this to the game and still retain that casual minimalism that I like so much, so I give it a pass on this issue.Overall I would recommend this game to any driving enthusiast.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic soundtrack and clean, stylish graphics make this rally racing game a relaxing but competitive racer. The handling and driving is solid and a lot more true-to-life than the graphics would make you think.All the classic rally cars are included, along with fictionalised tracks from the world's top rally locations.

_childDocuments_.review: For many years, the rally genre has been dominated by games from Codemasters and Kylotonn, for better or worse. This is why it's really nice to see a game like Art of Rally, when you're tired of banging your cars in DiRT Rally 2.0While the visuals are stunning and low-poly aesthetic mixes with synthwave perfectly, the driving mode in art of rally is suprisingly satysfying. While I don't find this game better than DiRT Rally 2.0, I extremely appreciate the effort. It is a really good game to play and listen to a podcast at the same time (I have a list of games to do that, seriously), especially since the career mode is lengthy and full of unlocks to discoverI got this game for free, however I think that the initial price point (89,99 zł in Poland) is a little bit too high for what it offers. However, if you see this game on sale for $10, do not hesitate. One note, I love how author of the game avoids licensing by not putting any names and brands on the cars and yet we can totally identify the rally legends, good job with that.

_childDocuments_.review: Funselektor's take on rally is a charming low-poly visual feast that delivers a competent sim-cade experience. The game masterfully captures the delicate dance of counter-steering, weight transfer, braking, and throttle control - all in a cutesy package. RWD is appropriately skittish but agile through the corners; FWD providing a more stable alternative. 4WD is predictably monstrous but require finesse negotiating narrow turns. Road surface, elevation changes, and weather are factors that actually affect how you'd attack a stage - adding a welcome layer of depth to this racer. Overall, a passionate love letter to the age of the supercar. Highly recommended for anyone looking for a racing game that has style and challenge in equal measure.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: Such a cool ass game, so addicting. Beautiful visuals and environments that make you want to take a photo from every stage replay. And the lack of some sort of pacenote system, but its understandable.Awesome game overall that makes me want to go for all of the achievements. :)

_childDocuments_.review: I'll start with the things I don't like: - The physics are generally good, BUT there are occasional wonky moments that are extremely jarring coming from games like DiRT Rally 1 & 2. For example, the moment after the car lands from a jump always feels weird. - I like the idea for the crowd "parting way" as you drive through them, just like it was in group B, but it doesn't really work in it's current state. If you're a fast enough driver you'll just plow through them and shove them aside.  - While the environments are unique and fairly interesting, the tracks themselves can feel same-y . The road is always roughly the same width and has similar curves/turns with very little elevation change or otherwise interesting features. I'd like to see them be bolder with the track design and add some crazier stuff. - I'm not sure if this is just a me problem but it won't let me remap my XBox One controller. I can use it fine with the default binds but when I go to remap it doesn't detect any inputs.These are my biggest complaints. Otherwise, I do feel like the game has been worth my $25 so far. The music complements the gameplay incredibly well, the handling feels good when you adjust to it, and frankly the game is just beautiful at moments, especially when there is soft orange/morning light coming from around a corner or something like that.

_childDocuments_.review: Let’s start with something which came as a shock to me. I rarely talk about the soundtrack of a game, but art of rally is a stand out case. The beautiful blend of synthwave and eighties beats gave me goosebumps. It fits perfectly with the retro aesthetic of this wonderful rally game. I will happily admit the soundtrack alone caused me to lose focus numerous times.No matter which location you drive at, the view is undeniably gorgeous. The low poly style combined with the vibrant colours, makes for a beautiful game. And this leads perfectly into art of rally’s photo mode. Which really lets you take in these sights, I'm a sucker for a good photo mode and there is no doubt in my mind that most players will end up giving this a try. It’s so easy to use.There is also a great commitment to historic rallying which is presented like a sort of encyclopedic. Each vehicle comes with a short history lesson, about the origins of its appearance and performance in the rallying world. When you enter career mode (which is split into decades and then years) you're provided with a short summary of the direction the sport was taking during those periods as you progress. Of course this is all completely optional reading, but as someone who is interested in the sport i appreciated the detail it provided.However, my one negative was the in-game camera as it does struggle from time-to-time, especially in the corners. You might find yourself unable to see around a corner properly, or in the event of having a handshake with a tree, positioning you so you can’t actually see which way your vehicle is facing. This honestly didn’t happen enough to be a major issue, but it did occur enough to be a slight nuisance.This year has seen some excellent quality within the racing genre. And this is one of the best of this year’s offerings, and one that I see myself returning to again and again. So do yourself a favour and jump into the driver’s seat. Can you master the art of rally?

_childDocuments_.review: Art of Rally is a colorful window into a bygone era of unhinged, unfettered competition. It’s a satisfying, mechanically complex racing game that hooks you into the mindset of “just one more race.” It’s also a tribute to rally history, and the developers clearly let their knowledge and interest of the sport’s past influence the game’s every facet.It’s minimalistic in the best way— you, your iconic car of choice, and challenging roads. An exceptional synthwave soundtrack aids in achieving the perfect flow state when you’re chaining corners together at high speed. If you’re on the fence, I’ll try to convey why I think the small team at Funselektor has earned your money with Art of Rally—and importantly, why this game deserves your time.This aspect is deeper than you might expect. It’s not a full simulation—but the handling model is no slouch either. Weight transfer is key, as well as speed conservation and grip limit. Utilizing real knowledge of car behavior and racing techniques will help you place first. There’s options for vehicle damage—the strictest of which will incentivize you to learn every corner and pick your driving lines thoughtfully. Certain cars you will naturally mesh with. You’ll wonder if you can push those cars further. In fact, at some point in your quest for speed you might actually find yourself wrestling with the controls. You may feel like they’re holding you back in some way, you may get frustrated. I personally had to adjust some game settings in order to fully bend certain cars to my will. There’s no vehicle-specific tuning options, which I think was the right choice. But there  meaningful adjustments you can make, to change the responsiveness of the cars.Consider changing the deadzones/steering sensitivity if needed. Some players claim the handling is outright bad. That’s an unfair assessment. The game requires you to understand it. The different driving surfaces demand your attention. Changes in terrain elevation are to be respected, as are puddles in the rain. Each car feels distinct. Each  feels distinct, and you’ll need to adapt to the changes that come with higher horsepower and the advent of AWD. It’s  rewarding and satisfying to master a car in Art of Rally.There’s a wide selection (62) of vehicles to choose from. Each car is lovingly modeled, with several livery options. They are based on real rally cars with a few easter egg vehicles thrown in the mix as well. They all have written descriptions, which are a blend of humorous and fact-filled.I’ve spent most of my time in career mode. It begins with the early days of Group 2 in the late 60s, and culminates in the era of Group A—which ultimately became the basis for modern rallying. However, the horsepower of Group A in-game is much higher than in reality. I’m ok with this for the sake of gameplay progression, and it results in these cars feeling like the pinnacle of what you can drive within the game.At the center is the mythical Group B. Car manufacturers and racing teams spared no expense in creating some of the most insane machines that were constantly pushing the boundaries of what was possible for vehicular development, within the confines of extremely loose regulatory restrictions. During this time in history, drivers contended with many obstacles. They had to tackle dangerous roads at near-inhuman speeds. They had to race the clock, and set competitive times against their peers to make their mark on the rallying world. And, they were also navigating through crowds of spectators—hordes of motorsport fans and photographers encroaching on their path for a chance to see the action up close. A perfect recipe for some of the most memorable moments in motorsport history, and an era that—despite its extraordinary danger and eventual loss of life—is looked upon fondly by rally enthusiasts and former Group B drivers alike. Art of Rally gets this era spot-on. As soon as you get into those cars, the feeling of pushing the limit of your vehicle is heightened. The stages you’ve been learning in the previous classes now seem more daunting, and you begin to morph your driving style to suit the new capabilities of your car. Taking things further, the game allows you to set foot into the realm of Group S. It’s often forgotten in other rally games, as it never saw the light of competition after Group B was canceled. But, the vehicles slated to compete in Group S are some of the most interesting and unshackled 4-wheeled machines ever developed. It's great to see them!You'll race across 7 countries in the base game. Each is varied, and feels handcrafted and engaging to explore—and they’re inspired by real-world rallying locations. They strike a balance between technical challenge and high-speed segments, with their own intricacies to learn. There’s 42 unique stages in the base game, and they can be driven in reverse which adds more variety. Elevation changes and multiple driving surfaces will keep you on your toes. Weather/time of day variation keeps the stages feeling fresh. The cars sound great, and have fairly distinctive engine notes. Details include turbo flutter, gearbox whine, exhaust crackles, and the thunderous staccato of anti-lag. Subtle ambient noises, such as the cheer of the massive crowds or the sound of gravel hitting the underside of the car add to the atmosphere. The game’s soundtrack is  and extra songs can be unlocked via free roam collectibles. The soundscape as a whole works wonderfully in pulling you into the world, making you feel like the hero driver at the starting line we all wish to be.The graphics are simple, but there’s robust detail and endearing care taken in the art design. The lighting and shadows at sunset are stunning. The stylistic choices of the game work really well, from the charming yet accurate appearance of each car model to the cube-like spectators which congregate along the roadside. There’s a full-fledged photo and replay mode which I’ve spent a lot of time in. Your screenshots will be displayed on the 5 polaroids in the main menu, which is a nice touch. I wish there were even  of those polaroids to show off my ever-growing album.Racing games are often misunderstood. Sometimes they get categorized with the likes of football or basketball games—but they aren’t like those. You don’t control a team of athletes. And in rally racing, you are alone on a stage with no other cars to consider overtaking. You aren’t looking at other competitors and trying to outwit or outmaneuver them directly. Instead, your fight is through the intermediary of the track. It’s driver versus road, and the one ally you have in that fight is a monstrous machine which isn’t interested in behaving. You must tame it, convince it. Become one with it. The best racing games allow you to feel a fraction of what it’s like to really be behind the wheel. They emulate what it is to extend yourself into the car, acting as if it is a part of you—and masterfully controlling it to the limits of human comprehension, all the while you’re gripped by the creeping sensation that it could all be lost at any second. That is what makes all motorsport compelling. And in my opinion, despite its simplistic looks, Art of Rally manages to capture that in an authentic and rare way.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is awesome! I haven't fully completed it and I've certainly wrapped myself around a fair share of trees, but I've loved every bit of it. The music is amazing, the art style is really cool, and the game play is certainly challenging. You work your way through faster and faster cars as well as the occasional weather condition. I don't know enough about actual rally driving to say how good the driving is in this game, but I certainly enjoy the process of trying the figure out the fastest way around these beautiful environments. The photo mode is great for capturing really cool screenshots.The only thing that really confuses me is why they need to know my blood type? When creating your profile they want to know your blood type and I find that very strange.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. Love the naming system of the cars as a work around for having to pay royalties, super clever. Controls are pretty solid from what I've played so far and the stages have wonderful variety. My only gripe would be that I would love the engine sounds to be a little more accurate to what each engine really sounds like, but that is very minor in the grand scheme. $24.99 feels a little steep but it is great fun. Check it out!
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very cute, and most of the time very fun. I enjoy whipping little blocky cars down the gravel and dirt.However, when playing the career mode it gets insulting to be told driving my heart out is 7th place, when I did all I could to WHIP my neutron star with bald tires down the gravel track. All of the cars feel weirdly heavy, and as someone who does a lot of driving in real life, sometimes in questionable terrain, the amount of grip (or lack thereof) makes the cars feel too loose. Cars in the real world - especially on tarmac - will corner *way* harder than you think they will before they lose grip.Maybe it's because I'm playing it with a controller, but to me the physics makes the cars feel dialed a few clicks in the wrong direction.Overall though, it's still a blast if you're not playing for times, and I recommend picking it up. Especially if it's bundled with the author's other game.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: Really conflicted about leaving a negative review. After playing through the career mode i'm left with a sense of what could of been, Pros:The game is incredibly unique and offers something that is quite unique between sim and arcade but it doesn't hit either of them at any great quality or level. The selection of cars and content are impressive but are ruined completely by the shoddy physics and map design. Cons:The game is incredibly poorly optimised, after 30 mins of play the GPU's on all 3 devices i play this game on go to 100% load... the devs have indicated that this is a issue.. especially when the game isn't graphically demanding and my selection of hard at my disposal is higher end.The physics and poor map design is a real issue, it feels like obstacles such as straw bales and crash barriers have magnets attached to them. As soon as you brush one of them the car spins and your facing the wrong way no matter how lightly you make contact.The Career mode which I've completed is boring and long winded. Whoever designed the Indonesia stage needs to be fired.The Tracks are not big enough for 90s early 2000s era rally cars, you can only use 1/8 throttle before the car is flying off the track in flames. Really poor  design with that era of cars, many have complained. On the whole its really hard to fully like this game, especially with devs who can't or wont fix the simple issues.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: What I Love: I absolutely LOVE the graphics style and scenery in the game. The gameplay itself is simple, yet concrete and addictive. The campaign is a trip through time, from the late 60s to the early 2000s. What I Don't: As of right now, certain portions of the game feel lackluster and incomplete in my opinion for spending 25 dollars... there are mobile games that have more content for 5 dollars. This game needs a more complete Group A class as well as one for modern cars. A few more locations on top of that to keep the game interesting would eventually make it worth 25 dollars.

_childDocuments_.review: The trailer makes this game look easy, but it is HARD. It will take you several practice races before you stop falling off of the track, or spinning out from hitting a tree. The cars all have some serious weight to them. You can feel the wheels lose traction through the controls. I am used to Need for Speed type games where you put the gas all the way down, but if you hold down the gas in this game then you will struggle to keep control. I had to use the brakes more in one race than I ever did in my NFS career lol. It takes a lot of skill and practice just to get through a track without making a costly error and suffering a 5 second penalty. Getting a good time on a track requires focus and rehearsal. This isn't meant to dissuade you from buying the game, my point is that this is more than just a cheap arcade game. Every car is unique in its handling, and you can tell a lot of love and care was put into every little detail. This is a game that you can keep playing for hundreds of hours grinding for track records if you wanted to. There is also access to community made content, which just keeps the fun going for even longer. If you are looking for a quality rally racing game that keeps you coming back for improvement, this game won't let you down. I'll keep coming back to this game when I want to relax but also still be challenged. Oh also the graphics are adorable. I love a good low poly game that plays like a modern high budget project.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a huge fan of rallying and I also liked Absolute Drift very much, so  was pretty much a must-have from the day it was announced. It has a great selection of cars, pretty varied stages and events as well as a great stylized look. I also like how it's focused on classic rally including Group S which never came to be due to the events in 1985's and especially 1986's rally seasons — do not expect to see the latest WRCs here! The dynamic crowds sometimes standing in the middle of the road further help to give this game a 1980's vibe since crowd control was pretty much unknown in south western Europe back then... The beautiful soundtrack furthers this impression, sometimes you feel like you're part of one of marvdogger's YT rally compilations. And that is pretty darn cool!The FISA groups assigned to some of the older cars in-game are kinda off — which is a problem for enthusiasts only, I suppose. Same could be said about technical data in many cases being on the fantasy side. But why even the very late Group A cars portrayed in the game lack a sixth gear... I don't know. And even supercharged cars at times feel like there's some lag present. Then again, this is no simulation by any means. The absence of pacenotes fits this more casual style and does surprisingly little harm, though there are turns which will run in an unpredictable way or simply appear out of nowhere during fast night stages. I was wondering whether this problem would worsen when advancing through the classes, but it didn't. Partly because even a 205 T16 does not feel like a cannonball on wheels in this game. For which, at least to some degree, the point of view is responsible, I guess.Loading times are (very) short and the game runs pretty much flawlessly. I used to get micro freezes every now and then (appear to be fixed with the latest update) and it only crashed on me once during freeroam with no progress lost.Originally, there were two things I was not overly fond of. One was the unpredictable behavior of cars after jumps. While it's still not perfect, it has gotten much better and is not really worth mentioning anymore. You have to get used to it at first, but that's about it.So there is one thing left, and that's the auto reset when leaving the track. It's far too aggressive in my opinion and disrupting the experience. Give me a (hefty) time penalty, but let me return to the track on my own, please.This on its own can absolutely not spoil the fun though, so  is definitely recommended!Addition: You have to give the dev HUGE credit for releasing content which would be a DLC elsewhere as free updates for the game, so that's a big PLUS which definitely strengthens my "Thumbs up" rating!

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, I do recommend the game. Art of Rally can be reasonably challenging but is also lots of fun. Tracks ranging in lengths from 3 to 12 kilometres are distributed over Germany, Japan, Sardinia (Maybe Spain), Norway and Finland and the game provides a big selection of the the most famous rally cars from the 1960s onwards, with brief and interesting anecdotes about each of them. Needless to say, the driving experience with each of them is unique. One could call it a wholesome game. With updates, they are adding new cars and other features like ghost cars etc. responding well to the feedback and suggestions of the community. The game also has a stripped down but very efficient version of the online daily and weekly events like what you find in the Dirt games. Overall, I find it a complete and very accessible rally racing game, especially for those with less time on their hands and seeking a reasonably challenging but not very tiring racing experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I have mixed feelings about Art of Rally. I have difficulties to drive the cars in this game, so bit disappointed by my very bad virtual car driving skill, still I had fun with this cute game....the artistic graphic. It is just awesome and somehow fills me up with nostalgic feelings. The whole game is colorful and charming, the cars look cute and many unlockable skins are available for them....the music. Additional extra, that not just a few soundtrack available, there is a great variety and additional music tracks could be unlocked in the game....the daily and weekly challenges so there is always something new in the game....the atmosphere. It is actually quite nice to drive in this environment. The difficulty settings still let you unlock each car and skins easily during career mode, even with the bad car controls I mention in the next part....the car control with keyboard. I know that I am not the best in these kinds of games. The game became slightly easier once changed to controller. I am a k+m player, and was always, so bit inexperienced with controllers. I believe the game significantly easier to any player who use controller a lot....the car control again. It feels like the car gets oversteered really fast. Push the left/right (A/D) buttons if you want to turn the wheels and the car starts to drift instantly and need to compensate again with the other direction. This happens already at a low driving speed. Taking a curve is already challenging even if you are driving at a very low speed. This happens to me a lot with controller too, but it is very likely that just because of my driving skill of virtual cars. As some commenters stated out it is normal for rally cars and need some practice, so this part is for those who like me and not playing many driving games: expect some (or lot) practice time:-)... the crashes. Slide to a wall or fence with the side of your car. No matter how you do that, it ALWAYS turns your car that way that you will face the object. WTF?...the double penalty. As I said already, it's hard to keep the car on the road. Now if you leave the road more than a few meters then you respawn on the road and you get a time penalty. Left a bit and trying to manoeuvre back to the road? Don't waste the time, just manually respawn to the road by hitting F1, if you try to drive back to the road you will still likely trigger the autorespawn. If it is not enough during the ~2sec loading screen time is still running and you get an additional 5sec penalty. Most of the time it would require less time to get back to the road. The game is not letting you do that.If you curious about gameplay here is a short content overview and 2 stages completion, so 5-6 mins gameplay:Nice little game for some fun, however I am not 100% sure I would pay 20€ for this game. Feels a bit overpriced, mainly because of my game preferences as i prefer to buy other kind of games first. If you like driving games and also an unusual cute art, then this should be a must buy to you:-) After 300k km in IRL I needed to realize in this game that I can’t drive. At least not virtual cars. Experienced drivers however stated out the driving mechanics is good, i kept the lower score on this only because of the weird crashing behaviour and because of the fact that the autorespawn to the road happens too early, while you still very-very close to the road. Bored and want some fast rally time? 2-5 mins each stage, so always nice to start up the game for some short (or long) play. Nice, artistic visual, decent soundtracks. If my car would stay on the track then it could be even 10/10:-) Nice looking game.. Decent soundtracks and a great variety of them. Also additional unlockable soundtracks by collecting items during free roam. I can drive faster IRL without any problem than in this game, but this based on my own skill, which is pretty bad on driving games:-)Perfection time: ~50-60h. Completing the career mode and getting all collectibles takes about 20hours. Now the annoying part is to play 1000 stages. How pointless and grindy achievement is that right? Now this is a good example of what is a hated achievement by those who like to perfect the game they like. Additionally driving 555km with the same car is grindy too. Only one difficulty related achievement, but right now, at the time of writing this review unlocks even if you not wins the rally on the required difficulty. This one probably will be fixed.

_childDocuments_.review: Art of rally is a really fun game that anyone can enjoy. It's definitely not a simulator, but it doesn't feel like a super ''arcadey'' game like some other racing games. It took me a few hours to get the hang of the driving mechanics on a controller and I could also see this being really enjoyable on a wheel.Some of the things I like about it were:- Art style that is simplistic and fun to look at with some cool environmental effects.- The car choices, car names and all the extra vehicles are a really awesome touch.- Courses; Unique, fun, and challenging at times, but overall a good time. It's refreshing to not play the same 10 courses that every other rally game has.- Settings that allowed you to fine tune all of the various in-game driving assists. I wish you could turn everything down to 0%, but that wasn't a big deal.Some of the things that I did not like:- Camera settings were odd at first. I wanted to a closer 3rd person view and after playing it awhile I totally understand why they want you zoomed out so far(no co-driver so you kinda need to see the turns ahead of you). After awhile I got used to them.- Some of the Norway locations, when you drove on the ice sections, during sunset were practically blinding. It turned your screen almost a pure white and could hardly see the course. One of my biggest complaints that hopefully will be adjusted in the near future.- Some parts on various courses the road was really jagged and bumpy that didn't seem to get built properly.It took me around 15-16 hours to complete the campaign and another 4-5 was just messing around and playing in free roam. The daily/weekly challenges are a nice touch to the online game play.Overall I would totally recommend this game, I got it on sale for $17 USD and I feel that price is perfect for what I got out of it. At $25 USD the price is a little steep with the little features and vehicles there are in the game. I don't think that takes anything away from the game itself, because it was a fun and relaxing game to play in the end. Great job to the small team of people who work on this game! :)

_childDocuments_.review: When was the last time you played a racing game? For me, it had been years. When I stumbled across art of rally, I decided to give it a try because it seemed to focus on mechanics over graphics and user experience before realism. In practice, this gave the developers the excuse to make assets that look aesthetically pleasing without aspiring to look like real life. It also allowed them to fine tune each car for the perfect (at least compared with other racing games) mix of respect for its real life counterpart and arcade-y motion.As you may have gathered already, I have an appreciation for this game that allows me to sing high praises, but there are a few points of criticism I hold as of the date of posting this review. Firstly, it would be nice to select a "ghost" to race against outside of one's own runs in order to better understand the mechanics. Second, any tutorial present cannot prepare one for the vastly different styles of driving required between cars--providing a tutorial for driving different cars might be a welcome addition.Overall, the game is a pleasure to play. There are no DLCs as a barrier to driving cars, only a simple unlock system. This is a no-frills racing experience that takes the best parts of racing games and leaves the rest out.

_childDocuments_.review: Art of Rally is a racing game developed by Funselektor Labs that celebrates the golden age of rally racing. The game is set in a low-poly world that is both visually appealing and immersive. Players have the chance to race across a wide range of stages and terrains, from the rugged mountains of Japan to the lush forests of Finland.One of the standout features of Art of Rally is its attention to detail. The developers have meticulously recreated classic rally cars, complete with accurate physics and handling. This level of authenticity makes the game feel like a true tribute to the sport of rally racing.The gameplay itself is both challenging and rewarding. Players must master the unique handling of each car and navigate each stage with precision. The game offers a range of difficulty levels, so both casual and hardcore players can find a level of challenge that suits them.The graphics and sound design of Art of Rally are also noteworthy. The low-poly art style is both beautiful and functional, allowing for smooth and consistent performance even on lower-end hardware. The sound design is equally impressive, with engines that roar and gear shifts that snap with satisfying precision.One potential drawback of the game is its lack of variety in game modes. While the core rally racing experience is excellent, there are only a handful of modes to choose from. This may limit the game's replayability for some players.Overall, Art of Rally is a fantastic tribute to the golden age of rally racing. The attention to detail, challenging gameplay, and beautiful visuals make it a must-play for any fan of the genre. While it may be lacking in variety of game modes, the core racing experience is so well-crafted that it is unlikely to disappoint.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a labor of love and it shows. The cars, the text descriptions of everything, the stages, the music... Whoever has taken the decisions loves rallying, drifting and general car culture. Even the achievement names are cool references for any racing nerd. When I unlocked the song of the Japan freeroam area (what a treat!), and right afterwards realized that I was in a mini Ebisu Minami... Absolute heaven.As cartoony as the graphics are, car control is very rooted in reality, weight shift and momentum are extremely important. My only gripe with handling is that the cars are extremely twitchy when landing jumps, you absolutely have to keep the front wheels 100% straight or it'll shoot off to the side, even simulators (and I suppose real life?) have a bit of leeway to make small corrections on landing. Oh, another gripe: Even though weight shift is extremely important and affects control greatly, the cars don't move on their suspension at all so there's zero visual feedback. Most of us will pick it up by feel immediately, but it would be cool to visually see the car leaning around.If you like racing games, this is a good one. If you are a racing fan, you will love this.

_childDocuments_.review: Art of Rally knocks it out of the park. Its goal: make Rally-racing fun again...Easy to learn, hard to master this indie gem finds succeeds in finding the sweet spot between accessability and addictive gameplay. Don't be deceived by the somewhat abstract visuals. The racing model under the hood, the way the cars handle differently and the great sound design (music- and engine-wise) makes for a compelling experience.AI times might be a little weird and need some tweaking but that's pretty much the only downside. Art of Rally focuses on the basics that made rally games of the 90s enjoyable. Take the likes of V-Rally 2, Colin McRae 1 and 2 from the glorious PSX era and put them in an artsy outfit with a wide angled 3rd person view and there you go...Highly recommended...

_childDocuments_.review: Art of Rally is one of the most enjoyable games of the past decade for me. On the surface it seems incredibly simple, but get down and dirty with it and you discover there's an incredible depth to the game. Sure, it's no master pf physics simulation, but it certainly has more than you'd expect, and more than enough to make the game feel more than just a no-name phone app, if you know what I mean.The game's art style is incredibly fun and pleasant to be in, and the toy car theme definitely has a vibe to it that I haven't experienced in any other game so far. And it's not cheesy either. There are a ton of tracks for you to race on, and all of them can be played in various weather conditions and even in reverse, so the game certainly has a very respectable amount of content to it. Even the music is nice to listen to while driving around in free-roam or whatnot.Racing is definitely fun on its own, but to me the real fun in this game comes from the challenge of getting mega fast lap times (I'm a bit proud of my world records I used to own haha). I suspect in order to find replayability past 100 or so hours in this game, you will also want to find something fun to focus on, like going for records or mastering all the cars in the game(of which there are many). But even if you don't, the game is still very worth whatever money you pay for it.On PC, this game 100% benefits from playing it on a controller. I actually have it on the Nintendo Switch as well, and it's certainly playable there, but the lack of analogue triggers for gas and brake force a different driving style. I'd recommend playing the game on PC over Switch, but can't deny that it makes a perfect game to play on the go with a handheld. Why not both?
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: Great rally game once you get used to the handling physics. Don't be fooled by the minimalist graphics, the game is not easy or something to just pick up and play. It took 15 hours to complete career mode, but there are also time trials, a free roam mode where you can explore all the different locations, and online leaderboards, so you could keep perfecting the art of rally.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: There are a couple of things I don't like about Art of Rally, like how I sometimes slam into hay bales because it's hard to see blocked off roads, or the insistent techno music that makes me think the guy with the chicken head from Hotline Miami is gonna come flying out of nowhere and beat me to death with a baseball bat.But I get it. The art style and the sound design is the way it is because Art of Rally isn't a game about actual rallying, it's a game about a dream about rallying. It's the place you go when you die if you've spent most of your life dreaming about screaming engines and beat-up suspensions, driven by fearless men and women through forests and country roads across the world. Art of Rally is Ral-halla.It's still extremely challenging, but the horror and violence of rally has been softened to leave only the beautiful bits. The little matchstick men politely get out of your way as you come roaring through corners, avoiding any chance of repeating real-life tragedies.It is also extremely fun to play. The camera means you're never quite sure where the front of your car is pointing, so you're constantly correcting and fighting to keep all four wheels on the road. The physics are really good, it actually feels like those little cars have suspensions, shifting the weight and pulling them towards the edge of the road in a corner.The camera also reminds me a lot of another rally game I used to play on the Sega Mega Drive called Power Drive. Art of Rally is essentially a cutting edge, psychedelic version of that.Most importantly, it's an extremely clear vision, perfectly realized. There's so much love in it. AI drivers have names like "Atilo Beggeta" and "Michele Moutun". Every car comes with its own beautifully written biography. It feels like a game that has been designed and crafted with love to be exactly what the developer imagined, right down to the last nut and bolt. It is fun, it is rewarding, and it is easily the most beautiful rally game you can play.

_childDocuments_.review: An essential game for anyone into racing games. It boggles my mind that a game of such quality and depth came out of just one guy (helped by a small team, afaik). And this is not a case of "Oh, it's pretty good for a game made by one guy! It deserves to be played!". No, this game stands head and shoulders above most of the arcade racing games out today, especially the AAA ones.Getting into some specifics. This is the first rally game I played, and I haven't played any sim racing games yet. The art is gorgeous, the music is top notch and fits the game perfectly. The handling of the vehicles as well as the camera angle is just right - it is difficult to pull off your first drift and do a clean turn, but you're gonna love it when you get it. The driving is not exactly realistic, but definitely much, much more challenging than your average arcade racer. For anyone else coming from other arcade racers into this, I recommend learning to drive with manual transmission - it helps with the drifts a lot. It will take a few hours (you are dropped in a free roam map when you first start-up the game), but the sense of progression from not being able to keep the car on the road to anticipating and pulling off drifts to navigate turns is immensely gratifying. Speaking of progression, the game has a fantastic career mode - with races in different eras in the history of rally. I really appreciate the small blurbs and quips about the history of the cars and events. It  makes the game more complete. Made me appreciate and want to go learn more about rally. The career can also be played through multiple times - since each time the tracks for a season are randomized.In conclusion, if you have even a passing interest in rally racing, and you love racing games, this game is an absolute must play. Chef's kiss. Bellissimo 🤌

_childDocuments_.review: aesthetically and feature minimal but a tightly honed gameplay with great game feel. if art of rally was a guitar... a guitar... then ummm if you were to play it good, you would need to do more than just learn the chords. you'd need to master it. until you can play a sweet lick. and that's what it feels like when you nail a track in art of rally. transcendent, greater than the sum of its parts.

_childDocuments_.review: Put your Helmets on! Fasten your seatbelts! Tighten your racing gloves! ... 3, 2, 1, and off we go!Right upon starting the game for the first time you're thrown into free roam of one of it's 7 countries the game takes part in. In order to unlock the next country for free roam you'll have to find all the necessary collectibles. The great thing about this is that you'll not only get a feel for the game and a certain map before actually racing on it but collectibles are picked up in this game mode so you won't have to restart a bunch of career races because you missed a cassette tape.The game doesn't seem to have official licensing for the cars but it found a fantastic workaround in giving each car a nick name like the esky for the Ford Escort. Also they look like a perfect miniature drawing of its original and come in a variety of liveries that have to be unlocked by progressing through the career mode.The career mode takes you through the years 1967 all the way to 1996 in rallying featuring all the important classes of it's decades from Group 2 to the unforgettable Group B and it's successors. You're racing against the clock on various stages randomly chosen by the game. The cars all handle and sound slightly different and therefore give you a real feel of depth. Different weather conditions and surface varieties will make your live misserable at times but it also adds to the games ralism that you wouldn't expect from it's initial presentation.A birds eye view accompanied by the cute graphics style suggest the game is aimed at young audiences and while they definately should give this a go the game can be very challenging especially if you up the difficulty settings. Handling can feel a tad unrealistic but also has some sliders in the options menu to adjust for example counter steering.The soundtrack is fantastic. If you fancy synthesizer music this will be right up your ally. Also car sounds are superb featuring sqeeky breaks, popping exhausts and rattleing gearboxes. Additional game modes like time attack and Online MP round things up.This then is a great Indi Racing Title with a lot of depth and love for the History of Rally Sport. I recommend taking the game for a spin and enjoy its soothing soundtrack.

_childDocuments_.review: Art of rally offers really beautiful landscape along with lighting, The driving style feels just fine as such indie game should have. It has decent amount of popular cars that existed in such Group leagues, quite maps to choose, pretty clear and modern UI. Maybe it is kinda overpriced, but that's not the main case. So what could be wrong with such ideal game?Optimisation. It really lacks any of it. And I understand that game made in Unity can be tough to be stable, but I am nearly sure that if devs really wanted it to run smooth on not ultra-high PCs they could do so. You only need time, huh? I mean, if my decent PC can run easily Forza Horizon 4, which you definitely could say that is one of the prettiest games ATM on highest graphic settings with no trouble at all, why it can barely hit 60 FPS on medium? And the FPS drops, when you enter into forested area - unpleasant. So grab your code and better fix it!And UI. I was stuck at least 4 times watching 1 line of sentence for 30 seconds just to realise that you have to press any button to get to next line. I thought it was a loading screen! Why won't you put ANY hint that would say to player "you gotta click something, John"? Also, the whole menu and "loading" word could be a little bigger or just at least customizable. Think about possibility to increase letters and maybe add option to customise whole white screen at menu, e.g fill it with some videos from the in-game. And don't get me wrong - it is really beautiful and has it's charm, but it feels kinda unfinished.At the day of release - I would not recommend it because of the optimisation - it is definitely horrible and devs gotta do something about it really quick, otherwise this game won't be as hyped as their previous game was.

_childDocuments_.review: Hello there! I first and foremost want to get this outta the way really quick.... I DID NOT OBTAIN THIS GAME FOR FREE IT WAS PURCHASED UNDER MY OWN FREE WILL WITH MY OWN MONEY.Secondly, i am a die hard Rally fan and i have been since i was a little child.I have a lot to say about "ART OF RALLY". Graphics : I chose to start with graphics because it is literally the worst thing about Art of Rally, and concidering the fact that the old school blocky art style of this game in my opinion is "COOL", "REFRESHING" and completely modernizes this game in some strange semi-arousing kind of way, only heading up in quality from here is a VERY good start.The colors are FANTASTIC!!!! The scenery is FANTASTIC, the stages are all randomly generated with an endless possibility of tracks plus the game uses models of "REAL CARS" (with different names) that are super important and only add to the overall immersion. Car models from old Cosworths, Porsche, Lancia, Audi AND SO SO SO much more. I was very VERY pleased with the overall car selection :) And to cap it all off a very simple and easy on the eyes menu system makes for a pleasant experience outside of the car.Music: The music is actually one of this games strongest points! Growing up in the 80s and early 90s i was exposed heavily to retro music. AND THIS GAME HAS NOTHING BUT RETRO !!!!!!!! Turn the volume up and prepare to get AN EAR FULL OF KEYTAR BABY LETS GOOOOOO!!!!!Gameplay: Initially i was worried about the game play..... I usually find myself playing games like "Dirt Rally" and "Assetto Corsa" and didn't think this game had a chance in HELL of being anywhere close to as enjoyable as those games to play... BOY WAS I WRONG. This game has VERY good physics to go along with a relatively controlable steering system that makes for an overall very good game play experience. You don't need to be f**king Mario Andretti to play this game is what i'm getting at. To be honest i'm fairly confident that someone who has never played this game could pick Art of Rally up and within one night be drifting corners up a mountain in Japan somewhere.... DON'T BE SCARED HOMIE, THIS GAME IS ULTRA PLAYABLE FOR ANY SKILL LEVEL!!!!!!Game play Options: Hmmmmm...... where to start??? Free roam mode? yes. Campaign mode?? YES! Time attack mode?? YESSSS!! Custom Rally mode?????? YESSSSSSSSS! ONLINE EVENTS?!?!?! YASSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSS!!!!!Price: .... This was a little touchy for me.... The game is rather expensive for a plain and simple indie game, however with that being said....... QUALITY OVER QUANTITY ANY DAY! I paid 30$ for this game and have not had a single regret about a single penny! Money well spent if u ask me! And if my 30$ is gunna go towards helping this kick ass DEV. make future badass games like this then i'm all for it!CONS!!!!!!! YES CONS! This game does have some things that in my opinion are lacking, nothing major.... But perhaps in the future they can be worked on.... Things like car camera views, the game only has about 7 views and they are ALL CHASE CAMS which kinda sucks but i understand the chase cam just fits the feel of the game. However maybe a bumper cam, or a roof cam would be a solid edition. Also i would love the chance to modify vehicles. Not large scale just things like rims, body kits, and suspension. OVERALL i am going to give this game a 8.5/10 !!!!! DON'T JUST SIT THERE MAN, YOU NEED TO LEARN THE "ART OF RALLY"! -Thanks Pat.

And the physics in Art of Rally is indeed simulation oriented. You can feel the grip of each wheel, the weight of the car shifting around during cornering, the difference horsepower output at different engine rev speed, etc.However, despite being simulation oriented, Art of Rally is . It does not have all those car modification such as suspension tuning, gear box tuning, and everything. . It is very enjoyable to go into some light simulation rally in Art of Rally, but if you aim to play some heavy rally game with extensive tuning, then RBR or DiRT might be better for you.A good thing about Art of Rally is that you don't have to use a wheel to play this game,  Take the physics part aside, the  in this game is just . It is called "Art of Rally" for a good reason.Instead of the boredom in most other simulation games, the art style in Art of Rally gives you a relaxation and zen-like feeling. It makes you feel like an artist, painting a beautiful curve when you drift.The music is also absolutely fantastic. _childDocuments_.review: One of the best rally game. Like the developer distilled the essences of rally into a pure, concentrated form.Great driving physics. Not quite full simulation, but detail enough  that all of the techniques from actual driving, like power slides, drifts, and weight distributions, work in this game too. Add in tons of cars and tracks, and you have one hell of a driving game.Do note that this is not an "arcade" racing game, and you will have to learn how to control your car. But the handling feel so good, that I kept coming back for more, trying to improving my time and my skills at drifting and power sliding through a hairpins.10/10: Just one more lap: the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Even if you don’t win a stage, it never feels like a failure. Controls are intuitive but challenging, giving you constant satisfaction of nailing a corner, even if you only do it once a race.At its core, Art of Rally occupies a perfect middle ground. "Rally nuts" get a new, unique experience to add to a surprisingly busy market that seems to stick to a rigid formula. Meanwhile, newcomers to rally–or even racing as a whole (like me) are given a creative, inspired and thoroughly enjoyable alternative to everything that may have dissuaded them from driving games in the past.All in all, Funselektor Labs has absolutely smashed it. More of this, please!!!

_childDocuments_.review: Preface this by saying that I would actually recommend this game, but that I "don't recommend it" purely so that this may get more visibility from purchasers who may find this specific issue to be particularly annoying. My original review was different than this one, I have updated it to reflect my impressions as I've played more and as some issues I brought up have been addressed. The main issue (the one causing the negative review) has been "solved" per say but the "solution" was less of a solution and more of a bandaid "this is the best we can do for now" so I'm keeping the review negative until a more appropriate "fully fledged" solution is added. Which it does look like the devs are working on :) .The Issue:Since my original review, the dev's confirmed that AI times were based on leaderboard times like I hypothesized. They also "reset" the AI times to a pre-release state. Originally here was a longwinded story. Since the issue is semi-resolved and this review was long. I will shorten it for you. Basically, the AI times (all of them) are based on human leaderboard times. Thus when the leaderboards were not kept "clean" of hacked/glitched runs, the AI (on master difficulty, maybe others) would go faster on stages than a car would be physically capable of doing, because their times were based on hacked/glitched runs that were also faster than physically possible. We aren't talking seconds, I mean whole minutes faster.  Meaning the AI were literally unbeatable. The example stage I gave was a 7mi stage where the AI set a 3min stage time, I set a 4:28, and the leaderboard leader set a 1min stage time. Here's the avg speeds:1min leaderboard time: 420mph avgAI 3min time: 140mph avgMy time: 93mph avgThis was in Gr.4 cars. 140mph avg isn't physically possible for cars in that class. At all. So my new findings are as follows:With the reset of AI times, AI on master do not set unrealistic stage times. I've done about 50 stages without a single dodgy AI time. HOWEVER, I also now pretty much slaughter them on every stage. I am not sure if this is the AI being worse, or me being better. I now consistently set top 100 leaderboard times on every stage, with most stages in the top 30. Much better than the top 500 times I was consistently setting before. But I'm also pretty sure the AI are slower than before, but I'm not sure by how much. I'm going to leave this info here and let you decide if you think it's me or the AI. Personally, I am unsure, but I'm leaning towards the AI being worse than they should be. Beyond this issue:At the time of my original review I had only driven Gr.4 cars. Since then I've driven up to group b. The RWD cars of Gr.4-2 are all very fun to drive and each vehicle handles uniquely. They don't handle in a "realistic" manner, most of the cars are able to hold slides much much easier than they should. If you're looking for realism here, you may dislike this. I like it quite a lot. RWD cars of Gr.4-2 are all dodgy over jumps, they do some odd bouncing on landing. It seems that jamming the brakes over a jump always has a better outcome than flat out, even if you have the runoff for it. Purely b/c the cars don't take hard landings well. It would be cool to be able to go flat out over a jump without fear of instant death, but I've been able to adjust my style to accommodate the cars. The one FWD car in Gr.4 (the meanie) is still weird to me, handles like a weird oversteery FWD car, not intuitive I find. It is also the only FWD car in the game afaik, so I'm sure not a lot of work was put into how it handles compared to RWD and AWD. The AWD Gr.B cars I have driven are quite a different beast and I'm still learning them, they seem to understeer a ridiculous amount. The Gr.B RWD cars just drive like more powerful Gr.2 cars, which is an easier transition. Graphics and art style are mostly very good looking and seem to run well at 4k60hz on my 1080ti. I would hope so. In my original review I noted that Pop-in of grass/shrubs seems to be the biggest issue, even with the draw distance set to max. Since adding more playtime, this issue seems to be less visible on pretty much every map, except japan. Down the mountain portions of Japan have some very obnoxious pop-in. Other maps do have pop-in but they are much less noticeable, you have to look for them to see them. Original review also bashed Norway for looking a bit barren, and in truth it still does, but I've grown to enjoy the barren nature. You may still dislike it, so I'm still mentioning it. But something about the barren landscape has grown on me to like it a lot more than I originally did. Original review also had some issues with crowds. 1) Was that crowds seemed to move in funny ways that seemed unnatural while I was driving Gr.4 cars. I chalked this up to Gr.4 cars probably being too slow. The "unnaturalness" is still prevalent, but is much much less noticeable in faster cars. Since I've also gotten faster, Gr.4 cars have also had a reduction in "unnatural" crowd behavior. So it wasn't the cars that were too slow, it was just the driver. So with that in mind, if you are not a fast driver, you may also notice the crowds behaving in odd ways when you are driving the lower tier cars. 2) was that dark colored crowd members looked like bollards and I kept thinking I was gonna crash into them. I have since realized there are no solid bollards in the game to worry about, so the dark colored crowd members no longer ruin my rythym. New things:Car sounds are not the best for some cars, the "wedge" (stratos) for example sounds terrible. Lots of the inline 4 cars don't sound good either, some turbo cars you can't even hear the turbo. Some cars do sound pretty good though, like the cozzie sr5 (sierra rs500) it has a majestic turbo sound that I am deeply in love with. Orange temporary fences, the ones that are like cheap and thin plastic. That easily come down in real life? Yeah those are solid as concrete walls. Kind of annoying, I can get used to it sure, but it might piss some people off. Night stages in this game are beautiful, the lighting is just amazing. But speaking of lighting, devs please turn on the headlights in all fog stages. Sometimes I get into a fog stage with the headlights off and can't see anything. Theres also tons of little annoying things here and there that I hate with a passion, but they are part of the games charm and SHOULD NOT be edited in any way. See tombstone barrier things in germany and all of finland. Things that kill your car super easy and make the game way more challenging. So I hate them, but like I  would sorely miss the added challenge they pose. Also the "das uberwhip" (M1 Procar) seems to damage it's engine much much easier than other cars in its class. Not sure if thats intentional, but it's caught on fire more than once for me, while in any other cars throughout the whole game I've barely damaged engines at all. As usual I'll update this review as I play more and as the devs change things. Feel free to leave comments asking questions or otherwise and I'll try to answer them best I can.

_childDocuments_.review: A driving game that can be at times relaxing or at times intense. Here you drive from a top down kind of view with there being plenty of different things to do. Different modes from a career mode where you explore the various large mapped area in search of collecting photo views and other items. The maps are quite big so it can take some time to find everything within, and at times circling yourself and meeting where you have before. You can also race among the many stages that there are and take part in time attacks where you go on a leaderboard to compete amongst your friends as well as other steam members who play the game. Customizations can be made when playing as well from setting the climate and weather of the area you play in to the class of your car. Physics is also a key component of the game, where going too fast and not managing your acceleration greatly impacts your course and can drive you other off the path. The game is nice to play when you just want to do some chill free roaming or replaying the maps and trying to best your time to beat others and be the best.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game that rewards  you for as much time as you're willing to put into it. This is not a silly little arcade game. This game isn't something you'll jump in and be amazing  at in your first go. This game is EXACTLY what it says on the tin. It's a game about the art of rally, and like any art it takes practice. I first picked up this game and hated it. it isn't as easily fun as Absolute Drift (the designers previous game) and at first I hated how bad I was and how I could barely make it through a stage without getting penalties or crashing or flying so far out of bounds that I might as well be playing a catapult simulator. This frustration changed from rage to acceptance to focus to zen. Now I peacefully am working on a time attack and slowly climbing the ladder. You can race against your own PB and just keep trying to beat it, slowly racking up ranking on the leaderboards and for some reason it's just... perfect tranquility and a delightful time. So... would I recommend this game to anyone? no. But I would probably recommend this game to anyone who's read this far.  If you've got the patience for my rambling then you probably have what it takes to really like this game because getting fun out of this game isn't about being good, it's about being zen.
