_childDocuments_.review: I was waiting for this since the second i heard about it. I love the style. One thing I felt was missing from Absolute Drift was color, and this brings that in spades. The menus are beyond simple and while i'd call them cheap in any other game, here, it just fits.If you love driving, drifting and rally games especially, you'll love this. It may not compete with Dirt Rally as you may assume, but it does use realistic physics the best way it can for aesthetic they're going for and offers a good challenge along the way.For a good sit 'down and chill with a controller in your hand' kinda game, i give it the ol' two thumbs up!
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, enjoyed it more than Absolute Drift (same devs). I dont have anything negative to say, it's all good, from audio and music, to the physics, car selection, and track selection. My only minor gripe is how much you can or can't cut the course as there are a lack of markers on a handful of turns but nothing gamebreaking.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: This game could be cool, however the design of vehicle controller makes it artificially difficult.  At low speeds the feel is okay.  However at higher speeds even just a single mm input on an xbox controller's thumb stick for 1/20 of a second can take you from one side of the track to the other.  This is annoying as the ability to chose a position in the lane shouldn't be reliant on ultra micro adjustments on a course input control.  It forces you to make long corners by using very small taps on the analog stick, rather then holding the direction of the curve the way a real driver would. If a real cars' steering was this touchy at high speed racing would not even be a thing.This could be improved by adding a setting to the players input. Allow input resolution to decrease with velocity.  Allow the player to adjust that curve to their liking.  Make it a toggle for players who want it.  So those who have become used to, and enjoy the current control style don't need to relearn the game. That would be a huge improvement imo.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: Not what I expected. I purchased Art of Rally expecting a unique looking arcade racer with some great music. What I didnt expect was the outstanding physics and unique car characteristics. With over 400 hours in Xplane 11 and almost 100 more in the Project Cars series, I am into simulation and realism. From the initial free play in Art of Rally I was hooked. Currently I am completing Series S and intend to play game through again with all assists off and manual transmission (its going to take a while).The physics of the cars and their interaction with the differing road surfaces is second to none. Each race, track, and weather conditions present unique challenges for the driver and car. Every car has unique characteristics. Every bend, curve, and undulation in the road forces the driver to maintain constant control correction and think about every input. The art style, graphics, and music are why I purchased Art of Rally in the first place. All three exceeded expectations. Art of Rally was supposed to be a relaxing break from the hard core racing and flight simming I normally do in VR (speaking of VR, Art of Rally would be a top notch VR experience).  Instead, I cant put it down and find myself challenged each race and struggling to find myself anywhere near the top of the global leaderboards. Art of Rally is a challenging racer which will likely exceed your expectations.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: Art of Rally is surprising deep, with rallies spanning different eras (e.g., 70s, 80s, etc.), a large variety of environments that change with the seasons and weather, and very accurate diving dynamics that apply to the many recognizable vehicles from the different categories and eras.I really did not expect to enjoy Art of Rally so much. The art style is as beautiful as the driving too. Crowds scatter as the cars approach sections of track with bystanders and the open world collectibles are a great way to get familiar with the race locations. Art of Rally is a great racing game and highly-recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: art of rally, i've been keeping an eye on this game for a while now and to no surprise it has exceeded what I was expecting.Beautiful scenery of each rally stage and the music just sets the mood in just right. Every stage has its own challenges and so does every car you choose to drive.If you like a challenge there's always the weekly and daily stages which you can compete against other players for the fastest time with the selected car.Dont want a challenge? Perfectly fine, enjoy cruising around in freeplay unlocking collectibles or just doing stages for fun.Definitely a game you can play to sit back and relax too.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: Basically the opposite of what you would expect out of an arcade rally experience, rather than being inside the car, you're far above it. Rather than eurodance and intense duels it's meditative solo racing. You get better at about the same pace as the cars get faster so by the end you can drive cars that felt uncontrollable at the start. If you liked their previous game, Absolute Drift, you will very likely like this one, it has a very similar vibe.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: The most zen and the most white-knuckle driving experience you can have with a controller. Feels like the baby of Micro Machines with Dirt Rally. Absolutely recommended.Visual style is whimsical and unique. Cars look authentic to their real world counterparts while still looking like a toy. Scenery is gorgeous and colorful, without compromising visual clarity. Music is chill and zen, perfect for disappearing into the background while you focus on the track. Car sounds are loud and authentic, and a joy to hear while you're tearing through the gravel.The driving physics are tight and responsive, not being too difficult that you can't control with a gamepad, or too simplified; real driving concepts and techniques still apply here. Hit the brakes on a straight line, control the weight shift of the car, don't accelerate too hard so you don't oversteer, hit the handbrake on tight corners to throw the car around. Feels like absolute joy to get things right and carry speed through the corners. This game made me wish Dirt 4 had these physics.Car progression is lovely too, as you go through the career mode you unlock increasingly faster cars, until you get to the fabled Group B. Each new class can be picked up in just a couple stages, and by the next rallies the speed will feel natural to you. Try out different cars, they all feel different and unique in driving style.Overall, a joy to play and an absolute recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: Art of Rally is a beautiful and soulful celebration of rallying in an accessible package.  Even though I don't get most of the references, you can tell a lot of love and care went into every aspect of this game.Because rallying is just you and the road, the handling has to be great.  Art of Rally's biggest accomplishment is nailing the feel, characteristics, and "soul" of rallying in a controller-friendly and accessible way.  Even though you're so high above the car, you get a great feel for how to take turns, how to get your car straightened out, and when you're going WAY too fast.This is a perfect "zen" game if you're into rally or racing games.  Just throw on your own tunes and handle the turns as they come.  Probably one of the best rally games of all time, up there with Dirt Rally, Rallisport Challenge 2, and Richard Burns.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting for this game since the demo started, and man I love the full game so much. Everything is organized and easy to follow, and the game plays great. The visuals are fantastic, and not just for a minimalist style. This is easily a 5 Star game, my only complaint is that I think the stability of cars after landing from a jump is a bit too erratic. While this may be accurate, I don't find it too fun for a video game. I was super hyped for this game, and it did not let me down.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: It's a very nice game, though really not well optimized. It runs slower than Forza Horizon 4 or Dirt Rally 2.0 on a fairly powerful machine, and given what's on screen, this thing should fly. Also it would be nice to know the position and which % you are while racing (optional).Another complaint is that while stages / countries should be random (right?), I've done Japan a whole lot more than any other circuit so far, like 50-60% of the time in the last 4 rallies.Other than that, the difference in gameplay between the different cars is very welcome (and well made), but some of them are almost undriveable. I love a challenge, but sometimes it gets a bit too frustrating (Stratos in a rainy day, anyone?) for a game that should be "zen".I agree with most of the reviews about the aesthetics and sound (both are great), even if I'm not a super fan of the extra liveries.A nice little game, but I find other games more satisfying from a driving perspective. I find this one doesn't really know if it's arcade or a simulation, since some things are really not realistic (collisions) while others are really demanding, and personally, I have a hard time getting the "feeling" of how some cars have to be driven (and usually I'm quite good at that in all the other driving games I've played in the last 20 years).Anyway, recommended, I still come back from more, so it's not bad!
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: This game looks awesome, the music is great, and the trailers are cool.  The physics are basically like your car is on ice skates.  People blame the top down angle and say there is a learning curve, but I think its BS.  Drive a car around a slight bend to watch your car fly off the track, if not tumbling down a mountain or into a lake.  Most of the time I put into this game is just trying to stay on the road in free roam.  I really don't recommend buying this game, but the free content updates have provided me with some awesome wallpapers over the years.  I have played a load of sim and arcade racers over the years, and have never ever had this much trouble with a racing game.  I honestly think its broken.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing since around 1.10 and the game has only gotten better and better the more I play. The achievements and car unlocks are fun and challenging, and flow well with the main campaign. This is my first ever racing game and I found myself having fun through every stage of progression, from learning how to maintain a drift, to mastering trail-braking, it's rewarding every step of the way. Only at 200+ hours am I running out of things to do in game, but (at the time of writing) luckily the Kenya Update is soon around the corner. I joined the Funselektor Discord soon after purchase, and the community has been incredible. From beginning tips, optimal setting adjustments, and sharing custom liveries, the community surrounding this game has helped tremendously. I seriously can't recommend this game enough, 10/10 experience all the way through.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: Update: After playing the first two stages (offline).  This game is a perfect blend of "Drift" mechanics and arcade racing. What are "Drift" mechanics? 1. You don't lose momentum moving laterally (sliding). Instead of your car flipping over you slide real fast. 2. To counter this, the game gives you super-counter-steer, the front wheels work real good when sliding. What this leads to is a different way of cornering. But here's the thing, you can still corner the traditional way, albeit at a slower speed, but once you get used to the "Drift" way, it's so much fun. So why did I hate "absolute Drift and love this game? A.Drift was a 2D open world parking lot with one car that you couldn't change. This is a proper racing game with many different cars, beautiful tracks, and you can adjust the "Drift" effects to match your style.---------------------------------1. There is a demo, try it.2. This is not Drift. I love drifting in 3D driving games but hated Drift. This has some similar mechanical aspects but you can adjust them and don't have to do 20 figure 8's in a row.3. You can adjust Stability and Counter Steer and and ABS. I've had luck putting Counter Steer at it's lowest and then adjusting Stability based in the speed of my car.  Fee Roam mode is a great way to mess around with settings, try different cars, and get collectibles.4. Finally, this game is like Trials in that there are no Skills, Abilities, or cheats. Once you have a car your time depends on you and not your level.5. There's a lot of content as far as maps and cars, and so far the cars seem to drive differently based on drive wheels and class, so whether you want to relax and drive around or try and 'git gud', there's a lot to occupy you.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: I originally wrote this in April 2023 but didn't upload it. I wasn't sure how to approach this game from the perspective of a reviewer because it's so bloody perfect, and a lot of these sorts of games I class as "unreviewable". As an example of what I mean, other games that would fall into that category are arcade classics that are still talked about and played over 40 years later such as Pac-Man or Space Invaders, or games with ridiculous amounts of memetic discussion surrounding them like Half-Life or the original Doom. Like, how the hell can words do enough justice for this level of quality and discussion? To be honest, a better review is simply a gameplay video. A picture can say a thousand words.---I haven't had this much fun in a driving game for a long time. It's incredibly hard to put my Deck down, like it was made for it or something. It's relaxing yet satisfying once you get into the flow state, and more forgiving than the developer's drift title. 10/10 soundtrack too. They didn't put "art" in the title for nothing either - this is one of those games that can be used to convince philistines that videogames are an art form.It takes a couple of hours to start driving well, especially as you're forced to drive crapboxes at the beginning, but that means that once you unlock the real rally cars you'll truly appreciate it and know how to use them properly. It's game blue-balling done right, in that it teases you until you desperately want access to a proper car and then oooh it feels so damn good.I guess it's a simcade, but it differs from other simcades in that the elements that are usually arcadey are simulation-like here, so it won't have you setting up your vehicles but you better know a bit about how cars behave. You just go straight into it. My only non-technical critique is that a view from the front of your car would be nice. Regardless, it is a beautiful game, and the minimalist menus bring that beauty to the forefront. You get into this sort of meditative state once you get good, and it feels incredible. Turn off the crowds not only for a performance boost but, imo, better atmosphere.Now for the bad part, and probably the most important: The Linux version seems to perform a lot better than Windows. On Windows the game has very little optimisation. Running a dual boot system with Manjaro, in one OS I can max the game out at 1440p 120fps, while on the Windows it struggles on medium (which are Deck settings at a higher resolution) to maintain a consistent framerate. In some ways it's amusing to me that *Linux* is the preferred OS for this game!!!

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game thinking it would be another small racing game for my collection that I would play every once and a while. Then I did my first time attack and was surprised by the difficulty so I tried again... and again... and again. I spent the first 4 hours on that race trying to slowly climb the leader board and once I finally got to my goal of top 3000 (Ik that's not amazing but it was good for me) I felt so satisfied. I cant even begin to say how much I recommend this game! Its challenging and unforgiving but extremely satisfying once you get a hang of it plus the low polly art style kept a light mood even when I got frustrated. So if ur looking for a unique and challenging rally racing game with a cool art style and realistic physics you should definitely try out art of rally.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: What can I say about this gem...Well art of rally is an arcadish rally game that reminds you that even if you think you're going fast someone is faster than you, either on a local scale or a worldwide scale. This game has been developped by Funselektor, the game Studio behind Absolute Drift and you can feel the studio's knowledge and experience about racing games and going sideways.You start in Group 2, the year is 1967 and you have a sole goal: to go . As time and rallyes go by you will unlock other groups (Group 3,4,B,S and A).Starting from Group B, some fictionnal cars will be present, and Group S is nearly all about fictionnal/prototypes. The game is well made, the sound design is great and the music is really nice. The maps and cars are a blast to drive, from a BMW 2002 to a Ford Focus through the Monsters of Group B like the Peugeot 205 T16 and the Audi Quattro, you wil have a wide array of cars to choose from.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: Simple Graphics, Beautiful music and awesome physics. Not the most realistic, but with stability assist turn off, you can comfortably slide your car around. The first few hours can be tough as you learn the cars and the roads but if you are a fan of rally it is most certainly worth it. I would also like to mention while there is no FFB this game DOES fully support a wheel (much to my surprise as I had bumped it while playing). Overall 100% worth the 25$ asking price, even more so if you can get it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game with great physics and brilliant soundtrack.  Make sure you turn off a lot of the driving aids like steering correction and auto gears, it really unlocks the game - the handling actually seems a lot better after that and you can actually drift smoothly around all the corners.  The presentation is fantastic throughout, there's a daft sense of humour in all of the descriptions too, and then there's a constantly growing 50+ tracks of varied synthwave ranging from stuff a bit like John Carpenter & Kraftwerk to some more more modern 'retro' stuff.  Wicked!
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: I've dabbled in my rally games, it's my favorite racing genre. I'm not great, but loved playing everything from RalliSport Challenge on the og PS against my brother, to Dirt 2.0 on PC. I saw this on sale today never knowing the game existed... and it is absolutely worth the $20 (hindsight, it's worth the $25 at regular).It's relaxing, which sounds weird for a racing game, but this just feels so clean and smooth and flowy. It feels less like a racing game and more like an adventure.Physics-based, good sound design, awesome visuals, good mix of arcade feel w/ drifting, easy to get a feel for, and it has my Swedish brick in it. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: A low poly semi arcade rally game where you play through the "history" of rally era across some fictional stages on different countries.Game has pretty fun handling once you get used to it, in some ways it's actually a better rally game than the recent rally expansion pack for Forza horizon 5 game, in this game rally actually feels more like rally and similar to games like dirt rally series than FH5 with rally skin from that other game.The game performance is quite disappointing considering that this is a low poly game, but it supports 21:9 display aspect ratio well.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a beautiful atmosphere, graphics, idea and it's really enjoyable to see all this. But it has a thing that unacceptable for the racing game -- really handling:  - Car's steering is so slow, its like a grandma trying to park, not a rally;  - The cars itself feels more like an airplane on each jump. There's more problem with sense of speed and cameras, I think, but about this later;  - I feel like the car automatically counter steer even with all "driving helpers" disabled;  - Sometimes you can randomly loose control after jump, even if you jump straight forward on the asphalt. It's really annoying considering that you can't do a fast counter steer;  - The "counter steering factor" option makes you loose control even on straight road, this was the first thing I've disabled;And with all this, there's another things that affect gameplay:  - No sense of speed, so 150km/h feels like 30km/h and at the start you will crash in every tree you see;  - Camera is to high above the car. You can't see the road with it, so on each hill that you don't know -- you will fly away and most of the turns -- will feel differently because of road incline you don't see.  - There's no mini map and/or navigator, you will need to remember all the tracks.Somehow I got used to this handling and even set some good times in time attack mode, but it's annoys me most of the time. I mean, this game still has better handling than all NFS's after 2010. :) But I don't think I'll play it after I get the achievements. My conclusion is if you prefer atmosphere, if you want some hard arcade racing game that will force you to retry the races, or you don't care about your race results, then you will definitely buy it. But if you want an arcade race to enjoy the driving -- this game is not for you.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: A love letter to the golden era of rallying, with a hint of alternative history, featuring a huge selection of iconic cars from group 2 through a suped up Group A (including Group B and Group S). This is not a sim racer, but it's no push over and is demanding enough to reward replay and mastery. The cars feel distinct and behave intuitively (RWD cars feel like RWD cars).The soundtrack is 50 tracks of great retro synthwave and the art style is clean, pleasing low poly.This is rally and chill. A zen rally game that you can play with having to intensely focus on pace notes. All I would add is more content (because I love what's here and want more) and more long term structure and incentives. The daily and weekly online events are nice, but pretty bare bones. You don't really get anything from playing them and the leaderboards disappear once they next event starts (unless I missed something).
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best racing games I've ever played.  I've tried all the Forza and Dirt games but I keep coming back to this one.  The rush of hitting a series of turns in a row perfectly in this game is without equal.  It takes a bit to get used to the timing but once you do, its awesome.   Trust me, you won't regret getting this one
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: Theres something about this game that keeps my mind occupied, the games fun, the stages are difficult to master but great fun to learn. I hope the developer knows that theyve created a game that genuinely feels like a love letter. I've never been much into rally but this changed my mind (although the cars also did that a bit). Its definitely worth picking up if you like racing & especially if you love drifting or rally games. And the low poly art style seriously makes it a thing of beauty. My only hope is that this game gets good modding support & tools, because if we could add our own rally cars, or build our own racing locations? I think this game would literally make me never stop playing it and permanently replace a few of my other racing games. I've been dying for a racing game with its own track tools, and I seriously hope its this game.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: Art of rally is a top down view racing game exclusively focusing on rally discipline in point-to-point special stages. What sets this game apart from others in the genre is it’s stylistic visuals and a handling model that is satisfying to learn.I have played only with the Switch Pro controller so far. The handling feels distinctive, and while playing I feel to be in complete control  of the steering. The game can be played with a keyboard, however. Something about the handling mechanics and the camera perspective evokes the feeling of playing around with matchbox cars and the like from my childhood, it is a very enjoyable and playful experience!The game features dozens of familiar looking rally cars from different decades beginning from the 60’s, along with six locations in Finland, Japan, Germany, Norway, Italy and Kenya.The career mode puts you through randomized sets of special stages with different car classes of each time period. In addition, time trials, custom events and community events are available. The gameplay is simple, and fun. The focus is on the experience of racing itself at is what makes it so enjoyable.The designs of the environments and cars are top-notch, and the visual aesthetics mesh well together. The game is also coupled with a soundtrack that fits the aesthetic to a tee.The game runs well enough on my laptop, I do not have complaints regarding optimization. For the price of the game I have received tens of hours of enjoyment already and look for more as I am learning to master all the car classes and environments. And in addition to that, the developers have added in the ability to mod your own liveries for the cars in image editing programs. The possibilities are limitless. Combine this with the robust screen capture mode and you can have countless of hours of fun hunting for perfect photo opportunities capturing your sleekest drifts or highest jumps.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: I just completed my first play through of the career mode and I've been overall very impressed with this game. It's a different take on rally compared to most other games out there, however, it's done it incredibly well. It's from the same developers as Absolute Drift, so if you've played that game you'll instantly be familiar with the art style and handling.Handling can be a little clunky at times, with the car reacting in ways that seem a little counter-intuitive, but you get used to it pretty quickly. It's nice to see enough differences between car dynamics in each category to be able to find one that works with your driving style. I feel there could still be some refinement that would eliminate some frustration (such as any small brush on a wall stopping your car dead and spinning it in a circle), but overall it's really good for an arcade-style racer.The graphics and level design are awesome! Each location has a very distinct feel to it and the variety of stages is nice to see. I'm a little disappointed to see semi-frequent hiccups in the frametimes while playing which give a little bit of a stutter in what is otherwise a very smooth experience. I'm on a 4790k and GTX 1080 and see small stutters at everything from medium to highest settings. Maybe it's on my end... Regardless, it's not enough to detract from an otherwise enjoyable experience.Highly recommend if you are a fan of rally games and are looking for something a little more laid back than the likes of Dirt Rally or other simulation-heavy titles.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: Never played a racing game that had such lousy, unenjoyable and unrewarding controls from the get-go.Will it get better with time and practice? Probably. But for a game that's relying on its aesthetics and soundtrack to sell itself as a light and accessible arcade racer, it just feels like it fails at what it's supposed to be doing. I haven't been this disappointed ten minutes into a game in a long time.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: I'll start by saying this game is hard. It's not an arcade game, so if you're expecting that back away now. But, that first time I power slid my Mk1 escort over a rise into an off camber left hander I felt like a driving god. This game will reward your practice and punish you if you push too hard. The cars are wonderful. The style is....art. There are a few ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, the engine sounds are a little weak so far, the brakes work a little...too well. But all in all it is a superb driving game. It's like an evolution of the old micromachines games. Utterly love it.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this game but do not be fooled by the cute graphics, you need a good PC to run it. I have an M1 Macbook and even on the lowest settings, from time to time it will drop to like 20 fps. Dirt Rally 1, a full fledged racing simulator with realistic graphics, runs much better than this game.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: Please note, I played art of rally on a controller with default assists and with vibration off.This game is pretty simple graphics-wise compared to other games, but it fits the style of the game really well. It's different from other racing games, which is a good thing when almost every other racing game looks the same. I find the graphics of the game very nice to look at.One thing to note is that this game has massive pop-in.This game has some difficulty settings, and I found this game relaxing and often played on a easy difficulty compared to what I could manage. The game doesn't give rewards for higher difficulties as far as I know, and that's fine with me, because that allows me to play on a more relaxing difficulty. I often played on the "novice" difficulty, when I still was able to win a rally on "master" difficulty.If you didn't know yet, art of rally DOESN'T have any force feedback. When I tested the game on my G923, I didn't feel comfortable with it. I do play a lot of "realistic" driving/racing games, often in interior view. With no force feedback and the camera being far away from the car, I didn't feel a good connection with the car.Art of rally DOESN'T have an interior or hood camera. The camera is far away from the car, and works well at what it's supposed to achieve: seeing the road and upcoming turns. Art of rally doesn't seem like a very heavy game to run, but for me, the game had some bad performance at the start. If you start to have performance issues after playing for some time (for example 1-2 hours), set the vegetation renderer to instanced. For me it fixed the issue, and the game runs pretty well.The photomode of art of rally is very good in my opinion. It really has everything I would want from a photomode. I enjoyed taking pictures of different moments when driving. You can enter it by pausing the game at any time while driving and choosing "Photomode".Art of rally is the best arcade racing game I have tried, and I don't have really have anything to complain about it.I would give art of rally a . The game is pretty short, at the time of writing this I have completed the career mode and gotten all the collectibles in freeroam, other than australia, which is dlc, and I am 1 achievement away from perfecting this game. I do recommend checking some other reviews, since most of this review is just my opinion. Thank you.Edit: After 24.6 hours of playing, I have now gotten every achievement.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: Don´t expect this game to be Dirt Rally 3.0 or Richard Burns Rally 2 because it is not. Saying that however the physics in this game are surprisingly good and you get a real feel for what the car wants to do. The career mode is amazing taking you from 1960s FWD regular cars to 1980s 4WD beasts of machines. I also love this games artstyle, it is different and many maybe will say that the graphics are bad but i quite like them and feel like they are very unique! Overall I will give this game a 8/10.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: A true homage to the sport. Such a fun game to play in and of itself, but also great to play in the background. Enough content that it really doesn't get boring quickly, even though it's such a simple idea. Controls are simple and really easy to pick up, but there's so much room for perfection if you want the best times. _childDocuments_.review: TL:DR: Great aesthetics, decent soundtrack, good amount of content, terrible controlsI've been a lifelong fan of racing games (especially sims) and I have to say, this game feels worse than any other I've played. My biggest issue is the way the game handles vehicle weight and weight distribution. When going over a bump or crest, your vehicle feels weightless with how easily it becomes airborne. When steering side to side though, the vehicle's weight gets violently thrown around, which results in you being tugged from side to side way more than any car would in real life (you can even see this in action in their trailers). Speaking of steering, there's an awkward delay in the steering with every car (on controller anyway). On top of this, cars turn more sharply when going faster speeds which at least I never could get used to. Another thing that is just way too sensitive is the brakes. Even with ABS turned completely off, i'm able to slam on the brakes and instead of them locking like you would expect, I slow down from 60mph to 0mph in about 1 second. My point with all of this? ANy experience you have is not going to help you in this game because this game does not handle like any sim you're used to, like any arcade racer, or even any real life car. It handles like... well... it.If you're looking for a racing game somewhere between sim and arcade, I'd recommend the Forza Horizon series, Dirt 3 or 4, or Initial Unity. Skip on this one.

Handling is riding a fine line between realism and arcade, but close enough to realism that simulation fans like myself who normally can't stand arcade racing games can still have a good time. The differences between cars of the same era aren't huge, mostly it's about the wheelbase and body length, but it's enough to give it color. And the car names and descriptions are a riot. I'm truly in love with this game, despite the few flaws it has. But when in dry conditions, night and fog, I usually get a 2-4 second lead and when I'm unlucky, I fall behind the pack by 5-10 seconds no matter how well I handle the stage.Mentioning this as I'm trying to have 100% victories and no restarts used but kept on getting unlucky with the end results of some stages no matter how fast I went. _childDocuments_.review: Let me preface this by saying it now: No, I didn't get this for free, I had to pay for it.TL;DR: It's worth it if you love racing, it's even more worth it if you're a motorsport fan. My god this is a fun little racer.While I don't have a whole lot of time logged into the game yet, I can say that I'm at least enjoying this like crazy, and don't plan on dropping it any time soon. The art style is so colorful and relaxing, which acts as a contrast to the surprising precision that the driving requires out of you.Learning to balance between the gas and the brake pedals is key to taking these tracks on. Elevation changes can occasionally be a little tough to spot, and taking on these too aggressively will result in you making a big jump and subsequently losing grip and control.I wouldn't call this a sim, but it's far from a casual racer either. It's also a wonderful love letter to the most insane era of motorsport, that being the height of Group B rally. I love this game, and if you love motorsports (particularly rally racing), this is definitely worth the pick up.

_childDocuments_.review: A meditative game in a year of patience worn thin. I open art of rallyand immediately, my eyes softly thank me, as the menu is a pleasant off-whiteUh oh I don't know my blood typegotta ask my mom, maybe put a slip of paper in my wallet--I love listening to the enthusiastic ramblings of friends. Or, anyone, really, about anything they’re really passionate about. One of my dearest friends is absolutely wild about rally racing. For hours he would go on and on about not only it’s history, but the kinds of cute, little cars fighting for victory and near-death (and sometimes unintentional death-death).This game in it’s synth-music laden glory presented me immediately with a comfortable and simple UI, giving me only what I wanted. (Maybe an enter button somewhere to click would’ve been nice though, not everyone has the gamer instinct of pressing enter on the keyboard.) I don’t know ♥♥♥♥ about cars, I own an old Honda Civic 2000 and soon I’ll have to find a replacement, but he’s worked a very strong 20 years in our family. I started the tutorial and a buddha emerges and gives me the kind of abridged summary I love to give other people about things I love. Trees are my friends, but I know it’s not a car’s friend. Deers aren’t cars friends either and living in exurban Ohio teaches you that very, very quickly. Naturally I chose the chunkiest boy I have available to me. I go at it. I feel cool as I feel out the controls to sick synth music and eat my morning oatmeal. I am bad at the game immediately, but as I get used to things I feel the adrenaline rush (or maybe it’s just anxiety). Crashing into anything is comically funny and that’s always a success in a video game for me. So is letting you just do whatever in a wide expanse to figure out how to actually play.  The game is downright gorgeous–minimalist `scapes bring a distinct feeling of lovingly crafted miniatures and not a second goes where you lose sight of your car. Anything blocking the vision of your beautiful, tiny, mechanical friend gently peels away in an imperfect circle. None will impede the beauty of your vehicle, and the vehicle will not destroy the precious nature around it. Trees can kill cars, after all. Every music track is the same. People jump out of the way for your car, but nothing else does. Everything is simple, but the immersion is true. It feels lived in. Whether you know how to drive a car virtually or in real life, or know ♥♥♥♥-all about rally racing, it’s a nice time. It’s not really my thing, but I’m already spending more time with it than I thought I would. If you’re even the least bit interested, try it.If only to have an experience similar to reaping controlled chaos in a Bob Ross painting.

_childDocuments_.review: 'art of rally' is a relatively simple game, but it is absolutely .The low-poly art-style looks great and fitting, the retro synthwave soundtrack is simply fantastic, but the sound and the aesthetics, while brilliant, play support to the thing for me that makes the game captivating - .Funselektor have managed to do something that games often fail, they've managed to make the car feel weighty, and they've managed to do it on a top-down, low-poly rally game. The cars don't just slide effortlessly, tidy cornering takes precision, and the feedback feels oddly good for a game like this.It's yet to be seen if there's enough content to justify a nearly £20 price-tag, but to me 'art of rally' really compels me to keep playing, learn faster lines and shave hundredths of a second from my time. I couldn't recommend it more.

_childDocuments_.review: I prefer the more hardcore of racing sims, so I was bit hesitant when picking this up on sale. However, almost immediately I was drawn in. This game is a love letter to the old days of Group B, hardcore, fast, unsafe rally that doesn't make you buy a wheel or understand pace notes. You have a road, you have a car, and that's it. Don't be mistaken, though. This game *is* difficult and you *will* crash. The car's handle beautifully, right up until you careen into a lake when you take a hairpin too fast. It makes getting a podium rewarding as you grind your way to the top specs. Add in a very lovely sense of humor in the flavor text and an adorable low poly art style, and you have a game that will devour your time.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't often post reviews but I was compelled to because this is an absolutely gorgeous game. If you like their previous release, Absolute Drift, then you'll like this too.There is a nice variety of tracks and locations which can be played at various times of day and in different weather. On top of the career mode there is a free roam mode where you can drive around the various environments and search for collectables. For me, as a fan of Synthpop and Synthwave, the soundtrack is great.Art of Rally is certainly the right title for the game, as it is a brilliant work of art and has bucket loads of charm.A couple of things I'd like to see improved or added:The replays are cool as they are now but I'd like to see a replay editor for saving replays and placing custom track side cameras, think of something a bit like what Driver had back in the day. It's not something I would usually be that bothered about in a racing game but here the environments are so beautiful that I actually want to spend more time flying a camera around and chopping together custom cameras in replays.More camera angles would be nice. Even the lowest camera option can get a little frustrating at times as changes in elevation can be hard to see. Or you can see a hill coming but then it turns out to be much bigger than you expected and you send your car rolling. I also find my eyes flicking between my car and the top of the screen a lot as I attempt to see what the track ahead is doing meaning is sometimes lose control of the car because I wasn't looking at it. I think a lower more traditional chase cam would help with these issues and would just be a nice additional option to have.But the camera doesn't detract from the game that much for me, although it can be a little frustrating it doesn't stop me wanting to do the next race and the next and so on.It's a beautiful, charming, addictive, game. I highly recommend picking it up, well worth the price in my opinion. 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible game! Beautiful art style, lots of great looking sceneries with numerous race tracks. _childDocuments_.review: What do you want out of a racing game? Most people want their favorite cars, customization, and multi player capabilities. All I want out of a racing game is good physics and good tracks, and this game delivers tenfold. The cars are all based on real rally vehicles, and the tracks real locations. There's plenty of opportunities to throw the cars sideways, reach high speeds in long straightaways, and wipe out of you aren't careful. _childDocuments_.review: This game has a few critical problems that made me regret my earlier positive review.>There is an enormous control delay, like I had never seen on a racing game before. It makes the controls intentionally artificially difficult. It can be very frustrating. It forces you to anticipate your every move on a very bad way. It feels like your controls are lagging badly as if there was something really wrong with your controller.>When using a controller, the controls are really unpredictable. Sometimes big clicks to turn don't do nothing, sometimes little clicks put you sideways in the trees. There is a problem there, and it makes it incredibly artificially difficult to keep the car on the track, specially on fast sections.>Car recovery when out of bounds (5sec penalty routine) are way too unpredictable. Sometimes you cut a corner by going beyond the tree lines, as seen on world record replays, and nothing happens, sometimes a little touch on the grass and its reset with +5s penalty. Its as if this game penalise honesty and prizes cheaters. Since there is no indication whatsoever of where the boundaries between valid track and 5sec penalties are, instead of driving well to be fast, you're looking for places where you can abusively cut corners without been penalised; penalised not by a natural feature, but by an artificial invisible boundary. Its not consistent and it's not fair.>There is also no mini-map or pace-notes and often the ground ahead is covered by a hill or tree line; a tree line well placed so you can't see the blind corner behind; just like a trap. This means that to drive fast, you need to grind and try the same track several times in order to learn where the artificial traps that are covered by the terrain are.>Cheating. Career AI times are adjusted automatically to an average of the "multiplayer" leaderboard. For a stage like group-b noormarku morning, which is not a fast stage, the average speed of the #1 of the current leaderboard is 172km/h AVERAGE! HOW CAN THIS BE POSSIBLE? And worse, this affects directly my career AI. FIX the damned cheater FFS!

_childDocuments_.review: First: the game itself. I've played a lot of trackmania and have really liked the way the cars handle. Art of Rally does not have extremely tight controls like trackmania, but they have a lot of options for how your car should handle. After about an hours worth of finagling, I was able to get a relatively simple control on the car. Honestly, the settings are only 1/4th of the equation. The meat is simply mastering the unique physics of the game, then you should be able to maneuver sufficiently with any car. The trick that I found is that slight turns are very responsive, but the 90 or 180s should have a good brake or lead up angle to make it without issues. It takes a ton of practice, but in doing so, I quickly entered the top 1% of a lot of the time attacks. The terrain is pretty cool. There isn't a large amount of variety in the design around the roads, but its on theme so it works. I don't get tired of playing the maps, however, it does make it harder to distinguish which map you're playing and, following that, any checkpoints to distinguish turns. Overall, the game is exactly what I expected. But the best part of this game is its support. I've been playing this game on an M1 mac. It runs great. I did notice early on though that my steam save was overwritten and wiped out half an hours worth of playtime. I thought it was a fluke so I kept playing. On my 24th hour of playtime, the error appeared again where my save was wiped and stored to the cloud. I sent a message to support and they worked extremely quickly to recover my save files. They weren't able to replicate my issue, but I think running games through the pinned app on the dock may be running a fresh save instead of running it directly through steam's library. For how quickly their team cares enough to have quality support, and for the great quality of gameplay, I would recommend buying this game and supporting this developer studio.

_childDocuments_.review: When one of my friends posted this game in the group chat on discord, I was very curious. After checking the steam page, popping in on the broadcast, and watching some of the store videos, I was hooked. It's not often that you come across something that draws you in like this.I. Love. Rally. I freaking love it. So I decided to give this game a shot, and I am  satisfied.This game appears to be arcade but that's it's trick. Every car and course will be different and new. You don't run out of track. You'll learn how to handle and master both course and car after a while. And while the maps are gorgeous; you'll be spending most of your time keeping your eyes on the road ahead. Check out the replay function and catch your best moments, which is also a great tool for studying your driving. There's a lot to explore starting off, and I don't want to spoil too much!Third person view from the eagle-eye perspective is alright, but not great. Something closer to a chase cam might be something for the future which would make the game probably feel immersive like other rally games. However for someone starting out, this view will help to teach them how to predict turns and calculate their slides.There's plenty I haven't explored yet, and I'm sure plenty is to come in future in the form of new courses, vehicles, and game modes. If you've got the money to spend and  enjoy the thrill of rally driving, this game is worth picking up!

_childDocuments_.review: A quite decent game with a great concept is undercut by invisible walls, poor attention to detail and a somewhat strange handling model leaving it somewhere in between a relaxing "zen like" tribute to the greatest form of motorsport and a rage inducing nightmare with frustrating map design, invisible walls and a lack of the finer details that would have made this game the love letter to Group B and rally fans it claims to be.  This game features a wide variety of rally cars from all different eras from the 1960s through to the 1990s as well as a parallel universe class known as "Group S" which is the developers interpretation of where rally development would have gone if Group B was not discontinued. Really this is one of the games main strong suits as it most certainly has a wider variety of cars than you would first expect (including my favourite the Ferrari 288 GTO EVO which never actually got to race as it was developed right as Group B ended). However a few let downs were the engine note of each car being far, far too similar and a few famous liveries being left out of the options, although these can mostly be overlooked.Another main selling point of this game is its somewhat unique low poly / cartoony artstyle this in my opinion works quite well with the semi arcadelike feeling that this game was going for with its more striped back approach. Overall I like it quite a bit (especially how the different time of day impacts the look of each stage) however some of the stages / maps have textures clipping into each other and other details which undercut what is otherwise a really appealing clean artstyle. The worst part is the new Indonesia maps don't have this problem which tells me that it is absolutely fixable and it is just a product of the devs not putting the effort in to get the game polished on release almost making the game feel a bit rushed when it should be leaning more in the labour of love direction, considering how this game is supposed to be a tribute to Group B and all.  Another positive of this game is the inclusion of different modes which can suit different play styles / moods and can add variety to the gameplay they are as follows:In this gamemode you play linearly through the history of rally starting in the 60s and working your way through chronologically until you reach Group A rally (Group S is slotted in between Group B and Group A and it is required that you play through Group S before reaching Group A). The career mode is broken up into the years each class of rally took place in (eg. Group B in the 80s and Group A in the 90s) you play through each year completing multiple rallies competing not only in each stage but each rally and also for the overall championship for the year. Throughout the career mode you will unlock cars and (if you have at least one restart remaining at the end of the year) bonus liveries which add a small sense of progression on top of the fact that you are progressing forwards in the history of rally after completing each year. this is my favourite game mode purely because it adds a sense of competition through the AI and it is such a satisfying feeling progressing into a new era of rally as the cars feel completely distinct across classes.This game mode has you compete against the clock in the car/stage/conditions of your choice nothing more nothing less. You can try to work your way up the leader board or just improve upon your own times using either the world record ghost or the ghost of your fastest time.Freeroam allows you to freely travel across a map (eg. Finland, Japan, Sardinia etc.) collecting the letters R, A, L, L, Y, to progress to the next map as well as collecting points of interest (which are spots where you can get a scenic view of your car against a backdrop of the map) and cassettes which unlock different songs for the soundtrack. All of these elements are hidden across the map encouraging you to drive around and explore, this gamemode is pretty good to unwind to as there is no real pressure to preform and you can just drive your favourite car as you wish through each map.For example there are a lot of invisible walls right next to the road on all stages, this means that for some tight corners for example cutting the corner close to the road is absolutely fine but for other corners you'll clip into an invisible wall which will send you tumbling through the sky ruining your stage and breaking any immersion / flow state you may have been in. This isn't only an issue when it comes to corner cutting however sometimes if you find yourself drifting slightly off of the marked road / track you will come head first into an invisible wall which will not only take away all of your momentum but if playing with damage turned on will ruin your car. I must stress that these invisible walls are  the road in a lot of areas and are in no way consistent making some stages feel like a game of random chance instead of a test of skill. What I will say however is this seems like it may not be as bad in the new stages added in the Indonesia update or at least it doesn't feel that way.As much as this is personal preference for me the handling in this game exists in a sort of 'no mans land' between being completely arcade like and being semi realistic almost as if the devs weren't sure in which direction they wanted to go and instead went straight down the middle. It definitely could be worse though and it is something you just get used to after a little bit of playtime, however I still sometimes find myself surprised when a car behaves unexpectedly relative to the road surface (tarmac, snow, gravel etc.) which can sometimes feel a little counter intuitive the main one that sticks out is the lack of grip on tarmac for example. As much as I want to love this game it is the smaller details and the frustrating at times gameplay that let it down for me, for any die-hard Group B / Rally fans I would still recommend picking up this game on sale as there are definitely a few details (especially the cars) that I'm sure you'd enjoy to see in a game like this. If you are just looking at this game for an arcade like rally experience I am sure there are better options out there that are worth looking at as it would be a bit harder to overlook the more frustrating elements of this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not a huge fan of top-down racers (specifically), but this has had my interest for a while and I finally got it from a recent Humble Bundle. If you're into top-down racers, you'll probably like this too. If you're not, it won't change your mind. + Graphics/AudioThe game is pretty, just look at the screenshots. The simplified car models look good. Cars sound distinct as well, which is great for an indie racer like this.+ Driving PhysicsCars feel nice and all feel unique to drive. Definitely on the arcady side of things, but you'll still need to take care to not put your car into a tree.+ Runs great on both desktop Linux and Steam Deck.- PenaltiesA penalty system should punish players who try to cut corners, and in some cases it can double as recovery time for major crashes. I think DiRT R/4/R2 nail this, here's how these games would handle off-track situations so you can understand why this is a negative for Art of Rally.1. Flying off a cliff, with no chance of driving back on track.DiRT: Immediately recover, time penalty added.Art of Rally: Immediately recover, time penalty added.2. Sliding off track, stuck in a ditch, etc.DiRT: May prompt to recover, but will not do so automatically. You can manually drive back on track if possible. You've suffered a time loss from the mistake, but that's it.Art of Rally: Immediately recover, time penalty added. You've suffered a time loss from the mistake AND you get a penalty for making the mistake, adding insult to injury.3. Sliding slightly off track, overshooting a corner or cutting a little too much with no need for a recovery.DiRT: No recovery, no penalty.Art of Rally: Immediately recover, time penalty added because screw you.I understand DiRT's track design is significantly more dense and makes corner cutting and track extending less appealing, but Art of Rally's automatic car recovery is so frustrating in comparison. More than 75% of recoveries in my play time I could've manually recovered from in less time than the penalty gave me. I don't think DiRT has ever recovered me when I didn't want it to across dozens of hours in those games.* CameraI'm not a huge fan of top-down racers like this, so this might just be me. I found the default camera configuration to be awful. You can't look ahead while retaining the ability to see your car or feel what it's doing. Luckily, you can max out the camera rotation setting to have the camera follow the movement of the car. If the car slides, your entire view follows it. This doesn't solve the problem, but was a huge improvement. I would've preferred a first person or chase camera instead, but that's not an option.Aside from those two complaints, I am still enjoying the game. 7/10 so far.

_childDocuments_.review: I am not someone who knows a lot about rally or racing. The only experience that I have with racing games is playing some of the earlier Need For Speed games ~15 years ago. However, I came across a video of art of rally on YouTube, and thought it looked gorgeous and might be interesting to try out. And wow, what an adventure it has been.The game (I will only be reviewing the career mode) is divided into 6 "worlds" or "groups", which each have 5 rally races, consisting of 2-5 tracks, within them. Each group has a certain specification of car, and the farther you get into the game, the more powerful the vehicles are. The earlier groups have shorter rallies, and as you progress, the rallies get longer, with multiple stages. The graphics and aesthetics of the entire game is absolutely stunning, as seen from the screenshots. There are a wide variety of tracks that you get to race down, with varied landscapes, from frozen lakes, to rocky forests.Playing with the controller is a sublime experience as the rumble and vibrations really help to get across what's happening in game. As you drift, the controller vibrates in accordance with your drift, and as you straighten out, your engine roars, but the controller becomes steady, matching your experience on the track. In a piece of beautiful design, unlocking a rally only requires you to have completed all the previous rallies. There is no need to win. This means that the entire game is just a long series of experiments to see how the cars work, and what is the best way to move all that power through the long and winding tracks.Being an absolute newbie to the genre, this experimentation was liberating for me. In the first world, Group 2, I struggled to control the vehicles. I searched a bunch on YouTube, but there were no guides for this game available. So I ended up watching a lot of real world rally content, as well as content for other rally games like Dirt 3, and I learnt that the "Meanie", with its front-wheel drive should be a lot easier to control, and I finished up the first group driving just that one car.Entering the second world, Group 3, however, I saw that there was no front-wheel drive available, so I was forced to actually learn how to handle the hefty backsides of the vehicles, sliding all over with a mind of their own. I realised that once the car is drifting, pressing the accelerator will tend to prolong the drift. This is useful in the early stages of a drift, if you have realised that you started off too early. However, this also means that if you are sliding uncontrollably, trying to straighten your vehicle on a straight, it's best to just lay off the throttle and allow the car to settle down. Slowly I learnt to understand the cars behaviour and got an instinct for nailing the throttle at the exact moment that the car has regained grip, and that was exhilarating.I found myself doing fairly well on the "Normal" difficulty, so I thought I would up it to "Skilled". The races became more challenging, and I found that I seemed to have a very wide range of performances depending on the surface. I struggled to perform on tarmac, and I dominated in rainy conditions. Again, I went back to watch some real world rally content, and saw my mistake. I had been treating all road conditions as equal, and was just drifting through all corners to my hearts content. I learnt that on high-grip surfaces like tarmac, it is better to spend as little time as possible drifting, as you be a lot faster by braking late and accelerating out of corners. On snow and rainy conditions, acceleration was much slower, so drifting was useful to maintain speed through corners.Progressing further, I decided that I wanted to try out manual gear transmission, just to see what it would be like. So I started off Group 4 by shifting the difficulty down to Novice, and checking the controls to see how to shift up and down. It took a while to get adjusted to, but soon it was even more fun. I slowly learned that shifting a gear up in the middle of a drift just because you engine is over-revving is not a good move, because once the drift ends, you will be a lot slower, and will need to be on the lower gear. I found that it is better to be on the lower gear and quickly shift up, rather that being in the higher gear and slowly gaining revs. However, I also saw that if stuck in a higher gear, it was better to swallow that loss than to shift down and shift back up, as it tended to be slower overall. It seemed that shifting into a higher gear near the end of a drift, can end the drift and get you accelerating out of the corner (however I am not entirely certain that this is the case, as it just might be that I have figure out the exact moment that a drift ends, and just happen to shift gears at that instant). The game got a lot more involved, and a whole lot more fun.Moving to Group B, I was back at Skilled difficulty, but now with manual transmission. The rallies were getting longer, and multi stage rallies were becoming more common. Now that decision to unlock progress based on completion rather than wins started to shine through and allow for some truly memorable moments. I was on the last track of a rally, and in second place behind one of the Finn AIs. I was around a minute and 13 seconds behind, with the Swede in 3rd being more than 2 minutes behind me. With the last stage being a 2.6 mile tarmac course, it was unlikely that I would be able to gain that much time. So I just blundered my way around the course, confident that I would keep my second place regardless of the result. I ended up finishing the race in 6th, but to my surprise, was leading the rally. Turns out that the Finn in first had hit a house on the race, and ended up 4 minutes behind the winner. I would never have been able to experience that rush of joy and relief if I had been forced to restart the whole rally for the sake of winning to unlock progress.Group S was when it all started to gel. I suddenly learnt the power that is available in first gear. The pure boost that you get coming out of a corner was almost palpable through the screen. I learn to take hairpins on 2nd gear, and then shift back down to first, as I straightened the car out of the turn. I felt the thrill of gunning down a straight on 5th gear, having absolutely no idea where the next turn would be, and absolutely fearful in the knowledge that there was a 20% chance I would not be able to slow down in time, and would probably throw myself off of a Scandinavian mountainside into the sunset. I found myself perfectly shifting gears as I slid sideways over the snowy track in the middle of a frozen lake, inches away from the edge of the road, which would be a slippery slide into oblivion (commonly experienced as a forced reset and a 5 second penalty).I cursed those pillars along the sides of the German freeways, which instantly kill all your momentum. I prayed that as I slid off the Japanese downhill slaloms, a tree would manifest itself, and perfectly kill my momentum, and leave my car facing in the correct direction. I finally learned to quickly recover from a spin-out, by shifting all the way down into reverse, gathering a little momentum, and start the rotation to face forward, while quickly shifting into second and maintaining all that momentum with a perfect J spin.I am currently in the middle of Group A, the final group. But the more I play, the more I realise that though I am almost done with the career mode, I am not close to finishing the game. I am probable going to go back through, and play on the highest difficulty, and try to win all the rallies. Maybe move to time attack mode, and memorise a few tracks and perform better on them. Maybe return for the daily and weekly challenges as well.This game has been an incredible experience for me. From learning about racing and all its intricacies, to to soaking in the Sardninan sunsets. I would give art of rally 5 stars.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is easily my favourite single player racing game and has been for about 3 years or so. I love physics based racing games with good drift mechanics and satisfying manual gear mechanics. I played in automatic initially but after playing for so long I wanted to add some difficulty. I am gonna break down my points in a bit of a section style starting with visuals:Visually really beautiful, especially if you like games that have retro inspired graphics but without any limitations to lighting and with lots of added variation. It has great weather and time of day represented through the sun position, really pretty sunsets and sun rises, rain effects and snow. Also night racing which is pretty sketchy too and adds a bit of difficulty. With lots of nice detail and clutter around the tracks to make it feel lived in and interesting to explore even though you are usually passing through too quick to notice.Mechanically really enjoy the feel of the driving, especially in manual which gives a lot more control in drifts in this game, every car has super unique handling, different styles of driving suited better for different tracks or weather conditions.Really tough to anticipate though as it is pretty random what the weather is like (which adds to realism for me), and the set pieces that make up the track each time is randomised which I really appreciate. Others might want to be able to prepare but having that random unpredictability is what has kept me coming back to this game for multiple years. Feels a lot less repetitive this way. Extra challenge in the difficulty levels of the AI in career and in the damage sustained from your mistakes and accidents are really nice ways to increase difficulty without just making weather and track conditions just being arbitrarily harsher.I really appreciate the attention to detail with concern to the damage the car sustains. from the gearbox to cleaning the mud off, when your repair comes in a long season on career mode, you feel the relief. Very well designed and very carefully balanced. There  are other game modes that I haven't really explored yet as I am still in the process of completing all career seasons and getting 1st with highest difficulty and most realistic damage with manual gears. So there is plenty of gameplay to get out of this game for the price I think definitely worth it.They have clearly put an insane amount of effort into the control and feel of each car as well, I cant stress that enough.It has the right atmosphere for me. And I enjoy the super hard core racing mechanics and punishment for mistakes whilst having a more arcade like camera view and graphical style. Definitely captures a bit of a minimalist feel, similar to Lonely Mountain Downhill which is also an awesome game.I would say it takes quite a great deal to damage a wheel and affect your turning from doing so, this is probably unrealistic but also increases quality of life in game play. In a game like wreckfest where realistic damage is on and one wheel is damaged, it does mean you will almost 100 percent of the time have to restart instantly so I actually kind of prefer this way although initially I found it to be too weak.Im pretty sure these devs have been consistently updating this for the entire time I have owned the game. They have been working on the set pieces and increasing the amount of variety in the generation of courses.Really love this game. Get it.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't know how people enjoy this game. The starting car feels like a complete boat and there's no way of knowing what's coming up ahead. No co-driver, pace notes or map. May be worth it on a heavy discount or if you've a lot more patience than me, but I wouldn't recommend it on it's own merit.

_childDocuments_.review: 40% budget was spent on camera and replay system30% budget was spent on original soundtrack25% budget was spent on making trailers n marketing5% was actually spent on gameplay, feels you driving the moonlander and there is no gameplay video in any of the trailers, well played psyop into selling you into the culture of rally but with no real content and floaty boating handling, if there was no fancy camera replay system or original soundtrack this game would have had zero magic or vibe to it and not sold as well as it hasif you want to play a proper fun arcade/simcade rally game pickup a key for DiRT3 Complete Edition it had a fancy replay camera system AND actual gameplay with proper handling physics where the car moves and brakes as you would expect it toofor 25-40 dollars and the lowpoly flat graphics this a very polarizing and niche game, the vibe is great but thats about all it has to offer, its just not for everyone or the average gamer, especially at that pricepoint for what you get, this game is like a fancy $400 meal at a fancy restaurant but its just a cilantro leaf on an icecube sized portion of beef - whereas DiRT3 was amazing both for rally enthusiasts and average gamers both of which could just jump into and genuinely enjoy, with zero frustrationthis game leaves you hungry for more n you just end up gaslighting yourself into thinking theres something there and you're having fun n theres more to it - when it just keeps leaving you hungry for something more, the progression and seasons is the only system I'd assume that keep ppl actually hooked and addicted - as for just jumping in n getting a dompaine rush of thrill, that isnt there in the slightest

_childDocuments_.review: A competent racing game, just not a very good  game. The irony is thick.Pros:+ Physics. The cars are weighty and different enough from each other based on rally class; they are a joy to maneuver over the many terrain types+ Graphics. The neon pastel colours fit the minimalist aesthetics of the UI / cars / terrain perfectly+ The sense of progression. Unlocking cars and new liveries while advancing from one rally class to the next is satisfying+ The cars. Most of the iconic rally cars from the '70s up to the '90s are in the game, easily recognizable (although with silly names and cringe descriptions that subtract from the immersion)+ The music. There is a variety of styles that suit the arcade-y nature of the game well+ Custom car liveriesCons:- No keys rebinding. This, along with the next two points, is absolutely inexcusable in this day and age- No pace notes, either as audible or visual indicators. In a rally game. Let that sink in- The dev obstinately refuses to allow for custom car and driver names, invoking the ROI (!) and the mess it would make on the online leaderboards. Quickly and easily debunked by the next forum reply:Shows that not everyone falls to the dev's egregious gaslighting attempt. He said numerous times that people come to the game with various expectations, and it's on them to adapt to the game's 'vision', therefore everything should be taken as-is and accepted unconditionally. To that I say that maybe it is him the one who is confused by what he wanted the game to be vs. what rally racing actually is. When you call your game 'the art of rally', people come with the clear expectation to play a rally game, not the dev's own vision of what rallying is, or should be- Inconsistent physics. Employing real-world rally techniques will not get the fastest times (despite the presence of  in the game's name and even having the  achievement hinting to this effect). Instead, touring-car type cornering is the way to go, as advised by one forum user:- Inconsistent physics. Side-swiping the guardrails will turn the car 180 degrees. On purpose, just to fxck with you, courtesy of the dev- Inconsistent rules in regards to corner-cutting. On some you need just touch the grass to be auto-resetted while on others cars are allowed to pass through unpunished. This, in turn, leads to the next point- Uncurated online leaderboards. Instead of promoting fair-play racing - in the spirit of rally-racing which the dev claims he tries to emulate - people are encouraged (through non-intervention) to find how much they can cut corners without penalty. As a result, the leaderboards are populated at the top only by 'cheaters' and no-lifers- No multiplayer of any kind. No online servers, hot-seat or split screen, nothing. Daily / weekly challenges are no substitute for head-to-head rally racing- Weak, buzzing, unconvincing engine sounds, particularly the Mazdas' rotary ones which verge on the unbearable- The camera. Only external cameras are allowed during gameplay. No optional hood or bumper views, let alone car interiors and view- Extremely short stages that average 6-8 Kms / 2-3 mins, with the longest being about 13 Kms / 4 minutes long. Again, not very rally-like (hillclimbing would be a more appropriate description but I don't think the dev loses any sleep over such trivialities)- While on the subject of rally stages - the dev has a strange way of choosing new countries to be added to the game. Indonesia and Australia (outrageously priced for what it offers) are in, but no Monaco's Monte Carlo, France (Tour de Corse), Greece (Acropolis Rally) or Great Britain (RAC Rally) to name but a few

name: TUNIC
detailed_description: Full Controller Support TUNIC on PC is best experienced with a gamepad or controller. About the Game Explore a land filled with lost legends, ancient powers, and ferocious monsters in TUNIC, an isometric action game about a small fox on a big adventure. Stranded in a ruined land, and armed with only your own curiosity, you will confront colossal beasts, collect strange and powerful items, and unravel long-lost secrets. BECOME A LEGEND Stories say that a great treasure is hidden somewhere in this land. Perhaps it lies beyond the golden door? Or somewhere deep beneath the earth? Some tales tell of a palace high above the clouds, and of ancient beings with incredible power. What will you find? REBUILD A SACRED BOOK During your travels, you’ll reconstruct the game’s Instruction Manual. Page by page, you’ll reveal maps, tips, special techniques, and the deepest of secrets. If you find every last one, maybe something good will happen... BE COURAGEOUS, LITTLE ONE! Dive into varied, technical combat. Dodge, block, parry, and strike! Learn how to conquer a wide cast of monsters, big and small — and discover useful new items to help you on your way. Explore a hostile and intricately-connected world of shady forests, sprawling ruins, and labyrinthine catacombs Fight mighty bosses deep beneath the earth, high above the clouds, and in places stranger still Collect the missing manual pages, bursting with hints and original full-color illustrations Discover hidden treasures to help you on your way Unearth secret relics, secret techniques, secret puzzles, and… listen, there’s a lot of secrets! Featuring sound design by Power Up Audio And an original soundtrack by Lifeformed (Terence Lee and Janice Kwan) Keep your wits about you and be brave, little fox!

_childDocuments_.review: A nearly flawless adventure game that goes far deeper than you might expect. Tunic is a masterclass in air-tight game design, with a particularly keen sense for how and when to influence the player. It manages to nail down a particular kind of old-school childlike wonder that I didn't think a modern title could really faithfully emulate. If you're a fan of exploring and secret hunting, and you enjoy the look of the combat and aesthetic, I cannot recommend this game enough.I recommend playing Tunic completely blind, from start to finish, with no guides. It's tough, in a lot of ways, but it's extremely gratifying to unravel the game's web of secrets as the developers intended.If you're well and truly stuck on something to the point of giving up, the "Spoiler Safe Guide to Tunic" on the Steam guides page is a great way of giving yourself a nudge in the right direction. I needed this a couple times - though frankly, every time I looked at it, I felt pretty dumb afterwards.
_childDocuments_.name: TUNIC

_childDocuments_.review: Playing with a controller makes this game a whole different experience. I've finally given in and gotten a controller and I must say that this is one of few games that actually benefit from playing with a controller.So now that I've not been fighting the controls and have been actually playing the game, I must say that the game is very fun and the atmosphere is great the combat is fun and exploration is rewarded. The instructions are cute and I get what the developer was trying to do and for the most part it works very well, with some exceptions where it could have been more forthcoming with information. With a controller this game is an easy recommend. With a keyboard... no, just no.

_childDocuments_.review: It will be loved by all old school gamers, lots of secrets and nice fights with an up do date mechanic.Let me rephrase a bit:I really recommend this game for all those no longer young players, it is deeply enthralling for those who grew up with old nes/snes games like zelda, the exploration and secrets are amazing and always give the dopamine hit, maybe they are too obvious at times considering the sheer quantity of hidden items and secrets. the other hidden things / mechanics are so well hidden that I  was snitched were there.I have scantly looked at some guides just to understand a few things. I got to cathedral without help and its doable for everyone I think.Anyway, acquire this product if you fit in for the nostalgia demographics, if you are a zoomer you might try and enjoy something different.
