_childDocuments_.review: Tunic is SO GOOD.  I played Tunic in a frenzy.  During the few days it took me to finish the game, I played no other games, and booted up the game in every minute of my spare time.  This is not how I normally consume games, but there is something special about Tunic.  Tunic, on its face, is a three quarters view action adventure, with simple but beautiful and colorful graphics and a little fox hero.  The game wears its three biggest influences proudly on its sleeve.  Legend of Zelda: A Link to the Past, Dark Souls, and Fez.  Imagine A Link to the Past but with 20 years of quality of life improvements, and a number of Souls-like systems grafted on to make things a little more challenging and interesting.  There are hidden paths everywhere, many of them using the barely controllable camera as cover.  The combat is excellent, you have a strong dodge roll with invincibility frames, a sword, and a variety of special items that use magic.  The combat is not quite as challenging as something like Dark Souls, but it is certainly no walk in the park either, especially some of the bosses.  The engine is fantastic, everything is colorful and the artstyle is consistent and interesting, the animation and controls are smooth as butter.  If the game was just this, it would get a strong score from me, as it is so well done, and the moment to moment gameplay is very enjoyable.  But there is more to Tunic.  There is an alphabet/language that has been created for the game.  All of the dialog and signage in the game uses it.  As you progress, you find pages of Tunics instruction booklet.  These do everything from providing information on the basic controls of the game to showing you maps of various areas, and more.  Unfortunately, the book is in foriegn language as well.  Yet between pictures/screenshots, various random english words, and logic, you can piece together a bunch of information.  As you explore both the game and the booklet more, you begin to notice more and more secrets within both of them.  At one point you will discover a secret that will lead to a cascade of other secrets and information.  It astonished me because it had all been right in front of my face the entire time.  As you go deeper and deeper into the game, your focus pulls back in a way that every time you revisit a screen, you might as well be in an entirely new area.  I have never played a game that pulled this trick off so well.  Another thing that I found astonishing about Tunic is its “puzzle balance”.  Never have I played a game that contained so many absolutely devious puzzles, some of which I just had to sit and consider for a bit, or turn over and over in my mind while I was not playing, but that were absolutely solvable.  I completed the vast majority of the game, and there were four things I looked up.   A puzzle that I couldn’t get at all and I’m glad I did, I still don’t fully get it.  Bad puzzle, in my opinion. A puzzle that I solved in my mind, but didn’t think I was right and was too lazy to go back and try it.  I was annoyed at myself after, and it was a good puzzle.A puzzle that I missed because I played a lot of the game with the sound turned pretty low due to my personal life, it was a good puzzle too.A puzzle that I figured out, but was going to require so much time and effort I needed to make sure I was correct before I committed.  Thats it.  I only had to look up four things in a game brimming with secrets and puzzles.  Just amazing balance work by the developers.Tunic should not, and can not, be missed.  It is an extraordinary game that impressed me more and more as I got deeper and deeper into it.  It is the middle of April and I can say with confidence that Tunic is one of the best games that will be released this year, and will be remembered as an all time classic.10/10
_childDocuments_.name: TUNIC

_childDocuments_.review: I've been going back and forth on what I think of this game throughout my time with it and I think I've decided to go against recommending this.   On one hand the sound and visuals are immaculate.   I LOVE the way this game looks and sounds.   On the other hand I'm walking away from the game for a second time without finishing it due to the gameplay.   I've read some of the other reviews on here and they basically confirm how I feel.   On one hand you have a really difficult souls-like combat game- but then you also have a DEEPLY involved puzzle mystery.   It's not enjoyable for me, so I'm going to decline to recommend, but I can see that there are plenty of people out there that do recommend this game- so I'm glad they've found enjoyment in it.
_childDocuments_.name: TUNIC

_childDocuments_.review: The moment when you shut a game down realizing you just don't have fun and notice you're like 20 min past the refund window.I liked many aspects, problem for me was the main game loop. really did not enjoy the combat. slow attacks, some enemies that empty your health bar in one blow, a parry that sometimes works most often not and half the time he puts up his shield instead because you tapped the button for two milliseconds instead of the allowed one millisecond..Just feels clunky and I'm just not having fun.
_childDocuments_.name: TUNIC

_childDocuments_.review: tunic is a game all about the feeling of discovery. to me, playing this game feels like being a kid and not knowing how video games work. it's gorgeous, confounding. the riddles and puzzles never really stop, unraveling into each other right up until the very end. is it perfect? no; some fights are blisteringly frustrating, and the combat doesn't have a ton of depth to it. but what is here is simply indescribable. never before has a game made my jaw hit the floor so repeatedly.don't look anything up, don't spoil anything for yourself, just play this game through to the end. i'm near the end of the golden path and forsee myself traversing it again soon.
_childDocuments_.name: TUNIC

_childDocuments_.review: Alot can be expressed without words. Tunic is akin to older isometric adventure games like The Legend of Zelda. Its emphasis on the mystery of adventuring through unknown lands makes it unique. The soundtrack is my all-time favourite and always a treat. It instantly captivates you as you wake up on a forgotten shore and leads you to discover who you are meant to be. If you feel lost, afraid, and unsure of where to go, I encourage you to pick up Tunic. You'll continue to feel this way, but the atmosphere and puzzles make you enjoy the journey as with it did in my own life.
_childDocuments_.name: TUNIC

_childDocuments_.review: Abhorrent combat gameplay. I can't wrap my head around how terrible it feels to play tunic: roll, that Cutie Mc Fox starts with, sword that is shorter than gnome's ♥♥♥♥, paraplegic parry animations, MFing lock-on system in the isometric perspective and throwables that are affected by the physics engine - all feel like an absolute garbage to use. Music is bland. Visuals are simple, but unpleasant to look at, mostly because of the washed up color palette that clashes with eye-gouging visual effects and lighting. Manual, the main gimmick of tunic, is 50% window dressing for standard metroidvania power up progression, 50% FEZ puzzles.The only saving grace of the game is the competent level design. And, if you're into the stuff like that, maybe, the fictional language cypher(which is somewhat deeper than 1 fictional symbol == 1 English alphabet letter).If you want a competent 'what a twist!' game, where the twist actually affects gameplay, I wholeheartedly recommend The Messenger or Inscryption as much as I want to discourage you from playing Tunic. Hell, even the aforementioned FEZ I might consider to be a better game than this souls-like normiecore slop.Edit: Tunic is better than the Witness, though, don't you dare to play the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Witness!!!
_childDocuments_.name: TUNIC

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to love this game, and I loved the first half of it. But then it got so attrociously difficult that I couldn't fight any bosses without the no fail mode activated because the bosses were so out there. Then I stopped playing as the same difficulty suddenly appeared outside of boss battles.All of that really spoiled my experience of the game. Very sad.Edit: To be more precise, I believe the fighting system is not well suited for the combat itself it gets very frustrating when the little fox starts doing things that you did not want them to do, or attack into a direction that just came out of nowhere.
_childDocuments_.name: TUNIC

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game!I had a lot of fun exploring everything, the story is nice and the music is really good too!I can actually recommend it to everyone, play it and explore the beautiful world and story!I even bought the collector's edition because I really enjoyed the game... XDBig thanks to the developers for this game!I'm looking forward to more projects from you! <3
_childDocuments_.name: TUNIC

_childDocuments_.review: for all the metroidvania/soulslike games there are, this one doesnt do much to separate itself from the bunch. nothing special about it and the difficulty leans more towards unfair than fun and challenging. the combat is good and the items are cool but i dont really want to play this game ever again after the time i've put into it. there is no direction and you need to find your way on your own a lot which is fine in most games, but this one i had to look up a lot and it was frustrating. given the vagueness of the story i wish i'd given up sooner because there was nothing really rewarding about the experience at all. i love metroidvanias and soulslikes in this genre, isometric especially, but the most creative aspect of this game is the art style, it doesn't do anything innovative and the gameplay becomes far too tedious.
_childDocuments_.name: TUNIC

_childDocuments_.review: Tunic is a challenging but ultimately delightful game. Much like Hollow Knight, it's a labor of love from a small dev team. And much like Hollow Knight combined classic Metroidvania gameplay with charming graphics and Soulslike elements to create a work of art, Tunic does the same with a Zelda-like format. But make no mistake, this is no mere Zelda clone. Gameplay is tight, bosses are tough but not impossible, and most of the puzzles and secrets are fair. Like most Soulslike games, one has to figure out the story and what happened to the world, and boy are there moments where your mouth will drop open. I enjoyed Tunic immensely and cannot recommend it highly enough.
_childDocuments_.name: TUNIC

_childDocuments_.review: Tunic is an isometric action adventure about a tiny fox in a big world. Embark on an adventuresome questabout set in that place just beyond the farthest you’ve ever been. Explore ancient ruins, fight monsters and uncover mysterious secrets. The world is big and scary — so be brave, little one.
_childDocuments_.name: TUNIC

name: Phantom Brigade
detailed_description: PRESS QUOTES 'Phantom Brigade is a tremendous f***ing video game' - Waypoint 'Wonderfully clever' - Rock Paper Shotgun 'I cannot overstate how cool this is' - Kotaku 'A triple-A experience ... made by an indie game studio' - VentureBeat About the Game Phantom Brigade is a hybrid real-time and turn-based tactical RPG, focusing on in-depth customization and player-driven stories. As the last surviving squad of mech pilots, you must capture enemy equipment and facilities to level the playing field. Outnumbered and out-gunned, lead the Phantom Brigade through a desperate campaign to retake their war-torn homeland. KEY FEATURES: Cinematic spin on the turn-based genre – Predict enemy movements, orchestrate precisely timed countermeasures, and hit “execute” to watch the physics-based action unfold in real time. An exquisite arsenal – Railguns, beam weapons, missiles, energy swords, and more! Rain destruction down upon your homeland’s invaders with weaponry salvaged from each enemy mech you defeat. Strategy – Make high-level tactical decisions on the world map, manage your mobile base, and decide how to apply your limited resources. Tactical combat – Take command of your squad in varied missions ranging from sabotage of enemy equipment and convoy ambushes to liberation battles and challenging outpost onslaughts. Customization – Featuring a rich customization system, Phantom Brigade enables you to fine-tune the performance of your mechs, install a wide selection of equipment, and access a wealth of cosmetic options. Prepare your squad for any challenge - in style. Highly moddable – Phantom Brigade has been designed from the ground up to be highly player moddable. Mix things up by playing the game with a community mod enabled, or try your hand at creating your own modded masterpiece! Destructible environments – It's not a proper game about giant mechs without destructible buildings! Phantom Brigade allows every square meter of each battle map to be destroyed. Shatter your enemy’s cover and collapse buildings on top of them!

_childDocuments_.review: Lightweight hybrid of XCOM and BattleTech, with a new turn-based style of "paused real time".Looks nice, it doesnt take forever to load like parents, and its simple.The best selling point, from my perspective:MECH can actually run full speed ahead in other things !!! No melee, just plain ol' SHIELD UP and run into tanks, giant robots (or even buildings?)It's a steal for 20e, and we should support developers like these
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: This is a pretty tepid 'thumbs up'; the game's core time manipulation mechanic is such a great idea and so well executed that it carries the game through it's less glamorous downsides... namely the lack of mission variety and story.It's a better system than it is a game, but that system is so excellent that I think it's worth a try regardless if you have any interest in turn based strategy.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: I couldn't understand the tutorial at all - which is saying something, considering the only other game I've ever had difficulty figuring out was EVE Online.Also, I heard that things were cut: pilots leveling up and a nemesis system. Both seem important in a game like this.Maybe it'll improve in time. For now, I've refunded.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: Amazingly good game.  Simultaneous turns with prediction of enemy actions is incredibly fun to work with.  Varied weapons and gear make for lots of different strategies.  A surprisingly well designed game.  My only complaint is that it runs hot.  The computer is working harder than maybe is necessary for the graphics level, but that is a minor issue.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: This game has rne stupidest dialog and story. The invading army is evil for the sake being evil, the devs don't understand anything about proper military jargon, rank and dialog(why is a Cadet on a COMBAT mission in the tutorial? Why is a Cadet telling a Lieutenant what to do? Why were they packing live ammo on what started as an investigation on the local radio tower with ZERO signs of an imminent invasion, why is their a military mecha hanger smack in the middle of a cute village?)But ignore all that. The games very cool. If you missed the customization and tactics of front mission this game is for you. It's not turn based, buts not real time. Rather each turn is 5 seconds of battle, with time pausing at the 5 second and you adjusting from there.This gives more immersion and believability than everyone taking chess like turns and standing there and requires more tactical knowledge than a turn based game which is purely number and stat based instead of skill and tactics based. 8/10. Kickass gameplay. Love the style of the game(it has a civilian look for a military game. Kinda cementing the fact the war is on your homeland) but cringe dialog and lack of basic understanding of military concepts(like even arcade COD does better and non military focused games like CIV do better)But if thats doesn't bother you(it really shouldn't) its a genuinely good experience. That's a small downside for everything else being an upside.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: Not sure if i would recommend this game. Pros:Satisfying gameplay. The prediction mechanic is cool and the mechs and weapons are fun. Plenty of things to upgrade on the base. Not a bad looking game.Cons:The art generic. There is no storyline in the game. While it starts with some cutscenes with voice acting and some story it then stops having any whatoever apart from random text events. The mechanics aren't explained well at all. It presumes you have some knowledge to start with with this kind of game (If i did not play battletech alot beforhand i would be lost with a lot of the systems). All in all depends on what kind of game you are looking for. If you are looking for pure gameplay you will like this game since the gameplay loop is fun. If you are looking for story look elsewere. Maybe get it on sale to try it out.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: Phantom Brigade: A great titel for people who enjoy tactical turn-based battle games.Phantom Brigade is a fun, but long, tactical combat game. You fight to gather resources to upgrade your mobile base, mechs and of course to liberate provinces. The game feels decently polished, runs well and offers decent graphics.The game is not short. There are a lot of provinces to liberate. You might not have to liberate them all. I don't know since I haven't found an end objective yet. I'll try liberating the capital in a few days but who knows. At 60 hours of solid playing the game certainly qualifies as a long game. Because it's long battles can start to feel repetitive.The battlefields are  all kind of similar but of a decent range of tactical options. The unique system allows you to play around with accepting damage, taking cover or just avoiding contact in certain areas. The UI works well, the system is reasonably intuitive and combat feels rewarding. As said, the game can start to feel repetitive. It's also hard to estimate incoming damage so it's hard to guess when you can absorb damage or when your mech is screwed without diving for cover.All in all it's a great titel for people who enjoy tactical turn-based battle games.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: Quite good! Everyone else who has made a mech game in the last ten year should be learning from this one. It has an well done X-Com meets Mechwarrior vibe with a few others mashed in a well done, coherent package. The developer deserves credit for a well executed genre mashup.Combat has a nice feel with weapons, effects, map design, and atmosphere being quite solid. The mech combat and RNG loot creation is totally spot on. I suspect replayability should be high given the variety of gear available. As a suggestion to the developer, adding elite gear with "set bonuses" and/or epic "named" gear would be a really nice addition and add to the replayability.The tech tree for the base could really use filled out. I think there is a real missed opportunity to unlock more weapons and powers for both mechs and the mobile base over the course of the game sort of XCom alien autopsy style. A few examples - base unlocks such as air strikes, off map artillery, some type of sensor sweeps, pilots could use stats and special abilities to really give more variety and replayability.The mission planning UI could use tweaked a bit to be more intuitive and easier to use but its okay once you figure it out. A very solid mech title. Could become a real classic in the genre if the developer sticks with it and really expands the game over time. 7/10 currently with the potential to be a classic with a little support from the developers.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

I thought was absolutely terrible and stupid and every other synonym in the book is adding a "PRONOUNS SETTING" for set pilots. I hate it. So illogical and politically motivated. Keep that garbage out of this game or any game. I can't believe this... then again knowing how stupid some of this world is I shouldn't be surprised.

_childDocuments_.review: As most are saying, to be able to review the whole battle at the end would be amazing. I love the timeline aspect and being able to predict everything. Having an aresonal of weapons at your disposal and having the creative freedom to create a chonky mech that wields a heavy gun or a beam rifle or a light mech with huge movement range and a dash to complement is amazing. The UI can be a bit much at times but if you move past that you can dump hours into this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Gave it a good try, my initial impression is that it was very similar to x-com but it was just missing that critical piece for me that made that game great, just ultimately felt very repetitive to me.  I found the stats to be very obtuse and yes while I could have googled it or looked it up the game does not do very well to make the information available to you.  ultimately 6/10 for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: This is a well made; almost entirely bug free game with cool time prediction turn based combat. The mech customization is pretty cool and your mobile base can get some nice upgrades.So why don't I recommend it? It's misleading. -The story is misleading: The opening 20 minutes or so have:  dialog, cut scenes, tutorial; and characters with names and some personality that really hooks you in. Then it's all gone. There's a time skip; you start the game in earnest. None of the characters remain; there's no banter or story at all beyond an occasional text box with minor events. The characters are so bland they may as well actually be faceless.-The upgrades are misleading too. You start with 4 mechs deploy-able and have several tiers of upgrades increasing your mech bays and load-outs and pilot barracks: but you can never deploy more than 4 mechs. They all end up just being backup mechs in case you totally screw up (because every component lost is permanent). You can't see the battlefield till squads already chosen; so multiple load outs of equipment options are a random guess.In summary: It's very well made, boring, with no attachment to your squad or people at all. Things that could help IMO: -Streamline the controls: If there was a common accept or cancel button that oculd help speed things up tremendously. Like space accept / continue and esc cancel / go back for commands and menus. -Add personality: Combat voice lines, Banter, or at least some distinct appearances. The paper pilot options are surprisingly vast; but the profile customization is so blender bland that it ends up being "Helmet, Baldy; or Pilot with a visor"; with virtually none of the personality background stuff coming out. -Add Story: it's currently 20 mins of awesome, but generic, opening; then 20 hours (sofar) of playing risk. Add a big story event when you conquer a zone. Or some distinct dialog with the home guard forces. Add a Persistent named character with some presense.  With how many zones there are; I can easily see this game lasting 100+ hours or more; but nothing feels like it matters so it's hard to keep coming back to it.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know how I slept on this one. The art style of the UI and the game itself, the customization of the mechs, and the intense blend of strategy and tactics make this an all-time great game. I could easily see myself dumping 100 hours into this game's campaign.If you're unsure, here's the selling point: This game gives you the full satisfaction of perfectly managing an RTS game without the sweaty APM requirements, all while presenting a tactical territory control meta-game to keep you on your toes. Seriously, check this one out!
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: Fresh take on the turn based tactics genre of games that doesn't boil down to some surface level gimmick. Has some hard to learn mechanics (Melee most notably), and some missing ones (missiles should have a trajectory indicator like almost everything else) but is over all a polished game and worth getting if you are a fan of the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: It's hard not to like big stompy robots blowing the hell out of eachother. Mechs have a large amount of cutomization options, each weapon class has a good niche, and battles feel tactically sensible. Aside from some small hang ups I'm quite impressed by this game. As for those hang ups: Melee feels not quite worth the risk of using it because mechs sometimes crash immediately after using it rendering them helpless. Urban environments sometimes shear an arm off your mech and I don't think concrete and glass should do that on contact.Overall I'm liking it and after some further patching it should be even better. Props to the developers for the semi-realtime planning mechanic. Firaxis should be taking notes from this title for their next XCOM game.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay of this is based around a timeline mechanic that has you committing to actions before they play out.  It involves a lot of guessing that doesn't feel fun.  The UI is clunky and the time management is not something intuitive.  The voice acting and story are weak and play out as excuses to use the boring core mechanic.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay loop and idea is really fun, but the way missiles work became unfun to the point I stopped playing.They have great range, are guided, have no minimum range, and aren't tracked by the timeline, so you can't see which missiles are targeting who and when they are estimated to hit.This makes them really strong to use, but extremely tedious to fight against. Especially when the game decides to throw 3+ missile using enemies at you.So until they are reworked I have to give the game a no.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't played far into this game yet, but already I am in love with this game.While the story is so far, admittedly weak and far from a highlight of the game, the combat is quick to understand and the main mechanic this game advertises is refreshing and unique! In a way, its also functions as a friendly way to introduce new players to turn based concept.The main features aside, I must also PRAISE the customization and salvage mechanics! Both possess easy to understand UI and the 'mech customizer is WONDERFULLY simple while absolutely diverse. Giving you preset camo colours, while letting you apply them to individual segments of the 'mech and its armaments. Allowing for a diverse, unique stompy robit for you to pilot!Highly recommend this game, even if I haven't put many hours into it yet, its already hooked me.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: It's cool and all but early game you just have to equip all your mecs with missile launchers.The homefont allies are expendable so make em shoot like there is no heat.And get ready to battle on the same map 5 encounters in a row. They are not even changing the starting positions !The melee is wonky at best. And during my last battle the sound just stopped working mid fight.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. It has quite an innovative turn-based system. At first, it felt like too much fussing with the timeline, but I quickly got sucked into the combat. Each turn is broken into 5 seconds in which you can see the enemies' movement and actions. You can scrub, back and forth, testing out your movement and attacks. However, since projectiles have travel time, attack timing varies and requires interpretation. So far, the most tricky timing is catching a moving enemy with melee. I've seen comments on the UI not showing enough information, but part of the fun to this game is learning the timing. After your turn, you can replay the past 5 seconds and catch any details you may have missed. The combat maps have interesting topology that, when paired with different spawn locations, lead to interesting and different tactics. Mech customization is varied, with quite a few weapons and parts -- each with a number of trade offs, such as weight, speed, heating, hit points, etc. After combat, you collect a rationed amount of gear from enemy mechs. When building my early mechs, I really enjoyed this, as you need to decide on which pieces to take and which pieces to leave behind. Once you have crafting going, the rationing of post-combat loot is not as significant. With a fair number of preset palettes for each section, colors customization is decent, but I would like to be able to make custom palettes.There are features to this game that do feel minimally developed, such as the pilots, world map, and base tech tree. The combat and mech customization work so well that I don't find these other points hinder the experience with the game. The base game is great, as I'm still playing it, but I do look forward to any future development/additions to this.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game. I thought that customization was very nice and I'm always a sucker for inventory and long free-form overworld campaigns like XCOM and Mechwarrior 5. If you're a fan of turn based tactic games and like mechs you'll probably vibe with this game.The only thing I'd knock this game for is the user interface and navigating it, as well as becoming somewhat repetative at times.Other than that the gameplay is pretty fun, the campaign is pretty fun, and it has amazing music/soundtrack.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: This game is actually sick but it definitely needs more content. I've played for 26 hours and have liberated 4/5 zones out of like.... i think more than 20... and I already feel like I've seen everything the game has to offer me.Edit: To clarify a bit, for a tactics game, there's not a whole lot going on under the hood. Pilots have no progression. The only stats effecting mechs are based on your parts. There are no abilities or anything like that.You have Don't Move, Move, Move Fast, Shoot, Other Shoot, Block, Eject, Leave. That's pretty much it. Weapon variety on its own is good enough but I feel like there's a level of impersonality in the game. I don't care about my pilots because there's no progression or voice lines in like 90% of the game. I don't care about my mechs particularly beyond the amount of work I have to do to rebuild one if it is lost. The most mechanically interesting thing I found I could do is some Iron Man/Captain America ♥♥♥♥ where I can bounce my own laser off a shield for a cool angle attack, but the sheer damage that does to the shield makes this tactic pretty useless for any fight, and the damage the heavy laser does doesn't justify the damage my unit takes in doing it.Music can do with a lot of improvement. It's not BAD but it's not really exciting. I've just been listening to like... retrowave and mechwarrior music instead. Home base progression is kind of uninspired. Research is non-existent, you just get Workshop charges for weapons and armor, etc. Which is fine but I feel like that system could be fleshed out a bit more.Big things I would like to see more of:More customization options that I DON'T have to mod inAbilities/More in depth progressionMore opportunities for skill expressionMore exciting music More map varietyMore mission varietyUnguided missiles that are actually unguided (Seriously, why are they guided when they're clearly called out as unguided?)Different tiers of like... generators and thrusters please....
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: It is a fun game, but once you get certain gear the game is too easy. I don't want to give any spoilers but I just have no desire to finish the game at this point. There is no challenge except if you are too aggressive you will lose pilots and mechs. That's literally the only losing strategy is blatant aggression.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: Mechanically pretty good, it is rather padded though. It's in an awkward place.There is an overworld you move around on like in Mount and Blade. There are occasional missions. Most missions take the form of parking somewhere for a little while or having a fight. Which is where the problem comes in. There is a big country to conquer and not too much variety in missions. It's gonna take me like 40-60 hours to complete a campaign. I'm like 4-5 territories in and every one works the same way.The equipment system is complex and interesting, but lacking anything too spicy. No crazy weapon variants, just incremental changes in various statistics. There is a profound lack of personality. It needs more voice acting, especially for the pilots. As it stands all they are is a portrait, they don't even seem to have specific stats. Just a kill count. With a campaign so long it really needs more short term goals and surprises. Hopefully patches will add things like pilot weapon specializations, maybe personalities and quest interactions. I want more worldbuilding, more detail, more personality/creativity. This game is fun for the gameplay, but there is nothing that sparks the 'one more turn/one more fight' feeling that X-com and Civ provide.  It's very close to being great, but somehow doesn't spark much emotion.I should note that their recent patch made numerous positive changes to the gameplay, hopefully they're still working on it :)
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: I have enjoyed the game for about 10 hours, got to learn and master the combat mechanics, got to try new weapons, tried diffferent builds on my mechs, but in the end, the game is too shallow.There is simply no challenge once you understand the timeline and get to effective builds. The AI simply cannot deal with the player ability to predict its move.I also feel absolutely no attachment to the rest of the game. I don't care about my pilots, they are just hitpoints bags. I don't care about this country I'm supposed to liberate. "Town", "Base", everything is bland and generic. Enter a region, call on the guard (how do they get the mechs and tanks btw?), easily defeat the ennemies in 3-4 battles, liberate the region, resupply, rince and repeat.There is no "doom clock" to push you and get you out of your comfort zone, the ennemy doesnt recapture the liberated regions, and the escalation effects are not even felt.It feels like more like a demo than a fully fledged game. It's not that expensive so I don't feel bad for playing it, but it will be   a forgettable experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Incredebly fun expirience! The only negative side - not really much of interesting encounters. Almost all encounters goes by the same scenario (except the final battle). _childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: It's a relatively early review for me, but I'm having a blast with it so far. The hybrid of realtime and turn-based is amazing, and it's got all the crunchy mech stuff that I would hope for. In many ways it feels like an evolution of Slay the Spire's "intent" system, just applied to an RTS.On the downside, the story seems to be just kind of ... there. There's a war, you're fighting with mechs, and that's about all you have to sink your teeth into. I would say that it couldn't be more bland if it tried, but it seems to be trying to be bland, and has nothing to say about war, fighting for your homeland, fascism, occupation, or anything else, which seems like a bit of a missed opportunity to me. Thankfully the game doesn't dwell on any of that stuff, and doesn't expect you to either, just be warned that it's a bit of a hole where I'd expect there to be something.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: Great addition to the turnbased genre, very well thought out and solid core gameplay. Just for that, it's definitely worth a play. However, there's not much more than that - in terms of long-term motivation this feels almost like early access, apart from the inital setup there's no story or campaign to speak of, basically you sandbox your way through a VERY large number of random encounters.Can someone please create a campaign for this? Would love to return at some point.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: Prays for something new have been heard!Beside the rather innovative turn-base prediction planning mechanics the game includes:+ Mechs ^_^ The variety is not as rich as in Mech Warrior or Armored Core, but you'll have what to choose from. Models, animations - good level. And I want to that the studio for that they don't have a market for bying tons of stupid cosmetics.+ Weapons. Many types, different mechanics, customization. Heating management.+ Locations provides variety, destructible buildings, weather that matters.+ Global map management. Including events. Strategic tweaks help when tactics is not enough.+ Nice user interface. I'd say that it is not trivial to create an interface for such a game mechanics but they did and it is rather easy to use, including hotkeys.+ Graphics is nice. I have a half-wooden PC but anyway it looks good.+- There is a rather juicy melee, but for me it works weird, hope it will be more transparent in the future.I strongly suggest bying this game. There are some things to improve but I'd really consider them minor. We should support studios that have enough courage to introduce something less reflex-based but more for thinking. Waiting for the next products.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: Played since beginning of Early Access on Epic for maybe 50 hours more before I bought it again on steam. The turn based strategy mixed with the mech theme and the limited precognition is something you wont really find anywhere else. You can minmax to your hearts content with a dozen stats to your hearts content with a whole slew of equipment types, slots on each of those equipments with even more subcomponents, but you dont have to. You can combo your actions to amazing mecha anime moments or you can efficiently execute your enemies without much fuss. This is very much a "you make your own fun" game. It is not a story heavy expierience but you get very attached to your mechs and getting them injured or killed in battle is sometimes even more heartwrenching than losing your favorite character in XCOM.The game is still being updated with more and more content like items, whole systems and some storylines and still keeps suprising me when I start to get comfortable with my strategy and keeps mixing it up.You currently cannot save during a mission which means you will need  ~45 mins of free time to get somewhere in your session. I believe save during missions is still somewhere on the roadmap.Very much recommend this game. Do check out the other games they made and published.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: It's such a cool game, but that is all it is. As it currently is the game simply doesn't feel like a 1.0 finished product. It feels like half a game and you won't notice until you've played it for about 1/2 your campaign. You'll slowly start noticing how everything in the game feels incomplete in some way. The loot just isn't exciting at the mid/end game, the story is non existent, and you'll notice a distinct lack of polish in most of the games systems. I just found myself wondering why I would fight the next fight because I knew how it would play out with my squad and there was no story to seek out. I'm just a little sad that I don't even want to finish the game. It starts out strong, but it's a short burn.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a fascinating concept with control over time to build your strategy. It makes you believe it should surely be easy to beat an opponent when you see their next move coming, but by having you be on the backfoot as a resistance with overwhelming odds against you, you find yourself constantly backed into a corner having to make calculated sacrifices for victory.The concept is interesting and well executed. I recommend this to any strategy enthusiast if they want something fresh.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: I've played near 60 hours so far, and I've definitely had a good time. It's a game that I recommend, with a few qualifiers on that statement.The game still feels like it's in early access. There's a number of things that are unexplained (eg crafting), broken (eg missiles entirely despawning before reaching their displayed range or duration), or incredibly imbalanced. Things that feel like they should be a part of the game - like a full mission replay system for the "cinematic" combat, a story, or a progression system for pilots - are missing. The game's difficulty is a downhill slide, with the hardest fights being in the first few hours, and the end of the game being so easy that I spent multiple turns on the last map just waiting, because enemies die so fast by that point.If you can get past things like that, the central concept of the game is fantastic, and the fights it creates definitely live up to the cinematic combat it is described as. It wasn't uncommon for me to replay the end of a turn to show my wife, because the game is designed to create fantastic looking (and feeling) combat, with the collision system being a particular standout in my opinion. The feeling of shield-bashing an oncoming mech so hard that it cripples the mech and kills the enemy pilot on impact is a wonderful mix of satisfying and hilarious, to name one example of the quality situations the collision system creates.The devs also seem to be hard at work addressing player issues, with a number of patches in the last week to fix balance problems, so hopefully this review is eventually incorrect. I look forward to the potential day where I can remove the asterisk on the recommendation here, because the core of this game is so fantastic.

But once you have cleared one or two areas, and youve learnt all the basic mechanics, all that is left in game is to clear more areas.  With the same mechanics. _childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: This is an absolutely fantastic little tech demo / toy.The fundamental combat is astonishingly gratifying. Every turn is a little puzzle where you put together the perfect 5 second automated combat ballet for your mechs... weaving behind cover, squeezing out a quick shot in between enemy bullets, dancing through a line of fire to set up the perfect kill. (Oops, looks like you planned it out wrong, you collided with an enemy and now your mech is crashed completely in the open getting focused down - your own damn fault!)And it looks and feels great. Sure, it's indie and the graphics can't be compared to Cyberpunk 2077, but it looks like a really attractive mid-2000s big budget game. Explosions, bullet impacts, building collapses, are all super crunchy.Unfortunately there's not good-feeling progression or balance. Once you're into the meat of the game with a few basic upgrades each individual combat is enthralling. But progression through the campaign feels floaty and empty, and certain builds seem to be completely overpowered. I can imagine a lot of people will be left feeling unsatisfied by this, especially considering how gratifying and complete the fundamentals of this game are.I still strongly recommend this game. It has fantastic, original ideas excellently executed in its base combat.  I got it full price and consider it totally worthwhile - if you like the look of the trailer, and you can get it on sale, you'll definitely get your money's worth. Unfortunately the campaign and progression system isn't there yet to make this into a real classic. It feels like more of a sandbox toy than a full game. But, for sure, I'm super excited to see what this team will do next - and what other developers will do with the concepts showcased here.

_childDocuments_.review: It was truly an amazing experience during the first 5 hour. It felt so fresh and so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ fun when you outmaneuvered an overwhelming odds. But then it turned into a tedious mindless grind.When you get the hold of it, you will soon realize:+ The AI of the enemies are as dumb as potatoes. They will NOT adapt to your decisions, instead will blindly follow their original plan. So if they targeted one of your mech, you can let said mech jump all the way to the back, and the enemies will keep firing at it, wasting all their shots.+ Itemization in this game has the same issue with Diablo 4, gears do not have a fixed level, instead the enemies still slowly scale up, making your gears slowly losing effectiveness. It forces you to, find the same type of gear, same name, same appearance, with slightly higher stat. There is no end to it.+ The mech and their pilot has no character, nor personal skills and traist. If i lose any of them i can just savage the parts, put it on a new mech frame, grab a random pilot. Boom, you're back to 100%. I don't feel bad losing one of them, only the annoyance that i have got to replace them.Even after 2 years of selling their soul to Epic, the game still feel like an unfinished product. Truly a phantom of what could have been perfect.

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay is very fun and satisfying, I wouldnt say that for the most part it was too difficult the appeal is mainly the spectacle of it all along with setting up a build you like by cutomising mechs in your teams.But even with a very basic team you effectivly have by design a massive advantage being able to see the future, so losing fights will really only happen if you do something really reckless in my experience.The main problem with the game is the massive lack of content outside of fights, they make up 90% of the game and after doing like 5 regions/10-15 fights you will have pretty much experienced everything the game has to offer.There is really no story at all outside of onetime events and the tutorial, take regions is pretty much the same everytime, the base upgrade thing is very basic and the upgrades themselves are pretty minor for the most part. When your not in a fight you'll just be tinkering with mech parts really, there isnt really anything else to the game going on.One good thing I find is that since the fights are pretty smooth it makes the transition between them and the overworld not as jarring as I personally find most other games with this sort of format. For example in Xcom I tend to 2-3 fights feel burnt out or annoyed when another one comes up, but I think this more due to the fact that this game is pretty easy by comparision and there just isnt anything going on in the world mode.I will admit I havent finished the game, aka take the capital, as I just lost interest as it seems like really there isnt much point doing anything other than just rushing to the capital and ending the game right away.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: I highly recommend it if you like XCOM, Battletech and Front Mission.It's a bit disappointing that the enemy AI seems a bit mindless, they just kinda randomly move around and randomly target friendlies. They seem incapable of prioritising targets as I've had mooks with shotguns persistently try to attack my sniper mech from half a map away, ignoring a friendly literally on the other side of a wall.There is also no story at all despite the fact that the game tries to make you care about what's going on. Hard to care when you don't even know the name of your nation or who the enemy is!Despite those shortcomings, if you enjoy intense micro, planning your squad loadout for an hour or agonising over the orders of your units for the next turn like I do (and most importantly: mechs), I am certain you will enjoy this game. It's a bit odd that some other people are complaining about this aspect as its this game's biggest strength. They seem to be expecting the wrong kind of game.I just wish we could see a replay of an entire battle! Devs, get on it!

_childDocuments_.review: I hope this game makes it big. It's just excellent. It is such an incredible fusion of mech games like armored core and battletech, turn based strategy games like x-com, and an incredible re-imagining of "time-line turn based tactics." What bugged me about games like frozen synapse and breach & clear was the fact that you basically had to prepare for every single surprise that could possibly happen. This ended up making the games very slow and tedious. Not necessarily bad, but it just wasn't for me. The prediction system here is spectacular, basically you can see 5 seconds into the future (even what the enemy is doing) and plan accordingly. I understand that some people might feel like that's cheating somehow, but this being a singleplayer only game, it makes it much more fun. It allows you to literally choreograph a beautiful dance of mech destruction. It's splendid. I love it. I wanna coin the genre of "cinematic turn based tactics." Because every 5 seconds in this game feels like a movie. Hell, even the in-game timeline makes it feel like I'm messing around with adobe premiere lol.I have literally ONE gripe. JUST ONE. So much can happen in those 5 seconds, that I spend a ton of time in replay mode watching everything that has happened. And it's awesome. What I would LOVE to see is a type of cinematic camera that would focus on big events like crits or a kill during a replay. As well as an ability to watch the entire fight after the game ends. I mean, I haven't played all that long, but if you stitch all the 5 second events together, I can't imagine a fight lasting more than a few minutes, which I would love to watch in real-time.

_childDocuments_.review: Every once in a while a game comes along and gives you a new, unique experience. Phantom Brigade is one of those games. It is well-executed -- especially for a small indie team -- and has wonderful graphics, animation, industrial design, music, and effects. As an old-school BattleTech fan I was impressed with the meaningful variety on offer in the mech building and customization system, as well as how it integrated with the salvage and strategic upgrade system - very impressed! It reminded me of the old Mech Commander games, but with a new angle, polish, and style.I highly recommend the game, but have the following suggestions for the team, should they happen to read this review. This game desperately needs the following: - AN END BATTLE FULL REPLAY (and save/export video option) - PILOT PROGRESSION - STEAM WORKSHOP SUPPORT - DEEPER MISSIONS    - A deployment zone mechanic    - Slightly larger maps    - More varied missions like raid (destroy target), retrieval (get target), etc.    - Weather effects (reduced vision from fog, rain increases heat dissipation, etc)    - Map generatorI'd like to see multiple factions, mercenaries, and extra arms manufacturers in expansions and sequels.

A good start to a game, but with much more work needed, I plan on returning to the gam elater, unless the keep mechs locked at 4 units,  I want the more grand battles

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR I loved mecha games in the past. This one is a mostly polished gem I happily spent years keeping on my wishlist and bought for myself one launch.I've been missing games like Front Mission, where I got mecha on mecha tactics, and I can safely say Phantom Brigade has been scratching an itch that has been neglected since the PS2. While Phantom Brigade lacks a lot of things I really feel it should have the game is pretty amazing.Pros.1. Giant Robots.2. A cool 5 second turn all at once tactics.3. Multiple play styles in variant of your mechs loadouts.4. A decent but very lacking Pilot and Mech customization.Cons.1. 4 units. You will only ever get 4 units on the battle field at once. What idiots decided to make all games only 4 units where the enemy always is x2-x4 stronger then you and get reinforcements as well as always constantly more units then you but you only get 4. Even if you upgrade to have more mech and pilots. You can only sortie 4 units at one time. 2. A bad tutorial that doesn't fully explain some things. I understood it just fine from so many games like this but I see streamers and friends always sucking at this. It agitates me how bad some peopleare playing cause they don't get explained properly enough how to play so it isn't exactly their fault. It's the game design.3. Not enough things to create and no control over if the axe/sword/saber you create will be for the main hand or off hand. Or if it'll be a normal axe or a Plasma Axe as you can only just create Axe.4. A WAY too small cap on your resources so you always hit too much for uncommon parts but normal and rare you don't ever seem to have enough of.5. Lack of customization in many ways. I personally hate the three fixed color selection as I wish to mix and match colors.Pilots all look like garbage I barely tell the difference between them, their hair, and beards all suck. Worse hair color sucks.6. Power Creep to the extreme. I wasn't even grinding and the enemy and I were basically max/all equipment unlocked by the second provinces. So I found myself feeling little reward afterwards just higher level of the stuff I already had unlocked. But never the parts I actually used in my playstyle.7. STORY IS WHERE?! Big of a game becoming boring because no story in a story game.No really I've played it quite a lot and find myself constantly asking "Who are we?" games answer "Our Countries, Home Guards, Phantom Brigade." but who is our country? The game says The Enemy came and took our country... WHO... Who is the enemy. Where are they from? Where is their country? What is their name. I hate the game keeps just referring to them JUST as "The Enemy" it does pull me out of the game. How the hell did we suddenly turn the tide so quickly and fast we're nothing special aside from prediction system which feels like the enemy has as well in later levels.---------In my personal final notes. Awesome game and idea. Hopefully the Devs don't just drop it and abandon it but improve on it better. A lot of the changes I'd love are simple fixes in truth. But I'm just that weird guy who always loved giant robot games, tactics, and customization so I can make my characters correctly.I feel this game is at the current form only worth $15.99 in all honesty. So if you're gonna buy it get it on any discount you could. With all my praise it's current form I don't feel it was worth the price.

_childDocuments_.review: While game concept and mechanics are not bad, there are soooooo many minor things that add up to ruin all the fun you can have in the game. For example:1) A grand total of 5-6 maps rotating over and over again, with only difference being spawn locations and camera angle. You can even get same map twice in a row...2) Action bar is very fiddly, especially if you want to insert a "Move" command in the middle of turn (You need to manually place "Wait" first). Why can't you just drag "Move" command and game would automatically pad it out with "Wait"...3) In some places (up against structures or cliffs) it is hard to tell whether or not enemy attack will hit you, because dashed line indication that enemy will miss is obstructed by obstacles. (And even then, it sometimes lies and enemy will hit you)4) While mech customization is cool, the only difference between these mech parts are purely in stat numbers. And pilots are just there... staring at you with there soulless eyes, being nothing more than exact copies of each other...5) No official modding in a Unity engine game in 2023, bruh...There are a lot more to say, but even these 5 points i made would've been enough for past me to skip this game.So in the end i'd say wait for patches\updates, maybe it will become better, until then, stay clear.

_childDocuments_.review: game is oozing with cool. surprisingly cool cinematics for a game like this. excellent writing, which is a nice bonus considering how unnecessary it really is. high level of polish in general. this ability to manipulate the battlefield via time prediction makes for some exciting spectacle. The replay features are so fun. if you come in mainly hoping for that, you will have a great time setting up some epic firefights in destructible suburban environments. If you're the kind of person that enjoys just gazing at miniatures, you'll enjoy this spectator aspect quite a bit I think. Negatives: I've only played for a few hours, so it's tough to say for sure, but the AI seems way to easy to manipulate and exploit, which is encumbering the strategic fun. I'm starting to feel like I might end up bored because of this. In the end I definitely feel I got my money's worth. I'm optimistic about everything I pick up, but I feel like this once could turn out quite good with some balance patches and additional content.

_childDocuments_.review: Joined in Early Access in early 2021, contributed to modding system and also saw this game growing like a plant.Since its release in EA, the game did lots of progress with new contents, mechanics and parts/weapon. Basically everything. At version 1.2, the game is shining on my opinion, except for some things:- Story: linear, the classic "they invaded us, we will take it back" thing makes the game a bit linear so, the endgame is nothing new as well. I am sure it will be improved at some point after QoL fixes;- New game+: the biggest con of this game. No NG+ forces the player to do everything until the end, and after that nothing will change as you can further do unfinished things or restart the game since the beginning.Other than that, mechanically and gameplay wise is a good game, in a certain way similarities are encountered with X-Com for instance (ambience or elements/mecha design), and it helped me spark the interest into RTS games.A good game that has potential for sure, but still has lots of things to be improved.

_childDocuments_.review: I love the battles!The graphics and sound effects.The map game play is charming, seasoned with little text-story incidents.However the salvaging, crafting, and refitting after every battle when the enemy will instantly adjust its difficulty based on your spec improvements renders the entire affair null. If the player works so hard to intercept convoys meant to make  strategic points more powerful, why should the player be robbed of the ability to hit those hard points OP?In this design there is no sense of reward, just the risk and struggle against the odds. The map is very large, but really once you take the first tile the player has experienced most of what the game has to offer except for a few weapon types.You will not know what gear the enemy will be using, all you know is that the enemy will ALWAYS have something better (to salvage) and we can only GUESS we've fitted our mechs right for the next fight or we'll have to trade our hard won supplies for more pilots to build up. Which is tragic because there are upgrades for radio and recon drones - such a missed opportunity to give the player more detailed information about the enemy to assist with how to gear before a fight.There was a sufficient quantity of items that can be customized that would already provide a fulfilling experience, but having included "LEVEL" to equipment only ever reminded me that the enemy has better stuff no matter how many of their convoys I intercept.I loved the battles easily enough to play this game 5x longer but also had enough of the headache that the refits gave me between every battle when the spec-depth is as bloated as it is making the between-battle-process feel like grind.However since the Devs recent update to include modding Support I've updated the review and have a reason to pick this up again and hopefully be able to tailor the experience more to my tastes.

_childDocuments_.review: A (simultaneous) turn-based tactical game. With mechs.  The game looks and sounds great. The graphics is stylized. The mechs look great and can be customized with different parts and color schemes. Even with this diversity the mechs are not as diverse as in Battletech. The maps look great and are partially destructible, but their pool is limited and they repeat often. There are cutscenes of a good quality, but only at the beginning and the end of the campaign. There is only minimal voice acting (2 cutscenes + some unit callouts). The music is excellent and it shifts dynamically depending on environment or game mode.  The core game mechanic - simultaneous turn-based tactics with planning phase that shows all future actions, even for the enemies, is very fun. It allows the player to use cover effectively, force enemy to suffer friendly fire and so on. Some mechanics do not mesh all that well, like slow projectiles, but this may be on purpose. Melee weapons are potentially strong, but hard to reliably use (this may be patched). There is a varied selection of mech components, subsystems and most importantly weapons, both ranged and melee, from mundane like machine guns to exotic like rail guns (with penetration of terrain and other objects!), plasma guns and beams (can be reflected around). Components can be salvaged after battle or manufactured in the mobile base. The base is the core of the strategic layer of the game, where it moves over the country, evading patrols, attacking outposts or ambushing convoys. There are several types of tactical missions, but they mostly fall into extermination or capture (which can be solved by extermination). There are possibilites to improve the odds before mission, like disrupting calls for reinforcements or calling your own. There is also a researchable tech tree, which improves the abilites of the base.  Unfortunately, the storytelling is very minimal. Besides generic story of the campaign (liberate unnamed homeland from unnamed invader), there are some random side quests and events. Some of them were nice and once it even tied to a pilot and his personality. They are however purely random from a limited pool, so they may not happen for a long time, suddenly happen quickly and they repeat a lot. There is no progression of pilot skills and though they have an assigned personality, it does not seem to have any effect. Once you acquire all weapons the game begins to feel repetetive, with only motivation being increasing the level of components and capturing provinces.  A great and fun tactical game, unfortunately missing almost all story and with a limited content (maps, events).

_childDocuments_.review: Phantom Brigade has enough goods in store to hold for 10-20h of gameplay, afterwards various issues just glare at the player so much that its not worth continuing. Lack of QoL, repetitiveness, pointless objectives, shallow overmap gameplay; the list is long.Phantom Brigade is a very enjoyable game. Cinematic fights, enjoyable combat system, simple progression with enough depth to allow for distinct roles for each mech.And yet, for every good thing in this game, there are 3 frustrations of various levels just bringing the whole experience down. Its not even bugs; the game is relatively bug-free, but it has serious lack-of-features problem.In no particular order:-  despite there being one for last turn. This game has plenty of wonderful animation work and is a joy to watch, so this is probably the biggest turn down.-  other than being a stats recorder and concussion gauge. Customisation options are also really lacking, with few preset faces and very low amount of hairstyles. At least helmets look good and hide all of those issues?- , which happens often and is especially frustrating with reactor cores that can change 4-6 different things. You get a stat preview for entire parts, so I'm not sure why this is not in the game.-  Its far easier (and more lucrative) to knock every enemy on the map out than to spend 2 turns next to a supply crate to claim it. Enemy reinforcements often take 8-9 turns to arrive, whereas the combat often ends after 5-6. Tutorial mentions alarm bells for reinforcements and power generators for turrets that seemingly have no mechanics tied to them out of said tutorial.- . Getting better equipment boils down to getting rare parts with higher numbers so you can customise them better (Or at all, in case of weapons). There are upgrades for main base, but outside of unlocking more mobility options they all seem like busywork at best - with drawbacks, too.- . One of your pilots says its their birthday, so you can either spend 15 hours in middle of enemy territory doing celebrations for 40 points boost to all pilots stamina, wish her happy birthday for 10 points, or say that there is no time for birthdays during war for -40 points. It might be good for roleplaying, but this game has so little story that its hard to justify.There are more, smaller things, but the list is already long enough. The point being: The game is good for first 10h, then the realisation sets in that it could be . It feels like the team got a time cut on their project and had to wrap everything up to ship a title that is playable, if very unpolished.I really want to like this title. Perhaps it will receive updates down the line to address those issues; until then, however, it will be a disappointment for me.

_childDocuments_.review: If there was a neutral option for reviews I would definitely pick that. I will give it a yes because the game has a good foundation, it just needs content. It really feels like another one of those "early access" games that gets sold as a full release. Other than that I will go over the pros and cons of the game.Pros-The core gameplay loop is great.-Build variety is amazing.Cons-Foresight is a bit OP. Makes combat too easy.-Mission, map and enemy variety. Once you liberate the first 4 or so provinces, you have pretty much experienced the extent of the combat variety.-Some weapons just straight up don't work.-UI could use some major improvements. Especially when modifying mechs. The symbol the give for weapon heat generation does not take into account how long the weapon fires for. So a weapon with, lets say 1/6 of the circle full for heat generation could generate more heat during combat than a weapon with 3/4 of the circle full because the one with 3/4 generates that heat over 3 seconds while the one with 1/6 does it in 0.7 seconds. (Also please show us the value or add a value that changes the damage type taken depending on the armor class used. IE: Heavy armor decreases concussion damage by x% and so on)While there are more cons than pros. Like I stated before, the game has a good foundation. Now it just needs the content.Would I recommend the game? Yes, but on a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: Innovative Combat system. Battletech meets BSG:Deadlock. Combat plays out in 5 sec chunks. Where you can plot your next "turn" and then watch it in real time. Lots of fun mech customization. Again reminiscent of Battletech. Good soundtrack.Cons: The story has no depth. Unlike Battletech, which had fantastic lore and used it to great advantage. This story is generic as discount meds. You're not even told the name of the country you're defending or who invaded you in the opening. It's literally "Us" vs "Them." You see province names on the map. But that's it. There's nothing grounding you in the story. In no small part because:Pilots: Nothing but generic stat-blocks with claymation faces. Customization on par with FM23, which is not a compliment. There are personalities mentioned. Do they influence anything? Don't know. They don't change the dialogue. And since the mechs fight precisely as you direct them, there's no evidence of a pilot being more or less brace. More or less clever. Add to that there is no pilot progression. And they're literally interchangeable. I have no reason to care if one survives or not, other than I may not find another stat block anytime soon. Bugs: UI imposing on top of one another. Save/loads are terribly optimized. Combat balance: All over the place. Missiles are absurdly overpowered. To the extent that one would have to ask why you'd use any other weapon, given a choice. Combat is fun. But this needs a pass. All in all, this is a game that I might change my stance on in a couple months. But I can't recommend it right now.

_childDocuments_.review: Blatant Battletech rip off, content is shallow as a puddle and the game just isn't finished.Yes I understand the studio was a small team. Yes I can tell they have put a lot of effort into the game, making a genuine effort.I would compare this to HBSBT (Harebrained schemes' Battletech) in that they both take the Battletech formula, tweak it a little to make it more accessible to a wider audience while drastically simplifying it. Overall making a shallow copy of the TT  but for a dumber experience. What they added with the "Hybrid" turn system isn't a bad idea, but isn't an original one either. It also makes fair and balanced multiplayer basically unachievable.Oh and the writing is pretty lame too, but at least they have pronouns! How inclusive! If they developed this with another year and more staff available, this could have been an interesting spin on the formula that inspired it. However it is a shallow copy that just doesn't offer anything worth your time. If you want the Battletech experience without being a sweaty TT mech dad, pick up HBSBT, which while a diluted BT experience, gives you more for your money and has excellent mods available for those who want the full merc experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Solid and enjoyable although there are some noticeable issues that hold the game back.The good: Extremely satisfying gameplay with a lot of tactical depth. You have enough flexibility to play a fairly simple game, with a strategy involving 'have mechs with guns walk up and shoot the enemy' being completely viable but still requiring some thought in target selection. The graphics and presentation are excellent and enough to make blowing up mechs over and over again using the same strategy not get repetitive. On the other hand, there is also a lot of room to experiment with unusual builds - the difficulty is in a good spot where you can try sub-optimal strategies for fun, but not easy enough that it gets dull.The bad: Lack of any pilot progression or skills is a glaring omission. This was planned pre-release so hopefully it will be added later, but at the moment the mechs and pilots are all interchangeable. If you want to build, say, a sniper mech, you just have to find a sniper rifle and bolt it onto one of your mechs. There's no need to have a pilot who is a good sniper, or any investment required in building up a mech that can use it. Similarly, if your sniper mech gets blown up, you can just take the sniper rifle and give it to another pilot and mech who can use it instantly. This contributes to feeling less attached to your units than you should in this kind of game and sucks a lot of personality out. Other issues which are less problematic but will frustrate some players are the barebones story (boiling down to 'we are good, red mechs are bad') and the challenging UI, which I got used to after a few missions but may put off some people.Overall, if you are a fan of the genre I would have no hesitation in recommending this, and I'm not regretting my purchase at all, but it is unfortunate to see a game this good being held back from being truly excellent.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fine, but there's almost no part of it that couldn't be designed better in my opinion.The UI is functional, but cumbersome and unwieldy. With unnecessarily difficult to understand icons and design. Performance is atrocious and GPU heavy for no apparent reason as the graphics are mediocre at best. Animations are good, but I personally do not like the art style. Tactics so far been superficial and arcadey, you often feel like there's nothing to do besides positioning and shooting. There's no sense of tactical depth besides you just get your mechs out of harms way by the time the enemy fires back.I believe the expected target audience for releases like these heavily favors older gamers, but almost everything about the design, story, and style of the game caters to the youngest of the Fortniters. There's nothing inherently wrong about the game(except the lackluster performance/optimization at launch), but it fails to spark my belief in any longevity. It's so arcadey at times you almost do not understand why it's not an action release instead. If you are a fan of all things mech, sure, grap this title, but I'd at best only recommend this at a discount, and preferrably not until its feature locked, optimized, bug-sprayed and golden.

_childDocuments_.review: The system is novel and the underlying mechanics are present for a stellar tactical mech game. The content and customization is entertaining, hence the hours of gameplay I've on record. That said, a number of things stand out that keep me from playing more, beyond the usual "there's no storyline" kind of deal.Idgaf about the storyline. I care about this:1. My pilots are meatbags I don't have a reason to care about. No skills, no real expertise.2. The game keeps throwing enemies with increasingly powerful mechs, which is not very interesting in the long run. This arrangement boils down to a series of scenarios in which the numbers are different, but everything else is effectively the same. The enemies' and my own mechs might as well all be rocking the same Lv01 loadouts. Given that most looted parts are just upgrades rather than sidegrades, the looting doesn't actually do much.[Put effort into making sidegrades. The upgrades are effectively a waste of time.]3. There is no counter to missiles. Ducking behind cover is unreliable, putting a shield up is unreliable, and with no concern for pausing the aim, missile users can simple keep running around at full speed with no need for line-of-sight. Talk about an immersion breaker.Until these three points are addressed, as much as I enjoy Phantom Brigade, I can't recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Has an exceptionally unique and fun core gameplay loop and an outstanding visual style, but is held down by just about everything else. The campaign is sub-par, the story lacking, and the soundtrack forgettable. It's like someone came up with a really cool idea for a mech combat system, and just put the game around it in order to sell it as a game.The base is amazing, but it gets quite repetitive after some time. This isn't a huge problem due to the fact that the base  so amazing, but it makes it feel like something's missing. I'd say that something is primarily new methods of interacting with the game. As the game progresses, you don't get stronger by gaining completely new abilities or weapons, but rather by just doing more damage, getting more health, and maybe getting a little faster. The game gets more refined, but it doesn't . Rather than the core gameplay enabling the development of a good game, the game seems to exist solely as a vessel for the gameplay. I'm still recommending it because the gameplay inside of it is so good, but it's important to note that the gameplay is really all that's there.

The combat is pure strategy in which you can decide how much you want to risk to get the job done at the cost of your resources. But developers, add icons on the buildings so I can identify what is what, (not that it matters too much because I just nuke the turrets or draw the enemies out, but it'd be nice).
