_childDocuments_.review: I'm really not sure which way to go on this one. Lots to recommend the game, but there are some distinct problems that detract from the experience, from the game's primary conceit, and from the fun in general.I'm going to go with "Thumb's up but complains about the game all review."So the idea is probably pretty clear to you if you're considering buying the game. It's big stompy mechs, chock full of customization options, and asymmetric warfare. You get fewer dudes than there are enemy dudes, but you, and this is very important, can *see the future.*Except for missiles. Missiles are outside the timestream, nobody knows how they work, and that's why they're an invaluable part of the armaments of both sides.Missiles sometimes take a while to reach their target. They also sometimes just miss their targets because of oblique angles. Different launchers have different speeds and accuracy, different firing arcs which determine what cover they can get around (yours and your enemy's), a wide variety of ranges.But you can't see what they'll do. Can't see the progression of the missile into next turn. Can't even see if you've already targeted one of the largely fungible little red targeting markers last turn, which is important for salvaging purposes. Your missiles will miss constantly, while attempts to slip enemy missile fire with anime-style rapid dashes through city streets and multiple 90 degree angle turns will shake approximately zero to one missiles out of twenty.You can easily see if an enemy firing at you will be able to hit you with your future sight. If the line they draw to you is dotted, some or all of their shots will be intercepted by your cover. Sometimes you will forget than an enemy shot an especially high arc of missiles at you one or two turns ago, and your guy behind cover will be very upset at their timely delivery onto his or her noggin.Fascinatingly (to me, anyway) I discovered that the max range of my missile launchers... wasn't. It's not the max range. The actual max range was about 15% less than it said on the tin. I replayed the same turn over and over with the replay button, watching a vast host of missile shaped death approach my enemy sniper, and they all exploded midair at the same time. It was in range according to the range finder, but not according to the missile fuel budget. This, too, would have been a nice inclusion in my future sight.Also, as a small aside, never trust the dotted line when the enemy firing at you is a sniper. If the shot can possibly get over the lip of that ridge and hit your dome, it will.So the future sight is wonky, a category of weapons that is wildly useful to everyone seems to be made out of Time Free materials, and this is, frequently, more frustrating than fun.But I really, really like customizing robots, so here we are.

_childDocuments_.review: X-COM + Front Mission + Battletech = This game. I have been looking for a game like this for a long time, this is an awesome mix of Turn-based/ Real time strategy. Great customization, sending out orders with a timeline system is the most ingenious way of doing a game like this, Being able to send out an order to not only attack an enemy, but to defend from fire, move closer, use my shotgun and keep moving so you collide with a different enemy target all because I custom built my turn, and that is just for one mech. If you have any interest in mech TBS gameplay with a twist, I implore you to get this game. For $30 it is well worth the asking price, a way better game than most. if not all AAA games coming out today that are asking more than double what this is asking for.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't want to call this a bad game because all elements that need to function do in fact function very well. Combat system is fun and innovative, mech building is interesting, mobile base expanding does function and has meaning, item construction gives items which have oompf and there are so many parts, weapons etc. that I'm absolutely positive I haven't tested even half of all weapons and items available in game when i'm all done with it. In all these regards Phantom Brigade isn't a bad game, its quite excellent in fact.. but.Game is built with so vague way words cant ironically even described it. Its like majority of the material which would make the core of the story is just shining with its absence. Story begins with you, assumed soldier or officer, testing a new system given to your, assumed special, unit for testing. A force of generic evil army attacks, you protect civilians while enemy facerolls over, assumedly your, countrys army. Someone called Cadet does a heroic schpiel about protecting civilians and paying back or returning.. aaaand game skips to a point where your now guerilla unit returns with remnants of the homelands army and starts reclaiming areas with your help.The vagueness of everything is just highlighted by everything that follows. There are several counties with their own filler information, plenty of small events in habitation hubs you can fight in and reclaim.. It feels like there is a lot of content but what would glue all of that together, the core of the story.. backstory... what is your country and who is the enemy.. "the WHO ARE YOU?" is missing. That all doesn't mean the say the game isn't fun to play.. it just comes in a form which doesn't make you feel invested or interested for a long period of time. I'm gonna finish this game some day.. but its gonna be a long long process of barely bite sized chunks of me just enjoying gameplay rather than diving in and being invested into the story which stretches playing sessions to unhealthy lengths.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: It's not Battletech. What do I mean by that? In BT there is a dichotomy between the metal, ie the big stompy robot and the meat, the fragile monkey who pilots it. That's what makes the mecha genre interesting, from Voltron to well, Battletech. It shouldbe a tragedy when either your mech gets shot up or you need to hose out the cockpit and now install someone with flippers for hands instead of the skillgodwho unfortuneatly now is being sent home in a matchbox.In Phantom Brigade all pilots are the same. Losing one isn't a blow because theres a new pilot who is, just the same. stepping up. The Mecha are also generic and felt like they were from IKEA. A mecha should have it's own personality and not feel like it has been assembled from legos.The strategy phase was interesting, even if it was designed by an autistic nutcase for whom intuitive is an alien concept.But even if, and it's a big if you work that out you still quickly realise your driving IKEA mechas who are piloted by interchangeable nobodies.Which is why I reloaded Battletech and installed some mods.

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished the game. It is a huge disappointment. I suffered through it - save yourself and do not play it. Certainly don't buy it.First gameplay, then aesthetics.Gameplay:You "win" by taking the Capital Province. That took me about 35 hours. There are a ton more provinces to capture, but I'm not playing past this point. If the game has anything more to offer, then developers are foolish to gate it behind 30+ hours of gametime.This game was in development for Lord knows how long, but the developers failed to include basic quality of life features that you encounter within an hour of playing. You have to fight with menus to see what equipment modules do. Most of the items' descriptions don't say what they even do. This is a big problem in the crafting menu, where you can craft items... but aren't allowed to see what their stats are! You have to go back to your inventory and hope you have one in stock to look at.There's more. Your attack information sometimes doesn't show up when you mouse over your icons. You have to constantly place & remove & replace your orders to get something that works right.There are major problems that directly affect gameplay. Weapon balance is all over the place. Plasma Launchers are ridiculously overpowered. Cannons are worthless. Some subsets of weapons are worthless too. If you play this you'll find some weapons are good and others are not worth even considering. That said, despite the bad options, there is enough variety that it feels interesting.Some people complain about missiles being too good. The major problems are:- Dash lies to you. It says Dashing breaks missile lock, but this is not true.- You can't track projectiles after they've launched. You're telling me our time travel device can tell what enemies' exact actions will be in the next 5 seconds, but it can't track projectiles?You don't get to choose where your mechs deploy. Every battle starts you off in close range to the enemies, often from terrible tactical positions. Like, ambushing a convoy by running straight down a wide open road with no cover. Why would we do that? It looks as if they had a deployment mechanic and then scrapped it for some reason.The Concussion damage type is overpowered as well. It is both the best tactical way to destroy enemies, and the best strategic damage type to use, because you get more rewards for enemies killed via Concussion. The general rule for design is that something good tactically is bad strategically. Think of the explosives from modern XCOM 1. It helps you win the battle, but in exchange you lose out on strategic resources. That's the correct way to implement this sort of mechanic. The numbers involved with Concussion damage vs regular damage needs to be seriously modified to make it worthwhile to not focus on Concussion.Barrier is a bad mechanic, yet it takes up half of the game design space on armor. It's supposed to let you regenerate HP mid-battle. But there's a major flaw in this design: Time-to-kill on mechs is 1-2 turns. Neither you nor enemies have meaningful time to regenerate HP.Speaking of damage, every time you land a hit, damage numbers fly up all over the damn place. There are so many numbers flying around you can barely tell who's doing what. After a while I just gave up trying to figure it out.There are rumors on the discussion forum that there are hidden mechanics that further obscure numbers from you. If true, any developer involved in that ought to be fired. Hidden mechanics affecting your stats in a game that's entirely about making decisions based on those stats is directly counter to the core gameplay. But, I don't know if that's true, so I won't go off too much about it.Aesthetically, the game is soulless. Utterly soulless. There's no love put into it. There is no story - everything is written so generically that you don't care about your guys or the enemy in the least. This game does nothing to advance mecha games. It's a worse game than mecha tactics games from literally 20 years ago.Here's another aesthetic failure of the game: Every turn you can replay the last 5 seconds. But:- You can't see the last 5 seconds of the fight, since you go straight to a victory screen after winning or losing- You cannot save the entire battle and play it back!- You can't see damage numbers in the replays. Remember how there are numbers flying all over the place? Maybe you thought "it's okay, I'll watch the replay to sift through that noise and make sense of it." Well, too bad. The devs didn't deign to let you see the damage results from thatWhat's the point of a replay mechanic if you can't understand what happened to improve yourself, or watch the entire battle for fun? Toribash got this right 15+ years ago. Why can't you?Don't play this game. Do not give them money for this. Do not reward releasing unfinished games.

_childDocuments_.review: The unique cinematic combat is pretty great. I was a big fan of the Battletech game and this one is a more Japanese-style take on giant robots blowing the hell out of each other. There are a ton of weapons to choose from, and a bunch of mech styles to select, but you won't see them all right out of the gate and you'll need to raid supply transports to unlock crafting most items.The biggest downsides to the game are just about zero plot to speak of, and the UI leaves much to be desired. The in-combat parts are pretty straight forward, but everything in the 'overworld' including building and outfitting your giant death machines is relatively unexplained and you'll have to figure it out mostly by trial and error. There also isn't as much map variation as I would have liked.It also bears mentioning that the 'loot' drops from each map are pretty RNG. You might find the part or weapon you're looking for, but there is no real guarantee it will have bonuses you care about. Fortunately, there is a lot of loot so you get a lot of chances to find what you're after.For the price, it's a pretty good deal. The studio could have spent more time adding on more like additional maps or a bare minimum of plot, but even as-is I've bought worse mech games for more money.

_childDocuments_.review: A simultaneous turn based mech game.  Has part salvaging/customization, collision/physical cover system, and mod support (Check NexusMods).  Good controls, with every useful button on the screen being bound to a hotkey. Just a solid game on launch; no early access.  That said, it does have a severe lack of story content.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty dope.Im just past the tutorial set of missions and im impressed with what ive experienced thus far.The game offers turn based combat, with some real time aspects as well as a 5 second rewind-time-to-fix-a-mistake feature and a "timeline" action sequence where you plot out your moves and attacks for your squad, in sequential order as you watch the enemy's moves that happen as yours do. So far, Ive seen loads of different types of robots, which you can scavenge parts from after battles and equip onto current bots or put together and entire mech from the scraps. There is crafting, though i have barely scratched the surface of the game so i dont know enough about deep that rabbit hole goes. Tons of customization for each of your robots.Good graphics, good audio quality. Voice acting doesnt seem too terrible so far. This game was a sleeper that i had forgotten on my wishlist, then i saw an article about it on Kotaku, saying it hit full release on March 1. Decided to pick it up, then realized i had been wanting it, so i didnt get the typical buyers remorse of adding yet another game to my ever expanding games list.TL;DR Buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: Combat is good. Well, more like 'ok'.You can paint your mechs, but no real camo is available. Same thing goes for OPFOR. Seriously, who is going to field a _white_ tank?Story is crap, can't get any immersion from that. Alien invaders would be better, but what do I know.Engine is not optimized enough. Trying to render a forest pumps up GPU usage by 30% or so, I dunno why trees need to be so detailed in such a game.Strategic view is garbage-tier. You will grind supplies as if it is a f2p mobile project.Enemy bases just respawn after some time out of thin air.Tactical view offers no choice of unit deployment, your units just spawn on the map and that's it.Ai is dumb and will try to shoot your through LOS blocks on its own volition.If you are going to play this - set your expectations a bit lower than you wanted initially.

_childDocuments_.review: Its a good base for a mech game, you can get a few hours of it before it gets repetitive but its little more than a tech demo. The focus was the visual presentation of the battles and it exceeds expectations at that, but not much else.This is not a complete game. Most elements in the game are half baked, unbalanced, poorly thought out or just missing. I am only giving it a thumbs up because i think the price is right for what they are offering but i would really like for an actual, proper game to be made out of this.This is THE MOST BASIC mech builder i have ever played and depends way too much on RNG, crafting new parts is a pain because the attachments are random (yeah, in this game universe, when you ask for a sandwitch you roll a dice to see what its made of, only using the space & time defying power of save scumming you can choose what you want)Just to mention some other things that annoyed me: there are weapons that never hit target, heat damage does nothing on enemies, melee weapons are impossible to aim correctly, you are forced to wait real world time to craft items but there is no time pressure ingame so the game is WASTING YOUR TIME, pilots are a pointless mechanic (plus i dont know why they changed the handrawn heads they had in earlier versions, they looked a lot better), your biggest threat is concussion damage because you cannot defend, block, regenerate or increase it in anyway (your 5000 hp mech can be downed by a single missile that hit you from behind doing 20-30 concussion dmg), heavy mechs are useless because you have to give up pretty much everything for a more hp that does not protect the pilot, missiles are not tracked by the prediction system, are extremely good at tracking moving targets and can be very hard to avoid, tend to hit you in the back, oh and they do concussion damage so they will down your guys in one or two hits

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good game. Biggest issue is the maps/battlefields are incredibly small. Your shooting on turn 1 before you even move. Out of any xcom style game this one has the smallest maps. everything feels like a rush. you can win alot battles but just shooting and not even moving lol. no counter to missiles. aslo the AI never change targets it seems. so if you kill whatever units are targeting your fast flanking mech he has free reign to run around with no one shooting it. can literally just walk up to behind other mechs and knock them out.alot of bugs are present like stat bonus not applying the correct bonus, starting armor you unlock is pretty much the best. has more subsystem spots then any others in the game. some odd design choices when it comes to heavy mechs. there formula here is there so heavy you have to use thrusters to jump/move them around. i personally don't like it  and there is a reason you dont see this in any other mech genre games/anime because its not logical. they should be a slow walker and powerfull. feels like a win lose on the upgrades for the base, the whole crafting gear really makes picking up gear from battles pointless there never gonna be better then what you craft. You also really need a color wheel instead of the premade patterns. Another suggestion is why are there no shoulder equip spots. why cant you install a secondary rocket pod on your shoulder like every other mech genre does. Alot of the tooltips need to give you more information as most of the stats display incorrect info or leaves out things. And it really really needs a stat overview to see a breakdown of all stats on your mech like the base does. Game needs alot of work. Edit: and another thing the whole game is you being reactive to your enemy, they have a predetermined behavior that does not change. so they will not really react to what you do. they do there path and shoot there guns even if they have no line of sight or cant hit. its weird. the only reason the game even works at all is because you have less people. this is why every battle has reinforcements and the ones that dont have more then 4 mechs. Needs a whole ai rework. The more I play the more it feels like its flawed at its roots.

_childDocuments_.review: At the time of writing I've only played the Steam version of Phantom Brigade for about 2 hours, but I've played it in early access on The Other Store for over 120 and watched it get better and better with every update. (Well, mostly: I maintain that it was more fun when you could more easily knock enemy mechs over, but that did tend to make things a *tad* easy.)It's always tempting to say "if you liked X then you'll love this" but truth be told, Phantom Brigade is pretty unique. Another reviewer describes it as "Front Mission meets Adobe Premiere" and honestly? Probably the best, most succinct description possible! The hybrid turn based / real time combat is extremely satisfying and also great to look at: replaying your turns and slowing down the action to see that moment where your melee unit blasted into action, or when your sniper's bullet hit home, never gets old.A couple of other reviewers have complained about a lack of tactical depth, and I can only assume they've basing this purely on the opening hour or so because once you get further in, get more weapon options, start building your mechs into more distinct archetypes rather than general damage dealers, and - most importantly - once the enemies start getting tougher, there's definitely a good amount of tactical depth to be found. Overall I can't recommend this game enough. It's been a long road to release and I hope this sees the success it deserves.

_childDocuments_.review: 1 hour in and this game is blowing my freaking mind at every turn. I am loving how this game plays. I am a huge Armored Core fan so this game really does something for me. Incredible value of a game.Highly recommend to anyone who likes strategy and mechs.6 hours in. I get the feeling that I've barely scratched the surface of what this game has to offer. Down the rabbit hole I go, for this game.... oh baby, this game is something else.-I find the story to be captivating. -The game mechanics themselves are amazing. -The overall aesthetic looks bright and vibrant. Shadows and lighting look realistic.-The animations are surprisingly good. The one that caught my eye the most was the sword animation. It's fast and fluid. There is nothing like melee dashing through an enemy, while performing a horizontal slash motion, and as a result see behind you the legs of your enemies buckle. All of the weapon special effects and project animations are beautiful. That's all I have for now. I am not one to review video games often by any means, so the fact I am even here typing this right now means this game has got it goin' on!

_childDocuments_.review: I played the demo and loved it and the main game is just more of the same. I very rarely feel so passionate about a strategy game but this one gave me moments that would compare to Total War or XCOM. I'm my opinion it's in the top league of strategy games. The mix of turn based combat and real time is just brilliant. With turn based strategy you lack that epic action and with real time strategy you often can't look at the action because you're too busy micro-managing everything. This game takes the best of both worlds and combines it with awesome mechs, destruction, beautiful art direction, AAA level of quality animations, amazing sound design. I really hope the devs will keep fleshing out the game and releasing content, paid or free I'll be there to play it. This game could turn into a strategy classic.

_childDocuments_.review: What do you get when you combine the best bits of Battletech, Invisible Inc., and Flamberge? Hypothetically, a fun, engaging, and original take on tactical strategy. But in practice, all of that is washed away under a tsunami of Diablo-style loot management and level grinding that makes progression feel like a meaningless treadmill.I really want to like this game, but each update makes it less of a puzzle game about mechs and more of a gear grind, and for me, that means it keeps getting worse.

_childDocuments_.review: As of the 1.10 update i can't wholeheartedly recommend this game. But you can see it, you can see how awesome this game could become.Pro'sClean and concise Art direction.Combat and the timeline function is smooth and easy to operate.Con'sSimple enemy A.I. It will always attempt to attack any unit in their optimal attack range.A somewhat hollow objective: you are meant to go to the capital and liberate it, you can B line for it and ignore all other provinces, the fastest i was able to do this was clear six provinces (first play through) and then just do the end mission. I reckon you can smoothly do this on two or three provinces. If you get some god tier luck on gear,supplies, and energy you could potentially do it on zero provinces.Pilots:The mechs have pilots but they don't provide much of anything. The most you will get are little events that say oh your pilot is doing this or that but nothing of substance. just a pretty picture No voice lines, no boons, banes anything. I am not saying they need to be super detailed like "you pilot sneezed and are now off course". just start with simple things like pilot does more damage with certain weapons, Pilot is experienced with certain mech parts and can move further.Weapons: Some weapons are just objectively better than others. Snipers, Rifles and missiles are all you will need. this could be fixed by adding weapon abilities or passives to make other weapons an option. Take the Typhoon machine gun. it looks Awesome with its hail of bullets  but you will be spraying bullets at the same enemy for the whole turn (yes even if they are dead) leaving the unit occupied for the time being. the Machine gun could have an ability to sweep the area, shoot any enemy in a cone, or a simple damage reduction when firing.Pet peeveWhen customizing the Mechs they do not keep their color when you switch out parts.

_childDocuments_.review: Ever had toy robots and played with your neighbor but then fights broke out because he keeps coming up with stuff to avoid your attacks like teleportation and invisibility? Ever played tabletop battletech but then fights broke out because someone forgot to bring the maps or broke the miniatures? Well, have I got the game for you. Phantom Brigade is the most advanced tabletop mech combat simulator. Being able to adjust replay speed while moving the camera around is such a cool feature I find myself using regularly whenever particularly incredible plays need to be seen again up close and in slow motion. The night fights are a joy to watch with beam weapons, explosions, thrusters and muzzle flashes lighting up the battlefield. There is a campaign mode to get you started with a premise and goal but the game is kinda open world and unscripted for the most part. Essentially, you ride around in your mech mobile base liberating provinces from the enemy by sabotaging power plants, raiding equipment convoys, protecting historical buildings, destroying patrols and outposts, etc. Don't be fooled however, they are basically scenarios in which you are tasked to defeat enemy mechs so you can get their goodies in the form of parts which can be dismantled for supplies to build everything from mechs to base upgrades. Playing under the default settings will be a lot of fun for most players. You will get to stomp on the enemies with an abundance of offensive and defensive options for your highly customizable mechs. Not only are they superbly animated, they look really good from the beginning and get better looking as you progress. With the right paint job, they even look like expensive real world die cast figures.  Turn based tactical strategy connoisseurs will appreciate playing the game under the hardest difficulty settings using only 3 mechs and not the 4 maximum allowed. Not being able to loot a rare part after winning a battle due to severely reduced salvage points earned will make you sad. Not as sad as finally having enough salvage points but unable to loot anything because there are no intact parts. The struggle continues so you must try to make it back to base for a resupply while being chased by patrols because all your mechs have missing limbs and you are out of materials due to increased repair costs. If that wasn't enough, you can try doing a speedrun because time is tracked in game hours. Nothing bad happens if you take forever to finish the game so I suspect there may have been a leaderboard function with scoring planned but not implemented.   Phantom Brigade has so much potential. So much to like about it from music and sound effects to the sleek, snappy, slick UI. Many aspects of the game are very forward thinking in terms of design. The base game and its core mechanics are immensely fun and we could be witnessing the birth of a new franchise if the title is deemed successful and worth further development by the studio. For all its imperfections, if the studio was a restaurant, it would surely have received a Michelin star for this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, was really fun the first 5-7 hours but then got stale pretty quick. The fighting system is unique and innovative and (for the most part) implemented thoughtfully. Of course there's a lot of stuff you could still improve on, but as it is right now, it functionality is pretty good. But, in my opinion, it shouldn't be ALL there is to combat. There are times where it doesn't seem necessary to use your 5 seconds fight editor, when all you need is basic movement or waiting orders. Mecha-customization feels like a lighter version of Mechwarrior. Instead of individual frames for mechs with different stats, you get a barebone mecha skeleton on which you can install different torsos, arms and legs. The mixing and matching of different parts is fun at first, but lacks depth as you progress. There's a ton of stuff the game can and, well, needs to improve on, but as it is it's well worth the money. Just don't expect something to dig your teeth into and binge it - just take bites and enjoy it for a few hours every now and then.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is really fun and I love the designs. Some of the movement animations could have been better. And gosh, I hope that whoever wrote this game wasn't getting paid for it and was like a game designer or something. Cause its not like the game really needs the story that much, but whoo boy are the parts we get awful. I don't know if I've ever had my brain get so mind numbingly bored with a cutscene that lasted under 30 seconds. Actually kind of impressive if you think about it. I'm not expecting a masterpiece, but even a game with almost no story at all "into the breach" executed that far more functionally than this game.Great games like this take a long time and a lot of investment to make. So its a bummer that the story was written by a child with short term memory loss. Because a game like this deserves something more interesting.Game would honestly probably be better without the intro cutscene and stuff.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a "great" game. Why great in quotations? Because it could be MUCH better. So much potential and at best this should of been an Early Access game and in it's current state I'd say its a version 0.5b. I don't mean it's buggy I just feel like it's a preview of a game without much else. The game is a box with packing peanuts from wish and the innovative gameplay is the packing peanuts. The innovative gameplay is just an over glorified auto pause button  every 5 secs with pathing enabled on enemies to see their movement.The story is bland, not much to the story, nothing much to inspire you to keep going to finish. It's basically a sandbox game with very little customization to the mechs. There isn't even anything to customize the pilots stat wise just a hand of visual customization. meh. The ground work is there to be a great game, but I think a lot content missing to be a polished game to want to make you keep coming back. I just want to finish the game just to finish.

_childDocuments_.review: Big fan since early access. You get to be clever in setting up your turn, then get a reward of a slick looking mech battle (or are shamed by your inadequacy in the replay). Add to that a ton of customization and an extraordinary soundtrack, and you have a game that punches many tons above its already considerable weight.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: Please note that this is only a Positive review because "Mixed/Maybe" isn't an option.The combat is phenomenal, and made me feel extra big-brain whenever a plan came together, or when managing to turn a mistake into a massive advantage. It's a very Battletech-y affair; destroy enemy mechs, pick em clean for goodies, upgrade your mechs, rinse repeat. However, the gameplay loop as a whole seriously needs help.The game is effectively JUST the combat and mech-building, and there's nothing else to it. While that might sound like a lot, there's a lot of redundant weapons that do the same things in only marginally different ways, and due to the Borderlands-esque loot system, it's entirely possible to just get something busted early on that lets you mow through the game without too much effort. I've had mechs go into level 6-7 battles with level 1/2 parts because those parts were just that good.There's no story to look forward to. No world-building, no information besides what you get exposited at you in the beginning, not even really a name for your enemies or a reason to hate them. Like, sure, they blow up a town and set up military guardposts...but why do they do it? It wasn't explained from what I played. They're even more faceless and have even less motivation than The Empire in Star Wars.At a $30 price tag, I'd be very hard-pressed to say that's the right price. At $20 or any sort of sale, then the game is probably worth picking up if you think you'd enjoy the tactical pseudo-action combat and looting mech parts for the 60+ hours the campaign will last you.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: This is a tech demo for a really cool new combat system, with just enough padding to seem like a game, at least for a few hours. I've lost count of how many times I've come back to it, thinking there had to be more, something I was missing, but there just isn't.The combat is smooth, and if I could just cut that part out and paste it into most of the Turn-Based games I've played, I absolutely would. Crazy cinematic potential, or there would be, if the devs had thought to include a cinematic replay option.The gear has no actual level cap, which might seem cool, at least at first, but it means that no matter how far you progress, you can never actually build your team up in a way that fits with whatever strategy you prefer, instead you're forced to use whatever has dropped, just to stay competitive against enemies leveled to match. This means there is no mid- or end-game, just the same game, forever, and the usual reward loop of new gear isn't one, when nothing is ever going to be worth keeping for long. There's nothing to strive for; there's a point to having a maximum level in a game, and the devs here somehow never learned that.If it had a story, I'd call it shallow, but this is less of a puddle than it is a slightly damp tile floor.I really, really wish I could recommend the game, it does come out with an innovative, fun, and cinematic new combat system, but that's literally all it brings to the table.I can only hope for a sequel in which the devs actually build up a full game.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun tactical game with minor weaknesses and a unique control system that allows for an unprecedented level of control over your unit's actions: Your AI can predict enemy actions for up to 5 seconds and allows you to plan your moves accordingly. You then plot you plan on the timeline and let them play out when you're done.Although the UI can be a bit clunky when it comes to actions carrying over to the next turn and I find the melee controls more confusing than helpful, it's a lot of fun and a unique seling point for the game. The only downside of the control system is that planning in increments of 5 seconds means that your pilots won't respondy dynamically when the situation changes. They will shoot at an enemy just as planned, even if that mech already blew up earlier that turn, shoot their own comrades who couldn't clear the line of fire because they stumbled, or try to jump onto a building's roof while that building is collapsing. That's when the mechs start to feel more like dumb robots than machines piloted by skilled soldiers. It would be more believable if the pilots would just skip certain planned actions if they were no longer neccessary or helpful (not shooting dead enemies, hold fire if a friendly is in the line of fire) .This, however, is more than compensated for by the tactical depth the system creates.The campaign could have received some more love from the devs, as its minimalist presentation leads to a lack of motivation. The first and the final missions are scripted and tell a story, everything in between is randomly generated standard encounters and a few story missions (standard missions with a bit of fluff text) every once in a while that are randomly generated from a pool of about 5 (!) different templates. You move around an enemy province with you mobile base, capture strategically important places, ambush convoys and evade or engage enemies hunting you. After each won encounter you loot and salvage ressouces and mech parts. Each won encounter also reduces the enemy power in the region by a certain number and when the enemy power reaches 0 the province was liberated in the release version. Since update 1.2 a boss encounter spawns instead wherin you have to defeat some variation of giant walker, from a very big spider mech to a walking gun-toting fortress, to capture the province. Rinse & Repeat ad nauseam. There is no strategic enemy presence in the game. Each province exists independently, there is no support from other enemy provinces, the enemy never counter-attacks or tries to recapture provinces. Whoever the invader was that captured the homeland, on a strategic level they are completely apathetic in regard to the insurgence.I got some fun out of building and modifying my mechs and improving the base. You can craft parts and equipment once you have the blueprints and enough ressources. There are three quality levels and mod slots come with pre-installed mods, most of which can't be changed. The higher the quality level the more mods can be changed, but even at the highest level you will have one fixed mod. With high level ressources being rare, crafting items and ending up with mediocre or detrimental mods can hurt and encourages save scumming. I wish that at least at the hightest level all slots would be modifiable. Eventually the game became rather repetetive and I aborted my first playthrough about half-way through the campaign. Then update 1.3 dropped. This update brought some radical changes (most importantly to heat management) as well as new gear and a new equipment slot for support systems (missile defense, mine-layers, missile launchers and artillery missiles. Tactical depth has improved and thanks to the new heat management, the missile nerf and the new support systems many new mech builds have become possible the utilise previously underperfoming gear, encouraging players to experiment and diversify their arsenal. The only minor downsides are that it can be tricky to chain heat venting actions between turns, causing mechs to overheat and go up in flames (the solution: only use H1 vents, avoid the H2 vents and dont ever use modules that prolong the venting process; you will only be able to vent for 1 second, but you can infinitely chain these actions even between turns in about 95% of cases), and that the boss fights from update 1.2 can become trivial beginning mid-game, because you will be able to field a squad of dedicated artillery mechs that can just nuke the ♥♥♥♥♥♥ from safe cover.With the new update I had so much fun with the game that I finally played through the entire campaign and kept wanting more. If the next update or a PB2 brought a dynamic campaign as well and maybe dropped the bloody "at least one mod slot on every crafted item comes with a mod that can't be replaced" rule, I would be in heaven.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: Played a good couple of sessions now and I'm pretty engrossed. The game isn't without it's foibles though (see later in the review). I do recommend it, but appreciate that it's eccentricities may turn some people off and that it has some way to go to being a truly great mech strategy game.The storyline is basically non-existent. Everything is talked about in abstracts and the game is pathologically incapable of giving you a proper noun to hold on to. But I expect that most people aren't here for a story, just a competent sandbox. I am in that camp, and I am feeling right at home here.While you're not going to end up with winged gundams or Armored Core spider mechs, the customisation is robust and gives you plenty of options on for both unit and squad composition. Battles feel gratuitous, with nice visuals and satisfying impact to a lot of weapons. I've had a couple of close calls despite the precog nature of the game mechanics. Being able to come out on top when you're outnumbered and facing reinforcements is deeply satisfying.Overall, once I got past the cryptic interface, I find my turns taking less time and my build choices more definitive and I'm loving it. I look forward to seeing how the devs follow up (shout out to Brace Yourself for providing rapid fixes and a dedicated feedback button).For a more balanced review - these are my current issues & things I would like to see built on:~ The game presents a lot of information to you at once, but often sacrifices clarity for a clean aesthetic. ~ There is a tutorial, but it covers only the very basics of taking your turn. More granular information is left for you to figure out. The most egregious for me right now is the relationship the generator stats affect practical performance of a mech, so I'm left just dropping in generators until I have a stat spread I like.~ As others have echoed, the ability to see the entire battle play out would be amazing. And I would like to be able to see damage being applied during replays. As it stands the damage is applied to units only when the turn is first executed, but when replaying the units health is at it's end value.~ Some way to access your mech roster during the post game, whether a carnage report in the salvage screen, or giving us access to the normal build page. It can be difficult making salvage selections when you don't know your entire team's parts make-up off by heart.~ Custom paint schemes. This should have been a shoe-in for a game that provides 60+ paint schemes by default.~ Better filtering for the inventory. There is no option to filter by item level, and no select all, with highlighted selections sometimes all being deselected when you click on a previous item. As it stands I find myself having to scrap entire item levels of gear (once I have accrued enough of the next tier to default to the higher tier) but have to manually select each, then scrap.~ Pilot customisation. This is a big shortcoming as the Mount & Blade-eque presentation had be expecting squad management like Xcom (skill trees), Mordheim (highly visually customisable plus positive and negative perks) and heck even Mechwarrior 5 (incremental skill gains). The pilots are just names and faces, they have no defining character, and no mechanical use other than being another health bar to keep tabs on. I would like to see more customisation options, and potentially some mechanical use breathed into them.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: 9/10this game is goodIt's a turn-based mech game with a "prediction" system that lets you see what the enemy is going to do on the next turn. The style is fantastic, the physics are awesome, and the effects and animations are also well above the price range. You can shoot through buildings with a laser beam to attack vehicles hiding on the other side, it's sweet.You can thoroughly customize each mech, and building a balanced team is pretty fun because of the diversity of weaponry. A mech that runs fast and uses a sword is going to play completely differently from another one that tries to shoot missiles from a vantage point. Armor choices drastically affect the mobility and survivability of mechs, and so it is important to build them correctly for their role. There are also mods that you can slot on armor to increase their ability to do certain things.The story and characters are OK, and admittedly i haven't completely finished the game yet, but I'm 16 hours in and still haven't even been told the name of either my own country or the invading enemy's. This is weird because it seems like every other character knows exactly what's going on but nobody's told me yet. The game has a real Ace Combat vibe, in that it doesn't really make any sense but somehow every other character in the game understands completely. The game also has this weird fixation on gender pronouns, which seems to be a mainstay in indie games now.The main progression in the game is through equipable items that drop from battle. There is a workshop where you can collect blueprints through combat and then craft the specific items that you want, and it works really well. The level of crafted items scales with your team, so you never feel like the crafted stuff is going to be worse than what you'll randomly get from battles. There are a few problems though:--Melee Weapons. I have been using at least one mech with a melee weapon for pretty much my entire playthrough, and I'm still just guessing every time i make an attack with them. You get a prediction of the swing path to show you if you can hit an enemy or not, but most of the time it's just completely wrong and doesn't correspond to what actually happens at all. --Map Diversity. You will play the same maps 50+ times each. They are pretty unique in how you can use the terrain, but it does get old after so many times. It also doesn't help that this entire country looks the exact same, so there's not much in terms of desert, or snow, or rocks, it's pretty much all just a neighborhood or a military base with a forest around it.--Awareness. There are times where i'm commanding a squad of 4 of my mechs, and another squad of 4 AI friendly units, and one of my mechs will get killed somewhere on the battlefield and I have no idea until the end of the battle. There's nothing that displays the status of all of your units, so its up to you to click on each individual one to see how they're doing. So if you want to keep track of them you have to pretty much replay every turn and look around the whole battlefield to see everything that happened to each mech. I would love a UI element that just shows me the health of all of my mechs and tells me if one of them is concussed, crashing, or deceased.Overall, The game is great and just needs a little polish to be a masterpiece. Definitely worth the $30 asking price.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: I have a lot to complain about / long for in the game although it is enjoyable. Gameplay is pretty basic but a few tweaks could make it much more exciting. The wait mechanic is pretty wonky and i wish it was entirely removed for you being able to place any action (including run) at any point within the timeline. This would be a smoother and faster experience to play. The customization is pretty bad. I hope they improve it. Colors are bunched in groups of three which limits the options for some strange reason. And Also I feel like the Light, Medium, Heavy armor literally makes zero difference in what the performance of that armor piece actually is. I've found heavy armor that's actually less mass then light armor which makes me question, why add it in the first place? Also there doesn't seem to be any use in the heavy armor class to begin with because they are so slow they spend most of the game running towards the enemy only to get caught out in the open by faster mechs and not have the armor to be able to withstand an appropriate additional amount of damage for the trade off. Then they also heat up faster leaving them with less damage and being quite useless since they end up being knocked out from concussive damage anyways. There is a need for a major rebalance for these heavy mechs or else nobody is ever going to use them.Most attacks with weapons also use two bursts which makes attacking in small time frames impossible, which limits possibilities even more. Just split it into a single burst from a weapon and allow players to use the attack twice, simple fix which allows more flexibility in strategy. My final gripe about gameplay is that the beam weapon in the game cannot sweep attack like it does in the trailer (which was very hype and something i immediately wanted to do in game) kinda a let down. And lets just not talk about the mission brief table. It offers even less information than entering the level and looking at the screen for two seconds. Improve or remove please....Then there's the "cinematic story". It would have done more good for the game to spend time solely on mechanics and leave this aspect completely out. Its terrible. There's no reason for the two completely unnamed armies to be fighting, no name of the place they are fighting over, other terrible names like the "Home Guard". And for some reason all this emotional dialogue like we care about a place referred to as "Home" with no setting that we learned about within this exact same cutscene 10 seconds ago. Seriously if its this low effort just leave it out of the game because it seriously subtracts from the overall experience. Dialogue stops after the first couple missions anyways so there was no point in doing it to begin with. I can fully understand if it wants to be a moddable, sandbox experience where you make your own pilots, mechs, and stories, that makes sense, just leave the story element out then. And more importantly don't falsely market it as cinematic.If you want to create a baseline environment for people to create their own stories in, at least name the factions, give them a motive for fighting, name the region they are fighting over and give it a little history, just create SOME FORM OF SETTING. a modding community isn't going to do this for you and they're most definitely not going to voice characters. I've played plenty of sandbox games, and the experience of no story is better than this randomly cut off 15 minutes intro that is as shallow as a puddle with like 20 voice lines. TLDR: It's a fun, albeit gameplay limited game with some very questionable choices made by the dev team in terms of story, setting, and gameplay that subtract from the overall enjoyment. At least it's not full priced, maybe wait or get it on sale. Only recommending if you enjoy sandbox, and are hoping that the devs continue to tweak some thing like I am.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: Phantom Brigade's graphics are as satisfying and clean as a freshly ironed shirt, but they aren't going to knock your socks off.The overall look of the game is functional and modern, and the mechs themselves are nicely detailed, for an RTS that is. It's nothing revolutionary, but that's also something you wouldn't expect from a rts.One of the strengths of Phantom Brigade is its user interface, which is as intuitive as it gets.The game is easy to navigate, and what buttons do what is easy enough to learn that a trained monkey could do it (not that we'd recommend that if you value the lives of your pilots, but you get the vibe) its the opposite from an eyesore.Unfortunately, Phantom Brigade suffers from a lack of mission variety and story. It's like Groundhog Day, but with mechs. You just keep moving around, claiming territories and fighting nearly identical battles.The story is also a letdown, with little to get excited about. It's unfortunate that the game lags a little here, as it could have added a lot more depth and variety to the experience. You'll feel like you're trapped in a time loop, and not in a good way.Phantom Brigade's gameplay is fantastic, but it does require a lot of guesswork at times. You'll put in a lot of time learning the game, but it'll still feel like a game of chance. Setting up an elaborate plan and watching it unfold piece by piece is entertaining, but it can also be frustrating when things don't go as planned. It's like playing Jenga: you carefully stack the pieces, but they can all fall down in an instant.Phantom Brigade is the ultimate game of micromanagement. It's similar to a puzzle game, but with guns and missiles instead of puzzle pieces. It can become very micromanagement-intensive, which will hurt your head a lot.Especially since it can sometimes make fights too long to enjoy. You might find yourself playing for 30 minutes for only 1 minute of actual action. However, for micromanagement fans, it's a dream come true, so this isn't necessarily a negative; rather, it's a warning that this game isn't for everyone.Phantom Brigade runs flawlessly on my PC, and I can enjoy the satisfying gameplay without interruption. However, other players have reported some performance issues, so keep some cooling fans nearby in case your pc turns into the core of the sun.Phantom Brigade's visual customization options for your mechs are a nice touch, but they don't quite hit the mark. It's like going clothes shopping while under the influence of every substance known to man; you just can't seem to get the color or design you're looking for. It's a shame because there's so much potential for making your mechs truly unique and personal.Phantom Brigade provides a wide range of choices for mech loadouts, and it's honestly overwhelming in the best way possible. You can customize your mech to your heart's content and play however you want with so many weapons to choose from. Phantom Brigade is a solid turn-based strategy game with a distinct twist. For those who enjoy micromanaging, the graphics are pleasing, the user interface is simple, and the gameplay is enjoyable.However, the lack of variety in missions and story can be disappointing, similar to receiving a toy you already own for Christmas. HowHowever, It's still a game worth playing, and with a little bit of tweaking and updating, it has the potential to be even better. Overall, I give Phantom Brigade a 7.8 out of 10 - it's a good game worth your time if you like the genre and blowing stuff up.

_childDocuments_.review: Bought the game in pretty early access, gave it some time for new content. Took out a boss, moved on to another area and I just dont find the game fun. The game just does not feel engaging or exciting. Weapon or backpacks, just arent dropping with much variety. For example, ive had the 2H Minigun drop and 1 Beam weapon drop only once, each, in around 15 hours of playing. I feel like I have to grind out on patrols and roaming enemies to get lucky, even then, pieces of armor and weapons look like they have random perks attached to them, so I have to grind out decent ones just to survive enemies that get harder with each destroyed patrol. Made it to the 2nd boss and its such a slog, nothing im expecting from an early game boss. The early game being this tedious and sloggy only makes me dread mid and late game. Not even looking at the gameplay, the events are so uninspired and feel like they do nothing. For example, you can capture enemies in small, random events, to keep as "captives". Its treated like some sort of resource. What do they captives do? I dont know. Then theres events like getting a surplus of parts after a battle, so your engineers ask for some time to fiddle around to make something amazing. I waited till the end and BAM, nothing. The game doesnt tell me what I got and I couldnt find anything that made me waste my time. The game feels like the tedium was intentional, in order to pad out the play time, even the story feels hollow and generic. I dont mind when games are hard, with you have to work your way up, but this just is not fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Good idea, but very shallow. The Good-Interesting, responsive combat system.-Some variety in mech part designs.-Decent array of weapons.-Ability to create weapons and mech parts as you travel around is pretty neat. -Nice mech paint system. The BadI have to compare this game to three similar-ish games.  Battletech, X-Com, and Warhammer: Dawn of War -Story is a single sentence : Another country has invaded, push them back!-Liberating an area does not provide any benefits/bonus. See DoW and Xcom. -Pilots may have visual variety, but don't have any personality. Can't specialise and level up your pilots. No voice either. See Battletech, X-Com.-Maps come in three varieties - no buildings, some civilian buildings, some military buildings.  That's it.  No other variations.  See all 3 games. -Some of the upgrades to the mobile base don't seem to offer a lot of benefit based on the massive investment required. See Battletech, X-Com.Seems like a cool combat system wrapped up in half baked overworld/tactical map.  Which is really sad. Dawn of War, Battletech and X-Com are not new games.  Ideas from those games, and many other games could have been implemented to give Phantom Brigade more flavour.  Pick it up if there's a sale maybe, but I do regret paying full price for this.

_childDocuments_.review: Waited to see if this would get any updates, but sadly there is nothing and it looks to be abandoned.As many other reviews say, this game is a very good shell of what could have been an amazing tactics game up there with the greats like XCOM. But sadly, a shell of a game it is.Once you liberate about 2 regions there is nothing new to be seen. Every combat becomes the same rinse and repeat strategy and on the same handful of maps. The story is virtually non-existent and even the evil empire your fighting doesn't even have a name or any motive to speak of.Its truly a sad state of affairs. An excellent foundation, but with nothing built upon it.

_childDocuments_.review: There's a lot to like here and I've enjoyed my time with the game quite a bit.  Went from a couple of 10+ hour sessions of rapt engagement initially to only feeling like playing a fight or two before wanting to put it down but I expect to be returning for these short enjoyable sessions daily until I've crushed the invaders and liberated all the provinces of our beautiful nation. The overland strategy portion is dynamic and has more than enough things going on to be surprisingly enjoyable.  Additionally, the destructive capacity deployed by friend and foe alike is quite satisfying.  Units can be cut down quickly and that's much more engaging than having to slog through turns and turns of chopping off tiny health percentages (something I consider a huge design mistake in many other games, one that's especially easy to make when large mechs are involved).  There's also a pretty decent array of weapon types and they're all deadly when used properly so quite a few different kinds of tactics are available.Biggest complaint is, I like timeline mechanics in turn based games but in this case getting to see exactly what all the enemies are going to do makes the combat far too easy.  This can be slightly compensated for by not playing an overly cautious strategy and really overextending your reach into enemy territory but that's not an entirely satisfying substitute if you're looking for the feeling of serious risk and being on the verge of calamity with any misstep.I really wish they'd gone with more of a Frozen Synapse timeline approach (maybe overlaid with a branched set of likely enemy actions) and played to the timeline mechanic's real strengths of allowing you to simulate as many different enemy paths as you can think of in order to thread the needle of optimizing against all the possibilities.Pathfinding can be a little annoying (but hey it's a fully 3d somewhat dynamic environment so just be patient with it) and the AI is pretty dumb (seriously exacerbated by always knowing exactly what they're going to do).  Additionally, the npc unit weapons seem randomized when it would have been nicer to see groups with weapons and tactics designed to work together.Had a couple crashes but only if i left the game running overnight.

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to like this game, and there are a lot of fun moments, but the early game is exceptionally tedious before you get to the interesting parts and CTD's are frequent while often outright computer breaking. The last CTD before posting this review burned a number of white pixels into my screen that lasted until a full computer restart. Funnily, the crashes are often tied to memory space in your C drive, the time between them gets longer as you have more room, because some Developer thought they were being smart to hard code virtual memory allocation as a vital system that you can't disable.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall 6.5/10. The first 10 hours were very enjoyable the first time around, but then the game got... repetitive? It's a unique combat system that really lets you plan around enemy tactics and movement, rewarding smart gameplay with the ability to consecutively hop into the action mission after mission. The glaring faults exist in the equipment/crafting management and mission planning, and the boss fights all felt very similar and methodical. Oh, and I crushed the "final" mission about 1/3 of the way through the liberation, so it all felt very.... low investment afterwards.The different mech parts and loot the game throws at you is high volume, low quality, meaning you need to sift through loads of equipment looking for anything that is incrementally better. My experience led me to having equipment 5-10 levels below the enemies I'm fighting because some good pieces dropped and I never got anything better over the next 10-15 hours. The crafting didn't make up for this unreliable method since crafting blueprints were rare and cranked out mid-tier items at best that I salvaged 9.9/10 times. While the "predictive software" element was neat, you still dropped blind into the mission and had no control over placement, leading to a dance to untangle your mechs for good positioning.That being said, the variance of the weapons and different action times / damage per shot and heat management really brought a lot of flavour, creating a fun and at times challenging balancing act of outgoing damage vs repositioning to avoid damage and blow off heat. Adding to freedom of experimenting with play-style is the ability to choose your missions: raid static bases or intercept convoys and roaming units. Each requires different focus for your mechs and favours different strengths. Would have liked to see more/multiple elite enemies as they were the only "challenging" factor in the later stages of my campaign. IMO, worth the buy if you can get it on sale, but don't expect 50+ hours out of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR Fun core game with a weak overarching structure. You will enjoy the first 10-15 hours, and then it will grow a bit stale.Straight up front, this is a really fun, satisfying core premise. The Mech fights are exactly as satisfying as they look in the store media. Combat is visceral and fast, effective attacks will rapidly destroy the enemy - or you, if you're not playing smart. The prediction system means you can actually survive such a dangerous combat environment reliably, as long as you're smart and don't over exert yourself.The process of building and upgrading them is also nice, salvaging the defeated enemies for parts. The salvage mechanics encourage some additional tactical decisions in combat, and the mech design and their stats means you are actively rewarded with new options based on your salvage and assembly decisions - There is not really one singular 'best' path, as much as their are multiple good ones of equal capability.Unfortunately, the external campaign loop is extremely shallow. The overworld is boring and static. Enemy patrols and convoys are relatively static, predictable entities in the map. The enemy forces will not attack or pressure you, and once you have captured a region, it is permanently secure. You can slowly march as you wish across the game map. The main base upgrades are marginal at best beyond a couple cheap early unlocks to enable sprint/4 mechs/etc. You can easily afford those in zone one, and the rest is just the same old. There is very little motivating plot - Your liberating your country, but you don't know anything about your people, or the enemy, or why they invade,d how they won, etc. Even the pilots you take into combat are interchangeable - They have a written backstory blurb, but no skills, no abilities, no differentiation, and completely replaceable.This lack of overarching tissue amplifies a few issues with the actual combat encounters as well - There are a limited set of maps, they are extremely small, and once you get good with the timeline management of the game, you become basically immortal. You will end up with the same fights, on the same maps, where the enemy can't touch you. You will repeat these fights over every region, with no change or threats, as you march across the map to fill it with your color because the tooltip says so.Don't get me wrong, its still fun, but it rapidly becomes the exact same fun, with no stakes or variety. The ear to ear smile of the first missions as you dodge between beam cannon shots while threading the needle to keep an enemy mech in optimal weapon range will grow weary as you do it for a third, forth, fifth time. The games just lacking staying power, narratively or mechanically.Luckily, its something that I'm confident can be solved even just by expansions in the future, if not dedicated modders, as the game does have good modding support. More maps will reduce the map fatigue, and an expansion dedicated to overhauling the campaign overmap and its interactions would go a long way to dealing with these issues, without requiring a total rewrite of the real guts of the game, which are genuinely solid. We just need more places to fight our battle, and more external reasons to want to fight them.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: Story is terrible, it's so barebones that it's entirely worth skipping so you don't have a worse opinion of the game for it. Just assume it literally doesn't exist.Mechs can be customized, with a framework that should allow for a lot of customization options. However, the cosmetic options are extremely limited though, so it kinda detracts after you realize that the nice customization system is also, like the story, pretty barebones.Combat's good, though it's really frustrating how bad melee is. The prediction system doesn't always work perfectly. Which when you're playing a game like this, that's extremely important to get right. Though it does an amazing job 99% of the time.Lastly, and this was huge for me as someone who played "YOMI Hustle" before this. There's no way to watch your fight in it's entirety after you finish it. I feel like having this feature would increase the replayability a LOT since watching the cool fight you choreographed after 20-60 minutes of intense deliberation would be an amazing way to let you sit back and be rewarded for playing well. Instead, you're just sent back to the overworld with no break. This works fine for entirely turn based games. But Phantom Brigade is based on timed actions, so I think this was a huge missed opportunity.TL;DRIf the combat is really appealing to you, and I mean VERY appealing. Yeah this game is worth picking up. Otherwise, all the extra features you might expect from a game that 'looks' this polished at first glance simply aren't there. So I'd give it a pass or wait on a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: EDITED: Some grammar, and expanded thoughts on mechanical depth for mech pilots.The simultaneous round-based combat is a marvel that I want to see in more games. There is just something so gratifying in seeing a well thought out tactical battleplan coming together with solid physics in the mech movements (and collisions) and environmental destruction lends satisfying power to the the array of near future weapons your mechs can carry into battle.However, the satisfying moment to moment gameplay is let down by how empty and repetitive the main campaign shows itself to be, and how token your pilots are as of writing.The campaign, where you liberate your unnamed homeland from a vastly powerful (and also unnamed) invader is rendered sterile by a lack of any distinct people or cultural hallmarks within your brigade, or on the sociopolitical political layer, apart from some vaguely European city names. Who are the beloved leaders of your homeland in peril? Who are your plucky resistance pilots? Who is the hated commander of the enemy force? As generic as this sounds, its better than the nothing we currently have.For example, XCOM 2 has the brutal Advent alien collaborators vs. the fleshed out human resistance leaders who act as your advisors between missions with your personalized soldier's stories playing out in gameplay through emergent storytelling, empowered by a robust appearance customizer (supported by thousands of mods from an amazing community), and even a Persona style bonds system that enhances the performance of particular squadmates with one another (admittedly introduced in a later expansion). With these personalities, you have figures to root for, to worry for, to despise, who are worth remembering and emotionally investing in until they die tragically because you made a mistake or got unlucky in a turn.Hand in hand with deep character customization of your squad's appearance are mechanical customizations: traits, skills and special abilities that further individualise your soldiers in battle. This allows the exploration of synergies between the soldier and their kit, tailoring each to specialized roles based on your preferred style of play. By contrast, Phantom Brigade pilots are nothing more than a name, birthplace, a personality adjective, and biography text, if they are given one at all. If the developers' intention was to make just an in-depth mech tactics game without focusing on the pilots, it might have been simpler to remove the pilots altogether. Having the pilots exist as is just draws attention to how bare bones the feature is. Hopefully they can expand this and make pilot choice more meaningful with more cosmetic appearances and mechanical depth that promotes keeping veteran pilots alive and caring about their growth and development.Without emotional investment in those who represent the society and way of life of your homeland, the faceless Home Guard, or even the vaguely threatening invading forces, what is the Phantom Brigade fighting for beyond better gear? Every city you liberate is just a point on a map, and every squad of enemies whose lives you end are just a pile of XP, scrap and colour graded weapons for your squad to pick up. There is text here and there for the occasional event and description of specific locations, but they are so lacking in distinctiveness that they all end up looking the same. The near-future sci-fi aesthetic of blocky tech buildings and farm houses doesn't help with this, but can be overcome with better writing and more distinct characters on and off the battlefield.In closing, once you get used to the incredibly fun tactical combat, there is little more to keep you going to realize the final liberation of your homeland beyond shinier mech parts and guns with better stats. For those who like mechanics and equipment grind or optimization, perhaps this game in its current form will be enough. But I prefer some story and character in every game I choose to play.I sincerely hope the developer's announced intent to continue expanding Phantom Brigade brings about more content that fleshes out the unnamed nation and war we are called to fight 5 seconds at a time. Phantom Brigade has so much promise. This simultaneous round mechanic is worthy of praise and should be spread throughout the industry. Please don't let it be buried by a lackluster campaign, setting, characters and story that sells the tactical combat short.

_childDocuments_.review: Confession Bear: By default I wouldn't unconditionally recommend this to friends but it's actually a lot of fun if expectations are set right.I dislike how half-baked a lot of things in Phantom Brigade feel, like they gave up at some point after taking that EGS money. Strategic layer is a disappointment compared to Highfleet, the latter which portrays in a more sophisticated manner a small elite group being chased by an incumbent aggressor.  Specifically, it's kind of weird that the opposing force never counterattacks any of your provinces despite having numeric superiority, especially when there are other strategy games which model that kind of changing battleline. Other systems like pilot progression feel abandoned and then band-aided with simplified placeholders.  In general, I understand some of the excuses the dev team makes about things like how replay is limited by RAM, etc, but it sometimes feels like the devs sunk into a technical debt hole with their promising tech demo, and have given up on tackling more comprehensive systems.But the procedural destruction of the tactical combat phases looks so pretty (it's cool that every projectile is modeled with physics), so I like turning the difficulty all the way down so I can watch mechs spray tracers each other while innocent buildings get wrecked in the crossfire.  It kind of ruins the challenge, but honestly the AI decisions are kind of silly looking, and most of the difficulty was from how overpowered the AI team is numbers wise, while their actual movements are kind of primitive (shoot, move random spot without coordination with teammates, shoot again).  The AI won't even change targets if the target they chose moves behind cover.  It's more relaxing to acknowledge the AI is kind of dumb and to set up mechs shooting each other in a replay loop while zooming the camera around at various angles.  It's one of those games where it might be a neat marketing trick to have an integrated gif recorder, so players could export a particularly fancy view of a battle as a sharable visual snippet.Anyway, I have no hope the devs are going to revamp the game, so I'll recommend this if you can get it cheap, as well as if you understand that you'll probably abandon the campaign at some point. The story has no sense of progression (the random events feel disjointed and unrelated), so you better be okay with treating the game as a sandbox for mech battles.I also recommend DoSsMode's replay edits of battles.  I don't exactly know how they remembered which camera angles to stitch together to make edits seem relatively coherent between planning gameplay, but it's fun to see battles from start to end even if the devs gave up on full battle replays:PS Edit:I thought this discussion about Phantom Brigade was interesting and highlighted some neat systems that I didn't know about:It's also interesting that there was only 1 developer working on the game systems over the years, so now I'm a little less baffled as to why there wasn't that much progress on the early access roadmap.They also highlighted that there are mods that can add different mission scenarios to the tactical battles:That gives me a little more hope that the community could breath some life into the game, as Phantom Brigade was really at its best early in game with more intentionally crafted scenarios.PPS more musings:It's funny that both the Three Moves Ahead podcast, and this video commentary:... point out that there's an interesting potential story thread that the actual game never pursues. (Plus the YouTube video references Highfleet too, a bonus in my mind.)The Phantom Brigade is a rogue military squad with weird prediction technology fighting with guerilla tactics, why doesn't the Home Guard or the government in exile have more of a uncertain relationship with the brigade? There's a missed story opportunity where your friendly side really should initially distrust your rogue insurgent group. I get that the devs didn't want to veer in to political territory, but it's odd that the story is so boring when there could have been some really interesting story beats.Honestly I hope there will be a mod that just does a linear scripted campaign that iterates through all available maps, because I'm starting to notice repeats of maps, both in my own playthroughs and also from watching others' campaigns.I guess why Phantom Brigade bothers me is that the core tactical loop is really promising, and it baffles my mind that the rest of the game feels so empty. I don't have any expectation that the devs are going to continue development, it just strikes me as tragic the apparent lack of funds to further develop this concept.

_childDocuments_.review: Not quite finished with the user experience. It's difficult to fine-tune everything with the pseudo-turn based system in particular. It's one thing to have a better part, but MMO loot drop style for a game as complex as this has no place.Finally, there's a ton of stats that are an absolute chore to track, which, with some sensible game design, could have, and should have, been way easier to understand.I haven't gotten that far into the campaign...And I don't think I'm going to.
