_childDocuments_.review: Whelp here we go again. Do I recommend this game? Short answer yes with an if, long answer no with a but. I was really excited for this one because I loved Mordheim,  the tabletop version of this game, and tabletop kill team. Got pretty worried when this got stuck in development, not sure what happened, whatever. The setting of this game is perfect, dark, rusty underground facilities that are all stacked catwalks, tis great. It adds dimension to the arena and looks fantastic. Fun to set up ambushes, block exits, and crowd around the occasional healing station. The options for gang customization are nice looking, fun to play around with. Graphically Necromunda looks amazing. Turn based gameplay is one of my very favorites, and I love all the little tactical options, all of this is fine. 3 houses is all GW gave us to start with. Goliath (hulking brutes), Escher (All ladies), and Orlock (team generic). I wound up going with Orlock because I like a mix of Guys and Gals, however, and I know this is subjective, but if i have the option I'd rather not play human in my fantasy games... I get to do that in real life every day. I was really hoping for some Genestealer Cults or some Chaos, I'm into the really unique and grotesque that goes along with the high gothic fantasy that is the Warhammer universe. The lack of diversity is compounded as well, in that the gangs are just really not that different or unique. All weapons can be used by any different house, stats are flexible enough that your skinny Esher girls can be just as brutal and hearty in melee as a Goliath gorilla. Its too easy to compare Necromunda to mordheim (which i put about 600 hours into over many years). That game each warband had its own strong and unique flavor. Tanky caster sisters of battle, Flintlock firearms and stealth with the skaven, magic and mutations with chaos. The uniqueness of the factions, the tactics you had to employ with each, and the weapons which were unique to each added a ton of depth to the game, strategy, learning curves, beautiful asymmetry, and replay ability. They really need to do something to give each gang their own unique flavor because as it stands its purely an aesthetic choice, which makes the actual replay kind of boring. I'm assuming multiple of the other gang houses will be released as DLC, which seems to be GW's MO at this point, I've accepted it as an unfortunate fact of life, and at this point I'd welcome it, I really want to play my Genestealer Cultists. This has many of its own problems as well though, will the new gangs have anything new or different? Will there be a power creep to encourage people to shell out money for the new warbands? Probably... Mordheim's 2 DLC factions were laughably more powerful than the originals, Witch hunters being pretty strong, and Vampires being completely OP. Theres always the possibility also of them just not being made because of lack of interest due to the oddity of Necromunda's release or the mixed reviews. I worry about these things. Basically I recommend Necromunda if you're a die hard 40k fan, or if you know for sure you like this type of turned based tactics, because there's tons of room for improvement. Hopefully the game wont be abandoned and we'll get to see the Necromunda the fans deserve. GW has a quantity over quality policy that's always really rubbed me the wrong way, with this game all the elements of a great turn based tactical arena are there, a few tweaks and this could be a really standout game. I just hope that GW and Rogue Factor have the grit to address the issues rather than shelving Necromunda and moving to the next project.(Edit) *  So, I changed from recommended to not recommended for a few reasons here. First off, having to play through the single player campaign to unlock cosmetics is incredibly stupid. People like me, who've played a lot of games like this and just want to build their own gang and play are bored to tears by a 15 mission tutorial, no thank you. Second are the "Vices" targeted to your class? Played through with 3 gangs so far. My leader, first time out was a sniper. Got the vice that gives you -10% Ranged damage and immediately scrapped the gang. Its easier to just start over that level a lowbie leader with high level followers. Second time went with a melee boss.... -10% melee damage. Third gang, made a heavy weapons leader... -10% ranged damage. If this is just epic bad luck then thats great, but when perks are things like (gets extra healing from healing stations) amazing thats useful for like 1 out of 50 battles, but taking a 10% hit to all your damage is unacceptably punishing when the perks are generally trash. Third the AI is terrible. The camera zooms in on them, then you wait about 90 seconds to watch them take an elevator to the top level, then jump down to the lowest level, to walk past 2 enemy gangers and call the elevator back and take it to the top floor and end the turn. They dont know how to destroy barriers, so you can just wall off the exit. Then position your guys around the barricade, picking off all the enemies that collect the loot and bring it directly into your trap one at a time to die horribly. Also, don't start releasing paid DLC before the basics are working.-TLDR-Ultimately the incredibly vanilla feeling of all the gangs, the broken AI, and the tedious nature of the snatch and run missions make this a forgettable and often boring game.

_childDocuments_.review: It's every bit as bad as the last minute game play trailers looked.Nearly everything wrong with Mordheim is still in there:-Tons of stats and abilities to sift through, while only a handful actually matter.-The character models are very nice, and they force you stare at them, thanks to the senseless over the shoulder camera perspective.-It is based off of a table top game, and plays much like one but is nothing like the game it is based off of.-Everything in the game is a dice roll or arbitrary and the huge open environments mean that the game is ever more dependent on the dice than Mordheim, since there is relatively little strategy to be had outside of your character builds.-The mixing of single player and multi player is still a poor idea in my opinion.-Being forced to watch a dumb AI move it's pieces around while you watch is incredibly annoying.-Three gangs with the same five character classes don't really make me feel like I have a ton of options in builds or play styles, just 3 slight variations on the same set of tools.-The sandbox/campaign system is incredibly shallow and uninteresting and the tactical battles are just repeat skirmish fights against the AI that feel repetitive after like 3 matches.The only real improvements are in the way they changed the campaign/sandbox mode and post battle looting. You don't lose just because you can't collect enough resources, you can concentrate on playing the missions and the campaign doesn't just put you up against a gang of exactly the same power level each time you go into a battle, the other gangs seem to level up and evolve as yours does. Also, the game now allows you one extra turn to move around and loot the map rather than just giving you a random amount of what's on the map after you win. But those two improvements while needed, aren't enough to fix the real problem which is boring, repetitive game play that just seems like grinding for the sake of grinding.

_childDocuments_.review: *EDIT* putting in a ticket for refund. This game might have been worth picking up in a year when they have it fixed up and the price is 75% off. Then again, for their first community update, they are announcing that they will be "working" on fixing major game issues which they simply can't have missed in testing, while also announcing DLCs. Basically they released a game they knew weren't done and didn't have sufficient content. Do the gaming community a favor and stay away from titles that use these tactics. Put out a working game with plenty of content, this trend with releasing non-working games with a long line of DLCs prepared is just pure ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.Currently the positives review are just fan-boys who are getting defensive, because the game is rightfully being called out on being a mess that got pushed through release.Go see the forum before buying, the people who "like" this game are literally defending it by saying "It's only 30 euro", "I expect a new games to need patches", and similar.----------------------tl;dr: Not worth buying at this point, get Mordheim and play that for a year, then come back and check on Necromunda.If we pretend that these guys didn't make Mordheim and this was the first game they put out AND it was the first game to ever be put out in this genre. Then this game might not be half bad, but that's not the case, which makes this game really bad.Why do we need to spend so much time going from one round to the other? Why do we need to spend so much time picking characters? The only real defense for the lacking rosters for the clans and the size of your party, would be speeding up multiplayer. But then we got all this other stuff just taking up time for no reason. Seems like half of the gameplay time is going to be spent watching "End of round X" etc. Why leave the movement system from Mordheim behind and not improve it? I guess there has been some attempt to smooth out the movement from Mordheim. However it doesn't work as intended, the movement is cluncky and it's unclear what the limits are and this just leads to even more backtracking than Mordheim had.So we basically got a lot of effort/budget put into cut scenes, voice acting and visuals, I'm not sure who decided these were the important parts for a decent turn based strategy game, but they probably shouldn't be invited onto new projects. Unfortunately they only spend 5 minutes considering what worked and didn't work in Mordheim, and then decided to remove the things that worked and left the things that didn't work. Like the AI will still run into walls for a couple of seconds, before just skipping their turn.Even the graphics options are lackluster, why are we forced to have motion blur on?At least now we know why they didn't put out any actual gameplay until 6 days before release. This just feels like an instant refund, guess it still has around an hour to convince me. At this point Mordheim is just a more complete game, which tries to do the same things, but actually succeeds at it. It's hard to believe that the same people made both games.Someone who hasn't played Mordheim or similar games and gets Necromunda without any expectations for the gameplay and wants a generic WH40K strategy game might enjoy this.

Pros: -Good atmosphere (music and design)-Great customization options for your own gang (weapons, skills, colours, etc)-Good and interesting leveling system-Long (potentially never-ending) campaign mode-Up to 4 player multiplayer matches (2v2, 1v3, free-for-all)-Good gameplayCons:-Bad AI! Needs some tweaking to make them not complete morons-Really annoying tutorial/Story mode-Various bugs (getting stuck, crashes, freezes, unstable camera on corners, etc) that need fixing!Overall, the game needs work, but I would still recommend it for fans of the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Editing just ahead of the first DLC's release. The game is now in a much less buggy state, although some gamebreaking bugs persist which isn't ideal when save files can't be loaded in an indefinite campaign relying on ironman saves. The AI also is a little more challenging, although it is still prone to bizarre behaviours at times. Even under the latest patch I've seen an AI gang member try to 'nade himself to death, and heading into a corner to overwatch nothing still happens.Turn times are much faster however. Although the fixed camera angle is still fixed in place.Would I recommend this game? No. Not really. Or at least not without caveats as there is no doubt a niche market for it. There are good things to this game but they are still buried under design decisions which really don't work for me. Whether further work on the game will escape the strait jacket the developers made for themselves, seemingly intended to balance an MP scene which never came to exist, remains to be seen. But as it is this is a game relying on its very well done 40k aesthetic to carry it in SP while it has died on its backside for MP.-----I know I'm only an hour in. But I'm already considering a refund. If you check my reviews, I do try to be really fair when I review before that option.Good things first. It looks fantastic. There's so much care gone into detail of environments and gang members themselves. The actual gameplay, the skills and the mechanics of combat, are very similar to this developers' Mordheim with some refinements and they play really nicely once you've gone through to figure out what's what.But there's some pretty major problems right now. The first should be a relatively minor one in the grand scheme of things but is exacerbated by the second. The game's got a problem in SP when the first melee fighter I come across runs up to my character, runs around my character, and then heads off to a corner and kneels facing away from all of my gang members. One off? Not really, in just 1 hour I've had an enemy 'nade himself almost to death against an object. I've watched enemy gang members go on weird detours to sightsee I don't know what. Now it's not always that bad at all. In fact, it can also be very impressive with using the environment to get around to make a shot. But all these AI glitches are really thrust into your face because of the second issue. Which is...You're forced to watch each and every AI gang member take its turn. And from a fixed camera. If you can move it so you can look about, I've not found it yet and apologies for being wrong. But fundamentally, there's no tension to this at all - you know where everyone is all of the time. Even if you don't want to. Even if you'd just like the AI to crack on so you can finish a full turn. It's a really, really bad design decision for SP. I can't honestly recommend this game. Hopefully the AI issues will be further patched and this review will be laughably out of date very quickly on that score. If you can live with the slow turns and the fixed camera to watch it then there's a lot here to enjoy. It's just a deal breaker for me on such a fundamental level of playing TTB.

_childDocuments_.review: It's in a bad space right now. It's no wonder we didn't see any gameplay footage of it until about a day before its release. I've had characters fall through the floor (rendering my team composition effectively meaningless), the AI is a buggy mess of absurd decisions (such as throwing grenades at literally nothing, walking into terrain until they decide to give up, or even walking into their own traps), and the UI, in my opinion, is a mess of bad decisions (unclear or too-similar symbols, no designation of sight-lines for overwatched enemies). All of this I can personally play through because I want to enjoy the game, and I do still find some enjoyment in it, but then it is compounded by even more fundamental issues, the most egregious of which is definitely the fact that the hit chance calculation lies to you and will frequently bug out, rapidly changing percentages when standing completely still. It doesn't help that the game also feels generally underdeveloped in the options it affords the player to customize their squad. Every House gets the exact same skills and abilities, except for the six specific to that House. This will likely pigeonhole players into a specific playstyle that their House prefers, which isn't necessarily bad, but I can't see much reason to play each House more than once to a relatively decent power level and then just giving up.I think this game has the potential to be really fun, and I would love to play it more once these issues are fixed, but as it stands right now, I can't recommend it to anyone who isn't super into tactical, squad-based games like this.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to like this game, I really do.Downtime between turns you play is staggeringly long. Especially in 1v1v1 maps. Being able to see what the opponent/AI does is powerful sure but Mordheim's way where you could only see them if you had line of sight was better.  Ambush is a pretty terrible ability with the lack of stealth lol.Speaking of the AI, too much potato in its current form. I had to watch an AI run cross 3 paths to take the wire down to where they started just to attack my character... It doesnt seem to really care about overwatch, my heavy weapon guy with barrage (Overwatch but can fire off multiple times if they move a certain amount within the sphere of influence) is making an absolute murder.I realised quickly theres no incentive to go for the objectives, just kill and loot the opponent and then try and grab objectives on the "loot round" after defeating the enemy factions. The AI likes to prioritize objectives over you so you can get some free encounters/first attack. In Mordheim looting as much warpstone you could get your hands on felt super important where balancing between skirmishes and running around and looting felt like an attractive style of play.There are good things about the game. Most of it you can experience in Mordheim. Removal of the upkeep is nice. Giving them gear and watching them getting some strap of metal attached to that part is nice.But the core game experience is not refined enough for me to recommend this game. Mordheim is great, there was a lot of fun in that game with the varied factions (here we got 3 different types of human factions) and the varied units inside the factions (no "champion" or "monster" units in this).I think the different classes are good too. Some do feel more basic than others. Saboteur and Engineer (whatever its called, the one with the servo arm) feel like the most fun classes to build. I keep the devs in good faith however. If they can improve the AI and give this game some QoL changes I can see myself changing this to a thumbs up review. But right now, Mordheim's base game is the better experience of these two.I hope there will be future DLC if the games sells good enough. I know there are other gang houses for the game, but I'm more so interested in seeing genestealers and ork warbands.

_childDocuments_.review: PRO+/-CON Review:PRO+For its current price (£5) it is worth every penny. Its fun, the voice acting is cheesy in the good sense, and the graphics look nice. The setting is exactly what you'd expect from Necromunda. The sets really feel like a high-budget tabletop setup.The AI is a bit dumb, yes, but you don't get the XCOM AI treatment where they all hone in on 1 unit for the sake of p*ssing you off, which is nice.The game's pace feels like an actual game of Necromunda. If you've not played the tabletop game you might find it a bit alien the way the chess-like turns work and how action points are used.Honestly I don't get why there are so many negative reviews.-CONUnless you have friends, don't expect to play multiplayer. It is almost completely dead.It is a little repetitive, but just do a mission or 2 when you want an inject. Unless there are timed objectives to secure, you've no reason to plan your strategy for the mission. The enemies don't usually pose that much of an intellectual threat. There is no perma-death in the main story. This is a CON purely from my own opinion because I love the likes of Darkest Dungeon and XCOM where this feature heavily weighs in on the risk/reward, much like playing Necromunda SHOULD feel.Finally, The characters aren't that cool. You'll find your favourites but personality wise they're forgettable and if one falls, meh. They'll be back next mission. The custom gang feature should be in the main story as it is in the skirmish mode.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to thumbs up this game so badly, it's so damn close but so far from completely playable...I'll start with the positives: The graphics and Necromunda immersion, maps, weapons etc etc are all on point.  I spend so much time just messing around with my gangs in crew management.  The skill system, general gang creation, customisation and personal touches are honestly amazing.  When the game-play does not bug out the combat and non-combat in match mechanics are excellent and in-line with the tabletop game.  It's so damn close to being a top tier gameworkshop inspired game....Finally the reasons why I cannot thumbs up....Ok here goes... The AI is only describable using foul language and expletives.  I personally have not experienced excessive game crashes however they do occur.  The crashes also have a tendency to bug other things within the game.  Case in point a previous match a deadeye of mine was injured and I had no stims left to get him up.  Unbelievably I actually had a good injury roll and he lost an eye only to get my second ever bionic upgrade giving him increased ranged states (oh hell yeah..) the next match my game crashed and what do ya know... it somehow healed his permanent bionic and his real eye is back.  Explain that one.  The only other bionic I got was also on a deadeye who lost an arm and now has increased melee stats with his bionic arm (yipee...) and he has retained that amazing improvement.  So on bionics... honestly - once a body area has a permanent injury like stupid stomach bugs that somehow you can't get some damn anti-biotics for permanently ruining the AP cost of everything on that character you've heavily invested in and became attached too.... rant over.. you should be able to opt for bionic replacements.  The only way you can get them is permanent loss of said area which only happens in death/downed end of matches risking everything.  Tier 6 chest pieces are like hens teeth.   The AI is stupid almost selectively.  The AI makes me angry.  The AI sucks.  Ok so there are times the AI even in a 4 way winner takes all... just B lines it for you.   They ignore the other gangs and focus kill your dudes.  Interestingly enough when they actually do fire at other AI opponents they almost always graze/evade or do minor damage.  But wait a second... when they shoot or hit my dudes with maxed out stats and gear they always do max damage or critical's then loot my stuff and run away with seemingly infinite action and movement points.  The amount of times I've been watching an enemy turn and just put my hands up in the air and said a lot of expletive remarks for an excessive amount of time is silly.  Personally I don't mind DLC pay barriers for new teams but when its released so close to launch while the game is in a barely playable bugged out state then you know too many people involved in the games creation couldn't have cared less amount the longevity of the game.  They rely on diehard fans of gamesworkshop IP like myself to just play anyway.  Judging player activity in this game on the "players currently in the hive" stats would say to me - you failed - you failed miserably and should hang your heads in shame.  There were clearly some people involved in this game that cared, honestly I believe they cared a lot and it is a shame others ruined their game.  To the people who did their best with this game - you were so close - the game is so close to being amazing...  but once a bad taste is left in a persons mouth the odds of them trying the improved version is little to none.  If you ever give a .... and want to put a little more effort in - a campaign based version of this game in a deathwatch format would have soooooooo much potential.  Just don't Necromunda it...

_childDocuments_.review: Would I recommend Necromunda? Not in it's current state.There's nothing wrong with the game, but really there's nothing outstanding about it either. Lets ignore the clunky UI and AI, lets get over the sometimes glitchy graphics... lets actually look at the gameplay.When you look at the concept Necromunda should be good, the foundations of the game are solid and the replayability is there. But the devs missed a key aspect of game design, the gangs are essentially all the same. The only really difference is how they look, besides that they play pretty much exactly the same... and that really detracts from the experience.My other gripe is the lack of strategic depth, tactical gameplay exists, but the overarching strategy level is missing. Basically you load up your highest level toons with your highest level gear and set them loose upon the map. Give us a point limit for our squad and actually make us think about how to best use those points, do we run 3 high level well equipped mercs, or do we run 10 low level expendable guys with basic gear? The other thing they need to do is make the gangs different, Van Saar are meant to be technological advanced... they're not. As I said earlier there is no real difference between the three gangs and there should be.If the dev does that then this game will be great.At the moment it's rather meh, good for a blat... but not worth full price.

_childDocuments_.review: So... stay with me here, I like this game. I really do. But it just has too many flaws and unbalanced elements as well as some notable missing things:-The Good:-Gorgeous graphics, environments that are vertical and close quarters, 'balanced' gangs (they are all the same!), great sound work, ok character progression, single player story is nice if a bit long winded as a long tutorial, Operations (the random single player non story part) is great if not so random sometimes.The Bad:Crashes (too many different crashes), bad AI (gets stuck sometimes still, takes forever on its turn, sits in a corner and does nothing), bad movement system (does NOT take the verticality into account, can you say infinite movement so long as you go towards where you started via a long loop?), 'balanced' gangs (they are all the same! no variation!?!? just cosmetics and 'House traits')The Ugly:Multiplayer is non existent, there is no support for it whatsoever. Hopeful for a 'casual' league system like Blood Bowl? Nope. Game just shows you how many players are 'playing the game' - wait times are not shown as nobody plays random multiplayer. Also when you 'finally' do get a match it's not gonna be balanced gang levels wise, expect it to crash as well at some point.Classes are the same approximately for whichever gang you choose. Heavies are pretty much broken due to a consumable and 2 talents = shots for 0, your heavy can pretty much shoot down 4-5 people in a turn if you are good.Crashes, so many crashes. CTD happens too often for a game like this.Devs are 'hinting' at a new gang coming in the next patch, sadly I am guessing this will be just a few more different cosmetics for the already tired same same bunch of classes (there are loading screens with mention of Cyberhounds being used by 1 gang for instance!).

_childDocuments_.review: This a borderline positive review.  I am not objective.  I am a Games Workshop fanboy.  I enjoyed Mordheim, for all its faults.  I expected nothing more than a reskinned Mordheim.  I am writing primarily to address those people who have compared Necromunda unfavorably to Mordheim.Necromunda is directly comparable to the way Mordheim was at launch.  Indeed, some of the most obnoxious AI issues were never fixed in Mordheim.  Knowing nothing about AI programming, it's certainly easy for me to say that Rogue Factor should have figured out by now how to avoid AI characters getting stuck on procedurally generated terrain.  But they haven't, and at this point I guess they're not going to.One significant change is that the single player experience (after the bespoke Story mode) lacks the special campaign missions that marked progress in Mordheim.  Personally, I found those missions to be hit or miss in Mordheim, so I'm not bothered by their absence.  So if you're looking for a Necromunda version of Rogue Factor's take on Mordheim, this is the game for you.  If you're looking for anything other than that, you probably aren't reading this review in the first place.

_childDocuments_.review: Better movement system than Mordheim, though similar play. If you liked it, you'll probably like this. I had one crash to desktop in the three hours I played for, but did not experience any other delay-of-game stuff. Edit: Nine hours in, and still only the one crash to desktop. No stuttering or other issues to report - but there's a minor annoyance when an enemy walks through a doorway and the game tries to figure out the point of view - it can rapidly zoom in and out, but it goes away as soon as the turn ends. The complaints about the AI are deserved; I had an enemy hide in a container and throw grenades on himself for a turn or two. Also, seeing all the enemy movement is not a particularly great game choice - it really takes the nerves out of it to know exactly where the enemy is at all times. I would have preferred they stayed closer to Mordheim in that regard, actually. Campaign play is fun so far, and I don't regret going over my refund window of time played.Edit: nine hours in - the campaign is good, haven't beaten it yet but the turns are pretty slow, especially in the 5v5v5 missions. The voice acting is pretty solid, especially for a GW licence. The level design has been really interesting too - not too cluttered that you /have/ to get to melee, but not so wide open that range dominates at all times. I find myself taking a bunch of screenshots that I may use for inspiration for making terrain for the tabletop version. (If I ever get off my arse about it). I'm really rather enjoying the experience, but I also find that 9 hours in two days makes for a little bit of burnout on it ;) I'm going to take a break for a while I think. 7/10 if you only kind of like games like this, 9/10 if you're a big fan of the setting.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who loves Mordheim I enjoy the game quite a lot, but there is considerable caveat caused by some flaws the release version has. The most annoying and primary issues to me are mostly technical problems and design choices. I will exclusively focus on these most pressing issues, but know that I like the game none the less.=Current issues=-The AI is mediocre at its best, and crazy/suicidal/illogical at its worst.-I've witnessed AI units countless times running unecessary loops using the maps verticality, just to end the turn very close to the location it started its turn. I've witnessed the AI several times throwing grenades straight into friendlies or a wall, even though no enemy unit is located anywhere near the area or direction. The AI pathfinding gets frequently stuck on flavor objects that hamper movement or edges/ledges that the AI can not interpret. Luckily I never experienced a softlock or something as sincere as that, but once the pathfinding is completely glitched you are forced to watch that unit trying to get out of the mess, which usually takes roughly a minute before it gives up or manages to do so. While not gamebreaking, it can ruin the challenge, the immersion and waste your time considerably. Improving the AI needs to be a priority.-Technical crashes and glitches.-In my 16 hour playing the game I had it crash 2 times on me. The frequent autosaves prevented that being more than an annoyance. Additionally there are some infrequent visual glitches, which don't affect gameplay.-The unit variety feels lackluster (especially compared to Mordheim).-Of course this comparison is unfair since Mordheim, including its dlc and free updates, features especially good unit variety. But imo the three factions are not differentiated enough gameplay wise. I can't comment on the Tabletop since I never played it.-The campaign is suffering from the missing warband management.-To me this is a weird design flaw. It is relatable why this descision was probably a lot easier to implement, but customizing, "build"ing and equipping your warband is probably one of the most valued feature of this genre. So far I enjoy the campaign, but for me this devalues it and I have no clue if I will ever finish it. The story is interesting, the cutscenes are nice, but I still prefer the "real" gamemode with warband management and actual progress and consequences.-Turning the camera while you are forced to watch the AI take its turn.To me this is just a missing quality of life feature. I don't mind watching all turns and I don't mind knowing where every unit is located. But I would appreciate it if there was a moderate speedup option AND the camera perspective could be controlled, since this would actually help you plan your moves while waiting.=Conclusion=Especially for the modest price this is was an easy purchase for me, but you should be ok with putting up with the things I pointed out. The developers improved the game a lot compared to the predecessor Mordheim. We have actual coop skirmishes, the presentation is great, the visuals almost stunning for this genre. They did a great job with most of it, but some of the existing issues can subjectively be severe. They are for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Necromunda is a really good game with the looks and gameplay style of X-com but with a far more in depth tactical combat system than X-com. Most of the negative reviews you see are written by players who have been too eager to create a gang and jump into the game. Instead of taking the developers advice and playing the story mode tutorial first to actually learn the combat system.I say this because after a player finishes mission 05 of the tutorial you receive the achievement "On the Hunt" simply for completing the mission. Now i was stunned to see only 10.2% of players have the achievement, so that tells me almost 90% of players most likely have never even tried the tutorial missions of the story mode. And therefore they do not fully understand the combat system or how to play the game properly.People are writing the AI runs past me ,goes up the stairs to the ledge above me ,then jumps off and lands near me ,runs past me again up to the ledge above me and kneels. Oh the AI is broken or stupid they say! Well i disagree with that assumption, it sounds to me like the AI is first gaining the high ground so it can jump down and trigger the "Death from above ability" then it is running back up to the high ground to gain a combat bonus, it most likely activates overwatch so it can attack you on your move turn,before it kneels and has no points left to use. If players learnt the game they would understand situations like this, and not mistake them for faults in the game.I have never done any tabletop wargaming but i am a big fan of this now. If you decide to try it ,learn it first and you may be a big fan too.

_childDocuments_.review: Played the game on release and jumped back after a break to have a bit of fun. Game decided to comically crash, but the few hours I got out again were fine. Sadly seemingly no major changes to the game, even considering the early feedback they got. To the review, to start with a lot of people feel the game is lacking in mechanics and AI. This game seems to mostly run the same level as mordheim. Of course improvements should be expected, but I don't take it that seriously. The AI has always been a bit goofy, but being a bit overpowered ain't always that bad.Game looks the part and units are nice. Gangers are a bit dead, no characteristic animations outside moving. All and all aesthetics are above par.Operations game mode is fun, much like the mordheim single player. When it comes to the mechanics only oddity is that you have a hard time spending your credits which are big motivation for me, making looting a bit pointless outside just looting the best weapons to actually equip. Feel bad to say this, because obviously some effort was put into and they were trying something new out, but the campaign is a disaster. They seemed to have forgot what makes mordheim great. You with your customized warband playing against other warbands. The campaign had you play with 3 different gangs, I couldn't care less for the predefined members, the enemies came in infinite waves and there barely was anything interesting the game phase. I slogged through the campaign essentially only for the cinematic intros and the decent story scenario. As a whole I feel confident saying that I actually spoiled the game for me by playing the campaign. I felt already burnt out after playing it. Should've just jumped into the operations and watch the cinematics on youtube.Game is buggy, ain't much more to it.Pretty much exactly as I said in my mordheim review, I feel like this game is overpriced considering the actual standard of gameplay. _childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy this game so far, but it does have a lot of issues and there are a lot of things that I think could be better. That's basically the tl;dr of the this review, so while I recommend the game, its probably best to wait until a few patches come out.Also, I've yet to play the story mode outside of the first mission, so I can't really review that. Which also means that there may be stuff about the game I don't know about yet. I also haven't done the multiplayer and can't give any insight into how good it is. The Bad:I figure its best to just start here really. There's a lot that needs to be said.1. The AI. Its pretty bad right now. Enemies will just walk against walls or other obstacles for about 5 seconds before turning around and just going a completely different way. I've seen the AI throw a grenade on itself. And I've seen it completely ignore my units even when it could have probably killed them easily and still gotten away. The AI just seems to be a big issue for right now.2. The Stats. I kinda hate how the stats work in this game. They don't really contribute anything to increasing your damage, outside of increasing penetration. I can understand guns not getting more damage for being better at shooting, but melee weapons should deal more damage the more strength you have. Melee prowess is fine, no reason to really change it, but add a melee damage modifier to strength. Also, add a health increase to toughness would be nice too. So far, I don't really know how to increase my unit's health at all, outside of the passive skill Vanguard which increases max HP by 25 but decreases action points by 10. I think adding a health increase to toughness would be nice, but maybe also just increase health by like 2 points when you upgrade any of your stats and then increase it by like 6 for each point in toughness. That's just a thought on how to do it.3. The Factions. All of the factions' house perks just seem pretty underwhelming. If the house perks were a little better or if the factions had like 2 special career paths for your units, the factions would feel a lot better. Also, only having 3 factions feels really low. Even just one more faction could help a little bit. Another idea is that each faction could specialize in a certain career so that their units in the career have a slightly better bonus. Its just another idea on how to help improve it.4. Unsafe Zones. The little metal bridges or the areas right in front of the zip lines are unsafe zones that your units automatically get moved out of if you end their turn in them. I think it would be far better to let people stop in those zones. If someone comes across the zip line and someone is in the way of the destination, make it so that the person in the way gets knocked back and lands on their back and have to spend action points to get up. If someone ends their turn on a bridge and the bridge gets destroyed, let them fall down and take damage. If it makes them fall off the map, you could either make it so they get put back onto the platform that they had been on, or just make it and instant KO. Either one would be fine by me.5. Bugs. Overall, I actually haven't encountered too many bugs. Except for one where my game has crashed about 3 or 4 times. Its a little annoying, but the game saves after each turn so it doesn't cause too much of an issue. Its just an annoyance.I think that about wraps it up for my big issues with the game.The Middle Ground:This is just stuff that isn't necessarily bad, its just not great.1. Unit Customization. It is nice to have some customization, but the customization is far from the best customization I've ever seen. There's enough there to work with, but you won't really get any impressive looking units out of it. I do like that the units' body changes based on which physical trait you choose. That's pretty cool.2. The Careers. Overall, they hit the basic types of careers you could want. Most of them don't feel particularly special, aside from maybe the lay-mechanic who have a servo arm that can have a drill or power saw and can build barricades and health dispensers. I don't know much about the lore around Necromunda(or Warhammer in general), but I'm sure there's more that can be done with this lore than what has been done so far.The Good:1. Personality Traits. These consist of a virtue, vice, and talent that can be discovered upon leveling up once your unit has reached level 5. While discovering a vice for your character could be a bit of an issue in how you use that character, I like how it helps give each character just a little bit more of their own identity.2. The Combat. Now, I'm mostly comparing the combat in this game to the combat in Mordheim. Overall, I feel like this is a decent improvement from Mordheim's combat and I'm happy with it. Movement points have changed in this game from how they were in Mordheim. You generally have 60 points of movement that you can use to move around. Similar to how Mordheim worked, the area you can move in is still a circle, but its a giant circle now rather than a collection of small circles. I also like the change to action points. My two-handed axe wielders can actually attack twice already, as long as I have some action points saved up or I entrench them. Also, this game does a better job of taking line of sight into account compared to Mordheim. The new action points system just feels like it really allows your units to do more on their turn than just swing once and be done.3. Unit Experience. I just really enjoy how it works now. Your unit gains XP and you use that XP to buy stats and skills for your unit. After having purchased so many stats and skills, your unit ranks up. I just think its a cool way of doing it. Very happy with this system.4. Operations. I like this mechanic as well. Basically, you choose a sector and you have a certain amount of missions you can do before your time in that sector ends. You want to try and collect as many resources as you can in that sector before you have to move on to the next one. There are 3 tiers of rewards you can get based on how many resources you collect. The third tier gives 4 chests with random items and money. Just to be clear, the chests aren't able to be bought with real money, just the in game currency.5. Infamy/Facilities. The facilities give you a passive buff for the duration of the operation. Something like giving your units extra XP after fighting or giving you pieces of armor after each mission. The infamy system gives you points over the duration of the operation that you can then use to give yourself a bonus on the next operation, like decreased cost of items or a new unit or pieces of armor. There's a lot of stuff it can give you.6. Injuries. I just really love this mechanic. I love it in Mordheim, I love it in Battle Brothers, and I love it here too. I like the idea that you units aren't dead just because they fall in battle. They can end up having received an injury that gives them a debuff. You still have the character, they are just a little worse off now than they were. I haven't had too many different injuries yet, but I'm hoping that the types of injuries have increased and that the injuries can open up new possibilities for characters.Overall, I do recommend the game. It can be a little rough around the edges, and there are some things that need to be fixed, but those don't ruin the game. I still really enjoy the game and believe its a good game, but I also know it can be better with some changes, which is the entire reason I'm even writing a review. I like the game and I want to see it get better.

_childDocuments_.review: So this is a bit of a tough one to review. For starters the Environments and the feel of the world is really good. The character customisation and gang customisation is good too. Though the different gangs use the same kind of clothing and customisation there isnt really all too much difference visually between them. Thats one of the things i think could be fixed. Different gangs that really are different both with how they play and how they look isnt a thing here right now. As of now they all have that samey cant tell the difference feel to them. Once you have customised and created your gang with their skills and stats. You will find that the Gameplay is a little slow sometimes but still interesting. It keeps you engaged but again that has some issues too. The AI is as dumb as a bag of bricks. I am constantly sitting here cringing at the choices made by the AI. They are not at all threatening or pose a challenge to you no matter the difficulty. They will get stuck on objects and run for a while until they realise they are stuck and give up and go into over watch mode. They grenade themselves to death...They make you feel like you are playing against a 4 year old quite commonly. Id like to say this isnt often but it is..Though the devs have said they are working on this. The other issue is watching every AI take their move. again this wouldnt be an issue for me if they actually could make good choices but again i am forced into internal yelling at the ai as to what they hell they are doing.  The ability to speed this up would be great. The levels are always interesting and well layed out. I have had plenty of fun moments setting up traps and watching as a plan goes really well. Again if i could give this a neutral score i would but id say it just passes as a thumbs up for me. If the issues are fixed then this would be a for sure thumbs up. Maybe buy it if you want to support it or just wait if you are unsure. Atleast until the issues are fixed as some of these issues can really ruin the fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Compared to Mordheim that plays a bit similarly in terms of movements, usage of skill, mechanics and interactions between characters, Necromunda does a few things differently, one thing is apparent and fairly obvious, verticality and range, the maps are a lot bigger and not just in size, making use of height advantage is a big factor that comes into play and given the nature of the game itself, with this game shifting from a melee oriented to a range oriented formula, having the bigger guns with the longest range will generally be a smart idea. What also changed is now the story elements are sparated from the main course of the game, now we have a campaign, with cutscenes, which are absolutely great. Game modes are for the most part the same and plays a lot the same as Mordheim, other than the campaign, you make your own gang, chosen from 3 different houses, customize it, lead it into either single player operations or multiplayer skirmishes and based how you do in those, your gangers will net experience that'll make them stronger, raise stats, buy perks and skill, insert implants for more aimed quirks, suffer injuries both permanent and non-permanent if they fall in combat, loot treasure in the field and extract with it so you can sell it in the market in exchange for credits, useful for new and better gear, it's a very customizable experience that leaves you the freedom to play this game however you want. My only complaints are that the AI, at times, may take stupid decisions such as sit in a corner safe from harm and just spam overwatch while their respective team is getting slaugthered, or, abandon what they were doing so they could pile-on a vulnerable and dying adversary, moving from one corner of the map to the other and potentially suffering from multiple overwatch shots because of it, its very inconsistent.Another complaint is the number of houses present at the moment, only 3, but this can easily change if the game does well in terms of sales, which i hope because i like it a lot. All in all, for the price it's well worth it and it can only get better with time.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: The devs have now released a series of tip trailers for a game that exists only in their minds. There has been no patch. There has been no act of good faith in even addressing the issues beyond a compilation of them. No one should support this kind of business practice. It's simply not worth it. Perhaps, one day, the game will be playable -- but there are core gameplay decisions that will likely never be addressed if they are this willfully ignorant to the truly abysmal state of the game. It is, at best, a time waster in singer player and at its worst unplayable in multiplayer. As my original review shows -- I was in high spirits and had hope but this is the worst kind of management on display and should come with some kind of consequence for those responsible for it.In good conscience -- I can't call this unsalvageable. Perhaps I've simply been in the UnderBustle for too long already. Still, it is, indeed, a representation of the Warhammer tabletop experience. You gather your crew. I like to make mine unique by making them all women. Since that's what makes them interesting, it's the ways in which they're all ubiquitous with one another that highlights their ability to carry a gatling gun in sensible wedges. It's very hip, you just likely wouldn't understand the references -- given your upbringing. Look, you'll get it just watch out for traps, okay?Then you make sure that they are looking just -- gorge. You let the paint dry and possibly realize it's long since time to open a window or two. Then you go to your local game/hobby/tiny space-cult battledome campaign simulator longhouse and sit in an empty room while you move the figurines around a elaborate 3D map your mom crafted from things she had left over from scrapbook class. Don't worry, your Elite Halfway House 4 Wayward Industrial Ne'er-Do-Wells get chased by the manager's Gang that he set up on hotwheels and programmed to stunt on ya for an hour and a half until closing time.You laugh now, but once Kryla-T600 Death from Above's you into another dimension twice, you realize that it's not magic -- but where else? Where else could you get this experience? Even X-Commie: Alien Hater 2 only let you dress them up funny, but never really took it to outerspace. You could crawl inside the Snake Queen's body, buy you couldn't play the campaign AS the Snake Queen! It's not Mordheim, but it is a small unit tactics experience from the Warhammer lich masters. Because that was also a deeply flawed, poorly tended & ultimately still somehow the best option contender in its magical wonderbox of the small-unit tactical murder-o-rama and Polly Pocket genre at the time. This lacks much of the charm, story and ultimately diversity (class differences don't make up for fielding an iconic House/Faction/Archetypical Thingamadoodle to scramble up nearby walls while your dim-witted, but hot bodied, Leader gets pummeled to death by rat goblins. I think that's a shame, others may not.) It does make up for it with promoting a heavier use, or at least opportunity for, skills and that's fun.You win some, you lose some. I don't regret giving them the money. Even if they just ran Mordheim: Mord Simulator through this graphics engine and called it a day, I'm glad that they're still trying to make whatever this is into something that is playable. Since this is, when compared to the starter kit and my empty padded cell anyway. There are definitely circumstances by which I think it could be something that the same people who regularly turn dice and plastic into hellscapes of enjoyment for the whole family will manage to arrange for themselves eventually.The only real advice for what to do with -- whatever this currently is would be ... maybe stop trying to appeal to the Mass Market with Slaanesh & Papa Nurgle. I don't think it's going to be everyone's thing and when you try to reskin a cat that's been anointed as sacrifice to the personification of humanity's collective resentment -- like, it just kind of going to come off as inauthentic, ya know? Silly shooting games don't make up for it, sorry Dad-Mom Hellbeast, it's not a phase and I'm not just going to get over it. Mordheim was a trundling mess, but it was full of life. This is a slightly more polished mess, but is a little soulless in the bad way. As a tech demo, it's cool.Like goat simulator, but you sacrifice it into the void at the end and I can't say I regretted my time. Then, I waste that on all sorts of poorly thought out dumpster fires. No one called me a newb or a dweeb and none of my figurines got Mountain Dew spilled on them. The future is now! Your experience of the Necromunda: SpanxHive Hardcore Space-Ganger Team Dressup Sim-Opticon may, of course, differ. Just don't throw the baby out with the bathwater. Just the baby please, the water's fine -- jump on in!

_childDocuments_.review: The Issues as I see them...Munda has a lot of potential but most of it is potential that is wasted in its current state. Let me start with the positive. I like the look of the game and the Gangs. I like the ability to do do Co-op and PvP. I like some of the attention to detail. I like the 40k universe as so this tickles my fancy quite a lot. All of those things turn a lack luster pain in the butt of a game into something that I still like playing even though it is nearly as frustrating as it is fun while hoping sincerely that the game gets some heavy overhauls.Now to the bad stuff. I have a reasonably nice gaming laptop; not top of the line but better than average and its struggles to  keep up with the visuals as soon as auras and environmental graphics like sparks and ash become persistant on the screen. This feel like its most likely due to some poor coding than an hardware issue but that is admittedly not my wheelhouse and I am just guessing based on personal experience. That said what is there I like a lot.... Id just like it a lot more if I didn't have to play the game at its lowest graphics setting to stop it from lagging out even during single player.The game difficulty feels like it was designed for a preteen/teen demographic. It is far too easy with rudimentary at best strategy involved. All the tools are there in one form or another to make the game either challenging, like the table top game, or both but they all feel dumbed down to attracts children with a 15 second attention span.The story mode is a long drawn out and nearly useless tutorial since many aspects of the game are not even explained, and you never really get used to any build because they are changed from chapter to chapter. A better idea would have been to build your own gang and run through each of the three versions of the story arc dependent on which gang you built. That said the cut scenes are great (minus some truly horrific voice acting choices).There is FAR FAR FAR too much capacity for movement and action in the game. Tactics become almost pointless because most fighters can almost endlessly traverse vertical distances and can cross most of the map in a single turn. In the correct circumstances I have traversed bottom to top the entire map and gone 180 degrees around the outside of the map using only my normal move, my hook, and some jumps. To make things worse you can intersperse all that movement with far more actions that is reasonable. There really should be a single bar of "actions pool" that counts toward movement and actions both which forces players to decide between more movement or more actions. This is truly one of the most disappointing aspects of the game and its correction would lend toward a pretty simple and vast improvement. My buddies and I found that putting a 60 second turn timer on our PvP and Co-Op games forced a bit of speed and was a bandaid correction for this problem.The Camera positioning during animated scenes like attacks and actions often leaves you either staring at a wall close up and missing the action OR doing its best to give you a seizure by flickering at a rapid rate.Object location is an issue particularly with the Gangers. Try to activate an elevator going down with a toe still on the level and you will see the elevator descend with you hanging in the air while you little toe presumably supports your body weight. Or allows you to walk off of a platform into mid air because there is a crouched bad guy below you but then forces you to be stuck there. On a similar note if you kneel (which is often what I do when Im at the end of my movement) and attempt to end your turn but are in a Danger Zone (basically on or in the path of terrain that can be altered) you are forced to move off of it in a computer defined manner after a warning and often into a senseless location (like under a bridge rather that to one end or another). However the warning comes too late for you to not get screwed out of the points you just spent to kneel. No I understand that at a certain level big boy rules should apply but seriously either allow us to cause harm to players who end up on dangerous terrain OR give us a better warning indication so we aren't wasting actions. Preferably let us harm characters that are silly enough to put themselves at risk.The game makes you go though a senseless amount of turn burning when there is no enemy left on the field. On a similar note the game play is aggravatingly slow due to silly messages that essentially tell you the obvious but spend forever tell it to you and making you watch the enemy do their actions in what seems like slow motion. There is just a lot of time wasted.The game has repeatedly crashed on it's own during multiplayer and in single player. The AI is hopelessly stupid. I was going to list the ways in which the AI is just abjectly useless but it would be easier to point out the positive things about the AI and that is really just to say...... They on a rare occasion take an action that almost seems like a sane and rational human being would have considered making it. I'm currently writing this as I sit here for going on 30 minutes while an AI character stares at a wall and am hoping (foolishly) that it snaps out of it and I can complete this important mission without having to forfeit or crash the game intentionallyMany of the abilities and smaller screen icons are never really explained in any way leaving us to guess at what they meant though trial and error.It would be nice if captured weapons retained their original appearance if they came from an opposing House. It would add variety and make for a fluffy and fun trophy appearance.

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game as a table top game when I was younger.  It was great then.  This is an interesting take on the same game.  The worst part about the game is the AI doing some strange things as well as the story missions being a plain pass because it takes away what makes the game great, the gang members and making them into individuals.  Over all I like this game.  It is strategic, I play single player, and have found it to be a tad easy but fun.  They are updating it and have improved it already, so that is a bonus.  You can outsmart the AI in a battle of attrition and have them do a lot of dirty work for you, but that is part of the joy of it all.  The Operations are what make it fun for me and seeing how I can come out of one with more resources than the other gangs is fun.  The sense of height in the maps really is meaningful as well, if you have the high ground you tend to win more than not.  I have to say if you are a tactical fan and loved Mordheim you should pick this up and give it a go.  Great Game and helps bring back that feeling of leading my game in Necromunda back in the day.

_childDocuments_.review: So I've seen a few other people speaking to most of the problems I see with this game. It feels like a huge step backwards from Mordheim. Every improvement they have made comes with serious drawbacks around this.-Loading times have been cut down, in return the game "revamps" the initiative system, and intersperses each turn with (and I have counted) 4 completely unneeded 3 second pauses, as well as a higher than 50% chance of between 30-120 seconds of following the AI walking into walls and throwing grenades at themselves before you get to take a turn.-the much better map comes with no fog of war, cutting down on the amount of tension in the gameplay as you always know exactly where every enemy character is.-The story is completely separated from your custom gang, instead of building up your team, learning how to use each type of character in your gang and developing their abilities you get handed a squad with not real indications of what each of them actually do unless you navigate something like 6 different menus during the mission for each character, then after a few missions they hand you a completely new group of people so you have to figure it out all over again. -Nothing really differentiates your characters besides what weapons you choose to give them, at least when you are starting out. all the "big" variety in builds comes down to small mechanical things that the colour of your clothes gives you, and they seem pretty low impact.At the end of all this though this game has so much potential to be great that it makes it all the more frustrating. I really really hope that I can come back to this after 6 months and see a game worth playing.

_childDocuments_.review: Five hours played and starting to appreciate the tactical aspects of this game. The turn system is unique, both/all sides select their character, Then you get to see the opposition choice...and what order of activation based on Initiative number.  Do I activate a high initiative character early, or save that for later in the turn ?..With up to four players in a battle, getting this stage of selection right  can give a critical tactical advantage.Maps are another aspect of the battle that need to be factored in, there is a very nice Map view that lays everything out simple and clear, and holding the CTRL key highlights gang members and other important features clearly. Presentation and personalisation has been created by a team who understand what Warhammer gamers love, personalising their figures. There is a comprehensive Gang creation system that allows almost limitless customising of each gang member. I have played for five hours and barely scratched the surface, personally I have not encountered game bugs..though I am aware of them through the feedback section. Overall I am more than happy with my game, of course there are those who disagree.....but that is what Necromunda Underhive was created for, settling Disagreements.

_childDocuments_.review: This may sound like a negative review but, all in all, it is what you expect from a first release these days. It is buggy. It crashes unexpectedly. Some things don't work correctly and some descriptions contain the programming code rather than the description. All in all not a bad successor to Mordheim. These days most releases are buggy with a zillion patches to come. Also I would expect many DLC's, with the usual Games Workshop price tag, as the board game had 8 clans and this version has 3. Having said that, if you enjoy turn based strategy with good list design depth this would be a game for you. If you missed the sale then I would not buy it straight away. Play Mordheim some more, unless you don't mind debugging this game for them for free. It should be a good game in about 6 months and I will try to update this review then.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really enjoying this game so far. If you are a fan of Turn Based Tactics games, you might find something you like here. It looks great and is very atmospheric. At first I had a few teething problems. For example, found the camera quite janky, but changing graphics settings (to medium/60fps) sorted it out. I also found switching to controller made for a better experience overall. I've played 11 of the tutorial story  missions so far, as well as about 10 missions with own gang. I couldn't complete story mission 11 due to a bug (Vex couldnt put down the toxin container , so couldn't enter the vent) which was annoying, and I'll have to replay.  So far, I much prefer the missions with my own gang, and enjoy the progression. Some of the skills are very very satisfying to use. As other have stated, the cons are the AI, which can be hit and miss, and the long turn times due to the camera following the AI throughout their turn. However, I found I got used to this after a while, and it's only annoying when the AI wastes it's turn (which it does from time to time). Finally, there are some issues with pvp - in my second match we found a bug that caused both players games to crash to desktop. So far 6 out of 7 pvp games have crashed. So if you are interested in pvp, wait to see if it is fixed. If you are on the fence about this game, check out some of the gameplay videos on Youtube (AirsickHydra or GamekNight). However, if you have a low tolerance for buggy games, it might be best to wait for some patches.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR (quite long) - Wait until on sale, wait until patched, Wait.I understand I am in the minority of positive reviews, but hear me out.I'm gonna break this down through the different modes of play, and end with thoughts. If you actually read this, thank you.General Issues:Expect the occasional Crash To Desktop. Expect the AI to be poor. Expect items and abilities to have {Damage_Value%} placeholder tags. Even when just playing a match, expect things to be Laboriously Slow as every ganger has a "Turn Start" and "Turn End" screen that you can't tab past. Expect a whole lot of Bugginess. Expect, above all else, to be Confused All The Time.Now, on to how this game works.Campaign:The campaign is a mission-by-mission storyline that follows three different gangs as they race for archeotech. The voice-acting is middle-ground, the music is average grungy sci-fi and the the storyline is  blase, but we're here to watch gangers kill each other over perceived sleights and need for resources. This aspect gets a pass.Gameplay wise, though, it's a tutorial. The whole 15 something missions, just one big tutorial, teaching you about different game modes and class abilities, items and weapons, interactables and the like. But... It doesn't actually teach you how any of those matter, outside of the campaign. You don't keep the items you pick up from one level of the campaign to the next. You don't get to decide what skills your gangers get, or what your crew is made up of. It's a mechanical tutorial, and after about 6-7 missions you're pretty much able to just drop it and go play Gang Mode, unless you're truly invested in the storyline. (you won't be.)Gang Mode:The game will suggest you finish campaign mode, but trust me, it will not brief you on the things you need to know; like what character statistics are, how you choose different abilities and passives for a gang member, how to SHOP, and how you manage everything. You're thrown to the wolves out the gate with Gang Mode.Mechanically, Gang Mode is the meat of what Necromunda is. You make a gang, and through dozens of matches try to make them rich and infamous. You're given complete control over how your gangers are leveled up, spending earned experience on upgrading statistics that effect the ability of a fighter or on actions or passive buffs that WIDELY change how your ganger is going to work inside the game; You also spend currency an time managing what equipment your gang hoards and wields. None of these are taught to you, and understanding them differentiate a gang that'll durdle in a match or a min-max'd crit build on a heavy with an stubgun that drops two gangers turn one.There are currently two ways to play Gang Mode: Skirmish, and Operations.Skirmishes, right now, will be pretty much against AI only. The queues are empty, but you can always set up a custom match against AI, or if you have one online, a friend. Custom Matches with friends would be, imo, the sole way you will want to play this game.Operations, as far as I can tell, are vs AI exclusively. You're given some extra loot, the ability to use your gang's infamy to acquire more, specific loot, or cheapen the prices of leveling up your characters, and as long as you preform well and complete some side-quest style missions you can walk away wealthy. The fact the AI will spend a lot of your games running into crates and path-finding poorly means this is the place to Grind.Now, for why I'm giving this game a recommendation.I grew up playing first edition necromunda with friends. We still fall back on stories and characters that we built together as our gangs clashed on the tabletop (or countertop, or floorspace). The fun of Necromunda is in the emergent narrative- in making something living and the shared experience of characters rise, fall, and recuperation. I think, honestly, that Underhive Wars could be that. I've had a BLAST playing gang mode and building a gang. Watching characters grow, seeing how they take on traits that change how they'll fight, and even feeling outright outraged when one of my gang members died. I actually tunnel-visioned an AI character for the purpose of enacting a revenge for a passed on ganger. In this game is a glimpse of what Necromunda is.You will need friends, people who will slog through the Much Less Than Acceptable bugs of this game, to find it. You'll need dedication to finding a story together and a whole lot of patience. But I love what this game reminds me of, and I love that right now (written in a US State that is still enforcing shelter-in-place measures) I can play a game of necromunda, with my friends, if I want to.So what do I suggest?I think with a lot (and I mean a LOT) of love from the devs, with patches and quality of life updates and serious focus, this game could become something really memorable. Personally, I think the game -looks- good. It's atmospheric, the environments are grungy and fit 40k, and character models can actually end up looking pretty damn impressive once they have some gear on 'em.But if you a. don't have a group of friends willing to slug it out in a game with bugs, b. don't want to spend more than an hour to play a match where you take 3 turns, or c. Just aren't willing to play games that aren't up to polish, do NOT get this game right away.Get this game when it's been fixed, or is on sale.I want people to get this game; I cannot tell you to get this game NOW.

_childDocuments_.review: This game didn't get the support from fans that it deserved. Now that Chaos Gate: Daemonhunters has been released you can go back and see how this one succeeded and failed.I think the Story not being tied into the Gang Campaign either split work or otherwise hurt the initial launch. Perhaps instead of a linear narrative story mode the writer could have written "scenarios" where you have occurrences and events interwoven into the gang management campaign, something like Wildermyth has, which subjects your gang members to vignettes and events that could randomly change things up. The pathfinding at launch was pretty bad, and while it has improved drastically, there are still some issues with NPCs trying to navigate sharp turns and makeshift (destructible) terrain and bridges. Sometimes you glitch out if you hump on objects too much. It's much improved and functional given the amount of verticality in this game (zip lines, grappling hooks, fast rope, etc.) I know people would like squads to be bigger, but the 4 Gangers per deployment have a lot of progression and customization and can pull off crazy turns. It's not like Mordheim where you have a lot of cannon fodder that get one attack and pass. I would have loved more support for this, like the oddball gangs of Scavvies and Ratskins, or Hired Guns to change things up like Mordheim, but I'll be coming back to this after the "newness" of CG:D wears off   :)

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking to scratch a 40k/ gritty sci-fi itch, Underhive Wars does this reasonably well. The game looks nice and the aesthetics of your gang make it much more enjoyable. Though, only 3 factions being available leads to some disappointment if you dont like Roidy Beef Boys, Coomerbait, or Biker-Looking-Dudes. I haven't gotten too far in the story, but the ball really feels dropped in the voiceover department; despite everyone wearing masks and rebreathers, they sound way too crisp and bland; the voices should have been put through a filter.If you're looking for a challenging and deep squad based tactical skirmish game, you probably won't be too enthralled. The AI still has the same problems that come with the free movement system and probably wouldnt be as bad if it was just made gridbased. It's very easy to create broken characters once you start getting experience. In the beginning it will seem like a slog where everything takes 3 characters turns to take down, but with a couple skills you can easily burst 1 or more enemies with a single character's turn. There's even a melee passive for leaders that makes it impossible for enemies to engage you with melee unless they are prebuffed to reduce AP costs. Once you get a hang of the mechanics, You can easily beat gangs of 1k score higher than you.So far loot is the same weapons with stat bumps per level progression; I would have hoped for an actual modding system, but this still works just fine because there is no health creep on character leveling. Some weapons and abilities do seem flat out better than others. For instance, grenade abilities for saboteur do the spread weapons job better and don't restrict what's in your hands. While unpolished, I do find the game pretty fun. I feel like with enough care and content addition in the form of gangs, modes, and maps it could be much better. If this was priced at 60, I wouldn't recommend it, but I definitely enjoyed my time so far for the current price.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, so, let me first say that I almost quit and uninstalled the game within the first hour.  I'm very glad that I didn't.The setting is amazing, the character design is amazing, the story is great, except...  The quest design is so unclear it becomes very frustrating.  You'll have a 5 turn limit to do a task, only for that task's completion to give you another task.  (Example:  You have 5 turns to get supplies to a door, but once you do that, you learn that a specific character now needs to complete another task with no additional time.  That character may be no where near the objective as you haven't been planning for them to need to do that task.)  Its also unclear of what you have to do, lacking very good quest indicators.  So in short, the tutorial is terrible at teaching you the game.The pacing is slow with certain unnecessary slowdowns that just add up, (Like when there is only one character to select in a turn, why does it ask you what character you want to select?) There is also a pause before each enemy moves which is a few seconds, and the pathfinding is pretty bad with enemies trying to walk through fences and obstacles.All that said, they did such a fantastic job with the world, characters, and most impressively; the customization.  Compared to Mordheim, Necromunda has a lot more running and gunning which is a lot more fun.  (Played both)  I also have always loved the setting of Necromunda more as you can really get a taste of gangs struggling to survive vs just a bunch of adventurers trying to get rich.If you can struggle past the unclear story missions, and bad pathfinding, I think this game starts to shine.I can't wait for additional gangs, especially if my Cawdor fanatics ever show up!

_childDocuments_.review: It breaks my heart to say this because I love Mordheim but this game isn't ready for a full release. It's clunky, buggy, poorly balanced, uninviting and very disappointing. It could well develop into something as good as Mordheim, but it's going to need some work - and, even still, some of the core design choices I find strange. The lack of movement pips, like Mordheim had, removes all nuance from a well executed turn - instead, you basically have a big circle that you can move anywhere within. This, coupled with the fact that everyone seems to have vast amounts of MP, means that a unit can literally assault a building through a window then make an attack before leaving again through the same window and returning to the original cover outside. This is utterly ridiculous. Turn-based squad combat games are all about the cunning use of combined arms, moving and covering, flanking and out-flanking. In it's current form, Necromunda is about dog-piling the weakest enemy unit in the hope your foe goes a unit down before you do. It's like the designers wanted all this gimmicky verticality and wouldn't budge on it and the actual game-play has been the price.I dunno. Maybe I'm being harsh. I've not given up on Necromunda. But the fact is even in it's rawest beta state when there were no skills, no legacy, no campaign and a gazillion bugs I genuinely loved Mordheim - it just had this certain magical something. And I don't see that here.
