_childDocuments_.review: It is exactly as expected - Necromunda brought to the screen with similar mechanics as Mordheim, but of course adapted to the newer Necromunda rules and setting.There are some minor glitches and bugs, but nothing which is not expected on a launch date.I highly recommend playing the storyline / tutorial, because it teaches you about all the skills, setups, objectives, tactical map, etc. Yes, it does not cover clan management, something tabletop players look forward to, but it has a nice fitting Necromunda storyline and teaches you at the same time. And even there are even some tricky situation where not so tactical players might want to start again ;) is there room for improvement? Yes, some part of the handling feels slow, some AI glitches, etc. But nothing which is game breaking. I look forward to play more and wish for more gangs and maybe even some more campaigns as DLC (with full clan management).Update: I have played now over 60 hourse and still can recommend the game and do so if you like these kind of games. I did not suffer from the safe game bug and had no problems with MP and I understand that they are annoying. But the game is worth the money. The above mentioned flaws and bugs like the AI or some glitches can and will be fixed, especially the pathing issues (which do not come as a suprise with such an enviroment). But even with the AI doing strange things sometimes, it often also suprises with very nice actions putting me or some other AI gang in trouble. So the potential is there. Also regarding the campaign/tutorial - I hightly recommend playing it. Yes, it can be annoying sometimes (especially mission 5), but it also teaches you a lot about tactics and strategy in this game and forces you to think a bit different than in other comparable games.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is full of flaws and bugs. The AI is horrendous. The Story Campaign is so bad it reaches the point where progression in it is harder than driving your own head through a brick wall.Endless Mode though, is fun. This is the mode where you manage a gang, and take them through multiple fights, levelling up, gaining injuries and equipment as you go. This is where the game is at it's best. Unfortunately, the AI really lets it down. Turns are incredibly slow as you have to watch the AI move each individual turn in full -- and it often runs in circles or spends 2 minutes trying to run through a wall -- you can't do anything while the AI does this, you just have to sit there and watch. Each and every time it does this, and it will do this multiple times in a mission.So, a very flawed and often frustrating game with game breaking bugs and terrible AI. This may be fixed with significant patches, and I hope it is -- because I always loved Necromunda. The environments are pretty nice and the soundtrack is dope. The actual models and customisation (at least the stuff not locked behind the frustrating Story Campaign) are sweet. There is great potential in this IP, it's just been squandered here. TLDR: If you do buy it, skip the story campaign. Don't even bother, it will just make you angry. Play endless mode and maybe read a book or something while the AI turn plays out.Edit: Came back to play again in Dec 2020, after the Van Saar DLC released. The game runs slightly better. The AI decision making is a little better, but mostly really daft. The AI still gets stuck on obstacles and sometimes tries to run through walls. The campaign feels slightly more fun to play. It's still buggy, and you'll still crash to desktop. If you're interested in the universe/lore, and you can pick it up on sale, then maybe take a look. Otherwise don't bother.

_childDocuments_.review: I've given this game a conditional thumbs up. while the game play is solid and the setting is very good whats missing is more gangs. the story mode and "campaign" is extremely good, most of the weapons feel right for the setting, I'm a massive Warhammer nerd so i know what what I'm talking about, the exceptions are plasma weapons and melta, these need to be rarer and seriously retooled to be more powerful. the turn based game play is mostly a direct copy of the table top game, the graphics are great and it is thoroughly enjoyable, but wait for more gangs, in this kind of game 3 gangs is no where near enough. Bugs: people are saying its buggy but the only bug i have experienced is a slight camera bug when the camera is following an AI player and they go close to a wall and the camera isn't sure how to handle it resulting in it twitching back and forth but that's been very rare for me. detailed_description: Special Offer Owners of Blazblue Centralfiction on Steam automatically unlock exclusive Jin and Ragna cosplay items in the Pixel Lobby for all characters. Owners of Skullgirls 2nd Encore on Steam automatically unlock exclusive cosplay items in the Pixel Lobby for all characters: Cerebella's Hat Vice Versa, Peacock's Hat, and Bomb minion George. Owners of GUILTY GEAR Xrd REV 2 on Steam automatically unlock exclusive cosplay items in the Pixel Lobby for all characters: Sol Badguy's Outfit/Hairstyle, and Ky Kiske's Outfit/Hairstyle. About the Game Them’s Fightin’ Herds is a 2D fighting game featuring a cast of adorable animals designed by acclaimed cartoon producer Lauren Faust. Beneath the cute and cuddly surface, a serious fighter awaits! Key Features Streamlined Combat - 4-button fighting mechanics, magic system, enhanced super attack, and juggle decay to prevent infinite combos. Story Mode - An episodic adventure filled with exploration, combat challenges, minigames, and boss fights! Chapter 1 (starring Arizona) is available now. Additional chapters are in development and will be released as free updates. Local Versus and Online Crossplay Matchmaking - Fight opponents offline or battle across the globe with GGPO’s powerful rollback netcode. Tutorial and Training Modes – Learn the ropes with combo trials and guided tutorials, practice combos in the data-rich training room, and view replays from your matches! Pixel Lobby - Unlock accessories, customize your avatar, and explore a top-down visual lobby with other players online. Dynamic Music System - Rockin' battle music adapts to the characters to make every match feel like a clash of champions.

_childDocuments_.review: Them's Fightin' Herds is a two player children’s game, the object of which is to pick up your treasure chest on the central island and sail back safely. Each player has a giant sailing ship as their main game piece. Each ship has a removable sail, two trigger-action side panels, and a huge spring-driven cannon. Players take turns moving forward along a prescribed track and shooting bean bags at their opponent’s ship. A hit on one of the side panels will force it to pop off and give the player a free shot at the other side; a hit forcing the sail off becalms the ship for a turn. To add to the pirate flavor, each player also has an eye patch. Wearing these will slightly affect depth perception and add a marginal bit of sport to the shooting. This game retailed for the somewhat impressive sum of $16 back in 1962. With its huge plastic ships (close to a foot long), giant vinyl play mat, and the eye patches, it may well stand as one of the more overproduced games of the early 1960s. Them's Fightin' Herds?

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of fighting games, you should give Them's Fightin' Herds a chance.Whatever its origins, it's a fun, balanced, mechanically deep 2D fighter - and if you don't believe me, just search Twitch VODs for all the pro players who woke up to this game when it got an EVO slot and suddenly love it now.Features include:* A roster where every character plays very differently, and every character has stuff that makes you go "is this allowed??", and yet no character clearly outclasses any other.* Combo system that limits combo length and damage, incentivizes on-the-fly routing, and keeps both players thinking.* Top notch training mode, including dummy playback, built-in and downloadable combo trials, hitboxes, frame data...* Unusually comprehensive tutorial that comes in 3 parts: the basics (including move explanations for all characters), an intermediate section to tackle once you've played a while, and an expert section that gets into stuff most fighting games force you to go to a Wiki to learn.* Runs on a toaster; my 2012 Thinkpad with integrated graphics gets 60fps at 1080p.* Best-in-class GGPO rollback netcode. As long as both players have a wired connection, you can play intercontinentally and still feel like you're local.* HD 60fps 2D animation straight out of Saturday morning cartoons.* A story mode that's equal parts fighting game, long-form tutorial, and RPG - a far cry from the "cutscene, fight, repeat" story modes of Guilty Gear and its ilk.* A soundtrack that adapts to gameplay - character themes get interwoven into stage music depending on who has the momentum in the match.* Works bug-free in Proton if you enable it, as far as I can tell.* Technically zero ponies, as the only equine playable character is a full-size unicorn. :)Caveats:- Story Mode only recently got its initial release, and was designed by advanced fighting gamers, so it's still got a rocky learning curve for casual folks. If you're new to fighting games, it might be best to wait for this to get smoothed out.- There are only six playable characters, and there are unlikely to ever be more than ten. I'd argue that a small roster makes for a more balanced game, but if you don't like any of the options you've got, there's not much recourse but to wait for DLC (a seventh character is confirmed, with more hopefully on the way after).- Online lobbies have voicechat; if you don't like that, you need to disable it in the menu (turn "Voice Chat Volume" to 0%).- The training mode menu is huge enough that it's kind of hard to find your way around it.- Tianhuo's voice actor mispronounces the Chinese move names. :(

_childDocuments_.review: I was enjoying this game a lot when I originally reviewed it, but the devs have failed to deliver on their ambitious promises for years and the issues that myself and many others had with the game were never addressed. As of today, they have announced that development will cease after the season pass is finished. The game was already on life support 2-3 years ago, but now it is officially dead. My thoughts from my earlier review below:1. Story mode. This is the #1 criticism you see in steam reviews because it's still only got 1 chapter out of 8 (finale + Shanty) after almost THREE YEARS of this game "releasing" out of Early Access. There's no excuse at this point. Give people what they paid for. The devs chose to prioritize Level 3 supers and, generally, the competitive scene over finishing story mode. I can sort of understand them making Shanty (who was originally a DLC character), because the other most common criticism is that the roster is small, but delivering what they sold people should take priority. At this point, I think people should be getting refunds because they were not given the game that they paid for.2. The game balance is utter trash. The devs must have an unhealthy attraction to Oleander because they refuse to nerf her in any meaningful way. She's been top tier for the game's entire lifespan and just gets privileges that other characters don't. In the most recent patch, they made it so that Pom's dogs (puppets) can't attack if Pom's in blockstun, but Oleander's puppet, Fred, does not have that same restriction. Why? ♥♥♥♥ you, that's why! Though I'd argue that's not even the worst part.I mained Velvet when I played this game and enjoyed her a lot, but it became evident, even in my amateur eyes, that she was just blatantly worse than every other character in the cast. She has no ways to really open people up and is supposed to rely on chip damage to do most of the work, but her zoning requires resources to be good and even with said resources, every other character has tools that just invalidate half her moveset and force her to rely on her garbage normals, all of which are mids. The devs did buff her chip damage in 2.0, which was at least a step in the right direction, but what did they do to her most recently?They nerfed her. They nerfed the worst character in the game. Her ♥♥♥♥♥♥ DP, which requires a resource to even use and can be easily jumped over, was nerfed yet again to be even more minus and will now trade way more often, because god forbid this character be allowed to play or do anything at all. This nerf is made even worse by many universal changes in 3.0 that made defensive options way weaker. You can't tech roll safely, ever, you can't backdash on wakeup for 8 frames of invincibility to mix up your reversal timing, you just die now. Cross canter (alpha counter) was also gutted, where it was one of Velvet's few strengths thanks to her meter gain in 2.0. A lot of people didn't like these changes because matches tend to snowball way more than before, but for a character like Velvet who desperately needs to keep the opponent out, but can't do so reliably, having basically no defensive options makes her painful to play.3. Selling DLC when the game isn't finished is not okay, especially not after 3 years of being out of early access and promising people the game would be finished. I could forgive Shanty if the very next thing the devs did was Chapter 2, but that's not how things played out. Apparently, with Texas, they're going to add him as a boss fight to Chapter 1 and do something similar with future characters in the season pass. This just strikes me as pure scope creep. I also don't know why it took another 15 months for them to finish the level 3 supers after they showed them on a stream being basically finished, but that wouldn't have been a problem had they just prioritized story mode like they should have in the first place.Do not buy this game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game's best unique feature is probably it's lobby system. The lobby system hasn't been done like this in any other game, as far as I'm aware. You're sent to what looks like a sprite style game mode where you can walk around on a small town map. You can interact with, and fight other players you find here. Treasure chests sometimes appear, and you can pick them up. During the 10 second window after you start interacting with the chest, another player can challenge you for the chest's contents. You can gain currency called Salt, which you can use to buy hats and other customizations for your lobby character. The shop is located in the town map your character walks around on.The best thing about the lobby is the "Salt Mines" lobby game. It's sort of like a PvE dungeon exploration salt collecting game that gradually adds more elements of horror as time goes on. Players in the mine try to explore and mine salt, while avoiding or fighting cpu predators in the game. The predators get more difficult as time passes. At the final stage of the salt mine mode, the player who has gathered the most salt becomes a predator character with a ton of health that scales to the number of players, and gets to hunt down all the players currently in the mine. Meanwhile, the players have to navigate their way through almost-complete darkness in the mines. This turns the last stage of the Salt Mines into a surprisingly good asymmetrical horror game. At the end of the round, everyone gets a certain amount of salt, which can be used to buy cosmetics for use in the lobby. If you get knocked out before the end stage, then you can spend salt to re-enter the mine.While the cast of characters isn't the biggest here, each character is radically different from each other. They all have unique mechanics. Even the way characters build up their magic gauge for special attacks is different from character to character. Arizona needs to use her lasso to grab an opposing character in order to get magic charges, while Oleander needs to sit and study her book in order to gain magic, and there are other characters that just passively gain magic over time. What makes it slightly easier to learn the characters is that each character has a small number of universal inputs, like a simple combo string, that the player can learn to add on to.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastically designed fighting game. Chain the chain combos in this game are a great setup for learning how to combo in other games. Story mode is short but surprisingly fun. Characters are very well balanced, I have yet to hear a good case to state that any of the six cast-mates are un-viable at pretty much any level. Animations are pretty and the designs are unique. The only glaring downsides are twofold: the number of players and number of characters.The player-base is so small that most of the people who still play are very very good. Its overwhelming. This is still a fun game to lose at, i guess, but I wish there were enough players to properly represent a full skill curve. Meanwhile, six characters, while true to the roots of the game and the name of the studio, is a very small amount. However, the game is cheap and more content should come every year or so, so its an investment. I'm sure that after another story-mode drop, two or three more characters, and some proper exposure at a major tourney this will be one of the best fighting games on the market. I would buy it now, sitting in your steam library for a year or two is worth it to support a game this well made in order to get it to get the community it deserves.

_childDocuments_.review: Full disclosure: I backed this game and received a closed beta key.Them's Fightin' Herds is a fast, fluid four-button four-legged fighter featuring a cast of fantasy quadrupeds. The gameplay is butter-smooth, with easy-to-grasp controls and a satisfying whump to every hit. The characters, designed by cartoon producer/director Lauren Faust, are colorful and full of personality. It was kind of amazing to see these characters come to life as their "cardboard" placeholder animations were gradually phased out. The music is crazy good, and hearing the character instruments dynamically take over the song over the course of a match is just fantastic. The voice acting, which was just recently implemented, surprised everyone with its highly experienced cast. This ain't no fan project!Netplay is generally pretty good, but it obviously depends on your connection. I've had a few bum matches in the past.It's also kind of easy to get comboed to death if you go up against someone who's real good, or fight the CPU on above the default difficulty. That's just how fighting games go, though.Overall,  I'm running out of ways to say this game is real good. If you like the hand-drawn cartoon style and/or quick, responsive fighting action, give this game a shot.Touch the COW. Do it NOW. (9/10)Full release update: The game's still excellent, but now even more so. Pick it up.

_childDocuments_.review: So a little backstory. It was around 2013/2014 and I was a complete noob at fighting games(still kind of am). I was however very into MLP:FiM. Now I understand this game has it's own identity in no way related to MLP but back when it was still 'Friendship is Magic', I gave it a shot mainly playing Applejack and really enjoyed just messing around. It also showed that the team at the time had a lot of potential(which now a lot more people have come to realise). 'Them's Fightin' Herds' is a really solid fighter for veterans and first-timers alike. Don't judge it by it's aesthetics and solely by it's gameplay. The tutorial is solid, detailed, and will show any newcomer to the genre all they need to know even including topics like hitboxes and frame data. The music is amazing and it shows they really put in a lot of love into this game. There are only 6 characters which some might call a con but they're all very unique and spread out. There is a Goat character coming in the next major patch as of this review and hopefully more after. I can understand they wanted to polish everything in the game for their 1.0 release before working on the roster so imo shouldn't really fault them too much for that. The story mode beats imo most other fighting games period. Great dialogue and it goes over some basic character movements in the platforming sections. The lobby is arguably the best in the genre. Fun customisation, PvE in the salt mines which leads to more cosmetics, and a cutesy little hub to just vibe in. Netcode is just as great as people claim and it's only going to get better from my understanding as they plan to get the same update that Skullgirls got for their netcode. The developers are involved with the community and open to play matches or discuss issues or ways that the game can be improved. I love that in games in general. There aren't that many players at the moment but the numbers are steadily growing and I really wish the team great success because their dedication and passion definitely merits it. Sorry this review's on the messy side but just wanted to give my thoughts in no particular order. Great game, great community, and great team. What more does one need?Also TIANHUO REPRESENT!

_childDocuments_.review: It is Melty Blood for fans of the works of Lauren Faust and Craig McCracken.A country bumpkin must stop the return of genocidal predators. This brings them to the racially segregated Reindeer village where she is immediately discriminated against. It is wild.The gameplay itself outside of the actual fighting (especially that platforming in the story mode) is not fun, but the presentation, music, setting, spirit, soul, passion, art and humour - as well as the relentless charm of the dialogue and every little hidden detail... is top tier.Game itself is most fun playing competitively against others, however. Storymode's worst part is the actual gameplay outside of exploring and fighting the fantastic bosses. It is an experience more fun to watch than play.The controls for fighting could be a lot tighter, with more accurate hitboxes. Some fights felt like I was trying to tie an octopus together in a knot during an oil spill. It felt messy and uncomfortable, often wrestling with the left stick for certain moves. The achievements are there, but no one has the ability to unlock them yet.I will definitely return to this game when the story is finished, which I am guessing will go along with the eventual console port this month."Agh, Lutefisk!" - Velvet, ze best

_childDocuments_.review: This is a quick review after playing for a couple of hours.Short version: Even after such a short amount of time I highly recommend Them's Fightin' Herds. Go buy it now.  Long Version:  I love fighting games and have done for many years, but not just *any* fighting game will do. I'm happy to say this isn't just a low effort game and I would recommend it to any fan of the genre. Them's Fightin' Herds' (TFH) fighting system isn't breaking new ground, but it has enough features to have it's own feel. It feels kind of like a dialed back anime fighter. There are no air dashes, super jumps or double jumps outside of unique, per character passives. The combo system is the usual Light > Medium > Hard fair, but there are variations based on each characters individual moves. The magic button handles auxiliary special moves and features of each character, somewhat similar to Blazblue's 'Drive' system.Pros:-Solid fighting game mechanics.-Beautiful hand drawn graphics.-Great net code (GGPO).-Unique characters.-Fully, I mean FULLY featured training mode.Cons:-Only 6 characters (I think they are adding more later).-No story mode (as of this review. It is being added later).Honestly, if you don't mind the small roster and like fighting games, it is well worth the asking price. Bear in mind, the small roster still represents a lot of variety; there are no shoto clones here and you are sure to find a character you enjoy playing. The net code is solid and I've been able to find matches easily and play with minimal lag.Buy.This.Game.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a long-time fighting game fan, and this is one of the best fighting games I've ever played. On a technical level, on a design level, and with a focus on welcoming newcomers to 2d fighting games into the core concepts without holding their hands. The animation, character design, tutorial mode, and overall fighting mechanics are wonderful. The first chapter of the story mode is challenging and charming in equal measure. The fighting is fast but responsive, fluid, and with a smartly designed combo system and a clever character-unique "magic" system.I love every single character in this game, they all pop with personality and their fighting styles match them perfectly. As mentioned, their designs and their animations are top notch.That's all why this is such a tragedy. This is a lovingly-crafted fighting game made by genre enthusiasts and fans of animation... that has been taken away from its creators and shuttered, unfinished, by an uncaring publisher after they acquired the rights.I love this game, and it's immensely well-made. But recommend? I can't. It's quite literally unfinished and never will be finished. And this publisher does not deserve to have this stolen and hollowed-out project make money for them. A sad, sad story.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who watched the Fighting is Magic development from start to untimely finish, including the migration to Them's Fightin' Herds, I was very excited to finally see this game come out. I'm in the middle ground when it comes to fighting games: I like them a lot and pick up the basics pretty quickly, but nowhere near the competitive and skill required by tournament level players, so here's a mid-range fighting game enthusiast's thoughts:Pros:~Tutorial system is very comprehensive, with a reasonable enough learning curve to allow beginners to become comfortable with the game pretty quickly.~Lots of humor and fun in the game's style. From the names of each pallette swap, to the witty quips that fighters give eachother, the game's atmosphere comes off as not afraid of getting silly. ~Gameplay is fluid and adaptable, allowing for a good amount of challenge and plenty of room to master the tougher stuff.~Music is kickass. Nuff said.Cons:~A roster of 6 characters is extremely low for a fighting game. Expect things to get repetitive.~Online play, for the moment, is bottlenecked by tryhards who care more about winning at all costs than having fun.PS: Yes, I'm a brony. No, my opinions on the game weren't influenced by being one. (although I did appreciate the nods to the fandom.)

_childDocuments_.review: This game is more astonishing than you may believe at first glance.Aside from the beautiful art style of the always astounding Lauren Faust, the play is extremely smooth, each character generally offers something different, and the game is genuinely trying to be a great fighting game.I'd like to first build on the art style. It's your typical Lauren Faust art, simplistic yet detailed, smooth yet much depth, forward yet much care put into them. The backgrounds follow what most 2D games attempt to do, make a 3D or layered background: that means the backgrounds have depth to them that help wrap the player into the game.Next to mention is the gameplay. Everything flows very well, as a person who plays many fighting games I can happily say this game nails it. I personally tend to struggle with arena sizes and height of characters (generally how high they jump or how far the screen goes up) which is a constant down fall in fighters that either tug the screen so one player is out of the screen, or the arena is too big and i'm left helpless against some spammer with no approach... Hugo mains lyf. This game mirrors Skullgirls, the game it's built off of engine wise, with a decently sized arena and abilities that use said space pretty well, I myself taking Pom under my wing and letting me float around as I need.Which leads me to characters. The only concern I have going into this game is the ability for characters to abuse range, long or mid range, I often struggle against people who have the fast, instant range bolts or massive area mid attacks when playing with friends, though to answer that most characters lacking in that department have answers. Paprika does... whatever Paprika does, some good range mixed with tossing stuff. Pom (my spirit animal no doubt) has a float that juuuust tops off some projectiles, as well as her evasive dash that can either set you up or bait depending on the light or heavy varients you use. The designs are brilliant and unique, and stick to quirks that I personally find just adorable to no ends. Silly llama, southern belle cow with an attitude, shy sheep, angry warmonger dragon, it's all so great for design.As a fighting game, this game isn't hard, and it isn't easy, it's a solid inbetween. You struggle but the layouts are so simple you can quickly pick it up, everything seems very balanced except a few small adjustments needing to be done (which, early access, duh).I have high hopes for this game, and I hope Mane6 sticks with it and makes it a brilliant game it deserves to be!

_childDocuments_.review: I may not be a brony, but when I first touched base with this game, I somehow grew an interest in it. I was even more intrigued after seeing famous people in the FGC like SonicFox and Maximilian Dood play the game, and seeing what can be done as a pro player, it just draws me in (I actually fought SonicFox a few days after I bought it, and of course, they destroyed me because of my unfamiliarity to the game. Now that I think about it, I might want a rematch in the future with them as of 1.0). Since I'm an experienced fighting game player, it's pretty much any fighting game these days that get my attention. Anyways, this GGPO powered game is the second to use Lab Zero's Z-Engine (which was first used for Skullgirls), and that is where the mechanically deep gameplay comes in, just as the description said.Them's Fightin' Herds is a perfect example of combining Marvel vs Capcom's and Skullgirls' gameplay, with a hint of Killer Instinct's combo limit mechanic and Injustice's gravity scaling mechanic, only instead of causing a blowout like in KI, it allows you to continue the combo, but after you have filled up a bar underneath your health bar, your opponent will fall faster and faster with each hit, making it harder to keep up your combo.Since there are also pixel lobbies in the game, which is the more popular form of lobbies in TFH, the game offers up a really good way to interact with fellow players. You can customize your character in it, like in other games with those types of lobbies (i.e. Blazblue Centralfiction and Cross Tag Battle, Guilty Gear Xrd, etc.) and request matches in it as well, like in any other game with this type of lobby. What's different with this particular lobby system is that it has voice chat, and more recently, channels you can switch from in order to talk to anyone in that channel you'd like without being disrupted by other players. Also, you could do memes, roleplay and stuff if you really wanted to.It might be in early access right now, but I still feel that getting this game was totally the right call for me! Hopefully you consider it too! It's a pretty neat fighting game! And as a friendly tip from my experience, the game appears to be more active in the evening (Eastern Standard Time Zone), so I think you could find some matches in the pixel lobbies then. Alright, I'm done here. Have fun with TFH, or don't. Doesn't matter to me. That's right, I'm talking about the Story Mode! It's real good for people who want to experience the lore of the game, and unless you either don't care for spoilers or have already played through the story mode, don't head into the spoiler zone. Go play the story yourself and find out just how good it is! Find some secrets, get some jokes, and just have a good time. It's all the way down there under the 2.0 edit so nobody accidentally goes over it.All I have to say here is that Shanty is a fun character, and now I main her.Anyways, you can get to the story now if you either went through it already or just don't care about spoilers. Have a good one!

_childDocuments_.review: I am a competitive fighting game player with multiple Top 8s across different games. This was the best fighting game I had ever played, despite the gameplay and balance issues. I played this game, competed, and did pretty well in events for the majority of the pandemic. This really was the best fighting game I had ever played during that time, despite the gameplay and balance issues in older versions (which, while annoying, weren't any more overblown than any other fighting game). I don't regret my time with this game at all. However, it's gotten extremely hard for me to recommend as more time has passed. For every strong point in this game, there's something else about it that is frustrating for a competitive player. This has some of the best QoL features of any fighting game, yet major bugs go unfixed for long periods of time. There are some really dedicated, awesome, passionate players & staff members who will give up everything to teach you and make your time with the game loads of fun. Yet, there are also insufferable members of the staff & community who may make discussing and grinding the game as a competitive player more frustrating. This scene has always been very tight knit and close, which means it becomes harder and harder to avoid those people- thus souring the experience. Every community has its issues, so whether or not this affects your experience may vary. Personally, in spite of it all, am very grateful for the friendships that I made during through this game.If you're looking for a fighting game that feels good to play with friends, or you have a small scene with your friends- I would still recommend it. Especially if you're in EU or Asia (look up Fauna / EU discord for this game, they have great scenes full of passionate players). It's also a fantastic casual game, with a groundbreaking story mode for fighting games and breathtaking aesthetics. As a competitive player, though? This game has turned into a hard pass. I finally sat down with the newest versions on console after not playing at all since 2.X, and while the direction of the game seems more sound- it's still not going to be a great fit for everyone competitively. Knowing the team, this will get better with time- but updates and fixes have slowed down over the years.Still worth checking out depending on your goals and interests in the genre. But if your interest lies in competing- look elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: The animations are great, the characters amazing, voices, personalities. The powers are not too amazing but look good. But the fighting mechanics, or maybe just because its a low budget game, are not great. The area of the hit effects, the knock downs, the blocking... In particular the AI (even in normal) is bad, knowing exact ranges and sticking to "going back and forth in the same zone" as long as it "knows" you can't hit it. The flaws, plus the dishonest AI (that also keeps blocking everything) kills the solo part of the game.The story is also quite basic as are the maps (art is good though...) and bosses continue as, or even more, irritating; with some weak mechanics that make us have to either spam or retry constantly. Its a game BUILT around combos, you HAVE to use the low hits, and keep using those crappy hits until you can. I prefer a Street fighter approach, there are also the low hits(kick, punch) but we can very well use the strongest punch to have fun. Here? impossible, gotta spam those low hits while the opponent is down or being knocked.I like the game but I wont be playing it much because of these mechanics.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright let's cut to the chase right away and worry 'bout the details later.The game is fun. It is the testimony that crowdfunded games can still be made and not be awful. It's the very opposite of awful. It is amazing.The inclusion of a pixel lobby transforms what would have otherwise been just another fighter game(but with quadrupeds), into an almost RPG like game... you could probably role play too if you were so inclined. I've spent hours playing the dungeon raids to get more interesting wearables and it is fun. The fighting feels good and exciting and the graphics are beautiful.There are a few graphics and artwork missing here and there and some still having the sketch placeholder but those are just in a couple of places. They delivered an almost complete game, it was stable with only one minor crash when I changed resolution but it didn't reproduce. The game works really well with a controler (tested with Xbox 1 controller), and has a voice chat and text chat, as well as a small board with quick responses such as Hello, GGWP, and a couple quick question buttons to ask others to fight you or train with you or maybe reconsider that rematch they declined.The game's roots from the original Fighting is Magic are still present. The characters are very familiar to anyone who has watched MLP:FiM, yet they are completely new and unique. They truly managed to strike the center of the target. Making something completely new and giving players exactly what they had wanted back in 2013. An amazing quadruped fighter game.Netcode worked quite well. When playing with nearby players or even slightly further away the experience was good.Though if you intended to match with your friend from Australia you may experience issues with performance and everything stuttering. Which isn't to say the game is bad, quite the opposite, the game deals well with the issues of high latency, as much as it can. It's just not a problem that can be fixed, unless someone makes a really fast internet connection from Europe to Australia. Players are given an option to tweak some settings and try to achieve better experience while playing with distant friends. I've not had the time to test or play with them but the game does well with default ones, even recommending different values so you don't have to do the guesswork.The game comes with plenty of options for new players to practice, such as practicing their moves and combos without time limit or health limit, and you can also do it with another person if you want to take your practice to the next level and simulate real battles with your friend.  You can play against an AI in arcade and practice your skills against someone who is very much not fair (though you can make the AI easy, normal and so on all the way up to unfair difficulty). The game also has a list of challenges you can complete in the Target mode where you have to destroy the target's in a specific way as quickly as you can.If the game is this good on release, who know's what it will be like when they polish it up with updates and the additional character the Goat, and the Linus/MacOS support. Unfortunately the Story Mode didn't make it into the release but I will definitely eagerly await for them to finish this piece of the game. Cause who doesn't like a story mode?Happy Fighting.

_childDocuments_.review: For the love of god could you make fix the key binding in this game already? I like to play on keyboard but the fact that the controls have both the first and second player mapped all over it non negotiably makes it impossible to rebind. I like WSAD for direction buttons, UIOJKL for combat buttons. But when I try to map it like that, the UI starts putting imputs in for second player to mess everything up. I try to map my combat buttons to the number pad and it won't read 5 as a button at all because it only reads the pad as directional keys.I bought this game when it came out because it looked like a cute idea but I haven't been able to play more than a half hour since owning it because the defaults are far too unintuitive and usually I spend all of the time in game trying to figure out some way to bypass the awful UI until the whole program comes crashing down in a pathetic blaze. This is the worst I've ever seen out of a fighting game and its surprising this was made in the Skullgirls engine seeing as that game has one of the best UI's I've ever seen.

_childDocuments_.review: This review will be going against the grain a bit, but I wouldn't recommend this game based on its own merits. For me, the story mode is always the most important thing of nearly any game, and that's where this one disappoints the most (even without being apparently unfinished).The actual fighting game core mechanic is fairly well made, though I'm personally a fan of controls that don't require using your movement keys to block (my preference is more Smash Bros, less Mortal Kombat). That difference of opinion aside, however, the fighting controls are serviceable and the action fluid, so no real complaints.The problem comes with the story-mode integration. Injustice is a great example of how you can tell a great story through a fighting game, and integrate non-fighting game elements (mostly quick-time events in that game). This game, however, takes the wrong approach in trying to integrate both RPG and platforming elements into the game, some aspects of this work well, while others are atrocious and ruin the game.The RPG elements are mostly moving a character around on an RPG-maker style map. This is very basic, but adds an interesting exploration element. Something like this is an easy way to add story, with the fighting gameplay being the result of "random encounters" on the map. It's even designed so that losing a fight doesn't immediately cause you to lose. Instead, you lose an amount of your overworld hp each time you lose (or a smaller amount if you win, based on in-fight damage taken). The problem comes mainly in the form of bosses being instant game over - the hardest foes are the ones you aren't allowed to lose against. This is made worse by these enemies having very unique moves, like involving multiple opponents, or dodging attacks the boss spits from the background. While fun and interesting mechanics, these new strategies to adapt to are exactly why bosses should  be an instant game over if you lose, especially given the length of time needed to get back through the RPG elements.And then you have the platforming. Do not make a platformer without a jump button. Just don't. Not only does this game not have a jump button, but it has three different jump heights depending on how fast you move the controls. Frustratingly, this is  sensitive, and counter-intuitively both short and long jumps require faster presses. Protip: if a handful of ledges are your entire puzzle, your control scheme is f***ed.So in conclusion, if you just want a fighting game with cute characters, this isn't a bad choice. If you want to play the story mode, you should probably choose a different game that doesn't try to dabble too broadly.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing fighters for basically my entire life, stemming from the Street Fighter Alpha series, Tekken 2 and 3, Ultimate Mortal Kombat 3, and pretty much everything that came out after. I also have a natural knack for these kinds of games. A few minutes in training mode to fiddle around with the characters and mechanics, and I'm basically ready to compete with high skill level players.Fast forward to somewhere in 2012 and Skullgirls is released, and I have to say, it's been my favorite fighting game the day I downloaded it on my Xbox 360 even until now. I can go on about why it's the perfect fighting game, at least from my perspective, but this isn't a Skullgirls review.While Skullgirls is arguably the best indie fighting game ever made, Them's Fightin' Herds has potential to be the next indie fighter powerhouse. It may be it's close resemblance to Skullgirls in which that it uses the same engine as it, or the hand drawn characters, or the GGPO netcode, but those are all things that made these games spectacular. I've only been playing for a few hours, but it's held my attention more than any fighter that came out since Skullgirls, and that's why I'm certain that this game will proseper. That is, if the devs keep up with it, which they seem like they are.This is in early access, so obviously there are going to be bugs, there are going to be modes missing, there aren't going to be many characters, so critiquing the game being unfinished would be just plain foolish. The game is playable, the online is smooth, and it's just plain fun. If you like 2D 4-button juggle heavy fighters, Then this game is for you.Also I'm not a brony by any means.This game isn't specifically for bronies. You don't have to be a brony to buy this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I've known about Them's Fightin' Herds for a long time and it wasn't until I bought a gaming laptop that I could finally try it out. TFH is not my first fighting game as I dabble with Guilty Gear and KOF mostly but I can say from my previous fighting game experience that TFH is a very solid fighter. Don't let the cutesy characters fool you, this is a robust fighting game through and through with combo strings, push blocks, and character specific "magic" abilities. TFH also boasts a beginner friendly tutorial mode that will teach you things from basic combos to framedata and hurtboxes, so if you want to try out a fighting game but feel too intimidated, this game will walk you through all the lingo that's common in a fighting game so you'll be ready to go online. Speaking of online, it's probably the best online experience I've had. TFH has rollback netcode which makes playing other people a breeze. I truly love this game and can't wait to see what gets added in the future!

_childDocuments_.review: Those of you that have been following the games development will know that the developers really care about this game to continue after their struggles in the development of their games.Each charecter has a unique fighting style, design and personality to each of them.The stages are as unique as the charecters.The game has a lobby system that allows you to select a pixel version of one of the fighters and chat with other players in the lobby as you explore a hub world of a lobby. You can also dress your charecter in their pixel form with a bunch of items. Skull girls players will get 2 hats and a neck piece.The pixel version of the charecter you pick matters as there is a feature in the game that allows you to go salt mining in the caves of the lobby world and find chests full of salt but in the caves are shadowy predators of herd animals that will chase your pixel charecter and begin a fight. They will keep coming until you have been beaten. The pixel charecter you chose will be the charecter you fight off the predators with.It is important to note that the game is still in early access meaning that it is not quite complete yet and some charecters still have frames of attacks that need to be finished first. Currently the game has card board cut out like sketches as replacements for missing frames on some charecters and their attacks. Some of these are quite distracting. I have no doubt that they will look as nice as the rest of the animations once complete though.One personal complaint I have about how the game plays is the dashing, it is short and does not close much of a distance making getting in close for an attack difficult. I have encounterd multiple fights where I have had to dash many times to get close to the other player as they keep a large distance with ranged attacks. This is a problem in many fighting games but with the dash in this game it feels harder to close the gap than others.Like Skull Girls this game is a good game to start with for those of you who that may be intrested in getting into 2d fighting games.

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like I've played enough to give this game a fair review:This game is basically a non oficial My Little Poney Fighting Game (it was an Oficial MLP FG at some point but Hasbro chickened out). Just to be clear, I'm not really into this My Little Poney /Furry/Anthro/Whatever coummunity(nor do I have a problem with people are into that kind of thing), but I can appreciate a Damn Good Fighting Game when I play one, and fortunately, this is the case here. Also I think the concept of cute Ponies fighting each other is hilarious, in a good way.Them's Fightin' Herds is a 4 button 1 v 1 Fighting Game with 6 characters Total, I know, not a very impressive number, but each character is so Unique that I feel you are trading Quantity for Quality.  Their animations are all unique and full of personality, also the music kicks ass most of the time (there's one or two and not a big fan of, but most of them are pretty good). You'll probably find one or two characters that'll suit your playstyle, Personally I really enjoy playing Paprika for eg: The crazy Alpaca with a lot of gimmicks, random moves  and a fighting style that kills your opponents by Smothering them with love, literally, she doesn't want to hurt anyone, she just loves too hard... The Netcode is pretty Good, it uses GGPO Rollback and you can find quality matches with people from arround the globe. Trust me, I'm from SA and I'm finding good games with people in the NA and EU. The community for this game is not big, but I feel It's not going to die anytime soon, I've bough this game when it first launched in Early Access and I've been able to always find people to play with, and now that the game hit 1.0, I feel like it's more populated than ever.The game uses a lobby system thats really interisting, dare I say, the best lobby system in the whole industry (Learn from this game ArcSys!). You basically have different scenarios where you can walk, participate in community events (salty Mines), customize your character(and there's a lot of customization to your Lobby Avatar), and of course fight people, you can also train the lobby and the best thing, you can do all of that while Matchmaking (You basically can enter the matchmaking in almost any mode in the game, online and offline), meaning it's a lobby that never limits you.If you are a casual, this game tutorial got you covered, it's pretty good, one of the best I've played so far . It teaches you everything about the game system's and also fighting game in general, even Frame Advantage, Hit and Hurtboxes. If you are new to fighting games, I feel like it's worth a buy just for the tutorial, you'll learn a lot of fundamentals that applies in basically every other 2D fighting game.The Story is kinda of a Hit and a miss. I feel like the idea is in the right place, it's really unorthodox  compared to other fighting games story (and that's great, because I think most of them suck), you control an avatar just like the lobby system and you can explore through sections of the main adventure, basically advancing the story whenever you fight a boss. You can find secrets, explore secret areas and there's minigames that are really cool because they test your movements skills, it's almost like a Drill, or a mini tutorial in Super Jumps and Hops.The miss is the spikes in difficulty, some of the bosses are really unfair, even on casual difficultiy (wich you'll probably will have to play to win some fights ). If you are casual , I think you'll have fun in this game until you hit a Boss, then, I can see a lot of people dropping the game because it's not really casual friendly, it's not even beginner/ intermediate friendly. You'll have to get good if you want to beat the Bosses. One cool thing about the bosses is that they are really unique, they added different phases to them testing different skills of the player. (the biggest problem is that they always seem to recover Health when transitioning to another phase, meaning you basically have 1 health bar to defeat a boss that sometimes you'll have 3 healths bars, or 1 health bar to defeat 9 minions + the boss, that where the game is really unfair to you)There's one last thing I want to warn you about this game, it just hit 1.0 and got out of Early Access, but the Story is not complete (each character will get a chapter and currently there's only one chapter out), the Level 3 supers (the most flashy moves in the game) are not out yet, and the last character (a goat) is still development. The Goat I understand, but I would not really consider this game out of Early Access if those other features are not out yet. Will the developers deliver them? Most Likely, since the first day of EA they've always been very communicative, and they are still talking with the community through Discord, Steam Forums and Reddit. I trusted them a year ago, and I trust them now. But Since it's out of Early Access, this means technically they don't have to obligation to deliver this things. I believe they got out of EA for populate the lobbys or make a console port (with crossplay I hope) since you there was not really many people playing online back then and you can't release an Early Access game to consoles. But yeah, keep this in mind, Until Know the devs earned my trust and I really believe this will come out, but you never know, I'd say the chance of we not getting the rest of the content is less than 10% tho, the people behind this game are good people who are known in the community and have a reputation to maintain.Pros:Fun and Unique CharactersBeautiful GraphicsGood SoundtrackGreat TutorialBest Lobby system in the industryReally good Online (GGPO Rollback)Creative Story ModeCons:Story Mode difficulty is unfair, possibly the hardest story mode I've ever faced in a fighting game (casuals beware)No level 3 supers yetOnly One  chapter in Story mode is outI believe this game should've not leave Early Access yet.Story mode might be patched, if that happens I'll edit this review.

_childDocuments_.review: The thing that influenced me to buy this game the most is the great netcode. The game uses GGPO rollback netcode and even though I'm playing on a wifi connection my online experience has been great. Other than that, the gameplay and combat mechanics resemble many other anime fighters/capcom fighters like blazblue or marvel vs. capcom. This makes TFH not only a great starting point for people who want to get into the FGC but also a fun experience for older fans of the genre.The animations, the soundtrack and the visuals are great as well.Even the story mode which is pretty lackluster in many triple A fighting games was done very well in this game. The rpg style made it pretty refreshing for me as well.The only thing I criticize is the small character roster. But I understand that Mane6 is an indie developer so I'm excited about new characters being added in the future.All in all I think TFH has everything a fighting game fan would want in a fighting game and more. I'd totally recommend this game to veteran fighting game players but also to people who want to get into fighting games.

_childDocuments_.review: I normally don't review games but this game is so frustrating that I felt obligated to. _childDocuments_.review: So what is Them's Fightin' Herds?Well, Them's Fightin' Herds is a 2D fighting game about quadrupedal animals hitting the snot out of eachother either offline with/without friends or online against strangers.First thing immediately seen from the visual design of the game is the main menu, and it gives off a great first impression for the game, from the simple but clean visuals of the menu to the amazing main theme of the game.After firing up the game's Practice Mode and getting greeted with the character select screen showing all 6 characters of the game and demonstrating the dynamic music system a bit.After checking out all the different characters i decided to go with the adorable alpaca named Paprika whose dialogue consists entirely out of different squeaks and funny noises.The spritework inside of the game is quite smooth and looks pleasing to the eye, the hitsparks and hit noises give enough feedback to feel good about hitting a poor wobbling lamb in the face with a potted plant. Visually the game has little to complain aboutNo fighting game review is complete without talking about the meat-n-bones of the game, the gameplay itself.Them's Fightin' Herds plays like a pretty traditional Anime fighter like BlazBlue or Under Night In-Birth, With 4 attack buttons, A (X on xbox) for light, B (Y on xbox) for Medium, C (B on xbox) for Heavy and D (A on xbox) for MagicPressing these buttons does different attacks.The game provides you with a practice mode and a command list for each of the characters for you to learn their various moves.The game is very combo focused and every character has a universal launcher move (3+C) that can be used to propel opponents into the air for even longer combos, so far it sort of feels like Skullgirls crossed with BlazBlue. The footsies are a bit awkward though with the characters having four legs.The game's online is quite interesting, The online is focused around Pixel Lobbies, which work sorta like the lobbies from Guilty Gear, allowing you to customize your tiny avatar and challenge other people to matches. The game's netcode uses GGPO and it has been pretty great so far with little to no lag during online play.Them's Fightin' Herds has a unique dynamic music system that depends on what characters are fighting currently, what stage they're on and who is currently winning. The soundtrack has some amazing music such as Paprika vs. Oleander on Woodlands or Arizona vs. Arizona on Sunset Prairie.Overall, Them's Fightin' Herds is an amazing fighting game made by passionate developers, It looks good and plays well, featuring some amazing music to boot. The tutorial of the game is one of the best i've seen in a long time in fighting games too! With the game's low price, there is no reason not to pick this up if you enjoy fighting games.9/10

_childDocuments_.review: I've been looking into this game ever since I heard about it in a few YouTube videos. I love fighting games (have since I was a little girl, since back in the 90's the genre was the only one that had decent, strong, female playable characters on the regular), I love games with a colorful aesthetic (Why are games that are supposed to be "realistic" looking cursed with muted color palettes 85% of the time?), and I love animation, so this game was one I was really excited to get."Them's Fightin' Herds" has a very good tutorial section that covers most of the game's mechanics fairly well, and a roster of colorful characters who are full of charm and personality. You can tell this evolved from a concept of a "My Little Pony" fighting game not just because of the visual style but, if you've watched at least the first season of the show, you can tell which characters are based off of which member of the Mane Six (and I'm sure someone is already writing a cross-over fan fic). My favorite of the bunch so far is Velvet the reindeer, who reminds me of a certain purple-maned, white unicorn (come on, replace her ice with gems, and she's totally a snootier version of Rarity). The combos and specials are fun to use and challenging but rewarding to master, and I'm having a blast trying all of the characters out.I also enjoy this game's approach to a story mode. Most fighting games I've payed have a story mode that's just arcade mode with dialogue and cut scenes, but TFH has taken the approach of blending RPG dungeon crawling and puzzle solving with platforming and the game's base combat mechanics into a very interesting and fresh take on the classic story mode. The dialogue is pretty well written and there are hidden goodies and side-quests to uncover all over the place. My only two gripes about this mode are the decision to use the game's combat movement mechanics in the platforming sections and the fact that boss battles with playable characters have them pulling ultra-moves that you don't have any access to as a player.In terms of the platforming, let me be clear that I've been playing platformers for almost 30 years. I know how to negotiate traps, moving platforms, bottomless pits, and those annoying "Surprise Sucka!!" enemies that come out of nowhere just to mess with you. I know my stuff. So, believe me when I say that because of how precise the inputs for the super jump are, it makes platforming very annoying at some points in the story.  You have to hit down and up or up-diagonal in such a rapid succession that if you have a slippery thumb stick and a D-pad that puts those darn divots in the diagonal spots, you will not have a fun time executing this maneuver at all. You will think you did it right, swear you did it fast enough and accurately enough this time...and then you fall though some troll gap between the platform you're on and the platform you need to get to and you end up 5 levels down! It's very, very frustrating. I understand the input timing for when you're fighting, but when platforming, they should tweak the input timing to be a little more generous. You know, like 0.5 seconds instead of 0.2 seconds. With the timing as it is, it makes platforming more of a chore than an enjoyable addition to the game.My other gripe, the one about the ultra moves for player character bosses, is not only because it's slightly cheap. I'm used to fighting game bosses being cheap. It's a staple of the genre at this point. However, when a boss is also a playable character and they're being cheap with over-powered moves and mechanics that you have no access to when you play the character yourself...that's a little annoying. It took me about 5 or 6 tries to beat Velvet's boss fight in story mode because of her tantrum tornado at the end, and Oleander...well, all I have to say to the devs on that is: You know how wrong that was.Other than those two minor complaints about some frustrating design decisions for story mode, however, this is overall a great game. I, for the most part, recommend this game for players of all ages and skill levels, from experts to your 5-year-old niece who you're trying to introduce to the genre. The characters are fun and full of personality, the art style is colorful and cartoony, and the music is pretty good too.My Final Score: 8.5/10Overall great game, but there are some cheap and trollish moments in the story mode.

_childDocuments_.review: While it is sad that active development of this game will be ending soon (though it has been an impressive 7-year dedication, which we all must acknowledge), that shouldn't stop anyone from picking up this title's deluxe edition.First off, the story mode is very nuanced and inspired. There's a full story, some adventure elements, and, I must admit, it is cool to have a boss give you grief from the background. Though, as mentioned above, we'll likely never see the conclusion to the story, so a bit sad on that point.Never-the-less, the overall gameplay is solid. Special moves and supers are kept to simple haduken inputs, and the mechanics for just about every character are diverse, yet not super complicated once you see how they work in examples. You can pull off stellar combos, the palettes are fun to customize, and as a rushdown player myself, I had a blast with Shanty, truth be told.And, can we talk about the stages?! The fact that there are so many, with day, night, and twilight variants, AND amazing themes. That's a pretty deep layer of icing on an already meaty cake!If you couldn't tell by now, I love this game, and can't recommend it enough to other fighting game enthusiasts, as well as those who want to get into fighting games, but want something a little more cute-n'-cuddly for their first outing.The only downside I see is the lobbies. Either their at capacity, or they're ghost towns. My advice is to make sure you have some online or IRL friends who want to play and are already set up.Solid 9.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Dang, this game took me by surprise. I was always somewhat aware of Them's Fightin' Herds since it was in Early Access for so long and it had already developed quite the story, but I never had that huge an attachment to Fighting Is Magic so I just never really thought about it... until it finally left early access.This game is the real deal. The system is simple but all of the characters have such an interesting kit, the animation is top-notch, and (in what probably surprised me the most) the soundtrack is stellar and dynamic from match to match. For a little indie fighter, the presentation is seriously impressive.It's, of course, also a fully functional and super fun fighting game with cool universal mechanics that each character puts their own little tweaks on. The tutorial is really great whether this is your first fighting game or you're an old hand, with subjects ranging from simple movement to more advanced topics including blockstun, frame data, and how hitboxes and knockdowns work. It also has combo trials to get you started, although accessing them via training mode is a little more of a headscratcher than most other games. Throw in GGPO netcode and I think it's a no-brainer.If there is a concern then it has to be that the roster is pretty small (six characters), but the game is cheap and all the characters we DO have are very interesting. Keep in mind that Skullgirls also only shipped with eight characters, which turned out to be PLENTY to play and learn with.Another pain point might be that the story is technically unfinished--with only one chapter available as of this writing--but given that the fighting system itself is fully fleshed out, I'm not too worried about whether or not the story gets finished, even if what we have is pretty charming (if also a bit difficult).Overall though, I think TFH is very accessible and very fun, and (probably) the most fun I've had since Under Night, which you should also get... but be warned that it doesn't have rollback.

_childDocuments_.review: Now I know what you're probably thinking (unless you're not the kind of person who takes things at face-value). Yes, this is a pony-based fighting game. We get it. Y'all think it's trash just cuz the characters have very distinct similarities to that one very familiar pony show that everyone seems to love to hate on. We get it. But if you're gonna just disregard this whole thing based solely on its surface-level design decisions, then you're gonna miss out on a hell of a good game.If Skullgirls is an introduction to Street Fighter based games, this game is the Skullgirls of games like BlazBlue or Guilty Gear. Which is also kinda funny since this game is built with the Skullgirls engine, so you catfighting fenatics already know that the engine certainly works smoothly. And it's not just that part that works either! The controls are responsive, the gameplay is fun and easy to pick up, and the characters are very diverse and introduce players to different styles of fighting characters. (Except grapplers. Unless you count Arizona as a grappler, which...I don't, really.) I had never even considered picking up a zoner character until I played Oleander, and it's the most fun I've had with the archetype.The game also comes with a Pixel Lobby, which basically functions as a way to find players to fight without having to directly seek them out and make a lobby with them, while still having a bit more interactivity than the Skullgirls Quick Match system. The game itself has about 8 official lobbies, with a whole bunch of fan-created lobbies to spice things up if those ones are full. When entering, you are given a little avatar you can customize with hatsand accessories. Bored of the hats you're given? Go to the Salt Mines! There you can fight Predators and open chests to get salt which can be used to open more expensive chests to get the aforementioned Hats and Accessories.Cons? Well, it's hardly finished, for one, though I wouldn't let that bother you too much. All that's really "missing" per se are things that wouldn't really affect gameplay otherwise, like missing animations and stuff. That's not counting things like Story Mode and quick matches, but you can get a lot of the content missing there through other means, like Arcade mode and the aforementioned Pixel Lobby.In the end, I'd say the game has a lot of potential, and definitely is a lot of fun right now. I implore you to look past first impressions and give the game a try. You just might find a fighting game that you'll really enjoy. I hope this helps you in your purchasing decision.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, let me preface this by saying: Them’s Fightin’ Herds is, or at least was prior to Modus / Maximum Entertainement, a great game, which I’ve praised publicly many times as one of the best packages you could get in terms of fighting games: Good and compelling story mode (even if it was just Chapter 1) which actually taught you how to play the game, solid netplay feauring rollback netcode and crossplay, as well as functional lobbies, a fun PvE side mode, feature-complete training and tutorial mode, a fun (if small) cast of diverse characters with lots of depth and unique mechanics… This was, for all intents and purposes, one of my go-to recommendations alongside Guilty Gear XX Accent Core +R’s PC port, which was also ahead of its time.And then Modus happened.While the buyout of Mane6 by Modus did come with the added perk of console ports, localization and the promise of extended support through a Season Pass, it has been clear for a while that this buyout was not a good thing. Already, Stronghoof’s release felt a tad unpolished, and a lot of cost-cutting measures could be seen. (Stronghoof’s VA acting as his own announcer, low res trap textures on even the Series X port, the lack of a dynamic musical theme…) We get it, crafting a fighting game character, let alone a fully hand-sprited one with huge, HD sprites, takes a lot of time.But what really broke the camel’s back was the fact that between Stronghoof’s release and the Nidra / Baihe patch, the entirety of Mane6 was laid off by Modus save for 3 employees, two of which have since left of their own volition, cancelling the continuation of story mode, and leaving ONE PERSON to have to craft two entire characters on a strict time constraint. And it shows. The official TFH Discord server was left abandoned and prey to p*** bots, and the final patch breaks the game like never before. Both Nidra and Baihe come with a load of infinite combos and bugs which break the game in a significant way, the combo trials are broken, and all of that was discovered in less than an hour after the release of said patch. Who knows what else we could find on legacy characters.As such, it kinda breaks my heart to tell you: DO NOT BUY THEM’S FIGHTIN’ HERDS. Maximum deserves no money for what they’ve done to this game, and that’s without mentioning whatever is happening with their other fighting games, God of Rock and Diesel Legacy. It also serves as a good overview as to what to expect with their upcoming Avatar The Last Airbender fighting game. If you already got scammed by Maximum Entertainement, revert to the previous patch by going to the "stable" beta branch in the Steam settings. If you got it on console… Well RIPMaximum Entertainment is not worth your time. Steer away at all costs.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: The devs have announced the end of active development for this game. Do NOT buy this game as it is quite literally a scam with fine lettering to make it look like it's all fine.-------------------------------------------Fantastic fighting game with a great story, but ruined by changes to development direction.I really, really want to recommend this game as it is one of the most well designed games I've ever played, but ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ I'd be lying if I said I trust these devs in any shape or form. They've been changing their development direction ever since the game's inception, though it never *actually* hurt the game until what they had done to it a year ago.It's frustrating, and maybe even depressing to look at this game's announcements. They've completely shifted aside the story mode and they just focus on new DLC which people (mostly the big fighting game fans that cycle between the games as they go up in popularity) swear is required to be in the game because "other fighting games do it too". Then the comments section is just as frustrating, mainly because they have one dude trying to shut down any criticism ever made in the forums, to the point it feels toxic. If I kept my comments open here I'd probably get a reply from that one dude, if my review doesn't just get flagged and taken down.We were given the (over ambitious) promise of getting the entirety of story mode complete by the end of 2022. Obviously, that was too good to be true and it was clearly a big promise made to be reduced to much less than that, so it'd be foolish to blame them for not delivering on that. However, they didn't deliver even a bit. We got absolutely *nothing* for the story mode. Not one chapter or even any previews for the next one, literally nothing. They just brought up a season pass DLC that they claim you "don't have to buy" and that if you don't like it then you don't have to get it, etc etc, you get the idea.The most we got was them claiming that the story mode is indeed "in the works", and that's it. But now we got yet another DLC reveal and there wasn't even anything for the story in the announcement for it. Hopefully I'm just speaking too early and the next announcement has real details about the upcoming story chapter and not just "yeah it exists". But even then I'd expect the release of just one chapter to be delayed to the very end of this year, and that feels like too much to ask for at this point.It doesn't just stop there, though. This game is pretty much well on its way towards an early playercount death, even during their cherished DLC scheme. The playercounts are REALLY LOW. And to be honest, a lot of people are swayed away from the game solely for the fact that it's a "pony game". It is by all means a "pony" game, and I could try all I want to say otherwise (like the fact there's actually only one pony character), but it all comes down to the same thing: People know Them Fightin' Herds as the MLP fighting game. It's the hard truth and i've watched multiple fighting game fans completely avoid this game regardless of how good it might actually be, solely because it is what it is.So here's the thing, they don't even actually get to attract these players with their DLC season pass scheme, because those people are NOT going to play anyways. And all they do is scare away other potential players AND existing players due to the questionable pricing. The game has been price hiked AND it has multiple DLCs now, seriously.I really want to say what's actually good about this game, but it kinda falls flat because the best thing about it is the story, followed right up by the actual gameplay. Both are absolutely just great. I ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ love this game. But the story has been outdated for years, and all we're getting is DLC. I seriously cannot recommend this game to anyone, I'd have to lie to your face to do so, and hide all the little details about what's wrong with this game.EDIT (DLC2 Update): It gets worse and worse. New update has absolutely zero mention of story mode (effectively shelved), and moving forward new stages aren't going to have fully dynamic music like what TFH always had. It's become a pretty terrible DLC platform in my opinion. I advise you do not buy the DLC for this game.Honestly, I don't even want to actually give this game a rating. It's almost perfect, but the DLC hell and the broken promises are just making it so I get really angry just looking at this game. I'm now setting it to hidden and possibly looking back later this year, but with low standards.Should you buy this game? Only if you absolutely ONLY want the gameplay and nothing else. And only if you're okay with later having to pay 20$+ to get the DLC. And if you're okay with the development direction changing regularly. And if you're okay with the potential death of this game in a not so distant future. EDIT: DON'T.Man.EDIT 3 (Announcement of no active development): Literally everything I said got validated. All that shilling for DLC was for nothing. No story mode, no further content, the last bit of "content" we're getting is a reskinned character. So ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cool.This game quite literally destroyed my faith in indie devs. I always felt these devs were untrustworthy, and now they've really confirmed it.Get as far away as you can. It's over for this game and these devs. Do not look back, there is only a hollow shell of what could have been.

_childDocuments_.review: Not an avid fighting gamer so I can’t comment on how good the fighting mechanics are. What I can comment on is the atrocious game design present in the story mode.Major-Difficulty is all over the place. You can leave a encounter where there was just a single hostile, and then go into a encounter where you need to beat 9 of them up in a row on a single health bar. Playing on normal I can come out of a encounter with no damage, or be slaughtered having barely touched there health bar.-Boss fights are poorly designed, often having nothing to do with fighting game tactics (have to dodge attacks for awhile while the boss is invulnerable), and difficulty ramps that happen over time instead of based on how much damage you do (aka if you miss the first attack the battle becomes way more difficult)-Controls are not great. Everything movement related is bound to your analog stick/arrow keys, which means a bunch of double taps and combos to do things like jump or dash. When you need to be precise, having buttons that do different things depending on what you did before is unacceptable, and its not like they are using the dpads or the triggers for anything important.Minor-The tutorial only seems to teach you attacks, but not really how to use them effectively. -Default controls are set up so that right hand handles movement instead of-button prompts are displayed as A,B,C,D, instead of the buttons or keys that those actions are actually bound to.-Can’t rebind keys unless you are in a fight or the main menu.-Game lets you record up to two macros, but you can’t put in directional controls and it only lets you do 4 buttons which makes it useless.-Key rebinds-Changing resolutions seems rather buggy and has a good chance of crashing-Weird binding limitations like you can’t bind anything to escape (like the back button in the menu) and the enter menu and confirm buttons must be different buttonsOther then these criticisms the game seems alright. Art, music, and story seem fine, but if you are buying this for the campaign and you are not already a pro at these kinds of games, stay the heck away.
