_childDocuments_.review: There's a variety of reasons I can say that it's a great game, but at the moment there's a lot of weird issues that shouldn't be happening.The game was set to release in full the same day it came out in early access, and 2 days before the release date they announced the game would be releasing without story mode. While fine, there's a few issues with this. It seems the build up at the moment, is one that must be quite a while back in development. There are multiple things that are definitely not release quality other than story mode missing. Many characters have fill-in animations, much of the UI feels odd, and even intro animations in battles are wonky and unfinished.However, if you really don't care about these problems, and trust the developer to patch these issues, as they claim they will do soon, then the game itself is great and solid for the most part.The game plays as some kind of weird amalgamation of Guilty gear and Blazblue, with a hint of skullgirls feel. The game has a Light, medium, heavy, and a Magic/Gimmick button. Each character has a 'magic' bar in addition to their super meter, somewhat similar to the V-System in Street Fighter V. Every character gains magic in different ways, some over time, others by confirming certain moves.Pros!+The 6 characters feel varied, and feel unique to each other in their playstyles.+The movement and combo flow is extremely fluid and feels great and intuitive once you get practice in. +Match-ups seem, at least at face value, mostly evenly matched, and it seems like no character has anything more than a 6-4 matchup on another.+The game's training mode, as it is Skullgirl's heavenly Z-Engine, is amazingly robust and has plenty to work with for practice.+Pixel Lobby system s'alright, and there is a private lobby system as well.+I haven't played the Salt Mines mode yet in the Pixel Lobbies, but from what I've seen and heard it's decently fun+The music in the game alone is great, but the dynamic music system adds to an already great soundtrack. It swells and calms down at appropriate moments, and seems to decently follow the pace of the match. Mostly.+The animations look and feel great on many of the characters and their attacks, and have a lot of personality to them.+The character designs are 'unique' and have a nice artstyle to accompany them.Edit: The first patch has gone out and fixed some of these issues, I've marked them with a @, and moved them lower.Cons!         -Intros and Victories are so horribly bugged and painful, it kinda deflates a victory. Many of the intros will only have 1 character talking, their mouths flapping at random after they finish their line, while the other is silent but mouthing words. Then, an odd pause later the fight countdown will start. Same with victories.     -There is no where NEAR enough lines for characters and their intros/victories. It seems like most have maybe 2 or 3, and some of them will cut themselves off, like Arizona's victory. She has only 3 victory lines, which are all terribly out of sync with her talking, and one of them completely stops at the last line. "Kickin', Stompin', and Ki-" gets real old, real fast.     -While in theory this would be a good and simple game to have beginners in the fighting game genre start with, there is absolutely no tutorial of any kind for even basic game mechanics. Even the combo trials for the game are hidden inside of training, in the training options.     @-Hot damn that AI is a piece of ♥♥♥♥.It's understandable that AI in fighting games are always gonna be BS. atleast in some way, this game takes it back to the Mortal Kombat 3 era of enemies being absolute brickwalls with perfect punish strings. It doesn't help the AI isn't even set to Normal by default, it's set to Competent (Hard, essentially) @The AI is now set to normal by default, and it seems to not be so godly at defense and combos. They still occasionally do insane combos after a punish, but fighting a zoner AI won't make you want to bite through your own jaw.     @-Damage numbers feel incredibly wonky. As Arizona, a standard bread and butter (Gatling>Launcher>Special>Level1Super) does an okay amount of damage, but heavies from other characters seem to do as much as the simple combos I've figured out so far. It's possible this is on me, but it does feel unfair that a single projectile from Velvet does as much as a standard gatling gun combo. @After playing a bit more, I think I figured out what my problem was, I was fighting a mirror match in practice, and Arizona has a bit more health than others, so after optimizing my combos a bit and trying them on other characters with lower health, it looks like they're mostly fine.      @-The art assets on a few stages and characters are absolutely ABYSSMAL. Arizona, on her front fore leg facing the camera on any color that has a splotch, shows that it's almost barely attached to her skin. This is especially bad since her default design has this issue, and colors with monotone colors look better than the default. Some parts of the background stages, specifically the characters, are pixelated to hell and back. @Arizona still has that odd floating splotch, but I can't seem to find any background characters like I saw before the patch with horrible pixels on them.If you're looking for a good fighting game, and you're not stopped by a lack of polish and even essential features, this game will do great as a budget title.

_childDocuments_.review: Very smooth and solid gameplay on par with Skullgirls. Definitely a lot of potential for this one to grow.Some standout positives have been:+ Great animation (with a few exceptions in certain visuals)+ AMAZING soundtrack+ The feel of gameplay is just as good as you'd expect from most anime fighters+ Netcode and the pixel lobby experience has been a treat.Of course this is an early access title and there are some changes I'd like to see made:- This game heavily assumes you have prior fighting game knowledge and can be off-putting to newcomers, as evidenced by other Steam reviews- Combo trials are buried within 3 Training menus, definitely would like to see them in their own mode- There is no proper tutorial when you first jump in. The game's tutorial, as of right now, is pause the game and look at your command list. A proper playable introduction in the vein of Guilty Gear, etc. is essential imo.- A couple of visuals are off-putting. Velvet's Tornado is a moving jpeg. Backgrounds are almost completely static. These are nitpicks, but polish in these areas can go a long way.- The six characters the game has now are quite varied and unique, but I would love to see at least double this roster in the future./ And of course there's the elephant in the room. My Little Pony. I do not like My Little Pony. I am not a brony. I have accepted the fate that if I play this game I will be labeled a brony. I will die with no regrets.I can look past it all. _childDocuments_.review: Overall Impression: 4.0 out of 5. Them’s Fightin' Herds is an inspired, unique, and solid fighter that seems to be aimed at veterans of the genre. While the overall game is a solid buy, it is an unevenly polished product. If you love 2D fighters such as Killer Instinct, BlazBlue, or the more modern Guilty Gears, do not let the cartoon characters and few, but glaring, flaws of the game make you pass this by.Pros: Wonderful, funny, and extensive tutorial.Fast, smooth fighting system that allows for a lot of tactical flexibility.Parts of the story mode are clever, funny, and provide interesting insights into the world the characters inhabit.The small cast of characters have a surprising range to them when it comes to fighting dynamics.  Almost bug free as a whole and solid online fighting match making.Cons: Overpowered AI opponents.Cheap, unfair, and frustrating story mode bosses that the team has had to nerf once already due to even seasoned fighting game players calling foul.The platforming sections in the story mode are not needed, irritating, and poorly designed.Two of the characters allow for some nigh impregnable defensive tactics that can be exploited by human and computer players alike. (Velvet being the queen offender, followed very closely, at times, by Pom.)Overall Impressions:This game is a blast to play with others so long as they do not abuse character exploits. The AI ramps up from 'this is quite easy' to 'knock you flat before you know what hit you' fast, as you change difficulty levels. New players to the genre may want to stay to the lower levels to avoid frustration.While the game has a detailed tutorial for the games fighting system and aspects of each character, unless you put the game on its easier modes, the computer has a tendency to use wipe the floor with you in no time.The story mode is a mixed bag. The bosses are not fun, frustrating, and grind your progress to a halt. The platforming sections are ill designed and seemed to be aimed at being a painful chore that extend the playtime for players rather than adding anything to the game. The humor, world building, and light puzzle aspects of the story mode just make up for the flaws, as long as you have it on easy mode, so the whole story mode experience is neutral. I find this tragic since part of the reason, from what I understand, the game was delayed was due to the team getting the story mode into a working state. The fact that the story mode is incomplete does nothing but rub salt into the wound.Conclusion: If you are looking for a good fighter, Them’s Fightin’ Herds is a good choice so long as you stick with the fighting aspects of it and do not expect too much, if anything much, out of the story mode.  A concern of mine for the game’s longevity: While the Mane 6 team is very responsive to player feedback overall, a couple of complaints about difficulty have been met with ‘get good’ responses. As someone who has beaten Furi, Ninja Gaiden II, the original Xcom, and Ghosts ‘n Goblins, among other 'hard' games, I believe I have enough experience to back my decision to add my voice to those who suggest the game’s AI needs a little tweaking. A small, but telling, issue that I had with the tutorial’s AI is that while training you to launch your foe and follow up with an air combo that the window to do so is almost too small for a couple of the characters. For a tool that is aimed at beginners, it requires too much precision. The platforming sections of the story mode have also garnered a ‘we made it as part of a planned tutorial system that wasn’t implemented’ response that indicates the team knows there are problems, but have done little to fix them. Please, Mane 6, go back to your gaming roots (which are showing), and aim at making things fun for newbies while allowing competitive and hardcore players their options to get the snot beaten out of them as they would like. It is clear you have the talent to do so.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a very stable and neat little game. It has smooth and solid gameplay, both offline and online. The game offers a (in my opinion) surprisingly big variety in game mechanics. A story mode in which you roam through different landscapes in top-down view, ocassionally with 2D jump and run elements and encounters with folks, enemies and bosses at the end of each sub-chapter. These bosses have special story-mode exclusive attacks, which really tops it off and makes the fights more interesting.  The online mode has pixel lobbies in which you can fight it out with other players and even explore caves for chests with accessoires for your avatar in them and of course farm the in-game currency, salt. The only downside to this game is that it (currently) only has six playable characters and also only a single chapter in story mode. Next to that, the online lobbies are not that populated. The current state is that mostly the first lobby is full and the second mostly is empty.Overall, if you like beat-em-ups or don't mind the aspect of it being in the game next to the other elements this game has to offer, this game definitely is worth a try.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent graphics. Fun, interesting characters. AI that cheats like a motherbucker.Don't let the cute graphics, childish characters and dead easy early bosses fool you, this is the Dark Souls of fighting games. When you first fight a champion, even on easy mode, this fact get hammered in *hard*. You are thrown into the deep end almost straight away. The game teaches you nothing of the controls, at least nothing of worth. If you don't spend two to three hours in training mode, have every combo memorised, the characters mastered and already have a decent win streak in multiplayer, youwillnotbeatsolomode.This is not a game to have fun with. This is not a game for even decent level fighting game players. This is for hardcore masochists who want to be punished. Do not buy this game for your kids thinking it is an introduction to fighting games. Do not buy this game because you have some misplaced nostalgia for My Little Pony. Buy this game because you hate yourself.Or better yet, just don't buy this game.Edit: Don't get me wrong, I'm going to keep butting my head against this brickwall of a game. But the game doesn't present itself as being this stupidly hard, nothing about it indicates that it should ever be this hard. I hate games like Dark Souls that punish you for just starting to play. That are nothing but god awful slogs until you get lucky and beat a boss, only to die repeatedly against the next one, without any sort feeling of accomplishment, just the ever building dread that the next fight will be an order of magnitude harder.Yeah, fighting games are kind of like that, but never before to this extent. Bosses don't just challenge you, they cheese like a bad player who discovered an exploit and they exploit *hard*. The AI doesn't key read, because they don't need to, their prediction algorithms are down right *precognitive*.If all of that doesn't dissuade you from buying this, well... there are easier ways to commit scuicide than giving yourself a heart attack out of sheer frustration. But hey, all the power to you.I know I'm building up to one...

_childDocuments_.review: If you can look past the visual theme and want a good fighting game, pick this up. I had little to no interest prior to it's release but I owned Skullgirls(which grants you a discount) so I figured,  for 11 bucks it's worth checking out. My mind was almost instantly changed to loving what this game has to offer from a gameplay and feature standpoint. - Character variety rivaling that of Guilty Gear and Blazblue. Puppet characters, zoners, hyper aggressive rushdown with fly mechanics, grapplers, you name it. Somehow with just 6 characters the game managed to have more variety and creativity than that of Marvel or Dragonball.- More training mode features than any AAA fighter out there. Most notably the ability to save and share combos through files that can be then added to your own game with ease and shown on the screen for you to do. - Better netcode than most fighters out there(GGPO). Gives you actual ping stats, not just ambiguous bars. GGPO then allows you to also set a delay to better accomate bad connections to make it much more seemless than most fighting games.- A lobby system that surpasses that of every other game out there, this ♥♥♥♥ has it's own single player elements woven into the 2d lobby you can run around in. Treasure chests will even appear in this lobby and you can challenge a person trying to open it to see who gets it. The lobbies also feature voice chat and highly accurate ping bars. Which could be toxic and bad for the game, but there is a mute feature and so far nobody has been toxic on the mic to eachother.- Gameplay is smooth and  intuitive. Combos and moves flow nicely and have enough freedom for higher level players to come up with crazy ways to combo without hurting beginners.

_childDocuments_.review: Now before you get off put by the notion that this is just a My Little Pony fan game, just listen... With the help of MLP FiM's creator, Lauren Faust, the devs created a new world filled with new characters with unique personalities.As mentioned before, the colorful world, and it's inhabits, of Fœnum was created with the help of Lauren Faust. All these lovable characters are voiced by a unique cast of voice actor and actress. Also, if ya peeps are curious to know more about the world Fœnum and the combatants you'll be playing as, check out the devs site under the Book of Lore section. But the good news is there's a training mode for newcomers to learn the basics,  the definitions, and mechanics of a fighting game. Also, if there's someone kind enough to do so, there are players in the games pixel lobbies, a place where players can square off and get in game cosmetics, willing to teach a combo or two to help ya get started.While I'll say this game might not be for everyone, I still say this a game worth buying. _childDocuments_.review: I like this game, but, as many others have stated, you will HAVE to turn the difficulty down on the bots unless you are VERY familiar with similar fighting games and are able to exactly press (NEVER spam) controller buttons, or play very well with a keyboard (for some reason I can press the buttons on the controller (wired XBox 360) and get a 50/50 response after a couple hits (unless you are VERY careful about exactly when you press the buttons, it seems to act as if there's a delay of about 100ms after most button presses, which can *easily* wreck your combos if you spam) but this issue is not present with keyboard, from my brief combo testing). The art aesthetic is the main draw (for me, anyways), and the combat system allows for skill and growth to most definitely be major factors. However, unless you can fairly capably beat Normal difficulty or better, you really should stay away from online fights; you will be destroyed. A lot. This game has definitely drawn its number of skilled players, and it makes most fights against them very one-sided. This wouldn't be much of a problem, except that they reward winners with salt, while losers get nothing, and you need salt to get cosmetic items from the salt mines, which you *also* can't even enter without salt. At least *most* of the players are sportsmanlike, but the ones that you come closest to beating (who also lose to everyone else) will more than likely spam-taunt you and abuse your/your character's weaknesses to the point of rage.Furthermore, I seem to be finding glitches that crash my game or make me spazz out pretty bad online (no crashes, glitches, or jerkiness offline, from my experience), which, combined with my lack of proper experience with 2D combo-based fighters such as this, inclines me to avoid online in its entirety for the time being. The single-player currently just consists of Training and Arcade at the moment, and they're adding a Story Mode, which I will be very glad for, as well as at least one more character, so, while I recommend this game to both fighter fans and fans of the artstyle, I think I'll be only occassionally playing this game until the Story Mode is in (Arcade gets fairly stale after about 10-20 times, and being beaten to a pulp too fast to even see where to improve or getting tilted doesn't strike my fancy, either). Of course, if you have friends that will also play this game with you, that definitely would change the whole online experience, so be sure to take that into account, as well. TL;DR: It's a great game, but most average players will have to start off slow and really hone their skills to get the most out of this game before they add Story Mode, unless they have friends who enjoy both fighters and Lauren Faust's artstyle.

_childDocuments_.review: A great game that is being regularly updated by a dev team that really cares to make the best possible game and a very lively, passionate community of players who are FAR better than I am at the game. Netcode is great bar very occasional hiccups. I adore the character designs and the animations. The contextual taunts at the beginning of matches are a wonderful touch. Online lobbies are easy to navigate, though I usually play the Pixel Lobbies. Not a big fan of dressing up my character, but that's there for the sort of people who love TF2-style cosmetic items out of fights. Salt Mines, Story Mode, as well as the Tutorials and Training Mode are a great way to sharpen your skills offline. For new players, I'd recommend the Tutorials to learn the basics fast, as Story Mode is still pretty lean on the instructional side of things and kind of assumes you know basic combos. Apart from Story Mode, the rest can be accessed from the Pixel Lobbies while online, so you can practice while you wait for matches.TFH is an all around excellent title that will get even better in the future. One warning: I play with a 360 controller and I would warn that it is NOT an ideal input device for Them's Fightin' Herds. Proper arcade stick is the best option or perhaps a dedicated fighting game controller like a Hori Fighting Commander. You REALLY need to reliably differentiate between cardinal directions and angles as all of the attacks and blocks rely on those specific inputs. The 360 pad will give unintended inputs for days unless you take exceptional care and that WILL cause frustration aplenty and lost fights.

_childDocuments_.review: I fnd this game  hard to recommend and it just narrowly gets a recommendation from me.Based on the skullgirls engine the game runs fluid and looks mostly fine, although it can be a bit jarring seeing static characters in the background of fights but I assume they will be animated in the future and honestly it is a fighting game so we are mostly focused on the main event, which is the fighting itself as opposed to some fancy backgrounds but it is jarring when you first notice it.Which is as good a way as any to start and end this review, a lot of things look good until you notice something weird or jarring, for example every character has a magic meter of some sorts which is not the super meter as you may expect but a seperate meter similar to v-trigger in streetfighter 5 or the auxillary meters in vanguard princess. This seperate meter is important to different characters in different ways and for some it is mandatory that you fill it in order to maximize damage/combos but others can seemingly ignore it altogether.At this point I would liken this game more to vanguard princess and have to call it an "anime fighter" as the focus is on big flashy combos and not on fighting fundamentals, so if you were expecting a footsies game or a projectile war then you are wrong as this is more akin to he who hits first, (and doesn't drop the combo) wins.Unlike skullgirls which featured a combo-breaker system, I could not find one here which was a mixed blessing as I either completely styled on opponents, securing a 35 win streak in the process or I get completely stomped with little to no middle room. Skullgirls had a very similar problem however the ability to break combos at least gave you something to do when you were getting beaten unlike here where you may as well put the controller down and grab a drink.Compounding this issue is weird controller lag/input detection that means you have to input combos immediately without hit confirming first or else they will immediately fail, which is problematic because it means blindly hoping your attack landed. This wasn't an isolated issue either, I have come across quite a few people complaining about this and I know this is not a ggpo specific problem because skullgirls uses ggpo and it manages just fine online for even the most terrible of connections.Infact in the case of skullgirls, it is much more likely your opponent will be teleporting around the screen and the match will disconnect due to being unplayable than your hits and combos will fail. I don't buy the argument that the game is in early access and so these issues will be fixed simply because it has been 4 years of games in early access (on steam) and you just roll the dice and hope the game gets fixed/patched/ but this is one instance where I would hope to be wrong and the final product does come through polished.Hope however is the first step on the road to disappointment and although I have rated the game highly I did mention that it just ekes out a recommendation and that is because we are innundated with fighting games right now so the competition is stiff. If you are a casual you will probably get a few hours playtime that honestly hardly warrant buying the game and if you are a hardcore fighting game player, well, you are being spread very thinly right now!The game comes at a very bad time and honestly this was the best time it could possibly come out regardless since even more fighting games are on the horizon so they cannot delay release forever can they.Back to talking about the game however and it boasts dynamic music although honestly I did not notice it but what I did notice was that the music would frequently cutout, unless dead silence is a part of the music, so there is that. Dynamic music is as old as Phantasy Star Online and that was over 20 years ago, come on guys, sort it out.The graphics, well look at the game, it is a cartoon come to life but then again so was skullgirls and dragonball fighterz so there is little praise I can heap on this game that it sadly is not outshone by from its direct competiton and that is a huge, huge shame because this game feels like it is coming from a place of love.With all that said, you can see the game has issues of which the biggest is the flow of fighting and while you may or may not have liked skullgirls there is no denying that the playerbase for skullgirls was small and if this game follows suit then consider if you want yet another almost dead fighting game on your hands. At this time of this review I found one lobby with 20 people in it and a whole bunch with 1, 2 or 0 and 0 was the norm!Join Grumpy reviews because I am a miserable old man with bills to pay.

_childDocuments_.review: Short review of Them's Fightin' Herds after the first hour I did some training and arcade mode.This is an indie fighting game, powered by Skullgirl's engine. The original name of the project was My Little Pony: Fighting Is Magic. An fan made game based on . They sadly had to stop the project, renamed it and change the characters, that's why the game was delayed. So, what we can find after those changes? A good fighting game, powered by the most interesting and latest 2D fighting game engine created by Lab 0 for Skullgirls.The main system of the game is close to Blazblue. 3 attacks levels (light, medium, strong attacks) and a 4th button for chara spec abilities. I don't remember abilities since I don't play enough, but the cow can throw a losso, the unicorn can charge the super bar, ect...Wait, did I speak about cow and unicorn in  a fighting game? Yes, they change My Little Pony's characters for 4 feet animals. That sounds logical indeed, but there is the originality of the game. Your hitbox is very different of others games, and you have to keep it in mind for your spacing.The only bad things are the soft feels unfinished yet, but it's an early access so this can change in future patches. Some animations are missing, sound can be delayed sometimes, and small things like this. Stages are not bad, but motionless/lifeless. Not a lot of characters for now, 6 playables chars and a boss wich is 4 animals (a bear, a snake, etc...) to beat with only one life bar.But because all of this can be fix in the near future, and because this is a cheap game, I highly recommend to go for it.

_childDocuments_.review: "The cow goes yeee" - Nov 25, 2021---------------------------------Nov 25 2023 Edit:As a long time follower and player of this game, the recent negative reviews have given me a good reason to give my own in depth review.TFH is a fantastic 2D fighter, and could be considered one of the most well-made fighting games of all time. It is more than worth the purchase price of $20 by providing a fun, fluid, and balanced fighter with GGPO rollback netcode and is (mostly) crossplatform. (More on that later.)Within the last week, the developers Mane6 announced that after they release the next two characters of the season pass, they will cease development on the game, except in the case of "game-breaking bugs." As of today, saying that the game has ceased development or is dead is not true. However, this means that the majority of story mode, a goal promised in the Indiegogo campaign, will not be finished. The devs have not given any reasoning and have said they are not at liberty to say anything more. I have followed the devs' communication since day 1, and I know that this is not like them at all. I can only assume they are under NDA from their publisher Modus. It would be extremely inconsistent for Mane6 to want to stop developing TFH or feel no need to explain their actions.Regardless, this does affect the value of the game depending on what kind of player you are. If you want it for story mode, sorry; for the foreseeable future it won't be happening. If you want a good fighting game, it is and will continue to be a great value even after active development ceases. The devs always intended for the game to be playable even after they are dead and gone. Fights are peer-to-peer, and lobbies can be hosted by anyone. Unless they fix crossplay on independent servers, though; that will only be possible on the game's official servers—the future of which is unsure. The game's playablility will ultimately be determined by you, however. Buy the game, join a discord, get some friends to play with you, etc.; and you will add value to the game. In full disclosure, the game's active playerbase is currently shrinking slowly; but if for that reason you decide to quit or not buy the game, you are only cementing that further.Setting aside this recent drama, let's look at the fighting portion of this game. It's phenomenal!  Visuals and sounds are pleasing with good feedback. Characters are unique with a broad range of playstyles. Combos and attacking are beginner friendly while maintaining a lot of nuance. The soundtrack is amazing and the game has a dynamic music system. Online play is smooth as butter. Training mode has many useful features, and combos + replays can be saved and shared (on PC). The tutorial is also the best FG tutorial out there, teaching universal concepts along with specifics to the game. The community has also always been receptive to new players and there will always be people willing to help.Negatives: A few moves are not visually consistent with their hitboxes. It can be played around just fine but makes some interactions feel bad. That's all I can think of.tldr; Play TFH

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: Since I reviewed this game 2 years ago, there have been plenty of updates, including the long-awaited arrival of Story Mode (Chapter 1, at least), tutorials (including in-depth concepts such as frame data, advantage, and negative edging, which is very useful to newcomers), and quick matches. The cons from this review have pretty much been eliminated, and I am also happy to see this game get a resurgence, _especially_ given the current state of the game. The review below will be left for posterity, but know that it is now outdated. (Also, paprika is _still_ best. {•ᴗ•} )TL;DR: A cute exterior with well-polished mechanics complex enough to be engaging, but not so overwhelming as to be unwelcoming to new fighter players.Pros:+ Built on Lab Zero's engine (Same as Skullgirls)+ Very well done aesthetic and art direction+ Normals feel very snappy and satisfying+ Not too focused on infinite or super-long combos (see: skullgirls)+ Each character has a distinct playstyle and character feel+ Pixel Lobby has a PvE environment to grind out cosmetics for Pixel Lobby (TF2 fans, go nuts)+ Various QoL things, like context menus for pixel lobby on chat with controller, or keyboard chat+ The soundtrack is surprisingly good+ Each character has a well-established personality, and this combined with the aforementioned playstyles make each character stand out and feel uniqueCons:- AI (as of this review) is overtuned, and the gaps between difficulties are staggering- Art is currently unfinished with certain vfx (e.g. Oleander's Magic Teleport) being rendered in animatics- Online matchmaking is limited to lobbies (as of this review)- No story mode as of yet- Extra cosmetics (i.e. Skullgirls, Blazblue, et al.) only are obtained if you have the "full" game (second encore for skullgirls, rev 2 for xrd, etc) [this is in the fine print but just in case people get confused]- No tutorial (however, there is training mode, and there are combo lists within training that you can practice)Overall, the game is very well done for an Early Access title, and I feel like the state of the game can only improve over time. If you are just starting out at fighters, maybe wait until the AI gets fixed, or persuade a few friends to help you learn, but this is a very enjoyable experience for those who are even remotely interested in fighters, while also having enough detail and potential to be mastered by veterans.(p.s. Paprika is best ' ͜ > ' )

_childDocuments_.review: Game was announced and started development in 2013.This game was supposed to be released in 2015 after completing a successful crowd funding drive. They raised enough money even for their stretch goals to add a story mode.It's now 2023 and the game is being abandoned unfinished after a decade with only the beginning of the first chapter of the story mode added.---This isn't normally a genre I dabble in and it's not a storyline I would have invested in (and I didn't). Personally I ended up with a key from a random bundle that cost me less than $1. But since I ended up with it, I'm gonna review it.1. The story for me is nonsense. It obviously has a target audience, I'm just not it. I wouldn't hold this against it really since it's pretty obvious from the store page what they were aiming for.2. The gameplay has two types. Mediocre 2d fighting for the combat and super-basic RPG-Maker style for the story mode exploration. I don't know how a story mode this simple should be incomplete after all these years unless the developers simply flat out ignored the game for most of those years. I've seen amateurs put out RPG maker games like this that were longer and more complete after just a few months, let alone an entire decade.3. Without the story mode (which is what many of the core fans invested in specifically during crowd funding) what's here is a 2d arcade fighter with 4 legged animals. It's OK, but I find myself winning just by button mashing without really needing to put much thought into it other than occasionally blocking. It's functional, but not impressive.As I said, I had no expectations for this, I didn't seek it out and buy it and I wasn't an early investor like so many others. It was just a cheap random key for me. But when I play things I look into them and try to get a broader perspective. I could probably have found an excuse to give this an upvote if it was a complete game. But it's not and with it being abandoned it never will be.The animations, story (what little there is) and voice acting would probably all be OK for someone who enjoys this style and genre, there just isn't much of it. Or rather, it would be OK for a game from the early 2010 time period. It certainly doesn't feel like a game from 2020.I'll probably finish grinding out the achievements, uninstall and forget it exists.---Bottom line: A mediocre 2d Arcade fighter with an amateur tacked on RPG maker story mode that isn't even complete.---

_childDocuments_.review: This is yet another game that is way better than it has any right to be. Similar to Power Rangers: Battle for the Grid just one look at this game makes it obvious what it's based on and immediately, at least in my case, didn't expect much from it. I initially bought it as a joke since another friend of mine had the game. After actually playing it I would highly recommend it to just about anyone, even people that don't really play fighting games. The tutorials are surprisingly good which help introduce players into the game. Additionally the story mode that's available has multiple mini-games and bosses that further help develop new players in basic mechanics.Of all the good I've said, I've yet to mention how the game actually plays. There's good news and bad news to the actual gameplay outside of the learning tools. For example this game makes launching much more fluid than in other fighting games that I've played to the point I do it regularly when before I always stayed grounded. Another thing is how distinct all the characters are with there being clear good/bad matchups between them all, bad news on the other hand is that there are only 6 characters. For a fighting game this is shockingly small. Like Power Rangers I'm quite certain there will be more added to the game in the future and with the amount of depth from each character I can easily see this game being played for a long time even without it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was well worth the multi-year wait for it. The animations are solid, the voice acting beautiful and the fighting fluid and quick. This is definitely a combo fighter's game for sure.Pros:-Music is amazing and the dynamic music system runs almost flawlessly-Pixel lobby is a great way to experience and explore the realms, though I wish there was more to do in them. It's early access so can't expect a huge amount.-Fighting is crisp and fluid, though the characters feel a bit heavy at times. Makes your hits seem sharper and more damaging, but it makes it a bit harder to start and maintain decent combos.-Lauren Faust's designs are beautiful, the voice acting is spot on, and the multiple color pallate options give each character a sense of personalization that you don't get from other games where characters may only have 2-6 colors.Cons:-The game, especially the arcade mode AI, is insanely unforgiving for inexperienced players. Combos can be hard to get started and maintain, and when you are trapped in an AI's combo it ranges from hard to downright impossible to break free without taking around 20-30 hits.- Some content is missing, though the developers are upfront about it and what we have avaliable is well worth the price of admission. This isn't a critism as much as it is me wanting that missing content (Story Mode, Quick Match, etc.)- The roster is small. This doesn't bother me in the slightest because there is so much to learn in the game I could spend hundreds of hours learning and mastering the movesets of the 6 characters. Would I like to see more characters and lore in the future, of course. _childDocuments_.review: Product was purchased by and reviewed for Early Access Watcher.Review of version 0.1 9139McThis game is very flawed and you'd expect 5 years of development to have a bit more polish than what we're given.While the music and graphics don't really do anything for me, but I have nothing personally against it so I won't be criticizing any of those.As an Early Access game, it's understandable that you only have an Arcade and Online mode and a sparse roster of six characters, so my criticisms won't reflect that either.The gameplay is the large issue.Combos are unfilling to learn because damage scaling is so punishing that a 2 hit combo often does as much as or more damage than a 12 hit combo, which also incorporates the aforementioned 2 hit combo. It's entirely possible that damage scaling is bugged, but as of now I have no reason to truly believe that it is.Furthermore, hitboxes and hurtboxes are deceptive. It may not seem like it'd be a big issue but it causes problems since many hitboxes and hurtboxes are deceptively big or small, you may often see yourself going "Wait, I should've landed that hit" or "how did that hit me? The animation wasn't near me."These are my primary issues with the game. These faults may be changed in future updates, but as the game stands now, it's just not a good fighting game.There are better fighting games to spend 15 USD on.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: On November 22th it has been officially announced that there will be no more Development for the game once season 1 is done, and that Story mode is officially cancelled, after lying for years that it was coming. Without releasing a **single** chapter after chapter 1. Its safe to say that this game was a complete scam for most people that backed the game originally. Shame on the developers. As an old backer of this game when it was announced, I personally feel pretty cheated out of what was promised.The idea of the game other than being a fighting game with amazing feel (which it does have), was a focus on the characters and the world. A lot of the campaign to fund the project and updates focused on presenting the Lore of the characters and how they even got Lauren Faust involved to get this all done.However, at some point, they stopped focusing on any of this, Story Mode has been stuck on chapter 1 since the first version of the game came out, and it has received 0 updates in over 3 years. Instead of working on anything related to the story as the fundraiser had originally promised, they shifted their focus on DLC characters and the online PvP. And It wouldn't bother me as much if this hasn't been a thing for years now. Not helping how dismissive and rude some of the developers can be on their own discord server to user feedback.There was clearly a big disconnect between what was presented and what the developers want, as in the end, the game we have right now is for those that are hardcore into fighting games. And the playerbase reflects this: Try to go play online, and you will mostly find pretty hardcore players that will mop the floor with you. In the end, game's fine but incredibly disappointing for people that were tricked into playing it based of the story aspect.

_childDocuments_.review: - Them's Fightin' Herds has been in the making for an insane amount of time, starting out as a My Little Pony fangame, and getting shot down by Hasbro. Until the Mane6 team got support from all kinds of direction, and soon the game resurfaced as what you're seeing now. Well, it took a lot of time to get HERE, but here we are now, the game finally at the 1.0 mark, and EVO 2020 giving it a fair nod for good rollback netcode. But what else is there in store? Set in the world of Foenum, the narrative (and introduction) tell of a distant past when all animals lived together. Until the predators began opposing the herbivores and started hunting them. The greatest champions of each major species fought against the fanged hunters, but it took "divine intervention" to finally seal them away and hide the key to their new "home". But the harmony was destroyed. Filled with fear and doubt, the major species split up and proceeded to take residence in separate places, away from one another. But now, the predators have been spotted again, and new champions are needed to determine the strongest of all, one powerful enough to be a worthy keeper of the key. From that point out, you take control of Arizona, a cattlekind from a nomadic tribe of bovines, who volunteers to represent her people as "Champion of the Prairie". Aiming to find clues about the key and its location, Arizona will travel across Foenum to prove herself worthy, meeting different characters along the way. The story itself is a bit weak, and through its RPG-esque exploration, feels disjointed, since most of the "Story Mode" is spent solving puzzles, fighting beasts, or looking for goodies. To be fair, fighting games are in a tough position with story presentation, since it's not easy to involve all members of the cast in meaningful ways while upholding a sense of rivalry between them. Within that context, Them's Fightin' Herds does a passable job at providing interesting banter between the combatants. Meanwhile, NPC interactions range from cute to hilarious. The game is littered with witty remarks, silly exchanges, and funny encounters, and fill the environments with a lot of charm. The generally lighthearted humour is a good reason to talk to literally everyone and everything multiple times. Of course, this is still a fighting game. And a fighting game needs some good fighting. Which kind of is a problem here. In a good ol' beatdown with a friend next to you or a stranger somewhere on the globe, this is a fun time for a while. The combo system is surprisingly forgiving and, despite the somewhat fast pace, feels very intuitive once you have a grasp of the basics. Them's Fighting Herds employs a control scheme very similar to the BlazBlue series of fighters, in that you have a weak (A), Medium (B), and Strong (C) button that you can chain together in sequence for a basic combo. A Magic (D) button then grants you access to the chosen ungulates' unique gimmick, which shakes up the simple combo structure. Then you also have Specials that are executed with quarter-circle-forward/backward motions in combination with one of the four Action buttons, and Supers that require you to build up a Super Meter in battle. Of course, there are advanced mechanics as well, but those are explained thoroughly in a very comprehensive Tutorial Mode. But there's more than just the classic 1v1 here. Story Mode is mostly traversed in top-down RPG style, pixel graphics included. But mostly means not all the time. This is where the above-mentioned problem comes into play. Every now and then, the game introduces small platforming sections, and these are a bit of a pain. The first few are inoffensive, if boring, but once enemies are thrown into the mix, things get uncomfortable. Enemies cannot be blocked in these platforming segments, since your character turns around instead of blocking when holding backwards, and can easily throw you down a platform to have you starting over. Not to mention how ill-suited fighting game controls are for platforming. But the difficulty becomes especially obvious when you encounter a boss fight. When facing off against other characters as bosses, they generally consist of three back-to-back fights with no checkpoints or healing inbetween. This is already a tad exhausting, but it turns into a test of patience when you're suddenly thrown off by boss gimmicks in the final phase. These aren't neccessarily HARD, but they're a stressful finale slapped onto two rounds of stressful combat. Getting defeated at any point means back to the start for you, and that gets old fast. Generally speaking, there's a lot of room for imprevement here, but it's mostly the single player that suffers from odd design choices and overly punishing encounters. Either placing checkpoints or restoring at least some health between boss phases would be an easy way to counteract the frustration here. Everything else is either fine or related to balancing, and I'm already writing way too much crap. On the graphical end, Them's Fighting' Herds shows a lot of personality. While the character designs are pretty simple, they are full of charm, with loads ridiculously expressive combat animation. Just watching the various ungulates flail wildly, poof up, delivers kicks, and serve headbutts, is satisfying as hell, and makes for an entertaining spectacle without having to resort to massive particle effects. The combat arenas follow suit with nice decorative lements and environmental designs. Some of the unmoving character sprites in the background look a bit awkward, though. The praise also extends to the pretty RPG visuals. While the pixel graphics contrast the combat style a fair bit, they are very well done, and provide some good variety to certain areas. The dungeons are a bit less impressive overall, but still hold up well with their often moody atmosphere. The pixelated sprites are similarly expressive, although various emotion bubbles are also used as expression stand-ins. With little accessories found in Story Mode, you can even outfit your character in many ways, allowing an extensive level of customization. This also being the appearance for the Online Lobby system means there's a lot of cute stuff constantly bouncing across the screen. There's a lot of effort behind the visual design, and to say it's pleasing to the eyes is an understatement. This is where the game truly shines. The soundtrack is a unique affair, in that the music during a fight depends on which characters are engaged in combat. During the character selction, this is already exemplified: each character provides a different main instrument to the song, while the opponent provides a different percussion element. This means a lot of combinations to diversify the multiple songs, and a little different touch to each fight (until you've gone through all the combinations, that is). The soundtrack is a joy to listen to, and further helps in keeping things fresh. The voice work is also very solid. Both established and new voice talents lend their voices to the (currently) six combatants, and while their performance is only available during combat (story segments are unvoiced), they all sound fun and adorable, as it should be for a fun and adorable game.... Them's Fightin' Herds is the result of a committment to a funny idea. By now, it's far more than just a little fangame, but the roots are still noticeable. You feel the years it took to get to this point - for better or worse. It suffers from inconsistencies and odd difficulty spikes, but has a very strong foundation to work with. I certainly hope for the best, and despite some reservations, give this game a recommendation. A fun time is still a fun time, after all!

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not going to pretend to be good at this game(or fighting games in general). But having said that theres still fun in this game to be had, even for a casual player whom may have never been into fighting games before (such as myself). Between the charming charters and quirky dialogue the game just oozes with charm and personality that can make even losing occasionally bring a smile to my face just to hear different characters quips. Though that's not to say the game is shallow, far from it. Like any good fighter their is depth in how characters play and have to change play styles between different matchups(though i'm probably not the person to speak too on all those intraciese, but as someone whos just a passive observer I can tell you I can even see a few). All this is to say if your looking for something to sink your teeth into and practice to “get good”  without worrying about the frustration failure this is a great game for it, as the community is nothing but kind and will provide dozens of helpful pointers(while kicking your a** of course). Whether it be against bots, people, win or lose you're sure to find enjoyment. It truly does feel like a passion project of people whom have a clear love for their product. The only game I can think of that manages to do this same thing is Team fortress 2(in reference to how community and the charming nature of the setting can help stop frustration and make it fun to learn). P.s: while i'm in the subject, give this game “the best soundtrack”, it really is a banger, really listen to it yourself if you haven't heard it. I can think of few other game soundtracks I love as much as this, plus the deves deserve some kind of acknowledgement for the hard work they put into this wonderful game.

name: The Outer Worlds
detailed_description: The Outer Worlds is an award-winning single-player first-person sci-fi RPG from Obsidian Entertainment and Private Division. Lost in transit while on a colonist ship bound for the furthest edge of the galaxy, you awake decades later only to find yourself in the midst of a deep conspiracy threatening to destroy the Halcyon colony. As you explore the furthest reaches of space and encounter various factions, all vying for power, the character you decide to become will determine how this player-driven story unfolds. In the corporate equation for the colony, you are the unplanned variable. KEY FEATURES The player-driven story RPG In keeping with the Obsidian tradition, how you approach The Outer Worlds is up to you. Your choices affect not only the way the story develops; but your character build, companion stories, and end game scenarios. You can be flawed, in a good way New to The Outer Worlds is the idea of flaws. A compelling hero is made by the flaws they carry with them. While playing The Outer Worlds, the game tracks your experience to find what you aren't particularly good at. Keep getting attacked by Raptidons? Taking the Raptiphobia flaw gives you a debuff when confronting the vicious creatures, but rewards you with an additional character perk immediately. This optional approach to the game helps you build the character you want while exploring Halcyon. Lead your companions During your journey through the furthest colony, you will meet a host of characters who will want to join your crew. Armed with unique abilities, these companions all have their own missions, motivations, and ideals. It's up to you to help them achieve their goals, or turn them to your own ends. Explore the corporate colony Halcyon is a colony at the edge of the galaxy owned and operated by a corporate board. They control everything... except for the alien monsters left behind when the terraforming of the colony’s two planets didn’t exactly go according to plan. Find your ship, build your crew, and explore the settlements, space stations, and other intriguing locations throughout Halcyon.

_childDocuments_.review: I planned to write this review a bit later, after I finish the game.But as the game is currently being included in the Humble Bundle this month - I decided to write the review early, to help people decide if this game is for them.This game was created by Obsidian entertainment, the creators of Fallout: New Vegas (and of course the original Fallout games).Which creates pretty high expectations of them from the get go.If we compare Fallout 3 (Bethesda) to New Vegas (Obsidian) - we see that Obsidian are much better in storytelling, side quests and humor.But on the other hand, F:NV had loading screens every time you switched locations - while F3 and F4 contained a huge open world.Looking at this game: it is also an open world RPG in a futuristic setting (which begs the comparison to F:NV), but this time it's also an original IP from Obsidian.And I must say, it fares pretty well.Not perfect - but still, pretty well...RPG elementsFirst of all weapons - there are 4 categories of weapons (melee, light, heavy, long), of each you have sub-divisions (for example: 1-handed & 2-handed melee weapons, light handguns, rifles and machineguns, etc.).In addition there are also 4 categories of damage (blast, plasma, corrosion, N-rays), which can be applies to any gun in the game.Each weapon starts with a basic version, and as the game progresses (and you level up) you can find additional (stronger) versions of the same weapon.In addition, there are "unique" versions of weapons, which you cannot mod, but have special mods already installed.And on top of that, there are completely unique (science) weapons which you find usually after doing special quests - which have unique death mechanics unlike any other weapons in the game.And on top of that - there are 3 mod categories for ranged weapons, 2 categories for melee weapons and 4 categories for armor.And speaking of armor - there too you have variety, with different bonuses and debuffs, and progression over the game.So weapon and armor-wise - you have an amazing variety of different and interesting weapons. And weapon-crafting in itself is a game-within-a-game.Skills-wise, you have several levels of skills distribution you can choose from, when creating your character.During the game, when you level up, you have both skill points and perks/bonuses you can choose from.And every 20 skill points, you can an additional perk/bonus to that skill.In addition, you are occasionally offered to take a debuff, in exchange for an extra perk/bonus point.And on top of that, you also have the ability to redistribute your points (for a small fee) during the game, if you discover you did not distribute well enough, or you decide to try a different build mid-game.So skills-wise, the game also offers a large and interesting variety.In addition, you have up to 2 followers you can take with you.And the followers have bonus points of their own for you to distribute, and weapons and armor they can use.And if you choose to go solo - there are perks that give bonuses to builds without followers.So overall, as you can see, the Role Playing element of this game is very well made, and is one of the strongest points of the game.Open WorldOne the one hand, in open world games you want a big map. And the game is pretty huge here.You have several planets you can visit - each with it's own biome. And each will building or even whole towns you can explore.And some planets you can land on different parts of the planet, and get different maps in each.Or sometimes land in different locations on the same (huge) planet map.On the other hand, many buildings and cities you visit, are not actually part of the same map (in-game) and require loading times when moving from/to them.Also on a less positive side: there is almost no diversity in creatures. Same creatures can be found on every planet.Over all the planets there are only 2 distinct species of creatures (ape-types and arachnid-types). (and 1 more in one of the DLCs) In addition to humans and robots, which can be found throughout the game, but besides being togher in late game (deadlier and harder to kill), they remain pretty much the same (same weapon types, same armor, same loot, etc.)Story / QuestsOn the positive side:This game epitomizes the cornerstone of any Open World RPG - (almost) every quest can be solved in few different ways.You can go in guns blazing.Or talk your way out of a fight.Or sneak in and do what is needed without being discovered.And as an added bonus: More often that not, you can negotiate your reward after finishing a quest (if you pass the required skill checks).And also, as was tradition in Fallout games - this game also has a sense of humor.There are plenty of easter eggs scattered about in the world.And in general - many of the quests have a funny side to them.Now to the less positive side, I've seen mentioned in other reviews as well.The plot/story here is simply weaker than Fallout. I'm not sure what's the reason. If the world is just less interesting because it's too much apart from ours.Or maybe the writing is not as engaging. Or the factions are not very thought out.But the bottom line is - as much as I enjoy the RPG-style gameplay of the game, the main story itself does not feel engaging to me.The factions all seem like ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ - and don't make me want to help any of them.And there is simply too much text terminals. Every large rooms contains at least 1-2 terminals, and some even 5-6 terminals. And each terminal has several messages (half a page long on average) - so in an average location that's dozens of pages of text to read.And 95% of them are just superfluous text, that adds nothing to the plot.At some point I just stopped reading them altogether. I'm pretty sure I missed some jokes, and probably some dialog options for talking with people - but that's just too much text to read.Some additional nitpicking:At least in the original release - the graphics seem very cartoony. Even too much so.A serious Open world RPG, needs to have a serious look.You can't look like a $10 indie game, and expect to be taken seriously.Also stealing mechanic is not very well implemented.Stealing / Lockpicking / Hacking has almost zero repercussions, and are very easy to perform even if you're playing a completely non-stealthy character.It's so easy - it takes all the fun out of stealing :(After I already had around 20 hours in the regular edition, I upgraded to Spacer's choice edition - and can attest to the differences between the two.The new edition has much better graphics. Not just better resolution, but many graphical changes.The people look much more realistic (to the point that some have completely different faces), planets have additional huge structures in the background, which make them look much better. And other minor changes as well.It does come with a cost though. It definitely takes up more GPU resources than the original, and some people have reported bugs & crashes (although I must admit, in my 40+ hours I have not encountered any)In addition, the new edition has more/better Steam achievements.And the game itself is slightly more difficult - when playing the same difficulty level as the original.Overall I felt the new version was the better version, and having the choise - the one I prefer to be playing.But that may not be the case if you have an older/weeker GPU...The game has 2 DLCs (for which I will post reviews separately):Peril On Gorgon - Has a whole new map filled with enemies to kill. And an engaging story (better than the main plot of the game IMO). In addition, this DLC has more skill levels, and more bonuses (for the higher levels).Murder on Eridanos - I have not finished it yet, but it's a kind of a detective mystery. With some new creatures and fun guns to try out.

_childDocuments_.review: My first playthrough of this game was on the Gamepass (2019) and loved every minute of it. So much so that I bought the ultimate edition on Steam and played through the game again while playing the dlc for the first time. This game is Obsidian at its best. Rich characters, incredible environment, and some very impressive graphics. I love that this game is a hybrid FPS RPG as not to many games come out as that and as a fan of both genres I can sink hours into a session without even noticing it. The RPG elements are pretty deep but Its not to intense. And the shooting is spot on for me. I even wish sometimes there was more of it but I like how you are rewarded more if you think your way around situations instead of going in guns blazing all the time. _childDocuments_.review: Very steep learning curve at the start - you can tell you are making important decisions about your character right from the off, so it's worth goggling beginner tips on skill stats, perks, and also constantly saving your game manually before talking to people and also after modding inventory and looting gear because if you die you have to repeat everything you just did all over again otherwise. Get involved with every NPC you see (everyone with a proper non-generic name) and STEAL EVERYTHING you see (as long as you're not in line-of-sight) because you can get rich quite quickly in doing so. Lastly, you'll need as many dialog skill points as possible because the conversation options are delightfully complex and it's impressive how colourful you can be in conversations and still ultimately get what you want (BIG decisions often aren't quite as binary as you'd expect) - for example, you can solve many issues without using violence if you have the skill points.

_childDocuments_.review: From the very beginning, I was hooked. _childDocuments_.review: If you go into this game expecting Fallout in space your going to disappointed. Its fallout like, shares a lot of its DNA and mechanics, but it isn't the same style. its also not as big, and there are a lot less types of enemy's and guns to find.I went into this thinking it was going to be a fallout game and originally didn't find it very appealing game play wise. I started to play it more so I could get thought it to uninstall it, but fond myself enjoying it more and more once I stooped trying to play it like a fallout game. This mostly meant that I stopped trying to stealth snipe everything, and relied more on tactics and companions. What you do with stat points matters a bit more, but overall isn't as granular as fallout, and tells you everything it does. From what I have found, lock picking and dialog options are some of the more common checks you will run into, so having higher stats in these is desirable, but you can still get and do things in other ways. Guns have limited verity, but come in different variants that indicate what there starting level is. upgrading stuff takes more bits each time, but is dependent on how many upgrades it has. a level 32 items first upgrade cost is the same as a level 2s upgrade cost, so you will end up changing up gear once you find better versions of them. There are also mod slots on guns, and mods to put in them (usually about two to thee options per slot), and engineering skills makes these both easier to find and to use. there are are 5 different element types a gun can use: concussive, plasma, electric, corrosive, and N-ray. the most common are going to be the first three, but you can mod things to change there damage type anyhow. N-ray is basically Slag from Borderlands 2, and has an infecting radios to spread. It is probably my least used type.Unique guns and armor exist, but for the most part are the same models as the normal varietals, and are pre modded. Some of them are just normal guns with high quality mods installed, or have a minor difference from a gun of the same makeup mod wise, such as increased critical hit, less recoil, or a different shot package. Some are a bit more unique and do extra effects or have mods you cant find otherwise. Many are not as exciting as a unique in fallout or borderlands,  with the exception of science weapons. this version, and hard to find one of a kind things, do very strange stuff and effects. they are all unique models as well. I think my favorite is a goo loncher that turns off gravity. there are only a handful of these, and a few more in the DLCs, but they are interesting. it also scales off your science skills rather then normal gun skills, so its a way for intelligence based builds to do damage still. Each gun type fits into light, long, or heavy, and take light, heavy, or energy ammo.You also have a time slow ability that is pretty neat and can be upgraded to do more damage. its similer in effect to vats, or at lest cats of fallout 4, but works better. you can see a readout of enemy data if you scope over them, and at later levels can unlock the ability to do body part specific damage.Enemy veriety is also limited but has a number of factions and monsters. each planet isnt very much diffrent other the color pallet and armor type, but some monsters are more common on one then the other.The maps and planets themselves are interesting. rather then having a large open world map, its a smaller "open" world section that you can travel to in your ship. you move the base with you and then get to explore. there is still a lot of empty, open areas between points of interest, and a lot of it blends together, but its a nice approach. All in all, its a rather good game. it can feel pretty short however if you are not doing all of the side quests.

_childDocuments_.review: Firstly I will mention that I played this game on launch through Xbox PC Game Pass and did a full play through, so the 3.5 hours on Steam does not reflect my overall experience with The Outer Worlds.The Outer Worlds is an excellent game in similar veins as Fallout 3 and New Vegas but more linear.  It has excellent story telling with interesting lore and great humor and plenty of interesting characters to interact with.  The gun play is a lot like Borderlands but a bit more refined in my opinion, and the melee weapons can be really fun and unique.  Armor has lots of variety in this game and some of the special armor is really powerful.  The gear can be modified and upgraded a lot as well.The Attribute and skill system in this game is not quite as in depth as other games similar to it, but has enough choices to create a character to your liking and play style.  The solar system travel in this game is interesting yet simple (Point A to point B), leaving more to be desired.The graphics are fairly good, but the art style is truly beautiful with so many things to look at, especially when on planets that sustain life.  The overall combat in the game is fun, albeit it very similar to fallout with similar features such as time dilation (VATS from Fallout) and companions to run around with whom you can equip with the gear you acquire through the game as they level up with you.The game has 4 difficulty modes with the most challenging one being Supernova, which can be really easy to die in early on.  In this difficulty mode numerous things can happen, such as injuries and broken limbs, and permanent death for your companions.  Sleep is important in Supernova, as is keeping hydrated and eating food, as you can die without either of those 3 things.The rest of the game you can find out for yourself, but if you like Fallout games or other similar games, then you will likely enjoy this game.  It has it's faults no different then other games do, but I would suggest giving it a try.The Outer Worlds gains much of it's strengths from the style of Fallout games, yet not different enough to stand on it's own as a true innovator due to not doing quite enough to separate it'self from it's predecessors that set the bar for this genre.I give this game a generous 7/10 score.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: If you want a pretty good choice-driven, first-person RPG, I think you will enjoy The Outer Worlds.  I really enjoyed the dialogue and social side of this game, it is among the best in any RPG I've played.  The game gives you near unlimited freedom to make choices, and has consequences that feel appropriate.  If you want to kill quest givers, you can.  Hell you can murder every single person on the playable space of a planet, and the game can account for that.  It's very Fallout: New Vegas in that regard, and I love it.  However, the writing isn't great.  This is far from Obsidian's best work in that regard.  The game also feels surprisingly lacking in content once you get about halfway through.  I can definitely understand why many New Vegas fans would give this a negative review, because it's very lacking compared to that game in many ways (such as theme diversity, writing, companions, and world building.)  Judged on its own, it still has issues, but I think it is a quality experience.  It certainly was worth my time and money, even if the game failed to blow me away.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: I can see the parallels others have drawn when they say it's like Fallout New Vegas. TOW is a lot of fun, so far. It's about as addicting as the Fallout games. Which I've sunk 100s of hours into over the years. Let's get to the meat of the game.Pros:* Beautiful game - vivid colors, creatures, and environments * Story seems interesting thus far and so do the people you meet - companions are unique with diverse back stories * Lots of different loot including guns, armor, and consumables * You can give your followers armor and guns along with upgrading them as you level. You can also customize their behavior in fights whether that might be stand back and snipe or get up close and beat enemies with a baton * Many different side missions and quests along with lots of secret areas with hidden containers filled with loot*TOW's equivalent of the VATS system is pretty awesome, it's basically Max Payne's bullet time Cons:*Even though there is a lot to see, I feel like its quite dead in some areas. Very little wildlife or enemy activity. I haven't noticed yet like patrols of enemies or even friendlies walking around (this might be because I'm not far enough into the game) but still its pretty quiet as you are exploring most areas *So far I've noticed it seems like your character's dialogue makes you seem like a sarcastic and emotionless prick. I like playing the good guy in RPGS at least in the first play through, but so far I feel like an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ when I say anything*I did mention in the pros lots of loot, but this is also a HUGE negative in my opinion. There is SOOO much useless crap, that's only useful to pick up and sell. *There isn't a crafting system, you can tinker with weapons and armor, but all that does is add a minor bonus for a fee. So, with all this useless crap I previously mentioned, you can't build anything with it. *All the consumables in the game are pretty worthless, I've never had to use a single one besides the main health item. I guess my problem is they are just wasted weight in your item bag. I'm still in the early stages of the game and this is an early review. But I wanted to make sure everyone knew while the game is 50% off on Steam that's 100% worth it. I've been enjoying myself so far. Now things could change, but I highly doubt it. I will add or revise my review as I've played more of the game. FYI, I've read the negative reviews and I don't see their complaints. The game runs fine and there just aren't many things to complain about at this point in time. So, with that being said GO BUY IT! Enjoy!!

_childDocuments_.review: Short Summary:I really enjoyed this game and had a lot of fun. There are some flaws that I would like to see adjusted in future games but would buy an Outerworlds II. Keep in mind that the game is extremely short even with the DLC, and should be bought on sale if possible.Below is a in-depth look on some cons and pros of the game. I tried to focus on some unique aspects of the game did well and poorly with instead of pointing out what most people have probably said. Pros:> Fun and "life-like" side companions and NPCs.Both your companions and NPCs actually have a personality. Some of them are 2-dimensional but it is better than most RPGs I have played. One thing that I really loved was the interaction between all of the NPCs in the world. For example, you will be talking to an NPC about a quest and then your companion will chime in with their thoughts. They will also interact and greet NPCs that they know personally instead of acting like they never existed. Your companions will also give their own opinions during quests and express whether they agree or disagree with your decisions. > The worlds were interesting and a lot of fun to explore.I never found myself getting bored, even on wastelands such as Scylla. You can tell they really put their all into creating unique environments for each planet. I wish the worlds were a little larger or we had more of them, but the ones that are there definitely make you want to explore and learn all of their dirty little secrets. > Too short. This is both a con and pro. Pro: It doesn't overstay its welcome and get stale; Con: I want more, dammit!> Gorgon DLCI think that this DLC is necessary for end-game play since it unlocks another world that is extremely overpowered (which you are by this point). The story is slightly predictable (and confusing) but still keeps you interested. The world is fun to explore and does a good job trying to kill you.Cons:> Too many "cut and paste" enemies. It has the same problem as a lot of other RGPs where you fight a wolf in one area, then go to another area and fight the same wolf with a different skin. They explain why enemies are the same within the lore but it does get a little tedious killing the same primal over and over again.> There is a story issue near the end. If you decide to go against the corporation you'll become the enemy of Byzantium. This doesn't sound too bad until you realize you have story related quests you need to do within Byzantium and cannot walk two feet without getting shot at. I ended up just committing genocide so I can finish the story.> The end game boss.If you are a sneak-based sniper character who didn't put most of their points in lock-picking, then good luck! Without a 100 in lock-pick, you are forced into one of the toughest fights in the game that will wreck this type of player. > Missing DLCAs of March 2021, the final DLC hasn't come out. I feel like buying the all access pass at this point is a waste and a scam.
