_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: If you liked Fallout: New Vegas, you'll get a lot of fun out of this too. You can easily get 30-40 hours out of this, but it has issues. Get it on sale. I highly recommend getting the Peril on Gorgon expansion, it's some of the best storywork in this game.Setting:A rogue scientist gets onto a lost ship floating in space with hundreds of colonists frozen in suspension. He only has the time and resources to unfreeze one of them, and that's you. It's a dystopian (or utopian if you're a libertarian) hellscape where corporations own everyone's life, and their children's lives through employment contracts. Most people barely survive, to feed the elite living in luxury in Byzantium. A group of the biggest corporations form the ruling council for the solar system called The Board. Together with the scientists, you have to go out and save the rest of the colonists and break The Board's tyranny (or not, if you want), picking up side-quests, companions, and shooting stuff along the way.Graphics:The game generally looks very pretty, often. Really gives you the "spacer" experience. However, there are not a lot of different planets to go to, but they still look very similar (except the gorgeous one in the DLC). It's kind of the same trap that most space-themed games fall into. They say you can visit loads of different planets, but they still all look like a brown/green blob. Visually, it's like Fallout and Borderlands, with a good dose of Bioshock, especially in the cities. The characters also look really well in conversations, although the faces could have shown a bit more emotion.Gunplay:Being a Fallout-esque game, you're gonna be in fights a lot. This is probably the most lackluster part of the game, sadly. The weapon variation is pretty low, and the shooting is pretty boring. There is sort of like a bullet-time mechanic, but it's nowhere near as fun as Fallout-gunplay (as broken and dumb as it is). There is weapon-augmentation, but very basic. The enemy variation is also pretty low. You got your crazy bandits, bug-monsters, robots and monkey-monsters. That's pretty much it. There are some cool melee weapons and some crazy "science weapons" /which require you to spec into for them to do any damage), so to maximize your fun, I would advice one of those builds. Gameplay, dialogue and choice:Being a Fallout-esque game, dialogue is going to be a central aspect of this game. And this is where it has it's strength. The voice acting is pretty solid through and through and the dialogue is mostly very well written and often quite funny. But it's funny in a very dark way, since the setting is so dystopian. It also has the computer files you can read, that we all know and love from Fallout, and they're also very well written. The companions you pick up go from very interesting to completely forgettable. Each companion has their own questline. The two first, you pick up, Parvati and Vicar Max, are by far the best ones. Parvati is an asexual lesbian engineer, who falls in love with another engineer and has you set up the perfect date. Max is a vicar in the corporate propaganda religion, but struggles with his faith and the meaning of life. None of your companions can be romantic partners, which is honestly refreshing. Also, this game doesn't have a dialogue wheel, like in Mass Effect or Fallout 4, which is great.The game takes a dive into different ideologies and looks at life. However, I wish it went a bit more in-depth. For instance, on one planet, two factions are fighting: one is a company that was pushed out of the board. The company isn't completely horrible to it's employees and tries to do good for them, but they're under embargo from the board and can't afford providing very much for the employees. On the outskirts of town, the former partner of the CEO went his own way after an argument and has now formed a sort of anarchist militaristic cult. He thinks he's better suited to run the town. You have to decide what to do, and get to have conversations with them about their ideologies. My problem is that it doesn't really go deep enough. I have conversations about the fundamentals of these ideologies that I don't get to ask. This game has been held up as some sort of scathing criticism of capitalism, but it really isn't. It doesn't really ever dive into capitalism or alternatives to capitalism. You will never encounter a socialist in this game, and you don't really get to be one yourself. This game has loads of different endings (although they are mostly variations on about 4 basic endings), but none of them end in a fundamental change of the economic system.This game also handles the choices where there are no clear cut answers and where you can see benefits and detriments to the different solutions. This is seen in the first major choice of the game compared to the first major choice in Fallout 3. (LIGHT SPOILERS FOR THE FIRST MAJOR CHOICE IN BOTH GAMES). In Fallout 3, your first major choice is to either nuke a city, or help them. In The Outer Worlds, the first major choice is about where you want to supply the power. There is a small town, where people are literally being worked to death and there is a plague. The robots in the power plant went haywire, killed the workers, and now no one can get in there (although it is heavily implied that the robots went "haywire" on purpose so that the corporation owning the settlement could collect the insurance). There is also a very enviromentalist faction that has formed a settlement in the outskrits where their leader has managed to spread some plants and returned nature somewhat. The settlement is mostly made up of deserters from the town (quitting your job is punishable by death) and they grow their own food and seem much happier. The leader of the corporation in town wants you to divert the power to the town, destroying the enviromentalist settlement and the nature there, hopefully leading the deserters back to work, so they can raise productivity and make the lives better for the inhabitants, but you don't really know if that's going to work. The leader of the enviromentalists wants you to divert all the power there so she can continue her work, however, this would render the town out of power, making lives worse for a lot of people who can't make their way to the settlement. She also gives off a vibe of wanting the town to suffer. There was more detail in the game, but this choice was actually very difficult.Overall, an enjoyable experience, but clearly has some issues and could go much more in-depth. I'd give it a 7/10, buy it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: The game has so much dialogue that I don't care for. It wants to tell you how bleak the world is where everyone are enslaved and owed their lives to corporations. But, these themes, these characters, these people, they are trapped inside dialogues that are just . There are no exploration in this game, just objectives and checkmarks. NPCs exists for the sole purpose of giving you quest as if you're the center of the universe or something. Really breaks immersion especially when no one actually seem to give a ♥♥♥♥ whether you do them or not.Even the combat is boring, like the enemies are just there for you to shoot and kill. I don't know if this is about the AI, the enemy placement or whatever that made the enemies feel soulless, but something feels wrong and it didn't make the game any more fun.Guess I just expected too much out of this game. It's really not something special.

_childDocuments_.review: What gives me the right to write a review?I beat it on supernova class without following the online guides.What do I have to say?This is downright one of the best sci-fi RPG games ever made.  It's not truly experienced though until you immerse yourself in supernova mode.  Without eating the food, drinking the sludge, and getting intoxicated by the hundreds of boosters you don't get what makes the NPC's tick.Until your butt is on the line and your friends may die do you take the battles and the looting seriously.  It's missing some elements I'd love in a deep and rich RPG, such as a romance system, a smarter opponent AI, less exploding barrels, and a better bartering system.  With 121 hours into the game and 40+ of them in Supernova mode I can tell you that you will replay this game and enjoy it every moment.Can't wait for the sequel!!

_childDocuments_.review: It is more or less neutral for me. I am on the verge of not recommending, but mostly because of high expectations. Visuals are beautiful, but often so painfully colorful, that the head starts to ache. Dialogs are witty and fluid, but the story is almost bland. The satire of space capitalism is so acidic you stop taking it seriously, and yes, satire is expected to be taken seriously, this here is slapstick comedy.Some people, me included, like playing dress up with characters. Here, armors all seem to be either robotlike or slapstick (MoonMan hat is probably the top of it). So, no dress up here either. RPG elements are bleh, skills are neither original nor very useful. No minigames for lockpicking and hacking is disappointing. Contents of documents and terminals are boring.Hm, how am I still giving a thumb up? Because it is overall engaging space opera, somewhat worse than Mass Effect, but definitely playable.UPD: Since I've played Murder on Eridanos, I can only confirm my previous assessment. The plot is ridiculous. It is silly but not funny at all, and some elements, painfully visible on the screen like the critical infestation by alien parasites only can be discussed after a couple of hours of "investigation"... It is definitely not worth the money. And reused faces makes it hard to remember, whom you are talking to. I still  recommend the game, but there were no lessons learned in making the DLC. Gorgona seems a bit toned down in comedy department, but I have not finished it yet.UPD2: Gorgona is indeed less silly, but the dark tone of the narrative is not supported by the actual story and visuals. It is just too cheerful to make a player feel the suggested creepiness.However, the game has some replay value - there is an atmosphere of alien planets and space, that can be experienced at the expense of following the plot.

_childDocuments_.review: Playing the Outer Worlds was a lot like paying for a Ferrari and getting a Honda Civic. It still gets you from A to B, but at the end of the day you are left wondering why you paid top-tier price for mid-tier performance. The story had less depth than a bathtub, the side-arcs were about as exciting as cold oatmeal and Obsidian still stubbornly refuses to properly optimize its games so as to prevent infuriating micro-stutter while in open areas (looking at you Monarch). Also I'm not sure what your creative team has against in-game romances, but it makes your games ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and really shows the lack of talent present in your studio.TL;DR: Wait for at least a 75% off sale f you want to play this. It just isn't worth 80 bucks.

_childDocuments_.review: I was so hyped for this game, but in the end it just turned out to be as average as a game can be and perhaps in some areas even worse. Didn't buy it first because of EGS exclusivity and now I regret that I did.My first gripe is the weapon levels. I thought we were over this BS. How can a gun have levels?It's one thing that in a fantasy game a sword can be made with better materials, imbued with magic, etc...This whole levelling system makes skill points pretty much useless and mods as well, just go and tinker the s**t out of the guns or buy a higher level one when you can. Problem solved.3 ammo types.4 weapons slots and 3 ammo types just shows how they try to peddle the melee combat.Yeah, because bringing a knife to a gunfight always ends well. I know it's the far future and everything, but how do you put the same ammo into a shotgun and a pistol? Shortcuts, that's how.You can't go and use a pistol and a shotgun as you will eat the same ammo with both and after the first hour you realise you are out of ammo.Armour.It consists of 1 suite and an head piece. That's it.No mix and match. No boost for putting on same faction stuff. No mistaking you to be an enemy when you waltz in to a city with a full marauder armour on with the helmet hiding your face.Consumables.They litter the whole world, but never felt the need to use them. Giving personality boost for 20 seconds? Useless...All of them.Small, but empty world.The places you can go on a planet (a whole planet) is very limited and they are small. Small settlements cluttered here and there, but nothing out of interest. And the worst part is, that it is empty. A lot of crap around you, but somehow it is still empty. Enemies are scarce and a lot of buildings are closed, so you can't even go in. And the ones you can go in, they are either mission related or just asset flips. Why not just make everything an asset flip then? Wouldn't make any difference at this point.Story is bland.The BIG BAD CORPORATIONS ARE CONTROLLING THE WORLD!!!!How original is that? Not much.There are a couple good parts where you can feel the negative side of your decisions, but in general it's bland. It's so bland that I don't even bother to read the terminal logs if there are any. Fallout games (not 76) were oozing with story on every corner. Every terminal, diary and letter had a lot of stuff to tell about the people writing it.Characters look and sound bland.Besides all of them looking the same, they have nothing interesting to say.Old characters look like a young actor who was made 30 years older by a makeup artist.None of them are interesting and most of the time they are annoying as hell and listening to them makes your ears bleed. At least you can kill them if you feel like it.This game was piggybacking on the success of Fallout New Vegas, but it doesn't come even close to it on any level. Which is bad as the world has so much potential.And besides this it's not even an enjoyable FPS.

_childDocuments_.review: The Outer Worlds is the Fallout game that Fallout always wanted to be.  The Writing is amazing, truly amazing.  So amazing that I referred to it with a capital letter in the last sentence in case you didn't notice it.  The gameplay is exactly what you want it to be.  I completed it on Hard, and it provided a substantial challenge throughout and the entire time it was an experience worth having.  I have criticisms, because nothing in life is perfect.  None of them are particularly noteworthy and if you're sitting on the fence about this game pay them no mind; they won't really affect your experience.  I recommend The Outer Worlds with no hesitation.  If you hated the experience of the Bethesda Fallout games, give this a miss, if not you'll find more than enough here to enjoy.  So my biggest complaint: The handling of the end.  This is not the first game to do this.  I love games where I complete the story and then I get to wander around in my newly peaceful world tidying up loose ends and just in general bathing in the milieu of the world I've orchestrated.  The Outer Worlds doesn't do that.  There is a point in the game, and I'm not going to truly spoil anything, don't worry, where the game straight up says "There's no going back from this point, save now or forever regret your decision."  It's not lying; There are only two possible outcomes: The end credits or a Game Over screen. The game makes this clear multiple times and ways, you can't miss it.  I respect that they want their story to end and I also recognise that the world isn't built to be infinite, but I also don't appreciate this as a way of handling the ending.Other than that nitpick, I have nothing of note to complain about.  Applause and Applesauce to Oblivion for a(nother) job well done.

_childDocuments_.review: I have no clue how this has such great reviews. It is one of the least interesting, unengaging, and all around boring games I've ever played. I feel bad calling it trash, but it's straight up trash. The Outer Worlds is not a game. It is in fact a collection of poorly developed ideas and mechanics borrowed from other much better games. It has weapon degradation, which never actually becomes an issue. It has crafting so rudimentary it's hardly worth mentioning. It has factions and favor which do little more than slightly adjust the cost of junk at vendors, which you'll likely never buy. There's skills and perks, none of which really matter.You will spent the vast majority of your time in menus and loading screens as you complete quests. Quests themselves consist of little more than navigating menus to select a quest as active, going to the map to fast travel, walking a few meters to a way point, and then fast traveling again. If you're lucky you MIGHT encounter some enemies on your way.Which brings us to the actual gamplay, which there is actually very little of. The shooter mechanics and AI feel like they are out of a game 10 to 20 years older than it is. There are very few encounters with enemies: those that do exist are brief, poorly designed, and unrewarding. The combat is laughably basic, there's some time manipulation mechanic which you'll likely never need to use if you have an adequately leveled gun.This game is bad. So bad.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of FPRPG, you'll love this game. The supernova difficulty lives up to its name. It's the only way to go! This game is porn for anyone with looter OCD. Combat is pretty good, haven't seen many pathing issues with the AI either. If you haven't played this yet, get it when it's on sale next... worth its money at reg price even.50 hours (approx) into current game update: Time for a little critique. Even on supernova difficulty, the game got too easy too fast. I'm trying to wrap up the main quest line now as combat has all become unnecessary for me unless I'm soloing.  In fact I highly recommend soloing in this game and there are 4 or 5 perks to facilitate just that. Minor spoiler, there's a perk that gives a 10 point skill bonus if you never even recruit a companion, 5 if you do but leave them on the ship.ENDGAME UPDATE: took me about 90 hours on supernova to do all the DLCs and finish up. Thankfully, I started getting my butt kicked again in the DLCs, and that breathed life back into the run. I think I could shave at least 25% of the time it took to finish by not looting 3/4 of the time, or just looting bodies and unique items. The amount of loot in the game is superflous. My only other criticism is the 6x scope should've been the one that extended that guns range, not the 2x... Ay considering all that this game gets right, one nonsensical aspect of the game is easily forgiven. GET IT!

_childDocuments_.review: Fun gameplay with a deep, engaging story and lighthearted, tongue-in-cheek humor all throughout. Also has a high level of replayability due to the constant decision making and it's far-reaching implications on the state of the game and outcome of the story. Can feel a bit on the shorter side, especially if you stick primarily to the main storyline. However, if you do all side missions and extras, explore the maps a little, discover and read the various sources of lore, etc it fills out nicely without getting to the point of being too much and feeling tiresome or tedious. Overall it felt like it lasted just around the right amount of time for me (~50 hours) and was very enjoyable from beginning to end. Definitely looking forward to the sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: A very solid RPG, The Outer Worlds is a game I really, really like, but I can't say I love it.A lot of this game is great! The writing is top tier, other RPG elements all handled very to fairly well. You'll laugh, you'll cry, you'll drink Spectrum Brown and throw it back up. The setting is engaging and doesn't require too great of a suspension of disbelief, despite it's obvious absurdity. No complaints on visuals, both in the UI, and in the world.But does it deliver a compelling FPS? Ehhh....Maybe it's the difficulty I played it on. Maybe it's the fact that I kinda ignored several mechanics almost entirely, like the slow-down effect and the defense skills. Maybe the combat in this game just isn't outstanding. I can't point to any real specific issues, it's just kinda standard gunplay, which looks bad in the glow of the shining gold that the rest of the game is. And given that it's most of what you'll be doing in this game, that's not ideal. Beside one or two specific instances, I rarely found any difficulty in the combat, and my build was hardly combat "focused".I would say that this game has some GREAT bones for a new series. In that aspect, it reminds me a lot of the original Assassin's Creed: some serious baggage holding it down, but it's got the foundations of something great. I will be buying the sequel ASAP, because it will either be a masterpiece, or a faceplant, and I think I could enjoy both.I heavily recommend the DLC if you purchase this game. Both are late-game additions, so you don't need to buy them when you first get the game, but, you'll know if you like the game or not by the time you set foot on the Groundbreaker, and if you are liking what you are seeing the DLCs are very good. Peril on Gorgon is an extra 5 or so dungeons exploring the ruins of scientific installation, while Murder on Eridanos is a great romp of a murder mystery, with more of a focus on the skill-based dialogue system.It's a good game, don't get me wrong. Solid 9/10, maybe even 9.5/10 that I can't recommend enough, but I just can't call it great, and I wish I could.

_childDocuments_.review: Nice, solid gameplay with Elder-Scrolls-style combat. Well furnished maps with options for all the gamer types, from sneaky scout to brute force bludgeoner. Well thought out, immersive world, with fun enough storyline, plenty of sidequests, and good humor. The Item + crafting system is a wee on the meek side, though. Missing skip option in dialogues makes you think twice about chatting up your more long-winded companions. The current price is a tad high for the amount of content in a solo game, IMHO, but definitely worth buying for an RPG fan when it's on sale.7.5/10 from me. Going up to 8.5 once the price is halved.Also, the game might grow if expanded properly, let's see if there's more DLC coming...

_childDocuments_.review: It was a fun experience.I've completed most of the side-quests and small locations that were optional, and i gotta say it's been enjoyable.Combat wasn't so bad [atleast the Gunplay, didn't use melee] and it was straightforward.After finishing it , i kinda felt burned out to be honest. I think it's because of the last location and bossfight?Can't really tell, but i didn't follow the Main story that much, i kinda lost the grip on it after halfpoint of the main questline.I mostly focused on Side-quests and optional content which i found more interesting than the main story.As for the gameplay itself , it was quite Challenging. I played on the highest difficulty and there were times i had to step out of the combat and just run away. It was mainly caused by my lack of weaponry that would have good enough Element damage. As far as the gunplay was decent , some enemies were incredibly annoying to fight. Especially the fauna. Fauna was the worst. The main problem with animals and beasts was that they all have some sort of brute force attack that sometimes can one-shot you. They are incredibly tanky and are very fast. But as long as you stay on main road it's not much of an issue.One thing that was really stupid is that AI has very high precision and timing, so everytime you would peek around the corner or enemy would get around the wall, you will be instantly shot, no matter what happens. So in some cases if you played on highest difficulty there was a high chance that you will die by getting one shot because you didnt hit few mili-seconds earlier than enemy who didn't had a clear shot.That was making some of the situations a sure Damage-trade and you had to be prepared with additional heals [which wasn't really the problem because you would get them everywhere].Also i felt like the later weapon designs [different brands] were kinda lackluster. Some of the weapon types were completly trash and barely do anything. For example there was a shotgun from one of the brands that would show up in the mid-game. It was way higher damage and better stats overall than my last gun and even with the gun literally glued to enemies heads, i would do pretty pathetic damage so i had to switch back to the old gun that was under-level to be able to kill anything.Also armors were kinda meh, since 50% of them are just reskins of other company armors. Not really a big deal but still kinda disappointing.What's really shines in this game is definetly the design. The open areas and architecture is beautiful. I really liked the exploration , because there was a lot of variety in the locations. Music was also very thematic and enjoyable. Overall the atmosphere in the game and visuals were very good.As for the story im not going to get too much into it, since i barely remember any of it. It was decent, nothing crazy really.Some of the characters were pretty interesting. But i really didn't follow the companions story, since i just didn't care so i can't tell anything about them. One thing though is that they are incredibly worthless if you not going for companion skills. They would just keep dying in my playthrough because i packed everything to my Weapon handling and damage perks. But i heard they can be pretty OP once you start making those builds.Overall, it was fun experience. Story was okay, the gameplay was not bad. Atmosphere , music and locations really helped me get immersed in Outer Worlds. I would recommend it for people who are looking for some light-RPG FPS game.Wait for some sale and get it.

_childDocuments_.review: This has been the most fun I've had with a game in a long time. _childDocuments_.review: I got both this game and Disco Elysium during the sale and while everyone seemed to say this game was "meh", it's actually much, much worse than meh. I'm about 15 hours into OW and about 45 minutes into DE. The difference in writing is staggering. OW is written with the maturity and competence of a Young Adult novelist, especially given the obvious...let's say "tilt" to characters, setting, banality of conversation, lack of "punch", etc.Everyone already knows that the male/female issue is very present - the women are all variations of Mary Sue and they are basically all in positions of authority, only held down by evil/incompetent men. That alone is enough to destroy a universe. But add on top of that the ludicrous setting where capitalism is this cartoonish evil (that couldn't possibly exist as presented for longer than a week),  and you have all the tact and wisdom of a middle school student hearing for the first time from their public school librarian that money is the root of all evil. Quite simply, the characters and setting are totally unbelievable. They lack all humanity and there is no way the universe could possibly have gotten to this state and then maintained an equilibrium long enough to stay that way.The best case scenario is that they made this game for as little money as possible and pocketed the profit in order to fuel other projects. I'm hoping they just put their B team on the writing because it waffles from blandly tolerable to head-palm cringey.As for the gameplay, it's the bare minimum. Exploration is crap, immersion is nearly non-existent (the ease with which I break into people's houses while they literally watch me is pathetic) and combat is...fine I guess. The enemies zip around so quickly that aiming and shooting at them is terrible, which is pretty obviously why they give you a bullet-time button. It would have taken actual effort and money to animate smooth-moving NPCs like other games have (Far Cry, Red Dead, etc).Pillars of Eternity 2 might be the last good game from Obsidian. What a damn shame.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: The Outer Worlds is a fabulous and well written RPG. I highly recommend this to anyone who enjoyed Fallout New Vegas. The main quest line is short which is why when played a second time It can provide new ways to complete quests and experience the story. The companion quest lines and input during dialogue felt properly fit to the overall theme and provided further context to the story. The gun play was decent, a step up from previous RPG shooters. Its also worth mentioning that the 2 DLCs  have their own very distinct "vibes" and have solid quest lines as well. 9/10 (Would give it a 10 if it had more depth to weapons, crafting and character building in general)

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game about brilliant but greedy corporations who deliver sub-standard products because of incompetent management and impossible deadlines, made by a brilliant but greedy corporation notorious for delivering sub-standard products because of incompetent management and impossible deadlines.That isn't actually a joke. The first DLC - Peril on Gorgon - is an intense ultra-violent meditation on how a confluence of bad management, impossible deadlines and total lack of concern for the lives of employees/customers can come together to produce a disaster so much bigger than the sum of its parts. I seriously think the writer was working out some game development trauma writing it.The Outer Worlds is the semi-competent first draft of an RPG shooter which copied Fallout 3's homework and set it in space. It has zero polish: the game - nearly four years after release - is still rife with bugs and built on a foundation of objectively terrible design decisions.If you really liked Fallout 3 and have enough brain damage to not notice how poorly-made it is, you will like Outer Worlds. If you didn't and/or don't, then your fun will probably barely outpace your frustration until you complete exactly one playthrough, then uninstall this moderately-radioactive dumpster fire and never touch it again. Note that I said Fallout 3, not New Vegas - which is a much better game than Outer Worlds on every level.Before I get into details, here is a :None of my complaints about this game have anything to do with difficulty. This game was not difficult. I did not have any difficulty beating this game on Hard. I didn't even get the achievement for using the healing inhaler a lot, because I rarely needed to. If you think this is a hard game, then you're bad at videogames. Don't project your stupidity and lack of gaming skill onto me because I criticize the bad game you like.The dialogue is fairly good at times and the voice acting is more than competent. It's not Shakespeare, but it's a step-up from Fallout 3. Again, not nearly as good as New Vegas.Thematically, Outer Worlds is fairly shallow. Expect several dozen different variations of "CORPORATIONS ARE BAD". But occasionally the game poses serious moral questions that are actually intriguing.The worst part of the writing by far is the corporate slogans and jingles and over-the-top goofy "comedy". Your mileage may vary, but I find the Fallout 3 style of blunt-force satire repeatedly slammed into your face undermines the emotional impact - the whole game is basically a joke.This game is NOT a gritty first-person shooter.  My first experience with combat on Hard mode was walking up to a marauder and watching him tank HALF A DOZEN pistol shots to his unarmored face before dropping. Until you mega-upgrade all your gear and invest enough points in your shooting skills, expect combat to be bullet-sponge hell. Again, the combat isn't actually DIFFICULT - it's just tedious.Science weapons are special unique items that scale in effectiveness based on your Science skill, and are useless unless you invest maximum skill points into Science, at which point they become absurdly OP. I tried and failed to find any use for them until the late-game, at which point I re-specced to 150 Science and found that the Mind Control Ray turned the hardest and tankiest enemies in the game into chunky salsa so fast that they barely had a chance to hurt their teammates before dying.Even for a dyed-in-the-wool obsessive RPG nerd, the amount of micro in gear management is INSANELY STUPID AND TEDIOUS. It appears that one half-competent designer outlined a somewhat-interesting level-based gear progression system and another less competent designer who didn't like the idea proceeded to ruin it by implementing it very poorly.Gear is leveled from 1-99, but - with one exception - the maximum you'll get is 41. It appears that the original idea was that you could take starting items and continually invest in them with money so that they keep pace even to the end-game, with a continuing cap of +5 above current level. That would have been a really cool way to help players become emotionally invested in their gear and preserve unique weapons, but somebody in the dev team apparently didn't like that, so the cost of "tinkering" increases at an absurd exponential rate.To put this in perspective: purchasing the absolute best non-unique armor in the game cost me 570 bits. Upgrading my favorite pistol from level 28 to level 41, even with the Science skill bonus that reduces tinkering cost by 90%, cost about 50,000 bits.This was presumably to force the player to buy higher-level gear... which is usually just lazy re-skins of weapons you already had with a number tacked on the end - like "Plasma Rifle 3.0".Babysitting weapons and damage types like a fussy schoolmarm got a lot easier when I realized that no enemy in the game is highly resistant to both Plasma and Shock damage, which both scale in damage with more Science Skill. So - if you're maxing out Science - you can safely ignore the much more expensive N-Ray and Acid weapons.Towards the end-game, I was continually struggling with the weight limit. Then I realized that I was carrying roughly 100 lbs of healing items because I'd used so few of them throughout the game (again to neuroatypicals: THE GAME IS NOT HARD).Both DLC are meaty and fairly well-written, but - like the rest of the game - are implemented like hot anus on toast.The first DLC - Peril on Gorgon - becomes available at the END of Act 2 of the game and is recommended level 25. The second DLC - Murder on Eridanos - is available at the START of Act 2 and is recommended level 30. Read that again and roll your eyes with me.By the time you start Peril on Gorgon, you will probably already have beaten Murder on Eridanos and reached the level cap and have the best gear in the game (unfortunately for the fashion-conscious gamer, this gear will mostly be pink). That means all gear/XP in POG is worthless and any combat is extremely easy. The DLC's increased the annoyingly-low level cap from 30 to 36, but also unlocked an additional 50 points of progression for each skill... while only giving you only 60 extra points to work with. Does this sound like all upside to you? Au contraire, mon frere. In addition to raising level caps and skill caps, they also  to compensate. Several dozen skill checks randomly strewn throughout the game have been increased from 150 for REASONS.Near the end of the game, I did a full respec and made different buff outfits for Unlock, Hack and Persuasion buffs, then painstakingly curated my skill points so I could reach exactly 150 in each of these with any of the four companion-skill-bonus combinations of Parvati/Felix and Max/SAM (meaning two entire NPC's were completely worthless to me). The precious minutes of my life that I wasted doing this will never return to me and I will never forgive Obsidian for that.I'm not a big UI guy, so I'll just make it simple: the interface is clunky garbage and the gear stats shown are clearly rife with bugs. Expect armor/damage ratings for a given item to halve or quintuple depending on which of multiple menus you look at it from.I have played practically all of the western CRPG's ever made, and Outer Worlds is one of the rare few that I sincerely regret playing. Whatever magic Obsidian might have had with KOTOR 2 and New Vegas is gone. Face it: they are never going to release a complete game that lives up to their potential. It's just not in their nature.

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot get over how good this game is. Nor can I wait for the sequel. Pros: -Great story-Lovable characters-Great sense of humor-Quality worldbuilding-Replayability (I'm friends with someone who says she has beaten this game 7 different times)-Good art style-Decent combat-Excellent voice acting-Good selection of perks for hoarders (there's a fast travel while encumbered perk available immediately)Cons:-You won't realize it your first time around, but your choices have little to no actual effect on most dialogue and story elements-There is definitely a combat meta-Weapon stats seem simple, until you find a gun that should be better than what you have but has a lower DPS. That's when you open up the extended stats and realize this game's weapon stats are actually over compliocated. My solution was just to find a gun I though looked cool with my character and run with it.-No 3rd person camera. You can only see yourself in menus or in the idle camera, which is at a fixed angle and rotates slowly around you. -Character appearance is a little lacking, but it doesn't matter because of the previously mentioned point. -The best armors in the game are just reskins of each other with different stats and paint jobs. -For some reason, you cannot remove armor from companions. You can only swap it. It took me a few attempts to appreciate this game, but it turned out that's because I was playing a character that didn't really fit the way I play. The skillful rogue/smuggler archetype is definitely the way to go here. It rewards the most money, experience, and interesting gameplay of any playstyle. All in all, I love this game. I cannot wait for the sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of being lectured about the proper pronouns for robots and computers or really like it when every woman in a game looks and behaves in stereotypically masculine ways this is just the game for you. If you always wondered why not every single female character in a video game wasn't either running a powerful criminal organization or a space station or multi-billion dollar company while all the idiot men weren't either evil or simply incompetent this might be the game for you. If you want a laughably over the top attempt at commentary on capitalism and the free market that strays far beyond parody into the realm of a socialist fever dream you might consider picking it up.  If you work for Kotaku, you will love it. If you can get past the patronizing political and social messaging that you are essentially beaten over the head with from start to finish you will find a mediocre FPS with light RPG elements in the vein of the Fallout reboots (unsurprisingly given it is made by Obsidian.) The gun-play is so-so, the story is derivative and trite. Your companions are boring at best, with at least one of them being tear-your-hair out irritating. "should i ask her out? what if she doesn't like me? I think I am in love with this person I spoke to for 2 minutes and now need you to take me across the galaxy for special things to give her! Also, what if she doesn't like me?" This is the first time I ever decided not to complete a quest line purely out of spite. It wants you to care for your companions but they're so bland and derivative I just couldn't. Technically it is a mixed bag. The performance is good aside from the biggest pop-in issues I have ever seen when transitioning between areas. It's a fairly ugly game. Character models are good, but everything is muddy. It all just kind of bleeds together into this green/brown mess when you are outside of the various settlements. They seem to have gone out of their way to place ample road signs and markers which suggests they knew that the environments were redundant with very little to distinguish one area from another. The overall gameplay is by no means bad. it is enjoyable for the first 10 hours or so, but it wears out it's welcome fast. Obsidian's return is "meh" at best.

_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a huge fan of the Fallout games and I'm also a big sci-fi space nut. So when my son told me about this game, I was skeptical. But after giving this more than 10 hours now, it's easily my favorite sci-fi first person RPG. The graphics, design, sounds, and dialog make this immersive and engaging. The only complaint I have is the amount of clutter in the interface. It takes a little effort to navigate the screens and while there is a handy written tutorial, the interface is simply not intuitive enough for me. But it never detracts from the game too much.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: Well. That was....disappointing. The game is fine, if a little lurid in it's colour scheme. I won't complain too much about the way survival is a difficulty, not a setting (wrong approach - makes survival a bad option). And the gameplay is good - lots of dialogue, very amusing in places. I even laughed out loud a few times! But there is just so little of it! The game is over within a few hours. For a full RPG game I expect more. Less than 50 hours to work through the main quest and most of the side quests is not a game, it is a DLC. I have seen mods developed by hobbyists that last longer than this so-called game. Very frustrating, and with little or no replay value as the quests are essentially linear, and the different role play options fairly limited. As I say....disappointing.

_childDocuments_.review: The story and skills are nice.  The combat, armor, and weapons are good, but not top tier. No throwables, and the level system for weapons and armor is confusing.  There are various recolors of the same thing, higher levels mean higher stats even if it's the same item, and on top of that you can get a "mk2" or "ultra" of the same thing that looks the same, just has better stats.Overall I give this game an 8/10 and you should definitely pick it up if you like RPGs and haven't played it yet. It's almost like New Vegas in space.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: A spiritual successor to Fallout: New Vegas? Possibly. Perhaps more likely the second grandchild of FO:NV, Bioshock, and Borderlands. It had characteristics of all three without their moments of glory. It was simultaneously too short and felt like it carried on too long; I wanted more depth, but I don't know if I would have played MUCH more without getting bored. It is a weird feeling for me. I did enjoy the game, and will probably have a second play through.Pick it up on a steam sale, and be in the mood for an action RPG would be my recommendation. Cheers!
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: The amount of hours I have is not "accurate." I have about 60-80 hours actually in-game. I had to AFK a few times and forgot the game running.This has to be one of my favorite games ever. The DLC story-line alone was worth it. It is made by Obsidian, the same company that made Fallout: New Vegas. As others have said it's kind of a Borderlands 2 and Fallout New Vegas mix. Ended up adoring the characters, wish they had a bit more depth though. Story telling is a 7 to 8 out of 10, would love even more planets, creatures, zones.I most enjoyed how the companions interacted with dialogue with NPCS and even conversed on their own a bit, would love to see more games incorporate that, gave it a bit more of a "real" feeling. Graphically was gorgeous and ran well. I plan to do more "play throughs" on different difficulties and eventually 100% it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: From an avid Fallout fan, and of these kinds of RPG games in general - It's really fun. Kinda generic, pretty easy. But it feels like a classic RPG experience, and the side quests are what fully flesh out the game. Humor got me more often than I expected. Just finished my first play-through in a little under 20 hours, and I feel very fulfilled and satisfied with the experience. Although I think comparing it directly to Fallout does the game injustice, I recommend Outer Worlds massively if you love Fallout 3 and New Vegas. Just don't expect it to be revolutionary.Verdict: Pick it up on sale rather than at full price.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: Would give this a "thumbs sideways" if possible. Buy this if you're really looking to scratch a Fallout itch, because that's what it was clearly made for. The best part by far is its presentation, but as someone who was (and still is) a big fan of the Obsidian cRPGs, I was pretty let down by the hollow gameplay and non-reactivity. I haven't found anything here that really sticks in my brain like their other games, and that's a shame.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: 11 hours in at the time of writing.I like it. Other reviews will do better justice on the good and bad points so I'll let them do that. Instead, I want to talk about one issue I have with the game.It's trying too hard to be fallout new vegas in space. This game has an identity crisis, where it wants to be it's own thing, but it's also obviously trying to grab the nostalgia from new vegas and ride that at the same time. What it ends up being is kinda a sad mix of properties that almost feels like a toned-down borderlands rather than it's own thing. The whole game is supposed to be a commentary on the oversaturation of commercialization, but you don't really /see/ it. Sure, every npc with dialog will tell you how oppressive the different megacorporations are, but the advertisements and product placements aren't any worse than most other games. Borderlands made me hate corps more than this. Hell in mass effect, hearing commander shepard repeatedly mention his favorite store on loop was more annoying - and I know it sounds strange that I'd take "less annoying" to be a bad thing, but it's sort of indicative of the whole game. It's... watered down. Like it's missing part of it's soul.Fallout in some ways has a similar feel, but that's actually fine - fallout is very much about life after death, and if it feels like there's something missing, that actually adds to the theme rather than detracts. I think that if they really wanted to ride the nostalgia train, they should have simply made a fallout clone, like wasteland did. It didn't help that they also marketed this to basically be new vegas 2.0 when it's clearly not a AAA title.All in all, it's a good AA game. Just a shame they felt the need to stick so close to their previous work.

_childDocuments_.review: i feel kinda bad not recommending this game but to me, the thing that made the fun/wacky quests and storytelling in fallout new vegas work so much is that theyre sprinkled throughout. not every single thing i do has to be an SNL skitThe Outer Worlds has most of their quests be full of jokes or just 'dumb haha funny look at that... why arent you laughing' moments. Seriously why should i care about any quest/objective/character when i just spent the last 4 hours finding a tablet, just for the quest giver to say "this is in french? i cant read french!?" haha yes very funny. BUT THATS EVERY QUEST. THAT QUEST WOULD BE A HIGHLIGHT IF THE REST OF THE GAME WAS FINE. BUT EVERY SINGLE QUEST IS LIKE THAT.i said quest too many times. Basically my point is: Imagine in Fallout New Vegas if Mr. House made a fart sound and said his favourite number was 69. thats what this game feels like sometimes. Why should i care about anything happening in this RPG when not even the characters or writers care enough to have a story. oh yeah also the 'planets' are really small. whats the point in scratching the surface of multiple things (having a few boring uninteresting planets) when you could just have one giant map or like 2 that have effort put into them but theres just kinda nothing here. I honestly was kinda surprised how hollow this game felt at times.They clearly put effort into some planets but theres no point in stopping and smelling the roses when theres only about 30 mins of content per place you visit.this is just the very pinnacle of an average game to me. its not bad. its not good. its fine. its just fine and from Obsidian, thats really disappointing.I don't hate this game and part of me feels bad for ragging on it but its MY review so this is MY opinion of the game. Time and effort has clearly been put in, but its been put into the wrong places. There is just genuinely nothing in this game that makes me wanna keep playing. it feels like a chore half the time, and not even a chore that gets something done, because at the end of a chore at least u have clean house or something, at the end of an outer worlds experience/chore, you will always get a dumb joke or stupid twist that makes everything youve been doing pointless or just a miscommunication. It doesnt help that the jokes they make arent even funny, all i can remember is the french example i used above because that one actually made me laugh... because i hadnt realised literally every quest is like that. the devs essentially tip their fedora and say "i did a funny m'lady" before giving u dumb hat as a reward, sheathing their samurai sword and running away.In Conclusion, like i said before i dont hate this game, its not terrible and it does have its small moments. but i feel like it wants me to hate it.

_childDocuments_.review: I've seen a lot of folks comparing this game to Fallout New Vegas and if that is truly case, then I would say this game is far better than NV. In my opinion, NV had real potential but the company put out a flawed product that was riddled with bugs and difficult to play because of that. To the best of my knowledge, the company did not try and patch their problems and if they did it was a half-arsed attempt. Based on that, I was reluctant to play another game by this company. I took a chance with this one and was glad to see whomever was in charge on the NV project apparently had been let go because this game was galaxies better than NV (if you're the type to compare this game to NV). Game play, graphics and overall control mechanics are top notch and worked well! The story line (for me) was intriguing, engaging and adventurous. Companion NPCs were good but in my opinion could've been a bit more fleshed out but overall are interesting and bring color and humor to the story / quest. The overall length of play for the stand alone game for me was perfect... not too long but long enough to enjoy and develop a good plot with twists, turns and mystery. In other words, my character found himself understanding both sides and at times a bit conflicted on the best course of action for the overall good. Fortunately for the hero character I played, it came down to the attitude and overall intention of the other NPCs as to the direction my character chose. Combat portion was good and did not seem to go on and on for ever. However, I did play on a bit of a lower level so as to really let the story be the focus. Therefore, I cannot comment too much on the combat on higher difficulty levels. For me and my "in your face, gung-ho" play style, I thorough enjoyed what combat my character was involved in and how smoothly it was to conduct fire / move maneuvers. There's abundant loot and gear rewards from the combat and simply laying around. Again, this aspect may be a bit more scarce on higher difficulty levels. From what I've read, the game only takes about  27 hours or so to beat. I tend to go slow and look for all the loot and rewards I can find and try to explore as much as I can. So please don't let the number of hours I played mislead you. I play slowly and enjoy going over every nook and cranny the world had to offer. All in all, I'd give the game 8.5 out of 10. I will play again in the future and would recommend giving it a try at least for one play through. Peace and cheers!

_childDocuments_.review: The Outer Worlds made a big splash on release. Even with the whole Epic exclusivity kerfuffle. A cRPG created by icons such as Tim Cain and Leonard Boyarsky and developed by genre regulars Obsidian, would turn a few eyes. I certainly was intrigued. Obsidian having an axe to grind with Bethesda over their treatment regarding New Vegas, certainly added an extra dimension to this story, with Obsidian trying to present this game as a New Vegas "spiritual-successor" of sorts. The next thing to make an impression was how quickly the game disappeared from public discourse. After a couple of months of everyone ranting and raving about this game... silence. Now, well after the game made its way to Steam, the time came for me to experience it and see what the noise was all about.Let's begin with the basics, some story. The Outer Worlds takes place a few centuries from now, near the middle of the 3rd millennium. Humanity, spearheaded by powerful corporations has begun colonising the stars. Great ships, carrying skilled labour in hibernation, are regularly sent out to provide the necessary manpower for the various fledgling colonies. One such colony, situated 10 long years away from Earth, is Halcyon. One such skilled worker, making this long 10 year journey, is you. The parallels with the modern "private" space race and the rise of the megacorp are pretty obvious. Naturally, your trip goes wrong and after a long long time in hibernation you are awakened by a renegade scientist and introduced to a colony that is not quite the paradise that was promised. Halcyon is instead a civilization of the space-western/cyberpunk disposition, ruled by decadent megacorps and seemingly in terminal decline.Capitalism is a primary thematic focus and the game takes an extremely critical view of it. It incessantly parodies corporate practices, makes a complete mockery of advertisement, constantly pokes fun at the endless greed permeating business and so on. The irony of a product with that message being sold for money, relying on advertisement, even going Epic exclusive, was not lost on me. But I digress. The problem is not the message. The problem is that the game takes the mockery too far and forgets that it needs to be serious for a moment too. How are the corpos presented as a credible threat when they are all degenerate buffoons? How are they a faction one would even want to join when they are laughably irredeemable? The game supposedly offers you the option to join them, but why would you? What could possibly narratively compel you to?Playing through the game the question that kept coming back to my mind is how could this social structure possibly last this long. Indoctrination and oppression can only take you so far. The stick can only take you so far. You need some carrot too. You see, by presenting everything as one big joke the game misses the point of why capitalism is all around us. That's because, for many people, it works. Or at least works enough. Both the narrative and the message would have been better served if the game dealt with it slightly more seriously. If it afforded it some gravitas here and there. If the corporations were actually presented as slightly less incompetent. There is so much darkness to satirize in capitalism, but even that darkness isn't enough to ground things when everything is treated as an opportunity for yet another flippant take-that.Moving on, the game's presentation is great. Beautiful graphics, nice music and acting. Some pretty decent gunplay and an interesting, if eventually uneven character leveling system round the experience. The game is quite fun to play and yes the humour is often top-notch. I was constantly smirking at one joke or another. This great presentation would explain I believe the initial enthusiasm over the game. On the flip-side the game went by fast. It is pretty short for its genre and after the initial enthusiasm wears off the issues described earlier come to the fore. The game is vacuous, the plot unmemorable, there is no staying power. Even the NPCs are forgettable, with the exception perhaps of Parvati. The sole exception would be possibly the initial area of the game, Edgewater, there things do have some nuance. But that quickly disappears by the time you reach Monarch. This, I expect, would explain why the discourse over this game went subsequently silent. There isn't much to talk about.I am rather disappointed by the Outer Worlds. Not because it's a bad game, in fact it's a rather decent game. I'm disappointed because it's not a great game and from the likes of Tim Cain and Leonard Boyarsky, from the purported spiritual successor to New Vegas, I expected nothing less. The game falls decisively short of the hype it generated and I doubt it will be remembered much. Nevertheless, if people simply want to have a fun romp and a few superficial laughs at the ills of capitalism without expecting anything deep, then sure this is a great way to waste a few dozen hours. I do recommend it. Afterall, to quote one of the game's companies, you tried the best, now try the rest.

_childDocuments_.review: It was actually really hard for me to decide if this was a thumbs up or down. It kind of gets lucky because if feels most games now don't put much stock into writing characters worth coming back for. Unfortunately for this game, it suffers from something similar to Buffy the Vampire Slayer. The only characters to have any personality tend to be aligned with the plot; and even within them, they tend to be pretty straight forward.What's worse than that is that everything outside of that, is almost completely flat. Now I know Obsidian may have legitimate reason to be bitter against corporate processes and organization, but the game really feels like you're being beaten over the head by a mediocre political cartoon from beginning to end. Because this is easy to pick up early on, most of the game becomes very predictable. In fact, I don't really remember what happened in the game much aside from Max's decent but rushed story arch, and Parvati's cute but visual novel quality drama.I feel like the best work Obsidian has done is more DLC level, smaller tighter packages. Having a whole game to contend with, the overarching story feel spread way too thin, and generic themes used way too often.Gameplay is passable, C+. Everything works, but none of it gets you excited while playing. It's also very unclear about what N-Ray actually does, and how its numbers work comparatively to other elements. It's very easy to cheese because your followers, of which you have two, don't consume ammo. So once I equipped them with the highest dps weapons, even unmodded, most fights were over in 3 seconds.I think I got this game while it was on sale for $25, so about two cocktails plus tax and tip, or one good glass of wine. So worth that. But it's a bit lucky that gaming in general has lost a lot of quality in writing in recent times.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game but dislike it just as much for the jarring end.  The Outer Worlds suffers from a problem that plagues Obsidian titles.  They've created such an interesting and compelling new IP then only gave us content to constitute half an RPG.  Just as the game is really starting to pick up steam and you the player are ready to tackle the multiple unused worlds on the galaxy map... it's over.  I would have preferred to wait another year or two than to have a game with such potential end as abruptly as Kotor 2.  Gameplay is stellar, rewarding and very challenging on 'Supernova' mode.  I only played once, on Supernova and finished in 18 hours.  If you're looking for the next Skyrim or Witcher 3 to carry your gaming experience for the next month or two this game is not it.  You'll be done in a week, maximum.  If you're looking for a quick, fun and challenging sci-fi experience with some compelling and quirky characters then you've come to the right game.  Some highlights for me were Parvati's companion quest chain, anything to do with Sam, and Byzantium.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: Not even nearly finished enjoying this game but its already absolutely fantastic. The reason I felt compelled to write this review was Parvati's storyline, and how important she is to me as an asexual person. Seeing a character so perfectly reflect all of my thoughts, feelings, and worries, explored in such an empathetic way has made me beyond emotional in the best way possible. She is by far the best asexual representation I've encountered in any piece of media, and having the dialog option of telling her that I am the same as her, that I understand - that she's not alone - is healing in some small way; I was able to tell her everything I wish someone had told me. Just an absolutely wonderful storyline, and character, and I'm so thankful for the people who made that possible. I hope they know how significant that is to me (and I'm sure the many other ace folks who played the game).

Combat is simplistic but there are many builds you can try to keep things fresh. All in all I'd give this game a strong 8.5 out of 10.Things I'd add1. More enemy types and tactics, the AI is decent and the enemies we have are good, but there aren't all that many of them.3. I know writing romance is hard, but the fact there isn't any option to have a relationship with any of these fantastically written characters saddens me.4. Proper boss battles. _childDocuments_.review: An excellent but rather flawed first entry into this new IP. There's the amazing writing for some of the folks who gave us New Vegas, but you can definitely feel that the budget ran out as the story meanders and fizzles out during the third act. The Factions are completely forgettable - which is the story's biggest weakness. The main cast is brilliant though; in particular, Pavarti, who is extremely endearing and her personal quest is so bloody cute. I really liked Ellie and Max, with Felix not being quite as interesting and Nyoka is the weakest by a fair amount. They are all entertaining in their own way however. The aesthetic style is also super interesting, with a pulp sci-fi aesthetic, it's almost the antithesis to Star Trek's luxury space communism. The weapons are really cool, but using anything other than the science weapons seems benal in comparison. I see Obsidian really building from this game. The orignal Fallout was far from perfect, and this would likely be the same. A jumping off point. Worth playing if you're a fan of the Fallout games that have something to say. :^]

_childDocuments_.review: I'm giving this game a thumbs up because so far the gameplay is fun, the story is serviceable, and I won't give a game a thumbs down because of one (giant) nitpick.Are there any men in this game with skill? Outside of the guy that rescues you, every capable leader, every capable scientist, every capable engineer is a woman. The scientists that are men, are screw ups, or jokes. The male leaders are all dumb, or insanely corrupt and incompetent. Amongst your crew, out of the 2 men you get, 1 is a priest and the other is a drifter sports fan. Of the 3 women, 1 is a doctor and the other is an engineer. Men simply don't have any actual skills in this game, it seems. Is this a product of female writers or "male feminists"? This stuff aggravates me to no end. It's insulting. But hey, shooting stuff is fun, flying around and doing quests feels nice. Grab it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: A meh one.The game play is a modification on the standard Bethesda formula, which is no longer enjoyable by itself now. It usually served a purpose in supporting the plots, explorations, or RPG expressions.The setting and plot are bad. Dear Obsidian, you need to have a grounded tone first, and then break the tone for jokes, otherwise there would be nothing to break in the first place. The Halcyon system does not feel real at all, it does not feel like a place that can actually exist. And I do know how stupidly incompetent companies and managements can be, I really do. I have visited enough countries and academic establishments to know that we humans are fundamentally stupid and I fought off the urge to to kill myself everyday in the face of the absurdity of life. But you need to have a realistic world first and then explore the absurdity of its culture. The place cannot be so stupid that it cannot exist, or the immersion would be broken. Right now everyone's a fool and you are left to wonder how is this system only 'about to fall apart' not 'already fallen into utter chaos.'And I do not care about the ♥♥♥♥♥ on my ship either. So all in all I feel no motivation in playing it. There are games with better combats, better RPG expressions, and better stories. I know that if I keep on playing, all that would turn up are more repetitive jokes about immersion-breakingly stupid people doing stupid things to my not-so-expressive customizable character.Production value: 7.5plot/lore: 6Core game play: 6Overall a 6.5. Ok for a first game. I still finished it, if only for the Obsidian name attached to the product. But please impress me with the sequel, Obsidian, you can do better, I know.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: It's a first-person rpg like the Fallout games except with outer space/alien world themes.  Very colorful - it can actually be too colorful compared to say the absolute dismal gray of everything in Fallout games.  That's probably my only very minor quibble; it's too colorful!  lol  --> I'm having fun and played 6 hrs. straight once I started.  No bugs or glitches either.  It may be too easy (esp. using the TTD slo-mo skill for targeting enemies) but you can crank up the difficulty in the menu at any point.  It's pretty easy to just jump right in and start exploring and doing whatever you wish - a bloodthirsty murderer or a good samaritan - all up to you.  If you require direction(s), fixed structure, and linear games on rails then you're probably better off playing any of the Metro games.  Nitpickers criticizing and comparing The Outer Worlds to Bethesda's games are gonna dislike it no matter what - and I'm glad I ignored their extensive overly critical reviews.The Outer Worlds is like a different cousin game to Bethesda's fps rpg games.  Open world, do what you want, enjoy how you wish.  Very easy to jump right in and play with a very extensive in-game reference logs.I paid $20 for The Outer Worlds on Steam sale - definitely an excellent purchase - even if it were $30.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ this game ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ slaps, I honestly think it's better than Fallout: New Vegas (however they are both very good games that I will continue to play). I got the game for a discounted price for $25 dollars off of humble bundle, worth every cent (and if I knew it was this good I would have bought this for anything under $70). The way I played it was by going through the normal quest, taking on any side-quests that were given to me, but not actively seeking them out. After that, I bought both dlc and reloaded a save previous to the final event. I completed both dlc (both having about 5 hours of content using the same strategy that was used for the main quest, not actively seeking out side quests). This game feels very fluid and there were very few times that I felt as though something was boring or useless, every activity was done with a purpose, not "go complete these 17 fetch quests for basically no reward." The fetch quests that did exist were side quests and. in my opinion, the least fun part of the game, the reward is significant, but as some fetch quests rely of random chance event (ie: getting a specific item to drop from a specific enemy). Even though that was my least favorite part of the game, the game was still enjoyable as the stunning graphics and visuals make walking for long distances a more enjoyable experience than it would otherwise be, you will also never be walking too far, and enemy camps being scattered around gives you plenty opportunity to think about what you are doing, do you sneak past them, oh but they have loot. Now the story, the main story is one of them favorite parts of the game, I wont go into detail here in case you haven't played the game before and I don't want to spoil anything, but everything I learned about who you are and what the world around you consists of, is believable, there are many sides to every story and this is no exception, you have to choose how you go about completing the story, and I may not know all the ways, but rest assured I will be figuring them out. Now to my favorite part of the game, the companions. My two personal favorite companions to bring out on quests with me were Ellie and Parvati, but other companions were used whenever their skills would seem to be needed in the near future (and oh boy were they). I love the passive dialogue that happens between your two companions in the wilderness, I love they have in-depth personalities and opinions on what you're doing and what you're being offered, I love that they interject during conversations to add their opinions to the conversation. I also love the quests that they offer you, whether it is to make peace with dead partners, to find love, or to screw over your stuck-up family, I loved every second of learning more about my crew and helping them out. I never felt forced into doing anything (other than the main quest, obviously, but I could take my time as there were many side-quests to do). I didn't gain access to them until later (because I am a doofus and forgot to level up the required skill) but companions abilities are an extremely fun part of the game, what they do is while looking at an enemy, pressing a designated button (default keys are "c" and "v") to have one of your companions (depending on which key you pressed) do a special attack on that enemy with a special animation and has a decently long cooldown (about 30 seconds to a minute from what I remember). These abilities can also be improved as the companions level up. Now the skills, I really like the way the skills were done, putting each skill (which are affected by you base stats) into a category and allowing you to level up the category (usually with 3 skills) until each skill is level 50, at which point you level them up individually, getting bonuses for every 20 levels in that skill (and 150 if you have the dlc). I played the game on hard mode and that forced me to always be in the moment with the game as many of the high-level enemies could kill you before you can even say "oh ♥♥♥♥!" But, when all else fails drugs are always there for you. Now the non-game aspects, the load times are definitely longer than New Vegas, but, as a trade-off, the majority of buildings do not require a loading screed, they were already loaded in by the time you get there, meaning you are in way fewer (albeit slightly longer) loading times, I would take this trade-off any day of the week and love how the implemented it. I intend to play much more of this game with many more characters and choices to make.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: Pro's: The writing is absolutely superb; story line decisions are satisfying; nice atmosphere in general. This game is focused on the different decisions you can make in conversations with NPC's. If that part of RPG games generally interests you, I can recommend this game. Cons: The game is very easy and I recommend to play on hard-mode or higher. The quests are repetitive and have no puzzling or challenging element to them. The game is short and feels a bit unfinished. If you like open world games where you can explore and hone your character's skills and items to perfection, I do not recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: When I was buying an old-school RPG in 2020, I didn't mean it lacks mouse support.Mouse works for me in menus, but not in 1st person mode.Also, screen resolution was overstretched - only the top-left quarter was visible, so I had to disable full screen optimizations for the executable file to fix that.This game was originally released a year ago, but it still has core technical problems.Obsidian, this quality of code is embarassing - The Outer Worlds can be a ten times great game (and I am sure it is such), but if you don't give players any chance to play it, they'll become upset.I am afraid, I cannot recommend this game in its current technical state to anyone.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed the game however i somehow beat the game in 12 hours without any idea of what the game was and what i was suppose to do , i  was that confused i went to a hard difficulty planet without even knowing and obtaining some really good guns whilst only visiting 3 planets .I was quite dissarpointed with how easy some of the mobs are.I didn't like some of the game play features such as persuade and intimidate i was basically walking around robbing everyone and it seemed fine as i only had to threaten them and it was done with.overall i enjoyed the game but it was way too easy , a lot of the guns especially energy guns are overpowered and i obtained them within the first half hour of the game but because of how fast i completed the game and how easy it was to get around certain areas i have to not recommend for the price ,i was very unsatisfied when i reached then end and wished there was more content.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok'ish Game when on sale. But its far from being a full price game. The further you progress the more linear it gets. Quests become like: walk, loading screen, walk, walk, loading screen, talk to person X. walk , loading screen, loading screen, walk, pick up Y. _childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game so much, the framework is great, great gunplay, great systems(weapon tinkering, modifying, speech stuff, perks and stats), but the game doesn't really use the, like theres 4 weapons mods and there just isnt a lot to do, not a lot of weapons, and a meh story.
