_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the game, and what a ride. I defintely recommend the game.Reasons to play:- The main story (and side stories) are relatable and engaging. The story is quite grey and it is to you to make the decisions of how things are going to unfold. Choices feel like they have impact, narratively at least, not so much in actual gameplay per se- Many different viable playstyles. The devs really want it so you play like you wan to. You can play super sneaky and charismatic if you want and this way avoid many confrontations and the like. Melee-tank is super cool too and the deadly sniper or heavy weapon plus shotty. It is all viable and fun to play. For example, when you do not have a very good combat build, you can actually skip the (only) bossbattle in the game if you have maximium lockpicking. - Progression and combat feels very right. At start of the game you are pretty weak, but when you play it with some actual thought and start to upgrade yuo really start feeling like a baddass. Finding better weapons feels great and powerful, while still being vunerable when you start blazing without really regards. Enemies will kill you when you are not careful, and I like this danger which makes that feeling of being a badass feel worth.- All quests are handcrafted and felt good to do. There are many secrets alll around for the observant and patient players.- The environments are beautifull and detailed, although a little too vibrant in a way for me somehow, so I turned some of the details down... personal preference - The game is not open world and smaller than a fallout game. This is not really an issue but it does lower that sense of scale somewhat. Also the game ends somewhat short. But it does not diminish the quality since there is no filler content.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: I don't get why this game gets so much hate from the Fallout community. While this game may not live up to New Vegas and this isn't the same Obsidian as back then, this is still a really great game, better than anything Bethesda has ever released and probably ever will I think.If you're tired of playing New Vegas and want something new to fill that void, this is it. While the story may not be amazing, it's passable and the characters may not be ♥♥♥♥♥♥' Garrus from Mass Effect (there are a couple of stand outs being Parvati and Ellie), and the progression for gear is admittedly not good, oh and there are some pretty noticeable performance issues but nothing too bad.. unlike Cyberpunk. But apart from that the dialogue is fun and well written, there's so much freedom in how you tackle quests and how you complete them and branching paths, the combat gets the job done, I personally really like the art style and I think this game is, for the most part, really stunning.The DLC; is ok overall. I think you can skip Perils on Gorgon as it's very short, yet feels very padded too, feels very rushed and the new area is AWFUL- but if you get it all cheap then ♥♥♥♥ it why not. Murder on Eridanos is great, the new world is interesting, the characters are fun, it has a lot of intrigue (even if it's admittedly quite predictable), and long enough to be satisfying while now overstaying its welcome.I finished my playthrough after almost 2 days of playtime, even though I am quite slow and like to see everything a game has to offer the game felt satisfying to play through and apart from a couple of small bits here and there, I didn't feel like it dragged or was too padded.Overall I highly recommend this game, although I'd recommend getting a cheaper code from "A2G"  or someplace like that, but I'd definitely play it again in the future and I'll 100% be getting the sequel whenever it comes out.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: Welcome to SpaceThis is the pseudo-RPG we should have gotten instead of Fallout 76.  This is a game that looks at our current world and shows us what could happen, while maintaining the light-hearted attitude a la Borderlands.Is it the greatest game ever made?  Eh.  It could be.  That's a subjective thing, thougn.Will you have a good time shooting stuff and looting anything you can open?  You betcha.Is it worth the price of admission?  Absolutely.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: 3/5 starsPros: Mildly amusing in general. Custom characters. Very spacey themed which is fun. You can kill anyone which is fun. Choices make some difference. I can talk like myself in the dialogues more or less. Auto run button. The science weapons are kind of fun.Cons: Extremely short, this is the main reason i dont give 5 starts. Less than 18h for 1 char when i explored like crazy & was afk so in reality much less than 18h the 2nd run could prob be done in less than 4h including the side quests.The lighting is rly bad when creating the char.The companions & ada wont ever shut up, so i wish there was a mute option.You have to return to the ship to switch companions.No auto walk button which is very annoying when you're encumbered.The looting is extremely annoying, you cant loot even when in range & looking directly at items sometimes, you have to walk up to it & spam e to find an angle to loot despite nothing being in the way so now my finger hurts.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. A lot like Fallout with Wasteland 3 humor.  The game is not optimized well and needs tweaks to function properly. Run in Full Screen. Frame rate at 60fps. V-sync off. Motion Blur at 0%. Screen effects low. View distance = medium. Shadows = low. Visual effects = medium. Foliage = medium.  These settings will make the game perform much better and reduce any lag or stutter.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely underrated game! The base game + the DLC adds plenty to do. I honestly can't understand why people said this game was short. The side quest heavily influence the main quest, and the main quest is only like 5% of the game's story at that. So unless you intentionally bum-rush the main quest the game it's impossible for it to feel short at all. The game severely lacks a New Game+. Attributes and flaws are permanent (skills can be respecced), and enemies don't scare with you. So if you want to see all the different endings and consequences with different builds and playstyles, you'll need to start a new game each time...which unless you have a lot of time on your hands can get repetitive quickly.I reccomend mods:Dev-Console Unlock Guide - So you can level up quickerEnemy Scaling Overhaul and Level Cap Increase - So enemies scale with your new level.This way you can have a New Game+ experience without starting from scratch. You can so you don't need to wait to get certain gear again. I highly recommend these mods after your first playthrough.Overall, great game 9/10.  Makes Fallout 4 look grey and boring in comparison.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: Its gameplay is faster paced than Fallout 4 or New Vegas but slow enough to make it an alright RPG, its story line is lukewarm and kind of comical, and its glitchy at some times, characters no clipping through the map, et cetera. Overall I'd recommend, I have it on 2 consoles and my PC, but highly suggest the PC version because feels more open and the combat is faster compared to the consoles.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: Great game that does something different. It DOES have shades of Fallout, Bioshock, Dishonoured etc, but underneath the gameplay is a smart satire of unfettered Capitalism and the direction we're heading in. All the moving parts of The Outer Worlds combine to make it a step above most other games of this style, the soundtrack perfectly fits the mood, the graphics really shine and what i've seen of the story so far, while bleak, is engaging and actually has substance to it, whereas a lot of games can feel like gameplay with a story thrown on top as an afterthought. I also made the mistake of paying full price when it was available through Xbox gamepass but the game is that good IMO I still don't feel it was money wasted.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: A fun little game that has the charm of those old Space Quest games and the vibe of Fallout: New Vegas. _childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately the game doesn't live up to its reputation. The worlds are repetitive and every world is basically the same village with a different look... with a world built around it. The worlds itself are "flat" you cannot go everywhere - they're full of barriers... It feels like an old half life or quake or unreal engine game. There no way this thing is "open world". While the worlds themselves look pretty even the enemy types repeat. This is a pattern that goes through the whole game... The characters etc... But I've to add that it feels like an Fallout ripoff where they weren't able to actually catch the humor Bethesda and Obsidian offered in the Fallout universe. Its for the most part simple and boring conversations with the same repetitive jokes. it feels like as if a 10th grader hasn't done his homework properly and copied it from various classmates while the atmosphere got somewhere lost.I wouldn't buy this game again. It's a waste of money, you're better off trying anything else. Even the gameplay is repetitive, the weapons are boring too. There was simply no effort put into this game. I play usually a wide range of games and never felt the urge to actually warn people to buy something in the last 10 years, but this game really needs the stamp "at least you tried". Not even one part of the game is worth exploring it further. Maybe in the future when I forgot how bad it really was I will try again. But its one of those games that force you to take a route in a open world game. But the only thing that is open about this game is the devs wallet. everything else is limited like the levels.... However, if it would still be possible I would ask for a refund, so better watch some gameplay videos and decide for yourself before spending money on this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Obsidian definitely took what they learned from making Fallout New Vegas, and applied it here.  There's room for improvement, yes.  For starters the planets need to feel bigger.  I know the open world areas were huge, but we're talking about planets.  Whole epic games can occur on a massive open world map that only translates to a spot on our globe.  Space games in general don't do a good job of making a planet feel like a planet so much as an individual city, and this game is no exception.  One thing that adds to this feeling is having the same ten or some monsters present in all locations no matter what planet you're on.  Different planets should have different flora and fauna, with the invasive species transported by humans being the rare exception, not the norm! For space locations like asteroids and space stations, the devs should definitely play around with the gravity and make low and micro gravity environments part of the gameplay.  This isn't something new to games, and I feel like it could be incorporated into space games with starship travel.Other than that, make sure your hardware meets the requirements and you should be fine.  Solid gameplay and story.  I feel like there needs to be a cookbook that explains how to make an imitation of the food in the game.  I want some Lemon Slapp for a hot summer's day, some Glacial Aged Whiskey for special occasions, a sampling of every color of Rizzo's spectrum vodka, I want to know what tripicale is even supposed to be so I can attempt tripicale pasta, and, OH YEAH, the cystypig food items now have me wondering if you can actually cook and eat a pig's cancerous tumors!  No kidding, I'm morbidly curious about that now.  Thanks C&P!  Also, EVERY purpleberry product in the game is making me wonder about whether you could engineer a berry to taste like the purple grape koolaid flavor and make all of those products with that.  GOD the capitalist advertising stuff in this game actually gets in your skull!  Now when I go to a bad hotel I'm telling people that the hotel "is not the best choice, it's Spacer's Choice!" As a way of telling them how bad it is!  Obsidian really nailed soul-eating, mentally cancerous late-stage capitalism in this game!
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. Enjoyed it immensely.This game had way more of a cyberpunk feel than cyberpunk 2077 and that wasn't even the main thing. This is how you portray a world where corps own everything, where human life is valued in how much money it brings and nothing else. As an example, found in one of the random texts you can find: If someone commits suicide.. The next of kin or, if lacking, coworkers get a bill for the estimated rest of live profit of the dead guy. I don't know if it had bugs at the start, but I was surprised how few I had. It gives you a Fallout feel but.. All the bugs are missing! The only ones I can recall is that your position on the map was borked a few times.Usually I can go great lengths about the bad things of games. I'm the kind of person that remembers the bad things way more vividly.  Only things I can think of are nitpicks/quality of life. When buying or picking up armor/weapons, you don't see what you wear as a comparison, you can only do that later. What the different damage types or science weapons do is never explained, you have to google it or try out. Most if not all unique weapons you find are woefully underpowered to what you have. There's apparently no mod support.  To change team mates, you have to return to your ship. Sex apparently doesn't exist what I always found weird in cyberpunk-adjacent games (I wanna be a sexy ship captain ffs XD). Weapons could have more variance, after some time you'll find "Mark 2" of the ones you already knew (still plenty different types tho)All small things, but I can't think of big ones.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: Played the game on game pass when it first came out, finished it three times to get as many different outcomes as possible and decided to buy it again so I could play through the game + dlc as I've heard that the dlc isn't good endgame content but is apparently quite good as midgame content. It's a good RPG. It's not a great RPG, no. The decision making is weaker compared to Obsidian's other work and a little bit brainless from a player perspective. You don't exactly feel like you're at any difficult crossroads despite the initial appearance of some decisions as being genuine moral dilemmas. The game won't "challenge" you as a player in an meaningful way. Despite those criticisms it's a really fun game, with the right hardware it's absolutely gorgeous and although some parts weren't well optimised on launch, the game has very few technical flaws now. Or at least nothing that will grind your gears or break your game. No companion romance which I know for a small subset of players is a bit of a deal breaker - it didn't bother me personally as i rarely engage with romance content in games anyway (although you can find love FOR one of your companions). The companions are great company though, they all have their own dialogues with each other which is at this point kind of par for the course for an obsidian RPG coming off the back of party dialogue in POE 1 and 2. They all have a personal questline, some are better than others in my opinion but I'll let you be the judge of that as different characters resonate better with different players.Combat is solid. Ranged combat is a bit so-so, it doesn't come close to the tightness of games like Doom but it's passable and there is a new spin on the fallout VATS system for those who need the crutch when using guns in games like this. Melee is fine too, a bit more responsive than Fallout and Elder Scrolls but fairly similar in design and execution. At no time will combat blow you away and depending on your build it's very possible to have quite a low number of combat encounters. I haven't done a sneak build yet so I can't really comment on that. The AI is pretty ordinary so I imagine stealth players will be able to take full advantage of them in any case.The writing is A tier. Not S tier, but it was NEARLY S tier. not QUITE as good as POE 1 or NV but better than Tyranny and POE 2(i'm mostly referencing Obsidian's recent works in this review). It is distinctly Obsidian style writing all the same and anyone who has played their previous games and enjoyed the writing will feel right at home here.All in all, Obsidian is absolutely onto something here. They've filled a market gap left wide open by Bethesda and Microsoft would be smart to let Obsidian keep filling the gap with content like this. Their pedigree with development staff who have worked on previous Fallout titles as well as a long list of other RPG's shines through in the Outer Worlds. I'm excited to see what their DLC's have to offer to the game as well as possible sequels as well.If you like RPG's, just buy Outer Worlds. You'll enjoy it. To what degree? Your mileage will vary, but you WILL enjoy it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: The Outer Worlds... Now, where do I start?I'll start with the disclaimers: 1) what I write in here is my own opinion, and 2) possible spoilers ahead. There are many other things people could be doing with their time other than reading stuff they don't agree with and finding out about in-game stuff before they wanted to. With that said, let's continue...I have the impression that the team who developed TOW was aiming pretty high, but budget constraints and white collar executives got in the way as usual, and spoiled it for everybody else.Other than being (in my opinion) a mediocre console port with all it's console hardware impairments and limitations ported over, the game feels unfinished and it seems a lot of content was crudely severed at it's final stages of development.The companion AI is plain stupid. Where their behaviour settings read "Passive/Defensive/Aggressive", in reality it is "Dumb/Dumber/Suicidal", particularly true when playing on Supernova - which by the way is the only difficulty setting to go, if you want half a challenge.If you put them on Passive or Defensive and hell breaks loose, they just stay around as if nothing's happening, they won't take cover and worse, they place themselves between you and enemy NPCs, taking fire from both sides. Put them on Aggressive and first thing they do is charge a Sprat when you're trying to sneak past a Mantiqueen. You get the picture.The companions themselves, with the exception of Parvati and maybe Felix, are pretty annoying and totally forgettable. I only took them on their very own quests and only for the sake of getting that much needed XP out of that. There are lots of stuff copy-pasted from other games, the more charitable among you may call it "references", I just call it blatant stealing ideas already seen in other games because they couldn't damn well come up with something new.I could make a long list of stuff they put in there which I've seen on FONV, Deus X Human Revolution, Mass Effect and others, but I can't be bothered, really. Even Guild Wars 2 has been stolen from: the Mantiswarm is nothing but almost a carbon-copy of the Mordrem Troll Insect Swarm from GW2.Anyway, the only two locations I enjoyed was Monarch and Tartarus. Had the dev team pushed through to deliver the remaining part of the game they abandoned, it would probably be a good game in the end. It's kind of frustrating seeing so many locked out locations/planets and not being able to land on them and explore at least.Does it have any replay value? I don't think so. I might start another playthrough only to get a few achievements, but maybe I won't even bother, as the consequences to whatever choices are pretty easy to predict, and not very exciting to experiment with.So, to finish it off, I'd give this game a fair score of 6/10.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: I rather am depressed playing this game. It feels so... so... thin. It's more on par with Bioshock: Infinite instead of Fallout: NV. The Character Creation (as far as looks) is pointless. You'll never see your character (outside of Idle Screen animations, when you AREN'T playing it).The UI/UX is that nasty form of flatness, as if you're looking at your stats, inventory, quests, and everything else as a separate accounting form on some proprietary software you'd get trained on at your 9-5 job, and even they got it on the 'cheap'.The (physical) world doesn't feel real, at all. You can walk completely through plants that aren't thicker than a tree, but you 'slide' off of marginally-inclined rocks as if your feel are made of butter suddenly.The story... well... there's worse, yes. This plot feels like an overwritten fan-fiction, however it's lacking a Mary Sue to vent your frustration on.I played 31 hours. I can't remember anything of relevance other than what I've written here in this review.I expected better. Not a whole LOT better. But... better.3/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: Yet another huge Fallout: NV fan here coming into this game with high expectations. The game looks and sounds great, and the NPC interactions and dialog were on point with plenty of opportunities to use stats and skills to influence people.Sadly, none of this mattered. The other crucial component of this game for me, the combat, is deeply and fundamentally flawed. Enemies with guns do not seem to miss. Cover? Didn't matter. High ground? Didn't matter. If you have even a pinkie toe exposed, you're getting hit. As a result, although the game pretends like it might support basic tactical gunplay, it seems to lean much more towards run-and-gun with RPG-style stat checks and potion chugging.I found the accuracy immersion-breaking as well. The first enemies you encounter are marauders, people apparently so stupid that they are considered sub-human. Many of those marauders also wield Spacer's Choice weaponry, guns that NPCs joke about being poor quality. Despite this, you want me to believe these marauders are absolutely ridiculous sharpshooters?To be fair, if I encountered Outer Worlds without the expectations set from other impressions and previous games, I might have found it to be a good game. But that isn't the case, and I did not find what I was looking for here. Perhaps I will revisit the game in the future. (But would I be better served just reinstalling Fallout: NV and throwing on some mods?)
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: IntroCaptain of the unreliable I presume? Solid RPG with an interesting backstory, although a little shallow at times. In my mind this is a shorter version of what Fallout 76 should have been.Story – SPOILER ALERTThe outer worlds starts with you being resurrected by a ‘crazy scientist’ who says you need to help him free he others. Sounds familiar although I don’t know from where. You go on to become a leader of a ‘rebel-kind-of-group’ which decides what is best for them. You have multiple options when completing quests, and after having finished one run, I am certain I can reach 2 different endings than what I had at this point. Personally, I think the writing of the overall story has a solid base, but it lacks that final oomph, that little spark which could have really set this game apart. Don’t get me wrong, I loved going through missions and I almost never felt bored doing quests. But I feel like there could have been more. Certainly, at the end of the story, I felt as if there could have been an ‘act two’, as the final battle comes relatively quick. Overall, enjoyable and on certain points quite original. 7/10GameplayBefore addressing the gameplay, I must admit I left a big chunk out of my playthrough. I didn’t use consumables (other than the occasional attribute inducer), heavy weapons, melee weapons and slow-motion combat. This certainly limits my view of the entirety of it, but I still feel I can accurately say: It is good but needs a little bit of work. At the start, surviving was difficult, and I found myself dying more than I expected, not helped by the awful and garbage heal-system (Come on guys, fix this s***). Spamming ‘heal’ during combat and hoping you get a little room to breathe thanks to your companions isn’t constructive nor fun. After a while however, when putting skills into specific perks (long ranged, crit damage, …) the combat became a breeze towards the endgame. Looting, stealing, transporting and going about felt satisfying most of the time and fit right into the theme of the game. Although, I must clarify that this is not a ‘borderlands’ kind of loot. You find a good gun, upgrade it to whatever max it goes at your current level and then use it for the rest of the game. I used exactly 5 different weapons from 3 classes throughout the entirety of the game and was disappointed that I just started selling everything I looted. No loot had a specific value or advantage, everything was just replaceable.Overall, fine for a casual playthrough, although a little bit shallow. 6/10 (7/10 If combat was a bit better).MusicThe music in the outer worlds never really stood me by, but I think of this as a good thing. Never had I felt that it distracted me from the game or its gameplay. I enjoyed the encompassing soundtracks, Although I have a hard time remembering any specific thing about it now… 7/10Artstyle / graphicsThe graphics of this game are fine. Just, fine. Not bad, not the best I’ve ever seen (certainly in this day and age), but it didn’t take away from anything. I liked the artstyle from the start and loved the environments. Variation was not the most important value when developing this game, as every asset is the same on every planet, but this can be addressed to story-related reasons. Lootbox = yellow, door open = grey, door closed = red. Could it benefit from better graphics? Hell no. Could it benefit from more assets and more variation in these assets? Certainly. Overall 7/10Oh and I have to mention: The first 10 minutes I had to adapt to the first-person view of this game. It was really difficult to focus on my screen and not get sick. I have never experienced something like this and at first I thought it was a setting that got screwed up. After session 2 or so, I got pretty used to it. Still, people with glasses or depth-perception problems, beware.AftermathWhen finishing the game, I didn’t feel empty, I didn’t feel the urge to overthink everything or wanted to start the whole experience again. Instead, I thought ‘wait, what? Done already?’ It felt like whole sections where left out of the game, or as if the second half was left for a second game. Leaving the game felt a little incomplete, but returning and starting over again knowing where it will end again kind of deters me. I will probably not play this game again for the coming years, but that doesn’t mean I didn’t enjoy my time.To summarizeOverall, the outer worlds is a good game with a solid base. Although noting really stood out to me (personally), I enjoyed playing and was kind of invested in some of the characters. As for the total score, I value the whole game a lot more than just the sum of its parts. The latter would result in a 6.5/10, but this game deserves a lot more. Everything together puts me in a place where I can easily recommend this for the standard price, IF you are into the RPG-genre. If not specifically or if you are just curious, picking this up on a discount is an absolute win.  Final score 8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: It is an enjoyable story and has some challenge on harder difficulties. The different planets originally seemed like they'd be fun to explore but they turned into 2 or 3 loading screens to get there, although load times aren't bad it kind of breaks up gameplay a bit too much.The gun play is fun and they are satisfying to use however, enemy type and amount is limited and you end up facing the same enemies over and over depending on what planet you are on.Player choice is there and has a couple meaningful outcomes but don't go in expect New Vegas style endings with many possibilities. Overall it was enjoyable and worth the price (30$) on sale when it came to steam. I'd be curious to check out the DLCs now and see what else Obsidian has planned for this game

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed this game a lot. Unsurprisingly, this game reminds me a ton of Fallout New Vegas, and really scratches the itch for a solid 1st person shooter/RPG game. It was somewhat shorter than expected, taking about ~20 hours to finish the story and maybe half of the available side quests (not including any DLC). The re-playability is high, and I anticipate enjoying many playthroughs of this game to experience some of the many different styles of character development. Highly recommended for fans of RPG games in general, or fans of Fallout 3/NV.

_childDocuments_.review: Took about 30 hours to finish this game on normal and exhausted all dialogue options and looted most of the stuff on the map. _childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: This game is basically Fallout/Skyrim in space. Instead of running around a post-apocalyptic wasteland or a fantasy world full of dragons, you are instead placed in shoes of a colonist who has to quest around a solar system. However, this game, despite containing a lot of content, is still probably not as in-depth as those.Nonetheless, it is a good start for a franchise that could probably reach that same potential and is still a fun experience with hours of content and variety. It is a solid role-playing game with some decent customization, dialogue, and branching decisions.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: This is, sadly, the conclusion I have to say about this game. I got hyped about it by some YouTube comments and bought it in good faith. I would'nt buy it again. The characters and dialogues are so generic and bland. The only good character arc I could find was Vicar Max's with his enlightenment in the end. Every other character arc was excruciatingly boring. Yes, my descicions had a lot of impact but the things they impacted -the world, the people in it, even the political system - were just not interesting. If at least the combat system had be good. Then it might be comparable to Borderlands. But nope! There is no real variety in enemies nor in weapons. For half the game I just had one rifle and it cut through every enemy like through butter so why go further? The aspect of looter-shooter failed for me as well because the legendary weapons are almost always weaker than the standard issues the same weapons. I'm tired of writing now, because English isn't my native language and THIS GAME JUST ISN'T WORTH IT.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: Very enjoyable game.  It had vibes of Bioshock and Fallout.  I loved the quirky advertising of various corporations.  I completed the game, doing all the side quests I could find, in 41 hours.  My advice is to spent you skill points in hacking, lockpicking and dialog (persuasion, lie and intimidate). _childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: After a very thorough Playthrough including the DLC's I have to say there are some interesting ideas but some absolutely terrible ones too plus bugs that remain still,  including the whole draw your weapon every time you talk to someone problem that is still not fixed after all this time. _childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: It's a cool game. Don't expect huge depth or physics, BUT being able to use speech a lot and get more stuff from convos, is pretty fun.Fighting, in general, is good. _childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: I was hoping for Fallout New Vegas in space, but all the difficult moral choices, exploration and mystery were stripped away and what's left isn't worth your time and energy.I skipped almost every dialogue in order not to be bored to death. _childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: Couldn't figure out why aiming felt so weird after playing for a few hours. I realized after a bit it was aim assist. I didn't think much of it until I went into the settings and noticed that this feature is not optional. Auto aim, at least for me, makes games almost unplayable. I'm not mad about some folks wanting the feature, it's none of my business really if other people like it. Buuuut it is utterly debilitating for me so, yeah, I bought a game I can't play and that's an awful feeling, cause I was looking forward to diving into it. I wouldn't be nearly as negative about it if not for the fact that apparently it launched with no aim assist, and aim assis was added later with no way of turning it off. Adding aim assist without offering a way to disable it just seems like such a slap in the face to anyone else who might have the same issues with it I have. And if that's the attitude the developers are going forward with, adding non optional mechanics that drastically change the gameplay for lots of people then I don't want any part of it. Like I KNOW the game is more about the rpg elements than the gun play but I mean, hey, it's not turn based is it? There IS gun play right? So it's an action rpg and the action is just as much a part of the game as the role play, so there you have it. Half of what makes this game what it is isn't usable for me. 0?0 flurbos

_childDocuments_.review: In short: This game is OK. Not brilliant, not terribly bad. Mediocre. Buy it on sale with a 70% discount. I'm still voting for it because despite it's not a masterpiece by any means I can see developers were trying to make it a good game giving it their love, care and dedication. At very least there are no microtransactions which is already nice.Quests and story are well written but don't seem to be real exciting or thrilling or having unexpected twists or deep moral dilemmas. They're just OK. You have some choices but those are quite straight forward. There is a considerable amount of backtracking involved  especially if you try to complete all side quests. The game partially mitigates backtracking with plenty of fast-travel points.From time to time I was under impression game devs tried to include some references to iconic RPGs like Mass Effect or even borrow some ideas. But unfortunately the execution is poor and don't stand a chance in comparison. Shooting and gameplay mechanics are OK. Weapons made fine and look nice and have mods and options to be upgraded. However fights are just too simple made. No covers, no tactics, no throwables. Some very basic stealth mechanic is also there.Loot system is very excessive and overburdened. You're drowning in tons and tons of differently named but doing precisely the same consumables. It makes you try to never open up consumables tab of your inventory to avoid pain and suffering of sorting those things up. Also there are really plenty of weapons and armor and you gonna spend a lot of your play time sorting/breaking to parts/selling your loot if you tend to be greedy and can not stand any pickable object laying around.Graphics is fine but it's heavily styled and includes visual filters some people might find hard to look at. Partially the visual effects can be disabled in video settings which makes it somehow easier to look at the picture. I'd say it could use some more optimization to my liking. Even though I play in 4K resolution with all video settings set to ultra, I don't really see the picture that could possibly cost me frame rate reduced to 40FPS on i9 and 2080.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: The Outer Worlds has great RPG elements, a lovely look and feel and some of the best/most interesting dialogue options I've seen in a game. World design and look and feel is just great.However, the game falls short in the combat department and overall game play just wasn't enough to carry me through. Guns and enemies all feel more or less the same, and the Tactical slow down time doesn't seem to work as well when compared to VATS from fallout for example.Quests got old fast, running errands from one spot to another got tedious. Walking takes for ages, until you discover a place and unlock fast travel. I like that you can make a choice and feel the consequences during some of the quests, but its such a slog to get through.This is a pass for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Jesus Christ, game is nuts and why am I compelled to finish all the quests, I never really do many quests on first runs of games but I did all that I could find in this game 10/10, was expecting it to be like fallout or as bomb as Fallout New Vegas seeing as obsidian did New Vegas, Laws no honestly it holds well against Fallout especially Fallout 4 which looks bland in comparison I recommend this game 100% Im super late to the party and Im sad its taken me 4 years

_childDocuments_.review: I got this for $17 on GMG. I would recommend it for $20 or less. This is absolutely not worth $60, so shop around or wait for a steep discount. At first it seems like Fallout in space, but eventually you see how much is missing compared to a FO title and it starts to feel like a knockoff FO you bought at KMART. Enemy respawn rate is weird as hell, in a lot of areas enemies flat out didn't respawn. Stealth system is pretty bunk, if you stealth shot one mob, the rest usually know exactly where you are and buzz straight to you. Reading the consumables descriptions is an eye sore (seriously what the ♥♥♥♥ were they thinking with UI there), so it's easier to just ignore them and spam sell them all since they're entirely unnecessary anyway unless you're playing on Supernova mode which requires eating. And the buffs are next to useless.It's not a true open world, changing planets is just a menu click away and each planet is rather small for a game like this. It basically is a hub system with tiny zones, reminiscent of a PS2 era game. For some reason there is a large woke culture overtone that is kinda weird the longer the game goes on, it feels very overly token.The loot system is pretty meh, usually in a game like this you'd be able to take pretty much every single item an enemy has when you kill them, but here it's a bit random where you may or may not get something they're using and when you loot the gear it's still on the corpse. Sometimes you get locked into dialogue and have to spam a few responses until you get to one to end dialogue. I've had keys to doors disappear after I picked them up, some disappeared after using them once despite still having doors that need the same key. Not sure if that's a glitch or a dumb decision to make keys one time use?The color gamma in this is weird and tough to find a spot that looks good without being washed out or too artificially rich looking.This is all odd because Obsidian has worked on the Fallout series so you'd expect this to be a lot better than it is and have added features not less. The gear mod system is pretty restrictive and trash. For some reason you can mod body armor, but not helmet armor; kinda weird decision. Some weapons that clearly should have multiple attachments only have 1.The skill/perk system is pretty bunk too. You level cap at 30, so that means you can only max 3 skills, 300 SP/100 SP. Then out of the 42 possible perks, you can only safe unlock 15, because you only get 1 perk every two levels. Although you can unlock additional perks through the Flaw system, that requires being subjected to certain enemies, items etc, repeatedly; to unlock the option to take permanent stat debuffs, in return for another perk point. Only 20 flaws, so even if you find each one you can still only unlock 35 perks in total. The ♥♥♥♥?It's basically knock off Fallout. I enjoyed it because I bought it cheap and it slightly scratches the space game itch, but it's a solid 3/5 game. Nothing particularly unique or great, but not entirely ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ either. It's alright, but I don't look forward to grinding achievements for 100%.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: Decently fun but buggy despite having been out for years. _childDocuments_.review: The game is fun, when it works. My game crashed repeatedly right after character creation. It never saved so I had to make my character over and over again. I was finally able to fix it by putting the game into Fullscreen, Locked at 60 FPS, and Vsync On.It worked for about 4 hours and then it keeps crashing in the Geothermal Plant whenever I get melee attacked by a robot.You'd think after an entire year these issues would have been resolved.So far the game has been a lot of fun, and the dialogue choices have blown me away. Obsidian did a great job.But until these Crashes get fixed, I cannot recommend this game.Edit: I am running a i7 8700K and a 1080ti with 32GB of DDR4 RAM, it's NOT my hardware.HOWEVER. I found that disabling the Steam Overlay seems to help. I will continue testing it.Edit 2: Nothing works. I disabled every running process in my background. I disabled my AntiVirus, I ran it at a lower resolution, I turned off the Windows Game Bar, I ran the game as Admin. The crashes have increased as a matter of fact.I give up.EDIT 3: I built a new PC back in December and just recently managed to get back to this game. It seems the crashing issues have stopped, so there may have been issue with the underlying hardware and not the game itself. I apologize this review got so popular while 'negative'. I changed this review to positive and hope more people will give this great game a try.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR - The strength of the writing and dialogue is severely hampered by the gameplay and world exploration. If you're going to buy it do so only with an extreme discount.After waiting a year for the epic games exclusivity deal to expire and the game to come to steam, I'd forgotten the game existed and went in with absolutely no expectations. I don't think The Outer Worlds is bad by any stretch, but design choices regarding the planet layouts and gameplay cause a disconnect between what the game wants to be and what the game is. The game wants to be an open-world space RPG with vibrant and dangerous worlds populated by quirky characters. But it fails to deliver successfully on all but the quirky characters.Firstly, the art direction regarding the alien worlds, colonies and spaceships is great. The game looks very good. However, when it comes to exploring the game world, it is segmented into pockets of explorable areas making the game feel much smaller in scope. Rather than having an interconnected area for each planet, you have something like "Town 1 and surrounding area" "town 2 and surrounding area" which will consist of a big town, outside of which there will be several smaller buildings dispersed around the map, and each building will be surrounded by enemies. Each area of a planet is like this, so once you've explored one area, all of the areas you will unlock later will feel similarly laid out and these 'explorable pockets' feel a lot less exciting due to the repetitive nature of the aforementioned pockets.Lastly, I want to talk about the gameplay, specifically, the combat. To be blunt it is lackluster. You've basically got the option between bullets, lasers and melee. When you attack an enemy numbers pop out of them indicating how much damage you have done, which could mean your cool weapon you've picked up will be under levelled and quickly become useless. While many RPGs use this 'number popping' system to great effect, it makes combat seem more like a chore in The Outer Worlds. If you're on your way to a waypoint and you meet a tough enemy, you'll just have to use your weapon that makes the most numbers pop out rather than the weapon you feel is cool. The way the combat is designed forces you to use the most effective weapons rather than a weapon that feels cool. In a game about player choice, this is a pretty big misstep. The repetitive world layout and combat corrupt The Outer Worlds into a run of the mill RPG that fails in any way to deliver anything new and exciting to players. Whilst the dialogue is incredibly strong slogging through the game is not worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: Good game, but don't come in expecting New Vegas. The tone is much different. The combat is much more stale and less dynamic. Resources are tight in the early game. Really cool setting and amazing story, but the gameplay is just too bland for me to give a full price recommend. I knew this when I saw the trailers back in the day (no explosives, and the enemies being much more "stiff"), so I waited for a sale. I made the right call. Its too boring for me, the story so far was great, but sadly not enough to carry my attention to the end. I'll beat it one day. Buy on a sale, might be worth it for you. 6/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: The Outer Words is a space-pirate, swash-buckler in the tradition of Serenity and Firefly.  The game play and story components are a space-version of Fallout.The game is a lot fun and the story line is entertaining.  In reviews and also in the promotional materials it has been described as the "next Fallout"  While there are definitely similarities, the game overall has less depth and versatility compared to the fallout series, especially Fallout 4.  The character, armor and weapon customization is much more limited, and the environment customization is non-existent.  Also the open world is much smaller and far-less rich with limited options for exploration.  In fallout you could spend an evening just exploring and foraging for useful items, or working on the design and layout of your settlement. In TOW exploration is limited, due to the smaller size of the world, and unfortunately there is nothing similar to the settlement building.The game  didn't capture my interest and imagination like  FO4, so  I doubt I play it multiple times.  Also the DLC seems mostly limited to the online version-- which also limits replay options.    However, if you like Fallout 4 and the  Serenity/Firefly shows then you will probably like this game. It is pretty fun and the story interesting, and definitely worth a play- though-- especially if you get it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: It's fun and reminds me a little bit of classic fallout and the spacey Victorian era theme is very aesthetically appealing and is just a fun atmosphere. the laissez-faire feel of it is nice and provides an interesting setting to immerse yourself into, though I will say some parts of the game are a bit more dull than others. The mechanics of the game are nice too but took a little getting used to when I first realized how it worked. I look forward to hearing more about Outer Worlds 2!this was my first review so forgive me if my review is a bit confusing.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: -Choices matter-Fun whimsical roleplaying experience-Science weapons are cool-Customizeable weapons and equipment-Really fantastic and well written characters-Respec machine allows experimentation with different playstyles within a single playthrough-Plot-twist reliant storyline reduces replayability-Limited areas to explore-Short campaign (100% completion at 25 hours)-Stealth doesn't really... work. Alright, this game is really pretty great, it just needs more content.  I'm thrilled to have gotten this on a sale, but I would have been angry if I had paid the full price.  The gameplay is fun, and there's so many different builds to experiment with. The guns and weapons all feel different.  The plotline is equal parts funny and depressing and riveting.  The choices you make matter a ton, and you have multiple chances to go in many different directions with the plot.  There's even a "dumb character" unique ending.  I loved every second of it.Now the downsides.  Stealth doesn't really work.  You get one shot, it won't kill the target unless you're way overleveled, and then you have to fight normally.  There's no quest that relies on stealth either.  There is a big plot twist halfway through the main questline that enlightens you on how your choices so far have actually mattered.  This plot twist also makes the rest of the game painfully predictable.  And replays have that same problem... the driving force is also very predictable, and the choices have predictable consequences.  And the game is very very short for a roleplaying FPS game.  25 hours to 100% a game is too short.As a plus, this is a very Firefly-type game.  You even have a cute innocent extremely talented mechanic.  And a preacher with a past.  Corporate futuristic dystopia with a lot of well thought out characters and great jokes and funny situations makes this game a lot of fun to experience, and at no point did any gameplay stuff get in the way of the experience.  For how short it is, it is flawlessly executed, and I can't recommend it enough. Get on a sale just because it's so short, but definitely recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished this game and I loved it so much.Yeah, the game was really easy and the balance was off but that isn't really the part about rpgs that I enjoy, the dialogue and conversations were top notch (although were some things I wanted to say that weren't options). I definitely recommend getting the two DLCs, I enjoyed Peril on Gorgon more than Murder on Eridanos, mainly because of some really just weird things on Eridanos that no one acknowledges until the very end (you'll know what I mean if you play it)I can't say if it lives up to Fallout: New Vegas since I've never played that game but I def recommend this one

_childDocuments_.review: Basically just another boring shoot em' up game with tedious quests. It's not rewarding, there's no sense of accomplishment from finishing any of the quests. There's an astonishing amount of dialog options, but from what I've seen, they have no bearing on game play really. The companions are all incredibly annoying. The weapons are repetitive and uninteresting, instead of adding a new weapon as you level, it just becomes a "mark II" or "ultra"... Nothing about it is truly "open world" you can only travel to new locations as the story progresses, and the idea of "exploration" is pointless, because you're not going to find anything new or creative. If you're like me and waited an extra 363 days to buy it on Steam - either to spite Epic Games or otherwise - I think you'll be happy with this game. _childDocuments_.review: Honestly I was super excited for this game and have had it on my radar ever since it was announced. However, I feel like it honestly fell very flat. The character customization is lacking and games much older have more options. Not to mention it's almost null and void because there's no third-person option in this game so the only time you see your character is in the menu screen.After binging this game in a few days I found there was very little weight to your choices. Companions pop into your life with very little prompting and there's not many of them. Their companion quests can be incredibly short or mind numbingly long and have you run from one place to another just for one sentence. I was excited to travel from planet to planet and see the variation, only to sadly find that nothing stood out. The same four enemies cycled through these planets despite expecting to find a little bit more variation among wildlife. I understand this isn't an alien oriented game, but we're in SPACE. Shouldn't there be a bit more variation than giant bugs, giant gorillas, random goons, and generic robots? The planets felt like tiny restricted maps with very little to experience, not to mention not all planets are even explorable. I expected vibrant and eerie landscapes, not just grass and some weirdly shaped plants and rocks on every single planet. But honestly the thing that cripples this game the most? Lack of mod support. If the developers aren't going to fix things, the community would... if the game was actually easy to mod. There's so much potential for tweaking this game to make it just right, but with it's hard to change system there's no creators making new content. It was a boring game with boring characters in a generic dystopian future. As much as I wanted to love it, and I REALLY wanted to, it fell flat in the face of much older story driven games.

_childDocuments_.review: The creators of the original Fallout 1, 2, New Vegas, and the game I love more than anything Arcanum: Of Steamworks and Magick Obscura made this so I was like, hell yeah dude. There's so much that the game gets right that feels good on such a deep level but then it also falls flat in places.Pros------------------------Great Music - A highly underrated aspect of games is the music. Most games have generic orchestral music or wub-wub music, but the music in this game perfectly sets the mood and is delightful to just listen to as background music. Stellar Bay is particularly moody and really emphasizes how run down and hopeless everyone is.Voice Acting - The acting is really solid. Everyone has a natural cadence and speech that you'd expect from talking to a real live person in these settings (with the exception of Ellie who is written like a badass and her voice actress thought monotone was the best way to portray that). Not only do people act well but everyone you talk to has a voice that doesn't drive you up the wall (again with the exception of Ellie).Combat - Gunplay is solid. ADS is smooth, fast, and where you put the dot is where the bullet goes. Leveling up your gun skills increases damage and reduces sway and spread. Melee feels like what you'd expect. Click to swing. Hold to powerswing. Block just before getting hit to deflect and stun. Also wanna mention you have the ability to slow down time which allows you to do various things based on where you target so if you're not some zoomer who can 1080 no scope headshot, that little feature makes some otherwise hectic fights tolerable. Your companions have an activate ability you can use at any time they have energy for it which freezes time and damages a particular enemy. Fun applications are when you're about to be hit by something, use that and you become invincible during the animation effectively using i-frames to avoid damage.Exploration - Exploring feels good, it's almost always encouraged to explore so that you can find loot. You often find quest items or just fun bits of lore or dialogue from going off the beaten path. The visuals on each location are varied and the differences are stark. None of the places feel like another place with just a different color. The music, the colors, and the atmosphere go a long way to help each place feel unique.Cons----------------------------------Repetitive themes - You can almost always bet when you're reading about something bad to people, the emails from their employers is friendly and warm and completely disregard their value as humans. Yeah it's funny at first but when you're reading emails about an employee getting wrote up for not volunteering for voluntary overtime because they already had overtime assigned, you really just roll your eyes and groan. I am usually excited to read messages to get a better feel of the world I'm in but I can almost always predict what's going to be said because EVERY employer email reads the same.Missing Quality of Life things - No flashlight? What? 300 years into the future and I don't have access to a flashlight? Some of the caves and vents are really dark and you can miss items unless you are looking at them and close or have a mod that increases the items highlight range. You have to go to your ship to change teammates. Can't lock items and sell everything except locked items in one go. Difficulty Curve - I like to challenge myself so I usually play things on hard mode first. I was get annihilated really fast. Dropped it to normal. Still getting worked but could manage. Now I'm level 21 and it takes a lot to kill me so I bumped it back to hard and I got wrecked immediately. LMAOWUTNo Romance - You can't seduce anyone on your crew which I understand for professional reasons but still, a shame.--------------------------------------------------------------------All in all I would give this game a very solid 8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Please read this before buyingThis game is like a "crab" stick. It may look, smell and even taste as a deep story-driven RPG, but it is not the real thing. Look just a bit closer and you may see that it is just a shooter with an excuse for a story dressed in token Action RPG mechanics to imitate classics of the genre.The Outer Worlds takes place in a space system ruled by the conglomerate of corporate monopolies. It is the world of rampant wealth inequality, no labor rights, oppression by force, corporate propaganda, poverty etc. Most of the places you can visit are controlled by various companies, while some are taken over by the people resisting this way of life: hippie and survivalist communes, remnants of the army, marauding savages, terrorists etc.That's pretty much it. That's all this world has to it. Anti-corporate satire mixed with space travel, one of the most generic sci-fi combinations there is. However, what really makes it fail for me is that there is very little depth to characterization of this world. It is pretty much exactly what you would expect from a story like this. Pro-corporate characters are exactly the profit-obsessed caricatures you would expect to find. Resistance characters are exactly the well-meaning but morally grey freedom-fighters you would expect to find. It is as if the story went out of its way to be as unimaginative as possible. One over-used trope after another, after another, after another, played completely straight. It is not limited to the world and plot, but to small details as well. The companions, the enemies, even the ship you fly on are derivative, sometimes carbon copies from other fictional worlds. The game wants you to feel like you are in the Firefly's world, so you are going to fly around on the replica of the Serenity. Again, while it may look like the thing, it is not. It is a poor quality product trying to emulate a better one, and if you see through it, you are unlikely to get the feeling you want from it.A special mention should go to what the game says and how it says it. The game revolves around continous anti-corporate satire. First time I met over-zealous pro-corporate guard it was somewhat funny. Second time someone pointed how pro-corporate the world is, it was not funny. Third time it was annoying. "Isn't out-of-control corporatism stupid, eh? Isn't it stupid, eh? Just look how stupid it is! So stupid, right? Did you notice how stupid it is? Here, let me show you again! Can't believe how stupid it is!" A repeating joke that is not that funny to begin with, over and over and over, the opposite of what a good satire is. It is not creative, it is not insightful and it just is not funny.There is nothing original here either. It is a standard kit of Action RPG mechanics. There are skills, levels and perks; stealth, lockpicking and hacking; melee and range combat; speech checks; bullet-time; reputation system; needs (water, food, sleep) etc. You can follow story or go exploring various settlements and wild planets. There are some side-quests. I don't believe keeping the Outer World's gameplay conservative was a bad decision, but there is just not much a player can do with the tools provided.To be honest, most Action RPGs are about exploring an area, killing enemies there, looting all you can get and moving to the next area. However, there are usually some attempts to make it seem like there is some variety to what you are doing. Some mini-games, unusual goals, puzzles. At the very least different types of enemies and locations. The Outer Worlds does not really have that. As far as I can tell, quests and general gameplay are limited to killing people or getting items through stealing, killing or talking. Most of the time the enemies are the same marauding savages that you can kill liberally because those are evil by default. Usually I finish the games, even the ones I don't care about, but in this case I made an exception. The story and the world were way too boring to get invested. The gameplay was way too by-the-numbers and repetitive to have any sort of fun. It has no creative spark.I've seen defenders of this game arguing that the Outer Worlds should be judged on its own merits and that a player should not bring "expectations" to it, just shut up and enjoy, but this argument is just a silly nonsense. First of all, if you buy a product, of course you have every right to expect something it from it and compare it to your experience. Second of all, I personally did not want the Outer Worlds to be a clone of other games, what I expected was quality: a good story and a good gameplay, and I got neither. Ironically the game is everything it wants to satirize: a low-effort, disingenuous, over-priced corporate consumption product.In case you never played a good Action RPG game before, you may found the Outer Worlds impressive. Just like how if you never ate a real crab you may find a "crab" stick impressive. There is so much to enjoy out there, starting with sci-fi classics like Bioshock, Mass Effect and Fallout. These games are of much better quality, sold for a much lower price. Do try them.

_childDocuments_.review: This game very much feels like you are going through the motions to get to the end. Fun but a pretty standard game model of fly between hubs (planets) using your home base (ship) to store your collectables (ship decorations). Recruit companions along the way, who live in your ship, and do their companion quests to unlock a unique trait (perk) in their skill tree. A few moral choices along the main story line impact the ending, and some optional faction quests that dictate very little beyond how the end narrative cut scene plays. Stop me if you have seen this show below.Pros: - pretty graphics style - think Bioshock in space - interesting story theme (although not taken to its full potential) - science weapons add some much needed differentiation and combat tactics - time dilation - bullet time in spaceCons: - limited perk and character builds. yes you can create different builds, but they are a variation on a standard theme (melee, range - combined with stealth (light) or tank (heavy)) - weapon and armour progression is bland.. half a dozen different types of armour (with a light, medium or heavy variant), that level up as you go...and a few unique variants. Weapons types are greater but similarly limited (4 different damage types to choose from)- unique weapons and armour don't scale as you level them up, and quickly get superseded by standard variants of newer armour in newer zones- weight limitations are quickly hit with the almost useless (at least on easier difficulties) food/buffs or weapon mods.- boring and repetitive enemies. - companions are shallow and have little to no interaction with each other. Baldur's Gate this is not. 6.5 / 10. Buy it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Some pretty average reviews on this one....People comparing to Fallout, or Borderlands....While i can understand the comparisons, I think this game is great blend of the two.  For all the reasons I hated Fallout (hacky, weak story line, unnecessarily open world, clunky combat system and constant game ending bugs) and the reasons I didn't like borderlands (terrible story line, missions/quests that had no importance) this game i felt like got it right.  Also keep in mind I do like BL and FO, but if everyone is comparing to these two, I think Outer Worlds is hands down the best.  First, its a fully fledged game, and I encountered ZERO bugs...ZERO! I cant think of the last time I could even say that about a game.  That is no small feat. especially in this day of rapid development.  Took me 30 hours for my first run through, and I did every mission.  I will definitely play again to see the alternate outcomes, and check out the DLC.Graphics are great, sound/audio was great.  The story was fantastic. lots of sub plots that actually were intertwined into the main story and weren't pointless.  Your main companions also showed some character development as well.  The combat was satisfying, especially after modifying weapons and tinkering.  The ability to equip your companions and change their tactical approach was nice.  I found that special abilities confusing at first but they were useful.  The different weapon classes were good, and and offered variety.  I enjoyed that this is not a full on open world game. It gave enough space to explore and find hidden spaces, and i didn't have to walk for 10 minutes or ride a clunky vehicle to get where i was going.  Also the fast travel was fine IMHO. I hate it when games make you walk or travel endlessly.  I found this a good blend; yes you will still have to manually go places, but it takes maybe 2 minutes where in other games it can take you 10 min or more. I was able to stay immersed into the story and wasn't distracted by unnecessary long hauls on random terrain. Also i enjoyed that enemies just didn't randomly respawn.  I feel like if you go into a town, and murder everyone, they should stay dead....seems simple. If you like a good story in a FPS with some RPG aspects, this is it.  My only gripe would be that they do try to blend in some comedy here and there, but it never really hits and I found it unnecessary.  Its not a genre defining game, and its not going to start some new benchmark in gaming.  It IS a well thought out, and entertaining game.  8.5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm obsessed with dystopian novels, games, and the likes. It's a combination of the way it makes our reality seem a little less disastrous and it's just plain interesting. So when I heard about this game I immediately had endless fantasies about how exciting it would be. I knew these fantasies were impossible to accomplish, though. I was wrong. This game is everything I expected it to be and more. It was worth every cent. I can't stop playing it, I'll even play it during online school and miss important things just because it's so entertaining and exciting. The maps are beautiful, the characters are cute and memorable, the story is interesting, and the quests are enjoyable. They have a Doom-like aspect to them but with a bit more story and less murder. If you love sci-fi then I DEFINITELY recommend this game. Even if you don't, it's a great challenge and a game that you can never really get sick of. Not for me, anyway.

_childDocuments_.review: The problem with this game is the comparisons. Obsidian just came off on PoE 2 and also released Grounded the year after. This game came out when they were clearly spread thin, but the writing itself is still top-tier.The comparisons to Fallout:NV are bound to happen, but this engine was created from the ground up. New Vegas had the models and engine established already. I love New Vegas, and it is clear they want to go back and touch those old moments, It is semi-open world rather than just open world, but I think the writing is too good to just dismiss this game as subpar. I believe the sequel to this game will be an event worth attending. Hopefully, they don't do too much at one time again, since Avowed is coming out soon too. This game feels like a satire of the Mass Effect franchise--I would recommend it for anyone who enjoys it, or wants a small time RPG with big aspirations. 30-hour wheelhouse, but very polished and hilarious story. _childDocuments_.review: I beat the game once with the full evil (side with the Board) playthrough since I figured it would be the quickest.  You feel like a real scumbag after going that route, but it also brings out the worst side of all the other characters in the game, which is pretty interesting.  Your "good" companions will berate you for committing genocide and murder but in the end they're fine with wiping out their hometown or doing heinous deeds, showing they are just as rotten as the player can potentially be.  And Phineas' arrogant berating of the player for their betrayal shows him for the whiny, egomaniacal character that he is.  He unfroze a random person and expected them to be his willing slave forever after and save the world, what could go wrong with that plan?I'm working through a full completionist good guy playthrough now which is more what I prefer to play.  I'm about halfway through the main game and have completed the Murder on Eridanos DLC.  So here's my review.The game engine itself is not great.  I've got a good rig and had issues with lag and performance, as have many others.  Setting the graphics all at about medium at least made it playable.  The combat and game are good enough that I can deal with the technical issues but it would have been nice if the engine were more optimized.There were mechanics that were entirely pointless.  Namely, the weapon degradation and the tinkering were really annoying.  Game devs need to understand that games are meant to be fun, not grindy.  If they cannot implement a mechanic in a way that makes it fun and not just a time sink, it would be better not to have that mechanic in the game at all.  And as a gun owner IRL I can say that quality arms can fire thousands of rounds without parts failures, so weapon degradation as depicted in games is something I usually hate because it's so poorly done.  In TOW both degradation and tinkering felt like they were just there to be able to add features on a checklist, but they detracted from my enjoyment of the game.  Fortunately there are mods to get around this.Another thing that was annoying was the Parvati romance quest, which I decided to just not do (and actually shot the one gal on my evil playthrough just to get the quest out of my quest list).  There's no option for romance or relationships with any of your companion characters, but for some reason the devs thought it would be a good idea to have this drawn-out, fetch-questy, ultra-cringe lesbo romance that you, the main character, have to assist Parvati with.  It felt unnatural, counter to the point of a video game, and preachy, to be honest.  For a game without other romance you are rubbing a side character's sexuality in my face a bit too much.  But the quest was completely optional so I can't complain too much.Things that TOW did well?  Gunplay was really fun, though sadly there were just not enough enemies if anything.  The game is also much better with a mod that makes gunplay more lethal and realistic.  The weapon mods and variety of arms, and their different feel, really were done well.  I'm a real gun nut so gunplay is super important in any game for me.  Weapons felt solid and impactful.  There was a good variety of normal firearms, energy weapons, and the mods allowed for changing things up and fine-tuning even further.  Very enjoyable.Characters, quests, and settings are interesting and unique.  Lots of choices on how to play.  You can just wipe everything out and keep on rolling (not recommended though) or work around major tasks several different ways.  There are several different endings to the game.So the only real downsides here are engine optimization and the busy work features of tinkering and weapon degradation.  Honestly it's a fun little game so far and it really does put a spotlight on a lot of societal ills facing us in the modern world right now.  There were parts of the game that were downright thought provoking.  If you like sci-fi spaceship shows like Firefly, Dark Matter, Farscape, etc then you should give this game a shot.The game is rather short, so I would recommend playing the base game, and if you like it grab the DLCs which are each about as long as the main game itself and I actually enjoyed Murder on Eridanos more than the main game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a casual RPG with a semi-linear story line (you can do some things out of order but various locations remain locked until you progress). Your choices will matter (particularly in the end-game) but are not really critical - you can certainly get by having made the "wrong" choices.  There is more than one ending and the character build is varied enough that you can easily play through a few times to see the different paths and still have a different gaming experience (melee vs sniping vs close in weapons just as one example).Also, I swear the voice of ADA is actually GLaDOS from Portal - which totally freaked me out the first time I heard it.

_childDocuments_.review: Outer Worlds is essentially the spiritual successor to Fallout New Vegas. It is an RPG shooter with a focus on a darkly humorous, heavily satirical story. The game delves into some DARK themes but does it all in the name of satire.The visuals and sound design of the game are all well done enough. Not the cutting edge, but pretty enough when it needs to be. The planets and general setting are reminiscent of old sci-fi movies, with lush, little bit ridiculous plants and fauna, and old retro-futuristic robots and spaceships. It all works well and has a cohesive feel to it.Gameplay wise it is your fairly standard RPG fare. You level up from XP which you get from quests, dialogue and kills. When leveling up you get skill points and every other level you get a perk. You spend maybe half the time in game in combat, with the other half being talking and exploring, so lots of skills focus on things other that shooting. They designed the system to get you up and running quickly, where you points go a lot further lower levels, so you feel like you are improving a lot, very quickly early game, but then it slows mid game, and basically stops late game when you hit level cap. The armor and weapon upgrades help you feel like you are getting more powerful when levels start lacking to make up for it. It is all good enough in my opinion, and it felt good early game, but really lacks punch late game. I both felt like I didn't have enough skill points in the end and didn't actually care in the things I could invest them as I hit levels above 20.While all the above is fine, maybe a bit mediocre actually, what you are here for and what takes center stage is the story, writing and characters. This is game is funny, messed up, and an absolute joy to explore. For example, early on you go on a quest and discover that the corporation has a gravesite tax for when the employees inevitably get killed by their job. And if you accept to collect it, you find out one of the people who is being charged the gravesite tax as "next of kin" isn't related to the deceased but just found the body. Meaning she was "next to" the body when it was found. Its just that sort of game. I of course butcher the joke here, but the games delivery is spot on. And there are just so many funny, memorable moments here. You just want to talk to every character, find every conversation, get every bit of hilarious lore. You want to talk to Martin the depressed mascot, the bowler hat wearing man who says "wink" out loud, even just the postal clerk. Everyone has a personality and something worth saying. And that isn't even mentioning the companions,  who are well developed, varied characters that stay with you almost the entire game. While I could gush over the great writing and characters forever, it is clear however that towards the end of the game they started to run out of steam and ideas. You spend a lot of time sneaking around abandoned corporate labs reading about insane corporate policies, to the point where it loses its novelty. I didn't really notice a drop in quality so much, I just started getting dejavu. And the last two planets you visit don't feel like they have nearly as much stuff in them as the previous ones. It is a little bit of a pity, the game makes me want to explore every nook and cranny and find every scrap of writing, but it all starts to feel pretty samey. Outer Worlds is best suited for a casual run through, going through the main quest and the big sidequests, because delving into all the side content is not as rewarding as I'd hoped. In the end though, if you enjoy good writing and dark comedy, this is the game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Aloha, this is my review of Outer Worlds. A FPS RPG set in a science fiction dystopian future, and plays like the love child of Fallout, Max Payne, Bioshock got drunk and watched Flash Gordon. You are the lone wanderer, awakened from a lost colony ship and can choose to help [or kill] the inhabitants of Halcyon. I played as a stupid "Starbarian" that punched, shot, and stabbed through the galaxy to a bowl of ice cream. The game is an space themed amusement park, you pass through, shoot the cans, talk to the fortune teller, leave with your stuffy space gorilla.The Good: the graphics were colourful, the setting was unique, combat was fun [you get to use Bullet time to do strategic attacks], character customization was decent with multiple builds being viable, and sliding difficulty and multiple factions and paths to take to encourage multiple plays. The story was decent, from what I could tell and there are multiple ending depending on who you help or kill. I really liked that I was able to play through the entire game by shooting mindlessly until the end and still got a half decent ending, even after eradicating an entire town [something that would usually plot break another game] the game was like "Okay, their company now hates you and charges you 50% more" instead of the usual "you can't kill him, plot armour reasons", I even killed one of the main companions accidentily because of this, so good on you.The Bad: The characters were unique... but spelt yuniqweh, everywhere you went there was "Hey, I'm quirky, notice how quirky we are." then they would say or do something to tell me how quirky they were. After the first hour I started skipping most of the dialogue, because Lord suffering was it bad. The characters were flatter the further you played, and the more cardboard cut outs I saw, the more I shot. Until eventually it was like an Undertale genocide run. The companions were meh, and I spent most of the game with the emotionless robot that was obsessed with cleaning, because we shared a similar goal, eradicating all life. Which despite my best efforts to play a stupid "Starbarian" I got a pretty decent and optimistic ending, with ice cream!The Ugly: "Don't worry boss, I'm good with numbers."
