_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed the Outer Worlds, it really scratched an itch I didn't know I had for a fallout-style space western game. It has its limitations, a lack of mechanical depth in certain areas, but its clear that these largely arise from a limited budget during development. For what it is, The Outer Worlds is an excellent and enjoyable game. The writing and voice acting is really good, all things considered, and definitely beats out that seen in comparable Bethesda games. The factions and world are interesting and the companions and side-characters are well developed and extremely likeable. The gameplay is good, but not exceptional. I can't pick out anything specifically wrong with the gunplay and combat, other than it just seems a little off at times. I think the game could maybe benefit from a more developed combat HUD, since I often found myself losing track of enemies, but that could just be a skill issue on my part. As a fan of Firefly, I think the Outer Worlds captured the vibe and feel of that setting very well, and I really appreciated the homage paid to the series. One of my larger critiques would be the weapons. There are simultaneously a lot of them, yet few feel particularly distinct. This even goes for the unique weapons, which rarely have an effect that makes them stand out beyond just a stat boost, and as far as I'm aware (outside of the Science Weapons) none have unique models or textures to differentiate them from regular weapons of their type. The one unique weapon that stood out to me was Irion's Flintlock, which had a truly unique effect, firing in two-round bursts rather than single shots like the regular variant of the pistol. It would have been nice to see more things like this, unique effects that are more than just a specific stat modifier, or an effect that can be made obsolete through modifying a regular weapon at a workbench. The inability to modify unique gear also remains a huge drawback. Ultimately though, I'd highly recommend the game, and I can't wait to see what Obsidian can accomplish with more resources going forward. I'd give the game a solid 7 or 8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: - It feels polished, as in animations and controls are mostly smooth, feels mostly optimized.- Yet still has glaring issues such as sounds will cut in and out, Save bugs, and performance issues carrying over from console.- Shameless low effort Console Port, developers didn't even bother putting in keyboard for control layout screen.- Only 6 companions total in game, you get to use 0-2 at a time. ( I liked Parvati best )- Rewards feel underwhelming.- No prompt that you can skip through dialog using  key.- Inventory seems to clog fast- No indicator/Feedback when you have same model weapons with better stats then currently equipped.- Beyond face customization, expect a very lackluster character customization system for the current generation of games. (very disappointing)- Story and characters often feel, shallow & hollow as expressed in other reviews.- Many dialog options will lead to same/similar results (big turn off, given it is so story focused.)- Though it is open, feels very linear, there is definitely a specific order they are pushing you towards visiting places to unlock the broader content. Places you visit before intended time in main story feel lacking in purpose to be there.- I appreciate that they didn't hypersexualize all the women. (You can give your lady a beard)Due to my love of Fallout 3, Vegas, Morrowind, Oblivion, Skyrim etc... each of the titles listed I have put in between 700 - 1200 hours of game play EACH before thinking about putting them down for another game. Players loyal to this genre should not expect the same mileage and replay-ability. After only 20 hours I found myself missing my other games and finding "The Outer Worlds" much less engaging, juicy, or as open world feeling as I would like.After 20 hours of playing the game I just don't care or feel any emotional attachment for 99% of the characters or the fate of this fictional universe, I feel apathetic towards the story/world.The series of map levels, lack of variety in mechanics, and equivalent fetch quests, betray the beautiful art style, audio work and concept this was built upon, and sadly I expected more from this studio especially vs. Bethesda.I just can't recommend this game a this time even for the 50% off price of $29.99, and would advise anyone to give it a hard pass for any higher price. I can see the passion put in, it isn't technically bad, it simply just isn't a fun or rewarding game to play if you have played many games from the same genre before.Could be a solid experience for first time players into games like this.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game. Writing this as the final credits roll.It takes a little while for this game to get off the ground, but once it does, you can really see that this is the true successor to New Vegas. There is so much you can do that you don't necessarily have to, that ends up getting you better quest results and better story endings for characters/factions. It rewards you later on--and in better ways than just loot--for exploring, reading every scrap of info you can find, searching for every hidden area.On a slightly negative note, the combat very much inherits from New Vegas. VATS has been replaced by Tactical Time Dilation, and there just aren't very many interesting/creative choices you can make in combat. Using cover is fairly worthless except for reloading because the enemies don't really miss shots. And apart from a few encounters, the difficulty of combat is trivial. In playing through this and learning to enjoy the combat, it was much less about how to beat an encounter and survive, and more about how badass you can feel by selecting the right weapons, spamming your companion abilities, and mowing through enemies like the killing machine that you are.Overall, the story felt good. It was familiar and comfortable. Your choices mattered. It ended well.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a little slow to start and the gameplay is a little stale shooter but once you actually get past the first hour or so of setup and you meet the people inhabiting this region of space you kind of get attached. I ended up doing all the side quests even though they were mostly fetch quests because I enjoyed the story bit it would unlock. If you just want kind a mindless shooter with some interesting story and decision making then this is the game for you. I wouldn't say pick it up full price but at 50% off this is definitely a steal.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: I've played for 17 hours. I don't want to go back to it. an "RPG on Rails" with heavy-handed political correctness. Most women are basically good, most men are basically bad (and other standard PC tropes also make their appearance). I didn't appreciate that (SPOILERS!) the good vs bad choice in the first area was essentially tyrannical poverty over liberal-minded cannibalism. That's ... that's modernity. I don't come to RPGs to have an exaggeration of reality thrown in my face.A separate note is required for the visual style. There are jaw-breaking areas, but 90% of this game is ugly. Just straight up bright-colored and ugly. I don't know what they were thinking with their stylistic decisions.Some of the humor hits me the right way - it's the blackest of black humor with sarcastic and satirical elements, but it is too few and far between.I was fooled by the fact that some of these people worked on Fallouts 1, 2, New Vegas. That feeling is very sparse here.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay is very repetitive and you get bored of it after awhile. Hard was difficult when there was a lot of enemies so I just changed it back to normal and I enjoyed the game far better. Consumables were mostly useless. Most last about 15-25secs and even deduct attributes of your character. Kind of pointless.This was the only game I bought an expansion pass for and I've got to say that although I got bored of the shooting, the story, characters and the characters dialog was very enjoyable. I would play it again but on Story mode.Would recommend it to someone who's just looking for a single player campaign game but only if it's on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: Good quests, interesting story, reminds of Fallout a bit but flashier, pretty funny at times as well. Very nice art, sort of like a space western, it has some of the Firefly (the TV show) charm, especially with regard to your ship. Downside is that it's still bugged a few years since release. Crashes and broken quests happen. There's also a low level cap.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: As a big fan of both Mass Effect and Skyrim, I never really thought of those two as having a baby together. That's what the outer worlds felt like to me. The weirdest part is, I ended up enjoying my first run through of outer worlds waaaaaaaaaay more than i thought i would. There's something about running through a derelict planet, fighting off weird creature, and then stopping to take a break only to realize that you've wandered into the house of cannibals. The story is interesting and the voice acting is outstanding. I really felt for the characters and the delivery was quite enticing. Whether you enjoy a real challenge or just casual gaming this game has something for everybody. I highly recommend it and will update this review after my second play through.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: You can see the Fallout New Vegas in this, but just barely. Pros:- the concept of a dark humored unknown world, Obsidian spent a ton of time creating the world- there are very clear takeovers from FO - NV, no fancy cutscenes, and the conversation is fun, simple but not annoyingly simple.- the RPG system is fantastic behind the scenes but maybe a bit too simplistic- the guns are funCons:- sidequests mostly consist of fetch this, talk to that. You get bored of that very easily- Borderlands (=outer worlds?) type respawn, enemies everywhere without sense, go and kill and die many more times is an obvious filler, maybe Obsidian had no time left- the plants, why do they feel the same? no change in gravity, no affect on your skills- difficulty: you start on hard or medium as I did and you WILL lower it just to get through a barrage of enemies
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: The Outer Worlds is a decent game with an alright story. It includes really good RPG mechanics with in depth and meaningful choices which is to be expected as it was made by Obsidian. The world, or should I say universe is really well built with lots of depth and lore to each of the factions, just like fallout. The gunplay is also decent, not amazing but it works.Overall, it was a fun experience and I would for sure recommend it to any RPG fan, especially fallout fans.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: This game makes Fallout 4 look good. Todd Howard is laughing his chess-club ass off somewhere on a giant pile of money.This is not a review. These are my impressions after 4+ hours of playing.---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------The Outer Worlds is probably the dullest RPG I've played in awhile. The choices are lackluster due to everything being black and white as far decision-making goes. The characters are generally uninteresting and unlikable save for the odd companion and NPC. The story lacks any sort of motivation to keep me playing too. For an RPG, that's the kiss of death already and the gameplay isn't much better. Weapons aren't very fun to use, RPG gameplay mechanics like lockpicking are just there because they have to be. This game can't live in New Vegas's shadow let alone by itself surrounded by almost no competition in this space where true 3D AAA 3D RPGs have been dead since the mid 2000s with the odd exception every now and then.There's some decent fun to be had surrounded by all the bad writing and mediocrity but it's not worth $60, not even $30. In my 4 hours of playtime, I did not care for any of the characters, story or any gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: I am a big fan of games like these and it does have some similarities with Fallout, but is way shorter. I got it at 67% discount and for that price I can recommend this game as it is fun and I like exploring.  To pay 60 euros for it, nah, it is not THAT good or long. I also played the DCL's and finished most side quests, all done in 50 hours including the main game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a big boi now and cannot afford to sink 1500+ hours into a game like I used to in other Bethesda games (I know, I'm bad). That's why i love the Outer Worlds - The story has momentum, the characters all have a purpose and THERE ARE NO RADIANT QUESTS that can occupy your time!Here is a game that you can get everything out of without getting that open-world exhaustion. (Having said that, I think when I'm done I may go back to Fallout 4, as I miss all my settlements!)
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, really enjoyed it. I love how everything you do before will contribute to the ending. It was such a surreal experience seeing the people I helped out in the past come to my aid in the final quest. With that being said, It sucks how romance option isn't a thing and it's actually impossible to romance with anyone. Though the romance thing is a minor-setback compared to what the game has to offer in other areas.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. The combat felt a bit wonky at first but once I got used to it, it was enjoyable. The RPG elements of the game are really strong. Lots of meaningful choices and difficult decisions to make.  I bought both DLC and I'm glad I did. Will definitely be picking up Outer Worlds 2 when it comes out,
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: this game is the one of the best single player rpg's bar none. the only draw back their is, is the games play time i did nearly ever single side quest and main quest for the game and the dlc and just managed to hit 50hrs but ever second of that game time is soooo worth it. stop reading this buy the game and start playing!!
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most tedious, un-enthralling and genuinely uninteresting RPGs I have ever played. Amazing idea, absolutely awful execution. Combat is woeful, levelling system is completely unneeded (really adds nothing to the game other than you can sometimes say another line of dialogue, which changes practically nothing, wowzers!). People will rave about the amazing world building, I have just finished the game and honest to god couldn't tell you the main antagonists name, they're so undeveloped and irrelevant to the whole plot. The world is pretty enough but thats about it. The worlds dead, the NPCs are lifeless, you fight the same 5 enemies over and over. It's like a proof of concept that got released as a full game. Quests are tedious and uninspired (oh cool, a mysterious family has invited me in for dinner, I'm sure they wont be cannibals for the 5354th time), the quests for your companions especially so. By the time I got to Byzantium I was so over even pretending to be invested in the story that I just shot everyone I came across, which given how awful the combat is didn't really improve the experience. I played it back on release date on the game pass and found it boring then, I had hoped that with updates and time that would have changed, but no, it's still an overhyped pile of trash. Avoid, unless you feel like wasting a few hours and can get it really cheap.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think people are playing the same game I played because I don't understand all the positive reviews. 1) When I leave the cave and blow up those explosive barrels I see one of those little green lizards clip into the ground (it was the ground not just hiding in the grass.2) Draw distance is limited and pop up was bad even on ultra setting. (I know it's not my system, Ryzen 7 5800x with a gtx 1080ti.)3) Enemy AI is bad, the human Bandits just run stright at you, the one that have guns just run to a certain distance and start shooting in the open with no cover.4) The NPC animations of those 2 cops when you make it to the ship kept repeating and mirroring each other.This game was bad, Skyrim has better AI and draw distance and that game is 50 years old. The game probably has a very good story but with all the problems I couldn't last longer than  an hour.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: Best game I've played since New Vegas.   This game has an abundance of heart & intrigue, and a very relatable anti-corporatocracy vibe that was very satisfying to dig into.   Of course, that's just the path I chose.   Whatever style you play, and whatever choices you make, the game will have a few hidden gems for you along the way.    Thanks, Obsidian; I needed that!    Looking forward to another playthrough, this time on Supernova!
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: Optimization is still dreadful. 2070s and Ryzen 7 3700x get around ~80fps on High settings at 1440p.The gameplay is just boring. Shooting is barebones. Leveling combat abilites only grants you some passive effects that are quite shallow. Exploration and loot are boring. All you find, wherever you go, is ammo, cash and random consumables sprinkled with n'th of the same gun model. Within the first two areas of the game you will have seen 80% of gun and weapon models the game has to offer. Weapon and armor modding are boring, uninspired. Just slap a +3 mag size or +x physical dmg reduction.I decided to go a lone wolf path, because i cba with these companions. So... uninteresting. Boring characters... Writing is somewhat interesting at times, if you can get past the Talking Heads From Oblivion. They even give you an option to turn in your biggest ally at the start of the game. Sadly it doesn't do anything and the story just goes on as it normally does.It's a watered down and minimized New Vegas. With little to no innovations to push the game into 2020. It feels old and boring.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: My friend got me this game for my birthday. I was skeptical at first because I have really bad motion sickness and I tend to stay away from FPS games. I decided to give this game a try and I couldn't put it down. With some simple setting adjustments, I was able to play the whole game without having any headaches or dizziness as the game doesn't have intense fighting scenes. The story line is amazing and if you are the type who gets engrossed with stories, then I think you will love this one! Loved it so much that I bought the other 2 DLCs. Base game took me about 17 hours and the 2 DLCs took me another 15-20 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: Whilst I wouldn't consider it to be nearly as good as it has been hyped up to be it still stands as a solidly enjoyable experience. I encountered a couple of crashes and bugs in my playthrough although nothing too difficult to deal with as the autosave is pretty frequent. It really does feel a lot like fallout and I'd say that if you enjoyed the feel of the fallout 4 nuka-world dlc then you'll probably like this a lot, it's got quite a bit of charm and even though they really went in on the 'corporations bad' route it didn't always feel like simply opposing them at every turn was the best choice. Solid game 8.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: This game is unbelievably short. Its a good game, unique mechanics, all the right parts are there. But I finished it in 17 hours - trying to do all the sidequests and everything available. The main questline is just ridiculously short, this is a good passtime, but there is simply not enough content to make it as great as it could have been. The worldbuilding is a exactly like mashing Bioshock 3 and Fallout New Vegas together - clearly heavily inspired from both games and taking a lot from each. Its a good game, but not great, though it really seems like it could have been, and I really wish it was.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: I've honestly never played fallout and haven't played many rpgs either. The last one i played was kotor and i absolutely loved it. I never found a game I enjoyed as much until I found this one. Story is great, companions are cool, and the lore is pretty amazing. The music aint half bad either. Overall i definitely reccomend this game if you're looking for something to put many hours into.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent story - definitely not shoot me maniacs. Graphics are OK and for once the avatars are not ugly. When playing, you would expect more from it. Being able to settle your own colony,  being able to do quests or trades  in order to increase your appreciation.I definitely await the version II with a more flexible outer world, more alien creatures (not always willing to kill you, some shy to hunt, others to catch for breeding, etc...).All quests done is a starter to a new adventure, but adventure never came as the game suddenly ends when the main quest is completed.Respawning  is slow and the item to loot/collect is not always replenished - maybe something to work on. _childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: The game OK-ish, but in no way what I'd hoped. Story starts of nicely enough, but kind of grinds to a halt as you are left on your own to explore and go wherever you want. It seems they wanted to make kind of a mass effect/fallout hybrid, and in doing so really failed to do both. Your companions and their troubles are a bit bland and devoid of much personality, and after too long the main quest becomes so much on the back of your mind that it's in no way motivating to carry on.  This, of course, doesn't have to be a problem if the open-world component of the game is good, but sadly it really isn't. The world just feels....bland, and for the most part empty. Nothing in terms of wonder, tension, and exploration... The humorous tone of the game is often quite well done actually, but also downplays any sense of urgency you might still have had given above-mentioned problems. While the game gameplay-wise seems lost between something open world and story-driven, the most annoying part is perhaps the performance on PC and the fact that it's an incredibly lazy port. The most telling example is perhaps the V-sync: The in-game V-sync absolutely demolishes your framerate, to the point where the actually advise you in the game NOT to use it. Without v-sync however, the game stutters quite frequently when moving around and looking around, even when FPS is decent. Now you'd say: just enable it via your NVIDIA driver, but here's the thing: you can't. It has something to do with it being a Windows Store application, and therefore being 100% shielded from any outside interference. Only way I've found that works is use rivatuner and force a global framerate. Long story shot, I might see myself finishing the game because it's not THAT bad, but I certainly wound't recommend it to anyone, and kind of regret my purchase.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: What an amazing game....I was gifted The Outer Worlds as a Secret Santa present this year and while I am only ~10 hours into the game, I absolutely love it! This game offers so much potential to create your own story and to play the game the way YOU want to play it. Feel like being a no-nonsense space cowboy? You can do it. Want to be a "by-the-book", straight moral compass hero? You have the power. This game is literally all about making your own choices.I'll update this post as I go further into the game but I can't imagine I'll do anything else but rave about it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fun, but I feel like there could definitely be more customization. The first planet felt pretty empty other than the environment.  Another thing I would like to point out is how fast the evil questline takes place , it felt very rushed as though I didn't get to stop and smell the roses as with other games like Fallout and Elder Scrolls. On the positive side, I enjoy the lack of microtransactions and getting a full game for the money I paid. I just hope that Obsidian keeps this up and doesn't try to monetize the hell out of their next game.  I expect good things in the future.How well does it run?I think this game could definitely use some performance enhancement. Running it on a GTX 1070, an I7-7700HQ with 16GB Ram on Ultra setting produces frames of around 40-70 FPS on my unit. Not sure about how other PCs perform with it but I feel that it could be better.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: I have not enjoyed a game like I have this one in a long time. The gameplay is so much fun and the story/world building is incredible. I cant wait for the second one! They prove that if a world has enough detail and life to it, it doesnt need to be 500 miles across. Everything in this game feels so handcrafted and thought out.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: It's just so f-ing boring. Story is uninteresting. Quests are uninspired and repetitive, the RPG elements are bland (although special science weapons are a nice touch). The most OP/GOAT/META build from combat perspective is one focused on simple and passive HP and DMG buffs to companions - which leads 0 necessary engagement from the player. The abundance of dialogue and texts however also prevents this game from being a chill experience you can turn your brain off and listen to podcasts.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: My only critique in this game is: There isnt enough content..I want more!Seriously, the game itself is quite entertaining, but for me its the lack in variety in this game.Every part in this game feels kinda the same.Good story, good flow, good visuals, meh/ok gunfights, over all pretty solid game.The DLC's doesnt change much, its rather just adding few additional questlines, and a slightly higher level cap, a bit too less for a DLC, still entertaining.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: I am only 5 hours in, but I'm kicking myself for waiting so long.I bought this game because I'm a huge New Vegas fan. It has a very New Vegas vibe with the way the RPG elements are front and center, strong story, funny/interesting characters, meaningful character choices. The world is well developed and exciting so far.That said, it is pretty different from Fallout in refreshing ways. The world and the lore are a lot different. The art style is more colorful and light. The world and atmosphere are beautifully realized.The weapons and combat are just alright. They don't feel as exciting as some other games, including New Vegas. Again, I'm only 5 hours in, so maybe this improves. I don't think you can use grenades in the game, or at least I haven't found any, which seems like a weird omission.I have seen other people mention the game is too easy, and I would agree with that. I don't really mind, but that might bug some people. I might try turning up the difficulty, which I usually don't do because I like feeling powerful in games.Overall it's fun and exciting so far. I feel invested in the story and excited about seeing the impact of my choices play out. I just finished the first section of the game where you are already making some big decisions about which factions to side with and who to make hate you. It is reminding me a lot of the New Vegas factions, which were an amazing part of that game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: Good game for a discounted price. Once its over 50% discounted its definitely recommended. This game has good mechanics but nothing that you've never seen before. The reason why I recommended getting it only when on discount is because I experienced a constant lag and stutter while playing the game. There was no fix to this online. I lowered the settings but still had to endure this annoying stutter. Good game bad coding.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, love it, and I've played through it several times. But I don't agree with the patch being something you have to pay for. Anyone who already owns the game, deserves it for free. Dynamic weather isn't something people are going to be willing to pay an extra $10 or so for, when they already have to pay the $63.96 to buy all the DLC content. And the game on it's own is $59.99. I love Obsidian Entertainment but this is just too far. I hope it was because of Private Division instead because I'd hate to see Obsidian go down this route.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: I like it, wish it was longer and had a new game plus though. Base game is about 40 hours if you do everything going to 60 with 2 DLC's (again if you do everything). If you're an achievement hunter then you'll need at least 2 playthroughs or save a lot before big decisions. DLC's are decent but the last one was released 4 months ago and has had zero updates afterwards so has noticeable unfixed bugs.Excited for the second game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: I would much rather play league of legends tied to an electric chair than to play this game again. The game met expectations that only obsidian games can do. But the enemy types were limited but good and game-play was fun.  It had many ups and then the ending. You talk to some dude and the game ends. with a mediocre photo montage of characters I really did not get to know or at that point even care about. The game fell short of the biggest expectation and that is story arc, character depth, and all around making what could of been a great game that turned into a piece of garbage right in front of your eyes. It made my girlfriend and I really disappointed. we wouldn't have paid over 15$ for it. I WOULD RECOMMEND TO MY GREATEST ENEMIES ONLY.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: Solid RPG from Obsidian. The story is nothing special but it kept me interested. The companions are mostly good. Some of them are rather uninteresting. The AI of companions isn't really good neither is the AI of enemies. Gameplay in general is rather simple but not exactly bad. Dialogue choices are plenty and excellent and gave me a real laugh a few times. Voice overs are mostly good but sometimes you meet an NPC where the voice actor seems pretty bored. Equippable items could have used a bit more variety. There are many armors that are just recolors of each other and weapons don't look very interesting design wise.I listed many things here that are mediocre but all in all I had fun with the game. And the dialogues make up for many of the cons. But I would recommend buying it on sale like I did.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: I know I'm late to the party, but I'm really digging Outer Worlds after I picked it up on a recent Steam sale; it's nearly-perfectly filling my favorite gaming niche of single-player open-world shooter RPGs.Outer Worlds feels like Bioshock and Fallout had a baby, with a little bit of a Borderlands vibe thrown in for garnish. I'm only 5 hours in at the time of writing this post and have barely touched the main storyline so far, but I'm already adoring nearly every aspect of it.If I had to pick something to complain about, I think it would be the HUD/UI. There's a few things that seem a tad counter-intuitive or that they could have been implemented differently, but I'm not expecting perfection; I can easily let these minor annoyances slide when I get into the groove. I also understand why they didn't include a minimap in the HUD, even if it is the #1 feature I miss most.All in all, I strongly recommend picking up this game if you're a fan of games like Bioshock, Fallout, single-player Borderlands, Skyrim, and others in that niche.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: I would call this a generic RPG, don't get me wrong it is done well. It has all the necessary mechanics and they are polished, mechanically this game is very good. However it lacks a certain spark, it lacks a soul if you will. While playing the game I was initially interested in the story, but I quickly became bored with it, I never felt attached to the characters, everything felt generic and not immersive. The side quests, armors and weapons feel bland and uninteresting,  not once have I found an armor that I would call cool and nice looking... Same goes for the weapons.I am really on the fence about this one, however I give this one a negative score, because I finished it half way and I am not planing to pick it up again.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: I think if you're looking for that old Fallout nostalgia you won't be finding it here. The Outer Worlds takes on a life of it's own and while it isn't for everyone I do find that putting past games out of mind when starting in really helps. The game has good basic character design (there's not a lot of customization to be had). The control system whether on keyboard or game pad is manageable. There are some difficulties you may find if you don't remap some controls for companion abilities. Aka you may accidentally kill civilians. Graphics in game are very striking at times! The atmosphere, different terrains and plains could have you in an onlooking gaze before you start moving around the map again. I recommend playing this game for it's story value. There a few different paths you can take, but other than that it's pretty linear. Would definitely like to see a secondary game for this other than DLC.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game as Obsidian have made some of my favourite RPGs over the years, but I just can't.I played it through to completion a month ago and I honestly tell you very little about the world, the characters or their motivations.  It's a game devoid of polish.  Multiple worlds with carbon copy corporations, enemies and plot.Overall a very dull game made very much worse by technical limitations such as no support for ultra-wide monitors, regular crashes and glitches (getting stuck in rocks is always fun) and graphics that makes this modern Unreal engined title look like something Bethesda created a decade ago.I don't recommend this game unless you can buy it at a very heavy discount.  Even then I'd play any other RPG in your list first.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: Positive1) It is great story campaign + good soundtrack2) All characters are great and interesting 3) It is Fallout New Vegas in Space4) Interesting quest lines5) Detail locations with two cool DLC6) Old school inventory + skill distributionNegative1) It is short.)2) Miss survey frome Fallout 4 or New Vegas. Small locations without dungeons or multiple locations.Result: Definitely wait for sale but than you will find pleanty fun.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: It's an interesting successor for the intrepid developers of F:New Vegas, but here's the good and the bad.The bad, in my opinion, it's lacking in terms of combat and tid bits of story, has well has it's never noticeable music or sounds that accompany the adventure, but i assure you the dialogue is top notch, the characters interesting, the companions so good, i wanted more adventuring with them, the visuals altough filled with this annoying neon everything gets corrected with amazing DLC's that showcase the studio's magnificent potentional in detective and mystery stories, with so far two magnificent tales, in a grand exodus through the system, where your actions feel like they have impact.I certanly wished for more grandeur in some of the quest lines, but the madness of the surrounding world proved itself to be entertaining.It's a grand tale, with you at the center of it, and i'm glad to have embarked in it.TL;DR, it looks like New Vegas, but it's lacking in some aspects, but rest assured, the dialogue and the story is not one of those. Get it, i loved each moment of it.

Because literally every single thing about this game was crap. thank god i got this on big sale. who the hell would pay so much for this game?

_childDocuments_.review: All below is my own opinions onlyMain Plot is quite shallow there isn't any gray zone in it and believe me i did try.Side quests at least some are quite interesting and few have quite interesting consequences.Maps are kinda small apart from Terra 1, thus making different types of enemies almost standing on each other. Exploration is hurting, there isn't much stories you can find that are not part of quests.Combat is lacking, in more enemies. Currently enemies groups are to small or/and to space out to appreciate the combat. Ai is well like Ai in this type of games. Enemy design on the other hand is quite good, especially love the guardian robot type, they look very unique and weird.Inventory got a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ filtering, yes you heard it right its in vanilla version and its quite useful if your a hoarder.Equipment itself for me is also nicely done, there isn't much of weapons but each of them behave in its unique manner. So you don`t spend a hour in store comparing 30 different pistols. Armors on the other hand are plentiful but they are quite nicely done especially the difference's between cloth/light/medium and heavy.And if that wasn't enough you get armor kits and weapon attachments to customize their bonuses even further.What i don`t like in equipment is the tinkering system. In case of weapons i would prefer just better/different ammo types, don`t have a idea for armors through.Skills are quite interesting. Especially the dialog ones, love how its also useful in combat.Perks are in need of more and more unique similar to Black Widow from fallout series, also icons and better/funny descriptions would do the trick. Inhaler is quite a interesting idea, but require some more work, since at the moment consumables aren't really that useful.Companions that are useful is a rare sight is this type of RPG and i like the skill system, but it would better if the time would stop when they do their skills so you don`t waste it while in animation your other companion already killed that enemy.And beside ship bonesaw is the best companion :DMy biggest let down apart from exploration was the difficulty level, seriously supernova should be renamed to normal.So even through game feels more like a demo and apart that wall of text above i did enjoy the game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: A solid showing by Obsidian here. Even minor quests had many ways to complete them, and quests were intertwined in ways that made you feel like everything had a sense of purpose.One thing that really stuck with me was the opportunity to venture into a higher-level area soon after the start of the game. The goal is to get to that area, and you can just... walk up. But only if you can fight your way through. The "normal" way to get there never felt like a MacGuffin solely meant to get in your way.The storytelling through logs, messages, and the environments really sell the setting. Somehow notes from middle-management say more than a dialog tree can.I will admit that the combat is more on the basic side, and there's limited variety to the weapons. If you really like using a pistol there are like 7? There's like 3 sniper rifles? 5 machines guns? Across the whole game. At least it feels that way.This isn't an fully open world game, but that's fine with me. I think it lent itself to a tighter experience, even if some of the joy of discovery was missing.I enjoyed the banter with and between the companions. It often made me smile.I would be disappointed if I bought this at full price, if I'm honest, but I did enjoy my romp through The Outer Worlds.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely NOT worth it at full price. I got it on a sale, but still f I had known better, I wouldn't have paid more than 10€ for it.I wanted to love everything, but I really disliked the workshop stuff (though I usually hate crafting systems, to be fair). Graphics are poorly optimised and my framerate danced. Enemies feel like bullet sponges so, as basic as that is, I don't feel like rushing in and shotgunning them, which is something that I usually love. Heck, even the story and the level up perks were somehow not interesting enough. Now the good thing: ALL the NPCs are adorable and dialogue is 10/10 in my opinion. Funnily enough, if this was a book or a visual novel I would have read it to the end.I love the companions very much and I want to see them grow up healthy but I've read other people say the story has an abrupt ending and the companion questlines suck, so... what motivation do I have left to play?Still upvoting it because I understand the devs had difficulties due to COVID and I wish them the best.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend this game to most people, especially fans of fantasy rpgs. It's kind of like Fallout and Mass Effect had a strange love child that doesn't quite live up to either one of those great franchises but has some of the things that made each great.There are plenty of planets and moons to explore, chocked full of lore and environmental lore to discover. Many different enemies to fight, factions and corporations to side with or go against, and multiple endings for each part of the game with two (3 if you count the bad/joke ending) main story endings.My only complaints are the depth of the crew you'll adventure with and the length of the main story arc. Don't get me wrong, some of the crew (Vicar Max) have great quests and thought provoking stories attached. Others simply don't. The main story itself is satisfying but only around 10-12 hours or so, not what you might expect for a game like this.Overall I really liked it and was happily surprised with this game, 8/10.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: I would overall give this game a overall 8/10 for many reasons which I will address in a bit, the game would have scored higher but the DLC "murder on Eridanos" is what really brought the score down. I honestly could not stop playing this game until I finished it including all DLC's.The Base Game: On its own this game was a real treat for me, I love the crew from Black Isle and Obsidian and have missed playing a game with a kiss of their twisted humor. The dialog and questing in the game are really balanced to me, if you specialized into a leadership build you can talk your way through the quests instead of guns blazing. This play through on PC I went with Leadership/Companion build opposite of console I went Solo/High DPS, the difference was very noticeable. The world building is great and I always felt the "edge" of living in space and the consequences of colony collapse. The graphics are really good, the planets you visit are not too big or too small to get exploration fatigue, and the fauna/flora are new and unique. I did not encounter any bugs in the base game, then again I'm playing after they should have ironed them out (foreshadowing). Peril on Gorgon: I actually enjoyed running around the asteroid called "Gorgon" trying to figure out this mad house of horror. The DLC does a good job showing some of the tragedies of scientific research being balanced with the greater good of all. Gorgon itself is amazing looking up and seeing nothing but a thin dome between you and the void game me chills sometimes lol. I liked the quest lines and the areas the DLC will take you through, as well as the new fauna/flora are pretty cool especially the frost creatures. Murder on Eridanos: This DLC evolves around a "who done it", I absolutely love "who done its" in games, movies, books, and shows. However I felt like the pacing for this DLC was slower then I would have liked and it felt kind of like a slog for me. Also having a cheater item to lead you through the mystery shouldn't exist to actually make the player take time to find clues. The new area looks nice and introduces some new flora, and gives off a Venusian floating city feeling. This DLC cost the game a whole point due to the BUGS. I was having combat bugs, audio file bugs, and animation clipping; the whole game was flawless and then this DLC literally crap the bed lol.  My only other complaint is add more guns/armor/mods. I highly recommend this game if you like SciFi/RPG's.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good game, I had fun playing it and it was much better than a lot of the recent games I've played.  I happy that I purchased it; I also purchased it on sale.The game is good but it feels derivative.  In a  lot of ways it didn't have it's own feel, rather it often reminded me of many other games.  Don't see this as a harsh criticism as it draws on some very powerhouse names.  If you like games Fallout 4, BioShock Infinite, Mass Effect, you'll like this game. That is, if you don't mind being reminded about Fallout, Bioshock, and Mass Effect.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: This game has got to be 100% better than Fallout 4. The balancing structure of what you can do in game is great to a point(if your cocky like me you'll keep dying a lot) like in the Groundbreaker when going down a level. The way you can modify guns and tinker with them is so good, the amount of customization you can have is lovely and can be great to settle with your character set. The customization with your character too is great! You have so much freedom making your character what you want them to be, you have actual representation for black to asian which you don't see often. Along with the point and perk system, they are great too! It was confusing at first for my first playthrough especially with the point system. It got better after awhile.The only things I would personally change is the loading screen. I'm unsure if it's me, but I have this game on Switch and PC. And the screens are soooo loong.Bonus points for the LGBT rep, I love you Obsidian!
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: This game is hard to judge, mostly because it has great stuff, decent stuff, and mediocre stuff.Lets be brief.1) GREAT STUFF - Worlds and background/lore/story are great, they did a really good job, the various planets are super nice, and some environments are pretty damn cool ( especially dlc's)- Skill tree/builds/traits are really really well designed, - Irony/trolling on most of the dialogues ( even crucial) is genious, probably they exagerated tho a little bit at the end.- Companions are finally usefull ( in new vegas for example they are a waste of time)- Scientific weapons are great  ( SOME of them at least) -DLC's are really good and fun ( until you get bored of the boring gameplay) -Game runs well and has almost 0 bugs, feels very polished in a lot of tech aspects2) MEDIOCRE STUFF - Gameplay is not good, may feel like good the first 10 hours or slightly more but sadly its too damn uninspired. They added the Q slow mo ( VATS wannabe) that essentially has no utility whatsoever, except the first 4-5 hours, after this amount of time Q can be unbinded because has no use,- Due to the problem above, the game is stupidly easy, too easy, boring easy. And yes if you run a companion build, they are broken AF.3) BAD STUFF- Consumables are useless, they added 1 milion different type of stim, drugs, food, drinks, and every single of them are useless. Except the med stim, nobody knows why. Yes at supernova you need that stupid stuff to survive, still no need to have 40 milion different drinks ( many of them do the same thing)-Unique weapons are trash, crafting is trash, modding is trash.- Extremely limited amount of weapon types and armors, making it very boring in the long term, since theres no real fashion like new vegas where you have a lot of different stuff that you can switch to your wish,- The menus are not intuitive and feels very old while in new vegas you have the pip boy that helps you feel like still "into the game", TOW menus feels like a start menu and feels very outdated.- This is personal but, THIS GAME IS NOT NEW VEGAS, some ppl still don't understand that, and to me, thats a big problem, because unlike new vegas, it lacks what makes new vegas a masterpiece after a decade. This game is cool, but far from what i wish it was.I still reccommend it tho, but only at discoutn

_childDocuments_.review: "The Outer Worlds" is even better than I'd hoped. I'm a big fan of the play style of Prey, Bioshock, and similar games, but I had a difficult time getting into Fallout because it was just so dull to the eyes. TOW is like an amazing update in a futuristic SF setting that I deeply love. I actually care about the characters, have been reading all of the documentation and notes around the world with its lore (not typical for me), and haven't been skipping dialogue the way I typically do when getting impatient. Deeply enjoying this game and look forward to replaying it with a different build later on.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: I think 20 hours are enough time to form ones opinion of a title. This game is pretty much like all the bad things from Fallout New Vegas and I do not understand the hype that surrounded this game. Then again, I also do consider Fallout New Vegas way overhyped.There is no exploration in this game. Invisible Walls abound, making sure you have to stay in the areas and no location, which offers something to find, isn’t bound to a quest in some fashion, thus disincentivizing exploration entirely. Just like New Vegas.. This is a game where you are expected to turn your brain off and let the quest marker guide you.Usually I would read every Mailing log and entry I could find in these games. Here? Those are boring and usually super mundane. Reading someone gripe about inane things like having to keep some animal cages locked doesn’t really add anything, other than stealing my time.There is barely any environmental storytelling, as you might know from Fallout 3. Where you’d walk into a location and go “Huh? I wonder how that happened!”And worst of all, you are expected to make big choices, like the fate of a colony with barely 10 sentences being exchanged. Worse, if you then make the choice you think its best, after you read some mails about how the corporation send killer robots to punish workers, you can’t even use that knowledge as justification.This game is so full of needless jokes it undermines itself. The world is a caricature. Corporations that refuse to supply meds to workers, because apparently nobody told Obsidian how much cost is associated with training workers and they easily outweigh the cost of some meds to keep them healthy and productive. Its like Apple Iphone Production Plants with Suicide Prevention Nets dialed to 11 and used as a joke. “Haha, look how bad corporations are, get it? Get it? Haha!”Obsidian, how about you stop treating people as if they are children? Do you really want to tell me you made a hybrid of Borderlands and Fallout to be aimed at small children that needed to be beaten over the head like this?I am honestly just disappointed. I got the game because I thought it was a good Roleplaying game but the story sucks. The only interesting characters, where the Devs put some effort into are the companions, and everyone else is a bad stereotype.If at least the combat would be fun.. But i am more than half way through the game, at this point (and i am probably not finishing it) and been to 4ish planets and its the same enemies everywhere. Robots, Apes, Raiders, Dogs and Bugs. Only the bugs will be new, the first 4 you will meet on the first starting planet.. And that is as good as it gets.It is just not enough. This game is so worn out in its tropes, it even has the “cannibal family” storyline in it.This game is just unoriginal and trite. I expected so much more and I am done forcing myself through this.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: The game is too simplified. There's only 3 types of ammo and there's a plenty of it. Also, companions can use any weapon and don't use any ammo, so there's not much tactics involed during combat as you can just outfit your companions with the most DPS weapons and just blast through everything. Also, the attempted humor is really bad. It's really a shame, as the graphics are nice (although too colorful, I prefer the apocalyptic look of Fallout). I think  the main problem is that after all the hype and marketing saying it's from the original Fallout creators, I was expecting something very similar to early Fallout games. But this game reminds me more of Borderlands than Fallout, so I am very dissapointed.I will try to finish this game, just for the sake of it, but it's not what I expected at all. If it's on a 70+ % sale, then go for it.

_childDocuments_.review: Not worth $60, i got in on sale for $30, which I feel was fair but overall lackluster experience. Reputation with factions only gives a discount on their vendors, and they also join you in the final battle which feels very forced. Alot of the decisions you make ultimately don't matter, while some have small impacts there is no nuking the starting city, blowing up a secret technological cult, or turning an army of weaponized robots on their owners. The character who saves you is wanted by the police, I made it my first mission to turn him in (the charges of which included forgery, conspiring, fraud, which was a nice touch) but i was able to continue doing missions with him long after I "turned him in". He was never actually imprisoned until the final mission, which seemed like it was going to happen anyways. Combat is generic which is to be expected from Obsidian, but the fact that my companion who's from Edgewater, seems to not give a ♥♥♥♥ that I'm salughtering her home town with lazer death robots, is pretty disappointing. Overall was a nice experience, but I cannot seeing myself playing through it again for any reason whatsoever. Can only recommend if its on sale

_childDocuments_.review: I played The Outer Worlds on Game Pass for PC and absolutely loved it!  I never purchased it on that platform, mostly due to the social limitations.  The Outer Worlds is some of the best writing from Obsidian and it definitely has all the best nostalgic feels from New Vegas and other RPGs they have developed!PROS:+ Excellent storytelling+ Excellent character development+ Lots of humor throughout+ Fun side quests and crew storylines+ In-depth RPG elements (weapons, armor, player choices, etc.)+ Tons of loot to keep you looking for hours on endCONS:- Graphical pop-in can be aggressive when fast-traveling (reminds me of the first Mass Effect)- Short game (can be finished within 20-25 hours easily)- Limited crew member storylines (shame since it's an extremely enjoyable part)"It's not the best choice, it's Spacer's Choice."

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay looked fantastic, the story seemed deep and well thought out. Plus, it's a game made by Obsidian. What else could I ask for! If I'm not being clear already, this seemed like a game I would enjoy a lot.+ The game is somewhat large.+ Biomes are interesting, varied enough.+ The mood is dystopian and eerie.+ A good reputation system.+ A Time dilatation system! Amazing for sneaky sniper gameplay!+ Characters are deep enough so you care (albeit, barely).+ Fun character-specific interruptions during dialogues to make it feel for alive.+ Weapons aesthetics are great.+ Non-speaking protagonist, it's very well suited for this type of game.+ Good UI. Stylised, without being over the top. Some quirks but nothing game breaking.The game controls are slow and clunky in general, especially noticeable in combat. Buttons not responding, a typical scenario: Heated battle, can't jump over that, can't reload press twice, try to step back a bit from the heat, hit a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ sliding rock, stuck in between them, thought you reloaded press and hold the fire button, nothing happen, release it gun finally reloads, HEALS NOT HEALING AHHHH WHY?! You die, from that stupid reptile thing aimboting you with an acid vomit ball projectile from 300m away.Basically, you can't jump higher than a foot. Rocks are all slippery and clearly act as annoying invisible walls yet rocks and stuff are everywhere.Omg. There are 4324892 kinds of food and potions and whatnot that barely feels like it enhance your stats. You're not sure where or when to use them since you have but one of that type of potion from that corporation confusing everything. So they all get stuck in your inventory because ♥♥♥♥ might be useful when I'm getting my ass kick at some place! Look, I could go on, I hate it.There is something wrong with the visuals of the game in general. They introduced the option to remove the chromatic aberration without any INI hack, thankfully! But there is still something wrong. I can't play this game more than an hour or two because my head hurts and my eyes become strained. I am used to play way longer sessions on other games without any problem. I cannot pinpoint what's causing this.They barely do anything. All they do is complain and die. It's not even funny. At least they serve a good taunt before dying. They always scream at you for not using the "right weapons" when I 2/3 shots a mob.Yeah, if you thought Mass Effect Andromeda was bad, think again.I am sad.

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished the game and i feel very disappointed... I felt so excited to explore the vast new universe of Obsidian, to search and find interesting enemies and environments, different planets and a whole bunch of quests and sidequests with twists and turns.. Instead i got a couple of small maps with the amount of enemies that i can count on my fingers and quests which because of the layout of the maps felt linear as f... The main quest's were underwhelming to say the least... The last boss fight felt like an encounter with a nightkin in fallout new vegas, so after the fight i was like: "wait... thats it????"... And the worst thing is that the story line kinda kept me misleading that i will eventually encounter some culmination or big twist, that never happened.... This game had so much potential.... And now i don't even wanna buy the dlc because i'm afraid that i will play it through in 5 hours.... If Obsidian did such a great job story and quest wise in fallout new vegas where they were under such time pressure, how did they do such a below average job in this case???? I'm  just sad.... To everyone who has no problem with paying 60euros for a total gameplay of 40 hours i would still recommend the game...

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not like any first person shooter I’ve played. The best story in the game is actually about one out of five companions plus a cleaning robot. A story which I enjoyed. The story of the main game is far from any good story you can find in a good movie, for instance. I don’t like the concept very much, either. It’s not an open world game. You follow the journal and pointers related to the main game, side quests, and companion quests. But any quest is welcome. Run into people and talk with them. Collect things. The planet called Monarch can be explored freely, although it makes the game more difficult. You should be lead through. It’s about upgrading your skills, your armor, your perks and your guns, which you’ll find if you follow the nearest pointers, before you attack in the open. The shooting part can be pretty easy, although you’ll get surprised by hordes. You can avoid any difficult situation by using Dialog skills and so-called Stealth skills. Stealth is, however, massively disappointing. The companions are both very useful or very useless, depending on the situation. They can suicide in battle to nearly kill the great boss without aiding them in battle. I still recommend the game, which is pretty average. Although, an unusual game. Do the math if you want to play this game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game. Excellent, complex, and dynamic narrative and story that reminds me of Fallout New Vegas and other more "old fashioned" RPGs in many good ways. Beautiful world building, art, and graphics, everything is extremely colorful and detailed. Mostly bug free and very stable too, which was very surprising for a game of this genre.My only significant complaint is that the perk system is a little small and simple, which makes character building less variable and replayable than a game like New Vegas or Fallout 4. There aren't all that many perks and no limitation based on skill or attributes so every character build ends up feeling roughly the same with only a few gameplay variations. The story has enough variability and freedom that it mostly makes up for it.

To me, there isn't anything special about this game, its just a time killer. I don't think I'll be finishing the last portion of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Liked:  Fantastic story, wonderful graphics.  I enjoyed the weapon system... the fact that I didn't have to get a new weapon every 8 minutes was refreshing, and the customization of the weapons made them feel like MINE. Like I had built them and owned them.Average:  I spent about 30 hours total on this game and I kinda wish it had been longer.  I know it's crazy to complain about that length of time, and I didn't feel ripped off, but I guess I wanted ...MORE.  Also the combat was very quick and abrupt.  The final fight I had lasted about 30 seconds against a big robot and the strategy was "spray with bullets."  Not great:  My one complaint here is that I spent quite some time creating my character.  But I NEVER saw that character in any cutscene or... at all. Why even make a totally custom character if you never see it? That was odd to me.Overall:  9/10 Terrific game. _childDocuments_.review: Simple "Would I Recommend This?": Yeah! If you get it for $15 or below it's well worth it. But it's nowhere near a masterpiece, as much as I love the characters.The performance is the worst part of this game. Nearly no matter what PC you have, you're gonna have stutters when on the move. I've got an i5 11th gen, 1660 Super, 16 GB 3200 RAM, and a SATA SSD - not anywhere near the top but nowhere near the bottom either. 60 FPS with stutters on mostly high settings is my experience, and I do not think it should be.The main story is short and mediocre, the gunplay is a means to an end that is only better than Fallout 4 by being less glitchy, customization is limited. The visuals are generally nice, but everything looks like plastic, and the more gritty locations that are supposed to be dangerous or gross are weirdly sterile.The characters are what make this game's case. All of the companions have some aspects to them that make them compelling, particularly Parvati, a very warm, kind, and naive frontier girl who you help set up with her girlfriend. It marks the first time I've seen asexual representation in a non-indie title, and it's done heartwarmingly by a writer who is asexual herself. I just wish Parvati was in a more compelling game. She and the other companions keep me coming back every so often - the banter they have with each other and you is great and each of them have at least some decently written story arc - but the rest of the game usually makes me lose interest before the end.

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome game, though a bit short.Pros:-- The art and atmosphere is great.-- A whole story universe of unique items and vistas.-- The mechanics of game play are familiar and intuitive.-- Good story with various splashes of humor.  Great character development among the NPC's.-- The game has varying story objectives, so there's no shoot-em-up monotony or battle fatigue to ruin the overall entertainment.Cons:-- The game is just too short.  The developers created a whole unique story universe, full of potential, but only delivered a short story arc.  Even with the Gorgon DLC, it was so short.I would definitely recommend this game to those who like Fallout, Borderlands or Far Cry.I really want to see more DLCs from the developers.  This game has a lot of potential.  It's a shame game is over so quickly.

_childDocuments_.review: This game had promise from the outset, until you play it. I do think that it's incomplete without the two DLCs. Yet, the game is rich in lore and the world that is painted is dark yet vibrant. The game is to short compared to Fallout New Vegas and that is disappointing. The mechanics involved are to simplified but the game does have potential if the developers are willing to work with the idea. Overall, the game isn't bad, it just needs to be flushed out with its mechanics and length of story and paths for the character to take.
