_childDocuments_.review: Love it! While not as great as Fallout:NV, that is still a high bar to set. But if you love the humor of fallout 1/2 and NV, then get this game, period. End of review.I stole this game originally from a certain Bay controlled by Pirates, waiting for its Steam release. Yes, I stole it as I do all Epic games, as a serious F YOU to EPIC. I despise Epic. As I usually do, when they are good games, I promptly bought the game once it had a Steam release, despite already beating the game at no cost to me. Once again, F you Epic. Die horribly, Epic marketers.So there is my endorsement on whether this game is good or not: I paid money I hardly have to support the devs even though I had already played this game and beat it. (Plus, to be honest, I want to play the DLC, which unlike a lot of other modern games, looks to be good, an actual expansion of the game.)The story is not completely original, but I still found parts of it to be fresh and quite funny. The combat was decent, and I enjoyed playing it on supernova difficulty. The companions are trash, but few games have good companions, so no big problem there.If you like Fallout: NV, then get this game. Period. I have more fun with this exploring than I did with Cyberpunk 2077, let me tell you. The gear here is more fun, and exploring is more fun than Cyberpunk. And also 99.9% less bugs!
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: It's an actual space colony game. It is from the team that created Fallout so the setting is charming, the people are cool, and the factions are neat. The crew are all well realized, and the mechanics are better than a lot of games. Combat was the part I liked the least, but honestly it's fine, my only major issue was that a lot of the goons look the same, and there are some endgame areas that have multiple factions present, which made this section hard as they will react to friendly fire. There are some bugs here and there but honestly I didn't mind them.Game feels like it was made with some love. My only true complaint is that I wish it were longer and bigger, which won't be an issue as they're making another soon.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely fell for this game! It took me a couple of hours to fully immerse myself in the story and the world, but after I oriented myself a little I really started to love it. I especially enjoyed the way it looks. Locations are very interesting and beautifuly crafted. The storyline is good as well. Its nothing totaly new, but I enjoyed it nontheless. What I find to be very good are the companions, they really felt like people to me and there were many moments when they reacted to something or had a little chat between one another which made the game all the more enjoyable. Not to forget about the ship and ADA, who I've grown rather fond of. All in all, if you miss some good old time Fallout-like game, this one is definitely for you.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a really good foundation for future Obsidian RPG games. I love the direction it's going in, yet again it's limited by the amount of money and time that was spent on it. There are things that need to be improved upon but I see an upwards trend in the quality of first person RPG games coming out of Obsidian, and I hope Avowed and whatever else is in their pipeline continues going in the direction The Outer Worlds took.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: This game has some weird 3D effect or something that hurts my eyes, I enjoyed what I did play, but it is unplayable for me.I searched google and I'm not the only one with this issue, other people said it was Chromatic Abberation however I already turned this off and it still hurts my eyes, makes me feel like i'm going cross eyed.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: The Outer Worlds is what I, an avid fan of Fallout, have been crying out to the heavens for for years. I legitimately believe that this game completely outshines Fallout 3, and definitely Fallout 4 (though that's a pretty low bar.). It does what Fallout 4 set out to do in the first place: Bring the fallout series together as an FPS AND an RPG. The skills actually have weight, the story is compelling, the NPCs are brilliant, and the gunplay is amazing. Happy sailing, Spacer.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: This is not Fallout New Vegas 2.I'm actually a bit disappointed that I have to start by stating the obvious, I've seen a lot of reviews that complain about this not being as good or better than Fallout: New Vegas. People had set their expectations way too high for this game, and it ended up hurting the review scores of this game. Seriously it is a good game regardless.If I were to describe this game by comparing it to some others, I would say this is more like a Mass Effect game with gameplay mechanics from Borderlands, and a skill tree and reputation system from Fallout: New Vegas.Basically in this game you don't have a huge open world to explore, instead you have multiple different locations with varying map sizes to which you travel by using your spaceship.You will face different types of enemies, each of which have their own weakness like shock or corrosion dmg. You will also face marauders which are kinda like raiders of this game and of course faction specific enemies depending on your reputation.I won't go too much into the story or characters of this game, mainly to avoid spoilers. Let's just say that yes, this game has multiple different endings which are affected by your decisions.The characters, especially your companions aren't anything special, they're quite forgettable really.The graphics of this game are decent, textures are pretty high quality and the lighting is great. My only complaint is that the characters look a bit weird, almost waxy.Soundtrack is not amazing. I mean, there was not a single track that made me go "Woah, I have to look that up later!", it was all just pretty generic scifi action music.Same goes for the sound effects in this game, guns don't sound powerful, explosions are underwhelming...At least the voice acting was good, there was no "skyrim guard" effect anywhere and the cast did a good job with their roles.Oh btw, no microtransactions whatsoever, thank god.Honestly in conclusion this was actually a good game in my opinion. To get the most out of this, try to enjoy what this game has to offer, take your time with the side quests and build your character. Don't rush it.TL;DR: It's not a FNV2, lower your expectations. No microtransactions. Has multiple endings, decent game mechanics, ok graphics, meh characters, unmemorable music. Take your time and enjoy it, it's actually pretty good.    (Edit: Fixed a few typos)
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: I have mixed feelings on this game now that I've beaten it. At times it feels like a 9/10 game and I love it, but I felt like I was grinding toward the end. The pacing is uneven throughout the game, the food and drinks are numerous and mostly I didn't care about them at all, a lot of the sidequests for your companions and their storylines just aren't interesting(Pavarti!) and the skill/perk trees are so streamlined that they feel a little shallow which leads to me not wanting to immediately replay the game(like I do with Fallout 3/4/NV). Not having VATS kinda hurts this style of game for me, the gunplay just isn't that fun. That being said I still enjoyed the game and it was way worth the money. Give this one a try if you like modern Fallout games, you'll get some enjoyment out of it for sure even if it can't quite live up to those standards.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: The game is great, the DLCs (especially Murder on Eridanos) are better. My only downsides are that the variety of weapons is kind of low, companions are more trouble than they're worth financially, and the DLCs not locking you out of the rest of the solar systems allows you to get to level ~12, go to Eridanos, get level 30+ armour and weapons and go right back to the main campaign, basically trivialising the progression. Other than that the game is absolutely great and worth the money (on a 20% or more sale).
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: The game is not funny or memorable or even challenging. You can skip most of everything by pressing shift and outrunning 99% of fights, the main story is meh. Overall - the game's a decent time killer and nothing else. A shame since it's THE OBSIDIAN game and somehow they made a game that is even less engaging than Fallout 4.Buy on sale.(wish there was "so-so" evaluation score)
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed the game to the foolest. Fallout in Space. Kinda. Dialogues are gold. Characters are gold. Story is fine because every planet and character has its own charm. Though gameplaywise it is kinda simple really. You become very powerful pretty quick. It took me roughly 50 hrs to play through the main campaign and all the DLC.My two main gripes with this game are that you don't get new compainions (not even temporary ones) in the DLC and that the quest design is not even close to the level of Fallout New Vegas (but nevertheless enjoyable!).
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: After playing for 5 hours I started crashing repeatedly.  About 2-3 minutes after loading into the game I'd crash again.  I tried everything I saw online, I'm not using an overclocked cpu, im not using gamebar, I'm running in admin mode, etc.  Still consistently crashing and cannot play.  I liked the game, it had charm and heart despite being clunky.  I wanted to enjoy playing it through to the end.  But It was a complete waste of money for me.  Even Cyberpunk, with as many bugs as it had, I was able to play for 163 hours with only like 3 crashes.This is an old known problem.  Outer Worlds is 1 1/2 years old, there is no excuse for a blocker severity bug like this to still be in game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: The Outer Worlds has a lot of minor negative sides. But the storyline, dialogs, characters and the atmosphere completely compensate for all the shortcomings. Despite the low-budget it leaves a very pleasant aftertaste. Highly recommend to all fans of space fiction, the Firefly series and sarcastic humor.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: Its like Skyrim but in space. OKay maybe not as much open ended, and with alot more humor and without the mods. But if you like action rpg Outter Worlds is not a skippable.Some remarks:No 3rd person view (its very anoying, but you will get used to it)Dont let the size of the maps fool you, they may be small, but if they any larger you would get lost and never progress the story(hence the skyrim comparison)Get ready for some witty humor. Swap your companions around for some diversity!Its fun to customize your arsenal, but using it is even betterSolid 8/10. If you like the genre is a real shine
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: Damn this game is good and very disappointing at the same time :\Coming from Obsidian it has a fun story with plenty choices, but it also keeps reminding me of how much I love and miss Fallout, New Vegas in particular.The good: +++ It's kinda what you may expect, nice scenarios where you can be who you want, do whatever you want, piss off whoever you want, and massacre them too if you feel like it, that's something I always appreciate.+ The general sci fi ambiance and scenery, nice exotic views+ The combat has some nice improvements like the location damage that you can use for status ailments, and the dash move which I have some fun using with my melee character+ Follower control is perfect this time, I like having hotkeys to send them places immediately anytime and trigger their special moves, feels inspired by Mass Effect which is not bad in this regard. This made me have my main character with a follower build.+ Parvati and Nyoka, kinda, Max I thinkThe bad: -- It's not really an open world, you have a handful of places, somewhat open, but somewhat annoyingly linear and often restricted to paths. The playable areas feel tiny and too few, and the travelling between them is annoying, this is something I also recall from Mass Effect but I didn't miss.- The decissions, ew, I often find myself thinking: Why do I have to choose between these 2 things? I'd suggest a bit of this and that. I'm not clever enough or I don't have an otherwise pointless skill high enough to suggest some common sense and I have to stick to taking a lame side in this conversation? Ugh, so be it, I'll pretend the bs didn't happen during the ending.- The combat again, yeah it has nice new touches but it still feels obsolete in a world where games like Dying Light exist and have plenty moves to keep things interesting- The balance is non existent, I find great difference between builds, a companion focus seemingly overpowered in all senses compared to other archetypes, damage wise and skill wise with the big boosts you get to things like lockpicking or dialog.- How useful everything is, is never clear from the very beginning when you have no idea what you're selecting for your character attributes, let me respec everything including the basics, any limitation to this is a massive waste of time.- Ellie and Sam.It's still money well spent, much more so during a nice sale.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:-outstanding storyline-good gameplay-smooth combat (not clunky)-similar mechanics with fallout new vegas-outstanding graphicscons:-too shortfor fallout new vegas player, i can only say this game is worth full price~but for you who havent, i should say this game is very good and you should play it~(hol on... but are you really havent played FO:NV yet ? ;;) )
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: I am thoroughly shocked by how much i loved this game. There were two things which really stood out to me: 1. The large amount of well written female characters! I was so happy with all of them, it's rare for a game to have enough female representation that is ALSO well written and not riddled with subtle misogynistic stereotypes or only included to advance the plot of some male character2. There was a queer asexual woman!! And she wasn't just mentioned on the side, she was an important character. This is the first time in my life that I have seen myself fully represented in any video game.Besides that the game is really colourful, the 3D graphics are so nice and i would often just run around and look at how everything would independently move in the background.The story is super interesting and has some great anti-capitalist and anti-government undertones. You are able to choose who to side with throughout the game, from all of the different groups who have conflicting interests. It's also quite lighthearted and funny instead of being uber serious and dark. Definitely gonna play this again to make different choices this time and see what happens!
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: Outer Worlds has a problem with expectations. If you go in anticipating an open world RPG with entertaining combat, meaningful character progression and interesting synergies between weapons and items, you will be disappointed. You have every right to expect this based on the images and videos previewing the game, and it is further implied in the discussion of "builds", "perks" and "flaws". None of this matters, at all. Playing on hard, you can use whatever stupidly designed build you want, with all possible flaws and the combat is trivial and boring. After about 10 hours I was losing the will to continue, but my own personal character flaw is completing games, so I kept going. I stopped investigating the entire map (finding nothing interesting) and getting into more tedious fights, and focused on the quests alone, fast travelling as much as possible. Then it became clear, Outer Worlds is a choose your own adventure game and in that context it is quite fun. There are choices (I am an adult, and there is a pandemic, so I will not call them meaningful), entertaining companion interactions and the odd, quite good story arc. I suspect, with an optimised tactical combat engine and levelling that you actually care about, this could've been very good indeed. Still, it is ok, if you manage expectations and ignore the (paid for?) glowing reviews.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: Good lord, am I disappointed in this game..I've tried several times to like this game. I have given it chance after chance until it's now officially unplayable due to the game crashing to desktop without any warning at the same part of the story every time. I really was looking forward to playing OuterWorlds as I am a huge fan of Obsidian's Fallout NV (which could honestly be my fault to compare the two), but this game was just a complete let down. Even if it wasn't for constant game-breaking crashes, the amount of times I've gotten stuck/glitched on an object and forced to reload is insane for a game that has won so many awards and currently has very positive reviews on steam. Aside from the bugs, the gameplay just felt like a lazy mix of Fallout and Borderlands to me. Cons:- The game has crashed to desktop without warning several times.- The difficulty Supernova is unplayable due to it the crashing or getting stuck on objects. You can't save manually in Supernova so If either happens then you've lost any forward progress that wasn't auto-saved. - The AI companions are dumb as rocks. Also, if you shoot a single enemy within a group then the entire enemy group becomes alerted exactly where you are regardless if they are in different rooms or buildings. - The gameplay is very linear. After playing about 5-6 hours, you've pretty much seen it all aside from some enemies with special abilities or more health. Pros:- The different dialogue options and voice acting is done very well. - The weapons are diverse enough to keep the game somewhat interesting. - The story line was okay. What keeps the game entertaining are the different choices you can make between factions.If I were to rate my overall experience with OutWorlds: 4/10Let me end with this: I bought OutWorlds 50% off and I'd refund if I could. Very disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: This game would need a "meh" review button.It is not horrible, but it just got.... boring.In the beginning I had high hopes. It looked like Fallout New Vegas in the Borderland Universe.But after a few hours it felt like a Walmart version of it. Like Fallout 3 in Mass Effect Andromeda.Pro:- The writing is mostly good, and quite fun at times- The worldbuilding is fun (although nearly a carbon copy from Borderlands)- You can play as non combat focus character and do fineCon:- The combat system is tedious. Enemies are bullet sponges. You are a bullet sponge. At least ranged combat is boring (I havent tried melee). I dont know how, but the combat in Fallout New Vegas felt more fun and refreshing, and that is 10 years older- The world itself feels empty. It is less open world than Fallout, and still manages to feel less rewarding to explore.- A lot of the worlbuilding is : "Read this e-mail conversation" - The mainstory was relatively boring.- A lot of side quests are: Go to building A), press button B) bring Mcguffin C)Final Score : Fallout 3/New Vegas
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: It's Obsidian, so a certain level of quality is baked in. The originality of the setting and story are very good, but as usual with Obsidian games, the ambition overreaches the format. A game that is fun to play, a world that is fun to explore, and a smattering of mechanics that are fun to utilize. As a place marker for Obsidian's production quality this checks all the boxes. As a revolutionary or ground-breaking game however this leaves a lot still on the table.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: The dialogue in this game is very well written and its mechanics are well integrated with the RPG elements of this game with skills, character traits and perks all allowing for plenty of unique dialogue choices. Companions and their respective bonuses to skills and perks are clever and actually give you a reason to vary which companions you use in different situations as well as complete their respective quests. I think food could use a bit of tweaking, it provides bonuses to stats and the hangover mechanic is a good idea but I think the option of a 'Hardcore mode' with hunger mechanics might also work well. Will definitely play a second time, looking forward to all the DLCs. Not as big as New Vegas, but weapons and combat mechanics are miles better. The moniker of New Vegas in space is apt and fair. Loved it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. Story is good and has choices, voice acting is good, music and sound is great, graphics and style are nice too, runs very well and havent encountered a bug in 10 hours yet. Good game overall, much better than anything bethesda ever made. The only downsides its nothing new or revolutionary and the gunplay lacks depth.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: I was expecting a lot from the developer's of Fallout New Vegas, one of the most critically acclaimed Western RPGs of the 21st Century, but clearly this is a Left 4 Dead vs Back 4 Blood situation. The game is fine aggressively average at best, the gun-play and world is serviceable. The real problem is the writing, the game is written like you're the dumbest person alive, nothing feels genuine, nothing feels satisfactory, it feels like a serious borderlands game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. Both DLCs are great and add a lot of content to the main game. Quality of writing in the DLCs might even be better than the main game. Full attention to detail in every corner. Outer Worlds is very obviously a labor of love by people who had fun making it, and that is a joy to play.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: A great RPG! Gameplay, combat remind me of Mass Effect series. The story, characters are well developed and interesting. The game is not too long in a positive way. It has just enough of everything in a good way – it is not filled with repeatable, boring filler-quests etc. like some “open world” games these times, which I find simply boring. I highly recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: Decent game, excellent story, fantastic atmosphere, characters are varying in quality, hilarious, tedious and repetitive combat, map could be bigger since its a newer game, but it's sufficient. Overall 7.5/10. Obsidian usually makes good stuff, but they forgot they were making a game and instead of an interactive story. Definitely pick it up if it goes on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: A nice mid-range game, would recommend it.The writing is top-notch: the world and characters feel alive, locations are fun to explore, and the tone is consistent. It's what I keep playing for. Nothing really sticks out as remarkable besides the jingle for Spacer's Choice, though, everything feels very... standard. Just not that refreshing.The graphics feel dated, somehow. It could be the raygun gothic style, which I've seen enough of by now, but I think blurry and muddled visuals are not part of the style. On Monarch especially I have trouble telling things apart both in the wild and in the towns. The movement and combat controls are nothing to write home about either, but I like the bullet time. It flows better than VATS did, more interactive.So far the game hasn't crashed and there have been no bugs besides creature names flickering behind terrain when the creature spawns in. Definitely worth mentioning in this genre.If you'd like an anti-corporate sci-fi RPG, this is an easy game to recommend.PS The game seems a little heavier to run than its physics and visuals would suggest. Since it's been out for a while, I don't expect patches to change that.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: This is, without any exaggeration, the most mediocre game I ever played. The fighting is mediocre, the graphics are mediocre, the open world and exploration are bad but the writing is mostly good so it sums up back to mediocrity. It's like Fallout NV 0.5 at best.After such positive reviews and critical praise, I expected much more.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: The game is pretty good. I enjoy that they added some comedic elements to the story telling. The difficulty of getting a weapon that can equip a silencer mod is weird but after levelling they become more abundant.After almost 60 hours, I have completed all the side quests, main quest and DLC. I really enjoyed the game and the story telling. There were even a couple of plot twists that I didn't see coming.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: Why this games has so many good reviews is beyond me, is so boring, the items are especially horrible and the player progression is so bland. It's the only game where the unique waepons are worse than the normal ones. Also you reach the level cap too soon! I hate the games that do thatif you like to collect food that's the game for you
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: This game was pretty fun.  Kept me engaged the entire time even during the side missions.  The story is well made.  Each companion offers different perks.  Most choices in missions actually change the outcome of the end game.  I beat the game on the 2nd hardest difficulty (which is pretty easy if you are used to first person shooters) and plan to do the hardest difficulty which seems a lot like Fallout 4's hardest difficulty setting but a tad different.  I played a normal "choose all the good options" play though and now I am just going to be a complete butt and choose every worst option possible.  The atmosphere of the game is almost like a combination of Mass Effect, Fallout, and Bioshock.  The game was pretty short, including the side missions, for a total of only 17 hours of game play.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoyed Fallout 4 or the later Bioshock series, you'll probably enjoy this game. It's about 40 hours for full completion, which in my opinion is a pretty nice sweetspot. If I'd wished for something it would have been more character development from a stats and gear point of view. I used the same weapon and armor pretty much the whole game. But the story (which is the important part) and the characters are well written, and I really enjoyed my time in the game :)
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: I just beat the game on my first play through and I had a fantastic time with the game. Stat and perk distribution is fantastic, music is immersive, dialogue is funny and witty, character design is very well executed. As for some of the cons, the combat is very easy on a normal difficulty, there's a lack of interesting weapons, armor, and mods, and the game definitely gives a little bit more to some followers than others. Most followers have a fairly quick 1-3 quest line side quest, Parvarti however took me considerably more time than any of the followers. I'd almost go as far to say her quest line = all of the other followers minus MAYBE Vicar. 8/10 Game for me.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: Love this game, 100% completed it on Xbox Series X. Wanted to play it again on PC but I simply cannot recommend it, the constant random hitches for seemingly no reason makes the game damn near unplayable for me. Tried all kinds of solutions and my hardware is plenty strong enough. Its an excellent game but I recommend playing it on a new gen console if you have one.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: A great visual art style, diverse dialogue choices to fit any personality of character, interesting/detailed quests including the overall story arc is what makes this a solid game. Combat is simple and straight forward, but has just enough weapons and perks to not make it monotonous. The skill tree is diverse enough to play any type of player you would like. Companions you choose to play with actually are helpful and have there own traits and personalities to make you invest in them. Map design is traditional RPG open world however the maps are small by today's standards, but detailed enough that there doesn't feel like any wasted space plus there are multiple maps to make up for the size of the maps. Especially well done is that you feel like your choices in the game do have an overall impact on you and the game. Lot's of reading can be done at terminals to get more context/backstory to quests, but doesn't feel forced to extend game time or save development time.Standard game is around 20 to 25 hours if you plan on completing all the story and side quests. Though this is multiplied if you plan on playing multiple types of characters and different story/quest outcomes.bonus points: no micro transactions.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: IDK what about this game didn't do it for me. I love obsidian, fallout, TES, and other RPGs, but for some reason this game was just "ehhh." It feels incredibly boring and does nothing to keep me interested. The only reason I have 40 hours is because I at least wanted to play an hour for every dollar I paid for the game. I don't even know if I'll finish it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: I have loved every second of playing this game. The story lines are interesting and the side quests keep me well entertained. I like that companions have their own quests too and you can recruit multiple. Other FPS RPGs have gotten repetitive for me but this has brought me back to the genre. It is very unique, colorful and all-around a great design for a game and would definitely recommend to others.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: Great game but as with many newer games the levelcap is too low. I saw a lot of comments on it usually being reached by the end of the game, whilst I was checking if there was a mod to raise it, and those people must have missed content because I reached it fairly quickly. Story is great, though some aspects have me wishing I could make the logical decision without it being "evil" or resulting in a poor ending for some reason that defies logic. If you liked Fallout: NV you'll probably like this, the combat is more refined than anything from that series though it lacks the same amount of options in terms of weaponry.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: I have desperately wanted to play this game, but it has failed me to be even slightly optimized.Texture Pop-in:The game looks pretty good when it works, but god awful when blurry textures get stuck. It seems load time in general are fowled up. On my PC requiring me to go into ini files (Which I couldn't even get to) to fix the issue. Another issue, is the garbage rim lighting that turns everything blue when it should be dark while first-person. Cross-hair and damage:The Cross-hair is not in the center of the screen, and the only fix just breaks the game.This game needs a lot of work and isn't for me.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: PLAY IT PLAY IT PLAY IT PLAY IT PLAY IT PLAY IT PLAY IT PLAY IT PLAY IT PLAY IT(ahem) okay now that I have that out of my system...If you are a fan of the way Obsidian makes RPGs then this game IS FOR YOU. i only have 6 hours, I've done the first planet and already know that this is going to become one of my favourite games of all time.this is really space new vegas, IN THE BEST WAY POSSIBLE. well written dialogue, choices that make you really judge the morality of two equally grey options, clever wit that can (AND WILL) get a chuckle from you.in short, if you like RPGs and like a western style with awesome writting then you should (deep breath)PLAY IT PLAY IT PLAY IT PLAY IT PLAY IT PLAY IT PLAY IT PLAY IT PLAY IT PLAY IT
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: I'm playing through the story. Having fun gathering weapons and xp. The worlds are really beautiful. The creatures are unique and you never know what they will do. The artwork is kind of a pop / art deco combo. Retro and futuristic at the same time. I'm havin' fun playin' and I think it's worth every penny. Great story lines and well written characters.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: What a cool game! I love the embedded criticism and cynicism of this game. It made me laugh a lot of times. The combat is interesting, the character progression and customization is good and the plot is very enticing. A very good experience. Plan to play again in the future with different choices. Totally recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: This is easily my favorite game i have ever played. I could write a novel proclaiming my love for this game. If you like Borderlands, Fallout, Mass Effect, or any of the greatest games ever made, you are sure to love this. I have replayed this many times. Favorite game ever. Highly recommend. If you're curious as to why its my favorite game ever, just a short reductive list: highly dynamic experience all around, gory and humorous, incredibly beautiful and colorful, lots of control and choice (not just illusion of choice, what you do matters) lots of different play styles for great replay ability, challenging but not frustrating, did i mention how cool and colorful and unique the design is? I could stare at screenshots of this game all day. This game is just super fun and chill, its just straight up fun to play. Love Love Love <3
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: The base game is a good time, with very nice graphics and amazing writing 99% of the time.  Some of the dialogue choices you run into a simply perfection.  The gorgon DLC was very interesting, and I enjoyed the style of it.The new murder on eridanos DLC was also interesting, but the "detective gun" mechanic lost its appeal after ~20 minutes.  Sure it has some funny quips sometimes, but mostly its a weapon slot I don't get back for the entirety of the DLC.  The DLC is still fun, and was worth purchasing however.  Lots of cool locations to explore and things to murder.10/10 would be space based psychopath again
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: Humorous, intense, and Tactical Time Dilation is fun, but FAR from overpowered. I recommend multiple playthroughs. I'm doing my first one now, and leaning on companions heavily. Consider a stealth/persuasion type playthrough and a guns blazing playthrough, at least. It is very obvious that DLC and sequels are planned. Great game. Not super long, but still satisfying.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

It doesn't allow for players to live with their decisions at the climax of the game, which is always a bummer.Overall, I wouldn't recommend this game, especially with the new announcement of the Spacer's Choice paid update.

A reminder to myself is to never bring any companion into any of my missions unless I boost my leadership skills, and even then they are going to die regardless, and I will have to redo the entire mission in order for them to remain alive on the board of my ship.Btw there is no replacement for them, lol.And there death are permanent. it's not Xcom.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: The planets aren't exactly enticing, they definitely do not keep me interested in the game for long play sessions like similar games in this genre. That said, the freedom you have in The Outer Worlds is pretty fun to experiment with. I actually enjoy having less to manage in my inventory. I never care about how my character looks, I rarely see them in 3rd person anyhow. I've enjoyed how characters are written, I quickly decide if they're a friend or someone I don't need in my game, IE just offing them entirely. The freedom is immense. Have a serious playthrough or just go into everything like you're Doom Guy and rip n tear. Combat could use some work but the game is likely not going to see a change that large anytime ever. I really enjoyed the game at the time of release, haven't had a ton of reason to pick it up lately other than wanting an easy chill game that has achievements, lots of them. Over 45 I think maybe? It is worth it to get on sale, arguably full price if you've got past experience with Obsidian or just like a good space mystery. I have yet to play any of the DLC content but I will get that when I 100% this game. Overall, buy this if it's just sat in your wishlist. Sale or not, worth it imo.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: This game is based around nonstop jokes and since humor is very subjective you may have a different experience, but, personally, the writing in this game drives me crazy. It's practically the same jokes over and over mixed with nonsensical quips every few lines and basically every character in the game is an idiot, insane, or possibly is suffering from some type of neurodevelopment disorder.The FPS gameplay is serviceable, but not really all that fun and exploration isn't nearly as necessary or rewarding as in your typical Bethesda game (or many other RPGs). Overall, I'm just very bored and felt it my duty to leave a review as "Very Positive" does not reflect my experience with this game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: This game has its strenghts and weaknesses, overall my rather thorough first run was 30 hours so it's pretty short. The replay value is questionable, I may do one more run on the highest difficulty. The concept was very promising, but in the end this game is far behind the more fast-paced and vibrant Borderlands 2 and doesn't reach the immersion of open world RPGs like Fallout NV or Fallout 4. The biggest drawback was really a lack of atmosphere on some stretches.Positive:-Voice acting is excellent-Story is ok, though as always your choices don't matter that much and many side arches just die out-Combat system is pretty fun with the time dilation, even though the AI is borderline stupid-RP is decent and you can be rude or nice in any dialogNegative:-Weapon choice is limited and low effort, for a Borderlands style game very disappointing-Armor is also not very intersting, I used 2 armors and 4 hats for the whole game-Modding of the armor/weapons does't make up for the lack of options, you pretty much have 1 option per build-The soundtrack is dull and is probably one reason this game lacks immersion
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: If you hate your boss you'll love this game,Most fun I've had in a sci-fi since Mass Effect 2. Less cinematic but more than makes up for it with player choice (in everything, story, build, gear). Balances hilarity with high-stakes drama and tragedy quite well. It's a bit light on content for an open world rpg but the quality is high and that just means you don't need 200 hours to complete the game. Like everything made by obsidian, this game is amazing and feels like if it spent another year in development it could've been perfect.  Get the DLC on sale but do get the DLC. It is a tad predictable but still very entertaining.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good game - dying genre. A wonderful and pleasant journey in open world, that is more than rich in several factions, places of interest and side quests to get full imersed into the world. Solid 30-40 hours of single-playthrough of gameplay with high re-playability.Absolutely wonderful leveling system, which allows you to pick 'the way you want to play' - without 'punishing you' for 'not taking' certain traits and skills. You can absolutely "ruin" your character and still finish game smoothly (yes, you will be lacking in several apsects, but you wont 'lock yourself away')Armors that are plesant visually. Weapon customization system which is simple, but not 'insulting' to the player. Colorful (both litreally and methaporically) world with interesting characters. Here and there you can see certain 'flaws' - some planets are "insultingly small", and content which is put on them could be easily fit into some 'more empty' places on 'bigger planets', as well as only 2 companions seemed to have actually 'bigger' quests line to their names - max and parvatti (if i dont butcher the name) - it took about 'hours and some' to finish their quests - other? Minutes - it "smelled a little bit" of devs being rushed.That aside - Weapons? Beautiful. Ammo system? simple and enjoyable. Game is often funny, sometimes dreadful. Game worth full price and 'cheff kiss' to whole staff. More of that please!!!Solid 9/10 title
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: As far as gameplay goes, this game's pretty good! Everything else was pretty lackluster. For starters, the game is VERY short. -I beat it in less than 20 hours, which is horrible. Though I have to say that I was almost never not doing something. They did a good job of keeping you busy all the way through the game, and there was rarely a dull moment. -I felt that the role-playing element was dull and uninspired. Your crew just follows you around and goes along with almost everything you do... except when I murdered Ellie's parents, she didn't like that and left. All the factions have you do tasks for them. Eventually, you'll have to choose sides and it's mostly between supporting or not supporting the Board. The most interesting part of the game was getting the Iconoclasts and the Monarchs to make a peace treaty, but the path to do it is pretty specific on how you complete the tasks. I actually had to start a new playthrough just to do it right. -Which reminds me, I'm not 100% sure if it's just me, but the saving system seems a bit off. I was unable to access previous save files (They were not auto-saves, because I play a lot of Fallout and make normal saves often). Could be me though, not a huge deal. -I thought the ending was uninspired, I won't say anything to spoil it if you do play it. However, I will say that I don't feel like I missed anything in the game to encourage me to play again. Only the achievements. -Speaking of replaying, I would definitely come back if there were any decent mods available, and maybe new game +. -If you are interested in buying this game, I encourage anyone to buy it on sale for less than $15.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: Do you want to captain a spaceship and skip around a decaying colony taking on odd jobs? Do you want to take on a crew made up of people looking for adventure? Well I did. I have one whole play-through under my belt and I'll probably pick up for a second once the second DLC activates.I was initially drawn to this game based on how much better Fallout: New Vegas was than the other Fallout games (the former made with help from the same studio that made this game and the latter made exclusively by Bethesda). While there is not as much of a sandbox open-world scope to this game, it's still a large game world once all the planets and asteroids become available. But the characters and the setting and the story were all deeply-engrossing. The combat needed a little work: I needed to raise the difficulty to Hard a few hours in because it was too easy to get through battles, the special Science weapons don't level with you so they have a limited window of utility; nevertheless, combat is a big core to the game and never felt repetitive or boring.I've only finished one DLC (Peril on Gorgon) and thought it was also well-written and meshes well into the game so that it doesn't feel like something tacked on, but more like a questline for another faction. But I'll cut to the chase: this is a very good game. I felt it was as similar to Bioshock as to Fallout New Vegas, so if you are a fan of those games, I think this is a good addition to your library.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: The Great: It truly does play like Fallout New Vegas: Space Edition. The art style is heavily inspired by Fallout, while having it's own unique "space-y" touches.  It's very visually stimulating without going over the top. The different worlds and towns are unique to themselves, and don't feel repetitive (yet).  The satirical dialogue is done well, you'll get some laughs out of the goofiness or downright stupidity of the cast.  The companion system is well done, with lots of dialogue options as well as character and location specific commentary. Most importantly they almost never get in your way or slow you down.The Not-So Great:The entire combat system feels weak, especially in the beginning. The "dodge" skill feels useless against enemies that mostly have guns - The melee weapons all seem to have the same drab 3-hit combos - and the special weapon effects don't feel very powerful. The exploration and looting systems also don't bring anything new or unique to the open world RPG genre. Although it's definitely not "bad" per se, it just feels stale. Overall I would definitely buy this game again. Story-Driven Open World RPGS like these will forever hold a place in my Hard Drive.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: This game is boring, which is unfortunate because I was hoping for more. I waited for this game to be available outside the Epic platform, intentionally ignoring news and articles about it with the intention of experiencing it without any preconceptions.The game starts in a humerus fashion with some quirkiness at the start. I am then introduced to "light sidearm weapon 1", a nondescript pistol. It turns out that nondescript weapons are throughout the entirety of the eight hours I played. It kind of reminds me of Borderlands in this sense - you pick up nondescript ammo for your nondescript weapon, which can be modified with nondescript modifications you pick up in nondescript ways from places that sort of make sense, but not really. If you want to make your weapon better, pay money and it's done. No real mechanics to it - you just increase the number of damages it does, and there you go. Boring.Anyway, you get a few melee weapons, find the first character you can speak with, and find a ship that you need to *ALARM* FETCH AN ITEM TO FIX *ALARM*, and are sent to a town full of boring people. A hint to writers: if it's your intention to create a city full of boring people who hate their lives, and that's the first place you're going to subject a player to, what do you expect to have a player experience? Elation? Excitement? Boredom?A compressed conversation with the first denizen I find from the city: "Hello, what's your story?"*ALARM FETCH NUMBER 2* "I'm a grave digger who needs to collect money from living people. Go bother these poor ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ for money plzkthx and come back to me with the money."Then I go inside the town, speak to the town leader, and am given a fetch quest where I get to screw over a bunch of people I don't care about. Fetch quest 3.After that, I go and get a fetch quest about robots (this is a three part fetch quest, fetch quest 4, which extends to 6). Then I get a fetch quest about a religious text (fetch quest 7). Then I get a fetch quest about some medicine (fetch quest 8)...You get experience discovering nondescript locations which are given names to somehow imply importance. The first place I ran into was something like "ship wreckage". I believe I also found "cargo wreckage" and "cave hideout". You're telling me that there's only one of these named instances? Is this the only wreckage in the game? What's the story behind it? Why are there dead bodies all around? What attracted gigantic monkey-beasts to this site to kill all the marauders? None of this is made apparent.There's a lot of garbage which can be collected. Junk can be sold to vendors at prices which imply they're not junk, but money doesn't seem to mean anything because I never really ran into a proper vendor. Maybe I wasn't paying attention, or maybe I didn't really care at this point. Unsure.Armor is found on the dead. Weapons are scattered everywhere, and ammunition is generic and plentiful. There's no real need for inventory management, you can disassemble everything to its basic components as you acquire it, and making tough choices for bartering isn't really something that you run into.The AI is not fun or smart, the enemy models aren't cool or interesting. Actually they're really generic. I think I ran in to about four or five different marauder models. They have different names, sort of different weapon configurations, and behave the exact same: run toward your character, and hide behind something to fire a weapon. No need to take cover. No need to hide from sniper fire, nothing like that. When you fire a weapon, everyone knows where you are, and make an immediate beeline toward your location. There's some sort of gorilla which comes in three different models - two of the same color, and one different color which is a little bigger and more dangerous.The concept of a company owning people as chattel for their entire life is interesting, but it's played out in the most ham-fisted way possible.An example:Old man: "I AM AN OLD MAN WHO IS DYING. THE COMPANY NO LONGER THINKS I AM WORTH KEEPING AROUND, AND I'M RESOLVED TO MY DEMISE. I NEED A MEDICINE TO LIVE. PLZ HELP OR NOT WHATEVER."Me: "Well golly, that's just awful. I'll be glad to help you out of the kindness of my heart and the money you may or may not give me later on. I just want to drive this story, old man. Whatevs..."*fetch old man medicine*Old man: "THX DUDE. HERE. I GUESS I GET TO KEEP LIVING OR WHATEVER."Me: "yw. have a life or something. I dunno. Bye."Nothing useful or interesting. There's no "good part" to any of this. I am left wondering if helping him live was better than gunning him down right there.The dialogue was skippable, the discussions were mundane, the concept of corporatism and morality is hit with glancing blows. I have no idea why people would pay for a grave site when religion seems to be only mildly adhered to. From a futuristic perspective, why would you care where your body ends up? Are you religious or not? No discussion of an afterlife or heaven, just an intention to deal with ones corporeal leftovers in a fashion which implies that they care where their body ends up. Yet there's LITERALLY DEAD BODIES EVERYWHERE.This game isn't fun. There's nothing good about it. I am really happy Steam offers refunds. Even if I'd pirated it, I would have uninstalled it by now.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: A really good game. The characters are well written, the story and lore is interesting and keeps you wanting to learn more, and it is a really fun time. I felt it was a little short, though I don't have the DLCs yet and also I blasted through the game by playing it for like 3-4 days straight so my perception of time might be off.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: So far so good...even though I am not the furthest into the main story at this point...I have been thoroughly enjoying The Outer Worlds thus far! Character interactions and a comedic overtone right off the rip grabbed my attention and continue to keep me coming back for more. The character customization, from visuals to stats and skills, was almost overwhelming, but after some reading and in game time things really started to make sense. The combat is fun and on the right difficulty challenging, and allows for a number of game play styles. Weapon/armor system is interesting with a built in level system and degradation for weapon use and armor damage. There is a fairly simple loot system with everything from weapons and armor to trinkets, crafting and quest items scattered throughout a semi open world environment. Your choices and alliances seem to impact the overall story of the game, and it will be interesting to see how all of them come together further down the road. Overall, I was looking forward to experiencing The Outer Worlds for quite some time now and am happy I finally have the opportunity to do so. I look forward to continuing to rack up the hours and see what the main story and plethora of side quests have in store for me!
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: Its not for me. I am a little surprised how positively reviewed this game is. Ill try and break it down by parts: - It feels very much like a persons first world building for a custom D&D game setting. In person, you can ask a question that the person probably never thought of, but seems obvious to you, and they give you answer. In a video game, that cant happen. There are a lot of eye brow raising logic in the way people behave that is hard to really take anything seriously. The corporations are comically evil, and everyone is just okay with it. like you would suspect there to be much more dissent in the populous the way they are treated and arbitrary penalties. Its a culture where Mass suicide would make sense because no sane person would look at the world and want to keep participating in it.It has the same kind of energy of a horror movie where there is clearly a knife welding killer in the house and the characters all just kind of wander around in their undies saying "Hellllllo?". Just destroys any verisimilitude of taking the world seriously because the people don't act or behave like people. its a big pet peeve of mine. - I found this to be pretty lack-luster too. There was never really a character I enjoyed. Similar to above with most of the characters - they seem unable to grasp that the corporation is clearly evil. Every one behaves like they need help using a microwave, or use only Velcro shoes. Even the 'smart' characters seem a bit too dumb. The dialog options are usually like:1) Progress quest2) Some boring world building in which the person will boot lick the corporations again3) some other question which will end in a 2 word reply4) leaveThere may be some branching dialog, but I never found any of it interesting to listen to or surprising. it was all very 'meh'.Every quest felt the same. It always person A tell you Person B is bad, but wont really tell you why or elaborate on it, usually some paper thin reasoning. you talk to Person B and they say the same but provide proof of person A. You confront Person A and they have this like scooby-doo monologue "I would have gotten away with it!" or something similar. All of the quests are like this. - I found the combat to be difficult until about level 4 or 5. at which point you get way better weapons and the combat becomes much easier. There is also this whole thing they are trying to sell you on when you play the game called something like "Taking flaws". basically when you are playing the game the way you like, pop ups will occur outside of combat when something happens, like you took 200 acid damage total, or something like that. It will ask you if you would like to take a flaw. The flaw will give you a negative to the way you currently play in circumstances related to the pop up - like when you take acid damage you have -1 perception and 10% more weapon sway etc - for 1 perk point. Normally you get 1 perk point every 2 levels, and the perks are very disappointing. There was never one I was excited for, or looking forward to getting. whenever I had to select a perk, it was always kind of a chore to find the least bad one / most helpful. Some example of perks are like "walk speed is 25% faster", "Carry weight is 30kg more", "you can move faster in slowmo mode". Nothing that gave me the feeling of "Wow! this will help me I cant wait to try it" It was really just for fixing inconveniences which, honestly, probably should have just been fixed without the need of perk points. The walking is slow, just make the default 25% faster.You get companions, you can take 2 with you out of a selection of 6. They are all very bland. No one really had an interesting story. There is a crisis of faith priest who is/was a criminal - it was not totally clear to me. A gay engineer who wants a girlfriend. Doctor with daddy issues. The guy who gets fired from minimum wage jobs wants to me find his friend he has not heard from in a while. And Lady who wants to bury her old friends.I don't think I am being too unfair with their characterisations because they felt very 1 dimensional. to be fair I used mainly doctor with daddy issues and Gay engieer who wants GF real bad. They seem to try and do something like give the companions an "arc" in that they will bring up the same issues and stuff when you go outside of the ship. They also interact with each other when you enter the ship, but there seems to be like only 10 interactions when you enter the ship, and you will enter the ship a lot. The ship will inform you they are interacting when you want to go anywhere it becomes quite annoying. Similarly annoying is that every companion has a special combat ability, and they shout 1 line every time you use it. some characters have a stun or do damage or something - its usually useful, so you will be using it a lot! I heard the same line like 25 times and I just muted the game. I had the companion for only their "companion missions" which was total like 1 hour it sucked. "AYYYYYAAAAGGHHHHYYYYY" please don't do this, i just need your damage. When you use their ability the camera pans on them and you have to watch them use their power for like 3-5 seconds which is also annoying when you are in a gun fight.I just really did not enjoy the game so much. I felt like I was being hit over the head with ideas that are not subtle but the game thinks is. I don't know if its a case of "But the players wont get it unless we spell it out for them 3-5 times" I get it, the corporation is evil, but can they have a better reason? There is a "Twist" at the end, but it changes nothing and is not interesting. Your perspective on the factions should not shift at the revelations. I will spoil it to give you the whole deal and save you 10-15 hours of play. . Overall its okay, but very disappointed its a 5 or 6/10 for me.

_childDocuments_.review: The game isn't 0/10 bad, but it was a huge disappointment for me.I was hoping for more of a specialised character feel, but it really just ends up being an fps. Unlike an RPG like New Vegas, Outer Worlds doesn't let you solve many missions in any way other than fight and kill -- sometimes break into a container. The decisions in your character build feel essentially meaningless. Will buff a few qualities, but nothing changes the way your character feels in the world. I certainly wouldn't be motivated to try a new playthrough as a 'different' character (something I often do in Skyrim fallout, ME, etc.)Your squadmates can't use cover, you can't order them to do much, in hardest difficulty I just tell them to wait back because they just die and then I feel bad.The world isn't open and is instead made of multiple, small areas you can travel between. At first I thought this would be rgeat because I expected them to be dense,d etailed and interesting. Instead they were small AND cookie cutter copy/paste buildings and objects. The world wasn't much fun for me to explore.5/10. First 30 mins seemed like the game would be awesome. Kinda just kept going downhill for me.

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of gamedesign elements fall into the uncanny valley and thus the game suffers from immersion hick-ups. The game feels like a demo addressed to investors of what could be. Half backed very much.This opinion contains spoilers.* Compability:** This game works great with proton on linux. It's the only reason i considered buying this game. Big plus.* Gameworld style:** The designers succeeded in implementing a style that is similar to the old 2D games. The retro-future style transforms the game into a fantasy game rather than a sci-fi game. But it has downsides. More later.* Visuals:** Very often i came across a wallpaper like scenery. Often very appealing.* Quest GUI:** I liked the summary bullet points in the quest log. They were very helpful.* Enemy design:** This game has all of the possible enemytypes. The enemies feel like static papertargets (obviously except the chargers). It's apparent that this game was made for consoles.* Companions:** In dialogs with NPCs the companions occasionally have some remarks. Interesting concept. Unfortunately it’s not possible to ask them anything about the current quest. ** The companions are boring with boring quests and forgettable. The only one interesting one was Felix with his uplifting remarks. I liked Felix.** I don’t understand why do they have to wear the armor that i assigned to them inside the unreliable. Don't the have their own wardrobe?** If ADA says that some of the companions would cause a disturbance, there is no gamemechanic for me to interact with them and knock it off.* Dialog options:** There is a lot of dialog in this game. Sometimes too much. My first meeting with Sanjar ate up 30 minutes. There was a lot of uninteresting stuff to discus with him.** Lots of options. Different decisions have different consequences with little reward. The consequences are shop prices, some mid level armor or gun and the diashow you get when the game ends.* Weapons:** Weapons have levels (what i think shouldn't exist in any game at all). Bad is that the higher leveled guns have just an postfix to their name (like mk2 or Ultra), but the model and texture remains the same. IMO it's much better to introduce a new 3D-model for a higher tier weapon.** The shotguns weren't that impressive and were rendered useless by melee weapons.* Leveling:** The leveling is so extreme that going back as a Lvl 30 to the first area kills an enemy with just one bullet while before it required some 100 bullets (for strong enemies).** Skilltrees aren't skilltrees but bufftrees. The only skills that can be learned are dodging and powerful melee attacks. Everything else are just buffs.* Character control:** Without hesitation i can say that it's the worst that i have ever experienced. Player will on specific terrain parts just randomly slide around and get stuck, because of the awful gameengine charactercontrol implementation. Now i understand why there is every 3 minutes an autosave. I had to use it often because of that.* World mechanics:** Besides of the NPC's the world is dead. The complete lack of physically interactive objects kills immersion.** No climbing, no tossing, no risky exploring, awful jumping rounded up by invisible walls (to prevent you from trying out swimming, because swimming doesn’t exist).** Also gravity is everywhere the same. On big planets and on asteroids. No zero gravity mission/area. There is no variety here.* Gameworld style:** The retro-future style didn't work for me. The colony is dying, there is resource shortage and (supposedly advanced) inter/stellar traveling but there are resourcehungry 1930s ornaments. The industrial dieselpunk appearance doesn’t fit, was immersion breaking and it didn't catch me.** Also the rounded and comical design of houses/ships/etc.. hindered every raise in tension. Round things don't catch humans attention, sharp and edgy stuff does. Very often i would overlook things because the environment is cluttered with the same roundy shape.* Atmosphere:** The colorful appearance and passive NPC's don't fit into the story. IMO the presentation of the story failed. It would have been better in a thick horror-thriller atmosphere.** No NPC/Storygiver had an extreme emotional expression. Best example of how bad it was, ** No demonstrations/panic/any other extreme expression because  There was simply nothing to react to except the enemies with guns and claws.* Exhausting quest structure:** Very often the quest at some point would boil down to the question 'either them or the others' and you decide. Those dilemmas are cheap and aren't entertaining.* Missing story theme:** I never had the feeling i would solve a mystery. The biggest mystery was raised literally just 1 minute before the game was over.* Quests:** The quests were just quests. Very often detached of the main story, or in other words, no side NPC had a rational problem because of what's going on. Rarely were they interesting. Mostly just fetch quests.If it's important, I played a max speech, gun wielding character and managed to talk the end bosses into just leave, not killing any corporate soldiers at all.

_childDocuments_.review: So far, great atmosphere, immersive, and captivating. I have a wide screen monitor but the graphics are really good. The missions are all interesting and keep you wanting more. Usually with these games I lose interest fast/don't find all of the small missions fun or find there's too many, but with The Outer Worlds, I've struggled to put the game down because I want to see what's coming nextWeapons are all cool and fighting mechanics are simple and easy to use too, coming from someone who never plays any sort of fighting games, I find it fun and easy
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: The Outer Worlds is a Satirical Joyride through a capitalist hellscape. It's charming and campy (like, the good kind of campy) with Easter Eggs and chubby snakes. You get Fallout and Bioshock vibes off of this game like crazy.You also feel like one of maybe 10 people that's actually free in the galaxy, and when you're sitting in your ship listening to the calm background music, looking at the stars and talking to Ada, you honestly feel a little more free in your own life as well.There are more role-play opportunities in this game than the vast majority of action RPGs, and it's honestly a breath of fresh air for the Genre.The Outer Worlds is an excellent game that's a bit on the short side as far as the base game is concerned, but if you do all the companion quests and a bunch of side missions, then go back for a second run, you definitely get your money out of it. I originally owned it on PS4, but I got it on here as well so I could keep playing it now that I don't play my PS4 at all anymore. The reasonably priced DLCs help a lot. Murder on Eridanos was excellent, and I only just started on Peril on Gorgon. I'm excited for what comes next. Both for this franchise and for Obsidian in general.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: I'll admit the actual gameplay of the game is really not that special...BUT - the characters? I'm very invested in Parvati, she's got my heart - and there's def some things in the game that make me smile bright. _childDocuments_.review: You are special just because you are is not a good premise for an RPG. At some point I realised I'm not enjoying this title and I would have to force myself to continue any further. Everything about Outer Worlds is very generic and average. I love the sci-fi theme, but that's about it. The missions are predicable and the characters are annoying or dislikable. In general, the characters just seem a bit out-of-place or linear. I did like some of the dialogue and choices given - there really is an RPG here, with good open decisions, but everything else is so shallow or takes away immersion. For example, why is it ok for me to hack someone's computer right in front of them?   Why do most characters think the protagonist is extremely capable without knowing anything about them and why do characters spill their entire lives in front of the protagonist the second they meet? I played on supernova difficulty and it has quite a few problems. Followers are useless if you can't revive them, the survival inventory requires dire reworking, and the saving mechanic for this mode is garbage and easily exploitable. In fact, the entire inventory system is tedious. Story wise, I noticed quite a few missions have a grey moral area - especially for solving it -, which I love. However, it's marred by tedium and shallowness.  It's nice that there is no clear good vs evil to a story or mission - this is what reality is like. Nonetheless, The Outer Worlds does it far too often and it feels more like a placeholder than something meaningful. It's like the writers knew how to write a morally grey story, but they did not have enough time for any build up and/or for the player to view meaningful consequences. Also I have to stress that The Outer Worlds quickly expose the grey moral area. To me, this is a really bad move. There needs to be an appearance of good vs evil for the story to be realistic and compelling. This is exactly why everything always feels a bit off.In general, I'm afraid The Outer Worlds is a bit boring.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is like if Fallout: New Vegas had been removed from the Fallout universe and set in space instead.  The setting is more reminiscent of the Borderlands universe, with ridiculous corporate entities and space cowboy style.  The writing is great, running the gamut from hilarious to crushingly sad.  The characters are interesting and well-developed.  It would probably be easier to talk about what I haven't liked so far.  The combat is good, but the learning curve is a little rough.  I feel like I'm cheesing most difficult fights, and it's not really clear how the different damage types and mods will affect the various things you fight.  I am learning things by experimentation, but in the early game, the mods are expensive or hard to come by and cannot be retrieved once used.  I made a silenced pistol thinking that it might help to get some stealth kills, but since the pistols don't do a ton of damage per shot, the target will almost always alert anyone nearby before you can finish them.  Also, I've been having a weird interaction where the game keeps detecting my controller and making my mouse cursor disappear.Anyway, I highly recommend the game.  It's what Fallout: New Vegas should have been if Obsidian had been given the time and resources to finish developing the game.  I look forward to anything else they release in the future!

_childDocuments_.review: So I've been a fan of Obsidian ever since KOTOR2. Before that, if we count the games some of the folks there worked on back in Black Isle. Despite the tight schedules those early sequels were on and some resulting clunkiness and bugs, I loved (and still do) most of their games. The Outer Worlds though? Well, it's complicated.Lets knock out the visuals first - graphics are about what you'd expect from 2020 game, still looking good. Visual design though? Not a fan. I feel like the whole retrofuturistic vibe doesn't fit the setting at all and is only there to emulate Fallout - where the 1950-60s vibe was much more fitting and plausible. Everything being oversaturated to the point of being painful to look at doesn't help in the slightest.Alright, but RPGs should shine through the story, not visuals. Does the story hold up to Obsidian standards? Yes and no. There is some really great writing and fun quests in there, but it's in the minority. Overall impression the game left me with is "Stupidity written smartly." Dialogs are witty and competently written, but they hardly compensate for 85% of characters you meet being complete idiots. Game actually touches on some serious issues - big corporations destroying environment and ruining people's lives for profit margins - but then goes out of its way to make a mockery of it all by turning stupidity to 11, from blabbering idiots of npcs and corpospeak emails present on every in-game computer to majority of sidequests being idiot plots (that is, stories which only happen because everyone involved has an IQ roughly equal to comfortable room temperature). "Corporations. Pretty stupid, hehe." is the one and only note writing has for the majority of the game. It's most prevalent in Emerald Vale, the first area of the game - which might be why almost 30% of players dropped the game at that point.The only time I actually noticed the brief respite from everpresent idiocy and some real, human emotions was during the Gorgon DLC. My companions' reactions to some horrifying experiments were written extremely well and it's probably the moment that stuck with me the most.Gameplay wise - not much to say, it's still the basic Bethesda RPG game loop. Exploration, looting, some mediocre shooting, more looting, pick some quests, sell loot, some more shooting, some lockpicking and more looting. Loot is not all that exciting, as you'll rarely find meaningful upgrades, aside from unique Science Weapons, which are probably the most fun to play with. Enemy variety is nonexistent, consisting of about 4 types of animals, 3 types of robots, melee humans and ranged weapon humans with AI that's as basic as it gets.There's now also a 'Spacer's Choice' edition, but it seems the only major changes are turning up color saturation even more and raising level cap from 36 to 99, so you don't have to make any build choices/sacrifices. At 9$ upgrade price, I'll pass.Overall, The Outer Worlds is not a bad game and there is some fun to be had. Still, it's mediocre at best and definitely the weakest Obsidian game I've played, which makes it hard to recommend. At this point, I'm much more interested in Avowed than Outer Worlds 2.

_childDocuments_.review: Far and away one of the better FPS RPGs out there. This is like Firefly (the TV show) with heavy sci-fi meets a Fallout RPG.  You can say it's a spiritual successor to Fallout:NV but I think Outer Worlds is a better more refined game. Obsidian really nailed this game.  The game is short - 20-35hrs depending on how much you read. Which I suggest highly that you do read - lots of story to fill in some blanks.  Choices matter - and the dialog trees are great.  I played a pistol wielding smooth talker.  I was able to avoid many conflicts due to talking my way out of things.  Excited to play another play style and make different choices.The companions are interesting (some more that others) and the side quests for them give good back story and I actually felt genuine joy and happy for them while helping them through their quests. Overall - 9.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Finally finished the game and now time for the review! I see where comparisons can be drawn to the Fallout series and while YES it is similar in genre, but that is were the similarities end. Outer Worlds stands firmly on its own two feet as its own very promising game series and does no justice with comparisons to Fallout. This game is well thought out and could have easily put in another 10 hours if I hadn't botched several quests and explored more of the more remote planets. This game has a high replayability factor and I immediately want to jump back in to play it all over again, but with an entirely different play style. This game truly made me think, ponder, and agonize over some of the choices it forces you to make which is GREAT! This game is solid and I look forward to more content. Only wish the game was EVEN LONGER!

_childDocuments_.review: Played at launch on Epic and loved it. Currently going through the DLC, and it's great. A good game is still a good game, even with its tone-deaf publisher deciding to charge $10 for a performance patch for a game that pokes fun at corporate greed. The term "performance patch" is getting thrown around a lot in reviews, but for good reason. Spacer's Choice is a game of the year edition that includes performance and visual improvements that owners of the base game aren't getting, and you only get the $10 discounted price if you also own the DLC. There's no new content, so all the $10 gets you is a face lift and a shot of steroids. If you're playing Outer Worlds for the first time it makes sense (just like any Game of the Year edition does), but if you're a returning fan just stick with the copy you have.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a fan of Obsidian going back to their first games, and to Black Isle Studio before that. So it's a bit sad that I find myself spacing out while playing Outer Worlds. There's a competent enough FPS somewhere in there, though I'm not really playing an Obsidian RPG for its FPS. The world built starts out fascinating, though as you progress it's clear they ran out of imagination after the opening world. But it's the characters and writing that's the let-down, in a game from Obsidian of all places. Individual characters are 2D caricatures, the philosophy espoused is shallow and hamfisted, and the dialog drags longer than a bad year. It's sad, because I forgave them so many bugs in KOTOR2, or FO:NV, or NWN2, because the games ultimately had so much soul and love. With Outer Worlds you get almost none of the bugs. Too bad the soul was extracted alongside them.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a great game with many similarities to Fallout New Vegas, Borderlands, and Bioshock. Like the former, you'll be presented with an A- story that suffers from C+ first/third person shooter elements. I think the developers knew this and provided a system similar to VATS from Fallout that helps the combat in many ways. The story is decent, and there is enough of an open-world factor to reward some exploration. I bought the game on sale and I feel I got my moneys worth. Just a quick sidenote - I'm a geologist and I was blown away with the level of world design these folks did. Volcanic areas have jagged features that hold jointed basalt and mafic lava flows (both geologic features that I'd expect in the real world). Sedimentary-dominated areas have visible stratigraphy and accurate erosional landforms as well as cave systems. These developers are incredibly detailed with something mundane for most people and it shows how much thought they put into the design and art. 6/10 game, 10/10 geology*Edit* After finishing the game completely I feel about the same. The story was a bit shorter than I expected but I felt it was satisfying. The Outer Worlds is absolutely worth the sale price. At full price I start to compare it to AAA games and studios, which it falls a bit short of.
