_childDocuments_.review: I'm so conflicted on this one.I'm by no means the first person to say this, but I wish I could give this game a "mixed" review, because there clearly WAS love and effort put into this game.A lot of it, in fact.The gorgeous visuals feel like a natural evolution of the original Super's scrappy art style, the cutscenes are rad as hell, I've seen the developers talk about how much this game means to them. It really feels like a passion project and a love letter to Meat Boy as a whole....𝘉𝘶𝘵 𝘪𝘯 𝘢𝘭𝘭 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘸𝘳𝘰𝘯𝘨 𝘢𝘳𝘦𝘢𝘴.The game emphasizes flash over function, style over substance.The emphasis is placed entirely on the visuals, the story, and fanservice/references to the original Super Meat Boy. And I gotta say, nobody really cared about the story of Super; the game has a bare-bones, generic "save the girl" plot, and that was the entire point. What people cared about was the gameplay. Super Meat Boy was a game that was defined by its tough-as-nails platforming, razor-tight albeit slippery controls, and its edgy 2009-era Newgrounds humor. It was a scrappy little indie hit that took the world by storm and skyrocketed Edmund McMillen from a weird animator to one of the industry titans.One of the biggest complaints regarding Forever is that they turned Meat Boy into an auto-runner, like that in itself is a point against it.I actually disagree with that.You can absolutely turn Meat Boy into an auto-runner, but you have to do it WELL. The idea of an infinitely replayable Meat Boy game sounds like a godsend on paper, but the procedural generation and auto-running gameplay actively clash with each other. The levels lack the hand-crafted cohesion that the original Super handled so well, which oftentimes can lead to a lot of incredibly cheap deaths. One generated level chunk had me repeatedly flung face-first into a wall of buzzsaws upon respawning, and I had to brute-force my way across as I trial-and-errored my way through it. It felt like it was entirely the game's fault, and not mine. It's laid out like a linear game with a definitive start and end, but it's generated like an endless runner. I can't help but feel bad for Tommy Refenes and his team; they poured so much love, blood, sweat, meat and tears into this product. But in my opinion, Super Meat Boy Forever on its own does not suffice as either a standalone Meat Boy spin-off game, or a successor to the incredible Super Meat Boy.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Meat Boy Forever

_childDocuments_.review: I went into this game knowing full well it was an auto-runner. I gave it a fair chance, played it for about four hours, went through most of the main story before deciding nope, that was enough. This game is the antithesis to fun. What made the original Super Meat Boy fun was brutal difficulty with incredibly tight controls, such that you could really test the limits of your skills and ingenuity to overcome the challenges. This, on the other hand, decided to forgo good level design and precise controls for what feels more akin to a mobile game. The auto-running limits your ability to control your character; the fact that getting turned around and running into the left side of the screen can actually kill you because you can't stop or turn around just feels more insulting than difficult. Most levels are fairly one-dimensional as well through the story, adding one new gimmick per level and making those the emphasis rather than increasingly difficult platforming challenges. And sadly, this also makes levels feel rather scripted; generally there's one solution to each level, because the auto-running limits your ability to execute such that it pushes you to do it one specific way.It's not all doom and gloom though as there is some sense of satisfaction from overcoming the platforming levels. The same cannot be said for the bosses; fighting a boss in an auto-runner is just flat out frustrating and not at all enjoyable. It didn't feel like I was dying because the boss was challenging, it felt like I was dying because my inability to control my character limited my ability to execute. There was no room for creativity; the auto-running typically means there's one specific way to beat a boss, making it feel more akin to a puzzle, but again, one that's crippled by an inability to control your character. Every time I beat a boss, I didn't feel a sense of satisfaction or elation. I just let out a deep sigh of relief that the horrible ordeal was over. If you want a great 2D Platformer, this is not it. Play Celeste. Play the original Super Meat Boy. Play Super Mario World. Play literally any other 2D Platformer. As someone who grew up with 2D Platformers, and someone who loved the original Super Meat Boy, this game was a monumental disappointment in every way, shape, and form. I am reminded of an old saying; "If it ain't broke, don't fix it".

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately, people here either rate it positive because it's super messy boy, or they rate it negative because it's an endless runner. And... Neither are really fair reviews.But if you ask me, super meat boy forever (smbf hereafter) simply isn't a good endless runner.It's kind of hard to pinpoint why. Controls are okay but not perfect(which is almost too say they're bad in this genre). The music i really started to dislike and the sound effects are passable at best... Which is weird because i hardly ever care about those. Maybe it's because it's just 'there' and not tied to the challenges like rayman jungle/fiësta run or bit. Trip runner?But it's more than that. It's hard, yes, but not insane. maybe that's just that others have a more smooth learning curve? No... What irked me more is that on others in the genre i can grasp instantly and intuitively what to do. Smbf has spots where roads fork(either you walljump to above or you don't), but it seems like there is a 'correct path' to find.... Which would be fine if it was a platformers, but you don't have the time because you're running.I also really wasn't a fan of the turning around. That is: you can bounce from the wall in the opposite direction, but if that leads you back to the starting point you're dead... So why keep running there? The idea of an endless runner is to go fast (canabalt had you running during an invasion). Maar not happily running backwards makes him seem stupid rather than the reckless running mode that's shape of the genre.Now... Each of these would be nitpicks by themselves, but they add up. Frankly, i just like it less than bit.trip Runner (1 and 2), the rayman games and even canabalt. Heck... I think even mario run might be better, and I've only played that for like ten minutes.So... Sorry, but i can't recommend it. It's not like it's really a BAD game, but i have to agree with the critics that this just isn't a good entry in the franchise. I want super into meat boy, but i respected it. This... I can't recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Super Meat Boy was an absolute phenomenon when it released over a decade ago. It was perhaps the first real mainstream hit of the precision platformer genre, merging lessons from classic run & jumps and more sadistic offerings like I Want To Be The Guy to form something that would influence indie games to this day. That’s a hell of a legacy, which makes it all the more bizarre that its own sequel seems to have forgotten so much of what made it good. I don’t know what compels a person to look at the acclaimed challenge and tight controls of the original, and then try to follow it up with a deeply flawed infinite runner. But I do know that it’s a curse that dooms Super Meat Boy Forever to be nothing more than frustration and tedium.Meat Boy and Bandage Girl are back, along with their adorable offspring, Nugget. Of course, the irascible Dr. Fetus is back too, and snatches the little bundle of gristly joy away. Thus begins another deadly odyssey of navigating levels full of sawblades, syringes, and horrors to rescue the sentient McGuffin. But things are a little different this time. In stark contrast to the compact platforming challenges of the original, Super Meat Boy Forever sends your chosen character sprinting relentlessly towards danger. You’ve got to time your jumps, dives, and punches to match your pace, as well as puzzle out the order of operations to work around your directional limitations. Then you’ll need to do it faster to meet the strict time targets on levels, more carefully to get the sadistically-placed collectibles, and repeatedly to work out the precise moves expected to beat the bosses.Straight away, if you’re here looking for more Super Meat Boy, you’re not going to get it. As I’ve repeatedly alluded to, the shift to infinite runner takes away a huge element of control that made the original so gratifying. Meat Boy (or your character of choice) is forever sprinting, stopping only when hitting a wall and changing direction only when leaping from a wall. Aspects of the original, like momentum from wall slides and carefully-planned wall jumps are present, and that’s where the game is most familiar. The rest of the time, you’ll have no control over your approach to a pit or obstacle, only the timing of your jump or slide. Early on, this can be maddening if you keep dying over and over to a jump that would have been elementary if only you had the least amount of control over your velocity.Instead, Meat Boy is given a few new tricks in this one, namely a punch and a slide. The punch is a dramatic change, sending your character dashing forward in midair and destroying an enemy. You can do it again if you kill, leading to sequences where you time punches to levitate over yawning pits. The slide is a logical choice for an infinite runner, letting Meat Boy squeeze under traps he’s too dumb to stop running face-first into. Your movement options are all responsive and allow for entertaining combinations, at least when it’s clear where you should be using them. Instead of the tight, flowing levels of the original, Forever’s levels are randomly-generated, stitched together from sections that offer their own challenges.It’s really here that the whole thing falls apart, and distances itself not only from the legacy of Super Meat Boy but quality infinite runners. These sections are often poorly-designed, requiring too specific jumps, twisting sequences of wall jumps that can turn you around, and other frustrations. One section literally had a trap area, where if you ran forward instead of taking a small upper path, you were simply doomed to run off a cliff. Some parts require you to sit and wait against walls to time your next moves, which isn’t bad on its own but hurts the flow of an infinite runner. And all of these irritations are only magnified when they’re mashed together into an incongruous level that has no flow between sections, and has to be completely restarted if you miss your chance at a collectible or secret.I could go on about how aggravating the bosses are, throwing up walls and beams of death that can only be avoided by matching whatever pattern the designer forced on you, or how punishingly tight the time limits are to unlock Dark World levels, or how much worse all of these problems are when you get to the Dark World. But it should be clear by now that Super Meat Boy Forever doesn’t just fail to live up to its predecessor, it fails as an infinite runner on its own. Its greatest sin is certainly being a gross misunderstanding of its legacy, but even removed from that, it’s just not fun for what it is.Did you enjoy this review? I certainly hope so, and I certainly hope you'll check out more of them at  or on my !

_childDocuments_.review: I don't often write reviews, but I thought I would with this game since I do foresee this review section being mostly negative. As someone who actually really likes this game, I thought I'd give my perspective.(Also, if you're curious about my playtime; I bought this game on it's EGS launch day and have completed it 7+ times since then).Super Meat Boy Forever is... polarising. That's definitely the word. The biggest (and most infamous) change with this game, is that it's an autorunner. There is no manual left or right movement - Meat Boy is constantly moving in some way or another. People will read that and envision a game like Geometry Dash, but this game is nothing like Geometry Dash or anything of the sort. When I played this game, I was actually surprised at how little the autorunning affected the creativity, scale, and difficulty of the level design, especially with Meat Boy's new move set. Meat Boy can now punch and slide, on top of his typical jump. Punching also serves as a 'dash' manuever. The levels aren't just Meat Boy constantly moving left to right, occasionally jumping or sliding whenever something comes towards him. There's verticality, timing, precision and focus required with each jump. Exactly how it was in the first game.Another big difference is how levels are generated. Each level is made up of 'chunks'. According to the developers, there are over 6000 different chunks that the game can make levels out of. Every single one of these chunks are hand-crafted by the designers - no random generation, all hand-crafted, polished, play-tested and given their on par-time to beat. These chunks are then put into their own specific pools, and when you go to play a level for the first time, the game will take around 8 of these chunks out of a specific pool, put them together (in a surprisingly seamless manner), put checkpoints at the beginning of each one, add the par-time for all of the chunks together as the overall level par-time, and voila. You have a Super Meat Boy Forever level. Most of these chunks, while not exactly Edmund-level, are actually quite well designed. Very rarely do I see a chunk that is just plain bad. 95% are very well put together, and are fun to figure out even while you're getting your arse walloped.Now, why did they do this? Well, for replayability. Each level has about 100 chunks in their pool of which they can be drawn from. Which means that when you finish a level for the first time, there are about 90 chunks you haven't seen. Apply that to the 70+ levels in the game, and that's a lot of content you're missing out on! When you start New Game +, the game remembers the chunks you have seen, removes them from the pools, and draws JUST new ones for you to play. According to the developers, you can NG+ a save file around 8-10 times before the algorithm starts re-using chunks you've already seen. Chunks are typically the size of a regular Super Meat Boy 1 level - around 10-30 seconds long. Each and every single level introduces some sort of new mechanic. In the early chapters, it's usually just the typical saws, dirty syringes, fans - things that Meat Boy fans are all too familiar with. In the later chapters however, the game starts to go in its own direction and Meat Boy is given whole new abilities that change his move set. The levels go into slightly a more puzzle-y direction as the chapters progress. They're still very platform-y, however.Clunky segue but it is partially related to level design; the boss fights and warp zones - they're fantastic. Both are a HUGE step up from the first game. I think we can all agree that the boss fights were by far the weakest part of Super Meat Boy 1. They were way too easy, forgettable, and lacked charm. They're still a little easy in Forever once figure out their gimmick (and there are still unfortunately no dark world versions of the bosses), but they're still fun to fight on subsequent playthroughs. And warp zones... I don't really want to spoil the warp zones. You know a warp zone is nearby when the screen starts to glitch out. Just find them and enjoy. They really caught me off guard.Yet another big difference is, of course, the art style. The first Super Meat Boy game had a very Newgrounds-influenced art style, with very "blocky" looking environments. It still looks great and definitely has a unique charm to it, but it does look rather dated. Forever's art style takes a more cartoon-y approach. While it may not be quite as "unique" as the art style of the first game, it still looks beautiful and no two levels look the same. The cutscenes are sublime, too. Everything is so bouncy and lively, it's able to be humourous without a single word of dialogue, and there are a lot of details that I don't notice until I watch it for the up-teenth time that just make me smile and appreciate the effort that went into these. Team Meat hired professional animators and artists to make this game's visuals, and it shows.This game is difficult. VERY difficult, at times. I have come across a handful of chunks that have honestly given me more trouble than even Super Meat Boy 1's hardest levels. Is it harder than the first game? Well, Forever takes on a slightly different approach to it's predecessor's "trial and error" style of difficulty. In the first game, more often than not, the camera was zoomed out so you could see the whole level right as you spawn. You can plan out the path you need to take, it's just actually executing it is where you'll have your difficulties. Whereas with Forever, it's almost the opposite. The camera is quite zoomed in, so you can't map out the full chunk right off the bat. You will have to dive in head-first into a lot of these obstacles to get an idea of what you're supposed to do.This isn't necessarily a bad thing on it's own, but there is also a collectable required for 100% where you have to beat the whole level without dying. This, and the "die to learn the level" approach this game took, it becomes more of a memory game than anything else. And with how many obstacles you face in each level, you will inevitably forget *something*, and you have to restart the whole level just because the game expects you to memorise literally EVERYTHING. It's quite unfair, and has honestly discouraged me from going for max completion. These levels were just simply not designed with deathless in mind. Questionable 100% completion and minor nitpicks aside, Super Meat Boy Forever is really solid. To quote an article, "...it does more with 2 buttons than most games do with 14." In a lot of aspects, this game is actually an improvement on the first game. It does sadden me that most people wrote off the game as soon as they heard that it's an autorunner. Games like Temple Run or Mario Run (games that Forever annoyingly gets compared to often) are NOT representative of what an autorunner can be - this game is, and it does a hell of a job at it. There is a question I often ask myself; is Forever a step forward or a step backward from the first Super Meat Boy game? Well, I don't think it *needs* to be a step forward. I can't really call it a step back either since it still does absolutely everything it sets out to achieve with flying colours.I'd consider it more of a step to the side. I don't think it tried to 1-up the first Super Meat Boy - it just merely built off it, and spun the gameplay into a different direction. For better or worse? Well, that's up to you. But just be sure to go into it with an open mind. You will definitely be surprised.

_childDocuments_.review: At this point, Meat Boy has become the (insert popular sci-fi franchise here) of indie games. Most of the discourse surrounding it peters down to reviews simply telling you to not listen to the other guys, while lacking any substantive discussion or genuine points of interest when it comes down to it.In one camp, you have the people who will tell you that it's a legitimately fun game and a worthy successor to the original. In the other camp, you have the people who are quick to put it down by calling it a disgrace that spits in the face of the original.At this moment in time, having served as one of the most vocal individuals about the game and rising to a bonafide LOLcow status within the confines of the Meat Boy Discord, I would say that I am very much in the middle.There is a version of this game that I love to death and will defend. There is a version of this game that does everything right within its own bubble and can provide a hearty dose of fun. Not the Meat Boy brand of fun, but simply fun. Let's be real: Tommy Refenes and the team behind this game couldn't reach the level of Edmund even if they tried. Hell, it's reasonable to assume that they will never strike gold, no matter what avenue they take. Deep down, though, there is a version of this game with an iron concentration that could've made a very unique experience if all of the cards were placed just right and all manners of bull were stripped from it.This is not that game.For starters, the ranking system is the worst part about the game. I understand that playing the game for a short amount of time and refunding it is a meme within the positive reviews, but I can say this with confidence: If the autorunning didn't scare them off, the ranking system would have, and they've saved themselves a boatload of time in jumping ship so soon. It's the least confident part about the game, to the point that Tommy didn't know what the ranking system would look like until damn near two years into development (the game took four years to develop). If it was done away with entirely, that's a start.We then need to address the level design. At its best, it's straightforward platforming with very little to it beyond your skill. At its worst, it's a incomprehensible puzzle that guarantees your death, which also isn't helped by the camera that prevents you from seeing the gauntlet you're about to be thrown into. If the level design was stripped bare and simply made into thousands of simple, yet addicting platforming bouts, we're getting somewhere.Finally, the control scheme. As is, it's far too restrictive and guarantees a very bland gameplay loop with no real agency on your part, simply going where the level will let you and punching when the level says you're supposed to. The two-button control scheme is very underutilized, and it's downright confirmed by Edmund that the original draft of the game had content-sensitive controls that allowed you more freedom, with Edmund explicitly saying that an uppercut was to be part of the main moveset, but it is relegated to a power-up in the final game, further emphasizing your lack of agency in the gameplay. Taking away the ability to move manually isn't a problem. What IS a problem is then not supplementing the missing space with more moves to compensate. To be as blunt as can be: An uppercut and the ability to turn around saves this game.That's it. If those things that I just mentioned were fixed, the game is redeemed. I've virtually given up on expecting a solid narrative or unique artstyle, since I suspect asking Tommy to be creative is much like asking a fish to do your taxes: It can try its ass off, but just looks really stupid in the process.My brother in Nycrama, Gavin the Scavenger, made a great point when he wasn't preoccupied with scamming people out of their TF2 hats: This game should have never been marketed as a sequel. This is something even Tommy has agreed with fairly recently, and came away from this game having learned a lesson. This is ultimately what the new team lacks when it's paramount to undertaking a franchise you didn't create: humility. Unfortunately, the Epic Games cash-out was the main goal on Tommy's part, and the reason this game was elevated beyond mobile game status, as one of the fundamental facets of the Team Meat Split was Edmund wanting to leave Meat Boy be and move on to other games, with Tommy wanting to do the opposite, as it was a safe title to milk for cash.Ultimately, a dozen sporadic YouTube rants won't ever be as powerful as looking at the playerbase for the new Meat Boy games. Decade old games, including the original, eclipse the new games overwhelmingly. Barely four years into the new team's tenure with the franchise, and its already stale.Let this be a lesson to everyone: Breathing new life into a previously defunct franchise only works if you're one hell of a dev team. Unfortunately, the franchise ended long ago when the rights were stripped away from Edmund. No amount of money can mask the stench of rotting meat.

_childDocuments_.review: People can call this a mobile game all they want for being an autorunner. I don't care. At it's core it's a pretty decent-designed one. It's still hilarious and has all the Meat Boy charm and I honestly wouldn't fault people for just looking up the cutscenes since they are fantastic. It is unfortunately kneecapped by larger problems.-The controls are unresponsive. Thought it was just me, but returning to the first game it was clear that this just doesn't feel good. This is its biggest knock and it's a BIG one considering it's a precise platformer.-It's also unintuitive. Dash-diving through every level isn't fun. Very few levels offer non-obvious optimal paths and exploiting this lackluster movement for necessary rankings is what ultimately prevented me from 100%ing this.-Some levels, by nature of being an autorunner, aren't clear. The "Final" boss had me stuck for a long time simply because it did not frame or explain anything well. Another had me confused because it just wasn't visually clear with all that was going on what to do. Levels themselves don't have as many problems until later on.-The game is fglitchy. I can't count how many times it teleported me across the screen into a blade or wall or something or I just fell through the ground or it didn't register me hitting enemies or whatever. It's not consistent and just dying or resetting a level (By the way, no "reset". You have to leave to map and reload it.) fixes it, but it's common enough to be annoying.-The music is unimpressive. In fact, I ended up playing most of it muted eventually. It's not  and I was never particularly attached to the original's, but it deserves more after the love put in to the rest of the game.-The price. I don't mind because it goes on deep sales often enough, but it is essentially Super Meat Boy RUN, a mobile game, and people getting it for the nostalgia of the first game's gameplay are getting a dumbed down version of that. They , however, getting much refined cutscenes so take this one as you will.Team Meat are good guys. They make these games with love and I don't want to, but it's a tight thumbs down from me. If you're like me and don't mind treating an autorunner like any other platformer and enjoyed the first game, I don't even wanna say "Don't get it," but it's not a recommendation.

For Super Meat boy it's not in the spirit for a sequel to the original and what the fanbase generally wanted-The difficulty curve is all over the place world to world -Procedural generated 'chunks' for every playthrough rather then a purely hand crafted experience-The boss fights are more awkward then enjoyable-Two different crashes in 10 hours of gameplayOpinion:I'm having fun with it hence the positive review. _childDocuments_.review: TL;DR --> An amazing, brutal autorunner with tons of replayability that keeps a good spirit of the first game, despite changing the mechanics. Some bugs were encountered but only on very late game content. On the bad side, performance could be better, music is very forgettable and so much content will be unseen due to its seed-based design.------------------------------------------------------------------------------First of all, I'd like to say that I was very tempted to downvote the game due to its EGS exclusivity period, but seeing how damaged it already is, I think it's unnecessary and I will just review the game itself, which in my opinion is very good. Super Meat Boy Forever (SMBF from now on) continues the events of the previous game but basically provides for the same concept: Dr. Fetus strikes again and this time it kidnaps Meat Boy and Bandage Girl's child.Unlike the first game, SMBF is an autorunner. There are only two controls: one button for jumping and punching (if you press jump in the air) and one button to crouch and rapidly fall while in the air. With only those tools the game is provided with an staggering amount of levels, combining tons of elements that at some points they feel like literal puzzles you need to figure out.In terms of content, this game has  of content. When you start a new savefile, you are provided with an specific seed, and like in procedural games, this seed will decide how your worlds will be shaped. There are thousands and thousands of level chunks being designed for each level, across all sorts of difficulties; some of them will be chosen and be set for your seed throughout the whole savefile. There are 6 levels on each world, with a final boss on them. Like in the original SMB, there are Light World (LW) versions of levels and Dark World (DW) versions. The game also has those nostalgic throwbacks from classic titles to be discovered and played. In terms of difficulty, I found SMBF to be much harder than the original one. Being an autorunner limits your recovery options enormously, and while LW levels are usually fine, DW levels will break you. The spike felt much higher than in SMB, so have fun suffering!Once you beat the game, you can start a New Game+. You keep some stats but levels are reset and you are given harder chunks. You can repeat this process indefinitely. I found the sountrack to be very generic and forgettable, and considering I spend much time on each world perfecting them, they became quite annoying rapidly.If you intend to go for very late game content (e.g. all achievements), keep in mind I found some bugs on how cycles work for some chunks. With all the amount of combinations and levels I guess it's logical that not all those situations could have been tested. Lastly, I would like to say that I felt this game runs on 60Hz no matter what. Timings were a bit weird to get used to and even when I was very experienced I kept having issues with it. Overall, despite the hate I've seen for the game, it is a very, very solid title if you treat it for what it is: an autorunner with both brutal and puzzly elements to have fun with. Absolutely recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: The original Super Meat Boy is one of my favorite games of all time. It is a masterclass in game design, it holds up extremely well, and it proved that there was an actual market for independent projects. Hell, most indie games today probably wouldn't exist without it. However, after Edmund McMillen left Team Meat to work on The Binding of Issac and other projects, Tommy Refenes and Team Meat decided to create a mobile game spinoff of Super Meat Boy. They then for some reason thought it was a good idea to turn that spinoff into a sequel, which leads us to Super Meat Boy Forever.I originally played this game on Switch, and I wish I could get my money back. The controls are stiff, the level design is repetitive and boring, the story is a Steven Universe tier fan fiction, they butchered the art style, and worst of all, they turned it into an auto runner. If this was still just a spinoff, this auto running aspect would have been fine, but this is a sequel. As a sequel, it is meant to improve upon the original, but it does the opposite. It takes away the freedom you had in the original and just constantly throws hastily slapped together "obstacles" while you move to the right constantly. It's honestly both insulting and kinda funny that the cutscenes have more effort put into them than the ENTIRE GAME. And for what? So we can see a boohoo sob story on Meat boy and how he and his family might die? Does nobody remember that in the original he was basically immortal? Like, that was the whole gimmick of the game. Maybe I wouldn't take the story so seriously if the gameplay wasn't the most unfun thing ever.This was the only reason I got this game again on steam. I thought the Forever Forge would've allowed fans of the series to make new levels that could have fixed the boring levels of the base game, but seeing that the player base for this game is basically dead, I don't see that happening. Not to mention they f#cked up the +A times by having you require to turn into a tryhard sweat who spams the punch button every 0.2 seconds just to see a letter show up at the end of the level.This game is a lot like the Megamind sequel that recently came out. Both are primarily aimed at 5 year olds, both are sequels to cult classics that completely miss the point, and both are PAINFULLY unfun to sit through. I'm honestly getting sick of sequels these days that don't bother improving upon the original in any way, and in some cases doing things that are worse than the original. Luckily, I was able to beat the main game in under an hour (without rushing) and spent 30 minutes in the level editor, so I now see no reason for me to not refund this trash pile. You're better off playing literally any other platformer.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Meat Boy Forever

_childDocuments_.review: Super Meat Boy Forever is a hardcore precision auto runner. The game is very aesthetically appealing, but level design feels uneven and unsatisfying. Rather than testing the player's reflexes, each segment feels like a puzzle that could be easily solved if it weren't for the arbitrary pressure exerted by the automatic movement. I have enjoyed the Bit Trip Runner games but otherwise I don't have a lot of experience with this genre. It seems to me that the meat boy treatment doesn't really mesh well with this type of game.

_childDocuments_.review: , have hesitated on getting this game for years, but finally decided to give it a fair shot since it was on sale for 2 dollars.even if it's beating a dead horse, the autorunning is definitely a point of contention in the game's design philosophy. while the autorunning itself is not as bad as some say, it ultimately works against all of the other ingame mechanics, including meat boy's moveset. especially later on in the game, new mechanics are incredibly finicky and unintuitive to play with (in particular the teleport and cube powerups) and would work as well if not better if you had the ability just to stop. not being able to stop and process any level really does hurt the game and leads to challenging sections becoming exponentially frustrating and teeth grinding.smbf has a sispyhean level of trial and error in its gameplay loop, and will most certainly treat you like its meaty ♥♥♥♥♥-- expect to start cussing out the t-bone in your freezer if you don't have the fortitude to deal with such a kind of game play loop. many chunks (human made pieces of the procedurally generated levels) are much more difficult and confusing compared to what is in the rest of the level, exasperated by the autorunner aspects. feeling like you completed the chunk wrong was much more common for me than a legitimate solution. poor mechanic usage also bleeds into the bosses, with the final 2-3 bosses in particular being confusing to baby kicking levels of frustration as you learn 30 minutes into the final boss fight that a duck punch doesn't activate the cube powerup while a dash punch does (WHY AREN'T POWERUPS ON A SEPARATE KEY)the art style is fine, didn't really bother me. the lack of edmund definitely shines though as any scrappy and crude humor is absent from this game. a lot of elements did not really match something edmund would do either, but that's to be expected if he simply wasn't working on the game. while there are def good tracks in the game, some of ridiculon's music work on this game is unfortunately not very great, and i wonder if it was less them and more thematic restrictions / guidelines from the smbf devs.this game just makes me really sad considering how long it was stuck in development hell, and just how much love and effort was placed into an ultimately flawed game. part of me wonders if the determination to keep the game as an autorunner ultimately worked against them in the long term, but were just too far along to make any major changes without even more delays. also wonder if the game would've stayed an autorunner if edmund was still present for its development.

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game quite a lot. Yeah, I honestly don't really get the hate for this one to be honest.Is it better than the first proper game? No. But, it is a good game. According to the devs this is the canonical Super Meat Boy 2, but don't be fooled because this game does play completely differently to the first game, and you could say that it isn't even similar to the first game at all considering how different it is. The game is an auto-runner, yes, but unlike most cheap mobile games, I think this game has great controls, great level design, and addictive gameplay. You can now punch while in middair which acts as a mid-air dash, and it completely saves the game for me to be honest, and actually gives the game speedrun potential and the level design is very much built around it with possible intended and unintended skips. The game is also randomly generated, so that of course, opens the door for an infinite number of playthroughs since there is an insane number of levels. This is great, in a sense, that makes this the Meat Boy game that will never end, however I would say that this makes the level design feel a little less... intentional? It's still good stuff, but sometimes it feels like certain levels don't really connect properly to each other, still fun, but it isn't anywhere near the level of carefully crafted level design in the first game. I actually like the visuals in this game a lot more than the first game, looks like it's going for a hand-drawn aesthetic, and I dig it hardcore. Animations are silky smooth, the sprites are on-point, the game runs buttery smooth (at least for me, I've heard others have a bad time with performance, but I can't tell if that's due to poor optimization or their PC being bad), the only thing I don't really like about the visuals are the fact that some elements and objects do have a very thick outline, which I see why they chose to do that, but it does make the game look more like a mobile game than it really is (despite the fact that it IS coming to mobile soon, if not, out already). OST is decent, nowhere close to as good as the original, but there are some bangers in here. The game does have flaws, but the thing I liked the least were two of the boss battles, the second to last, and the final boss. The 3 fights beforehand are decent, I like how they have a health bar now, but the last 2 bosses, without spoiling anything, feel very repetitive and cheaply designed, the final boss in particular has more trial and error than anything else in the game, which wouldn't be too bad of an issue since this is still the series known for its instantaneous respawning after dying which eliminates most frustration with the game, but they can take longer than a minute, which makes respawning a lot more annoying when you have to repeat the same process all over again. But yeah, at it's core, it is a Meat Boy game, it has the things you'd expect in a game in the series like tough but fair platforming, saw blades, death, and middle fingers, but it does play completely differently and that can be a turn off. If you look past it though, it's still a good game, it doesn't live up to the original, if I were asked to recommend one or the other, I'd recommend the original all day everyday, but this one is fun too, and it's one of the better auto-runners out there, has good level design, it's fun to play, has most of the charm of Meat Boy, it's a fun experience, but you'll have to subvert your expectations, if you're looking for a true Super Meat Boy sequel, this isn't it. I'd lean on like a high 7 or a low 8/10 for this one, if you're feeling cautious on it, buy it on a sale, or get it for $10 if you have the first game before the half-off deal is up.

_childDocuments_.review: Super Meat Boy Forever is an auto running platformer that is as good as an auto-runner can get.That's the thing though, auto-runners lose most peoples interests very quickly and this game is not so different. Sure, after beating the game you can continue playing it since the levels are generated randomly from a pool of sections but will you ?I beat it once and i don't think i will come back to it. Keep that in mind when you are buying it. 1 Playthrough will take around 3 to 4 hours if you solely focus on the main game.Other than that, getting used to only using 2 buttons is not easy and also results in a lot of miss inputs. Not being able to be precise with your inputs in a precision platformer is just wrong.One thing i loved was the cutscenes. The animations and the artsyle are both incredible. To sum it all up, the game is thoroughly fine but never great. If you are ok with playing slightly above average games go ahead and buy it but don't expect a masterpiece.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a huge fan of the original Super Meat Boy so I tried to go into this game blind, ignored videos/reviews/ratings/etc and gave the game the benefit of the doubt. Unfortunately I still ended up regretting and refunding that decision. I gave the game about an hour and a half and in that time completed apparently a bit over half of it but I found the game to just be boring. It’s not as awful as people seem to say it is, but it’s just not fun. The lack of control (even if it’s literally advertised as an autorunner) still hurt it in the end as a lot of deaths felt unavoidable due to it. Gameplay wise it ends up being very simple: you jump, punch and dive/duck. These controls don’t feel that great in practice and I often found myself frustrated with the boss fights due to either just BARELY missing a punch and flat out dying for it, having the dive keep me stuck on a boss when it was about to kill me though the game trains you to dive through enemies prior, The little control you are given feels unfortunately clunky and made a lot of the game feel like a very tedious trial and error with little say in what happens, or genuinely frustrating when you know what to do, how to execute it but are either a few frames off or meatboys autorunning screws it up. One positive aspect I’ll list is that the cutscenes are wonderfully animated and fun to watch, with Nugget and Dr. Fetus imo being the stars of the show. The music is also decent, albeit feeling a bit uninspired compared to their other games in the past.All this to say, I’m still disappointed unfortunately. Even disregarding the controversies surrounding the game’s exclusivity elsewhere, avoiding reviews and attempting to go in blind, the game itself still ended up just not being worthwhile. I personally wouldn’t recommend it, but if you are a fan of autorunners or speedrunning, this game may have potential for you, it just didn’t for me. That’s all.

But as bad as it is... .... ehhhhhhhhh, I don't think it's refund worthy - not really.  Maybe one day it will just click back into place like a rusted replacement knee.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to preface this with I absolutely loved Super Meat Boy I 100%'d and did everything except the No Death Achievements.I bought this game at 2.00 and feel it was just barely worth it Let's discuss the game on it's own merits firstI have a massive problem with auto-generated levels as there's usual a lack of cohesion or it feels like there isn't any charm to the level design.Like everyone who plays it won't be able to go oh remember that segment in this level or that level or how much fun it felt once I got passed X.For a game about auto-running there are periods where in my seed I had to wait in order for something to move in order to progress. Which just isn't fun doesn't feel good to just wait.So much of the game that I experienced was me needing to solve levels rather than doing a bunch of cool movement to overcome the obstacles.Now I will say I did experience bits and pieces of the game where it did have those moments and it did feel really fun, but those were really few and far between.I will say there are a ton of gimmicks in the game but it feels like there's just gimmicks to have gimmicks none of them really felt special or memorable in the design of the levels.The Final Boss is complete memorization.The First Boss is the best boss.Every other boss is forgettable and uninteresting.The game doesn't feel difficult in the sense that I made a mistake but more so I didn't move in the exact way the game demanded of me or moved into this exact position. Rather than tight controls and building a difficult game around it.What I will say is that passed the 2nd Area the game does improve it feels less waiting around at least in my seed and more action oriented that didn't feel as tedious or puzzle-like.The references in the game are cool for those who get them.The warp zones were done really well.The music was really good overall and the story was ok.All in all I cannot recommend this even on 2.00 it's just such a forgettable experience and a reminder why auto-generated content doesn't really work well for platformer type games.

_childDocuments_.review: NB: My review is not impacted by Epic Store exclusivity, or it being an auto-runner, or it "not being meat boy" like many reviews seem to be.Repetitive level design within worlds, an unnecessary level of precision in many places (within a game engine that doesn't seem well-suited to provide said precision to the player), and a general "lack of freedom of movement" (granted, a feature of an autorunner).They all add up to a game that is unfortunately just not terribly fun to play for me.These may be features that you are seeking from a game, but in a world with many other far superior avenues to utilise your limited time on this earth, I just don't feel like this game cuts the mustard.

_childDocuments_.review: As a huge fan of the original Super Meat Boy this game is incredibly disappointing. There is no reason why this should have been an autorunner. The whole 6000 chunks nonsense means the difficulty is all over the place, conveyance of direction can be really poor and every level in the game has this sort of samey feeling since every chunk is strung along by a flat path. A+ time in levels is a huge pain to get now since levels are longer instead of cut into bit sized chunks. The autorunning strips any precision out of this precision platformer.Forget about this game and buy the original instead. And if you already have that buy The End Is Nigh, a proper successor to Meat Boy.

_childDocuments_.review: Super Meat Boy Forever is a runner/platformer game made using the Super Meat Boy characters. While the aesthetic of the game matches the really great Super Meat Boy well enough, the actual game itself is pretty bad.The problem is that this is a runner game, and it is difficult to make those particularly good. It tries to use the Super Meat Boy aesthetic of stages full of horrible dangers, but because it is a runner, it doesn’t end up feeling as fun to beat as it does when you’re doing the precision platforming of Super Beat Boy. The constant forced movement forces the levels to have particular sorts of designs, and while they do a fair bit with it, the self-imposed limits make it hard to really feel like this is all that great. 2D platformers are just more interesting than runner games; while taking away your ability to slow down is an interesting concept in theory, in practice it is more of a gimmick than a genre for a reason. It's basically a game where you have like two buttons, duck and jump, and there's only so much you can do with that.In the end, I gave up on this game after clearing a few worlds and realizing I wasn’t really having fun with it. It wasn’t too hard; it just didn’t hold my interest.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, it's okay in my opinion. I can recommend this game if you're completely fine with playing auto-runners, or just like Meat Boy. Controls can be kind of wonky at times. For example, not registering your attack/slide in time. If you're used to playing games with uncapped FPS, then this game might bring you difficulty since it's capped at 60 FPS. The so called "chunks" can be very difficult at times since the game is an auto-runner, so it works off checkpoints for every level. (not to say EVERY auto-runner does this but still.) To me, I think BIT.TRIP RUNNER did it better because there's more of a grace period, along with better spawn positions. The difficulty from the previous game is converted over to this game well, and dare I say this game is harder than its predecessor, Super Meat Boy, as its stages are much longer along with supplying more gimmicks to trip you up. Also, since you're always on the move, that only supports the challenge since the game forces you to play the levels in a very linear manner whilst never stopping. The inability to move freely makes finding optimal strats or methods that could make the level/area easy difficult, since you have to adapt to finding these while moving 24/7.  Don't be surprised if you find yourself strenuously trying to complete a level you've been stuck on for a long time.As far as I can tell, the unlockable characters in this game all function exactly the same, as in they're all Meat Boy/Bandage Girl clones, which is kind of a bummer. I guess that's thanks to the limitations of it being an auto-runner. Not really much else to say about them except for that. If you were wanting a different experience while playing the game, I'd stick with Super Meat Boy.The music is okay in my opinion. Not too much to say about this either. It holds up, but I don't think it has that hook that Super Meat Boy's music does. It's made by Ridiculon, the same band that made the soundtracks for a good handful of Edmund's more popular games. I enjoy their music a lot, but I don't believe this game's music holds up to their previous work, like The Binding of Isaac's OST, and The End is Nigh's (even if they're simply rehashed classical music).And the art is also okay too. It's definitely much better than Super Meat Boy in terms of looking more clean and polished, along with having a ton of smooth frame-by-frame animations. I say it's okay because it doesn't have that charm the previous game has, and by that I mean it has a really cutesy and glossy look to it which I would never find myself associating with Super Meat Boy. This is more of a nitpick because the Flash era was part of my childhood, so Super Meat Boy's style appeals to me more than this.There's a lot different between Super Meat Boy and Forever, more than simply if it's an auto-runner or not. Personally, I'm enjoying the game. It's fast paced, has that high difficulty ceiling that I tend to like, and simple controls. If you aren't turned off by any of this, I'd say go on and play it. If you were, then hey, nothing wrong with still playing the good ol' classic Super Meat Boy. Hope this helps.

_childDocuments_.review: Started off having mixed feelings about the different direction taken with this game, ended up liking this one more than the original. Assuming at least some significant chunk of the negative reviews have to do with Epic, when evaluating the game itself, i'm honestly not really sure why people are so bent out of shape over how this one plays. It's put together pretty well for a small team, seems to have replayability specifically in mind, brings the same kind of hardcore challenge the first one gave us, and is simply overall designed better than the original. It feels good to play, is satisfying to clear the difficult portions, and I sat for almost twenty minutes trying to find a single thing to criticize the game on, and really could not think of anything of substance.Sorry, I don't care about drama with other storefronts, I don't have beef with Epic or Team Meat. The game is good, and I'm glad it wasn't just more of the same.

_childDocuments_.review: Once again I find myself wishing for a neutral rating. The OG Super Meat Boy was one of my favorite games for a long while and I was legitimately excited when I heard there was going to be a sequel. While it's fun enough in it's own right, the auto-running aspect takes a lot of getting used to and I feel like it detracts from the game as a whole. Super Meat Boy was all about finding creative ways to get through levels fast, but something is lost when the levels are all randomly generated. There are still interesting shortcuts to take, but executing them doesn't feel as satisfying here. I appreciated the cutscenes and hidden content paying homage to classic games and most of the mechanics are interesting. However, the game has a tendency to eat inputs now and again and the one button jump-dash mostly got me killed when I would try to wall jump a frame too early and punch instead. Bosses are mostly a chore. There are things I like about SMBF, but like many others, I'm mostly disappointed it's fallen short of the mark. Wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Had been debating whether to leave the final veredict as positive or negative, but the 4th boss was what finally called the shot...Yes I'm aware of all the fanboyish of "iT's NoT dUh SaMe GaMe!", when it comes to comparing it to the original Meatboy. However, if this is literally a sequel (Nugget pretty much nails it), it's impossible not to draw comparisons.I like the fact that you're given more mobility options, and a way to finally attack enemies. Some mechanics definitely feel refreshing and at first, the game feels like going into the right direction... Until about halfway thru The Clinic. Afterwards it feels rather clunky with the mechanics, and they feel like they're just there to hamper progress, some more than others, and the perma-scrolling is definitely something that takes away more than it brings to the table. Several sections feel like if you were able to at least change direction, or not be constantly pushed, would be way more fun to play. Checkpoints are nice and all, but some sections you have to make really convoluted jumps without really any time to assess the situation because you're frantically pushed forward without really any time to think about the puzzle; if I had to draw a comparison I would directly compare it to the running away sections from Silent Hill: Shattered Memories. You just blindly run in the general direction away from the danger, hoping to eventually reach the exit.Back to 4th boss, it felt so unnecesarily clunky and "pray to RNGesus" due to the disjointed hitbox and the random nature of objective staying in place, or landing 12km away from you, as well as the timings where the obstacles can change literally while you're standing on the wall. Too much button mashing and hoping for the best, instead of good old OG Meatboy calculating and figuring out the puzzle and actions. So yeah, this one's definitely a no from me.

_childDocuments_.review: I hate to add to the pile of negative reviews but I have to. _childDocuments_.review: Quick score: 5/5Notes: Don't buy it expecting gameplay similar to the original meat boy. However, if you are a fan of platformers in general, this game is actually great. It is an "autorunner" technically, however there is a LOT of depth to the mechanics and plenty of room for speedrunning and shortcuts. The overall game feels much closer to something like the chase sequences of rayman than a typical "autorunner".Lots of people crying about the auto runner aspect don't seem to recognize that once you start speedrunning and optimizing most platformers, they all devolve into auto runners to some extent. You hold the run button and time your button presses, the only difference now is that the game holds the run button for you. Look at almost any speedruns of platformers like Rayman, Donkey Kong Country, Super Mario Bros, etc. and they are almost all indistinguishable from "autorunners" 95% of the time.And for the record, I usually hate autorunners such as geometry dash or the bit trip series. But there is so much depth and nuance to the seemingly simple mechanics of this game that it honestly shouldnt even be considered an autorunner at all because it doesn't really play like any other game in the genre. You can use walls to completely stop, and you also frequently change direction, both things that pretty much break the rules of the genre.While there may be a bit more trial and error when it comes to learning the stages, you are given plenty of checkpoints and they are often spread less than 10 seconds apart so deaths are not at all painful. People also like to pretend that the original super meat boy didn't involve trial and error, but that is absolutely not the case. Not even to mention the homing missile and and homing black ball enemies, super meat boy was all about dying repeatedly until you "figured out" the timing of levels and mastering the inputs. So while in some ways it is different, in practice it is really not that different..

_childDocuments_.review: I tried, I really tried, but this game just isn't good. I don't care that its an autorunner, but I do care about the difficulty that isn't difficult in a way that Super Meat Boy was, but instead only frustrating. Some levelpieces are so incredibly tight to get through, that if it wasn't for all the checkpoints, I would have quit way earlier.I played through many hard games in my life, but this one is hard for all the wrong reasons.Yes it is hard, but it isn't fun.I had no problem, trying a hard level in Super Meat Boy for multiple hours, because it always felt like I missplayed and it was fun getting better.In this game however, it always feels like the game wants you to already know everything there is to know about the game, which only happens if you die to each obstacle to understand how it works. But with enough patience, you'd eventually have memorized everything. But I don't want to play a puzzle, I want to play a platformer if I'm playing Super Meat Boy.The worst part are the bosses. They just don't work. The first boss was easy, saw no problem in there and honestly every boss should have been somewhat like that, but they aren't.The second boss is way too tight. It wants you to press down to fall faster, to be able to dodge its attacks. Fair, its an autorunner, what else are you gonna do? But it feels like you get a few frames to do so. It is unnecessarily hard, just a tiny bit more time, would make it feel much better.The third boss was alright, fitting for a third boss imo.The fourth boss feels like you're trying to fight a swarm of flies, but if they ever touch you anywhere, you're dead. But you have to touch them in order to progress the fight. Sometimes you hit the enemy and die soon after, just because you didn't hit the entire mob and one tiny piece kept running at you, even though you're in your attack. It took me way too long to beat it and it didn't feel satisfying at all.The last boss i fought was the fifth (I don't know if there is more) and after half an hour, I still haven't figured out the puzzle on how it actually supposed to be done. I only ever get to the first time hitting him, but climbing up the wall to the second part seems to already be the hardest part of it. I don't know wether I'm supposed to be quick, save an extra item or I'm just running a wrong path. No idea. Sometimes it worked, sometimes it didn't. More times it didn't...Up there I didn't even understand how to proceed at all. The game has two controls, what is there that I could possibly be doing? Seems like its once again something very tight... and feels like that boss should have checkpoints there.So, I gave up. I didn't even get to see the Dark World. While I did do 100% in the original Super Meat Boy. What the hell man....

_childDocuments_.review: There's a lot of things to like about this game, but most of them are not the actual meat (not much pun intended) of the game.  The cutscenes are cool, the slightly-more stylized art is appealing, the in-your-face support for rando racing is fantastic for those in that niche....but.  The pure platforming charm of the original, which was so-finely tuned to work both to train the casual player and reward the master, is completely gone.  In its place is a runner game controlled with a slide button and a jump-punch button.  There are nuances here, but you can't ever walk up to them.  You're running running running and the game simply demands that you react, and do so perfectly.Even the so-called tutorial bits come at you at absurd speeds.  A little sub-window shows off what a button does, but only about a half-second before you need to use it, and use it with precise timing, or you get splatted back to the start/checkpoint.  This isn't just ignoring new players, it's outright hostile.The original Super Meat Boy was an all-time classic.  This disaster of a jumped-up phone game sequel is already being quickly forgotten.  I picked it up at 90% off via Summer Sale, and I'm thinking I regret it already.  Seriously, though.  Who thought that  degrees of freedom of control in a platformer which otherwise has the same game-world physics was a good idea?

_childDocuments_.review: Oh boy, this game. Super Meat Boy Forever is a hardcore precision platformer, and it's definately not for everybody.SMBF is an autorunner, and that intriguing modification of classic formula divided community straight in half. That said, this game is extremely well made and polished, do not compare it to your generic free to play mobile phone autorunners, quickly slapped together to make some bucks on ads.Clarification of some crucial points:1. Not an endless autorunner.2. Not randomly generated.Each world has 6 levels and a boss fight. Levels are made of hand-made chunks of varying difficulty, randomness only comes from order and selection of said chunks.Team Meat not only managed to perfectly recreate original fluid and highly responsive movement of Meat Boy, but to add so much more new mechanics and gimmicks to every single of 5 worlds, while not damaging core gameplay in any way.This is still a Super Meat Boy game, you still have your wall jumps, warp zones, traps, global timers, intricate, borderline convoluted level design and a lot, a lot of trial and error and frustration. Some chunks even feel more like a puzzle now, you actually have to understand what the heck is going on before making progress.Original Super Meat Boy is a hard game, and maybe my memories of it are a bit blurred, but man, SMBF actually feels so much harder. This game is . Insane timings, tight squeezes and nuclear mix of absurd mechanics are already melting grey matter, now try adding generally faster gameplay on top of that.They did such a fantastic job with visuals in this game. Every world is distinct, every color palette is balanced and pleasant. Light worlds are filled to the brim with vibrant colors, while Dark worlds are gloomy and bleak. More than that, every single level has its own style, lighting and background, depending on what gameplay mechanic it represents. Also I absolutely love angry Sun in Tetanusville.Storyline is served via cinematics after each chapter, totalling up to about 40 minutes long cartoon.Every sprite is crisp and readable, every animation is smooth and well telegraphed. Well done, Team Meat.I find it kinda hilarious that some people claim music being bad in this game. World 1 music is pretty bizarre, I get it, I also understand that most of people claiming said thing never actually did make it past World 1, but come on, haven't you heard main theme, its right there, on title screen, which comes before World 1, have you? Well, at least that's a good sign of a person whose opinion is not really relevant, I guess.Also, simple fact that music was done by Ridiculon and Scattle already ensures a lot of bangers in here, ye know. Overall musical arrangement is fitting and well made.Super Meat Boy Forever is a very fun, extremely challenging and so different, yet so familiar precision platformer.If you are able to leave "used to be better" mindset behind, you will get many, many hours of entertainment out of this game.If you enjoy difficult and diverse platformers - give it a shot, don't let negative reviews with 15 minutes of playtime scare you away.This game clearly is a labor of love, and I'm giving it my wholehearted recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll give my positives first, because I have to give this game SOME credit. the presentation is ultimately better than the first game; they clearly had a bigger budget and created a fully 2D animated game that adds more style and detail to the setting and character designs. And, while not as memorable as the original Danny Baranowsky score, the soundtrack is pretty good, with a wider range of instruments.Also, just like the first game, the controls are super precise and immediately respond to the player's input. Another cool addition is being able to attack enemies.Finally, getting the true ending doesn't require finishing the Dark World, and you'll appreciate that, trust me.Otherwise, this game was TERRIBLE! From what I heard, it was originally planned to be a spin-off game exclusive to mobile devices, but then they turned it into a direct sequel on consoles, and it certainly shows. They didn't put in any of the effort it takes to turn a mobile game into a console game, and it's even worse that THIS is considered the follow up to the original Super Meat Boy from 10 years ago. My problem with this game is its design. No matter how good the control is, no matter how hard you try, nothing will prepare you for the gameplay and the stage design. Unlike the first game, this is an AUTO-SCROLLING game, and each stage is comprised of several pre-made fractions of a stage; when you create a new file, all of the fractions of each stage are RANDOMLY GENERATED, so you can't even use a guide for this game, unless it's the first stage in a world. You're constantly running forward, and you cant stop, unless you stand in a corner or pause the game. And there's little breathing room for finishing a stage however you want. Even if you move faster or earlier than intended, there's a 90% chance that the obstacle in front of you will kill you in one hit, because it moves slower. Granted, you have checkpoints this time, but most of these stages go on WAY longer than they did in the first game, sometimes going on for 5-10 minutes at a time. Each world has a different stipulation, all of which should have been a part of your basic move set, i.e. turning back without wall jumping, and air-dashing up. And I bring this up, because this game also brings back the time trials. If you complete a stage with a Grade A+ rank, you unlock the Dark World version of that stage, a.k.a its hard mode. But NONE of these stages, or the pre-made fractions, were designed with time trials in mind, because you have to constantly dash to the goal-post, and you may end up losing by just ONE second. But, more importantly, HOW do they expect us to complete time trials in an AUTO-SCROLLER?? To make things worse are the boss fights. ALL of them go on way too long, and they, once again, have to be defeated in the most specific way possible. If you try jumping instead of ducking, you'll die. If you attack way too many times, a projectile will come up from behind you and kill you. Unlike the regular stages, these multi-phased boss fights have NO checkpoints, so you can be stuck on them for over half an hour!None of these issues are made easier with the unlockable characters. Most of them are just a change in cosmetics, with no unique abilities of their own to make the stages easier.In short, this is a poorly designed platformer, and a worse sequel to such an amazing indie game. Just stick with the original. It's much easier to pick up and play, and it's nowhere near as punishing for making mistakes. Best of all, you have complete control of your character, and you have the ability to come to a complete stop. MAYBE play the next game, because the ending implies that there will be another sequel. But do NOT waste your time or money on this game, it's not worth the frustration.

_childDocuments_.review: I knew this game was going to be an auto runner before it came out. As a huge fan of platformers, I was surprised, but trusted the studio to bring the same quality to the game as the first. I've even enjoyed plenty of auto runner games, from the most basic Temple Run to the Bit Trip Runner games that I'd say Super Meat Boy Forever most closely matches. But after having played the game up through to the boss of Tetanusville, I had to put it down, cause I was just not having fun.Super Meat Boy was a devastatingly hard game of precision platforming, and this has some of the same spirit. But the de facto inability to control your movement, and more importantly, many of the games puzzles and bosses being built around these limitations, will be a constant burr in your side. IF you've never played Super Meat Boy, and you enjoy auto runners, give this a try first. Maybe you'll like it for what it is, and you'll be able to look past the things it so clearly isnt.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, still. Let this genre be known as a chunky-environment-puzzle-platformer.4K on a GTX1070 is easy, 8x AA, no issues. Let's get this straight from the start: The game is auto-running for you, but that doesn't mean the control of movement is not there. There are specific golden triangles that enable you to stop, and/or change direction if required. There are more frequently enemies that are near the spinning blades but when sliding in crouch , you may easily attack, as if to be sweeping the yard.Playing with the controller is awesome. You will generally be double jumping, once to jump - Hold it for longer/bigger jumps, and then tap again for Kick or Punch, LT is a way to kill yourself, and restart the current chapter you're on.The auto-mechanic mechanism has cleverly caused each level to be broken up into chunks that you pass, and 'conquer' while trying to reach the end. Instead of best times now, it's more like, how many deaths per level. Could you do it with 0 ? practice of 2-3 per level -yes, you easily could. The constant challenge is now present, unlike Super Meat Boy which originally had many fast-paced levels , where even shortcuts could make up some time,  this game tries to punish you, and make you look ahead, even when you are surrounded, and trapped at the same time. You need to be looking for ceilings to slow yourself down/prevent your forward running, and go the other way, while the environment initiates traps as it enters the scene.All the traps, and interactions await your arrival to begin.Sweet Replays are still there just like the first one, and it's pretty awesome to see it happen as one smooth timeline after you have conquered any given levels. You actually appreciate these replays even more than the first, because you can spot your own mistakes here too. The level design, Spawn random seed at the start of each Save/Campaign is probably where this game will blow up. The value of this game is actually infinite, when you think of 6000 chunks, and 70+ levels, which use roughly 100 pieces per level, to bring your chapters that you pace through it in.I won't lie, there was incredible anger, and energy on not passing a specific spot, but the beauty is that you can just proceed to the next level - unlike last game-  and still play the same levels with different characters. The character roster looks HUGE - obviously, as a noob that just started, I have bandaid and super meat beater, I'm sure the originals and more will be there too, with some new spices to add along. What Super Meat Boy was famous for was level-design, and how quickly we got through them. This is exactly the same, whilst actually ramping up the times that you spend per level, because you are not fully in control. So, what this causes is each level to be a puzzle. It is up to you to scout ahead with the parts you see in your window currently.The biggest big is the menu not having a Quit button ?  -> Probably a Forever™ joke, It's fun, it raises the heart rates, and gives good sense of accomplishments. You may challenge friends with the same Campaign Seed-generation, but no co-op is here, maybe it will arrive in a DLC, Overall, the original formulae were amplified to cater to an even larger audience, while adding, and subtracting from what made it great, it's still a gem to behold, and all the negative reviews are either Epic-store haters, - [ungrateful game claimers] or people that are not able to mentally stimulate themselves to play a classic™ genre with a 2020's concept, even if it were to be put on rails for them.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a runner. Pretty good one, but still a runner (it looks and feels like a mobile game). If you ok with this, then go ahead and get it – it's good. If you expect Super Meat Boy 2 – it's not that, because controls and gameplay are different.If you don't know what the runner is, you should consider if you should play this – character runs AUTOMATICALLY, you can only control the character with 2 buttons (A - jump or punch in the air, Down - slide or start fast falling with a punch in the air).A few things about the game:- It's fun, if you like runners and/or hardcore platformers.- Pretty short (5-6 hours to complete the main game), which is not bad. There's a lot of additional hard levels though (dark version of every level and at least one additional world).- It's not the same as the Super Meat Boy game, though the feel of the game is pretty much the same.- Doesn't require too much brain juice. Playable with some TV show on the second screen.- It's pretty hard (mostly on bosses). Sometimes you need to spend 30-60 minutes on the same level. If you are not into hardcore games, it's not for you.- Level design in different then Super Meat Boy, seems more like The End is Nigh: there're checkpoints on the level, levels are longer then in Super Meat Boy, but there're ~10 checkpoints on every level.- Plot is pretty strange. A lot of animated scenes. Feels like a cartoon for small children. It's not bad, but not my cup of tea.- Graphics are... Well, they are ok, but feels too cartoony. Some stuff looks great, but if you see the game on the stream, you probably will not want to play it (too mobile visuals, I guess?)- Music is ok overall. Although World 1 music doesn't fit, it still sounds nice.- This was supposed to be a mobile game if I understand right. Somehow it's a PC game now, and there's no mobile version of it, which is pretty strange.- After some time of playing you want to play again Super Meat Boy.If you ok with controlling only jumps and punches, get the game. If not – don't. The game is good, but not for all.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought Super Meat Boy and got an auto-runner. A masterpiece? _childDocuments_.review: I was exciting to try this out, but I am incredibly disappointed.  I am not even giving it much time because I do not want to waste my life away with something that I know I do not like.  I loved Super Meat Boy which is made clear by my 30+ hours on record.  Even after beating the game I kept playing.  SMBF, hereafter referred to as F, is not fun -- the only requirement for a game.  You literally press one button.  It runs for you.  You have no control.  It is like watching a movie where you need to press a button to make the frames move forward.Games with simplistic controls can work, but those games still need polish.  Autogenerated, autorunner levels where you press one button lack quality control.  For example, One Finger Death Punch, is an inventive and fun game.  They took the time to make sure it was carefully balanced and the controls feel tight.  SMB had tight controls and was fun to play even if you died over and over again.  If you wanted more challenge, you can have it.  If you got frustrated with a level, you could simply come back later.  And it even had competitive aspects for speed runners without randomization.  F completely lacks the qualities that made SMB good.There is no way this game should be priced higher than SMB.  It is like a bad mobile app.  I do not recommend purchasing F unless it drops to $1 or below.  I hope that the next game learns from the mistakes of this one.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a great game, but not what you want from a sequence of Super Meat Boy...There are great visuals, the story it's there, like in the first game (although, in the near the end things get a little uninteresting to me), there is a gameplay that works (with its flaws), there are few songs with eletric guitar that are very good, some secrets that are fun to unveil and it is a Super Meat Boy themed game. It's a good game...While in the original game every stage is a little obstacle course where you have to keep improving your skills and trying new approachs in order to get the rankings (You die, you try again from beginning until you improve your skills or find a better route to win), in Super meat boy Forever, you are challenged with long stages divided in little segments where you have to find out what is the solution for each segment by trial and error and, if you want a better ranking, you have to memmorize every obstacle of a stage and hope that the gameplay doesn't screw you. It's not satisfying, feels like a chore honestlySMB1 - Fast-paced short trial and error stages with room for exploration.SMBF - On-rail long stages with patterns to memmorize in order to execute precision commandsSo, you see, you take a game with stages with a lot of room for exploration and different ways to win and switch it to one that takes away any agency from the player to show its skills and force it to do precision memmoriezed commands.... You just can't simply take away resources from your player and demand it to do it in a harder and more boring way.I guess, in the end of the day, it's a good game, the main issue lies in having it marketed as a super meat boy 2, not a spin-off. People waited for a Super Meat Boy but got a Geometry Dash kind of game...
