_childDocuments_.review: This is a yes and no recommendation.  If you are a fan of point and click games then definitely get this title.  The visuals and sounds are great and the hint system gives you subtle hints to help you along with no hand holding involved.If this is to be your first attempt at a point and click game then I would advise against this title.  It is slow and can be a bit tedious at times.  Some puzzles take a bit of trial and error to achieve even with the hints given.
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: Quick:3/5.  A sight to behold, Papetura is a visually appealing point-and-click game with a novel art style.  As its name suggests, the game is designed presumably by taking photos and videos of paper characters and backgrounds, that I believe were modeled by hand.  The art style is phenomenal.  It has a great soundtrack, and pretty decent game-play.  I recommend that you play this game if you are looking for a very short, and unique point-and-click game. More:Papetura is very pleasing to look at.  I have never played a game with this type of visual aesthetic.  If nothing else, the appearance of Papetura will keep you interested throughout your experience.  There is a slight orange / sepia hue to the game that is very relaxing and easy on the eyes.  Though great to behold, you probably won't be wowed by anything in this game.  I can't remember being excited or overwhelmed at any time, however I did feel good while playing it.The main character appears to be a sheet of paper.  You take control of them, and set out on an adventure through a strange, and flammable world.  There are many puzzles that you will have to solve, some a little more obscure than others.  You will eventually find your way if you persist.  I was stuck perhaps once during my play-through, but I did not have to look up a guide to progress.  I enjoyed the music a lot while playing this game.  There are no tracks that stick out in my mind, now, yet I remember thinking that the audio was great while playing it.  All of the music in this game was immediately copyright struck in any video that I tried to upload or stream... so if you plan on making a YouTube or Twitch video of this game... just be aware of that.  I do not fault the developers or composers for this, because the music is that good and unique, in my opinion.Character designs are very fun, and you may even learn to love some of these critters during your short romp through this paper world.  Yes, the game is short.  It took me 98 minutes to play through this game from start to finish.  I have the impression that it could be finished in an hour if you already know what you're doing, though.Overall, I do recommend this game.  I have never played anything quite like it, and I greatly appreciated how different it was.  In the future, I hope that these developers make another game just like it, only much longer.
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: That was a superb experience for two hours of my time. None of the puzzles were overly complicated, and the environment was a staggeringly impressive feat to explore. The details kept a fairly simple game so engaging. I love that the hints themselves were a mini-game! Highly recommend for people who want a chill experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: The game presents astonishing art and imagined world worked out to the detail. The fairy tail story charmed in the paper and motion. Saying game has amazing graphics is like saying nothing. You can be dumped into architected world where emotions and values plays a role. This is enjoyable playable game. You won't be challenged with extremely sophisticated puzzles therefore it is very suitable for kids. It can turn to family play if you would like, what I did with my daughter.
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: A delightful game that's worth a buy!Here's why. (unintentional rhyme)Pros:- FANTASTIC soundtrack. Audio in a game is just as important as everything else, and this game has an incredible score to really bring you to a new world.- Smooth controls. While it's a simple Point&Click style gameplay design, the path-finding is very nice, and usually very responsive. Even the hint feature has a gameplay mechanic that works very well for challenging players that want to be given the solutions to the puzzles.- INCREDIBLE environments, that are all REAL! The dedication, time, and creativity put into designing and crafting each level, lighting and all, gives this world so much more heart and life! It's what makes you fully respect and agree with the choice of pricing it at 12 dollars.Cons:- Short. I don't blame the people behind this game, as for the number of levels there were, each one got a crazy amount of work put into them. But it is something to keep in mind when going in.- Not a lot of replay value. It's short, so it's no hard work to go through. And you could challenge yourself to a speedrun, but there's no secrets or alternative endings/decisions you can do. You'll get all the achievements on your first playthrough, as they're all based on progress.- Weird pacing. Most of it is very well paced. But some points you'll feel like things jumped ahead a bit, whether it's escalation in tension, or exposition dumps. Makes it feel like the levels and puzzles were thought of first, then the story/plot that we follow with it second.Overall, I highly recommend this game, just to bring yourself into this fascinating, beautiful, atmospheric world!
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: Papetura is a puzzle adventure game, it is beautiful, short and sweet. You can tell the dedication the developer has towards the art in this game, it is made out of real paper and therefore, the art relies heavily on the paper texture and the lighting, which makes this game art unique and original. The simple color scheme suits this game a lot, if not it actually enhances the graphic even more. The environment design is great, and character design is adorable as well. I actually regret not taking any screenshots in the game, mainly because I got too immersed in it. I received this game from my friend as a gift, but I say this game absolutely worth the price, for it is a masterpiece.
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: I really recommend this cool little Indie puzzle game though be aware it is only 2 hours long. It's funny how I completed it in only 115 minutes and could have still been eligible for a refund. I am not going to refund though that would be an unfair thing to do because Papetura is a fun, charming game and has obviously been made by some talented people. The puzzles are simple but fun to solve and quirky. The main appeal is the world design, it's all real miniature sets made from paper and cardboard. You can tell it's "real" just as you could tell Wallace and Gromit animations were made from real modelling clay. The character and creatures are well animated with some real imaginative designs. There is a very basic story which is very cute and put a smile on my face. It's a short puzzle game but for the creative talent on show and the games charm it's worth every penny in my book.
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: Simply gorgeous game.  Original paper design that is beautifully executed.  The soundtrack by Floex is a wonderful complement to the flow of the game. Yes it is very short and I agree with the other reviewers that it is worth it.  A huge labor in background and detail of movement and puzzles.  I took my time to enjoy the play time.  Most will finish under 2 hours.  Kudos to the developer.
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: this game is relatively simple, but it is also rather challenging in some parts. its a cute little plot, but what really blows me away is the animation; everything in this game is made of paper, and i couldn't be more impressed. its games like these that really make me appreciate video games as an art form (which i know sounds weird but iykyk). totally recommend, especially for those who appreciate the time people put into making interactive works of art :)
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: Stunning game. Gameplay is fairly easy -- a couple puzzles might take a moment to suss out but mostly it's a feast for the eyes and ears. The care put into the game is evident, and I may have fallen absolutely in love with the little kitty (although I will fall in love with any cat). I may have actually cried at one point...I wish it were longer! Well, I wish it went on forever. That's the pain of these handmade pieces of art, they will rarely be very long, but gosh was it ever worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: This game was so beautiful to play through! I really appreciate the time and energy it took to make the sets and characters. There were parts of the game that made me laugh out loud from the effects/characters and I thoroughly enjoyed every minute of playing. I will say that there were some parts of the puzzle that were difficult to complete and took me a while to get because there are no written cues, but it could just be me! Overall, loved the aesthetic, soundtrack, and gameplay. The characters move really slow and that bothered me a bit at first, but then I realized that the game itself is not actually that long. I guess the speed of the characters moving helped compensate for what would have been an extremely short game had they not moved so slow.
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games than I have played in my life. Respect for the team, I'm impressed for the handwork and all dedication on it. While I was playing the game, listening to the perfect soundtrack, I could feel all the love that you put on this project. Congrats, I wish to know more about you soon guys.
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: There are a few gameplay issues with puzzles (mainly the process of solving them because there is a help button with a cute minigame in case you get stuck) but other than that amazing and very unique game with an interesting worldview. The absence of words even in menus means anyone can understand it no matter how old they are and where they are from. Hats off to the developers for the colossal paperwork and sticking with it for such a long development time.
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: I love the mood and ambiance of the world. Really incredible work. The puzzles are tough sometimes and will stump a person for a bit. That being said, some effort is required and they can be overcome. I love how unexpected the results of certain encounters are- totally unexpected results sometimes. I also love the plot.About 2.4 hours for me to beat- I usually like to take my time on these sorts of games and really try to understand the ramifications of my actions.I'd love to see more of this game style.
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: A cute point and click adventure with beautiful visuals it's got a great soundtrack by Tomáš Dvořák (Machinarium)At it's core; it's a basic point n' click adventure, nothing groundbreaking mechanic-wise.It's got a neat hint system, when you click on it's icon it prompts a short mini game.When completing the minigame it gives a visual clue to where you're supposed to go.Nothing too challenging, but alot of charm.it's very short game though, i completed it in just shy of 2 hours, for some people that might be an issue.The value is in the experience, not the length.I'd give this a solid 7/10
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: A very short (1-2h) but atmospheric experience with great music.The gameplay isn't all that fancy, if you have played Amanitas games you know the drill.A few cool concepts though that stand out, just wish they'd done more.Hopefully they can expand on what they've learned and make a longer game later on.
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: Great little game!  The artwork is made entirely from paper and is amazing.  Music is great!  It reminds you of the games by Amanita-Design.  If you enjoyed playing Botanicula, Creaks and Churchel,  you will enjoy this game. The price for the game is fair considering the amount of effort that went into designing the paper art.  There is a video out there that shows how the art was made. Well worth a peek!
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: Was enjoyable, entertaining and good quality, as well as very original.The puzzle/logic aspect combined with the story adds to the fun and charm of the game, with just a touch of humour.I would recommend this if you are looking for something that is both an adventure and puzzle.Only change I would have liked is that there were more levels or stages (if you can call them that).
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: Echoing sentiments of others. Beautiful game with wonderful music. The gameplay is where it falls short. Character movement and interactions are so slow it discourages experimentation, and the puzzles almost exclusively exist to just be in the way, there's nothing particularly clever or interesting about any of them. it's also a very short game. Recommended for the art and music with the caveat that you probably have to be a fan of games-as-art and the point and click genre to enjoy yourself.
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: It's a delightful little game with some good vibes going on, I wasn't sure of it during my first couple of minutes but warmed up to the whole thing right after. It is rather on the short side, which is represented in the pricing, but I would have been happy if there were more puzzles and time spent in each location so you could take in the sights and sounds more. Make sure to stop occasionally or just do another playthrough if you want to take in the world a bit more. It is very much in the vein of Amanita design point and click adventure games, so if you enjoy the vibes those games have, you will enjoy this one without a doubt. I especially love the creature designs and their sounds and the way they move! I think my favorite were the tiny round fishes or the flying fishes! All of them are fun and delightful designs.The story however I was expecting to go to more places and was a bit disappointed to see it end where it did. Despite that, the ending still gave me some good vibes and was nice, but I just wanted a bit more (I mainly just wanted the bird to not die in the end as I felt they were a bit undeserving of such fate!) Good music, good sounds and good visuals, if you want to be delighted for 1.5-2 hours, this is it right here!
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: Truly an artistic triumph that looked and played great on my TV using Steam Link + Steam Controller (using a mouse configuration). From the astounding paper craft world and engrossing sound design to the charming hint system, I wholeheartedly recommend this short but sweet experience to anyone that's a fan of quirky/surreal point and clicks inspired by Amanita Design games.
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful little game, but it is shorter than I was expecting. The soundtrack by Floex is beautiful - you can buy it on bandcamp or on vinyl with download.The puzzles are not too challenging, the pacing is a bit more like a walking story than a game. It's a well crafted story - I hope the story evolves and that the puzzles are harder next time around.
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: This beautiful little game is an art, nothing less. Instabuy, instarecommend, instadelight. A cozy, soft, pretty experience that even non-gamers would enjoy.The developer said, "I want to make an  perfect game". Well Tomasz, sorry, but you've failed at that and made an  perfect game instead. Thank you, it was worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: I played the game mostly for its unique artstyle, and it delivered! The visuals and the lighting are really striking. The adventure is good, although nothing groundbreaking as far as point-and-click games go. As someone who doesn't play a lot of them and usually doesn't have the patience required to finish them, I was happy with the hints system implemented.Really worth trying if you're in for a short game with a lot of charm.
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game creator work and great effect. The game is very addictive and difficult at times, but solving the puzzles gives a lot of satisfaction. The characters are charming (the kitty - I love him), the sounds and music are well-chosen (again the kitty steals the whole show). Great job. I recommend it to all those who like to activate their gray cells a bit and explore the strange and amazing world of Papetura.
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun and gorgeous game, it's a point and click game thats very simple and easy to play. it's about 45 minutes of playtime if you go back and know what to do but if you don't and just enjoy the game it's probably around 60 - 90 minutes. Visually amazing game thats created by hand using paper. PAPER!!!have a 4K playthrough on my channel here :
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: This is a gorgeous little game! It was clearly inspired by Amanita games like the Samorosts and Machinarium, and I think that's a great thing - those are some of my favorite games, and I love to see another in a similar vein. I can't imagine how much work it must have been to create the entire thing out of paper, and it makes sense that this is a short game given how time-consuming that must have been. To me, the tradeoff of shorter play length for absolutely stunning graphics is definitely worth it. Gameplay is pretty simple, but there is an elegant hint system that, I admit, I did use a couple of times.
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing, you can see the inspiration from Amanita Design games and so much more built on top. Great respect for the creator and for Floex for delivering yet another beautiful album. The game is short, but worth every penny, it's one of, if not THE most beautiful game ever. Thank you for bringing Papetura to life and I'll be waiting for whatever comes next.
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: I have always wondered why there weren't more developers emulating the Amanita Design style. This game does just this and does little to separate itself from it, which is fine since it's something I can always use more of. It is however disappointingly short and feels a little expensive from less than 2 hours of gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: Very cute game. The visuals and music are the best part of it! The puzzles are not very challenging, although a couple of them were not very clear to me. Maybe it was just me though. Story was nice also. It's a liiiiittle bit shorter than I expected, but that's not a big problem for me. Overall it was a very nice experience. Totally recommend it!
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: I was alittle weary purchasing this for some reason and I'm not sure why. Once you watch the trailer and how everything is made, once you jump in game you appreciate it that much more. I obviously love the fact that everything is hand made but the interaction between the character and the environment is super easy and the hints are a plus! (love the mini game addition.) With only an hour in I have ran in to some difficulties with the puzzles, but once you figure them out it clicks. For sure recommend for the price. link for reference.
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: Really was looking forward to play this one from the first moment I found it. As a big fan of Amanita design and Floex, this became another must have game. And I wasn't dissapointed at all in my expectations. The feeling is really close to Samorost, both with graphics and sound. And the fact that the creator made the whole thing in real from a paper and used the paper structures to work with the light, that's unbeliavable and I am glad that I could play the game and know the fact that everything was made by a real hand. I can't imagine the amount of work you had to put in the making. Hope to see soon your future projects, hopefully you will find other talented artists to help you with creating so you can make bigger and even more beautiful games in a shorter time!I really wish the game would last longer. For the price I couldn't ask more, it's just that I would really like to enjoy this world more, well, surprise us with your next game! Papetura 2 or a DLC maybe? :)
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: Papetura is an atmospheric point & click adventure game, handcrafted entirely out of paper. Little creatures Pape and Tura will face monsters that will try to burn down their beloved paper world.
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

name: Visage
detailed_description: WARNING: This video game may potentially trigger seizures for people with photosensitive epilepsy. Player discretion is advised. IMPORTANT NOTE: The game focuses on exploration and builds tension slowly to create a deeper and more meaningful experience. Its story is unveiled through surreal imaging and subtle environment details. Be mindful that it is a difficult game in unconventional ways. Visage is a first-person psychological horror game. Explore a mysterious ever-changing house in a slow-paced, atmospheric world that combines both uncannily comforting and horrifyingly realistic environments, and enjoy a genuinely terrifying experience. Environment The game is set inside a huge house in which terrible things have happened. You’ll wander through the gloomy corridors, explore every dead room, and get lost in endless mazes, your head filling with memories of the dead families that once lived in this very home. This twisted environment, void of any life other than yours, takes you to places you couldn't even bear imagining. Storyline This house is stained with a terrible past. Families were brutally murdered by their own family members, people went insane, many committed suicide, and other grisly events occurred. Each and every room has its story painted on an invisible canvas. As a player, you will relive parts of this dark past, and each of its fragments will leave you restless and terrified. You’ll soon wish you could join the dead's ranks in their abyss, but death won't help you leave this place. Will you run from it, or will you try to uncover the truth behind the shadows? Dark entities The families that died in the house will haunt you and leave you restless. They’ll follow your every move, watch you from every corner, play tricks with your mind, and try to attack you. Why do they haunt you? What have you done? This you have to find out on your own. Gameplay In Visage, you are defenseless; no weapons could save you from the dreadful entities stalking you from the next corner, the next door, or underneath your feet. You’ll be able to pick up key elements, interact with the environment, and search for things that may help you escape this nightmare or pull you deeper into it. Dying is part of the game. You need to avoid terror at all costs, as dark entities are attracted to it. Maintaining your mind as sane as possible will keep you from joining the ranks of the dead. Doing so will not be easy, and you'll have to figure out ways, like staying in the light, to avoid going insane.

_childDocuments_.review: I logged about 6 hours into the game and for early access 20$ might seem like much but it is 100% worth it. PT vibes but stands on its own ground and merit. Plus the game isnt even done yet which leaves me excited for more. Now to the actual Review.This is a horror game that feels like actual love and skill went into it. Sounds and music are never too much or too little. Jump scares are not particularly overuse so when you do get them they have actual impact. And the story does feel a tad lack luster however there is soemthing there and hopefully is touched on with the same amount of love that went into this small piece of the game.The only problems i had with the game were actual items and how you hold them and how they interact with the envirement.  Items being held holding onto walls or open doors and staying there until i go back to fix it.   Also every so often after a cinematic my items in hand would swap hands.  However I absolute love the swap hands mechanic.  Also at one point i picked up a lightbulb and i was stuck in place until i died.My other problem with the game is the camera. Once your eyes are adjusted to the dark and you use it it hurts a lot to look at. And if you accidentally flash a wall your against its an instant headache. I would suggest one of two ways to fix this. Either have it so the camera flash lingers for a couple seconds, and/or change the effect on it so that it is more appealing to those of us who played this game in the dark (which honestly if you didnt then you are only cheating yourself). My final problem with the game is maybe lighters should slow the drain of sainity and its hard to tell how many pills are in a bottle sometimes.
_childDocuments_.name: Visage

_childDocuments_.review: I hate this game!! But it's for same reason I love this game. This is as close to a perfect horror experience that you'll get. When it comes to the scares, they throw them at you randomly with little to no warning. I get extremely uncomfortable every time I click play. I haven't felt so much anxiety playing a horror game since the first time I played Resident Evil 4 over 15 years ago. I HIGHLY recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Visage

_childDocuments_.review: Visage is one of the scariest games that I have played in a long time that doesn't rely on cheap jumpscares or generic horror scare tactics. It scratches the "itch" I've been having ever since experiencing PT for the first time.  The atmosphere and visuals are expertly done, and it manages to tell a story using symbolism and imagery without being overbearing like a lot of other games. As of writing this review, there are 2 chapters out which totals to roughly 6~8 hours of game play, with the third chapter coming soon in the future. If you are looking for a polished scary horror game then look no further.
_childDocuments_.name: Visage

_childDocuments_.review: I knew this game was fu*ck*ed up from the beginning i saw it...I saw a trailer back in 2016 and i was so eager for this game to come out.I'm a big fan of horror movies and horror games, that's why i've decided to buy this.  For all you kids crying about this game and complaining that it's not scary, try this: 1) Make sure you're home alone2) Use Headphones (loud) 3) Wait until 2 A.M.  4) Drink coffee5) Play visage alone in the dark 2 a.m. in the morning with no one in the houseIt's a way different experience.  Stuff like this are meant to be enjoyed , late at night when you're home alone.  Same applies to horror movies.  Stop crying about the game and follow the steps above.   10 out of 10 .  This game and resident evil are my favorite horror games.  Well done developers.
_childDocuments_.name: Visage

_childDocuments_.review: Extrodinary game that keeps you on your toes, and has incredible atmosphere. The game visuals are very appealing, and the pacing is okay too. I do wish it was a bti more interactive, rather than just running away, but i cannot complain. It was a joy of a ride, and i cannot wait until the next chapter.
_childDocuments_.name: Visage

_childDocuments_.review: >My thoughts on Visage- Perfect, & it's only Early Access- Stunning graphics & atmosphere- Sound design was my favourite part, flawless- Well paced progression without relying on jumpscares- Start to finish, I was in a constant state of stress, panic, anxiety, or fear- Voice acting was well done and believable- Telling Lucy's story was well executed, build up was well timedI could go on and on about it. As a broadcaster who plays horror primarily, this was a much needed breath of fresh air 2 years in the making, Ty Sad square Studio for this haunting experience!I am honestly so excited to progress with the rest of the chapters as they become available, & I might get my Vive going to get the full experience. Anyone who hasn't played Visage yet, it's worth your $20 without a doubt
_childDocuments_.name: Visage

_childDocuments_.review: Visage is Scary. When you get the clues in a decent amount of time you will come across sections that hit you in the face with scary. When these sections happen they are great and the scares do what they are supposed to do. After a while though the fact that every single item needed to be found to progress in the story started to wear on my patience. I had a very good pace for the first chapter. Items were hard to find but only a little poking around and you were golden. The chapters after were much harder, it was like a slight curve for searching every nook and cranny for the first chapter and then the second and on chapters was like a mountain of hidden clues, horrendous amounts of backtracking and the death of a steady pace were prevalent in the game after the first chapter. I love looking around for items but for a casual horror fan be ready to search everywhere for every little item you can find. I want to reiterate when you get to the horror it is great sometimes even amazing, creepy figures in the dark, killer grandma ghost stalking you and trapping you in rooms, the little girl driving your sanity into the floor were all great. This part of the game I loved and is a shining game in light of the P.T Craze and Silent Hills cancellation. I just feel that in the early onset of the later chapters the steep cliff of searching and backtracking for items is fun for a little but wears out the fun after about an hour. This will get better if you start finding items in the chapters it becomes better in each chapter once the game focuses on horror and give you easy to find items to keep the momentum going. The One thing that will keep you wanting to play this game is the amazing sound design, stellar atmosphere and all around great horror moments and elements injected into this game. Just be ready to fight tooth and nail with the items to find them, find where they go, and how to utilize them. all in all a great game.8/10

It made me paranoid about things I shouldn't be and it is cleverIt's a bit short as I write this review but it's worth a shot. Jumpscares are a thing though... A lot of them. _childDocuments_.review: This is one house that will stick with you. Much like the halls in P.T., SadSquare's vision of a haunted house in Visage is creepy enough to be unnervingly memorable long after you've finished playing the game. While it clearly borrows inspiration from the cancelled Silent Hills project, Visage manages to stand on its own remarkably well. It utilizes a sanity system that will see lights turning off on you, doors closing suddenly, radios activating themselves, and more, as you scramble to stay out of the dark and take your pills. Though the game leans heavily on the atmospheric, the chapters into which it's divided tell stories that are as brutal as they are frightening. Each chapter creatively seems to diverge from themes and ideas used in the others, so that what will aid you in one could almost get you lost in another, if you're not careful. Surely, one of the highlights of the game is Rakan's chapter, during which you make a little detour to one of the most unsettling abandoned hospitals ever created for a video game.Unlike many psychological horror games of its kind, Visage is not afraid to really keep you guessing at its puzzles. The creators seem to well understand the usefulness of leaving the player scrambling around in the dark, literally and figuratively, having to put real thought into what has to be done to progress. The game even warns you of its own difficulty in the beginning, but rather than being too frustrating an experience, this provides a level of immersion and scary problem-solving rarely seen in horror games.The voice acting is perhaps one of the few things I found wanting with Visage. The sound design is phenomenal, and will likely make your hair stand on end at times. Unfortunately, it's obvious in more than a few key moments that amateur voice actors were used for the game. Though the effort poured into Visage is admirable, this is one aspect of it that may detract players from the overwhelming atmosphere. Aside from this, the punishing learning curve and occasionally imprecise controls are other areas for improvement, although they honestly do not get in the way of the experience.When I first purchased and planned to play Visage, I had hoped to get it working in VR. I soon found out this feature has apparently been removed, but after actually playing some of the game, I'm admittedly a bit thankful for this. Visage is a genuinely terrifying game, one that I, even as a big-time horror buff, have doubts about experiencing in VR. In that situation, no amount of pills and no time in the light will help one's sanity all that much. If this in itself is not a shining recommendation of the quality and originality of Visage as a horror game, I'm not sure what is.

_childDocuments_.review: A pretty solid horror experience. Even kind of a surprise in a genre that's so often left behind recently. I really appreciated this!Very good art direction and mood across the board. Some legit scary moments full of tension! And I don't mean only by effective, while sometimes fairly predictable sudden jump-scares - in fact the general atmosphere is often very, very tense and it literally makes you wish you could just open the front door and run away from that place. Some of the tricks get spoiled after while though... as they start to repeat themselves, but that's fair and to be expected in an experience lasting relatively long like this one. I wasn't always a fan of the creature design and some artistic choices in that department, but the real star of the show for me was the environment itself - and that is working and very moody 100% of the times. Add to all this a very good sound design with all sort of creepy moans and voices, organic-like disgusting sounds and...you get one of the most convincing horror games I played in some time!Most of the gameplay bits are simple but functional. It works.However I personally found the inventory and general item management to be very counter-intuitive and needlessly complex. You get used to it, just like anything, but I found that you just needed to remember too many buttons and multiple times I found myself having to stop, take a breath, read again the UI suggestion and...try again to do what I was expecting to do by instinct in less than a second.There's a few gameplay other elements that are promising but not quite reaching their full potential like the candles and light bulbs. Technically I was very surprised by the visuals! It's remarkable how the team managed to use Unreal so well. One of the few bad sides are the animations though: the player moves probably a bit too slow, I didn't mind it all that much myself... but i'm sure it could be sort of an issue for many as even the 'run' is kind of limited and very slow. In some instances where a more complex animation pattern started I found the items from in my hands stuck and bugged mid-air. I understand the choice of making the player completely invisible from a production point of view... but I think the choice broke the immersion in several occasions, especially with the more complex animations that'd normally have the player see their own hands or arms.---Overall i'm very satisfied, the game is more than worth its price and I genuinely look forward to any other future project by this team! Great job!

_childDocuments_.review: Visage is not quite there yet. It carries the burden of succeding to games like Observer and Soma, both of which handle narrative design, quest structure and overall fear factor with much more subtlety. Very mild spoilers ahead, but you might continue reading if you're planning to play Visage from start to finish.Visage's narrative design is a mixed bag. It really wants to be this deep dive inside the daily sufferings of troubled minds but can sometimes feel heavy handed -in a "bruh, schizophrenia" kind of way. However I ended up really invested in the different chapters, and the game is clearly empathetic towards its characters, which is a nice touch. "Rakan" is my favorite.The quest structure is shoddy. The fact that the game heavily relies on clues (both comitting suicide in the basement and watching tapes on the TV will point you to the next task) is a confession that the developpers haven't really thought out how to build proper puzzles. The "Aha" moments are more "sh!t, seriously ?" moments, and it can get tiring to shuffle through the house looking for one particular item to progress. Kudos to the portrait room in Dolores's chapter where I had to turn up the gamma just to see the room at the end of the corridor.The fear factor is by far what Visage does best, with a sanity meter that threw me back to Eternal Darkness on the Game Cube. This, and the light and dark system kept me on my toes all along. However, apart from the "Lucy" chapter, you'll quickly (hopefully) devise strategies to avoid death. The best part of the game was getting familiar with the house's layout to have fall-back plans.As it is, I see Visage as a foundation for a more polished and refined game, but overall it's still a jarring experience if you're hardcore into horror walking sims. Oh, and it's pack full with Silent Hill easter eggs.

_childDocuments_.review: Visage is an amazing horror game that will remind you a lot about P.T. It's incredibly scary and unpredictable, difficult but not unfair. This game is meant to be challenging but the game will provide you with helpful items once you think you're in a tight spot and unable to move forward. The game does have some bug issues.. the one that stood out the most to me is the manequinn-chase scene in Rakan's chapter. When you hide in one of the control rooms, there will be a corner around a plant which you simply cannot move again once you have entered that space, it is really annoying as it forces you to restart the chase part of the humanoids, and that part is the hardest one in Rakan's chapter. Otherwise everything else was fantastic This is my 3rd playthrough of Visage, first one with my boyfriend, second one on my own through Steamunlocked and a third time on Steam for a speedrun. The hallways are very narrow and will make you feel claustrophobic. The ghosts that are haunting Dwayne can spawn in the middle of nowhere and kill you on the spot, they are unpredictable but the game will warn you a couple of seconds before the ghost even appears. This is usually through flickering lights, loud music followed by a strange noise, each ghost has their own authentic sound depending on how they died. Visage is also very open for interpretation and as the player you are thrown directly into the game without any clue or context and what is going on. You play through 4 chapters, the 4th one only being unlocked once you have finished the other 3 chapters. The environment is semi-open and you will find helpful items spawning randomly around the house but you must be very careful about traversing through the house as you are never safe and a ghost will ALWAYS be stalking you and hunting you regardless of whether you have started a chapter or not. You are never safe in Visage. Like most other hardcore super-fans, I do also need to criticize it a little, tinsy bit for the very limited inventory system. You'll often find yourself dropping random things, picking it up, going back to the storage room, leaving, picking up and repeat. The storyline is very deep and all equally disturbing but in their own way, I found Dwayne's the most emotional and I really felt for his family at the end of the game.I love Visage, it's one of my favorite games and despite the bugs and limited inventory system I would recommend it to everyone who loves psychological horror. The atmosphere is just great too, you need to have a lot of patience with the game. The ghosts that haunt you are made to be even scarier if you percieve them to be scary. For example it's very easy to forget how many mirrors you can escape into in the Dolores chapter to stop her from chasing you because of how terrifying she looks and if it is your first time playing you might end up standing still, panicking and not knowing what to do. That was definitely what happened the first time I played Visage, but so long as you stay patient with yourself, allow yourself to feel the fear but do it anyway, use your items sparingly and take advantage of the environment around you, you will be fine Again, Visage is difficult but it is not unfair. Sometimes the game will be helping you out, other times it will punish you. Learn to identify the patterns of the ghosts too that will be very helpful.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most terrifying games I've ever played. Visage is clearly heavily inspired by PT, which remains my favorite horror experience to date. It captures a very similar feeling of dread as you explore this exceptionally detailed haunted house and try to uncover the horrifying events that took place there. The puzzles, insanity-mechanic and sporadic chase sequences end up making it more than a simple walking simulator.Chapters 1 and 2 were amazing and felt better thought out than chapter 3, which had some unmistakable Outlast vibes, and "chapter" 4, which consists of scouring the house looking for certain (sometimes very well hidden) items. While the chapters do feel a bit disjointed, each one is unique in their own right. It took me about 15 hours to go through all of them, but I did spend quite some time getting stuck, so I would consider 10-15 hours of playtime for a first playthrough unless you truly take your time.Except for some janky animations and cheap looking character models, the game looks excellent on a visual level. The sound design is fantastic as well and really brings the haunted house to life. My only real complaint would be with the clunkiness of the controls and inventory system. However, what Visage lacks in technical polish it more than makes up for in suspenseful atmosphere and scares.

_childDocuments_.review: Let's start with the positive things: I really like the atmosphere, graphics and mystery. And I can honestly say: yes, the game is indeed scary. As a fan of horror games and movies, I thought that nothing would scare me and that this warning addresses only people not used to horror. It did not cause sleepless night, but it indeed contains some scenes that scared me.In the negative side, the developers made some design decisions that are annoying. I see that the game is on "exploring the environment", but more hints on what to do would be nice. Most of the time you just walk around, interact with everything and hope that something would happen. The story is hard to follow (paranormal events, etc), so one is basically left alone. This alone would be acceptable, but together with the fact that there are unnecessary hardships it gets annoying sometimes. These hardships can be summarized as follows: IT IS WAY TOO DARK (yes, horror games must be dark, but dark should not mean a completely black screen). You can use lighters and candles to get some light, but 1. candles are basically useless (cannot be used while walking), 2. lighters are very rare and they also have a very limited usage time. Also, you can carry only 5 items at a time, so sometimes you even have to leave helpful items behind. One very often runs out of light while trying to figure out what to do (and running out of light basically means death within seconds). Also light switches sometimes have to be pressed TWICE. I assumed that if the light is off then pressing the button turns it on, and if this does not work, then the light is broken. At some point I found out that pressing the button twice may help. If you don't know this, you might walk around in the darkness even more than necessary. And as if this was not hard enough, sometimes the very few light bulbs in the house get broken or the electricity fails (in which case you have to find the electric room in the dark basement to restart it). Even with a walkthrough guide, it is hard to master this game because ... you. don't. see. anything. This is not challenging, this is annoying. To summarize: devs should have added more lighters, increased their usage time, or make you able to walk with candles. So simple and would have been a great improvement.I was thinking for a while if I should suggest this game. Finally I did because the developers added clear warnings on exactly the points I did not like.

Your blood pressure will be high the whole way through, and at times you'll be stricken with grief at certain instances as the story unfolds.  An emotional roller coaster the whole way through, I certainly recommend this game to any and all horror fans.

_childDocuments_.review: This review contains some gameplay mechanic spoilers so be careful of that.By the way, this game is extremely ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up and deals with subjects that some people simply cannot handle (Deaths of loved ones, dementia, other mental sicknesses etc) and uses them as catalysts to make the story into what it is. It isn't entirely reliant on the supernatural. There is some real ♥♥♥♥ in this game so if you can't handle that then the game is not for you.I have literally hundreds of hours in horror games across steam and ps4. No other horror game has gotten close to being as soul-crushingly oppressive and dread-inducing as this game. And the best part is it never, and I mean NEVER lets up. I have 4 hours in this game because I need a break after an hour or so. Just a few things the game does really differently that make it stand out.           -Pressing escape is not a pause button. To pause what is happening, you need to press escape and click "Pause Game". IT then counts down slowly from 3, and THEN it is paused. The game requires you to be able to keep your wits about you when you are being attacked. I died 4 times out of panic until I finally managed to get away by the skin of my teeth.           -  On the topic of being attacked, it is completely random when it happens. You will be walking along with nothing happening just long enough to let your guard down and then the ghost appears, which means you need to run for your life.           -  Random scares are peppered throughout the game, constantly surprising you with things like ghosts peaking their head around a corner at the end of a hall about 7 feet from you, or a random light switch turning off to drain your sanity, giving you the immediate panic of trying to restore it to lower your chances of being attacked.Play this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ game. Do yourself the favor. One of, if not the best, horror games I have EVER played and I WILL finish it and update the review.

_childDocuments_.review: Not a bad horror game but there's definitely scarier ones out there. I may be one of the outliers in my views on the game though as most people seem to think this is the top-tier horror game. Hellseed was better in my opinion . Not trying to sound macho or above-it-all in any way--I get scared in games like these at times, yes--but I guess someone like me just wasn't legit terrified in a game when the main monsters happen to be: a little girl.... an old lady...... and an old man with a crutch. Getting chased by the monsters was more annoying than scary for me, especially since the pills and lighters were in limited supply and I kept running out. Kind of funny too how you're literally holding a sledgehammer but stand there and let an old lady kick your ass (though she may be a ghost, but still, lol). Basically the protagonist does absolutely nothing but turns into a body bag whenever the monsters attack him (another example: walking straight up to a friendly guy with knives jabbed all over him and just standing there while he grabs you, removes each knife from his body and violently stabs them into you one by one).     I'll give it some credit though by saying that Lucy was probably the creepiest because of her torn-off jaw, but that's mostly when she's seen from a distance because when she kills you and gets up in your face the graphics aren't that great. Don't get me wrong, there were times I was definitely startled and caught off guard in the game, and I enjoyed it overall so I would still recommend it, but nothing was particularly memorable to me.

_childDocuments_.review: This is easily one of, if not the best horror game I've ever played. The atmosphere is perfect, the scares are genuinely freaky, and for the first time in years I felt afraid to keep playing a game. Speaking of scares, something I absolutely love this game for is the fact that it doesn't rely on cheap jumpscares to get a reaction from you like so many other modern horror games and movies like to do. The horror is genuine, and it makes you dread turning that light switch back on or opening the ominous-looking door just ahead. The game's mechanics are simple enough to understand as well, and while the story is somewhat vague, that's actually a good thing because it leaves a lot of room for interpretation. It reminds me of a good ARG in that there's a great story present but not every question is answered, not every loose end is tied up, and enough mystery is still present at the end that it keeps you thinking about the game long after you've beaten it. My only complaint is that Visage can be rather vague about what it wants you to accomplish. You'll often find yourself wandering around an area trying to figure out what key goes in which door or where exactly you're supposed to go next, but that can be forgiven when the rest of the game is as perfect as it is.Visage is an excellent game and an amazing horror experience. If you're a fan of the genre, make sure to check this one out.

_childDocuments_.review: Right off the bat, you can tell what sort of influences the developers had when Visage was made. A lot of people tend to think PT is the big inspiration here, but that's a bit of a stretch to me. Sure there's a few nods to it in map design and so forth. But I personally think Silent Hill 4 and Amnesia was the big source material here. The bulk of the game mostly consists of exploring the house and letting the enviroment tell the story. It's up to you, the player, to put two and two together to figure out what's going on in this unsettling house of yours. But tread lightly as something is in the house with you. Whatever it is, it sure as hell doesn't like you very much. This is where the sanity mechanic comes in. Witnessing strange events, standing in darkness for long periods of time, and just being in areas of frequent hauntings will drain your sanity. You will need to keep your nerves steady in order to proceed forward in the game. Getting too cracked will leave you vulnerable to danger and cause a game over. You can recover sanity by staying in well lit areas, moving away from hauntings, and taking your pills.  But keep in mind, paranormal events can and will happen anywhere you go.Ṉ̵̆̇̓o̷͎̿ẉ̴̖̈͜h̶̯̞͈͝e̵̮͋̔͆ŗ̵̠̰̍̒̒e̶̱͛̅ ̷̖̩̽́i̶̮̱̽̿͝ͅș̶͕͇̿͠͝ ̴͉͖̌͑̓s̶͉̈́̑a̵̼̫̜͂̕f̸̢͝e̸͈̦̝͒̏.̸͚̗̒.̵̢̯͂.̷̜̒̈́͗.̷̮̖̈́͊͝ͅ.̷̗̳͚̽̔.̴̧̤͖̍͒My only real gripes with the game is that the sound design could use tweaking.  It's unsettling and provides a creepy atmosphere, sure. But it can make the scares kinda predictable after a while. It also doesn't help that some scares are repeated a little too much. Too much repeatiton like with the clock scare can really just dull their effect. On top of this, it really can make scares confusing to know which are dangerous and which are not. And the music still plays regardless if you witness them or not. So if you walk into a room and a horror occurs in a certain spot that you're not looking. The music still plays even though you just missed out on the event entirely.  It's a bit of an atmosphere killer.  Also, some more signs of sanity status would be good. Like nervous breathing, twitchy movement, chattering teeth, irrational thoughts, etc. Anything to give a more clearer status of your mental health would add to the immersion and balence.  Some of the items could use some work. It really doesn't make sense to me that the player has to carry around several pill bottles at a time just to hold three pills. Why can't they just dump them into one pill bottle if they're the same medication? Also, candles could be better IMO. I never really saw much point in them as half the time a regular light source would do. They're not very bright and just jarring them even slighty puts them out. They're honestly more annoying to use than being useful. Also, the dynamic inventory system is the same in this regard. The controls could be better here. Accidentally throwing away items/storing them when trying to use them just gets annoying after a while. Also, there's no way to organize your items to make them easier to equip on your hotbar. This feature would be nice to have. But apart from some minor gripes. This is a pretty good concept we have here. A good little spooky romp perfect for Halloween.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR It's overall one of the better horror games but it has a good handful of flaws that you'll have to be patient with.When it works, it works, (even if it does use a lot of horror tropes and ideas "inspired by" PT) but there's still a lot of things that hinder the experience. There's a sanity meter in the game which is a cheap way to build tension. Not only that, but the sanity meter will occasionally bug out and the medicine you take or the light you stand in won't properly fix your sanity, eventually resulting in an insta-death. Speaking of glitches and bugs, there's a lot of them. There's the aforementioned sanity bugs, Items will frequently spawn in, floating in mid-air, there's a few sections where the player character can get completely stuck in place and others have reported other, more game-breaking glitches. I'd also recommend having a walkthrough on hand because sometimes, the way forward can be pretty convoluted (many instances of "Oh, how was I supposed to know that you could go there?"). The puzzles are extremely easy though, with the game often just telling you the answer so don't worry about getting stuck with any of them. Again, it's not bad and worth a try, it's just not "amazing" either.

_childDocuments_.review: Visage is a very atmospheric horror game with puzzles that doesn't take you by the hand at all. There's scratches on the wall? That's the best hint you're gonna get for a path. 3 Chapters and a "sidequest" for the ending is gonna get you a good 10 hours of spoopy playtime, and 2 hours for the Rakan chapter. Which brings me to my ranking (spoilers ahead now):I think Rakan's chapter was by far the weakest aspect of the game. I definitely recommend playing this one first, as it does ease you into the game somewhat. It's absolutely not worth going into it as the 2. or 3. chapter, as you will be disappointed severly.Followed by Chapter Lucy for being a very scary experience that plays the trope of the possessed child seeing a creature to (almost) perfection. Many terrifying scribbles further play with your fear of the imaginary friend.But my by far favourite chapter has to be Dolores' chapter. It's the longest (or I'm just braindead), has a very decent amount of fear to throw at you, and an excellent view into the psyche of a demented old lady (especially the ending and the talking kitchen bit)So my final ranking would be:Scariness: Lucy >>> Dolores >> RakanStorytelling: Dolores >> Lucy >> RakanAmbience: Dolores = Lucy >> RakanMind♥♥♥♥: Dolores >>> Lucy >> RakanThe game's definitely worth the money in my book, and I recommend everyone that is interested to go for it. Though, I will reiterate that I think Rakans chapter is pretty bland and should be played first.

_childDocuments_.review: Love this game!Took me 12 hours to complete the chapters, not including the bonuses at the end of the main chapters, and that's with the use of guides halfway through the game. Visage is definitely one of the scariest games on the market currently, especially in the psychological department. The atmosphere and slow build-up of a tension has been utilised masterfully. With heavy inspiration from PT, arguably the greatest horror game that never was, you know you're in for a ride with this one.This game can be quite rough to navigate without the use of a guide, as things aren't necessarily spelt out for you. Occasionally it can take a few strolls around the house to trigger the next sequence of events to progress the story further, and they aren't always obvious. Some of the puzzles can also be confusing, so if you're wanting to go into this game completely blind without the use of guides, good luck to you!Overall, very much worth the price if you're into psychological horror narratives.

_childDocuments_.review: Some feedback after playing your game in early access. Please note: I REALLY want this game to succeed. We need more in this genre.So, on one level, it was the scariest game I’ve ever played. I kept getting the “shivers” as I walked into dark and incredibly atmospheric rooms. I love horror and that never happens to me! A huge achievement. The way it plays with your fears and anxiety of the dark is just next level creepy! Graphics and sound design are fantastic!Where it falls over are the gameplay mechanics. You have a sanity meter that fills up if you stand in the dark too long. When that happens, lights start to switch off and there are more paranormal events. It worked at first, but then just become a major hindrance in the immersion of the game and quickly replaced all feelings of fear with frustration. This completely pulled me out of the game. Seemed like it was unnecessarily overworked with gameplay mechanics to increase the game length when just a simple and short “walking simulator” horror story would of been brilliant. _childDocuments_.review: Visage is a very good horror game. I really enjoyed it! It was one of the scariest games I've played in a while. The story isn't something you can figure out from the start, you need to search and find things that relate to each chapter and Dwayne. I'm gonna start with Lucy's chapter: It was a good chapter for the first one. The chapter had a really nice atmosphere and many jumpscares but in my opinion was the worst between the 3. Dolores' chapter: This was a very very good one. The atmosphere was just insane, Dolores can kill you anywhere. The only thing I didn't really like was the puzzles wich were pretty hard. The story in this chapter was the best out of all. Rakan's chapter: This one was my favorite. It started strong with jumpscares, then you go into the hospital wich was a very scary place and then at the end it became a pretty repetitive chapter but it was still the scariest in my opinion. And then the final chapter is about Dwayne. What I understood is that Dwayne was working in the water plant from the affliction tape. His job was to poison the water and that is how Lucy and Dolores died. And then when Rakan came into the house he was an agent and he was the one that spied Rakan and locked him in the cell. And then Lewis was another resident of the Visage house but we do not have a chapter about him. He found out what Dwayne is doing and Dwayne killed Lewis. And then when Dwayne moved into the house the factory was closed. He had the guilt of killing the four and he started drinking alcohol and drugging himself. Then, because of the guilt he killed himself and his family. When you play through the 3 chapters ( Lucy, Dolores and Rakan ), he was a ghost, that's why he didn't have a reflection in mirrors and we didn't see his hands. So the family reunion ending is about Dwayne joining his family in heaven even after what he's done. The purpose of the 3 chapters was for Dwayne to feel the pain of his victims ( Lucy, Dolores and Rakan ) and then he could go in heaven along with his family.

_childDocuments_.review: Ever since playing this game, my wife and I quote the opening warning card that shows when you start it up, "Visage is hard," which feels like a defensive excuse fired off for the obtuse puzzles and relentless death mechanic you're about to embark through.That obtuseness is why I don't love this game, but there's too much it gets right to not recommend it; the atmosphere, the sound design, the writing, all knocked out of the park. But the journey to get through it is a trudge; not quite the lightbulb in a tin can nonsense you'd get from SH, but enough like that without any direction to become understandably frustrated. Pair that with haunts that can kill you and the lack of a quicksave option and you get moments that become unimmersive and just plain maddening.It's hard to work in a death/punishment mechanic in a horror game that doesn't result in these unimmersive moments (i.e. I've already been through this part, I'm not scared, I'm just trying to progress!), but it would've been appreciated to have difficulty options to lessen the death moments so I could enjoy all the work put into the game environments without the added pressure of punishment, like a New Game+ mode even.Oh well, again, not enough of a problem to not recommend because it's heart is most definitely in the right place, but you should be aware that "Visage is Hard," enough for them to disclaim it and enough for it to frustrate a decent chunk of the playerbase. If you are in that playbase, there is no shame in using a walkthrough, of which there are some great ones in the Community Tab that don't include spoilers.

I spent 30 minutes trying to figure out how to not select two items at the same time and light a candle and then put a flaming candle in my pocket. Some of the models need to get polished, but that is forgivable.The game is virutally unplayable due to the bugs and ambiguity with UI interactions. The key selection was the worse part! _childDocuments_.review: Review as of Oct 27, 2018.One of the best horror games i've played. The only other horror game I can say I truly enjoyed is Amnesia The Dark Descent. However, Visage is early access at the moment so you'll run into some doors and other parts that will remind you that the content is not available yet. But for the review of it's current status: Visage is one of the best horror games of this year. There aren't many any jump-scares at all compared to a lot of other horror games. As of now, the only jump-scares are when the it/she catches you, but because of the trial-and-error nature of the game, dying is normal, and you'll get used it to it to advance in the story. But that's what makes the game good, it's not built on the premise of jump-scares like a lot of the current horror games are. It's built on a creepy, slow-built, psychological horror that leaves you saying "oh ♥♥♥♥."The story is actually pretty good, maybe typical (movie like story) but good nonetheless. Visage is dark and eerie, slow-built and random. At the end, it will definitely leave you wanting more.I still recommend playing even in it current state, but because it is early access, you will end up wanting more at the end to uncover the story. Either wait until the story is completely finished, or play now and possibly go back through to uncover some once-locked content.

_childDocuments_.review: As Jon Padgett so eloquently described in the opening to 'The secret of ventriloquism', horror runs along several vectors, it can be visceral and violent, the cosmic horror of the unknown, and the internal, cloying horror that lurks in the jungle of one's own mind. It is this third brand of horror that Visage does so well. It tracks this internal horror splendidly, and reminds us that the terror of being consumed by guilt, depression and nihilism lies not just in the truths it reveals, but in the sense of reality slowly slipping beneath a pearled darkness, as the sunlight appears through the ashen surface of the water to a drowning man.The game takes place in a purgatorial house, with superb attention to detail in both image and sound, as confusion and discomfort slowly rise to disgust, horror and despair. The atmosphere of this game is excellent,  and the opening scene sets the tone of a quite unsettling and adult exploration of regret. The pacing is a bit slow at the start, and it takes a bit of time to get the hang of what the game wants you to do, but it builds effectively and most of the game is neither too fast nor too slow. The puzzles are entertaining without being taxing, and there's not a lot of pixel-hunting. It is a story-driven game with little action or stealth.It reminded me somewhat of Danielewski's amazing postmodern horror novel 'The house of leaves'. As a fan of both very bad and very good horror, I recommend this as the latter. If you care to spend an evening wallowing in a self-loathing Hell as grief and madness suffocate what is left of the world, then, this may be for you. Or, if you just like creepy atmosphere.

_childDocuments_.review: What a terrific experience. As a horror game, it is up there as one of the scariest I've played. The most important part in my opinion is audio and the sound effects as well as occasional music in this game are of very high quality. The superb use of lighting and shadowing are top notch as well. Coupled with the high quality textures and ultra realistic shader usage, this is the "P.T." that we've always wanted. I highly recommend this game to anyone willing to ruin their sanity.As a side note, I love how some of the achievements are ordinary stuff like 'collect all the things' or 'finish this chapter' but there are others that happen to be ridiculous, silly or even referencing a film of some kind. I really enjoyed the special little things such as that.My only complaint has nothing to do with the quality of the game. I am not a fan of the psychological stuff. I would personally prefer just good ole fashioned paranormal activity for the sake of things out there wanting to kill me. Having everything be related to a feeling of guilt or greed or whatever doesn't suit my fancy. With that said, it doesn't matter one lick...the game is absolutely phenomenal and I have nothing else negative to say about it.Extra note: the devs warn you as you start a new game, this is HARD even on the easiest setting. There is literally no hand holding whatsoever. You have to go around exploring and figuring out what to do or where to go next on your own. I don't like repetition so after getting lost for a bit or repeatedly killed, I eventually used a 'no spoilers guide' here on Steam and loved every second of that. As indicated in the title, the guide helps you figure things out with hints and doesn't spoil a thing. If you start to lose patience or get frustrated, just look up this guide and don't feel guilty about using it.

_childDocuments_.review: Most of the way through this and it is a visually rich and very anxiety-inducing game. With a darkness-based 'sanity' game mechanic which took complete 'inspiration' from (read: lifted from entirely, call the lawyers) Amnesia: Dark Descent and an inventory management scheme that gets in the way at every turn, this game most assuredly brings the pressure in both good and bad ways.A lot of the tension comes from a total sense of helplessness against an ever-present, randomly lethal force as you struggle to find the square block to fit in the square hole. The puzzles you're meant to solve feel arbitrary and and the solutions are poorly-hinted at.This amounts to running around the house depleting resources, turning lights on, looking for a clue all the while the big bad evil force pranks you by closing doors, turning lights off on you, turning on/off appliances, and doing other things often well out of your sight - each with an accompanying musical sting. Most of the time this sting is the only way I know something has happened. Whether or not you see it - it still damages you.Occasionally and arbitrarily, this force will just outright murk you though, jumpscare style - regardless of the sanity mechanic.I still recommend it though, because despite all of this it makes me want to complete it. I can't really explain that.

_childDocuments_.review: is a game a long time coming, it’s original announcement rising quickly off of the excitement surrounding ’s release, popularity, and Kojima’s subsequent falling out with Konami and the shuttering of the  title.  is a clear attempt at bringing that title’s meticulously crafted sights and scares to a wider market, while additionally building upon and expanding outside of the playable teaser’s short scope. Unfortunately, while  delivers in spooks and sights, it falls short in a department far more critical: gameplay design. At the time of release, I have experienced several issues pertaining to gameplay. The game often fails to provide sufficient audio and visual clues to indicate to the player where to progress or what to do, which can be fatal during chase sequences. Enemies that chase the player regularly spawn in areas you can’t effectively escape from, and occasionally insta-kill you through walls and other geometry. The “advanced” control option for doors that allow you to swing them open gradually with the mouse is far too underpowered, and will sometimes “slip” off the door as you attempt to drag it open. While the door controls can be changed in the options to a “simple” mode that will fully open the door by clicking on it, this removes a significant amount of interactivity that would otherwise contribute to the game’s atmosphere. The controls for manipulating examinable objects is additionally clumsy. Objects held in the character’s hands are actually physically modeled, meaning they can and do unintentionally get stuck on geometry and be pulled away from you. And I’m sure there are other minor issues that escape me at the time of writing. A shame, as this game genuinely does well in building atmosphere and setting scares. Sure, there are several occasions of simple jumpscares, but few ever feel cheap and are often bookended by crafted moments of drawn out dread and tension. Many of these scares owe their effectiveness to the excellent environmental, character, set piece, and audio design. The developers have come up with some effective and clever ways of putting players into situations they don’t want to be in. I just wish all of those were due to scary moments, rather than the rough gameplay. Ultimately, I would suggest those interested to wait a bit for more updates to be released before dropping full price on the title. The developers seem to be addressing major bugs and technical issues. With luck, they’ll tweak gameplay issues along with it. For those who can’t wait to see what the game has in store, perhaps consider watching a playthrough on YouTube. You’ll get many of the spooks without all of the frustration.

_childDocuments_.review: Take in mind I play a lot of horror games. I was told to play this and recommended it a lot, so I did and was highly disappointed and frustrated the whole time.First, game mechanics are horrible to access inventory and manage inventory. You cannot access inventory and switch items/drop items quickly. Let alone the items you need to survive rarely spawn. I rarely found candles, pills, or lighters. But again, you can be insta-killed no matter your sanity level, so there is little to no logic behind it. Times when you need to be watchful of something wandering that can kill you, you have zero visibility. So good luck attempting to figure out if they are pathing or if you can be sneaky. I got so frustrated with the random insta-kills and restarting that I looked up a walkthrough because I just wanted to finish and be done with this horrible game.Otherwise, I think they worked a lot on the story-lines, background, and graphics which seem great. The authors added some mechanics, like sanity, candles and replacing lightbulbs, but you can just safely ignore them. It will not affect the game. You can die from monsters encounters (which is excellent), but any monsters are slower than you. The solution to all of these hauntings is just to run away. Progress is very linear with the most boring psychological horror cliche you can imagine. But there are several funny easter eggs experiences that put a smile on my face. The music is astonishing, very lovely and atmospheric. But cutscenes? You generally just wait one minute in the dark for something to happen or for a jump scare.Man, oh, man. I think I hate this game. If you like psychological horror (what is wrong with you?), you will love this game. For the rest of us - well, it really is a mixed bag.

_childDocuments_.review: Early Access review for chapter 1 of Visage:This game is a psychological and paranormal survival game with currently only 2 hours of gameplay. Here's what I thought about it so far.It's very rare for a P.T. clone to actually pull off a decent result, but so far Visage looks far from expendable. I have very mixed feelings about this game. Half the time I enjoyed it. The other half I felt annoyed and frustrated. I can't say much about the story as it is unfinished, but I can talk about everything else. The gameplay mostly surrounds the concept of an interdimensional house with sequential events leading to psychological environments and atmospheres. You progress to new events and occurances through investigation, puzzle solving, trying to unravel what the game is telling you to do, and this is one of my biggest complaints about the game so far.The puzzles and detective-like nature of this game are more frustrating and boring than they are scary or enjoyable. A major reason for this is the sanity system. Your sanity decreases so fast and so easily that you will find yourself a lot more focussed on keeping yourself from dying than solving puzzles. There were 5 instances in my experience where I had to look up what I was supposed to do because I got so annoyed and so bored of burning through my resources and dying because of sanity over and over again due to the ridiculousness that is the sanity system, which really ruined the immersion for me. I have nothing against puzzles in horror games no matter how hard they are as long as they're done correctly. It's when you put such an irritating and crucial obstacle in between me and the puzzle that I start to a have a problem.One thing I do like is how this game handles its scare factor. The atmosphere throughout this game both visually and auditory are captivating and kept me on the edge of my seat, dead silent, which I respect. This could have been THE scariest game I've played since Amnesia, but unfortunately the frustration over the complex puzzles and sanity system just ruined it for me. The enemies aren't too bad either. The only problem I have with them is that they're a bit too random. There isn't a single scripted encounter at all, which creates the possibility of not encountering them whatsoever. I don't expect only scripted encounters, but creating a nice balance between the two I think will make this game a lot more engaging and intense in certain areas.I could mention a few other criticisms I have, including the inventory system, lack of lighting, overuse of paranormal events and the tediousness of the first chapter. But many people have already mentioned these things and I just wanted to talk about what I liked and disliked most about Visage since my opinions on this game are very mixed.Since this IS an early access build, I think this game has potential to be a great atmospheric horror/puzzle game, the successor to P.T. everyone's been waiting for. I hope the developers will take what I and a lot of other people said into consideration to bring us an interesting second chapter. At the very least, make the game a lot less frustrating during the puzzle sequences, which essentially means the sanity system needs to be reworked IMO.At the moment this is a very "buy at your own risk" type of game. $25 for what is currently 2 hours (at most) of gameplay isn't very promising. I believe it has potential, though. I like the direction it is going and I respect the effort the devs are currently putting into it and how much they're paying attention to user feedback.Pros:Great atmosphere (both visual and sound wise)Concept handled wellGood use of subtlety and immersionUltimately, has the potential to be greatCons:Sanity System (everything to do with it)Puzzles too complex (which wouldn't be as big of a problem if it weren't for the first con)Mechanics are sloppy and all over the placeEnemies are way too infrequent and easy to avoid (can get underwhelming after a while)Not much content for chapter 1.For now I give it a 5.5/10. Though I wouldn't advise refraining from buying it due to my rating. A lot of people seem to really enjoy the game in its current state even with the majority of the game unreleased.
