_childDocuments_.review: As someone desensitized to horror media these days, I can say for a fact that the feeling of a ghost or spooky entity standing behind me and breathing down my back is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ horrifying, and that's exactly why this game is so scary.Right now this game is a bit bare-bones, with "4-6 hours of content" (though from what I've seen, it's more of 2 hours average-- must have used their 12 year old child to test length, or embellished the time), but the content that is there is downright ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ evil with how spooky it is. The comparison has been made 100 times, but if you've played P.T. you have a general idea of what's going on here:You start as man, presumably the antagonist and protagonist of the story locked in a house with a very dark past that you may or may not have had a hand in. I'm not quite sure of the player character's motive, whether he just has the world's biggest balls, or the house literally just wont let him out, but as with any video game  you're gonna keep going further in. As you proceed further, in that Silent Hill/ PT fashion things slowly ramp up, doors start slamming and opening themselves, light flickers, shatter, and even turn off moments after you just turned it on so you can proceed further into a room. Footsteps, knocks, items falling; it has it all and with a good pair of headphones you'll hate and love every moment of it.Gameplay-wise, what sets Visage apart from any other walking simulator horror game is not combat, but a sanity system reminiscent of Amnesia, and an inventory system.... also reminiscent of Amnesia. The inventory system is your usual puzzle item/ key Resident Evil style system, but you can store pretty much anything you can pick up. A variable amount of minutes into the game you're given a small zippo lighter that provides your means of lighting when the lights don't work/ don't shine far enough to light the whole room for you. This zippo will eventually run out of gas and you'll have to find a new one, or be stuck in the dark searching frantically for a new one or a light switch as your sanity goes down. Once your sanity hits the floor you begin to see more paranormal events which as far as I've noticed only consists of doors moving/closing/slamming, the sounds, and an enemy to locate you and stalk you. I wont spoil when, where, what, or how, but at some point in Chapter 1 a ghost or two will begin stalking you everytime your sanity reaches low levels, making it important to manage how much light you are around. If it gets too low I think it's an instant death/ the ghost just teleports to you and kills you. The ghost itself is not that disturbing when you're caught to be honest, so you might not really be jump scared when it does catch you, but the  is where it truely shines. That ♥♥♥♥♥♥ is just so creepy to see wandering around. This isn't the only entity in the house in Chapter 1 though, so keep an eye out...Graphically, the game is top notch. It's not quite the level of P.T. but it's slightly better than Resident Evil 7; it's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ gorgeous to look at, and downright photorealistic at times. Not to mention it runs beautifully. The recommended settings to run on Max at 1080p is an RX 480 with a Ryzen 5 CPU, and I have exactly both of those, and it does not disappoint. For all of Unreal Engine 4's opimiztion woes, these guys know how to make it work, while delivering a very eye-poppingly depressing experience.As EA notices say, if you're excited to play the game in the state it is/ with the content it currently has, absolutely ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ buy it. I've been waiting for a real full length game in this style for awhile, and since it's currently October I have been in urgent need of something to get me spooked.As for the EA model the game seems to have, they said they will add content on a "as it's done" basis, hopefully meaning we wont have to wait all 4 months to get more content, so that's a very good deal as well.

_childDocuments_.review: Visage is one of the scariest horror games ever on flat screen. To find similar sensations my mind has to go back to Alien: Isolation! I specified flat screen because, talking just of fear, it cannot compete with VR horror games like RE7 or Paranormal Activity. VR adds an extra dimension to horror! I hope developers are working on the VR version! The best feature of Visage is the lore, so tense and deep, like in the ghost story of the Lucy's chapter. You feel really immersed in the scary house thanks to AAA graphics, audio and state-of-the-art illumination. I loved the main mechanic of avoiding the dark by turning on lights and candles.  The sequences in the house are clearly inispired by P.T., but Visage is more than that, you explore several locations and play in the shoes of different characters. Luckily it's not an action horror, forget RE or Dead Space. And it's not based just on jump scares. It's a psychological horror, fear comes from insane sutations and extremely thrilling atmosphere. However Visage comes with some defects. The inventory management is a pain in the ass, I cannot understand why developers have not implemented smarter solutions. Puzzles are boring; you have to find too many items and they are too much hidden. You have to go up and down the house countless times; sometimes you don't know what to do and end up consulting youtube. Puzzles interrupt the lore, the immersion, they distract you from the story. The latter on paper is interesting and original, but storytelling is disappointing. Story is splitted in four chapters apparently disconnected. The excessive focus on puzzles leaves the story in the periphery, on the background. In the end you don't understand what you played! You can guess something, get a vague idea, but not the whole story! Again you have to google the web for finding explanations! And explanations are not satisfying! In conclusion I suggest the game to horror fans because of the incredible graphics, audio, illumination, lore, making it one of the scariest flat games ever. However it is far from perfect because of silly inventory management, too hard and boring puzzles destroying the lore, interesting story marred by disappointing storytelling.

_childDocuments_.review: Before starting the game you should know that it is advisable to play the game in the dark with the sound at a good audible volume. *wink wink*Visage is divided into 4 chapters, which together can take more than 20 hours.These are a nice number of dark evenings that you can fill with the jump scares that the game has to offer.Often you will do it with little or no clue's until you find a clue while searching or spontaneously, so that you can work in a more focused way and know where to go or what to do.The house where Visage is set is also very large and contains many rooms, it is therefore important to keep a map in your head so that you do not keep going in the wrong direction.Also always look out for candles, you often find them in numbers but often they are also scarce and it takes a while to find, also be careful that when you use a candle that this candle is lit in a useful location.While you shouldn't waste enlightenment, longer periods spent in the dark can trigger fear and the paranormal.To prevent this you need to find pills, these pills you can take when the tension gets too strong so that you always keep both feet on the ground when you wander through dark corridors or rooms.What is also very useful are the double controls, by this I mean that you can use both your left and right hand to hold two items, both items can then walk around with a lighter and a jar of pills in both hands.Before starting the game myself I read quite a bit about 'Visage' and also heard about it from a friend who was very actively playing on _childDocuments_.review: I’m forever chasing the high that few games other than the Outlast series and Resident Evil 7 have given me when it comes to horror. I’m always optimistic and often disappointed by what’s out there, though every once in a while I come across something that’s at least not a complete waste of time. A title that offers some enjoyment and even an occasionally legitimate horror atmosphere that keeps me pushing through to see what’s next. Visage falls into this category, and although it doesn’t quite hit all of the marks that I was hoping for based on its price and Steam reviews, I will say that it satisfied me enough that I wasn’t dozing off an hour in.The house that you spend most of your time in during Visage is not a pleasant one. Even when everything is relatively low-key, lights will flicker and go off, radios will pop on, and doors will slam around you. When the house has started to take its toll on your sanity, you’ll experience much, much worse. Four chapters detail the stories of the unfortunate souls who have lived (and died) here in the past. Each of them has its own theme that stands out from the others with puzzles and game mechanics that are different enough from the others that they keep the experience from becoming stale. As a matter of fact, I would even say that most of them are grade-A horror if you were basing it solely on the narrative and terror-inducing atmosphere. On a less fortunate note, the quality among the chapters varies wildly.By chance, I ended up doing Rakan’s chapter before the others, though most seem to agree that it should be done last. The story was fairly bland as it involved a rugby player who was out on an injury that suffered from extreme scopophobia, a fear of being stared at. Although it’s nice to see that this character was worked into the game due to them being a backer who’s similar to the character involved, this chapter truly feels like it was forced in without the same level of passion and skill as the others. By the time I’d reached the end of his story, I was concerned about whether or not Visage was for me.I decided to press on and see if the rest of the game was as dull and I was pleased to discover that it wasn’t. That’s not to say it was a masterpiece, there were plenty of flaws that I’ll dive into in the next section, but I played Lucy’s chapter next and found it to be worth the wait. Lucy is a young girl who you quickly learn had an ‘imaginary friend’ that she had bonded with. This friend was important to her, but as time went on, it began to become increasingly dominant leading to plenty of terrible events to follow. As opposed to Rakan’s chapter, Lucy’s was marred only by the rough-around-the-edges gameplay that seemed to not really know which sub-genre it belonged to, the primary flaw of this title overall.Visage builds tension and atmosphere better than most horror titles that I have played and I can say that with full confidence that most fans of the genre would agree with me. The house is big and creepy, the locations that you visit outside of it keep you on your toes, and the stories of those who came before are well-written and keep you wanting more. What frequently gets in the way is the gameplay though. Well, that and the Rakan chapter…You’re informed that Visage is a difficult game from early on and this is accurate. You’re likely to die plenty of times from start to finish, though being chased by the entity of the chapter isn’t particularly exciting. There’s no way to hide, you simply run away until they disappear or they catch and murder you in an animation that loses its luster and takes up way too much of your time after you’ve seen it the first time. The scripted encounter sequences tend to do their job admirably, but the random appearances get old quickly. Puzzles are the name of the game here and I can’t even count how many times I was interrupted and chased around as I was trying to figure out what I was supposed to be doing next. You’ll likely find yourself forgetting about the excellent atmosphere often as your awe and suspense are replaced by frustration. At least the auto-saves are placed in convenient locations, for the most part.An equally irritating flaw comes in the form of the inventory system. While I’m certainly not expecting to have my mind blown by a walking simulator-ish horror adventure, this one really took the cake for being a pain. Just about any time you’re going to use an item, you need to navigate through an inventory window while the world around you continues. I consider myself lucky that this didn’t kill me far more often than it did, though I’m under the assumption that others won’t have such luck and will become increasingly frustrated with it. I’m unsure whether it was the intent to have the feeling of digging through your pack while danger is closing in on you, but it was more of an irritation than an atmosphere builder.Visage is one of the better horror titles that I’ve gotten my hands on lately, though it’s far from perfect due to several notable flaws. An excellent setting with a flawed chapter is forgivable enough, but a horror game that loses its thrill by consistently killing the player is inferior to one that forces them through near-death experiences due to the simple fact that the segment is no longer new or frightening, but exactly what you’ve already seen. Others manage to strike a strong balance here by offering additional action and stealth mechanics that allow for these close calls, though Visage does nothing of the sort, forcing the player through events that require them to escape but without giving them any of the more fun and creative methods of doing so.At the end of the day, Visage is a solid enough horror title that shows its PT inspiration, but it falls short of becoming an instant classic. I’d recommend it to horror fans who are looking for a new challenge and interesting setting to explore, though I can’t help but think that it would’ve been a significant improvement if it had leaned more into its excellent atmosphere and story more and its running sequences less.

_childDocuments_.review: Aight, just played through the game...and its extremely hard to say if i recommend it or not.It really depends on the player.The good things first.The horror is as good as people praise it to be, its very well done. Jumpscares are there but theyre not too excessive and the atmosphere is astoundingly creepy. Good visuals support the atmosphere and generally the feel of the game quite a bit. The story isnt bad either, its very interesting and involves mental illness, addiction etc. and is pleasant to puzzle together and experienceNow to the bad Part:If you love finding little secrets, that are partly extremely well hidden with little to no proper indication, this game will be a treasure trove for you.If not, everything will just start falling apartThe outstanding horror is overshadowed by the sheer "complexity" of the game, to call it nicely.Progress has to be made by obtaining different items, interacting with different objects or generally through triggering events which can vary from picking up a clearly visible key, to something as stupid as looking at a seemingly decorative stain at a ceiling and clicking on it. This wouldnt nearly be so annoying if the "house" wasnt an entire palace.There are so many different rooms filled with so many decorative and inspectable items, that  searching for important stuff becomes extremely frustrating and time consuming.I needed to look up guides at least 5 times throughout this entire playthrough and would probably have needed multiple more, if i wasnt just lucky at times and found what i needed by randomly clicking things.And lastly the inventory system.What the hell were they thinking?You get used to it but its very unintuitive and annoying to deal with at first.Which doesnt help is the fact that the character doesnt have arms or a body, which firstly takes a massive amount of the immersion out of the game, especially in cutscenes and secondly, items in your "hands" are just "free floating". Something like a lighter can just get stuck on an object that you passed and fly into your face again after some distance, which jumpscared me multiple times.Additionally to that, in this game you get chased quite a lot.These chases are random at some points of the game, which will lead to you dying because the chase started a centimeter next to you and you just couldnt get away in time.Also, i dont think the "stress system" was a good implementation.Its more of pain to deal with because in most circumstances, when you need to explore in the dark, your stress meter goes up and you have to return to a light source to regain sanity (not every *visual* light source counts btw) . This added nothing to the gameplay besides being another frustrating nuisance.Which lastly brings me to the "random paranormal events" around the house.I really liked those at first, they kept me on my toes and scared me from time to time. The problem being, after a while it was just the same thing over and over and over again, bringing your sanity down and slowing your progression because you had to sit in the light for half a minute until your sanity is recovered again.TLDRIn conclusion id say that the horror and the atmosphere, as well as the story and graphics are amazing and very captivating. The "game" part of it is just sadly all around terrible, with a clunky and unrefined inventory and stress system, very directionless tasks with little to no indication at some points, in a gigantic house, with repetetive  random events or unforgiving chases, which slow you down or even kill you because of bad implementation etc etc etc which overall just makes the "game" more of a chore than an engaging experience, especially for the pricetag. If you dont believe me that this game is frustrating, look at the games achievement statistic with only 10-15% of the players having completed the endgame.IMO this would make a better movie than an actual game but maybe im just stupid.

_childDocuments_.review: After 3 years of waiting, I finally was able to play Visage. I have to say, this is one of the most terrifying experiences I have had with a survival horror game, in years. I couldn't even imagine playing this in VR. Which I do hope the devs put in later. This game feels like a love letter to "P.T." and it is wonderful! After the disappointing news of the cancelation of Silent Hills, I always wondered what the game would have been like. I think Visage is very close to what P.T. (Silent Hills) would have been.Right when you start playing, the tension and atmosphere start to build. Which turns to dread and fear later on in the game. This, I think, is mainly thanks to the photo realistic graphics and it makes you feel like you are investigating a real home. (if that makes any sense)Unlike most horror games out there today, which rely heavily on jump scares, this game has far and few of them. The only scares you will encounter, is the feeling of what could be around the corner. I felt like I held my breath most of the time just to prepare myself of a scare, when in turn, there is nothing and builds the tension even more.Even the music and sounds in the game put you on edge the entire time you are playing. During the game you encounter events that trigger certain sounds, which really don't help when you are already about to ♥♥♥♥ your pants. (in a good way? LOL)So, the combination of the graphics, sounds and atmosphere make this a true horror experience. The only problem I have with the game is the inventory system and confusion with certain items (which have been fixed). Also, I had issues with items that I had in my hand clipping into doors and walls.But with those things aside, if you love survival horror or psychological horror, pick this game up. As of right now you can get a good 2 hours into the game in early access. I honestly can't wait until full release of this game.9/10!

_childDocuments_.review: Probably one of the most scary games I've played and a fantastic homage to P.T. The atmosphere was masterfully created and well maintained throughout the game. Exploring the house and being caught in darkness/paranormal events was deeply unsettling and often left me sprinting for known sources of light. Using the fear of what lies in darkness as a tool was extremely well done, in particular with Lucy's chapter. No spoilers, but the camera mechanic was terrifying as it was unique and I held my breath for *probably* the entire chapter. Whoever worked on the sound design deserves all the praise in the world- the subtle sounds like glass crunching, light switches being turned off, the chandelier swinging, light bulbs breaking, and footsteps elsewhere in the house were a really nice touch, while moments of silence that were randomly shattered by the chiming of that damned clock and hall radio instantly made me tense up. Some minor criticisms were the lack of direction in some parts, the darkness of the game (I was torn between turning the gamma up and losing some of the atmosphere, or wandering aimlessly and hugging walls in some parts), and some minor controller issues that felt counterintuitive at times. All of these things weren't too glaring of an issue- as the game does warn you right from the beginning about the difficulty of the game- but I had moments where I literally had no idea where to go/what to interact with to progress which was slightly annoying. Overall I highly recommend it, especially if you were a fan of P.T, and I REALLY hope SadSquare Studio comes out with another game like Visage.

_childDocuments_.review: It has potential, but it's not there yet.This game is absolutely fantastic at creating atmosphere. The lighting is sublime and the audio work is spot on, so it's really good at creating a sense of dread. However, the control scheme seems purposely designed to be obtuse. I know the idea of having to move the mouse to open doors was popularised by other horror games, but it's just garbage. It's not adding anything to the gameplay and it's made even worse in this game with its terrible implementation. Sometimes you have to move the mouse horizontally to open a door, whereas other times its vertical and it just makes you motion sick because your head ends up moving all the time when you don't guess at the correct direction. Then the core mechanic seems to be built around depriving the player of light. There's electricity in the house, but for whatever reason 90% of the light bulbs are burnt out so you have to find replacement bulbs which are somewhat rare, or find candles and a lighter with which to light them. Both the lighter and the candle eventually burn out which wouldn't be bad if I could keep more on me, but going back to the purposefully obtuse design, you can only carry an object in each hand and 5 that can be dynamically swapped out from your inventory. I quickly found myself in a situation where I knew there were lighters that I left behind in the basement somewhere, but I couldn't find them because my lighter ran out and the candles burn out if you move with them. That's when I decided to call it quits. After nearly 2 hours of gameplay, pretty much nothing happened. There were some creepy audio cues which definitely scared me, but it was all auditory. I did get one ghost like person who appeared conveniently right after I ran out of lighter fluid, and that was an awesome moment. Otherwise, I knew where I needed to go, but couldn't find the item necessary to give me access to that part of the house so I decided to give up. If the mechanics were changed to be less about frustrating the player, then I could see myself really liking this game, but as I said, they've designed it this way on purpose, so I don't see myself coming back. Can't recommend it right now.

_childDocuments_.review: Swinging lamp.As the Congressional Debate over gun control flares up yet again, we regret to report the murder of the wife and her two children by their husband and father. The father purchased the rifle used in the crime at his local gunstore two days earlier. This brutal killing took place while the family was gathered at home on a Sunday afternoon. The day of the crime, the father went to the trunk of his car, retrieved the rifle, and shot his wife as she was cleaning up the kitchen after lunch. When his ten-year-old son came to investigate the commotion, the father shot him, too. His six-year-old daughter had the good sense to hide in the bathroom, but reports suggest he lured her out by telling her it was just a game. The girl was found shot once in the chest from point-blank range. The mother, who he shot in the stomach, was pregnant at the time. Police arriving on-scene after neighbors called 911 found the father in his car, listening to the radio. Several days before the murders, neighbors say they heard the father repeating a sequence of numbers in a loud voice. They said it was like he was chanting some strange spell. There was another family shot to death in the same state last month, and in December last year, a man used a rifle and meat cleaver to murder his entire family. In each case, the perpretrators were fathers. State police say the string of domestic homicides appears unrelated, though it could be part of a larger trend, such as employment, childcare, and other social issues facing the average family.

_childDocuments_.review: Simply amazing. This game was a ride, horror done right. _childDocuments_.review: This game may be only Early Access but this is by and large one of if not THE scariest game I've played. I can't explain to you how many times I screamed like a little girl and had wanted to stop playing. At one point the game actually scared me so bad that my chest genuinely hurt. I had to take a moment to catch my breath before returning to the game. It's not just cheap jumpscares, and this game does a great job of playing up the scares and building the tension before giving you a release worth the wait. It does start a little slow, but the first real enemy encounter/scare left me terrified to explore. I would definitely not suggest this for someone who doesn't handle horror well. People who try to act macho and as if they are impossible to scare will definitely have their work cut out for them in this game. So let's get down to the specifics.The graphics are gorgeous and truely suck you into the terrifying atmosphere of the game. The ambiance from sounds alone is enough to rival Dead Space's sound design, except with far more subtlety and nuance. The game's controls can be a little unintuitive, the amount of times I accidentally dropped something by pressing F is somewhat annoying. I remember losing a lighter that way and being unable to find it later. The way the world interacts with the physics of the objects you're holding can provide some goofy weird moments, including getting objects stuck on the other side of doors only to have them teleport into your hand or having them knock against walls and behave awkwardly.The only other slight qualm I have with the game is that once your sanity is in the danger zone candles seem to offer no actual effect on refilling your sanity. I may have misunderstood, but I definitely had 2 candles directly next to me and stood there for a while suffering all the ill effects of dangerously low sanity.That is literally all I can think of as far as negatives, and honestly they're almost non-existent enough for me to not care. The items and resources can be a little scarce but I do not find that a negative, it just adds to the challenge of the game.Honestly I can't believe this game is in early access. Even as is for the asking price and the incomplete product I'd say you're getting far more than your money's worth. Not to mention the cute little easter eggs at the end of the game and the reference to another survival horror series that I was quite entertained to see. So devs, color me insanely impressed. I can't think of another horror game on steam that would even come close to being on par with this if I'm honest. Not even "Triple A" releases. Thank you for the clear hard work and love you've poured into this game and I cannot wait to see what you add to the final product. Even if I may curse your name when your game makes me scream like a big ol' baby.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the (s)cream of the crop, an essential for any horror lover and easily one of the most graphically-impressive games I have ever played. _childDocuments_.review: I've played literally every horror game I could get my hands on, and lemme just say, Visage is possibly one of the scariest ones I have ever played. Not enough horror games can build up dread the way this one does. The atmosphere itself feels very realistic and creepy, very immersive. Ghostly events like lights going off, doors opening or closing, footsteps, ghoulish sounds, ghosts following you around, etc offer a diverse unpredictable set of scares to keep you always on edge. The environmental storytelling is both its greatest strength and possibly its biggest weakness, and it can be difficult to figure out how to progress a storyline. You have to really look closely at your surroundings, as you start to see patterns that push you in the right direction. For any horror fan, this is a MUST play!

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to preface this right now: this game is getting a positive recommendation, but I'm going to have a lot of criticisms. Ultimately, this game is tantalizingly close to brilliance, and so its shortcomings become all the more sharp. It makes some big errors, but ultimately I would tell you: if you want a scary and good horror game, this is that. It's exactly what you want from a horror title and a genuine step above the common chaff. So then, with that being said...This game's ending sucks eggs. And that's not the only problem. (Some spoilers BELOW)Some more pros first: the atmosphere is absolutely stellar. The concept of a haunted house is well demonstrated here, and I love the way they take advantage of the space. I like the concept of the Sanity meter and I like how it serves to make any and all progression potentially threatening. I do think this creates an arbitrary element to the difficulty, sadly -- a trope of modern horror games that this one doesn't seem to shake. Sometimes enemy spawns just straight up kill me, other times I'm faced with an adventure-game like scenario of having to find the correct spot to go to or else die. This becomes more common towards the "end" of the game, though since you can play the chapters in any order, the "end" may be very different for you.Either way, in terms of being "a scary game" this is an A+. Absolutely terrifying, the way they build tension, the way they ensure that a "scare" in-game has negative consequences on a mechanical sense, this is all great. Graphics are really good as well. I do think the game suffers for being way too obtuse -- a little more guidance or a means of finding out where you need to go would be great. Why not have the Compass point me towards quest items that I haven't collected, or help locate collectibles? Why is the camera useless outside of Lucy's chapter?I see so much potential to build upon for a prospective sequel. The chapter tools could have been used to unlock whole sections of the house. The house should have had multiple house layouts as well -- I enjoy the use of the static space, but you can tell that the development was maybe struggling to find new ways to remix it. Delores' chapter has the best in that regard, with the mirrors transmuting the space and you needing a key item to unlock them. Having new mirrors spawn after that chapter that'd create new pathways in the house would have been cool.This could almost have been a sort of horror Metroidvania, but sadly its structure kneecaps its own tension-building. Each chapter can be done in any order and you're locked into the chapters you choose. Each chapter has its own enemy ghost, though two of them largely function the same way and one is largely part of scripted chases. The distinctions and similarities are kind of moot, these Chapters form the bulk of the game's actual gameplay and they are wholly self-contained. The items you gain from them have very, very little use outside of them.So "outside" the chapters is the secret "fourth chapter", where you uncover the protagonist's backstory that led to the traumatic incident the game's start. For how much effort is put into this, this is the part of the story that feels the least fleshed out. For one, most everything is communicated in vague metaphors. This allows some very interesting interpretations of the plot, but it means for most of the game, you're just gonna be confusedly wandering from one set piece to another, one creepy cutscene to the next.I had a hard time feeling sympathetic for the main character and it's hard to see him as a blank slate when he most clearly isn't, yet the game tries to treat him like one. The way the game handles the main character is very odd -- it reminds me strongly of the Seventh Guest, an old PC adventure game. The way the camera moves and the overall tone is actually pretty similar to that game as well. The story fails to resolve any of the supernatural mysteries. There's so much left unexplained you could write whole novels of subjective interpretation and probably be just as valid based on the evidence as anyone else. If you are playing hoping for some payoff at the end, don't. The payoff is lame. Play it for the experience the tension and the great creeping dread. There's some beautiful scenes of horror and misery, there's some great scares and some fantastic tension. I just wish, dearly, that this game could have delivered better on tying it all together. The plot is the weakest part and I feel like this will severely hurt my willingness to replay it.It's definitely a game where you'll get the most out of it in your first playthrough. The majority of your playtime and the danger you'll face comes from wandering around in search of the next puzzle to solve. My playtime reflects a single playthrough with only minimal outside help sought. There is a LOT of head scratching puzzles to solve here. The game also generally just declines in quality towards its end. The non-early-access chapter is the weakest of the three by far. It is basically Alone in the Dark without the combat; but it's quite good. Silent Hill has a worthy up-and-comer to challenge it, and the work and effort in this game is worth your time and money. Just, don't expect much replay value.I will say, as well -- I wish there was more you could do to interact with the enemies in this game. Unlike Alien : Isolation, there's really not a lot you can do but run and take advantage of the weaknesses of the AI in order to evade threats -- most of the time you just leave the area until an enemy despawns and then continue whatever it was you were doing. But there's very little you can do to impact the enemies, and that's a real shame. For the record, I never once had to use a light bulb to fix a light fixture. Not once. I don't know if it's random or what, but the a.i. never broke a single light bulb. Take of that what you will.

_childDocuments_.review: I previously reviewed this game, but I hadn't beaten the game yet. I now have all the achievements in the game so I feel like I can give a pretty in-depth review. To start, Dolores's chapter is deceptively long in comparison with the other three chapters in the game. You can do the chapters in any order and I just so happened to do Dolores's first. Like many others have mentioned, I eventually felt compelled to look up a guide to save my time and sanity. I was a little disappointed in seeing how linear the game actually was in the guide as the game gives the impression that it's very asynchronous and able to be completed in a multitude of ways; not true. It took me 7 hours to complete Dolores's chapter and another 7 to get every achievement in the game. Granted I started relying heavily on a guide after getting completely stuck which likely shortened the time substantially, but the problem is the game NEEDS a guide because the way the 'plot' progresses makes zero sense.Speaking of plot, I am beyond disappointed with the story. I previously gave this game a 7/10 but I think I am leaning more towards 6/10 because the endings (there's 2) sucked so much ass. The problem with the story is that it seems like it's starting to make sense around the 3rd~4th chapter but then the ending is like a slap in face. I'm pretty sure this game just set the new "worst video game ending I've ever experienced" for me. It makes me feel like I just wasted all my time playing the game and working toward the "good" ending when the devs couldn't be bothered to spend more than like 10 seconds on a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cutscene.I guess the devs spent all their time on programming the mechanics of this game because despite what everyone else has said, there isn't many bugs at all. Your items will occasionally get stuck on corners/items, the music will bug out and play or not play correctly at times, and the reflection/depth-of-field effects don't always work correctly and end up ruining the ambiance at times. Otherwise there are zero bugs in this game, but the bugs aren't the issue. The developers know that the game relies solely on music to scare you, this is why you can't change the music's volume individually from the game's master volume. It's a shame because there are a few times where the music doesn't trigger and the scare lands perfectly, but 90% of the time you're going to be scared from the shrill violin sound that plays very loudly and comes across as cheap. I recall I was in a room looking for an item and I turned around and there was a person there unexpectedly and I audibly screamed. Unfortunately this is very rare and the game seems to opt for rapid fire constant jump scares using music rather than letting the situation carry the fear (which it's capable of doing).{Potential Very Light Spoiler}Lastly, there are a few cheap "chase" scenes that made me so mad from how ridiculous they were. For example, the PRISON VHS tape challenge where you have to change the light bulbs around to see was unbelievably frustrating. If I didn't bring pills to this challenge I would've been absolutely ♥♥♥♥♥♥ and for some reason 2 of the guides I followed didn't mention this. Imagine a hallway that you need to go back and forth in and a monster appears in the middle and chases you for some undetermined amount of time. Now imagine the hallway is basically pitch black and the monster one-shots you every time it comes close. {Potential Very Light Spoiler Over}Lastly, why does the game have such a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ pause mechanic? I understand if you want to make it so the escape menu doesn't pause the game so you need a button, but then the button takes 3 seconds to pause the game. I'm pausing the game because I need to respond to somebody on discord, or there is something in real life that needs attending. The way the sanity works in this game means you basically screw yourself any time you want to pause cause you have to just stand there in game for 3 seconds while your sanity is dropping. Please, if you're going to use this system make the pause button instant, it's annoying as ♥♥♥♥ having to wait to pause a game when time matters quite a bit.TL;DR It's not often I finish a game and my opinion of the game actually goes down, but this game is still very scary and fun. I really wish the devs could've found a way to make the objectives a little more obvious and especially more poignant to the story. There is a few scenes where I'm like "Oooooh I think I get what's going on now!" only for the ♥♥♥♥ endings to totally slap me in the face and explain NOTHING. You should only get this game if you are into atmospheric horror with a lot of jump scares, the game mechanics are very basic and the story is one of the worst I've experienced in a long time. On sale around 20$ (what I paid) I'd say 7/10For 35$ I would avoid this game. The game plays best as a shallow horror walking simulator. The story is unbelievably bad and the progression of objectives makes ZERO sense.

_childDocuments_.review: It's got a lot of potential, but it's not there yet. There are a lot of mechanics in the game that are half-baked. Managing resources is rarely necessary, if ever, which makes the painkillers, zippos, and light-bulbs redundant. I'd say always carry a lighter and a bottle of painkillers, and you'll be fine. Honestly, it's so basic that the game would almost be better without having to manage these items.The controls are clunky and not intuitive. For a game that doesn't support controllers, it barely makes use of the keyboard at all. Inventory management is an absolute chore. Items you're carrying in your 'hands' (your hands are never actually rendered) exist physically in the world and constantly get stuck on doorways and other objects. I had multiple occasions where an Item I was carrying was stuck on a wall after walking through a door and I had to walk back through the door to carefully guide the object around the corner. The Dolores chapter is astronomically better than the Lucy chapter, which essentially involves a semi-linear maze full of jumpscares and item hunting in pitch-black rooms. The Dolores chapter at least had some fun puzzles that reminded me of old Silent Hill or Resident Evil. It is scary enough, I guess, and it's alright if you want something spooky to fill up a few hours. The atmosphere is decent. But the gameplay is rough. Very rough.

_childDocuments_.review: Visage is - without a doubt - the most frightening and unnerving game I have EVER played. Coming from a deep love of horror (both games and movies - yes even modern horror movies), this game had me completely on the edge of my seat, the intensity so overwhelming that I couldn't play it for long stretches of time. This is particularly true for the first hours, that largely take place in a medium-sized suburban house where each and every dark little corner or horrible hallway can and will hold a harrowing twist that will knock your socks off. Scary old crones peeping around corners, phones ringing, lights going out, doors slamming shut, Visage just makes scaring the player into a dark, completely intimidating and very efficient art.Unfortunately somewhere after the two thirds mark the game starts to lose focus. The house is largely abandoned and replaced with boring tunnels, esotheric dream segments and a claustrophic asylum. The constant tension of the first few hours makes way for uninspired chase scenes, hunting around for keys in the dark and tired old gore. It's still enjoyable, but it's nothing we haven't seen before and it stands in stark contast against the damn near perfect beginning of the game. And then there is the obtuse inventory system that has you collecting lighters and pills to ease your sanity. Doing something as simple as lighting a candle takes way too many steps and feels completely unintuitive. It is often quite hard to understand what the game wants you to do. Without a clear list of objectives, you are usually wandering around in the dark, hoping that that will set off a new chain of events which really takes away some of the tension. Still... Despite these shortcomings, the first six or seven hours are simply wonderful. Anyone interested in the genre should check this one out. I guarantee you haven't played horror like this before!

_childDocuments_.review: To an individual such as myself, horror has never really felt the same. Having played countless horror titles, I have become desensitized to the genre. Well, until I found visage. This game stands as a horror master different from the rest. Everything from the horrifying and standout locations, disturbing story, and even scarier encounters. My explanations no matter how long or in depth can justify the experience that is given by this game. Standing as the only game to truly scary me, visage is worth its price tag and much more. Taking the role of Dwayne, a man overcome by grief and pain, we are trapped within a house composed of only the most nightmare fuel horrors. Trapped, whether it be a dream or purgatory, Dwayne is forced to live through the story of the houses future inhabitants including his own past.  If you are seeking a horror experience that will really stick with you, I cannot recommend this game enough.

_childDocuments_.review: If your a fan of psychological horrors with jump scares, then this game is for you. Overall, this game was extremely fun even though I am not one for these types of games. This is the first one of hopefully many games that I will play in regards to this type of horror. A couple of pros and cons about this game that I do have and will share with the community.Pros:- Awesome story within each chapter that will be revealed the more you proceed with each chapter. Even though there is only two chapters out so far, the story of each has left an everlasting impression on what more is to come.- The music and the ambient sounds from the game are memorizing. It always leaves you on the edge of your seat as your proceeding through the chapters of the game.- The random generated events requires you to have your head on a swivel and will always pull your attention that something may happen or not. Your attention is always stuck on what is going on and the game does not leave any room where you can take a break from the chaos that you will eventually run into.- Critical thinking in some part of the chapters makes you rethink everything that has happened thus far and try to figure out the next upcoming step.- The First Person Point-of-View gives this game a more intertwined and immersed feeling as you are viewing everything first hand. What the character sees and hears, you feel that your actually at that moment and time within the chapter.Cons:- There have been a couple of spots where I have randomly got stuck and unable to move. With that said, I would have to reload the save file from the latest auto save. Whatever the case may be with that, kinda glad that I was in a somewhat "safe" part of the chapter that I was proceeding through.- Items randomly floating in the middle of the room or staircase. Thank you for the extra items but it is a little weird in seeing them floating around randomly and in random locations. Always thought that they would be empty or not usable anymore but they were.- When sprinting through the game, there are a couple of lag spikes where you wont be able to move or interact with anything in the game. Not terribly bad, but that couple of seconds with something coming after you, you need to run like hell.- When exiting the game and proceeding back to the main menu, it will crash most times then not and I would have to restart the game.Overall, never thought that i would enjoy this game apart from the funky glitches and bugs I ran into throughout the game, however, it has become my "must come back to" game once the next chapters have been revealed. I cannot wait to see what is in store next with this game.

_childDocuments_.review: This may contain spoilers to some degree, nothing crazy but more my theory on what was going on.First two chapters are really freaky and some of the scariest in a long time. Lucy's aka the first chapter was by far the best of them all. It felt like they went all out on the first two chapters and scrambled for ideas in the next two.The new two chapters are kind of a letdown, somewhat creepy but felt like the game was more confused about what to do next. Rakan's chapter felt all over the place and we never understand how he's connected to Dwayne. Also felt more jumpscary than anything else. Mirror Mask was an interesting idea but kind of felt like it explained some things twice when it wasn't necessary. It felt like these chapters didn't really answer their own questions.There's also a tar monster that everyone seems confused about, me included. I think it may be Dwayne's evil self coming back for his conscience after killing his family and committing suicide. This is to stop him from seeing the truth perhaps, which makes me think this may be his purgatory.Some neat little easter eggs here and there and The Neighbors comic sets Rose in a completely different light than just that of a nice old lady.For what it's worth the devs have made something pretty incredible to be such a small team. I applaud them for the lengthiness and quality of the game overall. Controls are also better than before but still takes a little getting used to.

_childDocuments_.review: [SPOILERS] The first hour of the first chapter was horrifyingly shivers inducing. I played Chapter 2 (Delores) yesterday and unfortunately, the mechanics of the game become more of a chore after playing chapter 1. I listed the points in Here is a summary:- The random events like lights turning off become boring and have no horror value to it. As soon as a light turns off I just go and flick the light back on without even fearing anything, it became far too common. The events became boring, a chore and takes away from the gameplay.- The chore of walking around the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ house.....I now memorised the house more than my own. Walking is so slow, and I spent the Dolores chapter in a walking simulator. You travel for so long just to retrieve an item back and forth, back and forth that it became hectic.- Not knowing where to go. How the hell am I expected to know what to do next? It's just all about going everywhere (walking simulator) until you hit a trigger for an event or a new room. There is no indication of what to do next, where to go, and what is expected. I did enjoy the first few hours of the game (First chapter), especially that I didn't know what to expect. Before all the events became too repetitive and boring, it was fascinating and I thought this could beat P.T. The first time we got the camera and scribbles on the wall appear with it... That was damn horrifying. I wish the game kept that atmosphere and not be a walking simulator with the chore to turn lights, TVs and breakers back on.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great and one of the scariest I've ever played. There's just one downside that I urge the developers to fix: the controls are very counterintuitive. _childDocuments_.review: I got this game when it was in early access and only had one chapter and it was a must have for any fan of the horror game genre back then. Now there are 4 chapters and the game is one of the best horror experience I've had with a video game. amazing atmosphere which always has you tense and on edge. About 10-20 hours of story gameplay when going in blind with a couple more hours on top of that when going for all the achievements.Each chapter is unique and offers a different play style along with the traditional horror game tropes.Inspiration can be seen from the original Resident Evil trilogy in terms of item based puzzles and backtracking through a claustrophobic environment, Silent Hills (P.T. more than anything) level of psychological horror and tension, and a chapter which pays tribute to Outlast's chase simulations and setting. 1 chapter is admittedly not as good as the other 3 in my opinion but the game is by no means a cash grab, walking simulator. Some jumpscares are present but the game has no need to rely on them. Puzzles are challenging but not too obscure. Exploration, perception and experimenting is encouraged.The story is fairly cliche and obscure, and i found myself slightly confused by the time the credits rolled, but the atmosphere, tension and length more than make up for it. A must have addition for any horror fan.

_childDocuments_.review: I am 32 years old.My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and we adopted our son together. Both are now 4 years old.When we were going through our separation, I felt lost and unhappy. I was self-destructive. One day, I was so angry with everything spiraling out of control that I punched a concrete wall in a moment of overwhelming emotion. This resulted in breaking my fifth metacarpal in my right hand—the hand I worked with, played games with, and used to carry my children to bed—the hand I desperately needed to ensure I could continue providing.Upon learning the severity of the self-inflicted damage, I became almost suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man, with no history of depression or anxiety. I had never experienced anger outbursts, nor was I the type to break down and cry, but I was in a tough situation that truly prevented me from seeing the light on the other side.With nothing better to do, I looked for a game I could play WITH ONE HAND while recovering. Somehow, I stumbled upon this game and read some of the comments. I decided it was worth a try... I must admit I didn't beat the game, nor did I play as much as some of you. In fact, I may have played this game for only a day or two. That being said, after doing so, I had a new joy and hope for life. I managed to leave behind the pain and suffering that had been thrust upon me. I could experience the joy and happiness of other people. I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥ minutes listening to this music, long enough to realize that I would be okay.After realizing this, I turned off the game and went back to work. My hand hurt a lot, but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so sorry for myself and became the father I needed to be at that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving like.Today, I am close friends with the mother of my children. We don't fight, argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents and friends.Now I have 3 children. My third child is, wait, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my separation, and we just unexpectedly stumbled into each other's lives. We have been dating for a year and are very happy together.Moral of the story: you never know what life has in store for you, and if I had given up when all odds were against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.Thank you.

_childDocuments_.review: The only truly "scary" thing I've found in this game is the control scheme, which is part of the reason I didn't play this game for very long. For mobility reasons, I can't play on wasd like most other people. I need to be able to edit keybinds, which you can't in this game. And even then, the control scheme makes NO sense. If you're going to be mostly interacting and looking at objects, PUT THAT ON LEFT CLICK. Have use on e like almost every other game.The second "scary" thing is the tutorials, which randomly pop up in the worst way. With the way the game is made, where you have a sanity meter that can be effected by "paranormal activity" in the game, you NEED to pause the game while those tutorials are up so people can actually read them if you're going to shove them in their faces. More than once I was trying to understand what the block of text was and there would be a "scary something" that happened in the background, usually a lightbulb breaking or switch being flipped, which lead me to cancel out of the tutorial before I could read it and have to find a place with light so my dumb character wouldn't be afraid of the dark for half a second. Which brings me to another annoying part of the game, if you're in early access and want to have particular parts blocked off for the main game, for the love of god don't say something's 'not available in early access' in the game. Just say the door's locked or the lock is broken or something. It kills the immersion that should be in a horror game to make it scary as badly as the tutorials. Personally, I didn't find the game scary. Maybe that comes with how little of the game I could play, but having stock 'you should be scared now' sounds happening when I'm not looking at whatever should be scaring me is more annoying than anything else, especially when it tanks the character's sanity meter and I'm left spinning in circles asking wtf is supposed to be scaring me. At the very least the scares should happen when I'm looking at the light, or the radio should pop on when I'm far enough away that's it's not 'oh, the radio again'. Not only that but the scares should be spead out enough that I wasn't thinking 'oh, it's been 45 seconds, time for another spook.'If you're going to have a mechanic that lowers sanity in the dark, don't spam that you shouldn't stand in the dark for so long when someone's only been in the dark a couple seconds, especially when there's items that you have to get by going through dark areas to get! For a game that tries to brag that it's a hard game, which is suspect and laughable in most cases because the devs shouldn't have to try to convince you that a game is hard, it does a LOT of hand holding. If it's an exploritory game, let people explore without so many warnings and pop ups. If you're worried that people are going to quit the game because it's artifically hard, then drop it! Make it a more casual and enjoyable experience if you want to tell a story with your game. Otherwise, actually make the game hard and not just annoying because of bad qol changes. I honestly had high hopes for this game, but it's left me laughing and wanting a much better experience. Unless there are meaningful changes to the game, I'm not going to pick it up again and I certainly won't be recommending it to anyone.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm an avid horror game fan and IMO this is one of the best horror games out there. I started Chapter 2 first (Delores) and I loved every minute! Absolutely terrifying and the way the game builds tension is undoubtedly one of the best I have experienced. Although chapter 3 was no where near as well crafted as the two that came before. If someone explained this game to me prior I think I would consider the concept pretty tame.. Just another game similar to Layers of Fear, although there are some similarities IMO 'Visage' far surpasses anything else in its genre. I personally never had the pleasure of playing the PT demo but if it was even half as good as this game I realise that I have missed out big time. The graphics were also a surprise to me as for the price I wasn't expecting the environment to be so detailed. I have only two little criticisms really -1) I played about 7 hours in and then due to a bug I couldn't proceed. I don't want to give anything away so I will not explain further, fortunately I enjoyed the game so much I just started from the beginning and due to the nature of the game I was able to get back in a fraction of that time, and still enjoyed playing all those sections again.2) Some of the puzzles are a bit WTF, I mean I love a challenge as much as the next person but I would be lying if I said I didn't need a guide to get past some of the harder parts.My final thought was imagining what this game would be like if they modded it for VR..... _childDocuments_.review: Is the game scary to play? Yes. 100 percent. It nails sound design, tension, visuals, art direction - all a home run. Like wow. I love horror games and this could've been one of the best horror games ever made, but it fails miserably in progression and puzzle solving. You would need hours and hours of aimlessly walking around and not knowing what to do without some type of guide. I got to chapter two where you need to smash mirrors throughout the house to solve puzzles and found around 5 mirrors and went into them, not completing the vast majority of the puzzles. Why? BECAUSE YOU MAYBE DIDN'T FIND THAT SINGLE MIRROR HIDDEN IN A CLOSET IN THE DARK THAT YOU NEED TO GET A SINGLE OBSCURE PIECE FROM TO SOLVE THE NEXT PUZZLE. Which next puzzle you may ask? Oh WHO THE F*** KNOWS? You just have to hope to go into the next mirror and have the right tools/equipment to solve that one from a previous mirror. This means that my intellect or any type of game knowledge or environmental knowledge I've gained from the house means absolute bunk. It's whatever the devs have in their own mind with ZERO CUES or hints to point you in the next direction. Do some people love this? Yea because they are masochistic. But wandering around for hours aimlessly trying to solve obtuse puzzles that require a guide isn't my idea of a fun time. Absolutely dropped the ball on this one. What could've been a 10/10 game has been destroyed by obtuse puzzles, aimless wandering, and a story that has no cohesiveness.

_childDocuments_.review: In any format, the horror genre is completely subjective to each person.I think of myself as a horror connoisseur and can appreciate horror for what it is even if it doesn't necessarily scare me.Visage, as a horror game - fails at being a horror game for I would say 95% of the time playing.The first chapter is very clearly inspired by the legendary P.T. and it wears its inspiration on its sleeve which I can appreciate. The game involves you wandering through a house trying to trigger certain events, all the while trying to keep your inventory stocked with light sources and sanity pills, as well as the "mandatory" item for the chapter. The inventory management system is ok but ultimately falls flat and becomes more of a nuisance as the game goes on. I'm sure it was supposed to be inspired by the classic survival horror games like Resident Evil and Silent Hill, but fails dramatically at replicating those.I can forgive the shoddy inventory management however, the real issue with the game comes from the "threat". At a certain point in each chapter, you will eventually begin being hunted by that chapters villain. Half the time it seems completely random when and why they attack. I'm sure most of it is driven by sanity but your sanity may as well be 0 because even if you pop your pills they still hunt and kill you immediately, forcing you to watch what feels like a 10 minute death animation and restart from your last checkpoint.The best horror experiences are the ones where it feels like you are at risk of dying. Walking simulators are great for narrative and jump scares but you'll never feel truly terrified if theres no real risk attached.Visage attempts to solve this issue by making it a walking simulator with a threat, and it fails spectacularly. Nothing is more annoying that being forced to explore the map to solve a cryptic puzzle and then suddenly have to do it all over again because you took too long. After 3 or 4 deaths it stops being scary and just starts being frustrating.After the first chapter I had to force myself to slog through the rest of the chapters and it was just not an enjoyable experience. Each chapter has a single moment that I could consider a good example of horror, but is it really worth playing 8+ hours for 3 minutes of good horror? Absolutely not.I will admit that I did not finish the "final" chapter, which involves you completing the main 3 chapters and then finding a bunch of collectables to unlock the "FINAL" chapters. After completing chapter 3 I was done and will not be returning or even bothering to look up the final chapter.I would highly recommend avoiding this game. It does go on sale quite often which is nice, but it really isn't worth the time investment in my honest opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is easily the best horror game around and arguably the scariest horror game ever created.  The developers did an excellent job in combining many different elements to horror and throwing them all at you at the right moments.  Loved the fact that it wasn't repetitive in the sense that in previous horror games, if you played them more than once, you knew a jump scene was waiting around the corner.  You don't have that here.  Similar style to the horror game PT, but Visage ticks more boxes for me.  Aside from the fact this is a true horror game and raises the heart rate, it also doesn't hold your hand in the puzzle solving aspect for progression.  This is fantastic.  The puzzle solving can be simple enough at times, but elsewhere they can be very difficult, and it really makes you think to what you have seen, where you have been in the game to solve what is in front of you.  A master piece in that the devs really hit the nail on the head and got this game right.  highly recommend this game if you love the rush of jump scares, creepy game play, twisted game play and puzzle progression solving that doesn't give hints to help you along.  Fantastic game

_childDocuments_.review: Before I get into the major problem I ran into with this game, which ultimately led to me quitting it and uninstalling it to save space on my computer, Visage DOES have many redeeming qualities that I want to list first because I don't think it's fair to just turn away because I marked this review as "not recommended". Honestly I wish you could give neutral ratings on Steam because that's probably more fitting for what I'm about to say. Onto the good qualities! Visage is expertly crafted on a design side of things! It's like a full-game version of the PT demo from back in the day, which really hit some nostalgia (or would that be ptsd since it's a scary experience? when you're talking about horror games it's sort of a mix between the two isn't it) especially early on! I found this game very fun for the first 4 or 5 hours I played it, visually it looks great, the sounds and music are top-notch, and it relies mostly on psychological horror and paranoia triggers to create fear, and it's legitimately very scary!Now for the reason I don't plan to continue playing: Progression without following a tutorial is painfully slow, it's almost like this game was designed for you to have to follow tutorials honestly. It really got to a point where I was no longer afraid whenever stuff happened and whenever I heard certain sounds in certain places I knew what was coming to the point where I just sat there and nodded as scripted events unfolded in front of me, simply because I'd seen everything many times by that point from all of my wandering in circles trying to figure out where to go and what to do. I'd play this game in hour long sittings like I do most games I play, and I'd probably progress 1% - 2% according to the completion meter in-game, maybe 3 or 4% on a good day, within that time span. I stopped playing shortly after I finished Dalores' chapter (which is chapter 4 if I remember correctly, fsr the chapters are numbered without any indication of which one is which in-game) and had started Lucy's chapter, and it got to the point where Lucy's ghost had taken away all of the light switches and strewn them across the floor, and I just can't be bothered to deal with that at this point so I stopped playing. Maybe I'll revisit this game in the future (with a tutorial pulled up of course) I'm not sure, but if you don't like having to practically rely on tutorials to make any legitimate progress in a game then I don't think you'll want to play this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I initially planned on completing all of the content in Early Access before writing this review, but this just couldn't wait!First off, I've played them all when it comes to horror - Alien Isolation, PT, Amnesia, Soma, Outlast, Resident Evil 7, Dead Space, etc. etc. So many good games, but lately it seems like the horror genre hasn't surprised me lately and gotten my heart rate truly elevated or goose bumps on my body.Visage has scared me more in the first 90 minutes than most of those games put together. I just now had to stop and turn the lights on and pick up my guitar to go back to my happy place. HUGE props to the 2 developers - you guys have truly made something special and I can't wait to pick it back up and continue on once my heart can take it!PROS:Unreal Engine 4 graphics are fantastic and runs at a perfect framerate on a 970 graphics cardSound design is on point, giving subtle hints but nothing that gives it away, great job managing tension and releaseA few moments lifted from PT work very well - this actually feels like what PT should have been if given more timeA great mixture of mechanics from other games that I won't spoil - they also use them in ways I've never seenStory is heavy and intense so far, but works with the world they've builtThe house really has a character of its own - I still am not sure if it changed by itself or if I just missed something beforeJust the right mixture of explaining mechanics/tutorials without making things too easy - it's a good challenge so farCONSTUCTIVE IDEAS:Text in the menus overlaps in a few areas - most noticably when changing brightness in gameWalking speed is great, but the jog/sprint is pretty slow, maybe speed it up just a smidge?10/10 would recommend - just have a stuffed penguin nearby to grab hold of when necessary!

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a rather huge fan of horror games, so you can imagine the joy I felt discovering VISAGE thanks to a recommendation of a dear friend of mine. The atmosphere and tension is next level - I had to fight the urge to just save and turn the game off various times while opening a door. Very intense but more than worth the ride.+ Beautiful graphics+ Challenging puzzles+ Tension never goes away+ Stream it for friends to let them make fun of you pooping your pants+ Great sense of humour where you'd never expect it to occur, had me in tears a bunch of times!- Clunky inventory, took me way too long to get used to it- Sprint can get really frustrating, there are times the sprint is slightly faster than walking- Random ghost attacks can come when you have no place to escape- Slightly difficult to know where to go next sometimes- Some clipping with your character and items getting stuck around a cornerHowever, solid story, great gameplay, haunting music and fantastic use of tension and horror. I have not been that scared playing a game in quite awhile. I highly recommend this game to any and all horror game enthusiasts out there.

_childDocuments_.review: Update: Tried really hard to gather courage and actually played through the first chapter. Game IS scary, atmosphere is phenomenal. This game has a little bit of everything that may scare you. Are you afraid of the dark? Of the unknown? Of being stalked and followed both by things you can and can't see? Maybe you're scared of narrow spaces. Or scared of wide open areas. Scared of not knowing where or who you are. Maybe you're like me and loneliness is terrifying. This game has a little bit of all of those and more. Do be careful if you suffer from deep trauma, mental or cardiac illness, and stop playing if it's too much. The game will be waiting, and it won't punish you for it.I will preface this by stating that I haven't played more than a few minutes for reasons I'll explain below. My opinion on the game might change after I man up and play more, but so far first impressions are a resounding 500 out of 10. The atmosphere and mood set by the game are downright terrifying starting with the subtle and eerie sounds of both an empty, quiet house and things that go bump in the night, all the way through an intro cutscene so tense and chilling that you can't help gagging and wanting to run away to spare your eyes from the evil developing right in front of you. But Visage didn't let me look away. It gripped me and went "you're going to witness darkness and gaze deep into it with no way to escape".I'm not really into spooky stuff, since it's never done anything even close to making me feel uneasy. I played Visage because a friend said this one is actually scary and yeah it ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ is. This is the first game to ever give me a sinking and ever growing feeling of dread that just screams something is about to be very, very wrong and you can't stop it. I had to steel myself to even consider looking down a dimly lit hallway, nevermind the dark nooks and crannies you can peek into. The game does an amazing job of making you ♥♥♥♥ your pants with every small creak emitted when you open a door. How? By letting you go around a few places shown in the videos in the store page. You see that closet all the way in the back and your gut starts screaming no, but you press on, and slowly pull the creaking, whining door open, peering into the murky black inside, afraid you'll get snatched. But then there was nothing. But what about next time? What if you turn your back and then it gets you? The game nails the feeling of being small and helpless in the face of eldritch abominations and ghosts with unknowable motivations.Indeed the game isn't perfect, but it's still in early access. I've only played a few minutes before being spooked into waiting for someone braver or stupider to play with me, with lights on of course. At the very least, Visage deserves massive praise for sheer presence with its sound design. Best wishes for the team behind the game as a whole, I'm looking forward to getting a heart attack while playing one of your games

_childDocuments_.review: I've barely accomplished anything in this game and I'm mentally exhausted.  This is a compliment to the designers who have absolutely nailed the atmosphere.  The tension (especially with some good headphones) permeates through every step you take.  Something as simple as opening a door or flicking on a light caused me incredible amounts of anxiety. _childDocuments_.review: Let me start by saying this is the scariest thing I've played since P.T. It's fantastic, and I absolutely love the respectful nods it gives to Silent Hill 4 and other classic horror titles. It's the first-person horror I've been waiting for, and there's so much love poured into every scare. Fascinating visuals and a gradual descent into surreal horror makes it a vivid, uncomfortable experience from beginning to end.Now let's talk controls. My brother and I played the original scheme for our first playthrough on his account, and I picked up the controller on my account to try out the new scheme (which is why my playtime is so short, and yet I comment on the entire game). It's an improvement, but it's still very unintuitive, I feel. It won't let me store candles in the dynamic inventory, and I can't figure out whether or not this is intentional. I don't care for the "hold to use" as I feel it sprinkles frustration in when you're rushing to use things, and diffuses tension. I assume this change was made to avoid bugs or something, but I liked it the original way better.I like the fact the two inventories are now combined. I wish the dynamic inventory had more slots, but I'm an old school Silent Hill fan who wants bottomless pockets, so I think that's more of a subjective opinion than something to be taken as serious criticism. But it's a little annoying that the dynamic inventory is so small and the key inventory is so massive when you never have more than a few key items at a time. Maybe this changes in future chapters? I'm not sure, but for now, it comes across as not very well thought out.Picking up, storing, and retrieving items from the dynamic inventory is still a nightmare at first (there were no tutorials to teach the new scheme, either, so that was an experience of button experimentation), and even when you get used to it, there's a lot of fiddling that completely ruins the immersion for me. I would strongly recommend the devs pick a more classical inventory system that players are familiar with and stick with that rather than trying to reinvent the wheel. It's still very clumsy and frustrating. I've dropped way too many bottles of pills just trying to back out of the inventory screen because I'm so accustomed to "B" backing out of a menu.However, the candle placement has improved massively. I love the new red cloud to indicate sanity loss. The sanity system overall seems to be better balanced (but perhaps it's just a result of having a more clear UI that allows us to better manage it). I really appreciate the updates to drawings on the walls for hints to puzzles that are very unclear otherwise. They're done in a way that maintain the atmosphere and don't make the game feel "dumbed down".Overall, I would recommend the game, but with a disclaimer that the controls still feel very experimental and unbalanced. I love the fact the devs are listening to feedback, however, and I'm happy to support them. If you're not willing to purchase a game that's still experiencing growing pains, be sure to at least keep an eye on this one, because I think once it's been ironed out, it's going to become a horror icon. I can't wait for the next chapters.

_childDocuments_.review: My review, decent horror walking simulator but not worth the full 30$+ price tag, if on sale for around 15$ then I would suggest getting it, but after playing I am glad that I didn't pay full price and waited for a sale.  Story: not much there, I wouldn't consider it bad but just feels like a lot of other horror walking simulators Graphics: the photo-realistic environments are impressive but in certain areas they look outdated and so do the character models. Even though there is a lot of talking you never see anyone move their mouthsGameplay: you do use items but they are mostly context sensitive and even then not really useful but it does add more life to the game then just the walking (random nitpick why is it on horror walking simulators, when trying to run it feels just as slow as walking?).  Also no real replay ability unless looking for achievements or to get all easter eggs.  Not really interested in playing again just to get the multiple endings and will just watch the missed ones online.Puzzles: some hard some easy, as long as you find the hints (or answers) and know where to use them, they are self explanatory, most of the times the issue is searching every corner trying to locate them.Scares:  There are quite a few but mostly jump scares that happen so often you get used to them and are also annoying when trying to solve puzzles and lights keep turning off.  Chase sequences end fast too so no real scares there (another nitpick for walking horror simulators, why can't a full grown adult fend off a little girl, a guy on crutches, or an old lady, even though he has a sledgehammer or crowbar?)Sound: very good, they go well with the atmosphere but sometimes the music can get a little blaringBugs: heard there are some but haven't encountered any in my play-throughOverall a decent game and I do recommend it if you like scary games, but wait for it on sale.
