What's good: Beautiful artwork and detailsGood musicGood ambienceControls seem to function as intendedWhat's bad:Everything other than those things. I know it's brutal and vague, but unfortunately, it's accurate.My experiance upon launching the game:The game starts, I set my gamma balance as requested, then I see the whole opener, and wake up in the hall with the Mary statue. I find a candle which says it needs a lighter, but no lighter to be found. I spend a significant amount of time scouring my surroundings for one, and not finding any. So then I begin to press a few random keys thinking maybe I start with a lighter in my inventory, and there is just no prompt as to which keys are bound to it. Still nothing. I notice there is a prompt to press M1 and M2 together to combine a candle and lighter to make light, but nothing happens, confirming I most likely don't have a lighter. So I put that aside and begin to explore the house for approx. ten min, being introduced to a few of the game's features and mechanics, when suddenly 2 "paranormal events" occur simultaneously, locking me in a pitchblack bathroom. I can't see anything, my monitor is literally just a black screen, and it's not like real life where I can just feel my way around, so I have to go into the options and turn the gamma WAY up just so I can see a door. While all this is happening, the pills I found that are supposed to repair your sanity are all consumed, one by one. Then because I was in the dark for so long, my sanity has gone to ♥♥♥♥. _childDocuments_.review: Great horror game, not focused on jumpscares but on building up the tension and making the player always feel uncomfortable.The house the game takes place in plays a major role in all of this, with paranormal events (flickering lights, turn on and off of electronic appliances, sudden closing of doors) and strange sounds constantly surrounding the player.The narrative is divided in chapters, that can be accessed by interacting with specific objects inside the house. When in a chapter the tension and the horror factor ramp up, as you are not simply pressed by the events inside the house, but also by other entities which threaten your life. The story of the single chapters is interesting and delivered in a crude but effective way, even if its difficult to relate to the opening cutscene.The game lacks a bit of polishing here and there (understandable considering the early access), but it's worth the price considering the overall length (6-9 hours up to now) and the fact the are still half of the chapter missing (2) which must be released to complete the story.In addition the improvements made in the design from the first to the second chapter, clearly shows how the team is improving while creating the game, which bodes well for the future.EDIT:After having completed the game, my final idea stays in line with what I’ve written above with a couple of additional considerations.Chapter 3 and Chapter 4 do not achieve the peak reach by the first two, with the third more similar to an outlast-like horror with a lot of chasing and scripted sequences and the fourth one which is not really a full chapter but a collection of micro sequence needed to tell the overarching story of the main character. Still both of them deliver good horror moments and are enjoyable to play. The change of setting in Chapter 3, in particular, is an interesting and refreshing twist.The overarching story is quite interesting when the pieces are all put together (not only from through the narrative told in the chapters but also through some collectibles, like the comic’s pages), but it’s too cryptic in the way is narrated. This is purposely done to keep an aura of mystery and leave space to interpretation, but, at the same time, it is highly likely that most of the player will finish the game without understand it.To summarize for all the people who played the game in early access, the final product provides solid additional hours of entertainment and a good conclusion to the story.For all the people new to the game who like horror, instead, this game is a must buy, capable of offering one of the most frightening experience the genre has to offer.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a creepy horror experience, Visage is a good buy. Technical performance is good, it does have quite a number of gameplay issues but those are not serious enough to ruin the game. Pros:- Excellent horror experience without overdoing it- Great graphics, sound design and voice acting- Feels like an escape room- Good amount of content and variety to keep things interestingCons:- Inconvenient controls and inventory management are really unnecessary- Cryptic puzzles or weird "video game logic"- Level design of the main house- Chases in the main house are unfair- Needle in a haystack situationsWrt the chases: yes, you will get chased and die if you get caught, but there are so many situations (thanks to slow movement and level design of the main house) where you start off cornered with no escape or you get stuck in the environment, making these chases unfair. Players should die when they make a mistake but Visage will kill you off at random. However the game does not set you back or punish you if you die, you resume at the last checkpoint so although really annoying this flaw is forgivable. Some parts of the script are way too cryptic, I do not expect a lot of players to make it through without a guide. In some cases the devs were aware that it is too cryptic and they "solved" it by simply telling you the problem/solution and that is disappointing. However, since the horror experience is REALLY good (without going into detail) it is definitely worth recommending. I felt that consulting a guide did not ruin the game for me.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a massive horror fan and I've been playing horror games since back in the PS1 days with the original Silent Hill and Resident Evil, and I can unequivocally say that Visage is the scariest game I have ever played. Is it perfect? No, the controls are awkward and the second half of the game doesn't hold quite the same magic as the first half, but despite that the game delivers a kind of consistent horror and cohesive design that so many other games promise but don't deliver. I'm still in awe of how well executed the atmosphere is and it gives me the same feeling of dread that I had playing Silent Hill for the first time. _childDocuments_.review: I've played a plethora of horror games and it's been tough to find a good one recently. Visage shows an EXCELLENT amount of promise. It does horror perfectly, has a compelling story, and looks great doing it. Graphically the game looks very impressive with just the right amount of film grain to add a subtle cinematic feel. Visuals are photo realistic and is similar to an unfortunately cancelled horror game. The gameplay is like a walking sim, but with a bit more engaging gameplay. Managing your sanity through light sources is key. You'll go digging around to find lighters, candles, and a camera flash is a great and eerie way to explore dark areas and the game accents this wonderfully. The story starts with a bang (pun intended) and you'll spend the first chapter figuring out what's going on and I felt myself geniunely curious as to how everything fit together between the themes of the horror elements and the narrative. The drawback is that a lot of the areas are closed for Early Access, however the first chapter is completely available and the game won't let you stray off somewhere only to run into areas that are inaccessible. The game takes awhile to build up the horror elements, but once you met your first paranormal experience, man it's all a roller coaster ride from there. Horror. I hate shrilly cheap scares from games that resort to loud audio noises to be "scary." On the other hand, I hate games that strictly just have a creepy atmosphere, but never any sense of danger. This game was super creepy, great well timed jump scares, but maybe the only thing I didn't like is that if you linger in an area too long, it'll spawn one of the ghosts to kill you. Overall it's not horrible, but it's meh. All in all, great graphics, compelling story, engaging gameplay, great atmosphere, well placed jump scares. It's a great horror game and well worth your time and money!

_childDocuments_.review: I was all over very dissapointed and frustrated with this game due to it's huge missed potential.The main problems of this game come from it's missuse of difficulty that completely ruin the great tension it tries (and rarely succcedes in) building.It has a great setup that evolves and developes in interesting ways, but is ruined time after time by lackluster, clumsy puzzle design that is cyptic (but not in a fun way). It forces the player to navigate areas over and over, which wouldn't be a problem in its self if it were for other reasons than flat out bad game design. It comes to a point where it is immersion breaking due to boredom and frustration with little payoff. The biggest missdirection in my opinion is the use of each chapter's antagonists. They are always introduced and presented as mysterious, menacing entities thanks to some truly great sound design, and terrifying situations. But this is all counteracted by the game's desire to make them actually "dangerous" to the player in a missguided attempt to create stakes. It ends up leading to the complete opposite effect where they become more of a dull, unfair, unballanced, poorly designed nuisance. They will constantly insta kill even the most careful player, in a way that destroys all sense of tension and mystification that the previous buildup created. After seeing each enemy in closeup detail many many times throughout long death animations I no longer feared them and saw them more as an annoyance to avoid solely out of fear of seeing the cheap payoff of them catching me again. I should add that they often seem to appear out of litteraly nowhere right next to you in a way that feels cheap and almost comical (if it wasn't so dull, painfully long and frustrating). Whenever I thought I had worked out some form of pattern for each enemy's movements, player detection and aggro, I always ended up by being crushed by the realisation that there was simply not that amount of thought put into them (or if there was it was so poorly executed that it was as good as useless).All these aweful game design decisions leave me with an all over dreadful, frustrating, tensionless experience. Which is such a shame when paired with all the things the game does really well. it has a really interesting premisse and amazing location and sound, design. but those truly aren't enough to justify the rest of the experience in any way.Sadsquare give the impression of a team of skilled craftsmen who ultimatelly just don't understand horror, nor how to create the effective, tense, mysterious and dread filled game they were aiming for.This one really left me very empty and reminded me how good countless other horror games truly are.It definitely got a visceral reaction out of me, but not a good one.

_childDocuments_.review: First and Foremost, what this game excels in is eerie atmosphere building. It's all Spook City here. Through my first go, anxiety is through the roof with scarce lighting and some well timed "paranormal events" that built me on edge to the point where it seems unbearable. The details of the scenery are well designed.Someone else had pointed out that the influences are too strong on the sleeve here. The beginning was an exact match to walking into the first door of P.T. . The monster's moans are very similar to that of P.T's as well.Being early access, faults are expected.- The handling controls between using the lighter and other objects felt a little clunky/difficult to navigate and use your items with fluidity in my opinion. - The paranormal events happen too frequently and fast. I wouldn't even notice it happened in my surrounding if it wasn't for the constant audio cue, which is overbearing from the event itself.- The sanity gauge is told to negatively affect you but the game doesn't punish you for it. I held myself in dark spaces after exploring to see the reaction yet was meet with nothing to show for. Past that, some phasing objects here and there but that's nothing I'd expect to see in the final cut. While some of these things stuck out for me, I'd be lying if I didn't say I was a nervous wreck the majority of the time. If you're fan of horror, of course you should check this out just in time for Halloween. Could be a little cleaner in mechanics but good for a spookin' I say.

_childDocuments_.review: Visage is a game where you can encounter some genuinely scary events that can be marred by its gameplay. Lucy and Dolores' chapters are the scariest, by far, while the others pale very heavily in comparison. I played back when it was in Early Access and found that the first two chapters mentioned above were very good and promising despite some gameplay elements such as puzzles being a bit too cryptic (though there are very few of those). I would still recommend the game to others simply because it's one of the only PT inspired games that is pretty good outside of it's very abundant and apparent flaws. _childDocuments_.review: Alright, as a person who has been exposed to TONS of psychological horror I can say without a doubt: This experience is not "stupid scary" as some would put it, more "scary stupid". In fact the scariest aspect of the game would be how unpolished and dumb its mechanics are. To start off is the whole mechanic which guarantees your survival, the light/sanity meter. It is a dumb concept, as survival horror is supposed to make the player feel as the victim, this does the exact opposite. The inventory system is a pile of steaming garbo designed by some deranged lunatic that has never heard the word "intuitive".  The items literally do not make sense (lighter light v. candle light) and for survival horror there are too many items lying around; so much that its both gamebreaking and laughable. The monsters are cheap rehashes of J-horror antagonists from at least a decade ago, stupid really. Also the opening cutscene is so try-hard edgy that I almost threw up, its edgier than the one kid in my highschool class that claimed he could swallow razors (complete with mascara, black fingernail polish, Hot Topic, and My Chemical Romance). I saw him for what he was, an attention grabbing loser, which also sums up (in parallel) my opinion of the game.Now an address to the developers. Wow, talk about leaving a polished turd, not finishing it, charging pretty highly for what it is, then somehow managing to deceive the rest of the horror "fans" (check the rest of the reviews on this game, my god, they wouldn't know scary if it shot it's family then itself.) into greedily scarfing down your doo-doo sandwich and calling it "good".  Bravo, on successfully pulling off the most blatant con-job of this decade.Tl;dr:This game is baby-go-waaah levels of scary, its unplayable and its mechanics gamebreaking. I am glad I was able to get it refunded. Also I know there is a lot I missed in this negative review, but its so much a chore to even think about that I cannot take the time to go into any more depth. Do yourself a favor and keep looking for better (albeit more realistically priced) horror experiences, I know I have played excellent and well made horror games which are a fraction of what this costed me.

_childDocuments_.review: After all these years I finally found a good horror game, one that does not rely just on cheap scares but instead messes with you constantly inducing fear and panic slowly. 👍 +Excelent atmosphere.+Great sound design.+Psychologically scary.👎-Ending is garbage.-Rakan chapter doesn't feel as connected to the main story compared to the others.Let's be honest, it's a horror game so don't expect an emotional, detailed, and oscar worthy story, you won't find that here. Instead, you'll find a heavily inspired story from other renowned horror games such as Silent Hill. The first time you start the game it immediately and brutally puts you in the shoes of Dwayne who murders his own family and then kills himself. After that, you somehow reawaken in the house all alone with no task at hand. As you explore you find unique objects which start a chapter. There are 3 main chapters and each tells the story of previous tenants that live in your house and their tragic story. When I say tell, it's mostly through visual horror and you just have to deduce what happened to them as you reach the end of each chapter. There's no order in which you have to play these chapters so feel free to start with whichever item you find first. Lucy, Dolores, and Rakan are the 3 main chapters with the 4th being, what I'm assuming, the present where you are situated in time before starting a chapter. Lucy and Dolores's ones are really nice and extremely frightening to experience, and they somewhat feel attached to your character and the house more than Rakans who honestly feels very disconnected and kinda pointless as most of the action in that chapter takes place in an asylum. It's also the least scary of them all. I won't go into detail to avoid spoilers but as you complete all the chapters and find the final object to end the game, you are booted to a credits scene with no explanation whatsoever and that's it. It was sh*t. No nicer way to say it. One can guess what happened but honestly, it felt incredibly rushed and way too "happy"? If you can even call it that. Story rating: 7.5/10Visage is a first-person puzzle/exploration horror game, where you're tasked with, surviving, investigating, and solving several exploration puzzles, all of this while being mind ♥♥♥*ed by the game. What I mean by that is, as you explore the house and whatnot, whether you're in the chapters or outside of them, the game slowly builds panic into your soul by handling objects around the house, such as closing doors behind you, turning on the radio, etc. Those small cheap scares are just the beginning of the nightmare as you being a chapter the environment changes more or less and you slowly descend into horror and oh boy there are a lot of scary moments, especially in the Dolores and Lucy chapters. If you have some form of phobia against scary little girls and old ladies then be warned as you will get chased, haunted, and scared the living hell out of you. The Rakan chapter while it has its scary moments some crippled nut job did not have much effect on me. Avoiding the monsters in that chapter was pretty easy. Besides exploration and surviving you'll have to solve and figure out a pretty big number of environmental puzzles, more so in the Dolore chapter, a lot more so. Half the game is probably spent on that chapter alone and it's quite hard. Imagine being stressed by not knowing what to do while in the meantime being stalked, and messed around by the horrors around you. It's definitely not for the faint of hearts. I really loved the Dolores chapter and Lucy as well but sadly the quality suddenly dropped immensely in the Rakan one. The game was in early access for many years and it's a clear indication that whoever worked in the previous two chapters was no longer a part of the final one or they just didn't bother anymore. A shame really, as this could've been an incredible experience completely but instead it falters in the final hours.Gameplay rating: 8/10A horror game is nothing without a good sound design and luckily Visage does a good job at creating an eerie and scary atmosphere. It's not filled with aggressive and loud spammy sound effects like other weak horror games. Instead, it relies on a quieter environment with small sounds here and there slowly crawling into your ears. The same thing applies to the music, there's barely any songs in the game but when the tension rises you'll hear it and you'll dread it. It's simple but effective. As for voice acting, there are some well-voiced characters in the game, especially Dolores and your neighbor among others so overall I have no complaints regarding the audio. Well done.Audio rating: 8.5/10Yes, visually the game did take some inspiration from PT, Silent Hil, and some other horror games but it's far from being just a cheap copy. The game looks gorgeous as hell. The house is filled with so many details and the way the story is presented most of the time visually is also a nice factor. The models, the scary ones, also look scary as hell and quite gruesome. Sadly the animations are not as good and most of the actions you do are with invisible hands and legs and you just float around the objects you use. What the hell were they really doing all these years in early access? Anyway, the level design is fantastic as well and you will backtrack a lot so if that's an issue for you, this game might not be for you. The house is the main protagonist of the game and while you may reach other places they're all bound to the house. The house has many secrets so make sure to watch the tapes after each chapter. As for performance I had no problems running the game maxed at 1440p on a 2080. There were some small bugs here and there but nothing that hampered my experience. Graphics, performance and tech analysis score:  8/10It's good to have finally found a nice horror game. I haven't felt stressed and scared while playing in many years and while certainly, the final parts are not so good, overall the game is a great horror and I highly recommend it at any price.

_childDocuments_.review: 9/10 for me! One of the best horror games I have played for a very long while. A few gameplay issues and little things stopped this being a 10.My favourite things about the game:•	Overwhelming sense of suspense around every corner.•	Dark and eerie rooms.•	The amazing story.•	In depth character story and lore.•	Well created map and different environments are awesome to explore and learn about.•	Inventory management is a cool mechanic in the game, kind of feels like RE games.Things that are kind of meh:•	The controls are a bit frustrating at times.•	Unavoidable deaths at times.•	A bit of lack of information at the start of the game.•	Character feels annoyingly slow for someone who is being chased by spooky blokes.Things that really sucked:•	The pause menu still leaves the game running in the background, so no respite when trying to solve puzzles etc.•	HAVING A BORDERLINE HEART ATTACK WHEN A HEAD PEERS AROUND THE CORNER ☹Just some info for new players. A lot of people have said about the game not giving much information, this is true the game DOES NOT spell out how to complete it and how to do the multiple puzzles and tasks. This is a pro for some and a con for others. I found it to be okay once i got into the grove of the game but was very confused at the start. But I will say please bare with it if you can as it is so worth it.The area’s in the game are there for you to explore every nook and cranny of and find out more regarding this grim and extremely unsettling story.TL/DR: This game is awesome and if you are a dedicated horror game fan then you should definitely purchase this game, but just be aware this game is challenging and it’s up to you to solve everything as nothing will be explained.

_childDocuments_.review: Over the past year, I have almost exclusively played indie horror games. Visage was one of the first games I purchased on that journey. I can say that I probably tried a different game weekly and have become immune to the tropes and scare tactics, I love the horror genre, but good horror is hard to find. Visage is the scariest game on steam. It deftly wields every tool at its disposal as a weapon on your psyche, It borders on the cusp of an interactive nightmare.  Very few games since or  before it's release are capable of inducing a similar sense of fear and unease, and I recommend it to anyone remotely interested.

_childDocuments_.review: I just want to start with, after 4.5 hours of gameplay (enjoyable horror gameplay, coming from a horror fanatic) my entire game was wiped by the developers themselves because of a botched update. (it makes me anxious it'll happen again)Regardless of that though...This game is very fun, for the most part (I'm at a part now in which FEAR has worn off, the old lady keeps popping up every 4-5 minutes and it's more irritating, like I'm playing HOME SWEET HOME). It's very horrific, some things happen such as walking around, you turn around and there is someone looking round a corner, in silence and just hides away. It's a creepy psychological horror, people standing in bottom of the hall way staring at you. The sound effects throughout what I've done is amazing, especially when lights just flick off, and the sounds of floor boards creeking making you feel someone is always behind you or near you. I found the insanity a little too easy, it's very hard to go insane, which I guess is a good thing, considering I hate not being able to explore much or being afraid to try certain things incase I go mad and start "LOSING MY ♥♥♥♥ AHHHHHAHAHAHAH" *takes pills*One thing I did hate, is if you ever get lost or stuck on what needs to be done (hardly happens) but there is no objective or hint or anything really towards a goal. If you forget aswell which portal goes where, you run around the house looking for it, it's especially irritating when the lights go COMPLETELY off and you're running around in pitch darkness with a little lighter, trying to find the right door.It's a very creepy and good horror game, a unique horror with things that get you by avoiding some stereotypical predictable horror moves horror games do these days. Aside from the very irritating mistake the developers made by erasing your saves, and eventually the old woman constantly chasing you, it's a fun game, a very long roaded game rather than cut into pieces. I'd recommend it... so far only on discount though

_childDocuments_.review: So far, this game definitely lives up to the hype, though I'm finding a lot of issues with the interface that make it feel very early-access. As another reviewer mentioned, the candles are really confusing. Their time limit feels almost random and arbitrary, and god help you if you don't have the lighter on the entire time the candle is going, otherwise it will last around 3 seconds. Another issue I had is that the candles aren't handled in the same manner as the lighter, and you can't move doors and interact with objects as long as a candle is lit and you are holding it. While I did manage to make a rhythm for it (drop candle, open door/activate object, open lighter, light candle, pick up candle, pocket lighter, repeat), it felt more like a game bug than a difficulty setting.The inventory system overall is confusing, and items such as lighters, pills, candles, and lightbulbs, which I've found are in abundance, should be stacked so as to avoid clutter, particularly since when a lighter dies, it has to be replaced anyway and can't be refilled. It might also be beneficial for a lighter in that stack to auto-drop once it runs out (I wasn't sure if it already did, but I had moments where a lighter would drop and still have fuel in it). Games like Amnesia and Layers do this quite well, so that might be something to borrow from. Also, having 6 hotkeys for a single item, when we're only going to use 2 or 3 of them is quite excessive (2-4 keys for rotating an object when you can do most of it with your mouse). The hotkeys themselves are also weird and feel random and poorly-thought out, so could be good to borrow from other similar horror games for those as well (click and drag for opening doors instead of E and mouse movement). Also when picking up essential items, you should be able to click out of the explanation of them if you already get the idea (if I restart a section, I know how lightbulbs operate, I don't want to click around desperately to get out of the "Lightbulbs: here's how they work" window).Another thing that felt very tedious and detrimental to gameplay was the key system. Either have one key open a single door and have the other doors beyond that would use the same key unlocked, or change the system so the door automatically unlocks with the key in your inventory. Having to fumble with the keys (of which the key icons and many of the menu settings were offset so I had to click farther to the right and far lower than the icon/option for it to highlight, though that could just be my wonky screen resolution settings), while creating a sense of urgency, began to feel tedious and like a gameplay bug, especially when I've already opened the basement door and there are five doors beyond it that use the same key. You also probably shouldn't be able to drop a key, because I had to reload while trying to figure out how to unlock a door (the highlighting of the basement key was offset and I accidentally dropped it and it vanished).When it comes to story and atmosphere, however, this game excels, the tension and dread was palpable from the first cutscene, and felt relentless, which made the UI feel even more detrimental while fumbling with it and meanwhile trying to experience all that Visage had to offer. That said, the optimization is pretty great, I have an average-at-best build, and it ran smooth as butter on the highest of settings, with only slight fps drops that I didn't even really notice.TL;DR: rearranging and getting rid of some hotkeys, streamlining some of the UI, and just polishing that all up would go a very very long way into solidifying this as one of the best horror games out there right now, and I can't wait to play the final release.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been an owner of the game since the early access and have been waiting to leave a review until the full official release of the game.  Now that time has come, I'm very happy to be able to recommend this to others looking for a genuinely scary, atmospheric horror game!  Clearly inspired by PT (and thank god, we need more good psychological horror), Visage pulls no punches off the bat.  One of the most atmospheric games I've ever played, I feel uneasy just walking around the house in-game, let alone when things start getting really terrifying.  I generally don't get scared by most horror games anymore, but this games scares the hell out of me.  It excels in creating anxious moments full of tension, and capitalizing on them when you least expect it.  If you're looking for a slow-burn, melancholy horror experience, you'll find it here.No game is perfect though!  Sometimes the item-management controls can feel clunky ("I just want to drop this stupid beer can!") and there appear to be some bugs ("I just opened this door and now one of my pill bottles is gone?") but the pros strongly outweigh these issues.  Congrats to the devs in pressing through to get Visage officially released.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is definitely good it focuses in on atmosphere and the jump scares are for the most part really timed out well so at it's current state 20-25 bucks for the game is a really good deal in my opinion the graphics are amazing and the scares are pretty good and I would definitely recommend this game for anyone looking for a good horror game.Now for my gripes about the game. The mechanics are a little confusing some if not most of the time it terms of your psychological meter (your brain meter) is a little confusing to understand in terms of understanding when it's being affected ex ; when you're losing sanity or when you're gaining it back. There's no clear indicator on what counts as enough light and when you sanity is dropping besides a brain feeling in and the constant reminder tip at the bottom of the screen that lighters are not helping sanity or that sanity is decreasing fast even when sometimes you'll be standing directly under a light source. Not to say a tip bar for each indicator is the solution but I don't know make it apart of the game where if you're losing sanity you start hearing whispers louder and louder not too obnoxiously loud  but like they're getting closer and when you find a light source they start to back off not to say that is the solution but just an idea. Which follows into my next gripe is the tip bar. Now for the beginning of the game  would say the tip bar is kinda useful but after a hour or two of playing the tip bars get obnoxious and take the immersion out of the game. A possible solution to not needing the tip bars so often for the same tips over and over is to make items like the lighter when it starts to lose fuel instead of getting a tip for it every time to make it flicker on or die out so that it indicates that it's losing fuel. And lastly the predictability of the scares. This game does scares really really well up until the end I was still getting scared. BUT after a couple hours you kind of get a sense of what's a threat and when that threat is coming and easily get away from it enough to where you don't have to worry about it. A suggestion is to add them silently in and since a big focus with the game is to listen to the environment to them sliding their feet across the floor towards you or scratching or something.These are only suggestions so take what I say with a grain of salt. I really enjoyed this game and definitely recommend this game to anyone looking for a really well executed game even given it's flaws you can really see the heart put into this game and I hope to see more for these developers.If you would like to check out my game play of it  look up DanniPai Gaming.

_childDocuments_.review: The good- Nice visuals with good graphics quality and mostly cool atmospheric lighting. Some regions that are very artistic and worth hitting that screenshot button.- It has some interesting gameplay mechanisms like the walkie talkie and the compass. They are pretty refreshing and fun, but also inconsistent and don't last long.- Dolores chapter has good structure and pace. The house gets transformed into a big puzzle full of mysteries. Unfortunately the rest of the game gets pretty linear with less creative mechanisms and questionable decisions.- If you like to explore every corner of a game for hidden secrets and collectables this is a game for you. It can get pretty tiring though when you don't know what you are looking for.- Initially it has a calm, sick, dark atmosphere that makes it really scary. Unfortunately after some hours tons of silly jump scares, and cheap tricks ruin it.- The fact that you play the game using daily life objects, like lighters and candles is a nice choice and makes it more scary. You don't always need to be the super human that runs and guns everything.- Cool enemies. They're nothing unique for sure, but they're creepy enough to give you some chills.- If you like splatter scenes, well, it has a lot of them. They tend to be pretty cliché though.The bad- Very bad puzzles' logic and structure. The player doesn't feel like having a purpose to fulfil and this is mainly related with the random outcome of each puzzle and the fact that they seem like not actually supporting a storyline based on a series of logical actions. You can anticipate most of the staff you have to do in order to solve the puzzles, but what comes after it seems random. For example you see only one slipper on the bed, so it's easy to understand that you have to pick the second one from the floor, but the result of doing this is to open a door. You end up doing things casually because they are there but without knowing why. The story moves forward when you solve a puzzle but has no real connection to it. There is no logical series of events. It's like they initially designed some cool puzzles and threw them inside a house without minding that all these are actions of an actual plot. You just explore solving puzzles while lights turn out and creepy things scare you. Also, in many occasions it doesn't give you enough clues for the next puzzle. It gets transformed into a "spot the difference" game that forces you to endlessly circle around the house trying to figure out what has changed.- It doesn't have a specific design language neither a consistent horror concept. It's like they just threw in there every cheap, worn trick that they came up with. Dolls, little girls in white dresses, hanged bodies, faceless people, optical distortions, rotten rooms, trails of blood, flickering lights, random screams, babies' cry, creaks coming from nowhere, doors shutting by themselves,  scary music turning up mostly for no reason and of course tons of silly jump scares. Even an Esser's painting is in there to indicate the protagonist's mental complexity. Too easy and cliché . A horror theme park just to impress.- Awkward controls and tons of glitches. Interactions are messy. Opening doors and wardrobes is slow and problematic. Examining and rotating objects is clunky. The tools that you carry and are floating in front of you (yes, there are no hands) get into other objects' geometry. In narrow passages they tent to get stuck and left behind you. When carrying big objects you cannot see where to go. There are many completely dark regions, that you're not allowed to use your lighter for some reason. You end up doing circles without knowing where to go. Some scripted events get triggered with much delay so you just stand for a while wandering what to do next. Running is annoyingly slow.- The sanity meter, that it is supposed to drop when being in dark for long periods is inconsistent. Sometimes it drops, others not. A core gameplay feature that doesn't give you accurate feedback is one of the most annoying things in gaming for me.- For some reason it allows you to carry only one "key" tool. You have to go to the storage room every time you wanna equip a different one with a result of adding a few more hours of pointless wandering around the house.- Except of the Dolores' chapter, that has some creative ideas, all the others are pretty linear and force you mainly to search for keys, exits and locked doors while scripted encounters happen around you.

_childDocuments_.review: ***Initial Review: Read the edit below it***I picked up this game after hearing that it was a very good horror experience with strong P.T. vibes. What you do get is pretty good. The house is unnerving, the sanity effects are ominous, and the current/only monster is creepy as hell, both in the way it looks, as well as the way it moves around and disappears. It's all quite tense.However, there is, and has continued to be a general lack of content. I was under the impression that the game was mostly complete as the page seemed to suggest they only planned on having the game in early access for four months while they finalized the rest of the content. Well, I completed all available content in ~1 1/2 hours ( note that what you see in the screenshots for the game is not representative of what is available, and I'm not sure how much of it will actually be in the final release ) and  many months later and there still hasn't been any content update to the game.This wouldn't be a problem if they perhaps communicated progress through the updates on their steam page. I went as far as going to the Kickstarter, though I am decidedly not one of the backers, to see if there were updates there. Nothing. The most recent update was an update updating the users on how sorry they were for not updating them more often and promising more updates and saying things were being finalized. I also learned that this game had some pretty lofty expectations initially, but didn't raise enough money to reach them ( i.e. multiple endings at 160K, some surprise at 250K , and the game taking place in a town at 1M. It only reached 120K).Now as of current the game feels like a very good demo, but nothing more. I understand why the community would be upset as the estimated delivery date on Kickstarter was 2017, the steam page suggested the full game would be ready sometime early 2019 and now as of mid 2019, there is still only one of three chapters available with no real estimate as to when the second or third will be complete and how much content it will add. It feels dead in the water.For these reasons I am giving it a negative review which is subject to change if and when more content is made available.***EDIT***About two weeks after posting this I was informed that new content was available. At this point I've played through the new content after having started a new game and running back through Lucy's story. If you're observant and don't miss to many items, then you'll get about an hour and a half of additional content  in Dolores chapter. If you're prone to missing stuff and or are a completionist, then there's around 2-3 hours of additional content. This puts the game at around ~3-4 of content currently.While I do like the new chapter, I don't think it's as good as the first. For one the monster/ghost for this chapter isn't nearly as horrific to look at. That's not to say it wasn't creepy, but it wasn't nearly as disturbing as the first. There are a few more jump scares than Lucys chapter and quite a few more Layers of Fear-esque visual gags and general gross out portions of the chapter that are kind of reminiscent of Agony ( you'll know when you get there ), but at no point was I quite as afraid of being caught by the monster. In fact, I felt pretty safe throughout the chapter as there are certain rooms that Dolores wont cross and always contains light so if my sanity started dipping lower than I'd like I could just run in and crouch in the light for a little bit. That and unlike Lucys chapter, the house lights are, for the most part, always available so I didn't get the same sense of urgency or foreboding as I did with the Lucy chapter.While I do appreciate that additional content was added, it's not as much as some people are claiming or as much as one might expect from almost an additional year of development, nor was it as polished as one might expect. There are quite a few visual and what appears to be physics bugs in this chapter. It is early access though so hopefully these will be fixed on the final release or sometime before the next chapter is released. While I'm a tad bit disappointed with the new chapter, I'm going to change my review to positive because I am glad that the developers did not abandon the project like it seemed they were going to and the game is getting closer to feeling like a full game rather than a demo.

_childDocuments_.review: In 2014 I played through Silent Hill P.T. with some friends. We found it terribly unpleasant. Visage is very reminiscent of P.T. The house in Visage has an extremely eerie setting. The lighting is perfect. Visage succeeds well in building up an unpleasant atmosphere, before all hell breaks loose. Me, my brother, and two friends played through the game on a 100 inch projector screen with surround sound in a pitch black room. We really got the best horror experience you can get from this game. Visage has many panic-inducing moments and very good jump scares, and nothing feels cheap.The story in Visage is okey, and the voice actors weren't very good. Visage has 3 main chapters and a chapter that kind of takes place before, between and after those 3 main chapters. You can choose which of the 3 main chapters you want to start with by finding and interacting with the respective item that starts that particular chapter. We started with Dolores' chapter, then Lucy's chapter, and finally Rakan's chapter. I would recommend another order than the order we did it in. Start with Rakan's chapter because it's the least scary chapter and also the shortest, as well as it takes place in a different place than the house you start in. Rakan's chapter wasn't that interesting story-wise either. Then move on to Dolores's chapter, and finally Lucy's chapter. We definitely thought Lucy's chapter was the scariest.We played with mouse and keyboard, and yet the controls were a bit awkward and it took a while to get used to. Mostly because you can have an item in each hand, and we always had to think at first which hand we wanted to use or if we needed to use an item with both hands at the same time, such as a sledgehammer. Items that require you to use both hands cannot be saved in the inventory, so you have to drop it, and if you walk away from it, it goes back to your cabinet in the basement, which is your storage. This became very complicated and tedious during Dolores' chapter, because several of the house's doors get chains on them so you can't take the usual way down to the basement. We had to take a much longer and unnecessarily more complicated route every damn time we needed the sledgehammer again. They should patch this in my opinion. Either by designing a new route to the basement during this chapter, or by adding more storage cabinets throughout the house. Regardless of chapter, they should add another storage cabinet in the upper part of the house.We also found it very difficult to know where to go or what the objective was. The game is not very good at guiding the player. It's also possible to pick up almost every single thing in the house and put in your inventory. Things that you don't even need or have any use for, you can take with you, for example empty soda cans. Why? This only confuses the player and is unnecessary.Despite some small flaws, Visage is a fantastic horror game. Ever since we played Silent Hill P.T. we've been dying to play a similar game, as we were so disappointed that Silent Hill P.T. was canceled. Visage is the game we've been waiting for, even if it took us 7 years after release to get around to playing it. It was probably a good thing we waited anyway, until they finished Visage, since it was in Early Access for a while. There is more content now than on its release. We had nightmares and trouble sleeping after playing this game, especially me, as it took me several days to recover mentally, which is a good rating for a horror game!If you are also looking for a really scary horror game similar to Silent Hill P.T. then Visage is the game for you. 9/10.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are looking for an actual scary game that doesn't hold your hand whatsoever, pick this up. I have played countless horror games, if you picked a random one that's worth its salt, I have probably either watched it in its entirety or played it myself. I cannot stress enough that this game's status in the horror genre surpasses any other I've played, and gives other well-known games like the Outlast series a run for their money. The game has four to five chapters, depending on how you look at it, to play through. With the first two being easily the scariest to complete. Although the following two are scary in their own right, they mainly serve as a progression in the story, having more (intense) environmental horror scenes than jump scares. The jump scares that do occur throughout the game can either be effective throughout the story's progression, or they are just initially scary and then end up becoming annoying, especially in the chase sequences or if you end up stuck. There are two ways I would suggest playing this game depending on the desired experience:1. Playing the game as it was made without external help is massively challenging in multiple aspects, and in my opinion, becomes immensely more scary to get through. I say this because you will definitely become confused, stuck, and without a sense of direction at some point or another. At which you will progressively lose your sanity, and start to visualize more hallucinations of the demons prowling in the dark. The demons can and will kill you, but the way to remedy this is by taking the pills lying around the house. It is important to note though that there is a finite amount of materials in the house that don't respawn after each chapter, I would have liked to have known that before I took all of the pills in the house prior to even beginning chapter 4. When playing without assistance, you are going to see some freaky stuff, but good luck getting through some of the chapters in doing so.2. The second way to play this game is to have a walk-through for it open while you are playing. There are still plenty of effective jump scares, especially if you are following the guides loosely and are at least attempting to get through it on your own. Perhaps only using the guide as an objective marker would serve best in balancing the game to avoid spoilers of potential scares to come.Overall, I highly recommend this game to anyone who is a fan of the horror genre, particularly if you enjoy intensely horrifying, immersive, mind-bending, story games. I suppose one of the things I liked the most about this game was that all the stories told, including the alleged protagonist, connect in an overarching way, that is if you pay attention to the finer details in every scene and piece of evidence you find.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall. I'd rate it 7/10 out of all games I've ever played, and a 9/10 among horror games.Visage follows the style of PT and delivers what could PT have been. One of the scariest (and thus best) horror games ever made. Especially the chapters already released in the early access, "Lucy" and "Dolores", convince with interesting puzzles and gruesome threats. The full release adds two new chapters which fall behind a little, but are nonetheless very well done and tell interesting stories.Is the game flawless? No. One might argue that most puzzles boil down to "find key, open door, go forward, repeat", the notable exception being the "Dolores" chapter. Especially in the "fourth" chapter you'll find yourself wandering around for hours, searching for the missing item... you'll die many times, and if something kills you too often, it stops being scary and becomes annoying. Also, I had some technical issues. I fell into a void twice when going through a door and regularly, the graphics wouldn't properly load, making the game look like it was made in 2001. My pc is not a potato, but it might still be a problem on my side. I don't know.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think the game is all bad. The grandma chapter was enjoyable to play, original and good at guiding you from one item to the next. You really have no idea what to do or where to go most of the game.It's a bummer that the scarier parts are pretty much ripoffs of PT and Silent Hill, without nearly as much impact or meaning. The imagery too. Wheelchairs, umbilical cords, chained doors, a creature emerging from a stain on the wall, blurry spinning heads, all copies from Silent Hill.The grandma chapter was pretty much the only time it felt like they were trying something original.Not a total waste of time, but not as good as people claim this to be.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could choose a neutral recommendation for this one. Firstly, fantastic ambiance, setting, visuals, sound design, all that jazz. Unfortunately all that is really held back by the gameplay. The hand system and two inventory system is funky to get used to but not a deal breaker, the sanity system I feel is unnecessary and really takes away from the moment, and I spent all my playtime wondering what it was the game wanted me to do even though i'm just one chapter done so far. For instance: in one chapter i'm supposed to avoid flickering lights and spooky sounds because it means i'm about to die from something invisible, but at the same time the game cues me into where to go in the big maze of a house by guiding me with, you guessed it, flickering lights and spooky sounds. Is it where I need to go or sudden death? Who knows? Half the time when I died I didn't know why, and upon reloading and doing the exact same things I would be fine. The sanity system is a steep slope that's hard to climb out of to boot. I loaded up some auto saves after dying only to be instantly killed by an invisible entity a second later I didn't know how to run from. When your sanity gets dangerously low you need pills, but they're super hard to find if you have no lights which you probably don't if your sanity is low in the first place. I feel like I can't take the time to feel spooked either because i'm only worried about my sanity level. I would really really like to enjoy this game and appreciate its magnificent ambiance and get spooked but the gameplay keeps interrupting the fun and replacing it with confusion and comedic untimely deaths instead. Maybe the other chapters are different and I just started out with a bad one, but so far the good in the game is really being held back by the bad. It's not a bad game at all, it just has a few design choices that really step on and cover up what's special about it.

I played Visage. This game was by far the scariest game I've ever played. I was on edge the ENTIRE time. I felt like I was about to ♥♥♥♥ my pants several times. I had a huge sense of dread throughout the whole game and was even sweating lol because I was so scared. Definitely check out this masterpiece, it will not disappoint!   10/10

_childDocuments_.review: For me, the etalon of horror is Silent Hill 2. Never ever played a game which gave me that kind of scare... until now. Visage is the game we horror fans were waiting for! The atmosphere is just amazingly terrifying, everything looks beautiful and detailed. You just feel so alone and helpless walking around. The sounds... Damn, the sounds are perfect! Especially the sound of the ghost, which has those big nails is so scary, that when I heard it first I got shocked, I was like oh my god, what now? What the hell is this? And then I got killed. If Death makes a sound, when he comes for you, that should be it.I loved the parts where you had to think, look around, or remember for older places where you've been. The game plays with your mind in a way like no other game does. You even get scared when browsing the settings menu, because everything happens in real time. The whole house is haunted, paranormal events happen everywhere, and can happen anytime. No event happens twice in the same place, they are not scripted, which I found damn amazing. You'll always feels paranoia wandering around... Oh, and it's pretty long for one chapter (it will have 4), tho I like searching every cm.Some small graphical glitches here and there, but the 1st chapter is 100% doable, you even get achievements.I recommend this game for all horror fans, it's an absolute 10/10 in the genre! The best horror game in many years, can't wait for Chapter 2, and for the whole game!

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to recommend it for people who like scary-type games. It hits that part pretty well, with nice chase scenes, a very dark atmosphere, plenty of jump-scares as well as non-jump-scare scares.And i just want to say: i read several reviews for this game on steam, and one of the reviews complained about the hospital level, which confused me - that's probably my favorite level in this whole game, the only level that really got my adrenaline pumping. Which leads me to think that person didn't vary their tactics for parts of the game, leading to constant death? That's all i can figure. I enjoyed that level, though, personally. That all said... There are some very serious issues with this game. First, of course, bugs: the biggest bug i ran into had the game seem to not recognize where i was, and kept having me crawl through a wall, even though i had gotten out of that wall, until the game just yeeted me out of the whole game area. And to make matters worse, i couldn't even hit the escape button to exit the game or load a previous save. I literally had to task manager that to exit out. That was the biggest bug, there were some minor ones with random floating things, but overall, it wasn't bad enough to make me hate the game for it. And, after I got back on after that one bug, i was able to progress without issue. My biggest complaint, though, has to be the non-existent story. You start out in a room, where a truly tragic incident occurs, and then wake up in, what i assume is, your house... only, weird things are going on in your house. And then, for absolutely no known reason, you have to learn about the lives of others... well, not really their life, but their downfall... I have no idea who those people are or why i have to learn about them. The game gives no real information to anything, at all... You can certainly piece together things and make assumptions, EVENTUALLY, but in the beginning, you're just like, "i have no idea what's going on or why. Why am i doing this? Who am i? Oh, someone seems to like a lot of beer i guess???" and still, even after you beat the game, you will still not really have a clue what's TRULY going on or why you had to do everything you did. Finally, i do want to touch base on the "puzzles." You will, on more than one occasion, find yourself having no idea what to do. To this i say to you: just keep meandering around and clicking on things. Eventually you'll just happen upon whatever it is you needed to touch, or click on, or open, or whatever. Very few hints, but at least the game is linear enough to mostly force you into a specific direction, you just need to find that item that pushes the game forward.So, as long as you don't care about knowing about anything, and just want a scary-ish game to play... yeah, play it. I mean, despite the lack of story (which really does annoy me), i still mostly had fun playing the game.

_childDocuments_.review: It'd be scary if it wasn't so much of a pixel hunt. After the initial bit, I'm running around looking for clues WISHING for a new jump-scare, because that'll tell me I'm at least making progress. They said the game was hard, but really it's just confusing, which makes for a frustratingly boring horror experience.The best scares are in cinematic set pieces when you're moving forward, not through gameplay. For example, when your sanity is low, there's not much you can do except die, reset and continue searching for the next clue. This turns the sanity feature into a nuisance rather than a scare, because it's entirely out of your control (remember: You're often just running around in circles trying to find the specific strand they want you to find in a large series of clues). It's become "You didn't know where we wanted you to go fast enough, load save" rather than building up tension and making you feel chased. It needs to be slower with more buildup, and the ghosts need to not jump-scare kill you instantly. And more importantly, there really needs to be more clues as to what's the intended goal or not.Play until you get stuck, then use a guide. There's some wild typical adventure game moon logic in some puzzles. With a guide for the stupid puzzles, it'd be a good horror game with a great setup but not much payoff.

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the most terrifying game I have played to date, and I don't think it will be topped anytime soon. _childDocuments_.review: The only game to even COME CLOSE to capturing how I felt about P.T.Very scary and interesting, very few problems.Love pretty much everything about it save a few fairly minor gripes that are probably just due to it's early access state. Assignable controlls is a MUST for any PC game, and I feel like we could really use a sensitivity slider exclusively for opening and closing doors, dressers, drawers, etc. While I had no problems using a controller, it wasn't nearly as sensitive as I'd want it to be while using my mouse and keyboard. My only other real complaint would have to be (*SPOILERS*??) the evil entity ghost thing that chases you. It wasn't very scary, due in large part to poor animation.I guess if I wanted to get REALLY nitpicky I would say that some of the writting was a little clunky and the voice acting a little hammy. name: Freedom Planet 2
detailed_description: Join the heroes of Avalice as they face their greatest challenge yet! An ancient terror has emerged from the depths of the ocean. Merga, a water dragon from Avalice's oldest and deadliest war, has been freed from her crystal prison as a consequence of the Kingdom Stone's destruction. War is imminent once again, but this time, the heroes are split between sides. As friendships are tested, will the girls stand united when Bakunawa rises? Features Four playable characters available from the start, each with her own unique fighting style: Lilac the Dragon (Speed Type), Carol the Wildcat (Brawler Type), Milla the Hound (Explorer Type), and Neera the Frost Knight (Power Type). Explore the world of Avalice in Adventure mode. Travel through a sprawling world map filled with treasures, landmarks, and over 100 unique animal NPCs to interact with and catalog. Dive straight into the action with Classic Mode. Accessible after completing Adventure mode once, this streamlined navigation screen gives you quick access to stages and other important features without the need for travelling. Test your fighting skills in the Battlesphere arena. Once reached, the Battlesphere hosts a variety of challenges featuring enemies and bosses you've previously encountered, along with brand new surprises! Parry enemy attacks with the new Guard button. If timing's not your thing, an Auto Guard option in the Assist settings makes your character automatically guard against attacks if possible. A new Revival system gives you a chance to clinch victory during very close battles. Use it wisely - it costs a stock and two more hits will knock you out again! Power up your heroine with customizable potions. Collect and mix a rainbow of ingredients that boost her vitality in different ways, such as increasing her stock count, shield durability, attack power, speed, and more. Change the rules with a multitude of equippable items. Amulets and Charms provide helpful effects, while Brave Stones make combat harder in exchange for bonus crystals.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not good at writing detailed reviews, so this is all I'm gonna say.In a world dominated by sprawling open world games with realistic graphics, this humble retro platformer managed to keep my anticipation for it higher than anything else for the 6 years I was waiting for its release. And you know what? It's already worth it. Highly recommend it whether you're already a fan of the first game or if you're new to the series because it delivers the same fast paced, incredibly fun gameplay of the first game with vast graphical improvements, *many* new features, quality of life improvements, and of course, the new story.Hats off to GalaxyTrail for setting a fine example for the gaming industry. It took a long time, far longer than even they anticipated, but they used that time to make sure they delivered a quality game to the fans.It's really nice to be back in Avalice.
_childDocuments_.name: Freedom Planet 2

_childDocuments_.review: Freedom Planet 2 is like Freedom Planet but with more Freedom. And more Planet. And more good.It's good.Go play it.EDIT: I have fully completed Freedom Planet 2, so here's some more in-depth opinions.The game is very fun, and the story is a wonderful improvement over the last game. It's also an improvement over the last one in basically every relevant fashion. But it's not perfect, and my criticisms mainly come in the form of two areas.1. The S rank system. The way the HUD presents it is confusing, as it makes it appear that collecting gems is actually important for getting them when it's exclusively about that multiplier. In addition, the entire challenge is completely ruined by three bravestones - Expensive Stocks, No Revives, and No Stocks, as getting the S ranks requires not dying with two brave stones equipped (or not taking damage with one brave stone/no items equipped, but that's far more difficult as-is), and these brave stones quite literally only punish you for dying rather than actually making the run more difficult. I would suggest a rebalancing of the multiplier bonus you get from the various bravestones to make the others more appealing to use.2. Neera. Lilac is fun to play and a surprising powerhouse, Carol is my favourite to play as and feels even better than FP1, and Milla remains an amazing character locked behind needing good skill to access, but Neera feels lacking in comparison. Her mobility options are poor as they require utilising enemies and the floor to make use of, making most of them completely unattractive to use, Focus conflicts with the intended purpose of Guard, forcing you to choose between avoiding damage or conserving your Energy for where you need it, and in actual combat her attacks are close range and precise but don't deal quite enough damage to make up for that finicky precision, despite being labelled as the brawler character.That being said, this game is still absolutely amazing, and the 8 years of development have most definitely been worth it!

_childDocuments_.review: Hard to find anything Freedom Planet 2 doesn't do that greatly improves over the first game.Everything about the sequel is DAMN good, from the gameplay and visuals to the music. Mix that all together, throwing in a fourth playable character while also enhancing upon the pre-existing trio from FP1, and you got yourself an extremely solid platformer that'll bring back those ol' Treasure vibes.I'll always be thankful to Sabrina and the team over at GalaxyTrail for not only gracing us with an absolute banger of an indie title, but also bringing this wonderful game to fruition at a particularly rough point in my life and indirectly helping me push my way into a better spot. Much love to you guys!

_childDocuments_.review: Look at this absolute unit of an action platforming game.Look at this enormous chunker-on-a-bone with over 25 fully-fledged levels. Each different than the last.Look at this thick behemoth of a production values, outclassing everything in its genre.Yep! That’s Freedom Planet: The Second: Electric Boogaloo baby. First game is still to this day an incredible benchmark of quality for 2D action platformers and straight out of the gate I can say that most of the good qualities you could attribute to that game, apply to the sequel 1:1. Sequel retained it's identity as a high-speed joyride: mixing gameplay mechanics from multiple sources (mostly Sonic, Mega Man X and Gunstar Heroes), that are delivered with excellent feeling controls, creative gimmicks and stages, jaw-dropping setpieces and multiple characters to choose from with vastly different playstyles.Freedom Planet 2 never ever drops down from a set baseline of quality at any given moment and despite few minor flaws or disappointments (in comparison to the first game), it maintains a package of speed and solid quality that could go through military grade blast doors.Improvements over the first game include a higher fidelity graphics which exchange Genesis charm of the first game for the gorgeous details and colors of Hi-Bit aesthetics, which is awe inducing in multiple places. All playable girls each got themselves major or minor changes to streamline their gameplay plus new 4th hero joins the fray with difficult but definitely unique playstyle.Game also addresses most of the common complaints from the first game. Bosses are still tough as nails, but this time not only I didn’t encounter any mishaps with missing telegraphs or unfair moves, but also a new item system was put in place that helps you modulate the amount of pain you can induce on yourself. This system is incredibly flexible and shall you look for either smooth sailing or ultra-nightmare experience, you can set up those pretty easily.Story is also a good improvement over the first game, especially when it comes to pacing. There are no longer 20 minute cutscenes between levels. Odd tone shifts are gone as well. Plot still isn’t noticeably unique and themes lack subtlety, but great character interactions never left and it is a joy to hear and see. Highlight goes to some minor villains that do often steal the show because how entertaining they are. It’s just a little shame that the main antagonist isn’t as memorable this time around. She is not Lord Brevon unfortunately and she doesn’t have the impact on narrative and gameplay his shenanigans brought.I also need to bring up, that while there are absolutely truckton amount of levels, those are a little less dense and evolving this time around. I do miss the two act structure of the first game quite a bit. I believe this was made to keep the game’s scope in check (which you can also see by some enemy recycling mid-game).However as I say that, the individual levels themselves are designed with no major flaws and they are still as fun, creative, fast, unique, colorful and expertly designed as in the first game. Again, nothing goes here below that baseline.The only thing that sadly could be considered below that aformentioned baseline is the OST. It's a big shame, since first game was all bangers all the time and it's a big part of first game's charm. FP2 delivers a lot of great stage themes and character motifs but boss themes mostly lack that excitement pill that elevated the first game. I wouldn’t be honest to myself if I didn’t mention this small disappointment.But that’s the end of downers. Most of other users mention the 7 year wait for the game and if it was worth it or not. I’m biased here – I’m a fan of a first game and of course I could weigh in on this question. However, I do consider this a bad metric to actually answer what does Steam ask you.  - to a random Joe that might stumble over this game an wonder if it’s worth their hard earned cash.To those people I will first say, Have a nice day! And secondly… It is a bit expensive, but Freedom Planet 2 seriously blows away all the competition out of the water with sheer amount of quality content that will occupy you for hours on end. First playthrough took me 9 hours which is double of the first game! With ONE character and NO side objectives! We are talking about Hollow Knight levels of measuring contest and everybody knows how that game was severely underpriced at launch.Freedom Planet 2 deliver top-of-the-line 2D action gameplay nowhere to be seen on the market, despite few flaws here and there. I’m still fresh of finishing the game. I might change my stance on few things later, but at the end of the day, like its predecessor, it’s a top tier gem waiting to be discovered and cherished by you and your friends. I highly recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Forget Sonic, there is a new here in town!In Freedom Planet 2 you and the heroes of Avalice fight against the greatest threat ever.An ancient danger has awakened in the depths of the ocean.Merga, a water dragon from the time of Avalice's oldest war has been freed from her crystal prison and war is about to break out, but our heroes are divided.Will the girls manage to stay together during these difficult times? _childDocuments_.review: Literal Masterpiece. 7 years in development well spent, and they DELIVERED! First off, this game's gameplay improves massively over the first game, which was already fairly good on its own. This? This is just the perfect 2D speed platformer. It's so good it basically puts every 2D Sonic game to SHAME.It's gonna take you a little while playing around with the controls to understand how to make the most out of the mechanics in this game, so please do not get discouraged early, there is a very rewarding learning curve as you progress through the game. Not to mention that many of the stages are meant to be replayed, either to lower the time, or find new secrets. Your first run of a stage might take you, idk 7~10 minutes for most. Then once you get acquainted with the mechanics, you'll see that time be cut in half if not even more. All 4 playable characters have their own strengths and weaknesses, but they all perform about the same once you've picked up some practice. Often you'll find yourself going to different parts of the stages with different characters. The story? TLDR: It's a story about colonialism with a tragic character. Not spoiling much else, but do go out of your way to collect the time capsules, they hold some VERY juicy information regarding the lore. Another thing of note is that each character has specific cutscenes throughout the story, so I highly recommend playing through it with all 4, or at the very least with Lilac and Carol, since those two hold the most specific cutscenes of all the 4 characters. The 2D sprites in this game are BEAUTIFUL. The main 4 characters are extremely expressive, the side characters have pretty good variety, the NPCs are honestly really cute, I love how bats look in this game. I know that the lead dev's favorite animal is a bat, so no wonder why they look awesome. The stages are wildly varied, with many details hidden in the background, as well as other attention to detail elements that you'd only noticed if you stopped to look. THE VOICE ACTING, OH BROTHER THE VOICE ACTING. General Serpentine's VA is awesome, love hearing him. Both Neera and Merga have crazy good emotional performances, love them both. Milla's voice fits her character way too well, and a massive improvement over the first game. Same for Carol. Glad to hear Lilac again. Despite all the sadness in the game, there is also a lot of hilarious stuff, a lot of which you'll find in those character specific cutscenes I mentioned earlier. BUY THE GAME, IT'S STUPID GOOD! I 100% it and speedran the game with all 4 characters, managing to beat it under 2 hours with each. Short and sweet. Your first run will definitely take WAY longer however. Btw Neera supremacy.

_childDocuments_.review: Ever wonder what games would look like if 3D didn't happen and major studios kept pouring the lion's share of their effort and resources into 2D games? Well you can stop wondering, cause Freedom Planet 2 is what that timeline looks like. Bigger, better, faster, stronger, everything about it screams "Extra."The most immediate and striking improvement you'll notice is the pixel art. It is  detailed. On everything, from playable characters and stages down to each individual NPC and bossfight. You jaw will drop the first time you fight one of the larger bosses. Then it will keep going through the floor when you realize there's 39(!) of them. You'll also notice that almost everything has a unique track on the OST - each level, hub area, and subsection of the map has a unique, certified-GalaxyTrail-quality musical piece attached to it.On the gameplay side of things, the addition of items and the guard button makes for combat that's easy to get into (just like the original) but satisfying to master for the game's later, more complex fights. And you'll have plenty of time to master it as well, on the whopping 24(!) levels that you'll be traversing. Their count does not diminish their quality - each one is tightly designed, with different tempo and memorable gimmicks to make them stand out. It also does not diminish the storytelling. Quite the opposite - the new episodic chapter approach makes it so the plot advances at a brisk pace, whilst also finding plenty of time to develop each character's personal stakes.Throw in high replayability in the form of 4 playable characters, the ability to talk to over 100 NPCs (who all have unique sprites!), tons of extra challenges, and an effin' museum for the spritework, and you get a dizzyingly rich package for the asking price. The only possible flaw that I can think of is how that sheer size makes for less cohesive narration: The episodic format means that the player characters get a lot of air time, but the main conflict and villain do not. This can often leave you feeling like the story is... unfocused, that certain levels are unrelated side-quests at best, even though they are still mandatory. Other than that, though? Practically flawless.

_childDocuments_.review: Sequels are never easy, even more so when the original is so beloved. Balancing the things that made the original great with innovations that make a sequel stand out is a difficult act, and not one every studio can succeed at. When done poorly, players just get more of the same, or in the worst cases, a whole that is lesser than the sum of its parts. When done well, players get a fresh experience that iterates on the original's successes while avoiding its flaws.Freedom Planet, a love-letter to the 16-bit era, was one such beloved title, and the developers had their work cut out for them. With such a fantastic first entry, the sequel would need to do so much more, while still keeping the spirit of the original intact. A seven-year development period followed, and at long last, the game was released. But how did it do? Was it a fantastic follow-up to the original, or does it fall short--Of course it's good. It's really good. It's so good. It's one of the best 2D platformers, period. We can cut the theatrics now.Almost everything the first game did, the second game does just as well, if not better. The artwork is more detailed and thematic, and the visual effects are fantastic. The gameplay is refined far beyond the first game, giving the characters a new array of well-balanced abilities that give them versatility without making them more powerful. Every character is fun to play. Nearly every stage flows immaculately, even on a first play. The mechanics are beautifully balanced, allowing for a surprising degree of player expression without any blatantly overpowered options. The sound effects are great, and the voice acting is as well. The music is thematic and fits the setting perfectly. The story, probably the most contentious part of both games, has a great degree of depth and thought put into it, and it avoids the tonal and pacing issues of the first game's.The game has been out for two years or so now, but I bought it a little bit later. I just got around to writing a review because I couldn't find the right words to accurately express how good this game is. Even this barely scratches the surface of how I feel. There's so much to it, I couldn't possibly cover it all.Are you on the fence if you should buy this game? Here's a quick guide:*  This game is everything you could ever want in a sequel and more. You should buy FP2.*  FP2 improves the weak aspects of FP1 while improving the strong ones. You should buy FP2.*  FP2 is a great game, even on its own. You should buy FP2.*  FP2 isn't the same, but it's similar, and it's very good. You should buy FP2.*  FP2 is a good 2D platformer. You should buy FP2.*  FP2 might change your mind. You should buy FP2.*  The console releases are coming up very soon! You should buy FP2.*  Now you are. Also, you should buy FP2.Also, there's a free sample version of the first stage, so try that out! The full game is even better.Okay, that's all. Buy the game.
