_childDocuments_.name: Freedom Planet 2

_childDocuments_.review: An improvement on the original in every way possible. The game oozes polish, love and care all the way through. Gameplay has gone through a number of improvements to suit the chaos and better define itself as a mixture between high speed platforming and breakneck combat. Boss battles are as exciting as ever, and the levels are tons of fun to go through. Even the story mode, despite actually being longer than in the first game, is far better paced and is better at respecting the player's patience, on top of just generally having better written dialogue and dynamics. The voice acting I don't think was ever bad but it's definitely at its absolute best here.This time around in the art department, Tyson Tan lends his distinctive art style and designwork to Freedom Planet's cast and world, and there's never been a better fit- it's clear they want to use his work to help define the visual identity of the series. Overall, Freedom Planet 2 just reeks of "we figured it out" energy across the board- this is a good thing. The first game was an excellent experience that felt 80% there - but this game feels like it has properly realized how to establish its identity as something truly unique and remarkable in its own right. Everything feels more purposeful, planned, and adds up to one of the most fulfilling gaming experiences I've played in a minute.To say I'm addicted is an understatement. For anyone worried about a lack of content, don't be. This is 20+ full-fledged levels, each with their own themes and ideas they used to the fullest. Four playable characters all with their own distinct gameplay identities and feels - Sonic/Knuckles/Tails scenario this is not - the way you approach combat, speed, and platforming with each character is completely different. Items that allow you to customize your character's stats or play the levels with a tighter challenge. A "Battlesphere" mode which not only lets you rematch individual bosses but contains new arena challenges and obstacles courses for you to beat your records on. A sparring mode that lets you fight other characters in 1v1s or smash targets within a time limit. There's just so much here and it's all very well-thought out and meaty.I can see some not liking the "cringe" story like with the first game (read: they're boring people and just hate a fun time) or the long, highly involved levels, but everything comes together for me in a way that feels remarkably solid, refined, and entertaining. It's just a blast and I invite anyone who loves action platformers to give it a try. But please, I implore you, don't go into it treating it like it's Sonic, and don't play it like it's Sonic. Because it's an entirely different beast - some things in common, but it must be tamed anew.Mega Man Zero + Gunstar Heroes + Sonic the Hedgehog for people who wear thigh highs. play it.
_childDocuments_.name: Freedom Planet 2

_childDocuments_.review: I want to preface this with a little storyI loved freedom planet 1, and I beat it on the hardest difficulty on every character simply because it was really fun, and I have always enjoyed a good platforming challenge. The OST was incredible and the story even pulled me in a little bit (I was interested in the larger world they lived in.) However, it did have some frustrating moments, and I never did find every star card. But I did always remember my time in the game fondly.After freedom planet 2 was announced, I was excited. And that excitement was burning for years, as I figured the development might take a while. But after the demo drop, I became discouraged as months of waiting became a year. And another. And another...I began to lose hope, to worry the project was secretly abandoned and nobody wanted to say anything, as other games released (Petal Crash in particular) in the interim. It got to the point where I just...stopped checking.Last month, my passion reignited with a burning vengeance as I found out that not only had development continued, IT RELEASED! I was beyond ecstatic, but I had to wait for the funds to get the game. I thought 25 was a hefty price tag, but I was willing to give it a shot. I set aside a weekend, got the game, and I dived in.I was blown away. The story, the world, the new controls, the characters, the sprite work, the levels, the OST, everything hit me like a truck. I started my play on the hard setting, and I was blown away by how even that worked, and the menus assist settings to help newer platformer players get into it! (I love settings that help new players enjoy the genre, as I enjoy seeing new players succeed and get better!)I'm going to be honest, I have never had a game make me feel like a kid again before, and I don't know if I ever will, but this is a thank you to the devs for allowing me to relive those kid-like feelings of wonder and amazement, and even accomplishment at achieving victory. Even the final boss theme hit me different. It made the fight intense and sad at the same time, gave me the feeling of "this is IT, all or nothing" as I fought my hardest, using every trick I'd been taught to win.A satisfying ending to a seven year wait, this most definitely was.My list of Pros:-Difficulty customization is unique, and I think it's a great addition to the game. You can choose the way you want to S rank a level if that's your goal, or you can choose the best items to achieve your victory, or even to help you beat a level faster than ever before.-Level Designs are great. I never really felt like I had to slow down too much in a level. There were a couple puzzle segments that upset me a bit, but since I'm biased against most puzzles, I will abstain from judging that as a negative.-Boss Designs are incredible. All of the bosses felt unique to fight, and all had their own patterns of movement and attack, No boss really felt too frustrating for me, save one, It's mostly because the boss is frequently off-screen and that makes it hard to tell where the boss is. I had to use particles to guess the buss location and hope I aimed right. If the camera in that fight zoomed out a little bit to accommodate the boss's size, I think that would easily fix my negative view of that particular fight.-Lots of levels! There are an incredible number of stages, and thus content, in the game. I have put in about 20 hours on Lilac's story alone, and there are four versions, one for each character and their particular journey in the world.-The Sprites are very fun! I enjoyed the large variety of characters and sprites, and if I recall correctly, almost all were unique sprites, giving each character their own life and appearance! In addition, the stages are GORGEOUS. they look incredible, and the backgrounds are no different. Everything just feels and looks so good, I was never bored by the appearance of a level!-The story is good. They actually explain a lot more of the world's lore, and dive into the history of their planet. I had been curious about this since the first game, and I finally got some of what I wanted. Excellent execution and very good characters (especially the voice acting improvement! Great job!) help make the world come to life.-The OST is bangin'. I love almost all the music in this game, there was never a time where I wanted to mute the music. Sometimes I boot the game just to play some of the OST collectibles in the jukebox because they are so good. A certain boss theme really does it for me and hits me in the emotions.The Cons-There are still some bugs in the game. I've been thrown out of the level in a few maps and either got soft locked or just...arbitrarily cleared the stage by hitting some unseen flag. I'm unsure if this is an intentional "recovery" feature (no matter how good your programming and testing might be, someone is still gonna find somewhere to break your game! Hello, speedrunning community!) but it was a tad confusing/frustrating when it happened.-Some hitboxes are not obvious that they are hitboxes until you've died a few times to it. One particular attack that got on my nerves with this was an attack with a dagger that had shockwave clouds around it. Little did I know, not only did the line the dagger traveled hit you, but the cloud shockwaves would hit you too! (cost me my rainbow s rank a couple times and believe me, I was heated)-Some spawn checkpoints are a tad far, from bosses enough to be annoying, but not enough to constitute a game design sin. As someone who likes to go fast when I get good at something, having that delay every time I go to fight them was definitely something I found zero fun in.-some items are able to be selected even though they do nothing for you in that stage. I think the items should have a clear warning if you can't use them in the stage, or be locked. (Final stage Timer Badge is one I can think of immediately)TL'DRGame's really good, got a couple minor gripes but nothing too major, definitely worth your time for players of all skill levels. And I think the overall quality justifies your money expenditure, as well.Final Score: 9/10Very good job, devs.
_childDocuments_.name: Freedom Planet 2

_childDocuments_.review: Going into this, already being a massive fan of the first game, it would have taken something truly special to blow me away like the first game did. But, not only did Freedom Planet 2 live up to the first game, it surpassed it in every conceivable way. No, it went even beyond that.The genuine surprise and joy of playing Freedom Planet 2 doesn't come from saying "Wow! This is like if Treasure made a Sonic game" it comes from the realization that this game is BETTER than that hypothetical game! Every element comes at you with the energy of what had to be the happiest game makers on the planet. There's ALWAYS something new coming at you, and with the quality of the art, music, level design, enemies, and game feel, you'll be surprised to know the amount of content this game has. Freedom Planet to just about triples the amount of content from the first game, and that's not counting the fact that there's 1 more character, and 2 more adventure campaign stories than last time. This could have easily been a $40.00 price tag, but at it's current price, it's more than a steal.This game puts FREEDOM in Freedom Planet. The movement options and level design go together so well, you'll find yourself in a constant loop of speed, exploration, discovery, and combat ALL AT THE SAME TIME!To all video game fans out there, this is a genuine victory for the industry, and not something you should pass up. In a year with Sifu, Bayonetta 3, and God of War Ragnarok, Freedom Planet 2 will still probably speed away with my game of the year.
_childDocuments_.name: Freedom Planet 2

_childDocuments_.review: The sequel that got hit with 4 years of delays, maybe 5, it was so long I can't remember. With all that time, it had big expectations from me to live up to, and fortunately it came out pretty good. It's clear if you played the first game that with the sequel they wanted to set themselves apart a bit more from the spiky blue guy who runs fast, redesigning the characters and adding a little more focus to the combat. Fans of Sonic games or the first Freedom Planet should absolutely give this one a go... There's even a free demo!In general, the entire scale of the game compared to the last one is much larger as one would expect. While the levels are shorter, being comprised of one stage rather than 2 parts separated by a miniboss, there are a lot more of them. There's an additional playable character bringing the total to 4. There's an area you can freely revisit that has a bunch of short challenges and a few minigames to partake in. There's even a secret ending!Every character's mobility has been improved since the last game as well, so navigating the stages can be a little easier, and there's an ingenious option to zoom the camera out when you're speeding around! And there's a new guard feature, so incoming unavoidable attacks can still be dodged with some good timing.It's hard to comment on the game's difficulty, as it's tied to optional items you can equip/remove when selecting a stage. I found it to be pretty fair overall, though without the items I believe it's a little too easy, and using those items increase your rewards at the end of a stage, so they're worth using if you care about ranks or 100%ing the game.Possibly the most welcome improvement of all: The voice volume slider. No longer do you have to subject yourself to the sometimes grating voice acting this game offers, though you'll miss out on one NPC voiced by Chris Sabat if you do.Oh, the soundtrack is good too. It's a great game overall, and a worthy sequel. It may be even better than the first, personally I'd say are equal.
_childDocuments_.name: Freedom Planet 2

_childDocuments_.review: Freedom Planet 2 is amazing and better than the first one in every way. I have waited a long time for this game and i can definitely say that it was worth the wait. Freedom Planet 1 was pretty much my favorite game of all time and they managed to make something that i love even more and i'm very thankful for every hour that was spend with making this game!!The Levels are incredibly creative and every single one of them has something special that makes it stand out. The Leveldesign is also absolutely amazing, really intuitive and fluid. The controls are just as fluid and it's just fun to move the Character around. The Bosses are also really creative and can be a great challenge, once you've learned them you can whack them easily and that's really fun! So yea, everything about the Gameplay is perfection! The pixel art is probably the most beautiful pixel art that i have ever seen, espacially the Hub Worlds are so pretty. Same goes for the Character and Enemy desings, really detailed and you can tell that there was put a lot of love and care into designing everything. The music is just as great as in the first one, pretty much every song is a banger. Only complaint is that it often sounds a little too soft, i prefer the powerful songs with guitars in it and there was a little less of that in this game then i would have liked but it's still amazing. The music also often captures the feelings of the Characters really well in specific situations. Now to the Story. I already loved the story in the first game but they have gone wild with the Story in this one. I loved watching every single Cutcene and Learning about the lore. It's often really dramatic but also has a lot of jokes, sometimes it can also get really dark and i just love it regardless of what is happening right now, it always has my interest. The Hubworlds also have a bunch of NPC's that have a lot to say so yea, you can learn a lot about the world and their Characters and i love everything about it. The Game also has so much optional content that you can really spend lots of hours with completing it and every second of that was amazing for me. Now to some of the bad stuff, which isn't much. So the only thing about the Story that bothered me is that it kind of ends with a teaser for more of the story and it took 8 years for this game to come out, so i want to know more about the Story and how it will continue but there i will have to wait a lot of years until anything will be continued. I like the ending but i just want more of the story xD The other thing that is bothering me (mostly for the first days that the game was out) is the lack if polish. I encountered a lot of bugs and softlocks and i didn't expected so many bugs after the game was being worked on for so long, but they are fixing it faster than i can look so that isn't a problem anymore. So yea, the game is just amazing, amazing AND amazing. I want to thank Sabrina DiDuro and everyone at Galaxytrail for making this masterpiece of a game. I'm incredibly thankful for your hard work, thank you. I can't stop gushing about it, buy it, play it and fall in love with it. 10/10 My Favorite game ever.

_childDocuments_.review: Very Satisfactory this game is absolutely worth your time!Very Satisfied, it runs well even with Proton emulation under an obscure Linux Distribution.There have been FPS issues in the first Freedom Planet during certain scenes like when the bosses exploded or during certain boss fights, i am happy to Report that there are no noticeable FPS issues this time!My hardware:CPU: four core, Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-4670Graphicscard: GeForce GTX 1060 6GBRAM: 16 GB DDR3OS: Arch linux (proton was used to run the game)Same or even better then FP1, the Music is very nicely done and reminds me of games like jazz jackrabbit.You can choose between four different characters, each of them has different abilities and play styles.I also like to mention the way difficulty is managed in this game, because the player has a lot of options to tailor their gaming experience. You can either be the super hardcore player by actively sabotaging your health and lives with certain items to create an especially hard challenge for yourself, or you can also craft or buy certain items to make it easier on yourself. There is also a timer for each level and high scores which makes the game interesting for completionists and speed runners.

_childDocuments_.review: Based on early impressions: Lovable heroines: CheckBangin' soundtrack: CheckTight controls and fast paced platforming: Check Brutal boss encounters that will keep you on your toes: CheckCheesy dialogue: Check It's a Freedom Planet game. The core mechanics of the original are improved and expanded upon and the heroines have been re-balanced giving Milla and Carol the same satisfying feeling to play as Lilac (who in the first was arguably the best kitted character by a long-shot) while retaining the unique play-style between all 4 playable characters. Neera's kit, unfortunately, I feel plays a little too stiffly for the high-speed action. For the platformer expert the boss encounters, so far, have been easier than in Freedom Planet 1 but it's definitely balanced out by the fact that the difference between a death and a game over is no longer mere formality. On expert mode a game over will leave you with the choice of either restarting the stage from the beginning or buying your way back to your most recent checkpoint with a not unsubstantial sum of your hard-earned crystals. There are items that can be obtained that can offer nominal improvements to your characters (or even add additional challenge in exchange for a higher bonus at the end of the level) but for the purist it is far from a mandatory part of the game and empty item slots give you a nominal increase to your end of level bonus so the item system is definitely balanced with the purists (who would probably rather ignore the item system) in mind- even to the point that two key bonus challenge items are automatically equipped at the start of an expert play-through. My two biggest complaints would be that Neera just doesn't feel anywhere near as satisfying to play as one of the original trio and on some of the longer boss fights the boss music will stop dead for a couple of seconds before restarting instead of looping smoothly. I will update the review later if the experience falls off, otherwise just assume that the entire game is rated: out of 10

_childDocuments_.review: It's been a long 7 years but it was worth the wait! I love the revamped artstyle, the plethora of stages (haven't even finished it yet and holy crap), and while I can see how the hub areas might be a nuisance for some I personally love exploring them and getting all the little tidbits from NPCs. And hey, if that's not up your alley it's easy and quick enough to go straight to your objective and skip cutscenes if you're really itching to just scoot on through. Rather enjoying the fleshed-out world map as well; since the geography of Avalice was really only suggested in snippets in the first game (from what I remember, at least) it's nice to now see where everything is in relation to each other. And the music, not surprisingly, is wonderful. If the OST is released like the first game I'll be all over it!Thanks so much to the team for sticking with it over so many years, much love to all.Now if you'll excuse me, I have to get back to hanging out in Adventure Square vibing with that music.

_childDocuments_.review: Freedom Planet 2 is quite a beautiful and content-rich successor. It features astonishing BGMs and exciting stages with pretty details that make everything feel a lot more alive while also adding interesting mechanics to the gameplay. Stages such as Zulon Jungle, Zao Land, Phoenix Highway, Shenlin Park, Sky Bridge, and Globe Opera are outstanding and creative. On the other hand, I couldn't appreciate the red stages quite as much. They felt like shallow and repetitive boss fights that require the player to wait too long for an opportunity to attack rather than give their best. Even more if you're playing on Expert and looking for an S rank as Lilac, whose move set isn't as compelling as other character's. What's worse is a part of the game has quite the streak of red stages and cutscenes that would be a pain to watch were it not for the quality voice acting. Don't miss out on this if you're a fan of the genre, but expect to get dragged into dull fights and rides as you approach the lategame and the game decides to go longer than neccessary. I'd rather have a slightly shorter campaign to play and collect everything once as each character than having such an extensive one I don't feel like going through a second time.
_childDocuments_.name: Freedom Planet 2

_childDocuments_.review: Took me a solid 42 Hours to complete the 4 characters campaignsCarol was played firstMilla secondNeera Li Third Lilac 4thWill challenge the rest of the 17 achievements left (mostly speedruns and collectathons.) in which I will update this review.At the time I would say this.Its a decent game but it feels a little cut around the edges for some parts of the game especially art materials revealed in the past 7 years since the Freedom Planet 1 release (July 21st 2014). *A photo of Lilac's gang + Spade/Dail alongside Carozon Tea on a airship. Probably just for promotional sake to stir hype. Sadly the same event doesn't happen in the game.  Majority of the music is solid for the most part but it does not leave much of an impact as the first game. Sadly only 7 stages has leitmotifs from the first game. While the Soundtrack is indeed weaker then the first game, it makes up for it with nearly 17 more songs of the song-list (FP1:72 tracks / FP2-89 tracks) from the first game which is quite nice.Story Mode of Carol Tea is quite endearing but it leaves more to be desired with interactions to her and her sister. Only a few instances are just her meeting her sister and her sister just jets with a warning. I feel Corazon could've been made to be a more integral part of the game itself. But it be how it be I suppose. Not much of her past is revealed. Only references of her previous occupation before teaming with Lilac.Milla the Hound while her past is mysterious since the first game being adopted to Carol and Lilacs' care, it comes to light in this game. Which I believe is to be the most impactful of all 4 Plots within Freedom Planet 2.Story mode for Neera Li left more to be desired, hardly put nothing is revealed about her past, mostly a soldier through and through being quite focused and tempermental.Lilac story basically gives more depth to what Lilacs' motives are especially with her kind. But it falls a bit short somewhat as it just makes her more of a worry-wort instead of the determined and focused character from the first game. Though it is questionable of the *Past* of Lilac of how she became to be considering how the ages are. The new antagonist while the initial reveal shows them to be capable, gets a bit lamp-shaded being behind the scenes for majority of the game until 3/4ths of the way through the campaign. Brevon from the first game had more of a existent threat than she was as he was making loud moves between the three kingdoms of Shang Tu, Shang Mu and Shuigang. Not until the reveal of the antagonist of the second game to the cast did it felt that the world was coming undone.Strengths4 different styles of playA expansive world map that expands around world-building of planet Avalice.Bigger soundtrackSome characters backstory is revealed but not fully.WeaknessClassic Mode locked after first completion of Adventure Mode which can be a bit of a slow-going but I'd feel after first playthrough Classic Mode would be a must to play for a streamlined exp. without the padding inbetween stages.Soundtrack is less memorable than the first game with some tracks placed in, however there are quite a few bangers within the game.  Game feels a bit straightforward this time around which is quite weird. After you play through the stages first time around or so, you start to feel that the stages are quite easy to memorize and quite very so you can breeze through them quickly as possible. (Even one of the achievements is to beat the game in under 4 hours time from total time of the stages.) Still, longer than the first game which *CAN* be completed in under a hour or two if focused.Story seems a bit cut out. Some moments seems to be omitted out to make the game much more flow through. I prefer the first game story overall to be straight blunt with you. But personal preferences aside. Its serviceable somewhat.You will notice that the further you get into the game, the more enemy spam placement there will be. In most cases they are merely hindrances that you can ignore (however upon defeating some enemies you get Energy Cores in which you can redeem for Gold Gems to unlock items/potions to enrich gameplay.)Serpentine isn't a jobber anymore? Maybe? Maybe not? You decide.The new characters (outside of Carol sister) are questionable at best for their purpose and being in the game. They feel out of place and out of sorts compared to the other cast. At least talking to some of the NPCs is quite nice for the first romp through the game however on subsequent playthroughs I just wanted to blitz through the game to complete it. Would be nice to implement some additional effects from chatting with the NPCs such as quests and what-nots. Mayhaps for future implementations there would be a reward to enhance the game with more content? Who knows.For under $22 its a good game to get. $25+ unless it has further updates and DLC included within would be more appetizing. I feel the game is lacking quite a bit. Need more story implementations for the characters.But I recommend it if Spark 3 being 3D isn't good for you. Then the old 2D-platforming Razzle Dazzle would be perfect for you.*Update*70 Hours upon completion and I got my time in the game 100% with every achievement managed to unlock.My entire playthrough can be watched here. 13 Videos chronicled for the game. Mistakes were made, improvements were done, and shortcuts were taken. Regardless I had fun. Here's hoping you do the same if you purchase this title for its full amount that it is worth.

_childDocuments_.review: Basically everything there was to love about the first Freedom Planet, refined and built up for an even bigger, better, gayer experience. If you liked the first one, you'll find plenty to like here too. If you didn't, well, this one might not change your mind either. Shikata ga nai and such.On the whole it feels more balanced than the previous one, so no more having to stockpile extra lives for an endgame meat grinder. However, there's a lot more boss fights with multiple phases/enemies that can prove frustrating. There's also a new system of held items and potions that can be confusing at first, but useful for boosting your characters or providing different, additional challenges. It's completely optional too, so you can just play how you like.The soundtrack is as great as ever, sprites are detailed and well animated and backgrounds beautifully rendered, and the voice work is lively (admittedly some of it's pretty cringe but by now that comes with the territory. I accept and am at peace). This sequel isn't breaking a lot of new ground, but it's a solid and fun game regardless.

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing action platformer with blending its speed and characters' combat abilities for fresh feeling fast paced game play. The varying play styles of the characters allow replaying the stages as each one to offer its own challenges, and sometimes shortcuts (Ancestral Forge is the best level to try to exploit everyone's abilities with, it was really fun seeing a potential way to skip parts by either freezing enemies and making a nice staircases to areas early with Neera Li or flying as high as I can then giving myself a little boost with Milla's projectile power.) Only downside I could list would be seeing the story from multiple sides, the game offering 4 playable characters with some unique cut scenes for each. It really feels like the story was written with only playing as Lilac in mind as playing with the other characters makes the story feel a lot more underwhelming with character specific cut scenes outside of Lilac's story sometimes feeling like afterthoughts.For an action 2D platformer though, its a must play.

_childDocuments_.review: Freedom Planet 2 is 50% a great time 50% unnecessary additions and bloat. It's clear that a lot of passion and time went into a dream game but the developer was never told what ideas might be working and what would have been better to cut.The template is the same as the first game. It's a heavily Sonic platforming game with some light combat elements. The core Sonic platforming is the strongest part and though the physics aren't quite as well tuned that's probably more of a consequence of more moving environment parts and it never broke in any significant way. There's a huge variety of levels with unique stage mechanics: one of my favourites being a giant bat that shoots you off a baseball miles across the stage. The main issue is everything else.There are some stages that have more of a puzzle element, collecting machine parts or keys etc and sometimes these are interesting diversions and other times tedious chores. My main contention is the bosses which are memorable artistically and often conceptually but just aren't fun to play. It's like you are playing Megaman Zero bosses but without the deliberate and tight movement akin to that series (point stolen from Stu Gipp). It doesn't help that boss stages are often so large the enemy moves offscreen, potentially throwing attacks at the same time. I think I enjoyed only one or two bosses throughout my entire playthrough.I should also touch on the story. It's very much bunk but unlike the first game which has a classic mode to skip through it, this one makes you play through the whole story first. I'm assuming you get classic mode after finishing the story. There is no option to fast forward the dialogue so you if the voices are driving you nuts, or you just read the text as quick as I do your options are either sit through or skip. I honestly don't think this games has a subtle enough touch to be talking about species genocide: maybe don't have the antagonist sporting Dr. Wily skull mechs as a minimum??I've played about 7 hours of the game with one character, Lilac. In terms of content that's impressive because there's still three other characters with unique gimmiks. This would be great if I wasn't dreading taking those characters through the aforementioned aggravating parts. I didn't enjoy taking Lilac through the mecha piece hunt, getting dogpilled with enemies and walls/ground of spikes; why would I enjoy it with Milla?There's some other issues to briefly touch on. The music is good but I don't think it's a cut on the original game. The pixel art is very detailed with wonderful animations but the background art can often be so cluttered that it's hard to tell what's foreground or not. It feels like GalaxyTrail is equally committed to undercutting it's great ideas as it to passionately crafting an engaging game. I really don't want to mark this down because it has so many fun ideas and level mechanics so I would say pick this up on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a much more fleshed out sonic game, that lets you go faster faster, with more flexibility.  Sonic was honestly always held back by its desire to keep things simple, and a bit of level design and screen size, sonic mania showed what really good level design and even a slightly bigger screen can do for the game.  Freedom Planet 2's addition of a screen that can zoom out really highlights how nice more information is in these games, though it's unfortunate that the pixel count doesn't increase as the game zooms out, as it makes some sprites look a little wonkier, but it's not too bad.  The addition of attacks, guards and some special abilities makes their characters feel unique and increases the things a character can do, at the exchange of having to use more than one or two buttons.  Playing as Lilac, you can use her Dragon Boost ability to speed up from a standstill, like sonic's spindash, but since it's assigned to a single button, seperate from the jump button, rather than a combination of down and the jump button you can use this ability much quicker, in addition in being able to do it while still in movement, even using it in the air and angling to fly through the air.  It results in a more flexible move, which will make obstacles easier to by pass, but,the move itself is insanely fun to use.  The invincibility on the move does have the potential to make it kinda OP, but the short cool down and direction lock on it is usually enough to keep you from spamming it and just never dying.The other 3 characters all offer their own unique play styles, though I haven't played much of them.  A big portion of this review is coming from my experience with the previous game, and finding this game to be a big upgrade to what they did previously.  The voice acting and story are a bit too anime and cutesy at time, but there is plenty of charm and the voice actors are actually quite good, just know if you're some hardcore cool guy you might feel like a bit of a weirdo showing it to friends.  I know playing it in front of my D&D nerd friends resulted in a bit of joking about the story and characters.

_childDocuments_.review: Ignore my playtime, almost all of my playtime was when I had no internet. I have finished the game as Lilac and Carol.I think for how closely I followed the development of this game, for how much of an absolute ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ reply guy I was in Sabrina DiDuro's and GalaxyTrail's tweets just expressing how hype I was for this game, I have done a disservice for not writing a review sooner.Let me start by saying, I do not consider either of these games 'Sonic' games, and their identity should not be likened to Sonic. They are wholly different experiences that only ultimately share the very baseline DNA of 'Going ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Hard' with the blue blur. With that said, Freedom Planet 1 was, for many years of my life, what i considered 'The Best Sonic Game'--if Sonic made a game exactly like Freedom Planet, just with a sonic skin and sonic-themed movesets, it would probably still not be as fun as Freedom Planet. I've played Freedom Planet 1 so many ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ times, at this point, it's probably more than I've ever played Cave Story.Freedom Planet 2 is  After completing Lilac's story, I said, holy ♥♥♥♥, I feel like I got my money's worth and a half. I can't bang out a run of FP2 in one day like I can FP1, but that's more than okay to me. The game is immaculate. If you played Freedom Planet 1 and you thought to yourself, damn, this can't get better, well, TOO BAD, MORON, because  The combat feels better, the characters have all received a massive glow up that makes them so much more fun to play that after playing this game, I don't think I *can* go back to Freedom Planet 1. Much like Freedom Planet 1, the crown jewel of this game is Lilac. With new moves that interact with her dash, the ability to uppercut out of a jump, and her cyclone no longer taking any meter, it's like Freedom Planet 1 was you playing the game with ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ training wheels. Carol and Milla are both very fun to play in this game, way better than they were in the first game. Had Lilac stayed the same as she was in FP1, I would not be able to pick a favorite. However, for all the improvements made to Carol and Milla, Lilac matched those in spades. If I had one complaint with this game, it's that Lilac is *too fun.* She makes me not want to play as the other characters, because even though they ARE fun, Lilac is so well designed I start to feel like everything in the platformer genre was just the buildup to Sash "Lilac Freedom Planet 2" Lilac.One other complaint I would say I have, unfortunately, I don't think Neera is very fun at all. The power character type is interesting, but I don't feel like she does anything particularly useful with it and she doesn't make fighting feel any more satisfying than it does with Carol, and neither of them are as fun as Lilac. Even so, at her worst, she is still inherently fun to move around with like the others.The soundtrack to FP2 is, much like the first game, an absolute ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ banger. Just amazing all around. Like, if I had to make any criticisms, it's that Merga's motif isn't quite as good as Brevon's. The storytelling in this game is also far better than it was in FP1, managing to stick a lot closer to the tone I think they intended. There are still a few moments, jokes mainly, that I don't think landed, but at the end of the day I think the game does a much better job, though I do think while Merga is a great villain, she does somewhat live in the shadow of Brevon and how perfect he was.My only other complaint regarding the story of this game is something I hope can be adressed in Freedom Planet 3, provided it happens. There will be some story spoilers for the ending of Lilac's story ahead, so just, you know, read at your own risk.The ending clarifying and establishing Lilac and Carol's relationship as a romantic one is something I'm sort of conflicted about. In my head, when I think about it, I like this relationship. It makes sense. They're cute together. However, unfortunately, this is only really something that extends into my head. Part of the plot of FP2 is based on Carol going off on her own and getting into trouble, and Lilac and Carol having these repeated disagreements that put strain on their relationship. This makes sense and I think is a good hardship that the two overcoming helps them understand their feelings for each other better, but my real issue comes in the fact that we unfortunately only see them disagree and fight. There are so few scenes in Freedom Planet 1 or 2 where the two of them are shown to be friends, to know each other well and get along in a way that isn't specifically a team rally declaring that they can do anything. Off the top of my head, I can only think of the scene where they're watching the movie in the first game, and even then, part of that is based on Milla, and more serves to establish Milla as a friend of Carol and Lilac, but not actually doing much in terms of the friendship between Carol and Lilac specifically. To be clear, I don't say this because I want to pick apart the writing of this game, I just want the relationship between the two protagonists to be as good as possible because I love these games. I hope for the future of the series, we can see more interactions of the two of them just being... friends. Lovers too, of course, but I think first and foremost friends.

_childDocuments_.review: Freedom Planet 2 is an improvement in every sense of the word. As much as I adore the first game, FP2 completely blows it out of the water with wonderful level design, bosses, artwork and sprites, the list goes on. The items and potions you can acquire are a nice addition to make the game easier or harder, the latter greatly increasing your odds of scoring higher ranks. The soundtrack is a great listen, on par with the first game in terms of overall quality, some of my favorites being Shade Armory, Lightning Tower, and Ancestral Forge. The only thing this game didn't deliver on was the extra save icons and secret bloopers, but maybe they'll be added in a future patch? Who knows. Despite the 7+ year wait, Freedom Planet 2 is everything I could've asked for and more from a sequel to one of my favorite indie games of all time and is easily one of my favorite games of 2022.

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't finished the game lol but I've played over 60% the game probably as Neera.Feels like the first game, which I love, although SOMEHOW with all the bugs the first game had like if the system was ported. The bugs aren't bad though, they won't usually ruin anything. They're more-so the FUN type of bugs.I genuinely think FP1 and FP2's boss design is some of the best boss design I've seen in a game, well... this and Pizza Tower. I wish more bosses in games allowed you to absolutely floor them if you exploit every nook and cranny of the boss or if you have the know-how to attack the boss and dodge simultaneously.The new parry system is fun too once you get it down, it allows you to get through stuff way faster with a little bit of timing or to even attack bosses faster, it has it's limits so you have to understand those before you REALLY get into doing that stuff. _childDocuments_.review: In this spoiler-free discussion, I talk about why Freedom Planet 2 is the greatest indie game ever made! It's the best indie game of all time!This is a game where you control four anthropomorphic animals who have to fight off the robots, criminals, and invaders of Avalice by beating the crap out of them. It's basically a character action game similar in vain to Sonic the Hedgehog and Gunstar Heroes. The game is divided up into levels where players are tasked with fighting off enemies in close off encounters and then players are then ranked at the end of the level based off their performance. How ever unlike most speedrun action games where you play as a blue hedgehog fighting against robots by jumping into them, Freedom Planet 2 task the player to fight robots in combat by using a bunch of unique special moves. Lilac can speed boost and a spin attack, Carol can do claw attacks and rides a motorcycle, Milla can create cubes and use a shield burst, and Neera uses a spear and make some ice attacks. Unlike the first game where it's just a speed platformer, the sequel itself have put into more into that, like hub worlds, shops, and even battlesphere challenges. Not only that, but this game also added in some collectibles and secrets where you can find in the game like brave stones, power ups, music vinyls, and tons of other items which I don't want to spoil. The game takes the speed combat pushes it to it's absolute limits and creates some of the most unique gameplay mechanics to a video game I've ever seen, and while I can't spoil everything about this game in order to entice everyone to play it, it's best just to discover all of this stuff while you're playing the game yourself. I mean it's one thing to watch a let's play of Freedom Planet 2, but it's a completely different experience while you're controlling the game in motion. Now let's not to say that the gameplay is the only great thing about this game because the story and the cutscenes are really amazing. Even if you're playing the game on the lowest difficulty setting and fumbling your way through the combat system, you'll still be able to enjoy the colorful cast of characters and all the crazy set pieces. The entire game is heavily inspired by Dragon Ball Z and Sonic Adventure, it's like this crazy saturday morning cartoon where the stakes constantly scale up to borderline ridiculous scenarios. The boss fights are these mecha animal creatures where you need to fight a week point to fight off the boss itself, and the game just constantly one-ups itself until it escalates into one of the most over-the-top mind-blowing hype as hell endings to a video game I've ever seen. And you're just sitting there watching the end credits feeling incredibly happy, and exhausted like getting screwed. Still for the majority of players who will most likely put the game down once they've reached to the end credits, it's still a completely fantastic game that anyone can enjoy, and I highly recommend it to everyone. It's one of the greatest indie games I have ever played! In conclusion, Freedom Planet 2 was the best indie game on Steam, it's easily the best game of the year, and possibly most likely the greatest game ever made of all time!

_childDocuments_.review: This was worth the wait! The first Freedom Planet stole my heart with the possibilities it presented, and now after about 8 years, it delivered. I love that the level design adds so many unique elements to it, as that's honestly the most you can ask for in a platformer. It's surprisingly hefty, too; my first full run as Lilac was an impressive 10+ hours, which is over double the time it took me for a run in the first game. That's a lot of content, considering the other  character routes that await me someday! For now, though, I'm content after playing my heart out over two days.Probably my only nitpick is that the action gets a little too chaotic when there's a ton of regular peons in your way, but everything else was fabulous. The team is quick to smooth out any launch day bugs, and personally I loved the fact I could learn the boss patterns as I went to overcome the challenges. The game is really flexible on your difficulty curve, and avoids a lot of problems afflicting certain Sonic level design tendencies. If you're either passing time until Frontiers comes out, or just want another experience on par with Mania, I think this will get you your fix!

_childDocuments_.review: (As of writing this I have only beaten the game as Lilac.) Freedom Planet 2 is more than just a game for me, it was an EXPERIENCE. This game is a prime example for how to create a sequel that's even bigger and better than the original. From the core gameplay tweaks, the level design bursting with really fun and creative gimmicks, more balanced bosses, the more appealing and improved character designs, the improved combat thanks to the new abilities and the guard move, and the gorgeous spritework--some of the best I've ever seen in a videogame--there is a lot to love about this game. It really says something about the game’s quality when I’d even consider the weaker stages to still be good at the first least. Combined with the items and the ranking system on top of that, you have a game that’s endlessly replayable. But the aspect that has seen by far the largest jump in quality in my opinion is the story and the overall writing. I'd say that the story is really good--great even this time around, thanks to the improved presentation, very likable characters (with Lilac being one of my new favorite characters of all time), great voice acting, tighter writing, fairly high stakes, really funny humor, and better cutscene pacing to name a few things. Merga especially runs circles around Brevon from FP1 when it comes to being the main villain due to how compelling her backstory and motivations were, and how the story explored her relations with Lilac seeing as both of them are the last known water dragons. The overall tone is much more consistent as well, as while the game has its fair share of comedy, it knows when to slow things down when it has its more serious moments, compared to the first game which had some serious tonal whiplash issues. The game even did a fairly good job at tackling more serious themes, such as the effects of colonialism, mass genocide, and historical revisionism to name a few. As for some other aspects, I even really liked the addition of hub worlds as a nice break between the main action stages and the NPCs as well! They also do a great job when it comes to the worldbuilding of Avalice, and how it makes the world feel properly lived in. When it comes to the soundtrack: while FP1 might have arguably higher highs, I still think FP2 has a really awesome soundtrack in its own right, and I really appreciate the wide variety of musical styles. Overall, Freedom Planet 2 is not only one of the best 2D platformers out there, but it's also one of my new favorite games of all time while probably being one of if not my favorite indie game of all time. 10/10, this game is absolutely worth picking up if you're a fan of 2D platformers and women. You don't need to play the first game in order to enjoy the second, but I'd still recommended playing it as it's still a great game in its own right, and it makes it easier to appreciate the changes 2 made. Definitely looking forward to doing future playthroughs with the other 3 characters at some point.

Ok, but it'll still get boring to-... is that items that make the game harder?All by themselves are nothing to write home about but combined!There's where your hours will go away.I feel like this is the type of game where you pick up where you left off, play for an hour, and then stop because it can be hard sometimes (especially the bosses).

_childDocuments_.review: I had high expectations for Freedom Planet 2, but the game somehow still managed to dragon boost itself past them! The game is full of little details that makes everything feel alive. You can really tell that a lot of love has been poured into it. Even just dashing around in the tutorial level is a lot of fun since the controls are so spot on! While it would have been nice with a native Linux build, the game runs great in Proton Experimental.The only issue I had was the frame rate of the final stages. I play using an iGPU on a rather old machine (Ivy Bridge, fourth generation i5). The game ran perfectly up until the final stages where it dropped to just a couple of frames per second. Changing the graphics form 1080p to 360p for these parts brought the frame rate back to more-than-playable levels. This probably had something to do with the combination of my old GPU and Proton, but it might be worth keeping in mind if you use an older machine as well.I found everything about this game to be top-notch. The gameplay, the artwork, the music, and the way the story brings everything together. The things I wrote in the first paragraph after a couple of hours still stand after having finished my initial play-through. The game kept raising the quality slowly all the way through. I don't think I've ever had such an intense adrenaline rush before this, even if Freedom Planet 2 felt easier than its predecessor!I strongly recommend both Freedom Planet and Freedom Planet 2 for everyone who enjoys side-scrollers!

_childDocuments_.review: Freedom Planet 2 is, in pretty much every conceivable way, a superior game to Freedom Planet 1. It took 8 years to develop, and it shows.FP2 is a speedy platformer with diverging paths and lots to explore. It draws heavily on influence from both Sonic and Megaman in pretty much all aspects. Combat is snappy--you never spend too long on a single enemy in the field--with just a pinch of depth that makes conquering boss fights feel rewarding. The stages are beautiful, with powerups and secrets to find. Difficulty in this game is easily modulated with helpful and hurtful items, so you can find that perfect balance of a playthrough or mess with fun, wacky combinations.The story itself is pretty middle of the road, which is fine. FP2, like it's predecessor, is dedicated to easy-breezy saturday morning cartoon vibes, and the story beats fit perfectly in line with that. The tone gives way for some moments of drama and tension which I personally appreciated.Like with FP1, the thing this game excels the most with is its visual story telling. There's a ton of dialogue to be had in FP2, but I found myself most engaged in the story and stakes in many of the later stages where GalaxyTrails' spark for visuals comes to life. There is a lot of care poured into each stage that tells its own story, so much that playing in classic mode with barebones story still contains the same sense of motion and tension.10/10 Best unexpected game of 2022
_childDocuments_.name: Freedom Planet 2

_childDocuments_.review: The game's genuinely fantastic. It's a pure joy to play, evolving the gameplay and stepping up the level design present in its action platforming inspirations, like Sonic, and continues taking only the best parts from FP1. It's fresh, fast and fun!The graphics are more detailed and prettier than FP1, and are impressive in motion with how well-animated every single one is. The sound and music quality is AAA.Overworld map design is SMB3-like and therefore great. It's great how city hubs were implemented, and the NPCs therin were all funny, witty or both.Story mission being available in almost any order does wonders for replayability, and was a genius addition. Story pacing, along with tonal consistency, was an improvemnt over FP1, and the optional lore collectibles were a nice side quest.The difficulty curve is very finely tuned in the second half. The bosses stage bosses becoming cuphead-levels of hard near the end made me very nostalgic for the first game.(Don't know if the devs've said for how long these updates currently being released twice a week will continue for. But I hope they eventually include fixes for some some nit-picky details like:Remains to be seen, but at this pace they'll surely be done polishing this up before the summer 2023 console ports.)

_childDocuments_.review: I wish Steam had a sideways thumb button to check. As much as I love the Freedom Planet universe, and with as far as I've gotten with the second game, I have a few problems to point out first.The gameplay is alright. Doesn't change much than the first game, at least for Lilac and Milla. Having played the demo recently, Neera and Carol feel alright as well. Every character is enjoyable on their own. Only thing is, is that I just can't get through the game while forgetting to guard. I'm glad Auto-Guard is an option though... But I can never get used to doing it manually.The problem mainly lies in the fact that the game no longer feels... fluid in it's progression. [SPOILERS AHEAD.]The first game was simple: Get through a stage, get a few cutscenes showing the transition between one stage to the other, then progress.Here... We have a lot to do to get from one stage to the other. The map feels disorienting, and it's annoying that you have to go by feet to a certain spot to advance the story. The world doesn't feel very organic this way.Either way, the map and hub system doesn't stick to me well.And if it isn't the map, the episode system is pretty slow. When I got to the first episode selection, I was somewhat fine with it. I get that all of them link back to each of  but... when I got through it all up to the second episode selection... It quickly drove me away. I just don't like it. I know I'm gonna have to finish the game by forcing through all 3 of them though...Aside from all this, this game is still very solid. The level design is very good, not as good as FP1, but still decent. Music bangs (but hits a bit less than FP1). Art direction is chef's kiss. It looked way nicer back then.I guess I'm too much of a nostalgic person but FP1 stays my favorite of the two up to this day. _childDocuments_.review: Upon completion of Lilac's story, my thoughts of the game have changed entirely from when I first played it.  At first, I thought Freedom Planet 1 was the better game, however, with more experience with this game, that was clearly wrong.  The only things I can say are better in the original are the level-to-level gameplay rather than a small hubworld, even though it doesn't really hurt the game, and theme song, which in my opinion is still better than this game's theme, but that is subjective.  In terms of story, this game takes what the first game did and amplifies it by adding more character drama, more intensity to the character interactions, and genuinely helping to make the villain more connected to the main characters, something that Brevon lacked.  In terms of gameplay, nothing bad to say, takes everything the original did and amplifies it ten fold.  The Sonic influence is still very much present in this game, even down to adding grinding as a mechanic, and I am truthfully a huge fan of this aspect of the game.  Sonic is my favorite franchise of all time, and to see those who understand the reasons why the classic 90s Sonic games' levels worked so well and apply them with a unique and fresh touch that not even Sonic Mania has.  Well Sonic Mania suffers from originality issues in terms of level themes, this game does not, which is awesome to see.  Bosses in this game are fun as well, retaining that classic sense of timing and waiting for an opening.  Music is fantastic, no complaints there.  Overall, this game takes everything that was fantastic about the first game and amplifies it.  The first game used to be my favorite indie game of all time, ever since I first played it 7 years ago, but now I am happy to say this game lived up to all of my expectations and is now my favorite indie game of all time.  I have huge nostalgia for this franchise and I really do hope GalaxyTrail continues with another sequel.  This game is not just a fantastic treat for Sonic fans, but fans of classic platformers as well.  Classic platformers in the vain of Sonic and Mario are my favorite genre and this game knocks it out of the park in that category.  Exquisite work GalaxyTrail, here's to hoping for more successes in your future!

_childDocuments_.review: Warning: This review contains major spoilers for the story of Freedom Planet 2. If you do not want to be spoiled, please avoid this review until you finish the game. Howdy! Player of the original Freedom Planet here. Cracking good game, that. And after getting the sequel, I can conclusively say it's a drastic improvement in a lot of ways. +Characters got a lot more moves and rebalanced mechanics+Soundtrack SLAPS+Story has a better time balancing the tone+Voice acting is better. My man Alejandro Saab still shines!+The art is gorgeous. Which art? Pretty much all of it. Sprites, backgrounds, you name it+There are a lot of levels.+Lot more stuff to do, such as the Battlesphere and purchasing items.And a downgrade in others. Allow me to elaborate:-A lot of the game makes callbacks to the first game, Freedom Planet 1. It's not detrimental to gameplay at all, but noticeable from even a casual glance during cutscenes and dialogue.-Difficulty spikes, the level where you  being a particularly bad offender. The enemies take ludicrous amounts of damage on Normal. The game is practically screaming at you to use the new parry/dodge system when this isn't normally the kind of game that has that and its predecessor didn't.-The levels are longer. That's subjective, but some levels were simply wayyyyy too long. Cripes, one took me upwards of 20 minutes because I just kept getting lost!-The items you can buy are uninteresting for the most part. Playing as Milla, the life-steal item is practically useless because her hardest hitting attacks are ranged or non-physical.-The characters are fun, but often are written pretty wonkily. There's also a distinct disconnect between how some characters are described (*cough*Astal*cough*) and how they actually act. The character dialogue is fun but can sometimes fall flat. Milla's dialogue is the biggest offender. I get she's a young girl, but she is older now. She doesn't have to speak like a five-year old all the time now. And now you're saying she's some kind of science genius? Please. I approve her character growth but this dialogue is just way too childish.-There's a hub now and that's great, but 99% of the NPCs don't offer much of value other than odd chatter. One may call it world building, but there should be some mechanics built in somewhere. Such as side quests or something. There's shops yeah, but you put a "quick shop" option up there to skip walking to the shopkeeper. Also kind of hard to tell who the shopkeepers even are.-Distinct lack of character growth over the course of this game.-The Story itself and how the characters act. Wow. Ok, that's really subjective, but let me explain. This game does a lot good in terms of story. Heck it doesn't even commit the cardinal sin of "gameplay and story are segregated". Seriously I absolutely LOVE how Freedom Planet 2 merges story and gameplay. Other characters helping you out in cutscenes? There's a good chance they show up in levels  All the playable characters have aged several years and are a lot tougher, represented by expanded move pools compared to the first game. All that is awesome. This is the biggest critique I have of the game--plot holes and the characters sometimes act or talk like complete morons, and the general disconnect between the background fluff and what happens in game. Massive spoilers ahead. Sorry that got lengthy but felt it had to be said. Overall this game is great and a definite must for anyone who played the first game or wants to play a hearty side-scrolling platformer action game. And at its current price? A steal. An absolute steal. Bless GalaxyTrail for being so generous. I mean it. 8/10Edit: Spelled Askal's name wrong and removed unnecessary ranting.

_childDocuments_.review: After several hours in I can tell you this is the epitome of what a modern 2d sonic inspired platformer should feel like. It mixes in stage elements from Sonic 3, Sonic & Knuckles, and even some aesthetic from Sonic Adventure 2 even though it's not a 3d game. The combat mechanics also have a modern feel to them where stage bosses feel like stage bosses, and it can take a little bit of effort to get the patterns & mechanics down. It's not as brutal as something like Hollow Knight, but brings that same vibe that has graced a lot of the platformer & metroidvania genres in modern time that makes the battling a part of the game. This makes a lot of sense from a design perspective considering that there is more emphasis on non-Lilac game play.This game was a solid buy out of the gate, and it remains that way as they have continued to drop patches to fix bugs and tweak based on feedback every day since the release. -------------- Original Review -----------------Freedom Planet returns for a 2nd entry finally after many long years. It still holds the same charm as the first game with a bunch of new features, a new character, and new levels. The game's medium difficulty feels right, and for players who struggle there are assist options available such as auto-guard to not exclude anyone. This makes this both an incredible throwback to the era of 2D Sidescrollers, but also an easy title to jump into, or even have children play if you set up the accessibility options for them. I did have a bit of an issue getting used to the default control scheme, since it feels like it's from the Playstation 1/2 era, but the good news is there are options for changing bindings if you're really frustrated as well! Worked out of the box with a PS4 controller directly connected.Additionally it seems like there may be some bugs that haven't been fully worked out - I killed the boss on the second stage & got the achievement for killing it with dragon boost, however the stage didn't end, and it was then further immune with no health bar. After letting myself die and go back to the checkpoint, killing it the second time worked without issue, and hasn't impact any other level so far.Overall, this is a solid buy and I'm glad I bought it at release, it was worth the wait!

_childDocuments_.review: SOME SPOILERS AHEAD IF THAT MATTERS TO YOU.Freedom Planet 2 is probably my favourite platformer i've played in the last few years. Being a mix of speed and action with the occasional precise sections, the game reminds me a lot of S3&K with a dash of Shantae, which is a great mix if you ask me.To start this off; the first thing I always look for in a game: music. It's great. All of it. Go listen to the soundtrack if you haven't, you wont regret it.The levels are all designed well with multiple routes through most of them.The 4 characters all control near perfectly. every issue I had with the control in the first game is gone (Milla is fun to play and wildkick is gone)boss fights are all very fun both the first time and the 5th. they're simple and can be cheesed but are fun no less, and the music is great. (Vs. Corazon my beloved)The story is engaging with a near perfect length. if you want more, each character experiences it from their own point of view and are all fairly different. It's essentially 4 for the price of 1.Merga is a great villain, and her motive is understandable and hell, even justified.the twist supporting antagonists were all great. (and one of them is Vegetable which is an automatic +1(5?) from me)As for the side content, it's there but not needed which in my opinion, is exactly how side content should be made. and the extra boss and ending for completing the battlesphere is a great incentive to complete it.TL;DR: If you like platformers, action games, or are just looking for something casual to play for a few hours every now and then, Freedom Planet 2 is a near-perfect experience that you're bound to love.

_childDocuments_.review: Perspective: Just finished the game on Normal (middle difficulty) using Carol earlier today. Still intend to play the other characters. I also played a ton of the first game and considered it one of my favorite 2D platformers ever. If you haven't played the original then this may not be quite as good a review for you, but if you're at all a fan of fast, action focused 2D platformers and don't mind a challenge then definitely go for it.Pros:-Music slaps as expected-Movesets of characters are expanded from the original, Carol's shuriken is very fun to use-Love love LOVE the level aesthetics and variety, every level feels super distinct and always challenges you in new ways, and some just look amazing-New interactivity with NPCs and world map is minor but helps make the game feel more grand-Nice ways to customize your difficulty and character using handicaps or potion buffs-Sprite work during story conversations are more expressive, and general dialogue is more enjoyableCons:-The story did its job but I failed to get too invested in it. This may be due to the character I chose (Lilac seemed to be more integral than Carol). The main antagonist's motivation was more relatable than the OG game's Brevon, but from Carol's perspective she's very one note-Main gameplay critique: your character's volatile moveset and the more intense levels backfire on the game a bit in that it makes the game very hectic. It's very easy to lose your bearings and struggle to find the exit to a level segment for a bit, or miss items like hidden collectibles or life flowers that you'll need to keep yourself alive.-Limited view around your character can make some bosses annoying to keep track of. One boss in particular I found myself waiting until they entered my view because pouncing around the arena looking for them would put me at risk of taking a hit.-This game is surprisingly difficult on Normal, partly for the reasons listed above. I would definitely recommend either playing on the easier mode or allowing yourself whatever buff items you can find on your first playthrough. The lives system is more strict this time as well so you may find yourself replaying some sections fairly often.Overall worth the 7 year wait and I am definitely looking up the soundtrack later.

Better Sonic Game than Sonic games!Im being serious!Cleared the game first time as Milla.Anyways, the worst parts of the game in my opinion is still the camera not zooming out enough normally. _childDocuments_.review: It's hard to make a sequel. But even harder to make a sequel that's better than the original. I can confidently say this blows Freedom Planet 1 out of the water. The level design is awesome (only with a few nitpicks on certain levels), the character moveset is awesome (I've only played Lilac at the time of writing this though), the sprite work is beautiful, and the music is amazing. All of it comes together in an amazing 2D platformer package and I loved basically every minute of it. The game is challenging (I played on normal) and definitely took me a couple continues, but it's the fun kind of challenge and not the frustrating kind. The game also offers a easy and hard mode as well as an item system. I wish this game didn't have lives, I wish they'd be gone from gaming as they're a relic of arcades and it's 2024. Fortunately this game is very generous, checkpoints are wisely placed and after every death you can choose to continue on super low health (good for landing the last couple hits on a boss) or respawning at the last check point with normal health. And if you run out of continues you can use the blue gems (coins basically in this game) to get another continue. The items system also helps a lot, it doesn't feel tacked on but I didn't use until the last few levels. I never once felt like the game was blatantly unfair. It also contains a couple water levels and I usually hate water levels but they're done so right in this game. And the sprite work in this game is amazing, it's colorful and bright but not eye bleeding, the high detail pixel art is enough to make the characters expressive and give the game a nice look. it reminds me a lot of Megaman 8. The game also has a dodge mechanic the original didn't have and it feels so nice. This game makes you feel powerful for being good at it, it encourages you to dodge although you don't have to do it. The music in this game is amazing. The plot is fairly predictable, it's engaging and the voice acting is decent. It tends to pick up a bit in the mid game. The characters are likable but some of the side villains are under developed. I would say you don't have to play Freedom Planet 1 to enjoy the game but the plot is a continuation of the Freedom Planet 1 plot, so you may miss some references. Overall highly recommend if you like 2D platformers.
_childDocuments_.name: Freedom Planet 2

_childDocuments_.review: Fun time like the first game, but it has moments where it feels overcooked in a lot of places.It may not be for everyone but I do think it's perfectly enjoyable.It does improve upon FP1's elements and while I do think there are things FP1 does better than 2 and overall feels more consistent, I think for those who enjoyed FP1 or other fast paced platformers, they should consider giving this game out if they want.
_childDocuments_.name: Freedom Planet 2

_childDocuments_.review: Back in 2015 the first Freedom Planet was a kind of anti-depression for me at the time. It was colorful, amazing soundtrack, had the pixel graphics I missed a lot and had a great personality to it. Sure, the dialogue oftentimes got a little cringe, but it was an indie game. Fast forward to now and in the sequel they improved upon pretty much everything. The dialogue still tastes the same as the previous game which may throw some people off, but it's cute if you try to embrace it. The graphics are bloody amazing. Some levels have like four levels of background scrolling and it looks incredible in action. There are sooooo many little animations and details. The water even has animations when you interact with it. I know how difficult it is to make pixel art and animating, so the fact they managed to cram so much of it in here is amazing, and with FOUR playable characters that are nothing alike. Even the music, just as the first game, remains catchy as heck. So yeah, definitely get this if 2d games are your thing, the levels are much bigger and more elaborate than the first game's, and overall amount of content and polishing is exactly what you'd want from a proper sequel. No wonder it took seven years. On Normal difficulty the bosses to my pleasant surprise actually get challenging too.
_childDocuments_.name: Freedom Planet 2

_childDocuments_.review: Well, the game was worth the wait. But did it live up to my personal expectations?Not quite sadly. It's still quite good but there are some issues that sadly soured my experience with the game especially nearing the end and prevented it from being great to me.Well let's start with some of the good:- The story is quite good, the comedic scenes made me laugh sometimes (otherwise atleast grin) but the serious parts were more earned than the first game- The presentation of the game is quite good, the artstyle is unique and really colorful- The game has loads of fun gimmicks that kept each level fresh- The hubworlds were a welcome addition which made the world of Avalice feel more alive- The game has a big cast of main characters and more minor charactersNow for the bad:- I like the new artstyle but it made it really hard to see what was in the foreground and in the background in some levels. Causing me to get stuck, not understand where I could land or even die- I ran into quite some bugs that usually were to my disadvantage (once it helped me beat a boss though) - though with all the patches coming out this should get better with time- The music clearly does not loop, which is very noticeable in some levels- Most of the hubworlds were fun but I wish there were some more things to do- Some parts of the story felt "off" to me (one choice seemed to lessen the impact of the main villain to me)- Some levels were kinda annoying to beat (the puzzle based levels mostly)Back to some great stuff to finish this review:- That title screen is just amazing, when a game opens up like that you know if will be good- The game is very well balanced each boss encounter felt like a threat but not straight up impossible (Playing as Lilac)- 80% of the levels were very fun to play and had loads of very cool features- The game has tons of moments where the WOW factor really was present (elevating it the best 2D platformer game you can find gameplay wise)- I like the episode format, gives more choice and personality to the world- There are loads of nice little references for long time fans, which felt very earned after replaying the first game- There are loads of fun levels making the game really worth the asking price (heck it may even be too cheap for what you are getting)If I would give this game a grade... I would give it around 7.5/10Definitely recommended

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could give some sort of "meh" or "10/20" review. There are some bad stuff in this game like some levels going on for too long, having cluttered visuals and bad enemy / obstacle placements, being forced to play the story (whereas in the first game you had classic mode), and some good like the characters sprites, some levels actually being fun and the game controls well.But I'm giving a negative review because of one big problem. And it's a warning to potential buyers: Of all the games I played in my life, this is the only one that gave me motion sickness and almost made me puke.Some levels when they are really cluttered visually, and when you are going really fast can make you sick. The Battlesphere and the Lava / volcano levels later in the game are prime examples.And the boss that came after the lava levels had a background animation that was going so fast, not only was it distracting, it also gave me motion sickness and I just had to quit the game.If you had experience with motion sickness while playing games, don't buy this game and instead check out the first game. As for the others who didn't experience any, be careful.I reported this issue in the discord server but was told it was spoilers ¯\_(ツ)_/¯

_childDocuments_.review: The levels are all so much fun and enjoyable to get through, there wasn't a single one that I though was bad. The spritework in each of them is gorgeous, every song in every level is so insanely good and the level design is so well made. Seriously, there was one level in particular that was absolutely massive and had quite a lot of puzzles, and it took 28 minutes for me to beat it, and yet it didn't feel like it took that long at all, I was actually surprised when I looked at the timer and saw the time, I was having so much fun I didn't see it pass.The bosses are all so great and enjoyable to fight now, especially with the addition of the guard/dodge in this game. This one move completely erased all of the problems I had with a portion of the bosses from FP1. Now when I get hit by an attack I think "Damn it, I should have dodged that" instead of "There was no possible way I could've avoided that, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥". I also absolutely LOVE how, when you're defeated in a fight, you can use a stock to choose to either go back to the last checkpoint with full health to try the fight again from the start or you can revive yourself immediately with a tiny amount of health and resume the fight. This completely eliminates any kind of possible frustration that there could've been from nearly defeating a boss, but then getting hit at the last second and having to do it all over again, as it allows the player to have control over that and have him choose what would be the best play. I've never seen a game do that before and it's such an incredibly INGENIUS idea. The story is just SO much better than the first one. It's so engaging and interesting, you're just constantly at the edge of your seat wondering what's going to happen next and you just never know. The characters are all so well written and awesome, and the voice acting is so well done.I could go on and on about how ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ fantastic this game, it's seriously a masterpiece, and I'll remember it as one of the best I have ever played.HIGHLY recommend anyone to check this game out, it's an unforgettable experience.
