_childDocuments_.review: This is probably the singular best sequel to a game in terms of sheer execution of the ambition and improvements. Considering FP1 was originally a Sonic fan game, and then comparing it to FP2, it's a straight 5:1 improvement on a galactic scale. Everything is leaps and bounds better: story, pacing, character gameplay, level design, enemies, graphics, art diversity, world expansion, and voice acting. There is no singular element that wasn't massively overhauled to improvement while fitting with their new designs.Gameplay:All characters--sans Lilac, I think--got overhauls to their gameplay kit to make them unique, but also much more fun and capable to play. Each character has various methods of attacking, and they all have different mobility options.While Lilac plays largely the same, she gained the Guard function like all of the characters, but hers comes with a character-specific dash attached to it.Carol got a *massive* gameplay improvement overall, primarily to her motorcycle functionality. She is also wildly faster than the first game, so she no longer feels miserable to play off of her bike. I actually played most of the game off of it, and didn't practice with it, and I never felt like she was 'slow' because of. I enjoyed her playthrough a lot.There's a big emphasis on speedrunning this game, as well as multiple difficulties, and further ways to challenge yourself or make it easier. If you are not into this game's difficulty, you can set it to easy and use items and potions to make it even more accessible. You will NOT miss any story if you decide to do this; nothing is locked behind Hard Mode, etc.Milla has also received gameplay improvements, though I didn't play her in the first game. She has a shield, multiple ranged options, a float, but is relatively slow on the baseline mobility. This isn't actually an issue, and she is actually capable of beating stage times faster than Lilac when you use the various techniques available in her kit to maintain speed. I'm not finished with her playthrough, yet.Neera is the new character, and her gameplay was actually quite enjoyable. She has the simplest method of acceleration, and an incredible horizontal mobility available to her. While her combat kit has more of a 'stand your ground' feel to it, she has some interesting tools that can help her out in situations. Like the other characters, she has variances in her kit that make her better or worse than others, depending on the situation/boss.Story:All cutscenes, and including in-between stage dialogue, are fully voice acted. The voice acting has improved a lot since FP1 for each character returning. There is some incredibly emotional deliveries by several characters, showcasing their range and skill. The story itself is quite expansive, namely building the world, and continuing from the first game with a lot of cohesion. The writing of the dialogue is strong to every character's personality and presentation, and no one feels "dumb" or out of place in how they respond to situations. This is used to be both comical, and serious, at times. Each character has special interactions with other characters in their own playthroughs, and additional cutscenes the others won't see. For example, Lilac has more/special interactions with Merga, while Carol has additional ones with Corazon. Due to some timing of how missions play out in the sequence in each story, characters will have perspectives from different cutscenes in different places, even. They really put a lot of effort into fleshing this out, and it shows. As for the totality of the story, it's not bad. Some might find it generic, but it's very polished otherwise.The addition of Neera was a surprise, but welcome design. She is actually a great character, and I think they did a fantastic job with her inclusion.Level Design:Some of the new levels are fantastic, both visually, and gameplay-wise. Some kind of drag, and how you feel about that will be subjective. I don't enjoy Shade Armory or Ancestral Forge that much, but Lunar Cannon is an absolute visual masterpiece and experience, and Weapons Core is incredibly sad in relation to the story. No level was absolutely painful to play, and due to the differences in the characters, they will each have varying levels of difficulty/ease in each one. I like this differentiation between the characters' kits actually making them unique to play.Art:You can just look at a screenshot comparison if you want to see how big a contrast is. FP2 has solidified new designs for every character, and they are fantastically detailed, with the sprite work going so far as conveying their emotions in tandem with the voice acting super well. The levels are pretty, and distinct, and the game never feels like it has a visual clutter to it. The bosses are also sporting fantastic designs, along with the visual effects. Truly one of my all-time favorite sprite-centric games.Music:This soundtrack is amaz~zing. Absolute bangers on it. Even the opening menu is fantastic, though I think Lightning Tower or the final two boss tracks might be my favorites. Seriously, give it a listen.FINAL WORD:If you are into action-platformers or any kind, I cannot recommend this game enough. Recommending FP1 is... hard, though the story is extremely relevant to this game. Whether you want to get the first is up to you, but I absolutely think this is worth a play. It spent a long time in development, but what we got is a masterpiece of a sequel through and through.I'm curious about the inspirations to this game, as Lilac plays most like Sparkster from Rocket Knight Adventures (2), though each character sort of functions like they have a similar charge system for their strongest abilities. Sometimes I also feel like Gunstar Heroes was an inspiration. And, of course, Sonic was the original inspiration.

_childDocuments_.review: Freedom Planet was one of those games I shaped a lot of my interests around, and it heavily influenced what circles I've come to hang around with to this day. However, I slowly fell off of the series over time, since I began to kinda see the cracks in the game. When FP2's release date was confirmed, I can't really say I was excited, but I did want to see how it came along. When it finally came out, I bought it, but to me, it felt like it was more out of obligation. Eventually I played it, and, well...My philosophy is that if you go in with no expectations, even the mediocre games are enjoyable. Despite having no expectations, FP2 was the biggest surprise hit of the year for me. So far, I've only cleared Lilac's story, but I went for all the Time Capsules too, and it's been a really fun ride.Here's what I'd consider the biggest pros:- Selectable story arcs. I like how you can not only set your own path through the story, but play with the difficulty in a way that still keeps every story beat intact.- The original game's levels felt like they dragged on a lot. However, this one's levels lean a bit more into the speed-based gameplay, likely a result of Christian Whitehead's assistance on programming and level design. A typical level in this can take 6 minutes to complete, which works perfectly for stages that combine a Sonic stage's two acts into one.- The voice acting is very much improved. In FP1, a good amount of the VAs were relatively new to the scene, or had come from the Internet. Dawn M. Bennett was a particular example, having no experience prior. However, in FP2, a lot more professional VAs were cast, and the VAs from the original game have hit the big time, having gotten a lot of training and more roles under their belt.- The story feels a bit more... direct now? The first game's story had a number of things that just felt unnecessary, and didn't do much other than show characters' personalities. This one still gives them plenty of character, but shows it more in how they react to situations in the story, and there's less that could be considered unnecessary. Even the Battlesphere episode, which seems a bit disconnected at first, turns out to be important to the story as it introduces Captain Kalaw.- All the characters feel far better to play as. Carol's Jump Disc is a brilliant way to give her a new ability on the level of Lilac's boost, Milla's combat has been heavily reworked while still keeping her primary gimmick, and Neera is great for the players who want to focus more on combat. Lilac has been changed the least, but the boost cancel ability is incredibly satisfying to pull off against a boss.- The items are fun to mess with, allowing you to create your own gameplay experience. While I haven't played around with them much, there's a lot of potential combinations I've seen.- Unlocking the extra final stage involves just playing through a set of short levels that play like the normal game. While things like Sonic's Special Stages can be a fun change of pace, they can sometimes be infuriating if you're not good at them. This method ensures that as long as you can play the main game well enough, you can unlock the extra final stage.- I enjoyed the extra final stage's aesthetic. That's all I'll say because of spoilers.While the game is fun, there are also some other things I want to point out. While they aren't necessarily bad, some may see them as such.- Some bosses, particularly in the late game, have too much HP, and can be hard for those who want to just play something Sonic-like.- The ranking system relies entirely on the crystal bonus percentage you get at the end of a stage. If you want to get a high rank, you need to use items to get a high bonus, instead of just going for a high crystal score.- The storyline feels like a lot was taken from Sonic Adventure 2. While this necessarily isn't a bad thing, it still comes across as somewhat unoriginal.- In a later level, a boss enemy appears as a normal enemy. However, its HP remains the same. If I were designing a game like this, I'd reduce the HP quite a bit. That's what makes it work in games like Space Invaders Infinity Gene: bosses appearing as normal enemies have less HP so that shooting them down makes you feel strong.- It can be easy to not realize the Time Capsules exist on your first run. I definitely wasn't aware myself. I'd probably add a post-credits scene showing the museum in Parusa where you can find the only non-Battlesphere one.- The museum side quest is fun, but it can be hard to get all the cores you need to complete the exhibits.- The game ends on a bit of a cliffhanger, and we don't know if it's going to be resolved or not. This is kind of unfortunate, especially after seven years of development.- One of my friends mentioned this, but I don't see it as much of an issue: the game's visual identity was made to set it apart from Sonic, but the levels and story still feel very Sonic-esque.All in all, I firmly believe the positives outweigh the negatives. No matter what, no matter how hard a boss was or how much trouble an enemy gave me, I kept going because it was an enjoyable time, far better than I thought it would be. Seven years of development may have killed my interest originally, but it's clear that instead of sitting and doing nothing the whole time, Sabrina spent a lot of time making the game fun and enjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: The original 'Freedom Planet' was always going to be a hard act to follow, but 'Freedom Planet 2' somehow manages it. The controls are tight, with an interesting and diverse move-set for each of the four playable characters. Thoughtful level design makes for a varied gameplay experience that never loses its lustre - and with the sheer size of this game, that is quite an achievement. The difficulty curve is a little smoother this time around, simply owing to that increased scope - later levels present a suitable challenge. At two junctions, the player is provided with multiple branching pathways to choose between, determining which levels they will tackle next. While all paths must be explored in time, this does help provide a visible structure to the game; meanwhile, the inclusion of an arena area with a wide selection of challenges ensures that the player is not bound to a single path of progression for most of the game's runtime. While many of the game's (over thirty!) boss encounters refuse to pull their punches, I never found myself stuck on any one boss for too long - echoing the first game, they remain a real highlight of 'Freedom Planet 2', providing a number of jaw-dropping moments of paired spectacle and peril.The story has the same cosy nineties Saturday morning kids' TV vibe that the first game nailed, complete with the shockingly dark elements that characterised many examples of that genre. The hub areas are a sensible choice to help dispense with the long cut-scenes of the first game - here, players can more easily choose how much of the story they engage with. Some of these hub areas feel underutilised - while some offer secrets and mini-games, others are little more than vehicles for dialogue. The voice acting is, on the whole, enjoyable to listen to - it is clear that the cast are having a lot of fun with their roles. The dialogue is somewhat uneven, occasionally lapsing into clunky pop-culture references that suggest a lack of confidence in the franchise's own charms - at its best, however, it by turns warmly humorous, engagingly dramatic, and genuinely affecting. It is a pity that the tension only really starts to build towards the end of the first half of the game - the story might have benefited from a few more early hooks.This is a beautiful game - it is often tempting to pause just to admire the backdrop of a stage, or to appreciate the fluidity of characters' idle animations. While all character sprites receive a greater level of detail this time around, some have changed significantly - Lilac in particular has received a notable makeover, and while others have debated the relative merits of her old and new sprites, I did not find that such changes distracted from gameplay. Perhaps the most impressive graphical assets belong to the game's bosses, each of which is intricately created out of sets of moving parts that are fittingly displayed in a gallery in one of the hub areas. Sound design greatly enhances the game's aesthetic pleasures - well-chosen crashes, splashes, buzzes and booms help make each level feel more concrete. The soundtrack is huge and wide-ranging, although its forays between disparate musical genres never lose it its coherence. You'll encounter several remixes of tracks from the first game, each of which manages to innovate and build upon its parent track; meanwhile, there is a lot to like among the wholly new musical content - I look forward to listening to the soundtrack a decent amount in the coming weeks.Overall, 'Freedom Planet 2' stands as an impressive achievement, a sequel that outshines its rightly celebrated predecessor. While occasionally frustrating, it is perpetually enjoyable, with strong replay value and deft game design that leaves it practically unmatched among high-speed platformers.

_childDocuments_.review: So i picked this game up a few days ago and well now i got 27 hrs in it.but for a more detailed review-(at the time of the review, I only have completed lilac's story, plan to do the others soon)First up, negatives. Weird start but its short so who cares-The only true thing that id say could use a look outside of the odd glitch or two is specifically the world map. Now I like the idea of the map, making the world flow better and giving you a break in between stages and cutscenes. However later on, once I want to practice stages to get better the walking can get tedious. A quick solution would be a fast travel option through the details menu, where you could select a stage to automatically start.Now onto the things that I dont exactly feel strongly about:Story- all the subtlety of a sledgehammer, but honestly, Im no writer so I feel a  bit unqualified to give a detailed critique hereMusic- Now part of this is the hype I had going into the game and honestly, I think the music will grow on me over time. But as of writing, I feel the first game had a slight edge in the soundtrack departmentAnd now the positives-Level Design- Holy mother of something this is good level design. Each level sticks out in a way, and none of the level mechanics are quite what I'd call "gimmicks" as they are fleshed out enough within the level to make it feel right. As well, the level design quite encourages exploration, which is always fun in these 2d games that give you great movement options. The amount of goodies scattered around is insane and I love searching each nook and cranny of a level and getting rewarded for it.Physics- Now most of the time its not worth mentioning, but since the game focuses on speed, it is worth mentioning that the momentum feels great, but still feels very controllable. As well, gaining speed is easy to do, but keeping top speed is difficult, and the physics play into this with how everything just feels. Just feels right, yknow?Combat- Now the first game has some issues with combat imo, with some enemies just feeling far too bulky, especially in the endgame. It didnt help that bosses did not have health bars so it was totally up to you to track it. Now with healthbars for bosses and enemies feeling less tanky (or your attacks dealing more, idk it has the same effect in the end), combat feels satisfying enough to learn and try to get better at, especially since bosses are almost always vulnerable to attacks meaning you can really shred them if you know how to. And finally some attacks have utility during platforming which always helps things feel cohesive.NPC dialogue- the game made me spit out my drink laughing. Don't know if that means my humor is just bad or if the dialogue is good but I frankly do not care. Art-Every single sprite is super detailed and looks great. Special shoutouts to the bosses being made of multiple stitched together parts by how it looks, letting the bosses feel alive, and letting them do expressive movements with them.If you liked the first game, you will probably like the second game is all I have to finish this review
_childDocuments_.name: Freedom Planet 2

_childDocuments_.review: The tagline surrounding FP2 is "There has never been a game like Freedom Planet 2." And that's true, though not for lack of trying! I get the impression a lot of Saturn and PS1 games were trying to have this kinda of impact, to be this sense of scale, but lacked the technology. Even the original FP1 lacks the experience that pulled off as complete a package as this game manages.If you have a nostalgia or even a retro-fascination for the cool-factor stylings of Gunstar Heroes or Astal or even something more world-building focused like Klonoa or Symphony of the Night, Freedom Planet 2 puts the vibes of the era together in ways I've never seen before: Fun, fast-paced gameplay with extremely interesting gimmicks and environments, all wrapped up in a fun story that actually manages to feel poignant and inspiring in a way so few games manage.Bosses take a bit of time to learn and 2 doesn't pull its punches - especially where the achievements are concerned - but that only helps take me back to an era that games seem to think they evolved out of, when really they just shifted away from something fun to something else equally fun. Beautiful ost and passionate creatives behind every pixelated corner, I wholeheartedly recommend anyone who's been wondering where all the good 5th Generation nostalgia games have been give FP2 a go.

Enjoy this fast-paced platformer with great art design that may or may not have actual fursonas on display for everyone to see! That is just to get people caught up so that they don't have to play the first one, if they don't want to. I HIGHLY SUGGEST YOU PLAY THE FIRST ONE FOR THE SOUNDTRACK HOWEVER. _childDocuments_.review: just finished lilac's story. let me get the good things out of the way first. this game is great. probably the best 2d platformer mechanically speaking i have ever played. the massive levels, coupled with the great physics, and updated combat is just great all around. as for the bad however....this game for having 7 years of development looks like its held together with we paper. i had more than a few instances of getting stuck in the floor, and having to restart a section. also had quite a few softlocks from just doing nothing. at times i would talk to an npc and then everything would stop working. also the game looked like it was falling apart by the last few levels, with every death or reset melting the screen together (tho this did make the last level add to the horror element. nothing makes everything look more grim with a what looks like blood covered lilac sitting at the bottom corner of the screen) the last negative is the story. first off, retcons. while not bad to have them, it feels really off playing the first game having dragons be pretty generalized and then everyone stars calling lilac a water dragon. speaking of, the world itself feels like its playing tug of war as to what it wants to be, one hand people think water dragons dont exist any more and are savages, on the other, nobody bats an eye at lilac and calls her a water dragon. actually character development is another. huge missed opportunity at the games mid point where def not vegita has a philosophical talk with lilac, i first saw this and thought, oh cool we are going to have a (which is mostly the story, the rest can be patched out) i still think this game is great, and it was worth the 7 year wait

_childDocuments_.review: I'm someone who always gets... worried when a game spends a little TOO long in the oven. While having the time to do game development responsibly and fill out features is good, this also costs a lot of money and can lead to things like game engine changes, a lack of direction clarity from leadership, or just a game coming out far after it's relevant star has shone.I am overjoyed to say that Freedom Planet 2 is a game that was worth that long gestation period. 7 years of passion has lead to a game that by and large smooths over it's original's roughest points, fleshes out it's world, and comes out as a speedy platformer with excellent pacing as a first-time playthrough with plenty of reason to revisit the game thanks to the combination of it's various difficulty modifying item loadouts, levels that adopt the multi-tiered and routed style designs of it's inspirations, and the 4 different characters to take through what is a dense indie title.I am very glad Freedom Planet 2 didn't shy away from narrative beats after the harsh criticism that the first game became bogged down in it's melodrama and overly long cutscenes. They still are here for Freedom Planet 2, and the much more brisk 'classic' mode is locked behind first-time game completion. However, I think that Freedom Planet 2 thrives in it's adventure mode now, with a narrative that is far less uneven than the first Freedom Planet, and one masterfully broken up between delivering lines through radio banter, having hub areas to fill out lore and character interactions that would have been a cutscene in the previous game, and keeping things brief save for the climaxes of Freedom Planet 2's 3 act structure. although so far I've only experienced Sash Lilac's path, I'm even more endeared to the characters here then I was in the original game, and I'm excited to delve into the other three girls' paths through the game, hoping that the likes of Milla and Neera get as much fleshing out as Lilac does here, given how... personal of a story this suddenly becomes to her. Also, it should be noted that there's clearly much more emphasis put into the quality of voice work, with much of the FP1 cast reprising their roles and feeling much more comfortable in them. Andi Sina in particular sounds much more comfortable in her role as Carol Tea and less like she's recording from a bathroom. Also, I need to give a special shout-out to Merga for being... so much better of a villain than Lord Brevon. while the intergalactic warmonger did his job and provided that fun gutteral growl, Merga is a tragic figure who provides some much needed pathos to the journey and also has some amazing moments of her own.Freedom Planet 2's gameplay does much of what it's predicessor did; channeling the energy of Treasure co. ltd's seminal works in the 90's into a shell that is much more Sonic the Hedgehog like. I would say that Sonic Mania is a game that has since stolen some of Freedom Planet 2's thunder if not for the fact that Sonic Mania director Christian Whitehead contributed level design to FP2. The cast all has wildly different ways of traversing the multi-tiered, winding levels and dealing with the frantic but fair blasts of bullets, blades, bees, and bombs that tend to fill the screen in spectacular fashion, with Lilac being a speedster with a Rocket Knight Adventures inspired Dragon Boost to really get her going and offer her tons of invincibility while moving fast. Carol is a swift combatant with wall jumps and an acrobatic disc she can throw and teleport to and a motorcycle she can ride, while Milla shoots telekinetic projectiles and cubes that she can use to propel herself and flutter about like Yoshi, while (playable) newcomer Neera muscles her way through enemies and freezes them to use as platforms and the like.I'm also happy to say that presentation-wise, Freedom Planet 2 feels SO much more cohesive, with chinese artist Tyson Tan's art style giving Avalice the glue that the original game was missing. seeing the variety in NPCs and the way Tyson's redesigns of the cast came together was a big joy, and I popped so hard seeing the likes of the director's dog (Sammi Diduro) working at the museum, or characters who are clearly fursonas or mascots of various devs throughout the adventure (Verse for example, is the composer's fursona, or Libbie being a mascot Tyson Tan designed to be... I think Huion's mascot?) There's so many cool and very... 90's sorts of graphical pops... things like line scrolling to create the illusion of 3D with the many, MANY layers of parallax, the zoom in and out of the camera as needed, the stage that clearly is meant to be a Super-scaler that made me think of afterburner... there's so much smooth pixel art animation and explosions and cool VFX going on at any given time and it's SO stimulating, but never overwhelming.Of course, Audio is pitch-perfect too, with SO many numerous bangers or songs that use lietmotifs from Fredom Planet 1 to flavor them. I remember being super impressed with one of the levels in the Suigang arc having a bit of the Lord Brevon theme weved into the harmony of the piece JUST as I was getting to a part of the level that had remains of the invaders from the original Freedom Planet coming back. ALong with the frightened tone of Dawn Benett's delivery upon seeing it struck such a powerful chord of... what fighting a war like that must do to a hero seeing their nightmare come back.Freedom Planet 2 has so much love and care put into it. it's why I felt it nesessary to put out this review and implore you all; PLEASE Play this game. yes, it came out a bit hot and maybe needs a couple of minor bugs fixed, but FP2 has SO much dang content and awesomeness in it. PLEASE play it.
_childDocuments_.name: Freedom Planet 2

_childDocuments_.review: A great sequel to a great game, adding in some new ideas and doing them well.Both games feel like a cross between 2d Sonic and Megaman Zero to me, with the focus on mobility and ability to speedrun levels combined with a health bar and focus on melee combat: especially against bosses.The biggest change is the dodge button, which puts your character into an invulnerable state briefly, lasting a bit longer if something that would have hit them is blocked, while preventing them from attacking for the duration with a brief but potentially punishing cooldown. This can let you take down bosses aggressively with good timing.Each character moves and fights differently, with an expansion on the movesets of Freedom Planet and good use of a quickly refilling Energy meter tied to signature moves.For instance, Carol the Wildcat is the only one that can roll and do Megaman X style wall kicks, with three unique attack options in the air. Her signature move is the Jump Disk, which she throws in a direction of your choosing for decent damage, and can jump to it for roll damage and invincibility frames for a time, comboing into her aerial moves.Neera the Frost Night, on the other hand, has a double jump, lunge combo, down attack, slower hits with a bit more reach, a focus state where she attacks faster, and what I'd call spells that use a full energy meter each and come in big vertical attack, freeze/ damage horizontal projectile, or a down attack that makes ice traps she can consume to bounce off of.The stages and bosses are (mostly) the same for different characters with, but they all have some exclusive scenes and information to their point of view for extra variety.The story fits the old mix of a lighthearted base with big stakes and darker moments overshadowing it, and being able to talk to NPCs in hubs really fleshes out the world.If you liked the first one buying this is a no brainer: if you haven't tried it I'd recommend starting with the first for context, though I think this is the superior game.

_childDocuments_.review: Now, while i do recommend the game because first off it's just as beautiful of a game as the first, sadly there are a few negative points i MUST bring to light.Now this is merely my personal opinion, so anyone can disagree with me as they wish, but i personally think the first fight with Serpentine Phase 2 is not balanced properly, first off, his double slash attack you can not block it completely impossible you ALWAYS get hit on the follow up attack 100% of the time, 2 his projectiles he spams during phase 2, i honestly can't count how many times ive been fully in the clear where the projectiles do not reach you, and i still get clipped even when the space between the projectile and my character is half the width of my finger.Now onto Final Boss Merga, oh boy this one is a doozy and probably the biggest grievance.To put it lightly, she is completely BS and unfair, especially with her Final phase after you take out all her moon forms her attacks are far too fast, Far too frequent, every projectile she does has multiple hit frames so guarding isn't even useful, you literally have to run away avoid her like a plague, and using anything you have that can deal damage and give you an iframe in the process. Her fight literally forces you to play like a complete coward, which is a complete contrast too the first game, the first game you actually have to engage with the boss, rather than disengage with the boss.A boss that forces cowardly play to have a chance, is a poorly designed boss, and that sums up my opinions with Merga, she needs to be reworked entirely she is not an enjoyable fight, not because she actually hard, shes not fun because she was intentionally designed to enforce Cowardice during the fight, that is not how you want you final big bad to be remembered as.And this is why i would rather fight Brevon in the first game on highest difficulty despite the fact he basically 1 shot kills you with multiple attacks, but he has a rhythm too his fight and if i died it was because i didn't time my attacks or iframes correctly and died as a result.With Merga you can have perfect timing for all of your dodges but you ALWAYS take damage.So while i do recommend this game, be aware of those 2 boss fights, as they aren't really fair, or made with much thought in mind.

_childDocuments_.review: Great follow-up to Freedom Planet. Neera is a good addition to the playable cast being more combat-oriented than the other characters, the returning characters have new moves and are more fun to play as (especially Milla), the new Guard mechanic is a lot of fun to play with once you get the hang of it, and there's a huge new set of varied levels. The new graphics look great - if the first game felt like a long-lost Genesis game, the sequel feels like a long-lost Saturn game. The music doesn't have as many catchy melodies as the first game's soundtrack but it's still very good.There's also a new item system where you can buy and equip items before a level, but I mostly didn't bother with it because almost all of the items are to make the game easier in various ways and I felt the standard difficulty was reasonable. There are a small handful of items that increase the difficulty but also give a bonus to your ranking at the end of the stage.My biggest complaint is that Classic Mode isn't available from the start like it was in FP1. I didn't like the first game's story/writing at all, and I gave the sequel a chance but I didn't like this one's story/writing at all either. Adventure Mode at least lets you skip all the cutscenes, but there are still occasional interruptions like mid-stage dialogue and hub areas, and you don't get the short dialogue-free boss intro scenes that Classic Mode has.
_childDocuments_.name: Freedom Planet 2

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best video game experiences I've ever had, made even better after playing through the first game. I could see a lot of passion was put into it. It feels great controlling each character, smashing up robots and speeding through the large set of stages. The hub areas do a great job at making the world feel big and each npc gets their own unique dialogue, with their own personalities. The music is great as well. The story, writing, and voice acting all come together to make something pretty cool. The visuals look spectacular, with some of the best sprites and backgrounds I've ever seen in a game. Everything looks so beautiful.
_childDocuments_.name: Freedom Planet 2

_childDocuments_.review: I liked the first Freedom Planet game a lot. Freedom Planet 2 is even better.The Freedom Planet games are often compared to classic Sonic the Hedgehog games, and for good reason. However, the similarities go beyond surface details (such as the lanky furry cast, the robotic enemies, and the Genesis/Saturn look and sound). The best trait Freedom Planet 2 shares with classic Sonic is that each character, even when playing through the same levels, has a unique set of tools for traversing said levels that playing with each character is a new experience.The spritework is very good in this game. It has an appealing style that is consistent throughout, level themes are varied and creative, and the cast of characters and bosses are colorful and charming. The soundtrack is, like the last game, very good, with plenty of high-energy songs to keep you moving fast. The controls are tight and responsive, and the level design complements the intended high-speed pace of the game while leaving plenty of room for secrets to find. The game also has a ranking system for players who want to challenge themselves as well as an item equipment system that can make levels easier for players who need it or more difficult to up the rewards for players able to handle the extra challenge.The one point of contention for this game may be the story/voice acting. I personally like it, and if you liked the story in Freedom Planet 1, you should like this one as well. However, it is over-the-top, hammy, and loud, so I can see some people not liking it as much. Also, Classic mode, which would let players go through the levels without cutscenes, is unlocked in this game rather than being available from the start. Still, every cutscene is skippable, so if the story really isn't for you, it's not hard to skip it.
_childDocuments_.name: Freedom Planet 2

_childDocuments_.review: A sequel that surpasses the first game in every way, and the first game was already an astounding love letter to a generation of 16-bit platformers. Beautiful visuals, amazing soundtrack, great characters, and excellent gameplay variety make up a solid title that anybody who loves 2D platformers should definitely check out.
_childDocuments_.name: Freedom Planet 2

_childDocuments_.review: I'd have to write a whole essay if I wanted to praise everything this game does right, everything I adore about it, and it's actually a challenge to find things I don't like about it. There are some issues I have with the game, but they are so small and insignificant that they're not even worth talking about. Now that's something to be proud of! This little review can't do this masterpiece proper justice, so please just go play it yourself. Give them your money, you won't regret it, but I will try to give you a mini-review of sorts (well, at least mini in comparison). This game is the perfect sequel, and a perfect evolution of an already established formula. It's mind-blowing just how good this game is, no joke. This beautiful title is way too underrated.Wow. Just, wow. This game is absolutely fantastic! The first game was already pretty great, but this is just such a big improvement in every way. The graphics, art-style, sprite-work, gameplay, story, music, and voice acting are all great and better than before, and all of the additional features, such as hub worlds, a world map, updated movesets, a ranking system, a parry button, more collectables, a fourth playable character, an enhanced classic mode, a revive system, assist options and more just make this game feel very fleshed out. The difficulty is also more balanced and fair, and has a unique system that involves these new items called "Brave Stones", as well as other items and potions. It's also lovely that each character plays quite differently from each other, and gets some unique cutscenes, which helps make each playthrough feel fresh and varied. The boss battles are so intricately designed and perfectly challenging. Every single level in this game is fun and unique, and there's literally no bad parts. The story is delightful and engaging, and the characters all have strong personalities.One thing I like about this series is that it feels like it has a good balance between upbeat and dark. It's not afraid to get mature and serious, but it's also often lighthearted and humorous. While to some this may seem to cause minor tonal issues, I personally believe that it never pushes it too far in either direction, and I enjoy this style. Like the first game, it's not just a Sonic-clone, and stands out as it's own thing, and in fact, it stands out even more this time. This series could blossom into something truly beautiful and unique, and honestly, if the Sonic series died tomorrow, this would be the perfect replacement (although I wouldn't actually want that to happen!). Despite this, the game still takes some inspiration from the Sonic series, among other sources. The main difference between Sonic and Freedom Planet is the heavy focus on combat in the latter. Plus, there's two main references to Sonic that I found. First of all, there's this one scene were they all say "long time no see", which made me chuckle (if you know, you know), and secondly, there are two NPCs named Sunny and Amelia, who are cute little hedgehogs who resemble Sonic and Amy, and make references to Sonic in their dialogue. I love these nods to this series' original inspiration.Many things carry on from the first game, but pretty much every single thing was improved, even the things that didn't require improvement. There is just so much passion, care and polish oozing out of every crevice in this game. Playing this game feels like a warm embrace, it just feels so comforting and soothing, and it makes my heart sing. It's infinitely charming! It has a high level of replayablility too. And they're still updating the game and removing bugs, which is unnecessary yet much appreciated. Also, the soundtrack is absolutely one of the best I've ever heard! A big round of applause from me to every composer, but special shout-outs to Woofle, she knows what's up. This game in general is one of the best games I've ever played. I love how much this game respects, references and is connected to its predecessor, despite surpassing it so greatly. I just really love this dang game! Seriously though, this has become an easy contender for my favourite game of all time, if it isn't already, and it's absolutely amazing. I never expected to find a game I loved more than any Sonic game, but here we are. I'm pumped for the console release, will happily buy this game multiple more times. It's not a perfect game, but with just how much I have enjoyed it, I'd gladly give it a 9.5/10 score. One last thing that I want to mention is that I appreciate how the achievements (known as badges in-game) are set up for both games. At first, I looked at the achievement  list and it felt like an insurmountable task for me to accomplish, but here I am with only 6 achievements left, and I've never felt like any of them were too hard. Plus, I feel confident that I can get the last ones. A test of skill and patience for sure, but none of them crossed the line of being a big pain, and I am very happy about that. And by the looks of the first game, it appears that it will be a similar story, so I'm going to try and get the achievements in that one too. The achievements only made the game better and were quite fun to collect, and encouraged me to appreciate the game to the fullest. That's pretty cool, in my opinion. I also love the GalaxyTrail Exhibit in the gallery, that's a really nice addition.Thank you very much, Sabrina DiDuro and everyone else at GalaxyTrail, for creating such a magical and amazing experience (twice), and I can't wait to see where this series goes in the future. This stuff is so good that I feel like I'm not paying you enough! Even if the next game costed $100, I'd still buy it in a heartbeat. Also, take as much time as you need if you plan on making another sequel, even if it takes another 7 years or more. Even if I'm married and have kids by the time it releases, I'd still drop everything to play the game on launch. Whatever you guys choose do with this series, know that you have my full support. Even if the series ended here, it's one that I'd never forget. I know that I've been gushing a lot, but I can't help it. Ciao!

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game, nearly everything feels better than the first one. I really recommend it, and it was a fun time for at least 75% of my playtime.Some pros and cons:PROS:- Amazing OST filled with catchy and groovy songs. It might not be as consistently strong as the first game's but it's nearly there. Ancestral Forge's BGM is incredible.- Lilac, Carol and Milla play better than in the previous game, especially Carol (she's actually fun now).- A LOT of very different levels, each with its unique gimmick.- The story is definitely better in many regards. The true ending was pretty satisfying. Overall the story feels less like a saturday morning cartoon and more serious (except for the whole Battlesphere arc).- I'm on the minority here but I greatly prefer this game's villain compared to the previous. On a regular playthrough you might miss why she's interesting, but getting the required items for the true end gives you a lot of backstory on her.CONS:- The endgame takes a nosedive in quality and the challenge feels really cheap in a few levels, especially with the gimmick of the final proper level (Lunar Cannon) and the extra level (Weapon's Core). Both the final and extra bosses have way too many forms (well, in the case of the extra boss, you have to get it's health under 50% at least twice before you actually get a chance to beat it.) The devs definitely didn't have any restraint here, for the worse.- Playing as Neera is a miserable time, both if you want to go fast or battle. She has some strong moves, except that they're so hard to hit fast targets with that it balances out, but her speed is flat out horrible compared to all other characters.- I feel the difficulty of the bosses is programmed around the ability to shield\dodge\parry attacks, but this mechanic is very hard to master, and sometimes feels like it doesn't mesh with the rest of the game.- The time capsules really shouldn't have been rewards for the Battlesphere challenges. It doesn't compute why they're there instead of scattered throughout Parusa or even the whole game.While I had more to say about the negatives, I'd say this game is extremely good overall and still recommend it. I just hope my criticisms are taken to heart by the devs. I wouldn't mind seeing balance patches to iron out the issues with the final levels and bosses and maybe even buffing Neera to be on par with the rest of the girls.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm prefixing this with the fact that I WILL be getting into Spoilers, nothing heavy like outright revealing something at the very end of the game, but I will be discussing parts of the story.To start off with a generally good note.The gameplay isn't terrible. There's some glitches, which definitely pulls me out of the experience if the glitches in question get intrusive.But otherwise, aside from some general gripes I have with the gameplay, mostly with the overly robust combat options paired with momentum that feels slippery on occasion, I say the game plays alright.Not great, not exactly good, but far from bad, and definitely not the worst it could be.: I believe some of the bugs I experienced could be fixed by now, I hope so anyways, I can't bring myself to play this game again.Now, onto the big piece of this that caused me to really dislike this game.The story.Between the touchy subject matter it gets its hands on, and the characters it has at its disposal, the big story beats end up being horrendously cheesy, what with a reveal with Askal, and a story beat between Lilac Neera and Milla.Askal's reveal as a villain was something I heard making the rounds literal years before release, which is just lovely considering it's an actual story beat that's meant to have impact.As for the scene between three of the four main characters, I get a character being angry, really, I do, but does that scene have to have what's essentially a gun pointed at one of the characters?And now, for the real part with the story that I personally feel is too much.The Time Capsules, and the lore contained within.Granted you care to try the Battlesphere, which is a side mode I believe you're encouraged to play, you get all but one of the Capsules for finishing select challenges.Don't bother looking for them anywhere else say for the hub world of Parusa, because all of them are shoved off into Battlesphere Challenges as I mentioned.They end up detailing what happened in the past, specifically with Princess Cordelia.As great as this would be, if it was handled correctly, I feel like them ham-fisting in Colonialism, and dealing with the aftermath both of that, actual species genocide, the uprising from those affected by it, and what reads to me as racial tension masked through different species was handled very poorly, to the point that it comes off as Tone Deaf, or worse, Insensitive.There is some genuinely nice things in the story, as well as things that made me feel a bit bad, for a good reason, like some lore reveals for a character and such.The reveal for Milla's backstory, and Cory reasoning with Carol are two examples.But the lore included in the Time Capsules, and the lore included after collecting all of them just ends up being like Cheetos, Dangerously Cheesy.To cap that section off, I believe Creative Freedom is a thing, but Creative Freedom and Proper Execution need to go hand-and-hand to create a story that's both cohesive, and create a story that handles topics as sensitive as race relations in a way that ends up being respectful.As for the other good thing with this game.The soundtrack.Now don't get me wrong here either, some tracks in here aren't exactly perfect, and some I won't see myself listening to regularly, if at all outside of the select times they appear in the game.But the game's soundtrack, as a collective whole, is genuinely really, REALLY good.By no means is the soundtrack enough to save the game's reputation for me, but the soundtrack itself takes the game from a tolerable experience, to one that I ended up enjoying on a few occasions, specifically with Robot Graveyard, Shade Armory, and Airship Sigwada.The only thing of note that I have to mention, at all, is the fact that the soundtrack leaked actual years before the game properly released, which ended up making the game's soundtrack, for me, feel a tiny, tiny bit repetitive in some select points, (Specifically with the end-game level themes, and Magma Starscape.)There's also the disappointment that some of the tracks that got distributed didn't change in the final, or got cut as a whole. Some of these tracks sounding genuinely good.: As ironic as this is, what with the soundtrack not being purchasable at the time of writing this, it's one of the few things tied to this game that I can actually come back to, as some select tracks are genuinely good. Ones to note are Cory's Theme, Shenlin Park, Ancestral Forge, and the removed track JC101A, as they're ones I keep coming back to.Overall.4/10, 5.5/10 for the soundtrack quality alone.The gameplay is alright, passable at its worst and actual fun in some rare scenarios, the story and its subject matter are written and handled very poorly where it matters, and the soundtrack is a shining jewel that lifts the game up even if only slightly.Even through editing this review my standing with the game and its intricacies stand.

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine a really good game, that you play the hell out of. And then imagine it got a sequel, that's even better. You don't have to imagine it.No but, like, for real, FP2 is on basically every front, just... better Freedom Planet. The characters feel better to control and are a lot more balanced while also feeling much different from each other - Lilac's still my go-to, and generally the easiest, but even Carol and Milla feel really good in their own ways, and Neera... well, she struggles a little, but, she's not unfun to play either since the game's core movement mechanics are just, really good, and she has her moments. My biggest gripe is... her focus ability is just, useless and actively obtrusive to using her other special moves, and tying it to her guard makes it impossible not to use it... it's not great. Oh speaking of which. The guard in this game is SO GOOD. But the game never tutorializes it! It's practically essential to fighting bosses and even platforming through stages at times, but the very extensive tutorial stages all leave it out for no good reason! Use the guard more. It's worth it.The stages. There are even more of them than before. Blew my mind when I got to what felt like an endgame sequence only to discover I was only halfway done and there was so much more left. Every stage has its own gimmicks, whether they be platforming mechanics, structure, or remixes of previous elements into something new. And they each have so much personality as a result - I feel stages trend ever so slightly shorter than in the first game (for the most part) but all leave their mark even stronger because of it, and just on the basis of how good movement feels in general, they're almost all fun to play.The bosses, I feel like one thing the game learned was to throw in more "duel" type bosses than the first game had, since they tend to be the most interesting and challenging, and, yeah, all of those types of bosses rule, but the giant robots are of solid variety and generally exciting to fight as well, though there are a few exceptions - hello, giant clam of tedium - and I feel like the primary reason bosses overall feel better in this game is simply due to combat as a whole feeling better, but like... it's good stuff.The story is... so, so much better. Merga is an actually compelling villain with complex motives and actual emotional stakes... like, Brevon is cool as a "love to hate" type of villain but... the game has Serpentine for that, if you really want that type of villain, and a whole gang of co-villains backing up Merga for just, all sorts of chaos. Top that off with improved character interactions and better voice acting (Merga's VA in particular just does an incredible job) as well as a story that both does well to flesh out the lore of the world and tell an engaging tale in its own right with an obvious real-world parallel... it's a bit optimistic in its outlook, sure, but I think it works given the style and target demographic of a game like this. Also, no torture scene this time. That's pretty important.If I do have any criticisms with the story, it's that... Neera's role is questionable. She kinda feels there just to be there. She doesn't drive any portion of the plot, has almost no unique character scenes (besides two alternate scenes with one character where... they ultimately play out the same as other characters' and don't really add a ton). And on the flipside... on the whole, this is clearly Lilac's story, and the others are just along for the ride, which is obvious when you consider who each main characters' foil is - Carol, Milla, and Neera each get co-villain foils while Lilac's is Merga herself, and only she gets some of the most key story scenes that /really/ drive home the emotional stakes. I guess there's nothing that could be done about that, but, it's at least noticeable.I'm not really a fan of the lives system in this game - it encourages exploration within the levels, I guess, but you're only really gonna do that once, to look for each stages' collectibles, and then after that it's not really worth the effort to gather 250 gems just for an extra stock. The lives in the first game were... meaningless, basically, but I think that was for the better, because lives systems just suck and, considering gems already have their uses outside of gaining lives, it really feels like a mechanic that could've been easily removed without hurting the game in any way. Just, like... limit the # of low-health revivals you're allowed and, boom, lives no longer need to exist.I also just think the true final stage sucks and... doesn't have any purpose, either, really. The stage is an annoying stealth level, the boss is dramatically less interesting or fun than the normal final boss, and storywise it just serves to throw an extra wrench by way of an uninteresting antagonist character. Plus, the means to unlock it (by doing battlesphere challenges) is... fine, but again feels weirdly mismatched to what that actually unlocks, and, annoyingly, there's no way to view the last four time capsules before beating the game, which kinda makes the scene prefacing the final level come out of nowhere since a good bit of context is missing. I dunno, this entire last arc just feels mishandled.I do feel the actual difficulty of the time trial times in this game is much easier & achievements on the whole not as hard, but given the amount of extra time it takes just to clear the game (my hasty third and fourth playthroughs both clocked 6.5 hours) I think this was a change for the better, in the end - kept frustration at bay.Oh, and, presentation-wise, the game looks and sounds gorgeous, but that's like... obvious. Of course it does. It's Freedom Planet.Obvious I'm not without my nitpicks, but the fact that I played this game for 45 hours and enjoyed the vast majority of them despite going through the story four times speaks to the quality of the game as a whole - there's so much to do, and it's all so good. I barely even touched on the training dojo, the arena battles, the story hubs chock full of NPCs to speak with, the charm and potion systems, the ranking system - which, admittedly, is not super fleshed out or interesting, but whatever, it works.I guess this is just a really long-winded way of saying trans rights.

_childDocuments_.review: This game’s story is an allegory for the importance of critical race theory using lesbian furry dragons. Ok now that I’ve got your attention, please enjoy this wonderful game. I was a big fan of the first game and remember back when this one was announced. It’s been 6 years since then. I bought this game the moment it went live on Steam and after all this time I can say it was worth the wait. This game is an improvement on the original in every possible way. I’ve already beaten it twice as 2 different characters and plan to finish the other two stories soon.  Pretty much every quality of life aspect has been improved. The gameplay is still simple to learn and fun. Characters have new moves which make the game even more fast paced and fun (Milla can attack while moving and from a distance now!) You can revive if you’re just about to kill a boss but then die. Potions and items can give your character attributes to make the game easier (or harder). Every character feels unique. There’s even sub games! For a cheap indie game you will get more than what you pay for. This game isn’t super short like a lot of indie games tend to be so it is a worthwhile investment that’ll take you more than one sitting to beat (especially if you go for the true ending and beat the game as every character).Even outside of gameplay this game is wonderful. Every NPC is unique and the art is beautiful which allows the world to feel truly alive. The music is amazing. The story is fun and clears up some questions left unanswered with the first game. The animations are smooth and pretty and you can tell every pixel of this game was crafted with love. The only real cons I can think of are that some levels might drag on (ha) a bit too long - some on my first try took me more than a half hour on normal mode. The final boss has 6 (!!) phases and that’s not even including the optional secret true final boss after. I was exhausted by the end of it. The devs really didn’t need to make it 6 entire phases. Anyway this game is definitely worth the money. So back to my very first sentence. Get all of the optional time capsules and get the true ending and you’ll see what I mean.

_childDocuments_.review: Long story short; the game is definitely an improvement over the first game in all except soundtrack and I will probably come back to this game every now and then after finishing it.The long story though; I find it tough to actually call this game amazing. The game itself does get very bombastic in ways a Treasure game would go... But I can't help but think something is missing from the adrenaline as weird as it sounds?I'll start talking on gameplay, this game has 4 playable characters being Lilac, Carol and Milla returning from the first and Neera who was also that first game but was an NPC/Boss in that game.- Lilac practically plays the same as her first game rendition with her dragon boost being able to fire her in 6 directions at a burst of speed with a ton of QoL touches that have her game play feel more smooth. - Carol is a brawler/ninja hybrid character who takes after a ton of similar play styles, though definitely find a refresh in this game with some new moves and abilities- Milla has been overhauled to have her kit more geared towards combat instead of her weird puzzle platformer move set. She actually feels like a proper character in this game compared to the first.- Neera is more focused on heavy hitting combat, more so than Carol in the sense that all of her kit revolves around hitting things. She's probably the most awkward to get a hold on since stages are so big in this game with not many focusing on mini-boss/boss encounters.The variety in character does make it so there's a lot of variety in terms of approaching the game and what characters you may find enjoyable or feel fall flat. I'd still say Lilac is the main poster girl of the game though with Carol being a fun alternative, Milla being a little more tricky but fitting and Neera... Well I'll give it to her that she's relatively straight forward and not awkward to where she's a detriment.To bring attention to stages, a lot of them are pretty great in terms of set pieces and building up to bosses. This is where the Treasure comparison really steps in with bosses being more present within some stages before actually fighting them. It really sets a bombastic tone in which stuff is happening within the levels not always just being still pieces. Though there are later stages where enemies and obstacles can become more crazy than they probably should be. Now the game does have a "guard" mechanic that's more or less a sort of lenient parry but I don't think it's a mechanics that's fleshed out to the degree it should be. There are moments where the parry window do save me only to find that I'm still within an attack and take the hit anyway in some sections. I'd imagine if you're going to high ranks or stages this would be infuriating to deal with but just going from point A to B it's more slightly annoying than anything. I'd probably have some kind of invincible dash instead of a parry but that's probably due to what kind of games I play (I know Lilac has a dash like that but you have to hold down the button and I find that awkward).I probably should've mentioned story earlier but this is definitely more of a game where they want to sell you on the game play rather than the story. Not to dog on it of course as it's a pretty dense story and a lot of stuff happens that follows up the first game and does impact the characters. A water dragon named Merga has reawakened and is aiming to ressurect a warship called Bakunawa to eliminate the planet the characters live on and each character has their own perspective with their own stories.The story was a weak point of the first game for being INCREDIBLY melodramatic and going on longer than the actual stages of the game which thankfully this game tones the length down IMMENSELY. I would say overall this games story is much better... BUT there's still a sore point in the sense it still seems pretty melodramatic. This isn't helped by the fact most of the voice acting in the game is nearly as amateur as the first game. Granted a fair lot of the voice actors have done several voice roles before and do sound fine in this game, not gonna list VA names but I'll just say the player characters are awkward to listen to when they need to be stern or upset in cut scenes. I'd probably say Merga doesn't sound right when she's screaming also, the voice and the sprite are pretty separate from each other in this case. Everyone else is mostly fine though whoever came up with Aaa, who gimmick is that they're prone to screaming should be slapped on the wrist and I'm going easy saying that.Graphically the game is pretty great with a ton of lovely stage designs, though with how compared Freedom Planet in general is to Sonic it should be noted that the character design is leaning more into more furry and animalistic traits than anything resembling a toon design, though there are still elements of that for some characters and that's not to say it's all devoid of toon-ish designs. I think it's pretty apparent they're going for something more typical of anime and manga which does still have those exaggerations. I say this because there are hub worlds which have NPCs populate them and there is a LOT of variation between them. Though bringing up the hub worlds, some are definitely less pretty than others with a lot of them seemingly using assets that the levels don't use(?) especially noticeable with some elements of them not behaving as they would in the other levels.Sound wise it's pretty good, though I WILL say I do think the soundtrack is a bit of a mark down. There's definitely good beats still present here and there but I'd struggle to say that many of the tracks really assist the tone or bombastic nature of the levels or events. Crazy to say since Woofle does return for various tracks but I'd struggle to say some of her stuff here is truly strong? Granted there are four other people working on the soundtrack also with some of the people seemingly new to composition so I'd chalk it up to a lot of new talents trying to find footing here.Overall whilst I might've been more harsh for a positive review, I still think this is a game worth checking out. If you loved the first game then you'll probably love this game even more. If you liked the first one but had issues then this game is still worth it though it does still fall short in a few places the first did. If you didn't like the first game then I doubt this will change your mind.I like it enough to where I'll probably protest the third game that releases in 2040 to give Lilac a rival character in the form of some scarlet tiger which somehow encourages her to not be so melodramatic, Carol going through something that mimics her VA's carer path (lightly anyway) and Milla maybe losing braincells as she creates some things. Also make Spade playable you cowards.

_childDocuments_.review: Freedom Planet 2 is a game developed and published by GalaxyTrail and is the sequel to Freedom PlanetFreedom Planet 2, much like its predecessor, is a sort of retro 2D platformer, heavily inspired by the SEGA classic, Sonic The HedgehogOverall, the game is very good to play. The story, although not the greatest, is okay and didn't bore me at allThe graphics are in the same vain as that of Sonic classics, even some of the abilities, particularly Lilac's abilities look like that of SonicThe gameplay, although challenging and sometimes frustrating, very solid and very good. The music is very good and I loved every piece of music played in the backgroundThe voice acting for me was the weakest part, although I do appreciate when a game does full voice acting, which Freedom Planet 2 also does, I feel that the lines weren't recorded in a professional studio as I can hear background hissing on some of the voice actors linesThe voice acting too ain't bad but ain't the greatest either and the volume in the voice acting varied, sometimes, the loud music would drown the actors speaking completely which kind of bothered meBut overall, Freedom Planet 2 is a nice challenging game to play and I highly recommend it to anyone who loves playing game such as Sonic and wants a change

_childDocuments_.review: Game was beaten as Lilac, I plan to do the other characters at a later time.Boy, this series is incredible, what I call half 2D Sonic and half Gunstar Heroes/Dynamite Headdy, this is really a pillar of the indie game community. Compared to its brother series, Spark (yes, I relate the two cause Lilac made a cameo in Sonic After the Sequel, which was done by LakeFeperd), it stuck to its guns and stayed in 2D. This game took 7 years to release. For context, I went from being a freshman in high school to a senior in college in that time. But boy, it was so worth the wait. This game is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ amazing, from the platforming being great, the music being awesome, and the challenge being fair, but also not holding back.The story itself was not anything too groundbreaking, but it built upon what Freedom Planet 1 did right. The humor is incredible (Serpentine is the best character in the whole game), the voice acting is considerably improved, and the villains were both hammy, yet threatening at the same time.My only complaints are the price being a bit more steep compared to other indie titles, and I do wish GalaxyTrail would put the game on more of a sale than just 10%, but $25 is well worth the price of admission. Also, the boss music kinda sucks, and the levels are pretty maze-like, though I never found that much of an issue.9.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: I was just introduced to the series literally a week or two ago (as of this review), and after really enjoying the first game I almost immediately wanted to give the sequel a try. A lot of the issues I had with the first Freedom Planet (levels sometimes dragged on, some bosses had a lot of cheap tricks) are either completely absent or reduced to an unnoticeable degree, and everything I loved about the first game are kept intact and expanded upon. This feels like a game that took 7 years to make, and I'm fully on board for any adventure Lilac takes on next.

_childDocuments_.review: A great and proper sequel to expand upon the world and gameplay of the first one.I played through as Lilac, and the gameplay felt very familiar with improvements. Particularly, the added guard button and the ability to cancel Dragon Boost into an explosion just made my favorite character feel even better.The later boss fights certainly take the player's new moves into account with more intense attack patterns of their own. With that in mind, I also want to mention that the game offers greatly flexible difficulty settings, ranging from 1-hit death conditions to infinite revives, so that anyone can experience the whole story.The soundtrack is again , but unfortunately the boss tunes don't hit anywhere near as good as in the first game. They're either not as exciting or memorable, or they just don't manage to stand out amidst the noise of combat.The game feels like it has the right amount of ambition, with maybe one notable stumble (a vehicle section of sorts, looked janky but didn't play that badly). They've fleshed things out a lot with increased worldbuilding and there are some stunning set piece moments. I was often impressed and am happy for the devs for nailing this sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: Freedom Planet 2 is a game I’m going to struggle scoring. This game is absolutely incredible, it’s simply put one of the best platformers I’ve ever played and a crowning achievement for the genre. Every single step in this game had my jaw dropping from shock and excitement. Every single level stepped up from the last. Every single boss was more challenging and engaging than the previous. Every single song caught my ears more. This game is an absolute masterclass in pacing and design. It’s story is fun and memorable, with much better scripting and acting that Freedom Planet 1. Everyone who worked on this game should be absolutely applauded, as this game is something much more than the sequel to a game I love from 8 years ago. _childDocuments_.review: The fact that this game is released and I finally have a chance to play it is honestly almost surreal. I was in the middle of high school when the first trailer dropped out of nowhere, and here I am now, graduated and finally getting a chance to play the sequel to one of my favorite games.And in almost every way, it absolutely lives up to those expectations. First off, the game is BEAUTIFUL. The sprite-work was already fantastic in the first game, but Galaxytrail went above and beyond to make sure every inch of this game is dripping in color and detailed animation. It's absolute eyecandy and I can't get enough.The gameplay is just as fast and as thrilling as before, with huge, incredibly complex stages full of unique enemies, unique set pieces, and plenty of personality that make each of them super memorable. There were a couple stages where I ended up getting lost and spending a few minutes backtracking to try to figure out what my objective was, but those moments are rare and I'm sure those stages will become less confusing on multiple playthroughs. And while the boss fights in the first Freedom Planet are hard to top, I'd say that a few bosses in this game end up doing just that, with fast-paced, frantic fights that are extremely thrilling and challenging.The story is overall very good. Things feel quite a lot cheerier and goofier than certain moments in the first game, and while I personally missed those darker moments, I still appreciated the charming, fun-loving writing with a lot of strong humor. The heroes are all just as likable and as memorable as before, with a few of them getting some serious glow-ups. I always thought that Milla and Neera were both written just fine in the previous game, but this sequel's interpretation of them make them so much more interesting and enjoyable. And while I don't think that Merga, this game's primary antagonist, quite lives up to the awesomely evil Lord Brevon from the previous game, she still has enough impact on the story as well as enough of a cool factor to make her a strong, memorable villain.The only strict downgrade I'd have to mention is the soundtrack. The previous game's soundtrack is honestly one of my favorite game soundtracks of all time. It was packed to the brim with banger after banger, and it made the stages and the boss fights so much more exciting. And while this game's soundtrack certainly isn't bad, I also can't say it quite lives up. There were a few moments I was wondering why I wasn't feeling as pumped up as similar moments from the last game, and everytime I realized that it was because the music wasn't quite doing for me. Don't get me wrong, the music is still excellent and there are absolutely a few standout tracks, I just can't say it's all a homerun like the first game's.I can't recommend this game enough. The negatives I experienced are nothing more than minor bugs and nitpicks, and the experience was WAY more than worth the 25 buck pricetag. GalaxyTrail deserves your money. Kindly fork it over and play this game.

_childDocuments_.review: The first Freedom Planet game was what I always wanted from the 2D Sonic Series. Overtime, while I still love Sonic, I felt that the games had gotten kinda stale. There was no meaningful growth. Freedom Planet addressed all issues that I had with the series while, creating story and characters that I enjoy much more than what I get from the Sonic series. When I played the game years ago, I was hoping that there would be another one that pushed the Freedom Planet series forward. What I didn't expect is how much Freedom Planet 2 did that. This is an excellent game, and while I want to write a longer review for the game (which is something that I am going to do) I will leave my score for it which is 9.5/10. Damn near perfect in my eyes. One of the best indie games I have ever played not called Hollow Knight. I hope that the series continues after this and doesn't take 7 years.
