_childDocuments_.review: Like its predecessor, it's hard not to be awestruck by the sheer passion and ambition of Freedom Planet 2, which introduces a bevy of smart, thoughtful additions and improvements to the core combat and platforming across a healthy variety of stages and situations.  That said, much of the first game's signature consistency, intensity, and precision feels somewhat lost in the exchange, with levels and bosses sometimes falling flat, and the otherwise superb pixel artwork appearing somewhat mangled by the dynamic camera.There's also the questionable decision to lock the story-free Classic mode away, but thankfully the writing, voice work, tone, and overall pacing have been significantly improved from the original (and you can still skip any and all cutscenes if you prefer).  More problematic is the non-linear progression of levels, which results in a scattershot difficulty curve that squanders one of the core strengths of Freedom Planet.  Conversely, improvements to Carol and Milla's movesets, as well as the addition of newcomer Nerra, ensure each campaign is as much a delight to traverse as Lilac's. Despite a lukewarm opening act, Freedom Planet 2 at last provides a definitively superior experience over the first game, although which one you'll prefer likely comes down to what drew you to the series in the first place.  If it was the Sonic-like traversal and platforming, as well as the callous difficulty curve, then you'll probably gravitate back to the original.  If it was the Gunstar Heroes-esque combat, stage variety, and cathartic boss fights, then the sequel achieves the fullest aspirations of that gameplay loop.  Whatever the case, Freedom Planet 2 is an absolutely superb, polished, unique, elbows-out platformer that shouldn't be missed.
_childDocuments_.name: Freedom Planet 2

_childDocuments_.review: It's a trite comment at this point, but this is another case for "Steam should have a mixed recommendation option instead of just 'yes' and 'no'."First of all, it's impossible not to be impressed by the amount of real content in this game. The game could feasibly take someone 10 hours to finish on a first playthrough and I expect most will be over 8 hours at least. For an indie 2D platformer with a breakneck pace that's a lot of level. The level design is more ambitious than the first game with long, complex, multi-route levels. There are many gimmicks and almost all levels have a good sense of individual identity both visually and in terms of gameplay.This scope is impressive but it's clear that the developers had ambitions beyond reason, leading to both a lengthy development period and a really hit-and-miss quality to the levels and boss fights. Some levels, like the Ancestral Forge and Nalao Lake, are really bad, but there are also some great stages— Lightning Tower is my favourite, mixing in some very light puzzle elements with hazards that are activated as you turn on power, and generally a more calculated level design with a good sense of progress as you climb.Sadly, most of the levels are at least a little chaotic, as there are enemies and stage hazards that seem unavoidable given the speed of the game. In one stage, there is a crushing block hazard that drops so fast that you actually can't avoid it if you're stood still, which you may be if you boosted forward and bopped off the wall where it comes down. Enemies are almost entirely not worth dealing with, as many of them have untelegraphed attacks and a tonne of HP, but you will still take plenty of damage from enemies that attack as you run past. The added guard mechanic seems useless but thankfully wasn't required for Lilac, whose dash has about a billion i-frames and does good damage.In general, the difference between FP1 and 2 is that the former feels more restrained, with level design that guides you forward, whereas FP2 regularly makes it difficult to tell which way you're meant to be going. And unlike FP1, the core gameplay isn't quite as engaging, since besides some good platforming and gimmicks you're mostly just ignoring the enemies and taking random hits. It lacks that sense of connection. Doesn't help that when you do attack an enemy, there is no feeling of impact (unlike the player character who gets stunned by hits). The effect of this is that the game is quite exhausting to play at times and it took me a while to finish.And those bad boss fights... man. The fights against really large bosses are usually fine, mid-sized bosses are mixed and the player-character-sized bosses are almost all complete ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Why? Well, smaller foes are typically either off-screen, or close enough to instantly cause harm to you. Also, many of their attacks turn their bodies into instant hurtboxes, and often aren't well telegraphed. Some are less bad than others, but the absolute worst is , who does half-screen jumps into ground-slams, and spends half his time surrounded by little projectiles. Also a dashing punch that comes from offscreen that you have to anticipate every time he stops slamming, because there is no other cue.The writing for the first game was much maligned and if anything this sequel doubles down, but I can't bring myself to hate it. I love that the furry freaks behind these games put their all into making their fantasy about anthropomorphic cats & dogs, colonialism and historical revisionism come to life... sincerely, it's kind of wholesome. In terms of quality it's like some kid's TV show. Whatever. The lowest point is probably Captain Kalaw. He seems as if the writer played the Ratchet and Clank remake and though Captain Klark was sooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooo frickin funny. To be fair, that only jumps out to me because the writing is otherwise much less bad than that game. I also saw a reviewer compare it to YIIK which seems like a wildly unfair assessment. This is fine for small kids but also tedious to sit through for us because we are adults and we like to consume dense things rather than liquid slurry.I know that this review comes across as negative, and that's largely because I can't help but compare it negatively to the previous game. It's really not all that bad though, just hit-and-miss. Some levels are fun and suffer less from the general design issues. There were points where I'd sit down to play the game, go through two 8-minute levels and be completely checked out afterwards. Other times I'd get hooked on a really good level or set of levels and find myself playing for a good while.For a quick summary, if FP1 is an 8.5/10 than FP2 is like... a 6.5 or 7.

_childDocuments_.review: Freedom Planet, while a fun and enjoyable game in it's own right, had much holding it back.Freedom Planet 2, I'm happy to say, not only returns us to the fast-paced, action platforming of the first game, but surpasses it in every conceivable way. _childDocuments_.review: I am a huge fan of the first Freedom Planet, considering it to be the best of the Sonic clones we have seen in the decades since the original Sonic. _childDocuments_.review: Freedom Planet 1 was a good homage to Sonic games, with more than enough to set itself apart from its inspirational source. With its 16-bit styled graphics but refined controls, the game handled well and presented a high difficulty challenge, even on Normal mode. It had a good, compelling story, interesting world-building, fluid controls, excellent soundtrack and decent characters all around (albeit not perfect in this regard). What's most impressive about this game was that it was a passion project, made by a few fans from their homes, and still turned out as well as it did.Freedom Planet 2, which came out a full seven years later, proves that this new world of Avalice (the planet that Freedom Planet's series takes place on) can pull its weight, and then some. Everything that was present in Freedom Planet 1 has been taken and elevated to a new standard of quality:- The combat and controls are polished to a sliver sheen, with each character now having even more setting them apart than its predecessor allowed. Special mention goes to the new Guard feature, which allows you to precisely defend against and defeat tougher, more powerful opponents than what came in the previous game. This game does not pull its punches: you WILL learn how to fight, and fight well. Good thing this game's combat flows like a river of pure water and is a joy to figure out.- The level layouts show the series' homage to Sonic the most, being multi-layered and easily speedrunnable for those that have mastered the quick, responsive controls.- True to the generational shift, Freedom Planet 2 now emulates the 32-bit style found on the old Playstation systems, but still shows a serious upgrade to Galaxy Trail's budget and skills as developers and presents a wonderful charm to the world it depicts.- With Freedom Planet 1 laying the groundwork for its world-building, this game can now take the runway and fly high, telling compelling stories while digging deep into the world's lore--shaking up a few things along the way.- The next most notable upgrade comes from the characterizations and voice acting: everyone has improved from their record-from-home days with a bona-fide voice recording studio, courtesy of one Christopher Sabat (and yes, he too voices a prominent character in the game; bonus!). The characters truly have a chance to grow into their own as the story explores each of their backstories and personalities more.- Somehow, the soundtrack is even better than its predecessors' was. As of writing this, there is no immediate means to purchase it; this review waits (im)patiently for its release, so he can buy it post-haste.Overall, this game is absolutely solid and is a must-play for any Sonic fans, or any platformer fans out there. (And I recommend playing the first game so you can get a good idea of what to expect.) The seven-year wait was more than worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: Before I begin, a foreword is necessary. The furry/sonic fandom is strange and terrifying. Wariness of any title featuring anthropomorphic animals doing sidescrolling is wisdom.With that out of the way, the game is fantastic. After playing the original Freedom Planet this was at the top of my wishlist, and the game hasn’t disappointed in the least. Gameplay is top notch and each of the four characters is worthy of a full playthrough. The game also does a good job of balancing the tone for the kind of game it is. The game goes from funny/derpy moments most of the time to discussing genocide, but somehow manages to stick the landing. The story was consistently fun, and the serious bits felt dramatic/heartfelt. A lot of it doesn’t quite make sense if you examine it critically, but if you don’t think too hard on it and you’ll have a fun time. A few other game highlights, some already mentioned above:• Really nice sprite work with a lot of love to characterization. Unnecessary touches like special animations when your characters talk to smaller animals abound• Great music throughout. In other reviews you will see people note boss themes hit harder in the first game (and I agree), but the music is still awesome. If Magma Starscape doesn’t get your blood pumping, you might be clinically dead• Good challenge baseline with options for both those seeking mastery and those who are bad at videogames• One of the characters is voice acted by the guy who does PiccoloIt is just a really fun game and worthy of the “Overwhelming Positive” status you will see once it hits 500 reviews.On the downside, your steam recommendations will have suggestions like Fur Affinity 4: Beasts in Heat for a while after you buy this. Ignore those suggestions for a few days and eventually your queue will go back to normal. Probably. Hopefully.

It has so much content I'm not even half done with this game yet.I can only insist and say you must play this game if you haven't. You won't regret it.Thanks GalaxyTrail Team.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: Finished all characters and achievements. Gotta say that once you kinda know the layout of the levels and bosses, it gets a little better. But for a newcomer it's still confusing. Milla is obviously (again) the best original character, however it didn't save this game from my negative review :) Altough - maybe take it on discount?As quite a fan of the first game, I was sort of looking forward to this one. While the game does deliver somewhat of an experience not different from the first game, it's overall less effective for various reasons.First game featured small handful of levels with interesting biomes where each boss felt unique and thought through (some more than others, but still). This one offers you a s**tload of levels and about 40 bosses, where majority of them feel like a joke. Most of them only have three attacks and their animation is very static, it's clear devs love did not quite pour into these sprites. Same can be said about levels - they, unfortunately, follow same formula of the first game, which was already annoying, but they went bigger with this one, levels are larger and collectibles harder to find. There are also 40 of them, which makes biome specificity easier to overlook. They did have some interesting ideas, sure, but I found most of them annoying anyway and thats mostly due to inability to have the game zoomed out permanently, or at least, when you pick up speed. Its always just a blunt background and bunch of platforms. During the entire game not a one moment would come when I would think "damn, now the background really blends well with the foreground". It always seems like the background is there just so there isn't pitch black or something.Introducing hub mechanics to game was totally unneccesary and cities where you would buy items as well as items themselves samewise. I literally finished half of the game using no items, because I didn't know it was there (i knew there were potions, but I was saving them for when they will be needed - turns out they act as items, you can use them indefinitelly once you buy them - who knew...?).Photomode - wow, I mean... WOW. It must be first sidescrolling game where I've seen this feature. Saddest thing is that there is a visible amount of time that went into developing this... why? Why? It's not like this is a Horizon or God of War. The game doesn't look very good really, why would you put such thing in there?Ok so now that I estabilished what game did wrong, lets talk about the good part. Animations of main characters. I liked how they expanded upon sprites for all main characters and also I appretiated slightly more detailed models with introduced shadows and such. New guard blocking system was definitelly a missing feature in the first game, so nice job here. Bosses also look less like gunstar heroes/sonic bosses, but they paid heavy price for having detailed but overall static models.I have yet to finish game for other characters apart from Lilac, for which I unlocked everything that was unlockable in terms of collectibles and achievements including par times challenges and S rank in every level. I might change my mind, but right now - 7 years long work of a group of people seem like a lot for a result like this. Even if it was made by a single person over this span of time, I would still consider it a poor result. Other than that, fine addition to first game, except the first game was just better in terms of mechanics and redundant complexicity.

_childDocuments_.review: I waited 7 years for this sequel and it has been everything I've wanted and more!  -The movement is immaculate, it flows insanely well, using most movement options allows you to glide and slide, keeping the momentum you've earned, redirecting and adding to it-The level design has a beautiful, seemless flow, and they've solved the frustrations of 2d sonic games by making the game based on health rather than the danger being falling in frustrating random pits.  -The combat system allows for creative combinations of moves depending on the situation, and all of them keep your movement flowing and feeling natural.  The combat feels built into the game, rather than tacked on, and works well with the boss section after every stage-The art is BEAUTIFUL, the whole game looks amazing and I feel kind of bad for speeding through it when there's so much detail everywhere.  The game gives sections of time to just look at the world and appreciate it though, I love it-The story has gone further with themes and writing than the first game, and its really engaging and interesting to see where they go with it.  I haven't finished all of the stories yet, but though the story goes through the same flow it seems, each character has differing dialogues and situations explored in their story, and it seems you explore the whole story by playing all of themI can tell this game will be a long-term favorite of mine, it really encapsulates a lot about what I love about games
_childDocuments_.name: Freedom Planet 2

_childDocuments_.review: Freedom Planet 2 is a turbo version of Freedom Planet 1, with almost all parts of it being tuned up to be even better than the first one.While in the first game you would choose between Lilac and Carol (with Milla being a bonus character unlocked later on), here you have the option of the first three character plus Neera, one of the antagonists turned hero in this one.Not only that but the moveset for all characters were overhauled and added to, giving you way more tools to glide, fight and explore the stages, both at your own pace and on breakneck speedrunning speeds.The game plays really fluid and i had no problems at all on that department, the game does ask focus of the player and don't hold your hand at all in any way, if you don't up your own game, you gonna have trouble, even more so on bosses where they can very well drain your entire life bar in seconds if you don't focus.There are some hiccups here and there but they in no way get in front of the fun so i would give it a 9/10.Stage wise the game has more or less 30 stages i think, it's not a giant game, but it gives you enough content to deal with to not feel short, and that is not adding in the the campaigns of all 4 characters, since they all play different enough that you will have different problems to solve with each one. While i just finished the game i really want to get on the other characters to play through all the stages again from their perspectives, 10/10.Music is a blast just like the first one, even more so in some places, it's as close to perfection as i think a human made work can be, props to the musicians and sound design guys, they did one hell of a job here! 10/10!graphics are also amazing, everything is conveyed really well and danger is really easy to spot. Though the danger sign for projectiles outside of the screen does feel like a place holder and breaks alway from the game overall aesthetic, hope they fix that. 8/10.Now, story... that's where i think this game kinda fails, HARD.first, from a gameplay perspective, forcing people to play the game in story mode first before giving them the option to play classic mode (a mode more akin to old games where you just go from stage to stage without cutscenes or anything) is a step back from FP1, it reeks of writers throwing a hissy fit at the though that someone might not care about their work, and forcing them to it as an act of rebelion.Now, if the story was at least on par with the first game, where it was not good, but did things interestingly enough, i think it would be ok to suffer through it once, but ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ FP2 story drops the ball way too many times to be passable.The main villain is a walking cliché of rebel without a cause and the writers trying to much at making you want to like her, most actions of Merga in the game comes off as a child throwing a tantrum, and basically boils down to "bad people did bad things so i will destroy the world, even tho the bad people don't even exist anymore".Then you have the plot points that only serve to futher themselves instead of fleshing up the world, and to be honest, just feels like the writers are spending way too much time on twitter.At no point in the first or second game we see any sign of slavery, yet somehow the story talk about it as if it was the most important part of the entire history of the world, the first game makes no distinction between dragon races, but now they have to because they need to push the story forward.In the first game we had a completely ruthless warlord that would get things done and had no time for ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, here we have a child-like snowflake taking her problems on the rest of the world because it hurt her feefees.And again, the story would have zero importance... IF they didn't held classic mode hostage so people would be forced to play through it.Galaxy Trail dropped the ball HARD here, there are some funny conversations and cool secondary characters in it, so it's not all lost, but still a 4/10.So yeah, gameplay, amazing, sound/music, amazing, graphics also amazing, if you can suffer through the garbage story, go for it, i hope they just give us the option to start on classic mode from the get go.all in all, i will still give the game a 8/10, would be a 9/10 if it didn't had any story/if you're playing through classic mode.

_childDocuments_.review: It's been almost two years now since I played the first one and if you remember my review to FP1, you may remember that I really loved this game. Meanwhile, the awesome team at GalaxyTrail was cooking the second game of this young franchise. And after years of waiting (like, the game was announced in 2015), September 13, 2022 rolled around and the floodgates opened. Ladies and gentlemen - Freedom Planet 2.And...with the nearly 11 hours (by the time I write this) invested and the Lilac story finished (complete with all time capsules. Trust me, you want to collect them!), I came to my conclusion rather quickly. FP2 is not just a sequel, no, it feels like an entire revival of the series. While the first game was more on the lines of a 2D quick paced Sonic like game, FP2 feels unique. There is right now no other indie game with that feeling. There's so much you can do - you can do challenges, you can just talk to NPCs, unlock neat Easter Eggs, on top of the core gameplay that remained mostly the same. And yet, it feels refined. You can fight the way you want, you can cyclone into enemies (which no longer uses energy), you can dragon boost into them - or just combine these to deal massive amounts of damage. And that is just Lilac's gameplay, as you can also play with series staples Carol and Milla, as well as the fourth playable character, Neera.Story wise...oh boy. I don't want to spoiler anything, but Merga and the Bakunawa situation were perfectly set up and after the story is done, you are satisfied. There are even some questions you may have from FP1 that are answered in FP2. If you would force me to choose between FP1 and FP2's story, it'd be latter anytime. And Merga is a fantastic and understandable villain. But that, explore for yourselves. Even the length is perfect - with Lilac, I took around 9 hours to finish the game. If you want to go for all characters, expect around 35+ hours. Not even counting the challenges.Ultimately, Freedom Planet 2 takes what made FP1 so cool and does it much better. I don't regret my Day One buy at all, as for me personally, this is the one of the best indie games that ever graced this platform. Absolute recommendation if you are a fan of 2D high speed adventures in the vein of the older Sonic games. And fans of the first game can get this one without doubt. Trust me, you will not be disappointed.Freedom Planet 3, whenever it comes out, will also be a Day One buy. Because if I learned one thing with Freedom Planet 1 and 2, it's that GalaxyTrail know their stuff.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing and loving the first Freedom Planet back in 2015, I've waited years for this sequel to release, and I can happily say this game was WELL worth both the wait and the price. Many improvements and QoL changes have been made to gameplay, art, and presentation compared to its predecessor; the whole experience feels very streamlined and engaging the whole way through, every character feels very action-packed and fun to play (not to mention REALLY entertaining to watch in cutscenes as well), there are a whole bunch of levels with great variety to both explore and speed through, and it runs fast and smooth on my piece of junk laptop which is a miracle in and of itself!I'm nearly 40 hours in and still have 1 and a half campaigns left to finish, and that's not even including completionist tasks and additional challenge playthroughs. _childDocuments_.review: It's taken me quite some time to find how I want to say the praise I want to say, as It's easy to gush so much your feelings come off as insincere.This game.... is so freaking good it  It took 7 years to make, and it shows in just about every aspect of the game. Every. Single. Aspect. Sometimes, such a long dev cycle is a death sentence for a project, and this is THE POLAR OPPOSITE of the case here. I have 11 hours in and I'm not even 2/3 of the way through the first campaign, and have only done a few sidequests and battlesphere missions. THAT is how much content we have here. We have collectibles, a minigame zone in the battlesphere, the achievments.... $25 is a freaking steal for how much there is to do here.I have not tried the new character Neera as of writing, but the three other characters are an absolute delight, not just in fun gameplay and mechanics, and character design, but in POLISH. The game feels as snappy and fluid as something like Rayman Legends.  While the game is fully its own thing, I've noticed several other elements that feel born from criticisms of the same sonic series it's inspired by as well as a bunch of other things. Too many reused levels? Each level is vibrantly crafted to a T and visually distinct; the pixel art feeling less like pixel art and more like the effort Studio MDHR put into Cuphead. Can't see where you're going when you go fast? The screen has an adjustable zoom. "Souls" -like difficulty getting jack.d off to no end? The Game has a casual mode to get you adjusted, as well as a slew of items and settings to truly make your play experience your own, with really the only penalty being fewer rewards at the end of a stage. Story too long, inconsistent and not engaging? The game is much more well-paced, with a MUCH stronger narrative which was confirmed to be inspired by Zootopia and Black Panther. In other words, it explores some darker themes but does not have something like the torture scene from the first game. Some Dialogue still feels off, but that is a nitpick. Even the hub worlds are small, compact, and .Even if you are not a fan of 2D action platformers, I'm willing to bet you know someone who does, and I'll say it once I'll say it again - This game is a worthy inclusion to your library. To list negatives, sometimes the difficulty does not feel balanced, and the aforementioned dialogue feeling off, but really, THAT'S IT. There is no other way to say it. To Miss Diduro, the Galaxytrail team, and contributors like Christian Whitehead, Chris Sabat, and anyone else not mentioned, your game absolutely ROCKS.EDIT: Also behaves quite nicely on steam deck!
_childDocuments_.name: Freedom Planet 2

_childDocuments_.review: More Freedom Planet means more fun!This game is really good. It's fast, it's smooth, the bosses are cool. Even the few glitches that exist don't kill me like they do in Sonic games... and they are getting fixed consistently. Absolutely worth your money.EDIT: 8 more hours in, having a great time. Music really bops. Sky Bridge is probably my favorite stage so far. Think I'm about to beat the game for the first time.Freedom Planet 1 is still tied for my favourite 2D Sonic Game (with Sonic Mania), but dang, this gives S3&K a run for it's money for  second place.
_childDocuments_.name: Freedom Planet 2

_childDocuments_.review: I've played a good amount of 2D platformers, so I'd confidently say that this game is great. If you liked the first Freedom Planet you'll probably love this one. It's a fast-paced, momentum based action-platformer with excellent music, visuals, and level design. There's some really fun boss fights, a surprising amount of fully-voiced cutscenes, and a good amount of replay value.First playthrough took about 9 hours, but I redid a few levels, finished the Battlesphere mode and just generally screwed around a bit. If you're just gunning it the entire time I would say a decent player would finish in 5-6 hours. I'll probably come back and rewrite this after I finish a playthrough with all 4 characters to see what's in store. You can also get a lot of replay value redoing levels to improve your time or get a better ranking if you're into that. Stages are typically under 10 minutes, so you can run through them multiple times pretty fast.So yeah, if you're a fan of action-platformers, or if you're not and just looking for a good game to try out, definitely worth your time.
_childDocuments_.name: Freedom Planet 2

_childDocuments_.review: I was a Sonic fan for nearly twenty years, almost from the very beginning. The first Freedom Planet managed to impress the hell out of me by out-Sonic-ing Sonic (not that that was hard at the time) and throwing in a perfect blend of elements from classic Treasure games like Gunstar Heroes, and even a bit from my beloved Rocket Knight games.Now, eight years later, here's the sequel... and not only does it out-Sonic Sonic again, I'd go so far as to say it out-Treasures Treasure. This is hands down one of the most impressive platformers I've played in years. It looks and sounds gorgeous, it plays like a dream, its story is wonderfully deep, its mechanics are brilliant, its boss fights are spectacular, and its setpieces keep getting more and more hype, topping themselves with every new level. Everything done well in the first game isn't just done better here, it's given a shot of pure adrenaline and turned up to eleven.If you are or were a fan of classic Sonic or if you like 2D, sprite-based platformers at all, buy this game right now. It's a blast from start to finish.
_childDocuments_.name: Freedom Planet 2

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of people are going to compare the Freedom Planet games to just Sonic, but at this point it's more doing its own thing with an eclectic mix of inspirations from all across Sonic, Treasure's game library and more classic retro platformers besides that. Which is absolutely a good thing.This game is a huge work of passion and you can feel the effort coming from every little detail, to the gorgeous sprite work, the remarkably expansive level design and the great story told through the games main adventure mode.I did definitely get my face beat in by several of the bosses on my first playthrough, and each time I got better- only to get floored by another tougher key boss fight later on in the game (before improving again), which if anything is a sign of a good difficulty curve considering I was constantly improving. But if the difficulty every gets too much at a particular point, there are good assist options in the menus such as infinite revivals (the ability to get up for free after losing a life) and more. To make sure you don't get stuck and unable to continue if platformers aren't your usual game genre.Overall, really, this rules. Loved almost every moment of it, currently on my third playthrough. Sometimes video games can be good it turns out.
_childDocuments_.name: Freedom Planet 2

_childDocuments_.review: A worthwhile sequel that was worth the wait and deserves your money. Seriously, would recommend purchasing this and the previous game if you have not already, one of the few competent 2D sonic-esque side scrollers you can get in this day and age. The sprite work, characters, music, it all oozes charm and passion.
_childDocuments_.name: Freedom Planet 2

_childDocuments_.review: There's more than enough content in this game to keep your sonic itch scratched, and if you were a fan of the first game I would wholly recommend this sequel as it improves much of what has been done before. The story itself will build on a lot of the same characters you've seen before and introduce new ones who are equally intriguing and have a lot of personality. It answers a few questions while still keeping and introducing more.And there's an emphasis on either plunging the levels' depths to get the most possible out of your run or going as fast as you can, to reach the end and to beat the bosses quickly. And hoo boy, they have a LOT of boss fights in this one, there's at least one per stage and the toughest encounters have their own stages so you won't have to worry about getting sent too far back for dying too much.If it's the only few critiques I can give it's that changing the lives into "stocks" and not providing much opportunity to gain more outside of crystals, potions, and items can put a lot of pressure on the player to avoid restarting the stage once encountering the boss. There is an easy mode, but if that's for new players then they'll have to treat this game as a self-contained adventure rather than a continuation in the world of the previous one.Speaking of the story, for as much as I like the foreshadowing and buildup to the reveal of Merga's plans, I do admit she feels like she gets left on the backburner of the first act a bit long.But these aren't to any detriment of the game itself. If you want the challenge, it's there for you and it's welcomed with open arms.All in all, 11/10 this is a Must-Buy for those that enjoy 2D Sonic and Freedom Planet 1 or other skill and speed-based platformer games as well as people who enjoy the art and style of many genesis classics, fantasy and space sci fi mixed together, and pretty pixel art.
_childDocuments_.name: Freedom Planet 2

_childDocuments_.review: I've been following this project since it was first announced in the last days of 2015. Over time, the project kept getting pushed forward but with each set of updates, the world and the game's content gets richer and richer. Lots of love and effort has been put into this and I give it a big thumbs up!I enjoy the diversity of paths you can take for a platformer. I hope the franchise continues to grow!
_childDocuments_.name: Freedom Planet 2

_childDocuments_.review: The first game was rad, but the sequel is better in every way. The visual look incredibly good, the redesign of the main casts make them much cooler than before, and the animations are just so smooth! (Special mention to Lilac's running backward animation, which I find simply awesome!) This franchise as a lot of potential, and I really hope to see more of these characters in other media, and of course, in another potential sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Freedom Planet 2

_childDocuments_.review: I played through Lilac's story, and it's like like Treasure made Sonic the Hedgehog. A frankly unreasonable amount of gorgeous spritework, a charming story, and a tour of a world the developers clearly give a ♥♥♥♥ about. And it keeps surprising with the cool stuff it does. This is a fun ride, and a video game that so clearly wanted to get made. Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Freedom Planet 2

_childDocuments_.review: AMAZING gameCouldn't recommend it more, great visuals, a great soundtrack, great controls, and much more11/10, banger, fire, GOTY, etc.the only cons I could see so far are:Milla whenever she receives damage does a sound that may or may not obligate you to use headphones whenever you play with her, so keep that in mindother than that, it's perfectAnd ive only played as Lilac until now!!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Freedom Planet 2

_childDocuments_.review: Freedom Planet 2 is what I call a fantastic sequel. This game is packed with so much content than its predecessor and that is a good thing I wasn't expecting 24 levels in this entire game. My first play through of the game with Lilac which was really fun and i still enjoy playing as her because she's a faster paced Zero from the Mega man games mixed with Sonic's speed. The graphics look like a polished Sega Saturn game and to me it looks timeless and the boss fights just like the first game were pure adrenaline rush and make you learn their patterns  My flaws with the game would only have to be the later levels being a bit too long taking about 10-15 minutes to complete. All in all Freedom Planet 2 is a really great game and I think more people should support games like these ever since I played the demo back in 2017 it made me excited to see what Galaxy trail was making due to the delays I can't believe the development was all the way back in 2015 and it was worth the wait
_childDocuments_.name: Freedom Planet 2

_childDocuments_.review: I have been waiting for this game a long time.As an enthusiastic fan of platformers, given my gaming career began with Sonic 1, I have played many from various different subgenres in my time - all of the Sonics, more technical/precision based ones like The End is Nigh and Wings of Vi, and then I found a little game named Freedom Planet many years ago... and fell in love.The first Freedom Planet was easily one of, if not the best platformer I've played. Out of so many. I adored that game, and couldn't wait for a sequel. Now, after many years, avidly looking for news of it, it finally emerged.Is it a worthy sequel?I would say that while Freedom Planet 1 felt like a new team finding its feet, Freedom Planet 2 is handled with a lot more confidence - storytelling is more streamlined and well-paced, with no very long cutscenes breaking the pacing, while simultaneously telling a surprisingly good story. It feels much wider in scale than the previous game, and makes you think of aspects to the world of Avalice that are not solely related to the current conflict (in comparison, in the first game, everything was against Brevon).The music, unfortunately, I must say is not as good as the first - there are some standout tracks (first Dragon Valley is incredible), but overall I'd say they feel a bit more generic than before. The power of the first game was that each stage had separate music tracks, where the first part would establish some musical theme and the second would develop it - things like Aqua Tunnel, Relic Maze, and Jade Creek from the first game were incredibly beautiful and exciting tracks, and I still listen to them on a regular basis.The game's level structure in the second one no longer has "split acts", and thus the music mostly remains constant throughout - still good to listen to, but I feel that levels generally don't have a distinct theme to them.Gameplay-wise, it's like a smoother and more varied version of the first game. I've only played as Lilac so far, but the change they made to her Cyclone means she's considerably smoother to play. There was no level that frustrated me or that I felt was unfair, and all of the bosses felt good (even if there are some significant difficulty spikes, but only on really climactic bosses, so I thought this was fine - the first game also had big spikes on key bosses, and I think it elevates the moment). I've seen some people complain about the boss design, but I thought they were all fine on Lilac - the true final boss required me to exploit the invincibility of her Dragon Dash, but again - this is a design feature, and in the previous game using it was also baked into my strategy.Overall, if you have any interest in platformers whatsoever, you should buy this game without a shadow of a doubt. It's a more mature story, with very likeable characters and fantastic platforming gameplay. The second-to-last boss (as in, non-True ending boss) may be one of the best fights I've seen in a platformer, period.My only problem with this game is that there will likely be a very long time to wait until the third!
_childDocuments_.name: Freedom Planet 2

_childDocuments_.review: This game is way superior to the first game, and I think the first game is already a masterpiece!The level design has improved so much... there was no stage that I didn't like...On the other side, I think the bosses are great but not as great as they were in the first game... same for some boss themes...Overall, I think this game is way better than the first one!
_childDocuments_.name: Freedom Planet 2

_childDocuments_.review: Freedom Planet 2 is a big improvement over the original game.  Better graphics, more mechanics, more stages, and a new playable character.  Also has a fantastic soundtrack.The biggest change of them all is adding items and assist options to make the game easier for those who struggle with the game's difficulty, especially the later bosses.  This is certainly easier than the first game but still has some challenging bosses later on so these features allow more casual players to still experience the whole game.Overall, if you enjoy fast paced platformers then you will almost certainly enjoy this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Freedom Planet 2

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely astoundingly good platformer from start to finish. The music, art, animation, gameplay mechanics and level design are all top notch. This game's predecessor was already one of the best games i'd ever played, and this improves on it so much - and in every possible regard - that it isn't even funny. There is no praise adequate for this absolute masterpiece. Play. Now.
_childDocuments_.name: Freedom Planet 2

_childDocuments_.review: Just like the first game, but even more of it. Fast paced gameplay, varied levels, great visuals+music, and a ridiculous amount of content.The level design is still top-tier, with huge sprawling levels full of fun stage gimmicks. Levels are fun whether you're exploring for gems and secrets, trying to beat the par times, or just trying to survive at all. There's around twice as many levels as the first game but they're substantially shorter, but that's fine since the first game's levels all felt like they should have been split in two.The returning characters each got a rework to their moveset, for the better. Lilac only got minor additions, but Carol and Milla got substantial reworks which make them much more fun (Milla is a lot more aggressive, Carol has a more interesting special attack which also provides more moevment). There's also a new fourth character, with her own extremely varied moveset.There's more bosses this time, and more variety to the bosses (lots of 1-on-1 duels with other human-sized characters, in addition to the giant robots with obvious weakpoints). An unfortunate number of them tend to spend most of the fight offscreen in the large arenas, but otherwise their design is quite good. Regular enemy design is good too.Overall, there's lots to love. If you liked the first game, you'll like the sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Freedom Planet 2

_childDocuments_.review: Hecking great time! The gameplay is much better in this one, many actions don't break up momentum when you're trying to blow through levels fast, the characters all play differently and feel there was a lot of time committed to making them play well. Levels are often awesome, think my one complaint  The returning cast is even better in this game, one of the antagonists chews up the scene whenever they appear! I did like this story more too, even though Merga didn't have the same presence as Brevon (guy was a menace) I did like her. Some of the boss fights were also amazing, over the top, spectacles. Play this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Freedom Planet 2

_childDocuments_.review: Freedom Planet 2. I mean, it's Freedom Planet, more refined, with better and more interesting stages, full support for 2 more playable characters, and a new item and revive system. Also they found a way to make lives work as an interesting system without them just being this thing you hoard across the game so that's good! The only major flaw I'd say is that the first few story cutscenes are a bit awkward, like they were a rough draft or wasn't fully polished. They had the issue in the first game, and like the first game, it all gets a lot better as the game goes on. The whole thing is an uphill road in terms of quality. Level design, writing, encounters, bosses. Heartily recommended! Also an hour of my playtime is just me vibing to the final overworld screens music.
_childDocuments_.name: Freedom Planet 2

_childDocuments_.review: Gotta say, this impressed me. I feel like every aspect has been expanded on in a positive manner, although the length and story are called into question.It feels a little longer than I expected but it was very satisfying, I enjoyed it amply and I never encountered any issues.Combat is engaging, although I don't feel very comfortable with the new dodge move it feels very strange for a platformer but it's something that doesn't feel mandatory at least.The returning characters all have expanded plots which feels great though the game very visibly has a problem with juggling so many new antagonists. Askal and Kalaw especially. But Serpentine is great, Syntax is great, Merga is great and all the returning characters feel wonderful to play along with the new character Neera Li.They took a character I very much disliked and made me feel pride when I completed her story. That takes a lot of heart. And I respect that. You should buy it if you like platformers and support galaxytrail for their hard work on all fronts.
_childDocuments_.name: Freedom Planet 2

_childDocuments_.review: After being delayed like 200 times, this game finally came out, and man it was worth the wait. There's so much love put into it, it improves everything from the first freedom planet, which already was a fantastic game, gameplay is fast and smooth and music is top tier. It's one of the best, if not the best 2d platformers out there.
_childDocuments_.name: Freedom Planet 2

_childDocuments_.review: It may have taken seven years since this game was announced, but the payoff's pretty damn great.It's a lot of what a sequel should be, bigger and bolder.Featuring a new playable character, larger skill set for all cast members, more stages, a good chunk of side content.Rankings, par times, accessories, potions, tons of good additions.Only major complaints I have is that the physics are still kind of jank, best way I can describe it is unnecessarily sticky and could benefit from a bigger focus on momentum, but what we have isn't bad, shame the rail sections ain't faster though.Bosses aswell have some camera issues I find, they're fun but some of them could really benefit from having the camera zoomed out way more.Besides that, it is just a joy to go as fast as possible, finding new ways to cut off seconds and get better and better at mastering each stage, it's exactly why I loved the original and why I loved this game.Really hoping we get DLC or a third entry.Game's great, well worth your money, easy recommendation.
_childDocuments_.name: Freedom Planet 2

_childDocuments_.review: The second entry to the Freedom Planet Franchise does well on delivering the high-speed platforming, puzzle, and combat gameplay established by the first game.The Characters and Story are still VERY well written, and voiced, and the difficulty curve (to my noob ass) is fair, but fairly challenging.I Highly Recommend Buying This Game.
_childDocuments_.name: Freedom Planet 2

_childDocuments_.review: The first game was good, but this one is even better. Doing my second playthrough now and still enjoying it. I like how each character requires a different style of gameplay to be successful. The story is also very good. Was surprised to notice some bigger name voice actors as well, like Chris Sabat.
_childDocuments_.name: Freedom Planet 2

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't beaten the game yet, but feel the need to leave something after getting halfway through the game, since I already know what lies ahead of me. I'm a huge fan of the original Freedom Planet, I might not have a ton of hours logged into it on Steam, but on Switch I've played it more. I truly believe this was worth the wait, granted the wait was agonizing, I can't remember the last time I waited almost 10 years for a game and walked away satisfied after playing it. It is clear that there was effort here to make Freedom Planet something other than a Sonic homage; in fact I learned the hard way that you shouldn't be rushing through these stages, take your time and explore. What I truly think gives this game replay value is the stage gimmicks, I say gimmicks in the best way possible since most levels bring some platforming twist to the table, I won't spoil them, but it is satisfying to memorize a level layout and flawlessly reach the end of the stage. Lives are contained to their level and acquiring an extra life isn't as easy like the first game, lives only exist so you can chase those perfect rankings.In the original game if you timed your dragon boost, you could cheese the game; I'm happy to say those moments aren't in this game as much, bosses screen filling attack patterns punishes reckless play. I know I might be made fun of for saying this, I find some of these bosses harder than Hollow Knight's Galaxy Trail really went above and beyond with the challenging boss fights. If there are some negatives I can list, I'm adjusting to navigating the map, I would have preferred a linear point A to point B like the original; but then you wouldn't see these amazing hub worlds that are do detailed I end up hanging out in them anyways( preference I guess). I find healing items a little unnecessary, I believe you should fail to master the game; I welcome the items that handicap the player for extra bonus points. Lastly the pixel work is breathtaking, I would say the 8 year development cycle has paid off. I've been tired of indie pixel games for a long time, I can make an exception in this case since this might be the best sprite work I've seen in a side scroller; it really shows the jump from the original game which used multimedia fusion and this game uses Unity. What really impresses me more than character animations are the background HD sprites, it truly feels like Avalice is a living breathing world. I'm currently on my default Lilac run, I'm itching to get to Milla since she is my favorite character and it looks like she's received the most improvements as a fighter.I would highly recommend this game, it is currently in my game of the year list alongside Bayonetta 3.
_childDocuments_.name: Freedom Planet 2

_childDocuments_.review: Freedom Planet 2 expands on everything in the original game and mostly upgrades it, gameplay is even smoother, abilities chain into each other or have new capabilities. The music is fantastic like the first game, but with some added variety. The storyline was probably the biggest surprise, considering how some people didn't like the darker tone of aspects with the original, they doubled down here but balanced the darker stuff and comedy in a much better way than the original. Aspects from the first game play a big role here, and i'm all there for that. This game also has room for a sequel which I hope happens now.There's a massive amount of stages and collectables here, it's overall just a really magical experience. My only negatives are I feel some of the bosses are a little too awkward, the fact you have to unlock Classic Mode this time, not that I didn't like the story, but I feel some folks aren't going to care and gating Classic Mode behind a first run feels kind of strange. Also where's my mahjong? Full thumbs up though, fantastic followup.
_childDocuments_.name: Freedom Planet 2

_childDocuments_.review: I thoroughly enjoyed the first Freedom Planet (even platinum'ed it), and this one goes beyond FP1 in all directions: the art has now moved to more or a 32/64-bit look (Saturn/Dreamcast-era), and the scope of the game is much larger. There is a great variety in stages, each with its own quirks, and all the characters seem to have had some new techs added. I'm still playing through my first character as Lilac, but so far it has been a blast. Highly recomended!
_childDocuments_.name: Freedom Planet 2

_childDocuments_.review: Loved the first game, this has practically blew it out of the water (pun 100% intended)I love all the little citizens you can talk to and all the extra stuff you can do after you finish the game, and by the looks of it, the different characters perspectives are more fleshed out this time around! (i only have a little bit of millas story to go off of rn)The gameplay of everyone feels great too, it was already great in the first game but this one adds some new things (as well as a completely new playable character, Neera, which btw had the biggest glowup of the century with the new and improved art style, shes so pretty!!!)The voice acting is for sure leagues better than the first (but i still loved the first games voices despite that) and the humor of this game is on point, I especially adore the little mascot otter in purusa!All in all, even if you DIDN'T play the first game, this is well worth the play! I beat the main story as lilac in 10 hours, and there are 4 total characters and many things to do after the story, do the math, the experience is well worth the 20 something dollars!!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Freedom Planet 2

_childDocuments_.review: At the time of writing this review before, I had not finished the game. I am updating it now to show that I have finished it on at least one character. I will say this: It isn't a perfect game, but the passion OOZES out of it. It plays incredibly smoothly and really pushes the player to get good. It does well to recapture the feel of the SNES and SEGA Genesis days, and some of their difficulty. I played it on the hardest difficulty to start with, and it was a painful journey, but it was worthwhile, as it really helped me improve my play. The Normal difficulty will be accessible to people starting the game off or just picking up the genre. The bosses are far more lenient without Hard Mode's doubled damage.The Character designs are even better than they were in the first one, and it really feels like the voice-actors not only enjoyed voicing the characters but had genuine passion for the project. I can only really remark on playstyles I'm proficient with, and I have to say that I am bad at Lilac and Milla, though players good with them in the previous game will have an easy time using them in this one. Carol is a titanic step up from what she was in Freedom Planet 1. Her DPS is much higher, and her gameplay is more streamlined and intuitive. I cannot speak for fans of Carol with the Motorcycle, as I barely used it. To me, it feels and plays worse than without the Motorcycle, but I grew up playing Megaman X and Zero. Since Carol reminds me so much of Zero (Zero series on GBA) in gameplay, I really meshed well with it and it felt amazing to play as. Her kit is excellent, and, once an opening is found, she can eviscerate Boss' health bars with stunning ease. She really plays like a cat.Neera is more sluggish, but she is a precision powerhouse. She is less agile but still quick, more relying on careful positioning than merely blasting through a stage with invincibility (though she is still capable in that regard). Players that like being close to enemies will like her, especially once they really get good with her slower attacks and utilizing her "Focus" self-buff.The Guard System can be thought of as more of a Street Fighter Parry with massively lenient timing. It is required for some Boss fights, and makes some stages much easier, and it is very easy to use (I'm bad at parrying in Street Fighter but I got pretty good with it in this game. It's not hard).The stage design is imperfect but pretty smooth for the most part. There were times where I got lost and questioned which way I was supposed to go, but a little exploration and a lot of going this way and that sorted it out. The terrain is a little frustrating in some places, as surfaces meant to be walked up vertically will throw the character at a sharp angle if a jump is done while running on the wall. Since some terrain behaves in such a way in Boss fights, it makes them unnecessarily difficult, and makes the losses inflicted by them feel unfair. That said, It's all very smooth barring that one hiccup and it will not stop me from recommending the game because it can be played around with even the barest amount of experience. Some enemy placement is annoying, though. On-screening an enemy and then feeling like there is no time to react as one takes damage from something one couldn't have possibly seen feels bad, though, again, it's not game-breaking and these instances don't occur often. The warning markers are a bit large, and, at one time, prevented me from seeing something I was supposed to be avoiding. Not perfect, but still able to be played around and still tons of fun.The story is actually pretty decent for what this game is. The team respected the characters. They expanded on them and leaned into their personalities pretty hard. Carol was already my favorite, and, as a Carol fan, I was exceedingly well-pleased. I'd heard the same for Milla. I'm sure Lilac and Neera's characters are just as well-represented. As a bonus, Neera is actually likable in this game. Hints are dropped of developments in the other parts of the stories, so it really encourages the player to play through with all characters.Merga is a villain that was done well with the narrative and "show, don't tell" techniques used. She was done far better than Brevon, but still, somehow, lacks his innate menace. That said, I really have very few complaints, if any, about the direction the story took. This is how a sequel should be done.The music is excellent, by the way. Maybe not as punchy as some of the first Freedom Planet's tracks in some spots but definitely, DEFINITELY amazing. This OST is a whole lot better than the first Freedom Planet's. I only found a few of the themes not hitting as hard, and that was rare. I also was concentrating on tough boss patterns and trying not to die so I will have time now to appreciate the OST more since I'm not trying to survive something that will delete my health bar.Games like this don't come along too often. Makers rarely have this kind of passion anymore and they rarely execute it even half as well. This is a sequel done right. This is what the Triple A industry can't seem to get right, and yet this little team of developers with gobs of passion and a fraction of the budget did amazingly well. This game is worth every penny and I am glad I could support it.
_childDocuments_.name: Freedom Planet 2

_childDocuments_.review: I am utterly speechless. After just finishing this game completely, I only can say one thing: Thank you, Galaxytrail. Sabrina, you and your team gave us a work of art that I'm going to remember for a long time, and one I'm DEFINITELY going to replay and recommend to others. Worth the 6 year wait by a long shot, even if it is a little buggy still.
_childDocuments_.name: Freedom Planet 2

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic sequel. Takes the first game, makes it bigger, and INJECTS IT WITH DRAGON STEROIDS!The new:- World map- Hub levels (First game was supposed to have them, but were cut, and I see why, because they are HILARIOUSLY glitchy)- Equippable accessories and passive potion charges that alter various stats/effects (but appear to degrade your rank, because REAL MEN DON'T EQUIP RPG TRINKETS TO MAKE THE GAME EASIER (I am not a real man apparently)- 1 new playable character (Neera)- Generally improved combat, as well as a new Dodge/dash function. It works pretty well. I am now going to go back to the first game and try pressing the nonexistent dodge button in vain.- And a bunch more.I'd say the difficulty of bosses are overall a bit harder than the first game's (minus pre-nerf steroido Brevon of FP1), but the ability to dodge-dash makes bosses more tight. Most bosses are fought in the middle or end of a stage, but every now and then it pulls a Klonoa 2, and puts a boss only stage on the map, which is neat, more games like that should do this, at least at times. Speaking of Klonoa 2, just like FP1, some levels do indeed drag on for quite a bit, which I'm fine with, but some people like their bite sized levels. Good old Klonoa 2/Freedom Planet level syndrome.In the hub levels, there's tons of charming characters to talk to for lots of optional dialogue. Soooo many npcs. Some of the characters are designed by Tyson Tan, which I somewhat know from DA eons ago, his artstyle is cool and all, but sometimes its "Hyper cute", whereas I prefer the more consistent artstyle of the first game (Although, I'd say the artstyle of this game is generally better, and certainly more detailed). Whenever I saw something that looked overly Tyson-Tan-y, it kind of took me out of it (both in a good and bad way). Especially that one mech fight. I'm like "Oh no, it's The Tyson Tan Mech" weirdly enough, it's the boss I had the most trouble with, needed like 2-3 continues, didn't think I needed even 1 continue for every other boss. I feel kinda funny now for getting my ass handed to me by something so cute. Speaking of lives, you can't horde them like you could in the first game, but on the flip side, you always start with a few every level (can be increased with a potion effect), as well as having the choice of using a life to start from last checkpoint with full health, or start off exactly where you died, but with low hp (hp recovery can also be increased with a potion effect).How the potions work is that they are passive, you do not actively drink them. There are 5 slots to put whatever potion effect you want, you could have 1 charge of 5 different effects, or 2/3 charges of 2 different effects, or 5 charges with 1 effect, if you want to focus on your favored effect. Makes me feel like a Witcher mixing these potion charges into the bottle. Milla is a Witcher confirmed.You can buy potions/accessories/music from various shops in various towns, by spending either gems, as found in the first game, or enemy cores, dropped by most enemies, or gold pieces, which can be bought with gems/cores, and sometimes found in chests. Several accessories can also be found in chests, but most of them make the game harder in exchange for a bigger gem bonus (reminds me of Supergiant difficulty gimmicks)The music is superb as usual, the levels are fairly similar to FP1's in structure, you have your normal/action stages, puzzle stages, some key item hunty stages, and sometimes a mix of the above. As well as a few SCHMUP stages, just like the first game. That one mech schut stage was pretty ridiculous/chaotic and kind of glitchy. Loved it.The voiceacting is as good as the first's, there's a good lot more of it, and the main villain is likeable and sympathetic . Unlike the first game's villain which was just SCUMSCUMSCUM that you love to hate. I like me a good hateable villain (Brevon), but I usually prefer the more likeable ones that you can sympathize with.There's also some neat twists in the story. Such as the Magister revealing his face

_childDocuments_.review: A modern masterpiece. This game should set the standard for all other games in its devotion to just  in whatever ways they want to.There is an insane amount of quality and polish to the game, even on day 1 of release. It is obviously a labor of love and that is felt through the way its design meets players at whatever level they want to engage with it. Do you just like platforming? Here's ~30 stages for you to run through with unique set pieces like low gravity, air bubbles, boosters, darkness, etc. Quick-reflex combat? Got tons of that with a huge variety of bosses. Story? Dive in or just skip it if you want. Achievements and challenge modes? Go wild. Favor different play styles? There's 4 unique characters you can be. Find the game too easy or difficult? There's assist options and items which augment the difficulty. Speedrunning? Plenty of in-game timers and record trackers available. It's just.... overwhelming. There's  here. There's a museum of collectibles to fill up. There's a photo mode that I don't know who asked for but it's in here! There's hidden collectibles that unlock multiple endings. There's a jukebox. There's dozens of unique fully animated NPCs with distinct character. Basically every single thing from the previous game has been refined and improved to make gameplay more fun and dynamic: cancelable dragon boosts, instant Milla cubes, a guard / instashield button, a broader moveset in general like Lilac's up-slash, Carol's Jump Disc and bike stashing... and also she's actually fun to play as now ( :-P ). Neera adds yet another playstyle to the mix. Bosses do that thing I love where they're actually involved in the course of the whole level and not just showing up out of nowhere at the end. For the most part their fights are fun (maybe just a bit pattern-heavy) but there are a few stinkers (pretty much any water-based boss...) Those are balanced out by the few that had really unique mechanics or were just eye-popping WOWZA the whole way through.There's a lot more I can say about specific things but I want to keep this somewhat brief. Freedom Planet 2 is an easy Game of the Year 2022 for me, and if you ask me in a few months I will probably agree it is one of the finest games I have played in my life.

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished it as Lilac. The game absolutely blew me away on multiple occasions. The levels are many but are fun, unique, and varied. Combat mechanics are refined, so many bosses and yet they're all unique and fun to fight. There were so many times where I truly felt like "now I can see why this game took so long!" I really think GalaxyTrail went above and beyond with this game!My biggest gripe would have to be the last two levels. Just like FP1, the last couple of levels feel unfairly difficult. It throws so many enemies your way and traps (like spikes on grind rails while you're going super fast so barely any time to avoid them). These levels did have unique mechanics just like the rest of the game which is very impressive considering the high level count in this game but yeah I think the last two could've been a bit more polished.There were also a few levels where I couldn't figure out how to progress for some time due to unclear objective/path so I think that could've been made a bit more clear.The story won't blow your socks off but as someone who isn't crazily obsessed with finding the best writing ever in video games (like so many gamers tend to be...) I very much enjoyed it. Lots of high stakes and emotional moments. The dialogue is heavily refined from the first game and there are lots of really neat reveals about the characters we know and love from the first game. The music was, as usual, really good but unfortunately nothing really stuck out to me as much as FP1's soundtrack. Still the composer did an excellent job.I hear lots of people have ran into bugs and personally I haven't experienced anything too bad or annoying. I did have trouble setting up my PS3 controller using the Playstation button icons. Lots of the buttons displayed in the game did not match what I pressed on my controller. However, setting the icons back to the default "numbers" made everything a non-issue. I think its worth bringing up to people reading this that, for now as of writing this review on 9/16/2022, you shouldn't bother trying to change icons. Just stick to the numbers!All in all, I think the game was very much worth the wait. Definitely one of my favorite 2D platformers of all time now. I replayed FP1 many times because it's just really fun to play but now I don't think I ever see myself going back to it and instead probably going to replay this game a whole bunch from now on! Thanks GalaxyTrail!

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing masterpiece of a sequel to one of my favorite speedy action platformers of all time. I played the original Freedom Planet, and waited 7 long years for Freedom Planet 2. I appreciate the transition from linear classic story progression to branching adventure quests that meet back together into a main path after completion, while exploring various maps with town hubs in between...There are also plenty of items that you can alter gameplay with as you unlock more shops, whether to aid you or to make the game much more challenging which is sometimes required to get the highest ranks.Boss battles are notably memorable and numerous as well in Freedom Planet 2. Many bosses follow a changing pattern, however the boss 'characters' that you can battle are surprisingly responsive and certainly provide that spike in difficulty when a change of pace is needed. Not only that, you can fight the bosses again later after a certain amount of progression.All four main characters are unique and dynamic from everything I've tested. The only things I can say I find lacking, is that I want more playable characters if there aren't any or some kind of online or local PVP character fighting arena...Regardless, the swath of gameplay additions and improvements to Freedom Planet 2 enrich the experience enough as is. The upgrade in graphics certainly has done wonders in the sprites and artwork too. 10/10 I will be taking my time playing this game, that way I can enjoy it for long as I can.

_childDocuments_.review: There's a lot to this game, There's 4 characters with their own skills that completely change how you play the game. Lilac can pull a Rocket Knight and shoot in any of 8 directions with Dragon Boost and she has a double jump that has a slight hover with Cyclone. Carol has a variety of martial arts with a Wild claw for extra damage, wall jump like Mega Man X she can roll to damage enemies and gain speed, can get  a motorcycle to change her moveset entirely where she can backflip, boost and such. Neera has a wand to shoot ice projectiles from, she can cover enemies with ice and bounce off of them or shatter them and even skates at top speed.Milla can build up murder cubes to either spam light attacks or shoot a big shot. She can flutter her limbs for a Yoshi style jump.All characters also have basic attacks and this is my BIGGEST TIP when playing either Freedom Planet 1 or 2:When attacking if you hit up or down will give you different attacks- and different attacks in the air. They're very, VERY useful and most people I've seen play ignore them and these are some of the more damaging attacks.Lilac's up+attack is an uppercut that not only goes a bit higher than her jump, it does far more damage than her cyclone attack- and you can go right into a down+attack that is a stomp that also does a lot of damage.Neera's attacks in the air are vital to her gaining speed, you can really, really make her go super fast and stay in the air a long while.  Carol's down attack is great for her gaining speed and her disc will help you get around the map or double team an enemy since you can attack while it's doing damage on it's own. I haven't played Mila but I know her changes are pretty big vs her in the first game. She can be more aggressive with more attacks for one and I think has more HP than she did previously. So the characters themselves have a ton to offer in terms of variety and replayabilty. The game itself (So far I'm only 4.6 hours in) is crazy just how much they packed in. Huge levels with tons of routes and spots for characters to use their skills to get around with. The game has much improved writing and  voice work over the first. That's not to knock what the VAs did in 1, I felt a lot of it was their equipment being so different - which isn't the case here. I wish I could explain that better, just know if you thought the story and dialog was a bit lacking in 1- 2 is does it all so much better. The game also has items to help or hinder your gameplay.Hindering items are there to 1- challenge yourself and 2- get your bonus up for a higher rank. Potions & positive items will lower your bonus and your rank.So if you have a item with a negative that boosts your bonus by 75% and you fill a potion to a full 5 you lose 25%. Tie that in with a no-hit bonus and you too can get the fancy rainbow S-Rank.Or you can ignore all that because ranks don't really effect anything from what I can tell. The game feels, so good to play. I can tell I'm going to put a lot of time into this one over the years. The one gripe I think someone could leverage against the game is you have to play through the adventure mode once before unlocking classic mode. Classic mode being you just get the stages. But seeing how much work they put into this and how good it is? It's worth it. This is a heck of a game, they really upped everything in this, the art design and visuals are a big leap over the first game, the stages aren't cut into parts anymore and it's just one large stage with SO many routes to go through. They leave it up to you to explore or blitz through. The music is, so, good. Performance: What I really like is the game can run at over 60fps, I don't know all the numbers off hand but I know it can do over 144hz. Other good news the game can run on a potato, my laptop sporting a 5 year old i5 and a HD620 runs the game at 1080p/60fps just fine. Just make sure you have a good set of speakers, the music is worth it. Edit: The bugs I had in the review have been addressed & I beat the game as Lilac (I'm aware there's a 'true ending' but haven't done that. I think Freedom Planet 1 had better bosses & boss music  & FP2 has a level I'd equate to Sonic CD's Wacky Work Bench in terms of "Really bad level design" as it has teleporter walls that send you all over in a disorienting way. But that is just one bad level out of a ton of them and as a whole FP2 is a really great game with a lot of fun levels, great music & fun levels (except the 1). Tons of replayability and I'm sure in a few months I'll have a bunch of hours racked up & will be revisiting this like Sonic 3 & Knuckles since I first got that.

_childDocuments_.review: A new engine, a new artstyle, new tricks, and a new plot.just beat Lilac's story and hoo boy is it a ride. i'll have to beat the other character's stories to see where they diverge, but for the most part all of them stick together as a party.that said, if you hated FP1's level design, you will loathe FP2's design. not my problem, however, i actually love the ♥♥♥♥ out of this since it's more than "hold right to reach the finish" and offers rewards for more than just simply "reaching the end of the level as fast as possible" and while i did do that with Lilac, i'm definetly going to take my time with the rest of the cast that isn't her. there's so many secrets i have yet to collect so that'll be a while.did get softlocked on one boss but that was during Day 1 and it was easy to just restart the fight without closing the game. kudos for making a solid game that has some (even if unintentional) anti-softlock measures.the art and music is absolutely amazing. 10/10 would gawk at a boss and drool at how they look again. _childDocuments_.review: An awesome sequel with great improvements all around! Highly recommended buy to fans of action platformers.Compared to the sequel it has a ton of new features, modes and content. There are many challenges and the achievements are really fun to complete. The engine is different from the original and thus more robust and stable, I had only very minor technical issues with setting my controller and nearly getting stuck in an area but these are easy fixes and to be expected from a project of this size on release day. I had no major technical or gameplay related issues otherwise which is a lot more than you can say from some AAA titles.There is a ton of character variety and replayability, tons of music that all sounds great. The artwork is beatiful and if it interests you there's many cutscenes and hubworlds with NPC's that are almost entirely voice acted. If that's not your thing it can be skipped more or less in its entirety.I'm singing the game's praises here because it's really just that good and I think there's something here to enjoy for everyone as long as they enjoy platformers at least. The game also has a very good difficulty curve but if you find it too hard there are items you can use and game settings you can enable.If I had to give it a score I'd give it a 9/10 so far. It's engaging, challenging and just plain fun. Definitely a must-buy from me.EDIT: I have now finished the game and it definitely changed character in the end-game. The quality of the level design fell sharply after the first 2/3rds of the levels and even with 7 years of work the later levels feel like they are padded and they lose their sense of direction in a few places. The first game had much better end game both in design and story and the last boss left me feeling quite unfulfilled. The game as a whole is still a definite recommend from me and there are plenty of great parts to enjoy in the mix but I'd probably drop my score to a 7/10.
