_childDocuments_.review: So I will do my best to explain my feelings regarding this game and my opinion. I do not often review games but I will do a quick TL:DR and then you can continue reading if you want. Warning, there will be spoilers. Pretty game, bad story and many glitches. Pros- Pretty world- Combat can be fun- Lots to exploreCons- Story is honestly not that great, maybe a 3/10- Quiet a few areas glitched to where you cannot finish them.- Characters felt rather boring. Now the rest of my review and the spoilers. So when it comes to games like this I am a big time explore, like straight up just walk off ignore the main quest and start looting and exploring areas. I loved that so many areas had goals to encourage you to explore the area and get loot or other good things. I went through going everywhere I could to try to get as much loot as possible and see this beautiful world that was created. Problem is there are quiet a few zones that when you enter and try to complete they are glitched so you cannot finish them. Which frustrates me when I am going through trying complete all the areas. Now onto the story, you have to unite the tribes and kill all the boss monsters eating the trees. At the start you get to pick the evil tribe or the good tribe, no in between.  Each boss fight is going to require you to use the special mount for the area which is a nice touch and kind of fun.  So I choose the good paths normally, going through and exploring helping everyone and that good jazz. But what gets really old is the narrator just randomly talking about how you have to save the world, or when you enter a area you have to hear about how to corporations killed the world and this is all their fault. Gets really really old really fast. Each tribe did not feel really different from the last one, felt like a re-skin of the previous tribe and the same couple of things to be able to take a base and then the fort. For the bosses they felt the same for the most part as well, you shoot the boss use the special for the mount you are using and keep shooting between cut scenes. Over all I will say if you are interested in this game get it if it is heavily on sale, not a lot of replay value to it and not a lot to keep ones attention. That has been my opinion on it, as I said I do not review often but this game honestly just left me so disappointed I had to write something.

_childDocuments_.review: I just started playing this game, so this review is subject to change over time. So far, the game play is fun. Yes, eventually you experience an open world with very few invisible walls on cliff sides that you're evidently not supposed to climb. The combat is fun.However, what's easily the most irritating part of the game is the fact that there's a narrator in the game. And ironically, you ask the narrator questions... as in... you break the 4th wall...Ever play a game called Hyper Light Drifter? In THAT game, there's not one bit of text, and not one bit of dialogue. It's a 2D game, but it's after the same target market. A similar Genre. And the fact that there's no dialogue and no text in Hyperlight Drifter -- it makes you more and more interested in discovering the world, and discovery truly feels like discovery.But In Biomutant, the narrator makes the game feel discovered. Before you can discover anything, most of the time, the narrator has already described everything. It's the polar opposite of what Hyper Light Drifter did. Although I don't think every game needs to model themselves after Hyper Light Drifter, I do feel that the game teaches some great things about game design... Things that the developers behind Biomutant could learn.Often times this narrator describes things either as you're experiencing them, or he's telling you what the developers think you, the player, should be thinking and feeling... and to me... it just seems like if the developer doesn't trust that I can observe, think, and feel things without being told... then it's not as enjoyable of a video game as it should be... And that's not the case, actually. I start to observe, think and feel something, I can begin to really get into it. And then the narrator speaks and ruins the experience. The narrator needs to be 100% deleted from this game. He ruins so much of the experience.And the narrator just wont freaking shut up. If there's any moment where you're content, looking at the beautiful world and graphics, enjoying the simulated nature, the narrator will randomly spout off some idiotic bit of fortune cookie wisdom like "He who stands on toilet is high on pot". But fortunately there's enough of the game that's sound and solid. When you talk to NPC characters -- they speak a type of gibberish, like they do in Zelda. But instead of you just reading what they're saying directly, the narrator describes what they're saying from the third person. So, as an example, the Narrator will hear the NPC say something and then he'll tell you: "He says that there's a bug in your ear."This makes the game feel like endless exposition. In a book, endless exposition is a sign of a bad book. And in a video game, endlessly listening to the same narrator spewing exposition and then spewing dialogue as if it were more exposition... that gets really irritating... to the point to where you just want to skip conversations with NPC's entirely -- even during your first play through... because you're not missing out on anything. And I say that because skipping it feels like ripping a leech off. Why is that? Because you're not talking to the NPCs'. When you try to talk to an NPC, there's that Narrarator's wall of "He says this" and "He says that" and "He's worried about this" or "that".... You're disconnected from the plight of the characters because it's all filtered out with the narrator.Picture this: OPTION 1: What's more compelling, an NPC is running up to you, as monsters are chasing him saying "We're all going to die! Someone PLEASE SAVE US!!!!"OROPTION 2: An NPC is running up to you, as monsters are chasing him, he makes some squeaky weird noises and the narrator says: "Through the rising sun you see a friendly creature running through the leaves fearful that he's about to die and politely asks if you'd vanquish the very thing that is his worst nightmare." (I may have phrased that oddly, but that's how the narrator kind of talks... that's how he comes off. The formality and inflections of the narrator is hard to translate into text. And this is my best impersonation of all of that with only and just text to work with.)Personally, I'd take "OPTION 1" in a heart beat, EVERY TIME.Maybe the developers didn't think they had the budget for OPTION 1, but Zelda has done it just fine, for decades, without hiring a bunch of voice actors... So... I don't see the excuse.Also -- sometimes you're posed with moral situations... and just like Kronk in "The Emperor's New Groove" you have an angel on your left and right shoulder. One good, one evil. And they argue it out with possibly the most annoying voices ever.So the only voices you'll hear in this game are a narrator that spews endless narration, or these annoying angel things... In essence ALL DIALOGUE IN THIS GAME IS ANNOYING AS ALL HELL!Whoever came up with these ideas was a moron.You're never interacting with anyone but the Narrator and these stupid shoulder angels. And if you try to interact with someone else, you only experience this other person with third person interaction... through the narrator... It really pulls you out of the game, every time.I'm going to continue playing. I do enjoy MOST of this experience. It's kind of cool. I WOULD PLAY A SEQUEL -- however, they'd need to add actual voice actors into the game, get rid of the shoulder angels and they'd have to 100% get rid of the narrator.In fact... I WOULD SUGGEST TO THE DEVELOPERS to work on patching THIS game so that those things happen for THIS game... why wait to fix the sequel if you can fix the game you already have?Another thing that's been irritating me to no end. This game is hyper political and preachy. It's set in a world where the big bad humans poluted the world. Blah blah blah, social commentary... blah blah blah... we should have used green energy... blah blah blah... no one ever had anything nice, we just had things that were new... blah blah blah... we should have known better... blah blah blah... now it's up to this new age of mutated animals to rebuild the world...I don't want to be preached to. I actually want to escape all of that crap when I get into a video game. I'm kind of insulted that the developers thought that placing Ferngully into this game would be an intelligent idea. I'm surprised your mom wasn't killed off by a human hunter like Bambi.Or that the story isn't about how a truck has spewed toxic waste, like in "Once Upon A Forrest".Don't preach to me! DON'T PREACH TO ME!And there's no escaping it either. The narrator just won't freaking shut up about it. It'd be one thing if I could just SEE evidence of it. But it's like having that one irritating person that held the open secret that he hates you, following you around all the time telling you how much he hates you, ALL THE TIME.Quite a bit of the game deals with this magical tree. When you get close to it, you see that it's roots reach out into the sky, and so I used my hang glider to get up onto those roots and I clipped right through them. This killed my sense of wanting to discover more about the world. When I see something so cool I want to jump on to it, and I can't.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, it's hard to say if I recommend this game in its current state. $60 is a lot of money and we all want to know we're getting our money's worth. I'm easy to please when it comes to post-apocalyptic animals games, but this review is for people who are thinking of purchasing this game (not for clones of me)...I wanted BIOMUTANT for a while and I'm loving things about it, but sadly, there are some deal-breaking flaws. Please read below for the PROS and CONS that I discovered within the first 1.5 hrs I have played the game (thru the first chapter).PROS: BIOMUTANT has that classic star-quality potential. The game is very wholesome and sweet. It kind of reminds me of Kameo. Anyone remember that adorable game? It was on Xbox in the early 2000s. To me, this is somewhat of a positive because of the whimsical nostaglia; however game quality from the 2000s is nowhere close to what is should be now...so, that is probably a negative for most you who are wondering if you should buy the game. BIOMUTANT has that magical Spyro or RAYMAN quality to it, too, which can be nice for someone who likes pleasant, straightforward  games. They give you an option on your preferred difficulty level, so that's a plus. The first chapter helps you along in gentle way while showing you the ropes (teaching you the controls etc). The story has potential and right out of the gate (pro or con -- you decide) you begin to understand your place in a beautiful plagued World. The first chapter is a great introduction for someone new  to this genre of game. The graphics are insanely gorgeous. Hypnotic almost. You're so charmed by the colors and beauty of the environments that you forget about your computer's mortality. I'm enjoying the game quite a bit, so far, despite the CONS that I will talk about in a minute.  The characters you will meet are presented in an abrupt but pleasant way...even the baddies (meaning the story feels rushed). So, to me, this is a great game for kids to play if you parents are wondering if BIOMUTANT is appropriate for your child. So far, it seems to be the perfect game for kids whose parents are looking for a game option that isn't aggressive and gory. CONS:The developers have really dropped the ball with respect to the game as a product. It sucks to say that because obviously this is someone's baby, ya know? Sadly, even if they are new to the gaming biz they should have a pretty strong grasp on the key components of what makes a game great (as gamers themselves) if they're going to ask for $60. So, this disappoints me, greatly. BIOMUTANT is too expensive in its current state. I think Experiment 101 should have taken maybe 6 more months to a year to develop the game. It feels pretty clunky (character movement/mechanics) and feels moderately unpolished. The story, though passable with potential... is way too rushed. There's no real 'sink your teeth into it' sort of development to the story, so far. It feels forced. The pace makes you worry that your journey in this new World is going to end too quickly. I like to become attached to my own character and develop some empathy for her and wonder, 'What the heck am I doing here?' before I'm forced to become acquainted with a new character. Even if the developers polish up the game, I really see no way to come back from such a fatal flaw. The story is out there. Open-World? Not really. feels very small. Fishbowl small. It almost feels like a platformer and I know that wasn't Experiment 101's intent. Then again, I'm only on the 2nd Chapter so this could change. I hope.It's feels bad to leave a negative because I'm enjoying the game overall. It does feel nice to progress through a game without having to think too much (I'm lookin' at you DARK SOULS), but this could cause some people to become bored pretty quickly, especially for people who are mainly fps. I enjoy wholesome games just as much as I do the less wholesome ones...so again, I'm easy to please. I would say the quality of the game as it stands is probably worth MAYBE $29.99 but during a sale for like $24.99. I hate to say that...I had such high hopes for the game and I still have faith that the developers will take on board the post release reviews and improve the game (if that's possible);  polish it a bit and PLEASE optimize the game so the graphics don't destroy everyone's motherboard.I hope the developers continue to tweak the game because personally, I'm loving it....just a bastard of a game on my computer and I have a decent-ish set up:Alienware Gaming Laptop15.6in Full HDIntel Core i7-7700HQ16GB DDR4 RAM256GB SSD + 1TB HDDGeForce GTX 1070I wish I could recommend this game in its current state but $60 is too much for a game this rushed that was released in 2021. Experiment 101, I'm so sorry for this negative reveiw. PLEASE polish up the game so more people can enjoy the idea and the gem that I know this game can become. Show these folks that the game is worth $60 and that you care about their gaming experience. _childDocuments_.review: Ok so I originally gave this game a negative review but after spending about 50 more hours in the game and unlocking all of the achievements I'm gonna give it another go.So originally I wasn't very happy with this game because it seemed impossible to go for an only melee build because of how clunky it felt and how some bosses are built for ranged. Throwing that idea out the window and conforming to weaving guns into my playstyle, combat actually started to feel good. And after getting better gear and the fixes they implemented to melee, melee was feeling a lot better as well. So overall combat is pretty fun now, although I still wish it was possible to do melee only. But with Super Wung fu only activating after doing 3 unique wung foos and certain boss mechanics, it's just not possible without shooting yourself in the foot.There were some other problems I had with the game like bugs and the annoying narrator's dialogue. But they quickly started throwing out patches, fixing the bugs and providing a small fix to speed up the dialogue if either the narrator or the mumble the npc's make are disabled. Having both on at the same time is still completely annoying, but I'm glad they did something to make that part of the experience feel decent. Overall, I'd say this game is definitely worth the buy IF it's on sale for $40 or less. _childDocuments_.review: Aight look. This isn't aiming to be a direct thumbs up. This is aiming to be an average middle star because it made me think about something. Balance.On a technical level it isn’t as in dept or life changing as some other open world RPGs. It wasnt trying to crush your soul or take you on a wild ride. Biomutant felt more like watching an off brand muppets adventure show. The first thought I had was “This is the kids show of open world RPGs” it’s not meant to be overly complicated with a million combo move sets, tear jerking roller coasting stories, or mind numbing min max number crunching.The stakes were low considering the worlds survival was on the line. There was no feeling of actual rush or dread. The NPCs went on with their lives, greeting your dark or light character fairly the same as if it were just the worlds nature to spit out chaotically beautiful mishaps. Things either go right or wrong, but life continues.The game had its flaws. Odd animations, graphical oddities, and the occasional stuck quest. The gameplay felt very repetitive and linear. The crafting system became a recycling nightmare when all you want are good parts.Yet the game also gave me something to do, something for me to smile at and not have to worry. The stakes were so low and the expectations were just as low. I just wanted a game to loot and beat stuff up. Nothing more, nothing less. Just like when I was a kid (and adult) I just wanna turn on the TV and watch some cartoons to just smile and have fun without trying to feel invested.It was charming~

_childDocuments_.review: I had a lot of fun with the game, as I think it has one of the coolest and prettiest game worlds out there (on par or better than botw), but is ruined by the lack of meaningful changes in combat. The combat is very interesting for the first 10% of the game but then after you've learned all 2 extra skills for your weapon or 3 or so for magic, literally nothing changes beyond that, just stat increases. Similar thing with enemy design but not quite as bad, the monster type enemies are fine as they have interesting attacks (if buggy at times) and are diverse enough, but the npcs are pretty static. The progression is also really bad, especially for melee, because magic users don't get any real benefit from finding weapons so your just screwed until you level up, and melee weapons damage seems to cap out like 75% through the game but is really overpowered until then, so you are just wiping out all the enemies, until you're not and then all enemies start taking forever to kill which makes combat even more annoying. I again cant stress enough how cool and fleshed out the world in this game is but I really just wish the developers will come back and add some more content, I really think just 2 more talents for every weapon and some more talents for magic would pretty much fix combat/combat progression. Overall I recommend playing the game for the exploration but the combat really just feels like chore getting in your way and really damages the experience.TLDR: Beautiful fleshed out game world ruined by extremely repetitive combat and bad progression that could all be fixed by some relatively small content updates.

_childDocuments_.review: I read the bad reviews and wanted to give it a try myself, and i must say, while many of the critics are justified, it is a good game. It's just not the amazing game many people expected. The first few hours are a bit tough to get through because you get a huge tutorial. Then you explore the world, which is the most fun part of the game. Now it depends on the people how long they can find enjoyment out of that, because tasks and areas become repetitive after a while. If you can platin Assassins Creed you might find to love this game. If you find AC boring and repetitive this game wont be for you. The reviewers were right in saying that the game had a lot of good ideas but did not think it through. Or maybe they just released it early. The main story is really bad, but the side quests are better. I could have seen the story being a pc/console version of "the little prince" given its a fable, but it does not live up to that. Also it's indeed unclear if this was meant for parents or for kids. I also want to address one of the biggest issue that takes out the fun for many people early and that is the loot spiral. Around level 18 you easily find and use ultimate weapons, which are the strongest in the game. From then on every content is easy, which is one reason players complain about the difficulty and even worse, every loot you find is worse than what you have. Pros:+ unique world and exploration+ graphics+ photo mode+ crafting+ combat+ extensive update after 1 week which addresses many issues such as difficulty, the intro, which was too long or annoying gibberish+ environmental story telling + post apocalyptic setting + side questsBiggest Cons:- Everything related to sound- balancing and loot spiral - main story is just bad and poorly executed- rpg elements such as classes are half baked- easy puzzlesWish list for improvements:+ Voices could have really brought the characters to life and increased the immersion. It could have also worked if the narrator would have made "voices" for them, like a parent telling a fable to his child or an audio book+ transmog or cosmetic slots for all the cool gear you find. Right now you have to decide between stats and looks+ quest lines for ultimate gear and weapons should be only available later in the game around level 35-40Conclusion: I bought this game, because i'd rather support a small developer studio with unique ideas than a triple A studio milking the same franchise over and over. It depends a bit on what type of player you are if or how much you will like this game, which is why it is so polarizing in the reviews.

I've beaten the main story and I'm starting a NG+ file. It's my game of the year so far and I truly have no complaints. When I wrote my initial review I didn't appreciate the combat as much as I should have and when I got the hang of it I loved the variation in weapons and admittedly would use weaker weapons simply because they were more fun.If I had to give criticism now that I have played more, I would say the story was a little lackluster with my biggest complaint being the seemingly crystal clear line between "good" and "evil"... _childDocuments_.review: ✅  Impressively made by a 20 person dev team✅  Major patch released just six days after release day. Not a late day one patch, but an update that addressed some of the biggest bugs and fan complaints of the game. The speed of this update is unprecedented, and shows how much the devs really listen to their audience.✅ Top-tier graphics and performance at a stable 60 FPS. Photo Mode lets you bask in the environment around you✅  Big and beautiful open world. I'm at 25 hours and taking my time on my first playthrough. My progress is at 8% according to the in-game Completion% and I feel like I have so much more ahead of me.✅ Customizing your character and selecting their perks is really fun. Innate aspects of your character can be changed after character creation later in the game, but there is no option to respec your perks. That's ok.🟨  I can't put my tongue on it, but the combat leaves a bit to be desired. Combat is for me, really one of the best parts of the game. I feel incentivized to fight every enemy I see. It's fun unlocking new Wung-Fu and other special attacks. But I give the combat an "ok" for "more of this please". More enemies, more combos, more ways to defend yourself against gunfire and ranged attacks besides having high agility would be super.🟥 Story really leaves something to be desired. As far as I know, the only voice acting is the Narrator and two NPCs you are introduced to in the tutorial and that later show up from time to time. Often times I wonder why the team didn't hire voice actors, because I thought they would have fit in just well. The Narrator though is cheeky, so he'll suffice.The game isn't for everyone for sure. _childDocuments_.review: This review turned out a bit long, so here's a short summary:Promising and ambitious but is ultimately incoherent and feels like a chore. Grab it if it's on a significant sale and the world looks interesting to you, otherwise don't bother.~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~Pros:- Art style is delightful, world is intereting enough to draw you in, and has a ton of charm.- Combat is easy to learn and feels extremely fun once you get the hang of it.- Giant open world with plenty content to do.- A lot of choice when it comes to progression AND story both, with a dark / light path you can choose between in most situations. This includes freeroam interactions or interacting with specific objects on the map that can tip the scales either side, making it very helpful if you need to correct a mistake or simply want to cap out one or the other.- There's a LOT in terms moves and special abilities to use and level, so regardless of starting class, you can deviate away from that and build your character how you feel comfortable, swapping spells around depending on combat or traversal, if it comes to it.- Very high amount of customizing possible including looks, armor, weaponry and mounts, with the ability to alter your appearance later on if you change your mind.Cons:- Narrative and story are disjointed, weightless and at times make no sense at all. Characters react seemingly at random to what you say, and your dialog options jump between straightforward and overly cryptic nonsense, making it impossible to discern what you're about to respond with.- Interacting with NPCs can get downright irritating; them speaking an otherwise charming gibberish with the Narrator voicelines overlaid 'translating' them (even if this can be finetuned in the options somewhat).- Some sidecontent doesn't give you a clue on how to figure it out, so you can be stuck near endlessly trying to find a key to open a door, only to find the monster that swallowed the key did not show up where the map tells you it should.- The above can mean you cannot complete one or two things on the checklist associated with a specific zone, which gets annoying for map completions' sake, besides literally barring you from possible loot. Sometimes loot you need to find for these checklists is also in unmarked dirt piles which are hard to spot and can be missed entirely.- Puzzles work on limited steps you can take, and if they run out, you lose health and have to retry. You can pump your intellect stat to get more steps, but even then some puzzles just can't be solved in the allotted number of those, forcing you to retry until you get lucky, and the puzzle starts in a state you can solve with how many steps you got. (This includes story-critical puzzles.)- Enemies and bosses do next to no telepgraphing to some attacks they do, nor do they have recovery time between them, but YOU do. This can result in getting completely obliterated by repeated combo spams by two giant enemies, while you were either animationlocked in a dodgeroll you might not even wanted to do, or out of stamina, unable to avoid anything. Did I mention some enemy grab attacks also ignore you dodging? Because we got those too.- The above point also means that some fights are nigh impossible with melee, making you have to kite and use ranged, which in turn can completely suck any enjoyment out of fights.- There's so much stuff lying around as loot that your bags will be completely full of useless equipment that you're forced to either sort through, scrap or sell every half an hour.- Crafting is made generally obsolete very quick due to loot that's just simply better and found out in the world. This only worsens the previous point, as now you have components to manage too.In the end, I really, really wanted to like this game, but it just turned so frustrating and confusing after a while rather than enjoyable. The style and premise made it incredibly interesting to me, and this weird, semi-magical post apocalyptic scenario is charming as hell, but there're so many things weighing it down, that for me it was disappointing.Like I said at the start of this (incredibly wordsy) review; if the initial looks from the store page are enough to draw you in, AND the game is on a big sale, give it a try. Otherwise, it's an over-ambitious but ultimately under-achieving game that isn't really making it worth the time, and especially not the default price it has.

_childDocuments_.review: Ah, so these are the adventures of Rocket before he met Groot. It looks like the Dark Souls of Ratchet and Clank.In reality it’s like Kung Fu Panda meets Fallout. It really makes you FEEL like a Biomutant.It’s a great game that’s not perfect. I felt like people have been overly negative. The world is fun to explore, the RPG character stuff is great, combat is fun but not hard. I didn’t mind the story, some people think it’s meh. I wanted to enjoy the narrator, but it got annoying for me, thankfully there are a plethora of options including changing the language, frequency or toggling it on and off. TBH I just wanted to hear the narrator say goofy things for as long as possible. I enjoyed the repetition, I’m weird like that.The game has a lot of flaws, particularly in regards to the storytelling, but I compensate for that by immersing myself in my character and imagining a slightly more personal narrative. Other than that, it is shallow but absolutely dripping with charm and a unique style that you can’t find anywhere else. If you need to be really invested in the story to like the game, maybe this isn't for you. But if you'll enjoy this world of wonky creatures after humans ruined the planet and you'll like the combat/crafting loop, this game is totally worth it.My favorite aspect of the game are the side quests, but it’s best going in blind. For me it is a great game. It's one of the best I've played in awhile, I haven't put it down since I got it and I think about it all the time. I have different tastes then some though I also thought Dragons Dogma and Kingdoms of Amalur were fantastic games, it feels similar to those titles. Big but still indie.I’ve enjoyed it for what it is, a fun sandbox to run around as a mutated rodent, build cool stuff and meet cute critters. People take it way too serious and thats why they are disappointed with it.Biomutant begs the question… Can any small team make a smash hit open world RPG like Fallout New Vegas? The answer is no, but its fun as f*ck to strap literal garbage to your character and role play as your average rat from New York. So I say wait for it to go on sale and then go wild.Better question is, are you worth it for Biomutant?10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Almost every video game I have ever played has had at least one part that felt like a chore to me. You know - that mechanic or minigame that makes you groan inwardly and think "Crap. Another one of these." The unfun part of the game you muscle through so you can get back to the fun part of the game.Biomutant doesn't have any of these. The game is pure fun.The loot/crafting system, as well as the skills systems, make it incredibly easy to customize the game to your liking. The game is slightly repetitive, but only in the ways that all video games are (re-used assets, similar puzzles). And Biomutant is more creative about it than most. The world is vibrant and feels alive.The real selling point of the game, though, is movement. This is one of those rare games in which the simple act of moving through the world is a joyful experience. I am a lifetime lover of maps, but when I play Biomutant I hardly ever look at the map (in fact, an absence of a minimap is usually a deal breaker for me in an RPG). Mainly because the world is so full and interesting (and therefore distracting). You see a thing. You go to investigate said thing, and during the process you see another interesting thing. And from there you see another. And an hour later you find yourself wondering what it was you were doing when you noticed the first interesting thing.Biomutant is interesting and fun. And more. It is an absolute delight. I highly recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, I'd like to say that my recommendation is only about playing the game, not necessarily if it's worth purchasing. This game has sadly skates a fine line but has shown to make changes very quickly. This optimism has left me to ultimately decide to recommend this game. The biggest feature of this game is the wide and expansive world to explore and loot, which feel absolutely great. You can just walk in any direction and continue to find new things. That, and the combat at first, and the most excellent and redeeming factors to this game.However, there are some very major flaws that you should be aware of.Mostly revolving around one main feature of this game, "Crafting".This game advertises it's expansive crafting system. While it's true that you gain a lot of different parts and potential part combinations, it's ultimately meaningless. Essentially a random cosmetics system. Gear crafts for example: can add resists/armor with an added benefit of potentially some crit in rare circumstances. These are the only stats that you can impact with gear crafts and since resits can be capped via bio-points, that portion is a non-factor. Leaving just armor, which is level based, and crit %.Since luck also adds crit and loot %, it does help you cap crit early on in the game. However, later in the game it's only relevant for characters that are melee and stacking strength, or casters stacking int.There is no stat that scales ranged damage, thus luck tends to be one of the better options outside of vitality. I was stacking pure luck, in excess of 400, and the new "harder difficulty" is still not punishing enough to really need any vitality. Personally, I didn't really even feel impact from any stat outside of potentially cosmetic, which can be changed anyways.  Secondly, weapons.They have very similar issues, while certain things like the scope and handle may affect accuracy and range, the barrel mainly for penetration, and the magazine for clip size and reload speed. Generally speaking, there is not enough variance in these parts at the same level. Some just provide clearly more stats across the board and really don't illicit any build variance at all. Not to mention, outside of perhaps range/accuracy and even then, it's very hard to notice any difference. (As a note: magazine has the biggest variance, but the "perfect reload" perk nullifies any real variable in this)The main issue I have is with the base. Some weapons have very different rates of fire and that can't be augmented in any way, forcibly making certain types of bases just simply better despite perhaps looking better on paper, the dps numbers aren't really intuitive.Lastly for weapons and crafting. Bases sometimes come with passive perks. Unfortunately these are not balanced and honestly add more of a problem than excitement.Different elements/passive perks roll on each base and there isn't any way to change this. Effectively turning that base into scrap even if it's the highest level drop you've found, which doesn't feel good or rewarding.For melee this is seen by the 2% damage per x strength passive being the only viable passive and the only effective way to scale melee damage. For ranged it's usually chain that is insanely strong, but there are potentials for more perks in the ranged section simply because none of them affect the scaling exactly, but slow firing weapons in this game feel absolutely terrible so that instantly throws out that base. For casters, nothing matters at all... Lastly, perks. Very little character customization. No class identity to the point that it's essentially scrapped in NG+, as of the new patch. to provide some incentive to play it.The only perk that was a bit defining was the deadeye perk that was nerfed. Otherwise, they are small and relatively meaningless. Moreover, perfect reload becomes the game if you're playing ranged, stacking strength and usually a 2h becomes the game if you're attempting melee for the sake of melee, and well there is psy freak, which I haven't played since it was fixed but might be the dark horse to have a less linear setups, but mainly because there is nothing that really benefits it other than stacking int. This last point is that, while there are some interesting skills in the game, you can much too easily pick them all up easily. Even the light and dark restricted things are far far too easy to just collect. To me personally, it hinders the chase aspect. Where you can essentially hit final build in terms of skills you'll use for the entire next 30 hour loop within the first few hours of the game. Sure, you can try other things, but in my case I kept going back because nothing I tested was remotely as good. The main takeaway and TL;DR here is that despite looking like there are a lot of options to customize and build a character that plays in some unique way that fits your style, it's essentially a facade and honestly has some of the least variance I've ever seen in a game like this, which honestly makes me sad at the lost potential. Though perhaps in future patches these issues will be addressed and fixed, because on paper it sounds like a great and fun concept. Sadly, it's far too shallow and sometimes the game feels like one of those educational games from the '90s.

_childDocuments_.review: Biomutant is a game developed by Experiment 101 and their name exemplifies exactly what Biomutant does. _childDocuments_.review: I played this for 2 hours but out of those 2 hours, only 20 minutes at most was actual gameplay. The rest of the time was spent listening to dialog, going on and on and on. Interacting with any NPC was a dreadful experience and far too frequent of a problem for me to become immersed in what is otherwise a gorgeous environment and setting. I really want to continue playing this game, but if the rest of the game is going to be sitting around tapping the space bar to skip dialog, I would rather play something else with actual gameplay. Devs, if you read this, having a character babble for 3-7 seconds before the narrator slowly translating one sentence at a time quickly adds up and leads to a single conversation lasting 30 seconds to a full minute longer than it needs to. Further more, if you have an area where you must have 5 or more conversations, these minutes add up RAPIDLY and very much bore players. Where I stopped I was skipping half of the dialog and it still lasted far too long. QTEs exist here, you first encounter one in the tutorial, simple mash the button thing. Later, while fighting an enemy, the same icon appears, but the success state is if you tap the button ONLY once. if you mash the button, you will fail. Combat was definitely different and would have taken time to get used to but in 2 hours, there were maybe 5 or 6 combat encounters I had. all of which were over in no more than 1-2 minutes on medium difficulty. It was fun combat, but I didn't get to play hardly any of it.As stated before, the world is gorgeous and the art style is fantastic. I wish more games would dare to be as bright, colourful and outright immersive just from the get go. But this is all ruined by getting stuck in the aforementioned dialog.Performance wise, I'm running 2k on a Nvidia 1070 and an i7 6700 on max settings. This is the best running at-launch title I have played in forever. I have no clue how they did it, but it was buttery smooth. Shame that it just couldn't let me experience the world rather than telling me about it non stop.In short, I don't recommend it unless you enjoy tonnes and tonnes of dialog being vomited in your general direction for the first two hours. I will be requesting a refund. If I hear of problems being fixed, I may come back and retry my luck.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, so let me try to untangle the kaleidoscope that was "Biomutant" while I was tripping on shrooms, battling my own inner demons, and managing my cravings. If you ever wondered what it’s like to experience a game while your mind is a swirl of fragmented thoughts and vivid hallucinations, let me paint you a picture.Gameplay: Playing "Biomutant" while on shrooms was like stepping into a bizarre dreamscape. The world is vibrant and teeming with strange creatures and colorful environments, which, let’s be honest, can be both mesmerizing and disorienting. The game's open-world mechanics felt like a labyrinth with paths that kept shifting, mirroring the unpredictability of my own mind. The combat is fast-paced, but sometimes it felt like I was fighting in a slow-motion sequence. I’d get lost in the visuals and then snap back to the action with a jolt, which made the experience both thrilling and overwhelming.Story and Quests: The narrative is pretty wild. It’s packed with quirky characters and a storyline that’s as twisted as my own thoughts. The dialogue and questlines seem to reflect a world that’s constantly shifting and changing, which was oddly fitting given my mental state. Sometimes, the story felt like it was speaking directly to my fragmented consciousness, making it a fascinating but confusing ride. The quest objectives often seemed like they were shifting with my focus, so I’d find myself lost in side quests or caught in loops of trying to remember what I was supposed to be doing.Visuals and Design: Visually, "Biomutant" is a psychedelic feast. The colors are bright and the design is full of fantastical elements that felt like they were coming straight out of my trippy hallucinations. Forests with neon hues and bizarre creatures fit perfectly with the shroom-induced wonderland I was experiencing. Sometimes it was hard to distinguish between the game world and the hallucinations, which made the graphics both enchanting and bewildering.Controls and Mechanics: The controls felt like they were slipping through my fingers, not unlike trying to grasp at my fleeting thoughts. The movement and combat mechanics were functional, but in my state, they sometimes seemed too fluid or too rigid, adding to the surreal feeling of the experience. Trying to coordinate my actions while my mind was bouncing around made the game feel like an intricate dance that I was constantly stumbling through.Overall Experience: "Biomutant" on shrooms was an experience I’ll never forget, though not always in a clear way. It’s a game that thrives on its whimsical, open-world chaos, which matched my own mental chaos in a way that was both captivating and confusing. The vivid graphics and unpredictable gameplay felt like they were a direct extension of my current state—both mesmerizing and challenging. It’s an immersive adventure that’s perfect for a mind looking to escape reality, but be prepared for it to be a wild, disorienting ride.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who pre-ordered BIOMUTANT upon its release on console, I found myself deeply disappointed and I decided to abandon this game. However, when Humble Bundle offered a PC copy, I decided to give it another shot. Sadly, my excitement gave way to frustration once more.The game begins with such promise. The world is vibrant, the engaging gameplay with a potential for something truly special. Yet, as I delved deeper, that promise crumbled beneath the weight of repetition and lackluster mechanics. The game's ambitious ideas are evident, but it feels as though it bit off more than it could chew.  The tone can be inconsistent between seriousness and whimsy, leaving the narrative feeling disjointed. Dialogue, in particular, falls flat (THE GIBBERISH DOES NOT HELP AT ALL!)While the world is undeniably beautiful and expansive, it lacks the substance to make exploration truly rewarding. Quests often devolve into mundane fetch tasks, and many features feel unfinished or underdeveloped.After 20 hours in, I am ONCE AGAIN exhausted and disheartened. It's clear that the game has a solid foundation, but it's buried beneath a mountain of unfulfilled potential.

_childDocuments_.review: Wanting to like it is about all that keeps me playing this fairly stock-standard RPG. Yet another example of why the words "open world" should instill dread in those that hear them. Biomutant does very little to set itself apart with its color by numbers story, blank open world, and combat that lacks any sense of impact or weight. Multiple story beats right from the get-go that lack any sense of timing, cinematic vision, or even tonal congruity with the rest of the game. While I've yet to run into any debilitating bugs, there is a distinct lack of polish about the game from the way rain falls through enclosed spaces to the way the protagonist slides up ladders and chains hang idle at 90° angles. Every npc interaction is belabored by having to be narrated as well as spoken in an intention to give a storybook feel but that instead comes off as immersion breaking and annoying. Manage your expectations for the character creation as well: I have never seen a circular slider be used to pick something as specific as a pattern before but the character transformations that result from these vague —at best— changes are almost as unpredictable as they are ugly. It must be said that there is an element of fun to be had in one's first few hours exploring the map and making choices along a binary moral choice meter, but how long after play will the "newness" of the world wear off before each scaling enemy encounter, identical grassy hill, and miniboss fight just become boring?

Oh, the game still believes the narrator is reading that for you so it'll just skip to the next line without a prompt. Nice. Thanks.2. The audio mixing. It was like the majority of my time was running around a (beautiful) waste land with sleepy relaxing music that never seemed to change. I never heard my footsteps or jumping or the foliage around me. _childDocuments_.review: Biomutant doesn't feel worth the $60 price tag; its content feels shallow and the entire time you're doing quest-related things, you feel like you're being hand held.Wait for the devs to fix the base-line issues with the game before buying it.I played this game for a lot longer than I probably should have. Even after the two-hour long tutorial sequence, I kept playing on, only realizing the longer I played that even after the extra time they took to work on it.. this game just..  feel complete. I've listed the things about it that bother me the most below.The tutorial lasts for two hours, and you're not allowed to go off-rails until you see the first boss in a light cutscene. The  boss, meaning this is the first big bad you'll be fighting in the order of big bads  you opt to take the "good" alignment choice.I beat the first main boss, and it automatically put me on a quest to beat a particular OTHER one. I figured I'd have more agency in its open world to do the bosses in an order of exploration rather than sequence. Even when you're out in the open world, you never shake the feeling that you're out of the tutorial.Once you set your character's appearance, I'm unsure that you can ever change it throughout your playthrough.. even after the time I've spent in it, I've seen no mention of fixing issues I have with my character now that he's moving. It doesn't help that you can't customize your armor aside from stat-increases.. I ended up using less armor on my character because I didn't like the way I looked.The factions are also limited to good and evil, it's not even a gray area or a yin/yang sort of deal, it's just,  versus,  There are no other factions and there are no gray areas. You are good or evil if you choose.The same deal goes for the alignment system.. which feels forced in how it presents itself and only truly has a purpose in the four skills you gain access to if you're good/evil enough. That's four total. Two in each alignment.That said, the skills you can unlock OUTSIDE of the alignment system are limited too. only having 8 mutations and 9 psi powers to unlock. Both types of powers are unlockable through different means, and serve to enhance combat and/or mobility. Those Psi powers include the four (total) alignment-specific skills.. meaning that for the duration of the game, you have access to a whopping 15 total abilities you can use. At 13 hours played, I got through the tutorial, explored an area a bit, and fought a boss. There are four bosses and eight explorable biomes. You'd have to use a combination of 15 abilities for a LONG time.The dialogue drags on due to the little assistant translating every gibberish interaction you have.. wherein you have to wait for it to say what you're trying to read to understand what the person you're talking to is saying.. and there's no option to disable or even turn it down.. it legitimately slows the pace of the game to a crawl if you don't spam through the dialogue.____________________________Biomutant has disappointed on every level except for its graphics and weapon customization.. it's  and you can do some  neat stuff with your guns, but almost everything it offers doesn't have enough depth to sell as a full-priced game.And that's the unfortunate thing about this, because they clearly put a ton of time and effort into making this game what it is.. Until its systems are fleshed out further and the tutorial and dialogue system are overhauled, I'd say anything over $40 is asking for too much.

_childDocuments_.review: When I was a kid, I watched Star Trek's "Wrath of Khan". I have almost no memory of it except a scene where it's described that Kirk is one of the only people to pass something called the "Kobayashi Maru" test. Now, in the mind of some ten year old, these were just sounds they said. It meant nothing to me and still barely does beyond a quick google search to make sure I spelled it correctly. Even though the scene stuck with me, it is the example I think about when universes just throw letters at the wall to make up random names for things. It is my chief concern with this game more than anything else. I will lead with this complaint because I don't have much else beyond mere petty annoyances, just in case you get confused at my thumbs up.Most parts you pick up are just random letters thrown around with the occasional vowel to at least make it pronounceable. I think I have a rifle stock named a "Skorp" or some nonsense. I cannot express how irritating this is. Why is it so difficult to just name it something like "Basic Metal Stock" or "Incredible Shiny Barrel". Nope, it's all Flips, Skorps, Smicks, Klobbs, Yrkums, Infs and Plockers. I literally only made one of those up. Some of it I can accept, like referring to the past as the "Once-was", but it's all so incredibly inconsistent. It'll call something the Once-Before and then go on to explain a polluting corporation destroying the planet in modern linguistics. Pick one, writers.While I do think the grumbling linguistics of all the NPC's should have just been subtitled than narrated, this little feature pisses me off a bit more than I think it should, but here we are.So what kind of game is this? It's an open world loot-shooter with some magic and melee thrown in the mix. It has the worldly vibe of a Chibi-Borderlands game while also giving me a Breath of the Wild vibe, though this game does marginally better at filling the world. Not necessarily with stuff to do, but more along the lines of hiding loot behind waterfalls. In BotW, I remember running across fields for minutes at a time, while Biomutant does a better job of giving me a reason to stop to explore some bombed out building because there is inevitably something in there to grab. I'm not fully sure what aligning the antennae on a television did for me (experience? I don't know!), but I still do enjoy running around as an adorable rodent to figure out how a toilet works as it spits legendary loot at me.I only have nine hours on it and some features still elude me, like crafting clothing. I'm not terribly fond of looking like a ridiculous clown but sometimes I sacrifice a few armor points so I can look like a fairly bad-ass automatic rifle shooting samurai warrior. The game honestly gives me the biggest BotW vibe but I think Biomutant does a few things better. Including the "more reasons to stop and run into those woods to see if that big mob will drop something good", but there's also a plethora of interesting hazard zones to give you a hefty risk-reward ratio. Do you have low heat resistance? Well, how's your move speed (upgraded through agility)? Because I've done a few encounters where I'd just do hit and runs on a hazard zone's perimeter, got some decent loot, dived into houses (which sometimes negate the timer), and shot mobs through destroyed doorways and windows as they chucked fireballs at me. I enjoyed that encounter.Another thing I don't always like are combo moves. I never got into street fighter arcade games when I was a child and I certainly don't have the memory to do it now. I've only once in nine hours been able to activate the "super mode" that you can get when you do three unique combos in a certain time frame, because honestly my two rats are just gunners so I just kind of click on everything until their health goes away. I will occasionally do a jump to get some bullet time in there but I mostly just rely on a couple of very specific combos that I can actually fulfill and they've carried me a decent distance so far. I have no real complaints on the combat. I've seen better, but I've seen worse.I'd say ignore some of the metacritic views and really base your purchase decision on what types of games you, the player, actually like. I see a lot of 6/10's thrown around and while I don't disagree with that numeric value, a 5-7 out of 10 always ends up translating to a "decent, with flaws" game and I've rarely been disappointed by a middle of the road type rating. I only get worried when I start seeing 4's, and this is not a 4/10 game. It's really not that bad.

_childDocuments_.review: So, like many, I got this game in the monthly Bundle. I had heard that this game was a pretty big disappointment upon launch, but I wanted to go with an unbiased and open mind, so I dove in and... I agree with the general concensus.First things first, combat. It's the main part of your game, it's open world so it's going to be pretty damn frequent. And it. Frigging. Sucks. Balls. Enemies being "harder" means they become bullet sponges; status effects, spells, and the such are basically meaningless, defeating an enemy means emptying clip after clip of bullets on them until they go down. Oh but don't go too far because the kiting system is pretty damn stupid! I understand they don't want players to drag an enemy halfway across the continent slowly chipping away with DoT until it dies, but these monsters have a shorter range than a LoL camp; you move half an inch away from the very limited spawn location, and they turn back and regenerate all that HP that you took four clips and five ki bars to deplete. I'm aware Horizon: Zero Dawn is a very high standard to compare to, but THAT is how you make combat engaging; I was eager to fight new machines, not dreading "oh my god here comes another 15 minutes slugfest where I hold down RT until bullets are out".And the narrator... oh my god the narrator... gets old and obnoxious pretty ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ quickly. Returning to the LoL comparisons, it's like when Caitlyn shouted "Boom! Headshot!" every headshot she got, which to the ones not familiar, was about once every five to eight seconds. Gets boring pretty ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ quick. And I understand not having enough budget to voice act every single character, but you can like... just leave the subtitles, instead of the narrator going "he's saying that...". I don't know how it made sense to developers, but it's annoying.I wouldn't recommend this at anything lower than a 70% discount and even then, I would encourage to refund immediately if you don't like the first few minutes of combat. Gets boring real quick and the game is very lackluster.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a mix up of Fallout 4 and Just Cause in terms of game play and design. While it doesn't have the polish of those games, but makes up for it with it's own unique charm. The setting is a weird mash-up of familiar mixed up with strangely unfamiliar and the story is at first glance a standard post apocalyptic setting trope but quickly changes to something else as the story progresses.        As far as my criticisms go, the game is a bit of a mess in the side quest category. Side quests are doled out at a prodigious rate and are almost overwhelming in the quantity. The weakness being that most of them are very similar in build and scope. I would have preferred fewer side quests with deeper and more varied gameplay. As it is, most of them devolve into the same "Go here, find this thing, interact with it" or the "Go here, kill this, rescue this person, go here" format. This isn't true for every one of the side quests, some have some variety that makes them interesting, but by and large most are a bit of the same design with minor variations.         In conclusion, I would say that Biomutant is fun enough, and has enough charm and unique npc design that I can forgive it's most egregious flaws. In the grand scheme of things, the game's flaws aren't the worst. It isn't a broken mess at launch (a la Fallout 4, Skyrim... really any Bethesda Game at launch really), and a lot of the core issues with the title have been addressed via patch 1.4. Overall, it is a fun and hopefully successful game that can be the start of a franchise.

_childDocuments_.review: Biomutant is an open world, action combat game, with a large amount of story and rudimentary gameplay.It can feel a little like a young persons game, with a naration style that is not too distant from watching a tv episode of Pocoyo (UK tv).The gameplay loop is such - explore, loot, craft, fight etc - with a nice array of mounts, gadgets, "spells" and weaponry to keep you constantly trying something new. The enemy types are varied, but similiar in nature - with alternate versions of colors and armors.The map is large, and full of interesting locations - some requiring resistances or gear to traverse and explore.Pros:You can play as you wish - creating your character isnt the final step - you can switch to swords or guns or magic at any point and play viably.  However, if you want to specialise, you can, and the gear supports this.Theres LOTS to find and explore.  This isnt a small game - you will be here for hours exploring.  If you get sidetracked easily, this is one of those games.  The music and sounds are pleasant, the animal gibberish is cute and the narrator is very chatty.  I did turn him off after a while however, but many love him.Controls are easy to use, hard to master - combos for fighting CAN be used, but if you cant use them, you dont get punished for it.Cons:The narrator is VERY chatty.  Its very childlike at times (ping pingety ping ping!) and sounds like a childrens program.  The story is quite complex in places, and the backstory is interesting.  I get vibes from MANY games, and i feel that some of them have been stolen slightly to make this game more interesting to many people.Its not always immediatly obvious how to work the inventory.  Items are not highlighted very clearly, and its perfectly possible to accidently sell everything you are wearing because its not obvious your wearing it.You can accidently sell or dismantle things because there isnt a 2nd "are you sure" option on legendary or ultimate items.  This is BAD.I got motion sickness from this - something i dont normally suffer from - i recommend a high FOV, and motion blur turned on to counter it.  I never use motion blur normally, but i believe the bright garish colors and fast movement cause it.Some things arent explained - if you complete a certain quest, you CANNOT go to some areas and aquire certain items.  This could do with a better explanation.  I get that it breaks game immersion, but a quest i got at the start of the game that i finished early locking me out of many sets of weapons and armor feels annoying.Rating:8/10Borrows heavily from many other game sources, to deliver a game thats many things all at once, that forgives alot of mistakes, has alot of content and alot of cuteness.  I like this game, because i can do anything i want - and ive got alot of room to do it - im not limited to "this power means this armor ONLY" etc. Id like a closer camera angle but more to the side to alleviate motion sickness, but thats my only annoyance so far.

_childDocuments_.review: If you miss the old era of gaming where the game didn't take itself seriously and think it was some kind of saviour of the social world then give this game a go. DON'T PICK UP THE GAME IF YOU'RE LOOKING FOR SOME KIND OF GTA/MASS EFFECT/CYBERPUNK EXPERIENCE. This game is geared towards the 90s and 00s gamer. You can feel inspirations from a plethora of games. The environment gives me huge Horizon: Zero Dawn vibes, the writing and VA is very Banjo Kazooie meets Spyro but for an older crowd. A tip for combat is that this game loads your actions in a sequence meaning if you jump while still attacking, its not going to cancel the attack rather your character will jump AFTER the attack animation has been completed. This is giving people the sensation of clunkiness in the combat when instead its a design feature that not many games use these days because it requires us as gamers to think instead of button mash.My one gripe would have to be the quick inputs are kinda touchy and you can accidentally use the wrong consumable very easily and i had ONE bug where my resistances reset after changing my appearance so i wouldnt advise adjusting your appearance just yet.

_childDocuments_.review: Biomutant was an  title that had me excited since it's reveal in 2017. It showed up something for everyone. Fluid combat, comic art style, aura system, custom weapons, etc.Although, this game was made by roughly 14 people, and I'd be a little more leisure about it, if it was priced at a AAA release. So just as everyone, I'll be reviewing Biomutant as a AAA experience. Biomutant has a great open world, visually at least. It's got story all over and pretty much anything is lootable (as long as it's in an area designed to be looted). The story is linear and bland with nothing more than fetch quests for the entire experience. Meet new character, get quests, pick up object for boss, fight boss. Nothing changes, and the side quests suffer the same way.The map is barren, enemies are few and far between and there is never really any danger at any time. There's always something to look at but also nothing at the same time. Thankfully you're given mounts to travel around and speed up the movement a little bit. Enemies are interesting and I mean that lightly, there are 3 various of enemies. Beast, humanoid, and giant, which all have the same 3 attack patterns. You will either be shot at, swung at, or stomped on. Which would be fine if the various enemies were actually eye catching except for the names being funny sometimes. The NPCs are voiced in gibberish, with the narrator speaking and translating for them. A very unique thing we haven't seen often. Except for when you catch on that the NPCs say the say gibberish voiceline over and over and over and over and over and over and over again. It never changes, they will say the same line, while the narrator changes what they say slightly each time. Which also isn't very different. It's always something about either being a good boy, and that my mooma would be proud or that I'm evil and need to find a spark of light. Nothing changes and I ended up skipping the dialog most of the times from that point. The narrator is charming when you're just walking around, but if you have a setting to make him shut up, then you know it's annoying and not very good. The AI is kinda bad too, they get stuck in idle animations or in mid swings. All I can say about this fights is that the enemies do make combat fun when it works. Guns, swords and spells, oh my! That's the weapons you get, those are yours arms in the world. Weapons can be crafted from dismantled weapons you find or dismantle yourself, axe blade with katana hilt? You can make it. The only that ruins the combat is there's no impact, two handed swords have no thud to them. It's like a two handed noodle. The guns felt like you're spitting on them, even upgraded they just feel like stronger spit. Enemies don't stagger often enough and just power through your hits and keep moving, skills don't affect the damage either since weapons are how your damage is modified. The spells pretty much don't do anything either except mucus bubble which is the only power worth the grind. Also, PARRY DOESNT F**KING WORK. THE AMOUNT OF TIMES I PARRY A HIT IS SO LOW BECAUSE THE GAME DOESNT REGISTER THE PARRY UNLESS YOU SPAM THE BUTTON.  Sorry. But if you have a PARRY you need it to be the most responsive action in the game. Clunky, and wacky. The amount of time my character just freaks out because he doesn't know what animation to show and then it decided to dump the first one it can. Other than that you don't really notice much of the problems, unless the game freaks out and doesn't work. Biomutant is a masterpiece as an indie game, and would've been higher on my ratings and likes if it was for the fact the game isn't just an indie game. It's an experimental game, made by first time developers, sold as a AAA game. That's why I'm giving it a negative rating, it's not worth 60$ and is very unfinished, and unpolished. At best its worth maybe 30$, just due to the time it was given. Although it's not worth a AAA price point when what's given isn't a AAA experience. , just wait until it's dropped or if they update it and add more or fix the content they have now.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun game once you get past what feels like a two hour tutorial.This is a story based game with poor story writing.  It has an annoying narrator who feels the need to explain and narrate EVERYTHING.  And the NPCs speak Gibberish (I recommend turning Gibberish volume to off in settings).  It does nothing to add to the content and the narrator translates it.  It is like watching a movie with someone who wont stfu.  It is a huge literary crutch they have abused in the worst possible way.  It could have been much improved by using voice actors for the NPCs and eliminating the narrator entirely.  It isn't necessary to tell me the obvious motivation of every character.  It also isn't necessary for me to know the motivation of every character.  I would argue it could make the game better if I did not always know it.There are also minor graphic glitches/hitches.  It has frozen on me once in 5 hours of play, forcing me to close it in task manager.That being said, I find the game otherwise enjoyable. 8/10 will play again.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm on an i7-8750H, 32gb DDR4 with a GTX 1060 6gb on m.2 SSD. Graphically this game is stunning, beautiful, adorable, and visually interesting. I've encountered no running bugs so far. Updates will follow below the original review. Final review TLDR: This game deserves a much better sequel where they learn from the failures of this one, because there is so much here that could have made this Fallout-level good. I plan to slog through and finish because the parts that are good are solid. This review will have spoilers. I mark as recommended, though I may change my mind in the future, despite many cons, which I will list first. If these are enough to turn you away, the pros won't change it. I still recommend the game as of this writing.Cons-Far too frequent interruptions for complicated, sometimes confusing and often nonsensical exposition-Complicated upgrade/level up systems that feel out of place-Unexplained events in game, like enemy faction leader having dialogue directed at you immediately after you choose the opposing faction despite not being anywhere present at the time, a creature in a wheelchair scaling out of a huge hole you had to climb to leave, talking about the tree of life without my ever having seen it directly, etc. (heavy ludonarrative dissonance)-Some controls are not as fluid or responsive as I might have hoped-Very repetitive world objects, the same broken down truck in every area you enter for examplePros-Awesome fighting, at least for the Saboteur class that I'm playing with-GORGEOUS world art, adorable characters-Ki power upgrades seem awesome and fun to use-A cool weapon and gear system I've yet to fully explore (sadly this long in I have no customization items yet...)I hope that some changes might get made moving forward to improve the game, even if they have to be big ones. I feel truly like it doesn't know what kind of game it's trying to be. There's a ton of promise here, and I've been keeping loose tabs on the creation of this game forever, so maybe take my bias into account. I think a fair number of people are disappointed in this game so far, and I too may reach that point (I'll sure update if I do) because of expectations of what this game would be vs. what it actually is right now, and I don't fault them at all given my list of cons. I will still give it a chance, and maybe the game will open up and be better as I progress.4 hour update: The game DOES get better. Lots of the mentioned flaws don't necessarily go away, but there's a lot more to do now. Though I consider it a hefty oversight that it took me 3+ hours to pick up customization items and stop having constant story dialogue interruptions, the game now is starting to make me think of a combination of Mini-Ninjas and Fable, but with a more fun weapon customization and crafting system. I'm liking it more than I was for certain, once you get some powers (though a few are confusing to use and not well explained before you unlock them) and weapons under the belt. Still struggling to incorporate the parry system. But now I feel much better about recommending it for sure. 14 hour update: There's so much to do in this game. Lots of territory capture. Factions. Crafting, upgrading, powers. Imagine if half a Pixar team got together with half of the Red Faction team to make a game, except they never quite settled on some details, got rushed in the 11th hour, and did the best they could to make it playable without everything quite in good order. That's about what this game is. Objectives have zero pacing, and zero time restraint. The narrator gives ominous warnings about night, and you can rest until morning at campfires, but night itself is no different than daytime. I've found the combat to be very fun if not always fluid, dialogue is fairly predictable and binary with lots of what feels like filler in absence of context or better words. Lots of things that give you the impression they make a difference actually don't. And the game DOES have some bugs. Changing out my top for example, on my avatar the upgrades I've made on my equipped top will remain if I change it to a new one. Shop selling lists often mark the wrong items as being equipped.  Small stuff. While lots of stuff feels unfinished though, what is finished is quite fun, and my honest review is this: This game deserves a much better sequel where they learn from the failures of this one, because there is so much here that could have made this Fallout-level good. Better even. I hope it survives the bad reviews to get that much.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is close to amazing, but a few very very odd choices hold it down. The first few updates were promising, but at this point the devs only drop occasional bugfixes. Overall, I would say it's worth picking up on sale, but not for the full $60.1. Your stats and appearance are linked. The "mutation" menu that lets you choose which score(s) to favor randomly generates how your favored stats affect your character's appearance. That means that going in and out of the menu will yield different results.2. The Narrator. There is nothing explicitly wrong with the Narrator's performance, but he just talks constantly. Not only does he act as... y'know, The Narrator, but he is also your translator. All the NPCs talk in a style similar to Simlish, and only after they are done speaking unintelligible nonsense does the narrator take his turn and translate for them. He doesn't put on a voice or anything, he just describes that they said and how they said it as if he's reading a book. "She tells you to head North, where you will find ______. She encourages you to move with urgency."They added a feature post-launch where you can skip one and/or the other and still get it subtitled. Unfortunately, they're the Narrator's subtitles - so it's still all second-person dialogue - but it's better than nothing. They also added the option to tone down how often he chimes in. Both were massive improvements.3. Certain words are replaced with soundalikes, gibberish, or baby-talk. Think the post-apocalyptic episode of Rick & Morty. Here is an excerpt from the narrator describing a toilet with a toilet brush in it:"A Flush-stool from the Back-In-Time. It's an Apparatus that sink-sunks yellow juice and Brown-bobs. Let's try out the Brush-away, see if you can off-chase some drip-droppings."This is just entirely unnecessary. It seemed kind of funny at first, by the time I was hearing the 300th cutesy tongue-in-cheek slang term for a normal object I was just groaning.4. The story and lore have the classic "wide as the ocean, depth of a puddle" problem. Your character's backstory, the Tribe War, the Tree of Life, the Evil/Corrupted monsters, the Ancient-but-Advanced technology... It all makes you say "Whoa!"... and then is either immediately explained, or there is nothing to explain.For example: The Narrator. At one point, one of the rarely-seen background characters just steps forward, speaking in The Narrator's voice and continuing his narration. He existed in-universe the entire time, and they never explain a thing about him.5. The balance is surprisingly decent, and yet the outliers are stunningly far from the average. Weapons skew towards the lower end, while enemies skew towards the higher. The weakest weapons are useless, while he best require some build or customization work to perfect. Enemies range from an annoyance to unkillable death machines. Even in endgame some random enemies gave me trouble. This may sound good on paper, but in practice it means if you ♥♥♥♥ up your build or get unlucky with loot you can end up struggling a lot.

_childDocuments_.review: Maybe a bit overpriced for $60. My only real complaint is that it feels like a lot of the systems are half-baked. There's no great sense of progression in the game that I've encountered. There's a fairly comprehensive crafting/modification system, but there's no easy way to compare weapons as there aren't basic metrics like DPS, or even something like attack speed. The same roughly goes for armor, after you upgrade your armor, it's hard to tell whether a new piece of gear is better or worse without modifying it since the base stats of the modified gear are no longer visible. The skill upgrade system isn't much better. I fully maxed out all the skills for my weapon of choice within the first couple minutes of unlocking the ability to learn new skills. It surprised me that there were no further skills that I could learn for the weapons. I didn't find the narrator nearly as annoying as people make him out to be. I guess the game was hyped which explains why people are getting so bent out of shape about a video game. I think it's definitely entertaining and I feel like I probably have another 10-20 hours to go in the story. This would put this game at about $2/hr of entertainment. Definitely not the type of game I'll be putting more than 100 hours in, but those types of games are pretty rare for me.

_childDocuments_.review: This certainly isn’t a perfect game, much like Mad Max, Mortal Shell, or Remnant: From the Ashes, it’s a small studio producing  a AA title that’s gotten AAA attention. While I understand the hype and the slow 2021 release schedule to be contributing factors to this game getting so much attention, I think it’s best to take the game as it is. Biomutant does a lot that is original and enjoyable and mostly everything I have a problem with are things they’ve addressed with coming updates and later releases. I get people want to hate it for its unfinished state but we cannot hold them to the same standards as AAA developers that promote crunch over employees health like the recent CD Projeckt Red debacle with the Cyberpunk release. If you enjoy the style of games like Oddworld, Mutant Year Zero, or games oriented to looting and exploring it is a good type with fun progression and gear. I just zen out and play. I also adjusted the narrator to 20% and found it fine. 7/10 solid but not perfect at 17 hours played. Purchased to support developers but much like Days Gone, I’d wait until price goes down to $40 and updates come. As they intend to address a large amount of fan issues but they need the game to sell to follow through on that. Buy if you believe in the potential.

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of the 'puzzles' are overly simplistic and the morality system is overall not very impactful... But overall, I really like it. The core gameplay loop is fun, with deeper combat than a lot of people realize and an amazing crafting system. The environments are beautiful and mostly worth exploring, hiding plenty of high-value loot away from the beaten paths. The world and characters are full of quirky humor, but also a surprising array of philosophical profundity. Every boss fight and the prep time leading up to them offers a satisfying mechanical distraction (without spoiling too much: vehicles!).Bottom line -- if you like open-world ARPGs and don't mind a little jank, you will enjoy BIOMUTANT.Edit: An update on June 1st addressed one of my main complaints in regard to game dialogue, by allowing you to disable the NPC gibberish, narrator's voice-over, or both. Doing any of those will make conversations much faster to get through because the text appears instantly, rather than after a delay you previously had to press a button to skip. Same patch also appears to improve the somewhat lengthy tutorial section's pacing, which is something I also felt needed work but failed to mention in this review. So... Good job, devs, keep it up.

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended at $30 or less. It starts out slow, opens up into something fun and novel, then quickly overstays its welcome. The gameplay is solid enough and there's fun to be had, but the overall experience feels a bit too shallow - like the game was made with procedural generation in mind. NPCs and Tribes could easily be randomly generated, loot already is, and quests might as well be. It's a great idea and the execution is good, but I think past open world RPGs have set the bar quite high in several areas, and that makes Biomutant seem lacking in comparison.I greatly prefer handcrafted worlds, but if it's going to feel repetitive and disjointed anyway, the game really could have benefitted from procedural generation. A roguelike DLC (with optional permadeath) should be an obvious target going forward.
