_childDocuments_.review: Charming, quirky, and fun.Biomutant is an open world RPG featuring an impressive amount of content and decent gameplay.The combat is not complicated nor hard and that is part of it's appeal.Game has a couple of innovative design choices like being able to craft on the fly (great) and scaling cliffs simply requires finding an anchor point and pushing in the direction you wish to travel with the thumb stick only.The RPG elements are levelling and investing skill points into different skills (these are quite limited so overly diverse builds aren't a thing but I don't think it matters). There is also a light/dark choice system.This game is more about exploring the map, meeting the quirky characters, looting/crafting better items and engaging in easy combat without any hardcore elements or pressure. A narrator gives voice overs along the way and adds positive comments that are young 'un friendly.A charming game that is as cruizy to play as it is fun.An easy recommend based on that.

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun exploration with tons of weird looking gear to loot, coupled with a really satisfying leveling system and an exceptional gear upgrade system that's so good i'll be surprised if other games don't copy it. While in my case these positives make the game worth it, the story so far is an absolute snoozefest and it's delivered in the most mundane way imaginable. Not even the stanley parable narrator voicing over every single ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ furry ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ i talk to is enough to make me consider NOT skipping all the dialogue. Some might say the combat is a bit clunky but after some getting used to it I found it pretty smooth and fun. Additionally the objectives of sidequests might seem mundane and repetitive but that's just what I've come to expect from big open world games. Game only recommended if you can stomach the fact that you will be better off skipping everything story related and if you're up for a fun, super casual action rpg experience with beautiful environments to explore, tons of loot to loot and disgusting mutated furries to kill.

It's big, vibrant and full of foliage, towns, and encounters so it never feels empty. Also the loot and crafting systems are very well done and feel like an important part of the game.  -The narrator, I really like the narrator. They way the devs incorporated him into the games makes it feel very natural, and it gives the game a sens of character that I haven't found in other games. I've seen people say you can turn him off, but i honestly feel like that would take a great deal of enjoyment out of the game.-The combat feels very smooth for both ranged and melee. I'm my opinion its one of the more refined and enjoyable combat systems i've experienced in recent memory.  Couple that with the slow-mo events and you can have some pretty ridiculous combos. -The story is good. Not God of War PS4 good, but as good as every other AAA game i've played in the last 5 years easily. Also, the side quests, at least up to the point i've played so far, are actually fun and rewarding. They arent just your standard "go get this, bring it to me, and ill give you money."-The puzzles so far, are easy. Now, this might come as a shocking surprise, but I didn't buy this game because i wanted to solve puzzles all day. I bought it because i wanted to beat up mutant trash pandas with giant hammer. So in my book, simple, quick puzzles are more than welcome.-The enemies are fantastic. There are so many different types i've already encountered and they are all vastly different in the way they look and fight. I have yet to find a new creature where I thought, wow that's kinda lame. So overall, i'm really enjoying this game so far. It runs very well, gameplay is smooth, the world is unique and fun, the characters and design are cool and funny. I'm very pleased.

_childDocuments_.review: BIOMUTANT is a great exploration/crafting game.The only downside and I see this mentioned often in all the negative reviews I’ve seen, is the first 2/3 hours of the game, which is, believe it or not, all tutorial and it's the longest tutorial I have encountered to date in a single player rpg.Since steam only lets you play 2 hours before you cant refund anymore I’m going to guess a lot of people haven't got past the tutorial, hence all the complaining about hand holding, narrator interrupting you every few mins with cutscenes etc.All of that stops after the tutorial. In fact until you complete the tutorial you cannot even craft nor explore. You are severely limited and it leaves a bad first impression.After the said first 2 to 3 hours depending on how much you skip everything, the game opens up just how you would expect from an open world title.U’ll be presented with main quests and side missions, all of which can just be ignored if you choose to do so. I personally just went ahead in a random direction and started exploring.Crafted my first buster sword, got my boat, and glider.The crafting system is really well done in this game. I've been upgrading my one gun for a while now, always finding new components which not only increase the stats but also update it visually. Some components will come with special perks such as elemental damage, buzz saws firing out of the barrel etc.Exploring is also really well done, I've been roaming areas 4/5 level higher than myself and having a blast.If you’re expecting a cinematic movie-like experience with rich storytelling, Unfortunately BIOMUTANT is going to disappoint you. Think of it as more old school rpg but with modern aesthetics and systems.What it is at its core is an exploration based looter/crafting rpg. It does it well, I’ve been having a blast with this title, and I hope we get a sequel in the future.For me it's a 9/10, get rid of the tutorial and it's a 10/10.(ps, I forgot all about this title till around few days before it came out so I was neither hyped or expecting anything, it looked fun to me so I gave it a go and I'm very happy that I did)(I play in offline mode hence the hours showed in reality I've clocked 15 hours so far.)

_childDocuments_.review: And and last, we have Biomutant.  What seemed like forever ago, I remember being absolutely stoked to jump into this gorgeous dystopian world.  I must admit I was getting nervous after waiting as long as I did.  Although it didn't end up being the polished gem I was hoping it would be, I most certainly am enjoying exploring Biomutant.  The combat does feel messy, but with the numerous amount of skills and weapons to discover and dabble with, there is sure to be a setup that will accommodate most players.  The storytelling is fun enough, even if it feels bare bones with cutscenes that don't seem to mesh or transition smoothly.  The narrator does a great job keeping things light and interesting.  There is certainly numerous replayability options available with plenty of dialogue choice and good/evil situations.  There are also numerous classes to begin with and many many many customization options as well.  As stated before, the crown jewel of the game is the freedom of exploration and discovery.  There is a lot to look at here, and it's all immaculate and vibrant.  I can get lost just running around, watching the setting sun cast amazing shadows across the landscape.  That being said, I feel most people's enjoyment of a title like this will vary depending on their patience with the games cluttered elements.  The tutorial throws a lot at you, and realistically takes close to an hour to dial down combat, crafting, etc.  Patience in this will be rewarded with a fun, but flawed, action RPG that is unique and interesting enough to be considered by anyone whose kept an eye of Biomutant for a long time.  I'm sure patches down the road will iron out the game's most technical and pacing issues.  Play away, yall!

_childDocuments_.review: I have never reviewed a game before because I just like to play and enjoy, however, this game is a unique experience so I wanted to share my thoughts. I was excited to play this game and was really bummed out when I saw all the negative reviews on steam. Do I think they are unwarrented? No. But I think they are specific types of gamers reacting to their expectations of the game, which makes sense. I actually made the decision to get it after watching many video reviews that included game play.Do I think the game is worth $60? No. But I do think this game has entertainment value and shouldn't necessarily be written off for it's short comings completely. I think that when this game goes on sale, many people could have a pleasant experience from it with the right mindset. Now if you are what I would call a more "serious" RPG gamer who enjoys picking the perfect class to make the perfect build, I don't think you will enjoy this game. Outside of a few class specific perks that impact combat on a rather minimal level, class and breed don't really mean much. If you are a more casual gamer who enjoys new experiences, flexibility, crafting, and more relaxed games I think you may find yourself pleasantly surprised by this game. I am more of a casual gamer and tend to only really get serious about certain games and I have had a good time with the game (though I do think it's worth closer to $25-30). Below are my pros and cons. Pros:I like that you can fight with any weapon you want at any given moment. I am a psi freak (focus on abilities aka magic) but I love being able to bonk enemies with a melee weapon if they get close or pew pew them when my energy runs out. I think the world is beautiful and I LOVE the creatures. Most of them are ugly or border on ugly/cute but I get a kick out of that. I love the variety of mounts. There are mounts in each area that are unique to that area. You just need to find a berry for that area and feed it to the mount. There are some genuinely funny moments (like the swimming animation OMG!) and I find myself actually interested in the character's story. There is lots to discover and do if you are patient enough to just check things out!Looting and crafting is super fun to explore and discover.Cons:The dialogue is repetitive and a bit silly at times (sort of stupid silly). I understand that they are going for the vibe that these animals are naming human artifacts but it comes off as goofy. It is true that the narrator translates everything for you and makes random comments but he really didn't bother me as much as the dialogue itself. Choices don't really matter for the story. I like the morality system and the idea of choices but outside of unlocking certain psi abilities based on how light or dark you are, choices don't change game play. The light side choice were usually too fluffy and often didn't result in anything. Example: one citizen asks me to help, I say sure, and end of conversation! That was the light choice. Later a citizen asks for help, I say you're on your own, and proceed to punch the citizen in the face. End of conversation but much more entertaining in my opinion. That was the dark choice. Choosing tribes doesn't really matter except to get tribe armor. You will get tribe weapons by conquering tribes. Some aspects of the game aren't explained super well and some important quests can be easy to miss. I would highly recommend looking up guides before you begin. The world story is confusing and mostly just hits you over the head with environment propaganda.Overall, I think Biomutant is a pleasant experience for the casual gamer who enjoys something new that they can explore and discover. I don't think more serious gamers will enjoy it and I think it's best to add the game to your wishlist and wait for it to go on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game - it’s not bad, it’s just mediocre. Definitely not worth picking up at full price.The world itself is pretty beautiful and kinda fun just to be in, but it’s like a strange mish-mash… it has this days gone / the last of us post-apocalyptic vibe (crumbled bridges and rusted out cars) but then it’s overlaid with this cutesy animal characters that give me Rare banjo kazooie vibes.On that - the characters are so dull and the writing so cheesy: it’s kinda Fable-ish but without the charm. Overall the actual game structure and gameplay feels very dated, continuing the banjo kazooie comparison, this feels like an N64 era game to me with modern graphics and open world - fetch and collect crap, defeat 4 mini bosses, best game. It feels like a throwback (so if you’re looking for that you might really dig it).This is overlaid with quite convoluted RPG character progression and weapon upgrades, but it all feels very meaningless and tacked on.Overall - I don’t hate this game, it’s not bad and if you want a nice easy going time you can do a lot worse…But the game is a lot like its protagonist - a slightly weird mutant mix of different parts. I’m not sure if it was just too ambitious, or the devs weren’t given the time to finish it properly, but it feels like there’s the makings of a great game here but it just never quite gets there.

_childDocuments_.review: I was excited to play this; it looks very good in the images, and I don't really care about the hype for big titles, either positive or negative. Unfortunately though, in this case, I'd say it's justified.- performance is weirdly patchy; frame drops in areas I wouldn't expect there to be, weird texture clipping and unloading sporadically, and sometimes it felt slow to respond to my inputs- there might be a lot of loot and etc to find, but it's not like other open world games where there are points of interest, a la Bethesda, FromSoft, Sony titles; in the few hours I played, the loot was limited to some buildings etc, with little to no reward for exploring off the beaten track. This could have changed further in, but I couldn't get that far, it's too tedious- combat is frustrating at best. There seems to be no interrupt to enemy attacks unless you finish a combo, but enemies normally hit so much faster than you do, do the point where it's almost impossible to actually finish said combo.- aesthetically it's very vibrant, but I'm not sure it's that great quality; the character and gear in the menus looks -great-, but I feel that in the open world, the clutter and colours are there to detract from the quality of some of the assets- sound is pretty nice for the most part, effects and music wise...- ...but the narrator and story presentation is infuriating. If your characters are going to communicate in a made up language, then fine, but let me have subtitles only. The narration is incredibly annoying, and makes for some really jarring cutscenes.I can't finish this, which is a shame, because it looks nice and seems to have some cool features and scale in the late game. But for a AAA title, it feels very janky for its release period, especially as the aesthetics and sound design feel so modern, but the gameplay and combat are so reminiscent of early PS2 era titles.

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels like a single-player version of an MMO that would get its servers taken down less than a few years after launch.It looks very nice, and I like the crafting system with its variety of parts, but that's all I can positively say about it. Its character creator is nice, but it's a cute and interesting veneer over a generic gameplay system. Its interesting premise (humans are gone, screwed the world over, and radiation made animals intelligent) quickly gets bogged down in tribal conflicts with one of the more binary "be nice or be evil for no reason" moral choice systems.The game has terrible pacing, made even worse by dialogue scenes being twice as long as need be by listening to animal gibberish followed by translation from the narrator. Having either the animals be voiced or scenes with no dialogue and visual storytelling might have worked better, but as it stands I felt no attachment to my character. The stakes felt non-existent, and I stopped caring about the tribal conflicts when I saw that it was just another "peace-lovers versus wannabe fascists" conflict with zero nuance. But what broke me was that I never felt like I left the tutorial, even after it introduced the four paths to go to in the wide-open map. Mechanics just kept getting introduced, a flashback sequence came up to introduce two kinds of crafting and introducing that you can swim. You can't get absorbed into the game's prologue because you keep getting interrupted with popups telling you the basic controls. With all of the mechanics getting thrown at you along with lots of exposition in quick succession, it can get overwhelming. The moment I realized I couldn't continue this game was after I did the first taking of a rival tribe's outpost. I thought that was the end of the tutorializing, but then an NPC tells me to go to one of the four main bosses. And that's when I realized this was too much to ignore. Six tribes you can join, but you're forced to pick one of two completely opposite tribes at the start. All of these different styles and upgrades in service of basic hack/slash/shoot combat. And a map that seems wide-open but still has a preferred way of going through it.There are specific games I won't name that I wish this was more like, but I saw so many ways this game could have been improved. As it stands, this game is not very fun to play, with an interesting visual theme to it, but almost nothing else going for it. I wanted to buy this and keep playing it to support the smaller team, but I couldn't even bring myself to do that.

_childDocuments_.review: People are being too harsh. This game isn't meant to be deep into the story or into any one thing. It's meant to be an open world RPG that you choose how quickly you want to progress through the main story, side quests, or just random map reveal. There is obviously some boundaries/gates to certain areas until you've "unlocked" the option to travel there, but it's been fun. I am playing Dead Eye first time around. The skills are pretty straight forward, and just enhance the gameplay without overcomplicating it. Some games incorporate skill systems that feel consequential, whereas this provides a good base for you to build off of with more skills. It's interesting, fun, and doesn't take itself too seriously. Story reminds me of Skyrim's depth. It would be easier to connect if the characters spoke vs the narrator, but I don't really care for the story of this game much. I get the concept of what we're trying to do and skip through most of the dialogue unless it's choice based. 4 hours in. it's fun to pickup, okay to put down after that period and come back to it again tomorrow to continue the exploration. Enjoy if this is what you're looking for. Stay away if you want a story-rich rpg story that you can connect to. This isn't it.

_childDocuments_.review: Note: Running with all graphics maxed on a 6gig 1060 without crashing or stutter so anyone with newer than that should be able to run it just as well.Day 1: I like it. It actually opens up a couple of times. Not everything works with everything else but there is a lot to do and a huge world to explore so I say it's a yes.Day 2: I spent the whole day exploring. Let myself just wander. Took to the rails to see where they lead. Let myself just go anywhere and if anything caught my eye I wandered off to investigate. Explored a lot of underground areas, and found a lot of secrets. Found so many things, and did so much. I had a lot of fun.Day 3: I had a plan that I was going to keep going out East farther than I had yesterday. But I ended up spending the whole day wandering around mostly searching through the devastated wasteland area in the West. I got the Mech and couldn't stop playing with it, and looking for more parts to upgrade it. So much fun today.Day 4: I finally took a good look in my quest log, and wow I had so many open active side quests that I hadn't really noticed I had. I hadn't paid attention to all of the citizens who had quest for me because they were usually asking me to go back where I'd come from, or off in another direction away from my main objective at the time. So I went through them and found one offering a radioactivity suit and was off. I spent the day trying to work my way to that island with the tiny bomb shelter on it. I just kept getting side tracked. Once I finally got the suit I finally understood that I had been relating the wrong colors to things. Biohazard is green and radioactivity is neon purple. So I went back to some purple places that I hadn't been able to get to before and then just wandered for a while. I am really loving this game and how free I feel. I like the way no matter where I go the fights are a challenge and feel fun. I keep upgrading my weapons and armor and there is plenty to do. Another great day.Day 5: The world just keeps opening up at this point. I made a point of looking for more of the hazard protection suits. I still have a bunch of open side quests 30 plus at this point, and I spent a lot of today trying to work those down. But yeah I got side tracked a lot. There is still some areas I can't get too and at least a quarter of the map I haven't seen. The cut and pasted objects, and map parts are no different from any other game. They do become repetitive but the enemies change a lot. Sometimes they fly and sometimes they can use the different biohazards to really hurt you. For most of today I was constantly finding new things and areas, and though some were very similar it's more like a store that is laid out the same for your convenience than a bad thing. I can feel the end coming but I know I have at least another good day ahead of me. 35 Hours in and I'm still having a lot of fun.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wish there was a mixed mark because there are some really good elements to this game as you can see by my play time, but there are many different problems also with this game,. I haven't encountered any bugs but there are elements that I don't understand how the devs didn't see. Like i'm playing this and thinking of things they could have done which makes me think if they have even played their own game.The mount system is cool but why can't we have multiple mounts on the summon button, literally had a really cool skeleton horse but did a mission to get Mjut because you need it to open certain area. As soon as it was completed my other horse just disappeared which is annoying as I have no clue how to get him back. Why include sales vendors of animals if you can only have one at a time, it just makes all the other mounts useless if you need one to open certain areas.The mutations and psi powers are cool. But again, why include so many when you can only have 4 at a time, it's mind boggling. Could have included a system like assassins creed where there are two layers to the powers. I will guarantee you will only use a select few as there are others that are basically useless. The dark abilities are weak compared to light so keep that in mind.Don't even get me started on the narrator, honestly so annoying. The amount of time i've heard him speak about activating the mainframe after completing a puzzle, or if you fail the puzzle he will just speak again, this is with the narrator on 20. I turned him off from translating characters as the dialogue was irritating.Talking of puzzles, jeeeeeeeeeeeesus. Never have I ever seen so many useless repetitive puzzles in a game before, at the start I was like ok, this is cool. However the more you play the more annoying they become and you find yourself traversing the land just to do these puzzles.The open world and environment is the best thing about this game hands down. Although, there are so many copy and paste jobs it's ridiculous, like some buildings are literally the same layout which removes the fun from the exploration element as well as the fact that some superb loot are in silly places so a lot of time you just completely miss them so I had to do a Youtube job a few timesAt the moment i'm level 40 and each new item I get I have to scrap because it is useless. Crafting system is also very unique, however like I just said I keep finding parts way below my level now which means that the system becomes useless taking the fun out of that particular elementMissions in this game is lacking. Had to do 4 fetch quests from the same character at one point. Some are so close to each other as well so you find yourself back tracking multiple times which just makes you want to stop playing the game and very infuriating to be honest.The combat element is cool and fun, although the enemies get tedious and very boring after a while as they are re-skins and you find yourself doing the same thing. Some there is no point fighting in close range because they will just flatten you, especially if there is two of them so there are a lot of fights where ranged guns are best. Melee weapons are way too weak compared to guns, can literally run around holding the trigger. This is the problem, there are so many unique elements in this game which is great, however there should be quality over quantity. Bought this on CD Keys for like £30 and i've got my time out of it for that money, definitely not worth full price though until there are improvements in the game.As the aforementioned summon feature, this is the reason for this review. I think i'm going to stop playing for a while as that really peeved me off.Great elements and it is fun to play, however many systems rip the heart and soul out from the game. I'd advise you to buy if on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I dig it so far. I think people are just spewing bad reviews because it's fun to pile onto critically disappointing games when they release. _childDocuments_.review: 100% Achievements - 49 HoursNot sure where all the hate for this game stems. It's a fun, often times silly RPG that gives nostalgic vibes in the vein of N64/NGC era games' charm. Did a melee playthrough and combat was fun, just smashing away at enemies and occasionally using super wung-fu for big aoe. _childDocuments_.review: Changing the language from English to Japanese is so much better. Completely changes the experience!!!! Interesting game from a small Dev team, that have poured their heart and souls into this project for quite a few years.  It's far from purrfect, but I have been looking forward to this game for so long. Initial impressions were not great, but as it stands I reckon it's probably worth a 7 or 8 out of 10. Obviously that may change, but all in all I'm pleased with it so far!!!!UPDATE:BIOMUTANT is a great game. Having spent more time with it, I can honestly say it's a very chilled Zen like experience with good combat and exploration and lot's of loot. It has a great crafting system and overall is fun to play, with an addictive game loop. Yes it can feel a bit childish and would definitely have been a far better game with a more serious tone. Survival elements would also have helped flesh out the game more, although there is no shortage of things to do or discover.In my book BIOMUTANT is a hidden gem and whilst it's rough around the edges, particularly in the beginning, the game becomes much more enjoyable and open when you finally get in to the flow of the game, and start to understand the mechanics.It's just a shame that some players will be turned off by this, because hidden within this game is a very fun, enjoyable experience to be had, if you only have the patience to play the game and find this out for yourself.Considering this game was made by such a small team, I think they have done a fantastic job.In my opinion this game is worth a buy in a sale, it should have been priced at £39.99 !!!!!Overall Score: 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Wait for at least 50% off. It is worth a play through but not worth $59.99. I waited for this game since the first time I saw it in a gamestop magazine. I have mixed feelings about the game. When watching the trailer for this I got this since of this deep story I was going to get into. Instead I got this boring narrator. I feel it was very lazy on the devs part. All the NPCs have nothing to say and your choices you pick are confusing. It is like it doesn't translate well to the conversation or something. Simply put I am about 20 hours in and I don't really know any of the characters or their stories and I am just wondering from objective to objective. I really wish they took a more mature approach to this game. You get options like kill this creature but then the narrator says moomsie and poopsi like you're a baby or something. Just goofy and awkward. Finally the last part I don't like is leveling. Thing I love about RPGs is character crafting. In Biomutant I do not get excited when I level. I pick my attribute and save my skill points. I save the skill points because the perks and skills are meh. Nothing really was screaming oh lets build this way. There are different classes but it isn't game breaking different. Each class has like 4 different "class" perks that arent' exciting and then they all get the same pool of dual wield, two hand, magic, general ect ect. Don't get excited about the mage class either. Be prepared to use the same magic you've been using since the start. Now for some things I did like about the game. The crafting in this game is pretty fun. I think other RPGs should take note and making something similar. You really get to make each piece of your weapon. The world is beautiful and there is a lot to do. The quests never felt like a chore but that is because I think I just enjoy the battles in this game. I love the free flow between melee and gun combat. It is just fun. I think the vehicles are cool but they should have added a better customizing system.

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately, I wouldn't recommend purchasing this game at it's current price.The game is quite beautiful, but gameplay is limited (the different weapons have very similar moves, enemies are low in variety, and every fight ends up being very similar) and the perk system doesn't give much variety.However, I could have forgiven above, but what really got me was the story telling. _childDocuments_.review: I find it wild how the creators of Biomutant did exactly what most developers don't do in present day. * When issues cropped up about their game post-launch they didn't go silent. * The developers listened to all player feedback, even the nasty stuff, most vital feedback is on their Discord server. * The developers then went about patching and addressing those issues as fast as possible. * As of today (6/1/2021) , Biomutant had a huge patch that fixed not only bugs with the game, but a vast sweeping majority of complaints and nitpicks players had. From combat sounds to narration,  loot variety, difficulty and even reworked their entire tutorial.  A team of 20 has pulled this off in under 2 weeks since the launch of their game. * The speed and dedication these developers have displayed on their attempts to make their game exactly what not only they want, but the players want, absolutely earns my recommendation to play this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I say recommended, because I have hopes for this game. To my understanding, the game was made by a small team, and I gotta tip my hat to them for that, but it seems to be missing a lot.Graphically, I can't decide if it's good or not. Being made with Unreal, I know how good a game CAN look, but this is hit-or-miss. Grass swaying in the wind looks good from a distance, but up close, it's pretty ugly. Some textures look flat or "waxy", and some environmental things like the cars and houses are pretty bland. A lot of reused assets everywhere, and a pretty small roster of enemies thus far. Animations feel pretty stiff and robotic, like climbing a ladder and some combat moves. The combat is pretty average in all areas, but it has something for everyone. If you're not bashing your enemies apart, you're pretty much just kiting around and chipping away at their health.The trailer made this game look like Bayonetta meets Conker, but it falls short there. My biggest gripe besides relatively repetitive quests, is that the world is big, but empty. It's Borderlands for furries, but without as many enemy engagements or things to find. Weapon and clothing customization is pretty sweet, but you'll end up finding a lot of the same items with slightly different stats, and eventually you'll have to give up that cool looking part or weapon, if you want better statsThe narrator gets pretty annoying and the huge amount of dialogue becomes a slog to deal with. Especially in parts you've already played after starting a new game. The character customization is cool, albeit limited in a weird way, and a missed opportunity. There are a variety of ways you can morph your character, and the changes range from cool, to cute, to comical, but it kinda sucks that you can't change specific features/shapes, like eyes, ears, or specific facial structure and stuff like that. I mean, with how the morph system already works, you cannot tell me that it wouldn't work here.. It's also interesting that stats are more or less kind of reflected in your appearance, but as you level up, it doesn't seem to matter. All in all, it's still fun if you like looter/shooters, but if you're on the fence about it, nobody will blame you if you decided to wait. Hopefully the devs don't leave us hanging, and actually improve their game incrementally....

_childDocuments_.review: I refused to look at reviews for this game until after I had an initial impression on it. I was one of those people who thought "well, I am going to judge a game for myself and ignore the reviews." Not so much because I want to discount what other people are saying (and continue to say) but because I judge games differently than other people.I'm a very casual gamer. I don't play for the challenge, I play for the experience. IMO, Biomutant ticks off everything for me in all the right ways, and while there are a few things I don't like, I am not too bummed that I spent the full price of 60 on it.Things I love: -the story. It's simple, it's quaint, and while it isn't deep I figure it does what it needs to do. Love the flashback bits where you steadily recount the protagonist's history. -Like the morality scale. It's nice you can play a jerk, even though I never will haha-Love the narrator. He's cute. While I wish everyone had proper voice acting and the narrator makes it sickeningly obvious that there wasn't a budget for that, it does give the game a "story book" vibe and I personally enjoy it.- Lol you pee on signposts to mark them for fast travel- The crafting!! It's neat and easy to understand, and not too convoluted for idiots like me!- the setting. Beautiful world, interesting to explore, lots to see!-THE VEHICLES/MOUNTS ARE AMAZING HOLY ♥♥♥♥-The puzzles are easy. I'm an idiot so I am thankful for this.-Goofy ass dialogue. Sounds like it was made by people trying to sound fantasy-like. Taking it seriously is not what I think was intended; the silly words feel very cheeky to me.-The combat. Flows well, not too sluggish, easy to pick up and learn.-The enemy designs are a mix between spooky, cute, and really unique. Love them.-NPCs are pretty. Mounts are pretty. Everything's super pretty and I wish I could pet all the bang bang raccoons I find walking aroundThings that kinda annoy me:-The animations.. or lack thereof, in some cases.. are a bit jarring. Most bosses do the same thing. Attack patterns really don't change.- The character creator. Why is my appearance tied to stats? That's a no-go for me, joe.-The combat difficulty, or lack thereof.. I personally don't mind the easyness, but I know some people are going to hate it.-Wish the NPCs had more to say. They all seem to say the same thing, with some words switched around. They say you're a good kid and go on some annoying speel about how life is deep or some ♥♥♥♥. Wish they were less corny or at the very least had some differentiating dialogue.-Wish the NPCs were.. well, more. They look nice but that's about it. They have no distinct personalities or histories or anything. It's either "I'm eeeevul and want to destroy da wurld" or "I'm a piece of optimistic soggy cardboard with no decernable personality traits other than I'm trying to sound deep but I'm really not"-....Also the combat. Too easy. No difficulty whatsoever. Not a deal breaker for me but I know it will be for others looking for a more standard RPG experience.-There *should* be an option for more difficult puzzles for people who want them. Think puzzle difficulty from silent hill. Not everyone is willing to trudge through easy puzzles and some people just want a challenge, and there's nothing wrong with that.All in all? I rate it a 6/10. A little above mediocre, but still veeery enjoyable imo. not really worth the 60 bucks but def, DEFinitely get it on sale. _childDocuments_.review: Definitely an 8/10. Minimum.I've been struggling to understand the negativity around this game. I purposely sheltered myself from any hype whatsoever involving Biomutant, only looking so far into it to make sure it's not something like rhythm based or PvP (things I Personally do not enjoy). Aside from that, I seen "Ninja Kung Fu Squirrel" and that was enough to keep me interested and rather excited to play.I was Not disappointed.I personally really have a lot of fun with the game for what it is: a large, post-apocalypse open world for you to explore and loot. Fight random baddies like you're in a martial arts movie, attempt to get old machinery or devices to start working again and salvage what you can out of it. It's your character and the open road, doing what you can to survive against how hostile the world has become due to the past actions of the species before yours. If that sounds fun to you, then you'll probably enjoy the game like I have.But let's go through some of these common complaints I see to satisfy the goblin in my brain:-The Narrator Is AnnoyingHe... Really isn't. He's got a pleasant voice to listen to, and though he doesn't have a 'Lot' to say about the current situation, he does make the journey less lonely. If you weren't bothered by the narrator in, say, The Stanley Parable, then you should be fine here. If not:Options -> Audio -> Volume -> Speech = 0, Frequency -> Narrator = 0.You Can Turn Him Off. You Are GIVEN That Option.Does it stop 'all' subtitles? No. But the ones that remain actually feels like it's your own character's inner thoughts. Or perhaps your conscience wondering if you're doing the correct thing, but that could just be me.-The Combat Is ____The Combat is fine. Maybe it's not "Insert Your Perfect Game Here" (like Devil May Cry 3), but it's not trying to be. The game gives you enough tools, weapons, skills, points, etc. to play around with other weapon/gun types- On The Same Character. There's no reason to Min/Max here: If you find yourself bored, try something new. Did you find a shotgun barrel with ice element that seemed interesting to try? Do so. Use your scrap that you've collected and put one together and see how it works out. Play around with different melee/ranged/"tech" abilities to find something fun. Is it always going to be the best thing to mow down all enemies effortlessly? Probably not, but that doesn't mean it's not fun to play around with. It's kind of a sandbox game: you make your own fun here, and the game gives you plenty of opportunities to do just that. I've played games that are more expensive than this that have faaaaarrrrr worse combat systems, the one in Biomutant is good for what it's trying to portray.-The Story Is Weak.It kinda is, very Black & White. But that doesn't mean YOURS has to be. The story is just a baseline to give you an epic, that's about it. Your Story can be whatever you want it to be.... Within limits. Okay, look, it's not going to be Skyrim or Divinity: OS2 levels of choices here. You're not going to be able to kill the NPCs and steal their homes/stuff. But you are alive, I assume, so you have the ability to use that imagination of yours. Stop waiting for the game to carve your story out and make it yourself, it's not going to be able to read your mind. No Developer can. I personally would rather have the freedom to make my own vs being pulled by the nose through a horribly boring story that I'm not engaged in. If you don't like the story in Biomutant, you can basically skip through it without missing much.-The Tutorial Is Long.It kinda is, and it can be very hand-holdy in the beginning. But I believe they're working on changing this a bit-Actually, I just checked, and they apparently altered the Tutorial for the better in yesterday's patch. I personally have to play through it again to really see, but they've made several fixes that should make it better.-QTEs Suck....You can turn them off. 90% of them anyway. Look into Accessibility Options. Seriously, thank the Devs for putting this option in, because Bloody Hell, I'm so tired of QTEs...-The Puzzles Are Bad.They're not "Bad", they're "Easy". They're just there to break up the gameplay loop a little bit and give you something else to do. I don't mind the fact that they're easy, better than stonewalling all progress just to open a door for a quick exit. And they do spice it up rather creatively, I thought. I don't remember seeing anything like them in other games recently. I honestly welcome them.-The Price Is Too High.*Presses the space between his eyes*Okay... Look. People who work on things like this DESERVE to be paid for it. Especially if they're doing it for a LIVING. Considering the hours and sacrifices they make to their own lives for Your precious entertainment. As controversial as this is going to sound, I'd argue that games should be more expensive- but I won't do that here. A review is not the right time. Yes, it's decently expensive, but you're getting a lot of content for that price. And you don't need to "Buy it now while supplies last". If it actually is too expensive for you currently, save up a little bit more next month/whatever and get it then. This isn't a "Live Service" game here, it'll be around for when you have the spare cash on you. If anything you'll be getting any bugs patched up by waiting a little bit, but it is Not "Too Pricey" in general.Look, the game isn't perfect, but it definitely does not deserve all the hate and the mixed rating. "Not Recommended" should be saved for actual bad games and crappy business practices/scams, not "6/10"s. If you didn't enjoy the game, that's Fine, but Biomutant... FUNCTIONS. It does a lot of things well if you REALLY take the time to look at it. It's not some broken mess of a game like some of the nightmare stories you've heard before (and you know the ones I'm talking about). They delayed the release of the game to AVOID that! Maybe it's not what you were expecting, but that's hype for you: it alters your perspectives of what a game can/will be. Learn from it; don't give into hype or set your expectations too high in the future. And hopefully we won't have another casualty like this in the future, because a "Mixed: 67% Positive" is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ shame for something as good as this.

_childDocuments_.review: For $60, I can't recommend this game. For the first couple hours it was fun, the story is somewhat intriguing and the vibrant colors look beautiful, but there's just so many areas that are lacking and with the lack of updates it feels like the game was abandoned as soon as it launched. There was a large patch just after launch that fixed numerous bugs and some changes to the sound elements but overall that wasn't enough to even bring back my interest in the game. The narration becomes stale after a couple hours, missions are incredibly repetitive, side missions are there just to waste your time, having to go through this linear progression of "get the suit, go here to this vault to get another gear item to then go here" can be completely bypassed by leveling up immunity but you still get stuck with side missions to get that past gear you no longer need. Sometimes you find items that are dozens of levels above you which you can't use and by the time you get to that level the stats are already outdates. All of the weapon sounds lack any depth, combos are basically narrowed down to mash left click until things die. The whole "ability" attacks are less effective than just swinging a blade and don't provide any use during combat. Overall, the game was a fantastic idea that if given more time could have been great, but without re-writing the entire story, getting rid of narration, making missions actually meaningful, or even just adding more weapons or improving sound design, it's a lost cause. If you can find this game for $20 it might be worth that, but do not pay a full $60 for it.

_childDocuments_.review: In Biomutant you play as a Kung-Fu mutanted animal after the world has ended. Your main goal is to either save or destroy what's left of the world. You get to pick from different classes, creating a character whose abilities can range from shooting lightning out of your hands Palpatine style, to giga chad bruiser juggling enemies around. Despite this set up the game is mostly about exploring to find better gear or upgrade what you already have. A lot of the game feels pretty underwhelming. During my entire playthrough it felt like something was missing. Something that would've made it great, but I couldn't really pinpoint what it was. Overall pretty meh. The dialogue is full of made-up words and other gibberish which takes away any motivation to actually want to talk with the other characters in the world. Melee combat has some janky hitboxes with pretty basic movesets. The psi powers and mutant powers are only good if you spec into intelligence, making it almost useless for strength focused builds. Once you find a good gun the combat becomes a breeze regardless of class. The highlights in my opinion where early to mid parts of the game, after that I felt like the only reason to explore was to try and find a slightly better piece of gear.Before you think about buying the game make sure to watch a little bit of gameplay, as the game is very repetitive. I was able to find some enjoyment out of it but I would only recommend getting this game if it's on sale. It's really only worth doing one or two playthroughs since the only difference will be your aura and class, everything else is the same. Overall, I'd give it like 5.5/10If you do decide to pick this game up, I'd advise really thinking about what class and attributes to take before finishing character creation because once you pick them you're stuck with them for the rest of the game. Don't worry too much about how you character looks besides their color since you're able to change it later on.

_childDocuments_.review: Tl;dr: I wouldn't purchase this for $60 unless you want to support THQNordic which I wholeheartedly endorse, because of movement being "feathery". $40 and below is a good price. 7/10 5 hours into the game.First off, thank you THQNordic for a key. I would not say it's worth $60 for one thing and one thing only: nothing feels like it has any weight to it. Movement is something that stays with you for the entire game and it basically feels like you're controlling a feather and slapping enemies with wet spaghetti noodles even if the damage doesn't reflect it. I'll say again: MOVEMENT IS A THING THAT STAYS WITH YOU THE ENTIRE GAME and should be polished to a SHEEN. Not a lot of games use "feathery, floaty" movement nowadays and I'm not sure who was in charge of that design decision but I'd rather things have mass to them than not.The characters are super unique, the world is absolutely gorgeous, the item design is excellently done, but... the movement and combat mechanics do leave a little to be desired unfortunately.I can also see the core gameplay loop: 1. Factions exist in the game2. You're a loner who's also a badass that everyone talks about whose parents died3. You help factions to damage the other factions/gain/lose rep with through quests (75% of the gameplay loop)4. A huge thing happens that every faction has to work together for5. You unite all the factions and live peacefullyI absolutely hate seeing through games like this but I'd be happy to be proven wrong.A full review will be forthcoming after I put some more hours into the game.

_childDocuments_.review: The post-apocalyptic environment is gorgeous to look at, whether it's the lush wilderness or the remnants of a city that got me to sing City Ruins (Rays of Light) from Nier Automata. It's also diverse too, which is definitely a welcome change from desert-y wastelands found in Fallout, Mad Max, and Fist of the North Star. I never get bored from looking at everything while heading to my next objective or getting sidetracked to what's left of a convenience store, houses, and other structures humanity left behind. The critters' design may be hit-or-miss, but for the most part, they look absolutely adorable! Their fur is well-shaded, and the various animations that The Protagonist has can be charmingly cute (i.e proudly posing with their hands on their hips after acquiring a spankin' new set of clothes). Plus, I find it strangely attractive to interact with various modern day gadgets like washing machines or arcade cabinet from the perspective of a mutated critter. I love the inclusion of Chinese instruments in the soundtracks, and they definitely give me the right feels from time to time when exploring the New World. My only complaint is that it changes abruptly whenever you go into an indoor area from the outside and vice-versa. I wish that it plays without any interruptions. The crafting system is rad (pun totally intended), especially when it comes to making your own melee weapons and guns. I can't say the same for clothes however, seeing as how most of the addons may not match the overall aesthetics. Combat can get somewhat tedious and frustrating, especially when facing off against a large mob of enemies that can easily interrupt your melee attacks and knock you flat on your ass. It makes it easier to fall back on the dominant strategy, aka using powerful crafted guns or Super Wung-Fu, to take shots from a safe distance. It's fun at first, but then it gets repetitive the more you rely on it. The lack of a dedicated lock-on system like the one in Yakuza or Nier means that it's really frustrating when most of your shots miss or they hit the wrong enemy. The Narrator is talented and has a great voice, but when overused, he becomes an annoyance. Because of how he translates  of the gibberish that the characters speak in using a relatively neutral tone, a lot of their characterization gets lost as a result. I find it easier to relate to characters when they are speaking directly to The Protagonist (and by extension, the player) without an interpreter doing all the heavy lifting. One way to remedy this is to either have the gibberish subtitled or let the characters (and the Protagonist) speak in partially corrupted English/Russian/Japanese/etc. The Light/Dark Karma System feels too simplistic to allow a lot of room for creating nuances in characters' personalities, especially when I want to roleplay The Protagonist as a flawed yet compassionate individual. It doesn't help that the six tribes and their leaders are given shallow characterization, and they don't do much in the story aside from waiting and hoping for The Protagonist to join them so they can further their agendas. I wish that they were more active in the setting, and perhaps scrapping or hiding the Karma System so the characters will be given more chances to develop. The game's exploration of the theme of balance feels to me that it's hampered by the presence of a mechanical scale. The sidequests, like killing giant monsters or finding and interacting with modern day technologies, are fun at the beginning, but they become a slog later on the in the game. The puzzles also feel too simple to be challenging.  The main plot doesn't feel cohesive. After finishing a pure Light side playthrough, it felt to me as though the writers were having troubles deciding on how to tie up loose plot threads, and one thing ended just as it's about to become interesting.  Some of the invented words are a little over-the-top that they don't appeal to anyone at all.Biomutant is, for the lack of better words, a flawed game. It deserves a try, even if it's a wait-for-sale type of game. It has a lot of interesting ideas that are cobbled together, but sadly, aren't fully developed. I believe that a game like this could benefit from either a soft reboot, a much-improved sequel, or a more refined spiritual successor.

_childDocuments_.review: It makes me very sad to have to rate this game negatively. I had high hopes for it for so long, but after completing the game it simply did not live up to the expectations they set forth from the trailers and teasers. I understand this game was made by a small and inexperienced team, however as a full price $60 game it deserves to be judged with the same criticisms I would judge any $60 AAA title with.I'll start by saying that it isn't that I necessarily didn't enjoy playing the game. I did have fun while playing. It is more so that the negatives outweigh the positives. The open world is vast, and it is beautiful. Stylistically the game looks very good. Unfortunately there isn't much to look at once you start to explore and look deeper. With a severely limited number of different types of enemies ( most just being recolored versions of others ) combined with the towns, tribes, bunkers, contamination/cold/hot/etc. zones, and all "areas of interest" having only one layout that is copy + pasted throughout the world you run out of interesting things to see exceptionally quickly. And though the game is stylized very well, nothing in the game is graphically impressive. The combat is severely lacking and the enemies all feel hollow and bland. Your attacks feel weightless and are interrupted by any move the enemies make as well as not changing much from start to finish of the game. As you level you don't feel any stronger or more impressive. The melee component is under-powered compared to the guns and it is noticeable from the very first encounter. Almost every fight in the game ( to include all bosses) can be fought with a gun exclusively and all you have to do in run in circles and shoot while dodging occasionally. The powers you get are underwhelming and once unlocked contain no progression. Powers don't level up, fighting doesn't level up, gun play doesn't level up and it leads to a stale feeling combat experience by the second hour of game play. There are also many bugs in the game. Sound effects don't play sometimes, bio points are incorrectly used while leveling up resistances, enemies glide across the ground to complete attacks that would otherwise miss and too many more to mention. While none of the bugs ruined the game for me they did lead to a much more frustrating and confusing experience. The last thing I feel has to be mentioned is the story and how it is conveyed to the player. About ninety percent of the story in the game is presented to the player at the very beginning. The beginning of the story is genuinely interesting however nothing after that point carries any weight at all. The morality system is a joke where when completing tasks or talking to NPCs they get as close as possible to literally asking you, "Do you want light points or dark points?". That is basically the gist of it. The NPCs all say the exact same voice lines, except the story important ones who have small parts of their dialogue tweaked to fit their part of the world. After defeating every boss (which is a series of fetch quests and then a very basic boss battle) the NPCs all say the same lines and if you don't complete the story in the exact order they expect you to the things they say might not even be true.A personal opinion of mine that might not be popular is that the choice to go with a single narrator who voices everything that happens in the game was a bad idea. After the first hour I was completely sick of him. Narrating me opening new doors, narrating every enemy that crossed my path, narrating which area I was entering. The narrator got so annoying by the end that I turned his volume almost all the way down and set his frequency to as low as it goes. It seems like someone on the dev team played The Stanley Parable too much and didn't really understand the relationship between the world, the player and the narrator very well. A narrator isn't a bad thing but having to sit through uninspired drivel while npcs make gibberish sounds for ten seconds, then the narrator translates with some dad joke tacked on is torture. TL;DRThis game under-delivers in every aspect it offers. A story that feels like it was written by a middle schooler, combat that only functions on the most simple of levels, a world where all the assets are copy pasted around it and it still isn't very densely populated, and an rpg system with uninteresting, bland looking materials and gear that are completely unnecessary and don't progress with you as the game plays out.If you want a gorgeous open world game with amazing combat play Ghost of Tsushima.If you want a fun to play RPG system where leveling up feels important and impactful play Skyrim, or Fallout, or Final Fantasy.If you want a game where you character mutates and grows and changes throughout the story to become stronger/faster/more interesting . . . well me too, but Biomutant did not deliver on that promise. If this game ever drops to $15 i'd say it's worth it to pick it up and give it a playthrough. I don't even think i'd be comfortable recommending it at $30. At $60 for this unfinished, uninspired and uninteresting game I'd say stay away.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR Game looks beautiful. Combat is very boring even with a lot of the abilities and moves unlocked. Enemies are literally just re-skins all the way down to their move sets. The super mode is very sub par and doesn't make you feel like a martial arts master. Quests are some of the laziest I've ever seen and the story is really generic, almost nonexistent. Wait for it to be at least 30-50% off and then i'd say that you will have a good time. At full price, you're going to feel burnt and may or may not feel like you are forcing your fun.  For $60.00 I cannot recommend it. There are other, cheaper games that will give you the same feeling of doing tedious side quests for almost pointless loot, bandit camps, rescue people, and bring me x item. I am having fun but it feels like a mix of forced and boredom since nothing else has really come out that I was looking forward to. The combat gets very boring in my opinion. It feels the same even after you have fleshed out your abilities and weapons. Every enemy fights the same to the point where I don't even know why there are enemies with different names. One large tribe member fights exactly like the other tribe member. The smalls are just rinse and repeat as well. The wildlife even all fight the same. It's either a charge move, side swipe, or pick up and throw you. The elemental style enemies use different elements but have the same animations and practically the same damage unless you are heavily invested in one specific type of resistance (which that is perfectly fine for gameplay). The super mode (don't remember the name) is very lackluster but it does do great damage. Don't expect anything like Dante's devil trigger or, Kratos's Spartan Rage here. It doesn't look very cool and the sound effects feel like a wet bag hitting a wall. It just doesn't make you feel like a badass when you use it. If you want to change weapons on the fly you will be seeing the radial menu A LOT. I see why this is necessary for controllers but on PC they should have done something with the other number keys. Finally, a lot of the psi skills just seem useless and a waste of time using. They look cool but that's about it. The game world is beautiful and the art department did an outstanding job. Weapons look really cool, the character design is interesting and the armor looks right for the setting. Sadly, that's about all I can say about that. It is beautiful and devoid of anything truly meaningful to do or life. The side quests are trivial and the puzzles are so lazy that I cannot even think about why they felt the need to include them. The only reason to go off the beaten path is to find money plants (literally pointless because the game throws enough loot at you to where money isn't a problem after selling it or not even needing it), and some shrines for extra points. NPCs exist for window dressing. They gave an option to speak with them but nothing interesting is said other than some form of, "Hello." Or, "I remember you. Goodbye." They should have just done what TW3 or even Dragon Age does and just have them walk by and maybe spout random drivel. The main NPCs all have similar dialogue and only exist to point you along the way. You won't learn much from them. If you were expecting to find out why a village is in a certain spot, or the history of the land, just use your imagination because you won't get much else. The story isn't anything spectacular. Generic save the world from the bad monsters. That is fine, in my opinion and probably not even worth for anyone to hate on. If everything else just felt like it had weight to it then the game would have probably been amazing. For what it is right now, it has few (no game breaking that i've noticed) to no bugs, runs very well and ticks most of the basic boxes. It doesn't do anything to innovate, which would be absolutely fine if the things it borrowed were done better.Quick Edit: Forgot to mention that I beat the game on hard at level 29. From 1-20 I slogged through the awful melee and only used guns to activate the special moves to use super wushu. After that and crafting a less damaging gun than my main hand weapon, I proceeded to never touch melee again in favor of just keeping it as a cosmetic on my character. The gun (non auto rifle) with almost 250 damage less was hitting for almost 400 more points of damage with the benefit of a status effect and more hits per second. The Devs really need to look into their game balance more. I also stopped using super wushu after getting the stupid kill 50 enemy achievement. It's literally quite useless vs using your guns. Even higher level enemies were dying before a reload.

_childDocuments_.review: Just few hours into this AAA game and I already hate it.The camera doesn't feels right. It is way too close, so I can't see ammo (which is shown above the gun somehow). The player character is way too small and camera makes it hard to observe surroundings, which are often much higher. I believe this game could be much better as a first person FPS.I dislike combat pretty much, was hoping it will get more interesting later, but not, it's just constant running in circles and pressing dodge, despite I am trying to build ranged, namely mage-type character... there is no stealth, tactical approach or anything: the enemies simply spawn and run for you. Playing it batman games way (pressing parry when seeing attack indicators) is surprisingly hard and unreliably, perhaps it's just my poor skills, though I didn't have problem to do perfect parries in e.g. Assassin Creed games.The game performance is very unstable. Maybe my system is not top, but turning everything on "low" and having stable 60 fps, then suddenly it drops to 30 and stay there in the city.. same with "maximum" where it drops to 30 under the ground. WTF? Why is it 60 or 30? It must be something hardcoded into game engine, made for consoles...Big locations with nothing. Occasionally there are chests. Then city with hundereds of chests everywhere. Exploring is most of time not rewarding. It's hard to see if location has something hidden and map is surrounded by invisible walls everywhere, feels really poor with double jump to hit such wall.The loot system coupled with craft system is not interesting. The inventory UI has problems (e.g. selecting head slot).The dialogues are dumb, I need to press key 4 times to just listen a gossip or begin trading, lol. The choices are unclear, several times the NPC reply something totally unrelated to the option I select.The narrator voice is annoying in Russian translation. It comments everything and I dislike the style where narrator translates what NPC tells, wonder if someone actually find that good, to me it's just a cheap way to simplify translation, but lack of good voices makes story telling really poor, imho.Not sure if I continue playing the game, but perhaps my and others negative reviews will prevent someone from wasting their money.

_childDocuments_.review: = Art = 10/10 - Has to be one of the most beautifully designed games of 2021 so far.= Combat =6/10 - Biomutant gives you countless ways to create a very distinct fighting style for your character. However, the enemies act as damage sponges. They give very little response to your damage. At times it seems like you are "fighting a health bar," not a challenging AI. = Story =5/10 - Decide the fate of the tree, conclude the tribe war, and settle a score with the creature who attacked your village. All of this is accompanied by a theme of pollution that is meant to mirror our own real life issues with pollution.  = Quests =6/10 - There are a view gems here and there. However, most objectives felt like glorified "go here, kill this" or "go here, get this" quests.= Voice Acting =8/10 - The creators of Biomutant took a risk with their unique twist on narrating the game's story. There is one main narrator who talks when prompted by certain things throughout the world and translates all in game dialogue. All of the creatures who talk to you in the game speak some gibberish language hence why the narrator translates. Due to the pause of the NPC speaking and the narrator translating, dialogue at times feels slow. However, I just got used to it over time and have grown to appreciate the quirky narrator. If you do not like the narrator's voice or don't want him to speak for other reasons, there is a way to disable his narration and commentary.= Exploration =9/10 - The game world is vast and built beautifully which only entices exploration. My time in the game has mostly been spent in abandoned villages, underground cave systems littered with old-world technology, using a  jet ski like object to explore distance islands, and using a constructed mech to explore a zone deficient in oxygen. All of that is experienced only within the first couple hours of playing.= Crafting =10/10 - I crafted a two-handed melee weapon that is a walking cane connected to a door that was ripped off of a safe. Oh, it also deals cold damage and freezes the bad guys.= Multiplayer =Not currently supported and currently no disclosed plans on providing this feature. = Overall =7.7/10 - Biomutant tries to do a lot and is not able to deliver in some areas due to their ambition. However,  they are really able to knock certain areas out of the park. Furthermore, the developers have already made it clear that they understand there are mixed feelings about their game and aim to improve aspects of their game that are viewed as lack-luster in future patches.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the game that I think they normally play when I hear gaming journalists say a game is too difficult.I really wanted to like this game, the trailers make it out to be really good and I'm a sucker for post-apocalyptic games but it's just subpar in just about every area. The story is your typical humans destroyed the environment and now it's the future where you must save the world, it's nothing special besides the earth was taken over by mutated intelligent animals.Pros:Scenery - You can tell they spent a lot of time working on the scenery. It looks very pretty; the color schemes are usually vivid and on point which makes running around the map kind of soothing. The interiors are well done, although reused a lot.Open world - Map is pretty big and you can just up and go explore pretty much wherever and whenever you want to. This has always been a plus in rpg games to have exploration freedom.Crafting/weapons - There's a large amount melee and ranged weapons of all sorts in the game and everything is customizable/craftable. From the hilt on a sword to add-ons for the blade, different handles on a gun to the sight and barrel, all the way to adding armor to your clothing, it's all changeable. So you totally have a lot of freedom there.Cons:The narrator - and this is a big part for the cons, so I'll break it down into a few points.1. There are only 3 voice actors so far in the entire game. 2 of them are good and evil fairies that show up when you do some quest choices (so rarely), and the rest of the entire game is voiced entirely by the narrator. He does everything from translate the npc's animal gibberish, tip pop ups, memory triggers, environmental ques, what your character is doing on screen at the moment, all the way to little quips and musings every 2 minutes. It's incredibly annoying, and makes the whole apocalyptic feeling go away which just makes the game very boring.2. The dialog - The way that dialog works with npc's is this. The animal says something in gibberish. You press A. The narrator explains what it said. You press A again (do this 4 or 5 times more). Then it gives you a chance to select 1 out of 2 or 3 responses/questions (That you never get to ask the others you didn't pick) followed by more of the gibberish, press A, narrator, press A. It seems like at least half if not more of your gameplay is going to be mashing A to get out of dialog.3. It treats you like you're a child. The way the narrator talks to you is exactly how you would talk and explain things to a small child. By dumbing down what you're saying while giving it the "This is so exciting" cheeky sound to it. Perhaps this game was made for children, and they just marketed it wrong? Mhhh. The narrator holds your hand through everything so puzzles and wondering what to do next in a quest is irrelevant. Having to look for loot and items doesn't matter since the narrator pretty much tells you something is right there. The whole thing is just a bad experience on the game, to why the devs decided to do it that way is a mystery.You can also turn the narrator off in the menu, but then you're just left with the same bad writing treating you like a child but this time you know the devs just didn't want to pay for voice actors.Cut scenes - There are so many dammed cut scenes and dialog in this game that honestly they should have just made this a movie instead of a game. in 10 hours playtime, 3 hours is exploring the actual game and 7 hours is cut scenes and dialog. It's so boring that I have to force myself to keep playing hoping that it's gonna get better, but I seriously have my doubts.Combat - The combat has a lot to be desired. There's a huge lack of enemy variety, just different colors and 3 or 4 sizes. The game relies on enemies being bullet sponges to give the "feeling" of difficulty, with combat being a somewhat rarity in this game, it really is a big letdown. Every weapon has only one attack, however you can unlock more attacks/attack styles in the form of attack combos. Pretty quick it's forcing you to try and remember 20 different button combinations to preform attacks that it just ends up being a button mashing game. (This game really really needs a lock on button)Crafting - Crafting is in the pros yes, but there's not really any challenge to crafting. All the resources you need to craft things for your weapons and armor you get from hitting these crude towers that are common in the map. Idk, it makes it easy to upgrade your stuff but there's no challenge to it.Puzzles - Why are there even puzzles in this game? Every single puzzle to unlock a door or elevator is turn these knobs to that the colors match, so far every puzzle is completed in 2 to 5 turns of a knob. Why? Just put keys in the game and place it right next to the locked door at that point.Karma system - I guess this is the rpg aspect that they were going for? Karma is on a point system, do a good thing and get a good point, do a bad thing and get a bad point. Your point totals affect the ending and some quest choices and let you unlock and use certain abilities. This normally is pretty good in rpg games, but here the main source of getting karma points is catching these little critters and either petting them for a good point or killing them for a bad point. So pretty much you can catch a bunch of them and both kill / pet them to unlock every ability to use. For the ending (based on quests so far) I'm 99% sure if you want the good, just go pet a few critters and so your good points is bigger than the bad points and boom, good to go.Character creation and leveling up - One of the big points the devs made was that there's a vast amount character creation and build making... There's really not. There are 5 or 6 races with about 6 faces with different sizes, color, and a build class. Making a build is a joke since every time you level up, you can increase a stat by 10 points, and you can use every weapon (level depending) on any build with no negatives. It's kind of a joke.Overall this game had a lot of potential but is so overwhelmingly disappointing. The dialog is uninteresting and takes up at least half of the gameplay. The narrator is so unbelievably annoying. The combat is lacking, it’s pretty much a button masher with no variety of enemies. There’s no real reward to explore places. There’s not really any build variety, within a few levels you can use anything. Having to force yourself to complete this game to try and get my $60 out of it, I just can't recommend this game. _childDocuments_.review: This game is largely carried by it's unique aesthetics and colorful themes. When you look past that, the one true word to describe this game is bland. Largely recycled areas with the exact same lootboxes placed identically from the last outpost/building you were in. Largely recycled 'turn valve lef/right' puzzles that are extremely easy, as in 99% of them a kid in kindergarten would be able to solve within 30 seconds (no, really). Largely repetitive combat playstyle early in the game, by level 15 I had unlocked all the main skills I would be using for the rest of the game. I got my best guns at level 28 and didn't change up my gear since all the way through level 50 and completion. Speaking of guns, even with a patch to decrease ranged damage over melee damage, you would never want to utilize melee weapons, solely because you can be interrupted doing your slow combos being locked in animation, and you also have no invincibility frames from dodging/parrying when you actually do get to use them, resulting in getting hit anyways. I was clapping 'boss' monsters left and right by just holding down the trigger button and strafecircling through it. There's a bug with the hitboxes aswell or bad design, so if you're dualwielding guns you CANNOT hit stationary turrets unless you unequip one of them. I was stuck on the first major bossfight for a couple tries not knowing why I couldn't shoot out it's legs, until a google confirmation showed me to unequip one of my guns, and badaBOOM the boss was dead within minutes afterwards.Another big issue I have with the game is it's 'save points' for if you actually happen to die. Early in the game I came upon a bunker in a frozen area and I saw my frost resistance percentages went up, although slowly over a couple minutes. I went to the bunker lair, killed the boss, and then my resistance bar hit 100. I took ALOT of damage very fast and died right after in a continous loop respawning in that bunker without the ability to teleport out, taking damage, dying, repeat. I had to restart the game and lost a couple hours of progress.A few saving graces are special vehicles that you get during the main mission or sidequests, but those are few and far between, are only utilized shortly  - as in limited to a small area - and then you'll be on your mechanical horse again riding between objectives. To my surprise, a special vehicle is unlocked for just ONE boss fight in this game and you're back to traversing on horseback again for 5-10 hours. Why?It is not worth the asking price, and even if it were 50% discounted I would not recommend this game to my friends over better more polished openworld games these days. I gave the game a shot hoping it would get better, but to no avail. Only get this game if it's heavily discounted, you're a fan of the artstyle AND you've already finished games like BotW or H:ZD.
