_childDocuments_.review: I'm only playing this game as a form of self punishment and because apparently I hate myself. There isn't a single positive thing to say about it as of this moment.COMBAT: It is slugish, your attacks do not connect well with the enemies, there is no impact from the hits, the enemies bug more than half of the time and every fight, be it against a regular mob or a big boss, feels the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ same, they are all boring.STORY AND CHOICES: The story and lore are as shallow as it can get. The game follows a choice system where your choices are supposed to impact the story, and the choices are literally like "That person needs help, do you want to help them or slap their mother in front of them?" or "Those kids are hungry, do you want to share your food or explode their school?". There is no nuance, the choices are stupid and the impact on the world building is minimal because killing a whole tribe weights the same as petting and feeding a bird on the games morality balance.NARRATOR: So, if you don't know, there is no real dialogue in this game in the sense that during the whole game a narrator speaks for the characters, and I swear to god, there is a point (like 30 minutes into the game) where everytime this narrator speaks I feel a primal urge to kill myself and end the pain. It is bad enough that you only hear the same voice over and over through the whole game, but the narrator also tells stupid dad jokes for every single thing you see, keeps the same dead tone for every event and does not shut up for a second. You need to pull a lever to open a door? The game take a minute to pause and make a small cutscene to focus on the lever, then on the door, and during this whole time the narrator is telling you "Go to the lever", "Go to the door" and this goes through the WHOLE game, not only during a tutorial nor anything. Every time I hear a dad joke from the narrator while an enemy bugs mid combat I lose 1 year of my lifespan and pay for a sin commited in my past life.EXPLORATION: The world has nothing interesting to reach for, the items are mostly boring and all the objectives are already marked on your map from the start in the sense that, let's say you trigger a sidequest to find 15 items around the world, when you do this the location of all 15 items will be given to you instantly. There is no real sense of exploration and most of the time you just find yourself running in an empty land from point A to point B,  which is a shame because the world itself is actually beautiful to be honest. And about the mount that you get, if you spend 5 level ups on agility you run faster than your mount, I don't know why it is even in the game.I don't recommend spending any money in this game, I'm only playing it cuz I got it from a bundle and because I want to atone for some of the mistakes I made in life to maybe guarantee a spot for myself in heaven through self punishment. If you also want to get on God's good side by paying for your sins, than I highly recommend this game, but if you have some level of self respect than there are a ton of open world games that are just better in every aspect.

_childDocuments_.review: Look, the concept, world and scenery is amazing. The game is beautiful, and theres a lot to love here, hell theres an elvis in this game that had me laughing for 15 minutes.But...The character customization was super underwhelming, the creation of breeds doesnt really do anything, as they all look extremely similar and some options like the dart frog-esque arm are locked in. Weapon customization may as well not be a thing because there is a clear meta in the gun parts that leaves you little option. Basically, DPS is the only thing that matters. Guns themselves are an absolute joke and trivialize most of what i saw in 5 hours; you become a turret that can sprint from spot to spot while enemies dumbly follow you at a snail's pace and few if enemies have anything but a basic melee attack, and any special attack comes with huge warnings and is child's play to dodge, and I saw no ranged attackers at all. Even worse was that no enemy, even boss types, had any way to counter ranged spam. In short, machine guns make this game a cake walk.World is so empty but so beautiful, and the biggest sin by far is the lack of voicing. Characters make these jibber jabber noises and the narrator translates, but he never sticks to one way or style, so sometimes its third person past tense, other times its second person present tense, etc. This MURDERS the immersion and makes dialogue very boring and since its ONE guy narrating DOZENS of hours of dialogue, you will grow to hate this poor man despite his incredible storytelling voice. Sidequests have no depth being shallow enough to win a bethesda award, and like i said the world is just so darn empty, the only NPCs i ever saw were enemies at specific, scripted locations, with no faction system so everyone is just naturally hostiel because guess what, all the world NPCs are magically the faction you didn't pick in the over TWO HOUR tutorial segment.Melee combat is okay, its serviceable but nothing special. Combos are often a waste of time apart from the dedicated boss types as generic mobs have neither the health nor the threat to bother combo'ing. Vendors rarely have anything for sale, let alone anything GOOD for sale, i mean every time i checked a vendor they had a few items and it was stuff i was finding 20 minutes ago.The tutorial HOLY ♥♥♥♥♥ this tutorial, it is literally like 2.5 entire hours, and in the last 45 minutes you get stopped every minute or two for exposition, or rather for the narrator to either translate the annoying jabbering of NPCs, or to explain something pointless over a near static image, sometimes things we would be much better off not knowing as they don't matter or just dont affect you as a character. Morality system is just garbage, the entire game is only good or evil, theres no grey areas or third options and the choices are clearly defined, i mean the options literally have a LIGHT and DARK sprite over them to tell you which to pick, and thats the only RPG element since you can only talk to quest and vendor NPCs who dont have any dialogue options other than "continue".Game has a solid foundation with great core ideas and the devs clearly put their hearts and souls into this, but theyre an inexperienced first time studio so to speak, and the game suffers greatly for it, with janky writing, an empty world, a completely boring cast of characters with no personality on account of not being voiced, and of course, the most cut and dry "good guy v bad guy" story since superman first appeared on screen. Hopefully theyll continue updating it with fixes, (Update: all theyve done in YEARS was a few bugfixes) but as it stands i give it a 5/10 (Updating to a 2/10. This game is effectively a $60 PC equivalent to an art book from a comicon artist) pretty average, sometimes below average game that only excels in being really pretty to look at at running extremely well (I used an RX 580 at the time).Hope the devs come back in the near future to absolutely slam dunk a reboot or sequel-boot, or even a new IP, but this game aint worth it. Like i said, its effectively an art book with a few jokes that you get to press a few buttons while looking at it.

_childDocuments_.review: I have strongly mixed feelings about this. It's Witcher 3 VERY LITE, if they were all cuddly animals. The creature designs are great! The open world is actually very well optimized. It plays a lot like much older titles; very simple in terms of depth, great combat(although sometimes frustrating). Many things to do, but they aren't too varied and unfortunately have no impace. If you're a k&m player, you might find combat slightly irritating(ranged special attacks launch in mutant's direction instead of crosshair). I wish the boss fights were better. The narrator is top notch but I have to agree with all the people saying that he's a little out of place, talking all the time. And you CAN turn him down all the way, which is sad, cuz he's the Attenborough of the New World.It certainly lacks polish. Looks great, but some of the animations look a little ps2-ey. The puzzles are there literally just to break the monotony. They're all the same, and they're all VERY simple. Some QTE here and there but nothing that will butcher progress.In its current state, get it on a discount at least. The devs did some good work here and I hope they update this a little bit. I fell in love in this game from watching the first trailer in 2017, and although it is occasionally a little disappointing, it hardly disappoints. A great time killer, definitely

I still cant recommend the game, the gameplays fun and all but theres just no immersion or flair, it feels like a cheap game in the mid 2000sEdit: Previous review left below for posterity, as many of said issues have been fixed.Solid 9/10 game, amazingly done devs in all gameplay aspects. Well, thats because the UI and some design decisions are straight up impossible to fathom having done so wrong.Your narrator and design decisions related to it, as well as general ui/tutorial/design decision problems, makes the game totally unbearable, especially for new players.The narrator is fine in the field, a lil irritating at points, but adds an interesting flair. However making him translate the dialogue like this slows down the dialogue significantly and any attempt to bypass the "gibberish to translate" pipeline results in skipped subtitles, accidently chosen dialogue choices, and just kills any character the npcs have. Let me just see subtitles with gibberish as an option, and more importantly make the subtitles the exact thing the characters say, not my lil automaton's interpretation of what they said.This isn't even the only thing that makes the game near unbearable to play despite amazing combat mechanics, cool world, terrain navigation, etc. The game has no faith in it's players, with a tutorial that literally is cutscenes every 20 seconds and a huge information dump of ♥♥♥♥ that you just straight up dont need to tell us, or is told in the most ham fisted, long winded way possible.This is not mentioning the outright confusing layout of the: feat choice menu, psi choice menu, mutation choice menu, inventory, gear, and character menus. Not to mention the problems with: character creation being randomized visual effects and a very poor way to select options in a character select thats really hard to use.This game striaght up needs  pretty comprehensive overall and rewrite of all of its dialogue to be from the perspective of the speaker, remove the narrator in dialogue, and fix the ui. Once all thats done, honestly the game will be great. I just doubt itll happen.

_childDocuments_.review: I tried to like it but ultimately got bored before being halfway done. The story of this game is utter nonsense and the clan I chose had no actual impact on how it turns out. The dialogue is not only gibberish from the mouth of the characters, but nonsensical gibberish for the names of locations, characters and items. To be honest, the only thing this game has going for it is the aesthetic. The audio does not feel impactful at all, and with some weapons such as hand-to-hand ones, they don't fit well. The enemy AI is stupid and easily exploitable with ranged attacks/dodging, and they also love to walk back to their spawn mid-fight, which heals them to full HP. Encounters are hilariously nonsensical, such as meeting a "mirage" that takes you to a flashback then just casually disappears or running into a giant bullying an animal you can mount and then it casually walking away once you defeat it, granting you said mount. Regarding clans, I specifically chose the Jagni whose goal was to use the worldeaters to destroy the tree of life to usher in the end of the world. At the same time, my "main" quest was to destroy these same world eaters. So, instead of doing the main quest, I completed the Jagni's quests (not all), only to find that it's a repetitive rotation of 3-4 different outpost scenarios that you must complete to capture the opposing clan's leader and conquer them. Upon taking each outpost, the SAME EXACT scene with the SAME EXACT dialogue plays, for EVERY FACTION. Once you defeat one faction, you repeat the same tasks to conquer the next faction until you conquer them all (I assume). The purpose of conquering them all is solely to get their clan weapon, as you can choose to simply end the war sooner.Regardless of my affiliation, I still had to do the story to kill the worldeaters. I ran into a worldeater by accident while exploring the ocean. They were in an non-threatening looking block of water surrounded by wooden pikes. I rode my boat into it thinking there might just be an outpost with loot and it turned out to be a main story boss with no warning. I wanted to turn back because I couldn't fight him, and there was a massive magical INVISIBLE WALL blocking me from simply leaving the wide-open entrance I came from.Overall, a terrible game with pretty graphics. The first few updates improved it a lot, but at its ore it's not very salvageable.

_childDocuments_.review: I believe that the developers worked really hard to make a game like this. And I commend them for that and for making this. Game developers work on tight schedules and sometimes to the bone. That being said, my experience with Biomutant has been strained. I want to like this game, I really do; but I feel as though I'm getting chicken wings with all the good, meaty bits already eaten.The combat in this system has the potential to be very, very fluid, but just does not have that "oomph" factor that makes it feel like I'm doing something impactful. The melee attacks are great and well choreographed on their own but connecting them just looks and feels weird. I have yet to see a random t-pose, but the fluidity between moves is erratic. The slow-motion elements are in all the right places, but where's the kick that makes it feel like countering attacks matter? I've been able to just run-and-gun and complete fights without ever having to worry about using melee, unless the enemy has a shield. Once I destroy that shield? Back to dodging and gunning.The game is actually gorgeous. Really, really stunning visuals. From the foliage the the way the lights hit, it's really good. I do get the occasional screen tear and hiccup in visuals but I suspect that's my own hardware not meeting standards all the way. Even dialing the graphics down to their minimums makes the game look a little above good, personally.The dialogue in this game and linearity of the story gives the illusion of choice. I thought I'd be able to have my own blended story that aligns with my own personal values (after all, it is a single player game), but I was left stuck between two choices and having to commit to the series of choices that follow. It's like choosing between water or soda. If you pick water, sure, you can add flavors, but in the end its just flavored water. Choosing soda means every choice later is some variation of a high-sugar drink. There's no back-and-forth here, really--at least not in the grand scheme of the plot.The UI is, dare I say, Fortnite-esque. Bright blue with comical impact-style font and bold shadows. Being guided through the UI for leveling up, the map, gear, and crafting is super clunky and does not feel at all intuitive. Visual customization is definitely top tier (imagine having a banana has a hilt with an electric blade), and I loved that. But the stats for any of these items (especially in crafting) just don't pan out so seamlessly. I can barely compare items without having to put an item on and then take it off. And mousing over them DOES show the change in stats, but sometimes it doesn't. Imagine if your current stats are X. If you mouse over item Y, it will show you what X would look like + Y. But then if you mouse over Z, it will show your stats as Y + Z. Why? If I stop mousing over Y, show me X, then when I mouse over Z, show me X + Z. I also barely know the emphasis of the different item types or rarities--I was encountering things like "Rare," "Legendary," "Abnormal," so early in the game it would confuse me. Why am I encountering high item rarities so early in the game?The dialogue in the game is a miss. Some of the dialogue choices I make don't get responded to accurately. It's like telling an NPC you're hungry, and they respond with "yes," rather than "what would you like?" Or if an NPC asks if you're hungry, and you say "no," they'll ask "okay, how many [food] do you want?" Also, the translator should just speak the entire way through what an NPC is saying rather than having to wait for the NPC to speak their gibberish.Guys, I really want to like this game, but it kills me to play it. It's a 5/10 for me. I'll edit this review when I finish the game--if I can. And I hope I can, because I want to.

_childDocuments_.review: The opening hours of this game are really difficult to get through. However, if you can get past those, you will find a unique, interesting world and some very fun exploration. Some of the games design seems firmly rooted in the last decade, such as a 'Fable' esque binary GOOD BOI or BAD BOI alignment that leaves zero room for interpretation. You are either furry Jesus or furry War Criminal.That being said, the game does have a lot of issues. Combat feels clunky / floaty. The 'math' of the game never really  makes sense, like they never tested the usability or results of some things in the game. However, the games unique aspects and build variety / charm do make up for this to some extent.Do not pay full price for this game, but I do recommend it as a unique and fun experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Not worth $60. I'd wait for it to be $30 or less. The art is good in this game and I love how big the open world is but at times it feels really empty. A lot of the free roam stuff is just copy paste. Some run down gas station with a few enemies outside and a bit of loot inside the gas station once you kill the enemies, copy and pasted multiple times throughout the map. Alot of the main story is like that as well. Go take this fort, kill enemies, get a reward after doing 3-4 of them just rinse and repeat for a lot of the main story. Combat in this game is sub par. The targeting system is whack, I feel like half the time I'm not able to attack the enemy I wanted. Melee only has like 2 combos really there's no diversity to it and the combos are shared throughout all of the different weapons. I was so happy to learn you can create different types of weapons and customize them but its really all useless because at the end of the day they are all the same with all the same combos so you just look for the one that has the best dps. Ranged weapons are ridiculously strong, I have a full auto rife that can kill elites in 3-4 magazines where as if I used melee it would take a solid 5 minutes to kill an elite, not to mention the fact that parrying doesn't work on elite units and they don't get knocked back at all so the only decent way to fight in this game really is just using ranged which gets super boring after an hour because really your just playing a third person shooter when this game was not designed to be one. The abilities are really neat in this game but like i said melee is just so useless you cant really use them to combine with melee and they dont really combine well with ranged either. If they had a better combat system this would be significantly higher of a rating for me but the combat just feels so empty and so cheesy with how op ranged is and how theres no point in using melee. 5/10 for me, would not recommend unless you got it on sale

_childDocuments_.review: Man oh man is this where I hate these thumbs up / thumbs down systems and long for the days of five stars. Nothing is binary and no-where is it more obvious than in games like this. A three-star, middle-of-the-road actiony open-world RPG with guns and wanna-be kung-fu action.It's self-irreverent, tongue-in-cheek, but holy environmentalism batman is it heavy-handed with the "humans are bad, we destroyed the world and now it's ruled by mutants what horrors have we wrought" BS. I love that the developers have been responsive and attentive. I love that they've done their best to give us a game that they felt would be enjoyable... but that doesn't make up for something that's, unfortunately, painfully generic and safe whilst at the same time not quite managing to hit that bar in a few places.Generic Ubisoft towers to gain visuals of a place? Check. "dangerous" zones that have been used before and were kinda popularized by Breath of the Wild? Check. Complete with specific armor that you have to get and wear in those areas to remain safe, disregarding any other gear you might have. Mutations can counter this, but there's little point when you can slap the armor on, duck in, do what you need to do, and leave. Combat is... unfortunately repetitive and tends toward spamming a few of the "Wung-Fu" or whatever they called it and - even then - the inputs can be finicky for pulling those off consistently. Would have been better off with them as. It simply feels like they tried to do too much with the combat and ended up making it a bit of a mess of one part action, one part fighting game combos, one part bullet time, and one part spamming the same three moves before activating you special mode and going ham on something. Overall TL;DR is that the game is perfectly average. It's perfectly playable, had petty visuals and playable combat, it's perfectly lovely, it's perfectly flawed, but I can't recommend it at asking price if you catch it on sale I'd say give it a go and enjoy the world for what it is for a while. Otherwise, you can have someone yell at you about giant gas plants creating "oxygenless" (read: "Air Made Toxic by Petroleum Fumes") environments, global warming making some places too hot to live, and improper dumping of nuclear waste leading to toxic environments on social media for free and you don't even need the $60 game wrapper for it.

_childDocuments_.review: The game has a charming art style and overall pretty map to explore, but its honestly kinda terrible.My 3 biggest gripes with this game are the following:1) The combat2) The way dialogue and story is delivered, as well as the "lore" and naming conventions for everything3) The gameplay loop of explore > loot worthless junk > repeatCombatI played on Hard from the very start and have found the entire thing to be devoid of challenge and strategy.The AI will literally just walk towards you in a straight line, taking a very long time to react, attack you, etc, you can cheese literally every encounter in the game by just strafing backwards and in a circle around the enemy.Guns (not the weapon class, just firearms in general) utterly dominate combat, melee feels extremely ineffectual, clunky and slow by comparison. Even among guns, not all weapon classes are equal. Most guns can't hit the broad side of a barn, shotgun pellets will spread at 70 degree angles out towards the sides of the screen and deal pretty abysmal damage.For 80% of my time in the game every single combat encounter consisted of me holding down left mouse button while using an automatic rifle and walking left or right until all enemies were dead.Aside from this you just press the dodge button to instantly dodge virtually any attack in the game, and sometimes you press the parry key to instantly parry an incoming melee attack. That's it, there is no more to the combat mechanics here.You get access to a variety of generic perks (stuff like +% reload speed, fire rate, damage, etc) that only help make combat even easier. If you really want to, you can invest in psi abilities and all that, all of which seem to be pretty terrible and kind of a waste of time. None of the attributes or skills felt particularly useful to me, so I dumped basically all my points into Luck and increasing my elemental resistances (which mind you are worthless until you get them to 100%).Dialogue/Story/LoreAll dialogue is, and I'm not even joking, delivered to you by a literal third person translating in rough terms what the character you are speaking to is telling you in a hyper obnoxiously vague and patronizing way.This is the narrator, some random british bloke who will speak to you for the entire duration of the game.The way he delivers all dialogue makes it impossible to take anything seriously, and extremely difficult to follow along what it is people actually want from you, or what the plot is even about.As an example, lets say you meet an npc, the npc is trying to convey to you that this one monster has been causing problems, can be found in a bomb shelter and that he'd appreciate if you could go kill it, the npc is also dismayed that you have decided to join a tribe that want's to literally destroy the world.This is how the narrator delivers this:"Smogums speaks of the Garglam. The munster has caused a big meanie-peanie and so Smogums asks you to hunt the Garglam. Smogums says the Garglam can be found in the boom-boom cave in the nono zone. Smogums is saddened to hear that you have decided to help the Jiggamans, but says its okay and doesn't matter perhaps."Initially I wanted to assume that this was him translating things for you (because I think he's the grasshopper that follows you around?), but he also translates what your own mom and dad tell you in these annoying flashback scenes, what various characters you supposedly already know and have spoken to in the past tell you, and no one else in the entire world needs any devices to speak to you.On top of the awful way of dialogue delivery, the narrator will also chime in with the most agonizingly childish quips and descriptions for random things in the world. It's funny or insightful, I'm not 4 years old, I don't appreciate walking up to a toilet and being told that the Flushy-Wushy from the-time-before was used to do the boom-booms uwu.All the items also follow the narrators naming convention too, it's like the devs gave a bunch of drugs to the local kindergarteners and wrote down all the dumb things they said for inspiration. It's so tiresome and childish man.In part thanks to the intrusive narrator and the way the devs decided to deliver exposition and dialogue to you it becomes brutally difficult to follow along the story or to even glean what characters are about or why you're even doing anything, so most of your encounters with npcs will consist of you being spoken to like you're mentally challenged and being sent on some random fetch quest without context.You have "dialogue options" which all result in the same response.What these usually do is give you dark/light morality points (which do nothing and have no effect). Waste of time.Same with choices, you are often given the illusion of choice, but nothing really matters and nothing seems to really change.The lore of the setting isn't super deep either. The tl;dr is that civilization has gone under """"eons ago"""" because one singular corporation dumped toxic waste in the ocean. The entire world seems pretty green and safe by the way, food appears to be pretty plentiful, everyone is a vegetarian (i think?) and everyone seems pretty cool and chill with things. But they will still insist that the world "is ending", whatever that means. No, they will not explain more about the locations you explore, this corporation that caused all of this, or why the world is ending, it just um, it just is, okay!You have one antagonist, some guy nicknamed "the meat eater", but its unclear if he's even relevant to anything, I met him one time, shot him, and he ran away. Your character sometimes mentions wanting to kill or forgive him, because he killed your parents I guess? But it's not really a big deal to you or anyone.Your objective also seems to be to either destroy or save "the tree of life", which is not explained, and to either stop or allow the "worldeaters" (big monsters) to destroy the tree (spoilers, you have to fight them either way because... idk, the developers were afraid you'd miss out on the epic experience of strafing left and right until you win?).Nothing makes sense, nothing is explained to you, you are treated like a stunted child and dialogue sounds almost AI generated.Gameplay loopYou go from location to location exploring, but all you find at all of these locations is assorted junk items and random clothing and weapons that you use to craft things. The system isn't very deep or complex and feels extremely tacked on and last minute.There is a rarity system, of course, because every game needs loot with different rarity levels in the CURRENT YEAR, but these seem entirely arbitrary. I found a LEGENDARY ugly hat, which has worse stats than a common hat I found a few hours earlier.Wow a LEGENDARY automatic rifle base (which is worse than an uncommon automatic rifle base I bought a long time ago).The real challenge when exploring is not getting bored and also finding gear that actually matches and looks okay.You can find a variety of merchants throughout the game (and by that I mean 3 different merchant types with randomized gear), but they don't specialize, they don't carry anything of particular interest, nothing. They are just merchants that carry random stuff. Going to a merchant in a Jagis outpost doesn't let you buy gear specific to their tribe, the inventory is just as random and boring as that of the Plingplong Wing Wang tribe down the road.A lot of random "sidequests" you get also ask you to find/do X of Y."Pluck 5 guitars (pling-plongers!)", "free 23 captives!", "Touch 9 scrotums-smotums!", "Dingelidang 4 Bibbidybabs!"There is of course a LOT to explore, but its purely quantity without quality, the first 1 hour of the game will be the same as your 20th hour of the game.There is a lot else to touch on, but why bother, plenty of other reviews have touched on the many issues this game has.

_childDocuments_.review: Let’s get the point for which this game, I think, gets the most hate, the price. If this was a 15$ game I hardly doubt it would have been this disliked. So it was 60 at launch now is 40, SILL, do not get it at this price, consider it during sales or I saw it in a humble bundle.With that out of the way I will have to mention the rest of the cons:-	The tribes, as a short description: tribes are factions you can join and you get a few specific weapons. Here is the thing, ALL OF THEM are almost the same. No quests, no unique NPCs, even the unique weapons are not wow, all you end up doing is say “I wana join you guys”, they welcome you in and off you go to conquer the lands from the other tribes and after you done you get a weapon, that’s it! This whole tribe system is so shallow, it feels like an afterthought.-	Specific mounts/vehicles. So you get a bunch of unique mounts like a scrap mech or a submarine. Thing about those is that you only get to really use them once or twice, and that’s it, you will barely use them outside specific scenarios. You go through all the trouble to get them (just a bunch of fetch quests, nothing special) and you don’t even need them much, you might use the mech for instance to explore one of the biomes since it allows you to breathe in it.-	The boat; speaking of vehicles, you got the googlide, a speed-boat, thing about it is that you can be fully in the water and you can still not be able to spawn the damn thing-	Underwhelming abilities. Compared to weapons, psi abilities are more towards support, so despite them saying it deals dmg, do not count too much on that. It is great to make all kinds of combo with them, but apart from a dash and a few elemental dmg is not something note-worthy, just stick to weapons-	Variety, enemies are affected by this, you will often see almost the same ones even if the biomes are different-	Friendly NPC, well speaking of variety, the friendly NPCs suffer too, every single on of them have the same dialogues! Even the ones which are met through the main story, despite looking unique outside quests, it’s the damn same thing…-	Quests. Basically all of them are just fetch or go talk to X, nothing special-	Class DLC, do not buy it, classes in this game are kinda the same, its one of those games which give +melee dmg, or +speed, passive stats like that, nothing special, so the DLC is just an Oblivion horse armorOh boy that’s a lot of cons, but it has pros too:-	Combat gameplay, if I could describe it, its like a DMC style, very combo based, at least for smaller enemies, heck there are moves which allows you to suplex small enemies, and if you are focusing on Kungfu you will get some cool combos; as for big enemies, just stick to high dmg hit and run tactics (hit them, and then dodge away, souls like)-	Exploration, the world is visually nice, and is filled with all kinds of things to explore and collect, coupled up with fluid movement and mounts and you will get you enjoyment just running around-	Audio, is good enoughAs neutral points I can mention the narrator, that’s a hit or miss depending on your prefs. Story, its meh, basically, humans populated the planet so now everything is ♥♥♥♥♥♥, and the only remaining hope is the tree of life which is being eaten so you gotta solve that issue and then gtf out on an ark. I liked it because you constantly find out more as you explore, because you wont get to know about it much just from the quests alone.Well, anyway, the game does not deserve all the hate just because of the price and bugs; regarding bugs, as I played this in 2023-24 and I was not impacted by them much, didn’t even encountered many, I mean there is the occasional clipping through big enemies so they are still present but it can be dealt with.

_childDocuments_.review: There are a lot of mixed reviews for this, and I'll admit there were a few things I wasn't thrilled about at first. The storytelling could be better, especially with several "flashback" segments meant to provide some backstory to your character. I also don't really like how you are reduced to either the "light" or "dark" end goal. But as I've progressed a bit through the game, it's isn't much different than a "light side" or "dark side" theme that would feel fine in a Star Wars game. There are certain psionic abilities that you will be required to have a "light" or "dark" rank to unlock. So far, it has felt pretty natural playing a neutral or balanced role. The narration thing is unique, to say the least. I kinda like the David Attenborough feel to it. Hearing the little furry creatures speaking in their own language adds to the immersion of being in a post-human, anthropomorphized furry critter world. The more I think about it, having English character voiceovers coming from CGI stuffed animals probably would have felt a little more Disney/Pixar than I'd have liked, so it was a cool creative choice in my opinion that probably allowed for more budget options in different departments and spared us the agony of sub-par voice acting.  The combat took a little getting used to. The targeting system could be better. You don't really have the ability to lock onto an enemy or control your targeting very much. You basically target whatever enemy you are aimed at. As I've gotten more used to it, there is more of a natural feel to the combat than I had at first. I can't help but compare it to the Darksiders combat (because that is what I was playing before installing Biomutant, not because of any specific similarities) and while Darksiders had really satisfying combat and targeting, I couldn't help but notice that with Darksiders the enemies will tend to hold back and let me finish certain combos rather than attack often. Biomutant doesn't do that. Your enemies will attack whether you're in the middle of trying to combo their ally or not. Maybe that is partly because I'm playing Darksiders on Nomal, I believe, and selected Hard for Biomutant, but it is something I appreciate about the Biomutant combat either way. Some people might prefer having that bit of pause from enemies so you can do cool combos, but I really like that the Biomutant enemies are actually trying to kill me and not just hanging around for target practice. There are obviously bugs and flaws to the AI, but overall the combat is both challenging and satisfying once you get used to it and unlock the special moves used to charge the Wung-Fu system. Basically certain moves, which you have to unlock for each weapon style as you level up, will charge your Wung-Fu ability if you land them correctly. Once you land 3 (you have to vary them, you can't just spam the same move) you can activate Wung-Fu mode which is basically a few seconds of being able to do several special moves like a super combo, or firing your gun at a dramatically increased rate, driving enemies into the ground by bouncing on their heads, or flying up and smashing down with AOE shockwaves.  It can be decisive in small fights, but will not finish off bigger enemies or larger battles in one go.  The mutation mechanic is a bit less involved than I expected. It basically just unlocks special combat moves like shooting a green bioattack missile or spawning a mushroom that enemies bounce on (actually way cooler than it sounds, especially if you bounce on it with them as you can do a massive melee air combo). I think there is supposed to be more to it as I think you eventually encounter bio-pools that will actually change morphology to some extent. There are definitely things I haven't progressed to yet, like the mech and other vehicles. That's probably because my play style is to do a bunch of exploring before reluctantly following any main quest lines when I have the option, which fortunately you do in this game. The crafting had a mild learning curve. It took me a little while to understand what components I was missing in order to craft a gun, but once I understood what the different component types were, it is very straight forward. You can craft weapons from scratch, or attach add-on components to buff stats. You can also use a crafting table to upgrade the quality or materials. Crafting for armor/clothing is basically the same. Overall, the customization options and aesthetic to costumes and weapons are pretty great. The world and exploration is where the game really shines. The graphics aren't anywhere near photorealistc by any standard, but the environments are truly gorgeous, and given the mild eco-warrior theme to the story, there is a really nice balance of natural beauty and the post-civilization remnants of a forgotten world. The narrator has funny names for stuff like microwaves and toilets which serve as puzzles to unlock special loot. The environmentalist message is there, of course, but it's not so heavy-handed that it feels like you're having political BS shoved down your throat. It's mostly a sort of "matter-of-fact" approach to "the old world was interesting and its inhabitants made some strange choices" explanation for the abandoned cities or the landfill or biowaste biomes (both of which will require buffing resistances with special suits to visit typically). TL;DR - I think the game has a lot more going for it than what it's gotten credit for so far. It's far from a flawless game, and like any new release has a few bugs. But they aren't Cyberpunk 2077 level bugs, and the overall experience is a great balance between world exploration, character building, crafting, engaging combat, and a "mild sauce" weak, but not that weak story. It will forever be in the shadow of much better open-world RPGs from much bigger studios, but it hands-down outshines plenty of other games from the genera that were solid, enjoyable games in themselves.

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately I can't recommend this game. It starts nicely, the combat system is fun, the world is big... Just shooting is straight up better than any melee skill, magic or bio power. There is simply no deep in it, is always the same, it's extremely repetitive. The enemies aren't even different.* The game has no idea what it want to be. It tries to be an open world sandbox and an action RPG but fails at being both. It tries to be all in once doing poorly everything. The map marks never work properly, enemies level up with you, doing whatever gear you have pointless, I've been using the same rifle since lvl 20. Doing sidequests is just meaningful if you want to go for the 100%, which can be done in less than 30 hours. The game is just empty.* It has 5 music tracks, one of them is the main menu.* I've encountered more than one bug but nothing game breaker. I couldn't jump, use items or roll from time to time. * The game has a positive and good eco friendly message but the story is a mess that you end up rushing everything. if you want a casual game to play once in a while, BIOMUTANT can be a fresh thing. If you want a fun adventure, it isn't. It's just boring and, sadly, I can't recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: BIOMUTANT is a strange one.It's hard to say whether I recommend this or not as I'm not really sure whether I do or don't like the game.Starting with the main feature of the game, it's story. There are times when it really captures my interest and others where I'm so bored of it I want to stop playing. Main missions feel samey and the characters in them feel like they're trying too hard to be different from the last character you met. Combat is another weird mixed bag, I feel like it's either really good or really bad depending on who you ask. Combat feels very weightless and weak because of how springy your character is, nothing ever feels like it hits very hard or with any real effort. Some people may like the light feeling of the combat, but it's personally not for me. Graphically the game is quite impressive and can't really fault it in any aspect of that.Customization is great and I like the character creation overall, though I feel it could maybe be slightly more detailed with not too many options outside of appearances vs character builds. Overall I feel this game is decent, but nothing special. The narrator is an interesting choice, but it can sometimes lead to dialogue being very boring as you hear the same voice over and over again making the different characters even less unique.Get the game if you can find it on sale for $20 or less, otherwise it'd probably be a waste. You may decide its your favorite game, or that it's the worst game you've played. Honestly I'm still 50/50 on it.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros- Visually interesting- Walking around and exploring feels very interesting and rewarding for the first 2-3 hours- Modular weapons with replaceable parts is coolCon's- Lot of copy and paste environments, mostly when it comes to indoor and underground areas especially- There is a severe lack of interesting abilities that are good, and especially a lack of abilities in general, I thought the mucus bubble would be cool but all it does is stick enemies to you and you pop it to make em go flying, doesnt do any damage or anything, lame.- There is a morality system but its extremely binary and all it amounts to is you gaining good or bad points so you can have enough to get the psi-power you want, spoiler, theyre all lame and not worth anyway.- Guns are overpowered and trivialize all encounters, so long as you keep upgrading the thing, or stumble upon the best one in the game, you can beat any enemy in the game with no issue at all.- Combat is just too easy in general, only thing that can kill ya are instakills- Game takes itself too seriously, but also is too goofy to the point its annoying, they come up with goofy made up names for stuff instead of just saying what it is. And theres also some story related to you about revenge and a cycle of hatred.......like a main enemy is called porky puff...cmon. - Narrator gets annoying since hes the only voice you actually hear besides the npc gibberish, and he comments on everything.- Looting actually becomes annoying after you get a good loadout since you need to watch an animation every time unless you spam the pickup all button, but it still takes up time when theres just so much to loot.- Not enough interesting enemy variety, theres small guys, big guys, and the handful of creatures that all kinda do the same thing pretty much.- All the boss fights suck, theyre janky, and are piss easy.- Charisma is completely useless, had base charisma and passed every persuasion check in the game, lets you skip fights ez pz.This game is charming in many ways, but janky, dumb, and obviously overscoped in so many others. Get it for like 10-15$ if you REALLY need something to play cause otherwise just go play a farcry game or assasins creed or something.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the main definition of a video game and I want to start by saying I personally like that aspect. There is a lot to do and a real choice system in how you tackle everything in this world. I am on the light path using the saboteur class. The Saboteur class is pretty cool, having started with two melee weapons, but honestly, you can build your character up to handle all weapons. I get the perks of it, but it seems not that important.You will also pick your resistance which comes in 4 forms of Ice, Fire, Biohazard, and Radioactivity. There is a choice to dump all your points in one vs. the other or keep its balance in between two. After that, you go into body modification where you put more into strength, agility, intelligence which morphs your body. I made my character both strength and agility. Figured the saboteur was more ninja than anything.This is where you are an animal version of Chuck Norris or pretty much any action star. You have your variety of dual-wielding guns and blades. Two-handed swords and Bos as well as rifles. It is up to you to put skills in certain attributes and unlock combos. There is a learning curve as you can’t lock on to enemies. This hinders your gameplay as you will miss a lot unless you are directly looking at an enemy.There is a perfect dodge that will slow all enemies down for attack, but the timing window is a bit small. The best part is chaining the dodges for a perfect slow-motion effect that leads to nice attacks.The enemies throughout the map come in all shapes and sizes. From giant rodents coming out of the ground that breathes fire or acid. Then other factions just want to bully you. However, do not worry since you can save at any time which makes sense for a game like this. An open-world where you can get attacked at any moment. It is a rule to save before you know a boss fight is going to happen. But keep in mind, the auto-save feature works really well.The World is Yours!There will be scraps around the world for you to gather and many chests to find. Crafting is crucial to enhancing your gear and making better weaponry. I like that I turned my one-handed weapon into a two-handed weapon. That also goes with turning a pistol into an auto rifle. This is the level of creativity I was expecting with Biomutant.You will have options of different rides to use in different terrain. Wildlife mounts all around the world that you will need a special fruit to tame. Once you do tame them you can call upon them at any time. Since you are not a great swimmer, it is wise to go with the jet ski that is fully customizable as well. For the hazardous terrain, you have a mech suit fully upgraded depending on the side quest you perform.Taking in the areas and exploring the world as a whole is a must for a full experience. You will find shops and old tech to mess with, but it still begs the question of were there people before human-like animals?The Bad:Honestly, the only issue I have is combat. Biomutant has a promising combat system but it needs a lock-on feature for it to be played well. Especially when you have to deal with multiple enemies at a time with a free camera. I mean you have guns that should at least have an auto-lock feature, but no it does not.Hopefully, we can get an update that adds this feature for Biomutant. This is the saving grace of today’s games for sure.Also, release the mercenary class that was exclusive to pre-orders. That made no sense to hide that behind a pre-order gate.Conclusion: Biomutant is a game that I have not seen for a long time taking a lot of liberties with anthropomorphic beings. Yes, there are games like Crash and Ratchet, but nothing of this scale really without boundaries and customization. There are human-like games like Skyrim, but Experiment 101 took a chance here. Their characters are not the cutest and the combat can get brutal depending on how dark you want to be. But, at the end of the day, this is a great game with full exploration.The story is all over the place, do not get me wrong, but I can get behind it. 13 hours beating it if you just want to do the story mode, but 60+ hours if you are a completionist. On my second playthrough going a full dark path I am 30 hours in and my character is on the god-tier level. But that is the beauty of it. You can make an all-around badass to make this game your toy box.Biomutant gets 4.5 beastly paws out of 5. Pick it up for yourself and give it a chance. Definitely has a lot of replay value for you to enjoy. It is available now on PC via Steam, PlayStation 4, and Xbox One with both having a next-gen upgrade. – Beast Out –

_childDocuments_.review: This isn't my typical review format, so I'll try to keep this as short as I can...I had heard very mixed things about this game and was holding out on it for quite some time. However, after having seen the 1.4 patch notes and how fast the developers have reacted to the community feedback, I figured I would give this game a try.Even though I knew this wasn't a AAA game, I was sadly still disappointed. The game feels unfinished, almost like it is in alpha. Here are a few of my issues: It's clunky, there's very little feedback which makes it feel like you're hitting air. Enemy targetting isn't reliable due to the lack of a "hard" lock-on button. The character movements are too light. (I know you're a critter, but I prefer heavier controls!)  Some animations look fleshed out, especially the more "advanced" ones, like when you perform a combo attack. But the simpler ones can be quite bad. I.e when you open a door/chest you often open "the air" instead. I feel like there are a lot of sounds "missing" and a lot of the ones that are there, aren't "meaty" enough.It might be unfair, but seeing a price tag close to  makes me expect a certain standard (even for smaller studios). The current  for how this game plays and I feel like  would've been easier to justify.Seeing as I could only get through the first  before I got too bored, I don't think there's much else I can add. Maybe the game gets better, maybe it doesn't, but the little I experienced simply wasn't good enough for me to recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: If you want to get lost in a beautiful world as an adorable creature, peeing your way across the map, this game is for you. There are slight annoyances throughout the game that some may be unable to overlook, such as annoying slowmode that lasts a little too long when clearing a pack of enemies. Also, despite being featured in earlier builds, there is no gender select. I usually like being able to play as a female in all my games for greater immersion, but as you're a small mammal, it doesn't detract from the game in my opinion. I suspect that they didn't have time/priority to animate a second peeing animation. I recommend turning the narrator down to zero, as he speaks far too often and repeats dialogue. The dialogue of NPCs is nice, but with the narrator translating everything, it feels disconnected. I do like that there seems to be zero fall damage, your character just splats comically when falling from great heights. You also cannot climb your way into other tribes fortresses. I like the story so far, but have not taken any interest in the worldeaters, only in the tribe warfare. You allegedly can change your tribe alliance, but I went to the Ankati, without being rivaled to them, and they would not allow me in the gate. This is quite frustrating, and I will continually look for a workaround because the only way you can unlock the tribe's outfits is through affiliation with them, and I also really dislike the Myriad tribe but I didn't want to destroy the Worldtree. The game seems to push you really hard along the story, not gently hand-holding but yanking your arm down the path. If I find out how to change my alliance successfully I'll update.Overall, I'm having a ton of fun with the game. I enjoy the combat, melee particularly after I've upgraded from the crappy starter weapons. Looking for loot and crafting stronger weapons are both great. The world is gorgeous and exploring is rewarding.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to start by saying this game is nothing like the Negative Youtube reviewers have stated.This game is basically similar to Fallout 4 and somewhat similar to Mini Ninjas. The world is beautiful and huge, the gameplay is hard if you play melee even on "easy" its slightly brutal as the dodge and block tells are very hard to see. Ranged combat is a lot easier in my opinion. Just a heads up if you and your children can handle mild violence then this game would be perfect to play with them together, as its exactly aimed for all ages.+Exploration is huge in this game and really fun to navigate.+Character creation is amazing+The world does have lots of enemies but you must actively search for them.+The world is full of charming little puzzles all very similar but not exactly the same.+Side quests are everywhere which helps lead you to enemies if you are lost.+The stories are varied and two characters can have very different game plays+Loot is amazing every thing has a purpose even if at first you don't know what its for.+Crafting is humorous and fun at least i liked it+Ranged is a lot easier than melee+Gear is really strange and quite funny.+After the early tutorial the world opens up immensely.-The narrator is annoying to many (not me) but he can be disabled.-Enemies can be brutal for melee classes even on easy mode-Dodge and block combat tells are really hard to see mid fight which make melee very hard to play.-No motion Blur removal can make customers sick ((me included) is it being added)For myself on an older PC the game has run very smooth and sweet and my Cpu is below recommended Core i5 3470 but still runs this fine, my Nvidia GTX 1060 6gb has had no hitches or stutter and zero crashes so far on 460.97 drivers. I even run the game on a standard Harddrive WD 1tb blue.I would have loved a fog removal option to make the game less intensive on pc's.So if you are looking for a Samurai styled cutesy version of Fallout 4 pretty much down to the wire go no further than Biomutant, and for me i've had zero issues the negative reviewers have said.One last thing i'd like to thank 101 for this game, its been a few years since i've enjoyed an open world sandbox game this much thanks. Great game all round.

_childDocuments_.review: I will have this review separated in 1. short, and 2.long version.. so here we go.1.  The game is an exploring game, with mediocre (at best) systems put in to make that experience worse.2.  To start off, its a beautiful game, in a short amount of time, it will touch your feelings, from feeling sad, to laugh and smile from ear to ear.Now... _childDocuments_.review: Another poor port from console to Mouse and keyboard.Game says you can re-map controls, but what it doesn't tell you is you WILL lose a lot of functionality when doing so.For Example: The default button to toggle you powers is middle mouse.  Since I want to play pure mage I remapped it to E (E is normally interact).  BUT using E instead of middle mouse breaks the ability menu.  you can only quick cast whatever power is your 1st power.  This means you can't access the other 3 powers using E like you can if using middle mouse.  It also means you can't charge up your "Spark Ball" and can only quick-cast it.Q & E are arguably the 2 most important keys for ability's in PC gaming.   So these dev's hard-coded those 2 keys and switching them out will break the game.  But even switching the middle mouse and the right mouse button breaks things.  Using default middle mouse will bring up a menu that visually shows your 4 power options.  Switching the ability menu to the right mouse button and it breaks it.  The visual will pop-up for a split second and then disappear.Hard-coding things to specific keys and not allowing them to be changed is frustrating for PC players and our number one complaint when it comes to ported games.

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely wouldn't recommend this game, at least at the price it's at currently. Cons:It's just as short as everyone says it is, with lots of side-quests, fetch quests, and random collectables to pad it all out. The shortness wasn't the worst part though - the writing and dialogue are what is truly awful. Everything has these dumb cutesy names, like pianos and guitars are called 'string-plongs' and 'twing-twangs' and the bad guys are named ♥♥♥♥ like 'Porky Puff' and 'Jumbo Puff' - it's hard not to cringe when literally everything in the game is named like this.The very worst part though was the narrator, and tied in with this, is that all the npc's don't have their own voices but just have some weird mumbly, Sims-like language. So the narrator does all the translating for each character, but in that ♥♥♥♥♥♥ way where they can't translate exactly what the person is saying; he just gives you an approximation of what characters are saying with his own bland commentary. This makes every conversation a bore and i couldn't help but skip almost everyone's lines. I have 31 hours in this game and I felt like I was actively avoiding finishing the game - if you just did the main quests and threw in a side quest here and there, you could probably beat this game in like 10~12 hours. 60 dollars is asking way too much for what you're getting. Pros:idk, the combat is great (although you will get knocked out of your attacks constantly, and every attack feels like they lack substance), the crafting is legit great, lots of looting which is fun,  and the world is pretty and huge. Also the music is great, although tracks will start to repeat pretty quickly since it takes forever to get literally anywhere (even with mounts, and even with the speed upgrades) (this is probably just another way that they padded out the game time) Another good thing is that this game didn't crash on me even once, and i only experienced one actual glitch that was easily solved with a save and reload - this felt pretty impressive with how poorly some games run these days. Only get this if you REALLY need another game to scratch the open-world BOTW itch, and only on deep discount

_childDocuments_.review: Thoughts on the game so far:Positives:- Creative character design- Wonderful art design- Graphics are nice- Fighting is fun (especially with melee and your added psi,etc..)- No bugs or crashes so far- Lots of ways to customize your characters build- Has a nice Chill, Charming and funny vibe ala Fable 1/2- There is a HUGE variety of enemies to encounter- Enjoying the music so far- A nice surprise is the crafting, some of the best around!- Fun to rip around the game world, movement and jumping feels goodNegatives/Things to Improve:- The quest design is pretty generic most of the time, biggest issue for me personally- Performance isn't bad but could be improved- The audio for when weapons hit should be better (this is probably my 2nd biggest issue)- Tutorial might annoy some people who just want to jump into the open world right away- The writing is a missed chance, I like the overall idea for the story but not executed well- Some elements feel half bakedHonestly surprised at all the negative reviews this game is getting. It is exactly what I was expecting tbh, a Ratchet & Clank, Fenyx Immortals, Zelda/Kingdom of Amalar style game that isn't super hardcore. You can relax and chill out and play this without worrying to much. If you went in thinking this would be Dark Souls or Divinity OS 2 level of complexity or difficulty I don't know what to say, I love those games to but this is a somewhat more casual action rpg. Right now I would give it a 7/10, won't win Game of The Year or anything but its about what I was expecting, maybe even slightly better in some ways (the crafting,etc..).Won't be for everyone but if you go in knowing what type of game you are getting (go check out some of the many youtube videos out there showing its gameplay) or don't have crazy high expectations you will find a game that is fun, charming and alot better than many of the reviews have said.I have played around 2 hours and have not had the game for 14 days, i could refund right now if I wanted to but so far I have had a good time on the game and not even thinking about getting a refund, whats here isn't perfect but there is alot of fun to be had here and alot of things done very well.Oh yeah.. and my character has joined the dark side, he is now punching injured travelers, joining evil tribes and burning down villages, the evil run experiment has started lolThis is a smaller scale open world game, it is not trying to be super serious or crazy hard, its about relaxing and doing some leveling up, customization, crafting, flying around the map and riding mounts around the map and soaking in the beautiful gameworld. If I was scoring it I would give it 7/10, it is a smaller scale game and not a AAA game and the price reflects that (AAA games here in Canada are 79.99, this game was 59.99).This is a better Feynx Immortals or the last few Ratchet and Clank games to be honest, that game had much better puzzles but I find nearly every other aspect in Biomutant to be better.**Will add more thoughts after I finish the game**

_childDocuments_.review: Game is fun, tons a missions, good visuals, interesting enough morality choices. I got it for $6 so the overpriced comments i cant speak to, its challenging (if you bump up the difficulty) and while repetitive isn't wrong i would say that any other open world RPG has the same amount, the only plus for this one is that in my 13 hrs of play i have yet to do an escort mission (fingers crossed). My biggest con is mostly a personal choice: I hate the narrator. Its the only voice you hear and i wish it reflected the situations you were in better than the constant goofy animal talk nonstop. Speaking on dialogue the Persuasion skill is useless it only changes the price value so if you put the points into luck you never have to buy anything because you will always find better loot.The game is not flush with originality, but all the mechanics work well, if you enjoyed Fable or Breath of the Wild you'll probably like it. The most unique thing about it is the setting so if you dont like the idea of being a mutant raccoon in a post apocalypse kung fu driven world don't buy it.I try to get a 1:1 dollar paid/hour played ratio to determine if a game is worth it and this game is probably going to take 30+ hours to complete main story and most side missions and even longer if there's a "new game +" mode. So with that math in mind I'd suggest it to anyone if its $30 or less, I haven't finished it and severely underpaid for it so its just a guess. It definitely does not deserve the amount of down votes its getting from people who probably pre-ordered it but if you've pre-ordered a game after 2008 you know that's a fools gamble. The sequel will probably be good and if no one pre-orders it they'll have to make it good!

_childDocuments_.review: I really really enjoy this game. It's one of only a handful of open world games I really enjoy! There is lots to do without feeling overwhelming, I love the various creatures and clans, honestly there is a lot to love about this game.The strong points for me:- World building. I know a lot of people don't like to be hit over the head with the "companies bad" thing, but I think it makes for really interesting and fun ways to ♥♥♥♥ up the world you're making. I like the various ways the company ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up the world in over the top villainous ways, I think it's fun and silly like a good b-movie!- Gameplay. It's as simple or complex as you want it to be. I like the combos and moves you unlock and how fast combat can be. It makes for very enjoyable gameplay. When outside battle you can really move fast, and exploring all the different environments is both easy to navigate through and super fun.- Graphics. Man I just love how this game looks, it's very beautiful, but then very ugly and decrepited when it needs to be. They struck a balance that I think is very fun to go through and keeps me engaged and excited for the next area.-Story. Overall I like the basic story. I do have some problems with it, which I'll explain below, but I like the basic idea of it. I've had fun so far!I do have a few issues. These aren't enough to keep me from recommending this game, but I feel people should be aware of them.- The narrater. I don't actually mind him too much, though I think this guy works better in a comedy situation then this big open world serious game. My only real gripe with this guy is that while you're exploring and doing other things off the main path HE WILL NOT SHUT UP. He's constantly reminding you that you have to do the main story. You cannot turn this off without turning off the whole narrater. I want to explore and have fun, I don't want to be constantly berated for doing that.- Light vs. Dark. This is such a tired and boring trope and I'm frankly tired of seeing it in games. The thing is that this game has a lot of potential for throwing out that concept completely and leaving it ambiguous to what is the "better" option. Both end game options can be perceived as overall good or bad, but by assigning this "Light vs. Dark" thing, it makes it obvious what the right choice is supposed to be. Also the light and dark pixies are annoying and I hate it every single time they pop up. I don't need to be hit over the head with this stupid concept when the core story of this game would be way better off without it. This also extends to the clear "evil vs. good" clans. It's annoying, get rid of this trope.- The clans. There are six in total, 3 light and 3 dark. I like this concept, it's so cool and could really show what each clan believes is the right thing to do. It simply doesn't though. Instead all 3 light clans are the exact same, and all 3 dark clans are the exact same. For example, if you go to the website talking about clans and read about the Netra it specifically says that the Netra want to defeat the world eaters but believes the clans (they're called Tribes btw, but I like the term clan so that's what I'm using) should remain independent and free. However, when you go to join them their goals end up being the same as the Myraid and the sifu's speech is the exact same, word for word. What your actually choosing between is clan weapons, which you get anyway by defeating each clan so there's no real reason to change clans.I know I went in depth about each issue here, but at the end of the day they really are small things in the overall enjoyment of this game. You can turn off the narrator. You can ignore the sprites. You can choose a clan based on which one you think looks neat or whatever. There's so much more to this game then three issues and I don't think they are nearly bad enough to take away from this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Summary / TL;DRIt's a great game, for some. If you are a so called zen-gamer this might be for you. It was NOT worth 59.99€, not by a long shot. I would recommend to pick it up at a sale if it goes down to about 20-30€I wish you could put both recommend and not recommend. It was not a bad game, it just wasn't worth full price. I don't regret playing it but I sure do regret paying full price for it. I did play it 60 hours overall, however I restarted the game after they released the new patch. So the save I did finish the game on had about 24 hours of gameplay of. I did put in about 30ish hours on my first save tho so I probably learnt alot about the game from my first save. If I hadn't played the first save maybe my save I ended up with would have been more like 40 hours I would imagine.CRAFTINGThe crafting system was a fun and great mechanic in the game. I had alot of fun going ham with a big club with a chainsaw added to the top held together with a banana as a handle. Yes. A banana, actually over ripe. It had some amazingly quirky and fun weapons, like the dial wield toilet plunger and the toilet brush, both with poison damage, retrofitted on a katana handle. At one point I also had a trumpet shotgun, with and powered by a screw driver connected to a car battery. you could go more classic with katanas, big sharp blades and normal-ish looking ranged weapons aswell if you dont like the quirky. There's upgrading and changing the weapons however you want. you can basically combine anything to everything. Same goes for the armor, the armor has it's initial health, energy and regen boost that doesnt seem to change, but you can on most armors add crap you find around the world. I had fun running around in a critter wearing an outfit looking alot like starlord from guardians of the galaxy except that I had bike saddles as shoulder armors aswell as a big kind of transistor or something as a "backpack". BIOMES and CONTAMINATED AREASThere's distinct biomes in the world of biomutant. It really feels great to explore them, they did a great job with the world they built. Probably the most stunning post apocalyptic game I've seen and played. Abanadoned and run over factories, suburbs, underground systems and more.There's also a few contaminated areas where you can enter at your own risk, with time you can up resistances so you can handle being there but it's a fun idea. It's a little to easy to get said resistances so it doesnt really impact anything. But the concept is interesting, the creatures within the contaminated areas are infused with said contamination so it feels it has impact on what you're doing there atleast. LOOTLoot, loot and more loot. It's fun, in the beginning atleast. The first half of the game I painstakingly searched through the areas to get everything. Get improved loot to being able to handle the enemies better. But after a while the equipment you have is so powerful it doesnt matter what you wear almost. halfway through my weapons was so powerful that I felt I had to downgrade to make the game interesting. The positive note on this is that you could very well chose the worse armor because it looks cool and run around looking your best! The negative note is that loot stopped having meaning, I found myself not bothering looting the areas I passed by because I just got more of the same and the power level of the loot didn't matter at all. In fact playing with the best stuff in you bags made the game so easy it lost it's touch for me. COMBATThe combat was fun, at first. The combat lost alot of it's appeal to me after a while, maybe halfway through kind of. Every weapon have it own set of "wung fu" which is basically special moves. Sounds great right? Every weapon have 2 moves each only, one "dodge attack" and one "follow up attack" from the regular normal combo from pressing the attack button twice in a row. Very simple combos, but they were there and had to be unlocked..Outside of that there's the mutations and psi powers and you could only bind 4 of them at the same time. Some of these were really convenient both in and out of combat. It was a fun addition to me, but my gameplay was focused on a melee and ranged weapon hybrid. If you do your combos in a certain way you will gain a sort of a power up that slows down time and let you do some thematically cool stuff for a short time while an energy bar of sorts depletes. It was cool the first 10 times. After that it was just a feature of the combat that I didn't use.You could do 1. some punching people, which did almost no damage compared to what I did normally.2. hammer down people like nails in the ground which was funny at times but also way too OP. It just ended combat because you just pressed 1 button 10 times in a row without actually doing much else. 3. you could fire your weapon max payne style without depleting ammo, which was kinda fun I guess. ENEMIESThe enemies look great, visually I love this game. The encounters and combat becomes VERY repetitive. everything feels kind of fresh for about 5-10 hours and then you will get a constant feeling of "Have I been here and done this already?".BIG BOSSESThere's 4 big bosses in the world that you have to face. They look great, but there is where the praise ends for me on most of them. I will give them credit for trying to make it interesting. I don't want to spoil the game and what to do but for me, the bosses was VERY underwhelming and also way to easy. atleast two of the bosses literally had 2 mechanics that also was easy to see and dodge. Dissapointed in those boss fights, the bosses themselves look epic and it's a shame I left every boss fight kinda sad that there wasnt more to it. MISCThey lifted the glider feature to the skies but it had little impact, it was nice. sure, but not anything uniqe at all at this point. For some reason you can't fast travel while on a mount, so every time you want to fast travel you have to jump off the mount to fast travel. Doesnt sound too bad but it's very annoying and also doesnt make any sense. I would assume that my character would travel on the mount to get to my destination asap anyway.DIFFICULTYI first played on hard difficulty at release since it was the hardest difficulty. It felt like playing a game on easy, it was not well tuned. However they got a patch very quickly where they added the difficulty Extreme which was way better but after a certain level you are way to powerful for the extreme difficulty to even matter. The game would need another notch of difficulty for a player like me. STORYThere is a story there, I just lost interest about 5 hours into the game. The problem isn't that the story is boring is that the delivery is not very good. None of the npc's have been voice acted, everything that is said by npc's is narrated. The narrator explains generally what was said. So most of the time characters that I wanted to like; I didn't. I didn't dislike them either. I just nothinged them. The delivery of this games story and interaction killed the soul of the npcs which made me not care at all. When you are in a conversation I felt like what I wanted to say was never represented, this is the first game I have ever felt like that. It wasn't really responses that felt satisfying to pick since the narration of what the other npc said was often very vague so the responses I could pick from was very vague aswell. The narration style of delivery was cute in the beginning but got old very very fast. You can still follow along with the story hooks of the game, the deeper story you can gather from learning about the world while exploring. You can find out alot of informations from posters and bulletin boards out in the world just to name a few.* The world is great visually* The combat becomes dull halfway through.* Crafting is great* Story was ok, Story delivery was bad.* Boss fights was not good.* Difficulty was way to easy.

_childDocuments_.review: Biomutant is a very great game that I am enjoying the heck out of, so here is what I think of it:It's a very vibrant and pretty world and all its environments.It's combat feels clunky at first but after about 2 hours you understand how it works and is much easier to combat anything.The leveling system seems adaptive meaning all foes you come across are either about 3-5 levels above you and always around 3-5 below you. With the odd health bar bosses randomly around the world possibly being higher (I remember killing at least 10 skull "leveled" enemies around lvl 5-9)I picked saboteur and am, at current level of 28, nigh unkillable and deal 90% crits of 700-1200 to nearly everything.The game allows a great amount of min/maxing right down to gear and their parts you can find and always recycle your weapons by dismantling them and replacing part to make them stronger.The game's ui is simple and easy to follow, doesn't crowd the screen(especially at 110 fov) and inventory ui is a bit rough when using the mouse but only keyboard it works fine.There are a ton of quests in this game and many that are requires for getting into certain areas that are locked/blocked off.My favorite stuff is the story related mounts and other collectible mounts you can get.Some dungeons after 8 hours of play you'll notice are going to feel fairly samey(especially the sewers and nuclear plants.) but overall it just makes them easier to pathfind to get your loot and get out.The story so far since seems interesting however I have avoided nearly all of it and have just been exploring the world, like I always do with open world games. I'll do the story probably around when im out of side quests to do or hit level cap (if this game has one).The narrator, same one who narrated in vermintide games, is a man with such a great voice and even with most random world dialogues being silly is still great to hear and the narration of the npcs of the game since they all speak gibberish is good. It's like being read a story to you by someone when you're a kid.The overall game is great and i've experience no game breaking bugs or anything that is broken and cant be completed yet.

_childDocuments_.review: I had this game on my wishlist for over 2 years, and I was getting a little worried about the mixed reviews, but honestly Biomutant is not a bad game. Yes, it is far more childish than I was expecting, and 'medium' difficulty is like any other game's 'very easy', but it is a fun experience nonetheless.The crafting mechanic is great, and this is coming from someone who usually ignores that kind of thing in most other games. Exploration is a major part aspect of the game, and piecing together the history and lore of the world can be so intriguing. The variation in combat styles is a shallow ocean rather than a deep puddle, so you can very quickly max out the rather samey abilities for your playstyle, but this does allow you to mix things up without having to worry about completely respecing.Some noticeable downsides though:- The combat can get pretty repetitive, even if you mix up your weapons- The narrator has been known to get on peoples' nerves when he chirps up unprovoked- The permanence/impermanence of your choices is not made clear, and it is difficult to tell whether or not a choice is permanent or can be changed at a later date- What was looking to be a more gritty post-apocalyptic game about mutations has turned out to be a casual 'Ratchet and Clank' style game- The puzzles are the easiest I've ever seen in a video game, and even if you fail one by mistake they can be immediately repeatedBasically, if you were thinking this game was going to be a souls-like, you'll be disappointed. It is, however, a great casual game for chilling out, and particularly a good game for young teens. So if you want a nice open-world game that isn't too big and you can relax while playing, Biomutant might just be for you.
