_childDocuments_.review: Ignore all the negativity,  this game is a wonderful time, and I haven't even conquered the first tribe yet!I won't lie and tell you it's the best OWRPG I've ever played, but it's a hell of a lot better than people give it credit for, if for no other reason than the world alone, it is absolutely GORGEOUS, almost without equal in the genre.In the most TL;DR way possibleCombat is fun but quirky, melee doesn't feel amazing but is perfectly serviceable once you get used to it, ranged combat is a little bit too easy, it's much lower DPS when compared to melee but a lot of fights can be won by going full acrobat in a circle around the areas boss (I am playing on the Hard difficulty) and the mutations (The games magic) are tons of fun, the bosses don't really care about your mutations but it's a visual treat seeing the minor ads being melted, yeeted' or simply atomised.The story so far, forget about it, I haven't even bothered with it yet, like a true gamer I walked off in the other direction and haven't had the time to come back yet, I've shot,stabbed or melted many fluffy beasts, some huge, some small, and one that looks like an elephant took an anteater behind the bike shed without it's consent, and 15% of the time they're hiding some incredible cave, with epic loot or an epic traversal (Some of the unique weapons kept behind mini bosses are game changing), Open the game, pick a side and GO EXPLORE, you'll have a much better time this way The graphics as mentioned are best in class, I am running all MAX 1440P on a 3060Ti and haven't seen sub 60 yet and I am so glad for it, every animation, every cave, every building is utterly beautiful and I just can't think of an equal when all things are considered together.This is trailing on to a point where you'd be wasting time reading any further, GO GET IT, it's just been on Humble so even if you didn't get it from your own bundle, someone else will be selling it for £5. You can't do much better for the price.

_childDocuments_.review: My previous review of the game was a positive one. However, I've changed my mind after thinking thoroughly.You are a furry little blighter who is being chased by a giant bastard. You go through an underground facility leading you into the world where 6 factions (3 good and 3 dark) are fighting for dominance. The game revolves entirely around you. Factions do not fight each other at all outside of the scripted events in the game. You are tasked to kill the 4 bosses who are on the vines too and also go to the tree of life to escape the planet (if you are a dark side character).The world is massive, but small at the same time. Each area of the map contains small sub quests involving collect X, Y and Z. The Biohazard zones are the only way to improve your characters mutation abilities and resistances (You can only level 4 of the 5 types of resistances). Mutations give a sense of fun into the game allowing you to mess around with specialisations. But Resistances are the most important if you are a completionist if you are too lazy to change gear.Leveling up doesn't really help you with any progression at all other than allowing you to wear stronger armour and weapons. if you play as a Ranged character you are most likely to go down the luck route increasing crits in general. Since your guns doesn't scale off any other stats. The Narrator is annoying in general (you can turn it off thankfully) the game tells you it when you reach the tree in the middle... When i am close to completing the game.In the end. This is a Furry Fighter with a Fortnite Asthetic. I do like some of the set pieces in the game though like the giant broken dam that looks impressive from a distance.

_childDocuments_.review: Neutral would be a better option but since everyone who wants to give neutral actually gives a thumbs down I choose a thumbs up.Pros:+ beautiful world+ entertaining combat so far (nothing special but arcade-style on a similar level like Batman Arkham Asylum)+ fun to traverese the world+ humorous at timesCons:- empty open world (aside from "combat arenas" you rarely stumble upon enemies or npcs)- in a game with rodent characters i would expect them to be able to climb some walls at least (climbing is possible at certain points in the world though)- The game tries to hard to transfer a Yin-Yang message. Every second or third sentence is some stuff you could find in a fortune cookie.- to much handholding. 4 hours in and there are still tutorials popping up and the narrator interferring with simple actions like activating a switch (i will give turning him off a try though)Story:+- not really a pro or a con since it is really up to the individual player: Humankind was bad and the world suffered. Overall I will continue playing but it feels like this world could have achieved more. I am not attatching to any of the characters so far because everyone gives me the Zen / Yin-Yang vibe. Which is fine, if it  wasn't so "in your face!". No character in particular stands out. They all blend together to an overall message.If you are looking for this kind of refreshing message and some not so difficult combat then this game might be for you, otherwise be aware.

_childDocuments_.review: Biomutant had a bit of rocky start with some bug crashes and other issues but currently its running very well for me on PC. I played on ps4 also with less success. It doesn't really invent any new mechanics but it combines elements of other games to mostly good effect. And it looks really cool. I'd say if you like open world action adventure and the theme of mutant kung fu animals appeals to you give it a shot. It's semi-open world really as you must methodically unlock access to most of the map. But it feels pretty open mid to late game with wide open areas to explore and a good variety of terrain. The strongest points I think are:  1. Combat. Not terribly inventive but it integrates enough different elements in a fairly intuitive interface to be really fun. You have guns, melee, wung fu powers, psi powers and mutant abilities from which you can tailor endless combinations and strategies. It rewards experimentation. 2. Crafting. The loot system is above average. Lots of open world games suffer from an overabundance of loot that eliminates the excitement. Or from an encumbrance system that makes collecting difficult. Here there is a good balance. Especially the spare parts. You can use the gear you find, buy, win in quests or that you craft yourself. It's not super critical to follow a curve and the quest lines supply you with what you absolutely need so, if you are like me, you can just have fun with it and dress your character in zany ways. 3. The world. The map,  enemies and NPCs are both clever, beautiful and consistently silly. Of course there are a few weak points also: 1. The game contains puzzles. They aren't good. Mostly they are easy but compared with other open world contenders out now BioMutant has some of the weakest puzzle challenges around. 2. The narrator. I can't figure out how to turn this off. It's incredibly repetitive and ceases to helpful after the first fifteen minutes or so.

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10So I'm writing this review after playing with all the new updates and fixes after week 1.  The game is perfect for you if you:- love beautiful visuals (can play around in photo mode),- love to explore new places while searching for loot everywhere,- enjoy customizing/crafting your gear and character themself,- enjoy continuing to new game plus,- simply like RPGs and want a decent pass time. May want to avoid if you:- Dislike weak storylines,- Dislike repetitive gameplay (tribe missions and many sidequests),- Dislike level caps (lvl 50),- Dislike having very few class specific skills.It's a pretty good game when it comes down to it, but its not life changing or anything. The early game and midgame experience is rather rewarding when first encountering new mobs and trying out new guns, melee weapons and skills, but lacks heavily in creativity when we constantly see the same pattern over and over in terms of lootable locations and mob types. The late game is very weak, especially if you like grinding like I do. I reached the level cap reasonably early and found the best gear I could and now finishing the game became more of a chore rather than actual enjoyment. Take your time, don't rush through it, its a nice experience as a whole.  I will say though, launching mobs into the abyss with telekinesis, can be hilarious, just saying.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly at $60 there's no way I could possibly recommend this game.Lets talk about the good first. 1: I love the setting, there's a lot of color, I think game developers are realizing that gamers are fatigued on games that offer nothing but  browns and greys.2:The game is very adorable and filled with cute fuzzy friends     Thats about it for me unfortunatelyNext well talk about what's just ok.Combat: While it's serviceable, it's not particularly satisfying. Enemies size and level's do not really seem to correlate to their combat ability, and neither does yours for that matter, I fought enemies who smaller than me and were 4-5 level below me that were absolute tanks and I've fought giant enemies that we're 6 levels higher than me that died in a few seconds, there really doesn't seem to be any real rhyme or reason, it mainly just seems like the level system is in place because that's how most open world games are. Also there's none of those satisfying moment's that make you feel like a total chad, you're not going to pull off an epic finisher and obliterate  anything, they'll all kind just fall down and that's the end of it, it's all very MEH. Gun play is also pretty lame, it works, but it's really just there to make ranged attacks so you don't have to risk taking damage, there's no real aiming or skill involved, just click the mouse in the general direction while the game decides if the bullet hits or not.Crafting: Poorly explained, extremely basic, and probably mostly unnecessary. I found this (Similar to what I said about enemy levels) to seem arbitrary. I would craft a new gun that was statistically way better than what I had been using and it seemed to make very little difference at all. Honestly it seems that the game scales so well thaat pretty much nothing seems to actually make a difference game play wise, just mentally which seems to be a problem with scaling in general, let gamers fail by trying to take on an encounter that they obviously aren't prepared for, just like letting gamers absolutely destroy that weak ass enemy who should have minded their own business, we want to overcome adversity, but also feel like a total Chad at the same time, do developers not know how boring scaling can be?Preaching: Yes climate change and pollution. We get it, and you're probably not going to change the minds of people who don't agree by smearing it in your game 50 times.Good vs Evil: Too in your face, you have a literal angel and devil that tell you if you're decision was good or bad, which is so painfully obvious that even a rat could have made the choices for me and I don't even thing it really matters so long as you unite the tribes and spare your childhood bully, Just seems like it was in there to make the game seem more dynamic than it really is.Let's talk about the bad.1: The missions are extremely repetitive, especially the main "world eater" missions which consist of; you need to use this vehicle, but it's missing parts! Spend the next 30-60 minutes gathering them and then fight an oversized monster that isn't much more difficult than anything else you've already been fighting. It's boring and disappointing, I didn't really find any mission in this game that felt genuine or original in any way.2: The dialog is so damn repetitive you will start hearing the narrator repeat the same lines in the first 1-2 hours and with every character you talk to. While I am sure they saved a ton of money by not having to hire 50 voice actors, and by having so few overall lines, it gets extremely boring and annoying quickly, characters in this game have precious few things to say, so it's sad that most of it is reused content. I honestly would have rather it had been Nintendo style where it's obviously gibberish and I just read subtitles, not that I want all of the narration removed, the narrator delivers his lines well, especially during cut scenes, but it's just rather obnoxious overall.Overall, this is probably a below average game for me. The extreme lack of variety, the unsatisfying gameplay, the unsatisfying crafting system, the boring level scaling, the repetitive boss sequences, the constant repetitive narrating, the preachyness, the lack of an actual feeling of urgency or importance. It's just not really that fun.Don't spend $60 on this please because honestly if this was like a $15-20 game, my opinion would be much higher and I'd tell you to buy it now, but it honestly lacks the care, attention and polish that is expected when you are paying $60 for a game .*I'll update my review when it's not 4am and I can check it for errors.* Hope this helps you,

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; Do not spend time or money on this game.I should not have spent this much time on it but I really wanted to see if I missed anything or if it would get better. It did not. The dialogue options are oftentimes gibberish. The melee combat is a janky hitbox mess with a very boring moveset. A good ranged weapon will beat everything. The loot is a very dry affair, the same goes for the quest rewards too. Most quests start at one end of the map and the next step is the other end of the map. Many times I bump into a quest character or item and I have to find where to trigger it. Traversal is time consuming, with your mounts marginally faster than your run. Quest related mounts are only used in that part of the quest which is mind-boggling. The only good thing about this game is the view. But when you venture into the dungeons, it is repetitive. The enemies are repetitive. A particular leveling material is so abundant, I have no use for them towards the end. I played this game on the hardest difficulty.Best part? I couldn't even skip the credits. You can only fast-forward it. What is wrong with the devs? Why? The players have already been tormented enough with all the time-wasting elements in the game. Even the credits.

_childDocuments_.review: Steam really does need a neutral option. The game is like a Reece's Spaghetti BBQ Cajun Fried Chicken and Egg Salad Sandwich. If you take it apart, all the individual pieces are good. Shooting feels good. The world is really cool. The narrator is funny, and well delivered. The ability co customize your particular little mutant is really great. And so on for all of the game's parts. But putting them all together in the way that they did made all of the parts lesser because of how they play off of each other. For example: The narrator is great. He is the same voice actor as the narrator from The Stanley Parable. They have him narrating/translating for every character and all of your own "thoughts" as well. But they gave him the same fourth wall breaking humorous style he had in the Stanley Parable. He is once again, an outside observer that not only narrates but has his own comments about events. But the game is post apocalyptic kung-fu movie about family, sacrifice, and maybe redemption (depending on your choices) and the narrator doesn't fit the vibe. And pretty much every system is like that. "The combat is fun, but...", "the customization can be deep, but...", "the world is fascinating, but..."We often find ourselves in positions when asked about games if we like it or not. But there is more nuance there. Media, and games especially, can be mediocre without being outright ♥♥♥♥. And I would say that this game is a solid 6 or 7 out of 10. Not ♥♥♥♥. But definitely not a masterpiece.

_childDocuments_.review: It has all the potential to be incredibly enjoyable and interesting and funny and proceeds to capitalize on absolutely none of it. I had zero expectations going in, but I'm blown away at just how much wasted EVERYTHING there is. Honestly it feels like a child's platformer designed by Nintendo. It isn't hard, it isn't interesting, it isn't clever, it isn't innovative. It's just the same thing you've seen a million times and all you really do is press a few buttons absent-mindedly. The environment seems dead and muted despite the colors and space. There is no wind, environmental effects, or interaction between enemies and the environment. The level design seems to consist of "walk through these 5 doors for no reason and, no, there isn't anything in any of the rooms either." Every mob is the same brain-dead AI shooting nerf darts. Despite the combat designer's intent to provide an engaging and fun game, all they've really done is create a standard auto-locking m1 and m2 spam fest similar to the Mordor or Arkham Asylum systems.

_childDocuments_.review: The issue with this game is that it's shallow. While some aspects are oddly not. Things like crafting are flushed out like crazy with a ton of options and personality for both weapons and armour (mostly the weapons though). The combat where you use the weapons is tedious and boring and after the first few times you really just want to avoid it because it's not that fun. every melee weapon basically functions the exact same way. Doesn't matter sword, hammer, axe, you do the combo and essentially the same move for all weapons comes out. Which does have its merits but also loses depth which it didn't have in the first place. There's no deciding what the best play style for you. Some of the perks exacerbate the issue with combat as well, taking all the challenge out of fighting. I played on normal difficulty at the start. Mostly because I didn't really want a challenge for a game that I really just wanted to look at. But when I was around level 5 or so, I found a weapon that had a perk called "Remedy" on it. This perk boiled down to 200% life steal, with no drawback. And with my crit based stat focus, I had zero issues staying at full health (not that I think a non-crit focused set up would fair worse). Even against mini/bosses. So combat for me stopped being about picking my timings and more about how can I do the most damage in the shortest amount of time. Not that I was worried about a timer or something of the like that I had to beat. It's just so boring to stay in combat for long. Then the obvious thing is that you'd think that the weapon would eventually fall off as I leveled and something that did more damage would come along and I had to choose whether I could still justify doing less damage but staying perfectly full health. Except no, weapons seemed to level with you, so once you found something it would just stay with you indefinitely. Even if it didn't there's a flat upgrade system were you could just upgrade the weapon overall, just by using the 5 basic materials that you naturally accumulate over time. So there was basically a 0% chance of me ever being able to realistically replace this weapon, unless A: I found something even stronger, or, B: I actively wanted to cripple my strength. So then the crafting. Weapon crafting is great. Armour crafting seemed basically pointless. Armour crafting/modding first. You can't (from my time playing) create armour from scratch. Meaning that you find, you wear it, you mod it if you need/want to. The issue being that the mods for armour are just more armour. There could have been mods that effect resistances and things of that nature but I didn't find any. Weapon crafting/modding was way better and basically made armour modding feel like someone said "Well if we can mod the weapons, we should have the armour mod-able too." Then prompty forgot until days before release. So again you can't create any piece of a weapon manually. But you do accrue a bunch of pieces for weapons at a fantastic clip so there's no shortage. You can combine any and all pieces at will, allowing you to create a weapon that feels like your own. Which you might as well do cause, kinda no matter what it doesn't really matter. Unless you stopped completely looking at the crafting/modding menu and just went on your way without thinking about it again. Until you're not dealing any damage or at least subpar damage and wonder what's going on. Go into the crafting menu, see you have a thousand new handles and choose the one that raises your damage the most. Next would be visuals. Probably the best thing about the game. It's cartoony and bright and vibrantly colored. The kinda overall issue is that it very much reminds you of Fortnite. To me at least it just looked like a zhuzhed up asset pack from Fortnite. Now not to put it down there's a lot more to it then it looks like fortnite 2. But if you're wanting to buy and somehow haven't actually looked at the game, do your own research first and come to the conclusion you want. Audio: it's good overall. Nothing didn't sound out of place, or wrong. Swords swooshed, hammers smashed, footstepps footed, jumping jumped. You get picture. The only standout sound effect was the crafting sound effect. Which must just be a UE4 stock sound cause it's the same one from Fortnite STW. Then there's the narrator, and no VA. This will split people and comes down to preference. No one talks it's only the narrator telling you what people are saying. The issue for me was that it slowed down conversations so much that I started to skip over any talking, story related or not. Because the narrator doesn't talk over the person you're talking with. So conversations go like this. You interact with someone. They chitter and squeak. Then the narrator says, "Their saying this." When it should go. You interact. They chatter and squeak in the back ground. And the narrator talks over them at the same time. Which helps speed things up, and makes so that you also feel, more or less, more attentive to what they're saying because it feels like their actually talking to them.TL;DR: play FFXV instead.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is kinda like the Mad Max game in a way, a jack of all trades but a master of none. Unfortunately for Biomutant, Mad Max did it better with handling all its elements, Biomutant just feels a bit more mediocre than Mad Max. So why do I recommend this game? It is still a good game in spite of its many flaws, the world is colorful and huge, the combat is fluid and fun, a bit too fluid at times that it feels floaty, but still fun. If a fast paced, post apocalyptic, mutant creature game with wu shu like martial arts combat in it sounds good to you then get it. Oh, and some stats look like they only affect only one or two areas, like agility for instance, but they actually affect other things too, sort of hidden stats, like agility also affecting gun damage. They do not make that clear in the game, which they kinda should have. Anyway, the game is great at what it does do. Fast paced action combat in a huge colorful open world.

_childDocuments_.review: Sub areas have little to add to the game but a random encounter with some boxes to open only to scrap or sell.You build the character the way you want only to fight bosses on a mount with a ranged weapon only and some press a button action over and over until it dies with little to no reward and a terrible short cutscene.You basically almost cant play psi powers if you tank any of the other path unless heavily investing in a stat which wouldnt be of much use to your actual main 'class' way.Again you fight bosses with your ranged weapon on a mount, so why did you bother building melee or psi ? Melee is highly clunky, I kept going till the end anyway, the lock target update made it better but still not enough.You can do a super move, with 4 different actions, but where only one matters really (gun based one) no matter what you decided to build your character and it doesn't feature your psi powers at all.No super move against bosses, again you are just a turret steering a mount.You are given a lot of different cool features, but unfortunately those are restricted to their respective areas in the map so theres less of a sense of unlocking cool stuff for you to have fun with. This was so frustrating.Its like 'heres a magic bike, it will appear upon your calling wherever you are, however, you must be in your backyard'. Overall theres little i can recommend from the game, but if you fancy furry characters, some ok combats with mostly free exploration and a 24/7 monotome narrator, give it a try.

_childDocuments_.review:
Biomutant is an open-word, post-apocalyptic Kung-Fu fable RPG, with a unique martial arts styled combat system allowing you to mix melee, shooting and mutant ability action. Your actions play a major part in the unfolding of a story where End is coming to the New World. A plague is ruining the land and the Tree-of-Life is bleeding death from its roots. The Tribes stand divided, in need of someone strong enough to unite them or bring them all down...
Although you are guided through the world by a Storyteller that narrates every step of your journey, it's your actions and choices that'll decide how your story of survival ends.

name: HUNTDOWN
detailed_description: In the mayhem-filled streets of the future where criminal gangs rule and cops fear to tread, only the bounty hunters can free the city from the corrupt fist of felony. Lay waste to the criminal underworld and make a killing in this hard boiled action comedy arcade shooter. KICK-ASS CO-OP, FROM NEAR AND FAR Hunt solo or give suppressive fire and advance on the enemy together as you run, jump, and take cover in the mayhem-filled streets of the future. Whether your buddy is in the same room or on the other side of the planet, wreak havoc as a team through couch co-op or Steam Remote Play. NEW ACTION-PACKED ARCADE MODE It’s you versus the world as you’re pitted against players from all corners of the globe in a brutal battle to pummel your way up the leaderboards. Innovate and invent new ways to pulverize your foes to rack up your score, whether you make use of combo-kills, quickdraw weapon-swap bonuses, or just hurl criminals off the rooftops. In this nail-biting race against the clock, collect as many bounties as you can while you watch the numbers roll and strive to be the apex bounty hunter. PLAY AS THREE LEGENDARY BOUNTY HUNTERS Anna Conda: Ex-commando, firearms expert, and full-time loose-cannon, Anna will assassinate without question or mercy, as long as you don’t mind the collateral damage. John Sawyer: Once a Special Forces cop who left the law behind. This scarred veteran has lost so many limbs in combat he’s practically half robot. Mow Man: Modified recon droid, stolen and empowered with banned software. Trades bodies for cold hard cash. Don’t expect to be taken alive if Mow Man’s on your six. OLD SCHOOL MODERNIZED Hand painted 16-bit pixel art graphics and hand-drawn animations combined with fluid 60-FPS gameplay and an epic synthesized soundtrack. 20 LEVELS Gritty, neon soaked, graffiti strewn 80s cityscapes to clear, each with their own infamous gang boss to terminate and bounty to collect. FOUR UNIQUE GANGS TO DISMANTLE Hoodlum Dolls: Violent feral punks winning the gang war with the toothless authorities Misconducts: Organised hockey hooligans, experts in robbery and extortion with a penchant for explosives The Heatseekers: Murderous motorcycle club. These rockabilly villains style themselves on the centurions of Ancient Rome NO.1 Suspects: Masters of discipline and organised crime. Martial arts experts, these slick psychopaths control the night through their casinos and nightclubs CHOOSE YOUR WEAPON Confiscate machine guns, laser weapons, katanas, grenades and more, and turn them on their owners. Stab, shoot and explode your way through swathes of gangs and bosses and collect your bounty.

_childDocuments_.review: Occasionally, I launch through RetroArch some old Sega Genesis / Mega Drive titles such as . While I enjoy the sprite work and feel, I only have fun for a couple of minutes until the approximate game design and dated level structure bring me back from the 90s. But now that I have , I can fully enjoy that 16bits era of time within a game that is undeniably excellent, benefiting from more-rounded modern design sensibilities... as well as from the crazy talent of the developers at Easy Trigger Games.You (and a friend in COOP) choose a mercenary upon the three available and get offered a campaign in the form of 4 consecutive areas each populated with a unique colorful gang. The backstory is minimalist, and there won’t be more than a few occasional lines of text or short cutscenes to introduce new threats. The end of a level is always crowned by a boss fight against a “bounty”, often a gang leader that marked the level with their footprints.While the story is appropriately barebones (and consequently will not go in the way of replayability), the world, rendered in gorgeous pixel art, is incredible. This is a perfect melting-pot of , , , , , , , and everything that is holy from that glorious era of science-fiction movies depicting an ultra-violent future. The references are everywhere, in the gangs and their style, in the cool one-liners from the main characters or their bounties, in the music, and of course in the dirty neon-infused levels, as the fights will be taken from the subway to the rooftops. Even the fonts are totally on point!Gameplay-wise, instead of trying to emulate the rough edges of old games,  removes multi-directional aiming to focus on horizontal aiming, but masters it. It is possible to dash or to take cover behind crates or within alcoves, allowing players to smoothly choose between frenetic jumping around in order to dodge, or smooth shoutouts from fixed positions behind covers. While these systems are often clunky in many games, in  the controls are very intuitive and there is little friction between what players want to achieve/what they picture in their mind, and what they can actually perform immediately in the middle of a gunfight.Each character has its own gun and an alt attack recharging quickly, so even after picking up a melee weapon there are options to deal with enemies farther ahead. Scattered across the levels are all kinds of weapons, from close-range shotguns that blow people to bits to destructive rocket launchers that blow people to bits; there are often several possibilities so players can pick according to their style or to their knowledge of the levels. I must admit that it is refreshing to play in hand-crafted levels rather than yet another repetitive rogue-lite game or a broken Metroidvania. Combined with tight level design and a huge variety of enemies and boss fights (each new boss encounter is pure bliss), we arrive at the best run and gun game that I have ever experienced since . Don’t get me wrong, this is not a replacement for  and its huge boss fights with spectacular levels at breakneck speed.  is another proposition, less free-form chaos and more toward grounded but tight encounters.Difficulty is a common hot topic concerning action platformers. ’s difficulty seems as well crafted as the rest of this superb game, with a campaign that starts relatively easy but gradually ramps up the challenge (I just hate the jetpack enemies that explode at my feet). Each level provides a fair amount of checkpoints, so you never have to go back too far when you die, although it’s still better if you can anticipate the threats ahead (damn those bikes). There are also secrets (3 briefcases to collect per level), and the extra challenge of completing a level without dying, to earn a medal. If you don’t want to occasionally have a hard time you can start the game on Easy, but if you are looking for a spicier challenge, there are more brutal difficulty modes with fewer health points, giving you little room for error and demanding that you both anticipate the threats and play more technically with the game mechanics. Finally, there is an Arcade mode, in which you get a finite number of lives (you can find a few extra lives in the levels and checkpoints still help) and you are tasked to complete one of the four areas. The levels have been slightly remixed from the campaign, your time is displayed, and skulls and other items are contributing to your score (with a satisfying “ting ting ting!”) as you compete in the leaderboards. If you just rush through the story on Easy, there will be at least 5 hours of play. But if you want to get all medals and play on normal, we arrive in the ballpark of 10-12 hours, and then quickly more as you get into the higher difficulty modes and the Arcade. Since the story elements and cutscenes are kept in check, the game is highly replayable, and you might want to invite a friend to share in on the fun.Once a player is down, there are 20 seconds to revive them by mashing the defibrillator over their fallen body. Otherwise, they simply have to wait until the next checkpoint. Coop is not available online (except through Steam Remote Play), only local. The keys are fully rebindable, and it is even possible to have two players on one keyboard. I just can’t find fault with this game.Oh, yes. The elephant in the room. First, this is an external issue and has nothing to do with judging the game on its own merits. Second, while it seems greedy for successful publishers with a hit on their hands to also take Epic’s money, smaller games and publishers always risk releasing their game in complete indifference on Steam’s overcrowded market, so Epic’s money is a safety net and a welcome financial security. At least, now the game is finally on Steam, and it deserves to become successful. Don’t pass on it, as even Electronic Art’s horrors find a strong audience on Steam despite forcing to install Origin: it would be unfair that the small devs get punished while the nasty companies thrive.

_childDocuments_.review: I own quite a bit of games on STEAM... but as I've gotten older I play here or there with my games for like 25 minutes, maybe 45 minutes, then move onto something else.  Gaming is more of a pleasant distraction these days at age 43.  I JUST SPENT 2 HOURS PLAYING ***HUNTDOWN***.  That like never happens anymore.  This game is simply amazing.  It's the Cyberpunk Action Game we all wanted 29 and 26 years ago but never got.  Think Elevator Action Returns (Part 2) meets Blood Dragon meets AD Police & Bubblegum Crisis Animes with a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥' soundtrack. Everything about this game from the 2D Pixel graphics to the music to the art is just amazing.  It's like someone hacked my brain and found my 14 year old self obsessed with William Gibson Sprawl novels of Cyberpunk meshed with Bladerunner.Don't hesitate to buy this game if you're a 2D freakazoid like me.  I could never really get into 3D (I play the games but never cared for it).  This is Phenomenal.

_childDocuments_.review: At first, I had my doubts. I kept getting killed constantly and I was scratching my head why as I've grown up on Contra, Metal Slug, etc so I should have this in the bag.But then I remembered when I played Broforce and did the same thing there- Stop trying to rush through and take a second to see what weapons are available, what's laid out ahead of me and move slower instead of trying to blast my way through. It has a lot of the older games DNA here for sure, but it's a approach is a bit more methodical. The pixel art is awesome and so is the soundtrack. They even have voice actors and they're actually REALLY good!!! Enemy placement and level design is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ top tier. Boss battles have their moves telegraphed like in the nes Mega Man games which is great so you can learn and adapt to their patterns. Everything felt very tight and fair on normal difficulty. And you can turn off screen shake thank God!!! The attention to detail is incredible all around.And one of the best parts is all the fan service to games of the era. And it's not the overdone stuff to death like, "It's dangerous to go alone" lines. I've picked up nods from Duke Nukem, Shao Khan from MKII and 3, and even movies too. It felt fresh to hear this stuff instead of the same old same old, and they were implemented well and not just shoehorned in. My ONLY gripe is the achievements. The ones here are...ok, but I wish it had more progression based ones after clearing levels, killing bosses, number of enemies, complete the game with x, y, z character etc. But not gonna complain about it too much since everything else is just damn near perfect. Hopefully the sequels implement this. They nailed it with this game 100% though. Please make lots of sequels, I will buy. My wallet is ready. My body is ready. Giant enemy crab. Riiiiiiiiidge Racer!!!!!

_childDocuments_.review: In the future, there will hopefully be no end to the flood of pixel art games reminiscent of the console era of the early 90s! But when a game comes along that is as rich in atmosphere and detail as Huntdown, then I can only be happy: The 2D action is rendered in a top-notch 16-bit pixel look. It perfectly matches the arcade-like gameplay and scenario.Huntdown sees itself as a declaration of love to the countless riot movies of the 80's. So you can expect a lot of explosions, noise and pixel blood, empty jokes, evil villains and a stylish synthesizer soundtrack that successfully accompanies the ballerfest. The story offers a loose framework at best, if you want to call it that. You play as one of three bounty hunters who earn their living in a dirty, futuristic metropolis. This means that you have to take on several brutal street gangs in a total of 20 levels, and at the end you always have a crunchy boss opponent to kill. Don't be fooled by the occasional short cutscenes with English voice-overs in between: The story clearly only plays a minor role.There is no online mode like in Streets of Rage 4, but you can play alone or with two friends in local co-op. My brother and I used remote play together and it worked great. You can switch between the three bounty hunters between levels, but the choice is secondary anyway. All three heroes play pretty much the same. The basics are always the same, even if they have slightly different standard weapons. You'll feel right at home if you've ever played Contra, Metal Slug, or its modern descendants like Blazing Chrome: In typical run-and-gun fashion, you can jump, shoot and dodge with a quick dash, which works well, but is nothing special. However, Huntdown also uses a handy cover system that is extremely rare in the genre: Your character can crouch behind crates or hug the wall to avoid getting hit. This doesn't necessarily add depth to the game, but it does slow down the action a bit. It also gives Huntdown a very unique feel.You'll collect many weapons along the way, in addition to the standard pistol. Once you've used them up, just throw them away and grab the next one. It's usually just around the corner. There are several shotguns and machine guns, as well as miniguns, rocket launchers, energy weapons, throwing stars, grenades, katanas, and so on. All in all, a great selection that will keep you entertained until the very end! The hit feedback is also great. You can clean the screen of your enemies, who are nicely animated in pixels: After a gunfight, bullet holes and blood splatters appear on the walls. When a street hustler is hit by a missile, the shrapnel literally flies. It is wonderfully over-the-top and not for children, but it is so satisfying!Unfortunately, the 20 levels are quite short. Many of them can be completed in a good quarter of an hour. I would have liked more scope, though, which is common in the genre. Because the action scores with variety, Huntdown never gets boring: You start your bounty hunt in dirty alleys, subway stations and sewers. Later on you can look forward to bars, garages, casinos, bathhouses, construction sites, factories and much more. There are no vehicle sequences or anything like that. But you'll have to fight in a moving convoy, take cover from helicopter gunfire or even flee from a monster truck. Not only the levels are varied, but also the different street gangs change several times during the game. They often appear unexpectedly and attack you with new weapons and tricks: In the beginning you'll only have to deal with lightly armed guys, but later on you'll have to deal with thugs with remote-controlled rocket launchers, automatic shotguns, hoverboards and exploding jetpacks, so you'll always have a challenge.The highlight, however, are the 20 different bosses. They've been implemented with great attention to detail. Giant mechs, attack helicopters, lightning-fast ninja sisters, mutated hockey players with mini-guns on their backs, or an Elvis impersonator with a flying motorcycle and lance - no two fights are alike. Most boss fights start out relatively easy. This gives you time to learn their attack patterns. However, there is usually a second phase that follows shortly after. This is when the action really picks up, and good reactions are required. Huntdown is surprisingly easy at the beginning on normal difficulty, but it gets much harder later in the game. To avoid frustration, there are relatively fixed checkpoints in every level, even right before every boss fight. If you die, you can try again immediately and don't have to repeat a long part of the level.A pixellated run-and-gun game isn't exactly the most fresh idea, to say the least. But who cares, if the resulting game is so much fun to play? Huntdown doesn't even have the pretense of being more than it is: You get 20 levels of focused, flashy sidescrolling action, great backgrounds, cool weapons, silly lines, massive bosses, and coherent 80s flair, all wrapped up in a really kickass pixelated retro style - no more, no less! Of course, I would have liked more scope, bonus objectives or replay value and for 16.79 Euros some games have already delivered more. But the overall package is still right: If Huntdown had been released for the SNES back in the 90s, I would probably be celebrating it today as a classic of the genre. In 2020 (2021 on Steam due to the EGS exclusive ....), however, it's simply a very good action game for retro fans. And that's enough.

_childDocuments_.review: Just when you think side scroll shooters were lame and belonged in the past, here comes Huntdown many probably confuse with another game. But let that be its only negative as the game really hits everything one could want in a simple side scroller modernized for people like me that didn’t grow up on these types of games. _childDocuments_.review: Huntdown is a side-scrolling action platformer with emphasis on cover shooting mechanics. It is set in a dystopian cyberpunk world, where crime is rampant and bounties high. That is all you need to know about the world. Well, you only need to know about the bounties as you take control of one of the three bounty hunters.At the start of the game, you get to choose from one of the three hunters. Each has a different starting loadout, which means a different gun and throwable weapon. A neat little feature is that you can change the hunters midway through a playthrough without losing any progress, letting you figure out your favourite while all hell breaks loose.On top of the characters, you can find various weapons ranging from guitars to heat-seeking missile launchers, which can either be hidden in boxes or secret caches or can be dropped by enemies wielding them. You can always carry your basic weapon as well as one extra you picked up. Found weapons have limited ammo so you cannot just spray willy-nilly even though you can find ammo for each weapon fairly often. These are accompanied by throwable weapons which include Molotov cocktails, grenades or throwing knives. All these things combined create a nice concise package where everyone will find a weapon that just suits their playstyle. is not a run'n'gun game in any shape or form. As already hinted, there are cover mechanics that you will have to use in almost any fight if you want to have a chance of surviving, especially on hard difficulty. You can duck behind boxes and cars or hide in the shadows on a garage, making you invincible to incoming fire but not explosions or melee attacks. Thus, even if you are hiding behind a cover, you are never truly safe.The game is divided into 4 major thematical sections, each divided into smaller levels. Each of the sections is based around one of the gangs occupying the in-game city. Those include brutal hockey fanatics, a biker gang or fashion obsessed crazies. And this is what made me fall in love with the game. You do not really get to know a lot in terms of story about these gangs or about why things are the way they are, yet these individual gangs ooze personality, mainly through the location and character design.Each of the levels is finished with a mini-boss fight against one of the side-bounties. These encounters are simple in terms of mechanics but fun in execution. As an example, one of the fights is against a hockey fanatic who just skates around and when she hits you with her stick, you just go flying around (and yes, you can end up in a goal). Another is against a biker leader, who has a huge javelin on his flying bike and behind him is a lady who keeps shouting how great he is. Simply put, the mini-bosses are a nice little treat after an endless gauntlet of enemies.Each of the gangs has their big bad leader and those are at the end of the final level of each of the sections. These are the big fights you were waiting for and they deliver. As the game progresses, each of the main bounties gets more complicated and challenging to face. Each of the fights has multiple attacks, special gimmicks and even multiple phases to keep you on your toes. If you are not careful, you will be demolished in seconds and have to restart the whole fight over. looks amazing. Even though it is a pixel-art game, there is so much attention to detail, from backdrops setting the scene to individual sprites. I am a huge fan of pixel-art and this game not only managed to satisfy that craving, but it also left a very pleasant aftertaste that I will gladly revisit.Same can be said for the soundtrack and sound design. The music has a cyberpunk feel to it and complements the atmosphere to a great effect. It is almost impossible to imagine  without its simplistic yet memorable soundtrack. Same applies to the sound design, where every single sound is distinct and by the time you are nearing the end, you will be able to safely recognize what kind of enemy is coming at you just based on the sound.It almost pains me to say but there are a few issues that the game suffers from. First, there is the typos and mistakes in the English text which are a minor oversight. When I first saw the main menu, I felt like I am about to play some random game made in 20 minutes during a lunch break.The second issue is that the game sometimes breaks the difficulty curve it created and leads to an unreasonable spike. A few moments ago, you were mowing down an army of gangsters only to get suddenly hit from 4 different directions, exploded, and hit with a baseball bat off the map. That is mainly the issue of enemy placement, which is fortunately not random, so you can create your own strategies, but some parts will feel outright unfair.Overall,  is an amazing title that I cannot recommend enough. If you are a fan of side-scrolling action platformers, this game will be right up your alley. At 16,79 euros, it is a fair price considering there are extra challenges for completionists as well as co-op mode, which adds more bullets and mayhem to the already existing one.

Feeble?You're having a bad day, craving for some easy, self indulgent gaming, and remember when videogames were just a joyfull rush of pixel, digitalized music and guns, tons of guns?You lost faith in this terrible, terrible world? _childDocuments_.review: It's Broforce with dash & cover mechanics instead of mostly-destructable environments, or 1st gen Ninja Gaiden with guns. Or 2D Snake Plissken, for the men and women of culture. This is a neo-80s cyberpunk treat, retro feel without retro clunk. If you're a gamer of mediocre skill like myself, Hard difficulty will almost assuredly grant a death or two per level, but no rage. Boss patterns are intuitive to memorize, and attacks are a treat to perfectly i-frame like it's Soulborne at times. Unexpected deaths from new mechanics like attack dogs and molotovs being unceremoniously introduced inspire appreciation for the details rather than saltiness. It seems like this one was a labor of love; I would gladly have paid more for it.

Its either you or them, and there will be a lot of bullet chewing time. Amazing art style design filled with many throw back 80’s era nostalgia and memories. Music makes this mayhem even more hectic and powerful, as if that’s not enough you will be surprised with many great level boss fights in the end. _childDocuments_.review: It is criminal that Huntdown didn’t get more exposure during it’s release. Boasting an stylish, colorful and vibrant pixel art graphics, coherent cyberpunk aesthetic, awesome 80s synthwave with convincing voice-acting all round and gunplay that is varies between action-packed and tactical, Huntdown is a near perfect recreation of the old-school run & gun format that would’ve stood shoulder to shoulder with Megaman, Contra and Gunstar Heroes. Developers Easy Trigger has accomplished something remarkable here. If you love 16-bit Run & Gun, Huntdown is a worthy purchase. Highly recommended. No joke, Easy Trigger put a lot of love in Huntdown and it shows. Every single element in this game is designed to evoke that 80s Sci-Fi action movie experience and they nailed it. From it’s neon  light Robocop/Total Recall atmosphere, the catchy 80s synth-wave soundtrack, the badass playable characters with memorable one-liners and the mad max inspired villains, Huntdown oozes and drips 80s swagger. This, combined with it’s excellent gunplay that includes cover mechanics, dash and melee attacks makes a satisfying combat with great flow, rhythm and progression. The great amount of distinct weapons will vary your play style greatly, from assault rifles, carbines, pistols, shotguns, laser rifles, sniper rifles, grenade launchers, flame throwers to even baseball bats, crowbars and katanas. This game is a lot of fun and it’s a damn shame that it did not get the reception it deserves. If you have the chance, get this game. It’s worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: HUNTDOWN

_childDocuments_.review: -This game is like the combination of old PC sidescroller like Duke Nukem (pre-3d), NES Contra, and arcade Metal Slug with 80s /90s cyberpunk and action movie tropes.-The cheesy humor, plot, and music is top notch. Might look like a shallow nostalgia at a glance but once you played it, they even spiritually nailed the silliness of similar games/story in that era. The guns, the character acting and lines, the costume design, etc.-It's not as fast paced as I thought it would be. But actually that makes it relaxing to play. Easy to get into and the challenge is just right for me without being frustrating. -I like how the enemies and characters are pretty diverse. -I haven't finished the game but I feel like this game will have similar replay value like Streets of Rage 4. Not because of there are many things to do or getting better at the game but because it's somehow just simply tight, fun, and arcadey to replay.
_childDocuments_.name: HUNTDOWN

_childDocuments_.review: Short form:- Synthwave soundtrack- Great sound and level design overall- Relatively fast-paced gameplay- Game is 3-5 hours long, but it's just enough to have a blast of an evening.If you fancy yourself some sidescrolling run-and-gun action like Contra or Metal Slug or even old Judge Dredd game (no longer on Steam btw), you are in the right place.10/10. Strong recommendation.Long form review part, so here's your only warning if you pressed "Read more".UPD: Fixed typos and whatnot.Story:Huntdown is a sidescroller shoot 'em up about bounty hunters trying to make a living by killing morally reprehensible gang members and their respective leaders. Clearly you are here for the action. However, you get an achievement by listening to all briefings, so at least for the first run just hear Wolfmother out. After all, she knows her children. All in all, it's an action flick type of story done in order to justify it being there. Glad that the developers respect their audience and aren't beating around the bush.Sound:First of all, gotta commend that there's voice acting present in the game. Even briefing parts are nicely voice acted and I feel like the VA part of the game is very good. Characters aren't shying away from throwing occasional one-liners akin to old-school FPS games. The lines are said with enough consistency to not be annoying, and somehow it's always on point, keeping that entertainment value along with giving characters enough of a distinctive personality, so it's worth replaying the game at least once per every character just to hear their lines, because even in briefings they reply to Wolfmother differently, even if they're essentially agreeing to take her contract. Still, it's a good touch. Over the span of the game you encounter different gangs, and each of them also say lines respective of the gang they belong to, and it's not just grunts saying those lines, even the bosses will occasionally say a one-liner that befits them as leader of their group, and I'm glad that small details like these are included within the game. It's full of these little touch-ups and I am all here for that.The soundtrack is superb. I know that synthwave nowadays is nothing to write home about unless it is done by some exceptional artists, or if it's a Furi/Hotline Miami OST. And yet it has enough impact in itself to perfectly fit within the setting. Makes me think of the montages by the 80's Guy where he edits footage from action classics of the 80-90's and puts synthwave on top of it. That's the kind of feeling this game gives me, and it's perfect for what it is, even if not specifically outstanding. There's a pretty wide array of weaponry in the game, each weapon sounds different and satisfying, as it should. Every weapon has a solid punch to it, not just in sound, but in animation as well. Animation and visual quality:Like I said prior, the game is abundant in details. I probably realized it later than I should have. At least the extent of the detail. I was just looking for stashes, minding my own business, and one of the sections had chain hooks. And when I jumped up to touch them and see what happens, expecting to phase through it like it's a piece of background, chains actually reacted to my presence and dangled. That's when I started paying attention to visual details and cues much more. And there's plenty of things to notice. Movements of hostiles, their jumps, idle postures whenever you're far enough or they don't see you, a character reloading each weapon differently (to name just a few, pay attention to rocket launcher and sawed-off reloads), it's all very dynamic and very reactive, so I encourage you to hunt for these details.Also, few extra details before I finish this section: First, this game has an achievement for making a dog fetch your grenade. Cruel, but funny. Second: gibs. Third: easter eggs to the action movies of the golden era.Gameplay:This section will be shorter because if you played any Contra game, then you already know the drill. You have your shooting button, your jump, your dash that has i-frames on it and acts like slide in Contra Hard Corps. The only difference that sets it apart is that the enemies drop all sorts of weaponry, and it's free for the taking. Sniper rifles, shotguns, sawed-off, assault rifles, SMG, flamethrowers, remote bombs. You even get to carry a portable howitzer on your shoulder at one point. Pretty impressive stuff. All of it serves only one purpose: making your enemies regret being on the other end of your weapon of choice. You have a choice between three different characters: Anna Conda being agile member of the group with fastest firing primary at her disposal, John Sawyer being the "heavy" class and having the most damaging but slowest primary in the game, and Mow Man being the balance between the two. Secondaries, those being whatever you pick up from dead enemies are the same for everyone.The only major difference from your "normal" run 'n gun is that this game has cover system. Approach any obstacle and your character will take cover. Be careful though, covers are destructible. Especially cars.And that's your gameplay loop. Difficulty:The difficulty is very fair. I'm not the one for ridiculous challenges or for extremely hardcore difficulties. With that out of the way, I found the game to strike the perfect balance between being challenging and fair at the same time. Deaths feel fair and I never felt like I'm at developer's wrath and that I should learn the trajectory of every bullet in the game to start enjoying it. No, in this game, regardless of difficulty, you're only as good as your momentary decision making skill is. Each attack and the appearance of every enemy is well telegraphed and I never had a section for which I wasn't prepared, because nothing ever shot me off-screen before I could even see it. The game prepares you for everything with enough timing. While not holding your hand necessarily, it's not beating you to a pulp either. One small complaint I got is that there's no player characters animated avatars in Points Shop. Perhaps something to consider? I'd love to have Mow Man animated profile picture! Wonder if developer is still reading these...Conclusion:Meticulously designed run-and-gun side-scroller with great pacing, great sound design, level design and balanced difficulty. A throwback done absolutely right. I wish I could have a "double recommend" button, or something that would express my satisfaction with the game in a proper manner, but alas. If you've made it this far, thank you. Have a good time of your day, and good hunting. The huntdown is initiated.Reminder: don't kill unarmed people and leave the cats be!

_childDocuments_.review: HUNTDOWN~~~~~~~~~~~Huntdown is a tip of the hat to a beloved genre of 16bit arcade shooters. And not just any arcade shooter, a proper 16bit, side-scroller action full of all features that we old-school arcade-goers love and adore. The game graciously sets up its tone for the chaotic nature of its gameplay and overall story-arc with a brief yet classic intro with one of the most 80s things imaginable; a heavy deep-voiced actor narrating a fantastic plotline.Plot: In the distant 21st-century nations have collapsed from the ruins of war. And from those ruins arose a society run by the mega-corporations. Fueled by greed and profits, these corporations provide jobs and security for those who obey their rules.An alternative path is one of crime and gang affiliations; a constant power struggle bowls for the control of the cities between these mega-corporations and the gangs. When the streets become too much for the citizens they call the authority’s ruthless law enforcers, who will go to any length possible. And when things become bad enough and the authorities are in trouble, the Bounty Hunters are called in; an elite group of mercenaries driven by profits and bloodlust. No matter how ruthless the gangs can be, these Bounty Hunters can go one up.Gameplay: This game is a benchmark of what arcade side-scrollers should be on PCs. The game starts off with a brief intro into the game's backstory; it pretty much sums it up and puts a great flavor into the overall theme and gameplay itself. The basic game is simple and tends to be greatly detailed after the old-school arcade, with its simple movement, jump, and cover machines. Thankfully the game provides much-needed key bind change for single and dual player modes. Although players won’t be able to use the same keys even when they use two different keyboards, which is such a bummer; it’s not the game's fault, it’s just windows. The game has two game modes to choose from: Story mode: Where you go after gangs in order to eliminate them and their bosses and sub-bosses, who count as a bounty. Before each mission and bounty, you are given a summary brief with Intel on each bounty. There are currently four unique gangs present in the game. The game does a great job at putting these different gangs and their bosses into different and sort of unique group according to their theme and outlook. The level progresses each time you collect a bounty by killing bosses. This trend will continue until you reach the final bosses and get to the end game where you beat his final form. Arcade mode: Basically the same as the story mode but here the motivation is very clear and streamlined. Kill as much as you can and get through all the checkpoints to get the game saved. You have a limited amount of lifeline and after you’ve died enough, you will need to pay from your profits in order to get back in the game with another set of lifelines.No clean bounties will be declared in this mode, but you will face the bosses and Level progression will mean leveling up the difficulty as well. Weapons: The game features a handsome quantity of weapons to go through. You will be given a primary weapon and a limited number of throwables, which are surprisingly powerful and balanced out to kill everything with enough shots. But the main fun and value of the game is where you get to use weapons dropped from the enemies; these are powerful, and some even come with a greater fire rate.Ranging from Katanas to Mini-gun-styled canons, they are balanced, powerful, and go great with the hectic gameplay. Bosses and enemy types: As mentioned earlier, there are four unique gangs throughout the city, and each has its own customs, style, and environment to rule. The gangs and bosses are very well detailed, and each can be easily identified. I can say the same for their fight style as well.  The bosses are really cool, with their own unique looks, play style, and abilities. As you progress through the game the bosses become more ruthless, powerful and altogether badass. World design: A fantastic looking, highly-stylized 16-bit aesthetic. The game pays great attention to detail and lighting. The levels are fairly spacious, although in certain areas and boss fights, I would’ve loved to have seen bigger arenas. Music and sound effects: The game features a banger of an intro music. The background music during the gameplay was great as well. The sound effects were bang on for the game's overall theme; from explosions to small arms fire, everything fits in perfectly. Positives: + Fantastic Story-arc + Shared/split screen co-op+ Fast-paced instance gameplay + Awesome music + Deep 80s-style narration and voiceover + Fantastic 16bit game design + Detailed environment + Unique and fun bosses Negatives: - I have no negative things to say about this titleHuntdown is just a perfect example of how great arcade titles can be on the PC side. From its fast-paced arcade action to its Steller authentic style.  This game is just perfect for arcade lovers. 10/10 Key provided by the developer/publisher for review purposes. Any opinions expressed are entirely my own!

_childDocuments_.review: I've spent (as of this writing) 57+ hours on this game. It is an absolute 10/10 for me. Arcade game of the year 1992 is exactly right, and honestly some of us have been looking for this game since 1992. Coop is rock solid, boss fights are fun (tiny quibble here: boss difficulty varies - still a 10/10, don't worry!), and the environments are dope. If you like any kind of dystopian science fiction media by way of Paul Verhoeven you really can't go wrong with Huntdown. Lately I've been listening to audiobooks and just vibing through levels, and it's perfect for that too.

_childDocuments_.review: Before getting into my lengthy and especially incoherent "review" about Huntdown, let me share a personal story. I was born in 1989, in Eastern-Europe, Hungary. Growing up, I was surrounded and heavily influenced by media from the 80s. Despite I was an 80s kid for only a month and spent my childhood in the 90s, the newly formed TV stations, and VHS distribution companies (and sometimes even rural cinemas) financially struggled to get all the hot new media from the west, so they aired and published movies from the 80s a lot and I mean A LOT. I grew up on movies like Tango & Cash, To Live and Die in L.A., The Running Man, and so on. When the 80s revival happened with Grand Theft Auto: Vice City then with Hotline Miami, I fully dived into it, and as a fan and listener, I was there when the early synthwave records came out in 2010. Having this background, I have a special spot in for games inspired by the 80s DONE GOOD. Because let's be honest, the retro-futuristic aesthetic especially on Steam is over-used, and you have to search for great titles with a magnifying glass. But when I saw the first trailer for Huntdown a year ago, I knew there's something good going on. Although, the trailer looked awesome, to be honest, there wasn't anything special what previous indie titles like Broforce and Mercenary Kings haven't already done. But from the video, I immediately fell love with the game’s art direction; and the gameplay did look great too. I'm more of a beat 'em up guy myself, but I like some shooting too. So I bought the game day one, and after sitting on it for a bit, I played it through two streams on my Twitch channel. And boy, I loved this game. When you innocently start the game, you don't know what to expect, but the intro with the arcade styled menus with that amazing music theme caught me off-guard and gave me a huge smile which lasted through my playthrough. For some reason, I started with arcade mode and it was a good lesson, really. It helped me to develop the necessary basics on my own, and prepared my bottom for the frantic action that awaits me in story mode. You have three different characters to choose from, each coming with its completely different basic weapon sets, and your job is to rush into the three distinctive districts in a crime infected city. You play as a bounty hunter, and you have two easy tasks: to kill everything that moves and to not get killed by the crazy punks who are after your blood. Your basic weapons are always with you, equipped with infinite ammo, and you also have throwing weapons which are also infinite but are on a cooldown. You'll find an incredible amount of various and strong (sometimes OP as hell) weapons and grenades, but most of the time, you'll have to rely on your basic kit, and it's really important to try all three bounty hunters to find who's kit will fit your play style. For me, it was Mow Man, a modified droid, and he was the one I started the story with on normal difficulty. I'm far from 100%-ing the game, but I have the desire to do so, because this game nails everything! Honestly. First of all, the gameplay. The gameplay is slick as hell: you can shoot, you can jump, you can switch weapons, and most importantly: you can DASH. And the dash is AMAZING. With a tiny window of i-frame and with a small but sometimes crucial cooldown, you'll have to abuse dash as much as you can, and every time you do so, it feels amazing. A badly designed dash could've alienated me from the game at the beginning, but it's just so damn rewarding to use, and feel so great, that I immediately fell love with that and I can tell you, there's not much better feeling when you dash BETWEEN TWO BULLETS during a bossfight. The length, the feeling of it, everything hits that sweet spot. And here comes my hot take. The game is clearly inspired by Contra, but for me, the game felt more like Mega Man (to be exact: Mega Man X)! No, I'm not high while I'm writing this. How the stages start, the dash system works, and especially the single-screen boss fights, it's just feel more like a Mega Man game than a Contra. And do you know what is also great in this game? It's not rougelike! Don't get me wrong, I don't have any problem with that type of games, but to this game, I just don't see if it could've worked. One of the key elements why this game works so great, it’s because it nails the difficulty. Again, I only played on normal (yet), and this genre is not my main one, but I never felt unfairness, and whenever I died, the only one to blame was me. The difficulty curve is spot on and from stage to stage it helped me to enhance my abilities, knowledge and necessary skillset to proceed further, and with a trial and error mentality, you can easily nail every obstacle you might meet during a hard part. The pre-deployed /determined enemy layout helps a lot, because for a successful run, it's a key point to memorize the stage and enemy spots, especially on later stages. And those stages... my gosh. SNK may be the true masters of pixel art, but this game is just amazing to look at, I kid you not, every single screen is background material. It's incredibly detailed with every part of a stage being completely unique looking. You'll never see the same shop and neon lights twice, and the bit darker tone of the stages with almost everything being brown, grey and black (well, we're talking about a literal concrete jungle) makes a great chemistry with the bright colours of graffiti and neon lights. And you'll make the stage mostly red anyways, because the game has some sweet gore in it! And the three completely different gang (inspired by the cult movie The Warriors) who took over the city, are amazing. Every gang has multiple types of goons and some of them will make your life hard! Each goon also designed well, they almost look like Streets of Rage enemies, nailing the punk and gang aesthetics. And one part which might look trivial for some, but made the game so memorable to me: the voice acting! My gosh, the voice acting is AMAZING. The dialogues (of course almost entirely made of cheesy 80s inspired one-lines) are really funny and entertaining, and from the nameless goons you mow down in hundreds to the unique bosses, everyone is memorable, and it's mainly because of the amazing voice acting. There's a ton of various dialogues, shouts, every boss fight starts with some great lines. My personal favourite is Teddy Taxman, who during the entirety of the first cycle, when you fights against security cannons, gets interrupted by his boss via a phone call, and it's just so damn funny to hear him talking like there's nothing going on, when you are literally under him on a platform, shooting as much as an entire army. Every spoken line well delivered and memorable, and shout out to all voice talents, who really made this game worth its price! The synthwave music is also amazing! Great tunes all around, and wink-wink, it's also available on vinyl, which I frankly own already. The absolute banger of the OST is New Hunting Grounds, which is an amazingly produced 80s synthwave song, but the almost horrorish and disturbing Restless Nights as well Entering Gangland, the break and funk inspired The No. 1 Suspects, and the song Gathering the Armies featuring an amazing guitar solo is just as amazing to listen to. The game might feel short but in reality, it isn't. What content is in it, is 100% crafted (the stock weapon sounds being the only exception), and there's a huge replay value. Two game modes, various difficulty and objectives to complete, the game does offer a lot. I'd love to see a sequel because for me it's not just a great indie title I really enjoyed. For me, Huntdown is the game of the year in 2021. 10/10. I absolutely loved everything and I can nothing but recommend it, and with its really-really friendly price tag, it's a no brainer to get. So what do you waiting for? The city ain’t gonna’ clean itself!!!
_childDocuments_.name: HUNTDOWN

_childDocuments_.review: One of my ultimate fantasies and one of the best games I've ever played. It's the embodiment of what I love about the 80s cyberpunk and retrofuturism greatness, with humor that fits the tone.The gameplay might feel a bit limited, but it's great by design, similar to old school Castlevania games. Plus, the variety of excellent level design and creative bosses greatly makes up for it. Arcade Mode also adds to replay value with new enemy and weapon placement and score attack challenge.The graphics make it feel like a Sega Saturn game, with stunning visuals and exquisite attention to detail and sound design - everything just feels right.The voice acting is great, and there are tons of references to 80s and 90s films, games and anime, which are too many to count. Some of them include The Warriors, Robocop, The Terminator, Running Man, Escape From New York, Blade Runner, Akira, Mad Max, etc. If you love these types of media, you will love this game.The soundtrack is legendary, and the game is worth buying for the music alone. There's a fantastic mixture of great melodic synthwave and rock music, with both head-bobbing tracks and more atmospheric pieces inspired by such fims as The Terminator and Escape From New York; some tracks even feature the sound of the good old Yamaha chip used in Sega Mega Drive. "The Troublemaker" is one of my all-time favorite tracks ever!10/10, will never get tired of this masterpiece. Please let there be a sequel (or at least some DLC with new gangs and such)!

_childDocuments_.review: Recommending with reservations. An arcade-style shooter but one in which your mobility and evasion is severely limited so your best bet in most instances is either hiding behind cover or ambushing enemies quickly before they can retaliate. In that sense it's less like contra or metal slug and more like a rolling thunder, crime city, shinobi, or elevator action returns, although it plays much faster than any of those games. It's kind of hard to draw a comparison because it doesn't have a distinct lineage, and that's what I like about the game. You have to work your way through incredibly dangerous enemies both tactically and efficiently, and moving down waves of bad guys feels good.I find the faux-80s aesthetic to be extraordinarily played out by now but the production values here in terms of graphics and sound are undeniably extremely high quality. I just wish the voice clips weren't so frequent, the repetitiveness gets very grating after a while especially when they're doing tired movie quotes.The difficult point is that I really disliked the boss fights - while most of them are fair, the bosses are extremely spongy and take eons to kill, even on the early stages. Given the limited life you have it means you have to dodge near perfectly for an extremely long time, and my hands would start to hurt after a while. I got extremely frustrated with some of the late fights which were impossibly tedious. With the bosses getting so much emphasis in the game that left me feeling a bit sour. It's possible the boss fights were balanced around co-op play? I never had an issue playing the missions solo though, so it's weird that there was always this extreme difficulty spike.I grabbed this on sale and felt I got fair value, but it wasn't something I felt strongly compelled to replay to 100% the missions or try on higher difficulties. Ultimately though it's a game that despite being retro-styled is distinctly different and I believe that sort of originality deserves to be commended.

_childDocuments_.review: This is as close to perfection as you can get in a retro action platformer. It was clearly developed by people who either grew up in the 80's/90's, or are in love with the era and studied it well.Everything in the game is polished and executed so well, I could easily ramble on and bore you with details I appreciate. I will say that I was particularly excited to see the "hide-in-the-shadows" mechanic brought back from Blizzard's 'Blackthorne' (1994).It looks great, it's nostalgic and it's fun. Heat up some pop tarts and invite a childhood friend over to play it with you!

_childDocuments_.review: Unlike what the screenshots may suggest, this is not a fast run-and-gun platformer, it's more like a slow technical sidescroller. It plays very similarly to the Shinobi or Rolling-Thunder arcade games. It takes a lot of level learning and memorizing.  It's not a movie game and the casuals will be filtered.The game saves after each level, and the difficulty ramps up generously for a very satisfying overall challenge. 100%ing the game on normal will take some dedication, but it's achievable to most gamers. Though getting all the achievements will be extremely difficult.The game is full of details, secret rooms, and little references to 80s culture.I like that they limited themselves to more or less megadrive graphics quality, which enabled them to create an ample amount of asset graphics with reasonable ressources. It's a good example of scope limiting. The pixel art is somptous although the theme is very banal and it's nothing that you haven't already seen before. And the over-use of pastel purple grades everywhere ruins a lot of the ambiance.I also enjoy the oldschool animations and movement speed, some will find them stiff, but I much prefer that to modern platformers where all characters slide and slash across the screen like hectic chihuahuas.The sound department is very rich with original music and voice actors, but nothing memorable unfortunately.
_childDocuments_.name: HUNTDOWN

_childDocuments_.review: Instead of having a long walk in a level, Huntdown divided one area into different smaller areas, giving each one around 5 mins of gameplay includes a mini boss to battle at the end. I suck at horizon scroll arcade games, I find in shorter levels I make fewer mistakes.Huntdown has a good control, a good variety of weapons and enemies, one of the few games keep me hooked and want to keep playing. On easy mode (yea, suit  me in well) I get a good amount of health pills when making a kill, so I can stay calm. The game is generous on giving supplies, yet still challenging. There are suitcases to collect, at least one placed on a higher floor, one you need to quickly take from an escaping target, the last one can be anywhere. For playstyle, you can clean the area or ignore everyone and head all the way to the exit. There are crate to stop bullet but will eventually be destroyed, oil barrels, doors to hide. You can always see health bar on everyone, easy to make the next move.Last thing is game shows 1P and 2P. I haven't tried out co-op, but can imagine the fun play with a friend.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun and intense shooter in the style of Metal Slug and Contra, with a good 80s retro look and feel to it.When I say "80s retro", I don't mean that they just smeared neon lights on everything and noodled on a synth for a couple of tracks.  The game has a beautiful cassette futurist look to everything, right down to the small details.  Instead of just dropping a couple of references, they built wildly entertaining themes around old movies and cliches.  The top-notch voice acting only helps make the game as aesthetically fun as it is exciting to play.
