For me, it got a little bit too annoying, so I ended up checking out a gameplay video to see how the game ends. Shame, because the story is really cool, and I enjoyed playing it.
_childDocuments_.name: Unto The End

_childDocuments_.review: Unto The End is a game that wants to tell a story first and foremost. The fights are not fair and the combat system isn't something that is designed to put you on equal footing with the worst enemies you'll face. The game is about the story of a father trying to get back to his family. He isn't some great warrior of legend or a chosen one; he is a big man with a sword who is nonetheless dwarfed in power (and sometimes skill) by the creatures he faces. This is the main premise that the combat system follows.  If you want to get home you'll need to stay calm, think and analyze the different enemies and environments you'll face. The game weaves the combat system and encounters into the story rather seamlessly and this naturally makes some fights quite hard, especially if you try to take enemies head-on with little to no planning. It's a mistake to analyze and criticize the combat system separately from, say the visuals or atmosphere of the game. Unto The End combines all of its elements together to tell a story and if you take one element on its own, it could very well look incomplete, out of place or plain bad. You might be disappointed by this game if you are looking for a fair combat system and encounters; where the only thing you need to do is put in the necessary time and effort to stand on equal ground with the enemies you'll face. That is not what this game is about. This is a story about a normal man, who is no one especially important on the grand scale of things. The combat system aims to reflect that fact and I think does a pretty good job at it. I wouldn't call this game a masterpiece but it was pretty fun and well crafted. I don't think it deserves the mixed reviews status at all. It's an interesting and (as far as I'm concerned) unique game and it's one I don't regret playing one bit.
_childDocuments_.name: Unto The End

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE: Maybe its just me, but reaching further into the game fighting becomes quite hard with really short reaction times. The most useful tactic quickly becomes just standing in one place blocking and then reposting. All other moves mostly complicate things rather than provide an advantage which is a downer. Still, I belive reconfigurable PC buttons would really help this as right now they just make me mess up everything after a move which is a direct death in this game.Have been waiting for this game for quite a while now and it was surely worth it. Expect no tutorials or explanations, but subtle environmental storytelling immersing you into a dark and atmospheric world where you feel small and often overwhelmed. That's right - sounds like Dark Souls and the game is also just as punishing although with regular checkpoints moving things forward. Still, dying is constant and I like this a lot - even with a checkpoint behind you the game is difficult enough to make you replay a scene more than a few times until you find your own way of beating it. Fighting system is innovative and a fair bit more complex than hit/block/dodge with a few more buttons and various actions all having their battle role. These different elements add up to each other beautifully for a very cinematic and bloody combat. Love the game, amazing work for a two person development team!

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game.Short version: The game is fun, beautiful, difficult, has a fair amount of secrets you can find, and a fair amount of places to explore. Combat will test you in many ways and will likely frustrate you a bit. Has multiple endings and a hidden feature. Most of the negative reviews come from the game's dificulty and rather short lenght but i believe if you are willing to look past that i think this game deserves your attention. Especially if it's on sale.Long version:It's rare to see games like this. Unto the End is a challenging adventure game, with beautiful aesthetics, mesmerising atmosphere, a solid story and deadly combat, with some crafting and survival aspects as well.Here you do not play the role of an epic fantasy adventurer, you are just a mortal man, and your goal is simple - find your way back home. The game will take you through snow covered forests and mountains, and through deep, dark caves. You will encounter various creatures, some friendly, some hostile, and some that just want to be left alone. The visual presentation is just stunning. Both the style and the UI of the game take a very minimalist approach, and the game has a very Samurai Jack sort of vibe to it. It feels like i can be at any location in the game, at any point and a screenshot of it will always make a great wallpaper. The scenery is just lovely, and  is just a joy to simply look at the game.The story is simple, but done well, and there is a lot of lore that you can piece together as well.Combat is deadly, and difficult to get the hang of at first, but also not your only option. Encounters have multiple ways of being resolved, and you can even complete the game without killing a single creature. And if the hostile ones don't get you, you have to remain sharp, as often times the terrain can be trecherous, and traps can be placed that you will have to dodge.I believe this game is best experienced by finding and learning new things on your own. It has a fair amount of hidden rooms/spots, often they contain some neat items that can help you out, or some additional recources that can keep you alive, or be used for other purposes. The game rewards exploration. It also features multiple endings, but which one you get will depend on how you've interacted with the world throughout the game. The combat is very well designed, and rewards patience, perserverence, and creativity. It is demanding, you *will* die, most likely a lot. Mastering the combat will not only require you to learn the oponents' moves, but will also at times require you to adapt, as the AI in the game  can learn your tactics and learn to dodge or counter them in the middle of the fight, so some of the tougher enemies will require you to utilise all your tools in your arsenal to switch things up and surprise them to finish a fight. Fortunately, the game also features a practice mode that you can access at certain points to familiarise yourself with all the available mechanincs. And you have a lot of tools at your disposal as well, Attacking, parrying, riposting, throwing a dagger, or using it to stab at close range, feinting, shoulder bashing, rolling away, which you can turn into a rolling attack, ducking under attacks (which you can turn into a ducking attack), jumping over attacks (which you can turn into a jumping attack), and throwing spears which you can occasionally find along the way. You can even kick dirt/snow into their eyes. The game gives plenty of options, which you will need to use intelligently to find success reliably.The game is a little bit short, most people tend to finish their first run of the game within about 4-6 hours, depending on how much you die, which creatures you fight and how much you explore. I finished my first run in just a bit before the 6 hour mark. If you complete the game 2-3 times and memorise where to go and what to do,  you can probably rush it it in about 45 minutes. I've seen speedruns of this game in about 29 minutes or so.The two major criticsms this game really gets is regarding 2 things - the combat, and the lenght. Combat: This game, without a doubt, will test your patience, your nerves, and your willingness to persevere and soldier on. this is not a game where you can simply roll away, attack, roll away, attack, roll away, repeat ad nauseam until the oponent is dead, this game focuses on a more read-react approach to fighting, you will have to obsereve, defend yourself actively and react appropriately to what your oponent is doing. Rolling and jumping around blindly and too often in an attempt to abuse i-frames will put you in a bad spot. Blindly throwing attacks and button mashing is severely punished. Each one of your moves and actions must be delibirate, and done with purpose. This is further compounded by the fact that this game does not follow the usual formula of "encounter new enemy-> learn their patterns -> thrash a bunch of the same enemy type repeatedly -> boss fight". Here each creature you encounter will be a little bit different, and you will have to adapt constantly. For that reason i believe many have chosen to  give this game a bad review, stating it's too difficult or that they should add an easy mode.Very few games i can think of really challenge a player in this way, especially with an AI that literally learns your tactics in the middle of a fight and starts to defend against them quite well afterwards. A lot of people are not used to this, and get frustrated. And you will probably get frustrated a few times as well. I know i did, for sure. Still, if you are a fan of difficult games, and feel up to it, i think you will love it by the end.Lenght: I can't argue that the game is a rather short experience. When i bought the game I already knew a lot of people complained that the game was too short, so going into it, i went in knowing that it will be a short game. Even then, i was caught off-guard when the game's ending came. At first i deffinitely felt a little bit upset that this lovely game ended so quickly. I wanted more, I'd fallen in love with this game so much. It's world, lore, combat, and general atmosphere. How i wish it was longer. Regardless, this game has zero filler, there is nothing in this game that i can say was just put there to pad the game out a bit. All of those nearly 6 hours of gameplay that took to complete the first run was pure quality. I enjoyed every minute of it. If you decide to play through the game multiple times (which i highly recommend) you may notice a certain detail about subsequent runs, but i won't say any more.Despite it's shorth length, the game has a fair amount of replayability, with hidden items, rooms and secrets to find and figuring out the different ways you can interact with the NPC's, the different endings you can get, the varous tid bits of lore you can put together, and of course, mastering the combat along the way. There is also a secret game mode which you can unlock, which is best found naturally.I fell in love with this game so much i ended up playing it through another 8 or 9 times, mastering the combat, exploring and finding all the hidden items, rooms and NPC's, interacting in various ways with them, made a run withouth killing a single creature, made a run where i ruthlessly slaughtered literally every single creature in the game, got all the achievements, played through the 'secret' mode and got all the endings.Overall, if the punishing combat, and rather shorth lenght of the initial play-through don't put you off, i can not recommend this game more. This is honestly one of the best games I've ever played, It is certainly a game that focuses on quality of quantity. I feel confident saying that this game was made with a lot of heart. You will be taken on a journey filled with fear, confusion, stress, frustration, but also beauty, wonder, a sense of accomplishment and serenity at the end of it all.An experience you will remember.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not  hard.I've played much harder games (Rainworld for example) and I've played much easier. I'm disappointed by some of the top reviews on this game, complaining about the combat. Once you get into the momentum of a good fight, it's extremely rewarding. Easily some of the best combat I've ever experienced in a 2D game. You're trading blows with your opponent, and sometimes come back from the brink of death to deal a finishing blow. It's spectacular. Your moves carry weight, momentum, and can stun you, and making the wrong move at the wrong time can be a death sentence.One contention with the game is the shoulder charge constantly being dodged by opponents. But this mechanic is extremely useful when someone is jumping at you, looking to bring their blade down on your skull. Your opponents move will knock your sword from your hand if you try to block it, but if you shoulder charge into them, they will be forced to stop their attack and dodge. It's easy to get frustrated when a move doesn't do what you want it to, but if you take a step back you may find another use for it.Another issue is the time to decide whether to block high or low. Some enemies have move sets that make it easy to distinguish, others not so much. Dodging is the best course of action against these enemies. Block the attacks you can, and dodge/charge the ones you can't. Getting in quick, low jabs and staying out of your enemies reach is a good approach. Blocking also has a function on the controller, where if you are blocking low, but want to block high at the last second or so, you can. Simply move the stick up as you read the attack.Lastly, reaction time is important. You have to react quickly, and if you can't then you may need to adjust the settings.I ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ love this game. I'm so disappointed others don't feel the same way. I feel like a legend when I wreck some cocky monsters ♥♥♥♥, it's like two seasoned warriors have stumbled upon each other and battle just to see who's better. I've spoken to the Dev on discord and they were very helpful and they should be proud of what they accomplished with this game. It's truly a work of art.10/10 easy game

_childDocuments_.review: I already owned the game, and I still bought it again on Steam; this should be an indication of how good I consider this product.It's a short and extremely intense experience, especially if played as suggested by the game itself: at the beginning in fact there is a notice that gives an idea of ​​how to approach it, explaining that the resources will be precious because they will be very limited, the foreigners encountered will not speak the same language, the fights will be difficult and always deadly, and the environment will be hostile and unpredictable.And our protagonist is not an invincible warrior hero: he is a Viking hunter, he does not seek conflict or adventure, because he is driven by pure necessity. He carries the sword in defense. He is certainly a tough, tenacious, tempered man, but he doesn't want anything else but to return to his family. When he is sitting near a bonfire he plunges into memories, and sees himself at his home, in the company of his loved ones on a hot sunny day. Try to open the inventory when it happens, you will find among other things - all moving - a useless STONE. Its description states that it is a gift from the little daughter to her father. If you have children you will understand how a wonderful detail it is; in order not to succumb to the cold, even clinging to the memory of that stone is important for our Viking.All of this is expressed without a single line of dialogue.The audio compartment is immersive: in the quiet you can hear the wind, the burning torch, and the trembling breath of the hunter. It manages to make you feel the cold of the environment and the weight of the sword in every moment, a truly remarkable result in my opinion. I would recommend using headphones to maximize this aspect of the experience.Visually it is very pleasing, so much so that almost every frame deserves a screenshot, even while immersed in darkness. I read that many negative reviews point the finger at excessively "black" screens. It's true, while exploring the intricate cave complex, the 90% of the screen remains completely black, but it's part of the atmosphere of the game, it contributes to feeling lost in the unknown. It also makes the torch indispensable - losing it means being forced to make another one by consuming precious materials - and makes you appreciate even more the few moments in which you can lead the hunter back into the sunlight.It is completely localized in Italian and many other languages, even if as mentioned the interactions with the other characters are exclusively non-verbal, which is another interesting aspect: not all enemies are really enemies, sometimes it is enough to sheathe the sword to get a positive reaction from the natives. Many of them don't want to fight; they just defend themselves to survive if they have no other choice.The gameplay system is functional and it's the bare minimum to hold and conduct everything written above smoothly. You won't need anything else.In summary, Unto The End is an highly recommended experience of a few hours (about 5 or 6), the result of an impressive work for only TWO developers. If the cost / hours of game ratio can make you turn up your nose, it is often on sale for almost half its price, and it is worth every euro.Get the hunter back home!
_childDocuments_.name: Unto The End

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely one of the greatest games I've played in quite a while. EVERYTHING can be solved by paying attention to the level structure and design, the sound effects are spot on and the combat is one of the hardest and most rewarding I've seen in quite a while. Some people may feel a little bit down due to its short duration but trust me: Unto the End is as long as it should be. This game will definitely get you charmed by its simple yet amazing visuals, its sense of exploring an unknown and hostile land and it's really tough (and sometimes even optional!) boss battles. A must own and must play if you are looking for something different that took its time to come out without having to rely on aggressive crunch practices
_childDocuments_.name: Unto The End

_childDocuments_.review: Looks good, intense atmoshpere, theoretical good fighting system... butProblems by blocking (to much knockback) big delay while fighting and an not really good tutorial. It need to be improved, for Keyboard and Mouse, atleast i played with that. The Char is to clunky, and in some close qaurter fights, you cant see the attack after goten pushed back, several times while blocking.So nah, dont buy it for over 20 bucks. Wait for Sale or improvement.
_childDocuments_.name: Unto The End

_childDocuments_.review: It is a 2D linear, narrative action game centered on fast-paced gameplay, with an emphasis on melee combat. But you can also influence which ending you get. In the game, you will have three weapons that really affect combat in very different ways.The main character has a combination of attacks. Each enemy is dangerous since TtK  is very low, so you have to be both cautious and aggressive. And you don't have a status bar here, you can only focus on the appearance of the hero and enemies. Also there are also classic dodges.You can bleed out if you are badly wounded, this also tires out the character and can set you up for a hit.We get a vague narrative about a warrior who wants to return to his family.Since there is no text in the game except for the interface text, which is very minimalistic and only activates at certain moments, it doesn't feel like a classic story, but like a myth. A myth about a warrior who wants to return home after going through some kind of war as an outside, random participant. A war between mystical races...In some cases, you can also avoid combat by showing your kind side.To fully unlock all the content and potential, the game is designed to be played through three times. But this is not a problem at all, as the game is quite short.A full playthrough of the game, depending on your combat skills and moral choices in the story, will take between ~1.5 and ~4 hours. The first playthrough will likely be longer than all later ones.This game won't take a lot of your time, but it will leave an interesting experience.The gameplay isn't an afterthought, it's really the core of the game. The combat system has a lot of potential for content expansion.I recommend the game to those who like adventure games focused on visual design, ambient sounds, northern and snowy mystical atmoshere.
_childDocuments_.name: Unto The End

_childDocuments_.review: This game was absolutely dreadful.It hurts to write that because the passion present in this game is very clear and there was a lot of effort put into it. This is something people really cared about and tried their best to make, but no amount of respect I have for developers can make me enjoy the game more.This starts out as a very cool, pretty and interesting game with a seemingly fun and deep combat system. The environments are cool and exploration is interesting and it very quickly spirals out of control. The games combat betrays itself and starts throwing enemy attacks at you that are borderline unreactable (some enemies have attacks that have to be about 200ms), while punishing you for defending yourself incorrectly. Checkpoints are frequent but the game almost feels like Super Meatboy with how often you die and how quickly you go back to checkpoints to try again, but this isnt in a good way. Enemies also dont follow the same rules that you do, having more health, damage and often not staggering when you hit them, so even when you manage to break through their defense and sneak a hit in, youre punished by taking more damage than you did. If that wasnt enough, your defense options are inconsistent with some attacks ignoring your block, rolls having iframes that dont work and its almost like they decide when they want to be hit or not. The tutorial or practice-mode actually lies to you and gives you information that isnt true, such as "after throwing an opponent off balance by defending their attack chain, strike in the opposite direction of the last attack that they threw", which I found an enemy half way through that this doesnt apply to. The story here is another "vague" story to try and make you understand the deeper meaning but this doesnt really work. You also have a good and bad ending depending on your actions towards neutral NPCs but its a lot like "offer the right item or they fight you and you get the bad ending" to the point where youll offer the wrong one and its better to just die and retry with another item than to bother with it. Its got nice music, pretty visuals, almost fun combat and I hate to dismiss their work, but this game was more than a chore to play. I wouldnt recommend it, honestly but if you do play it, I recommend turning on the "Assisted" mode which turns down the speed of attacks. It wont make some of the attacks reactable, but good luck playing this game without it. Id like to think im pretty competent at games and ive got a lot of experience reacting properly fast things, but thiis was beyond me.EDIT: While looking up videos on this games combat, I noticed how smooth it was. On relaunching the game, my game ran at a proper 144fps framerate when previously it was stuck at 60 for my whole playthrough. Im not sure how much of an impact this wouldve made for me, but its worth mentioning.EDIT 2 (2023): The developer has apparently made updates to the game to help many of my criticisms. Good on them for sticking with it.
_childDocuments_.name: Unto The End

_childDocuments_.review: i got this for 75% off and i think that its the right price point for this game. Don't pay full price cause it doesn't provide enough value for that. Now with that said this game for the short play time that it has is really good. the combat was pretty fun, it does feel a little unfair sometimes but then you realise that it was your mistake and you can win if you don't get impatient. The ending felt a little abrupt and unsatisfying but I've read there are multiple endings, i don't know the difference in the endings but i must of got the bad one. From my single play through i cant recall what i could of done differently to warrant a different ending and i wont be replaying to find them as while the game was fun it doesn't inspire replay, tho i generally will only play a single player game through to the end once anyways.If you can get it on sale then its a fun little experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Unto The End

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game knowing that it had mixed reviews and that would be challenging but enjoyed it none the less, it had a great way of showing its environmental story-telling through subtle hits while progressing in the different areas, and with its puzzles too. As for my problem with it, (and i know im not the first to say) its pretty short, and for how short the game is it definitely can't be worth 20£/$ unless you wait for a sale like i did. Other than replaying the story a couple times for a character skin change, there really is no other pull for replay ability, perhaps if its story was a bit longer or even had separate side story where you played different characters (like an orc or something) it would have felt more like a game and less like a slightly long demo. I enjoyed its combat mechanics and loved the simple line-less art-style, its bosses were fun (favourite boss is easily the deer wielding yeti) thumbs up to the DVS for trying something new. Overall i do recommend this game for those who want to try a short or challenging combat game, but people who are looking for story or replay value will probably feel like the wasted money.
_childDocuments_.name: Unto The End

_childDocuments_.review: It breaks my Heart to give this a thumbs down. But it just doesnt hold up. The game clearly has allot of love put in to it. Animations and visuals are really cool and fleshed out. There's a mythology that attempts to drag you in. Sadly it fails on allot of levels. Let's begin.First issue is the controls are all over the place and forces an annoying sense of frustration. you can really feel this was built for a controller. The combat is at first really cool it's fast and brutal. THen as you dealt with the first enemies you start running in to thos that doesnt just change the mechancis but downright abuses what you learned from before and uses things against you. For example you been tought to parry then strike only for enemy to not give a ♥♥♥♥ and not stagger and just keep on spamming. Your taught to learn enemy attack patterns and visual que's.. Only for enemy's to use the same que to feint a new attack. For a game with just low attacks, high attacks. Low block high block this shoult not be this complicated. The game throws in a pretty harsh resource management that focuse more on giving you what you dont need when you need it. Allt of times its more worth to just be killed then to win a fight with low hp and damaged armor. Since if you want the good achievments you gonna need that later on. The game throws allot of instant death yet your almost never further back then 60 seconds in terms of a checkpoint giving each death a sense of cheapness and feeling like you where meant to die for a laugh rather then a challenge to overcome. Then combine that the game is close to like 30 min or 45 min if you dont die allot or go for achievments. That in the end is a sin for me as you feel like you just paid 20,99€ for something that could been a newgrounds flash game. But the gravest sin of all is the story. It acts like it has this deep thing going. And your apperently this father sent of to somewhere to do something to then try and get back home. Thing is nothin is said or done to showcase this. you start by praying at a tree.. your wife and son give you some items and you run off to the right. Then your in the mountain.. For some reason.. Then your in a cave.. Then you fight monsters and meet strange things until your somehow back home.. Did you go out to hunt? Why did you hunt in such dangerous areas? did you go off to war? did we miss the war? I did not understand allot about the story and i feel it failed to captivate me. It's a sad thing but same time I feel there's hope and potential for an upcoming project from this developers. They have what it takes to make great things and therefor I will be keeping an eye out for what else they make.
_childDocuments_.name: Unto The End

_childDocuments_.review: The game can't decide whether it want's to be a skill-based beatem-up or an atmospheric game. The combat is great and stands on its own, but it is destroyed by the little time you have to master it. Throughout the whole game you feel like a beginner, not too sure how to work the fighting mechanics. Seeing as the game is only about 6hrs, you never really get past this stage. Even though the combat is fleshed out, it is still easily cheese able. simple combos over and over again can beat even the toughest enemies, making it feel like you didn't really earn your victory.The game has a cool concept but I think it falls short, especially for the price point.
_childDocuments_.name: Unto The End

_childDocuments_.review: Finished the game, had to restart only once due to something I forgot to grab. Pretty short, but very atmospheric. Combat was not as bad as reviews made it out to be, only frustrating due to me fat fingering a button and mis-inputting. Only two types of block and two attack stances which don't require stance change in addition to attacking. I liked the fighting, less get gud and more finding a rhythm between defending and attacking, I rarely play melee fighters because of all the inputs to memorize, this isn't a beat-em up and it isn't for Honor, comfortably its own. I admit I was drawn away because of the mixed reviews when the game first came out but it isn't bad for a 10$ USD or equivalent when on sale. If a 25$ USD or equivalent is burning a hole in your pocket then go for it. Otherwise wait for a sale. Definitely would recommend
_childDocuments_.name: Unto The End

_childDocuments_.review: This is my first review and I am writing it because all these negative reviews are unfair to the game. In short this is a a good game made with evident love and carefulness by a very small independent developer.In line with its' general vibe, the game is meant to feel dangerous and dark. You, alone, trying to not die and get back home safely. Many complain about the combat system but I find very appropriate it to be unforgiving. It may seem impossible at first glance but then there is almost always a trick or a simple sequence to learn in order to defeat the enemy. Impatience will only get you killed. Also, many combat situations can be avoided: for example you can just roll and run away (that is what I did many times in my first play-through). On top of that, the visuals and the sounds are nice.I just hope that the developers will expand what they made maybe with more stories you can choose from because it does feel a bit short (for me at least).
_childDocuments_.name: Unto The End

_childDocuments_.review: This game should get a very positive review rating!Basically you are an ordinary human warrior. No special powers, no level progressing, no combos. You can jump as a normal human jump, you can bleed out, you become 3 hits and died.So the game is very realistic, but this is a fantasy game. In the depths of the snowy caves you must survive against orcs, trolls, and other beasts. No handholding, no mercy. It feels like a game from the 90's. Impressive. The sound effects, OMG! So terrifying!Yes, it's a little short, but: there are multiple optional paths, secrets, 3 different endings, and (after 2 walkthrough) an old warrior mode, where you must beat the game with 1 life! You can even beat the game without killing anybody!If you want to see everything, and get all achievements, beat on old warrior mode, it will took at least 30 hours!It's a very memorable experience, just get it!
_childDocuments_.name: Unto The End

_childDocuments_.review: Good and deliberate gameplay that ties in with the story and the mood of the game. Combat easy to grasp hard to master, can get a bit tiring (after all you are just some dude fighting your way back home) but the game isn't long enough for it to cause fatigue (which is good). Won't be for everyone tho.
_childDocuments_.name: Unto The End

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE: I have finished the game now, I stand by what I said here 100% but would like to add also that the nonviolent options in the game and the variety in encounters is also super good. Well worth buying, do not listen to negative reviewsOk so I haven't played much of this game yet, but I want to very specifically counter a common complaint in some negative reviewsThe enemy AI does NOT cheat, and it is NOT unreactable.What people who have left these reviews describe is part of the combo system, enemies have combos they do and you cannot interrupt them consistently. You're supposed to block their combo, or dodge a high attack, using the shoulder check or the knife are not consistent combo breakers because...that's not how the combat system work. The game tells you this if you go through the tutorial. Those reviewers are being stubborn about how they think the game SHOULD play instead of just learning the combat system, and it's kinda frustrating.As far as reacting to the combos go, you can use a timer to count the startup, most wind up animations are pushing half a second in length. Average visual reaction time is 140 ms, or .14 seconds. You have nearly triple that to react, you can do it. My reactions are below average by a long shot, and I can react to all the tells I've seen in game, and I've even looked up late game enemies online and can react to their tells just fine.I'll update my review if my opinion changes, but at least for now the game is tense, gorgeous, and has a really thought provoking combat system I am enjoying learning and strategizing around. Will definitely play more, and I definitely think it deserves a higher rating
_childDocuments_.name: Unto The End

_childDocuments_.review: It's a shame this game has mixed reviews. It's a great game that doesn't give itself enough time to breath. The challenging combat puts folks off where I think they would appreciate if given time to acclimate. Art direction and sound are also great. I'm greatly looking forward to what this two person dev team dreams up next.
_childDocuments_.name: Unto The End

_childDocuments_.review: Simple yet incredibly hard combat that focuses on timing and defense.  Enemies have limited move sets but are not hardwired into which moves they use, as well as quickly adapting to your own movement choices, so each fight varies greatly from the next (even if you have to replay the same fight several times).A lot of hard work as gone into this game and it takes just as much work to eventually master this innocently (and seemingly) simple game.
_childDocuments_.name: Unto The End

_childDocuments_.review: Little masterpiece, recommend going into the game without any pre-constructions and enjoy the experience. However if you wish for a quick overview, see below...Visuals and sound is beautiful, the atmosphere amazing, the combat is satisfying and 'weighty. Important to understand that the combat is very challenging and you will die multiple times, but once you get into the rhythm of the game, you are in for a gaming experience like no other.You can feel the love and attention that has poured into the game and with each playthrough (currently done my 4th) you unlock subtle little details of the world that has been created.A little masterpiece!!
_childDocuments_.name: Unto The End

_childDocuments_.review: Things I liked: It's very simplistic visual style and storytelling that doesn't rely on cut scenes to be engaging, the lack of a leveling system and simple inventory is actually really refreshing, and there are a few really cool interactions where you don't need to kill every single "enemy" creature. Simple fighting mechanics that were annoying at first but I grew to like.Things I didn't like: The controls can be a little stiff and foreground objects get in the wayI recommend taking your time with everything in this game, especially the combat. Play the sparring practice tutorial early on and until you can win reliably and the rest of the game will be much more fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Unto The End

_childDocuments_.review: It is a very original game, although taking references from other games, it creates almost its own genre. A nice cinematic experience. Very hard though. It is not easy to react against enemies that has good AI. So you have to die a few times per combat until figure out how to approach or attack the enemy. Overall a totally solid game from an indie studio. Lots of work went into it obviously. Definitely worth the price and surely a one time experience of a game. Verdict:Artstyle: 9/10Audio Design: 10/10Gameplay: 9/10Story: 8/10 (although no text, its visually told)Combat: 8/10 (probably 9 with a controller)Overall: 9/10My only criticism would be it has an annoying combat for people who has keyboard. Its hard to use Ctrl, shift, q all together, they are pretty important moves. Even fake move. And you can't bind the keys, they are fixed. So i didnt really enjoy combats as if i had chance to reallocate keys or have a controller.Anyways, very solid game. Buy and support such games instead of million dollar games with no soul.
_childDocuments_.name: Unto The End

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the Demo version and bought released game straight away.But it is so annoying to play! No map, always dark, not really responsive control. Movement glitches and unresponsive control is especially painful in a game when everyone can one-shot you.The idea was great, and fights are great in some cases. But I'm really disappointed in the final product.
_childDocuments_.name: Unto The End

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game. It has a great atmosphere and many unique concepts (trading, avoiding fights, etc). Nice artwork and character design too. They convey a lot of information to the player with very little data given. However, the combat and movement is just broken. It's clunky and awkward. I found myself frustrated more than happy playing. The game is also extremely short making it not worth the $25 price tag. I felt like the world they showed us was just scratching the surface of what they had created. It could have been expanded on greatly providing many more hours of game play.
_childDocuments_.name: Unto The End

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know what to say other than, the first playthrough was infuriating. I almost lost my voice at how much I was yelling. The second playthrough involved a some yelling, but not as much. The next three playthroughs I was calm and collected the whole time.It's a great game. Your first playthrough will probably be about two hours, which may seem short, but the game is actually the perfect length .I will address the combat. It is insane. Enemies react far too quickly... Sort of. What I found was that the enemies you can skip are the ones that react really fast. The enemies that you have to defeat to complete the game take some getting used to, but can be taken care of easily with enough practice. I completely understand the criticism that this game gets for it's combat but really it's just the type of thing you have to learn, and most combat is avoidable, especially in the second half of the game. I understand there is a mode that slows down combat. I never tried it, but that is there to help you as well if you need it.This game is reminiscent of the early Nintendo games where a lot of the game involves memorization, and that might be something that newer gamers aren't used to. It takes practice and learning from your mistakes and you can do it.In conclusion, I'd say try it if you like any kind of a challenge. It's also got great visuals and sound design to match.
_childDocuments_.name: Unto The End

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game, very original, with a great atmosphere. For me it is like a combination of Inside and Dark Souls. The combat is very hard but it is very well done, it feels realistic, you feel like the violence and the action is because you are surviving, and some times you can avoid it. It is not some mindless action game like most are.  You can also help others from others tribes you find along the way. It is a simple, but beautiful, compact experience. It should have more recognition in my opinion. It is one of my favorites games of the year. Great job to the developers and thanks.
_childDocuments_.name: Unto The End

_childDocuments_.review: its a legitimate Adventure Game with the best 2d sword combat I have played. Music and Art Didn't really excel my enjoyment of the game they are in the foreground while the games main focus is on enemy animations and combat/exploration gameplay. You should go into this as blind as possible summed up think its like a Limbo/Zelda game with a branching story similar to The Stanly Parable. the sword combat and monster designs is what really pushes this game into a must Buy.
_childDocuments_.name: Unto The End

_childDocuments_.review: I understand how the devs wanted this to be a high stakes game, and you can see they unmistakably did put effort in it. If you're in because of the atmosphere and visual storytelling, probably you'll like it.But if you're also looking for a rewarding combat experience, give this one a hard pass. It's just bad. The isolated elements are great, but when put together they do not work.Combat surely sound awesome when you read the description. It has directional blocking, bashing and counter attacks. All winner features, right? Combat should feel awesome!Unfortunately it doesn't. Its purposed difficulty comes almost exclusively from clunkyness. It feels locked and imprecise. The fact you can't see barely anything due to the darkness of the setting just makes everything worse. Also your character drops his weapon like he's not even trying to hold it. Maybe the disparity of expectations v. actual game is due to it being lauded as a Souls like game, because it lacks in every aspect that makes Souls games' combat great.Souls games make you ragequit. But you come back to git gud because it's fun. This game you close because you feel like wasting time, and not compelled to click its icon again.
_childDocuments_.name: Unto The End

_childDocuments_.review: Now is playable, and if you are still having issues play at 50% speed, it will make combat less infuriating.They should had used 75% and 50%. I guess they went for 50% and 25% speed because they were extremely fed up with all the complains.MY only complaint, the 3 endings are ♥♥♥♥♥♥. Even for a short game, a little more effort next time.
_childDocuments_.name: Unto The End

_childDocuments_.review: Worth while journey full of challenge. Combat starts of tricky, but you'll soon get the hang of it, making it very rewarding. And if you find yourself at a particularly hard spot, look around and assess the situation, because often combat is not the only way to move forward. That's one thing that  really stood out for me with Unto the End, the fact that you could trade, fight or just run away from whatever it throws at you. In the end, the goal is not to slaughter things in front of you, but to make your way home any way possible. Having said that there are two endings to the game and each require certain key decisions from you. I finished the first run, which took about 4 hours and immediately started over. Unto The End is a great little game that deserves more love. If you're up for a fun and challenging experience, please do check it out.
_childDocuments_.name: Unto The End

_childDocuments_.review: This is a different take on a side-scrolling action game.  The dev says Punch-Out! was an influence on the game's combat and it shows. You need to read enemy tells, remember their favorite combos, and know whether to block with your sword or dodge by jumping/ducking.  It feels unique in the side-scrolling genre and usually works pretty well.I like the art style. It's simple but effective. It doesn't elevate the combat though. Sometimes it's tough to read the enemies since everyone is small and gray.  A zooming camera or larger characters would help. I couldn't play this at all on a 1080p TV from my couch but I was able to read the game well on a 1440p desktop setup.There's a light layer of story stuff in there - you can avoid fights by offering items to some folks and you're often stumbling onto battles that other humans aren't even involved in.  It's a mood-enhancer for the journey.If you like 2D action games (and Punch-Out!), give it a shot.
_childDocuments_.name: Unto The End

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting premise, but unpolished to the point of unplayability. Controls feels slow, unresponsive and weird, which is bad for a game which relies on its complex combat system. Difficulty is often too hard because of the controls and many important things like the option to avoid fights altogether is poorly communicated. Plus on many occasions the game takes over control of the character for a sort of cutscene, which breaks immersion and is a poor design choice, especially for the ending. With more polish and smarter game design, this could have been a great game, but not like this. I on PC also hat weird lagging sometimes when the screen scrolls and oftentimes the character kept walking for a while even though I released the stick.
_childDocuments_.name: Unto The End

_childDocuments_.review: This is an adventure platformer game. It is definitely recommended to play with a controller, you will have a hard time playing with keyboard.The game is different because you get to choose either to spare or kill anyone on your way. The combat is difficult though, you can die very easily or you can kill your enemy very easy if you do the right move.I'd recommend Unto the End to those who seek for a different experience in a platformer game.
_childDocuments_.name: Unto The End

_childDocuments_.review: I was very interested when I saw some footage of this game last week. There are a lot of things that I really like about it. Graphics, sound, and atmosphere are all great. The combat is brutally difficult. I think it's interesting, but not fun. There were one or two spots where I died at least 20 times trying to get past, and I even turned the slow combat on to get past a spot or two. I'm no stranger to difficult games, but this isn't even satisfying when you DO triumph over your opponent. When I get past a very tough enemy I rarely feel like I've learned anything, but rather that I just got lucky. Most of the enemies are significantly faster and stronger than you are. No big deal at first, but when you're stuck fighting someone who has unblockable one shot attacks it's just not fun. I guess I can't stress that enough where I'm at right now. The first hour or so was enjoyable, but I kind of hate myself every time I fire this game up for a few minutes to try and get past wherever I'm currently stuck.Edit: turns out I was finally stuck at the final fight. Unfortunately I've hated this game for the last three hours of play time, and now that I've seen the end (on YouTube) I can uninstall it and never touch it again. I really wish I would have waited to read some reviews before playing it. I really like supporting indie devs, and upon hearing it was a super small team I wanted to support it. As much as I appreciate the style and atmosphere I couldn't recommend this to anyone.
_childDocuments_.name: Unto The End

_childDocuments_.review: Buy it on sale.I had a great time with this game, the visuals are great and the combat and platforming was challenging and fun.But it is way too short for its price-tag.The game also has an issue of a severe lack of context for whats going on, why its happening, and what you're able to do in many situations.
_childDocuments_.name: Unto The End

_childDocuments_.review: - Unique art style that grabs your attention- Challenging- You actually have to learn combat system- Makes me want to rage quit but I can't help continuously throwing myself at enemies like cannon fodder.Overall a very interesting and challenging side-scroller with a beautifully dark and damp immersive art style that I would recommend to anyone even if they are not a fan of the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Unto The End

_childDocuments_.review: I really appreciate the artistry and the vision that went into this game. I personally loved the combat after hearing it explained by the developer in a live stream and reading the sticky post on Steam. I totally get what they were going for and, for the most part, I think it works really well. I actually wish there was much more. Each encounter was like a challenging puzzle figuring out how to time blocks and attacks, which I personally much prefer to hack-and-slash or souls style roll-and-slash. I wish the devs could somehow communicate their intentions with combat better in the game itself; I consider their post in the Steam Discussion required reading to get the most out of this game.Some things are frustrating. I think the game would be better with the bleed mechanic completely removed. There were too many times I won a battle, only to wander around and die 60 seconds later. Effectively, it just gives me one less hitpoint, since I'll just suicide myself if I know I'll probably bleed out even if I win the encounter. I didn't understand how armor worked, and while most of the checkpoints were generously placed, I ended up not finishing the game because of a frustrating checkpoint near the end.Sound, atmosphere, visuals - all top notch. You can really feel that your character isn't a heroic knight. His breathing, the weight of the sword, the threat of the encounters - all land really well.It's really great to see small indie teams put out games that try something new and pursue the kind of vision that doesn't shine in bigger productions. Great job.Ultimately, though, I'm not recommending it because there's a checkpoint nearing the end of the game that is just too frustrating - not challenging, but very far from two very difficult encounters. I like the challenge of combat in this game, but you need to design it so I can actually practice the fights.
_childDocuments_.name: Unto The End

_childDocuments_.review: This game is objectively bad.There are so many design decisions here that are simply just baffling. I've watched the developer commentaries, they are part of what interested me about this game, and you can tell that the developers had a specific vision in mind and were passionate about the project. However, the actual execution lacks any real understanding of what makes a game enjoyable.First, the good. The game creates an intriguing and compelling atmosphere. The visuals and sound, for the aesthetic they're going for, are done well. It's mercifully brief. (~2 hours depending how good you are at fighting)The bad.The fighting, the design (mechanics and UI), and the story (haha).Let's start with the story. There isn't one. There's no narrative. The game says that you're trying to get back to your family, but the very start of the game you're with your family and then you just leave. With no reason for leaving. Like nothing. You just walk away and that's the game. I'm all for games not holding your hand and giving clues to the narrative through gameplay rather than exposition, but this was ridiculous. There was absolutely no purpose instilled in the player. Like, why do I care if this guy gets back to his family? I don't know him or them, there's literally nothing that occurs that makes me want to get back to them or play the game. Then when you get to the end (spoiler, not spoiler), the game just ends, like you're walking on a hill and then credits. Like, that was it? I guess I got back home, but there was no indication along the way to show progress, like it's just through this cave, or over this hill, or something. Just not there and now there. Okay, fun. And this lack of purpose, makes the frustrating things we'll discuss next, all the more frustrating. Like why am I putting myself through this misery, what's the carrot you're dangling for me? It's nothing. Hence why there is no reason to play this.There are aspects to the design that make no sense to me. The absent aforementioned story is one part of this, but they've also done away with any type of HUD, there isn't even a start screen. The game literally just begins, no context, no options to select, nothing. Throughout the game there are no cues to things like health or stamina (which may or may not exist in this game, I never figured it out), where items are located, nothing. Your guy may breathe more when he's injured, but he always kinda breathes heavy, so it's hard to tell. Also, am I hurt, tired, near death, scrapped knee, you don't know. There are a number of items throughout the game, but there is little to no visual indication where they are, so I spent the entire game just constantly pressing the LB button seeing if there was something to pick up. That's poor design.The visuals are simply too dark and too obscured to be enjoyable. Your guy is constantly in dark caves, wandering a labrynth with no map, while 75% of the screen obscured by foreground stuff. It's like I'm watching my character from 200 feet away through a tube. Great at creating a stiffling and oppressive atmosphere, terrible at making a game enjoyable to play.Finally the fighting, which is supposed to be a selling point of the game, is both too simple and too complex at the same time. It's built off a basic defend high/low, attack high/low mechanic (you know, like what they did 35 years ago in Zelda II), but also includes things like feints, rolls, and ripostes.  While not the worst part of the game, it still felt very frustrating and relied more on trial and error, and brute force, than skill of execution. There is also a difficulty curve, where you can slow down the fights to 75% or 50% speed. While this sometimes helped, the way it was implemented was bizarre, rather than just slowing down the entire fight, it creates a bubble of slowed time around you and the enemy, so sometimes a roll would take you out of the bubble and suddenly you're moving at full speed, but they are not. Or vice-versa for some of the enemy's lunge attacks. Which really makes for a janky feeling in the fight. Overall it serves it's purpose, but the difficulty is not balanced and not enjoyable. This current trend of hard equals good needs to end. A good game has depth to it's combat, this is more like a rhythm game, where you just have to master quick time events, but rather than button prompts, it's memorizing split-second visual cues (from 200 ft away, in the dark, while obscured) so you can defend high/low. Each fight left me drained and frastrated, not elated and empowered. Oh, and you can drop your sword, and your guy does it ALL.THE.TIME. Get hit, drop your sword, roll too close to a wall, drop your sword, block an attack that's too strong, drop your sword. Maybe that's "realistic," but that doesn't make it fun.There is also an option to skip many fights, but again, this is all trial and error, you're not sure always which fights you can do this for, and you're not sure what to offer them to appease them. Sometimes what you offer makes them angrier and the fight still happens, so it's just trial and error to see what works. In all, this game is very missable. The simple balance of enjoyment to challenge is not in your favor.

_childDocuments_.review: Unto the end may be short, but its made by two passionate developers who clearly have a lot they want to say about games as a medium. In Unto the end you play as a father who has been separated from his family attempting to hunt a deer, resulting in him having to make a long and treacherous journey home through an active warzone. You must put what little defensive skills and survival knowledge you know to the test, along with every ounce of reflexes and perception. This is reinforced by gameplay in ways that, honestly may not initially seem super player-friendly. In similar games, you would simply power through tougher and tougher waves of enemies. Here that isn't the case: You will die and die and die,  grinding against tougher and tougher enemies with unintuitive attack patterns, if you even think about plowing through headfirst. And although you can master the combat (with some difficulty given a certain amount of jank), that isnt exactly the point. Slowly you will begin to see fighting as a last-ditch effort, reserved only to aid in escape; this perception is reinforced by the types scenarios the gameplay creates: desperately leaping out of the way of attacks, struggling to find your knife and sword in the snow, and hearing your flimsy crafted armour snap easily after massive effort spent collecting materials. Other than running away, the game is also an exercise in communication, leaving the most rewarding and beneficial outcomes for those who face beasts who speak another language, despite the possibility of attack. It creates an experience in which starting a fight is far outweighed by even the possibility of peace. This is alien for games, but an important part of the human condition. Kindness, cowardice, and ruthlessness, are choices that are made in a context of shared struggle felt by the protagonist and the beasts.Unfortunately the initial friction many have had with the controls and combat mechanics (which appear to be the main draw at first, hence "dark souls-esc"), have turned people away from the game, or at least some of its more interesting implications. The length also leaves some to be desired, the concepts dont have that much room to grow, or truly find any kind of conclusion. This is compounded by the fact that these concepts are interrupted by navigating maze-like corridors and attempting to decode the precise offerings and order to receive a special item, re-orienting the experience to be recognizably "game-like". With all that being said, a very interesting first title from a passionate team, and I hope they continue to get the opportunity to explore their ideas further.

_childDocuments_.review: To look at it, you'd never guess that this is a garage-band game. The simple visuals make this throwback side-scroller feel authentic, with the advantage of non-MIDI music. The plot is straight forward and doesn't get distracted by side-quests, puzzles or even dialogue. If you're not into challenges (to your skill or patience, either one), don't pick this one up. That said, if you're that 80s gamer who excels at figuring out the enemy's attack pattern (and you've got the reflexes of a much younger person) try it. Be warned that if, unlike me, you breeze through every encounter, this game is going to feel about 3 seconds long from start to finish.All in all, I enjoyed this. Made me nostalgic for the old DOS game 'Death Sword'.

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game on sale, and thank god for that, because this has to be one of the shortest games I've ever played. I'm not saying a lot of time and love didn't go into this, but a $15 price tag for a 2.5 hour game is a bit ridiculous. Personally, I'd say $9.99 would be a fair price, but it is what it is...Honestly, this game will be a hit or miss for people. Combat is pretty difficult and unforgiving (even on the easiest mode/50% speed). The atmosphere, artwork, level design and visuals are top-notch, but some of the foreground, especially in caves, may annoy certain players. While I liked it, because it gave a sense of claustrophobia, others may dislike it. Some of the puzzles are a bit... strange, as well. Like, why do you give one shaman bones and the other herbs? There really wasn't a reason or story behind it. Felt random. Also, controls can be a bit wonky at times. The devs went for a level of realism, too. You drop your torch, your sword, have to pick every item up... while this is neat, it can get a bit annoying. You also move at a VERY slow pace, and some scenes are drug out for dramatic effect. This is OK, but it does feel like "walking simulator" at times.Overall, I like the vision the developers had here, and the game is beautifully done. Sadly, it's way too short to really feel any sense of adventure, there's little to no story, the ending was just "meh" (unless there are multiples), and I can see more people disliking the game than liking it. While I enjoyed it for the most part, maybe watch a game play video a bit before buying. This may be your cup of tea, or a game that makes you want to break your computer monitor with your controller.As for my rating... if I could go neutral, I would. I'm giving it a thumbs up because I enjoyed it, but definitely research the game a bit before you spend your money.

_childDocuments_.review: I LOVE this game!  Man, I had no idea what I was in for, but it's been really awesome!  The overall aesthetic is incredible and so much fun.  The sound design in particular really just gives it such an awesome atmosphere, but coupled with lighting and overall graphics and it's just perfect - so nicely atmospheric!  This alone makes it worth it, but there's so much more to it than just the cinematic aspects.The gameplay loop is a ton of fun too.  I'm starting my third playthrough (the one where you're supposed to make it through without dying at all - not so easy!), so I've taken enough different approaches now to say that they're all fun.  Just the right pacing between exploring, figuring things out, and fighting for your life (often difficult until you get the hang of it - and sometimes even when you do get the hang of it). No real words in the whole game, though some creatures do communicate verbally, if that makes sense. And yet the plot still feels very meaningful, especially by the time you get the couple different endings.  (Can't speak for the third ending yet).  But being able to choose whether you want to fight, run, help, ignore, or bargain - I don't know, there's just something about having that freedom that really helps with the immersion.The whole thing is quite short.  If you're really good and know what you're doing, you can probably get through in an hour.  My first playthrough was like 3.5 hours because I spent a fair bit of back and forth on figuring out the combat or figuring out my options in a given encounter.  My second playthrough was still about the same, haha, mainly because I was working on trying different achievements, etc.  Not sure how long my last one will be, but considering I have to make it through without dying once, it'll likely be a bit fast, as I'm going to try to run away from every battle, haha!  We'll see.  Already died on one platforming element fairly early on (that I should've just been a bit more patient with), so I'll have to give it another go.All that to say: this game is short and incredibly rewarding.  Very much worth it.  If you only want to play short games, you can't lose with this one.  If you generally don't think short games are worth it - well, I'd say this one still probably is, because the multiple playthroughs are fun each time (so far anyway).  Really just a great and memorable gaming experience that I think just about anyone is going to want to have.
