_childDocuments_.review: Anyone who has worn out their copies of every XCOM game, as I have, knows there is not a wealth of new games in the genre. I appreciate what the Romeros are trying to bring to the table with Empire of Sin, but for now the game falls short in core aspects of execution. Hopefully, this will someday be a game that I feel gives me my money's worth. 2/5 stars.Last month I bought and completed Hard West, a game I greatly enjoyed for its combat mechanics and level design. A few days after my interest in HW ran its course, I saw Empire of Sin in the store. It seemed to promise a lot of the things I loved about games like XCOM and HW, but with an innovative scalable strategy layer and an emergent narrative based on 1920's Prohibition Chicago. Being a Paradox game I somewhat expected it to come out half-baked with a ton of issues, but this is a rare effort at an XCOM competitor and Paradox are generally good about supporting games for a long time.I hope that continued support is the case here, because the tactical gameplay in this game gets old very quickly. At the outset the game shows a ton of promise, in 3 attempts at starting a campaign so far my favorite part each time was the solo missions at the beginning. The "boss" character of your gang really lives up to this name, and taking down 5 or 8 enemy thugs in just a few turns is a great introduction to the combat system. After taking over a few rackets, earning a few made henchmen, then assaulting a rival gang's safehouse to overpower their leader and seize their territory, you can really immerse in the game's promise of being a criminal overlord with an empire.What follows is where the game becomes bogged down in itself. Running multiple gang wars when you own a sprawling empire is an exercise in tedium. Your racket guards are hopelessly inept at lower levels, and when a racket is raided by the enemy you're ripped away from your boss character and are stuck controlling "60 hp woman with lead pipe" or "55 hp man with short-barreled shotgun", typically against an equally inept force of random enemy thugs. Then, when your guards lose you immediately get to repeat the experience inside your racket.The tedious gang wars also highlight the repetitiveness of the different buildings. Each building can be "small", "medium" or "large" and the interiors of each racket type do not vary much. So, in a short span the game goes from being a very enjoyable stint as the baddest guy in town, to fighting through a hopeless slog with no-name characters in the same environments over, and over, and over. This is not an enjoyable experience for a turn-based shooter.The strategy layer provides more scale than depth, which would certainly be forgivable if the combat sequence was more engaging. Owning 30+ rackets in a neighborhood, each with 20+ upgrade levels, with 10 neighborhoods as default, quickly becomes a chore when the ultimate outcome is that each time you make slightly more profit or the guard battles become slightly less tedious due to upgrades. Immediate improvements to the tactical layer that I would suggest are:-Make the player character and their made men essential to the core game mechanic: turn-based tactics. It is not as enjoyable to fight battles where they are not involved, and these should be automated 100% of the time. It might be workable to give the player a way for responding to such events, such as posting made men at the neighborhood safehouse and having them immediately respond to help the guards against any raids in that neighborhood.-Make combat involvement mostly line-of-sight based rather than area based. Having a random group of thugs in an alley around the block or a faraway policeman become mandatory elements of combat because they were within X tiles of the ambush is never an enjoyable surprise.-The controls sequence for fighting battles with a controller is not intuitive to work through, and sometimes limits player options compared to KB+M. In my opinion, XCOM: Chimera Squad is the gold standard of intuitive controller support in the tactical layer and I think it would be a good thing if this game had a similar controls sequence.-Speaking of XCOM:CS, their breach system was a fantastic innovation in the genre. I think that a similar mechanic for raids in Empire of Sin would provide a sorely-needed breath of fresh air to the short roster of interior combat environments. Breaching from outside in would also help solve the disconnect between the outdoor and indoor environments in this game, which at present feel like different worlds (see: no-name guard battle progression).

_childDocuments_.review: Empire of Sin.... a 1920's prohibition / mafia themed, x-com-like strategy game that has a lot of potential but at the time of this review (about 39 hours of play time) I simply cannot recommend the game in it's current state. This game should have released into Early Access. The cons at this timely, simply outweigh the pros.Pros :- Game looks nice and plays smoothly- Mafia theme- Varied characters to choose as your boss / avatar- Nice variety of weapons- Gangster Roster - plenty of minor characters to choose from as your hired thugs- Music / Soundtrack really fits the themeCons :- Too many bugs and glitches for a full release- Unbalanced abilities - Repetitive combat at times when the AI attacks and you have to complete fight after fight- Game mechanics too bare bones- AI needs working on- Mission / quests badly paced outThis game has only been out for a couple of weeks but really needs some patching. Fun enough to play, assuming you can get past all it's current faults. Current recommendation : wait for a sale and/or for the game to be fully patched / updated before buying.Rating : 5/10 Average (but on the bit disppointing side).POST PATCH :  Devs have done some work to this game so it's time to change my review a bit :Pros : - Safe Houses are now hidden and you can't bum rush your rivals any more :)- A lot of the quests seem to work fine now- The "loot boxes" you can find all over the map have been re-balanced and are more rare- 12 different 'skins' for all the generic thugs makes for a better experience, rather than all 1 generic type- weapons and bosses have been nerfed a bit and difficulties have been adjusted- Ability to skip 'non essential' fights- Guards get better 'upgrades' for each upgrade levelCons :- Rackets are still a bit bare bones - need more variety- Animations of the in game models still bug out from time to time- Quests still seem to be assigned all together 'in a bunch' rather than spaced out more- Some bugs for first version of the game still persisting- AI still needs some workOverall, the new patch shows alot of promise. I hope the devs continue supporting and working on this game. It definately has improved since launch, but there still is a fair amount to do for it to be a truly GREAT game.New Rating : 6 / 10 - still wait for a sale or for further patching,

_childDocuments_.review: WAY TOO EXPENSIVE SHOULD BE EATitle says it all. At its current state, the game is way too expensive. I wouldn't give more than 15, maybe 20 euros for it. I have played early access games who where cheaper and with less bugs than this game! A shame, because in essence it is a fun and nice game. If it were an EA title and around 20 euros, then this game would be a good start and recommended. I like the graphics and the gameplay is okay. Has a nice feel to it. But seeing that there are already two DLC's announced, the game looks more like a money cow than a good game which was ready for launch. And I was really looking forward for this game. I played Gangland (2004) for those who know the game. Very similar to this one. But unfortunately I feel like Gangland was a better game than Empire of Sin, and we are talking about a 16 year old game...Pro's and Con's:Pro's- Nice graphics. Set a good atmosphere and ambiance- Nice music/sound- Selection of bosses is good (with their own traits and abilities)- Quite a few neighbourhoods/districts to take over- Seemingly a lot of missions and side missions (can also be a con, for sometimes it feels like you are drowning in missions and side missions and therefore preoccupied from taking over other NPC's and/or businesses and neighbourhoods- Combat has some decent options and ways to go about. AI is not that good though...Con's- Way too many bugs for a full release game- Way too expensive at current state (Also taken into account the two DLC's that are already announced and probably will cost too much as well...)- Game quickly becomes a bit repetitive - There is a tutorial but much is left to be explored by yourself (can also be a pro to some I suppose)- Unrealistic and frankly unclear economics (also seem quite shallow)- Really, really and than I mean really easy AI. Not that much challenge- Management aspect of the game really falls short.- Very, very little choice of rackets (when you take over a building and need to convert it into something)Like I wrote, if the game were EA and/or cheaper and if the devs make a fair ammount of (free!) updates, additions and bug fixes, than the game would be definitely be recommended. But for now, it's a no.

_childDocuments_.review: The boss I picked has an ability that lets him run to someone and perform 3 melee strikes; if he gets a kill his AP is refunded and he gets a pretty serious stacking movement/melee skill debuff.  Despite the debuff, I can pretty much always use the ability twice in a row at the start of every fight and instakill two enemies with it.  Once I got him a blue machine gun, I could then blow away a third guy with his refunded AP, no matter where he ends up.  This means every single fight starts with me doing the exact same thing with my boss which gets me 3 kills on one turn 99% of the time.  This tends to leave my boss standing out in the open somewhere, but since he has 2-3 times as much health as everyone else and the generic thugs are incredibly weak and stupid (even on hard difficulty), this doesn't actually matter.  Of course, once a gang war started, I did get to start playing fights where my properties were attacked and I had to fight back with 2-3 generic-ass boring guards, which was even worse.  Seriously, these generic guards can't get above like 55% hit chance even under optimal conditions, which means your generic thugs and the enemy's generic thugs just sit there and blast away at each other for 10 minutes.  Boring.I think this game has a lot of potential and if they hit it with some patches that improve it I will revise this review, but right now the business management part is confusing and not very rewarding, the RPG management is wonky, the UI is clunky and hard to navigate, and the tactical combat is repetitive and easy.

It is incredibly unbalanced, resulting in a strategy game that requires no strategy.1. AI will accept absurd trades. There are a lot of exploits that stem from this issue.2. You can trade for the AI faction's unique weapons and they'll never equip another one, leaving them weaponless in battle.3. Quick travel takes no time. This allows you to explore the whole map, meet all of the factions, and collect all hidden stashes in one in-game week.4. Stashes are on the map from the start of the game. This makes the game trivial. Collect a few good stashes, equip your team, kill every enemy. Why interact with rackets, synergies, trade-deals, or quests?5. Healing can be done instantly by quick travel to safehouse, which costs nothing. It can also be done using skills by starting an ambush, using healing skill, cancelling ambush, and repeating. This makes the doctor passive heal pointless.6. Weapon type traits can be earned by accumulating kills and thugs are crazy easy to kill and plentiful.7. Rifles shadow sniper rifles by doing similar damage for 1 AP instead of 2 AP. Same with Submachine guns and Machine guns. Shotguns spead shot has the same accuracy and damage as the single-target shot. Why even have a single-target shot? Just use the multi-target one every time.8. Explosives (excluding time-bomb) have no counter-play. Spawn into a fight, enemy gets their first turn, throws bomb into the pack where you spawned and you've lost multiple gangsters. All explosives should be timed or not an instant-kill.9. Better gang members shouldn't cost notoriety AND money. By the time you can hire the better gangsters, you've already trained up your cheap gangsters to be very strong. Additionally, 10% income cost is insane enough, but another $30,000-$70,000 on top of that? Never going to be worth it.1. No window-borderless option in 2020. Single person made early access games even have this.2. The hotkeys are dynamic and it screws me up constantly. One minute the [3] key is swap weapon, the next minute [4] is swap weapon and [3] is reload. This screws me up CONSTANTLY. Please make these static.3. The Escape key unpausing the game is annoying. I'm just trying to bring the menu up to save and you unpause it and then something always manages to pop-up at that very second. Let me bring up the menu while paused.1. Repetitive dialog option variety. I am tired of hearing Al Capone say "What's this a free lunch?" I don't need variety for everything, but the dialog options that are common, like making a deal, should have some variety.2. Thugs are all the same, weak and boring. Add more enemy types, both graphically and mechanically. They don't have to be strong, since they're thugs, but at least have them do something different.3. I would like to see more depth added to mechanics around rackets. Hotel synergy is nice when it works. Add more things like this.4. No more DLC weapons. Those things are OP and I would love an option to make them basic guns instead of legendary, aka basically a weapon skin instead.I'm going to keep playing this game. It can be enjoyable, but commonly comes with frustration. Please fix the bugs and balance!

_childDocuments_.review: First of all. This game is awesome. It's been torn to bits on different YouTube channels, "official reviews"  etc.) and in some forums, but I genuinely think it's got a bad rap for no reason. Firstly the concept is great. Who wouldn't want to run their own (virtual) crime business? You're your own boss, and you can be as kind or as ruthless as you want, with some obvious repercussions. But essentially you build your own culture within a mob and then you execute according to that culture. The fighting system is strategic, and more along the lines of Humankind's turn-based fighting brand. It's tactical and immersive, and despite playing 22 hours so far where probably 12 of that was fighting, I've enjoyed every minute of it. Despite the pain of losing some brave soldiers :'(. This game does have some improvements to make however. I think we were all expecting some more depth when it comes to distribution and supply lines. More opportunities to include battles of attrition. More variety in building styles, decor and upgrades and more "rackets" (illegal activities). But I imagine, more will be added to the game with each update, and I expect to see a lot more work put into this game, just because it's Paradox and they usually pay attention to their communities. All-in-all, a 6.5/10, but for me an 8/10. It has a lot of room for growth from a strategic point of view as there are some additional complexities I and the community are hoping for over time. But I genuinely love the game and currently, this is the only good one of its kind. Definitely buy, it's worth-it!

_childDocuments_.review: Short and sweet, save yourself $40-60. I really wanted to like this game. It had a lot of potential, but they missed the mark considerably.-There are significant, game breaking bugs at the moment. -The game is incredibly easy, even on the hardest difficulty.-Nothing you do in the game feels impactful or special.-The pacing of everything seems insanely fast, and the passage of time feels very disconnected from the gameplay. -You're not punished for your decisions, so there's no encouragement to think.-The game design and elements clash / lack synergy.-The music is really bad. (If you play The Godfather theme on repeat while you play it actually helps the game a lot though)In order to fix this game and make it interesting you would probably need not only a couple of good patches from the developer but most likely a player made overhaul- if that is even possible. A few thoughts of what I would do: Slow the game down considerably, make it dangerous to fight multiple factions and add opportunity costs to pretty much everything. Force characters to lay low after shooting in public, or taking over properties. Generally make me think more, feel more immersed, and make progress feel more rewarding and I'd be happy :)

If those bugs are fixed (there are definitely a lot more than just the game breaking one), the game would be better - but definitely still with a few things to improve. Some suggestions:- Add autoresolve for fights, as they get rather boring and same-ish after a while.- Add different game speeds, especially the first few hours you are just waiting on money, on gangsters healing, etc. It's almost like a free-to-play mobile game.- Add a quicksave function- Add a forward/skip dialogue button (also, some of those characters and their animation in dialogue are bonkers)- I don't want to have a sitdown and physically go to the other mob boss, every time I meet a new one or something changes between us. Give me the option to invite them to me, or to resolve a sitdown without phsyically having to walk the character there.There are definitely some more, but these are the main ones coming to mind. _childDocuments_.review: I really thought I was going to see and updated version of the old classic "Gangsters." Lets not forget that game was released over 20 years ago and was mostly watching little dots of your team colour moving round a gridwork "city" and grouping clunky looking still photographs of gangsters into specialist teams based on star ratings for their various qualities. Yet it still had more atmosphere and "feel" of running an underworld crime Empire than this aspires to. You would think 20 years would allow the creation of a truly sparkling game which matched eye candy with genuine hardcore crime empire management.  Instead you get a whole load of "Nos" in comparison. . No comparable team selection and building. No allocating time to the teams to go out on nefarious missions - Extorting businesses, tailing opponents, robbing businesses, making examples of anyone who crossed your path.No allocating turf to underbosses and managing their performance. No building territory by extortion. No smashing up, firebombing or intimidating foolish shop owners who wont hand over your cut. No buying up vacant lots, building "Front " Businesses and installing a Speakeasy, card game or loan shark in the cellar. No hiring an Accountant or Lawyer. No bribing Judges and Reporters. No intimidating jury members if your arrested Goodfellas are coming up on trial. No laundering money through Front businesses. No building stills and buying trucks to move hooch to the docks or your watering holes. No buying cars and weapons to tool up your hit squad for a drive by hit on a rival boss. No tailing his mooks to locate their head quarters and planning to dynamite it.Look at the string of things you could do to build your Empire on a game that ran on Windows 5 and 250 Mb of memory. Now consider this offering:No flavour, no atmosphere no Team or resource management to get your teeth into. Just four building types and selling various grades of liquor - to other Gangsters. Oh who cares? Turn based combat is based on "Omerta City of Gangsters" and is fairly facile. It is just dull and repetitive - I lost interest very quickly. I could live with a whole lot less chrome and with a lot more detailed management , money making options and atmosphere. If I can describe a twenty year old game with passion and happy reminiscences about its game play quality, you can imagine how gutted to see that if  Empire of Sin is anything to go by  the Gangster themed game has gone backwards instead of matching that style of game play with current visuals.Very very very disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: It has its flaws, but the flavor of the game is enjoyable. The combat is fun and not too difficult. The building up of your empire is enjoyable. But it hangs together pretty well, and it doesn't crash, and I wound up having fun goofing around with it. It's not a hard game, although they tried to make the 'Boss' level harder by changing it to have no auto-heal between fights. All this does is slow down the game, rather than make it harder or more fun. Meh. I've had 50 fun hours out of it, so I can recommend it as a casual tactical/economy type game.

_childDocuments_.review: A nice distraction before phoenix point. A great concept with nice graphics that suffers from what feels like a rushed release. Each boss feels different and the blend of turn based strategy with management is satisfying. However there are many glaring issues that will be listed and will hopefully be fixed. I unfortunately spent 70 dollars on this but I will not refund to support Romero games. Hopefully the dlc will fix the issues.- Glitches are pretty common. I killed an enemy boss that declared war on me and pulled in two other gangs against me. When I tried to make a truce, The sit down required that I talk to the dead boss. So all I could was walk into the building and do nothing. Another glitch that stagnated my mission progress required me to talk to a guard from a different gang. Too bad a completely different gang came in and murdered him so the quest marker was over a dead body. The only way to fix it was to take the place over and piss someone off.-Upgrades are way too expensive and take too long to finish. It's more beneficial to just exterminate the competition and take over all their territory when you murder their boss.- Enemy building types are not invisible to you. The first sit down also reveals the rival gang's safe house since it's hosted there for some reason. Guess who murdered the rival boss right after meeting them? Too weak to take them on immediately? That's okay cause you can fast travel to that rival gang's safe house at any point in the game and murder them. There's no hierarchy system so once that boss is gone that gang is done and all their stuff goes to you.- The enemy AI is pretty bad. Like throwing grenades at walls and constantly moving despite having a clear shot at me bad. If this were Xcom I would have lost a lot more territory since I never upgrade security. My security with only 3 people under my control can take on 5 enemies with only pistols and one double barrel shotgun.Regrettably this game is not worth the 40 dollars in its current state. It is entertaining so buy it 50% off.

_childDocuments_.review: Empire of Sin: Badaboom.Way back in the day of the forgotten PC demo, I played the snot out of Omerta: City of Gangsters. A clunkmaster of a game pushed out by Kalypso that died on the vine. But I did always like the concept of a game where you manage a criminal empire with XCOM stolen turned based combat. However the management was just Monopoly with extra steps and the turned based combat was jank. How do you fix a problem like that?John Romero, apparently. And giving the game about half a year to iron out the issues it had on launch.Empire of Sin is half crime syndicate management and half turned based combat where the game itself has a story that stretches for maybe half an hour and the rest is spent pummeling the AI for constantly starting gang wars with you. It hits the clicky part of my brain where I get sucked in and start slowly encroaching upon every district of Chicago and by the time I snap out of it, I have three districts on lock and it's 11:43 at night. I don't know how I got to this point but I certainly got there.It's not perfect. It still has the Omertas problem with the strategy starting to peter out by the late game. Once you get to a certain point, you don't have to worry about raids or anything and you have money to burn so you just buy and make criminal syndicates for funsies. Turned based combat is at least better with actual classes and weapons to choose from, and even the Rare guns aren't going to keep you from getting clapped if you aren't careful. The only con I can see is a lack of being able to drag your goons into fights, meaning you rely on the Black Book list of expensive hires to fill the blanks. And while I like the whole "like/hate" system requiring you to think before hiring 5 new expendable pawns, I'd like them to stop forming love triangles every 10 seconds. My criminal empire shouldn't entirely fall apart because of someone screwing someone else.If you want a good way to kill weekday nights and want to play a game that's half Monopoly and half XCOM with more jazz music and art deco everything, then Empire of Sins is your go-to game here. I would wait for it to go on sale however, as is the rules with any Paradox property. I'm glad it's at least now more functional then it was on launch, but still.

_childDocuments_.review: This game lacks content and will keep you busy for about 15-20 hours. After you took your first whole suburb, it´s repetitive and grindy. While combat and storytelling are very well implemented, the economy and diplomacy system is broken.You can completely ignore economy because you get all your income from combat. _childDocuments_.review: Definitely not as bad as people make it out to be but not perfect either. Gameplay is serviceable, if a little basic. There's really only 3 things you can do: Take over territory, build businesses, and manage your relationships with other factions. To take over territory, you have to send your crew to the enemy's depot, either taking out all their businesses first or dealing with a wave of reinforcements for every business they still have running. The combat is just a basic turn based system which is fine at first but gets boring after a while, which sucks considering you have to do at least 3 or 4 fights for each territory you want to take over (until the mid-game when your crew is so powerful you can basically rock up and take whatever you want). There is an "auto-resolve" button you can use to skip past the smaller fights, but there's always a chance that your entire crew will die so you'll basically never use it.Building businesses is about as exciting as it sounds; click on a building, choose what kind of business you want, and you're done. There are 4 types of businesses in the base game: Breweries, speakeasies, casinos and brothels. Breweries produce alcohol, speakeasies sell it, casinos sell half as much alcohol as speakeasies but generate a random amount of money per week, and brothels consume no alcohol but also make basically no money. With DLC you get access to loan sharks, which require a large investment up front but generate stupid amounts of money.Diplomacy, in my opinion, is where the game needs the most work. Your relationship with a faction is basically inconsequential. In the 20 hours I've played, nobody has ever declared war on me, no matter how bad our relationship was. I have never had my businesses raided by the police. None of my friends have ever joined me in a war I declared. The only useful aspect of diplomacy is trade, which you can use to buy alcohol or items from different bosses or, more often than not, just give all your excess items away for a huge opinion increase. If you have a good relationship with a faction you can have them assassinate literally anybody in the game and you can do this as much as you want, which is completely broken and I'm kind of shocked it made it into the final game.In short, the game is fine. Just fine. I picked it up hoping that it could capture at least a fraction of what Gangsters: Organized Crime did (since I can't get it to run on Windows 10) and it scratched that itch for a while, but I can begin to feel myself growing bored. If you're a nerd for prohibition era mafia stuff like I am, pick it up. But if you're not, maybe give it a pass.

_childDocuments_.review: I had hoped this game would be a modern version of Gangsters, the game from 2000 odd by Eidos, but its not even close. That on its own does not make it a bad game and it does have the potential to be a decent game, they just seem to have released in a pretty poor state. If you don't want to read further its not great just now, you could play it for a few hours before putting it aside, and is not in its current state worth the asking price.It looks good, the music is good, the whole premise of the game is great, but it lacks any real depth.The combat is okay, a decent variety of skills and weapons, generally enjoyable clicking away and ending folk.The Diplomacy is neither here nor there, just don't piss anyone off to much on the way up and you will be okay. Once you are strong enough you can just ignore what others think.The economy, what there is of it, I think its workable as is. There just is not a lot of incentive to upgrade and build tall and again it lacks any real depth or variety. After a while you run out of stuff to spend the cash on.Its buggy, not the worst I have played, but crashes a fair amount during missions and when you are interacting with people. Some you can sort just by leaving and coming back, others screw the game and if you don't save it before hand then its back to the auto save, which is frustrating if you have paused the game and done a fair amount with your businesses, gangsters and diplomacy in the interim.I would like to see them improve the game in terms of the type of illegal businesses you can set up, illegal money presses that kind of thing, it would also be interesting to be able to buy legitimate businesses to diversify your income, and have to balance illegal vs legal  income or face a greater level of suspicion from the Feds.In terms of spending the cash you make, it would be great if you could invest in other things like vehicles, which self respecting mob boss does not have a decent motor! All you can do just now is take a taxi! It would be nice if you could set up your own booze distribution network, which you would need vehicles and underlings for. On the underlings side of things (your mob gangsters aside), all you can have is guards, you can't even directly influence how they are armed (Or if you can I have not found out how to yet) . Again there is so much room for more here, intimidating and extorting your neighbourhoods for cash in exchange for protection (there in an element of this with the minor factions, but its so minimal). And loads of other underling things like distributing booze, patrolling keeping peeps safe, exploring, robbing banks whatever it is. Vehicles and weapons could make them more or less effective depending on what you equipped them with and if its sufficient for the task given. Its not terrible, its just not great and it could be epic. As Paradox are involved I fully expect to see more content, but at a price!

_childDocuments_.review: The biggest sin in empire of sin, is that of publishing this game as a finished product rather than an Early Access. I don't know whether the onus is on the developer or the publisher or both, but it's a blatant lack of ethics  and of respect for prospective custommers. Sadly, it is increasingly common in the gaming industry.The game is a bit further than one might expect from the initial release of an Early Access in that the storyline for each boss is already in, but as far as bugs and game mechanics polish go, I've played Early Access games that were further along the development line on day 1 of their Early Access (props to Fell Seal: Arbiter's Mark team) than Empire of Sin is on an official release.So if you chose to buy this game in the state as of this review, beware that you are buying into an Early Access for a game that will hopefully meet it's expectations only several months from now.I can't endorse this product because of the unethical marketing strategy. I would've paid full price to participate in an Early Access if it had been properly advertised as such because the genre is right up my alley and the game looked (and still looks) like it could have a lot of potential down the line.That's the end of the short version. Details below.As for appreciation of the game in it's current state:-The atmosphere and music is great albeit a little repetitive.-The voice acting embodying the personality of the bosses is enjoyable, although limited in scope.-The graphics are fine although still bug-ridden e.g.--Attack animations causing characters to go through walls or shoot through objects--Certain characters end "frozen" during some or all of their animations and when this happens, it appears to slow down the execution of actions.-Given the prevalence of tactical combat in the current state of the game, the fact that buildings where combat take place only have a handful few layouts for each building size quickly becomes very repetitive.-There remains a lot of gameplay bugs, even after 2 big bugfix patches. I have only experienced one that was gamebreaking and forced me to restart a new game, and it was in the intro tutorial with Goldie. However I've had to reload to last save for a couple of bugs, or save and reload right away for a handful few very annoying ones, and there are others you just accept to playthrough however annoying.-Gameplay is very shallow. And this is well above bugs as to why I feel this should've been released as an early access game. There are 2 main game systems, the tactical combat system and the empire simulation system. They intertwine by allowing you to hire better mercenaries or purchase gear or by hostile acquisition of revenue-generating buildings.--The game can be won while ignoring the empire simulation altogether. You can kill every other boss and win the game, no matter how well guarded they are, with your own boss alone on max difficulty. Part of this is game balance. Another part is heal/sustain mechanics and most likely a bug with a healing item. And an even bigger chunk is terrible combat AI.--The combat advantages gained from a good empire sim are very marginal, unless you purposefully stretch the game to wait for later game mercenaries to catch up and be fully upgraded as the cheaper/early game ones are. Gear from merchants is generally worse than the random loot you get from thug hunting/box farming.--Even with self-imposed rules or boundaries to try and explore empire simulation, the max difficulty AI is quickly outscaled. I won my second playthrough with self-imposed rules by 1923 because I had nothing else left to do than finish the bosses off. By contrast, prohibition lasted until 1933. Eventually you just realise that you would need to self-impose a lot of idle time to try and reel the player's growth potential in line with the poor AI and the simulation mechanics are neither sufficiently complex nor varied to where even very casual gamers won't figure enough out within a few hours.Despite all of that, I still have mild enjoyment playing this game because of the laid back jazz atmosphere and some of the more corny dialogue and the sheer laugh of breaking the game so hard.

_childDocuments_.review: So i got this one despite all of the mixed reviews because again, i'm just a sucker for mafia-related media and paradox-published games like Cities, Stellaris, HoI etc spoiled me too much i guess.People are comparing this game to XCOM a lot, and well, so will i, because thats the game that always springs to your mind when playing this thinking "why isn't this and that just done like in xcom??"First things first:- Graphics are fine. Everything looks grimey, theres smoke hanging in the air, the streets are littered and reflect the dim streetlights on a rainy night...just like you would expect from a 1920s Mafia-Movie. Nicely done.- Music is KICK ASS. So flippin catchy i got it stuck in my head for quite a while, fits the scenario very well and really gets you into the mood for beeing a wise-guy from the second the menue starts up.- SFX are...ok. Every SMG sounds the same, so do the MGs, the Shotguns, the Handguns etc...seriously? there are so many classic and iconic guns in here, you couldn't bother to get at least like 3 different sounds for each subtype of gun? Weak. Don't you just love when you are playing a game and can tell "Oh that guys got a (insert gun)!" Just by it's sound? well...not here.- Still on the Sounds-front, after hearing your boss saying his lines for the 1000000th time, it gets old. Even worse with some npcs that seem to have like 2 lines shared between them. So get used to hearing "Ahhh damn it..i'm ♥♥♥" A LOT.Now to the Characters, which like in xcom, is a huge part of this game.- The Bosses are all unique and interesting enough, though i would have liked some more "classic italian mobster" types. Really don't see myself running a Crimesyndicate as a petite burlesque dancer you know..- With that in mind, it's clear the game wants to push everything in a more "colorfull" and kinda funny(?) way with the bosses and squadmembers. Which is fine if you are into that but not so fine when you really want to roleplay as a classic mob kinda guy in this ROLE PLAYING game. There is absolutely NO character customization, so you have no choice but to have a squad of people cosplaying as cowboys, butchers, soldiers, indians and lunatics etc. In XCOM, you can FULLY customize every little thing on each of your soldiers. So you can go full lunatic with pink camo shorts and green iros, full simp by having your females running around the battlefield in hotpants and sportsbra or, if you want full tryhard and have everyone in buzzcuts,camo-facepaint and SpecOps-Uniform and Helmet. Well...not so here.- Your squadmates level just by existing. Excuse me??  There is no xp involved, there is no rank-system like in xcom (which would work for a mafia-hierarchie just as fine), NOTHING. they just fill a bar over time and every once in a while you get to pick a perk or skill whatever. They also just level their critical hit chance with the weapontype they use, but not their actual aiming, so they don't really get better over time like  xcom. So, you can either a) keep your first mates for rp or sentimental reasons or because they already unlocked so many skills even tho their aim is ♥♥♥♥♥, or you can kick them out and hire a new mate with better stats even though you may not want to. So you don't get attached at all to them, you don't care if they bite it or not, there are dozenz of BETTER mates just waiting to be recruited anyways.In xcom, your squad levels from rookie through the ranks up to colonel, getting better aim and awesome skills along the way. you know what they've struggled through, you where with them struggling through enemy troopers and barely making it until they became the one-man army they are now, you know their names and rank by heart, you feel proud when they get a hard mission done and earn a promotion...well...not so here. Their in your squad until they die or just become to weak for the state of the game...- So listen. I know it's 2022. I know how the world biggest coorporations and even goverments fear twittermom-♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. But there is a time and place for gender-equality. When i play a game set in the present or near/distant future, then YES, gimme female cops, agents, gangsters, soldiers. After all, that is what our society luckily evolved to after years of struggle and fighting for equality. Great! Buuuut....when i play a game set in 1920s chicago, you know what really breaks the immersion? Seeing a squad of six lady-cops wielding shotguns shaking down a mafia-owned bordello. Or seeing a 100-pound girl working as muscle in said bordello. Listen, maybe there where female policeofficers, FBI agents etc in that timeperiod, but i can say with certanty they weren't making uop 50% of that outfit. It just hurts to see something like this in virtually EVERY media nowadays and instantly thinking "ooof...way to sacrifice artistic integrity for blunt virtue-signaling" No one believes this is happening to fight inequality, or empower young girls or show that you don't only cater to fat guys eating pork rinds while watching them chinese cartoons. You do it so you don't get the "reeeeee there are no people of color in kingdom come deliverance set in 1404s bohemia reeeeeee you racists!!" treatment. And yeah...thats really sad. Get your integrity together man. Create a timepiece, or create a fairytail and market it as such...Ok, now gameplay.-Zzzzzzzzzzzzz- So i ran my first playtrough into a wall, because i didn't quite get all the mechanics etc. yet. On my second playtrough on medium difficulty....i steamrolled the npcs.- The thug-faction (acting as the civ-barbarians) pose no danger even to lowlvl squads. and you know, thats fine, they are supposed to be kinda weak.-The minor factions (the civ-city states) are tougher but managable, also fine. You have to think if you are rdy to take them on earlygame.- The big factions...well. On my first playtrough, i took my sweet time, looking around, reading every dialogue, exploring alleyways, just to notice sometime the npc took almost the whole district and sooner or later declared war together with another faction, so i thought damn, i was too slow. So i started a new campaign, rushing to establish myself. Naturaly the npcs didn't like, declared war, sent a pretty beefy squad or two my way and after littering the streets with them...he just gave up. i crushed him in earlygame. when i looked what the other big factions where up to...they don't even vlear out the thugs in their starting neighborhood...wtf man. So naturally you crush them with no effort, after you defeat one or two the others tremble befor you asking you for protection, non aggression pacts etc left and right, The sheer number of districts is what made me quit at the end because- When you fought one big fight, you fought them all. No big variety in maps, the streets are all the same after a while, the buildings also have like 2 variations to them each, the enemy grunts are "soldier" "tank/heavy" and "medic". thats it. In xcom, every map is something new. you don't know where the enemies are. you don't know how the map looks, you don't know what the best angle of approach might be until you scouted it out. There are many enemy types each with their own strenghts and abilities which you can exploit or get wasted by when you aren't careful. Speaking of scouting...There is NO tactics involved whatsoever. The only approach to any fight is guns blazing. you can't stealth your way in, get into position and ambush, you only can kick the door in with your 8man squad that doesn't even fit into the entrancehall of some buildings and start blazing them to smitherines.  And after the 58th time...it gets booooring.- rnd is out of control. Looting, the inventory of the black market dealer, it's all purely random. so you can be lucky and find the best armor in the game in your first hour and make your boss practically invincible, or be very unlucky and just get ♥♥♥♥♥ everytime, No balance at all.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has great potential HOWEVER, I will not be playing it again until a much needed patch is released. it should not have been released in this state - far FAR to buggy and just......empty.My main concern is that the overhauls this game requires are too far too many. It basically needs the below to make it playable:- DIPLOMACY OVERHAUL -. I rate games like this straight away on how they handle diplomacy. The sit downs are a great idea but are terrible. They should have functioned like an interactive story book with many unique situations coming from them. Also, you shouldn't always have to come off as an arsehole when speaking to other factions.....that is what diplomacy is! (Cant see this being fixed due to the costs involved with getting voice actors back).- AI - The Ai is shockingly bad. Standard issue in games but can be fixed- COMPLETE PLAYER / AI INBALANCE - Games like this desperately need to feel fair and that both AI players and you are doing the same things to reach the ultimate goal of winning the game. For a start, the AI player just constantly throws generic gangsters when at war - something you cannot do except for when defending. Any unique gangsters the AI may have will always be waiting for you at their safe house. The Black List of gangster shouldn't even exist, it should be that the generic gangsters evolve into RANDOMLY generated gangsters that can be customised like X-com - a game this heavily takes from. Doubtful this will get fixed due to the sheer balancing issues this would cause.- HEISTS/ROBBERIES - Why oh why are they missing in this game? You should have had to start at the bottom and work your way up. Simply to fix.- AUTO RESOLVE - I do not understand how this game is missing an auto-resolve option? Something i have no doubt will be added in the very next patch. With the constant generic gangster spam being thrown at my buildings - this was the main reason i stopped playing. Utterly game breaking.- LACK OF PLAY TESTING - I played on the medium difficulty and had three times more points than any of the other 10 AI players. Seems you can just take over buildings constantly with 3/4 strong gangsters and make money that way. Use the money to buy other buildings and you will then take over whole neighbourhoods shortly.  Rinse and repeat then expect the inevitable spam attacks...which is when you turn the game off. if you manage to stay sane enough to continue playing....use the shallow booze system to make the booze you need and then where it should be distributed. I can just imagine raising the difficult wont improve AI....just add cheat modifiers to the battles and stupid percentage hit chance increases. Will try this when the game is in a playable state.- NEW BATTLE MAPS AND LOCATIONS - Maps constantly repeat themselves...should have been randomised.There are many other things that can fix this game and fingers crossed a new patch will sort them out ASAP.

_childDocuments_.review: Firstly - im not a fanboi so this review is genuinely unbiased and based on my current gametime having bought it in the last 24 hours.Firstly - Ive been following the game since announcement. I havent bought it until now which speaks volumes as this was based purely on steam reviews. Having seen it on sale and with very little else on offering i thought, screw it lets have a punt even with mixed reviews.Summary:Ive got almost 12hrs game time which i understand isnt like 100+ however, i dont understand the negative reviews - and trust me ive read many reviews, hence why holding off buying. Yes the developers have only recently started pushing updates/patches  however in the last 12 hours game time, ive not experienced any bugs AT ALL. <touchwood>The game is very much a nostalgic nod to the old games of Gangsters: Organised Crime, Mafia and Omerta as many have said before me. The game is not designed as a quick fix. Its a slow burn. From my take im game its very similar to the old school strategy games - i say this due to the nature of jumping in game, spending a few hours sorting some business stuff  and enemy take overs and then coming back to it in a few hours or even a day or 2 and picking up where you left off. I remember fondly how i used to do this with The Settlers on amiga - player 3 or 4 hours solid gaming then come back in a day or 2 and carry on as if there was no interruption. If you play the game the way it is meant to be played  then you wont be completing a playthrough in quicktime. In my 12 hours, i own 1 neighbourhood and i find myself playing politics with the other 9 factions whilst im desperately trying to single out a specific weak link faction that i can eradicate. This isnt an easy feat by the way, unless of course you  get some intel on a boss safehouse - and even then, it takes some planning and purchasing of consumables to attack a safehouse and come away with all your capo's!I dont understand the moanings of people saying its broken as you cant get gold henchman - gold henchman are top tier. Why if you are a scrub mafioso would any gold henchman ally with you - doesnt make sense. Therefore the whole "endgame" henchman argyment is a moot point to me. Higher henchman are scaled for notoriety as they should be. I am still grinding loyalty with a linked henchman to get my first gold henchman - and i like that fact you have to work for it. To put in simple terms, since i clicked play, i went to the black book and began picking my endgame henchmen and have started my affiliation with lower henchman as a result. I love the fact you have to plan for long term in the short term  - amazing mechanic in my view.Imagine Shadows of Mordor's nemesis system whereby guy A doesnt like B but wouldnt have an issue working with guy C. However guy C is best mates with guy D who hates guy A - and each of guy A,B,C,D all have differing abilities. The possibilities are endless. Im currently using a demolitionist, 2 doctors, 2 enforcers, 1 hired gun and 1 con artist. The mechanics of the fights are drastically different depending on who you take and each fight can be totally different. For example one fight which was listed as a medium location ended up having 2 guys that could throw demolitions - when my team are huddled near the door as ranged characters - it was painful! The only gripe i would say is that auto resolve for fights is a total lottery. One of my brewery's got attacked by 5 enemy players and i had 2 guards. It was a clear loss so i clicked auto resolve just to get rid of the conflict and much to my amazment. I won /facepalm (clearly i pay my underlings too much!!) On that note i would suggest the enjoyment of the game is actually playing the fights anyway, rather than auto resolving - but each to their own.Pros:Games a slow burn - and it should be. (i bought settlers in my early teens and it lasted me well over a month or 2. nowadays im buying games once a week)Depth of companions and choiceAbilities and story of your main character choice (genuinely going to play a new game with a new character - which is rare in modern games for me)Graphics are solidPolitics with other factions Companion questsCombat escalates quickly - especially safehouses (took me 5 save reloads to drop my first boss with each fight lasting 20 minutes+)Cons:Doesnt suit the generation of completing a game within 20hrsLoot drops can be a bit rubbishAuto resolve is laughable so avoid itTravelling can be time consuming (use the taxi's they are there for a reason)Not many businesses to createSave system is a bit meh - would prefer ability to name saves and auto deletion of out dated savesOverview pages can be confusing and awkward to locate quickly a business you are looking for unless you remember the name of it (my naming of businesses aint the best - my latest brewery is called Capone Kissma Nads)All in all, this game is pretty amazing and considering there is little other choice in the genre and whilst its on sale, SNAP IT UP - you would be mad not to.Finally there is something special about hearing your irish main character saying Gobshite in a true irish accent as he hits someone in the face with his Shinty stick!

_childDocuments_.review: This game could have been very good. The potential of the game is obvious. However, potential isn't what people are looking for, or at least not what I am looking for. I like my games to deliver. Despite entertaining enough gameplay, albeit repetitive, there is one thing that screws this game over far more than anything else. That is the bugs. It is rare for me to encounter so many bugs in a game, that I feel it is game breaking. Here is just a few of the worse ones; -Some missions do not resolve properly, you get the rewards, but the missions do not clear away. Eventually the bad consequences of missions with limited time will happen as well when missions fail to complete properly. - Gang members, or the entire gang, including your boss, can disappear if you are inside a building while upgrading it and rushing the upgrades. I found this particularly true of breweries. The only character you can get back without loading is your boss character, by "travelling to", the other gang members are in limbo. - Enemy gangs can acquire characters without having raised their Notoriety Points sufficiently. All recruitable characters have a minimum demand for how Notorious you are. However the computer can recruit characters ignoring this, meaning the entire point of raising your Notoriety faster than everybody else is gone. The AI cheats in crew recruitment. - Once a Cooperation Deal was cancelled by a rival gang the dialog box refused to close. When this happened for me that last quick save was also corrupted. Progress was lost. Basically; the game has game breaking bugs.I rate games on a die of 1-6, but with 0 for absolute failures. Minimum for recommended is 3. This is a 2. Not complete crap, but it fails to reach the minimum, I do not recommend you buy this game at this point in time. Wait a couple of months and see if it gets patched up and fixed. If it is fixed, it can become a solid 4. Currently though it is a 2.

_childDocuments_.review: Jeez, this is bad.I was so into this game. I had it preordered and it was a tossup whether I'd be more into this or Cyberpunk. After all, it's a management sim with a mafia theme and tactical combat. It's basically made for me.Except it's not. It's not for anyone. Its initial strong charm wears off quickly when you get into the flow of the game, which it's clear nobody put much time into. Your character's unique traits, promising a customized experience, aren't particularly useful, coming in randomly once in a while, but never telling you exactly what happened. The sit-downs, supposed to be a clash of personalities, are invariably an exchange of zingers followed by an offer of sharing bonuses. The management part is fine for what it is, but traveling around the world map is an infuriating exercise in zooming out, zooming out some more, sometimes zooming out a third time to go to a place and then you can interact with a building and do your talking or fighting. There are a zillion missions that come in from nowhere, far too many to track, and all of them basically have the same flow. It quickly becomes clear that the game has shown its whole hand in the first minutes and you're just going to see the same things over and over again.Speaking of repetition, there's the combat. The thing you spend most of your time doing. You can essentially win any fight by just shooting over and over and over again. Terrain doesn't matter, placement doesn't matter beyond line of site, AI is terrible, and everyone is outclassed. And combat is the endgame of every interaction, as far as I can tell. There's no autoresolve; it's just endless fight after endless fight.If there's violence in a mob game, it needs to be visceral. And it's not. It's a sanitized gunfighting game where there are dozens of people standing in the line of fire, who you can't hurt. There are no civilian casualties. You can only hurt other criminals. Even accidentally. I don't WANT to kill civilians, but the fact that I never accidentally hit one in dozens of firefights kept taking me out of the game. The game might be fun enough without the combat, but the combat kills fun as efficiently as your gangsters kill nameless thugs. I want to wait and see if this gets patched into something good. But there's a fundamental sloppiness, from the animations to the systems that don't really interact with one another to the deluge of repetitive quests to the wasted subject matter and bland writing, that makes me think this is the game we get. Which is ultimately the sin this game traffics in.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun time-waster  but ultimately lacks depth in my opinion. The game is relatively easy and you can pretty much just ignore your rackets and concentrate on steamrolling safehouses. There are a lot of features in the game that I just didn't use. Diplomacy - Other than declaring war, I didn't bother. Black Market - After I got my first legendary from the first boss, pretty much didn't touch it.Racketeering - Generally only upgraded to level 2 at the point I got them, but honestly once you realise killing the enemy boss gives you their turf, it seems daft to take over rackets individually.Missions - I did the first few, and felt they were a faff. Not engaging, didn't really bother after that.Police - Did nothing. "Well this sounds pretty negative" I hear you say. Possibly. I think those features could add a lot to the game, I also think maybe it's just some balancing issues. I played Goldie and her ability lets you kill a whole raft of enemies in the very first turn. Perhaps other characters are a little more involved. But ultimately the reason I gave it a positive review despite my criticism is because it's fun. Despite it not being the game I expected, I had a lot of fun with it and while I can't imagine racking up hundreds of hours on this, I can see me maybe playing one or two other characters over a couple evenings when looking for something a little relaxing to play.At the time of review I'd finished my first play through, 7 hours. I could have done it much sooner had I realised just how easy it was to take an entire Gang's territory in one go. I'll update the review if other characters change my stance on anything. Until then, I'd recommend, but not at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: As of me last playing this on 12/13/2020, this game did not stand out at all. The game was simple to grasp, and might give you enough bits here and there to keep you going. Those bits are just distractions to the giant lack of features and mechanics that helps make the core gameplay interesting and exciting.* The core gameplay mechanics center around property management and turn based combat.Turn-based combat: It feels pretty ok at first but as the amount of enemies and tougher gangsters appear, it feels drawn out and unnecessarily long. You're also forced to manage the defenses of your own property when an enemy gang decides to invade you, which can feel frustrating if you don't have one of your tougher underlings stationed nearby. The generic units you get and face in the property defense feels boring and more of a numbers game, which further unnecessarily extends the length of the fight.Property Management: The concept feels pretty ok, but I don't think I've been able to generate enough money off the property and have been spending more time raiding and invading. Although I've only had a short time playing it, the upgrades don't feel impactful for the defenses and the payout isn't noticable in the long term for profits. Also there's a constant change in the areas that can affect the amount you can make, which is to deter you from monopolizing on a single product line.They have posted that they created a community group to gather feedback and directly influence the development, but I am still waiting to see something that changes to jump out at me. I'm sure that alot of people are enjoying what it has to offer, but it doesn't really make much of a good impression for me, and feels more like an early access game.If i had to give it a rating: 3/5There are some interesting concepts that they want to do but it needs further fleshing out to make gameplay more interesting and less of a chore for certain core mechanics. There is definitely room for improvement.I would not recommend this game in the state it was in, since I last played.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, I got this for free through my wife who works at Paradox. However, I've got nothing at stake here personally.I am still undecided what to say about this game, or if I want to recommend this game or not. After 17 hours, I just finished my first playthrough... first 15 or so hours I took it slow, then I got a bit bored (and overwhelmed with the management), so I just went around and killed everyone in a row, winning the game. But let's take a deeper look in things below.---The game's premise is pretty interesting. I like a bit of management, as well as good old turn based combat. The theme is also close to my heart, so I was very tempted to buy this game. Luckily I ended up getting it for free, so I launched the game and dug in.Within the first 20 minutes I realized that I am not actually playing a game made by an AAA studio headed by John Romero - I was playing a sort of an indie dev game that somehow had big names attached to it. The game feels like a small studio game, where the publisher has pressured the team to make a game too complex and too fast, without enough playtesting.The game is simply clunky. From controls to camera to combat to management, everything feels like there's a good IDEA behind it, but not enough testing and not enough planning actually went in to the features. You'll very quickly realize that the AI in combat is wacky to say the least and very easy to exploit. At the same time, the management of different rackets is a bit confusing and extremely cumbersome. The story is explained through quests, but they are not very well presented, they get a bit confusing and in the end I completely ignored them. They need to be paced a lot better.Once you snow ball in this game even a little, it's super easy to just go and take over everything, while ignoring the story, police raids etc. You just go from a generic battle to another. There's also plenty of weird little bugs that occur pretty much all the time. However I did not run into massive game breaking bugs, unlike some other people have.There's a few longer, better reviews that outline my feelings towards the game very well:---With all that being said... I wish I could go into more details about everything. With less than 20 hours though, I don't feel I can do that properly. The game has many glaring, major issues and it doesn't feel like a proper, released game. However, with all its faults it is a playable game and has a certain charm to it. Of the 17 hours I have played so far, 15 were somehow still enjoyable and kept me engaged. I had fun and I didn't hate the game, even with all its faults. In a way it felt like a game that was just deep enough to interest me and shallow enough at the same time to allow me to enjoy an hour or two after work.Even though the devs have announced that there'll be DLC's coming, I don't think anyone should bother with them. Get the game in a sale, hope the devs abandon this after a few patches. I hope - and so should you - that they'll get enough money and goodwill out of this demo of a game to get funding for Empire of Sin 2, which would be properly planned and tested before release.At the moment this game is only worth about 10 USD. I can recommend it at around that price range, and if you have tolerance for small issues. And if you like the theme. But it's not an AAA game. It's a game that feels like it's done by industry beginners.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, 7 / 10. Most annoying bugs were resolved in the first few days and the game runs just fine now. Its XCOM-style turn-based combat, fighting for control of illegal businesses, getting into wars with other factions, and ultimately trying to come out on top. You run a crew of 'real' gangsters, up to ten, and from 5 'classes', which can be further customized with a tree of talents to choose from, and further with their gear, weapons, etc. You manage various seedy businesses, but there's not much depth there. Missions drive some storylines, but aside from the first few that give you alot of cash to initially get started in the gameworld, they don't do much. The real fun is in taking over existing businesses from other factions, and growing your own empire. Hired Gangsters are powerful, and expensive, so your main goal is to have enough businesses to support both hiring, keeping, and outfitting your gangsters, so that you can stand up to the other major factions.Atmosphere is high quality, theres fun diversity in gangsters including their dress and special abilities, and the combat is challenging at higher difficulties. I'd play on the standard starting difficulty if you're not familiar with XCOM style games, and a higher difficulty if you are. The navigation of the world and in combat is a bit tricky to learn, but once you do you'll appreciate why they did it that way - becomes very easy.Big Pros:* Combat is fun* Leveling up and diversifying your crew's abilities and equipment has depth and value* Visuals and navigation are clear, clean, and useful, once you get used to them* Obvious room for growth in mechanics through future content/DLCs from great initial frameworkBig Cons:* AI on lower settings atleast, is weak, both in combat and their management of their businesses* Police don't seem to do anything but slightly annoy you, no matter how many of them you shoot* Current Balance around Safehouses is broken and allows too much progress too quickly* Too much of the game is not skippable, which is especially annoying at the start of a game talking to all of the factions and getting raided - an autoresolve would be niceIf development is continued on this game, the Con's can disappear quickly, and the Pro's will expand, so I recommend this game in its current state.*Says 56 hours but it was just running in background - more like 20 hours.

_childDocuments_.review: Well it's XCOM minus the stuff that made XCOM special.  You don't really have the care for your random gangsters like you do the soldiers when they are cut down.  What Empire of Sin does right is the look.  The game setting looks good, the concept of a open world meets XCOM style turn based game is very unique, and playing the mob boss from a more strategic level is neat.  The police and feds as a third faction that comes out of nowehere seemingly to ruin your day is a nice touch and the in game missions aren't bad either. That said it has some odd hang ups that prevent it from being a cult classic.-unlike other paradox games where historical accuracy is aimed for and alternative history is played up for a joke this game really mixes things up.  Example Hymie Weiss, the man alleged to be the only man Al Capone feared is someone you can just hire off bat.  -the gangs are very inclusive and open minded despite what history says, I wouldn't mind this if they did it like CK3 where I have options to play historical or non historical but a lot of these gangs won't even allow you to be in them unless you're of a certain ethnicity or race unless you're the bottom level guys-There's some sort of relationship system between your henchmen which is mostly just annoying.  I get the concept was some henchmen would not attack each other but mostly it comes off as strange.  Seemingly ALL my henches are bisexual evidently and I've had such strange parings as the black and proud harlem hellfighter and the refuses to be reconstructed ex confederate solider. I mean being gay in the era is wild enough much less the age and race issues going on in that relationship.  But it seems to happen with EVERYONE.  Everybody is just itching to get into some sort of sexual relationships seemingly just as an annoying game mechanic which is all it becomes in the end.  -Oddly enough the mechanic as progressive and ahistorical as it is, it also hinges entirely off mongamy.  Evidently all my bisexual gangsters refuse to share with anyone.  We run brothels, they're all bi, but no one wants to share or even consider a orgy.  So instead I have to keep my drama queens apart or my XCOM game becomes a slap fight between my crew except with guns.  It's beyond pathetic and really makes me feel like Al Capone should have been questioning his actions long before he had the mayor of Chicago murdered. -Honestly all the business management seems really secondary to the turn based fighting.  It's what earns you the money for vests, guns, etc but your best gear comes from other crime bosses which you get by killing them so really the money is just to buy better bisexual hench persons. -Oddly about every race is in this game minus hindus, arabs, and islander types...there are two full blooded indigenous Americans as well which can only seem so progressive about a game centered around illegal alcohol trade. Again it's an attempt to be progressive but at what end if you're also trying to be historical?  Henry Hill wasn't exaggerating about the whole not being full blooded Italian means you can't be made, ironically crime is not that open minded about race in fact they're the opposite but won't let it stop them making a buck.  -The rival gangs are mostly made up which I can somewhat understand but all the legit organizations should be in game.-All organizations cops, gangs, etc have females in them.  Again I get the progressive tone but it makes the game look more like Michael Jackson's "Smooth Criminal" because they all wear the men's attire regardless.  Only female henchmen, gangbosses, and prostitutes can dress like women.  The 20s must have been a strange time with bisexual criminals who are only into monogamy but have very odd dress code rules.  Overall it needs work and I think a historical option playing up the more edgy less progressive aspects of the organizations would be interesting as well.  So far this feels more like CK3 when you make everyone bisexual and XCOM combined.

_childDocuments_.review: Generaly I love Paradox games. This game however has been a bitter disappointment. At the beginning the game seems like fun. Combat is sort of challenging especially when you are not using any of the golden weapons that you get for buying the delux version. Soon after that you and your companions will become stronger and pretty much all the challenge goes down the drain. Having an AI that seems to make worse choices in-game then my Tesla on FSD in traffic doesn't help either. Then we come to the management side of EoS which feel even more rushed to the shelves then the combat system. There are a few options to make money, all don't require any interaction and aren't very interesting. Basically you claim a building and upgrade it to either a brothel, casino, brewery or speakeasy. The first two are nothing more then money overtime. The speakeasy is a little more interesting because you need a brewery to produce your own stock. Depending on the local economy you need to produce either low quality for poor towns and better quality for areas with a richer economy. All in all this has been a very big disappointment and feels like a big money grab where Paradox uses up it's  somewhat good name to make a quick buck. _childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game quite a bit, as I'm a pretty huge fan of XCOM-style turn-based strategy games. However, I have three pretty major complaints with it:1) The game is too easy. Like, waaaaay too easy. I love Paradox, and have a long history with their games (particularly CK2 and Stellaris). Empire of Sin follows in their footsteps in that you can reach a position that is essentially unassailable very quickly relative to the overall length of the game. I know AI "cheats" are annoying to some strategy game players, but the AI in Empire of Sin really needs some hidden bonuses to money/alcohol production and/or free facility upgrades. The AI is also pretty weak in the tactical aspect of the game. Even on the hardest difficulty, the enemy AI is not particularly tactical. They don't attempt to flank. They often use suppressing fire or overwatch when they could take a killing shot. In fact, the only difference I observed in different difficulty levels is that enemies have (slightly) more armour the higher the difficulty. Enemies should get a bonus to hit chance at least, even if it's not possible for them to get "smarter" on higher difficulty levels. 2) There's a lot of stuff you can do that should have a strategic effect, but literally none of it matters. You can just hire 10 gangsters and run around town steamrolling everything. You can upgrade your security, but it doesn't really matter. Just find the enemies wandering around the map with the rat icon above their head and kill them with your 10-gangster goon squad before they can take out your facilities. Cop activity is tracked, but even on the highest difficulty, it's no problem to operate at full capacity without the cops taking any real interest in your businesses. There is no strategic element to expanding your empire. Just... keep some money in reserve (usually 1 weeks' earnings is enough), and upgrade as many facilities as you can. That's not strategy. It's just busy work. You can assign a lieutenant to a safehouse, where they give a very minor bonus to the neighborhood's production and exist as a last line of defence if your neighborhood is attacked, but gaining money is not challenging (so you don't need the bonus), and your gangster is more valuable as part of your hit squad than waiting around playing defence. You can assign a mole, but that takes your gangster out of commission for six months and the effect is incredibly minor. Your mole can potentially steal some funds, damage a racket, or even assassinate a rival boss, but the % chance is incredibly low relative to the long time you lose a gangster to being a mole and in the six months a mole is gone you can easily (you guessed it) take your 10-man hit squad and take all of a rival gang's money, rackets, and assassinate their boss. Your gangsters gain loyalty and morale so quickly and easily that those numbers never made a difference to the game.There's a diplomacy screen, but it's also mostly pointless. Theoretically, you can buy other bosses out without fighting them, but you have to have been protecting them for 3 months first and the AI is (surprisingly) smart enough to break protection agreements when it gets close enough to possible to buy them out. There isn't really any consequences for refusing another boss. You might lose rep or honour, but those are again one of those numbers that appears like it could do something strategic, but doesn't really. Enemy bosses propose business agreements, but then rescind them randomly a few weeks later. 3) Game-stopping bugs. I only encountered the one, but it was enough for me to give up on the game. There's a story mission where you go to a casino to meet the mayor and chief of police. Then the game locks. It's a known issue, and has been a known issue for several months. I feel like a game-stopping bug in the middle of a main story quest is a pretty significant flaw.Suggestions:-Notoriety gain is too fast. I've maxed my notoriety after taking over a single neighborhood. Notoriety gain should be significantly slowed, and, in addition to controlling the power of the gangsters you can recruit, it should also control the number of gangsters you can have in your hit squad, starting with 3 gangsters at the start (so you can have a team of 4 with your boss), and expanding to a squad of 5 at 500 notoriety and maxing out at 6 with 1000 notoriety. Only being able to bring 6 gangsters into any combat would significantly up the challenge. I'd slow notoriety gain by capping some sources of notoriety. Like, after 100, you no longer gain notoriety for killing random thugs, or after 500, you only gain notoriety for killing enemy bosses and completing quests.-Take a page from Stellaris and give some enemy bosses an "advanced start" (use a slider at game creation so folks who hate AI cheating can turn it off). These bosses should gain more territory to start, as well as a huge bonus to their racket upgrades, cash earning, and booze production.

_childDocuments_.review: Updated review precinct patch: So the game is WAY more difficult but still lacks any real "strategy" to it. They took out some of the exploits and made the enemies tougher, but this is still a vapid shoot em up pretending to be a sandbox strategy game.  Spend your $50 on a deeper product.  The pendulum swung too far from being able to solo smash every boss on toughest difficulty to being unable to do the first few missions without having 3+ gangsters in your crew (not beginning content). Piss poor execution and imbalances galore. I don't want to only be able to play the same 3 OP bosses over and over, I want variety. If you are not playing as Daniel McKee Jackson, Sai Wing Mock, or Goldie Garneau, you will get ROFL stomped before you get off the ground. Time to uninstall this BROKEN GAME. NOTE: this is on toughest difficulty. After losing 5 games in a row to thugs before I could afford to buy a gangster, I am done with this POS pretending to be a strategy game. RUN AWAY!  Not even worth playing if it is free.Pros: Historically accurate, funny dialogue, multiple characters with unique back stories and mission arcs, the interrelationships between all of the gangsters makes for interesting twists, and the concept of building a gangster empire in prohibition Chicago is a fun environment to play.Cons :Combat is repetitive and draining (better spend all your cash on first aid kits if you don't have a doctor). Difficulty at the very beginning of the game is too steep forcing you to run around looting boxes praying to the RNG gods that you get a weapon that lets you compete in the combat where you are always outnumbered minimum 3/1. The empire management system is better than a year ago, but diplomacy is still lacking and there is not enough depth to the game besides the story.  For a sandbox game, the only fun is had playing the canned missions and not creating an empire. Summary: This game has gone BACKWARDS in the year since it was released. Still no real empire management, tougher fights means you die more often (lose and reload or start again), still can't name a save game (seriously, how do you overlook this simple aspect), the pool of randomly generated names for businesses is less than 10, and there is ZERO fun to be had playing this game.BUY SOMETHING ELSE.I will never pay money for a Romero Games product again. _childDocuments_.review: Reminiscent of Gangsters: Organized Crime (a classic from 1998) in a very fun way, so in that sense it feels like I've been waiting on this game for 20+ years. The combat is repetitive but still fun for me after @40 hours. The faction AI is solid and can be very punishing if you start a war before you're well prepared. Resource management is pretty good, although some additional nuance and complexity would be nice. There are numerous quests that pop up during play and these are fun. Many of them are tied to the particular gangsters you've hired, so there's good motivation to try out different people. Gangster relationships remind me fondly of Jagged Alliance 2, another of my all-time favorites. The city looks great and has a lot of wonderful immersive touches. Room for improvement? Sure. Playing on default difficulty the police/feds seemed like non-factors and the dynamic mini-factions -- while cool additions that make the city feel more alive -- feel easy to exploit to get ahead of the other major factions. Another exploit-y thing is fast travel (done via taxi) which allows you to respond too quickly to enemy attacks, thus nullifying their danger to a large degree. There are bugs as well although after @40 hours I haven't seen any of the game-breakers mentioned elsewhere.All in all, I'm really enjoying this game and am looking forward to continued refinements.
