_childDocuments_.review: I want to start this by saying I truly wanted to like this game more than any other I've played. I love the setting of 1920's Chicago, mobsters and love the genre of grand strategy. However, even though for these reasons I'll probably still occasionally play it, I would advise all others not to buy Empire of Sin in its current state. The issue with the game is not the ideas and concepts, rather, the execution. While combining business management, Paradox diplomacy, turn based strategy, and an RPG looks good on paper, they all have their own issues that break the game. Business management aspects are rather dull, requiring massive amounts of capital to upgrade businesses anywhere from 2-6 thousand an upgrade, while the income may only be a few hundred. The same applies for purchasing weapons, a normal pistol may cost as much as an entire brewery of yours. Diplomacy is fairly meaningless, as deals that are stuck are comically meaningless. The combat is alright, not new or innovative or bad and buggy, just average. RPG aspects are dull and lacluster, as character developments don't have much of an inmpact and negative effects can be easily circumnavigated. While these are all poor in their own right, what ruins the game is the AI. The AI won't attack, expand, or do much of anything. They just kind of sit there. As the player all you have to do, is kill an enemy boss at their safehouse and you win all of that gangs possesions, After killing two or three boses, you basically win the game. This coupled with completly dumb AI strategy ruins the game. This game is much closer to being in Alpha compared to a finally release state. I"m not one for complaining without offering solutions, so here are a few suggestions that I would make to improve the game. Overhaul the economic systems Completly fix the AI Make gang wars feel realHave enemy bosses switch locations, so you have to gain on intellegence first for a suprise hit Perhaps require a certain ammount of captured businesses before confronting a boss? Give other ways to win the game besides killing boses Overall, there a tons more suggestions I could make but I'm sure many more players will make them as well. This game is in need of a No Man's Sky type overhaul. The foundations are there, yet this game needs to work out all the kinks, bind the systems together, and vastly improve the AI's strategy for this game to become the ultimate gangster game it was marketed as and I hope it can become.

_childDocuments_.review: Short version: It’s a great game concept and some good elements but poorly executed and feels like it should be Early Access at best due to the decisions the game developers have taken. It has a poor ill planned UI, bugs and lacks a lot of content you would expect of a game of this price.I would buy this game but only when on sale (50%+ or around £20-£15) and maybe not then tbh.Long version:The game is set in 1920’s prohibition Chicago and as you probably seen this but, you play a gangster trying to take over the city against AI rivals. The visual style is appealing and there is some good voice acting and music. The combat system is the turn-based X-COM style that’s became popular on the Unreal engine. Generally speaking, these aspects of the game that are very appealing to me and something I could spending a lot of time playing and enjoying. However, there are several aspects of the game limited my enjoyment-Firstly bugs and crashes, they are there and in abundance unfortunately. As of yet there has been no patch (that I know of) to address these nor communication from the developer or the publisher to manage everyone’s expectations on when these will be addressed which is a shame. Secondly the game content. I’ve played this game for just over 13 hours and whilst I’m planning on playing more of the game (just so I can say I've ‘completed’ it), I don’t expect my experiences to change substantially. The side missions are pointless, lack flavour and are very, very repetitive of the game’s main mechanics i.e. go there, talk to this guy, fight this guy (and maybe his friends), go there, talk to this guy, fight this guy etc etc. The empire building exists of attacking ‘thugs’ (squatters in unused buildings) or attack other ganged own properties and that’s it. Which gets very repetitive very quickly. There is no need to identify potential buildings for illegal use or understand the illegal market needs for a brewery, brothel or casino in the neighbourhood. Your empire actions are limited to setting up these establishments in the neighbourhoods also. There is no need option to create ‘protection’ rackets take over legal business to launder money, no dealing in anything else but drink. Basically, it's setting up buildings and that’s it. Empire Management is also virtually none existent. You can upgrade most of the buildings in certain generic areas (like security, type of or amount of drink etc). There’s nothing else. For example, moving your guards from establishment A to B to meet potential threats, creating scouting parties or protection parties looking for enemies or police in a neighbourhood doesn’t exist.You can create a gang for you to run around the map with. Whilst each of these characters have their own back story, of which some are interesting and linked to some quests they can seriously break immersion. You and the AI’s have a set amount of characters to pick from but it’s a small pool and when they die, they are gone. Also, they have restrictions to hire which limits the pool even further. So, whilst you want to create a group of 3 or 4 Italians or Irish (or whatever culture you want to play as), you can’t. With my Italian ‘themed’ play I was forced to run around with an elderly Irish lady, a fat half clothed (southern American I think), an Indian Hindu, an Irish drunk and a Chinese lady. How can you pretend to be Ali Capone and the Italian mob taking over Chicago when your pool of side kicks has been chosen by the Race Equality Commission? Why couldn’t they just implement a procedurally generated pool of side kicks based on your background (if you’re the Irish mob, your enforcers will mostly likely be Irish!) with a couple ‘oddballs’ thrown in?The RPG element is very, very limited. Yes, you can equip your guys with weapons and items, and choose from skills to give the illusion of customisation. But in reality, this is very bare bones also. When you get an epic item it stays, you can’t customise weapons, nor your crews apperances, nor specialise down a certain path. RPG elements impact heavily on immersion and mechanics somewhat too. For example, you can get a Rosary that increases your initiative by 10, your health by 15% and increases defence skills by 5. Whereas weapons mods like increasing drum size for your submachine gun or sights, gun cleaning equipment, outfits (i.e police, smart, worker outfits) are missing. The games economy is also very skewed. For example, to run 2 hotels cost circa $10 per week but to buy a baseball bat (?!) for one of your crew to use in melee costs $6,725. I don’t understand what decisions developers took to come up with this economic scale but it’s ridiculous and feels like they were developed in silos.This game had lots of potential. I was hoping for ‘X-COM’ combat focused meets ‘Gangsters: Organized Crime’ Empire Management game but I’m sorely disappointed by both aspects.

_childDocuments_.review: Empire of Sin is a combination of  a gangster management sim and an x-com-like turn based strategy game.Neither are deep enough to really feel satisfying and both keep getting in the way of each other.I finished an entire playthrough out of spite.On the management layer, you open new illegal ventures, upgrade their security, profitability or discreetness with the push of a button. The numbers change slightly and you build up a criminal empire over time.You also manage relations with the police and other gangs, but often these appear only as pop ups with X gang requesting Y treaty with you, often at the expense of your honour because they previously broke an agreement with you within the last 30 days, which the game does not communicate to you in any meaningful manner. In fact most of the inner workings of the management layer are obfuscated.Lucky then, that you don't really need to pay attention to the management beyond ensuring you are making enough money and booze to fuel your empire.The other layer of the game is the turn based combat game.This is where the management becomes mostly irrelevant. You can attack venues run by common thugs for an endless stream of extremely easy battles and resources, all without upsetting rival gangs. This creates a fantastic risk free infinite funds tap to keep your gang well supplied. Also, no matter how easy these battles get, you can't rely on auto resolve. A battle that when played manually ends in a single turn will still result in injuries and risk for your gangsters when auto resolved. Go figure.The two games that EOS is trying to be get in the way of each other. The management game becomes pointless with the infinite funds injection from the combat. And the combat isn't varied or rewarding enough because it's just there to prop up the management side with something to do while you wait for your working girls to bring in that cash.EOS is a fantastic example of a developer spending far too much time polishing a bad idea rather than just making sure the game design is solid before pushing forward. Also most of the bugs the game had at launch (and there were a LOT) have now been fixed. You can't fix bad game design though.Skip this one. Wait for the zombie/ghost of Eidos to release a worthy successor to the original Gangsters.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game — I really do — because I actually enjoy these turn-based tactical combat games such as XCOM, Fire Emblem, Wastelands, Gears Tactics, Age of Wonders:Planetfall, Phantom Doctrine, Phoenix Point, Mutant Year Zero: Road to Eden, Battletech, Shadowrun series, and of course Final Fantasy Tactics. When I saw this game had that combat style AND it let you run a criminal empire that expanded into a living world in a deeper strategy game sense I was excited for that experience. Then I played the game. TLDR: Overall my initial reactions are the game is a really shallow experience. That empire management stuff and the economic systems in play are very shallow in particular. After combat you get to take over the buildings. There is little to no difference between the rackets though. When it asks you what you want it to be there is really only three choices. They each make you money, some more than others, they each have an upkeep mechanic you gotta pay, and that's about it. No difference between the three (Speakeasy / Brothel / Casino) though and you can literally spam only one type and be just fine. The Breweries are needed or you won't make any money in your Speakeasies. They need you to supply them with alcohol. You can trade excess booze for cash too which is a broken exploit right now because you can disguise it as Whiskey. From there you just spend the cash you make on more speakeasies (or upgrades) to make more money until you need more booze. And do the cycle again and again. It always seems to be the same repeat. Not a lot of depth here. It think the game's economy would be way more interesting if there was some kind of supply and demand system that is more robust than the preferred booze type that changes each month. Where if say your neighborhood of Chicago was oversaturated with speakeasies then it would become harder to attract customers and booze would have to be sold cheaper. Which means lower profits if you invest in only speakeasies. It would incentivize players to then try to monopolize a particular business in that neighborhood and cut out the competition maybe choosing brothels, casinos, or something else instead of a speakeasy. Hotels bring in more customers and double your synergies. If you have say three of a kind of the same racket type they give you like a 10% bonus. I think you can only have one Hotel per neighborhood though. The other thing you spend your cash on is hiring henchmen. Though the combat is so dull you really don't need a full 10/10.The game revolves around the combat and that isn't even all that special. The maps are tiny first of all. The combat is over in a matter of turns even when you're trying to take down a bosses safehouse. This is because the OP boss abilities. The other major flaw to the combat is the lack of environmental interactions. They are virtually non-existent. You would think people would be climbing over benches or vehicles to scramble to get out of the way of a gun fight that just broke out. And the player could be using the vehicles or other things in the environment as explosions or using explosives to destroy cover. It's very basic half cover, full cover, and flanking the enemy. Half the time there is no penalty to just running up next to them to get 100% and the kill but leaving yourself outside of cover. The AI is not very good. And when you kill a boss the game doesn't even replace the dead with procedural generated one, or even lesser factions. One would expect some lesser criminal would at least try to take up and assume the mantle and seize control in that power vacuum. I honestly think the combat is a step back from previous games in this genre. Instead of improving upon games like XCOM or Gears Tactics even Empire of Sin just does the bare minimum. The characters ( think xcom soldiers) do have classes and each class has different abilities you can choose in the skill trees but there is a lot of overlapping abilities even amongst the classes.  They badly need an auto resolve function for the combat because you'll get sucked into repetitive fights back to back to back when you're trying to manage your empire and forced to fight as your guards. I don't mind this every now and then I would even choose to fight the fight but you have no choice. It's every time you gotta go in and fight the fight.Also they really need a better way to compare weapons. Since your constantly upgrading and changing it's not a fun experience.  The UI functions and information is actually really shoddy. For being a strategy game and a Paradox published game you would expect more. Half the time I was scrolling over symbols and couldn't find a way to tell what it did or explain it and where i was getting it from. Not even a name to let me know what it was. Did I mention there is no manual even?I haven't even encountered any of the game breaking bugs reportedly out there either. The game is just a hot mess but there's hope that they'll fix it in that it just released and by and large it's been negatively received by the community. They got to do something. What do I like about the game? I love the setting and the theme. The time period of prohibition-era mobster ran Chicago has always been a fun time to play around in. The violence and intrigue of backstabbing and killing former partners in crime. The musical score is pretty good too.  It has a lot of style going for it and you can tell it was a labor of love for at least some of the devs. The game has it's potential but that's where my praise for this game ends. The theme alone doesn't even come close to outweighing the issues I have with it's design or mechanics. Which leads me to leave this game with a negative review rather than a positive one.

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay is way too basic, disappointingly one-note, you basically do the same thing over and over again. The environment on the surface looks pretty good but when you look under the hood it starts to feel inauthentic (were there really that many lady cops and male strippers in "1920s Prohibition-era Chicago"?) Not enough gangsters to choose from to keep things interesting, the interactions between your gang members are extremely lame and limited given how few of them there are (there should be a lot more, as a trade-off for such a modest roster) and the fact you can't send your no-name thugs out on patrol missions and such like the AI can do just feels like a missing functionality. Can't recommend this game in its current state, certainly not at full price, but there's definitely a good game hiding in here somewhere if it was given some serious work. (But I understand it's not being supported anymore so I wouldn't expect any improvements.)

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not sure what other reviewers are so disappointed by - I love this game! It's exactly what I was expecting. Xcom style turn-based combat, with a good amount of challenge but not so much it gets impossible.  Fun characters with several very different feeling gangs/bosses. Yes, it can get a little redundant as far as the later game neighborhood takeovers/development goes, but that's true for a lot of these types of games.  Devs definitely have some room to develop the nuances of the empire management side, but the base game and the combat part are tons of fun. I've got 10 hours in and plan to play more, but even that amount of fun is worth the sale price I paid. If you're hesitant, wait for a sale, but either way I recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: So, full disclosure. I bought this game at launch, but got it refunded because it wasn't doing anything for me....but I could see it had real potential. So I closely watched the development of the game over the next 12 months or so, and was very impressed with the improvements I saw....so purchased the game a second time. I certainly am glad I did, as its a lot more entertaining now. Locations feel a bit more varied, and the mission system is much more fun to engage with, as is the Empire building side of the game. There are additional improvements I'd like to see in the future (more character abilities, even more combat locations) but the game is a real hoot as it currently is.....especially for the asking price. Just don't go in expecting Game of the Year material, and I suspect you won't be disappointed by this game!

Besides being a completely buggy mess where you can't even use your characters inventory system, equip or unequip items, with majority of the items appearing as white boxes with the word "test" near them. I imagine in time these things can be fixed. However, the gameplay itself seems to lack any real polish. Besides the terrible voice acting where one guy even sounds like he was just recorded at a table reading and just got the script. The dialogue system is irrelevant since no matter your choice of response: it all leads to the same outcome!- AI improvement: they keep running out of cover while I'm shooting at them with a freaking machine gun.- Characters start battles in odd locations of the map: if they're entering places they should start by the door!... I'm going to stop here b/c I don't think all of what's in my mind could be saved/fixed. But then, there's that Rome Total War 2 anecdote, and No Man's Sky story... maybe?I will revise my review when this game is fixed. Until then, I feel I wasted a good $60.

_childDocuments_.review: Do not buy this game, it's a serious rip off, especially don't pay for the second DLC, it doesn't exist, and never will.This game is a complete rip off, and the developer, publisher, and even steam should be ashamed of the way they are still selling this product with a 2nd DLC that the publisher has already stated will never be delivered as the game has been "archived". For those, like myself, that pre-order this game having already paid for that second DLC. which as I just said they have no plans to ever deliver. They took money from people and never delivered the product that was paid for.The game itself isn't terrible, but yet at the same time isn't great either.Positives:- The visuals are nice.- The sound is good.- Combat is okay, fun at first.- Skills/Upgrades - it has a reasonable list of skills you can learn as each member of the team levels up. I won't go into detail, but some are useful, others not so useful.Negatives:- Combat - as I said it's okay, but it quickly becomes repetitive - AI regularly makes very poor decisions during combat.- - At the start of combat, they won't enter via the door you actually clicked on, they'll be randomly placed inside the building. Randomness in a game like this isn't necessarily a bad thing, but to me being essentially teleported to the opposite side of the building is a bit jarring. To me there are better ways to create randomess to this type of game. It also kills any real ability to try different strategies/tactics in combat, since you're just randomly placed, you can't choose how you want to approach combat.- - As combat triggers, they'll scatter, but the places they choose to take cover in often make no sense as they provide cover in the wrong direction, and leave themselves completely exposed in the direction fire will actually be coming from.- Businesses (legal/illegal) - too limited, not enough variety.- The city/map felt like a bunch of disconnected towns rather than one large city.- It HAD potential - however as noted above this game will never reach its true potential, it's been abandoned.- Dialogue is terribly cheesy, and the same lines a repeated over and over again. Not sure if it was bad writing or bad acting, I suspect a combo of both. As an example, you can fully upgrade one of your own businesses, and still, when you walk in with your chosen boss they'll regularly say "What's this dump?".... it's one of your own businesses you idiot, or worse, it's your home/safe house you dumbo.- What is there is good, but ultimately it lacks content and would need a few large DLC updates to be a worthwhile game.Would I recommend this game to others... NO, NO WAY!Paradox and Romero should be embarrassed to have released this game in the state that it was in. They should be ashamed of themselves for taking people's money and then running away without delivering what was promised, and yes, it was officially stated two DLC would be delivered. Avoid Romero games at all costs, a game about criminals, and in my opinion, made by a bunch of criminals. Will not be buying a game by Romero ever again.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: neither the combat or management in this game is good or innovative. It's not worth its price. I'm just glad I made that decision fast enough to get a refund.This game is a real flop on release, which looks like it might be becoming a trend for Paradox games. I don't have the faith that this game will be fixed like they're currently doing with Imperator though.In short, the game had a great premise but completely failed to innovate. It's buggy and quite dull compared to similar games, and certainly not worth its price point. The only way I'd recommend this game as-is is if it cost peanuts. The combat is in the realm of X-COM, but so much worse. Enemies routinely leave full cover to charge right into your guys. Bosses are OP, I played as the Vice Kings boss whose special ability allows him to unload an entire pistol clip into any enemies in range and killed the tutorial boss in 1 turn. You mostly expand early on by attacking unaligned thugs. The generation of these fights is tedious at best, you'll be plopped down (probably surrounded) in a construction site with a bunch of thugs who will try to rush you. There are two resources to manage in Empire of Sin. Money and alcohol. You start out with barely any income in either of these and are expected to expand. In the tutorial you are immediately pushed into the red by hiring 2 underlings, each of which has a minimum wage of $300. You don't need them this early. Paying to upgrade your rackets doesn't pay off nearly as quickly as going around fighting thugs and establishing new ones and you don't need hirelings to do this.Diplomacy is handled quite poorly. Every time you meet a new gang they will threaten you, and you have the option to threaten, negotiate with, or attack them. If you choose one of the first two then they will invariably demand that you pay them $2000 to avoid a relations penalty, possibly in addition to the penalty from threatening them.The voice acting is ok I guess. I wasn't really interested in the characters but I didn't have very long to get to know them. Story richness is probably the strongest suit of this game.

And some dumb decisions, like how you can click on a slot to promote someone but it does nothing. Instead you promote them from a small key command written in text on their character screen? Lots of overlapping information, most of which is useless, and other major rookie level problems. Overall, don't bother with this game. It never goes deep enough in the moment to moment play, nor in the strategy elements, to be worth your time. It will be really fun for a couple hours and then you have seen everything.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game because  I love the prohibition ganster era and having Paradox as the publisher I figured it has to be good. Well, It's not. In fact, it's pretty terrible. There are bugs literally everywhere in the game, useful tooltips to help you know what is what don't exist, and the pathing is a complete wreck. My party of 3 walks around at the speed a toddler does because they are trying to walk on top of each other, in fact I have kids, I can walk a toddler faster than they manage. The entire depth of running your business boils down to switching the alcohol type you're making and serving all the time to match the customer wants which is based only on neighborhood prosperity and that changes for no apparent reason constantly. You can basically ignore finances if you just run around killing thugs and smashing buildings, you won't even need good gangsters until you decide to fight a major faction and when you do that, just go straight to kill their boss and guess what... you get everything of theirs when you kill them. Going to finish beating this and likely will never play it again. Don't waste your money.Steam asked if I wanted to revise the review so I'll add an update. After a lot of playtime the game gets really buggy and freezing becomes more common, not sure if it is due to there being more going on or something else in the background. Battles fail to start properly and game needs to be restarted, pathing bugs become more frequent, and game restarts become more time consuming than actually playing the game. Now after an uninstall and reinstall the game won't even start. Not sure what has been going on in the background with game files but clearly, something is broken and reinstalling the game, or verifying file integrity does not solve the issue. Thankfully if I can't resolve it, that should be enough to warrant a charge back if I chose to go that route.

_childDocuments_.review: tldr; if you've played omerta - city of gangsters then it's that with more gangsters and mix in a bit of xcom. Lacks a sense of progression or reward. Minimal depth. Ends up repetitive and lacking. Buy at a discount, or when they finally allow modding.it's o.k.Not very fleshed out imo..I don't see what they did different really here besides the world view being expanded a bit.. but the depth is incredibly lacking. They really could have tied things in better -- always losing track of missions and not able to view multiple mission objectives on-screen at once.. A bit disorganized feeling.. _childDocuments_.review: This is a hard game for me to not recommend it combines a cool theme of the 1920's underground liquor criminal system, XCOM like combat, and a Civ like map. I thought it would be a recipe for success, however, the game falls short in practice. The economy once figured out mainly circulates around having well off breweries and investing heavily in keeping a good stock of booze. You have three ways to make money Speak Easies, Brothels, and Casinos. The first two scale with upgrades which are expensive and honestly are rarely worth the time investment. Casinos make money on an RNG factor and can sometimes break and net you a crazy amount of money if you scale them all the way up though they are frankly useless early on. Though you can pretty much ignore all of this since any game can be ended within an hour since capturing enemies’ breweries will kill their economy and you can just invest in guards and snowball the game from there. The diplomacy system is there but rarely if ever nets you any serious gain and killing an enemy faction is too easy to do. Declare war, Assault Safe house, Murder enemy boss, and now you own their empire and your economy is through the roof. Why pay for upgrades and wait when you can just lose your small business and kill their leader and get them all back and more. That’s what the game boils down to in any given campaign save up money buy gangsters get early kills on gang boss leaders. Then rinse wash and repeat. Any other method is slow and time consuming and doesn’t net the same efficiency. I like the idea of this game but the execution is shallow and feels repetitive after the first couple of campaigns.

_childDocuments_.review: Empire of Sin is absolutely brilliant step-by-step strategy game! Let me tell you why it is so:- It's not so popular nowadays hardcore game: you can choose a difficulty level you like to play the game with pleasure- Game forgives mistakes you can do along the way to victory. It's great! Hate these "one wrong step - your hero is dead!" concepts. Come on, gamers, we are here to have some fun, not for "sweat and blood"... Besides - you don't have enough difficulties in a real life?- Game combines "fast" and "slow" gameplay moments, and it's good. You should do something quick, but after take a break and thing about resource management or advantageous positioning your units on a battlefiled- Environment and Atmosphere of described time-range are ctreated to be 10 out of 10. Each of the characters of your crew becomes dear to you after playing some time. Many of them have a kind of "emotional spirit" if you likeSo my conclusion will be 9 out 10! Big thanks and hugs goes to John and Brenda Romero for the one of the best strategy game I've ever played. Recommended for thouse who like good step-by-step strategy games!

_childDocuments_.review: I was looking forward to this game because it seemed to promise a mix of tactical strategy with city/ business management games.Unfortunately both of these aspects are lacking in the published product. The combat system plays out in mostly very cramped buildings where on turn one a grenade could be thrown by an enemy taking out half your team before you can move them and the inventory management for items and equipment is painfully hard to use.  If there is any way to filter by item or compare two I don't know how or where to look for it.On the overworld and managing I found myself just teleporting around the city to the doorstep of buildings because moving through the streets was pointless, there doesn't seem to be any real issues with running of alcohol in the prohibition, I just found the biggest building I could to make booze in and then instantly sell it in whatever kind of place I take over.  The game encourages such wide playing that I hardly upgraded businesses because I could just take over more for free and not have to deal with small improvements.  The missions came in so fast after the opening that I couldn't even realize what was happening with them, never mind care about the story they presented because there was no clear meaning behind any choice.  It felt cheap to try and make a campaign out of the murder game (see following).After a few hours of try to play mobster defending my neighborhood and dealing more peacefully with those in others, I found out the only way to win or really progress is by murdering the other crime bosses.  Like I can get any gangster I want by calling them up after killing enough people but this dude who has two rackets to my 40 wont take like $50,000 to work for me or just go away?I'll look to come back to this when they release the DLC and hope that they add real functionality and not just new areas with the same bad gameplay loop.

Only seen one bug in the game, where a made-man of mine disappeared from the map so that I couldn't move him anywhere. Reloading an earlier save fixed the situation. Also, it's easy to see how you can get to steamroll the opponents if you move swiftly. Once you find the safehouse, hit them before they become too powerful. This is a game worth your money if management games are your thing. Or if you like X-Com -style battles.

_childDocuments_.review: I was hesitant to buy the game given the negative reviews. Now that I’m familiar with the game, I can see that many of the negative reviews are fake. They are likely written by a small number of people that have some sort of vendetta against the game. I call them fake, because they are from accounts with a small amount of playtime and complain of issues that only come up in late game play that are impossible for those users to have experienced. They do raise some minor issues, but they magnify them out of proportion. So I recommend the game, and if you can get it at a 25% discount, go for it. Any price better than that is steal!With that said, let me begin my review: Enjoyable game! A refreshing atmosphere with some character to enjoy the familiar mechanics from XCOM, but in the world of the roaring 1920s and prohibition!Explore your neighborhood, establishing your local rackets, and inevitable the neighborhood ain't big enough so mob war breaks out. The battles are a fun mix of your boss and powerful gangsters cleaning out the riffraff, defensive battles when riffraff attack your rackets and you only have your guards to defend, to the pinnacle of warfare when you attempt to end another mobster.It’s fun to hire a mix of gangsters with different abilities and weapon proficiencies, and go to war with pistols, sawed-off shotguns, Thompsons, rifles, and even machine guns and bombs!  The gangsters and boss develop some skills slowly over the course of the game.  You will need to hire more powerful gangsters later in the game, as the ones you could afford early just never had the potential to make it all the way to the elite skills that you’ll need to take down Capone and others.The game is not perfect but the defects are minor and the game is very much enjoyable. I’ve spent a few too many late nights, needing to take over just one more racket, with the energetic, tension building music keeping me hooked.Enjoy a fun ride with familiar mechanics and enjoyable atmosphere!

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, took a bit to come to a consesus about this game so let's get to the parts that matter.  Empire of Sin is a very simplified Gangster style XCOM, set in the 1920s during the Prohibition Era: Your goal? Conquer Chicago.  If a combat heavy (not even joking about this part) game of such style is of interest to you, then yes, I do recommend it.If you are however interested in a management focused game, or perhaps not having to fight (every) engagement all manual like, then I recommend sticking clear.  It's a game with a lot of potential, but I personally don't see going past more than one full run before moving onto something else.  Maybe only coming back once in a few months during a dry spell with other games.Each boss you can choose feels somewhat unique, even if their conquest of Chicago plays out largely the same.  While you certainly can spend time upgrading your empire's businesses, there will eventually be so many, and virtually no difference between them, you'll just want whatever increases profit enough to equip your gangsters for upcoming wars with your rivals.  Which can be short and brutal by essentially going straight for the leader, a departure from the methodical approaches of the old Hothouse Gangsters games of yore.Overall I'd say the game's relatively average, but definitely something you can sink hours into and have a degree of fun with.  Whether you'd have the endurance to take each boss onto the path of glory as Chicago's rising kingpin, well that's up to you.I myself, did get my money's worth, even despite various bugs showing up.  Not that detail counts for anything. :PHesitant buyers I strongly recommend waiting for a sale first.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright...Where to start? a couple of months ago I reviewed a similar game that I was expecting called Company of crime that is the same gangster setting but with a different timeline and in England. One of the biggest concerns was the bad design of combat and the fact that you can't explore the city like Empire of Sin. You might ask why I am starting my review with this, and the answer is that people like me that use to play Gangsters Organized Crime back in the day have been waiting for a solid game that can bring that amazing concept once again. On that note, let's start with what I think so far about the game and why I would recommend it. First and foremost, even with some people saying that is null and gets repetitive the game is still fun. The diplomacy might not be relevant but you do enjoy the sit-downs were you can actually negotiate booze, war with factions, and much more. Now the con on this part is that the conversations are too repetitive and the animation sometimes feels not real. For example, Capone always raises his hand the same way for all threatening responses and that feels really simplistic. I do hope this gets fixed. Again diplomacy at this point might not be very efficient, but I do believe it makes the gaming experience more meaningful. Please Devs, if you are reading this, work more on this and add more victory conditions. At this point, the only one you can have is by killing all the gangs and there is no fun in having alliances because they are meaningless. You have rackets, but there is no front for them. How are you going to have an illegal business without any legal business at all? There should be interactions with more NPCs like city officials, judges, witness and such that would add more immersion to the game. The game does feel like a strategy game but sometimes is too cartoonish. For example, some gangsters really don't make sense and this I know can be done better. Also, please add: banks that we can rob and make business in, hotels with more meaningful management, and more rackets. The combat in this game is good but sometimes is dumb. For example, the AI does need some work but for the major part is solid. One issue that combat has is that when you have a lot of guards and gangsters in a small speakeasy, it is very hard to tell who is who because the colors are not very helpful and all the guards look the same. It would be nice if the game could add some type of drive-by feature to kill the guards in front of a building, which would add more to the immersion of the game. Finally, and I don't want to sound that I'm complaining too much, but the game can add the stuff I mention and deliver a true 1920 gangster experience that will make fans of the genre like myself happy. On the bug notes so far I haven't had any issues on my PC, no issues with corrupt save game files, and crashes so on that part I can't say anything bad about it.so I must say at this point 6/10. It is a fun first version of the game but It could be way better. It is a bit pricey, so f you are looking to save money, wait for more work to be done on it and then go for it. But do I recommend this game? Yes, it is a solid concept that just needs some work. Hope this review gets to someone in Romero Games. Thanks for getting this far on this review btw. Cheers and remember power is taken never given!

_childDocuments_.review: Right now, as of 9th Jan '21, the game is not something i would suggest to anyone.The game has a lot of things i love, starting from the fact that's in 1920's Chicago, in the heat of Prohibition-induced criminality. It has the same combat style i love from XCOM and such, with different classes bringing different ways to play encounters. It alsohas the management side of the coin, bringing somewhat intresting combinations of rackets you can stack up for different and better bonuses, all the while choosing who to assign to each different neighbourhood to boost its capabilities.All of this and i still wouldnt suggest it to a friend.The game SUPPOSEDLY has an AUTOSAVE feature. It's ♥♥♥♥. Plain and simple. In nearly 15 hours of game i have seen it work TWO times, while it also takes a few seconds to save. The autosaves are WAAAAAAY to far and few for the amount of times the game crashes.I'm fairly sure i've lost ATLEAST a third of the progress i made in those near 15 hours due to random crashes/softlocks: the game will engage you in a fight and magically it soflocks, nothing you can do. Captured a racket? the game might softlock. Ambushing someone? game might softlock. Entering a racket you own? 1/5 chance it softlocks. playing your combat round? guess what, it probably will softlock every few hours or so.There is nothing you can do. There are a thousand instances in which the game might softlock that will screw you over ROYALLY, expecially considering the game probably autosaves once every few hours. And SPOILER, you cant save when the game softlocks.Right now, i would just suggest waiting a few months for the DEVS to patch the game, atleast reducing the times it crashes/softlocks and having autosaves 10x times. Also QOL accessibility to stuff is to be improved, a lot of things are flat out horrid to find or check.

_childDocuments_.review: A fast-paced, fun empire builder that's relatively easy to learn. Overall, it's worth putting a few hours into, but it will lose its entertainment value pretty quickly, especially once you hit the expansion content.

_childDocuments_.review: This game- Wow- I would like to start the review by saying it is not as terrible as people say it is, there is the basis and concept for a good game here. But it is not very well done. So instead of following what everybody else is saying, i'm going to write down my own personal issues with it.The game plays a lot like Xcom, I have never played the game but looking back on it I should of played that instead. The game is not as large scale as you think it is, as you start out with one gangster who had a ominous reputation. I started out as Al-capone because its a game about gangsters. Now, here is my main issue with the game. You start out with one guy and if you finish the tutorial three. The people you can hire are effected by your fame, or if you help them with a boring side-quest that allows you to get them earlier or for cheaper. This sounds like a okay system, a lot of games use it like Fallout New Vegas, the difference being that the game was story focused and you got invested into the people in your rag-tag team. In this game, they are not designed to be disposable- However, they feel disposable. If one dies they are gone forever. If you loose a good team mate this can be a issue or if you loose too many early game you will have nobody. If your boss dies then you loose so this leads to a spiral where new players assume you can hire the bodyguards (which the AI use as a replacement for the people you can hire) so you can end up either in two situations, the boss is the only one left (which is basically a game over) or you have AI on your ass because they have a infinite number of attacking forces. You have three people. The game tries to counter this by letting you have guards which can level up scattered around your large empire. Mid game-The main issues with mid-game is that by now the early game gangsters that you can hire are probably all dead. Either by your suicidal hiring system or maybe even the AI might of hired some they are set to hire. At this point you probably have a crew of 4, not including you, if they are high level enough maybe you are even at war with some AI factions- This is personally one of the biggest problems I have with this game, the AI has a infinite number of troops against your ill defended speakeasies and breweries. This would not be a problem if you actually levelled up your breweries however chances are that you have not. Another problem is that when I played this game there was no actual auto-resolve meaning you had to fight every single battle, even the ones you were going to loose. The AI can send out a ridiculous number of auto-scouts, and I have no idea why they even made that a thing because if they choose to attack you and you are on your own you are royally ♥♥♥♥♥♥. Seeing as we are talking about the way you make money in this game, its pretty broken. The more footholds you have in your owned territory such as speakeasies, brothels, hotels and breweries means the more customers are likely to visit. This makes it a race against time as you try to fight against the infinite AI troops to settle as much speakeasies or casinos as possible, since those are the only ones worth placing in my experience. I will give credit where it is due, hotels are pretty well done. They are a total gamble as they can either result in a big win or a big loss. As they attract more customers and can provide a bonus if placed near a brothel (; . But that does not really ease out the fact that if you don't place them, there really is no consequence. At this point in the game I controlled a entire neighbourhood and was in the process of taking over another, and I was rich, all this just placing speakeasies and the occasional casino. Really shows that it does not matter what you place. Another thing that just does not matter is the quality of the drink. I had the worst quality on my most recent save, the worst quality is so bad that is called "piss" yet this did not effect anything, in my eyes it just cut costs.Late game-Late game is uneventful, by now you probably control 2 neighbourhoods, maybe 3 if you are better than me, and are virtually invincible unless you get caught out on your own by a AI scouting party, this is where the real issue with the game became so much more obvious to me- Bugs, lots and lots of BUGS. animation breaking, sometimes just a game crash while trying to auto save. The game almost became unplayable at some point for me. e.g- the turns would take so long for some reason, that I thought the game had froze. Especially in big battles, which will happen often thanks to the amount of dumb AI ramming into you non-stop. It would give you a two minute breather sometimes, but considering you could not autoresolve at the time I was playing the game (even now the autoresolve is so clunky you will probably either win or loose based on a single thing) it was a nightmare. At one point I got sick of it and took a break- Such a long break that I never actually came back to it. Ever.Conclusion- The game is pretty sucky, i'm also going to mention the fact that they are releasing DLC and the most of the issues mentioned here are still not fixed. In conclusion, this game is not worth your time, I wish this 15 hours could of been claimed back, I could of got a girlfriend, talked to my family, maybe even got better grades- But since i'm writing this review to you right now what do you think my grades were /: . 4/10, go check out my friends review on Evil Genius 2 instead or maybe buy a decent game idk

What a shame.As other reviewers have discussed, the game is a rinse and repeat with little depth. _childDocuments_.review: Very rare for me to write a review but this I think deserves one.Foreword - This is a Paradox title.... expect things to be heavily supported and patched as we move forwards.Pro'sSetting - Both visuals and sound create an excellent ambience and the character models and speech really play into that era too. Gameplay - This is a mix-up of the original gangsters, omerta and a little port royal for the strategic and business side of it. However the combat side is a different kettle of fish, it is I would say a lite version of XCOM, more similar to something like vigilantes, where it is turn based but not as in-depth as XCOM. For me the balance of these two areas works perfectly, I am not going to get bored of being bogged down in long drawn out fights the way XCOM can be and the risk of permadeath for gangsters you have invested a significant amount of time into their development, really adds to the tension at times.Story/Missions - Having a good time going through some of my gangsters stories and missions as well as the more mainline ones, well-written and quite funny at times.ConsBugs - For me so far, nothing game breaking or really particularly annoying thankfully. Upon death, people coats tend to instantly change to white. When firing a two handed weapon (Shotgun, rifle, machine gun) even though the AP cost says 1, it ends your turn. I have a feeling these are meant to cost 2 AP as they are noticeably more powerful. (to beat this i just switch to my secondary, fire it off and then switch to main and fire it).Depth - There's a lot more than you may realise to fine-tuning and optimising your flourishing empire, than is highlighted in the tutorial. You are guided to a certain extent but then left to figure out the intricacies yourself, this may put some people off as it may be a bit daunting for newcomers to the genre.SummaryOverall I have been pleasantly surprised with this after reading some of the reviews and the poor scores given. I would definitely recommend this as is and it can only get better with future support and DLC!

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games where it's hard to decide whether to recommend it or not.  The game itself, in my 2 hours of play, didn't have any bugs or weird issues but the structure of the game itself makes this a lot less fun than I was hoping.I came into this hoping for a strategic crime family simulator with x-com style combat.  You sort of get that from this game but it's rendered a lot less fun by confusing menus, too much stuff going on, and a frustrating real-time with pause feature.In the game you control a squad of mobsters and can run around a map to attack other factions or neutral thugs to either ransack, destroy, or take over their rackets (the games term for illicit businesses falling into one of five or six varieties).  All of that is, in theory, good however the financial aspect of the game is pretty confusing.  The game seems to favor rapid expansion into rackets rather than upgrading the rackets you have.  I made this mistake early on by spending my early game cash improving my rackets rather than expanding and was stuck in this cycle of having to assault and ransack neutral locations to earn money or go to war with an enemy faction with my 3 gangsters.  The game's tutorial has you recruit two additional gangsters and that ends up costing you $600 in wages when my rackets (2 speakeasies and a brewery) earned somewhere like $400.The financial aspect was manageable but what really frustrated me was the absolute constant bombardment of missions and communications and events.  Within the first 20 minutes of the tutorial ending I was invited to war in conjunction with another faction.  I assumed it was in the neighborhood I occupied but, no, it was in fact a separate neighborhood I'd never been to.  I then was getting attacked in new businesses I got as a result of the war and didn't even know where they were and didn't have the ability to pay to upgrade them due to cashflow issues.I fully admit part of my issues are due to poor play and lack of familiarity with all the systems but the game honestly came off as a convoluted mess that couldn't really decide if it was a strategy game or an X-com game.  I know a lot of reviews have complained about bugs but I didn't really encounter any other than the game seemed very particular about clicking and sometimes something wouldn't work for no apparent reason and then all the sudden start working.  To me, the bigger issue is that the game itself feels haphazard and chaotic in an unfun way.  I never got to feel like I was a crime boss.  I felt like I was a street thug surrounded by bigger fish with the game constantly trying to pull me in 15 different directions and me having no clue what was happening half the time.

_childDocuments_.review: This game deserves it's mixed reviews. It's got some great concepts at its core, and cool ideas, but in its current state it completely fails to be a good gaming experience.Empire of Sin looks like it started as an ode to mafia strategy games like Gangsters: Organized Crime, but quickly got taken over by X-Com. That actually seemed appealing at first, but the two genres never really seem to mesh. Your criminal empire is made up of various "rackets" that generate different amounts of cash depending on various upgrades. There's a deep menu explaining the desires of each ward in the city, and how well the rackets are fulfilling those needs. There are bonuses for adjacency. There are special Hotel rackets that don't generate much income, but do generate more demand. There's a system of prosperity in the wards that changes what people in those wards want at different times in the game.None of that matters. None of it. There are just tons and tons of systems built for a Mafia strategy game that just simply don't matter at all to your success. The real game is in the turn-based combat. Using just a few men, you can easily take over most enemy rackets as they only start with 2 guards, and upgrading security is expensive, and takes a while. That means that most combat is a breeze, and by the mid-game you'll be dominating almost all battles.When you get to a certain point you'll be able to reliably take down enemy safe houses, which are the only challenging battles in the game. Once that happens, the game is just a few battles from being over, as taking out an enemy safe house nets you their entire empire all at once. That just makes the game feel like it could have been re-tooled to be a story-driven turn-based squad combat game, and strip out the totally unnecessary strategy sim. I don't know how to fix this. Maybe it's just core balance issues. Maybe Rackets need to start with more defenses by default so you can't just plough your way through the game with combat, but as it stands right now the game doesn't "work".That being said, I see a lot of complaints about bugs, and I only ran into one bug while playing, and it was fairly minor (a character always appeared to be dead, but functioned properly otherwise). Maybe some of the bugs are under control now.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't let the mediocre reviews from the critics turn you off the game, most of them got their copies before the Day 1 patch. The XCOM fights arent difficult by any means unless you crank the difficulty, but not everyone (myself included) needs a strategy game with soul-crushing difficulty.  Management of your businesses is mostly fire and forget, unless you piss off the wrong person - then you need to scramble to take out their guys before they take you out.  The missions arent noticable or exciting most of the time, but you really should do them because they give you some very nice rewards.Edit:  Bugs are also semi-prevalent, but nothing moreso than annoyance as of now.  Characters have an irritating habit of not moving a long distance once you have a big enough group, but it can be fixed by "waypointing" (making multiple shorter moves) or by just skipping it using the fast-travel to a closer point you want.All in all, this game has a huuuuuuge amount of potential, and i would totally recommend it to anyone who likes strategy games in the vein of XCOM, especially if you happened to like Chimera Squad.  I do hope the devs decide to keep pouring their love into this game, though.

_childDocuments_.review: About 12 hours played as of review in March 2021.Initial impression: 6 out of 10, based on potential. Unless you are bored or super curious, wait another 6 months.Game is passable but needs more improvement. Has the potential to be a lot better: key issue is to remove the tedious repetitiveness after a few hours.Some suggestions / weaknesses at the moment:- Need more ways to make money. The current way is to either go to war with another gang, take over their racket; or create a new racket from scratch by seizing an abandoned building (more or less the same thing). This gets repetitive. There should be a way to, for example, raid rackets of other gangs (without automatically starting a war), rob a store, and collect passive protection money. - The economy and $ values are a bit nonsensical. I could buy a crow bar or other melee weapon for approx 7,000. It costs less to open a new business, or even hire someone. Gangs will offer to pay you protection money of $70 a week. Why bother. It also feels like income from rackets is a bit low.- Combat: Not bad, but not exactly Xcom. A few things scream out to me: melee seems far too inaccurate to be useful and guns are too accurate. Some of the physics is crazy; I am shooting people with 90% accuracy across impossible angles, but i have less than 50% accuracy when trying to punch someone in the face at point blank range? Executing people seems to have no benefit at all.- to break up the monotony, they should have some combat missions to be timed (similar to xcom). Eg rob a bank and get out in less than 6 moves. - fewer gangs so defeating someone feels meaningful.- The grappling hook is immersion breaking and should be scrapped immediately. It also allows you to drag people through walls, which is absurd.- diplomacy: While at war, the only option is to seek a truce. If I am winning by a lot, I should be able to force a concession on my opinion (money, territory) on the loser (just copy the concept from other paradox games).- lieutenants: you shouldn't lose a combatant for appointing one-encountered a few bugs. Eg at war with someone but impossible to initiate combat, or it says I have lost a battle when in fact I have won.- automate explore function for gang members. AI does this, but human cant- right now one ends up spending too much time on combat, but combat is fairly boring. I would push the game towards more management and less combat and it'll be interesting.

_childDocuments_.review: I kept coming back to this game because I love the genre. And to be fair, I think  has an overall aesthetically pleasing set of presentation values. From the music in the background to the sound effects to the styling--you name it, this game brings a lot of style to deliver on its promise. I just like the look, feel, and so much about it. I think that's why I couldn't give up on it. I bought it and refunded it at least twice before finally picking it up as cheap as it's ever likely to get during the 2024 summer sales.Beyond mere looks, I can also say there's a fair bit of compelling game play to be had here. The turn-based combat portion is enjoyable to a point. I like the variety in classes of criminal and the different skill trees they bring to the table. I don't think it all works quite as well as some other games with similar mechanics, but I've tried a couple different bosses and can honestly say there's room to play in different ways. I think my favorite is Sai Wing Mock for his ability to throw devastating poison bombs. It's such a powerful skill, especially when you can make him a melee brawler and do it again after three turns of cutting down fools with single strikes.But here's why I have to give this game an overall yet qualified negative review: it just doesn't hold up for long. For the first six to ten hours I was still running into new things, learning, and enjoying finding my way in the gangster world. But somewhere around that time frame I'd pretty much seen it all. I hung on until hour fifteen because I'd basically been screwed over by Al Capone and swore myself an oath I'd put him in the ground. Doing so was very satisfying, though it was as long protracted battle that cost me one good gang member to wounds and another due to affairs of the heart.But beyond that, there's honestly little to no reason to keep playing. I'm already clearly the most powerful faction in the entire game. Expanding into other neighborhoods and taking over more rackets has essentially become grunt work. And the promise of what's left for me is... well... doing that same thing over and over again in the next neighborhood and the next and the next and... I just don't think it holds up for long.The bugs and obviously re-worked systems don't help either. I've run into a few real show-stopper bugs along the way. And I hate how some of the mechanics--like the adjacency requirement for precincts, the lines connecting one neighborhood to another, etc.--feel like they were added simply to pad runtime. For crying out loud, I'm playing as a criminal: I'm  to ignore rules and red lines in the sand! Sheesh.In the final analysis, I absolutely got my money's worth. I paid something like $10 for the game and had a solid 10+ hours of genuine fun. I'm a real sucker for this genre of games, so if you're like me and are desperate for another title in this under-served field, then you could probably have fun with it too. But I think for most players it's just not going to be worth your money. There are plenty of better games out there. Especially now that the publisher and/or developers have basically stopped working on the game, even screwing people who bought the promised second DLC out of their money. The game isn't great as it is, and it's just not going to get any better it seems. What a pity.

_childDocuments_.review: PRECINCT PATCH REVIEW:Always love when developers put i the time to improve their game and the precinct patch is a meaty update that makes the game more robust.  The issue here is that the difficulty gating still revolves around slowing things down.What makes the game more difficult in BOSS level vs the lower settings?- no passive healing- significantly lower starting cash- more difficult AI settings for trades / negotiating and making business arrangementsAt it's core, this is a great game but still falls short in terms of replayability.  The precinct patch makes it so you have better management of your neighborhoods but also tries to gate you by not allowing you to jump all over the place when taking over new properties.  All you need to do is just hire more guns, expand quickly, then shift into peace mode and start upgrading your properties in a certain order (upgrade alcohol quality -> abience -> word of mouth -> only upgrade deflect when the police activity is increasing) then hire a bunch more guns and go take over the rest of Chicago.This falls on the scale of sideway thumb.  Buy if it's on sale and only if you really like this genre type of games.ORIGINAL REVIEW (100 hrs of gameplay)If you combined XCom, Civ and The Godfather you would get a pretty awesome game.  Sadly Empire of Sin probably only gets 60% of the way there.I read a bunch of reviews but I decided to try this anyway and I completely understand all the frustrations that most reviews mention:- menus and controls are a bit clunky + too many excessive pop up alerts- turn based combat?  just bring more guns to the gun fight, not much strategy here- uneven pacing & leveling: I have restarted my game 3 times now to keep upping the difficulty, I am not a good gamer and would not have been able to do a first playthrough on a higher difficulty but once you figure out the "bring more guns" and get your economy going it gets a bit mundane.I really really do not like leaving negative feedback but I can't quite recommend this game.  I will play a bit more on the higher difficulty since there are tons of posts mentioning that the game gets fun / challenging in the higher levels but I do not see myself playing this again once I rinse through it to my satisfaction.I will probably end up reinstalling XCom and Civ 5 and just rotate between those two.  Or maybe I'll load up The Godfather because even though its super old, that one has a better story and makes being a mobster feel more fun.

_childDocuments_.review: I played around for 11.2 hours on the lieutenant difficulty. Beating game on the in game date of Sep 14 1920 by just clearing out the other mobsters. I beat the game without doing the quest the game gives you at the very start. Even beating the game the day I got it. You have a number of different bosses to chose from. With there people being from Hungary to China available for you to play as. Other bosses willing to team up with you more if you come from the same place as them or your personality match theirs. Which is what I saw in one youtube video on the game. Gameplay wise I love it. You have these different abilities to play with from your boss’s special ability to hinchmen’s abilities. With pistols to machine guns. Semi-autos to fully automatic weapons. The people you hire can be formed up how you like them to playEach henchmen have different relationships with other characters. Which may cause them to leave if you shoot the people they love. Which happened to me once in the game. The racket system is rather simple. You produce liquor for your speakeasy. Liquor to make your Casino visitors not be able to think. And you have hotels to bring people into your neighborhood to increase the amount of customers. If the customer’s tastes in liquor change, you can change the production of your breweries. I love the naming feature as it's fun to name something you owned after taking it over or buying it. There is diplomacy from trading to allying yourself with others against other bosses. I barely used it except for declaring war on everyone.There were only a few issues I had with the game. Fast Travel was too easy to use since there are taxis all over the place. My run as Sai Wing Mock Usually involved me fast traveling and poison bombing the guards out of nowhere. Another issue is that the boss' abilities are op. Sai Wing Mock’s ability can allow you to throw three bombs which poison an area for the rest of the battle. I usually clear out most of the guards in the battles thanks to me having three bombs. This would be more balanced if Mock could only throw two bombs. The third issue is that the unique items you get from the bosses are worth the risk of killing the bosses. Unique items pretty much turn your Zeros into Heros. I gave my mercs the unique items and they easily did their jobs well. It makes me wish the items could only be obtained through special side quests or could only be found in random locations. Another issue is that the other bosses very little through the game use their abilities. The only boss I saw use theirs was Genna after I ended most of the other bosses. When he threw knives at my gang during my raid on his safe house. Another issue I had with this was that you could beat this game with low tier mercs. The bosses only have one merc with them. With them usually being a medic. In the end I never got my hands on the best mercs and just swarmed the last bosses with low tier mercs carrying unique weapons.There is one issue I have that is a single glitch. The first one and only one I encountered was that gangsters from other gangs stick around after their bosses are dead. I had an encounter with the Vice Kings long after their boss was dead. By this time I’m pretty sure there was already a funeral for Jackson. It didn’t bother me much until I raided Colt’s safe house. After I defeated the White Circus while they were at war with Colt. I got war declared on me by Colt. I went in and the White Circus had the last laugh. As the White Circus guards teamed up with Colt and his gang. Making it impossible for me to take over Colt’s Safe house. So reloaded a save and waited for Dyer to kill Colt before I killed her.  Also during the lieutenant mode, I spent little on my rackets and never got raided by the police. I wish the game rewarded you for spending time waiting for more money even though you are strong enough to end the other bosses careers.Despite the issues, this was a fun game to play. It's a lot easier compared to Paradox’s other games like EU4 or HOI4. Though it could use a lot of additions to make the game a bit more complex then how it is. Which can be added over time with DLC.

_childDocuments_.review: On my 3rd playthrough I thought I'm trying to accomplish total control of the city, solo."this may take a while"So I'm taking it easy, trying to avoid the bugs mentioned on this forum and elsewhere, but that's (like many have said before) impossible. SO I try the 2nd best option... play with the bugs. Not all of them break the game entirely, and with careful saving and loading most of the bugs can be 'reset' and some even help the player, untill fixed.- For example: I'm getting the +20 health recovery from melee weapons, on my rifle shots.I managed to turn Angelo Genna into a solo beast. With all weapon-proficiencies maxed, this isn't that hard on any character I supose.All-in-all, I'm having a great time, between a couple of bug related reloads.SO far, perhaps nothing new for a couple of players that may just have been faster with the battles and conquering all 10 neighbourhoods. During all this I used the run to get a better feel for the economic side of things. Getting the racket bonuses, figuring out that upgrading ambience in them helps, run down, dangerous neighbourhoods back up to a more profitable level.And all this time I'm wondering how many of the players, have actually taken the time (and plenty effort) to work through the obvious flaws (bugs etc.) to do this as well.I've taken the challenge and came out the other end with a whole bunch of quests I had not seen before during the more "safehouse storming, boss killing, taxi teleporting" playthroughs I've done and read about, here.I'm going to put it out there...I think this is a solid game, that may or may not have been rushed near the end of production coming up on a releasedate. So it misses the finishing touches to make everything run smoothly. It may not be of the same caliber as, let's say "cyberpunk" but suffers from what I gather, a lot from the same production issues. Too much hype too soon, potential buyers, seeing all that good PR stuff roll over the Internet, wanting a piece of the action. Studios wanting to keep the fleeting attention spans of the Social Media Generation, focused on their product. Saturated Steam libraries with hundreds of games to choose from and nothing is up to the high standards of the "hardcore" gamers. Besides they probably already bought 3 new games on the next steam sale. Played those for half an hour and bash the producers and studios in the same manner, they do for this game.Nobody wants to accept that todays endless options lead to even more desire/greed, on both ends. Producers and studios feel the pressure to release a new title, in fear of losing their fanbase amongst the tons of other studios. The gamers have so many games to chose from, they throw any new title in the bin as easily as a banana with 1 little brown spot.Because we throw our money at the screen, we feel entitlement, the screen shows our wildest dreams and deepest wishes. And then anger, when it doesn't live up to our expectations.I, for one, enjoy this game thoroughly and don't regret the money spend. A little regret perhaps, that I fell into the trap of buying a new game on release, that obviously should have been given more time to be finished. But willing to support the designers with feedback, other than the profanity filled stuff I read elsewhere.If you beat the dog too often, he's not going to listen, or behave better.Let's hope Romero Studios and Paradox, are still willing to listen, and help the players to a better gaming experience. Then perhaps we actually get to enjoy the game they intended to make.

_childDocuments_.review: This game broke my heart a little bit... It's bad.I love gangster themed games. I have a particular love for the "management of the business" type of gangster game. Much like many of the other reviews, I was excited for a "Gangsters: Organized Crime" successor. This game promised that, throwing in some tactical turn-based combat (which I love too), as well as characters/stories to drive forward a motivation and a story (although not necessary, as I would prefer to write my own gangster story).This game pretends to do a lot of different things, and spectacularly fails at all of them. The "management" is laughable, the stories/voice acting is comically poor, and the turn-based combat is an abject failure.It's still buggy too in it's early state (so these will likely be patched after the time of writing this review), I have already had to restart the game twice as certain actions were not progressing (in a 90 minute run). The pathfinding is also a joke, with characters often not moving at all, and preferring to get intimate with nearby wall. This game feel like it was made to bank on a subset of interested fanatics (people who love gangster themed games), instead of being made to satisfy a particular itch that many of us have had for years.Paradox are really "Hit and Miss" with recent game launches. In some instances reading their target audience with lazer point precision, and others completely missing the mark and sparking anguish in their attempt. This one is a bit of a step too far for me. And I will not be pre-ordering a Paradox game until after user reviews are in. Paradox employee a fantastic team of creators to peddle their rubbish, so I cannot even trust some of my favourite channels to provide me with valuable consumer advice until well after the fact.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to like this game, I really do. I love Paradox Interactive, I think they're a fantastic studio/publisher. They've got some of my favorite games under their belt (Surviving Mars/Aftermath, Stellaris, etc), and I like the setting, music, and ambiance. The primary problem, in my opinion, comes from the game play. It's part of the core game play loop so I'm not sure if or how it could be fixed. The combat in this game is the turn based, grid based, isometric style any X-Com player would recognize. It is significantly simpler than X-Com2, which came out almost 5 years ago.  It gets repetitive, quickly, and there is a lot of it. Oh boy is there a lot of it. Seems like, with few exceptions when you're focusing on base building for a few minutes, there is a generated fight every 5 minutes or so. The maps get repetitive (you'll see repeats within the first 5 fights), it's basically the same 3-5 bad guy set up each time. It just is too much of the same thing. I would have liked to see this game focus a greater emphasis on base building / empire management. I'm sure the world opens up more as you progress. I've got 9 hours logged on the game in two playthroughs (I restarted after realizing it wasn't a great idea to pick a fight with Capone as a newbie, but the combat is easy enough where you think it might be.) I don't know, I want to like this game. It's got great flavor and the world building based on characters' backstories slowing coming out through interactions with other bosses is an interesting set up. It's just that you see that combat screen way too frequently for how simplistic the fighting actually is. Hopefully the fighting gets more complex, or the frequency gets turned down, but I cannot recommend this game in it's current state. Go find Omerta: City of Gangsters (Kaplyso Media game from 2013) for a few bucks on sale somewhere and you're getting a lot of the same game for 90% cost reduction.

_childDocuments_.review: So its been several months since this game has been released. I have come back to make some updates.While they have addressed a lot of the issues and concerns with this game there are still a lot of things left on the table that could have made this a much better experience.There are still a lot of bugs, especially those regarding your rackets and synergies. Tons of animation bugs, and various others. Nothing seemingly game breaking, or at least not quite as much as there was before.Some issues I have with the game...Maps are so small, and so repetitive. There are only a hand full of maps for indoors locations, and they get repetitive pretty quick as they are generally very small, and the enemies can just run from one side to the other in one turn to melee you. Some of the bosses will still continually spam you with standing offers even when you consistently decline them. The AI is pretty dumb, they tend to always rush you, it would be nice to see something like Omerta, where they would actually hold cover. Speaking of cover, its about the dumbest thing ive ever seen... When someone is hiding behind full cover and you target them to shoot them, they will just lean out of cover to let you shoot at them, kind of defeats the entire point of being in cover. I know this is done to make it look realistic when you hit them vs hitting them through a wall, but why would you hide behind cover just to stand well out of it every time you are shot at?Just about every one use item has the same one or two animations. If you use a healing tonic, you drink from a big jug, if you use SMELLING SALTS, you drink from a big jug. A little variation would have been nice.The very limited amount of dialog lines for the enemies to speak get very old very fast. When you're in a fight with 10 enemies and they all say the same 2 lines when the battle starts, and over half of them say the same thing when they die. Id just as soon have them say nothing at all. Nitpicky, but every sit down scene with a boss runs through the same couple animations, generally hand waving everything said by the other boss.Not getting into great detail, but its improved slightly over the launch offering. Hopefully it gets better.

_childDocuments_.review: I really do wish they had a neutral/check again later option vs Yes/No.  For now though, I have to vote no. I like the concept of the game, it just feels really unfinished.  Like it's an early access or beta.Combat feels like they tried to mimic xcom style games, but maybe haven't quite played those games.  It needs more polish and variety.  Strategic layer is both insanely overwhelming and underwhelming at the same time.  I know right? The overwhelming part is there are so many things going on and at such a frantic pace, you cannot keep up.  I ended up ignoring the some 50 missions I had simply because everything else was going on.  Forced to meet bosses from 10 factions despite only just visiting my burrow.  Forced into wars, a few missions etc.  Maybe if the speed could be adjusted on how many things are thrown at the player at once it'd be a good thing.The underwhelming part... You don't have to bother taking pieces and parts of another bad guy's area. just go take his safe house and you get everything he owned.  I took two guys like this before I really ever understood the complexity of how my own structures work with one another. Heck I still don't really, but I'm in the process of taking over a 4th bosses safehouse and territories. I think the team has something that could potentially be an amazingly fun game to play, but it needs to have some more thought put into combat, strategic layer and the speed at which a human can actually process and think about everything thrown at them.  Hoping they can re-evaluate, re-engineer and fix some of these issues over the next year.  Then maybe it'll be worth the $.  Certainly doesn't feel worth full price atm.
