_childDocuments_.review: I am only a couple hours in however I really do need to give this one a thumbs up. Yes the AI isn't the best (Neither is XCom's which is considered the "best" in this genre of combat systems) and there are a hefty amount of bugs. I am having a blast so far. The settings, weapons, music, atmosphere, characters. There's a lot of systems in play and they mostly work.  My biggest gripe so far is the lack of customisation. The trait system and the way your gangsters can form relationships is absolutely awesome. Far deeper than anything other games of this variety have pulled off. However where they're all pre-set characters I do find it hard to get immersed in their story. Definitely needs some bugfixes and a user created "Sandbox" mode. If I want my Italian Mafia to be all Italians that should be my choice, having some Irish debt collector, a scottish ex-miltiary guy & a west-indies singer as my "gangsters" in my ITALIAN MAFIA is very immersion breaking. I look forward to playing more!

_childDocuments_.review: I think the main take away from the game is that depending how you feel it is either not sure what it wants to be or it was a gamble that did not entirely pay off.The main systems that I view in this are X-Com (Remake) combat, Gangsters (late 90's game) concept, along with some very light business management, and quest and RPG elements.  On it's surface, those are all very good ideas and if they're put together, I would absolutely adore this game because it's what I want.  However, it suffers from 'just missed the mark' on every one of the things it sought to bring to the table and it leaves one wanting.X-Com style combat?  Unpolished and inconsistent with damage, character ability, mechanic function, item availability and trait development.  I'm not sure how the X-Com turn based firefight which has turned into the new standard could be so glitchy and difficult to implement for the studio.Light business management?  It's not as deep as the number of screens likes to make it seem.  It lacks any refinement and the depth of interaction that the Gangsters Game had with it's industries and businesses.  All money is the same, any structure is the same, the five illicit businesses are the same no matter where they are.  You can stick five casinos next to each other and they function the same with the same income, ditto with brothels, or speakeasies.  Fifteen illegal bars on the same block have zero impact on how much they earn.  Changes are incremental at best, and have no real effect.  There's no real techniques to hide anything other than investing in 'deflections' nothing as refined as Gangsters of hiding brothels in legit hotels, or speakeasies inside of resturants...just click the box and you're good.Quest and RPG Elements.  The game wants you to think that you're an RPG, that you have dialogue choices with other gangsters, make deals, have an effect on them.  Wants you to think that they might actually act differently depending on how much they like you and your behavior towards them affects the relationship you have.  Nope, someone can be polite and professional in a meeting, or act really friendly, and have MASSIVE debuffs towards you that makes war inevitable.  Your character can only click on tribute and hope that will help.The game wants to be far more than it is, far, far more than it is.  And while it's not a horrible game, it just does not really nail anything so well that you overlook the exceptionally mediocre other aspects of the game that miss their mark.  It might be worth getting if you haven't played the other games that this one is borrowing from, but if you're here, you already have.  It will get better when there's a modding community, and probably after the standard Paradox DLC business plan kicks in, until then, give it a pass.

_childDocuments_.review: So far so good. It's not the deepest game yet, but so far, I'm excited to start my Irish Empire of Sin with the Donovan Gang.I really like the graphics. Makes me feel like I'm in the 1920s. The characters and mobsters are interesting. I like how the mobsters have personalities, enemies, loves and friends amongst their associates, and bios. Reminds me of Jagged Alliance (Which Brenda Romero, designer of this game, worked on, so it makes sense). Each Mob Boss has similar spread of talents and bonuses to their empire, so take the one whose personality and looks match your desire. They all have fun personalities and voices.As for the strategic layer, it's not super deep, but it isn't boring either. I like taking over my neighborhood, taking out mobsters and enemy crime families.Combat is typical turn-based X-Com fare. You can buy new weapons and gear to equip your mobsters with and go at it with other mobsters. It's satisfying trapping a mob boss with overwatch and finishing him off with an execution.It's not as deep as Gears Tactics, but it's fun, and definitely better than Omerta.I like the music and presentation most of all. I think with the DLC and patches Romero games can really add some improvements if they will listen to the feedback of people here and elsewhere. I'd recommend the game. I think it will improve with time, and it's not terrible as is. I enjoy it so far.

_childDocuments_.review: Empire of Sin is a mess.  The common refrain seems to be it's just buggy and while it's certainly incredibly buggy that's not the extend of the game's issues.On the topic of bugs, in the fourteen or so hours I've played I've had multiple Quest triggers fail, animations routinely fail to load (with a handful of game ending freezes) and a dead man requesting we end our War.  I'm running the game on all of the preset settings.  This is literally the first run any playtester should have ran.  Take a glance at the official bug forums ( httpsforum.paradoxplaza.comforumforumsempire-of-sin-bug-reports.1086 ) and just read the thread titles as it's is a comedy goldmine.Now to the meat of the game; There are two major modes of gameplay.  The first and the one you'll be spending most of your time in is the combat.  There's UI issues abound and for the sake of brevity here's a quick list;Firing a Primary weapon ends your turn, firing a Secondary does not.  To swap to a Secondary requires you to, well, click the swap command and confirm.  Simple enough, yeah  There are literally two options for your secondary Fire and Reload (a Secondary Shotgun will have a Cone AoE option as well).  An average turn when you don't have to move is  SWAP Weapon  FIRE Weapon  SWAP Weapon  FIRE Weapon.  Just add the two options to the basic bar!  Fire (Primary) and Fire (Secondary) along with Reload (Primary) and (Secondary).The UI will list multiple instances of the same options - My Maria has three end turns.  They all do the same thing.  This is likely a bug, but it's pretty easy to figure out why it happens.  One of her Perks is to take a move after an attack.  This added it's own End Turn option.  As did another ability.Now we're actually playin', baby!  Well great, here's the thing about Weapon Balance.  There isn't any.  In a comical flaw, Burst Weapons roll to hit for each bullet.  This means that anyone that can wield a [Sub]Machine Gun should target the hardest to hit enemies.  45% to Hit  I'll take those odds on my five rounds every turn.  Oh, while we're here attacks are only modeled against the characters selected.  So if you hit and kill an enemy with your first bullet in a Burst fire the guy directly behind will not take any damage at all.  If you miss a guy in the middle of a crowd you will *never* hit anything.  Jagged Alliance and X Com had this in the early/Mid Nineties.Enemy AI is dreadful.  They charge.  Everyone.  Every time. Seriously.  This was supposed to be brief.  Jesus.The Available Gang members page is static game to game.  Getting the higher tier Gangsters means playing with the lower ones.  Every single game.  But don't fret!  The bonuses you get for using Characters means that you'll likely want extra bullets in your Burst fire conga line over a slight boost in higher stats anyways.The Second part of the tactical portion of the game is moving and controlling or defending the streets.  This is made laughable by a couple of systems.  Chiefly that your crew can instantly teleport to any location you have revealed on the map by right clicking on a building and selecting Travel Here.  The game gives you a notice of where the enemy is planning to attack so you can teleport to a location, massacre the assailant and repeat, with virtually zero time taken off the in game clock.Now you're given a map and on that map are various buildings, and most of them allow for you or rival gangs to control them as Rackets which feeds into the Economic side of the game (oh we'll get there).  You may attack and take over enemy turf.  Of which there is one map of each type per size of location.  The first, second and twentieth assault on a Mid Size Speakeasy will be the same location.  Any every time in between.Thankfully, there's a helpful catch pre programmed into the game for you. Successfully attacking an enemy Safehouse knocks that Rival out of the game... and grants you their entire empire.  There is no reason to ever attack an enemy Racket.  If you need quick cash, take out an identical derelict building or three.  It's way easier and it's way more beneficial for you to just declare War and take everything all at once against a Rival by teleporting directly to their front door and waging the shortest War ever.The game tries to discourage your time and space bending gang by having you not heal between battles.  But there's no different damage states.  So if you heal in mid battle you'll come out flawlessly....Which leads to pushing the Control key to instigate a sneak attack in your area, and in this case on nothing and then pressing Tab until you get your doctor and using their skill to heal.  And ending combat, clearing their cooldown, and doing it again.  Near instantaneously. On to the Economics!Want infinity money  Sell garbage alcohol to the smaller, Minor Gangs disguised as Whiskey.  For some reason, they have infinite money and will always accept your deal.Which is better than engaging with the actual systems present.  Your income randomly rises and falls, based on Customers Winning Big at your Casinos.  But you never get a notification that your House just took a loss.  It seems like it tallies up all of this at the start of a week instead of being organic and shifting through the day.Become a gun runner.  Sell everything you don't need. It's simply less miserable than trying to figure out how all your Rackets collide in it's huge mess.  It's almost indecipherable at the start of the game when you've got three buildings.  It's the spreadsheet from Hell by the time you're out of your starting Neighbourhood.Diplomacy!Hahahahahahahaha oh dear God I'm done.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is quite repetitive, you will spend time killing mindless thugs to build up cash or take over buildings. You can never call a meeting from behind your desk in your safe house and carefully plan your next move and send out your lieutenants to carry out hits. Everything is the character you pick running full sprint about the map doing same stuff basically. The business management aspects are bland as it can possibly get, and honestly you never at any moment feel you're running a "empire" but you will begin to feel a land rush attitude to take turf/new buildings constantly, least enemy get the upper hand. My biggest beef is the playable characters besides a couple aren't interesting at all, everytime you click them they repeat same cheesy phrase. Example Dion will repeat stuff like "I will be there in 2 shakes of a lambs tail!" Yeah he is a true gangster, I get shivers just listening to his corny 1 liners. The fact we have to use and look at our characters a lot and frankly they're bland. We can't gain outfits nor gear we can see visually change their appearance. Also some characters look as if they've had more TLC like Al Capone, he looks nice with nice strong details on his outfit/face. You can tell time wasn't taken for example Frank Regan whose 1 color outfit looks rushed down to his blurry MS paint tie. Then there's the voice acting or lack there of... its just not good and characters like Reyna are just plain bad with voicing. The dialogue isn't great either and I never felt like at any moment it even mattered, again bland. Its not terrible its just not good.The game gives you a list of characters you can hire at a big cost and a cut to your business earnings. They will run with you to fight etc. they're like crew members like in XCOM, but they're premades with small stories, background, traits. A lot have goofy outfits you can never change like a nurses outfit or ww1 style military officer outfit. They don't give gangster nor everyday vibes, they're very cliche. The world seems bland and everything seems like a rehash or a copy same object gives little reason to look at your surroundings because you've seen them all so many times in first hour you don't care anymore... this includes building interiors.Honestly there's little going for this title beyond 15 hours I'd probably put into it. The game does alot of things, but none of these things are great. If you feel spending $40+ on 10-25 hours worth of content is for you? Go for it, everyone is different. I mean this game could be good with a lot of content patching, DLC, and dev love over next 2 years for now I can't play it.. this is bugs aside, it's just not good. I will come back and check the game out in future, I love gangster movies and was hyped for this game but I fear if I keep it I will play 10-15 hours. Anyways, helpfully this bit of rambling helps someone out, I am not expert its only my humble opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: I was hoping for a new version of 'Gangsters: Organised Crime', an 1998 game that was a mix of planning, crew & empire management with the chance to cause havoc with the police and your opposition. Is it? Not exactly and that may be a good thing however in it's current state, it is a jack of all trades and master of none. You go from empire management in paused screens, turn-based combat (xcom style) in battle on the street or in buildings and real time while on the street, whether zoomed in to street level or over the city boroughs mapGraphics, audio and visuals are all good (some minor random glitching that fixes itself). Storyline tries but is weak at best with very similar mission lines for each playthrough (in theory each boss has their own unique story and mission lines but the generic stuff is too heavy and eats into the replay value)Gameplay is great to start with but soon becomes very repetitive. I made a playthrough last longer by being more purposely slow to expand but it is not difficult to just go all out. There are definitely some balance issues that need to be addressed. You can easily hire to many gangsters and kill your income through wages and appointing specialised roles seems more harmful than helpful at this time.Overall I don't want to be negative but try to be honest. it is a fun game, I enjoy it and continue to play it. I look forward to the upcoming updates with Precinct mode which looks to offer some variety and expand on replay value. I think it is worth picking up and given what they've learnt from this... a future update, dlc or sequel could something special.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is inherently flawed.The major gameplay and the economics are not at odds with each other, but they're essentially two passing ships in the night. I could probably play this game forever without having to spend money. I never would though. The combat is shallow. Some brand spanking new director said "hey we can do isometric turn based combat" and they made the basic implementation, brought in some cool, historically accurate firearms, then ♥♥♥♥♥♥ off to god knows where while the animation team was struggling to fix everything when this game first released.The combat is a pale imitation of the combat loop from a game like the XCOM reboot. It copies essentially all of the mechanics for the combat classes from that game, but without any of the depth to the combat encounters. Every single combat starts with you knowing exactly where the enemy is, the enemy knowing exactly where you are, and you are more often than not, in one of several incredibly repetitive and claustrophobic. The enemy is limited to the exact same classes, meaning you lose out on things like the asymmetric combat against the aliens from that game, or the mission variety. I have ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ never been able to finish the story to one of these boring ass characters, so there might be some tiny amount of variation, but I doubt its worth suffering through.There is also an incredibly pointless and essentially out of place RPG mechanic. Your Gang boss and hired hands all have stats, modified by their backgrounds, but almost all of them are safely ignored. Its not that there is absolutely nothing there, but they're so varied and so ticky tack that my mind smooths over. The only useful non-combat skills are the ones that you can use in the story missions to avoid the combat or avoid paying people to do ♥♥♥♥ for you.I think the worst system here is the districts and neighborhoods. Each district represents a famous area of Chicago, like the Loop, and each district is cut up into neighborhoods, which are the arbitrary blocks where you are going to have your various rackets. You have to ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ fight for each ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ block. If another main character gang doesn't have it on lockdown, it'll be controlled by generic "thugs" with enough firepower to shift the Somme. You need to take the central safehouse/alcohol store in order to take the block over and even begin to profit from it. There are like, 10 neighborhoods in a district, give or take. You can see what I'm getting at. Its a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ repetitive slog.The second most annoying ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ system is the notoriety system. In order to get effective gangsters on your payroll, you need notoriety. Notoriety is gained mostly by completing missions, cornering rackets, and murdering more schmucks than were ever involved in racketeering in Chicago. Unless you kill another boss, you'll have to commit a Valetine's Day massacre every month for like 8 years to even hire the people with decent stats. Watching that number go up is like watching my life tick away.Its like someone took Saints Row 2, then decided to make it a procedurally generated rogue like with the main character being essentially a Civilization 6 leader for their little gang. Except Saints Row 2 was more emotionally impactful than any of the story on display here and was actually a decent copy of what it was trying to ape. Its not a game where you go from small time gangbanger, controlling a block, to kingpin, controlling industrial crime in the city. Its like Dark Heresy in a Hiveworld without any of the things that would make a Hiveworld fun. No highrise firefights, no fancy balls, no huge warehouses, no docks, no variety. You fight on the street or you fight in an indoor dumpster.I can't even damn this game with faint praise. Its a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ chore to play. Every 20 feet some random ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ is telling me, whoever random mad bomber/mass murderer/war criminal I am playing as, that I need to do the random ♥♥♥♥ they tell me to. Its like watching my attention being split thinly with a razor like that scene with the garlic in Goodfellas.Avoid this ♥♥♥♥ like the plague. Do not waste your money or time.

_childDocuments_.review: Bottom line up front: Paradox already made buckets off of everyone that has bought this game, and they really don't care about the state of the game.  This is an MVP; the execs know it (and don't care), the product owners know it but pushed for something half decent, the devs know it and are slaved with work, and the playtesters know it sucks.  We'll only start getting quality games at launch when people stop pre-ordering/buying them at launch.The game is fun, but too easy.  XCOM but the aliens are Italians is perfect, except the Italians are fat and weak.  The game has long-term potential, but the economy isn't thought out and the fights are too easy.  There's so much that could be had with the alcohol procurement/delivery process, but instead there's a shell of a system there.  Additionally, I was really hoping to be able to customize the different rackets, but instead it's a phone-game-esque "upgrade this but oh wait you can rush it immedately for .5x!' ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.  And why bother since you can just take something else over in 10 minutes with little combat skill.The game was certainly released too early--but all the negative reviews surprised by that shouldn't be.  This is, after all, a Paradox game, and this has been their M.O. since Stellaris originally launched (if not before then).  It will eventually become a strong game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is based on early impressions so I may come around on it, but so far it's hard to find a reason to want to keep playing.The main thing I dislike about this game is how mindless and devoid of tactical thinking the combat is. Both your units and the enemy units have so much health that getting hit doesn't feel like a significant consequence, and it feels like the way hit percentage is calculated often doesn't make sense with your positioning (why do I have 70% hit chance to shoot this man 1 tile over with a shotgun, while I have 90% hit chance on this guy who is literally obscured by an entire truck?). All added up, positioning feels like an afterthought. I won the first story mission I did after the tutorial by pressing 1 (the button to shoot) over and over until all the enemies died, without moving.There's also other cases of dubious design: In said mission (this is in Stephanie St. Claire's campaign) the game made me run several blocks across town to meet a butcher, who told me to go back to my HQ to talk to a guy, who then made me follow him back to the butcher - and walking takes a long time! This also somehow took *twenty-eight days* in the game. That's more amusing than a real problem, but it doesn't exactly make for great immersion.Other than that, the UI is frustrating. Most UI elements either have no tooltips, or the tooltips only show stuff like how certain numbers are made up of other numbers. Coupled with some really cluttered screens, this feels like a big no-no for a strategy game in general, and in particular as a person with ADHD this makes this part of the game borderline unfathomable.It also has other problems like poor voice acting and animations, and some very stilted writing and dialogue, but I'm willing to overlook all that because I can tell they were earnestly really trying for something. But... it just feels like they didn't know how to execute on that ambition at all. It's a shame. I'll try to play more of it but I'm not hopeful.

_childDocuments_.review: So much unrealised potential. There's something there to build on, but currently the game is quite shallow and bizarrely balanced. Bad economy design, bad strategic UI. Combat is "ok" but some bosses are so incredibly powerful off the bat that they trivialise 95% of the fights you encounter.The default game settings has 10 districts with ~20-40 potential rackets in each, where there are only 4 varieties to build from. It gets tedious and overwhelming very quickly. It doesn't help that they don't have anything to interact with to help make them stand out. There's no reason to even visit them once you have them. Much like your own safehouses.Management/Empire UI is poorly thought out. Having so many gangs, including small mobs, but only being able to scroll through them one by one, without a list or search is again tedious. Minor factions don't even have unique portraits, they are all the same and blend together. Not being able to go to diplomacy or info pages on a faction straight from the map, or even by clicking on their portraits in other menus also seems like a glaring oversight.Game economy is really unbalanced. There's no real reason to bother upgrading your rackets apart from alcohol quality in breweries. Firstly because there are so many of them that it's just not feasible to cover the costs, but also because the costs are so high compared to the income each racket generates that the ROI is terrible. Negotiating "business proposals" with other factions for 2-4% discount buffs is almost useless considering the drama it seems to cause.It's more profitable to just mask cheap booze as whisky and sell it to factions. Also just selling whisky outright to minor factions is a faster way to make money than relying on your rackets. Item costs and sales prices, and the way your relationship score changes from trades is easily abused and mostly nonsensical. The cache drops across the maps at the start of the game allow you to decently kit out your entire gang before you even start a war, if you want to bother running around everywhere for 30 minutes. Gear seems to hit a peak relatively early as well, so you quickly run out of upgrade opportunities.The enemy factions also appear to struggle with the game economy, as they tend to constantly be almost broke and as such barely upgrade anything apart from their own safehouse security. Which means you can just declare war and blitz everything they have without much fuss. The only "challenge" is that there can be so much happening across so many districts that you can't keep up with any roaming gangs on the streets to cut them off before they attack your own rackets. Even that's not a big deal, as savvy players will just pause the game and rush security upgrades as needed before the building is stormed.Lieutenants, underbosses, moles etc all seem like cool ideas that never got past the first cycle of workshopping. You can't even use lieutenants again without "demoting" them and losing morale. There just doesn't seem to be much benefit of making new safehouses and paying to keep someone locked in there for the rest of the game, when you could keep them in your party and use the extra muscle to take down all the other factions faster.The story and side missions are all fine, nothing outstanding. It seems you generally receive the best outcomes by showing mercy or "being good" at every opportunity, which is a bit odd for a hard boiled gangster-themed game with a cast of sociopaths.I haven't experienced any particularly big bugs, so at least recent patches appear to have stabilised the game considerably.All in all I want to like this game a lot more than I currently do. It needs more flavour and more balance. I was holding off on getting it for a long time but finally caved. It was a mistake, as it will need many updates to really find some soul.

_childDocuments_.review: Feels very rushed, but I've enjoyed some of it and feel like I've gotten my money's worth. The aesthetic, music is nice, and the gameplay is xcom tactics/ basic management. The characters are colorful and unique, and its not a bad game if you are in the mood for some casual tactical strategy with a cool 1920s gangster aesthetic and a rudimentary strategic layer. Don't expect a deep experience or much replayability at this point - each starting character has a set of unique missions, but the gameplay loop is fundamentally the same. The basic idea is that you complete x-com-lite tactical battles to take over bars, brothels, and casinos and expand your empire while defending from AI attacks and doing basic diplomacy, and completing various battle and fetch missions. You control a squad of gangsters that each have unique traits and backstories and fall into one of a few classes with skill trees - doctors, gunmen, brawlers, etc. The tactical battles can be pretty difficult on higher levels, and you face off against both nameless AI goons and the AIs own unique squads of gangsters. You can upgrade your businesses in a few ways but it feels pretty meaningless currently. Some of the design choices (or choice of what mechanics to forego at release) are pretty frustrating. For example, you can recruit unique characters, but the bulk of your & the AI's forces are nameless goons. When the AI attacks your businesses, you may have one unique character defending, but it is usually a nameless goon vs. nameless goon slugfest where the goons all have a 50% chance at best of hitting each other and it takes two or three shots at least to kill a goon. Its simply boring - and there is no autoresolve, no way to speed up the fights, nor even an option to forfeit the battle, which I would gladly do since when you ultimately win a gang war by killing the opposing gang boss, you get all your businesses back anyways. A way to skip or decline minor, repetitive fights is something I would expect from any modern strategy release, and its absence here suggests that the game was shipped before it was ready.More evidence of premature release is that it is currently obviously unbalanced and full of game-breaking bugs. I've had saves corrupted and multiple freezes requiring restart. Some quests are just broken. There are the seeds of an excellent character-driven gangster sandbox strategy game here - maybe they will bloom in time, but its uncertain.

_childDocuments_.review: You can teleport to any boss fight at any time. There is no character progression so you can fight them from the beginning of the game. I never learned a third (or higher) skill on any character before beating the game and only got a 1st and 2nd by dragging ass and exploring all the non-content trying to find a use for it-Enemies never get any stronger, only 1-3 people during boss fights don't die in one rifle shot on the hardest difficultyAnd now a short list of the systems in this game that don't do anything and should be ignored, as it's as useful to you winning as playing cookie clicker on your other monitor.Managing customer draw and capacity at owned placesManaging tier of booze dependent on sector prosperityDeciding which building to make for highest profitsManaging sector prosperity by building qualityManaging your threat level versus other factionsTrying to not draw police attention (I shot every cop and never did anything to hide and they never did anything about it)Managing relations with other factionsBalancing security against likelihood to be raided (you never get raided, minimum security can beat any actual attack if you decide to not teleport and kill all 3 attackers with your Main Character)Hiring troops based on bonuses, traits and relationshipsInstalling troops in businesses to increase building statistics slightlyQuests

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game BUT wait for a sale or for issues to be fixed.I don't write reviews often but i felt it was needed here. The feedback in store although correct i feel is very angry. I wanted to get in some gameplay before posting a review and i think its best summarised by saying its A Swing and a Miss. For now at least.Don't get me wrong, I really want to enjoy this game (And I Do) But there are a lot of issues that need addressing which judging by the feedback on the store a lot of people have noticed and are angry about. If this was a £20 game then fair enough but paying a lot of money and getting hyped for this has been a bit disappointing seeing the state it is in at launch.  That being said, I fully support the developers and wish them the best of luck in resolving these issues, but there is alot for a £70 game on release.So to begin:The combat is X-com style i guess you could say but lacking the Umph. Ai isnt the brightest and charges straight at you, even if they have good cover. The animations feel clunky at times and if the animation freezes the game pauses for a significant amount of time whilst it catches up with itself (Sometimes resulting in a crash) Also seen issues where the character models stop walking or running, even taking cover correctly. They just start hovering and sliding their way across the screen, when this happens there is a significant wait time for actions to finish before the game carries on. (Like 20 seconds, its really bad xD)Executions are cool, however most the time I kill someone who's downed they stand back up before falling back down to their death.  If you get into combat and two other factions are fighting, you have to wait for them to resolve their conflict before you can carry on your game. (Very annoying when its 3 thugs and a few police whilst you're just sat there skipping turns waiting to raid the last boss's safehouse.)The gangsters you can hire are the same every playthrough, what i mean by this is that because there is a notierety structure for unlocking and recruitment, you get stuck with the same 5 gangster each time you start. Not neccassarily a bad thing, but maybe give an option to randomise it as it becomes very repetitive. Speaking of; the maps are heavily recycled usually featuring the bloodstains of past battles outside of the fighting area but still there even though its your first time there. Missions are chained and presented to you so fast that you never have time to finish them. Strips away any player autonomy in completing missions. (Reminds me of the Settlement mission questline in fallout 4)Diplomacy feels like a lost cause as its always better to just kill off the competition and take their rackets. As soon as you conquer their safehouse, all their empire becomes yours. Basically streamlines players to attack safehouse before rackets. If there is a way to finish a game with an alliance i haven't found it yet. Upgrading of rackets is incredibly costly and time consuming. Usually more cost effective to conquer others or buy new ones.  Also the hotel synergy could do with a bit of elaboration. There no customisation either with regard to your gangsters. You can edit their loadout but thats about it. Theres like 5 archetypes Enforcer, Con Artist, Doctor, Hired gun, Demolitionist. No real stand out qualities in any of them besides the obvious (Doctor can heal, Bomb guy has bombs.) But no visual customisation at all.Even though the city management is good and intuitive, it feels shallow and easily mastered.A few pros:Visually stunning,Unique storyline for each boss,There is alot to do. (Like any paradox game really)The music is great (There is one song with a very noticable loop though, please fix this, it breaks me everytime. xD)I want to reiterate however that this game has a lot of potential and its not awful its just buggy as s**t and needs some TLC. I feel alot of us may have boarded the hype train and its sadly crashed.We wanted an Xcom Omerta but we got a BTEC jagged alliance in a fedora. So, maybe wait for a sale to buy the game or buy it and enjoy but expect it to be unpolished and buggy. I don't think its worth £50 to £70 price tag in current state. Its not the end however, if they fix the issues (and I've seen that their working on patches already) then i'm all for the amount I paid. But please fix the issues. We got faith in you Romero. Don't let us down.

Empire of Sin is interesting for a short few hours when you first get into it and are learning the system. It borrows them and doesn't do much to integrate these elements into the game resulting in a game that has what feels like cobbled together systems. A 'fast-travel' taxi system, but no cars that you can buy or use to travel and explore faster. Henchmen for buildings; but no way to bring henchmen into your group for extra muscle or even send them out to explore (but the computer mob bosses can send out henchmen to explore the city). _childDocuments_.review: Take the turn-based tactical combat of XCOM, combine it with the management elements of a tycoon game, and slap a mafia skin on it, what could go wrong? Well, as it turns out, a lot of things, actually.So let’s just start this off by saying that I’m disappointed more than anything. This is a game with a fantastic concept, a game that could have been good. However, the execution is just shallow, nowhere near enough to really sell the experience.I have two major problems with Empire of Sin: its combat elements and its management elements. Considering that those are the two major areas to the game, we’re already off to a bad start, but I’ll talk about the combat first.This is a strategy game that has combat done in a turn-based tactics manner, similar to the XCOM series. You get your group of gangsters, enter a building, and have to eliminate all of the opposition to win. It’s pretty simple, but the real experience lies in the depth of that combat. I will admit, my first couple hours with the game, I was actually satisfied. The combat was fun and I was having a good time going from building to building growing my empire.However, I quickly found out that there is really nothing beyond that. The combat does not really evolve, it kinda remains static throughout the entire game, whether you be 2 hours in or 20. Despite going into different buildings, you’ll start to notice the exact same layouts, the same enemy types, the same weapons, and the same abilities used in every single fight. Sure, you unlock more abilities as your characters level up, but it’s only like four or five until they’ve maxed out, nowhere near enough to offer the combat depth required to avoid that feeling of monotony.Due to how simple it is, the combat eventually devolves into this repetitive sequence that you can apply to every single fight and win without issue. In fact, once I had a group of six or so gangsters, I pretty much steamrolled any competition. Whether it be a simple building takeover or a boss fight – they all felt the same and this alone honestly kills the overall experience.There is another side to the game though through its management elements. And unfortunately, those management elements are equally lacking. I would go so far as to equate them to a clicker game, as all you’re really doing is applying upgrades, switching which alcohol your establishments serve, and waiting for money to apply even more upgrades. There really is not much to do here, and it was so bad that at one point I was literally sitting there fiddling with my phone while I waited for money to come in so I could buy more upgrades so that the money would come in faster so that I could buy more upgrades and you can kinda see where this is going.However, all of that goes out the window when you realize that the entire management aspect is kinda pointless. Why spend time upgrading stuff or changing what alcohol your establishments are serving when you can simply waltz into an enemy safehouse, kill their boss, and acquire all of their buildings with just that one battle. Do this for each boss in the game and you’ve won, without ever needing to really engage with any sort of management.Really, the most management you get is with your characters themselves. They each have their own skill tree, a bunch of different equipment slots, and even traits and relationships. For example, a character that is in love with another gangster will not attack them even if they are on the opposing side in a battle. And sometimes a character’s loyalty to you will unlock gangsters for hire that would have otherwise been unavailable. Playing around with the characters was easily the best part of the management side to the game, but unfortunately the bulk of that side is managing your establishments – the boring part.During my time with the game, I ran into plenty of animation issues, clipping, and freezes during combat that would hang the game for seconds at a time. That and the AI is not the greatest either, oftentimes putting itself in really bad positions during combat or just acting in a manner that actively ruins their chances of winning. I was fortunate to not run into any crashes (the game has been patched up a bit since its rocky launch), but it’s still not an entirely smooth experience.I cannot recommend Empire of Sin. Patches may be able to fix the technical problems, but the core to the game is just far too shallow to be worth the time. Repetitive combat, lackluster management elements, it just loses its appeal after those initial few hours. A shame, as I really like the concept here, but the execution just doesn’t cut it.Follow my  for more reviews + videos!

_childDocuments_.review: With a decade's worth of competition behind it, Empire of Sin attempts to copy everyone's homework while trying not to make it too obvious. Players of  and  will immediately see the similarities, and along with it, every issue that riddled this game's predecessors.Its initial hours are to be praised; With a large cast of unique characters that all come with their own initial story, it's easy to get immersed in your narrative while short-and-sweet alternative missions keep you occupied between the game's progression loop. It only takes your first or second run of this loop, however, to spot just how shallow the ocean is... Its management aspect is almost identical to an idle sim, and its combat variety and difficulty scaling immediately default to more red shirts that take slightly more damage.The Bosses mechanics quickly boil down to traits and bonuses tier-listed into game-breaking or not worth playing at all, only serving to slightly speed up or slow down the monotonous board game format, making anything but smaller, faster playthroughs an unrewarding grind. Your , as the ability to hire lackeys or goons is barred for you, and only available to the opposition, try their best to tear you from any semblance of realism; Adamant to bloat the game with horribly inaccurate portrayals and tokenism while swearing they're a hard-researched, deeply historical game.With everything falling short of the mark, the developers attempted to fix, it and soon after abandoned the title. And it's only DLC showing a clear Paradox-style marketing scheme of selling you basic functions for a price tag. And even if they were to continue development, you'd still find more authentic and varied gameplay from a 2001 game than this.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a real toss-up for me. I'm basically 50/50 on it, and I wish Steam would allow me to post the review as neutral with information in here instead of a 'recommend' or not... because the game has the bones of something really cool. The structure is there. The visuals are wonderful. The systems in place have potential. The idea is great, and 'almost' executed well enough for a recommendation - but alas, the details were ignored, the pacing isn't right, the entire concept of the AI having even a 2nd grade reading level was overlooked, and the trade/barter/negotiation system is all one-sided. You have no say over the core of what makes this game great, and therefore, it becomes mediocre at best. It's an economy driven game, without the need to build much of an economy. It's a business simulator with no control over your prices. It's a multi-agency strategy game with no say over trades or negotiation terms (it's take what they offer you, or piss them off). It's a turn-based tactical combat game, without the need for proper tactics, even at Boss difficulty (the highest). It has many screens of in-depth information, but doesn't give you what you want to know when you want to know it. It'll interrupt your gameplay entirely with repetitive noises and loud crashing sounds for things you don't care about, and then fail to notify you on things you do care about. Even things like quest markers take an unusually long time to find on the map. It's as if they never thought allowing interaction with a quest would make the player want to know 'where' it takes place. A simple button to zoom in on the location would be best. Information such as what you're currently producing has no mouse-over at all (is that barrel swill or rack? I really don't know unless I go to another screen to find words next to the symbol. Why can't there be mouse overs on this stuff?).Also... the strongest weapon in the entire game is the taxi. Don't bother investing in security. It's not needed. Just pause, taxi there instantly during pause with your hero, and blow the enemy up. It needs improvements, and perhaps due to it's extensive modding capabilities, we'll get even more than the devs have planned... assuming they have it planned. I wish them well on their journey to make this game the great game it was meant to be. I hope they see the criticism in the reviews as an opportunity to improve it to something awesome, like No Mans Sky has done, and not something to abandon, like say... Phantom Doctrine. Overall right now, I give it a 6/10 -- and at $40, that's just not good enough. Wait for a deep sale now, or evaluate when it's had some patches, has improved it's AI greatly, has expanded it's availability of information, and hopefully has fixed Salazar's voice... because... well.. that voice has got to go. It's basically a non-native Spanish speaker trying to sound Mexican in the form of a TTS readout. I'm not kidding.

_childDocuments_.review: This game had (and still HAS!) potential, but as of right now, I just cannot recommend buying it at full price.It's super repetitive, and 3 hours in I've not even had to care about the actual business running side of things. But as it stands I genuinely feel like I've experienced all the game has to offer which right now doesn't seem to be much. It feels like I'm breezing by killing everyone and everything in my way with no actual strategy needed in attacks, who I ally with or who I make an enemy of - because I can legitimately just squash them all like ants with absolutely zero repercussions, as long as I don't just do it all at the one time. Combat has no difficulty, the AI is absurdly bad and opens itself to easy attacks like they're just begging you to kill them. There's no real strategy in what is supposed to be a strategy game.The characters themselves have no personality, which while isn't necessarily important for a strategy game, I feel that if you're going to give us the ability to become friends with and enemies with the other gangsters within Chicago, it might be best to ensure that they all don't feel like the same cardboard cutout with a different paintjob.Now, this game isn't terrible, it just gets really boring incredibly fast. I just can't recommend it at full price, but on sale? Absolutely. I put hours upon hours into other Paradox Interactive products (mainly Crusader Kings II), so I have faith that they'll eventually get around to adding things to make the game more interesting, so hey maybe even wait until then. The idea of the game, being a gangster and building up your empire brick by brick is a good foundation and I really wanted to like it (and I am going to keep playing it, so this review might change!). I just hope they can bring this game to the full potential that its bland self just can't seem to reach as of right now.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a pretty solid foundation for a turn based tactics game. However it is not very polished and has a lot of minor issues and a few major ones. For instance my best campaign so far was ended because I destroyed a faction, and that dead faction would try to talk to me later which would immediately freeze the game, forcing me to Alt+F4 it and restart. Loading back into that campaign would lead to that same thing happening soon after the save, so a multiple hour long campaign is just ended due to a bug. The minor issues include things like unskippable conversations (which are about the same between every boss, so get old fast), character pathing getting stuck while exploring on the map, and the game hanging mid-combat while it seems to be calculating something. The game is basically still in a beta state with many bugs, some of which are game breaking so I cannot recommend it in its current state.However, the game has a lot of upgrades over Xcom 2 which is the closest game I have played to this style. There is a percentage chance to hit predictor that updates as you mouse over tiles a character can move to. The percentage chance to hit does not lie from what I can tell, whereas in Xcom 2 the player will miss more shots the better they do in missions, so the RNG is wildly inaccurate once you get into a campaign. You recruit the same basic soldiers early, but with their relationships you can recruit some late game people earlier in the campaign so you can recruit a wide variety of people. You can also influence how their traits are gained to an extent, making each soldier slightly different in every playthrough. If the developers work on this game it has a chance to be great, it is just not currently in a fun state as players will just get frustrated with the glaring bugs and other issues.EDIT: As an update to this review, the bug that initially prevented me from progressing was fixed, and I was able to finish my first campaign. However upon starting a new one on the next higher difficulty I was unable to attack any territories as whenever I clicked to attack the game just ignored my input. The devs have been releasing fairly quick patches to fix bugs, however there are still some that break the game so my overall review still stands.

_childDocuments_.review: Beginner's Guide & Tips:Don't hire too many recruits at onceEvery recruit that you add to your team takes a certain amount of money from you. In the initial phase of the game, you have a limited number of properties, so your profits are not too big.Take over non-gang buildingsIn each district there are a number of locations that are suitable for running a business. Some of them belong to other bosses, and the rest do not have an owner (they can be bought or taken by force). To avoid disputes with other gangs, take over these abandoned structures in the first place.Limit your activities to one districtAt the beginning of the adventure, get acquainted with all the mechanics offered by the game. That's how you'll get used to the way the world works. Until you do, limit your activities to one district. This will make it easier for you to control a growing empire.Improve business protection on a regular basisThe buildings you own are vulnerable to attacks from your competitors. Therefore, you need to regularly improve security in your facilities. This way, they will be able to defend themselves. If you neglect this, the fight for the property may be doomed to failure.Do not accept every offer to join a warEvery once in a while you will get an offer to join a gang war. If it is not aimed directly at you, you can refuse to take part in it. Before you decide to join the fight, consider all the potential gains and losses that will result from this decision.Don't underestimate diplomacyDuring your adventure you can not only argue with rival bosses, but also join forces with them. Fighting on multiple fronts can quickly become burdensome, and you will not be able to keep up with improving the protection in your facilities. Diplomacy will help you forge alliances that can be helpful in a gang war. You will then receive additional military support.Avoid killing copsThe police are an important faction in the game - when your relations with the PD deteriorate, they will become interested in your actions. Fighting in front of buildings may get you noticed by some local officers. If any members of an enemy gang start attacking them, let them. That way, you'll avoid a bad reputation with the police. Also, during your free exploration, if you come across a patrolling officer, avoid him instead of starting a fight.Types of racketsBreweryThe place required for the production of alcohol. This is one of the crucial buildings in the game, because it allows you to supply your bars with liquor. At the basic level it produces the cheapest type of booze. After making some improvements, however, it will also be able to generate other, fancier kinds of liquor. It is important in so far as each district of Chicago likes a different type of drink so in order to gain more influence you have to cater to their needs.After buying a chosen upgrade, the brewery continues to produce the cheapest alcohol by default. To change this you need to go to the neighborhood panel and select the brewery in question.HotelThe hotel allows you to attract more potential customers to the area, which translates into increased profits. However, to build it you need to have the right synergy. Meaning, you need to accumulate your businesses at a fairly close distance.Illegal barA place where you can sell alcohol made in the breweries. If your bar sells liquor tailored to its neighborhood's needs, you will be able to cash in some large sums.BrothelA place of pleasure for the hardworking people of Chicago. The easiest source of income - its relatively cheap to set up (in most buildings) and do not require any alcohol to operate.CasinoA casino is a more expensive building than a brothel, but it allows you to generate more profits and also does not require alcohol to operate. Here, however, you are at a risk of having one of the clients win, reducing your profits (or generating a loss).SafehouseThe safehouse is one of the buildings that you will start out with. A single district can hold only one racket of this type. Theoretically, it allows you to manage your empire, however, the options that are there are easily available in the game at any time, so the importance of a safehouse is marginal.SynergysThe concept of synergy is understood as the interaction of different objects, so that the effect of their action is amplified. In the game, this effect occurs when you put the right number of buildings of the same type in a given district - you will get a bonus for doing that. In total, there are 5 types of synergies:Two Pair - own two pairs of two different kinds of rackets;Three of a Kind - you must have three businesses of the same kind;Full House - own three buildings of one kind and two of a different kind;Straight - own one business of each type;Five of a kind - you must have five businesses of the same kind.You can have several types of synergies simultaneously. The neighborhood panel will inform you which synergies are currently active.PS: THIS DEVS ARE SCAMMERS

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of people don't like this game and I can kinda see why, but at the same time I think its the most fun I've had in a while. You could then betray your ally with outside help and take over that district. I get why everyones disappointed with the racket system, I am too, but I think its a little too much to ask to have a system similar to Omerta: City Of Gangsters which was extremely in depth with several different forms to make the same kind of money. If they could do something like this, maybe in a huge update or DLC or something, I think this would be the perfect successor to Omerta, as this game is obviously heavily inspired by it. If you're looking for a semi-casual exaggerated mafia experience similar to Omerta, this is a perfect game. It may not be ALL perfect, but I still think its worth atleast trying it out.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a well researched visit to roaring twenties Chicago.  Unfortunately, every time I have played, the game session has ended in a crash.  That is at least ten sessions by now..  The mechanics of combat are smooth enough, the engine seems to have trouble managing itself.  A rival gang started a war and hit three of my business one right after another just as I had entered to clean out a third gang's 'racket'.  The engine froze.  If I play for over three hours, chances are I will have to 'end task' and gripe about not saving.  Autosaves seem arbitrary, too.  It just wasn't ready.  This is poor quality control on a game that doesn't seem to be too involved.  The database management could be smoother and the interface less obtuse, but they did a good job of keeping it from being a spreadsheet management game.  I look forward to the next six months of patches that will address most of the issues as that seems to be the industry model.  I had high hopes for this game.  It delivered as promised, mostly. _childDocuments_.review: Updated review as of August 25, 2022Came back to this game after a while and it's been improved slightly. However, not enough to the point that I'd say it was worth the price. Upon some reflection, I recommended the game initially due to what it potentially had rather than what it currently has. I haven't bumped into any game breaking bugs anymore so I guess that's a plus. Otherwise, it seems like the game has stayed nearly the same with some minor changes to combat, quests, and the businesses.In conclusion, I've changed my review to 'Do Not Recommend'. Additionally, the dev updates have stop and, newsflash, it's been 9 months since the last official update (last one was November 2021 and it's August 2022) so take that as you will. Do I regret purchasing it? A little but I did have fun for the most part. Probably will come back to it once in a while when I get bored.-----TL; DR: Bugs (quests, mechanics, and dialogue), repetitive visuals and combat, and feels like it's missing key features. Graphics are fine, has not crashed yet, stable frames, foundations for the game seem like they're there. I recommend EoS but only when on sale. Otherwise, just hold on to your money and hope it gets active support.First of all, some background, I only heard of this game through CallMeKevin and pre-purchased it after seeing Blitz and CMK's sponsored videos on EoS. I liked what I see from the videos. Two other factors that affected my decision to purchase the game were that a.) it was developed my Romero Games (I'm more familiar with John Romero's work) and b.) that it will be published by Paradox Interactive. Knowing Paradox Interactive their games (developed or published by them) tend to have long lasting support and DLC with two already slated to be released in the future. In its present state, the game has bugs, mostly found in quests, diplomacy, and combat. The quest bugs are really annoying and game breaking. It's either you can't find the NPC (High Roller Heaven quest) or the mechanics of the quest are broken (breweries remain closed after finishing the quest for Jacques). It needs quite a few quality of life improvements (like a better way to filter properties in your empire and a way to see the day progression maybe a clock or meter). The tutorial is solid enough though I had to figure certain things out myself. The economy and management aspects are pretty easy to understand but makes it feel lackluster. As for combat, it's pretty repetitive and loses its flare after a couple of fights. Diplomacy and interactions with the other factions are bland, making it feel unnecessary. Properties and the map could really do with some changes. It gets repetitive. One thing to note is it hasn't crashed yet, at least.It's not all bad. Even if combat is repetitive, it is currently not buggy (the same can't be said for the rest of the game), the existing aspects are decent. Map is big, even if it's repetitive like the combat, a single playthrough could potentially last hours. A decent number of mob bosses to start with (still hoping for custom character creation). Frames are stable for me. A few things that, in my opinion, could help make the game better, adding more roles and actions you can take as the boss, adding more kinds of businesses, and interactions with local politics (this happens through a quest and ends there). Just my opinion, won't really affect my review.I enjoy the game but it feels like it's missing a lot of features which I hope get added in free and not tied to DLC. Unfortunately, it feels like a game that could pass up as an early access game. I heard modding tools will be added which will, most likely, make it better off.  I recommend it for the potential and the foundations are there I can see that there are building blocks to make it a good game. However, in the state that it is in, I only recommend purchasing when it is on sale. I will probably update this review when I feel like enough changes are made or if I find anything else to add during my playthrough.Edit: Added quests can get extremely buggy and some are game breaking.Edit (August 25, 2022)

_childDocuments_.review: After over 20 hrs in the game I want t o say two things about it:First of them is, that it has a great potential. The idea of prohibition era gangster strategy/tactical game with x-com like combat is something that many of us waited for, even when some of us never knew it. Possibilities are endless and it will probably meet most expectations in the future.On the other side, sadly, this game is bugged to the level which will be untoreable to most players, or dissapointing  at least. Bugged quests, that can miss element required to finish them. Bugged fights, which can't proceed to the second turn or end due to enemies not loading on the map (can be ended only by loading a save). Bugged graphics, where model animations freezes, movement range and accuracy display vanishes, abilities grey-out even when they are usable. Bugged mechanics, where neighbourhood status lock's itself in poorest or highest prosperity rating, other mobster's pay you cash for alcohol You don't have, bussines agreements are constantly broken by AI without any reason, even just after singning them. Not to mention taht when You meet another faction You can kill their men, make a threat or request sitdown on the other end of the map, no neutral option...This game is marked as full release, in fact version 1.02.38890 as i write this review, but in reality it is early beta at most.If You buy this game now, you will be like a beta tester, finding many bugs in otherwise great content. It will give You joy and let You feel like a gangster, but it will bring You tears and anger at the same rate. If this doesn't scare You and You think that You will still enjoy  the climate of 20's era gangster themed game, then go ahead and buy it to have a great time (I do, that's why I still play it).But if You are not such a big fan of gangster era games, WAIT. Wait couple of months, until dev's fix all the major bugs and this game reach it's true version 1.x. Just then buy it and truly enjoy, becouse now You will think that marking this game as a full release and giving it a price like one is a true robbery.Till then, I'll go take over some rackets, if the game allows...

_childDocuments_.review: Ok this one is kind of a wild ride.Initially I gave this game a negative review because it was absolutely terrible at launch.More recently, I changed it to positive because the major changes that accompanied the DLC made it at least decent.Now, I'm going back to negative due to repeated game-breaking bugs preventing all progress. I'm sorry, I just cannot recommend this game to anyone. Don't be led astray by recent glowing reviews patting the devs on the back for "fixing" things with the DLC. They *had* to make some effort to try to turn some profit because the base game was straight garbage and they were legally obligated to produce DLC due to what I would *charitably* describe as an over-ambitious season pass.I would not hold your breath waiting for this game to get fixed again, or for the developers to suddenly develop a burst of uncharacteristic competence if and when that happens.

_childDocuments_.review: Encountered multiple major bugs in a span of two hours. - Side quests that can't progress because the objective is bugged. I entered a bar to kill someone but that person didn't spawn. Game thinks I am in a mission area and therefore locks me from leaving the room. Had to reload. He didn't spawn afterwards either. - Game got soft locked (can't even open up ESC menu to load old save) because a cutscene was supposed to happen but the something went wrong. Camera was stuck looking at the streets and I had to alt-F4.- Reloading wouldn't be that bad, but sometimes loading an old save causes an infinite loading screen. yep. Had to alt-F4 again.- The AI is dumb as nuts, enemies will run out of cover in order to close the distance, instead of going cover to cover. Had a situation where an enemy ran into the middle of my group of 4 just to shoot them at melee range.- Skills are unbalanced. Take the bomb skill of the triad leader for example, one shots almost any enemy, is AOE, deals poison damage, you get to throw it 3 times PER CAST, and you get it immediately at the beginning of the game.The foundation itself is not terrible, I could see myself giving this a 7 or 8/10, but the bugs are just too numerous and too glaring for anything to be enjoyable. I will definitely recommend this game but only after everything is patched.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, Empire of Sin is a fun game and I expect that I'll be putting in many more hours into it. My primary complaint is that the combat can feel rather slow if you're facing a lot of enemies. I haven't figured out if there's a way to skip through or speed up the enemy turns, but if that's not implemented that'd be something I'd want to see.As for bugs, I've only experienced one major bug that seems to have occurred when several of my rackets came under attack simultaneously. I defended both of them but once the second fight was complete, I was no longer able to return to normal gameplay. I could zoom out to the neighborhood view, but I couldn't do anything and it wouldn't allow me to save the game either. I was able to close the game and restart from the previous autosave but there was definitely 10-15 minutes of progress lost. The only other bug I've experienced so far is that when I use the "taxi" functionality while paused to move around the map, all my gangsters spawn on top of each other in a T-pose until I un-pause. It doesn't affect gameplay in any way but it's just one of those odd things that caught my eye.Overall, fun game, great voice acting, great concept, and pretty good execution.

_childDocuments_.review: Given the negative reviews I was actually pleased with my first 2 hours of play. Then as soon as  things started to heat up a little I realized what people were complaining about. Here's in a nutshell why I gave this game a negative review.1- bugs, yes lots but really I know this will be sorted out eventually so I'm not too critical about this one2- User Interface. This is a big one for me. Some design choices are really poor, and the information you need is all over the place or absent. For example your businesses keep getting attack during a war but they don't show you on the map where it is and don't give you the option to skip the fight if its a small one. At one point it took me like 45 minutes just to talk to someone because every time I tried i was getting interrupted by fight notifications from god knows where on the map. Anyway its just a small example. But the problems are plenty.3 - In the combat phase, it just make no sense that when you enter a building to attack you start the fight in a random place. sometime its even in a room in the back of the building surrounded by bad guys. Given that we can't decide which of our characters we want to move first (because we need to follow  the initiative order), this is a BIG deal. You can get almost wipe before even having a chance to do anything. When you enter a building to attack you should either get a deployment zone near the door where you can place your men, or you should be able to enter in real-time and have  the combat mode start when the enemy sees you for the first time like in Phantom Doctrine. Pretty basic.- Your whole organization is pretty much limited to the gangsters you can hire from the pool of 30 something mobsters with a couple of random pawns at each businesses. Yet your enemies have plenty of men and they seems to be able to attack, hunt, stalk targets and do plenty of things that you can't. Either that or I didn't found where to give these orders to my men.- I could go on forever about poor design choices but I will stop here. I've played for 5 hours and I do not feel like trying anymore. I think I will monitor the discussions forums to see if they make any drastic changes maybe i'll come back. But for now I do not recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I've kept my eye on Empire of Sin a few days prior to it's release and even watched the 30 minute tutorial by Paradox and it seemed like a fun and promising game. Bought the game on release day & have been playing it since. The aesthetic is impressive, I have to admit. The swanky 20's music gives the game a real classy vibe & makes it seem like you're really back during the prohibition era. The combat system took a little getting used to but by no means difficult to utilize. However, I found myself constantly bombarded with sit-down/non-aggression pacts/protection requests within seconds of each other. I'm not able to actually enjoy the game because I'm being attacked several consecutive times, and I'm only playing normal difficulty. It feels like I'm not able to focus on improving my rackets or crew member stats because there is always some pop up demanding that I dissolve my connection with a faction or I missed a sit-down. This prevents me from getting immersed into the game, and becomes more of a nuisance than anything else. The map UI isn't intuitive or user friendly. Having to pan to each city instead of a drop down list where I can click a city name would be useful. If I scroll too far out, I lose sight of my mission/crew markers forcing me to zoom back in so I can remember who is in what city and then zoom out so I can find the city I need to go to, and then zoom into that city so I can set my destination. It's a headache and I detest the way it's set up. The missions don't always complete properly. On more than one occasion, I have performed required tasks and upon completion, the objectives menu incorrectly shows that the objective was never completed even though a mission successful notification populates. The tutorial misses a few key points like the use of taxi's to travel from city to city. I learned this on my own but it would have saved me time if it was in the tutorial. Overall, the game is enticing at first & I love the voice acting but the constant pops up detract from the over all experience & the map system is just a hassle. I wouldn't recommend this game to a friend unless it was on sale, $40 isn't worth the experience. Maybe $30. So close to nailing this on the head, but no cigar.

_childDocuments_.review: What I wanted: mobster XCOMWhat I got: mobster XCOM Chimera SquadThe tactical combat is unchallenging since your character is going to be incredibly OP, aside from fighting other mobster bosses. There is an ability that trivializes those too. The base "management" aspect is basically non-existent. You take buildings and put a category on them, then they make you money (or produce booze to fuel the money making). Then you can upgrade them, mostly to either make them less likely to be attacked, better guarded, or better at...making money. Which you generally don't need. If you are aggressive about expanding, you'll rapidly find yourself swimming in cash. The gameplay loop is simple: attack thing to make money to attack more things. The icing on this mobster cake is that there's a ton of stuff that's simply under-explained. What actual benefits does an advisor or underboss give? What does the "draw" on the buildings actually translate into? What are the actual effects of hotels? What are the synergy bonuses? And most of all, why on earth is the diplomacy system COMPLETELY ripped from EVERY OTHER PARADOX GAME? John Romero, you could have been a LITTLE more creative here. It's literally the same thing in Stellaris or CK2/3 with the green+ and red- and the (+/-X) weekly or monthly or daily or whatever. This game is shallower than the average Crusader Kings gene pool. I recommend passing on this until there's some DLC (to make it actually interesting) and it's all on sale.
