_childDocuments_.review: Psychonauts 2 is a once-in-a-lifetime game, and I don't mean it's so good that nothing else is going to be made like it. I mean something else. This game is a long-awaited sequel to one of my favorite games of all time, Psychonauts. The thing about most long-awaited sequels is that they have a lot of trouble creating a similar feeling to the original. Take the remake of Battle for Bikini Bottom. That remake had almost 0 heart. This game has so much heart that it hurts. First of all, the game itself has a hit or miss art style, it always has, but this new game looks great. There are very few technical problems besides the not-so-often clip through something. As far as gameplay goes, expect a lot of cutscenes. I love this lore. I could not watch nearly half of the cutscenes because I just wanted to play the game so bad. The good thing is that they are all skippable.The controls are very tight. Almost all of the items and powerup you attain are very fun to use. The only problem I run into is how the button mapping works. You constantly have to assign different powers to different buttons, which can get confusing. The controls that worked best for me were picking one button to be my misc and only switching out that one. Overall the game is not too long, well polished, and left me feeling very satisfied with what I had waited so long for. This game is a win in my book, and if you were to buy this game, I strongly recommend purchasing the first one and playing it before.

_childDocuments_.review: The good (The subjective):-The game is overall great for me and most of my complaints are overall minor IMO. The delayed game can at some point be good while a rushed game could be bad forever is very much on point here quote.-levels are overall interesting, unique, and overall fun for me to travel. I loved the music overall as well.-New character wise Raz's family and the founding members of the Psychonauts were great character wise to me overall. Other old characters were great as well. I even enjoyed the bit faceless npcs bits like how 1 character was gonna cheat on their significant other with said other's friend but they were just planning a party for them instead for example. Loved the main villain as well.Gameplay I felt Improved from one:-Enemy variety and combat was overall far better than 1's. The leveling system letting you choose what to upgrade for the most part was a good move overall to. Use of old powers was made a lot better in this one as well.-Collectibles were improved on. Figments aren't nearly as bad to 100% in this as they were in 1. Gameplay that could use improvements:-The pin system is flawed. Changing the thought bubble to a different color shouldn't take the same amount or even 2 or 3 of pins as powerful ones like time bubble size increase or glass cannon. Several things like the shop discount, money x2, making paper Raz be quiet should have just been auto options you could turn on and off when you got them. Even stuff like the ground pound attack while using levitation really should have just been normal upgrades as well since the ground pound attack is a level up upgrade. Using a system like Resident Evil 4/Kid Icarus Uprisings grid system where better powers/weapons take more space to store would have worked great for the pin system in this game.-Even though combat has improved and so did this I feel the way you use powers has some flaws still. You can swap out 3 powers at any time (lets face it you are gonna have levitation on 90% of the time for one of the buttons, and the hookshot for 50% of the time). Making a button let you swap roles like how an older game like Phantasy Star Online let you have 6 keys instead of 3 would fix a lot of the need to go in the psychic power menu often (not as bad as u have to in 1 but still).-Give us something like a figment finder, you gave us thought tuner. 99% of the stuff done in a level and the last figment is a piece of grass in the book world pissed me off.-Even though the old powers were great in their use and expanded on very well from the 1st one I felt the new powers were overall a let down compared to the ones we lost. Well 2 of the ones we lost, confuse grenades are like Paper Raz is just never really made to do more but considering how it is the last one you unlock and you might only have it for 3 of the mental worlds I can get that, though you could use it to do things like catch the bunny in 1 easilly. The time bubble is never really used more for just platforming and combat so it being limited to those is fine as well though I could have found some other uses for it. Time Bubble and the way Raz can speed up stuff could have been used as well. Make it used to over run a machine to break a way forward for example.However, Mental Connection is just a hookshot once you get out of Hollis' level. Which is a real shame.Yeah the way mental connection Raz uses it for in game wasn't good and that is why it isn't used that way again but there was all sorts of small stuff Raz could have used it for that is harmless. It could have been used for puzzles still like use it to make a person think about if they want pizza or hamburgers for dinner or something else harmless like do I want to wear this shirt or this shirt today and those choices could open up a path in a level. The spot in the final mind where you are moving scenery to get to a hidden area could and should have been a mental connection spot as well.-Combat is overall too forgiving. Even with Glass Cannon on I felt I think the most damage I took at a single time was like 2 heart at the final boss. Compared to like several hearts of damage from the final boss in 1 and that is just silly. You being able to carry 3 dream fluffs, 8 psi suckers by game end as well pretty much will make it so you never have to worry about true death or defeat if you don't wanna it seems. The point of this is there is no option to increase the difficulty if one wants to. They made all these attempts to make the game easier for people who might not be able to play the game well because they are young or might need help in some way yet they won't make stuff that makes the game harder but fair still for people? I'm not saying that hard = good or that they shouldn't have had a invincibility mode. Just saying there is a way to make the combat more hard w/o making it unfair still. If I want my Psychonauts to be Dark Souls or Ghosts n Goblins difficult that is my choice as well just as it is someone's choice to use the easy mode stuff and if the game is gonna give me nearly unlimited resources I'd like to have a reason to need them.The opinion:-While 2 camps of new characters were good I didn't really care about the interns besides Sam compared to the camp kids from 1 or Hollis overall when compared to the the old teachers. I'll admit Hollis grew on me a little though with some things as the game went on. I'll admit it feels like there was some cut content with the interns that might have caused this view though.

_childDocuments_.review: A delightful platformer that successfully balances an impossible line in its story between treating mental problems with the seriousness they deserve, and Double Fine's characteristic quirky humor that distinguished the original game.  The gameplay has been refined and improved from the original; platforming is tighter, and combat much improved.  I laughed out loud multiple times from the wonderful writing.Level design in different minds never disappoint in variety - from a hospital-turned-casino where patients bet with their health; to a library populated by book characters, containing a whole other world rendered in paper and ink; to a music festival whose psychedelic visuals would fit right in with Yellow Submarine.This really feels like an indie game that has been given a triple A budget - it pairs the offbeat aesthetic and unconventional humor of an indie developer with the polish and cinematic flourish of a major studio.  A game of this quality absolutely ought to bring success to its creators, and if there's any justice they'll have the chance to make more Psychonauts games.  As of August 2021, this is my GOTY candidate, and if you don't absolutely hate platformers as a genre, I'll recommend it to you.

_childDocuments_.review: Psychonauts 2 picks up right where the first game/VR title left off in more ways than just its story. All of the platforming/basic psychic powers are available right after the first introductory level, unlike a lot of other sequels that wipe away the main character's progression from the previous game. However these powers have been expanded upon with the introduction of the upgrade system, and each tier of these upgrades feel impactful to gameplay. There is also the pin system, of which 3 can be equipped to give cosmetic or functional effects to your psychic powers. These systems add linear depth to previously simple abilities without making the base abilities weak or the fully upgraded varieties too strong.The depth of these powers as well as other improvements play an important part in the much improved combat from the previous game, which was the weakest element. The biggest improvement to the combat is by far the enemy variety. Rather than having just censors populating every mind in addition to level-specific enemies, there are now 7 more consistent enemy types with their own weaknesses. This further elevates the upgrade system by allowing players to make reliable decisions in regards to making certain enemies easier to deal with. Changes to Raz's abilities also make combat more engaging, such as the addition of dodge attacks and making the PSI Blast on a sectioned cooldown instead of using ammunition. The addition of new powers also helps give the game its own identity separate from the first. The controls for PC also feel much more streamlined than the original game.Excellent level design and pacing make the game a joy to adventure through and explore. Every area of the game oozes style, personality, and care, while maintaining unique challenges and visuals that keep things fresh. There was almost never a moment that felt like it dragged on or was too confusing. Every mind and area outside felt memorable, and made me intrigued to keep looking for nooks and crannies I had yet to see even without collectibles to incentivize me.Part of this interest in discovering all of the level is due to the interesting character designs and interactions with said characters. This applies more-so towards the main world than the minds, but there are well-written and humorous characters in them as well. There are many optional conversations Raz can have that world-build and are just entertaining to listen to. Some conversations also give Raz side quests to further incentivize world exploration.The writing of the game's main story is an excellent expansion of the first game's loose ends and mysteries. Just about every major character from the first game makes a return, and maintains their defining attributes. New characters are introduced when necessary to create new plot developments and dynamics between characters, and while they have a minutely different style than the original cast they are just as well-written. The Psychic Six are a good example of introducing new major characters without sidelining the original ones.Every moment and area of the game has an excellent soundtrack backing it up, composed by Peter McConnell. The music reflects every situation perfectly and greatly helps players feel immersed in the emotions of the story and the environments. The sound design is also top-notch, with every important sound being recognizable and identifiable to the player for good flow, all while sounding good on top.Psychonauts 2 is just as good, if not better than the first game. It improves upon aspects such as platforming precision and combat depth while maintaining the personality of the quirky psychological collectathon the original set out to be. Psychonauts 2 is the perfect example of what a sequel should be.

_childDocuments_.review: It's really rare that someone can walk into a genre as saturated as the ubiquitous platformer and make a mark as indelible as Psychonauts did. It's rarer still when an iconic game has a sequel that lives up to the original - but this does.Waay back in the long long ago Tim Schaffer was *the man*.  Tim was responsible for groundbreaking games like Day of the Tentacle and Grim Fandango (maybe ask your parents). He's had hits and misses with Double Fine Productions in the last twenty years but Psychonauts was undoubtedly a masterpiece and arguably the best game Double Fine has ever made - it's sequel is very nearly as good.The gameplay is similar to every good 3D platformer you've ever played, controls are tight, and the mechanics make you feel powerful without being wonky - but there's not really anything groundbreaking here.  The real star is the plot and the level design.  Interesting characters and clever but clean humor are the rule of the day. Even experienced players will see things they've never seen before and the level design will stick with you no matter what kind of gamer you are.

_childDocuments_.review: Psychonauts 2 delivers on the promise to transport players back in time to the glory days of Invader Zim and Tenacious D, when movies based on comic books were a thrilling concept and the original XBox was blowing minds left and right. _childDocuments_.review: Psychonauts 2 is the type of sequel that greatly expands and elevates the ideas of its predecessor.Visually the game has improved on a technical level, of course, but it still retains the same overall art style. There is a shift in focus between the first and second title. Environments are much bigger both in the overworld and within levels. There's also more obligatory verticality which is nice. The levitation ability has been nerfed which is welcomed because it makes platforming more engaging.The first game was a blend of platformer and adventure game, while Psychonauts 2 is firmly a platformer. There is an expanded focus on combat with many more types of enemies as well as specific weaknesses for certain foes. Abilities are also upgradable in an order that you choose. They can allow customization in how you go about combat.Story and plot take a focus, continuing off of the end of the first Psychonauts game and their VR-only adventure (I suggest you look up a playthrough if you don't have VR and want to be informed on the plot). Returning characters are present but not the focus with most of the screentime dedicated to introducing and developing the new characters we meet at Psychonauts headquarters. There's an engaging mystery, callbacks to the first game, and a couple key memorable moments between Raz and the characters from the first game he idolizes.As for critiques I have there's one big gameplay one and one big story one, both spoiler free. The gameplay gripe I have is the pin system. It feels needlessly restrictive to have only three alterations to your abilities via pins active at a time. Some of these are just cosmetic and should not occupy a slot. Pins are also expensive so unless you spend time grinding for currency as well as prioritize the pins that generate extra income or earn discounts you won't have access to even half of the pins before the final levels. The story gripe is that specific characters are neglected and could have had more screen time. Returning characters have a lot to do at the start of the game but for most of the rest of the game they stand around in a way that feels quite static. The new characters like Raz's new piers are more dynamic but we don't get as much time to spend with them as I would like. There are also far fewer than the large cast of campers for the first game so there is a slight feeling that headquarters is somewhat underpopulated.Despite small criticisms, it is an amazing fact that this game exists. After the financial failure the first was and the decade it took to get another game the fact that this game isn't a cash-grab or a pale retread but rather a shining examplre of how to make a sequel shows that there genuinely is a spark to this franchise that makes it unique. Psychonauts 2 delivers not just on the premise of being more Psychonauts but also a solid 3D platformer in this age of the genre's revival.

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't realize that I had forgotten how to enjoy and have fun playing games like a child again until I experience Psychonauts 2. • This game was stunningly good and was definitely a palate cleanser. Game's writing and character interactions are one of a kind and I laughed out loud countless of times during my playthrough. • Its approach to somewhat taboo subjects in public like mental ilness and psychology is certainly spectacular and makes it more approachable and understandable.• Gameplay is so fun and fluid that I didn't want it to end. They give you a brief introduction about the first game so that you have an idea about what's going on. • Voice acting is incredible and I cannot express this enough. You can even say it's one of the best in the industry and I hope you experience it yourself. • Although kind of underwhelming, there are couple of boss fights in the game that look grandoise and fun as hell. • A lot of the collectibles embedded into the game/progression and it's easier to get back to a level and collect all the missing items easily.• The dialogue and the story elevates the game into GOTY category and it's criminal that not a lot of people recognized the success of this game and it has kind of been the underdog. • Technicality and performance is very very good. It's not an exaggeration to say that I have yet to experience an AA/AAA game this bug free for a while. • I'd wish that you could equip more than 4 skills because that kind of hinders the combat fluidity but nothing major. • The story ends kind of abruptly but certainly acceptable. I just hoped that it would be more majestic and expected more cinematic with the characters.I am blown away by the beauty of this game and it is easily my GOTY for 2021. I hope that Xbox and Microsoft would fund the studio more and give them all they need to publish incredible games and continue their stories in this world. 100% recommended, you MUST NOT miss.

_childDocuments_.review: It took me a while to settle on a rating. Psychonauts 2 is honestly a fantastic game with great visuals, a good story and a likable enough set of characters. But it's marred with incredibly frustrating gameplay and combat, ultimately resulted in me really not enjoying it as much as I'd hoped.Platforming is hit-or-miss (mostly misses) especially when trying to collect figments. Items always seem to be a few pixels too near/far, Raz's movement speed is inconsistent which affects timing and in my opinion, he's too heavy. Mario games for example, give you an amazing sense of fluidity and weightlessness, making traversal fun and liberating. Where as Raz feels like he's wearing an invisible ball and chain, not to mention his balloon power is practically useless unless there's a wind source nearby. Combat is janky and spammy and is coupled with fairly boring abilities and some of the most irritating enemy types I've ever faced in a video game. Finally there's the, at times, tedious missions that always require you to do 3 things to progress. By mid-point, every new character or area I was introduced to was met with a groan.I've read other negative reviews and many of them admit that the game is still good, and it is. If you can ignore it's problems then I wholeheartedly recommend picking it up now, on sale or better yet, trying it through Xbox Game Pass. Unfortunately my experience just wasn't fun enough and I kept praying for it to end.

_childDocuments_.review: A genuine 9/10 for me. Otherwise, an incredibly wonderful experience, and a loving sequel to one of the most original games.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the few games I've played to completion without skipping any cutscenes or skipping out on character dialogue. A beautiful, story-driven comedy/mystery platformer that plays out with some of the best writing and VO work I've seen in my entire lifetime of playing games. The way the game tackles mental health and familial trauma is also very mature; it's clear the subject matter was approached with a thoughtful, empathetic eye. I'm really grateful for that, I hope other devs take note.On top of all that, the gameplay is absolutely amazing as well. They really refined and fleshed out the platforming compared to the first (which I enjoyed but nowhere near as much as this one) and the level design is just unreal! Every environment is distinct and beautiful, each one organized around a different theme or motif relevant to the character whose mind you're in. It is inspiring how creative the writers and designers got with every part of this game. I've got a lot more playtime logged offline but the game is still relatively short compared to many big $60 titles. As someone who bought it full-price, I'm absolutely okay with that. It is worth every penny. All killer, no filler, as they say.Loved it! One of my new favorites, easily.

_childDocuments_.review: A few years ago I purchased the first Psychonauts game after having seen a few youtubers gush about how great of a game it was and after playing it for myself I would still absolutely recommend that game as well as this one. The original release date for the first game was over 16 years ago so the wait for this game has been long and though I never played the original I believe the wait might have been worth it for those that played the first game all those years ago. The controls are tight and responsive with challenging and fun platforming as well as combat using the full array of powers to tackle situations in each, the writing and script for the story and interactions between characters is hilarious, tragic, and engaging, and each level has felt unique and incredibly well designed so far. As of yet I haven't completed the story mode but I would certainly recommend this game to fans of the first game and if you're new don't worry they have a recap of the first game at the beginning but you'd be missing the great levels that game has to offer. Over all if you want to get this game now it's well worth it and an incredibly well crafted game in every aspect.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game, I would recommend playing this game too if you enjoy 3D platformers.  This one is light on the Collectathon; with a rich story, great characters, and amazing settings/levels, and fantastic graphics. This game is a fantastic modern platformer, that amazingly goes beyond the cult classic original.The first game still holds up to this day, I would still recommend playing that one first, but cause of its age it did show some issues with its UI and equipping abilities sucked.  Those issues were minor though, so really go play the first one it does still hold up.All issues I did have with the first game have been resolved in this game, it feels very polished and the UI and abilities are much cleaner to use in this game.  This is also a platformer so levels really keep you engaged, each offering a new setting and challenges.  For this game and the series each level is unique in its presentation.  Its hard to describe but Psychonauts' levels are otherworldly and feel more like an unraveling presentation as you platform through it.  Each level and mind in this game are unique,The first game had a rich story and great characters, though it did suffer from not utilizing them as much as it should. Halfway through the first game, .  This made the world feel emptier and made me the player feel rushed to get to the end.  This game does not have that issue, and with a new cast of characters the story feels much livelier and in my opinion has a better flow from the beginning of the story to the climax.

_childDocuments_.review: If you've played the original Psychonauts (there's also a VR mini game to bridge the first and second game - haven't played it) then this is beyond a worthy successor to the first. I could go into all of the nuances of the game, but to put it simply, this is beyond a worthy successor. The atmosphere, theme, and implementation mirror that of the first, but with the added flair of modern graphics. I am truly impressed with all that were involved with its production. You don't often see platformers in 2022, but if you're looking to develop one take notes from this game. This is premiere platforming, with great story and character development. Beyond impressed. Hats off to the devs and teams working on this. As a person enjoying the game, thank you so much for creating such a memorable piece. I remember playing the original on steam (I didn't play this as a kid because in the Blockbusters shop it was distributed in I didn't want to rent a "dangerous" game") a few years ago I was warily delighted that there was to be a sequel given the timespan. If you loved the original Psychonauts, you should absolutely play this game. It's like you never left. I'm thoroughly impressed. Also to add, if you're coming here as an original Psychonauts fans, the original plots hinted in the first are more fully explored here. This game is truly a treat, and one I wish I could play again for the first time.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the few games where I had so much fun and enjoyment I was genuinely smiling most of my playthrough. I can't believe they've done it and made a sequel that's a genuine improvement on everything that made the first game so memorable.Probably the most amazing thing about Psychonauts 2 is that compared to its' predecesor, its' quality and creativity is consistent throughout the whole adventure. There's never a dull moment, a level that feels weaker. While we may not have standouts like some of the popular 'brains' from the first game, it just means in 2, they're all fun to play through and memorable for their own right. So much care went into making sure that these levels are not also enjoyable but also woven into the story and this game does it with a lot more confidence than the first game which speaks a lot about its' improved writing as well. Seriously, all the characters and their dialogue are great (Raz is still one of the best if not the best video game protagonists), there are so many moments when I ended up chuckling!If you are a fan of the first game, don't even think about it and grab this, you will not be disappointed. If you are and you are looking for a cool platformer with a focus on exploration and story with themes of psychic meddling and solving mental issues, mixed in with Bond-esque spy bits and a soundtrack to match, give this a shot (better yet, start with the first game).Psychonauts really is the Incredibles of gaming.

_childDocuments_.review: The first game, but without the bad parts! In other words, a masterpiece. People give away the term "Super Mario Galaxy 3" to any good 3d platformer, but THIS game deserves it. It actually uses non-planar gravity, like galaxy, and quite a few mechanics are similar to ones from Super Mario Galaxy. Sure, you don't go into space, but going into people's minds is also very interesting. The hub world feels like a theme park, with themed restaurants, learning centers, and bowling. There's a bunch of other locations you can go to outside of the Motherlobe, too, of course. And if you don't want to explore, you can use the fast travel. The Cosmic Observatory wishes it could be this cool to walk around in. The game looks beautiful, the humor is fantastic, the characters are great, the story is interesting, the gameplay is engaging and smooth. One of the best 3D platformers I've played in a while.

Getting it for half the price now feels like a steal, at least in my opinion.Edit: 100%-ed the game and I stand by what I said.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game. Remembering the first part almost 20 years ago, I do remember some tedious parts about this as well. Walking around the summer camp has always low-key bored me, searching for psi cards and other gimmicks and finding ways how to reach difficult spots - not really my jam.What was pretty cool were the minds of people, carefully designed levels, each on their own pretty cool, with interesting and unique gameplay parts and differing greatly in style. The milkman conspiracy, Black Velvetopia, the theater, the Napoleon guy - it was epic.What have we here now? A bunch of the same old mechanics that weren't fun for me back then and aren't fun today. Boring and large hubs. Yes, they are beautiful, but I simply do not enjoy exploring them. They're too normal. The mind worlds I have seen so far were pretty lackluster but they would be okay if there were more of them and I could explore them more often. Instead I have to walk around a hub and finish tedious tasks, and between every single step, there is a cutscene.This should be called Psychonauts 2 - the movie. I hate switching between the psi powers because it feels annoying, here you need to burn something, here you need telekinesis, it's all always pretty obvious and I have to switch powers using some mini menu. It's not TERRIBLE but has me roll my eyes. Then there are tons of parts where I am not sure - can I go there? Will I slip? Am I supposed to jump on here?The jump and run mechanics are partially annoying and tedious but manageable *cough cough comb tower* Wish it was less of "here a platform and there some moving thing pushing you down and here some obstacle and here a bomb" and more of "wow this looks actually amazing and going there feels like actual fun and like it belongs to this level design and isn't just here because platform platform jump jump curse curse"So it's basically all the parts I disliked about Psychonauts 1 minus the cool parts of it. I've seen that there are not that many minds to explore and some seem to be about war. If it continues like that, I might not even finish this chore of a game. Cutscene 2.

_childDocuments_.review: I played Psychonauts 2 to completion on Xbox (approximately 22 hours gametime) and am replaying it now on Steam. This game is incredible. I went back recently and replayed Psychonauts 1 and this is one of the rare occasions where the sequel is just as good or better than the original. I've had a strong urge for more PS2-like 3D platformers lately, and this game is a modern take on it. A lot of the mechanics from the original have been refined and the platforming overall has been tightened. The story, humor, and art design are fantastic. There are some snags: the controls for your powers can be a bit cumbersome as you sometimes need to manually switch them out and the boss fights are somewhat underwhelming. Some of the platforming sections can be occasionally confusing. But, that's all the negatives I can think of. This game gets everything else right. Not playing it should be a crime.Now all I need is a good Sly Cooper continuation...

_childDocuments_.review: +++++ : Levels or "brains" are what puts Psychonauts apart from other platformers. Always visually interesting and always goes deeper than it looks. Some levels feels like Inception because of their size, cramming tons of ideas segments inside sublevels inside levels.+++ : A very satisfying Collectathon with many Collectible types. Perfect game to not think to much and just touch the shiny objects and see the numbers go up. ++ : They finally made fun 3d Platformer combat segments, the secret? Allowing experimentation, combinations and requiring dodges.++ : Also known as "Pins". Not many of them useful when you have 3 slots but some of them can change the game. I am especially fond of "Glass Cannon" Pin.+ : Developers did everything they could to make the experience smooth as possible. For example in Psychonauts 1 when you missed an easily missable "figment" of /300, you had to replay the whole level and your best bet was to watch a "All Figments Walkthrough" 1:1. Now, you can skip to points in a level and also the camera highlights the missed figments. Many improvements like this over the original.-- : Not a huge problem but 30% of the cutscenes of this game could've been ingame dialogue instead of ruining the pacing. I want to move and jump in a 3d platformer, not sit and watch.--- : 75% of the runtime and missions of the game is about making certain people feel good that will have no effect or far-fetched effect on the actual mission of the game. Psychonauts 1 kinda had this issue but in a smaller dose. It is not that big of a negative because it makes the story unpredictable to where will it go. It's just that when i look at the total story after finishing it, most of it was unnecessary tangents. *Don't use healing items or the entire challenge of the game will evaporate.

_childDocuments_.review: A game I have waited a long time for, and I have to say that I have mixed feelings right now. The gameplay feels more varied but is not as fun as the first game that came out over a decade ago. The upgrades used to be given on level ups and frankly over powered Raz by the end, but almost all of the upgrades now kinda suck or are something that you could just have because you already had it in the first game. Perfect example you need to once again acquire the ability to chain hit enemies with you PSI Blast. You can also modify powers with badges but they (again) are mostly useless. The only two that are truly worth a damn are the glass cannon and the fist power up. Another problem for me is the story is kinda meh. The overall story is fine but the beats in between are not fun to play through.  I did not care for almost any of the new characters outside of the Psychic 6. They just were not all that interesting when compared to what we had from the first game. Two of the many standout characters for me in the first one were Clem and Crystal, two cheerleaders that tried cheering everyone on while secretly holding suicidal thoughts. If you just did the story you would not have seen any of that but I liked them so I kept checking in on them only to see one of their attempts. This was missing in this game to me. Characters that I actually wanted to see out of the story beats, and the ones that where there just deus ex machina themselves into whatever situation need at that moment. The game I wanted to like is in here but all of the bad drags it down for me. Off sheer value that the levels were neat (nothing comes close to Milkman or the Waterloo levels) I will recommend this game but DEFINITELY not for $60. Barely $30 and if you can get it lower you should do so.

_childDocuments_.review: Such a fun game! Not the greatest ever, but a solid 9/10 from me. The sequel of a good platformer from Double Fine. I like their other games like Brutal Legend as well. Playing the first game is not needed (but highly recommended), there's a small recap video at the start.Pros:- Great story, characters and a nice twist in the end- Good to great soundtrack (Could be better. Some level themes are too short and annoying after a time. But some I could listen for hours, depends on the mind/level.)- Voice acting is superb. Really cool that a lot of characters returned from Psychonauts 1 and they have the same voices after 16 years. It's like only a few days passed, just like in the story.- Smooth controls and game mechanics.- Excellent level design, REALLY creative minds and worlds. Even better than in Psychonauts 1.- Stable frame rates and no freezes for me during the 38.1 hour to 100% complete it (stuck once in the terrain, but it was my fault, and a quick reload fixed it without even exiting the game).- A lot of side content, tons of collectibles(Small) Cons:- As mentioned before, some music/songs are either too short or annoying and they repeat (although one particular song could be stopped, not going to spoil how).- Some collectibles blend in the terrain on super colourful levels and had to use a guide for it. Maybe it was my fault not seeing those after I passed them like 4-5 times. Thankfully found around 95-98% of the collectibles on my own.- Only 4 psi powers can be active at once and it is quite limiting, since some stages require at least 3-4 of them at once. The game isn't too challenging, but switching in the middle of the combat can be frustrating for some players.

_childDocuments_.review: So I played the first Psychonauts in 2012. I generally dislike platformers and am absolutely terrible at them, but it gained a spot in the list of games I periodically replay anyway. Yes, I have voluntarily subjected myself to Meat Circus several times, I love it that much. I say this in order to emphasize the following: Psychonauts 2 is everything I hoped and more. This game basically radiates joy. It is a precisely-engineered joke machine that dispenses humor and emotional sucker punches. I admit I was (briefly) disappointed that none of the memorable campers from the first game reappeared, but I got absolutely sucked into the story of the Psychic 6, and the Sensorium might be my favorite level in basically any game, ever. (Also, Sam. I adore Sam.)I will say that this feels different from the original, in one distinct way: the first game felt, fundamentally, like an adventure game, because a lot of its interactions were based on "use X on Y." As funny as I found it to use random items (tickling everyone with the crow feather, introducing Mr Pokeylope to the camp, showing literally everything to Crystal and Clem to see if they had new cheers), generally refining/streamlining narrative and character elements into more of a pure platformer makes for a much more cohesive experience overall. This isn't a complaint - far from it. The original game (and I say this with nothing but love for it) is a strange and often janky grab-bag of things. This game, for me, maintained much of the weirdness, that sense where you never knew what would happen next, and it does so in a context that feels much friendlier and more polished to actually play.I went in absolutely blind, knowing nothing about this game other than that reviewers I trusted thought it was great, so I'll limit my comments on the narrative to this: I loved the way it handles mental health, which reminded me of the best aspects of Gloria's Theater. Sometimes I use "dear universe, please shut up" as a weird little mantra when I'm stressed, but there isn't a single level I didn't adore. The balance of humor and compassion felt spot-on - sweet without being saccharine, funny without punching down.I wish I could forget it so I could experience it for the first time. But I know I'll be going back, and I look forward to seeing what I missed the first time through.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh my god, I can't even think where to begin with raving about this game. It's well worth the $60. It's well worth the 16 year wait. There are so many plot threads pulled up even if you don't notice them being there, and ALL of it gets tied up into this cathartic knot that you can actually UNDERSTAND unlike some media. Are there plot twists? Yeah. Is there foreshadowing? Yeah. Is stuff from the previous games overwritten? In a couple places, yeah. Some of the plot twists come out of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ nowhere with foreshadowing you didn't even realize WAS foreshadowing, only for it to hit you that ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, it makes perfect sense-- and the ♥♥♥♥ coming up to change what the first game told you isn't even retcons, it's recontexualizing information that was purposely given to you under the wrong pretenses previously! it's just- oh my god. _childDocuments_.review: What an incredible game! _childDocuments_.review: If you haven't played Psychonauts 1 and are reading this review, just stop now and play that game first. At this point, EVERYONE should just play it, even if you're only slightly into platformers. It's funny, strange, laugh out loud funny, and a work of art unlike anything else. Psychonauts 2 is pretty much a direct sequel that delivers a great experience, but it's not the work of creative genius that the first one was. DEFINITELY play that game, and if you want more, then come back to get the sequel. Psychonauts 2 could be better, the gameplay hasn't really evolved at all and it isn't as imaginative as the first one, but it's still a great sequel.The story is great. We see much more the world of the Psychonauts, the real one, not just the summer camp, and we also see more of Raz's family and the mystery of their family curse. We learn more about Ford and how his mind shattered, and we see into the minds of more messed up people. I feel like Raz did a lot of growing up in this one.Unfortunately, a lot of the strangeness of the series has been toned down for this installment. Psychonauts 1 had a lot of iconic levels inside the minds of people around camp. And those levels weren't just interestingly themed, there were some real interesting mechanics in there as well. Of course, everyone knows about the infamous Milkman level, but I also loved the Waterloo level, where you were able to move between levels of abstraction on a board game. You could be on the board itself, moving tokens with telekinesis, head up and talk to the people playing the game, or go deeper and the board game became a living world and the game tokens people with problems to solve. A lot of the brains you entered had strange and fun mechanics like that, but in P2, you're pretty much just doing normal platformer things. Jumping to ledges, using a grappling hook-like power, grinding on rails, etc. The levels still have some interesting set dressing on display, and there is one standout level that comes close to the genius of P1, but otherwise it's pretty standard fare.The brain worlds are a little less strange and colorful. That might be a side effect of trying to make a more mature game that plays better for a 2021 audience. A man with a split personality who sometimes think's he's Napoleon in P1 was straight out of a book of cliches, and the people you encounter have more genuine mental woes. I think it's great that they're taking mental health a bit more seriously and respectfully, but I think they could have injected a bit more whimsy in there too. Nevertheless, I left each mind feeling pretty empathetic for the person I just met and felt like I really helped them.Mechanically speaking, the game plays about the same as P1, or maybe a bit worse. I know P1's platforming was a bit rough around the edges, and it seems like they didn't spend much time trying to fix it. It still works, but you'll be continually frustrated of things like changing your power loadouts on the fly because you don't have enough buttons for all the powers you need to explore AND fight, and there are some collectibles that you will really struggle to get, and not in a fun challenging way, but in a frustrating way. It's not a deal killer, but it lacks elegance, and that's kind of a big deal for a platformerI could nitpick and dissect this game all day, but the bottom line is I truly loved it and returning to the world of Psychonauts. As frustrating as I found it at times, I found myself trying to 100% the game, just because I wasn't prepared to leave it. The emotion the story kicks up makes up for the lack of gameplay refinement and while there's nothing quite as memetic as the Milkman Conspiracy, you will still frequently be left in awe of the worlds on display. The world of gaming is a little more colorful and special thanks to this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: I really REALLY wanted to love this game.  I'd been psyched (no pun intended) when it was announced.  When I finally sat down to play it though...?  The magic was just gone.   If the articles I reviewed about the history of Psychonauts are accurate, I understand how this game let me down...but maybe not why.  From what I read, the original game development process was INSANE.  There was a game department and an art department, and they weren't exactly talking to each other.  When it came time to move the game forward, Doublefine kicked out the game designers, and held onto the art team instead.   That choice is how you had five different forms of gameplay (the neon matador level, the crazy milkman gravity level, the kaiju water level, the pachinko-feeling moments in the general's mind, and that damned meat circus jumping game) all come together, unified by the story and the central camp area.The sequel?  Not even close to that.  Instead, it's just a jumping platformer with a few artistic twists and turns.  Like, they put a standard game design, and then layered it with art.   What made the original game awesome was how they layered the gameplay over the art, rather than art over the gameplay.  Even the bosses in this game showed a unified experience that take you away from it.  Psychonauts felt like playing a single story across 6-7 different realities.  This sequel felt like playing one game across different levels with slightly different art aesthetics. If they ever do another sequel, I hope the focus is on ensuring each mind you enter feels like an entirely different game, not just a different setting.   It's what made the first so great, and why this one feels like it's missing so much heart. Takeaway: Psychonauts 2 is an exercise is flexing Intellectual Property that misses the mark by over-correcting for the same development-process errors that produced serendipitous success the first time around.

I know the developers to be very inclusive, but it's still really heartwarming to see. This franchise will forever be my favorite. There's so many elements to it, so many details, it's very obvious the people making it had fun, and that's one of the many reasons it's so great. The sequel in particular (since that's what I'm commenting on) was an incredible adventure with a great story, and an important message behind it. It's made improvements to an already extremely unique game and made it even better, which I didn't even know was possible. My only complaint is that it doesn't last forever.Thank you, Double Fine, for this unforgettable experience, looking forward to whatever the future holds, I already know it's going to be great.

_childDocuments_.review: Spectacular game, all around.  There are plenty of reviews that go into all the detail - but some of the "little things" I found most welcome:1)  No part of the game was frustratingly difficult.  Challenging, yes.  But unlike the game's predecessor, there were no points that put me in a "ragequit" mood.  The most difficult portions of the game took me perhaps three or four tries - but never more than that.2) When you quit the game, the interface displays the expected "You will lose all progress since your last save" message, like any other game.  However Psychonauts 2 also tells you how many minutes and seconds it's been since your last save.  So simple, and so useful.3)  Holy hell ... Psychonauts 2 lets you PAUSE CUTSCENES!  Yes! _childDocuments_.review: The original Psychonauts is one of my favorite ever games, and I was one of the backers for this game in 2015, so I'm not exactly an unbiased observer, but I'll still give my opinion. The best summary I have is that this was a great game, one I had a lot of fun with and have no reservations about recommending, but one that just doesn't quite live up to the original Psychonauts. Not this is much of a ding, since I still think that was one of the best games ever.The story this time is more serious than Psychonauts 1 was. It's still a comedic, silly world in many ways, with a ton of laughs to be found, but it's definitely a tone change compared to the first one. Overall, I prefer the more silly tone of the original, but also like that they changed it for the sequel, so it wasn't just more of the same.Something that I am certainly in the minority in, as far as I can tell, is that I wish this game was more difficult. I really only started to enjoy the fights and platforming near the end of the game, and even then I found it to be generally too easy. To be fair, though, I remember liking the meat circus back in the original game, so I am obviously very unusual in my preferences. That's just for the general gameplay, though, finding all collectibles was still just as much of a challenge (I'm no longer as patient as I was back then, I gave up and went online to find the last few figments).One little thing I noticed immediately was that the levitation ball was nowhere near as bouncy as in the first game. I just absolutely loved how high you cold jump with in the original Psychonauts, and I did feel that lack the entire game. I can understand why they got rid of it, though, it must have made any platforming challenges so much harder to properly calibrate.Psychonauts 2 is still wildly imaginative, with fun and diverse levels to explore, and some pretty cool platforming along the way. If you enjoy 3d platformers, creative and surreal worlds, or are a fan of the original at all, check this game out immediately.

_childDocuments_.review: I feel that I was fortunate in just playing Psychonauts for the first time a few weeks ago - I only had to finish that game before I could play this one, instead of having to wait for 15 years. I very much enjoyed Psychonauts 2, but to be honest, if I had waited that long for it, I probably would've found it to be fairly underwhelming.To be clear, I had a lot of fun with Psychonauts 2! It was absolutely gorgeous, the levels were bright and crisp, and the visuals were truly a delight. The music was wonderful, and the story, though simple, was engaging enough to keep me interested. The platforming was fun, the combat was adequate, and the collectibles and side missions were usually fun to hunt down rather than frustrating. All in all, it was everything I would want in a platformer/adventure game.However, I do have a couple of fairly major grips with Psychonauts 2. The levels themselves were a bit hit or miss - I feel like sometimes they went for quantity over quality. While the visuals and stories of each level were great, I felt that the gameplay started to feel a bit same-y after the first few. There just wasn't enough variety in how the levels played.Additionally, I thought that Psychonauts 2 struggled with tone at times. This game deals with some pretty heavy topics. I wish that they would have let those hit a bit harder, it's a little difficult to take a discussion about alcoholism or depression seriously when its interrupted by a "witty" quip or the kazoo sound of picking up a collectible. I think the topics discussed could've been better utilized if they leaned into them a bit more, but I do applaud Double Fine for broaching these topics in the first place.Overall, I found Psychonauts 2 to be a good time, but I don't think it's better than the original. If you're a fan of the first game, I think you'll enjoy it - just set expectations accordingly.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the first game and the sequel does not disappoint! The setting, humor and the whole concept of the Psychonauts just really strikes my fancy and I had a blast exploring the different inner psyches of the games' many crazy characters, most of which were completely original and fun to play around in. And while I loved the enemies, battles were becoming a bit repetitive near the halfway mark. That is when the game started to become a bit less fun. Which is a shame because those first 15-20 hours were wonderful.  Still, annoyances aside, this is a great, colorful and incredibly funny game with a ton of content, charm and amazing character design. I'd expected that I wanted to go for a 100% completion when I'd finished but in the end I was just happy that I was done and I wrote this review. 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Psychonauts 2 takes place directly after the ending of Rhombus of Ruin, a sadly VR-only game that takes place also directly after the first game. So despite the 16-year gap the games only take place between the span of a few days. In this game, Raz is finally able to join the Psychonauts as an intern, and after his supposed mentor turned up brainless, he investigates a possible case of having a mole. It is pretty similar in tone and atmosphere with the first game, but not too similar, just familiar enough to be good and nostalgic as well as adding unique touches.Gameplay is pretty much the same, an open-world platformer with several levels that takes place inside some character's minds. Unlike the first game, there is postgame free roam, allowing you to wrap up collectibles and sidequests as well as having new dialogue. There seem to be several point-of-no-return warnings, but none of these are permanent, just some areas you cannot return to before you complete the story. In fact, some collectibles can only be acquired during postgame because you need an ability that you get very late.The mental worlds are also pretty well-designed, each having a unique theme and aesthetic fitting the character whose mind we dive into. Some examples include a hospital-casino, a psychedelic music festival, and a historic amusement park ride. But most of these levels are linear platformer/combat ones, the more puzzle-centric levels such as the theater and suspicious neighborhood in the first game don't exist. Instead, we have quite many, perhaps a bit too many, ball-rolling segments. Whether its an upgrade or downgrade depends on you, but the neighborhood is one of my favorite levels.As you would expect, there are also some changes in the game's mechanics. While most powers return, there are some new powers, like creating a mental projection, but some powers don't return such as invisibility. One I really miss is the ability to use bacon to ask Ford Cruller for helpful hints, here you can only rely on Raz talking to himself if you take too long, or other characters if they say something. Collectibles are also easier to find, as there's a checklist if you collected everything there as well as adding a photomode filter that reveals every collectible once you finish the game.Overall, Psychonauts 2 is a really great game, just as great, if not better than the first game. It also explores several events and characters mentioned only in previous titles, like the Psychic Six and Raz's family. A proper continuation of a good game, retaining all the great aspects while adding some more and making it in HD graphics. If you liked the first game, you'll definitely like this one as well due to the similarities it has, while still being fresh enough to not be boring.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: Psychonauts has long been one of my favorite games ever. Doublefine has knocked it out of the park with a sequel that lives up to the original and exceeds it in many ways. The writing is fantastic, and the level design is varied and imaginative.  Every minute of this game is pure fun. Also cool to see the accessibility features included to allow players of varying abilities and skills to enjoy the game. A big thank you to Doublefine for getting this right.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: I have been waiting 14 years for this game (i didn't first play it until 2007) and it is everything I had hoped it would be and more. At this point, I've played the first game six or seven times (one playthrough being on PS4 this year). If you're a fan of the series, get it. If your a fan of action adventure platforming games, get it. If your a fan of weird art, get it. If your a fan of wit and silly humor, get it. At the time of writing this, I have only 7 hours in the game, but those 7 hours were consecutive because I couldn't tear myself away to do anything but pee.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked the original or have any interest whatsoever in 3D platformers, get this game. _childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not too far in, but I can tell this is a recommended game. _childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: I knew Psychonauts by name for years as a fan of Tim Schafer. _childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most gorgeous games I've ever played, in nearly every aspect. Not to mention the different areas of the hub world, each feel alive and vibrant in their own way. Imma say it, I enjoyed this game more than even Mario Odyssey. _childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: This game isn't perfect; the new combat took some getting used to and some of the flaws of the original are still in place. Annoying figments, collectibles getting lost in the bright and colorful worlds, and some slight looseness in the platforming are all everpresent.That said, this is ABSOLUTELY the kind of sequel I wanted for Psychonauts. The worlds are creative and interesting, the levels are much more dreamlike and surreal thanks to the reduced use of loading screens, and the characters are all interesting to interact with and bring interesting stuff to the story.I've 100%'d the game as of the time of this review, and while there was a certain amount of frustration with specific figments, I couldn't have asked for a better sequel to Psychonauts. It's not perfect, but it gets what's important about the series.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: Brain-tatcular game!!Recaps well enough for newcomers to understand. While still giving existing fans nuance and callback references throughout the game. Had a blast playing through the game and I can't wait to play it all over again to find more smaller details I've might of miss. Oh oh you can pet forest animals <3
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoy this game for a variety of reasons.Easier use and selection of psychic powers in comparison to Psychonauts 1, which was a bit of a rollercoaster for me in finding out how to switch and bind abilities to a certain key on a controller.Beautiful graphics that fit in with the theme and artistic intent of the game. One qualm is that Double Fine didn't make the interns or any of the workers at HQ look anywhere near as hideous as some of the designs in the first game, which is a pity because I was looking forward to gawking at some absolute monstrosities in the sequel.The levels are large and challenge you relatably to the psychic ability you've most recently attained while also making sure that other powers aren't sidelined, I also like how the game isn't quite linear in the choices you can make in fights and level exploration and completion with your psychic abilities, leaving nigh all of them quite viable in most levels and circumstances.I think the VA for Raz (Richard Horvitz) did an incredible job returning to a role from 2005 (though production on the first game begun pre-2002 based on E3 footage from the time).One really essential change from the first game is the ability to 100% the game after finishing it, which was a luxury those who did Meat Circus in the first game did not have, thanks Double Fine :)
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: this game is so wonderful. i loved the first psychonauts, so i had to play this one, and i was absolutely not disappointed. the writing is both immensely clever and beautiful, and also just wow. it's more of the first game but with updated graphics and some little quality of life improvements, and very wholesome character moments. just terrific, definitely recommend, especially to those who enjoy creative platforming collectathons and achievable achievements. also omg that's actually jack black
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: Psychonauts 1 was great but to me the second game just improves on the overall experience in every little aspect. The visuals are stunning to no end.  None of that photorealistic bs that most big devs nowadays drown themselves in, this is true style and creative expression compressed into one big adventure.The characters are well written and fan favourites are being expanded upon.The combat and movement has tons of variety and I honestly believe that everyone will find their favourites the arsenal of options you can choose from.The music is great and the composer improved over the years. The difference between the soundtrack from Psychonauts 1 and 2 is incredible, really.It was truly worth the wait.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not usually impressed by sequels, but this one went above and beyond my expectations, remaining true to the spirit of the original while presenting new ideas and mechanics to keep players interested and expand the lore.A few words of warning, however. The events of the original Psychonauts and the VR game Rhombus of Ruin are revealed multiple times throughout the game, so play those first if you want to avoid spoilers. Also, the environments and art style are just as delightfully creepy as the original, so consider steering clear if you get uncomfortable viewing anatomical cutaways, diabolical dentistry, vomiting goats, and squishy brains.All said, this installment in the Psychonauts series is more than worth your time, a masterful and tightly-woven tale of hilarity, absurdity, and tragedy. This series has come a long way from a kid at psychic summer camp, and I can't wait to see what they come up with next.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: look. i yawned my way through the first hour because of the dialogue. it wasnt my cup of tea at all. as soon as i started helping the mind of the 2nd person i got hooked. the problems these people have are very real and it feels very satisfying to give them solutions and help them solve their issues. i really like the way they tell the story of the characters. you start piecing what they've been through as you're moving through the world. the one that stuck out to me was Bob. seeing his alcohol addiction try to drown his traumas was heart wrenching. hope you enjoy this game as much as i did.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: Kept everything that was unique and funny about the original, whilst smoothing over some of the ps2-era jank the first game had.The only unusual decision was to add fall damage (which can be disabled). There were no areas that I saw where this mechanic added anything useful, conversely though, there were no areas that were really negatively affected by its addition, so wasn't a deal-breaker.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: a PHENOMENAL action platformer with all the charm of the first game, and some incredible level design. my only complaints would have to be that the side characters in the story don't get nearly as much development as the campers in Psychonauts 1, and the levels also lack the puzzle solving elements present in the first game. still a great game, and the parts it does it always does incredibly.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: Just like the first game, its creativity pushed to its extreme.You use the concept of visiting people’s minds to explore and talk about concepts like alcoholism, self doubt, failures, insecurities, responsibility, and so many other topics in a way that seems almost adult like. The commentary that folks have on how people feel is well approached and you really do feel WHY characters act the way they do and how you can take away lessons from it and grow more as a person. This game can’t match the first games' peaks of just sheer creativity, weirdness, and absurdity. But I think this game has more depth and gives you a reason to care more about the bigger picture. The levels are a bit inconsistent in their quality as I feel some of the later levels struggle in telling their struggles/themes correctly and drag a bit. But the highlights are def worth the slow parts.Gameplay wise, it’s the same as the first one but again with the edges polished a bit. It still feels jank in areas and I wish there was more creativity in the way it let you platform and sequence break. The combat is much improved IMO but does peter out by the end as the only challenge is more combinations and numbers of enemies. It’s not horrible but I did feel like just spamming my abilities at times.It’s a really good game with a good message that I really enjoyed.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: Psychonauts 2 is modern action adventure and platformer game akin to the style of games that were prevalent in the early 2000s. The game explores mental health in a positive manner with a focus on healing and understanding ourselves. The story is well written, weaven into each aspect of the gameplay, and with its own share of foreshadowing and twists.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty much now the gold standard for an adventure platformer.The caveat I'd put on this is that the raw gameplay and combat are not that interesting and are trivially easy - so if you don't care for environment design, dialogue and story, but prefer engaging mechanics - then this is not for you.It's theme park ride of a game, you strap in and marvel at the bizarre but brilliant levels, excellent writing and quirky characters the world has to offer.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: This is EVERYTHING you want from a sequel. It expands upon the ideas of the first, beefs up the details, softens the edges, and keeps it just as fun as the first, if not more. The graphics and run smooth as honey and it suits the distinctive art style, the voice-acting is PHENOMENAL; as in SO consistent with the first game that it really does feel like a couple days instead of 10 years (plus Jack Black and Elijah Wood I mean come on), the gameplay is incredible to the point where the diversity of play allows you to breeze through the game quickly or take as much time as you want (combat included). The story itself is honestly beyond perfect in my eyes. They expanded the universe and its lore, whilst also expanding what we know about established characters, and it's all done in such a way that it's never overwhelming or jumping the shark. It's just.. Ough... Perfect is a strong word, and I get that, but I feel the writing and design of the script couldn't have been done better from an artistic standpoint.It's got COMBAT, it's got PLATFORMING, it's got COLLECTABLES, it's got STORY and LORE and INTERESTING CHARACTERS and an ESOTERIC ART DIRECTION.It's a good game and well, WELL worth your money in my opinion. <3
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: A very well made sequel to the amazing first game. Psychonauts 2 is a platformer with a lot of focus on mental health and trauma. At times lighthearted and worth a few laughs, the game focuses on Raz and his adventures in to becoming a full time psychonaut. I found the game at times being a bit weird to control and randomly laggy when entering new areas or fighting on my 1070, but for the most part it held up well. What most important to leave in my review is that its worth the purchase. Both games are fantastic work by Double Fine.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a sequel to one of the best 3D Platformers of all time. After being delayed for what felt like forever, this game became one of the most massively anticipated releases, being hyped up to unimaginable standards. This game had TALL shoes to fill and a massive cult following to satisfy. Now, over 15 years after the first game's release, I am so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ happy to say this game lives up to it's predecessor's legacy and completely deserves all the praise in the world.This sequel manages to capture and stay true to the wonder-filled style of the original while reaching for new heights far above expectation. The humor, the platforming, the powers, the combat, all of it ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ rocks. This game is such a wonderful treat, a fantastic sequel, and an excellent stand-alone (Tho I do recommend at least familiarizing yourself with the original and it's story, if not outright playing the original game). I absolutely love this game and I love Double Fine Production for their dedication to this sequel and making this game a worthy successor.Sidenote: Obviously I'm very vague here and not giving specifics, but I believe this game is best experienced yourself, no spoilers. I want you to be open-minded going in to this mind-bending game about opening minds (and occasionally bending them), enjoy this big-brained masterpiece from the creative heads of Double Fine, headed by the creative Tim Schafer!10/10 I wouldn't mind paying for this again! Wait a second, I would mind a double fine! I hope I didn't make your head spin
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: Doublefine did it again! If you've never played a Tim Shafer game, this is a great one to start with. There is _very_ little I don't like about this game. Let me think.... sometimes the platforming is a little janky and takes a couple of tries, but nothing to really break the flow. Oh and there's some places where the signposting got me confused, but not enough to really annoy me.Other than that: Falling into pits cracks me up everytime, I can't unhear Invader Zim's typical voice screaming. The acting in this game is just GLORIOUS, a cinematics cut of this game would already be worth the time.Did you notice this game is WEIRD? Just when you thought it couldn't get any more outlandish, something stranger happens, but somehow it's all grounded in familiar themes and so recognizable at the same time.Anyway, what a fun game, I want to play it again, just buy it and have a good time. :D
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: I love Psychonauts 1. I played it back in the day when it came out and to prepare for the second game I played it again a few weeks ago. I started playing Psychonauts 2 and first few hours were great. The combat is so fluid. Now you can use your abilities while moving. Raz, now have a dodge move. Combat encounters are enjoyable. The graphics are superb. Every character looks the same like in the first game. Sometimes in sequels devs change character's appearances and it really kills the mood I think. Original voice actors are potraying their characters again. The npcs are annoying and boring compared to first game. Some of the levels and interactions with the npcs are just plain boring and uninteresting. These are my observations. Now let's talk about 2 things that killed my enjoyment and made me wish I was playing Psychonauts 1.Firstly, levels. Even though I finished the game recently, I hardly remember the levels. Other than music festival level, other levels didn't impressed me that much. While playing I always felt like something was missing. Even though I played the first Psychonauts years ago I was still remembering most of the levels before replaying the game again. Coach Oleander's Basic Braining, Mila's Dance Party, Waterloo World are amazing levels. And let's not forget one of the greatest levels ever made in a videogame Milkman Conspiracy. These levels are so good and so enjoyable to play that it is impossible forget them. There isn't any level in Psychonauts 2 that comes closer to Milkman Conspiracy. Especially 3 levels that take place inside Ford's mind are so short that you don't understand what is going on and level ends. It is disappointing. Secondly, cutscenes. First Psychonauts had the right amount of cutscenes. The story was good, and it was not getting in front of the gameplay. Psychonauts 2 however, bombards you with cutscenes. There are too many cutscenes that I just gave up on watching them and started skipping. For example, in one level you enter the level cutscene plays. You take a few steps a fight is about to begin and another cutscene plays. You finish the fight another cutscene plays. You take another few steps and another f*cking cutscene plays. Just in 20 minutes game shoves down 4 cutscenes down your throat. Enough already! I like to PLAY the game not to WATCH IT. If the game is %40 gameplay and %60 cutscene, then I don't consider it a game. Just go make an animated movie.These are 2 reasons that killed my enjoyment. I was so excited to play Psychonauts 2. I pre ordered it, started downloading as soon as it became available but my disappointment is immeasurable. This is definitely not the sequel I was hoping for. In future I'll stick to playing Psychonauts 1.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: don't play it on game pass too long if you're enjoying it. there's no way to transfer your saves once you purchase it on Steam.i'm a good chunk through the game and it doesn't fail to surprise me consistently. my mind was blown after a few hours when the greater hub world is revealed. just when you think you might be coming down from your trip, the game throws something else at you.the levitation ball is a really fun way to get around the world, and exploration in general is very rewarding. combat is also great, requiring you to switch up attacks against a variety of enemies with different weaknesses. the writing is wonderful and all the different facets of the game cohere because of it. it plays out like the movie adaptation of an imaginary cartoon show.i love the music too.so good.highly recommend. wholesome experience. not done yet. don't want to end :(

_childDocuments_.review: I'm about 2 hours in, and really enjoying it so far. _childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: Psychonauts 2 is a wonderful game that surpasses the original in every way. Its funny, its got great action and all of the powers are incorporated in a way that makes them feel useful. They just released a patch that helps people 100 percent complete the game with tracking things by location and a photo filter to help with looking for collectibles.  My hope now is to see a psychonauts 3 someday while the story as it is feels complete and it ends on a high note should it end here the world of Psychonauts feels like a world that could always have many tales to tell and characters that will never lack well... character.
