_childDocuments_.review: This game is very fun. The plot is as twisty and turny as the minds Raz encounters on his journey. It's an absolute blast from the moment the players starts a new save file to the final boss' last moments. Each level provides new exciting challenges, and the music and level aesthetics work together to create atmospheres unlike any I have ever seen. Each power is an absolute blast to use in their own unique way (except for clairvoyance and projection is kinda weak but eh, it works). I can confidently say this game will not disappoint anyone with the slightest interest in platformers.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good sequel of Double Fine's best video-game so far.Not as excellent as its predecessor but extremely enjoyable nevertheless.Compared to P1 this P2 is technically better and artistically as good (which it's a lot), but I found the levels' design a step lower than the ones in P1... It could be because I'm (much) older or because I've played a lot of games since then (though I was far from being a kid or new in the video-game industry when I played P1)... This sequel has not blown my mind as all the asylum levels/minds in P1 did back then. I would rate it as an 8.5/10.NOTE: You should play P1 and the VR Psychonauts game before (the order would be P1, VR, P2). The stories of the 3 are connected and you will miss details otherwise.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: This is a pretty good game. Many people on Metacritic bash it for "aged" graphics and not having Russian localization which isn't such a problem for the most. The graphics are good for a game with a great and unique art style and pretty interesting choices of portraying different minds. This game might not be for everyone, but I personally enjoyed it.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: New Review: This game is truly one of the best platforming games I have ever played. It has the same charm and feel of the original game and just expands on it. I played the entire time without feeling bored or like the game was getting monotonous. There are so many ways to use your powers and go through fights with different combos and strategies, as well as using your powers to solve many puzzles that leave you thinking.Pyschonauts 2 is easily my GOTY 2021. It has beautiful graphics, very fun and fast paced gameplay, great level design, interesting and likable characters, fantastic story, and made it easy to relate to parts of the story.If you are looking for a new platformer, it won't let you down. If you are looking for an enticing story, you'll be hooked fast. I myself have suffered through my own tragedies and the way this game handles mental illness, regret, and doubts and other feelings really hits home and left me with a very wholesome experience.Early game: Wow this is very entertaining. Starting after the story of 1 and the VR experience Rhombus of Ruin (which I have not played), Psychonauts 2 jumps right in without skipping a beat. It feels like a sequel game in true fashion, and has the exact same feel that the original did for me. It's really neat to see the original cast and personalities are back along with the powers and gameplay of the first. Just about 2 hours in and I am thoroughly enjoying the game. The level design is already fun and trippy. I can't wait to play more and discover what else this game has to offer
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely incredibly fantastic! They didn't waste a PENNY on this game from the kickstarter, and this game is filled with so much care, it really does rival the first game.1.New powers are SO FUN. We don't have a few of the powers from the first game, but these are honestly way more fun to use!2.Level design is just *chef's kiss*, perfect. Each level feels so incredible to play, nothing feels reused. 3.Combat has REALLY gotten an upgrade! No fight will ever be the same, and the new enemies and powers are just half of that! They've made it so that all censors are harder to fight. They have new moves, and the AI's for them are also better! No more easy punch stun lock for them anymore.I could go on, honestly, this game was a true treasure that, in my opinion, is on par with and could honestly surpass the first game!
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: A solid platformer with an excellent story, dialog, and quirky humor. Combat can be a bit basic, but there are plenty of in game modifiers that can be obtained to customize powers to be more towards your liking. Very creative level design and exploration opens up after the first few levels.If you played the previous games, this is a must have as this is an improvement over the original. For those of you that haven't played any of the other games in the series, the first boot of the game has a short summary to cover the basics References and callbacks to the previous games and some of the game mechanics may seem even odder without the context.As far as negatives go, finding collectibles in the levels can be bit of a pain as there's no easy way to know what specific items you may be missing. And for anyone finding the game too difficult, there are readily available difficulty accessibility settings to mitigate damage or boost your own.If you aren't interested in collecting every little bit of everything, this game will probably clock in at a solid 20 or so hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly creative settings and story throughout this game. Playing the first probably helps, but I didn't have it fresh in my memory and never felt lost. Fully voice-acted, I love the writing and performances, and loved the collect-a-thon side of things, though probably should've saved some of my collecting efforts until postgame.

_childDocuments_.review: Once again Double Fine has made a wonderfully made game with a compelling narrative and fun gameplay. The story was very exciting from beginning to end and gave much detail on lore details that was absent in Psychonauts 1. The game had wonderful and comedic dialogue akin to the first game and I fell in love with a lot of the cast. I just wished we got to see more from the returning cast like Sasha, Milla, and especially Lili. While I do like a lot of the characters especially the Psychic Six, I had a hard time liking the interns, notable exceptions goes to Sam and Gisu, who had the most character and the best design respectively.The gameplay is 100% an improvement from the first game with a lot more fast paced action sequence to go along with the platforming and puzzles. The added feature of being able to move while using an ability, which is absent in the first game minus dodge-psi blast or levitation, creates a much more rapid combat sequences. All of the psi abilities had some uses in combat and I rarely find that a psi ability was going to waste in combat unlike in the first game where most combat situations could be solved with psi blast.Psychonauts 2 introduced 3 new abilities while removing three others. Replacing invisibility, shield and confusion, we were given mental connection, projection, time bubble. While I would miss shield, I could not remember a time that I would be using invisibility for combat situation or use confusion outside of the bull fights. In the first game there was a noticeable power imbalance between the different psi abilities. Levitation and psi blast rained supreme in many cases. Levitation broke platforming and stages, making puzzles trivial and psi blast made combat too easy especially after the shot scatter upgrade, the other abilities was niche and was used in some puzzles. The second game fixes this issue by revamping some abilities and adding enemies that had specific weakness to certain psi abilities. I found myself switching from one ability to the other not just level to level, but by combat encounters. Every encounter was different and needed different abilities, and it was fun. I found myself using so many more abilities and this is helped by having some of the more hard to used abilities being revamped in this game such as Pyro. The previous game had pyro be very difficult to use since you had to stay stationary while casting it, stopping your movement and made you vulnerable, in this game however pyro can be casted while moving and you get an indicator on the are of effect which made pyro very fun to use in combat. Standout abilities that I had most fun with was definitely mental connection and time bubble. Being able to drag opponents closer (or pull yourself closer) was amazingly fun and slowing down opponents so that you can dodge and land more hits before they even finish swinging was hilarious. While some abilities got changed for the better, levitation has taken a very big fall from the godlike status it did in the first game. No longer can you glide indefinitely which is a shame, but I welcome this change. Levitation was downright broken in the previous game and now it is line with the other psi abilities. It is not all bad for levitation, no longer do you need to equip the levitation badge in order to glide or activate ball, there is an option to allow glide to be activate by pressing the jump button 3 times and ball to activate by pressing jump while gliding. This change made levitation much more fun to use since one does not need to keep switching between levitation and other abilities, and it doesn't take a slot that could be used for other combat focused abilities.The game also introduces badges alongside permanent upgrades. These badges add effects or change effects for your abilities or give you passive skills. These range from giving you discounts at the store and changing your orb color to blue, to allowing you to drain the life of an opponent using mental connection or instead of slowing down time, speed it up. You can have up to 3 of these badges at a time and you can change them up on the fly.Psychonauts 2 was an incredibly fun experience and personally I feel like it captures the essence of Psychonauts 1 while also breathing new life into the series, making for a much more exciting entry to the series. I adore this game and cannot wait for what the future holds for Psychonauts. Defintiely 100% Recomnended.P.S More Raz and Lili please.

_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: Psychonauts 2 is the long, long, long awaited sequel to the 2005 classic and it delivers. The creative level concepts of the first game are still on the table but bolstered by a much stronger art style and level of detail to the visuals that's equal parts beautiful and disturbing. The gameplay is a HUGE improvement from the original with much finer controls for platforming and an actual combat system. But the thing that caught me most by surprise was the story. The different mental disorders explored in this game are handled with great care and there's multiple emotional moments that have really stuck with me.It makes me extremely happy to see that Double Fine was able to fully put to page what they've always wanted to with this series. The first Psychonauts was this mangled web of quirks and fun ideas that when mixed together was a unique experience, but one that I thought could be so much more if given the time to grow. Cut to 15+ years later and I think they finally nailed it with their... second entry into the series. Glad to see that the time was well spent.

_childDocuments_.review: Very few games have ever taken more than a decade to release it's sequel without it being terrible. It is a testament to Double Fine's commitment to its fans that Psychonauts 2 has even been published. The original Psychonauts game did not have a great initial release and became something of a cult classic, beloved by those who actually did stumble upon it.I must admit I was one of those fans of the quirky original, but Psychonauts 2 has proved itself to be one of the truely incredible games having received overwhelmingly positive reviews both from original fans and gamers who are new to the franchise. Psychonauts 2 is that rare thing, a sequel that is not only better than the original but stands entirely on its own. The original was great (yes it had flaws, but those were largely the same flaws all games of its generation had), and this sequel is even greater than the original without requiring the nostalgia of playing the original. In many ways, Psychonauts 2 resembles a scrappy underdog, well liked by their small group of friends, after going through multiple intense training archs and finally gains the respect and adoration of of their larger community.If you have not played Psychonauts, but are considering playing Psychonauts 2, do it. You do not need to have played the original. As well loved as the original game was, Psychonauts 2 is so good it turns the original game into a worthy prologue. If you are seeing this because Psychonauts 2 was nominated for a Steam Award for Visual Style, understand Psychonauts 2 has a higher review score than any game that won any of the categories. While I might argue that the wrong game won the Visual Style category purely due to the size of its fan base, I wouldn't necessarily say Psychonauts should have won that category. It however, should have won Outstanding Story-Rich Game, and should have been nominated for Game of the Year, though I will admit Resident Evil Village is also an incredible game and I don't know if I could argue that one is objectively better than the other.If you need to know what you're getting into before buying a game, this is an exception platforming game centered around the psychology of people that have been through various kinds of trauma. You will help them come to terms with those traumas, though you will not do so entirely alone, or without making mistakes. You will learn and wield incredible powers, discover long hidden mysteries, and even discover secrets hidden in your character's own history. You are not some destined hero, you have your own reasons and motivations for what everything you do.While the story is exceptional, the game play is just as good. You will explore many unique worlds, each an inner mindscape reflecting the distinct personality and experiences of the character it belongs to. You will re-master abilities from the original game, but you will master even more new abilities in pursuit not only of helping those around you, but to become a true Psychonaut!
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: I have a lot of great things to say about this particular game. Especially compared to my childhood - high school days, I've become a lot less lenient and lots more harsh with my tastes and reviews with any form of media over time. Used to give a lot of high marks, but nowadays, almost nothing I watch, read nor play feels that same way. This is a very, VERY rare game with a very ambitious scale which actually lives up to it. So much so I'd even say it's a shame people aren't paying full price for the game because of XBOX Game Pass. Like, seriously, this is the best $60 I've ever spent. Psychonauts 2 was, and is, a treat from start to finish and ultimately set a record-high bar for my standards for "excellence;" a game that's newly bestowed my honor of "one of my favorites, ever;" best $60 title I've ever had the pleasure to not only spend money on, but preorder. This game only ultimately suffers from bad marketing, which... isn't even the game's fault. This is sadly an issue the other Psychonauts titles have suffered as well.Way to go, Tim Schafer. Thanks for one of the great experiences I've had the pleasure to play in gaming! Easy Game of the Year 2021 for me.Pros:+ Aesthetically stunning; Better than the likes of Red Dead Redemption II, EA Star Wars Battlefront II and Destiny 2.+ Story was near-excellent: Amazing followup to the first game that really fleshed out the Psychonauts universe and added tremendous depth. Coulda done mildly better developing the [REDACTED] subplot, but that's just me nitpicking. Writing doesn't feel politically shoved down your throat like most media nowadays as well so that's incredibly nice.+ Game controls are some of the best: simple yet flexible, optimized for both controller and keyboard/mouse gameplay+ No microtransactions nor paid DLC? You don't see me complaining.+ Incredibly rewarding and in-depth exploration+ Gameplay mechanics are very diverse whilst maintaining its form of identity as a cartoony-platformer++ Jack Black. The legend himself is a pro no matter how good or bad any form of media is. His singing earned bonus points.+ Soundtrack is incredible: classics from the first game also remixed whilst adding fresh new songs which fit the themes of each brain you enter.+ Still a better love story than Twilight.+ Level designs are unique, wacky and fresh, with a much improved camera system+ Tons more enemy variety than Psychonauts 1.+ Pleasing UI that gets its job done and looks nice doing so.+ Phenomenal voice acting from both new and returning voice actors.+ Genuinely funny during its comedic moments+ Length of the game is more than satisfactory; it fits the game's ambitious scale and plot.+ Difficulty of the game got the job done; required some variety in psychic power combo-ing whilst dodging during combat; the real difficulty lies in finding all the hidden secrets. Invincibility mode is also there for people who just simply want to experience this story.+ A great game to serve as healing and empathy for people who feel hurt and trauma from their mental conditions. Neutral:+- Characters have a lot of depth and personality, but a good handful of side characters could have been utilized a little more; they really deserve it!+- Performance: 98% of the time, the game runs crisp and smooth, but there are very few areas with performance dips, albeit nothing gamebreaking.Cons:- Replayability: Minus some of the figments from Loboto's mind in the beginning and two achievements, you can continue playing after the main game to finish side quests and collecting collectibles, so there's no reason to replay the game. I don't know if I'm missing anything or being biased, but I really can't see anything bad with this game minus the replay value. I normally don't agree with most things people find popular or highly-rated, but this game more than deserved its "Overwhelmingly Positive" status on Steam. This game's a hidden diamond and a half.

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished 100%’ing the game. I’ve always loved the Psychonauts franchise. _childDocuments_.review: All these years later and Psychonauts still manages to deliver both in gameplay and visuals. It is hard to explain to anyone who has not played the original just how fundamentally different each level is. Some are massive and sprawling while you search for items. Others are tiny and require you to collect items. Some are bright and loud, while others are more muted and somber. The story is fascinating as well, delving into themes of mental illness, wrestling with the consequences of bad choices, and the idea that people are often much more complex than we may realize.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most imaginative, brilliantly art directed games ever. Each level is so full of personality and vision, each character designed with such idiosyncratic care. Even its old-school platforming jank somehow adds to its considerable charms. The writing is top notch, the voice acting perfection, the story compelling, fun, and endearing. Do yourself a favor and treat yourself to this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: You'll get about 20 hours of content - from my point of view, it was totally worth full price. There are no repetitive fetch quests, no missions just to artificially stretch the game. The game is incredibly high quality. Areas are artistically diverse to a point you won't find in any other game. The world designs are so creative and the stories of the individual minds you visit have a great balance - fun and engaging in terms of design and gameplay, but with a solid foundation in serious topics of the mind: Loneliness, depression, sadness, madness, alcoholism, losing loved ones, bullying, war, death - the game covers a breath of topics people suffer and struggle with without leaving you feeling down or horrified. The 12+ tag fits the bill, kids that age will enjoy the game as much as adults because the heavy topics are covered with such a delicate and good storytelling that it works great for younger audiences as well.A wonderful game that left me deeply satisfied after finishing.

_childDocuments_.review: I greatly enjoyed this game. _childDocuments_.review: Psychonauts 2 is pretty much the same as the first game, but more of it. It stays true to the style of gameplay and platforming where any review can sum up to:  It's decent in length, at least what I expect this game to be. Expect around 10-15 hours on a casual playthrough. bit less if you don't wish to collect everything, and if you enjoy the game enough to 100%, expect it to take about 16-22 hours.This game is a direct sequel to the first game, and the VR spinoff, so story-wise I highly recommend playing at least the first game before going into this.While I do recommend this game, it's not without some flaws. Some 'worlds' feel a bit on the short side, and 4 of them feel like it was meant to be a single world, but split apart to make there look like there is more places to go to, and with there being much more abilities in the game, but only 4 assigned buttons to use them (since this game highly recommends a controller) You'll be using the ability switch menu a lot throughout the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: This game is highly recommendable.If you liked Psychonauts, then this is a worthy successor. If you dont know Psychonauts, then you should definitely try this gem of a game. It is quirky, dorky and unconventional. But it is also heartfelt, funny and adorable.There is so many things to like about this game.A well crafted and captivating story with an upbeat message.Well formed characters with (literally) multiple layers.A unique and visually appealing art style that changes significantly between game stages.Fresh (and child-friendly) approach to the depiction of mental illness, addiction, narcicism, etc.Every aspect of the game is coated with uplifting humor.Solid gameplay from predecessor refined by some new mechanics.Motivating, yes not too tedious, collectables.Manageable difficulty.Well-rounded length (20-30h gameplay)There are only few aspects that could have made the game even more perfect:two achievements are tedious to get (1 is missable, the other one requires to grind money or not purchase anything, both could be easily be more intuitive to take)dark nodes are still just a gameplay component, while i would want them so much to actually open up the dark side of the mind instead (not just a mental vault, but a real hidden part of each persons story, a reason to revisit each mind, plot-twists!). Second time this opportunity was missed.there are still empty frames in the collective unconcious, it would be nice to fill it with some content (e.g. have all the people appear that do not have their own respective levels, see some background info, talk to them without having to track them down, teleport directly to them, something convenient)
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: It's not for everyone, but if you have the taste for a story oriented lite-platformer, lite-collectathon, it's very good. It was very fun seeing a PS2 game lifted right out of the early 2000's into modern day graphics. The story, characters and voice acting are all top notch. The gameplay could have been much better. Particular problem I've had with it was that you've got more abilities than what is assignable to the controller, so you're constantly pausing to re-assign new abilities that are needed to the shoulder buttons. That doesn't sound so bad if you've played Ratchet & Clank or something, but it doesn't feel ergonomic at all in practice. It made me wish some of the abilities were context sensitive and automated. Like, imagine if you played Ratchet & Clank and you had to manually select the slingshot every time instead of it automatically equipping when sling targets are near. At any rate, I recommend getting on a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: Psychonauts 2 is perhaps a rare success story in video game history where a sequel not only manages to outshine its predecessor in every way possible but also manages to expand its universe and lore with equal if not more depth and details.From the wacky characters, ingenious Brain level designs to a much better control system and excellently designed semi-open regions, Psychonauts 2 always kept me on the edge of the seat to explore more and was an absolute delight! Psi King level is going to be the new Milkman Conspiracy! This time the game gave more emphasis to character developments and the conflict in our own minds and addresses some sensitive mental health issues which were really refreshing to see!Praises aside the game felt it could have expanded and explored more with the story-line and there are too many new characters who quickly go into the background without too much emphasis to the story. The ending also felt rushed, and the new powers you learn are still not as useful like the powers you already start with, barring a few locations where it is needed, which only bolsters the fact that the first game was so good!Is it a perfect game? No far from it. But then again which game is?Wait for Psychonauts 3 begins! ❤

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best action platformers ever made, if not THE best. Period. Just like Psychonauts 1, it's overflowing with character, humor, creativity, but all of the factors that made Psychonauts 1 memorable and lovable are cranked up to 11 in Psychonauts 2. The platforming is much more tight, and the combat is far more engaging, encouraging you to mix and match your psi-powers to deal with enemies in whatever way you want. Exceeding the first game, the soundtrack is PHENOMENAL in Psychonauts 2, and it makes revisiting minds to gather 100% of the collectibles a treat.The story is also much better than the first game. Every character is written like a real person, with flaws and mental disorders, and thought processes that are both unique and completely understandable. I won't spoil too much, but the story is also much more personal to Raz, and as a result will get you much more invested and immersed.Each level is entirely unique and enjoyable in its own way, from its music, to its NPCs, and (of course) its distinct aesthetic. You'll jump into levels that look almost exactly like how you'd imagine the concept art to look like, with their tall and twisted heights, their curving roads, and their mind-bending illusions that shift gravity and bend reality in a way that isn't nauseating, really pulling you into a world beyond reality: the mind.With the Quality of Life patch released in November 2021, 100%ing the game is also much easier, making collecting all the figments manageable and easy, but without entirely trivializing the difficulty of exploration. The only problem is that the X-Ray/collectible finder lens doesn't work on aforementioned reality-bending impossible rooms that are bigger on the inside, but it makes sense as to why. With how colorful and lovable this game is, with its wonderful soundtrack and unique characters, you'll want to 100% it just to spend more time in the seamless, perfectly-executed world Double Fine has crafted.This game is nothing short of art. The level designs are like paintings, the story is like a book, the music is fantastic, and each mind -- the way thought processes and disorders are translated into physical objects, worlds, characters, puzzles, and enemies -- is like poetry. I cannot recommend this game enough, and with the accessibility options that are provided for people who aren't looking for a challenge (invincibility, removing fall damage, etc.), there's no reason NOT to play this game. Buy it for full price, or wait for it to go on sale like I did, I guarantee you're going to enjoy every second of it.

_childDocuments_.review: Tim Schafer, and his crew over at Double Fine have made one of the best sequel games I've played in a long time. Broken Age really put a bitter taste in most fan's mouths, but this game is so sweet. I really enjoyed this game, but I won't exclude my critiques. It's been about sixteen years since the last full fledged Psychonauts title has been released. There are a couple blatant cracks at that, and by the second time it got old.As for graphics, there is quite a variety of settings Raz traverses. The rendered environments were beautiful and left me wanting to explore more. All are quite vibrant and nostalgic notes of the prior games hold throughout its style. Although I wish there was more variety to Raz's outfits while in levels. The visuals have gotten a huge upgrade, but there was something I missed. The faces in the sky. The ones that the clouds formed to be exact. I may be just overlooking them, but I never saw them. They were so perfect for the game's tone when the player notices them.I should mention at this point I 100% completed this game at around 60 Hours. I genuinely believe that this game feels short. I can almost overlook it, but there is really nothing to do in terms of endgame. It is very linear, but has a very open feel to its play-style. Going back to previous levels is easy, but some objectives are unrepeatable. Those are ways to lose out on collecting some figments. Some Psy Challenge markers require some really skillful jumps. Specifically the one in the main Atrium. This was the last item I collected in the game.There was some hate with the LGBTQ+ cast characters in some Steam reviews. The story in the game was genuinely organic, and it's nice to see a studio getting with the times. Their implementation of the story arcs are as genuine as any other video game.To end this succinct review, Psychonauts 2 was well polished and ran beautifully. A very refreshing game in a year with many disappointing releases. Definitely get this game on whatever sale comes your way, because $60 seems like "a fan of the series" kind of price.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a sequel to an early 2000's cult classic -which you should absolutely play, it's like $5- and it has made improvements in every regard compared to the original.The story: not going to spoil anything, but to say that the writing is incredible would be an understatement. There are few moments in this game where the writing is anything short of stellar, and when you do see the points where the writing is not up to the highest standard that the rest of the game exudes, you will be given the contrast of great game versus best game ever. It's that good. Also, the ending isn't a mess like the first one and is actually a great conclusion to the story. Overall story grade IMO: 9.9/10, nearly perfect.Mechanics: This game has a lot of really fun abilities that will all be useful at multiple points in almost every level. The abilities are all really fun to use and feel mostly quite responsive and interesting... I rarely used only a few of them. The only one that feels anything short of incredible is the last one you get, but it's fine; it just doesn't feel as polished and well-integrated as compared to the other ones, but it is voice acted by the same voice actress that played Gir, so it technically makes this game an Invader Zim fan game, so it's alright I guess. Mechanically very good, an 8.7/10Visuals: The game is ugly. That is a good thing. The art direction of this game has many different ways that goes in and they were -no doubt- the most demanding part of the pipeline since they are all very, very, very well done and give the game cohesion despite the many different directions the art goes in. Every level's art style is unique and beautiful and it never feels like an afterthought; instead, it generally feels like the nexus around which the level is made. Art direction, 10/10. A masterpiece.Music/sound design: This game sounds great, the voice acting is all very well done, and each character is brought to life through their voice. The characters are highly expressive and funny and they all feel like someone that you could meet and have a long conversation with. The music is incredible and always very fitting for the mood of the story that is taking place. The sounds of the game are all very well put together and are just the right mix of unsettling, silly, and fun. 8/10.Now down to the brass tax. This game is incredible and I want more. If the developers do end up reading this, this is my suggestion to you guys.

_childDocuments_.review: From someone that didn't really vibe 100% with the first entry, Psychonauts 2 grabbed me from beginning to end. Art direction (and the variety on offer) is the main standout, with palette choices and composition constantly forcing me to stop an gawk in fear of being overwhelmed (in a good way). Animation is a close second for me, with all of it actually being animated by hand rather than supplemented with mo-cap. Most of the animation work is great (if stiff at time in regards to the canned stuff during dialogue scenes), with several fantastic set-pieces sprinkled throughout that genuinely floored me. Blizzard's top dog in video games for animation and, at points, Psychonauts 2 approaches that level of quality.Voice cast is stacked, which seems to be the norm for Double Fine. Music pretty nice as well, and as varied as its settings, but not as memorable for me. In fact, the only real knock I can give this game is it's bizarre audio mixing during a few cut-scenes, where it seems some foley effects are missing or muffled.Everything is wrapped together in a surprisingly personal story from the expected psycho-spy adventure. Truly, just fantastic, from beginning to end.

_childDocuments_.review: A worthy sequel to the original - not better, which is likely partially my own fault.Pros:* Signature DoubleFine humor all over the place.* Great level design and music.* Great plotlines and voice acting.* Nice wrapping-up of loose threads from the original.* Mostly great re-implementation of fundamentals, to streamline the game.* Excellent new enemies and groupings of same, requiring switching up strategies on the fly.Cons:* Freeze bug when examining objects in inventory system; gotta kill  the game to get around it.  WTH?* None of the levels are quite as... bug-f*ck nuts, as the original. (which  based in an asylum, though?)* Levels seem a little more... formulaic, than in the original.* When replaying a level, I miss the teleporters at the end of the level; instead, have to either retrace steps to a teleporter, or jump entirely out of the "mind" then go all the way back in.* The game's just not as... original?...  as the original.  Likely just because I've played the 1st one to death.* Lots of missed opportunities with the other interns - the "fellow kids" shtick was done much better in the original.* No longer can punch while on a levitation bubble. Ditto w/ gliding indefinitely. WTF?* Cosmetic changes (bubble color change, idle dance, etc) now need to occupy an equipment slot I'd use for fighting enemies... which means I'll never use them.* $60.  Really?TL;DR: If you merely liked the original or never played it at all - and it's not on sale - then 5/10.  If you loved the original it might be worth your cash at full price, else if it's on sale, 7/10.Edit: Added more details and dropped scores by 1 - the nerfs (cosmetic & levitation) and high price are serious dissatisfiers.

_childDocuments_.review: If you loved the first one, you'll be mindblown on this one. I loved the open-world exploration feel, the unique and fun characters with their witty banter and interactions, the rich and ever-changing inner mind-worlds, the gradual increase in difficulty that is challenging but not punishing. This has it all. I'm probably only about 30% the way through the storyline, but I am 100% confident that this game is everything that I had hoped it would be. The game feels like a continuation of the first, not a shoe-horned repetitive call back to the original, and stands on its own in its own right (though you should probably play the amazing first one too). Everything that was great about the first, they brought it over and continued it. The controls feel smooth and camera is much improved from the first. They've somehow kept the graphics seamless with the first without making it feel dated. I am savoring this game and taking my time through the game, cause I don't want it to end.Edit: Finished the main storyline and am continuing finding all the secrets, it's so good! Also I should probably mention that I am not typically a fan of platforming games, but this game is sensational and I love it. Nominating it for 2021 GOTY, it has my heart.

_childDocuments_.review: Short version: A juice-less collectathon with stale controls that's fun to look at and marvel, but not to listen to it's characters natter. Compared to Psychonauts 1, the controls aren't as fun, the audio design isn't as juicy, the characters aren't as unique. I have only played one level, and it was heavily designed around exposition rather than exploration, which it did not deliver as engagingly as P1's exploration gameplay.Psychonauts 1 is a classic. Unfortunately, it feels like Double Fine didn't really understand what was fun about Psychonauts 1.The first fun thing about P1 is the characters; instead of honest and out-there kids (and adults) with barely-hidden issues, the characters in P2 are completely interchangeable, and either snide middle-schoolers from Rich Kid Prep or office workers from any office ever. The P1 characters could only ever be from P1, while these P2 characters don't bring any edge, any voice, or anything to tell them apart, really. There's no Dogen, no Vernon, no Bobby Zilch, and the characters have no relationships with each other. Maybe that will change, and more of them will be revealed as the game goes on, but after 3 hours I started skipping cutscenes because I don't want to hear fancy children in scarves be vanilla-smarmy to each other any more.The structure of Psychonauts 1 is also really fun for me, as I dig exploration games, and the levels of P1 always found new ways to reward exploration. So far in P2, it's been very linear and plot-focused. There have been many, many cutscenes, and some of them really try to be cool and stylish, but they never land right. So far, the exposition has really chopped up the gameplay, either adding sequences that make the level design confusing and disjointed, or adding macguffins that completely stall the plot for barely justified reasons.The premise ditches the Summer Camp Adventures! theme for an office building and spy-kids. The office building, even in the goofball-expressionist style of Psychonauts, is still a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ dull-ass office building, and a humongous step down from bunks, a lodge, and an outdoor toilet. And the spy-kids concept just doesn't blend right here. There are parts of the game that want to be cool Psychic Spy Adventure! (which is an incredible concept!) but it doesn't sit right with with the ponderous walk speed and the clumsy controls. (The control scheme is the same as from P1, which feels like a bellweather. What Double Fine thinks is cool and what is clunky from P1 is clearly very different from what I think. You still run out of buttons for psychic powers and why don't you hold jump to float and slow your jump like in EVERY OTHER ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ GAME EVER AGHGHGHGHG)From Psychonauts 1 I remember bumping around on my levitation ball, collecting bouncy, nigh-invisible collectibles that make delightful noises, making huge, exciting, floaty leaps, and charging into and slapping enemies. P2 delivered none of that. Besides the walk speed being slower, the ball feels slower and like it jumps much lower, you can't attack while you are on the ball (but there are more aggressive enemies with better targeting!), and, worst of all, the noises collectibles make on collection is PATHETICALLY UNSATISFYING.(Enemies are so much more aggressive and dangerous, and Raz is so much doofier, that his health had to be DOUBLED for P2. Another sign that Double Fine has taken Psychonauts away from what I think is cool.)The audio hasn't struck me at all yet. The new voice actors all have pretty straight lines they deliver in a generically mediocre way. I've only fought a few different monster types so far, but the censors, the same enemies from P1, have the same sound effects (which are great in P1!) just with less focus. They sound further away, not highlighting that rad NONONO sound effect, and they don't have very noticeable entrances. No new enemy has matched the awesome squeal-POP noise of the exploding kamikaze fireballs of P1. I've only played one level, and it combined a hospital with a casino. Rad idea! I didn't notice the music doing that at all, just fading out for the hospital part and being loud and brassy for the casino. That might be a problem with the disjointed design of the level, though.In P1, there is a collectible you have to chase like the bunny from Super Mario 64. It's a little, four-legged vault that gallops away from you. It's aggravating to catch the squirrely little bugger! But it never takes too long, and when you hit it with a big SLAP, it immediately flops down, opens up, and gives you a cool slide-show cutscene of the secret, hidden troubles of one of the games' characters. Very cool, very satisfying. In P2, the same little, four-legged vault is more irritating to catch (because you go slower and can't attack while riding the levitation ball, so its less fun), and it takes three hits to stop instead of one. Those hits just make the vault flash red, I couldn't discern it playing any hit animation. It doesn't slow down or anything when hit, so it's just dull repetition with less exciting payoff. That means the same creature in P2 is less enjoyable to try to catch and less satisfying to finally capture. I found two of these vaults in P2: the first one showed me backstory that the game literally just said to me in the previous scene, and the second one I skipped because I was done with the dull characters. The reward for getting the collectible didn't feel special or important. This was never true for me when I played P1.There are a lot of ways P2 really pushes to be unique and special and show you something new. And it does! I've never in a video game run across a landscape of X-rays, jumping from X-ray photo to X-ray photo with a cutscene in the background explaining the past of the character whose mind I am exploring. That's cool! But when the platforming is banal, the characters are loud and flashy but don't have the hook or uniqueness I expect, and the cutscene is exposition that's being explained to me for the third time, well, that all makes me withdraw.So yeah. Psychonauts 2 hasn't really drawn me in much at 4.5 hrs on record. I fought a boss that looked really cool, (an electric phallic squid lady!), and I was okay with the solid-but-simple platforming mechanics to beat her. But beating her was confusing (partly because a half-dozen, interchangeably-snarky middle schoolers WONT STOP SHOUTING AT YOU, while the boss is ALSO SHOUTING AND COUGH-VOMITING THINGS AT YOU), and the gameplay hasn't gelled any more than the narrative (which pushes you to do cool spy stuff!) has gelled with the goals of gameplay (do an absolute ton of side-stuff and uncover a random character's backstory with no urgency to move the plot forward!)The list of little touches that P1 does better is very long: the attack combo is animated and sound designed with so much more impact, the leap arcs are so much more dramatic, there are more collectibles in more interesting positions and level design flows better, the characters say less but with more character, etc, etc. It feels like more time was spent building cool ideas for P2 than refining them. So P2 doesn't hang together in the special way that P1 does. However, I will very likely play Psychonauts 2 again. I will probably beat it one day. There is a small chance I will 100% it. The game has really cool parts to it, like awesome outside-the-box level ideas and style that is very much it's own, even if it's not as unique as P1. Those positives don't really make up for the fact that controlling Raz is less fun; he feels much less nimble and beating enemies and collecting things isn't as rewarding. It just REALLY sucks that finding and seeing all the cool parts of this game means playing a juice-less collectathon with stale controls.So, not a heartbreaker sequel. But definitely not the game I was hoping for. If you haven't yet, play Psychonauts 1 or Brutal Legend first instead.7/10; do not recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: It's not often that a sequel meets or exceeds the expectations of the original - especially when there was so much time in between the two.  Psychonauts 2 definitely lives up to the hype.  A charming, fast-paced, medium-difficulty platformer (like the original), Psychonauts 2 shines in the uniqueness of the level design, game mechanics and storyline.  With solid writing and acting, the characters are engaging, while the gameplay and plot keep the story from ever stagnating. Upgrading from the older graphics without losing the charming character designs was a challenge, I'm sure, but I'm glad they did.  The big-headed, spindly characters lend an almost Tim Burtonesque feel fans will remember from the first game, and it keeps the game riding in that part of the uncanny valley that keeps everything a little off-kilter.  Adding an even more diverse cast of characters in the form of interns was a good design choice, though I felt it was a little pushy at times.Bringing back all the original cast members (as well as adding some heavyweights like Jack Black), was a stroke of either luck or genius, but it paid off.  Additionally, the perfectly matched music made for an incredible audio experience. The overall feast of the senses is almost meta, given one of the primary level concepts, but regardless, it makes for a most enjoyable game.10/10 - Solid work by the Double Fine team!   (And don't forget to play the VR game "Rhombus of Ruin" for the complete Psychonauts experience.  It's a totally different kind of game, but follows immediately after the first, and is referenced several times in this game).
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: Coming from Psychonauts 1, this game blew the graphics out of the water. Everything is so detailed in the way the world is presenting it. A lot of the mental worlds you enter are very enjoyable to just look at, let alone play. They improved the movement greatly, but I wished Raz had his levitation skill permanently bound to something, as his on foot speed is so slow. The story is pretty good, but you kinda need to know the characters before you play this game to get the full effect of the interactions. Otherwise, I'd totally recommend this game if you need a new platformer that is eye candy.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: It's a stunningly well-made brawler/platformer touching on mental health issues that somehow isn't out of place in 2021.  \\SPOILER WARNING\\The levels are well-designed, the dialogue options are expanded and just as funny and rewarding as the original, the game is much prettier than the original, you actually get to go in Ford's mind this time (kind of a glaring omission in the first one if I'm being honest), there isn't a point of no return like last time around, there's an actual opportunity to explore in the post-game, and the hub world is bigger with even more collectibles and fast travel options. They put five years of serious work into this game, and it shows. Somehow it even runs on my laptop at medium quality, which I was super pleased about. Besides all the crashing, which you probably won't encounter if you meet the minimum system requirements.The game isn't flawless. There's a bug in Bob's Bottles that forced me to restart the game, and anti-aliasing doesn't always work (again, though, the second should be solved by having a good computer). Also, when I said the game touches on mental health issues, I mean that it shies away from anything hard to swallow like psychosis or schizophrenia. Probably for the best, as the first game had a whole chapter on paranoid delusions, but the way the game portrays alcoholism and multiple personality disorder is the opposite of hard hitting. On alcoholism, you're physically going into the bottles, jumping around on bottles as platforms, and carrying plants' bulbs and seeds around, all inevitably culminating in a kind of a letdown of a boss battle. On multiple personality disorder, the story is compelling throughout each personality, but each personality is more of a mini-level with many fewer figments than a normal level. Kind of makes sense, but there were more than three personalities to Ford. I feel like this is the part of the game they could have expanded on, with maybe five or six total shards to the mirror? Ford's fully-there mind, though, doesn't disappoint at all.The only other problem I can think of is how anticlimactic the final boss battle is, making it seem like the main antagonist was never really a gigantic threat in the first place, cut-scenes notwithstanding. All you do is dodge and PSI blast repeatedly. That's it. Otherwise the game is really great. Ford's true mind is chilling and foreboding, Compton's mind is a serviceable representation of anxiety, Cassie's mind accurately portrays how people can have a healthy amount of "sides" to their personality, and how, unhealthily, they can allow one side to completely take over. The visualizations of psyches really make the game, though the game-play, exploration, dialogue, characters, story, and music certainly help make it that much better. The voice-acting roles by Jack Black and Elijah Wood are fantastic, too.//SPOILER WARNING AGAIN//There are some plot-holes. Why did the mole mail his body to the person whose mind he stole? Why did he chain that person's brain to his wrist in a box? How did he overpower that person in the first place? Why did he mail a clue to that person? How did he know Raz curing Ford would help the mole toward his goal? Yes, they mostly involve the mole, but otherwise the story is fun to work through and sensibly constructed.Overall, the game is alternately funny, sad, cute, and joyful, allowing for both gamers from 2005, looking for a worthy sequel to a beloved game, and gamers from 2021, looking for an interesting game on their Steam queue or wish-list, to experience a well-written, expertly made, beautiful game. Try it for yourself.

_childDocuments_.review: If you loved the original you'll love this. All the charm and humor that made the original a cult classic is back, but with improved gameplay and a more involved and interesting story. The new mental worlds are tons of fun, and while there's nothing as memetic as The Milkman Conspiracy one of the levels in particular is so delightfully bat**** insane that it more than makes up for it. My only complaint is that the game is a bit pricey for the length. Obviously if you want to 100% the game you will spend a lot of time hunting down every collectible. But, if you just play it to completion, trying to do as much as possible without tons of hunting and backtracking, it's under 20 hours. This is the perfect length for a Psychonauts game but a little light for something that costs $60 in my opinion. Still, it's a 10/10 from me, especially if you can grab it on sale for 25% off or more.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not kidding when I say I'm one of the people that have waited 15 years for this game and even though I already beat it just a few days after launch, I  can't believe this game exists.  Double Fine did so much right with this game that any negatives I have feel like nitpicks   What can I say that hasn't already been said? The tight platforming, the funny and clever dialogue, the lovable and unique cast of characters, the rock solid level design, just the unbridled charm and love this game exudes? It's all been lauded time and time again.

_childDocuments_.review: 15 years, at least for me it's been that long. Through out that time many people would discover the gem that was and still is Psychonauts.Over the course of 2 weeks I not only played the game from start to finish but also 100% the game, all with in a play time of a little under 2 days.When this sequel was announced about 5 years ago, I was instantly hyped for it like many were. Unfortunately a lot happened in that time. Many games were announced, came out, and were just one disappointment after another. Game companies bumbling into any number of scandals ranging from intentionally shipping bad games, intentionally shipping incomplete games, or intentionally violating the rights and sense of safety of developers.It was easy to grow bitter and distrusting of any upcoming video game and the people that made/published them for that whole time. Even when game play of Psychonauts 2 was shown off, I still had my doubts about it.To say the least, it is truly a breath of fresh air to have in my possession a game that honestly feels like the people worked on it actually cared about it as much as I did. I honestly can't be happier about this.Sappy stuff done and out of the way, what's my review?Pros:1. It's Psychonauts through and through. If that is what you expect to get when you buy this game, that's what you will exactly get.2. Game play is tight across the board. You'll find it hard to point out moments in the game that you feel like you have no control over Raz.3. Fun every step of the way.4. Funny, even when it gets too cheesy you can't help but laugh.5. A true collect-a-thon done right.Cons:1. Steam version is a bit buggy. You'll find a few issues as you play but all of them sort themselves out in the end. One in particular though quite literally sort itself out but the end of the game for me to finally go back and finish that one level.2. Easy to sequence break in a few places. It's not too bad but it did throw me off when Raz said something that I didn't know anything about until I made my way to where he was supposed to go first to learn that information.That's about it. This was an amazing ride and a satisfying ending to a long waiting part of my child hood. Hope you all find the same satisfaction in your own ways.-Gently

_childDocuments_.review: There's a lot to truly love about Psychonauts 2. The aesthetic and the characters within this world charmed the bejesus out of me, a hallmark of Double Fine. There are some smart moments of writing too, especially in the way the game addresses mental issues with a gentle humor and underlying seriousness.  And as a complete package, this might be the meatiest Double Fine game to date, with lots of levels and exploration to be had. But.But like so many Double Fine games, this is a chore to actually play at times. Platforming elements often feel just a hair off, like the main character Raz should either magnetize better or make easier connections with the next environmental object. There are also some bafflingly difficult portions of the game that are only that way due to the controls or frustrating elements within the environment. For example, a clever bowling alley-themed level is nearly ruined by having to negotiate a bowling ball like a marble through jumps and turns meant for a game that controls better than this.That too is a depressing hallmark of Double Fine games. They're often very clever but hampered by having to actually play them. In Psychonauts 2's case, that cleverness and the sense of love that went into this game are enough to pull it out of the fire, but there really needs to be much more playtesting and a general questioning of "is this element fun?" in future games.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:- Looks great, very vibrant colors and character designs.- Consistently good voice acting performances and the worldbuilding is very in depth.- Fun and charming!Cons:- Feels clunkier than the first game in my opinion, I don't know how to explain it- Too many cutscenes, wish there was more gameplay in a game.- Story is a lot more underwhelming than it was in the first.- The humor is very hit or miss.

_childDocuments_.review: I think my biggest mistake was to play this right after finishing the first one. It makes the flaws and issues so much more apparent. Here's a summary;Pros;1-Vibrant, colorful world2- fluid gameplay, responsive controls3-  Interesting story and intriguing plot twist. I got the feels in a few of the Ford quests.4- some lovable and unique character designs, and it was nice to see the old characters back!5-  Sound design is spot on and fits very wellCons;1- The newly introduced sidecharacters are lackluster, mean and boring. I felt nothing for them, and wanted to skip almost every dialoge they had. Most of every other character without a role looked like a muppet.2- The game has gotten much more child friendly, which isn't necessarily a bad thing since it is a game for children... But most of the humour the old game had is gone, and you're constantly handheld and backseated the entire game. 3- The levitation skills have been so nerfed it's almost sad. Even fully upgraded, there's hardly any difference...4- The game felt short, and it felt like there was nothing to do but the main story most of the time. I might not have been able to trigger some events, but honestly the game felt so empty..5- I began getting bored early on, but the main story kept me playing. It felt like such a dissapointment considering how much I enjoyed the first game.---So, honestly? I was pretty bummed out. But for a child, or someone who hasn't played the first game in a while, I fully reccomend the game!There was so little to do. So few minds to explore. So little character interaction with anyone, and what little you got were just Raz being belittled or abused by almost everyone around him. When the other 'interns' were redeemed, I still fully despised them, and felt nothing for them. The same goes for the older siblings and your mother.  In the first game, you were basically only bullied by two people, but that was the steriotypical bully pair. Even though there was a lot of side characters, you still wanted to save them in the end, or listen to their dialog.  I can still remeber half of the names of the people you met in the first game, but nobody in the second, at least the side characters.I have a lot more to say, but I feel like it'll be too nitpicky. so I'll leave it at that.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: It's really good and it's exactly what I wanted as a longtime Psychonauts fan. As proof... it's been out only a week and I already spent 30 hours playing to 100% the game. This game is the first game in a long time that I can say is completely worth buying at full price.It's more of that Psychonauts platforming goodness with a few extra mechanics/psi powers thrown in the mix to add a little more variety. For completionists, the collectathon gameplay is still there. With hundreds of figments to collect, mind vaults to punch open, emotional baggage to sort, and nuggets of wisdom to find... there's plenty to keep you occupied for a good chunk of your time. The platforming feels nice and Raz controls really well.This is where the game really shines... just like the first one. As fans of the original know, the levels themselves give you insight to various characters because of the premise of the games (You are diving into various character's minds and the levels themselves are a representation of that character's mental state). There are a lot of really great levels here and while the first game probably had some of the wackiest levels out of all the games, I would say that a lot more of the levels in this game come to a heartfelt conclusion on various characters. If you are looking for trippy levels that play with the laws of gravity, physics, etc. this game has that in spades. I can't really go more in detail without spoiling anything, but if you liked the levels in the first game, you will like them in this game.Wow! Everything about the world is expanded on! We meet new characters. We get to see Psychonauts headquarters. We see more of Raz's family. We get to see the origins of the Psychonauts organization. And more! And it's all a really well told story too! While I liked the story of the first game a lot... this one took it up a few notches! They really spent a lot of time on trying to convey why characters were the way they were and the way they dealt with revealing this information always felt sincere and heartfelt (sorry if I am using that word too much). Every story character was treated with respect by the developers and no one was really "the bad guy". Everyone had reasons for why they did what they did and the developers really tried to make you understand how that character came to believe what they believed or do what they did. Like it states at the beginning when you start up, the entire game is about empathy and thus understanding others and their own motivations is a big part of the story. And the developers also tried (and I think succeeded) in clarifying that Psychonauts is not about "fixing" people but about helping people address their own personal demons. All in all, the unique premise of Psychonauts allows for some really interesting stories to be told and the writers took full advantage of that!It is very stylized and faithful to the original. They stylized art helped make sure that the original still looked pretty good even after all these years... and this game is just that but with an upgrade.

_childDocuments_.review: Do I recommend this game? YesKeyboard accessible controls as well, controller not necessary. I do believe the first game is definitely a prerequisite to play before this game for mainly story, this is a great continuation. The areas seem stunted as continuation seams are cut to now allow easy flow between areas. While this could be an issue due to loading, it just really makes continued exploration seem more of an afterthought than a catered experience like the previous game. Especially with certain powers only being achieved in late game and fully explored in post. I kinda would like it to be able to skip the interrupting tutorial if you had played Psychonauts 1 with how certain powers worked. Wall jumping is a nice surprise, and the limit to levitation hover is understandable considering how easily it could break the challenge in the first game. Challenge wise, I would say it is definitely more to juggle than Psychonauts 1, especially with more complex enemies as a focus with the mix of combat and powers. _childDocuments_.review: The wait for Psychonauts 2 was like the wait for Incredibles 2. The difference? This time, the wait was worth it. Psychonauts 2 is a fantastic sequel that, like its predecessor, oozes style out of every wrinkle in every brain. While it does look and feel a lot brighter than the original, it explores the darker tones and details in a way that gives the game a more consistent theme of tragedy and healing. Psychonauts 1 gave countless clever details relating to characters' mental disorders and history, but 2 expands upon them and makes them the heart of the narrative. With how well this game's story played out, it could have gotten away with being worse than the first in every other aspect, but they really gave it all to us. The new powers are fun and interesting, the platforming is unique (though not particularly challenging), and of course, the visuals are absolutely phenomenal. Far and away the coolest looking game I've played in a long time. Most people seem to agree, though, that combat is a bit awkward. It was never a highlight of the original so it's not a downgrade or anything, and I do appreciate that they attempted to flesh it out, but it was pretty clunky.Phat 9.5/10, immensely satisfying experience

_childDocuments_.review: is a fantastic follow-up to the cult classic original. The best way I can describe the game is an interactive Pixar film. I was glued to the game from start to finish, although there were some bumpy patches along the way. Raz finally arrives at Psychonauts HQ, the Motherlobe, after his misadventures at Whispering Rock and the Rhombus of Ruin. However, he quickly finds that his promotion to Psychonaut isn’t official and is demoted to an intern. Now he has to climb back up the ranks, all while dealing with a whole new work environment, the other interns, his estranged family, and a new psychic conspiracy that threatens to drown both the Psychonauts and the world. In a world of psychic espionage, there are some secrets best left buried…The story was pretty great. There were multiple twists and reveals that had me eager to see what the next bend had in store. While nothing terribly new or innovative was used in the story, the execution was exquisite and I rarely felt bored. PN2 has a huge cast of new characters and continues the witty writing from PN1. However, I feel that some of them could’ve used more time in the spotlight as they quickly became background characters. Nonetheless, I really liked everyone and they all contributed something to the journey. This time around, a greater emphasis is placed on mental damage and how Psychonauts can help heal people. While specific disorders and diseases aren’t directly mentioned, their inclusion helped make their owners feel like more realistic and relatable characters. Healing, growth, and connections are central themes, and PN2 does a nice job exploring them all.      PN2 is a massive glow-up from 1. Essentially, every area has been refined and polished, making PN2 a blast to play. To start, platforming is much more engaging and challenging, mostly due to great environmental design. Often times, navigating the terrain is a puzzle in of itself. For example, trying to navigate a cave network via wall ivy, stone platforms, mine rails, and more. As a result, each new real-world zone was thrilling, with different terrain challenges and nooks and crannies to explore. Thus, you're always on an adventure, even when just wandering around the real world. I’ve spent a lot of time just wandering around the real world, scraping around for collectables and enjoying the views.In order to compliment the platforming, Raz’s powers have been refined and the game truly feels built around them. You can find challenging far jumps requiring skilled Levitation jumps and tight hovers, or use Pyrokinesis to clear areas or even create new pathways. As a result, you'll be tested on how well you can use your powers, and some interesting puzzles are made around them. Additionally, every power has combat applications to make your toolset more versatile. On that note, combat is very engaging and involved. Encounters are pretty frequent, each containing multiple enemies, and most enemies take some time to put down. While they all have pretty straight-forward tactics, getting swarmed and having to counter all their strategies at once is an exhilarating feeling. Since all your powers are usable in combat, you’re free to create your own strategies for victory. Raz’s powers operate on a cooldown system, so knowing the proper time to use a power always feels rewarding. I'm pretty conflicted about most boss battles. On the one hand, their presentation and thematic mechanics are excellent. The sheer scale of the fights is amazing, and each boss feels truly personalized to the person they torment. On the other, the rule of three is heavily used, so encounters feel very scripted and rigid. Certain gimmicks are also really annoying to deal with. For example, digging specific items up to use against a boss as they attack you. All in all, I think the style outweighs the substance. Collectathon elements felt like they could’ve used some work. There are 5 types of collectables and their main purpose is to allow Raz to level up. However, keeping track of them all can be a hassle. The completion page bundles all the areas of a level into one page, making tracking down missing items downright painful and annoying. Likewise, since the scope of each level has been immensely increased, finding those very last collectables can easily get tedious and frustrating. For a casual playthrough, this is a minor inconvenience. For completeionism, this is a nightmare.  I did a lot of collecting and exploring, so I finished in around 18-ish hours. 100% completion took around 25 hours. While the game is of moderate length, I feel the ride was enough to justify the price. There's also a proper free-roam mode after completing the story, which is a very welcome addition.I absolutely love PN2’s visual design. Modern graphics elevate the eccentric design of the series to a new height. Mental worlds are the clear winners here, each being whimsical yet profoundly telling of their owners. While I described PN1’s worlds as “unique amusement parks”, PN2’s all feel like different planets due to their wildly different themes, scales, gimmicks, and more. The visual design is marvelously done and I found myself enraptured in quite a few. Character designs for the series are rather unique, taking a 3D approach to cartoony designs. Admittedly, some designs look a bit strange, but the sheer diversity helps create memorable characters. Overall animation quality is pretty good, aside from clipping and lip synch issues distracting during certain cutscenes and talking segments. The soundtrack really hits all the right notes while playing. From nostalgic remixes of PN1 tracks to new and emotional ones, I always had a smile on my face when taking in the music. Many original voice actors also reprise their roles, which is phenomenal. Newer voices were also great as well, although some lines felt weird from a directing or quality standpoint. Sound effects were pretty solid across the board.  Overall, the Steam version ran pretty smoothly. There were some stuttering problems, but they seemed to smooth out after a while. I also experienced one "Fatal Error" crash. However, people have been reporting various other issues, so your experience may vary.A nice amount of graphical and audio options are available for tweaking. You're also offered an impressive amount of accessibility options to make the game more approachable, such as larger fonts and colorblind filters. I played with a Xbox controller and everything functioned well. You are able to rebind both controller and KBM controls.  I am in love with what PN2 has achieved. The 16-year wait was well worth it and the product is something I feel anyone can enjoy. Practically everything is an amazing step up from the first game, and I thoroughly enjoyed the journey as a result. Replayability is a bit limited due to its linear nature, but collection completion will take a lot of time and effort in the meantime.

_childDocuments_.review: Presentation (3.5/5) - visually creative settings for a game with creative world building and theme. Cartoony 3d style with some scattered 2d textures mixed in. Music is pedestrian, sound goes well with the graphics and also has character. The visualization of mental health concepts as enemies to fight is cleverly executed and rather amusing. Voice acting is good, sometimes overenthusiastic to a fault.Story/Dialogue (3/5) - Heavy on exposition at times and backstory briefly explained in still images. Story and dialogue resembles a merely above average children's cartoon with hit or miss humor that overemphasizes puns and gross gags. Story seems oddly paced because its progression centers around 'let's get into this person's mind'. Sometimes game does get into very dark territory though without matching visuals (let's have a crying pursetag while discussing death or alcoholism). While the story is likely great for most, I found myself disengaged and even checking my phone at times.Gameplay (3.5/5)  - A mix of adventure and platforming mechanics where you gain a larger number of skills as you progress that can be exploited in some platforming scenarios, These skills also have their uses in combat, excelling in specific circumstances. Boss fights are complex and require you to adapt to what is being thrown at you. The gameplay is in other words adaptable, if a bit easier than it should with no difficulty options for a bigger challenge. The gameplay suffers from having too many cutscenes, often interrupting the flow.

_childDocuments_.review: This one was a long time (5 years since the crowdfunding campaign in 2016, 16 years since the first Psychonauts) coming, and the wait has absolutely been worthwhile. Double Fine have taken the gameplay of the original Psychonauts (Story-heavy 3rd-person adventure 3D platforming) along with its charming characters and wonderfully colorful, surreal, and cartooney art design and brought the experience out of the 00's, into the '20s, and for the better. The control scheme and feel of Raz's movement in the first game was a pain point for a lot of players, since his movement could feel at alternate times too loose and too sluggish. That complaint gains less foothold here; the movement scheme has been honed to be more fluid but retain much of its feel from the original. Complaints about infrequent punishing platforming sections in the original (merited, to be sure) and frustration with extended collect-a-thon patterns have also been addressed.Psychonauts 2's story feels like a step forward as well -- 2005's release had excellent theming around persevering through and overcoming individual trauma to be healthier and more whole as an individual, while this outing focuses more on community/friendship/family and being accepting and caring as support for mental well-being, and it feels much more cheerful and encouraging for that slight shift of emphasis.Double Fine have outdone their first release, and without diminishing the original's appeal. Yes, 2 is a mechanical and (arguably) thematic improvement but the original had so much charm that the small improvements here feel like they are hardly changes at all. This makes me want to invent a new term for simultaneous experience of nostalgia and novelty just to put a term to what it evokes.

_childDocuments_.review: An incredibly worthy sequel and a great game in its own right.I consider the original Psychonauts to be one of my very favorite games of all time, and this is pretty much a perfect way to continue the series. It's a thorough and imaginative expansion of the original world, mechanics, and cast. All the new powers have interesting uses in and out of combat with plenty of old favorites returning as well. The mental worlds are quite varied with some very unexpected theming and clever ideas, while still working in callbacks to the original (my personal top 3 being ). The new and returning cast of characters is quite good, with Forsythe, Lizzie, Adam, Frazie, and Gisu being particular favorites of mine. Even the trademark Psychonauts attention to detail with things like character reactions and ability reactions is also back in full force, along with original's great sense of humor. The story was great and twisty as well, and while I called a few of the turns it was still fun to see them through and certain ones still caught me off-guard. And that whole ending sequence was phenomenal, just about the perfect way to tie everything together.

_childDocuments_.review: An improvement on the original in some ways, and a huge letdown in others. If you want more Psychonauts, this is for you, but if you just find the premise and story interesting, the first game is a better bet.While this sequel does make the platforming less frustrating, its combat is almost unplayable, and large parts of the game clearly haven't been tested. The side characters also aren't quite as interesting as they were in the first game, and you'll find nothing here as iconic as the milkman conspiracy or lungfish city.On the other hand, if you've been waiting a decade plus for a Psychonauts sequel, you largely won't be disappointed (as long as you can make it through the train wreck that is the first level). However, coming from that end, you'll also be utterly lost if you happen to be one of the vast majority of people who doesn't own a VR headset and was unable to play the (story-essential) Rhombus of Ruin spinoff.Ultimately, this review is marked as negative simply because I think the people who would enjoy this game won't be deterred by anything I have to say, and those who might not enjoy it should know up front what they're getting into.EDIT: It turns out you can (and, frankly, should) essentially turn combat off in the accessibility options--both by making yourself do extra damage and/or by turning yourself invincible. This definitely makes the game easier to recommend, but still leaves me recommending the first game over this one, as while its combat could be frustrating, I never felt the need to do anything as drastic as disable it completely.

Having watched Rhombus of Ruin on YouTube, due to not having a VR Headset, I do not believe that anything happened to Raz to cause this change in personality.I also feel that the studio was trying to be  careful with trying to make sure that the mental crises that Raz encountered weren't offending. Psychonauts 2 didn't feel as free and whimsical as the first game did, but I would much rather have this Psychonauts 2 than nothing at all.All in all, 34+ hours very well spent. I don't know that I would recommend anyone else spend $60 on this title, but at the same time, buying at full price may lead to Double Fine working on more of their historically fantastic games.

_childDocuments_.review: One bit of advice: I started with a keyboard and mouse because that's always my default control scheme and to be clear it's fine that way, but it seems this is best experienced with a controller.I can't believe it's been 5 years since I backed this on Fig, and over 15 years since the original.I've got dozens of development updates that I haven't read, and I've avoided the trailers and reviews because I didn't want any spoilers - I wanted to go into the sequel to one of my all-time favorite games with fresh eyes.It has absolutely been worth the wait!  It's exactly what you'd want in a sequel - the same heart as the first game, but more and, frankly, better.  The story respects and expands upon the groundwork laid in the first game, while delivering a depth and complexity that was frankly surprising given the generally whimsical tone of the game.
