_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely incredible sequel ripe with highly memorable artistic worlds, characters teeming with personalities, and one of a kind designs and creativity. This game's wordplay, symbolism, and thematics are some of the best and most unique I've seen in any game to date - even when compared to its predecessor. There are non-euclidean environments and weird concepts that expand in bizarre and allegorical ways as you progress, always hiding collectibles and lore to those with more keen eyes. This game - in my opinion - is and has been heavily slept on by the gaming community. In some ironic way, this game was memory holed and I'm genuinely surprised that it hasn't generated memes or content publicly stirred from this series in any mainstream way. I know people who loved the original, and didn't even know a sequel existed.Jack Black makes a VA return, along with all of the wonderful voices from the original series. Tim Schafer hit a grand slam with this one, and I hope they continue on with this project, and/or Brutal Legend. While the combat isn't the most interesting, and there are areas I wished they would have expanded upon further (more pin options, more equip-able slots for loadouts, Easter eggs impacting gameplay, etc.), the set-pieces and bosses more than make up for it. Definitely give this game a chance if you love scavenger platformers with quirky gameplay mechanics. It's short and sweet, and really highlights what a talented non-artistically bankrupt studio can commit to reality when supported and fostered.

_childDocuments_.review: Having enjoyed playing through the first Psychonauts game this year (2022) my expectations for the long awaited sequel were quite high. I can say with confidence that Psychonauts 2 absolutely delivers as a sequel to its predecessor and even exceeds it in many ways.Quality-of-life experience is improved across the board and the production value is comparable to many 3d animated films. I also found myself more attached to the cast than the original game and the environments are full of various, eccentric NPCs that establish a more immersive environment than ever before.Psychonauts 2 isn't perfect: combat can become a juggling act with PSI-powers, Raz's fellow interns become less involved and underdeveloped despite their importance during the game's climax, and the final portion of the game is underwhelming despite how brilliant everything leading up to it is. Some may also find disappointment with the more platforming-focused level design compared to the more experimental level mechanics of the first game.Regardless, I consider Psychonauts 2 a must play and the best 3D platformer I have played since Super Mario Galaxy.

_childDocuments_.review: DoubleFine doesn't disappoint. They are truly masters at creating living, breathing characters and unique settings that totally immerse you into the game. Don't let the simplistic/childish design aesthetic fool you, it is in direct contrast to the darker aspects of human psyche that the game deals with such as loneliness, abandonment, regret, shame, and guilt. The gameplay is possibly the weakest element in that it is fairly rudimentary for an action-platformer, Towards the end it clearly takes a backseat to the narrative experience. _childDocuments_.review: After waiting since the naughts for a sequel I gotta say that Psichonauts 2 left me disappointed.Double Fine promise twice as many levels as the first one, It doesn't, in fact it's the same number of mental worlds.Most of the levels feel very samey and the central gimmicks for most of the others are not that fun, the bowling level comes to mind.The over-world is larger but that is about all I can say about it.There was also a lot of implied relationship building in the dialogue with the fellow kids that clearly never happened, leading me to believe some of them were supposed to have their own levels. I'm paraphrasing one kid who said something like "remember what I thought you about [etc]" which they most certainly didn't do. Those kids could have certainly benefited from better character development and having more redeeming qualities because as it is they were just brats the whole game through.This has unfortunately been a pattern with Double Fine since Brütal Legend, promising a lot and only delivering half the product.The game-play runs smoother than the previous game, unfortunately the charm didn't carry over. Apart from the dentist and the psychedelic levels, nothing really stands out.If you compare it to Alice: Madness Returns from the interim, you'll see that Psychonauts 2 falls short creatively.The supporting characters from the previous game were relegated to mostly background decorations and the competence and helpfulness they showed previously has been greatly diminished as well.Honestly the Rhombus of Ruin had a lot more going on even though it was a short experience.Even though I played Psychonauts 2 when it first came out, I wasn't sure how I felt about it but remembering my love for the first one compelled me to get this criticism off my chest.Psychonauts 2 falls shot in the charm department compared to the previous title and while the game-play is smoother, the creativity is lacking. If you're really jonesing for another Psychonauts experience, Alice: Madness Returns will better serve you.

_childDocuments_.review: I remember when the original Psychonauts first released, and I learned about it on an old TV show called X-Play. Anyone remember that show? _childDocuments_.review: tl;dr - Buy Psychonauts 2 with money.Just as excellent as the first game for different reasons. Where it lacks the same sharp and relentless sense of humor from long ago, it makes up for it in well-explored poignancy of its characters. Perhaps at the risk of losing some memorability or opportunity for creative puzzle-solving, the gameplay is much more streamlined and will never leave you looking up guides--a lack of obtuseness I welcome after a certain amount of frustration with lack of clarity in the predecessor. And dear god, the presentation. The soundtrack is a standout of the experience (the way the orchestra swells during the late-game combat theme, WEW.) Higher fidelity models and textures are one thing for enhancing the visual style, but the animation is what really gets me--fundamentally, Raz doesn't look too different when standing still, but in motion the kid's got a better energy about him than ever before. Some character designs look more in line with the likes of Broken Age this time around, and I welcome that eclecticism. It shows how much the studio has learned and grown over the years. They did a double fine job on Psychonauts, yet again.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: Great writing, creative levels, and some of the absolutely worst 3D platforming I've ever encountered.Most of it is OK to mediocre, but occasionally the levels feature very difficult to execute jumps. It's absolutely clear what you have to do, there's no puzzle, it's just a matter of the jump being so unforgiving that you have to time several key presses exactly right, neither too fast nor too slow, or you fail. The jump is right on the edge of what's possible, so if you're off by of fraction of a second, you fall.Which is bad enough, but it's pretty common for making a mistake on a later jump to drop you back earlier in the level, so you have to go through attempting the same <expletive> jump again. And again.After a while I just reached a point with one of these jumps where I didn't want to play anymore, and couldn't see myself ever trying it again. The reward of getting to see new funky levels just wasn't worth the aggravation of the actual gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: My current time with the game (17.4 hours) isn't entirely accurate as I've left it open once or twice and spent a LONG time exploring all the stages because I like the art so much.Basically I waited until I was at least 4-5 stages in before deciding to recommend the game. I've been waiting for this a long, long time and have avoided all media about it. I was both excited and worried because how it was a crowdfunded game to begin with and how, while I love Double Fine's work, traditionally they struggle with compelling and polished gameplay even with a normal budget.I'm glad to say it looks like my worries were unfounded. This is easily Double Fine's most polished game to date. It's super fun to control Raz, and you don't lose any of your abilities from the last game, you just get more and upgrade the old ones, all of which feel much better to use.Everything's just as good as ever and in many cases better than ever. Voice acting, animation quality, music, stage design (good lord there are some amazing transitions/special effects) and all that good stuff.I'm not done with the game so I don't want to write a comprehensive review or anything, but I think if you enjoyed the first game, this game should feel even better. Some of the new levels are instant classics, and small things like little 2D representations of Raz as he's viewed by other characters/enemies/critters (with updates depending on how far the story is of course) have not been forgotten at all.I'd say the thing that took me the longest to get used to was a few of the new characters, namely the other kids. Now that I've played for a while and had more time with each of them, they've grown on me, but my initial complaint was that they were introduced too quickly and that they have "normal" voices. Rather, in a game full of cartoon character voices, it's weird when someone sounds normal. That said, they're not the only "normal" sounding characters but there's also still a ton of cartoony voices, so at this point it just makes the world feel more varied and I don't mind anymore.At this point in time, I highly recommend the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: After hearing that the game is short, I waited for a sale to pick it up. _childDocuments_.review: The headlines are:-If you are a fan of the series, this game is good but it focuses more on linear set pieces and less on crazy amounts of detail.-If you are new to the series, don't start with this one. It does give you a summary of the story so far so it could be played first but there is no reason to play this one first when the first game is on steam dirt cheap and is just as playable. If you don't like that one you wouldn't have liked this one either most likely.In more detail, the gameplay is fine although you feel less powerful than before, especially in terms of mobility. You can still only equip 4 psychic abilities at once which just seems dumb at this point when they could do something with button combinations instead.The story is much more involved and takes some odd turns, particularly towards the end where the story pretty much takes over everything else.With the exception of the vaults which provide interesting context, collectables are mostly not really worth getting as all they allow is level ups to get upgrades that don't matter much anyway and extra health which you probably won't need most of the time, Personal opinion, it's not as good as it could be with just a bit more fleshing out to it's characters but it's also nowhere near as bad as it could have been being brought back after such a long time. It's worth playing although the launch price seems a bit much since I got 27 hours out of it and that was including a good few wasted hours 100% completing it for really very little payoff.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR Overall I believe the rose tinted goggles many of the fans of the cult classic are wearing means that I won't influence those who've spent hundreds of dollars on the crowd funding campaign. They need the game to be what they invested into. For everyone else, get the game on at least a 70% sale if you feel you want to play it, or watch someone else play through and save your money for a game worth your time. Review:Personally, I think that there is nothing in this game that will draw people back to replay it after beating it, that the poor writing/pacing are only appealing to fans who already beat the first game and are able/willing to fill in the gaps themselves, and that the game is either blitzed through just to beat it and not worth your money, or you'll play trying for 100 percent completion, you'll reach a point of boredom and then rush to beat it or stop playing. The attempt at continuation after the VR only sequel to 1 is recapped in game with a regression in most of the character's personalities away from being fleshed out to becoming rather bland and plain. The story as other reviews will note is worthwhile only if you've been invested in the series, which is there is a mole in the psychic spy agency, and the only one who can save the day is the mentor character and his friends. Notice I didn't say main character there, your role in this story is to fix bolster everyone else, be subtly considered the mole, and be the hypocrite who is told not to try to “fix people”, who then proceeds to fix people to help magically save the day. The game itself is combat focused and the humor is at best a sad chuckle at random one liners that are as forgettable as what you had for dinner a week ago. Don't expect this game to pander to anyone not already a fan. The sad reality is that if you remove the collectibles (which are only needed if you like seeing the numbers go up and have the tacked on “upgrades” to your moves), you have no reason to appreciate the interesting and pretty visuals, and will get just far enough into the game to get bored and be unable to get a refund. I will say after reading many of the positive reviews, that the “focus on the healing of mental damage” is a theme in this game, literally to a cliché degree that makes Saturday morning cartoons feel like adult themed content. It does tickle a nostalgia bone for many people, and it does tackle adult problems in an almost naive and joyful happy ending redemption way. Many of the “plot twists” aren't really unexpected, though some of the clues are really obvious when doing one of the side conversations that aren't needed to advance the game. As far as aspects that don't really fit in anywhere else. There are only 3 or 4 side quests in the whole game. The music is orchestral, and can either be amazing or just boring depending on how you feel about that type of thing. Anita Sarkeesian was a consultant on the game, and while no politics are preached, sudden moments like a gay wedding scene or the fact that many diverse strong female characters are being more capable or show affection through punching all seem like ways to try to subtlety point out “Hey, we're not going to cram our beliefs down your throat, but this is what we think, it's normal to have it this way now”. There are game breaking bugs still, there are many places that you can get the main character where he shouldn't be, some people have lost progress, and this game appears to be console focused. There are options to become invincible, do extra damage, and basically skip combat. There is a point of no return for the first 3 areas that you can't go back until after beating the game. There is a reference to Gir from Invader Zim.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great platformer. This was one of the games I was most hyped for this year. I thoroughly enjoyed it. The game is quite trippy. I am not someone that cares about graphics, but this game looks exceptionally good. I don't usually buy games full price, but this game deserves it.I only have a few nitpicks/complaints. -The new "campers" (interns) are all awful. Sam is the only one with any kind of likable character. The rest just treat you like crap for 0 reason and then there is no character development or interaction with the rest of them like at all. It almost makes me think that they had planned to expand on them but didn't have the time. They matter almost nothing to the story. But then they swoop in to take credit. It just made me hate them more.-It's also a bit annoying that they nerfed the balloon glide. (At least I think they did. I feel like I remember it lasting until you touched ground in the original.)-The music seemed all over the place. Some of the music was fitting, but so much of it was unmemorable. To be fair, there wasn't much memorable music in the original, but it still felt like there was more than here.-95% of the voice acting is decent-good. But there was one character and one section of the game where the voice direction was so off. I was so jarred by it because the rest of the game was good.

_childDocuments_.review: The first Psychonauts is a very important piece in my mind and in my heart. 16 years have passed, and we REALLY got this, the Psychonauts 2! To be honest, I was very sceptical... how the time will mess up the whole thing... will the game give me those goosebumps... will it really be THAT Psychonauts? And the answer is - after playing it through - absolutely!The music is fantastic, every track was a pleasure to my ears. I think this is the first game in a long time, that I played with headphones from the beginning to the end. The visuals amazing. I mean what the heck?! I started each new place with a 10 minute look-around and my jaw dropped. The story is so deep, it could contain the whole Mt. Everest. 100 times! While playing it, I really felt joy, sadness, excitement. I felt impressed that there are people, who actually made it into a real thing.So I just want to thank this piece of a heaven, it goes next to the first Psychonauts in my heart. Hope to see maybe a 3rd part, see you in 16 years, take care.

_childDocuments_.review: Aside from clear pacing issues in the endgame, Psychonauts 2 does everything right. With refreshingly diverse sets of levels, characters, themes, ideas, and even art style, Psychonauts 2 goes above and beyond in the presentation of all of them. It's unfortunate that it ends on a somewhat unsatisfying note, with strange plot twists and abrupt cutscenes. However, it's important to remember that the journey there was utter bliss and unlike any other. I fully recommend giving it a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely phenomenal sequel to my previous favorite game I've played in 2021, everything great in the first game this game does even better. Combat is actually fun with me being indecisive on my main moveset in game, which usually means I'm enjoying everything I have. As soon as the game felt stale it introduced something's new that blew me away and kept me interested, with 4 enormous areas, I found myself exploring every area I could. With an amazing story, great characters, and near perfect visuals, this game kept me hooked from start to finish. The new point system and item shop streamlines everything, from improving and prefecting what you already know, to strengthen your new moves, and the new pins make exploration, combat, and even spendings much easier. Plus, 100%ing the game is even easier now with a postgame item.This game is even better than the first, with my only complaint being how you can't enter your Levitation Ball from midair. 11/10, would absolutely recommend again.

_childDocuments_.review: Psychonauts 2 is a deep, complex, emotional, and thought provoking game that DOESN'T sacrifice it's fun factor, nor "game-y-ness" to deliver it's message of empathy, self acceptance, and healing. It features some really creative level design. The humor isn't as crude or mean spirited as in the first game (which was a bummer), and though there is a lot of creativity in the art direction, and plenty of surreal visuals, it doesn't quite get as surreal as the first game either (nothing will top the Milk Man Conspiracy). I also don't like the interns nearly as much as I liked the campers from the first game. The game still gets REALLY dark at times, but it's more serious instead of played for laughs. Still I appreciate that they didn't sacrifice gameplay in favor of narrative, a trend all to common these days... The platforming is still a blast. There's still a lot of fun things to collect. The combat is improved over the first game. And like I keep mentioning, the level design is top notch.Definitely worth playing, even if the humor isn't quite as good as in the first.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: Psychonauts 2 doesn't quite have the freshness of the first game, and I also think the self-contained world of Whispering Rock Psychic Summer Camp works better than the Motherlobe, the Psychonauts HQ introduced in the sequel. Nonetheless, if Psychonauts 2 didn't quite bowl me over the way the first one did, it's still a more than welcome return to this world and its characters. I have some quibbles - one or two levels are less inspired than others and border on the incoherent, there's no utter standout like the Milkman levels in the first game, and the final confrontation and aftermath seem a bit rushed - but Psychonauts is still one of my favourite games of the year and absolutely a virtual world I want to hang out with. Double Fine has clearly put a lot of love in their game, and it's impossible not to feel this love when running around as Raz Aquato once again. And while the story comes to a proper end, I do hope that this isn't the last we've seen of the Psychonauts universe.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow. The first Psychonauts is a pretty formative game for me. I first played it on release more than 15 years ago as I was exited by a console platformer from the people that made Full Throttle, one of my favorite classic Point and Clicks. Psychonauts stuck with me because it was the one of the early times that a console game showed heart and humor above anything that had come before. Then Brutal Legend and a host of Double Fine productions came out over the years and were just that... fine. By the time Psychonauts 2 landed and was on my radar, I had zero faith that Double Fine had it in them to attempt to reignite a classic. Well they did it, and they did it well. I'm genuinely gobsmacked. The core of Psychonauts is still there. DF did not attempt to break the wheel and reinvent it at all. They made a genuine sequel that builds on the original in every way possible. Gameplay, innovation, creativity, character, and story. All there and better than ever. Rarely has a fun family platformer captured the same spirit, humor, and tenderness as some of the best Dreamworks/Pixar films out there, but Double Fine did it with this sequel. My only complaint is that P2 nearly felt too long, but humor and heart for miles isn't a bad thing. 10/10, well done.

Speaking of fighting, they throw this smorgasbord of abilities at you, and none of them really have much depth or combo well together in a satisfying way. The balloon is the shortest lasting BotW glider thing of all time.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is SO GOOD! So many quirks, the characters are so expressive, the story is PERSONAL!Somehow Psychonaughts manages to be funny and lighthearted while dealing with mental problems in a very respectful way. Love Raz, he's a lil' man with a big plan. Despite this game releasing when it did, I really felt like I was back to playing a game from the 2000s / early 2010s so it was incredibly nostalgic for me.Can't believe I'm saying this, but Psychonauts was able to really make me feel for the characters. For every tragic character's trauma revealed (especially Ford). _childDocuments_.review: I have been one of the biggest fanboys of Psychonauts ever since my mom got me the first game for the Xbox when I was a child. Even when they announced it was in development years ago I still was in disbelief, especially seeing how long the game was delayed.But here we are now, the wait has finally paid off. The game so far has shattered my expectations into a million beautiful pieces. It still holds the original spirit of the game but improves upon its predecessor in almost everyway possible. It shows that the extra time and money that they spent on this game was well worth it. The level of polish and detail is incredible. By no means could you compare it to the new Ratchet and Clank games in terms of graphic fidelity, but the art and design in Psychonauts 2 is a shining example of creativity and genius that is not seen very often in the cookie cutter game industry that we now have.You can notice the love and devotion that Tim Schaefer and the rest of the Team at Double Fine put into this world, and it really shows even a few hours in. I'm more than happy to support a game studio that supports their team. Here's hoping that more studios follow suite with a no crunch policy because I genuinely believe that having a mentally well team is the secret ingredient to success when all of your resources are tight.Thank you Double Fine, I think this game is something that a lot of us needed recently. _childDocuments_.review: ~ DIFFICULTY ~🔲 My 90 year old grandma could play it🔲 Easy✅ Normal🔲 Hard🔲 Dark Souls~ GRAPHICS ~🔲 MS Paint🔲 Bad🔲 Meh🔲 Graphics dont matter in this game✅ Good🔲 Beautiful~ MUSIC ~🔲 Bad🔲 Not special✅ Good🔲 Eargasm~ STORY ~🔲 This game has no story🔲 Like playing Temple Runners for the story🔲 It's there for the people who want it🔲 Well written✅ Epic story~ PRICE ~🔲 Free🔲 Underpriced🔲 Perfect Price✅ Could be cheaper🔲 Overpriced🔲 Complete waste of money~ REQUIREMENTS ~🔲 You can run it on a microwave✅ Average🔲 High end🔲 NASA computer~ LENGTH ~🔲 Very Short (0 - 3 hours)🔲 Short (3 - 15 hours)✅ Average (15-50 hours)🔲 Long (50-90 hours)🔲 Extremely long (90-110 hours)🔲 No ending~ FUN ~🔲 I'd rather watch paint dry🔲 Hard to enjoy🔲 Repetitive🔲 Actually pretty amusing✅ Ride of your life~ REPLAYABILITY~🔲 It's a one-time experience🔲 Only for achievements🔲 If you wait a few months/years✅ Definitely🔲 Infinitely replayable~ WORTH BUYING ~🔲 No✅ Wait for sale🔲 Yes----------------Psychonauts 2 is a long-awaited sequel to the cult classic Psychonauts, a 3D platformer that lets you explore the minds of various characters with psychic powers. The game follows Razputin Aquato, a 10-year-old aspiring psychic spy who joins the Psychonauts as an intern and gets involved in a conspiracy that threatens their existence.The game is a delight for fans of the original, as it brings back many familiar faces and locations, while also introducing new ones with their own quirks and secrets. The game's humor is witty and charming, with plenty of references and Easter eggs to spot. The game's story is also engaging and emotional, as it explores themes of family, identity, trauma and redemption.The gameplay is mostly similar to the first game, but with some improvements and additions. Raz can use his psychic abilities such as telekinesis, pyrokinesis, levitation and clairvoyance to navigate the levels and solve puzzles. He can also equip pins that modify his powers or give him cosmetic changes. The levels are varied and creative, each representing a different aspect of the character's psyche. Some levels are whimsical and colorful, such as a psychedelic music festival or a cooking show; others are dark and twisted, such as a hospital full of nightmares or a casino full of bad luck.Overall, Psychonauts 2 is an excellent game that lives up to its predecessor's legacy. It is a rare example of a sequel that improves on almost every aspect of the original without losing its charm or identity. It is also a game that celebrates diversity and empathy, as it shows us that everyone has their own struggles and dreams inside their heads. Psychonauts 2 is not only one of the best games of 2021; it is also one of the best games ever made.Psychonauts 2 gets an 8/10.For more reviews check my Steam profileHope you enjoyed my review, god bless you

The story picks up where the first game left off and offers a lot of closure to the story of Raz Aquato and Psychonauts as a whole. Sticking to the OG artstyle, but using UE4 was a well thought-out decision. Sadly, that same decisions had its downfalls. Like stuttering issues and occasional framedrops. _childDocuments_.review: Story spoiler-free review below!If you're coming straight from playing the first game, there will be a bit of adjustment to the controls you'll need to get used to, but I believe the changes make it overall a tighter platformer. If falling off of ledges makes you frustrated, you can turn off fall damage. If you feel the enemies are being absolutely relentless, you can turn on invincibility. I never ended up using these, but I can't say I wasn't ever tempted. It's nice that they're there for people who are struggling, or just want to chill out and enjoy everything else this game has to offer (which is a LOT). The game feels, for the most part, fair in its challenges though. Leveling up abilities is satisfying in how much stronger it makes you feel, and between that and buying pins you can really choose how you want to buff combat strategies for different enemies. Or just pet the animals and have rainbow trails on your punches. Whichever. It's a bit more linear within the levels compared to the first game, so collecting everything your first time through a mind is often impossible (many areas seal off when you enter the next one as you progress). That said, cleanup is way easier when you do get to reenter minds, since the areas within each brain are fairly self contained as a result. I think the impact this design decision has on the story each mind tells is worth it. My advice if you like to 100% collectibles? Play through each mind as you want the first time and enjoy the story beats fully without worrying about grabbing everything. Then come back to collect the rest. There is a post game too, so though there are some "point of no return"s (and the game will warn you!), you're never truly locked out from 100%ing the game. In fact, there are some overworld collectibles that you CAN'T get until the post-game (looking at you, doors with mailslots).The story and writing is again A++. Talk to every NPC at LEAST once - some of the most unexpected will have dialogue trees of absolutely hilarious content. The endgame twists and turns are surprising and satisfying, while feeling connected to everything that was set up earlier in the game. Many heartwarming and wholesome moments throughout, but some absolutely dark ones as well that ground the story and make it feel meaningful. I absolutely devoured this game. I'm sure I'll come back for seconds, once my memories fade a little, so I can discover it all over again.

_childDocuments_.review: The perfect sequel to the original! To make a new game, on new technology, and make it feel sooo much like the original in terms of controls, is mind-blowing to me. Now imagine making a game, but every "level", you throw out all your artwork, and make a complete new set? That's Psychonauts!  A lot of work went into this one, and it shows. All the different characters are well developed, and interesting, and piecing together all the different details of the main story, through the experiences of everyone involved is a lot of fun. And then there's all the "extracurricular" stuff you can do outside the missions, just like in the original. Pros:* More Psychonauts! A worthy successor. * Interesting story* Very creative, and interesting level designs. * Good atmosphere* More dynamic and interesting combat.* Plenty to explore, and secrets to find.* A whale called "Esmerelda"Cons:* Controls can be a bit frustrating sometimes: for instance, jump distance can be hard to judge at certain spots. * Lacks some more "puzzle"-like minds, where you go back and forth finding a solution. Most minds in 2 are fairly linear.To me, psychonauts 2 is a game about compassion, and I think we all could use a bit more of that right now.

_childDocuments_.review: In short: Psychonauts 2 is a fantastic example of what a modern platformer could be, with fantastic visuals and art, tons of charm and genuine humor, and lots of fun exploration to do. In long: This is the longest and dorkiest review I've made for a Steam game, and nobody will probably see this, but I have a lot of feelings and nostalgia associated with the original Psychonauts that its difficult not to express all of my thoughts about this sequel. While I have my misgivings, Psychonauts 2 is a worthy sequel, and I certainly wouldn't complain if someday we miraculously were gifted with the announcement of a  Psychonauts 3. Psychonauts 2 is a great, charming, sometimes surprisingly emotional journey, and one that I recommend to fans and newcomers alike. Final score: 4/5

_childDocuments_.review: Psychonauts was one of the first games I have ever played. It brings me so much joy to know that this underrated classic got a sequel, knowing that it might have never even gotten one. This game is what I think makes a perfect sequel. It carries a lot over from the original game like abilities, collectables, and the platforming. It also features newer abilities, and an enhanced combat system which I thought the first game really needed. It just feels so good to bash through newer enemies, and using a bit more thinking to which powers would come to use during combat. I love the level designs, and visual aesthetics all of them bring. Also, staying true to the games original surreal experience. It's also great to see a bunch of returning characters such as Raz, and all of the Psychonaut Agents from the previous game. Even expanding upon some of them and making more room for story telling. This games story does a good job carrying out the first games plot, and dives deep into the origins of the Psychonauts agency as a whole. A minor complaint being the protagonist Raz, not being as snarky, or smug which made his character in the first game. Though, it is very nice to see all of these characters set in a new environment, and we get to see more of them in action. It's amazing to get to experience this franchise again. I would definitely recommend this, and the first game to those who enjoy platformers. It's such an amazing experience to go through first hand, because of how unexpected the game can be.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is impressive, with a rich lore and a diverse cast of characters. However, in my experience, it tends to drag on at times. The narrative often detours into what feels like endless side quests, many of which involve fixing random characters' minds. These detours branch into numerous sub-quests, giving the impression that the game is stretching out the experience unnecessarily during the middle sections. This can make the gameplay feel tedious and repetitive, but it does regain momentum towards the end.From a technical standpoint, the game is well-crafted, with impressive graphics and strong art direction. While the combat system is somewhat basic, it fits the game's style and serves its purpose adequately.I might not be the primary target audience, as the game seems geared toward a younger demographic. However, I did appreciate its exploration of themes like psychology and mental health, which were handled thoughtfully.If the developers trimmed down some of the content in the middle of the game, focusing more on the main storyline, it would significantly enhance the overall experience and keep the player more engaged.For context, I love Grim Fandango.

_childDocuments_.review: A game that had a lot to live up to. The original Psychonauts was a fantastic game with a creative premise, interesting and funny characters, and great art direction. It was criminal it wasn't more on more people's radar. When a sequel was announced, I was very excited as well as a tiny bit apprehensive. After all, revisiting a project you did more that 15 years ago always runs the risk of missing what made the first game great by relying too much on nostalgia and playing it too safe. Thankfully, Psychonauts 2 avoids these pitfalls, and improved upon the original in every way. The main story is more streamlined into every level / brain seamlessly, the comedy feels better than the original and the themes hit harder. The old and new cast are great and a higher emotional and philosophical depth is achieved. The combat and platforming are a massive improvement. The visuals, sound and level + World design are technically and artistically brilliant. Two smaller things to add is that it's a breath of fresh air that the team making this game were not subjected to crunch times, and they knew when to delay the project to avoid it. And the LGBTQ+ representation was handled really well. Overall, it feels as if the second entry blows the original out of the park, and cannot recommend enough.

_childDocuments_.review: Psychonauts 2 is a masterpiece. Amazingly fun and inventive. Actually funny, even despite the usual Doublefine puns. Perfectly stable, even when playing in widescreen or when using 5.1 surround. The music really makes this game special, I don't think I've ever heard such a diverse and entertaining score. I still have the Grulovia song stuck in my head. The game feels like just the right length, and well paced. The one improvement it could easily make is having a harder difficulty setting - I figured one was unlockable at the end, like a new game + mode, but there wasn't any. On the good side, the post-game world is very well thought out and there are plenty of surprises to discover even after finishing the story. Excellent game!

_childDocuments_.review: Psychonauts 2 blows me away. Released on August 25th, the game's garnered some pretty good reviews overall. Be it for the great visuals, creative level design, and brilliant writing, Psychonauts 2 is the embodiment of a sequel done right. After 16 years and a VR spinoff, it's pretty surprising to see a game turn out to be this grand. And for me, personally? It's very well done. I played the first game in 2018, being some guy in their mid-teens with a love for 3D platformers, be it for the nostalgia towards Ratchet & Clank, Sonic, and Crash. And where it impressed me, I could tell there were a few things rough around the edges. Does Psychonauts 2 fix these things? Absolutely. Aside from a few things we'll get into later, I find this to be a blast.

_childDocuments_.review: A quick, spoiler-free review... Level Design: Brilliant. The platforming and puzzles are fun and challenging. Psychology is creatively integrated into level design. Graphics: Gorgeous. They preserved the art style of the first game and polished it for modern systems. Music: As good as the first game. In fact, they even reused some pieces from the first game. Voice Acting: They got ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Jack Black. Dialogue: Witty.  Characters: Colorful, both literally and figuratively. Plot: Messy, anti-climactic, and disappointing. Had some good moments, but when the credits rolled, I felt unsatisfied. Length: I finished it in about 20 hours. 100% will take a little longer. Audience: Appropriate for kids, but intelligent enough for adults. Kind of like a Pixar movie. Portrayal of Mental Health Issues: Accurate, respectful, and creative. Controls: Use a controller, the keyboard controls are ♥♥♥♥. Bugs: I haven't found any. Do I recommend it: Yes. Should you play the first game: If you want to get all the jokes. Also, the first game is a masterpiece and you should play it anyway. Value: Just buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: Very few games really stand the test of time and most are forgettable. This will stand up for another 20 years and you can quote me on this. Really tight controls and very few glitches. High quality control and memorable story. This game will make you laugh and cry. It's my top contender for game of the year next to It Takes Two. I am so glad that this game made a come back. It started as kickstarter and Microsoft added funding when they purchased the studio. This allowed them to bring back cut content and I am really excited for what they do in the future. I really hope Michaelsoft will allow them to create more amazing games like this. I don't want a sequel right away because this feels like such an amazing and well written game that knew where it was going. Don't force out another game unless you have another amazing story to follow this up. Because many movies or games devs who try to make sequels to older properties fail because they don't understand characters or continuity. They understand all that has happened before and creates around it so seamlessly. Even the vr games is included with the story and what is amazing is you really don't need to play those older games to enjoy this one. It will add little references to older games, but isn't necessary which adds to it's amazing story telling. This is must play for anyone who like platformers, humor games, or just great stories. It reminds me of no more heroes 3 because of all it's different art styles and designs choices for levels. So much love was put into this game and even if you don't have much money wait for a game pass deal with 1 dollar for 3 months. Check this game out and enjoy something that will stick with you. 10 out 10 must play keep this Overwhelmingly positive review because you deserve it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game hampered by poor controls.The control scheme operating on an XBox controller is really, really bad. When you move the stick to move Razputin, he rotates to the position that makes sense according to where you moved your stick. This means in tight situations, you'll find yourself constantly rolling off objects or platforms you want to stay on which is really annoying. I'd love to have more action oriented controls, so if I'm facing forward but move the stick left, snap Razputin to the left immediately rather than make him rotate. Sure, it's not realistic, but neither is the game, so this control feature would be just fine.Since I switched to KB+M, the difficulty in controlling Rasputin decreased immensely and I'm way happier with the game. But there is one problem though...The M button is hardcoded to bring up the menu. There is no way to re-map this button to something else. It's not in the control settings. Hey... could you let me re-map the menu button? That'd be great. Thanks!

_childDocuments_.review: A sequel that takes its cult classic predecessor and improves on its best qualities. Hasn't fully escaped some of the first game's problems, but does alleviate them to a degree. A game you can easily sink 20+ hours into, especially if you're a completionist. If you liked , chances are you will love .  is an adventure-platforming game, and the long-awaited sequel to the cult classic . If you haven't played the first game yet, I highly recommend stepping back and picking that up before you jump into this (though you can get away with not playing the VR-exclusive ). If you have played it, though, then you mostly know what to expect: a mix of platforming and exploration, tons of collectibles, wacky characters, psychedelic levels, a story of secret agents that's full of twists and turns, and a whole lot of imagination throughout. All of these were staples of the original game, and each one returns with at least some improvement in the sequel:I managed to sink over 20 hours into this game, and I definitely feel that it was time and money well spent. Searching every nook and cranny for 100% completion made things start to drag at times, but playing through the main story and just grabbing whatever collectibles caught my eye along the way was a satisfying gameplay loop that never stopped being fun.  I'll admit that I was very skeptical of this game before it launched due to Double Fine's more recent track record with games, especially crowdfunded games that undergo years-long delays. That said, they managed to live up to the hype and make the long wait worthwhile, and I hope that this game is just the start of an upward trend for Double Fine and their future projects.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the sequel I waited over a decade for. The first game was one of my favorite platformers when I found it, and when I had heard there was a sequel coming, I was READY. Now, when I had heard this game was coming, all I wanted was a follow-up to the cliffhanger from 1 (and Rhombus, after that came out). It could've played the same, and I would've been fine. HOWEVER, not only did the story surpass my expectations of what they could build off of from the world the first game created, the gameplay received so many major improvements. Each power was improved, and could be leveled up after unlocking. New features left and right, each of them incredibly useful and creative. Mental cobwebs were replaced with collectibles that were much more fun. And the devs are always listening to feedback, and that meant so much to see. Given the game's themes and the target demographic, it deserves that accessibility and attention to details and playerbase. This game blew me away, and while it will never replace the original, it certainly lived up to it.

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot praise Psychonauts 2 enough- it's been so incredibly long since I played the first game, but PN2 has been able to suck me in completely. Every single part of this game is just oozing with personality and humor and emotion, including the incredibly expressive character facial/body animations, the extremely inventive and unique levels that are chock-filled with details reflecting the characters' minds, and the well paced and very personal stories being told and interwoven with each other.The only thing I can complain about is that some movements are finicky- e.g. jumping when pressed right up against terrain objects that aren't perfectly vertical (because the environment is so stylized) can fail, and sometimes jumping while climbing depends too much on the camera being mostly straight behind your character. Beyond that, this is simply a masterpiece.

_childDocuments_.review: Psychonauts 2 was an amazing experience to play through. It's a perfect successor to the original that captures everything that I loved about that game and build upon it.  I just finished the game to 100% today, taking me around 34 hours to do.But every hour of that was pure enjoyment. The world is beautifully weird and wonderful. Character designs and personality are unique and individual. And the story was written exceptionally well to boot!The mixture of platforming and psychic abilities is a lot of fun to play with. For me, if you can make getting from point A to B entertaining, you've done a good job. As a result I didn't feel in a rush to finish this game. I wanted to explore everything the developers had taken time to build into the experience. It's a pure joy to bounce from area to area on my levitation ball while psi-blasting enemies and trashcans away, and collecting sweet psitanium ore as I go.The characters are really unique and special. You can see the love crafted into this game when they've written distinct and purposeful dialogue for each character. I love exhausting all dialogue with each character to hear everything they have to say. Especially in the post-game, where characters will tell you what they're going to get up to next. I love this so much! It makes them more than just NPCs. Likewise, each environment has had so much time invested into it. If you visit a person's mind it reflects them, their fears, and backstory. This makes them feel so human and real. Double Fine Studios are great at creating engaging personalities.This game combines complex psychological themes into interesting game play elements in creative ways. Literally fighting doubts, anxieties, and panic attacks is so cool a concept! If you haven't played this, I highly recommend you to. In an era of triple-a game studios pumping garbage into our libraries, this is an absolute gem!

_childDocuments_.review: I was very skeptical going in. The goofy graphics, the dated combat, the floaty platforming. They all looked like deal-breakers to me. Yet, I heard so many critics singing from a rooftop: "The level design and artistry of this game are unique, lovely, exceptional." It pulled at my interest just enough to get me to buy the game. And you probably saw it coming: I'm extremely glad I did. I haven't quite finished it yet, but I feel safe singing Psychonauts' praises as follows:This platformer is more about exploring and enjoying a piece of art than it is about game mechanics or snappy controls. If you are at all interested in games as a form of (artistic) expression and story delivery, this game is for you. The story is thoroughly compelling: up there with the best in gaming and refreshingly unique in its themes and subject matter. The artistic execution and creativity of the Psycho-premise is great. But the way that level design is leveraged to execute that same artistic premise is *second-to-none*. Best ever I've seen in a game. I now understand the GOTY nominations.Is the *game* the best ever? No! The combat? Passable. It's like Fable games back in the day. RPG elements? Bulk-standard: little bit of respeccable customisation and some perk points. Platforming? Fun, but nothing spectacular - though its worth mentioning that the floatiness isn't bothersome. Remember the difference in snappiness between Gamecube Smash Bros. versus the later ones? Psychonauts' platforming is like those later, floaty Smash Bros, where the snappy platfomer would be like Ori or Mario. Fortunately, the slowed down pace is matched by the pace of the obstacles, so it doesn't bother you at all while you're playing. And if anything, its actually a sort of boon: it gives you more time to appreciate the environments. The same can be said of the Ubisoft-esque collectible scavenger hunts: I don't give a sh** about collecting cards and markers and blah blah blah... but that busy work is fine if its just a byproduct of exploring these excellent levels. I think the developers also understood this, because the collecta-thon is pretty easy to complete. It's just a way to get you to look around. At the end of the game, this game does 1 thing great (story) and 1 thing exceptionally (artistic level-design), and rests those on a foundation of unobtrusively adequate gameplay mechanics.To wrap this up, it bears repeating: This game is a beautiful piece of art you play a game inside of. I highly recommend spending your time enjoying it.

_childDocuments_.review: The most important thing to note here is that Psychonauts 2 tones down the edgy, early 2000s cartoon feel of the first game in favor of a lore-heavy drama about mental health. The interns are also some of the most underdeveloped and downright unlikable characters I've seen in recent years and I constantly wanted them to leave. However, it definitely tops the original regarding visuals and playability. The mental worlds are beautiful and just as imaginative as ever. There's a stronger emphasis on platforming and combat, which are both simple to pick up and surprisingly complex. The glaring gameplay flaws of the first game have also been stamped out -- looking at you, Cobweb Duster. It's a thoroughly enjoyable game overall, but certainly not worth the $60 price tag. Since the writing was always Psychonauts' strongest aspect, I would recommend the first game if you haven't played it. Psychonauts 2 is still a very solid package overall for Psychonauts fans, but I'm less inclined to suggest playing this instead of the original.

_childDocuments_.review: Like it's predecessor, Psychonauts 2 is a great throwback to the platformer genre.The humor, animation, and character design is absurd and zany, and it works perfectly. Everything about the game is just a little off kilter in the right ways. The hub world is expansive and features lots of areas to solve, and each of the levels (which similar to the first game, involves solving the psychological issues of various characters by literally hopping into their brain) is uniquely styled and thematic to the mind of each character you delve into.Like most platformers, in addition to just figuring out how to make their way through each level, there's plenty of interesting combat, puzzle elements, and collectibles. In addition to the Figments which return from the first game, there's a lot more collectibles that work more towards improving Raz's abilities. Speaking of which, Clairvoyance, Levitation, Psi-Blast, Pyrokinesis, and Telekinesis return from the first game,  but now in the place of Invisibility, Confusion, and Shield, we now have Mental Connection, which allows you zap yourself from mental node to mental node through the air to reach areas you otherwise couldn't jump to, and also to pull enemies toward you for an extra punch. And then there's Time Bubble, which creates a bubble of bullet-time slowing down faster enemies allowing you to attack them while they are slowed and can't fight back easily.  And lastly there's Mental Projection, one of my favorites, which creates a little 2D version of yourself which distracts enemies and slips through hard to reach places, and is voiced by Rosearik Rikki Simmons, who also did the voice of Invader Zim's GIR alongside Raz's VA who did Zim, which was a combination I was surprised and overjoyed to hear.All of those abilities can also be upgraded with enhancements using skill points RPG-style. There are a few other trinkets you can acquire along the way, along with pins that you can swap in and out for other smaller abilities and bonuses that are useful in different situations.The story itself continues from the first game (and the VR game, Rhombus of Ruin) pretty much immediately after, so Raz is still much the same 10 year old Psychonaut-in-training hoping to become a famous psychonaut like his heroes, the Psychic 6 (err... 7) which feature prominently in this story, tho I don't want to give too much spoilers, but it delves a little bit into Raz's backstory, as well as the history of the psychonauts.I did play Rhombus of Ruin part of the way through, though I never finished it, but its not at all necessary to enjoy this game, as this game gets you up to speed on what happened in the VR game pretty quickly (which wasn't all that much, basically you rescued Lili's Dad and brought him back to the psychonauts HQ.I will say though, I feel like it would be difficult to get too into this game if you haven't played the first one, storywise, since this is really just a continuation of that story, and while the game does summarize things in the beginning, the first game does a lot to setup the world and what the psychonauts are.I only have a few complaints with this game. Firstly while the graphics have improved since the first, and its cartoony aesthetic means that it won't necessarily be going for anything hyperrealistic, I found a lot of the textures seemed very low resolution and grainy, even on the highest settings.  It's using Unreal Engine 4 but I didn't see any evidence of tech like raytracing or more modern illumination and shading effects, so the game looks a bit dated for something that came out in 2021.While I still loved most of the levels in this game, a few were pretty dull and monotonous. They seemed larger than the first game, with more collectibles and things to find, but that resulted in even more backtracking and running around to try to find what I missed. Fortunately once you complete a level you can go back and find a fast travel system implemented, but there was still a bit more backtracking than I would have liked, since there's a lot of content you can't even reach until you unlock abilities only available much later in the game.I'm hoping if they do make another psychonauts game we see Raz's character aged up a bit, as one of the drawbacks of this one picking up precisely where the last games left off is that he's still just a 10 year old and there hasn't really been much character development other than his gaining new abilities and becoming a more skilled psychonaut.  It would definitely be cool to see a psychonaut game playing as a young adult Raz. Who knows if they'll ever make another though.That all being said, I enjoyed the game thoroughly, enough so that it's one of the few games I've nailed 100% of the achievements for, collected all the collectibles, and acquired all the items and abilities. And it didn't overstay its welcome after playing it for a casual 26 or so hours off and on. I imagine you could have gotten through the game a lot quicker than I did if you just focused on getting through the story and not so much 100ing each level.Overall, I certainly recommend this game to anyone who enjoyed the first! Though I do recommend playing the first game too before this one. It's fun, psychological, psychotic, and psychedelic.

_childDocuments_.review: When I heard my favorite childhood platformer is finally getting a sequel, I've  my dudes. The game was officially announced after a big crowdfunding effort. As a huge fan of the original, this review might be biased due to nostalgia. If you want to hear me out anyway though, get comfortable. 	The story picks up right after the original (except for the fact that the VR title “Psychonauts in the Rhombus of Ruin” explains the small, but pretty important gap between the two games). The Psychonauts try to find out who was really responsible for the incident at the Whispering Rock Psychic Summer Camp and the abduction of the head of the whole organization, Truman Zanotto. In the meantime, Raz finds out more about himself and his family, and delves into many interesting mentalscapes and their backstories. Although the game tries to recreate the atmosphere of the original to some extent, it mostly does new things. We still have mysterious campgrounds inhabited by mutated psychic animals to explore, but the campers have been replaced by a completely new cast of characters. That’s not necessarily a bad thing though, considering all new interns have pretty colorful personalities and we’re getting to know them fast. There are also some reoccurring characters such as Lili and Ford. The minds themselves are where the game truly shines. All of them are unique and amazing, resembling the character's mental state, and so, the turmoil within. Unlike the first game, this time Double Fine consulted actual psychologists to ensure the adequate portrayal of various mental problems in their product. The way it handles mental health is very interesting: problems are shown in a comedic, cartoonish manner, fitting in the game’s atmosphere and aesthetic, but still designed in such a way to give you an idea of what a person experiencing, for example, sensory overload or a panic attack feels like. I recommend watching “Psychology of Psychonauts” series by Gaming University for cool breakdowns of the individual levels of both games and issues they portray. I really enjoyed shining some light onto Ford’s backstory and other founders of the organization. Story ties up a lot of loose ends from the first game leaving us with a complete and satisfying journey. Although I'd love another sequel, I was actually surprised when Tim Schafer said that they aren’t currently working on the third game, instead of saying something along the lines “That’s all the story Raz could tell us and time to move on” or something. I guess there is hope. Platforming is even more fluid than in the original and it’s just a pleasure to jump and bounce around with Raz. His move set makes it really fun to move around. In terms of abilities they kept the best in, while getting rid of some less enjoyable ones replacing them with new stuff. What’s really cool is that every ability in addition to just being useful in exploration and moving around is also functional in combat. An exception from that is clairvoyance. It may be funny using it on some of the characters and puzzles, but in combat it’s only useful with one specific enemy. Speaking of combat, it’s a lot more dynamic and engaging now. Game encourages you to use everything you have at your disposal. Different powers are more effective on different enemies. The only drawback I see is the fact that you can equip a limited amount of your powers at once. Switching back and forth between abilities by a radial menu is annoying, especially when you’re playing on keyboard and could map everything if only given an option. Music is amazing, probably on par with the original, but again, I'm blinded by nostalgia. I’m going crazy when they play old tracks, but the new ones are incredible too. Personal favorites are probably “Maligula Unleashed!” and “Fight in the Library”. Generally good sound design. Graphically the game has a very unique aesthetic and design. The reflections, lightning and stuff look very good, but similarly to the first game it will probably look good years after anyway thanks to the characteristic art style.  Game has lots of accessibility options. Achievement-wise it’s pretty straightforward. You can do everything on the same save and nothing is missable. Pretty chill to do a 100%. 	My final thought is that it’s a perfect sequel. Ties up a story that has been incomplete for the past 16 years. Does improve gameplay and leaves you satisfied. It owes a lot to its predecessor, but is a great game in its own right. Again, it’s probably thanks to nostalgia, but it has been a long while since I was smiling every minute of playing a game, 10 hours into it. And it’s not only because of hilarious jokes, but also out of pure enjoyment. This was a real treat.

_childDocuments_.review: I rarely 100 percent games, but I felt a sense of reverence to psychonauts that I had to. It was a bit of a slog finding the LAST figment in each level(the last is always the hardest when you miss it), but it felt great to be back in a world I felt like I may never see again. Psychonauts inspired me, before life got in the way, to become a concept artist for games, and it influenced me in a number of ways, in empathy, in aesthetics, in exploring one's personality and dredging up and working through mental issues. Psychonauts 2 was perhaps better than 1. It more succinctly portrayed the journey that people with mental illness or at the very least trauma go through, and it did it in an equally if not more creative way than 1. And the gameplay segments all felt tighter, faster, and more varied than the original, which still holds up even. A bit of flash to the presentation sold scenes even stronger, and it fleshed out the world and most of the core characters to be miles deep. I do think some of the new kids couldve been improved, or more of the older ones couldve been brought back, but its adherence to the timeline is a blessing. it shows how much double fine cares about this, their baby. It's stronger than most other remakes/distant sequels/etc. I only dock it slightly as it didn't feel perfect. some weird performance and graphical issues, but these were rare. I'm excited that Microsoft money might make psychonauts 3 uber polished, and this already notched the bar up several times. It brought tears to my eye at the opening scene because of how important it is to me, and seeing it play well, look great and still feel like the original. I hope we get a psychonauts 3 in some form, but if it doesn't happen, 2 has thoroughly satisfied me.

_childDocuments_.review: I've never reviewed a game on Steam before, but Psychonauts 2 is the sort of experience so fantastic that I genuinely wish I could forget it all and play it for the first time. If you're a fan of the original game, rest assured that this sequel is likely everything you hoped for and then some. The levels here are insanely creative - all visually and thematically distinct from one another and delightful to explore. The controls in the first Psychonauts could be mildly janky at times, but that's been ironed out here and it's a lot of fun to move around. The story and characters have a surprising amount of depth and I was surprised at how emotionally invested I was in how things would turn out. If I had any minor nitpicks I'd say that while the enemy designs and weaknesses were conceptually neat, the basic combat encounters aren't quite as impressive as the rest of the game, and a lot of those encounters are easy enough to get through by moving around and spamming attacks, so I didn't make much general use of the pins you could buy. Even then I can't say this is something that really bothered me. Overall, the world of Psychonauts -from its humor and passing conversations to its art direction - is vibrant and memorable, and when the credits rolled I still didn't want to leave it behind.

_childDocuments_.review: oh my gosh this game is so goooodThe first Psychonauts is a pretty good game. It blends incredibly creative levels with superb writing, but it's held back by an annoying leveling system, bland combat, and some pretty meh animation. Psychonauts 2 took  a very bold approach called TAKING EVERYTHING THAT BROUGHT THE FIRST GAME DOWN AND MAKING IT ALL 100X BETTER. Everything is polished to the extreme. Movement is snappier, combat is deeper and feels much better thanks to the incredible animation. Like, this game has some of the best animations I've ever seen in a game, and that doesn't even take into account the cutscenes which could basically just be a Pixar movie. In fact, the entire game could be a modern animated movie. This is one of the most gorgeous games I've ever played. Every mind has its own distinct artstyle and all of them look incredible. From the cel-shaded psychedelic mind of the Sensorium to the Lady Luctopus Casino to Compton's Cookoff, every mind is brilliantly designed and really helps you differentiate between them. Each mind also features the amazing writing Psychonauts is known for, blending humor with thought-provoking depictions of anxiety, depression, multiple personality disorder, and alcoholism. This game takes the mental issues it depicts very seriously, and it makes the story of the second game much more personal and gut-wrenching than the first game and its very...loose depiction of mental disorders. The game does falter in one area, which is the bosses. I really didn't think many of them were that special compared to the first game, although at least none of them reversed my controls (I'm still angry at that tank from the first game). The leveling system is also very improved. No more do you need to reach a certain level to access the next mind. Instead, levels are used to upgrade the abilities you already have to allow for more power in combat or more movement. The abilities from the last game are also much better implemented. While most of them felt a bit janky in the first game, here, they're all wonderfully implemented and feel great to use. The new abilities are also excellently melded into the platforming and the combat, and they all felt like great additions to Raz's arsenal. Everything in this game is just amazing. This might just be my favorite platformer ever, and it definitely is one of my favorite games ever. If you ever want a fantastic platformer with incredible writing, wonderfully charming characters, and some of the most creative platforming ever, pick this game up. You won't regret it. I give Psychonauts 2 a Where did you get the milk/10

_childDocuments_.review: Psychonauts 2 is a game of the year contender. I remember playing the original game (Psychonauts) way back before the it even hit Steam, all the way back in 2005 when I bought it brand new, and I remember being heart broken that this great game probably wouldn't  have a future.  It's been a wild ride watching Double Fine emerge from the ashes of near collapse. While I didn't have the money at the time or the Psychonauts 2 funding campaign, it feels good to have funded things like the Double Fine Adventure. This game will probably be the highlight of my year.The story of the game picks right up from the VR game, Rhombus of Ruin, but it's not required to know the story as the game gives a good recap of the events of the first game. You could probably play this game without the first game too, but you lose a lot of neat references and emotional attachment. Sadly it's kind of hard to write more than the plot synopsis without spoiling the game. If you're on the fence though the writing is both thought provoking while also meeting the full range of chuckle, snort, and laugh out funny. The game does deal with a lot of family related issues as well as dealing with the results of political destabilization if that's something that could bother you. I'd also warn there might be some stuff close to body horror as well.The gameplay of Psychonauts 2 is a well refined version of Psychonauts 1 if a bit striped down at its core. Some powers are missing despite being important, canonical abilities from the first game (Shield, Invisibility, and Confusion). Each power is upgrade-able and thankfully there are plenty of points to get the powers improved enough there's no pressure if you feel like you messed up. Improving some of the new powers right away though is kind of a must, sadly. The new pin, side grade, system is interesting, but the extra effects aren't really used all the much. I'd had preferred a point system where cosmetic pins were zero points and didn't compete with combat abilities. I only cycled through about five of the pins at any given time. My biggest grievance with it is there are hardly any over-world use cases for a lot of pins. For example in the first game you'd use Invisibility to sneak past things. I saw there was a pin that gave you the ability to speed up things, thinking it would be used for a collectible I bought it, but it wasn't used for anything. I also couldn't find any use for the ability in combat either. Getting money can be a bit of a chore as there's no dowsing rod so you'll get betting money in 1-50 chunks. Wasting it on pins that do nothing can feel kind of bad.When it comes to collectibles I found them refreshingly less frustrating than some of them were in Psychonauts 1. There's no Millo's Race Track shenanigans this time around, but please stop putting figments on perfectly arked jumps. I got most of the collectibles on my first run through of levels. Though, there are still some super tiny figments (like coins in other games) that are hard to see physically, which is kind of annoying given how well done accessibility is done in other parts of the game this time around. I was kind of hoping for a figment finder or an in-game list where you found each collectible, even if you get it was super late game item. Hunting one figment of 200+ in some levels or a single card is literally the worst. My biggest frustration was missing rank 102 (100% completion) before the final boss because of a bug. In one of the levels that if you fail one of the challenges' time limits you're locked out of 100% that level until you beat the game. The last level seems to force you to come back post game to get the last few figments. You do get a post game to wander around, so no real Point-of-No-Return, but you won't get to use your infinite ammo and skills on anything important.All-in-all, this is still a great game. 100% completion in 25 hours. I'd actually love to see something like DLC for challenge rooms or something. Really I'd recommend the whole franchise to people. This is pinnacle game writing. I want to see more stuff like this in the medium.

_childDocuments_.review: Played the first game around 5 years ago for the first time after hearing a lot of good things about it from a close friend, it was one of the best 3D-platformers I have ever played. _childDocuments_.review: This is almost a perfect game. And by almost, I mean, that it's an amazing otherwise perfect piece, limited by game mechanics and technology, such as graphical glitches or bugs or controls.Though, my playthrough has been almost bug free, and they were minor too. I only saw one glitch on somebody's facial animation once. And I had a bug where my bacon bounced off the plate (and if you think that sounds weird, then you don't know what kind of game this is)Gamewise this is comparable to a Super Mario World style of gameplay, a map, collectables and combat, that is not very challenging. If I can do it, then everybody should be able to.Theres no difficulty settings, but for once, I think the game doesn't need one. There's no real penalty for dying. You simply retry. The respawn points are generous. This game isn't meant to be challenging or tricky. It's fun. And amazing. The controls feel a little clunky at first, but mostly only because your dodge does not cancel out of an attack animation. So you can (and will) get hit while you swing. A small change to let you cancel out of your attack swing, would make the combat much more fluent and make you feel more powerful. But it is doable for now. Especially since you are not limited to melee combat.What the Game, in as much as being a game, lacks for being a game, the rest of this masterpiece makes more than up for it. This is a piece of art. Character Design, Voice Acting, Level Design, Writing, Story, are some, if not THE best, I seen in a game yet. Usually I dispise it when a game takes gameplay away from me and locks me into a dialogue to push the story forward. But in this game, those dialogues were super enjoyable and some of the best parts of this game. Additionally theres so much environmental storytelling going on here, that you could not even fit it all into a full sized analysis.The implications, the themes, and the way the characters are treated, is stunning and wonderful. These characters are people with flaws and addictions, regrets and mood swings. And I think I love all of them, even the 5hitty ones. Theres no feminisation, no over sexualisation, no bias. And that's remarkable.This game won me over within hours. But it captured me for years. And I'm so glad I played it.

_childDocuments_.review: The unique aesthetics and approach to storytelling of Psychonauts have benefitted quite a bit from being brought into the modern sphere, and this sequel improves on its 2005 predecessor... a lot. The combat is more fluid than the original's, with a variety of psychic powers that can be used strategically against the uniquely themed enemies like "Doubts", "Panic Attacks" and "Judges", and these abilities also tie into the level design and platforming in all sorts of creative ways. The colorful modern graphics accentuate the unique character designs and trippy mental worlds. The puzzles are far more intuitive than the original's obtuse puzzle logic, while still being thought-provoking. And the constant stream of collectables (all of which tie into the different level themes) are woven into the upgrade system in a way that encourages the player to look for secrets and rare items hidden in these intricately designed worlds.There are some rough edges to the movement and animations from time to time, plus a few tedious sections of the game, like missions in the main hub world that involve lots of drawn-out dialogue options. Even with these occasional annoyances, though, I had a blast playing through Psychonauts 2. For anyone reading this who's new to the duology, the first one still holds up well today and I would recommend playing the original first - but this sequel outdoes the first game in a lot of ways, and this has got to be one of the most freakishly creative 3D platformers I've ever played. 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Psychonauts 2The game I waited 15 years to play.Retains the soul of the first game.Grinding on rails is still a pain, the lock on when jumping from rails to rails or when grabbing poles is a bit tighter.Levitate is one of the best powers since you move fast and there is a LOT of walking. As a bonus you can dodge most enemy attacks and use powers while levitating.A big problem for me personally is the game not giving players powers early on when needed. In fact, you cannot 100% the game on your first time through. After the ending credits the player is placed into free roam and there is a ton of new conversations, plus some areas change up a bit. Some powers are AFTER the point of no return.A bit heavy on the cutscenes, in certain levels you cannot go 10 minutes with a cutscene playing. This game is also really dialogue heavy if you go through all the options when talking. I believe it may have to do with Tim Schafer writing for adventure games.The first game overall felt better. Had more weirdness, creative stages, and a creepy factor in the second half. Also, Raz changes clothes often.This game is still a solid platformer and happy it kept much of what made the first special.20ish hours taking my time in the story. 24 hours to 100% the game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the sequel we have been waiting for.  It's polished, expanded upon the original story, they didn't do a typical opener where suddenly all of your powers are gone and you have to get them all again, they added new powers, the enemies that come after you are more varied and are deadly in various combinations while still being fair, they've reduced minor nuisances from the first game, they've utilized non-Euclidean geometry to make small spaces open up into new open areas (like the concept of the Tardis from Dr. Who)...This is a collectathon done right.  At first I was bummed to find out there weren't more worlds/content to explore once I realized my level was nearing 100, but then I realized that this doesn't need to be a collectathon odyssey that takes 60+ hours.  They prioritized the story and gameplay over unnecessary fluff to drag out the game length.The only criticisms so far are under utilization of some old characters like Sasha and Milla, and bugs ranging from minor and largely unnoticeable to game-breaking; fortunately much of the latter type of bugs have been few and fixed since launch.This game is worth full price and I'd gladly pay for any DLC if announced.  I know we waited 16 years for this but I'm already  looking forward to a hopeful third installment in the series.  (double fine pls)TL;DR: It's good; well worth your time/money
