_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game, I really did. I did a 100% run of Psychonauts just before playing this, intending to play them back to back. After playing this game for several hours (I was offline on my Deck for most of it, so it doesn't show on my profile), here is my conclusion....If you liked the first game, don't ruin it by playing this one. I don't see why this game is so well received. It's just a mostly typical 3D platformer, running on Unreal.The music uses motifs from the first game, which would normally be charming, except they're used for mostly unrelated things, which kills the effect.The story.....oh where do I start. It's basically a cookie cutter style checklist. Cringe moments with family members that don't have a good reason to be present? Check. Tough boss? Check. Very obvious plot twists? Check. School bullies? Check.Speaking of school.... The psychonauts are an elite group of secret agents. Why are they somehow a school now??When Raz is bullied or mistreated by anyone, he doesn't even react. He just acts like it's all normal and fine, and still hangs out with the bullies afterward.The game will also force you to do things that are clearly bad, and that you may not even want to do. Bad design, in my opinion.And finally.... The level design is pretty bad, too. Many of the levels are small but very tedious. They are also not very friendly to the Steam Deck, as some things are pretty hard to see. The level designers also have an odd obsession with the....grotesque.Overall, the game just feels uninspired and subcontracted. It's a harmless game to let a child play, but there's little value for anyone older. I would say the original game is superior in nearly every way. And that's saying a lot, because I had to fight to get it to work on my Deck. But it was a far more enjoyable experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't finished the game yet, but I can say with 100% certainty that this game improves on just about everything Psychonauts 1 had. The new psychic abilities you get are all incredibly fun to use, and what's even better is that every psychic ability has a use in battle, so you're not just spamming your fists and psi blasts everywhere. All the new enemies have a weakness to an ability you have, which makes combat all the more interesting. That was probably one of the best changes this game has made. The environments you explore are colorful and memorable, the characters are just as lovable, and the game is just overall fun to play and explore. The only thing I wish was different is the first new ability you get. _childDocuments_.review: Super good, honestly lives up to the original, which I did not expect. The artistry in this game is incredible and they cranked up the wacky level designs to 11. Took most of the best parts of the first game and made them even better, took most of the worst parts of the first game and fixed them. Solid story, solid characters, solid all around, and extremely creative and simply a joy to experience. I spent so much time playing this game with a stupid smile on my face.There are a few negatives, firstly: the game is extremely easy, and as far as I know there's no option for harder difficulties. I didn't ever die or even come close to dying during my entire playthrough, and I'm not particularly good at video games. The only exception was the final boss fight, which I did die once during, and I might just be salty but I think it's because the boss' reach is bugged to be too far during the second phase haha. The combat in general can feel good sometimes but be pretty janky feeling other times, but in either case it remains true that you don't exactly feel much of a threat from the enemies. Some boss fights were fun but some got old pretty quickly. The design for each one was super interesting though and the art team really knocked it out of the park.The puzzles aren't really puzzles, and any time there is actually a puzzle the characters just tell you how to solve it, so you don't really often have to think through things on your own. The game is just a bit of a walk in the park in this regard, it takes you through a lot of fun experiences, but you don't actually have to do much beyond press buttons in order to progress. The only time you have to figure things out on your own is for getting certain collectibles, which I have to admit are really fun to hunt for, at least in my opinion. The levels are so fun to be in and look around that it never gets boring to look through all the nooks and crannies.Sometimes things just take too long when you are at a critical point in the story. You're getting an exciting story beat but then forced to play through three separate 10 minute segments in the middle of it that maybe aren't super fun. Not a huge deal but it can interrupt the pacing at times and feels like they included a gameplay segment just to pad out the runtime of the game instead of adding something interesting or fun to the game.My only other main critique of the game is sometimes characters just get annoying. Not because they are written that way, but when Rasputin repeats for the 5th time in the last 30 seconds that he hears a collectible nearby, it's like, alright game I get it. Or when I go off to do a sidequest and Rasputin feels the need to remind me that I should actually be doing my main quest. Mainly it's Ras getting on your nerves by constantly talking during gameplay, but that seems to be an issue for single player RPGs across the board. What really gets me are during boss fights, hearing the bosses repeat the same 4-5 voicelines over and over and over again during the entire bossfight. It's just irksome and there's no reason for it.Over all super positive experience, just hope for the next game DoubleFine tighten up a couple of things and spend a little more time asking themselves "is this going to be fun the third time?" before working really hard to implement something.

_childDocuments_.review: Gems like this a so rare in gaming nowadays, I feel.Psychonauts 2 is a continuation of the much-beloved, but fairly unknown, Psychonauts platformer game that was released in 2005 for the PS2/Xbox/PC. 2 retains all the charm, wit, and excellent gameplay of the original, with an expanded storyline, voice cast, and, of course, updated graphics. The main difficulties lie not in the gameplay itself, but rather the "extra" objectives, meaning this game is great for casual and "less-casual" gamers.This game is full of charm, and also does something that video games so rarely get right (with the notable exception of Hellblade: Senua's Sacrifice), which is to positively look at mental health issues.I bought this game full-price soon after release, and I think it was worth every cent!

_childDocuments_.review: it was everything a sequel should be and much, much more. it completely kept the feel of the first game with the depth of the stories it tells, its humor, the style, the richness of the world and minds, and even the controls (just obviously smoother). the assist features were fantastic additions, they make the gameplay very comfortable and they do not keep you away from completing every achievement. the levels were all unique, maybe not as challenging as the past ones but still fun in their own way. about the story in short: whole and brilliant.theres a short recap at the very beginning on what had happened previously and an introduction on how already usable abilities work early on if people need a refresh or are new to the game. _childDocuments_.review: It was the Psychonauts I was waiting so long for and more.It really feels and plays like the much deserved sequel (although I would prefer to have powers earlier rather than later).The gameplay is nice, the music is nice, Raz, Lily and Agents are nice. _childDocuments_.review: I'll swing back around and give some commendations because Psychonauts 2 has plenty of positives, to the point where if you just made a list based on pure good vs bad, the good would seem to completely eclipse the short comings. HOWEVER, it feels like this was made by someone who forgot what a video game even is. Barrelling past some smaller gripes, the central issue with Psychonauts 2 is the sheer pretension. Every five seconds seconds of gameplay is interrupted by cutscenes. I'm not talking about over world story progression, I'm talking about the levels. Play a small segment, get a cutscene. Walk literally five feet quick cutscene to establish the new scenery. Cutscene for set pieces, cut scene for you name it. It's mind boggling how obstructured actual game play is at any given moment, and even more infuriating, the levels are designed around this segmented design. Most--not all-- levels are short sixty second obstacle courses and then you get telaported to the next one. I was curious how you could even replay levels designed like this, and it turns out you just get a teleport option to play each tiny chunk. The core design is so grand, so up it's own butt. The first, what? Three hours? The first three hours of this game is completely on the rails with no overworld exploration, no stage that attempts to be cohesive. I was actually miserable at first. And while it gets better, you better beleive it never goes away. There was such an emphasis on produtction value and constantly showing you how crazy and weird the world are that the developers literally forgot to let you play the game. Which is highly ironic because being up their own butts made me hate the levels. I really want to emphasize this. There were sections where I could not possibly explain why control was taken away from me. Dialgoue? I can listen as I platform? Want to show me a view? I can see it; you really don't need to. Past that, the overall pacing and structuring is janky. Like I mentioned, the first three hours was on the rails. And even when you unlock the over world, it's structured around 3 stages. This means the majority of powers you have going into it, and by the time you get additional exploration abilities, you're locked out until the post game. You lack that joy of exploration where you see something and you can't get it and then you come back stronger with new abilities. A collectathon is thrust on you for two hours and then it's over. And again I emphasize, there was no reason for this. It's unconscionable that the developer thought: let's make sure they can't explore for most of the game. So focused on their own vision how they wanted the game experience they forgot to structure it like a video game. We're almost done with the negatives. I'll also throw some general negativity toward some stage design, combat, and difficulty. The game is very easy with a lot of what's being asked of the player not properly balanced around your powers. But combat gets ratcheted up which is an abysmal choice. It's not deep, just annoying. Time for some glowing praise:1) The ambition of the game is insane.2) It's gorgeous and creative, especially the stages. 3) The way powers are implemented as a sequel is refreshing. You don't have to reearn anything and they still found an on rap to create progression and make it not feel like you started on the plateau. Not perfect, but still a bold choice that worked. 4) The story. If there is one thing that didn't work about the first game, it was the story. This game takes it past competent to surprising. It's still relatively simple in the way a game structured as this is can be, but I give full points to what they worked in here. Overall, so many elements that are sterling on their own right fall flat and I put the fault squarely on the game direction. Not to get too personal here, but it feels like a George Lucas situation with the natural restraints and needing to rely on others. You write that man a blank check and it's a nightmare. Which isn't even to say that this director's track record is impeachable when working on smaller projects. Brutual Legends is just a cocophany of: "Why would you design this."I digress. As someone who loved the original (I say as someone who isn't nostalgic because I played the original three years ago) I'm not sure this is worth you're time. It's fine. There's some cool stuff to see, but you'll be trudging through it. 5/10

This advisory, well-written and considerate, is the start of the game's rock-solid core of care and consideration. Where the first game stumbled in how it showed the mentally ill, and ways of "treating" their illnesses, this game shows how- even in a world of bizarre psychic brainscapes- it's possible to be sensitive in how you show and care for these people. And as a bonus, that level of care and extra attention extends to the rest of the game too, from the creativity in the art and level design, to how good the game feels to play. One of the very few games I'm more than glad to have paid full price for, because it's been worth every cent for me.

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent platformer, with a fantastic sense of humor and wonderful style throughout.  It didn't quite feel like it reached the heights of its forebear and there's a definite shift in tone from "wacky hijinks in troubled minds" to "mental health is a serious issue and all these people have experienced some horrifying things in their lives."  I understand the reasoning and can appreciate a more serious take to fit with Raz being more of a Psychonaut now, but the child in me definitely preferred the former.  Still, the increased budget led to some truly impressive mindscapes (although hiding colorful collectibles in a 60's drug trip was a ♥♥♥♥ move), and I quickly settled in and felt like I was just playing more Psychonauts.The combat is vastly improved and feels a lot more varied, focusing less on expendable ammo and more on recharging powers.  That said, even with four slots to freely swap between, each enemy has two or three ideal ways to handle them, and in later fights where they're throwing a wide variety at you, I found myself having to pause the action frequently in order to swap out powers.The story was good, though it lacked the same kind of over-the-top feeling as its forebear.  It did do a better job of focusing in on the secret psychic agent angle, though, and I appreciate that.  Raz's new group of 'friends' are introduced as they're bullying and hazing him, though, and I never quite felt that any of them really manage to redeem themselves for that, especially since in the scenes where they're helping him out, not only is Raz still taking the lion's share of risk, they're all actively patting themselves on the back and telling him how much he owes them.  Plus I couldn't shake the feeling that the group had a diversity quota as unsubtle as the Burger King Kids Club, right down to the one wheelchair-bound member.Be warned: the game does start with a "Last time on:" segment, but it does NOT hold your hand to bring you up to date.  A solid 30%-40% of the jokes and story beats are going to go over your head if you have not played Psychonauts 1 and at least seen a playthrough of the Rhombus of Ruin.  The former is understandable considering it's still available on Steam, but the latter being so integral seemed like a horrible decision considering it's a VR exclusive.In all, it doesn't quite hit the same highs as Psychonauts 1, but is still VERY worth your time.

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably the closest thing to a perfect sequel I can think of. Everything I loved about the first psychonauts is here and some more. All the dialogue that's somehow sarcastic and sincere at the same time, the goofy character design, the amazing environmental storytelling. Honestly the way this game handles not only mental illness, but relationships, group dynamics, and coping mechanisms I'd be suprised if this wasn't referenced in some type of psyche class. The weakest parts of this game are probably the combat and platforming and they're not even bad, the writing just outshines them.The platforming can be hit or miss sometimes but I was never bored or majorly stuck in any area. it all moves at a very good pace and is constantly introducing new elements and aspects, its just no Super Mario or anything. When it comes to combat I've heard in other reviews that its nothing special, and I'll admit its not the hardest, But the amount of enemy variety and the way each power factors into combat I was always happy to jump back into it especially in the latter half of the game. Also pretty much every boss is awesome, can't really think of a bad or lame one.The only two "complaints" I have is there are WAY too many fragments and the pin system is a little under-cooked but still cool nevertheless. I think two more pin slots would've helped and maybe cheaper prices. But bedsides that this game is stellar. 8.5-9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start by saying this game delivered on everything I hoped it would, I'm honestly sad it ended and that there isn't much more after the credits rolled. I played the first Psychonauts fairly recently and loved it despite the faults it had, of which most were a byproduct of the time/zeitgeist the game came out in. And when you drop into the sequel it really feels like not much has changed between the characters, both narratively and visually. And don't get that sentence wrong, the game looks absolutely stunning in UE4. They just translated the artstyle so well (and improved a lot of it's aspects, like animation) into the "next-gen" space. I also need to add that the music and voicework is once again top-notch, with lots of returning roles which really helps move the experience forward that much more. It takes me back to the cartoons I used to watch during the early and mid 2000's.My only real issues with the game were me getting stuck between bits of scenery about 2-3 times (particularly in the beginning, the casino levels) which forced me to restart a checkpoint. The fact figments were hard to keep track of (returning issue of the first game). And I found the (SPOILER ALERT maybe) final boss, while well presented and told, a bit of a pushover. But the game makes up for it with some extra bits that help bring closure to the whole thing, so it's easy to forget.A must-play for fans and newcomers alike. I'm really hoping they get to do that remake of the first game they were spitballing around in several interviews. I think it deserves a proper makeover.9/10

_childDocuments_.review: The Overall Verdict: 9/10 - A fantastic new addition to a loved series! They tried some new things, not all of them worked for the better, but the heart and soul of Psychonauts lives on stronger than ever through this long awaited sequel. 8/10 if you want to 100% it. Story: 9/10 - Enticing and emotional plot that smoothly continues the story from the first game and greatly expands lore with only minor (practically unnoticeable) alterations to the original plot.Dialogue: 10/10 - I'm ecstatic to say that they managed to perfectly maintain the humor and delivery of the incredibly comedic dialogue from the first game in this one, but with slightly less crude humor this time. It may have lost a bit of its edge, but it's still hilarious and you'll be surprised by how much they can get away with while remaining "appropriate".Visuals: 10/10 - The art team has earned a LONG vacation and hopefully a bunch of awards for this one. Though some of the NPC's may look a bit muppety, The unique style of Psychonauts 1 has been masterfully recreated in this high rez sequel. Each mind has it's own unique style and the overworld is a stunning masterpiece of environmental design. F$%&#@! nailed it.Movement: 7/10 - Reliable and fun. But compared to the first game it feels very stiff. This is more of a personal gripe, but Psychonauts 2 makes it very hard to stray from the intended path. This makes navigation throughout each level and the overworld much clearer and easy to understand at the cost of an overall feeling of freedom. The level design is much better engineered both visually and mechanically than its predecessor. But this new style of movement makes discovering secrets and finding collectibles more often reliant on unlockable mechanics rather than purely exploration, which was a huge draw of the first game for me and many others.Combat: 9/10 - VASTLY improved. What we lost in Exploration and Movement, we regained in the form of a much more in depth combat system. Each power is used in some way to expand your options in combat and combined with pins that alter the way your powers work, combat has become more of an event than an obstacle. My only complaint is that some of the most basic abilities from the first game have been either completely removed or locked behind upgrades or pins. Requiring you to spend precious resources or pin slots in order to be able to use a once standard technique. Progression & Flow: 8/10 - Solid consistent progression, but occasionally restrictive and slightly tedious if aiming for 100%. The game starts out a bit slow, but rapidly begins to open up after the first few levels are completed. Your goal is always clear and available to review with countless hints scattered throughout the levels and dialogue to ensure you never feel completely lost. Sometimes the hints can be a bit on the nose or become annoying if you just want to wander around for a bit. But overall they come in handy and aren't annoying enough to be a problem. My main issue with the flow of this game is that many mechanics required to complete certain tasks are locked behind upgrades and unlockables available only in later parts of the game. In the first few levels you are guaranteed to miss multiple collectibles because you aren't given the tools you need to reach them yet. Creating mandatory backtracking for mostly minor rewards. Some of these optional upgrades are also only used a handful of times throughout the entire game to minimal effect. Making them feel more like time-wasting filler rather than a sign of progress.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a masterpiece, without question living up and going beyond the original game. Each level is meticulously crafted and combines together to create an amazing narrative with consistently great theming, pacing, and quality. I have been waiting to play this game since 6 years ago when I played the first game and Psychonauts 2 got announced. There's a Miyamoto quote that's incredibly overused, but for redundancy: "A delayed game is eventually good, but a rushed game is forever bad". I am beyond glad Double Fine kept working on this game until they reached what it is now, instead of releasing a buggy game that lacks substance like most AAA titles in the past 5 years. The only fault with this game is that Double Fine didn't market it enough. I really hope that Pychonauts get the attention it deserves at the game awards later this year.This game is my game of the year.

Never boring,There are lot of differents univers, challenges, fights, design, musics...I loved it all.I found the main story well done and I liked that we were able to explore several characters minds (some are really crazy)Was able to complete it after about 37h which I found good enough.Maybe a small improvement would be that we can have a combat arena at the end to enjoy our full upgrade :)Thanks to the team for this amazing job

_childDocuments_.review: Razputin Aquato, trained acrobat and powerful young psychic, has realized his life long dream of joining the international psychic espionage organization known as the Psychonauts! But these psychic super spies are in trouble. Their leader hasn't been the same since he was kidnapped, and what's worse, there's a mole hiding in headquarters. Raz must use his powers to stop the mole before they execute their secret plan--to bring the murderous psychic villain, Maligula, back from the dead.

name: Hotshot Racing
detailed_description: ***Hotshot Racing Big Boss Bundle – Free new DLC!*** The Big Boss Bundle brings thrilling DLC to Hotshot Racing for free! New mode Barrel Barrage delivers the most incendiary action yet, while the Boss Level Grand Prix introduces an expanded selection of rapid racetracks. Hotshot Racing Hotshot Racing is a blisteringly fast arcade-style racing game fusing drift handling, razor-sharp retro visuals and an incredible sense of speed to create an exhilarating driving experience. Developed by racing game veterans SUMO Nottingham and Lucky Mountain Games, Hotshot Racing is an all-new driving experience which revives the classic arcade gameplay of the 90s and thrusts it into the modern era. 16 racing circuits provide the twists, turns and straights conducive to searingly quick racing. Take in coastal, jungle, alpine and Las Vegas desert environments, with each course modelled with the most vivid colours and blue skies for miles. Time Trial and Grand Prix modes cater to those who like to compete in classic racing formats, while ‘Cops and Robbers’ and ‘Drive or Explode’ modes offer exhilarating new ways to play. Each mode is available in single-player, four-player split-screen and eight-player online, while Time Trial is single-player only. Single-player modes run at a blistering 60FPS to deliver one of the fastest depictions of racing possible. Smash lap records to rise-up the global online leaderboards or download ghost laps to match your racing lines against the very best. MEET THE HOTSHOTS Keiko, Xing, Mike, Alexa, Aston, Toshiro, Marcus and Viktor - eight speed addicts that have dedicated their lives to the pursuit of being the greatest racing driver in the world. CATCH THE DRIFT Drifting is crucial in Hotshot Racing. Boost charges as the player drifts so maintaining it for as long as possible is vital to preserving maximum speed throughout a race. DRIVE OR EXPLODE In this mode each car has a bomb attached to it. Drop below a certain speed and BOOM! The trigger speed gets faster and faster, forcing players to maintain impossibly high speeds. COPS AND ROBBERS Robbers evade the cops. Cops catch the robbers, and in doing so convert them to the police side, leading to an exciting test of skill for the surviving criminals. A WELL NEEDED BOOST Earn boost by drifting and slipstreaming opponents and unleash a one-shot hit of speed to leave them in your rear view mirror.

_childDocuments_.review: A reasonably well executed arcade racer completely ruined by essentially game-breaking rubber-banding.Please hear me out, I actually don't hate rubber-banding and dynamic difficulty in arcade racing games. It's a mechanic that has its place and if executed well it keeps things interesting and engaging for all skill levels.But I have never seen a more extreme and broken case than in Hotshot Racing:Literally  the player does in anything but the final lap matters and no matter how flawless or clean the player drives for the last half of the final lap, an AI opponent will always finish within a second of the player. And this happens throughout all difficulty levels.This is so easily exploitable that it's not frustrating, it's simply broken: Drive however you want in the initial laps and consciously or not collect some boost via slipstreaming or drifting but don't ever use this boost until the end of the final lap. Boost past the AI near the finish line, finish first every time. This essentially works every time and for all difficulty levels.I like the presentation and the sense of speed, I don't mind the physics too much and even the overly aggressive AI at least fits the vibe of the game. There's nothing to truly write home about, but it's all mostly fine or at best inoffensive.But given that the single player gameplay is all but broken in its current state and that the multiplayer is and always has been dead, there really isn't much to recommend here.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of people complain about the rubber banding. They're mostly right, but really I think the problem is the way the AI racers will HULK OUT on you. Case in point: I was winning a race in expert mode, driving clean and all that like a ridiculously fast pacifist, until one of the other racers headbutted me into a wall so hard I glitched over it and fell through the bottom of the level into videogame oblivion. That's stupid. I still recommend the game though. It's amazingly fun in all these ways:Awesomesauce:- The gnarly visual style- No-nonsense balls to the wall arcade racing- The blistering speed- The spunky music that goes faster and more upbeat as the race progressesThat said, the agression is a problem. I'm fine with the 'rubber banding' system. I don't want to lead the race by a whole lap because the AI is inept. If I crash into every corner because I don't know the track, I should be punished for that and the AI shouldn't wait for me. In that way this game works perfectly because the racers will give it their all and since they also crash and make mistakes, it means I can get 1st, 1st, 8th, 3rd in a cup and still get the gold. Because racing in this game isn't always fair and there is a smidge of randomness added to the skill of blasting through colourful alpine racing tracks.  I love arcaderacers like an F-Zero, just ridiculous speed, high difficulty, a way too boost into the next dimension and a good beat to vibe to. This game has all of that and more. But eh... to the devs: please fix that agression. There is a balance between skill and luck. And there is getting HULK SMASHED THROUGH THE GLITCH DIMENSION, and that's a sign something somewhere, needs adjustment.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: The problem is that the developer seems to have completely abandoned their game. While this wouldn't be much of an issue as it's mostly working just fine in single player, it has rendered the entire multiplayer mode unplayable as there are no longer lobby servers that would enable players to connect to multiplayer lobbies. Even though I personally enjoy the game and its driving model, I can't honestly recommend supporting a developer that abandons a crucial game mode so soon after release. The game itself has only a few minor balance flaws that could probably be fixed with some minor tweaking and updates.

_childDocuments_.review: is an arcade style racing game that honestly doesn’t have much to offer. Despite the controls simulating the feel of an arcade racing game accurately and the art style fitting the genre fairly well, there are some odd design choices that should’ve been revamped or at least looked into as the game would be releasing on Steam rather than on an actual arcade.• Definitely captures the feel of a nostalgic arcade racing game• Cars have different stats that are suited better for drifting, top speed or acceleration• Soundtrack and art style have a very distinctive sound and feel to them• All 16 tracks and bland and boring• Rubberbanding 'balancing' and extremely aggressive AI• AI are extremely aggressive and can completely mess you up by ramming into you and making you spin out of control• You might get 5 hours max out of this game if you complete Grand Prix on all difficulties• Winning races earns you money, however you can only purchase cosmetic items, no upgrades or purchasing new cars• Quips from your character get annoying quickly, either have more voice lines or make them speak less• Nobody playing online• Despite there being at least some variation with the environments, there are some repeats of structures and environmentsPut plain and simple,  tries to simulate an arcade game and in that regard it hits the nail on the head. The controls feel responsive as you race down the track at high speeds, drifting around corners whilst taking over cars and utilising your boost at just the right time to steal the victory at the end of the race. However, apart from this, there isn’t really much else to boast about for this game…First off let's discuss the tracks you’ll be racing on, you’ll be given 16 tracks in total all which are only slightly different from one another and really aren’t interesting to race on whatsoever. It’s not like I was expecting  styled tracks in this game, but something more than just a circle or oval with extra turns here and there would’ve made it more interesting. For some reason, I quite like the idea of tracks crossing over each other in one way or another so you can see other cars that are behind or in front of me, but  doesn’t provide that at all. All the tracks are flat with only a couple of sharp turns that force you to drift hard to get around them smoothly.It doesn’t feel like there was much thought creating these tracks either, there aren’t enough hard turns to warrant a drift every time but you're basically forced to drift as much as you can because you need the boost. It also doesn’t help when the track has barely any turns that aren’t sharp enough and so you find yourself doing small drifts on long straights to fill up your boost. It's not like boost isn’t necessary though, especially on the harder difficulties since all the other racers will be using boost as well and are practically always on your tail no matter how fast you go.Winning these races aren’t all that satisfying either, there’s no sense of progression since you win money and only use it to purchase cosmetic skins for your racer (who you barely ever see so what’s the point) or your cars. It would’ve been a better idea to at least upgrade your car with better stats or purchase new cars as that would encourage the player more to play through the Grand Prix on the harder difficulties and try to earn gold on them.AI racers for some reason are extremely aggressive and love to bump into the back of you causing you to occasionally spin out of control. On the expert difficulty if you spin out of control and crash into the side of the track coming to a complete stop, then you’ve pretty much lost the race depending on how far into the track you are. I do remember that arcade style racing games had aggressive AI with titles such as  where you’d constantly be smashing into other cars and causing them to crash. But in , you’ll simply bump into them and they’ll lose a bit of speed before catching right back up to you. It’s practically impossible to secure first place during a track since, no matter how hard you try (even if you use all your boosts in one go), second and third place will be able to catch up with you and you’ll constantly be battling it out for first place.Rubberbanding AI seems to be very aggressive also, even on the easiest difficulties you will find second and third place right behind you in seconds no matter how fast you go. It's not much of a problem since you can easily steal the victory with a boost right before the finish line, however the rubberbanding on hard or expert is where it shows off the most and makes the game more unfair than challenging. Expert mode practically consists of being in the lead for a certain amount of time until the racer behind you bumps into your back and moves you forcibly to the left making you crash into the side rails, it's not challenging it's just unfair and frustrating. Sometimes you’ll be in the middle of 4 or 5 other racers all crashing into one another making it pretty difficult to escape from. You might consider that rubberbanding AI like this is part of the arcade experience and I would be all for that if I was playing this in an arcade, but I’m not. I’ve bought this game to play whenever I want to and don’t want to be frustrated with mechanics or something that tries to make me spend another £1 like the arcade games do.The one mode that could’ve brought this game out from the dirt was the online mode, however this mode is dead in the water and as we all know, you can’t drive a car that’s submerged in water. I never really had hopes for finding anyone online even when I saw the trailer for this game since online indie games like this usually don’t have an active community of online players, however there was still a small glimmer of hope that I held onto. It’s a shame because if there was an active community, then it would’ve gained at least some replay value as you raced against random people.The fast soundtracks add to the intensity of each race, with the majority of each track having their own old school soundtrack. Similar to the graphics, the soundtrack has a distinctively nostalgic sound to it as does the announcer's voice. However, their voice does get more annoying the longer that you play as you hear them talk every time you reach a checkpoint which is roughly every 20 - 30 seconds.The polygon graphics fit the style of an old school arcade racing game very well, there is at least some variation in the places that you race and give off a slight sense of nostalgia. However with such a short list of tracks, you would’ve thought that you wouldn’t see a repeat of structures you’ve seen before. Unfortunately if you play through the 4 Grand Prixs then you’ll certainly see some familiar structures which could’ve been replaced with something different. is nothing more than what it says on the packet, a simple arcade racing game. All the tracks are boring and dull with no creativity put into them, the AI is unnecessarily aggressive with extreme rubberbanding difficulty and you’ll be lucky to get 5 hours out of this game if you want to complete all 4 Grand Prixs on every difficulty. Overall, this game lacks content and for the asking price, you’d have to wait for a massive sale before even considering to purchase

_childDocuments_.review: Hotshot Racing is a new great arcade racing game with good oldschool graphics, but sharp, which you can fully enjoy at a complete 60 frames per second.Hotshot racing is insprired by classic racing games from the early 90's, give it a sharp modern makeover and you get something enjoyable like this game.The game offers several singleplayer modes and online multiplayer modes which includes different modes then in singleplayer mode.While you can do tournaments on singleplayer, there is an online mode where the race starts with 1 player in a police car, and whoever he catch will turn into another police car, this will increase the challenge to win as the goal is not to get caught.Hotshot racing comes with a large choice of vehicles and also customization options. There are currently 16 different different racetracks to race on. In the game you are required to drift in the turns in order to gain color in your boost meter, you'll get the boost without drifting as well, but much slower, and you'll need the boost!

_childDocuments_.review: First up I want to say that Outrun 2006, Daytona USA, Virtua Racing and Sega Rally are my favourite racing games of all time.. so I had high expectations for this.. indeed I bought it immediately on the release day.. Initially I thought it was great but, 56 minutes of play later and all 4 single player GPs finished, I have no urge to ever play it again and found it a flawed, rather empty experience so cannot recommend it.The visuals look the part, the music is ok (the character voices can be a bit annoying though) and for the most part the handling is fun and easy to master. The things that ruin the experience are the boring tracks and the AWFUL computer AI cars. The tracks look lovely but they just lack the fun factor that makes you want to come back and master them (like Virtual Racing or Sega Rally).. The AI is APPALLING.. you get a super start, they are instantly behind you.. bashing into the back of your car. You race a flawless lap, they are bashing behind you again. If you get knocked back a few places, they bash each other and you pass them again in a few seconds, only to repeat the process. It's very boring and irritating. Every race can be won by saving your 4 boosts (gained by drifting) until the last corner of the last lap and then letting rip to boost past the line.. the computer cars will ALWAYS be bashing into you, overtaking, then falling behind as you slipstream them.. It's really sh*t to be honest.What a shame as with some better course design and vastly improved AI, this could have been great! I tried a couple of times to play online but there were not enough players to start a race. I have no desire to play arcade mode to beat times on the courses.Close but no cigar!
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: The more I play this last update, the more I feel it's ruined the game. They haven't fixed the frame time bug that makes 60 FPS feel like 15. The car balance is still a mess. The physics still need fixing. The camera still goes crazy. Time Trials still have numerous problems. The Expert AI is still too aggressive (the AI really needs to learn how to yield; I mean, come on, guys.)You get the idea.Most of my grievances have to do with Time Trials. The Expert AI is too easy for me, and any challenge that it does have comes from it rubberbanding and going out of its way to slam into the player (seriously), which just forces a retry and isn't something you can always control. This definitely needs to be fixed, as it prevents clean driving and leads to a lot of frustration, but it's possible to get an early lead and win consistently. So, I've moved on.The only challenge left is Time Trials, and even then the leaderboards presumably have some cheaters.But it's not about competing. It's about learning racing as an art form. This game does an excellent job of teaching you about the geometry behind racing. That's why I've stuck with it. But now that's ruined.They arbitrarily made every car around 20mph faster. This throws off the rhythm of every track and makes certain turns extremely awkward.The game demands we take those turns at very precise angles, but the handling and physics are too broken to maintain that level of perfection.Every tool I have is now working against me. We're moving too fast, the handling of the cars isn't good enough, and the tracks were not designed for these speeds.I've said it in other reviews, and I'll say it in this one: If you demand perfection from me, you better make sure your game is perfect.I've uninstalled it. I could beat my latest time, but it's not worth the grind -- a grind that comes from something randomly going wrong, something out of my control, and then me losing 30 seconds of my life. 30 seconds that translates into hours of lost time because we have to redo the entire lap after every mistake.There is a retry button, but some genius decided it'd be cool to make us sit through a small cutscene and start the lap at half speed. As far as I'm concerned, that retry button doesn't exist.It may be a little better if there was an option to disable the ghost, but there isn't, and I'm tired of it flickering in and out of view and being distracting.It's so unbearably tedious. It's exhausting, frustrating, thoughtless, sloppy, and it rewards sloppy driving.The point is: I'm not learning anything anymore, not because there isn't anything left to learn -- there absolutely is -- but because the mechanics are holding me back from achieving a higher level of mastery.The tedium comes from fighting both my tools and the track, instead of using a tool to fight the track. Get it?This needs more testing. It needs testing from players who are truly honest and actually good.Someone needs to sit down and think about what the game does well and what it's trying to teach.

_childDocuments_.review: Forget the insane amount of grinding that needs to be done to unlock all the cars that require hundreds of replays, what grinds my gears the most on this is how the AI in this racer operates. The very aggressive rubberband AI makes any skill you have during the first 2 laps completely unimportant. If that were all, then I would simply just shrug it off, thumbs down, and uninstall and be on my merry way. However since I now have learned the developers have abandoned this game wholesale and shut down the servers barely a year after its release then I have to warn everyone to not buy this game. It's a waste of money, and I only paid a few USD for it. Beauty is merely skin deep, and the aesthetics mimicking Virtua Racing and Daytona USA aren't enough to keep me invested.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: I believe everything's been said already but I'm mostly doing this review in case any of my Steam friends feel like buying this game. So dear friends: don't buy that.The rubber banding is through the roof, the AI is way too agressive and winning a race only comes down to abusing the physics. You can do so by drifting ALL THE TIME for no reason, slipstreaming as much as possible, only to fill your boost gauge and use said boost to temporarily gain the first place… best course of action is to keep your boost until the very end of the race and use it all to make sure you pass in first place. Obviously, driving clean is not possible as the AI keeps on ramming your car and won't make you first.Just to convince you I'm telling nothing but the truth, the first most common achievement in this game (with a whooping 81% percent!) is "Phew" which you'll receive upon becoming first and finishing the race with less than a second after the second place. If that doesn't tell you something about the insanity of the rubber banding, I don't know what will.At the end of the day, the game still looks good and controls rather well so I believe the developers could save the game by a) tuning down both the rubber banding and the AI agressiveness, and b) removing the boost altogether for a more driving-like experience instead of this micro-management crap.As it stands I can't recommend this game. I know it's an homage to the SEGA racing games but playing Daytona, Scud Racer or even OutRun can be done easily and with good graphics nowadays. Just go play those if you need a fix of nostalgia racing. I know I will.

_childDocuments_.review: While the game itself is good, it's sadly unfinished, and from what i've seen from the discussions, the devs have abandoned this project.Here's some of the pros/cons i've seen so far:Pros:- The handling of the cars in the game is simple and easy to control.- Drifting is easy, a simple tap of the brake will allow you to go into a slide.- Normal difficulty doesn't feel too easy as the AI will keep rubberbanding to match your pace, a good thing in my opinion.- A nice variety of gamemodes, although small. There's the normal arcade racing mode, then you have Cops and Robbers, Drive or Explode, Barrel Barrage and of course, Time Trial.- Named characters that has personalities and their own cars. There are 8 characters in the game and each one has 4 cars to choose from. A great addition in any racing game.Cons:- Multiplayer is dead, the devs turned off multiplayer for this game a year after it was released.- Despite that, you need an internet connection to play this game even in single player.- No Steam Cloud support, which means if you uninstall the game and then reinstall it later, you'll have to start from the beginning again.- You can't remap the buttons on a controller.- In the Cops and Robbers gamemode, you can't choose if you want to be either a cop or a robber. It will be random every time.- Little variety of music.- Broken promises by the devs to include gamemodes that haven't been added yet.- No mod support to fix those issues.Thank god i didn't pay for this, it's so unfinished.

_childDocuments_.review: While it might not seem like I've played this for long enough to understand it, getting the hang of this game isn't exactly hard.Reading the other reviews for this game, I've seen lots of people complaining about the rubber-banding. As most have come to know it, rubber-banding has been seen as a lazy method of creating competition in racing games. People hate it in F-Zero, people hate it in Mariokart. But why? In both Mariokart and F-Zero, methods of catching up to one's opponents are hard, or random in finding. In F-Zero, one sacrifices durability for more speed. A solid system, if it weren't for the AI cheating, and making the race feel unfair. In Mariokart, one can catch up to his or her opponents by grabbing items from the randomized item boxes, and using them against the computer-controlled opponents. That sounds fine, a fun, chaotic party game. However, the AI in Mariokart tend to generate items and speed when they're falling too far behind. It's a method of compensation implemented by the devs to make up for their ♥♥♥♥♥♥ AI.While Hotshot Racing doesn't have good AI, the rubber-banding in this game is centered around the player's experience, rather than compensation for lazy code. Hotshot Racing offers many methods of catching up to one's opponents, and without punishment for doing so. The player acts like a driver, slip-streaming and drifting around corners, and they are rewarded with boost for doing so. At a certain point while playing this game, I learned how to counter the other drivers' rubber-banding by using my car as a wall. Say I was in front, and oncoming opponents would smash into my back end, giving me both a small speed boost, decreasing their own speed, and keeping me in first. With so many methods for catching up and staying in the lead, it's easy to see why this game's rubber-banding is so harsh. For those players who put this game down because of the rubber-banding, I would recommend playing a little more, and figuring out a way around it. The way forward is easier than one might think. Fending off against one's opponents in this way is exciting, and vaguely reminiscent to the precision of fencing. There's a challenge here, and it's a good challenge. I received this game from a friend, who got it from humble bundle.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a rock solid arcade drift type racing game. The controls, the customisation, AI, racing options, the levels, the racing, the difficulty... all falls perfectly into place for this game. Highly recommended on sale especially those looking for campaign and arcade local 2-4 player racer. The  is very good all around. The game has simple arcade , but everything about the game comes so well together. For example, if the player starts the race at the right RPM the car jumps forward with boost engaged. Shortly after a turn will approach and the player can regularly turn, or start drifting to acquire boost. Boost does player a role in the game, especially in key moments. This isn't the type of game where a player can simply run way ahead of the pack. Due to the drafting feature the game is constantly putting both the AI and players in a struggling situation. Some may like this sort of  with constant struggle, some may not like having a safety net to jump forward. However, with the right drifting methods to refill boost - sometimes things are possible. The computer players in this game were also really well done. They're not extremely annoying, but annoying enough that it makes the game fun. The  are phenomenal. Although the game strives to look retro, it's done well in its own right to show off its own style. I feel all relevant and required graphics and animations have been included from drifting to amazing level design. Some of the levels come at the player extremely fast. The game tries to combat that by providing clear turn signs for the player to observe. The cars, the characters, and the customisation for both give the player enough to spend money acquired from races. The  are also very suitable to the game's atmosphere. Everything in both these domains were done with care.Overall, highly recommended on sale. Such a great little racing game done with such care in all aspects. This is one of those games that was done right and deserves to be on Steam!

_childDocuments_.review: The game has a wonderful visual style and plays close to an arcade racer from the 90s. The huge problem that this game has though is the awful rubber-banding. It doesn't matter how well you play, there will always be two racers right next to you at all times, their acceleration gaining massive boosts of speed without them even using boost. And the boost is pointless. It doesn't matter how fast you get boost, when you use it, how much of it you use, the enemy AI will always be half a second away from you. I saved all four boosts until the last lap, one after another in rapid fire and before the third one even finished I had second-place pass me. It is just stupid.

_childDocuments_.review: Still one of the most disappointing arcade racing releases of the last few years.Hotshot Racing almost has it all. The visual style is fantastic, the controls are amazing and the overall vibes are great. However it's just so horrific when actually racing. The AI constantly bombards you with collisions, and the constant feeling of racing in a suffocating pack with the yo-yo of 'in-front, behind, in-front, BANG, behind, in-front, BANG' is legitimately DRAINING.Never have I played an arcade racer where the AI model is so entirely mis-matched. This is kart-racing AI in an arcade racer, and it feels wrong.I'll re-install this to play time-trial mode every now and then, and I've actually got most of my play-time on the Switch version, but yeah, I just felt like making it known that Hotshot Racing and the oodles of pre-release promise it had that has been entirely left unfulfilled still bums me out.This could have been an absolute classic, man.

_childDocuments_.review: There’s a style of racing game that disappeared a while ago; striking colours, upbeat soundtracks, simple car handling and exotic looking landscapes. This relates to Sega’s golden years, with pioneering 3D graphics with the likes of Daytona USA and Sega Rally. Thankfully, the developers have taken aim at this under-served section of the racing crowd and really hit the pedal with Hotshot Racing.It’s the sort of game that is everything a fan of arcade racers could want, especially if you had fond memories of those classics i mentioned. It truly captures a style of racing that is rarely seen these days. It’s fast-paced, easy to pick up and play and most importantly, it’s really fun to play.It may have its certain quirks like rubber-banding, but that just adds to the authenticity of the era it’s based around. This is a great racing title that nails the driving mechanics and delivers an experience for both newcomers and veterans alike.Get this game, it’s worth every penny!

_childDocuments_.review: Hotshot Racing: Rubber band racing this game is rough kind of all around but ill mention a few key points Prosi personally like the art style and i get what its trying to invoke but i do think at times its too simplistic there are 4 modes Arcade, Championship, Cops and Robbers, Explosion, and time trialsand that's about where it endsCons:It doesn't run particularly well, that may not show up in the video review but the screen tearing was pretty wild with either vsync on or off. with it off i also noticed the game would either stutter or completely freeze for several frames before picking back up. ill note i'm playing at 1440p but both monitors are specced the exact same and have gsync so even more to the point this shouldn't be happening. the cars feel super floaty for the most part, they don't really feel like they are ever gripping the track. this is really apparent when you play the f1 car as the wheels bounce around like crazy and the body of the car looks like a boat (last race in the video as example)there are no upgrades to the vehicles other than cosmetics. there as far as i can tell are no unlocked vehicles each racer has 4 cars that's it. that's not totally an issue but they all feel very similar and stat wise a lot of them are identical.the cosmetics are very small and sometimes clear at all and the color options all feel very similar its like a variation of the colors already available but you cant choose your own colors its a set swatch for each. or like some backlights will instead of have one line the light will have 3. there are also rear-view mirror charms and different steering wheels but even in cockpit view on most cars you cant see them. so further asking why are they there?Cops and robbers mode is awful, it could maybe be fun with friends but with ai its just terrible. it really highlights all the issues with the controls and game play and packages it all into one mode. its just not fun. i think this portion wants to be burnout to some extent or need for speed most wanted, and just doesn't land any of the flair or fun of those games. granted they had way better budgets and larger teams but still at that point just don't add it in and refine other things.  My Biggest Gripe The rubber banding is completely bananas. i played primarily on normal and tried the other ones but here is the breakdownNormal: the opponents are right behind you at all times they will get in front occasionally but you can catch up pretty easily and as long as you have a boost left for the final stretch you will not lose. however that said you are going to be constantly slammed into and bumped by drivers almost non stop. i finished all 4 cups and this was consistent throughout. you never feel like you are doing well, you are never far in the lead no matter what. i could be playing this game completely wrong but it doesn't feel like i am. ill also mention i tested this by saving all 4 of my boosts, i was in 1st the whole race and i blasted all 4 of them in row one after the other, and within a second all the opponents were right behind me and then passed me ( 4:10 in the video to see it.)Hard mode: they basically stay right with you or slightly in front of you the entire timeExpert mode: They're Gone, if you make even the slightest hiccup they are so far ahead of you might as well just restart the race. i do understand its expert and designed for the best of the best its just it seems your opponents are drastically enhanced over you and again your cars never change the stats are always the same. maybe i had the wrong car but it all felt pretty unbalanced throughout all difficulty modes.its also worth mentioning this was intended as others have said to be a Game called Racing Apex and from what i can tell this is basically that game with everything interesting ripped out and just the racing part left. this does not feel at al like a game thats been worked on for 4 years.in closing ill say its just not a great package and it isn't near as fun as you would hope or as the trailers may appear. if it shows up on gamepass play it there and if you do love it grab it but i think a few races in you'll see what i mean. there is room for improvement _childDocuments_.review: The game was in development for many years as Racing Apex and it looked much better years ago (look it up). After the rebranding many major features were cut, for example the massive upgrade system is completely gone and replaced by a half arsed visual customization that barely changes anything on the cars.It tries too hard to be like the 90's arcade racers people love, the visuals are the typical modern low poly stuff with no textures at all. It just doesn't look authentic. Look what Sega had in the 90's, those games look actually impressive, while Hotshot has oversimplified everything.The driving is somewhat decent, it gets pretty fun on higher difficulties until you crash into something (you will). No matter how hard you try to get away from everyone, the heavily rubberbanding opponents will ram your back and the physics force you to crash into the wall, causing you to lose almost all chances to win.I followed this game's development for years and I'm very disappointed with the end product. Instead of this, I highly recommend playing the actual 90's arcade racers, those are incredibly fun even after 20+ years.

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like a lot of the aspects of "Hotshot Racing" continuously work against each other.To build your boost gauge, you need to drift, but you lose speed doing so. AI opponents are constantly hugging you, so good luck trying to perform a drift that lasts more than two or so seconds.The aggressive rubberband AI means that no matter how well you drive and drift, your opponents will always be right on your tail, and that a lot if not all of the races will be decided down to the wire, so saving at least a couple boosts for the last lap is a must; in fact, I got the "Phew!" achievement (win the race just a second ahead of the 2nd place) on my very first race.Crash on rivals and nothing happens, but have them crash on you (that will happen a lot) and you'll be sent careening towards the wall. Have fun trying to regain positions every thirty seconds.The game looks great. Plays well too. But, with the annoying AI constantly hugging you and the drifting mechanic that punishes you, it just doesn't get it.

_childDocuments_.review: Impresses at first glance because of its graphics, but turns boring quickly. Hotshot Racing has lots of cool-looking cars from all kinds of eras, but it essentially doesn't matter what car you drive, as the game punishes players for trying to stay in 1st position as long as possible because the AI rubberbands like crazy and they have a massive slipstream advantage behind you (i.e. speed advantage). The game becomes much easier when you get a feel for how the cars should drift through the corners, building up boosts as you do and staying behing the leader, only to overtake them with one or two boosts before the finish line. This is not fun racing.It doesn't help that if you want to unlock all the cool customization stuff (apart from the stuff you can buy ofcourse), the game forces you to drive these cars a lot, artificially padding possible game time as you need to do certain things in a car (like boost 10 times in a single race or boost X amount in total or drift X amount in total etc) to unlock a hood, exhaust mod or something else.Obnoxious characters limiting what car you drive is for me the nail in the coffin. Characters spouting one-liners as you get overtaken, get a boost etc. when you just want to race. I don't get this addition to the game instead of putting all the effort for these characters into a character YOU can customize from scratch with different parts and suits and the like. In short, Hotshot Racing looks amazing at first glance because of its retro graphics but turns tedious quickly thanks to a variety of gameplay decisions.

_childDocuments_.review: Retro racing gaming is back thanks to Hotshot RacingThis game is a fast arcade retro style racing product. It was made by Sumo Digital and Lucky Mountain. Constant frenetic races are the fundamentals of this master piece well done game. It shows us the fascinating feeling of retro arcade era in just a simple gameplay with a variety of drivers, cars, customization and more great things that I liked a lot like how well designed were the maps and also the different modes that the game offers you to try.On the plus side, the soundtrack was great. Hotshot Racing has an original sound, with elements of the 80's decade. The customization is one of the main topics that I liked to spent my briefly time in the game. The cutscenes of every driver were astonishing, I mean graphically the whole game was on point on that part.On the down side, the online multiplayer is literally empty. I did not have the opportunity to play with other guys in a public match or even a ranked match because there was no one to play with. I checked SteamDB for more research and I was right: only a few people play this game nowadays.Overall, I would recommend playing this game with your friends and do not expect to play with someone else randomly in a public match. I am sure Hotshot Racing will have another opportunity to shine and the team behind this project will learn how to entertain their audience more as they get more experience.This is my first review in English. Thanks for reading my review.Thanks for the game, @Japani69Katti. You are a star.

_childDocuments_.review: This arcade racer looks, sounds and behaves exactly as you'd expect if you lived through the 90s. Drift or slipstream to fill up boost. Maintain throttle in yellow for turbo start. Keep the pedal to the metal for the entire race on most tracks if you just know when to drift around corners. Avoid collisions to achieve great sense of speed.Checkpoints are almost impossible to miss except on the hardest difficulty setting. It takes a short while to get used to the game's handling and bumper car physics but it becomes natural after a few laps and... it would actually be enjoyable if the unapologetically aggressive opponents weren't constantly rubber-banding and bumping the player out of control.The Grand Prix is the game's only structured selection. Though instead of offering a variety of challenges and game modes, it merely plows through every single track once on a basic 3-lap race to 1st place. The entire event, divided into 5 championships of 4 locations each, can be completed in 70 minutes on Normal difficulty.This game lacks a proper career mode. There is no car to purchase, no character to earn, no track to unlock, no additional challenges to complete. The game literally has no sense of progression whatsoever and after completing the Grand Prix once and trying out the few additional game modes as one-off races from the menu, I found no motivation to keep playing.The only thing to do with career money is purchase simple vehicle color schemes, plus car customizations that barely make any visual difference over the low-poly models.Each driver owns the same four equivalent vehicle types. Winning a championship plays a small humorous cut scene unique to each of them. All are caricatures of the countries they represent but don't seem to affect gameplay in any way other than through their sassy one-liners.The tracks themselves look detailed enough and are a mix of usual racer themes. They're all pretty nicely designed and look nice, though none of them offers anything particularly outstanding either.With fair AI and a properly structured career mode to showcase all its content in a rewarding manner, this game would have remained on my playlist much longer.

_childDocuments_.review: The physics feel really fun to drive with, the car choices are really good.But the game absolutely falls face first with its mechanics, the maps, ai, boost, and slipstream are completely out of wack.Every race ends up being a mindless rubberband fest with constant 3 wide bundle of cars, the ai rubberbands to the point of making actual arcade racers jealous.You'd think with physics made for tight cornering and quick acceleration, the maps would be designed more tightly with complex turns, but that isn't the case. Each map feels like a loop around roads the width of the purposed Texas highways, in most cases you accelerate up to 6th gear and never shift down.With the ai, they really wanted to put emphasis on "artificial" the ai cars constantly get up besode you and knock you around. It really doesn't matter what car you pick, the ai will always find its way to get up next to you. There isn't much for skill here, you just have to abuse the boost system as I will mention below. The boost mechanic feels like it causes more problems than to be a fun mechanic that rewards drifting, the problem with it is that its too rewarding.Given the overly rubberbandy ai, the best strategy is not to fight it, but to absolutely abuse it. Let an ai car take 1st as you freeload off the slipstream and when the final lap comes, just unload absolutely everything to secure first.Slipstreaming is an absolute mess, it's easier to catch up to other players here than it is in Mario Kart, the slipstream is laughably generous and lets you catch up from anywhere. This ends up feeling like a bad bandaid to the overly rubberbandy ai.This game had the physics to be a good arcade racer, but it unfortunately just fails with very confusing design choices. I really wanted to like this game but it feela absolutely awful to play.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't listen to the other dumbasses who reviewed this. You know this is an arcade racer, right? It's gonna have bs rubberbanding at points, right? If you can set this aside and overcome the impossible, then you can actually enjoy this game unlike the other slime creatures who've played this. Expert especially is really fun when you find a way to conquer it. If that's too hard, Normal and Hard are quite thrilling still; however, I feel the game controls and feels its best at Expert. It is difficult, and punishing, but oh so rewarding.If you like arcade racers, specifically older SEGA ones like Outrun 2, you will love this game. It has the perfected mechanics and drift of 2 decades worth of effort to make a glorious drifting system that feels great in both regular driving and boosting. It gives you a nice amount of control when turning into a slide and it improves greatly on Outrun 2's drift, which I already thought was near perfect.  Also wow, a game called HOTSHOT RACING has aggressive AI. Really makes you think. Can't believe some shmuck thought that was a negative.If you've only got into racing in the past 10 years with Forza Horizon, modern NFS, or some other garbage; this is not for you. You fundamentally do not understand what makes an arcade racer "arcadey", you play mid-ass sim-cade games; worse, all the same grey slop sim-racers. If you genuinely expected this to be like Forza in ANY way, you have no idea what you're getting into. This is, bar none, the best racing game on Steam. I say this, even though I love Burnout Paradise to death, this game is a masterpiece. For me, it feels like most of the best racing games are abandonware or emulated, but this is one of the few racing games on Steam to actually be good. Not just good, but amazing. Highly, highly, highly recommend this.P.S. A special ♥♥♥♥ you to the guy who said this was like a mobile game. If you compare this to smth like Hot Shot Unleashed or an actual mobile game like Asphalt 8 or 9, it is a world's worth of difference. Just because you fundamentally do not understand older arcade racers doesn't mean you get to spread libel like this. This is genuinely one of the best feeling racing games ever made, PERIOD, and I will die on this hill.

_childDocuments_.review: Hotshot Racing is the definition of aggressively mediocre. It's not good, it's not bad, it's just plain boring. It feels like it wants to so badly capture Mario Kart's audience, but doesn't want to be called a clone so all the best parts of Mario Kart are stripped. The AI rubberbands like crazy, which means you can be dead last for the whole race and jump into first on the last lap, or lead the whole race, get shunted from behind and finish 4th. This effectively means all racing until the final lap is pointless, and the plain ok physics don't make it fun to drive it either, rather it makes it feel like a chore you have to get through. All the characters have Marvel-esque one-liners which make you want to stop playing once you've heard the same line 20 times in the last 10 minutes. And the tracks aren't anything special either, not a single one is memorable in any way, and each has quite a simple layout. In general, the whole game feels like a corporate idea of "cool", it all feels so safe and bland that genuinely there is no point in playing it. You can have fun with a good game, you can have fun with a bad game, with a mediocre game all you get is disappointment, and that perfectly sums up Hotshot Racing.

_childDocuments_.review: Hotshot Racing is a nicely balanced arcade racer.  I play racing games only irregularly, but when I play one, I play it extensively.  My goal is to learn the limits of the cars, of the tracks, and to constantly improve my racing skills in the context of the challenges the game provides.  Other racing games I remember enjoying are Wave Race 64, Wipeout XL (on PlayStation), and Mario Kart 64.I am puzzled by many of the negative reviews of Hotshot Racing.  I can understand anyone disliking any given game.  But many of the negative reviews claim that (1) the (alleged) “rubber banding” is a flaw, or (2) the AI drivers are flawed, or (3) the boost mechanic is a flaw, or (4) the sometimes-chaotic collisions are a flaw.  In my opinion, all of these elements are intentional game design choices made by the developers, to achieve a certain result.  And the developers succeeded in creating their desired result.  Hotshot racing is an (arcade-style) game, not a driving simulator.  If you approach Hotshot Racing as a game, with an open mind, and without preconceived notions of what a racing game should be, then there is a lot to enjoy.Update:  Unless you are extremely confident that your GPU can output 60 (or more?) FPS, I would recommend starting with the graphics quality set to "low".  Then increase the graphics quality and see if the driving experience changes.  I have a much better driving experience with the graphics quality set to low.  My GPU is a very old 960 GTX, plugged into my very new 4K OLED TV.  (I'd buy a new GPU, but hey, it's 2021 right now!)

_childDocuments_.review: Want an arcade like racing game with silly mechanics, a checkpoint system and fun little game modes? Then this is a good pick. Wait for it to go on sale, because the $20 price tag does NOT make this game worth it. Online is weak, with not many people playing and all. But if two people have the game, you can have up to 4 people play with Parsec with no issues! If you can manage to get a full lobby of friends, game modes like Barrel Barrage would be insanity. Game modes explained quickly:Arcade: Just as it sounds, race the track and see who's the fastest!Barrel Barrage: Every time you go through a checkpoint, you get a barrel. An EXPLOSIVE barrel, you can hold up to 3 at a time (if you hold one actively, or else you can only hold 2), and you place them behind you as you drive along. You take damage when you drive through them, and you have a health bar throughout the race. Lose all your health, and you DNF.Cops and Robbers: Sounds like it does, you get some cops, they chase down the robbers through the race. Cops deal damage to the robber's health bar, once all a robber's health is depleted, they also turn into a cop. Then, a snowball effect happens, and chaos ensues. (Robbers get a "Bounty" and some health when they drive through checkpoints too!)Drive or explode!: Gotta keep your speed above the minimum required speed or you start to die! And then, explode! The minimum speed raises over time too, so make sure you keep going faster. Crashing into others lowers their health too, so some crazy shenanigans happen.Overall, this is a fun pick if you play it for an hour or so at a time with friends.Edit: While looking through some other reviews, people seem to hate the AI, and having problems with rubber banding. I play with a mate who lives in the EU, and I in America. We have zero connection issues with no rubber banding AI or anything. In fact, the AI being over aggressive makes this game fun! If you go into this game thinking its some serious racer, you're going to be mad and upset. It's more geared as a fun arcade style mayhem house of crazy. With that in mind, there's lots of laughs to be had.

_childDocuments_.review: The whole strategy caters around the final lap. That's all that matters. You have to save your NOS and plan to cut the last corner well and you will win every single race. Once you figure that out, there's nothing else to the game. It's a damn shame too because the tracks, graphics, cars, and racers are all interesting and fun. There seem to be no plans to fix any of this either. Rubber banding completely ruined this could-have been game, and it's a damn shame... I'm actually surprised there are positive reviews.And if you figure "whatever, I'll just play online!" Yeah, nah. The online is completely dead. Maybe one day when my internet is down and I'm extremely bored of all the other single player games on my library I will come back to this game and beat it.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun 1990s style arcade racer that takes clear inspiration from classic games like Daytona USA, Ridge Racer and SCUD Race. Hotshot Racing goes for a very similar aesthetic to SEGA's Model 1 arcade titles like Virtua Racing and Wing War and does a great job at emulating that style. The main focus of the game is on close drafting, clean drifting and a smart use of boosts. There are no combat items in most modes. Some of those secondary modes are a bit gimmicky and awkwardly balanced, but each one is enjoyable enough.Replay value is pretty decent even if you are going to play solo. There are over 30 vehicles with dozens of customizations that can be unlocked for each one through a series of relatively simple challenges. The paint options are a bit too basic for my liking, but I found that it was still pretty easy to make each car look cool in its own way.My one significant complaint is that the AI can be far too aggressive in a way that makes the higher difficulty GPs feel more tedious and frustrating than they have to be. This is worsened by the collision physics being absolutely chaotic in ways that can make you almost immediately lose all hope of keeping your place in the race from opponents ramming into you at awkward angles. However, with a bunch of loud friends that last point can actually become a positive.Wonderful visuals, solid controls, good music and especially great fun with a group of friends. A must play for big fans of the genre.
