_childDocuments_.review: The only reason HotShot is even mildly playable, is that SUMO has enough experience in the arcade genre to quickly push an almost competent if simplistic racer out the door. This team worked on 2 of the best arcade racers, one of them being the xbox/pc port Outrun 2006: Coast to Coast.And therefore, i find it the more unacceptable that both developer and Curve thought this product was ever worth selling for 20€.Not only is this not up against indie titles like Horizon Chase Turbo, it looks, feels and plays like many arcade racers on steam, games that were made by developers with very little experience. It's not terrible, just very lazily put together, with an artificial difficulty due to easily exploitable mechanics.Boost, slipstream and rubber band are a bigger factor to your victory, than actual skill. Your ability to take corners perfectly has no value, when you can slipstream all the way to the last lap and win with a boost finish.The only condition is that you need to drift on corners to get that boost.The progression system is painfully slowEvery single car has some of the worst and most repetitive challenge conditions. Drift xxx amount of times, or drift for xxx meters, or boost xxx seconds or boost for xxx meters (really shows how basic this game really is).Having to finish a cup with every single car, when there is only 4 cups and no reverse cup option. that's insanity.I have a feeling this game doesn't work 100% as it should on higher framerate.At 144hz v sync does fix issues with screen tearing. Some oddities still occur. In modes that require smashing into other cars, i can't damage anything.I also have problems with time trials. The game stopped adding my times or my ghost into the leaderboards. It doesn't even show that i have beaten the developer ghost. This bug occurred once i began doing the trials on reversed tracks.Be prepared for a set of stereotypical characters and obnoxious one liners.Info is also very poorly described or not explained properly.for example, Hotshot´s  take on difficulty is nothing more than the engine class used in Kart racers (50cc;100cc;200cc) without AI scaling.You might think this game is extremely challenging on expert due to rubber band, but its just faster.And with so many challenges, im surprised that you cant just check them in some info box whenever you select a vehicle for a race, you need to either open the customization or store and check which items are locked for each vehicle and what the challenges are.

You will never be able to establish a big lead against it. 2-3 cars will be close tailing you, no matter what you do. In one track not long before the finish I built up 4 (max) instances of boost and used them all one after another. And during the finish 2 cars were still tailing me a very short distance behind. There is no fair racing here. You can get left totally behind far away and thats not a problem, but getting a significant lead is impossible.The only viable way to play is stay slightly behind the first 2-3 cars, build up enough boost (by drifting during turns) and right before the finish use them to gain the lead. _childDocuments_.review: Arcade racing games have been a staple of my gaming career for some time now. I'm no stranger to what the likes of SEGA, Namco or other developers brought to the table. So when I followed Hotshot Racing, I just had to buy it on Steam. The flat shaded polygon aesthetic and Virtua Racing meets modern Ridge Racer game play were selling points to me. So, after clocking in a whopping thirty-four hours of play, how does Hotshot Racing fare?+ First of all, there's a ton of replay value involved. From a myriad of unlockables, to different game modes, local and online multiplayer, time attack leader boards, and a variety of achievements. Want to play cops and robbers in cars? This game has that. Ever wanted to simulate Keanu Reeves in the movie 'Speed'? There's a mode for that. Want to break a record and make the leader boards? There's that, too. This game will most certainly having you coming back for more.+ The gameplay and handling is easy for anyone to get into, yet it's hard to master. Expect to sink a lot of time in this game mastering the game's handling and boost system.+ There are eight characters with four cars each, all based off of real world cars while keeping a fictional design. The variety of each character's cars exists in one form or another. There's a car for everyone to choose from.+ This is a selling point for me, one of many. There's customization, all simple cosmetics, yet it's very deep at the core. Each character has a variety of accessories, skins palettes and other add-ons to unlock. On top of that, they can be mixed and matched. For example, one of Alexa's Palettes can go on Mike's cars, or Aston's palettes can go on Viktor's cars. You can even customize them to make them look like their real world counterparts. Or, in Keiko's case with the Eight Rock, make it look like Takumi Fujiwara's Toyota Sprinter Trueno; Initial D's mascot, as I call it. This is another feature that I sunk a lot of time into.+ The game actually gives you incentive to play on harder difficulty levels. From a variety of achievements to unlocks for characters and cars, there's a reason to play on harder difficulty levels.+ Again, the flat shaded polygon aesthetic gives it a classic arcade racing game feel. The various colors add to the look of the game. It's basically Virtua Racing all over again, and I like that a lot.+ The music is good and fits the arcade game feel. The composers did a good job here.+ The voice work is good, in spite of the game not being all story driven. The voice actors did a good job with their characters. I also like how they got Kira Buckland to be Alexa; Kira Buckland has a lot of roles--I'm sure some of you reading this review played Nier Automata, Danganronpa, Tales of Xilia, or Street Fighter V; or watched Kakegurui, Love Live!, Welcome to Demon School, Iruma-kun!, or Demon Slayer...- I'm getting this out of the way. That massive replay value? Most of it is farming and grinding for unlocks; and money to buy unlocks.Here's the gist: each of the cars have their own accessories, palettes and skins. However, they all must be unlocked. All of the cars have the same unlocks; boost a number of times in single race, drift for a period of time in a single race, boost a number of times, drift for a period of time, win a GP race, win a GP race on Expert, and the like. The majority of the unlocks can be done by doing a five lap race at Eight Ball Highway on arcade, which also unlocks a clown bobble head when doing this with every character. Then, spending twenty-three minutes and fifty seconds on Eight Ball Highway again--this time on time attack mode. Lastly, complete a GP race with each character's car, and mop up everything by beating staff ghosts, winning cops and robbers, and winning drive or explode. Expect at least ninteen hours of play time doing this to unlock all the accessories, skins and palettes. And that's not counting the time you'll be spending earning money, nor earning achievements.TL;DR, the time I spent on this game was mostly grinding.- The AI is also very dirty and aggressive--and they cheat, too, especially on Expert. The AI drivers will bash you in at the worst possible time, and bashing THEM in turns them into brick walls. Seriously, the AI is an incarnation of Forza Horizon online players, with their ramming antics and such. And the dreaded rubber band AI? It's here, too. Seriously? It's the year 2021 as of this review and this game has cheating, rubber band AI? I was hoping in this day and age for a smarter AI of sorts, instead of crutches and unfair advantages.Oh, and the AI also tends to make idiotic mistakes because of their cheating and aggression. I have seen the AI drivers drive so aggressively that they actually run into walls, even if they're on a straight line and there's no other cars near them. Again, this is on Expert.- The difficulty levels are technically a speed dial, yet the first two difficulties are situational. Normal is only for hunting achievements, Hard is if you're on GP mode and if you're in a slow car, and Expert is general purpose playing and earning certain unlocks. This is because Normal is slow as molasses, Hard is manageable, and Expert is stupid fast.- There are thirty-two cars in the game; eight characters with four cars each. Yet, only five of them are actually competitive. Marcus' Carbon almost monopolizes the leaderboards, with Xing's Sentinel, Keiko's Super F-90 and Eight Rock, and in certain cases Alexa's Diamondback standing a chance. You'll see other cars from other characters, if you're lucky. However, they're typically bottom feeder on the leader boards.In addition, some characters' cars have the same stats, like Alexa's Stallion and Viktor's Blade; as well as Xing's Sentinel, Keiko's Eight Rock, and Toshiro's Sky Road. Sometimes, the cars with the same stats perform differently. The Sky Road is slower than the Sentinel and the Eight Rock, based on my experience using these cars.Also, some cars have stats that lie to you. Xing's Alpha has a maxed speed rating, yet it feels slower than Marcus' Carbon and Keiko's Super F-90. And Mike's Athena and Eagle have heavy handling compared to other balanced and acceleration class cars, despite their stats.- You can select between an automatic and a manual transmission, but that's irrelevant here. For reference, Ridge Racer's manual transmission has benefits like rocket starts, and Daytona USA requires manual transmission due to power sliding via shifting. Hotshot Racing, on the other hand, it doesn't matter. Looking at the leader boards, some of the top times is more dependent on the car and not the transmission. Even speedrunners use automatic, something unheard of in the arcade racer time attack circuit.- All of the characters have a backstory of sorts. Yet, they're hardly touched upon. I understand this is an arcade racer and it's not supposed to be high art in storytelling. Yet, I'd like to know more about some of the characters. What injury did Marcus sustain for him to quit his athletics career? Who, or what, built Toshiro? What kind of hardship is Mike going through? All of this and more would be nice to know if there was a character database in the game.- Some songs, like the main menu theme, are not in the soundtrack. For some reason...Overall, do I recommend this game? Yes. It's not perfect, but it's better than a good portion of arcade racers on the market; much less Steam. In fact, next to GRIP, Horizon Chase Turbo and Distance this is one of my favorite arcade racers. There's lots of fun to be had, and the handling is easy to get into. However, there's lots of grinding involved, the meta game is imbalanced, and a little more lore could have been added. Still, it's a worthy purchase in my books.

_childDocuments_.review: Before I start raging: It's a great arcade style racing game, three difficulties (Normal, hard and EXPERT) and about 20 tracks and loads of cars, smooth, fast gameplay, excellent drifting (After you got used to it), but pretty basic. Fill your boost meter by drifting or slipstreaming, then use it a few times per race, that's it, no shortcuts, levelling up cars or much else.Overall a great arcade game, but a little short on the competitions, there's only 5 GP's of 4 tracks each, so if you come last in the first race, for example, it's pretty difficult to then finish top overall.Difficulty is fine, there's 3 skill levels and each GP is harder than the last. The person who said it's too easy is clearly lying and the one who said it's too difficult did say 'as usual' implying they're crap at games in general, so they can be safely ignored.The Problem is: The rubberbanding AI and you can clearly see this on "Normal". The difficulty basically only changes the game speed. Its your typical Mario kart 100CC / 150 CC / 200 CC thing where you just race way faster and the AI is taking shortcuts on "Expert" way better. The only way to win on normal is to hold your boosters onto the end and use them before the finish line. If you use 4 boosters - forget it. AI is right behind you anyways. I've played this game with my brother in co-op and whenever He was first place and used boosters, the AI flew to the first place like It's not even funny. Rubberbanding is a big problem here!The other thing the game really not need is straight sections / streets where left and right corners are built in (You'll see what I mean when you play it) and it feels like the game wants you to drift but these "corners built in" tkaes all the flow out of it just because they're like: "ahhh we don't want to implement another straight line - lets put in some extra corners or "S" lines. It feels "cheap" and the content is not that much. I've finished Normal cups (all 5) in 1 hour and there is no need to do the rest since multiplayer is also dead.The Price is also way too high (19,99€ for this). I got it for 2€ in a Fanatical Bundle and thats the right price to ask. I would go to 5€ or maybe 10€ MAX if you're a huge arcade fan - nothing more. Second player progress also not relevant. If First player isn't first - you won't get gold even if you (second player) are first place. Second / third / fourth player is irrelevant to progress which is.... ???Fun Game but these cons can't be ignored - especially rubberbanding.

_childDocuments_.review: I had some concerns, going in, over the infamous complaints of rubber-banding and overly aggressive A.I., which saw me scour the discussion boards for a more rounded view of the game, before making my own decision (much of this review is lifted from my edited reply, there). Came across numerous reports of semi-functional controller support, but wound up purchasing the game to see for myself, in the end.I can confirm, after playing for the better part of two hours, with the kids, that we had no issues with the game properly recognizing our Logitech gaming pads (2xF710 Wireless & 2xF310), which were plugged in prior to start-up, as ever; worth noting that these have a switch to toggle between both Xinput (the more common XBOX controller standard) and Direct (for older titles), where we mostly leave it on the former, as we done last night.Cheers to the developers, on a wonderful offering, and I can't wait for the planned updates (hopefully some verticality/jumps/obsticles/etc. for the existing tracks, or in all-new ones). Would be thrilled to get more game modes, but I was sold when I heard of the "Drive or Explode" and "Cops & Robbers" variants, if perhaps the latter were a tad underwhelming; was most looking forward to C&R, actually, but found it a bit skewed, in favour of robbers, as it seemed too difficult to catch them, especially for the kids—always groans, whenever the game decided you'd start as a cop.I also didn't find the A.I. all that aggressive, nor was the rubber-banding particularly bad, however, we played on the easiest setting (Normal), and had four local players, meaning four less bots. From what I've heard, they really become an issue as you increase the difficulty, so that would also be an area I'd welcome improvements on.Either way, I felt like there was plenty content, for what I paid (around half price, on sale, to be fair), and I highly recommend it, as the devs. seem committed to the cause of improving things, with time, and what you get, already, is more than enough to tie you over, in the interim.

Even though the arcade mode is default, the other modes are pretty fun, Drive or Explode and Barrel Barrage are probably the most fun i've had with friends.The attention to detail on this is absolutely crazy, each character has four cars unique to that character and they're all fun to play. _childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best retro-arcade racing games I ever tried, even throwing me back to my Daytona USA days with its vibrant and square-esque aesthetic while still feeling brand new, the soundtrack is nice but it isn't GREAT as we are used to in racing games, it certainly would benefit from the same style of music as Asphalt 8 (for example), being able to choose between 4 different genres of music.There are secret stats for each car that are not shown in the car's menu, the AI rubber-banding it's really awful but it's a great gameplay overall with its drift-and-boost mechanic being really polished and balanced (except for the fact of using all your boost in the final lap and getting a free win being a thing), 3 difficulties to choose from and many tracks, 4 styles to use in cars (velocity, acceleration, drifting and balanced), various camera angles, etc.As from the content in the game, getting plat is really difficult, but it is not a difficulty that comes to satisfy. The only thing to unlock are achievements and customization for the characters and cars, which ARE good but feel hollow to me for some reason. I'd like to get new characters and cars by advancing in the game, maybe in a new story mode or a greater campaign, the characters already have a personality, why not make them interact between them in a story?Overall, it's a great arcade game with not much to uncover and great (I mean really great) visuals which I've not seen in any recent game, it's a 8/10, greatly recommended.EDIToh and the gamepad being able to be re-binded would be a great addition =P

_childDocuments_.review: Often, I don't want to launch a heavy racing game and wait through multiple loading screens and slow menus just to start playing. I crave pure, simple arcade fun, accessible within a few menu clicks, and this game delivers just that. It has surprisingly weighty controls that you wouldn't expect from its arcade-like appearance. It's not your typical sliding-on-ice Ridge Racer physics but more methodical and weighty. The game offers a few different modes, challenges, customization options, and both local and online multiplayer. While the content isn't THAT vast, the base gameplay is so enjoyable that you don't mind the repetitiveness, especially in multiplayer.One thing I didn't enjoy at first was the visual appearance. Despite being detailed and colorful, it lacks a distinctive stylization beyond low-poly models. For example, games like Parking Garage Rally Circuit or Old School Rally have similar graphical fidelity but are much more appealing and eye-catching due to their retro aesthetics. However, this might just be my personal preference for such games. Overall, it's a really solid arcade racer with a full package at an affordable price.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, what an unexpected treasure.I found out about this game from a top 10 list on Whatculture Gaming and figured I would give it a go since it was on sale.  I am so happy that I did!I come from the days of San Francisco Rush and Cruis'n USA.  The N64 and Arcade racing era.  I had kind of fallen out of love with the simulation style racing games like Gran Turismo and Forza.  They just never kept my attention.However, this game feels nearly exactly like the old arcade racing games from my childhood.  From the announcer yelling out "CHECKPOINT!" to the amazing art style I can't say enough about how much of a blast from the past this is.Other "Pros" about the game are it's track selection.  Most tracks are short and sweet and you can mirror them.  The soundtrack is top notch.  Catchy and retro.  The voice overs from the in game characters are funny at times, especially Xing.  (He's my favorite)  Drifting feels GREAT.  I have never been big into drifting in racing games because I always felt like it could be a little to complex and take my mind off the rest of the action.  A tap of the break and you go into a very satisfying and controllable drift that helps you charge your boosts.  The grand prix and single race arcade modes are FULL of unlockables.  Over 700 to keep you busy and coming back.  There is a great variety of cars that changes with each character.  There are unlockables for the outside and inside of all the cars.  Each character has a funny cut scene for their grand prix wins.  There is also a variety of other modes like the newly added barrel blast and a cops and robbers mode.  Both of them equally fun.  I have NOT gotten into online mode yet so I cannot speak for it's quality.Some of the "Cons" for the game:There is a HEAVY amount of rubber banding in effect.  You will not be able to get a huge lead on the computer because they will rubber band every single race.  They also race extremely aggressive (which I happen to like in an arcade style racer, but some people do not.) They will "pit" you extremely often, but with practice on drifting it won't slow you down too much.Over all I would give this game a solid 8/10.  Certainly check it out if you are into retro style arcade racers.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a mixed bag. Arcade racing INDIE game? Unusual and commendable. I like the polygonal artstyle, makes it feel like an upscaled PS1 game, but the sharp polygonal corners look a bit jarring. The driving model is floaty at best, you're never in control of your car, the AI cars are borderline suicidal, they'll crash into you, T-bone you while drifting, it's a nightmare. It's not bad, but it looks and feels like a premium mobile game. It will run on low end hardware no problem, so if you have a potato PC, the AI drivers will make you feel like you're in a Forza Horizon lobby.

_childDocuments_.review: This is absolutely the arcade racer I've been looking for for the last decade or so.This game is absolutely awesome,  The physics play fast and loose in a true arcade manner that feels like arcade racing games from the 90s.  The game uses the same low-poly techniques to establish a feeling of intense speed, while minimizing required GPU power.   However, it still uses modern effects.I haven't yet played multiplayer, so I don't know if it has lag issues or not, but the AI is very fun, and aggressive. I suspect people who don't appreciate fast arcade racers, or get frustrated easily won't like the game.   I have to admit that I have to be in the right mood to enjoy this game, and I have to be at the top of my game. Those who want a realistic racing game should look elsewhere (if this isn't obvious enough). _childDocuments_.review: Hotshot Racing is great looking game marred by poor AI and poor mechanics. Hotshot Racing is about the graphics. The flat shaded polygons look fantastic with a Virtua Racing retro shine, but with far more geometry. There are some spectacular showpieces as well. The basic racing engine is good as well and gives you good control of the vehicles and real sense of speed. However, the game utterly falls flat in all other areas. Each character you play has multiple cars, but it doesn't matter which one you pick. The hyper aggressive AI will constantly rubberband its way up to your car, while also using basically psychic powers to boost when you boost, and try to spin you out. The boosting is limited, and feels boring. The drift mechanic is great, but pointless as it neither nets you enough boost or speed to be worth it.  Even if you nail a perfect drift, with a perfect boost, it's all ruined by a cheap AI. On top of this you have repetitive comments from your racer, and music that is all beat and no melody.  Bottom line: Once you stop admiring the graphics, this game lacks the polish to make you want to come back and play more. It's a frustrating experience. Grade: D-

_childDocuments_.review: Hotshot Racing has the potential to be a really great arcade racer, but it just falls short. It has multiple problems stemming from the physics, AI and boost system that hold it back. I have a video talking and showing the issues, but also for the sake of the Steam review, I also listed out the issues in written form below.One common complaint I saw was the amount of content at launch. A lot of the original game modes were scrapped, mostly likely due to their reliance on the weapons to make them function properly. This left the game with a lot less content than it was originally supposed to have. Due to this, the game had an anemic launch with only four tournaments and four gamemodes. Thankfully, it seems like we will be getting additional free updates to add more content, with the newest Big Boss update adding in a new tournament, a new gamemode and four new tracks.While Hotshot Racing’s tracks look amazing, their design is very lacking. All the tracks are very flat and way more simple than other arcade racers. I couldn’t understand this at first, but then it hit me: these maps were originally designed with the vehicular combat in mind. In a weaponized combat racer, it's better to have more flat and less complex tracks for the weapons to be usable. With the weapons now gone, it draws a lot more attention to the basic map design. While I don’t think they should change the tracks we have now, they should consider making more vertical and complex maps for the future.Something just doesn’t feel right with the vehicle handling in this game. I believe the issue mainly stems from the floaty driving physics. I noticed that when taking corners, my wheels would lift off the ground on relatively flat surfaces. This completely throws off the vehicle handling when it happens. While I feel like the vehicle handling and drifting mechanics itself needs to be worked on more, I would like to see how much better they would be if vehicles had way more downforce.Regarding the AI, they are WAY too combative. They hit, smash, and spin me like I’m playing a Burnout game. Seriously, I played vehicular combat games that have less aggressive AI than this. It wouldn’t be so bad if the collision physics were good, but they suck. Many times your car will lift off the ground when getting hit, causing the same vehicle handling problems I mentioned beforehand. Also, sometimes you don’t get affected at all and other times you are sent heading straight for a wall. For a game that demands perfect precision and control from the player, it’s out of control AI and terrible collision physics makes the racing way more frustrating than it should be.The rubberbanding is another huge problem. Rather than it being that hardcoded rubberbanding, where the AI increases their top speed to catch up, it seems to be moreso a problem stemming from how the boost system works. The boost works by giving you a huge increase of speed when you fill up one of the bars. The only way to get boost is either from drifting or slipstreaming other cars. It seems pretty standard, but the problem is when you pull out in front, you can’t slipstream any cars, meaning you can only get boost from drifting. This leaves you vulnerable in long straights as the AI behind you have been slipstreaming you or each other to build up enough boost to continually pass you. This also means that if you fall way behind, it can be extremely hard to catch back up. The game essentially encourages you not to get to the front but rather stay behind the leaders until the very end. This issue could be easily fixed by not giving boost from slipstreaming, but rather just giving enough of a speed boost to pass a player.Overall, Hotshot Racing is a mixed experience. I can’t not recommend it as all these issues combine to make Hotshot Racing a wildly inconsistent and frustrating experience. With more updates planned in the future, I hope one day I can say Hotshot Racing feels perfect, but it still got a long way to go.

_childDocuments_.review: What are negative reviews talking of? Rubberbanding generally in racing games is the effect of cars getting an advantage like a speed boost once they fall behind. Generally talking about racing game design of all racing games I have played in my life I remember two cases:  For me the rubberbanding is not a bad thing but a good thing, a feature of the game which enhances the gameplay experience! In Mario Kart they made the rubberbanding feature by giving players who fell behind get better items. In Hotshot Racing they realized rubberbanding with the slipstream mechanic. Every car has a slipstream behind it, a lack of air due to the car in front having pushed away the air. The slipstream is about 6 car lengths long and gives cars which directly follow the path a speed boost. This is physically correct, so the slipstreaming mechanic even makes the game more realistic! This means, that the pack can be faster together than a single car trying to increase the lead and set off. Grand Tour cycling know slipstreaming, seasonal moving birds know slipstreaming. It's part of the game and this rule is the same for all. Do bots cheat when they use slipstreaming? No, because this mechanic can be used by all in the same way. It's NOT like bots get a speed boost just because they fall behind or because they're bots. They get a speedboost because they use the slipstream which is part of the game and therefore fair.So is the gameplay like that #1 always changes?! Not necessarily, no, even though there is slipstream mechanic, you can set off off the pack and get in the far lead, even on the hardest difficulty setting.Difficulties can be compared to Mario Kart's 50cc 100cc 150cc (cylinder capacity) which gives the cars better motors. I have to say that the first two difficulty settings Normal=50cc and Hard=100cc are like the tutorial for the real game which is Expert mode=150cc. Expert mode feels like the game was designed with this speed in mind, but was too hard to get into from the start so they made slower modes before it.People complain that nothing of your skill matters, but only the last round due to rubber banding. They probably haven't played any one round in Expert mode. I couldn't keep up with the pack on Expert and didn't even reach the last lap before I learned the mechanics of this game better. Knowledge and skill definitely matter very much here! The essential mechanic in this game is drifting. It is made SO good! Feels super good to drift in the cars. Use the handbreak to get into a drift. Or if you turn too much with too much speed you get into a drift. Again, this is realistic. Also every car has different drift parameters where you really notice and feel that this car behaves different and this is enhaces the game experience! Every car can use boost once the meter is filled enough. The boost meter fills with drifting and using slipstream. So using these mechanics is rewarded. Drifting makes you slower slightly since you are basically braking with your rubber tyres (and the handbreak), but you can cut corners better with it, so it has a use of its own besides the boost meter filling. Still drifting is rewarded with boost meter, which makes drifting essentially important in this game. These are simple but ingenious game design choices in my view. Further crashing into the sides of the track is punished by losing boost meter depending on the amount of deceleration of the crash, so there is no exploiting track sides for a better time like in Need For Speed. Again, very clever in my opinion. This game is designed so that playing skillful is the best way to win and this is a big positive in my book. Speaking of good game design there is also the checkpoints, which not only serve as a time comparison, but give you more time until your timer runs out. No worries, the timer on you is not stressful or limiting the fun. Checkpoint timers ensure you cannot fall endlessly behind making you feel awfully lost alone at the end. They are an indicator for that if you keep falling behind too much, you should consider first getting better on the lower difficulty modes.Every race track has its own music track!I loved this game from the start to finish for its over the top characters and interesting gameplay mechanics. I 100%ed it in 25 hours. Only negatives I can think of is that there are no risk/reward shortcuts like other fun racers have them and that the last two achievements take a grind of several hours to get, but that is just nitpicking. Very recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: Such a missed opportunity in my opinion.I will admit though, it doesn't try to be what I hoped to find. Sure, there are things that would lead you to think SCUD Race, but in the end it claims early 90ties, so Ridge Racer & SCUD Race are not the games they strived to bring back. Doesn't change what I think about the game, but it changes what expecteations one should have. So. What would be early 90ties? Maybe Stunts, Outrun & Lotus Challenge or such where track design was mostly just some random corners. Not sure how well Virtua Racing fits as I never played it and am therefore not sure if track design was as much of a thing as in the later Daytona USA or SCUD Race. The only games I remember bringing up drivers would be Outrunners and Slipstream 5000, so that's quite a rare and cool feature.But first, let me shortly catch what I loved about arcade racers and what no arcade racer since Ridge Racer V ever got right. What made the all time greats great was:Easy to get into, hard to master handling.Sublime atmosphere and design, often accompanied with great music.Track design that was fine-tuned to be a puzzle to be solved by understanding the mechanics of driving - at first easy, later on you'd need to understand the mechanical depth each title offered (best examples are: Rage Racer, SCUD Race/SuperGT, Ridge Racer V).So with this game it's incredibly frustrating, because it starts off with banger music (probably not to everyones liking, but it fits so well and takes a nose dive into oldschool racing game soundtracks), stunning visuals that haven't been seen since the early voxel racers. A short shoutout to awful stereotypes just for the giggles. It's stupid, but that's good for a giggle.Then the gameplay is good fun although it's the old problem that nearly all boost games have: If no boost, you jug along as if this was a sunday drive, not a race. But then again, in time trial you start off with full boost and chaining them properly means you blast along for the full race course. That is good fun. So it's a bit simple, but many new arcade racers couldn't hold their audience as they were too hard, even if rather easy compared to the old arcade racers they were inspired by (think Xenon Racer). So - fair enough, let's have a more approachable game and enjoy the fun.After a few laps on various time trials, another feeling creeps in: This isn't an oldschool arcade racer as promoted, it's more akin to Horizon Chase. Corners are for gaining boost, not because the course is designed for the cars that we race. So: track design is bad. It has some nice throwbacks in the design, but the track layout is just some corners that lead to a circuit. Not sure if there was many though behind it other than: this should look okay, put an obstacle here and be done. That's why it's so close to Horizon Chase with better graphics, better atmosphere, smoother gameplay. While that could be fun, let's come to the last point.The AI drivers. No care in the world for winning. Not even on normal. Absolutely hell bent on crashing you. Yes, you can catch certain bumps. But there is no clean racing. Ever. It's more of a fun bump around until one lands in the barrier. This last part is a deal breaker. One could have still enjoyed a rather simplistic game with bad track design, but getting dive bombed all the time is just not interesting. Maybe people who like Mario Kart will like it, but I certainly don't.Now. Does that mean that you might enjoy it? Yeah, sure. It's just not for me and I wouldn't recommend it to anyone.I appreciate the design, the music, the car variety with the various handling styles and some fun on the Time Attack. The slipstream mechanic is rather neat to counter the boost mechanic and can feel awesome. But in the end it has too much variety, so it didn't have time to develop the things that actually make arcade racers great: depth in driving mechanics and depth in track design. Opponents can just be around to give you a certain time that you need to reach. I need noone to fight with me or bump into my car. Sure it's exciting and a great randomizer so you can't always win. But as it goes with randomness: it's also frustrating and unfair.So overall: Nice work, but lacks the essential depth that old classics had.

_childDocuments_.review: The first thing you will notice are distinct and colourful low-poly visuals which make each of the 20 tracks stand out. They are spread out in four exotic places - coast, desert, jungle and mountain - with five tracks for each. There is always something happening outside the track, but most of the time you drive too fast to see all the intricate details. A smoking volcano on the picturesque coast, a train driving around the track, speeding through an airplane cemetery in the desert… I genuinely think tracks might be the true stars of this game.It doesn't matter which driver you choose. There are eight of them, and they're just a caricature of the country they come from anyway. You have your British James Bond, Russian tough guy, American cutie, etc. Each driver has four cars with different stats: balanced, acceleration, speed and drift. Although the cars are not licensed, their nickname and unique design will look familiar to any car enthusiast. Staying true to its arcade roots, an ordinary car can still go toe to toe with a formula 1 car.While cars and drivers can be customised, everything is purely cosmetic. Moreover, selection is quite poor. Since the best things like car skins and driver suits are locked behind objectives (drift 250 seconds in this car, win this race…), you're stuck with only two or three options. Money for enhancements can be won in races. Game modes you can choose from are Grand Prix – the game's single player mode, Time Trial and Single Race which include races like arcade – racing against time, Cops & Robbers – chasing cars or escaping the police, Barrel Barrage – destroying opponents with explosive barrels, and Drive or Explode – racing the checkpoints before the car blows up. Sadly, the single mode is just too short. Driving couldn't be easier. All you have to do is keep your finger on the throttle and drift the corners. Drifting is actually the most important thing and generally the reason why you can't win a single race. Better learn it fast if you want to get somewhere. The goal is to maintain good speed in corners by holding left or right while tapping the brake which puts you in the drift mode.Nice thing about it is that you can still adjust by adding or releasing the throttle in order to come out of the corner with as much speed as you can. It's pretty easy with the first set of tracks where there's only one corner to worry about, but a totally different story when the turns come one after the other. You don't always have time to go from one drift to another and you have to remember every corner on the track. This is not a big problem as the tracks are less than a minute long and only last three laps.The other important element of winning is the boost. The boost bar is filled by chaining drifts and driving behind other drivers, and there's one freebie if you start the race by keeping your throttle within the yellow lines. Miss it and your car will stay put with black smoke coming out of it. But even if you make a mistake, the run is still salvageable on normal and hard difficulty. Play on the expert, however, and you've already lost the race. The reason lies in rubberbanding – a mechanic used in racing games to keep them intense, even on lower difficulties. I don't mind them when done right, but this game is downright brutal. Even on normal and with perfect driving, each race would've ended in defeat if I hadn't saved one last boost. Expert borders on cheating; enter the corner a bit late and you're already done. Rubberbanding apparently doesn't work when you're the one in the last place. Due to the reason mentioned above, I can only barely recommend the game. The Grand Prix is fun while it lasts and the other modes give you a few laps of enjoyment, but that's about it. Doing it all over again on higher difficulty is just frustrating and unfair.   Rating: 6/10Reviewed by:

_childDocuments_.review: Y'know how when you'd play a racing game with your little brother, and you'd be winning, and because he wasn't very good, he'd just slam you off the track over and over? Yeah, that's this game's AI. It's godawful. It's fun, but it feels more like a early access game than a finished polished product.It doesn't scale properly to high resolutions, rubber-banding is the only way the "AI" scales in difficulty as far as I can tell, there are a lack of settings and in general it needs some QoL improvements before I can say it's worth the 30$ AUD price point. This is one of those times when I feel a "mixed" review choice existed, as it is very much so. As it is, I would say $15-20 AUD would be a far more fair price for what you get.(The dev response doesn't change anything, I feel my review is still representative of the state of the game.)

_childDocuments_.review: It's a charming little throwback arcade racer with a lot of personality, and I haven't experienced any of the graphics or controller issues that a lot of others are complaining about, but there's nothing really special or unique about the gameplay and amount of rubberbanding is ridiculous. I don't mind a bit of rubberbanding but the way that the game significantly slows down any cars that pulls into the lead coupled with the way that you gain boost meter by driving behind cars means the game actually penalises you for playing well and staying in the lead. This also makes the Cops and Robbers and Drive or Explode modes unfairly difficult as it means you'll be constantly rammed from behind by the AI. There's some nice variety to the tracks but only in terms of scenery, once you get over the dinosaurs and UFO's and stuff in the backround they get very dull very fast.It's still not an altogether awful game, but I can't recommend it as there are plenty of much better retro style racing games than can be bought for less.

_childDocuments_.review: Hotshot Racing is an indie racing game and a really good surprise. I was browsing my library for something to play, picked this, and had a much better time than I had anticipated. The concept is simple : arcade races on short tracks with a big emphasis on drifting. You get boost by slipstreaming or drifting, and your job is to finish first. Pick a racer, a car, and get going !You'll immediately notice the colorful 90's esthetics the game went for, and it works really well. The twenty available tracks, split into four environments (seaside, mountain, desert, jungle), are varied and different enough to never feel repetitive or boring.Drifting is at the heart of the gameplay. This is not Ridge Racer, but you will be drifting half the time while trying to find the better spot to use your boost. Using it wisely, knowing the tracks and knowing your car will be essential to win on Expert difficulty, as the AI will offer a real challenge. On easier difficulties, the game will show some of the nastiest rubberbanding I've ever seen. I don't like it and I don't think that's ever a good idea, but it makes for more disputed races while you learn the basics of the game, and will keep you on your toes if you already know what you're doing.Outside of the Grand Prix, Single Race and Time Trial modes, there are also a few variants where you have to watch your car's health while racing and the more classic Cops and Robbers that can all be fun in multiplayer online, or with friends in split-screen. Winning, and even just playing will reward you with money that you can spend on customization options that you unlock by racing in the car of your choosing. With 8 characters, each associated with 4 different cars... That's a lot of cars to learn and find a favorite if you get into it ! The tuning doesn't affect your car's performance, so you can just gloss over it if that's not your thing, but there are many options and I found it really fun to just tinker with the looks of your ride before a race. It's something that is not mandatory in that kind of racing game but really adds a lot when it is available.Another nice thing to note is that the Dlc that added 4 tracks and a new mode was free. Yes, free, that still exists and it feels really nice when you're already loving the base game.Once you're done competing with the AI, you can turn to a Time Trial mode that is really smartly handled as it lets you race without stopping and refills your boost every lap, for a non-ending "One more, I'll beat it this time" and compete for the online leaderboards that are, as far as I can tell, devoid of any cheaters or fake times. Engaging !The only thing missing, really, would be a track editor as this kind of game would be perfect for it. But that's nitpicking at this point.The soundtrack, which is more of a background beat, is pleasant and fitting for the races and accelerates on the last lap for added pressure. Your character will also often make quips as things happen in the race, making it even more lively. The only issue that I've had with the game was some short but annoying lag spikes that I was able to fix after looking up online for a solution. After creating a profile for the game in the Nvidia Control Panel, turn Vsync on and set the Max Framerate to 60. This got rid of most of the lag for me, hopefully this works for you as well.Hotshot racing is not a game you will spend forever on, but you can easily have a lot of fun for 10 to 12 hours, and a lot more if you start going for perfect lap times or want to unlock everything. Looking for some arcade racing ? If you don't mind an indie look and some drifting, you can't go wrong with this. A really fun , for a game that has everything you can hope for in an indie arcade racer, and then some !

_childDocuments_.review: This is everything I missed about games like Rush 2, California Speed, and Daytona. It needs some re-optimization, particularly when it comes to switching between parts on the cars. Game would benefit from Cross Platform Play, a course editor, and better push to talk for VoIP. That said, this game is a blast to play.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to like this game I really do.  The artstyle and overall idea is fun.  I always enjoyed the more arcade based racers of the past.  The Ai is just so bad though.They are very clearly hard coded to rubber band like crazy in the first two laps to force you to compete for top 3.  Then the last lap they tend to drop off to pretty much let you win by a narrow margin.  Which you would think makes for fun racing but any exciting finish feels pointless when you know the game is just letting it happen.  Not because you raced well but because the final section you did a passable enough job.Also the Ai is just overly aggressive with eachother and the player.  The amount of times they have put me into a wall with a big push is pretty absurd.  It helps less that the game clearly knows this with collisions that prefer to shove cars past eachother rather than doing to much interference.So this game can be fun but the AI truely ruin it.  Just use a maxed out speed car and go down a straight even while boosting.  A handling car will easily keep up or pass you with 4 or 5 less top speed than you.  It is pretty stupid.Update: After beating 3 of the cups on expert mode my opinion still does not change.  The rubber banding works more in your favor at this level as some bad clips on the wall wont ruin your race.  But the AI are still way to happy to put you into a wall in the middle of a race.  This isn't even a one off thing either it seems to happen at least once per race series where an AI suddenly flings across the track and hits me or turns into the rear of my car and puts me into a wall.Also it might just be me but handling cars seem pointless.  Their top speed is to low to get any kind of good time out of.  For all my expert wins I just used the F-1 (whatever they call it in this game) car due to having high speed and acceleration which is honestly all that seems to matter.

Here is a select quote from the critique:"Hotshot Racing is a decent attempt at offering the kind of arcade racing experience that we don’t really get anymore and, if you’re pining for that sort of game, you may well find enjoyment in it. _childDocuments_.review: Not recommended. While it looks like Virtua Racing, the game comes nowhere near it when it comes to playability. Some bad points that make this game not a lot of fun for more than 30 minutes:- AI racers crash in you from behind, instead of trying to overtake. - World physics do not seem to apply to AI. They can overtake corners in full-speed without problem, and recover from crashes instantly.- The only way to take corners is by drifting. If you steer normally you will have to reduce speed so much, you will be overtaken by every AI car and will lose every race.- AI is always just behind you. You cannot outrun AI cars in this game.- Just 20 tracks.- Game is considered 'finished' by the publisher, so any issues or glitches will never be fixed.Basically: just get this on sale or in a bundle (which will most likely happen within the year after release), but do not expect to get more than 30 minutes playtime out of it.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT EDIT: I have now proceeded to change the rating to positive. The game's still a bit shallow and the controller's still un-remapable but... It works well enough with a switch controller and binding things on Steam. I still cannot use manual transmission tho.This is definitely much more worth your money than Virtua Racing for the NSWEDIT: Still will not reccomend on the basis of some questionable physics, and the pain the default controls produce. Would otherwise reccomend. I wish steam had a neutral button.Hotshot racing is an alright game. Honestly, if you were to compare it to something like the Switch port of Virtua Racing, you're definitely getting a lot more for your money. The game modes are alright and so far the online is somewhat alive, and there's a healthy challenge on the leaderboards to keep you busy, the 16 tracks are nice, people seem to complain because they reuse the same setting, but frankly i find that to be fine, i grew up with SNES mario Kart, where you'd have like 25 circuits and you'd have 5 variants of the same 5 track themes. So they're ok.Cops and Robbers isn't... amazing, but it's better than not having any extra game modes.I particularly don't like how the customization does not add nothing to your car's handling or speed stats. It feels like it was a missed opportunity, some of my favorite designs are balanced or drift category and they aren't really fun to use in higher difficulties.Speaking of that, i find the dificulty spikes to be very strange, with the rubberbanding on the hardest difficulty to be insane. It doesn't matter how much you manage your turbo, as soon as you finish a turn you'll have 3 cars turboing past you, making you crash into a wall and literally killing all your progress. That, if they don't position tehmselves in a way that prevents you from turning and you end up eating a roadblock, to the same result.You'd think needing to fight against the checkpoints would be enough, but nope.On top of that, you also get the issues i mentioned earlier with the default controller scheme. not really fun to play without hurting yourself, and the only alternative only makes things slightly better at the cost of broken menus.Honestly, if you take this like an old school arcade quarter muncher and just play like, once or twice every weekend, trying to do one or all cups in one sitting, yeah it's nice, but that's mostly about it. The controls are good and the gampleay is snappy and polished, so there is that.If i could reccomend this on a scale between 0 and 10, where 0 is "absolutely would not recommend", and 10 is "why aren't you buying this already", this would land squarely at a 5, not in the 0-4 range, not in the 6-10 range.Following is the original review i made on the day i purchased the game, and the subsequent edits i made during the following weekend, for preservation's sake:There may be a good game behind this. But i need to use paddles for gearshifting and i need to accelerate with A.There are no remappable buttons, so i literally cannot play the game. And i honestly cannot handle drift/boost/gear-change all with my left hand while my right hand is busy with accelerating and steering all using a keyboard.I can't even say how good or bad the gameplay is because i literally can't play it.Not reccomended.Let's hope the developers at Sumo Digital read this and patch it in an updateI have to make an addendum: The default layout is defintiely not like most arcade racers, and for me personally, is laid out in a way, that no matter what i do, i get hurt. I literally cannot play a game that actively tries to hurt me via awful design.It's 2020, every major game lets you remap controls, Even crash team racing on consoles has accelerate on X/A/B ( depending of your console ).EDIT 1: I'm playing some more using a mangled steam controller layout. It still hurts and i got to use the keyboard on menus, but it's something. So far i'm doing some practice laps, but i'll give more in-depth info once i play more of the game, rather than time trials.

_childDocuments_.review: Hotshot Racing, with its deliberate low-poly 3D look and plenty of fast cars and arcade action (both drifting and nitro) is a retro-style racing game that is a lot of fun, but the high rubber-banding makes for a sometimes frustrating experience. You can choose from a wide variety of drivers, each with a unique combination of cars with different ratings in speed, agility, drifting, and so on. The vehicles vary from rally classics to modern hypercars to even open-wheel racers.  And you can choose to race in first, third, or other camera angles. Add to that a large variety of courses, which can also be raced in reverse, and multiple difficulty levels, you will be going around these tracks for a while. And you will need to as the winning generates money, which is used to buy a lot of cosmetic unlocks to customize your vehicles. Modify the grill, the wing, the stripes, and so on. The AI is generally quite competitive but there's a strong rubber-banding in play, where the game will give a bit of boost to the slowest vehicles so the competition feels tighter. This can be a bit of problem if you're not a super-consistent driver where a slight mistake in final lap would mean you suddenly end up dead last. The different cars do feel different with different levels of under or oversteer, and different acceleration curve. So you need to compensate for different tracks, as well as learn the optimum place to use your nitro. All in all,  this is an arcade racer with its own aesthetics that is exciting to play,

_childDocuments_.review: I've seen a number of reviews saying the following:No reverse, color palettes limited for each car to each driver's palette selection, cannot drift two consecutive turns, poor controller support, and bad voice actingWell, there's reverse, you can use any driver's color palette on any car (there's even a special palette section with solid colors), you  can drift as many turns as you want as long as you're going fast enough and the car is capable of it, my 360 controller worked with no issues, and the voice acting is spot on for this kind of game; it doesn't take itself seriously, and some of the drivers lean heavily on pop culture references.This is a fun game, well worth the $20, and plays/looks better than an emulated Sega Rally or Daytona.

_childDocuments_.review: I know I'm going to sound a bit hyperbolic when I say this, but I honestly feel like this is pretty much the best arcade racer released in the last ten years.Okay, let me take a step back and explain.  is clearly descended from the old Sega arcade cabinets of the 90s, mostly  in terms of aesthetics, but you could argue at least some  influence and even some .The controls are mostly alright; however, as an XBox controller player, I wish they'd move the gear shift buttons from the bumpers to the face buttons. That minor issue aside, the game controls  well, with all of the vehicles feeling responsive and unique.The track details are admittedly a bit sparse; but each track really does feel like its own locale, even when most of them overlap with other circuits. The sense of speed is also there: I'm an  veteran, and I'll tell you that tackling the "Drive or Explode" mode can get  intense if you run it on a higher difficulty and/or for greater numbers of laps.There is a pretty decent amount of car customization on offer here; however, despite things like spoilers and engine blowers being able to be added or changed around, none of these customizations actually effect performance, which is a bit of a lost opportunity here. If you've played , you'll remember how important car customization was in that game for being able to beat your opponents;  doesn't have any performance altering effects available.The only other complaint I'd have would be the soundtrack. I know the aesthetic they're going for, and the music fits with that aesthetic; it just doesn't suit  style, but then my style of racing music is basically  or , so take what I say with a grain of salt.For the record, I nominated this game in the 2020 Steam Awards for "Outstanding Visual Style", because it was nice having a game with a clean and bright aesthetic like this. The cars all look great, if slightly blocky, and the myriad number of color palettes and skin combinations allow you to make your ride really stand out. In general, this is a fast, fun, simple arcade racer that goes back to basics and . I give  a 9 out of 10.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR:+ Really fun party game (when i say party I mean at least 3-4 people), very beginner friendly.+ The quality of the game is great, maps are fun, races feel intense.- Gets repetitive after some time because customization is limited to cosmetics. (GET IT DURING A SALE)---On the store page at the time of writing this review, the game is rated "mostly positive" but when you scroll down to actual reviews, they get pretty confusing because people disliking the game do it for petty reasons, and those who are praising it are often also including paragraphs of negative feedback.The reason?This game is amazing to play with friends, provided you grab it during a sale. This is probably the cheapest game in my library (winter sale) and I have gifted it to all my friends after trying it out because I just knew that this is an amazing party game, and I havent even bothered to check out single-player stuff (which is where most of the criticism comes from). People complaining about always-online drm? I support you but this is not the kind of game you'd enjoy as a single player experience for more than maybe an hour. Thats like saying MMOs are bad because they are designed for multiplayer.Don't expect online gameplay with randoms because servers are dead. The game is not particularly at fault here, the game was previously review-bombed to hell so I wasn't surprised to find this out. Gather a party and grab a few copies during a sale, and enjoy 5-10 hours of fun!

_childDocuments_.review: My Video Review can be found here:Have devs of HotShot racing delivered us a good arcade racing game that could be compared to the legends of the genre? I would say yes. It has many pros like the atmosphere full of adrenaline, sense of speed, good track design with variable environment, challenging difficulty, responsive control, nice graphics, great soundtrack and split screen multiplayer for up to four players! On the negative side are the absence of proper career mode, low effect of car statistics, sometimes irritating rubber band effect and maybe the lack of innovations. Thanks to the simple controls and fairly set levels of difficulty I can recommend the game for the whole family - especially with the local splitscreen multiplayer.Pros:- atmosphere- sense of speed- track design- challenging yet not frustrating- controls- graphics- soundtrack- split screen multiplayerCons:- no career mode- small effect of car statistics- rubber band effect- lack of innovationsIn general, I have been satisfied with the fun that HotShot racing delivered and thus I am giving it Thumbs Up and VideoGaming Father’s Index 8 out of 10 - recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: HOTSHOT RACING - A BLAST FROM THE PAST!Way back in early 2016, bloody four years ago, I was obsessed with old 90s arcade racing games, particularly SEGA's Daytona USA and its sequel. It was a rare chance to play these games as the only place I could play them was at my local movie theatre, but when I got my hands on that steering wheel, I felt like an actual racer going at ridiculous speeds and jamming out to cheesy 90s fast pace music. But one day, I stumped on a trailer for the Pre-Alpha build of Racing Apex and my mind was blown! The absolute hype that I had for this game was indescribable, It look like a proper spiritual successor to those old timeless arcade classics. So I waited and waited...and waited for it to finally arrive, but I started to lose hope on the project, that is until 6 months ago, they announced Hotshot Racing and I was back on the hype train. I preordered the game right when sales went live and played it on day on. My expectations were high, and they delivered!!PROS: Points that really shine through the game and great additions.GAMEPLAY - Firstly, the racing itself is phenomenal. It is an arcade racer, no doubt! It feels like you are playing those old SEGA arcade machines. There are many game modes to choose from:GRAND PRIX - The campaign which can be played both in single player and with a friend, has four GPs with four tracks each, three cups can be won for each difficulty so 12 GPs.ARCADE - The standard single race mode, both in single and local multiplayer for up to four locally. You have access to all the tracks, changeable laps, AI difficulty and management, etc.COPS AND ROBBERS - An infection type game mode where the cops have to stop robbers for getting as much money as possible before completing a race. Cops can aim for the most wanted robbers (Who have the highest amount of money) to takedown and steal their money from them.  Whoever has the most money at the end of the race or when everyone is a cop, wins the game.DRIVE OR EXPLODE - A high speed, chaotic mode where players have to stay above the speed limit or they will explode. Every player has a health bar that can be reduced by knocking into opponents or when you are not fast enough, causing your health to slowly deteriorate. Checkpoints offer health back to players, but also increase the speed. First to cross the finish line or the last player standing wins the game. TIME TRIAL - Beat the staff ghosts time or try your best against other players from around the world. A racing game essential.The physics are beautiful, not only is the steering and drifting perfectly adjusted, but it also gives the sense that every car has its own unique weight and feel. The drifting takes a tad bit to get use to, but once you get the hang of it, you will feel like a drifting king when taking those sharp turns. The game also has a boost system, that's charged by drifting and slipstreaming opponents. There is also an automatic and manual option for each car, for those who are use to pulling off the gear shift in Daytona. The gameplay here is fantastic and solidifies the old feeling of arcade racers from the 90s.PRESENTATION (GRAPHICS AND MUSIC) - The design of the game itself truly brings the 90s back from the dead and into the modern age, with polygonal graphics making up the cars, characters and the world itself. Everything here is bright and colourful and has many small, but defining details. Cars look and sound amazing when racing and the eight playable characters all have cheesy banter to themselves and to other drivers, kinda like Mario Kart. The music is on a whole new level, every track has its own distinct theme and they all totally kick ass! The music adds another level of thrill and detail in the gameplay that makes every race feel exciting, chaotic and most importantly, FAST!AI - Now when reading reviews of people who haven't played the game for a whole hour complain about the AI in this game, it really gets me going,. Because what Lucky Mountain Games have done with the AI here is great. The major complaint is the fact that there is a lot of rubber banding, which is true. However, I would like to believe that the developers did this on purpose to have more exciting races. Ask yourself this, would you rather have a hectic race filled with bumper to bumper action for the whole duration, fighting to cross that finish line first, or have a quiet ride by yourself ahead of the pack with no chaos, no action and no sense of achievement? Well I don't know about you, but I'm more of a fun guy myself so I'm gonna go with the first option here. The AI really give you a sense of action and adrenaline when racing, bumping into you, trying to spin you out, boosting ahead, etc. Everything that the AI does in the game is to give you a challenge (especially on expert difficulty) and more importantly, give you an action filled, yet enjoyable racing experience, which is the whole point of an arcade racing game.TRACKS - The track designs are done well here. There are 16 unique tracks split into four regions: Coast, Desert, Jungle and Mountain. All the tracks add their own flair and set pieces and show off the regional location its based in, giving drivers the chance to race through volcanoes, casinos, castles, a junkyard, a city, temples, etc. The tracks themselves have great atmospheres and have great turns and straightaways for boosting and slipstreaming opponents.CUSTOMISATION - The game offers a huge amount of customisation for each of the 32 cars to chose from as well as giving different outfits to the eight characters. For the cars, you can choose different spoilers, hoods, front and rear bumpers, headlight, colour palettes, car skins, interior designs like steering wheels and dashboards, bobbleheads and so much more. There are over 700 of these custom items and parts to buy from in game currency that you win from racing. CONS: Stuff that should you consider before buyingONLINE - This may change as more people buy the game, but there isn't much of a strong online presence with this game, which is a total shame. The online does run smoothly and has all the modes available (minus Grand Prix and Time Trial), Player hosted servers with essential race management (change laps, AI difficulty and track select), Hell, there is also a Ranked Mode for online! Hopefully people start to go online as there is great potential for online mode.PERFORMANCE - I run this game on the highest graphics option and it does run at 60FPS, but it does have these micro stutters that don't really affect the game, but can be annoying to deal with and get use to. This can be fixed easily I can imagine, so hopefully somewhere soon down the line, they can fix the issue.NOT ENOUGH TRACKS/LENGTH OF TRACKS - I do love the tracks in this game, but I do wish that there were more, which is happening in a free update. But what i'm mainly talking about is the track length. Each track length on average for me is around 1:20 to 2:00 minutes, which is great for short/medium tracks, but I would love to see some bigger tracks that go on for around 3:00 to even 4:00 Minutes. Maybe future updates can bring more tracks with longer lengths to the table, but it's not a big deal.OVERALL: 9/10Hotshot Racing brings the 90s arcade experience back like never before. The game truly does live up to its expectations and really does shine though as an awesome racing game, inspired by the 90s in every way possible. It controls amazingly, there are many modes to choose from, with more on the way, It looks and sounds beautiful, the AI give you a great challenge, tons of customisation, well designed tracks and cars and overall, Hotshot Racing pays homage to the timeless classics that were brought into the world 30 years ago. I hope you at least give this game a try to see how you feel about it, but once you start that first race, you won't regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: While I like the overall idea, the graphics and sound design, two major flaws ruin the experience for me:1) Frame times are wonky. The game is not at all graphicly demanding, but no matter if VSync off and 300fps or VSync on, it's still stuttery and doesn't feel smooth at all.2) The AI is terrible. It's rubberbanding a.f. (clearly not following the same driving physics as you do) and way too aggressive. Irrespective of how good you are driving, they will always catch up and bump you into obstacles and off the road while they barely ever lose traction or speed.

_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: got 1st place on 3 races in an expert difficulty grand prix and then on the last race, on the last lap, i got rammed into a wall twice i hate thisOk, actual review:It's a decently fun arcade racer, but it has a few flaws.First off, the difficulty setting doesn't just change the AI difficulty but also the top speed that everyone can drive at. Personally, I wish these were seperate settings, because sometimes I want to drive really fast against bad AI.Secondly, the rubberbanding in this game is bonkers. I only remember a single race where I've had a 2+ second lead by the time I hit the finish line. This also makes it so the best strategy is to stay close to 1st place and building nitro by slipstreaming. Then, on the last lap, you use up all the nitro to build up a lead right before the finish line. That being said, it does also make the game decently challenging, so it's also kinda an upside.Third, drifting and braking are both bound to the same button and you cannot have them seperately. I'm very used to using the S key to reverse and Spacebar to use the handbrake, but in this game, I use Spacebar to do both. I wish I could either bind both S and Spacebar to that function or have both functions be on separate keys.Fourth, I wish there was more content. The game has an alright amount of content for its price, but I wish there was more customization, tracks, cars, characters, modes and so on. I'd be down to pay for some DLC.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really great, with one glaring flaw that prevents me from recommending it. Until you notice this flaw, you will be having the time of your life, and after you notice, all enjoyment is sucked out of the game.The slipstream.It gives you so much speed and works from such long range that it creates a super strong rubber banding effect. There's no point to being in front, as everyone else can just catch up to you in no time. There's no point to use a boost, as everyone behind you can steal your speed. There's no point in even trying to be fast as nothing you do matters until the very end.This effectively means that the best strategy to win is to race meaninglessly with the rest of the pack for 2 laps and a half while saving boosts, and then pop them all at the end to get first right before the finish.There's also a distinct lack of a risk-reward loop. Once you get a feel for the game's handling, there's nothing to really do besides drift corners, as the tracks are so wide that you can pretty much co-exist with other drivers.If this one issue were fixed, I would recommend this game, but as it stands it's a no from me.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: A good arcade racer with some weird design decisionsLikes:I love the whole retro arcade vibe. From the clean untextured graphics, to the catchy music and the overenthusiastic announcer. It captures the aesthetics of a 90's era Sega cabinet perfectly.The driving itself is very intuitive. I play with a gamepad and never had to lookup the controls. Right trigger to accelerate, left trigger brake/drift, and A to boost. You gain boost by drifting and lose boost by crashing into things. Boost can be activated once your boost meter reaches a certain threshold.This is a interesting system, especially in time-trial (my favorite mode) where optimizing your boost usage becomes extremely important in order to do well.Dislikes:The global leaderboard for time-trial only shows the top 10. Come on guys, everyone (including me) wants to know their global rank. Improving your global rank is one of the main motivators when trying to improve your times.There is no replay feature in time-trial, whereas there is one for normal races... why?There are several characters in the game, each have 4 unique cars. But it seems like one specific car from one specific character is the outright fastest, making all the other cars and characters essentially useless.Racing and time-trial use a different driving model, so the skills you build up in one mode don't translate one-to-one to another mode. A baffling design decision. Overall:Whether you will enjoy this game depends on your expectations. The gameplay is fine. Personally I don't care too much about racing others, either AI or online. I prefer to race my ghost and try and set the best lap time possible, and for that the game (barely) works well enough. In combination with the overall look I would give it a 7/10.However the game is quite light in overall content/features, so maybe wait for a sale or some future updates.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: Would be a fantastic game if it wasn't broken. How can I be averaging 600+fps, but have stutters that slow the game to less than 1 fps??? I WANT to like this game, I mostly enjoy the time between stutters immensely, but multiple times per race, it's very frustrating.Also the AI have a tendency to PITT you, which is not fun, but it would be easier to deal with if the game ran properly.I've tried lowering the settings, I've tried capping the frame rate, I've tried v-sync on and off, nothing helps.

_childDocuments_.review: There's almost never anyone online to play multiplayer against. In singeplayer you have 4 GPs which essentially is a list of 4 tracks, where you run a given car on all of them one at a time against AI. There's a total of 16 tracks, but they don't feel all that distinct. There are a variety of game modes, but they're not used outside of single race against AI and if you play on a difficulty level above normal you'll be unable to take turns with most cars as you don't have a way to reduce your speed unless you engage a drift. Also neither the devs nor publishers seem to care enough to respond to me as a user.The game reminds me of a full version of the Unity Kart tutorial, not really a final product.

_childDocuments_.review: Nothing good to say about this game (but the drift, drift is OK).- Rubber banding is a plague. The races has a "Groundhog day" feeling, You always compete against 2 to 4 opponents (based on difficulty), you will always pass them and then they will pass you and try to ram you. If they succeed your race is over (but in normal difficulty). The most convenient way to win races is to build your booster level and boost 2 or 3 times on the final straight (just lame).- Nothing screams retro or arcade to me. Not the cheap placed "Easter eggs", reminders of other arcade games like Daytona or hydro thunder, not the use of a Sega-ish announcer not even the Virtua rally aesthetic, because the game-play is mediocre at best.- Use of bad cheap stereotypical humor.- Main "career mode" is meh at best, normal tournaments are boring, hard and expert difficulty are irritating, and the fact that you can't restart the race (it restarts the GP) is frustrating. They could implement the progression system into the game instead of making a shop to buy skins.- Bad optimization with choppy framerate on high settings and in some circuits on medium (Ryzen 5 5500U and RTX 3050).Avoid this one as a plague.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been keeping an eye on this game ever since it had the working title as "Racing Apex". It originally hinted at having VR support, weapons, and a unique co-op vehicle combat mode where one person could drive while the other player was a gunner on the roof of the car. Unfortunately, none of those planned features made it into the final game, which is now named "Hotshot Racing". I was still eager to play this game because of the retro polygon art style, which reminded me of Virtua Racing and the original Ridge Racer. My main problem with the game right now is how poorly optimized it feels on my PC. My specs are a 4GHZ AMD FX, 16GB RAM, and a Nvidia GTX 1070. You would think that a simple looking game such as this would offer silky smooth frame rates on my 144hz 1080p monitor, but no, for some reason the game randomly stutters and freezes constantly throughout a race.All technical hurdles aside, I stubbornly played through a set of races, which reminded me a lot of how Mario Kart games are structured. You play 4 consecutive races and try to win a gold cup. Cool, whatever. Something seemed off about the way the game played though. It reminded me of Road Rash 64, where all of the racers where tightly grouped together in an invisible bubble. No matter how terrible or well I played, I was always in close proximity to the other race cars. Even if I stocked up on the boost meter, which refills as you drift, I couldn't get very far ahead of anyone else.This type of gameplay mechanic keeps races close and "interesting" in theory, but it ends up feeling frustrating to lose a race because the AI is always rubberbanding back and forth. Even if you race flawlessly and time your boosts perfectly, the AI is always right behind you in your slip stream. Running into walls or knocking other cars into them seem to have very little effect as well, since you basically bounce off everything and recover instantly.Overall, I am left feeling very underwhelmed by this game. If you play it split-screen for a quick arcade-like experience with friends, there is some fun to be had, but there isn't enough here to differentiate itself from the sea of other generic racing games. As of now, the game is barely playable and very ordinary regardless.
