I would suggest creating "User profiles" that stores Driver outfit, Car customization and "Last Camera angle used" (I always drive in first person because the feeling when DRIFTING is AWESOME from behind the wheel!).
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: This scratches an itch that, until Daytona USA gets republished, is going to have to suffice.  Pros:* Honestly just fun.* Quite a bit of variety.* Kinda Daytona USA.  Kinda Mario Kart. * No silly powerups.Cons:* Every race seems to end with me hitting the boost button and just narrowly beating 2 people that have been with me the whole time somehow.   I can't say there isn't rubber-banding AI, but it sure seems like it.* Sometimes queues for the directions the turns are going to go just doesn't carry the articulation ---- or I'm getting old.  Just could use some shading and most turns do have signage.   There's a weird depth perception thing I'm having an issue with here.* The 'extreme' AI really is pretty brutal.  ...and by brutal I mean, aggressive and s**ty.  Fast, too, but it's frustrating to be slammed into a wall the second you get near them.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: This game is for you if you loved classic Sega arcade racing games like Virtua Racing! It feels like a natural evolution as if Sega kept making sequels and made good improvments to the formula, all while keeping with the awesome visual style and arcade sound effects! I blasted past the wirth GP race and I had a blast. I can't wait to play the others.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: I got this as a gift, so im not complaining. But.. theres absolutely nothing new to see here..The game is super bland, and follows a formula that we have seen a million of times before.Replay value is close to none, specially if played as single player.It reminded me alot of Outrun 2006, but less exciting. (and that its probably abandonware nowdays.. go get that instead)Think like this.. back in the day you would go to the arcades and spend a couple of dimes to play this game from time to time... looking at its price.. i dont think this game worth that many dimes
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: Pure arcade fun and a great little game! Captures the arcade look and feel perfectly and has intuitive and responsive controls that fit the game. Races against the AI were some of the best I've had in ages, in any game - every race felt really exciting, tight and not over until the finish line. There's not too many driving games like this on a PC, highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: Fun retro racer that's probably only enjoyable for those of a certain age who remember pumping quarter after quarter into games like this at an arcade. The recommendation is for the nostalgia factor. Beyond that, there is a lot wrong with this game. Aggressive AI and rubber banding impacts game play significantly. Online racing seems dead, as I've never successfully found a match. Customization is purely cosmetic. None of the upgrades change the stats on your car, so why bother other than to hunt achievements? And many features should have been implemented that aren't there. For instance, each car has challenges, like "drift for 250 seconds total". You cannot easily see the progress against these challenges without actually completing a race in the car and looking at the progress at the end of the race.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: Everything about this game is FANTASTIC except for one single little thing which can ruin the entire game, depending on who you are.Extremely unfair rubberbanding.If you're unfamiliar with the term, rubberbanding essentially means that the AI can catch up to you no matter what. This can be extremely frustrating as you can use four boosts in a row and be half way across the map where you  be extremely ahead of the pack. But for some reason, the enemy AI will be right on your tail without using any boosts, which can make the entire game seem pointless until the final stretch of the last lap where you can use a boost and win the race.But other than the rubberbanding, the cars are diverse, have great customization, and the game has a diverse set of tracks and characters. And best of all, in my opinion, this game has LOCAL CO-OP / SPLITSCREEN! Making it absolutely worth it on sale!Overall, it is not the perfect racing game, but it would come pretty close if it weren't for the AI rubberbanding and borderline cheating. But it still is a whole lot of fun and even more fun with friends.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: Ok arcade handling.Cons:Frame rate stutters despite running 90FPS. It's stretched on an ultrawide monitor, you can't even run it pillarboxed!Distant lines on the road are flicker with horrible aliasing.Default WSAD steering. Back in my day we used the arrow keys.It just feels like a cheap retro-styled cash-in.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: This game handles like a dream! And from the team that brought you Sonic & All-Stars Racing Transformed, I expect no less.Yes, the game has some insane rubber banding, and it may rub you the wrong way, but a friend of mine presented a case for it specifically for this game and it's stuck with me: Because of how intense the rubber banding is in this game, you will always have an opponent to slipstream against, which will allow you to earn even more boost to complete tracks faster.I'm normally not a fan of rubber banding, *especially* of this severity, but because of how the game rewards you fairly generously with boost for slipstreaming, it actually makes burning through GP races more interesting, in a different way. Give it a shot!
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: Let`s just say if you are a fan of multiple classic racing games like Daytona USA,Ridge Racer,Burnout/FlatOut,the 90`s NFS games,I think you are gonna enjoy the hell out of this game.The only problem is the rubber banding of the AI,doesn't matter what difficulty you play on.There is a car type for everyone some work better on some tracks than others tho:1: Balanced (self explanatory)2: Acceleration based3: Speed based4: Initial D based styleCars feel different depending on the camera you use,it even includes a first person camera which makes the game more challenging but feels better to drive imo.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: I got Hotshot Racing with the humble bundle and I was surprised by how fun this game turned out to be. It has very arcade handling with a boost (nitrous) mechanic but it's far from an easy game. The AI on the hardest difficulty are brutal and in order to keep up with them you need to be almost perfect. This involves full power drifting around every corner...which is very hard to do on a lot of tracks! The game really pushes you to improve.I've seen a lot of people complaining about the difficulty of the AI, but I love the challenge and think they did a good job with it. The retro artstyle the game uses is very cool, as is the music. By far my favourite thing about this game however are the cars. They're not licensed, but they clearly take "inspiration" from cars in real life. I'm a bit of a car nerd, so looking through the car list and recognising a lot of the vehicles used (especially for some of the more obscure models, like the old LeMans endurance race cars) is really cool.Unfortunately, the playerbase for this game is non-existant so the online is completely dead. I'd still recommend the game but be aware of this before buying.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: Best arcade racing game imo. No story, no free roam in between, no traffic in the road, the drifting feels as good as a drifting only game but it's being used to race instead of just collecting points. My only issue (not really an issue) is that the lighting and other visual effects are not all that great or smooth, playing in a 165hz monitor didn't feel much different than 60hz.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty cool game with nice colorful graphics. Played it with an XBOX ONE S controller via a USB cable and it works flawless. Has a decent difficulty balance and plenty of tracks to play. I can see myself playing this every now and then to satisfy my gaming thirst. Completed the GP4 races and I had fun racing in hood view mode. Didn't feel a sense of speed in chase mode so hood mode works best for me. I recommend it, especially if you get it at discount.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: There's no benefit to being good at this game, cause the rubber-banding AI will not care and constantly keep up with you. It's not enjoyable to race like that, it's insulting.Shame, cause the gameplay is genuinely fun.If players have the skills to be 3 minutes ahead of the pack, let them be 3 minutes ahead of the pack, don't insult their skills like this.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: Yeah, it's good.No fuss. Bright colours, going fast, doing cool slides. Pick a goofy international stereotype, pick a car, drive around the track three times. It's extremely polished, it's tight, it feels good to nail a drift. Sensory feedback joy.The AI seems pretty rubber-band-y and will pretty much never let you breathe easy in first position (which, I dunno, I guess some people might hate? I can see the benefits) although it feels like the game is self-balancing to a degree anyway, since slipstreaming behind someone provides both a noticeable speed boost and also bonus nitro. Difficulty is also a little strange; it feels like the 'normal' difficulty has you moving so slowly that engaging with drifting is almost a hindrance. I feel like 'hard' provides a much more satisfying experience, and isn't noticeably more challenging.Also I highly recommend turning off the character voiceovers. They all get grating pretty fast and one of them has a 'cake is a lie' joke.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: This game is arcade arcing done right. As someone who don't really enjoy most racing games i can fully say that this game is a joy to play.For an arcade racing game the key mechanic a developer needs to focus on is simple: Drifting. And my oh my does the drifting feel incredible in this game. The cars feel like they have real weight that you need to manage in a swing as to not crash into the sides. If you, like me, enjoy "sonic and allstar racing transformed" you'll most definitely like this game!Git it.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, a very marginal thumbs up because I'm feeling generous today.The good:A fun pick-up-and-play arcade racer, for the most part.Colorful, Sega Saturn-esque graphics.Sound effects and music all spot on.Tracks aren't super exciting, but colorful and playful for the most part.Drivers have some modicum of personality.The bad:As others have mentioned, there seems to be rubber-banding where you can really never develop a substantial lead.You'll often get rammed from behind, which will send you into a spin that you'll never recover from.There's no indication whether car customization effects your cars' performance. If it's not all cosmetic, it's certainly not clear.No real difference in drivers' skills as far as I can tell.I have not tried online, so I can't comment.I got this in the Humble Bundle, and I think in that context, it was a fun 3 hours or so of cartoony racing (on Easy - I shudder to think how bashed and bruised I'd be on Hard).  I would wait for a sale, though.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome, just started playing. Makes me feel like I'm back at the arcades.Wish they'd fix the Online mode though, especially if they wanna keep this game alive. It seems to freeze and crash every time I try to start an online Quick Race.Also, another pro being this game's requirements; even a potato can run this without making the game look like ass thanks to the low poly visuals.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: I will give this a thumbs up but would probably pick a "meh" if it was an option. Worth grabbing on sale.This is a super arcadey racer and has all the brightness, pace, and electronic music that comes with the territory.  Some other reviews had compared the handling to Burnout which isn't really true. Yes you can drift round corners, but the handling is far more twitchy.There are a few cool game modes beyond your regular race, plenty of cards and characters to choose.  I will say that the harder difficulties are pretty unforgiving, you will pay dearly for any mistakes.Also note that in my experience, online PvP is empty, so you're buying a single player game.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: It was fun until Boss map session came.. uncontrollable cars, sand makes it even worse. Buy Horizon Chase Turbo instead. It is capable for everything this game but doing it way better.. There is something I miss from this game the most, handbreak.. impossible to stop the car before the collosion if you are already lost the control.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: First impressions so far:++ Big variety of cars with 4 classes++ Characters with small background stories, which is kinda rare in racing games++ Good visual design+ Different modes+ Car customization+- Tracks are pretty easy, because they are wide- AI, while I haven't experienced a lot of rubberbanding, they seem to really enjoy smashing into you
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic love letter to retro Sega racing games. Characters look eccentric have cool quotes to say during racing. Each characters' vehicle roster is great and each of them work very differently in on each track. You can also customise them the way you want them, which is a neat touch. Didn't expected to have so many tracks to race in.However the game does show huge difficulty spike if you are race on the hardest difficulty. Even the opponents can bump you hard and throw you off the course. It is painful since you can't retry the race, you can retry the whole championship from the start.Overall, it is a fun and fast paced racing that should be in your library.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: Before writing the review, I just have to say: Having been just playing this for the past hour together with my brother, we both feel satisfied and having the urge to play more. It just honestly was a good fun for both of us, with both of us trying to outrun and outsmart each other in this exhilarating and chaotic racing game.If you see the complaints from others that this game is full of rubber-banding, I believe you would need to understand that this element for arcade racing games: especially such as this game that unabashedly pays homage to the racing games in the 1990's. I understand why many see rubber-banding as a terrible thing in a racing game, but honestly I think it is applied really well. I think it keeps you on your toes to always keep drifting if you are ahead, just to build the boost that you will need to retake your lead should you be overtaken.I mean, it is an arcade racing game. This game is not meant to be played with sim racing approach.If you grew up with games like Virtua Racing, Daytona, etc., you would spot several objects that truly captures the nostalgia of those games. I even almost believed that there is a track that is a carbon copy of a track in Virtua Racing. I initially wanted to buy the remastered Virtua Racing on Switch, but cancelled it when I saw this game. From a review I found on YouTube and the videos that show how this game looks, I can immediately see how this game tries to capture the feeling of Virtua Racing and other games that were inspired from it. In all honesty, I believed this game is worth every penny I spent. I am eager to find more content that the developer is seemingly developing. If it is sold as a separate DLC, I think I would buy one.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: Please, add control layout customization for joysticks. The standard layout is bad for playing with manual transmission.And also add more graphics settings, because I’m experiencing frame drops in some parts of the game.Maybe, provide a turning off option of the shadow effects and smoke could be a great option for a low end PCs.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: Puts the fun back into racing and a smile back on my face!A fun racing game reminiscent of Ridge Racer, Sonic Team Racing and almost every retro racing game ever created. If you like arcade style racers then this is for you. It's such a pity the (PC) online part of the game is virtually non-existent, however, the single player modes are great and dual player setting works well. For a casual way to spend a few hours I could not recommend this highly enough... but remember I was brought up on Ridge Racer, Virtua Racing and Sega Rally Championship... so I can't be wrong!
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: A game worthy of being called an arcade racer. Bright colourful visuals, an upbeat and energetic soundtrack and a driving model that puts an emphasis on fun over simulation. Yeah, back when the ideal method of getting round a corner was to drift around it and to catch up by injecting a little extra horsepower into your car with boost. On top of a timer that will end your race prematurely if you aren't driving fast enough. If you love arcade racers as much as I do, I can easily recommend Hotshot. Though, like any arcade racing cabinet, best played in short bursts or you will exhaust the game as fast as you cross the line.The only thing that's missing is a "de-de-de-de-do-dewe-da!" or "HOT-SHAO-OWWT.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: Before anything else, this game has a dead multiplayer community. That being said, the game is really fun, and brings back a lot of nostalgia for Daytona USA, SEGA Rally, and other retro arcade games. My main hope for this is they add crossplay and revive the multiplayer community, but the singleplayer seems to have enough to be fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine if Polyphony Digital had made Crash Team Racing in 1991.The makers of Hotshot Racing clearly have a deep love of real-world cars and motorsport. Every one of these cars is recognizable even when beautifully rendered in low-poly form.The four game modes each have their own charm and provide a variety of things to do in the game.And that soundtrack. Wow. It fits the game perfectly.I just bought this today — well, it was yesterday back then — and am now up entirely too late still playing it. Well worth the cost of entry already.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: Game is a lot of fun in the standard racing modes, but some modes don't work or need some touch ups. Drive or Die is particularly ridiculous. I'm sure it works okay if you're playing online with other players, but the AI isn't able to make the mode work. You can't get enough separation due to the rubberbanded enemies and the slipstream mechanic so they'll always be on your tail. Additionally, they hit you from behind often in every mode, but in this they deal damage without receiving any of their own. Nearly unplayable offline in that mode.I was able to load into the final Grand Prix at last, so now that's done, but there's just not much else to do. Once you have the skins and colors, the only thing left to do is unlock all the outfits and mods, but as they're only cosmetic, there's little interest to the player. I would love to see additional drivers or cars in the future, but for now, I think I'm done. 27 hours of play was all it took to complete the game on nearly all modes and beat the Grand Prix with all characters. There is some decent replayability, but without friends or online PVP, this isn't going to hold anyone over for long. 6\10.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: It's the perfect balance between oldskool and modern arcade racers. It's fast, simple, stunning andlots of fun. It's the first game after Ridge racer 7 that feels like Ridge Racer again, even harkening back to the Ridge Racer Revolution days. Simple, smooth, speedy gameplay on colorful and fast tracks with a lot of silky smooth driftwork. The graphics are simple yet very detailed and the framerate is what tops it off. One word of caution: this is not a game for days on days of straight up racing. It's more of an hour a day at most, just for the kick and the fun. But it will pull you back in regularly, because it races so damn good :)
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: Great game! I love the style, the driving feels good and the music is great! The only little changes I would like to see are when you are playing couch coop it shouldn't matter which player wins the game the trophy should be applied to the account. Currently only player one can win trophies. Also when you are done adding mods to a car it would be nice to be able to ready up immediately rather than having to go back to the car menu and then ready up. Also the voices which are all just stereotypes are pretty awful but I just muted those.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: HIGHLY RECOMMEND THIS GAME!!  This game taps into the arcade racing games of Sega's Golden Age (late 1980's to early 2000's) with one of the most visceral racing experiences to date.  On Expert (aka "150cc" mode), this game makes Mario Kart look like a kiddie game.  There's no reason NOT to play this game on Expert.  This game performs wonderfully at a near constant 60-fps which helps that sense of speed really kick in.  The environments are colorful and laden with landmarks to accentuate the grandeur of speed.  There's a wealth of cars from all walks of life worth appreciating--F1, Prototypes, GT, NASCAR, European exotics, muscle cars, JDM. The list goes on.This is honestly one of those rare games that both appeals to gamers and car guys alike.  It's a celebration of what makes racing so joyful and enthralling.  It's all the good stuff you like about cars and racing condensed into one package.  It's definitely more on the "shallow" end (since it is an arcade game after all), but if you must have the exemplar racing game, it's this one.  Everything about this game makes me smile (except maybe the VA's which can be muted).  This is an "easy to learn, hard to master," kind of game, so you can get a lot of replay value out of it if you are interested in competing.If you do play this game, play it with a USB controller (Xbox 360 or Logitech), or better yet, a steering wheel.  If you don't know how to configure the game to use a steering wheel, hit me up and I'll tell you how to set it up.  It makes the experience a magnitude better!
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: First of all the game is extremely short.That is still not the actual reason why I think that this game isnt good.I knew it was about drifting a lot, but jesus christ the game literally wants you to drift every single second. If you dont drift the car feels terrible to handle. But not just that!The drifting is so unsatisfying, it isnt fun. It feels so sluggish and just straight up bad.I was somewhat hyped, but this game doesnt even get its core mechanic right, it just looks nice and thats all.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so much fun especially playing with the bros in split screen,A lot of close calls and tight win.The only complain from me would be the inability to launch the game in offline mode. Sometimes I just want to play it offline with my mates, but ended up needing to connect to a wi-fi just to launch the game
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: The racing has a nice meaty feel and the drifting is lifted straight from the sonic all star series (same engine), and it feels great.  Everything from the soundtrack down to the UI is really refined to instantly teach you the mechanics of the game.  Getting good at it takes a lot longer.  Soundtrack is really infectious.  Honestly back when I was playing Stunt Race FX, this is the game I dreamed of.  One where everything just flows seamlessly.  Only minor nitpick is there's not 144+ support yet.  You can force it in driver, but there's serious frame pacing issues.On the other hand, the 60fps has such solid frametime that it feels great.  Devs are active in the forums so far.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic experience for any retro arcade racing fan. Interesting, colorful tracks, fun characters and exciting gameplay, all topped with an energetic, pumping soundtrack. Much like the retro racers this game pays homage to, there is a strong emphasis on drifting; and mastering those mechanics is essential if you want to play properly. I was, like some other people, annoyed that I couldn't change the steering to the d-pad; but, as it turns out, the thumbstick is very much necessary to perform proper drifts, since applying proper pressure can make or break your drift.The tracks all have some memorable moments and pretty much every turn has something beautiful to look at - whether it's a volcano ready to erupt, a casino-style stage straight out of the Sega racers, a water park with dolphins jumping out or literally driving through Jurassic Park with dinos roaring at you. Even Optimus Prime is hidden in one of the tracks - see if you can find him.Once you make your way through the default, racing mode, you have two other modes to have fun with: cops and robbers, where some characters play as the cops and are trying to stop other racers by depleting their health, thereby turning them into cops as well; and race or explode, where you need to keep your car above a certain speed limit, or - you explode.However, this game is not without its faults. I had some technical issues during playing - most notably, there were sudden framerate drops, seemingly out of nowhere. Also, for 20 euros, there's a surprising lack of content in here. Sure, racing on the great tracks this game has is a ton of fun and its 3 game modes definitely help with variety; but outside of some decent customization options, there's really not much else you can do at the moment. You have endings for finishing first in Grand Prix mode, but those are pretty lackluster and you get no bonus if you complete it on expert difficulty. I should also mention that expert difficulty is the way to go, since it's the only one that offers any kind of challenge and learning curve - other difficulties make the game way too easy. The AI can also be an absolute pain with how aggressive it is; there's nothing more frustrating than being first throughout the whole race, only for the computer to run you off the road and put you back about 5 places. With the huge amount of rubber-banding this game has, that's a big problem, since you are literally always neck-in-neck with the other racers. This is a double-edged sword to be sure, as it makes for some tight and adrenaline-filled gameplay, but also makes the whole experience needlessly frustrating at times.A free patch is supposed to come out soon, which will add new content; but until then, I'd wait for a sale before getting this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an absolute blast.It's perfect for when you want a couple of beers (14) and just big homie chill with friends.I will say the multiplayer isn't THAT active, so I would try to convince your friends to buy it as well.Overall though, lots of fun, causal and intense at the same time. For 20 bucks and some change, pick it up :)
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: Next best thing to Outrun 2006: C2C, which is my favorite racing game. Sad to say my CD copy doesn't work on WIndows 10 and that FXT mod didn't appear to work for me either when I tried it recently. Still regretting not buying the game on Steam before it went away. The overall driving experience of this game has that arcade feel and similarity to Outrun and Daytona USA. The in-game control system needs work as I had to adjust my settings in DS4Windows for it to work properly with a PS4 controller. You can't re-map any controls in the game.* I'm not a fan of this art style. It's difficult to recognize the track vs. walls and other obstacles.* The looping courses feel limited and nothing like that feeling of that scenic selectable journey in Outrun 2k6. There is no traffic or other considerations in the game besides the competing racers. * There is occasional slowdown on my i7-6700 and GTX 1060 system even in low quality 1080p mode. I'm not sure what's happening giving the blocky non-textured style of this game.* The characters seem very stereotypical. Kind of awkward to see and hear constantly. * The AI is extremely basic. Expect Mario Kart 1 level of cheap if not worse. It appears impossible to win by a wide margin unless you save your boosts and spam them toward the end.* There is a definite difference between the classes of cars for each character. I've been using Keiko and the F1 style car a lot, though I did use the Android quite a bit too. The drift car seems extremely difficult to win anything at expert level. So far I've gotten all golds in the first and second tiers, and one gold on expert. Haven't tried the tracks in reverse and haven't looked much into the two other modes.Very much not a replacement for my favorite racing game, but it gives me just enough of that similar driving feel to like the game. I'm overall happy with the game for what I paid at less than the already pretty low price. That said, I really wish Sega and Sumo Digital could somehow take the source of OutRun 2006 C2C and remove/replace the Ferrari stuff so we could have an updated improved version of that game. That's the game I really want...
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: I like how easy it is to get into this! After a workday it's nice to drift off some steam with simple controls. Cars feel unique and finding my favorite is challenging. I find myself picking different car nearly every time.  I Love over-all package, but it's not perfect. Balance issues with some cars in harder difficulties and needs more career options. I hope upcoming updates makes this racer even better.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: Not a fan of the crazy rubber banding, but the game itself is solid and the graphics are beautiful and satisfying.Plenty of cars to choose from and the customization options are a very nice unexpected touch. I think steam workshop support and modding tools will really help this game thrive in the long term, so I urge the developers to please consider these features.If they patch the rubber banding or make it an option, I will give this a higher score, but for now I will give it my recommendation.For those who think they may enjoy it, you probably will.7/10
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: This game has great graphics that capture the Virtua Racing style feel perfectly, and the music is OK, but this game would be much better without the rubber banding.I'm don't proclaim to be the best game player in the world, but I'm not totally crap either, and I absolutely love racing games, the Outrun series, Virtua Racing, Daytona, Sega Rally etc, but I found it very hard to win races in this game, even on the easiest difficulty setting due to the rubber banding, and any time I did happen to win seemed to be more by pure luck rather than any form of skill. And I can't believe this game commits the cardinal sin of racers barging you from behind, sending you flying and straight into the side of the track while they go through as if nothing happened! How is this STILL an issue in a modern racing game?The Cops and Robbers mode is awful too, and I couldn't find any way to select which one I wanted to be? It just selected whether you were a cop or robber at random, and then the second time I played switched from one to another half way through the game! wtf? The Need For Speed Hot Pursuit series did the cops and robbers thing far better than this,If I see this game in a 80% or 75% sale in the future I might get it again but at full price I just can’t find any value for money this in game. The rubber banding kills it for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: Initial couple of games but loving it so far. It's basically like if Daytona, Scud Race, Ridge Racer, Sega Rally, Beetle Adventure Racing, Sega Touring car championship, Burnout and Outrun 2 all had an orgy with VR and this was the result of VR's pregnancyThe only bummer so far is the lack of leaderboards. None for single race and only top 30 for Time Trial worldwide. No offline leaderboards (yet). I hope they patch some in. Otherwise, solid recommendation
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: Finally, Apex Racing, or now Hotshot Racing, is here.Pure Old School High Octane Racing game.  Nowadays, most modern racing games mostly trying to be realistic or way too easy, but Hotshot Racing (played a lot of Expert because it's the only way to play it) is just pure arcade racing game with a huge throwback to the good old days of the arcade. Honestly this game worth 20$ for me, And i hope to see more features, tracks or even cars for the game. Like the lack of night tracks is quite disturbing. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ steam reviews doesn't let me make the review tidy

(hate shifting with bumpers... looking at you to NFS Heat).Why no cloud sync (i have to go to %appdata%\local to swap save games back and forth between the two computers i use to play games).Saturation and Contrast slider settings would be useful. _childDocuments_.review: This game is great! It's easy to run (around 300-400 fps on 1440p at high settings with a 4GHZ Ryzen 5 1600AF and a GTX 1080), has a cartoony style akin to retro arcade racing games, and has a fantastic sense of speed to keep you engaged. HOWEVER, just know that controller support is known to be buggy. Manual transmission is also very fiddly, being slow to respond at the push of the button. There are also bugs that may lead you to be softlocked in the menu, forcing you to restart the game. The issues aren't that bad, but they can get old really quick when it happens so often. If the devs took note of this and fixed these issues as soon as possible, this game would be absolutely perfect!

_childDocuments_.review: I came into this game expecting Daytona USA and got OutRun. And honestly, thats fine with me. The car physics are very arcade, the characters are delightfully cheesy, the car selection is good and they actually do make a difference, and the tracks are colorful and enjoyable. Plus local multiplayer is very welcome. For a fun retro racer, its solid all the way around.

_childDocuments_.review: It's like if you took the fast wild action of a silly arcade racing game, but took out all the crap like power-ups or missiles or stage hazards- and it was just pure racing skill.Car selection is great, I love the aesthetic, and it runs smoothly on my crappy PC.My only gripe is that although there are 16 tracks, there's not much variety in them. If you stripped away the visuals it would be hard to tell the difference between a lot of them. Its mostly just vaguely circular blobs.Needs more gimmick tracks like figure-8s, ovals (like NASCAR), something with tons of hairpins in succession, maybe a long track that doesn't loop around. Get more creative with track layouts!!All in all, I'd give it a 9/10.

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of mixed thoughts in this comments section, here are my pros, cons, and whatever in between. I'd give it a 7/10 for solo content and 9/10 if you're derping around with other people. Man is it old-school. Love the design, bright palette, music, the feel. It's primary goal was to be an arcade-racer and, as for the theme, they nailed it. The driving is smooth and the AI is challenging (maybe too much so - more on this later). I play with an Xbox One controller and have had no issues, so I'm not sure what the deal is for other people.The characters are comical and the voice acting, be it for the announcers or the racers, is all top notch. I found myself laughing aloud at some of Viktor's lines.There's a fair amount of rewards to unlock, all cosmetic related. That's fine by me; this game was clearly made with multiplayer in mind and upgrading a car to give an advantage doesn't fit that vision (especially since there's no career mode).The additional game modes are all really neat. The cops and robbers "tag" game mode is a standout idea executed perfectly for multiplayer madness. Additionally, being able to download others' ghost times in time trials adds a fun competitive edge to a group of friends playing this game. My one wish here though would be that you could sort the times by your Steam friends list. The tracks don't feel all that different. I suppose that's a critique about a lot of old arcade games too - Cruisin' World maps were all pretty generic with layout, for example. Nonetheless, for a game with Mario Kart Grand Prix events on maps that lap, some additional hazards or challenges across maps would be welcome. Some people have complained about the AI "rubberbanding," which is not the case. The game actually uses a slipstream mechanic. The speed you gain while slipstreaming is incredible and can be more than a boost, which is partially how the AI keep up so well. Additionally, while  slipstreaming, you charge  your "boost" meter. So, if an AI is in your slipstream, not only are they outpacing you even if you're boosting, but they can dance around you and use their newly generated boost to plow past you.On one hand, this mechanic helps keep races tight and interesting, but it the raw power of slipstreaming seems overtuned to the point where good driving and being in first place doesn't feel rewarding. Sure, it can narrow the gap in multiplayer to ensure exciting races, but the handicap from slipstreaming is too strong.All in all, I think it's a pretty game that nails its core identity, creating an enjoyable and nostalgic experience. Again, I'd give  it a 7/10 for solo content and 9/10 if you have friends.

_childDocuments_.review: I think a lot of reviews seem to think that the game is the same on Normal, Hard, and Expert. _childDocuments_.review: Hotshot Racing is a fun little arcade racer that takes me back to the days of my childhood. Hotshot Racing's visual style is low-poly, obviously inspired by arcade racers like Ridge Racer and Virtua Racer. It's hyper-fast and it has a bangin' soundtrack that sounds like it would fits perfectly on any SEGA racer from the 90s. Each track has it's own theme, and while they aren't wildly different in feel, they are vibrant and have a fun charm with animated background props that you'll notice as you race, such as dolphins jumping over the track or a dinosaur roaring at you as you drift around a corner. There's a simple Grand Prix mode, with various difficulties to play through as you go for the gold in 16 different tracks that are split up between four cups. There's also 'Single Race', 'Time Trial', and a couple other modes "Cops & Robbers" and "Drive Or Explode", both which seem to boil down to the same goal 'drive fast, don't crash'. There's also multiplayer (offline and online) for these modes, though I don't have anyone to try the offline multiplayer with so I can't speak for how well these run. Online seemed to work great, when I was able to find a match. You can customize the handful of drivers you can play as (each with their own personalities and phrases you'll hear during the races) and each racer has their own set of cars to pick from, each with their own stats. As you play, you'll be unlocking more cosmetics as you make progress on achievements that are specific to each car. The cosmetics don't affect performance, however, but you want to look cool as you're drifting at high speed! Overall, I'm happy with this game so far, I hope to see more added in the future, and I recommend it to anyone that enjoys simple arcade racing games.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: There is a really amazing game underneath some technical and day one issues. I personally have not had any technical issues but I understand that it is a problem. More customization and more tracks are required but for $16, driving mechanics this smooth and fun are worth it. This might change in a year if the devs don't fix issues and don't add content.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: This game started out with tons of potential. It was a wonderful throwback to classics like Sega Super GT (SCUD Race) with tight driving dynamics and lots of personality. It was buggy and the online multiplayer had weird issues, but I left a pretty thorough positive review at the time.Sadly I'm returning to change my positive review to a negative one, for two reasons:- At launch, there was one car that was overwhelmingly dominant in the time attack meta. A few months later there was a content update; while the new courses were welcome, instead of rebalancing all the cars or nerfing the fast car, they made every single car in the game faster, which ruined the great driving dynamics in the upper classes.- The multiplayer is now completely non-functional. It had some issues at launch but it was at least possible to play online through the bugs. Now this is essentially a single player-only game.RIP Hotshot Racing. You had so much potential.

_childDocuments_.review: View my full review here:For fans of arcade racers (Sega Rally, Virtua Racer, Mariokart, etc...) You're going to love this!In the package you're getting Grand Prix (4 to play through, 4 tracks a piece), Single Racing, Time Trial and Online Play. I was able to play everything except for the online play, as this was pre-release.First things first, the cars control beautifully. There are several characters to pick from and play as and each character has  a distinct personality (complete with voice overs and phrases they say during races) and they each have 4 cars you can use. Each car actually does have it's own attributes for things like Drift and Speed and believe it or not, you can actually feel the slight difference from each car!The boost system is something I really like in this game too! You get 4 bars of boost but you have to earn them from drifting and slip streaming behind other cars. you get to choose when these are put to use, usually during tight sequences when it could mean the difference between 1st and 2nd place.The track variations are really fun! There is a dinosaur track, a casino track and an ancient ruins track - just to name a few. No matter the track though, the dev team did a great job of making all of them fun to drive on!Back to the characters themselves, the game features more story and characterization than I was expecting for them. Not only do they have voice overs as I mentioned above, but they also have stories! You won't really know what their background is until you finish with them in Grand Prix mode, but I was surprised to see that each character gets a cutscene, complete with some background about them and what they did after winning.The game also features an unlock system for each character and their cars. As you accomplish things in each car, like drifting and what not, you will unlock these accomplishments and then unlock money to buy customizations for all your cars! This also brought on one of my only complaints about the game, which is that I wish the accomplishment stuff was a little more "in your face" before you start a race. The accomplishments are buried in the menus if you want to see what else you have to do for them, which is annoying if you just want to get started.All in all, great arcade racer, recommended!

name: Desperados III
detailed_description: Desperados III is a story-driven, hardcore tactical stealth game, set in a ruthless Wild West scenario. In this long-awaited prequel to the beloved classic Desperados: Wanted Dead or Alive, John Cooper will join forces with the runaway bride Kate, the shady hitman Doc McCoy, the giant trapper Hector, and Isabelle, a mysterious lady from New Orleans. On Cooper’s quest for redemption, his adventures lead him and his gang from rural towns, over swamps and riverbanks, and finally to a dramatic showdown worthy of Wild West legends. Play smart if you want to succeed. A good plan can make the difference between survival and finding yourself at the business end of a pistol. Drifter, gunslinger, and natural leader Cooper can kill quietly with a knife, or take out multiple foes with his revolvers. Strongman Hector carries a giant bear trap and can slay the toughest opponents with his trusty axe. Cold blooded bounty hunter McCoy likes to be methodical, using lures, knockout gas, poison syringes and a custom long-range pistol. Kate can fool almost any man with the right outfit, and kills discreetly with her hidden gun. And then there is this mysterious woman from New Orleans, Isabelle… Combine your team’s special skills to overcome each tough challenge in your own style. Play five unique characters, each with a very particular set of skills Experience true freedom of choice with countless different ways to overcome any obstacle Defeat large groups of enemies with careful planning and execution Witness the glory of classic Wild West scenarios like frontier towns, mysterious swamps, sprawling modern cities, and many more Choose between non-lethal and deadly attacks, stealth and blazing guns Adjust the game to your playstyle with various difficulty settings and special replay challenges The Showdown mode allows you to pause the game anytime and react to ambushes or surprise attacks

_childDocuments_.review: I did expect a lot from this game, maybe to much!So now that I am done with the main story, here are my thought:Pro:* It is of course a great game, the mechanics are good if you like the genre, and the character of Isabelle brings a whole new type of approach to the common problems.However, cons:* Very short game... I know they plan a couple of DLCs, but seriously, 16 missions?* The story is very lame. The bad guy is known from the beginning, and he does not have much of a bad guy... el diablo in the first desperados was 100x better. There are also no particular twists in the story, and I did not feel much connection/emotion towards the characters. Maybe because not much happens... Shadow tactics was also 100x better in this regard.* A common critic in the negative comments is the way developers force the stealth approach to the players. Sad that one cannot hide behind a wall and attract and shoot down massive amounts of enemies anymore... :( * They have changed the drawing and the style since ST. Not really fond of that, and the power requirements for the computer are much higher now. Conclusion: Nice, but I expected better...

_childDocuments_.review: When you were 10-ish, did you play Desperados: Wanted Dead Or Alive? Yes? Then this you gonna love. Although there is some character switching, shifting and merging, it feels very good to bring myself to childhood again. Btw, Sanchez is now Hector, but with a cooler trap; Isabelle is something between Mia and Sam. But only very little of Sam. Unrelated, guess who's the fastest runner again. The story is not too original, but I enjoyed it either way.Absolutely loved the replays. It's can be a powerful analysis tool, but also looks insanely cool. I also liked the maps, the ambiance itself, and the fact that there are very few defects. In ~40h I had one crash (thanks to the automatic regular saves of the game it caused nearly nothing), once or twice the cursor got bugged (a quick restart fixed that), and the automatic quicksave time adjustment doesn't go very well with checkpoints.Much more can be said like how Doc is now a pompous ass (even more and in a bad way) and how enemies react randomly on crises. It sure can be pain to miss an opportunity.  Anyways, I just run through the main line and I'm still a little bit post coital, so take nothing from this and just try the demo, if feeling uncertain.

_childDocuments_.review: This review goes full western cliché.- Storytelling, atmosphere, animation, presentation, liveliness. Sterling all.- Good interface, improved from Shadow Tactics (which I thumbed down,) notably the gamepad controls, not perfect yet but adequate with some practice.- Amusing gimmicks, abilities and tactical options, either shared by some (climbing, swimming) or unique (traps, weapons, even magic,) including the reactions, comments, animations and frequent laughs that go along with them.- Excellent cast of characters (and of voice actors,) with clear personalities and attributes.There is someone for every player to like, to favour. Some might do the same job quicker than others, but none is either weak or indispensable.- Excellent level design.Not only are the maps gorgeous, they vary vastly in visuals and vibes, accentuated by local features and mechanics.The line-up of enemies is cleverly optimised and never feels small. Individual narrative roles help with that, as much as they build the environmental storytelling.- 1st-class save system.Manual saves, auto-saves, and cycling quick saves.Furthermore, all states are restored, be it point of view, paused mode, combat statuses, etc.- Sticky feet.My main cause of death, possibly.There's nothing like a timed sprint on a narrow strip in a narrow time window being stopped clean by an impassable pebble on the ground or a bulge in a wall.This is the one imperfection of level design. It ignores visibility constraints. A rush requires full view of the surroundings, hence a zoom out, but at such distance tiny obstacles are invisible.- You can have a good camera, and a good camera control with the gamepad, only not at the same time.When you toggle Follow Mode in the options, the input is also changed, against your will, and it shouldn't.- The contextual action prompts are clunky.They change in the millisecond before your button press. Hence an awful lot of jumping in front of enemies instead of opening doors, for example.When several actions are possible, the UI should open a radial menu on click, instead of relying on other buttons and labels that fluctuate between pixels.- There is an issue with the synchronisation mode.It works just fine for group orders.Individually, however, new orders for 1 character will interrupt the flow of a previously automated companion, who will then stop and stay in the open.Took me a while to figure it out, the hard way, and learn to avoid the practice.- Badges, namely the fact that they are only revealed after map completion.Players should always be pampered before replayers; there are many more of the former.The quirk partly achieved its goal; I did uncharacteristically replay a couple of maps to take on certain challenges. If I ever replay this title, however, it will be because it's a fun game, not for participation trophies asking me to forfeit fav mechanics.As a side note, it's odd that each map offers a speedrun challenge, antithetical to the genre, but no ghost challenge, fitting and expected.- As far as I can tell, the only use of RNG is to determine in which direction an alert NPC will move or look next.- If only we could zoom a little closer...In summary, this is the best entry in the Mimimi Games catalogue. So far.
_childDocuments_.name: Desperados III

_childDocuments_.review: I decided to buy this game after playing Mimimi's newest, Shadow Gambit, as I liked the mechanics of sneaking and using different character's skills to get the job done while having the option of "showdown mode" which lets you line up a sequence if you have to take out more than one enemy at a time. The top down asymmetric view works extremely well, I've played 100% on controller, it works fine on steam deck, its a western version of Shadow Gambit (and I'm told their first game like this, too, name I can't remember right now) and if anything its a little harder than Shadow Gambit - the enemies seem more keen to see you, the guard dogs can sniff you out, so be careful and plan or indeed just try out different ideas to get to the next stage - the instant save/reload mechanic works well here although if you've picked this up after Shadow Gambit be warned there are not as many active save slots (3x total in Desperados III)Its the kind of game you'll be thinking about when not playing - an idea will come to you about how to get past some enemies and you'll be keen to try it out as soon as you can.Overall a good game, not overly repetitive, the character voices are not too annoying (I found some in Shadow Gambit a bit grating) and for me a pretty much perfect sneak-em-up with just the right balance of sneak vs. kill. Its a shame Mimimi studio are closing as I loved both Shadow Gambit and Desperados III so would have bought whatever they came up with next in the same sneak-em-up genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Desperados III

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game overall, but you will quick save and quick load a lot.In the end, it's a puzzle game, you have some freedom in the approach but you have to kill enemies in a way to not raise the alarm. It is possible to play after an alarm was raised, but that means you planned around it (your characters cannot really have an extend fight with the enemies, they have to remain hidden).The characters are fun:- The seasoned bounty hunter, deadly with a knife and two guns, that I rarely used.- The very slow doc and sniper, not very pleasant to play due to his slow speed.- The strong trapper that can one shot the strongest guards in melee and has anifty shotguns for group of enemies.- The strong and independent woman that cannot tie up a knocked down enemy nor kill them in melee (only with her gun), but once disguised as a prostitute she can distract most male guards and even lure them. Helps a lot in the puzzles.- The voodoo woman that is also the fastest character, quite enjoyable to play. And she can posses an enemy. Not at all there to reinforce the stereotypical woman gender, quite refreshing.The enemies are limited:- Base enemy, nothing impressive, easy to distract, quick to kill.- The poncho enemy, harder to distract, quick to kill.- The big long coat wearing enemy, can only be killed in one shot by your big guy. The rest have to shoot him and then stab him in the back. They also see through the seducer's disguise.There is some achievements in the missions, most of them have a speedrunning objective of 20 minutes or less. I easily took 45 - 90 minutes per missions.
_childDocuments_.name: Desperados III

_childDocuments_.review: This is a real-time tactical stealth game set in the 1870s USA and Mexico. The narrative follows the origin story of the main protagonist, Cooper, in a classic tale of revenge.You control a colourful gang of characters with distinct personalities, tools, and abilities. This variation gives you a multitude of ways to complete each mission.You can use 'Shadow mode' to pause, then plan a sequence of actions for all of your characters before executing the plan (and executing all the enemies at the same time) - super satisfying!).There is lots of replayability; you could do a no-kill run or try to speedrun it. Still, I think the game is at its best when you fully utilise all the fun tools and abilities on offer - at least for the first play-through.Recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: Well, the game offers a lot of freedom in gameplay, which is good, but as I kept playing, I for some reason didn't feel much progress. _childDocuments_.review: This game was a real surprise; I didn't expect it to be anywhere near as good as it ended up being. I got about halfway through Shadow Tactics (by the same developers) before finding it too frustrating to continue.Desperados III is just an improvement in every way. The story is enjoyable and satisfying, with a zany cast of varied characters with a healthy dose of moral ambiguity about them. The overarching tale is of five people with almost nothing in common except a shared desire to take vengeance upon the bandit leader Frank, but the cast get into all sorts of amusing scrapes along the way. This story is mostly told via cutscenes at the beginning and end of each level, leaving the excellent gameplay mostly interrupted.Each of your five characters has a very different playstyle. It's quite rare that you're in control of all five of them in the same location at any given point in time, so you often have to experiment with synergies between pairs or trios of characters as well as with the layout of the levels and the characteristics of each environment. All of this succeeds in making every level seem completely fresh. You even learn to work with aspects of your characters that may initially seem like a disadvantage - Kate is much slower to move bodies than Hector or John, but she does so from a crouching position, which can help her to evade the gaze of nearby enemies.The difficulty is set just right. Many of the scenarios are pretty challenging and will take you several attempts to work out, but between the pause button (sorely lacking in Shadow Tactics) and generous quicksave/quickload functionality, you'll eventually be able to muddle a way through each of them. As you progress through the game's campaign levels you also unlock Baron Challenges, which I found significantly more difficult - it may be better to leave them until the end of the game, when you know your characters back to front and are able to co-ordinate them effectively.Desperados III is enjoyable, satisfying and full to the brim with varied content. Any fan of real-time tactics games should give it a try.

_childDocuments_.review: Desperados 3 is a Real Time Tactics game developed by the same group that did Shadow Tactics: Blades of the Shogun, so if you've played that you'll feel right at home with Desperados 3.The first thing I'd like to highlight, is despite Desperados 3 being the "Third" main entry into the series, the game is actually a prequel/soft reboot. You do not need to play any of the other older Desperados games in order to understand the story, this game is rather self-contained and doesn't require any prior knowledge of the other games; thus making it easier to get into.The game itself is very Trial and Error, you will be using Quick Save and Quick Load a lot, which isn't as bad as it sounds, to complete missions and have everything run smoothly. For those who have played Shadow Tactics you will notice that a lot of the abilities from that game carry over to this one.The cast themselves are all interesting characters in my opinion, to your standard Cowboy main character archetype, to the seductress all the way to the voodoo woman, utilising their abilities and having everything connect together to complete missions, is nothing short of satisfying; especially after you pull off all five people doing something at once using Showdown Mode.The story isn't anything to write home about but this is one of those games where the story merely serves as an excuse for the enjoyable and interested gameplay, it's unlikely you'll care about what's going on in the story but you'll be more interested in the set-pieces and enemy locations as to rack your brain to figure out the best solution forward.There are dozens of ways to complete any given mission, different routes, who to use, what abilities to prioritise, this for me is what makes the game enjoyable; you can play the same mission twice but you probably won't accomplish it the same way twice.Of course in games like this there are challenge modes, DLC missions and what not which are also enjoyable, I only just completed the main story when writing this review but I know some of them are effectively; "Do this mission with only these characters, instead of the original ones." And some are just brand new missions entirely, which means you can get a lot of time and content out of this game for what you pay for it.To complete the main story it'll take around 15-25 hours at best, since there will be times where you're just staring at the screen, watching guard patterns and thinking. "This is bloody impossible." Only for something to click, an ability you rarely use becomes feasible and then you've got it.Overall, this game has my recommendation, although I did prefer Shadow Tactics: Blades of the Shogun (Purely because I prefer the Japanese Sengoku Era aesthetic) This is a fantastic game and a great entry into the Real Time Tactics Genre and a must have for any stealth game enthusiasts out there.7/10, fantastic gameplay, lacklustre story.

_childDocuments_.review: Somewhat forgotten in the current obsession with Souls-like games whose game-play loop assumes a high level of failure and repetition is the isometric stealth tactics genre, which requires a similar level of self-abuse and reloading from it's players. Mimimi have seeming exhumed and cornered the market for this genre with masterful reinterpretations of the early 2000's Commando style of games by way of 2016's Shadow Tactics as well as this wonderful sequel to the long dormant Desperados franchise.If you, like Hannibal from the A-Team, love to see a good plan come together then this game will help you scratch that itch. Proper use of the tactical-planing "Shadow" system (now with a full pause at normal difficulty levels) results is a satisfying release of dopamine as you watch your crew of Desperados unleash a Rube Goldberg machine-esque sequence of fatalities upon the hapless guards that populate this western world. Or, just as likely, you will see your meticulously laid plans turn to hot garbage because of that one guard you forgot about. Reload and try again! A generous quick-save and quick-load mechanic rewards experimentation and allows fine tuning of your plans as you tip-toe your way to eventual success.If you dislike trial and error, repeated failure and tactical games that require explicit input for your characters to do literally anything then you should probably skip this one.Desperados III, through the character of Isabella whose skills step beyond bent reality and into the magical, dipped a toe into the vast pool that will likely become Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew (the next release from the devs) where undead pirates will employ a myriad of reality warping abilities. If any of the many companions in that upcoming game are half as fun to play as Isabella's mind controlling cat-lady shaman then Shadow Gambit should be an endless playground of amusement, much like it predecessors.

Yet, you made a great game!Usually not particularly interested by real-time tactic games, it took me several hours to really understand the mechanisms and to really enjoy planning a strategy. For a game released in 2020, I guess this is not really surprising to have a rather good AI for the enemies. They are not particularly clever but their reactions might give good opportunities or, on the opposite, ruin your plan.The 5 characters all have their own skills and it gives a large choice of possibilities. Of course you may end up choosing preferentially the same ones but the mission objectives (if you try to achieve them) won't give you the choice but to vary how you play.A quick note on the graphisms, they look pretty without being gorgeous. The physics gives you the possibility to eliminate enemies but the occasions are rare and scripted.In the end, a very good game. After more than 35 hours I don't regret my second journey in the far west! Yeehaw!

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of the RTS genre and you like stealth mechanics in games, Desperados III is definitely worth buying!The level design is excellent. Each level has a special theme. The mission objectives can be approached in different ways. Each playable character also has different strengths and weaknesses. This means that strategies have to be constantly rethought. Desperados III is basically a prime example for the trial-and-error method. A western film or game stands and falls with its soundtrack. An epic soundtrack is therefore essential. Desperados III delivers that. You only have to spend a few seconds in the main menu and the soundtrack pulls you into the Wild West.Each character is interesting in its own way. However, I would have liked longer and more cutscenes to introduce the characters in more detail. It took me several levels to develop empathy for The Magnificent Five.The story starts slowly, but really picks up speed in the middle of the game. The ending, however, has no depth at all. More emotional character development or a surprising plot twist at the end would have helped here. Besides, some elements of the story were quite predictable.Nevertheless, Desperados III is for me one of the best games of 2020! I hope that we'll see more games like Desperados III and Shadow Tactics from Mimimi Games in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: If you've played Shadow Tactics then the short version of this review is that the game is a direct upgrade to SS as far as most aspects of the game are concerned. Gameplay is better and has a lot of Quality of Life upgrades, maps are bigger and have more approaches, animations both in-game and in cutscenes are better, the medal challenges per mission are harder and more interesting, and graphics received an overhaul too. The only thing I feel is worse (but not bad) are the characters which aren't as fun/interesting as the SS group.  My time spent on each mission is pretty much the same as in ST so expect the same game length  (edit: finished the story at 19 hours on Hard, so it was longer than SS in my case, still not done with medals and the Baron Challenges though). It's well worth the purchase if you liked Shadow Tactics since it's pretty much Shadow Tactics But Better: Cowboy Edition.For anyone that isn't familiar with the genre, Desperados III is a RTT Stealth game where you control a group of vigilantes/bounty hunters/bandidos as they take on a greedy railway company that's too lazy to build its tracks around people's homes. The story is fairly simple and mostly acts as a backdrop to move characters from set piece to set piece, it's a solid story but it won't win any awards, the characters are fairly likeable and have unique quips for every missions which helps make them come across as proper characters. The gameplay is pretty great, it works like a Hitman game but with Real Time Tactics gameplay, you have a map, your targets, and must find the best way to deal with these targets (or the one you prefer). The game is fairly good on its own, and I recommend it for that alone, and if you're interested in getting into the genre then this game is a great starting point before getting into the harder titles like the Commandos series.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, this game is really great. Good art style, unique gameplay, fun characters. The game also has tremendous replay value.However, I don't think I'd recommend it to everyone. There are a few issues.The first is that the game, I would say, is a little too much at times. Even on the easiest difficult setting, the game requires a considerable time investment. Be prepared to spend at least 1-2 hours per level because you can spend a lot of time strategizing and save scumming just to make it to the next section of the level. You could probably try to go through it as an action game in some levels, but I honestly think that would be even more difficult. So much requires precise time, planning, organization and juggling of different elements. Obviously, that is the point of the game, but I do definitely feel that, for beginners and people with jobs, sex lives, etc. this could definitely have been toned down a bit.The other issues are very repetitive guard dialogue. I think that they only need to say some of this stuff a few times before it can just stop playing it.It also ridiculous that, in the Eagle Pass Bridge level, for example, that you cannot trade mission items between characters. For example, in my playthrough, since Doc has to unlock the door I made him pick up the dynamite. However, the level turns out to be very much designed so that Kate should have the dynamite. This resulted in me having to tediously hit and run everyone on the bridge with Cooper and Hector. In a game where you're supposed to change tactics on the fly, have free choice, and save scumming is an intended feature — this feels like punishing the player for not planning ahead. There are also some bugs. Sometimes, Kate's flirt ability lasts on guards indefinitely; long after she's left them. Sometimes, your settings in showdown mode don't seem to save. Lastly, pathfinding issues are to be expected, but it does get frustrating when sometimes they cause you to abandon plans that logically SHOULD work by the game's mechanics.Still, as I say, it really is a great tactics game and looks beautiful and is a lot of fun. However, I do think the stiff challenge of the puzzles/stealth tactics, even on beginner difficulty, probably results in a lot of people not finishing the game.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR -- Worth the money. Deeply satisfying RTS with pause/play tactics and no forced time limits. Quality production value with some minor skimping on narrative and character development. If you're a fan of stealth tactics games, you won't be disappointed. It's also a nice change of pace if you're coming from something like X-COM or TRPGs like Fire Emblem or FF Tactics.I remember playing the first Desperados back in the day and it opened my eyes to the RTS genre. I usually go for more SRPG/TRPGs, TBS, or straight sim, but I do love me a good stealth and kill game (OG Deus Ex anyone?). While this is missing the classic character development of RPGs given there are no character build or party build choices to be made, the narrative that they pack into the game is satisfying and each character in your party has a distinct persona.For those unfamiliar with Desperados, the game gives you a small group of specialist character types (the sniper, the brute, the witch doctor, the charmer, and the Clint Eastwood) each with their own skills in a verge-of-modernity Western setting (a la Red Dead Redemption). You navigate each map encountering preset patrols of varying guard types, which function as a series of mini-puzzles you need to work through to progress. You take down or slink past each group and move on to the next with an end goal of reaching a specific destination on the map.Player agency is preserved through your ability to navigate each map and each encounter however you choose. Wanna go in guns blazing and take out a group, alert the guards, and keep on shooting? Go ahead. Wanna play pacifist mode and only knock out and hogtie the aggressors? Sure. How about the John Cena? You can't see me. Why not. Or my favorite, the ninja assassin: silent blades only. Wanna speed run through and only see 30% of the map. You can do that. There's even some voodoo "magic" that adds some additional interesting options about halfway through the game.Navigating each map and making choices that do or don't work out (be prepared to hit F5/F8 often) is deeply satisfying. Figuring out just how to align your party's characters and execute a tactic you've trial and errored about 10 times gives you a series of "aha" moments and propels you through the game. The difficulty is well balanced that you will definitely feel challenged but the solution is always attainable.Being a $50 USD game feels like it might be a stretch for some, but given an easy 50+ hour campaign with plenty of DLC and freebie missions along with additional challenges for each map (speed runs, hardcore mode, no gun kills, only kill hard enemies using the environment, etc.) means double or triple that with excellent replay-ability.Production value and immersion for an isometric tactics game is also top notch. The environment is detailed and painstakingly crafted and comes to life as you navigate cities, ghost towns, mining sites, swamps, and southern manors. Voice acting is well done (a bit stereotyped, but still well done). UI is thoughtful and UX feels right, though I did often forget which character I had selected or action I had queued up, which led to some annoying surprise TPKs and plenty of blown covers.My only minor gripe would be the stereotyped characters. The only black character is a New Orleans witch doctor who plays second fiddle to the pretty white charmer that you know becomes a love interest for your standard gruff Clint Eastwood protagonist. The Mexican brute is really only there for comedic relief. Given it's a classic western, it's not surprising and seems to stay true to your standard character tropes with some subtle differences, just seems like a missed opportunity to change the narrative a bit. There's definitely a higher standard for inclusion now, but I also think it creates a more interesting story when writers don't rely on old tropes regardless of their political correctness.The rest of the writing is solid, but also feels like the actual narrative was probably much deeper and they cut a lot to ensure gameplay moved along. Cut scenes never feel too long and dialogue is whittled down to a core that gives the characters enough distinct identity without boiling them down so much that they become automatons. The small bits of environmental dialog and side conversations between the characters helps add to the immersion throughout the game as well, though it's definitely not as deep as something like Dragon Age or D:OS. Given it's a AAA game, the bar is high and while Desperados is satisfying, I wouldn't say it's a marvel in this regard. If you're like me, you'll find yourself casually watching the cut scenes with patient engagement and restraining yourself from hitting space to skip through and get back to the mechanics.All in all it's a very satisfying game. Worth the money, though probably also worth waiting for the inevitable price cut or Steam sale when you'll likely be able to pick this up for $20-$30 USD in 6-12 months. Definitely something I'm glad I now have in my Library and looking forward to finding this again in 2 years during a long weekend in winter long after I've forgotten I have it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a solid strategy game with some interesting mechanics and TONS of different ways to solving almost every situation. I can't stress how important that is to make a game like this fun. Too often developers make puzzles that require a single solution. Not here! They did a great job of giving each character abilities that give very different options, strengths, and weaknesses. The campaign combines different pairs of characters for most missions, forcing you to come up with neat new ways to synergize!There weren't actually many 'cons' to the game. I only experienced a couple of very minor bugs. My only real complaint is the way they implemented the Showdown mechanic seems like a mess. A 'pause' function with the ability to queue an action for each character would have been perfect here, whereas the Showdown is the only pause, but it changes all your controls to no real benefit. A good portion of my reloads were due to Showdown mode messing things up.

_childDocuments_.review: A majestic masterpiece in this underrated game genre.Like a lot of people, I discovered Mimimi developers through Shadow Tactics. I love strategy and tactical games and I love Japanese culture (the real one, not the weeb ♥♥♥♥), so it was a great game for me, who perfectly portrated this dark time of the country. If I talk about it, it's because I recommend it just as much.Then came the trailer for Desperados III, and I was so pumped until I saw that it was yet another game set in the Old West period (such an overrused time period, it's annoying at this point). But Mimimi had completely earned my trust after Shadow Tactics and I was ready for it.Boy was I not disappointed when I played it. Everything is amazing, and I'm being objective. The gameplay is exactly the same as in Shadow Tactics (at first I was almost let down), to the point that some skills are just a copy paste. But that's not really a bad thing, even if you played the previous game.The story is incredibly deep, I really get attached to the characters, and the motion picture was the perfect idea for it. The ambiance is very immersive, be it in the graphics or in the soundtrack.There's not much to say, all I can say is, just let yourself drawn to it! Every mission is different, the replayability is at its best, and if you're a completionist, it's both easy AND fun to 100% (it's rare!)I also encourage you to buy the DLCs, they add more to the story, and hopefully it will convince the devs to keep going on this genre, because one thing is certain:Mimimi are the new masters of RTS games.
_childDocuments_.name: Desperados III

_childDocuments_.review: The only RTT games I had played before Desperados III were the Commandos series and that was a long, long time ago. I have to say that this game brought back memories from those days.+ Game mechanics are taught gradually and in a very nice way.+ Excellent UI+ Pretty good story, all things considered.+ Very good soundtrack and audio design.+ Great character design with distinct abilities and visuals.- Sometimes the paths enemies take are bit RNG-based and you need to restart at a checkpoint to get lucky in order to progress through certain situations. Doesn't happen all that often, though.You can beat the main game in about 15-20 hours if you only play through the story. If you want the extra achievements and in-game challenges, you will have to play the levels again which adds another 15-20 hours to the gameplay. And thanks to the "Bounty" mode, the game is quite replayable, too.9/10, highly recommended.
