_childDocuments_.review: A few questions you might ask before buying, for detailed review scroll a bit down, Tl;dr at the end.Do i recommend? Yes, absolutely! Is it perfect? Not quite? Is there a difference between Shadow Tactics: Blades of the Shogun? Yes and No. Is that good? For the most part yes.Every level can be speedrunned in 20 mins, but normally it takes 1h, and replayablity... the replayablity: You could spend days just testing every strat.For those who played Shadow Tactics: it plays like Shadow tactics in all the right ways, and differs in all the right ways.Only one thing is as bad as in Shadow Tactics: the Guns.Now, you might think a Cowboy-Game wouldn't work without guns, but in reality, you seldomly use them.Guns need a buff. I'm playing in hard difficulty, but after the second level i adjusted the ammo spawn, just because you never had enough bullets. And even if, you wouldn't want to use it, because if you're caught the alarm instantly triggers. I would prefer if the foe which caught me runned around screaming, alerting everyone in their path, and rang a bell to sound alarm, just to give a few seconds to react, because once the alarm startet, you're overwelmed.So: buff the guns.A minor annoyance is that Kate has no permanent way of silencing someone except her gun, which i would gladly trade for rope to tie up knocked out enemys.Does this break the game? No. Is it still fun? Hell yes.Tl;dr: Buff guns, maybe give Kate rope.

_childDocuments_.review: - I used to be a huge fan of "Commandos" 1 & 2 when it came our 20 years ago... Since then, I was looking for similar strategy stealth games and finally found it in "Desperados 3"! The fact that it was well-reviewed on Steam made it a no brainer for me.- I personally really enjoy slow-paced stealth gameplays where you plan out every actions using logic from observations or eventually trial and error :-) Since I also like western themes it was a good combo and did not disappoint.- Most missions took me about from one to two hours and I enjoyed every last minute of it (completely lost track of time which is a positive). I only wish there were more included with the base game but I'm being greedy :-)- I had low expectations and really did not expect anything from the story. In the end I was pleasantly surprised. It was good enough for me to keep going, and grab onto something that was artistically speaking coherent & "believable" with even some twists in between that I did not always expect.- Using "showdown mode" also gave me oddly gratifying coordinated kills (really liked that mechanic).- Sound design passed my expectations- I enjoyed the cast of characters, the way they were introduced and the little depth developers added to them given the somewhat short storyline they were working with.- Good Job developers (keep it up)- Great strategy stealth game- Definitely was worth a buy for me (would recommend)- Very good replayabilityLastly, I'm a firm believer that an overwhelmingly positive review must contain at least a negative/ area of improvement in order to be legit :-) Thus, the only thing I would improve are the graphics in general. Again I'm really nitpicking, it's not a AAA game, it's a genre not focused on graphics, but it's 2020 and a little more character details (with better creative zooming options at hand) or dynamic scenery could be worth it.Hopefully Mimimi Games makes another title like this one soon!Following this game completion, I'm strongly considering buying their previous title of this genre "Shadow Tactics: Blades of the Shogun".9/10

_childDocuments_.review: 60 hours of enjoyment (and glorious frustration) in the main storyline alone. I haven't even touched the many additional challenges that unlock throughout the first playthrough. Desperados: Wanted Dead or Alive was the first PC video game I ever played as a kid, and I was genuinely scared to get this because of how special the first game was to me. I also found the 06 sequel clunky and second-rate. Even after I read some of the steam reviews, I was surprised and blown away within the first 20 minutes of play. Mimi Games has created an absolute masterpiece. Beautiful, genius map designs. Outstanding dialogue, cutscenes, and music. They managed to build upon, modernize, and honor the original in storytelling and game mechanics. It's also hilarious and features 5 characters that are ALL fun to play as and a necessity to utilize for each mission.My style of gameplay for the missions is ALWAYS stealth. I tried to take out every guard in every map (which is why the first playthrough was 60 total hours), but the badges and challenges encourage and incentivize the player to revisit each level. I did a lot of exploring and screwing around, but most players won't have to spend this much time in their first playthrough. An absolute must for anyone who loved the original. A great game to start with if you've never played this style of RTS (haven't played Shadow Tactics yet, but heard this is a little easier due to the updated "Showdown Mode" which is badass). Frustrating as hell? Absolutely. Rewarding, fair, fun, and nostalgic? Absolutely. One of the best games I've ever played.

It also runs smoothly, and the aesthetics are satisfying.Great game all in all. And a great throwback to simpler, more "chill" games that I once loved.

_childDocuments_.review: Graphics are good for its style of game. Works well on a Steam Deck at max settings for 90 minutes on a full charge. Saves sync with my Linux desktop running the game on max 4k using an RTX3090.Western themed top down tactics game. Most of the action happens real time but there's an added Showdown mode that allows you to pause the game and plan a single action per character then trigger all queued actions at will.  This allows a lot of inventiveness in gameplay as you can create some crazy chain of events that unlocks a blocked path of guards that would have been impossible to sneak past. Each character has their own style of stealth   based on their unique abilities. When mixed together, you feel like you're in control of a Western SEAL Team Six.This soundtrack oozes that Western cowboy vibe. Uses a Leitmotif in the main theme song that gets mixed into other songs. Such an earworm of a theme.If you enjoyed Shadow Tactics, this is an easy recommendation. It's the same formula of game, just a Western setting instead of the Japanese theme with some additional improvements. If you like stealth games like Metal Gear  Solid, and RTS games like Starcraft/Warcraft, this game is a fusion of both genres. Also has a great story to tie all the great gameplay together.2 thumbs way up.

_childDocuments_.review: Desperados Wanter Dead or Alive is quite possible my favourite game of all time (definitely top 3), so I had high expectations. Although I wasn't too worried as Shadow Tactics from Mimimi was superb, too.To some degree this is western-Shadow Tactics. If you liked that, this is a no brainer, just buy it and you will love it.Tbh, there were a few weird things for me at first. Why reset the relations between the original characters? Why only three of the old characters and two brand new ones? The new voice actors are totally understandable but man did they sound weird saying those well known old phrases!The story, while not a masterpiece but it is very good, did justify the choices around characters. And I did like the variety in the way the characters talked to each other and about the missions. Some of their sentences made me LOL, and I don't do that too often. So, all the weirdness I ended up liking quite quickly.From gameplay POV this is a masterpiece. Desperados and Shadow Tactics already were, so no surprise here really. The one thing I missed is the less predictable behaviour of the enemies from Desperados. But I also understand why it was easier to just use the enemy classes from ST. Would I have liked the game more with less predictability? Absolutely! Do I still like the game regardless? Absolutely!Desperados 3 does live up to its name. And from someone who loves the original, this sums it up all really. Must-play for the fans of its genre.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the greatest stealth tactics game ever! The whole picture is just as it should be: a very nice story with interesting characters, great Western atmospheric music, perfect graphics, intuitive game controls, and so on. It's absolutely worth every single penny. Especially because the game is being expanded while playing. That is: multiple extra challenging downloadable contents and episodes are being added when you buy a Season Pass. Believe me: even without discount you want to have this game including its expansions!When you loved the Commandos series, Desperados Wanted Dead or Alive or Robin Hood The Legend of Sherwood you will love Desperados 3 even more. Got disappointed by playing  Commandos 2 HD Remastered, Desperados 2 (Cooper’s Revenge) or Helldorado? Desperados 3 will comfort you and get over it in no time! You just notice that the developers took the greatest care when creating Desperados 3 and they still do as we speak (i.e. the game is being updated and upgraded continuously). The looks are absolutely picturesque and the game is overall pretty bugless, even for me as a very critical and demanding player. Moreover, conversations between characters are unexpectedly funny. But there is even more hidden entertainment. That is, in order to gain some rare badges you end up in some surprising scenes…Preferring some more challenge? Simply look up the full badge list and spend some more time on a mission by thinking and planning more thoroughly or simply do some extra trial-and-error exercises. I did and although the game is sometimes tough, it feels just extra rewarding if you finish a mission successfully. Nevertheless, even without gaining badges the missions are in general very rewarding.In short: stunning, challenging, highly entertaining, addictive, beautifully designed and absolutely worthwhile! Buy it. You won’t regret it!

_childDocuments_.review: A real time pauseable tactics game where you play rootin' tootin' cowboys in the old west. You get a bunch of characters that you have to control simultaneously and fiddle your way through gunfight stealth puzzles using their different abilities. Requires a lot of patience both in terms of waiting for enemies to arrange themselves just so to spring your trap, and also just trying over and over and over and over to get through an area without triggering an alarm or getting spotted. It is very linear, as your characters walk from one stealth puzzle to the next, and as a result becomes very repetitive.

_childDocuments_.review: Only bought it cause of Desperados: Wanted Dead or Alive nostalgia. So far, have not been disappointed. Yes, it is not the original game and some characters are quite questionable and feel op (Isabella, for example) but I have had quite a lot of fun so far. Contrary to what the negative reviews say, you do not have to kill all, there are other ways of completing the mission. The replay-ability is also quite good, you can try missions at different levels and without using certain characters/assists (like getting an outfit for Kate). Would recommend this game for sure but would also suggest waiting for a discount. I think £45 is a bit too much, I think at around £25-£30 is definitely worth the money and the time.

_childDocuments_.review: Hands down, the best game in it's genre so far. Flawless gameplay, lots of missions and challenges and lovable characters quite different from each other. If you like the genre, don't miss this one.A part from the perfect gameplay, the story itself and how they present it to you is another reason to love this game. The story is quite catchy and the way they have delivered it is amazing. The cutscenes and the animations are perfectly made and there are some jokes there that actually make you laugh hard.The missions themselves were amazing and the baron challenges added a lot of fun to them. There's a baron mission where you got a portable gatling gun and more than 100 enemies to kill. That just refreshes you from all the brain work for other missions. Speaking of which, the most challenging mission for me was also one of the baron missions where you had no other abilities but your guns. It was the only mission I had to try many things until I found my strategy which included very accurate timings.The hardest difficulty is Desperados mode which I suggest for the veterans of the genre. The only main thing that is changed is the time the enemy will spot you when you're in their view cone and it is very short in the desperados mode. You must always avoid being visible to the enemy which creates unique puzzling hard situations throughout the game, and I enjoyed dealing with those situation the most.The only thing I didn't like about the game were some of the level badges that made you not to use a character at all. Or there were some of the badges that were impossible to get in together in one playthrough. Adding that to the fact that you don't know the badges of each mission when you play it for the first time (unless you search them online) you might need to do a mission even more than 3 times to get all the badges. That can be very frustrating especially if you don't like the badge you're trying to get. Like finishing a mission without any saves.Other than what I said about the badges, I just can say right now it's the best game in the genre. So waiting for the "Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew!" game.

_childDocuments_.review: As a lifelong fan of Desperados and Commandos series, having enjoyed Shadow Tactics immensely, I had high very hopes for this game. Immediately after starting, many things felt outright wrong, but I kept playing and tried really hard to enjoy it. I would've probably finished the game despite my discomfort, but then a particular event just made me immediately quit the game with good conscience and not look back: the chapter where I got Isabelle, an actual "witch" character (as in fantasy RPG's) and her main skill is literally "Mind Control". Yeah, you read it right. It does exactly what it says, it mind controls enemies.What the actual ♥♥♥♥? Are we having super powers now?In my opinion, it was already such a poor decision to depart from the general aesthetics and seriousness of the "Desperados: Wanted Dead or Alive" that I was barely holding on. Then the mind control happened, and it was the final straw. Even when I ignore every subjective thought I had regarding the style choices, this single design decision immediately killed all the immersion for me, disregarded all the incentive to keep playing it and invalidated all the great quality of life improvements that were introduced. Imagine playing Red Dead Redemption for hours, finishing 50% of the game, just for the game to reveal to you that you can actually do magic.This was the biggest "♥♥♥♥ you" I could've ever received from a beloved game series.I won't be recommending this to anyone in their right mind.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't take my words likely: This game is  tactical. People who don't like tactical games (TRPGs) will hate this game. Just killing a single enemy often takes a minute or more of planning and when you're talking about 50+ enemies per level, you can see that playing this game is NOT fast and there is NO 'run-n-gun' option in this game at all... You literally are forced to play tactically or you'll just die. So, don't even try this game if you don't like TRPGs because this game makes somebody like me feel a little weary of playing this game for a couple of hours, and I'm somebody who likes XCOM2 and other TRPG games, so that's saying something. This game is easily 5 times more tactical than XCOM2.With that being said: If you love TRPGs then this will be the game for you. It has very smooth gameplay and it looks very nice. I'm particularly impressed with the fact that it only uses 50% of my 1070GTX, despite looking very nice. Each different character in your squad has various different strengths and weaknesses. Some of the characters can't even climb ladders, or swim, which I found very strange, but although it's not very realistic, I can totally understand that by them doing that, they make the game much more difficult and tactical, since you can't just use a single character to do an entire mission because of it.Overall, it's a very good TRPG. The two BIGGEST issues I have with the game by far is the fact that you cannot have dual-bindings for keys.. this fact irritated me constantly and often caused me to press the incorrect key as a result. If only they allowed you to have dual-bindings for a single action, then this game would have been amazing. The other issue is the fact that there's  character progression or character customization, meaning, your characters can't equip weapons, skills or abilities... they don't gain experience and they don't 'get stronger' in any way (like they do in XCOM2 for instance). These two issues takes this game from being a 10/10 to only being an 8/10. Still pretty good and well worth the money, but it could have been so much betterFor more reviews, visit my curator page: For my full recommended list of games:

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who have played Shadow Tactics before, I enjoyed many aspects of Desperados 3. Compared to ST, D3 contains more quality of life features (such as the ability to tie up the knocked-out enemies) and overall seems like a more polished experience. The characters are fun and likeable, and levels seem (mostly) reasonably challenging. There are also some new character mechanics that were not present in the previous game (although they are mostly related to one single character).However, I have some issues with several components of D3. Firstly, I feel like the game punishes you more severely for raising an alarm. I don't exactly know how to explain this (for the record, I played the game on Hard difficulty), but it seems to be a combination of a dense enemy placement, lack of places to retreat to, overall lethality of the gunfights and poor controls over many characters in the real time mode. Maybe I am just not skilled enough, but most of the alarm events felt like the game-over sequences. I didn't have this feeling in ST, where I could usually retreat from the combat very easily and wait out the alarm. Therefore, the D3 became even more quicksave/quickload-heavy than the ST for me. Couple this with a fairly long, repetitive missions, and the overall experience gets tedious towards the end of the game. The other weak point of the game is the story. It is a generic revenge plot, with some Western-related side-stories thrown in. Some of them are enjoyable, but mostly they are rather uninteresting. The missions are overall less engaging and fun than in the ST, where authors used some clever scenarios to advance the story and develop the characters. in D3, there is only a handful of missions I remember really fondly. While the characters themselves are fun, their motivations are usually unot very nuanced or non-existent. The overall blandness of the story coupled with the previously mentioned mission tedium did not help in keeping me interested throughout the campaign. I started pretty interested in the characters and the setting, but in the end I just wanted to get it over as fast as possible.Overall, I would probably recommend this game to the , but to others I would advice . It is still a good game in its own niche, but not varied and engaging enough to justify the full price. I got the game from HumbleBundle and for that price it is absolutely worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: Desperados 3, prequel to the rest of the franchise and a mighty fine one at that.  Any concerns that Mimimi might've missed the mark bringing the unique Wild West spin of the original Desperados title back to life in a Real-Time Tactics game, or tried to make it more in line with their previous works were thoroughly dispelled within minutes of entering the game proper.To make a long story short, if you're the type of person who can devote entire hours to analytical study and stealthy trial and error gameplay, then you will feel right at home.If you're the type to get impatient with real-time puzzle strategy games, well, it's probably not the game for you.Moving on, there's no denying the attention to detail the developers have provided to the game, especially for a known IP with an existing fanbase at that.  If anything this game serves as a proper successor to the legacy of the old development team.  This isn't just Shadow Tactics or Commandos in the Wild West; this is its own piece of beauty, it belongs in the setting, from the audio and visuals, to the characters and tools at their disposal, it's all fittingly part of the setting for the most part at the very least.Gameplay wise, it is very much a fluid improvement over previous entries, perhaps even better than Mimimi's previous work with Shadow Tactics even.  Every character pulls their weight, every level can very well keep you invested for hours studying, preparing, and gambling the pros and cons of every action.  Even going loud isn't off the cards either, with helpful hints from the interface helping you plan your every move, it's not really a question if you'll solve whatever level you're on, but when.Every level feels delightfully hand-crafted too, with puzzles that keep you at em with lots of replay value if you're into the challenge this game provides.  The options for creativity are incredibly flexible too, so experimenting is highly encouraged.Relatedly, I feel non-lethal approaches have been vastly improved in this compared to ST: Blades of the Shogun.  The simple ability to tie enemies and unhelpful neutrals up? So much cleaner. ^^Having said all these positive things, I must point out that there are issues with the interface when it comes to movement, with it sometimes being obsessive with jumping down Z levels rather than using the stairs, and other such unusual behavior.  Furthermore using the in-built tactical mode can be hit & miss, especially since far as I know, there's no way to tell characters to rush to their assigned melee targets, which can make things awkward if they notice their buddies getting punched.  Overall the design is sleek, but improvements still could be made.So in summary, I highly recommend this game, especially to fans of the older parts of the franchise, they did it justice, it cannot be said enough.

_childDocuments_.review: My muscle memory is attuned to tapping space instead of shift to pause, which resulted in some funny moments (mostly ending in death). The limited real time pause was a source of momentary mental stress for me. My gripe aside, this game is absolutely STELLAR. It doesn't over stay it's welcome and it doesn't wind you up in a pointless meta loops. The games plays out like a great spaghetti western. It's clear that the developers indexed for a solid linear tale with well crafted "toy box" levels. Mechanical breadth and depth, narrative design, sound and aesthetic polish makes for a deeply cohesive, cerebral experience.There's so much learn and experience here. Buy it at full price if you can. _childDocuments_.review: Honestly one of the most entertaining stealth tactics games I've ever played.The controls and mechanics are so crisp for executing a synchronised plan, it never stops being satisfying when you line it all up and trigger a domino chain that takes out half a dozen guards out of commission before any of them can raise the alarm. Lots of effort has clearly gone into the QoL side of the controls so that executing your plan isn't a far bigger obstacle than thinking up the plan in the first place.The story and voice acting are also great fun. It's all very classic western; avenged family, train heists, showdowns in the church yards. Full of tropes you'll know well, but done sublimely well so you can just enjoy the ride rather than roll your eyes.It's got a good pacing to the progression too, there's not only a goodly number of mission missions but they're also generally very distinct from each other, with new enemies, challenges, tools and combinations of circumstances introduced all the time. So you don't end up with the feeling of just going through the motions of doing more of the same waiting for a new mechanic to be introduced.

_childDocuments_.review: Mimimi have improved so much since Shadow Tactics: Blades of the Shogun.Characters are likeable, they interact perfectly with each other. Every one of them act according to their established character(maybe they could've improved Isabelle's story arc a bit more).Story is nothing special but the way they integrated these characters into it is amazing(there are some well done twists). Voice acting is on point, you can see that they wanted to make a perfect product.Music is breath taking, capturing wild west spirit perfectly + capturing mood of the gang most of the time.Everything looks amazing. Big improvement from Shadow tactics(it looked great too).Gameplay wise, damn. I felt that it was easier than Shadow tactics(even on hard difficulty), but there is another difficulty "Desperado" which is great if you want to challenge yourself. They have also implemented new challenges which are so much fun. Main story tho, first few missions are really easy, untill you pick up all skills with characters. Then we have classical: find one weak spot in an area and exploit it, which is sometimes really hard on first playthrough. Last couple of levels require of you to think hard, to plan out your every move(if you are playing on hard difficulty or doing badges, it requires of you to think even harder because you won't get away with some shenanigans).I really like what they did with characters.Cooper is really strong. You will end up using all of his abilities very often + he can swim, climb vines, climb ropes and has ~1s kill with melee.I found Hector useful only for carrying bodies, disposing of Longcoats and sometimes for sawed-off or Bianca.Kate is good for blinds and obviously distractions with disguise. She also has almost silent short ranged pistol which i didn't use often.McCoy is good only for sniping and occasional use of sleeping gas or dr. bag. Can't climb vines or swim, same as Kate and Hector.Isabelle...so broken. She is by far strongest one. She is fast while crouching, can climb vines, can swim, she can link 2 enemies(what happens to one happens to the other), mind control(used it maybe once per map but probably would end up spending hours figuring out how to pass guards), and cat as distraction(double distraction if you use link). I said that she is most broken because you can basically take out 3 enemies without raising alarm in area where there are 10 guards with link + mind control.Overall, game is amazing. Main content will take you 20-25+ hours to finish on first playthrough and there is bonus content with challenges and revisiting main missions for badges(which are well thought out).Also, you don't have to be RTS fan to enjoy this game or Shadow tactics.Definitely worth a buy.

_childDocuments_.review: I really ought to give Desperados III a thumbs down, but I just don't have the heart to do it.I love this genre too much. This style of stealth-based RTS-like gameplay just hits all my buttons: the slow, gradual, methodical cleaning of an entire map full of enemies, against all odds, with just a few units at your disposal. Observing enemy movements, making plans, testing plans, abandoning plans and starting over -- all just to get rid of one unit out of half a hundred -- just like back when I played Commandos as a child. But all the glitches and lack of polish in Desperados III put an ugly, dirty stain on the otherwise pleasant experience.There will be enemies noticing you in places they shouldn't be noticing you -- even in «safe» zones, like that one corner in New Orleans that your characters are going to path through. There will be broken enemy scripts, and enemies getting stuck in unfortunate places. There will be characters going invisible after exiting through a door. There is a softlock bug in the wedding level, requiring you to restart the map if you haven't saved. Your characters can be spotted and killed while a cutscene is playing. Your characters will do silly things like go around the entire map instead of going through the unlocked door right next to them. There are even obvious, simple things that should have been easily spotted during the most basic testing, like Cooper's throwing knife ability using the wrong voice lines, for whatever reason.For the majority of people, these sort of things won't be that much of an issue, because most people will savescum through the game and will just load the most recent save. The developers expect and encourage this -- there is even a timer enabled by default that reminds you to save if you haven't saved in the last nanosecond (thankfully, you can disable it). But I don't accept that excuse. I don't want to savescum, so I won't. I don't care how I'm "supposed" to be playing the game -- I went through the entire game, blind, on desperados difficulty, without saving even once. Took me just under 200 hours, which all the bugs mentioned above contributed to significantly. £33.50 is a laughable asking price for a product of this quality.You know what? I think I found the heart to give this game a thumbs down after all.

_childDocuments_.review: Desperados III is a tense, challenging, white knuckled real time tactics action adventure which combines Shadow Tactics with the versatility and replayability of the Hitman series. Visually portrayed from a top-down view, the player controls a total of five characters throughout the game (though some missions will vary these numbers depending on the event in the plot) to complete the objectives of the mission. Each character has their own unique inventory of weapons, gadgets and abilities which boast their share of strengths and relative limitations. It is this character diversity that allows for a substantial amount of the replayability because, like the Hitman series, it allows the player to experiment with different ways as to how they accomplish tasks. Such methods include direct assault, stealth, guns blazing and the staging of incidents to give the impression that the opponent death was an accident. To add to the replayability, the game offers various challenges and alternate modes to go about the various challanges offered by Desperados III.Visually, Desperados III is simplistic beauty by offering a clean and crisp top down perspective of gameplay. As far as soundtrack is concerned, it's barely noticeable but that isn't necessarily a flaw given that it keep the gameplay at the focal point (this is important since a mission can be ruined by the most miscalculation of space or time). The seemingly minimalist art-style of the game, overall is a strength. Specifically, I refer to the fact that this game features no pre-rendered cut scenes or cinematics. All of the gameplay is told from within the immersion and is very effective in doing so as the flow between gameplay and story is never broken. Desperados III is unapologetic in its difficulty but pays off by allowing the player to vary the level of difficulty along with a save system that outright reminds you to save - it doesn't hold your hand, as such, but is at least self-aware enough of its difficulty to not shame them into using the save system. While the year is far from over, Desperados III is shaping up to be the game of 2020. I enjoyed the tense and frustrating moments, I loved the way the game looked, the story had me immersed from the beginning and I thoroughly enjoyed playing as all five characters because each offered a unique gaming experience. A modern classic.5 out of 5

_childDocuments_.review: Mimimi have done it again.With the final release of the 3rd DLC on this cursed day, Mimimi's Desperados III finally gets my approval as GOTY 2020. You can grab all 3 DLC from today until 6 Nov. at the same discounted price as the pre-order people.Desperados III is a clear improvement over Mimimi's previous Shadow Tactics: Blades of the Shogun while still remaining familiar. Brown nosing out of the way here is the real review.Desperados III is a prequel to the previous 3 games in the series (so really should be Desperados IV), but back to the classic isometric view in the RTT genre, where we discover more about Cooper and his gang prior to the events of Wanted Dead or Alive. The Unity engine poses its issues but we have the game being able to run at a locked 144fps with close to non existent hitches. 99.9% of the time you won't have trouble when carrying bodies / crashes / jumping off a ledge into an execution / characters patrol routes messing up. The environments are rich in colour and variety but just don't look too far off the edge off the map to see the low res rocks :P.The game time wise takes a similar amount as ST, between 25-35 hours depending on player skill. Other than the purchasable DLC, akin to the bonus missions in Commandos 2, there are FREE "remixed" levels too after beating the main game, changing the layout and playable characters of familiar levels, increasing playtime and replayability.My personal pros for this new title are responsiveness and well done animations (other than for the DLC, no body capture animations were used there for CUTSCENES only), allowing both beginners and veterans to have a great time thanks to fluid gameplay. Other pros are the banter (improved from Shadow Tactics by a country mile, both in writing and voice acting), the soundtrack and the improved "Showdown" mode. In ST the Showdown mode felt a bit clunky and didn't pause the game, in D III, other than on the highest difficulty, you can pause and the UI is intuitive. One feature that I think all patrol-based stealth games should have are D III's fast forward mode which does what it says, and works in tandem with the showdown pause allowing for precise executions. Also more "in-doors" gameplay is appreciated, other than that it's a good modern RTT with many gameplay and decision choices. God bless bringing back the ability to tie people up and shove them all in bushes and the like.Now it's time for the D E B U N K section, especially for reviewers like Ranton. D III is not simply "Ninjas in the wild west" or "Cowboy Ninjas". While it's true again that only when carrying bodies and only on specific surfaces do your characters make noise, running past someone requires pristine micro executions and even though previous kits are utilised, the gameplay remains unique. Pretty hard to make innovative abilities since stealth is not new (Hayato and Cooper, Yuki and Hector, Katie and Aiko). There is however a very unique character, Isabelle. Isabelle was seen as divisive among RTT fans as "too overpowered" and "Voodoo not belonging as it's not a fantasy game" but her kit remains balanced and fitting for the game's Southern theme, especially in the swamps of Louisiana. Not like previous existing stealth games did not have something absurd going for them. As it stands Mimimi is the modern standard for RTT games and their new upcoming game should be great... in 3 to 4 years' time. For RTT recommendations see the end of my Partisans 1941 review.

_childDocuments_.review: If "Shadow Tactics: Blade of the Shogun" revives real-time tactics genre like "Wolfenstein: The New Order" with old-school shooter genre, then "Desperados 3" is the "Doom (2016)" of real-time tactics. Considering this is Mimimi's 5th game - and 2nd real-time tactic game - they have outdone themselves with massive improvements to both gameplay and presentations. Tl;dr. If you love "Shadow Tactics: Blade of the Shogun", "Desperados: Wanted Dead of Alive" or real-time tactics genre as a whole, "Desperados 3" is a must-buy. It is a massive improvement over "Shadow Tactics" and a streamline but faithful prequel of the first game, both story-wise and gameplay-wise. Yet, simpler but not easier, "Desperados 3" has its own set of difficult challenges that test the player's tactical thinking. "Desperados 3" is not a Western reskin version of "Shadow Tactics", it is an improvement in all aspects compared Mimimi's previous game:- Characters with great mobility - Cooper and Isabelle - are excel at killing but has limited distraction tools. The more powerful distraction tools - Hector's Whistle, Doc's Medical Bag and Kate's Power - are reserved to less mobile characters, usually require them to be at ground level to use their tools effectively. In "Shadow Tactics", Yuki and Aiko stay in the safety of rooftops and insane mobility to use their powerful distraction tools.- In addition to officer-tier enemies that can detect disguise, dogs and female enemies add to the challenge of disguise. Kate's disguise can now be spotted easier and not every enemy can be distracted by her. The disguise now require tactical thinking and proper positioning rather than being an invisible ability.- Guns are more diversified and more powerful. Each character has a different usage of guns - with their own advantages and disadvantages. The gun sound can trigger enemies alarm if heard, thus there is a certain risk to use these powerful tools.- Map designs and enemy placements are vastly improved. Maps are now larger and more vertical, yet enemy are strategically placed to cover all grounds - one guy are usually in sight of 2 to 3 other guys. Thus, not even the rooftops are safe. Environmental kills are generously spread around the campaign, and all of them are very satisfying to pull off.- Graphics and cinematic have been greatly improved. Using the same art style as "Shadow Tactics", every details in this game looks like a painting, now with more details. Environments are diverse and gorgeous. Voice acting has great direction, every characters - including enemies - sounds like emotional and believable (and there is no hiccup like Hayato's line in the bath house level). Custom animations in cutscene gives the story more impacts. In compared to "Desperados: Wanted Dead of Alive", "Desperados 3" is a simplified version of the game, for better or worse.- Running does not make sound, making it easier to run pass enemies.- Guns are more reliable, accuracy is not character based but has very limited ammo - Gun blazing is hardly possible in "Desperados 3".- Character movesets stay somewhat faithful to the original game, but tweaked to fit in with "Shadow Tactics" design. The tools in both games fits their respective design so this is not really an improvement or downgrade.- Different voice actors, while they all did a great job at nailing Desperados characters' speech, they all sound different, younger. This could be argued that this is the younger versions of them compared with their older, more experience versions in "Desperados: Wanted Dead or Alive", this could be off-putting to veteran players of the series to hear Cooper's voice throughout "Desperados 3".

_childDocuments_.review: There aren’t any rootin’ tootin’ cowboys here. Follow Cooper and his gang of misfits as they beat the odds in a heart wrenching story that take place in lovingly crafted levels.  The player is able to control up to five characters based on the specific encounter. Each character has a unique speed, carrying type, and special abilities. These abilities are introduced gradually so as not to overwhelm the player and it was fun to have every ability from every character, but the limitations created by only having certain characters required new strategies to be developed. A lot of the special abilities combo quite well, and the game is happy to allow the player to combine them however they see fit. One such example that I found quite interesting was the ability to connect enemies that makes them share state. This means that if one dies, the other does as well. There were two guards that I wanted to take out that were connected. I mind controlled one, which is unrealistic but has many uses that stretch the player’s imagination, and was unsure at first how to make him kill someone but have him perish in the process. It then occurred to me that my target was linked with the one that was mind controlled, so I had my puppet shoot its compatriot causing them both to die while looking like some insane suicide that didn’t create suspicion. This sense of freedom is what helps the game feel so fresh as a lot can be done with the tools given.Stealth is a big focus in this game as the player’s small group of vigilantes is quite outnumbered when compared to the forces that they are up against. To stay in stealth, each enemy has a view cone which can be viewed at any time. Viewcones have two areas, one is solid and the other is striped. The solid one means that any character within that space will be spotted quickly. The striped area allows for allies to stay crouched to avoid detection. Many times, these viewcones will overlap which requires the player to take enemies out of their defensive formation one-by-one. The tools given to enhance viewing areas to stealth are quite fair. A viewcone can be viewed, but only one enemy at a time. To get more info, a marker can be placed that will tell when an enemy is looking at a specific place but this doesn’t show exact viewcones so a player wouldn’t know what it looks like with without research beforehand. Breaking stealth causes a player’s trouble to triple in most cases, which is why it is important to use the quicksave quickload system that is recommended ingame by the developers themselves. It allows for experimentation without punishment which makes the game quite a bit more enjoyable. If stealth is broken then enemies will start pouring out of the closest guard post. There is a limited amount that won’t respawn, but the same can be said about the player’s ammo. Not only this, but every guard in the area will try to gun the player down.There aren’t a lot of enemy types, but they do their jobs well enough and more enemies would simply cause confusion in such a hectic game. Simple guards will be tricked by everything, but they can be killed instantly. Poncho wearing guards can’t be tricked by distractions and won’t let their nearby simple guards to get tricked easily either. Thankfully they die just as easily as their weaker counterparts. Finally, there is the long coats. These trench coat wearing mounds of muscle don’t get tricked at all and can be killed under special conditions only. There aren’t a lot of them, but they create quite the challenge to get around, thankfully the environment allows for some great opportunities for death and destruction.The environments in the game use their own art styles and layouts without any reuse of assets. This provides a handcrafted level that has love injected into every inch of it. Traps can be triggered to help get rid of pesky groups of enemies with enough planning. Environments are also quite vertical which allows for side paths which open up only more opportunities to the player.Side content comes in the form of some challenges which are difficult, but there aren’t a ton of them. The main side content that is offered is the challenges called “Badges” which are revealed after a first play of a level.The story is a hero’s journey full of twists and turns that I didn’t see coming. It is one that kept me riveted. The story is woven well into the gameplay as some of the exposition is provided by the characters as they enter a new area that they are commenting on. It makes the world and characters feel full of life. The game also flows seamlessly into the first Desperados game as this one is a prequel.The sound is top-notch with shots having powerful sounds to match their lethality. What surprised me the most about the sound design was the voice acting. I expected it to be cartoony and corny, but the voice performances found in this game are serious and heartfelt.The graphics are gorgeous. The three-dimensional models are intricately detailed and give great visual feedback. Every enemy has a piece of red clothing, with a red band around the hat being the most common. Every player character has a unique color scheme which helps identify them when the action gets crazy. The cutscenes are long sequences of animation that one can tell was mocapped due to the realism present that is usually unable to be achieved otherwise.The controls work well and there are quite a few customizable shortcuts that make the game quite a bit better. It can get a little difficult to click on specific objects in the game world due to the perspective being shown at the time, but it is simple to rotate the world : The game runs exceptionally well which surprised me based upon how many objects are on the screen at one time.One playthrough of the campaign on normal equates to about 30 hours which only an okay amount of value. If the player plays levels multiple times to get more badges, replays the game on hard, and finishes all of the challenges, then the playtime is likely at least twice that. There are so many different ways to solve all of the encounters so if a player enjoys this game quite a bit, there is a lot of replay value inside.👍  👍Great storyAmazing gameplay choiceIntricate detail in graphics.👎  👎Annoying hitboxes
_childDocuments_.name: Desperados III

_childDocuments_.review: Mimimi nailed it again. Everything about the game is great...so far. If you have played Shadow Tactics and liked it, this would be a must-pick. It has more 'personality' than the Shadow Tactics, which shows the devs are learning from their experience. If they can keep this up, we may find even better games from them next time. So what does this game have:+ Beautiful characters with unique abilities (just like commandos or shadow tactics). + Varied environment and interactive world. Learn to observe, adapt, and execute moves to dispatch enemies or get past them without being seen.+ Objectives (i.e. fast run, don't do dis or dat) make the missions more challenging if the higher difficulties aren't doing much for you.+ Beautiful character interaction makes the world feel lively and not just "okay, going there," "Okay sir," "Can't do that sir," type deal!+ Some missions will surely remind you of missions from previous titles like Commandos 2, but with a different twist to them. Day-night cycles included.+ Pathfinding for each character is great. I had occasional trouble with this in Shadow Tactics but here they ironed it out just right.+ The Slow-mo mode makes action theatrical and fun to watch.+ The end of the mission gives you a full playthrough of your movement and action on the map, showing how you executed each and every move. This is perfect for those who want to hone their skill and curve out the flaws in their plan for a perfect run. First time I've seen (correct me if I am wrong) this in this genre of gaming. The other really good version similar to this I've found is in Digital Combat Simulator with a separate software called TacView, but that is a whole different genre (simulation). Seeing the devs put effort into making this show great care and dedication for casual and hardcore gamer. + Music is..well western style as you would expect. It's a like or hate scenario with this one. Overall great composition that draws you in but nothing too fancy that your ears would have orgasm. So far I have not come across serious bugs, crashes or something along those lines. Game runs smoothly. Now to hope that Mimimi will deliver us a new game with even greater potential and expanded universe than this. Perhaps they will make a sequel to Desperados III, or come up with a whole new franchise of their own, or perhaps continue the story from where Shadow Tactics ended.

_childDocuments_.review: TLTR, buy it on sale as it's not really a fun package overall.I bought both shadow games for less than $10 each, but overpaid this one with $25.  I should have waited for less than $15 like what you could have bought nowadays with a sale.very much like some reviewers said, there is really just ONE way to solve a bigger puzzle.  Sure the encounters might be random as it's cone alert zone watch and time based.  But overall, you are really forced fed a particular direction to the end.  You do the same peel onion layers one by one routine for each mission, until the whole thing is dismantled.The story telling might be the only saving grace for this types of games.  The rest is really just the same trial and error boring gameplay testing your patience more than your intelligence.While I liked Shadow tactics, even with the same painfully boring repetitive gameplay, I realized the only charm is the presentation. _childDocuments_.review: A masterfully executed tactical RTS infiltration game in the likes of the Commando series, and a worthy sequel to the Desperados franchise. The story is good, but what takes you into the game is the mechanics, the great amount of content and the amazing puzzle-like design of the levels. The maps are huge but very detailed and well designed, from a graphical and a game-design viewpoint, the characters each play very differently (although if you played some games of the genre you might recognise some common abilities).I highly recommend this if you're looking for a good single player challenge, however if you're just looking to relax this game might be a bit hard or frustrating at times. These will probably get patched soon but I encountered some bugs, including one time a character teleporting from inside a building to a waypoint every time I pressed Enter from showdown mode, a few other pathfinding bugs but the game is pretty stable in general.If you're wondering if this game is for you, try the demo. It is great at explaining the mechanics and giving you an idea of the general ambience of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: "Real-time stealth-based old-west action CRPG" is a bit of a mouthful, but the game is effortlessly accessible to new players and seasoned veterans alike. Each and every stage is a lovingly crafted diorama of seemingly impossible stealth challenges that, after some thought and whittling away over time, are conquered utilizing the vast array of useful and unique abilities and tools the devs provide.Though definitely following pretty closely in the footsteps of Shadow Tactics before it, the Desperados legacy can be felt, even by new players, as it elevates the proceedings with unique and beautiful miniatures of the old west.Part Hitman, part board game; it's great fun through the campaign and has a generous offering of extra challenges that are, honestly, more fun than they even need to be.

_childDocuments_.review: Simply put: Desperados 3 is perfect. Imagine Shadow Tactics, but even better polished. The GUI is amazing, the devs thought about every little detail. Gameplay is very similar to the other games of the genre such as Commandos, Robin Hood or Shadow Tactics. This game, however, is the first one where you feel that the characters are truly balanced. In Commandos you spent most time Green Beret and characters such as Sniper, Diver, Sapper and Driver spent most time hidden, waiting for their one minute of usefulness. Subsequent games got better, but even Shadow Tactics had overpowered Aiko and seriously obsolete Takuma. Desperados 3 does this much better and you will find yourself using two or more characters at the same time to achieve your goal. None of them is a one trick pony, i.e. McCoy is a sniper, but also he is the only one with a lure (his doctor bag). Kate is the "spy" archetype, i.e. she will spend most of her time by distracting enemies, but you will also often call upon her blinding perfume (she is essentially Aiko, but less agile and without a lethal attack).Graphics are greatly optimized - the game runs smoothly (and looks superb) even on a laptop with a low end graphics card. I found myself very often using the hotkey that outlines opponents and objects, though that was more the force of habit rather than necessity.Story is ... there. It is actually the one area where Desperados 3 is kinda inferior to Shadow Tactics. Don't expect any huge reveals, massive betrayals, huge character development etc. After all you're not in this game for the story, are you?The stealth strategy genre has, unfortunately, only very few games. Among them Desperados 3 is the uncrowned king right now. If you like the stealth playstyle, you can't miss this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Desperados III is quite the rollercoaster of a game. The difficulty level is no joke - it often feels like I'm trying to crack some complex puzzle with each mission. While this can be frustrating at times, it's also a big part of what makes the game so satisfying. Every successful strategy or clever maneuver feels like a hard-earned victory.What really keeps me going is the quicksave feature. Seriously, this is a game-changer. Being able to save my progress whenever I want lets me take risks and try out different approaches without worrying about losing a ton of progress. It's like having a safety net that encourages me to experiment and come up with innovative ways to tackle challenges.The Wild West setting is beautifully realised. The attention to detail in the environments, the characters, and even the sounds immerses me in this world. I find myself getting lost in the dusty towns and feeling like I'm part of a classic Western movie.I won't lie, though - there are times when the difficulty gets the best of me, and I need to step away before I throw my keyboard across the room. It's a game that demands patience and careful planning, which might not be everyone's cup of tea. But when I do manage to pull off a seemingly impossible mission, the sense of accomplishment is incredibly satisfying.All in all, Desperados III is a tough nut to crack, but it's also a lot of fun. The quicksave system is a game-saver for me, making the challenge more manageable and allowing me to explore different strategies. If you're into tactical games and don't mind a steep learning curve, this game might just rope you in with its Wild West charm and satisfying victories.

_childDocuments_.review: Desperados 3 is not that bad of a game. It's a top-down tactics game whereby the objectives are clear and the area has multiple routes for you to choose how you achieves these objectives. Every character has different abilities, strengths and weaknesses. You could almost classify it as a puzzle game becasue once you get spotted you might as well reload the save. Don´t expect to just go in guns blazing and win it, the enemies are perfectely capable of killing you before you even have your gun out so a more thoughtful approach is often the best and the zerg rush tactic is best reserved for when you are close to the end.The reason why I don´t recommend it is thus: I have some experience with the developers of this game. Shadow tactics: Blades of the Shogun was a pretty good game and Desperados 3 is basically that but in the wild west with some tweeks and improvements to the UI and more options. The problem with that is that many of the bugs and annoyances are also transferred. Characters sometimes not running even though you double clicked or run when you only clicked once. Characters standing right up when they exit a ladder or a river are just a few. The greatest reason why I don't recommend this game is that one of these bugs doesn't allow me to progress the game. In the mission Mississippi River there is a pop-up of one of your new skills. You can't close it, the pop-up doesn't show anything and the game crashes. You can't reload the save and have to replay the mission only to end up with the same pop-up and the same bug and the same crash.
_childDocuments_.name: Desperados III

_childDocuments_.review: Desperados 3 is a great game for both old, and new fans of the real-time tactics genre. First and foremost, if you are interested in playing this game, download and try the demo out! Desperados 3 is in essence a great combination of old and new. While the developers Mimimi games borrows heavily when it comes to both gameplay and aesthetics from their previous game Shadow Tactics, they still manage to combine this with the feeling of the previous Desperados games. The world is portrayed in the same grim, but also humoros way as the original games and the characters are fleshed out in the often hillarious banter between them during missions. The gameplay is essentially the same as in Shadow tactics. The characters control nicely, and the skills given to each one of the characters feels different enough to make them all unique. Mimimi games makes both the characters and the missions of the game feel fresh by splitting up the team, forcing you as the player to reevaluate and use your characters in new ways when the composition and challenges of your team changes in between levels. This felt really refreshing to me, as I had to learn new combinations between my team members throughout the whole game. The maps are great creations, and always give you several options of how to take them on. This truly does invite the player to replay the game at a harder difficulty, trying out new routes and tactics. My one and only gripe with the game comes down to the enemy variety. While the combination of, and amount of enemies keeps increasing as the game goes on, the game basically consists of just a handful of different enemy types. This does in no way make the game easy, as the combination of enemies still makes them hard to take down, but it does at times make the encounters feel a tad bit predictable.All in all, Desperados 3 is a great and challenging strategic game which makes me incredibly excited for the future of both the franchise of Desperados and the developers Mimimi games.
_childDocuments_.name: Desperados III

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who has always claimed that Desperados: Wanted Dead or Alive is in my top-3 all-time favorite games, I'm super happy that Desperados is being seen by so many people and it's getting this much love. Not only I loved Desperados but I always thought the original game was the most underrated game I've ever seen (the original one, not Desperados 2. That was the worst).I loved the gameplay, the mechanics, and the level design. It was perfection. I enjoyed every second of the game and I don't think I've ever seen such a well-designed game in the genre. I can't express enough how much I loved their showdown mode and how satisfying it was to pull off a successful one. Oh, and the game summary at the end of each level was lovely.But, there were 2 things I didn't like about the game as a Desperados fan:1. I wish they recreated the amazing cutscenes the original Desperados had. Those were one of my favorite parts of the original Desperados as a kid and since I heard the news that Mimimi is developing Desperados 3, I was hoping they do the cutscenes again.(They did a similar one for their announcement trailer a few years ago). I mean the isometric cutscenes were cool too, but it was far from those magical cutscenes from the original game.2. The story wasn't good at all. I know that the original Desperados didn't have a superb story either, but at least it had some interesting twists and the theme of each mission was much more interesting than this new version.Overall, Mimimi Games did a great job with this game and I can't recommend this game enough if you're a fan of the genre.Bonus point: Their soundtrack is 10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Desperados III

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:+ nice graphics and animations+ quality themed music and sound+ great UI+ smart designed locations+ various types of difficulty from simple to crazy challenges within different locations+ variability of characters abilities and their synergy+ more types of opponents with different reactionsCons:- Reactions to environmental killings have a peculiar effect- Some characters and their abilities are very strong compared to anotherMimimi Games has already been scored in their previous game, Shadow Tactics, and Desperados 3 continues the trend. It is the same genre in the setting of the wild west, where the authors have brought many things to almost perfection. Here we have a group of characters in the observable story, who communicate together in the mission in well-spoken dialogues and voices under tones of a quality western soundtrack. The authors managed to achieve really nice graphics and quality animations within the unity engine.The player has a very well UI available for the elimination of enemies with various options for displaying patrol vision zones, there is also a time stop where you can plan the simultaneous execution of several character actions at one time. However, this option is not available at the highest difficulty of the game. The difficulty of the game ranges from a relatively simple to an insanely difficult challenges within individual 16 story missions or special baron challenges missions.The variability of the elimination of opponents, attracting them, hiding bodies, use of the environment are wide, but sometimes it is more interesting and challenging not to use some of the strong abilities of the characters, e.g. I used the mind control of the native Isabelle only in the turtorial of this ability.The reactions of the enemy camp for environmental killings does not work well (they look at it for a while and then it works as if nothing happened), as well as searching for lost mates does not end with an alarm but just returning to the loop. On the other hand, it is basically a puzzle game and not a simulation of reality.Desperados 3 is a great game, a must for fans of genre fans, where everyone can find their own challenge.

_childDocuments_.review: Very interesting fluctuation of emotions about this game. Started with excitement since I saw it announced maybe a year ago, since I loved the original, and still play it occasionally. Then moved into severe disappointment when first playing, particularly with the lack of infinite gun reloads which made the first game so fun, with the sort of blend of abilities from Shadow Tactics and Desperados, and with the fact that as soon as an NPC notices a body, the alarm will be raised sending tons more guys out patrolling so you can't just make a pile of bodies to lure everyone into a death pit like the first game. However as the game went on, I started also to feel positive about the changes, as it makes for not only a slightly more challenging game, but also it's done well. The balance of the game is good, and the final, fifth character's new abilities are seriously dope. The final challenge is really taxing, as it should be, but not so much that its unpassable, I managed it on the first go (I mean, of playing, not reloads haha, there was probably about 30-50 reloads just for that part). And at that point, I realised I loved the game.So that was my range of mixed feelings about the game.Some pros, cons, and deets i didn't get from the store page:pros:-characters feel balanced, all are useful in someway, more difficult to just smash through a level with just one of them-the map replay of characters and actions after completing a level is pretty dope-with achievements/goals for each level, plus the barons missions, there is tons of replay.-animations are realistic-storyline is good enough-the prequel that should have been like 18 years ago-characters conversations actually made me lol a few times-Hector's love affair with his bear trap Biancacons-mass killing is less frequent-setting off alarms is a lot easier-sometimes you have no choice but to set off an alarm-you can only really use characters skills to distract/move NPCs (which in some ways is also a pro, as it requires tactical thinking something something)-still one or two minor bugs, nothing game-changing or ridiculous though.deets-5 characters-barons missions: when you've completed enough of the game, you get special missions which are replays, but with different characters and with parameters like, only environment kills etc-17 story missions I believe.-the story of how john, kate and mccoy first started out together, plus two new characters-speedrun seems ridiculous. 15 mins for a mission that took me 2 hours to complete.... like whuuut

_childDocuments_.review: Desperados III is truly a masterpiece. As someone who loved Shadow Tactics, I can happily say that this game has fulfilled and exceeded all my expectations.First, let me applaud the visuals. The graphics are great, the maps are beautiful, and the level design is on-point. Be it the swamps of Louisiana or the city of New Orleans, there is no doubt that the environments you traverse are excellent.The story is well-presented, even if it is cliché. The story follows the exact same path as Shadow Tactics did. But every character has an intriguing background that makes them uncanny allies, making the story a great experience.The soundtrack, consisting of 75 tracks, is beautiful. Filippo Beck Peccoz and the team did a great job with the music. Not only does it perfectly fit the Western theme of the game, it fits the gameplay, too. You can play a level for hours and not be bored in the slightest by the song(s).Needless to say, the gameplay is one of the biggest parts of this game. And it is perfect. They took everything great about Shadow Tactics and made it better. There are 4 difficulties presented in Desperados III: Beginner, Normal, Hard, and Desperado. Each difficulty clearly explains what they do (more or less guards, less HP and ammo, faster detection, etc.) and you can control these individual elements independently.  The game is still a challenge, but a rewarding one.The five characters, each with their distinct abilities, has great compatibility with each other for you to use wisely. The Showdown Mode, in which you can stop time to set up multiple actions at once, is a great tool that adds to the gameplay.There are 14 main levels, and 2 levels used as tutorials/plot devices. Added in are the Baron's Challenges, remakes of existing levels with new objectives and limitations, adding a new experience to the game. A beginner or first-time player might take 45 minutes to 1.5 hours for each level. DLC and downloadable content adds even more excitement to this game that will keep your occupied for hours.It is highly replayable, and you are encouraged to do so. The badge system adds optional objectives to each level, from the bizarre, such as not touching bushes or haystacks, to the difficult, such as the speedruns or no-save runs. Getting all the badges might seem like an arduous task, but a fulfilling one at that.Easily my Game of the Year. Mimimi has outdone themselves with Desperados III. The story, the graphics, the music, the characters, and the gameplay have all been innovated and improved upon, all to make this spectacular game. If you don't buy it, you really are missing out. Great game!

_childDocuments_.review: Desperados III is by no means a bad game but after completing a few missions, I feel like I've seen all there is to see. It's clear the game is extremely linear and rather repetitive, plus the trial and error nature of the gameplay diminishes the satisfaction. The game does look artistically fantastic and the mechanics are pretty neat especially when you control multiple members of your group and can execute chained moves. Aside from that, most of the gameplay is stealthing enemies, hiding them in conveniently placed bushes to ultimately thin the pack. The AI is also very predictable, so once you determined their pathing and actions, you just have to strike at the right time. Their view range is also displayed via a cone. Each level is like a superbly crafted puzzle though and there are usually a few ways to complete each objective. Sadly, each route is rather one-dimensional and many lead to a specific pre-determined set-piece. Regular saving is encouraged by the game itself because you will often get spotted by enemies off-screen or something you didn't see at first glance. The game isn't difficult but it does have these instances where it trips you up out of nowhere and your cover is blown. If you enjoyed Shadow Tactics: Blades of Shogun, you will like this as it does share a lot of DNA from that game. The repetitive gameplay loop and lack of dynamic environments really disappoint though as does the linear level design and objectives.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic Sequel to one of my favorite Strategy Games - Nostalgia Galore included.The Characters are hillarious clichés and even more over the Top than in the Original, but i love it. Their Animations and Sounddesign are smooth and really satisfying to pull off (e.g. Knife / Buntline / Pistols / Bianca). The Soundtrack is an absolutely fantastic Mix between Rock, Western, Swing and Soundtrack. Although it can feel a bit repetitive in certain Levels and / or Situations if you spend too much time on them. While the Story is a bit lighthearted and overly dramatic at other times - and seems to be mostly about having reasons why certain characters are in certain Scenarios for the players to beat - that's not what the game really is about. It's about the great tactical riddles you have to solve however you want to. The Ingame-Banter on the other hand is fantastic and hillarious at times, with the Doc-Hector-Bianca-Love-Triangle taking the Cake. The well cast Voice-Actors make this ragtag posse a family I definitely didn't mind to revisit for Post-Campaign-Gameplay. It ONLY has 16 Levels - compared to the original that had 25 - but those 16 levels are almost all killer, No filler. On Desperado i needed 30 Hours on my first Playthrough and am still working on beating all the extra challenges, finding new ways to tackle the Levels included.  The extra challenges completely change how you have to approach situations and give this game around 100+ hours of Gameplay.If i had to criticize things it would be, that the AI has a few glaring flaws that can be abused once found out, making playing on the extremest of difficulties way too easy. They are generally way more predictable than in the original Desperados, where they would just frantically roam around in terror making life uneasy and the Gameplay more unpredictable for really long times. Also the Patrols are really easy to wear down (Bianca / Knifethrow / Voodoo) and never really make your game harder - Just artificially longer.The Game has some weird bugs that rarely happen, where it will just refuse to save a mission. I only encountered this once in my playthrough, which was a game breaking bummer and had me restart the mission.Overall it's a 9/10 from my side and i am really hyped for Potential DLC or Sequel!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a marvel to everyone who loves games of this style. I just finished it, and want to write a positive review right away, so I don't forget it.I want to write a detailed review, not just good words.This game is a prequel to original series, it shows the past and not future of famed John Cooper. If you played original game, you'll recognize two old heroes, except cooper, and there are also two brand new. Yes, there are five characters instead of traditional six. All of heroes are very useful, you'll want to use all their abilities, none are just to occupy skill slots. One of new characters has two skills that I've never seen in other games and I am sure the majority of players will appreciate them. The difficulty is fair. The start is very easy, and the further you progress the harder missions get. Yes, towards the end, there are some very hard places. But if you like games like this and have any experience in this genre, you'd never get frustrated enough to abandon the game.Some missions have different approaches, I mean not the variety of skills, but the physical approaches - like the final base can be attacked from the east or west, and both roads have their own difficulties. Or in another mission when you need to block the railroad, the game will offer two options to do this, each with own consequences. I liked that the game allows to cause "accidents" in the way of "Hitman" series. In many missions you can kill the "tough" enemy by dropping something heavy on him. So, not only you'll avoid fighting him - which is hard, but also "accidents" never cause alarm.As a con, I can only notice that the game only has cinematics with in-game engine, it won't show any full scale video like original Desperados. That's bad, but I can live with that.So, here's summary: if you loved original Desperados, don't skip this one.10/10

_childDocuments_.review: I only played 44 minutes of the game. The game had some graphical bugs that prevented me from enjoying the game or even playing it resulting in a refund, which is the main reason for the refund. I would probably have tried to play the game through a little longer, but frankly I was bored from the get go. All the hype meant nothing. This game is a big fat flop to me. _childDocuments_.review: If you've played Shadow Tactics, then consider this a ripoff of the same (in a good way). It's an RTS, stealth-based strategy where you line up various actions and then execute them in one turn. There are multiple routes to complete a particular mission which is one of the major positives here. However, at the end of the day, you employ the same tactics. Bait, kill, hide. Using lanterns, footprints, or other lures, but it's generally the same drill throughout the game. I'm personally a fan of turn-based games, especially XCOM and Divinity, and found this pretty repetitive in comparison. Some people in the reviews are saying that its better than Shadow Tactics, but I think it's somewhat easier. ST: BotS is more diverse in terms of tactics and the strategies involved. That said, if you liked Shadow Tactics, it's a must buy. However, if you're an XCOM fan like me, then maybe wait for a sale. Not worth the full price.

_childDocuments_.review: After having both the games "Commandos: Beyond the Call of Duty" and "Desperados: Wanted Dead or Alive" as some of my favorite games of all time buying this game didn't require much thinking. Is it as good though..?I am not sure how many who knows about it but the first Desperados game had TWO sequels that tried something different. It was good ideas and fine stories but rather lackluster in execution and definitely not worthy sequels as a whole.This game is more back to the original style. Offcourse the original came MANY years ago. Some who will be buying this game wasn't even born yet so naturally it's not exactly the same but I think they got most things right.Unless you are really talented this game does require more patience than most games out there. It's not about being the fastest or smartest it's more about seeing the whole picture and figuring out your next move. It is certainly not a style of game for everyone. Compared to food GTA is pizza and this is more like something your grandparents love that you don't understand at all. Thankfully.. Some of out there are "grandparents".The game does look like a better version than the original without taking it too far to the left or right. It certainly has a lot more details that I enjoy and I believe most others would too. Both in story of the missions but also small things in the gameplay. I remember Commandos 3 took some elements too far hoping to make the game better than the previous games but it didn't work. Here it's just enough.I don't think many play these types of games for the story but I do like what is here and most of the characters has very entertaining personalities. Most characters..? Yes, there is one brand new character which has some features I thought was a bit off. It is sort of a voodoo woman I don't think it really fits. Her abilites is too strong and make some things too easy. A minor issue for me but in future games I hope to find other characters or that she is changed up a bit. One thing missing is also the ability to have smaller characters for singular missions. They could easily worked in a couple to spice things up. Someone you meet along the way and after one or two missions their off somewhere. The levels are fun and creative. If you have played the game "Shadow Tactics: Blades of the Shogun" you will see that some levels are very similar. But it's the same type of game from the same company so I can't really blame them. Only positive things from me here.I have to be honest though. I never did finish the game. Just like in the original there is a odd "last battle" (the very end of the game) that in theory is very cool but just didn't work this time around either. I hated it back then and don't care for this even though it is a different type of challenge. It is the only time the game changes format and in my eyes doesn't do it well. Please! If you guys and girls do more sequels.. Just make the last level be a normal one, lol.So.. Is the game as good as the original? In my nostalgic mind? No. Because of one thing. This style of game is about slow strategy and should be a challenge. In this game you can often use your gun and get away with it. Which rarely was the case in the original. I might be in vast minority but I prefer the old style. This does look exactly the same on the surface but both here and there it's easier to push forward. Besides that complaint, which I don't think would occur to many at all, this game is stellar. I might not love it like the originals but I do like it a lot and looking forward to other similar games by the same company. I hope they don't go "Commandos 3" in the future and similar games might be even better!Grade? Easily a 8 / 10 game for me.
