_childDocuments_.review: Before you rate the review down let me tell you a bit about myself:I have been playing Commandos games since I was 7, I even created a hardcore mode for Commandos 2, I played every single one of them on hardest difficulty over and over again and I play all my games on insane difficulty.I finished Shadow Tactics and the DLC story on highest difficulty as well and then I got my hands on a garbage called Desperados 3 and here is the story:First things first, I never had played any Desperado game before, I never liked the Western theme and this was the first one I tried. The game is completely Shadow Tactics without any difference in gameplay. Now that being said I really hope Mimi studio becomes a bit creative and at least make the next game a bit different rather than a copy paste with different theme.That is not my issue at all for giving this a big NO, the big issue starts here:When you first hear "Western and Cowboys" the only thing that comes to your head first is duels + guns + gun blazing etc, and guess what this game punishes you badly for starting any gun fight. Unlike Commandos games that you can even go gun blazing and still pull it off if you know how to deal with enemy waves looking for you, Desperados does not give you any chance of winning a gun fight versus more than one enemy at a time with single character (Now that might be different in lower difficulties but I only played the highest one so I have no idea about other difficulties in gun fight).Shadow Tactics was completely the same but I didn't mind it, that game was about Sword vs Gun so if you get detected it makes sense it is game over and you gotta reload a checkpoint. But Desperados has your characters armed to the teeth and their firearms are completely useless.There is no innovation in passing the levels in this game, it is just a puzzle you need to find and solve and every time it is the same way cause if you do it your way it just doesn't work you need to reload a checkpoint and do it in the "dev" way. All missions are completely frustrating once you get to know this, there is only one way to pass there is only one puzzle hidden in every corner that you need to solve, it is always take Guard A and then B and then C out then proceed so they don't notice each other. You can never ever go against the order.The Story:Meh, a rip off from the film "The Quick and the Dead". If you have watched that film, you have played this story then. Don't bother!

_childDocuments_.review: Despite its title, “Desperados III” is as much a sequel (or prequel) to the “Desperados” franchise as it is a successor to “Shadow Tactics”—another installment of Mimimi’s uniquely flavored take on the real-time tactics genre. In fact, you’ll be much better prepared for this game if you’ve already played “Shadow Tactics,” as the gameplay is nearly identical. But don’t let the Wild West setting fool you into thinking it’s merely a reskin. Minor issues with controls and map design (particularly in narrow environments) aside, the mix of level design and gameplay mechanics in “Desperados III” is fantastic, making it another masterclass in this sadly still underrepresented genre. And it’s all held together by a solid revenge story and some cool dialogue.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok full disclaimer, this is my first ever desperados game and i am LOVING it. Ive done about 9.5 hours so far and enjoyed every second. I have not really played a game like this before although I am a big fan of beautiful isometric games. personally I find it very challenging. but that is not a bad thing! Usually if a game becomes too hard that it requires multiple attempts, i start to lose interest and say to myself "ill pick this up again another time and really give it a go", but not this one. the quick save and quick load buttons on screen are a great way to just reset and try a different tactic. it makes me want to try again, with a different approach, right away.I forget to save sometimes if im really in the moment and can see my next move right away, thats gotten me in trouble a couple times, such as not saving when you begin a new level. i had to keep going back to my last save toward the end of the previous level, but thats just my own forgetfulness. You have to really pay attention, think, study, plan your moves. Its so tactical, that a lot of the times it feels like a puzzle game as you stare at the characters on screen and watch and learn patrol routes and enemy behaviours to plan your strategy. Something i really like is the map replays you get at the end of each mission where you get to see the exact path and all the actions you took on an overview map of the level. One of the levels so far took me almost 2 hours to complete ( I know, i suck. ) but i enjoyed every second of it. to watch my movements and tactics play back on the map when i finally finished it was so good, i was remembering all of my actions and what i had done, even impressed myself a couple times haha.Anyway, this is a great game, really makes you step back, watch and think.  oh and the graphics are just beautiful! ive been looking for something that graphically rivaled Divinity Original Sin 2 and i think ive finally found it. its a different style of gameplay but that graphical style is just gorgeous. the levels i have been through already have been so intricately beautiful with so much going on, so many props and set pieces, it really feels like looking down on a miniature western world. I would highly recommend this to any fan of isometric rpg games looking for something different and more focused on strategy and tactics, but still with that beautiful graphical style. Id also recommend it to fans of puzzle games, people who like to sit back and study before making their moves, and of course fans of stealth, strategy and tactics. being able to pause time to plan your next move really allows you to think every outcome through before you execute it. Im having a lot of fun with this, I hope you will too! I must now go back in time and check out the other desperados games because clearly, i have missed something very special here.

_childDocuments_.review: No I wouldn't recommend this game. Why? Because:The game doesn't auto-save. This would be a hugely beneficial feature. It wouldn't actually undermine the experience to auto-save after every kill (for example). Hell, the game even gives you an indication, every minute, that you haven't saved in a minute or more. Here's an idea, just do it for me! You will quick-reload the last save, to find it to be several kills behind where you would have liked it to be, on more than one occasion. Trust me.What it does do right is at least load and save quickly. Except it doesn't give you a 'quick-save' file to 'quick-load' from at the start of each mission. Yeah. You will undoubtedly mess up on the first kill of a mission and go to reload, to find it warns you you'll be loading from another mission. Numerous times I wished it to simply restart the mission, not load a previous mission. Not once did I wish to load back into the old mission. You can of course restart the mission from the menu - at a slower load time. Such an easy fix here by auto-saving at the start of each mission - but that seems a foreign concept.One of the characters can 'link souls' - indicated by an icon above both enemies that are 'linked'. Trouble is the icon is quite large compared to the character model, and it's incredibly hard at times to decipher who, among say three enemies, is one of the two that are linked (and multiple mission have three man patrols). Could have given the enemies that are 'linked' a different coloured outline (like is already possible for the playable characters and differentiating between enemies and civilians). Easy fixes team.Sometimes your characters won't enter a bush (where they'll be safe from enemy view - minus dogs) even though you swore to all hell you clicked on the damn bush (the mouse icon even changes).Related to bushes, and including doors, sometimes your character will drop off a body next to the bush/door, which would otherwise conceal said body, awaiting it to be spotted by a patrol. This happens a lot and is easy to miss when you've already switched to a different character, unknowingly letting your previous character just lay a dead body for all to see. Again, you definitely clicked the bush/door - the damn cursor changed.It's also really easy to accidentally start running by clicking in two separate places within quick succession. You may do this as you try to quickly direct your character around enemy fields of view. Doing so will make your character stand up, in some cases alerting the enemy. Fun. Some form of sequence based movement could be implemented (by loading up different travel locations for example) to solve this. But nah, apparently, screw me.A movement sequence could also solve the terrible paths your characters may take. Some missions will require back-tracking through areas and unless you've painstakingly killed every enemy, it's likely you'll need to follow the same path you cut through, to get back through unnoticed. Don't you dare think about clicking where you want your character to end up, knowing there's a safe path through, because your character will take the shortest route through all manner of danger. Efficient! Enemies also tend to spot things outside their field of view. This happened on numerous occasions and I can only assume one of two things; the field of vision 'cone' is properly aligned with what this particular enemy will react to, or the developers are covering up a blind spot with some pretty bs tactics to avoid alternative means of approaching the puzzle. Either way, gross.A personal one - missions were too long. The game lured me in being fun and interactive with bite size 20 minute chunks at the beginning. The missions then draw out to 30, 40, or even 50 minute nightmares as even the seasoned yoga master will begin to lose patience. Losing patience in this game means making mistakes, reloading (hopefully you saved recently) and attempting most things multiple times - which only makes the mission longer. I understand this is effectively the core concept, but I could hardly manage more than one mission a sitting before I was trying to brute-force my way through sections with crazy approaches solely because I could no longer be bothered properly approaching the problem with stealth.This was painful. I would not play Desperados 4. If I wanted to torture myself I could save my money and punch myself in the balls for free.

_childDocuments_.review: Play at your own pace for the most part, difficult but not impossible, I like it! Big maps. Lots of variety in enemies, environments, team members and tactics. More resourse hungry than you might think but runs pretty good on my rx550 with some settings lowered. A lot of profanity which, I guess, lends a gritty authenticity to the Wild West theme but may come as a surprise if you figured this would be a good one for your young kids to play.All in all though a fun, well crafted world and semi-riveting story with gameplay close to perfecting a form that harkens all the way back to the 'Commandos' games of way back when-ever!

_childDocuments_.review: This is such a fun and well-made game! There's a demo. If you have any doubt give it a try. They're typically RPGs, but I'm allergic to many of their other systems like weapon/armor stats, crafting materials, upgrade trees, dialog boxes, quest logs, and other boring stuff like that. Diablo, Divinity: Original Sin, Titan Quest.I've never really been any good at Real Time Strategy - the only one I ever enjoyed any amount was Rise of Nations.I've enjoyed tactics games. Especially turn-based ones like the new XCOM games. But I've never been a big tactics buff.I also really enjoy stealth games, especially ones with bloody violence. Splinter Cell, Metal Gear Solid, Dishonored.This game is a tasty bowl of brain teasing gameplay. The story is fun and the characters are memorable and likeable with solid voice acting. The tone is more playful in this game - especially considering there's only one strait-laced member of your team (Doc) compared to Shadow Tactic's three (Hayato, Mugen, and Aiko). And don't let the setting of levels in swamps, deserts, and frontier towns discourage you - the environments are still quite nice to look at and admire.If you've played Shadow Tactics, this game is more and better. I thought going from Feudal Japan to the Wild West would be a downgrade, but it absolutely is not. And if you play this game and enjoy it, I would easily recommend giving Shadow Tactics a try when its on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Good:MusicVoice ActingLevel DesignCore GameplayGraphicsPerformanceAttention to detail and polish (did not encounter any bugs).Not so goodThis section is quite subjective, as I thoroughly enjoyed the game in its entirety, but people should probably consider a few things if deciding whether to purchase it or not.The story is fairly generic and not particularly deep, although I did find I enjoyed more as it went on. The gameplay is repetitive (as you get taught all the basic stuff early on) but I believe is carried by the level design and solid mechanics, which keep it interesting - almost turning it into a real-time puzzle game once you have a few scenarios under your belt. There isn't really any customisation of characters or 'rpg' elements to the game. You have access to 5 unique characters that are well written and very well voice acted. Each character has a unique set of skills and they work together to move through each level.Other commentsBecause the core mechanics are executed really well, there are a lot of potential ways to approach most situations in the game, which gives scope for replayability, along with some challenges and medals you can earn for doing things a specific way. I played through the game on Hard difficulty and got about 35 hours worth of gameplay out of it, which I was really impressed with for a single player campaign game these days. It could probably be done in around 20-25 hours with a bit more emphasis on haste or perhaps a lower difficulty, and certainly having gone through the scenarios once each now they would be a lot quicker to solve again, but some are very tricky the first time around. I certainly see myself doing another play through at some point to check out their hardest difficulty, so will likely end up getting a good 60-70 hours out of it at least.I would love to see a level editor where people could create their own maps and allow others to try them. It will be interesting to see what additional content becomes available in future, and I think the core concepts could be applied to many different genres and settings.It's a relatively simple concept with a great execution. It was refreshing and compelling to not have all sorts of skill trees and experience points, unlocks and upgrades, or to worry about min-maxing or grinding. It kind of goes 'This is what you've got, go enjoy yourself'. If you're more on-the-fence about the gameplay, I'd still recommend giving it a go but perhaps waiting until it's on sale. However, I do believe it's worth the full price for what the developers have delivered, which I can't say for a many games at that price point and above these days.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: thumbs down because D3 level design is apparently doing away with the ability to sneak through or punch through the clockwork, and instead seems to force the player to disassemble the clockwork gear by gear, the tedium of which is described well in this review: I loved Shadow Tactics so much that I put 400+ hours into it. People say Desperados 3 is a re-skin of Shadow Tactics, so why the thumbs down?It’s because the level design of D3 is contrived and amateurish compared to that of ST.As I wrote in my review of it  when you become more advanced at ST, you can afford to leave more guards alive on the map because you’re stealthy as a ghost. Or you can just become a tornado of destruction and rapidly obliterate everything, while still being stealthy enough to avoid alarms. Between these two extremes is the sneak-wait-kill-repeat approach, which in my opinion is the beginner’s approach to the game.D3’s tendency to make everyone always take this beginner’s approach is caused by pervasive use of complex cover formations, layered and spread out over large distances. This means you will have two, three, or four guards all watching each other, and one or more of those guards will be watched by another guard that is far away, and sometimes that guard is watched by another guard, etc.There’s a big piece of evidence to support my assertion that D3 level design only accommodates the sneak-wait-kill-repeat play style, and that is Isabelle’s connect ability. I was getting pretty frustrated trying to play D3 until I realized that these multi-cover guard formations are really designed around Isabelle.Her connect ability is tailor-made to address these formations, because when two guards are watching each other, you need to kill them both at the same time.Also, Isabelle’s mind control ability allows you to remove a guard from one of the complex cover formations, making it more manageable.I think the mind control ability captures the essence of the thinking that led to D3’s level design: why does it really matter where the guards are placed, if the player has the ability to just move a guard anywhere they want?The guns mostly just feel awkward. Kate and McCoy’s are a bit better, but the maps are just too crowded to use Cooper’s and Hector’s guns without setting off alarms. The obvious answer to this problem is to simultaneously kill everyone in hearing range of the gunfire, but then you’ve got those distant cover formations, which just makes the whole thing seem awkward, forced, and even cheesy, rather than the smoothness that I found so pleasurable in ST. Concluding thoughts… I heard something about Mimimi working with a certain “narrative development and consultation studio” known for their political ideology. I also noted there are some lines in D3 which seem to imply that Isabelle has a sexual interest in Kate. Whatever, I couldn’t care less, but when the game also seems to be lower quality than ST in level design, it all starts to have a familiar stink to it.

_childDocuments_.review: I love Desperadoes III.  (I might love its predecessor, Shadow Tactics: Blades of the Shogun, to which it is so very similar, just a little bit more, but that's neither here nor there.)  Mimimi's stealth-tactics formula is immensely satisfying.  I love stealth, I love tactics, and I love Mimimi's level design.  Each level is like a puzzle made of smaller puzzles, each of which usually has multiple solutions.  That allows for a lot of player creativity and does a much better job of making me feel clever than a more traditional puzzle with exactly one solution where I feel as though I'm expected to read the designer's mind or guess what he was thinking.In short, Desperadoes III is very, very good and you should definitely play it.  My only caveats are that the controls can feel a little imprecise at times and that unless you are sufficiently clever you may occasionally run into situations in the later levels where, due the real-time nature of the game, you will have to perform a bit of quick finger gymnastics.  I confess I am not always sufficiently clever.  Fortunately, the game has extremely fast quicksaves and quickloads.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun enough game, lots of enjoyment, but clearly a reskin of shadow-tactics. The story is cool and fleshes out the characters better than the original desperados and its interesting to see more of their back stories. The missions are interesting and trying to clear the maps is fun. Be prepared to reload a lot!Here are my complaints / room for improvements. Note that this doesn't indicate that I dislike the game. I would still recommend it. Maybe some fans of the game would agree with me below.1. Number 1 biggest complaint of this game. This game is fairly new but the AI of the enemies is quite awful. I am really bringing this up because the first game was made in 2001 and it had more realism in the AI than this 2020 game. Enemies would patrol around the map and would rally - it would really want you to prevent alerting anybody ever. Now in this game the AI pathing is pathetic. Like, I'd be embarassed to have programmed it if it was being compared to the game made 20 years ago. The complete randomness of the enemy patrol is unthreatening and braindead. Bottom line. Biggest disappointment.2. Minor, but some of the challenges can be soft-locked in missions or require many re-runs in order to complete. When I have to speed run a mission multiple times to get to the one part with the challenge, I get bored.3. Witch doctor that can possess people. Witch doctor doesn't really feel like she belongs in this genre or atleast in the period. Its a HARD sell for there to be magic in this game. I'm just not buying it. She's too overpowered too.4. Where was samuel? We get every character but him? What do you have against him?5. minor: I don't understand the healing mechanic of this game. by this I mean, why have it? Why let almost very character be able to do it? Why no resources and put it on a cooldown? This isn't call of duty and I found myself never using this mechanic ever.6. Why put weapons on a cooldown? What the hell? How does it make sense to only allow someone to shoot a gun once? I understand it would break your game the way you designed it, but maybe you shouldn't have made a shadow-tactics reskin and actually programmed something new?7. Glitch: I found this out by accident but it always works. If you are ABOVE a bush (like, say you are on a roof or a higher-up balcony), you can deposit bodies into the bushes without actually being anywhere near them. Simply rotate and position the map in a way that makes it LOOK like you are hiding a body in a bush and the body will disappear as if you are actually in the bush! Game breaking.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't recommend this game. Literally speaking, I personally don't. Is the game pretty and well produced? Do the controls flow well? Yes. I played it for a few hours during the free weekend and I didn't find it fun. The skills (and inabilities) are generic and spread out among different characters, the stealth is repetitive and the firearms are there to clean up or make you reload so you can do it stealthy again.The real tactics are in interpreting the map. By pressing H which highlights the traps, ladders, and other interactive objects so you can take out the enemies placed conveniently. You don't have to press H. You'll see the hints everywhere. If you have a sense for puzzles you'll know exactly what to do. Just don't time it horribly and you'll progress. Higher difficulty will punish your errors and make you reload more. The game gets interesting if you screw up and try to turn things around - but chances are you'll have to reload and redo it if you want to progress. With stealth. I can see why people wanted to pay for this. The other Desperados, Commandos and Shadow Tactics aged a bit and the replay value for this sort of game is what it is. There's not much to complain about, technically it's great, there is no frustrating moment, even in failure. So very few will say negative things. Maybe the free weekend helped more people realize that "Overwhelmingly positive" doesn't mean that a game is for everyone.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Second verse, same as the first.If you liked Shadow Tactics: Blades of the Shogun, you'll probably like this game.  The mechanics are identical, and with the exception of a few new abilities and a few swapped around (the big guy has the trap this time, for example), even the characters are mechanically pretty similar to their predecessors in Shadow Tactics.  The enemies are identical as well, with the little wrinkle that female characters aren't susceptible to the charmer's charms.  Basically, if you were comfortable with Shadow Tactics, you'll hit the ground running with Desperados III.So what does the game do better, what does it do worse, and what's just done differently? Starting with the good, the egregiously long legs of the characters in Shadow Tactics are gone, and the characters all have reasonable proportions now.  There's more information available, like how many guards in each region will spring out of their safehouses if you raise an alarm.  There are a few new abilities which can be used in very interesting ways.  Finally, the levels are all very sandboxy, perhaps even more so than in Shadow Tactics.The only complaint I have is the badge system - it's literally impossible to collect all the badges on a single playthough due to mutually exclusive rewards, forcing you to replay the game if you're a completionist.  And some that don't need to be exclusive are, like a badge for taking the left path and a separate one for taking the right.  Even if you clear out both sides, you only get one badge.  But given that the badges have no impact on the game itself, this sole quibble is an annoyance at worst.So what's just different? Well, the obvious things - it's a new setting, which means new maps, new characters, new music, and a new storyline.  All are quite good, but of course there's not much to compare between the two games in that regard.  Beyond that, I do feel Desperados III is a little easier than Shadow Tactics.  That can partially be attributed to my increased familiarity with the game and its mechanics, but there are more objective measures as well.  The levels only took about half as long to complete as the Shadow Tactics ones did, and only the final level put me over two hours (compared to over four hours for Shadow Tactics' finale).  And speaking of that last level, I had my doubts that I was at the end as I played through it because it seemed too easy to be the grand finale.  That's probably equal parts due to a more linear level design and the fact that you have all five characters available to work with (and they can meet up very early on), but it's still noteworthy.Overall, I enjoyed this game and would certainly recommend it to anyone, especially fans of Shadow Tactics: Blades of the Shogun.  The Western theme appealed to me more than the feudal Japanese one, and Desperados III certainly has more polish.  If you like the real-time tactics genre, definitely buy this.  If you're on the fence, wait for a sale and then buy it.  You won't be disappointed either way.

_childDocuments_.review: Once again we are back in the western era in United states, much like the setting of red dead redemption which we all have at the forefront of our memory.The game is a pretty decent and addictive piece. It can be frustrating at times, but very rewarding all the same. Much like dota 2, but without the hate and furiosity which is so common in online games. Clarification: I'm not saying it's like dota 2 gamewise, just what the game makes you feel.The game is stealth/strategic/puzzle/western-story, quite similar to commandos which you have probably heard of or even played some years or even decades ago. I don't think you will be disappointed picking this gem up, though the prize can come across as somewhat high for a game which is obviously not a Tripple A production, but rather a Double A one.The good+ Nice atmosphere+ Executing combos which works out well, is a total blast+ You will most certainly get a few elevated heart beat moments+ Nice voice actors and above average likeable characters+ Lots of replayability thanks to different challenges+ Gamepad and mouse/keyb-support which is well optimized for either setup. I play with both gamepad in front of TV as well as mouse/keyb in front of computer depending on mood and playstyle. The latter being somewhat more precise for challenge hunting.The bad- Graphics can feel somewhat dated and the character models a bit recycled for a 2020 game at almost full price tag, but the aesthetics are pleasing.- It feels as if the game sometimes doesn't execute the commands you intended which results in long series of quick loads. Thankfully, your last three saves are always available in case you accidentally save after you have ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up.- The controls can be quite clunky, even though it's probably hard to perform it otherwise.- Even though there is potentially 100eds of possible strategies to use, one tends to (I at least) fall back on what is tried and tested, resulting in problems being solved almost identically on every map. This esentially makes the game feel a bit repetitious, even though the difficulty bar constantly rises and the margin for error shrinks incrementally.Final score: 8/10 GreatGuide:1 - Abysmal2 - Miserable3 - Wretched4 - Bad5 - Half assed6 - Okay 7 - Good, 9 - Incredible, 10 - Amazing/Outstanding)

_childDocuments_.review: I'd describe this game as "Good but not great" If the price point were lower I'd have marked the review positive, but it doesn't live up to the expectation set by a £45 price tag. I passed on getting 2-3 other games to get this and having played the final level I don't feel like that was a great choice. If you're lucky enough not to have to care about money treat this review as positive.In a line this game is a very typical example of the isometric stealth tactics genre that delivers solidly on the key parts of the genre without doing anything outstanding.Compared to Shadow Tactics the interface is slicker, with the ability to speed up the game so guards move on their patrol paths being particular highlights. They've also added a challenge mode with special levels designed to make you use abilities in different ways or to avoid relying on your tried and tested solutions, which feels like a neat idea, but showing they're capable of making levels that avoid you relying on the same repetitive approaches just makes me question why that didn't happen more in the main game.The mechanics suit a western genre less than they suited a ninja genre. In Shadow Tactics creeping around stealthily taking people out makes you feel like a ninja. In Desperados refusing to use your guns in 95% of situations makes you feel like maybe you're not very good at this "western" thing.The characterisation felt a lot weaker. In part this is down to having established characters, while it's a reboot they're not going to do anything that surprising. It doesn't have any moment that comes close to the peak of Shadow Tactics, it's most dramatic moment felt more like "You appear to be acting differently to every other decision you've made so far in a really stupid way in order to have a dramatic moment". It also does a thing where it sets itself up for a little payoff (in a clumsy way but suited to the genre) and then squanders that in having one of those awful cutscenes where an arbitrary problem is introduced and then resolved without the player really being involved.I'm not sure that this is a genre that really suits sequels, getting to know characters and their personalities and capabilities is a big part of the game. I'd be much more interested in seeing a new isometric stealth game than either Shadow Tactics II or Desperados IV. Sticking to the established Desperados characters definitely hobbled it and it might meet a more positive reception from someone new to the series.Some of the design choices seem a bit poor. There's a tool to tell you who's watching a particular guard, but it doesn't work because a guard can stand on the edge of a vision cone such that they're technically not in vision but their hitbox changes slightly if they're dying so they're spotted by people who the UI said couldn't see them the moment it becomes important - the pixel perfect positioning in guard placement required to do this suggests bad UI has been implemented as a difficulty choice. Towards the end there's a section in which an action is queued by the game which will cause you to lose the level if it's carried out early, which is then triggered when you do anything with showdown mode, including clicking "Execute only this action" on a different action. Since there are some things that can only be done from showdown mode this arbitrarily limits a few abilities. There's not loads of stuff like this, more levels than not you won't encounter a single thing like it, but it comes up enough to be a ♥♥♥♥♥♥.It's still got very solid gameplay for the genre it's in. There's plenty of watching guard routes and forming a plan of attack and trying to figure out the perfect execution. A mix of guard types, terrain features, and player abilities stop it being as samey as it could've been. The new character introduces an ability I've not seen in other examples of the genre that opens up some genuinely new and interesting tactical options and is definitely the (mechanical) highlight of the game.If you liked Shadow Tactics, Desperados, and Commandos you'll probably have a decent time with this. "Good not great" means it's still good so if the genre is your cup of tea then you'd miss out not to play it, but maybe wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: From the creators of Shadow Tactics which was a superb game, the team has done it again and even better. Desperados III is the all new pinnacle of Real Time Tactics.  + Excellent gameplay.+ 2 New characters that are a great addition to the universe.+ Great progression to keep you hooked ( I played this straight throughout a long weekend).+ Improved gameplay from Shadow Tactics, now all of the characters can knock out and drag enemies; more versatility.+ Good story with suspense and some twists.+ Great voice acting and good chemistry between characters+ Great Wild West Setting.+ Unlike its predecessors, this game feels like the AAA of Real time tactics. + A significant improvement on the previous game, Shadow Tactics, especially in terms of versatility and a huge step forward for the genre especially in terms of being fast faced and accessible.  Warning: This game is very hardcore. Most people will probably get bored or give up. Do not buy this if you do not know what you are getting into. The first few hours for redemption will pass quickly but there is no guarantee you will finish the game unless you have lots of patience and will play until you win.If you are new to the genre better try an older game first, much cheaper and the same fundamentals.This is Desperados 3, a 2020 sequel to the 2000's Desperados game and a great entry into the series. It has stuck to the fundamentals of the genre, introduced two new characters and mechanics.With this game and Shadow Tactics, RTT is alive and kicking. While Shadow Tactics felt at times like a budget game, this one feels as much of a block buster as there can be in this small niche genre.It took me 24 hours to finish this game on a relaxed playthrough on normal difficulty trying to listen to all the lore and on some levels clearing out all enemies and always making sure no alarm is on. The rest of the time I spent getting badges and Steam achievements of which there are quite a few and some pretty challenging. After playing this I played Helldorado. Just don't. Shadow Tactics and Desperados 3 have made too much progress and set the bar very high for the genre now. Especially that these games can now be more fast paced and versatile.

_childDocuments_.review: A top-down stealth/shooter/strategy game where you play as a ragtag band of misfits in the West. There's a lot of depth to this game that, even on the second mission, you're looking at how best to approach each group of enemies. This only gets amplified with each character you add to your roster.One example of this, Cooper can do stealth takedowns at a range by throwing his knife, while Doc can throw his bag out to be seen on an enemy's patrol pattern to lure them in. Once they open that bag, it blinds them, and Doc can ambush. When you mix these two options, you need to weigh which one is better to use where, or if it'd be better to use in tandem with the other. If there's an enemy wearing a pancho, they will not go for Doc's bag, so it's better to use Cooper to take them out. Putting this in action, I used Doc's bag as a distraction for one enemy to pull his patrol pattern away from a Pancho that I had Cooper kill while the patrolling guy was distracted by the bag. When he got blinded, Doc stealth killed him.This game has many ways to approach each group of enemies. Stealth is the main focus so far, but is pretty satisfying to do. You could also just ignore a lot of them if you move right, and then there's going loud, which you'll find there's a time and place for.All in all, the game is beyond what I expected of it so far after picking it up for the sole reason of it being reviewed as overwhelmingly positive on here, and I absolutely look forward to whatever comes next.

_childDocuments_.review: If you ever liked Commandos 1 & 2, Desperados or Shadow Tactics, this is an easy buy for you. Beautiful graphics and animations, the puzzle-like environment you would expect, good level layouts. However, there are some points to consider: The story is... well, not really existant, it seems not really much is happening other than following the trail of one guy and some minor deviations on the way. I think the story of the original Desperados and Shadow Tactics was much more engaging. There are only 16 maps (+3 from the DLCs), with each map you probably will take 1 - 1,5 hours, coming up with a playtime of up to 30 hours maybe, for the first playthrough. However, there is so much replayability, challenges and so on, if you are really into it, you probably get more than 100 hours out of the game until all challenge modes are done. And yet, the original Desperados had 25 maps (if I recall correctly), maybe not so much replayability as Desperados 3, but the maps and environments there felt more engaging. Do not get me wrong, the maps in Desperados 3 are beautiful with a lot of details and showing some very nice locations (but also some very boring ones...), but Desperados 3 had whole towns engaged in fire fights, and more variety in map locations, so unfortunately the devs did not manage to keep up to this from my point of view. Technically the game is superb: controls, user interface, reaction - all is spot on, only on very minor occasions the controls are not precise (like you cannot issue to throw a body down while far from the cliff, you have to go there first manually, hence two orders instead of one). But all in all the game is a real joy to play, and the devs deserve all the support to continue to make such excellent games.

After trying the easier difficulty levels, I ended up playing the "Desperado" level which I would recommend to anyone who enjoys a sneaky-stealthy puzzle challenge that is never unfair or unsolvable.Well done Mimimi! _childDocuments_.review: Great game for those who love the top-down strategy "Commandos" genre especially for those who played Shadow Tactics and want more of that (though in a Western setting). In my opinion, the devs  got everything they did right with Shadow Tactics, fine-tuned them, then added some extra sauce. I liked this game so much that I recently bought Desperados: Wanted Dead or Alive just to have more of this.-----+ STORYTELLING: It's what I expected from a Western. Adventure. Tragedy. Revenge. Friendship. Guns. Explosions. It didn't attempt an complicated and as emotionally engaging a story as something like Red Dead Redemption but what it did simply, it did well.+ VISUALS: Comparing it to Shadow Tactics, they did away with the art style that I found really strange where the characters seem to be painted with Cray-pas in a beautiful 3d rendered world. Now everything fits together and is beautiful to look at.+ SOUND: Music, SFX, and Voice acting were excellent. I particularly love how when characters encounter each other in an area, they talk to each other or have some playful banter. It made me involved with the characters more than previous similar titles.------+/- GAMEPLAY: Not sure if I remember it right but there's some added gameplay elements here like the timed group and timed individual actions. While these are great additions to the game, it took me around 5 missions in to get familiar with the keyboard layout. I found it very complicated in the beginning as I felt like I was playing tense QTEs but with over 10 keys to press. It eventually became second nature by mid game and became crucial to some "puzzle" moments.

_childDocuments_.review: Really cool game, having a lot of fun with it for the very most part+ like the graphics and the scenery+ very cool mission design with great variety+ cool and creative indiviual character design/abilities+ cool features like showdown mode and lots of different interactable stuff+ quick save/load with automatically keeping last three quick savestwo things though i really don't like (sorry, second is a long one...)- badges should be visible sooner. maybe not before the mission so they don't spoil anything but maybe after the mission intro or once they become relevant within the mission. just feels like a really cheap and obvious way by devs to make you play each mission again ...- the difficulty of obtaining  the speedrun badges is just sooooo much higher than anything else in this game. now i personally don't like speedrunning at all, but i guess that's personal taste. i like watching them though. the game genre is however what i would consider the extreme opposite of a fast paced game. you often have to and are intended to take your time and observe situations precisely to come up with a strategy, even by going through many trial and error loops. speedruns of missions feel like you're playing a completely different game and i wouldn't think people playing mostly games of this genre are used to it/skilled at it just by default. i think in the last ten years i've only played two other games of this genre, which were one single playthrough of shadow tactics and desperados 2 (which i mainly played as a third person shooter). still i was able to beat this game on its highest difficulty on my first playthrough after ~40h while clearing ALL enemies on the maps. going for the speedrun badges however, even when i set the difficulty to lowest is just sooooo much more demanding and absolutely frustrating. it feels like you have to plan out the whole mission from start to end beforehand and have to time everything so precisely because you simpley do not have the time during a mission to plan anything or look at situations since time is always running even in showdown mode and the mission timer does not go back when loading. also it is just so frustrating if you realize near the end of a long mission that you barely cannot make it i time and you cannot even load a savegame but have to start the mission completely from scratch. the speedrun badges in general are maybe a cool idea for this game, being like "hey, just try this completely different approach to the game" and introducing players to it that otherwise maybe wouldn't have thought of trying it, but as it is so different to how the game in its "intended main mode" plays i think this should not make the very very very far most difficult challenge the game has to offer. in all honesty, when i've been playing through this game on desperados difficulty i've sometimes been playing for 6h straight and still wanted to go on. when i'm going for a speedrun badge (on beginner, with reading guides, etc.) i get sooo frustrated that i cannot play the game for longer than maybe 20min max and makes me want to uninstall ---> in short i think the speedrun badges should be far easier to achieve

_childDocuments_.review: Mimimi have done it again! Another brilliant title under the niche real-time tactics genre that appeared to be gone and forgotten only a few years ago. Mimimi had found the right formula for Shadow Tactics and have only improved upon that with Desperados III!This game has it all – interesting storyline, great level design, challenges that can be approached in a number of ways, memorable characters with diverse skills which allow for a myriad of combinations. Difficulty options make it accessible for newcomers to the genre. And while that’s not really my cup of tea, there’s a great potential for doing speedruns or trying to take on one of the challenges that get unlocked only after you complete a mission for the first time.One thing Desperados III really stands out for is that it came out as a fully completed and very well polished game. From day one, there were no non-negligible bugs/issues and having already completed it, it never felt like it would need to get DLC-ed before you can really enjoy it. While that used to be the standard some 15-20 years ago, all that is very rare nowadays so kudos to Mimimi for taking the time and effort to polish it that much before releasing it.Following the free content update released a few days ago, I’ve now invested 40+ hours in it. And that’s before the DLC’s that I’m eligible to receive having pre-ordered the game! While I’m certainly a completionist type of player, that’s definitely impressive for a single playthrough, i.e. no level re-runs, taking on challenges, etc.Overall, the game is very much worth the price. Can we have more of the same, please? It’s already perfect as is!

The story, graphics, and voice acting are all great. The western theme excited me more than Shadow Tactics (another game from Mimimi that I've been enjoying). The music, like most of the rest of the game, is amazing!If there were any cons it would be that sometimes the setup for a particular scenario takes a bit of work to get right, but it usually feels pretty rewarding once you've figured it out.I got this game on a discount, but I would buy it at full price given the quality and time I got out of the game. _childDocuments_.review: I was lucky to get an early copy of this game thanks to the guys at THQ Nordic (Thanks for hooking me up with the key!) and I’ve been playing this game steadily over the past month, while embroiled with editing and other projects.Made by Mimimi Games and published by THQ Nordic, Desperados 3 is an excellent sequel in the series, and by the same awesome guys who made Shadow Tactics.The gameplay…my word, the gameplay! You get a bunch of different, fleshed out characters, each with different and specified abilities, and you’re thrown a gauntlet of challenging missions to test your skills on. From Cooper’s knife throwing, loud guns and coin distractions, to Hector’s traps and axe play, to even some mind-♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ with Isabelle, you get a ton of options for completing the levels. The characters are well designed, and while I haven’t found anything particularly enthralling about the story, it’s serviceable and keeps me entertained.Shadow Tactics was known for it’s difficulty, and Desperados III is no exception. I’ve never been one for difficult games like this, so I look at my 38 hours played (by this article) and barely halfway through the game as a kind of humiliation. But it’s a good difficulty. The game blesses you with a no-penalty quick-save option and pause to plan your moves real time, and the sheer versatility and options it gives grants you a lot of replayability. I know i’ll be replaying this game on completion to try and get the achievements.As for flaws? There aren’t many. They did a really good job here. I have seen a few instances where my game refuses to load saves, forcing me to backtrack (though it may be to repeated quick saving and saving over them, causing corruption. Don’t abuse that mechanic like I have). The repetitive dialogue of the enemies when looking for you can also be a bit grating, but these are minor nitpicks. This is a chunky, well made game, and well worth its hefty price tag. Don’t be put off by that, give it a try.I rate Desperados III an easy 9/10. I’ll update the score when I finish the game, but I can already see this making my GOTY list in December. It’s that good.

_childDocuments_.review: pretty great follow up to shadow tactics: blades of of the shogun, albeit, not set in the same world or anything (obviously). i havnt played any other desperado games, and it didnt mater at all. this game builds on the parts that worked really well in STBS and it plays almost as the same game, only in a totally different setting. solid visuals. great characters, each with unique and useful abilities. multiples ways to approach any given level, and (finally) a real time pause feature to take the tactics to the next level. i know you can play gunz blazing, but i go stealth. one thing to note: the levels are huge, and if you are not going for the speedruns after really really knowing exactly what to do, be ready for each level to take potentially several hours apiece with a fair amount of reloading, and just staring at the guards walk around on their loops while trying to figure out where the weak point is, and how to get at them without setting off alarms (or you can just shoot them all but ammo is somewhat limited and alarms summon more guards). the plot is a little thin, but good enough to be believable for the characters' motivation for going on a massive killing spree, and there are a few pretty great reveals. the voice acting is solid (hector is my favorite), and the music is pretty good, albeit sometimes it feels a little repetitive (see earlier comment about level length). great game!my only critiques are that they overplay a few of the techniques in level design and are a little lazier with the badges than they were in the STBS. there are too many times when its a "good job you went on the left path," or the opposite, taking up two badges for what is essentially the same thing (and really just having the badge(s) be "you played the level twice"), and this happens on multiple levels, nor does it matter if you actually fulfilled the requirements for both badges, it only counts the first one you do, forcing you to replay the level to get the other one. i feel like there were very few of these style badges in STBS and that badges in general were often more creatively used than in this game. they also overplay the "you have to rescue some of your characters before you can use them in the level" mechanic too often. im also bummed that the cat isnt NEARLY as good as the tanuki from the last game (but will also admit that the rest of that character's abilities are amazing!).

_childDocuments_.review: Didn’t play their first game, but after playing Desperados III I’m going to have to go back. Desperados is simply fantastic, it never becomes too difficult to manage, but forces you to plan and perfect your maneuvers. You simply are not going to ever pass through without failing, that’s what makes the quicksave/quickload system fit so well. Sometimes you can picture what you want to happen, you’re just going to need to perfect the sequence of actions you will take to get there, and there is little penalty to experimentation. Of course, if every level required the same strategy, then you wouldn’t need to utilize that experimentation, but this is where the designers really show off their skills. Each level has varying objectives and the cast changes so you’re never quite comfortable.  The characters are of course varied and each one is capable enough to not allow you to bench someone. Those synergies are the real core of what you are going to be perfecting and where each character’s strengths are going to shine. Not to overly gush here, but even the story is fun. I really expected to skip most of it, but it plays out in such a way that it keeps you interested, and the characters are just fun to hear.  I would highly recommend this game to strategy fans or really just video game fans in general, it’s my GOTY so far.

_childDocuments_.review: Did you ever play Commandos back in the day? Well, Desperados is Commandos with cowboys, right down to the character archetypes.Okay, okay, let's get some detail. Desperados III is a character-based RTS, but before you scream "HotS, LoL" and run off, this is far more of a stealth puzzler than an action game. The plot (and it is entirely a campaign-driven game here, no MP) involves a handful of heroes from different walks of life fighting back against the predatory DeVitt railroad company. In doing so, you will be employing their special skills and dodging from cover to cover, hiding bodies in bushes as you go along and mashing the quicksave key like it fed you morphine.(Seriously, the quicksave/quickload functions are pointed out to be used , because you will screw up over and over and over again and need to jump back in time to when your characters didn't misbehave in the middle of a complicated move order.)Pausing to coordinate your actions is key, which is also why this wouldn't work as a multiplayer game. You'll quite frequently slam the "Showdown" button to pause the action and assign your characters to do their things all at once, because enemies will not hesitate to call for backup the moment anything is amiss and you'll need to handle a number of challenges in the same instant. It becomes a murderous football plan from John Madden's more violent dreams:"You toss the exploding bag to distract that guard, while you throw a knife at this other guy while the first is facing the other way, and  run over and tie up the guard who just got knocked out and toss his body down the well before anyone turns around, then run for that bush." When you line up the perfect moment and it all gets pulled off flawlessly, you'll feel great. More often than not, you'll be saving/loading to jockey your characters into the sightlines they need while staying out of enemy vision cones, or when you accidentally make a little too much noise and forget about the guy on the rooftop who sees much farther than you'd think they would.The levels are in full 3d and can be rotated and zoomed. You don't have full camera control, which is fine because you can easily highlight every enemy and object permanently at the touch of a button. The game wants you to succeed, but it doesn't pull punches: enemies have overlapping fields of vision and patrols, and your task is always to figure out how to untangle the web of killzones to slip your characters to the next objective.It is possible to go non-lethal, which is particularly challenging. All characters can "punch" instead of their "melee kill" option, and most can tie up KO'd foes to carry them to hiding places. I started out that way, but the allure of the various lethal options (plus the unsympathetic nature of the enemies as the plot went on) had me laying out bad gays with grim satisfaction.My biggest complaint is with the controls; with so many functions available the "default" option uses a terribly unconventional method of Arrows + Mouse, with other important controls clustered around the right side of the keyboad + numpad. As awkward as it was, I could not find a custom control assignment (and they do let you reassign anything) that worked for me better than the default.My other complaint is that characters will stop doing their assigned orders if you pause the action and assign someone else an order, because it reassigns the first character's order to "nothing," causing them to halt smack wherever they are when you paused the second time (usually in the middle of sneaking up on an enemy who will then turn around and discover them a moment later). I would much rather characters kept doing what they were told to do unless I tell them to stop.These learning curves aside, the game is satisfying and looks quite good with as dense as the environment is. When you finish a mission, you get to see a full-map view of all enemies and your characters's paths moving about as you played the level, compressing an hour and a half into a couple of minutes to make you look like a strategic mastermind (cutting out all your failures and showing you only your final success, though it does note how and where you loaded the game).

_childDocuments_.review: Desperados 3 really lived up your expectation exactly what you got from Shadow Tactics. It is exactly same experience you got from ST but with different settings and story. The gameplay they offer are the same from what ST got, even the skill set (just on different characters). I recommend this game if you love the previous ST game.The story itself is your average-typical revenge story, nothing special, though their story-telling is just as good as ST. The connection between characters looks good with their own personality they bring.The gameplay will as good as you remember back when playing ST, just with western style. Though, the level design (I think) is easier than ST. Every success strategy you pull will gives you satisfaction-- or frustrated when you failed. Save-and-reload scum still your best friends, with each mission will take approximately 1-3 hours depending on your strategy.There are a total 16 mission plus 3 from DLC, with its own badge to collect so you have tons of replayability if you are a completionist. The three part mission from DLC is decent, and will take you longer than your average main-story duration. When you complete them all, you still have challenges mode and bounty mode, which gives you a lot more of hours of gameplay.Soundtrack is decent, but not masterpiece. It certainly gives the exact ambient you need for your western game, enjoyable I'd say.Main story and DLC will takes you 30-35 hours. Add that up with challenges mode for another 5-10 hours. _childDocuments_.review: As with all games, it's down to personal opinion. I have really enjoyed it, however it won't be to everyone's taste. The gameplay is slow and methodical, with each action requiring precision timing and planning, so those looking for something fast paced will definitely want to look elsewhere. The levels are well thought out, and can be completed in a variety of ways. I personally enjoyed taking 2 hours on each and trying to take out all enemies before reaching the final objective.Each character at your disposal has their own individual skills and abilities, and getting them to function as a team is rewarding as you make your way through the map. Saving frequently is essential, as quick loading following a mistake is very frequent. This will be frustrating to some, but I enjoyed learning from mistakes and re-planning attacks. Helpfully, the game informs you when you haven't saved for a minute, which is very welcome given you will be saving constantly throughout missions.I may only have around 20 hours clocked at the time of writing, but I can already see considerable replay value with various challenges available for each level. You don't need to be a fan of the Wild West to enjoy this title, and for those looking for a rewarding stealth game, this deserves consideration.

_childDocuments_.review: is a real-time tactical stealth game developed by Mimimi Productions and released on 16 June 2020. In  you play as Cooper and his band of outlaws on a quest for revenge. Desperados 3 successfully expands on 2016’s ’s commando-like mechanics. While it doesn’t revolutionize the formula, it polishes and improves upon its predecessors on level design, map density, extra features, graphics and audio. In short  is a stellar successor to the genre. Players control between 1 to 5 people (depending on the mission) to achieve certain objectives. The objectives vary from eliminating enemies on the map, reaching a certain destination or interacting with certain objects in the game. Players control the characters in real time, with a pause button that allows them to queue actions to execute later. Enemies have a vision cone. If you right-click on them, their vision cone will appear on the ground. There are 2 types of detection areas: clear and striped. Clear green areas means any characters and objects are visible to the enemies. If you stay too long inside the green area, enemies will attack you and raise an alarm. Striped areas means your character can move through it safely if they are crouched. Striped areas are usually the spot behind short objects, or unlit areas at night. Some enemies might carry torches that turn striped areas into green one. Bushes are safe areas you can never be detected unless the enemy is directly touching you. Almost every action creates sound. If enemies are within the sound circle, they will be alerted even when you aren’t in their vision cone. Actions such as shooting with guns will have a large sound range, and throwing knives are more silent and attract only enemies in direct vicinity. There are surfaces that make loud sounds so even walking can attract enemies. Stealth is a very crucial part of the game. If you rush into enemies’ dens they will take a short work of you as you are outnumbered heavily. There are several types of enemies. Regular enemies are weak and distractible. They can be lured out of their posts and patrol. Enemies wearing ponchos are more disciplined so they cannot be lured or moved. Heavy are tough, and can only be taken down by one particular character or you need several characters coordinating. to take them out. Dogs can sniff you out even behind bushes.There are 5 playable characters each that bring their own array of tools and abilities to your arsenal. Almost all the character’s abilities can be separated into 2 categories: Offense and Distraction. Offense are the abilities that allow Cooper and .co to remove enemies from the level. These abilities can be lethal or non-lethal.Non-lethal attacks will leave enemies stunned for a time and if you don’t tie them up, they will wake up and resume their routine. Lethal actions are faster and safer. The game never forces you to use either of them nor it has consequences narratively. Non-lethal actions have their practical uses in certain situations, but the choices are mostly self-imposed restrictions by the player for either completing extra challenges to earn badges or just role-playing. You can hide bodies in bushes or throw them into wells and water to remove them permanently. Distractions are skills that allow the characters to attract attention, lure them to certain positions so it gives you time and opening to either take enemies out or slip past them. The 5th character has a slightly different, powerful skill set aside from offense and distraction. One of them is a “link” that allows 2 enemies to be linked, so whatever happens to one (like dying or distracted) happens to the other one. She can also take control of an enemy. The environment can be used to kill or distract enemies. Examples of these actions are dropping a boulder on top of their heads or putting off lamps and torches to lure enemies to light them back. Some levels also contain areas where you can leave footprints. If these footprints are within green vision cones, certain types of enemies will come and investigate your steps. Lastly, you can distract enemies with bodies. This is where the mechanical usage of non-lethal takedown comes into play. Upon discovering dead bodies enemies will immediately raise alarm and take more aggressive behavior. Discovering a knocked out person, they will just untie them and investigate around the perimeter but don’t raise alarm. All the elements combined create a fun, challenging gameplay. There is satisfaction in seeing your plans executed successfully. While it requires a lot of trial and error, the game has an easy quicksave and quickload option where you can easily access the last 3 quicksaves you made. Combined with outstanding level design, and even denser enemy population compared to previous games,  is a worthy successor to the long line of commando-like games. My main criticism is the fifth character’s abilities are too powerful and make trivial of most areas she’s in. The other 4 feel fairly balanced and each brings and complement each other, so the balance of the game can feel off whenever she’s usable. None encountered and ran 60 FPS perfectly in any situations.Overall the game looks good. It’s not fantastic, but it is an improvement over  by a huge margin. Character models look good at the distance you're looking at them from. they are animated well especially in cutscenes. Environment looks great and there is a good amount of variety from towns, to swamps and train bridges. There might be some spot on rocks or ground where the texture looks low resolution, but mostly the game looks good.The game sounds crisp and well-done. Several characters wield different weapons and their sounds are noticeably different, footsteps react to the surfaces you’re on and the ambient sound effects are spot-on. The named characters are well-voiced, but NPCs can feel samey like there are only 4 voice actors to fill the whole game. It can feel a bit jarring because there are at least 2 dozens of enemies on the map. Music is fantastic. It really depends on how you like western cinema music but the tracks are great in my opinion. The story is a typical wild west revenge story. It’s nothing special, but I like the chemistry and camaraderie between the characters. Desperados 3 is a fantastic stealth game, and improved upon every aspect of its predecessor. It is polished, challenging, and importantly fun. The gameplay is flexible, replayable and filled with extra challenges if you crave more challenges. If you love the stealth genre, this is the game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Desperados III is among the best games i have played this year and saying that after beating 125 titles during that timeline with few of turdaloos which did remove from the account.If you loved Shadow Tactics or even liked it, Desperados III will feel the same for the most part while feeling improved variously in gameplay. One thing that Shadow Tactics has over Desperados III is graphical style and seasons of the maps, like ones with snow and other hand very colourful summer maps. While Desperados III did have mostly very rocky/sandy surfaces in it.Gameplay and UI is really great, while similar to what ST had, it feels that it's easier to pull out tricks and do them in time than previously and on top of that you have the fast forward to use if you miss tight window to pull out the action without enemies noticing you. Getting timings right in group actions also feels better now from what remember it being in ST.Story is great with good voice-acting and music is amazing, especially the menu theme. Let it play for a while in background. Mimimi team has surely picked the blast from the past genre and bringed it to this day amazingly well in these two titles which both gave me 30h of great time in one play through, that is very long game time when compared to average.

_childDocuments_.review: Truly a masterpiece, a real homage to the original game. I have not played the sequels of the series before this, but I could say that this one is a must play if you like RTS like Commandos or Shadow Tactics. Especially on summer sale!What I like about the game is the fact that you can proceed with your choice however you like. The game constantly give choices whether you want to proceed on the left section of the map or the right one. Not to mention the unique mechanic of each characters also produce unique experience.I also like the showdown, a mechanic that is similar to shadow mode from Shadow Tactics. The original Desperados already has this mechanic which is quiet futuristic for their planning. I can't remember Commandos and its sequels has this mechanics or not. I only remembered using it once when I was little, it was also because it was forced (as in you would die if you don't use it) event. But in Desperados 3, I am completely addicted to using it.I like to play as the the blow dart character, Isabelle Moreau who is as fun as Mia Yung, another blow dart user from the first game. I don't know if it is a homage to Mia or not, but I really can't hide my excitement when I first play as Isabelle. Too bad on the first game you can only play Mia for a limited stage. But rejoice! In Desperados 3 you can play every character after you finish the stage. Which means you can play as Isabelle from other missions!I am really thankful that I can enjoy this game!RIP Mimimi games. May you rest in piece legend.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a masterpiece. Mimimi has built on everything that made their previous game, Shadow Tactics: Blades of the Shogun, great; they've refined the gameplay, created more excellent levels, have another compelling cast of well written, wonderfully voice acted characters within a equally great story, the characters skillsets are familiar but not identical, the characters are more balanced and unique this time around (for example, the character that can hitman disguise can no longer permanently incapacitate enemies on her own unless she shoots them, but has a new lure ability and has had her pistol silenced to make up for the nerf. This makes the game more engaging since you can't run around in disguise killing isolated enemies for most of the level.) Visually the game looks fantastic.Desperados III is flawless and the future season pass content will likely only add even more polished content to an already perfect game.

_childDocuments_.review: It's hard to write a review about Desperados without drawing from the previous games or Commandos as an example. Desperados III is a modern take on Stealth-oriented RTS games. With a modern UI and engine, they have outdone themselves from their previous game Shadow Tactics: Blades of the Shogun.I personally wasn't able to play these types of games as a kid (don't ask me about Hitman). These games were hard to get started and harder to master. However the developers did an extraordinary job to give you motivation to complete the maps. My mentality changed from: "Oh no a 2hr long mission" to "Damn it's already been 2hrs??". They have implemented such a great variety of ways of completing the map that the game really motivates you to play with your playstyle. Personally, I have been re-completing missions on Desperados difficulty after one playthrough re-applying tricks I've learnt.TL:DR If you were a fan of Commandos, Desperados, Shadow Tactics: Blade of the Shogun, or wanting to get into the genre, you will definitely want to grab this. In my opinion, it's easier to get into compared to Shadow Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: I had high expectations for the game since Shadow Tactics was such a masterpiece. Truth to be told, I am a bit disappointed. My disappointment comes from a weak story and a bit of boring gameplay in the first chapter. At the start of the second, you'll get your fifth character, Isabelle, which is essential, overpowered, and simply fun to play with. On the other hand, there are things which went great. The level design is amazing! In sixteen maps, you don't have a feeling of repetition. Voice acting and soundtrack are both excellent. Overall it's a good game, but I have trouble seeing it as better than Shadow Tactics. And I like the western theme way more than the Japanese theme. (15.08.2021)So I returned to do all the additional content, Baron challenges, and the DLC. I have to say I had more fun playing those. Baron challenges are surprisingly unique and indeed bring a challenge to the table. I have a slight issue with how much freedom and possibilities you have in the main story, and Baron challenges fix exactly that. The mission with train and shooting only was the most memorable. Badges try to solve the same issue, but the execution is horrible. There are two types of badges without any distinction, and the list is hidden in the first playthrough. Plus, I really don't like the speedrun one. While it is justifiable, it's still a tactical game. Anyway, the DLC brings back freedom, but I liked the story. I just wish there would be more character development, interaction, and, hell, even cinematics. I simply want more story, because the characters are fantastic! Overall I have now more positive experience with the game, and I can say it's on par with Shadow Tactics.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Great game, worth the buyWhen it comes to gameplay, Desperados 3 is much the same as its predecessor, Shadow Tactics. Don't expect any major new features. Isabelle is the only character with abilities veterans won't be familiar with, but then again, why re-invent the wheel?Where this game shines is in the areas of level design, atmosphere and content. The story mode consists of 1 tutorial and  missions that vary in length, but all were somewhere between 1 and 2.5 hrs for me. All come with special challenges, like in Shadow Tactics, so there's lots more for completionists.The  Baron's Challenges are a new addition. These take you back to levels you're already familiar with, but with different combinations of characters and objectives.The scenario is great, the characters are awesome and you get everything you'd want out of a Western story: .All in all, Mimimi has delivered the perfect follow-up to the already magnificent Shadow Tactics.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game about a band of sneaky cowboys who seem to prey exclusively on a gang of handicapped outlaws. The banditos all suffer from some sort of retinopathy that reduces their peripheral vision,  partial deafness, and some sort of very serious memory impairment. How they could ever have been productive members of society is beyond me -no wonder they turned to a life of crime. It might sound like the solution to this would be to increase the difficulty, but it's already a pretty challenging game because you have to brutally murder SO MANY of these handicapped people. The main characters all seem to enjoy murder though, so that's good for them I suppose, though it's deeply unsettling to hear things like "it's never enough!" in reference to the number of people one can stab in the back.There are 4 main characters, but once you unlock the sexy cowgirl it's pretty much over because she has the ability to walk into a group of bandits and lure them away one by one without any ever stopping to wonder why their friends (and soon-to-be eskimo brothers) never returned from the exact same rendezvous she is now offering them. There is also a Mexican cowboy. He is drunk and sleepy. You will want to skip all the dialogue and you should, it doesn't matter.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to start off by saying that I usually hate games that make you control multiple characters. I knew coming into this game what I was getting myself into, but even so I just couldn't get myself to play the game for a week or two after I had done the first (real) mission. The second I had to control a second character I just wanted to quit the game and never think about it again. Still, that week or two where I was not playing the game I was constantly thinking about the amazing sound, voice acting, graphic style and the small bit of gameplay that I had gone through and what the game might offer if I just force myself to play it for a little longer.Fast forward a week or two and I finally sit down and get myself to play the next mission, this time telling myself that I would go through that mission no matter what. Well let me tell you that was one of the best decisions I've ever made. Not only did I start enjoying both the gameplay and story, but I basically got addicted to the game. Even though I was playing on hard and sometimes got stuck it usually just got me more excited and determined to finish that mission. It's been a long time since I've actually played a game to enjoy it and not wanting it to end, instead of mindlessly rushing towards the end.If you enjoy the tactical stealth genre there is no question that you will enjoy this game. It provides a good bit of challenge on the higher difficulties and has some nice extra challenges in each mission if you want to challenge yourself even further. For those either new to the tactical stealth genre or are like me that either don't like the genre or don't like controlling multiple characters; try it. If you are playing it for the gameplay I very highly suggest playing on either Hard or Desperado difficulty as it becomes a completely different game. Other than that - just enjoy the ride as I have.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played through Commandos I & its DLC, Commandos II, Shadow Tactics: Blades of the Shogun, and now this game.This is the best RTT game in the market as of Dec 2020. The story of the game is at about 8.5/10, music is at about 9.5/10, and it's graphic is at about 9/10. The mechanic of the game is quite similar to the Shadow Tactics: Blades of the Shogun, but the level design has been the best for all the RTT that I've ever played, which is the most important part for this genre at 11/10.Each of the 5 characters have his/her unique abilities, and advancing every corner of any mission requires the development of cleaver strategies to utilize them. This is not a type of game for every gamer, but if you enjoy RTT games and/or their elements, this is the game that can't be missed. The German developers has done a awesome job of keeping this genre alive and making it better than ever. Watching/reading different coverage of them makes me think that they really treat this game with good passion, knowledge, and seriousness, and that reflect perfectly on the game.  I streamed and completed the game and its 3 DLC missions on the Desperodo (hardest) difficulty while killing all enemies melee with no injury and no alarm. I met some awesome people while doing this challenge, which includes the voice actor of Hector (a character in game). It was a very memorable 60+ hours.Special thanks to my friend Rexgar, who gifted me this game and its DLCs.

_childDocuments_.review: As these have failed this year:- warcraft 3 reforged- darksiders genesis- black mesa final xen chapters- doom eternalMimimi delivers a great game - as expected. Great game!The good:+ low budget but stylish cutscenes+ good voice overs+ game looks great+ runs super smooth+ cohesive story+ skippable cutscenes+ demo available pre-release+ fluid gameplay+ great atmoshpere+ great music building up tension+ character conversations done right+ ultra fast quick save/load+ just as quick load and save (except for first time load of the map)+ amazing maps+ alternative routes+ guards notice missing colleagues+ nice animations with Doc holding his hat when running for example+ different ways to finish the maps+ suitable for hardcore and casuals (with extra difficulty setting)+ additional challenge mode+ maps can take long to finish depending on your approach, but do not frustrate at any point, it's pure fun all the way, you learn different secrets and more optimal paths each time you play+ fleshed out differences between characters+ snow mechanic expanded to water surfaces, mud, dust - adding variety+ learning to use the environment to your advantage+ multi-stage levels+ after loading a save game you action does not start immediately, you are given a prompt to click so that you can better control it in tight situations+ 3 quick save slots+ showdown mode+ killing enemies, that had a particularly hard setup is soooo satisfying+ complex architecture+ environmental kills+ beware of the chickens!The bad (none of the below ruins the game or makes it unplayable, just a suggestions to devs what needs fixing):- difficulty seems uneven a bit- minor issues with pathing- some animations get stuck/janky
