_childDocuments_.review: This game was a lot of fun! Had not really played a RTS game in years (mostly RPG / turn based strategy / Building type of guy) but after having seen a couple of Lets Plays of this one definitely wanted to give it a shot.This one is very reminiscent of the old Commandos games i enjoyed a lot back in the day.I really like the Wild West setting too + various other settings like New Orleans / Swamps etc.All the maps have been beautifully created with a very cool style.I enjoyed the story and characters a lot too. Made you care that much more about the missions.Now the game is by now means perfect obviously... the main flaw for me? Its too darn short.I played on the easy mode (hard enough for me at least for a first playthrough) and i managed to get through all 16 missions in 28 hours. That is rather quick for a 50 euro game to be honest...Luckily the game does offer plenty of replay value. I dont think i am the type of guy to do a mission 10 times or more but i ll definitely try em all once or twice more.The game has a 'badges' system (which are revealed after first playthrough) with unique challenges like 'dont kill anyone' 'dont wear a disguise' 'dont use this character's skills etc.' you can aim for in future playthroughs.Also a lot of the later missions have two paths you can take towards your goal which by itself gives one a reason to try the mission again.All in all i d have loved to see a lot more missions but i have no idea how hard it is to churn these out. I am definitely looking forward to seeing more future missions though!The developers also seem to have added Baron Challenges. I THINK they ll keep adding new ones? They take place on existing maps and offer you more challenges to keep playing the game.All in all a very enjoyable game with fun characters and challenges but a bit short.I have no idea how crazy / impossible it is but a custom map / scenario creator mode for players would be an amazing addition i think!

_childDocuments_.review: This is undeniably one of the best games I've ever played. With a campaign that took over 40 hours, gorgeous graphics, and a soundtrack that is comparative to John Williams, Desperados III is one crazy adventure. There are 16 levels, and each feels unique and different from the last. This game will force you to think in new ways, adapting to different scenarios in real-time. There is a great deal of replayability here, with countless challenges for each level, such as not using any of a certain character's skills or taking a difficult route. I would recommend this game above any else that I have played, and highly encourage anyone reading this to buy it as soon as possible.

_childDocuments_.review: Welcome to "Shadow Tactics 2: No Guns Allowed"!There are other much better reviews that outline what I don't like about this game but let me summarize it for you:1) Guns have limited ammo. I can deal with that. What I can't deal with is the low amount you are allowed to carry. Would it have been too hard to give each gun their seperate chamber? Or too easy if we had more?2) Guns have cooldown. You are forced to go the stealth route. No quickly shooting three guys that inconvenience you. Nope.3) The skills are almost carbon copies of the ones in Shadow Tactics. Cooper has a Ninjato (Knife), Shuriken (Throw Knife), Throw rocks (Coins) and has two (wow) guns that share ammunition (Whole 8 shots! How generous /s). He probably doesn't have bandages because that would be too obvious.I thought playing a younger John Cooper would be a neat idea and it is. In theory. But if you take pre-existing characters and change them because they wouldn't fit your contrived stealth game otherwise than why not just create a whole new cast in the first place?Nostalgia makes a lot of money and this game is not worth that money. At least for the price they are asking.Don't get me wrong. The game is good. And I would like to play it eventually. But I will wait until the price is lowered. Because to me, this game is not fun. There is nothing "Wild" in this West. Please give players the option to go loud because that's what made the original so great. Maybe introduce a skill tree where you can tweak your characters towards a certain play style and watch them grow as they are becoming the bunch of badasses I know and love from the first game.But for now I will play the first Shadow Tactics again. The gameplay fits so much better with ninjas against muskets.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: After some thinking, I actually changed my opinion to a thumb down. While there's nothing really wrong with the game, I feel like the full prize would just be too much for a game that is essentially the very same puzzle game that Shadow Tactics was, but with slightly different graphics. It has the same issues (some people may actually think of them as features rather than problems, but I don't), and it's doesn't feel like the Old west any more than ST felt like Old Japan. If you're interested, wait until it's properly discounted, that's the best way to get real bang for your buck, otherwise you're just in for a bit of a disappointment unless you played ST previously and are still having wet dreams about it.Original: Does what is says on the tin. Yet perhaps a slight disappointment, if I'm honest, but as there is nothing essentially wrong with it, I don't want to give it a thumb down. It is a Commandos-style game, but it shares some of the same issues it's predecessor, Shadow Tactics had: the various characters are not really THAT different from each other. All but one are capable of doing the melee kill, which it what you'll be using 98% of the time. The system is utterly merciless when it comes to your dudes getting spotted, it's literally 1 millimetre or 1 fraction of a second that separates a clean kill from an ALARM that practically requires you to reload the quicksave since the UI and the game mechanics don't allow for a very flexible combat to occur once you've been spotted. At least this time the map design is slightly better than what it was in Shadow Tactics, but still I often get the feeling it's simply an exercise in getting from A to B and killing all the guards in between. The biggest issue is that just as in Shadow Tactics it didn't really FEEL like I was in Old Japan, Desperados III doesn't feel like I'm in the Old West. Both games are just too sterile somehow, they feel like puzzle games (which of course they are) with really pasted on themes that fail to fully immerse the player. If you're looking for a proper Commandos-style game, go for the Partisans 1941, it's captures the feeling much better and feels much more like a TACTICS game instead of a PUZZLE where there is only one correct solution.
_childDocuments_.name: Desperados III

_childDocuments_.review: A delight from start to end. I've played and replayed and re-replayed almost every level.Every minute is like a puzzle, trying to figure out the perfect way to kill, sneak past, or distract the obstacles in your way. It's often very challenging, but because of the ease of save states (and the encouragement of 'abusing' it), even the longest and most difficult stages rarely feel frustrating or anger-inducing. The game is tough, but it also gives you tons of options and freedom to get past every hurdle as you see fit. Add some great voice acting and writing, and you've got a real underrated gem, and one of the best games I've had the honor of playing in the last few years.
_childDocuments_.name: Desperados III

_childDocuments_.review: Well made levels allow each character to make good use of their skills. Excellent ability synergy. Even on the last level I was finding new ways to use characters together. An item like Doc's bag drawing the attention of enemies seems limited compared to other abilities until you combine it with Kate's lure or Cooper's coin, etc. Allows for more aggressive play but not to the extent you can just shoot everyone by moving your characters together and luring all the enemies to you like in the first game. Guns now have limited ammo and a cooldown but make much less noise. Challenge levels that change existing map's goals and characters, the game has five now and more are supposed to be added over time through updates. Three DLC missions for people that bought early or the season pass are still be to released.Poor pathfinding at times. They would take the long way to their objective, won't jump down paths, instead of just walking right to the nearby spot might climb a wall for no reason than take a ladder to it, or get confused when obstacles are partially blocking a path they can still fit through.Easy recommendation for fans of the old Desperados or Commandos games or for the developers previous game Shadow Tactics Blades of the Shogun.Screenshots:

_childDocuments_.review: Well, as someone who played the old Desperados games but never played a Mimimi game before this, I will admit and say I was a bit cautious. I haven't heard of Mimimi and didn't know what to think. I was excited about a new game coming out since a new one hadn't been released for over a decade.I did not watch any of the trailers for the game, but I did pre-order it. And I do not regret that choice one bit.The story, being a Prequel to the first game, is very well written and cleverly constructed. Seeing how everyone met one another, be it old characters like Doc McCoy or Kate, or new characters like Hector or Isabelle, and how they all worked up to being a brilliant team by the end of it... It was honestly so fun and exciting. The setting, the music and the many different levels, they all made the game feel much like the original Desperados. And it was both nostalgic, yet refreshing. The new concepts for me have been the "Showdown Mode" and the challenges. While I was initially confused by the Showdown Mode, I quickly saw how much it adds to the game, by being an option mode and not a mandatory one. Then the Challenges just give more reasons to go back to different levels and try and achieve them all, which I love as a concept. I haven't done it yet, but I am certain I will.Overall, Mimimi Games (And all the devs that I keep killing), have done a brilliant and beautiful job with the newest installment of Desperados. I cannot wait until the DLC missions come out, just to see what other little missions the team has in store for them.

_childDocuments_.review: Around 5 or 6 missions finished on hard difficulty and I can say it's an excellent real-time tactics game, super addictive and fun which is awesome because it was kinda a blind purchase on my side - I saw a lot of hype surrounding the Mac/Linux release and I decided to jump on the hype train as well.It's all about stealth and strategy, controlling multiple characters, each one with different abilities. The game has a story and characters who are not only well narrated but also have personalities and pursue their own goals. Audio is great and graphics is nice for a top-down game (as long as you don't zoom in too much but that's common for this genre).Missions usually take an hours or two, the game encourages save-scumming and trial&error as a game mechanic and indeed, trying and failing is fun.Performance is top-notch, 1660 Ti can handle either 1080p maxed out 150+ fps or ~4K (1080p with 200% rendering resolution) also maxed out ~60 fps. I found my personal compromise on 160%. I used to dislke Unity games for their (usually questionable) perfomance but this one changed my mind. What's more surprising, they managed to achieve this with OpenGL. No stability issues, no problems, perfect port.If you like stealth and strategy, I think this game can't disappoint you.

_childDocuments_.review: Very well put together game so far!I have played 2 to 3 hours and have had a great time so far.The game is pretty much the Stealth Genre, mixed with Immersion Sims and Strategy. It is real time and very tactical! You have many options for how to get through missions. Think of the options you have in say Hitman, Shadow Tactics or Deus Ex for how to get something done, the view is Isometric though. Vets of the Commandos and Desperados games will like this wonderful new game, but also people who never played the previous Desperados games can get on this and have a blast. Just as good for a new player as it is for a vet. This is technically the 3rd game but this Desperados 3 is a prequel of sorts so as I said above, new players should enjoy this game to.If you like the devs previous game, you are going to LOVE this game!Western setting, Isometric view, real time combat, tons of creative ways to kill people in the Old West, whats not to love! The music and Voice work are also very well done. Can't wait to jump into this more tonight and later this week! Nice surprise this game!Another great game from Mimimi Games, Shadow Tactics was very well done and so is this one! The combat is real time but you have the ability to pause the game and execute a plan that you can take your time with.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a reskin of Shadow Tactics: Blades of Shogun. Well, original Desperados series is actually older, but the engine is the same, the skills are pretty much the same - just rotated, the enemy level system and even character archetypes are same. It's a bit smoother and more devious/figured out, but there's a lot of "same".Which is okay, ST:BoS was an excellent game. What's less okay is the parts that aren't "same". Music of Shadow Tactics was extremely good. Story of Shadow Tactics was also quite good. So was level design. Characters were super loveable. Well, that's not same here. The characters won't make you love them. You won't cry when story takes a dark turn mid-game, and you won't cry again at the last level because music composer did godlike work for that one final track that puts your entire 30-something hour journey into piece of music (track called The Death of Noboru). None of those emotions exist in Desperados 3. It's just a Mimimi Games' victory lap, showing they've mastered and monopolized (in terms of quality) the revival of RTT genre.Also, the style of the game doesn't fit cowboy theme that well. Sure, I could try hard and remember all those stealthy knockout moments and tense firefights from Karl May's "Winnetou" series books, but still, for that to work, a game needs a story. Being a western, a strong story. Antagonists, schemes, danger. Desperados 3   to have a story, but hundred faceless enemies don't really fit a western and the story never grabs you. And while the soundtrack is passable and voice acting is pretty good, you never truly grow to love the characters so it all sort of brushes off. And ninjas are just so much cooler.When you dismiss the story, "Challenge" missions actually make way better experience, because they dump the learning process and try to be more original with goals and characters.The main attraction of this game is voodoienne Isabelle with interesting skill set, but due super tight way the mechanics work, she's  creative. Her mental bind ability basically doubles the number of "accident kills" you can have on a map and her three charges of mind control, when used perfectly, can remove 9 enemies from map "for free", meaning it won't raise any alarms. And that's... all.As a game in a genre, it's no doubt a high-quality product. As a video game in terms of experience and emotional journey, it falls somewhat short. It's hard to not recommend this, but it applies mostly to the genre fans.Now excuse me while I go back to listening to the soundtrack of Shadow Tactics and feel chills and emotion over memory of much better game I've played, from same developer.

_childDocuments_.review: Desperados 3 is the prequel to a classic series of tactical stealth genre which thanks to Mimimi Games, has been successfully revived, and just like Shadow Tactics, Desperados 3 is an incredible game.👍 +Tatical stealth gameplay done perfectly right. +Fantastic soundtrack+Missions are long and offer multiple ways of being tackled.+The main cast is nicely voiced.👎-The main story is pretty much the average revenge story.-The variety of objectives does get repetitive around half the game.Desperados 3 shows us the story of John Cooper and how he met his band of misfits made of Kate, Doc Mcoy, Hector, and Isabelle. Each of the characters you meet has their own issues to deal with and as you progress through the game you form a bond with them. John's main objective is to get revenge on the person who killed his father and he'll do whatever it takes. It goes pretty straight forward from here with the usual, arguing, disbanding, and making peace again with one another of his group mates and there really isn't anything that will shock or impress you. It's a standard story of revenge and comradery but even in its simplicity, you slowly start to like one if not all of the characters in large thanks to the good voice acting. I personally liked Doc the most. Don't buy Desperados for the main story. It's not what it was made for but who knows, we do lack simple cowboy stories in games these days and you might enjoy it a lot more. Story rating: 7.5/10If you've come for the gameplay well you're in for a treat. Desperados 3 does tactical stealth almost perfectly, so good that I just can't imagine what else can they cook up in future games to impress me. If you played Shadow Tactics then you know what to expect from Desperados 3 and if you haven't then what the hell are you waiting for? Just like their previous game Mimimi has managed to revitalize a dying genre which was no easy task. You're playing as 5 unique characters each with a set of abilities that will help you kill or knock out enemies in your path towards the objective. Enemies around the map and even the level design is masterfully crafted so that you'll always need to use your available skills and tools. For example, Doc Mcoy which as I've mentioned is my favorite character, can easily dispatch enemies from far away and quite silently with his sniper rifle or you can throw a decoy to attract and separate wandering guards from the rest so you can silently dispatch him. I can spend all day writing and describing each characters unique skills so I will just say this: not only you can freely use each skill but the game also has a number of hidden and fun ways of using some of the skills you have at your disposal such as combining them with the other characters or even allowing you to carry out multiple attacks at the same time with the showdown mode. Each level takes around 1 to 2 hours to complete depending on your skill and whether you're going to play stealthfully as it should be played. Playing this loud is a waste of time in my opinion but you are indeed offered that option. I also did mention that the objectives are quite repetitive after a while seeing how this game is a 30+ hour long however you are given free reigns on how to proceed with the entire map minus the tutorial parts and some small linear missions. You're also going to be rewarded at the end of each level with a star-based system where it shows you what you could've done to achieve those special objectives. I personally would've loved to see them all the time but I suppose this is a good way to increase replayability. Overall the gameplay offers a lot and it's fun, hard, and a lot of times nerve-racking which requires a huge amount of patience but I just could not put it down. Fantastic experience.Gameplay rating: 9.5/10The moment you boot up the game the first thing you'll notice is the fantastic main menu theme and just like that, you'll know the rest of the soundtrack will be great. It's a long game, no doubt, and many songs will be repetitive but not once did I get bored with them. The voice acting is another great aspect and it's honestly what makes the story tones less boring. Every character in the game is voiced and the main cast does a fine job at immersing you in the experience. Their banter is especially funny and great during missions. As for the other sounds, there's absolutely nothing negative to talk about. Guns, enemies talking, environmental sounds are all perfectly fine. Audio rating: 9/10Visually the game looks pretty decent and the way the levels are constructed and enhancing the gameplay is top-notch. Sadly the textures and on rare occasions, the lighting effects are not that great. They do not ruin the experience at all though it felt weird how those huge mountain rocks passed Q&A as they were quite in your face and looked pretty bad. Luckily these occurrences are rare and overall graphically speaking the game looks fine and the missions are very varied from deserts to crowded cities. Performance is perfect, at least on my machine. There were no frame drops ever and besides some minor enemy AI bugs I had no problems playing the game. Graphics, performance and tech analysis score:  8/10I don't know what to expect from future Mimimi games but along with Shadow Tactics and now Desperados 3, it's clear whatever the developers make I'll be there day one. Desperados 3 is a masterpiece in gameplay and hopefully, I'll see the same characters again in future sequels. Buy the game at all costs.

_childDocuments_.review: So I'm going to start trying to write my reviews much shorter; they always end up too damn long.To that end, this is written from the perspective of someone who played (and quite liked!) Shadow Tactics.I will say this: while I love gunslingers, I love ninja more. Keeping that in mind, I can honestly say this game is better. It's better made, and there are obvious efforts to remedy some of the more frustrating moments/mechanics from Shadow Tactics. Not surprising, considering the team had more experience, and I appreciated every single choice they made in making these characters (like your disguise specialist getting a "lead-away" ability or now being able to tie up knocked-out enemies and civillians, so you can non-lethal people PERMANENTLY), going off the people you get in the last game. They weren't as one-to-one as I thought they might end up being, which is rad. Also, if you're like me (and in my head, you are) and you're wondering how your fifth character will play before you get her, after having gotten the other four? You will NOT see this coming. She is AWESOME, and she is NOTHING like any of the Shadow Tactics characters.But yeah, man, it's real-time tactical stealth, it's extremely good, all of your characters are awesome, feel good to play, and have vital functions, and every level is a puzzle with multiple answers. It even does the same thing Shadow did, where the last couple levels are COLOSSAL hedgehogs right in the prostate, and, just like the previous game, I still ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ loved it.One disappointment: even though I'm an American, I think I'm a pretty ♥♥♥♥♥♥ gunslinger. I played this VERY much as if I was still controlling ninjas. To the point that the game was reminding me each of my characters was strapped with a projectile weapon of some kind, each of them. But I stuck to the Buck knife, the syringe, the axe, and the bootheel. The sneaky-sneaky stabby-stabby that I have always loved. At heart, I'm a ninja, not a gunslinger.I guess the real weeb was inside me all along.10/10P.S. Murdering real-life slavers in the American Old West with a Black female player character? ♥♥♥♥ YES.P.P.S. If you're worried; Shadow Tactics: Blades of the Shogun should be super cheap, doubly so if on sale. I say grab that, and if you even LIKE that, I'd wager you'll love this game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best real time strategy games I have ever played. It's impossible not to recall the old Commandos saga, not only because of the RTS camera and the stealthy approach, but also because of how the characters are developed throughout the game. I'd even say that it's a big improvement over Commandos 2 or 3.The story is simple to begin with, but pretty catchy, because everyone loves revenge stories no matter how simplistic these are. But somehow, the game starts to introduce characters that are linked one way or another, and the uniqueness they have in their personality is what caught me the most.I never thought someone could tell a story SO GOOD within an isometric perspective. The game made me feel happy, anxious, and even surprised as the story unveils major twists along the misadventures and unfortunate events that we are witnesses of.The core mechanics are incredibly well done. AI, puzzles, objectives, hints, and specially the amount of alternatives you have to sort out any mission is what made me feel I'm playing a true masterpiece.You can tell by the games I played: I'm not an RTS guy. But this game... this game man...Thank you Mimimi for making such an awesome adventure. Thank you THQ for publish it. I'm on the last mission of the game and I had to quit. I don't want it to end. I'll save it for another day.Thank you. Please make Desperados 4.

_childDocuments_.review: The best example of a Real Time Tactics game I have played since the original Commandos franchise which began in the late 90's. The developer Mimimi games have created a RTT gem. Their first RTT game was Shadow Tactics which was a great homage to Commandos series though a little rough around the edges but they have taken Shadows Tactics DNA and refined it to create Desperados 3. The game play is so addictive it's a game you don't want to put down. It's challenging especially on the hardest difficult "Desperado" but the sense of achievement when you crack a difficult mission or scenario is fantastic. I can only compare it to the feeling you get when you defeat a tough boss in Dark Souls, you feel so good about yourself like you're a genius. The game controls are very intuitive and the levels are super detailed, really high end visuals for a RTT. it's a very accessible game easy to learn but a brilliant challenge to master. The game is well worth it's triple A price tag due to having 50 hours plus of content especially on Desperado difficulty which I played it on and for it's high quality production. The game works perfectly I haven't experienced any bugs on PC and the game is extremely well optimised, my I9-9900K/RTX 2080TI machine can run the game at a rock solid 120 FPS at 4K resolution. I am now tackling the bonus challenges which are still keeping me playing even after spending 58 hours on the campaign missions. The story is good if nothing exciting but works for the narrative. There are only 4 different enemy types including guard dogs, I would have liked to see more variety. The voice acting is excellent with some funny one liners from enemies. The sound effects are high quality and the music is catchy I would usually turn it off to concentrate in Commandos for example but this soundtrack is worth listening to. Shadow Tactics came close to taking the Commandos crown as the king of RTT's but with all due respect to the 90's classic, Desperados 3 is the new king.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed my time with Desperados 3 a lot. If you want a quick opinion then I would say that this game is definitely a buy. At first I thought that the price is unreasonable, but after beating a game and discovering so many unique locations and a 30hr long campaign I think that 50$ price is totally justified.So, here is an in depth look into the game from my perspective.I would like to start from the story and I see a lot of progress compared to Shadow Tactics. The motivation for our main protagonist is clear as  a day. Yes, everyone is tired from revenge stories, but here it is only a boost for Cooper. I would say that this is more like a road movie, which concentrates on relationships between very distinct and unique characters, which I have fallen in love with. The dialogues, specific phrases for each of them, reactions when they meet each other and show their skills, all of that is top notch. By the way, the color identification of each character is a cool feature. They went so far, that tone of the characters voices changes depending on the current mood in the band. Considering the gameplay-centric nature of the game I would say that everything about the characters and the story is executed perfectly.Let's bring the big elephant in the room, which is gameplay. I highly recommend you to start your playthrough on a HARD difficulty, cos then you will have the most from satisfaction of executing a perfect plan. As you probably know, each character has a set of different abilities, which tie them to a unique play style. The balance is almost perfect and you need to use all of them on HARD in order to succeed, which is wonderful. You gain the most from using characters in synergy in tactical pause mode and the only feature that I miss is creating a few actions for one character in a row. Of course, some locations are created more for some characters than the others, but with enough creativity you can play as wild as you want. At first I thought that this will be less of a stealth game and more action based, considering the addition of the guns, but it appears that these are more of a ranged stealth tools. All the gadgets are extremely fun to use and some of them have a specific bond with the owner, like Hector and Bianca (loved these two so much). The enemy variety is almost the same as in Shadow Tactics, which is fine, but the cool addition is consideration of an enemy gender, which creates fun situations when you play as Kate in her disguise. The one enemy type that I didn't see enough were dogs that push you back from hiding spots and adding more tension to gameplay. Overall, I can't praise the core gameplay enough and knowing that there aren't really any alternatives in this genre I would say that it is the best of its kind.Finally a bit about the visual and soundtrack beauty of this game. First, in almost every location you feel the atmosphere of cruel and lifeless wild west, but the location variety doesn't stop there. You will travel across multiple biomes which sound and look nice. The esthetical part of myself was pleased every minute of playing. The sound of the game hits splendidly both purely technical, like sounds of abilities, and the artistic parts. Some of the melodies still play in my head, which is a defining factor here.In the end, Desperados 3 is a game like no other(not counting Shadow Tactics) and it perfectly hits the real time tactics niche. I am incredibly happy that there are still developers that are able to create such great games in this genre.

_childDocuments_.review: + Awesome real-time tactics mechanics+ Stealth approach is more than rewarding+ A huge amount of the content+ Five different well-written characters with useful abilities that the player has to use wisely depending on the situation+ A captivating story that is interesting to follow+ Thoughtful level design+ High replayable value+ Challenges that are really interesting to complete- Some levels take a lot of time complete, around 2-3 hours- Reloading saves feel tedious sometimes - Repeating character replicas can become a bit annoyingPlaying Desperados III was a really exciting experience for me because the original game was one of the first games I have played on PC when I was a kid back in 2001. As you can probably guess, gaming then was completely different than it now - we never had a library with thousands of different games, usually, we were limited to a few games, that we had to replay again and again and again. I never had the luxury to rage quit the game, so I had to think a lot of how in order to progress with the story.And Desperados was my first ever experience with real-time tactics games and I will never forget those moments. Constantly saving and loading, trying different approaches, consulting with my schoolmates - it was awesome. The reason why I am telling you all this, is because Desperados III brought me exactly the same experience, same memories from my childhood and I couldn’t be happier in this situation. Everything that I used to love in the original games has been saved in this prequel, so if you are the veteran player, don’t you dare to miss Desperados III.Desperados III tells us the story about John Cooper, a rough bounty hunter who has to revenge for his father’s death. During his journey, he meets a company of desperate characters with their own story, motives, and the reason to stay with John Cooper. So, in terms of the story, the main goal of Desperados III is to tell the player how everything started and how John met his gang members. The game is presented as an isometric real-time tactic game, where the player has to control different characters in order to complete the level. Each level can be completed in a loud or in a quiet way, however, the stealth approach is much more rewarding and it causes fewer problems for the player. During certain levels, the player has to control only one character or it starts with one character, and then another character joins a bit later. Every single character has their own unique abilities that are hopeful during certain situations and the player has to figure out how to use them properly. The way the game introduces the new character to the player is magnificent: it starts with a short story of what happened to them and then, the whole level is dedicated to that character and it’s designed to be completed by using the abilities of this character. This kind of approach lets the player to learn the character and to understand how to play with him.My favorite part of the game is the design of levels - they are extremely huge and thoughtful, the developers made everything to let the player finish it in a lot of different ways using different methods, where the player can go quietly or go loud. Most of these levels take a lot of time to complete, around 2-3 hours and this can be a problem for some players, I believe. Usually, the main reason why it takes so long to complete the level is probably the mistakes that the player will do during the playthrough. Speaking of me, I was constantly spamming F5 and F8 buttons that are obviously responsible for quick saving and quick loading respectively, simply because there were always some enemies that were appearing out of nowhere, spoiling everything for me.After the mission is done, the player can check on the results of the mission: the map with the movement of the characters, the number of saves and loads that have been executed and how many enemies each character killed. For example, one of my games has 103 saves and I loaded the game for 79 times. I realized that the whole concept of the game and my approach to it didn’t change too much since I was playing it as a kid back in 2001: I kill one, maximum two enemies and then I do an emergency save just to make sure that I won’t be forced to do it again if I fail on the next pack of the enemies. I can’t even describe you how satisfying it is when you can’t understand how to fool the big pack of enemies and to bypass them and then when you finally find a solution. Every single enemy has a cone of their viewing area divided into two parts: a solid one closer to the enemy and a striped one, a bit distanced from the enemy’s eyes. The solid area is the place that has to be avoided by any means if you don’t want to be spotted by the enemy and the stripped area only lets the character move around the enemy in a crouching position. If the player will stand for a long period of time in the stripped area, the enemy will trigger the alarm. Desperados III has a huge amount of content, including 16 long missions and 5 challenges that can entertain the player for a few more hours. This game has a pretty high replayability value, because it really differs a lot when the player switches to the higher difficulty. Every single level has special badges and unique tasks that the player has to complete in order to get them and this is something that will make the player stay in the game for a few more hours. I finished the game on the normal difficulty, some of the missions I was able to complete on the high difficulty and when I finished the game completely, I instantly started it all over again to try it on Desperado difficulty. Frankly speaking, after finishing the game and knowing everything on each level, I found it much easier to play even on this highest difficulty.Desperados III has a pretty pleasant graphics, this game never tries to impress the player with it, but it just the does the job in the right way. The game has short cutscenes during the levels and between them, however, they are all made on the source of the game.  The soundtrack in this game is simply amazing and it definitely fits the atmosphere of the game. Every single character of the game is dubbed by the professional actors. My biggest issue with this game was repetitive replicas of each character which became annoying especially after loading the same save for a few times in a row.Desperados III is an extremely quality game that is definitely worth picking up especially if you tactical games heavily based on stealth mechanics or used to play Desperados games in the past. It can be challenging at first, especially on the highest difficulties, but once you get into the mood of the game, it will become much easier. The great thing is that it has pretty high replayability value and it’s interesting to try new approaches in completing the level.

_childDocuments_.review: F5 Simulator, western edition!Heads up, if you take away anything from this review, let is be this: NOT worth 60 bucks. Not at all worth 60 bucks!If you ever played a Hitman game, it's basically that, without the nice perspective, variation and decent AI-Enemies. Otherwise it's a Hitman-Ripoff: There are stealth kills, accident kills, disguises, the whole shabang. Once the alarm is raised, you lost.The graphics look like a mobile-game from 10 years ago. A real missed opportunity. Get it? Missed opportUNITY? That explains the washed out, rough graphics.I don't know why they did that. The levels aren't big and there are no demanding effects whatsoever.Gameplay is fun, story is okay. In the Hitman games, you're one assasin with all the skills. Here, it's hero-based. They broke the skills up between 5 heroes.Also, the game is VERY challenging for me, for all the wrong reasons. Enemies have these (immersion-breaking) view-cones. Enemies spot you if you step into their view-cones.The most challenging thing in this game, is overlapping view-cones. You can't take out one enemy without being spotted by the other.I hear you say "But dude, that's the game!". Yes. But these enemies always do the same route, repeating every 30 seconds tops. They are dumb as rocks otherwise. And the ONLY challenge is their inconvenient placement. What I'm saying is that this game might as well be a chess-puzzle. There's no need for the "western" theme, you could just reskin it to a ninja themed game. Which the developer did: It's called Shadow Tactics! What a coincidence! Also: The "big map" is NOT BIG. Let me explain: You start a level, and there's a big map. On this map, you have 4 targets to kill. Those targets don't interact with each other. They are each in a separate part of the map, repeating their 30 second routine. These targets function completely independent of each other, in their own little segment of the map.Think of the map as a square. Divide this square into four smaller squares. Place a target in each smaller square. This is how the game works. The graphics make it look like one big interconnected map, when in fact, it just consists of little boxes holding one target each. Those little boxes are placed next to each other, giving the impression of a big map, which it is not, because the "boxes" DON'T interact with each other.One last point, because some neckbeard will come out of the woods and say "But man, stop comparing this to Hitman. Hitman is a Triple A game, and MIMIMI studios are a small indie-studio".Listen up, friend: If they charge me 60 dollars for their indie-sausage, it means they charge a Triple A price for it. And then, I expect Triple A value of a game. Which this game clearly does not deliver. Not at all.I love anything western-related, that's why I bought it. But you can buy the new Hitman games for way less money, if you're not into Westerns, DEFINITELY buy those!

_childDocuments_.review: I can honestly recommend this game not only to all the fans of the Commandos and Desperados genre, but also to all who haven't experienced this type of game yet and want to start with something accessible. The game holds the spirit of the first Desperados (let's forget the sequel and its janky 3D mode), with great western setting, likable and distinctive characters, colorful graphics and diverse environments. At the same time, it takes many modern tweaks from Shadow Tactics, making the gameplay smoother and more enjoyable (by the use of shadow mode). It's simple, but packed with details that not only create an interesting world, but also serve the gameplay.Great sound design and music - pay attention to short themes that are played after successful actions, the choice of instruments depends on character used.The graphics are very colorful, even a bit cartoony, but I think they provide great visibility and won't age too quickly.The game is long, has many missions of the main story, each mission comes with a set of special achievements requiring more than one playthrough. There is also a separate, additional challenge mission for every map - with interesting twists (limited skills, different set of characters or even one, where you play as animals). I also encourage you to play 3 DLC missions, they are of good quality. It's sure worth its price.The normal difficulty is quite easy - but that's good, Desperados 3 won't scare away the beginners. The developers let you adjust a few aspects of difficulty, so the game can be challenging on high difficulty even for experienced players. (and then you can always make it harder by aiming for an achievement).Great job, studio Mimimi! I'd love a similar game set in ancient Rome or Greece some day :)

_childDocuments_.review: [FULL REVIEW ON ]Desperados III is like a decadent cake. It’s very rich in detail and design, and highly recommended, but that richness is for a certain palette that won’t appeal to everyone. Yes, it can depend on trial-and-error and the loading times can be unsavory if you don't have a SSD, but it’s been awhile since a game plagued my thoughts like Desperados III. Getting a plan to work is a blast, and some excellent characterization prop up the mechanics nicely. Mimimi Games is a worthy successor to the Desperado franchise, and III will convert skeptics.

_childDocuments_.review: This is exactly the case when all the stars came together at the only right moment, giving us a miracle. Incredibly talented developers from Mimimi Games, who created «Shadow Tactics: Blades of the Shogun», were called to work on the continuation of the legendary title Desperados, and, «unexpectedly», created a great product. And if in the nomination “Game of the Year” it is too early for her to win, still there is still a lot of time and serious rivals (we believe that Cyberpunk will be released THIS year, right??!!), then for me it is the best tactical game it will definitely be. The game perfectly understands the most important idea of the best tactical games - providing freedom of thought to the player, the absence of linearity chains that hamper the possibility of improving it. We once again find ourselves in the deadly Wild West, in the company of old beloved adventurer heroes, who are threatened by many threats, including wild gangs, dirty businessmen with their mercenaries, and flocks of loud, annoying hens. Oh, how deadly these noisy hens are, and those who strive to get the attention of a random patrol. The story here is told incredibly skillfully, a fully-fledged western is unfolding in front of us, in which great attention is paid to both global events and small details that enliven the surrounding world.Each huge mission of sixteen available is not only large spaces, but also an incredible amount of opportunities, and this is incredibly important. The plot of each mission is almost a separate film, with a well-developed exposure, competent development of the action and an explosive climax. The respect that the creators give to the iconic spaghetti westerns and classic American westerns is palpable, in the game you can easily find references to many masterpieces of the genre. The player can complete missions in various ways, although it should be said right away that at serious levels of difficulty you can’t run with pistols, you have to wait and plan. Planning here is generally important, because enemies always have an advantage in quantity, they are keen to respond to any wrong step by the player, so you need to use the entire arsenal of tricks - distraction, adjusting accidents, calculating timings, using all the characters' capabilities. The game is difficult, but it does not break the player’s neck with something intentionally complicated, but simply gives him opportunities for improvement. You really feel the growth of your skill right in the course of the action, which creates simply magical sensations of unity with the game. And for even greater variability, the game has a system of stars that make them pass missions with certain conditions (they open after the first passage), which makes them even more varied.With the naked eye, the warmth with which the creators relate to both their project and their players is noticeable. Every detail of the design is made with love, many easter eggs are hidden in the game, which the player may not even find, but if he does, he will feel himself in seventh heaven. You see, even secret scenes, which almost no one can possibly find, are worked out with manic thoroughness and attention - is this not an indicator of incredible love for your creation. Desperados 3 is a diamond that deserves the attention of all players; games of this scale are not released as often as we would like. A stunning well-deserved success and an unconditional recommendation for a purchase

_childDocuments_.review: I adored Desperados. It was one of the first PC games I played and a huge part of my childhood. Then came Desperados 2 and I didnt like it at all. Until recently, I wasnt even aware Helldorado existed. So the franchise eventually died, both for real and in my memory. And so did the entire subgenre it represented. Fast forward more than a decade later and out comes little game called Shadow Tactics, from an unknown developer. Seeing those cones again woke up memories of Commandos, Robin Hood and especially Desperados. I had to play it. And it was phenomenal. And then those same devs announced Desperados 3. And it is glorious.This is the finest example of tactical strategy you can find. Everything great about Shadow Tactics has been improved upon and cranked up to 11. Every of the 5 playable characters is unique and combining their skillset is key to success. There is a huge amount of ways you can complete your objective and dispose of your enemies. One character in particular offers possibilities I didnt even think were possible in the genre. Each level is huge and methodically crafted to offer maximum amount of challenge and most of the levels take hours to complete (for us mortals). Story, although cliched, was surprisingly good and I loved seeing these characters again. Besides Story, which will take you 20-30 hours to complete, there are also badges to earn, baron's challenges and bounty mode. There is a lot to do and replayability is impressively high.Edition I bought also came with 3 dlc missions and I'm working my way through them now.The only issue I can find in the game is AI, which sometimes reacts in bizarre ways, but its an issue that still plagues entire stealth genre.To say the least, I'm impressed. Thank you devs for bringing this series and genre back to life. After Shadow Tactics and Desperados 3, I'm 100 percent behind whatever Mimimi do next.10/10

_childDocuments_.review: This game is basically like Shadow Tactics, except that it is set in the Wild West. That isn't a bad thing: Shadow Tactics was a good game. However, therein also lies many of its shortcomings. Desperadoes III simply fails to innovate compared to its 2016 spiritual predecessor. It's similarities run so deep to the point that the mechanics are the same, the archetypes for enemies are all the same, some assets are reused, graphics are the same and most importantly, the playable characters are more or less the same:1. You have a fast nimble guy that kill quickly2. You have a big strong dude than can kill elite enemies3. You have a sniper character4. You have a spy that can distract/seduce enemiesThe only 'new' character was fith one, Isabel, a voodoo witch that has wacky abilities. At first I felt like she was a bit much within the context of this game, but eventually I learned to appreciate both her as well as her abilities. She stood out as the strongest of the bunch, with her being able to 'link' enemy characters so that what you do to one enemy, happens to the other, as well as being able to control enemy characters. The game would be a lot harder if you'd play without those abilities. The storyline is your typical predictable revenge tale. The characters are likable, but felt one-dimensional. I did feel like there were too many missions however. Now, for people who really enjoy this game I suppose that is a plus, but for me it simply drags on a bit. I had similar criticism for Shadow Tactics. It would be alright if later during the storyline they would keep introducing new mechanics and new characters, but after mission 7 or so all the possible mechanics and characters have been introduced and there is nothing new to discover. That's a very long haul all the way to the last mission, considering the story has about 16 missions, if not more.Enemy line of sight in relation to height differences can be problematic and unpredictable, again an issue I also highlighted in my review of Shadow Tactics, yet it is even more pronounced in this game. Sometimes an enemy can spot you on the roof, another time he can't. The final mission has a lot of canyons and knowing whether or not an enemy can spot you can be quite tricky to gauge – sometimes your character doesn't even seem to be in the enemy FoV but you get spotted anyways. This has led to multiple frustrating moments. Don't let my criticism dissuade you, if you liked Shadow Tactics and the Commandos series, you will like this game. Though I can't say this game is worth the current full asking price of 50 euros. Buy it on sale.

Long-ass satire based, story-telling syle review beyond this point. Proceed with caution.Still here ? Ok lets carry on. Stay a while and listen, *insert meme quote from that game you can relate to"Good old me is no professional stream reviwer so don't expect bullet lists and other fancy bells and whistles. What I can provide you some ye olde style views so gather'round you young snapppers for the story.Out story takes place in the mythical BS ( Before Steam ) era...... Vicious times when poor players were bereft of the light of Almighty Gaben, Praised Be His Name, an era when internet connections were dial up and if you wanted a game you had to get them from those places called stores. You could say I was like Robert Downey Jr. of this genre of games. If it existed I definitely did it, some more than once..... Hell I have even played Desperados 2.... Not a high point in my career but whatever.After the Commando-like genre more or less sputtered out following the flop of Commandos 4 I was left with nothing but good old memories but I was happy. After all my Desperados and Robin Hood were like a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ bottle of quality whiskey. I knew that I could always reach into the ol'cupboard and take a few sips whenever I needed that hit of nostalgia to escape the grinding gears of being an adult. I could always get my fix of nostalgia, taking me back to more innocent times... Times when our rigs had less RAMs in total than some cheap-ass smartphones nowadays, RGB was nothing but dreams of a mind on an acid-trip but we loved our games not because they had über graphics but because they were good.Later on Almighty Gaben, Thrice Praised Be His Name but not his games, came and delivered upon us a new age. We were saved by the chosen one and safe in his bosom we laid our guard in bliss.Then the DLC nation attacked. Followed by the evil games as service. Like a plague it infected many of our loved ones.... Many fell during these times... Some survived albeit forever tainted by their infestation, a mere shadow of their former glory...... Some of our numbers sought refuge in the Groove of İndies while others offered sacrifices at the Kickstarter Temples to mixed results.....As time went on this pestilence grew and morphed, taking the form of Lootboxes. Just when we thought we were brought to our lowest a new hope rose. Like a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hobbit army showing upto mordor and beating up ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Orcs and big-ass evil elephants, us mere players rose up and start to resist.Just like godrays piercing through dark clouds, good games began to flourish once more. Even though some usurpers try to lead us astray from the Steam Engine of Glory, it feels like we are catching a glimpse of the lost Golden Age.Now...... Back to the topic.... _childDocuments_.review: Just like the THQ brand has risen from its own ashes, it is with great pleasure that I observe, play and review new titles from gaming series which were laying dormant for too long. Some might have called their return to be a lost cause. It was not. THQ Nordic continues to revive classic IPs and see them published on numerous platforms. Comanche got its reboot and now it’s time for Desperados III to get a fresh start in the form a sequel that’s delving on origin stories as much as the long-awaited return for a Western-themed RTT (Real Time Tactics) game. It is developer’s Mimimi Games secondary project to feature the aforementioned subgenre. Naturally, the dev team behind the excellent Shadow Tactics: Blades of the Shogun managed to deliver their revised tactical formula in an Old West setting which clicks as efficiently as it did for Feudal Japan.Both the last veritable attack chopper sim and the first Desperados to kickstart its series, have in common the date of their release: 2001 marked my second year of PC gaming as well, so I was in all regards still learning the ropes. Simpler times before stable internet connections for the general public or even digital licenses for gaming. CDs were all the rage and on such a disc, bought alongside a local gaming magazine, I got to feast my eyes upon a demo for Desperados – Wanted Dead or Alive! I want to highlight that while a rarity even back then, the demo level was entirely unique in comparison to the retail version of the game. A dying concept to this day and age where most demos fancy themselves as “prologues” instead.Irony has it that veterans of previous Desperados entries, might acknowledge in dismay that our story from this brand new, third iteration isn’t quite picking up the pieces from “Desperados 2: Cooper's Revenge” or even the “Helldorado” spin-off. That is because Desperados III is actually a “soft reboot” focusing on the events prior to the initial 2001 release, than a proper sequel and that is a great thing in spite of what some “purists” might object. You see, when you release one title in an eponymous series, roughly once per decade, you lose at least part of your player base, not just interest for the franchise or narrative coherence. So I applaud this decision to cater towards new players and finally explain some of the relationships from past titles as well as properly introducing the playable characters. It was rather awkward to “reassemble the crew” in Desperados 1, without having actually met them beforehand. Long story short, you can pick Desperados III up right now without having played any previous entries, yet you still won’t miss out on much. A clean slate for an old tale of revenge sees our protagonist John Cooper travel across the American Frontier from the rapidly developing Old West and all the way towards the resentful Deep South. From Colorado to Louisiana, with more than a few “stops” in formerly disputed Mexican territories. A classic setting and time frame, as we’re experiencing a slice of the late 19th Century from the perspective of a highly skilled team of US bounty hunters. Operating on the edge of legality themselves, one probably tends to be more lenient when delivering justice on the lawless fringes of a young federation which had just survived a costly civil war. But that’s not Cooper’s way of handling things. Promises must be kept just as debts are often paid in lead when fistfuls of dollars won’t bring closure…Rarely have I seen such a gorgeous Unity project. It stands testament to a graphics engine that doesn’t get enough credit since it’s sadly associated more with shovelware asset flips than obvious works of art. Which is exactly how I regard Desperados III’s maps, basically digital dioramas once you zoom out. Unity didn’t disappoint from a technical perspective either, as I had no issues whatsoever and to my surprise, I could run this title in 4K@60fps. Quite the feat in 2020’s new releases while still sporting an “ancient” GTX 1070. Even my “slight madness” in regards to HUDless screenshots was catered, granted that it’s still a compromise of sorts, before native implementation of an equivalent to a Photo Mode. See the review’s comment section for a link to my thread detailing how you can disable the in-game HUD for proper screenshots.Ennio Morricone has shaped the very foundation of the soundtracks breathing life into the Western genre. His influence can be heard in Desperados III’s OST, without the master’s direct contribution. A nod to him and several more towards the game’s voice actors which performed exemplarily. Not a single flaw was found, whether we refer to the accents, the quality of the dialogue between main characters or even NPC banter.Odd as it seems, this is a Western experience in which firearms play a secondary role towards the more close and personal form of combat. Or should I call it the “stealthy dispatching of foes without giving them the chance to fight back”? Cooper and his colleagues will forever be outnumbered and outgunned, but they posses sharp wits, plenty of patience and certain talents for distracting and silently eliminating their opposition. The game wastes no time in admitting that you’ll have to observe your surroundings and carefully plan your next move if you wish to survive. Going in guns blazing is a suicidal act for the simple reason that unlike in previous iterations, the third entry has opted to severely limit the bullets or shells you may carry with your gunslingers. For real, Desperados used to feature infinite ammo and sweeping the maps with a full team firing at the same time, was truly a sight to behold even in 2D.Desperados III diversified the enemy types more than any of its predecessors, so it adds an extra layer of difficulty on top of the existing ones. You will have to adjust your tactics, learn to use multiple bounty hunters simultaneously, as the enemy “vision cones” overlap as often as you can’t just silently kill someone who’s within earshot of another foe. The once reviled practice of “save scumming” is actually encouraged in-game now. Quicksaving and Quickloading are your new trusty partners!  RTT veterans will surely be interested in the speedruns and additional objectives during missions. These carry further incentives in the form of badges which eventually unlock rare Steam Achievements. There will be a lot of sneaking and hiding, far more than shooting anyway. As a stealth-centric player, this didn’t bother me at all, but you should be aware that Cooper & Co aren’t your typical Western heroes by any definition. A near flawless experience, it could just as well have been called simply “Desperados” and I doubt any fan would have found a problem with a fully recognized reboot rather than a “prequel with a sequel title”. Details, details. The devil is not here, but you should definitely give the 2001 game a run for its blood money. After you enjoy all that Desperados III has to offer, of course. Saddle up, this’ll be one helluva ride!+ Gorgeous graphics and sounds.+ Steam Achievements & Trading Cards.+ Proper showcase of the RTT subgenre.+ Lengthy and diversified singleplayer campaign.- Ammo scarcity in a Western…

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not sure what exactly I can add to the chorus of over 6000 positive reviews that have already been written for Desperados III. However, I have a habit of writing a Steam review for every game I play on the platform, so here we go.Desperados III includes basically every gameplay mechanic you could ask for in a real-time tactical stealth game. You'll know what elements you can interact with in each map, including both hiding places and environmental hazards you can turn to your advantage. With environmental hazards, you can even see the exact size of the area of effect. You are given extremely accurate enemy view cones, which will show you exactly where you can remain undetected as long as you're crouching and where you'll be detected regardless. You can also tag a specific location and the game will let you know who can see it and when. It's very clear when an enemy is "on the hunt" and will deviate from his usual route and pattern. Lastly, when using any of your characters' abilities (for instance, shooting a gun), it's clear exactly which enemies will hear and which will be affected.The icing on this already-extraordinary cake is the game's "showdown mode," which (at least on most of the game's difficulties) will pause the game and allow you to plan out actions for each of your characters. You can then either have all of your characters perform their planned actions at once, or un-pause the game and keep this plan in reserve until a specific moment. Keep in mind that can perform an action in real-time with a character, and then still activate the action(s) that you have planned in reserve (for that character and others). This system is tremendously useful, and you'll often find it important on occasions where three enemies are all keeping an eye on each other and you need to take them down simultaneously.If this isn't enough, the game features excellent playable characters. The characters are well voice-acted, and have unique strengths and skill sets. They also pair together in compelling ways. Although Doc was my least favorite character to use, a friend of mine loved him. This same friend found Hector to be less than optimal, but I got plenty of use out of Hector even up to the end of the game. There are many approaches that can lead to success, and you'll develop your own as you play.I also need to give a quick shout-out to Mimimi for their map and sound design. The maps are large, sprawling, and intricately designed, and often provide multiple routes to success. I also loved the game's musical score, and the ambient sounds that were present in certain areas (New Orleans comes to mind).The game has very few flaws (in my book), but there were a few things that stuck out to me:If you have some patience and could appreciate a stealth game that gives you all of the information you need to make sound tactical decisions, give Desperados III a try. Even with as much information as you're given, it's far from easy. A number of missions took me almost three hours to complete (though many finished the game more quickly than I did).

_childDocuments_.review: With a stellar job on  devs set their sights on a somewhat forgotten and, to many, dear franchise, . While I haven't played , yet, I am no stranger to the (RTT) genre. As a young slav, I indulged myself in the old  games that inspired these games, and even a lesser-known one . But good news everyone.  is a ; Welcoming with open arms, those alien to the franchise, like I, as well as returning players.But, we must start our review with its only but important con (at least to some) - .  tries and ultimately fails to tell an engaging story about revenge, loss, and cowboy stuff. As a prequel, it had to establish the main cast, their motivations and relationships.  Frick if I know. Perhaps all of this was answered off-screen during one of the many loading screens. Except for Cooper, no other character has the luxury of having their backstory developed and explored. In fact, my sex life is richer than their personalities, and that's saying something, considering it's non-existent. This lack of proper character development consequently drags down every emotional moment, making them fall short each time. And apart from Hector, the others have no logical reason to keep risking their neck for Cooper. Their motivation boils down to: “”.In the end,  vows an unrivalled cowboy revenge story, with characters as developed as newborns muscles, a villain that's in the game a whopping 10 minutes and a love story for the ages. If you enjoy sinking your teeth into gripping stories, I suggest you bring a straw.But abysmal storey aside, the gameplay is what gives  its allure. The RTT genre hasn't received much love before  stepped on the scene. And they strike gold once more. But they went for quality of life improvements this time, with no big additions to the already solid formula used for .The gameplay predominantly focuses on stealth, with each character having plenty of skills that complement this type of gameplay.  is your jack of all trades, master of none. He has both close and medium-range weaponry, some loud, some stealthy.  is the thicc boy and the only one able to take out Long Coats in one hit. He sports a sawed-off shotgun that alerts the enemies in the town over. And let's not forget his love, Bianca, a giant bear trap that munches on an unsuspecting enemy.  is the sneaky sniper, best used to take out guards in high places.  is your La femme fatale, using her god-given endowments to lure horny cowboys to their doom. And lastly, ; A mysterious lady from New Orleans that calls you sunshine constantly and has a spunky cat at her side. Using weird voodoo magic darts, she can  people who will then experience the same thing simultaniously, opening the door for some fun shenanigans.I did find this whole stealthy cowboy thing a bit weird, seeing as this takes place during the Wild West, a period definitely not known for covert cowboy operations. It didn't ruin my enjoyment of the game, but I often pondered how a cowboy ninja would look.And since stealth is necessary, I will share some important things. First, if one character dies, you fail. Next - each enemy unit has a view cone. They are separated into two parts -  and . Try and avoid the solid area; Guards can spot you or will investigate suspicious activity. On the other hand, the stripped area shows you where they can only see you if you aren't crouching or are doing something naughty, like dragging a corpse. Sometimes guards are stationary, so this is where  come in. They can affect enemies in various ways – shortening their view cone, making them look away or luring them to a more intimate spot. But, depending on the enemy, the distraction may fail, or the last shorter; The Long Coats and Ponchos have immunity to some distractions, so always take note of them first.As for sound, anything that can produce it will display its radius of effect, helping with planning your next move. But let's not forget the ; Time stops (or not, depending on your choice) and you can plan actions for each character. Then you can execute them simultaniously, or one after the other, dealers choice. I can't express how satisfying it feels to create one convoluted plan and have everything fall in line, perfectly executing it with the enemy being none the wiser. So master this and reap the fruits of your labour.But the fun doesn't stop there. Each level is just a giant sandbox for you to play in. There is plenty of bushes to hide in, and the level of environmental interactability is excellent, offering some quite fun ways to distract or get rid of enemies. Also, I have to praise the level variety, as no level has a similar layout. Sadly,  I really hoped more levels were like this; So much fun and scheming. Perhaps the Season Pass has some like this, but I don't own it, so I can't say for sure.And when you are all done killing every last red cowboy, the  await you. These are a set of missions with specific imposed conditions that you must follow. They offer a new scenario on an already existing map, but this time with a twist.As for the graphics, well, they are great. The models can look funky up close, but why would you zoom in that far anyway? Having done motion capture work, we received very fluid and realistic animations. As for the environment, their design is also top-notch. Overall, the aesthetic and feel of the game are phenomenal. From the lush mountains of Colorado to the heart of Louisiana, and finally, New Mexico, each area is sculpted with extreme care and attention to detail.And this excellence extends to the audio department. The voice actors did a great job making these characters come to life, especially Isabelle. I like it when she calls me . The banter between the characters is fun to listen to, especially between McCoy and the cat. Sounds generated by objects, environment, and weapons are all great, making levels feel alive. The music especially deserves high praise. The first time I booted the game up, I spent a good 15 minutes just sitting at the main menu and listening to the main theme.There is a saying in Serbia: "". Even tho I haven't played an RTT game in a long time, as soon as I booted up , that sense of familiarity struck me, and I instantly remembered my time with  and . And if you are a fan of the genre, heck, even if you haven't played any RTT games,  deserves your attention. And with a demo available on the store page, you can even take the game out for a test run.

_childDocuments_.review:
On his epic journey through 1870s USA and Mexico, John Cooper will have to take responsibility for mistakes that have been made in the past. On his quest for redemption, Cooper joins forces with the runaway bride Kate O'Hara, shady Arthur "Doc" McCoy, the giant trapper Hector and a mysterious lady from New Orleans. They make their way from the mountains of Colorado to the heart of Louisiana, then finally to New Mexico, right back into Cooper's past.

You take control of this ragtag band becoming a highly functional group of unlikely heroes and heroines. The leader of his team is Cooper, drifter and gunslinger, who can kill quietly with a knife or take out multiple foes with his revolvers. Strongman Hector carries a giant beartrap and can slay the toughest opponents with his trusty axe. Cold-blooded bounty hunter McCoy likes to be methodical, using lures, knockout gas, poison syringes and a custom long-range pistol. Kate can fool almost any man with the right outfit and kill discretely with her hidden gun.

Combine your specialists to overcome tough challenges in many different ways. Plan your moves wisely and execute them perfectly in real-time to sneak past your enemies while remaining undetected.

_childDocuments_.review: A quick and simple review just to throw my thoughts into the sea of red.GameplayPlays a bit like a half baked pc port and it really shows when you look at the controls.This probably wouldnt have been that much of an issue if the targetting worked properly,getting some of the moves off was a pain in the ass and some dont even respond to the correctinputs from time to time. Another thing about the targetting, i hope you like tunnelvision,The targetting zooms the camera so far into your character you can see every individual polygon, but heyatleast itll make the inputs for your moves easier.And if that isnt enough the amount of times youre gonna get hit because youre locked into attack animationswill eventually frustrate you. And no, you cannot animation cancel attacks into a parry, that mightve been a massive redeeming factor for this game if it was possible.EnemiesEveryone complains about the AI being less than ideal, yet people do not mention themeat shield big boy enemies that usually have a wake up attack that can hit youeven though you are behind them, wich will deal about half your hp in one hit and staggerlockyou into death even on the easiest difficulty, there are also normal enemies fully capable of doingthis in the later stages of the game.Not to mention the lovely bosses with their invulnerability phases, very fun boss design there.EnvironmentI liked the environment, reminds me of running around looking in every nook and cranny forhidden stuff just like i did when i played the old dnd games on xbox. Lovely trip down memory lane.I actually dont have any gripes with it, except for the invisible walls spread sporadically out everywhere.MultiplayerSo peoples main point about this game being fun, is it being best enjoyed with friends. We'll you see if youare one of the unfortunate people out there you might get hit with a disconnection bug, and thats frankly alli can call it. Even though ive got good ping and a decent PC setup, though that shouldnt really factor in the slightest, i all of a sudden started disconnecting constantly when starting or joining lobbies. Sometimes i could get into one just to get disconnected during the loading screen when we were about to start with a mission.I wouldnt try your luck with this if i were you.End note?Just wait, please just wait with buying this game. It is the best thing you can do for yourself.There is no reason at all to buy this game for 40 euros or whatever the price is where you're from.There is frankly nothing that this game offers in its current state that makes it worth it, and i do notbelieve one or two patches will be enough to make it worth it either. Try your luck somewhere else.Or rather, do not try your luck ever again. Trust the negative reviews from time to time and just wait for more updates and content, rarely do these types of single/multi player games get worse with time.Side noteThis text format looks like ass, but i cant be bothered fixing it. Just think of this review as early access.

_childDocuments_.review: Early Adopter ThoughtsDon't expect another Dark Alliance game as release on XBoxImagine Vermintide meeting The Lord of the Rings: War in the North.In theory this could be a great idea, but here is why it doesn't quite work in this game. You will also notice these issues link together in the perfect storm1) Solo feels unbalanced - if you can't find players at a similar level you play alone and are unable to rez in boss fights etc.2) Most players were highest level after a week - Got the game but was unable to play until weekend of release. Big mistake as enemies are levelled with characters for all maps3) Inactive Player Base after a month - Good luck finding anyone!4) No Bots - If you've played Vermintide you will know sometimes it is a better option over random players5) Clunky, boring solo Combat - To me it seems slow and clunky, if they have an arrow sponge boss, get ready to yawn6) Irritating environmental effects - Warmth to combat 5 times in one map or you die quickly7) No progress for failure - Got fed up with Vermintide runs where you lose at the last hurdle...8) Takes ages to level up on lower difficultysIn all fairness the story map and characters are nice and the game looks and plays fine except for the above. Unfortunately it becomes more frustrating than fun.If you can put together a team of like minded people, I'm sure it would be a lot better

_childDocuments_.review: Dungeons and Dragons: Dark Alliance is possibly the worst game I've played all year. I jumped into it with zero expectations and still came out disappointed.Let's start with what I found to be the game's two most egregious issues: the AI and the difficulty scaling.The AI has to be some of the worst I've encountered in any game period. Enemies do not react at all to projectiles or any character that seems to be outside of their combat arena. Not only this, but even when standing next to them, the AI takes several seconds to even react to the player's presence, and even then, occasionally during combat will seem to forget the player's existence at complete random.The difficulty scaling works on two different extremes: you either play the recommended difficulty and melt everything you come across in seconds or play even just one tier above that and every encounter takes several minutes to clear while almost if not every attack one-shots you.Something that I haven't seen mentioned much in reviews posted prior to making this one is the game's feat system, which is about as dull as one could possibly make a feat/perk system aka it all comes down to is minor stat upgrades (ex. 10% crit chance).Combat is unsatisfying and incredibly repetitive, at least as the archer character. As the archer, you will be spending almost all of your time holding down the aim button and spamming the shoot button for about 95% of your time in combat since doing literally anything else outside of your two specials will quickly bring your max stamina down to 50% leaving you constantly starved for said stamina. In combination with the AI issues mentioned above, it feels like the game was not built with the archer in mind and that the devs really REALLY don't won't you to play as her.Combat in this game takes up about half of the gameplay. The other half is running through empty hallways, occasionally solving what I could barely even consider "puzzles" and grabbing dull loot that's likely only a minor stat upgrade compared to what you're already wearing.To add on to all of this, the game is super buggy. My personal favorite that my group ran into multiple times was a bug where whenever we wiped on a boss, we'd end up stuck on a loading screen as we hear the boss kill our respawned selves and thus freeze the game, causing us to have to restart the entire level.I'm typing all of this up in a rush on a late night juiced up on three cups of coffee. There are a myriad of other problems like poor animations, bosses reusing normal enemy models, poor sfx, horrific lock-on camera, etc, but I don't have the time nor patience to go into detail about them especially since what I did talk about at some length should be enough to get the point across. It's not like I'm getting paid for this or anything.Some might say that the game is at it's most fun with friends, but that could be said for everything including watching paint dry. If you're looking for a co-op game to play with your friends, then there are better places to spend your money and your hard drive space.
