_childDocuments_.review: At this time, I can't recommend the game for a few reasons. - With the name D&D: Dark Alliance, it is implied that it is at least a spiritual successor to the BG:DA games, however it doesn't really correlate at all. It's one of those games where you have a lobby and pick a stage from there, much like Vermintide or Left 4 Dead, making what little of a story it does have mostly meaningless- The combat attempts to be souls-like, but is clunky and doesn't respond correctly most of the time. Also, even playing in modes designed for your character power level, you will be killed in 1-2 hits on some enemies that aren't even bosses.- The matchmaking isn't optimized. I was level 2 and matched with max level characters, allowing me to attain legendary level equipment, but not allowing me to gain any XP to level up. I understand the reason behind stopping power-levelling, however if I want to get XP, I have to play alone.What we wanted was a modern update to the Dark Alliance series. A good, simple D&D Hack N' Slash. What we got is nothing more than a generic time killer.

_childDocuments_.review: the difficulty is sporatic, the bosses are bland, the enemies' AI is on par with Alien: Colonial Marines, and the combat is button-mashy as all hell. Do not, and I repeat, DO NOT buy this unless you are DESPERATE for a Dungeon Brawler. There are so many games that do this better, and this does the Dark Alliance name a disservice. I'm sure it was rushed by the higher ups, and I don't blame the programmers at all for, what feels like, the most rushed bag of mish-mashed ideas.EDIT: Feel like I gotta elaborate on the difficulty and the combat. The enemies are either A: Childishly easy, who take 1-3 hits before dying and they can't do enough damage to kill you or B: Damage sponges who one-hit no matter what.As WhimsicalPlushie said, the feat system is bland as all hell, with basic stat upgrades being the peak of the system. In addition, certain characters feel more finished than others. Drizzt and Battlehammer feel fluid and playable, while the barbarian and archer are janky and, honestly, need a lot more work to make playable. To summarize, this needed another year in the oven and a whole lot more prep time to make this playable. Oh, also, the netcode kinda sucked during early review time, the bosses would kill us and then continue to kill us on the loading screen (causing a crash every time), and the archer is busted to all hell and back. 3/10, nothing feels good about it. at most, it feels neutral and passable.If you want a good dungeon brawler, either wait for the Dark Alliance remaster that's supposed to land on Steam by the end of this year, or tackle Remnant: From the Ashes, Outriders, Destiny 2, or Path of Exile/Diablo 3. It's unfortunate, but it's the reality we've been dealt.

_childDocuments_.review: It has bones, but arrived version 1.0 dead on arrival. Its design is pandering. It plays like a kids game, or a mobile game, often holding your hand with elementary school puzzles, terrain management, and platform jumping. A kids game would be okay it if were a kid's game, however it has a confusing dark tones regarding its subject matter, themes, and targeted audience of PC gamers and R.A. Salvatore fans. This game would blow my mind on playstation2 in 2004.  the gear grind feels basic, and RNG stats are uninspired. No micro transactions (good thing), but it still reveals loot drops like a loot crate game, which again, kind of feels out of place and really arcade/mobile for the themes of the game. Much of the set piece bonuses are just specific elemental resistances, but i've yet to identify an elemental damage theme by level with that would matter, which would make preparing an armor set for an specific level more meaningful. Sure, you can learn which levels have what enemies, but i don't see a real point in changing armor for the encounters when you can just stun lock the ai. Mundane gear can be transmogrified, but the Legendary gear can't be transmogrified. You start getting epic drops immediately, so after three missions, i was no longer wearing any gear that could be transmog to customize my style. in other words, my character in his best gear looks like my highschool "tacky day" on spirit week, and the gear is sort of out of theme for a grim dark tale in the great north of "Icewind Dale". My Drizzt Character has no hip bones and looks like david bowie in a tesla coil marvel super hero suit and yellow rubber gloves. My favorite outfit was his starting gear, but i can't transmogrify my epic gear.Levels are pretty., albeit pandering. They felt designed for a different game altogether, such as a souls-like, or a bullet hell game. AI logic doesn't know how to adapt to a terrain. so they can't follow you outside a certain aggro arena. You can't knock them off a cliff. The level designer seemed to work independently of any game play concepts.  Boss battles have no stages, no MacGuffin objectives, no strategy required, no witty banter or plot points. Bosses have the same move set as their lesser minions and can be stun locked just as easily. The hit detection feedback can be confusing, when you feel like you dodged something but get hit, or feel like you should get hit but dodged. Camera lock feels like it was designed for a different game. Stamina management feel like it was designed for a different game. The resting mechanic has little impact since you can run past almost every encounter if you reset before the ai responds to your presence. I say it has bones because some of the characters play style is under-cooked, but some of the characters combos feel fun and have a cadence/pacing to them. Drizzt is really fun to play when you unlock all his move sets. He's very mobile and it feels good to pull off a huge combo uninterrupted. I think this game was originally meant to be a "god of war"solo player game with drizzt-only campaign to honor the source material, since drizzt seems to be the most fleshed out with his combo attacks and animations. Somewhere along the line this was re-purposed into a loot crawl brawler with RA Salvator's name on it.  There is a chance for a redemption arc with patches and updates, maybe perhaps even mod overhauls if there were a community for it?  but if that happens, it would be probably 2023 or later before it would be worth buying on a reduced sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I got a few problems with this game.1. There's an annoying delay on some button presses, like when you open your menu, shop and character sheet screen.2. There's an annoying delay on item pickups that will sometimes make you come back to do it again because the loot just decides it didn't want to be picked up right that second.3. Combat is a bit weighty, and that wouldn't be a problem especially for the more beefy characters except there isn't much feedback and communication that you should be getting when you hit a goblin ( even that seems delayed).4. Combat can be devastating and satisfactory, but it also commits to that animation to do the attack, and there are only a few moves in your line-up that will allow you to react to an oncoming attack while you're the one attacking. I'm not sure if was trying to replicate the Souls combat style, but it doesn't really work for most encounters that are more unforgiving, and are often surrounding you if you choose to solo the dungeon.5. AI is like a trail mix bag if it also included melatonin and barbed wire. They stand around and do nothing if you are not in their immediate vicinity, and their damage can vary wildly depending on the difficulty you selected. I'm talking the difference between a tricycle and a 18-wheeler.6. Respawning is perhaps the dumbest I've seen in a video game. The party leader is the spawning point, so when you get incapacitated and decide to force a respawn, you at first get thrown back to the beginning of the dungeon, which sucks but the game sends you back to where the party leader is after 10 seconds. This is all fine unless the party leader is downed, and forces a respawn themselves. Excluding the boss fight at the end of the dungeon, all party members will get thrown back to the party leader's location, forcing the entire party to make the long trek back to where ya'll were last. 7. Disconnections isn't an unexpected occurrence in a multiplayer match, but when the games themselves are about an hour long with spongy trash and even spongier bosses even on easier difficulties, it just puts a bad taste in my mouth when  I can be disconnected even in a post game summary screen, and still lose all of my progress and rewards for completing the match (one of my achievements on the game turns out to be a farce because i lost connection at the very last second of the post game summary, I'm not kidding).Overall, it's a game that I can definitely see the potential to become a satisfactory game that most definitely needs to be smoothed with a steamroller. preferably if they can get rid of all the delays, breath a little more life to the monsters, and fix the respawn system they got, then i could see my self spending alot more time seeing what this game has to offer.

_childDocuments_.review: I normally don't review games, and definitely don't normally leave a negative review, but I just have to be honest for the people who are interested in the game.· I played this with a friend, and we didn't even realize there was a tutorial until we were reading the reviews.· Combat and movement feels very clunky. I had to change the camera speed to 100% so it wouldn't take me 5 years to turn around. You're basically limited to left and right for your camera. Up and down is very slow and very limited. Lining up for attacks is a 50/50. By the time your attack hits (Unless you're playing Drizzt and have a faster attack rate) there's a chance the enemy will move out of the way.· Enemies do weird amounts of damage. We did a campaign on a difficulty less than 50 above our power level. Mobs were easy, but the boss did some combo hit with no warning that one-shot.· Navigation felt off. Maybe it was just us, but it was hard to tell where we had already been.· AI is bad. If one of us got knocked down the enemies would just continue to target that person, leaving the other to do whatever. This really just made things easier because the other player could continue fighting their mobs before resurrecting, rather than having to fight more mobs.· In the settings, even though you have a cursor and the setting have arrows that appear to be clickable, most of the options require you to use your keyboard. This was really confusing for us.Honestly has a really similar vibe to Vermintide, but isn't nearly as good. I wanted to like this game, since I loved the Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance series as a kid. I wasn't expecting it to be like the old games, but I wasn't expecting to be this disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like Dark Alliance. I really did.I've been playing D&D for several years now, and I've played the previous Dark Alliance games too. When I first started playing this game with friends from my D&D group, I was hoping for a fun, fast-paced co-op experience set in the Forgotten Realms setting. Unfortunately, things went sour pretty quickly.First, there are the bugs. I know the developers have been fixing many of these, but from the first session we played, my friends and I have experienced game-breaking glitches that wasted our time and even caused us to lose progress. Sometimes, early on, my character wouldn't change levels with the rest of the group after a boss fight. More recently, one of my friends didn't get credit for finishing a level at all. Issues like these meant we'd have to replay an entire level, something that we didn't enjoy having to do.That brings me to the second problem. The game is just not very fun. You control your character in third-person perspective, and have various attacks and combos you can pull off. The combos almost remind me of a fighting game. You can also level up to unlock new moves, and pick up better equipment while playing to increase your character's effectiveness. This all sounds fun, in theory. In practice, the majority of the combos don't really matter--gameplay generally devolves into using the few really short and effective combos, or just mashing the attack and dodge buttons until enemies die. It's sloppy, and not satisfying.Also, the randomly-dropped equipment is rarely good for anything other than being sold to a merchant. Even after finishing several 'chapters' of the game, my character was still using the same old, weak gear.And the chapters feel pretty long. Each chapter has several levels, and each level is about 15 minutes long, on average. It does feel like there's a lot of content, which sounds good at first, but it doesn't feel satisfying or exciting to play through. It feels mindless.I will say that the art style is very interesting to look at, at least. Seeing the game artists' take on well-known D&D monsters, cultures, and locales was one of the few highlights of my time playing this game. Reading the in-game lore collection was another. It seems the developers paid attention to the source material, and I appreciate that.I think the game would have greatly benefited from reducing the scope of the moves you COULD potentially use in combat, and the options of the loot you MIGHT randomly pick up while playing, in order to ensure that you'd always have a small number of fun moves and interesting gear that you actually WOULD enjoy using. Maybe reduce or even remove the items that differ only slightly in their statistics. And test out a smaller roster of available moves for each character in different areas of the game. Maybe even shorten the levels! It's possible this game just tried to do too many things and ended up doing most of them to a mediocre degree.Ultimately, though, as it is now, I don't think this game is worth your time or money--let alone that of several people buying the game to play co-op together. There are better games using the D&D license out there, and better 4-player co-op games as well.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me preface this by saying I really enjoyed the small amount of time I put into this game. That said, I can't recommend it. I come from the land of terrible free to play MMOs, so when I heard that this game was bad, I took it with a grain of salt, and I'm glad I did. It was not nearly as bad as I expected, and I was able to pass off some design flaws as a "D&D-ified" quirk, like how you have to stop attacking to get your character to turn around, as something like that would affect combat in the tabletop version as well (at least the way my DM played).First off we'll cover the good. The locations are stunningly beautiful. The writing feels very on brand for the different enemy races, and each mission is written like an in-character DM narrating (in a good way). I only played as the Ranger, and I enjoyed the combat, it was a fun mix of dashing around the battlefield and brute force stunning/fighting some larger enemies. Each fight you have to consider what enemies are attacking in what way and dash past some to kill one that is more dangerous. I think with a full group of 4, this would be an even more fun dynamic, however I only played solo so it got frustrating sometimes when a single enemy would wipe the floor with you from behind 5 others.Now the bad. The main issue is a lack of polish. After a while it can start to feel like you're doing the same thing over and over. Almost every boss is a very generic enemy that has more health and hits harder. The bosses that are unique have really weird gimmicky mechanics that feel almost like a chore rather than an epic fight. The gearing system feels awkward, it plays like a gearset-based MMO, where certain sets will drop in certain zones, but on the lower difficulties they really don't matter. And once you hit the higher difficulties, it becomes so hard that the only thing you can do is focus on gearing. If there were an open world I would love this style, but it's a mission based game, similar to Vermintide. As such the gearset system just doesn't feel right, and feels like a way to artificially inflate the endgame. It feels like you have to grind missions you've already completed just to have a chance to attempt the hard version. At least in an open I could be exploring while I power up.Overall it's not a terrible game. If you don't mind less-than-great games, I would recommend trying it. If you have a few friends who want to play, I'd definitely recommend it. But if you're like me and just wanted a fun RPG to grind for a while, this isn't the most interesting one.

You will stay locked on to dead enemies.Some enemies will drop loot, if you manage to knock one of those monsters into a hole, the loot will forever be stuck hovering above that pit, unreachable.Any loot left on the ground before a short rest will disappear after a short rest.Loot can seemingly spawn in any direction around an open chest. _childDocuments_.review: 16 hours between Wulfgar / Drizzt Solo and Multiplayer before deciding to put my 2 cents.First I'll start by saying that two main complaints are legitimate but pretty exaggerated.- Netcode does need work and diminishes the value of twitch mechanics which otherwise work flawlessly Solo but at the same time you're in a group so unless you're the type to scream "But I pressed the button!" and rage. It's mostly an annoyance right now and not bad enough to kill enjoyment of the game.- Enemy AI is indeed a bit derpy taking "Action Movie" turns to attack the player. This is most notable Solo. At the same time if the enemy were to aggro stick the player all at once I doubt it would be Solo'd above 2. Hero difficulty. Far as I've seen the issue with hitting enemies from range, esp bosses is generally fixed and in the end this isn't a competitive game. I've seen 5/5 star games where the AI is still easily exploited. Just play the game and stop trying to break it.- The meat of this game is it's combat and in that it does a great job. The aforementioned twitch mechanics work great. There are a lot of different combo types that take talent to use properly well as different ways to open into those combos. There's heavy emphasis on positioning, timing and whether or not to dedicate to certain attacks. Some attacks are slow and you should not use them at the wrong time or you will be punished. Don't put yourself in a corner then complain you can't dodge out like some. That's dumb.- Enemy Telegraphed attacks are spot on but janky Multiplayer. It's quite easy to see these attacks coming and when / if the netcode is fixed there should be no problems.- Character Building. Feats and Attributes don't amount to much. In general each character plays like they're intended. However Armor and keeping different sets is where you can get some customization and on higher difficulties it's pretty much needed to keep different sets based on encounters in the mission. ie Resistances, support health drops, Reflect Damage, Lifesteal, Condition Afflictions and sets based on boosting certain skills.- Graphics are Basic. Draw Distance is short for ground objects. Distance LOD and texture are Average. - Atmosphere is Good. Each map captures a unique and interesting environment.- Sound Effects are Average. - Music is Good. *When it's playing.The main thing that bothers me as a PC gamer is neglect for PC UI interface. Thankfully menu interactions are done outside of missions. However a lack of 21:9 support and re-bind on WASD is a problem. Maybe not you though. Overall there need to be about 20+ more graphic & config options going on here that are missing.If they manage to check some of these boxes which I imagine they will then I can recommend the game. It's not bad by any means and I've been enjoying it despite these launch flaws. It just needed more time to cook. If you're curious still and esp if you're familiar with NWO combat this is essentially a new and more in-depth version of that which you might find worth your time. Otherwise just wait for some of those improvements.Hope this was helpful.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been desperately trying to enjoy this game for the past 2-3 hours. I adjusted the settings getting rid of the annoying HUD so that I could feel more immersed, so I could just focus on the "hack and slash action-adventure" game that I was promised. Maybe it could be fun if they had taken the time to actually finish this game. The combat is laggy, unresponsive, does not flow and that makes it rather frustrating, (especially for a game that is supposed to excel at hacking and slashing). Up close hack and slash combat wasn't even the worst part I noticed, the worst part was trying to use projectiles. Drizzt's sword throw? Forget it, a pathetic move in the state it is in, it has no stagger impact, super slow, passes right through enemies as if they were bloody ghosts, you can just sit there and spam his projectile while the enemies stand there like monstrous vegetables.This leads into my next criticism, a lot of the enemies I encountered don't chase you if you're standing far enough away, even when you're throwing a blade at their skulls they just ignore you like everything is fine, they don't even try to dodge your attacks. If I throw a sword at someone's face I expect them to at least have a shred of a reaction, stagger backwards, hold your face in pain as you bleed, something like that is to be expected. Speaking of violence, sure this game can be bloody as it should be for an M rated D&D game, but I was expecting better gore detail, like limbs and heads flying from bodies as I cut down monsters.It's clear to me after only playing a couple levels that this game fails to satisfy in its current state of development. Really hope Dark Alliance gets finished in future updates, but I'm guessing that will take another year of "patches" to even get this game to the state it should've been on release. Considering how hard this game has bombed I'd say we all deserve a refund for those of us who payed 40-60 dollars, this game certainly isn't worth that much, maybe in the future when it is fixed it could be worthy of a 30 dollar price, but maybe isn't this moment, and at the moment I feel cheated out of 60 smackaroos.

_childDocuments_.review: After finally finishing the game, I feel like I can accurately provide a review for this game...rather than just a list of gripes an complaints. Let's start with the Cons first. Because that way we can just rip the band aid off. - Glitches and bugs. Enemies fall through floors. Bosses become immune and prevent you from finishing a boss fight. The shields off of key items don't drop even once you try to trigger them. Some.... well.... almost all of these incidents require you to restart the round. Others are minor and merely warrant you jumping off a convenient cliff to reset your character. - Matchmaking. I am lucky enough to have friends to play this with which make all the difference. Randoms wont sit through the wipes and the frustration. No matter what you do, they just wont. The game needs help from a bot support system. Also FOR THE LOVE OF GOD, untether the party to the party leader. That is the STUPIDEST, LAZIEST mechanic to include in this game. This isn't early 2000's. Lets move on from that. - Enemy hit boxes are purely suggestion and sometimes... they teleport. Yes. Teleport. And sometimes the Veerbog will redirect in midair from a flying belly flop to land on your face. -Linear and Redundant level design. The levels are quite linear with only the illusion of branching paths. And there really isn't a replay value. If you want to grind for gear, that is about the only reason to replay it. And now for the Pros. - This game is a good 40+ hour distraction with friends. Just make sure they have a good sense of humor. - The characters do play differently, but I would not recommend playing them outside of how they were intended. And yes, CB is broken as hell. Play her first :)- The game is challenging and unforgiving, but you can dumb down the difficulty level to your preferred liking. So overall, if you have friends and you like dungeon crawlers, I would try this. Maybe if its on sale, probably not at full price. The cons alone don't warrant the price tag. But I think if this is your genre, you will enjoy it enough to ignore its flaws.

This game on the other hand leaves me disappointed that a developer team would have the audacity to take on the kindle of DARK ALLIANCE and develop it this way. The concept and lore are there, but the gameplay......Yikes. The thing we all know and love is completely and utterly ruined. If you can't remake the combat system, leave it how it always was in the last two installations. You can't mess that up because the resources are there. Top down with some 2021 flare. _childDocuments_.review: DO NOT BUY THE DELUXE EDITIONIt's a classic beat-em-up brawler, nothing fancy.  It's fun for what it is, if a bit tedious. The damage that you deal out feels inconsistent at times.One of my biggest gripes is having pre-ordered the deluxe edition, I was expecting access to special, unique sets of equipment as advertised in the store.  Come to find out, they were skins.  This was not mentioned and I would not have purchased the deluxe edition had I known this.On the note of skins, changing the skins of equipment can slightly but randomly impact the stats of equipment without any consistency.  If you were to cycle through the skins you would observe that the same skin will produce different results, if any at all.  I personally feel that skins shouldn't alter the stats of equipment, it's a deviation from the cosmetic nature of skins.Anyways, great fun overall, play with friends, don't buy the deluxe edition expecting to get actual equipment sets

There are  of people downing entire dungeons (bosses included) as Catti without them even reacting to her shots. _childDocuments_.review: I reviewed this for  and gave it a 5/10. There's lots to love about the setting, the comedic asides from enemies, and some of the expanded movesets you can unlock for the four pre-made characters. But make no mistake: this is a broken game that will frustrate you and waste your time.Enemy leveling is incoherent: there's no way to tell whether a trash mob is going to fall over in a couple hits or tank tons of damage and potentially one-shot kill you. Hitboxes are nowhere near the models on screen. Gear and stat adjustments make no difference in terms of how you approach the game, which doesn't change at all over the course of 21 campaign missions + dungeons.The levels themselves are occasionally interesting but ultimately they're all linear corridors that will sometimes stall you with a fight in a wider arena area. Most of these, it turns out, are entirely optional - you can run through straight to the end of most levels without fighting at all if you want to.Bosses are boring - they're mostly repurposed, larger versions of the handful of enemy types you encounter ad nauseam through the rest of the missions, just granted huge health pools and additional magic attacks in some cases. Don't worry though, since they'll only occasionally take note of your presence, and at no point will they attempt to avoid any environmental hazards that might be in their area.This is just an unfinished, broken game. If you want to play co-op, pick up Vermintide, Deep Rock Galactic, or even Outriders.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot of potential. There is a really fun 3rd Person Hack-n-Slash here, but one that has been released a few months too early. It's been made by people who clearly have a lot of love for the source material - as the characters and locations you visit have been depicted with incredible care and attention to detail and atmosphere. While the plot is as straightforward as the novels it's based on, the voice acting, music and overall presentation largely stand out. Underneath the occasional glitch, the AI hiccups and lopsided balance, there is a game that is easy to pick up  with a very high skill ceiling. My hope is that people will give it a chance and support the better game that it could become.

_childDocuments_.review: As the fan of Robert Salvatore's works, I am extremely glad I finally decided to buy this game despite many negative reviews. The game might have had issues at launch, but many of them seem to have been addressed.What I enjoyed so far (please, note that I have finished 3 chapters solo and played only one of five characters):- Lore: I like to listen to the introduction narrated at the beginning of each act. It reminds me of playing the "Legend of Drizzt" board game (the D&D Adventure System), where I used to read aloud the introduction to each adventure. I like reading the collected tablets, scrolls, and quotes on gear. The paintings and reliefs also add to the story.- Graphics / World: The locations are truly beautiful and provide grand views. The level design is relatively simple but allows both vertical and horizontal exploration. Locations are not unnecessarily convoluted. I like exploring and discovering hidden chests, collectibles, and secondary objectives before continuing down the main path.- Combat: The combat system is fun, satisfying, and challenging. Even at level 1, my character had a wide array of moves and skills. Unlockable moves add to the depth of the system. Combat mostly feels fluid and natural. Moreover, almost all moves, even the ones ulocked at lower levels, have their use. Blocking, parrying, rolling, sidestepping, and jumping are present as well.- Progression / Leveling: While not overly complicated, progression is present. Feature / skill trees are not elaborate but provide choice.What I found strange:- Itemization: While the set system is interesting in terms of set bonuses and appearance, items seem to have random attributes. Two items with the same name may have different characteristics. In my opinion, it would be more logical if sets had a range of dedicated attributes.- Story: While the chapters seem to be connected in terms of plot, the final task or even direction of the player is not apparent. It is not clear what exactly the player is supposed to accomplish. AI: Sometimes, enemies are excessively idle, particularly when there are many of them. Some monsters seem to be waiting for their turn to engage in the fight. However, when playing solo, that is a welcome feature.- Occasional texture issues: Sometimes, the bodies of slain monsters are slowly drifting away. When landing on a object after a jump, the character may be floating in the air above that object before touching the ground.Overall, despite some flaws, I enjoy playing the game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot of mixed reviews and I see why. It's not deep, its not nuanced, and it doesn't have much to offer in respect of RPG elements. It has nothing to do with D&D gameplay or the typical ARPGs that Wizards of the Coast are known for in their video games. In my opinion it plays like a cut-rate, bargain-bin Shadow of Mordor without any of the charm. There is a lot of emphasis on building hit streaks and executing special moves for your chosen character. There is a clear emphasis on multiplayer, but the community interest is not their to sustain it and I've not been able to experience it. I'm also willing to bet that 90% of players main Drizzt, although I've not personally managed to find the statistics. I'm guilty, I've been playing as the drow ranger myself. The missions are short and shallow and all access is from a central hub area. The only NPC is a merchant with no real characterisation and limited utility.  All missions boil down to go to "x location" and kill a thing, great now go to "y location" and kill another thing. What there is of the story appears not to have much continuity from mission to mission, or (if there is) the story is not compelling enough for me to care and I have been skipping all cutscenes even on a first play-through - not a good sign.  Also, on the subject of cutscenes they seem to be the only medium by which the "story" is told. There's no dialogue trees, there's no player choice and there's no interactions outside of the aforementioned combat. As a fan of the books, it is nice to see much beloved characters in this game, but the story does not do them justice and the "story" (such as it is) does not fit with the continuity of the books. The characters come across as shallow and do not have any breadth of character. There are also changes in appearance for several of them which is not congruous with the descriptions in R.A Salvatore's novels or wider D&D lore. However, I would still recommend the game for a casual gamer. As button-masher brawlers go, you could do worse (although you could also do better). The missions being short are in some ways a blessing when you have limited free time but want to jump in for a 20 min game of something. I work long hours, have little time for gaming, and come home exhausted. Sometimes I don't want an immersive, deep, genre defining game of the year. Sometimes I want to mindlessly hit light and heavy attacks - and you know what, this game scratches that itch. The loot grind and core game-play loop, though nothing to write home about, is implemented well enough to keep you wanting to play a little more, and surprisingly I have actually found myself having fun, despite it's obvious shortcomings. I'm now about 9 hours in so it clearly must be doing something right, and I am finding myself playing a quick mission when I have a dull moment. Is this going to be the best game you ever play? No, absolutely not. Is it good enough to kill a few hours here and there when you are in the mood for something casual? Yes, and I'd recommend it for that reason. Consider picking it up when it is on sale or if any of the "positives" speak to you otherwise it's probably one you shouldn't lose sleep over if you give it a miss.

_childDocuments_.review: Atrocious game, its a discgrace to Dungeons & Dragons franchise and Companions of the Hall. These are one of the most beloved characters in D&D and this is the game they get? I gave this game a fair shake, just for the characters alone, but I will not finish it, as its such a horrible experience.Everything about this game feels amateurish, broken and unfun. Combat is stiff, with unresponsive controls and poorly designed enemies with unclear hitboxes. Bosses are one of the worst I have ever experienced, they are just buffed versions of regular enemies, to the point of being huge damage sponges or gank squads. Fight with The Chef was the straw that broke the camel's back, his hitboxes are huge and he constantly knocks you down or kills you with 1-2 hits (on recommended gear level). Not to mention his arena is constantly sprayed with flames that don't damage him.Entire game is buggy, janky and oh so poorly designed. Nothing about these locations is interesting and you constantly encounter the same props and enemies. It wouldn't be so bad if at least combat was fun, but it isn't, you don't feel like these mighty heroes at all. Attacks don't properly lock onto enemies and there is no animation cancelling, so you are constantly flailing around hoping your dodge will become responsive when you need it.There is an enormous potential in making an action RPG with these characters, or at least with Drizzt, but D&D Dark Alliance doesn't come close to realizing that potential, its galaxies away. Its one of the most unfun, broken and janky games I have ever played. Stay away from this piece of ♥♥♥♥, believe all the negative reviews, yes - its that bad. Its high time Wizards of the Coast gave D&D license to good developers that can realize its potential, not a bunch of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, that don't know how to make a half decent game.

_childDocuments_.review: I saw this game advertised initially in the early part of 2020, perhaps 2019.  I kept an eye on the site and Facebook page because The Legend of Drizzt is one of my favourite book series ever.If this had been a hack and slash game in the vein of Demon Stone or even Dynasty Warriors, it would have been acceptable.  Listening to the Companions of the Hall banter as they sliced through hordes of enemies?  That would be awesome.Instead we get a sort of Vermintide knock off.  As my friend and I went through the levels, we could see and point out the spawning locations of monsters and what would trigger them.  Every single troll comes out of a hole in the ground.  Every. Single. One.  Verbeegs have out houses.  Sometimes there is a hole NEXT to a random wooden outhouse and BOOM, troll and verbeeg, right on schedule.The Akar Kessle fight (why the heck is Akar even in this game?) was a disgrace.  He just stood there and let us kill him.  Three times.  In the same fight.  No ads, no special magic mechanic, no thing.  Just slapped him three times.The cosmetic system would be better off not existing.  All, with very few exceptions, of the armours and weapons look silly.  I did not find ANY gear I could imagine any of the companions wearing.  Drizzt very quickly just became a drow assassin in all black or purple spider pattern gear, as if the development team were given a generic rundown of drow lore.Cattie's bow is so short it may as well be a toy.  That is all on that point.There are huge amounts of visual and game play bugs.  Sometimes the 'activate' button just breaks and you can't loot in this looting game, or pick up friends if they should somehow go down.The higher difficulties are beyond stupid.  Every weak goblin is now a near immortal god that will take combos of your whole stamina bar to murder, whilst his two godly brothers whack you from the sides.  Sadly, this applies to bosses too.  Their mechanics are so simple that it would make even Akar Kessle look competent, so the devs just gave them an extra few bucket loads of health to soak up the damage as they glitch around the combat arena.All you had to do was let us play as the Companions murdering DnD monsters.  Not try to retell the Shard's story as badly as you possible can.The environment design is awesome, very pretty, the guy that designed that needs a gold star.  Everyone else can see me after class.My friend and I plan to continue this game and finish it, as well as return when the free updates happen.  If things improve, and I hope they do, I'll update this review.  Until now, stay far, far away.

_childDocuments_.review: Given the bugs that currently exist in this game, I cannot in good conscious recommend this game. The fact that this is marked as a full release title shows us how low our standards for games have become and how meaningless the words "early access" and "full release" really are. It's clear that there either wasn't proper QA testing, or someone greenlit this for release despite these flaws.- Infinite loading screens essentially requiring you to restart resulting in you losing 1+ hours of progress (and any XP/gear you've obtained) just isn't acceptable. - Loot rarity has no meaning. Receiving an epic/ legendary item in the 2nd second stage makes the rest of the loot feel subpar. - Forget playing co-op because the desync is god awful. Enemies will teleport randomly, attacks will hit you before the animations even start, sometimes there wont even be an animation at all! (this isnt an issue playing solo)- Enemy AI is absolutely brain dead. Often times they will AFK as you're rezzing your buddy, or just sit there and watch you attack them. Others wont even move toward you until you stand still.+ Combat was pretty fun when the game worked.+ Decent level of customization with gear, consumables, unlockables, and combos make your character feel like they're progressing.+ Cutscenes were enjoyable to watch+ Exploring feels semi rewarding Supposedly there is a mage character coming to the game #SOON but who knows when you'll get that. There is "potential" (I dislike this word) in this game, however by the time a game reaches said "potential" it's often dead in the water. I understand there is a thing called a "marketing budget" but maybe instead of spending that money on hiring celebs and streamers to play your game, and invest a LITTLE bit of that on development we could have a solid experience here. Buy at your own risk.

_childDocuments_.review: After diving in all morning since launch, I can say that this game should've waited just a bit longer. All the parts are there, but with key components being very buggy, laggy, or downright not working at all, it's hard to recommend the game in its current state.NARRATIVE-It's no shocker that you're thrown into a virtual D&D campaign. You're not really given a large focal direction of a linear story, instead thrust into a D&D world halfway through and expected to understand where everything's expected to go. Backstory was either very limited or nonexistent. Each act you perform seems to operate on its own and has no direct connection the preceding or following acts at all.ENEMIES / BOSSES-Enemy & boss names either look like they came out of a random name generator or complete the phrase "(blank) the (blank)." Attempt at originality is there, but names don't really match the characters since all enemies statically move with the same personalities across the board.-Focus on the popular D&D enemies were very apparent from the beginning. Trolls, goblins, orcs, and the occasional wizards, all of which carry similar or almost exact enemy design.GAME / LEVEL DIFFICULTY-The difficulty setting for acts is a good touch. Being able to adjust your difficulty to increase rewards creates that high risk/high reward scenario that many gamers enjoy.-Despite the ability to set your own difficulty levels, there's basically only 2 difficulty settings: You become a tank and mow everything over, or you get 1-tapped by anything that's not a regular goblin enemy. Large-enemy or boss stomp mechanics and AOE range are beyond troublesome, if not impossible for close-range players who's characters, you know....have to be up close to do damage like the barbarian or assassin. Essentially, you will never do enough damage at higher difficulties before a major enemy or boss 1-taps you, making your character choice worthless to your party since you'll be spending your entire engagement trying to draw enemies away just for a chance to revive your teammate.-Act III boss battles are the standout encounters in each world area. They actually have somewhat different mechanics aside from other levels...until you realize that the majority of boss encounters in each world area are simply killing smaller enemies to open up the boss for damage. ENVIRONMENT / WORLD DESIGN-Players really do feel like they're immersing in a D&D world - caves, rocky mountains, glacier caverns, etc. The design of each level is unique to their own, but it's apparent that the developers attempted to make each level feel so similar that they almost look the exact same in aesthetic and design. Originality in level designs honestly leave little to be desired - smack a wood fence, blow up a door or two, jump and grab onto a ledge with a red cloth on them to guide your way, avoid damage areas on the ground, rinse and repeat. It's the same designs, reused in every level.LOOT / REWARDS / ITEMS-Loot feels damn good to pick up and receive when you complete a level. The tally screen at the end of an act makes you feel like you accomplished way more than you actually did. The game itself almost makes you feel like it's a looter shooter without the shooter aspect. Think Diablo hack-and -slash.-Rewards seem very limited to simply finding them in chests only. Rarely will you find any enemies that drop loot for you, and even then your loot is tied to the difficulty you're on, so if you're not the party leader of your group and they chose a lower difficulty, the chances of you getting gear in every encounter that you'll upgrade and/or use becomes slim to none. You'll most likely be spending your time in the merchant store selling every piece of armor you were rewarded.-Item builds in comparison to their actual use is nonexistent. The amount of stats you receive for a character are very reminiscent of a D&D campaign, but in a hack-and-slash design such as this they're basically not needed. Your life bar & stamina bar are the only things you're going to focus on during your entire gameplay. World design is so limited to enemy attacks and AOE pools that the amount of resistance traits seems needless.COMBAT-Combat is at its absolute best when you create attack chains and open up different move abilities, such as barbarian hammer swings shifting from light to fierce and spelling doom for enemies. However, it quickly shows when you become reliant on the same attack patterns over and over because the enemies are only one of two thing: Shielded or non-shielded. That's it. You'll find yourself becoming very repetitive very quickly.-I hate to bring this up, but combat, unless required to progress, is almost pointless. The amount of times I had an entire party down only to simply run back to where we were while avoiding encounters entirely was almost insulting. Enemies sit there completely oblivious to the fact you're running past them. The amount of experience you get for enemies in the tally  screen just isn't feasible enough to justify reengaging or even pre-engaging.-The frequent safe zone mechanic that pops up after specific encounters is awesome. You have the option to choose to save your checkpoint and refresh, or risk it all for a loot rarity bonus. Realistically though, if you're running 3 or more party members in your group, there is absolutely no reason to checkpoint. Battle are solid enough with 3 or 4 people in a group that the difficulty vs revive ratio makes checkpoints worthless when better loot is in front of you.AUDIO-Audio is traditional as to be expected for a release game. Sliders make the game easy to adjust from its preset ear-bleeding level.-Cinematic audio is not applied to audio levels and act independently, so they always remain extremely loud.QUALITY OF LIFE (QOL)-The combat tutorial was great for learning combat, but the absence of any other tutorial makes the navigation of the UI, menu, market, etc very difficult for players. It's literally a "pick it up and figure it out" thing at first glance. It's not "difficult" per-say to figure out how to navigate the game menus, but the sheer design alone makes a tutorial a needed thing that was never implemented. You're not told about adding moves, feats, or other character customizations such as equipment upgrades in the market or other vital gameplay options.-Keybindings on launch do an excessive amount of reversion to default settings. It doesn't happen in-game by itself, rather when the game is restarted. You'll find instances where any keybind changes made will not appear in the game U/I during play so you may find yourself accidentally hitting the wrong button because you either forgot that you changed it or it reverted and didn't revise itself.-The ring and necklace equipment options in the market rarely ever work when clicked on to either change, sell, swap, or upgrade your equipment. I found myself clicking endlessly on each 50+ times before they finally load the next screen.-Selling equipment requires you hovering over the item you want to sell and holding enter rather than mouse clicking, then if you attempt to sell another item you have to move the cursor away entirely and then back to refresh the market list so you can sell again.-It's extremely obvious that this game was made for priority controller use. The chest in the middle of the home area, nearly all menus and the trophy section of the game were clearly meant to be used with a controller stick because clicking on anything menu-related will have no response. Instead, you have to use WASD to move and navigate.MATCHMAKING-Two options: You host, or someone else does. Only available in the home area, never in-game. This creates extremely long wait times & sometimes severe in-game latency.OVERALL: 5/10It's got all the makings of a great, fun game to play with friends, but the repetition, QoL issues & matchmaking restrictions are holding it back.-Jake

_childDocuments_.review: This feels like a third person action game from about 2012 in a lot of ways, which I mean as high praise because I really liked those. You choose a character, choose a map, go there, kill dudes, hoover up some loot, tweak your gear and do it again. The maps have a pretty high density of secrets, but they're usually pretty easy to find with a little attention, it's enough to keep you clued into the environment but not enough to turn it into a puzzle game. There's also a fair amount of character in the environmental design and enemy chatter, which is funny to listen to. The combat system is surprisingly deep, with a pretty wide variety of moves for each character; if you keep the difficulty low you don't really need to worry about it, but higher difficulties reward understanding how to chain moves. Unlike a lot of similar recent games *coughEldenRingcough* combat is fast paced, and you're usually fighting lots of enemies at once, which definitely sells the whole playing as Drizzt fantasy. There's boss fights, but they aren't the focus of the game, and don't generally feel like you need to learn some dumb obscure gimmick in order to beat. Graphically it isn't the greatest, but once I'm playing, I really don't notice. If you're expecting something really recent and cutting edge feeling, this isn't it. If you go in wanting something that feels like it would be at home on the XBox 360 or so, you will be very happy.

_childDocuments_.review: To start this review, many of the first negative reviews, and highest rated ones, are both much too critical and based off of a low amount of hours.This game is marvelous, but it would be ignorant to write this review and say there are no issues. Of course, there are some glaring issues. But many of them are no where near as detrimental as some of the high rated negative reviews make them seem. The worst issue in my opinion is the lackluster AI. Many of the enemies, simply won't attack you, if you don't start attacking them. And you get warmed up to that very fast. However, there are some AI, who are very aggressive, and being warmed up to AI not generally attacking you, it makes it feel like... a normal game. However, if you're playing with a team, I have not yet encountered an enemy who will actively attack you whilst reviving a teammate. THAT BEING SAID, the monsters are VERY fun to fight against, when they actually fight back. Except for some. Namely, Verbeeg, Stygian Riders, and Trolls. They're simply bullet sponges. But, their attacks make it feel like an actual dungeon brawler. You have to actively dodge and evade and make use of it being stunned, to get hits in. There are some very enjoyable fights with enemies in this game. And it feels very satisfying to get off a long combo and kill an enemy. To go over the pros and cons;PROS:- World building and design. It's breathtaking. It's exceptional. Every map has some winding paths to follow that reward you with more loot and optional quests, or you can stay on the main objective and fight fun enemies, and reach the end goal. The design of maps, the look, being able to look out into inaccessible areas and see, for example, the bones of a dragon. It's great.-The music and audio. It's DND. What did we expect? The music is FULL. It's an entire orchestra, giving off the energetic highs and the scary lows of a battle. It makes the music fun to listen to while running a dungeon... for the 7th time. Trying to get your gearset.-The story! It's enthralling. Fighting giant monster after giant monster trying to reach the end, where your met with Icewind, the ice dragon trying to make good on her vows to destroy the party that killed her partner, Icingdeath. Fighting Ice Trolls, flaming verbeeg, goblin emporers, and finding yourself trapped in this magical world where you just want to keep going.-The endgame loop, it's just like any other arpg and hack and slash looter. You grind x dungeon for x hours to get x gearset to raise your overall "gear score" by a small margin. but its fun! The dungeons have some good repeatability that actually make you want to play the game after beating the 15-20 hours of story.-The promise of MORE. two free dlcs over the summer, a paid expansion with a new character in the fall, the fact that they actually ACKNOWLEDGE the community and have responded to known issues and are constantly looking to fix bugs. It's great and it makes me feel like there will always be more to the game.CONS.-Finicky AI. As I said in the first few lines. It is sometimes good, and sometimes it won't notice you.-The scaling for FIRST TIME PLAYERS, from CR1 - CR2, can be difficult, but also, its because the CR1 enemies fight back less, compared to CR2-6. I've tested it, and in my experience, the enemies are actually easier to face in CR1, not considering the lack of health compared to others.-Lack of content, kind of. It's no secret that for this game and many others like this, there is not as much BASE CONTENT as people would prefer, and some people who get these games don't have the mindset to max every character, get everyone good gear, etc. So if you're looking for something with 100s of hours of story, this, notably, isn't the game for you. -The community. The subreddit discord for this game is horrendous. People complaining about every single little aspect, saying how this is the worst game they've ever played and then going on to say that they only have 2 hours. Saying the game is insanely laggy and then mentioning they barely meet the minimum requirement for specs. Sure, it's not as good as Baldurs Gate Dark Alliance 1-2, yet. But it can be. And it is good to know the Devs are hard at work trying to make it the best game it can be.TL;DRThe negative reviews are much too critical, but the game is far from perfect. High potential, but also very good right now. Definitely could be better, but I would 100% buy on sale, and if you have the money, buy it now. Very good game with a good endgame loop. World is great, music is great. Ai could get some work, and some more base story would be nice. It's good to know the devs care about the game. Good amount of planned content for the next 1-2 years.Buy the game. It's great. :)

_childDocuments_.review: I really REALLY wanted to enjoy this game, mostly because it was set in the Forgotten Realms, but also because of its price. I still haven't completed it but I don't think it's gonna work out for me. Forgotten Realms is a great D&D setting to base a video game on, so a lot could have been done with it. Even though I didn't expect something like BioWare's golden age entries, since this game obviously had a different vision and audience, it still could have been better. But apart from some fairly impressive cutscenes (and there's a bit too much of them) and map designs, and obviously Drizzt and his companions, the game has very little to offer in terms of lore, which is quite a bummer. Well made cutscenes contribute to the storytelling in a game, sure, but when it's too much... It's just too much. It gets so incredibly boring after a few fights. Because all you do is fight the same types of enemies, loot, fight more enemies and boom, cutscene. So naturally you lost the fun. Which is what disappointed me the most in terms of gameplay. Just how much it looks like a generic hack & slash game and feels like one too. And that's not even a pro by itself since the combat and the enemy types is almost completely repetitive. There are some small moments that the combat gets a bit creative, but, it's mostly a small detail so it doesn't make the entire game enjoyable. If you still want to play and just looking for a reaaaaaaally smooth sailing game that you can just play to spend time, you can give it a go. I'd say preferably, wait for a sale though.

_childDocuments_.review: I ended up loving this game! I started playing with a friend who later quit, but I continued on after they fixed a bunch of the bugs to max out Bruenor. The gameplay is challenging, takes skill to use the character's abilities properly. If you're into button mashing this probably isn't the game for you on higher challenge ratings. The entire game can be soloed if you want, but it is better playing with friends. I'm a fan of the books, so to play in a world with these characters is really fun. I'm working on leveling up other characters at this point.  Pros: Game looks amazing, character Banter and dialog are great. Cut sense are good and some are funny!Game play takes skill to get good at, its fun and not overly frustrating to get down. I do recommend a controller. Really fun with friends! Recommend playing this way if possible.Lots of things to loot and pick up in missions, some exploration of the maps, can skip parts to make it quicker in some missions too. Can mix and match pieces to make a build to your play style. I like the hack and slash change of pace! Cons: The AI is idle at times, they won't follow past their spawn areas either.Some of the boss and mob tactics are repeated a lot. The online match making doesn't seem to work, I never find random groups.At least in solo play, it was quite a bit of grind to get all legendary top tier gear that I wanted. Overall if you're a fan of the books and characters, its worth a play! Enjoy!

_childDocuments_.review: Overall its not the worst game i've ever played, but there is one MAJOR flaw. The game is set up like a mobile game. You go to a main area, select a quest, get loot, back to same area, repeat. You don't ever feel like you are really progressing, just going out to cut and loot. Even that isn't too enjoyable because the loot is set up like a mobile game where rather than putting in a vast array of different items they just put in 4 or 5 per character and said "good luck farming for the right one for the next five years". I know this is a lot for "one major flaw" but the flaw is that is a FTP mobile game on your pc for 40 dollars.

_childDocuments_.review: Controls are stiff and janky. You can't change direction while attacking, you can't cancel an attack into a dodge or block, so defensive reactionary play is non-existent. Combat is more fighting with the camera to line up attacks than actually doing cool things.Edit (Elaboration):You can't do anything once you commit to an attack, not even change directions. This is a third-person character action hack-and-slash. Having even a modicum of directional control during an attack string is standard design, yet this game lacks that. The camera is too slow, even at max sensitivity. Trying to aim a character's attacks is obnoxious due to the lack of ability to adjust direction after making an attack. The character will constantly try to attack in direct line with the camera facing, mostly regardless of what direction I'm pressing at the time of initiating an attack. Only once was I able to get the character to attack away from the camera, but I was not able to repeat it in combat. Combine a stiff inability to change your attack string's direction with an inability to cancel out of an attack in any way and you have a rigid, janky feeling combat flow. Further, the camera rides too close and zooms in off-center from your character when you lock-on, to the point of removing your ability to see anything the left or behind you. Lock-on is also mostly useless as it breaks when your character is barely a brisk walk away from the target. Even when lock-on stays it messes with your view and makes attacking or reacting to anything else a hassle.

_childDocuments_.review: I tried to give this game a fair chance but I'm ultimately let down by the vast potential this game had and what was delivered.Pros:- The game looks beautiful, the levels are some of the best looking I've seen especially on my potato of a computer.- combos are fun and feel good and can be chained from almost any of the other attacks you can do.Cons:(there are many)- The controls, the fact that you are always strafing and the combos while feel good whiff constantly because you attack the direction you camera is facing. there is no omnidirectional control over you attacks and that is essentially because many of them require directional inputs concurrently but that is no excuse because games like Devil may Cry and Bayonetta still have similar mechanics for combos while still allowing for you to change the direction of you attacks without moving you camera like your a tank that is trying to drive through molasses.- The enemy AI is one of the worst i have ever seen most of the time they stand there and do nothing giving the appearance of being not aggroed or bugged but they defiantly have seen you and are just too stupid to walk towards you and are waiting for you to enter their small area in with they are programmed to attack around them. when enemies do decide to attack you have a 50/50 chance that the hit will feel balanced or it will one or two shot you regardless weather you are on powerlevel or not.- The bugs in the game are very apparent the first boss i fought disappeared when i got it to 2/3rds of its health bar and completed the mission instantly, invisible traps(in my case a pile of skulls that were apparently on fire but didn't load the effect) and damage circles that don't appear are rampant. any sort of verticality destroys any immersion this game might have been able to provide as any ranged effects and aoe effects don't translate to vertical at all instead sticking to the same elevation throughout the effect( The barbarians shockwave attacks and the ranges rain of arrows ability are painfully obvious).- the balancing feels like a mix bag of you don't know when the game will ♥♥♥♥ you, the first two levels i played at power level and felt incredibly tanky but as soon as i started the third level at a higher power than was recommended i was bullied into a corner by the one enemy type that seemed to have a brain and knew to walk towards me and killed me in three hits. the enemies themselves also have the benefit of randomly having super armor during their attacks or just always have super armor like the second boss i fought that dissable the players ability to actually fight in melee due to many of the attacks either being instantaneous or not having tells beforehand to properly react to them while also puting forth a relentless assault of attacks that don't allow you to engage at all ( the second lightning troll boss was a bad offender of this) and while it seems some of the enemies have stamina that their attacks consume like the goblins in the first level some of the big enemies seem to have endless pools of stamina to draw from to just keep attacking like the trolls and the drauger enemies that i encountered in the third level.Conclusion:Don't eve try this game in its current state i followed all the devs videos of them inviting celebrities to demo the game and most of what was shown during those prerelease videos don't feel like they match up to the gameplay at launch and they are misleading.They are supposed to have several free content patches later as well and all i can hope is that they get their heads out of their asses and listen to the feedback that the community is giving them and fix the issues the game has but for now dont make the same mistake i have and play past the refund mark and just refund if you already have the game and if you are thinking about buying it save yourself the disappointment and don't.

_childDocuments_.review: Will we ever get a good D&D real time action game? This isn't an amazing game, but what's there works. It's not quite a hack & slash nor is it a mash button to win game, it's somewhere in between. It suffers from console syndrome, controls are weird and they don't often make sense, skills aren't set to your numbers/keys, but are instead a combination of move sets pressed together, which is really hard to hit at times, especially mid combat. There's 5 characters and they're all fairly different gameplay wise, so you've got some replayability if you end up liking them. I would prefer character creator, tho. Environments are amazingly well done, characters look good too, but mechanically it's janky. If you can grab it on sale, go for it, as a D&D fan you won't regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: To be brief:-  The game is poorly optimized for online multiplayer, with constant latency issues and enemies teleporting all around the field.- Balancing is all over the place, with massive spikes between difficulty settings and, even worse, huge variances in difficulty within a difficulty setting. on top of that, some of the bosses require hit-and-run tactics not out of a design standpoint, but because there are no tells for the attacks, which means you cannot commit to your combo or your burst or else you get one-shot by an untelegraphed AoE (unless you're Cali, then you can just spam arrows to win)- the worst part of it was the controls themselves. turning was sluggish, even at high sensitivity, and the lock-on targeting was unreliable, moving from the enemy i just killed to the explosive barrel behind me instead of the other enemy in front of me on multiple occasions. all together, an unpleasant experience from the approach of gameplay, the only redeeming factor being the level design and aesthetics and the characters themselves. a seemingly rushed project that plays like a very-early access indie game, as opposed to a full release of a mainstream title such as D&D.

_childDocuments_.review: So, I got this game as a gift. I only knew it was based on DnD has some kind of co-op brawling gameplay.I was genuinely excited, as I love the DnD setting.If you're looking for a DnD game, look elsewhere. Also look elsewhere if you want to play any kind of dungeon crawler.Seriously, I'm not the guy to jump on any kind of bandwagon, I really want this game to become good, eventually.You probably already read the other reviews, and to be honest, I can't anything new to the list of complaints. But I want to try to give you more of a "feel" for the shortcomings of this game.The most glaring issue: The game feels clunky/sluggish. I played as the archer class, and the only thing that really felt satisfying to do was her primary arrow shot, which isn't bound to M1, as you'd think - you have to hold CTRL, which puts you into an aiming mode. In this mode you're just plain slow. On top of that, the arrows don't do a whole lot of damage. Sure, you have a charged shot, but the charged shot takes a pretty long time to prime and is bugged. Sometimes when I shoot a charged shot and try to charge the next one I get locked into the charge animation and have to cancel the charge. You're able to do a fair bit of melee fighting, especially after you unlock some fighting skills (by the way, for all arrow-related combat techniques, you have to reach Lvl. 7 first, which is kinda dumb when playing an archer). The main problem with the melee fighting: It feels . The animations have an awfully long windup and cooldown animation. Most of the archers meele attacks consume a HUGE amount of stamina, and you're also loosing max stamina when depleting your current pool, which just ends in you waiting after performing a single combo. Enemies react with generic and equally slow recoil animations, making hits feel weak and disconnected. Also, you can't really "aim" your animations, so your character just pushes through the enemies, making the last hits of your combo miss.Speaking of enemies: In combat, enemies tend to warp after they finished their animations. It looks like they're lagging, which only adds to the sluggish and weird feel to the combat. Also, the animations sometimes don't really match up with the actions. In some cames, the enemy model was facing me and charging up a projectile attack, but the projectile flew backwards to the other player in my party. It's not really detrimental to the gameplay itself, it just looks bad and makes the game feel so unfinished and unpolished. Players and enemies snap into long winded animations all the time.All of this just makes the core loop of the game just not fun to play. Sure, other games in this genre are grindy and you have to put in a fair amount of time to unlock cool abilities, but those game have an engaging core loop. Dark Alliance feels like waddling trough mud.

_childDocuments_.review: Hello everyone,given the amount of negative reviews, I decided to give my opionion on the game aswell.I have watchted the SkillUp Review of this game before buying it and was therefor very sceptical in the beginning.To keep things short:I have the feeling that prelaunch-reviewers might have played on a different version? I have not encountered most of the glitches/bugs which are mentioned in those reviews. Things i can say is that the animations are definitly worthy of some polishing, but its not nearly as bad as portraied in reviews. Some of the bosses i have fought can be stunlocked into corners, which has to change. BUT the combat experience for me (playing as dwarf) is good. Combat is fluid, i can chain my combos and dodge without delay. Everything feels responsive and parrying works fine too. I have 0 problems with my stamina bar, maybe that is infact bugged with the ranger, cant tell for sure, given I havent played him yet.A really positive thing so far is the feeling of getting stronger and finding better loot. When u play well and dodge incoming attacks you can skip rests and therefor get better loot when continuing your run. I have found multiple epic items (purple) so far, which even added new animations to my attacks (Axe with Ice dmg adds frost effects to swing and even on the ground when i hit i). All higher rarity items seem to have set effects, which at first provide % boosts to different stats and when full in set provide changes to abilities or give strong passive buffs.I definitly recommend to play on the recommended difficulty until you have upgraded your weapon, else it will feel spungy. But if you play on the recommended diff you will have great time and can combo your enemies into oblivion.There seem to be a lot of unlockable skills which add more and more combo abilites (like lets say in a fighting game).Overall I had a suprisingly good experience with the game and hope that more people give it a try.

_childDocuments_.review: I pre-ordered the game a couple years back because I love D&D and read all the Drizzt novels, and also played pretty much all the D&D games (including the earlier Dark Alliance games). At first I wasn't bit with this game when it launched. Actually the thing I really hated was the controls. You just couldn't turn the camera fast enough whether with mouse/keyboard or a controller. My friends and I basically just stopped playing until things got better.So yesterday we decided to give it another go. Read more reviews and got sad that the game is apparently abandonware more or something? But anyway, the issue my group had was basically fixed. The camera moves as fast as we need it to move. After that, the game is pretty fun. Maybe not full price fun, but definitely "buy on sale" fun. I bought my game full price as a pre-order so I could let everyone know to wait for it to go on sale. ;)The controls work fine. The boss fights are a bit of a pain in the ass with the monsters taking forever to go down, and doing insane 1-shot damage, but then again my group is playing with the difficulty always 1 notch higher than recommended gear level suggests.The game looks good, the combat is alright, and the loot is also alright. The set bonuses seem a little random to me though.I would recommend this game to fans of D&D, or the Drizzt series of books just to be able to play with The Companions (except for Regis). As for people that aren't mentioned...ehh, it's okay. If you have friends who are into D&D and have the game and want to play this with you, then I would get it, since it does have it's moments. _childDocuments_.review: So this game is sort of a mixed bag, On the one hand it's looks and feels like you expect Icewind Dale to be. The characters have a lot of moves and you can free form them together into combos. I did notice looking at the skills I can buy with the different characters, that the videos of celebs and such playing the game, were given all the skills. This is why I think the combat feels clunkier than what we see in the videos. They were fully unlocked.Even with only the base skills though, and spending time with the various characters practising on the combat dummies, there is a ton of moves you can do. From short combos, to very long combos, to mixing various hard attacks that will knock down enemies or knock them away, giving you some breathing room.I don't know why everyone thinks every game should allow you to animation cancel, this game forces you to think when you attack. You can't just swing away like a madman, and then vault away at a moments notice. You have to plan your attacks, make sure you don't start a big move, while a Verbeeg is trying to slam the ground. The characters are also all designed to play off of each other. Meaning you can have Bruenor up front, parry an enemy, which then allows Drizzt to come in and backstab them, which then allows Wulfgar or Catti-Brie to use their team attack to do big dmg. Obviously if you are soloing, that's not an option.The other thing I noticed people complaining about was enemies stopping their attacks, well they have shields, and they are blocking. Just like you can block the enemies attacks, to avoid dmg. Most characters have some way to deal with the blocking enemies, for example with Drizzt jump at them, and attack from midair. His dual ground stab, will knock down an enemy not blocking, or stun and break through the shield enemies. Leaving them open to a back stab.As far as controls, I found a setup that works very well for me on keyboard and mouse, I rarely feel the need to lock on to enemies in these kinds of games, so I really don't use that feature, except when the tutorial made me. =)I use space for blocking, e for jumping, r and g for the specials, 1-4 is potions, 5 is ultimate, (because it doesn't fill fast enough you'll be hitting it all the time) I use mouse wheel button for dodging, q for aim. I use F for interact and shift for sprint. I never ran into any issues using my attacks, and found it very responsive. This may be because I have played games with similar locked animation attacks, such as Neverwinter mmo.I have not encountered any bugs or slowdown or anything like that, so for me this has been a fun game to play.I still recommend trying it out, the majority of the complaints on here is the AI which is being patched, and the lack of animation canceling, everybody wants to have no risk for their combat, dodge out at anytime. The combat takes time to learn, to get used to when to attack, or when to block, or dodge. A note about the AI, when I played enemies didn't stand there, they came to me if I damaged them at all.There is definately more they could do with the feats and skins function, I am hoping they will eventually expand on it.

_childDocuments_.review: The game has decent bones, but sadly is suffering from a few glaring issues.The biggest IMHO is that the game has very low replay-ability.  It is definitely fun, but it's so repetitive that the fun doesn't last long.  There are basically only three monster types to fight in the game, which gets old.  And the dungeons are basically all the same, so it gets pretty dull pretty quickly.  With the whole dwarven fortress / undermountain type of setting they really had a ton of material to draw on it's disappointing that the dungeons are so lackluster.The second big issue is that since the game is very much designed for group play and not solo play, the player matching is really awful.  Unlike some games where you can see what games are available to join and what quests / dungeons those people are doing, you join blind.  You have no idea what dungeon / quest you are about to join and no way to control it.  You also have no way to control what level ranges or difficulty ranges you will be joining.  I've joined into several games where the party leader was 15 levels above me and playing on very hard difficulties and I was being one shot-ed by everything and barely doing any damage.  And that's when I was even matched at all.  Which either means the matching is horribly broken or there's not many people playing.
