_childDocuments_.review: My time played is not accurate - Steam tracked an initial session as being a minute long.The Invisible Hand is fine. Admittedly, I've yet to find a trading game I thought was super-interesting but it's largely the same issue with all of them - information is presented to you in ways which makes it fairly easy to deal with once you find that information. The Invisible Hand has the potential to do this if you ignore the core 'tips' mechanic of the game by outlining the core inputs and outputs of each stock in which you can trade, but those tips are so important to a good strategy to win that, given they exist and are as frequent as they are, they should be presented to players prominently (and are).You also sometimes run into an issue where the game can't decide whether it wants to be a satire of capitalism or a well-executed trading game. The narrative is too basic for the former, but certain mechanics (lobbyists spring to mind have little place in the latter.Do I regret playing it? No. Do I regret paying for it? Yes, absolutely.4/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Invisible Hand

_childDocuments_.review: I came into this thinking the game was going to be about how the stock market is hard to manage, so you resort to illegal endeavors to gain an edge. While that's certainly what the story is about, the gameplay doesn't really back it up. Once you understand the connections between all the parts, it's relatively easy to predict the market even without the illegal tools given to you. It makes the illegal endeavors your character is forced to do feel somewhat pointless as you could do just as well legally. The story is funny though in a sardonic sort of way. It makes for a fun experience but lacks in replay value. I'd recommend giving it a try, but it certainly won't be your new obsession.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invisible Hand

_childDocuments_.review: Let's state this up front, The Invisible Hand has spot on pacing and humor. I finished a play through in roughly four and a half hours, and that length gave the satirical narrative a fast and punchy feel that was supported by a game play loop I found surprisingly stressful.  That loop makes the game deserve an RPG tag because I felt like the stock analyst main character: under immense arbitrarily cruel pressure, coffee addled, entirely out of my depth, but with enough introspection to know I absolutely should not have been given the phone numbers of all those lobbyists. By 5 o'clock many peoples lives have been ruined, but I was also broke since I had accidentally hit the short sale button...again. It was actually stressful, so this might not be the for you if you want an immediately laid back stock trading fantasy.The Invisible Hand left me with an itch to play a bit more, so I will probably enjoy more hours of stock trading entertainment by continuing on to it's endless mode. That said, I can see how the game play loop will eventually wear out it's welcome in the not too distant future, so I am glad the story did not outstay it's novelty. Just to reiterate one point, the game landed it's jokes. Kudos to the writers of these insufferable characters.Disclaimer: I received this game as a bit of a surprise through Humble Bundle, so the price of the game was largely absent from my thoughts as I wrote this review.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invisible Hand

_childDocuments_.review: A fun "little game" featuring exactly what you can expect from a stock trading sim.Little as in there isn't much things to do appart from exponentially growing, which isn't a bad thing if you're into that kind of never ending grind/Clicker experience.It does feature a short but fairly alright story, and is packed with humor everywhere.The size of the story isn't a problem since the real game starts after the end of the main story, revealing the sucession mechanics and such.Trading is fairly easy but hectic and fun in this game, which is obviously a great thing.All in all, if you're looking for a "clicker" game that requires you to actually play the game instead of looking at numbers growing, and that you enjoy stock market related shenanigans, you will definitely enjoy this game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invisible Hand

_childDocuments_.review: Very clean game with lots packed into it. Market Simulator with a mini story line and creative game play. Anybody with a liking for simulation/money making games you'll probably play though this more than once. There's a few things that I would like to added though to really smooth out the game:-Let me delete objects off my desk, Frame rates drop once I own 20+ mansions-More to spend personal money on-Game tends to crash If you try to leave the game/return to menu-More variety of Daily Missions-Too easy to overtake the entire market, manipulate Dividends/stock prices in post game. I was making 23 trillion in dividends with a 20 million dollar investment.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invisible Hand

_childDocuments_.review: A good, short, funny story driven game. Is it realistic? No. does it need to be? Hell no! It gets the central point across and made me laugh. To the institutional finance reviewer, that's not what this ever set out to be. And if it was, we'd both probably hate it on account of being more work, after real work. Not that the mechanics are good, but they don't detract from the (at least story) experience either. They break down into endless mode. I give it a 6/10. And for the love of god, if you beat the game, even if it took you 90 minutes, please don't refund it. If you beat the game you enjoyed it enough that the developers deserve to eat and makes shorter games like this worth developing.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invisible Hand

_childDocuments_.review: Great little game about handling stocks with some humorous commentary every now and then. The campaign obviously didn't take itself too seriously and the game struck a good balance of balancing it's simulated stock gameplay with the humor and didn't go on for too long.The last half of the game devolved a bit into a numbers go brrr situation but it was pleasing to the eyes for the last bit. Definitely enjoyed my time with this game and props to the developers for continuing to release content for this game. Will definitely keep my eyes peeled on future titles.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invisible Hand

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine Tyler Durden created a game about the stock market.Not the way the stock market actually works or real issues - you won't find anything like "Liar's Poker" or "The Wolf of Wall Street" here.Instead you get a game that beats you over the head that the only ways to win are either to cheat the system or not play at all. Insider trading, magically teleport lobbyists, and more. By the end you'll have less idea of how the stock markets (and the game's mechanics) work than when you started.Mostly, this makes me wish it was a good, realistic, interesting game about being a day trader, or a stock broker, or even a member of the US Congress (who are legally permitted to engage in insider trading.)But, for all its faults, it was reasonably enjoyable to play, and I'll probably play it more in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invisible Hand

_childDocuments_.review: I used to be a trader for an equities firm. Its legal gambling. This is funny stuff. Worth it for me definitely. Worth the full price I would think so after playing 30 mins of my probation status. Might replay the first few stages as I wasnt so familiar with the UI. I guess the negative reviews hope that this was a full blown technical/fundamental hands on stock trading simulation which is not. Its a choose your own destiny Visual Novel. Kudos to the devs. They put alot of linggo and protocols that make it more realistic to the player. Which is all BS considering your headed to make alot of cash and be given alot of incentives for working for Ferios....hehe
_childDocuments_.name: The Invisible Hand

_childDocuments_.review: Great game! Lots of potential. But there is just not enough to do to make it worth the money. In less then 10 hours of gameplay I played through the story twice and got all the achievements. The trading is not that hard to master (it is easy to make a 50% return on investment in a day if you had a good one), so a more difficult mode would be very welcome to me. Also the ability to have trading tools, candlestick patterns etc would be good features to build on this game and give it more depth and a serious learning curve.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invisible Hand

_childDocuments_.review: Short, but a great game. Fun and funny storyline, good gameplay loop, I'm very glad I found this. I do hope they make a second version, a few more gameplay mechanics and a bias more towards a longer term play would be nice. But ultimately what the game does offer it does incredibly well and makes for an expensive, but exceptionally good, short little indie game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invisible Hand

_childDocuments_.review: Very funny (and eerily relevant) social commentary on capitalism and the stock market. Funny writing that adds to the social commentary aspect with core gameplay mechanics that are both engaging and addictive with new challenges and twists just when you start to get a feel for the game. Would recommend as a pick up (especially on sale), feels like it has *some* replayability but I wouldn't expect to get more than one play through unless you really enjoy the mechanics of messing with stocks and destabilizing developing countries.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invisible Hand

_childDocuments_.review: This game is brutal, but in a good way. It is insightful on being a broker or analyst , and the whole ethics behind that industry and it's impact on the world. The game itself executes the concept in a way that can rope you in, carefully reading between the lines or manipulating declines in certain goods so that you can make profit. If not, you're fired.Overall, good execution, good at roping you into the game, informative, and with some colorful language by the NPC giving it a touch of spice as you play.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invisible Hand

_childDocuments_.review: All I can say is that this game will not surprise you, if you think it'll be fun once you play it will be fun, if you think it'll be bad when you play you will find it bad, the mechanics and gameplay loop are not for everyone, but it is for me and I enjoyed it very much. I loved the concept of the game and it accomplishes everything it set out to be, which isn't that much but it's enough, I would love a more ambitious sequel though.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invisible Hand

_childDocuments_.review: I'm actually really upset here because the game itself isn't bad. It's okay (I wouldn't say great - the story could use a little work but shows a lot of promise!)But what annoys me is towards the end of the campaign where  I did this MULTIPLE times and the target just kept increasing by 5 million every time?It was that one piece of game design that really upset me. The only bad point i have is the clothings of the colleagues, they doesnt look like traders at all , and some of them wears aviators ray bans... Were are the suits ? the watches ?. name: Hellpoint
detailed_description: Featured DLC About the Game Hellpoint is a dark sci fi RPG that takes place on a derelict space colony in the aftermath of a massive quantic cataclysm. You play a Spawn of the Authority brought to this world to investigate the circumstances of this event and unravel this deep interstellar intrigue. You will explore the open world of the Irid Novo colony, orbiting in real time around an enigmatic black hole which triggers all sorts of dynamic events to keep you on your toes. Build your warrior according to your play style, and venture alone, with or against friends in online or split screen multiplayer. Once a pinnacle of human achievement, the Irid Novo space station has fallen. Its ruins are now overrun by cruel interdimensional entities acting as puppets of the malevolent Cosmic Gods. You have been created by the Author, organically printed on Irid Novo and sent on a mission to find out the unholy series of events that led to the catastrophic incident known as the Merge. Irid Novo is a massive interconnected world full of mysteries, hidden passages and secrets within secrets - all for you to explore in any order you like. More dread and shivers awaits you as you travel deeper into the darkest corner of this forsaken colony. Dozens of melee and ranged weapons and armor pieces to suit your playstyle. Every weapon has unique special abilities that unlock the more you fight with them. A fascinating new sci fi universe reminiscent of classic sci-fi movies, set in the aftermath of a massive quantum cataclysm and complete with a deep lore and goosebump inducing soundtrack. The space station orbits in real time around an ominous black hole that triggers various dynamic events such as boss appearances, horde assaults as well as modified enemy stats and positions. If you are struggling, ask a friend to press Start to join in a couch coop session, or call for assistance online. The entire game can be completed uninterrupted in coop. The loot is shared, and the experience of local player two is saved and not watered down.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all it supports 21:9!  That out of the way I gotta say the game is a ton o fun once you get some decent gear.  (sort of like most games I guess) I found a good grind spot and 9 hours in I'm level 65.  The game doesn't hide the obvious influence of DS, but I don't think it should.  I see it like a fan of DS made a game and added things that they liked to it.  There is the obvious allusion to Miyazaki's obsession with black holes, and the visual element of eclipses, accretion disks, fiery rings you get the picture.  I'm obsessed with that iconography too haha.  I have been enjoying the levels and the aesthetic.  The weapons feel as one would expect so far with me mainly having melee weapons. I guess I should progress a bit.   The fighting mechanics are pretty good with a few bugs that I think just got patched out.  I am leveling in anticipation of co-op working so I can play this with friends.    I dunno if everyone will enjoy it, but if you're looking to scratch that itch for a game that teaches you to get better, experiment, and explore i think you should give this game a try.Oh and can JUMP!  Plus riding zoomy ladders is dope.UPDATE AFTER 47 HOURS IN:  This game has so many secrets and hidden places!  Also the weapon mechanics are super neat.  It took me awhile to get it all but there are two different weapon mechanics for each weapon.  The catalysts you level up separately but install in weapons, but they can be swapped into different weapons and maintain the catalyst level.  It's cool because you can use a catalyst to improve weapon speed on a heavy weapon and increase stagger on a light fast weapon.  Or just buff the existing stats of a weapon's strength.  The weapons themselves unlock new movesets the more you use them up intil the gauge is full.  Most people probably got this pretty quick but it took me awhile to get it as I didn't want to risk any spoilers that may have accompanied tutorials.  I am still having a blast at 47 hours in I'm level 120 ish and looking forward to co-op to share all the cool stuff I found with friends.  I really think folks should ignore negative reviews and just try for themselves if they like difficult but rewarding third person action games with tons of hidden locations, items, weapons, armors, and things to find.

_childDocuments_.review: This one really took me by surprise in a very possitive way. I had heard that this souls-like game was buggy and glitchy as hell, and impossible to play without controller.. Nothing could be more wrong! first of all i want to adress the many reviews saying "jumping in this game is awfull, and almost impossible" Well i can honestly say that its no harder than timing your jump in the darksouls series, and way easier than in DS2 -to give an example. Also K +M works perfectly fine with this game, and you def dont need a controller to play it, but I have to mention that theres one achievement you can not get without a controller connected, but im thinking this can be fixed in the future, specially because the devs are still fixing small issues, and are very present in the steam forum. they listen to their players and always reply, which is a great +. Bug & glitches wise, I havent experienced anything out of the ordinary, and im in ng+3 now. a few glitches yes but you find that in all games. SO whith that being said let me talk about the game itself. This is definitly among the best souls-like games ive played, and i have tried quite a few. The exploration feeling of this game is through the roof! Its all the way up there with the dark souls series, and it reminds alot of ds1 in the way its build, the way you need to constantly back-track & tons of "this door opens from the other side", bonfire mecanism, yellow fog gates that you cant enter in the start game, npc side quests and so on.. so if you like the exploration part of the dark souls series, looking for shiny's, finding new paths and so on, this game will def please you. Its packed with secret walls, hidden items and secrets in general. The bosses however are pretty easy, you might have some challenges with one or two of them, but in general the bosses are the least of your worries. Its more about placement of enemies on the way to the boss, and about gravity messing with you. You'll find yourself falling over edges, or down in a hole, you'll get lost and stuck for a while but its all your own fault and you know it :)  Stay focused or you will die again and again from gravity and stupid mistakes. whats not to like right! Also many of the mechanics in the game are really brilliant, and I would go as far as saying that this game has some features and mechanics that ive missed in all other souls-like games. Such as the concept of "time" being intergrated into the game. Without spoiling to much let me explain real fast: you have a clock in the left corner of your screen and as time pass while you play there will be moments where you enter "horde hour" and "black (hole) storms" where you can collect special items, get access to otherwise closed areas, and even unlock stuff by doing certain things on the right location at the right time. Also several of the location gives you the possibility to enter "the underworld" where the area you are in gets mirrored, and new pick up items will appear + enemies will change & extra optional bosses and sidequests will be available!  going into ng+ is just as rewarding, new bosses, new paths, new items, new endings. And yes theres tons of dark souls references (and other reference for that matter) but I def dont see this as a dark souls ripp off, but more like a tribute to dark souls, by some Devs who loved the ds series themselves.If i shold compare this with other games i'd say this is dark souls meeting remnant from the ashes, but ofcaurse with a smaller budget. You can complete the game/your first run in like 25-30 hours, but if you wanna get all items , bosses, weapons, achievements etc. theres atleats a good 60 hours gameplay (and you do because the game constantly keeps you interested through those 60 hours!) On top of that there is co-op , grinding, pvp, arena battles etc ..The visuals works, is not astonishing or breathtaking, its simple in design, and reminds more of remnant from the ashes than dark souls, but it works. it gives you the feeling of being on a cold and dead spacestation, circling around a black hole in cold empty space.I really loved this journey! 8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: At the time of this review I'm maybe a third of the way into the game, enough to have an adequate impression of the game's performance. I mostly agree with a majority of the existing reviews, that it should be bought at deep discount. It's a decent game if you are itching to have a little guy to run around through a convoluted and interconnected set of secretive mazes, finding loot, leveling him up and dressing him in the latest fashions. It does fine at that.There are a few neat systems to play with. Upgrading weapons works a little differently in this game, where you slot interchangeable modules into weapons and thus are free to swap them around and experiment without a permanent commitment of the upgrade to a single item. You upgrade the slotted material, not the weapon, and you can simply transfer that upgrade to the weapon of your choice at a weapons bench (although these are rare locations, there's one in the main hub area).There is also a sort of day cycle where the black hole which the space station is orbiting changes position as the station rotates, causing more powerful monsters to spawn in when it is facing your location. A few special vaults scattered around the levels only open during this period as well. Additionally there are "accretion storms" which trigger other challenges when active. This is actually a pretty cool feature of the game, which keeps encounters interesting when revisiting familiar areas.The mag-ladders are also cool and zippy. There are also sections outside the station where your survival greatly benefits from wearing an EVA suit, although gravity is still normal somehow.The UI could be a little better, as you need to review multiple panels to really get a complete read on your weapon damage and the effects of certain items. In particular, a valuable tip to remember is that modules (read: rings or amulets) which increase a base stat such as Health or Strength actually temporarily boost your level in that stat, which increases your overall character level, and therefore the cost of leveling up. Remove these items before leveling up to avoid "overpaying" for additional stats. It's very easy to overlook and waste axions (souls) on, if you are not aware of this.The game feel and presentation is a bit rough around the edges, and while the combat does have the basics of Dark Souls melee, it lacks the versatility of its well-rounded move-sets and attack animations. For instance plunge attacks and backstabs do exist but do not reward you with a satisfying kill animation, it's just another type of hit you can land. That's okay though.Platforming is a nail-biting proposition in this game, and you even have a dedicated jump button and the tiniest amount of mid-air control, but the movement controls are a bit more fiddly, and you will die more than once from over- or undershooting a jump that you feel like you should have been able to make. Sometimes sprint does not engage promptly, or you may get snagged while jumping too near to a corner. Add to this, that these jumping sections can often be very far from a respawn point, placing successful retrieval of your "souls" at greater risk if you die.The camera is also wonky at times and will clip your view in tight spaces, sometimes due to the lock-on marker.The level design to me is the least appealing aspect of the game, as others have mentioned everything feels pretty samey, without much in the way of actual set pieces or landmarks, mostly some bigger rooms connected by a bunch of twisty passages or bridges, mostly diagonal or straight angles so the actual modeling work for the environments feels a bit uninspired and elementary. Graphically it feels more dated than even Darks Souls or the original Dead Space, and the layouts feel more like the arbitrary chaos of a Doom or Quake map, but huge. There's not much of a sense of place early on, although there are still some "a-ha" moments when you open a shortcut and realize where you are. The locations do become more interesting and detailed later in the game as it turns out, nothing I would call spectacular, but serviceable.Then there's the lighting. Many rooms and corridors are just murky brownish barely-lit metallic boxes. Though you can find light sources to equip later on, your first impression might be that they just wanted to hide as many of the bland textures as possible.As of yet I have not tried any of the multiplayer features, but it seems like co-op would be fun. I'm not convinced that the combat system is versatile enough to make for deep interesting PvP, but summons and arenas are there to bop other players with your stick of choice; if that's your cup of tea, might be worth trying out. The player hint system works similar to Dark Souls, providing helpful hints and trolling taunts.In summary, Hellpoint does have its charm, but it takes a while to really feel it. It does not put its best foot forward and initially may be off-putting. Proof of this is that in the Steam achievement statistics, less than half of all players even bother to beat the first boss, the very first achievement, and he's not hard. Many of the games systems are opaque as to how they function, and the early experience is riddled with confusion. I mean that's very Dark Souls in itself, maybe what is lacking at the beginning is just that critical first impression that draws you in. But if you stick with it past the first couple levels it begins to click, and if you can see past the shortcomings, there is fun to be had.

_childDocuments_.review: Really underrated game. I have played every soul-like titles and this one maybe not be the best, but definitely above average. It amazes me this Cradle Game's first soul clone title. I see alot of potential from those dev.Pro:Game is pack with secrets and shortcut, actually more so than other soul titles I have played.Interesting game mechanical such as underworld, black hole hour, storm etc.Air movement, there are alot of jumpping puzzle in this game and air physic is very well done, you can fine tune while in air. In general physic is good in this game.Weapons design are interesting, you can leveling up weapon to earn perks.Story and sound effect are good.Price, $39.99 not abusing full price like those AAA company.Coop, how many soul games allow you to coop full campaign?Con:Combat is toward the easy side. Mainly because almost every weapon you can perm-stun non-boss monsters.Character build: in this game stacking stats point has huge diminish return. So most peoeple just evenly distribute their stats. The benefit is that you can use all weapon and armor equally and try them all out. But at the same time you are jack-of-trades, master of none. I wish this game follow more traditional soul style game that STR and DEX build are more distinguished from each other. Also add respec option so players can experiment on builds. Overall this is a great game. In my 45+ hours play time I haven't encounter any crash issue. The graph is mediocre but the immensive si-fi theme kinda hides it away.

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay-wise, it's great. Relatively forgiving for a "Souls-like", with the option to increase difficulty at any time. The layout design is phenomenal. Environments are interesting and different enough where you won't get lost... and there are enough secret pathways to make backtracking much less cumbersome and boring. I really only have 2 complaints, and they are *very* minor ones. 1) There is a certain... lack... of variety when it comes to creature design. This becomes even more apparent when you run into your first boss... who then re-appears as a regular (A.K.A less threatening) enemy later in the game. 2) The story was a bit lacking as well. I get that a lot of it was meant for the player to figure out... but it all felt a little too disjointed. I don't know, it's a little hard to explain. With something like Dark Souls, you felt like you were dropped into this new world. It felt mysterious and wondrous. But the world of Hellpoint is... nothing but a puzzle. A problem that needs to be solved. It doesn't feel lived-in, if that makes sense. Still, I've had a great time with it so far!

_childDocuments_.review: While Hellpoint is not perfect by any means it puts a neat sci-fi spin on the souls like genre. In the end it definetly could have used a bit more polish and wider enemy variety but personally i am looking forward to a Hellpoint 2 someday.

_childDocuments_.review: Glome here--This is my new favorite indie Soulslike. It channels the spirit of Dark Souls particularly well; the real meat of Hellpoint is in the atmosphere and exploration. The combat is solid and fun as well -- I especially enjoyed the weapon familiarity system which definitely added a lot of depth to the combat in the later game. Ultimately, it's the presentation of the game that really hooked me. Irid Novo is a bleak and beautiful place, and a totally original one as well. You can get lost very easily in the labyrinthine levels but I loved this. This game is a dream come true for completionists and secret hunters. There is so much to see and do that it's overwhelming at times. The plot, while derivative in places, is nonetheless swathed in mystery and thus remains compelling. HIGHLY recommended for any and all Souls fans. 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: I played a lot more offline, real playtime is probably 30-35 hours or so.An excellent souls-like game that has a fun lovecraftian sci-fi take on the formula.  The major positives in this compared to other souls games are: - You level up things you attach to weapons, not weapons, so it's a lot easier to experiment with new gear.  However weapons can learn some new abilities via use, so there's still a reason to stick with a weapon for a bit.  A new weapon will need some time killing stuff with it before you can do all the fancy tricks with it, but if you swap your old conductor onto it will have about the same raw power.- The world is extremely dense and filled with stuff to explore and find.  Important items are often in two places in the game so that people who take varied routes through the game can still find stuff.  Less of a 'well this would have been nice but I found it 95% through the game' problem.- The game is much more managable with difficulty based on how much you want to level up / improve stuff.  People who want hard difficulty can avoid leveling or use provided items to raise the entire world's difficulty level, but people who like the concept of souls games but might find them too tough can also find a home here, it's a lot easier to grow your power.- The healing / magic system is also much better than raw souls, in that melee hits recharge your healing flask and your MP, so there's no pure caster style builds, but you can pick melee weapons based on how much 'drain' power they have over pure damage as well.A neutral is that you can jump.  I like jumping, but it didn't add anything to the combat for me.  I didn't have problems with the platforming but some people might?The downsides for me is that while magic is fun, certain spells are just absurdly overpowered on bosses.  It could use a bit of a balance pass.  The overall difficulty of the game I thought was well done, but wall of fire/light or the cluster projectiles need to be made so they can't obliterate large enemies with no effort.  Aside from early game bosses, I found the zones far harder than bosses simply because I couldn't just spam magic forever and needed to engage more with the mana drain mechanics.On the whole I'd definitely look forward to future content / dlc for this game or the next outing from these developers.

_childDocuments_.review: Hellpoint------------------------A lower budget souls like with a lot of charm and a few mistakes.The world design is not the best but it has a dark mood.Enemies look nice and the combat, altough not the best, still feels great.The game has a few bugs, but nothing to be worried about.The lore is really well done and deserves some praise !There are tons of weapon and armors to collect (but they are hard to find !)The crafting system can get irritating at times and the levels (tough well connected) can start to feel tedious.The fast travel system is my biggest issue, it uses a material to be able to synchronise a breach point.Sadly these don't come that often, so you will have to walk around a lot.The game is fun and has a charm to it. A pretty good souls-like. Give these guys a bigger budget and i know they can pull something off.Enjoy the game !!!

_childDocuments_.review: Decent indie souls-like game but there's so many things wrong with this game's system that could've been easily avoided🟢 Similar to Dark Souls🟢 Exploration is rewarding, lots of secret paths to find🟢 Heavy, fast or ranged build🔴 Lightning system is utterly horrible in this game. It's so dark that you'll have to max gamma and light setting in order to see anything in front of you🔴 Fast travel requires a special item to activate and not only it's hard to find but also very limited in quantities. With so many fast travel points, you can only activate a few. Why the heck can't fast travel be free? This forces you to needlessly walk back and forth so much🔴 Resetting stats is extremely grindy and expensive. Game forces you to make a melee build at the start due to strong melee weapon early on and it gets hard to switch build as you've already invested in a melee stat🔴 Status effect does not go away at resting points, only way I found to cure them is to either fast travel to another location or quit the game to menu and loading again🔴 Polarize can entirely ruin the game. It makes the game harder, enemies and bosses have massive health and damage. You do get more souls and level up very quickly. When you recess, the game becomes way too easy as you've leveled up too much. The balance gets lost. Polarize only makes sense at NG+ but manually being able to change too easily was a really bad idea🔴 Fall damage is stupid. You can jump two flights of stairs without dying but when you jump from 1 floor, you instantly die even if you have full health. Heck, when a elevator is going down and you jump up, you'll also instantly die. It's just ridiculous 🔴 Number of health potion does not refill to max at resting point/dying and can only be refilled to max at specific heal station. Mindbogglingly terrible design. You've to repeatedly travel back to base to refill it every time you die and it's a nightmare to do it before every boss battles or else you're just handicapping yourself for no reason🔴 Whenever you die, a doppelganger with the same equipment as yours spawns and it becomes annoying to deal with it repeatedly🔴 Printing is way too expensive. Why do we even need to craft weapons to get them which aren't even that good🔴 Performance can be very inconsistent with stutters and FPS drops🔴 No cloud save

_childDocuments_.review: This game has one of the coolest premise and setting in the Souls game genre. You spawn in on a colonial space station orbiting a black hole after a cataclysmic event resulted in a parallel universe colliding with our own. This event obliterated everyone on board both physically and mentally, turning them into deranged feral mutilated souls, and if that wasn't enough such an event attracted the attention of Cosmic Gods. You wake up in a vat and are basically told you are a human clone and some messed up things happened here and are then given liberty to figure out the details on how and why this all happened.The one thing this game does a really good job at is intriguing the player on exploring and discovering what happened on Irid Novo. Just like any souls game the story is not fed to you. Typically when I play DS I'm mostly focused on just beating bosses and clearing areas. I know theres a way more intricate story than the face value of your 1st playthrough but I never felt compelled to "understand" the lore as much as simply beating the game. Hellpoint actually makes this a part of the game by incorporating the lore into "data." You want to collect as much "data" to  understand what happened and you will miss A LOT if you do not look for secret rooms and passages. This game takes illusory walls to a new level. Sometimes there are secret rooms within secret rooms so the game encourages observation. All the information you can find is considered data that is broken down in bits of percentages. You obviously want to acquire %100 but there is more than that, I'm not sure how high you can get so don't think you found everything if you made it that far.The gameplay in general is great. Fighting feels like a mix of both Dark Souls and Bloodbourne. Is it hard? Yeah. Is it Dark Souls hard? Hmm I dont think so, but I don't see that as a detriment to the game. Interesting thing is the difficulty can be changed but not through the menu but rather through "effigies" you find in the game which are rare to find. One of the coolest things about this game is its co-op. You can play an entire game with a friend if you chose to do so from literally start to finish or anywhere in between either online or split screen which is really cool. Overall for its price I think it's well worth it for those who love this kind of genre of games, and its not that bad for someone who isn't sure, especially if they can get someone to play with them either online or split screen. It doesn't have great graphics like compared to DS3 from 2016 but they aren't bad. You'll still end up at some point just fixated at gazing into the black hole when you can. To me this feels like the movies "Event Horizon" and "Hellraiser" were made together into a souls game which is something I never asked for but I'm super glad I stumbled across.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish steam's review system was more nuanced than a Yes or No rating but I am slightly more in the Yes camp with thisHellpoint by all means is a very cheap and rough around the edges dark action rpg set on a doomed space station orbiting a black hole, you are supposed to gather all the information about what has happened here.Whilst the combat and environments and gameplay is rough the mechanics and unique ideas are utterly so, there is a clock that tells the time, whenever you enter certain parts of the clock the world changes whether thats when you're entering the hell dimension or you're as close to the black hole as possible, it alters spawn locations and enemy moves as they veer closer to insanity.The general enemies themselves are whatever to fight but the bosses have cool moves and cool designs, the moves don't vary much but I adore the designs a lot.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, so here we go. Hellpoint.... Do you like Dark Souls? Do you like The Surge? Do you like Sekiro? Do you like Bloodborne? Do you like Remnants from the Ashes? Do you like Any Soulslike? You'll probably then like this game....Probably. I say this not to be condescending, but to give you more of an understanding of how this game will play for you. It's got a hell of a good feel to it with a great sense of progression (once you understand it), a great aesthetic, if you pay attention, a great lore, and overall just a great game. Though with my optimistic tone, and high regard for this game I also must be frank. It is wonky as all hell, with some serious bugs in multiplayer, and an even more serious issue in level design and exploration. Lets get into it.Pro's- Combat - The combat for this game is similar to Dark souls, with a bit of extra speed, so maybe even say Elden Ring, or Bloodborne. You roll when not targeting enemies, and quickstep when you do target em, so I guess more like Bloodborne. All fights are mostly fast pace, with your toon getting incredibly overpowered towards end game if you really explore all the nooks and crannies, so fights become whatever. Personally I love it, because it shows me that not only am I actually progressing in the game, but progressing my toon towards godhood. - Aesthetic - This game is sci-fi as hell. Seemingly taking much inspiration from Dead Space, and Event Horizen. The look of the weapons, armor, enemies, and some zones (Especially the DLC) are incredibly original for the most part, so nothing ever looks same....however on the contrary.....- Weapons/Armor - The base game came with a decent amount of weapons and armor, not alot, but a decent amount either way, however with the DLC (once again) about 9 sets, and 14 weapons were added to the game with interesting ways of obtaining them further creating a better fashion souls, and ways for combat. - Multiplayer - I played the entire game with a friend, and co-op was implemented amazingly. Summon your friend and they stay in your game the entire playthrough getting loot, leveling up, and also creating their own personalized character. The only loot that your coop buddy cant obtain are the boss artifacts, but there are so few that it doesn't hinder the game whatsoever.-Exploration - This game has secrets upon secrets, upon secrets. There are so many ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ secrets in this game it could be called Hellpoint: Bet you Didn't find this. Luckily there are messages players can leave behind revealing these secrets, so it's not too overwhelming or anxiety inducing thinking you'll miss something.....but you probably will. - Leveling - this game has the easiest leveling system i've ever seen. Its just like any souls game where you have multiple stats, and based on those stats you can equip certain types of gear, as well as focus on a certain build. However weapons dont get upgraded, but an interchangable component can, so say you're using a hammer, you find an amazing sword you want to use. Simply exchange the component onto said swords from your hammer, and it will be current towards your players level. So trying out new weapons is definitely not a hassle or detrimental towards your playthrough.- Weapon skills - Most weapons come with unique skills that can be obtained through just using them. Using a weapon unlocks specific passive abilities, as well as usable abilities that can change how you play entirely.- Music - The music in this game is great. From what it seems, most souls like have incredibly music tracks. This souls like is definitely one of them, especially with those little juke boxes. Con's- Level Design - So as I said previously this game has a really unique look to it, however unfortunately about half of the base game looks sooooo identical that it gets mindnumbingly easy to get lost. Also it gives  sort of cheap feel to the game. I don't blame the devs due to their probably low budget for the game, however copying and pasting square looking designs is not the way to make your game vast. - Sound Design - The game uses alot of stock sounds that get very tiresome to constantly listen to. A small change for how weapons sound when hitting enemies would be very appreciated. Some sounds just well sound absolutely abysmal, and ugly. - Enemies - even though the enemies all look great with incredible imagination needed to create, the base game has veerryy few unique designs, so you'll be fighting alot of the same things. - Exploration - Even though the exploration is great, its only great when you know where you're going. Unfortunately since the level design is so same-y looking exploring can easily get you lost, and overwhelmed.- Multiplayer bugs - So even though multiplayer is very easy to do, right now the game has maaaaannyy bugs, and I wouldn't mind it if some werent soft-locking your playthrough which can only be resolved by killing yourself ( Friend locked me out of a room that was needed to progress the game, but since an option to open the door wasn't available to him and only be I had to kill myself to progress). There are a few bugs which aint too bad, but the bugs themselves are gnarly. I know I didn't really get too detailed about the game, I feel as this review lends a good mind on what to expect. A pretty damn good Souls-like which can sometimes feel a bit cheap, but overall fill that void in needing a new souls like to play. getting this game with the DLC for 40 bucks is a perfect price, especially with these devs. They seem to be very very passionate about their game, and continue to update it, and stay in the loop with their community. So overall i give this game a solid buy now and enjoy, especially if youre in a need for a good souls like.Personal Rating : 9/10Overall Rating: 7.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE: I have now finished the game, including getting the "true ending". Overall, my opinion is about the same, but there are some more gripes that have arisen. Notably-Many bosses are recycled smaller enemies with big health pools (though the bosses that are unique are fun and cool, I just wish there were more).-Some secrets yield the same rewards as other secrets, like armor sets and weapons, making them less rewarding. However, I think this was the devleopers' intent, as the game is EXTREMELY open in terms of exploration. I mean, you can go basically anywhere from the start of the game if you know what to do.That leads me into some more positives though!-Repeat playthroughs are fun due to being able to explore the world in a different order that you didn't know of before. My second playthrough ended up being even more fun due to knowing how to access a sort-of-later-game area early on and getting a good "magic" weapon. BTW magic is broken and super powerful. I melted the "true final boss" with a magic build in like 10 seconds, even with the difficulty increased a bit, so while that's not exactly a positive, it is nice to have a bit of a power fantasy after getting stomped by it for a while with a different build.-Build variety in this game is nice, if unbalanced, which is fine. Strength builds are viable and fun, but lose out to magic/dex builds easily. I haven't tried guns yet, but if they function similarly to magic, even if not as overpowered, they are probably really fun to weave into combat.Overall, I still really enjoy this game and will probably do a playthrough using guns. I might see about speedrunning it casually too, but not sure yet. The openness of the game could make it a fun speedrun game.ORIGINAL REVIEW:About 7 hours in now, and I am thoroughly enjoying my time with this game. It's definitely taken a lot of inspiration from Dark Souls in the best ways. Not just in gameplay, but also in level design. There's lots of interconnecting paths, TONS of secrets, like holy cow there are so many secrets that reward exploration generously. There's also platforming due to the game having a dedicated jump button, and it's pulled of better than you might expect! They seem to know what they're working with, and it honestly elevates the exploration (pun intended) and makes it even more fun and satisfying. The atmosphere and art direction of the game is extremely good, and it's exactly what I've been craving in a souls-like. Sci-fi horror is a fantastic combo, and they pull it off well. The lore is interesting, nothing mindblowing yet, but keeps me wanting to learn more. There also appears to be good build variety, which I absolutely love, as that will keep me coming back for more playthroughs.Also, this game has not only online co-op, but couch co-op as well! That's crazy and always an extremely welcome addition for people like myself who love playing games in-person with friends.The game isn't perfect though, and I will say my biggest gripe is the UI. It's not bad exactly, but there are things that could be communicated better, streamlined, and some things that you cannot even see. For example, the "tenacity" stat on armor doesn't have a sort of "total" amount on the stats page, which is pretty annoying due to it being poise. There might also be  some questionable design decisions with some weapons, but that's kind of always going to be a thing in a souls-like it seems. The only one instance of this that I've come across is the "Infused Column" weapon. It seems to make it into a hyrbid strength/magic stat weapon, but it doesn't seem to scale well off magic and makes it less worthwhile to use than the base weapon.Overall, I'd definitely recommend this game for fans of the genre. I can see myself enjoying the rest of this game and doing numerous playthroughs. Hats off to the developers for making a great game!

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, this type of game is rough with reviews... cause depending on when one reviews it the feeling can be completely different. Did you just rage quit cause you felt you got smoked by some mob in an unfair way?  Or did you just down a boss on your first try and are feeling mighty?  Truth be told, if you have either of these feelings chances are its a good souls game.  Cause both will inevitably happen.  I'm not far in but i can honestly say that the controls are tight (though sorta janky... hard to explain) and once you learn to be patient combat is really pretty fluid.  I played the demo and wasn't very impressed, mostly just cause it wasn't a good way to give people a true feel of the game.  Starting out with nothing and growing from level 1 is the only way to learn a souls game.  This also feels far more polished and "finished" (rightfully so) than the demo. Update after 8 hours in. - Still really enjoying my time.  Very pleased so far with the balance of this game.  It's been very hard at times and then also very easy.  The easy parts are nice breathers before the usually difficult but very fun and once learned, simple bosses.  So many satisfying feelings that remind me of the OG dark souls days.  Thanks Devs!Overall i'd give a 8/10 so far.  I certainly want to play more!

_childDocuments_.review: I've just beaten the game on splitscreen with my friend, and I need to leave this review...First, this was an excellent split screen choice to get into with a partner on a single machine. PC games just don't like to offer that kind of experience nowadays with some titles literally taking their already split screen titles on the console editions and simply disallowing the already existing feature on a PC. Cradle Games? Thank you for your contribution to the classic couch co-op.It's all downhill from here.The game play was relatively good as we worked tirelessly through many deaths and level resets to achieve our end goal of what we weren't sure. In classic Souls-like fashion, you spawn knowing nearly nothing and travel through a challenging but possible gauntlet with enough perseverance and skill.The boss fights are also satisfying. Very challenging, but possible once you learn the combat patterns.I don't recommend the game to the general public for these reasons:It's buggy, almost unplayably so.We had to do a full restate halfway through the game because a crucial peace of gear was bugged, and we needed it... literally required it... for protection from the environment. The gear would not function, and this bug just happens to some characters. Flip a coin. Good luck.Both myself and my friend have had our split screen characters reset entire 6 hour sessions. We don't get to sit down this long very often. Many people don't. A 6 hour reset would sometimes be weeks and months in real life for us. We alternated being player 1 and reset the story an additional time so that we could progress evenly again for attempt number 3 through this game.Lastly, we went through some major boss fights. We have sat down for an hour and a half for our longest and most satisfying boss fight in this game. It was glorious. After all of this pain and struggle, and all of the boss fights beginning to become a legendary endeavor, we stumbled upon the last boss in the game... The final boss in the story... Where the legend comes to life and you achieve something great before finishing your gaming experience... And we killed it in, not even slightly joking, 30 seconds. Roll game credits. You win. It's over.My friend and I finished this final boss fight and were both waiting for the next step to begin when the credits rolled and both of our shoulders and jaws begin to rapidly drop. The journey to get here was fraught with peril. Perseverance and determination abound to get us through this game 2 and a half times so that we can finally get far enough to beat it on split screen with an even playing field between us, and we received this as a closing to all of our effort?Cradle Games... Guys... You've wounded me...

_childDocuments_.review: I tried HP: The Thespian Feast and was not impressed.  Despite that, the main game seemed pretty appealing from the streams I saw so I decided to get the main game.  I don't know what it is, but the main game feels better than TTF and I am quite pleased.I've played all of the Dark Souls entries, Bloodborne, and Sekiro, but never made much progress.  I appreciate and admire soulslikes, but I just haven't been able to 'click' with them gameplay-wise - until now.  Hellpoint comes along with a great aesthetic and a soulslike experience that finally resonates with me.  Learning enemy attack patterns and strategies/weapons to approach with are much easier to grasp so far than other soulslikes and environments are open to plenty of exploration in a much more vertical manner than I expected.  Difficulty is fair and there's way more than enough room for exploration and discovery to keep things interesting when I run into a wall in on route.  I like it.There are still a few bugs in the game, but I haven't encountered anything game-breaking.  Aside from a few instances with bad hitboxes, everything's been good.I'm only 7 hours into it, but I'm thoroughly enjoying my time with this.  The demo/Thespian Feast doesn't do justice to the main game.  In my opinion, it's an excellent entry point into the souls-type genre with a forgiving and well-scaled difficulty and a big map with a great atmosphere.  I still haven't gotten through it, but Hellpoint has renewed my enthusiasm for the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played a lot of souls-like games, as well as every Souls game and Bloodborne as well.This game is amazing. If you enjoy souls-like, absolutely grab it.What you've got is a huge open world of a souls game. You have an incredible amount of freedom of where to go, and the game is pretty brilliant in how it paces you. You wouldn't be the first to think the game is linear, but some of branching paths are hidden behind secret walls and such.There are secrets EVERYWHERE.  Hidden walls, small platforms and rooms tucked away, edges hiding above and below, and they'll contain either useful items or paths leading to entire new areas sometimes.There's a huge amount of areas. The game reminded me of Hollow Knight in you'll keep thinking you'v run out of new areas to find before stumbling upon a new one.I really like how the weapon system works. Instead of directly upgrading your weapon, you install a chip inside and upgrade that, which you can pull out and replace in another weapon. Allowing you to play with new weapons without worrying about upgrade materials. These chips also have a progress bar attached to them, unlocking various skills associated with them. Using the catalyst weapons with these skills is how the magic builds work in this game. As a cool method to keep combat flowing: melee attacks will give you some mana back for your firearms/catalysts to use. It's a small but smart choice.Another smaller smart choice is having parrying not be attached to its own button, instead on having you time the bringing up of your block with the enemy's attack. It frees up the trigger, which is then the sprint button. What would normally have been a sprint button is now its own dedicated jump button. This allows for some more creativity in level design.I haven't even touched on the setting or the world yet. You'v got a giant space station,  orbiting a black whole, and some occult shenanigans that happened long before your arrival. It sounds a bit familiar when put like that sure, but I'm simplifying it.The sci-fi setting and the design of the space station is awesome. You'v got crazy looking gardens, a giant research facility, an underground mine full of blue liquid radiation, a golden pyramid like technobase, and an abandoned quarantine zone, just to name a handful. The ambient sound design for the game is incredibly well done too. It's creepy as hell the whole way through. Now, at the current moment, the game is a little on the buggy side. Constant work is being done, but just know it is a little rough around the edges at the moment. It's still one incredibly awesome gem, and I know the devs will make it ever better.Something I feel should be mentioned, the team that made this game consists of SEVEN people. That's it. And if I'm not mistaken, all the programming was done by just 1 of them. Considering the size and scope of the game, it's INCREDIBLY impressive how such a small team was able to make it.This is one lf my new favourites for sure, and I know I'll come back and replay it many more times.

_childDocuments_.review: Really don't understand why so many bad marks on this game; for a "Souls like" made by an indie studio it displays a lot of love for its creative gameplay roots by managing at the same time to convey an awesome dark sci fi horror atmosphere in the vein of Event Horizon. Sure it's a little bit clanky and buggy but an honest kudos to developers: the figthing mechanics are more than decent, there's tons of secrets to discover and the show don't tell typical of From Software games mixed with (implicit) item and environment storytelling makes this small homage really worthy of the "Soulslike" surtitle,

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games I played in 2021.If you enjoy souls-like games, this is for you. If you enjoy puzzles and hidden secrets, this is for you. If you enjoy space fantasy, this is for you. If you enjoy 'humanity truly screwed up this time' then this is definitely for you.This is a fantastic action combat game where you passively discover a really interesting story while trying to stay alive. The game is not easy. In a lot of ways it's harder than Dark Souls. But like Dark Souls, it gets a whole lot easier once you realize what's going on, the boss mechanics, etc. The combat is very satisfying. It is a solid mix of 'crafting' vs. skill.The only place the game falls down a little is in the middle of the game, where it's possible to sort of out-run the story and wonder what the heck you're supposed to do next. But that's kind of how it is in Souls-likes in general, I guess. There's no hand-holding at all in this game. And if you are like me, that's going to be just fine.

_childDocuments_.review: Hellpoint is worth playing if you are a fan of the genre. There is a large focus on exploration and piecing the world together as you play and the space station itself feels like a puzzle. What it lacks in environmental decoration and visual flare it makes up for with great level design, lighting, and atmosphere. The combat works well with a good variety of move sets for melee weapons and more than a few viable ranged options. With tight hitboxes, jumping and jump attacks, dashing and rolling attacks, combat animation cancelling, and whiff punishing just to name a few, the combat engine feels robust. Weapons will also level up from use, which unlocks new attacks and abilities, and you can also socket them with enhancements. It will be fun to replay the game to try different builds, weapons, and armor varieties. The AI is not great, and the boss fights and enemies could have been more challenging, but overall the experience is more than satisfying. I look forward to what Cradle Games will do in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm having a great time!Dark Souls, the Surge and Dead Space all lost their big budgets but made a baby.Has all the Souls-like features we have come to expect, but the package is actually good.The level design isn't as amazing as the Surge 2, but it does have secrets everywhere, and the zones are quite vertical so exploration is fun and tense.Combat feels good (I'm playing on mouse and keyboard) and when I get hit or killed, it's because I wasn't quick enough, not because of dodgy animations.The graphics are passable, but the sound is magnificent. The developers really took care in crafting the sounds. Weapons feel impactful and meaty, footsteps and groans are clearly audible and overall the sound effects are brilliant enough that I haven't noticed the lack of ambient music.There are a wide variety of character build possibilities, just in weapons alone there are strength based melee, dexterity based melee, firearms, magic and all sorts of hybrids. Hitting enemies with a melee attack recharges your mana/ammunition and estus flask which leads to fluid engagements and huge potential for all kinds of builds.I mentioned above that there are many secrets, but I want to touch on this subject again because these locations don't take the easy way out of hiding a bunch of souls or crafting materials, they can contain valuable things. Blueprints, shortcuts and even items like keycards. There are entire areas that some players will never see even after completing the game because they didn't notice a suspicious looking wall and pickup the key hidden within.So far, fighting mobs and exploring take centerstage over frequently fighting bosses, so players who loved the Surge will feel right at home here.The game is very dark and it is certainly a horror game in the same vein as Dead Space, but not quite as horrific.Also like deadspace there are opportunites to do spacewalks around the exterior of the station, which is cool.Story wise...I have no idea what the story is, what happened or whats going on, but I want to know, so in that case the passive storytelling of the game is working.Overall I highly recommend this game to any souls-like fans. It's not a cheap cash in, Hellpoint has been made with love, it is fun and worth the time.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll hesitate to recommend this one to Soulslike generalists, but push it more heartily if you're okay traversing massive, labyrinthine, brutalistic architecture a la NaissancE (a free platformer here on Steam) and like your plot to be about as well-spoken as EYE Divine Cybermancy's (a cult (or occult?) classic). It's also got a fair amount of that EYE-tier jankiness, which can try on one's patience.Warnings aside, I am enamored with Hellpoint.The world is massive and sprawling (if you can find the key items to let you get to different areas of course), which means that the route you find and take is likely to be different from the route the next player takes. This also means that it may take you a fair while to find new equipment, or end up rather out-of-depth if you take a wrong turn. It's, well, it's bleak and crushing in a way I find difficult to describe. There's a keen, peculiar sort of dread knowing that each room leads to two more rooms, and each to two thereafter, and then splits into three, never knowing which turn takes you to the tram to another zone or breach (this version of bonfires). This is honestly the game's strongest offering in atmosphere, besides the failed-state space station of occult power hovering around a black hole thing. Everything is sharp angles, shiny metals and obsidians, monolithic, bleak, and you, this wretched amalgamation some something calls 'human' are an insignificant visitor, a mote swirling in the cascading apathy of a structure ceaselessly reveling in its state of catastrophe. Every place is a liminal space because nothing belongs there, least of all you.The rest of it, though, well, it's jank, and if you have no patience for jank, or for environments that just don't respect casual or sensible player routing, you're going to struggle to enjoy Hellpoint. There's not a huge variety of enemies, bosses get recycled into common mooks depending on where you go, you may not find a set of armor or equipment to fit your stat set for a while (there's a few that require no particular stats), nothing is particularly well explained. Music cuts out immediately at area thresholds (well, ambiance, not music), some enemy animations are bizarre or not well telegraphed or just look awkward, your character spaghetti ragdolls out if you die while wearing the scrap shield. Laugh, sigh, move on, respect that the big bad you faced in the second zone becomes a casual mook later (as emphasis you're getting stronger, perhaps), and try a different path. Maybe you'll find a weapon to suit your Reflex/Foresight stat aspirations over there.Combat handles okay, though there's nothing exceptional to write home about. Dodges work, some attacks are worth blocking, back attacks do more damage, certain damage types are more effective against certain enemies than others, etc. I like that it's not the standard spread of fire/ice/lightning/etc, or at least it's decorated differently- you have induction (fire), entropic (cold), radiation, light, nihl, and physical. Killing walking aberrations of flesh and bone with the power of nihilism (assuming that's what nihl is) is pretty rad, in any case.The platforming is on occasions kind of touchy or kludgy (yeah, there's platforming in this soulslike). Oftentimes some clever jumping leads to a secret area with a secret collectible coin, new piece of equipment, a key item for cutting corners around the station, or just more axions (souls), but sometimes your inquisitive platforming takes you out of bounds and you clip through objects and fall to your death. It does take my immersion out a fair amount when the game is rewarding curious acrobatics without taking extra precautions to keep players from getting too inquisitive. Some thought went into making sure you try and see if you can make this or that jump or what might be around that cliff, and that scratches an exploratory itch something fierce.Bottom line is this, really- if you just want more Souls, pass on Hellpoint, it's just too divergent from what makes Souls a cohesive experience. If you want to get like SUPER lost and are totally down to clown with a game that doesn't tell you jack squat about where to go or what to do, Hellpoint looks a lot more appealing. Make sure you know you want this before you buy, and make sure you've got some patience to spare, but if you know what you're in for, you'll probably enjoy it. If jank scares you, wait 'til it's on sale. If you want it sooner, it's in Humble Choice for May.Edit: Doubled my playtime, got all the achievements. Every point made stands.

_childDocuments_.review: I do this review letting you know that I have not yet completed the game. Because the game won't f%#$ing let me.This is a soulslike game, and a pretty easy one at that. I died WAY more times to janky platforming than I ever did to actual combat. Speaking of which, whomever decided that platforming should be a major element of this game, should be demoted or fired. Your character platforms like a concrete shoed zombie, and the game expects competent platforming out of you. You can get it done, but you'll be fighting your character and constantly getting caught on terrain that leads you to your death.Am I rambling? I believe I am, because there are good things about this game. They are however, completely overshadowed by all the bugs and very questionable design choices along the way.Doing an escort quest? Gee I hope the NPC you're escorting doesn't bug out twice, causing me to need to reload the entire area and do it all over again losing me about 30 minutes of my time due to no fault of my own.Doing some combat? It's all fun and easy until you get knocked down, and then you realize, " ♥♥♥♥! I don't know where I put all my I-frames!." Causing you to get wombo comboed to death off of one hit.Status ailments? Mostly ok, except for cold and radiation. Cold as an ailment is fine, until you realize everything that inflicts it does so through a chain combo melee attack. What does cold do? You move more slowly and can barely dodge! Leading their easily dodge-able multi-attack to now be a wombo combo until death that you can't do anything about. Radiation (think poison) is just as bad once it hits it's second tier, because it starts lowering your maximum health. This would be fine, if it didn't persist until the next LOADING SCREEN. Seriously, resting doesn't solve it and neither do the anti-rad injections they give you. It's just GONE, until you reload everything.Sound would cut out, items went missing from my inventory, once I just died from full health while just traveling through a cleared out area, and I've fallen through the map more than once. It's just SO MANY BUGS and it's CONSTANT.The environments are super easy to get lost in as well, partially due to what I assume is an intentionally confusing layout tacked on to environments that basically look the same with the addition of secrets being ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ everywhere so you are never sure what path to take, you end up getting lost constantly or worse you know where you are but have a vague recollection of a place you need to go now where you've been before but that was 40 bland tile sets ago.Now onto difficulty. The game for the most part was piss easy. It was challenging at first until I was able to cobble together something of a build and then it was easy street with the occasionally insta death combos from enemies and bosses, very frustrating when are getting hit on the ground or are just stunlocked until death, but I've played and beaten a lot of souls games, so I expected the occasional jank. It was for the most part easy though, I died maybe about 7-10 times to bosses and enemies (around 50 or 60 to jank platforming or bugs though), and then from left field comes the final boss. Holy %$#@ is it frustrating. You get staggered or knocked down once, you are probably dead. Just one shot kills left and right, and if you survive you get crippled with radiation lowering your max health and doing damage over time. If you did your due diligence and did story stuff you have an NPC who will also fight you at the same time as the boss! Leading to even more frustration. Oh, and on top of all that, you will deal absolutely nothing for damage. My character is about level 80 or so, with a +11 espadon, and it took me about 80 or so hits to down the big boss, and then another 20 or so to kill the little guy, all while dodging one shots coming from all directions with some having little to no start-up animation.Do you know what happened after I beat the boss? I floated through ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ space forever because the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ game bugged out AGAIN. I, so far have beaten this boss now 3 times, and each time my effort is wasted since the game refuses to acknowledge that I've emptied the health bars.If I hadn't played so many hours, I would refund this garbage. This game lacks polish on every single level except the visual. Did I mention that a good chunk of the equipment legitimately does not work either? The game in it's current state is an embarrassment, do not buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is definitely one of the best 3D souls-likes I've played. I've tried a bunch of them, and they're usually pretty disappointing. This is kinda like The Surge but good.Overall the game is a little bit buggy and unpolished. Some gameplay elements are a bit janky and confusing, sometimes enemies or bosses will get stuck on the geometry or start T-posing.  Sometimes the sound will drop out into awkward silence. But it's all pretty rare, and it's not bad enough to ruin the experience. The game is definitely 1000% improved compared to the demo a few years ago.This game really shines from the lore, the characters, the environments and enemies. A really haunting atmosphere, like Dead Space meets Dark Souls, or with Event Horizon/HR Giger vibes. The combat is really smooth and enjoyable, and that's the most important thing. Usually this is where souls-like games fail.My biggest frustration is the infuriating labyrinth of the game world. I was constantly lost, and it's very hard to get your bearings. Lots of dead ends, and the game doesn't really tell you where you're supposed to be going. It's also filled with some platforming puzzles and secret doors. Very confusing at times, but maybe I'm just bad at navigating.Overall it's a flawed gem but I loved it. Worth playing if you like a challenge and enjoy this genre, but just be prepared to wade through a little bit of jank.

_childDocuments_.review: -------------------------------------Scroll down to the next line for the review--------------------------------Just quickly wanted to say that you shouldn't listen to a lot of the negative reviews, especially the ones that are complaining about level design and co-op. If they're complaining about the level design then they don't understand what good level design is. Yes, there are a lot of ways to go and you do get lost sometimes, but whose fault is it that you can't remember what way you went? Yours. That's your own fault. And the Co-Op is fine, yes there are some bugs with it but you guys have to understand that this isn't some massive AAA developer with hundreds of millions of dollars to throw at the game. The coop works just fine, the worst thing that can happen is that one of you have to reconnect. Seriously just how spoiled are some of you. Some guy was even suggesting that this 20+ hour game with tons or replayability should be priced at 15 bucks. Seriously if you're mad about spending 35 bucks on a great game then go get a job. Ridiculous. -----------------------------------------------------------Review-------------------------------------------------------The game is amazing in my opinion. Some bugs here and there but i haven't found a single gamebreaking bug thus far.What you get here, for 35 dollars is equivalent to a souls game in length. It also has high replayability. +Fun combat+Lots of weapons+Decent boss fights+Not a lot boss fights with ads/more than one boss(!!!)+Interesting story/lore+Amazing map design+Loot, LOTS of loot+A ton of hidden/secret areas+Multiplayer that doesn't despawn the other player on death or boss completion (It works great after the patch)+ Amazing, very immersive atmosphere- Some minor bugs here and there- Some of the bosses are a bit easy- Increasing the game actually makes it easier- Magic is overtuned, it is way to strong imo (But using it is optional, obviously)- Some puzzles i hate, i'm looking at you double artillery in Alma MaterOverall you get SO much for such a low price. I can see myself easily getting 100+ hours in this game. And even if you just rush through the game you're going to get a solid 20+ hours out of it. I've paid 60 bucks for less.I think the devs did an absolutely outstanding job with this game and it can only get better from here. I am hoping that this game gets at least one decent sized DLC. And i am looking forward to Hellpoint 2 if that ever happens. This is the best Souls-like i've ever played.

_childDocuments_.review: Great souls like game for what it is IMO.  Not the most polished game ever but thats okay considering it was made by a smaller studio and started out as a kickstarter.  The game itself is very exploration based which both hurts and helps the game.  You can choose to run around and find the best weapons and gear before even fighting any of the big bosses. Also the start of the game is pretty bad but if you choose to put more time into i promise it gets good.  In terms of difficulty it really isn't that hard especially if you have experience in this genre of game, however you can choose to raise the difficulty pretty significantly during later playthroughs.  Now if i am to just to give my opinion on this game while ignoring the objective flaws i would say it's pretty great.  I love the desolate and unforgiving atmosphere of the game.  The game being set on a space station in the middle of a black hole only helps to add to the overall atmosphere and feeling of isolation. In terms of builds and weaponry this game is fairly compact.  There are no spells because the magic weapons have there own built in abilities also i found that the guns are pretty boring to use. There still is some experimenting to be done with different builds but it's not nearly on the level of the souls games or games like NIOH but i honestly wasnt expecting that much from this game.  Overall i think this game has a lot of potential and i would love to see a second game.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR:I love the idea and the game feels true to a game a souls player can expect. However, shoddy/incohesive level design, game-breaking bugs (ex. disappearing projectiles, buggy hitboxes, invisible enemies, projectiles), and piss poor bosses hardly justify the $35 I paid for it. In it's current state, it's not worth any more than $15 max. It has so much potential and I hope the cons can be addressed and the game tightened up.Pros:- Feel is familiar to a souls game with secrets and interesting lore.- Cool setting- Overall interesting art styleCons- The level design is HORRIBLE. Arisen Dominion is one of worst of them and I couldn't wait to get out of that level. It's also super out of place to the rest of the game. The developers shove in jump puzzles everytime they run out of ideas in a map, there are long empty passages with no added purpose other to exist. For example, when taking the tram to Port Issoudun, there's an enemy right when you spawn in so while you're loading in, you're getting attacked before you can even see anything. I spawned in dead and lost all my axioms. There's also a ghost spawn next to the rift so you can die over and over before you ever finish loading.- $35 is WAAY too much for this game, especially in the state it's in.- Buggy hitboxes. Watch an enemy 10 feet away swing their sword and blood fly out of your back.- Invisible bullets, especially on the final boss, but you'll still feel the damage from them. Only reason I knew they existed was that the other player saw them. - Weak enemy variety- Poor boss design- The hardest battle is fighting against the ♥♥♥♥♥♥ level design.

_childDocuments_.review: Hellpoint is quite the indie gem, i was very impressed with how much they managed to cram into this game. If you're a souls fan this one is definitely worth the money.+Amazing atmosphere, with impressive lighting and sounds, giving Irid Novo a sci fi horror vibe. I like this a lot +While the soundtrack is a bit on the small side, what is there is very impressive. From boss themes to just crafting in the observatory, It does a great job of making you feel like you are isolated.+Graphics are very astounding once again showing what Unity can do. Amazing lighting effects, and shadows.+Level design for me was a plus here, got lost a few times, but eventually you map everything out, this point will vary between players though.+A nice variety of builds, from Strength,Dexterity,and mana based weapons and styles to pick from. +Performance wise the game ran very well i only had 2 crashes in my entire playthrough.FPS was pretty solid as well+Boss designs were fantastic! Love the animations as well, very unique.-Had an instance of a major boss glitching on me where he just stood still and basically let me chop him down. This was a one boss incident though, i have no idea how it triggered either.-Camera sometimes spun itself around while moving into a new area.-Platforming was fine, just sometimes my character kept running after sticking a landing, fortunately my deaths in this manner were low.-The game could have explained the dark hole mechanic earlier on, this isn't a huge gripe though. Just small feedback.In closing. If you're a souls fan or just looking for an action RPG to sink your teeth into. Hellpoint provides a ton of great quality and quantity gameplay for your dollar. The aesthetic is incredible, there is a lot of love put into this game. And you support a great indie dev team. Also, hopefully we get a sequel :D
