_childDocuments_.review: There's a lot to like in Hellpoint, but after 33 hours played I just can't find it in my heart to truly recommend it. The final boss fight highlights everything that is wrong with the game, from janky angles and camera work, to hitboxes that simply don't connect despite them clearly passing through each other. With an unskippable cutscene before every boss attempt. It just isn't FUN, and isn't that what games are supposed to be? Being spammed by locked on attacks from offscreen just isn't fun. It's the kind of artificial challenge that you can't "git gud" past. If I ever install the game again to try my luck against the boss one more time, it won't be skill that gets me through, it will be luck. A real shame endcap to a game with a lot of full elements, but between this and the third boss, I can see now that these are intentional design choices not bugs.I am happy to report that after 11 more hours of play, I've not found anything as janky or broken as the boss in Sohn. Enemies and bosses seem much better tuned over all, areas have got lots of cool hidden things, and there are sections of lore to read if you hunt them down. The game is EXPANSIVE and open, and I've regularly gotten lost or played for about 30 minutes to finally die and realise I haven't got a clue how to get back to my bloodstain. All in all, a solid indie experience that I can recommend — except for that damned twin boss.Really enjoyed the Thespian Feast, despite it's sometimes janky camera, but currently cannot recommend the full game, as much as I'd like to.Positives:- lots of exploration and secrets to find- while not amazing graphically, the game has a DOOM-like hell-on-Earth aesthetic that I really like, and it has great atmosphere- enemy design is decent, albeit mixed in places (what's with the green floating fish?!)Mixed:- controls are a mixed bag. Plunging attack seems wildly inaccurate, shield smash doesn't seem to do anything (unless it's just supposed to be 'running with your shield up' which you can do anyways.- areas just aren't super memorable. They have the really twisty maze-like style of The Surge 2 but lack a lot of the visual distinctiveness to pull it off. Many places with similar neon signs, for example, offer little more than confusion and dull backtracking.- some of the run-backs to bosses are too harsh and crowded by enemies. Yes there are shortcuts and closer breaches, but some of them are hidden behind secret walls that you might literally only find because someone else in the game has left one of their gold handprints on it.Negatives:- hit boxes. They're all over the place.- status effects. No idea what any of them do and there's seemingly no help screen for them. Two of the first three bosses have an affect that slows you down and I have no clue which resistance might help counter it.- collision. The pair of enemies that make up the third boss encounter are either really bugged or just plain badly designed. The one with the censer can stunlock you to death through scenery because his ranged attack (and they both have ranged and melee attacks) goes through all the terrain. The one with the staff can damage you by hitting his staff on the ground even if you're nowhere near him and are shields up.- clock thing. I get the idea that the black hole influences what is going on in the game world, but there's zero explanation of how any of it works and in a game like this where the difficulty already seems to vary wildly, a little bit more knowledge would help.- the ghost. I don't mind the mechanic, but they feel like a real waste of resources to beat, don't offer enough of a reward to compensate, and often ignore attacks after you've parried/shield-blocked them.All in all, with a few patches under its belt, Hellpoint will hopefully live up to the promise that I saw in the Thespian Feast, but right now it is more on the frustration end than the fun end, and no amount of cool secrets to find will balance out poorly-balanced combat and bosses.

_childDocuments_.review: I am really angry with this game. And if you follow them, like I did, but miss to talk to the almost invisible architect before the final (well not the "real" final) boss fight, you will be send to New Game + and you have to do it all again to have a shot at the True ending. I do not do replays, so even thou I was at the end, I was unable to "finish"the real game. Which is infuriating.Also, the achievements did not worked for me, but this was the lesser of the evils.I give the game positive rating, because it was fun and interesting journey with some great fights in it, but from all the Souls-like games I played, this one managed to screw me the most with this True ending ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.

_childDocuments_.review: I tried to like this game but ultimately I can't recommend it. The biggest issue is a general lack of polish for a game that's been out as long as it has. The game runs super poorly, apparently on any platform. I had turned off the blood effects because they looked so bad but then had to turn then back on because its sometimes the only visual cue that you are hitting something. The whole disk clock thing in the corner seems to not be explained anywhere and even after reading a guide on it I don't understand the point. The enemy design is OK for the mobs but then the bosses feel very lazy with narrow movesets and just spongy health pools.The hit boxes for you hitting enemies seems fine but hurt boxes from enemy attacks is awful. There were far too many times where the enemy was clearly out of range or their weapon clearly missed me but the game decided I still took damage.This game has an issue i also had with Dark Souls 3 and Eldin Ring where sometimes it queues your inputs, so if you are mashing the heal button during a boss then stop mashing after your heal goes through you will still sometimes healagain because you had previously pressed the button resulting in just wasting your limited heals.This might have just been me but at the end of the year they put a winter aesthetic on the main screen that caused nothing but the snow and xmas lights to display. I couldnt find anyone else complaining about this and it didnt resolve until after the event was over and the game updated again. On the pro side i do like the setting.The future outer space thing all looks neat and is intriguing.I like that what i saw of the story was intriguing and now the tired dark souls thing of being over ambiguous for no good reason.I enjoyed the idea of the crafting system even though I kept getting recipes for which i had no where close to the resources they needed. The areas are large and the low stamina consumption from running was an awesome idea over similar games. This also helps mitigate the common issue with this genre or the unnecessary and annoying "boss run"Movement feels really good for the most part and the ability to dodge cancel helped to make combat feel much faster.I can definitely see the makings of a good game in here but it really needs a once over to fix its issues before i could recommend it to someone. I am sure a hellpoint 2 would be killer

_childDocuments_.review: So continues the saga of trying to find a fun Souls-like game with uninterrupted co-op.  This one stands out more than the others with a lot of promise but with little delivery.  Once the charm of the atmosphere and Gigeresque aesthetic wears off, you're left with a mediocre experience.  I wanted to love this game because it's one of the best attempts at what I'm looking for with a Souls game but this wasn't quite it. It's not a bad game, per se, but it's also held back by the amount of jank.5 Platforming Sections out of 10

_childDocuments_.review: Hellpoint is one of many games taking inspiration from the Dark Souls series. Basically, it is Space Horror Souls.That is not really bad though.I actually quite like many of the core gameplay choices. The weapon upgrade system really encourages you trying out many different weapons, something I am missing in many of the From Soft Games where especially earlier in the game, upgrading multiple weapons will be a liability.The Weapon leveling and the skills also were fun, offering a nice variety of options.Many enemies, while maybe not as well designed as ones in later From Soft games actually are able to offer a fair challenge.And the atmosphere is nice and creepy.Platforming in the game was okay, I personally enjoyed it.Split Screen Co-Op is what really made me love this game. Playing it with my boyfriend was a blast and I really loved that it was completely seamless without any solo only areas.The Negatives:-At least in multiplayer, the bosses are just too weak. We beat pretty much every boss the first time around save for the first and last. Since he normal enemies often were challenging enough, this seems like something where more would be possible.- The lack of any character creation is a bit of a bummer.- I think free teleportation between "bonfires" would have been preferable. I do not think the limitations really added anything.

_childDocuments_.review: Take this game for what it is, a Dark souls like game but set in space. I strongly emphasize the word 'like' in the previous statement. This game isn't Dark souls and if you want an exact copy of Dark souls then you will probably be left disappointed. If you can get past the fact it isn't and never will be as good as a souls game then you will thoroughly enjoy this game just as I have done. It isn't as long or polished or detailed as a souls game but it also doesn't come with the same price tag so what did you expect? I found the core gameplay to be solid and fun despite lacking a bit of creativity at times. There is plenty to do and lots of little secrets to be found. _childDocuments_.review: Easily the best Souls-like (since surpassed by Lords of the Fallen from 2023) and I personally like it more than Dark Souls itself. However it is a little buggy, but nothing I encountered that breaks the game.+I totally love that with every melee hit you refill your mana and health injections, based on your weapon's leech stat. This gives you great sustain. and is a huge quality of life feature.+I like the sci-fi setting and weird monsters.+Combat feels responsive and great. Enemies and bosses (except for the final boss) don't spam bs AOE attacks constantly coughEldenRingcough.+Your melee weapon doesn't bounce off walls. Sounds insignificant... until you play Dark Souls and get killed repeatedly because your attack doesn't land because it bounced off the wall letting the enemy wail on you. Or worse, the bounce, which causes knockback, knocks you off the edge and you die.+I like that you can increase and decrease the difficulty at any save point (breach) using certain effigies. With higher difficulty the enemies are tougher but drop way more axions (exp).+If you want to you don't have to fight the final boss. You can just surrender your data and go to a new cycle.+I love the maze-like levels and how interconnected they are, like Dark Souls 1.+-Story is meh and almost non-existent, and told in a terrible way. I beat the game and I still have almost no idea what's going on. For some reason this seems to be a requirement for Souls-likes. Just because Dark Souls had a meh story terribly delivered doesn't mean you have to copy them there too.+-I would have liked more weapon and moveset variety, especially for the guns and catalysts (magic).+-There's a bunch of armor, but most of them have crappy stats. Aegis Armature is easily the best set and it's definitely worth it to increase your load stat for it regardless of build. Unfortunately you can't upgrade your armor like you can your weapon, so eventually you're going to be getting one-shot on the higher difficulties by the bosses anyway.+-I would have liked changes for new game plus, like the items found are different, change in enemies, and so on.+-The Omnicube is cool, but most of the programs are junk and you'll never use them. I don't even know what you're supposed to do with the cooling and warming programs.+-I hate when these games have secret walls. Worse, you're almost required to find these secrets to progress, at least in a timely manner. But once you learn what the secret door looks like it's pretty easy to spot. This is in contrast to Dark Souls that has illusory walls that are impossible to discern and you must read a guide.+-At first it really annoyed me that in order to warp between breaches you needed to find and use a breach synchronizer. However by the end of the game you have learned the hub areas and used your breaches there and have some to spare. Annoying as a newb, not so bad when you're experienced.+-I wish the game had a map, even a simple one that showed you what areas connect to what other areas. Expect to be lost for a long time.+-The black hole clock is an interesting idea, but unfortunately the game doesn't really explain what it does. When the orange symbol is at the 3 or 9 position that's when hordes will appear, behind an orange barrier like a boss, and reward special loot. Areas also have a gray circle and when the orange and gray circle meet then I believe enemies are stronger and reward more axions. Also that's when black hole (white) barriers are lowered. However some barriers need you to also input the correct eye codes (located at a certain place), and it's unnecessarily convoluted. Most of the loot behind them is uninteresting. Only bother with it to kill the First Archon Knight and the only if you care about the achievement. It also sucks that there's no way to speed up the clock.-The game is buggy and unfortunately the dlc introduced new bugs. The devs are supposed to be looking into it. The worst ones are you can't move after dodging and your character stands there waiting to die (only happened once), and the other bad one is your healing doesn't work (happened to me several times).-Stagger builds are useless on difficulties higher than 1. As you increase the difficulty all stats of the enemy increases, including its resistance to staggering. Stick to fast weapons.-Almost all of the melee weapon abilities are useless. You're almost always better off using an elemental conductor and activating its special ability to enhance your weapon with that element doing a lot more damage, especially if the enemy is weak to it.-------------Ultimately worth a buy, especially on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: 4 / 10.  Skip this game. I've now played through 14 souls inspired games and this one was the worst of them.  I very rarely finish a game that I'd score under a 5 but I powered through this one hoping it would get better and it didn't.   What worked is the core combat.  Its also why I played to the end.  The player controls well, it was fun going around zones killing dudes and the RPG systems work.  I especially like energy system being similar to the Surge in how it converts to more healing letting you stay out longer.   There was a also maybe 3 bosses that felt pretty fun to play and elevated themselves beyond 'meh'.  What didn't work for me personally was just about everything else: - Environments were bland to the point of confusion.  So many locked doors in a way that didn't feel 'fun' to unlock down the road but just added to the confusion of the area.  This is especially true when you go long periods of time before unlocking a door you forgot existed.- Areas lacked cohesion...I didn't feel like one space connected to another and when it came time to backtrack I was completely lost as to which area was where. - The fast travel system being linked to rare item drops is HORRENDOUS.  As a player you don't know the map or what areas are worth returning to so this idea only brought the game way down versus simply letting people fast travel freely.- Enemies were extremely dull.  Most stagger on first hit so 90% of this game is just getting the first hit.  You do NOT need to learn patters in this souls game and that's a huge fail.- This game doubles down on platforming and its just not a fun thing within the souls formula.- Most bosses felt generic and ultimately were generic due to re-use as monsters- Gear upgrading led to a feel bad moment for me where I dismantled old versions only to find out they were requirements for gear I wanted later in the game.  I was then at a total loss on how to get that gear again.- The 'other world' gimmick that's used in this game was a creative idea but felt like padding ultimately and did not serve to make the overall game more fun.

_childDocuments_.review: I would give this more of a maybe than a yes, but not a hard no. Unfortunately the lack of polish from what I assume is a small and/or inexperienced team really shows in comparison to other Souls-like games or action combat games - the keyword here is . The concept is very good, and it appeals a lot to me by being a somewhat rare type of aesthetic of light horror, sci fi, and fantasy. One of the only similar games I can think of was a (also janky) f2p MMO called Requiem. I wouldn't call any other part of the game great, I would call most of it so-so and a few things not good. People who don't normally like this type of game probably won't enjoy it much or be very impressed unless they also have a strong appreciation for this techno hybrid type aesthetic. It starts to feel more cold and uninspired after viewing many of the different areas in their sharp cube-ness, but it is still very very cool looking overall and I think quite unique.I really enjoy how they use the ability to be in space and paint large expansive backgrounds to be what stops you from going here or there, instead of the typical walls of rock, cliffs, mountains, piles of debris etc. It makes each level feel very large and maybe the levels are quite large even within the playable area - it's a bit hard to quantify because it's so empty and full of often seemingly pointless corridors of dead ends.Weapons seem unbalanced, and different types of armor seem fairly pointless. I suppose it's more of a "fashion souls" effect to have the different sets than an actual good reason. I'm sure however that you could easily complete the game with whatever you like best because it's just not that challenging. There are few types of enemies and very few types of attacks, and the AI is janky. Combat works, usually, but I really question anyone who says it's amazing. Some of the jank includes bugs such as a large monk man who casts light missiles - there is no way to interrupt this attack once it starts not even including his death. Granted it only takes 1 or 2 times getting hit by it to figure that out, but dying from such bugs is still unpleasant. There is not a lot of different attack animations or types so very few of the weapons seem like anything more than a different skin. There's no way for the average player to do a blind build of most of the weapons on your first play through. The access to the items needed for them is inconsistent at best and the knowledge of how to build them not provided soon enough - so you would have to be experienced enough to guess what type of weapon you want and start building early, or not spending in stat points at all for a very long time if you want certain builds.   The devs seem very active replying to people here on reviews and talking about wanting to fix bugs, and perhaps they are quite genuine, but I think there is just too many. I don't know how much they have actually accomplished but there is no way between the bugs and AI jank for them to get the state of the game to a level of full polish that would rate the game 7+/10. If you like exploration and finding obscure secrets you will really like this game. I do, but for me there is an extent to which it just feels pointless because the secrets aren't rewarding, the obscurity is for the sake of it and not in any way clever, and you have to do a lot of awkward platforming. Jumping is one of the worst parts, it's too slippery and fall deaths account for the majority of my deaths which is not the most enticing mechanic for a Souls-like.   Speaking of obscure they clearly tried to do the Fromsoft  approach to the story and direction, but the way it's actually structured makes it way too easy to skip the "proper" order and not even be able to find out what the proper order is or was. So you progress things past the point of being able to go back and complete them without any way of realizing it, or even just to the point of confusion, and without having technically done anything wrong. Even if I wanted to go play again to do it more properly I would need a guide to help me figure out what order to do things in. There are five or so fires in the game as part of a lore thing and the first one we found was probably supposed to be the third one. 15 hours in to the game I still don't know what the purpose of the Underworld is - to farm nihil shards, but why? As long as I'm mentioning nihil shards I might as well talk about loot. You get 95% Axioms (Souls) or crafting materials as loot and a ton of these things are just laying around on the floor. You end up with 1000% more basic crafting materials than you could possibly seemingly need and picking up some 50-500 Axioms at the end of a jumping puzzle or secret is not very enticing. Perhaps realizing their pacing was too convoluted there are also a few dupes of armor and weapons that I assume the devs wanted to make sure you would find even if you missed some areas. Then there are the crafting materials that are rare drops from enemies. This loops back to questioning how much exploration is too much when it feels largely pointless. There are very few enemies in each area and it becomes repetitive in scale. I have no incentive whatsoever to farm those materials, and it would have made a lot more sense to put them in the puzzles and secrets as rewards. The omnicube is a nice idea but too insignificant - actually same thing with body modules, mind modules, and different healing potions. The gain from min-maxing by swapping them is mostly too negligent to care because the bonuses are too small or irrelevant. I am just running antigravity module (reduces carry weight) so that I can wear all beef gear and not be slow.  All in all I am enjoying it because I am playing it with someone who I enjoy spending time with. The co-op is actually fairly poorly done. If they wanted it to be more Souls-like and not a full co-op experience then it should have been more limited as opposed to making us feel like it has more freedom than it actually does. Desync is a frequent problem, for example I use a 2H which flinches common enemies on every attack but my co-op partner sees the enemies attack pattern as if it was not being flinched. When they are target locked on him, as they rarely change target, they slide or teleport to him after getting knocked down. Anyway there is already plenty negative reviews of the co-op, my main point is I don't know if I would enjoy it enough to finish it on my own. I do feel bad saying mostly negative things about it, but that's how it often is when something has this much unmet potential. The larger concept to this game could have been something incredibly special if it had more resources and finesse, and so I'm more disappointed then I would be if I felt this way about some generic indie open world RPG or somesuch. TLDR buy it on sale?

_childDocuments_.review: This is my first Dark Souls - esque game and I absolutely love it. With that being said, the game is not without its issues there are plenty of bugs to be found but for the most part they are not game breaking. It does feel like the game could have used some more time with development before release but even so myself and my friend have thoroughly enjoyed our time with this title thus far.Let's talk about the bugs first. The BIG ONE, and this is probably the only game breaking bug I have experienced... This happens exclusively in multiplayer and has only happened to my friend in coop (usually I am the host) where there will be an enemy I can see but he can't, he can still lock on and attack but there is no way for him to properly defend or react, and depending on what type of enemy it is he could very easily die to something that he has no control over. This doesn't happen very often but when it does its definitely not fun for him. Other bugs in coop exist such as our characters appearing "naked" to each other, we can't see any gear or weapons equipped even though we certainly are geared up. Not sure if this one is so much a bug as maybe a design flaw but in coop, I can revive my team mate but if I die (as the host) then we both have to restart, I think we should both be able to revive each other, its not fun and makes the gameplay experience feel unequal and biased towards the host especially for a game that promotes making the gameplay experience just as valid for the second player. Another design flaw (not really a bug i don't think) I have found is when someone falls off a cliff, sometimes the area where it allows me to revive my team mate will have them respawn in a position that will cause them to fall again which means that now they either need to disconnect and rejoin or I have to suicide and reset, this shouldn't be happening. Other bugs include rooms disappearing randomly, textures and colors going all out of whack, getting stuck to slanted walls, some physics bugs, etc.With all that said, for me, none of these things happened often enough to ruin my enjoyment with this title so let's talk about the good stuff now....First things first the combat, as a game of this genre combat is central and you are going to be doing a lot of it and the combat here is really intuitive and enjoyable. There is a learning curve between getting comfortable with your fighting style and learning the movesets of your foes and once you get a hold of the controls the combat becomes really fun and really rewarding. You always get a strong sense of accomplishment after defeating your enemies and there is such a diverse amount of foes to always keep you one your toes, strategizing and maneuvering through their blows to each satisfying victory. There is also an incredibly diverse amount of options to build your fighting style, no classes in this game, just find the weapons that work best for you, and each weapon diversifies itself even further with each weapon having their own unique abilities once your level them up. Beyond that is level design and exploration, this game gives you no context for the story at hand. Instead, you are simply thrust into the world and left to your own curiosity to discover and the more curious you are the more satisfying the game is because the exploration here is extremely rewarding. Finding keys to unlock new areas, finding secret doors and pathways hidden in plain sight leading to special items and secret loot, this game also has a good emphasis on platforming as well and usually the platforming pathways lead to some of the best items in the game. There is a lot the game doesn't tell you and leaves it up to you to discover and for some that might be a turn off, this game doesn't have a "tutorial zone" you are basically just thrust into it and left to your devices to learn and grow, and this game will kick your ass but if you stick with it all the ass kicking will be well worth it.TLDR;CONS:- Some rare game breaking bugs/design exclusively in coop- Buggy rooms, physics, textures- No tutorial zone- No context for the story is providedPROS:- Platforming- Extremely rewarding exploration- Combat is intuitive and satisfying- Player choice is recognized, giving you plenty of ways to build your fighting style- Difficult but rewarding learning curve- Enemies are diverse and unique- Strategic thinking and patience is rewarded- (Subjective) none of the bugs were enough to ruin the experience for meRating: 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: First off, my friend and I are kind of suckers for the souls-like formula which is why this game caught our attention but here it goes.Pros :- Great aesthetic for pretty much everything (armor sets, enemies, general environment, bosses and weapons).         - Intricate level design with a lot of interconnectivity and secrets that will make you want to either take notes or draw a map of your own (big Bloodborne and Salt& Sanctuary vibes on that point).          - Interesting story and world to discover (well woven into the original's game ending and NG+ mechanic)Cons: - Extremely janky co-op sessions; enemies suddenly turning semi-invincible (only the host could damage them and yet the partner can still be hurt by said mob), random visual glitches where one of us would completely disappear apart from our shadows, getting stuck in a falling animation when walking on solid ground. Plus the longer we were in a co-op session, the more these bugs would happen.           - Horrible boss design; most of them end up just being damage sponges that penalise you if you do not have a specific build to counter their elemental weakness. They all have big AoE moves that will do half if not more of their arena. In that regards, the game nearly forces you to spec mainly for a ranged build with your melee weapon being there solely for the leech mechanic (which is pretty neat I won't lie).            - Unbalanced items/abilities; my friend went caster and I went melee. He would melt bosses in a couple seconds with most, if not all, of his caster implements whilst even if I went full glass cannon and with the heaviest hitting weapons I could  find I would barely tickle them. Some weapon abilities are downright useless in certain conditions because they would glitch on the surroundings and simply not work or output damage.           - Anti-climactic DLC; apart for the armor sets and weapons you can find in it, it adds nothing but frustration to the game. The bosses are even a worse offender in that vein.All in all, get it on a sale without the DLC if you're a fan of the genre. Otherwise don't bother

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10 - Fantastic cross between DS and DSp(Dead Space) with great elements from both with more than a few flaws+ Truly unique world building and design unlike anything else. Very pleased to see a Sci-fi entry like this+ Polished mechanics ported directly from DS+ Brooding overbearing atmosphere full of character in spirit of DSp+ Excellent variety of bosses with that interesting blend of organic Sci-fi horror+ An exploration based game first and foremost with vast, hard-to-describe VAST levels greatly different from one another+ The space station and its history slowly revealed over the narrative draws you further into the setting+ Weapon variety and abilities wonderful with some OP by the end+ Sci-fi future setting very close in spirit to Blame! manga+ Towering enemies provide a grand sense of scale even more so than DS at times+ You can raise/lower difficulty a limited number of times allowing for strategic grinding to help you along+ Well done mysterious setting with much novelty during discovery+ Secrets galore at every corner, ramp, hidden door (have to interact instead of smash)+ Leveling mechanics with an extra layer of unlocking abilities based on weapon usage and leveling weapon mods which can be moved around so you can experiment easily+ Upgrades only limited by currency: over-leveling only limited by patience+ Time cycle with extra secrets/challenges built around it are engaging and entertaining+ Can proceed through the game's areas in a wide open manner as the game gradually opens up in all directions+ One of those games where you're yearning for more content and enjoying all of its nook and crannies- Horrific, bastardized, ♥♥♥♥♥♥, obtuse, incompetent, frustrating, egregious, moronic platforming - 90% of deaths from falls. Devs really dropped the ball here with stiff jumping, unpredictable running jump delay and forced into many areas just to have it rather than be part of the environmental design- Bugs & defects aplenty, nothing game breaking: sound crashes on alt+tab, partial falls through floor, enemy ragdoll physics all over the place, texture clipping, targeting swaps between enemies force the camera to puke- Poor introduction of game mechanics. Nonsensical label descriptions. Poor tooltips and directions.Excellent game if you can stomach light bugs and soul-crushing platforming

_childDocuments_.review: Second playthrough (thanks again for the extra key) and there's a good deal of improvements. To be honest, I was spurred here to say something positive for once because of the negative review today from Jim Sterling, whom I generally agree with. To think this was done by such a limited team, I thought it was rather clearly a work of love.He thought this was a rather shoddy tribute and to be honest, after playing a good deal of "Souls-like" games, this really nails everything you could want and...want them to experiment with with a Soulslike. I've gone through the Surge series, Nioh, and Mortal Shell within the past year and while Nioh nails the combat feel and puts more emphasis on the RPG/weapon systems, Hellpoint feels so much more focused on the FEELING that was invoked with the original Dark Souls game on your first playthroughs: Wonderous foreign atmosphere that rewards and asks for exploration, tons of obscure data and a storyline that isn't forced upon you more than can be drawn from data you both seek out and things just shown/experienced by you, and combat incentives that continually grow (even if movesets feel pretty barebones) as your arsenal and stats grow, including a much more limited estus flask system that regains charge by you aggressively going after a foe.Yes, there's some jank, but I found it all charming and in tribute to the Soulsbourne series. There's nothing revolutionary here, there doesn't need to be but there are enough surprises and secrets to justify multiple playthroughs and I'm happy to be back.

_childDocuments_.review: If there was ever a game that I did not expect to resonate with me so much, it would be Hellpoint. When I tried the demo; The Thespian Feast I thought "Meh it's okay I guess", but I decided to take the plunge and bought the full game a couple of days after release to give it a real honest fair shake, and to support a new up and coming developer. And oh my did I fall in love so deeply with this game as it has become one of my all time favourite games ever. Yes it is a Souls-like and yes it is rough around the edges with some balance issues and bugs but it's one of those games I found myself continuously coming back to and loving every run I do because it always felt fresh and different trying out new builds, routes and seeing the game world change around me all the time as I discover new thing.However it's definitely far from perfect and as usual I break things down:Pros- Weighty, challenging and methodic combat- Beautiful surreal art style with a dark dreamlike quality- Huge interconnected non-linear world with lots of find and explore- Loads of secrets- Lore, lore, lore! There's lots of interesting lore to find- Tons of build and play style variety and viability- Excellent soundtrack- Almost every weapon has unique, interesting abilities- Enemies are very varied in appearance and fighting styles- Platforming that works surprisingly well in a Souls-like- Perhaps the best rendition of teleporting in a Souls-like, forcing you to use precious resources- Great multiplayer with co-op, PVP and splitscreen play- The clock mechanic can cause interesting world events- Daring and Fearful Effigies to change the New Game cycle are excellent additions- Every time you die the world can change in subtle or overt ways- A bunch of content, a first run can last 20+ hours- Insane amounts of replayability with different endings and new things to try out- Runs incredibly well even on low end hardware- Heaps of options to get the game looking and feeling just right for you- Plenty of fun Easter eggs and references hidden throughout the gameCons- New Game+ is sorely lacking with no new additions, changes or goals whatsoever - it really needs spicing up- The clock mechanic isn't dynamic enough, accretion storms and black hole hours could be far more dangerous with more high level spawns and environmental hazards - I'd love to see the world change in far more drastic and challenging ways- Eliminating cosmic gods doesn't have enough impact on the world, again I wish this could change the world in more varied and interesting ways - Outer space sections are underused and disappointing- Can be incredibly buggy at times albeit nothing gamebreaking- Sound and music frequently cuts off on all machines I played on- Two incredibly important NPCs are bugged to some degree, one randomly running around while the other randomly returns to the Observatory despite having never spoken to them- Certain elemental damage types are overpowered while others are underpowered- A bunch of enemies feel too weak in standard NG, especially the upgraded victims- Some weapon abilities are near useless- The Interface boss kinda sucks and is incredibly easy to cheese its AI- Lack of proper mod support- No map to any degree; while I know my way around the game, it would be a welcome addition-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------These next two paragraphs are directed to Cradle Games, the developers of Hellpoint: While it goes without saying that I want to see all the issues I mentioned ironed out, I do believe shaking things up completely for New Game+ would make me care about NG+ a lot, perhaps with random elements that change up enemy spawns, item spawns, NPC locations and perhaps a new goal to achieve that's different to the first NG cycle. Making the game clock and cosmic god kills have a far greater impact on the world in interesting ways would also help to make the game so much more dynamic especially for replays. For example a list of potential changes that could happen: more varied enemy spawns, new enemies in previous areas, ghosts spawning across the whole game like the one in the High Ateliers, opening the player up to invasions, gameplay modifiers e.g. mirror mode, enemy buffs, player debuffs, random elements, new gear, new NPCs and sidequests and so much more that could change the game in so many fun ways - even if it's just a separate game mode in the main menu if you'd want to keep the vanilla game intact. All of this would make Hellpoint even more special via forcing the player to adapt to new and different rules in the game world.I also believe adding proper mod support with the right tools and Steam Workshop to truly change every aspect of the game to whatever the player would ever want with new locations, enemies, gear and so much more created by the community would elevate Hellpoint to even greater heights and would likely keep me constantly playing non-stop. Making said tools as open as possible would allow the community to really fix the issues I mentioned and didn't even think of too. I would also love to see some more content updates and paid DLC too wink wink nudge nudge Cradle Games and TinyBuild bat eyelash bat eyelash.-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------As you can tell, I absolutely love and adore Hellpoint on so many levels but I do feel it was released before it was finished as there is still quite a bit of work the developers could do to make this diamond in the rough really shine and be hailed as one of the best Souls-likes out there. So yes, it's definitely not for everyone but if those issues I mentioned are something you can deal with and aren't enough to deter you from this gem then I think you will enjoy Hellpoint a ton. It's a game you can really lose yourself in, I know I often do.

_childDocuments_.review: I initially played Hellpoint on PS4 when it released but moved to PC for the DLC because 30 FPS is hard to go back to. It's both incredibly unique and also very obviously derivative by taking a sci-fi, cosmic horror themed story and placing it in a challenging Souls-inspired gameplay loop mixed with an environmental design that calls back to the sense of dread and isolation from the original Dead Space. It has a jank-filled charm and creates a really unique feeling that's difficult to describe. It won't be for everyone, but I absolutely adore Hellpoint.Pros:- Absolutely drenched in atmosphere. Hellpoint has a bleak, surreal, otherworldly futuristic visual style that really gives the game a really awesome immersiveness that I haven't experienced since the original Dark Souls or Dead Space- Fantastic level design that encourages exploration with tons of secrets to be found- A minimalist but very haunting soundtrack- A slower, methodical combat system, again channeling the original Dark Souls feel and (mostly) gets it right- Some really fun boss fightsCons:- Floaty jumping and forced platforming are a terrible mixture- Some bosses are more frustrating than challenging, and some bosses later are reused as normal enemies. - Random sounds not playing during combat- Occasional weird feedback during combat where the only indication you've taken damage is your decreased health- Some input buffering oddities where at times it can feel like you've queued up 2-3 actions instead of one on the next input- Some of the water reflections not only don't match the room, but look like they are stretched from 64x64 resolution even in the highest quality settings. It's the first thing I noticed after starting a new game since you're surrounded by water.Overall I'd give it a 7/10 for a general attempt at an "objective" review, but for me personally it's a 9/10. I love this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Spawn. Die. Repeat. Janky arse game that doesn't respect players, their intelligence, or their time. Hard pass on another sub-par tinyBuild (publisher) release.EDIT (8/12/2021): After being asked by one of the developers (Antishyr) to expound upon my above statements: the controls are janky, often a bit slower then they need to be, imprecise in frustrating ways, and they often just feel...cheap (this is a recurring theme through many of the issues I take with the game). You are as likely to roll/walk/run/jump off a ledge to your (9,436th) death as you are to fave an enemy, and that's WITH the lock-on.The graphics are muddy and uninspired, as is the level design, which seems slipshod and random in (on the portion I have played; maybe the level designs gets better as the game progresses, but I'm not going to bother sinking the time in to find out). Some of the game elements make absolutely no sense: Dark Souls weapons....on a space station? I don't know, maybe the dev's were taking inspiration from the Warhammer 40K universe, but it is jarring and, to again use my favorite word for this review, janky in the context of this game and its setting.The surest sign of a dev not giving to flying farks about player's time (beyond all the general jank of the game) is the respawning of EVERY SINGLE ENEMY every time you die. This is beyond stupid. Like, I thought Sekiro's implementation of respawning enemies was bad, but I'll be a monkey's uncle if it doesn't feel downright restrained compared to Hellpoint.In summation, Hellpoint is a janky game, which provides (at best) a janky experience while doing absolutely nothing to show it respects the people who try and play it. It may appeal to some of the masochist out there with time to burn, but I am not one of those. So, in my subjective opinion, you should value your time more than this game does, and give it a pass.

_childDocuments_.review: Hellpoint has a fairly unique plot and world for the soulsborne genre. The plot is probably the best part of the game as it's a good mix of science and science fiction. It's closer to Resident Evil in the sense of a dystopian yet semi-believable future. It also focuses heavily on platforming and hidden secrets. Although this may make it unique, it does add a lot of frustration.Where the game suffers most is in the combat. Although the weapon variety in the game is quite good, the enemies do not require anything special thought to kill them. In other games you are required to punish certain attack patterns. Hellpoint doesn't really have this. You can mostly get away with pre-emptively attacking smaller enemies or backstabbing larger enemies.  Once you get past the first two bosses the combat stops being interesting.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd recommend it, with some extreme caveats.You should check this game out if:* You're a big fan of Demon's Souls (not Dark Souls 3 to be clear, but the really unrefined first attempt of a souls-like)* You don't mind a game with similar visual fidelity to the original release of Dark Souls 1* You *super* love exploration - this is the game's strongest feature.* You don't mind encounters with somewhat simplistic encounter design.I think I overall experience with Hellpoint was enjoyable - getting the true ending took me roughly 18 hours, and there was likely about 2 or so more hours of content there for me had I done the black hole rooms.  My major caveat is that, as of 8/11/2020, the true final boss is a hard wall of difficulty.  If you aren't using certain builds I'm reasonably sure that your only chance is to rely on extremely lucky RNG.  Ultimately in the end I had to cheat to overcome it, and I've not had to do that with any of the bosses in any of the From Software souls-likes.

_childDocuments_.review: At the time of review, this is my most-played Soulslike not by Fromsoftware. That is quite a place to earn, as I also have Salt and Sanctuary, Code Vein, Pascal's Wager and Jedi Fallen Order. I strongly recommend this game if you enjoy souls-likes, while it doesn't have the level of polish of a AAA game, it makes up for that in being mechanically solid and distinct enough from Dark Souls.The world design is similar in concept to Dark Souls 1, with an interconnected world to explore. Unfortunately, there are loading zones around the world, so it's not the same seamless experience, but the world still feels satisfying to explore. Fast travel is restricted in an interesting way in order to keep you traversing this world, and my advice having beaten the game several times is: explore a lot, and don't think too hard about which checkpoints to enable fast travel on, unless you know for certain one you have already enabled is nearby.The combat is solid, and certainly the best of any Soulslike I have played other than the source material. Mechanically it is most similar to Bloodborne, but lacks the rallying mechanic and so is a little less aggressive. There are some hitbox issues, and the iframes are very low which exaggerates the issue, however if you focus on dodging away from attacks, you should be fine. There is a large variety of melee and ranged weapons, and all of the melee weapons feel unique and different. The ranged weapons are a little lacking in uniqueness, however it looks like this is going to be addressed in a future update. While there are some weapons that seem much more powerful than others, they all have unique skills and/or movesets and stat scaling to help differentiate them.The lore is also quite impressive, all previous Soulslikes I have played borrow heavily from Dark Souls, simply renaming the Undead Curse to something else (for example, the Lost in Code Vein or the Sendrils in Pascal's Wager). In contrast, Hellpoint develops it's own story, but it does so in the same way as a Souls game - through item descriptions, environmental storytelling, and also through messages in the levels.In conclusion, this game is definitely worth a try if you enjoy Souls.

_childDocuments_.review: Just giving a quick thumbs up review to hopefully pull the ratings up from mixed to positive.  This is a great souls-like game set in space with controls much improved over the demo.  I've noticed very few fairly insignificant bugs and certainly none that are game breaking.  This is something I expect on launch day, and honestly there are significantly fewer bugs than in most AAA games with much larger budgets.  The only suggestion I have for improvement is related to the healing system.  You start off with 2 potions (estus-like) which you very slowly refill when hitting monsters (40+ hits to refill each potion).  I just found the first healing potion +1 item, and noticed that after applying the upgrade, the number of potions still goes back down to 2 upon death (i.e. you have to again hit monsters 40+ times to refill the third potion).  Additionally, the potions are not refilled when you go back to the breaches (like campfires in DS).  Given the difficulty of the game (it's on par with DS in my opinion, maybe just slightly easier), I would suggest that the potions get refilled when you go back to the breaches and that your total number of potions get filled up at death.  Whether or not to increase the fill rate is up to debate, but I think increasing it by 25-30% (so 30 hits instead of 40) would help as well while still maintaining a healthy difficulty.Thanks to the devs for this great game.  It really is a blast to play and I'm enjoying it immensely so far.Cheers,H

_childDocuments_.review: For the love of us all, PLEASE FIX THE PLATFORMING.If you're going to have a jump mechanic, make it work.Especially when it comes to invisible platforms (using an in-game item, you can see invisible platforms).Two instances:At one point, I was jumping from invisible tree to invisible tree. These trees are not like the rest that have a flat platform on top. No sir. These trees are insanely easy to fall off of because you have seemingly less surface area to work with, coupled with only being able to see in a flashlight-shape cone in front of you. And of course, the trees are high enough in the air and inconveniently placed enough that whether or not you die from the fall, you have to trek back to them repeatedly. It took more attempts than was fun/interesting. I succeeded, but it sucked.Now the worst offender.At a certain point in the game, you'll find yourself in a decent-sized room, being shot at with giant blasts from two mechs on either side of said room, high above where you seemingly cannot reach them. Well, SPOILER, you can. You run through the room, dodging blasts, as you make your way to one side, where, after a couple jumps, you'll find a "ladder" to climb up to one of the mechs. You need to kill this mech, all the while being shot at by the other mech on the other side of the room. It takes more than a few hits. There are then invisible platforms to jump across while being shot at by the mech across the way. Of course, the platforms are high enough in the air that if you fall, maybe you'll just lose some hp, but it's also very possible you'll die. I've found that performing a dive attack sometimes negates/minimizes fall damage, but it's frustratingly inconsistent.Here's the issue. Not only are you being shot at, but jumping is WILDLY INCONSISTENT. You may RUN and jump, and overshoot. You may WALK and jump, and undershoot. If you get hit by a blast, you may fall, and if not, you'll LITERALLY be pushed to the far right edge of the platform. And I don't mean you'll be pushed when you're hit, I mean AFTER. You'll get hit, start to move, and your character will MAGICALLY warp to the right side of the platform, which just adds to this inconsistent mess and mentally throws you off further. Add to this a brief pause when changing your character's direction from standing still after sprint-jumping (which is an annoying issue on its own), and it is seriously nearly impossible. I've seen a player message on the wall across the way, so at least one person suffered and conquered this rage-inducing jank. Just imagine doing this over and over and over and over and over and over and over and over. Death after death to literally BROKEN MECHANICS.Even if, for this situation, there is a way to kill the mech that shoots homing blasts while you attempt traversing the invisible platforms (like with a ranged weapon I'm not spec'd into), or items in the game I'm unaware of that decrease aggro range or lower/nullify fall damage, the fact remains the platforming is overall atrocious.There are things to enjoy about Hellpoint, and I applaud the effort that was obviously put into this game. The Souls series includes my favorite games of all time, and I'm not referring to a "git gud" situation. An integral game mechanic is broken. It needs attention. I cannot recommend Hellpoint to anyone until the platforming/jumping is fixed.Perhaps allowing us more mid-air control of our character would be a helpful step to a resolution? I don't know; I'm just spitballing.
_childDocuments_.name: Hellpoint

_childDocuments_.review: A really impressive Sci-Fi Soulsborne experience - tiny bit janky in places (whenever I die my character clips through the scenery and then flies off into space rag-dolling furiously), but weirdly these bugs made me fondly remember the days of roll-tossing enemy corpses off cliffs in Dark Souls 1 and helped break the tension of dying for the 15th time.I'm not a huge way in, but already the game gets the fundamental joy of the Soulsborne: exploration and constant reward for progress. I spent most of my play time just wondering an area trying to find all the little items and secrets - I still haven't succeeded in this. And it's great fun. Combat is pleasantly fluid and the dodge mechanic works significantly better than many other 3d entries into this genre, which alone is enough for me to press on.Like many, I am... struggling to fathom why quite so many of the areas contain jumping puzzles when these are NOTORIOUSLY fiddly with this kind of game, BUT I have to credit that at least they help give the areas a real feeling of depth and cavernous space. Tip: if you're struggling, unequip all your armour, that seems to help me massively xDWould have liked to have seen a slightly more varied landscape BUT I can see why they have gone for the aesthetic they have, and it works very well in a lore context and to help the oppressive nature of the game. Really nails the themeOverall, I will definitely be playing more and can solidly recommend to anyone who enjoys Dark Souls 1 especially: you have to be a tiny bit forgiving of odd flaws, but the result is an absolutely enjoyable tumble head-first down the sci-fi rabbit holeP.S. Dear Devs - please: give us some single player/story DLC for this, I want to give you some money since this was gifted to me. _childDocuments_.review: Most Souls-like games do some things well, but fall short on others.While that's also the case here, I'd say Hellpoint is the closest to the "feel" of Dark Souls.Gameplay loop of this game is just Dark Souls. You kill enemies which nets you souls, or AXIOMS in this case. You unlock breaches that act mostly like bonfires. You can rest at them to fill your healthbar, but it will not fill your equipped healing items to maximum. You gain healing items (and energy) by dealing damage and you will respawn with 2 no matter if you have upgraded yours to +5. You need to earn those heals.You need to fast travel or die in order to respawn the enemies.Fast travel works between these breaches, but you need to connect them together in order to use them. Breach synchronizers are items that allow you to do hit. These are limited so you need to think a bit when to use them.Breaches also allow you to level up your character (does not require you to use a Breach Synchronizer) and to Increase or Decrease the difficulty of the game with items.The atmosphere is something closer to the grimness of the first Dead Space gameand Alien. The mood of the Irid Novo space station is fantastic. The soundtrack also relies on ambience and is missing some of the more epic tracks the Souls games have but keeps the tension alive while not being distracting. The Level Designs of this game is phenomenal. So many secret routes that connect different areas together. This is what most Souls-likes miss. The interconnection of different areas makes the world feel well designed. While not everything is connected, and there are loading screens between different areas, the way everything is linked together is so masterfully done, and in some parts it matches (or even surpasses) the source material. While the level design is one thing I praise about the game, budget of the game does affect this in a way. Many of the areas look the same, and while it does make sense (as the game is set on a space station after all), I wonder what wonders the team could have done with more money. There are few areas with different themes, but many places just look like dark corridors without soul. Thankfully the level design more than makes up for it. Other strong aside from Level Desing is the combat. While the animations might look a bit clunky at some points,the feel of your attacks if satisfying and doesn't feel janky at all. Many of the weapons will be quite familiar with anyone who has played other souls-likes, so when you get your hands on them you should feel right at home.Upgrading said weapons requires items, but those are not tied to weapons. You can remove those upgrades and put them to use on other weapons too which encourages trying different weapons and playstyles more.Most of the enemies in Hellpoint are well designed and look nice visually. There are a few that look out of place in my opinion, but other than that no complaints. There is enough variety when you move from different areas to others, and none of the enemies feeloverwhelmingly difficult. While most of the basic enemies are great, the bosses leave a lot to be desired. Many of the first bosses are later reused as enemies and I would classify as mini-bosses more than actual bosses. The "Actual" bosses are more special and I could see them appearing in Dark Souls. They do lack different phases but offer some challenge with their different movesets to dodge around.Just like the father of this style of games, Hellpoint doesn't explain it's story too much. Slightly more than Dark Souls, but most of the lore is up to the player to find and understand. Doing some sidequests also allows for true ending, which is a great way to get people to play your game more than once. There is also a new game+ mode, so you can continue where you left off.There are few things I didn't mention here, but I feel like that's the most important stuff out of the way.I hope more people give this game a change, it's much better than it might look at first glance (many saying it looks clunky).Cradle Games has created a fantastic game and I hope they will continue and make more games like this, since they clearly excel at it.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm having serious difficulties enjoy this game. Though I love the theme of an occult scifi game with a (literally) cosmic horror touch and have had thousands of (successful) hours of other Soulslikes on my track record... I think Hellpoint overdoes it.I cannot claim that I even laid one boss in this game or explored more than Pond + Embassy. And you'd be right by saying that I cannot possibly give this game any justice due to this. But: whereas other games of the same genre will gradually increase the difficulty and give you time to die and learn things step by step, Hellpoint doesn't. Even the tutorial area is already complex enough in layout to fully confuse you with extremely bad lighting choices, has tons of enemies and a prominently patrolling bully tank enemy that one-hits you if you don't constantly backtrack to level up. To get to the next area, you basically alert everything on the entire floor and have your first gangbang you'll likely not survive. Then you return, everything is back but there's also your green shade which spawns on death and pulps you with unlimited stamina as well as perfect knowledge of ALL the moves, stats and skills that your player character had at that point. And it also comes back again if you get killed by it. So even if you grind and level up, it's still better than you at this point of the game.Seriously, come on! This isn't even a difficulty curve, it's an overhanging cliff for crying out loud. I played Dark Souls II in Company of Champions mode all the way without even knowing and it was FINE. Combine this with really janky dodge mechanics and fancy but way too useless lighting if it comes to gameplay and you get a big gloomy mountain of frustration you need to -somehow- beat before even getting to the more interesting parts.And, again, you'd be right by saying that I'm not giving the game justice by not even mentioning the gorgeous architectural and cineastic moments it has. Or the soundscapes. If you've ever played E.Y.E: Divine Cybermancy - it's exactly there and gives you the same kind of awe in concept and flair. But to get there? Enduring all the uneven initial difficulty that doesn't care about ANYTHING that previous game did right? Sorry, no. Even Nethack did better and that's a masochist joke to begin with.TL;DR - the initial difficulty is so ridiculous at this stage that I'm about to get a refund. There's imho more rewarding games out there considering. Even if you enjoy a bit of masochism in your action adventures.

_childDocuments_.review: Full disclosure, I have not beaten this game yet, but after 9 hours of playing, there are a lot of glaringly obvious things about this game. Hellpoint is an absolute mess. TL;DR: Decent combat, lackluster bosses, some of the worst map designs I've ever seen in a Souls-like (maybe even a paid game in general), a slew of bugs, and incredibly poorly utilized mechanics that only aid to muddy the game's decent core mechanics. I'm a huge fan of souls likes, and I've played quite a few that left me in awe, and even more that left me with an awful taste in my mouth. Hellpoint falls somewhere right inbetween both of those categories. The graphics aren't anything special, yet on my 2080 and i9, it still makes my computer run almost as hot as Cybeprunk. The frames also manage to drop from. Considering the graphics that often look like a game from 2015, this shows a lot about the lack of optimization. That category definitely doesn't win it any favors. The combat, being a souls like, is definitely something of import. All in all...it's eh. Initially, it felt really great hitting the first enemies you're shown, as the sounds were punchy and satisfying. That, sadly, didn't last, largely thanks to one of the most frequent bugs throughout this game. I'll get more into it later, but put quickly for this, you often don't hear anything when hitting enemies later in the game. Weapons stop making noise on impact. The combat really comes to a crawl when fighting bosses, however, and this is where the game seemingly falters the most. Many amateur takes on Souls-likes struggle with creative bosses that have a balance between difficulty and diversity. Hellpoint dropped the ball entirely and decided to just make bosses kill you in 3 hits regardless of stats and armor. There is seemingly no balance between good and bad bosses in this game. Some you can literally circle around endlessly while they just attack where you were several seconds ago, and others will attack without end until you get hit once, and you're then chain stunned to death. The bosses go from low tier sponges to god tier enemies on a whim, and never is it because of creative design. If a boss is hard, it's because it will 1, 2 or 3 shot you regardless of how far ahead you are. It's not satisfying to overcome the bosses in this game because they're just so mindless. It's not skill that ends up beating them, and when you do, the rewards are always lacking. Map design. Souls-likes are notorious for having relatively complex maps with branching paths to make sure you explore everything, lest you miss out on important loot. The developers behind this, sadly, held an ambition leagues above their capabilities. Never in my days have I seen more complicated maps. Rarely do I find myself lost in a game after passing through the same area three times, but with Hellpoint I found myself hoping to stumble onto success after looping back through the very samey corridors of the station. This would likely not be so much of an issue if a Dark Souls style teleportation system was in place, but one of the peak examples of this game's eagerness to stand apart was taking the worst part of Dark Souls 1 and then making it even worse.  You need a single use item to allow 'bonfires' to function as teleportable waypoints. "Breaches" take the place of bonfines, and you need an item to turn each Breach into a point that you can teleport TO and FROM. This would be less of an issue if the map design wasn't so horribly sloppy. I've come across 15 breaches, and after very, very indepth exploration, 6 items for connecting those breaches. This means I can teleport to 6 of those 15 breaches. I have almost no access to anywhere on the map. Now ideally, you'd think that you could strategically choose these breaches. Sadly, you'd be wrong in this. The game will put two breaches almost directly beside each other, often separated by a mere elevator. It seems almost random how these breaches are placed, and it's baffling to think that they'd place them so poorly with maps designed so terribly. To finish, the map design of Hellpoint would be much like a visualization of Metal Gear Solid's plot using only arrows. Bugs. Oh bugs. The most annoying bug that happened for about 7 of my 9 hours playing came in the form of audio glitches. Elevators will make ear piercing screeches while cutting in and out completely, some armor sets don't make sounds while you're sprinting, some maps remove weapon sounds all together, and of course, sometimes the audio just cuts out. I truly cannot believe that this game isn't early access. A more pressing issue, in terms of playing the game, is how you can find yourself falling forever on flat items. Land wrong on a piece of nearly flat rubble and, uh oh, you're not stuck free falling in place. I waited a total of 7 minutes falling on one piece of rubble and, be it through luck or me mashing buttons, managed to escape. The second time I got stuck on a ledge (that I NEEDED to go up to progress) I wasn't so lucky, and had to manually shut down the game. You can't access the pause menu while falling, so it was an Alt+F4 moment. For a game with positive reviews that managed to leave early access, I'm genuinely befuddled that so many people are okay with these issues. A quick google search assures me I'm not the only one, yet apparently I'm one of few to take a real issue with it. In conclusion, between the droves of audio bugs, never ending awful map design, and god awful bosses, this is truly an amateur souls like. If this game were early access, I think it'd be a middling "Maybe", but with it not being such...this is a hard pass for anyone intending to spend money. It's commendable that the developer tried so hard to be original, but as is so often the case, struggling to hard leads to an absolute mess clinging to a fleeting idea of creative genius. This game being as small as it is also makes finding out information on the very, VERY cryptic elements within often impossible to find. There are a slew of mechanics never explained at all, and no matter what I searched, I couldn't find anything on it. Found some codes for free weapons though, so that was nice. This isn't an awful game for 10$, MAYBE 15$, but it's just so poorly polished that it's hard to claim the developer really loved their creation. When the audio is cutting out more often than it's on, that's a serious issue. When 5 bosses I encountered all became normal enemies to save on creating other enemies, that's an issue too. Reusing a few is fine, but every boss I've encountered thus far when I'm supposedly only 30% through the game? That doesn't bode well for the future. This game cuts a lot of corners, often cutting off crucial components of good games with it. Buyer beware, but if you still choose to go with this game anyways, I wish you luck.

_childDocuments_.review: Short Summary: Made by a group of 11(!) people, Hellpoint is a wonderful game, and as someone who played the soulsborne games for thousands upon thousands of hours, I can holeheartedly recommend it to anyone familiar with the genre.PROS:-Probably the most awesome ladders in any game I've ever played.-Fluid and satisfying combat (just like combat in Dark Souls 1, just a bit faster paced)-HUGE interconnected map (just like Dark Souls 1) with an almost endless number of fake walls and hidden things to find and actually good platforming.-Almost perfect difficulty, not too hard and almost never unfair but still can sweat even veterans of the genre (exceptions listed in cons)-Interesting and cool enemy designs with competent AI (although you can still trick NPCs to roll into falls)-Fantastic fashion and extremely varied and cool weapon designs, none of them being terrible for combat. Weapons also get passive and active abilties, all of them different ones, if you use them for a long enough time (not that long).-Very unique game mechanics with the blackhole and the clock which are a bit difficult to understand but once you do it changes your view of the game completely.-Splitscreen and online co-op just like in Dark Souls: summon,invade,duel. (didn't work at release but fully functional now in my experience)CONS:-(MAJOR SPOILER) The bigest fault of this game to me is , which I really hope is not intended because it literally stunlocks the player to death if not dogded perfectly (I had 20 vitality + Deamon Scythe passive health bonus). This to me is the biggest stain on the game's difficulty which is otherwise impressively well done.-Enemy variety is a bit lacking but hey this is still an indie game-There are still some minor bugs and glitches that don't impact the gameplay but still could use some fixing. Most notable bugs at the time of playing: some missing textures/voice lines, enemies sometimes start spining in place when you engage them which is quite funny, killboxes when falling are missing in some places.-Environments can get a dit dull with mostly everything being grayish metal panels but yeah this is still a indie game

_childDocuments_.review: Setting is a personal favorite of mine along with the general aesthetic, combat feels nice and chunky, level progression and secrets feel good and cryptic much the Soulsbourne series, and the no-nonsense aspects of online cooperative play are choice. A few glitches here and there, but it's to be expected. Overall, it's a game I enjoyed more than a lot of games I've played in recent years. I don't talk up too many games anymore. I recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Hellpoint

_childDocuments_.review: What if Dark Souls was in space, but the combat was twice as clunky, the dungeons half as inspired, and had awkward platforming and pacing sprinkled on top?Well, than you'd have this game.  It tries very hard to be Dark Souls, and comes close, but just can't quite figure out what made the original so good.  Which is a shame, because the game has real potential and some decent visuals.I hope it gets better.  But right now, I'd say give this game a little bit of time to breathe before picking it up.
_childDocuments_.name: Hellpoint

_childDocuments_.review: It's got a fantastic horror aesthetic and nice setpieces which for me is at least 50% of the joy of the soulslike genre. You'll explore a weird derelict space station full of undead aberrations and synthetics. The combat is solid but nothing special. The writing isn't very well translated but who plays soulslike games for the writing? I like it and I'll probably play it till the end, which is more than I can say for most games in 2020. Buy it if you like Souls clones, avoid it if you don't.
_childDocuments_.name: Hellpoint

_childDocuments_.review: The game look great and consists of several interesting mechanics that differs from other souls-like game. Exploration is and can be a bit dreadful, dark and eerie, and backtracking can be confusing, it still satisfying to progress through.My few complaints would be the limited weapon pool and enemy ai. Some enemies will just jump off a cliff and die, as bosses will do the same. In the Arisen Congregators boss fight, one of them just disappeared after their attack animation finished, and fighting Ozy on a second attempt somewhat caused him to not attack all. He constantly dodged and never hurt me, only walked up to hug me, such a sweetie.
_childDocuments_.name: Hellpoint

_childDocuments_.review: This game could be decent, but like all games of this type the camera issues will drive you crazy. There are constantly mobs above/below you and the camera locks can only go up/down 15 degrees, so you'll be staring at feet or heads of mobs and not much else. The constant jump puzzles and cliffs also take away from the game. I don't want to spend 5 minutes wondering if I can jump a gap, or having to run back to my body if I try and fail. Just too much annoyance, not enough fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Hellpoint

_childDocuments_.review: The learning curve is steep, and the game is not easy; but don't let that discourage you. The world building and content of this game are amazing! It is absolutely worth every penny. Game play continues to challenge you throughout the levels, and the open style of the game is super great. Don't expect too much for multiplayer, but if you use it - it can be fun. For game support, there is a wiki. Granted, the wiki kinda sucks and is missing like 90% of the content of the game. So basically, there isn't too much help outside the game. Overall:Combat: 4.5/5Content: 4/5World: 5/5Graphics: 3/5 (some leaks in world)Wiki: 2/5This is game is worth your time and I would buy it again! Hours of great game play, and plenty of ways to chose your own path.

_childDocuments_.review: if you like the original dark souls and have a knack for horror sci-fi, can't really make a mistake with hellpoint. being a kinda indie game, it's obviously a little janky and unbalanced at times (for example shields seem like a trap right now because of their high stamina cost compared to dodging and ranged weapon in the off-hand) but overall it's a very interesting and lengthy experience, complete with obscure item descriptions, loads of secrets and hidden items and intimidating bosses. 5/7 perfect score.
_childDocuments_.name: Hellpoint

_childDocuments_.review: honestly?it's one of the best non-fromsoft souls likes in the regard that it feels a lot like dark souls 1 or demon souls. it's clunky, it has a bunch of little mysteries, the balance is wonky and there's clearly some loadouts that surpass others but. it has so much charm, it has a lot of neat worldbuilding, and the environment is gorgeous.is it a good game? yeah honestly i'd say so. is it a game most people would enjoy? no, but neither was demon souls. if you really like souls-likes, i think give it a try without comparing it to others and you'll have a fresh and unique experience, if sometimes frustrating.if you aren't super in to souls-likes but you're into games you really gotta struggle through, you'll also probably have a good time - the game is punishing and almost unfair at times, but there are ways gear-wise to make it easier, and if you explore (or get a co-op partner) you'll find a way through almost any gate that tries to block you.tl;dr: lacks polish and has clear issues (with both balance, bugs, and gameplay decisions), but so did dark souls and everyone praises that game. it feels genuine and unique, and it's worth giving it a shot if you want that sense of mystery and difficulty that pioneered souls-like games.
_childDocuments_.name: Hellpoint

_childDocuments_.review: Just a first impressions for those wanting an opinion.So far it's running flawlessly on my laptop, it feels and controls largely similar to the demo you can find on steam (and console storefronts) I personally think the combat and movement is completely serviceable for this type of game playing this back to back with immortal unchained and this feels a lot better to control. Visuals are really decent for an indie game with nice art direction, have encountered some slight bugs with sound being too quiet in terms of running feels like demon souls hollow form quiet. Soundtrack is nice nothing special. Fought first boss and destroyed it with ma stabby stab dagger no probs. Games level design is rather labyrinthian in scale but this is more thought out and interesting than code vein where it was just corridors in some places.TLDR basically if you liked the demo you'll love this, it's clearly made with the fraction of a budget most souls like games have and it does it surprisingly well. I'm happy to have paid the price if the game maintains this level of fun

_childDocuments_.review: There is a lot of potential here that ultimately falls flat.The setting/atmosphere is cool, and the combat isn't bad. The mechanic of refilling your healing item by dealing damage similar to Bloodborne is nice, but that's about where the good ends.Animations are clunky, which causes some enemies and the player to glitch and get stuck in terrain.Movement (especially jumping) is imprecise and will sometimes leave the player immobile for a few seconds.The UI is very slow. Interacting with terminals is a pain since backing out of anything takes you to the start of a menu, rather than simply back one step. Dialogue in game feels like it requires multiple presses of the input before it's actually registered.Enemy and checkpoint placement is not great.Overall, if you can push through the technical problems and stick with it, you may like Dark Souls In Space.For me, there was just too much bad to outweigh the good.
