_childDocuments_.review: The eye divine cybermancy of soul’s like’s, keeps coming to mind now i finished my first run through. It's just as deeply flawed, overly ambitious but has atmosphere, gets enough gameplay right and you can tell it's been made with heart that i really enjoyed it despite itself.It's story is solid and told throughout with a nice mix of exposition and environmental details that felt a good balance of being explicit with what's going on but also telling it with different characters so you got some flavour to what's happened. Dealing with a neat mix of theme’s so it's not just a re-hashed doom demons in space story once you get into it. Topping of with a neat ‘true’ boss that ties up the story, themes and game systems.Combat wise it's let down by a lack of variety in enemies, you get like 3 or 4 per the 3 different archetypes linked to the story. With multiple also being palette swapped for bosses with little difference other than bigger numbers and mode, including the same movesets. For the most part they are fun to fight, with a handful of hit boxes feeling inconsistent or unfair, or some attacks feeling overtuned. But enough that felt right that I still enjoyed the combat, with plenty of options of weapons and types to use.The levels I'm conflicted on. Overall they have the sort of interconnectivity, hidden off shoots and spots to explore that give me vibes of demon souls and dark souls 1. Loads to explore and see, but the quality of the places to explore is a bit hit and miss. Some zones feel tightly designed and have a good pace to explore through, then you take a turn and it can end up a bit barren and sparse, but in an unfinished sort of feel rather than what feels intentional? Like there's a zone with a large park in it, but it's mostly barren and has the same creature 10 times followed by a large barren road with nothing at either end, followed by a large building with one fight followed by multiple large rooms with nothing apart from some text and a location for a npc if you deal with them. But then at the other end a zone called the arisen dominion, it's fantastic, visually and the spaces you explore in it, fantastic, top to bottom, just enough things to fight throughout that's tense when first exploring. Multiple points whilst exploring it just stoped and though ‘man that looks cool’. When they nail it, they nail it really well, but when they don't, levels never felt broken just like stuffs missing.Visually, it's not gonna win awards for technical prowess. Even with settings maxed, some textures are a bit interesting and the lighting has that flat unity light engine look to, it's fine but never great. But what I found great is it's art direction. It reminds me of Blame and other works by Tsutomu Nihei. That far future stark dark concrete and steel brutalsium, it's not pretty but at times striking. And this game at times captures that feeling at it's best moments. The main character and several npc’s even have that far future transhumanism look very reminiscent of niheis work. Some people are gonna hate it, but if you can put up with dark future sci-fi corridors, they have some serviceable ones and some really good ones with what they could do.Systems wise, it's a darks souls mostly. You got your not-future-souls currency to spend on stats to boost health, damage weapons usage ect. That you can lose on death, save them from your corpse or lose them on death before collecting. The fairly standard solid system. It's bonfire equivalent with it's spin on it having a consumable allowing it to become a stop to teleport to other bonfires that have also been connected with the consumable. Also you can raise or lower the new game plus stats of the world with consumables at the bonfires, that's a cool idea. For the most part it's nothing new but solid with some new ideas here and there.It's also a bit janky bug wise. Audio levels would peak and blow out on foot steps. Corpses would play audio constantly when dead. Menu ui selection would flicker, sometimes select, sometimes not. Enemy ai would spin on the spot looking very daft at times when trying to track you behind a pillar. Ragdoll on deaths can sometimes be very funny, multiple of my deaths or kills just seeing a body crumple into a jittering ragdoll mess as if stuck in geometry. Mostly not game braking, but noticeable in that janky unpolished sort of way. I did have one full unity engine crash to desktop, fortunately with no progress loss. But other than that one crash I never had anything game breaking.This isn't a great game, it's got a bunch of flaws. But I really like it, it's got heart. It feels like this was a first attempt and I want to see what a second try would be like. They tried and got a bunch of stuff right with some cool ideas and art direction.

_childDocuments_.review: This was a pleasant surprise, that came at the exact right time for me.I just played (and reviewed) a soulslike that ended up being the quickest a soulslike (or perhaps, any game for that matter) made me feel it wasn't worth my time. So I'm going to do something different in this review, list the major things I felt were wrong with that other game, and how these DON'T apply to Hellpoint.In order of least to most severe (for me) these points were:4. The game was trying so hard to be Dark Souls that it didn’t have it’s own identity, and yet…3. it managed to fail completely at creating the experience you hope for in a soulslike.2. It was loaded with artificial difficulty, the bosses I fought were only difficult because of their large health pools, and because...1. the combat was extremely sluggish and unresponsive.Hellpoint, on the other hand, is incredibly unique aesthetically; it's scifi, but that kind of far future scifi where things are almost (but importantly, not quite) magic. It also has a few unique mechanics, rather than naming them all I'll just mentioned my favourite; your healing items gradually restore as you deal melee damage. This is a small change that quite drastically changes the way you play in an interesting way, as the lower you get on healing items, the more you're actually encouraged to play aggressively (somewhat like the newer DOOM games). Yet despite managing to be unique, it absolutely nails the feeling you'd hope for in a soulslike, in fact I'd go beyond that and say it actually feels like closer to an actual soulsborne game than any other souslike I've played; sure the lore isn't as deep, and (as I'll get to in a minute) the environments are built different, but it absolutely nails the atmosphere and the feeling of the gameplay itself.I also don't think there was any artificial difficulty in this game; it absolutely gets right that feeling a soulslike should have, where you might describe the combat is tough but fair, and that if you're struggling it's because you (or your character) need to improve. In other words it doesn't feel like the game is 'too hard', it feels like you haven't yet mastered it. Most of all though, I don't think anyone could describe the combat in Hellpoint as sluggish or unresponsive with a straight face, it is perfectly responsive and gloriously fast paced.Don't get me wrong, I wouldn't say Hellpoint is perfect but any negatives I could list are basically nitpicks in the grand scheme of things, and pretty much all of them are a matter of personal preference. For example, my opinion on soulslike environments is that they should somewhat mirror the combat, you enter an area and it seems impossible to learn (in the same way a boss might seem impossibly to beat), but by the end of the game it's hard to even remember a time where these seemed that overwhelming. Hellpoint however is just an outright maze from start to finish, I'm fairly confident if I jumped back into NG+ right now I'd still get lost in the majority of areas.I also found the difficulty a bit weird, progressing through the actual levels was almost exactly the level of difficulty you'd expect, but then the majority of the bosses were quite easy for a soulslike. Then if you attempt to go for the true ending of the game, the true final boss amps up the difficulty to insane levels; I actually think I might literally have died more to that boss than all the other bosses in the game combined (and also once you start the battle, you're locked in to it, so no heading out to improve equipment or farm some levels).There's a few other small things here and then, minor glitches and that sort of thing, but again I think these are all nitpicks. At the end of the day, I thoroughly enjoyed Hellpoint and can easily imagine myself playing through NG+ in the near future.

_childDocuments_.review: Only buy it if it's on sale and you don't care about the bugged achievements.Despite having many many problems and bugs and typos, it's a very fun game.The multiplayer features suck and barely anyone plays the game. There are 4 endings and you are forced to play the game at least 3 times to get all the endings (unless, like me, you back up your save games and edit the files). Everything is a mystery and nothing is explained so you'll spend lots of time googling around.There's an achievements that's meant to be unlocked only by googling it and using a controller (not keyboard) and took me forever to unlock it. I was also only able to unlock the "coins" achievement by cheating because who has that kind of time to find all the coins.I also don't like the fact that there's a dlc coming when there are so many bugs and problems to fix instead.In short, it's full of problems and bugs but it will give you a lot of hours of fun.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game but it's a little too janky.It was really really weird that the controls are explained in the hub area AFTER the first boss and it doesn't even teach you the basics,I only found out there is a parry in the game from a google search and I never managed to do a shield bash. The jank is okay in early game,most bosses don't demand any skill tbh but as soon as you need to do those precise rolls you realize that hitboxes and iframes just don't function and the game is intentionally hiding any sort of help from you (such as healing upgrades and the cube modules,which I again had to find out about in a search). I understand some people would phrase that as "encourages exploration" for me it's tedius and unfun coupled with a system that doesn't quite work. Good game idea, fun for an hour or two and then it becomes annoying more than anything else, play something else in my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: The setting and overall environment for this game is amazing. I love games that are not afraid to explore the occult and experiment with demonology. The camera in this game feels very unpolished. There are times where your camera will struggle to adjust to moving around the environment and with how fast-paced the boss fights are, this is a massive issue. The balancing for different builds is not the greatest. Through personal experimentation and reading experiences of other players online, there are some builds that are objectively better than others. Also some builds are completely unusable. The biggest gripe I have with this is that I love heavy strength weapons but in this game, there's no use in using them. In most souls-like games, the heavier weapons stagger opponents or deal significantly higher damage and while those elements are present in this game, they are extremely nerfed, making it nearly impossible to use those weapons.If you have motion sickness, I HIGHLY do not recommend playing this game. There is a debuff that a boss gives that causes the camera to zoom in and out in a nauseating manner. The problem being that this boss is bugged and this debuff will not go away, even after dying. The only fix I could find online is to save, quit to main menu, and load back in. Occasionally, this fix would still not remove the debuff, meaning my save-file was plagued with it, even HOURS after beating said boss.With a souls-like game, one of the biggest things that you have to get right would be hit-boxes. This game has some very, very wonky issues with hit boxes. Some bosses are able to shoot through walls, some enemies will ignore being hit, and sometimes their attacks that very obviously hit your character, don't do any damage. Overall, this game is something I want to love but it feels like there is too much holding it back from being something I look forward to diving into. I'm extremely disappointed because the premise, environment, and story is amazing but the game itself leaves a lot to be desired. Pick it up on a sale but definitely don't pay full price.

_childDocuments_.review: - Atmosphere- Sound Design- Combat- Boss Design- Exploration (There are secrets and secrets within those secrets)- At the time of this review optimization is great and the game runs smoothly- Enemy types are repetitive (Early game at least)- Enemy AI is easy to exploit and overcome (As far as early game mobs go)- Too many pitfalls in overly dark areas (Bad game design in my opinion)- Some environmental pop-in here and there- Speech audio bugs out sometimesOverall enjoying the game so far. Feels like a Dark Souls 1 level of clunky when it comes to movement and combat, which is acceptable. Don't be expecting Dark Souls 3 level of fluidity in player movement. Boss designs are cool so far. Music and sound design are superb. Graphically the game looks great, it's no jaw dropper by any means but they are nice to look at aesthetically, but if you're buying a game solely on graphics then you're playing the wrong game here. As for what I've played so far, it looks like the story will mostly be weaved into pieces of lore found throughout the world, which is fine. I'm not here for the story, I'm here to immerse myself in this dark, spooky world with creepy space monsters. This space station is pretty large too, so be prepared to get lost and explore, which is another thing this game has a lot of.As a Kickstarter backer who has been here since the beginning, I'm happy with the final product. The developers are and have always been open to constructive criticism, and only work to continue improving on the existing product.

_childDocuments_.review: Very charming Souls-like in Spaaaaace! The atmosphere is really on point and the game looks appropriately future-spacey and derelict at the same time. I might like this more than the actual Souls series of games (this is not saying it's higher quality).One of the few Souls-likes that actually feels fair, in the players favour. I just wish there was a series of primers in-game on the Underworld (not even sure that's the cannon name for it).
_childDocuments_.name: Hellpoint

_childDocuments_.review: This is a brilliant game. It scratches that souls-like itch very well while adding verticality its own personality. The highlight for me was the labyrinthine level design that left me feeling truly lost many times. With multiple paths available at any time and a beautiful world to explore I'd definitely recommend this to fans of difficult games.In terms of difficulty it was very reasonable aside from a spike with an end boss that I was not a fan of. From what I read I did encounter the hardest version of this boss but it very much frustrated me having to fight someone in melee while being hammered by long ranged attacks that had the potential to one shot me at times. While that end boss has left a minor sour taste in my mouth it pales compared to what the rest of the game has to offer in its immersive well designed world and reliable combat. Highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Hellpoint

_childDocuments_.review: A sci-fi souls-like that takes most of that souls-likeness from the first Dark Souls; areas are extremely interconnected with many shortcuts to find and exploration to do, and since the bonfire equivalents don't allow fast travel between them until an item has been consumed, you'll be doing a fair bit of exploring. For me this was a point very much in the games favour, encouraging me to become very familiar with the world and find every hidden thing it had to offer, but allowing the convenience of fast travel once it had been earned. There are a few bugs, and it is janky in parts, but if you enjoyed Dark Souls 1, you'll likely have a good time with this.
_childDocuments_.name: Hellpoint

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed the game. I was on a souls like kick and played NIOH, Code Vein, The Surge 2, Mortal Shell and this back to back and I was surprised at how good the game was. If you enjoy Dark Souls, you will enjoy this. I actually thought this was a better value than Mortal shell considering the length of both games.
_childDocuments_.name: Hellpoint

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who didn't even care for Dark Souls when it came out, or any of its sequels, after I started playing this game i just couldn't stop  I had to know what else there was, what was next, what I could find, and there's SO many secrets.It plays very smooth, I've only run into a couple render glitches, but a quick reload solved that. The controls are easy to learn, tricky to master, and so satisfying when you do.
_childDocuments_.name: Hellpoint

_childDocuments_.review: This is a scifi horror souls like. The problem with souls-like games, is that players are always extra critical when it comes to the mechanics of the game compared to Dark Souls. and you see it in some of the negative reviews for this game. This game isn't Dark Souls and if you're expecting a Dark Souls clone, download a DS mod instead. Hellpoint is it's own game. has its own charm. yes a lot of the mechanics are similar to dark souls but the gameplay has its own identity. combat is not even that clunky, similar to The Surge. The Music is awesome, sound effects are cool. This is a good game!
_childDocuments_.name: Hellpoint

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game to play with a friend and honestly I'm so disappointed. We played it for an hour and had a decent time so we bought the dlc as well because we thought it was going to be a fun game, boy were we wrong. The difficult ramped up quickly and with the jank controls that already felt awful it was almost impossible to feel like I was having fun. I like souls-like games, I love dark souls it's one of my favorite series but this kind of difficulty is just awful. The atmosphere and environment are great and it tells an interesting story but it's ruined by it's jank af horrible gameplay. The enemies do either too much or too little against you and have horrendous movesets that are sometimes undodgeable early game. Honestly I'm so sad I couldn't enjoy this game. I'd give this a 4/10 for lore and setting but horrible everything else. Worth about 5 dollars if you're willing to fight through the jank I respect it but that's not worth it in my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: A synthesis of Event Horizon and Dark Souls with less emphasis on brutal difficulty (souls-lite?). Despite its buggy and sometimes labyrinthine level design, it has the same fun and quick-thinking combat as its inspiration, and will keep you engaged, if not necessarily challenged. Great 'starter' game for getting into the genre, or just something to tide you over till Elden Ring comes out.
_childDocuments_.name: Hellpoint

_childDocuments_.review: It had some problems and bugs in Co-op at its launch, but must of them were fixed a few days later. I really liked the trist, dark atmosphere (especially the ambient music) and the overall setting of the game as well as the - in its functionality - better made co-op experience compared to Dark Souls. We didn't find all of the hidden things, but it was a fun searching for them as the space station is like a mostly very logical labyrinth of sorts.A little tip for immersion: If you arrive at the hub (you will recognize it) then better take the big elevator down to the Arcology instead of going to Port Issoudun if you managed to find the key. It will be a much better experience lore- and immersion-wise. My friend and myself found out really late that we totally mixed up the whole experience by accident. Interesting that this is even possible though.If you want a straight path to follow or a non-cryptic storyline, then better don't get it at all. The game's price is fine in my opinion, but you may better wait for a lesser or major discount if you're not sure about it.

_childDocuments_.review: Good quality/price ratio and best souls like game in the market. This game don't just put a green endurance gauge with dodge mechanic and calls it a souls like. It's more than that, an interesting world to discover. Exploration, item description is what you need to understand just like a souls game, good job. But it's also have a lot of downside.The good:-Combat is good-Using weapons to unlock their skills + upgrade "mod" to level up your weapons is nice. And you can switch your powerfull mod to another weapon if you want to change.-Immersive and interesting world, I love sci-fi and dark souls so having both is a little paradise for me.-Exploration, you have hidden wall just like a souls games-level design, doesn't feel linear. I have the impression I can choose where I want to go + different path to go there. It can even be confusing sometime as you don't necessary need some key item to access some part of the map depending on your path.-crazy ragdoll, yes for me it's good, it made me laugh a lot lol. Ennemies that start doing break dance when they die can be funny.The bad the ugly:-Maps are too similar-Ennemy variety, you will kill the same things over and over again-Invisible wall, invincible ennemy sometimes when they are stuck-stamina too low, sometimes you just don't have enough stamina to dodge and the investment in it cost too much., some ennemies will unleash so many attack you can't dodge all of them. At higher difficuties I'm sure It's a one shot.-no parry, why ? With this low stamina that punish dodge, parry would have been perfect.-stats doesn't scale very well imo, it's basically useless in your first playthrough, you just want the minimum to equip your weapon but it start scaling when your weapon is fully upgrade. Most player would just finish the game and quit before starting a true build.-Elemental are very unbalance, everything is bad except one.-The stunlock is crazy sometimes, you can't do anything and you will die if you have 2 ennemies that block you. You can't roll past an ennemy and it's frutrating. Never fight against a wall, it's your worst ennemy with gravity.-Limitation on teleportation, you have item to use and it will decide if your "bonfire" will have the teleportation or not. It's just a way to force backtracking and add play time, I lost a TON of time roaming around because of that.Despite all he downside, the global experience is great but it really feels unpolish at times.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is what I would call endearingly janky.  It has some frustrating platforming, but absolutely nails the atmosphere, build versatility, exploration, challenge, and ambiguity that make the souls-like genre great.  Definitely the best souls-like that I've played outside of being developed by FromSoft, and it's refreshing to be in a Hellraiser-esque sci-fi world.
_childDocuments_.name: Hellpoint

_childDocuments_.review: It needs a bit of polish but I think it does what it sets out to do. It's a solid souls-like and adds some of it's own ideas. I hope people that like the genre don't overlook it, there is enough here to scratch that itch and the potential to become even better. The combat is what you would expect, different melee weapons (that each gradually unlocks passive and active skills as you use them), "spells", ranged weapons, armors, etc. Manage stamina/ block/ dodge/ hit, etc. It works pretty well, normal enemies even 5 hours in are a bit too easy though, personally I'd rather there were fewer but stronger enemies, but that's personal preference.There is a lot of exploration to do, maps are rather intricate with a lot of secrets and shortcuts to findThe environments could be more varied, but there is so much you can do in a spaceship and at least the atmosphere is good.I can't comment much on build variety and balance because I haven't played enough yet, but there seem to be enough moving parts in regards to stats, abilities and equipment to support several different playstyles. Then again, we'll see.Things that I think should be polished/ improved: There are some objects without collision, some weapon movesets feel a bit janky, some bosses need better sounds and visual effects when they hit you, they can feel like they don't have impact even when they smack you for half your health. Will update if my feelings change as I play it further, but atm I think it is worth playing.

_childDocuments_.review: So, I picked up this game almost at random and thought about it approximately not at all for months. I only picked it up a few days ago and found a game that was a passably enjoyable Souls-like, with a decent enough story, a solid enough art style, and some fun mechanics and gimmicks, with tight combat and characters I did have interest in. but one that slowly wore its welcome from me accepting it with open arms to "I'll probably finish it and never play it again". Above average for an indie soulslike but only a little better than mid overall.As the fact that: most bosses were bigger versions of normal enemies with an extra attack or two, which was especially apparent when I went even slightly out of order and ran up on bosses I had already seen the enemy designs for, areas had load screens between them, some areas have screwy geometry, near the arena tower in the Sohn district has a ledge you can drop onto that looks like there should be something there but there's no way to return from, and the walls of the outside of the temple I would get consistently stuck on, an invisible wall or two and other assorted jankiness. also I really just, personal preference, didn't like the fact that an AI ghost of your character spawns on where your souls dropped.All became apparentI was still enjoying it, especially as it it had that feel of clearly being a game the developers cared about, but I couldn't recommend it to anyone who wasn't already very versed in the souls-likes already out. Out of the people who were watching me stream on discord and the people who owned the game, I was probably the only one willing to finish, but I found it honestly pretty enjoyable despite the intense jank, and sometimes even funny because of it. This was the limit of my review until someone watching me who had the game and was more down on it asked if I wanted to make a new character and just run the game as best we could together, see if it was more fun that way....I am now a massive fan of this game, not just out of "jank is more fun together" but because the multiplayer experience is outright *phenomenal*. Compared to your usual soulslike, this game's ease of co-op is unheard of, but it even stands out as easy to use across the entire indie market, You just have a code for your play session in your multiplayer menu, you share it, your friend heads into the multiplayer menu, hits join match and inputs it while you're connected.They can connect to you and join your game from pretty much any point in the game, wherever they are and wherever you are.You don't HAVE to set yourself to be invaded if it's just you and a pal playing.Both players can pick items up, and both players get a copy. P1 is the only one who gets key items, however.The netcode is more than enough to get the job done, I haven't once questioned getting hit and we've only had DC issues once in the 16+ hours we've played so far.You can change areas with your partner, no being cordoned off to x section of the mapYour visiting partner goes down? you can revive them where they died for half your total health pool, you go down? they don't get ejected, they teleport back to the most recent rift or area change with you.Also it has local co-op and steam remote play together just in case you needed that as well or your friend doesn't want to buy it themselves.Just the sheer simplicity and friendliness to the multiplayer experience changed this from a solid mid game I'd wait to see if there was a sequel to, and recommend, but only if you were a person into Souls-likes who was done with Fromsoft's offerings alongside the Nioh 2s and maybe even Code Veins in quality (or was SPECIFICALLY looking for something more akin to Demon's Souls), to a game I can honestly recommend a playthrough to anyone who enjoys action games and has someone to play a game with, that I genuinely can't wait for the DLC for.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to recommend this game, but currently it has so many bugs, some of which are game-breaking, that I could not recommend it currently. The gameplay is fun, and the world is interesting and well designed. Probably the only major complaint aside from the bugs is that all the enemies are hit point sponges. You are not rewarded for skillful attacks so much as just never ending patience. This game has a lot going for it, but when a 12 hour save gets bricked because the final boss fight bugs out, right after several other bugs that I just accepted and overcame.....Nah man, wait for them to fix these things before buying.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic gameplay, interesting aesthetic and design, flipping incredible co-op.The game has a few bugs but nothing game-breaking. A lot of the levels suffer from being too enclosed and maze-like but there's only one level where it's truly a problem. I would have liked to see more variation in the 'magic' and guns but I appreciate that you have a version for every damage type nonetheless. The stats and debuffs aren't explained very well or at all sometimes but a quick google search will fix that. I wish the quests were a little less souls-like to be honest but there are only a few, the rewards are mostly cosmetic and the game overall is very short if you end up missing something.The co-op was incredibly fun, way better than anything fromSoftware has offered. Any item/equipment that you or a friend pick up while playing together gets awarded to both of you which is absolutely fantastic. This includes boss items but unfortunately you can only talk to the npc who turns them into boss weapons in your own game which is the only flaw with that.... There's also a split-screen option though it would be nice to be able to swap between vertical and horizontal since larger weapons can block the screen. I truly believe that the only thing this game is really missing at the moment is a little bit of polish and I'm very excited to see more content in the new dlc. Fantastic souls-like, 10/10, just want more.

_childDocuments_.review: **This game is a Hard sell, Had to retype after some more gameplay**Tl;DR: This game feels early access, Parts are not working right, portions seem unfinished & there's frankly a lot that just annoys me in its current state. Including bugs & limited features.If you're cool with that buy this, but this game is pretty much ball torture for me & playing it further is only me trying to get a reward from a game that constantly punishes me.So i enjoyed the concept originally. "Hell souls" & playing it is more like Doom Slayer-souls with that robot 'Mister Deadly' who wants to explode from Archer season 10. But after 15+ hours..things have started to bother me. The following things in mind, i cannot recommend this game to 'souls' fans. Unless you enjoy torturing yourselves then go ahead & leather up.Controls:So theres some input lag on some controls, Ground smashes with R2 repeat sometimes making the idea currently unusable unless you're always on point with them. There is also some input lag in regards to spamming controls.Bosses:This game seems primarily designed for the dark souls fans who enjoy just boss fights. I like time to breathe between boss fights, i like to be able to explore & Farm & get better gear before i am forced to fight another boss. I am up to the third boss & i really cannot beat it with its nonsense, nor do i seem to have any gear to counter it(Such you'd expect from a souls game)Enemies:Enemies have a weird scaling, its essentally the same zombies (At least early on) for awhile & they don't really change. You then go around the corner sometimes & there are 'mini bosses' that are always present that are leagues ahead of the enemies around them (or if you are in an unlucky location during hell hour)Lighting:Game is dark, Really ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ dark. So dark i had to bump brightness up to 90. Its so dark they even give you a flashlight?? Weird design choice.Hidden doors:So it wasn't until a few hours into the district around the third boss that i read online there are secret doors that you have to find, I thought all doors would be the breakable doors you find in the first area. This is frankly confusing to me to give us an example of 1 doorway & then use another.Pathing: The pathing is so damn annoying. I can't make a clear mental map of where i am going sometimes as theres just so many dead ends & locked doors. Not to mention the amount of BACK TRAVELING. The idea of a shortcut is to make travel short, not just more..tedious.Teleporting:So you can teleport through the rifts, but only if you have synced them using an uncommon item that i have only found about three of...Whats worse is you have no idea when to use them or when you SHOULD use them, making me wish to go back & undo my choice.Builds:So like most souls games you make a build, you get weapons that help that build & you go a long way. Hellpoint doesn't really give you any gear for your build. I have found more reflex weaponry than anything (I went Str build) & there is no way to Undo your choice (at least this early on) So i have a str build with 1 str weapon & i had to grind to 'fix' my build into a reflex build with a reforged glaive.

_childDocuments_.review: Delve into a cosmic horror with Hellpoint, a dark and atmospheric action RPG that channels the eerie vibes of classic sci-fi horror. Set on a space station plagued by otherworldly entities, it challenges players with its tense, unforgiving combat and deep, intricate lore. The game's environments are richly detailed, creating an immersive experience that feels both claustrophobic and expansive. The blend of sci-fi and horror elements, along with its challenging gameplay, will appeal to fans of intense, narrative-driven games. Expect a gripping journey through a nightmarish world where every encounter and discovery keeps you on edge.

_childDocuments_.review: For those of you skimming: It's a really good game that's short of greatness, but still only really good.It's a souls like, it's familiar but also different in ways that make it a loving advancement of the genre. While I've yet to play the game in full, the combat is fun, the systems make sense, exploration is rewarded and while it lacks polish it has refined the core gameplay of hack n slash exploration adventure through death. In the short time I've owned the game, many of the bugs I have noticed have been ironed out. I strongly believe I'm going to be putting at least +50 hours in this playing with builds.Hellpoint isn't perfect and before I confirm its flaws I'll put out a few merits. Multiple styles of play are supported and encouraged; weapons are interesting and even moveset clones have advantages between them that are unlocked as you use them. Attributes are never wasted, all builds can find value out of obscure stats. Enemies have quirks that make you learn to respect them when you first encounter them. Jumping is a thing, and its even somewhat useful in combat. Heavy attacks are significantly more useful than most players expect. Dodging is fluid, it's rare to get totally stunlocked yourself. I've been encouraged to use a shield but punished for relying on it; blocking light attacks with a heavy shield creates openings on enemies, and blocking without stamina staggers you for several seconds. Elemental damage also gradually dissuades you from simply clenching your left index finger. Armor is varied and offers a way to customize your character visually. Healing and ammo is replenished through combat, encouraging active melee combat that the games excel at.Now for the bad.Environments are largely interesting but each metal corridor feels the same as the last, and the lack of detail leads to a banality of the space station.This also ties into the directionless feeling of some of the clustered halls in its levels. While there are tools to navigate the world effectively its easy to just lose track of which hallway leads to where and what elevator is connected to what because they all look the same. The soundtrack and sound design in this game is also lacking. The drone and clang of the Space Station sets a tone, but the lack of a musical score in its more boring areas can fail to set the game to that next level. The lack of sound design also hurts player feedback. Its not uncommon to take damage and not notice because nothing alerts you. Similarly if you're not paying attention to the UI you can become irradiated without realizing.Speaking of hurting things, most enemies are simply disposed of by chaining light attacks to stagger them to death. I will remind veterans that even Dark Souls is guilty of this and I will admit I have not seen a wide variety of enemy types yet for lack of play. That said the only enemies that are resistant to this are bosses.This game has a clock, and if you don't know what I'm talking about its a criminally unrealized feature of the game. Once a day you're set to 'NG+', twice a day you're 'gravelorded' or at least allegedly. In practice I have yet to see significant impact on play from this system.Lastly, this game is made with Unity. Theres an unfair stigma to that, so in fairness I will remind us all that Unity games are still fun and enjoyable games. Furthermore the game is buggy, but post launch patches are doing wonders and I fully expect the game to be ultra stable very soon. No, when I say this game is made with Unity, what I'm getting at is it carries its failings. The game looks good in motion; it's actually really visually satisfying to play. But when you're given highlight shots and backgrounds, it fails to hit "Gorgeous View Ahead". Buildings often come off as impossibly rigid, textures appear smoothed over, backgrounds look painted in an otherwise generated landscape, and the lighting while good still behaves like a Unity game.This is a good game, and I look forward to playing more of it. Its systems are phenomenal and I'm willing to overlook its more peripheral flaws to enjoy the parts of the game that are rich with detail. As mutliplayer is rolled out I have high hopes for the future of the game and even dare to dream of post launch content for the game that helps to fix its polishing issues.

_childDocuments_.review: I first played this game about two years ago and I thought it's like 90% done, just needs to fix the GLARING issues with movement, platforming, combat, level design, exploration rewards etc. the list sadly goes on and on. They did not fix a single issue. I don't even think they see them as issues because they released DLC without addressing any of the fundamental and foundational problems which only serve to compound consistent issues further.I think the main problem is a lack of systems integration, it seems to me that a bunch of teams worked mostly independently on the own parts of the game, barely ever interacting. Like the art department makes a massive impractical room that looks pretty, but is very impractical and a boring play area. You're supposed to build the map out digital feature-less "cardboard" first; play test that first, if it's not fun without the bells and whistles; it still won't be fun with them. This is a microcosm of the issues plaguing this game. I really wanted to like this game, but it fills me constantly with frustration and anger, there is clearly a lot of talent that is being squandered by the blind fools who have final say. It's such a disappointment, fix your problems!

_childDocuments_.review: Tedious. That is the most succinct description of this game i can think of.For a souls-like this is not as grindy as one might expect but every aspect of the combat slows the player down. The first level has two very good examples of this. The best tactic for defeating the Embassy Knights is to back off till they start a range attack, rush in, attack, repeat ad nauseam. Tedious.Worse, the first boss freezes you when you stay too close. You can be perfect at dodging its attacks, it still freezes you, which slows you down, till your character is too slow to dodge, forcing you to back off, artificially slowing you down. Tedious.Then there are the secrets. A lot of secret areas are hidden behind wall panels, that are not visually distinct from other walls and do not show an interaction prompt, but that you can interact with to open them. You have to literally know where they are, or start humping every wall. Tedious.

_childDocuments_.review: You know your game is pretty good at copying Souls games when the best you can make is a boss with a ton of target points that make your camera completely ♥♥♥♥♥♥ and when you die the camera janks into oblivion. Amazing job with this one.The fact that when you get knocked down you can still get infinitely hit is amazing, borderline the most amateurish game I've ever played of this kind.As an avid lover of souls-like games, I don't recommend this game the slightest, it's riddled with bugs, bad level and game design, and I would have requested a refund if I could (my playtime exceeded 2 hours). Having defended this game back when the Thespian Feast was released, it is a dissapointment to see the game has barely improved (if at all) and the final result is pretty bad.EDIT: after writing this review I started over with a different build (i was doing reflex and conjecture or whatever the tech one is and instead just went full STR and used the tutorial level column for the rest of the game up to the final boss). I got to the true ending of the game completely by accident, I met NPC's that acted as if I had already interacted with them, only to find them in previous areas and acting as if we had never met. I did everything completely out of order, I did not understand anything about the plot, but it seems to be just a bootleg version of Event Horizon.Nothing I wrote originally changed throughout this new gameplay, with the only difference being that I could now effortlessly stunlock bosses and even strong enemies into dying just by mashing attack. The damage I was dealing with inferior stats on STR were drastically super by second compared to my original build, and the difficulty of the game overall changed drastically from way too hard to way too easy at some times. I understand this is more or less common in other souls games, but I never saw the disparity this hard, and being someone that usually replays souls games multiple times with different builds (rogue, warrior, sorcerer, nightblade whatever) I never felt the difference this hard.Overall the ending was lackluster, and I left knowing the same as I started, and honestly only finished this game out of the habit of finishing games I start. I hope the devs can learn from whatever they learned technically, and actually make a solid game with a solid storyline next time.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll have more impressions up as I play. While this game has some problems, it's so far the best AA Souls clone I've played yet. Note that this is not a review. I don't have nearly enough time in this game to fully judge it.Video impressions if you prefer the format:They got the controls and combat near perfect, at least from what I've played so far. In Dark Souls, it was about getting the biggest sword to stagger enemies or getting the biggest shield to block even the most dangerous attacks. This game plays a bit more like Bloodborne or Sekiro in that your mobility is more important. However, unlike those games, Hellpoint doesn't ditch the value of shields. Offering a very good hybrid of fast-paced dodging with shield defense play as a strong supplement to attacks you can't quite dodge. You can dodge-cancel out of attacks, you've got a big, MEATY, dodge and a massive jump which makes movement much more fluid then the intentionally-clunkier, slower, Dark Souls.Attacks in general feel great. Weapons have plenty of weight to them and the controls as mentioned are super fluid and make the game really fun to play despite being a fairly straight-forward Dark Souls clone. The only exception being the jumping/platforming. There is a small amount of platforming in this game to reach certain areas with hidden items but the jumping is too slippery and often times you overshoot your target far too easily.The game also has a solid sense of character progression. Armor looks pretty cool, you feel like you're improving as you play through leveling up or just getting better at the game in general. The enemy designs are a bit generic but they are modeled well and fun to fight. The first two bosses had some fun mechanics and were extremely satisfying to beat.Art direction is also great. Enemies are so-so but the geometry, backgrounds and the modeling of enemies is pretty good. Backgrounds are jaw-dropping at times for how much this game costs. There's a great sense of atmosphere here in just the art-direction alone. It's not always great, though it doesn't feel like it came off the "generic unreal engine aesthetic" assembly line.There are two major issues I've come into while playing so far:Staggering and audio mixing. When you take damage after losing all stamina, you get stunned. That's fine, but you get stunned for what feels like an eternity and if you're not careful, it's incredibly easy to get stunlocked. This doesn't need to be removed or anything, just tweeked a tiny bit (like, seriously devs, a half second shorter or even less than that).The next is audio. This game has some really great atmosphere and sound design. Some of the work in the environment can sound incredible but sometimes certain things lack punch. I fought a really fun and interesting first boss and there was almost no sound upon accessing the door, nor was there a ton of punch to some of her/his/whatever's attacks. It didn't take me out of the fight. The sound can be so much better considering what I've heard throughout the game. Plenty of sound effects in addition to the boss fights are just lacking and some are just flat-out grating (some of the player-character walking sounds terrible)I have not tested the alternative weapons or multiplayer component. Story I have barely progressed so I'm not sure regarding that. Will update as needed!So far I do recommend giving it a look or at least waiting for a sale. It's definitely worth keeping an eye on.Thank you for reading! If you want more recommendations, I have a curator page you can check out:

_childDocuments_.review: Everything about this game seems off at first glance. The graphics, animations and sounds all seem so undercooked. This is true, to a certain extent. Hellpoint's charm and artistry lies in how the developers have made it work so well in bringing the game to life! The atmosphere, lack of concrete story, multiple poorly explained side quests, weapons that gain utility and abilities as you use them and a surprisingly complex upgrade system all combine to make this game more than just another souls-like and allows Hellpoint to carve its own unique and often disturbing identity. There are a few issues with the game though: The game requires platforming but sometimes the jumping and physics aren't conducive to a pleasant experience in that respect. Animations can sometimes feel clunky and the action queuing system can be frustrating with certain weapons. This is the best value I have found in a game in the last few months. I look forward to future content for Hellpoint and to future games from the developers.

_childDocuments_.review: Avoid this game if you've played Dark Souls, Nioh, or even Code Vein. Hellpoint does not live up to those titles polish and general design philosophy. If you've never played a proper "souls-like" title, you might find this passable if you are interested in a different angle of ARPGs. Equip a glaive, throw away your shield and stunlock enemies to oblivion with your overhead L1 strikes.A Souls-like game with a futuristic setting on a spacestation where strange, hellish creatures warp in and cause chaos. You have just awoken on this station and are trying to figure out what exactly is going on. It's a combat-focused game with sparse narrative tid-bits strewn around in forms of messages left on walls, text dialogues from computer terminals, and conversations with a few NPCs you'll meet along the way.I like the setting and situation you find yourself in. Feels a bit like a blend of Hellgate London, Dead Space, and Dark Souls. Although a very misguided and ill-tasting blend. Beyond this, I can only say the crafting mechanic was a bit interesting at the start. Mostly since you could upgrade and refurbish old pieces of a set into a better, and more effective set. I also like searching for hidden rooms, even though most of them are easy to spot once you recognise the copy-pasted wall asset.The visual fidelity seems fine at first, but later you realise the environments are mostly in grayscale and/or very low saturation, with lots of copy-pasted structures. You will find segments of walls you saw in the early game in every single locale on this space station. Not only are many assets reused, but some have low texture resolution even on maximum settings. (I play with a water-cooled RTX 2080.) The lighting is hit-and-miss. It works in some environments when it's a bit varied, but when it's a flat light level with no variety the scenery feels very empty and soul-less (hah).It's your standard souls-like control scheme with the twist that you have a dedicated jump button. The combat animations are stiff and has a very awkward delay on . Trust me, it's not because of the anticipation frames. You frequently make an extra attack, or two, by accident and if you are unluckily positioned it'll cause you to tumble into a death pit.The battles themselves are either a stunlock fest (both ways), a horde of enemies piling onto you, or getting juggled into a corner and locked in. Shields are obsolete since most large enemies can hit you through them and stun you for three whole seconds. Bosses can combo you like it's Marvel vs Capcom since you have  meaning you may get unlucky and get caught in a high-damage combo with no hope of getting out. Many powerful boss attacks doesn't even knock you down, instead you're locked in regular hit stun until you die.Many weapon movesets are reused for other weapons in it's category and the glaive (even though it's a one-handed sword) was the one I found most serviceable, but not good. Most movesets are delayed, sluggish, jerky, and has abundant action queuing to a fault.This is the absolute  aspect of this game.Depending on how meticulous you explore, you'll encounter some platforming sections with great items hidden away. You'll have to climb the environment to find these treasures. That's fine by itself, but the controls are so painfully stiff and the momentum is so awful that you have very little control over your jump velocity. More often than not you will fall to your death attempting these stunts. Many times you'll walk through a doorway only to find yourself falling to your death. Lots of sudden drops where you cannot see past corners or slopes because of terrible camera angling/lighting/room design.Tiny rooms, narrow hallways, small arenas, and miniscule platforms.The entire game is very claustrophobic. Every single locale is built out of tiny rooms and narrow corridors and lots, and lots of doors. Majority of fights are a struggle not to collide into walls or fall off ledges while trying to dodge sweeping attacks from enemies of all kinds. All areas look very similar and It's easy to lose track of where you've been since most assets are featureless. Lots of locales loop into each other several times over with the exact same door+button combo that you'll be unsure if you've already been there or if it's a new area within the locale.Many sound effects are missing completely.Running has no sound effects at all, some enemies' attacks (including bosses) produce no sounds at all, the very aggressive object culling in the game engine cuts away sound effects coming from outside your viewport.Many sounds are horrible mixed/normalised. One example, a thrall's unarmed swiping attack has a higher base volume than bosses large slamming/exploding attacks. The voice acting are just incoherent mumbling causing you to only read the text and not get any sort of emotional reading out of any NPC.Bipedal xenobytes convention.Almost all enemies you encounter are bipedal humanoids with four body type variants and palette swaps. After 15 hours I only encountered five enemies that weren't bipedal. Even then, two out of those were disembodied humanoid torsos. Extreme waste of potential to throw yourself to creativity and create any amalgamations of horrible hellish creatures.This game had high potential, but it was utterly wasted on repetitive locales, bad/forced platforming, confusing level design, awkward combat, and really uninspired enemy designs.

_childDocuments_.review: Again I wish for a thumbs sideways, because this is right on the fence for me for recommending. On one hand there were many enjoyable elements and improvements on other souls games, but on the other hand some design choices and bugs detracted from the experience. TL;DR more enjoyable co-op than DS3, but not nearly as good as Remnant: From the Ashes.Hellpoint starts off strong, and for the first third of the game I was hooked.The combat is solid and the co-op was not janky when compared to other soulslikes. You're not constantly being invaded because there is a matchmaking option for co-op and pvp separately, or you can invite a friend and they progress with you and the loot is shared (for the most part, and the exceptions to this are aggravating).The weapon variety gives more builds viability, and many builds take advantage of the unique ranged weapon integration (melee hits charge your ranged weapon of choice) but this is squashed by the inability to respec so you are locked into one playstyle and lose the ability to experiment at all, so 90% of the gear you get you will never be able to check out.Lastly my favorite part of Hellpoint and the most unique is the time-related difficulty. There is a clock in the upper left at all times and when your orbit around a black hole aligns all the enemies get harder and some special events spawn. It really mixes up the gameplay just a bit which is enough to keep engagement and freshness. Really should have taken advantage of this aspect in naming, something like HellHour or HellTime... Hell O'Clock.... obviously something better than that but I never formed a connection between the game itself and the name Hellpoint...   Hell Noon!!! Boom perfect name.The environment looks good and enemy and level design is not bad, but that's where things take a turn.The biggest issue is not being able to teleport freely between bonfires (data breaches). An item is required to link a bonfire to the network for teleport-able ones, and those items are very rare so you're hesitant to even use them at all. This makes forming a cohesive layout of the world much more difficult than it needs to be. There is no map, which would be fine if areas had distinguishable landmarks or features instead of labyrinthine indoor corridors. Some of the connections between areas are not obvious, leading to substantial searching for where you need to go next which is very difficult if you don't even know where you are and have no way to return to anywhere familiar.The second factor that made Hellpoint slip for me is the difficulty curve. It was not super difficult to start but I attributed that to going through the game with a co-op partner. About midway the enemies and bosses started to get even easier... and at each bonfire there is an option to increase or decrease the difficulty of enemies "in this area" which I did not want to mess with because I would like to experience what is laid out as it is intended not trying to predict how difficult I think each encounter should be.. Towards the end of the game we were splitting off from each other basically unkillable even though we never grinded for level ups, and my friend killed the final boss in three seconds with magic before I was even able to land a hit. We had more deaths to falling than to all enemies and bosses combined.

The 5 major bosses however are very well designed and provide a good challenge for different reasons (Sentient especially). _childDocuments_.review: Things I do like about Hellpoint:• The art direction. Looks like a mishmash of Synth, Hellraiser and Renaissance and as weird as that combo might sound, it works pretty well. Really cool and unique.• There is some level of challenge to it, you can't faceroll enemies like you can in most other Souls-likes if you go for a non-magic/ gun run, melee can be pretty challenging.• The soundtrack doesn't stand out outside of the game but while you are playing, it does its job well enough.• The upgrade system is split into stat leveling and weapon leveling, and the weapon leveling itself is split in two parts as well - conductors, something that you slot into weapons and is what you actually upgrade to + the weapons, and familiarity. Familiarity unlocks extra weapon-specific passive buffs and skills, and it builds up as you use the weapons. Conductors on the other hand give the stats increase and can be removed and re-slotted in at any given time. This means you don't have to upgrade every single weapon in the game to use it, you just slot an upgraded conductor into whatever you wanna try and it instantly gets the + level of the conductor. A pretty elegant solution to weapon upgrading that even Souls games get wrong.• The narrative and dialogues are interesting. Surprisingly it isn't a riddlefest or edgy as ♥♥♥♥, like other souls-likes tend to be (Mortal Shell and Lords of the Fallen I'm looking at you), so reading and listening to audio logs is enjoyable.• Platforming. I love jumping puzzles in games that have them. In Hellpoint, it is a love-hate relationship and I will elaborate on why that is below.Negatives:• Optimization is kinda ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥...• Bugs. It is extremely buggy. Hellpoint was released 3 years ago, received many patches since as well as a "Next Gen" update alongside its DLC and yet it is still buggier than your average Early Access title...• Level design. Some moments and shortcuts are memorable, however the design leans heavily on being convoluted. I've seen some compare the levels to those of Dark Souls, which I totally disagree with - shortcuts in DS are kept to a minimum and they all serve a purpose. Level design in Fromsoft games in general is complex (complex =/= convoluted) but clean in design and full of landmarks that help you memorize areas. In Hellpoint, most levels are pretty much labyrinthine corridors that look samey. It can be extremely tedious to navigate this world.• Mechanics and progression are obtuse and convoluted. When the community has to rely on the devs' Discord posting "Spoilers" so the player can find pathways, items and even bosses, you know something has gone wrong in terms of making an intuitive game.• Fast travel is tied to something called Breach Synchronization, which is done through a limited (per NG cycle) item that you'll always find far less than there are Breaches (bonfires). This will create a situation where you can unknowingly mess up your mid and late game as you won't be able to synchronize later bonfires. This issue is further compounded by the convoluted map design I mentioned above, as well as that Synchronizations are undone and don't carry over to NG+ cycles. Mind you the DLC does fix this problem by making the otherwise extremely limited items reliably farmable, but it never feels right to me when devs create a problem and then paywall the solution.• The combat can be a bit of a mess. Attacks, especially ranged ones (magic and guns), will miss constantly because the lock-on system is unreliable and enemies' hitboxes seem to bug very often. Some enemies have really goofy combos that go on and on, some of which can stunlock you (hello mindflayers). Attacks that clearly didn't make contact with you, will register as hits. Sometimes during combat everything glitches out in a way that freezes you in place. The game doesn't accept any inputs afterwards, only dying or task manager "fixes" the bug.The worst and at the same time most unique thing about Hellpoint is its platforming. There is a dedicated jump function here, which already sets it apart from other soulslikes and even most Souls games. There's lots of platforming and jumping puzzles and in theory, they are well designed. In practice, because of how buggy and glitchy it is, you will grow to loathe the platforming and JPs. Invisible walls that clip you and bounce you to your death, dubious ledge placements where you'll clip your head and your jump momentum will disappear, inputs lagging out of nowhere after landing (I'm talking 2s delays), losing momentum randomly as soon as you jump, getting stuck in terrain... When latched onto lifts, jump direction doesn't depend solely on the movement button input, it sometimes also depends on where the camera is facing, which will bug things out so badly that you'll jump off the lifts in completely random directions, probably to your death. It is unfortunate that the one feature that helps Hellpoint stand out from other soulslikes, is the most poorly executed aspect of the game that might just make you hate it.If you are interested in Soulslikes, Hellpoint is definitely worth a playthrough. Maybe buy it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: It's Dark Souls meets Dead Space. What's not to like?Pros:A true Soulslike - large but tight world with rest points, shortcuts and different path choices, player/equipment upgrading, secret areas, collectibles, interestingly vague story, and unforgiving combat.Great graphics - looks great while keeping very low VRAM usage & GPU temp, with very high FPS on max settings on a GTX 1650 Super. Other developers should look to Cradle Games to learn how to have great graphics without the horribly common sacrifice of performance so many other games have.Probably the only Soulslike that actually plays very with with a keyboard & mouse, despite for some reason the store page strongly recommending a controller.At least 20+ hours for a first playthrough if you like plenty of exploring and uncovering secrets but aren't a completionist.Cons:Movement and combat are sometimes a bit too clunky and actions sometimes don't immediately register, especially with non-default controls.Custom keyboard controls still reset upon exiting the game.Basic graphic options - the game looks and runs great, but it would be nice to have some better or more options.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed the combat system, it is better than Dark Souls. Simply because you can jump on command. Also the co-op function is spectacular. Your friend can join you in split-screen mode with their own character,using their own game data. Almost no games have such a luxury. The weapons are interesting, but the crafting process and upgrade processes are complex and overall not exciting. Sadly, this game is very confusing as far as where to go and what to do when you get there. Most of the levels are restricted by locked doors or otherwise impassable obstacles.Every attempt at communicating with the user online sucks. Just a stupid gold handprint that upon inspection shows you an assortment of symbols that could mean nothing at all. There are very few NPCs to interact with, making it even less human, if that was possible. The story itself is dark, and a little hard to follow due to a mixture of dates showing up at random times due to a library level.Visually this game is very dark all over, it gives off a spooky vibe. One level in particularhas a terrifying sound track if you give it some time and a dark room with headphones by yourself. The graphics add to that spooky atmosphere and a thought that you are the last surviving human in some kind of future apocalypse. The bossfights are interesting, and the regular fights will tear you up if you have never played a Dark Soulsgame.  The jump puzzles are absolutely the worst, your character has butter on his feet for some reason. Because you will always slip and fall off a platform after jumping a 5+ foot gap in front of you. Overall I enjoyed it in the beginning, called it future Dark Souls. But now I feel bored when loading Hellpoint due to being completely lost.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; Great game to play coop and actually has a functional splitscreen. Second player won't get kicked from your session after beating a boss and generally has some super smooth multiplayer. Just join and go! Solo on the other hand is very frustrating.. not just because it's a soulslike game, but Hellpoint has a lot of bugs and balancing issues that can ruin the experience. Highly recommend if playing multiplayer, if playing solo wait for a sale.Now that I've had some time with Hellpoint I can share my honest opinions about it.. keep in mind my entire playtime was splitscreen coop, and while there were a few bugs that I'll mention, the overall experience was great up to a point.See, the problem with Hellpoint is the level design. It starts out simple enough with a bunch of secret branching pathways, but then out of nowhere you hit the observatory and the game leaves you with no direction / goal. I'm sure some people will enjoy this aspect, and for the most part we were excited to play a soulslike game coop that we pushed through, but from that point on the rest of the game just gets more and more confusing with multiple pathways that lead to bosses which lead to other bosses.So after playing for so long we managed to track down most of the world bosses by accident by just wondering around and finding different paths we hadn't explored, some taking hours to complete with no payoff while others might unlock a useless shortcut and some lead to the final boss of the area.As far as I can tell the goal of the game is to kill bosses to collect passes which allow you to access areas you couldn't, but how do you know what pass goes where? You don't. The worst part is there's no in-game map to speak of which sucks because I feel like this would really help this game.. or if there was like a "Boss List" somewhere, or any type of objectives really.After about 5 hours of playing, we were pretty much done, the last 2 hours was wondering around trying to find some paths we hadn't explored or aimlessly searching for items required to progress when we finally decided "what's the point?" and stopped.Up to this point, it was an enjoyable experience that I can easily recommend to play with friends, but playing solo? No thanks, this would've been awful. Hit detection, auto-aiming enemies combined with brutal damage amounts don't really add up to a challenging experience you might see in other soulslike games, this just becomes cheap shots and luck.. luck whether your hit registers, or your dodge avoids damage etc. In coop, you can usually just have one person lure an enemy while the other one attacks, which didn't always result in a win, but it was a fun casual experience without much frustration.Hellpoint also has a dedicated jump button and boy does it use it.. there's TONS of platforming and some of them are brutal.As far as we're concerned, we beat the game. All that was left for us was to find some armor required to explore an icy area so we didn't freeze to death. At the end of that zone is some key item for a good ending apparently, but frankly there's not enough people playing this game to find enough info online about how confusing some elements are.Overall it was a blast playing a souls game coop. Unlike Dark Souls, the second player won't get kicked after you beat a boss and can simply continue playing. In fact, if the second player dies, the first player can bring them back to life at the cost of half their health, but if player 1 dies you both respawn at the nearest Breach (Hellpoint's Bonfire) and since player 2 didn't technically die, they'll keep all their XP, meanwhile player 1 will have to grab their death pile to reclaim lost XP.. Player 1 will also create a clone of themselves to fight where they died which is pretty fun...I hate to nitpick, but the game also has a space theme near the beginning, which is cool, but right away the enemies, bosses, weapons and armor turn into Dark Souls stuff.. my coop buddy kept asking "why do I look like a Dark Souls knight instead of a cyborg?". I would've liked to see Hellpoint do a few things better than Dark Souls too, because honestly with this being such a clone, the best weapon is the medium speed longswords since heavy weapons are too slow and fast weapons too short-ranged. Everytime we got a new weapon we were disappointed it didn't compete with the swords.Weapons also level up as you use them which is a cool mechanic, but the game won't calculate leveled stats correctly.. the only way to find out if a new weapon will be higher damage than your current one is to level it up and 90% of the time, the new weapon might have higher damage but has a slower attack animation or takes too much stamina or something and we'd swap back to the longsword.RECOMMENDED if playing coop / splitscreen. Solo isn't awful, but it's pretty pricey for a Dark Souls clone and has quite a few bugs that become more obvious the further you go.

_childDocuments_.review: Hellpoint is a crudely polished gem in the rough.While this title may not have all the resources to become a masterpiece, it certainly makes the most out of what it has. It is a damn solid souls-like with a fresh atmosphere, engaging lore (albeit not entirely fleshed out at times) and a variety of different builds to play around with. My only two complaints are the bugs and some combat animations. Don't get me wrong, being an avid fan of Bethesda games and Cyberpunk 2077, I am no stranger to bugs, but at times these ones can hinder your expedition if you are unlucky enough experience them. Most notably, NPC's can sometimes get stuck before they move to their next quest location or you might get stuck in the floor and die, with no checkpoint for miles around. That being said, nothing was really game breaking, even when my nerd rage warmed up to a light simmer. As for the weapons, some feel weirdly janky, while others had a much better handling (cheers to you, spears and halberd gang)  though none of the equipment felt ineffective.The setting of this game was fresh and varied, you could be slaying a highly advanced army of monastic hell worshipping robots, in their pristine halls while their golden pyramids tower overhead. Or you could be wading through a valley of blood and viscera, while some skinned torture victims (of a demonic cannibal cult) eagerly wait to punch the ♥♥♥♥ out of you if you wander too close.If you get this game, make sure to get the DLC's too.Is it Elden Ring? No.Is it absolutely worth your time and attention when it goes on sale? You bet!All in all, a small studio brought us an entertaining sci-fi horror/action game and I will eagerly await a sequel.(P.S There are multiple endings, though witnessing them is about as unceremonious as an escort splitting as soon as you pay them. The journey up to that point is a wild one, but you'll be left with a yearning for a deeper connection.)

_childDocuments_.review: Hellpoint is a game for people who thought Dark Souls 1 was too linear and straightforward. The map in this beast is impressively complex, interconnected and difficult to navigate. It doesn't have the polish of DS1, but it was also made by literally 11 people so try to have some perspective.It maintains a real sense of mystery and exploration right to the climax and working out just how to reach the next area is often more challenging than the bosses. Despite borrowing heavily from the Souls games, there's no shortage of creativity on display here. The healing and consumable-based fast travel system are just straight up better mechanics than anything Fromsoft has done in those fields, and the unlockable weapon skills are a unique and satisfying progression method the genre hasn't seen before. Also, the player messages being pictographs instead of words is extremely clever and it's fun trying to decipher their hints.This isn't the hardest game ever, but it's filled with cryptic puzzles to solve and remains consistently engaging in a way few other souls-clones can claim to be. It demands your attention, lest you be utterly lost in its labyrinth. I just skated by and went with the motions in "Mortal Shell" (which was pretty formulaic at the end of the day) but that's not an option here, just like it wasn't in Dark Souls 1.

I was just pretty randomly investing stats and used random weapons (ie I used an agility spear on a strength build and it was the best weapon, kind of weird).Anyways, I recommend it for true Souls vets. _childDocuments_.review: Pros- Aesthetics/lore are the standout aspect here: a mix of cosmic horror, Cthulhu stuff, space and tech- A lot of different influences: Dark Souls 1-3, Bloodborne, Dead Space 1-2, Hollow Knight, Metroid Prime 2, Grim Dawn, maybe The Surge?- Inherits the NG+ system from Dark Souls, but IMO has a really cool lore-friendly implementation (certain progress also carries over, not only your levels/equipment/the usual stuff). Also there are Bonfire Ascetics from DS2, but they're a little more flexible here.- Certain boss designs and arenas are pretty cool.- Lore and implications are really interesting, philosophically.Cons- CLUNKY CONTROLS. IMO this game feels terrible to play, and many boss fights come down to poor AI and obvious tells. I finished a lot of fights feeling accomplished, but also annoyed.- Non-obvious controls: upgrading conductors at a weapon bench, and leaning left/right on ladders- Certain boss fights ruined by sudden OHKOs, _no sound effects_ (which is incredibly weird), lackluster camera, and additional enemies.- Very indie. Leftover bugs never patched, including bad/wrong hitboxes (i.e. your weapon swinging thru an enemy doing no damage, or taking damage from a projectile a mile away... happened to me a lot, in a certain fight in the Port)- The space station looked a lot bigger w/ more variety when I started the game, but ends up feeling like a long corridor. I often felt boxed-in.- Critical NPCs can die even though they might not show a HP bar, so your playthrough is screwed. (You could redo it on NG+ and reduce the difficulty to NG though.)- Blue Sun (DLC) is tempting if you want to fully experience the game, but allegedly it's of mixed quality... read reviews carefully.Tips- Victim Poker weapon is good IMO, I liked STR build and upgrading the Strength Conductor to +2 and beyond.- Check Steam Guides for the "Stat Breakpoints" guide, but I kinda wish I stopped upgrading STR at like... 20-25? instead of 35 which is suggested.- Ignore Coins- Use a guide for the ending you want, *however* i admit the game felt more natural when I didn't get that ending on NG but got it in NG+. To repeat what I said earlier, the NG -> NG+ transition is really lore-friendly.- Certain rewards for hidden content are.... terrible. Use a guide to see what you'd get.

_childDocuments_.review: There have been plenty of souls like clones all over the internet lately, which have been nothing but a copy-paste of multiple art styles, combat, or even the weapon UI. Glad to say that Hellpoint is not one of those clones. It is an inspiration taken from Dark souls for sure, but it stands out entirely on its base with proper and profound lore and its world build up.After several years into its development, Hellpoint finally releases today on Steam and consoles. Special thanks to Tinybuild/Cradle Games for providing me with a key early to do a proper in-depth review.I always wanted a soul-like game in a futuristic space setting for a long time, and I finally got to experience it. The game feels exactly like dark souls in both combat and visual aid, with its own futuristic/cyberpunk-ish vibes and colors with black contrast to complement its visuals.Hellpoint is set at a space station called Irid Novo, where you take the role of a 3d printed pawn of your creator whose agenda/scheme is unknown to the player, and you are given full control/freedom to do whatever you want.Your primary mission is to collect a minimum of 100% of the data by going through different areas and exploring the deep space station and opening up breaches for checkpoints for easier traversal. There are multiple endings in this game and after you have beat it once, you will be taken over to New Game+ where you will have your current arsenal and weapons and would continue with your old knowledge of things to trying out different dialogues/ pathways leading to newer areas or even more unique enemies.Several boss battles feel easier than the dark souls games, at least the early few enemies are more manageable for those who play RPG/soulslike games a lot. It will be a decent challenge for new players but would get easily adjusted to their attack patterns since most of them have 2-3 unique attacks and skillsets.The attack animation, the enemy hitboxes, and the boss locations are well thought out with excellent visual fidelity. The entire Irid Novo and the surrounding areas in the space station have their designs and live characteristics, which makes it seem unique in its way.Hellpoint has its weapon variety, including melee weapons, ranged weapons, and magic weapons. While opening breaches, you will be greeted with the character augmentation screen where you can level up your character in whichever way you please.Read More by visiting Us at :

_childDocuments_.review: If you need a game to scratch that Soulslike itch, Hellpoint has you covered – but anyone looking for a completely fresh take on the genre likely won’t find it here. There are some intriguing mechanical changes and the sci-fi setting mixed with splashes of cosmic horror do make for a delightfully spooky combination, but one can’t help but feel like a bit more could’ve been done with it, especially in terms of visual design and enemy variety. Having said that, I can still more or less recommend Hellpoint if you’re a diehard fan of this genre – it may not reinvent the wheel, but it certainly hits all the notes needed to be a sufficiently solid and worthwhile addition to the ever-growing Soulslike family.Curator page:
