_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR It is an atmospheric game, but is it a good one?Wot I liked- Dark, gloomy grimdark techno atmosphere - pitch black dark sky with blinking stars and that humongous black hole;- The great maze of a map - there're quite a lot of ways you can explore Irid Novo space station;- Dark music ambience is one of its saving graces; - The story, or what glimpses of it I learned, is pretty fun and reminds of Event Horizon meets Pandorum; - Those black hell whatever hours, eye codes, secret doors & walls reward you (mostly with useless junk) for being on the lookout;- There're some decent monsters out there (zombies, cyborgs, robots, mutants, demons, gods, ETs), just don't expect to meet them right away; - There're even a couple of tough bosses - you just have to look for them;- It's pretty addictive for a short time;- Pummel guys with a stone tp roll or skewer them with a demon poker.Wot I disliked- I very rarely complain about graphics but the game just looks too unimpressive - everything's blurry, contrast is all messed up - you either don't see anything or are blinded by the white shining;- Most mobs (and a good chunk of bosses) have 1-2 attacks, they have no AI to speak of and would quite often get stuck or just plummet to death from some ledge without any encouragement from your side;- Combat, the spine of this whole game, is broken. There's no blocking, no dualwielding, no backstabbing, no stances, no special moves (to speak of). Jumping attack / kick allows you to stunlock most opponents, sometimes even bosses!- The weapons are sameish, the armour is even worse. Spells and ranged options are few in number and lacklustre in performance; - Levelling your character adds little - my level 1 character killed mobs with 2-4 hits of his pipe, my lvl 80+ character killed mobs with 2-4 hits of his stone tp roll. You might say that my opponents grew in strength, but not really. In the first couple of hours of my playthrough I had access to the mobs I was fighting at the end of my playthrough;- There're only 1-2 attack patterns for your weapons. There're more attack animations overall, however its number per category is nothing to be excited about;- Everybody's animation is stiff;- That clock mechanic, while being an interesting twist, forces you to waste too much time waiting for the clock to strike - the devs should've introduced a timeskip mechanic as there's literally nothing to do while you're waiting;- There're few items, what's more - there're even fewer useful unique things which would give game some flavour;- Missing textures pop up quite often; - Shortcuts kept resetting each time I started the game; - Controls in menu and game are different;- Menus are unhelpful and look too small in 1440p;To sum it all up, after playing the game for ¬10 hrs I found that it's bad, then I played it some more 20 hours and found some redeeming features. The combat is bad, however the story is pretty entertaining and the space station of Irid Novo is an interesting locale one wouldn't mind to get lost in for a couple of days. I wouldn't recommend the game, though, due to its current state and the quality of combat.

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't had so much fun exploring a souls-like since Dark Souls. The world seems huge and the level design is just amazing, with secrets within secrets and cryptic stuff tucked into every nook and cranny. When I entered the Observatory, the games main hub, I peered down into the abyss of what I thought was just lod scenery, but no, loot was shimmering down there. Then I looked up at the distant ceiling structure, realizing I could get up there as well. This has defined the whole experience so far - much of what I think is just scenery turns out to be clever level design, reachable, somehow, either by ways of agility or ingenuity.Unlike most souls-likes the game also sports a jump button, that helps take the level design to the next, vertical level. Some jumps can be tricky, but I personally like it tricky, and controls feel just precise and responsive enough to make me feel like it's my own fault for missing a jump.While you've probably seen "cosmic horror on derelict space station" before, it does a good job to set itself apart, both tonally and visually. The writing/story bits are good, leaning more towards interesting obscurantism, than lazy techno babble. The black hole/space station setting is intriguing from the get go and a lot of the cosmic horror enemies are genuinely creepy to a point where I ran past the first many heavy hitters, not due to fear of combat engagement - I was simply intimidated and unnerved by how they looked.I'm still in the somewhat early game, but so far, combat seems fine and bosses are nicely balanced. I've died a couple of times on each, not enough to be frustrating, but just enough to be satisfying when you finally put them down. They don't feel like Nioh/Sekiro-esque skill-gates to slam your head against 40 times to unlock the next wee bit of locales. Some people may not like this, but my aging fingers and affinity towards exploration loves it.Finally, I know a lot of people's experiences differ from my own, but I haven't encountered a single bug so far, no dips in performance and nothing in the world that seemed so bare-bones as to feel unpolished. I could nitpick a few nuisances, like lighting could be a bit better overall, having to move your hand to press "enter", when all other keys lies comfortably within hands reach and maybe most irritatingly, ambient/atmospheric sound is tied to the same mixer as combat sound, so if you want to take combat noise down a notch, you mute the entire thing instead.But those are minor complaints in the grand scheme of things. This is a big, satisfying AA title, made by a tiny indie-sized studio. Technical difficulties aside, Cradle Games should be satisfied and proud of what they've achieved here. Brilliant game.

_childDocuments_.review: Mystifying, cryptic, strange, and I can't have enough of it. Hellpoint is a soulslike which doesn't deviate from the formula. It knows what it is and it doesn't pretend to reinvent the wheel. It's as solid and sturdy as it needs to be, with its own variation to make it feel truly like its own game and not just Dark Souls In Space. Where Hellpoint shines the most is in its lore, in the themes it chooses, the unraveling of the story, the exploration of every nook and cranny of Irid Novo. There's so much going on that -even if the answers were to turn out ridiculous - I still enjoyed the feeling of the mystery, the intrigue and the sensation that we are here just to take notes after the apocalypse and have a chat with [one of the last remaining] god. It's buggy af and it needs some good polish in the multiplayer department though, but so far, we still haven't found anything that stopped us in our march.

The huge window you get staggered into when out of stamina wouldn't be so bad if stamina didn't run out absurdly fast. At several points, I've died while standing still in safe environments just because (no oxygen/cold/heat etc. meters).  Some enemies are invincible for several seconds when you approach them just because.  If you join a multiplayer game before you finish a corpse run, your hard earned souls disappear.  At times it literally feels like this team wants you to hate them, more than any FromSoft game I've played.  "Difficult but fair" this is often not.  "Artificially hard for horribly designed reasons," it is.That said, it's still pretty fun when it isn't being mindlessly horrendous to the player.  It scratches the itch when it plays right.

_childDocuments_.review: I tried really hard and waited a long time... but I came to the conclusion that I can't recommend this game even to die-hard souls-like fans. The game was seemingly only made worse over time. Especially the release of the DLC made everything even more janky.The game has a great atmosphere and some interesting monster, weapon and armor designs. The gameplay systems are overall quite nice... if they worked properly.Let's start with clunky combat. Imagine Dark Souls 1 but with clunkier controls and everything is trying to hit you through a wall, will then actually glitch through the wall and then fall through the floor. That is not a rare occasion in this game, something this happens every 15 minutes. That's something I could still deal with even though it is annoying. How about you are in the middle of a boss fight and suddenly can't do anything anymore? Happened to me 3 times in 1 day.The world in the game is okay. It looks good if you don't look too closely. Lots of blurry textures, invisible objects and seemingly random level design at times. Jumping puzzles that will ruin your day due to the clunky movement and terrible collision detection.The game also has some quests. Like kill 10 enemies of a type. Also some well hidden quests that would be quite fun, if they didn't constantly bug out. I just wasted 3 hours on one of those hidden quests because enemies fell through the floor or it was just impossible to complete for no reason.A word on the balancing: It's terrible. Really terrible. I can see why so many people quit in the first few minutes of the game. And I'm not talking about the tutorial boss itself. It's not that difficult if you are accustomed to souls-like combat, but enemies mixed in that will kill you instantly on level 1 and a 5 minute walk to go back to where you died because you tried to explore. This is not just in the beginning of the game. Especially in the DLC there are enemies that will randomly one-shot you. There are bosses that are insanely weak and other bosses that are complete damage sponges and require specific items to be able to stay alive long enough.But hey at least the game never crashed for me. I'm not even sure if I will ever 100% this... it's just so exhausting to play when you get so many bugs and such annoying gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really surprised that the game is as good as it is. I initially dismissed it as a crappy souls clone but there are some fantastic aspects to this game. I think its biggest achievement is exploration - you will likely enjoy this game a lot if you're a completionist and like searching every nook and cranny for secrets (because 95% of the time you'll actually find something). There's good world interconnectivity and verticality - you'll constantly find shortcuts to unlock as well as different ways to enter areas you've previously explored, often to blocked off sections that contain secrets, gear, etc. I haven't explored too much into it but making different builds seems to be pretty fun and encourages multiple playthroughs. Weapons have a familiarity system which unlock passive buffs (e.g. increased health, stamina) as well as active weapon skills. you gain familiarity by hitting stuff with said weapon. Melee weapons seem to get 2 active skills (for example, the ceremonial dagger has a backstab ability and later on the ability to throw it) so it's basically the weapon art system from dark souls 3 but with more variety. Combat is decent. It's not amazing but not terrible either. Thankfully the controls are for the most part responsive. Enemy and boss variety aren't as good as they would be in a souls title but it's not really to the point it's egregious.Also this probably goes without saying but there's quite a bit of jank - I believe this is the first game this dev team made. Personally I'm not too bothered with a lack of polish in certain areas but I just wanted to make clear that this game is rough around the edges in certain aspects.Overall I've really enjoyed my time with the game so far. I usually stay away from alleged "souls-like" games like the plague but I think this game deserves a spot in the pantheon of souls-like games that aren't a complete ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ along with salt & sanctuary lol

_childDocuments_.review: In short, great formula and some interesting ideas buried underneath a ton of minor issues and probably a lack of budget to flesh them out. Personally I had fun at start, mid game I was annoyed by technical issues and backtracking, by the end I just wanted it to end ASAP.ALTHOUGH, If you are looking for sci-fi soulslike on a spooky space station just to have some fun for a few hours then go for it if you can get it for cheap somewhere.If minor issues like stuttering, falling out of bounds sometimes, npc escort that sometimes buging out, audio not playing or cutting out sometimes or ragdoll on death being broken irritate you then stay far away. This game is very rough around the edges and I mean very.PROS:- setting and atmosphere- plenty of weapons and armors + weapon leveling unlocking new perks for it- many secrets to discover- enemy design and boss design (but not true final boss)- the "clock" which is a fun concept on paper, it introduces some variety passively (black hour, demon spawns)- cosmic gods take over mechanic, if you kill one of them his minions get replaced with the other god's minions, fun idea but could be fleshed out more- 3 bosses can give you quests, this was a fun and unexpected discovery- mirror world, a great idea (timer sucks tho)- easy to change difficulty, the effigies are a nice idea. game is too easy, pop some daring effigies, it's too hard - fearful ones. Very user friendly difficulty system (you have to find those tho and be careful to not overdo it)CONS:- too much f***ing platforming, really, and it is not fun platforming like in an action game, your only tool for platforming is a jump and that's it. If you jump during a sprint tho the character does a stutter step forward which mostly kills you. Easily 70% of my deaths in this game were fall damage or instant death pits.- the "clock" and locked black hole doors, who thought waiting for this garbage would be fun? do devs like wasting people's time? full cycle of that clock is like what 2h? terrible idea- if you want to go for 100% achievements be aware that one of those is locked behind a controller or twitch integration + coin collector does not carry over to ng+ and you will have to start all over again with the whole 66 coins set (there is a tram section that can f**k you over and block a coin for a playthrough)- tons and tons of small issues, stuttering in many spots (mostly when looking in the direction along the location's length), falling out of bounds when doing special moves, audio cutting, stuttering or not playing sometimes, ragdoll is broken because apparently some cretins found it funny and now it is a feature, getting blocked by seemingly nothing sometimes (esp. on the pyramid), some elements of some armor sets disappear when you look at them at certain angles, npc can get stuck on some wires during escort (and btw his questline might just reset like out of nowhere) etc. As I said before, VERY rough around the edges.- Only 5 bosses (3 gods, 1 robot and 1 true final boss), all other bosses are literally just big versions of common demons walking around the station, same movesets, same look, just bigger.- Enemy variety is on the low side,- It is a worse maze than The Surge 1- Station is big but that means there is a lot of empty space and you will have to walk and backtrack a lot because...- bonfires (breaches) are not connected to fast travel system and the items you need to connect them to fast travel system are limited and usually well hidden so better look up which ones are crucial and activate those first,- elevators are too damn slow, like really, why? there is a lot of elevators in this game and it is a pain to take them- environments are kind of the same which makes remembering the way harder- no real voiceacting which is even worse then they say the same gibberish line multiple times in a row + kind of boring NPCs and quests,

_childDocuments_.review: Yeah, so... Barely an hour or two in, and I've come to the stunning realization that this game wants to be Dark Souls, but cannot achieve what Dark Souls did.To explain: COMBATThe combat in Dark Souls (to me, other's will have different opinions, and as such will be respected by me while writing this) feels grounded, a bit slower paced but also methodical. You learn your opponent's moves, you fight them, you die, you come back with that knowledge, and you do it again.This game? This game feels beyond floaty and doesn't feel nearly as fleshed out as Dark Souls was. The game is okay, at best in terms of combat, but nothing makes sense. Enemies turn around without warning one time and start swinging without any regard for their wellbeing or yours, but the next time you fight them, they just sit there. As if they had been here before, agin and again and again. There doesn't seem to be consistency with the grunts that you start with, BUT, I will say for the larger enemies (looking at you, sword bastards) they have a "moveset" but that set of moves doesn't feel like that means literally anything.STORYDark Souls has a story, yeah I know. Do I know it? No. Do I understand or pretend to? Nah. I tried, didn't work, I just played the game. This game's story? Uh... Where is it? Where actually is the story aside from an unseen "guiding hand that created you" that actually explains things along the way? You know what I learned from him? I am the perfect specimen and I live in Irid Novo. THRILLING RIGHT? Except it's not. Being told "you are the perfect specimen because I created you" just kinda... Ruins it for me. Why am I perfect? Why do I look like a prototype sex doll? Why did Dark Souls literally make you a dead person just to come back but this game's approach seems 100% memier? Nothing makes sense.In short, I genuinely cannot recommend this game unless you want another Souls Like. It's okay, at best. That's about it.

_childDocuments_.review: THE COMBAT IS BAD!For some reason a lot of good and bad reviews say the combat is great. It sucks. This is a souls-like, so it automatically has to be compared to DS1/2/3 and BB. Between steam, xbone, ps3, and ps4 i have put probably 2,000+ hours into the souls/borne games. I have no comment about the lore, because I'm not a dork that likes fantasy BS. I like combat. Combat is the only purpose for these games to exist as far as I am concerned. The combat isl unbalanced and wrong in every way it could be unbalanced and wrong. Its not too hard. In fact, I didn't find any aspect of this game challenging before quitting out of sheer tedium. The failures are as follows: 1. Character hit box lag. Did you dodge that hit? well your hit box didn't. Sorry jack. 2. Character animation frame delay or intentional stalling. Do you think a character using a fast weapon should be open to counter attack for less time than a character using a significantly larger weapon? Well, the Dev's didn't. Good luck having the weapons feel any different from one to the next other than damage. 3. Character movement doesn't make sense. Do you think a stationary character should be able to leap forward like 9 feet at a time from a standing position? Well, the Dev's did and they thought that would make for good platforming. It doesn't. Have fun wildly over jumping platforms by 6 or 7 feet at a time. 4. Either lack of Iframes or iframes work in someway I can't understand. If you are a veteran of the souls games you have likely learned to roll into big attacks and away from small attacks. Not applicable here. In fact, i found that jumping up and down was better than using the dodge feature. 5.  Projectiles don't come out of the tip of the gun, they come out of the wrist for some bosses. That big long barrel is over your head? You are using distance to choke a projectile so it can't hit you? Not going to work. The gun is a prop, and the blast comes from the character model wrist area. You will be shot through the top of your head while 2 inches away from a boss holding a gun that is 8 feet long. 6. Lack of poise. We aren't even talking about DS3 poise for hyper weapon animations. You can stun lock or be stun locked by almost any enemy at any time. Can you beat this game. Yea. I don't think its all that hard, except when they pull a fast one  and trap you in a gank, but the combat doesn't feel fulfilling. Don't be fooled like me. This will not quench your thirst for Elden Ring.

_childDocuments_.review: Recommend to developers: fix gameRecommend to players: Play at your own risk, 35$USDAs of 2020/08/12 this game should be in early access. It has been released for a couple weeks, and it feels...so broken. I've played mostly co-op with a friend and we have experienced numerous, persistent bugs. I'll list some below:When I host and he joins:-We can play for some amount of time with frequent problems.-Enemies respawn "invisible" to him. They can hurt him, but he can't see them.-Enemies can't be damaged by him. They appear to take damage to him, but they don't take damage in reality (my server).When he hosts and I join:-I randomly disconnect.-Damage I do is "laggy", meaning they appear to take damage from me, but he always has to finish them off, or they appear to me to die and don't.Hardware:-Both our computers are fairly good, ryzen 5 3600, xmp enabled, 2070 Super (overkill for this game), NVME drives (blazing fast)-Both our connections are 100meg+-We play many games on Steam, Epic Store, Xbox live together, seamlessly.To put this in perspective: I have had Satisfactory Early Access, for a period of time, never experienced issues like this. This game is extremely buggy, to a fault, and frustrating to play online. We have played tons of Dark Souls 3 online, Division 2 online, the list goes on. Hellpoint is very broken, and should not have been released, because it isn't finished.I appreciate that the developers update this game regularly, but it is not nearly finished. The broken co-op is the most frustrating, because we were looking for a new "souls-experience" to enjoy together. We've both beaten DS3 numerous times on Xbox and on our new, beefy PC's. We are huge DS fans and wanted a new game to scratch that itch...this is not it, unless you love encountering hours of bugs, and chatting in discord while reloading. Maybe the game works better in single player. I don't really care, because when a game ships with co-op, I expect it to work. As a stand-alone single player game, it's probably more playable. If I have the time to check it out more in sp, I might. It's more on the Bloodborne-end of the DS series, but it lacks the polish and perfect-parry timing that that game (and ds3) embedded). If you're going to buy and play it: ranged combat is necessary. Use guns or magic, and use them frequently. The game builds your "magic" meter back by hitting w/ melee, so you absolutely want gun-play or magic. Otherwise, you'll spend a lot of time whacking away at enemies that can attack with their own ranged abilities. I'm not saying you shouldn't buy it ever. However, you definitely shouldn't pay $35USD for a game that doesn't work as it is described, and is fatally flawed in one of its best playstyles: co-op. Oh, and before the "git-gud" crowd arrives: yes, I love a challenge. I beat ds1r and ds3 numerous times without co-op help. However, I also helped my friends beat it, and they joined in on my many successive runs for new builds and boss runs. We were looking to play the game as advertised, with co-op. I don't mind extra enemies and enemy respawns to crank up the difficulty -- but it doesn't really matter if they're invisible, or you disconnect. FIX IT.I'll update if the game is fixed.

_childDocuments_.review: Hellpoint has a huge world to explore and lots of hidden secrets, puzzles, and mysteries. With a non-linear story line, the player forges their path through the game! Its up to them to seek out and piece together whats happened to humanity and whats become of this advanced civilizations AI. Find terminals with excerpts of the past, commune with beings outside your understanding, or find NPC's to bring you up to speed.  Fairly difficult combat reminiscent of Dark Souls 3 and a fairly diverse pool of weapons and armors. For the aspiring mage or gunslinger, there are catalysts and firearms found throughout the game- not to mention the many weapon skills available that explode, buff, shoot, and heal. For the good ol' hack and slasher or simple barbarian, there are a number of unique long swords, great swords, axes, clubs, A WHOLE PILLAR. Good times.  Awesome movement mechanics, the platforming gives exploration more depth. There are tons of challenging puzzles and secrets that require utilization of the players jump, and finesse. Dodge mechanics feel solid, there is an iframe stat which means the player can have items/armor either increase or decrease their dodge margin. Its a nice balancing feature. If you wanna dodge like its Dark Souls you better get stacked.  Which brings me to my next point- the leveling system. Near identical to the souls series- Axioms are the currency and XP in Hellpoint. When the player dies, all their Axioms are dropped and they spawn at their last visited 'bonfire'. Remember that 25k Axioms you just got off a boss but forgot to spend? BETTER BE CAREFUL ON YOUR WAY BACK!!  Hellpoint has a really sound online interface. Having trouble beating a boss or clearing a new area? look around and find a blue hand on the wall. Interacting with it will summon a player into that world. Alternatively a player can place a blue hand to be summoned. RED HAND! Now were talkin PvP- seeing one of these bad boys slapped up on a wall that means they wanna fight. Interacting with the red hand accepts another players challenge and summons them to that world as an enemy. Now featuring a ranked arena system!                                                                                 Final verdict: 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: There are times when I hate reviewing games I'm not good at. It can make for the live broadcasts to get dull do to repeating the same thing over and over again... like 30 deaths in a 4 hour stream. But this was not the case. I had an absolute blast playing Hellpoint. The controls are smooth and reactive, the artwork for the different areas is stunning in it's bleak sci-fi temperment, and then there's the rag doll. Oh yes... unlike other souls-like games, when you die, your body rag dolls all over the place like somebody forget to program that part of the game. In Hellpoint: it's a feature.There was something about the game that I really loved and hated at the same time. the addition of a "ghost". Not so much an illusory image of yourself or someone else beating a stage. But an actual tainted ghost with your stats, attack style, equipment... everything. It even attacks in a similar style to you. And if I am being honest, I have probably died more times to my ghost than any of the denizens in game. Even the first boss! Normally you die to a tougher enemy, so now you have to fight yourself AND that enemy at the same time. HUGE, but welcome challenge .I really enjoyed playing this game and I am looking forward to dieing over and over and over again as I push towards the DLC that's already out!

_childDocuments_.review: 4.1/5 :  Amazingly robust 3D world, FPS.  More Z (vertical) in each zone than any game I've played before and I've played a lot.  We played entirely on macos 14.  Ran fast and clean most of the time, but had to restart after 3d errors cropped up after hours of play. If we'd judged it based on the first few hours of play, it would have been a thumb's down. There's something deeply wrong with the balance in the first zone.  The opening is fine, the tutorial method (green hands on the walls) is good, but the first zone boss is impossible to beat without a LOT of grinding and the first zone is too small.  I played it side by side with my partner (each on our own machines) and we would literally just stand waiting for the MOBs to replot. It was super tedious. We almost quit several times.   Also, the inventory system is a disaster. It is way, way too easy to accidentally destroy unique items and there's too much garbage not to 'disassemble' things consrtantly or the inventory becomes overwhelmed.    One can replace unique items if one has  a friend with the game. Player1 creates a new character, which re-generates the universe, then the player  (Player2) missing the item connects to player1's "match", runs through the world to get to the item, picks it up, both players in that universe get the item, then Player2 disconnects and can go back to playing their own universe with the item.   Without that, it seems impossible to finish the game if one accidentally destroys the wrong item.Also, I accidentally killed a key character and there was no way to recover from that. I have read it's possible to finish the game, so I'll continue through, but it's an example of some of the flaws with the game.But for a very strong 3D run-around, detailed, hack and slash with big distant graphics and amazing vistas, Hellpoint is fun.  I was re-reminded how strong the human vertigo and dizziness at heights .  Uncontrollable yelps as one unexpectedly comes up to a 500 foot drop. The game isn't perfect and there should be more story, but it's fun to play co-op.  For those, like us, who strongly prefer desktop games, Hellpoint is very strongly designed around controller play and there are a lot of controller-type special fight actions using quick key combos. Takes a long time to learn them and each weapon is unique in some way. I broke my alt / windows key on my keyboard bashing it to pop my shield up.  oops.We haven't finished it yet, but we've been to every major zone and are now tying up loose ends as we kill each of the top bosses.  There's still grinding, but it's fun to get tough enough to be able to beat the impossible bad guys from the early part of  the game. The in-game mechanism to increase and decrease difficulty is interesting, I'd not seen it before. I wish it were slightly more granular: changing to a more dangerous universe changes the difficulty A LOT. MOBs go from easy to almost impossible.  I'd rather the jumps up and down in difficulty were 50-60% as big as they are in Hellpoint.Definitely recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: - A SoulsBorne Fanboy's Review of Hellpoint -My review will be broken down into Five sections: Base Game Personal Impressions (Things that stood out while playing the game), The Good -Base Game- (Mechanical/Technical/Overall Features that were Positive), and The Bad -Base Game- (The opposite of The Good section). The Blue Sun DLC (A summary of new mechanics and content with my impressions, The Good, The Bad), Final Thoughts and Score for both the Base Game, and The Blue Sun DLC.- Impressions and Thoughts (Base Game) -As a longtime fan of SoulsBorne and SoulsLike games, finding a Souls like game that stands out and feels unique can be a somewhat daunting task, with many games getting a SoulsLike label that shouldn't. So to begin this is a SoulsLike experience. Meaning that the combat and difficulty is SoulsLike in nature. Now how does this game tread new ground and attempt to stand on it's own in the genre? What does it do that makes it a unique experience? Exploration and secrets galore is your answer. Player progress is tracked through collecting data. You collect data by locating new items, weapons, enemies, bosses, blueprints, messages, secret codes, hidden rooms, NPC quest Progression, and even figuring out how to talk with ancient Gods and gain their favor. After collecting enough data you will be able to challenge the final boss regardless of how many areas you have gone through, regardless of which bosses you have killed or not killed. Speaking of bosses besides the final boss, there are three big bosses (Enemy Faction Ancient Gods), and killing on will not only yield plenty of data, but also change which enemies spawn in different areas, as other factions take control of an area no longer inhabited by a slain God and that Gods minions. That is a surface look at the game progression. Is the game feeling to easy for you souls vets out there use a Daring Effigy to increase the difficulty of the playthrough by 1 new game + increment, you will find multiple so feel free to stack, but if you find that maybe you increased the difficulty by to much, then use a Fearful Effigy to reduce the difficulty. Now to look at the exploration, you can progress through this game and enter the many different areas of the space station in many different ways, there is no real linear progression through the interconnected areas of the space station, and the more you explore the more you realize how much freedom you have in your progression. Tools like the Quantum Light will reveal invisible platforms, allowing you to discover new paths and items. There is always a reason to look for more hidden doors, paths, keys, and secrets as you progress through the space station. Speaking of the space station, it is actually orbiting a black hole. Depending on the position of the space station relative to in orbit in the black hole, enemies will get stronger, or hide in terror as you approach, stronger enemies may spawn, events that spawn a wave of enemies yielding a reward for completing will appear, if you have discovered and kept track of the many different secret codes for the ring puzzle, and found out where to use them, and use the correct series of codes, you will be able to access ring puzzle doors which have hidden bosses or other items/npcs behind them. Are you starting to get the picture? Exploration is this games forte. And if you enjoy exploring in soulslike games you will love what this game has in store for you.The Good (Base Game) -Exploration - I think I have highlighted this enoughCombat - Both Mechanically and TechnicallyCombat  Balance - is great and being able to increase/decrease the difficulty makes it easy to be as challenging as you need it to be.NPC Quests - There are quite a few and completion does effect the games ending.Replay-ability - Well worth playing through multiple times. I discovered new secrets and areas my first 3 to 4 play throughs.Weapon Types - Plenty of different Primary and Secondary Weapons to choose from.Crafting - Break Down Weapons/Armor Pieces, and find crafting materials to use for crafting different weapon and armor blueprints.Secrets Galore - Seriously there are so many.The Bad (Base Game) -At a certain point progression can feel rather slowCombat can feel somewhat easy when compared to other Souls LikesPuzzles and Secrets can at first feel overwhelming or unclear and take a bit of experimentation to figure out. But guides can help make it easier to understand.The Blue Sun DLCThis DLC adds Factions with contract rewards, multiple new areas to explore ,new enemies, bosses, npcs,  new puzzles, new armor sets, weapons, ect. to the base game. One of the coolest mechanics is weapons that include a single hand and two handed attack modes. Some in a Bloodborne like fashion change appearance and size depending on how you are using them. Pros -Two Handed Weapons -Multiple New Large Areas to Explore-Faction Mechanics are enjoyable and straight forward to try,Cons - Major increase in difficulty feels somewhat unbalanced- How to get into the new ares is somewhat confusingFinal Thoughts and ScoresHellpoint is a extremely fun SoulsLike I enjoyed the game immensely, and would recommend it to any fan of the genre, if you enjoy the base game the DLC is well worth getting as well. With my scores being based on a scale of 1-10 I would give the base game a solid 8 out of 10, and the score for the game with the DLC I give a 9 out of 10. The game is seriously fun at a reasonable price point, and while not flawless, does indeed deliver a unique and enjoyable experience to the SoulsLike Genre.

_childDocuments_.review: (tl;dr version)This game is legit. It gets a lot more right than it gets wrong. This is your sci-fi Souls that you've wanted all along.---(Longer version)You know how a lot of Souls-likes try, but ultimately kind of fail at really capturing that "Souls" feel? Usually due to overly janky and/or unsatisfying combat, milquetoast level design, tepid atmosphere... there's always something that's missing, that makes you think "yeah, no, this just doesn't cut it". Hellpoint... is on point. Despite being crowdfunded project made by an experienced, but small, indie team, and not a high-budget endeavour, it gets a lot more things right than it gets wrong, and is overall on of the better Souls-likes I've played.But, naturally, being a budget game and all, it does have a fair bit of jank, I can't lie. So let's start with that and get it out of the way:- Jumping feels clunky at times, and a missed jump usually means certain death, which can be frustrating. I would say that easily 80% or more of my deaths have been through falls. Some of them were my fault, but some of them were, IMO, annoying camera or clunky jumping mechanics. The upside is that the more annoying platforming parts are completely optional.- It has a number of small bugs that can be annoying, though not game-breaking fortunately. - The UI, especially to manage inventory, is not great. There is no "storage" option to stash away gear, making equipment clutter a real problem especially in NG+ and onwards.- Some mechanics are poorly explained. I didn't realize I could upgrade weapons further until someone in their Discord pointed it out to me, for instance... eep. 😅- Enemy variety could be better.So, what's GOOD about it? Well, quite a lot:+ Level design. This is the strongest aspect. I was surprised to see a few reviews panning this aspect. The world itself is fully interconnected like Dark Souls 1 (though some areas are still separated by loading screens). Individual levels vary in quality, but some of them are completely bananas... in a good way. Loaded with verticality, secrets, looping shortcuts and all that good stuff.Arisen Dominion, for example, is a huge, huge maze-like area, full of verticality and filled with secrets to find. Some of those secrets I found in NG++ despite thinking I had already explored the whole place thoroughly already. And just when you think you explored a huge chunk, it just keeps going until you get completely lost, which can be daunting as you carry all those axions (equivalent of "souls"), and then you end up looping back to a familiar place and go "ahhh, this place again!" with that familiar sense of relief.+ Fast-travel is limited; "breaches" act as the "bonfires" somewhat, but outside of a few specific ones, you need to use a semi-rare consumable item to make it "warpable", so you sometimes have to really decide if you keep going or backtrack and retreat to a safer area. It's also interesting that resting at the Breach  respawn enemies (nor does it refill your Healing; more on this later), so sometimes you can just retreat there to refill your health. (Yes, turns out you  need to copy bonfires and Estus to make a Souls-like, who knew? /s)+ Atmosphere. The game is set in a hellish, derelict space station set in the far future, with the dark occult sci-fi mood reminiscing of Event Horizon and Dead Space. There's a lot of really cool futuristic space vistas and impressive brutalist and alien architecture, with lots of suffocatingly dark and creepy areas making you rely on your Omnicube Light tool to navigate.+ Combat is pretty tight. Controls are responsive, the dodge is generous (similar to Bloodborne, it's a side-step when locked on), there's a decent variety of weapons and builds, some weapons have really cool and satisfying abilities. I played a Reflex (dex) / Cognition build, which focuses on faster weapons and a firearm as ranged support, and it worked well for me. In NG+ I experimented with "Foresight" abilities (basically magic), and found them fun and quite powerful.+ Build variety and depth. There's lots of options and possible combinations in there. I barely scratched the surface, honestly.+ Secrets. Soooo many secrets. Exploration is very rewarding in this regard. But hell, if you enjoy the obtuse Dark Souls secrets, you'll be spoiled by Hellpoint there. Some doors only open when mysterious conditions are met (and good luck figuring all of them out on your own xD). I even missed the "true" final boss because of one secret I missed and had to try again in NG+.+ Cool unique mechanics. For example, the Accretion Storms and "Black Hole Hour". The game has an internal "clock" in the top left corner, showing the station's current position in the orbit of a.... black hole. :D Depending on its current position, sometimes, special events happen, spawning enemies in places where there wouldn't be (such as during Accretion Storms), or unlocking chambers that are otherwise locked. Another cool mechanic is how you refill your Mana bar and your Healing items by attacking enemies (how much gets refilled depends on your Leech stat). I wasn't sure about this Healing mechanic at first, but it grew on me as I played more. You can find weapons that have extremely good Leech properties, so for example you can have a loadout that focuses on guns or magic and melee attacks are mostly support for refilling your mana.Honestly, if you crave a sci-fi Souls, I think this is the best you're going to get at the moment. The Surge didn't do it for me, but this one ticked the boxes.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; Bit low budget souls like that has some great unique ideas and does enough things really well to be worth a look. I don't think it is going to change anyone's mind on the genre but it is a very good one if you want more souls and are ok with a little jank. Very fluid combat system with many tools at your disposal. There is dodging, running, light/heavy, mid-air light/heavy along with special abilities that cost mana. Combos often carry progress between light / heavy attack chains so you can go light attack -> second hit of the heavy attack chain. Many special abilities are attacks you can use even without stamina as long as you have the mana to spend. You always have a lot of options available to you at any given time and it just feels good to hit things. Also rather than backstab attacks being big lock-in animations you just do significantly more damage to enemies backs. This encourages aggressive forward dodges with high damage but doesn't give you any invincibility frames for the attack. There also is a nice variety of daggers, swords, staffs, magic catalysts guns etc.  A key part of what made this work so well is mana and healing items recharge on melee damage. This means that you do not have to really save your powerful attacks. While it hurts to miss these moves it doesn't feel like you are screwed if you are out of mana without a nearby resting spot. This also lets you expend all of your mana on say ranged shots to kill a problem enemy without feeling busted as restricted until you get more melee in. Healing items being recovered on melee damage also is great as it lets you keep exploring as long as you don't take too many hit in a row. It also has a nice ebb and flow where you can play aggressively when when at healing cap or more methodical if running out. Frankly I hope future souls like games take this idea it just works so well. weapon upgrades are tied to an item which you slot into weapons. These change the stat scaling on weapons and provide a stat boost. They can be transferred somewhat freely (at the firelink equivalent main area) so if you find a cool new weapon to try it can be upgraded very quickly. Also as you use a weapon you unlock new passive and active abilities. These include things like lower weight, different firing modes for guns, ranged attacks for melee weapon etc.   Enemies have sweep attacks you can jump over and levels are designed with a lot of verticality and interesting platforming required. This is reflected in the level design and is just a nice feature.  the areas in this game are choked full of secrets. There are constantly hidden doors, items over gaps, secret elevators etc. The game constantly taunts you with items just out of reach encouraging exploration to find these hidden areas. The levels are also often have multiple paths through them, interesting shortcuts and are visually pretty cool. One of my early game favourites is a city district; as you enter the area you see an overhead view of tightly packed buildings before having to descend into the city streets fighting through narrow narrow alleyways full of ambushes. You eventually can climb through and jump in between buildings. So many levels are just really fun to explore and I think they nailed a lot of them. You also often have multiple accessible at any given time so if you are a bit stuck of feel under powered can go try somewhere else. There are many places in this game where you can feel that this is not an AAA game. Many regular enemies in the game are fought as bosses, you will find duplicate weapons and armour sets or weapons functionally the same with a different element, some of the animations are a little wonky, etc. Finding hidden paths and secret areas is a really fun process but it is a bit of a let down finding a duplicate. I also think the enemy variety issue was a bit exasperated by a design choice as well. As you progress through the game enemies are replaced with harder ones. While a neat idea, it meant the last few hours I spent secret hunting I fought a lot of the same enemies repeatedly. Perhaps instead they could've gone with some random replacement to add unpredictability to play into the horror theme a bit while keeping variety up.  I ran into a few bad ones including: unable to use or change left hand weapon until returning to main menu and rejoining, an NPC who`s dialogue indicated we`d already met on first time meeting him, an NPC`s quest progress reset to an earlier stage and steps had to be re-completed, a hard progression lock preventing going to a particular area. Props to the dev they have been very good about quickly fixing the worst of these which would break save files; my particular progression issue was fixed within a day but the game has some rough edges. There are some more minor things like getting caught on terrain and needing to jump out.A very good albeit a little rough souls-like with absolutely stellar level design, great sci-fi horror theme, and fast varied combat. _childDocuments_.review: Pros:-Interesting story that is fed to you by small snippets you find in the environment.-Fun combat, cool looking weapons and armor.-Interesting enemy and level design (dark souls on a far future space station)Cons-Bad collision, you'll find yourself getting stuck on random things.-Truely terrible platforming, like it's actually the worst part of the game because you have...-Clunky darksouls movement-Fast travel clearly limited for padding purposes.Seriously though, it's a fun soulslike from an indi studio, so give it a try. Unfortunately, fast travel is limited by items with which you can connect the bonfire analogues, which means that there's quite a bit of backtracking on foot. Truly unnecessary amounts of backtracking on foot, there's no reason that you can't have these points connected except to add hours of padding to the game. It should also be mentioned that this is one of the few 3d souls likes that has a jump button, you can in fact jump on command whenever you want. Unfortunately, this actually detracts from the game as there are platforming sections because of this, they are by far the worst and most frustrating parts of this game. Word to the developer if you're reading this, in the future for Hellpoint 2 take out the jump button and put the development time you put into platforming over instant death pits into something else. Over all though, I would recommend it to anybody who loves souls like games. Despite all my criticism this clearly has a lot of love put into it and its a really good game. It just turns out that there's a reason that platforming usually isn't a part of 3d soulslikes.

_childDocuments_.review: One question: Why?Souls-like in space? Sure, go for it, I guess, but at least put some effort into it.In the hour I've played I'm just turned off by how "bare bones" this game is.The UI is straight out of hell, combat feels "alright", enemies are so far "alright", level design is ... "convoluted", "resting" does not exist apparently? Then the game throws enemies at you you likely can't defeat, so just run past them ... oh, for some reason you are getting attacked by your "ghost" if you die and revisit the site of your gruesome murder. That ghost is a lot stronger than you and a lot more agile. Nice.Then you get to the first boss, no rest area in between, alright just rush through it, call the elevator for the umpteenth time and have at it.Boss is easy.Now, the big BUT ... everything is unpolished. From animations to sound design to actual graphics. Sounds cut out 80% of the time when running, when fighting ... the Boss didn't really make a sound at all. Attacks were barely telegraphed at all, I just chanced it proactively, because you have no idea what or how sth hit you.And the story... well, I dunno, it's some Russian space souls with so far little cohesion.Dark Souls 1 came out years ago and is still playable and enjoyable today. Not up to Dark Souls 3 or Bloodborne standards of course, but still. This though? If your very first boss seems more like an afterthought than an actual boss ... nah, I dunno. I'm not really interested to see if this gets marginally better.If it was at least polished, I might stick around, but it doesn't feel satisfying playing it.

_childDocuments_.review: It's very reminiscent of Dark Souls 1 - hits the same vibes of wonder and exploration. The level design is very good, with tons of secrets and looping corridors - the only downsides are that the areas do not transition seamlessly (loading screens), and maybe that it's not landmark-oriented which makes it very hard to predict where certain paths will take you. Though the sci-fi horror setting kind of necessitates this type of a claustrofobic design. There's also lots of very good ambience and stunning art direction. There's a system which you could call 'dynamic weather' which influences the game world (enemies, open locations etc.). The game is just as enigmatic with its lore as DS, maybe even more so. It's all interesting, and the setting really sells it. Overall, if the above things are what you are looking for in your Soulslike games, do not hesitate and play it already.This game can get janky at times but I wouldn't say it's much jankier than the first DS was. Combat is fun, with a pretty basic but sound souls core, and with some welcome twists (like ranged weapons actually belonging in your rotation). There's crafting and a good amount of equipment to use. The default difficulty is ok for me so far, and there's also a system similar to the bonfire ascetics in DS2 if you need a greater or lesser challenge.So far I'm very impressed. I would totally recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Hellpoint : By Triple F"Hellpoint", the 2020 action RPG from Cradle Games, throws players into the derelict space station Irid Novo, a labyrinthine monument to a fallen civilization. Borrowing heavily from the "souls-like" genre popularized by Dark Souls, it offers a challenging experience steeped in a nightmarish atmosphere and cryptic lore. While "Hellpoint" delivers moments of genuine brilliance, its execution is often hampered by technical shortcomings and uneven design choices.The game's greatest strength lies in its visual design. Irid Novo is a masterclass in oppressive world-building. Brutalist architecture, rusted and decaying, looms over the player, creating a sense of claustrophobia and isolation. The bioluminescent flora and twisted, grotesque enemies add a layer of unsettling beauty to the otherwise bleak environment. The art style, heavily inspired by H.R. Giger, evokes a sense of unease and dread, perfectly complementing the game's narrative themes of cosmic horror.Combat in "Hellpoint" is deliberate and unforgiving. Unlike its inspiration, the focus here is more on mobility and strategic use of stamina than slow, methodical attacks. Dodging and parrying are crucial for success, and mastering these techniques is essential for overcoming the game's formidable challenges. While the core mechanics are solid, the hitboxes can occasionally feel inconsistent, leading to frustrating moments of undeserved punishment.Exploration is a double-edged sword in "Hellpoint". The interconnected world is vast and full of secrets, rewarding players who take the time to delve into its depths. However, the lack of a proper fast travel system and the repetitive nature of some areas can lead to tedious backtracking, especially after death. This is further exacerbated by the confusing map design, which can leave players feeling disoriented and frustrated while navigating the station's labyrinthine corridors.The narrative of "Hellpoint" is fragmented and cryptic, pieced together through environmental storytelling and cryptic item descriptions. While this approach can be intriguing for players who enjoy piecing together lore themselves, it can also leave others feeling lost and disengaged. The lack of clear direction can be particularly frustrating, especially for those unfamiliar with the "souls-like" formula's tendency towards minimal hand-holding.One of "Hellpoint's" most unique features is its local and online cooperative multiplayer. Teaming up with a friend can significantly alleviate the game's difficulty and provide a welcome sense of companionship in the face of overwhelming odds. However, technical issues like occasional lag and connection drops can disrupt the cooperative experience."Hellpoint" is a game of contrasts. Its captivating atmosphere and challenging combat are undeniable strengths, but its technical shortcomings, repetitive level design, and cryptic storytelling hold it back from achieving true greatness. Ultimately, it caters to a specific audience: players who relish a high degree of difficulty, cryptic lore, and the satisfaction of overcoming a brutal but rewarding experience. If you fall into this category, "Hellpoint" offers a dark and compelling journey through a derelict space station, but be prepared for a challenging and sometimes frustrating one.

_childDocuments_.review: A super convoluted mess of an alright game with at least a well-working online co-op mode. Played through the game in coop, and I don't think I would've had the interest to play through it alone.Pacing:I enjoyed the first half of the game, while wandering around still felt interesting and new, but by the second half of the game the running around looking for whatever random golden item I needed to proceed through a random hidden door got very tedious.Combat:Following in the footsteps of Souls games, the combat should be familiar to anyone who's played any. It's alright, and can be quite challenging at times, but once you find a move that either stunlocks enemies or simply instakills them, it becomes very trivial. I built for full strength, and I never switched from the first Column weapon that you get 5 minutes into the game, because there simply weren't any better choices. Jump attacking with this weapon one or two-shotted every enemy in the game, not counting bosses.Map design:While the different areas you visit look somewhat nice, the map design is just awful. So many paths just loop around and lead back to wherever you started from, and everything is so dark you get lost easily. You have means to fight both of these problems in the form of a flying cube that provides light or breadcrumbs to mark your path, but in place of random gimmicky game mechanics I'd much rather have sensible progression instead of constant backtracking and getting lost.You have multiple ways of getting the items you need to progress, but it's very confusing when you randomly get an item -- such as a key that lets you progress to a new level -- from a normal enemy, yet you get the same item much later in your playthrough from a high threat boss in a pit in some random corner of the world.Story and lore:While the setup is interesting, in-game lore is close to nil, and unless you're ready to visit forums to read discussion on what everything meant you will be left in the dark. You're first guided by a voice on a computer you reach after the first boss, but after that it's just pure luck if you happen to find any new NPCs that speak in convoluted sentences that mean absolutely nothing to you. Good luck remembering where these NPCs were after you find them the first time, since the quest items you need will be found much later on. The overall backstory is explained about halfway when you find a library and read some books there, but after that it's back to random stuff about light, darkness, creation, death, whatever. It means absolutely nothing to you.The last boss bugged for our coop game, and only the host was able to hit it. Reconnecting multiple times caused the boss to do nothing, so an easy win. Quite disappointing, though.If you like Souls games, it can be fun for a while. Play it in coop. Buy it from a massive sale, or from a bundle.

_childDocuments_.review: "Hellpoint" is an indie RPG that strongly adheres to the formula of FromSoftware's Dark Souls series. It offers a fascinating blend of science fiction and occultism that, despite some shortcomings, provides a captivating gaming experience.The game begins with a cloned body on a massive space station where you must fight against demonic beings and god-like creatures. The narrative is cryptic and leaves many questions unanswered, leading to constant tension and curiosity.The graphics of "Hellpoint" are impressive. The interiors are stylishly designed and the exteriors offer breathtaking views of outer space. Despite the dramatic changes in color palette and lighting, the game feels consistent and coherent.The combat system is solid and the enemy designs are interesting. The bosses are challenging and the music contributes to the atmosphere. There are many unique weapons that unlock great abilities with increasing use.However, the game also has its weaknesses. The controls can sometimes be a bit clunky and the performance could be better. The space station is a labyrinth of interconnected passages and regions that are confusing to explore. There are little to no signs of where to go.Despite these shortcomings, "Hellpoint" is a worthwhile game for fans of the Soulslike genre. It offers a satisfying adventure experience and can captivate you for several hours. So if you're a fan of challenging and merciless action RPGs and don't have too high expectations for the graphics, "Hellpoint" could be a good choice for you.I must mention in conclusion that Hellpoint was my first Souls-like game and thanks to the game, I have developed a fascination for the genre. I would like to thank the developers for this. I love the game and its atmosphere so much that I start crying just from the title music because I'm so happy to finally take a look again. Sometimes I listen to your soundtracks on YouTube, just to lose myself in them. When it comes to sound and atmosphere, probably no game has ever touched and captivated me as much as Hellpoint. I would be happy if this game and its developers received more attention. Thank you for this great game.

_childDocuments_.review: Hellpoint, game that just came across and didn't really have almost any expectations of. Knew it's souls like set in space and that it certainly was. You can expect weird NPCs, locked doors, secrets, boss fights, mobs lurking in the dark, getting a space suit or dying outside of space station and more.Gameplay felt quite fluid and jumping mechanics are quite much used if you go out of the beaten path. It's much easier that your original Souls game and that's good things, as some of the routes are quite treacherous and look like where one shouldn't even try to go, but in the end there is path and there's a way to get those shiny loots from far away places. Combat was also quite familiar and felt responsive and fast enough to deal with. This time though mainly had melee weapon in main hand and blaster in the other. Blaster and the like use energy or what ever the blue bar is and you can recharge it by hitting enemies, which was pretty solid idea. On top of those things you have floating bot with different mods like in Nier Automata, but it doesn't really have damage mod, instead of different lights and the like, so those hidden paths are possible to find.Locked doors and opening routes play big part along with those breaches which open like eye of universe before you giving sight on how to improve yourself with quite familiar stats. Think mostly the dark halls and futuristic space station gone to hell was pretty fine to look at, but some of it was pretty ugly to look at, especially own character which looks quite something you wouldn't most likely create in character creation tool, but at least can cover up that mug with armor. About armor and weapons, think armor variety is pretty low in game, but all builds/stats should have their respective set, though felt that game served you better by balancing the stats. Weapons have usually hidden abilities which come out after whacking enough enemies and then give out solid bonuses or charge hits, buffing weapon or character.Variety in areas and enemies is solid enough though it's shame that most bosses are pretty much your average enemies after first encounter. They should have given them unique skins at least and something more over the normal mob. Though it makes sense that they would be similar looking in a sense. Areas change from mostly dark alleys and cities to brighter regions and each of the god bosses who are the most unique in this game tend to have their own theme going on. Be it more faithful buddha bois or meat curtain fellows with severed hands or daemons and undead looking mob.Few of the pretty unique implements in game were based on Black Hole which you can see every now and then all around the place, especially at hub area. There are some locked black hole doors around with secrets, also blackhole hour is a thing and was wondering what the heck is going on when it first hit, as whole space station was vibrating and soon noticed how big ugly mutt was clanking it's big metal staff in midst of familiar mob, black hole open invasion possibility for daemons during it's hour and you get bit more aggressive and stronger enemies around it around several places challenging your progression along with arena fights with mobs that give rewards for completing them. Also there is dark mirror world with it's own enemies and bosses to encounter at few places.Can recommend the game even though it's not great, but think it's good solid title with pretty solid stuff going for it. Getting that space suit fixed against radiations and not becoming breathless is a good thing, as if you go out of your way to find the true ending, you need everything you can, or more likely just right thing to beat a fight have never seen before.

_childDocuments_.review: So I really enjoyed this title at first, but the longer I played it, the more frustrated I became.  The combat is my favorite part of the game, I enjoy the weapons, skills, and the interesting "black hole" mechanic.  The game hosts lots of different skills, lots of different ways to customize your character, but some of the animations are wonky.  What frustrated me during my playthrough was the map design.  Hellpoint has some of the worst level design I've seen in any game.   You're supposed to be on a large space station with a city inside, with lots of different mechanisms but instead it feels like you're in a brown maze where everything looks the same.  There are a few places that stand out and have really awesome vistas, but for the most part I just see a lot of copy-paste corridors that make no sense.  When I'm supposed to be inside an arcology, why is it mostly hallways with the same texture everywhere?  How about inside a city?  well in the city you see what looks like a city in part of the map, but majority of the map is also just a bunch of corridors that don't make any sense.  Some of the rooms you enter are just empty, with nothing inside.  It makes it hard to believe it's a city.  The frustration I had the most is just how lost I got and how often I ended up in the same room over and over again, or was it a new room but looked like the last one?  There are hardly any "landmarks" - and while many soulslikes incorporate labyrinth style of design, they don't "feel" like a maze because the "walls" aren't literal walls but some interesting design that helps you tell one place apart from another.Because hellpoint just has nothing but rooms that look the same, with hallways that look the same, it is very hard to tell where I'm at and to tell one place from another.  It also makes it very hard to believe this is a place that would really be built, nor does it make any sense.  It's just a confusing mess and honestly it feels like a lot of the level design was done by amateurs, or was a rushed job, or was just lazy.It's like they made some really cool looking areas and then they were like, "oh well we need to make the place bigger so lets just add a bunch of random hallways and then plop some random enemies in there, let's add a bunch of deadends and rooms that have nothing in there"The level design is just garbage.  I don't know how else to put it.  It makes the game just feel very tedious to play.  IT's a shame becuase the combat feels great and the general atmosphere is awesome.  Also some of the areas are really great looking too, it's just a shame the majority is just brown hallways and empty rooms.

_childDocuments_.review: Hellpoint is a soulslike action rpg set at a derelict space station Irid Novo where things have gone horribly wrong, you are a spawn created for the purpose of investigating the station and uncovering the truth of what has occurred on the station. But to do that, you need to survive the horrors that now stalk the station.Gameplay and combat are similar to the original Dark Souls and features several familiar mechanics, although on a smaller scale, less polished and often feeling a little clunky which is to be expected as it is an indie title with considerably smaller dev team and significantly less resources.But there are differences such charging up your healing items by killing enemies, weapons having familiarity experience which in turns improves the weapon and in some cases unlocks special abilities, a real time black hole / storm mechanic that spawns powerful enemies, new encounters, allows you to access some areas and even rewards you with some additional items and of course, the futuristic dark sci-fi setting with things such as no oxygen areas, firearms and advanced tech.Graphically the game is average at best, even if the art direction does a good job of nailing down that darker atmosphere - enemy & armor designs range from futuristic, disturbing, demonic and even at times venturing in the realm of body horror, be it in amalgamations of flesh and metal or things similar to Hellraiser. Environments range from somewhat bland space station corridors to larger/open and architecturally pretty interesting looking areas.One particular aspect that Hellpoint really nails down is its level design and perhaps even more so how rewarding exploration is. Levels are often interconnected although with loading screens in between, feature multiple shortcuts to unlock, optional areas with bosses, hidden doors and plenty of secrets to discover such as areas that are accessible at specific times to actual vertical exploration that leads to hidden sections of a level. For me, it managed to capture that same sense of mystery and the thrill of exploration I had when playing FROMs souls games the first time.That being said, the exploration aspect does have its flaws especially for completionists as you'll see plenty of duplicate weapons, some armors and items as loots due to some areas acting as sort of like alternative routes through the game. Additionally towards the end of a completionist playthrough, you'll be way too overpowered.In terms of audio design, I think the game is somewhat boring. While the sound effects do their job, nothing really stands out and sometimes it almost feels as if some of the sound effects are entirely missing. Music is rarely used and isn't really something that stands out.Aside from that, Hellpoint does have some general issues:- Bugs: While I didn't bump in to any game breaking or otherwise serious bugs, I experienced things such as missing collision, getting stuck in geometry, falling through the world, environment not rendering and some enemy attacks ignoring collision along with myriad other small issues. But I've read reports about some more serious bugs.- Weapon balance: In particular heavier melee weapons feel extremely weak compared to the faster weapons, especially when taking in account the required stat investment.- Difficulty curve: Could use some work, as you end up getting a bit too powerful towards the end and even by accessing some areas too early in the game (such as Port Issoudun) you can trivialize a great deal of the game.My first playthrough of the game took slightly under 20 hours and I had plenty of things I planned to explore, but accidentally ended up finishing the game instead and was put straight to ng+. Fortunately I had so much fun exploring the sprawling levels, surprisingly interesting lore and even the gameplay despite its flaws that I'm eager to do another playthrough.So would I recommend the game? Yes, but with some caveats. I think if you're a fan of the genre, have played and enjoyed other soulslike games (apart from just FROMs output), have a tolerance for some amount of jank & slightly clunky combat and enjoy exploration - it is pretty likely you'll get some fun out of Hellpoint. For everyone else, I'd say go in with tempered expectations - it isn't a AAA title. That being said, in general it may be worth waiting a couple of weeks while some of the bugs are ironed out.

_childDocuments_.review: Some advice:* Invest in more health and stamina before anything else. Then put the minimum number of points towards whatever weapon requirements you need. * Upgrading your weapon conductors influences your damage more than leveling up your stats.* Shield bashing is a reliable way to stagger even the larger enemies. Parrying is trickier to pull off, and the parry window seems to depend on what shield you're using, but it's also quite powerful.  * Two-handed weapons aren't really better than one-handed in terms of DPS, but they are *much* better in terms of staggering. * Guns use Cognition - they are relatively common and useful. The humble railgun is a reliable weapon for much of the game. Catalysts use Foresight - they're somewhat rarer, but also more powerful. Putting points into both Foresight and Cognition would be expensive but also give you a huge range of options for combat at any distance. Or you could just focus on one of them, and make sure to have more than one elemental weapon at any given time.

_childDocuments_.review: That was a fun ride, although a bit rough around the edges.If you like Sci-Fi with Eldritch-Horror and some Occultism sprinkled in there, this game might be interesting for you just for it's atmosphere. Movies like Event Horizon, Manga/Anime like Blame!, Warhammer 40k, and some retro-sci-fi Movies/Series come to mind.The gameplay is okay. Combat feels good, albeit a bit clunky at times. Many different weapons, but not an obscene number - you don't get showered with new shiny toys all the time basically, but every now and then. The energy system is a nice touch, and gaining healing-charges via dealing damage is also neat as it promotes an aggressive playstyle.The Leveldesign is interesting yet a bit maze-like (reminded me of The Surge 1). There's a lot of connected maps and passages, and a lot of secrets (or hard to reach places). Exploration feels rewarding. Sometimes it feels like you don't know where to go next or "is this the right way i'm heading?", however, there's multiple ways go through the game and you always end up progressing. There's no long one way roads that just lead to some random, non-progression thing - as far as i'm aware.There aren't many NPCs or Quests, but that's fine, as you don't get sidetracked a lot and just focus on exploring the space station by yourself.The Story & Lore is nice, IF you like to piece things together yourself and IF you can accept that by the End of the game, you'll probably only have "a good idea" of what this all was about. I enjoyed the mysterious vibes that came with exploring places and reading messages, figuring out what the hell is going on (where are we even? what is this space station? black hole? demons?!).The Artstyle varies from great to "you tried", but it feels surprisingly cohesive. Animations can be a bit rough. The music and ambient sounds are great and set the mood without much effort - it just works. However, some sound-effects can feel like they haven't been mixed well (too loud foodsteps, and god forbid that concrete-pillar-weapon smash sound).There are platforming elements to this game. They work, IF you take a moment to figure out how different jumps work and that mid-air attacks can help you with controlling your jump. I have maybe died a handful of times due to not making a jump. I do get why people dislike it though, but for me it worked and gave the game a sense of variety.All in all it was a really enjoyable game and I do hope there'll be a second installment. Excited to see what the DLC will be about.

_childDocuments_.review: DOOM meets Souls, in essence. I won't spoil anything, but if you like the general story of those two, you'll appreciate the writing of this one. It has its flaws - it's certainly the "worst" soulgrinder I've played - but it is by NO MEANS a bad game. Weapon variety is limited in terms of basic moves, but it makes up for that with an evolving weapon system where your favorites get better the more you use them (some minor exceptions). Exploration is detailed with very good level design that loops back on itself with an appealing aesthetic, plenty of little nods to "Ahh, you managed to actually GET here? Good job." Unfortunately, many of the bosses are just recycled basic enemies with an extra move or two. I think that's somewhat made up for by the main bosses of the game, including the potential endings.All in all, worth the time I spent, worthy of sequels or spiritual successors from the developer, worth the price of admission, but not a game I ended up sticking with beyond my initial playthrough. See the playtime for how long it took me, including thorough exploration and the completion of all the side-quests I found.
