_childDocuments_.review: Is this game perfect? No, but few games are. Is this game a good horror souls-like? At least for me, hell yeah! I didn't have many problems with bugs like other players, and I played the game for almost 40h. It was a lot of time that I didn't enjoy a souls-like so much. Everything you hope for a good souls-like is there: huge interconnected levels, a lot of weapons and armors, cryptic secondary quests, many secrets, and huge-challenging bosses. The space station is full of secrets, dozens of secrets walls, switches, and hidden pathways This, combined with an oppressive horror sci-fi atmosphere, makes the exploration so rewarding. There are also many mechanics and improvements not common to souls-like games. The station is orbiting around a black hole, and this has an effect on the levels, with new and powerful enemies appearing, secret doors opening, or tough challenges against hordes of enemies revealed only at a specific time. Also, there is the possibility to increase and decrease the overall difficulty using rare items. Some areas have a parallel universe to explore, with powerful items to collect in a limited amount of time. But be aware that dying in this underworld means losing the items collected there.Weapons and armors are what truly shine here. Many souls-like end up with very few elements, and all very similar to each other. Here every weapon feels completely different, both for shape and moveset. From the backbone of a space-whale, to the animated severed hand of a grotesque flesh god, every new weapon is a joy to discover. Plus, the more you use a weapon, the more it levels up unlocking new skills. Sometimes the skills are huge magic that will completely change your approach. This feature increases a lot the depth of the game, and sometimes you just want to level up a weapon to use the cool skills it unlocks, like generating a small black hole. Playstyles are also very diversified, and if strength-based players will have a tough time, using magic and firearms is instead very rewarding.  But for sure you will find a strategy that will suit your style.If you don't mind some bugs and a modest but satisfying graphic-style, and you love souls-like, Hellpoint has a lot to offer in terms of atmosphere, exploration, and mechanics to reward even the most exigent player.
_childDocuments_.name: Hellpoint

_childDocuments_.review: While the gameplay itself is great fun, with fantastic controls, storng level design, consistently good graphics (except for monolith sections) and really fun weapons, Hellpoint suffers from a severe and disgraceful lack of enemy variety. It took me 18h to beat it and I could count 15 enemy types, including bosses because only 3 bosses were actually unique and not just a big version of a regular enemy. That's less than one enemy introduced every hour, which is quite saddening because the very first two areas have pretty much 95% of what you'll find later on.Enemy variety aside, this game was really fun to play. It follows the same groundwork from Dark Souls with a few tweaks to the formula, such as a dedicated jump button (together with air attacks), unlockable weapon skills and a fantastic healing system far superior to the estus flask. It's got some key differences too like how you must spend an item on Braches (bonfires) to connect them together to allow fast-travel, how enemies don't respawn if you just rest (they respawn with the real-time clock thing and when you die), and the unfortunate lack of a parry equivalent.Apart from that it's all the same Dark Souls stuff, but in space. Interconnected levels filled with hidden passages and items to find, weird NPCs that laugh at the end of sentences, a completely arbitrary plot that's old told in dialogues and interactions with world stuff, slow and deliberate combat focused on positioning, timing and stamina management, leveling up at breaches by spending the resource dropped by enemies that you lose when you die.It's a very safe pick if you enjoy Dark Souls and don't mind fighting the same guys over and over.overall 8.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Hellpoint

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome! I am having a blast. Still early, but this is Dark Souls meets Doom and Event Horizon...incredibly unique and fresh formula for a souls-like. The atmosphere is top notch and the combat, where souls-like games tend to falter, is superb. One of the better souls-likes I have played. That said, it could use some polish. I don't get the complaint about there being "nothing new here". That's really comical. It's like Dark Souls on a space station orbiting a Black Hole! Nothing new? Really? There are also really cool mechanics around weapons and the black hole that are obviously new and add to the formula...totally not getting the nothing new grind.   However, it's not perfect. The fast travel system is horrible and will have you covering the same ground over and over. The level design is top end, but it would really benefit from unfettered fast travel. The fact that they added jumping is really cool, but some of the jumping sequences feel like you have to be more lucky than good...which is the cardinal sin for souls-likes, imo. Simply dying a lot is not what makes a souls game. It has to feel fair, and while the combat here is fine in that regard, I died way too many times to jump falls rather than enemies, and I died at least 10 times on 3 specific jumps in the game. Basically, it just feels gimmicky in a game like this, not unlike the fast travel mechanic. Falling from the same distance will also do different amounts of damage. There doesn't seem to be a real formula to it at all, it just arbitrarily decides if you will survive or not. Finally, I don't even want to remember the final, "real" boss.   Hellpoint is awesome and feels like it could have been a gem on the same level as its inspiration. Hopefully it will continue to be patched and improved. I expect that it will only improve because the devs have done an awesome job supporting it thus far. Prepare to be frustrated, but it will keep pulling you back in. Well worth the price, solid 8 as it stands now. Solid souls-like!

_childDocuments_.review: Hellpoint is a wholly different souls-like when it comes to character progression. It took me until my 3rd playthrough to figure out that leveling up isn't really part of the progression system. You only want to meet the bare minimum stat requirements for your gear; after that raise Health, Stamina, Energy, & "Load" to preference. Beyond those only put your Axions [this game's version or Souls] into upgrading weapon/shield/firearm/catalyst chips. Upgrading these chips is very important for gameplay. The minimum for a shield chip is "+8 chip" on a Tribal Shield(DLC) [any other shield needs higher rank] to not lose Stamina while blocking. There is no upper limit to chip upgrades [Ex: I have a +744 Martial Melee Weapon chip].

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, so, it's a little clunky, but it is fun.If you're a fan of 80's sci-fi and HR Giger then you'll appreciate the work that went into this game.It is a Souls-clone, but it brings a few elements that make it unique.The game throws enough new things at you that it feels like it has it's own stamp on stat building.You have a hub (space port) like DS, the hub is huge and contains *secrets*You can tell the developers had fun making this game, you can leave messages, invite, weapon customization, material break-down, NPCs.This game is not ground-breaking, but it does scratch the itch until Elden Ring launches....someday.

_childDocuments_.review: Really exceptionally well-done for this studio's first foray into the world of games!Action RPG in the Soulslike box, really interesting designs, fun and enjoyable weapons with a knowledge system for each weapon that really adds a lot to things, world design is fantastic and the lore feels absolutely perfect for a Souls fan like myself.My only gripe, and unfortunately a big one, is the platforming. There are some platforming sections in the game and it is definitely not the game's strong suit. Moving through the air feels far too floaty in comparison to normal movement, sometimes jump inputs are stored resulting in a death, and there are literally a few spots where it seems like they didn't really test out the platforming themselves as the character clips against objects and plummets to death when trying to jump to the intended ledge. That being said, there aren't too many of these moments, and most are just optional paths for random loot so you can avoid them mostly.If you enjoy soulslike games, get this one, it's absolutely a treat and the "anger" it has made me feel at times, due to my own mistakes, was one of the closest to the "anger" that Dark Souls made me feel.Can't wait for their next project!

_childDocuments_.review: Genre - Sci-Fi Budget Dark Souls LikeI am late to the party, but that isn't always a bad thing. I have finished the final boss on difficulty 1 with much co-op play, and here are my thoughts.Hella fun, the game has some of the dark souls elements but with a reliable co-op and fair breach (bonfire) spacing it doesn't become frustrating. You can increase/decrease difficulty at a whim allowing for a more sandbox play style.The bosses are varied enough and offer a decent challenge, but have clear weaknesses. There are also multiple ways to defeat them (Sekiro!). The mobs are quite varied and offer variable difficulty. Some are like mini bosses, whilst some are cannon fodder.The travelling around can be confusing at first due to there being no map, but with co-op you can always get a 2nd pair of eyes. Your skill allocations are locked so you might need to create multiple character builds though as I can't see a re-spec option yet.Weapons, Armour and accessory drops seem fairly unique and will encourage you to collect them all. There are also at least 2 different ways to heal (flasks), which allows you to customise your build more. Ranged is key and also varied from staffs and guns to laser cubes.I think this game has become a gem in the rough over the time and deserves a look (especially on sale).

_childDocuments_.review: It has been years since I have wanted to complete a game more than three times. This has broken that trend, and I haven't fully completed it yet.This game is very difficult, but that is what makes it so satisfying. Where you die, a ghost of your former self will be waiting to slay you. Items and materials are well hidden and/or hard to get from a trapped room. Enemies pack a punch, and can surprise you out of nowhere. Energy (mana) and health regen options are filled by landing blows on enemies - not by going to a breach (hub). However, after you get through the challenge, you feel like you've accomplished something great.Level design is absolutely stellar. The whole game world is connected in some way, and I found myself being able to traverse it faster as I progressed through each stage. Some of the areas can be confusing, but it's easy enough to distinguish areas that you have been to before.The art style is dark - I would dare say darker than Dark Souls. It will really make you feel like you are in a dark, occult-filled sci-fi atmosphere. Enemies, the play areas, armor, weapons, effects; you name it. It's engrossing. That said, a few textures are a bit low res (mostly the outer scenery, but is rare), but it won't detract from the experience.The sound is nothing short of amazing. The soundtrack fits this game perfectly, and really adds to the overall atmosphere. The enemies sound menacing, weapons have appropriate "meaty" sounds, and they don't get repetitive.Combat is exactly what you would expect out of a souls style game. You can dodge, block, activate projectile based attacks, and link combos. They added jumping into the mix, and it helps bring another dimension to the combat. My only wish is that they would add in a back stabbing animation and knockback for the player when you are hit.All in all, this game is a massive win for this studio. I really hope they decide to make DLC and possibly a sequel. This universe with its atmosphere, game play, sound design, and overall attention to detail is second to none.I would actually say this is a near-perfect souls like experience.

_childDocuments_.review: For me, this is the closest I came to reliving that "What is going on?"-feeling of mystery and being lost that I got in the first Dark Souls (and none of the direct sequels, before you ask). The design of the world, how cramped and bleak it all feels, and even that some mechanics are very obscure and not explained at all, but you have to piece it together yourself bit by bit. So yeah, if you loved the first Dark Souls and still love it today, I think you will love this as well. It gives the same feeling - that includes the jank, by the way. From Software games have become way more polished than 10 years ago, but this does not try to be Dark Souls 3 in space, it's Dark Souls 1 in space. And I love it for that. It's dripping with atmosphere.

_childDocuments_.review: The last true ending BOSS IS GARBAGE, ABSOLUTE TRASH, I had great fun playing this game, going for almost 100% completion, then this spit in the face appeared and made me consider sending hatemail to the devs. I officially give up and will watch the endings on yt, ♥♥♥♥ it.So I really recommend this game, but either skip the true ending bs, or make sure you have a good build to live through that.So hellpoint is a very soulsy game, no question about that. Almost all mechanics you'd expect are here, builds, secret passages, this doesnt open from this side, roll dodging, stamina management, renewable health items at checkpoints, and currency to be retrieved on death.The interconnected world with a very labirynth like layout is a huge highlight of this game, definitely reminding me of exploring DS1 for the first time. There is a lot of obscure stuff you can miss, so you can go through the game normally for like 7 hours and complete it, but if you're exploring all branches, all secret passages, then that really adds to the playthrough, easily doubles that.The levels have a really good sci fi horror atmosphere to it, with a religious art deco district as well. Probably the biggest gripe I have about the atmosphere is the enemy variety, especially all those recolored fish enemies.Visuals are good too, works silky smooth on my PC in 144 fps, and looks appropriately flashy. Animations are also well done, I see that the kickstarter money was put to good use in this department.Sound is off unfortunately, soundbytes sound ok, even if they're not really varied, music is ambient and suitable as well, but there are constant issues with it cutting off, drowning out instead of overlapping, as well as bad audio mixing at parts. Audio is also terrible in that aforementioned last bossfight.Controls are responsive for the most part, but platforming in the soulsy games apparently must have jank and awfulness to them. Sprint trigger is inconsistent on platforms so small, jumps may have oddly varied distances sometimes, and on landing there is a slight slide, the absolute worst thing to put in in a precision platforming. A small nitpick is an odd and small window of animation cancelling, I understand why it might be small for attacks, but cancelling healing to dodge could've been much easier.So the combat for the most part is pretty good, I haven't used to many ranged weapons, but no doubt the biggest cheese potential is there. All weapons have also very varied movesets, even if similar to DS3, straight swords and other fast weapons like that are clearly the best melee choice. Especially weird for me were halberds, their standard attack is stupid slow, has almost no stagger to it as well, while sprinting and dodge attack are better in both those aspects. Armor also is kinda secondary, you will probably just go for best defense to physical and other common damage, if equip load allows it.While the regular enemies are easily dispatchable, while still posing threat, the most interesting fights would be with the bosses, and here a financial shortcoming is bright in display.There are only 3 unique bosses, 2 final bosses, and rest is reused assets, that is 11 reused enemies, that is a very disappointing thing for a game like that, variety in bosses is something that may keep you going back to the game after completing it, and here that is a one less reason for it too.So the 2 final bosses I didn't really count as the same as unique 3 bosses, I have a very simple reason, they are completely terrible. To let you visualize it - first end boss is like a bed of chaos, while second is like shadows of yarnham combined with wintern lanterns in there too.To say it disappoints me, is putting it lightly.The first awful one I can manage, but second is just a nightmare, here's why:It consists of an npc that chases you, hits you and stuns you, it is a nuisance, but the most managable part of it (even though the arena is so dark you barely see that idiot). And then the biggest fnnnnn a-hole floating in the back.It's a teleporting boss who's got it all, unlimited range, as well as AoE, on all "melee" attacks, a laser projectile spawning every 15 seconds as well, most of the attacks have high radiation (basically poison), so you're limited to heavy armors or dodgin perfectly all that stuff. If it wasn't enough, 2 of his attacks are an almost instakill, they have very little tell, to easily differ them from others, not to mention those attacks have heavy stun, so if the one hit kill attack didn't kill me instantly somehow, it put me on the floor, then the follow up killed me with no option to dodge. There is also the sound mixing part of the problem here, the attacks have unlimited range, but they have barely audible sounds to them, and the one shot attacks don't have special sounds either, not to mention those sounds being so quiet, that I had to mute the song to actually dodge them better.The devs will probably not read this but PLEAAAAASE, change some stuff about it, it's just a furstrating mess and a combination of all the worst elements in bad bosses from the souls series. Just nerfing the circle of laser projectile barrage would be nice.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok wow, first of all. Ignore the negative reviews.People see things through rose colored glasses, no one remembers how the first Souls game was actually like...Now, onto this game. I played the beta over a year ago and loved it, and it was super unpolished, the controls weren't too responsive, the attacks felt floaty(like dark souls 2 cough cough) I am happy to say that it's been addressed. The combat feels great, there's weight to the attacks, it doesn't just feel like you're waving a weapon around the dodge feels sooo good, think Bloodborne. The graphics are not some omg out of this world graphics, but they're really good for what it is, people are expecting some insane budget from a super small studio here, they are good, shadows look great, it's detailed enough to appreciate the art and locales. I really think the style of graphics suit this game perfect.The exploration, the exploration is really good, there's a lot of hidden passageways to be found and shortcuts galore. I accidentally fell somewhere and turned out to be great as I found a weapon in some nook, exploration definitely pays off in this game, and the ability to jump around allows you to get to a lot of places, I love the vertical exploration aspect. The skill system is pretty good, usual build situations, strength for heavy weapons, their version of dex for quick weapons. The death system is interesting, it spawns a ghost that you can kill and should kill before it kills you(think Hollow Knight). The music is good when it's there, again, it's the usual gloomy type of environmental music you'd find in this genre. The gameplay overall feels very very smooth, again, this is coming from someone who played the beta and found it wonky and janky.  It's good, the controls are responsive, and I do think that with a couple of patches they can fine tune them even more, but it's not like you press a button and the character doesn't  move right. This game has definitely scratched that Souls itch. Honestly, it feels like a DS in space. I honestly hope it sells well because I'd love to see what they can do in the future with a bigger budget. And finally, I can't complain about the multiplayer because I haven't tried it nor am I going to anytime soon. I love soloing my games, as I like to say "git good" and very good job peeps at Cradle Games. This game was well worth the wait, just a tad more polish and this gem will shine to bright. Now, back to playing, I'm spending precious time away from this baby<3

_childDocuments_.review: The fact that this is a sci-fi Souls-like is beyond obvious to everyone, however what makes it more of a souls-like than most others is the exploration. The level design, intricate shortcuts, ways around and even legitimate jumping puzzles with a dedicated jump button are excellent additions and something that people don't realize about the "souls formula".Sure the bosses, combat and enemies are important but for many Dark Souls games (specifically Demon's and Dark Souls 1) the level exploration is a huge aspect, something that later Souls titles forgot and focused more one difficulty and combat, making them more linear in the process. In Hellpoint you get so much exploration that a secret area like Ash Lake can be in every other area, expanding the level hugely if you just find a hidden wall or turn away from the road leading to the boss.The only real issues are a few minor bugs (like off-hand weapon stops firing, which reloading/level transition fixes) and some collision boxes either being too loose or weirdly absent from objects (like jumping on a pile of rubble and floating on top of it since the character can't land there, though moving fixes this)For any souls fan this is a must get, and for anyone who just enjoys expansive sci-fi worlds to explore while going through an RPG progression system.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played, finished and gotten every achievement in every Fromsoft game since Demon's Souls. I've tried most of the not-souls and bounced off each one for some reason. This not-souls is the best one I've played.It absolutely captures the sense of mystery and discovery of Dark Souls. Every area is jammed full of passages to explore, with strange things, people and loot.The combat is excellent, taking the quicker style of Bloodborne but keeping the possibility of slower, more methodical combat if you want it. It has streamlined a few things, making it easier than a Souls. You gain back your Estus charge equivalent through combat, resulting in fewer trips back to the not-bonfire and less overall difficulty. The sound design is excellent, perfectly emulating a dark, spooky, empty space station. The place groans and echoes as you wander in the dark.I haven't run into any bugs. I honestly don't know where the claims of jank are coming from. Could it be better? Sure, but it doesn't need to be. We don't get spooky games that aren't about running away from boring things anymore. This is the direction horror gaming should have taken.

_childDocuments_.review: Hellpoint is essentially Dark Souls, but with an aesthetic resembling a mix of Alien and Hellraiser.  The gameplay resembles Dark Souls to a tee, with similar movement, blocking/dodging, leveling and death penalty systems.  If you enjoyed any of the Soulsborn games, you will get some fun out of Hellpoint.  The mood and environments in this are great.  Taking place on an immense derelict station infected by madness and dark gods, Hellpoint is filled with gigantic rooms built in a grandiose architectural style.  You really get a sense of the scale, with enormous pits, drop-offs and a feeling that--at any moment, you could fall to your death or get sucked into the vastness of space.  Unlike Dark Souls, this game features a jump button, along with a number of harrowing platforming segments that are both nerve-wracking and potentially frustrating due to so-so controls.  While I enjoyed the Giger-esque style, the creature designs did not have much variety, and I did not find any of them to be particularly threatening or creepy.  The same goes for the environments.  While I loved the expansive abandoned station, I feel that Hellpoint could have used a few more really weird alien areas to fully take advantage of its theme and style.  The weapon/armor sets and build options were fine, though nothing remarkable, and I feel that the game could have benefited from a more robust character build system, with a some more interesting options.One fun aspect to the game was the secrets; with items hidden behind secret doors, or along barely-visible (or even normally invisible) ledges.  There were hidden codes for optional areas, multiple endings, and more.Overall, this was a fun game and I would recommend it.  While it's not anything revolutionary, Hellpoint is a fun soulslike game that will entertain any fans of the genre.  7/10

_childDocuments_.review: It’s Dark Souls in space. No pause menu, a small nudge in a singular direction that can spiral into several paths toward an unknown goal. It lacks the polish that would make it a pretty good game, but this lack of polish does not hamstring a competently made Souls-like.The sound design of this game wobbles back and forth between awful and just good enough to be useful in combat. Most of the things that need sound queues, like attacks from giant bosses, have those and were what I used to avoid/guard against their strikes. At other times the sound is either absent, too quiet, or horribly inconsistent. The lighting works very well with the ruined derelict space station you are tasked to explore, almost excusing how the sounds do not work all the time.It’s Dark Souls, but with less options that are locked behind a needless crafting system. To get most of the interesting weapons require crafting, which means finding useless items in the field and bringing them back to a 3D printer with a specific blue-print and spending Space-Souls to get a new item. Upgrading said items requires upgrade chips which then can be boosted with more Space-Souls.Your three methods of damaging enemies is to bonk them in melee, shoot them with a space gun until you run out of energy, or shoot them with a space-magic stick until you run out of energy. Considering the main way you regain your energy with which to shoot the guns or space-magic is bonking the enemy with a space-stick, you will always be reduced to cave-man bonking with various degrees of sharp space-sticks.Unique to this Souls-Like, as far as I am aware, is that weapons earn EXP when used to bonk/blast things. These unlock passive perks granted when the weapon is equipped, and special attacks that are assigned to the special attack button. These attacks also consume energy.Healing in this Souls-Like is restrictive, and you never have as much as you’d like of it. Healing has its own resource which is only replenished in three ways:All of the healing methods in the game, sparing your Omni-Cube’s very slow heal, fully heal you with varying degrees of speed. The blue med-hypo, which also purges Radiation from your system, is arguably the most important healing item as Radiation is the most deadly status effect in the game. You will not find enough healing upgrades to max out your healing capacity in one playthrough, so you are better off committing those upgrades to a single healing source.There is a jump button in this souls-like, and the game’s tips encourage you to use jump/dodge attacks to deal extra damage. This extra damage is significant and the extra finesse needed to get that extra damage is engaging and needed. The jumping is a pseudo-commitment; you cannot adjust your jump after leaping, but that means with practice you can gauge how far you can jump. Jumping about can lead to interesting places, and potentially interesting loot.There is a clock in the game that has unique bits attached to two specific time frames. Whenever the clock’s fast moving circle is at the 3 or 9 hour position, the chance for loot or better loot from enemies increases. And when the Eclipse Hour occurs, special passages or things open. I did not discover these things, but the loading screen tips suggest as much.There are also secret doors that are opened by smashing your face into a suspicious wall and pressing the interact button.Finally, there is only Opt-In PVP via duels. You will never experience a player purposefully invading your game to impede your gameplay.Your space-man protagonist is a synthetic human-being created by the space station’s AI for the task of figuring out what the heck is going on. This encourages you to sniff out logs and situations that help explain what everything on the space-station when to pot.Much like all the other Dark Souls games, you can completely ignore the plot and still beat it. But finding info can give context which can enrich the struggle. If you’re into that sort of passive, subtle story-telling.It’s Space Dark Souls, without the hateful PvP griefing but with a needless crafting system. The healing in the game is hamstrung compared to other souls-likes I have played, which did not allow me extra time to better learn the bosses’ attacks before a death. The combat gravitates heavily to melee attacking, so any character build is going to have melee be at the core. Dodging is more encouraged than using a shield, as dodge attacks have extra damage and your dodge mobility is faster and greater than that of a super cheetah. Additionally, hitting things in melee replenishes your healing resources, ensuring all combat will have you hitting your enemy with some sort of stick. Translate this to a New Game+ where enemies hit even harder and the only means of defense are dodge or grind levels until things do not hurt as much, and there is little reason to play after the one go.The story is there. I did not find it engaging or satisfying.I would only recommend this game to diehard Souls-like fans that need to scratch that difficult combat itch. The game is competent enough to do that, but does not do enough to innovate or break from the Dark Souls mold in battle or story.

_childDocuments_.review: What a tough game to recommend. It's very rough and has a lot of faults. If you like the look of the setting and have already played all the FromSoft games and still wanting more then I say give this a go. It really is a cool setting and every time I thought about stopping it surprised me with something that kept me going.The enemy variety is really low. Not only do bosses get reused as regular enemies but the more you play the less variety there is as enemies actually get removed from the game. Due to the more open design I ended up fighting mini mob versions of a boss before the actual boss itself. Really disappointing when the movesets are exactly the same with only a health bar to mark the difference. None of the bosses were memorable. Only the final one was even a little interesting and that was a negative because it had too much going on (if you're going for true ending).Exploration started off really great. I appreciated that they wanted to encourage this. But the jumping was horrible and you can't fall far without dying. I had more deaths from falling than from enemies. That's a bad sign when you're not playing a platformer. And when you finally made it, the reward was hardly worth it. Some of the rewards I got near the end of the game which were also hidden behind long secrets were duplicates of things I had been using for most of my run.Combat is janky. It felt like the Elex of souls-likes. Telegraphing felt pointless when you couldn't tell when the attacks would come due to long wind-ups then quick releases. Then even if you dodge the attacks will often track you anyway. If you do die to enemies then next time you face them you also have to contend with a ghost of yourself. Super cool idea that just ended up being annoying. I got that feeling a lot playing this game. Things that made me say "wow I would really like that if only...".Yet after finishing Elden Ring which I thought was great and having these complaints (and so many more) I still somehow recommend it. Maybe it was the obvious Hellraiser inspiration letting me play as Pinhead with my own cube.

_childDocuments_.review: Hellpoint, although it falls short on a few elements along the way, delivers a satisfying RPG/dungeon-crawling experience. The lows are unimaginative and confusing level design, nauseating visual effects with no accessibility options, and a vague sense of direction. Fortunately, these lows are countered by the highs of incredible science fiction visuals, a unique cosmic horror theme and a visceral combat loop that will manage to keep most players hooked. Hellpoint's draw is complete with it's splitscreen local co-op and replay value. If all this sounds good to you, then give it a go (but use a controller, because apparently every studio taking notes from From Software refuses to address the horrid keyboard playability of the genre).

_childDocuments_.review: Version played: Steam Build 357 - Server 1.03 - Excellent atmosphere. It's Dark Souls meets a tamer version of Dead Space.- Game has an decent-sized arsenal and armory for a indie souls-like.- You won't feel guilty for using the same weapon over and over. The game has a reward system on each weapon that gives passive buffs and/or skills after you hit enemies a number of times. - Weapon upgrade system is neat. Instead of grinding for upgrade stones for each weapon, you have chips that enhance certain atributes. You can equip and unequip the upgraded chips from your weapons and put them on new ones. No more regrets from upgrading weapon x and then finding a weapon y that is cooler to use.- A fair amount of content to consume because of level secrets, multiple endings, collecting items, co-op and duel PvP. - Game's music is forgettable.- Too many bosses are reused as normal enemies.- The game is quite janky. Examples: Many animations from the characters are weird; The UI for your items when you need to pick one for crafting/upgrading is just a list of all your items that you need to scroll through again and again; Your inventory can't be sorted and you can't drop your items.- Game has a lot of bugs. Examples: Sound effects become mute for no reason; Certain loot will vanish from the game after a certain point of the game is reached; Enemies pop up in your face or become invisible; If you hit the final boss as soon as its speech ends, the AI turns off; Running sometimes isn't activated when you hold down the running button.- The game has a platforming system that seems either bugged or badly crafted in regards to fall damage. Some jumps to other platforms will kill you while others with same height from other areas will deal a small amount of damage. Some jumps will kill you if you press the jump button to leave the platform your character was standing at but if you just drop down, you recieve a small amount of damage instead.- I'm not that much of a fan of this game's Fast Travel system. You need an item called Breach Syncronizer to connect one of your checkpoints to the others that can use fast travel. If you search every nook and cranny, you can find enough Syncronizers to connect all the important checkpoints. If you don't, you're going to have a bad time with the long backtracking in certain areas. Also, the checkpoints need to have their fast travel capabilities reactivated by Syncronizers each time the character starts a new game cycle...- Game has 66 coins scattered throughout the world to collect. Getting them all doesn't give you any rewards besides a Steam Achievement. Really lame to get just an achievement after all the effort.TL;DR - Recommended but i would wait for a sale. It's better than most indie souls-like games that i've played but the bugs and certain design decisions would make me hesitate picking this game up without a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Re-writing the review, as I've had a ton more time in it.I enjoy it a great deal, I recommend it still - just wanted to contextualize some of the pros and cons a bit.1- the game is rather janky at times, you can get stuck in geometry, or get the camera stuck in an odd place, making you die unfairly.2- the world is MASSIVE. maybe TOO massive. I am still finding new areas, still finding new weps and enemies and ways to die. I've only taken out 3 bosses so far, the game is big to the point where you aren't fighting 40 bosses. They're mostly spaced out pretty well.3- perfromance for you may vary, keep in mind you can only set graphical options in the main menu, not during game[play.4- the weps you find can be upgraded with " materia like " stones that you can find or craft, and you can upgrade those stones, unequip them from a wep, and place it on another 0 decent systemI addition to this, weps have an experience meter that gives you latent or active skills just by using them for awhile.5 - when you die, your ghost goes after you - these are literally your character - but they have seemingly unlimtied stamnina, much more attack and generally have the best AI out of all the enemies i've faced so far - they can path find you from alarmingly far distances to the point where you died. 6- bosses are fun, if too few ( so far ) My original review cited I didn't know if there were checkpoints ( ala bonfires ) there are, and you can connect them to each other using items ( which kinds sucks ) as the world is so large, you're gonna wish you could remove the links you've made, for future ones you discover. ( ie; fast travel is a bit of a pain ) there's some terrifyingly bad platforming, but that's always for additonal secrets and loot, you're not forced into precarious platforming to progress (not yet, at least ) The lighting may be too dark for some, and I agree - you can also adjust the power of the light sources in game, but I feel when you brighten it up, you lose atmosphere, and things get TOO bright for your eyes in some areas.few more minor things, no char creator, online is currently out of service sadly - but it does exist. The world is labyrinthian in nature, so it's easy to get lost. You can craft weps and armor, but not very often.I love the art direction, creature design, and mood the game presents in it's appearance. is that enough to justify it's shortcomings? no, but it's worth keeping in mind this is an indie team's first game, I've certainly played worse " souls like " games.

_childDocuments_.review: I've put seven hours into this game over the past three days and I wanted to put down my tentative thoughts on the game. I'll change this as I play more.Okay, I hesitated for a long time on this game. I was fairly intrigued by the Kickstarter. A game promising a soulslike experience with influences from Event Horizon, Lovecraft, and Giger sounded right up my alley. However, I've been burned before on that platform. I backed Stonehearth and Chasm, two mistakes that still haunt me to this day. So I didn't back it. What's more, the reviews on Steam didn't seem promising. The good reviews seemed lukewarm and the negative reviews looked downright damning.I can now say that I regret not backing it or buying it sooner. This game succeeds because of two elements: level design and world-building. I almost wanted to say that, in this game, they're one and the same. You see, the abandoned world of Irid Novo feels like a breathing corpse. The sounds, environments, and characters paint a picture that, true to the Souls formula, could not be told otherwise. The level design allows the world to be an interconnected maze that genuinely feels like a monumental space station.And speaking of mazes, there are secrets galore thus far. In just seven hours I've stumbled across at least four secret doors. A quick google search showed me that I have missed a fair amount already, so I'm excited to retread or replay in the future. This brings me to my final point for now.The comparison to Dark Souls will be inescapable. I'm a fan of the genre. Hell, Bloodborne is my favorite game of all time. I firmly believe From Software pushed game design into a different direction for the foreseeable future with their work. In the case of Hellpoint, the comparison to Soulsborne is fair and accurate, but there's a nagging thought I keep having. When Miyazaki made Demon Souls and Dark Souls, he achieved the, up to that point, impossible: he and his team made some good 3D Metroidvanias. And that's why Hellpoint works for me so far. This game reminds me of a Metroidvania in the best way possible. There's a breathtaking world to explore and unravel at your own pace.Wanna grind into until your character is as powerful and destructive as a black hole? Why not! Wanna poke around in everyone corner? ♥♥♥♥ it, you do you! Wanna speed run the game as fast as humanly possible? Go to town!So to wrap things up, I have to mention where I started this review-in-progress. This game isn't for everyone and that's totally fine. However, if you want to explore a mysterious haunted space station, take the leap. I didn't regret it and I hope you don't either.PS: Hellpoint and Sekiro have officially convinced me that more Soulslike games need a dedicated jump button. It allows for whackier combat and better exploration, end of story.*Edited for typos*

_childDocuments_.review: The dated visuals could be forgiven if the gameplay was somewhat decent. Things I don't like about this gameNonsensical level and redundant level designs. Huge areas and paths that end up to completely empty places with nothing to interact with. Rooms with a short set of stairs that lead to walls. Darkened areas in the first part of the game designed to make you fall to your death (if you think this is to teach you to watch where you step you're wrong, because this kind of trap doesn't come up in the later levels which are more well lit)Getting stuck on geometry, especially annoying when it happens on narrow ledges.Movement lacks weight/feedback, it almost feels like your character is ice skating.Platforming. Absolutely terrible. The number of times I've fallen to my death because the sprint in a sprinting jump didn't activate. The level design that has 1-way platforms where if you've landed on the wrong platform you have to either die or teleport back to the last checkpoint. The forward momentum on landing that makes your character unresponsive for a brief moment which can cause you to walk off a ledge. The lack of mid-air control to correct a jump if you overshoot it.There is currently no way to respec your character if you didn't like how you levelled them. Kind of dumb considering a first time player wouldn't understand where to put their points on the first playthrough. Punishes players for not looking at a guide before they play.You character going in to a frenzied break dance every time you die. Seriously Cradle Games, I know you seen this during testing. Just play an animation if you can't make the player rag doll properly.There are just too many little things that spoil the experience before I can recommend this game.I got this on sale for 1/2 price and I still feel ripped off.

_childDocuments_.review: The game was fun and had an interesting story - I really did enjoy the time I had playing. _childDocuments_.review: UPDATE: My complaints for this game still stand, with even more attention to even more bugs that cropped up during my playthrough, but I finished the game. This game is much more enjoyable in co-op.-----At its core, Hellpoint is a copycat. The combat is reminiscent of Dark Souls, its dodging mechanic almost identical to Bloodborne. In ways, its lore is hidden, just like Soulsborne games, if not a little more direct in its delivery. Bonfires in this game are known as breaches, and serve the exact same purpose as their counterparts.Orbiting around this core, however, are features and details that separate Hellpoint from its peers, make it a game of its own. Most people are quick to dismiss Hellpoint for its similarities to -- let's face it -- superior games, but those who give it time and attention will notice that it does tend to stand apart and establish its own identity.So, why am I giving this game a thumbs down? Poor game design and bugs, much like everyone else who finds themselves ultimately not liking this game.A fairly big bug that tends to get me killed more often than not is when the lock-on refuses to switch to enemies that are close to me. I've encountered this more times than I would have forgiven and, as of the time of this review, am dealing with it in a particularly frustrating boss fight.Another example of poor game design is the stamina drain. When dealing with stronger enemies, it feels like it takes two hits to drain your entire bar and, if you happen to be stunned, a full five seconds or longer to recover and move again, but in that time, you can get stunlocked over and over until you're dead. This is the most debilitating issue. Decreasing the difficulty often doesn't help because, even if the damage is slightly lessened, the stamina drain and overlong stun-state will just kill you anyway because everything's hitboxes are strangely wide.I want to like this game. I think the atmosphere and the setting are pretty great. The story is interesting as well, but it's hard to like a game whose design actively fights against you every encounter in which you find yourself. I'm not done with the game just yet, but if I can't find a way around issues that should have been fixed a while ago, I might have to drop the game for good.

_childDocuments_.review: A really solid entry to the souls-like genre that's worth checking out if you're a fan. If I had to make a quick comparison it's somewhere between Dark Souls 1 and Remnant: From the Ashes (leaning more towards the former).While it lacks the polish or graphical fidelity of something like DS3 or Sekiro, combat still feels solid with only a handful of hiccups, and a very strong art direction makes the game interesting to look at and dripping in atmosphere despite some relatively dated texture work and VFX.The space station is expansive and an explorer's delight, those who enjoy scouring every nook and cranny will appreciate the sheer amount of hidden goodies tucked away, and you're encouraged to return to areas as you get new tools to find even more.There's a surprising amount of platforming too which helps to make the environments feel a lot more open as you can freely jump about and are often required to do so.I appreciate that ranged weapons and the sorcery-equivalent feel more viable as main weapon choices due to the replenishing energy system and the ability to equip catalysts or firearms as an offhand weapon. Less restrictive stat requirements than a souls game also means I have more build flexibility and am more freely able to try new weapons I find, instead of most of them being completely useless if they don't align to my stats. Weapon upgrades are also more flexible with a system akin to Bloodborne's gems - rather than level up individual items you invest in chips which can be freely swapped between weapons.One of the major downsides is a gated fast travel system. Any breaches you find can be turned into nodes on the fast travel network but you are required to expend a limited item. At first I appreciate this as it encourages you to explore and use these more thoughtfully, balancing between resting now or going deeper, but later in the game it can make backtracking a chore - especially if your early ones were used carelessly. I would appreciate a way to craft this item or something to alleviate this towards the later parts of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Not recommended. There are better alternatives for a similar price. Here's just some of the problems I had with the game.I experienced a game crash the reverted my character file back a whole session. I lost 4 hour of gear and axioms. Do NOT alt-f4 out of the game, as that can cause you to lose progress.While playing multiplayer, the final boss broke during the last battle and the co-op player wasn't able to target them or take damage from them until we did a full reset.  is a huge problem in multiplayer. Enemies that are knocked down or stunned don't appear to be on the other player's screen. Bosses that move around quickly just teleport all over the place.  Some levels were pretty okay, but by and large it is a mess. Most maps are labyrinths that lead to dead ends (sometimes literally rooms that serve no purpose and have no loot, or stairways that go nowhere) with repeating items and gear sets that make exploration mostly meaningless. Lore is spread all over the map in text files that dump exposition on you in the worst way. You will unlock many pointless shortcuts, sometimes going through elaborate dungeons only to pop out in the very first area of the game to unlock a single door so you can ... idk, back track all the way to the start for no reason at all? There are no mini bosses, and only a handful of NPC's to interact with. After you defeat a boss expect to see them copy-pasted all over the map for the rest of the game. There is little to no enemy variation at all. The enemies you fight in the first few seconds of the game are pretty much the same enemies you'll fight for 80% of the game.Most weapons and movement don't seem to have any weight to them. If you lock onto an enemy, your character snaps onto them and all your attack animations just spin around at light speed to wherever the enemy is located. This is true for enemies as well. Massive bosses will spin on a dime to attack you if you get behind them.The floatiness is excusable with combat, because, well, no one is expecting this game to be AAA quality anyways. But for some reason they decided that this game needed to be an action platformer. Your character jumps 8 feet in the air, and slides on the ground like butter. If you've ever played crash banditcoot, it is sort of like that, which is totally out of place for a souls-like. You WILL jump on tiny platforms and slide off of them. You WILL watch your friend bump his head on a ceiling and die. In Co-Op the bosses are all trivial. 90% of the bosses will only aggro on one player, which allows the other to follow along behind and kill them without any effort at all. In my play-through with a friend, we defeated the final boss by: player one dodging attacks while player 2 used a catalyst to kill him. Player 2 did not even move during the whole fight with the FINAL BOSS. The single player experience on the other hand is atrocious, especially if you make the mistake of using a slow strength weapon like I did. Almost every boss past the first two will one shot you, or use a combo to kill you with no chance to put an input in to escape. If you plan on playing solo, I don't recommend playing a str. build. With a weapon like the column you can only land about 1 light attack safely in most boss fights before you have to run away, unless you get a lucky stun. Heavy attacks are almost always punished by an instant death. I ended up having to find a kickstarter code for a long-sword that swings much faster in order to even stand a chance against most of the bosses.There is no cheat protection in this game and it is trivial to boost your stats. Take that for what you will. Player characters will never have enough health to survive more than a few hits from another equal-level character even with the best armor in the game and a large healthpool. Playing pvp at the end of the game was a game of who could land a single melee attack first. Not fun. There are two separate crafting tables with large menus to craft items. You find blueprints around the map and huge amounts of materials if you explore. No problem. Most of the materials you need to craft the actual good weapons are not dropped by enemies, but are a single item sitting somewhere in the dungeon. Get the wiki out boys.There is only one single weapon upgrade bench in the whole game, and it is in the hub. You put a component in the weapon and now it has an ability. Awesome. But, what you probably won't know or figure out intuitively is that you can press right and left on the arrow keys to upgrade the weapon to more than +1. The game's only tip about this is the word "increase" on the bottom of that crafting menu written in 5 point font. Ok here is where the real salt comes into play. There are two key items in the first area that you will almost certainly miss without a guide. Both the EVA suit and a key to the horrible flesh hand boss area are behind hidden doors. If you don't grab them, tough ♥♥♥♥. Your only hope is to run around the whole game mashing interact on the walls (specific ones that have two black vertical bars) if you want to be sure you can play the game.The EVA suit could be a topic on its own. In order to get it, you have to find a hidden door, find a hidden elevator, go through an airlock, and do a suicide dash out to it. You MUST have this item to go to an entire area of the game. FUN.Last thing about the hidden doors. They are hardly hidden 90% of the time. If you play in offline mode, the devs have put yellow handprints around the doors so you know where they are or instructions to unlock them. What is even the point of the hidden doors if you are going to make them mandatory parts of the game AND display where they are with neon lights?This is the nitty gritty stuff but: in the final few areas of the games you fight enemies that drop 500 axioms each. Why am I still picking up axioms off the ground that are like 200? Why? Why? Why? Catalysts and reflex weapons are the best in the game by FAR. That would be okay normally but there is no way to reset your stats, so you either have to start the game all over again or just tough it out. I went with the latter and surprise surprise I had a terrible experience. The art was okay so basically 2/10. Still better than anything Ubisoft has put out in the last 5 years.

_childDocuments_.review: First i would say any Review that is below 3-4 hours is invalid. The game gets much better after the first 1-2 areas. perfect.Pros:-a LOT of levels that are interconnected-diverse Areas, most have their own charm/atmosphere, i love the art design, it gave me Bioshock in space vibes-Levels are logically designed, and memorable for the most part, many souls like dont achieve that-the backstory and lore is interesting and does a lot for the world building and atmosphere-weapons, all your weapons have exp bars and can be upgraded by killing enemies to unlock more powerful active and passive abilities, i absolutely LOVE this system, it is amazing, not only can you upgrade your weapon stat wise like dark souls but you have an alternative progression, it keeps making me want to try them all and see what i unlock next-so many hidden secrets and loot, i loved the exploration so much, if you explore all in your level or looking up a guide now and then, you really appreciate the art and level design-steady good progression, i dont know if it got patched after launch, but i never felt overwhelmed or out matched, if you do your exploration, slog through the first 1-3 levels, it has a great difficulty curve(as in most souls/like games first few levels are hardest then it gets better)-sound design is great, it makes you really feel like you are on that alien space station, with creepy sh*t around every corner-a lot of replayability, trying new builds, unlocking different encounters in NG+ and so on, i will continue my journey sooner or later-the black hole clock is a cool idea, and unlocking those secret gates was also a nice exploration, i just wished we could skip time/fast wait, sometimes i just stood around waiting for the clock so i didnt need to go back and forth again-art and graphics are decent and clean, not next gen but good enough, the atmosphere and design makes it even better-THE GAME ONLY NEEDS 6 GB, ALL DEVELOPERS SHOULD BE ASHAMED BY THEIR 100GB+ GARBAGE GAMES FFS-jumping puzzles are fine after you get used to, all people who fail, get gud, same as combat in souls likes-long game, depending if you kill optional bosses, do exploration, side quests, black hole events, use guides or not, this game can easy take 30-45 hours for one playthrough, and then you get more with NG+ and other builds-great art design on weapons and armors, i just wished we could upgrade all our armors as we do weapons, unlock abilities or sets gave us boni-Catalyst weapons are f*cking amazingCons:-the Space background when you look outside is too low res, i dont know who did this , but please just exchange a high res picture, the galaxys/stars look awful-the Sentinels in the first level are just bad, yea you can kill them if you know how, but still... many people got problems with them, they are also one of the few enemies that have "cancer movements" what i mean by _childDocuments_.review: I beat this game in local co-op and can't really recommend it. It's not *terrible* but it's extremely mediocre with several glaring technical and design issues. My partner and I were pushing to finish this game ASAP once the end boss was in sight.Pros:- Pretty cool atmosphere and lore- The combat ..feels OK outside the often poor AI.- Local split screen coop is rare for this sort of game and was appreciated- Some of the environments were visually pretty impressive for an indy gameCons:- This game has a debuff, "insanity" which I ♥♥♥♥ you not *zooms your camera way out + fish eyes it* for several seconds. It's never explained and is very common. This coupled with the already poor camera and smaller view in split screen made me wonder what the devs were thinking...- Terrible lock on system (the "lock on" indicator is tiny and hard to see in the dark which is where you spend the entire game, the right stick switching enemies often won't work or will lock onto mobs through walls). The camera will flip around or stare at ceilings / floors very often in all sorts of situations.- Coop has all sorts of bizarre design issues like if player 1 dies, player 2 dies instantly too. However, player 2 doesn't lose their "souls" if this happens so by end game player 2 will be several levels higher than player 1. - Player 2 also can't interact with quest items, npcs or doors.- Map areas are huge mazes that branch off constantly, and all the corridors look the same. You're going to get lost and waste time. Walkthroughs online were mediocre.- Many of the map branches just lead to dead ends or have very little payoff- Most of the weapons and armor you'll find will be useless, there's way too many stats to pump  points into. I think maybe 10-20% of the equipment we found were equipable, the rest were utterly useless besides scrapping.- Too many places to fall to your death right around corners or due to darkness. The jumping was kind of awkward, the amount of HP you'd lose from falls was wildly inconsistent too.- The levels are insanely dark and your flashlight takes constant energy to use (flashlights in the future go out in 15 mins? what?). Energy is also how you use your weapon's special move, so.- Energy and healing pots won't recharge at checkpoints- You seem to gain both heals and energy from damaging enemies, but in co-op it doesn't share so if one player is in front getting all the kills, the back person gets nothing (you can't swing through partners and there's a lot of narrow corridors so this happens often).- The bosses and enemies in general have AIs that simply can't handle 2 players, one player can literally just kite them while the other wrecks them from behind. We beat the entire game this way and the bosses were mostly a joke. Considering tough bosses is kind of a cornerstone of soulslikes, this was pretty disappointing.- Had random game stuttering on a high spec systemTL;DR: if you're desperate for a co-op soulslike and have a ton of patience maybe this is worth it on sale. Overall the terrible level design, camera (featuring "insanity") issues, bad / easy AI and other weird design decisions hold this game back from being anything other than a mediocre souls imitator. Would not recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Needs more work in my humble opinion; Spawn timers should be shortened as farming is a chore right now. Combat for the moment is really just about either A) killing the enemy before they can attack  you, or B) waiting for them to overextend - I know this sounds fine, but Sekiro really raised the bar in terms of active engagement in combat. Theres a lot of minor tweaks that should have been done before this was released but I couldn't possibly give this a thumbs down. Its fun in spite of its problems. its a 6.5 or 7 out of 10 in its current state. the atmosphere and world to me is a 10, and whoever did that alien voice should win an award - so awesome. Give it a shot if you're a die hard souls fan, its definitely not easy and u'll find it refreshing, in its own dysfunctional sort of way. _childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic souls-like title that is a perfect example of how to make a souls-like the RIGHT way. A lovely blend of Dark Souls and Deadspace, Hellpoint has a lot of great potential and fun.Exploring:Took me a while to complete, I like to explore everything before going down the 'right path'. Only this games map is so huge and seemingly interconnected that I found myself finding entirely new areas to explore every time I went down the beaten path. Turns out there is no 'right path', and you can find another way to get to where you need to go most of the time. Truly, this was a fun and enjoyable outcome for me, I felt blissfully overwhelmed and constantly had to plan and think about my path, especially since there is limited fast travel. Combat: The combat is familiar if you have completed a dark souls title, feels very similar to DS1 in my opinion with its low complexity. Weight matters, builds matter, and there are guns too. Its a little unpolished if you're coming from a newer title like Elden Ring, but still very enjoyable. There are some bosses that become enemies types, but there are a handful of very unique and interesting boss designs as well. I did encounter a few bugs, such as a boss that dodged through a wall and fell to their death, or myself falling through the floor to my death; but these bugs where minimal and not game breaking. Weapons and armor are pretty slim pickings in the early game, but later on there are several different builds and styles you can pick and choose from to round your character off. Lore:This game has some crazy lore, and the environments fit the theme and story telling very well. Being on a dying space station that orbits a black hole and has 3 demi-gods on board is something I was not expecting going into this game. The  usage of time was also a very unexpected mechanic, where we orbit the black hole and even have two times a day when the station goes through the accretion disc of the black hole, creating a nightmarish skybox and spawning some unique encounters across the map. I especially enjoyed how the story unfolded as we learned more and more by exploring the environment and reading notes, wall markings, items, etc. This title is a must play for Souls addicts like myself, and has quickly become one of my top ten souls likes

Then i found out the games' absolute worst mechanic "black hole hour". Basically there is a clock in the top left hand corner of the screen with a minute hand going around it in about an hour. There is a circle on the clock and when you minute hand reaches the circle its the "black hole hour" for about 5 minutes. during this time enemies drop more souls and you can access some special rooms but certain bosses also drop unique items only during black hole hour so if you want the item you have to wait around for it to be black hole hour and then beat the boss in 5 minutes. _childDocuments_.review: A highly enjoyable souls like. So far the areas are all really well interconnected, like the first half of Dark Souls 1. A lot of hidden stuff to explore and shortcuts to unlock. The atmosphere is incredibly well done with the sci fi architecture and ambient noises, and the enemy design is varied and a lot of detail went into their models. Combat is a little faster than DS1 and a little slower than DS3. The bosses are challenging and need strategy to tackle. IMHO Co-op is better than most soulslike games because you can follow the host across multiple zones, and you share resource pickups.There is a little jank in the movement and some invisible obstacles (very few I've noticed), and sometimes the netcode is kind of funky. The only real problem I have with the game is that in some cases you need to set up port forwarding to enable co-op, and not all players know how to do this, so sometimes it's hard to find a co-op partner. I've enjoyed my time so far. Not sure if this will hold up for the entire playthrough, most games start to peter out a bit by the 3rd act. Will update this review when I complete it.

Despite overall positive feeling i have to start with cons as there are things new player should be aware of. - Exploration      Hellpoin is fairly large game and exploration is at least 30% of playing time but it so unrewarding and dull. There are many istances where level desing it done well to encourage you to look there and there, sometimes they also throw little puzzle at you but after you get there the item what will you find will be:  1. Duplicate item you have already found few. And it even happens in puzzles which that type appear only once. I remeber once after finishing puzzle located in the final parts of game i got same item as i found just lying on the floor in early game.  2.  Axioms ( game´s currency for leveling up ) which are pretty useless coz in the most scenarios you can find 100-900 of these but what for when to lvl up i need 20 000.- Platforming     There are load of platforming segments but platforming itself is exremely simple. Just jump and land. If you will miss plaform 0,1 mm further you will fall , there is no edge grabbing ,nothing. And most of the time it leads to death as if there is no death pit, platforms are so hight  you just cant survive it with some character builds. Cherry on top , prize at the end is the item you have already found.- First ending       I am not talking here about overall story but there is ending which is really simple to get without even having beaten all bosses and explored all areas. And you dont know that end is coming. It is so anticlimatic you dont want to believe it is the end.  , at this part player is expectig twist. Not the end. When u will finish the game , there is no asking you if you wanna go to NG+. They will yeet you right there and will take some collectibles from you which were pain to find as i mentioned exploring becames really repetetive.- Bugs     Yeah , there is still load of them. Updates every now and than but u know , its just too much. Biggest shame is that multiplayer is hardly working now. Second player do not have animations , he is naked , flying or stuff like that happening. From PvPing you get nothing, not even those measly Axioms. _childDocuments_.review: This is going to be a weird one. Quick note, love Soulsborne games and have I don't even know how much time I spent on them. I've seen a few videos of Hellpoint, and figured after seeing the overall ratings, decided to give it a try. Played the game to a completion.Story, you're a Spawn created by the Author, a super AI. You are created for the purpose of collecting data and finding out what happened to the station Irid Novo. That's about as deep as I was able to tell: There's some cult stuff with Cosmic Gods but I never could find anything deeper than that.Gameplay, it's a Soulslike:  You start as a clean slate character with base stats, no classes to choose from. This gives you the freedom to create your character exactly how you want: Pump it in Strength and wield big weapons (what I did) or focus on occult things with Foresight and have access to unique tools.Healing and Energy (Mana) regenerates with melee attacks, kinda similar to Surge 2. It's still a good system and works well here.A neat thing is that various weapons can be passively upgraded just by using them: You start using a Demon Scythe and it's alright, but more you use it you can unlock unique passive and active abilities. Not all weapons have this, but a good number do.In addition, you can 'transfer' weapon upgrades between weapons. You put in condenser to increase the scaling of a certain stat, and then you can upgrade the condenser itself. Then, if you get a new weapon you want to try, you can, for free, yank out the condenser and place it in your new weapon. This makes trying out new weapons a breeze and is a great change, as Soulsborne games require you to upgrade new weapons from scratch if you want it on the level of your currently equipped one.One complaint about weapons: There's such a small variety. I'm a Strength build kinda guy, how I did my first run. However, I only found around four Strength weapons? All of which paling in comparison to my big greatsword that gave more Stamina, increased Strength scaling, and a run/dodge attack that hardcountered almost all the enemies in the game.  Think there's two Quality (Str/Dex) weapons. Total. Probably don't go that build.To build on that, there's duplicate loot. Near the start, I found an armor set that I couldn't use. That's fine, not expecting to use everything. Then, 30 minutes later, I found the same exact set! Why is there two? It makes finding loot, one of the most exciting things about Soulsborne exploration, feel lackluster. It's like finding Havel's set, then going to Archives and finding it again. Even some KEY items are duplicated!The UI is messy: Inventory cannot be sorted, meaning you have to dig through it every time you get something new (Even more of a pain with duplicates). If you want to break down materials (for crafting) or gear, you have to select the item, then confirm it with a different button, and then you are booted back to the main crafting menu. You have to break down every piece of gear individually. I tolerated the duplicate items because navigating the UI was just that annoying.There's a TON of secrets, some involving puzzles that you have to find clues for. I know I didn't come close to finding everything my first time. There's some really obscure stuff to figure out, which is really neat! What isn't so neat, are items required for progression hidden in super secrets.To access a new area to complete the game, you have to first find a hidden door (It's Dark Souls 2 rules: Interact button against doors). You access a hidden area, get some stuff and a crafting station. Did you know, though, that there's a SECOND hidden door in that hidden area that contains a key to a late game area containing one of the three big bosses you must fight? This kind of exploration should be for secret areas, items, or encounters, not for progression through the game.You are given no actual direction. "Go out and collect data" doesn't help when I'm wandering a hyper huge area looking for the one button, item, or trigger I happened to miss. Sure, being lost is part of the experience, but even Soulsborne games at least point you in a direction. 30-35% of my gameplay was just wandering around completely lost, fighting the same enemies. This is made worse by fast travel being a consumable item you use on Breaches, 'syncing' them to other Breaches you used the item on. This item is very rare, and of limited supply. Also requires knowledge of where best to use them for convenient travel.Enemy variety is extremely weak. There's some neat variations (especially later on) but even they get old fast. Get ready to fight the same zombies, fishes, and demons, especially when you get lost.Bosses range from absolute jokes to good to cheap as hell. There's a boss that 'poisons' you with radiation with a single hit. Not only do you take damage over time, your max health also starts to decrease. The chances you found the radiation cure item before this point is very unlikely. Another stuns you with a single stomp and then swipes at you before you can recover, likely cleaving your life bar in a single combo with you helpless to stop it.The final boss I fought, it's own arm blocked one of it's most powerful attacks, and I was out of range of it's melee, meaning it could only zap me with a weak beam as I just chopped it's arm. Another boss literally died in 4 hits. It's all over the place. There's good fights, of course, but the extremes really stand out.Finally, this game has a healthy amount of jank. Your character 'getting down' when they die, enemies getting stuck on terrain or flying at hyperspeed through walls, you getting stuck on invisible walls (fun when doing jumping puzzles), had a boss not move or react to me...There's a lot of weird stuff that happens here. It's a smaller studio, but man, the jank is hard to overlook.I missed a lot, and want to play again just to see if I can get another ending with a different build, or find some of the secrets I missed, and it will be better since I know my way around more, but I don't know. My playthrough was one of annoyance until I got my super sword, spammed Run/Dodge R2s (which pancakes 90% of the enemies and staggers bosses quickly) and found that key hidden behind two secret doors. Then I just didn't really feel much of anything. Some neat things at the end, but that's it.I don't think I can recommend Hellpoint for the $35 it's asking for. Unless you're really hungry for a new Soulsborne experience (And already played the heck out of the Cinders mod) and can tolerate/laugh at jank, I would recommend picking it up on a sale, if at all.Better than Lords of the Fallen, though. By multiple miles.(RE-EDIT: Experienced online, expressed views in the comments. Doesn't really change the overall tone of the review, sadly.)

_childDocuments_.review: It has its quirks, but beyond that I feel as though Cradle is on the right track and did well with their debut title.Anyone familiar with souls-likes will immediately feel right at home in Hellpoint.  The biggest distinctions I noticed was the focus on uncovering secrets and somewhat of a platforming focus (which isn't a downside by any means, it helps that there is a jump button and a degree of air control for these sections).For a first playthrough it really feels like you are seeking out to explore what exactly Irid Novo is since that's exactly the objective you are given from the start.  I feel this requirement eases newcomers in since it isn't giving a specific location to go to, just to explore at your own pace (and explore some more to find gear and stuff to help you explore parts that couldn't yet be accessed).My enjoyment of the game aside, some bugs I ran into were phantom hits (being hit after it seemed an enemy shouldn't have hit), being clipped through the floor a couple times, and enemies/myself getting stuck a few times on geometry.  Depending on your tolerance of bugs then a little jank like this won't sour the entire game, it didn't for me at least.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start by saying I am a huge souls-like fan so this is not an unbiased review, but on the other hand it also does make me more critical. This game has its PROS and CONS and this review will include some spoilers so TLDR: overall good game: satisfying combat, upgrade system, some environments, disappointing bosses and plenty of glitches.-Satisfying combat- Multiple weapons with different movesets, although i found a weapon i liked quite early and stayed with it throughout the game.-Interesting upgrade system- Upgrading in this game works by adding a catalyst to your weapon of choice and then upgrading your catalyst by pouring currency into it. Catalysts can enhance scaling based on different stats as well as to different damage types, making multiple builds possible. You can take the catalyst out of a weapon without losing any upgrade and put it into a different weapon, which allows the player to try out different playstyles without losing viability in their current area.-Some environment- For a game that does not look as good as many souls-like counterparts ex. the surge, this game has a few beautiful areas with great level design. Variety in asthetic as well as interesting jump puzzles made exploring great fun. Some great hidden gems and rooms throughout the levels made the level design stand out.-Bosses- Okay spoiler alert from now on. ONLY 3 BOSSES IN THE ENTIRE GAME WERE UNIQUE. One was the same as in the demo, with literally 0 changes. One was a huge fire demon that was literally the easiest boss to beat. The last was the final boss, who was a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ computer with a really bad arena design and boss mechanics, not to mention glitching out every other attempt. Every single other boss was repeated later in the game as a normal enemy, making the encounters with the boss not memorable and souring the experience. I can appreciate one or two slightly harder versions of the normal enemies as boss, BUT 6+ BOSSES???? That is just bad game design and lack of originality or creativity. The first three bosses were the only decent ones with decent mechanics (all 3 showed up as normal enemies later on). -rotating black hole and storm thing- An example of a great idea executed very poorly. To be fair I did not find many of the secrets during the black hole time, but the cons of this outweigh the possible pros. The mini dungeons that spawn during the storm do not spawn minibosses or new interesting enemies, just a ton of the same boring old normal enemy. If you have a weapon with a wide quick swing able to stunlock them, you win, if not, you get buried in a wave of bodies in a tiny arena. Secondly, its such a burden when you are trying to fight a boss which you may be having trouble on. I experienced this with the twin boss, the 3rd one. I did not want to fight an empowered version as I was having trouble with the normal one, so every time I had to wait for the dark hole or storm to pass, spent much time just waiting around.In summary, its an enjoyable game with fun exploration but forgettable and some poorly made bosses. I still recommend it as it is fun and the world is interesting to explore. I bought it for 20% off right before it launched, and I would recommend waiting for a sale.
