_childDocuments_.review: Imagine the slow mobility of DS1 mixed with the bosses of Elden Ring doing 25 hit combos that can end or continue seemingly at random, as well as having very few open windows to counter attack. also the bosses deal way too much dmg when compared to the amount of enemies in each area and how many axions (souls) they drop to "farm", which leaves the impression that you are supposed to farm every area 10+ times and lvl up or stick with the starter items and only lvl health. Often times when I beat a boss I don't feel like I "got gud" and learned the bosses attack patterns it feels like I got good RNG and that the boss decided to use attacks that weren't BS. I looked up an online guide to make sure I didn't accidentally wander into the harder area early(the catacombs in DS1) only to find out I was in not only the right place but in area 4/14 3 of which are DLC... I really want to like this game but when I walk through a boss fog and get half of my health bar obliterated While wearing full armor by either a ranged attack or a BS move its just not fun. I can't recommend this at $35 with a $8 DLC. but I will absolutely recommend this if its on sale like an 80% sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly I was pretty excited for another Sci-Fi  "Soulslike" game, but this one had been a disappointment for sure.  This game has some issues for me personally that make it entirely boring and annoying to play.  I think the controls are not responsive enough and are at the bare minimum needed for a game called "complete".  I think that the map designs overall are boring to look at and have the issue of all looking similar so no only is going through the world boring, it is far too easy to get lost or turned around.  I feel like a good portion of the early game bosses are either 2 extremes:  either way too easy with little thought put into how players would abuse them or way too unfair for early sections of the game.  I don't say too hard because in my opinion as soon as a boss is unfair its no longer "difficult" if that makes sense.    The bosses early in the game presented no challenge whatsoever when the environment they are in can be used to abuse them.Early in the game you get a way to choose which district of the station you go to, I haven't started over to pick a different district first to see if its possible, but if it is I think forcing a decision on where to go and not allowing back tracking at that early of a point in the game is a pretty poor game design.Overall game experience is just OK, with negatives on level design and exploration.  I don't know if bosses get better later, but it doesn't matter much if the game stops being fun before you reach that point.  Definitely not worth the 30 or so dollars I spent.  I think my biggest gripe is the overall game play experience so far for 30 dollars when Mortal Shell is coming out at the same price point, or lower, and is fundamentally better in every way from graphics, combat, and level design just from what I saw playing the demo.I would recommend for people to wait until its on sale later down the road.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing! I really think this is my favorite soulslike out there. I love the hidden secrets/areas, the verticality/platforming and the scifi setting. _childDocuments_.review: For those of oyu who are on the fence about this game: - Do you like Dark Souls (esp. the first one)? - Do you like exploring the world on your own with little to no hand-holding? - Do you like dodge and skill-based combat, where you can complete the game with your fists only, if you ahve the skill? - Do you like a setting that is a healthy mix of dark sci-fi, akin to Event Horizon, and cosmic horror? - Do you like the ability to play through the whole game with your buddy, or challenge them to a dual?If you said yes to more than 1 question from above, you'll enjoy this game.Of course, there are some things that are not perfect. Some visual bugs are there, some AI issues, and it's not always clear what the upgrades to the weapons actually do. That said, these issuaes are in no way game-breaking, and do not significantly reduce the enjoyment. As a side note, there is a surprising depth to the exploration aspect, with some puzzles and/or platforming. That said, these are optional, so don't worry too much if you don't like jumps.Overall, a solid effort, and a very ncie addition to the skill-based action-RPGs. Currently in my second playthrough, trying one of the many possible builds! Looking forward to updates and mroe content!

_childDocuments_.review: Hellpoint, like the B indie horror movies it follows, isn't a good game but it has a lot of heart. Combat is acceptable but janky, platforming is okay, graphics are okay but what it is good at is atmosphere and a sense of exploration.It has some interesting ideas which aren't executed well. For example, it starts you off in small tight dark corridors to evoke the horror movie vibe. However this means the introduction levels are too cramped small, narrow and disorientating. You're constantly having to fight the camera and lighting, getting ambushed or falling off the platforms. The best levels are those later on that are much bigger and allow you to see landmarks in the distances so you can properly plan your route and avoid enemies.There is a 'timer' in the game for the station and when a certain amount of time passes, certain areas in the game will spawn more enemies and become 'challenge' arenas. In theory, this adds excitement to the game as 'safe' areas in the game become full of monsters and will drop special rewards if you defeat them all. In reality, because these areas are completely blocked off and it just stops you exploring and you have to wait for it to pass if you feel you are underleveled can't handle the monsters.You can jump in this game and this allows platforming and vertical exploration. Unfortunately the jumping is imprecise and some platforms are very narrow. It's too easy to overshoot or accidentally fall off.Half-baked ideas like this just make the game feel more annoying than fun.I don't think this game is bad but the game I played before this was Prey and the game I'm playing now is Surge 2 which are much better games. I would recommend playing those games first rather than this one. This will appeal to a core niche audience who are looking for a sci-fi Soulslike with heart and are able to overlook the flaws.

name: Maneater
detailed_description: Wishlist Killing Floor 3! About the Game Become a MANEATER Experience the ultimate power fantasy as the apex predator of the seas - a terrifying SHARK! Maneater is a single player, open world action RPG (ShaRkPG) where YOU are the shark. Starting as a small shark pup you are tasked with surviving the harsh world while eating your way up the ecosystem. To do this you will explore a large and varied open world encountering diverse enemies - both human and wildlife. Find the right resources and you can grow and evolve far beyond what nature intended, allowing the player to tailor the shark to their play style. This is fortunate, because to get revenge on the cruel fisherman that dismembered you will take evolving into a massive shark, an apex predator of legends. Eat. Explore. Evolve. Unique Story Play through a full narrative, story-based campaign narrated by Chris Parnell (Rick and Morty, Saturday Night Live, 30 Rock) and set against the backdrop of a reality TV show. Diverse, Compelling Combat Battle fierce wildlife including other apex predators or fight against various types of human hunters ranging from town drunks all the way up to the Coast Guard. Evolve Into a Legend Feed on humans and wildlife to grow your shark, and find shark loot to evolve your shark down multiple possible paths. Explore the Gulf 7 large regions including bayous of the gulf coast, resort beaches, industrial docks, the open ocean and more. Experience a living world with a full day/night cycle.

_childDocuments_.review: Hesitant recommendation. Just a wacky collectathon that doesn't take itself too seriously, and although the game's fun even at a 50% discount this game is extremely short. Even the DLC (which was only 25% off at $11 at this time) only adds about ninety more minutes to the game. Also note, the DLC is only for people at the end of the campaign, you can't access anything from it until you reach that point so I would recommend just getting the base game and later deciding if the price of another hour or so of the same wacky stuff is worth it to you. When I mentioned the game was short, I 100%'d the base game in about 10 hours and finished the DLC in about another 1 and a half. Add in idle time and you get my total 13.5 hours complete game 100% finish. Also even at the time I played this game, January 1st 2022, it is rather unstable and prone to crashing, autosaves are abundant so that wasn't much of an issue but it was annoying having to relaunch the game and get my ear drums blasted by the TripWire video a couple dozen times.

_childDocuments_.review: Maneater + its Truth Quest DLC was a fun and enjoyable ride. The game's essentially a giant weird open world rpg shark simulator game with lots of dark/cruel humor. You play as a shark out for the revenge, trying to find the man who killed your mother. While doing so you'll level up, unlock new abilities n upgrades to you stats and your shark's appearance. There's a ton of mild boss fights in this game (I don't know if any boss in Maneater can really be considered a boss except the one at the end of the base game and at the end of the DLC). The difficulty scale for this game is like a 3/10. I think I died a total of maybe 5 times at best? It's all rather easy. The only difficult part about the game is playing around the dreadful auto targeting system that decides who you attack. The atuo targeting system is fine for the most part, but when you need to attack a very specific target in a group of 20 targets then good luck hitting the right one! The base game never gets too, it's as if JAWS was a video game but it's also a comedy instead of horro/thriller. Truth Quest (the DLC) takes the game in a much better direction, here they don't hold back and the enemies and storyline gets way too crazy for anyone to believe. This is what the base game should've done too. Overall the story's alright, it's just humor mostly, the combat's okay at best, the rpg elements are neat and the game looks beautiful. I'd recommend Maneater to anyone who just wants a chill time without a challenge. Oh yeah and the collectables in this game are nearly impossible to miss. Overall it's a 6/10 game, nothing too special but not a bad at all! only slightly above average. If it wasn't for the auto targeting system I'd give it 8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: While I did enjoy my time playing this game, I would probably say that was due to the fact that you get to play as a shark and you get to grow and eat larger fish like classic arcade games. The evolutions/mutations are interesting and provide some variety of gameplay, but overall you'll just be following a path to an objective with a world full of filler content (Consume 10 Sailors / Kill this Animal / Destroy this Ship).The saving grace of the game would be the narrator, but that's about the only thing that made me truly glad I kept playing a little longer. _childDocuments_.review: First of all this is not a serious game. This is not a social commentary on ocean pollution, the shark hunting or general ecological stuff. This is a game about equipping your shark with electrical teeth so she can stun whatever he bites. I can recommend this game like i would recommend a good b-movie (which unironically is where the shark movies are). Sometimes you just need to be a shark which eats and kills everything that moves, with some cool powers. That’s the entirety of the game. There is a lot of black humor, citation to water related movies and a lot of snickering on the american television shows about shark hunting. The game is very easy and it’s a 10 hour on average marathon of pure rampage. There is no big challenge (except maybe finding all the collectibles) and the gameplay reduces to destroy  boats, eat humans, eat sea wildlife, nothing more. The visuals are ok, nothing on the likes of Subnautica of course but it gets the job done.Buy it discounted, it’s a good fun for 15-20 bucks but don’t expect anything else except what you have been reading so far.

_childDocuments_.review: Maneater. A game developed and published by Tripwire Interactive.Over the course of millions of years since the age of dinosaurs, there is one fact in the animal kingdom. That the greatest killing machines of the world, need no improvement. The Crocodile and the Shark being the most prominent creatures of this fact. Which leads us to this, Maneater, a game where you take control of a bull shark pup and begin the process of growing her, and evolving her until she is the epitome of destructive capability. You start the game as a fully grown Bull shark, and you will control this until you learn the controls and subsequently begin the "story" where your mother is killed and you are left to fend for yourself and seek vengeance for her death. A fairly standard revenge story, where you continue to get stronger until you finally face off against the ones who wronged you except this time you're a shark. The game taking place in Port Clovis, a fairly diverse biosphere of varying flaura and fauna. Long story short here though is that there really isn't a story, and definitely not enough to pay attention to, It earns a five which is about the borderline between horrible and okay. As you can imagine in a game like this (If you can imagine it at all!) the movement has to be fairly on point, as it'll be the major mechanic for you to traverse this world at all and there really isn't another mode of transport to use. Thankfully Maneater pulls this off extremely well and in a fairly seemless and fluid manner. There are a few short comings in this department mainly relating to speed as the map is quite large and even at maximum evolution the Bull shark isn't very fast at all. I think a major aspect with any game like this, is the biome diversity as it can make or break the game as a whole. Half the fun is exploration and finding new biomes that you haven't seen before or wouldn't have experienced or thought you'd experience. Maneater sufficiently provides enough sustainability here that you can get to the end of the campaign without running out of things to experience. The map isn't amongst the best maps i've ever seen, but it does make navigating the game ALOT easier. Clearly the shark doesn't have a map in it's pocket but the developers obviously chose ease of navigation over realism in this regard, the map helps find objectives in the world, paths to use and also gives you important information about the development of each biome as the game progresses. Not to be confused with customisation and Evolutions which i discuss a little later on in this review, i really liked the premise of starting off as a pup shark and growing older, learning from the enemies i've fought and growing stronger with mutagens and evolving my shark. I wish this premise was expanded upon though,which i touch on later as mentioned above. And now we've stepped into the negative points. The quests, oh dear god the quests!!! If you really want to call them that. Maneater does so much of its base concept so exceptionally well, and then completely goes numb on the pulse of keeping the game interesting, The quests essentially boil down to the fundamental, You go here, eat a few of these and you're done, rinse and repeat possibly 7 to 10 times per biome, and eventually face the "Apex Predator" of the zone which is essentially just another quest where you fight a slightly higher level version of the same threats you've faced in the zone already. Extremely disappointing as the options here could have been phenomenal. In a game where the sole premise is to evolve your shark to astronomical levels, you would imagine or in the very least hope for a Baskin Robbins array of choices, flavours and options. Where in sad reality the games maximum amount of mutations/evolutions and customisations sits around 25 or 26. This is extremely sad, and really broke my heart as a player hoping for more, Not even the capability to choose colours of your shark or skin patterns. The bosses are lackluster to say the least, they are extremely simplistic in their design and their diversity, They all have some sort of weapon they shoot at you with varying basically from pistols in the early stages to shotguns, assault rifles and some kind of basic missile launcher, they don't do anything particularly special, and realistically by the time you've evolved as much as possible, they won't cause you any issues anymore in the slightest. I honestly don't know what the intention here was, truly. Because it almost seems like games like Carmageddon back from the early 2000's did a far better job creating a fearing civilian AI. The human AI here is stupid, incapable of anything but screaming and huddling down into a ball as a giant shark comes bounding toward them, the wildlife aren't much better, seemingly swapping between bite attacks and tail swat attacks to throw you off guard which is extremely easy to learn as every single enemy does the same combo and has the same tells for what is coming. If you're willing to grind for achievements you might spend at most 20 hours in this game. 20 hours for at full price a $57 game....The hours don't equate well to me and probably won't to you. I wish there was more to do, more to explore but once you've finished the story and maximised your evolutions as much as you care to, thats about all the game will offer you unfortunately.Maneater is far from the best looking game on the market, and i think it was made that way specifically to take away from the severity of the subject matter, too much realism and viscera in a game of this calibre would be hard to push over the line for most viewers. However, the game does still make you stop occasionally and absorb the atmosphere of the environment you're in, the days cycling into afternoon and night is pretty stunning and the overall underwater effects of this game is fairly sensational, There were very minimal graphical issues here such as tearing or glitching. And i sat a fairly comfortable 60 FPS throughout the entire game on my system (See profile for specs).Much akin to the visuals, the audio doesn't take itself too seriously which is good due to again the subject matter here. The bright poppy sounds help elevate the experience as well as a fairly atmospheric ambience to help keep you in the feeling of being underwater, the sound of waves crashing and tides rippling around is really quite stunning, There really isn't a soundtrack here though and doesn't really have much music at all, there are the occasional bursts of music when you activate some abilities to make you feel powerful, very DOOM-esque but otherwise focusing much more on the atmosphere here.I waited a long time for this game, and sitting here now upon it's completion i can't quite comprehend why, I guess i was  hoping for something more along the lines of Hungry Shark, a mobile game that i truly adore to its exploration, its vibrant world, its intense boss fights and its replayability. However i was given a fairly bland interpretation of it. That's not to say this game is bad, but its extremely short and feels like its missing a lot of what could make truly astounding. More evolutions, more growth, More exploration could all lift this game to a truly amazing standard. In its current state though, its hardly worth its full price, and its not worth much more than a 50% discount. Hopefully with time this game is given the love it deserves from the developers to add what is missing and to make it what it should have been all along. "Welcome to Port Clovis."

_childDocuments_.review: I like a good stupid game. Something with a simple silly premise, easy to get into gameplay, good length. Something to just sit down, play, enjoy and move on, maybe replaying it again a few years later. And Maneater turned out to be a pretty good example of a game like that. Less than 10 hours of simple gameplay loops of swimming and chomping fish and people, upgrading the shark to be more ridiculous and finding secrets.Maneater is an action adventure with light RPG elements set in a big open map that opens up bit by bit as you level up and progress through the story objectives. It’s extremely simple – you’re a killer shark, you swim, you eat, you gain levels and upgrade your abilities and you also mutate into more horrifying forms, gaining special abilities. The map is divided into several zones and each zone has several activities, like “eat x humans in y area” and some collectibles. Eating anything gets you resources that you use as upgrades and also levels you up. And that’s about it. It’s this simple gameplay loop that’s repeated over and over as you go to newer areas and get more ridiculous abilities.It’s fun as is. It would get boring if it lasted longer, but luckily it last just enough to be fun. It’s a bit grindy. It’s very stupid. The whole “cable TV show” style of the game, with a narrator commenting things that you do, isn’t as funny as the developers thought, but does have its moments. And did I mention that it’s fun?Even apart from its repetitive nature it has some weird issues. Controls are a bit off, sometimes the game can’t load areas seamlessly and gives a short loading screen, combat with more resistant enemies can become boring rather than challenging and the upgrades don’t go quite as ridiculous as I would’ve wished. The game is, in fact, surprisingly restrained in its stupidity, despite the premise.But it’s some good silly fun. A lot of people might not find the game to their liking or grow bored. Some might find it just a bit too stupid. But I enjoyed it. And if you like a bit of simple underwater exploration and a lot of shark chomping, give Maneater a try.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Maneater is one of the most unique games you will likely ever play. Playing as a shark and going on a rampage while levelling up your abilities and finding secrets is tremendous fun. However, it sadly does not last, and there is little replay value aside from starting again on a higher difficulty. I did 100% of the achievements in 9.5 hours in the primary mode and 4.5 hours in the DLC. Based on this I think it is too expensive for what it is. 29.99 for the base game is reasonable, and 9.99 for the DLC is also acceptable. Get it on sale if you want it. Also the CEO is undeniably based. Garden tools mad because they need to have some personal responsibility for their actions. Shame on Tripwire for caving to the woke mob.Full Review:For me, one of the most unexpected parts of the game was the attention to detail the developers paid to getting all the information on the sea life you encounter in the game. When you combine it with the announcer, give you a play-by-play of whatever you are doing, be it eating everything in sight, fighting one of the apex bosses or just swimming along taking in the scenery, it makes quite the combination. Maneater is one of the most unique and enjoyable experiences I have ever had as a gamer. The visuals are vivid and crisp, and the combat is fluid and well designed. The quests are unique, named in very humorous ways and fun all around. I would recommend allowing players to lock on when tail whipping to destroy the towers in the DLC and putting options so players can adjust the HUD clutter. You can get very cluttered with all the sea life around you in the underwater biosphere, and when you are looking for hidden objectives, it can be hard sometimes.My main complaint is that Maneater is just too short for the price. I completed 100% of the game in 15 hours, with no new game+ or any incentive to go back and do it again. I hope the developers come out with more DLC as it is a great and enjoyable game, but I can't help but feel that it is a wasted opportunity.I give this game an 8/10. You may not go through Maneater more than once, but if you get it on sale, you will not feel bitter about it. It is a gratifying, fun and unique game like no other.

_childDocuments_.review: This isn't as arcadey as I'd expected, but it's still fun. Munching whatever crosses your path is very satisfying, and the world is interesting to explore.There's just the right amount of content - the world feels large, but it's broken into more manageable areas, and each area has enough collectables to give you a reason to explore without going overboard and becoming tedious. The narration at times can be quite funny, and the sense of progression was nice.Overall, I'd say if you can get this for £10 then it would be a good deal. I'm enjoying it enough to aim for 100% completion, but I don't think I'll go back to it once I'm done.One thing to note is it's very easy to die in the early stages of the game, so very casual gamers may struggle.

_childDocuments_.review: Its pretty funny that Jerry does the narration of this game! It is a good game, but not a 45.49$ game. At the time of this review, I've completed 100% of all the base game. (I haven't done the Truth Quest).The length of this game makes it very enjoyable to not get bored before completing it.It has its annoyances, but honestly for a first in that kind of gameplay, it is really a good stepping stone to start a new genre. I would definitely love to see a sequel with more evolution variations, better AIs, less repetitive fishes and maybe a frenzy mode where you can get as big as you can survive haha. In term of difficutly, it was a bit harder at the start where almos every enemies are a potential danger, but until you reach the end game, everything else will be extremely easy if you do all the side objectives.The movements can be quite frustrating sometimes and feel slow, but you'll still be able to destroy everything in your way. The story line is quite funny and a classic, so you should just play it casually a few hours here and there. If I'd rate this game, I'd say its a 7/10 if it would be 20$. But for a 45$ game, I'd say its a 4/10. So get it only on sale. Otherwise, its not worth it!

_childDocuments_.review: I was pleasantly surprised by Maneater.  I thought the gameplay may get repetitive or that there wouldn't be much of a story.  The story is not super complex, but it does frame the game nicely and give you reasons to progress.  I did like that the story is set from a Shark Week type documentary on shark hunting.The environments are beautiful and swimming through the water never gets old.  It was easy to control the shark and the lock on made it easy to eat or attack the things I wanted to.  I also found it very empowering to start the game afraid of some sea life and then by the end, feel like I could eat any creature under the waves.The game offers a variety of upgrades and ways you can evolve your shark and tailor it and the combat to your play style.  It also offers a variety of wildlife to consume and boats to sink.Overall I recommend this game, would eat again.

Most are amusing.The game is super fun if you just want to sit down relax and be a shark. The entire focus of the game is to eat. From the moment you gain control of the baby, you need to consume everything you see, be it fish, turtles, or even license plates.One of my favorite parts of the game is tracking down landmarks, which brings a fair bit of humor, some great pop-culture references, and cool visuals, or even dark humor, like the Titanic landmark.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game that I never heard about! Seriously, how did I not know about this game until a streamer I follow played it recently? Honestly it's pretty different perspective wise, never played a game as an animal.I really enjoyed the dark and irreverent humor of the narrator as well as the numerous pop culture culture references throughout the game. It kinda reminds me of .There are some unfortunate drawbacks to the game. The physics can be a little wonky at times or maybe just too accurate and I need to git gud as more often than not my shark ended up flipping over on her back when jumping out of the water. Also the content is very limited. The main game only took me 24 hours to complete and that was with a lot of just roaming around chomping things! Also I found the main game to be very easy but I kind of enjoyed that as a change of pace. I found the DLC much more challenging, like insane at higher threat levels! Speaking of the DLC, it seems to be very poorly optimized. The main game performs fine but when going into the new area for the DLC, all of the menus would cause a massive drop in my frame rates to the point the game would hang for a second or two. Also had a couple of random crashes while playing, we can chalk that up to COVID I guess! ¯\_(ツ)_/¯I got the game during the 2023 Autumn sale for $18 and some change, at first I thought that was a little much considering the lack of content but you can keep playing it and just being a murderhobo and the amount of fun I had playing what content there was, I decided it was money well spent. Just sad that they don't seem to be developing this game anymore, it has lot of potential. Hopefully there will be a sequel at the very least!

_childDocuments_.review: "Maneater" is a unique action RPG where you play as a shark on a quest for revenge. The game shines with its open-world exploration, where you can swim freely, hunt, and evolve, gradually transforming from a small pup to a terrifying apex predator. The mix of dark humor and brutal gameplay makes it engaging, though the missions can feel repetitive.The DLC, Truth Quest, adds new areas, mutations, and tougher enemies, expanding the storyline with a conspiracy twist. While the added content is enjoyable, it doesn't drastically change the core gameplay. Overall, it's a fun, tongue-in-cheek experience for those who want a break from traditional RPGs.
_childDocuments_.name: Maneater

_childDocuments_.review: I purchased this on sale after a brain numbing night class, hoping to tune out. Perfect choice. If you're looking for a unique game to zone out, mash some buttons and have a good time with, I can't do much better than suggest Maneater. Growing and evolving is the core of the fun but even finding all the landmarks is rewarding due to all the humor and pop culture references they hide (IT, Rick & Morty, the banana stand from Arrested Development, Spongebob, Pacific Rim etc etc). Evolving to the point you can fly through the air like a rocket or breathe and bounce along land is great fun. Chris Parnell does so much amusing voicework, he's kind of an unsung hero for this title. He really ties the package together well. The level design is interesting, each area is different than the others; from the deep ocean to the bayou, to a Palm Springs style ritzy neighborhood. The areas are full of interesting things every where you look, so traveling never gets old. Level design is also considerate, there are locks you can open later in the game to make travel to earlier areas easier. Grottos are easy to find thanks to the neon lights that lead into them. Underwater caverns which had the potential to be disorienting have a familiar orange light around entrances and exits to rooms. The only thing I would say is it is short and sweet. I'm glad I waited for a sale because you are going to get roughly 10-15 hours until you have 100% the game. I wouldn't blame anyone for buying it at full retail bc its a good experience, but the cost/playtime math isnt as favorable currently. I would happily pay the 40% discount I got, for 40% more playtime. I wish there was an endgame difficulty to unlock. I cant wait for the DLC in August though!

_childDocuments_.review: A fairly humorous yet exciting "collect-athon" that reminded me of classics such as Feeding Frenzy. It isn't perfect, but the flaws can be easily disregarded.Click  to see my other Reviews or follow my  for more recommendations.The thing I didn't expect from Maneater, was for it to be presented like some kind of fishing show you'd watch on TV, ala Deadliest Catch. To top it off, the narrator is funny and there's a lot of small references and originality scattered all throughout the early stages. Especially enjoyed the Lovecraft references.There is a lack of polish, however, as I ran into bugs and frame-drops/stutter during the entire playthrough. Some animations (not limited to your shark, but everything), are very janky. In a few instances I got stuck in geometries and was forced to quit and load. The mouse in my UI wouldn't always be able to click on the things I hover over. Near the end of the game the narrator started skipping sentences or just cutting them short. Audios overlapped, and it was a mess in cutscenes. Restarting seemed to fix this, also. To top it off, there were periodical crashes, especially when alt-tabbing.The gameplay itself was fun. It took a lot of adjusting and getting used to, but it soon became simple, although aerial controls are quite a mess and I hated doing it. The best way to grow quickly was to collect POI's and caches - with this method I found leveling up to be fun, instead of grindy. There's a decent amount of mutations/parts, but not all seem very useful.I love the fact that eating animations don't slow you down or prevent you from acting, and there's some neat indicators for things, such as the red cables leading to the grotto, or orange corals marking exits and such. Unfortunately they don't have any indicators to track stuff such as stacks of poison or other effects, and fast travel is horrible because it keeps telling you you're in "combat" - and by the time you're out of it, you've already gotten to your destination by "fin" (heh, get it?).It feels like there's a huge hole in the variety of edible critters. It's really unfortunate they didn't add anything like large crabs or lobsters on the sea floor to change things up. Perhaps some rare jellyfish as well, and big birds like pelicans, or even seagulls, as edible creatures on land/bridges. With such minor additions it would've truly brought the game to life.

_childDocuments_.review: A spiritual successor to Jaws Unleashed. This would have fit in well with the PS2 and Xbox era of villain games like Destroy All Humans and Stubbs the Zombie. While it shares the same dark humor, over the top action and colorful settings as those games, it also features the same downsides. Such as repetitive game play, a shallow open world and short playtime. That being said it's a very enjoyable and unique game, definitely good for killing a weekend. The art style is beautifully grotesque and there's a surprisingly engaging and conflicting story being told. Chris Parnell is a great narrator.I'm actually hoping we see an expansion and sequel as there's a lot of good game play and world building to add on to. It could use some more enemy types, upgrades and cosmetic options. It is also a bit short ( I beat it in 8 hours. I wouldn't recommend it at the full $40 price, but It's one of the more enjoyable new IPs I've seen in a while.

_childDocuments_.review: Game with a unique concept that plays fine for the most part, but starts to feel repetitive fairly fast. You will be doing quite a bit of combat, which has some cool moments, such as dodging past torpedoes and then throwing them back at the attacks(Yes, the shark can throw people and certain projectiles, it's awesome.)but it left me wishing there was a bit more to it. One major point of criticism is the slow progression rate at the start of the game. It can feel like a real drag until you get a couple upgrades. The upgrade system system is well done with visually distinct Evolutions with different stats, set bonuses and an ability for the body part. The story, surprisingly enough, made me feel sorry for a couple of the human characters, but for the most part it's comedic in tone, with almost all of your actions being accompanied by a documentary-esque narrator.Overall, I did have fun, and I hope the developers decide to do a sequel with improved combat, new evolutions(glider shark and landshark, please!), and a bit more meat on it's bones.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game to just shut your brain off and de-stress with. The basic gameplay loop is not complicated. I didn't need to look at a WIKI once on this game. The story is engaging and entertaining, though the game is very short. 14 hours of play, and I have just about 100% it.Gameplay wise, this is what I thought Depth played like, though I have never experienced it, with a little bit of Feed And Grow Fish thrown into the mix. As for RPG mechanics, I came into it the combat expecting a challenge, like Dark Souls or Monster Hunter, where if you don't time you dodges correctly, you will be greeted with a death screen. What I got, however, was much more forgiving. The combat portion can be solved with "dodge if they are bigger than you, thrash if they are not."As for experience and leveling, "XP" is broken down into 4 different resources you use to level up your abilities. Every resource is used to level your shark, which leads to some level cheesing very, very early on.All in all, I would highly recommend this for anyone looking for a casual game to unwind with.

_childDocuments_.review: Grade A certified to drastically reduce the lifespan of your controller.Tl;Dr; I went in pretty blind, I had heard about there being evolutions and the sort, and that's pretty much what I hoped for in this game. I was immensely disappointed. It's 5$ or 10$ at most, and the thought of someone paying 40$ for this is genuinely appalling to me. Ironically has extremely shallow gameplay and progression, while also being painfully repetitive. Just watch highlight clips on youtube or just a compilation of all the landmarks, you'll save on time, money, and your controller/keyboard will thank you.  - GameplayPlain and simply, it's controller-abuse, drastically overstays it's welcome, barebones, and the amount of things to do is greatly underwhelming and pitiful. The entire game is a slow grind at it's roots. It takes FOREVER to get enough materials to upgrade. The core flaw however, the things to actually do.There is a SINGLE mission. It boils down to going to place A, kill 8-15 of a specific animal or humans, mission done. That's it, that's 90% of the game. The wildlife diversity is immensely lacking, and the humans are boring and mind-numbingly boring to fight. The combat is painfully lackluster and lacking any real options. 99% of combat against wildlife is biting a couple times and backing off to dodge an attack, and thrashing is simply just masked controller-abuse. Fighting humans is boring doing the same thing over and over and over and over again. You either leap out of the water to grab someone out of a boat or you ram/bite the boat to damage and eventually destroy it, it never advances past being more than that, boats are far tankier than they have any right being, and destroying them takes soooooo long, even with the full bone armor set. - Collectibles There are 3 types of collectibles, and only 1 is even remotely interesting. -License plates, which offer absolutely nothing, uninteresting, and are literally just filler. They are littered everywhere and look amazingly fake and out-of-place, and you collect them by biting them, nothing happens when you get them, absolutely nothing noteworthy, I think they just give a tiny amount of exp, if even, honestly never noticed if they did even that, because of how worthless they are.-Material Caches, these are scattered everywhere, you get them by biting them, and they give small amounts of all materials and a decent bit of exp. That's it.-Landmarks, these are by far the most interesting, they are more-or-less what you'd expect, just random unique landmarks or quirky things the developers modeled and put in, and each one has unique narration. They range from literal trash thrown underwater to man-made statues to random references. At it's best, these are just "haha look, I got that reference" low-effort referential humor.  - EvolutionsVirtually identical to armor sets in any other game. Except THERE'S ONLY 3, or 4 if you buy the lackluster and overpriced DLC. THERE ARE ONLY 4? Really? Calling them evolutions is also quite an overstatement. They're functionally identical to armors, with armor set bonuses.The most unique one lets you shoot a projectile using your tailwhip, and another one visually changes your dodge into a lightning stream, but it's still functionally the same. That's the best it has, ALL the other 'evolution' parts are boring as heck stat buffs. I expected a cool evolution-tree of sorts, or anything to do with picking and choosing from multiple branching paths, and instead got three boring armor sets with boring attributes. An extreme letdown.

This game is a grind fest of blood and gore. You start out as a young shark in the swamps of the Louisiana Bayou feeding on small turtles and catfish. _childDocuments_.review: TLDR - Here i thought i could relax and play a dumbass game about shorks eating those pesky humans.Instead i am just angry, kinda grossed out and want to break my controller. Thats not right at all.Heres a great game ruined by bad audio, extremely limited control over your button setup and just gross ass atmosphere. (I used an xbox controller, have not tried with keyboard and mouse, but i assume it would be worse somehow. ♥♥♥♥ all if im doing that)I want to know what the play testers told the developers... because this is bad...The fastest way to move in the game is not by holding bown a button, but instead cycle through three buttons in a row and listen to grating chomp noises while dealing with variant speeds.Each move in the game adds acceleration and removes it also. So you are swimming along, and you see a bit to eat. when you bite, the shark moves forward quickly then slows down just as fast. This is faster than your normal "sprint" or whatever shark equivilent.  This is super ♥♥♥♥♥♥ because it entices you spam the button to move faster. But also you constantly miss your target and it completely throws off any inertial greatness that could ever happen.  This also makes breaching the water a logical paradox. I cannot figure out how to breach properly and get to certain heights while maintaining control. Now here is where i start to get pissy...The intro to the game sends you off in a vendetta against some shark hater guy, cool, swim around eat some stuff. Reminds me of those stupid fish feeder grow games when i was a kid. Alright i like that.After the intro is over the shork hater guy cuts you open to birth a baby that you now control.Now i basically have to relearn a lot of the momentums and various changes that come with it.Which is heavily lacking and thats fine. But then they lock you in a disgusting tiny alcove and swamp marshes with crap objectives like collect license plates, kill this or that, find these boxes, its just fantastically annoying in any respect. Tied in with already bad game mechanics, so im not interested in those things right now. I swim off to try and just enjoy the game and grind for a while. To quickly discover i have to complete every objective in order to pass this damned level.Now im getting really angry, ive been fighting the controls more than the aggressive wildlife. More times than not, its what got me killed. Thats not cool. Your controls should enable you to obviously ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ control what your doing. But as i described above, all those factors get worse when you cant lock onto a target or go jetting off half a click. Often times i found my self just sitting there spamming the attack button because all the random accelerations made it impossible. Since the lock feature just looks at your target for as long as you hold down the button you have a much harder time doing other things like ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ control your shark.The graphics are awesome, but ruined by level design and actual filth. Both the levels i have seen so far are highly detailed and very well done. But its just very displeasing to look at and i cant find myself enjoying it. Your surrounded by nuclear power plants and trapped in relatively narrow play fields absolutely filled with trash and scummy water, i know this design is a part of their story and is completely intentional and i respect that. But i cannot say im a fan or enjoy it. Its just a huge turn off to see such nice graphics intentionally ruined.... (not sure if that logic makes sense for others but im going with it....)Lastly the audio, i flat out turned it off. The music, i really honestly dont remember if there was any. The narrator is that voice actor who played Jerry Smith, and it shows...... Alot...... Overall this game is a huge let down. _childDocuments_.review: I thought this was going to be another meme game.I thought this was going to be a Depth clone.I was excited to find out after purchase that it's an RPGOverall: 10/10Explore, Kill, Eat, Grow, Mutate, Kill some more. It's set up as if it's a show on the discovery channel with a narrator dropping facts and some dark humor. Feels like an Underwater Tomb Raider with the open world and unlock-able, up-gradable abilities. Add in a 3-D hungry shark game from your Droid in 2008, with the DNA (Nutriment) collection of Spore that you use to upgrade the above-mentioned abilities. Something I appreciated was rather than playing a Great White, you're a Bull Shark. Bull sharks can be found up in the Mississippi River and are known for their aggression.Story Line:  10/10Short enough to keep you attention without being so short that it's a letdown, and revenge should be pretty swift, right?Giving a ten because the story made sense, even if it's not super intricate. Besides, all a shark is going to know is "I'm Hungry" and "♥♥♥♥ this guy in particular."Combat: 10/10You can just bite if you want to, but you can also Dodge and Tail Whip like a pissed off Pikachu with ruined vacation plans. You can also bite down on some poor soul and drag them to the depths and either chew em up, thrash 'em to death, or lay a backhand courtesy of the caudal fin. For full entertainment effect, best done with humans. Not too complicated, not over simplified.Abilities: 10/10Basic - Tail Whip, Bite, Lunge, Dodge. Stir it, mix it, remix it, and drop that album on your ops.Organs - Advanced Sonar, Nutriment Digestion options, Brutal Muscles, Reinforced Cartilage and more that I'm forgetting.Make a Mix Tape and lay waste.Electric Set - So a bull shark and an electric eel... you get it. Add electricity to the basic abilities and you can leave your enemies temporarily paralyzed or spam it til they fry. Makes for great crowd controlBone Set - If Wolverine was a shark. It slices, it dices, it makes julienne fries. Best for Offense and Tanking.Shadow Set - Poisonous Vampire Shark. Bite enemies to drain health and lunge or dodge to poison them. Graphics: 10/10I was quite happy with the graphics. Cranked all the settings and still got 60 frames on my GTX 1050TILooked fantastic, and was optimized to run pretty well at max settings.And swimming around is pretty relaxing when you just enjoy the view.Quests: 7/10Think back to World of Warcraft. Go here, Kill X amount of Y. Do this three times and kill the Boss. Bored with that? Munch down on a few humans and have fun fighting shark hunters to the death, increase your infamy rating, and you get to fight human bosses. Some had complaint about this, but to be fair, it's a shark game. And just like in WOW, you might need to go grind some XP before you fight that boss. Or, you can try and finesse the sh!t out of your opponent until you go from Baby Shark to JawsCollectibles: 9/10License Plates, Landmarks, and Nutriment Caches. Normally I see the "find the thing" part of games to be a chore, but it was quite enjoyable in this game. Nothing wrong with spanking a few seals while looking for trash in the ocean. And Collecting everything actually rewards you with new abilitiesIf you want a fun RPG, get this game. If you just want an eat 'em up shark game, get this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: ★★★★☆ (4/5)Maneater is a unique and delightfully absurd take on the action-adventure genre, and my 18.8-hour journey into its chaotic waters has been a mix of aquatic mayhem and offbeat humor.The game casts you as a ferocious and ever-evolving shark, driven by revenge against the menacing shark hunter, Scaly Pete. Your goal is to grow in size and power while exploring the open-world waters, feasting on unsuspecting prey, and occasionally terrorizing the human population.Maneater's most striking feature is its tongue-in-cheek narrative style, presented in a reality TV show format. A witty narrator provides humorous commentary throughout your aquatic adventures, offering quips and exaggerated tales that enhance the game's comedic charm. It's clear that Maneater doesn't take itself too seriously, and this lighthearted approach is a breath of fresh air.Gameplay revolves around exploration, combat, and progression. As you devour smaller sea creatures and humans, you gain experience points that allow you to evolve and unlock new abilities, such as improved stamina, electrified bites, or a tail whip attack. The game encourages experimentation with different abilities, which can lead to some absurd and hilarious encounters.Maneater's open world, set in the fictional Gulf Coast, offers a colorful and detailed underwater environment teeming with marine life. The exploration aspect is quite engaging, as you uncover hidden collectibles, caves, and various underwater locations. The game's world is surprisingly rich in detail, considering its unconventional premise.The combat system, while simple, is satisfying. Chomping your way through schools of fish, snatching humans from their boats, and battling other sea predators is a visceral experience. As you grow, the battles become increasingly epic, with you taking on everything from alligators to giant squids.While the game's quirky humor and unique premise are major selling points, it does have some downsides. The gameplay can become somewhat repetitive over extended playtime, and the camera can be a bit finicky, especially during intense battles. However, the occasional absurdity of these situations often serves to add to the game's comedic appeal.In conclusion, Maneater is an offbeat and enjoyable gaming experience that offers a fresh perspective on the action-adventure genre. Spending 18.8 hours exploring the game's absurd waters is a testament to its entertainment value. Its humorous narrative, chaotic gameplay, and vibrant underwater world make it an excellent choice for those looking for a break from the conventional. While it may have some minor shortcomings, Maneater's unique charm and comedic flair are sure to leave a lasting impression and a smile on your face.

_childDocuments_.review: Peter Benchley, author of Jaws, spent much of his life campaigning for the protection of sharks. His book, and the subsequent film adaptation, changed the public perception of sharks so wildly that it led to mass hunting. In fact, shark attacks are incredibly rare, and deadly ones almost never happen. 2019 saw an estimated 140 worldwide human/shark interactions according to research conducted by the Florida Museum, less than 100 of those were unprovoked and most resulted in no injuries at all. More injuries are caused each year by staplers. The point is, sharks aren’t anywhere near as dangerous as you might think, but Maneater isn’t a realistic game so none of that matters and you can have plenty of fun chomping on humans.The premise of Tripwire Interactive’s latest title can be pretty much summed up in the simple phrase “♥♥♥♥ you, I’m a shark”. It doesn’t come up in the game, but it’s the ethos behind the game. You start out as a cute little shark pup, and through eating lots and lots of fish and random seabed junk, you grow up to be a bigger and bigger shark with more skills and plenty of over-the-top enhancements like echolocation, electric teeth, and the ability to jump higher than Kriss Kross and Van Halen combined. The developer describes the title as a “ShARkPG”, and it delivers on that promise. This isn’t just a chaos-causing sandbox like Goat Simulator or Untitled Goose Game, but a full-fledged open world adventure with a storyline, missions and a detailed levelling system. The aforementioned enhancements are earnable through gameplay and changeable depending on your tastes, meaning you can customise your shark to your particular playstyle. You are the daughter of a shark killed by “Scaly Pete”, who is a legendary shark hunter. Your task, in the long run, is to defeat Pete, but along the way, you’ll be eating basically anything that fits in your mouth in order to level up and collect nutrients to spend on upgrades. The game also throws nutrient caches liberally around the seabed, which give further boosts to spend on making yourself the most powerful fish to grace the ocean. There are various sections of ocean you can unlock as you progress through the game. Usually these are kept shut with gates that you need to reach a certain level to be able to bash open with your tail. Each area contains different fauna to swallow, as well as various quests, usually surrounding the consumption of either fish or people. There are often “boss” type quests with larger predators such as Mako or Alligators to go after. In addition there are 10 landmarks such as statues or shipwrecks to visit in each section. There’s certainly a huge amount of content to see, and completing it gets you ever closer to the final showdown with Pete. There’s an air of cartoon-esque horror in Maneater, but at the same time, there are some gruesomely realistic moments. When you grab a human from a boat and drag them under water, they often continue screaming below the surface, making distressing gurgling sounds along the way. I felt bad for finding this to be amusing, and there’s a reasonable chance that you will as well. I don’t think there’s any shame in it, just keep reminding yourself that they’re not real people. Also, a lot of the time, the people you will be eating are shark hunters anyway, so they kind of deserve it. Visually, it’s a nice but not amazing game. Graphics are solid, but not groundbreaking. Some of the underwater vistas are lovely, though I wish little bits of my shark didn’t keep clipping into them every now and then. It’s not a gamebreaker, but don’t expect to be wowed by the visuals. The style is realistic but with some exaggeration such as with ridiculous amounts of bleeding from anything you attack (even empty boats for some reason).Combat is a little bit repetitive after a while, with most fights just being a case of evading an attack from an enemy, chomping on them for a bit, then repeating. You might also nip away to eat a fish to get health back in the meantime. It’s still good fun to partake in, but don’t expect to find a huge amount of tactical depth. It’s more about brute force than elegance, and this wouldn’t be so surprising if it wasn’t for the fact that the initial gameplay turned out to be a lot more involved than first expected. You can rush through the main missions in about ten hours too, but there are enough side missions to keep you occupied for a while.There’s a danger with this type of game that the novelty factor becomes more important than the gameplay itself. My time with Maneater showed that the developer was clearly aware of this danger, and did their best to avoid it. With no multiplayer and a relatively short campaign, it could be said that there’s not enough time for it to overstay its welcome, but nonetheless, I do feel that enough was done to avoid the problem of the novelty wearing off. Overall, it was good fun to play and exceeded my initial expectations for the game, and my only criticism would be that I wanted to rule the sea for just a little bit longer.8Maneater (Reviewed on Windows) This game is great, with minimal or no negatives.With more in the game than the concept might suggest, this is a fun to play title and exceeded my initial expectations of how the game would be. It’s a little short and I would have liked more of it, but this is definitely worth picking up.SummaryOUR VERDICTManeater is a fiendishly original concept that just about lives up to expectations when it’s focused on chomping humans. However, its formulaic open-world design and repetitive mechanics don’t sustain for a deeply satisfying experience. You’ll still enjoy having your fill but it won’t be long before you depart for new waters.PROSGreat varied and gory visualsAttacking and eating humans is a devilish good timeEntertaining narrationA few absurdly fun abilitiesCONSMissions quickly get repetitiveArbitrary progression systemUnderwhelming underwater combatPlease give me award

_childDocuments_.review: The game is great. It's a comedic take and homage towards Jaws: Unleashed and a great follow-up for the devs that worked on it coming from Depth. But, I *have* to leave a bad review. I've beaten the base game twice, once on Epic, and now again on Steam via family sharing. I've done everything up until the final encounter in Truth Quest and it's genuinely unplayable at that point because of the God forsaken stuttering and freezing. A LOT of people have complained about this in the past on initial release and the developers have outright ignored the issue. I've scoured the internet for hours looking for a solution, to no avail. All you'll find are complaints. No fixes. I absolutely agree that this game is a gem, if you're able to play it without the stuttering issues. Buy it and find out if that's the case. You'll notice very quickly whether or not it is. But if it is, I urge you sincerely to just refund the product. It's an awful experience if you're one of the many unlucky people who are stuck with that problem. All it will do is piss you off. It breaks immersion, it ruins the flow of the game, and it will sometimes get you killed, more than it has me, if you're new to the game. And if you do draw the short stick, just go buy and play Depth instead.

_childDocuments_.review: So, I got this game through Humble Choice.  I was expecting a decent game involving a shark eating people. Maybe get 20 to 40 minutes out of it before it gets boring. How wrong I was.You start off as mommy shark, the tutorial is very thorough and very good at illustrating what this game is: You're a shark, you eat. Everything. Biggest fish in a small pond. There is none bigger. You feel quite powerful and its awesome! Then you become baby shark, and the REAL fun begins. This is an action-RPG. You level up, you overcome challenges. First time I om'd a gator I felt accomplished, because I spent the last hour running from them. Then I'd level up and grow, mutate and evolve. By now, I'm roaming around devouring overly-ambitious barracuda in an old sunken nuclear site and it's fantastic. the zones thus far have been absolutely beautiful and the violence has been satisfying. The difficulty is effectively gated by growth and levels in a literal sense and watching yourself literally grow and make easy meals as you become predator of what you were once the prey of is distinctly an awesome experience. I only have 2 mutations but from the tool tips I'm picturing the end-game being a mutated monstrous, Cthulhu-esque megalodon making light meals of what were once apex.The only negative is that it was definitely made to be used with a controller, which I'm not a huge fan of. You press F to lock-on to threats and have to hold it. The tracking kind of sucks for real fights but once you get used to it, it's not a big deal. I don't even use F on enemies I'm used to fighting. I just can't honestly get over how satisfying this game is as an experience.

_childDocuments_.review: This game isn't all that long, even to get to 100%. But every minute of it is amazing fun. Maneater is surprisingly beautiful: it's got a really gorgeous aesthetic that combines undersea lighting with saturated neon cities. The best way I can describe both this style and the gameplay is, "GTA but as a shark." Gameplay-wise, you're following a solid storyline while a. collecting collectibles that can be a challenge to find/get to; b. eating to empower yourself and mutate specific body parts to customize your powers and appearance and c. doing missions around the map. Non-required missions include killing swimmers, beachgoers etc. (the humans in this game have wrecked the environment and you're a sort of accidental force of natural retribution). During those missions, the GTA style comes into play: a bounty/chase system where increasingly difficult shark hunters come after you in groups, including progressively harder bosses. But you can flee and drop your bounty if you escape.The game's hugely satisfying, beautiful to look at and just generally lots of fun. I definitely recommend it for a few days' happy relaxation!

_childDocuments_.review: Funny and unique shark simulator. I really enjoyed it. Pretty straight-forward revenge story. I found all the license plates, locations, and chests. It's pretty doable. The game is kind of like Borderlands with sharks. That's kinda how it feels. Things I would change: There is really no way to sustain the life of your shark other than eating other animals, which is really inconvenient during hard encounters. You get one mod (I think it was shadow jaws or something) that gives life gain on hit. I basically used that mod the entire game because otherwise it would be really hard to keep leaving combat to eat and then come back. It would be really nice if you could just invest directly into stats that gave you life/damage reduction/damage/regen/etc. By the end of the game you have a lot of resources that you won't ever use. They should really increase the level cap. I got to level 30 about 75% into the game and then there was no progression after that. It feels really bad to play the last portion of the game with no more improvements to your shark.The quests become pretty repetitive, it wouldn't be so bad if there was more things to invest into to make your shark stronger/more tanky. Game performance was good, I never experienced any poor framerate (other than when opening chests, there is some weird effect that causes stuttering) but the game does crash kinda frequently. I'd say once every 2 hours. I don't know if this is because of something in the game engine. Some other users mentioned something about anti cheat software built into the game. Maybe that is the cause.There's no replay value to this game. Once you play through it and collect everything, there is no reason to play it again. I would play a new game plus or something if there was more progression to your shark. Despite all of this, it was a very cool game. I would like to see a sequel with some of the suggestions that I mentioned. It was definitely worth the money to me (I bought it on sale for like 30 something dollars).

_childDocuments_.review: I have an irrational fear of sharks. You might ask "why irrational". Well, I only shower. I never bathe, because the bath reminds me too much of open water. My wife thought it therapeutical to buy me this game.Good thing: for some odd reason it is very fun to play, the mechanics work well and it is a joy to cruise the ocean. The upgrades all have their place and a fun to mix to approach battles in a different way, or depending on the task at hand, focus on speed, defense, offense, stealth attack, etc. What I did not like as much is the leveling speed, which was rather fast and you outlevel your area pretty quickly. Also, I completed the game before the final area was discovered, which made me think that that final area (actually the pre-start-of-the-actual-game-area) served another purpose in an earlier iteration where you could also do some quests.It's quite easy to obtain all achievements (32 out of 44 that is), but what I don't get is why no achievements were included that had you interact with the environment a bit more. So many possibilities have not been used. The hoops in the arena for instance? Sprint races on land? When you consider the creativity with the sight seeing location, you'd expect there be tons of creativity that could have been used in this area as well.last comment: when the game is done, it sort of seems that there is not really much to do besides cruising the ocean. There's no more challanges, such as trying to get as many hunters as possible. But you know what 30 hours of gameplay (due to lost save games...) is pretty cool for 22 bucks. I had fun. Thanks !

_childDocuments_.review: Whenever I would hear someone talking about Maneater it always left me with the impression that it was a trashy satire game with little enjoyment to be had as a "real" game. As it turns out, this isn't the case at all. Maneater is absolutely a satire game don't get me wrong, but it's unironically really fun and holds my attention for hours too. The camera and lock-on system could use some work, and it's not very long, but if you just want something simple and fun to sink your teeth into (ha) for a day or two and then uninstall, you could do far worse than Maneater. Highly recommended, especially on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Maneater is an open-world action-RPG (ShaRkPG) where YOU are the shark. Starting as a small bull shark pup you are tasked with surviving the harsh world while eating your way up the ecosystem to become the ultimate apex predator. Eat. Explore. Evolve.As you explore the large open world locations you will be faced with some of the harshest predators known to man from small muskellung to enormous sperm whales, and it’s not just limited to the creatures of the sea being a threat, you will also have to face off against 10 of the toughest hunters to really crown yourself king of the sea. As you chew your way to being the fiercest predator you will need to find and collect all the right resources to be able to defy nature by growing and evolving far beyond the average shark. Each evolution types tailors to all types of players being able to mix and match to create the ultimate beast. All these perks are to get revenge on a cruel fisherman that goes by the name of “Scaly Pete” which killed your mother and left you with a nasty slash to remember him by; revenge is a dish best served cold and it’s never been sweeter.When controlling your shark it really makes you feel like you are the ultimate predator, grabbing small fish in your giant teeth absolutely tearing them apart with one bite to special moves like breaching out of the water spraying your victim’s blood all over the ocean. One of the abilities you have access to is the “Sonar” which is used to track both prey and collectable items throughout your searching allowing you to see who is, and isn’t a threat nearby allowing you to avoid possible bad encounters with larger species early on before you’ve had the ability to evolve and conquer all. The collectible items include POI’s (Points of Interest), Nutrition Chests and Licence Plates. Some of these collectibles aren’t easy to get to and do require you to be at a certain level to reach them. But don’t worry, you can go back to any area of the game you’ve been to at any time. Everything you do, collect and eat all goes towards your XP bar, so it’s worth collecting everything.There’s also 3 incredibly large doors operated from a switch at the very top making it near impossible to get through but with the ability of grabbing larger prey you can hold and precisely launch them in any direction you want with the force of your caudal fin whipping into the victim. With each evolution (Bio Electric, Bone & Shadow) they all have their own perks to help in different situations.I have found that when encountering boats/hunters the bone evolution is best due to its course body and brute force it provides allowing you to strike right through some vessels at an alarming rate, whereas the shadow evolution makes for more of a swift getaway after mutilating your prey at the bottom of the sea. Of course as mentioned earlier, you can mix and match these abilities to whatever best suits your play style.Maneater is a really good looking game and Tripwire have done an amazing job. The crisp look of the creatures and atmosphere really makes it feel like YOU are the shark. The deep scar that was left from Scaly Pete really gives it character and reminds you of how much you want that revenge. Whilst rummaging through the swampy type areas, the murky waters surrounding you keeps you on edge from the aggressive alligators that lurk close by, though making for an easy escape from the hunters once you start adding to your infamy rank. Each area you reach and unlock is far different from the one you just came from, with one section being the waters.This was one fantastic game taking me around 13 hours to complete to 100%. While it is a single player based game, I think there is plenty of opportunity to open it up to an open world multiplayer or at least a 4 player private lobby style as once completing Maneater there is a substantially large area not used that could incorporate a multiplayer section to take out numerous apex predators with levels that are far beyond you alone to take out and require a group to take them down. Players could then be rewarded with prizes for your efforts such as a whole new style of evolution for your shark.The only downside I have found with this game is that once completed there is no incentive to play again. As sad as that is, Maneater is everything and more that I have been looking for in a single player story, it grabs my attention and wouldn’t let me go until it was complete. I grinded hard for the 13 hours and I even completed it twice because I ran into a glitch that stopped me from acquiring 100% on my first save.Overall, Maneater is a game like no other and I would 100% recommend to anyone, I got so lost in the scenery and evolution once I completed the campaign I would often find myself just rampaging at the bottom of the gulf trying to take on multiple high level threats at once proving that I am the ultimate apex predator.

_childDocuments_.review: I had fun.... but.....I have very mixed feelings after 100% completion of the base game and DLC.It took 13.2 hours to complete everything the game and DLC have to offer. For me this is an extremely short amount of time, as I tend to take the scenic path in games. I didn't follow any guides, and to me this just showed a lack of gameplay.Sure, the game was enjoyable and both the storyline and narration were always funny. However controls were clunky (keyboard and mouse) and the lack of depth in gameplay really sank in about half way into the experience. There is a rinse and repeat cycle of 4 or 5 different tasks in each area of the map, and other than evolving your shark which is admittedly satisfying thats it... Nothing else to the gameplay at all...The reason I am leaving a negative review despite having fun playing the game was that it was just too expensive for the lack of gamplay available. Even having bought it on sale I feel a little ripped off. This game feels like wasted potential. It looked amazing, and was very fun but was lacking overall.

_childDocuments_.review: Review time, never really expected about this when it comes to Maneater. But overall what do i think about it someone might think? It seriously needs more time and effort put into the game, I loved playing as my bull shark and grew her up into the mega that she was made to be to end scaly Pete and go through port clovis and getting 100% for each area. But yet the story was just short it really didn't appeal to me, there were some glitches and some bugs with not attacking right when looking at targets and being flung out in the water and in the air along with having an apex go out of the boundary nets from the dlc and having to crash twice because of being hunted down by hunters while trying to do the story. But i really think that the game could have used some more work and time put into it even if the game play is really smooth and effective as well with putting some very nice references of shows, real life, and some games into the locations you can find. Though does this mean i should really recommend this game? Yeah, but no i really don't see the point in it when we recently also gotten the new first DLC of Truth Quest which i will get to.Now what's so bad about the game and truth quest besides base game being so short and quick to complete? Well I'll tell you, the problem is that it's more of the dlc barely adding anything into the mix. Yes there is a new location and new fish, but it's not many, only 4, and three being used over twice but just given a little extra added which i will go about. The dlc only adds in ONE NEW SET of body parts and only count them up 5 different organs along with adding in another organ slot to have 4 slots at the ready but you have to be level 35 to get. Oh yeah did i forget to mention that not only is the base game short but this one is too? Yeah the only thing you'll even get is military of Sailors in both areas during the truth quest events, you'll only find the 3 of 4 new fish at the Island from what i know of, unless someone can correct me on this then please do let me know. Time trials will also be added and the truth seekers which will be quite a while to find if you use others help from looking up online and such or even longer if you want to try on your own.Now here is going to be where the spoilers will be so if you wish to read do carry on but if not I'll let you carry on with looking elsewhere.So this new set you're getting is called the Irradiated set, you'll basically look like the shark in the loading screen for the truth quest dlc in which you got to kill Scaley pete to go into the new area of the Island. There you will only get 5 new bounty target as before saying of the 5 new organs, one for damage reduction, one for health regen, and the last three are going to be for your sonar. The only way you can get the whole set is simple, kill the final bounty target, find all locations, and kill the main targets at the Island and there you go, but yet once you have it on you'll notice something different. For one your dodge animations is basically bio-electrics animation, and the tail whip attack is shadows but no DOA but deals more damage and looks like the plasma ball from the bfg. The super power you get is just shooting plasma balls that does heavy damage and it's full set is quite decent as you also don't take in the negative effects of the poison from scaly pete or the final boss. Though you might see that i haven't explained the fish yet so here you go as to what they are, the 3 of 4 fish you'll find are the following: A electrified great white shark, the shadow orca, and the bone sperm whale. You'll also be given a bonus only when using the body of the three to get an advantage from no stun from the great white or orca, and no poison from the shadow orca. These three will also have an irradiated version as well so it's copy pasted but adding an additional power to them but what about the fourth you may ask. Well the final fish is the boss which is known as the atomic Leviathan which just about looks like a mosasaurus. You fight this beast and it'll be able to grab you, launch radiated spines to damage you and shoot off a beam to radiate your shark, but once it's just about dead it'll call in the three irradiated apex creatures in which you can try and fight all 4, or just go for the leviathan and end it. Do that and kill the beast and the other three are just gone with the body still floating where it died at and not at the top, the ending cut scene shows that there may be more to this so maybe more possible dlc in the future but yeah you can just complete this within under 3 to 4 hours at best. If anything save for a sale to happen and get it if you want. If not then go ahead and get something different but honestly to me this looks about like a 6.5/10. Tripwire you have a lot to think about when it comes to this game and the possibilities of what dlc you can create, maybe give us new sharks to control and not always having us using the bull shark, and please do add in more then just 1 or 2 new sets to collect as well when it'll make the expectations less than what the players want. Bigger maps, brand new fish, etc. so much can be put into this game if given enough time and effort to make this the perfect shark game people are looking to play .

For me the only problem this game has is that there is not enough to do, and too much of the same stuff repeating. Don't get me wrong, the collectables were fun and there weren't too many you see early on and have to go back for later but especially the locations. you go there, you find it, thats it. you don't really get to interact with them or have a funny thing happen, they just are places to go and get the tick for. There is also a period in the very late game where you need to get more upgrade points and you have to get on that grind of just eating that certain colour fish for them and that gets abit tiring. But don't let these cons make you hesitate on buying the game. it is still very much worth it and very enjoyable for a full days worth of fun
