_childDocuments_.review: Maneater: A brief reviewPossibly like many people out there, I came to this game to look for a "shark eating things" game for P.C, because Hungry Shark World was way too much fun than it should have been. Did it satisfy me?Graphically speaking, it's acceptable, but not something I would write home(or to other gamers) about. Think better than Assassin's Creed Black Flag, but less than A Plague Tale: Innocence. But it's well-defined, the objects are clearly realistic, and the shark itself is a marvel to look at. It's not bad to look at(the game), but not very impressive either.Surprisingly, this game has a story. And like the graphics, I'm not much impressed by it, but only by the fact that it has one. It's quite enjoyable, I think. It's like watching a horror-comedy film from the perspective of a shark.And not surprisingly, in this game, we play as a shark. Although different from Hungry Shark World, in which you progress and then jump on to the next shark, this game tied you to a specific one(hence the story mode). The game offers different customizations and abilities for your shark, and you also progress by leveling up your shark by consuming organic materials(although for a game titled "Maneater", eating a human is not that much fun; it's quite tedious). The game itself is a never-ending GTA-esque cathartic rampage, in which your trigger-happy-free shark swims through the water, jubilantly destroying/ consuming everything in its path(and is subjected to human punishment, as usual) while accompanied by the dry and transgressive comments by Nature television host. The swimming control is fun and easy to master, although the 360 degree angle camera is quite bad since it always trying to screw up your fight with superior prey or human watercraft).And if doing all these things aren't good enough, then I think just being able to prowl in the blue ocean's water as a shark like in an aquarium is definitely an experience to be had.Overall, "Maneater" is fun to play, and fun to immerse yourself in, but it's not perfect. It's good in a few aspects and quite lacking in several others. It's certainly a good shark game for consoles and P.C, although I think it's optimal to buy it on sale. What I want you to know is Shark game is quite a unique concept for a niche market, it's not a game for everyone since not everyone cares about sharks(while also a game for everyone at the same time due to its sheer stupidity and zany idea). If you think you like playing as a shark chomping things, go for it. I went for it and got what I wanted (a shark game). I like it and enjoy it. Certainly there is fun to be had.Also, I think this is definitely a holiday game since you could just sink into it for a good couple of hours and then forget about it until the next play.

_childDocuments_.review: Maneater is actually a social critique/commentary, about human intervention in wildlife and society’s  at solving the impending ecological crisis of our time. It’s all delivered tongue-in-cheek, though. It works mostly because the narration by Chris Parnell is pretty good by video game standards, but in general terms I’m not a huge fan of this approach. If I had to choose, I much prefer  (a game I have also reviewed) style messaging. I think it gives the weight these topics deserve their due gravity, but I don’t think Maneater’s is terrible, either. It’s comedic at times and it fits the tone the game is going for.The sequences with the antagonist, Scaly Pete, are actually pretty good in the first part of the game. His initial motivations aren’t exactly explained, and  doesn’t really match up with his early game characterization, but they are such a great break from the monotony of the  when you’re still not very fast or strong or capable. It’s a shame that there isn’t more substance to these cutscenes. They’re well done and awesome.It’s a shame the other characters have practically 0 defining features or moments. The hunters who come after you as your infamy/bounty level grows are introduced like they’re game-world established folks, but not only do they die as fast as they arrive, but they don’t even put up a fight in any real distinctive way, both in terms of difficulty or approach. There’s very little  about anything. The environments are gorgeous and diverse, as is everything in the game, visually, but from a gameplay perspective the game doesn’t really , which is a bit odd considering the basis of the game’s progression is you as a shark evolving and having adaptations to allow you to do different things. These adaptations hardly change the gameplay though, and the  fights, which pretty much serve as zone boss fights, don’t evolve much either.The final boss fight is unique among them and is actually good! But after 8ish hours of doing the same thing it’s a bit of a weird feeling in your mouth, like One thing that you absolutely never tire of though is  They are  cool. The leaps, the barrel rolls, the final hit animations, the people flailing in your jaws. They’re all elite, and the apex predator  are sick. This helps a lot in the mid-game when the missions becomes a major pushover. If you do any side-mission accomplishing at all you’re bound to out level the main story by a large margin, and things become a complete joke until pretty much the very end, when the game arbitrarily caps your level at something less than the last few major enemies.The music and sound are nothing really to write home about, but they’re not bad either.  For some this is perfectly fine, and for others it’s a disappointment. I am pretty much square between these two camps. However, I can’t say I’m not surprised this game has a  recommended rating on Steam. I  would not recommend this game for full price, both for the enjoyment and the length. It seems like the DLC adds some new ways to play and some additional length, which seems like it might be good, but it’s hard to think about shelling out more money for a game that is lacking on value in the first place. I may pull the trigger, though.Anyway, Maneater is fun. The visceral carnage is enough to keep your blood pumping and you engaged to get you through most if not all the game. But as much as I’m left with a smile at what a stupid and ridiculous slamfest this game is, I’m left with a twinge of disappointment for what it could have been if the devs had been more ambitious with the story building, mission typing, and creature expanding.If you wanna have fun playing as an all-powerful shark, I would still recommend  far more, even knowing it’s a game that has been  and is no longer receiving updates.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is great fun, not sure what these "bugs" some people are talking about are because I encountered none during my entire playthrough.I'm hoping that they plan to release some DLC for it as there is only three choices of evolutions, shocky, bone and bitey, all three offer differing styles of play which is fine, BUT, they get a bit tiresome after a while and I found myself wanting more diversity in what I could equip.There's a bit of a grind when it comes to certain materials to level up your pieces of equipment.Story is unfortunately "meh" and I could have happily done without it, but it allowed them to throw in various Jaws references and the like.Plenty of collectables throughout each of the 7 levels, some you need to evolve to the next size in order to reach different areas.The Apex Predators were kinda fun, not overly challenging unless you face them at low levels.The narration is what made me stay, the witty comments he comes out with often brought a chuckle and a smile to my face.Performance did start to wain a little as I played, could be that there's a memory leak somewhere as I did feel my frames starting to drop a couple of hours into playing without quitting.I would suggest looking on Kinguin for cheaper versions as the 15% off is just.. it ain't worth £30 not now, not ever. _childDocuments_.review: Not worth 40$, but I got it on sale for 23.99USD$ and I'd say about 20-25$ is a great price for this game. I completed the game in about 8hrs, 100% the entire thing, all collectables, missions, unlocks, etcetera and It's a good game. A great time filler, that you can pick up and put down anytime and is pretty fun. My two complaints about this game is basically the combat and materials for upgrading.      Mats first, the material gains isnt bad, but with 3 sets of gear each taking a different resource, and 2/3 of the resources are kinda annoying to farm, it kinda promotes the one set, and its not the set you get from going through the main story but collectables. Even though I did 100% of collectables meaning all the resource caches, AND not spending any of the other resources either, I still didnt have enough to max upgrade 2/3 sets and easily as the other, since its upgrade mat is gained from anything fights and you gotta fight, so you gotta get that resource no matter what.      Now with combat, the game starts off with combat being VERY hard, mainly due to lack of power obviously but also just to get use to it, its weird and unusual but is satisfying to do and can be enjoyable. However the camera can be very obnoxious with the way movement works when knifing on the surface of water and when below, it can drive you mad early but later when you get use to it, its pretty good. The main issue with combat is human combat, cause you can't really target that well it can be pretty frustrating to fight boats where you keep jumping in the air to bit humans but keep biting the incorrect things. but luckily the game isnt long enough where it will frustrate you to stop playing.     One of the GOOD things about this game is the collectables, great even, the collectables arent overbearing in rewards or numbers, but the rewards are enough to make it worth your while, but not force you to attain them, and there is like, the perfect amount of them where they are in good locations, are fun to grab if you like collecting,      Another good thing that took me by surprise was the story/characters/voice acting. I believe it's a satire(?), not entirely sure cause I dunno these things, on shark shows and fishing shows and such, but the game didnt take itself too seriously with it, and Scaly Pete's VA is actually great, I loved hearing Pete talk.      TL:DR 7/10, definitely worth 20-25$, I will be playing the DLC eventually

_childDocuments_.review: While the basic premise of the game is entertaining, marauding around as an increasingly large and lethal shark, it fails to delivery in a number of respects.  Most notably, the gameplay is *incredibly* repetitive, showing a sharp lack of creativity.  The storyline has you progressing through "zones" of this world, and the pattern in each zone is the exact same:* Go kill a specific target, which is usually a beefed-up version version of one of the normal aquatic creatures in that zone, but is sometimes a boat of humans on the surface.  Once you kill this target, go kill 3-4 more (different type) targets scattered around the zone.* Go kill 8-12 of a specific type of aquatic creature at a specific location, which also has a number of larger predators roaming around it that you'd ideally like to avoid.  Once done, go do it again, 8-12 more of the same creature type at specific other locations, 3-4 more times.* Go kill 8-12 humans at a specific location.  Usually this involves you comedically flopping around on land eating people until your O2 gauge runs low, refilling it in the water, and repeating, but occasionally you get to eat swimmers instead.  Once done, you guessed it, go do it 3-4 more times at other specific locations on the map.* Once done, find and kill the apex predator, which is a very beefed up version of one of the creatures in the zone, though they really aren't that difficult or dangerous.  Each apex predator awards you an evolution item.* Go to a spot, watch a cutscene, possibly fight a boss fight, move on to the next zone.Wrapped around that, you have a GTA-stype alert system, where if you kill enough humans in the area, hunters are spawned, and continue to spawn until you hide from them for about a minute.  As you kill those hunters, you gain "infamy ranks", and at each rank a boss spawns.  Killing each boss grants you an evolution item.Other than that, the basic idea is to just kill and eat everything you can to generate the 4 types of organic currency used to evolve your evolution parts, which you can mix-and-match to change up your playstyle.  However, those evolution parts are wildly different in balance and effectiveness, and the set bonuses means that it's rarely useful to *actually* mix-and-match them, and instead just pick one of the 3 sets of items (bio-electric, bone, or shadow), and use that, with the only "mixing" coming from your pass trait slots.There's also a collection game around that, with each zone having 10-20 landmarks (collecting all of the landmarks for each zone also grants an evolution item, so it's semi-required), 10-20 chests that contain massive amounts of resources and XP in each, and then 10-20 floating license plates that are there just for the sake of completion (and function, in some cases, as jump puzzles, though the *controls* for jumping around on land and in the air are *atrocious*).The story was both trite and rather boring.  It involved no twists, it had precious little in the way of redeeming qualities, and served more than anything just as an explanation for why you have Jerry from Rick and Morty narrating your life (which was, incidentally, the *best* part of the game, imo.  Chris Parnell nails the humor in the dialog).Overall, the base gameplay loop gets boring about 1-2 zones in, the evolution system is about 10% as deep as it seems, the storyline felt like something written by a 6th-grader, and the <20 hours of gameplay time to complete the story, for a $40 price tag, is laughable.  I hard recommend *against* buying this game, regardless of how fun it might seem to swim around as a shark, because the novelty of that concept is the *only* thing this game really boasts (well, and Chris Parnell's excellent comedic delivery).

_childDocuments_.review: Nothing groundbreaking, but it sure is fun to be a shark. Makes me wonder why there aren't more underwater games.Fun, but man the controls kind of suck. You can't lock on to a target, which makes fights really frustrating. And on top of that if you are near the surface you end up going into "fin" mode, which locks you to the surface and you have to hit a separate button to go back underwater. I found I was losing fights to the bad camera control and being forced to surface mid-fight when in shallow water or fighting near the surface. Thankfully that's mostly an issue early on, once you get stronger it's less punishing and you are in deeper water more often. Fighting the shark hunters gets pretty old, but I can't stress enough that you end up as a giant killer shark belly-flopping over golf courses chomping on everything that moves. _childDocuments_.review: A Masterpiece! If you wanna waste time swimming around meaninglessly eating fish, this game is just for you. _childDocuments_.review: There is an old game called "Jaws Unleashed" and chances are, you are thinking about buying this game because of it. If you liked that game and how it allowed you to destroy ships, eat and dismember people and sea life and allowed you to upgrade your shark and gain new moves / skills then you will like Maneater, and will find it does many things better than Jaws Unleashed.The game plays as this: You start as a baby bullshark and eat / destroy your way up to becoming an elder. The game world is split into areas with different settings that has different types of sea life. You have collectables, bosses and sidequests to keep you busy in each area. The more you kill people the more you get infamous and shark hunters start looking for you. There are ten infamy stages which spawns a boss hunter when you hit it. Killing each hunter grants you a new upgrade for your shark.Some keypoints I want to mention:- The map is split into sections and each section has a boss battle with the "apex predator" of the area such as an irradiated barracuda or a great big whale with many spears and wounds on its body (basically Moby ♥♥♥♥). When these bosses show up there is supposed to be a cutscene introducing them with their name presented after a freeze frame effect like Borderlands. This never worked for me. Everytime the name popped up but the game softlocked and I had to go back to the menu and try again. It seems to work after the first time, no big deal for me but the issue is there. - The game is pretty unrealistic and doesn't take itself very seriously, in fact the whole game is about a show called "Maneater" with a man called Scaly Pete hunting sharks and you, a bullshark, find yourself forced to star in it. There is a campy show narrator that has things to say to your actions and you can make your shark spit poison, attack with electrical shocks and do double or even triple jumps in the air. With that said, the tone isn't overly wacky. The narrator doesn't speak after your every action and the jokes aren't that bad. The graphics also has a cartoony style, especially on humans, mentioning this because screenshots doesn't really reflect that.- This isn't an overly long game, I finished it 100% after 10 hours and I took my time messing around too. Not a bad thing in my opinion, it ends when it just starts to get a bit boring.- The animal variety is okay but isn't anything special. Most of the fish you encounter are tiny and not very interesting. There are one, maximum two new animals for each section and many of them are nothing special. You mostly deal with barracudas, groupers, catfish, muskies, seals, swordfishes and other sharks with sperm whales and orcas at the final area. There are no dolphins, squids, octopuses, elephant or leopard seals, walruses, narwhals, manta rays, whale sharks the list goes on.- It's an easy game, there are some sections that might give you a hard time, especially in the beginning where your shark hasn't got very good stats but generally you have to make an effort to die in Maneater. I died four or five times and everytime it was battling hunters.And that's about it, if you liked Jaws Unleashed or simply want to wreck havoc controlling a shark, buy this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Game can be completed in about 5-8 hours (WITH DLC)Game can be 100% in about 11-15 hours (WITH DLC)*Recommend playing with controller*- How powerful your shark feels and how well it controls (on controller)- The power progression of your shark- The world and how dense it is visually- Cool Looking Mutations (Interchangeable upgrades)- Repetitive Quests and same pattern of quests every area you go to.- Story wasn't very good, but that's not why we're here anyways- Tiny hostile fish are never scared of you even if you become Mega+- AI is very dumb especially humans and the Hunter AI- Not enough build/mutation variety (4 Shark sets, +1 with DLC)- Grinding infamy levels (not shark levels) on main game is a pain- Narrator talking alot more than I feel he should- Auto surfacing is annoying and makes fighting near surface tedious- Lack of Human uh... reaction? I feel like when there's a massive 10 meter shark tossing ships around and killing armed hunters and throwing explosives back at them there should be a bit more of a reaction than just screaming. This is a lot more important than people realise when it comes to making the player feel powerful. Specific lines relating to what the player is doing would help a good deal. Example: THE SHARK IS SHOOTING ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ LASERS WHAT THE ♥♥♥♥Now, it might seem like there's a lot of things I didn't enjoy, but overall I liked the game a ton. I just feel like this game/genre has so much untapped potential.The DLC's Value is questionable. It does add a cool new area and cool new shark set / mutations, but everything else it adds is basically just chores. It does also add some decent new bosses, especially the new final boss, but its locked behind a lot of tedium. Finally, I personally didn't mind them, but alot of people didn't like new time trial thing.

_childDocuments_.review: Maneater is fine, $40 is just overpriced. You can finish the main story in 5 hours and complete almost every achievement in hours, that means total game play should be around 10 hours. Should wait for the sale or go Game Pass.You might think human is your main villain, most of time you fight sea creatures such as a crocodile or some aggressive fishes. The difficulty is easy, and you have few ways to attack them so the combat is pretty simple and repetitive.The map is open world like. There is over 5 sea areas and you can unlock each area step by step, each area has unique color and city vibes, those are relaxing and enjoy to explore.The mission is problematic. Basically to unlock each main/boss mission, you have to finish bunch of same quests like "killing some fish" or "eat human". The enemies attack patters are very similar including bosses that makes you bored after defeating a few of them. Other quests are collecting items/signs that give you few rewards and no fun. The combat and missions are not great though, this game is very fast paced that you can level up quickly and beat enemies and finish quests so easily. You would have no regret if the price was low, so wait for the sale if you interested.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun game but in the end isn't worth getting unless its on sale. For a sub 20 hour game, it's pretty tedious after the novelty wears off, which happens pretty quickly when you reach a high infamy level. The narration is excellent, and definitely a big redeeming factor. This review was originally a recommendation but the more I wrote the more I realized I wouldn't recommend this.Pros-Shark: It's genuinely pretty fun to swim around gnashing your teeth at people in unicorn floaties-Eat People: You can flop around on land for a limited amount of time and eat people there too-Narration: It's well written and well read. Not the funniest, but definitely a high point for the gameCons-Tedious combat: Combat is fun until you're doing it for the 100th time. Either due to bugs or oversight, using the bio-electric set made combat trivial due to stunlock. This goes for every aquatic creature, as far as I can tell. The only real difference as the game goes is you get attacked by more things at once, and are eventually forced to use the tailwhip to use projectiles-Projectiles: God awful. Its very amusing when you find out you can grab stuff and tailwhip them into the sky. That amusement lasts until you actually try to hit something. You send it flying either straight where you're looking, or at the highlighted target WHICH YOU'VE GOT VIRTUALLY NO CONTROL OVER. This mechanic more or less becomes necessary in the DLC while also putting your intended target behind a dozen humans, all of whom you are much much much much more likely to target. Supposedly there is a button to help with this, but in my experience all pushing it does is slowly wear away at that key on my keyboard.-Build versatility: The variety is "there" but each of the shark evolutions have specific uses that you'll be too annoyed to return to the grotto for. I found most of the organs to be useless as they're mostly niche use. A few are always helpful, the rest are not. Being unable to change them outside the grotto makes them extra useless. Oh hey I found a use for that organ I don't use! Just a quick swim back to the grotto and then back here! Or I could just do it without the organ since the benefit doesn't outweigh the time it takes to go swap.

_childDocuments_.review: I found this game very fun, you do need to grind a bit in the beginning to take care of alligators. Later on i spend alot of time just swimming around and just looking at the world, and throwing fish around. Its super well made form every angle. I like how it starts out very realistic, but then you can literally turn into an electric shark, witch ties in with the DLC nicely, as far as i can tell.I f*ing love the narreration and story, it took about 3 days for me to finish it, so its a nice size. I really do wish there were more, but the DLC will do. I havent played that one yet, but seems fun.If you consider buying it, just go for it, i was not disapointed.

Mutations and perks keep the game refreshing as you go through each location, evolving and growing in size.The missions in each new zone are repetitive (like far cry games).  DLC added some cool mutations but the level was small.  The final apex predator was very awesome and a lot of fun to fight.  Overall a very fun enjoyable game.

_childDocuments_.review: When it comes to my favorite games, Maneater is pretty high up there. The graphics are great, and the story is simple yet intriguing (I'm a sucker for games that play out like a movie). The mechanics, though probably inspired by Jaws Unleashed, are still decent and easy to pick up on. The only problem I got with this game is the price. Any game that can be completed in only 14 1/2 hours should NEVER cost $40.00! Nonetheless, Its still a great great game that's still in active development (Truth Quest DLC). So, to summarize, if you've got money to burn, or find a better sale (cuz 15% aint it), you should definitely give this game a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: Awful, repetitive combat. Very little story - the vast majority of the quests are "Kill X number of Y mob" or "Kill Generic Boss Z." The thing that saves this game is the narrator. Its the guy who plays Jerry from Rick & Morty. He does a very good job... but honestly, you're better off watching "Best Narrator Comments Maneater Compilation" on YouTube rather than actually playing this game. What would've saved this game is more evolution variety - evolutions in this game is essentially gear, and while its all unique, there isn't much of it, and it doesn't impact combat enough. The DLC some unique gear that adds a more powerful ranged attack that's actually worth using, apparently, but a game shouldn't need a DLC to have actual variety to the combat.  3/10.

_childDocuments_.review: I first found out about Maneater when CallMeKevin did a video about it a year ago.  It's been sitting on my wishlist for a while, since I liked the campiness of it.  The game plays up the tropes born of Jaws and continued by Discovery's Shark Week, painting sharks as senseless killers with a taste for human flesh.  Framed as a reality show, the game follows the adventures of your shark as she swims the waters, consuming everything from other fish and sharks, to humans, licence plates and mutagen-laced waste dumps.  All this effort, just to grow and evolve into one of three variants: A Bone Plated Tank best suited for taking down ships and working up your infamy as you eat the waves of bounty hunters coming after you, A Shadowy Speedster great for taking down the late-game enemies with agility and poison damage, or a Bio-Electric Living Lightning bolt that can stunlock enemies for a fair amount of time.  Even better, you can also mix and match these various body parts to best suit your own playstyle, and even augment them further with organs.If you're looking for a game that is good for letting off some steam after a frustrating day, this is the game for you.  Over-leveling makes the game super easy through most of it, and it is so, so satisfying to over-level.   The one downside is the post-game and DLC, where the show narrator becomes consumed with conspiracy theories.  I haven't played the DLC and will probably be dodging it, mainly because in today's day and age, I get enough chatter of that nonsense from my coworkers.  My Rating: 4.5 out of 5 for the base game.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a really fun game and is worth playing but with a couple caveats. I finally found a fix for the issue but it was very frustrating. Also the game is short, it took me under 12 hours to 100% complete the game and that was with me taking my time and also wasting a bunch of time trying to get around the cutscene issue. So that being said I would recommend buying it when it's on sale, I definitely wouldn't pay $40 for the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Well worth the price! Don't go into Maneater expecting a huge open world AAA game. Exploring the waters is relaxing and a lot of fun.There are a couple of different areas in the game, each with their own story objectives and side missions.You start out as this tiny shark and as you progress grow into a beast!Pros:Fun gameplayImpressive and colorful graphicsRuns really smooth at high settings8-11 hours gameplay not counting side questsPrice of gameYou play as a SharkCons:Story a bit too shortCould use more varied side missionsMore locationsFor the price you can't go wrong with Maneater and there's even the DLC which at this time I have yet to play.Also hoping there will be a sequel. There is a lot they could expand upon and improve!

_childDocuments_.review: I literally just completed Maneater after 10-12 hours of gameplay.I collected everything and I scoured the deepest depths of the ocean.So what is Maneater? It is basically the best "shark simulator" (fish simulator?) out there right now. I know there are a few "fish eats fish to grow" games out there, but most of them back from the Flash days.This game is on a different level, while essentially using the same mechanics.I felt the balance of the game was pretty good, the controls felt a lot better than I thought. At first I was annoyed that I got out my PS4 controller, yet the game just wouldn't recognize it. But it is a lot easier to play with mouse and keyboard than you'd think.Now this being a PS4 (PS5?) port, of course there are some drawbacks.There are both neutral and aggressive fish in the waters. One thing I don't understand, is how a lvl 1 muskellunge decides to attack a lvl 30 Mega-Shark. But oh well. Logic programming aside..The game design is pretty nice and the different types of fish are too.However one thing that really annoyed me:There are multiple stages: Pup, Teen, Adult, Elder and Mega.I was swimming around in the first two areas of the game until I turned into an Adult. Being the achievement ♥♥♥♥♥ that I am, I of course proceeded to collect everything, given I had access to it at the time.I hit level 30 as an adult, only to realize, I just completed 2 areas of the game and maxed out my level.I really feel having the cap be at 30 is a bit low. Especially with all the collectibles that also give you EXP in this game. I'm not kidding when I say, I could've probably hit level 60 from doing all missions and collectibles alone. Yet here I was, pointlessly collecting caches for achievements. That is a bit demoralizing.The second one, also probably port-related: Over the course of these 11 hours my game crashed 10 times. Every time was either while loading a cutscene or triggering an event. I hope there will be quite a few bugfixes in the future.Anyway, to sum things up, I definitely recommend this game. It is both fun to play casually and has enough content to tickle your inner achievement hunter. But given the current state of the game and my experiences, I'm limiting the score to a 7/10 - 8 if they fix the crashes, the rest maybe if they add more late-game content.It's just weird jumping from Adult to Mega within one second.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not a LONG game. I 100% it with 15h played. That's a good thing. It's a grind + a story, and as soon as that grind starts to not feel fun any more the game is over.Don't expect deep mechanics. You mostly swim fast towards stuff and left click, but it manages to be fun while it lasts.The game is constantly being narrated documentary-style by Chris Parnell. The VO is mostly comedic social commentary that I would have expected to feel too repetitive and preachy, but it didn't. It's a great game to play as a break in between sessions of whatever rage-inducing competitive game you take too seriously. It's also a nice break from any of the popular genres currently flooding the market. You probably haven't played something like this since (if you're old enough) Feeding Frenzy.

_childDocuments_.review: Very glad I finally played this. It's like a cheesy but charming shark movie, except you get to play the shark. It might make me a little biased, but I always enjoyed those movies even though they were terrible. A little janky, some bugs - had a "boss" / elite mob fly into space and it eventually came back after re-opening the game, and towards the end of my playthrough the audio just started cutting out with dialogue overlapping itself or just not playing at all. However, the game's movement and your progression are what really sold me on the game. It's fairly short, I 100% the base game in a little over 7 hours or so, but the pacing is wonderful, and I always felt motivated to grind towards something and continue evolving the shark. The missions that pop up are simple and repetitive, but it sort of works given the whole "turn your mind off and have fun" feel the game has.Some stuttering as well but it's a UE4 game, nothing new there. Besides those issues, it's a very fun game from start to finish and I think the game actually lives up to its self-description of being an "ultimate power fantasy as the apex predator of the seas".

_childDocuments_.review: First I would like to say in 12 hours I was able to beat the entire game, I also collected and unlocked everything in that time. When you first start off as a baby shark the only big threats are a few alligators, you can either fight them or leave other than that the beginning is easy to get your bearings on it. The story in the game is there for the sake of being there, I wasn't really driven by it to keep progressing. My reason for moving forward in the game was to unlock more stuff and evolve my shark. When it came to the music I didn't really notice it probably because most of the time I was eating people, fish and destroying boats. The people that fought me while I played weren't much of a threat so just keep attacking and if your health is low swim away and eat a few fish then attack again. If your into speed running games this might be a game for you. I would consider this a mindless game that isn't to say it's bad there are many mindless games that are good but if your looking for complex characters and a rich story and replay value look somewhere else. Now if your looking for a game with senseless violence and you like to toy with your prey and something to waste your weekend on then check it out.

_childDocuments_.review: An okay little mayhem simulator. Clearly could've used a few more honest months in the development oven since, during the few days it took me to finish the game in its entirety, it crashed a couple of times and I also experienced some other oddities and glitches, including enemies just yeeting off into space all of a sudden, the shark making a sudden 180 degree turn out of nowhere, and a bunch of graphical hiccups where the textures wouldn't load.Despite these smaller flaws I had a good time for the vast majority of the time as developing your very own Garbage Disposal Unit of the Sea was fun; watching it grow and evolve into this absurd monster with a helmet made out of bone. Missions got a bit repetitive and combat mostly boiled down to mashing the attack button and dodging button in sequence until either you were dead or the enemy was dead. The narration was the best part of the game by far.
_childDocuments_.name: Maneater

_childDocuments_.review: Like many others, I got this as part of the Humble Bundle Choice pack. At ~9 hrs in, I've cleared the base game 100% and upgraded all the shark bits to max. So, that's basically everything I could do other than swim around aimlessly.Was it fun? Sure, it was fun.Was it challenging? Uh, not really.Maybe there are ways to do combat or upgrade combinations that I didn't explore, but overall the "combat" is really repetitive. It pretty much boils down to whether you're fighting fish or not fish, there aren't really diverse enough enemy patterns that I'd say anything else stuck out to me.Some of the environments are pretty cool, I think a lot of it is ruined by your fishy body though so if you'd be looking to purchase it to get some of the scenic views they show in the slideshow...I'd skip it.I would pay probably $15-20 for this. Overall it's a fairly entertaining 9 hours of hitting the sonar button constantly and chewing on things as you swim around. If you skip some of the collectibles, I'd expect to only need about 8 hours to clear this. If you skip all of them, you could probably clear in 5 hours or so but would likely require more strategy against bosses.I think they missed a lot of potential replay/added value areas by having very limited upgrade choices and locking you into growing bigger. I would've rather seen "size" as something that could be upgraded or left as-is in exchange for something else (speed, damage, whatever) and it would've been cool to see a bunch more upgrades early on and as the game progressed, I think the last boss was the only time I swapped out some parts specifically to do something.

_childDocuments_.review: I had a ton of fun with Maneater. Two things I didn't expect to appreciate as much as I do are the game feel and the writing. This game could have been a frustrating and janky experience, but swimming around feels so absolutely natural once you get down the controls. I never feel like I'm fighting the camera and I'm always immediately able to gather my bearings after getting turned around. The combat also feels very satisfying and easy to overcome. The game progresses at an extremely comfortable rate, never forcing you to grind for xp or something since the game's mostly balanced around a very streamlined experience. Doing sidequests and spending more time beefing up your bull shark is more rewarding as a result. Also the writing is really amazing. I can't believe I was genuinely laughing at the dialogue as much as I was. It's surprisingly in-touch with modern social politics in a tasteful way, and very well learned in the sciences behind the game's genetic mechanics and marine biology. I have a lot of respect for Maneater after spending as much time with it as I did. My only complaint while playing was how collectables and landmarks disappear from the map after you find them, but after 20 hours I realised you can actually toggle them to be visible while on the map. I guess that means, aside from the fact it crashed twice, it's basically a perfect game in my books. My only caveat is that you have to be the type that actually enjoys doing sidequests, otherwise you're gonna get real bored real quick.

_childDocuments_.review: Maneater is a wonderful Sharkventure.It is so good in fact that after beating the game on Epic Games I decided to buy it on Steam to do 100%.After 25 hours I now finished everything the game has to offer and it was a blast.The Game has some flaws however:- Underwater Combat can be sometimes confusing due to fast camera and the softlock on enemies- Sometimes crashes because of U4- Presentation can be lacking sometimes or feels unfinished- The developement and story felt kinda rushed could've been a longer journey imo- some DLC late game ships are kinda unfun to fight against What it does really great:- Beautiful underwater locations (except the Gulf, was a bit too foggy)- Sound design, especially the transition betweeen being under water/on land is great and feels immersive- Sonar makes the collectibles actually fun to collect and a part of the game instead of just being a unnecessary addition- The speed challenges, Bosses and Humor in the DLC was great and a lot of fun- A lot of ways to "build" your shark which is insanely funWhat I hope to change for a possible Maneater 2:- The Nemesis system from Shadow of War would be perfect in this game and could be implemented for Shark Hunters and Underwater bosses, could improve the sometimes rushed character development and adds infinite replayability- some more factors regarding the horror you bring upon humans like a scare scale or something to give more ability to immerse as a maneating shark- More possibilites for modifying your shark (coloring etc.)I would recommend this game to anyone who has fun developing and upgrading your character and anyone who likes to feel absolutely OP.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: First things first: This game isn't great, it's not even "good", but it IS unadulterated fun being a shark gobbling up humans and other marine life... ^^I got almost 12 hours out of it with the Truth Quest DLC, but be prepared that you WILL be doing the same thing over and over again.Your goal is to grow and to kill. You'll start off as a little baby shark, growing to a teen, an adult, an elder and finally a mega (+10 more levels in the DLC). Along the way you will kill animals for 4 different resources, unlock mutations to make your shark your own and explore the area for collectibles.Starting off in the Bayou, a shallow swamp, you'll be extremely underpowered and even smaller alligators can prove a serious hurdle. By the time you're an adult at the latest, nothing will really pose a serious risk, however, until the very late game perhaps or if you decide to just gobble up humans and hunters en masse, thus triggering the next "escalation stage", which IS permanent, but also rewards you with more mutations.The three mutations are "bone" (the tank and ship destroyer), "shadow", extremely quick and uses poison attacks, and "electro", which can stun enemies. Truth Quest adds another mutation called "atomic", which basically irradiates enemies and deals more damage to them.Exploring each habitat is surprisingly fun although the game severely lacks in the "uniqueness" department. Every cave, every canalisation is basically the same. Still, fighting Sperm whales and attack helicopters in the end, throwing torpedoes back at your attackers, just fulfills some primal desire. Combat is otherwise very basic, you either bite or thrash smaller enemies, or hit them with your tail. You also get a dodge button that you can improve via mutations. And that's basically it. Eat, explore, grow.Truth Quest adds another area to the game and brings the story to a close (for now) as well as new mutations and things to do once you've beaten said area, which unlocks after having beaten the main game. Whereas the fight against Scaly Pete in the form of a documentary (mostly voiced by Jerry from Rick&Morty I think) is reminiscent of an over the top retelling of Jaws, the Truth Quest DLC completely jumps the shark, pun intended. You will either love it (like me) or hate it, I guess. Play a bit and then decide whether you want to invest more time into it. If you don't like it after 1 to 2 hours, you won't like it after 3 or 4 hours or after 10 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Maneater

_childDocuments_.review: Great power fantasy game where you play as a shark!This game does something new and lets you play as a shark that grows up and evolves as you make your way to the top of the food chain.There's a story in the style of a Shark-Hunter TV show, where the main antagonist is trying to hunt you down, and you want to get revenge on. The story is fine, but not the main focus.The game itself is on a big map that you keep unlocking more parts of by leveling up and doing missions and collecting things. Most actions you make are being narrated by a pretty entertaining narrator, as if you are being watched by a documentary film crew.The game also offers some shark upgrades that you will be able to equip and unequip at any time. These upgrades effect the visuals, speed, damage and defense of your shark. Most pieces are also part of a "set" that will provide extra bonuses when equipping multiple set pieces.Generally speaking, this game was a very fun experience. But I will say that the main thing that kept it fun was the satifying gameplay loop. Eating and destroying things is simply satisfying, and that's what keeps this game from becoming boring.However, the game does have a lot of the typical "open world pitfalls" that it could improve on.Don't get me wrong, I fully enjoyed this game. But a potential sequel would really need to add a lot more things in order to not become boring.Basically: If this wasn't a game where you play as a shark, but instead you'd be a soldier with a gun, it would pretty much be like a bad Far Cry clone. It would be another typical open world game filled with busywork.And most of the missions and collectibles are kind of busywork. And as I said, the satisfaction of destroying and eating things is what stops it from becoming boring. Since we haven't really had games like this before.The amount of equipable shark upgrade sets are somewhat on the low side at 3. 4 if you count the DLC.And as I just stated, most of the missions are just busy work, meaning copy-pasted missions of "kill this, kill that, destroy this, go here and kill that". Again, it only works because being a shark is very fun.I'd love to see a sequel, but it would really have to innovate on a lot of things.More indepth missions than "go kill this". And definitely a lot more possibilities for upgrades for the shark. It has the potential to become an in-depth shark RPG with new mechanics and playstyles.There's a lot of stats that get changed around with certain upgrades, and some passive upgrades also buff certain abilities and such. But it is very unclear what some stats directly effect. And there is no screen to see your total stats all added up for example. It doesn't matter that much, but it's definitely something that could be pointed out that could be improved on.The visuals of the sharks and their upgrades are beyond stunning, and make me excited for any potential future game that could be made with a ton more content.A sequel would be awesome, but really needs a lot more innovative improvements and more content and care.All big franchises thankfully started somewhere smaller scale, so here's hoping!

_childDocuments_.review: Right off the bat I'll tell ya, this is a pretty good game, short and sweet are the words that will define my review. This game makes you want more, and I missed playing games like this!It's a different take on the Shark games you know, definitely not what you'd expect. RPG like with a level system, upgrades and a bunch of collectibles for you to find! And a fun narrator to listen to.I love the shark design, and how you can grow accordingly to your level, besides all of the beautiful gear you can get, which looks astonishing when fully upgraded, they also come with custom effects, abilities, and even great music once you use them.If you're someone who likes to explore, then this game is for you. It will heavily reward you if you get all collectibles, which is also a good thing if you're a completionist.Besides collectibles, there are lots of fun challenges to work on, from fighting apex predators to gaining infamy.Also, I love the soundtrack, ambiance, and every single small detail, from sea creature noises to music.Now, personally, the main downside of this game is that, it is a short experience, especially if you're not going to collect everything (Including DLC) I managed to complete everything under 15 hours. Personally, it would've been amazing if they made 3 large maps with the same size as the main one, which has around 8 areas.. As well add more gear and everything, maybe make other creatures playable. I'd pay extra money for that amount of content.Also, we don't get enough time trials (Something you can only get from the DLC) One last thing, when you jump out of the water especially to reach collectibles that are high, it can be difficult. There's this thing the game doesn't teach you, but if you jump and constantly look up, your shark will do a backflip. The trick is to look down after a high jump and center the shark, so it won't backflip, making it easier to get some collectibles and go through time trials. This could be somethinig to work on, if they make a sequel.Overall, great game, the price is not bad for the amount of time you'll spend playing, but still.. I'd get it on sale, same with the DLC (You'll need it, great extra content)I already miss this game </3
_childDocuments_.name: Maneater

_childDocuments_.review: Remember Jaws: Unleashed on the PS2? Imagine that game, but with controls that aren't clunky. Seriously, I've played way too many games with poor swimming/flying mechanics, and the controls in this game are buttery smooth. I want to see a Superman game with flying mechanics that kind of function like this, or maybe an Ecco the Dolphin game.Also, the game's graphics are super gorgeous! Definitely the Unreal 4 engine at its best... for the most part. What I mean is, the first level starts you out in Fawtick Bayou. No matter how pretty your graphics are, it's difficult to make a swamp look good. The following level is "Dead Horse Lake" which is SUPER polluted & gross. This is meant to fit in with the game's constant theme of "mankind hurting the environment & nature" which is an important motif throughout the story, but can make these two areas look a little gross. After that though, the game looks absolutely gorgeous! All other levels feature beautiful, exotic sea life & imagery. It's kind of a feast for the eyes, like watching a nature documentary or something.The game definitely has a tongue-in-cheek sense of humor, and if you're a fan of the show "Archer" you'll probably never be able to not notice Cyril Figgis' voice actor as the narrator. If I can't hear it, then neither can you!The game is very stable, and runs great on Highest graphics settings on my Windows 10 machine. Don't get me wrong, stability in games should be EXPECTED rather than appreciated & praised, but with how many games release as a buggy mess these days, some even remaining so forever, it's worth mentioning.Maneater can be a bit repetitive at times, what with the missions being all like "Go here, eat that" and "Get these collectibles AGAIN but in a different area" but somehow I don't really get tired of them. Also, the light RPG elements work really well for what the game is. My only complaint about the leveling up is that there's no customizable shark body parts that give you frikkin' laser beams attached to your head that you can unlock as a reference to Austin Powers. The game is also fairly short & can be beaten in a matter of 10-15 hours, but it'll be 10-15 hours of FUN, so what's the problem? If the game is too expensive, wait for a Steam Sale.Overall, the game does have flaws, but it's far more good than not and I had an absolute blast! I'd honestly recommend it. 4/5 stars for sure!

_childDocuments_.review: Maneater is a great game that I was thrilled to see be brought to Steam after its initial release on Epic Games. This game is a spiritual successor to a game called Jaws Unleashed that I played on the original Xbox, where you play as Jaws and go around eating people and fighting shark hunters, and it was an amazing game. This game is very similar to Jaws and is a lot of fun to play.In Maneater, you are a baby shark that's mother is killed by a fisherman and his son that are the stars of a reality television show about shark hunters. There is a narrator that speaks throughout the game as if the events are occurring within the show, including interviews with the human characters the shark goes up against. The game is set in New Orleans, and you explore the various areas of the city from the swamps to the open gulf ocean that each have their own unique species and types of people to eat. Your shark grows up as you explore the city and set out on your revenge against Scaly Pete, and you develop your attack abilities and other upgrades as you age. The upgrades consist of more realistic looking ones, but also special radioactive mutations like bioelectrical teeth, bone-like skin, or poisonous capabilities.There are various types of fish, sharks, whales, and humans to eat. Humans will be in many different types of boats, from kayaks to yachts, and will also be swimming and playing along the beaches. Each area has its own sea creatures that are difficult to kill, like other sharks or whales, and you slowly become the apex of the sea as you defeat them. Your shark can go on land and grab people or items and bring them back into the sea, a funny thing players of Jaws Unleashed would do that was given its own mechanic in Maneater. There is an infamy system depending on how much destruction your shark causes, and the human response to attacks increases with each level. Humans will send out under-equipped mercenaries and increase their ships and weapons to the US Coast Guard. There are famous fisherman and sailors that can be killed for each infamy level that unlock special upgrades. The boats are a lot of fun to fight, and have great destruction physics. It is always satisfying to hop onto a boat and grab someone off of it to be eaten. The game world has many collectibles throughout, some of which require abusing the mechanics or certain upgrades to accomplish, but even with this replayability design the game is still surprisingly short. The game can be played after completion to finish the collectibles and attack people for fun, but it is limited in what you can do. The combat and exploration are a lot of fun, and the game's atmosphere of being presented as a reality television show is a great framing device. The narrator is really funny to listen to, and makes great jokes that keep a lighthearted and ridiculous tone that fits the story. The game is worth the fun it provides, and for the nostalgia for those who have always wanted another shark game, but is really short and maybe better left to a sale for those that are not really interested in the premise.

Though even without that, the game will often just crash for no reason. And in many cases, you'll either lose your save, or it just won't let you load after hours of gameplay. Only limitation is that you have to hit "Teen" level to get out of the first zone. And you're free from there.Cons about the world: World of the ocean is... underwhelming. No octopi, no strange eels or anything. You have aligators and fish. And that's it. (and cetaceans, but those also kinda look like fish... )I liked the game controls... not the battles every time but i general it's good. It's fun to swim around.Also the collectibles are fun, especially the signpost-things.Graphics and also good. Game looks nice. No weird glitches most of the time.Bad stuff: a bit repetitive. The story (which is actually kinda deep and good) only covers about 5% of the gameplay. Mostly you kill 10 X and cosume 15 Y...Humor: Top 10. Especially the miillion little mentions of other pop-cultural stuff.(the 3 shells and the toilet thing... that's an ooold one :D ) Bad stuff: The DLC: Don't activate it. If you have it, skip it. _childDocuments_.review: Enjoyable, but extremely short and very repetitive.Overall it's a nice, easy-going game, the narration is very good, it looks pretty, sounds decent, but there isn't much to do.The main quest is about 5 hours, and in my 15 hours I completed both the base game and the DLC to 100%, and it's not like I was speedrunning it or wanted to get it over with. Even on current 50% sale that's 25.63 euros for 15 hours of gameplay.There is no difficulty setting, very easy overall. The only difficult fight I had in the game was going against a lvl 8 enemy right at the beginning when I was lvl 2-3. But soon after that nothing can stop you. The DLC does provide some challenge, but again: not much.The evolutions (special parts that you can add to your shark) are fine, but since there's no difficulty they're not relevant enough. They're nothing mindblowing either. The problem is that your main damage is your bite against most enemies, and you get that right at the beginning. This means that besides small increases to your bite damage, damage resistance or movement speed, you won't really get anything exciting or useful.Nothing even close to what you experience in Evolve or Prototype. In fact if you like this evolution thing and killing stuff in open world, then you're better off with Prototype.. they're probably cheaper as well.The 3 kinds of quests in the game are eat 10 fish of a certain kind at a certain locations, eat 10 humans at a certain location, and kill some enemies at a certain location. And you're in water mostly, so while the environment looks nice, mechanically it's irrelevant, you're always just fighting in water.Again, everything in the game is at least decent, but there isn't much in there.

_childDocuments_.name: Maneater

_childDocuments_.review: Maneater is a good choice of game if you want a few hours of causing some mindless chaos.It's a pretty cool idea for a game. You start off as a shark pup and through the course of the game your shark will grow as you level up and you can add mutations that you unlock to beef up your sharks attacks and defence.The sense of progression in levelling up your shark is pretty satisfying as you outgrow the predators that would have caused you trouble earlier in the game and the hunters become the hunted. You can level up your mutations which improve their stats as well so you can turn yourself into the perfect killing machine whether thats a bone covered battering ram or a bio electric shark.The underwater environments look great and theres a nice variety of areas you'll explore from the swamp you start in, to quays alongside wealthy mansions and eventually out to the ocean.While initially the game is quite fun it does start to get repetitive after a few hours. You basically follow the same pattern every time you progress to a new area. It usually goes enter new area, find cavern which acts as your respawn/upgrade point, do a few missions which are usually kill a predator/ consume humans/ hunt a set number of fish, kill the apex predator for that area and then move to the next area. The lack of variety makes the last few hours feel like a bit of a chore.I found playing this game in short bursts of about an hour to be the better option, as it helped alleviate the repetition a bit but I did find, even doing that, my interest waned for the latter parts of the game. Fortunately it's not an overly long game so it doesn't become a major downside.So while it may not be a particularly deep engaging game it works well as a game where you can just shut your brain off and cause a bit of chaos as a mutated giant shark.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a unique and exhilarating experience where you get to play as a shark and wreak havoc in the ocean. _childDocuments_.review: I've loved playing Maneater. It is exactly what it sounds like; you swim around as a hungry shark feeding on absolutely every creature around you - including humans. You level up as you eat things, unlocking new and exciting abilities along the way. The game is a bit grindy if you're looking to 100% it, but I found the grind in this particular game to be rather cathartic. It felt very gratifying to go from not being able to safely hunt any baddies to eventually being able to kill them all. The narrator was mostly irrelevant, even though he was talking in your ear , but he made some witty comments that had me laughing out loud. There were some graphical bugs that were distracting. The apex predator cut scenes would almost always bug out, and I would then have to reload my save to continue. Also, given how little content there is (even though the content is entertaining), I would say this game is very overpriced. Definitely wait for a sale before purchasing.I would give this game 8/10 stars.

_childDocuments_.review: I got this as part of the Humble Choice bundle and I'm glad I didn't pay full price. I played a bit over an hour and the game is already incredibly repetitive. The quests just feel like fetch quests. "Go here and kill this one particular fish." "Go here and kill 10 of this type of fish." "Go here and kill 10 of these humans." Looking at the list of quests and the map, all my new quests are the same thing. Swimming around and eating whatever your objective is is really repetitive and all you do. The combat feels really clunky when you're going up against something that will actually fight back. You don't feel like you get much speed which I guess helps a bit with combat but makes general exploration feel like a chore.I'm genuinely surprised this game has as high a rating as it does. It looked really fun but in the end, it's just the same monotonous thing over and over everywhere you go with no signs of anything interesting happening.

_childDocuments_.review: Most of my hours are from the early alpha build before the devs were bought out by Epic, i'm giving the game a 2nd chance now that it's on steam and on salehere are my initial thoughts:Pros:+ Beautiful environments+ Shark model and model of other creatures look good+ Music is nice+ Day and night cycle+ Mostly different animals in each Zone for variety + Customization of mutations and upgrades (Though I did a default shark because the mutations made things way too easy and looked dumb)Cons:- Shark movement leaves a lot to be desired. It is stiff, and barely curves its body when turning in circles/strafing. It feels more like piloting a helicoptor than a creature in water- Camera is awful- Lock on ability is useless. the moment the enemy darts past you, you lose your lock. And they dart past you a LOT- Quests are incredibly repetitive (kill X of this thing, now kill X more, and X more, fight boss, move to next zone)- too much blood, it's stupid. Can barely see what you're attacking with all the gore - sound effects are annoying - narrator is annoying and repeats the same lines over and over- Quest objectives don't always spawn in (kill 10 humans, but the quest humans do not appear)- Going into photo mode sometimes bugs sound out- Had 1 crash so far when entering a cut scene- Short. I 100% the main game in 12 hoursOver all, so far, it's a pretty game but i don't see a lot of replayability to it beyond taking screenshots of the environment. The fact they sold out to Epic and dumped us alpha testers without another word still rankles me, but that isn't anything to do with the actual game itself Buy it on sale. Don't pay full price for it

_childDocuments_.review: Not a game I can truly, 100% recommend, but I will recommend it regardless.First:The game has a few bugs, and crashed a few times but nothing major as it saves continually. Also it can be a bit hardware intensive. The gameplay is fun, but honestly I was hoping for more "realistic" situations to develop, for example, you eat some people on the beach and the police arrive, ambulances, the media etc. which over time leads to a more hostile environment in the ocean as the coast guard is called in. Unfortunately, this game has a pretty simple system where people pretty much stand still to be eaten and boats instantly spawn behind you similar to how GTA's wanted level works. I personally enjoyed this game because it felt like a spiritual successor to the "feed us" flash games from years ago, but even then I'm not super enthusiastic about recommending this because of how grindy it is, how button mashy the combat feels and the length of the game to 100% completion being roughly 10 hours, which translates to over £3 an hour for content (most of which is grindy fish eating with button mash combat, spamming radar to find collectables, or swimming to things miles away). Don't let these issues completely put you off the game, the criticisms sound a LOT worse than they actually are in the game itself, and this is easily seen by the amount of positive reviews this game has that state the issues directly and feel the exact same way as me. The TLDR is to buy it on a sale if you think you are interested, as chances are you will enjoy yourself for roughly the amount you paid for the game on sale. The final point I'll mention is that this game has clearly been made by a passionate dev team. The amount of quirks and attention to detail, as well as some "strange" design decisions clearly show that the team behind it had a great time making it (even if it feels like they were under time constraints). You could even tell in the interviews before the game released that the devs were pretty excited and proud of this silly game, which is always a massive bonus point for me personally. There is nothing worse than the soulless, sterile, uninspired games that are infecting the market nowadays.

_childDocuments_.review: By all rights, I should hate this game. I'm one of those people who has a grudge against Jaws for what it did to the public image of sharks. This game is in that same vein - you are a shark and you are violently hungry and angry at all times, murder humans for fun, and never stop eating, but honestly? I can't hate it. The game doesn't take itself seriously enough. There's enough distance between what this shark is and what an actual shark does that I'm okay with leaping out of the water and over a bridge to consume the human on it. I'm okay with grabbing a turtle and tail whipping it into a sperm whale's face because honestly, screw the both of them. I love the character of Scaly Pete. Not because he's particularly deep, but he is interesting. And also hilarious. And for all that wackiness there, there is even some depth. At the end of the game, the narrator says there's "something to be learned here", but then cuts himself off because it's "just a show about people killing sharks, and sharks killing people." But he's not wrong! Man Eater is a game about the cycle of violence and revenge. Both Scaly Pete and The Bull Shark (who I have affectionately named Shania because MAN she eats all the humans) lost their parents to the Port Clovis Man-Shark War, and they’re both literally scarred by it. It’s really interesting to me that everything bad that happens to Pete is his own fault. He loses his hand because he just has to mutilate a newborn shark - something he only did because he was trying to avenge his dad. He loses his leg, his son and gets half his body exploded because he then needs to get revenge for losing his hand. He then dies because he wants to get revenge for the loss of his son. At any point, Pete could have stopped and saved himself more grief.But that’s the rub, isn’t it? He can’t. He’s a shark hunter, through and through, born into this life and more than happy to die in it. It’s almost a classic tragedy in that way. Had it been anyone else, none of this might have happened. But he can’t. So the cycle continues.As for Shania, she’s a hoot to play. At first I didn’t think she had much of a personality, and in the same way that Samus Aran or Gordon Freeman don’t, she doesn’t. But that doesn’t mean she’s an empty blank slate. Assuming all the missions you do are things that Shania is interested in doing, she too is focused only on vengeance. An entire category of her missions are called “Revenge”! And a lot of the revenge missions don’t target random humans, they specifically target places Pete likes to visit or deal with. She wants to take everything from Pete, and then kill him. But she’s also a shark, so she’s interested in defining her territory - the entirety of Port Clovis. Her slaughter of the Apexes is something she does to set herself up as the Apex. But then you get things like the license plates, and it seems like she has hobbies. Maybe that’s why she lives at the end? Shania has something to live for, Pete doesn’t. Or, maybe, it’s just a silly action game about a shark going ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ because that’s fun. And on that level, it DEFINITELY succeeds. The controls are ever so slightly wonky - mostly in regards to trying to fight near the surface when you suddenly start knifing when you certainly DO NOT WANT TO - but I don’t entirely know how to fix that? I feel like having a button specifically to enter knifing would be even clunkier. I also would’ve liked a lock-on mechanic instead of a focus-threat mechanic. Also, jumping out of the water is…weird. I never really figured out how to get Shania to go where I wanted her to when getting air, which became especially frustrating in the time trials. Lastly, other people have told me they felt the game got samey towards the end, and I can definitely see why. A good example is the bounties. Fighting boat after boat after boat after boat to then fight a bigger boat can get really boring. I avoided this by diversifying my activities. Instead of leaving the bounties for the end, for instance, I’d work my way up to the next bounty boss while clearing the Revenge mission, and then take them on roughly every time I cleared an area, letting me do other things in between to keep things interesting. Pace your playthrough and you’ll be fine.FINAL ASSESSMENT: If you’ve ever wanted to play GTA, except you’re a shark violently mauling people in an attempt to seek revenge, then play this game. If you want a fun, over-the-top action game, then play this game. The high points way, WAY out pace the few lows. The only reason I can see people who like action games not liking this is that they think it’s too crazy. But then, if you feel that way, why are you here?

_childDocuments_.review: this is a rough one. the gameplay loop is mind-numbingly repetitive, there's only 3-4 different types of missions and you have to complete them over and over and over again to finish a region. after you clear a region, you get a (luckily skippable) cutscene that advances the completely uninteresting and half-baked story. you can expect to repeat that process 10-12 times over the course of the game. not to mention the unfunny and needlessly pretentious narration that just continually grates at your psyche until you decide to turn it off. none of the mutations are exciting. the currencies are meaningless because you'll be able to afford every upgrade for every mutation about halfway through the game. some of the animations are pretty janky, the character models are godawful. the combat is totally underwhelming and you'll quickly learn that spamming dodge and bite is a hard counter to just about every enemy in the game. last of all, the exploration is purely underwhelming. every so often you'll come across a cool easter egg, but the rest of the exploration comprises copy/pasted sewers or caves that have literally zero variation. on a positive note, the game is really beautiful, especially the ocean areas.

_childDocuments_.review: This seems like it should have all the ingredients for a jolly good time. Yet, after half a dozen hours with Maneater, I still haven't found my sea legs. _childDocuments_.review: It's an okay game.  A lot of basic button mashing until the near the end of the game when it finally starts giving body parts which offer different strategies, fighting with the camera, and a god awful breach mechanic which is too random to be reliable.  It's the main reason I didn't 100% this game, because I couldn't be bothered to keep going through the same breaching motion over and over until it decided I did whatever right and actually gave me the height I need to collect something. Man Eater is barely an open world game.  If you try to play it like an open world game, you'll be at it forever.  Instead, it leads you around by the mouth with quests and bonus objectives like "eat 10 turtles" or "kill this somewhat higher level than normal predator" or "collect 10 license plates" which give colossal rewards, completely removing any reason to actually play it like an open world game other than to alleviate boredom with occasional murder sprees.I'd recommend waiting for a sale to try it, but it's okay.  The novelty is there and it's a simple, yet still fun game.

_childDocuments_.review: The objective of the game is to go from little fish to big fish by eating other fish, humans and random junk. Grinding (killing things for currency), collecting and doing other repetitive things like kill x of x or kill the Apex predator (boss) is how you progress. You just swim, eat, collect and grow bigger. That's the whole game pretty much. Grind and repetition. The novelty of playing as a big, bad shark and eating humans wears of pretty quickly and you start off as a baby shark anyway so it takes a lot of time to get there in the first place. There's a story tacked on (avenging your mother or something) but again it's just travelling from area to area, killing things over and over again, getting bigger and stronger and then taking on more powerful foes until you finally avenge your mother I guess. The game has a habit of crashing randomly too. For the asking price of £33.99 I'd absolutely not recommend it lol! Graphics are pretty nice and there's some Killing Floor references which are a nice touch if you like that game. An alright time waster but with so many games to play and so little time who actually has time to waste? Not me.It would've been nice to play as other predators, more customisation and really just more to do apart from killing things and levelling up. May as well go back to playing World of Warcraft. More variety in the type of quests would be a good start.

_childDocuments_.review: Make no bones that this IS a fun game. So why the downvote? Well if you look at achievement percentages only a little over 1/3 of all players made it into the 2nd half of the game. This is because a single piece of the electric set you get through killing Bounty Hunters makes you op and then everything is a walkover. Attack, swim off, grab some nearby feeder fish to stay alive - rinse and repeat.Amusing then that I saw several reviews saying the game gets too hard the more hunters you kill. I can only suggest that those people didn't understand upgrading and changing evolutions (equipment).You've seen pretty much all the game has to offer well before hitting 15 hours play time. This doesn't mean the game is too short though because it's a wild ride that is already overly bulked with grind quests. But there are so many of these quests that you will hit the lvl 30 cap long before you complete the story and from that point it's kind of disappointing. The DLC is more of the same but harder and even though it IS more of the same the game isn't really a complete game without it. It's also kind of irritating that the 30-40 cap change doesn't come into effect until you complete the main story and move on to the new area.If this were £25 including the DLC then I'd give it a thumbs up for novelty value and pure visceral fun. If it's on sale then it's certainly worth having. At the full price that many paid though it needed something more.Regardless of the overall negative for the reasons mentioned above I have to give Kudos for making a pretty cool game that dares to be different. Once again proving that Steam needs a neutral sideways thumb for reviews.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok so i went on this game with no expectation, i bought it on sale for 4€ i have to say i really enjoy my time on this one taking 16hours basically too beat 100% of the game. Now lets talk on what did the game brings to you. U start as a little shark and u will be challenge trough maps to beat bigger predatores and generating threat on the population making so that the AI attack u too with boots, and they also have some bosses that u have to beat while u gain reputation. While u progress u will unlock several mutations that can allow u too build your shark on different ways and let me tell u that each one of them provide diferent uses for sure! Some of this mutations comes from finding "Secret Places" that are not that secret since when u upgrade your sonar all the loot is really easy too find and the maps in my opinion are really a pleasure to explore. Now i saw alot of people bashing this games cuz of the controls and crashes and i will give my honest opinion about this one! !! I DIDNT USE A CONTROLER !! i play the whole game with mouse and keyboard and never had any problem with the controls of the game or controlling the shark even on the time trials that alot of people complaing on the DLC but i will get on that part too. Its true that sometimes when attacking humans the aim/control looks a little junky but overall i enjoyed my time playing and had no issues with the control itself. Now lets talk about crashes i had 2 crashes playing the whole game and never had my progress deleted as some players talk. One of them when fighting peter for the first time it did crash when i smashed the cage, and i had another crash after purchasing the DLC on a time trial. So lets talk about the DLC.I definitly feel that the game was a little bit more "clunky" with the DLC not sure why but u can really feel some optimization issues when playing on the DLC but like i said never had any really problems and i think that the whole DLC adds some new interesting fights from new predators with same mechanics and mutations that u have to some new AI fights on some crazy boats withs nukes and helicopetrs and as expected some more normal missions but overall i think if u grab the DLC on sale too its defenitly worth the time and i did really enjoy the challenge of the time trials that werent really a challenge but it was fun having a new mechanic on the game(where the shadow build/speed build trully shines). Now i have to bash the dev's for 1 thing only that i cannot agree on any game and that is putting DLCs achievements to force players buying extra content i never agreed with that and i think thats not the way things should work.But overall its a fun game to spend some hours if u like the sea theme while being one of the biggest predators that exist definitly worth a pick up if u grab it on sale on my opinion!

_childDocuments_.review: It's a generally amusing game but you really have to buy it at the right price. 12 hours is enough to 100% the whole thing, so keep that in mind when you consider what price you want to buy it. This might last you a chill weekend or a week at most. I really wouldn't consider buying this until it's under 15 bucks, and absolutely don't buy it until it's on sale at minimum.It's an RPG, but a bare bones one. You have 3 builds (chosen via armor sets) basically and a couple options for powers like echolocation or damage resistance, etc. You have to eat creatures for resources (there's 4 max) and just doing the side content is enough to get you most of what you need for the entire game.The story is goofy, which is to be expected, and the mock "Deadliest Catch" style keeps it entertaining.Few minor criticisms - the random dialogue is fairly repetitive, and this includes the narrator. t's noticeable but not terribly annoying. The jumping mechanic is really janky, which becomes annoying the handful of times you're asked to use them. It frequently doesn't do what you want, either leading to a really shallow jump, or a back flip. Coupled with a camera flip when this happens, and you might be able to land where you want, but then accidentally jump back in the water because of the camera lock.Buy it for cheap, play it over a couple days, then go back to playing something more substantial.
