Cons: - Stunted growth, you cant grow past level 30, lost opportunity Imo, since this is the kind of game where you want to be a demigod shark. - lack of skins, as of writing this there are only 3 types of skins you can get, Bone, Shadow and Electric. yes they are sets of armor essentially, but still the lack of  skins is a - in my opinion- the hunted and Apex predators were too easy, yes the first apex and hunted  ones off to be easy  to get you used to it, but  Even Moby ♥♥♥♥ was as easy as a normal Sperm Whale.  You could have put them in pods since both orcas and Sperm whales  travel and hunt in pods.  -collectables, way too many per zone specially the Gulf area, not to mentions they might have been a bit fun the first 4 areas but after a while  they were too much. - limited bounty system, why only 10 hunters, it would have been cooler if you gave us 100, killing hunters was fun, having to learn how to kill them all was fun. IF  you can get this on a discount, wholeheartedly recommended, it a fun sgort game that makes you feel sad for the  bad guy.      Overall  8.5/10  IMO

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could give a middle thumbs up. The game's okay, I did have my fun with it but there's too much grinding. Took me about 10 hours to finish the main game. The story is all over the place. Are we supposed to feel empathetic to the shark hunters that kill for fun? Shouldn't we just focus on killing rich people for ruining the environment? Aren't we supposed to be empathetic to the shark we play as and understand why it must kill humans? Put a little logic and depth to its motives from birth to adult life. It tries to set up the villain and make him empathetic but he's just a shark hunter that (again, just kills for fun) tries to find the shark that killed his father (and he never does).I adore sea life so exploring it was nice, but I wish there was more to do in the open waters. It's just barebone and finding collectibles. The busyness of it all is in the crammed beginning areas for some reason.Overall, okay game. Not really worth $40. Get it on sale. I have yet to try the DLC and I'm seeing that it's pretty mixed.

_childDocuments_.review: The game can be terribly frustrating, it's short, and there really isn't anything to do once you 100% it, but I still really enjoyed playing it. I think the most frustrating moments (without giving spoilers) were.. a boss fight where I struggled to beat the boss and was low on health with other mobs agro-ing on me, so while I fought them, the boss's body disappeared because there is a corpse timer mechanic whyyyyyyyy!? I wanted those points for eating that! Then there was the final showdown where the game suddenly without explanation introduces a new game mechanic that had me dying repeatedly until I googled it. Once I knew what I needed to do, it was no problem, and the fight was really fun. I started to crash quite a bit near the end, but I was playing windowed while watching a movie (Jaws of course) so that might be on me. My number 1 complaint though, would be the narrator. I know you can turn it off, but for some reason that would sometimes mute dialog in cutscenes, and I actually like the little quips when I find a new landmark, just not when I'm in the middle or a fight, or every single time I smash a nutrient cache. LOVE the game though! I can't wait for the DLC!

_childDocuments_.review: I got Maneater on sale for under $30 and the DLC for 50%. For that price, this is a great game and a fun, solid experience through the entire main campaign. While the game can feel pretty easy, it does a good job of making you feel like some sort of SyFy channel movie monster, the transition from baby shark in the bayou to super-powered megalodon bodying sperm whales in the gulf feeling satisfying. Story's clearly secondary, but shows that the team cared, as it's a step or two above story for the sake of it, with the Moby ♥♥♥♥ inspiration coming through well. Gameplay is solid, though lock on can frustrate as it's more of a soft aim-assist, but gets the job done 9/10. The other obvious flaw is how janky land movement is, sometimes taking away directional control or throwing you random directions. Despite that, the base game doesn't ask much of you on land, and with 90% of the game in the water, you'll find the game is controls to generally be tight and consistent, with movement underwater letting you really feel like a giant underwater death machine. If you're looking for a rampage game crossed with a collectathon, get it, especially if it's on sale. Don't bother with the DLC if you don't feel like fighting the jankier parts of the games controls.P.S. Would love to see more games with this concept, normal animal becoming a big monster. Cool ♥♥♥♥

_childDocuments_.review: I'll keep this a bit shorter than my usual reviews.You play a shark. You swim around, kill and get stronger. The game feels very grindy in the beginning, but I needed about 20 hours for the main game, but I also did everything. Kill all the bounty hunters, get all the powers, etc. Even some of the collections. (I'm not a completionist when it comes to collecting stuff...)The game is not particularly difficult. While playing the shark, you get comments from a fictional nature show moderator, who sometimes tells interesting shark facts and mostly spews funny, cynical background information. Really enjoyed that.Now, is the game worth it's full price? To be fair, I think it is a game you should buy in a sale. Unless you are really into mutated sharks, dark humor and clicking left mouse button a lot.The DLC costs another 15 Euro. I checked some YT videos, it seems to have about 3 hours or so of play time so I decided to not buy it at full price. Maybe in a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: At this time I've finished the main story. I've played a bit of the.. epilogue (?) which seems to direct me to the DLC content. This made me unsure if I've bought the DLC or not since I got this game in a humble bundle and the DLC is not on my account. Anyways, confusion aside here are my thoughts:The start was excruciatingly slow. You'll feel that you're really at the bottom tier of the food chain. That is until you leveled up into a teen that can handle the endless waves of shark hunters (and mini bosses) to power level into adulthood. Doing that somewhat broke the game for me which is fine because all I want from this game is some "brainless, power fantasy, and consume everything" kinda fun. You know, channel your inner shark animal spirit kind of thing.The story is passable. Just some excuse to kill the baddies. The sarcastic/clever lines by the narrator added the necessary spice to enliven this seemingly mentally bankrupt game.The evolution mechanic seems lackluster because of how you unlock them. You just collect and complete mutation sets by completing objectives instead of something more creative like having new abilities based on defeated enemies or a skill tree. By sticking to a "set" they limited the possibility of mutations because they have to follow a theme.Boss designs are uninspired. The apex predators are like ordinary enemies but have a larger health pool. The apex sperm whale was a joke after stun locking it with the electric shark build. The shark hunter bosses are just people with guns instead of introducing new mechanics or interesting attacks. Just "snipe" the mini boss and voila, you get a new mutation. I finally had to use my brain for the last boss which surprised me and highlighted one of the missed opportunities for the game.The game looks beautiful and runs well but you'll notice pop ins if you look too closely.If you're bored, this game is on a deep deep sale, and want to play as a shark, get this game. I guess it's a casual's first game kinda good but for long time gamers don't expect much. At 10 hours I think I've gotten what I came for but it's too bland to keep me playing. Maybe a sequel or a remake would be better.Overall, a mediocre game. I wish Steam has a "Maybe" rating since I didn't regret having the game but I can't see myself recommending it so I have to rate this game as a Not Recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Loving sharks and all things ocean my entire life, this little game is fun to play after a long day at work and you just want to blow off some steam! Maneater could loosely be described as a shark RPG game, where you start off as a baby bull shark and work your way up to becoming one of the biggest terrors in the sea. The game is very button smash-y, it's pretty short and I could see how people don't like it because of its "repetitive" nature. But the dark humor story flipping the script and making it about a baby shark out for revenge against a reality TV shark hunter film crew is hilarious. Plus it's packed full of all sorts of shark/ocean movie references and narrated by Chris Parnell who routinely says how the actions you're taking as the shark aren't typical shark behavior. Brilliant. Overall, I'd give it a 7.5/10, grab it while it's on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: A game where I can be a shark and eat people? Yes please! In Maneater you play as a bull shark who is the main focus of reality show featuring shark hunters. Gameplay is straightforward, they give you quests, you complete quests. Pretty simple, just be sure to eat lots of fish (fish are food, not friends!) and people to level up. As you progress you gain mutations that allow you to upgrade your shark as you see fit. And the best part is they can always be swapped out if you find you have need for one over another. The storyline and narrator are entertaining. The graphics are good. The controls are pretty simple to learn. There's a lovely map to help you keep track of quests, both completed and in progress. And the best part, you get to be a shark! The camera takes some getting used to. While not a problem for me, I've seen that some people have issues with the game crashing. Some quests can be a bit repetitive. There is no in game instructions on how to do more advanced moves with the controls.Is this game worth full price? Probably not. The base game took me about 24 hours to 100% and other then the entertainment value of eating people, I don't see a reason to replay. At least not anytime soon.

_childDocuments_.review: From start to finish, Maneater was a really fun game to play and was well worth the time i played it. The start of the game can be difficult, although as you level up the game becomes more fun, that's not to say the start of the game isn't enjoyable.Overall brings me back to the Jaws game on the PS2 but in a much more modern and delightful experience. Cop this game on special for sure!

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a great game! Outstanding graphics which I enjoyed greatly as the scenery is fantastic. Not to mention the eargasmic sounds of human screams and yummy crunching noises.My only issue throughout 100%-ing the game is how much targeting munchies relies on camera view which results in various annoyances such as constant jittering, and the shark losing focus on an intended snack, especially when surrounded by a f**ng deadly buffet. Might have been only me, but I think it could have been improved by 1.) being able to actually lock on and focus on a specific snack, especially during boss fights (e.g., bounty hunters in Truth Quest), and or 2.) have a mechanic such that a focused foodie, like a boat, can be focused by the camera so that we can properly monitor the attacks of the deadly food, and avoid having to turn around for unbearable amounts.All in all, a fantastic game! As someone also said in their review, I also bought this on sale when it was afterwards free on Epic Games dang. Nonetheless it is worth paying (maybe on sale) and playing for (granted you have time to grind).

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: ★★★★☆ (4/5)Maneater is a toothy, blood-soaked delight. Playing as a vengeful shark on a mission for payback, this open-world RPG offers a unique and thrilling experience. The gameplay, centered around evolving your shark while causing chaos, is addictive and surprisingly easy to pick up. While the story is a bit thin, the stunning graphics, immersive underwater world, and replay value make it a must for those seeking a carnivorous gaming adventure. Jump in, devour, and relish the sheer absurdity and fun of being the ultimate predator.

_childDocuments_.review: I never realized how much I wanted to play as a shark until this shark game. And boy did they let me live my dreams. It was good, clean, casual, circle of life, nature is metal, terrifying, predatory, gratuitous violence and gore, fun! A polished game that looked, played, and sounded great. Quality work and it showed. It's not a terribly long game as single player campaign games go, but it felt like there was enough variety and content that I was more than happy with the price of admission. It makes for excellent casual gaming and there's some replayability. They even found time to make a story that I was able to follow and even cared about, and narration with lines that kept the game light-hearted,Definitely recommend it for when you're looking for casual gameplay and don't want to try too hard, just mess around and have some fun.Tripwire: definitely make more of this! I will pay for more content! I could easily see this as being a fun (and hopefully profitable) franchise.

_childDocuments_.review: ***I will change this to a "Recommend" should they ever remove denuvo***After having removed it from my wishlist, because of denuvo, I was gifted this game by a friend. Aaand it crashed in the first 15 minutes.. Denuvo ALWAYS causes problems!  The Game:The game is dumb, turn your brain off, kind of fun..  The only point is to cause mayhem, and get bigger, to cause more mayhem!  And sometimes, thats all you want at the end of the day... "Some men, just wanna watch the world burn" (fish, in this case)-AlfredIt has light rpg elements, with a sort of ability growth, and loot system. The loot is color coded, and has linear upgrades, but it is your fins, teeth, skin, etc.. Its what gives the sense of progression, and keeping you playing. Otherwise, I would imagine the fun factor would wear thing in a few hours.. Its frankly quite astonishing that theyve been able to turn the simple behaviors of a shark, into a game that remains fun for ANY amount of time, let alone hours.. Ive gotten back on for three consecutive days.. In short bursts, but, I am coming back!My one complaint is that it can be changed, like its a helmet.. These choices should be permanent. This would also provide replayability, in trying out a different evolution.Control:Controls are somewhat odd, but thats because youre controlling a shark, I think. Targeting, and breaching, and some of it does feel quite cumbersome, but I am still very early in. Several hours later, it still feels to janky, and inconsistent.. The controls are quite poor, imho.UI:The in game menu, specifically the "Log", are amongthe most frustratingly stupid designs Ive ever encountered! It appears like its section off per zone, but as you scroll down the list, it jumps up and down at random! Its infuriating! It looks like it has a secondary horizontal sub selection, but you can not manually access it. Visual:Graphics are fine. Im playing in 2k, and its not intended to look realistic. As is often the case, the screenshots on the store page Im willing to bet are upgraded. they always look markedly better than the actual game. But the game doesnt look bad either, dont misunderstand. It can be difficult to see in dark areas, or at night. Performance:Framerate has been fine thus far, with graphics maxed, at 2k, on a 3060, ryzen 5 5600x, on SSD.. Though the game crashed as I exited, and wanted to send data to "Unreal".. 3 hrs later, I experienced a 2nd crash, this time being a hard crash that shut down the game during play.Ill reiterate.. The ONLY reason I am 'Not Recommending', is specifically for Denuvo.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: #1. The game runs very well#2. The graphics are pretty good (above average certainly)#3. The narrator actually sometimes mentions some cool facts about fish#4. Starting out as a wee-fishy and becoming a 10metre (33feet) chompy-boy is fun#5. The shark design is really cool (especially with the different augments)Cons: #1. A massive and constant stream of overlapping dialogue by the narrator#2. Jumping into the air is extremely finicky and the game actually requires you to get to high-up places very often, which exacerbates the issue#3. I'm not joking about the Thalassophobia. If you suffer from fear of deep water, then you will absolutely want to avoid this game. I personally don't suffer from it, but my heartbeat CERTAINLY shot up a couple of times because of the deep water#4. The game is very short. $40 for just 8hours of gameplay is bad (and the DLC costs $15 and can be finished in 3hrs)#5. No multiple save slots (you just get ONE save slot)#6. No UI options whatsoever (no colorblind or opacity options)#7. No photomode#8. There's quite a lot of 'walking simulator' stuff going on. Sometimes you travel multiple miles just for the narrator to spew out a few one-liners and then it's off to the next location, which is again miles away#9. The narrator being a conspiracy theorist in the DLC isn't exactly funny. The devs tried to squeeze some humor out of the premise, but none came out.#10. I wish there were more types of augments (4 different ones isn't enough)#11. The game is quite grindy, especially in the mid-to-late game#12. The fact that the hunters from their boats can shoot you with bullets while you're 100feet below the water is counter-intuitive (haven't the devs watched Mythbusters ever?)Overall it's a really cool game, and the devs can absolutely turn this game into a mega-hit, if they allow you to choose different starting predators (instead of just a shark). Like, starting out as a Crocodile or an Octopus, would be super, super, super cool. Anyways, at the end of the day, if you're OK with paying $40 for just 8-10hours of gameplay, then have at it... it's a good gameMy wishlisted games if you wanna be a bro: For more reviews, visit my curator page:

_childDocuments_.review: A fun, fast paced exploration/collectibles game with perk/upgrade progression where you play as a customizable shark and kill everything on sight. I picked this up on sale, and recommend others to do so as well if they are unsure they'd enjoy it. While buildcrafting my shark and unlocking new perks was enjoyable, there ended up not being too many of these to choose from, even counting the ones added from the expansion, Truth Quest. The maps are quite beautiful and detailed, and cool landmarks and references are strewn about, making exploration easily one of the highlights of the game, though the presence of invisible walls blocking off sections of the city, and the lack of an option to disable antialiasing detracted from the freedom of movement and visual fidelity aspects for me. Honestly what kept me going probably was the movement tech and high apm potential in combat. And playing as a shark. Although, I wish there was just a bit more depth to combat other than bite/tailwhip/evo ability/sonar. As for replayability, I see myself coming back now and then if I'm bored to try doing stupid ♥♥♥♥ or take screenies, perhaps more if there is an update or new expansion.The story was really meh, the missions were repetitive and uninspired, and there was so much unfulfilled potential. But...Pretty cool game--pretty much what I expected, plus a bit.

_childDocuments_.review: As much as I love being able to play as a shark and cause havoc in the water. The game is buggy and refused to pick up my PS4 controller no matter what I tried. So I was forced to play on janky as hell keyboard and mouse controls.Threat builds too fast, hunters hit stupid hard, not nearly enough information on how to open buttons for gates. I had to google how to open the gates because my shark would not bite onto and HOLD onto the thing. It just kept biting until I found something sturdy like a human or a turtle. The fact you require an "evolution" to have predator creatures lower than you to leave you alone is stupid. No predator Barracuda or Musky fish would be stupid enough to attack a full grown shark without an entire school to back them up.The narrator is annoying as hell, spouting misinformation every five seconds and I didn't turn it off until I was finished with the story because I wanted to hear what he had to say. But there should be an option to turn off the constant "blurb of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥" whenever you enter an area you have already been in. Because sometimes a fight takes you in and out of a border and having the narrator repeat himself ten times over because you kept going in and out of an area during a fight with ships or a whale or w/e was exceptionally annoying.Controls: I can't speak for how this works on a controller, but I was forced to use keyboard and mouse. Jumping I would not keep my momentum, I could not get the shark to turn how I wanted. Dashes would just turn off even if I'm still holding the dash button down to keep my speed up. My camera would randomly switch directions when I hit the land after a jump, forcing my shark to go in an entirely different direction even though I hadn't moved my mouse. I would get stuck on ships, props, people, anything and everything and couldn't get out sometimes for 5-10 minutes. It was rage inducing.DLC: Time trials are stupidly difficult when using Keyboard and mouse. Jumping is inconsistent on a good day, but trying to get over a bloody bridge with a timer!? Forget about it. The military ships were kinda fun at first, but the torpedos were nearly impossible to catch unless I was in my atomic body and dodging them. Any other body? Just trying to catch them? Nope. Impossible. Also why is the atomic body forcing you to be a Hammerhead shark?! Did you lose ideas and cop-out to a lame "well you're mutated so you gotta look like the weirdest shark species, the Hammerhead!"!?!? Like come on! They made the other irradiated animals look like themselves and cool! Why did we have to suddenly turn into a Hammerhead!?Overall: Play this game if you like being a shark and just killing everything in the ocean. It's pretty fun! I enjoyed the difficulty of the fights with alligators, the Apexes of the area, and even the story with Scaly Pete. Getting my Shadow evolutions as early as I did because I wanted them so badly allowed me to just breeze through some things in a super fun fashion. Original hunter fights were fun, then got annoying after Pete because almost every ship had that stupid shield and refused to drop bombs. Tail slap targeting when you did have a bomb was inconsistent and frustrating. Narrator is annoying, keyboard controls are a nightmare on the wrists/fingers and for progressing game-play.

_childDocuments_.review: I used to have a jokey positive review for this game, however after returning to it recently to play through the DLC I feel I should get more serious.Maneater is a good game I feel. You start off as a little fish hanging on to your life by a thin thread, and by the end of the game you're the king of the seas, snacking on whales and obliterating sea vessels with your mere presence (alright that last bit might be a bit hyperbolic, but just a bit).The game isn't for everyone however. The various activities are pretty samey in every location, and most hostiles can be dealt with the same way as well, with very few unique encounters towards the end.Personally for me, the positives above outway the negatives.What completely drags the game deep down into the depths of non-recommendation for me is the game's poor performance. At the start of the game it played very smoothly for me, but as I progressed I began running into constant FPS drops and even some freezes and crashes. Things simply got worse and worse.At first I didn't really feel it fair to put that into consideration for my opinion of the game, thinking perhaps the issue was with my previous computer, as it had various issues in general. However, I've since gotten the computer maker to replace my faulty computer with a new, way better one, yet now as I return to Maneater, it suffers from the exact same FPS drops and freezes/crashes. Literally the first time I loaded the game up on this computer it brought up a game crash report dialogue box instead of the game.On forums I've seen people complain about these issues for at least a year, yet whoever's in charge of greenlighting a possible fix in Tripwire doesn't seem interested in doing anything about it.As such I can't recommend Maneater at this time.

_childDocuments_.review: I have unlocked 100% the main game and started Truth Quest. It's still a very repetitive experience. Hardly any variety to the content. Each area of the game has the same mission types. Mostly kill/eat a bunch of marine life or people. If you aren't doing that you are swimming around finding collectibles. I've maxed out all the main game's evolutions and at level 30 I still don't feel like a dominant ocean predator. Humans have ridiculous auto-aim that hits you every time. Fighting them mainly consists of ramming their boat. Ram, ram, ram, spin, ram, ram, ram, spin. As a mega-shark I should be able to completely decimate them with just a few bites. Fighting boss creatures consists of the same patterns. Bite, bite, bite, dodge, bite, bite, bite, dodge. Starts glowing, dodge and bite. Rinse and repeat. The only variety to the enemies in Maneater is aesthetics. The game really needs some patches to allow you to dominate after you have put in the required time to max out everything. Also a patch for the swimming function of the game. My left trigger finger is sore from repeatedly holding L2 on the controller to speed up. This could be fixed with a simple toggle-speed mode feature.  I will say that the narrations from Chris Parnell of "Rick and Morty" fame are hilarious and basically the only thing that kept me motivated to play the game to it's entirety. Overall Maneater has a great sense of humor and it's the levity that makes it an enjoyable experience. I'd only recommend buying this game if you can get it and the DLC for $10-$20  on a Steam sale. Otherwise don't waste your money.

_childDocuments_.review: I own the XB1 version of this game, picked the PC port up in a recent sale as I thought it would be fun to play at 60 Sharks a Second.And yes, the game is fun. It is repetitive, it is a bit grindy, the targeting could be better, but it is just good silly violent fun. Never takes itself too seriously, some funny dialogue, a decent gameplay loop that makes you feel like a beast. And you cannot deny jumping about the beaches eating humans left and right is a great laugh.But. This version of the game is riddled with problems.Many 12th Gen CPU owners simply cannot start the game. There has been no official patch for owners of today's current tech and the workarounds vary greatly in success. I was lucky enough to not have this problem but instead have another.I can only play for about an hour at a time before the game crashes with an Unreal Engine error. My guess is that it is a memory leak. So far nothing else has happened, but other users have reported game save wipes and even total PC shutdowns from the game crashing. So not good really, is it?I understand games, once done, are done. We're not asking for content, we're just wanting to be able to play a game on current hardware technology without issues. The game is still on sale, any stability problems should be addressed or the game should be taken off the store front.This isn't some retro Win 95 classic, nor are we running the game on outdated hardware, customers are moving with the times yet the game is not.However the Devs/Publisher seemingly do not give a damn. No mods active on these forums, nothing about hotfixes or similar. Zilch. Yet, the game is still on sale.A super fun and bizarre "rage em up" akin to early GTA or Destroy All Humans, but a technical experience that really isn't worth the effort.Only buy if these issues do not deter you, and really consider refunding within that 2 hour period.Win 11 i7 12700k 3.6ghz, RTX 3070 8GB, 32GB DDR4 Ram

_childDocuments_.review: Really funny and original game. It's a very relaxed Metroidvania-style underwater exploration game, where you can relax and work on getting to each collectible and each trick jump at your own pace. The combat is really satisfying, especially with a gamepad which gives force feedback, but it's great with keyboard and mouse too. The story is funny and intriguing, and the world is constantly narrated by a sarcastic narrator voice as if it's a nature documentary. There are tons of pop culture references to find under the sea, with references to popular movies and games.One of the most unique and entertaining games I've ever played. Reminds me of Subnautica, if you were the monster instead.The base game is the best by far. The DLC goes in a totally different direction, and mostly consists of artificial padding (going back to all previous areas to collect items) but at least offered some really fun and intense boss fights. It's worth having the DLC.The game is definitely pretty long if you do everything in the game:- 100% base game with all achievements, all quests, all collectibles, at casual pace: 15h 21m- 100% DLC: 6 hoursMy only wish is that there was something else to do after 100% in the game. Such as random encounters with mutated fish that have random boss abilities, so that you could fight endless bosses in a roguelike way. Sadly there's nothing like that. When you've done everything, there's nothing left to do but swim around as the apex predator with nothing threatening around anymore. I hope they create another DLC or sequel for this game.

_childDocuments_.review: When I first saw this game announced at E3 a few years back, I though it looked pretty cool. Then I heard about the game going Epic exclusive and I lost all interest. The most annoying thing about combat is the targeting system which doesn't actually lock-on to enemies. This makes it hard to keep track of where your enemy is during a fight. Combat itself is very shallow, consisting mainly of mashing the R2 button over and over.The missions do not offer a lot of variety. Really the only types of missions are collectathons in each area of the map, and missions where you go to an area and kill a thing. That's about it.The graphics and presentation are nice, but overall this is really just a mediocre game, like a 69/100. That combined with the fact that the game went Epic exclusive at launch leads me to not be able to recommend this game. It could have been a cool game but instead it's just wasted potential.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is ridiculous and stupid and I love it.It's one of those games that I adore in large part because the game knows exactly what it is and doesn't try to be anything else. It never takes it's self too seriously. It knows it's over the top and just leeeeans right into it.What is Maneater? Well you play as a shark and your goal is to grow and eat, eat and grow, and kill loooots of people in increasingly hilarious ways. And it's one of those games that's a kill fest but you will feel 0 sympathy for the npc's you murder. Why? Because frankly... if someone looks up and sees a shark the size of an orca, glowing purple with bones on it's face... just casually hopping across the green before lunging towards your golfing buddy... eating them whole next to you... and your response is to just stand there waving your arms and screaming?... at that point it's natural selection and it's me... I'm the natural selection.But for a better picture. Maneater is Spore mixed with the mobile game Hungry Shark. All wrapped in a package that looks like a Discovery Channel show like Deadliest Catch. Eat things to gain points of various kinds. Use points to upgrade things to become stronger and weirder looking (the bone stuff is nightmare fuel... mostly the teeth). As such the first bit of the game is... admittedly rough. Surviving against the alligators in the swamp as a baby shark is really difficult. I died to those damn gators more than anything else in the whole game. Once you get a handle on things though, and if you do EVERYTHING in an area that you can before moving on to the next area, you'll find the game easier and easier to progress through.There is a story here, and as part of the story and to get various upgrades, you'll be trying to become more notorious causing various hilarious hunters to come after you on your quest to chew the face off a guy named Scaly Pete. Not gonna lie... I actually got into the story in a way I wasn't expecting to. I got VINDICTIVE at a certain point because I was all team shark. If you've ever watched Jaws 2.... this game has HIGH Jaws 2 vibes.As for graphics and performance I gotta say this game is prettier than it has any right to be. I never had any performance issues. The water graphics and physicals is freaking amazing. It took me till like half way through my play through to realize that I could fast travel between grottos (the little underwater safety caves in each area). I just swam everywhere. It got kinda tiring but honestly I never got so tired of it that it was annoying because the game was just so damn pretty to look at. Plus swimming around so much gave me plenty of opportunity to just eat everything I passed which got me more points to level stuff up. Which I think is in part what kept me ahead of stuff a fair bit.I ate so much stuff and made very sure to leave only stuff behind in an area that I couldn't physically do yet. That I'd get into a new area and very few things could do anything against me and missions were a breeze. I beat all Alpha's on the first tries. I beat all hunters on the first tries. The only struggle I had was the end battle with Scaly Pete.I didn't have a problem with it though. I wasn't here for difficulty. I was here for the over the top ridiculousness of the game and the game kept that up to a point that I never stopped having fun. I've 100% the base game and upon finishing picked up the dlc and am starting that now.With all that praise being said.... I do have some issues with the game.The primary one being that the price tag is egregious at best. I got the game in a humble bundle forever ago, but if I had paid $40 for it I think I would have been kinda disappointed. I feel like $30 is as much as I would pay for it, especially since the dlc tacks on another $15. Because again... I've started the DLC. My play time says 19 hours, but I finished the base game in like... 18 I think? Then when you take into account that I swam EVERYWHERE for half that play time. I probably could have finished the game in like 13 hours had I known I could fast travel. Because at a certain point a lot of my play time is backtracking to areas to get things I couldn't before getting whatever upgrade I needed.The other thing that's frustrating is the grates in each area. You'll find grates you can break to go into underwater caves or old sewer systems. Usually with goodies inside. I have no problem with that. If you pass one on the map and don't break it, it stays marked on the map for you to get back to. If you break it though? The marker is gone and that's SUPER frustrating. There were a few areas where I couldn't figure out how to get to something so I'd make a note to come back later and try, but then couldn't find the entrance. It's not bad with the sewer caves, but once you are in the ocean and finding openings to underwater caves it becomes REALLY hard to find an entrance that you broke before. I spent a solid 30 minutes trying to find ONE supply crate I was missing for 100% because I couldn't find the entrance I broke at some point but didn't go inside.Another annoyance is the controls for the jump on pc. It took me FOREVER to get some of the collectables you had to jump out of the water for because if you don't aim juuuuust right you won't get them, and if you pull back on the mouse the tiniest bit your shark does a backflip. I feel like there HAS to be a better way to do this.Other than those few issues I"d say pick up the game when it's on a decent sale. It's humor is great and it's the kind of stupid fun you can sit down with and have a blast. It's also a decent "I'm angry and just wanna murder things" kind of game. Like this game is gonna be my anger relief game for a while.

_childDocuments_.review: I remember seeing Jaws: Unleashed on the PS2, at the video store back when I was a kid and I always wanted to play it but never got a chance to. Maneater is basically the spiritual sequel to that game, and I'm glad I checked this one out! The story has you play as a shark, who's mother is killed by a shark hunter, which puts you on the path of revenge. The story is pretty basic, but good enough to keep you going and I liked the reality TV/documentary style they told the story through. It also helps that this game is narrated by Chris Parnell who voices Jerry on Rick and Morty! He adds a lot of funny quips and he definitely made the game a lot more enjoyable for me! Maneater builds on the concepts of Jaws: Unleashed, where you start as a baby shark, and have to evolve your shark eventually to a megalodon level shark, by eating everything you can and battling other apex predators! It also throws in RPG mechanics where you level your shark, and equip different evolutions (in place of typical gear) that buff your shark in different ways. I like that this game had a very Arcady nature to it, in that you can just cause so much mayhem and destruction. You even get an evolution that allows your shark to jump onto land, and eat people for an extended period of time. Its stuff like that just adds to the fun factor of this game! Music as well was also really good with my favorite track being the track that plays in the grotto, which is your sharks lair, where you can save, fast travel and upgrade your evolutionS. I also just enjoyed that the map was small, being split into different zones. It made the world not feel bloated that so many other open world/RPG games can feel at times, and with it taking me only 16 hours to complete everything (though some I heard have done it a shorter time) it felt like a nice pallet cleanser, in between bigger games. There is also the infamy system which is basically like the wanted level system in Grand Theft Auto, where when you caused enough chaos, you get shark hunters after you, which are like this games police. This also unlocks special bounty hunter bosses for you to fight, however its pretty easy to beat them as all you have to do is pull them into the water and eat them, and they have no real defense against you. Its fun to fight them and easy to escape them which I like, since many of the more recent GTA games made it hard to escape the police, to the point of it not being fun anymore for me at least. Combat is fairly decent as you pretty much just have a bite attack and tail whip to knock enemies away. It would have been nice to have a lock on feature, specifically when going up against other apex predators. But at the end of the day, it didn't bug me so much to the point of the combat being frustrating or anything like that. Some negatives, the enemy A.I. can be a bit dumb at times, particularly with the shark hunters, but like I said earlier, I prefer it being easier to escape them and then come back later to cause more chaos. The game can also be a bit too easy at times, as I wish there were different difficulty modes to pick from, as there is only one default difficulty. While performance was smooth with no major bugs, there were some humans enemies that would float in mid air, doing T poses, as well as on glitch, where I would break open a grate to get into hidden areas, only the grate would stay in place and not let me progress. It happen to me a few times and I had to quit to the main menu and reload to fix it. Otherwise, I really enjoyed my time with this game and I recommend it to anyone who wants a shorter, less bloated game or if you just want something different to play, compared to most other games on the market.

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the game a few minutes ago and i'd love to say a thing or two about this superb game!Evolution:When the game starts your mother gets killed by the hunter called Pete, who is assisted by his son. He is not fond of fishing, but thats not the main detail here. Pete gets you out of your mother's womb, which sounds weird but thats how it is. He scratches your fin, so when you grow up he will hunt you down and basically will reminisce the time, when he murdered the "mommy shark". You play as a bull shark. Start off small, but as the time progresses you gain evolutions, level up, obtain new body types, fins, jaws and so on. There're a few ages: child, Teen, Elder and Mega (if i am not mistaken those are the ones). Different body types and other armor can be unlocked by playing the game, visiting new locations, searching for underwater sightseeings, killing different types of Apex predators and etc. If you are into games where you evolve and go from child to an absolute monster, this game is genuinely amazing at it's job. I was thrilled to see the same enemies i was scared of being scared of me! Its not even a big game. 10-11 hrs and you will finish the whole story with all the side quests.Story: (no spoilers only the beginning part)As said, the Hunter cuts the bull's belly and you are there. As Pete scratches your fin you bite his hand off, but he gets a new one. You are in a swamp, small, helpless, scared of it's surroundings. However, environment is full of different types of fish, that are small and can be devoured by the small bull shark. As you level up and gain more evolutions story line progresses. Each time you explore a new location a cut scene appears, that shows what Pete and his son are up to. Once you've finished the particular location at 100% or 98% you unlock another cut scene, which, again, shows their work and where they are at. Trust me when i say this, i have never played such an immersive game ever. Oh, forgot to mention, Pete is being recorded by some studio (not sure which), i would assume they are creating a documentary about shark hunters, but it did not go as it had been planned. Excessively heartbreaking story, which i did not expect from this game. When i finished it, i did not want to do what i was supposed to, but, unfortunately, i had no control over a cut scene.P.S this has nothing to do with story, but since it goes along with the game why not elaborate for a bit. During the gameplay one person talks over and gives you details about the bull shark, different ares and all about ocean life (not literally everything but you get the point). This will help you learn more about Sharks and sea life. For example i've learned that Sperm Whales eat sharks!Enemy types:When it came down to potential preys and predators of the sea, i did not expect such a diversity. Now, i know ocean is full of undiscovered creatures, places and what not, but this game had it all! You start off being scared of alligators, then Mako sharks, Humans, Great Whites, Orcas, Sperm Whales, Hammerheads and some other. Best thing about enemies is that, you'll encounter buffed types of the predators. For instance, once you've finished exploring the area you'll have to go against an Apex Mako shark, or Apex greatwhite which adds up to the game. Killing humans can get you in a huge trouble too, as you kill hunters your bounty hunt levels up (not sure what its called exactly, but basically stronger people start to come at you), it can go up to 10 and at that point if you dont possess the bone armor there will be no chance of surviving Pete or ordinary hunters! Furthermore it has its own twist, you must get to lvl 10 in order to obtain unlockable evolutions, hence you become stronger!What is left to say? the game is fantastic! as long as i know it is also getting an expansion. I am extremely hyped about that too!Things i did not like: The game glitches out rarely and it does not work untill you quit it and turn it on again, Apex predators dont show up on the screen which also bugs out the game and you have to go to the main menu then try again, It has quite a lot of stutters and frame drops but dont take it from me, it may be just my PC. Thats about it.I would give it solid 7.5/10, because of the bugs.

_childDocuments_.review: This game makes you feel like a shark and you have a mission. It is somewhat open world and wilder than an aquatic Rick James party. Now, I don't know about you guys, but I don't like Sharks, I know they only attack you if you are wet but some part of me hates them instinctively. Despite that I always wanted to be a shark. Not just any shark, but a giant, ferocious one that eats everything in sight. And that's exactly what you get to do in Maneater. You play as a bull shark, the game lets you explore the underwater world like never before. You can eat anything from fish to humans, and chomping on some unsuspecting beach-goers is one of the most satisfying experiences you'll ever have. And if you're lucky, you might just find yourself a little cat named Fluffy that makes for a tasty snack (and you get to call yourself replace the word "man" in the title with ♥♥♥♥♥).The game has it's fair share of memes narrated by Chris Parnell (so hide the women-folk). You've got the "Shark Week" reference that will have you laughing your dorsal fin off, and let's not forget about the "Maneater" song that will have you humming along as you devour everything in your path.Maneater is a fun, easy and short game but well worth you sinking your teeth into, if you catch it on sale. It's got everything you could ever want in a shark game, from the humor to the carnage, and it's all wrapped up in a nice little bow of memes. The DLC content bring a bit more fun mechanical skill, but so broken! It makes everything way too easy.-Most fights against predators and infamy hunters are too easy.Pro Tips:-Utilize, upgrade, and abuse the Sonar ability asap. I was pretty lost and confused for a while till I understand that I gonna spam sonar on cooldown. -On a DLC quest, you will need to destroy a tower. It was very frustrating till I figured that I gonna hold the bite when I whiptail the sailor toward tower. It became easy after that. So, what you will need to do is to bite a sailor, go back in water and head near shore (keep holding the bite button), jump high enough till you can see your target marker is on the tower (keep holding the bite button), whiplash the sailor toward the tower (keep holding bite button when you whiplash), and rinse n repeat from there for a few times!- On a DLC quest, you will need to destroy a tower. Once you have the automatic body activation power, just use a few of that against tower. It is easy from there.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just okay. I bought it on sale because I really wanted to play it and like it, but the game mechanics leave a lot left to be desired. The game doesn't do a whole lot so it's tough to excuse. The story was non-existent for me. I didn't play it for the story, but I initially tried to at least pay attention to it but by the end I was just skipping it. The RPG elements are alright, though there really isn't a lot of variety. I pretty much used one set the whole game.All in all, it's a fun experience if you think you'd like the game and it's on sale, but I would not buy it at full price. _childDocuments_.review: At about 18 hours of gameplay to 100% achievements & content, I'd say Maneater (with the Truth Quest DLC) was a worthwhile purchase on sale (at about $20) once I got past the near-constant crashes.This is a fun action game with an arcade-y feel.  I guess it's technically an RPG since you're "role-playing" a shark, but it's much more an open-world game.  You're able to freely change your unlocked upgrades in your home bases (grottoes), which is helpful to tailor your shark to the specific challenges you're facing.  I found the sense of progression to be nice, balancing side-grades with upgrades of existing abilities (which is at your discretion - you spend resources gained from eating).By the end of the game, I felt fairly "done" with it so I thought the game length was good and didn't overstay its welcome to 100% it.

_childDocuments_.review: Janky but fun shark power fantasy. Climbing the food chain and becoming able to devour the predators that gave you trouble before is the core of the game, and it feels very satisfying. The game can feel grindy (there isn't all that much a shark can do, between eating things, fighting things, and finding collectibles) but as long as you find the core gameplay loop fun, it'll keep you entertained. The DLC is fairly short (~3 hours) but has a ton of fun mutations, and takes the power escalation to ridiculous, over the top levels. Definitely worth it if you enjoy the power fantasy.
_childDocuments_.name: Maneater

_childDocuments_.review: I'd just about recommend it if the concept appeals to you and if you play it in short sessions.Overall I had fun exploring the environments and being a badass shark while devouring everything in my path with cool animations, but the poor combat and linear progression prevent the game from reaching its full potential. It gets old and grindy just a few hours into the game.The combat is simply a joke, you can just spam dodge and attack simultaneously and win every encounter with your eyes closed. No challenge whatsoever.The progression is very linear and unrewarding. You start out as a baby shark but you're already overpowered, all the enemies around you are the same level, you can eat and beat everything in your area. There should have been threats to avoid and meaningful places to reach until you become larger and better equipped. You're always OP in each new area you enter, and all the quests are the same grind of eat 10 of this, eat 10 of that.They should have taken lessons from Hungry Shark World, a mobile game which I played many years ago and was way more fun and rewarding to play.Overall this game is a waste of good assets. It could have been so much better if they had a clue about game design.

_childDocuments_.review: I had no idea that Prototype, except you're a Shark, would be so much fun. As with Prototype, the game is all about a power fantasy where you rip through scores of enemies, eating them to heal. Any dodging mechanic is made superflous as a result, but I'd say the game is better for it. I wouldn't say it's difficult at all; I haven't died even once yet and I'm almost done with the game after beating all of the named hunters and the apex predators.I don't expect much replay value out of this game, and the timings of the special sets could be made to be a bit earlier (you don't get complete sets until you are mostly done with the game) to give us a bit more time to use them, but I also won't begrudge the devs for not cluttering the game with tons of useless items that won't ever be used; I've tried 2 out of the 3 sets so far and I'd say they're both equally viable, giving you the chance to pick based on your aesthetic and playstyle preferences.Overall, I'd say, buy it, it's a solid 8 hours of fun at the least. Or maybe I'm just under the influence of nostalgia for that shark game whose name I can't remember I played as a kid. But yeah, as long as you don't go in expecting a shark simulator, Shark Prototype is a great game accentuated by the documentary-voiced narrator with good and witty writing.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm recommending this, but with caveats.I really, really want to love this game. It's a fun roaming, chomping game where you grow a bull shark up from a brave little pup to the ridiculously absurd 9 meter "mega" shark. Along the way you swim through a variety of environments from bayou swamp all the way out to the deeper waters of the Gulf of Mexico, hunting for food, fighting with competitors, and, yes, eating man, just like it says on the title. Along the way you get to engage in a ridiculous set of mutations and run into a variety of ridiculous pop culture references. The narrative conceit of this being some sort of nature documentary is excellent. The game is narrated by the ever-hysterical Chris Parnell, who manages to deliver the lines with just the right mixture of seriousness and amusement. The other voice actors you hear are pretty solid as well, and the shark hunter, Scaly Pete, is surprisingly well-executed for how thin and light the plot actually is. A full movie of the cut-scenes, start to finish, will run you less than 20 minutes. This is not a game for those looking for dramatic story.The graphics are fantastic. The fish all look incredibly realistic, and it's easy to while away some time just swimming around and watching the fish of all kinds swim to and fro, and occasionally scarf one down, or fend off a predatory barracuda or hammerhead, and just chill.It's almost a great game, and that makes where it falls down that much more painful.1. The AI is abysmal. Prey fish ignore your presence until you bite them; hostile fish, no matter how large you are compared to them, attack you relentlessly once you swim within their attack bubble. This means that you have individual barracuda lashing out at your megashark, when you literally rip them apart in a single bite. 2. Nothing recognizes each other. Makos, hammerheads, and swordfish will all combine to attack you on sight, but ignore each other. None of the sharks, gators, or anything else will actually EAT any of the small fish. Other sharks don't react to blood in the water. While human hunters will come out in force, wave after wave of them throwing themselves to their deaths to kill you, they will ignore other sharks completely and focus on you. You can even end up being attacked by other sharks WHILE the hunters are after you!3. The controls are a little fiddly. At times your shark will bite the wrong thing, or suddenly spin about to attack back at you, and it's not quite clear why.4. After 18 hours of play, I think the game has crashed to desktop at least 20 times.5. The combat gets a bit boring after a while. The individual mutations change things up a bit -- giving you bio-electric powers, or the ability to drain blood, or poison your foes, or what-have-you -- but ultimately it's a set of three or four maneuvers that you need, and button-mashing will suffice in many combats. 6. The lesser shark hunter bosses are terribly boring -- you get the sense they were supposed to be a bit more developed, but they hadn't gotten their hands around it by the time they had to go to press.Like I said - it's ALMOST a great game. I certainly enjoyed it -- but I wish it had spent just a bit more time in the studio. More voice acting, better AI, and a bit tighter code, and this would be as close to perfection as could be.

_childDocuments_.review: Maneater geniunely sounds and looks like fun on paper, and it is - for an hour or so. Then you have a good idea of what the game has to offer: mindless ‘fun’, frustrating controls and extremely repetitive gameplay.It’s a shark’s revenge story in which you start of small. Growing up can be done by feeding on wildlife and humans that will earn you experience, therefore making you bigger and stronger. Eventually you will also unlock more skills. It’s all still pretty good for now.The levels themselves are nicely made, with plenty of details, plenty of ways to get around and a good population of humans, wildlife and vegetation. The activities you can do are okay to do, but since you’re a shark there’s not all that much variety. These activities range from finding landmarks and treasure chests to finding license plates and more.All still kind of good here.But then the combat: it is repetitive and frustrating, having you mash buttons to attack other smaller (underleveled or equally leveled) wildlife and humans. And there are overpowered (higher level) species lurking in these open waters that are tough(er) to take down, naturally, and give chase (but they give up rather easily). Same story goes for human hunters, and they’re even harder to take down because the target lock system doesn’t work properly (or for me anyway) and they’re naturally above water (until the boat is destroyed), meaning you have to use the previously mentioned frustrating controls.The combat is so mind numbingly simplistic because of the (initially) rather limited moves of your shark and the button mashing just doesn’t help either. The whole thing just doesn’t gel together as it should. Here’s when the game is at its worst. Unfortunately, it’s also the most important aspect of the game.Your shark can also be leveled up by eating wildlife and humans. Eventually you will unlock some skills that can make things a little easier and less stale, but for me it just wasn’t enough to keep my entertained. It’s a very superficial game and I think it knows but that doesn’t make it any better in this case.Graphically it’s kind of a pretty game. As I mentioned the levels are pretty open, with wildlife and humans swimming around, humans in boats and on land and lots of vegetation that make the levels look natural and semi-real life.The voice acting is over the top, but it fits the (narrative) style the game is aiming for. The screams are fun at first and then they’re not.Would I recommend this? I think you already know the answer: it’s a definitive no. Would I recommend it in a sale? No, unless you can maybe get it for $10 or less. I didn’t have fun with it, maybe you will, but I can think of 10 different games that *are* fun instead.

_childDocuments_.review: It's if they were trying to copy Burnout Paradise in style, but you're a growing/evolving shark monster thing. Exploration is bland in general, there are landmarks to visit that are all parodies or references to other things, but they don't really add too much to the overall game. _childDocuments_.review: I was looking for a fun game to fill some time, and was intrigued by this game. It ended up being really cool. You play as a shark that swims around, essentially doing...whatever you wanna do! The world is, for the most part, entirely open to you, and while there are goals and challenges for you to complete, you could also just swim around, taking in the sights and occasionally terrorizing a few humans. I think the idea was great, and overall was executed really well for a great game.I did find that the controls for jumping out of the water, especially to higher places, were a bit difficult, and I never really felt like I got the hang of them. Nevertheless I did end up being able to complete all of the challenges and story in about 10 hours of gameplay.I also thought the price point was a bit high for this type of game; once you complete all the various quests and such, there isn't a ton to do, and if you're like me and need some sort of goal to direct you in games, you might find yourself getting a bit bored once you finish the main game. I saw that there is some DLC coming, and while I think it will probably be super cool, I'm not sure if I'll spend the extra money for it, as I already paid $30 (on sale) for the main game.Nevertheless I wouldn't want to discourage someone from this game, if it seems like something you would really enjoy, I think it's definitely worth checking out, and it's super obvious that there was a lot of care put into making the game. The story is delightful and overall the game is just chaotically...fun. Not for people bothered by blood or gore (definitely an adult game), or for people afraid of deep water, or of sharks (obviously). Overall, 9/10, I would play again, though I might would wait for more of a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Maneater

_childDocuments_.review: The only other game, that I'm aware of at least, that has attempted this concept before that wasn't multiplayer only was JAWS Unleashed almost 20 years ago, and it was pure garbage. Maneater is pretty much what that game SHOULD have been. You play as a Shark terrorizing a Southern port town. If that on its own appeals to you, you can stop reading here and just buy it. The game is really fun if you can just enjoy it for what it is. It doesn't over-complicate things, which is both good and bad. Youre playing a shark and youre going around eating people and other sea creatures, that base concept never changes, and while thats fine for the most part, There are times where it can get repetitive and some of the progression feels needlessly grindy. The controls can also be a little awkard at times. Its not game breaking and you can play this just fine with a mouse and keyboard, but it was pretty clearly made with a controller in mind. Bottom line, if youre looking for a game where you get play a shark, basically playing the main role in a b shark attack movie story, this will scratch that itch.

name: Risk of Rain 2
detailed_description: SURVIVE AN ALIEN PLANET Over a dozen handcrafted locales await, each packed with challenging monsters and enormous bosses that oppose your continued existence. Fight your way to the final boss and escape or continue your run indefinitely to see just how long you can survive. A unique scaling system means both you and your foes limitlessly increase in power over the course of a game. DISCOVER POWERFUL NEW ITEMS More than 110 items keep each run fresh and full of new challenge. The more items you collect, the more their effects combine, the more surprising some of those combinations might be. The more items you encounter, the more lore (and strategy) you’ll discover through the logs. UNLOCK NEW WAYS TO PLAY Unlock a crew of eleven playable survivors, each with their own unique combat style and alternate skills to master. Learn the secrets of the Artifacts to toggle gameplay modifiers like friendly fire, random survivor spawns, item selection and more. With randomized stages, enemies, and items, no run will ever be the same. PLAY SOLO OR CO-OP Tackle the adventure solo or with up to three friends in online co-op, or compete in the rotating challenge of the Prismatic Trials. Brand new survivors like the Captain and MUL-T join classic survivors such as the Engineer, Huntress, and--of course--the Commando.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really fun and well executed on very many levelsCombat: each character in this game feels totally unique and has a fun and devastating move set, and each boss and enemy in the game is equally as unique and fun to fight against, especially the final bossExploration: each stage is grand and epic to explore with beautiful scenery and graphics all around, even on low settings like mine. Finding every hidden thing is a super fun part of the game and will take dozens or hundreds of hoursDesign: the whole design of the game encourages risk taking for reward. Go fast and have less items, of go slow and have more items, while the enemy's are getting stronger by time. It's a very fun mechanic that puts a ton of pressure on the player while still totally allowing for freedom to play how you wantUnlockables: this game has toooons of unlockables that will take many hours to unlock, but they are all fun and completing the challenges to unlock them is fun as well. Highly recommend for people who lov to unlock abilities and itemsMusic and sound: both the music and sound design in this game is phenomenal. Despite the variety of dozens of monsters, you will always know what monsters are near just by the sounds they make. And the music is outstanding. I have played the game for hundreds of hours without getting bored of the soundtrack. The ambience of each stage music, the intense battle music, and the beautiful guitar solos make this one of my favorite video game soundtracksFun with friends: this game is so much fun with friends. Obviously that's not for everyone, but if you have a group of friends you love to game with, introduce them to this. The games scales very well with groups of players and using your different members abilities to team up and survive is very funVariety: there is soo much variety in the gameplay. Not only do you have different classes, but each class has tons of unlockable abilities and powers to use. Additionally, with hundreds of items, you can make tons of different powerful and unique loadouts to wreak havoc and become an unstoppable killing forceIn summary, this game is just very fun for people who love combat, abilities, unlockables, exploration, goofing off with friends, or even music. Even some interesting lore to boot, if you're into that, however it's not necessary to enjoy the gameplay. Overall it's just a very fun game and very much worth the price. I recommend just about everyone should give it a try! :steamthumbsup:

_childDocuments_.review: I have been a Risk of Rain fan for a decade, the first game was my favorite game of all time for a while, I used to play it on my mom's laptop sitting in our living room. I can remember where I was when I got the notification announcing RoR2, I can remember making a tumblr account just to ask questions on Hopoo's blog, I remember the day it launched in EA and rushing back to my dorm to try it. Suffice to say the series is very close to my heart. When they announced Gearbox would be publishing RoR2 I was concerned but I trusted Hopoo and figured it couldn't be that bad. 5 years later when they announced GB would be taking over the IP I was VERY concerned but tried to stay optimistic. When GB’s very first action as owners of the IP was to announce a free to play mobile gacha game, I realized it was over. GB did not care about the game or the IP, they had no intention of respecting, and wouldn't even do us the favor of leaving it alone. Despite that, some small ignorant part of me wanted to believe the base game would still be there to enjoy. That part was wrong. The new DLC feels underbaked and unpolished with items and characters that clearly had zero playtesting and even less thought put into them. The new boss and characters have reused abilities and animations that look worse than a mod. While the DLC being bad was essentially a given, GB decided to ruin the base game too. They brought the code of the game in line with the console ports that they had made, the ones that had been famously broken for as long as they have existed. There are literally hundreds of game breaking bugs, soft locks, and general jankiness. A lot of it is caused by the fact that many things in the game are now tied to your FPS (you know, that thing every game dev knows you're not supposed to do). This includes things like Loader’s grapple, enemy attacks, and enemy spawn rates. GB says they are working to fix these things, but remember that they created the console ports that have been broken for years. If they couldn't fix the issues then why would I believe they can fix them now. They have demonstrated that they do not care about RoR and are too incompetent to fix anything even if they did. At this point I would be shocked if their bug fix patch does anything other than add more bugs. The future of this franchise is bleak and will only get worse.  Hopoo sold out, they are still saying they believe in GB which is essentially proof they were lying from the start. I love this franchise and this game, but it is dead and GB will continue to beat its corpse.You can still have fun with Risk of Rain. This game can be downpatched, Risk of Rain Returns is still untouched and great, plus many similar games exist. Roboquest is an incredible arcade FPS roguelite, Gatekeeper is a top down heavily RoR inspired game in Early access right now. Go do those things, don’t give GB any money. Goodbye Risk of Rain, its a shame it had to end like this.

_childDocuments_.review: First, I want to say thank you to the Gearbox developers for letting the community know that they have a passion for not only fixing the game, but seeing it thrive. Its very rare for a company to admit their content has balancing issues or straight up flawed design. Hopefully this sentiment sticks around for future patches and updates. If it does, my opinion will certainly become more positive.  The new Seekers of the Storm DLC is in a bad spot. I know most people believe this to be because of the bugs, and yes the bugs are rampant throughout the game and are diminishing the communities enjoyment significantly. But there is a bigger issue with this DLC that the majority seems to either be turning a blind eye too, or is just completely unaware of. I'm talking about the games Item Balance and how the majority of the new Items destroy the games Item Balance and are just simply not well designed. Items are the core and pinnacle element of Risk of Rain 2. In Risk of Rain 2 your power is predominantly measured by your items, a lot of the best items are the most basic ones that give you: Crit, Movement Speed, Bleed, Attack Speed, etc. And the more unique/situational items having more complicated or interesting effects. Generally the basic Stat Items, (White Common Items,) have positive synergies with the higher tier unique/situational items, (Green Uncommon Items,) that creates a positive feedback loop for the player to continue power spiking and progressing through the stages. (Ex: Gas & Ignition, Crit & Predatory Instincts, etc.) It feels like these new items were not designed for what the game needed, but more like the new developers had a wild hair of "...you know what would be cool?" and just ran with it. The items range from completely useless, literally broken, or detrimental, to straight up instantly run winning. The worst part being, because certain item types are so limited within the Item Pool already, such as movement items or healing items, the new items this DLC added that don't benefit the player in any meaningful way still negatively effect you every run by making your chance of getting useful items worse overall. (Because your percentage chance for an item goes down with every new item of that type added to the pool.) I cannot stress enough the rough shape that the Item Pool is in because of these Items. Lets look at some of the worst offenders. Antler Shield - relies on the player taking damage to be useful. Risk of Rain 2, on Eclipse 8, hell even Monsoon, is a game about not getting hit. The difficulty ramps tremendously and attacks begin to deal massive damage to the player. From a design standpoint, Movement Speed is better defense then... well actual defense. Why bet on tanking a hit when you could just be fast enough to never be hit in the first place? Not to mention the damage it deals back is percentage based and monster health scaling is multitudes larger than the players, so this item becomes exponentially less useful as time goes on. This item needs to be completely redesigned. Knockback Fin - not only is practically useless on ranged characters, but its actually a detriment to melee and short-range characters. Pushing an enemy away from you as Mercenary or Acrid or Chef only makes it harder for you to kill them quickly and move on to the next objective. If they are a ranged enemy, its even worse because it gives them a better chance of landing an attack on you. Even if a single character could use this item, its too niche and should never dilute the common pool of items. Warped Echo - is interesting on paper because it synergizes with medkit. Finally an item that has synergy! But... it makes your Rejuvenating Slug and Personal Shield Generator take longer to activate their effects, and this might be a bug, but it also allows certain damage types to pass through your One Shot Protection such as debuff damage. So it has one synergy and adds three detrimental effects. No Item in the game should make other items worse. Simple as that. If the interaction isn't positive or neutral at best it shouldn't be in the game. It doesn't service the player or the feedback loop of Risk of Rain 2. Noxious Thorn - looks terrible. Its a giant green blob that has a description which the Pentagon couldn't decipher. It just feels so... unfun to play with. Why is it also based on getting hit? Why not make the Item with 'Noxious' in its name deal Poison Damage instead of Bleed? We already have multiple sources of Bleed and only Acrid can use Poison. It would synergize well with DoT builds, Acrid, and Death Mark. Unstable Transmitter - might be the worst offender. Its explosion is pointless at high time or stage counts. and its effect is buggy and weird. It takes 3 to 4 seconds to activate and doesn't flow very well with the speed and feel of the game. Basic Movement Speed Item are already more effective at getting away from things like I said above about Antler Shield. Why is this DLC trying to push "Defensive" Items so hard? Defense in Risk of Rain 2 is: Don't get hit. Kill stuff before it kills you. Sure there are times where nobody is perfect and takes a hit, but that is why Healing Items and One Shot Protection exist. Plus, what Unstable Transmitter does... already exist in an item combo! Old War Stealth Kit paired with Power Elixir will proc simultaneously to let you get away at low health, without breaking your game. This bootleg combo has a surprisingly similar effect to this new DLC Item without being buggy, awkward, and taking up a Green Item Pool Slot.Sonorous Whispers - This item is broken by concept. No amount of balancing could fix this item. Risk of Rain Returns has a similar item called the '56 Leaf Clover' which grants Elites a 4% Chance to drop an Item on death. Of course its all RNG, but this averages out to about 3-5 Items in a standard run depending on when you obtain the item. The reason it works in Risk of Rain Returns and not Risk of Rain 2 is that there are no Hidden Realms that stop time completely in Returns. In Risk of Rain 2, if you ever pick up this Item, you can find the Lunar Altar on a stage and repeat until you obtain Gilded Coast, where time is stopped and you can farm large monsters, bosses, and elites indefinitely. If you get this Item, even on Eclipse 8, you instantly win the game. This should never happen. No Item should ever instantly win you a run. The simplest solution to this would be to disable the Item in Hidden Realms, but I still think it would be to powerful. This item needs to be reworked entirely. The biggest thing that I can say is that items in Risk of Rain 2 are deceptively simple. Its very easy from an outside lens to think of so many items that could be good for the game, but when they are actually implemented do not fit in to the ecosystem in a useful, fun, or meaningful way. Items need to feel good, be at least somewhat useful, and play/interact well with one another and the survivors, without getting in the way of other items or diluting the pool, the enjoyment, or the balance. Item Balance is probably the most difficult aspect of the game. Items do not need to be overly complex. The complexity creates itself through the items synergies with one another and how each individual survivor interacts with these items. This game is Item Soup, but the Soup has been carefully crafted and maintained. You can throw a lot of basic ingredients into a soup to make it taste slightly better, like potatoes or carrots. But if you start throwing in random, complex ingredients that you like, like gummy bears or beef jerky, the Soup can quickly begin to sour and lose what made it so special in the first place. Even if you fix every bug in the entire game, if the items and item balance are not well designed, then the game won't ever feel 100% right

_childDocuments_.review: I would like to start off this review by saying that Risk of Rain has been a franchise that I’ve held near and dear to my heart for years now, I still remember finding the game initially through Chris Christodoulou‘s music (specifically the rain formally known as purple <3) in the original risk of rain. And I want nothing but the continued success of the game no matter who is currently developing it. However the recent release of seekers of the storm is nothing short of a disaster that should have been delayed, and the fact that it was released in this state is unacceptable. I have never seen a game that was so fundamentally sound and stable so brutally dismantled by an update that had received nothing but unparalleled hype and praise before it’s release. The whole laundry list of game breaking bugs and poor design choices that were introduced in this expansion is mind boggling, I genuinely believe that this update was not playtested OR that it was playtested and known that it was horrendously buggy but shipped anyways because of higher ups at gearbox. Randy Pitchford went on record saying “This is some jank we’ve just sort of tolerated.” when discussing the new dlc and that is by far the most baffling statement I’ve ever seen said about a disastrous content release. How can you in good faith say that there is just some “jank” in the game when the game is currently unplayable on console, or that the flag ship feature of couch coop can permanently corrupt your save data if a second controller is plugged in. The current major issue of your FPS being tied to almost every form of physics in the game is game breaking on pc, I genuinely do not know how this got past QA unless they only tested it on a 60 fps locked ps4 and nothing else. The new content that was added is the only saving grace this update has, as the new stages, survivors, and items are all awesome and welcome additions to the game IF THEY WORKED! Warped echo making the MAIN BOSS UNKILLABLE is a laughably pathetic bug, seekers meditation is terribly inconsistent and buggy, chef does not feel good to play on higher refresh rates and ends up being a clunky mess because of it, and the new secret survivor (no spoilers :3) feels very unfinished, playing more like a low effort modded character than an official survivor. In its current state, I do not think anyone should purchase the game or it’s DLC expansions, it really pains me to say this because this is one of my favorite franchises and games of all time. But gearbox has horribly managed this update and put the game into the worst state I have ever seen it in. I genuinely believe that if swift action isn’t taken to address the laundry list of game breaking bugs that this game will not see the successful future that it deserves. I hope for the best, but with gearbox and it’s misguided management at the lead I do expect the worst.
