_childDocuments_.review: If this was merely last week, I would've said this game was absolutely worth every penny and hour I spent on it.But I cannot in good faith recommend this game in the current state is in now thanks to the newest DLC and patch Gearbox released.I cannot fathom how you could take a game that, while a little rough around the edges, was a very streamlined and absolutely blast of an experience and turn turn it into an buggy mess that feels AWFUL to even play. The amount of issues I got in merely the first few hours of the DLC is so egregious it makes me wonder how it was even playtested in this state - let alone shipped.By trying to make console and PC versions """consistent""" with each other, Gearbox just broke both versions. Misery loves company, I guess. Every tiny little thing that you wouldn't expect to annoy you now does. The health bar looks awful, pressing tab to look at your inventory now stops your character from sprinting, terminal shops have broken shading that looks poop brown (fitting), and EVERYTHING is now tied to framerate! You know, the ONE THING that's prone to drop when your run gets a little too silly? As much fun as looping can be, it's now just no longer an option (funny considering the new boss practically necessitates looping if you don't wanna die instantly). And you better have it capped to 60 fps like the consoles or else everything BREAKS. Fantastic. I love it when a product that used to work that I put 300+ hours into suddenly doesn't.This game was prided on EVERY character feeling clean and smooth to control in some capacity, but with the new patch so many skills just feel horrible to even use. Collision is wonky, hitboxes disagree with the animation, it feels AWFUL. I should not be fighting against the game physics themselves.And then the DLC itself is just aggressively average. Stages are alright, but only 4 new enemies is disappointing. Music is INCREDIBLE, but that's Chris not Gearbox (shoutouts to Chris). The new boss just flat out ending your run also sucks especially when it can end as early as Stage 4. And then some of the item choices convinced me that nobody who created these items actually played the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ game because how the hell do you make me wanna consider Low Quality Speakers from Starstorm 2 over some of the stinkers they added to item pool???Honestly speaking of mods, the microsecond the wonderful and talented modding community fixes all of the mistakes Gearbox created I will be playing that instead. I thought going back to vanilla risk would be rough with the long scrapping times, but I didn't expect everything to just be broken? But knowing Gearbox, they'll probably just wait for modders to fix everything then yoink the code and claim they fixed it themselves.Fix the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ game and I'll recommend it again. For now, I award you no points and may Providence have mercy on your soul.

_childDocuments_.review: I never do this in roguelites, which I have played a ton of over the years, but I just quit to desktop out of a strong run. How do I know it was strong? I wasn't taking noticeable damage in boss fights and enemies died when I clicked them. I don't really know why this was happening, but it was. Why did I quit to desktop? I loaded into what might've been the 5th or 6th area, after about a 30 minute play session, saw some familiar, boring enemies spawn, and said to myself, "I'm tired of this."I dont get the goal of this game. Is it 'be a badass spaceman'? Is it 'carefully concoct an efficient build'? What's the end-game? Are there 7 levels? 12? The answer to my questions about Risk of Rain was constantly, 'I don't know'. Why does my spaceman have no map? Where's the teleporter? Is now a good time to do the teleporter? What do the items do? What does leveling up do? Why do I have to move so far, so slowly, when there's so much empty space? How do I spend this 1,200 dollars? Where is the FUGGING TELEPORTER? Why don't I keep money between levels? Why do my support units never lose HP? I don't know. I don't care. There'll be no joy in finding out.An absence of information makes this game feel empty and cynical. It is torn between 'frantic shooter' and 'Walk through empty space until you see the next loot/macguffin/money.' Chests good, going slow bad. There are all these beautiful environmental installations and life-forms which end up feeling like so many miles of pavement. When I loaded into a new area with a bunch of chests nearby, my reaction was to stand still until enemies auto-spawned, so I could get money to spend on the chests, which give... random buffs. Fish after fish in a barrel. Something was lost when I realized I could hold down primary-fire. Something was lost when I stopped checking my cooldowns and instead just periodically hit every ability key as I dodged around. You just keep shooting guys, that's it.This is one of those roguelites where I kept restarting in hopes of reaching the fun part but it was always just out of reach. Didn't hold my interest.

_childDocuments_.review: Risk of Rain is a Rogue-Like shooter similar to newer titles like Returnal. You and up to 3 other players must run through a gauntlet of increasing difficulty to the end in one go without a party wipe. You can customize the difficulty to an extent to be as punishing as you really want it but this is by no means an easy title regardless. To supplement the ever increasing difficulty is the various items you can collect throughout the levels to increase your odds of survival. This game is hard and it can get repetitive since it does not change much throughout playthroughs. Personally I did not like the title due to how grindingly repetitive it got after a few difficulty (to me frustrating) rounds. However, I can respect the vision of the developers as well as its affordability. Just because this title was not for me does not mean its not for you. If you like games where you have to "get good" and are a fan of the rogue-like genre you will enjoy this game, especially if you have a team to play it with.

_childDocuments_.review: There is a cancer at the heart of Risk of Rain 2: it fundamentally does not respect your time.I think this is a symptom of it being developed in Early Access for a long time. There used to be only a couple levels, and looping through them to get more and more powerful was basically the entire game. But now that we have a final boss and enough levels to get to him without repeats, the game still expects you to play in the same infinite way: you get stronger, the enemies get stronger, until you're committing genocide with every mouse click, but also can potentially be two-shot by dozens of enemies at any given moment. This might sound thrilling, but the visual noise and sheer chaos means that focusing any specific enemy is often impossible, and you just find yourself going through rote motions. Depending on your character, that might be simple (Huntress), complex (Loader/Mercenary), or somewhere in between, but it's never actually challenging -- you just either have the damage and survival to make it through, or you don't. I've never been as bored in a game while simultaneously being moments from death.It's a real shame, because there is a fun action game in here, but once you've played for some hours it becomes equivalent to sitting at a slot machine. You're just gambling for the right set of items which makes you absolutely unstoppable, but simultaneously makes the game play itself. Death comes quick and almost never feels like it happens because you made a legitimate mistake. 95% of the time I can only identify what killed me because the game identifies your killer, but it could have been any of the hundreds of projectiles, damage fields, lingering DOT effects, etc. that were on the screen at the time. There is now a final boss, but he feels bad to fight, tests skills that you're rarely asked to demonstrate in the entire rest of the game, and the biggest sin, he takes away your items for a while. This could be cool if it was a normal boss fight, but because this is a permadeath roguelike, it's infuriating. To get to the final boss you're looking at a minimum of a half-hour run, but most players will want to loop through the level set at least once. I've seen people play single runs in this game for upwards of three hours. That's insane to me. I guess if you're the type of person who just loves to watch numbers go up, that could be awesome for you. It's like Cookie Clicker with much more involved gameplay... but yeah as a big fan of Roguelikes, this just isn't doing it for me. You can see how much I've played, yet so little of that time has been really *fun*. Similar to something like World of Warcraft, it's compulsive. And the lack of a save-game feature between levels, which almost every other game in the genre has had for years now, just multiplies all these complaints.

_childDocuments_.review: My disappointment is immeasurable, and my day is ruined. For those of you who don't know, Gearbox, a couple of months back, bought out Risk of Rain 2. And for those who understood and knew what was going on, there was some protest about it. But it seems Gearbox is like the opposite of King Midas, where everything they touch turns to, well... nnhngn,... a mess. Gearbox, everything they touch is just garbage, and it's terrible. And as soon as they bought Risk of Rain 2, I had this sinking feeling—Gearbox would ruin this game, wouldn't they? And that's exactly what they did. Just like everything else they touch, really. nhnhngn.... they ruined it. Um........ terribly disappointing, what um- I'm experiencing here. Risk of Rain 2 was one of my favorite games, I kid you not. It was something special on its own. The gameplay used to be - I mean, it was so smooth, so polished. But after this new DLC, it’s something else entirely. I mean, the game is almost unplayable. The FPS now dictates the gameplay speed, the final boss is invincible, and on Xbox, you can't even get past the main menu... oh~ so frustrating~..... I tried everything, but no patches are going to fix this atrocity. None. This comes down to the quality of the game itself. A perfect game should just run smoothly. This is broken. And that's disgraceful, really is. And it brings a game that was excellent to something that is now below average. And it's not completely unplayable, mind you. It's technically functional, granted. Uh, but when you're used to expecting... Sips water ...excellent quality gameplay, some of the best from an indie game, and then you load it up, and it's all just buggy... and rather lackluster in terms of performance, it's such a terrible, terrible disappointment, ladies and gentlemen. And this was such a good game. I would've recommended it to anyone, and now it's essentially a piece of garbage. So -um-uh- so I hope you can imagine my disappointment when I know likely it's never going to go back to what it was.

_childDocuments_.review: Risk of Rain 2 is probably one of my favorite games of all time. Like hot damn, if I would have known that I would have loved this game so much I would have bought it years earlier, but I eventually got it in a Humble Bundle, so I guess fate was on my side.Risk of Rain 2 is a roguelike like no other. First of all, most of the roguelikes that I have encountered are 2D and when I saw that Risk of Rain moved from 2D to 3D I was skeptical if I was going to like it as much as the first one, but I am truly impressed how well it translated. The gameplay loop is so satisfying, the way that you acquire loot, the ways that you can end the game, the variety of characters, items, and builds you can have, the smooth controls… All of it is near perfection in my opinion. There is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ reason I have spent over a hundred hours in this game and took the time to 100% this game despite the difficulty of doing so. Oh speaking of 100%ing the game, every achievement is based around unlocks, so the progression length is massive and there is so much to try and play with. I found every class to be so fun (except mercenary, which was just meh to me), most of the items have a purpose and when playing with the ability to choose items building is honestly a treat that involves picking up at least half the roster of common and uncommon weapons because it simply just helps you build better so just about everything is useful in some way. Combat is fast, bosses and enemies are unique, and the environments feel fun to explore and can also play into your combat positioning and speed running significantly. The difficulty of the game feels appropriate, the modes are pretty good, and the modifiers you can add are fun to play with as well. I know all this praise sounds a bit disconnected, but I just don’t know how to describe how much I love this game.The game does have a story, but it is largely irrelevant, it is good though. I watched a couple of YouTube videos on it and found it just fascinating. But if you came looking for the story expect to read a lot of logs, or just go and watch a video. I think it is worth it, but I could understand if people thought it was too cryptic.Graphically this game looks quite unique and overall I find myself liking it quite a lot. It has high contrast, various colors, vibrant glows, and simpler models and it all plays so well together. It is also worth noting that for every item your character acquires a new item appears on you, which they didn’t have to do, but it really is a nice touch. In the very late stages with hundreds of enemies the game can run a bit hard, but beyond that, I think the graphics are spot on.The music and sound design are phenomenal. I love many of the tracks to the game (especially one of the new DLC ones) and would casually listen to the music on occasion. All other sounds feel appropriate, have weight, and give adequate feedback. Honestly, they have gone above and beyond in the sound department.I love this game. And I think you should try out this game. It is just an absolute blast and though the DLC started out rough because they ♥♥♥♥♥♥ the balance for a while, I think it has improved the game substantially. See but the thing is I think that is my only criticism, “it had a bad couple of patches” is all I can say as a negative, I think it is pretty telling. To conclude, normally when I 100% a game I kind of step away from it, but I don’t think I will be doing that with Risk of Rain 2, it is just too good, I can play this game for hours straight and have a great time. And that is what really matters after all.

_childDocuments_.review: Long story short, with all the current customization options that the game provides with the current update (and even before then), this game is a blast to play both solo and with friends. Chaos incarnate best describes the gameplay the longer you stay alive, so mastering a character is key to stand a chance in the higher difficulty Monsoon, which that process alone will give you more than enough reason to keep getting better and better at the game. Multiplayer with randos can be a bit annoying, seeing how the servers are client based, so if the host leaves, everyone gets booted out of the game, and also the fact that not every person plays the game the same way, so inevitably you'll come across someone who either rushes or takes an eternity to collect every, single freakin item in the area and spend almost 30 min trying to farm, but with friends, at least you can coordinate with which style of play you prefer.  And even tho the items are randomly generated from each chest in a basic form of a rouge-like, if you last long enough, you'll eventually get the very item you need to secure a "god run" in this game. Overall, this game is solid in every way. Multiplayer's a bit wonky, so best have friends to play with. But ye, an amazing game for sure!!

_childDocuments_.review: Rainbow Cake Layers:3 cups all-purpose flour (390 grams)3 cups granulated sugar (600 grams)2 1/2 tsp baking powder (10 grams)1 tsp salt (6 grams)1 cup unsalted butter, room temperature (226 grams) - 2 sticks2 tsp. vanilla extract (8 grams)1 cup pasteurized egg whites from a carton (or about 7 egg whites) (235 grams)1 1/2 cups buttermilk, room temperature (345 grams)1/8 cup vegetable oil (28 grams)Red, yellow, blue, and pink gel food coloringVanilla Buttercream Frosting:3 cups unsalted butter, room temperature (678 grams)11 cups powdered sugar (1375 grams)1 tsp salt (6 grams)1/3 cup heavy cream (or whipping cream) (75 grams)1 1/2 Tbsp vanilla extract (18 grams)Red, orange, yellow, green, blue, purple, and pink gel food coloringInstructions:Rainbow Cake Layers:Preheat oven to 350°F. Line four 7 inch pans pans with parchment rounds, and grease with a light spray of non-stick cooking spray.Mix together all dry ingredients (flour, baking powder, sugar, and salt) in a stand mixer with a paddle with a few gentle pulses.Mix chunks of room-temperature butter slowly into the dry mix, on a low speed. Continue to mix until no large chunks of butter remain, and the mixture becomes crumbly.Pour in egg whites, and mix on low until just incorporated. Mix in the buttermilk in two installments, on a low speed.Add in vanilla and oil, and mix at a low speed until fully incorporated. Scrape down the sides of the bowl with a spatula, then beat on low speed for about 15 seconds. Divide the batter evenly between four bowls (about 450 grams of batter per bowl). Create red, yellow, blue and pink batter using a couple drops of gel food coloring. Mix by hand with a spatula until the batter is evenly colored.Pour each color into one of the prepared cake pans.Bake for 34-37 minutes, or until a toothpick comes out clean. Allow the pans to cool for 10 minutes, then run an offset spatula around perimeter of the pan to separate the cake from the pan.Place cake layers into the freezer for 45 minutes, to accelerate the cooling process. Once the layers are fully cooled, carefully flip the pans and remove the layers from the pans.Use a serrated knife to level the tops of the layers, and then frost as desired.Vanilla Buttercream Frosting:While the cake layers bake and cool, make the vanilla buttercream frosting.Beat the butter on a medium speed for 30 seconds with a paddle attachment, until smooth. Slowly add in the powdered sugar, 1 cup at a time. Alternate with small splashes of cream.Once fully mixed, add in the vanilla and salt, and beat on low until the ingredients are fully incorporated, and the desired consistency is reached. If the frosting is too thick, add in additional cream (1 teaspoon at a time). If the frosting is too thin, add in more powdered sugar (quarter of a cup at a time).To create the colorful the buttercream used to fill the cake, place 1 cup of frosting into three separate bowls. Color them orange, green, and purple with a couple drops of gel food coloring.Leave the rest of the buttercream white until the cake has been assembled.To Assemble The Rainbow Cake:Stack and frost cake layers on a greaseproof cake board, using a dab of frosting to help stick the first cake layer to the board.Start with the red cake layer on the bottom. Top with a thick layer of orange buttercream. Leave about 1/4 of a cup of frosting in the bowl, to decorate the sides of the cake with later.Top with the yellow cake layer, then frost with the green buttercream, reserving a tiny bit of green buttercream.Next add the blue cake layer and top with some purple buttercream (leaving a bit for the decoration later).Top the cake with the pink cake layer, placing it upside down to make it easier to frost (with the caramelization from the bottom of the pan facing upward).Apply a thin coat of frosting around the the cake, to fully cover the cake layers. Smooth using a bench scraper, then chill the cake in the fridge (10 minutes) or freezer (5 minutes) until the frosting is firm to the touch.Add a second, thicker layer of frosting to the cake, and smooth using a bench scraper. Place the cake in the freezer to chill for 10-15 minutes, or in the fridge for 30 minutes.Place about 1 1/2 cups of white buttercream into a piping bag fit with an Ateco 869 frosting tip (a very large french tip)In four other small bowls, color about 1/2 cup of frosting to make red, yellow, blue, and pink buttercream.Using a small offset spatula, spread dabs of each color of frosting around the chilled cake. Feel free to overlap and have with the step!Top the cake with a boarder of white buttercream frosting, and then cut in and enjoy W recipe, W game

_childDocuments_.review: I can safely say with a doubt that Risk of Rain 2 is a fantastic game to play. The unique cast of survivors, the different skills you can unlock for said survivors, and all of the items in the game have different impacts in which you can play every run in this game.One thing I can say about the survivors is that they are all fun to play. I can't really say I got bored of playing one specific survivor in the game. There's just so many ways to play certain survivors that every time I've played, I've had a new experience for a certain character because of the blessed RNG I have in this game. Some of the survivors from Risk of Rain 1 return to this one with some new additions like MUL-T, REX, the Captain, and Artificer. The new survivors in this game are really fun to play, especially REX and MUL-T in my opinion, you can easily get overpowered runs with these 2. For the returning survivors of the game, they are still a blast as well. Of course I have only 7 hours in the first game compared to my 400+ hours on the second but I still liked the reaction from my friends on the returning characters back when this game's early access released in March.Very, VERY, solid gameplay. I can't say it enough, I love the game's gameplay so much. I really like rouge-like games and Risk of Rain 2 has not disappointed me in the slightest. From it's enemies, to the maps, to the items that you get, all of it is entertaining to play. One slight problem I have is just the lack of alternate 2nd, 3rd and 4th stage layouts (like the 1st stages have) but this game is getting future updates so I still have high hopes for it. _childDocuments_.review: Solid 9/10. For me to give a game a 9/10, it has to be extremely fun and fresh (originality is a myth, freshness isn't) with no glaring flaws in the gameplay experience. Risk of Rain 2 is a roguelike (fight me) action game where you go to a strange new world and kill its god. The core gameplay loop is exploring a level, killing enemies to get money (and xp but eh) and using that money to open chests and the like to buy a variety of items to help you on your journey, then activating the teleporter and fighting a boss before moving onto the next level until you eventually get to god, at which point he kicks your ass because he's god, but after a couple more tries you eventually manage to kill him and escape the planet. It's got a wide variety of characters who all play in very different and interesting ways even before getting into the items you collect, which vary from increasing stats to making it so that you're immune to damage on Tuesdays, adn sure it's Wednesday, but the damage doesn't know that! and everything in this game stacks, allowing for some truly crazy ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Difficulty increases as time passes, pressing you to find a balance between being fast and being thorough. The variety of characters, the variety of items and enemies, and the depth of the aforementioned balancing act adds an immense amount of depth and replayability even before getting into the artifacts and the loops and the alt gamemodes and the skill unlocks and the like. I'm nearly 400 hours deep, and the game's still getting more and more fun. Also i ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ love the lore, but i'm not gonna factor that into the review

_childDocuments_.review: If I could give RoR a "mixed" review, I think I would. The first 20 hours was pretty enjoyable indeed, and if the game stayed at that level of enjoyment I'd recommend it heartily. 20 hours, 20 dollars - passes my test, therefor up-vote.As you play the game more, however, some pretty noticeable design flaws come through that really spoil the experience a bit as you go through run after run. First of all, once you're skilled enough to get past the first few stages of the game consistently, 100% of runs will be ended by 1 shots. That means all items that don't increase your chances of avoiding 1-shot attacks are effectively bad choices every time because, well, they don't make you miss getting 1-shot., which is how you're going to die. I'd love to have a reason to choose anything over the teddy bear or feather or bronze pendant thing, but if I don't I'm guarenteed to lose the run much earlier than if I just chose the defensive items outright. It's to the point that if I find a printer for a small pool of three or four items, I will dump literally every other I item I have of that tier into the OP defensive item and often go hours further into my runs because of that decision. Not so fun.The fix here would really be to give a hard cap on individual attacks not being able to deal more than half your max health in damage - that change alone would legitimize so many of the other cool and interesting items in the game that just aren't useful because of the over-focus on needing defensive and "avoid-focused" items.Possibly because of this issue and because of the lack of real variety in classes that are fast enough to survive, the game becomes very stale very fast. There's just not much variety here, to the extent that after 40 hours I don't really even have much incentive to pick the game back up even after updates have happened. I played over 100 hours of the original - this one just isn't grabbing me in the same way, and I think it's because there aren't many interesting classes or ways of approaching combat.Finally, on a technical end - the multiplayer is a little rough around the edges in the netcode and unfortunately my group of friends and I are no longer able to play together during LAN parties as the server keeps dying a few worlds into the round. I do streaming multiple times a week and generally have decent internet all around - but for some reason this game in particular gives us some issues.Overall, RoR 2 hits my mark of "a dollar an hour of legitimate fun" and so I'd still recommend picking it up for good value and a good time. Hopefully the team addresses some of the design issues so I can turn this review from being positive to glowing.

_childDocuments_.review: Note: This review was made before the 1.0 version of the game.No other game has gotten me to play this many hours in this short of a time frame. Gameplay:Risk of Rain 2 has all the parts about rogue-like games you actually like, and actually manages to avoid many of the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ traits rogue-likes have that nobody likes. Obviously, since you'll have different items and, by extension, different strengths and weaknesses every run, the game has a lot of replay value. There are also new items, modifiers, skills, and characters you can unlock to change future runs, for better or for worse. You'll always be kept on your toes, as you never know what to expect because each run is completely different from the last in regards to the stages, boss fights, etc. But this is all stuff you've maybe probably definitely heard about any other rogue-like game that's ever gotten any praise from anyone. What makes this one any different from the rest of this super over-saturated genre? ...Well for starters the game doesn't ♥♥♥♥ you in the ass at every twist and turn.Sure, being a rogue-like, RNG is absolutely a factor that largely influences the outcome of each run, but the fun part about this particular game is that if you're good, you don't need Godlike RNG to win. Each survivor (edit: most survivors) has all the resources they need, in order to actually complete stage 8 (the earliest point at which you can complete a run) right from the start. Hell, the game even encourages you to rush through stages quickly without picking up all the items, because rather than getting more difficult each level, the difficulty in Risk of Rain 2 scales as time passes. If you dwell on one stage for too long, it will usually hurt you more than it will help you. Each boss also drops a green or yellow (higher rarity/power) item upon death, further encouraging you to progress through each stage quicker for the promise of a strong item. There's even an achievement for completing a run in less than 25 minutes. You don't need an amazing combo of items to carry you through each run. This game encourages this quick progress because it is designed in such a way that the player's skill will almost always matter as much or more than their luck, and that's what sets it apart from most other rogue-likes. Sound:The sound in this game is both the best and worst thing about it. For starters, the music is fantastic. Chris Christodoulou really went all out when making these songs, following suit with his amazing work on the first game's OST. The main stages all have a similar vibe to each other while still being different enough to have their own musical identities, while the secret areas tend to seem more ominous or mysterious. The "void fields" theme in particular gives me chills when I hear it. But... despite these tracks being arguably the best part of the game, you'll probably have to turn them down a bit when playing on the hardest difficulty or when going for a very long run. Due to the nature of how enemies spawn and attack, you'll need to listen for audio queues to avoid a strong one sneaking up behind you and obliterating you and your will to live. Now, save for a couple exceptions, these audio queues are all very unique and usually not hard to pick out from all the other noise that comes from combat (except maybe during boss fights because the bosses are very loud). The ability to recognise the moment an enemy spawns isn't the problem though, it's more so the fact that you have to do it at all. This means you'll have to turn the fantastic soundtrack down or off to perform optimally. Perhaps the addition of a minimap that display nearby enemy locations could help with this problem? Maybe it'll happen in a future update. Nevertheless, this problem is pretty minor overall, and it certainly doesn't make the game less fun. Visuals: The art style is overall pretty aesthetically pleasing. Sure, it looks a bit basic, and it isn't the most unique-looking game out there, but this style is perfect for what this game is. It allows the player to instantly pick out a particular enemy they're looking for from everything else on screen, which is essential once actual threatening enemies start spawning. So even if the visuals aren't your cup of tea, you'll probably appreciate the simplicity once you actually need to shoot things. Story:This is probably the game's weakest element, as the developers have taken a "let the player figure it out for themselves" approach, but to be honest, you're probably not playing this game for the story anyway. Verdict:Buy this game. Now. Even if you don't like rogue-like games, I think you'll find this one might be an exception.Edit: Nominating this for the labour of love award in the 2021 steam awards.

_childDocuments_.review: Risk of Rain 2 isn't exactly a rogue-like in the same way something like Binding of Isaac or Enter the Gungeon is. In isaac , each run is unique - the combination of items you get on one seed is never going to be the same on a different run. You don't have a lot of control over choosing your own "build" at the start of the run - instead you more or less so base your playstyle off of whatever the first good item you are going to get is.This is where RoR2 differs from the other roguelikes - when going into a run , you pretty much know what you want to (and will probably) get. Each of the 11 (+2 dlc) characters has around 2-3 efficient builds that they can achieve by getting certain items. Most items are small stat boosts or little "perks" that can be stacked. By the end of the run , you can expect to have gathered around 50 items. Their (by comparison) small pool lets you optimize every run since you can expect to get at least some of the things you need. The existance of item scrappers and 3d-printers gives you unprecedented control over your run - dont like the useless med kit you got from a chest? Turn it into scrap and exhange it for something that gives you missiles or makes dead enemies explode instead. Thats what Risk of Rain 2 is about. You arent guaranteed to get the stuff you need and some runs may force you to completely abandon the build you had in mind. Your job is to make the most out of what you get and optimize. The timer that keeps making enemies stronger exemplifies this - you have to get as efficient at getting stronger and outscaling the difficulty as you can.You wont spend as much time here as you could in most other rogue-likes. However the time that you *will* spend is going to be a very fun and unique. Risk of rain is popular for a reason - the unique art style , ost and gameplay make it stand out out of the wider genre.

It was something that was hyped up since its announcement, and the BOGO deal for the first 2 days of launch pretty much sealed the deal. As far as marketing strategies goes this I feel was a tactical masterstroke. Just look at how many reviews this game has gotten, and a significant proportion of them are Steam-purchased reviews, which is an absolute necessity nowadays.Enough comment on that, though - Risk of Rain 2 neatly transitions the game into a full-blown 3D roguelike looter shooter, and it's totally a blast. You'll meet enemies old and new, and they all have a bunch of new abilities. Maps might be the same (the choice of artstyle is great, the colours are vibrant and is generally easy on the eye), but loot and teleporter location isn't, and there's enough variety with levels switching between a few different ones. Occasionally finding the teleporter is a bit of a chore, though.Risk of Rain 2 also sports a vastly improved multiplayer system. Setting up sessions in the old game was a chore due to port forwarding, but that's a thing of the past. A quick play mode even matches you up against random other people. The fun and excitement (as well as the teeth gnashing when a greedy teammate steals all the items) is all there.The current character classes that are playable are all neat in their own right. Old favourites like the Huntress and Engineer have their own new twists to help with the transition to 3D. The Mercenary's transition to 3D is an especially interesting one, and has shades of 's Genji, in my opinion.Of course,  holds it all together with his usual masterful command of polyrhythms and weird time signatures, all while retaining the famous motifs from the first game's soundtrack. All of these factors have combined to immediately skyrocket the game into one of my favourites to play.Chances are if you're reading this now, you missed the day 1 BOGO deal, sorry! But I can unabashedly say it's still worth the price even now. For the penny pinchers, get in quick before it gets raised; still a fair and justified increase, in my honest opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: Early access done right. Fairly well polished game that has aced the transition from 2D to 3D and incredibly retains all of it's predecessors legendary level of fun. Here is the reasons you should get it and like it:Great fast paced game-play with plenty of unlockables and unique characters and abilities. Tons of items to combine stack and exploit to become godlike, creating an immense level of replayability.Big open levels that have algorithmic item spawns and are partially randomized portions that reward you for exploring (lots of hidden collectibles and secrets).Plenty of enemy diversity and intense boss fights that continue to escalate and change.Very challenging with a well balanced and unique difficulty progression mechanic.Visually pleasing as a simplistic style without looking cartoonish.Sound design is phenomenal, from distinct audio queues for each enemy, item effect, and ability to an incredible game soundtrack that never gets old and seamlessly adapts to the intensity of the combat.The icing on the cake is that there is non-buggy multiplayer that fits perfectly and scales to create a unique role-based dynamic that encourages players to work together.Devs are highly transparent and have a clear progression of content planned for the future of the game that removes the gamble of "will there be more good content?" from the early access purchase. Don't sleep on this game.

_childDocuments_.review: edit for 2020 awards; very cool game.i'll start by saying i have not played the original risk of rain, i've only seen some footage and heard pretty great things from my close friends. i played its sequel very much blind and unaware as to what i was getting into.i have absolutely fallen in love with this game even during my first playthrough with one of my friends, it was just so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ good - and it still is. i've very much enjoyed grinding with three other players on monsoon, getting our asses handed to us as the match goes past the 45 minute mark, or when we accidentally take too long looting and suddenly we're at HAHA... difficulty.the visuals? ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ this is a pretty game. it's colourful atmospheres remind me of the witness or splatoon. very pretty, good for screenshots and wallpapers.the game is pretty comfy when playing alone, especially on drizzle. just getting super overpowered and taking your time with each stage is a blessing, a great way to kill time considering every playthrough, either alone or with a full party, is always different despite always ending the same way - death.it's a pleasant surprise finding easter eggs in this game, especially since the most i have found were by accidentally falling off of the world or by hopping through a portal expecting to be taken to the lunar coin shop but instead arriving in - with bosses, the imp overlord and magma worm (either single or multiple, depending on the difficulty and player count) can be so grindy and these battles can be so drawn out and lengthy to the point of it just getting very boring and pretty demotivating.- fire damage should not be able to kill players directly, just like fall damage.- the huntress' inability to sprint sideways is a tad bit frustrating and i'm hoping in the future that she can sprint in any direction she would like. alternatively, make her sprint permanent/constant, replacing her CTRL ability with something along the lines of changing her currently selected target.- also the huntress will have a gap between the hoof and leg when using paul's goat hoof, devs pls fix. - the engineer's mines seem to be hit or miss, more so on the miss with some not even triggering when near enemies.- an item drop button would be great too, especially after killing a boss with friends and you just so happen to be in the exact place a reward spawns.- shift abilities shouldn't cancel your sprint.- the downtime between starting a new map and enemies spawning can be so long, having this be quicker would be great. as soon as i start a new area i want there to be monsters trying to kill me from the get-go. - sometimes it takes a decade to find the teleporter, could be a bit helpful if it was included in the radar scanner even if it still shows as a question mark.overall,9/10. absolutely loving the hell out of this brilliant game and its mechanics, hoping to see more characters as the game gets closer to its final release.ps. bandit's gameplay looks great, can't wait to see if he ever gets released.

_childDocuments_.review: Endless enjoyment. This incredibly fun game combines the rogue-like genre and the third-person genre so well that it makes a unique experience that you'll never want to put down. This is a game that makes you feel POWERFUL. Kill enemies, gain money, open chests, get items. Items benefit you in various ways, and they can all stack infinitely, making for some of the craziest attacks you'll see in any game you've ever played, (be careful what stacking 52 fireworks does to your CPU tho, lol). What makes this game endless enjoyment is its randomness. Enemies, maps, items and more are pulled at random, making every run unique in its own right, and one that you'll remember distinctly. It's not all random though, keep playing and you'll get better and have better runs. I can't recommend this game enough! Give it a try either by yourself or with friends! Be careful though. I heard there's rain coming.

_childDocuments_.review: This game got me into the roguelike genre, it's my first roguelike game and I love it. If you're familiar with roguelike games, I'm sure you'll like this game. If you don't recognize the genre, absolutely try it. I truly recommend this game.The gameplay is absolutely amazing.  The characters are well done. Hopoo Games know what they're doing here.  It's what makes them all fun to play. Their abilities complement each other and are well balanced. If you learn their abilities and master these characters, you will become stronger, better than ever. There are so many items in this game and the fact that you are NOT limited to a number of items is amazing.  You can combine items with other items to create a godly build. I love it.   A great twist to the game that I enjoy a lot. This makes you value time more, and strategize how you're gonna play.  You know how this game is titled Risk of Rain 2? Well,  Lunar items, Shrine of Blood, Shrine of the Mountain, I can name so much. It doesn't even have to be an in-game item or structure. The player could take risks themselves like staying on a stage to farm for more items. The fact that making these risks can be worth it or screw you over is fascinating.  Each stage has multiple environments except Stage 5. There are also hidden realms that can be accessed through portals which add on to the run. A great addition that makes your runs more interesting, if you enter them that is.  Not even my damage hits as hard as The Rain Formerly Known as Purple. The music needs all your ears a listen. Chris Christodoulou is a brilliant composer, and it shows with his work on this game. The music bops and encapsulates well the expressions it was supposed to capture. My absolute applause. Dunno what else to say. The developers put heart into this game and I can tell.

_childDocuments_.review: Summary of all the stuff below: This game is an addiction and for all the right reasons. Risk of Rain 2 is a sandbox of chaotic fun, its sights and sounds are stylish and unforgettable, and the quality-of-life is pristine to a point I’ve never seen achieved anywhere else. It takes a little while to learn how to play it, but once you’ve been hooked, you’ll be playing it for months. If you enjoy roguelikes, shooters, or multiplayer PvE games, this is a must-play masterpiece I can’t recommend enough.More detailed review:Starting off with technical stuff, I want to talk about Risk of Rain 2’s quality of life. I’m not sure if other players had problems with this or not, but I adore how easy it is to learn everything on your own. There’s no pop-up screens telling you why you should kill enemies, no NPCs stopping you dead in your tracks to tell you how the levels work, you learn everything on your own without interruption. Other quality-of-life stuff includes no loading screens, a non-intrusive story with hours of optional lore, and hand-crafted levels with procedurally placed loot and objectives to keep everything familiar but still engaging.While it works totally fine as a single-player experience, the game is at its most fun when you’re playing with friends. Another example of this game’s super friendly quality-of-life: if the host of the party has stuff unlocked, new players can have that stuff too while also working on unlocking it for themselves at the same time. It’s still a fantastic game on your own, and even though everyone will have to own a copy, I highly suggest grabbing a friend or three for this.Onto the gameplay, your job is simple: investigate an alien planet via violent greetings and pile on enough junk onto yourself to make it back into space. Each level, you take the locals’ life savings, spend it on chests scattered around to get items, and then head to a teleporter to face a boss. The items range from the expected to the insane: you could find a syringe that boosts your attack speed a bit, a ukulele that grants chain lightning, or a bazooka that makes all your attacks explode. You will have to memorize the items, but thankfully you get a little description telling you what you just picked up and how it works every time you find it. And even though there’s almost 200 different items total, most of them are simple enough to remember the second or third time you find it. But since there’s so many, that special Roguelike addiction keeps you coming back to try out different builds. Especially when you realize that items can stack, leading to all sorts of power-hungry temptations. Even better, few items can’t be stacked infinitely. When the potential for a god run is so high, while also keeping the game an engaging challenge simultaneously, that’s when you know it’s gonna be a good time.Speaking of challenge, the difficulty balancing is incredible. You see, the longer you take to clear a level, the stronger enemies become. So, it’s this balancing act of taking the time to find items while also frantically finishing the levels to keep the upper hand. The easy mode turns the game into a fun sandbox experience (especially when you get that one cheat code), the normal mode keeps you on edge but plays fair and consistently, and the hard mode is great for the usual Roguelike masochists. When it comes to the characters to brave this planet, they’re all fantastic. Each one’s a sci-fi spin on the traditional class system opening whole new opportunities for experimenting with items and builds. You got your archer, rogue, mage, dog, Spider-Man mech, etc. Some classes can overlap each other when it comes to item priorities, but not too often enough for it to become annoying. There’s this great feeling when it clicks into your head what stacked items can make which classes become overpowered death brigades.One of RoR2’s most impressive feats are its 3D visuals. So many Roguelikes are built off sprites and pixels to save time and energy on the gameplay. It’s a perfectly fine compromise, but this game went above and beyond these common restraints. Many of the designs for the models and environments choose vibrant colors and minimalism over details and realistic features, giving a cartoony yet surreal look to everything. This is probably the least best aspect of RoR2; it’s impressive and perfectly serviceable, but not as outstanding as everything else.I’m not gonna talk much about the music since it speaks for itself but this a rare time when a game’s soundtrack is as stellar as the game itself. If you take anything away from this review, give a listen to the music, both from the base game and the DLC. I’ve heard tracks like ‘The Rain Formerly Known as Purple’ and ‘They Might As Well Be Dead’ dozens of times playing this game, yet they hit just as hard as when I heard them the first time.The only major criticism I have with RoR2 is unlocking new character abilities. I really like how you need to learn and experiment with items to solve most of these, but some are just way too much of a hassle. It’s not that they feel too impossible, but that they can feel, ironically, restraining at times. It’s only a handful of them, but it’s annoying how I can get all of one class’s abilities in two runs while another takes ten due to bad chance or strict guidelines. In a time of predatory monetization, unpolished releases, and uninspired ideas, Risk of Rain 2 revolutionizes both its genre and recent gaming as a whole. If you’re thinking about buying it, get the DLC too! It’s just as high quality as the base game and I can’t imagine playing without it. I’ve barely played the first game or tried RoR2’s modding, so I can’t say much there, but as for Risk of Rain 2, it’s a smart game that encourages fun and creativity unlike any rougelike before it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great, and carries a lot over from the first, but it currently has a huge flaw - there is basically no health management past the first handful of stages. You go from 100% health to zero in a split second, usually via random attacks from offscreen that you didn't even see coming. Every game I've had for the past few months, every *single* game, has been a "wait I'm dead what hit me" moment. As a result, there's really no strategy to managing your character's safety, which makes lategame somehow both boring and stressful as you know you can die at any second but there aren't any *decisions* you can make to prevent it. It's a cakewalk, right up until the moment you go splat. If they fix this over the course of early access I'm sure I'll return and give this a thumbs up. Much like the first game, the gameplay is intense and keeps you coming back, despite the consistent frustration over how every game ends. But not every game that's addicting is a masterpiece. And unless they actually start including the health bar in the game's mechanics, I'm worried that RoR2 will never hit that bar.EDIT: it might seem a little hypocritical that I keep this review with so many hours in the game. I play with friends, and I recommend *any* game that you play with friends. But the health thing still sucks and it's why I don't bother playing it solo.EDIT for 1.0 release: health still doesn't matter past stage 3. Almost all final boss attacks are one-shot kills. If you dodge, he then one-shots you with your own homing missiles. Still don't recommend unless you're playing with your friends, and even then this release patch is still pretty lame.

_childDocuments_.review: I was late to the party, and when I finally checked this game out (when Survivors of the Void came out) it was already a very vibrant game, full of snappy mechanics, interesting items and lots of cool quality of life features. It really felt like it got the full early access treatment. It felt good, playing it was the most natural thing in the world. Besides the quality of the DLC, it's incredible how many quality of life feature they broke and how much instability they introduced. I think we never ever saw a game regress this much in a single patch. It's driving me nuts. Tri-shop items not highlighted ? Void bubbles (witch can kill you) turn invisible, items can now fall off the map, loader is spinning like a mad man. Some chests are invisible ? Is that like an new mechanic ? Or is it a bug ? Does this item actually work ? Did I instantly die because of my hubris or some incompetent programming ? The big bugs ? We restart the session. Whatever. The small ones ? They just drive my paranoid brain into insanity. As a programmer, I would cry myself to sleep knowing I damaged such a cool codebase.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best sequels in indie gaming.Risk of Rain 2 takes the addictive and replayable rogue-lite elements of it's predecessor while it pumps up the combat and visuals. Risk of Rain 2 will have you and your friends looking to discover every hidden bit of gear or lore, working together and sometimes against one another in an incredibly well though out set of levels. The visuals are stunning and simplistic, they accomplish everything they need to while never growing old. The music is easily top of the line, your battles will be accompanied by the loving sounds of guitar rifts and heavy synths. _childDocuments_.review: GameplaySee also: Risk of Rain § GameplayRisk of Rain 2 follows a similar approach as the first title, in which one to four players must progress several levels while killing enemies. On each level the goal is to locate a teleporter, randomly located on the level; once activated, the players must defend themselves from an onslaught of aliens, including bosses until the teleporter is fully active. Killing aliens gains experience and currency; the currency can be used to open chests that drop random items on the level. These collectible items offer a wide range of boosts to the players carrying them and provide both synergistic effects and the potential to stack their effects if multiple copies of the same items are acquired. However, the strength, difficulty, and numbers of aliens increase every few minutes, thus making the game harder the longer the players stay on any level. In the metagame, players unlock access to new playable characters, items, and game modifiers by completing certain in-game achievements; once unlocked, new characters (called survivors) or modifiers are available to select from at the start of the game, or the new items can start appearing randomly in-game.Risk of Rain 2 features several of the same playable characters, creatures, and items from the first game, but transitions the game from 2D to a 3D environment.DevelopmentWhen they started development on the sequel, Hopoo started with a 2D-based prototype with the player in control of one of the monsters in the first game, as to mix up the formula for the sequel. [1]The transition to 3D was partly inspired by fan art for the original game that showed the various objects the player collected shown on the character. Hopoo wanted to use this approach for the sequel, but the 2D graphic approach did not give them enough visual space to work with. They transitioned the prototype from 2D to 2.5D, representing the character in 3D graphics but otherwise playing as a 2D platformer, however this did not work to their satisfaction and felt it was better to move the game fully to 3D, with the transition being relatively quick to complete.[1] Hopoo Games noted that the 3D option provided "much deeper design spaces and more possibilities for cool gameplay" as well as more ways to artistically express themselves.[2] The sequel was first announced in May 2017, at which time the team had already been working on the game for 6 months.[1] The sequel uses the Unity engine, which Hopoo had to learn to use, and 3D levels which the team spent a long time making.[1] In designing some of the returning monsters Hopoo noted that they had to design new attacks to make them more challenging in a 3D space.[1] Items also had to be redesigned to deal with the dimension change.[3]Hopoo released the game into early access on Windows on March 27, 2019, at the time they estimated that the full development process they would take another year.[4][5] During the early access period, Hopoo signed with Gearbox Publishing to release the game on Nintendo Switch, PlayStation 4, and Xbox One.[6] It was also released in early access for those platforms on August 30, 2019.[7] Its full release was initially scheduled for Q2 2020 but was delayed in order to expand the scope of its 1.0 update.[8] A free content update titled the "Anniversary Update" was released on March 25, 2021.[9] A paid expansion for the game called "Survivors of the Void" is currently under development, slated for release on March 1, 2022 for Windows, and Q2 2022 for console versions.[10]

_childDocuments_.review: The original Risk of Rain was one of my first experiences in PC Indie Gaming, and it left quite an impression on me. From its stylistic character design, to the 2d side-scrolling ability spam fest, and an ending with music so beautifully appropriate it ended up permanently etched into my mind. So, when Hopoo Games, a studio of 4!!!! Individuals announced they were making a 2nd game and it would be 3d, I was all for it. I haven't written a review for this game yet, but I've owned it since it was first available in early access and with its first DLC on the horizon I think its time. Theirs a lot of reasons why I think this game is one of my favorites, and why it succeeds so much over its predecessor, which in its own right is fantastic:The transition from 2d to 3d while keeping its style is incredible. From the ability usage, to the items, it all feels amazing as your character transcends into a beast until you either beat the game or loop until you die.With the items you can feel that rush of getting a red on stage 1, or simply feeling happy at finally getting those damn crit glasses for when you desperately need one. Every item serves a purpose that benefits you in a very direct, observable way.Plenty of secrets to unlock and explore, from hidden stages, characters, and items, it can keep you busy for a long time.A wide variety of characters that all allow for a distinct play-style while also having switchable abilities that changes elements of their kit. It is one of the best soundtracks that I've ever heard. From the active teleporter boss jams, to the quiet serenity of the earlier stages, to the absolutely fantastic finale of  it's an incredible listening experience, every time.Easily accessible coop through steam, alongside the new addition of challenge modes for people who want that extra difficulty or variety in their runs, So, should YOU buy this game? 100%. Play a few rounds on your own to get the hang of it, then once you inevitably get hooked, tell all your friends to buy it, and jam out with them. Your music will be electric.

_childDocuments_.review: You should probably read some other reviews if you want a more in-depth analysis. I just wanted to share why I find the game so enjoyable :DRisk of Rain was a phenomenal game which included a refreshing item mechanic and diverse range of interesting, characters, environments, and enemies. It's you against swarms of enemies accompanied by music that makes you chew bubblegum and kick arse. It consumed a fair good amount of my time for the game it was, and it was the absolute bomb when you grabbed a couple of mates. Hence, I felt I got the 'complete experience'. I was fully satisfied, not feeling disappointed in any remark. Risk of Rain 2 (ROR2) however...WOW! This is an amazing entry to the franchise. A 3D ROR?! I mean killing enemies in the first game was fun and all... but now that it's in a 3D vibrant, traversable environment, it's on a whole other level. Also, as this is only in early access, the developers have lined up a string of new content, which is really exciting. As we'll be introduced to new content, whether that'll include features, characters, enemies or maps. This game has a lot to offer in terms of improvements.Basic Overview:VisualsThe visuals are a major obvious step-up from the original 2D sprites. However, they still somehow capture and embody the nostalgic essence of the predecessor. This title is accompanied by an amazing palette that I find really aids in the enjoyment of the game. Watching the effects and animations within this game is so satisfying. It has an amazing visual aesthetic which complements the mechanics of the game smoothly. Everything that happens looks like how it should happen.GameplayPlaying this game, you'll experience a fast-paced gameplay, that's complimented by tight, concise and engaging player/environmental mechanics. You are able to select from a range of unique characters all having exclusive (and might I add, freaking awesome) abilities that make your experience 10x more engaging. The AI will progressively overwhelm you, but it will offer challenge rather than a chore, this being due to your characters progression in-game. The item mechanic is so refreshing compared to other titles. I don't think I could find this as well executed anywhere else. It offers a range of unique items that enhance your character and overall experience playing. Adding explosions, electricity, visual changes to your character and just so many more elements to the gameplay.  I'd recommend this game to anyone who loves a fast-paced, action packed shooter and enjoys rouge-like elements. I'm not too good at reviewing, however I am really passionate about this franchise and want to try to express how amazing this game is and that others should try it!  Thanks for reading this far, I appreciate it!

_childDocuments_.review: Risk of Rain 2 is simply one of the best rogue like games ever made, an evolution of the core gameplay that will serve as the gold standard for any other 3D rogue likes. Playing very similar to the first Risk of Rain, you fight monsters on an alien world to collect gold and buy chests, acquire items, fight a boss while charging a teleporter to the next area, and repeat until death or success in slaying the final boss. What makes this game stand out is the fantastic transition of Risk of Rain’s 2D gameplay into 3D space as well as rock solid mechanics and great presentation. Movement is smooth, precise, and incredibly fun to traverse with. Combat is addictive and modular that offers ten characters that play differently, and swappable abilities specific to each character. With a strong initial setup, randomly generated variety spices the game to excellency. All the game’s maps offer the same basic template, but with variations that make each run unique. This includes certain paths being present or absent, numerous interactable shrines and their locations, and the many chests and drones available for purchase. The effects of items stack in various ways when picked up multiple times, which can completely break the game without any limitations. This is balanced by the ever-increasing difficulty tied to the time spent during a run. Multiple secret areas, unlockable items and characters, and information logs for every location, monster, item, and character add a lot of replay value to an already addicting experience. If this was not enticing enough, the game allows for up to four players for online multiplayer, including difficulty scaling for each new player. The game’s blend of sci-fi technology with natural wilderness and bright colors turn simple models and textures into a visually pleasing aesthetic that is nice to look at and easy to render. A nice additional touch is that each item picked up is added onto the character, decorating them in the plethora of various goodies acquired throughout the run. The excellent soundtrack combines kick ass electric guitar with ambient electronic sounds for music that never gets old to listen to. The most lackluster aspect of the game is the story, which continues from the previous game. Aside from an opening cinematic, story is told through logs picked up in game. These give little bits of lore and world building about galactic civilization, survivors of the first game’s crashed ship, and the creatures of Petrichor V. Outside of this, there is little connecting story, and the excellent self-commentary from the first game seems to be absent here. Additionally, there are some minor performance issues, mostly relating to internet play but can also include single player glitches. These problems are a far cry from the rest of the amazing experience. Currently there is an active modding scene for the game, with more official support for modding talked about by the developers. Hopefully, this includes Steam Workshop support rather than the current unofficial mod loader required to load mods. There are also talks of DLC content packs being developed, but at the time of this review these are not available. Tailing points based on several attributes (Story: 7/10, Gameplay: 10/10, Controls: 9/10, Content: 10/10, Presentation: 8/10, Music: 10/10, Performance: 9/10, Multiplayer: 10/10, Bonus 3/5 points for modest and simple to install modding, 76/80 total), this game scores a well-deserved 95/100. Do yourself a favor and pick up a copy today.

_childDocuments_.review: I couldn't have imagined a more faithful recreation of the original in 3D. Unfortunately, that includes the rough start. If your first few games leave a bad taste in your mouth, give it some time. More than half of the game is locked behind achievements (sorry, "challenges"), but once you've unlocked the  items and found a character or two you enjoy, the game really opens up. And it's a good one.For anybody put off by the early access tag (and who could blame you), I wouldn't worry too hard. The game may have a few "under construction" icons sprinkled around, but consider it new content for the future. The game doesn't  incomplete; it plays just fine as it is. If that doesn't assuage your concerns, you might like to know that the developers are maintaining and following a basic roadmap to a 1.0 release, which you can easily find in the news feed. While you're there, the patch notes for this game are a joy to read, often containing specific numbers and  (Full disclosure, I like changelogs.) Really, if you have misgivings based on the early access banner, read the language of the patch notes and other communication, and decide for yourself if this is a developer you trust to maintain their promise.Maybe I'm gushing a little overmuch, but it's been a breath of fresh air to see an early access title managed the way this one has. All I mean to say is that I enjoy this game, and I wouldn't regret the money paid even if this was the final product.

_childDocuments_.review: Risk of Rain 2 is an absolute blast for group play, offering a chaotic and entertaining experience filled with silly shenanigans that keep players coming back for more. From the moment you drop into its procedurally generated worlds with your friends, the mayhem begins. Whether you're frantically fighting off hordes of alien creatures or strategizing how to take down towering bosses, the cooperative gameplay fosters camaraderie and laughter as you navigate the chaos together.What sets Risk of Rain 2 apart is its unpredictability and the sheer variety of items, characters, and environments that ensure no two runs are ever the same. The game's replayability is off the charts, as each session presents new challenges and opportunities for experimentation. Whether you're unlocking new characters, discovering powerful items, or pushing the limits of your survival skills, there's always something new and exciting to discover with each playthrough.But perhaps the most memorable aspect of Risk of Rain 2 is the sheer absurdity that ensues when playing with friends. From accidentally activating game-changing items at the worst possible moment to narrowly escaping death with a well-timed ability, the game's unpredictable nature often leads to hilarious moments that you'll be reminiscing about long after the session ends. Whether you're a seasoned player or new to the game, Risk of Rain 2 promises hours of laughter-filled entertainment that makes it a must-have for any gaming group looking for a good time.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to wait for the full release to have my final say about the game but honestly with how each update has been and how amazing the game is even in its uncompleted state, I feel confident enough to say this is probably one of my favorite games of 2019. The original Risk of Rain was such a great and addictive game, when I heard about a sequel happening, I was both excited as I was skeptical. How would a game like this even work in 3D, and would it make the transition well? I can safely say yes, absolutely. I'd go as far to say this is even better than the original which I loved quite a bit. In terms of art direction and graphics, the game looks fantastic, it's great to see the old cast updated in 3D along with cool new classes, and the entire roster of enemies just look fantastic, and the various areas you find yourself exploring are vast and have a decent amount of hidden goodies to warrant getting creative and making sure you check every nook and cranny. Performance wise the game runs fairly well on my 1660 Ti but considering the main gimmick of the game, pushing runs over an hour and a half the game will understandably dip into lower framrates considering the amount of enemies, particle effects, and a bunch of other nonsense is on the screen at once. I play with the Ultra settings so if I really cared, I could reduce some settings in order to maintain a consistently high framerate even after 20 or so stages, but I was never bothered by those performance dips enough to really caring about reducing graphics settings, especially since if I'm playing the game for that long, the game becomes therapeutic in its insanity. Before that tho I used to run the game on my Ryzen APU with low-mid settings and still got decent performance out of the game even in late game portions of my runs, and it was just as addictive back in its initial release. To get it out of the way, as I'm making this review the game is not finished with about 2 or so updates left to be released. Aside from a minor delay, everything has maintained on schedule and there's always consistent feedback and updates from the devs, this game has lots of love and care put into it and its easy to see that they're putting their all into this game. I'm only noting this because as you can expect, changes may occur in the future regarding the game that will be different from the version I'm playing (The Hidden Realms Update). Honestly, the content is stacked with tons of characters to choose from,dozens of items to use and unlock, 8 or so levels with two level receiving alternate formats for the starting areas, as well as a few secret locations too, and unlockable character weapon loadouts to change a class's play style a bit. All the characters have their ups and downs, with some needing a bit more work to be made more worthwhile to enjoy (Rex and Mercenary are my least played of the bunch). Characters get their own batch of unique abilities that generally manage well for single player, but combined together in multiplayer, there's a bunch of ways to tackle co-op sessions and allow for great enjoyment with friends. Multiplayer is probably one of the best incentives to get this game if you're looking for a new co-op game to check out as it offers lots of variety and challenge, and thankfully I've never had much issue with online connectivity with others. So the game looks great, plays great, and is great with friends? Is this just a perfect game? Of course not, a lot of the issues that persist in RoR2 are in regards to some balance issues with character abilities, items, tweaks to level design to kink out minor imperfections in the randomization aspects (I've had teleporters be completely out of sight or spawn in strange locations making it difficult for me to make progress in runs because I check entire levels only to be dumbfounded where the exit is), there's also the addition of items, enemies, character loadouts, etc. to be added to the game that are still under development but the biggest issue of all..... there's no end game portion...kinda. You can sacrifice yourself to a obelisk but that's really it at the moment. All you can really do is complete objectives for items/character loadouts and sacrifice yourself or see how far you can get before you die or when things get way too mind numbing, the game is still very addictive, but I would like something a lot more satisfying to look forward to when ending my run that isn't just killing myself, the original game had a pretty fun final level followed by a multi phase boss fight that was satisfying to complete, but we won't see something like this until this game's 1.0 update in Spring 2020. That being said, this game holds lots of great qualities that warrant checking it out now, especially for the co-op, or if you just want a video game equivalent of crack to distract you. This is very well worth the $20, its a phenomenal game with tons of great qualities and replay value that even in its incompleted state will have you returning to complete another run over and over and over and over again. If you like games that encourage speedrunning, unleash your inner kleptomaniac, give you a difficult challenge, or just play with friends, this is a must buy.

_childDocuments_.review: Risk of Rain 2 is a third-person shooter roguelike with a distinct art style.Features:- At the time of writing this review, there are 10 characters to play as, each with different play styles and unlockable abilities earned via completing specific achievements.- Stages are procedurally generated, where chests and other interactable entities spawn randomly across the stage.- The difficulty is always increasing, with enemies gaining health & damage modifiers as well as rarer and more dangerous enemies being added to the pool of possible combatants.- At the time of writing this review, there are 2 alternative game modes; time trials and 'Eclipse', where the game becomes harder each time you beat it.- 'Artifacts' which dramatically change the way the game is played, with some Artifacts allowing you to choose your items, enemies exploding upon death, enabling friendly fire etc.- Can be played solo & offline as well as up to 4 players.My only quarrel with Risk of Rain 2 is that the update cycle is slow, with content updates coming every ~3 months

_childDocuments_.review: The game is overall pretty good, if you're looking for mindless-- (except not entirely, because there are tactics you can apply for better survival, even down to time management) face rolling combat and monster mashing then this is a pretty fun way to do it. Of course, you're going to have to accept the game is a roguelike... meaning that your character and all their items will be gone once you die, and then you start all over again... so please understand what you are buying into before you buy it! Luckily, I myself was able to get my copy free through a friend because of the buy 1 get 1 free deal they had until the 30th, which was absolutely an amazing deal and more than worth. That being said, the game doesn't just leave you with nothing to gain from your adventures, there is a sense of accomplishment to be made through unlocking new various characters, obtaining lunar coins to use in your adventures further down the road (won't spoil as to exactly what they do), and for you completionists there is a logbook in which you can fill by way of obtaining new items, monster books, enviroment datas.... Your presented with 4 varying skills to use per character, all of which are unique to each and vary wildly different than the last.. and each skill and character serves a certain role in co-op play, though of course each can still lay down the pain on monsters as needed, some just possibly might serve that role better but also might not be as good for raw survival... you get the idea. At the same time however, so far from the characters I have played I wouldn't say that any one is just inherently "Better" than the last, they all feel pretty well balanced *in the roles they are intended for*.. it really comes down to learning how to play them well and whatever suits YOUR play style the best, so don't let anyone tell you "Oh, pick X character because they are the best."... no, it's the best for THEM.The game being an early access title, of course naturally is going to harbor a lot of suspicion and caution.. and well, you should be! However, let me at least put some wary to rest in that reassuring you that in the games current form even, it is quite enjoyable and replayable to an extent you can well worth get your $20 out of it, after all... most $60 campaign games run a storyline of usually between 20-40 hours and then you're done, which you can easily get out of this! Save for the enemies mostly, no two runs will be the same either (the maps ARE mostly the same, but they have different a few different versions you might end up with). The game seems like it still has content it wants to expand upon too, so hopefully we'll see more of all of this soon (new characters are definitely confirmed).Definitely give it a try, I think you'll enjoy it as long as you are into face pace smash-em-up combat games! I would also like to point out that earlier I said I'd got this for free from the 2 for 1 deal from a friend... don't let that be a discredit to what I'd left you with here, believe me... I regret plenty of money I'd spent on absolute garbage throughout the years, and if only I could get that back to make up $20(s) to buy the game not even for myself (since I already have it), but even for some other friends I would do it.
