_childDocuments_.review: GAME IS GOOD. No, but for real this game stands out as one of the best examples of an early-access game ever, up there with the likes of dead cells, factorio and subnautica (and of course the original risk of rain!!) I have to say I was super sceptical about this game when i first saw the blog posts about it around a year ago. I genuinely thought there was no way they would be able to pull off transitioning such an iconic, tightly designed 2D game into a 3D environment, i thought there was no way the unique feeling and rush of the first game, but i have to humbly admit; i was wrong. The game feels amazing to play, the movement and the animations of everything feel absolutely fantastic, and so satisfying, dashing in and out of combat, carefully managing not only your health and your abilties, the ebb and flow of combat, but time itself and the money you have to earn to buy new items. the game feels extremely oppressive, even when you are STACKED with heaps of powerful items, you still feel like you could die at any second if you're not careful. The enemy variety is impressive for an early-access game and I assume it can only get broader from this point on, and they also read extremely well against the background and environments, which is something i was worried about, and im utterly surprised they managed to make it work, as in, you can tell that there's a brass contraption 30 meters away from you readying up to transform you into a red splatter across the ground, you can tell that there's a burning greater wisp in the distance or around the corner because of the uniquely coloured glow;  nothing ever really gets lost against the background... until the screen inevitably becomes a flood of numbers and particle effects a couple hours in.I am a massive fan of "survival" games where the only objective is to last as long as you can in a state of constantly increasing difficulty, and to date no game has ever more perfectly captured this concept than this one. It does an even better job already than the first game, because everything is coming at you from every direction, even in the sky. There is something deeply and viscerally exciting about dashing through hoards of enemies, barely surviving, knowing you could be dead at any second if you dont move perfectly or you get too greedy attacking a boss, and once youre about an hour into most runs you get to the point where you are slaying literally dozens of enemies every second with your abilities that launch missiles, chain lightning, runic explosions, sticky bombs and more. Pushing yourself to survive for longer and longer only to get brutally cut down each time, and don't let me sully your expectations; this game is absolutely brutal. But you live for those rare times when you get the perfect combination of items which lets you ascend into godhood, becoming practically invincible and making the planet fear YOU for a change. The only real reason i wouldn't recommend this game to you is if you aren't a fan of a game where you have to sit down and play functionally the same thing over and over for quite a long time, a single run can be upwards of an hour, with the really crazy ones being upwards of 2 or more, with no option to save and continue later. currently the levels are quite samey, each of the 5 or 6 levels is much more static than the original, largely the same map with small variations like an open door or not (i assume this will stop being the case later on, as the game is in early-access), though obviously the loot is randomly placed.But yes, overall I am extremely impressed with the game and it is an utter joy to play. i truly believe that this could be the next great rogue-like now the age of isaac is coming to a close, since hopoo have made clear their intentions to constantly improve the game like the first one.

_childDocuments_.review: A game that I would probably never have looked twice at, if not for recommendations from friends that had already played it. Don't make the same mistake I did - the reviews do reflect just how great the game is!Gameplay consists of being dropped into a world that is beautiful and crazy. It's slick FPS shooter with roguelike roots that is a blast to play both single player and with up to 4 friends. A multitude of classes, playstyles, abilities and items will make every playthough different and keeps things fresh and fun every time you play. It's fast-paced and unrelenting, but rewards smart decisions, exploration and PEW PEW.It has a novel graphical look that is surprisingly good and great music alongside it. Things can get very chaotic as you advance through the levels, yet the game always seems to maintain a nice balance and not go over the top to a point where it's a lightshow. There are plenty of unlockables - in the form of abilities, characters and artefacts. Some harder to figure out than others. Exploration is key here. As you begin to understand the systems in play, you can start to work out a character build that fits the way you play - and luckily there is plenty to chose from. Fancy a bow and arrow huntress with seeking arrows? Got you covered. Fancy a mercenary with a lazer sword that dices enemies at close range? They got you covered. They have engineers, gunners, aliens, robots and more. Sufficed to say, you will find more than one way of playing - and all of them are fun. Where it shines, however, is multiplayer - where teamwork comes together to form a really slick and enjoyable game to play.

_childDocuments_.review: Risk of Rain 2 was an impulse purchase for me. A few of my friends described the game to me when it first appeared on steam and I just sorta... bought it. I had heard of the first game but never played it. I had no expectations, no idea what I was getting myself into.Boy do I not regret it.I've never been one for roguelike games but Risk of Rain 2 just hits the spot. It's a fantastic experience whether you tackle the elements alone or you conquer them with 3 others (highly recommended). The environments are beautifully designed, the music makes me wanna buy an official soundtrack and the gameplay itself is addictive and punishing if you choose to play on the hardest difficulty. I've been blown away by how progression works in the game. The madness of being able to stack the effects of the items you collect means your character can become near-godlike. It also means no two runs will be the same. One run, you'll be stacking damage items and you'll destroy enemies in a few hits, in another run you'll be jumping in midair multiple times and running across the map in seconds.There aren't many games where I don't have to hesitate and ask myself "do I really wanna play this right now?"Risk of Rain 2 keeps me wanting more after each run. I can go further. Faster. I can do better. I need to go AGAIN.EDIT// Artifacts just released and they change the entire game up. Wanna do insane damage but have to worry about dying to someone sneezing on you? Get that glass right up ya.

_childDocuments_.review: Risk of Rain 2 is incredibly fun.It's a roguelike based around the concept that you're stuck on a planet and need to get off. You collect items, power up a teleporter and kill bosses to progress to the next level, all while the game ramps up in difficulty. What can seem like a serene walk in the park during the first few minutes can quickly turn into a festival of chaos where you have no real idea why you're still alive.RoR has tons of items that can all be stacked and used at the same time, often leading to overpowered builds if you're lucky enough or can create a build that suits your playstyle and your character. Whatever you get can be useful if used right and your experience is different with every playthrough.Outside of the gameplay, the game has hundreds of challenges and unlockables as progression. You can do easy things up to downright insane challenges to unlock new items that you'll encounter in your runs, or entirely new characters which you can use.The playable characters are all incredibly unique with their own skill sets with secondary skills that can be unlocked via challenges that replace certain skills, allowing you to create the character you want to play as. There's the Artificer, a glass cannon that can be stressful yet engaging, the Commando, an all round character that anyone can understand and play as, and a myriad of others.And it's still in early access, with frequent updates. 1.0 is just around the corner, however, but even when it is released the devs have stated they won't stop support and will continue adding characters and other features.It's also friendly to new players, with an easy difficulty to help you get into things, and the locked items help new players slowly get introduced to new mechanics as they unlock new items and characters over time. It's also co-op, so you can have a blast with your friends, newbie or veteran. (items aren't shared though, i'd recommend installing a mod for that)The game has it's charm and it's very unique. Even if you spent 2 hours on a run just to die, you'll still want to play another round.that's the basic gist of it i guessgo shoot a crab or something idkalso it's in 1.0 now and the music is probably some of the best i've heard even if you don't play it give the soundtrack a whirl

_childDocuments_.review: This is the second installment in the Risk Of Rain games, the first was a 2D shooter as this is a 3D shooter, other than switching from 2D to 3D there have been many quality of life changes.QOL CHANGES :The portal when activated you are required to kill a boss (or many) and charge the portal in the red zone that it puts out, this is much better than the system in the previous game which was kill the boss wait for charge (there was no marked zone) and kill all enemies to proceed.Many of the items have been tweaked to fit the 3D gameSome characters that were more suited to 2D have been brought to 3D seamlessly (though mercenary is still a bit under other characters as he lacks range and mobility)THE CONS :The game looks amazing and is decently optimised, but once you get enough items and start shooting the game bricks, even with my 2060 it dropped from 180fps to 40fps when all items were activeThe artifacts, in the first game there were artifacts hidden in secret areas for the player to find, and they could be activated before starting a game to give a augment to the game, though they have not implemented this yet as they are currently developing them for this gameThe characters, they are all well balanced don't get me wrong but some characters are much better with their kit than others, take mercenary and artificer, merc has little range but a double jump, his dash is meh as he can be damaged during the dash and it does not go as far as huntress' blink, merc suffers late game as if you don't have alot of survival items he will get 1 shot as soon as u run into a few enemies as his 4th ability is his only invincibility ability, and artificer suffers from different problems, his attacks are very good but his one is on a recarge basis and having a item like soldier syringe is only beneficial to his 2 which is his charged attack, though his 2 does put out massive damage the downsides are that you need at least 2 items to make it work well, soldier syringe and back up magazine, and his final issue is that his kit does not have a dodge or a movement ability, his 3 which is usually on other characters a dodge is a ice wall, his wall doesn't black bullets as well it only damages enemies that you spawn it on (he is also one of the hardest characters to get as you need a lot of lunar coins). This is not to say these characters are bad in any way, they are just a little below the others.Lunar coins and lunar items, the coins are a random drop from enemies which can be picked up and can be stored between runs, they are used in either the shop or lunar bulbs, the items are mostly a tradeoff so most are detrimental to your game unless u have rng on your side and u have all the items you need for a lunar item to work well.To tie this up this is a great game to play, and is even greater with friends, though there are some issues and minimal content as of saying this, but there is a lot of replay value and though it's a early access title it is well worth your money as these developers are dedicated and will not abandon this game, we just have to wait for new content (Btw rex a new survivor dropped)

_childDocuments_.review: Risk of Rain 2 is the sequel to its older, 2D self of the same namesake. This one features 3D, open areas, and a lot of new ways to play the game. You can pick from a variety of various characters to play as based upon your personal play style, and there's a few variations of abilities per character. It keeps characters feeling fresh, and since this game is a rogue-like, it has plenty of replayability.The game features a standard difficulty mechanic with your typical Easy/Medium/Hard, but newcomers to the series may not know that it has an ever-increasing difficulty naturally. The longer you take to complete each level, the more difficult it will get. You'll want to grab as many items and whatnot as you can before it gets too hard or you may find yourself struggling. In co-op, I personally find that the difficulty spikes aren't too bad. This leads me to my next point.Risk of Rain 2 has wonderful online co-op. You can play with up to 3 friends in each of your runs. It helps balance out enemy numbers and even bosses. I personally think it makes challenge totems easier and more worth the effort. It's also a great game to just generally kick back and enjoy with some friends if you're looking for something to do and burn some time.Overall, I think Risk of Rain 2 is a steal, and for the amount of content they're adding/already have added combined with the near infinite build possibilities circa Binding of Isaac, you'd be silly to pass this up if you're a fan of roguelikes or looking to get into the genre as a whole. If you want to wait for a sale, that's even better because you're REALLY getting a bargain at a sale price.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, this might just be one of the most enjoyable games I have played in years, definitely the most enjoyable game that I've played this year. The premise is so incredibly simple and for that reason, its so incredibly sweet and captivating. The game isn't in of itself difficult, but the difficulty increases in the form of stats and the quantity of mobs as time progresses, this is what makes longer runs feel so high-octane and seemingly endless. You can easily spend several hours of your day doing runs either alone or with a team of up to 4 friends and time seemingly just seeps away right through the palms of your hands. In the first 7 days of owning the game i racked up 62 hours in it, i feel like that could give you a good idea on how enjoyable the game is when you first lay your hands on it.In a time like this, where most people are sitting at home with nothing to do, this kind of escape really is very special. I would recommend this game twice if i could.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: Well, a few years later and I finally came back to this one after playing a bit right when EA started. Pleasantly surprised at the amount of content that was delivered yet baffled by some of the weird game design decisions.Really wish there was a neutral or mixed review option here as the game is mostly good, but the few flaws that are there are glaring.- the levels are too big and the teleporters are too hard to spot. There is no map. There isn't even a minimap. Seriously? The levels are quite large, tbh, excessively so, so this is a puzzling omission.- This means that a large part of the time is spent being in that annoying state of "Where the heck is this thing??" searching high and low for the teleporter and generally not being a pleasant game flow.- forced platforming in some spots is pretty clunky. You can prioritize items that boost your jumping though.- The final boss is straight out of dark souls.. the problem is not every character has a dodge roll type movement option that is fast enough or on a low enough cooldown to keep up with him making it rather unfun with some characters. Again, trying to build for mobility will solve that issue but it's either RNG or relying on the 'cheat' relic that lets you pick your items.- Runs are very time consuming, often upwards of an hour or more. There is no save and continue. Again, NO MID RUN SAVE and runs are 1hr+ ?- Character balance seems pretty out of whack. Some characters (Engineer, Artificer) seem to just do way more damage than everybody else. Other characters (mercenary, loader) are just a chore to play.

_childDocuments_.review: Risk of Rain 2 is perhaps one of the most, if not the most polished Early Access titles in recent memory. The game feels like a finished product, boasting a lot of content for roguelike fans while attracting new kind of players with its charming visual style and engaging gameplay. Going into RoR 2 after playing the first game I was pleasantly surprised at how well the gameplay translates to a 3D environment. It feels fresh yet familiar, and improves a lot on the limitations of the first game.The star of the game is obviously the gameplay. You pick one of the several characters in RoR (you start off with 1 but unlock more through gameplay), and starts off in a level with nothing except your abilities, but you get to improve your character through purchasing items and equipments scattered throughout the levels. Collecting items is the name of the game here, as there are tons of different items in the game, each having their own unique traits that will improve your character as you purchase more and more items. That's the core loop of the game, just keep purchasing more and more items until you went from a weakling to a gun-toting ultramarine that can run faster than Usain Bolt himself. As this is a roguelike, a playthrough won't last you that long, and when you complete a run, you usually get achievements that unlocks new items in the game, attracting you to play through another run. The game is addictive and engaging, and does not have the slightest hint of microtransactions. The devs are also releasing a stable stream of updates that keeps the game from being stale, and they even announced the Full Release date.Risk of Rain 2 is a wonderful gem, a shining star amongst other Early Access titles, and one that I will keep returning to play. If you're a fan of roguelikes or just good old fun video games in general, get this game. You won't regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: Risk of Rain 2 is an extraordinary roguelike experience that excels in its mechanics and power progression. With an assortment of diverse characters, each offering unique playstyles and captivating exploits, the game consistently surprises and delights. Item and enemy log books satisfy collectors and lore enthusiats alike. The dedication to power creeping yields exhilarating moments as you stack items and witness the gratifying display of damage numbers. Despite the predominantly vacant level design, an aura of exploration and concealed discoveries beckon to be unveiled. Cooperative play with friends further enriches the adventure, fostering camaraderie and engrossing conversations. Risk of Rain 2 presents an addictive odyssey of ascending the power curve that is absolutely irresistible.Definitely a must have in my book. Whether you're the man with the plan or "Leeroy Jenkins" prepare for an absolutely roaring good time.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game a lot and have a ton of memories with this with friends. I love the environments and atmosphere, the soundtrack, the survivors and gameplay, the community, and all of that. It's one of the most engaging rogue-likes out there imo, and it's an absolute blast that I'd recommend to anyone.Thats what I would say in the last update or so, because while I enjoy the new content of Seekers of The Storm, some of the odd decisions regarding the new elites and new items seem strange and as if they were either an afterthought or lacked playtesting, but that's more a matter of opinion than anything. What isn't up for debate is the absolutely ♥♥♥♥♥♥ code throughout every aspect of the game. I have no clue what they did exactly from this update to the last, but the plethora of bugs completely prevent some characters from functioning how they used to, how some items interact with eachother, how some enemy encounters go, and even some game breaking bugs as well. I absolutely love the music, the new stages, and so far am having a blast when the game works for longer than two seconds, but that only makes me more frustrated when it doesn't. I have friends on ps5 as well, who can't even open the game after this new update even without owning the DLC, it doesn't even allow them to play at all, which I honestly think is proof of how the game is currently being handled at Gearbox. While the last DLC was buggy at the start, it was nowhere near this level and the amount of care Hopoo put into each and every update and fixing bugs, communication with community, and so on is sorely missed. Whatever is going on at Gearbox regarding ROR2, whether it might be management, or a lack of care, or anything else it could be, I hope its addressed sometime soon. I'm not gonna go and start hating gearbox devs or anything like that, just wish for better with an IP that I deeply care for.If you read this far, thanks lmfao, lets hope for a big patch soon. Maybe next time, some community playtesting or communication might help a bit. I want to change this review to positive as soon as I can.

Don't mistake this change as a flaw; on the contrary, the game excels in various aspects, often matching or even surpassing the original.the most captivating aspects of the game is in its enchanting soundtrack and visual design. They effortlessly draw players into immersive worlds, enticing them to spend countless hours exploring, conquering formidable challenges, and unlocking an abundance of items.the developers deserve praise for their efforts in improving the netcode and enhancing the multiplayer experience. It's evident that Hopoo knows what they're doing, and it's encouraging to see such wise decisions being made throughout the development cycle.risk of rain 2 is great and hopoo continues to impress; I'm eager to see what's in store for the future. I recommend monsoon difficulty.Pros:*gameplay is intuitive and easy to grasp.*well-thought-out design.*engaging core gameplay loop.*sound design is masterclass.*improvements to multiplayer make it more accessible and enjoyable.Cons:*the difficulty might be off-putting to some players, especially newcomers.*the game's requirement for constant attention, along with the absence of a pause button, could potentially be off-putting for some players.

_childDocuments_.review: Steam really needs an "on the fence" or "mixed opinion" option for reviews. But we don't have that so I'm gonna go ahead and say I don't recommend this game in its current state. It's not because the game is bad, not fun, buggy or anything like that, but simply because it's the most repetitive roguelike I've played. The music is cool, I love the way the levels look and the characters pretty much make this game fun. The big problem I've found is that it's not random enough. I've found myself getting bored cycling through the same six worlds over and over. Additionally, while the items are cool, they hit a point of diminishing returns around level 25ish and just don't make characters feel different enough. With all my runs using the same character, the experience felt very similar after I'd cycled through each world despite picking up different loot.Having said all this, it's a great early access game and the roadmap looks very promising. I'm greatly looking forward to seeing how the game develops and changes all the way up to release.

_childDocuments_.review: The art style is easy on the eyes early on, but as the run continues and your screen starts to fill with clutter, the diarrhoea christmas lights at later stages can be seizure inducing. RoR2 doesn’t hold hands and guide you through its story because honestly there is not much story going on here. There is rich lore to explore for people who want to. The lo-fi melody perfectly fits the perilous environment and matches the gameplay with synced rhythm and tempo. Sound design is good too.Drop into a planet, kill monsters, get money, buy items. Rinse and repeat until you become powerful to one shot God himself. Fast paced with constant running, jumping, sliding and juggling between primary weapon, secondary weapon, abilities and equipment. In each run the difficulty increases over time, which is an innovative approach to deal with difficulty. The roster is filled with unique characters who each have their own gameplay mechanics, making the game feel completely different. Most items can be obtained by completing specific challenges. You can also unlock game modifiers to make the game easier or more difficult to your liking. The challenges are one-of-a-kind, and the rewards are meaningful enough to keep players interested.There is no limit. It stops being fun when you decide so.There is co-op to enjoy with friends and difficulty scales with the number of players. And if you have no friends, rest assured because all achievements are attainable through single player.No bugs or technical issues. Without a decently powerful PC the game faces severe lags and occasional crashes in long runs where you loop multiple times and a million things are happening in the background. Lowering graphical settings can help to an extent.Survivors of the Void DLC adds excellent new characters, stages, items,  enemies and alternate endings.Worth every penny. The Devs are continuously supporting and updating the game which is commendable. The community is very active and you can add tons of community made  to breathe new life into your game. I highly recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: I believe that the core of what makes a rogue-lite addicting is the power fantasy. When the RNG hits just right during a run, you become a God... and becoming a God is fun! Risk of Rain 2 understands this concept so incredibly well. In other rogue-lites, a good run means you feel powerful. In this game, you have the capability of becoming so insanely overpowered that you can barely even comprehend what is happening. Hundreds of enemies will spawn only to be instantly killed with a casual glance in their direction, exploding in a fountain of coins. On your tenth loop, you become essentially omnipotent - flying around the map at mach speed, thoughtlessly burning everything in your path as you stack another teddy bear on top of the pile and put on your 10th pair of red-tinted glasses. Until finally, like Ozymandias, your empire collapses in an instant when you greedily stop to scratch your nose, atomized into a million pieces by a random flaming jellyfish.In RoR2, chasing that power fantasy dragon is so addictive on its own, but this game also happens to have the added benefit of featuring extremely engaging combat, interesting enemies, intense boss battles, awesome level design, a ton of fun items, a diverse cast of playable characters, multiplayer, challenge modes, and to top it all off... what I would consider the greatest video game soundtrack of all time. The music is just so incredible that I can't really put it into words.Risk of Rain 2 is hands down my favorite rogue-lite, and one of my favorite games ever.

_childDocuments_.review: Short version:Pros:+ Highly replayable+ Tons of variety (survivors, abilities, items, builds, modifiers, etc)+ Absolute blast with friends+ Simple but pleasant art-style+ Good soundtrack+ Risk vs Reward mechanics and items+ Frequently updatedCons:- Enemies become bullet sponges after a while- Some items are just terrible- You can die almost instantly at times (even though devs claim there are no 1-hit kills in most scenarios)"Long" version: is a third-person shooter with roguelike elements developed by Hopoo Games and published by Gearbox Publishing.You land on a mysterious planet and must fight your way through enemy hordes while purchasing items that give you better stats and versatility.I am a big fan of the original game and I was happy hearing it was getting a sequel. Some gameplay GIFs popped up online, before any official video and I was not a fan - the original was a 2D game and it just seemed like an odd choice. It just did not seem like a good mix. My hype for the game was replaced with apprehension and I forgot about it.Fortunately, my concerns were gone after they released some gameplay and launched the game. I ended up buying it at launch and got an extra copy to gift to a buddy for free. doe not really have a story, but I feel like it does not need one. You get some very basic cutscenes and exposition, but you are swiftly thrown into a very enjoyable gameplay loop.Gameplay is amazing.You can pick a single survivor when you start out but you quickly unlock many others. Each survivor has a specific playstyle, with strengths and weaknesses - mobility, utility, damage, defensive capabilities, etc. They are very different and fun to experiment with. While some are not as useful unless you find very specific upgrades, they are all entertaining to use.You get money per kill and can buy/find items to increase your stats and get new passive effects. Most item drops are random and their sheer number is outstanding. It takes a while to memorize what each item does, but once you get familiarized with most of them, you know which ones to pick when presented a choice or which one to leave behind because it is not worth the price or is better for a teammate. Item effects range from increasing your attack speed to turning you invisible for a few seconds upon taking heavy damage. Pretty much every basic videogame passive is included - mobility, attack speed, passive healing, life leech, critical chance, etc.Items also have rarities; white being the most common items and red being the rarest. Your goal in each level is to find a teleporter that summons a boss. After defeating said boss and charging up the teleporter, you can move onto the next level. You can take as long as you'd like in a single level, unlocking all chests and finding all secrets, however, the game gets progressively harder the longer you take, so there is a risk vs reward factor going on. You might unlock more items and be more powerful, but if you take too much time the enemies will eventually overpower you no matter what.This leads me to the only factor that frustrated me and my friends while playing. The game is perfectly balanced at first and, after extended periods, enemies become super spongy and take ages to kill. They also deal insane amounts of damage that will often kill you before you can react. While enemy 1-hit kills are not possible (apart from an enemy or two which are very easy to avoid), you can get spammed by high-damage projectiles so quickly you cannot possibly react. So basically, you do not die instantly or in a single hit, but you die because you got hit twice in less than half a second from something that just spawned in. A way to avoid this is to keep moving and never really standing still, but some survivors are not as mobile and do not feature any escape mechanism. It certainly does not ruin the game but it is frustrating, as you do not get any more items until you respawn (at the beginning of the next level, if someone survived).My friends and I still hate some of the enemies because they are simply too cheap - Elder Lemurians, Mini Mushrums and Malachite Elites can f*** right off.With that small detour out of the way, let's get back to the good stuff!If you complete a few runs, you will be able to activate artifacts before you start a playthrough - these are modifiers that can completely change your session. While there are too many to name, I can give you a few examples - artifact of command allows you to pick your items, while the artifact of swarms doubles monster spawns and halves their HP. These grant a bit more variety to an already extensive and highly replayable game.Graphically,  has a strong art-direction. The graphics do not look amazing but the presentation is solid, colors are vibrant and character design is interesting. After the first few minutes there is always a lot of things on-screen - enemies, projectiles and particle effects. It gets crowded and sometimes there are frame dips because of it. Sound is up next.I love the soundtrack - it reminds me of synthwave and it fits the game's vibe perfectly.Sound effects are good but nothing to write home about.The game is still getting major updates semi-regularly - which is pretty epic. Some of the items used to be downright useless and, after some tweaks, the devs made them a bit more viable. There are still some that need some upgrades but fingers crossed we get a new update soon!Certainly enjoyable on your own but an amazing experience with friends. Random lobbies are a bit... frustrating - people just hoard everything and do not share items (played it twice with randoms and just gave up). After extended periods of gameplay, over a week or two, you will most likely get really bored of it and only come back to it a few months later - the gameplay loop is always the same, no matter which character you pick. You find items, activate the teleporter and defeat the boss. It gets a bit repetitive no matter how many items or characters you have.Easy to recommend - plenty of hours of content.Final score: 8.5 out of 10.If you enjoyed this review, please consider joining my  and following my  on Steam.

_childDocuments_.review: I confess that I did not like the previous version - Risk of Rain. I am not good at roguelike games and I just couldn't go far with that 2D game. Soon I lost interest despite the fact that almost everyone who plays that 2D game loves that game.Fast forward to Risk of Rain 2. I am a fan of third person shooter. And the co-op option is good. I am still not good at roguelike games. At least, now I get to play with my wife. So far we have a lot of fun with it. RoR2 certainly has exceeded my initial expectation. Pros and considerations of this early access version as follows.Pros===+ Very fluid game play. Camera setting is perfect. Mouse and keyboard setup is very responsive. I have played many third person shooter games. RoR2 is among the best when it comes to control and camera.+ Very colorful. Love the cartoon-ish backdrop.+ Boss fights are epic.+ Very fun when co-op. The difficulty does escalate. There is a constant sense of urgency.+ Very much the same game design as RoR. While I am not a fan of RoR, I must admit that the game design is very good. There are different loots, different buffs, turrets / healing bots etc., different maps that make the game unique for each round of play through.+ There is an easy difficulty for more casual players.Considerations============- If you are not good at roguelike games (like me), you would probably get frustrated with the default difficulty setting. I don't think it is a game whereby you can get better as you go (e.g. past success doesn't get carried to the future games). There is a limit to what you can do with experience and awareness.- I wish there is a slider to adjust difficulty setting. I find that easy mode is too easy when a game can last like an hour. But the standard mode is too hard (yet to pass the first round). This means the fun part for the easy mode only kicks in after 45 mins of game play while the standard difficulty is just way too frustrating.- There is no revive. At least I don't seem to be able to find one. If your partner and you have a difference in terms of skill or in terms of loot progression, one of you may end up in spectator mode after his/her character dies. That is not really that fun after a while. There should be a way to revive because watching someone plays is just not as fun as playing the game with someone. Or some ways for spectators to participate in the game.- Teleport is a small device in the map that spawns the stage boss. It also helps to clear a stage and progress to the next map. The goal is to find the teleport. The challenge is that it is rather tiny and is not that easy to find, especially in a 3D world. In some maps, it may take a long time to keep circling the area and still not finding it. With experience, it does make it easier. Still, some maps are just harder than others (I guess one could say this is good design as this should give you a more varied experience).Game Video=========For those who are interested to see how this game plays like for two newbies to this game / genre, this are 2 videos for you!

_childDocuments_.review: While watching Gearbox PAX East 2019, I wasn't expecting to encounter a game that would draw my attention more than the game everyone tuned in for. An amazing game that can have its already fantastic gameplay loop quadruple in value with friends (you know, as long as you coordinate slightly). The satisfaction of somehow winning with the items you are dealt will never leave me. Main menu Logbooks provide the subtle and not-so-subtle lore that exists. Deciding to piece things together rewards you with the context that is very important to me. (I'm a sucker for juicy lore).Top that off with the beautiful music and great playable survivors and I could just gush about this game for hours.In conclusion, Risk of Rain 2 is the game that I will always recommend to someone looking for something to play.I'm looking forward to the next expansion and beyond.

_childDocuments_.review: , like its predecessor, is a roguelite. It is also a 3D 3rd person shooter, a drastic change from the original game, which was a 2D action platformer. However, the game feels true to the original and exceeds it in every way. The gameplay remains immensely satisfying , the new art direction is gorgeous, and the music is as killer as ever from the composer Chris Christolodou, who continues to work with the game’s developers, Hopoo Games. The core gameplay loop of  consists of the player spawning into the stage as a chosen survivor. They can then explore the map, killing monsters for money, which can be used to buy various things including chests that drop random items, drones that fight for you, and shrines that have different effects. After the player has powered up, they need to interact with the Teleporter, which spawns a boss enemy and a large wave of monsters that need to be defeated before continuing onto the next stage, where the process repeats. Dying at any point in this process is a permanent death, and while you keep any unlocks, you will have to restart from the beginning the next time you decide to go for a run. An important part of , much like for its predecessor, is time. The longer you survive in a run, the more difficult it becomes. While time passing doesn’t have such a drastic effect as it does in the first entry, if you fail to pace yourself in completing stages, you will find yourself being unable to defeat monsters as fast as you would want to, to the point where the swarms will eventually overwhelm you. The importance of time brings about a constant stress to move forward, preventing the player from staying on one stage for too long and becoming too powerful. As of writing this review,  has 11 survivors, each with numerous unlockable skills that change the gameplay drastically. These 11 survivors , combined with those skills, add a lot of variety to the initial starting game state, which is extremely nice for a roguelite, where a lack of variety would lead to the game becoming stale. However, the survivors do not contribute to the most of the run variety -- the biggest contributor would be the items.  has a much smaller array of items  compared to other games in the genre, such as  and . However, the lack of items is not a detriment to the game, as these items interact with each other in deep and unique ways. While other roguelites often have situations where there are completely dead items, such as  with its superfluous amount of bean items that vary in quality, almost every item in  is useful. Many items activate upon hitting a monster, such as the Ukelele . These on-hit effects can trigger other on-hit effects, leading to a cascade of visual eye-candy that decimates the oncoming swarms of monsters as the items synergize. Item synergy is also intuitive -- If you think an item will work with another item, it probably will! This makes collecting items a blast, as every run will be unique at least in some way, even if you decided to play the same survivor over and over.  also offers a variety of goals to strive towards in the form of challenges. These challenges unlock more items, characters, and several other unlocks. These can range from trivial to complete to pretty difficult. Since these challenges have parity with the game’s Steam achievements, it makes achievement hunting for 100% completion a blast. The combat in  is very fun. Since there is so much variety with survivors, their skills and the items they get, each run is played differently. For some runs, you may need to stay back, dodge oncoming fire and whittle down enemies with your spray of bullets that release a cascade of electric mayhem -- other runs will require you to get into the thick of it and clobber enemies at a vicious speed with your giant explosive gauntlets. If the playstyle of one survivor doesn’t match your tastes, another one probably will. When compared to the first game, it’s clear that  certainly took some liberties. The most obvious is that this game is 3D, unlike the 2D original. While this was a risky choice that I wasn’t sure about going into this game, Hopoo Games did an excellent job of transforming the 2D game into a 3D one that feels so true to the original while still being its own thing. Exploring the stages is fun, and the increased verticality combined with better momentum physics introduced in this game lends itself to more enjoyable movement compared to the oddly clicky feeling of the original . It’s surprising going back to  and seeing how much Hopoo took from it and expanded it in the sequel in such a well-executed manner. Visually,  is gorgeous with a cel-shaded style that makes it feel like the first game while still having its own style. Even though long runs can devolve into utter chaos with miasmas of particle effects everywhere and massive swarms of enemies, the game runs very well. I rarely drop below 60 FPS on my rig, though sometimes the FPS can drop to 30 or even 20 during especially chaotic moments. However, the game usually recovers really quickly, within seconds, and keeps chugging along like nothing happened. Chris Christodolou did as excellent a job with this game's soundtrack as he did with the first title. Both soundtracks are incredible. ’s best tracks use grand solos to convey a sense of power and scale that is very befitting of the game’s experience, especially in the final location and boss encounter. Video game music should really use solos more; it adds a lot to the experience. Audio in general is very well done -- there are many sound cues that help the player determine which enemies are around them at any time. This helps alleviate problems where you don’t realize an enemy has spawned behind you, as almost every enemy has a unique sound effect as they spawn. The hit sounds are also very satisfying, especially for items that trigger on-hit, such as the Ukelele mentioned earlier. Overall, the presentation of  is top-notch.  ★★★★★ is an indie game that does something that many major, AAA titles fail to do -- make a sequel that expands and surpasses the original in almost every way.  does a fantastic job of transforming the 2D experience into a 3D one that feels different, though also the same. The gameplay loop is satisfying and doesn’t get stale after hundreds of hours of gameplay. I’ve practically done everything the game has to offer, and yet I still want to play more. The graphics and the audio are also both incredible.  is truly a gem, and you should absolutely give it a try.

_childDocuments_.review: Risk of Rain 2 is a true testament as to what could be achieved by migrating an already well-polished and hard as balls game from a platformer into 3D.Being a direct sequel to the story and mechanics of the original Risk of Rain (which recently got a remaster, RoR Returns, highly recommended, too!), it is a roguelite shooter set on the surface of a fictional planet of Petrichor V, where up to four (the game supports cross-network online co-op, more on that later) from a pool of eleven crash survivors attempt to traverse four deadly zones in order to get to the planet's moon, where a rescue ship would allow them to go back to the safety of space.The gameplay loop is simple, but immensely satisfying. Each survivor gets four skills: regular attack, secondary one, mobility skill, and a special, all complimented with a singular slot for additional equipment. Over the course of the game, killing monsters earns money which can be utilized to open chests scattered across the semi-randomized environments. Said chests contain items that enhance the surivors' basic abilities, such as attack speed, movement speed or ability cooldowns. Additionally, some items, such as will-o'-the-wisp or the ukulele allow single-target attacks to attack multiple enemies via post-mortem explosion or arcing eletric shocks. As such, earning gear is necessary for progression, which is done by finding and activating a teleporter hidden away somewhere on each stage, noticeable by floating red particles in the air.Activating the teleporter doesn't mean a character is instantly transported to the next environment, though, as it needs to be charged beforehand. The shockwave emitted by the teleporter activation summons a boss monster which needs to be taken care of in order to allow the device to fully charge. At the same time, the enemy spawn rate is increased dramatically, which, coupled with the limited area that the player has to stay in for the teleporter to charge provides a stimulating, nail-biting experience to both fresh and experienced players alike.Another important factor of the game is the difficulty. In the menu, the player can choose one of three base difficulty levels - drizzle (easy), rainstorm (regular) and monsoon (v. hard). All those affect spawn rates, player health recovery speed, and difficulty ramp-up speed, which brings us to another gameplay loop element that leads to the breakneck pace of the game: the timer.As the timer ticks up, enemies gain experience levels, their spawn rates increase and their damage output rises.  This forces the players to make their way as fast as they can, as lingering on a single level can make the difference between having to defeat a single boss enemy or three of them during a single teleporter event.The game's fun factor rises immensely with the addition of four-player co-op. The game is adjusted accordingly, spawning more chests and enemies the more players are on the server. Additionally, the game supports cross-network play (unfortunately no cross-platform), meaning Steam players can join in on the fun with their Epic games acquaintances. It needs to be said that this feature is opt-in: having cross-network disabled routes the gameplay through the steam relays, while with the option enabled, Epic Online Services are used instead, and the implementation of Epic services in this particular game is... shoddy, at best. With crossplay enabled, expect frequent disconnects and server crashes that rise in frequency as the game progresses, none of which happen when using Steam Networking.Risk of Rain 2's performance is nothing to scoff at, lending itself in no small part due to the minimalistic graphic design, but also the the optimization made by Hopoo Games and Gearbox Software, who now owns the game and provides support for it. It is not without issues, however. In later stages, or after looping the game a few times the enemy AI count can, may, and will bring even the most powerful machines to their knees. With my rig, an Intel i7-9700K and an RTX 2070, having a run last more than 100 minutes brings the frame count to a movie-like 24 fps. This is most likely caused by a QA oversight, as the enemy stat changes are calculated each rendered frame, proving to be a bottleneck for the engine more than the device it's running on. In normal gameplay scenario, even on a mid-spec device like a Steam Deck, the late-game performance is quite acceptable, as, at that point, it is not the player who will be doing the most damage to the enemies around them.The game is constantly developed, too - as of the time writing this review, Gearbox offers a DLC pack to this game, Survivors of the Void. This expansion adds new environments, two new survivors, entirely new gamemode and new "void-corrupted" items, which provide new twists to an already established formula of the game. Currently, another expansion, Seekers of the Storm, is announced and in active development, which I, personally, am looking forward to.All in all, Risk of Rain 2 is an immensely satisfying experience with tons of replay value. If you're looking for a great roguelite to play with up to three friends, great community support with tons of gameplay mods and ongoing development worthy of the "Steam Labor of Love" award (for real this time), don't wait and hit that "purchase" button. It's highly likely you won't be disappointed in the slightest.

_childDocuments_.review: I went into this game having practically 0 experience or knowledge of how the first one played, only knowing it had a garnered a great amount of positive reviews and a dedicated fanbase. I knew a lot of people were hesitant about the new one going into 3D and since I had no idea how the first one really played, didn't have an opinion on it. It wasn't until the game's surprise Early Access release that I began to look it because of all the glowing reviews. I honestly wasn't sold completely yet, while it didn't look bad by any means, the game play footage wasn't really doing much for me and I already had a huge backlog of games to work on.Well, I am ever so thankful that a good Steam buddy bought me this game because ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, is it some of the most sincerely fun games I've played in the last couple years. Everything about it feels so smooth and well thought out, which is insane giving how early in it's release we are. The gameplay loop is satisfying and leaves so much room for replaybility because of the sheer amount of items and weapons at your disposal, not to mention the ability to stack them all. The game developers practically encourage you to be an overpowered unstoppable killing machine, but thanks to an innovative and dynamic difficulty mechanic, the game keeps you on your feet while still making you feel like your making progress. The worst thing I have to say about the game are things that the developers have already acknowledged, such as some minor networking issues that cause disconnects occasionally and the somewhat lacking of variety of levels/biodomes, which are currently being worked on. Lacking in content in some ways is pretty expected from a newly released early access game so that's fine. I honestly can't recommend this enough, THIS is how Early Access games should be done. A perfect example of using the platform to both the advantage of the consumer and the developers. I cannot wait for more content and patches to make this already great experience an even better one. +Addictive gameplay loop.+Smooth and slick artstyle+Nice background music and satisfying sound effects+Insane amounts of replaybility thanks to vast amount of items and classes to play.-Some networking issues cause disconnects midgame-Crazy amount of stuff stacking in later game can cause some UI issues (being able to tab to see allies health bars would be ACE)-Lacking variety in stages. (as one would assume though in early access)9/10

_childDocuments_.review: This is coming from a place of love. As someone who's put hundreds of hours into the game, and purchased it for others to let them enjoy it. I love this game dearly. But Gearbox dropped the ball with their latest DLC + Patch.With bugs ranging from missing sounds, to epilepsy-inducing visual bugs, to breaking nearly (if not every) character in one way or another, to immortal bosses, to deleting people's save data, the game has become practically unplayable.I'm not able to confirm this particular detail one way or another, but people are saying it feels like the PC version was removed, and replaced with a 'patched' version of the console version. Which, for those who are in the know, know just how awful that is.The content the DLC promised to bring itself isn't the issue, mind you. It all looks wonderful, and seems very fun. But that is not worth completely (and potentially permanently) destroying one of my favorite games of all time. I'm afraid that due to the nature of the content this update came with, that being a paid DLC, Gearbox may not be able to make this right. Somehow I don't see them delisting the DLC and refunding it, before proceeding to revert the game back to the version it was in before the patch. But that would be the best way forward. Doing this, apologizing to the playerbase, and going back to square one and developing the DLC again properly would be the best way Gearbox could approach this.The only real hope we have for this to happen is to make ourselves heard. For those that already have the game, make it heard through your reviews, discouraging new folks from buying the game. Refund the DLC if you bought it. For those that have not yet purchased ROR2, please don't. DO NOT buy the game in its current state. It's in shambles.For obvious reasons, I'll change this review if Gearbox fixes things. Because I love this game, and I want people to be able to enjoy it as much as I have. But right now, that's simply not possible.

_childDocuments_.review: Risk Of Rain 2, while still in development is a perfectly functional sequel to the 2D platformer of it's predecessor. This game functions as a rogue like with mobs that spawn in randomly and grow stronger over time. As the raising difficulty climbs you will need to grow stronger as well. Defeating monsters drop currency as well as experience to level up. With the coins you collect you will have treasure scattered throughout the map to find random items to aid in your fight to survive. Modifications to your abilities, strength, speed, etc... can keep you going longer and longer.      In the base game, there was an end game boss you could achieve, however, right now in RO2 it is endless survival. I've had countless hours of fun with friends online in this game and would recommend it to anyone curious.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been looping the OSTs for Risk of Rain for a decade now. In the game, computer, phone, and in my mind when I turn in to sleep every night. But what is sleep but another moment in which to appreciate the subtle tones of "Petrichor V" or the gradual buildup in "Nocturnal Emission".There's two interactive music videos (Risk of Rain and Risk of Rain 2) that offer up nice visuals to look at while listening to Chris Christodoulou's immaculate work. They even offer the option for co-op listening sessions with your friends. We use this time to discuss our favorite songs, especially when the game is kind enough to slow down to where we don't have to interact as much in later stages. While we lament the visualizer outputting a frame every other second, it does allow us to appreciate the music that much more.I sometimes wonder what a world without Risk of Rain would be like. But not for too long, after all "The Face of the Deep" is next in the queue and my air sax needs a bit of polish.

_childDocuments_.review: Risk of Rain 2 is the sequel to one of my favourite rougelikes: Risk of RainThe core mechanics are the same, with changes to fit the translation to 3D. You spawn with no starting equipment, and buy your items as you go along. The items are randomised, selected from a pool.The Lore is rather light currently, but there is a goldmine to be explored, with the actual gameplay providing the diorama which is backed up by the Logbook.The premise for this game is the freight ship 'The Contact Light' has crashed on an unknown planet, with it's cargo being spewed all over the planets surface. You start as The Commando, one of the survivors who was on the ship, and your main goal is to try and escape the planet. Along the way you will rescue other survivors, gain items, and explore the many areas of this planet.The Logbook is your main source of Lore (and mechanical knowledge) for the game. When you pick up an item, you find the shipping details for it as well. This provides you with some context as to what the item is, and how it came to be on the Contact Light, and as such the planet. Some items will have rather amusing logs, some that are adorable, and some that will just break your heart. It's a rather good way of giving you a story for each individual item.This game is addictive. Whether you had a good run that ended by obliterating yourself from existence, or a bad run that saw you killed in the second level, you will always find yourself thinking "Maybe just one more".The items are infinitely stackable. This means you can have insane combos, where opening a chest releases a barrage of fireworks that will seek out an enemy, hitting them and causing lightning to chain between nearby enemies, killing them and releasing a flock of spectral knives, which themselves in turn seek out enemies, exploding for each hit which chains lightning and kills them releasing more knives causing an explosion of fire...You will reach a point in the game, where you obtain THAT run, the insanely overpowered one, or the one with the most insane synergy, or the absurd amount of gold.This game is just . I nagged some of my friends to get this game. They agreed to get it, somewhat reluctantly, and within about, an hour they were saying "yeah this game is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ fun".You will love playing this game, and before long, most of your runs will end, not with death, but wi-

_childDocuments_.review: One Shot Protection, abbreviated OSP, is a hidden functionality in the game. No where in-game is it ever mentioned that this will likely save your runs countless times. One shot protections is a very basic mechanic, and it can rather easily be deduced from its name what the intention behind it is.You cannot be one shot in this game, meaning you cannot be killed in a single instance of received damage, but you can be killed in a single attack. As an example, the Greater Wisp fires two projectiles leading to two different instances of damage. If you're only hit by one of them, you cannot be one shot, where as if you're hit by both of them, you can be killed by a single attack, whereas this is technically not a one shot.Being one shot would make for a dull experience, as evading every single attack is a tough challenge, even for a veteran. As difficulty increases with run time, every single enemy in the game would potentially be able to one shot you after enough playtime, but luckily OSP is here to save you from the wrath of the planet.

_childDocuments_.review: Nominated for Best with Friends 2020Risk of Rain 2 is an amazing game that makes the transition from 2D into 3D astonishingly well. While it won't retain every character and item from the first game, it uses this opportunity to introduce new ones, while also keeping a majority of those which can take advantage of the 3D space and mechanics it allows for.The game still retains the level of difficulty the first is known for, while still allowing for you or your friends to absolutely break it when the opportunity arises. With over 100 items, 14 unique bosses, 10 characters, 11 "main" worlds, ,  and a handful of unique monsters, you'll certainly see some things repeat, but the runs will almost always end up different each time unless you try to force a specific build with a specific character.The Artifact system introduced during the early access hasn't been expanded upon since it's initial addition, but they allow you to completely change, break, or heavily increase the difficulty of your runs. I wouldn't be surprised if there are future Artifacts added to further change up how the game can be played.I've yet to try the multiplayer system again since 1.0, but from what I've seen, it's far better than  the original system, as you can now choose or setup servers in a browser system. However, I would still assume item "stealing," lobbies being ended early by the leader leaving, and lack of general team work in a random lobby, will still exist.Each character has their own unique skill set, and possible builds which can entirely take advantage of their skills or abilities, to break the game and make it very easy, however, with that said, the game will still find a way to eventually kill you if you don't pay attention, even if you become god-like (Some builds can avoid that entirely though).In terms of bugs/crashing/performance, I've not experienced anything aside from some decent frame drops (From ~140-200, down to ~15-30) when looking at massive groups of enemies/effects going off (Est  ~40-60+). However, this isn't very common if you're able to keep up with killing them all.There are some disappointments however upon release, that will hopefully be changed in future updates though. During the Early Access, a handful of abilities were still "In Development," and most probably would assume they'd be added in 1.0, however, no new abilities have been added, nor does there seem to be any public word as to why. I would like to hope that they will still be implemented at some point, since it does limit some characters to only have one ability for a skill slot.While there are certainly a handful of amazing worlds, there is only 2 possible variants per each stage (with their few sub-variants, with some exceptions to a couple worlds), I would like to hopefully see it be expanded to at least 3 or more in the future to further randomize runs.The final boss is very good, however, the stage leading up to it does seem very lack luster, and does possibly have some soft-locking for a few characters if you lack certain mobility items. I'm not sure how much testing or feedback was given for it, but I'd like to hopefully see this looked at and tweaked within a few weeks.Artificer (One of the characters you can unlock) still seems to be the worst & weakest out of them all. The concept is great, and she can certainly do well when played with a team, but by herself, the cool-down on her attacks really limits her and can put you in situations where you're just waiting to kill things unless you have very high damage, or a handful of charge increase items. I would like to hopefully see her tweaked, buffed, or possibly reworked. I do admit however, I could possibly just be missing some play-style to her that actually makes her fine to use.The following is just a simple suggestion I do have for the game;I would like to hopefully see more skin-variants for each character, as currently there is only the base skin, and a second skin for doing a specific task. A skin for beating the game as X character would be interesting to see implemented, and be another reason to continue playing the game as each character.Overall, I do highly recommend Risk of Rain 2, and I assure you, if you love rouge-likes, the first game, or just the game play of this alone, you should get it, and if you've got friends who can also play, I suggest grouping together as it can be even harder and more chaotic.

_childDocuments_.review: Holy Cow. Never have I bought a game in Early Access that i've been so impressed by in it's "Released as is" state.I picked up the game Immediately because I had played the previous Risk of Rain and knew that any new form of that would be enjoyable even if it wasn't quite polished yet, and the 2 pack was available so, hey, that was the prime time to do it.After playing for a day I decided to pick up ANOTHER 2 pack for two of my friends, because I liked it so much. It is unexpectedly polished and working quite well for being Early Access!Okay, let's throttle off the Praise and actually give you an idea what you are getting into with this game.So, if you have already played the first game this part is mostly pointless to read, but to anyone new to Risk of Rain, it works like this:You spawn into a map, and there are chests and interactables scattered around the map to pick up. Most of it is purchased with gold that you earn killing the enemies that spawn gradually here and there. Everything you pick up collects as passive bonuses. These are all basic things you see in most roguelikes. Area transitions involved activating a Teleporter that spawns a boss and several small minions to challenge you before you make it to the next area, and staying in that teleporter's radius (visual AoE, you need to be near it to charge it). It won't finish charging and enemies will keep spawning while the boss is alive.Here's where things really twist: As you play, you have a timer and a Difficulty Gauge underneath. The longer you survive in Risk of Rain, the higher the difficulty gets. Each rise in difficulty means more abundant enemies, tougher enemies, and higher chances to encounter "Elite" monsters that deal more damage and have special properties (As of now there are Fire, Ice, and Lightning). This means that as you keep going and grab more things in an attempt to grow as powerful as you can, you are also constantly facing bigger and tougher swarms of enemies popping up and trying to end you. This means it's a race to get as many items as you can find, activate the portal, kill the boss, and move on as far as you can go, before you inevitably get completely swarmed by 7-8 Elite Golems that all have their laser sights on you at once.This make the game extremely addictive in nature and incredibly fun to play with your friends. Most of what was in the original 2D Risk of Rain has been implemented while remaining true to it's origin, but now in 3D, with many extra things added to spice things up.Another important note I think anyone considering this game should know is the Devs are extremely in touch with their community at this time, and through both their Risk of Rain 2 Discord channel and their forums are actually actively looking over observations and suggestions from their player base. This review is being typed out right after their latest patch, build #3731106. Looking over this patch, a majority of it is changes made either by community suggestion or something reported by them. This gives me a lot of hope for the future of the game so far, and I really appreciate this kind of relationship with Developers. Thank you for your hard work thus far, Hopoo!So, if you haven't guess it by now I highly recommend this game to anyone (who enjoys surviving until they get ridiculously overwhelmed and die horribly to a Kamekaze Elite Jellyfish swarm, like me).

_childDocuments_.review: At the time of writing this, the large-scale DLC for this game is only about a week and a half away, and I wanted to post this in order to convince people I know to buy this thing, because I'll tell you, it's worth it. This is the highly-acclaimed sequel to hit indie game Risk of Rain, which has improved over the original in almost every aspect. I'm going to start off by saying that this is likely my most favorite game on Steam right now, so expect about 0% bias in this review.If you're unaware as to what the gameplay of this game is like, it's essentially a multiplayer 3D survival 3rd-person shooter (or melee even) rougelike game and, yeah, that's a beautiful mouthful of words right there. Upon picking a class to play as (more on that later), you crash onto an alien planet and it's up to you and your friends to stay alive from there while every creature in sight tries to kill you. The more you kill, the more money you get, and you use that to open loot boxes scattered around the area which provide you with a random item. Items basically give you passive buffs or abilities which make your character stronger the more you have, so the goal is to get as many as you can before the timer at the top of the screen gradually increases the difficulty. There are several types of enemies and items, but, again, I'll touch on that later on. You'll spawn into a randomly picked stage and to get to the next one, you need to locate a teleporter, activate it, fight a boss, and then proceed. You do this until you get to stage 5, where you can either head to the final boss or choose to loop through another 5 stages to get even more buffs. There are currently 3 ways to end your run, those being death, defeating the final boss, or mysteriously vanishing in a way I won't spoil.The first thing that really stood out to me about this game was the fact that you can stack any item in the game (save for special activation items) theoretically an infinite amount of times. Examples of such include having 100 double jumps or 100% critical strike chance. Not only that, but each item is pretty fun, unique, and game-changing in its own right. There's essentially an item for anything and countless amounts of character builds and synergies are possible. Plus, the developers are continuing to add more and more of them into the game. There are different tiers of items you can find, and they are ranked by rarity. Common items are pretty basic in effect and really just change one stat or effect one happenstance, while uncommon items focus more on synergy with other items and change your playstyle a little more. Then there are legendary items which are all just kind of broken and overpowered and will synergize strongly with other items. Other tiers exist as well, which include items from bosses that give you a bit of their power, equipment items which function as a 5th skill, lunar items which are weird because they are bought from a special shop with a special currency and provide both a strong buff and debuff so I don't wanna go into all that, and more to come.Arguably the most exciting part of this game are the survivor classes. There are a total of eleven (soon to be thirteen) classes in this game and all of them play in their own way. Each one is so very different and can range from a spaceman with guns to a robot to a lightsaber ninja to a poisonous dog. It's good to set out with several different classes at once in multiplayer so that everyone can support each other in their own unique way. Every single character is fun to play and all of them are functionally and aesthetically cool (likely objectively). You can really pick anybody to find a style for you. Even more variety can be found in unlockable alternate skills (which you only have 4 types of) that change how you can play this game even more, as well as what item build you go with.A few other things to touch on before I wrap things up. There are loads of enemy types and bosses, which I'd say are all never really redundant, along with the possibility for stronger versions to spawn. The stages are pretty nice, especially their individual vibes, although some are simpler to navigate and fight in than others. Several secrets and easter eggs are scattered throughout levels, items, or actions you take which can add a bit of spice to your runs. If you're into lore or story in any way, the game doesn't necessarily feed it to you, however you may find a good amount of that in log entries and such which you find across playing the game. Lastly, the OST in this game is absolutely S+++ tier, my man Chris Christodoulou is making music for the wrong evolutionary stage of humans on this planet.There are some more features in this game, and even more coming in the future, but I don't really feel the need to touch on them here. Plus, there are just several factors and things that go into runs, which make each one stand out on its own from the rest of them. This game is so damn amazing. I only want to play it more and I'm never going to grow tired of it. It gives you that high-action, adrenaline-pumping, occasionally funny, absolutely absurd, groovy, and ingenious kind of gameplay you need to make you feel like a certified god gamer, if you're into that sort of thing. Please buy it and play it with your friends, you will all have so much fun.Editing this review because I nominated this game for the 2022 Labor of Love Steam Award :)Doing it again for 2023 even though there are new devs :/Here in 2024, yes Gearbox kinda fumbled with the new DLC, but the sheer fact that they're listening to the community and actively trying to improve on it still has me nominating this game for Labor of Love

_childDocuments_.review: First off: I love RoR2! I've played hundreds of hours. If you haven't played it, buy the base game, right now!!! The reviews used to be overwhelmingly positive, until the new DLC tanked it. The base game deserves a high rating. Survivors of the Void DLC is also pretty good, and adds a fair amount of fun content. I recommend it as well. BUT....DO NOT BUY Seekers of the Storm DLC. Yes, they fixed some of the bugs that were glaringly apparent at launch, but it's still completely under-cooked and uninspired. First, let's talk about the price. $15 is insane for an expansion of a handful of maps, 3 half-baked playable characters, and however many items (17 I think), when the base games is around $25 or less.  You aren't getting anywhere near double the content of the base game, yet they're asking you to pay more than half of the base game cost. The new maps are just okay, but probably the best part of the DLC. A couple of them are well designed and fun, and a couple are the opposite. The new characters feel like modded characters. Modded characters aren't polished, many of them are still fun as hell to play, but they all have one thing in common that makes the lack of polish acceptable; the're FREE!!!!!!!!!    The new characters are severely lacking in creativity and polish. Worse than that, they aren't really unique. They all kind of feel like an amalgamation of already existing characters, but not in a fun way. I found them boring. For me, the worst part of the DLC is the new items. They aren't fun. Most of them are defensive, so you almost don't even notice their effects. They don't make you feel more powerful when you get them. Some of them are just objectively pointless. For example: Knockback Fin. Causes enemies to pop up in the air like 5 feet when hit. What could possibly be the purpose of this? If anything, it's a hindrance. More often than not, an enemy is launched and then you miss them with subsequent shots. Dumb. I find myself avoiding almost all of the new items. Again, there are a ton of mods for items if you want to spice things up, but for FREE. To be clear; I don't mind paying for content. I want to support games that I spend a lot of time playing. But, nobody wants to be taken advantage of, and that's what this feels like. It feels like they leveraged the community's love for the game to price gouge and put out a product that would take just long enough to realize how bad it is that you won't be able to refund it. You'll spend 2 hours hoping that there's more, just to find out it's too late, and you're a sucker. I see myself as one of RoR2's biggest fans. I've loved it since early access, and I still do. Corporate greed has just gotten the better of the new DLC. Yes, Gearbox released a statement promising to make it right, but don't give them your money until they deliver. They've done literally the bare minimum so far, which is fix stuff that shouldn't have been released in the first place. The sell now, fix later model has got to stop. It's BS. I'm tired of it. You're tired of it. You're going to see a lot of reviews saying to cut the devs a break and it's going to get better. I'll cut the devs a break when they give us $15 of content. Right now, I see it only as a cash grab. I will change my review to positive if/when the devs deliver on their promises.
