_childDocuments_.review: Read more of my short essays on video games at Time always moves forward whether you like it or not. In the blink of an eye, the present becomes the past and the future becomes the present. Every moment spent standing still is a moment not spent moving forward. We've all been standing still for far too long, until we can move around again, let me tell you about a game where you won't be able to stop moving.Risk of Rain 2 is a game that forces you to come to terms with the passage of time. Each decision you make has to be evaluated against the time it'll take to follow through with it as well as the expected value of the rewards you'll get.Risk of Rain 2 asks you to be quick on your feet and to think strategically, by working with what you're given and making the best of it. The core gameplay loop involves killing monsters, gathering items which make you stronger, activating the randomly placed teleporter on the level, triggering a boss fight and finally teleporting to the next level where it starts all over again.Imagine if you took a dozens of hours long Diablo-like game and condensed that entire experience into tight forty five minute runs of pure third person shooter action; that's what Risk of Rain 2 feels like.Playing well means getting as many items as possible as fast as you can because as time passes, enemies get stronger and more of them start showing up. Each level is randomly populated with chests, containing items, that you can open with the money you gain by killing enemies.Risk of Rain 2 requires you to use your big brain as much as your quick hands. Although, you have to rely on your intuition more often than not because of how fluid and random number generator dependent many of its systems are.Should I stay and gather more loot or travel to the next level? There's rarely a right answer to this question, and it's a question the game keeps asking you, forcing you to make risk vs. reward choices constantly and having you face the consequences.Risk of Rain 2 makes this question even more difficult to answer by allowing you to play as one of the ten different characters who all play quite differently from one another. Each character has four basic abilities; these abilities can be swapped in and out with a few more abilities that you can unlock by tackling tough challenges. Although the game doesn't feature much player progression outside of each run, players can unlock characters and secondary abilities for the characters they already have through play.Yet another example of a risk vs. reward choice present in Risk of Rain 2 are the Scrappers and 3D Printers spread across the levels. Scrappers allow you to convert items into scrap, which have no tangible benefit on their own but can be used on 3D printers, each of which can build one kind of item. Through this process you can convert situationally crappy items into great items. This gives you some power to influence the random number generator, and strikes a good balance between throwing random items at you while giving you enough agency to manipulate what you get and turn it into what you want based on the items you already have.Figuring out which items you want is already hard, but imagine how difficult this gets when playing with other people. Although Risk of Rain 2 can be played alone, it really shines in multiplayer. The game makes you feel a constant sense of urgency, encouraging you and your friends to stick together, cooperate and move toward your common goal quickly. Sessions are short enough to be easy to fit into a busy schedule while being long enough to feel meaningful. The default difficulty is "just right", it's not too easy, it's not too hard; but if it isn't to your liking then you can tweak it. There's minimal player progression outside of a run and so players can play with each other no matter how much time they've put into the game.Even though playing in multiplayer is my preferred way of enjoying Risk of Rain 2, I should mention a few of its downsides. Players can't jump into the middle of a run and runs are long enough that this becomes more than just an annoyance. Also, dying in multiplayer is painful because you can miss out on loot which leads to you dying again and this negative feedback loop repeats itself over and over again.Despite these flaws, I prefer playing in multiplayer because the game doesn't seem to be built from the ground up to support my playstyle in singleplayer. For example, my favorite character is Loader. She's a melee brawler who swings around with her hook shot, unleashes gigantic punches and generates a barrier whenever she hits an enemy giving her a lot of survivability.Although, theoretically, she can handle any kind of enemy the game might throw at her. In practice, dealing with strong flying enemies or fireball spewing lizards by yourself is quite hard. I've found playing alone as Loader to be quite deflating unless I get some very specific items. Then again, playing in single player makes getting the items I need even more unlikely because there's less variety of loot and less of it. In multiplayer, I can play to her strengths while other players cover for her weaknesses. There's more loot to go around, so we're more likely to find the specific items I need (eg. Focus Crystal, Soldier's Syringe) to make Loader strong.Whether you're playing in singleplayer or multiplayer, Risk of Rain 2, for better or worse, keeps you engaged by never letting you know what to expect around the next corner or in the next chest. One could say that Risk of Rain 2's main game mechanic is the Skinner box.In a world where Skinner boxes in video games are mainly used to scam kids out of their parents' hard earned money, I'm not offended by Risk of Rain 2's use of the Skinner box. Unlike many of its AAA brethren, it's a cheap game with no microtransactions. I'm a "human being" twenty four hours a day, I don't feel bad for activating the primal part of my brain for a few hours here and there.That said, addiction is addiction, and so I wouldn't recommend Risk of Rain 2 to someone with an addictive personality or with a history of addiction of any kind. The cost of becoming "addicted" to games like Risk of Rain 2 might seem relatively low, compared to the alternatives, but as someone who dove out of the womb and immediately started smashing open chests in the original Diablo game, I can't help but wonder what my life would be like today if not for the Skinner box…Risk of Rain 2 is a great game, and a great sequel. It smooths away the rough edges of the original Risk of Rain, adds another dimension, literally, by making the game 3D instead of 2D and makes the game playable with friends online. I haven't gotten tired of listening to the electronic prog rock soundtrack yet which is surprising because I've spent dozens of hours in the game. And, I intend to spend many more hours playing Risk of Rain 2 as long as I've got people to play with.

_childDocuments_.review: Do you enjoy multiplayer co-op and/or singleplayer "player vs. game" experiences? This game is perfect for you, even if you think you're not good at FPS games and it is worth every penny. The totally insane over-the-top hectic action with explosions, rockets, and  while headbanging to  might make you forget you're even playing an FPS. On top of that, forgiving aiming mechanics and large enemies take the focus away from twitch shooting and puts it on character abilities and movement, where it belongs. The game developers are so confident in their core gameplay that they created a character that uses only a sword, and after playing for about 9 hours I believe that confidence was well placed. The game runs very smoothly even on limited hardware, the soundtrack is , and the controls are tight. The maps are fresh, large, and conducive to player exploration -- there are no invisible walls and you can get outside of most maps.Multiplayer is quick and easy compared to the port-forwarding nightmare of the first Risk of Rain. This game is essentially the same as the first Risk of Rain with some minor character, monster, and item tweaks and additions. That being said, adding the third dimension makes for a completely different game stylistically and mechanically, so you're still in for a new yet familiar experience.I cannot comment much about replayability because I need more hours in the game, but I imagine there is a maximum of 50 to 100 hours of fun time. It's still early and tough to tell, but again, those 50-100 hours is worth every penny they're charging, and it will still be one of the best experiences you've ever had playing a video game with friends.

_childDocuments_.review: the latest changes and the whole dlc situation is just upsetting. i havent really bothered writing a review before but now i feel like this is just the perfect occasion.first off, the dlc. i obviously can't point out any issues with the dlc because good ol gearbox decided that because of the country i reside in, whether i support the political decisions of the president or not, i shouldn't be allowed to own the dlc despite waiting for it for a really long time now and never even being informed that it would be restricted. the store page was, mind you, open for everyone before the dlc's actual release. the moment it got released however it became "not available in your region". that's fun.now, the patch. not getting to see the dlc would obviously feel a bit bad for me and everybody else who also was caught off guard by the restriction, but even if you don't get involved into the dlc you still get ♥♥♥♥ on by the changes to the base game. now it just overall feels worse to play. these are some of the oddest changes that i can't even really guess the reason for. obviously the first thing you notice is the bugs. the moment you join the game you'll be shown a "new" marker on the settings menu. yes, there are indeed new settings, but the new indicator never goes away. it's just always there. now when you start a run you may or may not immediately notice that some sounds are weirdly bugged and just sound off. seems to be random from my experience. the next thing i noticed is that now for some reason elite lesser wisps don't get stunned when you shoot them, which just makes them... not exactly fair to fight. they're (almost) a hitscan enemy so seeing an elite one just means that you'll consistently get status effects applied to you until it's dead no matter what you do. then when i started the teleporter event it definitely felt like there were quite a bit more enemies than usual, but that might just be me being rusty, i can't really tell. what i could tell however is that for some odd reason the stone titans that spawned weren't flashing red when they took damage, and better yet, one of them was *permanently* glowing red like it was taking damage. i died there, and not even to the bosses.speaking of death, the new damage indicator is absolutely horrible. not only is it off by default, which means you don't get ANY feedback for taking damage, but even the one you do get when you turn it on is just not good. at all. it's supposed to be "directional", but it doesn't update its position when you turn so it could actually mislead you if you happen to be turning as you take damage. not only that, but it's also horrible at representing how much damage you actually took. taking 25% of your max health of damage looks pretty much the same as taking something like 90%, so you need to have a staring contest with your healthbar to even determine whether you need to be worrying about health at the moment (not to mention that fall damage gives no feedback AT ALL). but even that won't really help because now there's some sort of cosmetic change to healing/taking damage that makes the healthbar not instantly snap to the amount of health you have, but rather smoothly lower/rise to that point. while a similar effect was there before as well, it used to take like a tenth of a second. now it can take 3. the healthbar feels really unresponsive and it is impossible to just tell how much health you have by looking at the healthbar after taking damage/healing, you need to specifically read the number on it. not great for a fast-paced game.the item-related changes are weird as well. for some reason multishop items no longer have outlines, which just makes them look bland and sometimes even makes it harder to tell what item it actually is. and since the same multishop system applies to shipping request forms you can no longer tell what rarity the question mark item is as the outline was the only thing that showed that.they also attemped implementing the logbook mid-game and an "inspect" feature to let you read full item descriptions in the inventory menu, aka the tab menu. obviously the idea itself doesn't have any issues with it, in fact i'd fully support something like that. however for some reason you can no longer run/jump while the tab menu is open, so you can't actually do much in-game while inspecting items and you're kind of a sitting duck to be shot at by enemies, and the only way to counter that is the "pause when inspecting" option. this pretty much means that all this feature does is save like 5 seconds of looking up what the item does, as it doesn't really allow you to just do it mid-game as it supposedly should.these are just the changes i've seen so far. there might be more, but honestly i don't really feel like even trying to look for any more considering the game is now a lot harder just because the things that allowed you to tell when you took damage or healed just don't do that well anymore. i really hope that this stuff is fixed in due time, and maybe the dlc even becomes actually available for the solid part of the game's playerbase despite their location.

_childDocuments_.review: Asian food is not to everyone's taste but give these spicy and sticky Korean chicken wings a try, they make ideal finger food for a buffet, but don't forget the napkins!Recipe:Sticky Korean chicken wingsIngredientsFor the chicken500g chicken wingslarge chunk of ginger, finely grated50g cornflourvegetable oil, for fryingsesame seeds and sliced spring onion, to serveFor the sauce6 tbsp dark brown sugar2 tbsp gochujang (Korean chilli paste)2 tbsp soy sauce2 large garlic cloves, crushedsmall piece ginger, grated2 tsp sesame oilMethodSTEP 1To make the sauce, put all the ingredients in a saucepan and simmer gently until syrupy, so around 3-4 mins. Take off the heat and set aside.STEP 2Season the chicken wings with salt, pepper and the grated ginger. Toss the chicken with the cornflour until completely coated.STEP 3Heat about 2cm of vegetable oil in a large frying pan over a medium/high heat. Fry the chicken wings for 8-10 mins until crisp, turning halfway. Remove from the oil and place on kitchen paper. Leave to cool slightly (around 2 mins).STEP 4Reheat the sauce, and toss the crispy chicken wings in it. Tip into a bowl and top with the sesame seeds and sliced spring onions.Nutrition: per servingkcal487fat24gsaturates4gcarbs48gsugars35gfibre1gprotein20gsalt1.8gThe game is also good, a must play if for whatever reason you haven't already.

_childDocuments_.review: A thrilling rogue-lite experience, tolerably marred by its own clumsy implementation of difficulty.The base combat system is engaging and well structured, featuring a broad cast of unique characters each with their own distinct abilities and unlock requirements. Battles feel lively and quick, players chunking through swarms of enemies and dodging about as they unload their special attacks. There is a decent amount of item variety and most have distinct compounding effects when a duplicate is gained, allowing for all manner of extreme builds to emerge as the player stacks more items together. The graphics, animation and music are all nice to experience; giving the game a decent sense of polish and style. The world is interesting, offering a solid amount of area and enemy diversity along with written lore that can be acquired in various ways. A multitude of secrets and unlockables provide an extra layer of intrigue to the experience beyond simply finishing a run; which has multiple different conclusions based on the route taken. Despite how gripping the game can be it unfortunately does include recurrent moments of forced downtime, as players get currency by defeating enemies; yet those enemies do not appear at a reliable rate. Thus the experience has random moments where the player must wait for enemies to actually show up if they want to get more currency for acquiring items.While the game does well to keep the player active and engaged much of the time, its general difficulty is extremely precarious. Outside of obvious mistakes or trial and error many threats are simply a matter of bad luck. Various enemies have attacks which can obliterate the player if they do not react in a very specific way at a very specific time, which may be impossible if the surrounding terrain prohibits such. Characters with ranged attacks have the sometimes monotonous option of shooting these enemies from a safe distance away but melee characters have few ways to survive if the enemy shows up in a disadvantageous place. Meanwhile the accuracy of some enemies can seem totally inconsistent, with them missing or landing attacks regardless of how mobile the player is being.Although the game does have a mechanic in place to protect the player from getting instantly knocked out from full health, it does not stop them from getting instantly knocked out from high health; or getting instantly knocked out by multiple attacks in quick succession. As the difficulty levels increase and players get swarmed by foes, avoiding damage quickly becomes virtually impossible due to the sheer amount of incoming damage; and the distinct limitations on evasion and mobility in combat. The danger of a given enemy may also be obfuscated by how much their damage fluctuates with the level scaling and elemental variants, preventing the player from reliably predicting which incoming attacks they can absorb and which may instantly wipe them out. If they can even see the attack coming amidst the visual clutter of massive enemy swarms, or alternatively the player might just get hit from behind.The threat of being knocked out in either a single moment or a single chain of sudden events by an attack which may or may not have been visible or avoidable is a constant and pervasive issue; particularly in the higher difficulty modifiers. Fortunately this problem is not as prevalent if the player sticks to the default difficulty setting and avoids extremely prolonged runs, but even when playing on the easiest setting unfair scenarios do haunt the experience.Despite how generally fluid and comprehensive the game system feels it randomly becomes unhinged by compounding, unregulated factors that emerge as the difficulty amplifies haphazardly. Fortunately these issues can be mitigated by playing on the lower difficulty tiers, which makes them not entirely mandatory to this otherwise enjoyable experience.If you're interested in finding more games like this I've probably reviewed quite a few on my curator page .

_childDocuments_.review: I really tried to enjoy this game, I really did. Unfortunately, you can only slam your head into a brick wall so many times before you realize you aren't getting through. Risk of Rain combines two genres which I love, shooters and roguelikes which makes it all the more confusing that this game fails to impress.    - One major problem I noticed was that the combination of these two genres somehow managed not to take only some of the highlights of each genre, but also almost ALL of the lowlights. While many modern shooters are fast-paced with great movement, Risk of Rain somehow manages to feel slow both in pacing and in movement. You often have to choose between being fast and being powerful if you even have a choice.    - Another major problem is the simple lack of variety in gameplay. Unlike most modern roguelikes, the maps are repeated as opposed to generated meaning that every time you go to a map, it's almost the exact same map as last time. It's much akin to listen to a great music playlist over and over, it's cool the first couple of times but after a while you can't help but feel like you need more variety.     - In Risk of Rain, there is almost no critical thinking required. Great roguelikes such as Hades or Enter the Gungeon require players to think logically about whether or not it's worth the risk to get a new item as well as weigh different options to try to get items which synergize well with the items you already have but Risk of Rain is *mostly* absent of these mechanics. If you have the money, open a chest, if you don't, don't. There are a few places where you can decide what you get (outside of Artifact of Command) but these too leave little option in what to get meaning that you can lose (often) due alone to not getting lucky.Overall, I'm sure a lot of people enjoy Risk of Rain for it's unique characters and gameplay style, but for me it fails to impress. Risk of Rain fails to innovate and somehow manages to capture neither the charm and excitement of roguelikes nor the fun face-paced feel of a shooter. Despite this, I'd say the game is well designed and developed so I wouldn't blame anyone for enjoying it.

_childDocuments_.review: Risk of Rain 2, much like its Parent game is highly addictive and extremely fun. It's pretty well made despite being in early access. Everything looks so pretty! Plus, I think that some characters like the mercenary work better and are much more fun to play in the 3D setting . The teleporters are pretty hard to find because they look pretty plain and blend in with the environment. The only minor issues that I noticed are that some stages are super dark that makes it difficult to spot objects. They could work on the visibility and improve on the markers.There are lots of characters and items to try and lots of worlds to explore, so it's definitely a fun experience for both ROR fans and people new to the title. The art is beautiful, the music, even more so and the gameplay is fluid and engaging. I haven't tried multiplayer yet, but i'm sure it's just as fun. (oh and, no more port forwarding, yaaaay! xD )But yeah, I definitely recommend this game. i cant wait for them to add all the content in!EDIT: Game's now out of early access and the improvements that have been made throughout all the consistent updates have been amazing. Game now has an ending (Final stage + Boss), new items and a new survivor (The Captain), who is really fun to play with his shotgun and bots. All the items and survivors also have complete logs now and it's a fun read if you're interested. I've had a ton of fun with this and my experience has been amazing overall. The music's really good too (although I prefer ROR1's music over this. Definitely recommend getting this at full price if you can.

_childDocuments_.review: With a heavy heart, I can no longer recommend this game. Gearbox have shown time and time again they do not care about Risk of Rain as a game. On Christmas day of 2020, I bought Risk of Rain 2 on Xbox after having vague memories of ChilledChaos playing the first one and remember finding it interesting. After my first run, which ended preemptively at the first teleporter, I was hooked, demanding all my friends purchase the game so we could all play together. I sunk hundreds of hours on the console version despite its clear flaws. It was riddled with bugs, and even though SOTV was delayed for upwards of two years, I held out. When the first dlc dropped finally, I bought it on that day, having followed every word the dev team spoke about its release date, and it was worth it entirely. Sure, it introduced some new bugs, like multiplayer not working, but being on console, I was familiar with those already. It came with a brand new recoding of the whole game too, which had progress change over as well. Now, you may wonder what this has to do with the pc version. I say that all to show that not only did I love the game, I also could deal with buggy experiences and still have fun. It also shows that gearbox, the group associated with the console release were clearly incompetent before this dlc release, mishandling the console port for actual years before Hopoo handed over the reigns to them. From what I read, they sold the ip for 42 million dollars, which is not a number to scoff at. This dlc has ruined the game for not only the console players but also the pc players as well. When I bought this game back in December of 2023 and played it February of this year, even while heavily modded the lack of bugs was a new and exciting experience. You could boot up the game and play it, multiplayer or single player, going for as long as you wanted (or as long as the game engine allowed). That is no longer possible. Bugs riddle this game because low and behold, the console port's terrible new code was brought over to pc. It is so bad that people, including myself, recommend you downgrade to a previous patch to be able to enjoy your experience.You can patch the bugs, gearbox, but you'll never be able to patch the mark of shame on your company after so many catastrophic failures. Also, the new dlc just kinda sucks. The items feel ai generated and whoever made them clearly had no idea about the core gameplay look of Ror2. It's unreal.EDIT: Instead of fixing the bugs in a timely manner, they released a roadmap detailing how it'll take them several months to make fixes any semi-competent dev could do in less than a few weeks. This game is dead and gearbox killed it.

OH GOD. Is it buggy. Servers fail pretty often, but on the plus side they do alot of maintenance.- While I respect the decision to base the game off of the good ol' MMO trinity (Healer, Tank, DPS) there are alot of jutsus within the respective classes that are pretty much "the best option" for a teams success in the PvP meta. That's not to say that you can't upset the meta with solid strategy, because you can, but if you're trying to do something unique, or build a character with specific types of jutsu to kind of fit what you would want to be if you were in Naruto, you can fall short HARD against a team with best-in-slot tank and healer roles. Granted, ranged DPS and melee DPS are where most freedom of gameplay choices lie, but it would be nice if they addressed this. Case in point: Long range slug healing is THE healer Ult. It just is. However, this comes with the Trinity system, and it's to be expected. Honestly, I would have liked to have seen them do away with the class system all together. Which brings me to my next point:- With a good healer, and a good tank to protect that healer, if the opposing team doesn't have an optimal set-up, the team with the tank and healer is borderline immortal. I know that healing jutsu is integrated into Naruto lore, but the inclusion of it in this format either causes imbalance, or, in the case of two teams with optimal set-ups, LONG matches. Granted, the match time limits remedy this a little bit, but what it essentially amounts to is less aggression. One could argue that less aggression allows for more strategy, which is true, but not really what I was hoping for out of this game, but I DO understand that this CAN'T be the Ninja Storm MMO, regardless of how much I want that to be the case, haha. All in all, it's not a bad system, and I recognize that it is perfectly valid, I'm just letting you know that this is kind of what to expect. You have to play your role. Or you can do like me, pick the jutsu you want, and be happy when it works out, even if it doesn't work out as often as you'd like.- THE MISSIONS. Christ. VR Missions are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ atrocious. Non-skippable cutscenes, repeat bosses, repeat missions, repeat enemies, map-wide blasts that can go through buildings and obstructions without you being able to see where they are coming from, Gyuki's attacks drops the framerate of the game to about a half a frame per f*****g second, and you HAVE to do them all if you want access to all cosmetics. IF they make a second shinobi striker, they NEED to take a page from Xenoverse's book and make fun, interesting missions with a variety of characters.- Uninteresting Hub-world. This goes back to my Xenoverse comment. Look, Xenoverse isn't perfect, but the hub-world at least kind of makes you want to take a look around. The hidden leaf hub world, while easy to navigate, is just kind of dull. Nothing really interesting going on, and it just serves as a "go here to do this" spot. Which isn't bad. Again, I get that this is a game primarily about PvP, and the hub is designed to get you back and forth from merchant-to-mission-to-match as quickly as possible, but man, part of me really wanted to jump across the buildings of the leaf village, go to the forest where the chunin exams were, see the training grounds where Rock Lee and Naruto had their formative moments. Maybe have missions that actually take place IN that world. I guess I was just hoping for a more immersive experience out of this. Again, matter of opinion. I understand that the majority of this player-base is here to make an OC and kick ass (or a meme. I've seen you Zetsu-lookin'-ass bug-eyed rock lees. Fair warning, these are the players that will smoke you on the battlefield. They are dangerous. I'm not kidding), but I would have liked to have seen something more like Xenoverse, where there is a story that you need to be directly involved with, instead of cut-and-paste missions you get from a VR-Arcade that Kakashi runs on the right side of the village square, which brings me to my next point:- No real story mode. AGAIN, and I get it, this is a PvP game, but if you WANT all the cosmetics you HAVE to do all of the missions to get Jonin rank so that Ten-ten will pull out the top-shelf stock. If you're going to make your game require me to play the PvE content to unlock everything that is obtainable in it, then you should go the extra mile to make that content enjoyable, and uh, DUDE, THIS is NOT enjoyable. Almost all of the missions feel like chores, and as you climb the ranks from D rank to S rank you'll find that pretty much every mission in A and S with the exception of a few are more difficult copy-pastas of previous missions. Xenoverse (again, I know this game isn't Xenoverse, but cut me a break, this is basically the Naruto franchise's version of it) has a story that you have to go through to unlock the basic stuff, then extra missions that allow you to get items to upgrade your guy, but for the most part, it's a fun story, and the missions make you feel like you're actually doing something worthwhile for the characters in the game. Shinobi Striker straight up TELLS you that everything you're doing is in VR, and the only reason you're doing any of those simulations is to train for the tournament. Put that on top of the fact that the missions are repetitive and buggy, and it's IMPOSSIBLE for the PvE content to not feel like a chore. If you're going to make me play PvE to get cosmetics, give me a meaningful campaign in the second one, please? Or, if you don't wanna do that, just take it out altogether and have the ninja rank system integrated into the PvP level-up system. I'd prefer the good campaign, but if that's more work than you wanna put into it, Idk, don't half-ass it is all I'm saying.- No color palette for clothes. (At this point, I'm pretty much comparing this game to Xenoverse with every post, so I'm gonna stop apologizing for it, and you can move on to the next review if you take issue with it, but ONE LAST TIME, sorry, lol) So, in order to get different color options, you have to get these scrolls from playing the game, and you MIGHT get the color option you want. In Xenoverse, if an item is dyable, you can change it's color from the get go.  Just make a shorter list of clothing model options and give players the ability to change the color of the two to three changeable parts of said items. I can't believe I even have to type this. You're not even making any extra money off of having them not be dye-able.(at least this is true for the items available in ten-ten's shop. I understand that the different colored versions of the character outfits come from scrolls, and you can buy moonlight scrolls--DON'T by the way--, but even with the character outfits, I don't like all of their color options. Just let me pick the colors I want and where I want them.)There's probably more, but those are the main points. Again, if the price has gone back up by the time you read this: Dude. don't. seriously. BUT, if it's 10 bucks are less, sure, give it a go.

_childDocuments_.review: As a huge Naruto fan, I've always wanted a game that you can build your own ninja and extend your abilities in a hierarchical way just like in series (Genin to Hokage ) as you progress in the game. Shinobi striker first seemed like to me as a game that I described, but it fell short of my expectations. I've recommended this game(not in full price) because it's fun in general but there are more cons than pros for me.  Lets start with cons;- Altough there is a rank that goes up by completing VR missions(PVE), this rank only unlocks some gear to purchase from store for your character as you go up but doesn't have any effect to your abilities, which you unlock from known characters in series by choosing them as a master. I'd expect more "meaning" about ranks.- The game is not built in this way but it would be interesting to have a concept of Chunin exams with PVP involved that benefits player with new features as you climb up. It is a nice-to-have thing but the reason I added it to cons is the game lacks feeling of progress after you learned all jutsu from masters and this would also bring matchmaking a new perspective of matching the players with the same ranks.- VR missions are boring / repetitive. - There are lots of costume/gear with features (like boosting damage / heal etc.) but these features have a little variety.- Roles in a team is a good concept but unless you play without friends, most of the things that are happening in a battle feels like completely random. Game is strategy forced but it doesn't go beyond jutsu/normal attack spam in %80 of games.(In some battles I witnessed some well-thought and calculated moves)-The comment above brings a "relative" lack of content compared to the other battle arena type games; Tide of battle doesn’t change from early game to late game. Fight until your ultimate jutsu is ready, use it and then start over. It’d be good to have some additional abilities / features as the battle goes on. Like having an awakening state just like in other Naruto games which can bring different skill set, spree-based rewardings or giving an advantage to losing team (the list can be extended).-There are 4 battle types in PVP but the game chooses which you will play in tournament mode when you enter queue. -Some battle types are not enjoyable in my perspective. Flag battle lasts 2 mins max in 3 of 5 games and in base battle (which you own sites and gain points if they belong to your team) the players with  Gaara’s sand shield jutsu (impenetrable – unbreakable) blocks all the site until they own them. A rework both to the battle types and particular jutsus might be useful.-There are 5 maps since the release of the game.Pros:-Battles are fast-paced, Wall-running and wired kunai (like grappling hook) contributes to heat of battle.-Although I stated lots of cons, the game itself still enjoyable at one point in this current state. Especially if you come up to a good team.-Everyone is shouting jutsus. SHINRA TENSEI!-It is related to Naruto.TL DR: I recommend to those who like not-so-time-consuming and fast-paced PVP. There are lots of combination of jutsus(techniques) that you can try for each role and find your own style. Also new masters are being added as a DLC, you can play with those masters for free but you cannot learn jutsu from them. Still I wouldn’t recommend at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: ▷ This game is not worth over 25(euros/dollars/quids) but on sale you can pick it up with just 5€, I absolutely recommend doing so if you have the chance. You're also going to want to buy those DLCs due to that they give you massive advantage in PVP.▷ Naruto to Boruto: Shinobi Striker has many of the familiar characters from the anime and you start the game by creating your own character; character creation is very limited but in my opinion it offers enough options to be satisfied with. You unlock hairstyles by choosing your sensei and leveling up with them or by purchasing them from Tenten.▷ This game has very small hub in which you manage your character and builds, from there you go to main mission (pve) or queue up to pvp fights.▷ Main missions in this game are very very boring and you can't skip the horrible scenes that happen before every mission you go to, mainly in all of the missions you just beat up a lot of enemy ninjas that spawn in waves in different locations. This mode will show you how little money was put into making this game. But completing missions will eventually increase your ninja rank which unlocks new stuff in the shop so you should do them.★ PVP is the main stage in this game, where this game shines and the reason why I am recommending this game. You can choose 4 roles, (healer, attacker, defender or range), each role has their own jutsu styles, and weapons they use. for example defenders use heavy weapons with protective barricade jutsus etc, healers use jutsus to heal allies or buff them in various ways, attackers excel in hand to hand combat and get jutsus to support that aspect, range type gets jutsus to spam from further away with very heavy damage. Many of the best jutsus are unlocked with DLC characters, when you purchase the DLC you unlock character you can choose as your sensei and then level with them to get their jutsus. What gear you use matters a lot in this game as clothes gives you passive attributes to boost your fighting style, for the fashion gamers I have good news as this game allows you to pick up the gear you like for it's looks and then you can purchase what attributes that piece gives you.

_childDocuments_.review: Naruto to Boruto: Shinobi Striker offers a unique experience for fans of the Naruto universe, blending team-based combat with a variety of game modes that capture the essence of ninja life. Developed by Soleil Ltd. and published by Bandai Namco Entertainment, the game presents a dynamic and cooperative approach to the world of ninjas.One of Shinobi Striker's strongest features is its combat system. It is fluid and acrobatic, allowing players to utilize a wide range of abilities and moves characteristic of Naruto characters. The verticality of the maps and the freedom of movement are aspects that set this game apart from other fighting titles, providing a sense of authenticity and immersion in the ninja universe.Character customization is another highlight. Players can create and customize their own ninja, choosing from a vast array of outfits, weapons, and abilities (Jutsus). This offers significant depth and diversity, allowing each player to have a unique character that suits their playstyle.The game modes are varied, including base battles, flag capture, and elimination battles. Each mode requires different strategies, keeping the gameplay fresh and challenging. The emphasis on team-based combat encourages cooperation and strategy formation, making the gaming experience even more engaging when played with friends or other online players.Visually, Shinobi Striker is impressive. The cel-shaded graphics perfectly capture the anime's style, providing a visually pleasing experience that stays true to the original material. The animations of the Jutsus and special abilities are spectacular, bringing to life the epic moments from the series in a way that fans will certainly appreciate.However, the game is not without its flaws. For new players, the learning curve can be quite steep. The variety of abilities and the need for team coordination can be challenging, especially in competitive matches. Additionally, some players report connectivity and matchmaking issues, which can be frustrating when trying to join online matches.Repetitiveness is another downside. Although the game modes are varied, some missions and objectives can become repetitive after long play sessions. The lack of a more robust narrative content might also be a downside for those looking for a deeper experience. Moreover, the balance between different characters and abilities can sometimes feel uneven, resulting in imbalanced matches that affect the overall gaming experience.In conclusion, Naruto to Boruto: Shinobi Striker is an intriguing addition to the Naruto gaming universe, offering a fun and dynamic team-based combat experience. Character customization, stylized graphics, and varied game modes are strong points that appeal to both series fans and fighting game enthusiasts. Despite connectivity issues, the learning curve, and repetitiveness, the game successfully captures the essence of ninja life in an engaging and visually impressive manner.Final Score: 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot of potential, & I have to say, it's amazingly fun. Except....it has a LOT of problems. First off; the game's balancing needs work. Like, excessive amounts. It is way too easy to spam attacks, and some classes for some reason get skills that make them infinitely, excessively more powerful than the other classes. Specifically, the Attack & Range classes get most of the moves from the masters. Defense classes get nowhere near as much in terms of usable skills as the attack classes, and ranged class gets moves that can be spammed to the point of game-breaking strength from level one.Attack class' skills are also extremely overpowered, able to ragdoll you to death so fast the Flash would wonder 'what the heck just hit me?'On top of that, there's the DLCs. The DLC masters can be used freely with levelup, but they only give you skills(or literally anything other than the ability to play as them) if you buy said DLCs, and said DLC skills are MASSIVELY overpowered, moreso than most skills in the basegame, making the game Pay-to-Win.Apart from skill issues, the game is peer-to-peer in battle servers, meaning you will find lag. a. lot. And i'm still half-convinced that 90% of it is artificial, used by other players to give themselves an edge.There's also the problem that the voice chat systems don't work properly, and that's only when they work at all. The menu chat systems are almost as bad, being so minimalistic they're basically useless.So, to sum it all up; This game has amazing potential, but it's ruined by the game's lag issues, lack of any even remotely proper balancing, lack of properly-built communication systems, and pay-to-win tendencies.If you can stomach going into a battle and finding yourself dead in ten seconds flat because every other player does nothing but use the most broken, unbalanced, overpowered skills in the game, some of which they probably bought their way to instead of earning it via hard work, by all means, you'll enjoy this game. Otherwise, don't buy it. It'll save you money, as well as stop you from breaking your keyboard via pure frustration.

_childDocuments_.review: I liked the gameplay and some of the customization parts of the character creation. I think the developers had a good idea from the beginning, wanting to create a living world of Naruto including all the villages and characters. However, somewhere along the way they realized the project was too big for them and turned the "hype" of this game into a cash grab. As soon as you get in, about the first thing you figure out is that its all about grinding scrolls for a limited array of customization of your character. As far as the gameplay is concerned, I would have liked story based and longer missions, rather than a Virtual Reality simulator. Basically, they wanted to use all characters from the Naruto saga and couldn't do that without including (if you excuse my language) BS technology. The fighting controls is okay and the jutsu(skills/techniques) used is quite fun to combine, but also lacking in depth. The fighting reminds me of the Naruto Ninja Gaiden games only more spammy and chaotic. The graphics and models looks okay I guess, but still not better than the above mentioned game series from PS3. Overall I was hoping for a more MMO-ish type of game of the Naruto world, but it ended up as a "surprise mechanic" with season pass and PVP league game. Maybe I'll come back to it in a year or two and see what has happened, but I'm not hoping for much.5.5/10

But ok, I hear ya, most of Naruto is about the Ninjutsu! Ok. Ninjutsu is laughable. Healer has a cool CC, awesome. Tank has... well, useless stuff. Ranged has two Fireballs, woo... how diverse and interesting when they both act Almost identical, yea, one is faster and the other bigger, I got it. What really irks me, is that I have put Five Hours into the game.... and I still only have the Starters... a Salamnder summon.... and Rasengan.... Five Hours, two new Jutsu. So, I went and did 20 random grouped quests... everything still locked. This game can be Sooooo much more... but the bugs man, the bugs with the controls are Killing me. Like literally. Everything just needs refinement, and they need more Content, not more graphical cool looking stuff. and how is 4 pve battles just fine but the SECOND I start fighting in the 4v4 everyone starts teleporting? You can run on any surface then jump and latch on to another, it makes gameplay very dynamic. Also, you can charge your jump and overcome great distance with it (just like Sonic on SEGA). There are a lot of events on holidays.This game is not pay to win, but there are some skills and weapons that you can't earn without paying, so that's why sometimes in online you can get your ass kicked, but it's not critical. Missions here are like story-mode here and I was pleasantly surprised of these missions. There are a lot of boss battles and different modes so you will enjoy it. But some of them are just impossible to be done alone. You should find yourself some friends there. After completing all missions you can do it again, but with a higher rank and better rewards.Unfortunately, this game still feels raw. All updates just add some new characters (whose equipment and skills you can unlock, if you buy them ofc) and that is all. I really hope that developers will add some new missions or online-modes. But for now, I'm tired of this game. If you want to buy it, expect it to become boring in 2 weeks (just my opinion).

_childDocuments_.review: As an avid Naruto fan, I was SO excited for a team based game like this!Too bad its a GARBAGE HEAP to play alone.Pros- Its Naruto!!!- Custom Shinobi creation is SICK. It's so cool to have so many of the iconic looks of the Naruto franchise at your disposal to mix and match.- The masters and learning their abilities is a neat concept seen in past games.- The VR missions are super fun to run Co-op with friends! Definitely the highlight of the game experience.Cons- There is NO Matchmaking. Enjoy being level 10 vs the level 50s.- There is no true story mode experience. Just the VR missions. In order to unlock VR missions, you must wander around the central hub to find a character who then tells you to walk back to the VR missions person to get back into gameplay.- There is no warping, which means you must walk to each menu slowly but surely. You also can't enter a menu while in queue for matchmaking.- All the outfits have stats on them!! Did you want to make your own custom look? Well too bad, you chose wrong, you're gonna get beat so bad online.- This camera HATES you. To look around, it's right stick. To lock on, it's right stick CLICK. Once you lock on, if you flick the stick at all, it just switches who you're targeting so you must un lock on to be aware enough to move around.- When you get out of a match, the game requeues you but it requeues you into the SAME LOBBY. You must unqueue, which is a menu. Then you must re-queue, which is a menu that leads you to another menu. Speaking of...- There are SO MANY MENUS YOU HAVE TO WORK THROUGH JUST TO CHANGE THINGS. You cant' change your clothes, your weapon, your Ninjustus, your Ultimate, without going to a menu, which leads to another menu. Its tedious. You must WALK to the place that lets you get to the menu that leads to the menu to the next menu.- The lobbies are BARREN. You can't even SELECT WHICH LOBBY YOU WISH TO JOIN.EDIT: In order to quit the game, you must first connect to the server. However, if the server happens to be down, you can't connect so you can't even get to the "Quit Game" option. A M A Z I N GEDIT EDIT: Sometimes, the game doesn't allow you to see the end result screen, meaning you dont get ANY points from that battle. At all. You'll get RANKED points but no EXP nor any VR Master EXP. If you happen to get a fatal error while playing ranked, you lose an entire rank. xdthis is a port of a console game, not a true PC edition.I've never been more disappointed in a purchase that i was excited for since August 31st, 2018.EDIT: game is way better now, teehee. Most of the issues have been fixed but ALSO there's just a small PC playerbase :( crossplay would save it but the game is pretty damn great now thanks to patches and updates.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, so I figure I'm at a decent point in the game to make a solid review. I've played for 27 hours over the past 2 days and I am at a point where I can see the pros and the cons. If you would've asked me to review the game in the first 10 hours, it would've been a positive recommendation, no questions asked. And I will still vote this game yes, but not without detailing the flaws that I've found.Pros:- Character customization is great, it feels good to be able to make your own character and tailor their style to how you want your ninja. My ninja is the ultimate edge lord, and I love it.- Combat feels great. Some of the ninjutsu feel a little underwhelming compared to the anime, but hey, if all of the jutsu were as poweful as the anime, people would be dying left and right, so I get it.- Missions are exciting and encourage you to replay them, to get cool new accessories.- The game forces you to get good at the game, and it feels rewarding when you feel yourself getting better.- Overall fun factor of the game is very high.These pros are very strong, in my opinion, with a couple things that I go "meh" about, but it's no big deal. The cons are very disheartening though.Cons:- Matchmaking takes forever, probably due to the lack of active players.- Lag is unreal. I have lost matches and gotten draws on matches that should have been easy wins but when I use a ninjutsu my character lags over the side of a building and unloads his wrath on a wall. Happens pretty regularly.- The increase in difficulty from C rank missions to B rank missions is ridiculous. I mean, maybe I'm crazy, but I think the A rank missions are considerably easier than B rank and I have even done an S rank mission that wasn't as hard as some of the B rank missions. It's extremely frustrating.- Lack of communication with teammates. I have had so many matches where I want to tell someone to heal, or signal there is a potion, or just tell someone to quit being an idiot and knocking the boss over the side when we only have a minute to kill him and he's at 80% health. I have used Discord to converse with my teammates that are friends, but not being able to speak with randos on my team can really get upsetting.The fact that I got this game on sale for $20 was amazing, because I wouldn't have gotten it otherwise. I'll still play the crap out of it and I aspire to become a Jonin, but there are definitely cons to this game and I wouldn't recommend it at full price.TL;DR - The game is extremely fun, but problems with matchmaking, lag, and lack of communication bring it down. I'd wait for a sale to get this.EDIT: There is voice chat, but it is extremely hard to find. For others who don't know, you have to go into sound settings, turn on voice chat and then turn on microphone. What a pain.

_childDocuments_.review: This game saved my life.I am 27.My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and adopted our son together. They are now both 4 years old.When we were going through our separation, I found myself lost and miserable. I was self destructive. I got so mad one day from everything spiraling out of my control that I punched some concrete in a moment of overwhelming emotion. That caused me to break my 5th metacarpal in my right hand... my working hand... my games hand.. the hand that I held and carried my children to bed with.. The hand I desperately needed to make sure I could continue to provide.After learning of the severity of my self-inflicted damage, I was borderline suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man with no history of depression or anxiety. I have never had fits of rage, or been one to break down and cry, but I was in a low spot that just really buried me from being able to see the light on the other side.Having nothing better to do, I searched for a game I could play, ONE HANDED while I recovered. I somehow stumbled upon this game and read some of the reviews. I decided that it had to be worth a shot... I must admit, I didn't beat the game, or play nearly as long as some of you. In fact, I may have only played this game a day or two.. With that being said, after doing so, I had a new found joy and hope for life. I was able to put behind me the pain and suffering that had been cast over me. I was able to experience other peoples joy and happiness. I was able to see the fruits of my "labor". I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ minutes to this music long enough to realize that I was going to be okay.After coming to that realization, I turned the game off, and I went back to work. It hurt my hand like hell but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so damn sorry for myself, and I became the father I needed to be in that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving as.Today, I am close friend with my kids mother. We don't fight, or argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents, and friends.I now have 3 kids. My third child is, wait for it, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my own separation, and we just stumbled in to each others life unexpectedly. We have been in a relationship for a year now, and are very happy together.Moral of the story, you never know what life holds in store for you, and if I would have given up when all the odds were stacked against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. _childDocuments_.review: A fun and actiony game where you can create your very own character, but Steam reviews aren't asking me if I like the game, but if I RECOMMEND IT, and quite frankly, I can't recommend it to solo players like myself. Especially those who wanted to create their own ninja and see awesome feats done by them.My main issue is a minor gripe, but for people like me it might be relevant. I enjoy character creation games and injecting myself or my own characters into a game to watch them interact with other characters and the world. Unfortunately for this game there is no story mode really. ANY cutscenes you see in this game don't even include your main character in them (I could be wrong, but this is just based on the first 2 hours of playing and it doesn't take much to realize this is a multiplayer focused game). This sucks because I was really enjoying the idea of maybe having your character in cutscenes with your favorite Naruto characters doing crazy jutsu all over the place like how DBXenoverse 2 had you shooting ki beams in cutscenes and punching holes through people. This issue means you don't have anything really engaging you to continue playing the game unless you're a competitive pvp type which this game seems heavily aimed towards. No problem with that of course, but for solo players this game isn't really for you.There's also the big killer which is that this game is ONLINE ONLY. Meaning that even if you were okay with the no story mode and you simply enjoy playing the solo missions with your created character, then you'll have to be sure you're online to enjoy that experience. What's worse is that automatically gives the game an expiration date since, once Bandai Namco decides to shut down servers (as they will eventually in the future whenever it doesn't seem profitable to keep them up), the game will be unplayable. I've read on the forums there's a way to play offline but it involves deleting a file, so since it's not an official feature that the devs have and it's outside help you need I still remove the points from this game.Ultimately I will NOT be refunding the game, as I find it to be a very fun and enjoyable experience having my own ninja running around and fighting other people and doing missions, but this is a NOT RECOMMENDED for solo players and also a message to the Bandai Namco that I'm disappointed in them. When I see Bandai Namco games I have some expecations of quality from them due to previous games I've played of theirs that I enjoy like God Eater and DBXenoverse and such. Those games I mentioned allow character creation that feels meaningful as you progress through a story and your character forges bonds with some of your favorite characters. In this game you just get dumped into the hub world and do some tutorial stuff and it all just feels so joyless and mechanical without a soul. I know these guys can do better and I honestly hope they do. I know this might be flamebait to say, but I'd honestly be okay with paying +$10 for a Story mode DLC where they add cutscenes where your character shows up in doing action scenes and of course missions where you impact the story. Either way I like this game but solo players be aware of what you're getting yourself into just in case. Not a bad game, but a loooooooooot of wasted potential here.

_childDocuments_.review: The jutsus are cool and are fun to use. Building a character is also fun. Thats about all the positive aspects I can name. The VR Quests are boring and repetitive, lack any difficulty whatsoever and don't seem finished. For example, if you kill a boss, it stops your movement to force you into a small cutscene - Killing you if you're not on the ground, which in a game with good movement options is kind of a rare occasion. Pvp is sometimes fun, but more often than not it is frustrating. One, because the difference between a premade group of players and a team of randoms is immense and you dont have a real chance of ever even killing someone. This is somewhat excuseable, it does state on the steam page that this is Coop orientented. Fine. But why in gods name are there ZERO options to form a group inside the game?You cant friend a player after a match if you played well together, you cant talk to people in the lobby, you cant invite them to a group and to nobodys surprise theres no LFG tool either. Not even after you played a VR mission together. Even after that, you have no option to communicate with that other person. For a game that is supposed to be played with other people this game has far too little options to do so. Another thing that bothers me is that you cannot report people. Ive seen more than enough people with an "interesting" username, going by that I dont assume theres any sort of moderation going on. I also assume leaving a game early goes unpunished. _childDocuments_.review: One of my first reviews, so bear with me.This is definitely a solid game. If you're looking for a semi tactical, objective based, multiplayer game, and you happen to be a fan of the Naruto franchise this game is in your favor. It's not a straight up fighting game, so if thats what you are looking for try out the Naruto Storm series. The combos are are simple and the game relies more on positioning and timing on your jutsus. If you have a good team composition and everyone communicates you will see a lot of wins in the future. (Especially if you get a decent medic and defense style ninja on your squad). And even though the game can lack in a in depth combo system it excels in naruto immersion. It is absolute insane to traverse the walls and jump around the many open maps, while laying traps in this high action game. You really can lose yourself in being a shinobi.The game also has some single/co-op missions that aren't exactly story driven, but feel more like random tasks. You will find yourself not caring about the objective at all, but you will also completely forget about the lackluster story telling because the gameplay is just so damn fun. So the missions are not perfect, but they make up for it as a good time killer.Customization is more than decent as well. the big con is there aren't enough original designs like the Xenoverse series (which seemes to heavily inspire this game). All the customization items are just outfits and hairstyles that main characters in the series wear or have, but if you try hard enough you can still find a way to make your ninja stand out from the rest.Overall the games multiplayer is what will hold your attention the longest. The hight action and strategic gameplay will keep you engaged. And even though the mission system isn't the most interesting mode, it's still something you will see yourself playing as a time killer, or if you need to take a breather from multiplayer.game is a definite 7/10 in my book. Not perfect, but if you're a Naruto fan and enjoy multiplayer you will find a place here to spend quite a few hours.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game on sale for 13 dollars, and I have to say, it is amazing. There is a variety of different jutsu for every playstyle, and it hits hard with nostalgia, from rasengan to planetary devastations. The missions each have a rich, unique objective, and I can say the same for all the bosses too. What I find best about this game is the combat system. It is super smooth and incorporates different techniques very well into battle. Combat varies between the four different classes, and the interactions are different each time. Against a swarm of enemies(White Zetsu for example) the targeting system and your attacks transition fluidly between the different enemies, making it easier to lock on to an enemy and not jutsu the air.Each class in this game is balanced, and serves a different purpose. And by balanced, I mean insanely balanced. There is no broken op class, and most of it relies on pure skill. In a pvp situation, there will obviously be a rift in strength (Rangers at a distance can shred an attack class, however if the attack class gets close goodbye ranger), but it is overall very balanced.The sale is over and I don't suggest buying the game for full price(It simply isn't worth that much money from a gameplay aspect) but if Shinobi Striker ever goes back on sale, BUY IT. I highly recommend this, Naruto fan to Naruto fan.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, I'm not a Naruto fan. I liked the series when I was younger and forgot about mostly.So this game comes around it and it looks fun to do with some friends.I played Dragon Ball Xenoverse without much knowledge of the series so I thought this might be some sort of the same good stuff.Sadly this game is downright broken in its design, fails in its execution and is lackluster in content.I have a soft spot for character customization in general. I played many bad games just because It has a good creator but this is awful. - Very limited option. Most F2P mmorpg have better ones- Over 4000 Outfits Choices. About 40 to 60 outfits, all the rest is just reskins. I had duplicates in the first hour of playing.- There are passive attributes on those outfits, but only about 6 to 7 exits in total. Most aren't even useful at all.But hows the gameplay? It is even worse.You have 2 modes. Coop missions and MultiplayerCoop is one of the worse modes I have ever come across- There are ranks, from D to S. But the is no differents in content in them. S mission just hit harder- Most bosses are 3 of the tailed beasts. The others are a snake and 2 frogs. Now the problem lies it its design   All of them aren't made to fight fairly. All of them have a insta-kill laser the go's through walls and buildings.   This isn't intentional. It doesn't feel and looks right. 9 out of ten times you can't dodge it ether.- All mission your are fighting against the timer more then the enemies. Since you can   respawn infinitely, there is no reason  to play healer or tank.   Death is meaningless. This throws defensive tactics in the dumpster   right away, you don't have that time to play defensive at all.  There is even a passive clothing skill that reduces the respawn time...  This only proves my point even further. The other mode in Multiplayer which is at its best decent and at its worse ok.- But there resists the same problem the other modes has   There is no point doing it in the long run.Real rant comes hereThere is no progression. When you level up you get a lootscroll to get more useless outfits.Jutsu's are learn by your master or playing a class repeatedly.But there are barely any jutsu worth unlocking. Most do ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and have little visual impact. E.g Kirin or Kamui look lazy and loss to Pain's ultimate.And the biggest problem is their take on a class based system.Every class has their jutsu's and weapons. A healer class can't use a attacker class weapons or jutsu. Also only 2 normal jutsu and 1 ultimate jutsu are allowed. Very barebone.This is broken and destroys any creative builds instantly.The game even contardicts itself. E.g Melee fist based weapons are attacker class only, yet Sakura who is a healer use her fists. Healer can only use katana's, yet Sasuke is a ranger who uses a katana.Forcing people to play classes doesn't work when your game doesn't even follow the rule it makes. And last THERE IS NO POINT PROGRESSION THROUGH THE GAME- No progression- No creative builds possible- No story or concrete narrative- Your CaC HAS NO IMPACT ON ANYTHING. Everything is VR so nothing happens or changes the slighted.In Dragon Ball Xenoverse your CaC is a time patroller. A character that go's through time to help and save the characters and makes sure everything happens as it should. When you battle a God like Beerus, you actually fought Beerus. They even comment on that and remember you.It isn't a grand story but there is a narrative. It gives you motivation to learn and understand the game.In Naruto To Boruto you're a nobody that has never gone on a real ninja mission since you spent all your time fighting VR version of characters that are dead and/or don't remember you or give any ♥♥♥♥♥ about you. You are as much a ninja as a pilot that has 300 hour in a flight simulation and never flew a real aeroplane.There isn't a narrative. If the game doesn't care, why should I...Also Denuvo (See EULA - 24. THIRD PARTY SOFTWARE)

_childDocuments_.review: I did not like this game. Let's see why.THE BAD :-Ultimates one-shot you at full hp.-Useless Hub/Lobby replaces a menu or good user interface and is too big. You have to walk for 10 seconds to and from npcs to do anything. A pure waste of time.-The sub button (very important and must not be used randomly) is the same button as the counter button, chakra jump button and WORST OF ALL, the rope kunai button (that you will use to recover yourself when falling). Effectively accidentally wasting subs when trying to grab onto a wall to stop your fall.-Customization system. For a full priced game, it falls very short, only giving you 3 slots when it comes to armor. Character looks customization itself is not bad.-Maybe "pay-to-win", jutsus are locked behind paywalls, some of them i heard were meta.-Floaty combat. If you are a fan of precise, deliberate combat such as what is given in the Storm series, this is the opposite, and it gets worse with lag and desync.-The lock-on system is horrible, completely locking your camera and making it very hard to see whats going on most of the time.-The progression. This is a game that is supposed to make you create your own ninja, and fulfill your fantasy of being a ninja and growing up and getting stronger in this world. I am 2 hours and so in, and Im already able to do all the big boy stuff like sage of six paths, almighty push and etc. Theres no sense of growing stronger with time besides in the first 40 minutes maybe. Youre already at a top tier ninja level.-The maps, theres 5 of them. LOL-The feeling of belonging to the world, theres none. You just walk around your empty HUB talking to NPCS instead of browsing a menu. Effectively wasting your time. But it feels empty and hollow. -Combat can get very chaotic with people using jutsus and attacking everyone else from behind. Interrupted jutsus are common.-The UI is kinda bad, i have to equip an item to get rid of the "NEW" mark, means i gotta waste my time re-equiping my actual preferred item if i want a clean comprehensive inventory.-There is no way to transfer your outfit between builds.You know how some games get quality of life updates, or just release better than their predecessor in that regard (such as Monster Hunter : Rise), well this game needs a LOT of quality of life updates. Also you are DOOMED without a healer in your team. So i guess i need to play healer at all times now.THE GOOD : -Its Naruto, and thats damn well the only reason i think people are playing this.-It looks very pretty visually.-DECENT character customization (helped by the fact the game looks great).ONLY buy this if youre a hardcore naruto fan AND the game is on sale for 10$ or less.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't tell if the mechanics of this game were meant for an online, or offline system, but either way it works terribly on both ends.I'll make this short and quick, going straight to the good and bad points of this game, or at least my experience so far.Naruto Shinobi Striker is a Multiplayer PVP based arena brawler game, with the main focus being team based combat with your favorite ninja, or custom character with your favorite jutsu. It has a variety of modes ranging from Capture the flag, team deathmatch, control the points and "Barrier battle". Basically an attack / defend system.Starting with the pros:     - Interesting visuals on effects     - Fun mechanics and modes     - Very nice lobby with all other players     - Interesting take on classes and roles     - Great animationsCons:    - Incredibly unbalanced    - Cluster♥♥♥♥ of a mess both online and offline (Cant do much without getting interrupted all the time)    - Glitch abusers and no punish system do disconnects mid game    - Lootbox system to unlock items    - Very poor visual outside of effects. Characters look made out of wood and overall ugly. (Forgivable with the good animations and such)    - A lot of down time during combat, in a fast paced game. (Stuns and stagger last way too long)    - Combos and moves feel very unrefined with how often they drop    - Camera man feels like he had too many drinks and is trying to fly a hellicopter without prior knowledge.BIG CON: - There are hackers everywhere and nothing can be done about it (efficiently) - Report system very unintuitiveOverall, the game is fun and had potential to be something better. However with how it stands, Id say its only worth buying during a big sale, as full priced, the game is absolutely not worth it. Its cool to make your own ninja and use your favorite moves, giving that power fantasy we all love. However, besides that, the game is lackluster with mediocre visuals (excluding effects) with unbalanced mechanics and a crappy system.I cant say I recommend this game, but I can at least admit it has its fun moments. In the end Id rate the game a 4.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: At its core its probably the most fun I've ever had in an anime game. Balancing is pretty scuffed. Some moves, weapons, or tools are unnecessarily bad yet others are busted (an anime game having poor balance, ik, surprising).Base Battle, Combat Battle, and Survival mode are super fun and there are a lot of diverse builds you can viably play. Nothing is too busted in these modes. Flag Battle kinda sucks just from how few moves are viable in it. You can tell whenever they're balancing new moves the devs do not consider flag battle at all with how insanely busted some moves are in it. It's basically a stalemate for like 9 minutes of barrier and turret spam until an attack class with 2 mobility jutsu gets on the flag and then teleports across the map in seconds. I really hope it gets removed from ranked rotation. Barrier Battle was so poorly received it got removed from ranked.The base game jutsu are still viable despite how many DLC jutsu are out now. So you're not going to get ♥♥♥♥ on because you're too poor to afford the DLC. A lot of DLC moves are just more fun to use though even if they aren't necessarily better. The devs do have a tendency to overtune new releases and let them go for a while without being nerfed though. Its usually only an issue with ultimates which aren't up that often and the issue is usually the move being not realistically avoidable.I've seen a lot less cheating since I returned. However, the community is small so if you find one you're probably going to be constantly matched with them. Really your only hope is that the report button isn't just a feel good button and actually works. Please do not cheat. The community is small and its only going to get smaller if they have to deal with you cheating your ass off.

_childDocuments_.review: Based on the 6-7 hours I've put in the game, I can say. It's not worth $57.Pros:- From what I've played, the gameplay is fun. You get VR masters who give you an option to customize your loadout with whatever from Wood Style, Fire Style etc. - The VR missions can be a bit weird, one of the missions I played the boss was 130m roughly away from me and his tail went through a building and killed me. But, they are enjoyable. Beating up people with the Kubikiribōchō and strangeling them with Wood Style: Silent Strangulation. It's really cool.- The Customization is so varied, you can be the b-tec Akatsuki member you always wanted to be or be the new Naruto. It's all up to you.Cons:- The multiplayer, it's not balanced. You can be a level 19 and go up against a bunch of level 80's who can do a 30 hit combo without you even having a chance of getting up. + The connection, you run forward and get teleported back. I don't know if that is me or it's the overall EU server. It's annoying when you can't even get away without lagging back to the place where you got destroyed.- Even though the customization is really fun and varied. The flaw is that, it has "stats". An item can for example have:*The enemy has a lower chance of falling to the ground while doing short distance combat.*Temporarily boost your speed once you respawnIt's not fun when you get beat up because you were wearing something else that isn't the best pick.- It's all multiplayer, meaning if the game doesn't succed and people start leaving. You have no choice but to leave aswell, because you can't get matches. You can't level up and get more VR masters. You can't improve.In my opinion. They should make a single player type of "campaign". Where your character is essentially the MC, and you go through this tournament arc etc. It's something atleast.So, the question.Is it worth trying out?Yes. But, wait untill it's on sale to buy it. Right now, it isn't worth the money. You get so little for the price you pay. You get 6-10 missions each rank in the VR missions world. The multiplayer is laggy, and sometimes you can get disconnected from a mission if your playing with other people and The MM is not balanced.But I do recommend it. It has a ton of flaws, but at the same time it's really something I could play if the multiplayer gets balanced (+they fix the servers), and if they removed the skills on your outfit. Definetly not a bad game.

_childDocuments_.review: An outstanding game overall that I come back to time and time again.  This game offers an experience unlike other fighting/anime/brawler games.  It does this with the addition of objectives, teammates, and roles.  My personal favorite is distracting and fighting 4 people as 1 tank while your team gets to sit back, heal, and grab the objective.        The combat is actually deceptively deep with more layers the deeper you look.  I would recommend a controller unless you can get used to holding your mouse completely still so you don't frantically switch targets constantly.  When the connection is good, combat can feel fast-paced and snappy.  But, oh boy with peer-to-peer the connection can get prettyy, prettyy, prettyyy, pretty bad.  I'm talkin' take a break from the game if you are in slow hours bad.      There are some abilities in this game that are very anti-fun.  As such, don't expect to cap a point when it's only control because someone will be on it with an invincible force-field on an 10 second cooldown that lasts 10 seconds.  Also, you can only destroy these barriers with ultimates and a select few 20-second cooldown abilites.  On flag capture as well, there are exploitable abilities that will get quick and easy caps in as short as 5 seconds!  (A lot of these abilities are locked behind a dlc paywall btw so it's totally pay to win)       I must stress; I did not come here to complain, only to give a little err to caution on whether or not it's a game for you.  In fact, I urge you to observe the fact that I do recommend this game considering all said.  This game is just that fun!  In the end, if you have someone to play with or just want to play for fun and not take the game too seriously, then this game will definitely get a scratch itched you didn't know needed scratched.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is actually a lot better than I expected coming from the Ultimate Ninja Storm games. I enjoy the different format and it's fun to customize your own characters and the clothing they are wearing. I do feel the combat system is easier than the Ultimate Ninja Storm games, but at the same time they are different types of games entirely. Shinobi Striker is more of a jump around the map and use a target lock system on your opponents kind of game. It offers a fun and more creative playing environment to fight in than the linear maps in the Storm games. I do miss some of the aspects of the Storm games such as the chakra guage and ninja dashing. However, this game stands on its own well and I would recommend it to people who like Naruto in general.
