_childDocuments_.review: its a decent game, but not worth this price tag. buy it when its on sale and force your friends to play with you.i wouldnt reccomend making it 'your main game' due to how repetetive it is, but you can still have some casual fun with it for many hours.the game is fun. but it got its number of flaws you wouldnt expect in this price range.logging it for the first time, you make your fanfic self insert uchiha oc - please do not steal - with a tragic backstory. the tutorial is decent, basics are easy, you play some vr missions, they are charming - you think at first. they feel, well, naruto. we know those locations, music, characters. there is lots of fanservice - we are able to learn most iconic jutsus, the enviroments look great and polished. but then you do more vr missions - which you are forced to do, if you want to unlock more masters and abilities - and thats where the problems begin.even if areas are pretty, uhh, theres only 4 of them. i was not expecting the story to be main point, but i wish there was more to it than go on mission, mindlessly kill enemies, repeat. its grindy, its boring, it doesnt hold much of my attention. i really hoped pvp would be a different story. and it was different, but not enough for my liking.i am not very good at pvp games. my decisionmaking in wack, my reflexes are even worse, and lets not talk about sense of direction. but the game, after few hours of playing, was quite easy to understand. the gameplay is simple, yet engaging. the game is definition of easy to learn hard to master. and i quite enjoy it. i hate having to play 200 matches before understanding whats going on my screen, but after a few matches you will most probably get the hang of it needed for casual play. sure, sometimes you will wonder 'hello why i cant use my jutsus now?' or 'whats this and why it bursted my whole health?' but core gameplay is straight-forward even for novices in the genre like me. i reccomend watching some gameplay on youtube tho, to see how to move more optimally and learn most of jutsu.you are free to make a build to fit your playstyle and mode youre playing, even without dlcs you got your fair number of possibilities.thats the only thing keeping this game fresh. i think the most fun in this game isnt meta building and winning every game, but trying different loadouts. even if theyre wack its way friends. youre having fun alone, sure, but i believe solo gaming isnt doing this system justice.however, the similiar problem from pve missions occur - its repetetive after a while. its not mindless _childDocuments_.review: Cannot recommend this game in its current state. The camera and target system is some of the worst ive ever seen in my over 20 years of gaming experience and its a huuuge issue when you play pvp. For a game that has so many movement based actions you really need a good camera to keep track of people. On top of that theres also abilities in the game that will basically oneshot you even if you play a tank charachter and not being able to keep track of the people throwing these abilities because of the camera is a huge minus. The lock on function is just as bad. Sometimes you will have an enemy right in front of you 1 hit away from death, but the target system decides to target someone way behind him instead and he'll get away because of it. Very awkward to use, to the point where I dont even lock on to people anymore.Pvp is extremly unbalanced atm. The ranged class and abilities just dominate everything. They are supposed to be weak to melee classes if you can get close to them, but so far ive yet to see any weakness in the ranged class whatsoever. Not only do they do insane damage to the point where a tank feels like butter, but their abilities look like they have 0 cast time aswell.Another issue with pvp is that the matchmaking system lets you play whatever class you want and thats a problem. This is an extremly team based game where you HAVE to work togheter, which pretty much means that one game you will stomp the enemy team because you got lucky and grouped with players who pick the right classes and care about teamplay, while the next game you get unlucky, everyone picks dps, runs off on their own and you just lose without contest.Edit: Been playing for a few hours longer and found some more stuff that I do not like.Menus: It feels like they designed the menus in this game to drag out your playtime as much as possible, and it will. Not only is it slow as hell to go through them all but theres a crap ton of them and nothing is in the same place. You unlock scrolls in this game that you can trade in for items and currency, but you have to go see another person (npc) and go through a whole new set of slow as hell menus to equip these items.Being in a group is also a pain in the ass. You cant queue quests while someone is in a npc menu and if you try it will give you a message that says you cant and it will exit the entire npc menu and you have to go through all of it and find the quests again in order to try again. You also have to disband the group if you want to pick up quests from npc's and then remake the group which is just more time wasted.Gameplay is extremly shallow: Im not the biggest anime fan ill admit, im not even the biggest naruto fan (mostly because of filler episodes), but I do really like the naruto universe and the concept of it. I dont know how you can take a universe that literally has an infinite number of abilities, a crap ton of different weapons, characthers, tools, all sorts of cool variables and make that shallow, but they did. There are stats in this game, but they are basically non existent. You can get stats on gear but theres only like 4-5 of them, I dont know if ill unlock gear with different "endgame" stats eventually but I doubt it. The weapons only have 4 different stats on them and the strenght of these stats are shown by a number of stars on each stat. I think 5-6 stars is the max. You'd think that there might be a curve when it comes to weapons, that you unlock stronger weapons the more you play, but nope, first weapons you get alredy have maxed out stats in certain categories. Also the stats are not numbered. You have no idea how much damage your weapons do and if you wear something that "gives you extra max health", you have no idea how much health that equals.Matchmaking: The matchmaking in this game is just a group finder. Theres no such thing as matching you with equally skilled players in this game. One of the first missions you will have is to play a multiplayer game and you will be somewhere around level 3-5 when you get this mission. Thing is, you will get queued with people that are alot higher level then you and they will just stomp you while you wonder wtf is going on.There is also an event going on where you earn points based on a ranking. I say ranking, but there really isnt such a thing as rank in this game, infact you get rank points no matter if you lose or win and you can get grouped vs people who are at the highest rank while you are at the lowest.99% of the rewards in this game is just cosmetics. I mean there are stats on them but like I alredy mention theres just a handfull of them. It says that theres 4k items to unlock in the game, but in reality that number is only as high as it is because each items has like 20 different colour schemes and they all count as 1 individual item even though they are not.Connectivity issues: I wasnt planning on including this in the review because its technically not an issue with the mechanics of the game, but at this point its such a regular occurence even this early on after launch that its worth mentioning. Early on matches will lag like hell to the point where its virtually unplayble. You will run up walls only to be teleported down again, you'll get ontop of objectives only to be teleporter away while an enemy grabs it and you will use important abilities only to be teleported away from everyone and use them on nothing. There is also a huge issue in terms of connectivity in the game where the game will dc you from a match at the very end when the endgame score screen is supposed to pop up, instead your screen goes black and it skips the screen where you get your exp/rewards/trainer exp and you LOSE the rewards and exp you would have gotten from that match. Happens way to often, maybe 40% of the time.TL:DR: If im gonna sum this game up in 2 words it would have to be "wasted opportunity". It really does feel like its made by a bunch of business people who all sat down around a table and then someone said "hey I hear people like this naruto thing, maybe we can make a few quick bucks of it".

_childDocuments_.review: As a long-time fan of the Naruto franchise, I had high hopes for Naruto to Boruto Shinobi Striker, but sadly, it failed to meet even my lowest expectations. Here's why:Lackluster Gameplay: The gameplay mechanics are clunky and unpolished. Movement feels awkward, and combat lacks depth, making battles feel repetitive and unsatisfying. It's as if the developers took a step back in terms of gameplay compared to previous Naruto titles.Limited Content: Despite the vast world of Naruto to draw inspiration from, Shinobi Striker feels empty and devoid of content. The number of playable characters is disappointingly low, and the game modes are uninspired and quickly become stale.Technical Issues: From matchmaking problems to frequent crashes, Shinobi Striker is plagued with technical issues that hinder the overall gaming experience. It's frustrating to invest time and effort into a match only to be abruptly kicked out due to server instability.Questionable Design Choices: The decision to focus heavily on multiplayer leaves solo players feeling neglected. The single-player experience is lackluster, with a shallow story mode that fails to capture the essence of the Naruto universe.Microtransaction Madness: Like many modern games, Shinobi Striker is riddled with microtransactions that feel predatory and exploitative. Progression is heavily tied to purchasing in-game currency, creating an unfair advantage for those willing to spend real money.Overall, Naruto to Boruto Shinobi Striker is a disappointing addition to the Naruto franchise. With its lackluster gameplay, limited content, technical issues, questionable design choices, and excessive microtransactions, it fails to capture the magic of its source material and is best avoided by fans looking for a truly immersive ninja experience.Cheaters : When you are in the lobby there are lots of beginners who get rare skins with very low skills and levels, when playing with cheaters you feel very bored because when on a mission it is so easy to be defeated by casting the ultimate many times without cool down, this is very disturbing for beginning players.Not recommended to play 2/5

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly this could be such a good game. The gameplay is really fun but there is just some small yet serious flaws holding it back. Mainly focused around single player.Now yes I know your going to say "but this is a multiplayer game". While I would agree I'm lucky to see more than 200 people on this game ever... the problem is the game is so dead getting matches can be really hard, especially based on what area you live in. This would be fine if I had enough single player content to keep me happy. This brings me to the VR missions and the VR masters. To earn new stuff you need to select a VR master and playing the game earns xp towards them. The problem is that you get lots of xp for playing multiplayer (sometimes it can take me 10 minutes to queue for even one match). This would be okay if they had a bot mode that allowed for full xp or slightly reduced to allow us to level up even if we cant find other players but even a "bot" game requires one other player which takes forever sometimes. Then we have the single player/co-op missions. these give barely enough xp and if you fail and waste 5-10 minutes you get nothing, they are just wildly inferior to the pvp. Which makes this game hard to recommended because the games so dead you wont be able to experience half the content.6/10 - If the game let us play properly even with a dead player base Id consider giving this around a 7/10. Some of the new updates have made it slightly more enjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: Keep away from children, too much gambling in this game for them.Basically, this is Dragon Ball Xenoverse but with Naruto and Boruto characters. The principle of gameplay follows the same kind of structure: Go in an instanced area and complete objective, either alone or in group. There's absolutely no story to follow compared to DBXV.There's PVP but Im not participating in it, I hate PVP period. The game looks really nice at 200% resolution scaling. The auto-aiming system and melee combat is a bad mix, you often end up attacking the wrong target. The lock-in system is useful but slow and you have no more control over the camera, you become blind near walls.The matchmaking system for coop missions is bad as well, players have very limited information on the lobbies and the chat is super limited. If you don't like grinding, this isnt for you. Everything in the shop is overpriced for that purpose. There's obviously gambling micro-transaction but that's to be expected from a compagny who like to exploit people gambling sickness. The free lootbox system is decent, I got myself a couple of nice drops after grinding all the VR masters. Don't expect good rewards after though. I still think premium lootboxes should be dupe protected and only for SS if they insist on doing time-base content.Where do we buy older SS content?Network latency when playing with other players and you often DC from lobbies. (P2P)Season pass gives good content for the game but only if there's a discount. Voice chat volume is very low most of the time and no advanced audio options.The music is nice, never had a problem with it while playing.Perfect for LAN parties and people of the same country. Overall score: 4/10 - needs quality of life improvementPros:Graphics, Custom characters, DLC, Social, Cosmetics, MusicCons:Monetary system, Chat system, auto-aim/lock-in, matchmaking for coop, Network latency, Voice chat, No story

_childDocuments_.review: Get this game on sale if you can , not worth the $30+ dollars nearly $60 that it costs. i got it on sale for about 12 dollars or something like that. Game does combat pretty well. the moves all look and feel pretty good and is a pretty on point most of the time. Balancing is an issue as defense type pretty much rules this game. Basically you have moves like sand shield and petrification jutsu that if used right with your heavy attack IE my favorite executioners blade , you tend to be hard to interrupt and just whale on people. There is a laundry list of things that need to be improved or changed. 1.) balancing2.) make it so you can have a themed move set. (example: cannot have full byakugan moveset as palm rotation is set as defence class while the rest are healing class and i personally would have loved it to be an escape jutsu instead of a ability  1 or 2 .  same with trying to make a sharingan user moveset, can't really use kamui climax in order to work with sharingan and kamui etc etc. 3.) skill system need straight up rework in my opinion. There are not enough abilities in skill options to allow you to max out your cooldowns or max health or whatever.4.) need the ability to have a specific look without it being directly tied to skills. i want max cooldown but cannot make a outfit that doesn't look like everyone else. 5.) bugs, demon wind shurikan sometimes hits once and other times will hit you for almost all your health as it takes you along for the ride a lot of the time.  there are more too6.) more moves from characters in the naruto-boruto universe and their skill sets. so far i like what was added but also a lot of the moves are playing it safe or are literal copies of similar moves for example lightning blade, lariat , and chidori, (i like them being there but need more moves in general)7.) player base and matchmaking is low right now making it impossible at times to find games. I feel like it is mostly times i choose to play but also that i see crowds next to matchmaking npc but no matches are being found making it seem more like a bug. 8.)again player base, because that will be the death of this game. all in all, if you are looking for a fun naruto game with many of the iconic moves and jutsu /characters you love and duking it out in capture the flag and small events like FFA , hold the base , and some other ones i never got to play for above reasons, this game can be super super fun, but we need more people and we need bandai or whoever to do something quick because it seems like they kinda don't care about this game anymore from what i can see being semi new but playing  this game on binge. i know some people like games that are like this and the game is fun for sure, but just know that finding matches as of now is pretty tough. if you are ok with that or are on in prime time you will find matches but not necessarily the ones you want as again some game modes have lots of people and others are completely empty.  i have yet to be able to play quick match since getting the game and i see no news anywhere about how it is going to be fixed. BUYER BEWARE!! also DAMN FUNi recommend this game but only to the right people and with right expectations...and only if on sale

_childDocuments_.review: Hi Fellow Ninjas.Bandai Namco has long since catered to Naruto fans through its ninja storm series, wherein the canon played out in classic anime style with tag team fights in 3d arenas.This time, Shinobi striker gives you a chance to be your own persona in a living breathing Narutoverse in a pure pvp environment. Its a virtuous mix of rpg and moba (not top down like your fav Dota and League of legends, more like a third person shooter) ....wherein you'll capture flags, bases and many other pvp modes, my personal favorite being team deathmatch though :)Classes are 4, ala your everyday rpg,attack,defence, ranged and heals.Although base classes are interchamgeable on the fly,skills are not. Every skill and usable weapon is tied to a class.Bandai Namco and Soleil have done a great job in creating the sense of familiarity in terms of the characters, outfits and skills.Dress up ur female Uchiha in stylish Sarada outfit while slashing at enemies with Sasuke's Kusanagi sword. You can choose to maim the opposition with a well placed Raikiri or simply create epic moments standing still and burning your enemies to a crisp with Amaterasu. Pains famous jutsus, the Shinra Tensei and Planetary devastation are all there for keeps.This is surely a game made with Love. It has a few hiccups on the technical side , otherwise it is a good arena fighter. Naruto fans will savor the opportunity to be a proper Shinobi in Narutoverse and go toe to toe against the Uchiha brothers together in a mission.The PVP is polished. The Pve could have been better, but then that would make it a copy of its distant cousin,the Dragonball xenoverse series.Instead, Shinobi striker is its own game. And within its own unique identity, this game manages to impress.A lot.Non Naruto fans might also like the way pvp combat and its controls play out. One of the few games which encourages players to take risks, try out new ability combinations, and not confirm to the fatalistic idea of Meta gaming.In short, Shinobi striker encourages You to be You. Hope you find this review useful.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, this game grows on you after awhile.At first I was iffy, with the negative reviews, the backlash towards BANDAI NAMCO for matchmaking issues, trust me it seems very fishy. Hell I even sent a refund request, only to play the game more and fall in love with it. If this was somehow incorporated into a singleplayer campaign, oh my god it would be amazing and would knock these reviews out of the ballpark.This games price is too steep, at most this game should be 35$ for the content its selling, I would not believe the community who constantly write on the discussions on why BANDAI hasn't commented on something thats just happening today (as im writing this review), its not like the majority of their audience are english speaking americans and their own company is situated in Tokyo.Like ive seen with other quotes, issues do vary per person, and some people are just to idiotic to update their own reviews. _childDocuments_.review: Game on sale is worth grabbing especially if you like Naruto. The game does leave much to be desired and does make you think what could've been. Had there been more maps and variety of both offline and online game modes along with a good match making system in place this game would've been a lot better and I could've done an infinite amount of hours potentially.Shinobi Striker heavily lacks in creativity. A chance to add avatar parts in the style of Naruto instead of just mix and matching Naruto character avatar parts for example; Shikamaru's hair with Sasuke's face would make the game more alive. They do a good job with weapons and substitutions although weapons are set by class so if you want to be an attack type and have a katana this isn't the game. Developers should have included custom Jutsu along with the Jutsu from Naruto I mean this was the chance to be amazingly creative. Lastly if you are a Boruto fan you may be disappointed, if i remember rightly there is only 5 or so characters from the series including season passes. The game has bigger problems and the ball was fumbled. on sale its roughly £10 for the deluxe which I would recommend if you plan to buy as you get all season 1 pass DLC with the game and it can be a bit pay to win and if you don't have friends to play with, you WILL struggle online but you can still have fun. I've played 300+ Hours in game not to mention a crazy amount on Xbox One but I will no longer be coming back to Shinobi Striker and here's why;The community has been asking for variety of new maps since the game came out, match making and much more however the developers have only cared to put out season passes for characters and generate money from new and loyal players, which in fairness I have been one of but I am tired of being in the majority who just gets ignored. I've had a lot of good times and really enjoyed the game but i cant think of it without being disappointed immensely about what could've been so too summarise; I don't recommend this game at normal price its okay on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I have payed many fighting games in my time ranging from the original Virtual Fighter, Street Fighter, Tekken, Mortal Kombat, Dead or Alive ect, and I can say that some of the titles are flops and some are not. Naruto was a fantastic anime series that i watched about half the episodes and enjoyed it but have not seen Buruto saying that this game has all the classic characters from the series and it is great to see a new title release from an anime series. I will start with the cons and that is the game is just to short for a fully priced game and you are limited to a single area out of many villages that there could have been unfortunately in this there is only one and in that village you have a VR room to do mission battles and and online room to do online battles others include character customisation and rewards. Again with the crazy amount of DLC but you can get a season pass that will grant you access to a large amount of that DLC at a significantly reduce price. The other cons is that it can become repetitive after awhile and online battles can be extremely difficult and requires a lot of practise. The pros however are great, your ability to climb up and down walls and cliffs completely change how a fighting game interacts with a much larger arena area and the scope to move in ways that i personally have never done before in a fighting game and it just changes everything. Another great pro is the ability that you get in a game, you have to choose a type from attack to defence and then you have a set of four ability's the first two will be your main weapons so choose wisely, it is great fun to go through them to find the ones that work best for you. Overall in my opinion this game could have been epic had there been more work on expanding most areas and more of an interesting story line had that been done this game could have rivalled the final fantasy series in a big way and outclassed most fighting games while also giving a battlefield type feel to it, it is a real disappointment when you realise what it could have been and i would not pay full prices for this title when you could get a copy of the new FFVII remake for the same price, simply put the game is lacking a lot in many areas but is great fun and a new level of fighting game and for that reason i will not be recommending it.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought the game a few days ago during a sale and it was only 14 AUD, which is a heck of a lot cheaper than the usual 70, and for that price, you'd think that the game would have a lot to offer, but it does not. Bandai Namco has had 3 years to make this game better, but in terms of content, it's severely lacking. I'm not saying that I don't enjoy the game, actually far from it, but would I recommend this game to other people? Absolutely not.So far, the things that make this game pretty mediocre in my opinion is that the offline content is just a rinse-and-repeat type of thing, where you fight the same dumb enemies, proceed to fight the boss if there is any, and finish the mission. Now imagine doing all of that in the same 3 to 5 maps with the same enemies over and over again, sounds boring doesn't it? As for customization, it's alright I guess, but Bamco could have done more, because right now, your weapon type doesn't really matter, because they all function the same but with different looks.As for PvP, which is actually the main attraction of this game, the game modes are good but it gets a bit stale after awhile. Not to mention the fact that the game only gets patched a few times a year,, so don't expect the underlying problems like cheaters, crashes, and dark monitor screens (???) to get patched quickly. You'd think that, since Bamco itself announced that it's celebrating its accomplishment of having 6 million players play this game, they'd maintain and add more content frequently, but unfortunately, they don't.Overall,  the game seems like a cash-grab in hindsight, but I genuinely enjoy the game, even though the price tag is quite questionable, but this is not a game that I would recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; Game sucks, if you want a create your own character anime game, go play Xenoverse 2 or something more complete feeling.Don't buy this game if your looking for a game that feels complete. There is no story, the combat is very rigid and you will die to no fault of your own, and by the time you see the credits you will most likely still have the same ninjisu attacks you started with. The only good thing this game has going for it being the only Naruto game where you can create your own character and that's alot of fun, you can choose different weapons according to class, and all the clothes have special affects and variations on color. The combat can feel fun if you get a good rythm going, bouncing from enemy to enemy as you fight, but that comes to a screeching halt once you fight a giant enemy, they all have massive amounts of health, never move, and attack so rapidly and with such massive range you become forced to rely on ninjitsu to widdle the giants health down while dodging attacks, however dodging said attacks are easier said then done. In a game like Xenoverse with a combat style similar to this, it's easy to dodge, you can easily boost and fly circles around the attack. However, in Shinobi Strikers for the most part, you move very slowly, your best way to get around being jumping wall to wall using wire kunai, even then, sometimes you'll end up falling to your death due to the lack of range on the wire kunai. All in all, the game feels like an early access game that has yet to release it's story mode.

_childDocuments_.review: To be honest, I bought this game fully expecting to refund it after an hour and a half. After seeing the gameplay footage and heavy reliance on online matchmaking I really wasn’t interested leading up to its release. Being a fan of Naruto (Storm) games, I figured I'd try it out anyway, have some fun making a character, and end up hating the game.And so it turns out, the game is… not that bad? As others have mentioned, it does feel pretty empty at the moment, with only a few things to do in the desolate plaza of a hubworld. I expect (and hope) that more content will be added in this area, as the space is needlessly large for what’s currently in place. It would be nice to have more options for offline play too, especially in the almost inevitable event that the online scene dies out. Other than that, the combat feels satisfying and the matchmaking is fast paced, making it a good pick-up-and-play team fighter. The character customization is decent too, and probably the main reason I’m deciding to keep the game and hope for more updates. If you’re a fan of Naruto and had fun with the Dragon Ball Xenoverse games, you’ll most likely enjoy Shinobi Striker. If nothing else, try out this game for the character creation and just play a few matches. Pros:[+] Fast paced, high action gameplay[+] Solid character customization with plenty of cosmetic options[+] Basically fanservice for fans of the Naruto seriesCons:[-] Fairly empty world outside of matches; not much else to do[-] Potential for matchmaking to die out after a while[-] Somewhat overpriced in its current state

_childDocuments_.review: Alright first serious review. NARUTO TO BORUTO: SHINOBI STIRKER is awesome. I picked this game up not expecting that much but after playing 3 matches I was hooked. I got 24 hours in almost 4 days and I really enjoyed the experience. May aswell get all the positives out of the way now and get into the negitives later. Positives: Character creation gives you a perfect amout of creative freedom but not to much to the point where your overwhelmed with dozens of different options for like bone structure and useless stuff like that. Afrer you create your character you can edit it at any time but things like height and body shape you will need ingame currency to change but your not stuck with anything. After buying the game you can get anything in the game without putting money into it. Perfect amount of different ways to play the game, there are 4 classes (attack, range, defence, and healing) and each of these classes as up to 13 different abilities you can mix and match which makes you feel like your not bound by the default abilities of your class like in many other games. More on the abilites (jutsus). You can combine these jutsus any way you want which feels really fun and gives you reasons to keep playing and strive for your dream ability set. The VR Master leveling system is very rewarding and fun to use. Masters are unlocked through playing other masters or taking quests from npcs around the lobby and getting all of them and all they have to offer takes a long time and keeps you wanting to play. The gameplay is a balance of simplicity and skill. Skill in this game does not revolve around aim or mastery of controls, skill in this game is experience, coordination, and game sense. Negitives: The game requires coordination and is a big part of "skill" in this game but the game makes it kind of hard for you to do this. There is no clear understandable voice chat system that you can strategize with your team with. There is also no chat box where you can type to your team or the enemy for that matter. The game servers for online play are bugged and sometimes it will take over 10 minutes to even get into a game even though the game is pretty populated. Balanced matching can also be a hassle sometimes because you could have a team with 4 level 10-30s and the enemy team could have people level 100 and above. The VR missions can be boring and repitive sometimes too easy somtimes too hard. The tutorial says the VR missions will be from the "famous battles" of past ninjas but none of the missions connect to the anime at all and let down alot of people. Yeah thats about it, alot of the issues I have can be fixed easily so I hope they will be and yeahhhhh. I would rate this game 8.5/10 (currently rating may change).

_childDocuments_.review: I have a pretty fun time playing this. It's pretty simplistic in terms of gameplay, with a strong focus on pvp with a side of pve for missions. There's a couple of different gamemodes, some kind of event always running, and a lot of customization in terms of avatar. Events are mostly the same but provide unique cosmetics, weapons, and outfits to unlock.However, most of the jutsus are locked behind DLCs -- you have to buy characters or season passes in order to unlock more jutsu and some cosmetics, though the base game does have a fair selection of characters. If you're eyeing this game but aren't sure, buy it on sale. It seems to go on sale semi-frequently, up to 80% off. Wait for a sale to buy the game or DLC, you'll really save a lot of money.Regardless, I absolutely have a blast playing this. It's super fun to play and I enjoy making builds for different gamemodes. You don't have to buy the DLC to enjoy it, although you would likely get more out of the game for doing so.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like Naruto and world around it, I would definitely recommend this game. At the beginning it looks like a mess, but trust me once you get used to the maps, controls and get to know ninjutsu, everything is smooth and quite easy to read and react. _childDocuments_.review: I grew up watching the Naruto anime and playing the Naruto games like many others my age, so when i saw this game my instinct was to dislike it. This game is so different than any other Naruto game that has been released before. I grew up playing the fast paced, 1v1 fighter games they released for each season, the type of games where you followed the storyline for a bit and then could play as your favorite ninja against your friends and I remember loving this concept and thinking it could never be improved on. A couple weeks back Shinobi Strikers was available for only $10 and while i knew I wouldn't like it I chose to buy it anyway, it was worth a shot. BOY WAS I WRONG! This game is incredible, if i felt like a ninja playing the past Naruto games these made me feel like I was a member of the hidden villages. The ability to customize your own character is so fun and I enjoy that you can create your idea of a perfect ninja the more you play the game and unlock rewards. I feel an addictive pull to play this game whenever I'm not simply because of all the new things there are to unlock and equip. VR Masters is a great concept to use as an intro for those who didn't grow up on the manga or anime and its a great way to please the long time Naruto fans with some nostalgia. I would highly recommend getting this game especially on sale. The only negative I see that many may feel is the lack of a real 'story mode' that many of us are used to is replaced with VR Masters and, while it's a cool concept, there isn't very much material to work with for very long so it ends up being really short in length. This game is sort of what you make it, you can play whatever way you want using your favorite shinobi's jutsus to win matches. It's incredibly unique and it is difficult for me to name a game similar to it, it took a great anime and turned it into an incredible stand alone, online game. DON'T MISS OUT!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a Naruto game that has many fun elements to its combat and customization. The combat is mainly PvP focused, but there are some PvE missions that can be completed for accessory items. Customization is done in an RPG-like fashion where clothing and accessories can make your character move faster or do more damage with abilities. There are some clothing and accessories that are tied down to specific classes. These classes consist of Attack (Damage), Ranged (Damage), Defense (Tank), and Support (Hybrid, Healer).  Attack gets up close while doing a lot of damage. Ranged keeps their distance while attacking from a distance. Defense takes hits and thwarts enemies. Support hinders enemies and benefits allies. All of the classes have different types of weapons available to them. These weapons have different attack patterns for their light and heavy attacks. Attack is the only class that go into a fight without using a weapon.  Abilities are locked to each specific class. Two Jutsus/Ninjutsus, one Tool, and one Secret Technique. Ninjutsu is used to damage enemies and protect/heal allies. Tools are class specific items that can used to start combos, prevent enemy movement, or even stop a Secret Technique from activating. Secret Techniques can be game changers that each class can build upon by doing their designed role. Examples of this would be doing damage as Attacker, hitting enemies with Senbons as Ranged, reflecting attacks as Defense, and burdening enemies/providing boons to allies as Support. There are are some Secret Techniques that can be charged faster than others.  This Naruto game is online focused. The servers are maintained, at the very least, once a week. An Internet connection is needed to play. The servers tend to kick people back to the lobby. This happens when in the process of joining a match, while on the loading screen, and even while in a match. There is no matchmaking thus there will be a good chance that a group of new players will be fighting against a group of highly skilled veterans.  The combat in this game consist of Combat, Base, Flag, and Barrier. Combat has fights with a set amount of points. During Combat, if a teammate falls off the map or gets knocked out then the team loses a point. Base contains areas that can be captured and defended. Points are gained if your team has at least two bases while having three will give points faster. Flag is a mix of combat and base where if an enemy is defeated then their flag becomes easier to capture. The flag is placed on a pedestal near each teams spawn point. Four kills can make the flag easier to pick up. There is also the option of taking the flag without any points, but this will take a while to capture. Carrying the flag slows your character to a crawl. Barrier gives us a boss battle. This boss battle is done through an Attack or Defend style of gameplay. Attack must pull up pillars and then attack the boss. Defend will try to prevent the pillars from being lifted and attack the Attackers while defending their boss.  I have had fun playing Shinobi Striker. However, I can not recommend this game as of this review day. The main reason for this poor recommendation would have to be the hackers/exploiters that are currently parading the game. There are hackers that will use Secret Techniques at the start of a fight and will use them every second. Alt+F4 will be your friend if your matched up against these types of players.  Regardless of the parasites currently eating away the fun that this game is trying to provide. If your up for some Naruto based PvP with a customized character that can use your favorite Naruto character abilities then this might be the game your looking for, but I do recommend getting this game when it is on sale. Main reason I recommend getting the game this way is because of the season pass characters. They can still be played without buying them but their abilities, hair styles, clothing, weapons, titles, and lobby actions will be unavailable.  Starting out in Shinobi Striker I  recommend not doing the VR missions first. Focus on the PvP Rookie matches until account level 30. The reason for this is that the Rookie matches become unavailable after account level 30, and the VR missions give account experience thus making your time playing PvP less enjoyable.~Edit: 10/2/2021~Action is being taken to help the games overall enjoyment. They're banning hackers and the like. I have switched to Recommend due to these actions being taken.~Edit: 12/31/2021~I want to enjoy this game for what it is, but the constant hackers that pillage this game are strangely increasing after actions were taken by the company. I'm going to leave it as a down thumb. If there was a middle thumb then my review wouldn't keep getting edited. This will be my last edit though for it seems that there will be no way for this company to protect their game from these types of people. Recently learned that this game does not have dedicated servers. Meaning this game has peer-to-peer which can and will disconnect anyone that can not connect to the designated host of the match, or if the host of the match is running on poor internet connection. That does not mean that the game is unplayable with poor internet though. There are still players that are using exploits too, but they are few and far between.

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot recommend this game to Naruto fans, online fighting fans, or solo players. This game is an imbalanced struggle to enjoy and I'll go into detail as to why.I give my personal experience and thoughts on:Balancing (there is none)Gameplay (defense, movement, etc)Online componentsIf that's not something you want to read, thank you for your time and hopefully a different review can give you what you want to know!I still play for the co-op VR missons, those can actually be a lot of fun.I must say this first and foremost because  My first few experiences were grating, to put it lightly. At the time of writing this review, I was only maybe level 15, having only played offline VR missions, as they're known in the game, and thought I had a decent chance online. I first tried to enter the beginners matchmaking, but waiting for half an hour during the height of most games player count (between 4 and 6 PM) wasn't something I was willing to do so I decided on the main quick match.I was teamed up with fellow low level players and was pitted against a party of level 200s with master rankings. Needless to say we were absolutely butchered with no contest. I thought that was a one off and went back into matchmaking. Same situation, same exact players. I thought "third time's the charm" and was actually met with a fun game, but was disconnected for no definitive reason. Okay then, let's try again. Same low level team, same exact high tier party (legitimately the same exact players, too), same exact result.This game will not allow a new solo player any time to get accustomed to how it works without throwing them against literal god tier opponents who have all the DLC and strongest moves. The player base is also so low that you will frequently encounter the same exact players. First impressions matter, and this one left me in a state of confused anguish with no learning experience. It was just join a game, get wrecked, rinse and repeat. There is no way to "train to get good," there isn't even a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ training mode. The VR training is worthless, it gives you absolutely no way of experiencing the high speed bully sessions of the multiplayer. Throwing a literally freshly born baby into the depths of the ocean tied to a cinder block. Good luck. It didn't have that, "huh, maybe I can switch my strategy and try again," feel to it. It was just getting beaten to a pulp and nothing changes. Throw money at the game to get the best trainers, spam VR missions with your god squad, get the best jutsu, bully everyone in multiplayer. This is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Shinobi Strike me dead please.Amidst the chaotic agony of the sorry excuse for a PvP game, the lack of control over your own character became more obvious. Once you are juggled, you are dead. Once you are against two or (god forbid) more people, you are dead. If you are one-on-one with someone, but they have stronger moves, or a direct counter to your class, you're dead. So, essentially, especially if you're new, 90% of the time, you're dead. Team work is emphasized, but non-existant when playing solo. I repeat; The only real way to defend is to block, but a good chunk of moves are guard breakers, and the game seems proud of that. Other than that, you have the substitution jutsu. Useful, right? Well, not when it takes 20 seconds to recharge, doesn't bring you far enough away from the enemy so they can just rush you again, you can't block right after using it because you appear in the air, and oh yeah, the enemy can flat out disable it and pound on you until you throw your control/break your keyboard. There's a dash, but it's slow and goes nowhere, better off holding block until it breaks.Even moving around feels like agony. Running is super slow, dashing gets you nowhere, and your attacks often fling you in the wrong direction. Did I forget to mention there's no way to stop a combo once you've put in the inputs? Yeah, so while you're attacking nobody because they used the substitution on you, they can throw a Rasengan right into your back. It's especially frustrating since your attacks  at all once they get out of it, or in VR missions when you kill an enemy, you keep kicking the air around you rather than lock onto the next guy.Lock on, that's also horribly broken. The camera itself is a travesty, it's impossible to keep track of everything when there's so much happening on screen, let alone trying to find a person. So lock on is needed, but it doesn't stick to them as nicely as it should. Instead, it offers a side angle for a cool look that the enemy can dodge out of, set up an attack while you can't see them, and destroy you. Not locked on? Attacks fling you around, they do that for the enemy too, they'll be dashing passed you in every direction for those 5 grueling seconds until the sweet release of death.The audacity of this design choice is so astronomically awful that I can barely put it into words. Ya know that awful situation I described above of being unfairly matched? Wouldn't it be great if you could just quit and match make again while that god team is busy so you can maybe find a good game more your level? Too bad. No. Wrong. Bad thoughts there, pal, because you are stuck being bullied into the dirt with no means of escape aside from outright closing the entire game. Even worse, throw some hackers into the mix and that's a whole new kind of "I hate it here." That leads me to:There's no "recent players" either, so you can't find them post game.If the examples above weren't compelling enough, the combat itself is all about stun locks. A stun lock meaning  That is a huge chunk of this game and something mind numbing to be stuck in, especially when the substitution takes so long to charge. As a new player in PvP, you will spend far more time running, being stun locked, and dying than doing any damage yourself, let alone getting a kill or two.The game revolves around two attack types, strong and weak, as well as ninja tools and jutsu. Jutsu are there, they function well enough, but some feel obviously better than others, making DLC trainers, i.e pay to win, that much more overpowered. Ninja tools are just as bad in this game as other Naruto games, except they're on a cool down, like your jutsu, instead of some kind of limit. Doesn't make them any less worthless. Ultimates function as well, but suffer the same pay to win bias as the base jutsu. The weak and strong attacks can be fun, but they don't combo too well and can easily send you passed the enemy or into someone else's attack. Don't rely on them. Yeah, don't rely on your most basic of moves, the literal foundation of a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ game, which are supposed to be something useful.I mentioned the atrocities of the defensive systems above, but will reiterate here. The blocking is useless and easily broken, the dodge shouldn't even be there, the substitution jutsu is laughable, and there's this deflect move that doesn't work because the enemies attack registration lags, and even if you successfully deflect, they can rush right back at you again and break your guard. So, stop playing literally anything but mashing all attack buttons until you die. Because, ya know, playing a game to keep yourself alive long enough to play the objective is stupid.

There is also a solo/co-op set of missions you can do if you want to get certain jutsus first before touching PvP. However, they are not as interesting as the PvP modes.Equipment matters, and the best ones are locked behind a gacha. However, you can easily farm the currency used (scrolls) by playing a lot. The game lacks polish in some areas, but overall, it's a decent Naruto game. The only downside it has no matchmaking so prepare to fight against group of sweaty players and it crashes a lot. A LOT. If you are a fan of the franchise, I would recommend getting it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Before we start, do note this is a online multiplayer focused game before you buy it. If you're wanting a campaign or anything like that, this is not the game for you. Though there are "missions" you can play alone with bots if not with other players, you do have to be connected to the servers to play this game overall.It's a new experience for Naruto. It's not Ultimate Ninja storm, it's obviously not the classic 2D fighter. It's an semi-open world 4v4 PVP (or PVE for co-op missions) fighter. You have the ability to jump very high with distance, run across walls, ect. The fighting mechanics is like a classic fighting-adventure style game, mixed with MMO elements. You have your light/heavy attacks, two jutsu for abilities, ninja tools to help you and or your team survive, you can kinda make builds so-to-speak, and so on. It's basically something like Paladins or Overwatch, but it's a fighting game.The gameplay is fast and very fluid. Overall combat and stringing combos feels nice, movement across obstacles is nice... How the game feels when fighting and doing other certain things; everything feels pretty good and to me, it drives me to keep playing. The controls in my personal experience took me a bit to get used to, but they're not bad at all. The one complaint I do have is the blocking/dashing mechanic. If you want to block, you have to make sure you are standing still, not moving your character at all. Pressing the block button while moving will execute a dash. In general games, when moving, pressing the block button will make your character block right on the dime, while dashing is executed by pressing block twice whilst moving your thumbstick to your desired location, or maybe tapping the thumbstick whilst blocking. How blocking/dashing in this game works is unnecessarily difficult. Not to mention I feel like dashing doesn't have enough invisibility frames and it doesn't travel far enough. Also on that note, the lock-on system. Again, comparing to other games, when facing an enemy which your camera is focused on, you should automatically lock onto the next enemy after defeating that one. After you defeat one in this game, you'd have to turn your camera and spot the enemy who is still within your range and possibly is going to get the first hits in on you since you'd have to re-lock to that enemy. Despite these two annoying problems however, it's still fun.Customization...You create your avatar from the start, completing missions/multiplayer battles and training with "Masters" will earn you more cosmetics, weapons, jutsus, and so on. Cosmetics is not just for show though. This is one part where making your "build" comes in. Each cosmetic item has up one or two bonus effects such as boosting your maximum HP, break opponents shields easier, more damage, and so on.Multiplayer? Considering this is a multiplayer focused game, it's seemingly a bit unoptimized. Matchmaking in my experience takes a very long time to find players. Though it's clearly showing many people are online, I have to wait over 5 minutes to find a match sometimes...and sometimes it's instant. My experience in-game isn't very good either. Opponents hit me before they are actually close to me, and delayed inputs sometimes happen. These in-game problems aren't too bad, as they only occasionally happen, it's still playable. But they are flaws nevertheless and need to be fixed, especially the entire matchmaking.This game looks really great, graphically. The art style is the same as the UNS series, but with some additional textures, shadows, special effects and whatnot, everything looks so much better than UNS imo, and it's beautiful. I am running this game with a GTX 1060 3G, i7-8700, and 16 GB of ram. It's running at a stable 60 most of the time...most. Frames will drop when I run on walls for some reason. Not all the time though, just sometimes...it's random. It could just be my pc, but it is strange...Sure, this isn't UNS and it doesn't have a campaign. But if you are into multiplayer MMOs, like modes such as deathmatch, capture the flag, king of the hill, ect, and would like to create your own Deviantart Naruto OC? Give it a try. It's really fun. But again, matchmaking has issues. So be prepared to wait some minuted before finding a match. However, once you do, you'll typically stay with those players the next match or can easily find another. Not all the time, but it's something.

He threw the cigarette that was smoking on the floor and said he would never smoke again and tried hard to keep that promise, unfortunately, three years later he died of lung cancer. _childDocuments_.review: Naruto: Xenoverse, this is not.For what it's worth: What IS there is quite solid and could form the foundation of a genuinely good game. The problem is - there's very little there.First off, the single-player experience is unfun at *best*. It consists of the same 5 or 6 missions repeated at higher and higher difficulties until finally the credits roll, and there's nothing to them. Just spam buttons until the mission is over, and don't worry about dying because your only "lives" are the time limit, which you have plenty of time in every mission to finish.But of course, the main draw of this game is the multiplayer, so it doesn't lose that much for the single player. However, the player vs CPU just consists of more of the same missions over and over, just with 3 other human players with you. And what's worse is, as much of an afterthought these PvE missions are, you're REQUIRED to do them to actually unlock all the trainers that you have to go through to unlock more skills.As for the PvP...it exists. A grand total of 5 maps, with 4 gamemodes, 2 of which are locked in quick play and *3* are locked in ranked. The skills are all basically the same exact thing from a small selection of skill types, there's no matchmaking whatsoever, some skills are downright broken...again, the poor single player is excuseable because that's not the main draw of this game, but to compensate the multiplayer needs to *actually be good itself*, and it's not.Even character creation just amounts to "how tall do you want to be?" and "pick from a selection of very slightly different faces". There's no interesting outfits, nothing new to the game itself, every outfit is just the clothes from a canon character, and even that selection is relatively smallAgain, what is there is good - mechanically things are smooth, for the most part. Traversing maps with wall running and super jumping is easy and enjoyable, but you can't have a good game with just the foundation. I've seen game betas with more, and more varied, content than this

_childDocuments_.review: This game is hell on earth, one of the worst online games I've ever experienced. Unbalanced beyond belief, riddled with bugs, glitches, and crashes that will make you want to off yourself every time you read the word "fatal" or "error". Playerbase is either newborns who just picked up a controller for the first time or tryhards who play this game like it's their job. The sole developer working on this (nearly) dead game has no quality control team to test the new content they release, so every new weapon, throwable, or jutsu that drops is 9 times out of 10 a new cause for late stage cancer. The game is nearly unplayable without buying character DLCs as most of the starter Jutsu are mediocre, boring, or both. The gameplay is pretty enjoyable if you don't  match with a 4 stack team of nothing but meta builds, and to it's credit, it has been less frequent as of late, but that could just be on account of it being a dead game. For the first time in the 6 years since this game's release, the dev(s?) finally announced they're going to focus less on adding new content and work instead on performance issues (refer to bugs, glitches, and crashes mentioned previously) and balancing. Before this most recent update, the game was riddled with Kurama Claw users spamming the heavy to infinite combo, which you couldn't get out of because of sub locking. After nearly a year (literally 12 whole months) of the Kurama claw remaining untouched as the pinnacle of braindead builds, the single dev finally woke up from his hibernation and realized that only pressing heavy shouldn't be something that wins you 90% of your games. Also there is no crossplay, so you can only play with people on steam, making this game even deader than it should be. In summation, this game is genuine dog ass, the players are toxic as hell, and the word "balance" doesn't exist in it's vocabulary. But it's usually pretty fun.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: It is time for me to rate this game with all its aspects.After 50 hours of playtime, I have gotten to level 1 prestige 2 without any extreme amount of grind, although you will get free jutsus, secret techniques etc. it is most likely that you will have to spend money on about 3-5 DLCs one being of course Madara (majestic go brr). To get your first jutsus you just have to finish the “storyline“ aka. talking to NPCs, they give you a VR mission and you do it. Congrats you got a VR master, thats where more grind comes in. To actually get all their jutsus, you have to level the VR master to 10 stars, which alone takes about 5 games of multiplayer (from my experience). Now that you have done the storyline, you own the majority of free VR masters. After that all you mostly do is collect cosmetics and weapons and play multiplayer (with bad matchmaking) and play more VR missions. Once you play multiplayer you see people clapping you with jutsus you havent EVER seen in the game, and then comes the final act. The DLCs. Although, when on sales, the DLCs are very affordable, you wont be finished with just one of them. So lets say you buy a few DLC character, then you go to your mailbox and claim them, well guess what you still have to grind the VR masters to level 10. It isnt that hard, and usually, if you have a good build, you are having a tad bit of fun grinding multiplayer, but for some people it can be annoying.Ok, now enough of the stuff about grinding, heres some aspects that I think are excellent about the game:4 Classes with different playstyles.Satisfying movement system.Epic and very iconic ninja customization, with voicelines.TONS of jutsus and combinations with awesome VFX.Very nice combat system (except for fighter, just LMB)More than just one battle mode (wow, filler)Ranked system, that is pretty fun tbh.And the excitement of when you get a good S/SS from a scroll is just heavenly.And finally, the atmosphere in the lobby is very very nice.So a summary if you should buy this is:Yes - If you can withstand grindNo - If you cant buy DLCs and cant grind all the time :)

_childDocuments_.review: Normally don't bother writing reviews but here goes;I personally LOVE this game.  I feel it has a lot to offer as far as team comp and the combat is fun as hell.  I'll address the complaints for anybody on the fence.**Camera and Targeting**People complain about the targeting system and say its the worst in they have ever used.  I say, they have no idea how it works.  When somebody uses a substitution or escape jutsu, they become unlocked.  This is done on purpose.  Otherwise, why would it even be in the game?  It's a jutsu thats SOLE PURPOSE is to confuse and allow you to get the jump on your opponent.  HOWEVER you do have time to react to it if you are good enough.  The way they time the animations in this game, you will know you have been juked before you get countered.  As soon as I see the puff of smoke or the wood start to form on somebodies body, I just dodge blindly.  Sometimes I nail it, sometimes I dodge right at them.  What I will say is, if I use my camera correctly and look around to see them, I usually escape.  It's not easy BUT THATS THE POINT.  ALSO, PRO TIP: Put the camera on 10.  Its the best sensitivity for the frantic play style.  When you lock on somone you dont even need to use it and its best for situations i just explained cause you can sweep and snipe lock on in a fraction of a second to succeed in avoiding getting ambushed.**Combat And Combos**Another area where people are talking nothing but garbage.  I say, Get Gud Nerd!I play defensive style and I can formulate a TOD (Touch Of Death) combo if I can corner one or two people.  Yes its situational, but so are most TOD's.  If you can bait the sub jutsu, you can then try for huge damage.  That's most of the game.  Spacing, neutral, and trying to get people to mess up so you can punish.  Sounds a lot like a fighter.  When you add the smite style jutsu tug of war in the beginning, it makes for a solid 5 minutes of frantic fighting.**Content**Right now, it does seems a little lacking in content BUT, that's opinion based and honestly is really about whos looking at it.  For me, there is more than enough when I figure in the amount of masters and how much I would have to play to unlock everything to really start formulating serious builds.  I like multiplayer and picked this up with a MOBA mentality of "there is probably no story".  Those looking for traditional Naruto games, keep looking.  IMO, this was the way to go.  The original story has been done to death and trying to create something from scratch leaves us with DB Xenoverse, which I believe is an utter mockery of the series.**Improvements**The one and only thing I would improve on is the ability to form groups to play with and maybe an in-game friends system for guilds or the like.  It's possible that I just don't know how to do it but, from what I can see, it doesn't look "friends" friendly.  I am actually going to go open a discussion about that right now.  Even if it is just incorporated into steam.  Thats fine too.  With discord being the golden standard I'm actually okay without having a voice chat.TL;DRThis title is a solid 8.5/10.  If you have always dreamed of what it would be like to formulate real ninja ambushes and ACTUALLY have some team based combat, than this title was made for you.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know why, but this game scratched my splatoon itch. Does it involve inking the ground? Absolutely not. Instead it has a customizable ninja with insane movement options, 2 ninjutsu and 1 ultimate ninjutsu that you can customize, and a 4 v 4 format that works surprisingly well with the 4 "classes" in the game: Attack, ranged, tank, and healer. I've put in almost 20 hours into this game and I can say for certain that if you want to get good at this game you should at least get a basic understanding of each and be able to switch if your team needs it.Let's start with the attackers. Quite simply they hit hard but are thin as paper. At most this class is going to be in the face of the opponents spamming attacks and the usual kunai. It has a mixture of semi ranged ninjutsu that can counter, stun, or take a massive chunk of health from the opponent. Next is the ranger. It's kinda like attacker, but as the name implies deals with range. Their attacks and tools are mostly centered around range, but I've found that the rangers kunai does more than the attackers and can sometimes juggle enemies to death. As for ninjutsu goes, rangers do get some close range options, however most of there ranged attacks take a while to activate, so I wouldn't recommend pairing them. Next is the tank. They are built different and will eat most attacks coming their way. With the most defense and the lowest speed, they fit their role perfectly as they swing a massive great sword that plows through waves of enemies. As for ninjutsu, they specialize in making walls and making AOEs. Surprisingly, they also have a few ninjutsu that heal them, making their survivability almost as good as the healers. And speaking of which, healers. The game says that healers aren't suited for combat, but how boy are they suited for combat. With the fastest attacking weapon and their kunai replaced with a portable health potion, with the right ninjutsu you become nigh immortal. Yes, they have ninjutsu that can heal nearby allies and themselves, but they also have abilities that seal the enemies ninjutsu.Now, wants the best class? I don't know. With the amount of customization (I'll be it, most are locked behind a paywall, but I think they're worth it) your allowed to mix and match with, you could find something you like about all the classes and end up switching them in the middle of a match.Try it out for yourself. If you don't like it, refund it.

_childDocuments_.review: Those seeking out a fleshed-out Naruto story are better served with the Naruto Storm series. The little story content on offer here is stowed away in but a few repetitive co-op missions.  There is full character customization in terms of outfit, weapons, and ninjutsu skills. It is locked away behind an in-game lootbox system with ninja scrolls, basically a treadmill of grind playing the game. The problem is that you cannot dress up your character willy-nilly, for each costume carries certain passive stats that you might need for your character build.The fighting mechanics are serviceable and varied for a team battler such as this. There are four character classes to choose from, each with their individual role in the team (healer, brawler, ranged, etc.), ninjutsu, and equipment, all of which need to be unlocked first through playing co-op missions or versus mode.Movement and ninjutsu usage is fluid even if a little simplistic. The complexity adds up when fighting together with your team, though. The camera system with its lock-on function often gets in the way of the action, especially in battles against a whole pack of enemies and if you are trying to recover, or combo, in corners the camera is unable to recover by itself.Technically, there is very little to complain, as the title is running on a modern engine (Unreal Engine 4). The watercolory look to the characters may not be to every fan's taste but the game runs smoothly at whatever frame-rate you desire. Only but a handful of cutscenes in co-op mode are animation-locked to 30 frames per second but never the gameplay itself.Lastly, since this is a multiplayer game, the issue of lag in multiplayer matches needs to be addressed here. I suspect the game is running peer to peer which is why lag is inherent to everyone but the host especially if you are connected to players not within your general region, which you have no control over. This comes as a huge disappointment for an always-online game such as this.If you are in for a little bit of grind, this is a truly interesting take on an online Naruto team battler. Get it at a discount if you are a fan with the season passes included.

_childDocuments_.review: AN ABSOLUTE HORRORWasted money 100%Whoever designed this thing should be ashamed of themself, even more Bandai for selling this thing.-The fighting system is so basic I've seen better in indie games or even ROBLOX games.-Theres a sort of "story" told through pve missions you can do with a team but the difficulty is such that you can walk through it solo in about 3 hours, maybe even less, I wasn't rushing it.-ALL attacks are autoaimed, meaning the huge oneshotting blasts will follow you to your death unless you can cover behind something before they hit. The problem is there will ALWAYS be someone attacking you from outside camera view and hitting you no matter how much you're dashing and jumping around, you're always an easy target, period. -You have ONE substitution technique or similar every 20 to 30 seconds which makes it basically useless. Especially since the enemy just keeps spamming the attack button and the autoaim makes them turn to wherever you've moved to istantly.Once you've used your only substitution you are locked in an endless spam of attacks from which you have NO DEFENSE, no way of interrupting the enemy's combos. You just watch your character being used as a punching bag hoping for the enemy to make the mistake of kicking you far enough for you to get control again.All of the above makes so combat is literally reduced to: The higher number of players jumps the lower number of players and starts SPAMMING whatever they've got until the enemy dies. Total absence of tactics or any form of real skill.And at the time of saying this my K/D Ratio and WIN ratio are both about 2.00, so I'm not even on the losing side. This is not the rant of a noob.Now, if you're here for the Naruto content and are willing to buy this even if the combat and missions sucks, DON'T.You have a bunch of masters(main characters from the anime/manga) from which to "learn" some of their moves and get their clothes. BUT we're talking 2 techniques per master, not even the best ones in most cases, and they're so fast and easy to get every player already has every technique and you will NEVER have a cool unique character. Forget sharingan, byakugan or rinnegan, they're not power ups like in the Storm series, they just temporarily appear on your character's face during the animation when you use attacks as amaterasu or shinra tensei and nobody really even notices in the middle of battle.All aesthetic elements as clothes, hair, and such are ripped off the original characters so bad every player ends up looking like a recolor of a canonical character. Some people even go the extra mile of not even trying to look original and just remake the original characters so you get a dude name xXNaruto_Uchiha_RinneganGODXx who looks like an exact copy of Kakashi and shoots rasen-shuriken and amaterasu while running around with the ugly copy of raikage's lightning armor.I don't even feel like I can keep going, this is too much time wasted on this horror of a game already.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a long-time Naruto fan, and when I heard rumblings of this game back when, I was slightly excited, to have the opportunity to create my own ninja, and share a world with my favorite characters, doing missions with my friends and things of the sort. After I've learned what the game was and what it included, my excitement waned until it vanished completely. So after waiting for this game to go on sale and playing through most of what the game has to offer, these are my thoughts.If you're hoping for an epic Naruto story that revolves around your development as a ninja, don't. This game has no real coherent story, as you're introduced into the game and made your character, you'll be greeted with a boring dialogue that introduces you to the world and it's facilities where you'll do your missions, PVE, PVP, customization and all that. After that small introduction you're on your own. While the gameplay itself is fun, the missions are repetitive and get boring eventually, being redeemed only when you do them with friends. The missions offer no real story and just serve as a platform for you to level up, get scrolls (that net you customization items, like loot crates), and advance your master level which gives you all sorts of rewards.Now, in the customization part, I was very disappointed, with the lack of optional clothes and original content, what's the point of making my own ninja if 85% of the customization items are based on the original characters, like don't get me wrong, it's cool to look like them, I just wish there were more options for individuality, and this goes for hair-types, Jutsus (which is alright, I guess) and "make-up". In addition, something that really annoyed me is the recoloring of outfits, and by recoloring I don't mean you get to pick from a palette of colors or a slide system, oh no, they have made original palettes with color combinations that they chose, and let me tell you, I'm not exaggerating when I'm saying that the choices they give are some of the worst color combination I have ever seen, ugly can't even begin to describe them, so most of the time, you'll find yourself sticking to the original palettes as they look the best. Not only that, they added *some* differentiation to the costumes, adding ugly-ass patterns to already existing outfits, there's really nothing to look for when obtaining these items from scrolls and you're better off just earning cash to buy what you want straight up from the store.Now I know, there's season two yet to come, but I don't really see them adding anything original apart from more "masters" and a couple of missions, another lazy thing is, at first I had the idea that you would've picked your village at the beginning of the game and start there as you go through the villages for different missions. Nope, you get one boring and small map of Konoha, I can't even call it a map, it's pretty much a tiny lobby, where you can't jump on top of buildings, can't interact with almost anything, it's just bland and boring. The animations for walking around in the lobby are horrible, like the adventure mode in Bandai's Naruto games, and I guess it shouldn't surprise me that they've essentially ripped them from the games, while the game itself is graphically inferior to those games in every aspect.Overall, this game is disappointing, and as someone who hates live-service games, I guess I should've known, but my love for Naruto got the better of me this time, with the anime and manga ending, and Boruto being sub-par, who knows when and if we'll get decent games in the future.-sigh- 4/10 because you CAN find a cool look (it's hard), and there's a lot of Jutsus to choose from, and the game-play itself isn't that bad.

_childDocuments_.review: This is by no means a good game, or even the best naruto game, but in all honesty this my favorite naruto game ever. This game just has something too it, its combat is chaotic and unpredicatable, the settings (in my opinion) look great, and costomizing your own shinobi is just so satifying I don't want to put the game down. So basically this game really hits me right in the childhood nostalgia, allowing me to make the shinobi I always dreamed of. However this game has a lot of problems that come with it. I have heard and read about multiple game breaking bugs, sometimes the games just won't load one of your players in, some justu will just disable your charater for the rest of the match leaving them floating in the air unable to do anything (including die), I have even been put into other games voice chat and none of your volume settings can lower their volume so you'll just hear people in their match while you are doing nothing (no idea if they can hear you though). But by far the biggest issue with this game is the lag, I'll be in the middle of fighting another player and then suddenly be four buildings back running up a wall, this problem needs to be fixed if the game wants to survive. There is also a few problems with the competive mode that needs fixing, one there is no balancing in the match making I constantly end up in matches against the same four stack of players who are all S rank who crush me everytime, two there ranking system makes zero sense and seems to have nothing to do with skill, I'll gain points for wins, points for loses, and I never lose points only gain zero when I do very poorly and that doesn't seem fair to me that you can just get S rank by putting enough hours and, third and finally there needs to be a reporting system, the fastest way to gain exp to level up your masters is to get into a game and kill yourself until the match is over by just showing up you can get 100 exp and that has happened to me in multiple matches and it is so stupid that they can't be punished. And even with all of these issues I cannot stop playing this game and I am having a blast, I'd give it 3/5 stars with the potential to move up if they fix some of these issues.

It's at this point that I realise that im in an online lobby, and there doesnt seem to be a single player story mode. I follow the instructions, do the first few missions, and already the gameplay feels pretty janky, but comes the time to choose a master to train under, so I go through the list and that is when I realise, that more than half the masters in the game, are locked behind a 10$ paywall. On a 80$ game. Then I go check the scroll appraisal shop, and see that it has a frikkin paid gacha shop for the cosmetics.I've played about 3 hours, trying to justify at least owning the game, but I think I'm done. I can't believe this is such a greedy poorly made mess, add to that that the art style makes everyone look like zombies with dead eyed stare, the complete lack of depth for the battles, and the fact it all feels like a mobile game on which they slapped a AAA game price tag on.If you want to play a good Naruto game, purchase Ultimate Ninja Storm 3 full burst. it's only 35 dollars, has a ton more content, a decent story mode, good multiplayer, and the game is actually polished. _childDocuments_.review: First off I am not a hardcore Naruto fan, but I did enjoy it when I was younger, and I still enjoy anime to this day.With that in mind, this game is basically a team based fighting with "heroes" your character being the hero that you can customize. The biggest thing, is that this game in my opinion is a pvp game at heart, with different seasons and events every week, with different unique (sometimes) rewards. It only took me a few hours to get through the "story" (which was a slow and slightly painful) and unlock all the rewards that were worth it. So the game is a 3d team-based (sometimes again) brawl where the players can use custom ninjas to fight each-other. You only get to select 2 jutsu, 1 ult, 1 ninja equipment and a "dodge" ability. The fashion is very in-depth I just wish there were more jutsu and combat options, especially since you will likely have to follow the meta builds to stay competitive. That basically encompasses the problems with the game, as an anime fan and a hardcore pvp fan, I really love this game. No messing around, just que, pop in game, fight, earn rewards, repeat. If you really like the story and want to relive/ experience a new Naruto story with a sprawling open world with in-depth characters, then I wouldn't really recommend this game. Also grab it on sale, since the game and the character dlc are all fun. But not worth the original price sadly.
