_childDocuments_.review: Journey is a sublime, beautiful experience that you can share with a stranger (or multiple strangers). the desert landscapes, the ancient ruins, and the mountain summit are all gorgeous to look at, and the amazing music adds to the already gorgeous atmosphere. i don't really have words to describe it or the emotions i felt whilst playing Journey, so i'm going to make this review a thank you letter to the person who travelled with me on my Journeyto Green Brick,thank you for travelling with me. i never thought a chance encounter in the desert with someone else going up to the split mountain would wind up with me becoming terrified of not catching up with you in the ruins. i never thought that a 1.5 hour game would see me worry about what happened to you when we got separated again in the snowstorm. i never thought a game that serves as a metaphor for a spiritual journey would see me hope for you to make it to the summit before me. i never expected this game to make me so happy when i saw you waiting for me after we got passed the leviathan. the flight up to the summit with you was surreal, and i felt genuine joy and sadness when we went into the light together, knowing we made it yet we would probably never cross paths againi wanted to thank you from the bottom of my heart for making an already a amazing experience even more amazing. i only hope i made the journey as memorable for you as you made it for meyour desert friend,Shield
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: I've played Journey before it came to Steam - playing it again felt like coming home. The journey was just as heartwarming and touching as before. Beautiful world and fun gameplay. Each journey is short, but will definitely stick with you.Of course, the best part is meeting other adventurers and singing to each other as you make your way up the mountain. Maybe it's the quarantine speaking, but it feels even more sweet and poignant to swirl around the sand dunes with a new friend. 10/10 would and will play again
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: Expertly framed, stunning visuals, excellent music/sound design & an all round delight to play. It isn't complex, the game play is simple but enjoyable. The shortness of the game means that the simplicity does not become dull. In my opinion could of been improved with some way to improve the flow of game play between chapters
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: Meh. I'm glad I got it on sale because it was a very short experience and somewhat frustrating, at least with the companions I got. None of them seemed to realize we charge eachothers flight with our chirps, so while I would often follow them and chirp 'em up nice'n'good they would just use that power to fly away from me while I'm stuck on the ground. That ended up making it more annoying than it would have been just by myself, but I kept wanting to give them chances because it seems like the kind of game that would be much better done cooperatively. Thing is, now its over and I don't feel the need to play it again. $2.50 an hour aint so bad, but I would would have regretted it if I bought the game at full price.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: Thanks to it's multiplayer system, this game has a strange way of making you feel connected to someone you know nothing about. When you meet another player, you can't talk to them either by text or voice chat, and you don't even get to see their name, yet you can help each other through the level, building an odd sense of companionship as you go, to the point where I feel bad when I have to close the game and leave my new companion behind, likely to never meet them again.The game looks beautiful, and the music matches the visuals, but this way of sharing your journey with total strangers is what  really makes the game special for me, even more so since I never got to meet anyone when I first played on the PS3 version.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful piece of art. Amazing visuals, music and atmosphere. It tells a story without any wordsThe multiplayer aspect of it is really original and interesting as well.If you are used to only playing action games it may feel strange or boring at first, just explore with curiosity, without knowing exactly what you're doing.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: I remember when this game was released I wanted to play it but I didn't want to buy a PS3. Well 9 years after I finished it and I am not impressed at all.I will start with the negatives since I started this review in negative tone. The game feels and looks dated,I played many games similar to Journey and most of them are better...I know that Journey was one of the first games that went for this artistic life journey experiment but games followed that formula and evolved over 9 years. I am not saying Journey is a bad game it is just old and thats it. In my opinion porting  a console game 8 years after is just to grab the money because the port isn't that good to be honest (awful audio bugs).The game is a walking sim and if I hate something about walking sims that would be walking at a snails pace for more then 4 minutes(plenty of that in this game) . This game is at its best when it flows and I did had few WOW moments and I created my version of what the story is about. The thing that I didn't know is that others can join my game ,I found that annoying at times but also great at times...interesting decision by the developers,almost like a social experiment.Conclusion - Joureney is a good game but dated, a classic for sure but didn't age that well. I can recommend this game but at a discount.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic game, even though the "Journey" was short it was amazing and breathtaking in some scenes and honestly this has become one of my all time favorite games. I would recommend this to anyone who just wants to play a game to have fun, or just sit back and watch what is essentially a two hour long interactive movie. I mean that in the most positive way possible, I am a huge fan of Animation and Cinematography. To me this game was more like a movie that i could control how the story progressed at my own pace and for lack of a better term, I could stop and smell the roses, or in this case sand and destroyed ruins. I first tried this game back when it came out on the PS3 even then I was blown away by how it looked and played, this game's visuals, controls and mechanics have aged flawlessly. Overall I loved the game and thank you to whoever reads this review, I hope you enjoy this game just as much as I have.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: I lost my prior review when flipping from a thumbs up to a down... I was actually neutral on the title but after reading my review I'm leaning towards this title just being too boring for me to recommend.If you want a uneventful, atmospheric walking sim with unoffensive background music to get you through the 2.5 hour runtime then this game is exactly that. I'm currently at the base of the mountain which I think is near the end and haven't really experienced anything other than "going through the motions". The only time this game shined was when another random player joined my session and we blasted through the few stages we played together. As a solo experience, it's pretty boring.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: One of the prettiest games I've played in a while. The story was a bit awkward in my opinion because I couldn't really understand it my first playthrough, but maybe I'm just a bit stupid. The underground part with the stone creature? And my flying pal? Yeah, genuine emotional damage done to me right there. I'd rate it a solid 8.5/10. I wish it was a bit longer, but I have a lot of fun replaying it.Met up with a random near the beginning of the game on my 2nd playthrough and we stuck together through all the trials and levels. Every time one of us got attacked by those flying stone creatures, the other would chirp until we got back together again. We led each other to fabric places to lengthen our scarves. When we climbed the mountain together, they fell from the staircase and I leapt down to join them. At one point they sat down in the snow and I assumed they were just meditating for a while, so I sat down next to them, and waited... and waited... and waited...... Over 15 minutes of being tabbed out sitting next to my companion, wondering if they would ever come back at all but DETERMINED to not be the one to leave them, they finally returned... and we finished the game together. It's much more emotional to finish the game with a companion than on your own, I must admit.RiotoSato, whoever you are, wherever you are... I hope you know I would die for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: Journey constitutes a very rare case of a game that can somehow touch aspects of your soul with a unique combination of simplicity as far as the gameplay is concerned and wonderful music, while at its core there is a vague story with mysterious characters who communicate with melodies! It does not last for long, however after completing it, i consider the time which requires to finish it is totally satisfactory. You definitely must try it to truly appreciate it!
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: 2020/06/28not really sure what i just played...? but the game had great atmosphere at some moment, and i enjoy it, but... sadly i haven't met any other player... so it's a lonly trip for my frist walkthrough.2020/06/29meeting another player today in 2nd walkthrough, i don’t have words to describe feelings, but it's a pleasure to walk with you nice stranger! :)
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: Too bad there's not middle a ground in the reviews, it's either yes or no - how is that possible in a world that is nothing but shades of grey? Anyway, this is an OK game, but I'm not going to give it a Yes. The thing i hate about it the most is the way the program takes over the camera and the character movements, when there is no need to. You set the camera to a certain point of view and the game keeps slowly shifting it for no reason, so you are constantly having to readjust.  Also some of the actions, like along the ribbons, follows no pattern - just an exercise in frustration at times - adds nothing to the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: Let me preface this by saying that before yesterday I had never heard of this game. I had Stray (by the same dev) in my wishlist and it was discounted because of the steam sale. There was a banner that Annapurna had up to 75% off so I went to scroll through their other games and thought it looked cool. It was also only a few dollars.This was such an amazing experience. What a profound game. It has so many cool aspects. Not only is it just gorgeous to the eye, but the premise of it is so deep to me. I didn't even know I was playing with other real people until the end when it showed me the names. I was under the impression that I had a COM partner and they were supposed to guide me in a way. It's so cool that the whole thing is up to your own interpretation and there is no commentary or text throughout. I played it through in one sitting, it only took me about 2.5hr. I will probably play it again and try for more achievements. Just wow. I'm gobsmacked at how cool this game is. It's hard to put into words. Just get it!
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, over 17k reviews at the time I'm writing this. Not much more can be said, Journey is an incredible game. But I feel that many Steam players are kinda missing out on some of it's best aspects.1.  Yes you *can* play with kb/mouse, but you won't be able to do any trick moves. Even the simplest trick like doing a faceplant requires spinning the left stick, which of course is impossible with a kb/mouse. Advanced tricks like boosting are also impossible without a gamepad.2. . You just need to work around the games matchmaking. Coordinating with a friend so you both enter the first game level (the bridge area) at the same time usually works.3.  All those areas in the game that you can see but can't reach, like the far off bridges and buildings. You can reach all those places. Journey is the only game I know of that has such a rich abundance of exploration out of the restricted/designed play area. You can spend hours and hours exploring, and every single level has it's secrets, though some require advanced flight techniques to access.After you've played through a few times, you'll unlocked the white cloak. That's when Journey begins to open up like an oyster revealing it's pearl.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: There are games that let you spend a few hours of fun, and there are games - rare, rare gems - that allow you to feel something you've never felt before, to grasp concepts that seemed very distant just before. Journey is a masterpiece that everyone should experience at least once; for me, it rekindled a little hope in the bonds we share with all our brothers and sisters on earth. Don't expect a long game, for the whole experience can last between 1 and 2 hours, but there are elements of replayability thanks to the online interactions and collectibles. Also, the game features some surprising skill elements and a wonderful, wonderful community. I'm sure I'll spend many more hours on Journey.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: I've never played a game like this. The name is well suited because it is exactly that, a journey. It's not a long play through, but I'll definitely do it again. Randomly running in to a player with no way to communicate other than a chirp was actually incredible. The art is outstanding, the puzzles challenging. Honestly the game just flows and you figure out what needs to be done by the seat of your pants. I recommend going in without researching anything. It will unfold for you. The end without spoiling sent me in to tears.. just hit home for reasons. Not necessarily bad tears.. just made me emotional. And I haven't cried in years. So it was good, lol. Play the game!
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished my first playthrough and I want to start by saying thank you.The first thank you is for the team working on this game: The ambiance was grandiose and the music excellent. Each scene was a piece of art: The discovery where a lot of guided freedom is given. Then the ingenious puzzle that makes the player invested in the game. The slides mechanism that is fully mastered and is only able to give a feeling of joy, satisfaction and speed.The enemy which is at no point omnipresent, but have enough influence to give the player a sentiment of tension and powerlessness. A wonderful storytelling and sufficient lore to invest the player even more. And finally the last level being in a league of its own (I don't want to explain and those who played the game know what I mean).The second thank you is for the random stranger that I came across and ended my playthrough with. Being thrown to the unknown, but together is a total other experience that just being alone. We discovered the game and its implication together from the beginning till the end. Helping and waiting one another even when there is no benefit nor gain from it, just the beauty of a human interaction.I don't know who you are, how you or even where you are but the only thing I know is that this game made me fall in love with a stranger.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: A lovely little game (only takes 1,5-2h to complete) with beautiful art and music and (mostly) cute creatures where the protagonist travels to the top of a mountain through different landscapes, learns about the history of the world and meets companions (other players) on the way. The story leaves a lot for the players to interpret and the game is surprisingly emotional. Some players might rush ahead, making it easy for you to lose track of them, but others will continue travelling with you for the rest of the game, helping you along and waiting for you if you have trouble getting ahead or just want to look around. Fun to replay, as you can then help others on their journeys.I've encountered some bugs, but nothing major, though if you're an achievement hunter, one achievement might require you to adjust graphics settings for the game to register the achievement.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: Journey is an experimental surfing game with soulslike coop sprinkled with phallic symbolism. Themes somehow fit the modern ethos well.I like the idea of the ephemeral multiplayer component, which is integral to the experience but not to the play. At its best it reinforces positivity and thoughtfulness.I waited 8 years to play this game. It was a fine act to bring it to the PC.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: My teachers at my game art study highly praised this game for its visual storytelling and design and I get why! The environments are simple yet beautiful and the music completes it all, I felt very immersed. I do have to say though, it is more of an experience than a typical 'game'. There are some puzzles and flying mechanics, but it is fairly minimal (though flying around is really fun). Would love it if there were more complex puzzles you needed to solve with your buddy or so to bond with them even more!
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: First, a very small note of critique, I would just say that having to rely on one point of reference to find everything out in the desert can be hard, but that is more of an issue for anyone trying to achievement hunt in the game. Now for the praise, which I have large amounts of for this game. I am a very antisocial person, but in the vast nothingness of the dunes, just knowing someone else is there with you is a very comfortable feeling. I've finished the game twice so far, one run completing it alone, and the second was with someone with a white robe, and I can not emphasize how amazing and bittersweet the ending becomes with someone else. I don't think you can truly experience "Journey" until you have completed this game with a companion that you had from the very beginning, and while it is hard to manage in a game where there is no real communication with your partner, I think when you finally get the chance it will make the end all the sweeter, and I think that feeling would apply to anyone else. For a game with no words, it speaks to the soul in a way very few games can, and that seems to be the general trend for the games put out by this developer. "Journey" is a story, but more than that, it is an experience, and a great one at that.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game because I heard of the connectivity feature.When I first loaded into the bridge area, I was disappointed to see no one nearby, so I closed the game.Then I re-opened, now with the knowledge of the "white glow" and almost instantly noticed it, seeing someone sat in the sandUnfortunately they left meA few levels later however, I met someone that stuck with me right until the end, we completed the game together.Thank you Brananarama for making my Journey more fun. I had a smile on my face every time we interacted, and I got scared when I would lose you on certain levels thinking we would get disconnected10/10 game
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: Journey is one of my all time favorite games out there. With a scenery that will make you stand still and just take it all in, to a story hidden within the ruins of what once was. You connect with players from all over the world as you make your way to Eden. With the only way of communicating being chrips and calls you have to explore and trust one another to make it to your goal.  Note -  that this game is meant to be played multiple times, Trust me it will make sense when you go through it once. You can recognize Vet players by their cloaks having more rows of  simbols on the bottem. So dont be afraid to run off with them as they ( mostlikely) only mean for you to have the best experiance you can have in the game.With the sad undertone and new found connection you will only find out who your new found friends was that helped you along the way at the very end, So dont forget to write down a user name or two or 7 when you go to the ' Thank you or traveling with me' thread here on steam.Happy exploring -x-
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: Even if I completed the game in under 2 hours it is one of the most emotional games I've played. It's amazing how the game is able to tell a story with only visuals and music and not a single word. The soundtrack is unbelievably good and hits just the right time. I really like when I meet another player and experience the game together. Unfortunately that player left before the ending but the way it's executed is good that you can not see the name or communicate. The only thing you can do is make sounds to each other and it makes you care for that completely strange person. The end left me with a lot of thoughts and emotions. This is truly a masterpiece, it's a must play in my opinion.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: Love, love, love this game. Did I mention that I love this game? I usually go for survival/exploration games but a friend recommended I try Journey and I'm so glad I did. On my first play through I met several fellow travelers and while I'm late to gaming (I'm 59 and just really started playing games last year) I can say with 100% certainty that I've never felt such a connection to players that I've just met. I struggled with learning how to fly and they waited patiently while I plowed into walls and ceilings. They would chirp what I think was encouragement since they didn't leave me behind. And when I got to the stairs in the snow level and couldn't figure it out they wouldn't leave me behind. I finally had to quit the game so that my fellow travelers could finish their journey. Last night I finally made it to the end of the game. Wow was it amazing.This is the only game I've played where I felt deep emotions, met players who were selfless, and immediately knew it was a game I could come to to be uplifted.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: Journey is one of the most beautiful experiences since the creation of video games as a medium. The atmosphere/music/aesthetics are just all perfection, throw that in with some wholesome co-op with strangers where you can easily find a nice person to chime all game with and then just be sad that it all ended. Journey is a must if you believe games are an artform!
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game with a very clever incorporation of interactive sounds and music.The rewards for sticking to an unknown fellow companion is very rewarding in the end.There are very few games that can elevate the emotions that comes with it. Journey is such a game.I keep returning to this classic. Any self respecting gamer should have a copy of this gem.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: A game that made me laugh, scratch my head and afraid all in one.Journey ... It is in the name, isn't it? Once is enough to experience the whole game but the achievements are fun to do. Singing to one another as you slide down a dune, reassurance as the machines fly by, babysitting a single patterned companion and the end. The sands of this live will return to the dunes and i will be shaped once more.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: Why do people like this game? I'm not trying to be rude, I just really don't understand.I picked it up due to the overwhelming number of positive reviews that now seem like they were talking about a different game entirely.The Story was supposedly special and meaningful. I found it remarkably flat and predictable. I wont spoil it for any who still wish to discover it for themselves, but to be honest, it was basically exactly what I was expecting from the cover art and no more. The music did a good job of conveying emotion and the storytelling style was well executed, but unfortunately that doesn't come anywhere close to making up for the lackluster, played out content of said story (in my opinion).The gameplay was smooth and mildly interesting, it wasn't trying to be groundbreaking, and was mainly a storytelling device, so I can't fault it for being a bit... lets be kind and call it 'understated'.  It did have a distinctive dragging feel to it though. Maybe the devs were targeting a group with a longer attention span than I possess, but I felt like the levels were much wider and stretched out than they needed to be and the lethargic movement speed left me bored/frustrated and staring off into space for the half-minute it took to cross an empty stretch of sand. There is a flight/jump dynamic that made things interesting, but with a limited charge and a long space between recharge points, it felt just interesting enough to make me want to get to the next recharge place, but not interesting enough to prevent me from resenting the trek.The multiplayer dynamic was not something I was expecting, and solved a few of these balance issues. BUT I usually prefer to explore every corner of a space looking for secrets, view angles, and collectibles. I didn't feel free to take my time and explore while there was another player accompanying me and wanting me to follow them in order to progress. Especially when going over that ridge over yonder took a solid 2-4 minutes of them either following to pick something up they already had, or waiting around for me to return, pinging relentlessly. It was very short, which isn't necessarily a bad thing, but I was left with a feeling of waiting for the game to pick up, or the story to become something I hadn't seen a dozen times before, or to get another movement dynamic that would make things less draggy, or, or, or...... oh. its over. well. I guess no one can say I didn't give it a fair chance....All in all, I'm disappointed. Would not recommend. I apologize to any die-hard fans or Devs I may be insulting, but to me, it felt lackluster, poorly balanced, and led nowhere.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: Journey is a beautiful game with a confusing story that I found near impossible to discern.I had no idea quite why I was wandering through the deserts, valleys, and snowpeaked mountains of the game, but I knew that the game was quite pretty and had an amazing soundtrack to go along with my gameplay!Not a bad game, worth the 11$ and you get Flower free too!8/10edit: i also really enjoyed the random encounters with other players, waiting for them, doing the little "sing" mechanic to get their attention.Journey really is a good game, I urge you to get it while it's on sale! Give it a try! Pretty replayable game, too! Even if I don't see myself replaying it for quite some time... I won't be refunding it!
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game in a bundle since the difference in price was very small, expecting for it to be a short game that I will play once. It was  worth it, and even though game play is limited, it will take you a few run-throughs to get used to all the ways you could optimize the mechanics. I finished it at least 3 times now and will definitely come back for the rest of the achievements.I have never heard of anonymous mute co-op, but this is it. Doing it with a partner and no ability to communicate makes it more fun. It's definitely on the easy side and even easier if both players know the mechanics well, but the difficulty is not the point of the game as much as fun and wonder are.It's a delightful experience.

_childDocuments_.review: An interesting and bliss adventure.It's quite difficult to not hate this game and the main reason why is the co-op. I would have given this game a dislike easily, but the co-op made my experience special and gave me and my character a reason to push on because I wasn't going to give up and on my partner.Without the co-op implemented this game would fall flat because of activities you can do and the graphics. By all means it looks good, but it ain't on the level of ABZU. ABZU takes the cake for this genre and it has more to offer.On sale this looks to be reasonable deal. _childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games ever. Despite its short length, it has great replayability, and I'm sure the strong emotions felt during the initial playthrough will carry over to future ones. It moves you with its art direction, music, the feelings of power and hopelessness, birth and rebirth... Words fail this game. Buy it and try it yourself. You won't regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: It's cute. Much shorter than I expected (I expected it to be short, but I was thinking more along the lines of 3 hours), but it does make the most of its play time.+ Really beautiful+ Not a dull moment+ Gameplay varies between exploration, puzzle, stealth, platforming and... just sliding down dunes very fast+ Good environmental storytelling, does a lot with no dialogue- A little too short- Anticlimactic ending- Seamless multiplayer. One of the gaming industries' current obsession, and I really wish it weren't. Controversial, I know, seeing as most reviews are saying it was amazing how they became best friends with someone the other side of the world without being able to talk at all, but that wasn't the case in my playthrough. It was just annoying. I had 4 people pop in and out of my game - The first one was at the very beginning, and they just rushed forward, ignoring all collectibles and chirping aggressively, and then abandoned me when they got too far ahead. The second was just... standing still and not responding at all, and then disconnected. The third stayed with me for about 5 minutes, then I lost them somehow. The fourth disconnected almost immediately. I wouldn't say this completely ruined the experience for me, because there isn't much other players can do to interefere with your game, but it was pretty damn immersion breaking to have some other Journyer pop in and out and run around me when I'm finally starting to get invested. I would have just played offline, but there isn't any way to do that other than literally disconnecting my computer from the internet, and I didn't wanna do that.- Hidden collectibles. That's a pet peeve of mine. I hate it when games try to extend the play time by just placing a whole bunch of collectibles in various hidden places like behind columns or under the floor. If the collectibles are important, the result is I have to completely ruin the flow of the game so I can thoroughly search every room. I hate it. In this game the collectibles are only semi-important - they extend your scarf length, meaning you can fly for longer, but it's not actually  to be able to fly longer, so when I realized that I just stopped collecting them, unless I just happened upon them by chance.Bottom line - It's a cute, short, pretty game that's probably best bought on sale, and probably best played offline, unless you really like multiplayer.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: Bought this game because it was on sale for under $10. Had no idea it was multiplayer, no idea about it other than it got positive reviews. Went in totally blind. I ended up spending 4 - 5 hours playing and enjoyed it! Took a while to figure out what was happening, but it is interesting enough that I'll try again.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: I liked that this game metaphorically explains life, in general. You start out with nothing, small and innocent like a baby, as you collect scarfs in the game and gain the ability to fly as you progress through your path to reach the mountain. You might bump into a person, a complete stranger, while you travel with them throughout the game and become great companions. You face danger and difficulties but also experience joy and euphoria simply through singing in rhythm and always looking out for each other while it gets cold or they get attacked. In the end, through the short yet nostalgic or loving memories that you created with your friend, you become weak, slowly dying in the snow together. Having lost your ability to move around more, unable to sing, not having a scarf anymore and no more flying, it seems you are vulnerable again, just like how you used to be when you started out but this time, wiser yet fragile, like the elderly. After death, you seem to ascend up in the afterlife, reaching out towards the light as you and your partner say goodbye while parting their own way, having lived that amazing journey with someone else. This game had brought so many feelings in such a short amount of time and its truly one of the best games i have ever played. This game requires no dialogue to understand the story which is mind blowing because, you make your own journey in this game, just how you make your own story in your life, not in the game, real real life, your journey from being a juvenile to an elderly and the amazing memories you create, while overcoming challenges and obstacles that are being thrown at you are relatable in this game and in life. What i have learnt from this game is that it doesn't matter what happens to you, e,g, lose your powers throughout your journey, because you will lose your powers anyway during death, but the most beautiful thing about it is that you will regain them back in the afterlife and reunite with your partner once more. 100/10 Best game ever
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: 10000000/10. Walking simulator so beautiful you'll be crying at the end.I fell in love with this game back when it was released on the PS3, and I still love it all these years later. It's short, sweet, and poignant. Whether you're a seasoned white cloak or a first-time red cloak, the journey will always be a joy.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not for me. Not enough guidance (yeah yeah I don't have patience and I'm superficial whatever). When I wander in the desert with no direction and no guidance, I felt confused and kinda angry. Enough. I am not into meditation stuff. Running is slow as F. _childDocuments_.review: Journey isn't just a game, it's an experience. From the beautiful music, to the majestic landscapes, to the feeling of freedom when flying.This journey was able to get me emotional without any lines said. There is a story, but you need to have some creativity to understand it. The game mechanics are great! I knew about the 'companion-system' and smiled when I traveled with someone, just flying around together and making some noises. The fly-mechanic, my God, what an experience! And when you lose the ability by the storm, it makes you feel really powerless.Journey is a short but awesome game, you haven't tried it? Try it. This piece of art has to known.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: If you are looking for a challenging game, this is not it. This is not a game, this is an experience. You will meet companions and have a moving unspoken story. This game is like a living piece of art. I, as I was journeying, met companions, and then got separated from them. I was knocked down, got lost, had some setbacks, and felt like giving up at some points, but I kept on persevering. This is a game everyone should play. You won't regret it. It is short and sweet, which in my eyes is a bonus, but if you are looking for a long story then you, again, are looking in the wrong place. The story is simplistic, but beautiful and moving in a way. All this to say, buy this game, play this game, and start your journey.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: There's not one single word that could describe Journey. Amazing, fulfilling, mysterious, so many words could describe your experience with Journey. It's still one of the best games that I have ever played, even though it came out on the PS3 in 2012. Honestly, the journey is described differently for everyone. So if you're curious about it, play it. It's a very calming experience. Maybe I'll see you on your journey sometime.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: All I can say is WOW. This game is truly amazing, a piece of art. The adventure we partake in, is nothing compared to the graphics and sound design... I found myself lost inside this game, to a point where I didn't want to put it down. I wouldn't want to spoil anything for anyone... but truly amazing, a wonderful game. Great for anyone looking for a game to get away from reality.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: What a wholesome game.You might not be able to start the game with a friend (as a party) but you might make some on your journey. In fact you can meet several companions before you are even ready for it. So did I. I wasn't sure what's the deal with the rest of hooded weirdos and why they would disappear in the wind until one of them really actively tried to help me with very high jump. And then... I had to alt tab to confirm... you can meet OTHER PLAYERS in game! You don't know their names and there's no way to talk to them (except short or long beeps but obv I knew no universal codes as what can each mean) and yet... you find yourself caring for this newly discovered friend, looking up if you fall if at least they made it, looking back when you find a safe place to stand... and journey stops being about finding the end but making sure you both get to see it.Thank you for your kindness each of you who helped me and the one who made it to the end!First run thru takes about 2 hours and not knowing what to expect while finding out it's better not to stop I'd say it's a good thing. But what do you know I only got 3 achievements and I bet that's where remaining 22 hours are at >:DIf you look at store page, art style, tags etc and think you might like it, you'll probably give it 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: Journey is one of my all-time favorite games, and for good reason. It captures a sense of wonder with a simple yet profound story that draws you in without a single word spoken. The stunning visuals and mesmerizing landscapes feel alive, while the ethereal soundtrack perfectly complements the emotional depth of the experience.The beauty of Journey lies in its ability to evoke powerful emotions through minimalistic gameplay and design. Each step feels purposeful, and the multiplayer component adds an unexpected layer of connection without saying a word. Whether you're gliding across sand dunes or ascending the mountain in the final moments, the game's atmosphere leaves an indelible mark.It's a short experience, but one that stays with you long after it's over. Journey is more than just a game—it's an unforgettable experience.

_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: JourneyPositives:+ Beautiful and artistic+ Very atmospheric+ Nice sound and fantastic music+ Make you reflect about life+ When you fly or slide+ When there is some variation+ The creatures and travelers you meetNegatives:- Should have had more variation in landscapes and things too see- You walk a bit too much (there should have been more flying or sliding)- The few places where you must go a long way around if you're unlucky when jumping- Some parts are too cloudy and foggy- Some of the visual effects are a bit too much- Only 2 hours longI hoped this game was as fantastic as my favorite games in the genre, but to my surprise it was not.Dont get me wrong, the game is good, but its not fantastic. Its a bit overhyped, to be honest.I played their first game Flower, and I was really not impressed by it. But Journey is way better.If you like unique gaming experiences, you will most likely enjoy this game.But if you want a really fantastic game, then play What Remains Of Edith Finch and Brothers: A Tale Of Two Sons.Total Score: 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Can't believe now it's 2024 and it's still one of my favorite games to relax - breathtaking graphics, easy controls, interaction with other players and my favorite sounds effects (similar to thatgamecompany's Flower game). Most importantly, the philosophical thoughts on life. There is so much to discover, to admire, to enjoy and to love, while I'm flying my way to the destination as a white robe. If you are new to this game, please prioritize to become the white robe first, it will make rest of achievements so much easier, and the whole game will be on a different level. Life is a journey and every chapter is uniquely charming in its own way. Thanks to those who joined my journey at various points of each chapters, and those who walked with me till the every end.

_childDocuments_.review: Journey while short and simple, pans out to be one of the most beautiful games you could possibly add to your library. It doesn't matter your age, culture, birthplace, or language - it is driven the same through a simple system of chimes. Embark on a Journey, find a pal, and reach the peak together. _childDocuments_.review: Let me start off by saying that Journey has been one of my all-time favorite games since I first played it back on the PS3. It's a travesty that such a sloppy port has dampened the experience of this beautiful, awe inspiring piece of art. Although the pace is not for everyone, this easy-going ambient adventure is one I will treasure for years and I implore anyone who enjoys this type of zen game to pick it up... on the playstation.Though I heard musical cues were broken, I haven't experienced that except maybe once in the very beginning of the game and it was more like a brief hiccup in the audio files. However, I've experienced far worse and jarring bugs that disrupt my nostalgia chasing time in Journey. It's easy to tell that very little- if any- work went into porting this over. Which that fact in and of itself is a slap in the face to the developers who worked so hard on it. To tarnish this gem of a game with such lackluster effort really is something to be ashamed of.My character wigs out a bit in the beginning- jittering as the camera struggles to find its place- the camera of which is almost perpetually off-center and giving me a slight right lean when trailing through the sand dunes or walking through the gates to the next level of the zone. But perhaps the most disgusting thing to me about this port is that it has determined my computer can only handle MEDIUM settings... from a PS3 port. Let me clarify here:The Recommendations:- 64-bit (check...)- Windows 7 (I have Windows 10)- Intel Core i3 (I have a 9th gen i7)- 4GB of RAM (I have 32...)- NVIDIA GTS 450 (I have an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2070)As you can see, I clearly meet FAR beyond the requirements here, and yet if I so much as dream of upping the graphics on the game, it decides it can't handle it. The frames (even at medium recommended settings) get extremely choppy during certain scenes and this simply should not be. This game is NOT optimized by any means and what you remember it looking like on the PS3 will only tarnish your memory upon booting it up on your PC. On a rig that FAR outdoes what the PS3 once was, this game looks as if it were early PS2 graphics. There's really no reason for this. Also upon attempting to up my graphics it cuts out the backdrop of cutscenes, showing it as a black empty abyss and completely ruining the atmosphere.Now, I did complete this game again on PC from start to finish and it is PLAYABLE. But it's incredibly disappointing and lackluster to my vivid memory of the original release. As an avid fan and someone who has played hours upon hours of this game over the years just to relive the wonderful experience, I'm begging whoever is responsible for fixing and polishing the port.PLEASE fix this game. It deserves to make as deep an impact on new players as much as it should the nostalgia chasing veterans. If these problems are addressed I will change my review- it is with a heavy heart that I leave it on a thumbs down when I love this game so much- but this sloppy port doesn't do a fragment of justice to the original work. Please, Annapurna. Fix this.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: one of the best ambience games I have ever played in my life. I have been waiting for a pc release ever since I played the demo on ps3 a long time ago. Highly recommended with headphones on. This is not a game you dash through, because it's not hard if you want to finish it, you can do in 2hours. _childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: My Experience was immaculate. I walked through the sand. I walked through the snow. all of it was beautiful. I ran into a fellow along the way, something I didn't think was possible in this game till now. We ran along side by side, learning of each others backgrounds and history, his name was Jim. He had a wife and kids, and was doing well in life. One day he had an off day and was fired from his job, the reason was that he was seen tripping a homeless woman. As he was on his way home he was furious, and decided to do another unlawful deed when he was suddenly transported to here, what he thinks to be for his crimes. While I enjoyed his company, I realized what a fool I was to trust him and I went along to sled down with him. When he flew past me, he had swung out his arm and stole my wallet, after that he gained massive amounts of speed and I never saw him again. As I felt hopeless with nothing to do, I had met another fellow by the name of Bob. We rarely spoke to each other at first, but quickly realized what danger we were in. In the end we became friends, and even closer brethren. No matter what we were here for, we realize the place we were transported to, this journey, will change you for the better. Even if you are a bad person like Jim, you will find peace within yourself like this game brought me and Bob. Still missing my wallet though.

_childDocuments_.review: First time I played Journey was on the PS3 when it was first released. Enjoyed it so much it easily became one of my, like, top 5 video games of all time. It's been quite a while since then and I simply remembered it as a ''very good game I remember loving'', but started wondering if it's still worthy of the ''top of all time'' list. I wasn't going to buy it for PC because honestly why would I if I already have it lmao BUT I am lucky enough to have friends who hate having money and got it as a gift. Of course I played it and all I have to say is yes, it very much deserves a place on the top of all times list. 2012 me had a good taste in gayms after all.god the snow part still gets me every time, especially when playing with people who also try to stick together and make it super sad :''') Which is really interesting because Journey doesn't have chat or much ways of interacting with the surrounding and players. _childDocuments_.review: It's funny. I like this and I like Sky, but I have little patience for the Journey-likes that have come out since. You know, the linear, level-based puzzle platformers with an "emotional" story told through silent cutscenes (and in some cases, diaries scattered around the levels) and an "epic" and "emotional" soundtracks definitely not composed by Austin Wintory.Yeah, I'm not a fan of this type of game. I avoid them like the plague unless they have something interesting to show for (e.g. Jusant with its rather fun climbing mechanic and compelling world building). Journey (and by extension its little sibling Sky), however, stands out for not overstating its welcome and having a multiplayer mechanic that ties to that """emotional""" storytelling. That and flying around is actually rather fun.This is definitely one of those games everyone should play at least once. Its gimmick is a rather good implementation of online multiplayer and yes, it's a gorgeous game. Can't say I love it for spawning a deluge of copycats that don't come close to to it, but alas.

And now we're friends here on steam :DSo yeah, this game is absolutely awesome and I would recommend it to everyone to at least give this game a chance!
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: This game is such a unique experience. No NPC's, no character names, no quests, just shown a mountain top and you're off on your Journey. It was so interesting exploring the game and finding out things I could interact with by chiming some notes. Eventually I managed to run into another person and the game just felt so much bigger, just randomly running into someone like this and continuing your adventure felt so genuine. Your only form of communication is just chiming out little notes as well, it felt so wholesome to see something really spectacular(which you will find a lot of in this game) and watch my partner burst out in excited chimes like "DID YOU SEE THAT?!".Somehow they're able to pack such a genuine and spiritual experience into just two hours through amazing level design, incredible music, and the ability to share this all with a random traveller you meet along the way. Unfortunately I wasn't able to finish the game with anyone as they all seemed to leave during this one part in the snowy area after not being able to make it a couple times. Regardless I felt myself smiling through the whole thing and really enjoyed my time in the game.

_childDocuments_.review: At first I had no idea what was happening or why. _childDocuments_.review: I've never publicly made a review or a recommendation of any game before, really, but with Journey it's a bit of a different story.I won't go into too much detail here, because fundamentally I believe Journey to be a piece of art you yourself have to experience. This wordless story, a metaphor that will undoubtedly leave a personal impact on every single individual who plays this game, is beautiful. _childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games that could be classified as an interactive experience rather than a "game" strictly speaking. It's very light on mechanics, but heavy on visual, auditory, and interactive storytelling. The length of one playthrough is only about the length of a movie, but is still well worth the price for the impact it has as a literal journey distilled to it's essence.Everyone should play this game at least once. You will thank yourself.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: Journey is nothing less than visual poetry. From opening on rolling dunes and wind-swept stones, to the closing of a golden star, arcing through the night sky, this game had me holding my breath. Paired with a random other player with no way to communicate but your chime-like singing, you forge a bond with this unknown traveler as you explore the beautiful ruins, filled with magic scarfs and old stones. My first playthrough took 2 hours, and that was with me jerking my companion around to explore every ruin on the horizon's edge, and stopping for a potty break. The levels are linear, but wide enough to allow for progression at your own pace.((Note: I received this game as a gift for Christmas, but having played it would highly recommend anyone picking it up when it goes on sale. Heck, if I get as much enjoyment out of a second playthrough as I did the first, I'd say full price - $15 - is a bargain.))
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a bit impatient and didn't expect much so I was about to quit after 15 min but damn am I glad I didn't. God that was good (took me about 30 min to be fully invested lol). Also the mere fact I sat through the entire credits is saying a lot on its own

_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: It’s… an experience more than anything. The game itself is a walking simulator where you press forward. There is light platforming, some timing for a section or two, and some collection but overall, it’s not the focus. The game is really about moving forward, absorbing the world, and trying to piece together the story while pretty music plays in the background. It’s more about experiencing emotions instead of comprehending a story which is either going to work for some folks or not work for some folks. It was… OK for me as the story it does have is pretty simple. Although, even without the backstory presented in the world, you can understand that there’s a character going on a journey through a strange world with struggles and guidance along the way. The visuals and the music itself are really good so it’s just going to come down to if you get into it or not.The co-op mechanic is fantastic and the way it melds two players together who mostly just want to help each other in this journey without a single word is great. Hats off to that.

_childDocuments_.review: Very boring game. I have no idea why this game gets such high reviews. It's a walking simulator. You spend 90 to 120 minutes pressing W. There is a flying mechanic where you can glide for a bit with red cloth throughout the game. It doesn't help much because it runs out quickly. There is also a button that emits a chime sound. I kept trying to use it at various places to try to figure out what it does, but never discovered any use for it. I kept hoping some plot would emerge or the little bits of content in the game would be revealed to have some meaning. There are these stones throughout the world that I was expecting might be revealed to be gravestones, but that question is never answered. There is also a larger version of your character dressed in white that you see very briefly in cut scenes. It's never revealed who that is either.This feels like an unfinished game. It's as though it's just flat out missing entire mechanics or pieces of story. I enjoyed the art style. The music was okay. It wasn't great music, but it wasn't out of place either. I never encountered any bugs or crashes, so it's not unfinished in that sense. It just feels like the developers realized they couldn't meet their deadline, so they wrapped it up with what they had. Not worth the time or money.

_childDocuments_.review: At the time of writing this, it is currently June 15th 2020 at 5:15 PM, 7 minutes after the completion of my play through of this game.Let me tell you a story, dear reader, a short one, don't worry.I first saw this game on Steam's news page, and was instantly hit with a wave of nostalgia, having played a small portion of this game on the Play Station 3, I was happy to buy this game in order to live some of the joys of my childhood. I booted up the game thinking it'd be a simple console port, with the same graphics, same look... I could have never been more wrong. This game isn't just a console port, it's far from that, Journey is a beautiful game that blew my eyes away, gave them back to me, and then blew them away a second time. The graphics are simply stunning, and as a person who hasn't dusted their computer out in a couple months, i was running on the low end settings. That's saying something!The subtle music, the drifting winds, the calm serene atmosphere... all of it comes together into one to create this masterpiece of a game, this game isn't just something you look at or compete in, it's an experience. Exploration is awarded, and although it does do a slight bit of hand holding at the start, you're allowed to freely explore the majority of the world show to you. It's everything that my inner childhood was expecting, and so much more.A feature that I didn't know about before hand is the almost seamless transition into multiplayer that this game has, you'll be surfing the sands on your own, and then suddenly there's another person waiting for you at the next checkpoint, you each get to beep at each other and help the other through the game bit by bit, I walked through the final passage with a companion of my own, of which I stuck with thick and thin. We ran, we flew, and we surfed, the both of us having a completely new experience, just because the other were there to play too. There's no chat, no names, nothing, the only form of communication is the soft beeping of the other player. Anybody that you meet on the journey you take is unknown to you until you finish, where they are finally shown to you at the very end.This game is truly memorable to me, and will always have a deep place in my heart. It's worth the price, and so much more. It deserves the recognition, and it deserves all of the love that me and the fans of this community give it. I hope that i've helped give a good view of the game, and maybe even persuaded a few of you to buy it for yourself. Come join the fun! Maybe we'll meet each other in our travels, who knows! Have a pleasant evening folks, and happy surfing!

_childDocuments_.review: A metaphor for living, and for living with others. Reincarnation is an important part of it, but that could also be seen as a model of what it means to be old or young. You don't get that if you only play it once.The thing about multiple runs is that the early runs are mostly about exploring and learning, the later runs are really about helping the less experienced. All of which is like being young and being old, respectively. The middle runs are a mix of purposes.The value of the game is really in the relationships you have with utter strangers who just appear in your game (one at a time). You'd expect that some would be mean to you and out for themselves (as in life), but that generally doesn't happen. It has the effect of restoring your faith in humanity, and that's really the point. The game doesn't so much assert or impose this. It comes from fellow wayfarers, other actual human beings on this Earth now.The destination of the journey itself is death, but along the way there is beauty, fear, companionship, failed companionship, agreement, disagreement, opportunity, missed opportunity, frustration, fulfillment, bleakness, confusion, certainty, splendor, exhilaration, adversity, and achievement. Much like life itself.

_childDocuments_.review: "Journey" is a profoundly magical experience.I jumped into the game not knowing what to expect.  I knew the gameplay was similar to that of "Flower", which I had played before, and I did glimpse in the discussions that one could meet other travellers (players) on the way, but apart from that I had no idea what "Journey" was about.The simplicity and the alien feel of the game world is impressive.  But above all I was awestruck by the interaction with other players.  There is something extraordinary about meeting a stranger in this unfamiliar world and to then ally yourself to them in the common purpose of reaching the end of the journey set out before you.  This is done without clear language to communicate with (no voice server or texting).  All you have are chirp sounds, an accompanying visual sign (acting as a form of identification) and your movements to convey thoughts and feelings, wonder and appreciation, a warning or encouragement, a "Come over here!" or "Look, I found a symbol!"  I found that having this basic system is actually enough; it fits with the simplicity of the world around you."Journey" reminds us that there are others on this trek through life.  We are all on this same road that we have to figure out as we go.  There may be wonders and joys along the way.  Sometimes the road is filled with dangers and we may experience set backs.  But in the end we have a common goal: reaching or realising the destination, becoming the person we want to be, finding meaning in struggle, testing our resolve, and very importantly, sharing this experience with others, helping them or getting help ourselves, or simply just enjoying good company.  It seems a journey worth taking. In the end this journey is what it all comes down to.I loved the experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I have, in my life, been perturbed by video games. I have been shocked, excited, and certainly addicted. But there is no game that has quite brought the depth of feeling to me that Journey did. I had never been moved. I say had because in two hours, Journey completely broke me. I started skeptical of the game, not believing that it could possibly live up to its hype. The confusing control scheme and lack of plot left me feeling directionless. But some stellar level design pointed the way. It was good, but not great. And then, after a brief meditation, I got up, and there was someone standing next to me. I made a sound. They responded. And immediately I understood.I proceeded through the game. I lost some companions - one literally vaporised in front of me. One I was separated from by a great beast. And near the end, I surmounted what seemed to be the final hurdle with a companion, only to have my heart torn from my chest as they fell off the mountain below. I could not fetch them. I must not.And as the game ended in a great swell, I found, on the final screen, that there were two more companions I had been sharing my journey with along the way. I had never seen them. I had never talked to them. I did not even know that they existed. But, for a brief moment, they and I had been sharing an experience across cyberspace, wordlessly. Alone but together. Separated but connected. This was, I will confess, the moment for some tears.I cannot recommend this game enough. It is an astonishing accomplishment.Addendum: I still do not understand exactly what the control scheme was. I understand which buttons I pressed to make noises, but I don't understand precisely what they did. That in itself is a testimony of the utmost power to how profoundly intuitive and gripping this game is. Bravo.

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10Just finished my playthrough and it's hard to describe this game in a few words. It's truely an masterpiece in its own way.Usually I'm not into these kind of games but I got it a while back in a sale. Honestly...just try it. It's its own experience and very special but it will keep you stunned in front of your monitor and feel different emotions through the playthrough.While the start is rather slow, things start picking up once you meet someone else in the game. _childDocuments_.review: I don't have many hours on the Steam edition of this, but upon release on PS3, and then the remaster on PS4, I have logged several thousand hours on this game. The flow of this game allows for hours of nothing but pure bliss and ecstasy from the breathtaking visual aspect, to the absolutely wonderful musical score by Austin Wintory. The music has become a guilty pleasure, and would just love to wonder if there ever was more music for the game that never made the final cut.Journey is an absolutely wonderful game that tells a simple tale of how technological advancement can cause war between to factions among the same race. The game has you traveling through an arid desert as you slowly come to find out that the entire sand used to be open fields and the living cloth, that of which makes up your scarf, used to grow in the open. Something wonderful about the game is it shows how quickly the civilization had fallen due to their greed towards trying to be on top and instead it ended up costing these people, so to speak, to be killed by their own very creations. The constant visions that you are shown are the elders, the white-cloaks, trying to convey the message down to you, the red-cloak, the error in their ways in hopes that you (all players)can possibly fix the damages that they caused their world.Probably the best part of this game's co-op experience is you cannot have anyone join on you, and you do not know who you play with until the end of the game. Mind you, it can possibly be multiple people, because it's almost a bit like a drop in/drop out co-op but it's completely randomized at just about any point of any level. it's absolutely hysterical to play and it is absolutely a blast to constantly just roam about with new players or long-time players. The game never loses its touch, in my personal opinion, but I advise you give the game a chance in case it is good for you too.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: Somehow, without a single word, Journey provided the most profoundly emotional gaming experience of my life. I went in about as blind as I could for a game that came out over a decade ago, and that's absolutely the way the first play through should be. I found this to be a game where I often forgot I had a controller in my hands, multiple times IRL distractions broke my concentration and made me realize I was just witnessing the game with my jaw dropped, mouth open. As my final companion and I pushed through the last act, I realized I was actually crying. Just weeping as I pushed the joystick forward. There was a shocking level of catharsis for me, and I absolutely never expected that from this experience. It's not a game for everyone, but it was absolutely the game for me. My next play-through (once I've had time to process and reflect - which probably sounds so incredibly dumb if this game doesn't hit you the way it did me) will definitely be cozied up in a dark room with good headphones and no distractions. I rarely finish a game and immediately want to jump back in, but I'm really genuinely excited to explore this world again.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: Maybe, just maybe, my favourite video game ever.I can comfortably and confidently recommend this to literally anyone. If you have any concerns about whether this is for you, even if you normally don't like or play video games - lay those concerns to rest for this game. It can be experienced  by just about any demographic I can think of - I think the target audience must have just been "humanity" or something. I'm not a bucket list or "100 games every person should play before they die" kind of person, but this is one of those rare works that I really feel like everyone who has a chance should experience it.Only know that it's short, you're getting an experience you can complete in around 2-5 hours. It's also profound, and definitely should not be spoiled. Go in as blindly as possible (but not deaf, if it can be avoided! The audio experience here is as touching as the visual one).There are a lot of imitators and other games that try to do the "video games as art" thing by being either very on the nose about it, or just super duper abstract. Journey is much more subtle and sophisticated than a lot of other games trying to do what it does, and while I've played and enjoyed some of the things released since, it's actually difficult to capture in words how much more this one manages to draw you in. A lot of the emotion comes directly from the game experience, not from set-dressing trying to tell you to "feel" a certain way before getting back to the gameplay. The game gives you a title card - "Journey" and then no further written, spoken, or sung dialogue right up until the credits. Even if you haven't like a lot of the other sorts of things of this nature, I'd still suggest you give Journey a try.The PC port is ever-so-slightly more clunky than the original PlayStation3 release, so if you can play it on a PS3 or newer then go out of your way to do that. But for those who don't have access to a PlayStation system, the PC port is perfectly acceptable - just with some very slightly clunkier integration of the (ABSOLUTELY INCREDIBLE) soundtrack by Austin Wintory. The choppier bits aren't really noticeable unless you're very familiar with the original.I'd also recommend this educationally as a study on story structure for anyone interested - whether that's a highschool student trying to pass their short story exam or someone who wants to get into writing professionally. It's the most distilled version of the "12 stages of the Hero's Journey" you'll ever find.Genuinely a remarkable title. I cannot recommended it enough. Absolutely worth the asking price, stop reading reviews and just purchase it if you haven't already.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: Journey is a masterpiece, why? because it is beautiful and even though it has no narrative, the game conveys what it wants to say to the player very well. It tells us very clearly that each ending is a new beginning, a rebirth, and that is why I like it and recommend it even though it is very short, since every minute of play was worth every penny.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't have the chance to play Journey on its initial release in 2012 and later on I was too sick of its hype. But now that it is on Steam I had to try it and to be honest I didn't expect much. Over the past decade the number of good Indie games exploded and I've played so many "imaginative experience" type of games, that I expected an older game like Journey wasn't able to provide me something new.I was wrong. Of course it's not as unique anymore as it was eight years ago, yet it managed to get me hooked from start to finish. And yeah it's short, but it feels complete, a perfect example of knowing where to stop. The overall design holds up really well and the simplistic multiplayer aspect is still unmatched in this genre. I was sent on a magical journey following an ancient cult, wandered a scorching desert, felt melancholic, made a friend, grew stronger, climbed a towering mountain, uncovered the past, feared loss, defied nature and finally . All that in under 2 hours, amazing.

_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: To my friends Zoloft and Jobodo,I was excited to start my important Journey by myself. Proud and fearless. I start confidently repairing the giant bridge and see someone else dashing across it. Letting me do all the heavy lifting! Eventually they plopped down to help. Zoloft chirped at me, I chirped back and, eventually, I begrudgingly made my way with them, soaring across the bridge. Somewhere along the way Zoloft left on a different path and I ran into Jobodo. After being wary and annoyed of strangers I first tried to lose you in the desert. No dice. Looks like we were stuck together. I am so happy glad we were. You helped me discover, helped me hide, helped me learn to trust. We laughed, sang, surfed, got gobbled by stone dragons, cowered in fear, but persevered all the same. When the snow came and the dragons returned to blast your scarf into pieces TWICE I was so scared I would lose you. Watching you solemnly and silently press forward, tiny tail in tow, to meet back up to me filled me with so many emotions. I was relived, proud, scared, and protective. We went as far as we could, me trying to keep you warm with my scarf as best I could. Eventually it was too much. Our chirps faded, scarves shriveled, and our bodies succumbed to the cold. Suddenly, I rise vibrant as the sun, and to my absolute delight you are still there with me! You were soaring and filled with life! I didn't have to keep you warm any longer. You left me in the dust as I tried to keep up with you as we flew higher and higher, riding the backs of so many of the creatures we saved together. Such a beautiful sight! As we ascended to the top, our final steps all that remain in front of us, I can't help but think how lucky I was to have shared this experience with you. Our silhouettes slowly fade into one, and then diverge once more. Kindred and enriched spirits who shared a wondrous experience and who now must go their separate ways to help and improve others' journey's.What a game. So happy to end 2020 on this delightful little high note after so many ♥♥♥♥♥♥ lows.I will always cherish this experience and never forget you Jobodo (or you Zoloft...). I hope our paths cross again.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a bit of a comfort game for meThe way the story is told through non-verbal and indirect means, is very beautiful to me.The movement is smooth, the sliding and flying gives me very zen vibesThe way communication between players is nothing more than chirpingThe fact that despite there not being a single word spoken between players, you still feel a connectionIts amazingThere aren't a lot of people still playing, so if I don't get paired with someone, I can get through it pretty quickBut if I do find someone playing, I am more than happy  guiding them to all the secretsA short game, but an experience that I will remember for a lifetime

_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: If you look at Journey it seems to be a casual, visual, audio experience and not so much as a game. As you progress, you discover game like elements, but still it remains more art than a game. At one point I got a bit bored as the mechanics are quite simple. And that is one approach you can take. If you treat it more as a game - there are couple of achievements to complete..The visuals are good, the music and sounds effects are well done. Journey tells a story with no UI - it is a different experience than many other games try to do. Journey succeeds in it and gives just enough clues so you know where you go next, without getting lost. Journey is super short and it has limited replay ability unless you want to complete all of the achievements or . When you select high details, the sand becomes dull looking. To fix this:Thanks go out to It is a casual, chill out game . If you are looking for something like that, I can recommend it. It could also be one of those games to introduce non-gamers into playing games. Considering the duration, I recommend to only buy it when on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: I don't remember the last time a game drew me in as much as Journey did.  It was visually beautiful and the music and sound effects were wonderful.  The game play was fairly simple and intuitive, even for someone like me who often has trouble with 3D games.  The story was gripping, even though no words are spoken throughout the game.  I can't recommend this game enough.  It's been a long time since any form of media, be it a game, movie, book, or music, reached me on the level this game did.  It's hard to put into words why it did, but it did.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: My review: It felt nostalgic even though I'd never played it before. An experience, a duality. Steam review: Visually appealing. No instructions, no tips. Just drops you right into the game. Controls are easy and simple. As another user said the game is 'short and sweet' and I felt the play time was perfect.I plan on playing it once every year.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: The wheel in the sky keeps on turning. I don't know where I'll be tomorrow.Isn't that the truth. This is the type of game I never really expected to pick up and play....and well, lets get down to it.First off this is less of a game and more of art. It delivers a message more than wows you with extreme gameplay. So be ready and know what you are going into....or it won't last long on your screen. Art gaming isn't necessary bad (and in the case if Journey, it helps). It just makes the game a little more niche. But that brings about a big problem with it: being an art game, you probably won't get much more than one play out of it...maybe more if you really want to revisit. So to put it bluntly:You know I still love you, though we touched and went our separate ways.I got this on sale for a little less than $6, and i really recommend you do the same if you want to pick it up. Really this would be the perfect rental game, if that option was possible...because you will probably get about an hour to an hour and 1/2 out of it in one sitting, and then move on for a while. It doesn't feel like it drags on really, but it will be a one sitting game.The mountains we have climbed to get this far....On my journey, I actually ran into a player that helped me through about 85% of the game...which was interesting. It was weird seeing the screen name of the person that went with me during the credits...especially when we can't message each other. I wasn't sure if it was a real player or some crazy good AI. Sadly if you don't encounter anyone else....this will probably be more of a let down trying to figure out what you are supposed to do.But if you are in the right mindset for it...it will be an amazing experience. Just don't swallow the "I got so emotional" stuff...its really not that over the top like that. And in the end:Don't stop believin', hold on to that feeling.Streetlights, people......

_childDocuments_.review: Journey is one of those games that can't be defined by a review but hopefully, this will suffice. Even though the game is a walking simulator of sorts it happens to say a lot without saying anything at all. Even from the very first moments of the game, you'll be able to see the end in sight. I think everyone's experience with Journey will differ from what you take away from the game. The impression I got was of going into a world that you didn't know and discovering finally who you were. Ultimately you complete your quest and are finally able to pass on to a higher plane of existence. Again everyone's interpretations will be different and mine as well the more times I play it. Journey is an open metaphor most people can on some level relate to. Even if you don't relate to the story the visuals in Journey at times are just stunning. Some scenes almost feeling like you could've ripped them out of an art piece. The only problem I had with the game is that it's really short at about 1.5 hrs. On the other side of the coin that's probably the strongest aspect of the game since it only says whats necessary. One of the most enjoyable aspects of the game is joining someone else in their Journey. There's an odd dynamic when you try to converse with another player since you can't directly communicate with them. The only thing you have is little chirps and jumps to communicate some kind of message. I've never been so amazed but a simple mechanic before but this is by far is my favorite. Journey is an amazing game but the price of $15 is fairly steep for the length. I'd highly recommend picking this game up during a sale if possible. Hopefully, if you're reading this you'll discover your own Journey while playing. 85/100

_childDocuments_.review: If you aim to have a perfectly achieved game, please do not make purchase of JOURNEY.There is a possibility that you are not gonna complete the achievement 'Adventure'.
