The 5% players who got 'Adventure' are just because of their luck, good for them!🙄The game was decent, and the experience was pleasant though. However, being unable to get 'Adventure' really pissed me off.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: I'd like to tell a story about friendship—a friendship that will never reveal a true identity...I decided to launch Journey a week after my last play to get that achievement. And I thought, since I launched it again, why not try to get all of the achievements? They are quite easy to get, and there are plenty of tutorials. I already had unlocked a lot of them by just playing the game 3-4 times, but I still hadn't found a lot of secrets.So I launched it, went to the first story location with those carpet bridges. My first goal was to cross them, but one shouldn't be activated. I went straight for the last two and was afraid to meet anyone so that no one would ruin this achievement... but after the second bridge activation cutscene... boy oh boy, who I met!It was a full white person, with a little longer scarf than I had, and this guy was a freaking legend!(Because of his outfit, I figured that he already did what I was only going to.)In an instant, he understood what my goal was. He helped me climb up to the bridge, and...That's where our great journey begins!On each level, he showed me where all the walls, scarf letters, and secrets that I missed were located: the secret flower, the mysterious creature, and more. It's amazing how, in a game that only has a little song for engaging, we understood each other perfectly.My level of pure joy and excitement was off the charts. We helped each other the whole trip. A couple of times, he missed some letters, and I showed them to him, which added a little more of a teamwork feeling.A couple of times, he sat, and I figured that he wanted to make another achievement (which I already had at that time). Maybe he was hunting this achievement too, I don't know.But the funny thing is that I forgot which button to use, so I was furiously tapping every button on my keyboard, but NONE of them worked, and I don't know why!!! I mean, COME ON!!!Only two levels later, where for the first time you're hiding from the strong wind, it finally worked! :)There were a couple of "scary moments" when he was attacked by those things, and the most scary episode was when he was blown down by that strong wind in a staircase, but he quickly met me next to the next entrance.I think he was hunting some rare achievements too because at some point (a couple of times) he was spamming the "song" button like crazy and running around, the same way I did when I got that last "letter," "wall," or that mysterious creature achievement, so I think we definitely helped each other.And after all of this walking, sliding, flying, climbing, losing and finding each other, dying and resurrecting... when the only thing left was to walk into that mountain peak light, we sat for the last time for about half a minute in silence just to enjoy and to remember all this journey that we had, because we both knew that we would never meet here again.I was fully convinced that after the end credits, I would write down a nickname, to find and thank this person (doesn't matter if it is a guy or a girl, old or young person) for the help and for this journey that we walked together, from the very start to the finish.I waited for the end credits, then the black screen before the list of people you met, and finally...I saw my desktop wallpaper... (which is my profile picture)the game had crashed, leaving me with a bunch of mixed feelings and experiences.I didn't know if it was better this way or if I had lost an opportunity to meet someone interesting. I was a little confused if I can say so :)But what I knew for sure was that it was a great experience, and I loved it.I launched the game one more time, chose a white cloth, and walked a little in that hub location.After that, I didn't launch it anymore.Sure, I will do it at some point, but for now, I think it is not necessary.And that is my little story of a great Journey.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, this game is absolutely underwhelming. Having read the overwhelming amount of positive reviews for this title I came in thinking that I would experience something deeply emotional and moving and yet I felt nothing. However, if you're still interested then purchase this at a huge discount (at least 80% off) - current price is a rip-off.If you're looking for something deep and moving, try Gris.

_childDocuments_.review: It is a really weird experience. You don't know why you are going to the mountain, but you set your destination. The world is vast and the horizon awaits. _childDocuments_.review: Musical transitions are sometimes awkward or, in the Pink Desert especially, are just glitched to play weird static.Many sound effects stopped playing after my first playthrough.Connecting with other players after my first playthrough either didn't happen or was severely affected by lag.I'm disappointed by how poorly this game seems to have been ported. _childDocuments_.review: I don't really know where to begin with this.This game is great and it should rather be seen as an experience rather than a game actually. The images and sound are stunningly beautiful and the atmosphere is very relaxing. 10/10 for that!My biggest issue with this game is the co-op aspect. I would very much have liked to experience this game alone without being rushed along by other players and discovering all the nooks and crannies on my own. To me it felt like it was not my experience anymore. Sure, it adds to the experience going through all of it with someone else but still, not my cup of tea. You can disable coop in a couple of ways but I didn't know about all of that in my first playthrough. Another issue I have with this game apart from occasional crashing every now and then is the cut-scenes you can not skip. It can be quite annoying when you want to replay it in order to go for the achievements and things like that. Not to mention the weird way of selecting individual chapters to play.It is beautiful, emotional, atmospheric and just overall extremely enjoyable. I heard the PC port was not as good but as I haven't played it on console before, I can't say I have any issues with how it works in that sense. It's stunning and I am sure you would not regret getting it. I must mention the price value ratio is good too so you don't necessarily need to wait for sales to get it.9/10 overall
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: A really nice and short journey to experience in one sitting. You will meet random people through your travels ( you can only have 1 companion at once; if he leaves, another should quickly take his place ).The point is to travel with strangers, having just a chime to communicate. You can play alone or with a friend but it requires specific steps that you can find in guides.You quickly form a bond with your newly met companion and you can help each other reach the end. It is truly heartbreaking to lose your companion or say goodbye... if you finish the game you can see who you've travelled with and many people take this opportunity to thank their companions on the steam forums.But that's also the problem : in my first playthrough I only got great people so I was really enjoying the game. But on my other playthrough I encountered either annoying people or people that would leave after 5mins. If you're unlucky and you don't get the great people, it could really give you a bad impression instead of the good one =/I think the game's length is fine for this type of game but too short for the price, I would recommend waiting for sales. ~2 hours for the first playthrough + you can replay it to try and get all the collectibles and robe embroideries ( you get a new line on your robe everytime you finish the game, up to 3 times ). You start in a desert and are trying to reach the top of a mountain you can see in the distance. While you try to reach it, you will get visions showing you this world's past. The story is a bit vague but you get the gist of it and there are paintings scattered in the levels that give you other clues to what happened. You have two actions : chime and fly. Chime is used to communicate with other players and to activate pieces of cloth that allow you to progress in the world or you can use them to recharge your flying power. Fly allows you to reach places; you need "charges" to fly, those charges are represented with a scarf that glows and everytime you use a charge, a piece of your scarf stops glowing and you have to recharge it to use it again. You can make your scarf longer and therefore be able to fly longer too by collecting symbols throughout the game. You can also recharge your scarf just by standing next to another player, which is really useful.When you finish the game, you are brought back to the beginning and gain a line of embroidery on your robe, you can have up to 3. When you collect all symbols, you can choose to wear a white robe which starts with a longer scarf and said scarf recharges by itself when you touch the ground; you can't play with 1st playthrough players when you have the white robe.The gameplay is really smooth and it's pleasing to go from cloth to cloth, using your chime and flying to rise higher and higher. ~4 hours to get all achievements depending on your luck because there's an achievement where you need to complete most of the game with the same player ( you can also just select the last chapter and finish it with someone =P the game will consider that you've played the full game together ) + you have to sit and do nothing for 20s with another player.You have collectibles but you absolutely can get them in several playthroughs and there's a "chapter select" option to quickly go where you're missing something.You also have an achievement where you need to play again after 1 week without touching the game; but as usual with this kind of achievement, you can just change your computer's clock if you don't want to wait.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to write this review for a while now but somehow never did. This doesn't make a lot of sense taking into account the impact this game had on me. I've never had this kind of experience with a game before and it's truly unique.That said, let's go from the start: I discovered Journey back in December 2020 and when I bought this game I didn't know anything about it. The only thing I've heard was that it's supposed to be beautiful. I haven't done any more research on it beforehand and when this game was released in 2012 I haven't been that much into gaming yet. So it was basically a blind purchase. In retrospective, one of the best decisions ever.In Journey you go (surprise!) on a journey, travelling towards a mountain far away in the distance. It is a beautiful and very emotional game, that's the least I can tell you without spoiling anything. If you're interested in those kind of games buy it and don't do any further research. It must be said, though, you might need to play Journey more than once in order to grasp the concept and see what makes this game so special. Plus, stick to it till the end, don't skip the credits! Reading some of the reviews here, I feel like that's what some people overlooked and it makes me sad to know that they might have missed out on an amazing experience. I also recommend to play Journey in one sitting, it probably won't take much longer than two hours.Journey brought me to tears, made me laugh and feel happy and vulnerable at the same time. It evoked feelings of loneliness, warmth and curiosity, in a way few games can. As by now, I've played almost 150 hours already which might seem nuts taking into consideration the length of a single playthrough. But I can tell you, this didn't make certain runs less memorable. Every playthrough stands on its own and some I will never forget.

_childDocuments_.review: Garbage boring console time-wasting simulator.Atrocious low-quality sounds.Garbage clunky movement, garbage controls, garbage camera.No clear purpose, story, narrative, charcters, objective, or goal.No any explanation of what's going on.Very abstract (judging by other reviews, fans of this game consider this to be a pro, but I found it to be vague, aimless, and even confusing).The game looks pretty and thats it.The gameplay hardly ever had me engaged nor did I ever feel any emotional investment in the story or characters, especially since this game is so short.Game is designed to waste your time.The movement and progression is very slow.There were slow moments in the game, where you either hold 'forward' or sit through a cutscene you've already seen every run since your 1st. These were quite irritating to me when I was aiming for leftover achievements.After I beat the game, I didn't actually think it was the end till the credits started rolling and I was left with a feeling of "That's it?" I think reading all the reviews of people speaking of having zen like experiences, and achieving higher levels of consciousness and whatnot raised my expectations waaaaay too high for this game. It's a decent game but the repetitive game play and anticlimactic ending wasn't as life changing as I thought it would be.Having read the overwhelming amount of positive reviews for this title I came in thinking that I would experience something deeply emotional and moving and yet I felt nothing. _childDocuments_.review: Journey is an amazing game at non-verbal storytelling, not having any dialogue uttered over the game's 2 hr runtime and I think that's what makes the game work so well. It's a "Journey" and the contents of it can be left up to the player's interpretation. There's some guidance in the form of drawings and glyphs that appear in certain chapters but that's really it. I'm not really a fan of this amount of interpretation in a game's story but this game is an exception. It sets itself up to be a canvas for the player's mind to paint.On to the gameplay, it's simple and effective, only requiring two buttons to activate the character's abilities, and the rest is just walking. For a game entitled "Journey", they did a good job at making you feel like you're making this journey with your characters. The camera angles are wide, showing all of the land your person has to wade through. It adds to the immersion of the experience.Finally, my favorite feature of this game is the matchmaking system! I love how you can get into games with random strangers and they can become friends for the time you see them. You can add them after the game is done but I think the brevity of these tiny exchanges is enough. All in all, excellent game!P.S. If you like this game, check out ABZU. It's made by many people in the team who made this. Their 2nd title to come after this got shelved but if you want something to give you the wonderous fix, ABZU is your game.

_childDocuments_.review: I remember how stunned everyone was by thatgamecompany’s Journey back in 2012, when the game was released as a PS3 exclusive. I didn’t have that console and missed it entirely, but knowing Flower and flOw, I planned to definitely play the game some day. Well, now that the game is on PC that day has come. Except, it’s 8 years later. Does it matter?Journey is a very simple exploration-based title with simple controls and simple mechanics. You play as a mysterious robed traveler in a desert land trying to reach the summit of a mountain. You can chime, you can fly (depending on how much “magic” you have, shown on the scarf) and you can move around. The story is told via simple cutscenes that show a wordless story. And occasionally you may find yourself not alone but joined by a fellow traveler – an actual online player that you may travel with for a bit.It’s extremely simplistic and holds almost entirely on the game visual style and beautiful soundtrack. The colours, the shifting sands, the floating cloth creatures and great level design make this game work. With the online element being a really cute and surprisingly emotional cherry on top. And if you want something more, or dislike these kinds of ambient exploration titles, this might not be for you at all. But if you can lose yourself in these beautiful levels, this game still holds up and lasts exactly as long as it needs to, without outstaying the welcome.But we did get some beautiful games since 2012 that scratch the similar itch, yet might work for you even better. For me, for example, Abzû was a far more emotional experience. That game, developed by some of the same team from Journey, switched to the underwater setting and added some light educational elements to its world and to me that just made for a far more exciting experience. Perhaps, for you a more abstract experience of Journey will be more enjoyable, however.Whatever the case, though, it’s not an “either/or” question. Unlike Flower, which has aged a bit more poorly, Journey still feels amazing. And even though this new PC port isn’t as great as it could be (it can have bizarre hitching or audio glitches), it’s a wonderful way to experience this title. If you have a couple hours to lose yourself in a journey through a beautiful world, this game is definitely worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful and relaxing game from start to finish. The music is very good, and the game's story says a lot without saying much. Concerns for this PC Steam port date back to release at 2020, and according to the forums, not much has been done on thatgamecompany's part since then. Unfortunately, I can't recommend it because of it's playability on Steam specifically. Try a different port (console, maybe emu?). It's still worth a playthrough.Edit: Not all is lost, YMMV. After some research on the forums some say that turning V-sync on and lowering the graphics can help (it helped me, but it didn't help everyone). The forums were explaining that the problem lies in the frame rate. This is probably because the game was originally optimized for 60 fps (console) and the excessive fps of a high end rig causes artifacts, glitches, and crashing.

_childDocuments_.review: Journey is a 2012 adventure game, developed by thatgamecompany. The game was originally a Playstation exclusive, however 8 years later, the game finally saw a port to PC. And what a painful wait it was, as this game has been heralded as one of the greatest of all time. Multiple playthroughs later, I can certainly affirm that this is the case.Being dropped into a strange, magical desert land where not a single word of speech or dialogue is uttered, and not a single word of text is shown (minus the minimalistic, bare-bones title/pause menu), you take the role of a robed being, with one clear goal in view and in mind: Reach the summit of the looming mountain in the distance. And so your path across the landscape begins, surfing down sand dunes and riding alongside cloth creatures as you drift ever closer to your goal, as well as discovering the tale of the race that once inhabited it, and what befell them.At it's core, if one were to call this game a walking simulator, it is somewhat justified, as a majority of your time will be spent roaming the desert, exploring the buried temples and ruins, in a semi-linear fashion. Areas are self-contained with a few secrets, puzzles and achievements dotted around them, with them all eventually connecting to the next area.Graphics are clean with a cartoon-ish look, assisting the environmental storytelling in a grandiose fashion.Sound design is also on point as well, hearing the howling winds rustle by and shift the sand you're standing on, however I've noticed that the audio quality seems to take a dip in some segments, as if it was slightly bit-crushed. I believe a recent patch may have addressed that, however if it has then I am unable to tell the difference.And I haven't even touched up on what makes this game so special and what elevates it to an emotional level unlike most games I've played.At any point throughout the game, so long as you're online, you'll run into another robed figure just like you. That's not an NPC. That is an actual living breathing player, and fate has decided the two of you are to share the journey together.While you're unable to directly communicate with each other, only by small chirps and whistles, the way the game's experiences are structured push an amazing, undescribable feeling of companionship that stays with you throughout the game, as both of you face obstacles, overcome perils and push towards your mutually shared ultimate objective.The connection that is forged between the pair of you is something that lasts for ages, even well after you finish the game. And you only ever learn their name once it is all over, something I wish more games would do, as it helps break down the bias and misconceptions that people may have towards players. There are no arguments of differing opinions, no disagreeing on which path to take or how to take it.Just you, your partner, and the shared driven passion to attain your goal together.Austin Wintory's beautiful score also helps elevate the storytelling and important moments.Personal favourites from the OST are by far "Apothesis" and "I was Born For This", with a heavy emphasis on stringed instruments and a deep cello resonating all throughout.The game is certainly on the shorter side of a spectrum, with a normal playthrough only taking 2-3 hours at most, however secrets, achievements and even a sense of duty to guide the newer players through the land is what keeps me coming back every time, to assist others with their journey.Journey is also pretty well optimised and runs well, however I have noticed a problem where the game process decides to hog all of the CPU power available on your system, causing temperatures to rise quite a bit even though all that spare processing power isn't strictly needed. As such, I found it necessary to limit the game's amount of CPU power it can have, so my FPS does drop a bit because of this, however I would much prefer this than it conking out my fans because it's whirring all the time. I do hope they release a patch addressing this.That technical issue aside though, Journey is an extraordinarily unique game with an emotional and unforgettable way to connect players together as they travel through the land. What may seem like a stranger at first glance may very well end up being your best friend by the end of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Journey: Journey is one of the most beautiful games I've ever played. This game's artstyle is consistently jaw-dropping and had me taking ample screenshots of almost every single level. This game came out before but constantly reminded me of two games. Gris and Abzu. I think that this game has some of the best elements of both of those games, but doesn't have either of what makes both those games so so so incredible. For that reason, I really do like this game. It is a 'journey' that is borderline-unforgettable and treats the player to innumerous beautiful sights, but just doesn't quite scratch the itch that the very best walking sim/ artstyle extravaganza / puzzle type games like Gris, Abzu, and Journey do. The narrative was also not even nearly as profound as you would find in Gris, and while an enticing narrative with heart-striking beats is certainly not a requirement for a game such as Journey, but it is just another way that Journey has been passed by its successors. Don't get me wrong, Journey is still an excellent title with a really fun and interesting adventure to go on. Also, the addition of having other people join your Journey along the way is super super cool. More thoughts below. Feel free to comment if you have questions/ would like to discuss. Sights/Sounds/Performance- An incredibly beautiful artstyle with an incredibly beautiful soundtrack	- Textures/Graphics are not particularly stunning, but the visual style and amazing landscapes are bafflingly beautiful- I took a stupid amount of screenshots	- Such a beautiful artstyle and game- Sound design does feel a little muddy, however not a big deal- Flawless 144 frames at 1440p on a 3060 ti- 1 crash, nothing major- An incredible pause screen btw	- And the credits... DAMNGameplay- Gameplay loop is simple, effective, and very palatable- Movement feels quite smooth and fun- The addition of other players to kinda guide you around is really cool- Gameplay isn't really what's important	- It does what it needs to do		- Sits back, works how it should, and lets you experience the game- I am a sucker for varying cool environments, and this game (a lot like Gris) did that incredibly well, keeping the environments fun, engaging, varied, and interesting Narrative/Story- The goal is very clear from the beginning; make it to the top of the mountain- There is something so incredibly beautiful about going on this free, silent journey though the sand	- Incredibly fun to just run through the dunes, brings a smile to my face- While i didn't really understand the cutscenes all that much, the character progression was really cool to see- The darker undertones of the big stone dragon things destroying everything was super interesting and spiced up the 'journey'- The end was a really nice finish, capping off the journey by making it to the top and then watching your character ascend? and head all the way back to the beginning through all the rooms

_childDocuments_.review: 8 years and counting, Journey is a timeless classic based around something simple: the .  For those who don't know what the monomyth is, it's that underlying positivity/time correlation that makes so many movies and stories and epics so impactful.  Each area corresponds almost directly to a stage of the monomyth.  I'll let you research the details — to say more could well be to spoil the game.  In a way, however, this game is not exactly about emotion, but about   This is more or less the exact same awe that every religion in the world aspires to (NB word has it that even atheists can enjoy this game)....and if you don't know what Journey is, yes it's a game, but it's not a game.  Like so many games that came after it (e.g. GRIS, RiME), it is , first and foremost.  To judge this game is to judge art, so to judge this game for its gameplay would be wrong (granted, the gameplay is fun too).  And if you think this game is pretentious, then perhaps all art is pretentious to you — may as well stick to your pixel graphics games then.  Meanwhile the rest of us will take a moment to meditate in this game when we're feeling stressed (you can actually do that: press  to meditate).With breathtaking art by Matt Nava, a fine concept by Jenova Chen, and gorgeous music by Austin Wintory — 2 of these 3 are also behind ABZU — what's not to love about this game?  This is a game that turns strangers into friends.  Love and Peace are eminent...

_childDocuments_.review: Another banger from Annapurna Interactive. If you liked their game Flower, you'll love journey. It has the same beautiful storytelling environment and simple puzzle solving with the added feature of subtle co-op. I didn't even know until I finished my first playthrough that I was actually playing with other people and not just AI. Very few games can execute the same level of enjoyable teamwork with little more than a 'whistle button' to communicate with. A whole new level of meaning is added to the cliche saying "it's about the journey, not the destination" by completing this game, especially since we're never given a clear cut answer as to what exactly it is our character is trying to reach on top of the mountain. Overall, I highly recommend this game to anyone who can take the time to look around them and appreciate the natural beauty in things.

_childDocuments_.review: As a game designer myself I've always heard a lot of praise for this game from my peers. However to my shame I have to say that I never really touched the game outside of giving it a look or 2 on YouTube for reference material.However, this Steam Summer Sale around I gave it a shot, it's been on my to-do list for a while now and I figured I'd give it a shot!Wow... Just... Wow... Journey is an absolutely amazing game. Gameplay is buttery smooth and super simple to wrap ones head around. Level design is superb and I saw a lot of interesting takes on certain design principles; some really being stretched to their limits, yet they always manage to make it work. The game oozes dedication, love and attention to detail without losing sight of the bigger picture and packing it into a reasonable playtime.Aside from me fawning over all the technicalities and me going "oooh! aaahh! hmmmm interesting *scribble notes scribble*" I will have to say the game did touch the feels. At first I thought this was a solo game. And when I saw a carbon-copy of my player model appear out of the distance and pinging me in the Bridges level. I thought this was an enemy or something at first. I genuinely  had a "all hands on deck and focus" moment as the clone approached me. After it seemed that they were friendly I assumed it was a bot, which I found funny. But as time progressed I became more wary of the fact this "copy" might not be so much of a "copy" as I initially thought. In fact, it was another player. To say that my mind was blown was an understatement. Journey is yet another game that has a super unique, interesting and lovable play on multiplayer that reminded me of the way Dark Souls handles it's multiplayer (also a unique take on MP). Albeit this game does away with the murderparty and the like and is just pure jolly cooperation.However, due to the mute- less is more -nature of the game, the bonds you forge with the other players are quite unique. You really bond with the other player over your shared journey. Making sure they are okay and always try to stay close together, progressing together and enjoying the game together; as you can tell on almost a metaphysical level that the other player is enjoying the experience as much as you are. This along with the fact your only real means of communication being various degrees of pinging makes for an extremely unique MP experience. This will especially lead (at least it did for me) to very cathartic moments when you both reach the end goal. I had this experience 3 times now with 3 random players and it never failed to leave me with a bittersweet moment.But the Journey goes on even after "the goal" is reached, which ties in with the other strong point of the game. Symbolism. This game just oozes it left, right and centre and will leave you with much to ponder and philosophise about.This game is a defo recommendation from me for everyone that wants to experience a game that's truly outside the box and leaves you with something to think about.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played a lot of games in my life but this one is completely different. So respectful, so loving. It manages without any dialogue and still tells a story that picks you up emotionally. It's so relaxing, it brings you completely down. I think the last time I was this relaxed was after one of my yoga and meditation sessions. And as crazy as this may sound, I think this game is perfect for people who want to calm their monkey mind. Because many people who also like it have already played it umpteen times.If you get involved in this "Journey", have a decent pair of headphones, which are an absolute must here, and switch off all sources of interference for a moment, then you dive deep into a world that seems almost poetic. The game lasts just under an hour and anyone expecting a typical 0815 game will soon be disappointed, because:You don't die, you can't achieve any challenges, you don't get any names, no story, tasks or anything like that. But that's exactly the point! During the hour you experience wonderful scenery, music that has been thought through down to the last note and, at best, another player with whom you can share this experience. But without any chat or voice function. You only communicate through your actions and the other person's response.Maybe I've shed a tear and maybe the start screen with the sound is still playing in the background as I write this review (my first game review). After you have played the game, perhaps you will understand me a little. If not, that's fine too. I wish you wonderful moments with this game and other players.And if you like other games of this kind, then have a look at the developers page of thatgamecompany. Have fun!

_childDocuments_.review: I *definitely* didn't get the intended experience for this game, because I have annoying fickle, shaky internet. So this goes out to all of those other folks who also have shaky, fickle internet: don't play unless you got some stable internet.-------spoilers ahead-------From my understanding, this game is, in many ways, supposed to be joyful and heartwarming in the way it connects you to your mysterious "buddy" with whom you go on a roughly 3 hour journey. Even when things are at their most arduous, you and your companion pull through, for that companion to be revealed to be a fellow human being on the other end. Once the game is over, you've built an ephemeral, yet somehow lasting connection to another person who you might never ever meet or interact with again.This was not my gameplay experience. In fact, I had the opposite gameplay experience. The game was downright depressing. For me, I had a buddy for the first part, before my shaky internet basically disconnected me from anyone else after the first segment of the game. After that, it was a lonesome, fearful solo climb. Like, "you start the journey together, but you will die alone in the end" levels of depressing.-------spoilers end--------------so in any case, if your internet isn't entirely stable, avoid this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Polargamer101, this is for you, wherever you are.I started my journey as many of you did, confused, but intrigued. I sang to all around me, and watched as the wind and sand flowed through the cloth around me. I found small companions, and just as the gloom came, I sang once more, and my friends were freed.But then I saw one more friend. Who was that, in the distance just ahead of me? They just went down the path I was going to... I sang out, sang out as loud as I could to them, and at last, as we looked into the dunes to slide down below, they were there, waiting for me.We ventured, we slid, we bobbed and weaved together. It was a time of joy between both of us. Nothing could go wrong... And then we found the darkness. We were scared, we were afraid, but we still had each other, as we took each step side by side.We saw as the monsters took our joy, our hope. We could not let them snuff us out, so together, we made our way to freedom from the dark caves of misery. We cheered, as we had reached safety! We were still together, through all they searched to snuff us out.We climbed, climbed together into the light above us, seeing as our fate was laid bare in front of us. In our vision, there was only one of us, to start. As the vision carried on... There they were! My friend, we were destined to climb to our destination together, through all our struggles.As the winds blew, we pushed each other on, continuing to give our songs, to share our warmth. And that... is when disaster came.The monsters came, and my friend... was gone, swooped away, as I saw the sparks of life fade in the air...But wait, in the cover ahead! There they were! They were... alive!We kept pushing, kept going until we could not take one more step... so close to the end, they fell, and in the next step, so did I.Then hope shone on us, as we rose to the heavens, we didn't just sing, but we FLEW!We had made it. Together. Side by side, as it was meant to be. Our songs turned to hums, as we walked together into the light...Polargamer101, I couldn't find you when we were done, but I sing out now into the winds, that maybe, just maybe, you will hear me. I hardly know you, but I feel like I love you like a brother or sister. All I want to say is thank you for taking this Journey with me.

_childDocuments_.review: The setting of this game is a barren desert. As a result, gameplay objects are scattered across huge distances. 90% of the gameplay consists in holding W to get between landmarks. Not platforming; just walking forward. Normally I have no problem with games where most of the gameplay is just walking. However, games that de-emphasize gameplay do so to enable the player to focus more intensely on the environment and atmosphere of the game. Unfortunately, Journey has almost nothing to offer in terms of environment and atmosphere. Like I said earlier, the setting is a barren desert. The entire environment is one consistent dull orange color and some hills. The ruins are boring, uninspired, and sparse. Even when the atmosphere is boring, walking games can find some salvation in engaging movement mechanics. But the movement in this game is atrocious. You can't jump. There is a flying mechanic, but its use is limited . There is a mechanic to slide on hills, but it only works downhill. The walkspeed is agonizingly slow. You could recite the complete works of Shakespeare in the time that it takes to walk up a small hill in this game. The fact that the environment is so barren leaves you no choice but to focus all of your attention on these ♥♥♥♥♥♥ movement mechanics. If the walkspeed were tripled and flying and sliding were less limited the game would perhaps be bearable, but in its current state I find it actively painful to play. After 30 minutes of torture playing this game I watched a playthrough to see if anything changes later in the game. It does not.

I stop walking and so does the random co-op player, and I have no way to tell them to go on, because I'm going afk for a bit (Unless I learn Morse code).I know if the person keeps going on for a little bit, then they'll get another companion, but what if someone wants to get the achievement for completing most of the game with the same companion. _childDocuments_.review: I completed this game when it came out on PS3 and recently picked it up to replay on my Steam Deck. It’s just as beautiful and haunting as it was when it came out. _childDocuments_.review: Beautifully simplistic art, which is accompanied by a soundtrack that is fitting for each individual fragment of the game that  the player will experience.The story is never explained to the player throughout the game, nor is it at the end. The player has to formulate it's own interpretation of the story by experiencing the various spectacular events within the game, it has an allure which makes the game unique and powerful. Whatever you decide to settle with as your conclusion to the game's story, another player might have an extremely disparate interpretation, furthermore, due to the game's non-restrictive story telling, no interpretation is wrong, each is viable and of varying amounts of effort, all of which are nonetheless, feasible and satisyfing to the player's mindAnother delightful addition is it's co-op: throughout the game, you are able to encounter multiple players who - just like yourself - are on a journey, attempting to unravel the intriguing world laid before them. If you were to experience it with a friend, a beautiful dichotomy of theories and interpretations could shape which is even more interestingAll in all, the game is unique, intriguing, short and simplistic and often during the playthrough, your mind is on a longer journey than the character which you control.

_childDocuments_.review: Just another sob story from another emotional player who takes everything personally...This game means a lot to me. I played it alone countless times without any goal in mind. I would launch it and I'd just walk, surf on the sand, 'sing' with the clothes, fly with them, feel the music, take everything in until I get lost in the atmosphere. It is a safe place for me.It helped me get through some of the loneliest days of my life... only to be left alone again by my companion! Ha! Man did it hurt! One time, I waited for hours, no one came. I just want to finish it with someone! Why is it so hard? Am I playing it wrong??? Am I really that difficult that even in a made up world no one wants to be with me??? I felt so discouraged but... it's still beautiful.Still I tried and tried and tried, I memorized the map, I worked hard to get the white robe and I wore it all the time because I thought that would make them want to finish the game with me. It still did not work... but to my surprise, it's still beautiful.And through my despair, one time, I chose to leave a companion on purpose. . . "Now, how does THAT feel?!" . . . only to... immediately regret it right after. I still feel the lump in my throat from that time. I paid for that by dying alone. I would never do that again.I have finally completed the game after almost a year. What a journey.I want to cry. Thank you to all of the companions I have met along the way.Finished the game for the first time: August 12 2021 @ 10:05pmFinished the game for the first time with a companion: August 2 2022 @ 1:32am

_childDocuments_.review: This is a masterpiece. There's no other way for me to describe this. An absolute masterpiece.I think the power of Journey lies in how every single piece that makes it clicks just right with the other. From the beautiful visuals, through the wonderful soundtrack, to the simple yet grasping story; Journey combines them all together into a marvelous experience that feels flawless from start to finish. There aren't many games that leave me speechless as the credits roll, but Journey certainly left an impact on me.It's short - two or three hours at best - but that's all it needs to achieve its goal. In fact, I'm pretty sure that adding any more length to the game would've taken away some of its charm. Journey lets you peek into its world, experience it, enjoy it, and then lets you off to your own conclusion. It's very important to know how long your game should run for, and the devs nailed it just right.I think the best part for me was the surprise of finding someone else alongside my adventure. I didn't know this game had online co-op until that very moment. We went a few levels through until we had to part ways, but I kept thinking of this fellow throughout the rest of the game. Where are they now? Did they finish it? What did they think of it? Will I see them again? Then, when the credits rolled and I saw their name, I felt great. I don't know why... I'm just happy I found out who they were.Journey is one of these rare gems that leave you truly wondering at the end. I feel like there's a much deeper meaning to this tale than one might see on the surface, and I'll certainly ponder this for a while now. But for me, a game that leaves me with this feeling is a fantastic game - and Journey is, by all means, a true masterpiece.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: -Easy-Nice visuals-Lovely musicCons: -Very repetitive-There are probably only about 5 total actions you can take in the game, give or take-No clear purpose, story, narrative, objective, or goal; very abstract (judging by other reviews, fans of this game consider this to be a pro, but I found it to be vague, aimless, and even confusing)This game is pretty nice to look at, but that's about all it has going for it. The premise of the game is that you are making a journey across a post apocalyptic landscape, at points you are randomly partnered with another player who is also in the game. You can only communicate with this partner using short or long chirps. There are about 4 types of creatures in the game, one which is hostile, and which are re-occurring throughout most of the levels. As you journey towards your destination, you collect pieces of red fabric which lengthen your character's scarf and allow you to multi-jump or "fly." This in turn allows you to reach greater heights, but aside from the appeal of just jumping/flying higher, there is not much benefit of this from a gameplay perspective. It's just personally gratifying.I've asked a couple people what they like about this game and the general consensus seems to be something to the effect of "exploring for exploring sake with a stranger." Some feel that being partnered with someone you can't talk to or know their name heightens the sense of camaraderie. I can get that, but I don't think it's enough to redeem the game's lack of content. A good friend of mine said "the story is up to you to create." I don't understand this because there are no elements of this game that I would consider to be sandbox-like. Maybe they just meant it's up for interpretation.It's wholesome enough, but there's not much to it, and unless you are easily moved by pretty music and visuals, I don't understand how this is considered to be an emotional game. I found it to be a bit boring. It is a journey without purpose or explanation. And that's fine if that's what you're into, which obviously a lot of people are, but any of this sounds unappealing for you, I wouldn't bother with this game.

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic experiment in human social interaction.This game boils down communication with randomly assigned players to movement and simple audio chirps. What results is an improvised interaction with another human unflavoured by name, gender, speech pattern or fame. Language is constructed on the fly. How do you indicate excitement with such a simple lexicon? How about danger? You'll find that humans are naturally very good problem solvers in matters such as these and you'll build your own bespoke communication method with each player almost unconsciously.You may spend hours of quality time with someone only to find they are the kind of person you wouldn't ever seek out in real life.You might spend almost the entire game alone, only to be saved in the final hour by an experienced player who helps you push forward.The feel of the game changes each time because the human the game matches you with is different and the time you meet them varies. Even the most toxic of player will be hard pressed not to feel passion and empathy for their partner on their first few plays.It doesn't always work as it should, but if you get the right person at the right time, there is no equivalent in gaming as it stands.

_childDocuments_.review: Enter the world of Journey, the third game from indie developers thatgamecompany (creators of "flOw" and "Flower"). Journey is an interactive parable, an anonymous online adventure to experience a person’s life passage and their intersections with other’s. You wake alone and surrounded by miles of burning, sprawling desert, and soon discover the looming mountaintop which is your goal. Faced with rolling sand dunes, age-old ruins, caves and howling winds, your passage will not be an easy one. The goal is to get to the mountaintop, but the experience is discovering who you are, what this place is, and what is your purpose. Travel and explore this ancient, mysterious world alone, or with a stranger you meet along the way. Soar above ruins and glide across sands as you discover the secrets of a forgotten civilization. [thatgamecompany]

name: SCARF
detailed_description: Scarf is an adventure game mixing puzzles and 3D platforms, offering an allegorical journey through beautiful worlds. Explore and find the truth behind your story with the help of your partner, a dragon-shaped scarf. Unlock new abilities and discover your true destiny. STORY What does it mean to be a hero? To fulfill your destiny? Or to rebel against it? Scarf is an exciting singleplayer puzzle adventure that blends lyricism with a 3D platform game to offer an allegorical journey through beautiful worlds. Will you discover their secrets? And at what cost? GAMEPLAY Immerse yourself in a metaphorical tale that reflects on what it means to be a hero. With your scarf as your only ally, your mission is to trap the rebellious souls that have created their own worlds. Explore beautiful 3D landscapes, each with its own unique mechanics. Travel through different areas and learn new abilities that will allow you to overcome interesting challenges. Jump, glide, or swing as you discover the secrets of these new worlds. Discover a rich mythology and reconstruct your own version of the facts by exploring the worlds created by the souls. Enjoy an audiovisual section that will transport you to a fantasy dimension filled with light and color… but also shadows. Scarf is a slow-paced game that allows you to savor the beauty of each moment. Explore the world and solve interesting puzzles to uncover the truth and move forward with the adventure. Gather unique collectibles to unlock an alternative ending. Bond with your dragon-shaped scarf which, using different abilities such as the glider, the double jump, and the liana, will help you uncover the mythology behind the world. FEATURES A story for all audiences with multiple narrative layers Beautiful scenarios A stunning art style A mysterious polymorphic scarf in the shape of a dragon An alternative ending depending on the player’s exploration Adaptative orchestral music A magical world with a unique mythology Exploration, puzzles, and platforms make for a lovely adventure

_childDocuments_.review: Scarf is a charming puzzle platformer with gorgeous visuals, similar to  However, behind its bright colours and beautiful landscapes, there are many flaws. Scarf is unfortunately riddled with bugs that developers do not seem to be addressing and admittedly, I had no clue what was happening with the story. Despite this, I still enjoyed it for its core functionality, a casual fun platformer.Before I begin, I... am at a bit of a loss here. I finished the game and yet, I have little understanding on what actually happened, or what the nebulous story was trying to portray. I had to read the store page to gain a bit of a better understanding, but I am still uncertain.You play as a small blue glowing creature named Hero. Hero seems peaceful, but he has a red scarf that absorbs the seemingly friendly creatures around him. Or, this was my understanding at least. There is no dialogue, except for one sentence in a handful of scenes where a dark orb is collected. I get the impression these are *bad* as Hero begins to slowly turn black with dark ominous looking ink after collecting them. Upon finishing the game, I discovered there are other endings, I presume these have to do with the aforementioned orbs...? When I collected these, I had no idea of their implications and was just trying to pick up the shiny objects that I thought were mandatory to progress, but seem to be actually optional. I do not believe the game explained this at all. I believe the story is supposed to be an invigorating tale about what it means to be a hero, and the choices you make... but that is a bit of a stab in the dark. I would not say I am generally unperceptive, even in textless games, but this one did have me perplexed. Despite this, it did not bother me too much, as the gameplay was my main focus.Scarf is a simple, bare-bones type of platformer, and I found its simplicity to create a cozy,  relaxing experience. The main mechanics revolve around the scarf. It can be used to double jump, glide and even slingshot around the environments. There are of course, puzzles throughout, typically condensed into large sections filled with mini puzzles. Completing one of these puzzles will give you an object needed to progress. Collect all of these to get past the main gate. Towards the end of the game, I was starting to feel these repeated large puzzle areas were dragging on, but the developers' do try and keep it variable. There are memory puzzles, where the parts must be rotated to match the wall mural, interact with the environment by pulling levers or pushing blocks to transport an object somewhere (without needing to jump) or initiating a gear system and so forth. These environment-based puzzles are fairly straight-forward, the only times I was "stuck," was when I did not know where to go next, but I had always missed a lever to pull and just had to search the vicinity again to quickly uncover it.The scarf has a personality of its own and sometimes, light orbs must be found to give it its colour back, otherwise its abilities cannot be used. The scarf can even be consoled and almost patted. Giving it a personality was cute, and I am certain I am missing its ties to the plot, but at least at surface value, I still found it charming.The visuals are Scarf's drawcard, and rightfully so. The environments are intensely radiant, quite literally glistening in all daylight scenes. There are three main levels, the desert, ocean and forest. These biome levels are aptly named and all equally gorgeous. The clear vibrant blue water, topped with blue flowers as platforms to jump across, sand being blown away by the gusts of wind, or even just the sparkling red scarf gliding through the air were all lovely and captivating.The pleasant light soundtrack further emphasises the cozy nature of Scarf, but the characters constant vocal interjections were a tad vexing. This may be a bit of a nit-pick, but with the backing soundtrack being noticeably quiet, there seemed to be an unusual repetition and emphasis on Hero's continuous grunts of exertion, whenever he did anything. Despite my complete confusion over the story, the bugs and performance issues are by far the biggest issue I had with Scarf. I experienced many bugs including (but not limited to), becoming stuck inside an object, commands not being accepted, resulting in me having to restart, falling through platforms due to finnicky movement issues, and wildlife doing 360 spins on the spot.Performance was also lacklustre with an average of 35-45fps in almost all scenes. In the more demanding areas, where the water ball was used to traverse underwater, this resulted in even more severe drops to around 25fps. As a result, the movement is janky and does not feel responsive to controls, which caused me to occasionally miss a few grapple hooks. Despite the drops in fps and infrequent stuttering, the platforming sections were still playable, and the game is very forgiving with constant auto saves.  4 hours. For completionists, maybe around 6. Yes Yes, to achieve the other endings/discover all collectables.Scarf is a simple platformer with dazzling visuals, but it is riddled with bugs, performance issues and has a story that I did not grasp at all. On a surface level, I enjoyed it, and had fun swinging, gliding and jumping through the air. The puzzles are nothing strenuous, but were enough to keep me amused, and the gorgeous environments kept me coming back for more. I recommend Scarf at a heavy discount for platformer fans interested in the art style, but I would not be in a rush to purchase it, especially as the bugs and issues I mentioned appear to have been noted upon its release last year, but are still yet to be patched.

_childDocuments_.review: Scarf fails at being both a good platformer, and a good puzzle game. The movement is slow and stuff, and puzzles fail to ever be more interesting or complex than the maze on the back of a happy meal box. I have never played a game that is as short, yet dragged out as Scarf. My playthrough was only 4 hours and I was still bored out of my mind for much of that. While there are definitely some all right ideas, the developers have no idea how to properly scale how big a level should be, or how to build upon an idea to keep the gameplay engaging and interesting. This leads to levels that are far too large, so you spend most of your time running around in empty open space in order to go from one boring task to the next, something not helped by your slow movement. The story is uninteresting, and there are frequent performance issues present.  Scarf is a 3D puzzle platformer, but unfortunately is unable to capture what makes both of these genres interesting. On the puzzle side of things, Scarf fails to ever make interesting puzzles. 90% of the time, the puzzles you're tasked with solving will be so easy and basic that a toddler would be able to figure it out with no problem. They're not easy while being fun either, as most of the time all you have to do is pull a lever, or step on a switch to progress forward. Occasionally you will have to move tiles into certain places, but the game either puts the solution on a wall right in front of you, or forces you to keep mixing and matching until you find the correct order. Even when I solved some of these, I had no idea why the solution was what it was, as the picture the tiles formed didn't even make sense. On the platforming side of things, the slow movement and heavy feel to the character make moving around the world extremely boring. A good platformer should have fluid movement, and use that movement combined with interesting level design to create fun and exciting gameplay, but that doesn't happen in Scarf. Most of the "platforming" is actually simply moving from platform to platform that connect to each other, so a lot of the time you don't even have to press the jump button. You do eventually unlock gliding, and a grapple type ability but these are never used in any way that is even remotely fun or engaging, leaving you with boring platforming. The story is told using virtually no dialogue, and mostly consisting of wordless cutscenes. You can find some hidden story segments hidden away in the levels that do contain dialogue, although these are extremely short, and the only way that the "true story" is told. Why an already short game would hide away its story is beyond me. Luckily you can very quickly figure out what is really happening in the terms of the story and its "twist" so you don't miss out on much. It's not even worth going out of your way to find these hidden story bits either, as the game has nothing interesting to tell at all, and the story is extremely bland and underdeveloped. My guess is that the developers wanted the main focus to be on the gameplay and not the story, but as we already discussed, that was a failure of its own, so this was a baffling decision by the developers that just adds to the boredom that the player must endure in order to see the game's ending, which is extremely unsatisfying.  Perhaps the only all right part of Scarf would be its presentation. The world is colorful, and full of bright colors, nice looking scenery, and somewhat interesting set pieces. There are 3 different levels with their own themes of ocean, desert, and forest. They all felt different and were nice enough looking. the graphics style isn't anything special or unique but it fits the game fine enough. The music was all right. The soundtrack was decent, with every level having its own background music that fit the area nicely. Writing this review, I can't remember any of the tracks off the top of my head, but none of them made me want to turn the music off, or bothered me at all. While nothing in the presentation is fantastic, nothing about it is bad, its just all right, which is better than anything else in the game.  The levels are all very linear, with a few secret areas here and there where you can find hidden artwork, or those little story bits. This by itself isn't a bad thing but they're all far too big for your character's slow movement. I would estimate that 50% of my playtime alone was spent walking in a straight line to the next puzzle. This wasn't walking 10 seconds to solve a puzzle that took a minute or two to solve either, it was like walking 45 seconds to a puzzle that took 10 seconds to solve. Even worse were the times where you would walk forward for one or two minutes in order to get to the next section. There's nothing wrong with big levels but you need to fill them with engaging gameplay. I feel like many of the levels could've simply scaled down the walkways or empty areas by 50% and they would be fine. The amount of useless dead space absolutely baffled me. It felt like the developers were simply trying to pad out the run time of their short game in order to make the player feel like they were getting their money worth. Big levels aren't the only example of padding out the playtime either. On more than one occasion you are put in a small area and have to walk around collecting orbs to feed your scarf in order to heal it. These have 0 puzzles or platforming and are literally just you walking around a small area collecting multiple things and bringing them to one area. There's no reason these couldn't have been simple cutscenes.  Scarf isn't only riddled with underdeveloped gameplay issued but is also plagued by bugs and performance issues. There were multiple times throughout my playthrough where button prompts simply did not work. One of these is a known issue where in the desert level you sometimes cannot feed an orb to your scarf. This was known to the developers shortly after release and they said they would be working on it but it still has not been patched. There are also multiple walls that you can just walk right into, as if they weren't there at all. At one location I was able to simply stand on air. Frame rate issues and stuttering were very frequent as well. These were especially noticeable during the sequences where you use an orb to move water out of the way. On one occasion the game even crashed on me while I was gliding from one area to another.  In conclusion, Scarf fails to capture the great aspects of both genres it mixes together. The levels are poorly designed, being far too big causing dragged out boring areas that pad out the games playtime. These issues mixed with the poor performance and numerous bugs create a gaming experience that simply isn't worth your time, or money. For more reviews, follow my

_childDocuments_.review: SCARF is the singer without a voice, and dancer without legs. There are great ideas in the game, but none of them were given enough focus or care, so each and every one of them slowly fell short of what they could have been. With a gorgeous world only made prettier by the OLED display I played the game on, I truly wish I could give the game a higher rating. SCARF works best if you take it merely as a walking simulator.

_childDocuments_.review: There is a lot to like about this game, unfortunately it's overshadowed by some simple yet severe design choices>The first and most serious issue is that as a collectible platformer it's not possible to simply go back to a level and quickly hunt down the few items you missed the first time. When replaying a leveling, everything reset. You lose all abilities gained during the level, lose drawings you collected the first time, and must rewatch every cutscene in addition to redoing every puzzle. You also cannot simply exit a level once you've collected the one item you've missed, but must play it through entirely. Imagine my disappoint when I replayed the first level grabbing the one painting I drawing I missed the first time only to realize I would have to play the level yet a third time and do everything I had already done in one go simply to have the game recognize I've gotten all the collectibles.The second problem is far simpler, but yet a constant frustration. The walking is incredibly slow, the running isn't much faster, and you must hold down a button to run. There is absolutely no reason for walking at all in this game as its far too forgiving with platforming and both walking and running are far to slow. Running should at least have an option to toggle to default. What this means is that for the entire game you will be holding down a single button simply to play the game.

_childDocuments_.review: The game looks pretty, but that's about it. The performance is very poor, with problems like audio crackling and terrible, stuttering FPS even on low graphical settings. But even if the game was more optimized and performed well, it still wouldn't have much to offer. The controls are stiff, the puzzles feel like dull, mindless chores, and the story - which is clearly trying oh so hard to be very deep with its solemn narration - is nothing but vapid drivel and a waste of your time. The whole experience just feels a pretentious art project by some chuunibyou who played Journey and decided it would be cool to inject a bunch of DARKNESS into it (and also didn't know how to program a functional game). If you like quiet, relaxing and meditative indie games, save your time and skip this one and go play something like Omno instead.

_childDocuments_.review: I live in the UK. It would be underselling the political situation here to say the past few weeks have been an exudation of poo. My instincts are to follow such events with bloodshot eyes. To shower in the poo. Throw in January and February, where it’s eternally wet, cold, and grey, and you’ve got an especially exhausted, probably blubbering, Ross.A pair of like-minded friends retreated to Barbados. Unable to afford such an extravagance, I stepped into . Admittedly, it’s not quite the same thing, but stay with me.Far from Blighty’s miseries, here was a world that nurtured and healed, that popped with gleaming colours and sparkled with iridescence. Originality and depth weren’t among the popping and gleaming, but they didn’t need to be.It was , and sometimes that’s enough, y’know?Uprising Studios’  is beautiful in a way the screenshots don’t quite capture. Maybe it’s the undulating sands or the shimmer of the so-very-blue water, but the place needs to  to be properly appreciated. For the eponymous scarf to crest in the air, casting its majestic red glow on an already luminous world.The game bills itself as a hero’s journey with some standard fare about fulfilling your destiny, but that’s a stretch. A fantastical creation myth is spun in the game’s opening, birthing our protagonist who bonds with a lonely red intelligence. After introducing a set of tinkering souls who have split the cosmos, off we embark to bring order out of chaos - that red intelligence wrapped around our hero's neck.As with many indie platformers, the act of inhabiting the world and demonstrating agency brings life to it. The revolutionary act of just . Invisible platforms materialise and old machinery creaks into life once supplied with enough beads of light.You’ll do all this while performing classic platforming tasks. Jumping across timed pads, pushing and pulling boxes, and taking objects from one point to the next are just a few of the activities in store. You’ve seen and played most of it before, even if the scarf, which allows you to jump and glide, alters the flavour a little. If that sounds like a criticism, it’s not; this is familiar platforming done very well.If there is criticism, it’s in the controls, which aren’t as responsive as I feel they need to be. If you end up gliding the wrong way, for instance, you’ll have to try again – it’s like manoeuvring a 747. More fluidity would have gone a long way.On top of what I said earlier about the game’s lofty thematic claims, the narrative component is its weakest.  boasts respectable voice acting, but I question the necessity for it. Its narrative does a lot with symbolism and allegory, which is when it works best. It’s similar to something like  in this respect – walls painted with scenes that drip meaning, provide context. This is a more effective method for the story  is trying to tell, so whenever one of the two voices pops up, it’s a bit jarring. Perhaps it doesn’t help that the writing needed some extra polish.I’m nit-picking now, and I’d rather not:  was , arriving just when I needed it. Aesthetically, it was a bit like the hub worlds for the second  game, with its magic castles and chilled getaways. Nostalgia at play? Most certainly; platformers are in my blood. is appreciably short, absolutely gorgeous, and a lovely break from reality. Cheaper than Barbados, too.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is pretty, but that's about all it has going for it. It's incredibly poorly optimized, ran at about 15-20 FPS for most of the game, particularly in the third area. The "puzzles" and platforming are largely underwhelming, right up until the hide and seek game, at which point things become outright asinine. _childDocuments_.review: This game is magical and a feast to the mind with how beautiful it looks and sounds. I loved exploring, solving puzzles and collecting things. I'm giving this a negative on principle. This game is left in a buggy state that can be game breaking if you're not careful. Here are my main cons:1. There are sections in the game where your save can become useless and you have to start from the very beginning. I experienced one of those instances in the desert where I returned to a previous area to collect something I missed. The door didn't open on the way out and the game only has one save. There is also no option to return to the hub. You have to finish the level first. I was fortunate enough to be aware of the problems based on the impressions of others. So I've made multiple save backups to be on the safe side. 2. It's ridiculous that the game doesn't allow you to return to your hub whenever you feel like it. If you miss any collectible, you have to return to a level and finish the level in its entirety. There are 3 levels total but each one is huge and takes a long time to finish. This unnecessarily wastes your time. 3. The trophies for collecting all drawings and toys are bugged. Even though I collected everything, I didn't get them. Some did when you look at the stats. So I'm not sure what I did wrong. 4. The game is very badly optimized. I have a 4070 ti, i5-13400f and 32gb ram. My 1440p monitor allows 165fps and I was worried it would be too much on the highest settings. I put the game on 120 fps just to be on the safe side, there were still many instances where the GPU would need 100%. There have been brief moments where the fps dropped to 100 or there were stutters when parts of the areas were loading. I had a pretty smooth experience for the most part but I'm not sure about older hardware.This game is worth playing if you are aware of its problems and come prepared. Make sure you back up your saves. It might also be better to have a guide for all the collectibles if you know yourself to be impatient and don't like repeating long levels for them. If you prefer finding the collectibles on your own, at least the first time, then try not to backtrack while you're in the levels. It's better to finish the levels and then do them again. This game could have been so much better if the devs patched it at least once. They never did. They mentioned they would fix the bugs for a while around release, then things went real quiet after that. Those kind of devs/publishers are not worth supporting. Hence the negative review.

_childDocuments_.review: Scarf has little for itself. The first look impresses but once you get to control the main character and tries the first "puzzles", all the charm is taken away. Only subsist the frustration.The character's movements are heavy, the game-breaking bugs are getting numerous on the first-half of the game (2 in the second level , first time it happens in my years of gaming) and the sound design is clearly not what the devs have insisted on (sorry but the sound on the pause menu is irritating). It is a pitty for such an atmospheric game.Oh and the characters is making small sounds when moving, which is cringing as ♥♥♥ for my part ! But, you know, that's only my opinion.A little more polishing would have been welcomed to make this game good (yet not memorable). Especially as it looks like the story has more to offer than a "hero who saves the ecosystem/universe with some powers". .Move along is you don't want to have a rancid taste on a game that takes everything already made and doesn't succeed to deliver it right.

_childDocuments_.review: Many thanks to Uprising Studios and HandyGames for the Review key.I grew up on platform games of the NES and Sega Master System and its always nice to venture back that way and have a go. SCARF is a fantastic example of a puzzle platformer done well, vibes or Journey crossed with the likes of Mario with a stunning visual art style and superb orchestral music. It's story at first appears very simple but as you progress everything is not perhaps as it seems and frankly it takes a dark turn, though not in such an overt way younger players could not enjoy the game. Supporting the game are fantastically made animated story clips which would make for an amazing stand alone visual novel.I am not sure of the price but if its sitting anywhere up to around 14 USD/EUR then its worth a look. Initial play through took me just over 4 hours.You can check out my full review here:

_childDocuments_.review: If you can get past the poor optimization, bugs, and general jank (there's a very brief stealth sequence late in the game that's so clumsily designed that it almost made me quit the game in frustration)... this is actually a pretty fun combat-free 3D platformer with a focus on reasonably satisfying exploration and puzzles. I'd definitely wait for a sale, though, and I'd also recommend  over this one, as it's another recent indie 3D platformer that's attempting very similar things to  with its gameplay, atmosphere, and even art direction, but with significantly more polished execution.The story is also very questionably told and involves a "twist" that isn't actually a twist at all, since any potential impact has already been thoroughly spoiled by both optional collectibles and mandatory cutscenes. still, the focus here is more on gameplay than storytelling (this isn't , though that was clearly an inspiration), so the weak story doesn't hurt the game as much as it otherwise might have.

_childDocuments_.review: Like most modern games of this era you are thrust into the game with no knowledge of who you are, why you are here, what you need to do, or even how to do it.  It’s a delicate balance of frustration and discovery, as you slowly figure things out during your journey.    You’ll be playing as what can best be described as a young boy with white almost glowing skin, a hole through his chest, and a tuft of hair that would make Bart Simpson envious.  We quickly meet up with a magical red dragon – the Chinese serpent kind, not the D&D kind, who is able to shapeshift into a glittering scarf that you will wear proudly for most of the game.The game flow is fairly basic stuff.  After a short tutorial section you reach a hub area with multiple portals leading into themed environments like the ocean, desert, and forest.  You’ll enter into these wondrous worlds exploring and gathering the numerous collectible items such as scarf fragments, assorted puzzle-solving components, and a random assortment of well-hidden animal toys.  Much of the game is figuring out where to go and how to get there.  There are bridges and structures that are out of phase and you’ll need to find and insert purple gems into sockets to make them solid.  You’ll also need to collect all the fabric collectibles to use at the obelisk to reach the exit to each world.It’s also worth noting that Scarf can be finished in 3-4 hours – add another hour or two if you want to find all the collectibles and unlock all 25 achievements.  Arguably, that is a short game, but at only $15 the quality certainly makes up for any lack of longevity.  I’d rather have a compact magical adventure that I can finish in a couple of sessions than some game that was dragging things along just to satisfy the clock-watch gamers out there.  And based on how thoroughly you explore this enchanted world you may just discover an alternate ending.Read the full review at Watch our gameplay video of the first two portal zones (Ocean and Desert) at More Steam reviews on our Curator page -

_childDocuments_.review: Puzzle platformer game with a great setting, narrative, story and achievements. A more relaxing and quite enjoyable experience for achievement hunters.A small puzzle platformer game where you, together with your scarf, journey throughout different worlds.Scarf is a cute little adventure game where you use your companion to gain more abilities and explore different worlds. The visuals and setting are quite relaxing, with a interactive setting and a interesting narrative. With good narration and multiple endings the game is quite intriguing, providing the player with a great story to follow.  There are different achievements related to the story, collectibles and hidden puzzles. None of the achievements feel out of place for this type of game, which adds great joy to the achievement hunter. As you must play through the game around 2 times for the different endings the completion for Scarf takes around 8 hours. For it's price, and the game itself, the length feels both fair and satisfying. Neither the game or the achievements are particularly difficult and most can be solved without the need for assistance. It is probably better that the game has easy and more laid-back achievements as it would probably ruin the experience otherwise. If you need assistance there is a guide available on Steam. There is no dlc available or required. The game's base price feels relatively fair, but if you could pick it up on a sale, even a minor one, it would definitely be a great game to play! While not being a neither lengthy or difficult game to complete, it still provides a enjoyable experience for achievement hunters to complete.
