_childDocuments_.review: This game is great. I love turn based games, roguelikes, variable team composition, reasonably challenging combat that doesn't hold your hand, and good replayability in my games and this has them all and does them very well.TL;DR-Very well thought out and balanced combat system.-Choices matter during fights, no one is holding your hand. But not always "Darkest Dungeon" levels of punishing.-Roguelike meta-progression after every playthough, regardless of how far you've made it. -Map broken up into "Zones" where player gets to choose their own path to the end goal. Every encounter is clearly shown on the map. Some zones have easy fights that give low level equipment, some have mini-bosses that give better equipment, some give permanent party buffs, etc. kind of like "Slay the Spire" but with less randomness involved. You know what you're choosing.-Build a party of 3. As you fight and win through different zones, you get up to a party of 5. I think maybe the 1st playthrough you get more of a random party, but all subsequent playthroughs you get to choose your starting 3 from the roster. Final 2 are given as a choice between a small handful of different characters from the roster, so more roguelike elements come into play here.-Find gear through fights or map exploration. Equip gear to party. Certain party members only like certain gear. YOU get to CHOOSE which gear you get from a selection of 3 generated gear types per fight/chest. You are not randomly awarded some junk that you will never use. Only exception being if your units already have better gear or are too low of level.-Party members have certain synergies with each other that can be unlocked per playthrough to boost both characters' abilities slightly or unlock better abilities. The character chooses which relationships to focus on, you don't get them all every run.-On a lighthearted note, characters have interesting personalities and observations of the world; they are not just bland warriors. Adds a special charm to the game that I find nice.-World atmosphere is nice. I like the artstyle and soundtrack. If you want to read my essay on why I like the game, continue on.Combat feel can be described as playing similarly to Final Fantasy games. Each unit has a select handful of abilities. Some are defensive, most are offensive. Enemies display their intent for their turns, so you can know when you should attack and when to turtle up. In most cases, damage cannot be 100% mitigated. Enemies are still going to hit you and sometimes they'll hit hard. You can't just faceroll through encounters without thinking through your moveset that turn. Enemies can have various attack type weaknesses or strengths that need to be played around. Attack types can be AoE or single target and single target attack types are broken up between Light, Normal, Heavy, or Flurry styles. All of them have their own benefits and uses. Units have individual speeds and so do enemies. Different attack styles have different speeds and damages.There is also an initiative system so you actually benefit from moving first, and suffer from moving after the enemy takes their action. So sometimes you'll be able to smash full power attacks at slow enemies and have an easy time, and others you'll almost be forced to do little light pokes and try to keep yourself alive the whole fight. Striking the enemy first can inflict "Stagger" to them, which pushes them back in the turn order. If enough powerful "Stagger" moves are stacked up, you can make a particular enemy skip their action until next turn if they have a troublesome ability coming up. There is a limit to this though, and some enemies are outright immune. Each character has their own specializations, and every character gets 3 gear slots that can be equipped with randomly generated gear that can be found as you play. Different gear has different traits that can supplement your build choices per run. You get to choose from a set of 3 gearset rewards when you find gear, and benefits are clearly listed. No random guessing and hoping you get lucky. Swords, Pistols, Rifles, Gauntlets, Gadgets, etc. Each unit can only use 3 gear types, and they tell you what they are. The meta-progression of it being a Roguelike comes into play here because the more you play, the more gear you can unlock to give your next playthrough more customization options. But these DO NOT make or break a run. You do not need to unlock tons of stuff before you can beat the game. You can win with zero unlocks, or you can lose with tons unlocked. Variable team comps fighting variable enemy comps with variable buffs to their abilities is what will make or break the run, and this is all on the player to decide which battles they want to take and how they can leverage their abilities to get through. The player has the option to pick most of their fights leading up to the boss battles. I believe it is designed very well.There *IS NOT* a system where you just earn overpowered gear and win the game. Gear unlocks give very marginal benefits to specific strengths of specific characters, and you still have to earn gear through fights during every playthrough. You do not spawn into a new run with decked out characters. You at best start with a piece of basic level 1 gear. It feels pretty Dungeons & Dragons-esque in gear design choice. No individual gear slot is going to have such amazing stats rolled that you just slap it on somebody and run with it. The buffs are very conservative and well balanced. Overall one of the most enjoyable games I've played. Over 400 hours and still having fun. Definitely worth the purchase. Even better if you can catch it during a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Renegades

_childDocuments_.review: Though far from perfect this game has its charms and I think plenty going for it.As far as roguelikes go it's on the long side; both per run and for reaching "the ending." At its core the game is an RPG and while each run is short for RPG standards, taking at a minimum 4ish hours, that can be quite long for a roguelike. There is a save and quit feature though so one could do a planet or even just a single in game day of activity, then call it a night and come back later easily enough. Granted I often had that "just one more battle" feeling with the game, not wanting to lose the momentum of my run and plans for leveling and gear.The combat has a fun stagger mechanic making each turn take a bit of strategy. Once you find a good one for your party or with your gear its simple enough to repeat that plan for most fights but often times the bosses will throw a wrench into your plans with resistances or other buffs. BUT at its basics... every attack takes a certain amount of time to execute - if you go before your target you crit - most attacks when you crit also stagger which pushes enemies further back in the timeline letting you crit with harder hitting slower characters - if you stagger them off the timeline completely you break them and they don't get a turn that round. The character roster has a good balance of tanks for defensive play, healers to buff and keep your party's shields up, heavy hitters to finish fights quickly, and characters with high stagger to keep your opponent from taking turns. Difficulty wise the game is variable. You start with an easy and normal mode, you beat normal and you unlock the next difficulty up. Easy is fairly easy, you can't go in mindless but you're more likely to win. Normal isn't too bad. Hard will require a bit more planning. And Extreme? I haven't had a win on Extreme yet and there's like 4 difficulties higher than it.The dialog has a goofy sort of charm to it, almost leaning a bit meme-y with lines like "That guard works for Warmonger Corp... you can tell by his confident stride and the sure way he handles his weapons that he's ready to start mongering some wars." It's all rather silly but I can't help but love it. Eventually you will start seeing lines repeat but the game has a setting in the options to turn off idle banter which will cut these lines out (and speed up runs). The game also has a relationship mechanic where every night you will have action cards that you can play from one character to another giving them temporary buffs and increasing their relationship. This mechanic often was the driving force for how I planned my party as it gave the characters shared buffs, combo attacks, and for certain characters would unlock their progeny - giving you access to either slightly remixed versions of the characters or a new character entirely.The pixel art is gorgeous, the music is pretty good, the character designs are interesting, and all in all I loved the mechanics from combat to gear to the party relationships. And the extra content added with the free dlc updates that have come since I bought the game? Makes it all even better.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Renegades

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent Turn-Based Roguelike game similar to Darkest Dungeon, but set in Space and without all the eldritch abominations and doom and gloom. Not to mention, it has a magnificent pixel art style.The combat is clearly inspired by JRPGs more so than American RPGs. Anyone familiar with titles like Final Fantasy and Grandia will recognize the Initiative Display, which lets you see enemy actions even before they act, and let you plan accordingly. It's a game about reactionary tactics, which makes the whole combat feel way more involved than simply "Hit you, Hit Me".That said, although its inspired by Japanese Turn Based Games, it lacks in something this genre usually has: story. The trailer and even the tutorial are quite misleading, leading you to think you're gonna experience a Space Epic through the eyes of the flagship character, the Valkyrie Wynn. This couldn't be further from the truth.The plot is absolutely silly and doesn't takes itself seriously after the Tutorial is finished. You're basically a band of mercenaries whose universe is under attack by a strange army of inter-dimensional invaders. To stop them, you have to prevent their army from destroying energy Cores located in different planets (which act as the game dungeons) by defeating bosses known as Behemoths. When your party falls, it's game over, and you have to start all over from the beginning, while being able to unlock more character classes, weapons and abilities that make you stronger each run. You do this by jumping into another dimension to try and stop the army there. Even though it sounds quite serious, it isn't. I haven't spent a single moment of the game without any dialogue being some sort of unfun meta commentary or cringey joke, but... that's OK, plot isn't what this whole game is about, it's strength is the gameplay department and it really delivers.If you're looking for a game that will let you play through flashy, action-packed turn based combats without having to worry about endless exposition dumps and 10 minute cutscenes, grab this. If you liked Darkest Dungeon, odds are you're also gonna enjoy this game. If you're looking for a serious story, look elswehere.

_childDocuments_.review: It's rogue-lite, what did you expect? It's not completely random, but it does have strategic depth. You do get more variety as the game goes on and you unlock things. There aren't leveling branches for individual characters, but you do get progeny from maxed 4 heart companions that are either new classes (there are 4) or variants of the base characters with slightly different abilities/level unlock orders. You also unlock character perks to select from with intel that can buff a character from the get go. It's okay to lose a game, you get resources and hopefully a progeny or two unlocked. I beat it on my third attempt with a team of Aegis, Marksman, and Saboteur. I later got Valkyrie and Empath to join my team as I beat the 1st and 2nd behemoths. Your team's composition is important, but not rigid. I do recommend starting with a tank, a staggerer, and someone that can shred armor. I'm on the final ship on my 4th playthrough on the new harder difficulty with an entirely different team of Juggernaut, Saboteur, Commando, Paragon, and Archon. It is a hard game, but not like others where you just abandon a run just because you started with bad items. In terms of presentation, I find the art style and the special effects pretty good and unique. The music and sounds fit, but I'll probably start playing while listening to something else. It's not bad, but it's not particularly amazing either. The writing makes sense enough for the rogue-lite nature of the gameplay. I found all of the characters so far to be quirky and endearing despite being obviously memey in nature. It does seem like overworld dialog on the planets is not unique to each character class unfortunately. A bit of a mistake there imo.  My only major complaints with the game so far, is that while the enemy variety is pretty good and the sub-bosses do change, the behemoths are the same every time at the end of each world. Hell, the 3rd one follows the same attack pattern every time it feels like. I am way more cautious of the sub-bosses than the behemoths now funnily enough. Another complaint I have is with fleeing sub-bosses. While do-able, my current team of Juggernaut, Commando, and Saboteur were pretty bad on the 1st world. All of the sub-bosses ran away from me on the 1st world because I couldn't kill them fast enough once they initiated their retreat. It was very frustrating, but didn't gimp me too hard I suppose. You can delay the retreat with a stun but they still try to run the next turn if you couldn't kill it. Major kudos on the final boss fight though. Mechanics of the fight literally made me :O So did the ending. :O I feel like there is a pretty satisfying game loop with this game.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: I'm now 40+ hours in. I would recommend only if you really enjoy these rogue-lite RPG games; it is most similar to Darkest Dungeon, but not as fun.The game length is 6-8 hours so you cant always finish in one sitting- this was my biggest annoyance. too long that you cant keep playing after failed attempt (like an FTL), and is not divided into short missions even if it is long (like a darkest dungeon).After learning the mechanics, the game is almost boringly easy; have 1 hero that breaks ("stuns") enemy, 1 hero to tank, 1 hero to deal bonus damage to that stunned enemy. its very basic core mechanic is too optimal and doesn't have much room for other team archetypes to shine based on the bosses you will face (they are always the same bosses).The developers have been updating this game very regularly post-release, so that is a very good sign. They need to reduce the number of worlds to 3 (shorten the run time), then have the extra worlds rotate randomly each run so you face different bosses/mobs each time, and have the extra random events not as extra maps but as extra fights.-----+ POSITIVES+ a lot of customization. equip different weapons, devices, armor on up to 5 different heroes, and you can level heroes up to level 10, each level unlocking skills or temporary buffs.+ replayability with different heroes, and if you increase their relationship from previous runs they create progeny heroes+ cool persistent lives of enemies and heroes. if you die to an enemy unit ending your run, the game promoted the enemy and you meet it next run. I've only beat it once, but cool to unlock heroes and their progeny (lol)+ tactics matter and you're heavily punished for incorrect plays. deciding order of attacks on timeline, inspecting enemy traits, weaknesses, strengths goes a long way, selecting the correct skills and targetting the correct enemies is important+ each hero has multiple skills that are useful in different situations. - NEGATIVES-UI is overcrowded. overlapping hero models made it harder to select heros, determine where enemy attacks were targetted, and it got worse later in the game with more heroes on your team and more enemies- no explanation of any statuses and effects of items, skills, units and what they do. they dont have a complete wiki for the game either - item shops could be improved. they give you 3 options. at least one of the items have throwaway stats (e.g. sword that goes on heavy attack hero, buffing light attacks). items are usually higher level than current hero levels, which makes you stockpile DNA (and delay levelling) until you find item chest so you can see the item you want to buy then level that hero. what should be enjoyable is sometimes annoying- camping system didn't feel fleshed out, camping cards give temporary buffs, but you also want to send cards to and from specific heroes to improve relationships. sometimes i felt just spamming cards to build the relationship instead of caring for which buffs they are; the only cards i really cared about targetting was healing cards-map movement was clunky, often get stuck on autopathing around map-30% of game is down time just wasted in night time walking around map to pick up randomly spawned DNA/coins, walking around a new behemoth map that has nothing to explore and just a straight path, navigating UI to check shop and check inventory then re-check shop. there's already camp mode for downtime, the fun dies down a lot between battles.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Renegades

_childDocuments_.review: Star Renegades is a Rogue-lite RPG with graphics based in pixels that focuses on team building and a very unique turn based combat system. You'll quickly find yourself immersed in the world and wanting more as your heroes level up, get to know one another and even have PROGENY! Will you survive this dimensional assault? Or will you be forced to hand off the torch to the next in a multiverse of stories and possibilities.You're started off as the Pilot Wynn who according to the introduction video seems to have some type of backstory with the forces assaulting your dimension. Together with her comrade Davion she quickly escapes the initial decimation of their forces and regroups with him in the prologue of the story. From here the game does a wonderful job of walking you through controls and combat in the initial (and subsequent) battles. Explaining the timing of attacks, the crit system and how you can even BREAK an opponent's turn.  The characters are witty and fleshed out. The system used to build friendships and relationships with your fellow adventurers is blended seamlessly with the story progression. You don't feel like you have to go out of your way to build them. Plus you get combat bonuses at the same time as you build your relations. Now while I personally didn't create any children of my own while playing (as of this writing) I did manage to get two characters to max relationship status which I assume will eventually allow me to do so. The music and the art of this game is wonderful. I'm brought back to the early era of gaming with simple tunes and old style pixel art with a modern twist on both. Which is nostalgic and refreshing at the same time. This acts as a perfect icing on top of the cake for a game that I was already excited to play as soon as I heard about it. In conclusion, Massive Damage, Inc. did a wonderful job in creating this masterpiece of a game. I played about 6hrs of it in my first sitting and only got mid-way through the second world (out of 4). With that much packed in already and the fact that it’s a rogue-lite with infinite universes/heroes/enemies to go through you can expect hours upon hours of fun gameplay. If you are an RPG fan and a fan of Rogue-lite's, I HIGHLY recommend picking up Star Renegades and sinking yourself into the experience of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Renegades

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually do reviews, but this game gave me a bunch of conflicting feelings: I am very pleased with the some strong aspects of the game, but at the same time I am very upset by the shortcomings.An interesting game concept, excellent graphics and visual style, pleasant music are clearly the strong side of the game, but the developers clearly violated the basic rule of game design: if you set the rules of the game and explain them to the player, you will have to adhere to them so that the player can plan his actions and the plans were not suddenly disrupted by any unaccounted surprises. I'm talking, of course, about a deterministic system of combat mechanics and about decision predicament system, which obviously does not work: during a one run (to be precise, even a singular planet) I constantly had situations when the characters do not complete a kill attack, when it was clearly predicted. At the same time, many enemies have a variety of out-of-phase attacks that are executed at random, which can and will kill your fighters, and this will constantly frustrate you. I think it would be easier to disable the battle prediction system entirely rather than pumping the player into the wrong expectations.The second serious problem is the frankly weak interface. The screen is overloaded with many unnecessary elements: I often cannot simply see the predicted effect of my attack in battle due to the abundance of windows, or even select the desired character. However, there's a lack of crucial information (such as the effects of elemental attacks, or during the camp it's really hard to see which relationships were built between two specific characters in previous runs). Many windows require text scrolling , despite the fact that there is a huge amount of free space on the screen, and managing character inventory with the mouse is a real game design nightmare. Like, I can't move a certain item to another slot, if this specific character cannot wear that item — what the hell? Who coded this? I don't know if it works on gamepad, but I this this particular kind of genre is mostly for desktop players, while the interface if obviously not.All in all:10 out of 10 graphics, music, setting and game mechanics idea0 out of 10 interface, implementation of game mechanics and an excess of bugs.Perhaps a 2.0 patch is needed that would fix the main problems of the game, but for now I’ll probably put the it on pause.Sorry for my English, I'm not a native speaker, though I thought my review could reach out more people this way.

_childDocuments_.review: I usually write a lengthy pros/cons list for reviews.  But I'll get straight to the biggest point, since I have not seen anyone mention this.  THE GAME IS FUNNY.  The dialog and one-liners are real funny.  A mix of satire, camp, and absurdity, all somewhat subtle.  While also still being serious and dramatic.  Anyway, yeah, as others have said, it's got Fire Emblem style relationships, turn-based JRPGs combat (unique in its own way, but has some of the timing elements of FFX and Radiant Historia), Middle-earth: Shadow series Nemesis style system, typical roguelike/lite dungeon pathing/rewards, etc.Ahh, what the hay, I'll still do pros/cons w/ what little I've played.  Pros - Great visuals, solid music, very funny.- You can actually become attached to characters.  - Combat requires attention and planning to optimize results.  But still simple enough to sort of cruise control through trash encounters.Cons- UI can be a bit...overwhelming or abstruse?  Some concepts and iconography may need extra reviews of the tutorials to fully grasp or understand. - A lot of the midway stops in your "dungeon" path don't give any rewards.  Perhaps they're there to just worldbuild w/ minor lore bits?- It may take some time to I've been excited for this game for over a year and it has not disappointed so far.  It's much more rogue-y than I expected, but nothing too offputting as of yet.  The combat, humor, and visuals are just top notch.  I'm really eager to get deeper into the progressoin and character building in this.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot of flaws, but at the core of it it's pretty fun and entertaining.  I'd give it a 6/10 - which is to say that it's worth playing but needs some work.  A healthy dose of polish (see Cons list) could easily bring it up to 8/10 or 9/10.Pros: * Combat system is great if you enjoy turn based combat * There's enough difference and variance to keep runs interesting * Soundtrack is chill * Enemies ranking up for killing you is a neat touchCons:  * Dialogue is old and stale super fast, there's only like a dozen lines or so that just repeat all the time  * Typos, misspelled words, and inconsistency with punctuation shouldn't be as present as they are  * Character personalities are pretty non-existent, even for intentional caricatures.  * Not all combos seem viable or useful (*I'm not an alpha gamer, this is just my opinion I'm sure there's ways to make everything work that I'm not seeing) What would make this 8 star or better?  * Fix typos, spelling, and grammar mistakes  * Add new dialogue for everyone  * Better writing  * New behemoths/planets

_childDocuments_.review: Between the sprite-based art style, the chiptune soundtrack, and the smooth but throw-back particle effects, this game is a joy, and that's before even delving past the splash screen. The combat is fluid, clear but complex; the various systems-- from camping and relationship building between characters to timing break-- interlock and work together to make a seamless, truly enjoyable experience. What drives you forward might not be the story (though the dialogue quips are often hilarious) but rather the sheer curiosity of what equipment, abilities, and enemy types you'll discover next. I'm only 4 hours in, but I'm already hooked.

_childDocuments_.review: Another game I'd like to give a positive review, but now that I've played a couple more runs, I sincerely can't. This game had a lot of potential, but there a lot of tiny (and not so tiny) things wrong.- It really needs more variety. There's only one boss for each planet, and the enemies are always the same. - The turn preview is wonky as f***. Half of the battle time is checking and re-checking wth is happening. And sometimes it doesn't even work. - If you speed up the battles, there's a good chance that the enemy will ignore some of your effects like staggers or guards, screwing you. - This is more subjective, but the dialogues are pretty bad. I guess they tried to go for a "Marvel" banter, but it's cringy and unnatural. Feels forced in a bad way. - Runs take way too long. First one took me 10 hours, the rest were around 8. Many of which were spent on battle trying to understand what was happening.There are positives; but not to the point to balance out the negatives. It's sad to see so much wasted potential.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best roguelikes I've played.I've never seen a better storytelling and humor in a roguelike.On top of that - there are a lot of innovative mechanics in the game - I LOVE IT!Developers even understood that watching animations for zillion hours is boring and included the "speed up" animations option - something that is missing in most of the games and makes them unplayable without speeding up the game by cheat engine and the likes.Finally - it seems like a game made by people who actually play roguelikes.The worst part I've seen so far is the character sheet UI. _childDocuments_.review: 1) An option to turn on world-save states (so that a wipe just resets your run to the beginning of the world) is necessary. In fact, make that the default and add an Ironman toggle to make squad wipes reset the run/campaign (e.g. bad guys win all universes and the save file gets bricked), and maybe a bronze man to perform the default behavior now when wiping. I'm no stranger to strategy games, and it took me 3 runs (18+ hours) to beat the final boss the first time. Each defeat also felt very unfair since a lot of the game is explicitly telling you what's happening, but, because a few things aren't clear, a single boss mechanic can wipe 4-8 hours down the drain and then it's back to the grind of borderline boring enemies to get back to the interesting boss part. 2) I haven't heard anyone else mention this yet, but there's a very large spike in difficulty at the second boss. It's so big, that I went from almost being bored on the regular enemies in the second world to full on wtfomgbbq when I faced Big Bertha. In fact, overall, I think the generic enemies are a bit too easy, at least with the starting team, until maybe the third world, and the second boss is too hard. The anti-stun mechanic is super punishing, and there no way to know what "Rabid" means, even after proc'ing it since she already does 2x actions on her turn.Overall great game, but the "pacing" of the difficulty could use some work, or maybe just make there be an "easy" mode too so people can see the story their first time through. Adding default save states and bronze/Ironman toggles would also be great additions along with achievements or some other reward to compel those of us who just love the challenge.

_childDocuments_.review: The launch trailer made me think this would be a different type of game but after getting over that bump and understanding the gameplay I've been pretty hooked. I dig the aesthetics that are referential and nostalgic but stand on their own and have good visual flavor. Story so far is pretty meh.How I'd describe the game... an RPG with rogue-lite elements and a battle system that takes some cues from Grandia and FF XIII/FFXV with a more strategic focus of managing health and shields and lite party management and leveling mechanics.

_childDocuments_.review: This kept showing up in my "players like you love:" but I hesitated a long time, because I saw several reviews saying, "If you liked Halcyon 6, you'll like this too."  I did not like Halcyon 6.  That game didn't grab me, it felt like less than the sum of its parts, it was trying to a bunch of things at once that just didn't gel into a fun experience.  Star Renegades, I'm pleasantly surprised to report, is fun, and everything in it works together towards a more focused experience.  And it you missed the tags somehow that experience is a turn based tactical combat roguelite.The combat is fun, there are a lot of things going on with different attacks and defenses, damage types and abilities.  All the characters have enough different abilities to make runs with different squads feel unique.  Combat is deterministic, and you have a number of crowd control tools at your disposal to stun opponents or push them so far back in the turn order that they lose their turn, which is a cool mechanic I haven't seen elsewhere.  The art direction is great, the anime/mecha/pixel theme works well in conveying the setting. The giant pixel robots and the deterministic combat where your goal is to stymie often more powerful opponents kind of reminds me of Into the Breach, which is not a bad thing.Overall, it's a good time, not amazing, but I wasn't expecting it to be as fun as it is  and actually hold my attention, (when I finally gave in and bought it in a sale haha)  I see some negative reviews from people who don't seem to get what a roguelike is.  You will very probably lose the game a lot, and you can't save and then go back and retry a fight, so if that's not something you'd enjoy, this is probably not the game for you.  And if you're like me and you are on the fence because you didn't like Halcyon 6, well, I think SR is a better game and is worth a try.

_childDocuments_.review: It's alright, but nothing special. The artwork and animations are great—minus some of the portraits, like the main character with her mouth open. The music gets tiresome pretty quick; it's like a droning hum that you tune out, instead of having moments that get you pumped, or establish the atmosphere.The writing sucks. The attempts at humor aren't funny. The worldbuilding is poor, with little payoff for the lore. You're told about elements of the world and story, without ever actually encountering or interacting with those elements of the world. You just end up not caring about any of it because it has no bearing on anything. The character interactions are shallow, none of the characters are interesting, and they don't do anything interesting to each other. These may seem like unimportant points, but the characters talk a lot, and the description on the store page says "forge bonds between heroes". It's hard to care about any of these characters. Plus, there are errors in basic English grammar, showing a lack of attention to this aspect of the game, and a lack of writing experience by whoever wrote the dialogue. Among these careless mistakes are using the plural form of a word when they meant to use the possessive form (eg. “my friends name is John"), and capitalizing a word that isn’t a proper noun, after a comma (eg. "hey what’s up, My name is John").The overworlds aren’t interesting. You’re never rewarded for exploring or looking around, you just have to click the visibly relevant parts, so 90% of the empty space is pointless. When night rolls around, some nearly-insignificant amounts of currency will spawn on the overworld. You can backtrack to pick these up. There’s nothing fun or interesting about that. There are also some lore points and NPC dialogue to read, but, as mentioned, these are poorly executed. I don’t care about the agricultural techniques of the Zugwops of the Blorglorpulon sector if you’re never going to make them relevant to the game or story.The selling point is the gameplay, which is alright, but it lacks the depth of the games from which it draws inspiration (games like Slay the Spire and Darkest Dungeon). You aren't making that many interesting decisions, and some characters (like the archon robot that does AoE and can shield allies) seem to have such lackluster abilities that you want to just skip some of their turns so that they don't trigger small turn delays on enemies instead of big ones. There don't seem to be terribly many interesting abilities, just different amounts of damage and turn delay. The status effects I've seen that you can inflict (like armor corrosion and tiny DoT effects) have been nearly insignificant. A lot of enemies also just do generic damage. That's their threat—they're going to do damage to you. There are usually more interesting enemy interactions going on in games like these, like enemies buffing each other, or charging up for a big attack, or stunning, or disrupting you in other ways.The game tells you that delaying enemy turns is powerful, and it is... but only near the end of an enemy's life. Delaying an enemy's turn only really matters when you deny them a turn and then kill them before they act, otherwise they just do that same attack at a later time, where it'll do more damage and other effects by critting you! Crits happen when the attacker hits the defender before the defender acts. If you use a low-damage attack that delays an enemy's turn enough to make them lose an action this turn, that enemy will likely act before any of your characters on the following turn, critting someone. You have to delay their turn enough that you can actually act before them on the following turn, and make sure that your actions on the following turn will kill them. The turn delay stuff ends up not mattering a decent bit of the time, because some enemies have enough HP that you just have to do raw damage to them until denying them actions matters (ie when they're near death). This makes delaying boss turns not terribly impactful, since they live so long. Delaying boss attacks enough that you get crits you otherwise wouldn't is useful, but if you're not careful, the boss will just act before you on the following turn and crit you unavoidably, while preventing all of your characters from critting.Despite being billed as a deterministic game, the enemy intents are nowhere near as clear as they are in Slay the Spire. There are too many examples of this to list, but one is the first Behemoth boss’s AoE attack, Bullet Hell. The attack preview told me that the attack was targeting all my units for 284 damage. All of them were going to die from this attack (2/3 of my units didn’t even have this much max HP+shields!), and the preview predicted the death of my entire party. Once the attack came, the 284 damage was split between my three units, and none of them died. Why does the preview trick you into thinking everyone is going to take 284 damage? And if this is a deterministic game, why have a random attack, instead of splitting the damage predictably?The UI can be confusing, too. The game doesn’t tell you which unit is going to act first when two units are acting at the same point in the timeline. Attack order matters a lot for things like crits (am I critting the enemy, or are they critting me?) and maximizing the amount by which you delay enemy turns (is my big delay attack going to hit first, or my small delay attack? The small delay attack can hit first and trigger the enemy's immunity to further turn delay, wasting the big delay attack).The equipment choices that I’ve seen, even at epic chests, aren’t very interesting. The effects tended to be minor and not gameplay-altering. The same goes for the Darkest Dungeon-inspired camp buffs. Besides the heals (which seem to be the only way to restore health) their combat effects were not very impactful. -25% corrosive damage taken for the next 2 fights? What even does that kind of damage? Am I going to encounter that kind of damage in the next 2 fights? Is -25% really going to make that big of a difference when the enemy doesn’t even do that type of damage every turn?

_childDocuments_.review: After spending about 22 hours on this game I've decided to uninstall it and never play it again, in addition I'm giving it a negative review because of one enemy in this game that can put you into a loop where you cannot do any damage to it. This enemy is the Demolisher. I've fought this enemy about 5 times. My latest run I was pretty loaded with equipment having 4 legendaries as well as some epic and rare gear. I get wiped by this enemy every time. It's no fun to have 5 hours of progress wiped because of an enemy that has pretty ♥♥♥♥♥♥ mechanics in my mind. Here's how all my encounters have gone with this enemy:Round 1 - Demolisher summons bombs and then proceeds to protect them which initiates a retaliation if you attack them. Furthermore if you don't have a character that can attack the back row there's no way to lay damage to Demolisher unless you want to get pounded into the ground for attacking the bombs to get to her.Round 2: You can now attack the bombs but I never have enough attacks to knock them into the next round and even if you could Demolisher is still on the back row and you're unable to attack her. Oh and the bombs are now active and can detonate doing heavy damage. In addition the bombs act too early on the timeline for you to be able to push them back. So you're eating the damage.Round 3: All the bombs are gone and you can now attack Demolisher problem is she acts too early on the timeline for you to be able to crit and therefore you're unable to activate any of your crit abilities that usually have armor damage modifiers. You need to damage about 150 points worth of shields and around 52 armor before you can damage health. I had two characters that were built for armor piercing but it doesn't matter when you can activate your crit abilities. Rinse and repeat. Every time I've fought this enemy I get stuck in this loop. I can't damage her and I just get ground down until I die losing all the progress. I hate to give a bad review because I love rogue type games and have a library full of them but when you encounter enemies like this early in your play through they're just run enders and it's wasted time and not fun. Just wish I knew this before dropping $30 on this game.

_childDocuments_.review: ✔ exceptionally good turn based combat, with a lot of focus on turn order and controlling enemies in such a way to not let them act as much as possible✔ runs start with 3 characters and you build the squad up to 5✔ combat is almost completely deterministic and you are even told what the enemy is planning to do. Unfortunately there are a few attacks, which target random enemies. No idea why these exist, but they are rare, so it's not a big issue✔ there are healers... but you don't need them! it seems viable to run with a team without any sustain capability (at least on lower difficulty levels)✔ on top of that losing a character or two doesn't have to mean a wipe. There is no mid-combat resurrection, but if you know what you are doing and how to beat the enemy then losing crucial party members in the middle of a long boss fight isn't necessarily the end✔ life/armor/energy shield as three defensive stats, with interesting mechanics❔ a lot of difficulty levels, but they unlock one after another and you have to start from normal (I beat the game on normal and harsh, with no failed runs)❔ 6+ hour runs❔ some stats persist between combat encounters, which is fine, except for the Fury meter, which is generated on attacks/kills and allows you to use special attacks (ultimates, kind of). The difference between having a full or empty Fury meter at the beginning of combat is too big❔ story is very bare-bones, but that's not the focus here✘ extremely slow perma progression when it comes to progenies (different version of playable characters, allowing for more squad customization) and item unlocks✘ as mentioned the game shows you what damage your team is going to take and how much damage you will do with your skills. Unfortunately, in many cases it simply lies. It doesn't update when a character taunts, which is easy to remember. But there were damage dealing abilities, both from my side and enemy side that did far more (or far less) than the UI forecasted✘ gets repetitive. At least for me it's repetitive enough that I don't want to make more full runs with slightly different squad composition just to get to the true ending

_childDocuments_.review: The game has a surprisingly well-balanced mechanics which most of turn-based tactics fails. The system has its ways to avoid cheesing enemies such as stagger limit and resistances as well as undelayable attacks from the enemies. Soundtrack in this game did not fail to deliver. The rougelike element can hit or miss for other players but I enjoyed planning on how to get all the vital resources in the limited turns that the game offers you.as a turn-based tactics game however, it limits the creativity of the players on how to approach the game. Most of the time, the team composition would have a delayer, damage dealer, and a tank. with this comp, you can defeat the game easily multiple times. Team composition will also be primarily dictated by your 3 choices at the start since the other 2 recruitables are heavily impacted by RNG. Equipment, devices and implants are just boosts in characters and are often used as stat sticks as there are no equipment in the game that changes the play style of a particular character. The game also suffers from lack of enemy variety and redundancy of enemy design. Often, enemies have a repetitive move sets. primary damage, AOE, counters, and regens. There are no enemies that surprised me with their mechanics and for this reason, I was severely underwhelmed by the difficulty of the game (I have beaten the game 3 times and currently on my Entropy 1 Difficulty playthrough). The game offers different approach with the unlockable characters as well as variety when you unlock the progeny. However, the difference between each character's play styles are lacking, making the whole process of unlocking the characters underwhelming and tedious. Overall, I had fun with the game. It is your typical turn-based rougelike with a pseudo-nemesis system and I look forward to the further games that will be procured by the devs. TL;DR:Experience in the game: 5 runs, 3 completes, currently on my Entropy 1 difficulty (5th difficulty) playthrough Pros-Good battle system, avoids cheesy gameplay-variety of characters is abundant, can entertain different compositions-Good soundtrack-Limited time through planets gives extra challenge for playersCons-Lack of enemy variety/ Enemies often does not have unique mechanics-Difficulty of game is underwhelming and can be finished by using an almost dysfunctional team-Rougelike elements often offers stat buff and does not encourage players to change playstyles-Final Team Composition is heavily influenced by RNG-Difficulty increase is offered, but fail to make the game difficult in itself (usually a % increase in enemies' stats)7/10 good gaem

_childDocuments_.review: Really am having a lot of fun with this game so far and one hundred percent recommend it to anyone who enjoys games like The Darkest Dungeon or Slay the Spire.Gameplay: Combat is a turn based system on a psuedo timescale, with different actions placing characters in different positions on the timescale. Your and your enemies actions get a guaranteed crit if they hit a character that hasn't attacked yet. Throw in a diverse enough enemy pool each with their own ability pool and each turn feels like a puzzle and you wont be just making the same turn over and over again. It's honestly one of the best turn based combat systems I've seen that doesn't use cards to force RNG making your turns not repetitive. My biggest complaint is that a single run takes me on average about 3 hours, and a lot of that time is spent watching animations I've seen hundreds of times by this point. There's a speed up combat option but it has this terrible fast-forward animation it places over everything which is not what I want. I just want the animations to go faster.Graphics: The game has a pixel style and it's done really well. The overworlds are decent enough if a little boring and static. The in-combat stages are absolutely beautiful though and the devs did a great job making a 2.5D battle field. Combat animations are also big and varied and flashy. Character Design: It's okay. Most of the characters have a fairly generic look to them, and the enemies aren't all that inspired either. Bosses likewise are also pretty boring save for one that I really really like. Writing: This is easily the weakest part of the game. All of the characters I've seen so far, not having unlocked all of them, are basically just one note quirks. Enemies are basically just a list of phrases without any personality. This is fine to a degree as the fun of this genre of game mostly comes from the gameplay loop, however the devs made the decision to make the characters have personal moments with each other and to make comments on enemies and the environment while on the overmap. So they put in the effort to create systems where their characters can have personality, and then failed to deliver on the premise. It's too bad because the core systems they implemented are pretty good, the writing just doesn't live up to it.Music: It's not bad or annoying, but neither is it memorable in any way. Having played this game for 36 hours at time of writing I honestly cannot remember a single song or note or tune at time of writing. That's not a good thing, but it's also not bad. Sound Effects: These are pretty decent, enemies and allies attacks are all varied and have different sounds you'd associate to their actions and it mostly lives up to it. Final Thoughts: The core gameplay of this game is great. The devs did an amazing job of looking at the systems of the turn based rogue-lite genre and implementing one of the best versions of it I've seen yet. I highly recommend it to anyone who enjoys these types of games as it's a very solid experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't a big fan of Halcyon 6 (their previous game) even though it was certainly serviceable but I do really enjoy this one.  The combat is pretty engaging, there's an interesting camp mechanic that allows your party to use cards and gain relationships with each other that unlocks passive buffs and combos.  The timing system in the combat is well done and there's interesting interactions and considerations to take on what skill to use when.  There's also a mini-nemesis system for enemies like in Shadow of Mordor, though generally only one or two will get promoted a game and it doesn't end up playing a huge role in each playthrough.  Still adds a little welcome flavor though and makes you consider what route to take through each level a bit more.I'm not sure why people are saying it's too easy, I didn't find the difficulty to be exceedingly easy and I play a lot of challenging strategy games and original style rogue-likes.

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels a bit misleading.  You are not about to jump into a game full of tactical and strategic depth.  Instead, you'll be playing a game with beautiful pixel art, somewhat repetitive combat, minimal story, with some rpg elements.It's good, but it isn't quite what the Beta or even the trailer makes you think you'll be playing.The story isn't particularly strong or engaging, which is disappointing considering it has a very good premise.  There's a group of marauders answering to "Mother" that are dominating reality after reality.  You take the role of a group of characters that face this threat in any given reality.  When you die, your robot companion jumps to a new reality to try again.  This solves the problem of carrying over any progress for your characters, but it removes any meaningful attachment to the characters.  The ending reveal is fantastically disappointing.Gameplay consists of moving around on 3 worlds and 1 space ship, where you'll breach into zones and attack or loot.  At first combat seems pretty in depth, but it rapidly devolves into a Stagger->Attack->Stun->Attack->Attack-Shield type of mechanic.  And that's pretty much every battle.  You want to keep your shields up and prevent as much damage to yourself as possible, as shields will regenerate at the end of every battle but health will not.  You'll need 3 breaches before you can camp for the night and use cards to heal yourself.  This is also where you'll build your friendship level that builds some combo attacks and other bonuses with your characters.You find new weapons on the battlefield, or buy them after liberating a planet.  I found this to be somewhat disappointing, as the weapons and gear I found/bought didn't often make the same jump in improvement as I'd expect considering my level gains.Music, art, and the sound are all quite exceptional.  There's a lot of detail in the game, and a lot of love obviously poured into it.Overall it's a fun game, and I've enjoyed it.  Don't go in expecting deep combat, story, or rpg elements and you'll have a good time.

_childDocuments_.review: A great roguelike, I love the story and the in universe reason for more runs, and the gameplay is solid. As it is I'd give it a 8-9/10.Only notes are that some QOL and balance changes could make this game a 10/10, and the devs' roadmap says that's high on their priority list.

name: UnderMine
detailed_description: Delve deep into the UnderMine and discover its secrets, one peasant at a time! UnderMine is an action-adventure roguelike that blends combat and dungeon crawling with rpg-like progression. Mine gold, die, upgrade yourself, and try again! Discover hundreds of items including relics, potions, blessings, and curses that all combo and stack for a new experience every run. Challenge dangerous bosses and rescue helpful characters that provide new upgrades for your adventure. Decipher the cryptic messages of the Undermine’s residents and unfold the mystery at the heart of the dungeon. Discover relics, potions, prayers, blessings, and even curses to forge that perfect run. Watch as items pop off and combo with one another to make a god peasant of destruction. Discover friendly (and some unfriendly) characters in need of rescue. After returning them safe to the mine's hub they will offer powerful upgrades that can be used from run to run. Explore every nook and cranny to discover hundreds of secrets. New relics, potions, characters, and story bits lay behind the statues, rocks, and walls of each floor. Each area of the UnderMine contains one (or more!) deadly boss that will test planning, patience, strategy, and skill. Prepare well, because a test awaits! Wickedly Lighthearted UnderMine has a rich world to explore and discover with charming characters and a plot full of intrigue. Experience the plight of the poor Delvemore peasants. Told to brave extreme danger for a boss that doesn't quite care about them or their safety. A pretty funny situation when you think about it and something we can all relate to. _childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game for all the content up until the actual end of the game. Everything right before the end is some of the best roguelite on the market. Incredibly addicting, smooth as butter game play, gear combo's that will make you feel like you're more of a boss monster than the boss's. I absolutely do not consider this a spoiler because it's not story related, but your reward if you do manage to finish a run through the mines is to keep all your gold without losing any but every single time you're also forced to pick up a shard that makes the dungeon something like 2% harder. There's a reason that one of the least unlocked achievements in the game is 32 complete finished runs. I hate this feature, I feel as though I'm punished for playing well. I look at roguelites such as Hades or Enter the Gungeon and I see infinite replay ability. I got to the end of this and I felt like I had no reason to keep going. _childDocuments_.review: Flashes of greatness that are dimmed by a stubborn and unfriendly design. It's as though the designers thought over all the ways it could be made worse, and decided to adopt them. Here's a sample.- When you mine gold, little bastards spawn and start stealing it, forcing you to zip around collecting it all before they do. It's not a huge hassle, but just give me a loot magnet and let me move on to the next room. There's nothing fun about this. Why did it have to be EVERY room?- You can bank an item at a special room that comes up occasionally, for use in a future run. Great idea! except... you have to swap an item out to get anything from it. Kind of defeats the purpose, especially if you find it before you have anything you'd like to give up.- Taking a boon as you progress also curses you. Some curses are run-enders, like 'lose max health every time you defeat an enemy' or 'lose an item each time' for the same cause. While some curses are minor, many are hugely problematic and just sap the fun from the game. You can't know what they'll be. You just basically end up avoiding most of the curse choices because the results just aren't worth it. There are even mega-weapons and mega-curses, but they're so likely to end your run that they aren't worth the hassle.- Speaking of curses, they can be removed but the availability of the item that does so varies wildly. You might see zero in a run, or five in a single floor - and no, you can't take them with you - curse needs to be on you already. There's no guarantee you'll be able to ditch a curse before a boss, for instance.- This stuff touches on a bigger problem in the game, and that's the RNG design choices. You will frequently get a level where doors can't be opened, because you've received no keys. Chests can't be looted, 'cause you've been given no bomb drops. Later this is able to be influenced somewhat but pre-purchasing items that the dungeon might need just feels bad. You can't bail from a run back to the hub area, so you WILL lose any such items unspent. Experts will say it's just that you don't know which random rock to bomb to get a key; but that's far too ambiguous to be enjoyable.- Recipes for cool things are sometimes found and crafted - and you can use them the first time only. After that, you have to find them in a run. Additionally these things get added to the pool of drops, making specific things actually harder to get the more you progress.- You can't actually pick any specific boons or items to start the run.- Semi-rare shops with ability to trade items for other items are usually vastly overpriced and not worth it. - Healing picks up even if you're full on health - turning this off is a menu option that needs toggling. In nearly all circumstances you'd rather leave it untakeable if on full health.Overall, it seems the game makes too many things unavailable as a way to prevent singlar 'best ways' or cheese strats. But that's half of the fun of a roguelike. As such every run is left up to chance and you don't control much of the build.Most roguelikes unlock new weapons and abilities and give you at least -some- choice in which of these you use each run. See, Rogue Legacy, Hades, etc. But this game wastes some cool ideas by making it too difficult to enjoy the systems behind an otherwise good core gameplay loop.

_childDocuments_.review: Where do I begin? This game is splendid in so many ways I've already dumped so much time into it and it's still hard to believe its in Early Access. If you're not a fan of Binding of Isaac/Zelda you probably won't be into this game, period.PROS:Personally, the game feels fresh each run, albeit the combat is incredibly simple with that Zelda/Binding of Isaac fighting feel the game implements things like curses and relics that is similar to Binding of Isaac that makes the game fun each run. The story albeit incredibly simple is actually pretty funny and interesting, the game offers challenges through the Othermine, more shop unlocks, and difficult achievements to pursue to keep you engaged once you clear the game.The enemy variety is surprisingly pretty good; I found myself surprised with them not being incredibly repetitive in terms of just boosting stats on a same enemy type and actually finding ways of making some enemies a complete cluster ♥♥♥♥ in a good way (Like the troll bombers and their variants)The art style, the music ambiance, the bosses and their unique fighting styles, as well as goofy constant references to pop culture and other games really add to the games enjoyment. No major bugs aside from some surprisingly FPS drops when one specific enemy does an attack but it's rare to encounter and I usually kill them pretty fast enough (It's the mannequins that connect a lightning line between them) CONS:If you can even call it a con, I would have to say is the amount of content, but you need to take into account the fact that it's Early Access, and you can still spend tons of time on it and the devs are incredibly dedicated to the game and releasing new content that's not only free but also well done in my honest opinion.Rating AKA TL;DR: Personally I love the ♥♥♥♥ out of this game, and for the price it's definitely worth it. I'd give it a 10/10. This game is an exemplary example for how Devs should approach a game with accordance to what the players want. Cheers guys and thanks for the fun.

_childDocuments_.review: I will give this a thumbs up with a big BUT. Undermine is a fun rogue-lite with cute pixel-art graphics and a satisfying meta-progression where you permanently upgrade your character and hub base. At least for the first 10-15 hours. The game gets pretty grindy later when enemies deal out massive amounts of damage and also take dozens of hits before dying so that you have to upgrade your equipment to stand a chance. And upgrading equipment gets expensive ... very expensive. Later stages also feel overwhelming with how many enemies and traps there can be in cramped places. Sometimes there is hardly any room to properly react and you can get caught up in chain reactions that are out of your control.It doesn't help that the risk/reward mechanics in this game feel very unrewarding. 90% of any risk you take will be bad for you. The positive effects rarely seem worth the potential negatives. Or you will just straight out lose copious amounts of gold and health whenever engaging in one of the slot machines like the mechanics of the game. Which ultimately led me to just not engage in any risk/reward stuff and just go with what I get guaranteed. Another problem is that you can't really create awesome builds in this game. The temporary upgrades and potions you get feel like they hardly make a difference. Sure, some upgrades are really good, but the chances to get them in a run are small and most of the time you will clear rooms with a cumbersome mix of jumping around and throwing and swinging your axe, trying to not get hit. And yeah, those jumping mechanics suck. Instead of just having a button to dodge enemy attacks like in other rouge-likes you have to awkwardly jump around with your character often leading to landing in traps or chasms.Still, I enjoy playing this for "just another" run to get more gold, to work towards the next upgrading hoping to finally clear the next floor. It helps that runs can be quick and that there are shortcuts and unlocks to quickly get where you left.

_childDocuments_.review: An action-adventure roguelike with a bit of RPG tossed in. Adventure deep into the UnderMine and discover powerful relics, deadly enemies, hidden secrets, and a few friends to help along the way. You begin the game as a “peasant” with their adorable bird companion. You must figure out the cause for the terrible tremors going on and peruse the mines to find the root of the problem. During your journey, you meet various monsters and thieves along with some traps along the way. The game’s replay value and art style are its true winners here. As you die in the game, you must restart from the beginning which can be a pain for most. Undermine has found a way to overcome this pain by changing the map each time you die taking away the boredom that can come from repeating the same levels. As for the graphics and art, the overall graphics of the game are well-done and even goes into great detail with reflections and movements of the environment. While this game has great replay value, art and difficulty level, it did leave gamers clueless in some regards to gameplay. Receiving special items were great and the skills along with them but it took some figuring out on my own on how to use them.  There is definitely opportunity to have a guide or other ways to help out us fellow peasants.

_childDocuments_.review: Id like to support indy devs. The game seems mostly polished. The almost 2 hours of play time I have is go down, do a 15 minute run, save up enough for 2 upgrades at first then later just one upgrade per run. It feels like the damage and the prices are scaled back to impede  progress so the play time is longer but I feel like that hurts the game. Yes its a roguelite so that mechanics is expected. Its different when it feels like thats all the game has to increase playtime. No I haven't defeated the second boss but I have come close. I dont want to spend 15 minutes getting cursed or falling into a pit because I was close to the edge and a spider bumped me into it to lose 1/4 of my health or accidentally walk onto a fire that takes off 1/5 of my health over time.  Theres a landmine trap that I cant see until I run it over and by then its almost to late to not take damage, chipping away at the remains of my health. Food is scarce so far. If I find anything it heals for 20 health which is less then most creatures do in a single hit.Its just not a satisfying gameplay loop.Edit - I tried to give it another shot. While the graphics are nice and the controls are pretty fluid, there are some gameplay hangups.After getting the upgrade to increase how much health is healed with food, the cheaper food items in the shop end up healing more per gold.An hour long run nets about 25,000 gold but eventually thats only enough for 1 or 2 upgrades per run. Relics are locked away behind a locked door that require a key to unlock. Your not always guaranteed a key every floor. Relics are a way of gaining extra perks each run to increase peasant efficiency. Thus if the game locks them away and doesn't provide you the means to get a key for that floor, your taking a hit to your upgrade potential.  Some relics increase damage but neglect to mention the damage counter is reset when you g et hit.Food can be cooked to increase how much it heals but in the majority of my runs, I only been able to cook a few pieces of food because a source of fire is not always near the drop.

_childDocuments_.review: I have had lots of fun playing undermine and enjoyed the secrets that fill this game. Unless you want to just look up how to get things just remember this. Keep an eye out. There are few secrets that don't have a tell, and everything exists for a reason. If you cant figure out how to unlock something you found before, try re visiting it, you may have already picked up the"key".Another pro to this game is how even if you find yourself unable to skill past something, you can buy stats to assist you with it. some however may see this as a downside, but if you want to play without the stat upgrades you are more than welcome to, and it provides an excellent challenge.The early access on this title for me only means its going to get more content which as I already got more than enough enjoyment for my time makes me incredibly exited.Some things I dont like about this game is how bosses scale with each run clear. Every time you clear the bosses they stay dead until you clear the final boss as well.  Every time you full clear the bosses are reborn with higher stats. Things I would love to see in the future releses are: some sort of coop with either full other pesants, or the pets.multiple boss forms that unlock with rebirth levelUpgraded normal enemies that get more common with higher rebirth level (like the multi shot flys)Secret floorsSecret bossesMod support (always adds to game life)More creative items+petsEven without these I love the game so much and love to see what the developers do to improve the game.
_childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

_childDocuments_.review: The game definitelly isn't bad or anything. It's biggest flaws, as I see them, is a lack of originality, identity and content.It's very much like Binding of Isaac overall: each level is a set of random rooms with enemies that you have to clear to leave the room, shops, chests, keys, bombs and secrets identical to Isaac - blow a bomb near a wall to find secret room, blow a boulder to find random pickup or secret stairwell. Also there are treasure rooms - they contain random item that makes character stronger.  Also UnderMine has character progression system, similar to both Rogue Legacy (after death, a percentage of your found gold can be spent on improving your stats permanently) and Dead Cells (pay unique currentcy to unlock weapons and items, they will be added to game's pool). Rogue Legacy also has similar system of blessings and curses.Copying games as awesome as these isn't a bad thing, but somehow UnderMine manages to copy too much, and at the same time, not enough to be as fun. Unlike Dead Cells, weapons slightly differ in dmg and reach, rarely being impactfull. There's only two types of attack - melee and range, no combos, no special attacks. Basically each battle is you clicking enemies away and sometimes jumping to avoid attacks. There are items that increase damage, attack speed and reach, but combat becomes too repetative fast.Unlike Rogue Legacy, there are no character randomization and classes - you always play the same character with same abilities. You can change familiars at the hub, but they have very little effect on the gameplay. Blessings in Rogue Legacy are much more impactful - almost all blessings in UnderMine are just boring stats increases. Also progression is much more simple than in Roughe Legacy and it only takes few successful runs to buy out all the good stuff. Unlike Isaac, there are considerably fewer items and almost no items that would change the gameplay dramatically. Also there are very few bosses, and each one is kind of easy to learn.Finally, there's plot, but I can't decide wether they take it seriously or not. It kind of feels like the whole story happens in comedic setup, but during final boss battle, the game tries to act serious, but fails, because there's no characters that you'd want to sympathise with.
_childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

_childDocuments_.review: Not a bad game, but one I would pick up on a sale.  As others have said in their reviews, other roguelike games have done it better before and after this one.  The game has its charm and getting a broken build going is just stupid fun.  My main complaint about the game is combat.  While it is workable, there are moments where it isn't fun.  For example, you pick up a great perk to ricochet your thrown weapon to other enemies only to find out in later levels that some enemies can instantly retaliate from halfway across the map.  It also can just be too busy making it difficult to avoid significant amounts of damage.

_childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

_childDocuments_.review: I am on my second playthrough and enjoying just as much! Basically... you're a miner sent by a mysterious wizard to find out why there is a disturbance in the mine. That's a summary of the story without spoilers. It plays like The Binding of Isaac with randomized rooms and loot each time you venture into the mine (the rogue-like part), only the game is more forgiving and cute than TBOS. You collect gold that you can upgrade your stats for the next life and prep enough to kill all the bosses. The game is great because of how varied each run of the mine is. You might get really unlucky and have badly designed room with a lot traps and tough enemies or very fortunate with many perks and chests in one floor. These perks are called "relics" and have varied effects that can work together with others to change your playstyle. Like they might buff bomb damage or change how your pickaxe swings or throws. In order to access relic rooms, you need to balance your keys and bombs. Usually, shop, relic rooms, or secrets rooms are blocked or locked. Another layer to the experience is the curses and blessings. You'll eventually unlock shrine rooms that give you an option to pray and acquire a blessing at the cost gaining a curse. The blessing usually increases a base stat or amount of gold gained. The curses mirror them and you can even gain a curse the negates the blessing you just got, but later on you can find or buy potions that remove curses. Or the next shrine you can pray to remove an existing curse at the cost of life. There are little things you'll learn along the way. Like if fire touches food, it will cook and heal for more. And there are some rooms to appear empty but actually, there's some puzzle to solve that will reveal a chest. Hints like those you can google but part of the fun is learning I think... So the game becomes a balancing act of gathering keys and bombs to unlock bonus rooms and then blessings and removing enough curses... and yeah once you buy every upgrade from the hub shop NPCs, it's just a matter of having a lucky run that will give you the right amount of damage (swing or throw) with the right relics to defeat the final boss. There's a kind of endless challenge mode after completing the boss that provides some post game continuation. Ehhh but personally I enjoyed the grind of the main game more.For length, if you're decent at these type of games - it would take 20-40 hours I'd say to get all the upgrades and achievements. I am terrible but still had a blast. It's pretty exhilarating when you have a good run and bring have over 100,000 gold
_childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

_childDocuments_.review: I received a copy of this game for free before it was released as an early-access title.UnderMine is really enjoyable. The artwork and the soundtrack are excellent. Combat is tight--my weapons go exactly where I want them, hitboxes are fair for enemy attacks and projectiles, and because of my own sloppiness while playing I know exactly why it was that I fell into that ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ pit, again, for the third time in a row. There are enough unlocks in the game for players to make incremental progress, even if they are stuck on a certain boss. It's a pick-up-and-play game that potentially has the depth and strategy of games like Binding of Isaac or Dead Cells. And it's humorous the entire way through. I've already suggested it to friends.The game is, however, in early access. The developers actively communicate with their player base via patch notes and blogs here on Steam, on Twitter, and in their Discord server. Community-reported bugs and suggestions are actively being fixed and implemented. Two examples of this are an almost immediate accuracy fix for keyboard and mouse users playing at non-standard resolutions, and the implementation of graphical changes to aid players with color-blindness issues. I find this type of responsiveness on behalf of the devs to be promising.Story progression in the game could use a bit more cohesion. There's still some fine tuning needed to balance out the effect of all of the various items in the game. There is also a ton of room for additional content-- more dungeons, more items. But I think this one is a real keeper, and I expect to see it being a staple for speed-running in particular sometime in the near future.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, but oh my goodness, the bosses in this game are as hard as a Dark Souls game. The first boss took me an hour to defeat, the second boss, lets just say, right now, it's impossible to beat. I love this game and all rogue games, but this one, is as unfair as you can possibly imagine. If you who are reading this, are considering in buying this game, just prepare yourself mentally that you're going to DIE ALOT. _childDocuments_.review: At first, this game seems like a masterpiece. Plays like binding of issac, and is very polished. It has a lot of problems. First, it is way shorter than binding of issac, I could beat it in 5 hours if it were more fair. There isn't much to see, even though it is procedural, the rooms all feel similar, enemies attack patterns are repetitive, and there is only one unique boss for each dungeon. The leveling up system is fine tuned to make the you advance at the rate of molasses.I beat it after 19 hours, not because I am skilled or the game was reasonable, but because of luck, otherwise I might have had to spend another 10 hours upgrading. By luck, I mean you rely on the spin of the die, get an exploitable item, and use smartly to power up enough to face the final boss. I categorize this as a chuk e. cheese game because you know it is rigged and your strategy is to look for an exploit that the designers overlooked.

_childDocuments_.review: The basic mechanics appear to be all there, but you might find you run out of levels quickly at this stage of development.  The run-based gameplay is actually a benefit to this title in its current state because you're meant to play through the levels several times anyway, and the procedural generation can throw you some curve balls to keep you challenged.  You're a peasant and you're working in a goldmine.  Go deep, get gold, die on the clock.  Equipped with a limited set of moves- attack, throw, jump, and bomb- you work your way through NES era Zelda-esque dungeons and pick up gold.  Along the way you find relics to augment your character for the duration of the run and shrines that add a positive and negative effect.  Combat is rather unforgiving and the game requires a decent amount of attention and skill.Upon death you lose a percentage of your gold as your faithful bird carries your sack to the mine hub and you begin your life as a new peasant.  Effects gained in your run are gone, but you can spend the kept gold you earned on a plethora of upgrades and a few gadgets.  Then back to the mine!I don't want to spoil content length in terms of levels and bosses in a review, but I would expect roughly 15-20 hours of gameplay from the title in it's current state (8/23/2019) if you're a stubborn bastard.
_childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game!If you enjoyed Rogue Legacy (I absolutely did) - then you really should get this game!Undermine is a "Rogue-Like" game where you can expect to die, and die often, causing you to restart the procedurally-generated dungeons (mines in this case).  You lose a percentage of your loot (determined by your bag which is upgradeable) upon death - but the loot your next character enters the mine with allows you to upgrade different items (bag to hold gold, pick-axe damage, armour, glove for ranged attacks, etc.).You have a journal for logging a bestiary, artifacts and relics which offer bonuses, and viewing your stats among other things.The game is just plain fun - and because it's so fun, you probably won't feel the frustration of dying often, because each new miner will be slightly more powerful than the one before - making you say "Just one more try" more often than you'd expect.Look - for £15 - GET this game if you like Rogue-likes.
_childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

_childDocuments_.review: Solid rougelite game. Simple enough for first timer to learn, but more complex options available at the end of the game for the one who like challenge.Like the game title, your objective is to go deep under a mine. There are 4 floors for each variant of mine and each variant have different enemies, environment to interact, and specific rooms/secret.Your action inside mine including melee attack, range attack (using pickaxe), plant a bomb, drinking potion, and jumping. Each of this action can be upgraded to have other effect by collecting artifact which play a main part of your build.Because this is a "roguelite", in the hub/base you have option to upgrade the starting status of the miner as well as starting item.
