_childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

_childDocuments_.review: I think the game has potential but I just can't give it a positive review right now. It's far too grindy and I think what is getting most people to post negative reviews is something I haven't seen really mentioned... which is that you can't survive your adventure. It's like a 100% death run every time, and to me that is boring and a bit frustrating. I want to be able to decide when I've had enough, and try to venture out of the hole I jumped into... but the only option is to keep going down until you die.I get that it's sort of the premise of the game... the next similar looking dude replaces you and so on, but it feels like you're taking agency away from the player by literally forcing them to die to "get out". I think the controls also need work. I couldn't get comfortable using mouse and keyboard or just keyboard by itself. I ended up using mouse/keyboard but there were times I just wasn't enjoying that at all. Like when I would be in a frantic fight and forget that my mouse was up in one corner of the screen so even my mouse movement wasn't aiming my attack where I needed it because I needed to completely move it across the screen.Sometimes the enemies combo up in such a way that it makes it really hard to not take damage. The first worm boss is also a huge pain to deal with and I thought it would take me forever to beat, and then randomly I had a run where it was really easy? I'm not sure... I think I had the keyblade item and a couple of keys but I tore into the boss so fast that I was surprised when it was at 20% HP and I barely felt like I did anything.It can be a bit frustrating trying to jump around too... because there's no way to tell where you're going to land sometimes, you might miscalculate slightly which leads you to falling in a pit or on spikes.Also the randomness of the loot was nice sometimes and awful others. I'd get the popcorn buff moments before I had to go fight the boss, rendering the buff basically useless. Overall the game feels very polished and it's well made but I think there's some balancing to do and some work with fixing the controls. Also the whole forcing the player to die thing can get frustrating really fast. I was desperately looking for a way to safely get OUT and there just isn't one. It feels dumb knowing I'm only going to get to a certain point and then I have to suicide to go grind some more all over again.

_childDocuments_.review: Action, adventure, capitalism, and greeeed. Fast-paced, lighthearted, by turns punishing and super rewarding. Lots of value here for re-play.

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATED. At first this was a positive review.---IMPORTANT: You can't tell the game is bad unless you invest quite some time into it. This is how the genre works. So, you spend couple of hours into it, find it's flaws, understand that it's as raw as chicken in Ramsey's shows and BAM. You can't refund it.---So, if there was some sort of a book called "Action Rogue-lites: Do and Don'ts on example - this game would have a whole paragraph. Let me explain.The game is great: art, music, general ideas, mechanics. At first glance I gave Undermine a positive review. But as longer you play - the more you understand what's the difference between good game and "good looking" game.I don't want to compare it to mastodonts of genre like Isaac or Gungeon in this review, because this game is different (but I bet those two were the inspiration for Undermine), but I just can't. So...1. Item powerups. On each level there is a treasure room. Starting lvl 2 those demand a key. (just like in BoI) Each room provides you with an item that is supposed to aid you in your journey. But, there is a HUGE difference. - Item pool is really small. There are like 25-30 of items and 80% of them are useless. For example you can be on some deep level with a pool of: Item that expands the shop variety (useless, as shop doesn't provide any game changers), item that let you find leftover food in chests (though chests may contain food anyways), item that let you jump on oil (absolutely useless unless there is an oil spitting boss which I didn't find yet), item that does minimal damage to mobs as you pick up gold and so on. There are no items that affect your walking speed, there are items that were borrowed from other games without proper understanding on how they work in whole balance system.... Aaah!- Game advertises that there are item synergies. Well, yeah. There are. You have 30 items in game. I've unlocked like 75% of them. I got synergy. One! Two bomb items fused into one bomb item. That does pretty much exactly the same what any of the fused items did. Great job!- Item power levels. There are bunch of things that add X when you have Y: keys = damage, health high/low = damage, etc. They just suck. Do you remember "Money = Power" from Isaac and how it works? You get it, then you get some coins and suddenly you are a DEATH MACHINE! Here they do some really bad thing, for example: keys = damage. Having 6 keys at time makes you "wealthy" on keys. This adds something like +12 damage to your swing. How much is that? Well... Basic rat has something about 40-50 HP, and that +12 refers accordingly. +12 HP damage dealt each swing.I could go more with in-depth analysis, but no. There's too much to it.2. Whole progression. You're a dude, hunting for gold. Whatever. The aim is - travel deeper and get more. Ok.First boss (not the golem joke) is a giant centipede. It has some short cutscene and introduction. (Apart of thing, that it has some attacks that you just can't dodge and the whole combat mechanics... Whatever).So, after quite some time you kill it. And guess what? A ladder appear. Great job! Now go back and follow the rails. You get some money and unlocks. That's it. Why did I even had to fight it, anyway? Did it unlock another passage or biome? No. Did it give me some ability? No. The boss gives you an item (spawn minion at entrance of the hostile room. But it sucks, as it's blind and rarely hits the enemy.) and a potion that... spawns the same minion but once. Wow. Do you want me to avoid all bosses from now on? What's the point?- Leveling up is ehrhmahgerd. Let's say you start with 100 hp, 10 dmg and 10 range. You fight for your gold, over and over again. You level up everything once for the sake of it. Nice job! Now you're 120 hp, 12 dmg and 12 range. Try our new level up. We have like 40 levels of them. It feels exactly like playing one of those mobile RPG without donating for crystals. What can I say? I've spent almost 11 hours in game and all I did - killed two bosses and found a key that I can't get, as I need to spend another 3 hours on gaining gold to level up enough to make it happen. Nice!- Stats. Game has physical, lightning and fire damage so far. Is there a way to armor up yourself? No. Is there a potion? NO! Can I do anything to get less damage?! Well, you can get better at game... No armor. Period. Logic sometimes just leaves the room silently. You can pick up "flying boots" that let you levitate over pits. Oh, wow. So it's like flying, right? Now I can fly over those spikes... Whatta?!You can't affect speed of your character, you can't affect speed of your projectiles (which makes the upgrade of throw distance quite questionable), you can't affect critical chance, attack speed, anything that would make huge difference. Health, damage, distance and gold lost. All you have. And those are increased in 120 easy steps.- Damage. At first you'll be like "Oh, ok, I see". But then you'll get angry. The game has a jump as a dodging mechanic which is really questionable. Why not a simple dash, that would suit the game much more. As by jumping you really have no idea what you can jump over, and what will hit you for sure. So imagine this: you're in a rush, you storm the rooms. You aim for that left passage and you enter. The spikes at the VERY entrance greet you with -29 HP and send flying to that rat on tracks that gives you another -20 HP and then the incoming sawblade deals another -25 hp and sends you flying to a pit. It makes you fall to the room entrance with another -20 hp and since life didn't ready you for this you still hold "w" to run forward in attempt to escape and the spikes say "hi" again. What the hell? I've played  some IWTBTG and Boshy and those looked more honest in terms of damage dealing. Just why?I believe it's time to stop, though I'm not done yet.The folks that did this game are really passionate about their child, I believe. On all other aspects - the game is great. Those mobs dying gave me a feel as Paul Robertson walked in to the office and said: "Guys, I know a cool animation you could use". But the actual gameplay is so bad it made me create this wall of text. No hard feelings. I really hope the game will improve. Cheers!

_childDocuments_.review: There are aspects to like about this game and there are some issues, but honestly, this is more of a side-way thumb.The core issue I have with this game is a lack of focus and variation, as well as just annoying meta-progression quirks.Presentation (sounds, music, graphics) is pretty good.Please stop having perks or upgrades in games like these that boost your progression rate. In this game, there's a perk that increases how much gold you keep on death. Gold is used to buy upgrades and is accrued throughout a run. This means that this perk is generally speaking always your absolute top priority.Just tie it to general progression level in terms of perks or don't have it. It is basically always the optimal choice in games like these and that's kind of boring.Runs feel very much the same all the time. The game offers area skips if you've beaten the boss, but that's generally not a good idea because you kind of want the upgrades you'd get along the way to those levels.There needs to be more level-branches and stuff like time-challenges.In my general opinion, rogue-lites ought to fit in one out of two categories (with minor variations).- The clean rogue-lite where there's a few well-polished systems (examples: Binding of Isaac, Receiver, Ziggurat 2, Dead Cells).- The complicated rogue-lite with 15 (okay, maybe not that many) status screens and  a lot of different systems to interact with or handle (examples: Dungeon Crawl Stone Soup, Heat Signature, Caves of Quad).This game is definitively trying to be the former, but the gold gathering mechanic is frustrating. If you leave gold on the floor, slimes show up and start picking it up. You have to bash them away or have a canary with you to help you chase them down during combat. It is at the same time frustrating and generally free of consequences. The slimes might steal like a couple of percent of your gold, but having that task in the game of having to focus on getting the gold too is just annoying.
_childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

_childDocuments_.review: Undermine is a stellar game that suffers from one big flaw – lack of content. One would think that with all the beautiful pixel art, huge amount of items, and fun gameplay it could easily stand next to greats of this genre of games (rogue-lites such as Binding of Isaac and Enter the Gungeon), but only 4 bosses and biomes (5 if we count the conditional one, and 6th boss as the campaign end boss), coupled with such achievements as “beat the game 30 times”, really does no favors for Undermine. Had the developers gone that extra mile to at LEAST introduce one (or two) more bosses into the mix, this game would have been much better and more enjoyable, without egregious repetitiveness that I’ve personally experienced. This is one of those rare moments where I’d like to have a third (“mixed”) option instead of “thumbs up” or “thumbs down”, as the game can be enjoyable, yet becomes stale after some 50 hours of gameplay (and it is a general consensus that roguelites should be enjoyable for much, much longer).EDIT: oh, and ignore that "Story Rich" tag the game has - there is 0 story to this game, and what little lore there is is mostly item descriptions (it's hard to make another gem like HADES, after all)
_childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

_childDocuments_.review: This was a game I was originally on the fence about when I first saw it/heard about it. Upon watching some videos of the game play and seeing the mechanics, I was in love. This is a gem found in the rough (pun unintended). A great combination of RPG elements and dungeon crawler progression in this cute, yet addictive roguelite. Regardless if you're casual or hardcore at gaming, you can expect to see steady progression with upgrades, recipes, and item discoveries. The RNG can be punishing at times (the curses), but if done right can be turned around in your favor.  It saves at the beginning of each floor, so if life requires your attention, no need to worry about losing your entire mine delve. The controls can be purely keyboard, but can be paired with mouse for precision. When you reach the end of the mine, you can increase the difficulty each time for a challenge or keep it at whatever feels comfortable. However you go about this game, there is always something new to try, find, or attempt to achieve. For it's price, whether on sale or not, Undermine is something I do indeed recommend to try.
_childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

_childDocuments_.review: Well, I'm having a blast with it. (A little over 9 hours in)I don't really understand the people saying it's like a poor version on Isaac. Imo, it's not trying to be anything like Binding of Isaac. Also, people saying they don't like running after gold, that actually turns into a really cool mechanic. (Small spoiler here:) Once you get Geckos Foot (One of the very early permanent upgrades you can buy) You can throw your axe to pick up gold (Given, that's not actually explained, but again I kinda like the discovery aspect of it. Like, hmm, what does this new item do) Anyway once you figure that out, it's really fun. When you mine for gold little weevle things come out of the walls and try to steal it before you can pick it up, if you've killed all the enemies first then that's easy, but sometimes in the chaos of the room fight the gold might get sprayed everywhere and you've got to make a quick decision as to continue the fight and lose the gold or take a chance dashing for the gold but possibly taking damage instead. Equally, if you're nearly dead, you might just want to rush to pick up as much gold as possible before everything gets you, or play it safe in the hopes there's health in the next room. It's definitely an intended thing that adds risk/reward to the game, not just some lazy oversight.Also, I love all the little secret puzzles n stuff.  I personally love the way the game slowly drip feeds new stuff and makes you discover the next bit. Some people might find it obtuse. Though, I would definitely say (Again, minor spoiler:) you should absolutely buy the bomb upgrade as soon as you beat the first boss. It is pretty unforgiving, and the air controls when jumping are donkey ♥♥♥♥.I don't know, it might become repetitive, but I doubt it. Will update this review after another 10-20 hours in anycase.

_childDocuments_.review: To be honest, I wouldn't recommend it at it's current price tag and not even really on sale. It's a $5 game max. _childDocuments_.review: Short story is it's just a Binding of Isaac rip off with melee capabilities but worse overall quality, not worth the price or time spent in my opinion.Definitely would not recommend unless you want to waste your time and money playing a game that only really gets good in the late game and late mid game, before that it's just a snail's pace of a grind to collect gold only to lose most of it when you die, and what little gold you save up gets spent completely in a matter of seconds on one purchase due to overpriced "upgrades". The upgrades are really not worth the price at all because they are very very minor but cost hours of real world time to obtain. If this game enabled you to change difficulties, adjust settings such as gold drop rate or disabling pilfers, and had workshop/modding compatibility then it would be worth the price tag. However, as of right now it is just a worse overall version of Binding of Isaac. Check back a few years later and if they've added the above features or better, then I would recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

_childDocuments_.review: It's a pretty game but there are too many frustrations for me. The controls are a fine in principal, but they lack the affordances you might have come to expect; no coyote time over pits, being able to start the jump animation and still fall down pits, have jumps animate but cancel movement. The bigger frustrations, however,  are around the unfulfilling reward scheme. Losing some gold on death is pretty much par for the course now but the miniscule incremental upgrades that give you minor number improvements feel like a fruitless grind which is only furthered by that loss. Not to mention the critters who constantly try to steal it from you in the first place! Then there are the dungeons, where you will often find yourself using a bomb to get a bomb, or an empty room, or trapped chest. The few decent rewards you get are, within the first few hours at least, pretty dull for the most part, consisting largely of simple stat changes. Simply put, the enjoyment of playing is limited by frustrations and the desire to keep playing is removed from the unrewarding process.
_childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

_childDocuments_.review: This is my first ever Roguelike game.  I had always avoided this style of game because I assumed I would get too frustrated with dying over and over. I'm not a hardcore gamer by any means, but I really enjoyed it.  Because this is my first time playing this type of game I can't speak to how it compares to other games in the genre. But I like that the mechanics and controls are relatively simple,  there are tons of relics and blessings to experiment with and the curses add interesting challenges.  I don't know if I'll ever get good enough to beat the Othermine, but I've put over 100 into the game and I'm probably going to keep playing for while.

_childDocuments_.review: I have about 30hrs in so far and it's still really fun.  I'd say actually it's still climbing the fun curve which is awesome. It also adds some other mechanics from similar Rouge likes (rogue lites) such as Rogue Legacy and the like.Im happy and would recommend it and I'm excited to see what continues to be added and tweaked by the devs.
_childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fine, I guess: it works properly and there seems like a decent enough amount of content and the rogue-lite progress pacing isn't bad, but I just can't really say I actively ever found myself actually enjoying playing it.There's no story to speak of and the mechanics have simply been done better in other games, so there's little to keep me playing and when there are so many other games, I'd rather go play one of them.I know this isn't very constructive criticism, so if the devs read this then I apologise: it's hard to put my finger on precisely why, but I simply didn't enjoy playing this game and thus cannot recommend it to others.
_childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

_childDocuments_.review: Undermine is a challenging Game that can feel a bit repetitive for the first couple of hours but grows on you after you start to unlock more and more upgrades until you will be able to do godruns. The Endgameboss is a bit underwhelming but the Othermine is where the real difficulty lays. Getting the Aegis through to the end and getting a winstreak is what will take the most time. All in all i would recommend this game to everyone who likes challenging Roguelikes with some unique mechanics. Not as polished as Enter the Gungeon but still 8/10 in my book.
_childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

_childDocuments_.review: I had many hours of fun with this game even though I must admit that I'm still not very good at it and sometimes still feel frustrated for ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ I manage to do while playing it. There's still many things to discover, many relics, blessings and a few familiars to discover, the "Othermine" yet to be explored...The game's visuals are beautiful, the bosses, although they seem to be hard at first are not so difficult when you begin to learn their attack patterns, enemy variety is good and at later stages when you uncover more and more levels some of them begin to appear in the first stages just to add up more difficulty (but at least in my case it wasn't unfair or anything). I don't really like the game music, sometimes I mute it and then listen to other things.RNG of course will play a huge part when it comes down to the relics and blessings that can be acquired while the levels go on and then sometimes a run will be really messed up, Altars found throughout the game give blessings, but at the cost of giving you a curse and curses are randomly distributed too, some of them really hinder your progress making things more chalenging (although there are means to avoid this for at least a few times like one specific relic that I know about). Things like damaging you whenever you jump (little damage, but depending on your HP and the room you enter these things add up), inflicting more damage whenever you fall into a pit, breaking items or destroying blessings after some requirements are met (like killing enemies), giving you poison after each enemy lands an attack on you, summoning more spiders whenever you kill an enemy (these last two are somewhat annoying since Poison makes you slow for the duration of acthe status) and many mores side-effects that I can't mention here because of the text's size will give you a progressively harder time (There's Sho'guul's Lair that will give you a specific number of curses once you chose one of two relics available too).One of the cons (imo) is the currency issue, you'll spend too long trying to gain enough gold to buy upgrades in order to expand your inventory, to upgrade stats and some items that will make your characters better, there's thorium as well, a purple gem that can be used to a few things like crafting relics, brewing potions and making blessings and this one is even harder to acquire, the thing with gold is that even in further runs you'll be able to make more gold because you'll be progressively better or at least will have some strategies to do that these upgrades still cost too much (getting expensive as the time goes one however is not really an issue) to the point that depending on your style you'll spend more gold upgrading the Gold Sack since with each new one you'll lose less gold when you die at the cost of not upgrading things like Swing/Throw Damage, or HP, etc. About thorium, not only is harder to come accross (as I've mentioned before) and it usually comes in small quantities (small comparing the cost of things based on thorium expenses). As I said before there's a good variety of enemies and in further playthroughs some of the enemies that you've faced in other stages will star to appear in the first ones, sometimes right from the start, but the looks of these stages will be pretty much the same, although I can understand that each stage "features a theme" (for the lack of a more fitting expression) this quickly makes things a little boring, of the themes is the crystal caves, the difference between this and the previous one is not only perceptible through its general aspects but when you look at the hazardous stuff that is present as well and it's really easy to die quickly there because while trying to avoid enemy attacking you a rock exploded and sent crystals flying in your general direction of because you weren't aware of thorny bush next to some rocks and some grass. Again, at least for me, the music is not that good and it gets boring fast.The game is nice, you'll probably have a good time playing it uncovering the things that it has to offer.
_childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

_childDocuments_.review: I'm getting to the end of the base game now and I have to say, this game is insanely addictive. The curse/blessing mechanic is challenging yet satisfying when you amass so many. _childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

_childDocuments_.review: A super generic mine themed roguelite. It's doing a lot of stuff but none of it feels new or creative. You have your generic crafting, your NPC's that provide shops and stuff, your chunky pixel graphics, throwable pick boomerang, and randomly generated mine rooms with secret puzzles. There's also bosses. It takes a lot of the skeleton from Binding of Isaac including run killing items you have to learn to avoid.Generally speaking this game is so uninspired. It's just a mash up of tired old gaming clichés and does nothing original with them. The first 15 minutes feel like the next 8 hours. I got the gist and moved on.

_childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

_childDocuments_.review: What a game!The games developer (Thorium) has managed to create one of the most addicting dungeon exploration games to date. The blessing and curses system is perfect, each choice can either make or break a run, enemies are creative and simple, yet put a few different enemies in a room and suddenly it can be challenging or easy to make a mistake that will end that trip. Along with this the bosses are fun and challenging and if your new to the game can take multiple tries to defeat. The fact that the games does not make everything available and you have to find blueprints and then buy the blessing or potion makes the grinding feel very rewarding. Finally the dungeon itself constantly feels new, this is achieved by making the dungeon layout, chest locations, shops, power ups and enemies constantly different, after 22 hours of game play so far i can safely say that i'm not bored of this game and don't think ill be getting bored any time soon. Would recommend to anyone who wants a fun, interesting and attention holding indie RPG!
_childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty fun little rogue-like. I like combining different abilities together to make builds where I'm running 10x health or gaining ten thousand gold. Really enjoy the ability to teleport to different floors, since that reduces a bit of the grind and lets you play a couple of quick rounds.Mildly disturbing that I've killed about a hundred poor miners so far, but that's how the game goes. But also i get to pet a dog each time, so that's cheerful.
_childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

_childDocuments_.review: Heading into UnderMine, I was expecting a roguelite that wasn’t too bad but wasn’t anything great either. What I got instead was easily one of the best roguelites I’ve played since my time with Enter the Gungeon. The sheer attention to detail is staggering from both a visual and gameplay perspective, with so much to earn and look forward to. Combined with its high level of replayability, I found myself quickly addicted. It may have an issue in regards to a lack of high-tier passives, but the rest of the game overshadows this flaw greatly to still offer something equally engaging and endlessly fun. If you’re looking for a great roguelite, UnderMine is an adventure more than worth mining away at.If you'd like to read the rest of this review and more like it, check out . Thank you to Thorium for providing a review copy.

_childDocuments_.review: really bad controls/hitbox of your character ruin what could be an otherwise very enjoyable game. you will constantly get stuck on the terrain and get knocked or walk into the abyss in a way that just feels really bad. had to refund because of this. also losing half your gold on death mechanic just artificially increases game time and leads to you coming back and not being able to afford any upgrades.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite having less content than my Favorite Rogue-Like game (The Binding of Isaac with all DLC), UnderMine still managed to keep me entertained for 20 hours so far and I can already tell that I will spend likely 10-20 more hours (maybe even more if there are interesting updates after the game exits early access). It was totally worth my money and I can recommend it to every Rogue-Like fan. The amount of items, monsters, traps, room types, blessings, curses, potions, upgrades and even more is very satisfying and, most importantly, the fight feeling is super good.

_childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

_childDocuments_.review: A great rogue-like with a unique combat system and story.Out of all roguelikes I've played, I think this is one I've enjoyed the most followed closely by Risk of Rain 2. This game has a great combat system that becomes most comfortable and natural as you play the game, allowing you to dig deeper and deeper into the story and collectibles as you learn and adapt. The characters, items, curses, blessings, bosses, and pets help to make this game feel less than a typical rogue-like and more like its own unique game. I've done most things you can do in this game (If we are referring to Steam Achievements), so I can say there is a lot to do in the base game and a lot more if you want to pursue challenges and achievements.If you are looking for another rogue-like game with a lot of replayability, I think you'll be surprised by what this game has to offer outside of its cover. I am looking ahead towards Undermine 2 with all of this in mind. I know Thorium can reproduce what made this game special and I hope they can add more to make it a unique installment.
_childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

_childDocuments_.review: If you like Binding Of Isaac you'll love this game. I have 50 hours and 100% achievements with all relics/potions/blessings unlocked.The game highly rewards you for the play time you put into it. Progress is slow at the start but the game is still fun. As you get more and more gold and your character becomes stronger you'll reach a point where you get ALOT stronger every run and make rapid advancements.TIPS for new players: In your first save file craft every blue print you find, try to beat the game a few times and find alot of blue prints. Then start a new save file and only unlock the blueprints that seem good to you. Or just do it your own way and have fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Game's a scam. Undermine has such a high potential for greatness, and yet there's little issues that keep it from being the greatest thing since Nuclear Throne (Or the Roguelite Standard Supreme: MONOLITH. No game's better than that yet.)PROS:+Graphical Style+TRANSPARENCY OF ITEMS (Like damn I wish every crappy procedurally generated piece of junk showed me and outright told me what items did before I picked them up)+Jump function makes sense overall, is nice+Non-Boss/Big Enemy combat is fun.+Difficulty is WAY HIGH starting out. People jerk off over difficulty, so I guess it's a plus for you. Good for you.+Multiple Save Files. Why this isn't a thing in most Roguelites is beyond me, but I personally appreciate it...CONS:-Little slimes that steal your gold if you don't immediately dive for them ensures a degree of 'tism is mandatory at all times unless you lucked out and got the gold vacuum item that lets you pick up gold from a distance WITHOUT an upgrade!-Why the hell is picking up items/gold at a distance with your thrown pickaxe an upgrade that has to be purchased..come to think of it..-Why the hell is an upgrade mandatory to break all barriers with a bomb? It's kind of stupid that such a thing is locked behind a slog of grind just to unlock another NPC that is USELESS until later. COME TO THINK OF IT-Why the hell are prices so high in a game where making gold is a massive chore without blatant cheating? I've spent 3 hours just making my pickaxe good, and..it doesn't matter since OOPS RANDOM MINEFIELD LOL RUN OVER / OOPS MADE ONE MISTAKE DUE TO A CURSE THAT YOU CAN'T STOP FROM HAPPENING WHEN YOU PURSUE AN UPGRADE!!!!!!!! Like..it takes 50 years just to unlock basic measures, and if you fail (AND DYING IS KIND OF THE POINT OF ROGUELITES UNLESS THEY'RE PROPERLY SKILL BASED - Monolith, again. Even basic crap works well), you lose your progress. -Difficulty is WAY HIGH for starting out. You're either going to die to the knight and his healsloot, or you just die to the health sponge boss because HEY YOU THINK THE FIRST BOSS IS FAIR? ONLY ONE WEAK SPOT AND COLLISION DAMAGE AND FILLS THE SCREEN WITH ADDS AND THE FREAKIN' ITEM POOL SUCKS ROYALLY. HEY LOOK IT'S AEGIS AND OIL BOOTS FOR THE 45TH RUN! WOW!-Enemy design goes to garbage when dealing with most big enemies. The 'true first boss' was learnable and easy (Rock Mimic), but the first bosses (Big Centipede? Knight and Healsloot duo from Slay the Spire?)  aren't exactly learnable. Yes, they have actions they do. No, they're not in a pattern that's learnable and easily dealt with. Plus you die in four hits. Maybe more or less depending on items. Knight charges? You walk up to go for a hit? ♥♥♥♥ YOU FOR PLAYING KID, YOU EAT 40 DAMAGE OF 200 HP. He'll insta-poke or shield slam for another 24-50 too. Not worth trying yet.-Landmine rooms. No warning minus a sign you'll get blown the hell up going to. No little scuff of dirt on the ground to avoid. Just RNG pinball PLUS OR MINUS enemies. -I'll throw 'whatever lies ahead' here, since in my 3 hours, I haven't seen past the first floor. Perhaps I don't understand the game, but people wank over it and the devs themselves say it's Twitch popular (Not Fall Guys popular. Not DOTA/LoL popular.), so good on them for making a quality product. Be glad they got their game out before Spelunky 2, cause that'd murder this game in cold blood (Y'know. Superior roguelite genre in being a 'DIE IF I MISS A JUMP' platformer versus a 'DIE IF I ENGAGE MANDATORY CONTENT AND IT NEVER IMPROVES' roguelite thing.)Mad cause bad. Contrary to how I feel, I'll give it the thumbs up. Might just cheat the gold and see if anything changes...oh wait, multiple save files. DEFINITELY looking into cheating the gold and seeing if anything changes.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game on sale and I really enjoyed it. Its one of those games where you don't get mad even if you die because you're too excited for your next run. _childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game on launch because of the comments that it was similar to The Binding of Isaac, and that it was a "roguelite" with itemization and combos much like the formerly mentioned game.I bought this game mostly to play a few rounds in between my ever growing backlog of games that I keep telling myself I'm going to prioritize and clear up.Well, after 7 hours in two days (which is not a lot for some, but quite a bit for me) I can safely say this game is "it".  Do you wish you could find a game that makes you go "one more run" and then you realize you've spent the past several hours telling yourself that?Do you want a game that is difficult, but overall fair?Do you want a game that moment to moment has more to keep you engaged instead of zoning out during your repeated runs of the first several floors?Keep in mind, this is early access, there are a few bugs and a few strange interactions in the game.  But the devs have already put out a hotfix on Day 2 of the game's cycle and have been very active in Discord in talking with the community.This is a roguelite that is already well worth the admission cost.  The fact there is only more to come has me very excited for the future of this game.Highly recommended for any fans of Isaac, Enter the Gungeon, Nuclear Throne, the whole nine yards.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot of heart and style behind it. From the overall light hearted story with a serious undertone to it, to the smooth gameplay that really is tightly tuned. Pixel perfect hit boxes and a variety of mechanics that don't overly complicate things keep the first dozen hours interesting. In honesty, I have not beaten the game. This is just my synopsis based on what I've gone through so far. What I have played, however, is enough to encourage people to dig into this one. The price point is nice, the music is good, the gameplay is excellent, and the rogue-like build up is steady enough where each run through feels like your accomplishing more. Some runs seem to skimp on keys, some deaths are frustrating from how many things are shooting, exploding, and charging at you with pitfalls all around, and while the music is passable it really never sucked me in. That's probably the least I could say about the game. The most I could say has been stated in the first paragraph. The random dungeons keep a good variety and the evolution of the game is well balanced. In all, I encourage this to fans of Rogue-likes, Isometric overhead adventure games, and also fans of old school game design. A solid buy for the price tag at face value. A steal if you wait for a 50% off sale. P.S. So much love for the pilfers. They're just doing their job.

_childDocuments_.review: Undermine is a genuinely fantastic roguelike that deserves a lot more attention.It feels like a really neat halfway point between Spelunky and Binding of Isaac, with some of the best perma-progression mechanics I've seen in the genre. I'll elaborate on that.First of all, the world of the game feels dynamic. The reason for that is that there's potential for CHAOS. Slime enemies can change properties based on where they fall. Water slimes can jump into an oil puddle and turn into oil slimes. Oil slimes can spread further oil puddles. Oil puddles can catch fire. Slimes caught on fire turn into fire slimes. There's more examples of these kinds of dynamics in the game, and they're great. They can make deaths feel hilarious sometimes, just like Spelunky.There's also really nice item synergies. Nothing as visually distinct and crazy as in BoI, but mechanically there's absolutely some items that will combine in very exciting and interesting ways.As for the perma-progression, one of the stand-out features is that once you beat certain bosses, new enemy types will pop up in early levels. It's a nice way to keep things feeling fresh without going the more resource-intensive option of offering alternate level paths (like Dead Cells, BoI or Spelunky 2). Another really interesting thing is that bosses don't need to be beat more than once. You can just skip them after the first time (or even before the first time, if you'd like!). There's also little quests that unlock more upgrade options, and all their appearances feel organic. There's no quest tracker or progress log. The upgrades feel like they're less about making things easier and more about helping you progress through early levels faster and giving you more choices of how to do so. It's a smart way of opening up options to players as they become more experienced with the game, while also not making it feel like you're just grinding until you actually have a chance at beating the game.Speaking of, I haven't beaten the game yet, and I might update the review after that.But Undermine is already one of my favorite examples of the genre, and you should absolutely play it.

_childDocuments_.review: Undermine is an action roguelike with smooth gameplay, beautiful pixel art, varied randomized gameplay, and a solid meta progression system that provides long-term motivation.As typical for the genre, the game takes place in a randomized dungeon of connected rooms, with each room taking up one screen. If you enter a room with enemies, the exits get sealed until you have killed them. Not all rooms contain enemies though, some feature puzzles, shops, or treasures. The dungeon currently features 5 distinct biomes, and each biome stretches across 4 levels with about 15 rooms each, has its own set of enemies, features specific environmental challenges and opportunities, and has an end boss with unique mechanics. All bosses except the last one can be skipped if you don't feel ready for them.When you die, you automatically start a new character on the game's top level, which features a number of shops. You keep some gold from your previous run, and can use it to buy permanent upgrades for your characters. Another resource (thorium) can be used to craft powerful artifacts, potions, and blessings, provided that you found the respective blueprint / recipe / formula at some point. Most shops will be empty at the beginning of the game, but you can free their owners from various parts of the dungeon in a series of quests.I found the combat exciting and engaging. Each type of enemy has its own perks, and it was fun finding the best strategies to counter those. The game may feel a bit difficult at first, but actually becomes fairly easy as you keep upgrading your stats. If it gets _too_ easy, you can increase the dungeon's difficulty after beating all of the bosses. This will respawn the bosses, populate the dungeon with stronger enemies, and can be repeated indefinitely each time you beat all bosses.Meta-progression systems such as this one can feel a bit grindy, but Undermine implements it pretty well. You can find dozens of artifacts, blessings, and curses in each run, and many of those have such a profound effect on the gameplay that each run feels different. Also, after unlocking a new artifact / potion / blessing, you start your next run with it. For me, the curiosity of how a new artifact might work and how the next run might unfold, kept me engaged and interested. I had a steady feeling of progress.If meta-progression is not your thing, or if you'd like to shake things up a bit more, you can alternatively play a different game mode where you always start rather weak and face a dungeon with even higher degrees of randomization.Undermine won't revolutionize the genre, but is so well designed that it has quickly become one of my favorite entries. I also very much appreciate the focus on user-friendliness: the game controls very well with mouse and keyboard, all controls can be rebound (including an alternative key for each action), and mouse aiming can be toggled on or off. The game also autosaves at the start of each level.At the time of this writing, Undermine is still in early access, but it's almost complete and will soon have its full release. At that point its price will rise, so getting it now (or in the upcoming Summer Sale if it gets a discount) might be a good idea. The current price already looks like a bargain to me, considering how much fun I'm having with this game.

I'm only into the second the dungeon, but I can tell you that the boss's are challenging, but upgrading your characters overtime will lessen the challenge, and the time you put in feels worth while.I'd put this game in the league of "Rouge legacy" or "Spelunky" and not quite into S tier with "Enter the gungeon" or "Binding of Issac"   However, take in to account I've only played for five hours, and this whole rant is opinion based. _childDocuments_.review: Pretty good for a game with only one weapon and two attacks. I should be bored AF with how little meaningful variety there is in the gameplay loop but I'm still having fun. I couldn't tell you why, exactly, but I am.There are a lot of 'upgrades' you can find in a run but 99% of it is boring crap like extra attack damage or extra gold drops, stuff like that. Some relics add graphics along with the increased damage, but they don't change how you play. Basically nothing you find anywhere changes how you play the game. There are potions that are mostly boring, giving you a buff for a short time, or rarely, doing something interesting like dropping a chest. I guess it's more fun to find a potion that creates a chest than just finding another chest. Whatever. Honestly, all this game has going for it are two things: The engine is smooth and well-developed, leading to responsive and satisfying gameplay, and the graphics are great. Music is boring. The visual appeal goes quite a long way, though--there's a ton of very, very good pixel art here to enjoy. Playing in 4k has caused me no FPS issues, which you'd think would be the norm for pixel art games but it isn't. If it looks like fun, you'll probably enjoy it. Lukewarm recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: This game starts in out in long tutorial style where you have to defeat 4 of the 5 bosses to unlock Othermine (roguelike mode). You keep a portion of your gold after dying to unlock upgrades to make it easier to win.  The bosses on Ascension 0 (when your just starting the game) do not respawn after you kill them once to make it easier for you to complete your first run. After you defeat the 5 bosses you reach Summoning Stone 1 which respawns all of the bosses and makes the game harder. Also the Din, the Old King fight is unlocked.The true challenge of the game is Othermine (roguelike mode). Try to beat Othermine with Siegfried's Aegis for a real challenge.At the time of this review only 1.7% of people have beaten Din, the Old King and only 16% of people have even tried Othermine. So take these reviews with a grain of salt because they barely even played any of the content available.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been looking for a new roguelite for some time now. And this and Spirits Abyss are the standouts of the year. It takes mechanics and ideas that work from other well designed games:- Binding of Isaac: Level design and layout, engaging resource management (eg. only the item room on the first level is unlocked, for subsequent levels you have to have a key, and it's guaranteed that one will appear; Secret room placement and logic; secret passages under destructibles)- Rogue Legacy:  The idea that you aren't playing the one character each run, but that you play a series of characters.- Goshdarnit, there are more influences, but for the life of me can't think of 'em right now.Anyways, this game doesn't bring anything particularly new to the table, but what it does is combine good elements from other innovators and masterfully meshes the mechanics together.The humour is well done, everpresent, but not overbearing. The game is totally aware that its world is one that was explored to death and it embraces it. But what it does is season it with just a pinch of social critique (but you don't know what that term means. Do you PEASANT?The art, as everything else in the game is above competent. I mean that as praise - it is not so fluffed up to overshadow the mechanics. It perfectly serves the mechanics - every sprite is easy to read due to good use of contrast and silhouette. Everything has just enough frames of animation, and not a frame more. There is a graphical glitch here or there (projectiles drawing over walls they are behind), but they are so minor that if they never attempted to fix them, I wouldn't mind too much.And regarding the audio - Sadly, I can't comment on the music, because I tend to mute it, so I can listen to something else while playing. All the audio effects are quite good, with several touches that show that quite a bit of thought and care was put into them (the muffled sounds of the blacksmith pounding his hammer when you are in another room - *chef's kiss*)The gameplay is tight and responsive - I wouldn't call it the best roguelite I ever played (I guess that's the curse of not bringing anything new to the table) but gosh darn it it's somewhere up there!👍👍 Would recommend
_childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

_childDocuments_.review: Everything feels unrewarding about this game. Firstly, it is not a rogue like in any way, but more of an RPG. The game is very easy and the only thing preventing you from beating the game at first is your very low health and lack of gear. From this point, it is just a matter of die-and-retry.  You unlock all the items in a very definite order and you get to keep most of them for your next plays. Chest rooms and secret rooms feel so cheap, providing basic power-ups, potions and gold. There’s really no outstanding item, you never get this kind of excitement after discovering a new item. And you don’t really mind losing to the game because, anyway, you know you’ll get the same kind of items next try.Secondly, the jumping system is the worst. It doesn’t fit at all the weird top-down perspective. You never really know where your character will land. It feels also very unresponsive and sluggish. A very bad attempt at renewing the roguelike genre with a little bit of a platformer.Good graphic design and concept, but terrible gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: The more I play this game, the less I like it. The first few upgrades you find are interesting, but then you realize that that's basically *it*. The "hundreds" that the game advertises includes linear stat boost items that persist through the game (+1 swing damage, +2 swing damage, +1 throw range, etc.). The fact that you really only have two main attack types (swing, or throw pickaxe) also limits the build variety and upgrade possibilities. The weapon synergies are lacking the excitement of say, Binding of Isaac.The game also plays waaay too long. Each level has four stages, ending with a boss that you only fight the first time through. There is a fast-forward mechanic a la Spelunky, but given the massive item deficit you take by bypassing the first X many levels, it's not worth it. So instead you are forced to grind through the first half hour, only to have a realistic shot at the level's boss. The graphics are great, though the mustachioed man "diversity" gets a bit stale (I imagine they will add more enhancements in the future), but I find myself increasingly playing fewer and fewer runs per day, and imagine I will probably fall off completely soon. Hopefully updates can address the grind and tedium, but for now I'd say this game is only worth getting if you need something for a long weekend.

_childDocuments_.review: UnderMine is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ gem of a game.Get this game. See the Pros and Cons below for the Short Version:PROSApproachable and fair in its difficultyPolished in its mechanics and presentationMusic is absolutely stunningThe story and the characters you meet are interestingThe cultural references and humor of the game are hystericalThe order in which you address how you complete portions of the game depend on you as the playerUnique boss encounters that make the player adjust their play style to the gimmick of the bossCONS - all these can be remedied/improved upon in the coming weeks; some are just what I wish was in the gameBugs with swatting back the bone projectile that the skeleton throwsProgression does not reflect a visual change to the peasant or equipment; it'd be cool to see upgrades to the pickax yield a different pickax, etc.No female peasant; lets get some inclusivity in here! Make it randomly generate which one you are too!There are a few recolored sprites reused through the game; this could easily be remedied with simply more enemies and more complex enemy design.If you have played bullet hell genre games like Enter the Gungeon, this game is going to feel very easy to you, perhaps too easyLong Version:I have three files open on this game; myself, my wife's, and my son's. My son is 7 and an okay gamer, but not good enough to really make much advancement in a game like this. My wife is a pragmatic puzzle solver who doesn't like being too stressed by video games, so much so that she will put it down if it gets to be too much, but she will whoop the ass of a game like The Room. I am big ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Papa. I will ♥♥♥♥ all your games up.I am telling you this so you understand the perspective of my review and how that may relate or not relate to your own opinion.UnderMine is the kind of dungeon crawler that is equal parts personality as it is challenge. The game will absolutely floor you with its unique art style and presentation, catchy tunes, and voluptuous cast of characters to talk to and interact with. The gimmicks in the game feel so directly tethered with the central themes put out there that nothing feels out of place (e.g., the peasant dying and you playing as a new one every time, the progression systems in place, etc.)The game itself is incredibly approachable; as stated above, you can see that my family consists of a varied group of gamers. Despite what makes us different, I am fully entertained as a hardcore gamer, my wife is still very much so interested in the game despite its challenges, and my son loves the presentation of the game. For some, this game will be challenging, but it is fair. I see some reviews on here complain about the slimes, the progression system, or the combat. I find this interesting because the slime mechanic turns out to be one of the funniest ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ things I have seen in some time; wacking those little bastards and listening to them do a Kirby-esque scream as they projectile off the screen is hysterical. The loss of gold upon death is part of the experience; upgrades start cheap enough to help give you the necessary buffer to learn how the game functions within, but the progression to be had here is truly on you as the player. You can bump up your damage or have a higher HP count, but if you really can't deal with the dynamics of the game, you aren't going to progress. Also, you can upgrade your bag, so you don't have to lose as much gold each time you die! As for the combat, there are literally three mechanics: swing, throw or bomb. Time your swings with the behaviors of the enemies, use the throw for long distance combat or to kite enemies around, or bomb stationary targets. This is a simple system with not much strategy involved despite how fun it is. If this challenges you to the point that you are not having fun, this genre in general might not be for you.On the other side of the spectrum, gamers who frequent games like Enter the Gungeon and other titles in the Bullet Hell genre are going to feel like this game moves a snail's pace. Even the most frenetic moments can be boiled down to patterns that all the monsters behave in, and a smart gamer will be able to predict, and outmaneuver these moments. I have found myself most frequently dying when I, the player, am tired and not paying attention, not because the game outpaced me or caught me off guard. That is what will kill these kinds of players, not the game.For an early access game, this title has a lot of content. I have made it to the bottom of the UnderMine and beaten all of the bosses; I am currently working on rescuing everyone that I have missed and re-beating the bosses that are now alive again. Some additions I hope to see in the full game are: female peasants for the player to play as, progression in the form of gear changes to clothing and items used as you purchase better equipment, and maybe some more variation in the sprites used (recolors always make me laugh, then cry a little). Overall, it's already an amazing game. I would recommend this title to any player looking for a game with a hell of a personality :)

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR - This game is not worth it's 20$ price tag. Maybe worth it when it’s closer to 5$.Pros -It's really fun starting out and getting some cool things that constantly change your game and surprises you with some cool mechanics.The sprites and the music are very well done. I have the Bathcat/Toadvine track stuck in my head right now.Cons -Very repetitive overall and even though it seems like the rooms are random, you really start to see that they are not random but randomly place pre-made rooms. Very short game that gives the fake sense of content by ‘hexing’ you after you beat it and you do it again but harder.RNG is not your friend and it never will be. I went almost 5 floors without finding a single key and only 2 bombs, and on a few runs I was completely locked out of any sort of path forward and had to use the ‘give up’ option in the menu. This should never happen.The jumping mechanic feels extremely clunky and a huge problem being that it is your primary way of dodging attacks.

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy Spelunky and Binding of Isaac you will enjoy this rogue-like. It has a simple but fun progression system where every playthrough makes you a little better and you can venture deeper into the depths. Same rng level structure as Isaac but you don't get to replay seeds. The item variety doesn't stack up to Isaac but it takes a different close quarters approach to combat. You swing a pick axe that doubles as a short range boomerang. Get gold, eat food, find the hidden npc's to stock your base with merchants to help you explore, stay alive, kill baddies. I've only seen the first 2 boss fights, but with 15+ hours invested,  I would recommend this game for everyone who are fans of the aforementioned.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game and very fun, but is incredibly flawed.After 10 hours it feels like I made no progress. I can see what people mean now when they say it feels grindy, you almost NEED to upgrade all of your tools, armour and gold supply in order to feel like you are powerful enough to continue on.You can be 30 minutes into a run and you will only be in the dungeon area and judging by the big rock with the boss medallion things in it, I am assuming there is a few more areas I have yet to even look at. To be fair, you could just rush your way down the pits (It works like Stardew Valley if you mined in that game, area progression works the same way), however you will have to be god tier with your pick axe where you can only swing a few pixels in front of you.Also with your relics, there isn't a single relic that I am hoping to get. The one thing I love about rogue-likes is that there is usually a few different power ups that you are just hoping to get that helped a ton in previous runs. In this game, maybe the most useful I have seen is the axe that makes your swing bigger. The rest that I have seen so far almost feel like they just deal with annoyances rather then actually help with a run. Like that bomb that explodes in 4 different directions, its nice to destroy as much rocks as possible for powerups but I can't say you really need it as bombs are so RNG to the point where some runs you feel absolutely rich with explosives and others you feel like your desperate.Also... oh god the pits in this game are the dumbest thing ever. They are only there to annoy you. I would have rather the devs make the pits have invisible barriers and remove the jump mechanic all together. The jump mechanic is incredibly pointless and just doesn't work with the top-down camera view. It is so incredibly frustrating to being almost an hour into a run and you accidentally fall into a pit when trying to grab a steak and die. Dumbest thing in this game.That being said, here's some positives and general notes- Combat is fluid and fair, although not very interesting. Still fun and satisfying to hit things though.- The art style is charming, maybe a bit too generic and doesn't feel like it's own thing but still nice to look at.- I like the music, although that shop theme drives me nuts.- There are characters with names and such but they feel flat and uninteresting where you don't really care at all about them and just use them for their resources.- I think curses are a bit much sometimes and only 1 curse can destroy a run which sucks (There's one that takes away your potion slot, there is one that makes all locked doors only open with your health, there is one for when you get damaged there is chance you will lose a key... which happens a lot etc.)With all my negatives, it is still a generally fun game but I would 100% wait for a sale. As rogue-like it is an incredibly frustrating experience and progression feels slow and tedious at times. The game is still very addictive and will continue to play and at least see what the ending is.

Sorry.

_childDocuments_.review: Undermine is a pretty charming little roguelite for the most part. It's got a nice art style that generally clearly shows what's happening. It's got an excellent soundtrack. Responsive controls. Generally flows pretty well.It does have a bit of the "roguelite twinstick shooter"-issue where any given run is gonna be extremely random, however, and not in a good way. Instead in the sense that every upgrade you get is take-it-or-leave-it, it would be immensely benefited by having upgrades be "grab one of these two or three"-instead so you can actually have some influence on your "build" for a given run.It's also hard to explain the facial expression I made when reaching the final boss, because it didn't come at the end of a run, with all the upgrades I'd accrued and then proceeding as a result of how well I'd played. Instead it happened in the between-runs zone and just tossed me in there with only my persistent upgrades. It felt a bit awkward, frankly, and I don't understand why they chose to do it that way.The game also has a few hidden things that you would almost certainly NEVER figure out without a wiki. I'm looking at you, way to access "The Contested Bog," a thing that turned out to be so circuitous and riven with random chance that I just decided not to bother. Whatever content was hidden in there can't possibly be good enough to merit that level of wasted time and repeated runs.A couple of the bosses also feel pointlessly tanky. Most of the bosses don't really have multiple "phases," so once you know how to handle their first "phase" effortlessly, it's just a matter of patience. They could have benefited from more phases or lower hit points(perhaps with higher damage values so they were still a threat). Still, complaints aside, not a bad game, and be sure to get the soundtrack. It remains extremely good.
_childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: filled with annoying mechanics, game abandoned by devs. In a game where you need to get gold, you get penalized an awful lot for trying to get it. Die in a run? boom 1/4th of your gold gone.Took longer than 3 seconds to pickup the gold that dropped? Gold gone. Chased one of the gold thieves?*all* the gold that just dropped is gone. Truly, it is infuriating that you lose gold for not being able to pick it up fast enough?!  Gold spawns are random so you'll often get gold veins across vast chasms that you cannot reach.Items feel....poorly thought out and extremely underwhelming consistently though multiple runs. Your permanent upgrades and your current-run money share the same bank account. This forces runs to feel more challenging than they should & honestly just takes a lot of the fun out.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty fun game!It's challenging but the mechanics and enemy attack patterns are apparent enough that every successive fight becomes a bit more easier. _childDocuments_.review: It's a really good action roguelike with good progression mechanics. What I like most about this roguelike is how every item is helpful in some way. Compare that to Isaac where one bad item could mess up your whole run. Undermine instead deals you with curses in a way to even out the eventual powerbalance. These curses are more like stat downgrades than actually being game changing (which I like), these curses are also removable btw for a price. All in all it's superfun to play and there's plenty of secrets and upgrades to find. Even after 37 hours of play there's still more to unlock.
_childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

_childDocuments_.review: First, I must disclose I was given this game for free with the purpose of reviewing Undermine.This is a first impressions review.TLDR: If you like roguelikes/roguelites and want something that can be equally (and sometimes more) unforgiving as it can be generous with a sprinkle of humour then this game is for you.Now the first thing I have to mention is the art style, it's great! I love it, it looks a bit dated at first but once you play then you really start to notice how it definitely isn't. They type of art style matches the game perfectly, and is very reminiscent of Neon Abyss! The game starts off relatively slow and progression is also quite slow, however this picks up quite quickly. I did find that for new players this was more unforgiving than most, there isn't much in the way of tutorials to explain how to get through specific blockades or where to find specific items for quests, essentially it does not hold your hand. You also lose gold you find to pilfers quite frequently and whilst this can be annoying you will get used to stopping them. A lot of gold is also lost when you die, and the more gold you have the more you lose. With the gold you do return with there are vendors that allow you to upgrade your health, damage, throw range and upgrades to reduce the amount of gold lost upon death. There are also relics that you can craft however I've noticed even these can be pilfered! Something I massively disagree with, why would there be slimes above the dungeons that steal items you've just crafted after saving up your thorium?! Only for that blueprint to also disappear after crafting. Nonetheless the game keeps slowly unlocking things and you keep getting further and further through the levels whilst sometimes not realising you're getting further and further each time, whether this is due to skill increasing or upgrades, I'm unsure of at this point.This game is not for the faint-hearted, it is difficult and it is unforgiving, but that's what roguelikes are all about right?

_childDocuments_.review: The game is very addicting, which is good when it is incredibly fun. The enemies are the right level of challenging, the levels are well designed and fun to navigate. overall the game is very well made, and a lot of fun, even as an early access. _childDocuments_.review: Overall Undermine is a promising game that plays almost exactly as advertised. The RPG elements and steady leveling are highly reminiscent of Rogue Legacy. The frequent dying is reminiscent of, well, every other rogue-like and rogue-lite game ever made. Boss battles are varied in difficulty but can be challenging. Rooms are fairly varied in design so it takes a while for them to get repetitive. It looks like there is a lot of room for growth here, with multiple types of minions/familiars and many different types of artifacts to be unlocked.This is a very polished game, especially for an EA title, and I found no bugs or game breaking concerns. It is fun and held my attention for a good 16 hours.  Ultimately it got to be a bit stale, but I think that it will only improve as new content and features are added.  In its current state it was worth the money, and enjoyable, and it may end up being really great as new content comes online.

If you like either of those games, this game is for you, and at the price of only $14 it's practically a steal, to me at least.It has a lot of potential to become its own thing and become much better, its already half way there with this level of polish many Early Access games fail to have on release to it.
_childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

_childDocuments_.review: As a veteran fan of both traditional roguelikes and roguelites, I can safely say that Undermine is an average game at best. If this game is your first game of this genre, then yeah I can see you getting hooked, but when compared to some of the offers out there, it falls quite flat.While on a first glance, this game seems to have all of the markings of an indie gem: cute and appealing art, polished interface, catchy music, etc. But the truth is that Undermine doesn't bring anything new or even interesting to the table. Many other games did the same gameplay loop much better, either with more interesting mechanics or more compelling randomization.Even worse, this game pads out and tries to hide its barebones gameplay with the grind of the meta progression: all of the progression costs a hefty amount for what you can reasonably gather in a run, and of course you need it because by the 3th and 4th dungeons the enemies start hitting like a freight train. And therefore you'll have to run the initial dungeons over and over, engaging with the repetitive, uninspired and limited combat. As I mentioned in the 2nd paragraph, despite its aparent well polished aesthetic, once you get past that veil of lies you'll see the souless core whitin.If you're young or new to roguelites then yeah sure give this a try and honestly I won't blame you if you have fun with it. But for the veterans like myself I can safely say to skip this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Watching someone play this on youtube, and remembering those bootleg ads you'd see for this game eventually convinced me to get it. Its still in its development phase, and has a whole new dungeon and boss coming to it.  This is easy easier then other rougelikes, like Binding of Isaac and Enter the Gungeon. Good for welcoming someone to the genre without demanding alot of skill from the player.Movement is directional, with the addition of jumping, which functions like gungeon's dash, in that you can't be hurt while jumping. Surprisingly the two main forms of damage, swinging and throwing, work together quite wellGame works well to balance risk and reward, and is a bit more in your face about it. For example, you can pray at an altar to receive a free blessing, (Which gives you a staff buff of your choice) in turn for a curse (A debuff, not of your choice).Its replay-ability relies on you not discovering every relic, blessing, and curse. Beyond that though, the only thing different in each run is the ability to increase the difficulty of the undermine by stat buffs to your enemies. Overall a really solid game. I would definitely recommend this to anyone who wants to get into the rouge-like genre.

_childDocuments_.review: It isn't fun?It markets itself as a quirky, fun rouguelike with a lot of variation. Unfortunately, lack of variation is exactly what kills this game for me, and probably many others.One of the problems this game suffers with the most is that you (effectively) only have two weapons, melee attacks, and a thrown pickaxe. You can upgrade those, kinda, but those are the only weapons you will ever get, compared to many other Roguelikes with hosts of unique guns or swords or whatever. But it gets worse - You really only have one weapon, because attempting melee astronomically increases the chance of taking damage, and in this game, where healing is sparce, you can't take that risk. This leads to only throwing your boomerang-pickaxe, and constantly spamming the throw button as you frantically dodge bullets. Additionally, the rooms are nothing special. They are fairly varied, but only in ways that give you more things to worry about - holes you fall into, water that can be electrocuted, oil that slows you down and sets you on fire, and just random bomb barrels. A good 50% of the damage you take in a run will be ambient room damage, which is really, really annoying. Also, the game is unbearably grindy. Each run, you take all of your money with you into the dungeon (Why? who tf knows), and when  you die, you lose 20-50% of it, the idea being that each run, you get enough new gold to cover the losses of the  gold you just lost, and then you can use that gold to buy permanent upgrades. But, sometimes you just don't. Bad luck might have you die on lvl 1 with 100k gold from you last run where you got to lvl 12 or something, and you lose an astronomical amount of money. And because you constantly lose money, you have to grind the game over, and over, and over, to get literally anything. I had no idea a rougelike could be so grindy.ALSO, another issue is the upgrades. In terms of the relics, 40% of the time, the relic you get is just useless, 55% of the time, the relic you get is just +throw damage or +melee damage, and only in the final 5% of relics is the relic actually interesting or changes your playstyle at all. The +damage relics are incredibly monotonous, too - - More damage for each key you have!- More throw damage!- More damage the lower your health is!- More melee damage the more health you have!- More damage after throwing your pickaxe!- More throw critical damage!Soooo many of the relics are just mindless increases in damage, which really don't make for interesting runs. Anyway. Overall, the game is monotonous and grindy. It is fun to play for the first ~6-10 hours, but rapidly spirals downhill after that. I would not recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: i've played this for a bit, and honestly, its mid compared to the other roguelikes on the marketits not a Bad game, but its not a good enough game for me to want to complete it.i'd say the lack of variety on builds is what makes  this game mid, the relics that are supposed to change your gameplay arent impactful enough, the game feels like its constantly putting you in "power check".if Sho'guul, Opulent Demon(the vendor who gives you cursed relics) appeared more, it would be interesting as he truly gives meaningful cool relics (huge upgrade, huge downside relics)overall, i cant give this game a thumbs down, because it does its job competently well. i'd say its a good entry-level roguelite for anyone who has never have touched the genre before, the art style is decent, the gameplay is decent, the permanent progression is okay. and the game even holds your hand if you die deep in the dungeon (lets say you died at dungeon level 3) the game allows you to restart at level 3, and gives you a few relics to compensate for your lack of power. So for a roguelike this is as forgiving as it gets.7.5/10 make Sho'guul pop up more on my runs.

_childDocuments_.review: Have you played and enjoyed Binding of Issac but found you liked yourself a liiiittle too much? Have you ever thought a game like that should screw you over more by adding pits you can fall into, a melee attack with a boomerang ability that stunts your melee for a while, difficulty spikes and rooms where the moment you enter, you're punched in the face without any chance to react and enemies that try to steal the gold you try to collect every. single. room? Then Undermine is the game for you!The game also teaches you that defeating bosses is overrated as you'll be dying more to these damage sponges than you do to the ones in Enter the Gungeon. That said, those two games did not have the ability to jump which makes a ton of difference in controlling your character.I'm recommending because the game is fun despite the mentioned problems and I keep playing it so it must be doing something right. However, there are still other issues that the developer needs to iron out such as the lack of bomb and key drops in the first level despite needing both for quite a few of those rooms. This was a problem in Enter the Gungeon as well for a while and the rate needs to be increased a little for the first level here too.Game shows promise and being in early access, I hope the issues get worked out so that the game doesn't make you want to drop it in favor of other roguelites.

_childDocuments_.review: Great graphics, but a fundamentally flawed game. While I did play through it, and beat it. I can't see myself playing it any more. While it's a "rouge-like" it actually isn't, while I enjoy rougelikes, this borrows some elements from the genre and doesnt do a good job balancing them together. Ill give a couple examples.It's a game where you have to build up gold per run then to spend on upgrades. The thing is though, its not really possible to beat the game until you've died a bunch of times. So it forces you to rerun it over and over, which is fine for a roguelike, but the problem isn't that you're getting better exactly, you're just playing for long enough to have the game lower it's own difficulty for you. So in that sense, a game like spelunky where you can beat it all the way through in a run, is nice, and in theory something like this seems nice. But then once you're close to beating the end boss and have maxed out all your upgrades, all those lower bosses that were enjoyable boss battles once, just become chores.Lack of clarity for a variety of complex mechanics. I was on a good run recently, I picked up a "curse" bottle. thinking it was something I could drink, or swap out, I went ahead and picked it up, anticipating I might find a "clear 5 curses bottle". upon picking it up, I got like two dozen curses. it basically ended my run right there in the most painful way possible. What the game made seem like a slight debuff was a slap in the face. While roguelikes are painful, and unforgiving, they are at least fair generally. Well, at least the good ones are (which is why I'm saying no on the recommend)Uninspired procedural generation. Collecting gold, running through maps, its all just a huge chore. The game was fun for a little bit, and if you enjoy a grind then get a playthrough out of it, but it's all just so grindy, and unrewarding at the end. I'm kind of left with, why??I hate to say it, because the art is great, and I feel there was a ton of love dumped into that. But unfortunately, amazingly smooth pixel art doesn't translate a quality game. The guy has some great pixel art of his dogs. That's cute and all, but I was left asking myself when seeing those. How many hours went into this art? and how many hours went into game design? I feel like the relics obviously had a ton of game design theory put into them for all the ways they affect mechanics, but then the problem is that it's all just a slot machine. You're just hoping for a lucky run where it drops the right combo of items and doesn't hit you with too many "gotcha" situations for a win. It's a roguelike in the worst ways in that, it's not skill can prevail a bad run, it's that a good run is dependent upon your lucky pickups, and maybe you can win off of that.
