_childDocuments_.review: A lot of people will tell you how great roguelikes like Binding of Isaac, Dead Cells or Hades are and while I agree that those are great games, the one I always liked the most was Undermine. I think the reason I liked this game the most was because it wasn't overly complicated and had the core concept nailed down perfectly.Undermine is inspired by The Legend of Zelda and it shows in its gameplay. You play as a poor peasant who was forced along with many of his colleagues to get down a mine, investigate what is going on there and retrieve seal stones to deal with an evil god. A lot of stuff to handle for a poor overworked peasant. The gameplay of Undermine is easy to understand and never gets too crazy. You have a pickaxe which is your main weapon. You can swing it around like a sword or you can throw it like a boomerang. That way you have both a melee attack and a ranged attack which you can use however you want. You also can place bombs if you have any and those deal a lot of damage, unfortunately to you too. Bombs can also break stones and reveal secrets rooms if you bomb the right wall. You will also carry a small familiar with you, you start with a canary bird that collects gold for you but you can get other pets later. Each pet has three levels and on each level it gets a useful effect for you. You level up those pets during your run, each pet has a different method to get XP and some take very long to level up but have very powerful effects.Everywhere in the mine you can find gold embedded inside walls and rocks, hitting it a few times with your pickaxe will release it across the floor. But be fast to collect it because a neutral enemy type, called the pilfer, will appear if any gold is on the ground. Thiose little slime bastards will grab any free gold they find and escape with it, but a single hit will send them flying away. There are also different pilfer variants, like a bomb variant that drops a bomb if hit and a beefy one that takes more hits and pushes you away on contact. There is even a golden pilfer who will run aimlessy around and try to get away from you but drops a lot of gold if hit.Gold is your currency in the game buy items in shops, each floor has a shop but often the shop is locked behind a door. You can open locked doors and also locked chests with a key but those are rare drops. The shop usually has a selection of keys, bombs, food (which heals you), potions and even relics. The last one are items that give you a passive effect for your run. Relics can have all kinds of effects and can give you buffs for your attacks, your character, your bombs or even duplicate gold and items you find during the run. Some relics can be even combined for better effects. Besides relics, there are also blessings that you can unlock. Those are more simple buffs for your run. They usually affect your stats directly like attack damage, HP, how much gold you find and so on. You get blessings from shrines but using a shrine for a blessing will always give you a curse. Curses are the opposite of blessings and give you a small or big debuff depending on how unlucky you are, those are almost always simple stat reductions and having the mirrored versions of a curse and a blessing will simply negate each other. You can also use shrines to purge a curse but this will damage you and with each purge you take more damage from it.There are also potions which provide a tempory buff or can simply heal you. YOu can carry potions with you and use them at any point but you have a limited amount of slots for them.The general goal of the game is to reach the lowest floor and beat every enemy and every boss that is in your way. Each floor has multiple rooms that are connected together just like in The Legend of Zelda. If there are any enemies inside a room, the doors will close and you can only get out once you have defeated them all. Unlike The Binding of Isaac you cannot bomb open doors. On each floor you will always find a shop and a relic room but there are also secret rooms with additional rewards. You don't have to visit every room but it is advised because that way you get the most gold out of it, even if you take more damage on the way. There is usually plenty of healing, the game is overall more forgiving for a roguelike. The game is divided into multiple zones and each zone is made of four floors. The last floor on a zone will contain a powerful boss that, if you beat him, will give you one of the seals that you need to unlock the final boss. But, surprisingly, you don't have to beat the bosses to win a run. Each floor with a boss has a way to skip the boss entirely. And, if you have beaten the boss for the first time, you never have to beat him on any other runs. YOu can still do it for a gold bonus but once you have beaten him you can just bypass him completely. If you die or beat a run, you return back to the first floor of the mine which acts as your base of operations. Leftover gold you had can e used to buy permanent upgrades but if you died you will loose a god portion of it. You can also find Thorium inside the mine which can be used to unlock more relics, potions and blessings for your runs. There is also a small shop which sells you small items for your next run so you don't start emptyhanded. Investing in all those things will make the game easier over time which makes the game more of a roguelite. But fear not, for those who want a more challenging experience, there is also the Othermine. This part ofg the gameplay is unlocked once you have reached the end of the mine for the first time and offers a more traditional roguelike experience. All your permanent upgrades are deactivated here, only your unlocked items count. The Othermine also has some other rules to make the gameplay more unpredictble and give the player a good challenge. There is no big reward for beating the Othermine, it is simply meant for players who want a more traditional roguelike mode.And, if you want to play daily challenges, this is here too. The game offers "WHIP", a challenge mode flor the main game that adds different muttators to the usual gameplay. Getting high scores on those will also unlock alternative skins for your familiars. It does not affect gameplay in any way and is just meant to entertain the player. I like that about the game, they don't lock any gameplay elements behind harder difficulties and you either get nothing or simply cosmetics.Overall the reason why I love this game so much is because it is easy to understand, easy to get into but still has many good items and synergies that give you interesting runs. This is the type of game that I like to play after a hard day at work to relax, a game where I don't have to think too hard or need all my concentration for.

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly good in the early, mid and late-game. It is only after unlocking all of the content that the game falls short, where other genre-defining roguelikes shine -- the end game. After unlocking all content, you've likely already seen most of the combinations as cycling through 60-70% of the items in a single run is not uncommon, nor is it difficult. This is still a home-run of a game, with remaining opportunities to enrich end-game content with rare encounters and even more difficult enemies (and proportionally epic rewards). The art style is pixel-oriented but still has its own character. The music is charming and appropriate.The extremely early game and extremely end game both could use difficulty tweaks:- early game w/o blessings and w/o familiars or good items seems not very fun (fun measured in this case as discovery and progression in mechanics of the game). Runs tend to be cut extremely short and gold cannot be retained. It is a grind but not a particularly fun grind- Very late game with familars, blessings, items, potions, experience of the game, and upgrades is entirely too easy. As I mentioned before, where the great roguelike titles shine is the ability to maintain a challenging and enticing run after thousands.If you're a fan of Roguelikes, buy this game.Recommended price range: 20-30USDRating (03/05/2020): 4/5
_childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

_childDocuments_.review: You play as one of an endless horde of minions in service of a Wizard, that goes and explores the Undermine. You start with a flimsy, hole-ridden sack, which you can fill with gold in the Undermine. Half of it is lost on your death, the other half is available to invest into permanent upgrades for all of your future minions. Such as throwing range, damage, health, etc. Even the sack gets upgrades, making you lose less gold on deaths.You will mostly fight enemies in melee or ranged, loot chests or mine gold in this game. The attacks can be upgraded in many ways, throwing multiple picks instead of just one, chaining lightning and more. But you'll always fight with your mining pick.There's also bombs, with which to destroy blocks, secret walls, kill minions or even yourself, should you be unlucky.Water can get electric, oil puddles can start burning.There's potions and relics, which are temporary items, and artifacts, which benefit all of your minions. Also look out for the occasional curse or blessing. They can truly turn your adventure into a nightmare, or a cakewalk.All in all, this is an enjoyable little roguelike for an absolutely fair price (I'm looking at you, Triple AAA games).

_childDocuments_.review: Very great game! If you did like Binding of Isaac you will definitely love this one! It's very similar except that you actually keep a progression from your deaths. The more you play the more you get powerful so you can go even deeper and deeper in the dungeon's crawling. The way you build up your character is the same as Isaac. You get random relics with special effects that you lose on death. What you keep from death is all the gold you get. With that gold you can buy permanent power ups. Enough said, ill let you discover the rest of the game. Just buy it and enjoy!

_childDocuments_.review: Not a fan of how the game feels like doing whatever it feels like doing instead of the inputs I press to do a certain action.Like maybe it's just visually incorrect, because it doesn't look like I'm standing in oil, but I still can't jump.Or the game being inconsistent on how far you can jump because sometimes with a running start I'll jump two blocks, and others I'll jump one. So it's this game of wondering if you'll jump 2 blocks away and avoid taking damage, or jump 1 block and take damage which isn't very fun. I don't understand why you would have multiple outcomes for the same key presses. It's like RNG on whether or not you dodge, rather than being unable to jump two blocks if something is in the way, which wasn't the case, ever while I was playing this game.Like that would also be a strategy to stagger your dodge to avoid getting too far away, but this isn't the kind of game where it takes that into account. You're airborne the same amount of time regardless of how far you jump. It doesn't make any sense. The input necessary to jump just one tile is so finicky. Because most of the time I jump what seems to be less than a block, and the hitbox of a spike is more than a block. The game also sometimes decides that I wanted to pick something up, or wanted to click on something, even though I didn't. It just so happens that the action button for interacting is the same as the action button for attacking, or rather defending yourself. So even though you wanted to kill something, you accidentally interacted with something and it ate your swing input and you take a hit or you interacted with a hole and went deeper into the mines or dungeons rather than open a chest that spawned right next to it. Like this game's been out for a while, and man, oh man, did I not miss this kind of game.  The indicators for half the things are nonexistent so it's annoying having to guess rather than predict. Like even an audio indication of where on the screen the worm boss will appear from would've gone a long way, instead it's just mono audio and it could literally appear from anywhere. Like, I don't care if this boss is piss easy and I've already killed it three times in a span of twenty minutes.It's still f*ckin annoying dude.Get it on sale. F*ck the base price.

_childDocuments_.review: Undermine scratched an itch for top-down rouge-like action that i thought my 1000 or so runs in Binding of Isaac had bashed and bled out of me.The story is fun, the premise is interesting and different enough not to be derivative. The artwork is solid and everything looks distinctive; each layer of the mine has its own unique look.The gameplay is fun and there are plenty of different builds although your core combat remains the same.Honestly there's also a lot of future potential for improvements to the game but as it stands it's already great.

_childDocuments_.review: I thought I had found a gem, but I'm really disappointed...When I read about random relics I thought Binding of Isaac, Risk of Rain 1&2, Slay the Spire, Dead Cells, so it was obviously going to be SUPER fun, but no...I'm still rating it positively cause I know it will get better and I just don't want to be negative, but I really wish devs would go in a different design direction.Some of the problems, imo:- You get 4 relics maximum until the first boss (never beat him so don't know after) and they are almost ALL super bad:"Modifying bombs"? Useless. We can't afford to use them for anything else than walls. "More damage at high health"? Almost insignificant. I read damage boosts calculations have been changed, but in terms of relics it doesn't feel impactful."More gold"? We lose so much when dying that it's decent (even after buying the "lose less gold when dying") but still doesn't give my character anything."When gold falls it burns"? What even in the world is that?? How is it going to help me once in front of the boss?? I wanted something like "throw 2 pickaxes", "every swing attacks 2 times", "attacks poison enemies" or some other things that change the gameplay and make a real effect on the player! I read devs talking about "builds" when 1) we don't have ANY control over it, so not really a build and 2) I've NEVER had any relics synergize together. The videos show relics interacting together but it must be in endgame or something cause it never happened to me. I always get stuff like "more gold", "more damage per key", "bombs make fire", "more life"...The best one I found so far was "sometimes creates electricity when hitting", and it doesn't even proc consistently enough for me to feel good about it...Entire runs feel bad and relics are not engaging. We need way more, and way better ones! Devs may want to avoid the "Risk of Rain 2" effect where you get so many relics that you get completely OP (and even like that, it's so well made that it feels super powerful and fun, but you can still die easily) but they should find a middle ground between this and what we have atm...- The consistent freaking slimes appearing when you pop gold are completely useless and having to rush every single time to get my gold ISN'T fun! It simply isn't. The "mini game" doesn't even bring anything to the table. Why? I hate them. SO MUCH.- The controls are SUPER clunky...How am I not able to swing at every direction? Wanting a difficult game is okay, adding false difficulty isn't. Like when you're walking a liiiiiittle bit on the side of a bridge you fall?? Having to always turn around to hit instead of just hitting behind the character and having him turn around?? I play with a controller, and I tried M&K to see if it was better but even the "mouse aim" wasn't good either.- Everything in the hub is way too expensive, and doesn't improve the character enough. I get the point of having to do multiple runs, and I LOVE games like that, but it's just infuriating when I come back from a run and get "more swing damage" but it almost doesn't change anything...Devs should take a look at "Heroes of Hammerwatch" and its hub. When you come back you're so happy cause you buy meaningful improvements for your next runs. Every character empowers the next one so you always want to do another run to go further.- Curses? When you don't even have enough relics and meaningful ones enough too?? Really?! "I lost max health, yaaaaay"...- The first boss is stupidly strong. Can't tell for the others cause I can't beat him...Having to learn patterns is perfectly fine, but having such a clunky character AND having no useful relics AND having to deal with so much damage with a simple pickaxe doing 30 damage a swing isn't, and it's not fun either...I read about the update, and really wanted to check it out, but it appears I'd still need like 10-20 runs to be able to beat the first boss (unless I get good relics...) and it's just not fun anymore. I'll try another time maybe, and hope others may still have fun with the game! I'm having less fun than frustration, and it's the perfect sign to know when you need to stop.

_childDocuments_.review: Sure, it's probably worth 15 bucks.  It's basically a competent binding of isaac style roguelike.Things that are different from BoI:-melee focus, and you can throw your melee weapon like a boomerang, instead of always ranged attacks.-Progression is not just unlocked options (which are unlocked by crafting them, not just by discovery), but base stat increases between runs-expanded use of environmental effects (more than just those jumping things changing to fire - Undermine also has slimes that can become tar, then fire, or whatever, or throwing your pick through a brazier lights the pick on fire or lights the brazier if the pick is already on fire and the brazier is not)There are a few areas that it could improve, so if you are concerned about these, either wait or skip this one - there are a ton of great options in this genre:-has random relics, but they aren't even a little bit close to the level of crazy combos that you'd see in Isaac, at least so far as I've seen in the first 2 hours.  They're all pretty equivalent, and none make you feel powerful, just very minorly buffed (e.g. do 30 damage instead of 28).  There are a few slightly more interesting ones that offer utility (duplicating money or food, ignoring oil and leaving oil drops when you jump, bouncing ranged attack - which only works with launching, not when returning, making it feel mediocre), but even at their best, relics feel supplemental, not game defining.  And in any given run, I've never found more than 1 interesting utility relic.   But maybe I just haven't seen the Brimstone or Dr. Fetus style uber-relics yet.  But more likely, if crazy relics exist at all, they're blueprints that you'll need to complete tons of the game before they become available.-Mouse aiming support seems pretty bad at launch.  I'd recommend playing with a controller or keyboard only for now at least.  It seems like the mouse aiming might only work if you aren't moving or something?  I dunno, but I clicked enemies, but swung in completely different directions, so I ditched the mouse after like 2 rooms.-bosses feel.. grindy.  I only faced the first one so far, but I never felt like "oh, I can probably do this!"... It was "oh, I guess I need to go get more upgrades, because I can't get this thing below half HP, even if I stay alive for 5 minutes".  It felt like I needed to do like 30+ runs of the first 5 levels before I would even have a chance at defeating the first boss (I'm bad at games).  So yeah, if you're bad at games like me, this game could get to be a serious grindfest, and you might never see the later content, depending on when the upgrades cap.Still, that said, the 2 hours I've played so far have been fun enough to make me want to play it some more, so it's probably worth the asking price if you like the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

_childDocuments_.review: Heigh-ho! Heigh-ho! It's off to die we go!Check out my video if you want to see gameplay. UnderMine is what would happen if The Legend of Zelda - Link's Awakening was a roguelike with simplified puzzles and a boomerang that could deal damage. You play as a revolving door of miners collecting gold and treasure until they die, at which point the door turns, another walks in, and only you and the game counter are aware of how many miners have already died. Each new miner takes half of the previous miner's gold and moves on with any upgrades unlocked, but each will discover new relics as they dive into the mine. The combination makes for a good variety of what you've paid to unlock along with what you stumble across. You'll also rescue townspeople as you dive deeper, so the sense of progression is ever-present.Normally I would include some negatives in my review, but really my only complaint is that it didn't capture me as much as it's captured others. Which is a shame, because having a boomerang that deals damage felt amazing, especially when I found a relic that splits it into three boomerangs. Er, thrown boomerang pickaxes. Same thing, really. So pick up UnderMine. Odds are either you or someone you know will enjoy it.

_childDocuments_.review: Though I currently have 13 hours logged, probably about 6 of those are actually idle time.The game starts off fun enough, but it doesn't hold up as you progress. The overall premise is somewhat dark, as every character you play inevitably dies — there's no returning from the dungeon. The familiar carries back some portion of your gold, which you can then use to unlock upgrades. However, this can become a slog in certain areas; since you can't control what powers you go into the dungeon with (everything is randomized), you can't plan a strategy until you're already in the room, making it difficult to judge preparations. Even when unlocking items, you can't select them on future runs -- you have to run into them randomly. This can lead to a cycle of entering the dungeon, mining gold as much as possible, then dying without actually progressing in the game, sometimes without even getting a chance to use the item you just invested in.There are a lot of neat environmental variables, but that's not enough for me to recommend this particular game.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish there was a 3-star/middle option, because this game is simply not made for beginners. It has really cute art, fun sense of humor, everything works well, but there is no difficulty slider. The cuteness factor was what drew me to this game, and I love mining games like Steamworld Dig. I wasn't expecting the difficulty to ramp up so quickly before you have a chance to get upgrades. The minions running around the first few levels are very easy to defeat, and then the first boss is such a jump up in difficulty that I can't get past it. I'm assuming I'm not the target market for this game. But if you are like me and interested in it because of the cute art and mining premise, just know going in that this is a very skill-based game with absolutely no learning curve or difficulty setting. If you were attracted to this because you like Starbound, Terraria, Steamworld Dig, Graveyard Keeper, Forager, etc. This game is *much* harder and meant for experienced players only. But I'm sure those players have a ton of fun with it.

_childDocuments_.review: There's not a "mixed review" option, but the game is fun, it's well polished, it's not bad, it's just another game rogue-like following this tired formula where at the end of a run the items might make you 10-30% stronger and can be ignored for the most part. And for that reason, it will get the brunt of my complaints on where this genre has been heading in general.The developer intends for you to find fun in your motor skills subconsciously adapting to the boss's attack patterns, knowing if they introduced an item that gave you any real advantage at all it would let you bypass this  game-play mechanic. As a result the developers keep a tight lock-down on how "fun" an item is allowed to be. This is all by design, no mistakes.Common red flag for these games: if there's a "level skip" option, it means it's viable to skip floors, and power-ups. But you shouldn't  to skip power-ups, ideally the later floors should be  on the power-ups you get. Otherwise, there's no weight to the items. I find myself skipping shops and power-up rooms because I just didn't care, with virtually no impact on how far I got in the dungeon before dying to an enemy who's attack patterns are unknown, leaving behind a game that is "just OK". No dopamine hits from finding that insanely broken item, just a slow grind in a pretty linear basic game.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing for a while and giving this game chance after chance after chance, I just can't recommend it.But before I get into the review, I will mention that I am a completitionist. Always looking for secrets, always looking to complete the loogbook/Bestiary/unlock every item. Always trying to get all of the achievements, or at least as many as I can. So that said, I'm gonna get into it.It's a long review, so TL;DR at the endCONS:1.) First of all, game can be a grindy to get into. You can have quite a slow start. You are very underpowered, and everything is very crazy and damaging. From a tiny little fly that hits you with one projectile that deals 20 damage, or a bat that flies erratically and has decent range with the attack that does 30 damage, it can get overwhelming. Considering you basically never get health drops naturally, and the usual health item you get heals you for 20, it can get difficult.It wouldn't be so bad however, if the rooms weren't literally filled to the brim with these enemies that are never in sync. You can enter one room and your run is just done. I do not find the enemies -that- difficult anymore, but there are rooms that still end my runs if I'm playing with various challenges enabled (which I will get into later)You also need to collect gold. Which I really liked at the start. But your gold can get taken away if it's on the ground. After a while it gets annoying.You also need that gold for the items you want to buy in the shop during your run, but you also need the gold to buy permanent upgrades in the lobby area. And it makes the game EXTREMELY grindy at the start. You will never have a good run in the beginning because you will probably be saving up for the perma upgrade, where you wont even be able to afford 2 keyes that you need for two rooms that are locked.Now, I don't have issue with grinding. I love grinding. But even for me it was a bit on a tedious side at the start, so I'm putting it into negative, just because I know grinding isn't something people look forward to on average.2.) The enemy design and the enemy "interaction" is quite badAttacks are poorly telegraphed, with basically instant attack as well. Some enemies can be very hard to read and very unpredictable. And the attack/movement pattern and enemy ability just feels cheap at times. The hitboxes are absolutely horrendous though. There are some enemies that begin their attack and damage you before they actually finish their previous attack or start the new one. There is a berserking enemy "Bobo" who runs, then slams into the wall and slams his fist into the ground 3 times. You can be above him hitting him with your pickaxe, but he will suddenly hit you even if he didn't start his charge animation yet and is still in the animation of slamming his fists into the ground3.) Secrets are very convoluted. There are a lot that you can figure out on your own, but there are a lot of them where you just have to go look it up on the wiki. Which is not a big deal if you don't care, but this game is about exploring, unlocking new stuff, getting new items and all that, so having very confusing secrets with specific things you need to do, without having any hints in the game, really takes away from it4.) Meta game is too strong. Basically, if you don't make a ranged build, you will have 10x harder time getting through the game. Melee does more damage, but it's risky. especially early in your save file. Because it doesn't do enough to kill the enemies fast, so you just put yourself in danger of stupid enemies and wonky hitboxes. Later on in your save file you can destroy enemies with melee, but you can do so with range as well, from safety.And basically, whenever I had a melee build, I saw no reason not to use range, or not to go for range. I never see a benefit, although I use melee build to make the game a bit more engaging. There are also very good ranged items you can get, while melee items are "okay" in general, not really comparable with the items for the ranged build.So there is literally no reason for you to go melee if you have even a slightest choice5.) Bosses are BAD.There are 2 alright bosses (just looking at the base design), but most are just... no. I am used to them now so I don't really struggle, but I still think the design from the gameplay point is horrendous. And there is one boss I still despise and struggle with at times and it gets the spot on top 3 of the worst bosses in games I have played. They can be so tedious to fight. They can chunk your health but tank your damage, some spawning ads constantly, some having overlapping attacks, some just having undodgeable attacks. Oh, did I mention BROKEN HITBOXES??6.) The "challenge" I previously mentioned. Now, these are mostly optional. But with a game like this, you want to get your unlocks. And you might be a completitionist like me as well.The extra challenges are unbalanced and even grindierLets start from a normal game progression. Each time you defeat all 5 bosses in ONE RUN you get a new difficulty modifier, whilst before you could skip bosses and come back to them later. Now you need to kill all 5 bosses in one run (there are 6 bosses in total), which makes the game even more repetitive. If you want to get the difficulty modifier, you are forced to kill every boss in one run now. But okay, whatever! Game gets easy after a while so having a natural difficulty modifier is good, even though you're forced to get it one way now. But it gets insane after a while. The bosses get even tankier and can now 2 hit kill you, with their attacks being even faster and overlapping even more than before.-----OthermineOthermine is the game's completely roguelike mode. No perma upgrades. You start fresh, you die, and you repeat. it's very slow, it's very grindy, it's uninspired. The game forces you to take curses as well (negative modifiers) which I just hate. There is also a challenge in Othermine where you need to take the item that gives you a major curse every single floor that you can't remove. And those major curses can be very bad on their own. But now, by the end, you'll have 12 of them- There are also hexes you can take. Yet another way to add challenge and modify your game. And honestly, 90% of them are nonsense and I don't even see why anyone would play with them when not trying to get the related achievementsPROS:1.) I said that the game can be very grindy at the start, but it can be rewarding at times if you get a good run and progress. And maybe you like the grind as wellAfter you start unlocking more stuff and progressing a bit further, that's when the game is most fun. The enemies are still bad, but you are decently equiped to not feel it as much, but you're also not overpowered yet to breeze through everything. There is still challenge, but the bad things are mitigated2.) The curse/blessing system is a nice way to have risk versus reward in the game and I think it's done nicely overall (except in the scenarios I mentioned previously)3.) Pixel art and sound design are greatI don't know how to describe it, but the pixel art is very crispy, and the sound is very addictive. The clinks of the items dropping after you clear a room, gold plopping on the ground. That part is very nicely doneAlthough the rooms can get very cluttered at times, the art is still niceTL;DR:Very grindy at the beginning Bad enemy design, bad hitboxes, bad rooms filled with enemies and traps that do surprising amount of damage for early game. Bosses are bad as well; poorly telegraphed attacks, overlapping attacks, spammy attacks tanky health. "Challenge" and challenge modes, although optional, are cheaply made. Game can be rewarding though after the beginning and before later difficulty, and the pixel art and sound design are wonderful. But it's not enough to outweigh the negatives

_childDocuments_.review: Purchased for $14 AUD. Played on an Intel i7 10700K with an RTX 3080 and 32GB RAM. Performance and PFS was exceptional.Undermine caught my eye because of the art style, which is just gorgeous. I'm not really that into rogue-likes, but the trailer was good and the gameplay looked enjoyable. When I first started playing, I'll be honest, it was a big bummer to keep dying over and over, and I felt like I wasn't getting anywhere. I'd usually just do one run, then play something else and come back to it later. After a while though, because I was slowly getting more and more familiar with the game and because I was very slowly buying upgrades, it became far more enjoyable. I was dying less, earning more gold and getting further and further into the mines. Once you start finding altars in the game is where it really started getting fun for me. The boss fights were pretty sweet. Challenging enough and their mechanics were good, especially once you figured them out. The final boss was definitely the hardest, in my opinion. As it should be I suppose!Overall, I had a great time playing this game, especially once I got familiar with it. If you're feeling a bit like I was in the early stages....give it a bit more time, as it gets better!I finished the story and got all the upgrades within about 32 hours. If you're into rogue-likes, or even if you just like the art, I recommend giving this game a try.

_childDocuments_.review: This was a total disappointment for me as I had high expectations of Undermine.  I thought it was going to be a Zelda similar game, but I was way wrong.  I played 2.4 hours and I suspected it was going to be a game of lopsided random luck.  Since I missed the 2 hour mark...too badThe goods-  I like the RPG style dungeon with the subtle hints of the hidden areas.  That's about it.The Bad- I don't like starting over after each time you die.  You lose all relics.I don't like you have to start from the first floor to have the advantage.  when you start at the beginning you have a chance to get more relics making the lower levels a bit easier.  It gets boring doing the same level 8 freakin' times over and over and over and over....(get the point?)I don't like the randomness and luck to get keys and bombs.  I clear three areas in the game and I can't find one familiar.  Unlike Zelda you could use your bombs and keys to experiment, you can always get more.  Undermine you can't leave to resupply.  Maybe the familiars are hidden under stone or in chests that I never have enough keys.  There are times I may have 12 bombs and no keys or vice versus. Isn't this game already difficult enough to worry about this nuisance ?  I guess you can only have the blacksmith craft one item per run?  Didn't know that until a pilferer show up and I can't pick up the item.I don't like luck determines how much you can explore each level to find the hidden items.  Depending on how the room is configured, you may be able to tell if something is out of place.I don't like the slow progress doing levels over and over and over....(see where this is going?)Overall- I don't like this game!  Repetitive, frustratingly hard and boring.  Lighting my farts on fire is more interesting...

_childDocuments_.review: Heartily recommended. This is a lot of fun for the price, and really there's a huge amount of replayability...but there *could* be more.There's three things I'd have really liked to see in this game. First of all, a 'permanent' artifact system - a character you can add to the hub that lets you select a known artifact to play with at the start of a run. Something that unlocks after beating the game once, or some such.Secondly, I'd love to see physical changes to the peasant based on artifact combinations. I'm sure a lot of people have mentioned something like this, but...say you get all the armor pieces in a run, maybe you then turn into a knight, or something. Maybe if you get a bunch of holy stuff, you turn into an angel, maybe an archer if you get enough specialized throw stuff...who knows. Thirdly, after seeing the bog, I want more branching paths with special unlock conditions. How about Som's Workshop as an area? How about those woods that get mentioned frequently in the bestiary? How about an 'escape', where you take alternate routes all the way to the end, and your peasant leaves the mine instead of dying at the end? (yeah I know, kill Din to do that, but still). Or, maybe...how about journeying into the lost city, *after* beating Sear? Perhaps have a mechanic that allows you to present something to Death's Hand, such that the way into the city is opened...I'd love to see any of these things, and I think there's a lot more potential to expand this game, still. Regardless, it's a very good game as-is, and I recommend it!

_childDocuments_.review: Undermine is a fantastic roguelite game that gives you a great deal of variety in its procedurally-generated aspects, a charming visual style, and a difficulty that is less frustrating and more encouraging than most roguelites. I'm pretty terrible at this style of game, but I found this one to not be too unforgiving and actually very fun despite the repetitiveness that you might expect of this genre. The "relic" power-ups, as well as the blessings and curses give an incredible variety to the gameplay, and just when you think you've discovered everything in an area you discover a new secret or strategy to help you move forward.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, if you're reading these reviews, you've probably already vetted this game half-way decently enough to know its worth trying.  Its a nice little mix up of Stardew (without the farming, mostly the mining/fighting), Zelda elements that make me want to love it (yes the bombs being necessary to blow open walls to secret rooms is nostalgic as hell, sue me), and Rouge-elements that randomize each run-through, with more than enough variety in artifacts and other equipment to 'find' and 'REfind' each run, that it really is unique each dive.I normally get VERY critical of anything 'rogue'-like/lite, because I DESPISE randomness, and the more options remind me of despairingly bad board/card/deck-building games where you get ♥♥♥♥♥♥ hands and have no option but to suffer the rest of the game, basically knowing you'll lose after seeing your first deal/starting position.  THIS IS NOT REALLY TRUE WITH THIS GAME, I am HAPPY to confirm.The randomness actually adds to the diversity of the game, and has kept me playing for a good 30+ hours so far with only 80% of the dungeon explored, so I'd say that is $15 WELL SPENT!  (Found an early release copy still available, which others may be able to as well with a little effort...)  If you like any of the aforementioned games, or any of my ramblings, I'd say give it a shot.  Even at the base $20 price, its probably better than 3/4 of the Indie crap out there right now, and from me, that's sayin something!  GL/HF/GG

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent action roguelite.  It's pretty hard.  You will die a lot.  It has a great system where you can save the gold you earn during each run and use it on permanent upgrades, or you can spend it at the shop-keeper, which can be found on most levels and others at the main hub. You can buy health, keys, bombs, a wide variety of randomized potions, (usually not more than 1 available), or buff your character by purchasing/finding relics.  If you like the graphics of Link's Awakening, (SNES), you will find this game gorgeous.  Audio is low-key/unobtrusive.  It serves it's purpose, but it won't make you say "wow".  The same can be said about the story.  Gameplay is fun, but slightly repetitive, clear a room, move to the next room, clear that room, rinse and repeat.  Enemy variety is low at first, but after you beat bosses, you'll find new encounters on levels they weren't on before.  This is refreshing.  20 hours in, I have only beat the first 2 bosses, but I will be back for more.  Highly recommended!

_childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

_childDocuments_.review: Would you like a roguelike where, as you descend down the dungeon, you get weaker and weaker as the run goes on? Then this game is for you. You can get such curses as plants, torches, and rocks firing poison, fire and missiles so that every room you enter is a tedium to clear out. You can get curses that cause the artifact that you were about to pick up to be destroyed before you get there. Or if that's not your speed, you can get a curse that makes you lose max health every enemy you kill for the entire run. How about a curse that makes it so the healing items you get poison you? There's even curses that eventually build up to the point where you have to hit the enemies 4 times as much just to kill it. This might not be so bad if it weren't for the fact that curses are EVERYWHERE. Last run I accumulated around 40 curses in about an hour and a half of play. The artifacts you pick up tend to be unimpressive, not fun, and don't even come close to offsetting all these negatives.The worst part is the combat isn't even fun, and everything feels slow and awkward. The graphics are also rather ugly. How this game got such good reviews is beyond me.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're like me, you're bored with the 100+ other games in your steam library and are looking for a new game to sink some time into. You're looking for a game that offers an RPG element with lots of ways to upgrade your character/equipment and will keep you hooked for hours. Well, my friend, your search is over.I've really enjoyed the limited time I've spent on this game. It's very similar to Rogue Legacy; spawn, gather as much gold as you can before your inevitable death, purchase upgrades that help you get farther and repeat. That may sound boring but this game also has other elements that make you want to keep hurling the seemingly endless population of peasants down that mine. There's a main "hub" that you spawn in at the beginning of each run. As you delve further and further in the mine, you will come across NPCs that, when rescued, will set up in the hub and offer upgrades. One of those NPCs is blacksmith who will craft various Relics when you find the blueprints for them. To me, the Relics really make each run more fun. Want to add lightning, fire and poison damage to your melee attacks while stealing life with every hit and causing enemies to drop food on death? There's a Relic for that. You also end up with an Alchemist and a Priestess once you get far enough.It's tough to explain, but even after I make it so far with 15+ Relics under my belt only to die, I just want to keep going. Maybe it's the completionist in me that wants to unlock ALL the upgrades. Maybe it's wanting to find out what's at the bottom of the mine (still haven't made it that far). Maybe it's the fact that this game is still Early Access and I'm excited to see the future content. Not bad for $13If you enjoy games like Hero Siege, Rogue Legacy and Hammerwatch, smash that "Add to Cart" button. You won't be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: I love roguelites, and this one is fine by all means. _childDocuments_.review: UnderMine is a great game! It reminds me of Spelunky + Binding of Isaac + Hero Siege (an indie game on steam that used to be amazing until they changed the core physics.) If you like dungeon crawlers, getting money to upgrade better equipment and fighting/exploration with lots of RNG - this game is for you!The devs of this game seem like they're wonderful, and take feedback from players seriously. I love devs that are inspired by other games because that's how you know that it's going to be cared for (WELL.. most of the time.) That is another reason I bought this game. Being in early access, I haven't ran into ANY issues with the game ... at all.However, the game lacks some content. There are lots of things you can do in this game, so don't let me scare you saying that. Again, the lack of content is only a minor flaw and the devs just released a roadmap for this game that plans to add a lot more before 2020 comes. See Link. At times the game is a bit frustrating and grindy, due to how much gold you  earn, and how you lose a lot of gold when you die (you can upgrade the amount of gold you lose on death, the problem is it gets very expensive - very quickly.) I loooove grinding for things, but sometimes when you die in a very cheap way it can really offset your mood.Another problem with the game that actually really annoys me is the fact that you aren't sure what's permanent and what isn't until the item is in your journal. Relics that are used on your run look the same as items that are permanent inside of the journal. Sometimes I'm not sure if something is worth wasting gold on if it's a one time use. The blacksmith is a bit confusing to use too, because you have to craft the item, and then you get to use it for a one time free charge on your run that you buy it on. I feel like there needs to be more clarification here. I guess you get to buy the item in shops after crafting it?One more problem with the game that I could find is that the relics you pick up can sometimes be very underwhelming. Maybe it's just because they need to add more, which they will. And every time you die your character is carried over by a relation with the same upgrades and things. BUT, it would be fun to be able to choose a random stat every time you die (which shouldn't be permanent if that is added to the game.)Don't get me wrong though, I love this game. And if you love something you have to sometimes critique it. But all in all, you should pick up this game. The price point is very fair and it's a great quality game with great pixel graphics and mostly fun mechanics. I've been waiting for another type of Spelunky game!I have to stop here, as I have some grinding to do!

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly stale, shallow, slow and cumbersome roguelike.  Probably one of the most mind-numbingly uninspired and clunky roguelikes I've ever played.  There's also performance issues.  After running into "Missing Loc!" errors (which required 4 reinstalls of the game for it to go away), there were the "bog-down" slo-motion moments.  There's no reason this game, with these graphics, should get any kind of slowdown on any machine made in the last ten years.  Basically, on any map zones with more than 5 moving sprites at a time, it would drop to almost half gameplay speed.  There is no reason this should happen on an 5th gen i5 & 8GB RAM.To those who said this is anything like Wizard of Legend, you need to get your head examined.  Wizard of Legend is a fast, dynamic roguelike with responsive and precise controls and plenty of depth to its gameplay.  With WoL, I always felt like I could change my styles depending on the type of run I was trying to do.  UnderMine is just a bland slog that feels more like a monotonous chore than anything resembling fun.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best Rogue-likes I've ever played. The design and general game play is simple enough and enjoyable to master. The pets are a nice addition to the game play and can change things up based on your play style. Each relic and curse have been thought out and adds an interesting degree of variety to each run. _childDocuments_.review: Pretty amazing game, actual challenge that feels rewarding to overcome, good mix of randomness and skill involved, weighing risks, making the best of the hand you're dealt, gradual progress through more and more runs, item effects are pretty intuitive, secrets to discover, exactly what one is usually looking for in a roguelite. Some nitpicks: - The only difference in starting loadout comes when you buy the starting blessing or unlock the hub shop, which makes the early runs very same-ish. - Most relics don't alter the playstyle in any way, especially combat upgrades oftentimes don't do much, with some exceptions (ricochet is amazing, aegis is strong, this craftale crown), so the most important items to get are usually the ones that help you with healing. This does diminish replayability a bit when compared to genre staples like Isaac. - Many of the crafted items are underwhelming, including some you get from bosses, so for many of them I opted to just not craft them in order to not have them in my item pool.
_childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

_childDocuments_.review: After playing nonstop The Binding of Isaac, I was in search of a game that had a similar feeling to it (not just by being a rogue game). Then, after watching a couple of people playing Undermine, I knew I was gonna love it! Undermine is an amazing rogue like game, despite being on the easy difficult side in my opinion. Initially, the game is kinda bland with few options of power ups, but, as you progress and unlock new stuff, it keeps getting better and better. New combinations of relics and blessings, along with the curse system, gives the game a certain "gamble" feeling, which is good, because every run can be sorta different from the ones before and if you are greed, the game CAN become quite hard (depends on your luck as well). In general, there's just two negative points I would like to talk about: first, the lack of "mid-bosses". It can get quite repetitive with only 5 bosses on each run (excluding the final one). The addition of mid-bosses would make it more challenging and diverse. The second one, is the final boss itself, which I thought was... forgettable.  In general, if you love rogue like games, I strongly recommend this game! And let's hope future updates will bring us more content and dangers!

_childDocuments_.review: A solid action-roguelike with a few minor missteps. If you're sick of Binding of Isaak, Hades and Enter the Gungeon and want more of the same with slightly different flavor you'll have a good time here.The most unique mechanic on display here is the upgrade system. Some percentage of your gold is preserved on death, and that gold can be used to purchase permanent upgrades in the lobby between games. Whatever is unspent is carried into the next run. This is both kind of fun and intensely irritating since some of the more expensive upgrades require multiple good runs in a row in order to farm enough gold for them, and once you're able to play at that level they become mostly pointless. The game's still in EA though so I assume another zone will be added or the numbers will be massaged to make the lategame unlocks a bit less boring.The only other major complaint I have is that once you beat the game normally a true roguelike mode is unlocked, yet in order to play it you have to spend a currency that only drops when you unlock a new item in the hub. Hopefully this gets changed because this mode is brutal and easily the funnest part of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: So, overall, if you enjoy games like Enter the Gungeon or the Binding of Isaac, then you'll likely enjoy this game as well. That being said, this game has it's fair share of problems, and I'll elaborate on that below. Don't let the feedback below stop you from buying this game. It's very solid. However, the balancing issues and lack of depth are reasonably frustrating in this game, so be ready for that.(New biggest issue is item unlocks. I have had 999 thorium for 10+ hours, and I have dozens of items I've yet to find blueprints for. Blueprints give you the option to spend your special currency to see new items. Despite maxing out my special currency long ago, I still don't have these items unlocked. The developers NEED to let players find more blueprints to spend their hard earned thorium.A simple fix would be that each time you beat a boss again, the chest gives you a guaranteed blueprint. As is, it takes literally hundreds of hours to get lucky for the thorium chests. The devs have a lot of their gameplay locked away, and for no good reason imo. This would give incentives for getting the ascension stone high ranked, and it would let the new items come in at the same rate as you can spend your thorium. I'm not a gamedev, but this seems like an easy solution to implement.)First, certain items will kill you(Since the time of my review, most of these kinds of issues have been fixed. However, certain relics are still detrimental and not worth taking, EG, Karmic Scale.)This isn't the only item that gets you killed, but it's the most pressing example that comes to mind. Several of the upgrades offer so little benefit and so much visual clutter that they actually hamper the player rather than helping them. The synergies between items are multiplicative in nature only; they don't actually synergize. It's simple compounding bonuses like attack speed and damage.Yes, they synergize, but that doesn't really effect gameplay. It just allows you to maintain the core pickaxe swinging and throwing against stronger enemies.(This complaint has sort of been tackled. Some items have been added that do change gameplay a good bit. I simply haven't seen or obtained them yet after beating all three bosses 10+ times.)This isn't the only set of issues with the game either. The grinding between the floors is draining after a while. You can skip floors, but it's purely to your detriment. You are putting yourself at a massive disadvantage, and you need those items to compete with the enemies on later floors. Otherwise, you'll run into a particularly nasty combination of traps, hazards, and baddies before getting blended up like a meat smoothie.(Still not fixed, but they've worked on a few of the other issues. More variety in the floors has helped a bit here, but this is still a problem.)There's another issue. Some rooms are instant death if you don't have the right items. I know what you're thinking. "Dude, just get good! XD." Trust me when I say I'm not the kind of guy to blame the game for my own mistakes. Most of the dark souls series is hard yet fair. Same with Enter the Gungeon or the Binding of Isasc. The issue here comes with how the enemies and traps interact.In some floors, you'll face these very fat, tanky gargoyles. If you don't finish them off, they turn to stone and heal. They also shoot out walls of fire in the same pattern that a rook is allowed to move in chess. I faced two of them along with a few other enemies. The field was pure oil. Nearly 100% of it. On oil, you're slowed and you can't jump. To give you a frame of reference, this is like robbing you of the ability to roll in Dark Souls. Just like rolling in Dark Souls, most of Undermine's skill and depth is from jumping. Without it, you're dead in the water....Or oil in this case.Terrible puns aside, the gargoyles set the entire oil pit on fire, restricting me to a tiny piece not covered by oil. They then used their AOE attacks to force me from safety. Boom. I'm running through fire, swinging for my life, and my life bar is rapidly depleting. I'm attacking as quickly as I can with the range attack, yet it's just not enough DPS. These fat bastards are soooooo tanky, it takes about 10 seconds of dpsing them to take them down.Then they start to heal once the turn to stone.I think you get the idea. I had an amazing build that run. Full health. High deeps. Massive sustain. It was all made irrelevant because I didn't have...wait for it...the goloshes I mentioned earlier. It was so ironic because I found some and didn't pick them up because they killed me the run before. Hah. Hah. HAH.Maddening laughter aside, I gotta say, this game's addicting, but these issues are debilitating. Go into this expecting persistent frustration with the balancing.(This is not as much the case as before due to the better ability to get a LOT of damage. Getting that damage takes quite a bit of a grind though.)♥♥♥♥ it, I'll keep going.The blue-purple chests are NEVER worth picking up. They give you curse and items. It's rare they give you something useful, and the curses in this game act as negative modifiers. They tend to outweigh the equilivent positive blessings, and these chests in particular rarely give you a permanent buff. A permanent debuff for some generic items is just...so bad.(This has been fixed for the most part. The devs added rebalancing for curse mechanics in general. This has made the game some more replayability simply because it has given each run more variability. Nice one devs.)The story robs you of agency as well. It's designed around the concept of you being a pathetic, idiotic, easily manipulated peasant. You're sent down into a mine with the poorest possible equipment, and they expect you to kill elemental golems with a rusty pickaxe. When you do, guess what? They STILL mock you. There's no enhancement of your reputation, or perhaps a building up of your esteem. They game goes out of its way to make it crystal clear that you're a pitiful scumbucket that's being sent to his death.Even this many hours into the game, there's been no shift in that narrative feel. My character is still scrounging for scraps, and these rich ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ are lording over me. Over and over and over again. Come on man, give the poor peasants a break. He killed a shadow demon, an insect queen, and an overcharged lightning golem with a pickaxe. That's badass. Let me, as the guy playing the game, feel badass over doing that. But no,as the player, you're not given that satisfaction. Instead, it's made abundantly clear that you're still a peasant. I get it. I'm at the bottom, that's never going to change, and there's nothing I can do about it. I get enough of that from real life. I don't understand why I would want anymore of that from a video game.So to sum it up, yeah, the game had pretty solid game play. It has some pretty bad balancing issues(Mostly fixed, though a few sore spots here or there), itemization is pretty bland(Getting better), and the story beats you down instead of building you up(Could be fixed later, but hasn't been at all). You wanna feel like a peasant being sent to his death, yet overcoming the odds and prevailing? This isn't the game for you. In this game, you're a peasant. You will be addressed as such.Sit down, be quiet, and do as you're told. To the pits and to death, that's all that awaits you. And a bit of fun I suppose.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm about half way through the game (seem the boss of location 3 a few times).  I've had a good time so far and feel like I got my money's worth, but don't have the desire to continue, because it's already getting stale. My main problem is that the game feels pretty grindy and that the runs don't feel different enough.There are two currencies, gold and Thorium. You can spend gold on food and relics in the shops mid-run and on permanent upgrades between runs. Thorium is used between runs to unlock new relics and such.I don't mind progression between runs, but I really wish you didn't have to spend gold on upgrades, because the progression between runs already feels quite slow. The fact that you have to make the choice whether to spend gold mid-run or in between runs makes the slow progression even more annoying, because in the long run it's probably a better idea to save up your gold, which means your current run has less potential. It's a balancing act between risks and rewards, but ultimately feels like an artificial way of lengthening the game. The early game feels unnecessarily tedious (grindy + small relic pool) as a result. I do like the risk-reward decisions when it comes to blessings and curses, because this choice only effect the current run in most cases.The unlocks and upgrades are not that interesting imo. Very few relics are actual game changers and a lot of relics look and act similar, like the different bombs or boots. The same can be said for the enemies. There is some decent enemy variety, but a lot of enemies are basically reskins of earlier ones, like the different slimes, rats, flies, spiders  etc. It would have been nice to see more enemies that are actually different. The room types and locations also don't offer enough variation to keep things fresh. You do encounter some new enemies and traps in later locations, but that's about it. It doesn't really change your playstyle.It's a decent game, but the dev could have done more with the roguelite elements. The core gameplay is fine but there's not enough variation to keep me interested long term. I might come back someday to finish the game, but have seen enough for now.

_childDocuments_.review: The game was enjoyable when it first came out, then the updates started to hit. First 2 new zones were great, the last boss was decent as well. Pilfer's have always been my most hated thing in this game. The fact that it's ALWAYS a race whenever you destroy gold gold node as these green little annoying things show up and start stealing your gold from the floor if you're not quick enough... So, annoying from the start. They bring in an update that brings this HUGE pilfer that pretty much cannot be knocked away and can still 5-10 lots of the gold on the floor. Even more annoying.THEN they bring in a new thing where you put 100k gold in to a fountain to get a blessing, but don't mention anywhere that you cannot hit a pilfer AT ALL throughout the rest of the run, otherwise the blessing goes, and you can't enter the new zone. Stupid requirement hidden behind a buggy mess. Twice I've paid the 100k, twice I've accidentally had something hit a pilfer (Second time was through my gold exploding and hitting it), and it's IMPOSSIBLE TO RESET after it happens, meaning 100k is literally just gone..100k is about what you can get per run. Runs consists of 45 minutes to an hour and you average about 150-200k if you're lucky, or 100-150k if you're not. When something costs a LITERAL run, don't make it seriously easy to lose and impossible to get back as soon as it's lost.Not only did they do this, they also made it so you HAD to kill all 5 bosses in 1 run to be able to go to the higher difficulties. This has just been implemented. You used to, and for a long time were able to kill 4/5 bosses on a lower difficulty, then kill the last one on the highest to move on. Games been out for a while, and this has been a thing up until 1-2 days ago with the new "whip" update (A rubbish once a day thing to try to entice people to come back to the game every day). The new change has made it even more repetitive than it was before.I've put a lot of time in to this game, up until the previous update where the new big pilfer and the pilfer's world came in, and, these last 2 updates have done nothing but make the game a lot more tedious than it used to be. Yes, it's added a few cool relics, but, not many. Not only did it not add many, it nerfed several that were good, because they were good, rather than making the terrible ones much more useful.All in all, with the direction the game is going, I would avoid buying and playing this game, unless you enjoy stressful gameplay, dodgy "dodge" mechanics (It;s literally just jump, which you can't control well), holes that have the sucking power of a black hole and other bugs that have been in-game since it was first implemented, then you'd enjoy this game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a top down Rogue-lite game. A fair comparison is The Binding of Isaac or Enter the Gungeon, though with a bigger focus on melee combat and persistent upgrades. It's in early access, but there are already a few dozen hours of content. If you enjoyed those games, I recommend giving this a try.You play as a peasant who is summoned to rid a dungeon of its monsters, collect treasures you find, and complete quests from a variety of interesting NPC hub-folk. When you die, you play a new peasant while keeping most of the upgrades you attained before.The primary challenge of the game is combat. You have a short range melee attack and a thrown attack. Unlike many games in the genre, you also have the ability to jump. This is useful for dodging attacks and traps, an interesting alternative to a dodge roll or a dash.The monsters are of enough variety to keep the combat interesting. There are several bosses already in the game. They feel moderately difficult but pretty well balanced. Nothing stands out as cheesy or unfair.Exploration consists of finding Relics, potions and basic items that help you find go deeper into the dungeon. Relics are comparable to items in Isaac, mostly passively changing your attacks or the economy. The potions have a wide variety of uses, from healing you to shooting fireballs. The basic items are keys, bombs and food. All of these help you earn gold and thorium which can be used to buy persistent upgrades and unlocks which help your future runs.Like all Rogue-lites, death is part of the game. You aren't meant to take it in one go. Nor are you even able to. The satisfying part of this kind of loop is when your abilities begin to snowball. After a few hours in, I feel like my character is making a lot of progress. The first floors feel much easier and faster. The runs at the beginning took me about 20 minutes to a half hour. Short enough that I don't feel too frustrated when I die to a boss (or die walking into spikes.)All in all I'm satisfied with this purchase and I'm eager to see where they take it. I've had really good luck with early access games of this type. I feel like player feedback leads to a lot of positive changes, especially regarding QoL improvements.

_childDocuments_.review: controls for this game have some questionable design and ultimately it makes the game unplayable for me. using your axe to make a melee attack roots your dude in place briefly, which on its own is weird, but especially when you're in the middle of a pack of monsters trying to stick and move and weave attacking and dodging together, you literally can't. throwing your axe is janky on both controller or KB - on the controller the angular directions feel too narrow, making it very difficult to reliably hit targets on a diagonal angle, and on KB you throw the axe in the direction your character last moved & faced, not to the placement of the mouse cursor. also throwing your axe deals less damage than a melee swing, except once you throw your axe you also can't make another attack until it boomerangs back to you - this is terrible design and should be switched, so that the risk of throwing the axe and potentially being defenseless is offset by the reward of it dealing a ton of damage. as-is the throw move is weaker than a melee swing and it robs you of being able to attack successively.the game would at least be playable if the controls weren't utter ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, but currently i would not recommend anyone buy this game.

_childDocuments_.review: It’s very rare that I play rogue-like or rogue-lite games, simply because I tend to not enjoy the idea of randomly generated infinitely replayable titles, vastly preferring the hand-crafted games with a definitive end to them (that I can simply replay if I liked them a lot). However, there have been a few titles that despite all odds got me invested. And somehow Undermine joined their ranks. I’ll try to understand why.Undermine is a rogue-lite with room-by-room exploration in a layered dungeon, isometric view, permanent upgrades and jumping as means of dodging attacks and also exploring. It’s biggest influence seems to be The Binding of Isaac (which in turn has been influenced by the original The Legend of Zelda dungeons) and most of the basic ideas are the same. Each dungeon zone has several floors (4 to be precise). Each floor is divided into rooms that take up the entire screen and are connected to other rooms, sometimes directly, sometimes via a door requiring a key and sometimes via wall that must be bombed or destroyed by an enemy. Additional secret rooms and items might be hidden under/inside rocks that can be bombed or also destroyed by enemies. Rooms often include enemies, in which case the doors to other rooms get locked until you kill all of them, sometimes additional hazards, sometimes only hazards, and there’s almost always a shop somewhere in the level. Oh and also every floor has a Relic, which is a special upgrade item that stays with you until the end of the run, while in very few exceptional cases you might also find permanent items called Artifacts, or upgrades. Also, there’s lots of gold everywhere which you should mine to get upgrades in the starting hub.Most of what I’ve described is almost exactly the same as it was in Isaac, except now focusing more on melee attacks and almost entirely devoid of bullet-hell-like sections. Additionally, you can avoid all damage if you’re jumping as whatever is dealing damage passes under you. You will still take damage if you land on the damage dealing enemy or hazard, but, interestingly, vast majority of enemies in the game don’t deal contact damage and have attacks with clearly defined tells. Oh and, of course, the permanent upgrades are also a thing that clearly differentiates this from Isaac, as your starting area contains several kinds of shops that provide either upgrades, or new kinds of relics, potions, blessings and other kinds of things that you will encounter during the run.None of this is specifically fantastic, I must stress. The combat is pretty simple, though you do get to learn some tricks as you play, as you realize how to better use the melee and throwing attacks and how and when to jump or use bombs. Or get better at using the relics you find, blessings you get or even detrimental curses to your advantage. But it remains quite simple, as do the levels, bosses, enemies, hazards, “puzzles” and other things you encounter. You get more of everything as you play, but most of it doesn’t become much deeper. Yet… something about this simplicity clicks. At least it did with me. And the permanent upgrades and unlocks are often a good enough hook to keep you invested even in a run where you’re clearly going to die very soon.It also helps that both the visual style and the soundtrack are very nice. Also the story, as simple as it is, is doing what it needs to do. And the characters are cute. All of this is also not specifically fantastic, but simply very very good. And for those who like rogue-lites more than I do, there are even more additional things and run modes and unlocks that you get after you complete the game once, that I didn’t particularly care about, but you might.So, despite the fact that some of the enemies in the game are more annoying that anything. Despite the really visually inconsistent way you can fall into holes. Despite the fact that some rooms are poorly thought out and some are super easy to accidentally exit from before you collect everything you want. I really-really liked playing this game. And might even play it again in the future. And some of the music tracks are definitely going into my main playlist, even though at first I found them really silly. Undermine isn’t a game that’s really great, or striking, or memorable, or anything deserving an extreme kind of praise. But it’s really good and it’s very fun to play. And sometimes that's exactly what you need.

_childDocuments_.review: Being a big roguelike/roguelite fan, i picked this game up on a whim. I'm happy to say it is a pretty solid game. **Graphics** - This game is beautifully animated. The art style definitely sticks out among a vast sea of other games of this genre. Great colors, great character designs, and gorgeous animations. 9/10 **Audio** - The sound effects are pretty good, hitting enemies, using your pickaxe to mine gold, all sounds very solid. The music is good. Not anything to write home about, but definitely not bad. 6/10 **Gameplay** - With this game being a roguelike, you know for the most part what you are getting. You kill enemies, collect items to power up and try to progress further. After every run you have an opportunity to purchase upgrades to make your next run better. There are 2 main methods of attacking, swing your pickaxe, and throwing your pickaxe. Compared to other roguelikes the melee attack definitely feels clunky and awkward at first, while the ranged attack is far easier to use more effectively. But as you get more comfortable with using it, the melee attack is very good. There are a very good amount of items/unlockables. The difficulty between floors can spike at times, which can be frustrating, but practice makes perfect. 7.5/10 **Other Notes** - The game is very fun currently, but the devs have updated this game very frequently, with very sizeable additions, with more and more coming out all the time. The devs are doing a great job of supporting it.Final Score: 8.25/10 **Final Words** - A must buy for roguelike fans, and definitely a recommendation for anyone who is on the fence about it. Good Luck and Have Fun!

_childDocuments_.review: You ever heard of Binding Of Isaac? Think that, but instead of unlocking new characters, items, challenges, and bosses as you play, you get money and blueprints. Spend this money to get higher base stats, and unlock new items, and keep trying and trying and trying again to beat a run. Of course dying does set you back a bit of gold, but there's items and upgrades that prevent too big a loss. In addition, the combat is more than just ranged. You have a melee attack as well, which leaves you vulnerable in a way but has higher damaged than the ranged attack. There's also a curse/blessing system which can add a lot of variety to a run outside of the items you get. All in all, a great game if you've played the heck out of Binding of Isaac and are looking for a new distinct flavour in the genre. Just be ready to sacrifice a few peasants along the way.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing for 2.5 hours at the time of this review - it is the shortest i've played a game before writing one. Anyways, I feel like I am ready for giving my opinion about Undermine.Game is average overall. Undermine can't be classified as a good nor bad game either. The reason for my negative review is that after almost 3h of playing I feel like the only motivation for keeping on is for the sake of not wasting the 10€ I spent on this game.This game's progress is really slow and grindy. I defeated the first boss and I don't feel like I gained any significant power over the first area of the mine. Even after buying several gold sack upgrades I lose a sh$t ton of gold every time I die. Oh, 100 gold away from that 2k upgrade needed to progress in game? You can't do a "quick one" in order to be able to buy it, because you will die and loose even more gold, so the game always forces you to play conservatively, no matter how many upgrades you have or how many times you've beaten an area.I feel stuck doing the same areas over and over again without any satisfaction or sense of progress just to grind more gold and be able to buy more upgrades that dont give any sense of progress or added power to me. This is absolutely the most frustrating part of the gameplay experience. I don't like games that provide "more gameplay hours" if those hours mostly be grinding the same enemies over and over again.For a lot of features this game just feels like unfair and a pain in the a$$. Dont judge me, I enjoy hard and challenging games, and I wont even classify Undermine as a hard game, because it isn't. The gameplay just feels sturdy and kind of orthopedic for no reason, at least for me. Invincibility after taking damage is somehow broken, and several times I got "comboed" from attacks from different enemies and inevitably killed after concatenating several attacks and a pit fall.First boss experience was easy and boring. I feel like this game is so focused on combat and that it needs a lot of improvement on polishing this feature of the game,  because as I already told before, it feels really sturdy compared to other roguelite games.Also, I got a game crash that made me lose one of the best runs I had. For a gameplay of 3 hours this feels devastating after dealing with all the frustration I experienced before.

_childDocuments_.review: After having a disappointing experience with RAD yesterday I was pretty happy to see a more fairly priced and quite frankly better thought out and executed rogue like game today with UnderMine. I didn't have a long playtime in RAD, but I think it just takes a few runs to get a general feel for the gameplay loop and the gameplay, and I enjoyed what I saw in UnderMine a lot more. The core gameplay is the tried and true roguelike style gameplay, very similar to Binding of Isaac, but the emphasis of the overall game is less on getting amazing one off runs and more on progressing between runs, which kind of reminded me of a rogue legacy style experience. This is rally enjoyable for someone like me who is awful at these roguelike style games.Pros:- Art style is classic retro feel, with a good mining focused color theme that is comfortable but still pleasing.- Gameplay controls are responsive and intuitive, top down style camera doesn't move and change the way the gameplay feels like it did in RAD.- The progression system adds a driving force that makes me want to keep playing, as well as making it so a bad player like myself doesn't feel like I'm just killing time dying on the 3rd floor often.Cons:- Still the tried and true roguelike, so some people might only get 5 hours of entertainment out of it, some might get hundreds.- This bastard wizard keeps calling me a peasant. FeelsBadManThe game is definitely worth a buy if roguelikes interest you, whether you have experience with the genre or not. At a good price tag for a roguelike ($15 CAD, whereas RAD is nearly double that), I think its a pretty safe buy and you will probably find it was the price within the refund window anyways.
