_childDocuments_.review: Full of awful design choices, bad game flow and bad progression that other games in the genre that came before it fixed.- 4 direction swing? Why? Just feels like a lazy choice trying to ape 'retro' games when it's unecessary- Hefty animation lock and unresponsive controls- 'Feast or famine' RNG drops - no keys? no bombs? Guess you're not getting any items this run!- Needlessly starved progression, as the gold you gather and spend in dungeon is also used on permanent upgrades- Gold is stolen from you on death! Why? What's the point of taking a hefty percentage of it except to soak up money on the upgrade to lose less? If that upgrade is a necessity, it should just be baseline, or not exist at all! Taking more gold into the next dungeon run doesn't help anyway as you're reliant on a shop showing up.- 'Pilfers' show up and steal your gold if you don't pick it up quick enough - why? What does this add to gameplay except that you have to run around grabbing gold in an empty, or that you leave all the gold piles until a room is clear of enemies?- Hitboxes on attacks way larger than their animation- 'Vacuum' pits that suck you in despite not being close enough to fall in them - I assume this is because the game is lazily designed on a grid- Over reliance on spikes and traps- The majority of items aren't impactful, some are even completely useless, there's no feeling of growing stronger- No normalisation on curses - some are merely bad, some are utterly crippling, double costs means doors now take two keys? You barely get enough keys to begin with! That's an absurd 'design choice'- Bosses are just damage sponges with one or two attacks rather than having an interesting mechanics- Currency to unlock new relics is needlessly rare and far too much is requiredAny developer in this genre just needs to look at Enter the Gungeon and the patches they applied over time to learn how to actually make and balance their game. Changing key mechanics to make items accessible, improving gameplay flow and function, just overall polish!This game isn't it. Don't buy, not even on sale.

If being relentlessly ground under the bootheel of a sadist dev appeals to you, then by all means enjoy Undermine; otherwise get Rogue Legacy for a much better take on a generational rogue-lite.

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game back in early access quite a while ago and loaded it up a few times throughout. Now that it's been released, I gave it another shot. This isn't a bad game, but I don't like it, and therefore do not recommend it. The problem for me is that it just isn't fun. I love rogue-lites/likes and dungeon crawlers but there are a few gameplay elements here that add up to a final product that mostly just annoys me. A few things such as: 1) healing is very sparse and you take a lot of damage easily. This in itself wouldn't be so bad except that there are certain things that contribute to you losing health too easily such as:   -- getting any kind of "homing" or "duplicating" relics and hitting a lightning mite shocks you beyond your control (for a whopping 30hp)  -- it's very easy to get pinballed around the screen and knocked into holes  -- certain curses damage your health (I'm thinking of one that just changed all locks to require 50hp instead of a key)  -- potions feel almost worthless; they don't heal for much hp and/or they feel gimmicky (I'm thinking of the one potion I find fairly often that causes the next damage you take to heal you instead ... one time)- this all leads to a situation that constantly feels tense ... but not in a good way. Healing foods feel common enough but they heal a pitiful amount. 2) Curses! Want some blessings? Have some curses! Want to remove a curse at the prayer altar? Gonna cost you some hp ... and you don't get to choose which curse to remove! - some curses suck more than others (dropping one bomb uses 2; no more picking up potions; etc.)- I can't stress this enough -- it sucks that you can't choose which curse to remove but it does so seemingly randomly- you can't really avoid curses as they are packed in with positive thingsNot only does this mechanic feel unfun, it mentally feels bad because a curse is a "negative" thing and they just pile on. It becomes an annoyance. I think it is supposed to be a "challenging" mutator to runs, but I really dislike it. 3) Relics & blessings- They just don't feel as fun as they should. There are some that have cool effects, but lots of them are just "do more swing damage" -- which is often negated by the increasing number of curses you pick up. 4) Fast travelYou eventually get the option to skip ahead in the dungeon when you enter.  However, doing so leaves you woefully under-powered and unprepared. They tried to address this by giving you a "care package" with some relics ... but it doesn't include bombs or keys, so good luck navigating the floor you just arrived on. Overall, this game looks good and it's obvious work went into it. It's technically a good game and I know there are people who love it. However, I just don't enjoy it and find it more an exercise in frustration. It's not that it's even particularly difficult, just really annoying and dissatisfying.

_childDocuments_.review: The sense of progression is very solid and the upgrades feel diverse and well balanced. There's a lot of potential gameplay to be gotten out of it as well given that the difficulty can increase basically without end and you can always apply hexes if you want a larger challenge or enter the Othermine for more of a pure Roguelike experience: You go in with nothing and face the game with only what you can gather along the way.The downside is that there's basically no story at all and only six real bosses, one of whom is only worth doing a single time. It's also overly time consuming to increase the difficulty because each increase has to be its own separate run through the game. If you want to go from, say, +2 difficulty to +20 because you aren't being challenged enough that is going to take you another eighteen runs of the game. Given that a single run will probably take at least an hour, it's pretty daunting.

_childDocuments_.review: Disappointed with how the game progresses. At first Undermine comes off as bright and fun with lots of potential to discover while definitely hitting that "just one more run" mentality that steals hours from you before you realize the sun's gone down, but the further you get into the game, the more bafflingly empty and repetitive it feels.This is because of a decision that takes a lot of life out of future runs being that bosses do not respawn. So if you defeated the first floor's boss, it will never come back (until you complete the entire game) and since a lot of your progression will be tied to losing runs and using the gold you've gathered during lost runs to upgrade your stats, you will end up doing many runs that feel like slow methodical grinds for gold and not exciting unique romps into a fun randomized world with exciting battles and payoffs at the end of each floor. The further you get into Undermine, the worse this problem becomes.There is a system that lets you skip floors entirely, but using it feels like you're setting yourself up for failure. Not only will you miss out on all the gold you could've collected during a full normal run, but you'll lose out on tons of upgrade relics, blessings, familiar XP, and consumables along the way leaving you feeling completely underpowered (The game tries to compensate you by handing you 2 free relics per floor you skipped, but on average you'd get 4-5 relics per floor + many other minor upgrades if you played normally) Thus, if you wanna give yourself the best shot at overall progression, you have to slowly grind through the entire game sans its bosses every single time. This becomes incredibly boring when you're in the end game and have to go through 20 levels that take upwards to an hour to complete before having a chance at fighting its 5th boss.The bread and butter of a proper rouguelite, imo, is having enough variety to keep the many runs you're going to do feeling different and unique. Undermine is rather restrictive with its weapon which does not change or get altered in any significant ways from its items so the game never feels different at any point. At most, maybe you'll have a run where your melee has slightly more range, or you prefer using your ranged attack because you got several damage buffs to it. You'll also be seeing the same items all the time, many of them feeling rather unhelpful.Undermine has a lot of charm to it, great graphics, fun characters, and it controls very nicely. And at first, it feels very fun and fresh as you have plenty of mysteries to uncover from its mines and powerful foes to defeat, but the further you get, the more boring it all becomes, and a rougelite shouldn't feel like a sluggish grind before you've even fully beaten it once. After beating Undermine, I had very little reason to want to replay it or do more runs because all I could remember is the taste in my mouth of grinding gold for hours on end and the disappointment of runs feeling too identical to each other to at least add some excitement to the mix.If you're looking for something that'll kill a good 5-10 hours while retaining its charm or if you're someone who loves grinding up stats to better tackle future runs, you might like this game a lot! But if you're hoping for a rouguelite that'll let you replay it over and over always promising something fun, silly, or unique, this won't be your next Isaac.

_childDocuments_.review: It surprises me that this is sitting at "overwhelmingly positive". I... guess I would attribute that to Binding of Isaac players being starved for something new.  It's certainly not bad, and since it's still got "Early Access" status, maybe it will get somewhere interesting, but--currently--I'm done after an hour or so. Wish it weren't too late to get a refund.Why do I feel this way? How does it fall short? The art style is pretty good. The basic mechanics are... serviceable, if not exciting. The biggest problem with this game is that it feels samey almost immediately. The character sprites are compelling enough, but the elements used in the procedural generation are so few, and so consistent, that it never feels like exploration. It feels like what it is: a small network of rooms that will disappear forever as soon as I find a trapdoor. I can hardly tell one run from another. And the absolutely-never-fail nature of the creatures that steal my gold? Makes them groan-worthy. They always arrive, and they always arrive at exactly the same pace, and they almost always beat you to something. It makes me not want to mine gold. And I LIKE mining gold!Three things would thrill me, if achieved before the end of EA:1) Much more variety to the tiles and other elements that make up the procedural generation.2) Punchier sound / haptic feedback design. Make me feel the combat, viscerally.3) Here's a thought: folks emulate Binding of Isaac, but they never seem to go after what I personally think is the most intriguing element of that game: complex synergies between items. Novel combinations. Transformations (in the case of this game, maybe this could manifest itself as class-style equipment variations. And--hey--even though there's not technically much story to Isaac, the very NAMES chosen for the elements are colorful, evocative, and make each fresh run feel like it's got its own story to tell.I give this game a 6/10, and I will try to remember to check back to see where you've taken it.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; Worth it for <$8, could be a $20 game if the devs keep with it and sort out the issues. If you've played a handful of other rogue-likes, keep this one on the watchlist and wait for some updates before committing.I'm aware that this game is currently in development, but this has been my experience thus far:The game is fun enough, but at this point in does not offer much fresh material to the ever-expanding list of rogue-likes. The combat is stiff, your character is slower than many enemies, and relies on jumping as the only means of avoiding attacks. Armed with a boomerang-pickaxe, you must delve down through the levels to uncover the mystery of what's causing underground tremors. The art style is cute and light, but the systems in place for risky investments into your character are quite unbalanced. Ordinarily, such trade-offs are handled in the form of minor setbacks like max HP loss or minor curses. On two different occasions I accepted a curse, which caused my character to receive double damage, and in return I got one measly bomb, which there are usually plenty of lying around. The curse system does not ever seem  to make the investments worth the setback, and so far I have been completely put-off from accepting the risk, because no matter how far ahead I am on supplies, money, and health, the curses will inevitably end my current run short. Healing your character is no easy feat, as you rely solely on the RNG of food drops as you explore, or buying potions from the merchant. Even then, only so much healing can be done, and even if you are loaded with gold, you will have a hard time keeping healthy if you can't dodge all attacks headed your way.Also, jumping is clunky, as you have no control over your momentum in mid-air, and there are numerous traps and pitfalls that are rather punishing to the player. With jumping being the only means of dodging attacks, this lack of control requires extra precision and awareness of your surroundings. I think I end up taking more fall damage and trap damage than anything else usually. At the current price this isn't a bad game to add to the collection, nor is it unfriendly to those new to the type of game. However, compared to other games, there are many that are significantly better balanced, and just as affordable. This game needs time and care to reach its potential, but from what I've seen, dedication from the devs will result in a new favorite rogue-like for me.However, this level of unpolished code can't get a recommendation from me, but I will continue coming back from time to time, hoping to see some real innovation.

_childDocuments_.review: A twinstick shooter roguelike reminiscent of Binding of Isaac while also including some of the puzzle elements from Zelda. All of the pieces of this game create an atmosphere of exploration and mystery that provided a ton of excitement. The first time the player starts the game, they will be dropped into an empty hub world that doesn’t have much in it besides the wizard who is the one who wanted someone to check out the mines due to earthquakes and something he has lost. While initially devoid of life, the hub world soon becomes lively as soon as the player begins to rescue the NPCs trapped in the mines; often due to the wizard as well. All of the NPCs, except for the pets, have a purpose and are designed to help make the player more powerful with every subsequent run. It is fun to watch a former ghost town become full of life ready to assist the player, though for a price.Combat is the main gameplay loot for Undermine. The player has a few ways to attack. The first way is by performing a melee swing with the pickaxe which has decently high damage while also providing minor knockback against enemies which is perfect when defending against melee focused opponents. The second way to attack is by throwing the pickaxe like a boomerang. This attack is ranged, but does less damage and leaves the player vulnerable as they can’t attack without their weapon. Bombs are a last resort tool for attacking as they have a lot of utility, but they are also devastating forces of destruction with proper placement. Their main issue is that they are limited in uses and are not always easy to find. Combat stays interesting due to the large variety of enemies. Even ten hours into the game I found that I would find an enemy that wasn’t previously seen in one of my runs. Early enemies are focused on melee attacks, but more powerful enemies often focus on ranged attacks with multiple bullets creating a bullet hell style of gameplay. There are some enemies that are reskins of enemies found early on, but the new enemies have new attack patterns so I didn’t mind as much. They are also much more the exception than the rule. Finally, the player is able to dodge similar to the one found in souls-like games. The main issue is that it is instead a jump which doesn’t fit well with the two-dimensional play space. The shadow isn’t noticeable enough and can make it difficult to know exactly where the player is going to land. The best way to improve the player’s randomized character each run is by picking up the relics available every level. The items, known as relics, provide passive abilities to the player in a variety of ways. One such example would be the glaive relic which makes the pickaxe huge when thrown which makes it very easy to hit whichever target is closest to the player. These effects can be combined though, which creates some very fun combinations that can absolutely destroy enemies. An example of a combo would be the glaive along with the triple throw. This will allow the player to throw three giant pickaxes in a cone formation. Some relics are unique and don’t play well with other unique relics. This is usually due to the fact that they are quite powerful. Two examples that I liked would be the aforementioned triple throw which has the potential to triple to player’s thrown damage and makes the ranged attack more effective as a shotgun and the golden bomb, which turns rocks that are bombed out into useful gold.Secret rooms are easy to find as the wall has a small sparkle effect on it. Secret rooms will sometimes be treasure rooms, but it can also be a small puzzle that is solved using visual clues. It keeps the secret rooms interesting, but they are a bit annoying when the puzzle requires bombs or keys that the player doesn't have. There are also secret rooms hidden under rocks. A great way to  find these secrets is by using a rock breaking enemy to open them up for free. Every set of levels has an end boss which is a difficult test of skill that has a powerful gimmick. Once the bosses are defeated, the player gets a boss key and they can continue to the next set of levels. Once a boss key is used, the player doesn’t have to get another,  the doors to the next set of levels will simply be open. I also like how the player obtains the blueprint to a relic that allows the player to use the boss’ gimmick for themselves.Progression is cumulative and every upgrade bought is inherited by the future peasant after death. The upgrades are necessary to beat stronger levels and the player is able to gain some upgrades besides damage once the appropriate NPC is unlocked in the hub world. The main aspect of the progression I dislike would be that when the player forges a new relic from a blueprint, they are given the relic. Subsequently crafted relics are taken away by a pilfer, so the player is only able to have the first one. This is only a one time thing though, which makes it feel  like one might be gimping a future run by unlocking a cool new relic early game.Not much story in this roguelike. The player is one of an army of peasants that make a contract with a wizard to mine for riches.  The music is quite good and doesn't get in the way of the gameplay. It instead adds a layer of ambiance that can be tuned out when in an intense battle. The sound design is great an provides a lot of auditory feedback to the player. This is done through hit sounds and unique sound effects for certain enemy abilities. The game uses a pixel art style that has a lot of pixels that provides a smooth look with jagged edges. The graphics do a great job at relaying that there may be secrets or what a monster may do. One such example is the purple braziers will provide items if blown up, but also curse the player. This purple is consistent with curses which allows players to know when they should avoid things. The aspect of this game that is frustrating is that some enemies will jump which uses higher z-levels. Considering this game is two-dimensional, it can be very hard to judge where they are going to land.The controls work quite well using a controller. All of the buttons were easy to reach and were well laid out. The twinstick controls are easy to access while not taking away from the melee aspect of the game.: I didn’t experience any bugs.I had seen a decent amount of the content, especially the items and enemies, but there were always new secrets that would appear and would surprise me.  👍  👍Beautiful graphicsLots of secretsCrazy item combos👎  👎Annoying dodge ability

_childDocuments_.review: Undermine, a simple game that was made with love.This is simply my opinion and feelings about Undermine, so please try it out for yourself before you decide!At first I didn't expect anything other than a simple rouge-like/lite that was randomly generated as you played. What I ended up experiencing was so much more than that. Regardless of whether you enjoy rouge-like games or not, everyone should give Undermine a go.Gameplay: You have three basic movements. Close-up melee with your pickaxe, throwing your pickaxe and jumping. You will be jumping around a lot! I found the jumping mechanic to be so interesting in a top down pixel based dungeon crawler and it makes for learning some really fun quick reflexes as you learn the game. You will also use your pickaxe for the act of mining for gold, which you will buy items with or simply hoard all of your gold if you must. I mostly play throwing my pickaxe everywhere but swinging it as a close ranged weapon is also fun. I understand for some people this may sound a little boring, but the Relic system is really where the combat shines in this game.Every level offers a Relic, which grants you a special ability or buff. Some are better than others, and I love that I never know what I'll end up getting. You may get shoes that allow you to float over holes in the dungeon, or a relic that makes all gold explode on impact. There are also Curses in the game, which are a bit self explanatory but really kick up the notch in difficulty. Your healing items may be less effective, your potions may break, or all of the enemies turn into tiny spiders when they explode and die!All rooms are randomly generated and some offer puzzles that you can complete to get a chest full of items, or a relic. There are many secret rooms and levels in each play-through and some wonderful characters and situations to find. You can find recipes for crafting items and potions, as well as eggs for pets to help you in your journey.There is an amazing end game that steps up the difficulty quite a lot, and without spoiling anything, I really love what is offered in the endgame and I am still working on quite a bit of that. It's challenging, but also very rewarding.I'm so happy they included pets that you can collect that really can save you from some dire situations and help out a lot with combat, or doing very specific tasks that are immensely helpful. They are also adorable.Art: The pixel art is incredible, so much love has gone into the visual aesthetic and design of this game. From the peasants that you play that go down into the mine, to the small details like wiggling mushrooms as you stand on them, to the fun designs of each boss you will encounter at the end of each dungeon. The animation of the pixel art is also done so well, and I wish other games achieved it to this level of quality.Music: The music is great and really sets the tone for the game, it can get a little repetitive when you've played quite a lot but I still really enjoy it. The sound design is well done, I love the sound effects of jumping, using the axe, killing enemies and all abilities that are used. I especially love the sound that plays when you discover a secret.Story: This was something unexpected. I really did not expect much of a story, but as I played through the game I actually really enjoyed the characters that you begin to find throughout playing. They are wonderfully designed and are full of character. The only downside to the story is that I would love to have a DLC that offers some more story content. I enjoy that there is a bit of a mystery as to why this king is sending peasants into the mine and how that is just acceptable in this universe! The pilfer characters that look like little slimes are great, and if you play it enough there's some fantastic secrets about them that you will discover over time. There is also a great sense of humour all throughout the game that I really appreciated.Overall I just really love this game and continue to play through end game content. It has wonderful replay value and I hope to get all of the achievements at one point.The only negative about this game, for me, is that there isn't any DLC. There is also no co-op, which is a real shame as I think this game could be fantastic for either couch co-op or online co-op. I hope the developers work on some DLC, but I will also be very curious about any upcoming games they may be working on.I rate this a 99/100 gold nuggets. I very much recommend you play this game and I hope you enjoy it as much as I have.A big thank you to the developers who worked so hard on this game, you have given me so many hours of joy.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll keep this short. Roguelikes come in two varities usually: slow and tactical or fast and reactionary. Undermine does a clunky job at trying to have both. The axe throw is borderline useless, and this game commits a cardinal sin of action games of having some enemies that stagger on hit like rats, and others that do not like the jelly and bat. Why would you do this?Combat is really not fun especially versus bosses because the boss attack comes out so fast that you barely have enough time to do damage before you have to jump away. The hitbox is kind of ridiculous, such as when fighting the blue yeti monster the moment he finishes his claw attack you have like 10 frames to attack and jump away because the moment he is done, his body turns into a hitbox while he runs. Just silly. I killed the first boss in 10 seconds by spamming the Rook bomb (I somehow got 8 before floor 3). Without this, it would have taken minutes to kill this guy despite having a braindead attack pattern.I finally quit when I saw a room with a pit, and across the pit there was gold in the walls. "How do I get that gold?" I thought. I threw my axe, nothing. Maybe that sliver of space is enough to stand? Nope. Fell into the pit and took damage. Why design rooms like that? No QA?

Quite honestly The Binding of Isaac started out like this but it got better and better every update. Sadly I don't think this will be the case with this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I played my first 90 minutes of UnderMine last night and WOW this game is fantastic. I've watched bits and pieces of it on twitch but I finally decided to play it last night despite roguelikes not really being my thing.The first thing I noticed was the music. It fits the feel of the game perfectly: 8-bit vibes but the sounds are more complex than just beeps. The pickaxe sounds that make up most of the percussion remind me of old sound chips where all you had was a noise generator to make percussion sounds, but at the same time the pickaxes fit the ambience of, well, a mine.Beyond the music and sound, the dialog and character building is excellent. It's all in the subtle details like NPCs only partially acknowledging that you're a new person every time. They all know that adventurer after adventurer is being sent down there to die but they don't really want to admit it. They also have such different personalities. For example, some shopkeepers will just let you smash up their store but others will yell at you. All of these little details make the world so immersive that you just want to keep exploring.Beyond the ambience and storyâ€”although, to me, that is the most important part of a gameâ€”the gameplay itself is intuitive but interesting. It doesn't require an insane amount of mechanical skill to get through the mine (at least not where I'm at in the game), but at the same time it isn't boring at all. The way curses and relics affect combat makes it so you have to keep thinking for every fight; you can't just mash the attack button and hope for the best, you have to stay on your toes and keep adjusting your combat style.With the level of detail in this game, I can't wait to see what else is in store for me as I search into the depths. All of the subtle things, like rooms getting darker when you break torches, make me want to keep punching walls and blowing things up just to see what happens. All of that is supported by such excellent art (visual, and musical), and story telling. All things considered, this game is a big ten out of ten for me.

_childDocuments_.review: The graphics, sound & music, and art direction are all great.The problem is that the game lacks varied builds.  The game is extremely stingy with items, meaningful buffs that change how you can approach a run.Other Roguelikes seem to throw too many different modifiers, like an endless toy box of goodies, Undermine by comparision is like a scolding scour parent who just wants to be mean to you.The items costs ramp up way too fast and don't provide meaningful changes until you get like half a dozen upgrades into each one.The problem is that after a while, all runs start to feel like every other run.   Your stuck on an endless treadmill of upgrading 'x' stats in the starting hub before you can advance to the next area or beat the area boss.  Losing more than your stated amount of gold at each death might seem like a neat gameplay design, but quickly just becomes extremely annoying because of how human natural evolved to avoid loss. After you played all the better games in this genre, this might be worth looking into if you can get all of steep sale or on service like Gamepass.

To be fair if you're in the more "hardcore" group of players this game has less items and content than Isaac. But to be completely fair this game is much newer and still in early access. For being in 0.7 at the moment I feel this game has quite a bit of content. I'm not quite maxed out yet and I've got nearly 40 hours of playtime. This game is unique from games like Isaac in the fact that you can jump, you can also fall down holes. Another thing I've noticed is when you get two items that synergize together they actually combine to form a new item which is pretty cool. Overall I'd give this game a 10/10, the devs clearly have been putting a lot of love into this title within a reasonable time table and the game is challenging but not "punch your monitor" difficult. _childDocuments_.review: This game is and average rogue-lite at best. Most of the mechanics have been there before in other games but were either fleshed out more, better implemented etc. I tried to like this especially since it has so many positive reviews, but i can't.Graphics are charming, as far as pixel dungeon crawlers go.Gameplay is meh. It's always the same start (roguelike, duh), yet other games like hades, dead cells, risk of rain, etc. manage to provide a continously interesting experience while undermine generally fails to do so. Plain environments, unforseeale traps that have to be learned thoroughly before you don't die continously by falling into pits or get stomped to death by an angry chest that's jumping around towards you, while you can't determine when you're even supposed to hit it.Jumping feels like you're floating 10cm above the ground for 1 second and then hit the ground at a very hard to pinpoint location.Sense of progression went as follows for me: Collect some stuff, die, buy one thing, collect stuff, die, buy one thing, ... until i managed to kill some bosses with more of the same in between. The way you collect equipment makes it seem like this game will get way too easy once you've reached a high equipment score. But I might be wrong on this one. I ragequit this game atleast 5 times in my 5 hours of playtime.

_childDocuments_.review: Undermine is an early access game reminiscent of games like Binding of Isaac and Enter the Gungeon. Even with it being in early access, it's a pretty fleshed out game with a really cool underlying story arch. I find myself drawn to talking to the NPCs whenever i get to a new depth or kill a new boss just to see what bits of knowledge they might impart. To compliment this draw to the narrative, not all is as it seems, and you have to wonder if what you're being told is all the truth, or just a version of it that you are told to hear.With secrets to explore, items to discover, and a world that has so much depth with so few words, picking up Undermine for the early access price is a steal, and will most likely be worth the full price when the game officially launches!

_childDocuments_.review: If you are in it for the grind, this game is for you. It's a great game to pick up and play after a long day of work. It doesn't require a lot of thought, and the room gen is just entertaining enough to keep it interesting, but boring enough to be low stress. Not a great gamer? No problem. This game is all about slow and incremental progression that gives you enough time to learn how to git gud. I think playing this actually made me better at playing other rogue-like games. Plus it's cute, it has a lot of easy and satisfying achievements on Steam, and can be played with a controller or keyboard+mouse. It's probably not the game for everyone, but I am enjoying it for what it is!

_childDocuments_.review: Bit conflicted with this recommendation because although I had a lot of fun, there's some ideas and gameplay issues that could use some work. The positives are definitely the setting, characters and curse system. The pixel art is nice but is honestly too complex and detailed for a roguelite like this. Isaac, Nuclear Throne and the like have really obvious colour schemes that help the player know what is an enemy, and what is not. The first 10 hours of playing Undermine I had to really concentrate to figure out what was on screen in some rooms, and it doesn't feel like this was a factor that was taken into consideration.The leveling up system (similar to Rogue Legacy with a touch of Deadcells), while fun, sort of makes the early game a grind, and the late game feel less important. There is an option to skip ahead to lower floors as you progress, but the way the game is designed, I never, ever, do this. Not because I didn't want to jump ahead, but because in doing so it would absolutely cripple the run. It is the difference between coming into a floor with 10+ relics/blessings, over 2.I also feel like the basic 'stop and swing' attack, while true to it's Legend of Zelda roots, feels clunky compared to faster paced roguelites. Not to mention the awkward jump. I really don't understand why jumping was chosen over a shield. It would have lead to a lot of cool item ideas and combinations, and again be true to the NES LoZ.What I did really enjoy about Undermine versus Isaac (because there is a pretty obvious similarity between the two), is that runs are built not on OP items but on incrementally stacking up on the right stat improvements. Felt like I really had to think wisely at alters and was great to see some runs built on insane critical hit builds.I'll definitely be watching for updates, as I loved the overall vibe of Undermine, but it's hard to really want to go any deeper with it right now as the gameplay is not as sharp as some other games in the genre, and a lot of the runs feel the same.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game, with a lot of potential, but has some major flaws that keep it from standing up there with Issac.1. Runs always devolve into 2 builds. Swing fast with crits or ricochet throw build. There is no in between and no variance. 2. Bombs are more of a detriment than an actual powerup. You never use bombs inside of combat unless you have a very VERY specific build, even then it's more of a detriment than a blessing. Getting a bomb power up (other than gold, which is another problem) is like losing an item. (Also bombs build garbage hurts the Othermine runs as well). Bombs are only for out of combat and secrets.3. Armor is worthless, dots shred it and it only has a select few synergizing items. Of the two synergies they are bad and not remotly worth it. Once again, getting them feels like a dead item drop. 4. Not enough items work with one another. The fun of Issac is seeing all the wacky ways items work together and see what it pops out with. 5. Bosses are scarce and are a bit underwhelming. 6. The Othermine is a chore and more luck based than skilled. When I started the Othermine runs for the missing items, I just restarted until it would stop giving me horrid items that do basically nothing (like armor or bombs) or starting buffs like "Bomb 4" There is no reason to get bomb buffs already, ESPECIALLY in the Othermine. You need at least one of your attacks to do... well anything. 7. The Othermine should NOT cost resources to play! It's already a chore to play it, why give us a chore to keep playing it. Especially when you need to reroll horrid run starts. 8. The Slime boss and 100k gold given to get there is insane. It should be a 1 time payment. Don't E-paywall and force players to grind gold just do do more challenging content. 9. Pause and restart needs to be removed so you can't redo levels when things stop going your way. 10. Far too many relics and potions are so worthless you dont even want to craft them just to keep them out of your main pool. If you are going to keep the crafting to put things in the item the pool mechanic, you need to allow players to remove stuff too. If not it's better for me to make a new account and just never craft anything I know is horrid. 11. Many of the followers are broken as sin. The hand is one thing as he's a pain to get and is a cool "End of game he does cool stuff" item like Azazel from Issac. But compare the angel to the blue jay... jesus the Angel is broken. 12. Dear god, friendly electricity shouldn't hurt you. The bluejay is more of a danger than your enemies. 13. Issac has a buffer when you walk into a room. you guys put drops, traps, 1 step outside of the door, so when you are back tracking you take unessiary damage all the time. 14. Jumping in this game... it's so bad you guys even made traps that poke fun at the jumping being bad. Again, this game is great, it has amazing potential. I would not type all this if I didn't like it, but it really needs a lot of work before full release.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played many, many roguelites, and this game is the grindiest of them all. So grindy it is, I'd hesitate to call it a rogue-anything. It certainly has a randomly-generated layout of a few rooms each floor, sure, but getting past the second stage, even after several hours of play, is just statistically ridiculous. I managed to beat the first boss on my very first run after a 10-minute long battle, and immediately died when I finally reached the second area. I've been able to consistently beat this boss, but just don't do the damage to reliably clear rooms on the next floor, and I don't feel like I can be bothered to grind to see what's up next because the combat has near-zero skill expression, with only a jump, a melee attack, and a basic throw, which can  be modified by relics you find along the way, but never (in my experience) in a way that improves skill expression, and usually just straight stat upgrades. If you enjoy roguelites like Hades or Dead Cells, this game isn't for you.

This game really blinded me with nostalgia, and with the fun i've been having thus far, it seems i'll be playing a while longer.Some things that stood out worth noting:- I really like the artstyle. Nothing too flashy here, but the character design is quirky and memorable. I love the mustaches. - It seems like you never run out of new things to unlock/discover. I know meta progression is kind of an artificial way to prolong game time, but besides that.. the dungeons themselves get more interesting each new run.- Unique runs. This is so hard to do, and I think Binding of Isaac did it best. _childDocuments_.review: Quite enjoying this one and keep coming back to play for a bit when I get the chance, definitely has that "one more go" vibe, I've had many hours enjoying it so it's been worth the price.The graphics are good fun and the sound is fine, there is a good deal of variety in the dungeon rooms which keeps things fresh and they seem to be adding more which is great, the more the better for this type of game!The 3 bosses in the current build are all pretty decent and challenging at first, was a proper feel good feeling when killing them, tho the 3rd boss was a little easy I felt.  I believe there will be 5 in total on full release.One criticism is it might be a little slow at the start for some folks and takes a while before your really getting a lot of gold to upgrade with and repeating the same dungeons was slow at first, this was alleviated later with power, and you can skip them once the boss is dead, but took some time.If you like rogue-lite's and happy with the grind, that feeling of getting stronger with each run and exhilaration after finally defeating a boss... you'll like this, there is plenty of game here to have right now even in early access so highly recommend jumping in the mine now!!

_childDocuments_.review: Super fun. I really like the balance between the gradual progress you get from upgrading things and death penalty that drops a bunch of your gold. I feel like lots of roguelikes seem to get that balance wrong; this one feels great.Initially I didn't like that the first level seemed to have places to use bombs/keys, frequently without giving me any to use. But then I got further through the progression and realized I just hadn't earned the right to get them that early yet.I think the balance of loot drops is also great. This game feels like a more finely tuned Enter the Gungeon. I always felt like EtG had lots of super cool toys and never let me play with any of them (though I haven't played the more recent updates to EtG, so maybe they fixed this?). That's NOT a mistake that UnderMine makes. Just in my first 11 hours of playtime I've had some VERY stacked builds, and I already have a set of favorite items. And I haven't even crafted up most of the unlockables that I've got the blueprints for yet!

_childDocuments_.review: If you like this sort of game, it may be worth it on sale.It's not bad, but several of its mechanics are a little grindy --You have to pay huge sums of gold to make it so that when you die you get to keep more of your gold, but there's no way to head back early , so it just literally feels like that mechanic and the price to limit its impact is to make you grind more.--You unlock relics without a proper description of what they do, and now they're permanently in your item pool. Prayer beads that heal at altars? Dead weight until you've unlocked a certain NPC. Idol that causes you to "heal again" whenever you heal? 1hp added when you heal 25. And when you realize your mistake, you've now introduced a garbage relic into your item pool.Mining mechanic and the little chiming noises when you're mining for gold are fun though, as is the lore or being a stream of peasants forced to mine

_childDocuments_.review: TL,DR version: Unbalanced and a little buggyA great rogue-like that is perfect in the beginning, but hits some major difficulty spikes later on. Similar to Enter The Gungeon: go as deep as you can, die, get some stuff, get better, repeat. Every run you retain some of the loot you collected to spend on new upgrades.Progression:The one twist is that after defeating a boss, all previous floors will become more difficult. It's incredibly frustrating to go down 10 floors, make a lot of progress, and then find out that you can no longer pass the first 4 floors because they are about as difficult as the 10th floor. Instead of feeling stronger because of your progression, you feel weaker.There is the option to travel to the floors you have accessed in the past, but you miss out on the benefit of items, relics, and blessings you could have received from playing from floor 1. Even though you have skipped the BS enemies on the 1st floor, you now are up against even tougher enemies with the same stats as the 1st floor. It would make more sense if the player received some items/blessings/relics upon travelling to a deeper floor so that they are almost as strong as if they had played through the first few floors (similarly to Enter the Gungeon).Room Transitions:Whenever your player goes to a new room, the system does not seem to take into account where the player will be in proximity to enemies and/or traps. While you won't spawn ON them, you will frequently be placed right next to an enemy that will attack you immediately, with a less than 1 second window to dodge. A tile or two of safety would go a long way, or maybe a delay before the enemies and traps activate.Bugs:There are some bugs, (to be expected in Early Access) but none of them are too major. Most bugs I only encountered once, and the others were easily avoidable.Summary:I have enjoyed this game thoroughly (and I will most likely continue to play it), but I can't recommend it in its current state. Also, fifteen dollars is a little much for the current version.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm gonna start by saying that I actually really like this game. But sadly, I can't recommend it to anyone.Atomic Heart does a few things really well, but also does a lot of things very very poorly. Take note, I have not played the DLC's, I've only played through the base game. I am by no means a dark souls legend of old, and am whole heartedly a casual gamer who plays to have fun. I played the game on normal difficulty, and did find a few things challenging, but a few others really easy. Because I'm so in love with the setting and the foundation of the game, I had fun, and can forgive some major issues. That said, when the ceo of mudfish went on record to say they "believe that gameplay should be secondary in a video game". That ideology is felt hard in this game. A lot of the gameplay mechanics make it very hard to have fun, this game could have benefited from some more extensive play testing. I'll leave a brief pro's and cons list below. Pros.Setting: I absolutely love the Russian 50's robowimzy atmosphere, it's very fun, colorful, and unsettling.Soundtrack: This game has some absolute bangers for combat music! Voice acting: 10/10Perk System: Being able to refund perk points at any time, without taking a loss *chefs kiss*. More games need to do this. Give the player the ability to test and experiment with all the play styles without being punished or starting over. Change your mind and change it again!Graphics/Art: 10/10ConsGameplay: Oh lord the gameplay... the combat feels clunky, enemies feel way too tanky. The game wants you to manage your resources yet locks you into survival rooms where you're forced to fight waves of enemies. The game feels like the devs couldn't make up their mind if they wanted the game to be an open world game, or a linear story game. With zero incentive to actually go explore the world and waste valuable resources, I completed the base game in under 20 hours utilizing only weapons and upgrades you encounter on the main story path. The Story: I actually really enjoyed the story, it was the main reason I continued to play the game. However, the game ends abruptly just when things were starting to get really good. Which just left me unsatisfied and wanting more.Bugs: The game still has bugs, like random falling through the world kinda bugs.

_childDocuments_.review: First impressions:Combat is deliberate and fun, the amount of options you get even in the very beginning really allows you to customise how to approach situations. I have not put any points into health, so this might change, but so far every battle feels very much life and death struggle. Having seen some criticism of bullet sponge enemies, I gotta disagree, scanning new enemies resistances is a must, after that just use appropriate tools for the job and you can dispatch them in 1 to 3 hits.Main story so far is pretty straight forward, however, the world building from reading terminals and listening to recordings is superb. Game conveys both the shiny, euphoric futurism of post war, post Stalinist Soviet Union and its behind the scenes underbelly of elitism, prisoner exploitation, secrecy etc.Main character, in the original Russian voice over is gruff military type that feels real, unfortunately in English voice over it goes more towards a ridiculous, angry, non-self-aware, Duke Nukem like moron. So the game definitely suffers from poor localisation in that regard. Do yourself a favour and go with Russian VO and English subtitles, it will make your journey much more pleasant.Technically, it is gorgeous, runs smooth with medium settings 60+fps, or decent 40 fps on high settings. This is on my old Ryzen 2700X with RX580 graphics. In 9 hours so far no crashes and the only bug encountered, is some crafting items can get stuck with no ability to pick them up.

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE 10+ HOURS IN: This is probably the best game I have ever played. The dialogue is funny, engaging, and the characters feel genuine and not scripted. Being able to talk to dead people is a really interesting and fun way to incorporate different elements for the game. There is clearly *so much more* to do and see in this game, I feel like I have barely even started, and I can't get enough. This game is easily Game of the Year material.Before the game came out, people were saying this game is going to be a lot like Bioshock, which is another game I couldn't get enough of, and at this point I have to say this is much better than Bioshock. Pick this up if you want that feeling x10 that you got from playing Bioshock and Fallout 3. The only downside to playing this is it will spoil you and make other games pale in comparison.Fantastic job devs! I am so glad I purchased the premium so I can get access to all the future DLC to come.-----------------------------------------------------------I’ve only just begun but it is an *incredible* experience thus far and I don’t have any complaints.The optimization is phenomenal. 10/10 - Russian developers are doing incredible work and I can’t wait to see what they come out with next

_childDocuments_.review: Atomic Heart is exactly what we needed this year!+ PROS + ++++++++++ Awesome Plot and Story+ Awesome Gameplay Mechanics+ Awesome Game Visuals+ Awesome Skills and Upgrades+ Awesome Interesting Weapons+ Very Unique and Interesting Enemies+ Challenging at times when Enemy is in Numbers or In Small Areas- CONS - ------------ Story starts off suuuuuppppppeerrr long before you actually get into the gameplay and while it makes sense to build the story out until everything goes wrong of course it does feel rather lengthy, its tolerable but for those more impatient than me you won't be able to settle the score here.- Enemies don't feel all that challenging at first until you run into them in numbers or in small closed in areas where it then becomes nearly impossible to do anything at all. Highly unbalanced.- No Tooltips to tell you whats what in your Storage Inventory Items and such. I have something in my inventory that looks like a grenade yet I have no idea what the hell it is until I waste and try to use it or attempt to create it or just try to dismantle it.- Sprinting is kinda permanent and overly fast, it just feels weird, tolerable and different but weird.- The Crafting System is a bit of a mess and trying to get enough loot to craft items just doesn't feel like it is enough, I find myself barely getting enough loot for bullets unless I spent a lot of time just grinding enemies. - Weapon Upgrades are confusing AF, I have no idea what exactly I need to upgrade stuff, its just not obvious nor very clear enough when looking at upgrades for weapons etc to install.- A lot of the time during combat I find myself occasionally getting thrown into a group of objects in the environment that caused me to get stuck or not enough room to focus on the fight because of it which is rather frustrating because there's so many damn meshes in the way. The enemy seems to easily maneuver around and through these objects unfairly but doing this with the player character is not simple nor cohesive whatsoever and either forces you to become a sitting duck that is stuck with a hard time fighting back which almost got me killed on several several times if I didn't keep mashing down the jump button 500 times to get around and through meshes to an open enough area to fight back decently.- Trying to understand the Hawk System etc is rather confusing even though explained, same with the Secret Vaults, like I am really going to even remember all of that.- The Game Map isn't really marked that well unless you hover over things and can be confusing.- Issues with Crafting Window, sometimes the upgrade/install button and ui area will be slightly off the screen to the right making it difficult to know what you're doing with it.- Sneaking System is utterly useless and fails 9 times out of 10 when attempting to sneak quietly past large amounts of enemies in certain areas so you may as well just not even bother with any of it and just go in guns blazing with a plan to destroy everything in your path.- Safe Rooms being Safe my foot! Very broken! In the beginning when you reach the very first Save/Save Room it tells you that you are safe in the room but later on this is entirely untrue and the game is very broken because somehow I have had enemies chase me and enter these rooms therefore they are not safe for saving at all.= VERDICT = ============= Atomic Heart is an atomically astounding game in nearly and it is exactly what we needed in almost every way. It's riveting, interesting, and fun to play and definitely delivers. It is certainly worth the wait and now that it is here I am happy to be playing it. Additionally, be advised there are some false claims saying this is Bioshock 4, this IS NOT Bioshock and it is a completely different game. This game may share some similarities is more of a mix of Bioshock + Far Cry gone wrong, taken over by robot which then threw throws you into a different timeline within a Futuristically Historical Soviet Union Era.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed my time with this game, quite a bit especially later on in its campaign, but it has some issues which I'll lay out here.For starters the game looks great, it's built in Unreal Engine 4 and it shows. It's not the most beautiful game ever but it looks every bit the part of a 2023 game and just as importantly it runs great. I played it maxed at 1440p on an i9/3080/32gb and it ran at a nice high FPS way above 60 throughout most of the game. The most recent major patch, which was applied 3/10/23, seems to have caused some minor occasional hitching for me as I did my final play session to completion here yesterday, especially in the overworld. Not a huge deal but thought I'd mention it.Game has an excellent, excellent soundtrack. Some real bangers in here, but the game doesn't utilize them all that intelligently sometimes. There are some really excellent tracks that only get used for a single fight, and there is little to no combat music for the first 1/3ish of the game which is an odd choice. Overall though it's great, and the in between atmospherics are excellent with tons of environmental noises. In the overworld you can hear the booming and whining of all the crazy technology in the facility, and while inside underground facilities and similar you can hear the banging of pipes and machines and all sorts of other atmospherics. Sound design is mostly excellent like the graphics.Gameplay wise, the game is mostly great but suffers from pacing issues. Combat doesn't really start to come together into something great until about halfway through the game, early on it's just not that fun battling mustache bots with an axe and pistol. However by the end of the game with a full weapon and power loadout of heavily upgraded gear you're a walking machine of destruction and it's a lot of fun. The fully upgraded shotgun and pashtet are absolutely nuts when paired with cryonics and telekinesis. Fights that would have been a massive struggle early on turn into joyous bouts of epic destruction. Crafting is simple but gets the job done, and looting is great - your glove sucks stuff in from a reasonable distance and anything that can't fit in your bag is auto routed to your storage box. It's also worth noting that the game has pretty decent enemy variety, but you guessed it, it takes too long to present them. Ever present the pacing issues, it just kinda permeates the first half of the game - it's not bad by any means early on, but it's not until you leave the VDNH facility or a bit after, which is a solid 8-10 hours into the game, do things really start to click and does the games combat begin to elevate from "acceptable/OK" to "really damn good".Much was made of Atomic Hearts open world prior to release, and while the game does have an open world, it's IMO there more in service to the story and atmosphere than the gameplay. It's really there to provide an emphasis to the size of the facility and demonstrate the feel of the world they created in between major setpiece locations more so than a massive thing meant to be explored extensively. The only real "extra" content present in the open world besides basic scrap loot is the "Testing Grounds" which are big underground complexes of mostly large roomscale puzzles that grant the player with lots of extra scrap for crafting and most importantly blueprints for weapon upgrades. They are optional but collectively they only add about 3-4 hours to the game (there are only 8 of them) and are mostly fun to do, so just go ahead and do them. The later ones also add a good bit of story exposition that fleshes some stuff out and answers some questions the player might have.The story and characters are a mixed bag, but it's really going to depend on the individual player as to how they asses this. The main character, P3, is kind of annoying. He becomes slightly less annoying as the game goes on, and actually even has brief moments of thoughtfulness and endearment later in the game....but he never elevates to anything more than just kinda there. He didn't bother me but he might bother some, just depends. Charles on the other hand starts as just OK and becomes an excellent character as the game progresses and has a lot of great dialogue later on in the game as him and P3 start to soften up to each other, and he eventually becomes a core part of everything that is happening and acts as a very central piece of the game. I don't want to spoil anything, but Charles is great and will say a lot of stuff in later parts of the game that are genuinely thoughtful and chilling/sobering discussions on the role of governments and masters and power dynamics and the human condition and AI and robotics and all sorts of forward thinking subjects that go quite a bit beyond the average game. There is a reason for this as you'll learn, but again, no spoilers, so just know that Charles isn't just a fun AI sidekick. His presence eventually begins to elevate the entire story and game and that is appreciated because the game's story takes way too long to get truly rolling - again, pacing issues, and P3 alone could not have carried the burden of making the story evocative at all. It's also worth mentioning that there are some brief moments where I think the translation was not so perfect, although they are few and far enough in between not to interfere too much and they seem mostly to occur in the first half.The story itself is good, but I can't really explain why without spoiling important elements and plot twists. Those ever present pacing issues dampen the story at first but as you begin to learn more, and realize things are NOT what they seem you'll start to get hooked. The final act of the game especially, the final 4-5 hours, are incredibly intriguing as the situation begins to escalate and go far beyond the scope it's initially presented with. It's one of those stories where "once you know you know" - you can only truly enjoy the story once, so try and appreciate it while it's happening because if you ever want to play it again it will be with an entirely different lens. The ending is....uh....something; it isn't unsatisfying, it isn't particularly overly satisfying either. It's just kinda sudden and shocking. It's not as if the game doesn't answer your questions necessarily, it mostly does, but it's just....I dunno haha you just have to experience it I guess. Like I said you can only truly experience the story once. Overall I really enjoyed my time with Atomic Heart, and I really really enjoyed my time with the final 1/3 of the game in particular. It's not perfect but for a freshman effort it's great - you can tell a lot of love was poured into this project. It's a great game that a lot of gamers will really appreciate, but for all of its charms you can't help but also point at the flaws even if they don't drag the whole experience down too much. 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: A high-quality first-person shooter experience. I LOVED IT. The world is visually appealing and fun to explore. I have a sweet spot for this kind of eerie Communist settings and creepy machines. The game gives you an enormous amount of lore if you want it.The combat mechanics are generally well implemented, too. Neither too hard nor brain-dead easy, the devs nailed it just right. I had no issues playing on normal difficulty ("local malfunction") in my first playthrough and then Armageddon in NG+. There are good variations in both weapons and enemies so you will be rewarded for studying what sort of combat style works best for each particular encounter. If you struggle, use Zvezdochka special attacks. It's broken.Also it was great that the game allows you to redistribute skill points at no cost. That's a good way to encourage trial-and-error experimentation. Many games nowadays set a price and punish the player for resetting skills for no reason, so I really appreciate Atomic Heart's approach.Though, a big negative is the clumsy story telling. This game has a truly INCREDIBLE amount of trash talking that distracts our attention from the story narrative that actually matters. Apart from the cutscenes, dialogues with real substance are few and far between so it's easy to miss them amidst all the crispy critters. This game is definitely leaning toward adrenaline rush FPS so don't expect too much about its RPG aspects.Overall, this game is a no-brainer pick up if you are a Doom-style FPS fan, especially when it's on sale. I got it 60% off and it was worth every penny of it. Recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't need twins, I need a granny that can wield AK and rocket launcher, and watch "Well, just you wait!" all day.Amazing and beautifully done, I was worried as I thought this product could be a vaporware as it went through about 8 years or longer in development, but then there's an old man in Disney said this, "You can't rush art", and look at this Masterpiece called Atomic Heart.Setting in an Utopia universe of post WW2, where USSR has a major breakthrough with the robots, allowing it to co-exist to aid humanity in every way, yes "every" way ;)Art style is very similar to Bioshock Infinite's floating continents, absolutely love it with interior designs, not to mention my most favorite childhood cartoon called "Just you wait!" aka "Nu Pogodi!" is in the game as well. As you play through, you may have to make few judgement calls by yourself, and you have "choices" that will matter with the ending as well. Decision-making can sometimes be difficult, but that's why you should talk to every corpse and read every mails. Yes... I am serious, you can talk to corpses, gather clues or have a bit of chit-chat as your journey is mostly filled with robots that do not want to be intergraded with you, while some leafy-faced monsters want to have a fresh lunch.Combat systems are smart and exciting, and your enemies, aka, robots, they're not on power-preserve mode either, they're smart, they will dodge your heavy attacks, etc, but as humans, we must play smarter and better. Before you mindlessly swing your melee non-stop and gun blazing, observe the robot attack patterns, and make good use of dodge systems.Music pace will change as you go full commando mode in open area with high alert levels or multiple enemies, and boss fight music will get you in full adrenaline mode.Crafting systems is just as good as Fallout, every resource, from ammo to metal pieces you've been collecting, they all will come in handy and you always can't have enough of them. Be sure to pay visit to the fridge mommy, aka Nora, to upgrade your arsenals.Unlock abilities while improving your character, as you walk past trails of robot junks, be sure to always salvage anything from them with your Glove. I managed to max out my character's hp and get him deep pockets, turning him into a freaky god-mighty Jedi.Inventory systems is similar to Resident Evil 4, as you can manage your consumables, ammo, and guns in a limited space, which can be increased thanks to fridge mommy. Do not worry about carrying too much items, as any loot you collected when you have no pockets, they will be automatically sent to fridge mommy's storage.Smart saving systems, they will always be near Fridge Mommy, and always save for you before a boss fight.And no, you Cripsy Critters! YOU CANNOT INTERGRADE WITH THE TWINS, STOP!TWINS ARE TEMPORARY, FRIDGE MOMMY AND AK NANNY ARE FOREVER!

_childDocuments_.review: This game built itself up with extremely interesting teasers and showcases featuring bizarre architecture, strange mechanical devices, and the promise of a wild and deep mystery. On one hand, the game delivers. Every lab or underground lair you visit has this bizarre twinge of brutal devices carrying out strange tasks, seemingly nonsensical scientific experiments, and wild technology that seems almost like magic. Unfortunately, the game ruins all of this because Every single time you encounter one of these wonderful and horrible creations or experiments your companion character immediately explains exactly what's going on and the purpose of what you're looking at. You'll enter a room with giant, rotating platforms, strange mannequins strewn about, and a bizarre floating goo, and instead of letting you take time to digest what you're looking at and try to puzzle out what all this could be for, your companion will butt in and say "oh this is just how we test rockets," which makes what your looking at paradoxically banal and unbelievable. I enjoy a good technical explanation of strange technology in settings like Mass Effect, Warhammer 40k, or Death Stranding, but in a game that hinges on mystery and the bizarre, this ruins the effect immediately.Speaking of mystery, there isn't one. You immediately know who the villain and what you'll be fighting, and the only twists this game comes up with come completely out of nowhere and are either inconsequential or completely unbelievable. None of the characters come off as compelling, mostly just one-note actors going through motives we can't really relate to because they're either complete monsters or just idiots. A character like Andrew Ryan can be a complete monster but you learn enough about him to make him interesting, to really learn his points of view. Despite how much this game talks about the main villain and his views, I never felt I really knew who I was fighting, just some card-carrying villain who had to be shot.As for the gameplay, the reason it took me so long to get to it is because it's largely just fine. The weapons are fun and customizable in ways that suit your playstyle, and a lot of them are satisfying with a good punch. The powers are serviceable but never feel that substation, and the enemy variety is slightly lacking but decent enough. None of it ever felt tactical however. Most AI will typically just rush you down with little thought, or hang slightly back to shoot at you. I never had moments where an AI would try to go around and flank me or try to retreat for a better opportunity, it all felt very basic. In addition, with how many healing supplies you can carry and how prolific supplies are, I never truly felt challenged.This game also has no reason to be open world. The only collectable upgrades or items you can get are located in specific bonus buildings. There's never any reason to go off and explore or see what's over the next hill, no side quests or interesting locations, just a bunch of copy-pasted buildings and mindless driving that quickly becomes little more than a commute.Overall I really did want to like this game, and it just so borders on being good. If there was ever a mod released that completely cut out any of the over-explanatory dialogue, that would probably push this game to a recommend, but as it stands, it kills any sense of mystery the moment it happens and doesn't have a plot strong enough to carry its decent but inconsistent and simple gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: I think the first thing you should be prepared for in this game is a bizarre world that is very reminiscent of a Russian version of Bioshock. But apart from the 'flair' of the USSR, it is also a world with many boring building complexes, without much recognition value or uniqueness, which you have to fight your way through.Basically, I was always happy when I finally got back out into the daylight of the open hub area, which connects the complexes with each other. There it is much nicer (green sunny nature) and more interesting, even if you hardly have the opportunity to actually explore it without being disturbed all the time. You are constantly annoyed by enemies that spawn over and over again and quickly increase their party size. This leads to chaotic situations in which you are constantly attacked and knocked over from all sides. If you try to run away, they will follow you across the map until you have destroyed them.Other parts of the game including climbing and puzzles. First one were often tightrope acts, as the character often doesn't do what it's supposed to do, especially when jumping. The puzzles, on the other hand, were medium. Basically, I welcome a greater variety of puzzle types and some of them (for example the puzzle rooms where you have to move plateaus) are well designed. But there are also several fiddly (or buggy) puzzle mechanics that are more annoying than fun due to their implementation. For example, sometimes you have to throw balls to a specific receiver. You cannot use your crosshairs as a guide when aiming. It can happen that the ball lands in a corner of the room from which you cannot get it out again. This means you have to restart the level to try again. Another example are the time-based mini-games for opening special doors (you must press a button when one of several lights is flashing). Fortunately, you can deactivate this variant in the game settings.This kind of quicktime action also exists in some boss fights. In the final boss fight, I think it's buggy because I still died even though I pressed the right button at the right time. After several attempts, I simply pressed all the gamepad buttons at the same time for the entire scene, then it somehow accepted it after all.Finally, there is the story, which is actually interesting and a little philosophical with its utopia about a new social life and discussions about endless life, death or free will. But the main character gives you the feeling that you've come across a defiant toddler. Every time he opens his mouth, he attracts attention through arrogance, stupidity or irascibility.In conclusion I would say there are some good approaches (puzzles, story, shooter part), but also problems in the game mechanics or implementation. The game graphics are quite good and the same applies for the sound. The background music (not in-world music like radio) is often loud and droining. I turned it off at a certain point because it gave me a headache.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll give it a 7.5/10. I bought the premium edition (pass with glove, AK and Звёздочка skins).Minus 1 for the difficulty curve that keeps it entertaining in the very beginning, but flattens out and altogether plummets after a certain point in the game where you're just either fervently looting or nonchalantly dismantling mobs of bots and zombies along with unneeded ammo and unnecessary consumables to feed your arsenal. Only a few instances kept it interesting, especially where I was able to activate 3 Плющs and have them gang up on me. That, or the other times where you had gaggles of plant zombies coming at you. Bosses were also underwhelming with the variety (or lack thereof) of attack patterns. Mind you, I expected a challenge from Armageddon where game even warned about counting your ammo (I ended up counting the seconds between dismantling them). Mobs were interesting at first, but got boring after a while, I'd have liked more variety.Minus 0.5 for the bugs. You'd think they'd iron out *most* of the glitches in this game after 5 years of development (e.g. stuck in textures, uninteractable characters, unlootable loot, etc.)Minus another 0.5 for slightly unpolished design where there were literal blanks in map development, where you just cannot access certain loot/places.And minus the last 0.5 for weapon and upgrade choices. Some are just outright useless (The Fox, The Dominator, etc.).On the other hand...Amazing optimization to the point where I thought Atomic graphics would melt my laptop (2060 RTX, Ryzen 4800H, 1 GB SSD), but ended up just dropping fps to around 20. Hence, I was able to get a stable 60 most of the time on Ultra.Gunplay is great, satisfying and fairly realistic. Story was well-written enough to throw me for a loop with ХРАЗ and Сеченов's story. Environment was beautiful with only the occasional cheap cop outs (white background due to the sun? Come on, Mundfish).I didn't play with English audio nor text (and for good reason, according to comments and reviews), I can only say the Russian voice acting was great, very grounded and realistic, even though I expected more obscenities (then again, this IS the USSR and people were slightly more reserved with their swearing back then). Штокхаузен's German accent in Russian was great and added to the USSR experience.Eleonora, lmao. The actress must have had a field day with her lines XD.And The Twins. The devs gave them and the ballerina bots metallic nipples. What else is there to say? All in all, great game, cons notwithstanding. Would definitely recommend and will gladly play through the DLCs and grab AH2. Hopefully devs read reviews and deal with their bugs.
