_childDocuments_.review: What a brilliant game. I'm still unsure over what surprised me more about this game - the fact that the gameplay continuously remained fresh and fantastic or the elusively compact story and character writing. And yes seriously, even though the characters in this game look like Sesame Street stand-ins, each and every one of them present such compelling arcs that urge you to interact with them as much as possible. The entire game is a surprise in the best possible sense. Catching each and every uniquely designed Bugsnax is a treat within itself - that core gameplay loop never becomes stale thanks to the large variety of methods and strategies the game allows you to experiment with when it comes to snagging one. Mixing and matching the tools in your arsenal to fashion more effective methods of capture never gets old - and the game pushes you to even utilise Bugsnax themselves in your experimentation, which leads to even more fun and super satisfying outcomes when it all comes together. Can't stress enough how much I enjoyed the gameplay, real surprise it never got stale at any point. As with the gameplay loop, the game also provides you a surprising amount of customization when it comes to your home or even the characters around you, freely being able to transform each of them into any of the 112 Bugsnax present in the game. In short, every playable facet of the game gives the player tons of room to experiment - so it never gets old.The story, as many of those interested in this game may have heard, does indeed have a darker side to it. One of my fears going into this is that it would just be a random dark twist towards the end of the game - and while events towards the end are certainly more darker in tone compared to everything prior, there is a subtle dark tone of mystery that pervades the entire game, portrayed through ancient murals or elusive figures hiding in the dark... there are certainly secrets to be found that give the game a really compelling depth. The story never slowed for me personally, as its driven largely by a central mystery - one that really tickles your curiosity and keeps you going to discover more. The darker tones in particular are an awesome contrast against the generally light-natured surface of the game. I would write further about the characters, but this review is already so long and I'm tired - but I urge you to play it for yourself to find out. At the beginning, many of them aren't particularly likeable - at least I felt so - but the fact that I came to genuinely care for each and every one of them, even the ones that irritated me the most at first, is a testament to the progression they all go through, depending on whether you choose to interact with them or not. And the game actively pushes you to do so - the main story is essentially about uniting a town broken by strife and fighting, so even if some characters irk you at first, caring for one of them will eventually encourage you to try reaching out to the others more. Its great. My personal favourites are probably Snorpy, Floofty, Wambus and surprisingly Beffica. Chandlo deserves a shout-out too. My only complaint - and this isn't neccessarily a fault of the game - is that I personally placed too much stock in the "Psychological Horror" tag. Having been meaning to buy this game long before I finally did, my expectations of Bugsnax was morphed by continuously seeing people call it a horror and parade its darker tones - which made me expect far too much of that. So yes, personally I would say that the psychological horror tag on the game isn't warranted, but maybe that's cause my expectations for it in that regard were far too high. On the other hand, if you went into this game really just expecting a fun child-like game, then I can definitely see why you'd come away and slap a horror tag on it! TLDR: Play this game, you won't regret it. Pure fun.Edit: Even though this came out in 2020, I'm voting it as Steam GOTY. Because it is.

_childDocuments_.review: I picked up Bugsnax on sale because I had seen marketing for it a while ago, and being a fan of Pokemon and other creature collectors, I figured this would be fun. The story is a little off-kilter, but given the design of the game's monsters, it really works with the setting and other characters you interact with. The creature designs and names are cute and creative, and it was always fun seeing what new Bugsnax would appear in every new locale I visited.My first takeaway was the visuals. Overall I just wish it was sharper or cleaner. Considering this was a PS5 launch title, I'm surprised the PC port doesn't give the user options to increase the resolution scaling or other graphical options to improve the visuals. Secondly, it was a bit short; my playthrough clocked in at just under 6 hours, although I didn't engage much with the post game side quests and other content. In my opinion, the mechanics and runtime meshed together well, as I wouldn't have wanted to keep playing much longer to finish the game as is.The rest of the game was fine. Really, that's about all I have to say about it. By the end, I was more interested in just finishing the game than doing all the side objectives because I wasn't really having a lot of fun. I think that if there was more to the Bugsnax mechanic (like a cooking minigame, or maybe creating fusions of Snax) other than just catching them, I would be incentivized to explore the game's mechanics and catch rare Bugsnax. If a sequel is ever made, I'd love to see them add more depth to the Snax themselves. Overall I'd recommend Bugsnax, but only if it's on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: If this game was one of the bugsnax, it would be a nothing burger. There are some positives like the voice acting and a few clever ideas with capturing the bugs using interesting methods, plus the character design is pretty original even if it's not my favorite. The bugsnax themselves are cute and well made. Beyond that though, some of the bug catching solutions are more tedious than anything by trying to lure bugs over to each other with varying success or having arbitrary immunities to certain traps that don't make sense. The story I thought started off fine and near the end I thought it might actually get interesting with a big twist, but the finale was so meh and out of the blue that it didn't even manage to land that right. Another thing that brings the experience down imo is how many of the characters are defined by their romantic relationships. It's quite literally like 80% of them with some pretty upfront lgbt representation that doesn't really feel like it had the story in mind first and foremost. It's just not very nuanced and the whole game felt less immersive than when I started. Despite the praise, I wouldn't really recommend although it's not outright terrible.

_childDocuments_.review: Summary/Concerns: I loved the cheery aura from this game and genuinely looked forward playing each day. I was initially concerned about the reviews which stated there were same-sex couples involved, but their presence (although completely unnecessary) does not affect the game play to an extent that makes this unplayable. It is not a horror game in the slightest and will not give adults (or children) nightmares. The plot: You are an investigator who arrives in Snaxburg to investigate the disappearance of a famous explorer. When you arrive, you learn the explorer's disappearance led to the vacancy of the town as the residents could not get along with each other. It becomes your job to bring the inhabitants back to town and interview them so as to solve the mystery of her disappearance. The Gameplay: There are multiple islands to discover; each with different kinds of bugsnax. These bugsnax tend to repeat themselves between islands (ie a kweeble vs a yellow kweeble), but they may add an additional feature such as the bugsnax now being on fire (which changes how it can be captured). This can make gameplay a little boring at times if you are expecting all new and exciting bugsnax to capture, but it's usually backed up with a few new kind of bugsnax that you need to figure out how to capture. There are multiple weapons which you obtain throughout your journeys as well as multiple types of sauce that can be used as a weapon. You may need to wait until discovering certain weapons to capture certain bugsnax. There are also big boss bugsnax to defeat. Main missions, side quests, and mail (which are basically just more side quests) drive the game which is backed by a story line explained throughout the entire game (although it does get dialogue heavy towards the end). You can also choose to go hunting for bugsnax by free roaming while completing missions. Difficulty Level: There is not a health bar in this game which makes it very relaxing. The only way you can "die" is by falling off a cliff or the map which is not concerning because the game saves as you go. After 33 hours of playtime, I was able to complete ALL the achievements. Discovering how to capture bugsnax can be challenging at times, especially for a young child, but as an adult I was able to capture all the bugsnax (eventually).

_childDocuments_.review: On its face, Bugsnax is a relaxing first-person exploration game about using traps to collect bugs.In its heart, Bugsnax is a game about making new friends and then turning them into food abominations. Overall the game is very chill, except for when the really weird stuff happens, such as when mad scientist Floofty Fizzlebean asks you to chop their head off. You can explore different biomes, talk to the grumpuses, and customize your bungalo. Don't get eaten by a pizza.

_childDocuments_.review: Bugsnax is the most mid game in existence. In a world of so many more interesting and worthwhile games, like ULTRAKILL, TUNIC, and Elden Ring, a mediocre game like Bugsnax is not worth your time.It has:* A generic, cliche story* Mediocre, uninspired art style, with little visual flare* Boring ass dialogue* Mid voice acting by the grumpuses* Generic gameplay* Simple, flat, boring level designThe most interesting thing about the game is the namesake bug-catching mechanics, which, while having gotten the most focus out of any aspect of the game, still manage to be barely on par with Ape Escape Academy in terms of fun factor, player expression, and overall game feel. Also, the funny voice acting for the bugsnax is entertaining for a couple seconds every time you hear "Bunger!" or "Bopsicle!".Much of the quests involve - you guessed it - catching bugsnax, and it doesn't vary much from that. Unless you reeealy like catchin' those snax and listening to cringy, cliche dialogue, you're gonna have a rough time pushing through this game, much like I did.Maybe I'd recommend it to a young kid, who might be a more appropriate audience for this game, but even then there are plenty of much better alternative games I'd let a child play before touching Bugsnax. (Think Kirby, Mario Kart, etc.)All in all, you dont get much beyond what you see in the trailer, and if that doesn't absolutely captivate you from the first 5 seconds, i'd say skip this one.

_childDocuments_.review: On the one hand, this is a fun, cute silly little game... Lovely graphics, interesting gameplay, generally engaging plot, etc.On the other hand, it's the most aggressively misandrist game I've played in a long time. The way the characters are presented is EXACTLY what you'd expect from a game that introduces itself with the clunkiest depiction of a lesbian couple ever written. E.G.: The mayor (Filbo) is a kind, well-meaning guy trying to hold the (horrible) community members together after their founder disappeared. But everyone - EVERYONE - hates him and is abusive to him for no reason. The farmer (Wambus) is literally trying to save the colony from starvation, but the game is VERY clear that his wife's archaeological digs are more important than his agriculture; you help them reconcile, which ends with him agreeing to help with her digs...but her treating helping on the farm like some kind of ridiculous proposition. The rancher (Gramble) is presented as a bumbling idiot who foolishly loves the bugsnax like his family. All the female characters though? Well, they're exactly what'd you expect. They're all narcissists...but you can tell the writers didn't think they were. It's...awful. I legitimately hate everyone except Filbo. Is that the point? Is it supposed to be about the juxtaposition between the cartoony, childish characters and how horrible everyone except Filbo is? JUSTICE FOR FILBO. AND WAMBUS.

_childDocuments_.review: There's a lot I want to say on Bugsnax. First and foremost, it's a phenomenal game. Young Horses is a very talented team of developers that know how to create engaging characters in unique settings. That being said, I was biased and had high hopes for the game, and I think those hopes were definitely met, but there's a few key things that bothered me just a little bit that are a blemish on an otherwise incredible enjoyable experience.The gameplay cycle is very simple and satisfying. Anyone that enjoys creature collection, from Animal Crossing to Pokémon, will find that the way it works in Bugsnax is more akin to a puzzle than anything. Every time you discover a new region, it's exciting to see all the different Bugsnax, and I immediately found myself brainstorming "okay, how do I catch this one"? Each Bugsnax is a thought exercise on how to potentially catch them, and the variety in ways to catch them, including multiple ways to achieve doing so, are quite nice and it feels good. The small nitpick I have here is that the number of variant Bugsnax is quite high, and it feels like about 50% of them is just a copy of the same Bugsnax, but in a different color and a slightly different method of catching. This isn't a big deal, but it is less fun.The characters are fantastic and lovable, they mimic real people and are quite believable in a lot of ways. The dynamics and interactions feel really smooth and natural and it's a big reason of why the game doesn't feel like a chore. Many games struggle coming up with characters that are fun or funny which then lowers your investment. Even the inclusion of gay couples don't feel forced, in fact, I'd point to this being one the best game examples for how to do LGBT+ writing properly.Now, the story. It's... a mess. The setting and lore are great, but the way the story progresses is very hamfisted, without spoiling anything, the reason you're even beginning your adventure in the first place does not make sense once you see the full ending. There's also a lack of critical thinking among everyone; the game really does not stop for one second to make it's plot twist any more obvious. From the beginning it's painfully clear what's going to happen and the truth behind Bugsnax, and I don't even need to tell you what it is for you to already know. This is a shame, because I feel like more could have been done with it, and a subversion of a subversion may have been more enjoyable.The OST is quite nice actually, it hits a fantastic sweet spot between cute and adventurous, they're mostly light-hearted tracks that make you want to go out and explore, which I think is a great tone for the majority of the game that just works with the setting. But the soundtrack doesn't struggle to become more heavy when necessary either. Seth Parker did a good job on it.In summary, minus a few shortcomings, Bugsnax is really a great game anyone who enjoys this genre owes themselves to try. The environments are neat and the semi-metroidvania aspects of the way the progression works make it fun to come back to older areas, too. If you don't read too much into the plot the game is trying to weave, and you're just having fun with the gameplay and enjoy the character banter, you're in for a thoroughly enjoyable time.

The colorful visuals, cheerful soundtrack, and lighthearted tone create an atmosphere that’s perfect for a chill gaming session. It’s the ideal escape after a long day, allowing me to immerse myself in a joyful adventure without feeling pressured.Overall, I highly recommend Bugsnax for anyone looking for a captivating and relaxing experience in VR. _childDocuments_.review: One of my all-time favourite games. Completed it fully twice, done all the achievements. Why do I go back to it? Simple, it's fun, it's creative, it has surprising depth, and above all else it has such wonderful characters and writing. People talk a lot about representation in gaming, and despite being a silly goofy about fuzzy grumpuses on an island, it has genuinely wonderful characters, and has moments where you genuinely feel for or adore them. That is not a common thing in his medium.Gameplay summary, you run around a variety of areas on a strange island discovering bizarre food/bug hybrids, and catching them. Some are easy, others require specific tactics and tools. All the while, you're meeting a cast of bizarre characters each with stories, items and quests. As you progress you unlock more areas, more tools, more bugsnax and quests both big and small. As you do all this you're getting rewards to decorate your house back in town, and figuring out the mystery of Snaktooth island.All in all, this is a must-play for fans of fun. There's a good amount of depth here, lots of sub-missions, and some genuinely quite complex tactics to catch certain Bugsnax. Enough to keep you engaged throughout the whole experience. Play it!

_childDocuments_.review: Not my typical style of game, I played this on a recommend from my brother. I still absolutely highly recommend, even if it doesn't look like your normal style, due to its fresh feeling gameplay and well-polished (horror-ish almost) story.Game may look like a pokemon copycat, but it feels closer in style to games like A Hat in Time (minus the core focus on platforming). Your focus is not necessarily to "catch them all" but to use the bugsnax to progress and uncover the story.I do recommend you do the side mailbox quests, they have some fun interactions with bugsnax that you don't see otherwise in the main game (they focus on proc'ing specific interactions between bugsnax, solving clues, or a few speedrunning type quests).The game is definitely best played without looking at the trailer or too many screenshots. Part of the fun is the The character's backstories are some of my favorite parts, which you can only uncover through their side quests  is the voice of Gramble and he does a superb job, but once you realize that, its hard to unhear .TL;DR Great unique game with fresh gameplay and intriguing story. Psychological horror user-defined steam tag is deserved.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall impression: 9.5 out of 10. A great buy at full price. Bugsnax is clever, fun, and well designed all the way through. It is one of the best all-round games I have played in a long time.I will try to do a quick breakdown of what makes the game great without giving too many details. Players should dive in with little knowledge about the game and enjoy the ride.Pros: Deft writing that makes you care for even the more distasteful characters. Catching bugs is fun and requires a bit of puzzle solving without being overly complex. The overarching story is great. Learning about the various characters, their relationships, and the secrets of the island and the bugsnax is a great trip.Cons: I am having to nitpick, since the game is so good. Some of the mail challenges are either too obtuse or require way too much running around the island. The bugsnax on the DLC island are clever, but they lean too much toward being annoying in how you have to puzzle out how to capture them while avoiding the other bugsnax in the area.Conclusion: I read the great reviews and went in without spoilers. I am glad I did. Bugsnax is one of the best games I have played in a very long time.

_childDocuments_.review: isn't a perfect game, but it has a lot of heart.You play as a reporter who has answered the call to Snaktooth Isle, the supposed home of the titular, legendary Bugsnax, creatures that are "half bug, half snack." Not long before crashing on the island, you find out that the residents of the island are having problems and must help them to pursue your story. This, of course, mostly involves catching Bugsnax.The characters all have a charm once you get to know them, and the Snax themselves are all creative and cute. Some more so than others.Now, whenever a game like this comes out, the inevitable happens: comparisons to Pokémon. Other than being collectible critters that say their portmanteau pun names, there isn't much else that's similar.Unfortunately, the game does get a bit repetitive. In order to catch a Bugsnak, you need to figure out how to do so. Some can easily be caught by laying a trap in front of their path or even just walking up to them with your net. Others require using your different tools together, but none of them are truly that hard to get. The game is definitely geared for younger audiences in this regard.In the end, I overall enjoyed playing , and I would love to see the series expanded into something more.Also, *ahem* BUNGERBUNGERBUNGERBUNGERBUNGER!!!

_childDocuments_.review: GAME OF THE YEAR... ok not really, but it was a great game. The gameplay is mostly about doing quests for the characters, which usually involves finding and capturing Bugsnax. Each Bugsnax has their own quirks and patterns, and you must use your tools, the environment, and other Bugsnax to capture them. The Bugsnax themselves have simple yet creative designs based on food and googly eyes, and they are very cute thanks to the excellent voice acting.This voice acting also helps with the story and character development, which is top notch. Each of the characters has well defined personalities, and the game explores their personal and psychological problems. Progressing on the main story and the sidequests makes you feel like you're helping them towards overcoming their problems, or at least, helping them understand them.The main story involves finding all the characters that are scattered through the island, interviewing them and gathering clues on the dissapearence of the town's leader (Lizbert) and the nature of the Bugsnax themselves. There's quite some lore, and the big mystery isn't revealed until the very end of the game (try to avoid spoilers!)Be warned that, while the game is overall very cute, the final segment of the game can be a bit disturbing, so I don't recommend this game to little kids and people who can't stomach abrupt changes like these easily. Otherwise, I highly recommend checking it out.

_childDocuments_.review: Made for more mature audiences, the core story handles serious topics with a focus on relationships and the many, many ways they can and likely will go wrong. The game presents itself as bright and cheery but takes dark and serious turns that keep you on edge. it gets gradually darker as you progress, to a particularly jarring boiling point. BUIt has a compelling narrative, and I thoroughly enjoyed every single character. Each character and their flaws had a very realistic and well understood approach and presentation, and I truly felt the gravity of their unique situations.  NGThe gameplay is similar to pokemon, with more elaborate mechanics for catching different bugsnax. as you progress to new areas you unlock new tools that make the process gradually more complex until in some cases catching a snak feels like solving a puzzle. Catch bugsnax, complete quests, learn about your fellow villagers, and learn about what bugsnax are. ERAn unforgettable experience. 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: spoiler-free review!id like to preface this by saying i never write reviews but i felt obligated to here as this is one of my favorite games of all time.  the devs have done an incredible job on this game and the content update is no exception.i played through bugsnax when it first released, and just finished my second 100% playthrough on steam.  this game has been on my mind since launch, i desperately wanted it on steam for the achievement hunting and oh boy was it worth getting a second time!  i would have played through again despite the update, but i was pleasantly surprised by the amount of content that has been added since initial launch.  if youre a completionist like me, the update will bring you many more hours of gameplay with collecting things and new challenges presented to you.  there are some cute cosmetic aspects as well that i really enjoyed playing with.  not to mention how much lore they added!  there is a ton of lore and character development squeezed into the update, it was incredibly satisfying connecting the dots and theorizing things as i played through with friends.  we were all very happy to stumble upon the new worldbuilding; it really put the cherry on top of an already amazing game.if youve played this game before, enjoyed it, and havent experienced the new content yet, id say its definitely worth getting a second time -- especially if youd like to support the devs.if youve never played, but you like creature collection games and quirky little worlds, definitely give it a shot!!10/10 and i recommend this game to everyone.  cant wait to revisit it again next year!

_childDocuments_.review: Bugsnax is probably one of my top 5 favorite games in recent years. This game not only has adorable graphics, fun and varied environments, a plethora of cute and silly creatures to discover, and interesting mechanics that allow you to experiment and find your own methods of progressing - it also has one of the best stories in a game that I've seen. The developers also added free DLC earlier this year - the Isle of BIGsnax - which added even more story content, lore, and cute game features at absolutely no extra charge.The story topics are presented in a way that is approachable for older children and adults alike, with humor mixing in perfectly alongside more serious discussions that don't talk down to their audience. The characters feel real and have real issues; difficulties with intimacy, with their self-worth, with their mental health, and with their place in the world. Through the course of the game you are able to follow the characters in how they try to confront these issues, and there are some extremely good life lessons in there which I think anyone of any age would do well to think on. And, of course, the characters are funny muppets eating food-shaped creatures with googly eyes - the game knows this and knows how ridiculous it is, and isn't afraid to poke fun at itself at times. All in all, it's a wonderful experience and well worth the time and money.

_childDocuments_.review: Bugsnax is like if Pokémon and Ant-Man had a weird, adorable baby and then sent it to therapy. This game is an absolutely delightful fever dream where you hunt down snack-themed bugs — think Spaghetti Squash and Cheddarfly — and then you… feed them to your friends? Yeah, it’s that kind of game.You’re on an island full of eccentric creatures who talk like they’re one bad day away from forming a support group. The gameplay? You catch Bugsnax using an assortment of wacky tools, like a slingshot that shoots ketchup (because, of course, that’s how you catch a hotdog-shaped bug). The real twist, though? You feed them to the island’s residents, who transform into half-man, half-snack monstrosities. Ever wanted to see a person with a Strawberry Nose or a Hotdog Arm? Now you can, and it's... unsettlingly hilarious.The story is surprisingly deep for a game where you’re literally “catching” bite-sized creatures, with emotional moments hidden behind the goofy exterior. It’s like eating a delicious cake while realizing it’s a bit existential.If you like quirky games that don’t take themselves too seriously but still manage to sneak in some heart, Bugsnax is your snack of choice. Just, uh, maybe don’t think too much about what happens to those poor Bugsnax after they’ve been eaten. 🍔🐜

_childDocuments_.review: A mixed bag if ever there was one. Not really a positive or negative review; again, maybe one day we'll get a mixed option. sees you on Snacktooth Island, a land of creatures called bugsnax: half bug, half snack. You are a grumpus, some strange muppet-like creature, invited along for an expedition by a famed adventurer and her team of quirky companions. Things aren’t as simple as they seem though…Firstoff, and far and away, the best part of this game are the titular bugsnax. Their voice lines are perfect, and while some designs are a bit generic, others work quite well and leak charm. Hearing a giant popsicle scream “Paletoooooooss!!” as it burns to death in lava always got a good chuckle out of me. Cinnasnail and Hunnabee had adorable voices. And of course. Bunger. Needs no introduction.As for the rest? Well… it’s hit and miss. The main gameplay is catching bugsnax, either by luring them into a trap, or stunning them and catching them in a net. Some of them were fun challenges to overcome, though once you get the  most encounters are absolutely trivial. They did better in this on the extra island (DLC I think), and overall the mechanics and puzzle aspects showed through best there. (Minus the ball puzzles, they were awful) The game revolves around catching said bugsnax to feed to the expedition members in order to get them to return to town before you can look for the final member: the leader, Elizabert, who vanished without a trace one day. The gameplay loop is crude, but fun. Though by the time you get to late game grumpuses, you’ll probably be fatigued and catching the right snax will seem like more of cleanup than an exciting puzzle.The story is… there. Leader is missing, look for clues, look for expedition members, help with their snax-related problems, and so on, until you have enough to work with to find Lizbert proper. It has an air of mystery and foreboding… that they totally fumble at the end. Now, the twist in this game was predictable before you even played it. That is fine. I would be disappointed if they didn’t take the clear through line. However, it sounds off so lukewarm, worse than lukewarm in fact. As for the characters, they’re the cliches. The jock, the pop star, the bratty gossip, the conman, the stubborn farmer, and so on. They were fine, none struck me as too endearing nor too offensive. They just populated a town and gave you things to do. Admittedly, I didn’t care about the relationships and  not the romance, and watching two grumpuses make out with cookies and doughnuts for teeth is a visual I could have lived without. Especially because it’s kind of over-the-top, really distracting, and not really on theme in my game about setting hot dog snakes on fire and shooting ice cream beetles with hot sauce and stuff.Also, this game is oddly a big downer. Every single sidequest ends with you crushing the grumpus’ dreams, whether reasonable or not. Maybe it’s because you’re a journalist and that’s what they’re best at these days, haha, but still, it never hit well. I know most people hate every character in this game (I only really hate Lizbert; Clumby is 100% right about her from the start), but I found them at least a little endearing in some ways. Kinda disappointing to just systematically dump on all of them throughout the game. They almost all end up worse off than when you start with them.One other note, the horror in this game is borderline nonexistent. I got so excited seeing a monster prowl around town on the first party night. It was subtle, it was creepy, it was great. It never got anywhere close to feeling that tense after that. They should have gone full on with the horror, or not bothered. They walk the tightrope and thus it feels more like a waste than anything. More like mood whiplash. There could have been better ways to ease in the horror, but I digress.My reviews always seem very negative, and I’m sorry. For what it’s worth, I enjoyed most of my time with the game; it offered a decent challenge, and I loved the bugsnax a ton. It appealed to me but I also have a spot for relaxing not-too-challenging games, especially in between torture sessions with harder titles. Would I recommend it? Eh, if you want your weird fuzzy gremlin romance or if you like trying to do some creature catcher puzzle stuff, it’s fun. But once you’re about halfway through the game, there isn’t a whole lot of growth on the capture mechanics and strategy, sans the DLC. The DLC was better overall (minus Chandlo’s  ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥,) it left more mystery and intrigue than the resolution of the main game at least. Overall, uh… if it sounds like it’s for you, maybe get it on sale. There isn’t much replay value in it, it’s more a puzzle game than a creature collector. If you are not interested, then at least look up the bunger audio on YouTube or something. Trust me, you need to hear it.

_childDocuments_.review: A strange but enjoyable game that I'm having a hard time classifying. You play as a journalist that's trying to get an interview with a renowned explorer but your boss (Laharl) is having none of it. You decide to find them anyway and go to an island that has an abundance of these adorable small creatures known as the Bugsnax. When you eat one a body part becomes whatever it was you ate. Well not you personally, you can't eat.  The game is a loop of finding someone, getting them to come back to the town that has been established, then a new area opens  up, rinse and repeat. While going to new areas you will complete side quests to better get to know the inhabitants and their overall point as to why they came to the island. Some stories didn't really do anything for me while others where oddly gripping. Not to spoil anything but there was a guillotine in one of them. The main story itself was interesting enough and by the end I was pretty happy with what I got from the game. Gameplay wise aside from the side quests you will essentially play Pokemon and catch all the Bugsnax to fill up your book full of entries. Not much else. That being said I was happy they let it come off of being an exclusive and put it on Steam. For $25 I can say it is worth the time to play. Also once you get an ending it unlocks a new island as DLC so don't think it's over just yet!

_childDocuments_.review: An interesting game for all ages. The "overwhelmingly positive" is a bit of a misleading (I'd say it's a solid 8/10 game, without question) take on it. despite having a whole collection of tools and biomes to explore, it seemed like every bugsnax was essentially caught in 1 of 4 possible ways: put it in an opposing element, use 2-3 tools in a row, make one bugsnax attack another, or just toss a basic trap down and catch it easily. Since this is the ONLY gameplay in the entire game, I was a bit let down...but the short length is a blessing for this game! Beatable in 8-10 hours easily, so I have a feeling the devs knew their gameplay was a little weak. The narrative is alright, but its strength is in the characters and their development, not the actual story arc, which is reminiscent if every Resident Evil plot ever, but presented in a Muppet style, and to be honest not very satisfying. If it wasn't for the character development, I don't think I'd be recommending this game because the main arc and the gameplay really aren't that interesting once you get over the whole "they eat bugsnax and it changes their bodies" concept. If anything at all looks interesting in this game to you, 100% play it. But if you watch the trailers and you don't think it looks like your cup of tea, just move on to the next game. Bugsnax is a great game with a lot of love put into it, but its not a "must play" for everyone.

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE: Okay, my curiosity got the best of me, and I came back and finished the game. I still agree with everything I said below. The main mechanics of the game (capturing Bugsnax) are clunky and annoying. Sometimes you set up one of your tools correctly, but it just doesn't activate correctly. Sometimes a Bugsnak gets in your way while you're trying to capture another one. Most times, capturing is tedious, weirdly exact, and frustrating. For example, there's a Bugsnak that leaps from tree to tree. It cannot be captured while it's IN the tree. It needs to be grabbed or tripped during the brief moment it's leaping. But the best tool in the game, the tripwire, can only be placed on specific surfaces. So I needed to find somewhere I could place one end of the tripwire (I balanced it on the side of a tree), find somewhere close enough where I could stick the other end, hope desperately the tripwire was at the right height to trip the leaping Bugsnak (it's really hard to tell!), and then just wait for the darn Bugsnack to decide to leap between those exact trees. There are a ton of hints for puzzles involving the Grumpus characters (you often have VERY limited options for tools and locations, so it's obvious what you're meant to do), but the Bugsnax puzzles give you no hints and sometimes have weird and overly complicated solutions.Another capture required luring an ice Bugsnak to attack a fire Bugsnak. You can't capture a Bugsnak that's on fire, so the ice Bugsnak puts out the fire and lets you capture it. Clever, right? Yeah, except the fire Bugsnak is in LAVA, and you can't place any of your tools in LAVA, and you can't walk in lava, and oh yeah, the fire Bugsnak relights itself after a few seconds. Luring it out of the lava is annoying and adds a lot of steps, but it must be done -- oh, but you also have other Bugsnax randomly attacking you and throwing YOU into lava while you're trying to accomplish this. Oh, and the fire Bugsnax keep throwing the ice Bugsnack in the lava too, so it loses its freezing ability (making it useless) and it's nearly impossible to get it back out again.Is there a better solution to that? Maybe. A lot of the time, I couldn't tell if I was solving things in a roundabout way, or if this WAS the correct solution and I just needed to keep trying it. And trying it. And trying it. Did the Bugsnak escape my trap because I placed it wrong and I need to try something else, or was my timing simply off and should I do it again? WHO KNOWS!?It's annoying. But if you want to get the best ending (or care about achievements), you HAVE to complete all the quests. So if you're not going to sink another 20 hours into figuring out how to lure a Bugsnack aaaall the way across the map to another Bugsnack at a specific time of day, then you're just not getting that ending.I cared about the ending only because I wanted it to end.-----Original review----I really, really wanted to like this game, but I just don't. Let's start with the pros:The voice acting The unusual character designThe fun food-themed animals Now for the cons:The voice acting (for the characters, not the Bugs -- they're annoying) is great. However, the animation quality doesn't match the voice acting. The VAs are definitely putting a lot of effort into this, and the art in the credits is adorable, but the characters' actual movements are lumpy and awkward. I thought this was intentional at first (especially when I mistakenly thought this was mascot horror), but the gameplay mechanics are also clunky and awkward.On that note, that's the reason I quit playing: The actual mechanic of capturing the Bugsnax (the driving force behind most of the many quests) is REALLY frustrating! First thing, you're given a trap that you put in the bug's path and trigger as they pass to capture them. Great. Easy. Except then you immediately meet a Bug that you CAN'T capture with the trap -- they just bonk into it and knock it over. THIS Bug needs to be tricked into bonking into another Bug, and then while it's stunned, you just pick it up barehanded. But then you meet another Bug that you can't capture with the trap either -- you need to pick up seashells and throw them at it!? And you miss a TON of times even when the game went "ding!" to indicate you'd locked on? (EDIT: Turns out I needed a tripwire tool to capture this one, but I hadn't unlocked it at this point and had no way of knowing. Also the tripwire is only slightly less annoying than the seashell method.) And THEN you receive a launchpad ("lunchpad"), and now you find Bugsnax you CAN'T throw things at by yourself, you need to use this launchpad to throw rocks, and it STILL doesn't aim correctly even when it seems to be locked on. And the whole time you're trying to aim, other Bugsnax keep running up and punching your launchpad and sending it flying, or punching you and sending YOU flying.At this point, when I'm feeling invested in a puzzle-type game, I search online for enough of a hint so I can progress. But I'm not going to. I don't think this game is going to get less frustrating. I just got SO frustrated with the vague in-game instructions on capturing each Bugsnak, the trial-and-error and not knowing if I'm trying the wrong thing (or I AM doing the right thing but it needs to be sliiiightly different), and the awkward menu for juggling the different tools. More Bugsnax keep getting unlocked throughout the game, and I just found myself getting ANGRY about it because now I needed to learn (and remember!) what specific way to capture THIS one too!?If this kind of collecting-animals-game appeals to you, I recommend Slime Rancher instead.

_childDocuments_.review: Bugsnax is an adventure game released back in 2020 on Playstation 4 & 5 and Epic Games Store. It takes place on a mysterious island called Snaktooth which is a home for these interesting creatures called “Bugsnax'' which as you have guessed are half bug and half snack.You play as a journalist who writes articles about mysterious incidents and unknown anomalies. In the beginning you receive a video message from Lizbert Megafig the fame explorer essentially inviting YOU, the journalist, to the said island so you could investigate the Bugsnax being the best person to tell the world about them by making a huge article about it saving your career along the way. With her associates, Lizbert built a settlement called Snaxburg in order to better study the Bugsnax. Half bugs, half snacks - no one has ever seen anything like it and what awaits the protagonist on this journey is up to YOU, the player, to discover.I discovered this game on the Nintendo Switch over a year ago, and I was deeply invested in it until I caught every single snack on the island, completed every single quest, and unlocked every available achievement. This is truly one of my greatest achievements because not only did I really enjoy doing so, but it was also very rewarding. The game captivated me with its charm, uniquely designed characters and creatures, engaging gameplay that requires you to think outside the box from time to time, the catchy soundtrack, and the intriguing story that kept me engaged until the very end. I almost completed it in one go the first time. Later on, I purchased the game on the Epic Games Store so I could play it on my newly acquired Steam Deck, and I enjoyed it even more in high definition, with an increased field of view and smoother frame rates. This was indeed a dream game for me after a long while.Recently, after the announcement that the VR version of Bugsnax was in development and the public beta was available for virtually anyone with a VR headset, I reached out to the Young Horses Games Discord to ask if the beta would ever be coming to the Epic Games Store. Eventually, I was DM'd by one of the devs with a Bugsnax Steam key, a gesture I will definitely remember for a long while. P.S. The VR version is also great, although it's still far from being finished.The gameplay can be described as a miniature BOTW or, for comparison, "Journey to the Savage Planet." You are set in an open world filled with different types of "Pokemon-like" creatures. You are equipped with an arsenal of different traps to catch them, and all of them unlock progressively during the story in a sort of Metroidvania way. Each Bugsnack requires a different approach to catch them, and that's what makes it so fun - figuring out exactly how to do it. Whether you experiment or use unconventional methods because you lack a certain trap at the moment, it all works, and that's what I like about this game - the open approach and sandbox nature of being able to catch Bugsnax in different ways.During the story, you visit all sorts of biomes, each one very different from another, and they all feature their own Bugsnax adapted to live in these conditions. Some of them only appear during certain times of the day or under specific weather conditions, and this ecosystem truly makes the world feel alive. Some snacks appear more dangerous than others and require a special approach, but the game doesn't have a health bar or any sort of fail state, so you can try to catch them as many times as you need.The game doesn't consist solely of gameplay. Sometimes, the action settles down into narrative cutscenes, showing relationships between the Grumpuses, their daily life on the island, or sometimes their deepest secrets. The writing is genuinely good, even if it's overwhelming at times, but I still like it. The game also features bosses, but this is more in spoiler territory; it's best that you see them for yourself. Overall, it's very satisfying, has great controls, engaging puzzles, and a variety of different environments and characters you can love, hate, or Snackify to the point they're unrecognizable.The soundtrack is written by Seth Parker. The same guy who also wrote the Octodad OST and I noticed that they were pretty similar. The songs vary in genre from track to track, sometimes they give out a chill vibe, sometimes they are electronic or dramatic. Doesn’t matter what situation you're in, the soundtrack always accompanies the whole experience too well. If nobody’s got me I know that the Bugsnax OST does.10/10 - Hey, we're making this funny game about sentient food with googly eyes don’t go too hard on the OST. Seth Parker: hold my Sodie.Overall, Bugsnax is a fantastic treat for all indie game enthusiasts and those who are open to experimenting with new titles. It has the potential to carve out a special place in your heart, but it can also be enjoyable in any case. It's worth noting, however, that this game may not appeal to everyone. For instance, individuals who are arachnophobic, sensitive to themes of body dysmorphia, or uncomfortable with queer representation in media might not find it to their liking.But otherwise, The creators of Octodad did not reinvent the wheel and come up with another game with awkward controls and funny physics. This is a fun adventure for a couple of evenings that can be stretched out if you enjoy catching adorable creatures. The game is available on all modern platforms even on the iOS and SteamVR so you can enjoy the thrilling Snaxcatching action on anything, anywhere, anytime.

_childDocuments_.review: At its core, Bugsnax is a casual and relaxing exploration game. The gameplay loop consists of exploring new biomes, catching new and unique bugsnax, and interacting with the villagers of Snaktooth Island (which was the highlight of the game for me). All characters are memorable and unique in their own ways and the soundtrack is surprisingly great.Though the 'psychological horror' tag on the store page may seem like a joke, there are some dark and creepy moments sprinkled throughout the story for such a lighthearted looking game, though nothing truly terrifying.Overall, I'd definitely recommend giving Bugsnax a chance if you enjoyed games like Slime Rancher or are looking for a fun casual exploration game.
_childDocuments_.name: Bugsnax

_childDocuments_.review: Bugsnax is... surprising. What it is. is a game about catching bugs that look like snacks. But what it really is, is a mystery game about a missing person (sorry, Grumpus). But ACTUALLY, what it really is, is a game with a deep historical mystery. But really, though, what it truly is, is a game about goofy muppet people who all have goals and relationships being challenged by negative core beliefs about themselves, and your journey to help them overcome the obstacles within and achieve self actualization. But for real, though, what it really really is, is a game about Sandopedes and putting launchers under them so they break into little bits of sandwich that fly everywhere.This is a bafflingly captivating game with great characters, clever writing, and excellent voice actors all under the guise of a silly children's game. The story is engaging, there's several fun mysteries to be solved, there are tons of Bugsnax to catch (each requiring cleverly using your tools in different combinations to get them), and it's just straight-up fun. While the tag labeled "psychological horror" is not exactly lying, you will not be frightened by this game. There are no jumpscares or outright horror elements here, though if you have a good, hard think about some of the secrets you'll uncover in your time on the island, it will definitely provoke some creepy ideas and there are a few underlying mysteries with some surprisingly dark connotation--WITH THAT SAID, this is a peaceful, chill game. It's not very difficult (it's more about puzzling things out than having quick reflexes), it's got a really relaxing atmosphere, it is played all at your own pace, you're free to explore anywhere you go, and there are plenty of funny and wholesome moments to even things out. I found myself laughing often with the dialogue.I'm not yet fully through my first playthrough, but nearing the end at around 13 hours of playtime. I do plan to 100% this game, though, as it's such a great way to unwind in the evenings. Overall, I was really surprised by the emotional spectrum that this game explores and just how much authenticity is buried under such an absurd and silly concept. I was also surprised at just how much fun this game ended up being. It even runs beautifully on Linux. This is an easy recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, so looking at this Steam page and at the screenshots, you can probably conclude that this game isn't worth your time if you're above the age of 12. However, due to the writing and charm of Bugsnax, this game can be worth anyone's time.The characters were the biggest highlight for me. This game tackles some very serious themes and presents them in such mature and insightful ways. It was very off-putting to just to see how skillful the writing really is. When you meet all the characters, they start out as stereotypes, but as you get to know them, they begin to feel more like real, breathing people. There wasn't a single character I hated or even disliked, at least once I got to know them better.With the gameplay, it did get a bit boring for me. It started out great at first, where it treated the capturing of bugsnaxs more like puzzles. However, as you get all the tools (which happens really soon), it felt like 80% of the bugs can be simply caught with the use of a single tool (which I won't spoil here.) The game gave me so many options, but yet, I barely felt the need to use multiple tools together, which is a shame.Other than that, the only other flaw I can think of is that the AI of the bugs can break at certain points. It's nothing too bad, but I had a bug get stuck in a tree or even zoom into space.Overall, I recommend Bugsnax. If you're unsure about the gameplay, then I'd wait for sale. The writing made it worth it for me.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is one of my absolute favorites. While streaming Viva Pinata a friend said "What in the Bugsnax is this game?" and thus I was introduced to Bugsnax. This game is very similar to games such as Viva Pinata, Slime Rancher, Animal Crossing, and one could even say maybe Disney Dreamlight Valley. It is an adorable game where you collect Bugsnax and figure out what has happened to the Grumpuses (aka our main characters) that are living on Snaxtooth Island. Each Grumpus has such an in depth personality which makes them so lovable and able to connect with. I think having these diverse and in depth personalities is what kept drawing me back to the game. Each one of them is different, yet utterly adorable, and the sass that they can have makes interacting with them just that much more fun. I also liked the relationships between the characters themselves, including the development between a few (wink-wink). It was fun to see them gradually grow into their personalities and made the connection the player has with them so immersive. The graphics for this game is amazing. I would say that it is extremely similar to Slime Rancher in style. The graphics are astounding for this to not be a Triple A game and I appreciate the detail that went into creating this masterpiece of a game. Seriously so visually appealing. Artists, ya done good!The story line for this game was so fun and I had NO idea the ending that was going to take place! While 100% the game was a lot of running back and forth, everything from the graphics to the Grumpuses to the cute rewards you would get made it worth it! The story was coherent and made sense and the twists and turns along the way were shocking and exciting. The ending set it up to possibly be getting a Bugsnax 2, and I for one am screaming TAKE MY MONEY!!!! Young Horses, you did a great job with this game! I cannot wait to see what you give us next! (:

_childDocuments_.review: I like hardcore survival games, so this game is not the kind I'd usually pick up. Even still, I loved Bugsnax. This is the kind of game where you can play for hours, and then dream of it when you go to bed. This is one of my top 10s, and after I finished it, passed the remote to my girlfriend for her turn to play through. I'd really recommend this to all of my friends, no matter their genre preferences. Bugsnax is a unique take on the monster-hunting genre. You collect monsters, called Bugsnax, that are essentially a combination of food + bug. Each bugsnax has unique ways to capture them, and most of them can be captured in more than one way. It's creative, chill, and it's easy to become invested in all the characters you meet. This is the first game I have ever unlocked all the achievements for, and I wish I could relive the experience again. 10/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, one of the best little games I have played in years. I was looking for something casual, and got something so much more. If you want a casual experience? Every time you think you have something figured out, you're in a new area, with new Bugsnax and ways to catch them. I loved this game, start to finish. I think it's well worth its face price, so if you are interested, get it now, you won't regret it.

Highly highly recommend if you want something super chill to play, and of course if you like cute creatures. 10/10 highly recommend for Bunger alone.

_childDocuments_.review: Bugsnax premise is solid, a journalist (you) are sent to an island not so far away from regular civilization to find out the truth and gain first hand account from an explorer. What they don't tell you is that, all food on the island are living animals made fruit, veggies, fast food, drinks, and snackpacks. This game has charm at almost every corner, and relies heavily on the supporting cast of characters to really make you want to keep playing. But that isn't the only reason you'll play till the end, if you like completing the pokedex is all the pokemon games; you will find bugsnax to be significantly easier.  This a puzzle game at heart, but most are very simple to the point of almost boredom. I fought through this game, especially the collecting of all bugsnax. Normally you need to get atleast two of every snack, and some of them are more of a pain to get than others. Not to say the game isn't fun, it just becomes a chore at times. A majority of this game is fetch quests (who would have guessed), for the people of Snaxburg, these allow glimpses of these very very very common troupe of characters. All of which are heartfelt at times, do their best to keep you entertained. So lets get on with some true criticism. This game for being out since 2020 on other platforms, shows some issues at times. Mostly in the collision department, on quite a few occasions I was hit into walls, rocks, floors, and other things. This resulted in me being stuck with no way to get out, or even glitched to a falling animation. Luckily, you can restart from last save and that is usually within seconds of entering an area or doing a mission. BUT, my huge gripe comes with what happened during the end section of the game. Basically I had walked to a location that is entirely inbounds, used a tool and when I was done, an cutscene sequence started. But, because of the location I stood, my character could not get to the actual point to start the cutscene as I was trapped between a fence and a wall. Now this isn't a big deal really, but it is really the last thing you do before ending the game. So I just figured I would restart from the last checkpoint/save. And it had last saved 10 minutes prior. Basically the entire section soured me and I turned the game off. Today I turned the game on and finished, while also seeing a few very weird glitches happen in the same ending section. But I stayed in the most basic of areas as to not make it glitch me into being stuck again. With this I ended a game that I personally will never play again. One of those one and done games. Was it worth it? Did I feel like Bugsnax did exactly what it should have? Did i truly get the answers I was looking for? Yes, Yes, and Not really. The game is good fun, pretty much like everything I figured it would be after 10 minutes of gameplay, and I felt left in the dark of the story of the actual Bugsnax. The end does set up for a sequel though. Probably a 6.5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: better lgbt+ representation than the entire disney franchise catalogueNo, but seriously, Bugsnax is a charming, funny, delightfully well-made game. It has a great sense of humour, and a surprisingly deep cast of muppet-style characters, including the aforementioned LGBT+ representation (which was honestly incredibly refreshing, poignant, and all around wholesome). The story is well written, with mysterious twists as to the true nature of the bugsnax, set in a wacky, colourful world with plenty of secrets to uncover. The bugsnax are so well crafted, so creative, and collecting them definitely appeals to my gotta-catch-'em-all nature. There are plenty of sidequests and challenges to keep a completionist busy, and the gadgets and physics powering the game make for some genuinely surprising and funny moments, watching the bugsnax interact with each other and the cast.I wasn't expecting this game to be as good as it is. It's clearly a labour of love and a lot of good humour, hard work, and genuine fun, which makes for a really lovely game experience. I only wish there was more. The story and lore put forth in the game leave many mysteries unsolved and much room for another visit to the world the developers have created. I'd absolutely love to see a sequel one day - it's rare to play a game with so much heart and humour, and strawberries with googly eyes.

_childDocuments_.review: Bugsnax is an adventure game where you play as a journalist who is tasked to go to Snaktooth Island in search of Elizabert Megafig, a famous explorer who feels like you're the best person to spread the news of Bugsnax and how amazing they are. However, when arriving on the island, you discover that Elizabert has disappeared, and you're tasked with finding her while also doing a variety of other tasks across Snaktooth Island. The story is pretty straightforward. It is mostly what I've described already, but you also need to solve the problems of all the residents of Snaktooth Island and reform their community while also discovering the secrets of the island. It is a pretty basic story, but that doesn't matter, as the act of discovering Bugsnax and catching them is such a joy. It also helps that the characters are all a bundle of different personalities with great voice acting, so this helps improve the story even more. The main gameplay of this game is centered around discovering and catching Bugsnax. You're given a variety of tools and traps to help you with the task of catching these critters. You have snak traps, bug nets, sauce slingers, and more. They are all really fun to use and are pretty clever in their usage. It is a satisfying gameplay loop, and I found it very enjoyable. However, after you play for a while, the gameplay starts to become a bit annoying, as the later half of the game often has you catching Bugsnax you've already encountered in order to complete some quest for an NPC.The graphics are also a wonderful aspect of this game. Everything is stylized to suit this game. The NPCs, the Bugsnax, the UI, the items, etc. Everything looks cartoony but in a really nice way. The sound design is also quite good and comforting. The sounds that the Bugsnax make remind me of Pokemon but just a bit more tasty. The fact they are literal walking foods just makes their noises all the better. The music is also very calming and fitting to the environments you travel through. Also, as mentioned before, the voice acting is very good. All of the voices fit each of the character's personalities and actually make them feel distinct from one another.Overall, this game is a nice little gem. Sure, it seems a bit like a meme, and it does get a bit boring after a while, but it is honestly a good game. It is simple, effective, and engaging for the majority of the playthrough. I most definitely recommend giving this one a shot! Also, I love Bungers. They are wonderful little creatures.

_childDocuments_.review: Bugsnax is a video game that has been making waves in the gaming community for its unique and charming gameplay, lovable characters, and unforgettable storyline.The game takes place on a magical island called Snaktooth, where you play as a journalist who is tasked with investigating the strange and mysterious creatures known as Bugsnax. The graphics in this game are stunning, with bright and vibrant colors that bring the island and its inhabitants to life. The attention to detail in the design of the Bugsnax and the environments is impressive, and every creature has its own unique personality and quirks.One of the standout features of Bugsnax is its innovative gameplay mechanics. The main goal of the game is to capture Bugsnax using a variety of tools and tricks, and then feed them to the island's inhabitants. Each Bugsnax has its own unique abilities and effects on the characters, and figuring out how to catch and feed them all is a fun and satisfying challenge. The game also features a variety of different environments, from forests and caves to deserts and swamps, each with its own unique set of Bugsnax to capture.The characters in Bugsnax are lovable and quirky, and their reactions to the Bugsnax they eat are hilarious. The dialogue and voice acting are top-notch, and the storyline is full of twists and turns that will keep you engaged from beginning to end. As you progress through the game, you'll uncover the secrets of Snaktooth Island and the mysterious origins of the Bugsnax, and the final reveal is sure to leave you with a sense of satisfaction.In conclusion, Bugsnax is a must-play for fans of adventure, puzzle, and exploration games. Its charming characters, stunning graphics, and innovative gameplay make it a truly unforgettable experience. The game is a perfect example of how a game can be both challenging and fun, and the storyline will keep you hooked from start to finish. If you're looking for a new game to sink your teeth into, look no further than Bugsnax. I LOVE BUGSNAX!

_childDocuments_.review: Bugsnax was cute, amazingly voice acted, funny and oddly addicting in a calming way. The gameplay was basically about capturing ridiculous food themed creatures with a variety of silly traps in semi-creative ways to accomplish little goals in your quest to discover what happened to expedition exploring the island. The relaxing music is catchy and the characters are fun to listen to, going from fuzzy puppet-like beings to becoming more complex as the story moves on. The story isn’t too complex in itself, in fact the “twist” ending is very easy to guess if you are paying any sort of attention and the “psychological horror” tag featured in the description doesn’t really hold up for older audiences, but the characters keep you invested. The characters are amazingly voice acted and you do begin to care about what happens to them. Understanding them and watching them try to sort out their personal issues is the heart of the story.All told it was a cheery and relaxing experience from the gameplay itself. Much like a fishing or trapper game, except you listen to cheery music while gently puzzling out how to catch the adorable hamburger creature using ketchup as a lure instead of some fish. There are a large variety of bugsnax, some more complex than others to capture, all of them cute…until the last one, anyway. The only ping of stress occurs at the final act and that only occurs because it’s a contrast to the game being pretty much stress free until that point.I enjoyed it to the point where I got all the achievements and ended the game with a smile. Thumbs up, Bugsnax.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so good that I bought it at full price on Steam despite having it on Epic Games.Gameplay wise, it's like a mix of Pokémon and Ape Escape, using one or two of six tools at your disposal to catch over a hundred unique creatures. The twist here is that these creatures are food as much as they are animals, so you're able to feed them to one of the many townsfolk and turn their body parts into these snax. There are so many to mess around with, so you could turn your friends into utter health hazard disasters, just a singular food, or my personal favorite, try to replicate their original look as close as possible using snax of similar colors and shape.Speaking of the townsfolk, you have 15 friends to accompany you, and they're all endearing and fun in their own ways. Some of these examples are a mayor who's trying his best while constantly being scrutinized, a stubborn farmer and a nihilistic archaeologist in a struggling relationship because of their different priorities, a very shy and paranoid animal husbandrist who refuses to eat any Bugsnax, a snooty valley girl who thinks everyone has a dirty secret, a washed up singer who has one single hit she isn't proud of, a grimy salesman who resorts to scummy tactics because he thinks that's the only way he can get by, a friendly and surprisingly wise jock, a conspiracy theorist nerd who has feelings for said jock, his scientific sibling who has scorn with everyone else and has morbid tendencies, A meditator who despises bugsnax and tries to stray people away from them, a doctor with serious self esteem problems, and her adventurous wife who mysteriously disappeared, of whom everyone wants to bring back to keep things together again. And while these characters look like weird muppets and may seem one note at first, as you delve into their side quests you can see just how deep they are, find answers as to why they act the way they do, I won't spoil any of them, but even those who might be your least favorites have a sympathetic reason for their actions, will improve by the end of the game, and overall I just came to love each and every one of them for who they are,Overall, while it might not be everyone's thing, I highly recommend this game to people who love upbeat cartoony games and story driven games with character arcs. It's one of my all time favorite games, and it's made by the same people who made Octodad, so you can't go wrong there!Cinnasnail is my baby and I love it so much.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun, cozy little game about exploring colorful environments and collecting cute little creatures, all while interacting with a fun cast of characters.I enjoyed the hell out of this game, 100%ing it over the course of about a week. The designs of all the Snax are adorable, as is their sound design, and I enjoyed that the puzzle solving to catch most of them was challenging, but not frustrating. The villagers are all fun to interact with too and the underlying, somewhat sinister plot kept me hooked and asking questions the whole way through.One thing I particularly enjoyed was that the tools that you unlock throughout the game always felt useful. None of them felt like they were designed for one part and were just left in the wheel for no reason.Complaints? Only complaint I can think of off the top of my head is the transformation mechanic (where the villagers change attributes based on the snax you feed them) can't be undone, so character designs get thrown out the window unless you restrain yourself from feeding them snax. Apart from that, minor complaints such as the Lunchpad feeling sometimes weird to jump to a higher place is annoying, but not experience dampening.I would deeply, DEEPLY recommend this to anyone. ESPECIALLY if you dig chill, semi-laid back adventure games. Worth the money.

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10 I have this game on Playstation, PC, and Steam because this game has easily became a top 5 fav!Bugsnax is such a simple clever concept its remarkable beautiful yet cutesy Graphics is pleasing and comforting. Easily the evolution creature Collectathon games should be while not open world its unique and themed Levels with special bugsnax fill the land truly making the world feel natural and alive. The bugsnax are clever and amazingly designed while some are clones such as shishkabug and instabug being antlike Snaks the designs and locations make the bugnax feel related rather then Copys. The Unique and Puzzling ways to catch and find Bugnax can range from Easy to Tricky and sometimes you unnecessarily make it more difficult then it is. being able to change Grumpuses into Snax is a fun yet creepy form of Customisation you can make all sorts of Variants and combinations.Now the Story is the most amazing thing about this game with a wide range of characters with unique personalities and backstories. while sometimes border lining on Psychological Horror you will most likely relate to one of the characters struggles and the fact Lgbtq+ Representation is just in the game without the need to be Announced or Explained should be the new Norm for game titles and how the story tackles Mental Issues is serious and self aware without making fun on these communities.I could not recommend this game more what a unique experience I had in this game and not only do i look forward to a Bugnax 2 Im also excited to see what Young Horses will do next even if your not a fan of Creature Collectathon Bugsnax is definitely my go to recommendation for friends!

And something that a good game does is give you little hints at the end throughout the game and this game does that extraordinarily well. Third. The update was amazing and the new Shrink Spice and all its unique ways to use it is amazing. As well as The Triplicate Space was equally as amazing with the new puzzles and the Cappuccettle. _childDocuments_.review: You take one look at Bugsnax and you expect the absolute worst from it. And why wouldn’t you? It’s 202x and children’s entertainment is more annoying than ever. You’d think Bugsnax would be another one of those filler games only meant to milk money off kids. Just another kiddy game filled with bad writing and dull mechanics. And I honestly wouldn’t blame you, as it’s something that everyone has thought about this game. But Bugsnax isn’t part of this garbage children’s entertainment junk, it is so much better than that. I wanted to play Bugsnax the moment I heard it far exceeded others’ expectations and I’m hoping you will too.From a gameplay perspective, Bugsnax is fairly simple on the surface. It’s a first-person adventure game with a heavy focus on creature capturing. There are little over a hundred of the little critters to capture and while they do repeat some of the solutions, they used quite a few creative ways to figure out how to capture them. You’ll be setting traps and baiting Bugsnax into them in a large variety of ways. A big portion of this comes from the number of tools you have and having to combine them for certain captures. One example that comes to mind has to deal with capturing bugs that are frozen or on fire. You could lead them into a fire or pond with some bait, but you could also knock another Bugsnax into them and capture them both at the same time. The gameplay doesn’t just revolve around capturing insects though. The game’s quests mix things up enough to prevent the capturing from getting old. Some of my personal favorite sidequests involved spying on certain characters and others had me dressing up the characters in a specific fashion. That’s another big part of the game. Feeding a character a Bugsnax causes part of their body to become that Bugsnax. This resulted in the grossest game of dress-up that I ever found myself enjoying. I made one dude entirely out of popsicles and I made his wife entirely into pickles. There are also 5 optional bosses to fight, although 1 is part of the free DLC. The bosses all bring their own unique puzzle to solve to beat them and I’m glad they’re there as sort of a final test for the game’s simple gameplay loop.I found myself enjoying the quests, catching, and dressing up enough that I 100% the game. And there wasn’t a single dull moment.But the gameplay isn’t even the biggest selling factor for me. One of the strongest points of Bugsnax is, surprisingly, the writing. The characters may all look like discount Muppets, but the game’s cast is one of the most human ones I’ve seen in a video game in a long time. Let alone for a kid’s game. Bugsnax may have a cutesy exterior, but that never stops it from dipping its toes into more mature topics. One of my favorite examples would have to be Triffany’s questline. Her plotline revolves entirely around her obsession with leaving an impact on the world before she dies. Other characters delve into issues like depression, abandonment issues, and severe anxiety. Considering the kid-friendly aesthetic, this may sound jarring, but I promise you the game handles it well enough that it never feels out of place. And the more adult themes never stop the game from having a sense of humor. I think my favorite joke has to be that one of the characters keeps a cactus replica of his wife because he gets lonely sometimes. That and the absurd names like Gramble Gigglefunny and Wiggle Wigglebottom. I mentioned earlier that the lack of repetition helped me do all the sidequests, but seeing the conclusion to everyone’s arcs helped with that as well. I don’t think the characters would’ve been such a selling point to me without the voice actors though. Bugsnax has a shocking catalog of incredibly talented voice actors. Just take a look at the backgrounds of some of them, you’re bound to see someone you recognize. Roger Craig Smith and Yuri Lowenthal are the big standouts to me. They’re the voices of Sonic the Hedgehog and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Ben 10 respectively. All of the voice actors are really good is the point I was trying to get at. One quick look at some of their resumes is a quick way to prove it and I applaud Bugsnax for putting effort into its voice acting.My biggest complaint about Bugsnax may seem incredibly nitpicky, but I promise it’s not minor. The world map may cover a decent amount of biomes, but they’re all so enclosed and tiny. Every area is so small that a quick stroll throughout the island results in dozens of loading screens. I really feel like both the beach areas, desert areas, mountain areas, etc. could’ve been put together as one area. I don’t want the game to become open-world, but the number of loading screens between areas gets pretty tiring. I can imagine it’s going to be more of a problem for lower-end PCs. I just feel like the PS5 launch title could’ve gotten a little more intense with the map size. That and I feel like biomes get a little repetitive. As I mentioned earlier, half of the biomes just feel like an extension of the previous one. And it’s a little disappointing that the final area of the game is effectively a straight line. As some quick round-up points on my thoughts on the game: the soundtrack is pretty good. I don’t think I’ll be listening to it outside of the game too much, but the interview theme is an exception to that. A lot of the creature design is pretty cute and creative with the constant blending of bugs and snacks. I found the pineapple tarantula, hot dog worms, and sandwich centipedes to be a few of the pun names that stuck with me. I can not say the same for the Grumpus design. I just really don’t like the way the default characters look. Like I glossed over in the introduction, they look like discount Muppets. Oh and as a final positive note, I really appreciate the free DLC campaign. Too many game companies lock additional content behind a paywall and I always have to applaud companies that choose otherwise.Overall, I greatly enjoyed my 12 hours with Bugsnax. I completed every sidequest and the free DLC in that time and it never got repetitive.  I’m hoping to see more like this and less like Octodad from Young Horses in the future. For $25 it is definitely worth the price.
