_childDocuments_.review: Of all the games I've played, Bugsnax might be one of the more unique ones. Even the premise sounds ridiculous on paper; catch bugs made of food to feed them to muppet-like creatures so that they too will turn into food. But despite the ridiculousness, the game is cute, silly, and charming. In terms of presentation, the game is lovely! The character design is simply but visually appealing. The characters really do look like muppets, with flappy mouths and exaggerated body language at times. Meanwhile, the titular Bugsnax resemble insects and other animals made of food, with googly eyes on them. Absolutely everything in the game is charming and visually appealing to look at. The environments, while a little on the small size, all have a good amount of detail and environmental variance to make them stand out. There may not be a ton of areas, but the ones there are all feel unique. The gameplay loop for this game is very simple; catch the Bugsnax using one (or more) of your six traps, and feed them to the Grumpuses. Every so often you have to complete a puzzle (especially in the DLC), but by and large 90% of the game is catching those Bugsnax. Once you do catch them, feeding them to the Grumpuses cause their bodies to change into the same type of food that you just fed them. There's not a whole lot more depth to the gameplay beyond that, but there is an odd sense of satisfaction mixing and matching food parts to create the most ridiculous looking Grumpus you can. The one thing that sort of takes away from the experience is the complete lack of any threat. You don't actually take damage in this game, and it's not possible for your character to die. You can get knocked aside, frozen, set on fire, but you'll always recover after a few seconds. Is it a bad thing that there's no threat? Not at all! It creates a very relaxing environment, but at the same time, it causes some serious moments to lose a bit of tension since you can basically sit there and face tank anything the game throws at you. The highlight of the game is probably the writing and voice acting. Each character is charming with their own vibrant personality and motivations. The writing made me actually care about the characters, and had some moments that were just downright funny! The voice actors absolutely nail each character... but perhaps my favorite bit of voice acting is the Bugsnax themselves. They just... say their names over and over in an exaggerated voice, and it is seriously funny. I found myself saying it along with them because it was just so silly that it was fun! _childDocuments_.review: I think the worst thing you could do to Bugsnax is discredit it as some kind of "Knack 2 baby" type joke game. A lot the reviews are just "bunger", and while its funny, I do really want to stress that there is actually a really lovely game here.A nice little ~8 hour experience, Bugsnax is a tight cozy little game that feels like a PS2-era title in all of the best ways. On release it was nicely polished right out the gate back in 2020, and the version now available on Steam is its final form with the free expansion that adds a bit more to do in terms of optional content.The cast is really great,  being my personal favorite. If you engage with the optional sidequests, the characters all have a bit more emotional depth than you would expect from a game like this, and you can tell the guys at Young Horses really wanted to pump some life into these characters. They actually handle a couple of themes in a really mature way, and I respect the heck out of them for sticking true to their ideas. Not to mention, their voice acting is really superb. Heck, you've got Ryuji and Morgana from Persona 5 voicing a couple of the grumpuses, and Shinji from the Netflix Evangelion dub.Main plot-wise, the obvious weird body horror of the bugsnax leaves you intrigued enough to see the story through to the end for sure just to figure out the mysteries. I think its a nice mix of charm and intrigue that this game's story will please most enough. I do think that the relationships between the other characters are really where this game shines though.I would describe the game as maybe a mix of Pokemon Snap, and Slime Rancher. Its pretty unique though. Imagine if instead of battling pokemon to capture them, you had to solve a little puzzle. With half-dozen gadgets, its surprising how many ways you need to utilize them to capture every single bugsnak.Beyond that, I actually really like the speed of your character in first person. The movement is surprisingly snappy and feels good. Heck I speedran this game back when it was only on Epic Games store. There's plenty of optional challenges and things to collect if you just wanna keep playing like I did, so everyone should be pleased.Random aside: I would describe the game as having a colorful PS2 aesthetic. I think a demake of this game would be really neat to see, honestly. The character/bugsnak designs are all really charming as well.The music is surprisingly great. Hits a nice chill semi vapor-wave feel thats just nice and cozy.With the main "Brokentooth Island" content spanning about ~2 hours, I think it was just a nice little extra piece. I really like the designs of the dozen new bugsnax, and they have a couple fun gimmicks. I also appreciate that they got to give some extra time to a few of the characters that didn't get quite as much limelight or instant love. As a returning player, I did really enjoy the 100-ish challenges that they added to unlock pieces of furniture for you house. Its a nice throwback to old games to actually give you rewards for challenges that aren't just "currency" of some sort. The house/furniture bit adds nothing to the game, but its just a really fun little bonus for people who want more time with the game. On top of that, the hats were a cute little touch too. I think their additions with this expansion were super smart, in that they added stuff to collect that was just fun enough to actually feel worth collecting, but not game-changing.The expansion was free, but I loved the additions. Great work.Said most of this at the beginning, but the game is really special. Its unlike most other stuff you can play these days, and I think basically anybody will have a great time with it.

_childDocuments_.review: Graphics: 10/10 *super cute animation style that is so unique and works perfectly with a goofy/emotional story*Voice Acting: 10/10 *Honestly surprised at the quality of the voice acting; there's singing (actually quite catchy original songs), and the reactions fit the character design to a T*Control/Mechanics: 9/10 *TBH the controls were often goofy with some glitches; however, most of the time it works in your favor and its pretty fun to be thrown across the map*Quality: 10/10 *Art is unique and the style is consistent throughout the game.*Personable: 10/10 *I wasn't expecting to be able to customize anything but you can! You can pick the color of your fur and decorate your own house!*Bugsnax is a phenomenal game that everyone should get! It's cozy and really a play at your own pace type of game. However, there's drama, emotional baggage, betrayal, and more. I didn't expect there to be plot but the story is structured beautifully where it ties up loose ends and builds upon everyone's stories. I went in disliking most of the characters to adoring them by the end. The character development and issues that arise are great to investigate and watch. I felt like a detective for most of the game, so this aspect added to my experience. Although catching bugsnax became a chore three quarters of a way in, I can't believe how time slipped away from me as I would play for hours just figure out how to fulfill quests, challenges, and bugsnax captures. The puzzles were clever but not too hard. I had a pleasant time learning each region and uncovering its secrets. Moreover, each region comes with new characters, tools, backstory, bugsnax, and environment. I enjoyed figuring out new mechanics of the game. It really doesn't just throw you in. You have time to learn the game and its story. I'm not one to typically 100% games but this is the very first game that compelled me to do so! I captured all bugsnax, completed all main/side/mail quests, and found all secrets. For most of it, you don't need a guide (although there are plenty if you get stuck). However, unlike a lot of games, you don't need to really 100% the game to have 100% completion (for instance, once you have all of Gramble's upgrades, you do not have to keep donating other than quests).Overall, I truly would recommend this game to anyone who likes cozy games with good plot and fun game play. The silliness of it all added to the game as well but, dang, did it get serious everyone now and then. My end time was 27 hours but, assuming I didn't 100% everything, it probably would be a 15-20 hour game depending on how fast it takes you and how far you want to go in the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Let's dive into Bugsnax. This oddball odyssey by Young Horses serves up charm and humor that keep its gameplay engaging over its 9 to 10-hour duration. Despite the baffling trailers, Bugsnax is a story-driven first-person adventure with light puzzles, surprising depth, and delightful character development. It might not flaunt PlayStation 5's power, but Snaktooth Island is a must-visit—just be cautious about overindulging in its wildlife cuisine.In Bugsnax, you're a news reporter brought to Snaktooth Island by explorer Elizabert Megafig to cover its edible creatures. Yep, Bugsnax are animals that mutate consumers upon consumption. Totally normal, right? The island's inhabitants, grumpuses (fur-covered humans), add to the delightful chaos.Bugsnax are a visual treat, with distinct appearances from flying pizzas to swimming soda cans. The Spuddy, a butter-topped potato charging at you, is a personal favorite.The main task is rallying Snaxburg's residents back home for interviews. But each grumpus has requests, and Bugsnax, being the primary food source, are crucial. While the missions follow a similar pattern, top-notch writing and voice acting keep each grumpus unique and engaging.Bugsnax is absurd but also meaningful, touching on subjects like relationships, mental health, and loss. The humor keeps things light, and the game is full of laughter, both from the creatures and the grumpuses.Catching Bugsnax involves scanning them with your camera and using tools to nab them. The metroidvania-like elements add depth. However, the real magic is in Bugsnax's storytelling, keeping you hooked with its characters and narrative surprises.Bugsnax is odd and delightful. Its gameplay might have moments of repetition, but its heart—its story and characters—makes the journey worth it. It's a story with over 100 Bugsnax to discover, somehow making you care for these quirky critters.Anyways this game is a trip, have fun!

I love all the little side- side quests to collect new furniture while simultaneously adding more to do than just the regular side quests and story. Speaking of, both are really entertaining and pretty funny at times too. The ending is amazing and I will happily 100% this game. Overall, if it looks interesting enough, why not give it a try? :)TLDR;Great game that you should definitely give a shot...worst case you don't like it (sorry for hyping it, chief.) and can refund it in the two hours!

name: Boyfriend Dungeon
detailed_description: Date up to nine-ish weapons, from dancing swords to heart-piercing daggers Generated action-combat dungeons and challenges! Stay sharp! Various combat styles. For example, hit hard and dodge quickly with the dagger, or take on crowds with Lasersaber Inclusive, tasteful approach to gender and sexuality - male, female, and non-binary romance Let's get to the point: take your weapon-babes on romantic outings, such as to the club or the beach You move into your cousin's old apartment, rent-free for the summer. Plus, he'll help you solve your little problem... you've never been on a date in your life! To get some confidence and meet people, plus earn a little cash, you’re tasked with clearing the creatures in “the dunj”. Soon you discover weapons you find transform into cuties… and they’re SINGLE! (What a craaazy coincidence because you also happen to be up for grabs yourself.) But someone's abducting weapons and leaving them damaged in the dungeon! Who could do such a thing? Will you solve the blade-napping mystery? Will you find love? Or, friendship, at least? Craft gifts for your bae blades and give them when the time is right, whether it's in the dunj or out on the town. After all, a couple that slays together, stays together. Estoc (Isaac): the sharpest dresser Dagger (Valeria): tired of backstabs Talwar (Sunder): worried he’s becoming an antique Lasersaber (Seven): hard to get a handle on him Glaive (Sawyer): awkward in the wrong hands Scythe (Rowan): reaping what they sow Brass Knuckles (Pocket): loves cat naps Axe (Jonah): surfer sweetie Hammer (Leah): fashionable and cute Whip (Dr. Holmes): Cannot be wielded Date them all without a care, you polyarmourous dual-wielder, or just be best friends. Either way, you can reach max Love Rank, because platonic love is also real love. (Besides, you can't be romantic with the cat anyway. Calm down.) If that's not enough for you, mod your own! The devs have already added basic support for changing out weapon looks -- keep an eye on updates for more features to help you blacksmith your own sharp cuties and trade them with your friends.

short_description: Date your weapons! Romance swords, daggers, and polearms to level them up in this “shack-and-slash” dungeon crawling adventure.

_childDocuments_.review: A Dungeon Crawler merged with a Dating Sim sounds like something that would be impossible to pull off. However, Kitfox has done it so damn well! Creating charming and truly inclusive characters for a Dating Sim is hard enough. But, they also managed to fill this game with evolving combat that makes each character (weapon) feel worth dating to level up their skills and learn more about them! I discovered this game back at Twitch Con 2018 and have been so hyped to finally try it and can say that it was worth the long wait because you can seriously feel the love in the game! If you are debating picking it up I do recommend it! Now go smooch some swords silly~ <3
_childDocuments_.name: Boyfriend Dungeon

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun little game! I enjoyed the various characters and their personalities, and getting to know them was fun; the dating was a bit linear for all of them, and it might have been nice to have more branching or varied outcomes, but I enjoyed things as they were. I appreciated the variety of dates, and the different things they're all dealing with and the themes they each represent were surprisingly compelling and introspective at times, even though the story overall is still pretty simple. The final boss feels a bit tacked-on and I would have liked that fleshed out more, but the rest of the story is fun.The combat side of the game is pretty basic; eventually I got the hang of it and just sort of hammered (ha) my way through the game. It mostly helps space out and prop up the dating side, I think, which is fine. Overall it's a cute little game that I enjoyed my time with.

_childDocuments_.review: Exceeded my expectations. I was expecting this game to feel either like a dungeon crawler with a dating sim shoe horned in or a dating sim with a dungeon crawler awkwardly jammed in there. However, I was very wrong. Breaking character scenes with dungeon crawling does wonders to enhance the experience and my affinity towards characters I normally wouldn't be that interested in. Either I would not care for the characters personality initially but liked their play style, or the other way around. I really hope games like this get made more! This is such a fresh and innovative way to improve the genre.

The "main plot" isn't bad necessarily, the writers were just really good at writing an unlikable antagonist.In terms of being a dungeon crawler:If you don't normally partake- like me- Boyfriend Dungeon does a good job making the gameplay laid back yet entertaining. Otherwise, it's just a really simplified hack and slash.It is also important to note that this aspect of the game if very short, the game is far more a dating sim than a dungeon crawler.Overall, as a dating sim enjoyer, Boyfriend Dungeon is definitely a must play.

_childDocuments_.review: Boyfriend Dungeon is a great game. When I say that I really mean it. Usually, games don't effect me that much. I play them, I finish them and move to next one. But Boyfriend Dungeon really made a special place in my heart. I can compare BD to Persona. When I first started playing Persona, I wasn't expecting too much. I was assuming it was a simple JRPG but Persona surprised me and captured me. The same thing happened with Boyfriend Dungeon. First of all, if you are thinking this is just an average +18 visual novel, you are wrong. This game has so much depth to it. The characters, your interaction with them, special moments... everything is presented in such a unique way it is impossible not to love this game. The art style is fantastic. The game is eye pleasing to look at from beginning to end. The soundtrack is amazing. I finished the game, but I'm still listening to it while writing this. Tunes are so catchy, and lyrics for some songs are such a joy to listen. The gameplay consists of two parts. Dungeons and dating. Dating stuff is your usual thing. Your partner messages you, you go to a place, talk with them and end the day. You can give gifts to increase your love with them. Now, let's talk about the dungeon part. This people you meet and get acquainted with can turn into weapons. Dagger, scythe, estoc, lasersaber... variety is very good. Every weapon behaves differently and has unique skill set. The more you use a weapon the more love points you gain. Increasing your love rank unlocks new combos and abilities for that weapon. Other than that, you kill monsters, collect loot and recipes and gather money. With money you can buy clothes, gifts and crafting components. You can use your workbench to craft the recipes you've collected. Every dungeon has multiple floors. You can leave early by using the elevator if you are low on health. But in order to progress through the story you have to kill that dungeon's boss. Every dungeon represents your character's fear. When you kill a boss, you overcome that fear and move to next part on the story. Overall, Boyfriend Dungeon is a unique game, and I'm so glad I found it and played it. From start to finish it is masterfully crafted and deserves all the praise. I wish it didn't end but I guess every good thing eventually ends.

Love the characters, the music and the dungeon crawling. I really hope they add more content in the future.10/10, would recommend to any fellow slasher <3

_childDocuments_.review: Hmm ... What about this game? The music is very pleasant to the ear and can be listened to in a loop. The graphics vary between the cute and the gorgeous. I particularly appreciate the different personalities that are presented to us, although I am insatiable and I would have liked there to be more (but I am patient, I would wait for the next two!) In general, all the characters are endearing (except Eric ...) and makes you want to discover them all. A relaxed game very pleasant to play, the fact of replaying the dungeons "often" to increase the "levels / love" of the characters, is done very well and quickly, thus avoiding falling into the vicious circle of repetition! I am very happy to have supported this wonderful team from the start!

_childDocuments_.review: Despite the lengthy development (the game was first scheduled to arrive in September 2019) the game feels rushed and incomplete.The game is extremely short, 6-7 hours to complete - maybe 9 hours, if you want to max all the weapons. There are only two small dungeons, each with two biomes, one mini-boss and one boss. Combat is simplistic and easy - mashing the quick attack as fast as possible works on all the enemies and bosses equally well - although the latter can take as long as 20 seconds to take down! Despite the lack of challenge you will replay the dungeons a couple of times to max all the weapons/relationships, but at this point you won't even look at the abilities you are unlocking. The visuals are nice, but too often I was getting stuck in unpassable corridors or on holes in floor. In the town hub you can do some crafting, but it is equally boring - the outfits don't do anything, the gifts you have in over-abudance anyway, and the ingredients can be purchased dirt cheap from the stores (which does not involve the hassle of fighting the monsters).It seems this is not a rogue-like exploration game interspersed with romance (as there is barely any dungeoning to speak of), but the other way around - a visual novel artificially extended by the grind of mashing the buttons for a while and leveling up the weapons.So lets talk about the other part of the game. Visuals are once again top-notch... but the plot is bonkers. The workings of the world are not explained or explored (with the protagonist immediately accepting even the craziest ideas at face value). They are supposedly trying to gain confidence and grow as a person, but  - sorry, but I fail to see the connection. Final boss jumps in from a completely unrelated plot, which is flagged at the beginning and then forgotten until the very end of the game. But the craziest thing is that a game about healthy consensual relationships forces the player character into several unhealthy ones, and gives the player no opportunity to refuse dates or back out of relationships. I tried my best to avoid some characters by simply not replying to their texts - but it lock me out of the main plot, as this was not something anticipated by the devs. "You WILL play nice and obviously, that WAS a date, no matter what you say" - thank you game, should I just put down the controller and watch the playthrough on YouTube instead? Despite that, the various weapons are written well and they have their distinct personalities - I just wish the romance was not shoved down my throat so forcefully...Finally, I must mention the music. The slow and repetitive elevator tunes with weird pauses and electronically over-processed vocals are absolutely horrid. There was probably one track suitable to the pace of combat which did not make me want to turn the volume all the way down. What's worst - you can craft two sets of headphones in-game, but (contrary to description) I heard no difference in tunes.Despite some intriguing ideas this is ultimately a failed product which does not justify its price tag. There is not enough player agenda (or choice) in the visual novel part, and the dungeoning part is short and boring.

I did some digging and found it was NOT something I did, no matter what you do it ends poorly. (Unless you become Bella Swan and reject reality to cling to a fantasy and yet somehow Twilight IS the better love story by comparison.) I hope they change this I really really do but as it is I can't recommend this game, this is a dating sim not a rejection sim.

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful experience, though I find myself reminisce that it's such a short game. I found myself wanting to binge this game continuously and was saddened when I was forced to grind to ensure I got all the achievements before the ending came. The art's precious, the story is compelling without being ridiculous, and each of the characters have their perks and problems which makes their growth all the more meaningful. It's a self-aware experience whilst also addressing realistic and serious issues we go through in life such as death, loss, depression, failing, lacking and so much more. My policy is usually that I got 2x the amount I bought the game for in play time. Yet, even with 9 hours and I bought the game at $10 discount I don't mind. The entire time I was smiling, emotional, or just enjoying the genuine gameplay aspect and trying to do it all and everyone. I highly recommend this game and have very few and trivial grievances that are simplistic and have nothing to do with issues or problems. I wish that Olivia, Eric, and Jonah were also dateable. The whole time I was nervous as I'd invited Isaac to the BBQ party and Jonah the Axe never got back to me. Later on when I was scanning my achievements did I learn he wasn't a interactable character and I was at a loss because I was thrilled to dunj with him.There is someone in this game for you, and they might not be perfect but they have you and you them. Whether it's platonic or real, love has many shapes and one of those shapes is this game. So much love was put into it. : The last update included more achievements and access to the before-mentioned romance targets that I was hoping to see, Jonah and Leah! And despite not including Olivia to this roster they added not only a new character and weapon but also a sort of antihero in their own weird way! I speak of the Whip, Professor Holmes! While not actually a wieldable target they are still a romance option. From what I've found you have to fight them in order to raise affections - this is done by besting them in the last floor of the newly accessible area, the College. It's fresh and inventive considering that Leah and Jonah both join you in the dunj as well- and I affirm my earlier statement on Jonah being one of my new favorites for such as his heavy attacks are just  levels of wide and heavy.Along with the update I can also reaffirm that I double down on suggesting this game. I now have 22 hours in my belt, all achievements achieved, and I can still say this it a highly recommended game on my part. Even more so now with the update- the price is worth the fun it provides!

_childDocuments_.review: i cant wield the non-binary masochist so i hate itOkay, with that out of the way, I love Boyfriend Dungeon. It is genuinely so much fun, I have very little interest in dating sims but BD is a huge exception with its incredibly compelling characters mixed with its roguelike gameplay. It does LGBTQ+ representation wonderfully, having not one but *three* non-binary characters from all walks of life, being able to choose what pronouns your character goes by without it interfering with who you can date, and characters just casually being mentioned as gay. I love this, it's representation done so well. It's not subtle but it's also not in your face and the characters are more than their genders or sexualities. This is the key to writing compelling LGBTQ+ characters.The gameplay, while it can get a bit stale at times, is still quite engaging. it's somewhat difficult, and the theming behind each area is clear and well implemented. The enemies can be a bit frustrating, but the game spams you with heals enough that this becomes less of an enemy design issue and more of a game design issue. Don't get me wrong, that's also bad, but it's easier to ignore.The game also does an excellent job of introducing its main villain. From your very first date with him Sunders manages to establish that he is a narcissist who only gets by because of his looks, and a trusted advisor to him warns you that he'll chew you up and spit you out. And he maintains a constant presence in the dialogues between characters you can take part in while walking about town.Oh wait, sorry, that's not the villain. My bad.Sunders is the main weak point of the game for me. Even from your first date with him there are more red flags than a communist parade. There's not an atom in my body that was ever interested in his story, and I was already busy enough with the actual villain stalking me. I didn't need another one. On repeat playthroughs I never even touched his story, it just makes me sad.But looking past Sunders, Boyfriend Dungeon is a wonderful game. The setting is pretty good, the premise is heartwarming and the various ways you can interact with the characters add so much flavor to it. This game is a steal for the price it's usually at.but like i said i cant wield the non-binary masochist so 0/10 will never play again

_childDocuments_.review: Tl;dr: Play responsibly, but a fun and genuinely heartwarming (if short) experience awaits if you choose to play.I've been following this game for a few years and gladly bought it on launch - and for me it's been money well-spent, every bit of the way. Of course it's not perfect, but the overall experience has been  worth the wait.So much! The art is gorgeous, especially (and expectedly) in the visual novel/dating sim parts of the game. The weapon-to-human transformations were literally jaw-dropping, and the dungeons look slick as well. The weapon variety was great, and I loved rotating through all of them (lightning sword is the best though). Throughout my playthrough, I couldn't decide whether I liked the dungeon crawling or dating sim parts of the game better, and the loop of progressing through the dungeons and then developing your relationships with different characters was addicting. The writing was excellent - heartfelt, funny, and genuinely shocking at times. While there has been a lot of discussion online about some of the darker content in the story, I felt it was handled sensitively and the ending allowed for plenty of catharsis. Not much! As others have said, it is short - I was able to 100% the game in one playthrough of about 9-10 hours, and probably won't replay it unless new content comes out down the road. There are a few small bugs, but nothing broke my playthrough and I know the devs are already releasing patches. You'll end up running into repeated dialogue in the dungeons if you take the same weapon to the same hangout. And the combat, though it feels good, is easy compared to others in the genre - if you're looking for challenging combat, this won't be where you find it.Given the content included at launch, the price point may be unreasonable for some, but I felt it was well worth the cost of my enjoyment of the game and supporting this studio. I applaud the devs for tackling some of the more unsavory aspects of dating in this game, and doing so with regard for their players. Beautiful game. Smooch all the swords.

_childDocuments_.review: Skip to the end for a brief review. As a straight guy, I appreciate the nonbinary and girl being added in and allowing you to be just friends with the guys. The game is very balanced and nothing feels left out in the game mechanics. The dating mechanics are solid and the dialogue are both well made and written well, the gifts make sense for who you give them to. The actual dungeon part of this game is amazing, but I wish there were more areas you could go to, or maybe some after game content. Having just 2 feels wrong. I wish there was just one more area for you to explore. I enjoy the "date" areas and interactions you can have with your weapons. It allows you to talk and learn more about your partner and it's a nice touch. All in all, I highly recommend this game. Music is great, story is great and compelling, characters are very charming, dungeon and combat are fun and sometimes challenging. wish you could take Sawyer to the 4th of July BBQ  10/10

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to highly recommend this game but the reasons I'm about to go into, I can't. I would, however, say get this game if you like a short but pretty ok dungeoncrawler one shot.- Dungeoncrawling aspect done well- Beautiful art, beautiful characters - Diverse cast- Interesting characters- Shallow glimpses into the characters and finishes right as you start to care- No replay motivation (save for wanting to see dialogue)- Only 1 female dating option- Too little dungeons - No repercussions or dialogues of serial dating- Game so short it feels rushedThe characters in this game are interesting and they have their own stories that reveal afair bit of their past. There's an amount of diversity, although lacking in available female leads (there's only one), I really appreciate there being enby rep. But that's sort of where it ends, due to the games, in my opinion, worst flaw. . The character's stories are rushed through and somewhat shallow because they're trying to reveal their entire life story in (minus introduction) about 5 interactions. It's too fast to develop any kind of intrigue or emotions towards them. Which brings me to my next point.The gameplay is good, a tad bit repetitive but that goes for most games. The dungeon crawling aspect is done well but the dating sim area is incredibly limited. You can only date each person 6 times, essentially (i'm not counting dungeon crawling as dates, though there are a few interactions you have there) and after that you don't interact with them in the overworld ever again . Going back to issues that the game is too short, there's too few dungeons  and again, alot of it feels rushed. Also there's no real reason to date any of the weapons aside from seeing dialogue, which is not much of a motivator more most people, most dating sims have CGs or albums or something (not on the phone, somewhere on the main page. There's practically no replay motivation on this game at all, again, aside from dialogue options. There's also no repercussions on serial dating or anything, which i guess if you want to poly inclusive can still be done with like an option at the start or you might have to either convince everyone else on board or get chewed out for your actions or something.Again. Rushed. The main plot of you trying to get someone to date with a more serious plot doesn't balance at all. And Jesse not dropping Eric by how creepy he was, lowkey terrifying. That aside, going for what's typically a rom sim plotline simply doesn't work because the way they're trying to draw a big mystery in the later half of a game that lasts about 7 hours (take into account grinding for max levels and all items, it's more like 3-4). More so some bits write themselves into a dead end and feel unsatisfying and cut off  Of the characters we  see, we only get a portion of what makes them interesting and it's not expanded upon.There's no other way to say other than, I'm disappointed. I loved Moon hunter and Shattered Planet and when I heard that there was going to be combining two of my favourite game genres, I was hyped and waited for what felt like forever. I bought and played as soon as I could and was so excited. When I had beat the final boss, I had expected the game to go on and I could explore more dungeons and more of the character's backstories. When the credits popped up, I thought it would continue like a PMD game (or Hades) where there's a continuation, and epilogue to keep going. I tried a new game, I tried to load game but I was wrong. That was it. As a concept, I love it and love the incivility. I think Kitfox was going for a Hades x Monprom sort of thing where like it's fun even when it's repetitive but the biggest motivating factor for games like that is that the story expands on itself and it's character's every time you play it but this game kind of does both halfway. That said, I'm still going to play the game more because I enjoy dungeon crawlers and the visuals.I really want to recommend this game badly, but it falls short on the what I feel are the most important aspects.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a queer trans femme, and my problem with how they handled everything is this: The content warning that was there before said it "may" contain references to stalking. And I guess their response was "well other developers don't do good content warnings so why should we? people just want to hate queer people". No, people just want to be properly informed, and I especially expect other queer people to know to do better. When I Kickstarted the game, I had assumed it was going to be a happy game where you go on fun dates, instead it's what it is now. Even Sunder is a creep that you can't say no to, so I just avoided his storyline. They can make a game about dating ♥♥♥♥♥♥ people without consent if they want to, but if I had known at the start that it wasn't going to feel like a safe game to play as someone who's been abused, I wouldn't have Kickstarted it. There was nothing on the Kickstarter page that mentioned anything about themes of abuse. And the store page as of right now makes no mention of the abuse content at all, even though I know Steam has a way to put warnings in the bottom part of the store page. All that makes me wonder if they wanted to hide that part of the game from people. I'm so angry with how awfully they handled everything that I permanently removed the game from my account.And for the combat, I only played a little bit because it was boring, not nearly as enjoyable as Hades, and I kept dying so quickly that I felt like I wouldn't be able to make any progress through the dungeon.

_childDocuments_.review: Saw the name, saw the trailer, bought it on a whim. Been playing for ~3 hours now and I feel like I've seen enough to leave an overall review. The dating sim aspect of the game is... fine, I suppose? I like the characters and I like the stories they have to tell. Was personally interested in mister smooth guy Isaac at first, but then the game threw this adorable punk girl at me and I just have to say that was unfair. How am I supposed to choose anyone else smh. Anyway, the rest of the review...COMBAT! I've kind of been playing a LOT of dungeoneering/roguelike games these past couple of years, so I've developed a taste for them. This one... leaves me feeling strange. The dungeoneering aspect of this game is, to put it simply, very easy. I feel like I've been in the tutorial this entire time. Potions drop too frequently, dodge rolling has ten years of i-frames, the special parry move Isaac unlocks is WAY too forgiving... and you can upgrade it to be even MORE forgiving! Once you've ventured far enough into the first dungeon you unlock the K-pop guy, Seven. His heavy attack chain covers 30-50% of any given room, hits three times, does a sizeable amount of damage, and (most importantly) DELETES ALL ENEMY PROJECTILES. Its only weakness is that it's relatively slow but you can mitigate that by simply starting the combo with a single light attack. And when I say relatively slow, I mean it's really not even that slow tbh. (Additional note: It's not just that combo that deletes projectiles. All of the player's attacks delete projectiles. It's uh... a curious design choice, really.) Okay okay that's enough bashing. I am, truthfully, having fun with this game. But if you're someone who's interested in a hack-and-slash game where enemies actually have a chance against the player, this game ain't it. If you're like me and you could use a little power trip (plus some A-tier hotties) then this is a pretty good one.

_childDocuments_.review: There was a lot about this game that I liked. It was, overall, a cute, quirky, fun game that was quite quick to finish. But, there was also something about it that bothered me, and it took me a while to put my finger on what it was.First, I need to describe the game. You - a player-insert character with a fully customisable name and appearance - are spending the summer in Verona, California, with your cousin. Yes, this is a Romeo + Juliet reference. You haven't had much dating experience, so this is going to be your hot girl/guy/enby summer. Also, some humans in this world can turn into weapons and you can date them.Basically, this is a romantic visual novel/dungeon crawler. Like I said, it's quite fun to play. But...none of the datable characters really appealed to me. They were all very 'meh.' I don't care about them, I don't particularly want my character to date them, I don't think they're cute. This is entirely a matter of taste, and someone else might feel very differently.This does, however, lead me to the other problem which is, this game doesn't really care what you, the player, thinks. Despite positing the main character as being a self-insert, the game assigns them opinions and character traits. Don't want the dagger to kiss you? Tough, she's going to, and your characters reactions will range from 'happy' to 'super happy.' Don't particularly care if the talwar breaks up with you? No, you're wrong, you're heartbroken and your only dialogue choices will reflect that. Want a platonic relationship with the estoc? You don't have to agree to sleep with him, but the game still insists on treating him as a potential romantic partner which is, quite frankly, incredibly surreal placed next to the plot regarding an unwanted admirer. Oh that guy's creepy persistence is a problem but this guy is fine?Now, I don't have a problem with playing a character who is an actual character. Tbh, I kind of miss it. Most of the games I've been playing recently are self-inserts. But if you're going to give me an actual character to play, don't pretend they're me. Let them just be who they are. Otherwise, I'm just going to feel the incongruity of having words put in my mouth when none of the dialogue choices are things I'd actually want to say.I got this game in the Pride Humble Bundle, along with several others, so it worked out as costing £1.67. I played it for 13.8 hours, and I can't really say I wouldn't recommend it, especially at that price. What you get out of it will depend on how closely your opinions align with the developers. Someone whose taste or personality is more similar to the lead character probably won't feel the dissonance that I felt.

_childDocuments_.review: tldr; isn't not worth the price. This game just doesn't have the amount of content is should for the price. It is rare that a dating-sim by an indie team even skirts the $20 mark and it's worth it, and this is not an exception. If you still want it, buy it on sale.There was controversy around this game that can't be missed, if you look up anything about it, the reviews will often focus more on its stalker antagonist and the demand for the developer to remove him and really say nothing about the game itself. Defenders compare this game with Persona 5 and the lack of backlash when it had sexual assault and suicide pretty early in the game. "Why this game and not that one? People are just being too sensitive, if you don't want to heed the content warnings, you cant be surprised if you're triggered. We are holding indie developers to a different standard than AAA games."But that's not the reason I gave it a 'no' recommendation. The plot barely exists after the first hour, other than text messages he sends that you can just ignore and the very end, you move on to date the other people in the game. I wouldn't buy it because it is boring, the relationships shallow, the combat is bleh, and... well, I finished a game with 6 romantic routes in 11 hours that cost $20 and that in itself is a good indication of a lack of content for the cost.The "story" of the game is the relationships. Getting through their relationships is how you advance the plot. I tried to keep everyone at the same level so that I could have the plot line up correctly but, that doesn't exactly work well. At the end of the day, the pacing is weird because of this mechanic, and needing to go into the dunj to advance the relationships was a cute idea but ultimately ended up being tedious since... well, play hades. Play children of morta. Just, try another rougelite and it'll make sense. The battle mechanics are just not there, not nuanced, not reactive enough for a satisfying rougelite, especially if you are actually into rouge games. This version is a baby version. It seems to be designed for people who don't play games like this.  The love interests... Everyone has their flaws and in general... well, all of them are pretty one note characters that end up being boring and reductive of the "representation" they are supposed to highlight. Sawyer being the worst, you play babysitter to an adult with the mental capacity of a child, and oh yeah, dont you want to bang them? Rowan is best bae hands down, with the story that has the best handling even while taking on heavy subjects (grief) and a satisfying conclusion. Seven is a fanfiction version of SUGA from BTS whose entire personality is "depressed". Sunder doesn't have an actual platonic route when despite telling him you're just friends he breaks up with you and your character gets messed up about it? Valeria invites, and then justifies her weirdo ex intimidating you and you're supposed to be friends in the end with no real reason to even try. Issac is a wealthy religious black man and wants to give money to charity and invest in starts up, but his father won't hear it - even tho wealthy people use charities as tax write offs irl. The ends of each relationship escalate into ridiculous hi-jinx that are more frustrating than funny, and sometimes disrespectful of the relationship you've built or to the character & the community they "represent".And then the game ends with confronting your stalker, because of course you have to. So, this is where the controversy thing crops back up and...I didn't have any issues with it until it got to this point, I think the REAL problem is the execution of the ending. The writers were more concerned about pushing a "feel good be a goody goody person" agenda than they were writing a meaningful story, so you get this ending: Dude made a chimera from your weapon-friends (by assaulting and abducting them then mutilating their bodies), and now that chimera is trying to kill you. Dude's "self-loathing makes it stronger" so you have to comfort your abuser to beat the chimera and at the end it's like, "poor guy, you should seek a therapist." Like, . Sure, he should see a therapist, . And THIS is why P5 is not comparable to this game, why it got a "pass" and BD doesn't. The antagonists in P5 are vilified, humiliated, arrested for their crimes. Boyfriend dungeon does that whole meta narrative thing of "this is how you actually be a good person" bs and... basically it comes down to the victim to absolve the abuser and the abuser sees no consequences for their actions. The crime and the punishment . I'm sure if the villain got what he deserved in the end, it wouldn't have been such a big deal. I'm sure people are even more pissed about it because it was funded by a kickstarter campaign.But ultimately, the ending of the game, the stalker dude and his behavior was only the tip of the iceburg, and they would have been aspects that were tangential to the experience if the romances were more fleshed out and better written. it needed more content overall, and considering the outcome in hindsight this game should have been either or. the plot should be longer, there should be at least another dunj. Or they could just lower the price of the game and my expectations would go down.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I enjoyed my experience with Boyfriend Dungeon and I recommend it to others who are seeking a light, summer-y, queer-friendly dating sim. However, my feelings are mixed enough for me to say: you should probably wait for a sale.By the way, Rowan is the best.Pros:- You can change your name, pronouns, and appearance at any point during gameplay. - Decent story replayability, as the routes change depending on your choice of being platonic/intimate/committed/etc.- Routes are somewhat dynamic, and dialogue/options will (slightly) change depending on if you've done other routes or not. - You can fully complete the game by choosing platonic routes for as many characters as you'd like, and are not penalized for doing so. (As an avid dating sim consumer, I found this to be refreshing in comparison to the typical "romance everyone or be denied the full plot" shtick.)- There is no upgrading for the weapons, and all of them scale with your own level. (Personally, I consider this a pro, as it means you are not penalized for leveling a character's route late. Others may not.)- Voice acting was mostly pretty nice. - Music in dungeons is dynamic and changes smoothly between passive/fighting.Cons:- Extremely short game. The time listed at review (8h) is the amount of time it took me to platinum the game. You can finish it blind in around 4-5 hours, easily. - The routes are very short and shallow. Not as in-depth as many dating sims; however, if you are looking for a light-hearted dating sim, this may be a plus.- Combat/dungeon-crawling is very repetitive and uninspired, and essentially boils down to mashing the same button until everything's dead. Damage scaling is very bad and you will likely become extremely overpowered.- Extremely limited dungeon locations. - Very short and forgettable OST, although I didn't mind listening to what was there (except for the bloody racing game song)- Racing game is an affront to mankind and embodies all of its sins. ♥♥♥♥ that achievement. Other Notes:- The possible routes consist of 3 men, 1 woman, 2 nonbinary characters, and a cat. The game did not contain any bigotry towards these characters for any aspects of their identities. - Personally, I found the ending of the cat's route to have some uncomfortable dialogue choices.- The depiction of a stalker was done... okay.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is phenomenally fun and exactly what the title says. For better or worst. As is the gameplay feels very similar to a game like Hades, but I actually enjoy the aspect that I'm able to switch weapons midway through a crawl to both A. Ensure that I'm experiencing all the game has to offer and all the character routes and B. Keep the combat refreshing and interesting over the course of a crawl without the same couple combos getting Stiff. My biggest issue is that the game falls flat once you start diving into the meat of it. A lot of the characters end up feeling generic without a lot of depths and more so stereotypes of what they represent than anything, and the fights lose a lot of fluidity over time as you discover that so long as you dodge properly you can pretty much spam the same button over and over again until the enemy dies, and most of the enemies just slowly walk towards you trying to swarm you or launch slow moving projectiles at you. And my biggest(Spoilers), and mostly serious, gripe is that THEY JUST KNOCKED AWAY THE CHARACTER I WAS MOST INTERESTED IN. They introduced him as a potentially dateable character, even giving him an interesting premise of how he handled the stalker character, and he texts you the next day saying he's leaving town and you don't see him again for the rest of the game. It's painstakingly obvious that they ran out of time/energy with the character and had to last minute write him out of the story(Why they kept the cat over him I'll never know). But I don't find this to be much of a flaw, because I am hoping it was because the workers on the game were able to work at a speed and pace they were comfortable with and let the character go for the sake of their own work ethic. I do hope we get to see him in a potential DLC or future update, but until then, go ahead and try the game out, it's a great 10 hours of your life.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a very enjoyable experience, that gets a little brought down by the mix of its mechanics.Pros:-Well written and diverse cast-Lots of variety between weapons-Fun music and great art direction-Enough enemy types and scaling within the dungeons-Combat feels very fluid-Lots of inclusive optionsCons:-Dating mechanics put a softcap on dungeon progression, meaning you'll need to exit midway to scale up-Not enough dungeons-Once you hit a certain level, the rougelike element basically fades away into the dating simA lot of these cons basically mean you really need to be along for both sides of the ride in this game, otherwise you'll not really be able to take it all in. Hardcore roguelike fans won't like having to leave dungeon progress behind (even if you can elevator to deeper floors) and visual novel fans might find some of the dungeon sections tedious.That said, it's definitely worth giving a shot and I'm looking forward to more content being added in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Boyfriend Dungeon is a dating sim with dungeon exploration gameplay similar to Hades. Despite coming into this game with a pretty open mind, I left feeling like Boyfriend Dungeon was a little below average.Story and Characters:The story to Boyfriend Dungeon is pretty simple and not memorable. An awkward protagonist comes to Varona Beach for a summer getaway and becomes friends - or lovers - with people that can turn into weaponry. There's a little more to the story, so it's an inspired premise, but a lackluster execution - the overarching story just was not that interesting to me. Boyfriend Dungeon's bachelors, bachelorettes, and one cat are very much meant to be the actual stars of the show. There's a good variety of characters, but I didn't come out of this game with a character that I very much liked. Maybe it had something to do with the lackluster voice acting, or the character arcs that just didn't resonate with me, or me being a straight dude, but I wasn't enthralled.Gameplay:Boyfriend Dungeon's dungeon crawling gameplay is basically Hades without the significant playtesting. There are numerous poor design decisions made that makes playing the game frustrating, like enemies being able to hit you the moment they spawn in, enemies being able to shoot down hallways at you before you see them, and the most unrewarding dodge rolls I've ever felt in a game. Later, when you've finally unlocked significant upgrades for your weapons and leveled up, you can just button mash through everything later on, often ignoring the problems rather than playing around them. Even then you may fall victim to glitches, like how I got knocked out of a boss's arena and had to restart the fight because I couldn't claim my rewards. Boyfriend Dungeon is not getting a gold star for its gameplay.In the end, I played through all of Boyfriend Dungeon, and while the game wasn't entirely unpleasant, I find it very hard to recommend this game unless you're desperately into dungeon crawlers or very curious into the characters that are gonna be thrown at you.

_childDocuments_.review: Updating my review after the DLC's releaseI played this game to 100% with the base game, then I played this game to 100% on a new save file after the DLC was released. The writing is fun and delightful and the range of dateable characters is awesome. I love the new love interests, especially Jonah and Holmes. Isaac was my fave in both playthroughs though. The dungeons aren't super involved, but they're perfect for a 15 hour game. You get to beat them and maybe do a little bit more grinding if you want to collect all recipes, but the dungeon crawling is paced perfectly to keep in step with the progression of the romance aspect.  The actual combat feels great, and I really love the interactions with the weapon you use at the rest spots. With the addition of the DLC, this game feels just like the brief but satisfying summer vacation that the storyline takes place in, Just the base game left me wanting something more, but with the addition of the DLC, I finished up my playthrough happy and refreshed, feeling like I'd had a great time and I've been buoyed up by the time I spent playing. Everything about this game feels tight and perfectly paced. Nothing overstays its welcome. It also is fun and enjoyable on both the dating side and the roguelite side. The combat feels nice, and the actual interactions with the characters feel nice too - you don't need a guide to avoid bad ends, so its easy to "be your self" and actually enjoy picking dialogue options and interacting. It really helps make the dialogue parts feel like actually talking and interacting, rather than trying to pick the correct answer in a quiz. The addition of the additional short encounters that leads to some interactions between two of the weapons + you also really helps fill out the sense of the world. And the plot with your cousin's wedding is really sweet. In general, the DLC didn't just add in more dateable characters and dungeons, it also filled out some details and add a bit of polish and padding that really help bring things to life.I liked all the weapon characters, and each of them provided a different kind of pleasant interaction. Yes, even Sunder. I liked his storyline on the first playthrough, even if it was a bit of an unpleasant surprise, and on the second playthrough, without the element of surprise, I could really appreciate all the clues being laid down, and I actually felt a lot of affection for him and how things developed. This is the kind of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ I totally wouldn't mind being actual friends with, after a break up. 100%ing all the characters also makes the villain plotline and all that stuff feel less like a big part of this summer vacation of love is being soured by a creep, and therefore actually helps it hit better as the pinch of salt that helps bring out the depth and dimension of all that sugar.Also, Mandy is bae and I DESPERATELY wish she was a dateable character.

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly can't believe I enjoyed this as much as I did. Who knew an action roguelite dating sim could be pulled off so brilliantly? The artwork is fantastic. The soundtrack is easily the best I've heard since Sayonara Wild Hearts. The transformation cutscenes are some of the coolest things I've ever seen in a game. The weapons/romance options are a diverse bunch, and each and every one is well-written, memorable, and deeply, deeply relatable (for me, at least - your mileage may vary). Best yet, you can woo each and every one of them in a single playthrough, or pick and choose who you want to date and who you want to friendzone. Want to be polyamorous? Do it! Want to just be friends with everybody? That works too! (Although, if you forced me to pick a single character of the bunch to date, I'm going with Seven every single time.)Fair warning: there are multiple trigger warnings that can be attached to this game. There are instances of stalking, poor paternal relationships, eating disorders, anxiety, and depression, just to name a few. These are not shiny, happy characters - not even your player character. The entire roster is dealing with some stuff, same as anybody else, and - for me, at least - it made these relationships feel very believable.Of course, tying all of this together are the roguelite dungeons, which are no slouch themselves. It's pretty standard fare for the genre - each dungeon is different every time you go in, but it's pulling from the same catalogue of rooms, so there is familiarity within the chaos. The highlight, though, is the smattering of hangout rooms you find along the way where you can interact with your chosen weapon and get an extra little slice of their character. It's a nice little slice of relaxation tucked into your runs that I appreciated from the start all the way to the finish. The combat feels perfectly fine, too. It's nothing revolutionary, but never feels bad, either, and I found it pretty easy to get into a good groove with the unique combos offered by each weapon.The only gripe I have about this game is the length. I didn't quite 100% the game, but I came VERY close, and it only took 11 hours and some change. Seriously, I would have played it twice that long if I had the chance. Hopefully the developers will work on a sequel or more updates/DLC, because I genuinely love this setting and all the characters within it, and I would gladly return for extra content. In summary, if you are open to the idea of an action roguelite dating sim (a grouping of words so unusual that it bears repeating), you'll find a good time within. I highly recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great. From a pure gameplay standpoint, the dungeoning takes back-seat to the dating, but is still satisfying and challenging enough that you'll want to keep coming back to it after unlocking new weapons or abilities for your existing ones. There's a nice pacing to the game between the action-oriented sections and the story/character beats. I would suggest however that if you're here primarily for the visual novel and dating sim elements that you might want to turn on the shield of the goddess in the options.The story and characters here are the real gems though. Loveable leads that I guarantee you'll find one to suit your fancy, especially if you go in with an open mind. The development of the relationships is satisfying, and despite this being a game where you date weapons, the relationships are portrayed more realistically than most.Its only real flaw is that it seems to be short. I haven't actually finished the game yet, but at 3 hours it seems I might be closing in on max rank for my weapon of choice (Valerie) and the story seems to be wrapping up as well. That being said, if I am close to the end, I will have ton of things to do post-game. I've only cleared one dungeon (of which it seems there are 4), I still have yet to really dive deep into any of the other weapon stories, and I'm enjoying the game enough that I would definitely do a full playthrough later. The game definitely didn't have a multi-million dollar budget, but they use their resources well in a concentrated and consistently fun experience that I expect to come back to, especially for DLC or workshop support.All in all, this is sweet, sexy fun that I think a lot of people will enjoy. The dungeon crawl aspect isn't another hades, but the pacing and character-driven narative focus does evoke it at times. Big recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: I want to point out that this game has a great idea and there is some stuff that I liked. However, I just felt so disappointed by how shallow it feels. It wants to be both a dungeon crawler as well as a dating sim but the game feels like it isn't good enough to excel in either of these genres. I really hate saying what I'm about to say because I BADLY wanted to like this game.In terms of writing, it seems like a lot of it is missing and a lot of the character development feels rushed. It is technically possible to be friends with your possible love interests but the game still treats it as a date and everyone acts like it's a date. They still act romantically towards you as if you didn't say "let's just be friends." That's not to say the really bad taste it left in my mouth because they introduced Sunder as one of the first weapons you get. He's basically a really gross womanizer that doesn't respect your space and those types of people tend to turn me off. If other weapons like Sawyer or Rowan were introduced earlier, it would have been better.In terms of dungeon crawling, there is much left to be desired. The combat feels incredibly shallow. There is a variety of weapons but very little enemy variety. Plus, there are only two dungeons. This makes me think that there was supposed to be more but a lot of it is missing. Valeria is actually pretty unbalanced because you can dodge to confuse enemies and you also get a perk that lets you crit enemies that are confused. This is also a bit of a nitpick but in the second dungeon, enemies can do a lot of damage and you can get swarmed really easily by the smaller enemies. If you get trapped, there isn't a whole lot you can do since you can't boost stats with armor like most games and you can't grind for anything other than health. You do get perks in hats though but most of them are unhelpful.Overall, I felt really disappointed by the game since it had potential to be something great but falls short in so many areas. It's especially disappointing when non binary representation is practically nonexistent. I think it could have been much worse considering that I was there when the Elite Dangerous Odyssey expansion and...well...it was something. I still don't know if I can recommend this game and that makes me really sad. :(

_childDocuments_.review: It's been a hell of a journey waiting for this game to come out over the past couple of years, but it's finally here and it was SO worth the wait. I have adored every moment spent with this game, and having binged it to completion I find myself longing for more of it all. The beautiful world, the stunning soundtrack, the gorgeous animations and of course the utterly wonderful characters. Combat feels fast and fluid. Took me a little bit of adjusting to, but once I'd gotten used to my swords (And smooched them a little, for some tasty upgrades!) I was plowing through the dungeons. The weapon variety is really neat, though in my opinion a couple are a little overtuned compared to others. Not that I mind, because they're all fun to use regardless of the fact! The writing is pretty solid, though I do wish there were more of it! Maybe it's just because I have now beaten the game and want to play it for another 50 hours, but the story felt a little short and the different relationships felt like they could've each had more content. Though I know there's a good bit of choice and diversity in how they can play out, so I suppose that makes for great replay value! And the game supports just about every form of identity, as well. As a non-binary asexual, it was absolutely delightful to meet Enby characters and be given the chance to form meaningful platonic or romantic non-sexual relationships with every single weapon. Really affirming in ways that warmed my heart to its core. Even the way one weapon reacted to the fact that my character was Non-binary brought a little tear to my eye - it was really sweet. So on a personal note, thanks for brightening my day Kitfox. I needed it.In summary, huge recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: Boyfriend Dungeon is a good game! It's not fantastic, but I like it plenty, and I recommend it to fans of dungeon crawlers and dating sims, or even if you're a newbie to dungeon crawlers. Perhaps especially if you're a newbie⁠—one my my main negative criticisms of the game is that the dungeons are pretty easy for an experienced rougelite player (which I am not, but they were still easy). The weapons seem a little unbalanced in my personal opinion, as two of them make any dungeon a complete breeze for me, which I honestly don't mind much, but if you're looking for a challenge, you won't find it here.My other main criticism is lack of player affect on the end of the game. There are lots of minor choice impacts you can have, but there will be no large difference due to your actions. Disappointing, but not at all a deal breaker in my opinion. I was pleasantly surprised how much I liked that I had to use each weapon in the dungeon to progress the date bar, and it was a great motivator for me to keep fighting, as I wanted to interact with all of the characters. I'm not the biggest rougelite player, but I really enjoyed this aspect. A nice soundtrack plays as you fight! A lot of the songs are really similar, but I was fine with it. Character art is great, your little player character is fun to dress up. Writing can be a little sappy at times, but I genuinely was interested in multiple characters, a rarity for me when I play a dating sim. Conclusion: good game! Lots of fun, interesting characters, combat is just fine, nothing to write home about. Definitely worth the $20! I 100% the game in about 11 hours, but a free DLC came out with some new weapons (all lovely characters to add to the cast!) and I think I'll probably have 100% the game again in maybe 15 hours or so. If the trailers intrigue you, buy it!

_childDocuments_.review: I'll be honest, I really, really wanted to like this game. I even backed it on Kickstarter because it looked so good and had so much promise. Romance Although there are multiple romances in the game, and you can romance everyone at the same time, I never felt like any of them were all that deep. I didn't feel particularly emotionally invested in any of the characters, which is a shame because I liked almost all of them, and I think its because their routes, compared to other games, are fairly shallow They have some character building moments in them, I guess, but it wasn't much of a build-up to those moments compared to other games. 2. DungeonsWhen it comes to the dungeons, I was also very disappointed. There's only three of them, and although I enjoyed actually fighting in them, they got repetitive and boring after a while, just turning into a grind to get LI's affection up. I had hoped there would be several more, but nope. Just those. Once you know what to expect, it's not much of a challenge either.3. PlotIn terms of plot, it's sadly way too straightforward for my taste. You get to a point in the game where I hoped it would mean the intro of the actual Big Bad, which would mean new missions and plot, but nope. That was the end of it. It was severely underwhelming. And it didn't take too long to accomplish literally everything in the game, either. To get all the romances, all of the cosmetics, and defeat the dungeons really didn't take all that long for me. If I really wanted to, I could probably get it all done within a day or two.All in all, if you're looking for a simple game that you can kill some time with and don't care too much about having deeper plots, you may enjoy this game. _childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting for this game for like... 2 years or somesuch.  Saw a description, went 'wow, that looks like fun' and then it took a long time to release.  That said, it released, and I blitzed through it in about... Well, 6-7 hours.  Definitely not the longest game in the world, but a lot of fun in the time it took.Strengths:  The combat is satisfying, if a bit simple, with a dodge roll and combos for each weapon, with what felt like a fairly lenient level-up system that should let players more familiar with the dating-sim genre grind through the dungeon levels with relative ease.  The characters are excellent, and the voice acting is spot-on.  Every character I was able to max out a relationship with, I *wanted* to max out a relationship with, in one way or another.  Also, literally everyone is good to look at.  Also, in the interaction bits, 9/10 times, there was a response that matched approximately what I'd want to say, which was heartening.The game also paid off what it set up, by which I mean that it was pretty clear from fairly early on what the approximate ending was going to be, but it was delivered in a satisfying way.  (Also, I wasn't expecting ProZD as hot sword man, still surprises me when he isn't doing comedy).  After completing the game, your last save will be right before the finale, letting you retry all battle options with any character.Weaknesses:  There are no *glaring* issues, but there are a lot of minor things.  Sometimes, characters will know about things, and it won't be clear how the information got to them.  You get random events in the dungeons, and if the same weapon gets one twice, nothing changes about their dialogue, which feels kind of weird.  I cleared an early combat event I probably wasn't supposed to, and the mid-combat dialogues were messed up for another 4 levels before I finally got knocked out.  If you leave people on 'read,' long enough, text conversations triggered by game events will stack up.  They still trigger appropriately, but the jump from one convo to another can be a bit jarring.None of these issues ultimately ruin the quality, and the game feels complete, but it's definitely one to be played more for the relationships and characters than the combat (especially since, in my playtime, I managed to rack up combat levels several at a time probably meaning I was getting powerful faster than the game intended, ultimately meaning the final boss went down with very little actual time).  There definitely feels like an opening here for some kind of additional challenge, whether this be some kind of new game +, or optional modifiers to enemies or combat generally (Enter the Gungeon's sped up mode comes to mind)Ultimately, having played through this game in one shot, I have to say I enjoyed my time.  While this is not a $60, AAA game, it is an enjoyable, $20 game that I wouldn't mind running through again to try other paths.

_childDocuments_.review: Boyfriend Dungeon is a captivating blend of dating and dungeon-battling, a unique concept that surprised me in a good way. The game's premise is as odd as it sounds: dating weapons that can transform into people. Playing the role of someone spending the summer with their cousin, you're set up on dates that are anything but ordinary. These "dates" involve diving into dungeons that have sprung up around town, facing off against monsters tied to your subconscious.The dating aspect takes the spotlight here, with each weapon having its own distinct personality and storyline. Relationships evolve as you spend time together in dungeons and go on dates. The character writing is wonderful, with a range of personalities and diverse gender representations. The variety of characters is impressive, and the writing truly shines. Sunder's mixture of emotional neediness and distance, Isaac's sensitivity, and Seven's ethereal K-Pop persona all add layers to the narrative and there is plenty to explore.However, the game isn't perfect. The combat mechanics, while unique for each weapon, could have been deeper and more challenging. Navigating dungeons can feel a bit loose, but overall, it's manageable. The disappointment comes from the limited number of dungeons, which I had hoped for more of but as mixed genre game it does pretty well handling the sum of its parts. Dating multiple weapons to "completion" raised some eyebrows, but the lack of consequences for this action felt a tad unrealistic. Yet, it's par for the course in dating sims, isn't it? Although... it would have been interesting for them to cover topics of polyamory or add some sort of consequence for doing so as it never hurts to have more depth but I digress.Despite these drawbacks, Boyfriend Dungeon's strength lies in its ability to create connections between players and characters in an engaging way. It's an unexpected delight, fusing romance and action into a singular experience.If you're a fan of dating sims with a twist, Boyfriend Dungeon is definitely worth a shot. It's a game that manages to blend heartwarming romance with action-packed gameplay, resulting in a fun and unique adventure that I highly reccomend.

_childDocuments_.review: Boyfriend Dungeon sound so... fake that when I found it on Gamepass something like a year or so ago I looked at it and didn't give it a second thought. You date your weapons while dungeon diving? It sounds just so weird that I didn't think it would have too much depth. Even when I got it off Humble Bundle in a game bundle I only played it to tease one of my friends (who happened to be named the same as one of the weapons).Instead I found a fairly fun and decent game. The gameplay loop is pretty much what you'd expect. The game starts you off with one of eight weapons, more weapons progressively unlocking as you proceed through the game, where you delve into a dunji with a weapon of your choice earning affection points and progressing the story. The combat aspects CAN leave you desiring more. A lot of the weapon choices to me felt clunky and slow, particularly the hammer and axe, but still it was fun enough and even when grinding out affection levels you never feel forced to do insane feats to level up any of your weapons. The visual novel/dating simulator aspects to the game are also fairly decent, with nine different people for you to date all with their own personalitys. Some are less then pleasant, but everyone can find something they like out of the selection their given. The villain pretty obvious really quickly. The clingy guy who you don't want to date whos always judging everyone your around or even yourself, and soon starts to get to psychopathic territorys. The only downside was that there wasn't MORE dating simulator aspects. A lot of the conflicts that your dates have seem to be rushed through rather rapidly, with no real conclusion for many of them except for the thought that in the future they might be better. I guess in real life you experience the same thing, only a hope that the guy you dated in highschool will stop goofing off about football and commit himself, or the hope that the college stoner will finally get serious about studying and stop acting like a burnout.Over-all it was a good experience. With a fairly enjoyable selection of dates, a wide variety of personalitys and sexualitys, no need to commit to any one particular person or even interact with them if you don't want to, and combat that feels as though anyone can find something they like, even if it could be better. Is it the best game in the world? No, but it certainly is an experience.
