_childDocuments_.review: As someone who backed this during the Kickstarter, I really wanted to recommend Boyfriend Dungeon. For a game with such an awesome premise - Fight Your Fears with Weapon-People You Date! - it unfortunately just does not hold up in the face of other options out there, and thus I can't do so, past it being on sale.tldr: The premise is good, but the game ends just when it feels like it should be opening up. Romance options are hit and miss, feeling like they're cramming 12 one-on-one sessions into 6 scenes. Combat manages to remain fun, but with only two dungeons and a total of 4 bosses, you don't get to really play around with all your options. Snag it on sale, but not full price.Pros+The soundtrack is great. Sure, this is subjective, but every piece is smooth and sells the laid-back, fun atmosphere the game is going for.+The art style is lovely. In the dating sim aspects, character portraits stand out and tell you everything you need to know about a character (at first blush, anyway), while the somewhat blocky style in the dunj-diving felt oddly fitting. Enemy design also felt unique - don't think I've fought fanged-flip phones before.+The gameplay is fun. Each weapon has their own simple 3 or 4 hit combo, with a mix of light and heavy options. Leveling up your date-level with each one also adds more rider-effects or bonuses to your attacks. While enemies are largely simple, they remain fun to plow through.+The fashion aspect is a nice touch. I enjoyed swapping outfits.+No time limit. I did appreciate being able to see all the dating scenes for all the characters on one playthrough.+Ability to find love - platonic or romantic. This is something I'd like to see more dating sims take up, and I do commend the amount of effort put into this. +I enjoyed the text messages - Something about them was oddly charming to me.Cons-Length. I 100%'d the game in around 7 hours, and the entire thing could reasonably be finished in 5, if not less. Two dunj's, four bosses total... And there isn't exactly a ton of room variety in the dunjs' either. 1-on-1 moments with your weapon help break up the monotony in a dunj, but it just becomes padding after a while. It feels like there should have been at least one more dunj, if not two. There is just not enough content, outside of wanting to see all the different dates. And speaking of the dates...-The dates feel rushed. Every weapon gets an initial intro scene in some way, though Isaac and Sunder get the most by virtue of being the tutorial characters. But past that, everyone gets a very cramped story arc fit into 6 scenes - and for some, even parts of those feel a bit like filler! Pocket, by virtue of being a cat, gets that the worst, but as a cat, I can let it slide, especially for the bizarre finale. For the rest, dialogue in general felt a bit... lackluster. The best scenes were ones where the characters actually *talked* about something important - Seven's discussion of his problem stands out as a very believable scene that made me care about him much more than I had before. As a counter-point, I can barely recall anything I did with Sawyer, past 'bad at basic cooking.'It feels like the game needed more time in the oven, and I think Kitfox knew this - but in an effort to get the game out in a reasonable time, they pushed two of the stretch-goal characters out as future-patch/dlc and sent it out. Unfortunately, I don't see more dates + extra clothes or hats extending the game in the way it clearly needs - and deserves. At *least* two new dunj and probably some other villain would be necessary. The lore has some neat things going on, it's just a shame it never gets truly examined past offhand remarks. I want to know why some people can change to weapons, and others can't. I want to know what it is about Verona Beach that makes dunj's of people's fears appear. It's all got style and charm but there's so little substance...In conclusion, I want to recommend Boyfriend Dungeon - I wanted to love this game! But unfortunately, just like the MC's summer, this dunj-dive ends too soon to feel like something meaningful took place. If the game goes on sale, grab it for a dreamy afternoon, but at full price, this is not worth the cost.

_childDocuments_.review: A varied roster of choices, from a cuddly, beach loving-bear to an astrology freak that may or may not be human (ilysm). Each character is well developed, the art is so pretty and there is enough diversity to cater to all tastes.You get to design your own avatar/character, they're visible when you're running around the city or fighting. Diving down into dungeons is how you develop your relationship with your weapon of choice. Fight together, learn how to handle them and the further down you go, the more XP points you get to advance the story with your beloved by unlocking dates with them in the city. In the 'surface world', you're also able to text people, visit shops to buy crafting materials or gifts for your date, and you're also able to change your outfit to get buffs or extra skills.The combat is challenging but accessible and quite fun. Each bae will have a different combat style, for example a fast dagger versus a long range scythe. You also get to craft buffs that will alter your approach. You'll also get little date opportunities at rest stops within the dunj. You can complete multiple characters routes in one play through. But saying that, this may be a downside -  there's no ultimate happy ending with your blade of choice. It's kind of left open ended.As for the question all dating sim players will be asking - is there nsfw? Not really. There's some steamy written moments, spicy flirting, implied first times, sort-of fanservice-y transformation scenes but nothing explicit. There's enough to fall in love with your blade!!Overall, it's not the most in-depth romance game since the focus is more on the combat but I think Kitfox did extremely well in balancing all these seemingly mismatched aspects of Boyfriend Dungeon together.

_childDocuments_.review: I definitely recommend this as a dating sim/dungeon crawl.Some things I really liked:-You can romance any and every sword you want how you want (ex. no sexy times if you don't want, no conflicts if you pursue multiple story lines at the same time, etc.)-The characters are unique and show growth/development through their arcs-The swords are different enough that it's fun to do the differing styles-The dialogue options are awesome and varied-The SOUNDTRACK <3-The voice acting :)Some things I didn't like as much:-There are only two dungeons so once you beat them and you need to keep leveling up your romance with the swords, it's a bit grindy/samey and repetitive doing the same dungeons over and over-Some aspects of the main story line and each of the sword's story lines are triggering depending on what kind of trauma you have (but they do warn at the beginning of the game)-Maybe it's just because I binge played it and was in the right mode, but I felt like the final boss was kind of easy to beatI am going to replay in the future and would love to play any similar games/expansions/DLC that come out for this one! _childDocuments_.review: There is not enough content here to warrant a purchase right now, especially not for what is being presented as a finished product.  I'm 5 hours in and have completed the main story, the two (2!) total dungeons, and most of the available romances.The game fails both as a dungeon crawler and a dating sim at this time.   While the dungeon crawling mechanics are solid (if very simplistic) hack and slash fare, the very limited amount of variance in the disappointingly short procedurally generated levels in the two dungeons mean you will speed through them very quickly.  Coupled with the fact that the limited amount of discoverable items currently available as rewards for these dungeon crawls means that the sole reason to delve into these two dungeons is simply to max out your next bond levels with your favorite romanceable weapons.  Even this would probably be more forgivable if the romances were satisfying - they aren't.Boyfriend Dungeon currently has three (3) male romance options, two (2) nonbinary, one (1, ) female, and a single cat that mercifully only has a friendship route available.  Two additional romances have been teased as eventual Kickstarter-backed rewards that will be added at a later date,  one male (an axe, currently appearing only as a cameo in the early stages of the game;  also the only hypothetically romanceable character to feature a less 'conventionally attractive' physique if we remember that the cat is thankfully just your friend) and one female (a hammer, currently absent.)  There's an attempt to inject deeper themes such as issues of fidelity, living with chronic mental illness, and coping with loss into the romances, of which there are six (6) scenes total for each potential Boyfriend/Girlfriend/Theyfriend.  The problem is that these attempts to add more complex issues into each weapon's storyline does little to enhance them if each character amounts to little more than stock tropes.The Glaive recently came out as nonbinary and is learning to embrace their identity!  Cool, but what's the point of that if the writing for each of their scenes doesn't progress beyond   The Talwar attempts to reconcile a wildly polyamorous lifestyle with a desire to connect with people on a deeper, meaningful level, but what's point of that if his character can be reduced to  every time he appears on screen?  Special shoutout to the Laser Saber and the Scythe, who are both dealing with their own versions of depression, and that of course justifies how incredibly rude they are to you.  I dunno about you, but if I wanted to be negged for around $20 USD I'd just get a Tinder Gold subscription.I know that those of us who identify as queer people feel really starved for queer content, and that much of the time we're forced to satisfy ourselves with scraps - halfhearted romances with characters without unique facemaps in AAA titles, ambitious but poorly funded indie novels, the offhanded mention that one of your backup units has a husband in a jRPG - and Boyfriend Dungeon's announcement a few years back really seemed to be a breath of fresh air against that backdrop.  But as it stands, unless there's much, much more on the horizon?

_childDocuments_.review: Boyfriend Dungeon is a game that feels well intentioned, but does little to actually provide any meaningful gameplay or story. You are a nobody with no confidence who rolls into town for the summer. You are told there are dungeons that manifest your fears! So go in, kills some monsters, make some money, all while wielding a weapon that is also a person. With that premise, how does it fall flat? Well, to start, combat is very lackluster. It's usually a 3-4 hit chain of LMB for light and RMB for heavy. Enemies have extremely telegraphed moves and hitting them pauses their attacks wind up, meaning you can get through the dungeons with little to no effort. The layout of the dungeons makes it easy to kite them too, making the whole process of going through dungeons mostly thoughtless. You can also use "Zines" and "Beverages" to do special abilities and to heal, respectively. These items are found en masse in the dungeon too, making their potential impact on gameplay mostly meaningless. It also might help if there were more than only 2 dungeons with less than 30 floors between BOTH of them. You do also find money and crafting materials in dungeons, but I'll list why I don't find those to matter much.Moving on to crafting, you can find blueprints in dungeons, along with crafting materials. You can craft outfits for yourself, new zines, gifts, and helmets. The issue is that most of these things are quite useless, and you can only craft each item ONCE. Helmets (sometimes) give unique effects that make them worth crafting. Outfits just change your look, nothing else. Zines can be helpful, but they give you the arguably best one at the start. Gifts, well, gifts are worthless. Gifts can be given for potential boost in affection to any weapons you have. They would be good, if it wasn't so easy to just go through a dungeon mindlessly killing to get the affection instead of finding the materials for the gift, crafting it outside of the dungeon, finding a moment to give the gift, and then maybe they'll like the gift. Oh, and did I mention you can only craft a gift once? (I did.) That means that if you give a pizza to a guy, and he hates it, you can never give anyone else a pizza in that particular save.As for the characters, they're shallowly written and their stories are far too short. You get, in counting, 6 dates with them. The dates are... very short and often feel pointless. Cat goes to cafe, you see cat, cat hisses at woman, leaves. Go to movie with guy, he get's noticed, leaves, then you leave after talking to the person who noticed him. No real... substance. You also get some unique flavor text if you have them when you find certain spots in the dungeons, but the actual stories of the characters are only worth maybe 40 minutes of reading EACH. You have the horny stud at the nightclub, the renegade painter, the dorky college student, etc. None of the characters feel unique. The art is unique, but they didn't push themselves. Enemies are bar glasses, stereos, cell phones, etc. The overworld looks, ultimately, generic. The portraits have this uncanny valley vibe to them. It just feels... off. I would've loved to see the world they've made be given a true identity, as it feels like right now it has none.The story is messy and, I'm sorry but, it's utterly terrible. I'll summarize the start, and then put in the spoiler tag my gripes about the mid to late game story. You arrive at the beach town. Your cousin gives you an apartment for the summer free of rent. He sets you up with dates and the dungeon gigs. You find weapons down there who all don't remember how they got down there. Then, they come back to the surface to date you with dialogue that ranges from pretty good to downright cringe. Now, for the spoiler-y stuff: Now, you'd think that, at the very least, despite all the issues elsewhere, that the game that let's you smooch your weapons would have at the very least a CG kiss scene, right? Well, uh... No. There is no CG. Of any kind. The only visual cues are changes in the character's portrait expressions.So, in short, there are 2 short dungeons, 7 date-able characters with little depth to them, a lackluster art direction, and good intentions. It's not nearly worth $20. I'd say it's worth half that in it's current state, especially given we're missing one of the stretch goal characters from the Kickstarter and the other stretch goal one makes a one time story appearance only to disappear forever. As a Kickstarter backer, I am disappointed, as I backed it in the hopes that it would be far deeper an experience than it can offer right now. Wait to see how they treat post launch, see how their "lite modding support" goes, and then make your decision.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, I wish there was more! In a lot of ways..I felt like I blazed through a lot of the main game because I was enjoying the dungeon crawl and combat. _childDocuments_.review: I have mixed feelings, but I don't have such an option on Steam.tl;dr: dungeon crawler part - good. Otome part and plot - bad. Game short.Contains spoilers. It will be long.On the one hand, we have a decent dungeon crawler. Its strongest sides are for sure creativity with both ideas about enemies (as a manifests of player's fears) and about weapons (gameplay-wise, they feel original and I absolutely loved the idea of gravity skills on a scythe). It isn't difficult, so it is accessible for everyone - better player's will just progress faster and there is no skill-wall for the rest. The painful thing is that everything is short and can get pretty boring when you have only 2 dungeons for the entire game, but I will return to that point later. For me, this part was at least nice overall.And then came the otome part of the game... And its plot. I will divide this part on 2 sections: Rowan’s route case study (cause they are the only character I had a romantic relation with) and overall plot.Otome part feels just rushed. It doesn't give you a time to get used to a romance/friendship option; to spend time casually; to wait a bit with opening. We have only 6 meetings per character, so the writers had to pack a relation into these 6 meetings. And it was a tiny, tiny box. Valerie's route has the best pacing, I think, but for 1 Valerie we have 6 other characters, like Rowan. Then it turns out we know almost nothing about past of these characters, about their memories, dreams, favorite places – things lovers and friends should have an idea about.About Rowan’s route: its pacing is totally wild.First meeting: I want to kill you.Second meeting: I’m sorry I wanted to kill you.Third meeting: Eric is stupid.Forth meeting: Oh no, Crowley is gone, help.Fifth meeting: We will medidate. And, btw, I don’t want to date you, cause I will lose you just like I lost my grandmother. (what was their relationship with their grandmother even? All we know is that she was named Alice and was a witch!)And in the end they decide to stay with the relationship, because they met their grandmother… It doesn’t feel right. How about their feelings? Their own development as a character and growth as a person? About overcoming their own fear of intimacy, because they love player’s character more than they are afraid of losing someone once more?Also, Seven’s route has the same problem as Rowan’s route – a serious problem gets intoduced and just passes by with a divine touch of player’s character. Grief and depression aren’t things that can be easily overcome. Portraing them like that is simply wrong and misleading.Overall plot… It was just shallow. We have The Villain TM, who is So Evil! The game just shows Eric from the worst side all the time and it is boring: he dislikes cats, he wants to buy cheaply blades from Rowan, he is racist and most of the time will speak about it. Also, he exists to show how cool our love interests/friends are. It feels like a story written by a middle school girl, where a plastic barbie is a must-have villain. Eric’s motivations also aren’t explained well, we don’t have any reason to understand him or feel for him.Shortness of the game: it has around 10-15 hours of gameplay (I am not a dungeon crawler expert and I finished it with 96% achievements, so I suppose it is a normal time), which may be a reason why writing is so rushed. The writers may have interesting, complex stories in mind, but without enough time to expose them correctly… well, it hasto end up like that.A special mention: soundtrack! It was modern, fresh and it fits well to the game.In the end, the dungeon crawling part manages well, but is pulled down by the plot.

_childDocuments_.review: What a fun little game! I intended to just casually play this an hour or two at a time, but I got super drawn into it and wanted to see it through to the end, so I finished it way faster than I intended to. It's a simple game. The characters aren't particularly deep, but still plenty enjoyable and it's fun to date them (shoutout to Valeria and Seven for being lovely, and also (spoiler) ). The roguelite dungeon gameplay isn't particularly hard and I could get away with mostly buttonmashing even to finish the hardest content in the game (albeit with a few tries in the worst cases), but that's fine, I wasn't looking for anything challenging either. It's genuinely just a nice and casual game to get through, which was pretty much exactly what I was looking for. A huge bonus for me is also that it is just a delightfully queer game, and though that wasn't the way I played, even seeing the dialogue options where you can choose to just be friends or have an asexual romantic relationship was very appreciated. There are also a great amount of quite sensitive details put in by the devs, for example, you are asked in the beginning of the game if you are comfortable receiving supportive messages from your mother, and even though all those details aren't for me, it's still nice to see in the game. But here's the big one that this game has gained some notoriety for: as the warning informs at the very beginning of the game, it 'references stalking'. Only it doesn't just reference stalking, you very literally gain a stalker and the fact that you have this stalker is a significant part of the story. While they I think succeed in making this a deeply uncomfortable experience, it is an experience I honestly wish wasn't there in such a large capacity when I go into this thinking it's just a fun game where you do dungeons with weapons you can also date. I'm not inherently opposed to such a story being told and they did handle the storyline with care, but I do wish that the focus of the main story were on something else. But besides that: I genuinely had fun here and I'm glad I put in the time to see all the content.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: This game is gay as heck. The cast is great, gameplay is fun, there's a good but not excessive amount of collectibles, and the devs did a good job job of having a story that works with whoever and however many of your weapons you decide to date.  Definitely worth the $20, while short and pretty easy by dungeon crawler standards it's a fun and pretty unique experience. The gameplay isn't super deep, each weapon has a set of combos consisting of mixes of heavy and light attacks but almost none of them are more complicated than: press light as many times as you want, then heavy for the rest of the 4 or 5 hit combo. Each weapon does have unique abilities that unlock as you improve your relationship such as chain lightning on hit or critical hits if your enemies are confused. Combat feels satisfying and there's enough loot keep completionists occupied without being overwhelming. For the dating part of dating your weapons, you've got guys, gal (just the one for now but another is coming in an update or dlc), and non binary pals, and you can set your own gender to one of these options as well. You'll have a good mix of personalities amongst your arsenal, each with a pretty interesting and unique story to explore. There's no punishment for polyamory and there are aro and ace options for each partner. Although each of these "options" are set by a single dialogue choice each and you cannot change your mind afterwards. Started a relationship with Isaac because he was the first character you met but later decided that Rowan is the nb of your dreams and you'd like to be exclusive with them? Not today. Also depending on the character, platonic relationships can feel kinda weird in this game, sometimes feeling like your dates (spending time with a character is called a date regardless of what your status is with them) have only had one or two bits of dialogue modified ever so slightly to account for your decision.There is a disclaimer regarding this at the start but this game has some uncomfortable stalker moments in it and I'd strongly recommend treading lightly if that's a subject that you are sensitive to for whatever reason.
_childDocuments_.name: Boyfriend Dungeon

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. The dungeons are a fun dive and the music to go along with it is soooo good. The art styles and colors are incredibly well done. Each and every one of the characters felt like real, complicated people. This is more than just another visual novel meets dungeon delver, this is a journey into our own self worth, self confidence, and self identity. Yes the main villain is a creep but I disagree with the hate that this game has been given because of him. The content warning at the beginning was more than enough to sway someone away who might be triggered by his unwanted attention. They state outright: “play with care.” I don’t know any female friends who have not had an “Eric” in their lives. I myself suffered from this exact kind of manipulation and mental assault from an “Eric”for many years. When your character meets Eric in game and he begins to disregard your requests for him to quit his advances, I was audible with disgust because it brought back awful memories and made Eric feel even more like a real person. _childDocuments_.review: : A quick and cute fusion of both dating sim and Roguelike where you can make as many friends or more-than-friends as you want, and still get all the achievements easily. Take the "may" in the game's trigger warning as a "does" or "will" for the main story. Really hope to have another game at Verona beach soon....The game is a fun little hybrid of a dating sim and a Roguelike and I'm all for it.- Each "dunj" was a fair challenge. Not too hard, and didn't get too easy too quickly when levelling up.- I found the characters themselves to be a lot of fun to interact with.- Both the music and art style are great.- There's someone for everyone in this game, and you can choose if you want to just be friends with them, date one person, or date them all at once. This doesn't make the game easier or harder, and you can still get all the achievements, even if things are just platonic.- On top of saying the right thing or giving them gifts, you can bond with your preferred weapons by fighting with them "in the dunj". It makes sense to me, and it also makes it easier for people who aren't used dating sims. You can make up for wrong answers by just fighting together.- Voice acting in dating sims is always tricky to get right without making me, at least, feel embarrassed. I tend to turn it off, but I kept it on because I found  of the voice acting to be quite fun. Still cringed in most of the romantic bits, but that's me.- Weapon transformation animations were a nice treat. Hope we can see updated animations if the game ever gets a revamp.- Too short? The game is meant to take place over three-ish months, but It felt like maybe a couple of weeks. As a consequence, I feel like the characters kind of suffered for it.- Characters were deeper than many in dating sims, but because of this, I feel like the creators could've gone a lot further. I feel like more interactions with them really would've made them shine. This resulted in next to no heart-flutters for me, which I think is a significant goal for dating sims like this one. .- The auto-save was a champ, but I do like the multiple save file feature that most VNs have. If I could, I would've had a save especially made so I could repeat the last chapter for my favourite suitor. As far as I could tell, there was no way to go back to certain beats of the story.- For me, a couple of characters didn't have voices that suited them, which lead to me being taken out of the atmosphere and just thinking about them in the booth. No hate to the VA, but Holmes had the voice I took most issue with.- Didn't bother me, but it may bother others. Game has already faced controversy for this, but trigger warning needs to be rephrased. It effectively says you "may" encounter certain triggers, but they're all in the main story. _childDocuments_.review: SUMMARY: An accessible and surprisingly deep and emotional fusion of roguelike, datesim, and social sim.  Date living weapons, explore procedural dungeons, face your fears, craft goods, and find love (or just lust).  Boyfriend dungeon is the weapon-dating alternate-modern world dungeon crawler you didn't know you wanted - until now.Boyfriend Dungeon sounds like a bit of a joke - "Date living weapons to explore dungeons."  Though it will poke at some tropes, it's a fully-envisioned game that fuses Datesim and Roguelike with an actual plot (and many subplots), great art, and a lot of heart.  It's Soul Eater meets Persona that then goes beyond its simple premise.You're a visitor to a California City, Verona Beach, in a world of both modern technology and commonplace mystical happenings.  Some people can become weapons, magic is real, and dungeons made of twisted fears pop out of the ground.  You're in town to face some fears in the depths of the mind and maybe meet someone - fortunately plenty of attractive living weapons are here to make life easier.So let's get to the game:THE CHARACTERS: Most of the cast are living weapons, but they also have complete stories and personalities.  Don't expect to fully understand, like, or predict everyone.  Also expect to find that you have favorites as the cast is fully realized, and full of surprisies that may make you laugh, think, or feel your heartbeat speed up.  The writing is excellent and the characters compelling.THE DATING: Dating happens in various choice-driven segments and some random dungeon events.  Expect some pretty complicated plotlines, deep choices, revelations, and cuteness.  Give gifts, make choices, and be ready for surprises . . .(The game is inclined to those attracted to men, and even if that's not your preference, there are plenty of options.  Also, its a very RP-driven game, so it's fun to create a personality for your character and follow that!)THE WEAPONS: Most of your life revolves around the living weapons.  As you build relationships, new abilities come out.  Each plays radically different.  You'll find favorites, least-favorites, and plenty of strategies.THE DUNGEONS: Face weird monsters in procedural dungeons - that are also outings.  Beat monsters, stop for ice cream, find treasures and blueprints.  You may just learn more about your character.CRAFTING: Of course there's crafting!  Make gifts, clothes, and magical zines.  These affect the game of course, and are fun to try and collect.DRESS UP: Honestly, you want to be able to dress up, right?THE PLOT: Yes, there's a plot - multiple ones, really.  Don't think you know everything, and small and large revelations will challenge you.  The game INVITES you to role-play and be in character because actions have consequences and choices may be difficult.There are a few flaws in the game:* The in-dungeon fighting is a little "floaty" - aiming and play isn't that precise.* There's not a huge variety of dungeon levels or monsters.* It's relatively short (maybe 6-8 hours).  However, if you want to be a completist, there is a lot to do.  There's also a LOT to it, so in the hours you spent with it, it is very fulfilling.* You may have to grind a bit, but that's part of the gernes.  And yes, maybe grinding is a bit of a metaphor too . .Boyfriend Dungeon is worth your time if any of this intrigues you.  A fusion of various elements that we don't often see together, well-written, and heartfelt.  Hopefully, we're seeing the launch of a franchise of gorgeous weapon-people having romance and fighting monsters.

_childDocuments_.review: Boyfriend Dungeon is a short, sweet hack-and-slash game that you can easily finish within a day if you dedicate yourself to doing nothing but playing it the whole time. I completed it in about 8.5 hrs, and it was an overall fun experience. The keyboard controls were rather unpleasant for me, so I opted for a controller instead and found it much easier to wield my weapons and defeat monsters in the dunj (dungeon). I thought this would be a simple hack-and-slash game with some dating elements and was surprised when each romanceable character came with their own storyline. The player's own character also goes through growth, and it's satisfying to see how it wove in with the overall plot. I admittedly didn't like all of the romanceable characters because I found their personalities grating, but there's a lot of variety in who you can date (or just want to have as a friend!) and the inclusivity in the dateable characters is refreshing. The gameplay itself isn't difficult, especially after I switched to a controller. I do wish there was an option to just leave the dungeon after a floor is completed rather than having the option of swapping weapons and then continuing. Sometimes I would just let myself die in the dungeon just so I could get out of the dunj and go on dates so I could further my relationship with characters. I also wish that the player could make some craftable items more than once. Otherwise, a really pleasant game. Time flew by as I was playing it and I was surprised whenever someone in the game mentioned that my time with them was nearing to an end. If you want a short, creative game to play and the premise of Boyfriend Dungeon appeals to you, go for it!

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed all of my time with this game. Even getting to see the stories of characters I didn't really resonate with, and re doing floors in the dunj for love rank/ level was enjoyable. Just maybe not repeatable. I spent 13 hours with the game and could have easily spent 13 more. Pros:*Variety of characters and play styles- you have a weapon for every dungeon crawling preference, and a personality for every dating type. *Dating more than one character is okay- this is an odd one to considered a pro for most dating games, but it is nice to not have to replay the game over and over again to see the different character development paths. *Time restrictions- there aren't any and I love this. If you agree to date go on a date with someone but decide to spend the evening doing the dunj- its okay. The date is still there for you without a negative consequence.*The cell phone- usually reading text messages in games gets old but the conversations keep being interesting, and who can turn down cute cat pictures*Combat- tying back to my first pro, there is a weapon you will enjoy using no matter you play style. Don't expect the challenge of Hades, but do expect to enjoy yourself.*The option to be friends- some reviewers have claimed you can't be friends, even when given the option but that is only with one character and it is plot related. Every other character has friend paths, and you have enough variety in responses to decide later on that you might want to be more that friends, or you want to call it off and do your own thing. It nice.*Collectables/ customizations- you can find, and craft so many things. From gifts for your love interests to outfits you wear out and about town/ in the dunjCons:*Music- Although the music is good, there are a very limited number of tracks and if you take you time trying to max out multiple love ranks you will be tired of hearing the music in no time*Game length- Its short. I didn't want this game to be over. The beginning felt rushed, and the end did too. I had hoped for more dungeons to open up, and I really wanted more options concerning where I went after my experiences of the game. *Challenge level- I didn't mind the challenge level of the game, but I did wish that a difficulty level had been an option at the beginning of the game. The devs were thoughtful enough to ask if it was okay to receive texts from Mom, but didn't give me the opportunity to challenge myself in combat. Overall: great game that is worth the money despite the short length of the game. The variety and thoughfulness that was included in the game was fantastic, and I really hope that DLC content or something similar adds something more to the game later. I would love a reason to come back to VB.

_childDocuments_.review: I backed this game the first day it launched on kickstarter, so I've been excited for this game for a long time. Mostly I was interested in the combination of the two genres - a dungeon crawl and a dating sim all nicely rolled into one. I enjoyed it! I would recommend it if you're looking for a fun casual dating sim with some RPG elements and light crafting.It's LGBT+ inclusive which is a big plus, you can chose your pronouns and style your character however you want, it even includes two nonbinary romance options, and you can romance anyone regardless of your pronouns.However this game didn't really live up to my hype. It kind of seems like the two genres this game is supposed to represent didn't quite live up to either of their potential. The RPG elements are especially simple, I didn't have to mind or take note of any of the weapon combos in order to win, I never had to swap out my weapon abilites for anything that might be better suited. Honestly the combat is easy once you get used to the enemies and how they move. The game only has a handful of enemies, the stronger enemies are just stronger versions of the old enemies. And there are only 2 dungeons in the whole game, I guess with maybe a dozen enemies each and with a few unique bosses.What initially attracted me to this game was the idea of a fully fleshed out dungeon crawler with the added bonus of the dating sim on the side, and the dungeons were just super underwhelming. As for the actual dating sim part, I enjoyed that quite a lot, because I liked most of the characters. It's also very surface level. Your dialogue options really don't mean much and the dates are going to go how they're going to go. There's no branching paths or stories with any of the romance options as far as I'm aware. I'm not even sure if it's possible to reach max level with them platonicaly because the only romance option I turned down continued to persue the player character romantically anyway. I just gave in and decided to romance everyone for the achievement after that.That doesn't mean it's not fun, most of the romance options are a lot of fun just to go through the story with and find out more about them, you just don't have to think too hard. My main complaint is Sawyer, I skipped most of their cutscenes and dialogue because they felt a walking stereotype. They act like a child. As a member of the LGBTQ+ community myself, I'm glad Rowan was added to offset that or I would have been really annoyed.The "main story" of the game is completed within a handful of cutscenes. I know it's more about the dungeons and the romance options, but when both of them were kind of underwhelming it was a super bummer that the main story was so short! I felt like I had only just started the game when all of the characters started texting me that I'd be going home soon since the summer was coming to an end! I hadn't even maxed out a single character before I hit the final mission. Overall I just didn't feel like every character got to be explored deeply enough, ESPECIALLY the character that the main story sort of revolves around.Overall, I had fun with the game, but I am disappointed. I know more content is coming in the future, and maybe that will iron out these issues, but I kind of would have just preferred they waited to release if that's the case. I guess I expected too much, or something different, to what this turned out to be.

All of the characters feel real even when you're talking to a dagger, and I love the flexibility it gives you in how you develop each relationship. It's not about sleeping with everyone, you can grow closer just as friends, or even have a platonic romance, and you never feel like you're missing out on anything or like that sort of relationship is any less important.I'm not sure if "enjoyed" is the right word for it, but I appreciated the rougher aspects the game touched on as well. Unhealthy relationships and stalker behavior are covered in what feels like a realistic way. Well...besides the whole weapons and dungeon delving being literal, but they serve as good metaphors. On that though, I've seen in other reviews that you have to interact with the stalker, but you DO NOT need to ever go on a date with them to finish the game. You CAN ignore them and shut them down at every opportunity and never need to pursue them except to confront the problem. If it ever feels like you don't have other options, just spend some time with your other friends either dating or in a dungeon.-SPOILERS FROM HERE ON-I think my main complaint is that there were only two dungeons.  technically three, in that it seems to count the final boss fight as a dungeon. With how it was set up it really felt like there'd be more. Also, while I do love being able to guide relationships towards just friends, platonic romance, or sexual romance, I feel like that gets locked in very early. Like if early on I don't go full in on the romance or choose to start just friends, then it stays just friends with no way to change my mind later. So, be aware that if you get an option to say anything that says you'll be just friends, even if for just one event, that means you do not want to go further than that for the rest of the game.It can also feel a bit directionless at times on how to progress without interacting with Eric and it wasn't really clear that it was purely a progression event to "shop" at his store, and it's never really a shop. Also would have appreciated calling the cops on the guy or him having any retribution whatsoever for what he'd done, instead of just being forced to trust him at his word and let him walk away.Overall, though, it was a great experience. It really felt like I was saying goodbye to dear friends when the game came to a close.

_childDocuments_.review: I normally avoid throwing my hat into the ring when commenting about games as there is generally a large discourse around them already, but since I backed Boyfriend Dungeon, I'd like to place down my two cents.Currently the game does not have enough content to justify the price tag it comes attached with. I "finished" the game in around three and a half hours (there are only two "dunj"'s and a totally-not-slapping-you-in-the-face-obvious final boss fight), before doubling back to round out the rest of the romances and craft the remaining items I had missed. I think this game suffers from an identity crisis: it is effectively a combination of dungeon crawler and visual novel, but without doing either remotely . Gameplay in the dunj is, kindly put, bland. While each weapon does attack differently, at most you will be alternating LMB and RMB clicks (the game does list "combos" for each weapon, say LMB RMB RMB, but all this does is let you swap in to the RMB attack string from the LMB attack string. Only Sawyer and Rowan get different moves available to them by doing this, as their RMB attacks are standalone moves that do not chain unlike, well, every other weapon), dodge rolling, and occasionally shooting out whichever generic special move you've chosen from your collection of Zines--super powers in this game being determined by which 'zine' you have equipped and whose effects range from things such as breathing fire, summoning a decoy, or releasing a shock field. They're fine, but they're uninspired and don't contribute much to making the gameplay flow different or exciting.Alright, so maybe the dungeon crawling is a little tacked on, maybe the characters make up for it, right? Well, no. Boyfriend Dungeon uses the trope that Everyone Really Likes You that crops up in romanceable character games occasionally. Your sharp heart throbs do have some potentially interesting issues: Recently coming out as non-binary (...but the fact they can't cook seemed to be a larger plot point than that.), how do you find love and connection when you've lived for 200 years already (something many of us will obviously go through), coping with depression (by falling in love obviously and not seeing a therapist).On the flip side then you have things such as: rich attractive man disappoints his father by being philanthropic and "breaks away from him" but still seems to keep his expensive and cushy living arrangement...?But all of the potential interest, the good work in offering you platonic relationships as being equally important and healthy as romantic ones, pales in comparison to how little your input matters. All of the characters like you, and often times not for any explainable or obvious reason. They just happen to think you're neat, so neat that they're happy to pash you. I think the  with the setting of Boyfriend Dungeon remains largely untapped. What would it be like to actually wield another being? How would that impact your relationship with them; how would it grow that relationship? Is it comfortable or uncomfortable for the weapon-turner? Alongside this, text messaging system which is used to continue conversations with your bae blades outside of your heart dates/events is inane, slow, and does its best to reduce any connection your might be building. How are you supposed to be seriously invested someone when they send you four multiple paragraph messages in a row to which your response options are a single sentence, a single word, or a series of emojis? Despite being eerily reminiscent of what online dating can be like, it makes the situation even more unbelieveable that these characters are often entirely delighted and content with your measly responses, an experience which is repeated on your in person dates. How am I supposed to care about a person whose response to me, not matter which option I select, is approval, love, or wonder? What is heartbreaking about all of this though, is that Boyfriend Dungeon has style. To take a swipe at the low hanging fruit here: Boyfriend Dungeon is a good-looking bad date. It is well dressed, it sounds nice, it looks good, but when you talk to it you quickly realise that there's just... not much there. It is distressing when the only nice things you can say about a game are its art style, user interface, and music. It's like looking someone up and down before smiling and saying, "Your outfit is vibrant today."I'm not sad to have helped in some small way to bring Boyfriend Dungeon to be a game in the world; respectful and representative queer content is still sadly sparse, especially non-erotic content, but I am sad that the experience is so flat. I find it interesting how much Moon Hunters (one of their earlier titles) and Boyfriend Dungeon have in common. They are both rich in setting, visual storytelling, and appearance. But they're also sparse, and kind of empty. Outside of the dunj, and being texted by five people at the same time for a date, there's just not much to do in Boyfriend Dungeon, so there's little for you to fall in love with.

_childDocuments_.review: Boyfriend Dungeon is an absolutely delightful short dating sim in which every character feels like they have depth and their own quirks and secrets. There have been several times that the game surprised me, and others when I was simply delighted by what I expected. It has a silly premise, and it leans into that, making fun of itself and using the space that creates to have an absolute blast with the game that results. I'm not normally into dungeon crawlers or dating sims, but apparently when the two are combined, I'm smitten. The dungeon crawling has a bit of a Transistor vibe, for fans of that game, and everything in the game felt like it was designed with convenience in mind - the dungeons give you teleport points in the form of elevators, so that you don't have to start from the top every time you re-enter. The game was thoughtfully written, too, with bits of dialogue in one route being influenced by how far you are in a different route. Even the game's villain is well-written and well-conceived. Also - how could I forget? - the game mentions ethical polyamory, which is absolutely phenomenal, and allows you to choose friendship routes while still maxing out each weapon. I only wish it was longer, but truthfully, I think it's a pretty perfect length for what it is. Highly recommend checking it out, and supporting some lovely indie game devs.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR -- It's a lot of fun with bladed huns in the hot summer sun.Boyfriend Dungeon has been a much-anticipated title on my list, and after a bit of a scare with last year's Lucifer Within Us not being up to snuff (for me personally), I am very glad to say that BD is a fantastic game. The action-adventure dungeon crawling is smooth and fun, with a variety of different weapons that all have their own combo strings and mechanical niches. You've got a somewhat reliable stream of consumable healing items and combat-trick 'zines' for special techniques, and that all adds up to a great time.The actual dating sections are also good, smooth and pared-down compared to a lot of simulators or visual novels, but just the right weight for something in this style. _childDocuments_.review: How do I describe BFD? Well, mechnically, it's a hack and slash with very basic combos (either 3 or 4 string, depending on the "weight" of the weapon) and a pretty basic dungeon crawling aspect that becomes even more basic after the first dungeon. Every monster you beat, floor your clear, etc grants you XP at the end which contributes to your level, which not only gives you more HP, but improves your damage with each weapon.There's also the crafting element, where you use items you either find in the dungeon or purchase in or out of the dungeon to make recipes you also find in the dungeon. For what purpose? Getting to that. Point is it's really basic and you can only craft recipes once.Then there's the dating sim element! The characters are well written by all accounts, each with their own distinct personalities, traits, and flaws that, over the course of a playthrough or two, you'll either fall in love with or not. That said, it is limited to brief interactions in the dungeons, giving gifts, and 6 dates that, at least to my knowledge, result in a "Love Rank" increase regardless of what direction you take the relationship, but that's kind of necessary as these rank ups also add to what the your weapon partner can do down in the "Dunj".Over all, you might notice that I use words like "basic" and "simple" a lot. And that is gonna continue, because the game's setting feels a lot like if you simplified the dungeon delving and premise of the Persona games, and did something similar with the Soul Eater anime series for the characters and setting, but threw in a huge helping ton of realism, LGBTQ+ themes, and made a game that is dripping with charm, promise, and love, both in the narrative sense and in the meta sense.For those who haven't paid much attention, this game has been in development for *years*, struggling due to all manner of things, and I'm sure a lot of more advanced or ambitions elements had to be left out just to get the game out at all; two characters are going to come out as DLC specifically because there just wasn't enough time to include them in the game.And this is the part where I feel the need to point out the game's flaws. While the game stresses a Personaesque ticking clock of "you're only here for the Summer", and certain events and looming ends are brought up in conjunction with that theme, the truth is that you can freely ignore that time limit and max out all your relationships before you finish the second dungeon, or conversely not enough finish one before beating said second one.The game also requires a certain level of acceptance for themes, terms, and slangs that more than a few players might find "cringey" or "too SJW-y". And while I disagree with that notion, I can see people being turned off by the game referring to dungeons as Dunjs.Finally, I hate to say this; the games boss fights feel weak. I'm not sure what about them makes them feel that way to me, what design choices make them like that, but I can say this much: Do not make boss fights where the boss talks to you through text bars in a hack n slash action game. No player is going to have the time to read those. Either have them be voiced, or slow down combat somehow during the speeches.That all said, I've played through this entire game twice, with my first playthrough happening in basically the first evening I played it. It turned an awful day into one of the better days I'd had in awhile. I've written 80 pages of fanfiction about this game since the second completion.This game has inspired me like very, very few games or other media have, period. It's characters have my heart, and its world lives inside my head.If you're at all interested in dating sims, but not willing to dive into the deeper visual novels, or hack and slash dungeon crawlers but don't want that to be the *only* thing you're doing, then this game is a beautiful entry into either genre that'll leave you hungering for more.

_childDocuments_.review: Verona Beach – a chill place to spend the summer. Especially in a rent-free apartment previously occupied by your cousin. Kind of him to offer you the space, even if he’s one of the most obnoxious and interfering people you’ll ever meet. But hey, families – can’t pick ‘em.But you can pick lovers, and that’s part of the reason you’re here. See, you’ve never had a date. Not even once. Your cousin, under some duress from your mother, has been assigned your wingman, but it won’t be long before you’re able to make connections at your own pace.Connections that lead to a very interesting quirk: your ideal love interests are all capable of transforming themselves into wield-able weapons. Cue  core premise. Namely, dating the weapons you will take into dungeons – or ‘dunjis’ – to do battle with a host of monsters that reflect your deepest fears.It’s a neat, clever premise – the kind ideally suited to gaming’s specific narrative and  gameplay strengths, successfully mixing the dating sim with hack-and-slash (or "shack and slash") dungeon combat. Successful to a point, anyway.Throughout your summer in Verona, you’ll meet a host of potential love interests. Each character feels unique, carrying their own baggage, harbouring secrets, and needing you just as much as you need them.There's Valeria, a dagger, who also happens to be a talented artist in need of a new direction in life. Although initially resistant, your developing romance eventually allows her to open about her rather extraordinary talents. Then there’s Sawyer, a glaive, and to them you are a lodestone in their young life. They really did entrance me! There’s plenty more, too – seven, in total – and each feel fully alive, their personal dramas unique to their own lived experiences.Your time together is either spent on dates across Verona’s lovingly drawn romantic hotspots or in the dungeons.Dungeon combat is pretty basic, settling for fun, engaging encounters that are never too taxing. Each love interest transforms into a specific weapon – a glaive, a scythe, and so on – and as your relationships deepen, you’ll unlock more abilities, transforming you both into an increasingly powerful duo.There’s items to pick up along the way, most of which you can take home and craft into gifts (flowers, cupcakes, pizzas...). Like the combat itself there’s no real depth to the crafting process; all you need do is find the right materials and put them together at home. That’s not in any way a slight – just an observation on the game’s breezy and poppy tone. I wouldn’t have it any other way!I liked my dates. Their dialogue was thoughtful and considered, probing the complexities of modern love, sex, and desire. I’ve seem some reviewers lauding the ‘great writing’, but I can’t agree with that. They probe the complexities, sure, but the game never digs very deep. It’s  good, so let’s not get carried away, yeah?More importantly, this is an inclusive game with stellar representation. Proudly LGBTQ+, I was so heartened to see these characters represent our diverse and developing understanding of gender. It’s arguably the writing’s greatest strength.Yet, when it comes to the ‘game’ bit, I can’t help but feel  is lacking. I mentioned earlier that the game’s tone was poppy and breezy, and whilst that did work for me, I felt like  was in order in some crucial departments. There’s only two dungeons to complete, a singe villain to defeat, and, dates aside, that’s sort of it.As the dungeons are representations of the protagonist’s fears, it’s disappointing to see it handled in such a cursory manner. Sure, it's not meant to be a complex drama, but by the time the second dungeon concluded, I didn't feel like a complete statement on the game's many themes had been reached. There’s much more that could have been done to create a fulfilling arc worthy of the game's thematic interests. It’s fine that the combat and crafting are kept minimal, but I walked away from the game feeling like there wasn’t nearly enough done to properly capitalise on such a clever premise.Even if it did let you date a cat.But whatever misgivings I have about the game’s overall execution, I had a super fun time. The characters are likeable and compelling, the combat enjoyable and simplistic, and it’s loaded with positive vibes: a welcome relief in today’s angry world, drunk on hate and eager to lash out in fear of diversity, of difference.  emphatically embraces our differences, and for that reason alone, it’s worth giving it a try.And you can date a cat.

Seasoned dungeoneers might find this part of the game not that challenging but beginners or people bad at video games (me) will find it just fine.The dating sim aspect is where this game shines, seasoned veterans of this genre (me) with enjoy cool concepts such as friendship romancing, polyamory and being friends with an orange cat. The characters are very charming and all feel unique and different to wield. Though ofc, you may like a character more as a weapon than as a person you want to date. I'm sure theres a metaphor there somewhere.The story of this game is not very subtle but that doesn't mean it's bad. It's a cool story about gaining confidence and kissing swords.I am hopeful this game adds more content later, I would really like to play more of it.

_childDocuments_.review: Daggers, swords, laser weapons, brass knuckles or a scythe? Pick your poison and then romance them in . For myself, this is one of those games you start playing and look at the clock hours later and realise it is almost daylight. I do not get games that do that very often, have me so immersed. I love the soundtrack and the artwork. This is the first game I have bought and played from Kitfox Games and it is so much fun. A dating sim first and some light rouge-lite battle thrown in to level up your weapons (boyfriends and girlfriends), find crafting blueprints and materials. The humour is good too. Some naughty little jabs (heh...jabs) here and there but nothing crass or straight out sexual. Suggestions of intimacy but nothing graphic. Which is nice for a change. For a dating sim primarily it focuses on getting to romance potential suitors and gift them appropriate gifts for their individual tastes. Lots of cute hats, accessories and outfits to collect too.I hope they do a second game. This one was just so fun. I am a lover of blades in real life and the idea of dating your weapons is fun and certainly different! It was, for me, just a really fun time.  About 10 hours of playtime if you go for all the achievements and take your time dating each character/weapon. 🗡️❤️

_childDocuments_.review: I recently fell hardcore in love with roguelikes and the dungeon crawler genre. and saw this and said why not. _childDocuments_.review: I have some mixed feelings about this game.It's GREAT, honestly - cute guys, cool girls, fantastic nonbinary representation, AND a cat I would literally protect with my life. But without spoiling too much... the only character I felt inclined to pursue romantically (at least until Jonah's in the game) ended up dumping me right before the final boss? And I don't think there's a way around that character breaking up with you. So I went into the last act feeling kinda bitter and resentful, antithetical to the game's overall message of 'it's worth risking heartbreak to open yourself to love'. I know I was warned, but I didn't expect to be allowed to get so emotionally invested. It left me with a bad taste in my mouth, and the ending scene rang a bit hollow. Great game and I'm glad I played it, but I sort of wish I hadn't FINISHED it.

_childDocuments_.review: It's fun for a short night long play through, but lacks a lot of player agency and depth that I'd expect from this kind of game. If you're looking for a small self contained experience and nothing more, it's well worth the price tag, but the game itself left me feeling both sad and unfulfilled.For how beautiful the art is and how cool the concept may be I find it really depressing that nothing you say matters. You try to say no to someone? Ignored. I told several characters I'd prefer to be friends and yet the game FORCES you to continue going on romantic dates with them and flirting. The game lectures YOU the player about consent and then ignores your own consent later into the game. Maybe, you might think, you can just romance one person and ignore everyone else? Nope, you HAVE to romance everyone at least once for the story to continue. Your dialogue choices don't matter, your dating choices don't matter, nothing matters. It's an illusion of choice.And this goes for the ending too; this is going to dip into SPOILER territory so beware.  You have no impact on your relationships or the world around you, forced to follow the story directly. Either you ignore a character or you pursue them, there is no in between.This kind of spamming issue happens in the dungeons as well, the weapons all follow a basic combo of clicking that lacks a lot of variety. I didn't mind this as much myself but I know some people may find the basic nature of the combat and how easy it is boring after awhile. Doubly so since this game doesn't have difficulty changing options.To any looking to buy this game, I think it is very worth it if you're going to play it with friends, or if you want to appreciate the beautiful art/soundtrack this game has to offer. Otherwise, I would hold off to buy it when the game has more DLC or additional content to offer like more dungeons or female romance options (since there's only one as of right now.)
_childDocuments_.name: Boyfriend Dungeon

_childDocuments_.review: In a world of time-sinks, here is a game where you can experience almost everything in under 20 hours. Platonic and romantic options for every character relationship, among a cast of various genders and sexualities and species, with game play that is compelling without being overbearing and an excellent soundtrack. As someone who identifies as a heterosexual male, I found playing this thought-provoking as the game makes no assumptions about gender and sexuality for your character - only the choices you make can articulate those preferences. A wonderful, refreshing experience in a world of bloated, all-consuming sandboxes, this game respects your time and rewards you abundantly. I highly recommend it!*One warning - though I think there is now a CW in the game - not every relationship or person is healthy, and this game is authentic in that respect. If you have dealt with harassment or abuse in your life, consider whether you are in a place where you can deal with media concerning those themes.

_childDocuments_.review: This game takes a visual novel and a dungeon-delver and somehow blends the two together just right.  They never feel like they've overpowering each other.  The romance interests are mostly okay, and nicely written.  I like that you can tell the characters that you just want to be friends, but that doesn't necessarily lock you out of their content.  Platonic love is just as important and powerful as romantic love, and the devs seem to recognize that.  There's a cat you can befriend, that's also important.  The art and music are very nice.  My main complaint is that it feels like they tried to cram too much into too short of a time.  I'm three hours in and it feels like I'm at the endgame...but I still haven't found all the characters, let alone maxed them out.  Each character has six chapters to their story, some of which feels like a lot of filler (did Sawyer's cooking shenanigans really need to go on so long?).  They set up some of the more fantastic elements, but don't have time to really go into the lore of it all.  It just kinda...exists.  And I mentioned the friendship mechanics, but some characters feel like they were written specifically for romance and get passive aggressive when when they're delegated to friendship (Sunder, throwing a hissy fit in a romantic area because you were friendzoned isn't going to make me like you).  But at the end of the day, it's a very nice little romance game.  Even with the stuff I didn't like (which most of it boiled down to Sunder and Sawyer, so that's just a personal taste thing and not an over-arching problem with the game).  I do recommend it, especially if you're looking to add some romance to your gaming habits.Isaac best swordsbando, fight me.

_childDocuments_.review: I have enjoyed playing this quite a bit. I was a Kickstarter backer and have no regrets supporting this game. _childDocuments_.review: I want to start off by saying i ultimately really enjoyed my time with boyfriend dungeon and look forward to any new content they add in the future. the game's writing and art style are phenomenal and, for the most part, the characters all endeared themselves to me really quickly. the gameplay isn't difficult at all, to be honest, and I suspect it would be disappointing to a hardcore rogue-like fan. i rarely play those kinda games and i was able to almost 100% the game in around 10 hours. the controls aren't as tight as some of its peers, a little more slow and floaty than i like, but i still enjoyed it.the game's story does have some dark elements that could make someone feel uncomfortable, especially if you're sensitive to stalking. it warns you before you start and you should take that warning seriously. it also give you the option to turn off texts from your "mom", a feature that i want more games to include. otherwise, my biggest complaint is that there is only one female romance interest. i love the enby rep but it would have been nice to see one more lady round out the cast.

_childDocuments_.review: These characters talk a good game about consent and communication, but the game doesn't care at all. Isaac thinks we're Together Forever and I have no idea what I did to make him think that; he definitely didn't ask me. The scythe asked me if I wanted to try sex/romance/sex+romance at like heart level 3, and that was apparently a binding contract I never got a chance to back out of that wasn't "be an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥." Another character "broke up with" me and my only options are to be different flavours of sad+outraged, but I'd been looking for a way to tell this guy to chill and not been seeing any options that weren't "express disgust at his plotspoiler secret." Also, this character might have murdered or assaulted someone and I never get to care about this?!? But I got a lot of opportunities to tell the graffiti artist her ♥♥♥♥'s illegal, because I have Priorities, I guess. The dungeon crawl part isn't long enough to fit the story, even if you don't "date" all the weapons. The two dungeons are really simplistic, more like a dungeon-crawling minigame. The weapons get more interesting as you level them up, but by that time you're out of dungeon to fight, so I'm not sure what the point of having more powerful weapons is.Sawyer is so, so awkward. I don't mean "adorably awkward." I mean "it is deeply uncomfortable to play this storyline." This character is a literal child. They're an undergraduate and you teach them how to cook and they hero-worship you. It's gross. You shouldn't be this kid's romantic or sexual interest, and you shouldn't be their friend either. If you're young enough to be involved with this kid, most of the *other* characters should not be involved with *you*. If this is really supposed to represent a 20-something, well, big yikes. And *really* bad gender politics. AFAB trans people and nonbinary people get infantilized enough without being cast as "adults who are basically children."The concept here is wacky and fun enough that I'd still have been happy with a simple game, or a game that looked like it could have been more but was ultimately scaled back to get it done. This is both of those things, but along with being unsatisfying, it's gross about consent in nearly every way it could be.WARNING: the content warning at the beginning says something about how it "may" involve stalking. Your game WILL involve stalking. STALKING IS CENTRAL TO THE PLOT.

_childDocuments_.review: Started playing the game because a friend had recommended it to me and had absolutely fallen in love with it! Everyone's visuals and characterizations are so diverse and downright lovable; the game's entire vibe is a well-curated combination of calming (with its ambiance and soundtracks) yet thrilling (the dungeon crawling) and energizing (the incredibly cute character interactions) all at the same time; the theme songs are incredibly gorgeous and utilized at the most appropriate of times that it greatly affects gameplay so beautifully (I can never shut up about how certain songs pop up so perfectly at key-scenes with the romanceables that it made me fall for them and the game deliciously deeper and how I'm well into making them my nightly lullaby by this point); and, the diversity of activities the game offers are all top-notch! I also absolutely adore how the devs paced everything to be friendly towards dungeon-crawlers both old and new (the difficulty for the dungeons are gauged so expertly in-line with both the MC and the romanceables' in-game skill level so that it turns out neither too easy that it grows stale nor too hard that it gets discouraging).Overall a great way to end a strenuous irl day, an absolute feel good game that will make you crave a Verona Beach of your own time and again! (Now for a shirt saying, "I went to Verona Beach and a full armory and another ticket back is what I got."....)P.S: Also, already desperately wishing for another installment from the devs (人>U<) they did such fantastic work with this one that I just can't help but want to see more of it <3

_childDocuments_.review: So I've been waiting for this game to release for.... I don't remember how long, but as soon as I saw it out I snatched it up instantly. And played all of it in one 7.5 hour sitting. Here are my thoughts.KJBADFLJKBNADEFRJKUGHBANERIKUJYH I am in love.This game is gorgeous and the characters are great. The story is a little wacky but in the good way, I thoroughly enjoyed it and was incredibly upset when it ended. The play time feels just right, not too long and not too short, and the replayability is perfect anyway and I will be 100%ing this game. The characters are great- I won't say too much but I am beyond in love with Valeria.There are male, female and non-binary love interests and you can pick your own characters pronouns, name and appearance, along with the pronouns not affecting who you can fall in love with.I thoroughly enjoyed the gameplay, with each character having a different play style and new abilities unlocking when you reach higher love levels with them, and different combos of those abilities and combos of light and heavy attacks too. The difficulty was nice and didn't ramp up too quickly so it was a very enjoyable experience, the difficulty truly went up as you learnt.The soundtrack is phenomenal too which I feel was the main reason I became fully engaged in the game and everything.I do hope they add more in the future, more characters, more dunjs, etc. I'll happily pay for any dlc too.Also I only encountered 2 minor bugs in my time which is a brilliant feeling on a day 1 release compared to other games.Overall I finished this game in one sitting and I don't do that. _childDocuments_.review: I was really excited about this one, and while it looks slick, and everyone is beautiful, of course--even with limited time with it, it just feels pretty empty. The characters have no real 'hooks' to them, everyone is a slightly different flavor of smarm and/or already in love with you, and for all that there seems to be a sweet core to the interactions, it already veered into preachy from your very first interaction, maybe for fear of being labelled problematic (a common problem for LGBT+ VNs in my experience, as the call often comes from inside the house these days to rip LGBT stories to shreds for daring to have anything short of squeaky-clean Disney romances with perfectly upstanding model citizens as characters). With no risks, and pretty characters with no substance, it just feels like unprofessional writing with a nice package. Also the dungeon-crawling controls are extremely bad. They're too slow to respond, even for a mini-game, and as it is the 'main' mini-game, it seems like it should be more polished! The enemies are boring, the dodging is not reliable, and I had no fun at all. Gonna pass on the rest of this one. Sorry, guys. The idea is still so good, but the execution didn't hit for me from the get-go.
