_childDocuments_.review: kickstarter syndrome strikes againIF YOU LIKE: Supergiant (Pyre, Hades, Transistor, Bastion), Dream Daddy, Stardew Valley, Monster PromSEE ALSO: Hatoful Boyfriend, Going Under, Unpacking, Moonlighter, HuniepopPROS:- LGBT + PLATONIC RELATIONSHIPS: huge dub. breaks heterosexual AND monogamous frameworks, going so far to talk about polyamorous relationships and includes explicitly stated "we are good friends and are ok with romantic/sexual tension because we talked it out" scenes. heavily appreciate the nb and ace options/dialogue- TECHNICALLY POLISHED: little to no bugs, game runs great, loading times are quick, transitions between dungeon to overworld to visual novel is smooth and charming, controller supported and easy to switch to K+M or vice versa; game autosaves frequently and i never needed to worry about the game's performance for any reason- FUN AND CHARMING CAST: everyone is HOT and memorable, even if on screen for only a moment. there is great attention to keep characters consistent and the attention to detail in little decisions being remembered later is always a fun touch. while hinging on tropes, it's not a bad thing, and it was clearly thought-out and fleshed to be more than a surface level quirk.CONS:- TOO SIMPLE, GAME-WISE: it's sometimes hard to distinguish enemies from environment in the cell-shaded art style the game uses. there's no outlines between PC to enemy to environment, or other visual cues; i relied on the sound cues + dialogue more than looking at the actual environment to expect a fight. i have a gripe about variant enemy types only being distinguished by one/two (sometimes unnoticed) visual quirks. as a self-advertised "shack-and-slash" dungeon crawler, i would have liked seeing more completely new enemies rather than another slightly bigger recolored foes.- TOO CLEAN, STORY-WISE: interactions or entire arcs end up too clandestine or had realism hand-waved away. i sadly include the main story in this. story is subjective to people's taste, but multiple instances felt like talking to characters was a formula. meet, date, level up, some conflict happens: "haha see you in the dungeon, same time next week!" - some conflicts being solved in one or less conversation with little chance to be explored felt jarring and i had to coax myself into suspending my disbelief more often than not.- OTHER:- ACCESSIBLE: contains story content warnings, easy to understand combat mechanics + handicap considerations, relatively little to no penalty for "wrong" date choices, change your character's pronouns/appearance anytime- EASY FOR EXPERIENCED ROGUE-LIKE PLAYERS: dungeons are piss easy; baby's first isometric roguelike. every run felt like "go to dungeon, go through 12 premade levels, also we gave you 2x xp for whatever reason and now every enemy is a oneshot". weapon combos are not particularly spectacular or varied. you can travel to any checkpoint floor a la Stardew Valley dungeon-elevator. i was having no trouble walking past enemies if i didn't want to fight. this is a con for me as someone who plays a lot of technically demanding games, but shouldn't be considered an "always bad" trait as this allows for more people to play and choose to take it at their own pace.- INCONSISTENT: sometimes i can't tell if this game is meant to be funny and light-hearted... or serious and introspective. i honestly can't tell if the dungeons are randomly generated or not. some character portraits don't match with the rest of the game's artstyle. a whole metagame-y and completely bizarre character interaction is fully forgotten and forgiven in literally a sentence? sometimes an enemy telegraphs attacks, sometimes they just hit me as they fly into me? some characters i intended to have a platonic relationship with, instead were written almost entirely from a romantic perspective and made incredibly awkward scenes??? the cat said WHATNOTES:back in 2018, i backed the kickstarter for this game. the expected delivery date was uh... 2019. hm, steam page says the game was released in 2021... (not that it mattered, it took me until 2022 to actually boot it up lmao) but now that i've finally played it, i say "yeah, it's another kickstarter game!"it's rare for me to find a game to play that i won't close in an hour. i definitely didn't expect to finish the entire thing, especially in an impromptu stream call with friends ending with 12 hours of talking/laughing with the game, 9 being actual game hours - but it's hard to recommend this game when, in the end, i don't feel it's a "good" game. there wasn't anything that stood out to me, which is a shame considering that it's very clear that the devs put a lot of thought and love into this. it felt like a lot of concepts were presented with efforts spread too thin to in order for anything in particular to shine. i don't like any of the datable characters to be dedicated to them, which is a big flag for me in a dating sim. it's just a "fine" game; i jokingly give it a 6/10 if people had to ask, then steeple my fingers in a big grin and say "you wanna know why?"the stalkeri had no problem with them (thankfully w/ the CWs, was prepared to encounter) and had no intention of mentioning this element of the game, but seeing other reviews and talking about this created great discussion that i hope more people consider. i see players considered the stalker as distasteful, sometimes triggering, sometimes annoying (same for me) and wanted this to be completely cut out of the game or skippable. i disagree with this wholeheartedly (there's plenty of access ALREADY, considering *gestures at the first half of this review*) - aside from asking devs to completely rework their plot since uh, the stalker is the driving point and climax of the main story, feels unreasonable. and just. feels wrong. i don't want to play a game that always "plays safe" - i want to play a game to have fun, win, interact with characters in a thrilling way. there is no thrill without a little danger. the stalker ends up being real and valid motivation for the story to move forward. why the heck are people asking the devs to remove them? what else are the characters supposed to do? why the heck are people asking an indie game studio founded on diversity and exploration to... not be diverse and explore? this character was a highlight for me in the game as someone who (sadly) has had so many similar conversations and situations from that kind of person, and i sure wish my situation ended as happily and healthily as it did in-game. having that kind of closure, artificial and incredibly lofty as it is, is still nice. it's personal, and i feel more connected to the game even if by a tiny thread. i feel like the people who fight against "problematic" material lose sight of the main point; to repeat myself, removing that aspect of the game would have not made this game so heartfelt. i enjoyed the fights and annoyance that this character brought, and i fight for them to stay in the base game. i say all of this because if given the choice and the devs did remove them, i would have chosen to do so - and would have had a lesser gaming experience and impression of the game because of it.in the end i had fun! i see the love from kitfox and it's admittedly validating to see the LGBTA+/platonic rep in modern games. i ultimately want to support indie devs to make games, especially without having to worry about conforming to people's (corporation's AND fan's) will.

Became the manager of a k-pop group. 10/10 would date weapons again.----------------------------------------------------------------As someone who has never tried a dating game I decided to take a punt on Boyfriend Dungeon as it was on sale and thought it might be a bit of fun to give the genre a go. What I found was a really easy going intro to the genre for a newbie like me. The combat, rogue-lite, dungeon crawl part was major chill and shouldn’t be much of a challenge for most folks but if it is you can turn on easy mode. The soundtrack has some major bops (personal highlights included ‘Diamond’. ‘Twisted up with Me’, ‘Waves’, and ‘Without a Weapon’.). The dating part is easy going and you can take a full on romantic/thirst/lets bang approach or just go with a close friendship vibe with either option letting you make progress with each character. _childDocuments_.review: TL:DR: Good game, graphics and sound 10/10, ending kinda meh, funny weapon dating.I love this game. Always enjoyed dating sims but they can feel "idle" a lot of the times. Going into dungeons and fighting monsters inbetween is great. The sound design is great, though Isaac's parry sound always jumpscares me. The music is peak, the style is pretty and easy to look at, only getting overwhelmed with too many monsters on screen, but that is hardly avoidable gamedesign wise.Very inclusive and considerate. A lot of different characters, male, female, enby. Also covering some serious tones about self-care and self-growth. The characters don't feel flat, they have personality and often feel like real people, not just a cliche or steriotype of character. However wished your choices mattered more, but who plays a dating sim for the story anyways?Gameplay is great, feels fluid and every weapon has a different style, however that makes it difficult to progress with a character you like but hate how the gameplay aspect of the weapon is feeling. In my opinion every weapon has pros and cons, making this somewhat balanced, but if you really hate how the weapon is playing, chances are, you're not having fun in leveling their relationship. All of them are sweethearts.The ending is very underwhelming, feeling like the story is going too easy on the "antagonist". Disregarding my personal opinion of him, he comitted multiple criminal acts, many of them probably resulting in jailtime, yet he promises to do better and go to therapy? I understand the message of giving people a chance to better themselves and not to lose faith in someone for mistakes but he literally commited crimes. At least make him face those consequences too. Other than the ending, I quite enjoyed all the story around the characters and it feels like a world with lots going on, even if we "just" see into the characters lives. Also a little funny that they ALL know each other the instant you pick one of them up.Anyways great game.

_childDocuments_.review: The short version: There's nothing incredibly negative I felt towards this game so generally I'd recommend it, but more so if you like dating sims and less so if you like rogue-likes. Playing for almost 9 hours got me nearly all of the achievements. For me that makes the 20 dollar price tag fairly worth it, and any sale price even more worth it. The long version: Pros: There's a lot to love here. This game has a lot of fun queer representation and a very unique cast of characters. All of the weapons felt good to use in dungeons, and I didn't feel that any one weapon was more powerful than the others. Gameplay is pretty easy, maybe even accessible? Normally I don't learn combat very quickly in video games but after running the same dungeon floors twice or so it was pretty simple to get through. This may change player to player, but I was really appreciative of how the dungeon pacing matched the story pacing pretty well. It gets frustrating in games where you're left grinding for several hours to get kinda close to being prepared for a plot battle, and on the other side it's kinda disappointing when your combat is so far ahead of the plot that you two shot the big bad boss in the finale. The "final boss" here had good timing with how quickly I arrived to having a weapon close to love rank 6. There's only 6 dateable weapons, but I think it's safe to say that their personalities are varied enough that there's more likely than not a character you will be very attached to. The early game is a little rocky, because I felt that the combat was kinda clunky at first but once I got over that it was easy to put in the additional eight and a half hours. The cons: spoilers ahead. I will cover the plot related ones, but not the ones that deal with dateable weapons/the dates.A lot of the weapons definitely feel like shadows of characters rather than characters. I'm not sure if I'm just that far out from dating sims, if it was intentional since the story only takes place over a summer, or other constraints, but it made trying to get through some dates kinda painful.  I think the fun I've had with other dating sims was meeting a character, having a general feel for a character, then having some sort of wrench thrown in that mix, whether that be something very bizarre like being a secret candle reviewer online or having a double life, literally anything. The characters in this game definitely felt like the proverbial wrench was simply that they have fears and doubts about their life/career paths, which is realistic but really left me feeling like they didn't do much else. In the same vein, I kinda liked that all of the dates kinda flowed together into a cohesive mini-story, but I also kinda didn't like that. It goes hand-in-hand with what I said previously. I don't think it's a bad thing but I'll put it in this section anyway: the combat is kinda just button mashing most of the time. Sure you can do cool stuff, but usually if you mash Y instead of X. I think my ultimate disappointment is that I feel like the game could've done just a bit more. There's no penalty for just getting every weapon to rank 6, I guess I'm supposed to presume every character is polyamorous even though only one explicitly states it? You can even switch weapons between floors, so wouldn't it have been interesting to have the current weapon comment on the previous weapon you held in some way, not just jealously but admiration or even ambivalence? "Ah I see you wanted to use a *real* weapon this time" or anything like that?  Am I just supposed to believe that even though Verona Beach seems fairly small, that most of these characters have never interacted in any way? I was really left wishing that each weapon wasn't so...compartmentalized and boxed off from each other. Now...for Eric. More minor, but still worth mentioning: You're immediately dropped into the game and told that fighting through dungeons is how you can deal with your fears. Not only is it literally stated as plainly as that, it's not really explained further as to why dungeons manage to be both your personal therapy-through-fighting-cell-phone-monsters, and also a genuine hazard to the general public of Verona Beach. Also. They shorten dungeons as "the dunj." As texting slang, fine, but I'm pretty sure characters *say* dunj instead of dungeon. Maybe I'm old but that word is not hardly worth shortening...Even after all my complaining, I do still recommend this game, I think the 20 dollar price tag is fairly worth it and honestly, my complaints exist more because I liked the game enough, and not because I disliked it.

_childDocuments_.review: Boyfriend Dungeon is a unique twist on the dating simulator genre. You explore dungeons armed with your weapon of choice, but you also get to date your human-like weapon. While the game presentation and soundtracks are impeccable, the dungeon crawler aspect of the game can feel a bit repetitive. Overall, Boyfriend Dungeon is very engaging and fun to complete but way too short. With only three dungeons to explore, you can only wish that such a unique experience would have been longer. The dating sim aspect of the game is quite inclusive and well written which makes you even sadder that the experience lasts only 10 hours at best. Boyfriend dungeon is quite charming. It mixes different art-styles to create a cozy experience. It is quite similar to “Kitfox Games” previous entry: Moon Hunter. The main gameplay happens in a simplified and stylised 3D sprite work. Although simple, it still brings a certain charm and atmosphere to each dungeon, everything is clearly visible and still detailed enough to have its identity. The Datin Sim part of the game uses gorgeous illustrations for the characters and the backgrounds. Overall, the game gives a very warm and cozy vibe. Another very strong point of Boyfriend dungeon is its soundtrack. Most of the tracks have that “indie” vibes to them that really fit the “a summer abroad” setting. The simplicity of the tracks doesn’t take away their quality and they really fit perfectly with the art style. Moreover, of the 26 tracks, 14 have lyrics and singing on top of them. They are usually used during particular dialogues to reenforce a particular feeling. I personally think they are quite enjoyable. Those tracks are worth a listen:Boyfriend Dungeon is a unique mix of different genre. The first part is a dungeon crawler type of game where you dive into a dungeon with one of the different weapons at your disposition and the second part is a dating simulator where you date... the weapon you used in the dungeon. Don’t worry, those weapons can transform into human form so it’s... not as weird as it sounds. The dungeon part consists in exploring around 12 levels of a randomly generated dungeon, defeating enemies, collecting recipes and material for crafting and of course gaining love level with your weapon. This is however a bit repetitive and not really that challenging. By gaining levels you will quickly overpower everything in the dungeon, and you’ll just go through them without many thoughts. The same way, crafting is very barebone, each recipe can be used only once, and you’ll never have to really farm to get the materials needed. This part was still fun, but it lacked depth. With only three dungeons, you kind of miss some variety and challenges that a game centred on that aspect would have had. The second part of the game, the dating simulator is quite okay. You have a phone and periodically receive (A TON) messages from your lovers/friends and with each love level you gain in the dungeon you can further the relationship with a particular weapon. You can also offer gifts to strengthen your bond with them. Quite an important part of any dating sim. Here you can date 9 weapons and befriend a cat-weapon too. Kitfox tried to be as inclusive as possible while creating their characters. You can date any of the characters regarding of your gender. The roster is composed of four men, three women and two non-binary people with quite different personalities. If some of them seem a bit one-dimensional at first, they quickly show a bit more depth. However, I’d say that some of them can turn a bit annoying the more you date them. It’s very much a question of taste and what you like to talk about. I found some dialogues to be a snooze fest while others got me completely invested in them.  I also appreciate that a lot of the characters discuss important topics regarding dating such as consent, honesty, or even obsessive behaviours. Story is both predictable and trivial. You see it coming from the very beginning, but I don’t think that it was meant to be the centre of the game. It is a bit sad because the final boss is just as bland as the main plot. I would say however that I really like a story where the main character spends a summer abroad searching for themselves. You know you’re going to have to say goodbye at some point and every time someone mentioned it during the main game, I just didn’t want summer to end. You can 100% the game in one playthrough and in the span of 10 hours. I don’t really see what you could objectively do differently story wise except dating another weapon or friendzone some others. It is perfectly possible to date everyone in a single playthrough, so you won’t miss many things. I enjoyed the dungeon, but there’s nothing quite different about them once you collected everything to motivate you to go back to it.  The 45 achievements are quite easy to get. You receive them for collecting recipes, and basically dating the weapons. You can’t really miss any of them.

_childDocuments_.review: Having been waiting for this game ever since it was first announced years back, it did not disappoint. Though it's a short game at launch (almost 100% clear in about 7-8 hours), the characters are all interesting in their own way, there are a lot of branching paths, and there's plenty of room for replayability. The gameplay itself is sort of awkward on keyboard unless you remap the controls, and the glaive is not great without the mouse or a controller, which is unfortunate, but each weapon is equally good in most cases and although the second dungeon can be pretty hard, you're only really likely to actually die at the start of the game, after which there is a generous leveling system. There are some issues with the game that can be rectified - in town, some things have collision detection when they clearly do not need to, making things a little annoying. Also, I experienced a softlock on the final boss, which sucked, but it's only a day or two after launch so I can forgive that.Overall, short but sweet and I highly recommend it. Not just for the duck jokes or the 'use a whetstone on a lasersaber' or the cat.

_childDocuments_.review: is a rogue-lite/dating-sim. There are 3 dungeons, 5 bosses, several equipment pieces. The MC's name and appearance are customizable, level progression is completely automatic and linear (higher level = more HP and higher damage). Difficulty depends on the PC's level, because nothing scales and it is easy to out-level everything. There are no penalties for defeat in dungeons, XP and loot acquired are kept.The controls are responsive and rebindable, 5-button mice are supported. The game uses 1 auto-save. There are 9 weapons that are unlocked as the story progresses. It is impossible to alienate or antagonise them, they love the MC no matter what and always available to use after acquiring them.Dialogue choices are rather limited, but often reflected in following dialogues. The main story itself relies heavily on the MC's passivity and lack of attention, while the main antagonist is extremely obvious and ridiculously incompetent. There is no in-game journal or log. In general, clearing 1 floor of a dungeon is enough to trigger next event. I have not encountered any significant bugs.Recommended on sale, because the game technically achieves what it states on the store page - there are weapons who are possible to date, randomly-generated dungeons offer action-based combat, despite both aspects being shallow.

_childDocuments_.review: It made me smile, it made me laugh, and, when it was over, it made me cry.Action Roguelikes are not the sort of game I typically play, but hearing my friends gush about the game and learning about its character customization (Unlike 99% of games on the market today with character creators, the game allows non binary people to actually play as themselves and have both the game and its characters refer to them with gender neutral pronouns) I decided I had to give it a try. The combat is fun, the dialogue well written and voiced, graphics charming, music's a bop, and the boys... They're good boys, Brent. Except the ones who aren't boys, but they're also good and I love them.I recommend it, even if you're not into guys, in which case you have the option to simply play this game as "Friends with Boys Dungeon" and hang out with them instead.And yes, you can pet the cat.
_childDocuments_.name: Boyfriend Dungeon

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game; though a little on the short side, so maybe wait for the upcoming DLC to come out.Turns out Dating sims and roguelikes go pretty well together! The variety of cute characters to date and a decently fleshed out dungeoneering really help breaking up the monotony and faffing about of each genre. The dating aspects are quite engaging and  give you some goals to work towards where roguelikes can feel a bit aimless at times, and the dungeoneering add some game and actual test of skill beyond picking dialogue options. The way your dating progress is tied to the leveling the weapons in the dungeon also helps you feel like you're constantly making progress.For the Dating Sim there's plenty variety of characters to romance, each with pretty interesting storylines. The roguelike portion of this game is pretty reminiscent of Hades (in a good way), though perhaps a little light on  replay-ability. Not a real issue, considering the Dating/Story aspect is the focus of the game, just don't expect to sink hundreds of hours into it.:This free update is maybe not monumental in extra playtime, but does add a nice chunk of extra content in the shape of a new area, a new bossfight and three new characters (as well as some new collectibles). For old players this gives a nice opportunity to return to this game and for new this should simply weave into the main game seamlessly.The new area definitely provides a bit more of a challenge, and the boss fight has a nice scoring mechanic that provides a nice opportunity to get A+ with all weapons (easier with some than with others).I don't know if any new content will still be added, but all in all I definitely enjoyed this game and the update. Well worth a try!

_childDocuments_.review: I was one of the Kickstarter backers, and they did us really dirty. There's are two weapons that were fully funded (A Hammerbabe and Axebro) and should of been in the game at release. One of which is the Surfer Axe guy who clearly was coded to be in the game, has UI and sprites, but the character just abruptly leaves instead of staying in the game. So they took peoples money saying you could use Jonah, but just gave him a little cameo instead. They took our money, went dark for some time, and then cut content before release.The writing in this game is pretty bad, characters are as deep as puddles. Everything is about your feelings and magic and other crap. You can sum up the essence of every character with one sentence. The main character is a total loser that can't talk to an attractive person without freaking out, their cousin is obsessed with wing-manning us, Isaac has daddy issues and does not want to run his Conservative dads company, Sunder is a lazy ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ vampire, Valeria is your standard street kid artist from the barrios, Seven is whiny famous person that does not like being famous, the only regular smith in town is a human supremecist, etc. The problem is that every datable character is either a horrible person or a walking stereotype. As mentioned, there is a smithy character who exists to act racist towards weapon people so that you might be tricked into liking them more. This game can be summed up as "Trying to be Hades and failing" in that it really wants to be Hades but will never get there. BFD want's to do the same thing, where sexy characters explore a randomized dungeon to grow deeper relationships. The problem is that the modern setting of Verona Beach legit makes no sense, there are places in town that turn your worst fear into monsters that can kill you, this is a major plot point. WHERE IS THE NATIONAL GUARD, WHERE ARE THE COPS!? The game never addresses what weapon-people are, why they can do it, and why/where Verona Beach is like it is. The aformentioned monster place is... THE MALL AND NIGHTCLUB? So you are telling me that all of the social hotspots in this city feed on your dark emotions and breed monsters? No seriously where are the freaking cops. The other thing is that there's no real call to action, you just randomly start finding weapons down in the Dunj, who then hit you up for dates the second they leave the screen. Also, I refuse to interact with any person that calls it "The Dunj" like fighting monsters in bloody combat is some kind of quirky sexy modern activity. Now let's talk about the REAL reason I am not suggesting this game: It's too easy. Every dungeon run gives you XP depending on how many floors and monsters you fought. Even though the game offers you elevators to start deeper down THIS IS A TRAP. Because the game puts so much weight behind XP and leveling up, it behooves you to just start from the bottom every time to rack up fat XP with almost zero danger behind it. This also allows you to power through the XP you require to level up your weapons... I mean living people who we are dating.... and thus be able to do a dungeon run, do everybodies events, then power back down there. There is an your face gameyness here that drains any fun or romance out of it. In general this was an indie attempt to copy off another indie's homework, and it failed.

_childDocuments_.review: A nice short game if you want to chill for an evening or two. The dungeon crawling part can be a bit challenging at low levels, especially if you're using a weapon that doesn't suit your playstyle, but once you level up enough it's not too bad. The only dungeon I really hated was the third one because it had a really annoying gimmick, but even then the game is short enough that I managed to complete it without hitting the rage-quit point. The dating sim part, on the other hand, can be a bit hit or miss. On the plus side, there's a good variety of people/weapons to meet, all with their own quirks and interests. You probably won't like ALL of them (I honestly kind of low-key hated the scythe), but odds are at least one will catch your interest even if you just want to stick to being bros instead of boinking every person you meet. All in all, a nice, comfy game that lets you pretend to have friends that actually care about you - at least for a day or two.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh gosh oh gosh oh gosh where do I begin.So I am fresh off my first playthough, and I hope this is coherent. I love this game. Unabashedly. The characters are lovable and their character arcs are accessible, AND I got to smooch all the smoochable ones. The dungeon hack and slash was fun (and with 7 weapons to rotated through, I didn't get bored), I got to dress up my character. Pretty much everything I wanted from this game. AND TWO NONBINARY KISSMATE OPTIONS.That said, there are a few critiques I have, mainly about the storylines/dating parts [so possible spoilers ahead]! A handful of times, I would select a line and it felt like I was being responded to as if I'd chosen a different answer. And it didn't feel like there was a difference between the romance and friendship paths (ie, someone I had gotten full ranks with and invited to come home with me kept calling me "mon ami"). Just little things like that that made it feel like it didn't matter what I chose, which bugged me. I can only hope that it's not the other way around too. And just like there didn't seem to be a difference between friendship and romance, there didn't seem to be a difference between monogamy and polyamory. I chose full polyamory and I would have liked there to be a discussion with the characters about it; one of the characters makes it seem like they'd prefer to be monogamous, but it's never brought up again and they don't get bring up you dating other people. To me, polyamory is very much about open communication. Everyone needs to be on the same page, and the fact that it wasn't discussed at all did bother me. I wanted to make sure everyone was okay with it, and I wanted to see the other characters interact more!The character plotlines also weren't as... ironed out as they could have been. I don't know if I was pressing the buttons too fast and just not absorbing everything, but there were times when a character would say something about their lives, and I'd be surprised, because it felt like it'd been going on for a while and that was the first they'd mentioned of it. It felt like rather than an arc, I was getting little blips. My last critique is of the plotline behind the smooching. I know some people are bothered by Eric and his arc, and that's valid (I for one wish I could have been harsher to him), so if I'm in the minority that's fine, but I actually wanted more. Possibly more dungeons, more delving into what drove him. I wanted a real villain out of him, and I didn't get that. I understand why we don't dwell on it, this is a game of smooching sword babes, not delving into some weirdo's obsession, but the fact that we only got a taste made me want more. Anyway, for all the things that bugged me, and the interesting things that didn't pan out, I still enjoyed it for what it was. 7.5/10 for this game, I am still very satisfied with having backed it. Can't wait for the DLC! <3

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game on a whim and then forgot about for months, then decided on a whim to open it. AND IT COULDN'T PUT IT DOWN. I finished it in about 7.5 hrs, then went back in a 2nd playthrough to see how choices impacted play. One of the first things I noticed is that this game has some pretty incredible music that absolutely HITS at all the right times, I seriously recommend checking out the soundtrack. Past that, it does a very good job of... being exactly itself. The concept is incredibly cool, and if you don't take it TOO seriously, you'll have a lot of fun! This may be one of the few games I've played that featured romance-able characters where I actually nearly wanted to date everyone -- that never happens to me! Each character was unique, engaging and interesting. My main gripe is that I wish there was more content. Feels odd to be called Dungeon Boyfriend with only two dungeons. It almost feels like there's supposed to be more and almost feels absurd for there to be 42 dungeoneer ranks which is far more than enough firepower, and more slots on the shelf for trophies. I've heard there's some DLC to come in the future which is not a perfect solution to rectify this, but I'll leave my judgement until later. _childDocuments_.review: Boyfriend Dungeon is a game I picked up because I thought it looked cool. A dating simulator where the people you date turn into weapons and then you build relationships by taking them into the dungeon? That sounds pretty neat!! Except the execution left much to be desired. In the initial version of the game, there were two dungeons. That's it. Two whole dungeons in a game about dungeon crawling. The combat in the dungeons can feel shallow, with your moveset changing between your various partners. Speaking of whom, though the game is called Boyfriend Dungeon, you'll be met with a cast of men, women, non-binaries, and a cat, all of which you can swing at monsters with. The strength and abilities of each weapon are dependant on your relationship progress with each character, meaning the new weapons you pick up later will be weaker and harder to use against the current dungeon, forcing you to find a way to cope with it or to move back to an earlier section of the game. As for the bosses of each dungeon, they range from "incredibly boring and straightforward" to "how the hell am I supposed to even approach this". That mostly covers the Dungeon part, so moving onto the Boyfriend part; The game will not shame you for polyamory, though you do have the choice to keep a relationship platonic when interacting with the cast, which I appreciate. At a certain point, they released a free DLC that added three more weapons (only two of which you could wield), and a whole one more dungeon. For a total of three dungeons. In a DUNGEON CRAWLER. Yes I am still bitter about this. No matter which sword you choose to smooch, you will be harassed by a blacksmith that your cousin tries to set you up with. He is, undoubtedly, the worst part of this game. Using the game's texting system, he pesters you constantly, even after you tell him to go away. I wish you could just ignore him, but you are forced to answer to every one of his messages in order to move the game's plot forward, and watch as he stalks you on dates and harasses your partners. Then, during the final boss fight (spoilers, by the way) you are forced to tell him that he isn't a horrible person and that he's trying to become better in order to weaken the final boss.Overall, it feels like a waste of an interesting premise.

_childDocuments_.review: Since they've updated it a ton, even though it's still got the same issues I see it's not abandoned so lets give it a likeMy review used to be positive but I have changed it to negative after a replay and my initial giggle passed. (Will put updated at the end)I loved the game!There is space to improve but here's the good and bad sides for me personally.PROS: - A lot of puns, so the dialogue is fun- Fun combat system which is easy yet satisfying- You can romance more than once so you don't techically need to do multiple runs just to see what each character has to offer. However it makes me feel slightly guilty, despite the characters being okay with poly I IRL am not comfortable with it.- Wacky conversation option which are funny- Overall cool characters with lots of diversity- Good musicCONS:- Doesn't offer many chances to reject/friendzone characters. I wanted to go for a single person near the end but no longer could turn down other romance options- Only two dungeons, would be good if more were added with an update- Each dungeon only has one (or maybe 2) soundtracks, so it becomes slightly repetitive after a while, could do with more music optionsOverall Score: 5/7 :DSo, after sitting on it a bit and replaying the game...I've come to realise how the game is actually very railroaded. Your options, although often funny, always lead to the same outcome. Even if you attempt to friendzone them, they'll still love you. For no good reason. The PC can do nothing and still be loved. Nothing much changed with the ending, everyone still showed up and partied like we were friends. What really also bothered me was the inconsistency. For example the  and that even when you reject them, or friendzone them, they still act as if you're lovers and basically it is like they do not take no for an answer.For my second playthrough I wanted to do an experiment to see if anything would change if There were so many missed opportunties to make this game a replayable dating sim jewel. However the game ultimately falls short after you try to play it more than once. There's nothing more to do.There's only two dungeons which I have managed on my second playthrough to go through them whole in a single try, without extra levels or weapon upgrades. From what I could see, there were supposed to be even more romantic interests but they probably cut the game short just to release it, so hammer and axe got....axed.All in all, I had some mindless fun, just...disappointed now when I look at it again and see what it could've been.I hope the game recieves a content update with more 'dunjs', fixed writing that respects 'no' as a no, friends being just that, and actually makes your choices feel more relevant overall. When that day comes, I'll happily change my review back to positive and replay it all again.

_childDocuments_.review: After making your character, you arrive at Verona Beach so you can spend your summer there, with the help of your cousin Jesse letting you stay at his old apartment as the lease isn’t up until summer ends. However, this isn’t a summer that you can lay back and chill inside or soaking up the rays. Your mother has decided that this would be the perfect time to solve your problem of not dating anyone, not going on any dates, and your confidence problem (which is all true for me irl). Jesse has the solution for both of them: set up dates for you and have you go into dungeons that often appear at Verona Beach. While Jesse’s meddling resulted in some horrible dates, one of which proceeds to be a jerk stalker that doesn’t get the hint that you want nothing to do with him, the dungeon part actually works out. For both of the things Jesse is trying to help out with. You learn that there are some people (and animals) that can turn into weapons and you are sadly not one of them. But you can wield them. You meet Isaac first, an Estoc, that is happy to show you the ropes. While this is a great way to get some exercise in and make some money, Isaac also explains that these dungeons manifest based on your fears and insecurities, and the monsters there change their shape based on it too. It also seems like there isn’t a set amount of floors as it also depends on how deep your own fears or insecurities run (though both dungeons are both 12 floors). It doesn’t take long for you to meet another weapon, though it’s not in the best circumstances as he mentions that someone abducted him, chipped his blade, and left him in the dungeon. And you’ll meet the other weapons in the same predicament. Good thing that all they need is to have a day outside of the dungeon to rest to heal the damage and that they’re pretty open to letting you wield them and date them.In terms of the characters and the dating aspect, they’re both fine. The characters are the types where you’d like some of them, rather than liking all or most of them, but they are well written from what we got. I did enjoy the vast majority of the interactions and getting to know them. Past the initial meeting and the dialog you’ll get in dungeons (and the two parties where one weapon will come with you), they don’t interact with each other and you’ll really only interact with them when you rank up their Love Rank which they’ll text you and you can find where they are on the map (which your character can run on to get where they are) to get to their date (or it’s automatic once you reply if it’s happening at your apartment). However, they only have 6 ranks each, which can result in some of them feeling rushed, and you’re more or less pushed into accepting them as your romantic partner each time even if you want to keep them as a friend. This may be due to the game letting you be poly and date all of them at the same time, which none of them really care if you do and don’t tell them, but it is a weird choice considering the game says that it’s fine if you want just a platonic relationship with them.Anyways, onto the dungeon crawling part. There are (sadly) only 2 dungeons here, representing the fear of change and the fear of intimacy, that you can unlock and go to. And when you dive into it, it’s pretty easy to get the hang of it. You’ll choose who you’ll be wielding before going in and all the weapons are handled differently. They excel in different aspects based on their weapon type and have differences in their combos. They all are best or not so great in certain situations, like Isaac isn’t that great when surrounded by a lot of enemies (which happens a lot in the second dungeon), but they all handle pretty well. This is also a first for me where I was fine using any of the weapons and not dreading using one. Granted, I’m more of a person that like weapons (/characters) that are focused on attack fast and not the slow, but powerful, ones. You’ll also be able to dodge, which is best to get the hang of, and you’ll have several drinks (which depends on what you pick as a preference) that will heal you as well as zines that act as another way to hurt enemies or delay them. There are also certain hats that will give you an effect bonus like stunning enemies or having drinks heal more. Though, it does become easy enough to where you can just wear whatever you like best.Once you complete a floor, the weapon you were using gets some EXP for their Love Rank and you can switch it out for someone else before you get to the next floor. As extra EXP doesn’t overflow to the next, it is best to switch them out so that EXP don’t go to waste. You can also gift them something, each they all have gifts they hate, like, or love, to help them rank up, but there are only certain situations that the game will let you. Although, it has to be said that once you max one weapon, you are given an item that gives you double EXP and EXP overflow for the rest (which either was planned or is because it feels like one more dungeon was supposed to be included). When a weapon ranks up, this unlocks a date for the next day and a skill that will help you in battle. So the more you rank them up, the more helpful they are. Like Isaac will get the ability to riposte and charged attacks, Sunder will be able to inflict bleed, and Valeria can inflict Confusion. Some ranks will also have two different variations on the ability that you can choose to reflect how you wield them.You level up as well, but it’s only when you’re exiting the dungeon. This gives you more health to work with and, I believe, lets you hit harder so if you find yourself not doing a lot of damage when you encounter the tougher variants, you might want to exit so you can level up. Certain floors will have an elevator so you can exit early and let you start the dungeon at that floor (though you might not want to use this to skip floors so you can rank up the weapons and get money early on).There are various shops around, both on Verona Beach’s map and a secret shop in dungeons, that will sell different outfits for you to wear, crafting resources, and gifts. The crafting resources will let you make the various recipes you acquire. The best outfits and hats you’ll get will be from these recipes, you can only craft the different zines, and a lot of the gifts are from recipes (and aren’t as expensive).However, this game is missing some content and has the underlying feeling that it could have benefited more by having more time. 2 weapons are not implemented, Leah the hammer and Owen the axe (though Owen does appear briefly), and have already been mentioned that they will be added as DLC along with some additional stuff (though as far as I know, it’s not clear whether it’ll be free or paid for those that aren’t Kickstarter backers). It would be interesting to see how they would be implemented though. Would it be weaved into the main story where it supposed to have been or would it be in a post-game where you’d be visiting for a week or two (or full on moving there)?While I looked forward to Boyfriend Dungeon for a long time, I did enjoy my time with it, and I had fun playing it to where I barely convinced myself to complete it in 2 sittings, the more I thought about the game to write the review, the more I just found disappointing and wanting more of. There’s a lack of dungeons and there’s a lack on the dating sim aspect, so unless you’re someone that didn’t have big expectations and fine with this being more simple than it lets on, it’s going to feel a bit disappointing. I still recommend it, as it still is a fun game to play, but some might want to wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Boyfriend Dungeon offers a unique concept, mixing two improbable genres together in a very silly story about weapons turning into hot people. It sounds like a concept of a game you joke about with friends but never get to actually making. Well I'm happy the developers took the plunge and made that unlikely game.I found the core loop really engaging, and would find myself telling myself after every dungeon run "ok let's just have some date", and after every series of dates "ok let's go for one more dungeon run". The alternation between both kept the game from becoming repetitive.I'm happy with the care the developers took to make the experience both accessible and inclusive. They give content warnings, give you an option to opt-out of interacting with a secondary character called Mom, allow you to choose your pronouns, include non-binary characters (plural! a rarity!), and so on and so forth. I felt amazed by all this, and I really wish more games were like that.The soundtrack is catchy, and I kept listening to it after I've completed the game. I love playing a game with original tracks that have vocals; it's not common and it gives it a certain charm.I didn't feel like all the romance options were as interesting and likeable. For example, Valeria and Sunder are quite flirty with you, have some depth, include you in their hobbies and have some twists in their story. On the other hand, you get characters like Sawyer, who doesn't really have much to offer as a lover, and whose story evolve mostly around you helping them out to learn how to cook because their skills are very lacking. You don't need to go on all dates with every weapon, and even if you do you can do so platonically, but still in a dating sim I would have preferred if all dateable characters were romantically interesting.The fighting is not the most exciting, but it serves its purpose and it's decent enough for a game with more than one focus. I think it's a good thing that it isn't too complex or too hard, because otherwise a lot of people who came in for the dating would be stuck because of the fighting.Overall, great experience, do recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a delightful and lighthearted game! I wouldn't recommend it to someone looking for a hearty rouge-like or dungeon crawler, nor someone interested in an in-depth dating visual novel, but anyone who enjoys both those types of games and is looking for something to sink a weekend or so into would have a great time with this game.Combat: The combat is simple and easy to pick up, but I recommend trying it with a controller, as I found that much more intuitive than keyboard and mouse. It's not very robust and there's not a great deal of strategy to it, but the combinations of weapons, zines, and headwear could shake things up and it was fun trying out new things. Again, if you're looking for a game where the combat is the main focus, I would look elsewhere. It never hit a point where I was sick of it, but it can get repetitive, especially when getting everyone to max love level and finding all the blueprints (but that's not required to beat the game, so I did that willingly).Story: Avoiding spoilers, I thought the story was good. The main plot was basic, but it's clear the main draw of the game is the dates with the other characters, which shine. I appreciated the options for platonic or romantic relationships and how the game doesn't make you pick a single character and ignore the rest. Getting to max love with all the characters was great; their stories and lives were made with care and the writing is excellent. It's the kind of game where everyone who can be romanced is attracted to you and (mostly) never oversteps boundaries, so not the most realistic in that department, but this is also a game where people turn into weapons and the mall has monsters in it, so realism isn't really a big concern here. The more serious elements that they do touch on are largely handled appropriately, but I've seen some comments about the shifts in tone being a little strange, which I can agree with. But considering the nature of the game and how you can jump around between characters and quests at your leisure, I can see how that's hard to avoid.Value: I picked up the game shortly after the big secret weapons update, so I can't speak to what the game was like before then, but with it I thought the game has a good amount of content for the price. Not much by way of replay value, outside of going down different paths of friendship or romance with people, but the game leaves things open-ended enough that you never lock yourself into someone's route, which I appreciate as someone who doesn't have the time to put into replaying a game over and over. All in all, a lovely game! I hope to see more of it in the future!!

_childDocuments_.review: Boyfriend Dungeon is a story about you and several weapon-people who you get to know over the course of a summer. It's filled with funny, ridiculous and stupid moments. Some characters are great while others need as much therapy as feasibly possible or jail time. But let's not dwell on that as I go into more details!There's a lot I could say about the art style, mainly that it's distinctive and gorgeous. A lot of the backgrounds make you truly feel like you're there. The attention to detail is incredible!The animations are stunning for when a weapon transforms back into a person (or cat) and vice versa. It takes me back to watching anime with magical girls except less sexualised.I also love the design of the characters (even the ones who I felt awkward with). The highlight was definitely  because it showed one of the weapon-people in another getup that is very them.Speaking of which, let's talk about them! I'll try to keep my descriptions short and to the point as there are quite a few characters to get through.Isaac – Overall nice and polite despite having family issues. Valeria – Cool with an intriguing past.Sunder – Too much in every way.Seven – Distant but not rude. I'd say more like cautious and kind of cute.Sawyer – Filled with energy all the while being clumsy as they try their best.Pocket – Wary of strangers (as most cats tend to be) but also a sweetheart once you get to know him.Jonah – Sweet and respectful.Leah – Overall lovely.Dr. Holmes – Weird and reminds me of Director Qi from My Time at Sandrock in the way they speak. However, I much prefer Qi as he's adorably awkward whereas Holmes is just odd.Then there's also your cousin Jesse, his fiancée Samantha and the blacksmith Eric. Jesse is cool and Samantha is sweet. Eric on the other hand… I despise him. For obvious reasons. There's also another person named Olivia who is a worker but she doesn't play a huge role. She's the most side character to ever side character. There's also another weapon-person who I didn't get to know well and since I don't like their weapon style, the chances of me learning more about them is very low.It's smooth and quick but also challenging. Now, I'm not too well-versed in dungeon crawlers or roughlike games but I've played Pokémon Mystery Dungeon, Skul: The Hero Slayer, and Hades.I'd say this game is pretty up there in terms of enjoyment. I had fun trying out the different weapons and abilities unique to each character. Some may not like the repetitiveness in enemies but I don't mind it. For me, it makes it easier to learn their pattern (which is a saving grace when you're highly under levelled).I adore the music in this! It's a mixture of bouncy and chill. It evokes the adventure you feel when slaying monsters in the dungeons but also reminds you to take it easy every once in a while.In most soundtracks, I find one or two songs which to me are mediocre. Not in this though! I can confidently say I liked them all and will listen to the music for the next few weeks or months.The story in this is very simple: You're on summer vacation in Verona Beach where you meet up with your cousin and then date a lot of people. There's not much else to it apart from getting to know said characters. That's the meat of all this.If they weren't present (and the choice to date them), the entire thing would fall apart. It would be just another dungeon crawler. But it's not. It's a dungeon crawler with some interesting twists and turns.I have seen some pretty bad literature in video games. Sometimes I truly wonder if people even bother to have anyone edit or proofread anything before they publish. Other times, it's quite nice. I can tell a lot of work and love went into the making of the game.This one strangely fits right in the middle. Overall, the literature is enjoyable – it's funny, punchy and doesn't overwhelm you with descriptions. It gives you more than enough to make an image in your head.However, there were times where the text looked gross, namely from the overuse of two dots instead of three. Or just overusing in general. I also found a few sentences which made no sense whatsoever or when it should have switched to description but the dialogue box of the character persisted. That's probably more a design nitpick but I'm still including it!In its entirety, I'd give it a 6/10.Boyfriend Dungeon provides a wacky adventure filled with lots of dating and some internal struggles.

_childDocuments_.review: I would say I am about middle ground with this game, but I'd overall give it a recommendation for more reasons that I'd say I'd recommend against it. Here are my general opinions of the gamePros:-Really great LGBTQ+ representation in the game. Pronouns are a part of the game and can be changed at any time for your PC, and does not affect who you can date. Dialogue options make room for people of ace/aro/poly identities to be supported as well, and dateable characters are of differing gender presentations: some cis men, some cis women, some non-binary.-Great artistic style and great music soundtrack. Art is more unique for some games I've seen and music is generally pleasant and fun depending on where you are in the game. -Simplistic and easy-to-follow controls for combat, unique styles for each weapon used that give great versatility to each of the weapons you can wield.Cons:Storylines for each of the characters, and the game as a whole, lack depth and don't entirely make sense all of the time either.  There are separate romance and friendship tracks for each of the characters, which are mixed in throughout their storyline, but it's not always apparent which is which, and it doesn't always make logical sense why some characters would react the ways that they do to certain responses you can give. Sometimes, as other commenters have stated, it's a choice between the obvious positive and obvious negative choice, which gives the storylines too much of a railroading feel to them.-This is more of a middle ground depending on what you're looking for, but this game is *very* short. I'm typing this at about 8 hours of gameplay and I have completed the main story and maxed out all storylines for the characters. It's nice if you're looking for a shorter game, but you may have varied opinions about the pricing as a result. Best to get on sale I'd say.-Because of the game being so short, the main storyline does feel more superficial and streamlined. This definitely has a lot of railroading to it which can be offputting if you're looking for a good story game. This is more of a fun game to play if you want something that's easy to turn your brain off to and doesn't require too much thinking from you.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an absolutely fantastic game. I literally bought this like yesterday as soon as I got the email notification that it was available on steam and then did an 8 hr run straight through. While a game with some heavy themes, they are integrated really well, and the dating feels rather real too. Boyfriend Dungeon provides the autonomy that I really desire from games with dating mechanics. Here, you get to set your boundaries with the romance interests, so that if you want to just be friends, they understand that and respect that. Sure, they may question if one day you'd entertain the idea of being something more, but overall they respect your choice that maybe you don't want to bone every single weapon at the exact same time (although that's totally game as well). It's really nice that you can remain just friends with a weapon while still getting to know them, still seeing their stories, and not getting punished because "this secret is only revealed to romantic partners". Moving on to the combat-it's super fun. The different weapon styles match the various personalities and weapons you're fighting with, and it's a great mechanic to unlock more weapon skills as your relationship levels up with that particular weapon. The dungeons are fun to go through and your strength increases at a good rate so that you never feel like you really need to grind. Overall, seriously. An amazing game. The only real downside is the overarching theme of being stalked during the story (which is included as a warning prior to starting the game). _childDocuments_.review: GAMEPLAYBFD is a dating simulator with a unique twist that takes you on a summer journey of love, laughter, and self-discovery. Instead of dating humans, you'll find yourself swept off your feet by a cast of charming swords, each with their own distinct personalities, backstories, and emotional baggage. As you progress through the game, you'll embark on romantic dates, engage in witty banter, and uncover the hidden depths of each sword's soul. The game's branching dialogue system allows for multiple playthroughs, ensuring that each interaction feels fresh and meaningful.ART STYLE:BFD's art style brings the world of swords to life. Each sword is meticulously designed with intricate details and vibrant colors, showcasing their unique characteristics and personalities. From the elegant curves of the talwar to the rugged edges of the katana, every blade is a work of art. The backgrounds are equally stunning, immersing you in lush landscapes, cozy cafes, and visually pleasing dungeons. The game's overall aesthetic is a testament to the developers' passion and creativity, creating a truly immersive experience.CHARACTERS:The characters in BFD are the HEART of the game - pun intended. Each sword is fully fleshed out with a rich backstory, motivations, and desires. You'll meet the charismatic, shy, mischievous, and even downright sultry blades testing your resolve and your will to not "catch them all". As you get to know each sword, you'll discover their vulnerabilities, dreams, and personal struggles. The writing is refreshing, delivering witty dialogue, heartfelt confessions, and moments of genuine emotional depth. You'll find yourself genuinely caring about each sword's well-being, even the side characters push to warrant your attention in the midst of your decision-making.REPLAYABILITY:BFD has a mild replayability factor as it depends on how you progress through the story. I am a goal-oriented person so I tasked myself with reaching each goal and gaining every achievement before realizing I needed to complete the MAIN STORY. So if you want to choose one character, go through the story, and complete the game; you can! I proceeded to "catch them all" before returning to the MAIN focus... Slight spoiler as yes, you can, very well indeed, catch them all... I will leave that up to interpretation~ :3 TLDR - Worth the Buy?!:Yes! BUY IT!!! BFD is a heartfelt and unique dating simulator that stands out from the crowd. From the BOPPIN' music to the DELICIOUS characters and then the GORGEOUS art - It's a no brainer~ Whether you're basking in the warm glow of summer or seeking a romantic escape, BFD will transport you to a world where love knows no bounds and swords are the key to your destiny. Game has potential so I'll keep an eye on this one~

_childDocuments_.review: I struggled on whether I should put yes or no. I want to say that I was excited for the game. I followed the developers on tiktok and have been hyped for its release. But the best way I could describe this game is "almost enough." My time logged is the amount of time that it took me to 100% the game, all achievements, all character routes. -The art is beautiful, and while the moments of animation are short and far between, they really do add a lot to the game.-The characters are quite diverse, and the inclusion of nonbinary characters as someone who is nonbinary myself is quite refreshing. I appreciated that you could date anyone freely. I know LGBT friendly dating games are becoming more frequent, but I'm still happy for every inclusion there is.-You can be fully polyamorous with no consequence. Which means if you want to be like me and delay the end story point until you kiss all the characters, you can! Which is very very nice.-Your cousin Jesse. I love him. I love him so much.-The freedom you're given. Outside of tutorial segment, you're free to explore the dunj at your own pace. You could focus all your time on one weapon, or split it evenly amongst weapons. There's no real rush to finish the game, regardless of when in the summer the text messages say it is, so you can go at your leisure and really ensure that you see everything.-The length. There are only 2 dunj's in the entire game. Honestly I was expecting a lot more. My personal experience was having my birthday party, being told its the middle of summer, then immediately being told after one more dunj trip that my time was almost up.-Your choices don't matter. Now there is branching dialogue options a little bit, but 90% of options as far as I could tell lead to a few lines different of dialogue. Even if you choose an option a character really likes while on a date with them, it doesn't give any additional affection or change the ending at all. Which plays into my next point.-The surface level writing. There is a lot of diversity, yes, but the problem with the amount of characters is that if you were really only here for one, I feel like you'd be quite disappointed. Each story is very predictable, and it feels like you're going through a checklist of basic date ideas or story points with each character instead of delving deep into their psyches. Which for a game that has one of the main points being "overcoming your fears" really surprised me.-The simplicity of the gameplay. It was hard to tell if this was a real con or not, because I don't really mind easier games, but overall it was just a bit meh. It felt very barebones. I appreciated the different play styles with the different weapons, but this game felt like an emptier Hades, gameplay wise.-The way you unlock Rowan. This is more of a personal gripe. I believed I would encounter them like every other weapon through the dunjs, only to discover that I was supposed to run North past my vision at the beginning of the game. A lot of my playtime was just grinding their affection to catch up. A dialogue queue mentioning the mansion to the north would've been nice.-THE STUPID BUG RACING GAME. It took me an hour to finish it. Which doesn't sound like a lot, but it was only 3 races. F*ck those bugs.-Your inability to say 'no' to romance. You can deny the sex scenes in the game (their very PG anyway, so you're not missing out on much), and insist on friendship. Yet despite that, the characters still continue to regard you in a romantic way most of the time. The biggest example of this particular gripe is Sunder. I'll explain in detail below.Spoiler warning from here on out but these are massive cons to the game.Overall I'd say this game is almost enough. It should've been expanded more, given more time to breathe or had more people working on it. I imagine with the kickstarter and tiktok fame though, the devs probably only had so long they could work on it. That leaves the game feeling very shiny and polished, but overall hollow. Like empty calories. They're sweet, and I enjoy them, but it doesn't take me long to get through it and doesn't leave me feeling full for long, if at all. If the devs ever come out with expansions tot the game, such as additional dunj's or weapons, I'll certainly check it out, but outside of that, I don't feel any desire to replay it. If you believe that you'd enjoy this game, I say still go for it. Just be ready for a very short experience, and one that's very bare bones. I think with more time and experience under their belts, the devs can do a lot more, and I'd still be happy to watch their projects in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderfully enjoyable queer game made by queer developers. It's a fun concept, the gameplay is satisfying and doesn't overstay its welcome, and the story wraps itself up about the time I'm ready to leave. I'm so happy to see a game like this not only being made, but being made to such success. A few years ago, something like this would be unheard of.This is a game made by people who understand what it's like to be queer in the modern day, it radiates the energy in every facet and it really gets it. The characters are genuinely lovable, the chemistry ranges from being spicy to adorable, it's just an across the board great experience. I love that you can pursue multiple routes at the same time to no real ill effect.I'm excited to see that they'll be adding more routes too. I was a huge fan of each one presented, especially Sawyer and Rowan. As someone who is nonbinary myself, seeing two characters like me, and such wonderfully caring depictions warmed my heart. Sawyer is such an adorable and fun character, I loved every moment I got to spend with them and my only complaint is that I didn't get to hang out with that adorable little disaster for longer.I think this is a game that can help a lot of people become more comfortable and confident in their identity simply by seeing characters who remind them of themselves. Characters they can see themselves in. As someone who had only really recently come out, being able to see myself in people like Sawyer and Rowan was truly comforting. Characters who not just happen to be like me, but get my whole vibe. I'd also like to take a moment to talk about how well realized the male characters are as well! I was recently having a conversation with a friend of mine who likes to DM tabletop games, and a topic that came up was that he understands how to make a likable and attractive female character, which is not to say 'aesthetically pleasing' attractive, but in that he, as a largely straight man, understands the aspects he finds attractive in femme-presenting characters. With that conversation fresh in my mind going into this game, I was able to really appreciate just how much this game understands what people who are into men and masculine-spectrum people are into, what they find attractive about those kinds of people, down to personality quirks and the ways they show affection. Every character, from the men, the woman, and the nonbinary folk, are written by people who clearly understand what aspects make those kinds of characters particularly attractive. Again, not only in that they're handsome, pretty or whatnot, but in the unique ways people of those gender identities are attractive.In summation, this is a wonderful little game that I highly recommend to anyone looking for a fun spin on the roguelike and dating sim genres, especially people looking for LGBTQ+ games made by LGBTQ+ creators.

_childDocuments_.review: Queer players! Dating Sims fans! Hear ye, hear ye! Your search is over! I will go off and rant about this absolute gem for WAYYYY too long  but the TL;DR is: FUN! FUNNY! SWEET! ADORABLE! BUY ITTT.This game honestly taught me a valuable lesson in that you can find connection, warmth, kindness and depth even in the silliest of places. And here you can find it all while fighting a flip-phone in a shopping mall wielding your casual vampire situationship or your emotional support idol tsundere husband! The first obvious merit of the game is the game play loop. Being half dungeon crawler, half dating sim, the two halves complement and feed each other in really refreshing ways. The dating elements help vent out and air out the frustration of the dungeon crawling part of the game, while the smooth sword swinging (not that kind) mechanics help break a little of the monotony of only reading through pages of text. That way, the around 15 hours you take to beat it are barely felt at all! It's cutting edge, really (badum tss)And if they’d stop here, they’d have a fun engaging game. But then they had the gall to care! And now look at where we are! The first choice you make in the game is whether or not you want to enable a “Mom” character to send you supportive texts. Right then and there, 5min in, this game showed more care for the comfort of their players than anything I’ve ever played. Not only for making adorable mom texts a main feature, but even allowing us to choose our own relationship with something that is so often taken for granted as a good thing. It allowed me to have my own relationship with a thing, and respected my choice with no question. It's like... What if a game suddenly cares about your boundaries?! And this philosophy follows you all through the game!?You get to customize your pronouns and change them at will, your relationship with food, with gender, with relationships, with sex, with intimacy and have them so effortlessly respected that it felt... refreshing. You can even choose the drinks you like! When the game has this agency and comfort taken from you through the plot it hurts, and players should be mindful of the Trigger Warnings before playing because it does have a recurring character overstepping your boundaries. But even that to me feels in theme with themes of love, the softest and sharpest sides of it. I honestly couldn’t believe this level of thought was first displayed in the video-game world in a game about kissing sword-turning people! It sounds like a joke! All the love interests in this game feel unique, both for the dating sim and dungeon crawling portions. Each date felt nice, even the LI I cared the least about made me chuckle and smile to myself at some moments, and the ones I cared for have broken and mended my heart in ways that will always be treasured. In a game about, yes, kissing swords. How dare the developers make me embarass myself by talking to my friends about how a vampire sword broke my heart?The soundtrack is amazing, the art is absolutely adorable, the writing is hilarious, and the overall message of the game is the absolute sweetest. But my favorite thing about it is that it exists, unceremoniously, and it will deliver either a fun time or just the gentlest embrace that only a thing made with the utmost care can give someone. In my case, both! I’ll be on the lookout for more things like this on the making, and I hope you (the reader of this way too long review) can find the comfort i found ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ kissing swords in some game, any one! And maybe this one is it for you too! Take a stab at it!

_childDocuments_.review: I originally backed this game on Kickstarter, but waited to play it until the DLC was available so that I wouldn't have to remember to go back to it later.  I'm glad that I waited; I think that the DLC adds important content to the game, and getting a year's worth of bug fixes along the way was also nice.  Overall, I enjoyed the game very much. I think without the DLC it would have felt a little on the short side; I was able to get the maximum romantic level with all the weapons (including the three in the DLC), 100% all the collectibles, and get my PC to a level where the final boss fight was trivial, all in 17 hours; that would have been 11-12 hours without the DLC, as the newly-added "dunj", boss fight, dates, and "walking around town" character events add plenty of depth. The combat is, I would say, more comparable to Bastion than to Hades, but there's plenty of variety in how the weapons play.  I might have liked one more full-length dungeon, but then again, I don't think I needed another 15 hours of this combat, either, and what's provided is enough to max out all the characters' abilities and play through all the storylines, so I think the length is sufficient without overstaying its welcome.Really the only downer was finding out after I'd finished that there were videos for the character transformations that I wasn't seeing because I played on the Steam Deck, but YouTube mostly helped me out there. I'm not sure why those don't play on the Deck.  I did experience a couple of hangs, but nothing that couldn't be overcome by restarting the game, and I didn't lose any meaningful amount of progress when that happened. Overall I found the game quite playable on the Steam Deck, and although I didn't try playing the mouse/keyboard version, it's the sort of game that I think wants to be played with a controller.All in all, great job!  Whoever wrote Pocket definitely has had a deep and abiding relationship with a cat, which is something I can appreciate.  :)  I loved the art, the characters were all interesting, and the ones that either weren't my type or that I wasn't comfortable romancing were all cool with platonic options without taking away the ability to unlock all of their weapon abilities; indeed, a primary reason the villain is the villain is because that character doesn't understand the concept of consent or boundaries.  I know there was some controversy over the story but I can't speak to it.  I thought it was obvious very early on who the villain was going to be and why, and that's how it played out.  I am sure that people who have been through toxic relationships of the sort depicted here could find that part of the storyline triggering, but I don't have the personal experience to say any more than that.  The game has been out long enough and enough has been written about it that I think you could determine whether it would be right for you before buying it.Finally, the soundtrack is great.  I'm listening to it right now!
