_childDocuments_.review: Not the most detailed dialogue routes, but the mechanics and overall story are funny and cute. I still found myself genuinely invested in my favorite characters and genuinely annoyed at the ones I didn't take to, so I have to applaud the writers' ability. Not a fan of the final scenario/ultimate ending, but the rest of the game is a surprisingly solid play. I genuinely enjoyed the whole thing and actually laughed out loud a few different times.  It's also really thoughtfully designed in terms of warning you about potential triggers and asking your permission before engaging you in certain game elements, which I frankly really appreciated even though I'm not the target audience.Spoilers Below the Cut:------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------I wish the polyamory aspect was more fleshed out, you have the option to see multiple people and can tell "mom" that you aren't monogamous, but you never really get dialogue to officially tell your partners about eachother and they don't interact on dates. Hopefully an expansion down the line will offer a more concretely poly play style.I also wish they'd been a bit more subtle about Sunder's vampirism. Your first exposure to it, you catch him feeding on someone with exposed monster-eyes and fangs, though it's played off as a casual sex encounter. Then he has to be formally invited into your apartment every time he visits. Then he accidentally mentions being immortal a few times. Then someone references a dead body as a "messy meal" of his. Then, after all of that, they act like his vampirism is a HUGE SECRET that he's revealing and your character's responses are limited to one of two forms of surprise. It just felt like being bashed over the head and a bit clunky. It was still an interesting story element, I just think the dialogue around it could have benefited from a lighter hand.Sunder is also clearly and openly pursuing you casually, but they don't really give your character the option to express that their interest is purely casual too. The endings for him are all considered "bad" and act like he's breaking your heart, which is a little frustrating when he's very obviously the "fun ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ who isn't serious" route.Valerie I thought was handled very well, her dialogue involves slowly opening up to you and trusting you with more emotional intimacy over time as she's been burned before. As a bi/pan person, I would have liked for her to not be the only romanceable woman, but I understand the devs are a small team and the other romanceable female character had to be pushed back to an expansion down the road due to time constraints.I don't have any major critiques for the other routes, they were all fun stories and the weapons had enough concrete difference in-dunj for it to be worthwhile to master the different playstyles. Others have also mentioned this, but I genuinely dislike having to interact with Eric to advance the storyline (devs are apparently already working on a patch that allows you to ghost him, but as of my December playthrough you still had to talk to him or the game wouldn't advance in certain stages) and was disappointed that I didn't have the option to redeem Katana instead. Last, I know your character is supposed to be socially inexperienced and an introvert, but I found myself frustrated that a lot of the dialogue involved choosing between two nearly identical nonanswers rather than more decisive language. There are times when your options are between things like "sure." versus "okay.", or "Thumbs up emoji" versus "okay". With all that said, I genuinely enjoyed the game and I sincerely hope the studio makes additional expansions and/or additional full games in the franchise, the art was cute, the soundtrack was great and the whole play experience was enjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: WARNING: Some vague storyline spoilers.I followed this game from its kickstarter days, reading the dev blogs and first person character emails. The game combines my love of RPG hack and slash with my love of visual novel romance, but in its present state is unable to satisfy my hunger for either.Tl:dr – The game is unsatisfying and shallow in most criteria, failing to fulfil either a desire for a good and varied RPG experience, or an engaging, intelligent (see adult level complexity), immersive, romantic graphic novel experience.Overview:Considering the amount of time the game was in development, and Kitfox's refusal to announce an actual release date, stating only it would be released when the 'weapons [were] beautiful enough', I wanted to believe the story side would be meaty enough to offset the largely repetitive combat. Unfortunately, the end result is very shallow, and it's a shame because people-weapons being wielded by dungeon crawlers is a neat and unique concept. I may go back again and try to master all the weapons just out of sheer OCD, but given the unsatisfying ending to my first mastery and that the game cuts you off once you finish the final mission (rather than allowing you to continue crawling and develop relationships with the other weapons), I really don't fancy starting from scratch.Aesthetic:I like the art style of the characters in their cut-scenes, but the top-down style for movement and combat is a bit cutesy for my tastes. I suppose given very vague sexual descriptions at various points in the game I might have expected a little more maturity in the graphics, but then again the descriptions are VERY vague in a fade to black way. The music fits very well, but is quite repetitive and not really my genre.The voice acting is actually pretty natural and fitting for each character, but engagement could have been improved VASTLY by voicing all narrative dialogue.Combat and Movement:Left button. Right button. F to heal. Q to special ability. Space to dodge. That’s it. While the game does include combinations, and levelling up your relationship with a weapon unlocks new effects, you’ll be madly clicking your mouse buttons over and over again with little strategy required. If you’re looking for a challenge, you will not find it here at all – the ‘dunj’ crawling really is a mini-game to the relationship stories, levelling them up to max in order to unlock the next dating scenario.Storylines:I completed Sunder’s storyline well before the final overall game mission was available, and that left me pretty pissed off. It was a full stop to all development with that character, who I could still use in dungeons, but could take no further in a relationship sense; and the ending had me groaning a long fuuu$%uck oooooff and sneering “NOT a better story than Twilight”.  As an author myself, I recognise there is so much potential, but I suddenly found myself involuntarily taking the ice-bucket challenge.I got most of the way through Isaac, Seven and Valeria, and all but Seven had a curtain-fluttering, chime-tinkling, off-screen sleep over, but none of their stories were especially inspired.Sawyer is a nice addition as far as non-binary inclusion is concerned, but looks like a child, so ew, no, no romancing there.I did not unlock Rowan or Vitas Varnas.For the amount of potential the concept has, the world’s context and the world in general is sparse, and feels like, ultimately, they decided to release the game with super short, flaccid stories on a stage dressed with cardboard cut-out scenery. Tastes a bit like cardboard too.Adult Content and Questionables:OMG they said sex! Mwah mwah kisses happen! That’s about it. Nothing truly risqué happens. Honestly, the only thing that made me feel a teensy bit uncomfortable, was some none-to-subtle racism (in this case weaponism?) from one of the characters, who funnily enough, turns out to be the same type of hypocrite as those religious evangelists spewing homophobic hate out one side of their mouth while sucking a c0ck with the other.Conclusion:This game is rated D for disappointment, and I get the distinct impression, D for future DLC which I will not invest in without more confidence in Kitfox’s ability to deliver stories that rise beyond cliché.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm recommending it with caveats:  (Edited to add detail)This game is a bit like Hades, and a bit like a dating sim, with a little bit of crafting thrown in. It's all fine. It's not great, but it's fine.  Ultimately, it struggles with being shallow versions of better games. However, the mechanics are fun, and satisfying, if simple. However, the game is hugely problematic in the narrative. It presents as progressive, and in some cases, it is, but it also has major problems. Some of them:1) You start the game of with your cousin tells you that he's worried about you because you don't date.  Clearly you can't be happy unless you are dating someone. That's a problem. The cousin then sets you up on dates that you don't necessarily want -- basically forcing you into it "for your own good".  So... that's a major red flag.2) Pretty much everyone that you meet have major red flags. The most egregious is the stalker, but they are all problems in some way.  I believe you are supposed to help them, but I only played through a couple of stories. So either you should ignore red flags or try to fix people. Either of those messages are terrible.  As an example: one of the first characters you meet has their business partner mention that he has a history of violence and you should be wary.  This isn't something that you should teach people to ignore.  Another of the characters appears to be underage. I'm not sure if they are, but that I even thought that they were, based on appearance and how they act -- that's a big NOPE. 3) Near the end, you fight to overcome your fear of intimacy, where you are accused of being asexual like it's a bad thing. So, much as this game is progressive on gender fluidity, it's not great with asexual being a viable lifestyle choice.The cat, on the other hand... just be friends with the cat. The cat is awesome.

_childDocuments_.review: An interesting concept with charming characters and designs to match, but after beating the game and playing two more times to see if my choices have any impact to the story, it falls short.For it being a dating simulator, the stories for each individual romantic interest are linear.  What I mean by this is that no matter what choices you make in interacting with them, their story doesn’t change.  You can reject a character’s advances and they will still try to make moves on you.  This is not to talk ill of any of them as they each have their own unique charms that compels me to know more about them, but if I want to stay friends with someone or give consent to pursue them romantically, I’d like to explore those different outcomes.I come into this game wondering if I, as the player, can dive into a story and change the world around me with the choices I’ve made while also creating deeper bonds with the people I come across on the way.  I didn’t get any of that.  The ending was shallow and lackluster.  My relationships with the characters left me rather bitter and emotionally scarred (looking at Sunder who's the poster boy for the game's promotional material btw), and on top of this, it feels like me as the protagonist did not experience any actual growth.  It was like I was put in a movie and forced to ride it through without any means to change its course.  The game warned about elements of stalking and emotional manipulation.  These are integral parts of the story, they're triggering topics and I’m glad to see it.  But I wasn’t emotionally prepared to see the level of those elements into play, it left me scarred and uncomfortable that’s for certain.  I see the direction they were going and it’s a good concept, but the delivery hits home and not at all in a good way.Perhaps if the game receives future content that adds more depth and writing to the story (perhaps even fix some of the romance’s personal storylines to cater to player needs and satisfaction such as branching plots in choices), then I’d be all for it.  If you’re looking for a casual hook-up game with mindless dungeon crawling elements, go for it.  However if you’re looking to make meaningful connections with some hotties and explore a deep, rich story to boot, as it is right now, I cannot in good conscience recommend the game to anyone.

_childDocuments_.review: A mostly pretty good dating/dungeon crawler.I find it hard to recommend though since this is a very niche since you need to have like dating sim sort of games, dungeon cralwers and isometric hack and slash style combat. Which I have at least some interest in the first two, but isometric combat is kind of annoying, perspective making it hard to hit targets; especially with the Estoc weapon which is a thrust attack and your going to miss a lot at first. But the real problem with the combat is it doesn't really know how to make combat harder other then to just spawn more enemies. Which kind of sucks and I just ended up spamming Area of Effect attacks since I was constantly surrounded.Also the spell books are kind of useless. Like I get what the intention was, but most of the spells are meh at best and are out done by the weapons with AoE attacks. Also there is two hats that double damage and that just breaks the games tactics down to "melt the enemy before they can even attack"The love interests are... mostly fine. I did get through all the romance paths except for one, which was Sunder the guy on all the promotional stuff. But these aren't really characters I'd gush over how much I love. Also it feels weird, normally dating games tend to go through a number of archetypes that appeal very broadly but boyfriend dungeon kinda doesn't, which is kind of refreshing but also gives a sense of more limited options. Let that colour your opinion as you will, just something weird I noticed. Also it feels like they ran out of ideas since one of the "boyfriend weapons" is just a cat.Overall pretty good. If the concept sounds interesting then I'd say it will hold your attention, it is rather short. I wasn't really rushing and it took me less then 8 hours.

_childDocuments_.review: There is so much to love about this game, especially if you're LGBT+As far as the combat goes, it does a great job of giving each weapon their own intuitive fighting style that seems to really fit each individual's personality. I'd go into detail, but I don't want to spoil.As for the dating sim aspects of the game, there are men, women, and non-binary people to romance, which means there's something for everyone and it's great if you're pan. You can change your appearance and your pronouns anytime at your apartment, which makes it fun to play with your avatar a bit, and the pronoun flexibility is great if you're questioning or gender fluid. You can seemingly date everyone, simultaneously, and no one seems bothered by it which feels so great if you're poly, and you don't have to pursue any of these relationships from a romantic or sexual angle if you don't want to. You can just form a close platonic relationship with any or all of them, which is great for aro and/or ace folks.Love this game. 10/10 will play again.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted this game to be a lot better because of the controversy around it. Things that I personally experienced that I'm not nuts about:- the combat system isn't particularly robust- choices in your relationships don't really seem to matter- you can't choose how the M/C feels about people so it feels a little restrictedThings I researched before deciding whether or not to stop playing but have not seen for myself.- The game is apparently not complete. I would rather pay more for a complete game later. I'm personally not a fan of the installments model in games. Other people might not mind this though.- Choices continue to not matter.- I'm not nuts about the two nonbinary character designs as a nonbinary person. There's not a lot of representation for us in games like this. There's nothing wrong with people (esp other nonbinary people) liking the characters but nonbinary people tend to get perceived as either soft boi trans man lite or spooky witch enthusiasm trans woman lite a lot by cis people. I think if there were either more nonbinary and trans characters in the game it wouldn't feel so bad, but it just feels kind of weird for me.- I think regarding the above point and also some reflecting I was doing on Seven's plot, I feel like the game is marketed as and tries to present itself as socially aware (the economist is interested in addressing inequality, a character who believes in a system that's a metaphor for racial purity is a villain, LGBTQ options etc), but it gets complicated when marketing these characters in game and out of game has to do with desirability. These characters being diverse is in someways a commodity to sell a product and I was expecting some commentary on that in game (especially with how NPCs treat Seven and the way white people interact with K-POP as a commodity), but felt like that ultimately didn't pull through. I was hoping that maybe the writing on a character like Sawyer would be teaching people not to fetishize nonbinary people as certain tropes, but what from I've researched it doesn't turn out that way.In case the devs bother to read this I'm going to say some nice things as well because there's clearly a lot of love in this project and I don't want to trash it.- I appreciate that the game has an ambitious concept for people who are not accustomed to this genre to maybe play more (I've played a decent amount of VNs in my life).- the art and stylization looks great- Jesse being bisexual slaps- I want to date Noah so badly but I'm afraid of him being unemployed or fat being treated as a joke, and if he wants to resist capitalism and find his purpose through surfing and being kind to animals ♥♥♥♥ yes.- side note: frankly I don't need my dating sims to be progressive. I play a lot of ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up and weird games. But if that's your goal you have to fully commit to it.- back to compliments!! the break stops in certain levels that heal were a great mechanic and helped game play a lot- the idea of combos is good, they're just a little too unchunkable memory wise to be practical rn! Great concept to mix up combat though.- the monster design was very good and I enjoyed them- the rest spots in the dungeon all slapped

I just wish there was more impact choices or situations when it comes to that part of the game or get a more unique ending with them. After that it was very easy to beat the final boss.I don't know if more content will be released, but I am crossing my fingers for that as I think a lot more updates could help this game out to just feel more complete.

_childDocuments_.review: I did enjoy the game despite my problems with it. My main problem with the game is the Protagonist is a major jerk, from the first meeting with Eric your Protagonist seems to dislike him for some reason and just *will not* treat him with civility, courtesy or kindness... My next problem is that the game is far too short, and my last problem is that Eric is not a romance T_T. /RANTI decided to check this game out after the "controversy" and I discovered that I had absolutely no problem with it that people were "all in uproar" about lol XD. Maybe because I thought Eric was treated entirely unfairly from the very beginning of the game by our Protagonist. I don't think Eric is a stalker like the game is trying to write him as, his advances were never unwanted for me. I was only upset that not once in the game could I ever just have a friendly conversation with him, the writers are dead set on making our Protagonist hate him. WHY?! Why do you want us to hate him writers?! I felt like I was resigned to romance the shirtless wonder instead of romancing Eric. /RANTAnyway, I read that the dev team is planning on additional content for this game, so I want to recommend it so you can support the game and the team for that content <3 ^^. If you want to love Eric like I do, watch the BBC Pride and Prejudice and imagine having a conversation with him cause the game won't let you have any civil conversation with him... EDIT: Also Sense and Sensibility, Downtown Abbey, Frankenstein or Psycho Pass(you'll see a properly villainous character in Psycho Pass.)EDIT: Eric is not completely hopeless that everyone is hating on him about. If you've played Dragon Quest XI then you know of a character called, Vince Vanquish who abducts challengers and gives them to Arachtagon; before the Hero arrives on the scene, Vince won the tournament, so for a full year he abducted and let people *die* due to his actions. What Eric does is similar to Vince, I don't understand why the dev team and Boyfriend Dungeon are so keen on hating on the poor man.  Also dev team, please make him a romance. It is not impossible to keep everything exactly as it is in your story *and* have an Eric romance. For one thing, if your protagonist shows him kindness and a keen interest in Eric, then he will be pleased but feel extremely guilty and probably want to break off the relationship. At the end of the game when everything comes to light, you should be given the choice to accept Eric for every one of his faults, or stay with one of the other romances. I think that would be the best story for him <3. EDIT: Changing my review to "Not Recommended" because the dev team looks like they have no interest in adjusting their writing to make the Protagonist not be a total C-word and to treat Eric with civility, courtesy and kindness. If the dev team surprises me with an update to their writing in regards to Eric, then I will recommend it again. The story has strengths, but the writing team is much too heavy handed in forcing young people to *hate* Eric. The poor guy doesn't deserve the reception he gets. Eric needs our love <3.

_childDocuments_.review: I had a blast playing through this game and will likely play the entire story again at some point. The characters are interesting and the dating sim part is very fun, but simple. The majority of the story takes place through those "Dates" and one can always choose not to pursue a character further by simply not going on further dates with them. Unfortunately though all the "dating paths" are pretty linear with only slight variations here and there and only minor impacts on other "dating paths". The dungeon crawls are fun with each weapon feeling quite different and unique. The monsters are interesting but lack a bit variety with each dungeon coming with a handful of monsters, that then have a stronger  variant to them and one boss. Its also interesting to play around with different "spells" and strategies, though I found myself trying to maximize love with as many weapons as possible per run. Within the different Levels you sometimes find a place to interact with your equipped weapon - which is nice and flavorful, whit each weapon reacting differently to each possible place.One thing both the dungeons and dates have in common, is that there is not a lot of them. There are 2 dungeons that are really fun and each weapon has 6 Levels you can reach, which translates to 7 dates including the date in which you first meet them. There are a few events in between - but while being crafted beautifully, they do not add a whole lotta game to play. This might change a bit in future and mod support is in its way - but those are might and maybe. Overall I finished the main story and maxed all love ranks in about 8 hours, without too much grinding or time optimized gameplay - which left me wanting more, though I think replaying this game will be fun.Overall I can really recommend the game and think the price tag is good for this somewhat smalller unique fusion blend of genres.

_childDocuments_.review: I had a lot of fun with this game, it was worth the $20 to me. The only criticisms I would give are: * if you ignore dialog you can inadvertently avoid the main storyline* once you get the whetstone you end up powering through the dungeons and then just rapid-fire dates to max out the weapon quickly. Without the dungeon crawl between dates, it blends together and it's hard to get as invested in the later introduced characters and their weapon mechanics.* it's easy to overlook the Scythe character and his character was cringey and my least favorite. His fighting mechanics were fun thoughI don't play many dating sims, I do play hack n' slash dungeon crawlers. It's fun trying to figure out what gifts the characters might like and which type of dialog response the different characters will prefer. My wife and I enjoyed this game and its ludicrous premise. It is short -- we dated everyone, crafted everything, and bought everything in about 11 hours. I like that you can complete each character's story arc in a single playthrough -- it doesn't force you to choose between characters. The dungeon crawling is fun once you get used to the  style of play it encourages. The enemy designs are a bit hokey but it didn't detract from the experience for me.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a bullet hell game with little in the way of gameplay customisation, propped up by a barebones dating sim with a lack of actual varied dialogue choices, ranging from enthusiasm to teenage ennui and indifference. Dating is the usual pastiche of tired conversation options, affinity raising and wanton bribery.The gameplay is passable if basic, the content is so intrinsically Californian that I feel that the game is two steps short of asking consent before dealing damage to you. The character creation is possibly a hidden social commentary on how despite all the options available to you and your identity, none of them actually have any practical value. Certainly subversive, but it can't carry the plot by itself.I was hoping the content would at least be humorous, tongue-in-cheek and witty the way Monster Prom is, but this game currently reads more like a hormonal angst-fest with little in the way of plot (it has opt-in content warnings for people who are triggered by interactions with their mother, for goodness' sake). Perhaps that isn't entirely a bad thing, but I'm probably at an age where I find it a trifle tiresome. Did not live up to my expectations of something more in the vein of Hatoful Boyfriend (the pigeon dating sim).
_childDocuments_.name: Boyfriend Dungeon

_childDocuments_.review: This is a quick game, a dating sim with a dungeon crawler mechanic rather than the other way around.I love that some of the boyfriend's are just ♥♥♥♥♥♥ people who behave poorly. I can't tell if it's poor writing or a similar intentional statement about how ♥♥♥♥♥♥ people can be, but some of the people you say "I just want us to be friends" with make moves on you repeatedly anyway, or even wake you up with kisses. The game tells you explicitly you can be strictly platonic with people, but some of them will repeatedly try to re-negotiate that. My list of "characters in this game who are not ♥♥♥♥" got smaller and smaller over timeWhich is good. If you give people what they want, of course they're nice to you. You only really see how nice someone is when you see them facing rejection or other anger. People who romanced some of the people I think are gross, probably think they're great bois. They didn't see how they were when you weren't interested.At the same time, that is a bit too much realism for some people. So the game might be for you.The dungeon crawling is fine, especially as the weapon styles branch out from progressing each relationship.It's worth a shot if you want to play a dating sim with more three-dimensional people than normal. It's just, you can't just pick who you want and fix them. They stay who they were, and sometimes that means you get bit. Which to me was neat and a good truth to reflect in a game. To others though, dating sims are escapist fantasies they want to go well, and this doesn't always go well for you.

_childDocuments_.review: The dungeon crawling is an enjoyable and intuitive experience that invokes Hades/ Binding of Isaac-style gameplay. Everybody is written interestingly enough without feeling caricatured despite some of the romance options feeling like they've stemmed from a Y.A. novel.Thanks for making this charming game out of left field.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a true embodiment of fun. I'm not into women, but all the characters are enjoyable and have their own unique personalities. (Jonah is such a sweetie pie. I loved collecting all the outfits and hats and loved how everything tied in. The weapons are all special on their own and tie into them as people. Each story is noteworthy and makes you enjoy them as characters. This game has a good story and I understand the pet peeves other people have, but I feel as if they take it too seriously. If you see this to be a world changing game rather than enjoying the special little things, you're not going to enjoy it. This game is just people learning and loving life and the people around them, while having you be apart of their lives for a short time. This is truly a lovely game with lots of love and effort put into it. From the soundtrack, to art, mechanics, and everything in between. It's made to enjoy, and I know I certainly did. Thank you Kitfox, for a wonderful game.

_childDocuments_.review: I've had this game on my wishlist for a while, so when I saw that it was dropped suddenly, I was ecstatic! The game was actually gifted to me from my partner because they know I'm very heavily into romance novels and they like dungeon crawlers, so having this on an account with Family Share is a win-win! Onto an actual review: COMBAT: It's really simplistic but not in a negative way. I'm garbage at most dungeon crawlers because I struggle with timing my hits and dodges correctly. This game is super merciful and allows for beginners to get a sense of the genre without feeling like they're too in over their heads, which I enjoy wholeheartedly, and the different weapon types allow for several alternate styles of gameplay as well. My favorite weapons to use were the brass knuckles, the scythe, the dagger, and the laser saber. Each weapon has different abilities and as you level up, you can change the build your weapon has to be either more tactical or more damage-oriented. I picked the more damage-oriented skills most of the time because I personally just think they're really neat. Also, giving some hats some bonuses to combat is fun! I like that some of them obviously go with craftable outfits but do not strictly have to be with those outfits. Using the fox hood with the leather jacket or the bucket hat with the cultist robes is extremely fun to me. The zines are also really creative and clever! My personal favorites to use were Spooky Zine and the bug one (can't remember the name, sorry!). STORYTELLING: I. Love. This. Story. I really do. The characters are all so well-written and there's a LOT of side twists within each individual character's storyline, which is super enjoyable, and some of the characters overlap in strange ways which is cool too! The usage of the text conversations to advance the story is clever and the responses are super witty. Every character has their personality shine through and it's incredibly refreshing to see enriching characters portrayed so wonderfully. The voice acting is nice as well! I'm also going to mention that there's a few spots in the story where there are some hints towards characters making a return, or the player character also making a return back to town, so I am hopeful that this game will eventually make some DLC for the holidays or something. The game doesn't lock you into dating anyone. You have complete freedom over who you choose to date or not to date, and that's really nice to see. It's a fresh perspective for a dating sim to have a lot of inclusivity like this one does. Part of me is also really endeared that the developers chose to make the player's character model as androgynous as possible, because that way the outfits just appear as clothes, and are not specifically gendered. The flavor text on the hats/outfits is wonderful, too! SIDE COMMENTS: Truly, this game is worth the purchase! I think the big baddie was pretty obvious from the start (though part of me thought it was going to be a side character that ended up being a one-off...) but I also enjoy the curves and twists the story takes as you romance or befriend people and try to get through the summer. Sad it's such a short season though!! Also, the soundtrack is absolutely bopping. The headphone and ear pod hats change the music and I am so in love with all of it. Rating: 10/10, please buy the game. please.

_childDocuments_.review: I backed this game on kickstarted back in 2018, hoping to have a fun, queer experience smooching swords and battling monsters. That's also exactly what I got. _childDocuments_.review: Finally, a game that let's me smooch a sword! As far as the dating/visual aspect novel goes, I'm really impressed with the variety of characters (weapons?). They all have unique personalities that seem pretty darn realistic as far as how people actually behave (one character uncomfortably reminds me of an ex-boyfriend and the game lets me be as snotty to him as he deserves). Definitely A+ for the dating sim parts.As for the dungeon diving? I like it too! I appreciate how character growth is tied both to the standard experience points (killing monsters), as well as the progress of relationships with weapons. Combat is simple (combos are made with just two buttons and there's two more buttons for healing items or attack items), but effective, and the scenery in the dungeon is visually interesting.And now, the art and music! The backgrounds outside of the dungeon for all the date spots are detailed and really well done. Character portraits are fantastic and some of the best I've seen in any game, let alone visual novel style games. What's particularly cool is that all the major characters get animated introductions similar to the Sailor Moon transformation. Some of the non-character cutscenes are animated, too, and all high quality! As for the music, soundtrack is poppy, upbeat, and entertaining. I've yet to encounter a piece of music that's obtrusive or annoying as a loop. It's the kind of music you'd put on in the background while studying or doing some sort of hobby craft.TL;DR: Smooch a sword in a dungeon to the sick beat of a pop jam.
_childDocuments_.name: Boyfriend Dungeon

_childDocuments_.review: I... want to like this game, but I don't. I really, really don't. It doesn't have any ability to refuse dates, or turn people down, or set boundaries and then have them respected. I say I don't like dancing? Too bad, I must dance. I say something isn't a date? Too bad, everyone but me agrees that getting coffee with that guy was a date. I think my cousin's quest to make me have a date right now is kind of dumb, I'd really rather just chill and go slay monsters in dungeons? Too. Bad.More than that, though, it genuinely made me uncomfortable in a way the warnings didn't prepare me for. At the start of the game there's a warning "This game may include references to unwanted advances, stalking, and other forms of emotional manipulation. Play with care." which sounds fine, but in actuality it is not 'references.' You, the player, acquire a stalker. He leaves a rose on your doorstep. He follows you when you go on dates to other people and comments on them through text message later. He keeps calling you pet names even though you ask him to please stop.Stalking is horrible, and consent is important, and I can tell that this game understands that. Clearly a lot of thought went into it, because the interactions ring true. But I really feel like if you're going to confront something that strikes so close to home for a lot of people, you need to both warn them in advance better, and always directly show the difference between 'Okay' and 'Not okay.' Because having my stalker presented as messed up while I am incapable of refusing dates, or refusing to dance, or whatever else confuses the entire experience. I just feel trapped in every single interaction I'm having. The game will ask me for my preferences, and then completely ignore them.And that's not the kind of game I want to play, and it's not the kind of game I'd recommend to anyone.

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting genre mix for a game. Never knew hack&slash could work with visual novel. Turned out really fun actually.Music is amazing and fits gameplay perfectly. So much so, that I literally got goosebumps sometimes. I also love how it changes depending on how much enemies is around.Gameplay is not too hard, can be relaxing actually.Love the whole style. Very cute, very chill.Story is simple and kind of absurd, but pretty fun. Ending was cool, a bit bittersweet, but fitting.Characters - mixed bag. I guess it just makes them for every taste. Eric can burn in hell, Valeria and Sawyer are annoying at times, Sunder is kind of a ♥♥♥, Seven and Isaac are for the win, Jonah and Rowan are pretty cute actually, Leah is just ok and Dr.Holmes are fun. But oh my god, Pocket. Pocket! My MVP. My bestie. My partner for life (his owner doesn't exist, be quiet). Figures, that in the romance (kinda) game, my favourite character is a cat. But what a cat he is. Perfect, everything about him is perfect. His design, his soundtrack, his "dates", his resting events at the dungeon. Also, for some reason I expected him to actually talk (like a human), I mean, it does look like that kind of a game. But I'm really glad he doesn't. And, oh lord, he's ending is 100% the best, stop arguing, I can't hear you and you are wrong anyway. For god's sake, no joke, the  part - I never felt more touched. Brought tears to my eyes, smile to my face and peace to my heart. He is just the best cat ever and I would die for him.I enjoyed this game a great deal.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr: It feels rushed.When you start the game, it instantly charms you. There's so much to do! The visuals are pleasing, and they added some quality partial voice acting, to spice things up.Unfortunately, you quickly run out of content to do, which is a sin for anything that attempts to call itself roguelike. The dating part doesn't fare much better.There's only 2 dungeons for you to clear, and I managed to finish the crafting part of the game before even finishing the second one. That makes further re-runs pretty much pointless, from resource gathering perspective.The only issue I've encountered in the first dungeon, is that it doesn't seem to know how to handle the player surviving part of the tutorial, where you're supposed to die. Second dungeon is more buggy than the first.Once you reach max love level with one of the weapons, you get x2 boost for any love points you get with others, literally allowing you to speedrun the rest of this fairly short game.The dating aspect is diminished in its charm by how Everyone Is Totally Into You. You don't have to do much, for the weapons to throw themselves at you.While the possibility to pursue a platonic relationship is mentioned in the beginning of the game, if you do not choose "I want us to stay friends" as soon as it is presented to you, the game will proceed with understanding that you want a sexual relationship, with no option to back out of it.Some of the platonic relationships can be awkward. I'm looking at you, Sunder.And since I mentioned Sunder, spoilers for how his story ends: As for the game's ending, it's so heavily charged with combat, you may want to run it again, just to see what you missed the first time, by focusing on not dying, or maybe take another weapon with you... and the game doesn't let you redo the ending. Despite allowing you to continue playing after the ending, to deal whatever it is you didn't finish.All in all, I expected more, back when I saw this game on Kickstarter.

_childDocuments_.review: I blasted through this way quicker than expected, and that's the only complaint I have about this genuinely fantastic game. the voice acting is great, the art style lovely, the combat is nicely balanced with the story arcs so that neither ever outstays its welcome or drags, the characterisation is complex and the more difficult subject matter well executed. Finally the soundtrack, some amazing music that fits perfectly to the scenes, will be humming them for a while. 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: I was looking forward to trying out this game, but the combat mechanic is terrible and makes playing an annoying chore. You have a character that you move around with the AWSD keys, but if you use your weapon the character turns around unexpectedly and it is incredibly difficult to control the movement direction when you are fighting. You end up with a bunch of monsters who keep hitting you in the back because your character won't turn around. Another complaint I have is that this game does not allow you to save whenever you want. Given the difficult combat mechanics that is especially annoying.Finally, with this sort of game I expect to have CGs and a gallery to view the ones you have unlocked. Neither of those are available from what I can tell.I don't think this game was ready for release.

_childDocuments_.review: I think this game is a solid game, especially for the price. You have a little gender neutral sprite type character, and you can choose your pronouns out of the three basic ones (she/he/they). All of the chars could be attracted to you, so no matter what gender you are, the options remain the same. In the menu, I discovered you can reduce the damage you take, so if the dungeon style intimidates you, know that you can make it easier on yourself. Try it out!Each of the characters are unique, and they each of good and bad qualities. The game gives you a warning at the beginning, because it does have stalker types, and if you are an estranged kid, you can opt out of texts from "Mom." The game deals with how parents can be ♥♥♥♥♥♥, so there is a clear acknowledgement that the character may have a decent parent, but not everyone does. The clothing choices, just to start, are minimal but offer two different types of head coverings, for those of various faiths. Some of the dialogue is acted out, and done fairly well. I almost wish all of it could be, but I don't mind that it isn't. Characters are well designed, and generally very attractive. I have yet to see a character who is not able bodied (or at least doesn't show it physically), and who is not, in some way attractive. I'm not that far into the game though!The game also deals with social anxiety very well. The main deal with your character is stepping out of their shell and dealing with their issues. I def feel called out  LOL. So if that is something you don't want your character to delve into...be warned.Overall I absolutely adore this game. I highly recommend it. Just know there is, as one would expect, some seriously sexually charged dialogue, references to trauma, and overall deep topics it delves into.

_childDocuments_.review: First, the positives. Very inclusive, (ace, aro, nb and poly friendly options and 2 enby love interests. Rarely ever see that kind of inclusion and ALL for it). The premise is interesting and the dungeon and bonding mechanics are hella fun. Loved the intro animations and the art looks good for the most part. Some of the faces seem a little off at times though. The crafting and outfits are all really well done. The game has lots of charm and I desperately wanted to love, but also has a lot of missed potential and things that can feel...lacking story content wise. I really hope devs consider adding more plot content for all the main love interest, but ESPECIALLY Sunder and Jonah.My main beef is with Sunder who's basically a cheese grater for your emotions in the worst way possible. In short and without spoiling the details, he's a bad end only character. Tried two different playthroughs with the same result and as far as I know, no other players have found a good ending for him. I'll add more with a spoiler warning further down.As an enby I was so happy with Rowan's character and that there was more than one enby romance option, even if Sawyer wasn't my type. Rowan was incredibly well done, but like the other love interests, their route felt too short. As an ace I was thrilled that sex was opitonal and not required for romance. On the other hand, many of the romances felt very rushed and like there should have been more to them so much so it almost felt like a hookup focused game over a date sim. To be frank there's a lot that felt rushed or cut short to the point I feel the game's release should have been postponed a few months. There's only two dungeons with less than 15 levels each and they go by pretty quick. Didn't feel like there was enough time to flesh out the story and worldbuilding either which is a shame because I wanted to know more about the weapon people. Spoilers for Sunder ahead.Now for Sunder. Hoo boy, the man single-handedly soured the whole game for me. Everything else, I was willing to overlook til this point. Having one of the main love interests in a date sim exist only to break your heart in the most callous way possible with no options to discuss or address it or get a good ending is a very poor design decision imo. Especially since he was one of the main reasons I bought the game. If I wanted to simulate having my heart broken and reliving an extremely painful experience (charming older guy toying with my feelings and stringing a younger, more inexperienced me along as a way to pass the time), I wouldn't...be playing a date sim. I felt extremely emotionally manipulated by Sunder only it was worse because he had spent so much time gaining my trust and trying to convince me he was worth giving a shot. I expected it from the antagonist, but again, NOT a main love interest in a date sim. Despite other characters warning you about him. I thought it was just the vampire thing keeping him from intimacy in the past, not...him not having his $h*t together as a human being. If he was aromantic and wanted a queer platonic relationship with your character, I would've been fine with that. If he was poly? Would've been fine with that too. If he was both and just wanted a platonic, but loving relationship with you while sleeping with other people, I might've been fine with that too. I just would have liked the option to discuss it openly with him and explore it as an option together.. Not be strung along, jerked around, then dumped with no real explanation or closure.As for Jonah. for the life of me I can't figure out how you're supposed to unlock his route. You meet him, he texts to say he won't be there the rest of the summer, but he feels you'll meet again real soon...except you don't. That's literally all I can say about Jonah which is too bad. All I can think is that maybe it was the devs way of hinting they'll release content for him soon?Jessie also became extremely annoying because you couldn't say no to the pointless awkward dates with non love interests. The first one I get since it's essential to the plot, but the rest was just like "LEAVE ME ALONE AND LET ME DATE MY WEAPONS JESSIE." Even Jonah, is kind of forced on you by Jessie as a third wheel if you invite one of your own date's to an event later. For a game that has the sensitivity to ask about whether it's okay to send you texts from a character called Mom (which I was incredibly grateful for as I don't have a great relationship with mine) and brings up the importance of consent at multiple points, it's kind of jarring when you realize you can't opt out of or say no to Jessie about any of the dates he sets you up on.Also gonna repeat what other's have stated about the content warning. It's not adequate as written. It makes it sound like you can opt out of the stalking and emotional manipulation or like their sort of in the background, but doesn't tell you it literally forces you to keep engaging with an incel, "nice guy" stalker type in order to progress the plot. I know it's a game and not real life, but I found it implausible that your character wouldn't just block this character's number. That said, the devs have announced they'll be updating the content warning to reflect this, so hopefully that's in place soon.I feel like this game's release date should've been pushed back a bit and that there should be a good ending for Sunder, literally any content for Jonah and at least 10 heart levels and dates with each love interest,I'm hoping devs release a future update or DLC with more story content as this game still has the potential to be incredible, but in it's current state, I can't quite bring myself to recommend it to others. The outifts are cute, but the game really doesn't need more of them and I would have been fine with half as many and no craftable racing game, if it meant more fleshed out romances or at least getting a positive end for Sunder. Currently you can date every character (save for Jonah) and nearly 100% this game in about 6 hours or so.

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked Dream Daddy, you'll most likely enjoy this game too.The dungeon part has a nice difficulty curve to it and never becomes frustratingly hard (minus one very rare enemy near the very end that hits like a truck), in part thanks to the generous amount of healing sources available and the quick leveling. The way you acquire most craftables can be a bit annoying since it requires a bit of grinding, as you find practically all the recipes in random chests. I did enjoy using most of the weapons, they had a varied enough feel to them. There's only one I never really got into, it doesn't bring me the same level of enjoyment as all the others.My only con: depending on some of the very early decisions you make in your playthrough, the main plot point of the story may get spoiled. For me, it also made the interaction with a certain character awfully grating.

_childDocuments_.review: Such a great premise! Wish there was a bigger fandom for it! Really adore the queer/inclusive range of characters and options for the player character. It's a queer friendly Canadian indie game. What more could I want? <3<3Do wish there was a bit more polish re: game mechanics and difficulty, but it doesn't diminish the game enough to be a game breaking issue. The combat could be way tighter and less clunky honestly, and the levels could be better laid out/stick to cleaner metrics for use of space/where the PC and enemies can and can't move through at the very least.Above all else though? I just really REALLY wish there was a hard mode!!! I mean, whaaaat??The present difficulty level makes the game SUPER short!! The whole thing seems balanced as if it wanted to shepherd players out of the game as fast as possible! 100% Achievements in like under 10 hours if your trying for it. But I WANT to spend more time with it! I wan't to replay, try combos, grind and get recipes or dialogue with my fave weapons! (Without having to start a whole new file, and dumping said file if I DO die in the middle of a dunj and level my way into the difficulty being way too low again literally from that one, MAYBE two runs. ='( )Fantastic setting/idea, fun characters, inclusive and caring company, needs better balance, and to feel able to take up more space/time?? Honestly it's like it lacked confidence in itself!

_childDocuments_.review: Creative, visually stellar, and left me wanting more.The game description is exactly as it sounds - you run some dungeons and you can date your weapons. Or most of them, at least. For a short game, it packs a story that keeps you engaged. You want to continue progressing in the narrative to reach that supposed satisfactory conclusion.Pros:- Great visuals and animations for the weapons.- Dungeons were fun and liked the concepts of the bosses.- Variety of dateable characters, or can keep thing platonic!- Crafting system was simple and felt rewarding, not a chore.- Music is banging! I'm still humming the songs weeks later.- Inclusion of multiple pronouns, ability to change your avatar how you see fit.- Developers are listening to peeps and made effort to update content warnings and address concerns.- Story was alright. Some tweaks could be addressed, but appreciate the devs pushing the narrative into areas rarely discussed.Cons:- It's a bit too short for how much you pay.- Replay options are limited. it's easy to get most of the achievements in the first play through, and you can date multiple weapons at once.- Only 2 dungeons! I had a lot of fun running the dungeons, so I was a bit meh when a third wasn't available.- There are some problems with how the last boss is handled in terms of mechanics. It's a little cringy from a narrative perspective. Also not a fan with the conclusion of the overarching nemesis. It felt rushed.Something I hope Kitfox will do:- Add an "Endless Dungeon" mode! Instant replay value. With each floor increasing in difficulty, I would easily spend hours running the dung and be satisfied.Overall, I genuinely enjoyed playing the game. Though I wish there was more dungeon content, the core of it was fun. I'll be playing again for the soundtrack!

_childDocuments_.review: 6/10Overall a very enjoyable and sweet game, I definitely recommend it.Highlights first:- This game is inclusive as heII- The sprite artwork is gorgeous and the simplified character style in the dungeons and on the map is adorable- The music fits well and I liked the score a ton- The game makes you aware of its trigger warnings and overall makes you feel very safe- Every romance option has its own appeal, I didn't feel like any character had less depth than the other, they feel about equally as developedSome things that contributed to the low score to be aware of when picking up this game:- The voice acting isn't perfect: It doesn't align with the text boxes at certain points and characters are not fully voiced(which isn't an issue, but worth noting). There are scenes where one character has full voice acting, while others don't, which feels dissonant.- The game sets up themes and doesn't quite deliver on them (To remain spoiler free, I won't elaborate, but I'd have liked my choices to be viable and have actual impact on the story a bit more, especially during the finale.)- Although all characters are developed equally, they don't have many layers, which isn't bad, but in general leaves me lukewarm about them.In spite of all this, I had a very fluffy time with this game, 10ish hours of gameplay well spent. I don't regret picking this one up.

_childDocuments_.review: I had been looking at this game for a bit and picked it up on sale out of boredom. I wasn't expecting much.  I was hooked a couple hours in, but near the end I was bored. Starting off, I was impressed by everything it had: character customization, crafting, interactive texts, and a good variety of romances.  It has all the right mechanics and a great foundation, but the writing needs a lot of work. There are all these characters, platonic or otherwise, and this great little world the writers have created, only to have the story go nowhere when it hits the climax; then the story resolves itself quickly and VOILA you've hit end game :\  (Also the "twist" with Sunder? UGH, WHY. This felt like pandering to fans of that aesthetic, and it added nothing to the story line -- not even HIS story line.)The pacing through me off a bit, too.  Maybe I didn't dungeon enough, but it didn't take much to get 6 romances maxed out, so all I had left was the 3rd dungeon.  I didn't end up beating it because it got too boring.  I romanced a 7th character just to give me something else to do.Overall?  It's an okay game geared towards casual players, with underwhelming and uninspired writing.  If you're someone who likes challenging gameplay and a little more from your dating sims besides just, "Hey I'm a nobody that's new in town and looking for love, but no promises 'cause I'm leaving in 2 months anyway", then look elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun, witty, medium-length game (I beat it and completed every character's story in around 12 hours, and I'm a slow player) with dungeon crawler, visual novel and dating sim elements. If any two of these elements sound like your type of genre, I highly recommend checking this game out. This game will make you interact multiple times with a person who will later turn to stalking, threatening and then trying to more-or-less kill you. You have no choice about whether or not you interact with this person, the game makes you do it to advance the plot. Their antics  quickly dissolve to "how dare you reject me, you're a f*cking c*nt like everyone else". I don't mind the inclusion of such characters, especially because the game judges them HARSHLY for it. But the game also, at its very start, lets me choose whether a friendly parental figure will send me encouraging text messages in between, because that may be upsetting to some people, yet the game did not warn me about the stalker character, at all.(I went back and checked the game trailer and store description just to see if I missed out on any warnings, but no.)After starting the game and being pleasantly surprised at the opt-in option for the parental figure, this felt like a punch in the gut. I have not had stalkers literally trying to kill me IRL, fortunately, but I have met lots of people who raised red flags for me all over the place which made me get the F out, and I saw that reflected in this one character's writing. Kudos to the writing staff, but just please warn me first. Fiction is all about safely exploring (dangerous) concepts and that includes knowing what you're getting into.- the art is GORGEOUS! Not only the in-game avatars for everyone, and the cute outfit options for your character, but especially the animations that play when a weapon first transforms into a human- the dialogue and characterizations of everyone. The romantic partners are wildly different and all feel authentic, as in: They have their own goals, motivations and developments. Even your bystander cousin and your (if you opt-in) parental figure have distinct personalites I couldn't help but want to see more of- there's discussions of depression, of discovering yourself, of societal expectations regarding gender expression and it felt very diagetic and "this is this one person's opinion" instead of a lecture on how to do stuff, applicable to All People- you can freely choose what gender or sexuality you are (but the game is a bit weird on letting you express the latter, see "the negative" below)- the music is a vibe (I have not much clue about music, but I liked it, it felt very fitting for the setting)- as I've mentioned above: The stalker character.  Afterwards, there's more positive interactions with all the other characters and the game finally starts dropping hints and comments that the stalker's actions are messed up, so I felt more comfortable going forward. And I'm glad I did, because this game has a lot of good scenes where characters with anxiety or depression express their thoughts in ways I had not considered before, and I am glad for getting this experience. But I was really thinking about quitting this game . Which is a shame, because all the gripes I had, the games addresses eventually.- the dungeons are kinda boring. Combat isn't hard and after you've figured out how to play every weapon, the game becomes really easy- you cannot tell the game what your sexuality is beforehand, you can only choose in the moment. Which, I think, is a pretty great idea for factoring in that not everyone is always down for everything, but then the game also jumps ahead and makes conclusions like "You don't want to engage in sex on your nth date with this person? I guess you dislike sex then and I'll make this personwho asks to spend the night specify that they do it on the couch, far away from you."And then you get a tiny sad smiley from that character, sort of disappointed but NOT judging you, that you didn't want to have sex with them on that night (and for the rest of eternity, as the game presumes). Pro-tip: Track the PC's actions across multiple playthroughs, not just the one romance route they're currently playing. Also let us actually say aloud if we hate sex or not etc., please.I've ranted a lot about my perceived inadequecies of this game above, but I want to state: I recommend this game, whole-heartedly. I went into it expecting a whacky, campy, gay dungeon crawler, but then I also found glimpses into depression in ways and especially sensitity I had never expected it to address. This game made me tear up and reconsider how I have and will handle other people. If that isn't an indication of empathetic quality, I don't know what is.If you get this game: Go into it expecting it to be cute and then have your world shaken just the tiniest, good bit.

_childDocuments_.review: It's hard to know if this is a visual novel or a very light twin-stick slasher - there's a strong "what if Hades but way less roguey and way more dating" vibe! But whatever it is, I had fun.It's pretty short - I finished it in maybe nine hours? - and you'll only see four tile sets, six? monster sets and three bosses. That doesn't *sound* hugely replayable, but I'm still replaying it. Also, there is apparently DLC in the works.On the VN side: Everyone is bisexual, and it's notably not just "playersexual" in a couple cases. There's also some explicitly polyamorous characters (and "Mom" is supportive, if you tell her you're dating multiple people, "as long as you're honest and on the same page dearie" iirc). Dating options: three guys, one gal, two enbies, and one cat (cat route best route!) You can keep it platonic and still get the achievements.On the combat side: The weapons all feel nicely different, and there's some combos to learn - though I'm  more of a buttonmasher than a careful combo considerer, and I still got through. You do have to use each weapon to its strengths - e.g. the estoc has a unique 'block' ability you need to remember, or you'll have trouble getting mobbed when using it.Overall - it *does* feel a bit short for the price, but part of that is how refreshingly low grind it is. I definitely think I got value for my money and value for my time. Do recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: What do you get when you mix a dating sim, a roguelike dungeon crawler, a mystery, psychological baggage, and anthropomorphized weapons? Clearly, the creators of this game were set on finding out. This game is just . It's not too challenging, not too stressful, and not too serious, but still holds your attention with an entertaining (if kind of bananas) premise and enjoyable, easy-to-learn combat. You play as [insert your own character name here], a young [woman/man/enby--choose your pronouns] who is visiting Verona Beach to stay with their cousin for a summer. You have crippling anxiety over dating, something you've never done before. So your cousin sets you up with a few dates, but you find yourself falling for weapon-people: which are exactly what they sound like. But, lo and behold: you're a wielder! You take up the hobby of bringing your dates to the "dunj," where you can fight off monsters that take the form of your own insecurities. But something is happening to the weapon-people you find: many of them have mysteriously gone missing and turned up in random spots in the dunj. Can you solve the mystery while battling your inner demons  having the best summer flings of your life?That answer is yes. Yes times seven. (Well... six + a cat.)You should absolutely play Boyfriend Dungeon. It was a great 15 hours. Alas, summer's over far too soon.

_childDocuments_.review: A very good dating sim and a decent dungeon crawler/rogue like. Most or all the characters are very entertaining and likeable. Throughout my entire playthrough I never dislike any of the characters unless it was intended (talking about you ERIC). The dungeon crawling has a variety of weapons with different combos and strengths that can be expended depending on which character you go out with the most. You also unlock new swords by progressing through dungeons which adds more playstyles to experiment with. I also like how the game focuses on repressed emotions and developing the main character throughout the dungeon with the monster designs and environments layouts. Through the halfway mark this aspect of the game does get repetitive and tedious as most of the weapons have been unlocked, enemies generally stay the same level, and no new mechanics are introduced. I feel that the playtime for the game being around 10 hours could be extended to add more content for the story and the overall pacing of the game. The visuals are great and the cutscenes of getting a new sword are a pleasure to watch. Although I do wish they add more portraits for some of the characters for more expressive scenes. The music when going through dungeons and dating characters is a groove, with the vocals being the cherry on top of it. This game has already a lot of potential and I am eager to play more if more content is introduced and I will update this review if things have improved or not. Overall the game is fun and would recommend it if you're into dating sims. Also Valeria is the best.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this publisher - and last year I saw they were in progress for a dating sim I was excited! the kinda bombastic world of dating your weapons? neat! lets go!Positives first  1. Some character introductions are even so aggressive to the player character I would in reality never speak to these people again. To give an example I don't want to go into each characters break down but each one is like someone took a common dating sim trope and created a whole plot about how that isn't actually a fun/sexy person to interact with. nothing like a game full of people that feel like life lessons. now for the lesser negative points  1. The game is painfully short for $20 - there are only two dungeons and 6 levels/ dates with each love interest 2. While the reactions for friendship (yellow hearts) and love reactions (pink/red hearts) are clear I would like clearer dialog to follow friendship or love paths - some dialog options just 2 choices between unknown positive response vs negative response  3. If I were to change anything it would be - changing the dungeons to not reflect the PCs inner fears but reflecting the inner fears of the love interests so you could learn more about them - also then there would be at least one dungeon per love interest! rather than just the two

_childDocuments_.review: So originally I wish-listed this sucker for lonely b!#% reasons. And eagerly waited while desperately looking for other games to fill the void.Trying the game out after all the waiting was as fulfilling as getting a penny trick or treating as a kid. (Seriously Screw people that do that!) Characters and dates The art (janky in places) and animation is nice but I couldn't care less how pretty something when character development doesn't exit. I guess if you have time to kill and money to burn this might be a reasonable purchase but there are so many visual novels out there you can get (especially on those juicy sales) that'll give you hours upon hours of meaningful, memorable content and they are often pretty too. It's harder to find LGBTQ+ friendly polished work but that doesn't mean you should settle for mediocre. Oh about the stalker warning. It's a topic that's meant to be uncomfortable. I don't mind tense and traumatic experiences in a game/media (Psychological thriller/horror manga and Berserk fan enters chat) but if you dislike that sort of thing it's an unavoidable part of the story. And your character deals with it and typical fashion for them in almost every situation they are in - doormat. No matter what your illusion of choice is you often don't do much.I had a rough time relating to the mc and immersing myself. That's the reason I play a game where I can name my character. I enjoy placing myself in their shoes and I hoped there would be a variety to our options. Usually are shoehorned into what the story wants you to do. You have the illusion of choice. Make a choice that's wildly different from what the story wants - nope not allowed. Want characters to back off because you are uninterested? They'll nod, smile and keep hitting on you. I dabble in the video game harem lifestyle so while I'm cool with hoarding a bunch of romantic interests like Pokemon I send off into Mortal Kombat  it may not be your cup of tea. You'll feel like constantly bonking every mofo that bats their eyes at you.Combat is brain-dead. I love the overcoming your insecurities aspect of the dunji but it's so bland. You have 2 whole dunjis...so if you wanted more crawling in your dungeon get your fix elsewhere. Characters are very one-note, cliche and flat. I tried to force myself to play more (About 5hrs) with the Xbox pass but just couldn't. If you're looking for half-assed fan-fiction quality of depth then fine get this on a heavy discount or keep an eye out for news. Apparently there will be another character coming in but if it's in the same boring formula, no more dunji's are added with the same lack of lore and no actual  ...this stays refunded and a distant meh memory.

_childDocuments_.review: A B/G/NBxB/G/NB dating sim/dungeon crawler where you play as an individual (you get to choose pronouns and appearance) visiting your cousin's place for the summer in an attempt to gain some confidence in dating. To gain that confidence you have to literally fight your fears inside dungeons using a cast of conveniently single human-weapons. While I did enjoy playing this game for the most part, it ultimately feels like it was released in an unfinished state. There are a lot of great ideas here, but none of them are fully executed to the extent that I believe they should or could be.There are 7 romance/friendship options available: 1 female, 4 male, and 2 nonbinary. As far as I can tell each romance/friendship only has one ending and the overall story has a single ending. There might be different endings for friendship vs romance but I couldn't really determine which characters were on which ending if that was the case. It took me about 8 hours in total to complete all romance/friendships, both dungeons, and the main story.If there was a neutral rating for reviews I'd use it for this game. Since that doesn't exist, I'm going to be optimistic and give it a thumbs up based on what it could become in future updates. I paid full price $19.99(USD) for this game, but in it's current state I'm not sure I could advise spending that much on it. Perhaps wait for a sale or for more content to be added/updated first.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a cute little dungeon crawler and dating simulator I had fun with for the few hours it took me to play it through.Even though I'm not that good at dungeon crawlers it wasn't frustratingly difficult, so, for me, it has well balanced encounters. I got behind the combinations the different swords have, which also have different focuses regarding range, attack/defense, etc. But the combinations aren't so different that I had to remember a lot of combinations, at which I'm bad at. I'm usually a button smasher in these types of games, but in this one I wasn't so uncoordinated with the combinations after a while (I prefered gamepad over keyboard). Finding the zines and clothes didn't feel like work, but is just something that happens alongside. Some of the zines  I found a bit annoying, but I didn't have to choose them.Other than the title might suggest, you can romance and/or befriend sword characters of different genders. Each of the characters has their own arc. I liked all of the sword characters, some more than others, but the cat, Pocket, is my absolute favorite one, regarding fighting style as well as plot-wise: he protec, but he also attac. That the different answering-options indeed make a difference in how your relationship with the character unfolds is integral and well-made. The overall plot is good too. You get a content note for stalking, emotional manipulation, and domestic abuse before the start of the game. You have three different pronoun options (she/he/they) in your character creation and I deemed the varieties of possible styles for my character to be adequate to create a .I had a few problems in that I wasn't able to launch the game through steam, so I didn't get all achievements or only a random few, but I was able to resolve the problem by playing around with the compatability settings. This is why I played it again and, tbh, I hadn't as much fun the second time. I think with a bit more experience the dungeons and the dates felt a bit tedious and the music, which is good, became repetetive and annoyed me a bit. So for me it's more like a one time game. Or I just need a bit more time between replays. I'm still looking forward to the new sword characters though, one of which is already teased at.It's cute, it's fun, it's quite wholesome, it's queer, so it's right up my alley. ^^

There's a fair amount of characters to date (and subsequently weapons to murder VHS tapes with) but they only have 6 love levels, meaning they only have 6 events where you get more story around them. You don't get enough time to spend with weapons as I'd like, and you get love levels so fast it feels like a blur (Especially after getting your first romance completed).I wish there was more game here. Maybe a third dungeon and more levels for you to get to with your partners. But overall it's still a damn good experience. Just a rather light one that leaves you feeling like there should've been more there that you could've done.

_childDocuments_.review: The over-the-top, insane, steamy, sensational fantasy of this game is not romancing the hot vampire sword guy or the uber famous k-pop idol, it's living in a sane world where people are generally nice and treat each other with basic kindness and respect regardless of your sexuality or gender. Combine that with having a mother that loves you unconditionally and an entire village that cares about your emotional well-being and I was hooked.Partially kidding, but I truly did not want the game to end and was kind of sad to wave goodbye to Verona Beach. Even if the romances aren't that deep and the tropes were... well tropes... the game made me feel "normal" and happy in a world that always wants me to feel lesser for being my authentic self. This game is so committed to this that you can even change your pronoun selection during your playthrough without it being a world ending event. I started the game with one set of pronouns and ended with another and the game never comments on it being a big deal, everyone immediately understands and no questions are asked and it doesn't limit your dating pool. There's even two non-binary romance options with Sawyer and Rowan. Sure some of the enby stereotypes are a bit over the top and dated but I think it fits with the universe and overall vibe the game was going for. Outside of dating and romance, the game itself is actually surprisingly fun. It manages to find that "just right" Goldilocks spot of not too challenging but not so easy that it's a total cake walk. There can be a grind to it if you want that and that's how I played because I wanted to 100% it, but you don't have to do it that way if you don't want to. Overall a super fun, cute, lighthearted experience that lightly touches on some important themes like fears of intimacy and change.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to say up front that this game is a blast to play and as someone coming from a perspective of never playing a roguelike before -- this is a fun introduction and a great time overall -- with a few downsides. The story and dating sim aspects are very fun, if a little short. I loved how grinding in the dunj to raise your love rank so that  you can unlock more dates with whatever weapons you are using gives motivation to play the roguelike half of the game more. HOWEVER, I really really wish there were more than 6 love levels. Only having 5 dates mean that you progress very quickly and after 3 hours, my first run through the story was already over.
