_childDocuments_.review: This isn’t a complete do not recommend but more YMMV.Overall it’s a well thought out game with a good idea but I didn’t find myself enjoying it and wanted it to be over more than I wanted to keep trying to make it work for me.Combat: Felt to weightless and I didn’t feel like attacks or even dodging had any impact to it. That made a little difficult to get into the zone when in combat.I ended up prioritising who could get me through the dungeon and mobs the fastest rather than trying to get more use to the combat. Which doesn't sound bad, but I wasn't enjoying the encounters at all. The enemies are not particularly difficult but since combat didn't feel good it wasn't fun to play.I also forgot about the books half the time and rarely used them in combat until I was panic button mashing in a challenge room.Dating: Everyone seemed pushy/forward from minute 0. Other dating games start out with your candidates being more neutral toward you and it gets built up to romance or friendship route. But since everyone in this game, including your mom, starts out on a mission to get you dating all interactions = romance?Even the dialogue options that seemed more friendship (or flat out rejection) get you romance responses.At least for the first 3 (4?? If stalker lad is an option) I wish stuff started more casual. The dates and interactions feel forced, even more so when I choose “this is not a date” options. It felt  like working in reverse, instead of building up a relationship to romance I’ve got to convince them I just want to be friends.But I also was not a fan of the first available candidates. I ended up wanting to be their friends instead. A lot of their dialogue ignored my attempts at “let’s just be friends”….but that’s also probably because those options mostly trigger more pink/red hearts and rarely the yellow ones. That made it difficult to enjoy since I was trying to reject/neutral them and they stayed flirty at every turn.Even though I was interested in finding out about the other available candidates, I couldn’t stand the interactions with the first 3 and dreaded any dates. Dates are required for weapon level progression so I couldn't get away from them if I wanted. I was annoyed through most of my short playthrough and didn't want to keep going to meet the other candidates or unravel the story.Also, as nice as the game is to give you a warning about some aggressive interactions (à la stalker lad) his interactions and any extended dialogue with him is stressful and tanked the game experience for me by a lot. You may want to watch an LP or play with a friend first to get a good feel if you’ll be comfortable having to interact with this guy. Especially since he is also one of the shop owners. Though his shop dialogue is neutral-ish and (so far) you can get what he sells via dungeon grind instead.Other:- I kinda wish there was a day/night cycle. As far as I know you only sleep once and from then on it’s just go out into the overworld whenever you want and hit up shops or dungeon. I think it would help the pacing for when you go on dates. Especially when the dialogue is see you tomorrow or this evening, but it doesn’t match up with when you can go do activities. But characters will text you when a location is available to visit for an activity, most of the time the unlock is instant.- Navigating the overworld with your avatar seems unnecessary? Personally just cycling through buildings with a list or bright outlining the location you want to go would be just fine and simpler.- Too many text. I was getting overwhelmed with how much the characters text you. Going home I just wanted to see what I could craft or try on new clothes but the text were so much. There was a little downtime to not text but it just felt like a lot happening and waiting for them to finishing typing to see if you can respond or not.I don’t know if I could have just left people on read or if they’d continue to text you if you were in the overworld or dungeon. _childDocuments_.review: I left this game feeling very mixed. I really enjoyed most of it, but it feels like the beta version or play test of a game rather than a completed game. Starting with the areas without issue, the music is very solid, the zines are all fun to use, the crafting is excellent, and the enemies are all really fun to fight for the most part. Next, the problems. The combat, while fun at times, has so many interesting ideas that feel almost finished. Out of all the weapons, the only one that feels finished in combat is the dagger. Every other weapon lacks combos or synergy with it's abilities. The axe for example has only two combos which get boring really quickly.  Leveling up also feels lackluster when all you gain is health and monster damage scaling causes that extra health to be unremarkable. A stamina system or character abilities would make each level feel more impactful. Finally, there is no wave mechanic to stagger monsters spawning in and add extra strategy to combat. Monsters spawn in all at once and are mainly difficult because they swarm you.Then there's the dating sim side. Though the story is mostly fleshed out, it doesn't feel like you have much of an impact on it. Rather than having a major impact on how the story plays out, the story happens to you with you only getting to choose which parts play out around you. Each character is fairly flat, with a few exceptions, and any of the dialog choices you make don't seem to make an impact on the story. You can give people gifts, but there is no in game system to track their likes. Though such a system is not needed as each character's likes are extremely basic and easy to guess. The cat gets the cat toys, the surfer the surfboard, the business man the cuff links, and so on. Those things wouldn't be big problems if any of the character's were fun to date. The minimal voice acting and lack of diverse character sprites results in you seeing and hearing everything pertaining to a character after an hour or so. On top of that, the dates are all boring, predictable, or cheesy in a bad way as it feels like minimal effort was put into the writing. A final thing to add is the lack of character customization. While the clothing options are all fun and there are plenty of them, there's a disappointing lack of hair styles and no way to customize your body type outside of gender. All in all, I enjoyed my first play through, but won't be playing Boyfriend Dungeon again and can't recommend it. If you can get it half off like I did then it might be worth it for a lot of people, but there are also finished games you can get for the same price. Go spend that money on something like Cosmic Wheel Sisterhood or a better dating sim.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game, I truly did, but I just... didn't.I love dating sims with wacky premises. I love dungeon crawlers with rogue-lite elements. I'm VERY gay.But the writing in this game was just... not good. I didn't feel connected with any of the characters in any meaningful way. Most of them had a single one-note 'problem' that wasn't really explored in enough depth to make an impact on me.The only one I liked even a little was Hato Moa's doing, and that just made me wish I was playing Hatoful Boyfriend again instead. This is very much a personal taste thing, but all of these characters were too damn nice, and the only exceptions to that were: 1. a guy who stalks you. 2. the bisexual bad boy who only wants sex archetype. Neither of which do it for me. Robert from Dream Daddy did and subverted the latter with way better writing and more complexity. Where's my gay weirdos?Aside from that, there's only two dungeons in a game that's supposed to be equally about dungeon crawling AND dating. Once your character gets even mildly powerful the dungeons are completely trivial and basically a repetitive chore you have to do to get more story content. Combat isn't particularly deep. Having to use weapons I hated just to see their dates was annoying. The art style in the Dungeons is also completely different from the rest of the game and not in a way I like - I'm not expecting mind-blowing hand animated 2D art, but I would like it to remind me less of goofy party games when the 2D art in the game is so gorgeous. Yeah, the art's nice. Can definitely say that. Backgrounds are pretty, 2D animations are beautiful, portraits of the characters are visually lovely. But it absolutely cannot save this game from being a 'kind of okay in parts, wouldn't recommend'.TL;DR: Just buy Hatoful Boyfriend if you want a dating sim with a wacky premise that has deep characters and emotional writing in it. Just buy Hades if you want a dungeon crawler where you also get to date. This is less than both.

_childDocuments_.review: So I loved this game but I feel expectations need to be set in order for people to enjoy it:Difficulty is low so if you're someone that enjoys games like Elden Ring and Dark Souls this will maybe be boring for you.The sickly sweetest and earnestness of the games writing may also alienate people that don't go in expecting it, or just don't enjoy that kind of writing.Its also very very short, which the free-DLC should fix by adding an extra dungeon, but even then the free-DLC is only going to bump it up from 13 to maybe 17 hours of content.I do not care about this cause I have barely any free time to play games and 20 hour games pretty much suit the time I have available, but if you expect or enjoy long-ass games then this will disappoint you.The game also likes to have its cake and eat it to.There is the escapism of having 7 (soon to be 10) ultra-hot, ultra-charming, gender-diverse, polyamorous bisexuals (including a K-pop and a SPOILER) all romantically pursuing consistently and respectfully, initiating dates with you so you don't have to do that labour or try gage whether its okay or appropriate for you to initiate with them.And then also your being stalked and harassed. And then also you have one random date where the person isn't interested you just to remind you how 99% of your dates go in your real life. And then one character breaks up with you on reaching "Max Love".I'm not against any of this, it just feels really dissonant as it breaks the escapist vibe. The underlying message the game carries regarding relationships needing to be built on trust and vulnerability is important and it requires the stalker plot-line and instances of rejection to hit home. I just think the writers maaaaaybe needed to polish the scripts a bit more as there are tonal shifts in the game that (while do not justify the outrage and harassment that has been generated from it) are genuinely very upsetting.BUT - if you understand all these things going into it and still are interested in playing it then most likely you will also love this game. Great characters, great story, great art and designs, great game play. It basically succeeds at all the core things it attempts to be.FYI - Rowan is the best character in the game, make sure to visit the mansion in the top-right corner of the map after the 4th of July barbacue or you'll miss them.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a little strange to review but I will definitely try my best to encapsulate everything it seems to offer. Here are a few key points I made note of as well as a list of pros and cons in general! Hope this helps! This point is pretty tough to describe as the writing in the game does many things well and almost an equal amount of things wrong. First off, a lot of the interactions are weirdly both meaningful and shallow at the same time. It really feels like the writers wanted to make the interactions more realistic and deep but barely scratched the surface in their execution of it. This point is shown even more through the characters themselves as (once again) they are clearly very fleshed out in the creators minds' but unfortunately it does not seem to convey that way in its final execution. If I had to choose one phrase to define the writing it would be this: lots of potential, not a lot of results. The gameplay is very simple and relatively well-executed. This is an example of great execution but not a lot of creative thinking unfortunately. By no means is the dungeon crawling poor in my experience with it, but I did find myself constantly wanting more and knowing the team could have gone so much further had they taken more time and been a little more ambitious with the system. It always felt like there was a certain flair that was missing to it after the first few levels. Redundancy is not the worst thing to feel in a game, but it certainly does not help a game either. Ultimately, the dungeon-crawling is a very fun system with great mechanics and great execution, but could definitely have done more to differentiate itself and live up to its full potential. This was yet again a hot and cold situation for me. While I enjoyed most of the characters and believe almost all are very unique and clever (especially for a dating sim; i.e. the cat character is literally a cat), I also wanted a more characters in general. The cast is relatively small for my tastes. Perhaps the bigger issue for some is the pacing of a character's arrival. After 4 hours, I was still being introduced to new potential dates. While I personally liked the idea of some more spread out pacing so you can really learn more about a couple characters before choosing to move on to others or not, it will definitely be a turn-off for some people. I got somewhat "lucky" in that my favorite potential date was introduced very early for me (Valeria) which really helped to keep me engaged early on. This game really struggles to be a "dating sim" at times as the player rarely makes any real meaningful decisions when it comes to dating the weapons. In a game where the writers clearly wanted a more realistic dating approach, I was surprised at how even the worst answers just led to a successful date by the end of it all. Again, this is not to say the dating sim part of it is bad, but more so it was a massive missed opportunity that could have tied into the gameplay and made the game more challenging (where it can struggle at times). Ultimately, this game had so much potential and I was thoroughly excited to play it! Unfortunately, the game does not live up to its full potential. All is not lost however, as the execution of most of the game is very well done and it was clearly crafted with a lot of passion all things considered. PROS-Very unique characters-Fun dialogue-Well-executed dungeon-crawling-Great character designs-More realistic dating and characters (you know, with actual flaws)CONS-Many missed opportunities to better the game-Lack of meaningful choices in the dating sim portion of the game-Could have executed some of the writing a little better on certain portions of the game-Gameplay CAN get somewhat repetitive and redundant after awhile (particularly in long sessions)-A couple other characters would have gone a long way7/10 (Above average, and one I would still recommend for players who already enjoy dating sims and/or dungeon crawlers, but not many others.)

_childDocuments_.review: At present, I am very happy with this game. It is exactly what I have been looking for for years. Meaning that your waifu won't freak out when holding hand, but instead might even wanna head down to freak town on the first date. And as much as I love anime, Japanese culture, and visual novels, it is refreshing to break away from those archetypes and troupes, to a more western style'd game. I really like how flawed some of the characters are, to the point where you may not even like them until you get to know them. They feel like real people. Really thirsty people. The soundtrack is also banging. The combat is tight and snappy. You know you've got good combat when rolling just feels great to do.I am sure a lot of people will inevitably compare this game to Hades, and while it has similarities, this title has been in the works years before that game came out. _childDocuments_.review: It’s summer vacation and your absolutely amazing cousin Jessie is offering up his old apartment room rent-free for you to stay at while he and his fiancé live together and prep for their summer wedding! Verona is a gorgeous town with malls, museums, art studios, a college and cat cafes! Capulet Beach is a popular tourist spot with the Verona Lighthouse as a scenic landmark, and best of all, there are dungeons! The three dungeons are super popular dating locations between wielders and weapons, to clarify… people who wield weapons and people who transform into weapons. This summer, it’s time to be brave, step out of your comfort zone, identify your fears and literally fight them head on as you dive deep into the Labyrinths! 5-11 hours to complete, Boyfriend Dungeon is a Roguelike Dungeon Crawler that’s also a VN and LGBTQ+ friendly with non-binary options. There are 3 procedurally generated dungeons and 10 dating options  that can turn into various weapon types that leave a lot of room for creative and diverse playstyles that you can level up and unlock new skills! There are also plenty of customization options and outfits to wear, things to craft, and skill books to use. The music is notably made by Marksye and songstress Madeliene McQueen and is honestly really good to dungeon with. I only really have two complaints. Let me mute my phone! I get it! You have a lot of dating options. That’s great. But when you step out of a dungeon and you have like, 9 people blowing up your phone trying to get your attention and set up dates it just makes me not want to come out. This is made significantly worse by accepting the “Encouraging texts from mom” option when you start the game, which you can’t turn off unless you make a new game btw, who absolutely has no idea what moderation or personal space means. My phone was constantly popping off and it drove me ******* NUTS. Secondly, not everyone is super comfortable with polyamory! I only tried to date like, 2 people and one of them I decided I didn’t like later on, but I ended up pulling like, 6. If you don’t immediately tell the other person on the first date that you just wanna be friends, I think you just straight up get locked into the romance route; which is a bit terrible because at that point you literally do not know anything except a brief summary and first impression of the other person.

_childDocuments_.review: Boyfriend Dungeon is a gem of a game where you face your inner fears and dungeon crawl your way to romancing not just beautiful people, but the very weapons you're relying on to stay alive as you forge meaningful relationships with them.You choose your pronouns (she/her, he/him, they/them) which doesn't impact your relationship choices and can dress your avatar any way you want from dresses to suits or costumes. There's a fair range of skin tones, hair colors, and hair styles (curly, short, long, bun, kinky, etc.)When it comes to capturing hearts, options include 3 males, 1 non-human male, 1 female, and two non-binary characters. (Additional 1 male and 1 female to be added in the future). The characters are sincerely interesting with hopes and flaws that left me looking forward to more after each interaction. Boyfriend Dungeon shares the good and the bad of not just romance, but many kinds of relationships. And you'll see  reaching the end of your summer in Verona Beach is just so bittersweet. Gameplay is roguelite with generated dungeons, monsters, and treasure, but forgiving with the ability to jump to certain levels you've already reached and no other progress lost. You can make combat easier for more casual play via settings and wearing a hat with 1 extra benefit (more healing items, more damage, extra life, etc.) or unequip the hat to maintain pressure in your hack-and-slashing. The ability to swap weapons between floors reduces grinding and lets you try different weapons often - highly appreciated! Each weapon has its own quirks & fighting style where you make some choices how the ability changes (stunning versus more damage, bigger area of effect or more targets, etc.). The weapons' fighting styles change when you increase intimacy by experiencing the dungeon with them, giving gifts, and going on dates. What I appreciated is that not all relationships were forced to be romantic and I could choose to be friends with a character rather than kiss and romance everyone. Besides lovely art for the characters - including captivating animated transformation scenes for all the weapons - the game's soundtrack is a great one! I do wish the game were longer, as I did 100% the game in about 10 hours. However for the price I am satisfied. The game only has two dungeons with less than 15 floors in each. I understand the monsters in the dungeon are currently about the main character, but it would have been nice to have additional dungeons related to the other characters' fears and anxieties to get even a little deeper into their stories surrounding commitment, grief, independence, validation, etc. For example, I thought the second dungeon would be related to Sunder in a deeper way (but was mistaken) and would like to see more dunj appear in other locations related to some of the weapons.Overall I highly recommend the game and I'm very excited for the additional characters coming in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr Get Boyfriend Dungeon for the Boyfriends, not the Dungeons. 7.5/10Boyfriend Dungeon is great. Like a warm hug.If you think a simple dungeon crawler where you get to progress a relationship with a character by wielding them as your weapon in battle sounds interesting, don't be afraid to try it.The hand drawn introduction animations for the characters are gorgeous, the art style for character portraits is unique and different, and the game tackles romancing people in a way I've never seen before, and I'm more than grateful for the option to just be platonic with them. However, there are some drawbacks, mostly technical.- The combat is probably the game's weakest point. It's hard to explain, but it doesn't feel 'tight' enough. There certainly isn't a delay in input, but it feels somewhat sluggish at some points.- Smoothly flying through the dungeons fighting enemies is sometimes tripped up by awkward obstacles in rooms and unnecessary feeling walls.- The dungeons start out difficult, then when you get a few levels on your character, it becomes painfully easy.- Despite the weapons all having different mechanics, ultimately it feels like you're smacking around enemies with the same thing, just reskinned. (This doesn't carry over to the characters in each weapon though, thank goodness.) ps. pocket is best cat.

_childDocuments_.review: Short and sweet visual novel with an excellent soundtrack. The art is lovely, the characters are fun, and the combat is expressive if somewhat simple. The main event here is--perhaps unsurprisingly--the visual novel elements. It's light, breezy, sincere, and funny. The uses of text messaging as an intro and outro to the various date scenes is excellent and the game gives you a lot of control over when you engage with the dungeon and the various characters keeping the games pacing largely up to you. Don't go in expecting some sort of torrid relationship simulator that tests your ability to guess what the characters (or the writer) are thinking. Everyone's here to have a good time with or without the main character, and your interactions are part of that not a challenge or obstacle for the player.While the writing is largely interested--like the soundtrack--in good times and chill vibes, there's a creepy stalker fellow who turns up as a foil of the supportive supporting cast. It gets darker than I expected, but unless you're particularly sensitive to themes of stalking and incel rhetoric it shouldn't detract. I'm not sure how much the game benefits from going there, but the tones are blended well enough that it didn't strike me as a jarring misstep either.In principle, combat forms the other half of the game. In practice, it feels like less than half regardless of time commitment. Combat is fine. The game has the decency to stop before the simplicity of combat overstays its welcome though some of the late-game weapon upgrades are a lot more powerful than the enemy simplicity really deserves--it doesn't feel quite as good to go ham with late-game Pocket or Rowan as it would with a more sophisticated opposition and just adding health or damage to existing enemies wouldn't fix this. Dodging isn't quite effective enough and attacks can cancel all projectiles so its more about timing when you push into a crowd of enemies than movement or attack execution. Within the simple framework, each of the weapons has a reasonable amount of personality in combat--they require different footwork (WASD work?) and expose you to different amounts of risk even if they create unique tactics. Making any bumps in this road more palatable is the insertion of VN "hangout" scenes into the dungeons--they can be ignored if you've seen a particular location/weapon scene combo before and they add a nice breather and a reminder of the game's strengths that keeps the combat feeling a little fresher than it might otherwise.The soundtrack is also fantastic.

_childDocuments_.review: I understand the controversy of the premise of this game.Storyline was hit or miss, depending on your perspective. I found the games progression to be pretty simple. You can max out your characters pretty easily in the game before progressing to the end of the actual story. I ended up maxing mine out that way at least. The gameplay was fairly straightforward, in the beginning I expected to be overwhelmed a lot more but it wasn't as bad as I thought it would be. For people looking for a challenge, I wouldn't add this to your wishlist, its definitely a more casual type of game. The characters you meet are robust and distinct in both their personalities and abilities. The game doesn't make it as clear whether or not your romances affect your endgame... but I can say, it doesn't seem to affect it much. I kinda wish it did so I could have made different choices. You can gift items to your characters also, but it didn't seem necessary since I maxed the characters out and still had presents I could have given away.The music is awesome, and the reason I ended up clocking 10 hours into the game. It doesn't take nearly as long as I put into it, I just found myself listening to the soundtrack in the background as I browsed the net. Sounds and such, like attacks were fine and felt weighted enough so no complaints there.The graphics were alright, I definitely enjoyed the introduction animations for each character you meet. The end animation was pretty great to see also, slightly bittersweet.I think the best part of this game for me was the mixture of gameplay with visual novel. It allowed for a slightly more diverse type of game. Now as for the controversial stalking, Yes there is stalking in the game and no it is not horrifically excessive. However it is there and it is understandable for anyone who has been in a situation where that may have happened to them, it can be uncomfortable and I probably wouldn't recommend someone with that issue to bother with the game.For those who haven't and are looking for a simple game to sink some time into, I'd recommend this game to them.Overall rating 7.5/10. Needed more content and more weight to your choices to get a higher score from me.

_childDocuments_.review: Been waiting for this ever since the Kickstarter, and it did not disappoint! It's innovative and different, as well as feeling very, very real in the character interactions. I also adored how each character fits in a dating game trope box, but is also unique enough with their own little quirks and personalities. Two mechanics in the game really stick out to me and were wonderful as a player (and as a perfectionist!): 1) Polyamory is totally accepted, and there's no jealousy mechanic or anything similar (Isaac scared me when he said I would have to 'make a choice', but it was for his story, not the game, so no worries there!) and 2) You can also just be friends and go on friendly dates with the characters--no strings attached! Definitely going to be playing again to see everyone's full date and/or friend route, and I would recommend this wholeheartedly to everyone who loves dating games and wants something a little bit new and a little bit different.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: This game is SO MUCH FUN! If you even just remotely enjoy anything in the direction dating-sim and/or dungeon-crawl, you will enjoy this game!So, I've just got this game on 100% (with the steam achievements, my wielder lvl ain't maxed out yet, but psht!) and honestly? I thought it was about time to write a review.Playing the game through twice so far only confirmed my impression that Boyfriend Dungeon is so much fun and way better than I imagined when I first got it in the Kitfox collection that was on sale a few weeks/months back. I was already intruiged when I saw that there were more romance option than just some dudes but I didn't know there were nonbinary romance options too, which was a very pleasent surprise.I like the characters a lot, all of them. They're all unique in their own way and so much fun to be around! They don't feel bland and the backstories everyone has feels believable (to a degree, it's a funky game where people can turn into weapons after all).But it's not only the Weapons! But the "background" characters too! The MCs cousin for example is a sweetheart and while some characters are on the more annoying side, they are designed to be that way. And even if they are, they still have some sort of detailed-ness about them so that they don't feel... one dimensional, if you know what I mean.The trigger warnings at the beginning are an important addition and should be considered before playing and the fact that the game asks us if messages by someone called "mom" are okay is phenomenal too!These little details (asking for consent, the option to chose between platonic and romantic attraction, the fact we can chose they/them pronouns, polyamorous relationships etc. etc.) make this game phenomenal, plus the intuitive and easy gameplay make it a wonderful game to play casually!So, all-in-all, a truly amazing experience.I am very hyped for the DLC Kitfox announced a while back and will definetely keep an eye on the studio in the future.with kind regards,a queer person <333

_childDocuments_.review: The devs did a good job of making an enticing story to accompany the concept of a dungeon-crawling dating sim. I don't think people realise the character development for each character, including yourself (except maybe Jesse): it's very well-written. There's a focus on boundary setting and regulation which is something I appreciate. You can see that primarily in Rowan (Scythe) and Sunder's (Talwar) stories, where they attempt to establish a boundary with the player or take accountability for the fact that they made a mistake which could have overstepped your own boundaries. It's not specific to certain characters but those were the instances that stood out to me and it's something that really made me appreciate the game even more.Other than that, I really appreciate the inclusion of non-binaries in the player customization as well as the characters, Rowan and Sawyer (I may have missed a few others but they are the mains). I also noticed the headscarf and turban in the character customization: a suggestion I'd have is to make those a hairstyle as opposed to a hat. Aside from the hats that offer full-coverage for their hair like the Fox Hood, a lot of the people that want to wear a headscarf will have to sacrifice it in-game in order to reap the benefits of the hat that they want to wear. I know it's a lot that the devs would have to work on just to accommodate the hats to the headscarf and the turban but I do think it helps with the inclusion of these people that wear them on their day-to-day (and want to wear them in-game). I thoroughly enjoyed the graphics, art, and just everything in between. This game is so beautiful and there's a nice attention to detail in all of the explore-able places, as well as a careful consideration to the player's interaction with it. The dungeons aren't extremely difficult but they are challenging enough to do where it still feels stimulating even if you're maxed out on all of the swords. The inclusion of supporting characters like Olivia really helped with aiding the storyline (as supporting characters are intended) and providing a laugh: when Olivia was offended about the player and Seven being out together, I thought it was so funny (although, there is a lesson in that story for her to learn). All-in-all, a really well-done game and I look forward to seeing what else these devs come up with!tl;dr: Worth buying the game if you're looking to play a dungeon-crawling dating sim with some smooth voice acting and cute game design. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Boyfriend Dungeon

_childDocuments_.review: A very interesting concept for a dating sim game. I loved all (well, almost all) characters. They can get a little cheesy sometimes, but each one has a lot of depth to them. The main villain can get a little.... too much exaggeratedly villainous, but the romantic options (more like relationship options, really) more than make it worthy. The main plot is a bit nonsensical and you can see the twist at the end coming from a mile away, but it is also charming in its simplicity.The gameplay is nice, the way it combines dungeon crawler and dating is refreshing. The dungeon part can get a little repetitive and too easy towards the end, though, since enemies tend to just swarm your devastating area of effect attacks, the healing items drop multiple times in the same room sometimes and you just level up too fast. I barely used my special "magazine power", since I never seemed to need it. I understand though that the main focus here is the dating part and the dialogues, and they are very well done. The gifts and the social triggers each dungeon floor really add to it.All in all, I think the only actual fault that made me a little disappointed is the length of it. It's just too short, with only two dungeons. In the end you might find yourself grinding a bit just to evolve the relationships and play through their cutscenes before the final fight.It's a very creative and decently done game with a reasonable price tag on it, so if you're a fan of dating simulators I surely recommend it. Oh, and the soundtrack is just superb, seriously.
_childDocuments_.name: Boyfriend Dungeon

_childDocuments_.review: As I thought about what to say on this game, I realized a lot of it came off as pretty negative, so I want to start by saying I enjoyed this game, and I recommend this game. I took the time (~8 hours, maybe less if you're faster than I) to get all the achievements, and I'd play more of this if it were available.I can't speak to the developer and if this really was their goal, but this game felt like an attempt to pay homage to Hades* and/or Persona 4. If one were to take Persona 4's social systems and its general idea about enemy/dungeon themes, but then try to layer them atop Hades gameplay, you might get this game. The trouble is that it doesn't do either of those two sides of the game as well as those examples. Several other action roguelikes offer sharper gameplay, especially if you're looking for any sort of challenge, and other VNs offer arguably better stories and romances.Somehow it works, though. It's a pretty short game, especially if you find a weapon you like and level it a couple times - the content becomes trivial, more of a farm than a challenge. You get several romances with a pretty varied harem across genders and styles, and a lot of it is very charming. The look and sound is solid. I finished the whole thing in two sittings.*Post-review Edit: I realized after posting this that Hades is actually a pretty poor comparison for the gameplay this offers, but had been in my head due to the weapon system, which is something it does a bit better than this game to be honest. However, I realized there's actually another Supergiant Game that this resembles more closely - Transistor, in both the themes of romancing your weapon, and in your weapon having a personality that has certain skills tied to it. I came to the conclusion that the gameplay more closely resembles someone attempting to turn Transistor's systems in to an Action Roguelike than Hades itself, despite the similarities in weapon systems.

_childDocuments_.review: Number one complaint I saw about the game in reviews was that people felt like there wasn't enough content on offer. While I can definitely say the game left me wanting more, I can't agree with that criticism. The meat of the game is in relationship building, and the dungeon delving is a nice little thing on the side. Each of the dateable characters are charming and engaging in their own way, and you're not forced to date exclusively and replay the game several times over if you want to see everyone's story. The game is LGBTQ+ friendly and it's very easy to tell characters you just want to be friends, if you'd rather explore a purely platonic relationship. Mechanically speaking, the relationship building is super low risk, you don't have to worry about min/maxing dialog choices or optimizing gifts, just spend time with them and you'll get there.My parting advice to any prospective players is to max out your favorite blade early, rather than spreading your time out amongst everyone - and to make sure to keep an eye out for a date opportunity at the big house to the northeast of town!

_childDocuments_.review: I can honestly say i regret buying this game. It was a fun 6 or so hours of my life but for as much as it costs when I'm pretty poor it was not really worth it. It's a really great concept, just really poorly executed. 2 Dungeons (I refuse to call them what they call them in the game) and a very lackluster final boss fight were done in no time. The romances/friendships felt very stilted and somewhat confusingly written. I felt very forced to only do certain things, like being at odds with one of the friends of the character i was mainly dating, for example. With another character i kept telling him to back off but when I wanted to know why he was gone for so long, out of curiosity, ingame it turned into a moment of jealousy and supposed insecurity? Suffice to say, I really did not enjoy the writing very much either. I really wanted to though. There were a few moments i loved the writing, like how sawyer was so happy to know another nonbinary person. It felt like  a real human piece of dialogue, partially because that's the kind of thing i would've said in a similar situation.One of the main parts i didn't like was when the "main antagonist" rather patronisingly called another nonbinary character an enby, and no one called him out on it for being infantalising and that grinded my gears a bit. A lot of Nonbinary people don't like being called an "enby" and while i'm not one of them i do believe its a term others can use to be infantilising and it should only be a term used when its absolutely okay by the person in question. In that vein, i just hated that the guy who said it wasn't called out. I was ok with how the "stalker" character was portrayed he was oddly the most 3 dimensional feeling character in the end. While i liked how everyone reacted to him it all still felt like it was handled rather oddly. But really, as i said before, the writing was not very enjoyable.If the characters were rewritten, made to feel more human and 3 dimensional that alone would honestly make me want to play the game again. i really did love the concept and i loved the concept of the characters too, they just really didn't feel right. More dungeon content would also be nice, but i had some misgivings with the combat albeit that might be more the fault of my controller, but it felt clunky so beware of that possibility.I read that they were planning on adding dlc/more characters. If it was free dlc or just an update, I wager it would make the game more worth it, especially if the writing improves.All in all it was an ok game with a lot of downfalls, but definitely some bits that made me smile. I can only recommend you buy the game when its on sale though if after reading this review you still think you'd enjoy the game. 6 hours and completed is not a lot of time at all for a game that costs this much.

_childDocuments_.review: Well.  As far as realism goes.  This game nails socialization.  Being overwhelmed by text messages all coming in at the same time from different people.  Having to keep track of a lot going on.  Characters having real personalities with flaws and all just the right way to make you feel uncomfortable all over the place.  Game was totally right to recommend taking breaks as needed- and I was only 48 minutes into the game before I needed one… as someone who usually binges games and books for hours at a time, I feel like that’s saying something.  Even taking breaks, it was a bit too much.  I kept struggling to figure out what to say to different characters while worrying I said the wrong thing- which is realistic as well but perhaps too realistic.  Especially since sometimes the options are ‘be rude’ ‘be even ruder’ ‘agree to something you aren’t comfortable with’ in the dialogue options.  Instant stress.  The game is… kinda heavy.  It’s not casual, mentally-emotionally speaking.  It’s a lot.  No, but, really.  This triggers social exhaustion like crazy if you’re an introvert.  That’s pretty rare for a videogame of any sort, even one that’s mostly an interactive novel.  And the content warning isn’t really enough, I don’t think.

detailed_description: You are Cahal, a powerful Garou (Werewolf) who chose to go into exile after losing control of his destructive rage. On a quest for redemption and blood, Cahal plays a crucial role in the great war between the Garou and Endron, a powerful oil company that serves the Wyrm, a destructive entity ravaging the planet. • Transform into a wolf and sneak past enemies... • Or into Crinos, a ferocious beast that can rip those enemies to shreds. • As a human, interact with people, machines, etc. • Learn new abilities through the skill tree and perform devastating combos to exterminate all your foes. • Let the rage flow through you, channelling your rage into frenzy, turning you into the ultimate killing machine A unique experience full of savage combat and mystical adventures, inspired by the famous role-playing game

short_description: You are Cahal, a powerful Garou who chose to go into exile after losing control of his destructive rage. He can transform into a wolf and a Crinos, a huge ferocious beast. Master your three forms and their powers to punish those who defile Gaia.

_childDocuments_.review: Here's the thing. I really really really wanted to give this game a thumbs up.I mean its a werewolf game where you hack and slash your way through evil corporations. Whats not to love right?Except its not like that. Not really. You mostly sneak around from level to level until you reach a certain point. Then your character, sometimes for no good reason, will get enraged and turn int oa werewolf and THEN you finally get to rip and tear your way through badguys. But if you happen to get caught sneaking around before its time to change, its game over. You don't get to change if you get caught, its just game over. I feel like that was a very poor decision.Plus the graphics only look great in the opening cutscene and during werewolf fighting scenes. FOr the rest of it the game looks really shoddy and a little sub-par.The voice acting is bland and boring and its just not very good. I mean there are some serious dramatic moments that happen to these characters but their tone of voice is like they couldn't care less.The story itself is pretty unoriginal, just another revenge plot. But the idea is original and nice. I want more werewolf games but I also want better werewolf games. When you get to actually be a werewolf and do some fighting, its pretty fun I guess. But all the other stuff around it was so boring and so grindy that I found myself more bored than anything else.Maybe wait for a big discount before buying.Thanks so much for reading and if you want some more in depth info with actual gameplay then please check out the video on my youtube channel (link below).If not then I hope I was able to help some of you out there to spend your money wisely. Thanks for reading.

_childDocuments_.review: Contrary to what some people are saying in their reviews, you *CAN* absolutely skip stealth. You are *NOT* locked into stealth, and if you just want to rip and tear your way through nearly every level in the game as a 9 foot death machine engineered specifically to murder in the name of mother earth, you absolutely can.Anyone who says you get locked into stealth hasn't played much of the game at all. After you get to the CEO of the arms dealers, you are no longer locked to stealth. Everything before this is more or less a prolonged stealth tutorial. I urge you to KEEP PLAYING past this. The game begins to shine.Granted, a lot of people's complaints are valid. The cutscenes can use work, the voice acting is only passable, and the game feels like it should've come out ten years ago. I don't believe these are reasons to skip on this one, though. There are numerous more technically impressive games that are far less enjoyable.It's a setting worth looking into, a safe (albeit dumbed down) introduction to a compelling world, especially in today's environmentally conscious climate. Showing devs that this is a setting we want to see more of is worth the time. It's not a triple A title, and it won't play or look like one. It just needs to be fun, and this is fun.So allow yourself to fill the role of the Garou. You were born and blessed by the Moon as a Warrior in a warrior's culture, into a war that has been raging for thousands of years. The enemy has poisoned humanity. They're poisoning the earth, your mother. They're killing your brothers, your sisters, your family. They turn you against your own, against yourself. They are everywhere, behind every corporate corruption, their venom bleeding through the cracks in the world. The Earth bleeds more and more each day. It is time to answer the only question remaining.When will you Rage?

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to give this game a thumbs up, but I really can't do that if I want to remain honest.TLDR: A LOT of wasted potentialPro:+ Finally a game set in my favorite pen and paper setting+ A lot of Easter eggs for those who know what to look for with the companies shown and mentionedCon:- terrible camera controls- looks and plays like a PlayStation 2 game (and not one of the great ones)- annoying checkpoint saves- bland constrained levels- flat voice acting- bland boring combat- bland boring stealthThe worst part for me is that some of the potential that this game could have had shines through at times:- downgrading from five to three forms makes sense for a video game and their roles are set alright, but in practice, it feels like two games, a stealth game like so many sections in way too many games and a bland action brawler where you defeat scores of enemies which you can reduce by being good at stealth.- the idea that you gain spirit powers by helping the spirits just beyond the reach of regular humans is good and as an idea a nice translation of the role playing game, but in practice, it just means running around an area, hoping to find them so you can get generic upgrade points to spend in a bland and uninspired skill tree- seeing into the spirit realm is a great idea, but instead of making it a game of shifting between worlds to avoid obstacles and enemies and seeing the destruction wrought by the Wyrm on both sides, this wonderful power is reduced to being a generic detective vision like in so many other games.- being a lone werewolf who tries to help his people sounds fun, but this is once again a letdown for those who like the setting, where the pack and its totem spirit are so important. And now for the ranting part of a long time storyteller and player of the pen and paper:- Why on earth way such a bland main character chosen? There are thirteen interesting and diverse tribes to choose from! I personally love the Fianna tribe, but why is he so bloody bland? A rough man who actually cares for his family instead of abandoning them would have fit, so would a man who stands apart because of the fae blood in his veins. - From what little I have seen so far, a member of the Wendigo (Native American werewolves who follow a great cannibal spirit of winter) could have been a far better choice and could have lead to interesting conflicts of whose land that actually is- By the same token, a roaming Silent Strider (Egyptian werewolves who have been forced to roam the world after loosing their homeland to vampires) would have fit just as well- Why did you make him a warrior if half the game is going to be stealth focused? All garou are capable of ripping enemies limb from limb, but a Ragabash (tricksters born under the new moon) would have fit so much better for a lone wanderer who infiltrates- The inability of shifting between worlds annoys me to no end, this can be such a cool mechanic as seen in so many other games.- Instead of a stealth-action mix, why not make it a party based game with a rag tag group of garou from different tribes who have to work together? Yes, they are killing machines, but with the right enemy design that could be a lot of fun.- If you need to make it a game of a single character infiltrating then why not go for one of the other Fera( werecreatures)? A rat could have made the stealth part more interesting and focused it more into that direction. Want to keep it the same ratio? Use a Bastet (great cats), there it would actually make sense that the character could not cross into the spirit world and that they are on their own.In the end, I am mostly saddened by this thorough disappointment of a game and I sincerely hope that a far superior game in that setting can be made some time in the future.I will probably force myself to finish this game and will update the review at that point, but I highly doubt that I would ever recommend buying it unless you want to catch a glimpse of a really cool setting that was done a great disservice by this game.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all I think it's important to note that the top review which states that stealth is an instant failure, is not entirely true, it's in the game yes, but only in the first couple missions, once you've spent, oh I don't know maybe 40 minutes in the game there's no such thing, you can go into full werewolf mode whenever there's enemies, zero restrictions, and just rip and tear your way through them.I'm a big fan of werewolves, so when I discovered this game naturally I had to try it out right away, and I'd say it's somewhat of a mixed bag, if what you like is just some dumb action and ripping your way through enemies as a werewolf, then this game is for you, because that's what it is, dumb action, there isn't much nuance to the combat system, but for me there doesn't need to be.If what you're looking for is a in-depth combat system then keep looking, the combat is very simple, there's a grand total of 3 combat combo's, if you can call them that, you got left click and then right click, left click twice and then right click, left click three times and then right click, very basic, yes you can switch between agile and heavy stance but that actually take away 2 out of the 3 combos you have, in agile you only have 1 combo and you move faster, in heavy 3 combo's but move allot slower.Surely that can't be all there is to the combat you ask, and well there are also abilities, but they are limited by ''rage'' which you obtain by attacking and killing enemies so don't expect to use them a ton, 3/4 times a fight, you have a heal, a long range jump, long range projectile, a roar, and a couple others, honestly it would be far more entertaining if they were part of the combat system in some way instead of limited abilities as they don't feel impactful enough.But that's just the werewolf, what about the wolf form? Well supposedly the wolf form is for stealth, sadly enough when you perform a stealth take down while in the form of a wolf you turn back into a human, boy did that ruin stealth for me, here you have the fantasy of performing stealth as a wolf and then taking enemies down as a wolf but then I just turn back into a human? Missed opportunity.That said stealth isn't anything to write home about, expect to maybe be able to take down 2 enemies before you get discovered, because it really wants you to rip through allot of enemies and not walk back and forth to enemies all the time as a werewolf the rooms to fight tend to be rather small, so enemies are very close to each other and will quickly spot you.And lastly the human form, required to interact with objects, outside that useless, when you use your stealth crossbow after firing it you stand still for roughly 2 seconds reloading the damn thing, not optimal when the point is to try to sneakily kill someone and then walk away.The werewolf model itself, actually looks fairly good, this isn't some AAA studio we're talkign about so you shouldn't expect some insane werewolf model but it's still pretty good, the fur could use some improvement and the tail's movement is rather stiff, doesn't move much at all, could have been a bit longer as well.I've done a fair bit of complaining, and yet I would still recommend the game because this kind of dumb action as a awesome werewolf simply is just right up my alley. You may have noticed I didn't mention the story, and that's because it's a rather generic revenge + big bad evil corporation story, besides I didn't buy the game for the story, I Bought it to play as a werewolf.So basically in short, if what you're looking for is a dumb and simple game as a werewolf and nothing else give this game a try, I certainly enjoy my time with it and I don't think I'll ever get tired of being a werewolf.

_childDocuments_.review: This game looks like something you would rent from the Blockbuster bargain bin circa 2005.Werewolf the Apocalypse is that game that grandparents get you because they don’t know any better and you love them but you’re just a bit disappointed that they didn’t ask you what game you really wanted. “It’s got Werewolves, they’ll LOVE it!”Sadly I had more fun playing as a Werewolf in Skyrim, hell I had more fun playing as a Werewolf in Don’t Even Think, and that says a lot. I enjoyed the game but I can understand the criticisms. Still played it, but maybe up the difficulty to make the combat more interesting. The game would have been a masterpiece if it had released in 2009.Despite that I personally had fun with it.  Sure, the voice acting is lackluster, but the gameplay was just what I wanted when I got the game.  I played on normal, started areas being stealthy then tore them all apart when I was busted.  The game makes turning into a Werewolf feel like a Super Saiyan transformation. It's not a perfect game by any means, but it was exactly what I expected it to be so I don't regret the purchase.Werewolf Earthblood is a good game but just not a great game. If you're a fan of action beat'em ups and werewolves and aren't expecting the next God of war, it's a good but not great time. The comparison with Vampyr made by some is spot-on. Will it be an amazing game? Probably not. But it's not bad. Sure. It's not the greatest. But it never claimed to be either. I loved Vampyr, I love the Prototype games, and as a filthy uber casual White Wolf interested person I'm glad to get a game set up in the Werewolf camp.I still hope it has a modicum of success that might encourage the development of other products - Werewolf is a rich setting and deserves a bit more consideration.6/10

_childDocuments_.review: I have not finished this game.The Wyrm has been more powerful than me, but I got so bored that for a moment I fell into the Harano. I've failed the Garou Nation, but not as badly as this...thing.If any of the above terms ring a bell, congratulations, you know one of the most special games ever published by White Wolf in the 90s. Werewolf: The Apocalypse was, is, a role-playing game with a wonderful background that brought together spirituality, ecology, epic, tragedy and a stark (not always elegant) critique/parody of industrialised capitalist society. As of today it is clear that as a species we have sold out to the Wyrm and are killing Gaia, we live in the world that Pentex wanted to create and it is quite depressing. But that is not the point of this review. I just wanted to make it clear that I love Werewolf: the Apocalypse.And that's why I hate this game. Not only does it not take advantage of the universe it exploits, nor the very concept of the game. Garou herds hunt together, but in this product they go alone and it doesn't exploit that aspect of the universe at all. Garou are stronger when they work together, but here the Garou are stronger by collecting random spirits that are scattered around as collectibles.There is no exploitation of the fascinating spiritual world at all, no threshold travel, no garou rites, no use of the terminology of that rich universe, no spiritual fetishes or klaives. The character himself seems to ignore 99% of the aspects of the world in which he lives despite the fact that he is originally the second of an Alpha in charge of a very powerful Caern. Nothing. You have a hand crossbow, because they've decided this has to be a stealth game.And this is where the problem of the game really begins. Its gameplay is boring, very boring. Cyanide Studios seems to think that Styx: Master of Shadows was a great stealth game, it wasn't, but it was pretty fun, and they've decided to do it again. This thing has the WORST stealth design I've seen in a long time, with broken AI, surveillance patterns and mechanics so badly broken that it just manages to be frustrating. Metal Gear Solid, the one that came out on the PSX, is better designed and more fun than this game. The stealth mechanics are there, and you can skip them most of the time, but if you do, the combat arenas start.And the poo hits the cake.The combat, which you would think would be important and well-crafted, is the most basic thing that could have been programmed. Strong attack, fast attack, jump attack and a few powers that are triggered by Rage (if you're going to play, power up the healing power). It's a bland system, with no depth, that achieves something impossible: making a combat system where you're a giant werewolf boring. That the enemies aren't funny at all, that the camera goes crazy and that there's no interesting addiction to combat just makes it worse.If at some point in the prison part they put in some addiction, that's welcome, but my brain couldn't take it any more.And he's ugly to boot. The game is from 2021 but it looks like a mid-generation Xbox360 game. The designs (with the exception of the Crinos forms and some spirits) are ugly and boring, the animations are pitiful, and the voice acting of the poor actors who had to read the worst possible expository dialogue is pitiful. The story...as a kid, when I was DM of Werewolf: the Apocalypse and thought the Raven was the coolest movie of all time I directed much more interesting Chronicles.But the music is cool. That's true. Especially the more powerful themes.Conclusion: Cyanide Studios is a subdivision of Pentex, possibly belonging to Tellus Enterprises, which has created this mediocre and boring (I don't even know how many times I've written that word already) game to turn the garou into victims of the Harano. To avoid. And I hate to write this because I know it's a small game and not a big production, but honestly they could have done better with the great material they are working with. It could and it should.Remember the Litany: Combat the Wyrm Wherever It Dwells and Wherever It Breeds.

_childDocuments_.review: I swear if this came out during the 360/PS3 era, it would've been a cult classic by now, tho sadly not as big of a cult classic as VTMB ended up being. I had a pretty decent time with it. Werewolf gameplay is a bit janky, but fun. Stealth helps to keep the gameplay fresh and is totally optional if you prefer just ripping things to shreds as a werewolf. Story's decent, but characters leave a lot to be desired. I finished it around 7.8 hours, so expect a 7 to 8 hour experience. If short games aren't your thing, then take this into account when buying. I personally don't mind short games given my busy schedule these days.Overall I'd give it a 5/10. If you like werewolves and/or World of Darkness, I recommend getting it at least on a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: The reason I recommend the game is because it has no competitor. It's the only werewolf-centered game within its genre that I know. Overall the game is a bit mediocre and if it wasn't for the werewolves I'd recommend staying away from it, but I've got to admit that the game has its high points and they surprise you in very nice ways (I'm not going to list them because the whole "magic" of the moment was not expecting them).Now, to list a few problems as a warning:- The level design is pretty dull. Specially at first where every facility you sneak into feels almost copy-pasted. Later on it gets better, so hang in there if it feels a bit repetitive at first.- The stealth part of the game is bad in many ways. It's as easy as it's unnecessary. The good part is that you can ignore it and brute-force your way through. In my humble opinion, it would've been much better to focus more on making a better TPA or beat 'em up even if you're not in Crinos form (the werewolf) all the time. I understand the idea behind it all though. Turning into a wolf to sneak around, maybe take down some guards and build up tension for the climax of turning into a killing machine... That all sounds good in paper but in practice is not well delivered in my opinion. You get used to it though.- You gain most of your skill points by... Sniffing plants?- Animations are a bit bad. The Crinos animations are decent, the wolves' are somewhat alright, but every human including the MC move very oddly.- There is nothing half as good as the intro cinematic in the game.- Executions and other moves feel unsatisfying. Like you can grab a human and squash it but you don't really see or hear what happened so you're left wondering if you killed him or not.- Camera work is bad sometimes.And despite all those flaws I still had fun. The game gets better overtime and Cahal grew a bit on me (all other characters not so much). All in all it laid a good foundation for a better sequel. I liked the story too, it's easy to empathize with the cause and it doesn't feel preachy. Even as a unique experience I'd say it's worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: I like the tabletop game and its lore, but when this was announced I was skeptical. I wanted to find some reason to like this game, I really did. I decided to wait until I'd finished the game to give it a review. This was a frustrating experience, and I have a lot of thoughts. I have no intentions of playing any more, but maybe I'll come back to it.First and foremost, the game is not pleasing to the eyes (or the ears), even on max settings. The wolf and werewolf form are cool enough visually, but everything and everyone else is just... Hard to look at. The NPCs, the enemies, the environment, all of it. A large majority of cutscenes look like they were poorly animated in SFM and some of the voice acting is just jarringly or laughably bad. The maps are serviceable but bland and quickly start blending together. The music is just the same couple of songs on loop so at some point I turned it off and started playing my own playlist.Stealth in this game isn't just "optional", it's outright pointless and frustrating past the tutorial. The small size of most rooms, enemy placement, lack of any actual cover, and enemy pathing basically made it actually impossible to go through most rooms without tripping the alarm. Even in big rooms enemies could just see you over the short cover, especially during takedowns. I actively TRIED stealthing for most of the game and eventually gave up because there was no real reason to do so, and it was more frustrating than it was worth. Just walk into a room, press the rage button, go sicko mode. Ignore whoever's talking to you on your earpiece, move on to the next room. Rinse and repeat. It left me wondering why there was stealth to begin with, it seems like they just wanted you to focus on the werewolf stuff and the stealth was an afterthought. Combat felt good at first, but as the enemy strength rises you begin to feel less like a powerful werewolf and more like a pain sponge unless you find ways to cheese the enemies that constantly block your claws. Also get used to seeing the same 3 final kill animations all game, including for bosses.The story is a completely predictable train wreck. Nobody you talk to actually matters in the long run, even your allies. Combined with the bland voice acting and terrible animations, I couldn't find myself getting invested in any of the plot or anyone involved and just pressed the designated rage button whenever I could to get out of having to talk to anyone. I just didn't care. Every enemy with dialogue is just a plank of nameless wood for me to break over my knee. It's like the game had an identity crisis before release. At times it feels like there's almost something there. Then it immediately fizzles out and you're once again left with something that just feels unfinished. If you're dead set on playing it anyway, I hope you have more fun than I did and genuinely enjoy the experience despite its flaws. I'd recommend waiting for a sale to avoid buyers remorse, if possible.

_childDocuments_.review: As a WoD fan, this game is a huge disappointment. The story is flat. I was hoping for a game that followed the mechanics of the TTRPG in some way but no, it just lightly borrows from the lore and then goes off on its own tangent. As a gamer, the saves are frustrating. I've accidentally hit "restart level" instead of "load from last checkpoint" more than once and had to repeat a lot of content with no way of going back. The gameplay feels mediocre, the combat feels kickass for all of 10 seconds when you burst into Crinos form and then lackluster when you realize that it's repetitive and not very involved. The graphics feel dated. The voice acting is terrible. This would have been a decent game 10 years ago.I'm going to finish the game because it's WoD and I waited so long for this game to come out, but unless you're a die hard WoD fan or really want to play a werewolf game don't bother.

_childDocuments_.review: Oof, I hate to say this, but I have been highly disappointed by this game.This needs a modder's touch because it feels like it is a great concept but is missing a lot of what would make it great.The game portrays itself as a story driven action-stealth game along the lines of Shadow of Mordor or Assassin's Creed with elements of Arkham Asylum (Only Asylum though). It takes place in a classic TTRPG setting and uses that to lend itself an air of legitimacy in that area, and just falls flat.The story is boring, the gameplay is flat and generic, and the main elements I was looking for from a Werewolf the Apocalypse game are missing. I'm not normally one to criticize graphics, but these look like ten year old visuals. Add that with the gameplay and this may have been a top 50 game of 2012.If you want a mediocre and outdated hack 'n slash with some neat concepts that aren't fully explored, this game is for you. I hope that the mod community can bring this game to its full realization, because the Werewolf property deserves more than this.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm very sad about this.  I used to play Werewolf the Apocalypse way back in the 90's, and was a big fan of the universe.  I was very happy to see this story get a modern game treatment.  And boy did it look great. But unfortunately, it just wasn't that fun to play.  I'm sure there are cool moves and combos you can pull off as a werewolf, but there's no real opportunity to hone these skills, as combat doesn't occur that often, at least if you're playing the game as intended, which seems to be mostly a stealth game. I'm also very much missing the Glabro (Wolf-man) and Hispo (Giant Wolf) forms.  It would be so cool to have those as different "stances" as well.  And no attacking in Wolf form?  After that sweet opening cinematic?  C'mon.  The human form should be able to use everything that humans have too.  Just a Crossbow with 3 shots?  Well ok, but you can't pick up an enemy's rifle or handgun or anything?  Please.  The RP elements are nice....if you're a fan of the WoD already and know what they're talking about.  I'm not saying you need the characters to keep spitting exposition every scene, but even in The Witcher series, which also had an older more established fanbase, there were Glossary Entries for anyone who wanted to learn more about the world to read and unlock as you encounter them.  Not having this makes this seem very FFO (For Fans Only.)And finally, the transformations....  One of the coolest things about werewolf characters is that transformation, it's part of the fun.  This "Poof" puff of smoke transformation is very off putting.  I realize in the TTRPG, you can in fact do instant transformations, but it still should be more than a puff of smoke.  Anyway, as a huge fan of the Werewolf mythos in general, and Werewolf the Apocalypse at least from the 90's, this game just didn't meet my expectations.  Granted, they were probably too high in the first place. But Skyrim had better Werewolves.  There, I said it.
_childDocuments_.name: Werewolf: The Apocalypse - Earthblood

_childDocuments_.review: If you just want a werewolf game that looks like from early 2000s, play as a hot wolf man who can transform into werewolf and kill stuff, definitely get this game on sale.I understand the game was made by a small team with a tight budget but c'mon it could have been much more than this. I really wanted to enjoy the game but the lack of effort and ambition really put me off. The graphics, nothing worth mentioning here, just really dated. The animations are janky and stiff, it's laughable. The voice acting is generic, almost no expression at all and the lines are cliché, no effort put in whatsoever. Story is meh and side characters are just as forgettable. The gameplay:I like that you have options on how you want to approach the missions either stealth (still half-baked mechanic) your way in or go full-blown werewolf at any given moment, just comfortably play at your own pace. The werewolf combat stuff is definitely the best part about this game as it precisely gives off that feel of raw savagery of a werewolf. You can switch between Agile or Tank stances to your liking playstyle, there's also a progression skill tree, it's basic at best but it gets the job done. The combat is overall fun and engaging. Unfortunately, the fun wears off after few hours because every single level is literally the same thing over and over with few more unique enemies toss into the mix, same small square arenas and static enemy spawns. Additionally, the excessive use of slow-motions after every heavy attack string just makes it worse.The game is extremely straight forwardly simplistic and dull, overall, unpolished. _childDocuments_.review: I didn't like this game at first, but it grew on me after I realized how it was supposed to be played. It's part tactics, part beat-em-up in the form of an angry guy who changes into a werewolf. Immediately it feels like the game Prototype, but this is not an open world game and in most areas you are confined to a small section of a building interior.Supposedly this takes place in the same universe as Vampire the Masquerade: Bloodlines but I couldn't tell that at all from a playthrough so it's irrelevant. There's no mention of vampires in the game as far as I know. There are references to wolves and worms, or "wurms" as they call them. First off, the intro cutscene is very impressive, but the in-game graphics are a little disappointing. Especially since you have sequences in the wilderness and you encounter things like bears that don't even acknowledge your presence, as though they are animatronic placeholders for real things. The story isn't bad, it's your typical vengeance save-the-girl nonsense, but the game takes itself WAY too seriously. It's a game about a man who changes into a mutant wolf, a little comedy would've made it much easier to digest the dialogue sections. At first I hated the game play, but that's because I didn't understand it. Basically, you have a number of different enemy types, mostly humans but also mechs, turrets, etc. They are never alerted to your presence, so you can skulk around in a very bad steath-type scenario until one of them gets alerted and then they all attack. The game then shifts into an action beat-em-up, and while it is repetitive, I must say the combat is a lot of fun. There were many times when I was within an inch of my health so I had to run to the opposite side of the map and carefully build up a powerup to avoid dying. The stealth sections suck, but you can get through a lot of them without alerting the enemy. You can also do things BEFORE the enemy is alerted, such as take out some of the infantry with silent kills, fire an arrow to disable turrets and cameras, break panels to weaken mechanical enemies, etc. This is where the game gets interesting, because you can carefully analyze each room to determine the specific plan of attack. There are also oddly placed AC vents on the floor that are the perfect size for a wolf to fit through. It doesn't make any sense, but it is fun trying to navigate around the mazes without alerting the enemies. If the enemies are alerted, then you into kind of a beast mode where you can switch between two forms, use powerups and build up a "rage" meter. When the meter is full you can basically bludgeon everything to death with no resistance. I was really bad at this game at the start because I didn't realize you can heal as an ability, so you want to heal 2-3 times every battle since everything resets after the fight.The camera is a pain though, almost game breaking but not quite. You can lock onto enemies, which makes it easier when you're fighting one, but when you have a dozen or so enemies and need to move quickly you will probably find yourself rotating the camera constantly to make sure it stays behind your character. It's unfortunate. There are a number of decent boss fights, two endings, and a lot of collectibles. If you get the collectibles it gives you points towards perks that can drastically alter the combat. This I really liked because the perks create legitimate strategies you can use to beat the game. In some games the perks are useless, but the fights are hard enough in this game that picking the right ones quite often means the difference between success and failure in combat. Overall, a pretty cool game, the music is repetitive but it gets you pumped up, and it's nice that someone actually created a game where you play primarily as a werewolf, as I don't recall a single other game that does this.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the many times I wish there was a "maybe" option for reviews. This game at full price? No. This game on discount? Yes. Its a real mixed bag of good and bad that's hard to summarize when you get down to it. When Werewolf came out, I had the expectation it would have the loving care of another World of Darkness game you might recall as VtM: Bloodlines. Of course, both games are practically separated by a huge span of time, VtM being the earlier game, and a different dev team and perspective would provide a different kind of game than Vampire no doubt. That said, differences aside, they are not the same caliber of game. You want more of a WoD experience, play Bloodlines. That said, you want to play a monster in the same vein as Prototype? This is worth a go.Combat and stealth are the highlights of this game, hands down without question. Not terribly challenging, I had to crank the difficulty up to hard to really feel stoppable, your werewolf form starts strong and just keeps getting stronger as you put in points to developing your abilities. With a quick form and a slower stronger bruiser of a fighting style, theres some value in switching things up on the fly but it can get super easy at times to just dart around the map picking off people systematically as they try to gun you down. Stealth is an option, a doable option in most situations but certainly unneeded; just letting you set the fight more in favor to your advantage by sabotaging gear and reinforcements or altogether dodging the encounter completely. Enemies have a set and predictable route that if you wait around enough you can ghost on through but between the two styles the combat is probably going to be the more engaging option.The story is........ not great. It does root itself in WoD's lore, but it just doesn't do it for me. Maybe its predictable drama of the protagonist, or maybe how the villains are just one seal clubbing away from being 2D edgelord captain planet villains, I just can't take much of it as seriously as they are trying to sell it to me. Easily the weakest element to this game. The side quests in finding spirits and stuff through your special vision were obnoxious too, especially since I couldn't walk while having it enabled forcing me to flash them on and off as I search the map. The campaign itself is pretty linear too, having progressed a huge way through the story with little to explore off the beaten path aside from your occasional spirit to gain points from.In short, don't expect a VtM: Bloodlines kind of experience with this one; but then again its probably the point. Werewolf should be expected to run different than being a vampire. That said, its not nearly as enjoyable with its atmosphere and characters as the former. Still fun though, even with its linear design. For the discount I got it at for ten bucks? Definitely worth picking up.

It also does, for my money, the best demonstration of why Kindred are ♥♥♥♥ scared of the Garou. I know all the fluff and lore by heart, but really getting to see it shown off in a game that's trying to showcase the destructive potential of werewolves, I have to say: a Raging werewolf makes a Frenzied vampire look like a wet book of matches. Terrible. Models IN dialog? Terrible. Acting? Terrible. Writing? Terrible. Story? Negligible.Get it on sale ($10 or less), expect *nothing* from it, and just accept the little werewolf experience for what it is. I really didn't think I'd like this as much as I did.
