_childDocuments_.review: Werewolf: The Apocalypse – Earthblood – an Action-Adventure/Brawler, based on the Pen&Paper “Werewolf: The Apocalypse” (first published 1992), part of the “World of Darkness”.Before I start my review, two things up front: 1.	There are other reviews claiming that you instantly fail if you are caught during stealth. This is nonsense. Whoever claims this, has not played past the first mission, which is still part of the tutorial and the “don’t be caught”-mechanic is just relevant in the first half of that mission. After that you are mostly free to choose how you want to approach a situation: Stealth to take out as many enemies as possible before the bloody fighting starts or go in “Red in Tooth and Claw” right from the start.2.	The game developer, “cyanide studio”, is a rather small company and not a big shot with a huge amount of budget. So this is NOT an AAA-Game made by some huge studio and it is their first brawler game (other games by cyanide for example are “Call of Cthulhu” and “Styx: Master of Shadows”). So don’t expect top-notch-graphics by today’s standards and huge diversity in gameplay. This is a classic (some might even say “old-school”) Action-Adventure/Brawler-Game set in the World of Darkness. So keep that in mind.About the game: As a huge fan of the original Pen&Paper I was thrilled to hear that we would finally be getting a game based on “Werewolf: The Apocalypse” (there were two other attempts many years ago, both failed). Knowing it was a small studio and following the marketing and information about the game closely I checked my expectations concerning the graphics and focused on the gameplay and how the lore it was based on was treated.And I was NOT disappointed. I had a lot of fun playing the game, I enjoyed the story and characters, the stealth parts (although the AI could have been a bit more challenging), the ability to change between Human- and Wolf-form, but even more so the fighting style in the 9-feet-tall Crinos-form (the “warform” of the Garou). The animations and movements of the Werewolf- and Wolf-form are great and the setting, tone and music capture a lot of the atmosphere of the original Pen&Paper.*Maybe I should mention, that I bought it on Epic Games when it came out in February 2021 and played it various times before I decided to buy it here on steam a second time to support the developer*The story is fast paced and straightforward but decent and the depiction of the lore is mostly pretty accurate when it comes to the adaptation of the original source material. There are a lot of details that players of the Pen&Paper will recognize and it is clear to me, that the team of developers, though definitely limited by budget and time, truly love the RPG their game is based upon.That said, fans of “Werewolf: The Apocalypse” will indeed understand a lot more of the hints and details of the story and about what is going and why it is happening, than the average gamer. The developers present the quite complex lore of the Pen&Paper here in a more simplified way and let some aspects of it unmentioned, so anyone who is completely new to “Werewolf: The Apocalypse” won’t get “lore-bombed”. And they converted a usually pack-oriented RPG (Garou gather and fight in packs) into a straightforward single-player campaign.I recommend to every player: Talk to the important NPCs, and not just once but on several occasions. Gather as much information as you can, explore the hub areas and levels, look for spirits, read the documents and listen to the conversations of other characters. It pays of and you get a better understanding of the whole background of the story and feeling of the setting, which benefits especially those who don’t know the RPG. Is it a perfect game? No. Is it the Open World-I can choose my own character/breed/moon auspice/tribe-kind of game that many fans of the Pen&Paper wished for? No. Would I prefer if it would have been way bigger with a longer story, wider areas, more background and more lore? Absolutely. But it is a solid AA-game with a lot of passion for the source material, a fun hack-and-slash combat system and a great soundtrack. If you love Werewolves, Wolves or are a fan of “Werewolf: The Apocalypse” you should definitely give it a try.

The pack leader had this distracting blue glow in his mouth.The pacing was terrible and confusing. The voice acting killed any distant hope of making the emotional scenes interesting. The werewolf thing feels like it's supposed to be your handy dandy pocket knife rather than the .50-caliber rifle it should be. _childDocuments_.review: TLDR; Get it on saleWerewolf the Apocalypse: Earthblood is one of those games where most of what it offers is either mediocre or just a bad experience. However the combat does not fall in this category as in my eyes the team was able to convey the power and feeling of playing a Werewolf really well. The story is bland with no real attachment to any characters. You don't get to explore who anyone is, not even the main character Cahal. The only dialogue that comes up only involves 1 of 3 topics which is either, Endron is definitely the bad guy incase you somehow forgot,  , or  . You can also ask them to give you World of Darkness lore dumps. It's not that the characters shouldn't talk about this stuff or inform the player on the setting, it's the fact it's ALL they talk about besides the mission objective. I think just simply trying to explore characters emotions and motivations would have at least made this not such a big deal. Not to mention the story itself is very straightforward and is just meant to guide you from level to level. So the game doesn't have a compelling narrative, and it doesn't do a great job having you get attached to the cast. At most you get a decent idea on the Werewolf lore in the World of Darkness universe.You'll also notice real quickly that this game added stealth segments that are incredibly unrefined. When you move into a stealth segment, Cahal will automatically crouch. The stealth gameplay you get from mission 1 is what the rest of the game offers up to the end. Now if the levels had interesting design then maybe they could have salvaged this but this also suffers from the type of stealth design that ignores the puzzle-esc aspect those genres introduce. You are able to completely move passed guards without issue and can ignore whole segments within seconds if you wanted to. Not to mention it's even worse when the only advanced things guards can do is detect bodies (that you can't move at all). You then get to see how when alerted, most guards in the room will just casually walk to whatever location Cahal is hiding in if the ai knows that Cahal is currently in the room. The "stealth" doesn't need to be in this game, and luckily outside of the tutorial levels, it's optional and doesn't effect anything. However the action Werewolf combat is a full 180 from this.When Cahal get's caught or during designated segments he will transform into his Werewolf state. The first time I was able feel how the Werewolf is controlled, I was taken back by how well the dev team put it together. It's by no means innovative or a unique twist, it's just designed really well. You can earn new abilities with different purposes, you can (kinda) juggle enemies, and Cahal has stances that completely change how the flow of combat is going. The music being played and animations make it the icing on the cake for that Werewolf power fantasy. However like I said it's not innovative or a unique twist, if you play a lot of different action games then this won't surprise you in that regard. The only actual issue I have for combat is that stunning any enemy is extremely easy and removes any tension in boss segments or in areas with a high enemy count. However despite this, enemies that go down easy actually add more to the fantasy since you are able to pick them up and execute them while running by either tearing them apart, chewing their face off, or any other animation they have for this, with some enemies having unique executions. These executions are available for every enemy and boss with the only exception being a specific boss. If you also end a fight with an execution you get a cinematic view of what is happening to also add to the intensity. Honestly the ability to switch between a stance that makes Cahal fast and nimble with quick attacks that do little damage, or a Slow but tanky stance that does really high damage and more visceral moves. Not to mention both stances have unique abilities, specifically 2 that are only for that specific stance, one that works differently depending on the stance, and a healing ability. They also gave Cahal a rage that let's him have access to both stance"s benefits at once, and has a moveset that combines the best parts of both stance's basic attack strings, at the cost of being unable to use abilities. The combat has a great foundation and I would love to see this dev team just expand on what they already implemented. The only things that holds this game back is it's writing and odd choice of stealth gameplay.Overall the game is mediocre at worst and at best it's an enjoyable action game with a Werewolf flavor that can be really fun if it speaks to you. I would definitely recommend to only get this on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I am cautiously voting to not recommend this game, not because I don't think it's a fun game worth picking up on sale, but because it really does have a lot of quality-of-life issues that take away from what could've been a solid B-rated experience.I disagree with many of the really, really aggressively negative reviews (also people need to unclench, it's just a game). Definitely buy on sale so you don't feel cheated out of your money's worth. But yeah, little things like being able to move and have Umbra vision on at the same time would've been beneficial. Action was fun, you can tell most of the small budget was spent making sure your lupus and crinos forms felt slick and moved wonderfully. It's a shame that the budget wasn't greater or we could've gotten more detailed character models. The difference between how good the werewolf combat animations are and the awful NPC animations is palpable.There were little things too that I wish we could've seen more of, like the ability to interrogate people and flip out mid-conversation at a hair-trigger (if you so desired). But ultimately, if you're looking for stealth, there are far better stealth games out there. You want Splinter Cell, not WTA Earthblood.Finally, environments are lovely, and the Patron Spirits legitimately look incredible, but unfortunately for the first half of the game you're stuck repeating Endron HQ over... and over... and over. Take it for what it is: a low-budget rage-filled werewolf romp. 5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't have high regards for this one, because I believed all the big reviews and such when it came out. In a way, I can see their perspective, but Wowzers, I had a loooooot more fun with this than I thought I would. But some of that is because Earthblood was exactly what I was hoping for: a freaking WEREWOLF game! It's crime there's not more of these.Okay, I'm going to be absolutely blunt with you here. Are you looking for a good stealth game? Being able to ghost through levels without leaving a trace? One with interesting characters, dialogue choices, and heart-felt moments? Challenging minigames and puzzles to break up the main gameplay? Then move right past this game.Are you looking for a "Be The Monster" game? Something more akin to arcade and "Character Action"? Where you can just say "FISH THIS!" at nearly any point of the gameplay- even in the middle of dialogue circles, to 'Enrage The Beast' and rip and tear? Not to mention one that doesn't 'Scold you' or 'Give you the bad ending' for actually having some damn fun? That's Earthblood. That's this game.In the introduction, you are going to see why the reviews were quite poor. I swear that this game starts on its worst foot (or Paw) forwards; a few bugs, 'First-Take' voice acting, borderline 'bad' looking human models. Hell, I spotted someone T-posing and sliding in one of the cutscenes in the early game! It looks Rough, and again: I can see why the reviews didn't like it. The first hour is probably the worst.But I paid for the game so I kept going. Just taking it a few bites at a time, putting it down and returning to the game in a day or two; where the gameplay of just tearing through enemies didn't get tedious. Because of this, I had a lot of fun with Earthblood than probably a lot of other people did. The more I played the game, the less bugs I found, the less the voice acting and models annoyed me, the more I found the story appealing, and I still just found myself enjoying the game for what it was. People's reviews here are not "Wrong" or "Off". It just really depends on what kind of games you enjoy (and how you choose to consume your time with this one). This is a power fantasy, where humans are struggling to take your Lycan-self down and they're putting up quite the fight. It half reminds me of CARRION in a way, that "Monster Massacre" overpowered style. If you ever played Skyrim and loved the fact you could play as a Werewolf, and wanted an entire game based upon that: here it is. If that idea bores the fish out of you, you have your answer.

_childDocuments_.review: If this game still had mixed reviews I probably wouldn't have written a review. But at the time of writing this this game has mostly positive reviews, which I don't think it should have. It's not a bad game, and I did enjoy playing it but it is pretty mediocre on every point and if you do plan on playing this game you should go in with the right expectations.- The stealth is incredibly bare-bones, there isn't even a mechanic to hide bodies, enemy pathing is extremely basic. - The combat is serviceable and at times fun, the last two boss fights were challenging but the combat never really clicked for me.- enemy design is pretty lackluster for the first half of the game.- the story is pretty meh until the end, important deaths fail to have a proper impact- as far as I can tell dialogue options basically don't matter and there was only one choice in the entire game that had any impact on the story.- It's really short- the wolf form sometimes feels like an afterthought with the only thing it does is allow you to go into vents, even absorbing spirits transforms you back into a human.Again, this isn't a bad game, but it's not a good game either. There are so many aspects that could have been improved. The characters needed more time to be expanded upon, most of them are just sorta there. There's no character development. Cahal's whole story of giving into rage and going back to his Caern in their time of need goes nowhere.  He seemingly gets over his anger and sadness pretty much instantly when the moment passes. And again, stealth needed to be fleshed out. This game does not feel finished. I'm giving it a negative review because I know that with more time and effort this game could've been so much more than what we ultimately got.

_childDocuments_.review: Bought this at a sale long ago and decided to finally give it a go after running out of vtm games.I've seen a lot of reviews complaining about the graphics and they are indeed outdated for a game from 2021, but I've played games from the 90s so I can deal with it. Once I got into the game, I was surprised to find that this game was actually very fun. While the combat isn't my favourite, I did get a nice enough build towards the end. What I really enjoyed was the stealth portion and I'd reload the checkpoints quite a bit to get as far as I could without combat. One thing worth noting is that the studio did their homework with regards to the lore. While I had not played other wta games, I knew enough from reading to recognize most references down to even some of the background props mentioning pentex subsidiaries. It was quite refreshing to see them come to life in a game like this, even if it's far from perfect. I think my biggest complaint is probably split between the plot and the length of the game. I think it could've benefited from some more padding in between story missions, especially when close to half of the game is a princess in another castle kind of deal. _childDocuments_.review: Werewolf: The Apocalypse - Earthblood is a third-person game with light elements of RPG, stealth, and hack-and-slash. Set in the World of Darkness like Vampire: The Masquerade games, you play as Cahal, a werewolf who with his pack tries to stop Endron, an evil megacorporation from tainting the Earth which upsets the balance of nature. It might sound silly, but it actually works. You will travel to Endron's industrial areas and sabotage them.Gameplay-wise it's quite fun, you can sneak to avoid combat, or to slowly thin out the amount of enemies later. In werewolf form it plays like a hack-and-slash, chaining combos and it has a skill tree. Most levels can be stealthed through, but I don't feel it's a "complete" stealth since sometimes there are the big enemies which can't be stealth killed, and areas that where combat is necessary to progress. I recommend trying to stealth first as its more fun, but I do wish there was an option to stealth kill the big brutes or at least move dead bodies.My problem with this game is honestly the saving. It's checkpoint-only, and that kind of saving in a stealth game isn't really a good idea since you'd have to redo quite some more if you got detected. I know stealthing is not the only way, but it's my preference. And I experienced a bug trying to reload during a level change cutscene, it loaded me to a broken, locked-out version of a hub level in which I cannot progress or restart the level and must start a new game.Overall, I think Werewolf: The Apocalypse - Earthblood is a pretty okay third-person game, and if you're a fan of playing as fantasy creatures or the World of Darkness franchise you might want to give this title a try. Don't expect the same length and quality of their most popular title Vampire: The Masquerade Bloodlines though, but the setting might be able to scratch that itch.

_childDocuments_.review: I just want to say, I feel like werewolves do not get enough love in the videogame world, there is only a few games I know that you can even play as a bad ass werewolf. In my teen years I learned about Werewolf The Apocalypse and World of Darkness series paper and pen tabletop and I fell in love with the world, and loved the concept of the werewolf games. I was so happy to see that they made a videogame based on werewolf the apocalypse. I'm a little sad though that this was not the werewolf game I had hoped for. Id love to play a open world werewolf game where you build your character and choices matter, like a skyrim but with werewolf the apocalypse. If you are buying this game in hopes for the same thing you will be disappointed. That being said the game is not all bad ether. If you are not familiar with werewolf the apocalypse or any of the world of darkness this game gives you a little taste about the world.First of all, you play as Cahal, a badass werewolf. The combat is completely action based and honestly easy to abuse. There is a skill tree to upgrade your character a bit. Pretty environments. Overall it is a fun game if you like beat'em'ups.The downfall, the game is barely werewolf the apocalypse. It uses the concept but its a action beat'em'up first.Almost no reason to use stealth in this game. There is no reward for stealth killing enemies. Pretty much only reason to stealth is to ether A bypass whole rooms or B to sabotage the room to make the combat easier. Skill tree is lacking, although you can upgrade your combat abillities to help, there not very much reason to get anything else. You find spirits and huff them like a drug to upgade your skills in the skill tree which is a little weird. The pen and paper tabletop you had gifts which are basically powers, you had weapons, ect this game you get pretty much none of that. Like i said a beat'em'up.My biggest complaint is that the game has autosave and only autosave. If you reach a checkpoint, good chance your path backwards is blocked locking you from any spirits you could have found earlier. In fact I suggest going into the game knowing you will probably miss a lot of spirits along the way. Some are so well hidden that even with the spirit sense ability its hard to tell if there is a vent you missed or if its something you have to grab after a checkpoint. I just excepted that i was never going to get them all and just enjoyed the beat'em'up.Story is pretty meh. Dont expect a great story. Its predictable and just overall meh. The cut scene animations in this game are also very janky. Characters like to flail there arms around for no reason and seem a bit robotic in their animations.Overall the game id rank maybe a 6 or a 7 out of 10. Its not bad, but its not great ether. Very mediocre. However you play as a a big badass werewolf thought and thats pretty awesome. Id say if you love werewolves even if you never heard or played the tabletop, id still pick this title up but maybe wait for a sale first.

The controls were terrible, the animations were hard to watch sometimes, the stealth segments I began to just ignore in favour of the werewolf combat. The werewolf combat wasn't super intuitive and took some getting used to, but it was sick as hell and had crazy metal playing the entire time. The story didn't grab me at first, it was pretty bland and predictable, but I found myself getting more and more invested as the game went on. It was super stupid and fun and exactly what I was looking for. If that sounds good to you, I would suggest picking it up, but for the masses? Steer clear.

_childDocuments_.review: Diseases? Curses? Forget everything you heard about the werewolf mythos for this is a different take on it.Earthblood is based on Werewolf: The Apocalypse series which are pen n' paper RPG's set in the World of Darkness universe, created by White Wolf and acquired by Paradox.In such universe the werewolves (or rather, the ) are born that way and can shapeshift at will between three forms: human, animal and in between. They are also one with the earth i.e. it's protectors and can also see, hear and speak with spirits (sometimes even travel to the spirit realm).In Earthblood you're in control of Cahal, a garou from the Fianna tribe (which were pretty much bards in times long past, but not anymore). Cahal and his brethren (among some regular humans) are fighting against those who taint the earth, an oil company called Endron (reminds you of something else?). And with all the environmental destruction also comes evil spirits to feed off of all the suffering and controversial experiments so you can probably picture how everything is ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up. It's a losing battle for the garou but they don't give up.The game is a nice mix of stealth and hack n' slash and it's conversation bits reminds me a lot of the modern Deus Ex's. It's soundtrack is 99,9% metal as ♥♥♥♥. Voice-acting and graphics are alright and the length is just fine (with the ability to choose between two paths, in the end of the story). You spend most of your time in enclosed areas (Endron's turfs) but there's also a forest, a desert and a prison, as levels. Never had any bugs nor glitches but the game crashed on me twice.Overall, though, I had a blast with it. Give it a try.

_childDocuments_.review: Before you buy.It's important to note that I bought this game with the impression that it is a story driven game. The game is marketed as such, or perhaps that is what I wanted from it.Werewolf: The Apocalypse - Earthblood is better described as a hack-and-slash game.The story is horrible, and it is a shame, because there was good potential. You are thrust into the game without much context and back story, the first mission is a horrible setup. Your wife dies by a an apparent antagonist because she was sent in on a solo mission, but you don't really care because there was no time spent to showcase her character or make you give a ♥♥♥♥ about her. And then they proceed to let you kill the werewolf/antagonist immediately after he killed her. He also doesn't have a backstory, his only purpose was to kill your wife for no reason and die???The main character also has no backstory other than being a father and a werewolf. No backstory of how he became such. The setup is horrible, the animations look like they came from 2005. The gameplay is mediocre and the graphics look good until you see it's just pretty textures. The soundtrack is cool but repetitive.I actually immediately stopped playing the game after the first mission. This game is a scam, the marketing is the only thing good about this product. Don't buy it, not even on special.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd only recommend this for fans of the franchise or werewolfs in general. Fights are nice and gameplay is ok overall, but very repetitive. One feels very powerful as a werewolf and that much is fine really, but aside from that, about all feels wrong. I'm 70% of the game done after 10 hours (says my save file) and I feel like I've only done 2 things in the game :1- walk in a room, (weaken the enemy with sabotage, optional) kill everyone there. Again, nice fight, but repetitive, and in small rooms the camera can really be annoying.2- walk around as a wolf (human moving is really slow and unsatisfying), hearing myself pant every 5 seconds, and activate "vision" to search for spirits. And there are...tons of them ! Think 10 to 20 per section of the game. Really mind numbing after the 50th time. It's a real shame because the ability to search was a great idea, because it makes the search easier than say looking online in a guide, so it helps reinforce the immersion ; the amount of spirits to find and their stupid locations sometimes really kill the vibe around it.Sneaking in is not really a gameplay element, first it doesn't work that well at all and anyway is slow and annoying, but also, you don't get xp to improve your skills by doing so, whereas killing everything in sight will give you xp.Story is very basic and expected so far. Acting and voices is good though, MC especially.I would NOT recommend at full price, even for a big fan. 8 to 10, ok for a fan, but more than 10 £/$/€ is a steal. Important to note that although graphics are ok, it is limited to 1920x1200, so if you play on a big screen, it'll look fairly meh.Progress is very linear. This feels very old school in it's approach. It's :-Main quest (corridor, room with enemies, repeat until mini-boss/boss, next objective)             -1 secondary quest at a time, that will only reward xp if you do, but won't change anything if you don't.Don't get me started on programming laziness, eg a dialogue that triggers each time you pass in a specific vent. So if you pass it back and forth X times, indeed, there is no "achieved" marker, and the same dialogue may in certain occasions trigger X times (big yellow fans, to quote only 1 occurrence).I'll finish the game now that I'm there, but had I know before, I wouldn't have started at all I think, and I used to play vampire/mage/werewolf RPGs, and I'm a big fan of the franchise.

_childDocuments_.review: Didn't expect much from the game, bought it as it looked like the first 'serious' WoD game focusing on werewolves, trailers were fine and was really cheap but unfortunately the gameplay gets boring really fast due to how repetitive it is. We often have two ways of pushing forward - brute force or stealth, while combat can be fun for a while I find stealth really bad, which is a surprise as I enjoyed both Styx games (created by Cyanide), limited paths to take, skills not changing much, dumb enemies, not rewarding. Everything felt really old school, room -> kill/sneak -> next room -> rinse and repeat for entire game pretty much.Graphics and audio are fine, music during combat/menu actually fits the game really nice, liked the main protagonist, most NPCs are shallow and if they tend to disappear/die, no one really cares. Will forget plot next week, side missions were also boring and pretty much copy paste (either find something or kill), everything takes about eight hours to beat.Bugs, yeah bugs, couple times I ended up in a wall or floor and had to restart from last checkpoint, but once, when I was mid game after completing a mission I ended up in a closed room I couldn't leave, there were no objectives, mission description was suggesting it's 2nd mission and guess what? Had to restart ENTIRE game thanks to absolutely horrible save system, which lets you only use last checkpoint or restart mission. For achievement hunters it might also ruin your playthrough, when let's say you were getting all the collectibles (spirits that are easily missable) but for some reason you noticed one just after some door that just got locked for good, solution? restart level or entire playthrought if it was a spirit in previous level -> top tier design.Concluding I'd recommend the game only for WoD fans AND on a high discount, otherwise don't bother.

_childDocuments_.review: Werewolf game is about things that you expect from it and its doesn’t take things to serious. While we don’t have decent chunk of these types of games about this topic Im glad that I played this game. Combat is fast and fluid marked with fast and furious devastation of your sharp claws and teeths. You can lean from slow tanky movement to fast and even deadlier one but also more acceptable to bullet damage. Find a balance not always easy but its fun. _childDocuments_.review: Werewolf: The Apocalypse - Earthblood has potential. It proposes a universe and some attractive ideas, but they are not interesting enough to overlook a crude graphical performance and some really repetitive gameplay mechanics. It is little more than a C-tier experience that's unlikely to stick in anyone's memory for long.
_childDocuments_.name: Werewolf: The Apocalypse - Earthblood

_childDocuments_.review: For me, this game is ruined by way too many forced chaotic group battles and checkpoints that are insanely far apart. The stealth sections are quickly stopped down because you enter a room with too many guards all standing around facing directions that encourage you to morph into a werewolf and destroy everything. The difficulty of these battles gets excessively challenging too the further you progress even on so-called easy difficulty, especially when facing guards with full body shields. There is also no manual save, so you are forced to repeat extremely lengthy sections over and over again. I mean these checkpoints are so far away that you have to repeat multiple sections with multiple group battles. The graphics are also outdated, character models look terrible, and voice acting is atrocious. Overall, I found this to be a cheap and outdated feeling experience that I cannot recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Werewolf: The Apocalypse - Earthblood

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who extensively played the Table Top RPG this game is based off of, as well as most of what White Wolf produced, I have enjoyed it. It is very rewarding to get to play as the actual ripping, roaring, destructive werewolf I would write out paper and pen character sheets for. As other reviews have said, the combat mechanics and writing isn't anything new or groundbreaking, but it sure is viscerally rewarding if you like werewolves being gory.Stealth is a viable option, but I did not get this game to stealth, I got it to be a crazy roid rage werewolf and it delivers. The story might seem old or boring, but if you played Werewolf the table top game, it's the story you're here for. You wanna fight for Gaia using the rage of the wild, that's the root of it. I'm having a jolly old time being an eco-terrorist murder machine furry like I did 20 years ago playing the RPG.

_childDocuments_.review: Werewolf: the Apocalypse is my favorite WoD setting. So the idea of a WtA game made me overjoyed.Then I was able to actually play it, and by Gaia was I disappointed. Saddened, even. It's not like it's bad or anything, either. It's just so barebones, like buying a house and finding out its just the foundations.They axed glabro and hispo, so you're down to three forms out of the five a Garou actually has.The missions are repetitive.The combat is also just as barebones, and though mildly entertaining, always ends just when you really get into it.And hilariously, it just doesn't look good. Looks like a 2009 game made by a tiny company. Where are the banes? Where's the labyrinth that is the deep Umbra? Where's the klaive with a spirit of Rage whispering in my ear? Cahal falls to Frenzy, and instead of getting killed for the safety of the tribe and his own soul, which he'd be totally for, he gets to use it as a powerup into what I'd expect a WARRIOR OF GAIA to fight like? And then when the fight is over he just returns to normal?Skyrim did it better and that's NOT a good thing.Please, make another WtA game, but this time do better. Until then, I'd not advise anyone to get this game until it goes on sale for $5 at most.

_childDocuments_.review: So this is quite an interesting one. Since I pretty much played all of the games that Cyanide Studios made so far (except the cycling ones), I'm familiar with what they do and how they do it. Their games are often a bit janky, often a bit rough around the edges, but you can always see what they intended to and that the effort is there. They are, to me at least, the definition of a AA developer. Werewolf: The Apocalypse - Earthblood (what a name...) is no different.This game would have definitely been awesome in 2009 or so. For a 2022 game though, it's a bit of a disappointment. The basics are all here: solid technical side, solid mechanics in terms of character development and, for the most part, gameplay. The latter consists of dialogue sections on one hand and the stealth-action parts on the other, and those last ones are the main problem for me here. I like stealth games and I love action games. Cyanide themselves made some very good stealth-action games with the Styx series. But Werewolf lacks the clear and clean design that Styx has: Styx is almost purely a stealth game because the main character can't fight very well, while in Werewolf you have the ability to transform into a very powerful beast form, so they couldn't do the all-out stealth approach here, obviously. They want you to use the werewolf form regularly - and they designed the levels accordingly. That means, that there are sections in the game where it's almost impossible to get through in a stealthy manner and you're pretty much forced to do action sequences. And they're not the strongest part of the game. They're pretty messy with the camera, and the controls are not as smooth as you would expect. Also, basically all of them are arena-based, so kill a certain number of enemies (which you can sort of control by sabotaging the enemy spawn points beforehand) and then go back into the stealth part. Rince and repeat. And this gameplay loop gets kinda old kinda fast. I would've much preferred if you indeed had the option to go pure stealth, but that doesn't seem to be there.Giving a recommendation here is really hard for me. I really do like much of the game. But I just can't get over the fact that the gameplay design is so forced and restrictive. And that's why I can't really redommend the game to other people.Similar games I would recommend instead, in no particular order: Alice Madness Returns, Styx: Master of Shadows, Darksiders II, The First Templar and maybe also A Plague Tale: Innocence. Most of them are quite a bit different to Werewolf, but I feel there's some overlap in terms of mechanics etc.
_childDocuments_.name: Werewolf: The Apocalypse - Earthblood

_childDocuments_.review: I played better and I played worse. The game has significant weaknesses but reminds me of similar old-school games I enjoyed a lot around the 2000-2010s. For the nostalgia alone, it get's a freepass for a lot of nonsense from me (like semi-ideal graphics, wonky mechanics etc). The story is based on a pen&paper game that emerged in the 90's, so if it feels like a 90's plot...it pretty much is. It can get a bit jumpy from time to time too, but it's coherent enough to know at all times what's going on.Problem is, it won't satisfy people who expect a lot more from a game that was released in 2022. It's not bad and you'll get your wolf action - just not the way you probably expect it. It's biggest crime is the lost potential in that regard imo. If you're a diehard werewolf fan and just want to smash enemies wolf-style, then it's definitely worth a try on a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Werewolf: The Apocalypse - Earthblood

_childDocuments_.review: Earthblood is a very simple action game with an RPG-style dialogue structure to give it more depth. The graphics are simple, outdated by today's standards, but good enough to get you on board with Cahal's revenge. The gameplay is good enough to enjoy the bloodbath that you'll see frequently, as long as you don't limit yourself to stealth, an unnecessary element for a game whose protagonist can be both a wolf and a werewolf. For the right price, it's worth buying so you can enjoy the world of Werewolf: The Apocalypse for a bit.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, Playing an Unstoppable Room Wrecking Werewolf is Sick!... however ......The one thing this game does right is brutal werewolf combat! Also, contrary to some othet reviews that I have seen, you CAN turn big boy Werewolf whenever you want, outside of the tutorial and hub area, as you would expect. Also, you do not have to stealth as much as some people are saying. You can stealth, it makes things easier because you can sabotage stuff, buuut.. there is nothing stopping you from just walking into the middle of a room, hitting RB (B for keyboard) and laying waste to said room. Having said that, the animations, voice acting, storyline, environments, all of that, feels like a bad 2005 indie title. Just plain awful. I mean, it feels like they had a solid grasp of the werewolf mechanic, and everything else was just an after thought. Which makes reviewing this game a little tricky. I mean, if the ONLY thing you care about is being an unstoppable beast, then you may really enjoy this title. If you are the type of player that needs a storyline with more then an afternoons thought placed into it, animations that at least look better then your average unity default asset toss, you may find the game underwhelming. To say the least. Voice acting is... you ever play 'Two Worlds'? Youtube it and suffer like I have.Is it all bad? No. Again, Big Boy Werewolf is Sick! Everything else, not so much. My advice, wait for a sale that puts it around $10.Overall 6/10

_childDocuments_.review: Basically a generic werewolf murder simulator where you kill endless numbers of soldiers. It's good for that and not much else.You get way more special attacks and finishing moves than you actually need. You can tell they designed the combat around making you feel like a badass before they did anything else, because everything else feels tacked on. It's not particularly difficult either; it's just the simple joy of killing endless faceless grunts as an unstoppable murdermonster with a surprisingly good control scheme and satisfying combos and combat options.The storyline is as bland as they come, and the voiceacting and conversational gesturing are especially wooden. If you care at all about the tabletop RPG then you probably won't like this unless you really just want to murder things as a werewolf.

_childDocuments_.review: I was happy to purchase and try out a World of Darkness game. Couldn't force myself to finish it. There's no manual save, autosaves are mission bound. Cut scenes don't reflect emotions well. Combos lock you into motion while you can get interrupted and damaged. There's only one optimal way to play, no reason to replay. Stealth is adequate but not rewarding. One thing I liked was game's soundtracks.

_childDocuments_.review: I would give this a mixed review since the game has plenty of good and bad things about it, but overall I enjoyed it more so despite some of its flaws. If you are looking for a werewolf hack and slash game then this will fill that void nicely. On the other hand if you are a fan of World of Darkness looking for an RPG game then you may find the story lacking, predictable, and doesn't use a lot of mechanics from the core game.The story follows a garou pack with their never ending struggle against the corrupt human companies destroying earth. Thus aiding the Wyrm and harming Gaia and her spirits. As a warrior of Gaia, you must sneak into facilities and destroy these companies from the inside out while trying to save your pack. What I love the most about the game is that it lets you choose how you want to play. You can either sneak around, or brute force your way through each room. The later being a lot more fun and more effective to cleanse the Wyrm taint.Issues I had with the game was the way it saves onto one file. Once you hit a checkpoint it auto saves, meaning you cannot go back further unless you want to redo the entire chapter. Another issue is that it will lock you out of certain rooms and areas. So if you forgot to grab something too far back, you can't get it anymore. I didn't have much of an issue with the story other than it was super predictable with how it was going to end. I was able to figure out what was going to happen half way through the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Werewolf: The Apocalypse - Earthblood

_childDocuments_.review: The idea is great, a Deus Ex style game with sneaky werewolves in the World of Darkness setting. It's got evil corporations, cool powers, a mix of stealth and action, etc. etc. If that sounds amazing to you, you might enjoy it despite its flaws.The problem is not just that the budget is low. Lots of "janky" AA games surpass their origins and offer great gameplay (Elex for example). However this low budget is paired with a general lack of quality development, leading to a game with no heart or great gameplay to match its jank. At the end of the day you get a simple, low rent version of the genre in a cool setting. Maybe that's enough for you. It was enough for me for 10 or so hours, before I ditched it.
_childDocuments_.name: Werewolf: The Apocalypse - Earthblood

_childDocuments_.review: There are good games, there are bad games and there is Werewolf Apocalypse Eathblood. A third person action game with stealth elements. Story: Story is you are a shape shifting werewolf who choices to abandon his pack and family after he goes wild on a mission and kills one of his own pack and after the death of his human wife.  He comes back five years to find his pack under attack by the same evil corporation that he was fighting against then. Now he must make amends by destroying the evil corporation. He must slaughter his way through endless waves of guard, mutant experiments, turrets and big robots from Aliens. The story is utterly terrible. Everything that happens is very predictable (With the exception of the ending which I'll get to in spoilers). Not only that but these characters have some pretty dreadful voice acting. The main character for example has the most monotone "What have a done? I've killed them" I've ever heard and its hilarious. There is an even better example later on when a character dies off screen and he says "No" in the same monotone voice and it's never brought up again that they died or were even involved in the story. Some of this dialog is so bad it honestly wouldn't sound out of place in Daymare: 1998 or Hunt Down The Freeman. VisualsThings don't get much better in the visual department.  Models and textures look like they come from a mid budget xbox 360 game. Many textures and blurry, lacking detail and look surprisingly dated. Not in the charming way like a throw back boomer shooter but rather that they just look old and cheap. There are sections of the maps which have these ugly dark patches through doors and in huts where the devs didn't have time to finish modelling these are super frequent given enemy's spawn in these dark areas when they attack you. The game also can become somewhat samey looking in areas with the same lab and industrial areas repeated over and over. What doesn't help is these areas also use a lot of premade assets which just makes it look generic.As for character models, it's a mixed bag. I actually think that the werewolf's look pretty decent. They might still have low res textures but the models actually look like werewolves and there are a few nice looking animations on both the full werewolf form and the normal wolf form. I also like how the spirit gods look. There are two in the game and the second one which looks a bit like a bird snake hybrid actually looks really cool design wise. However things take a massive downfall when we look at the human characters. These people are ugly with some very cursed faces and super robotic animations when they are talking. Ganeplay:Now as for game play that's where things get interesting. The combat is split into two types. Brawler and Stealth. The Brawler sections have you tearing through large groups of enemy's as a werewolf in two forms, Agile and Tank. Agile is faster and Tank is slower, more defensive and deals extra damage. You have ability's such as a leap which lets you get through the environment and pin down enemy's. You also have a dodge to avoid shotgun blasts which have a visual cool down. After you've done enough damage you can go into rage mode which makes you much faster and more aggressive. Combat is brainless and silly, but it is kind of fun. At least at first. I know it a basic system but tearing through enemy's as a werewolf is still satisfying, even if it's rough and I don't see any other games that let you do it. As for stealth however that's a another thing entirely. The game lets you switch between two forms, human and a normal wolf. In normal wolf form you are faster and can slide through little grates into vents. Once inside vents you go into first person like it's metal gear solid 1. In human form, you can climb over bits of the environment and take down enemy's. Sadly you often have to switch into human form to do anything relevant like taking down enemy's, interacting with PC's to open doors or switch off camera or do other things. Personally I'd have liked it if they had animations for the normal wolf doing guard take downs or smashing the controls. I know they could have done it because the wolf has some surprisingly good animations when sneaking around. For the first few missions if you fail stealth you get a game over, but later on if you get caught you just go into brawler mode to fight enemy's. Personally I avoided stealth because A: Why would I want to be human in a game that's sole selling point is playing as a werewolf and B: The stealth is awful. Enemy AI is super inconsistent. Sometimes it can't see you stood next to them and some times it's got perfect vision from through a solid object. There is also no way to drag or move body's after you knock someone out which often means you'll alert guards even if you are super careful. How such a basic feature of stealth is missing I have no idea. Plus there are even enemy's you can't stealthy take down like the big robots which you have to ether shoot with a crossbow three times or go werewolf on. Even the game seems to know it's stealth is bad because it forces you into combat in some rooms.You also have a skill tree which also lets you upgrade both for stealth and combat.  However here's my tip, ignore the entire stealth section. Outside of the ability to shoot cameras nothing here is worth the skill points and you'll be better off inventing in combat for the later bosses.Speaking of bosses, most of them are super easy. Go into tank mode and spam left click. Occasionally heal and use your rage mode and that's it. Most of the time you can out damage them. There was only one boss in the game this didn't work for and that was the two werewolfs you fight near the end. Even the final boss dies using this trick. At first I still liked the gameplay despite it's many flaws. Being a werewolf slashing apart evil guys is just so conceptually fun. However by the halfway point, that fun had faded. The game took like 10 hours to finish including most of the side quests but it runs out of any new ideas before the 5 hour mark. You'll be stuck fighting growing numbers of the same enemy's over and over and it eventually becomes tedious rather than fun. Speaking of side quests one of the literally broke on my in the second half and wouldn't let me finish it so unless you want the extra skill points don't bother.Spoilers: (Skip to conclusion if you want to avoid)This games ending is awful. After being dragged to four different locations to find you're daughter you are forced to kill her in this big monster form. Then you are given a choice, kill the annoying bad guy or save your friends. As far as I am aware this is the only choice in the game. I picked to save my friends which started a long wave of the same enemy's over and over until my friends got away. The bad guy left alive, my daughter dead and finally to twist the blade a cliff hanger of the corporation trying to group back together as if setting up for a second game. Perhaps If I had killed the guy it would have been different but to be dragged on for so long only to achieve literally nothing left a real sour taste in my mouth. Conclusion:When I first started playing Werewolf I actually still kind of liked it in a "So bad it's good" kind of way. I've often said I miss the older AA style of mid budget games with wacky and strange concepts that you won't see in other games and even if it was janky I was still exited to finally have one again. As the game progressed however the "So Bad It's Good" faded away into just being another bad game. Whilst the price I payed on sale might be fair it's still a very rough game that's carried by it's concept alone. The saddest part however is the fact this still might be the best werewolf game we've ever gotten. That alone is the real shame of this entire adventure. One day someone will finally give me that dream werewolf game, but for now this is all we have.

_childDocuments_.review: Werewolf: the Apocalypse – Earthblood manages to marry action and stealth in a manner where neither is slighted, but action is the real deal here. Werewolf Cahal returns to his Pack after five years of exile following a disastrous mission only to see they've gotten in deeper fighting an evil corporation out to endanger the world. Get ready to hunt for spirits throughout levels with magical vision in order to upgrade your skills, skulk around as a wolf and cause havoc in werewolf form once the alarm starts blaring. Story is there with all its “save the planet” glory, but it's the freedom to play your way that sold Earthblood to me. Even if you'll mostly fight similar enemies for a while and monotonous warehouses and office locales. Good pinky dip for the franchise and here's hoping for more.Compared to World of Darkness' better known vampire counterpart, Werewolf: the Apocalypse has flown under the radar as far as video games go. Now finally Werewolf: The Apocalypse – Earthblood gets to take center stage. There's a matter of tempering expectations first as Eartblood is not an RPG some were lead to believe, but rather action meets stealth. Was it worth the wait, though?It doesn't take long for disaster to strike our protagonist Cahal of the Fianna tribe as he loses his wife in a raid on an evil corporation called Endron. This results in him abandoning his own pack as well as his daughter, and going on a five year self-imposed exile after losing himself to Rage. Until he hears they, now operating with human activists, continued to fight the good fight and his daughter Aedana had stepped into her mother's former role – being an inside woman. Looking to redeem himself Cahal returns and if there's a chance he gets to avenge his wife all the better for it.In this setting werewolves, or Garou, fight to save the world at the behest of its very own spiritual representation called Gaia. This “saving” takes place in many shapes, but is primarily characterized by maintaining the balance between material and spiritual realms. In modern times this tends to effectively mean becoming eco-terrorists who fight polluting corporations, literally or otherwise seeing as everything has a spiritual equivalent in the realm of Umbra, acting under the auspice of less well-meaning spirits. These entities seek to unbalance the status quo for their own benefit all the while Garou serve as Gaia's warriors combating such incursions.There's a metric TON of lore to all of this and I've given you the cliff notes version which is more than Earthblood does because it aims to keep your focus grounded. This can be somewhat jarring as you get to interact with your pack's spiritual Totem spirit, for example, but still.What struck me as strange is just how minimal the experience you're getting here is. For example, Cahal's tribe? Game will barely even mention that unless you read the notes scattered about. That's not even getting into his character. He's a gruff and almost stoic type which seems to be at odds with Fianna image of warrior poets or loud braggarts, depending on who's answering. Characters themselves never really get much attention and it's fortunate that goes hand-in-hand with a likewise simple approach to story game has. There's two pillars to it: avenging those you cherish and saving the planet. It just so happens that, be it your hacker Kinfolk or Silver Talon pack leader, everyone can conveniently direct their anger at Endron. I did like how there were some attempts to ambiguity later on, but it's portrayed in such obvious manner you can immediately figure out something is wrong. Only people who may be fooled in this instance, ironically, are fans of the property who know about a certain anti-human tribe's ways.Enough waffling about the story bits because it's time to get into gameplay. This is where I got blindsided by how the game approaches action and stealth so they work perfectly together. You have three forms to work with, after all.Stealth in a game driven entirely by turning into Crinos aka hulking wolfman destroyer form dedicated to combat alone, which comes with its own Agile and Heavy stances, is tempered by the presence of Lupus form where you assume the shape of a regular wolf. Now that I think about it Cahal's human form is mainly there to press switches and talk to scant few other characters, it's the action and stealth ones pulling most of the weight. So how does an action game manage to integrate stealth without it feeling tacked on? Simple – by making stealth entirely optional, but beneficial to engage in all the while keeping the doors ajar enough so stealth can always escalate into action. I had a good laugh when the only mission where Cahal is seemingly set for a stealthy approach can just be hacked and slashed through leaving your contact wondering what you're going to do now. Protagonist answers he'll think of something.I wish Earthblood had more there to work with. For me it boiled down to “stealth became too cumbersome, combat became too annoying” as game kept throwing more obtuse level layouts and enemy compositions at you. Probably not helped by the fact you're largely confined to corridors with plenty of chest high walls to hide behind, cameras to avoid and fuse boxes to sabotage incoming reinforcements with. Reasoning behind why you would want to do SOME stealth has less to do with thinning out enemy ranks, as they'll send waves of reinforcements, and more with building up your Rage which lets you use special abilities. You can also generate it in combat, but why not prepare beforehand? Cahal can also use a crossbow to deal out damage and flasks to increase Rage, but I honestly never found much use for either. On normal difficulty cameras were never an issue because combat isn't really an issue to begin with. Sure, some enemies are trickier as silver damage can limit your max health until you upgrade your skills a bit, but nothing you can't work around with some dodges or target prioritization. I also wish an action game like this had more worthwhile bosses instead of couple I actually remember.Skills? Yes, I've saved the best or worst for last. Further enforcing the whole “play it your way” is the way in which progression via Spirit points isn't at all tied to how you play. You get some from mission completion, but 90% comes from tracking down vagrant spirits scattered throughout levels. This means regular backtracking throughout the level to find the ones you've missed with your Batman, errr, Umbra vision and Lupus form's detection upgrade should be the first one you buy. These points can then be spent on Tactical or Combat skills. Just keep something in mind – Earthblood doesn't feature level selection. Make sure you get them Spirits as you need them if you want to get ALL the skills by end game.In conclusion I can say game had me hooked enough to not only collect all the Spirits along the way, but also to replay the final mission to see both endings. Amusingly enough side missions ended up being the most frustrating aspect of a game that teaches you to rely on Umbra vision only to expect you can locate things without reliance on it. As far as soundtrack goes I cannot remember much, but sound effects were crunchy enough even with general lack of gore. I'd say they nailed the overall feeling of Werewolf: the Apocalypse down to how the game ends.

_childDocuments_.review: I probably would have really liked this about 10 or 15 years ago.  However it coming out in 2022 does make it feel very dated.   If I paid $30 for this in 2022 I would have been pretty pissed and much harsher in my criticisms.  I paid $3 in 2024 and think its money well spent.  If they were to develop a sequel and improve on it a lot then I would happily pay full price in the future.The game is fairly short and a lot of the gameplay is repetitive; however, I did have a lot of fun with it.  Imagine every stealth game you played, sometimes you fail the stealth section and think "ah screw it, im just gonna go loud and kill everyone."  That happens in this game except its to an absurd degree.  If you are a fan of the tabletop rpg World of Darkness setting and more specifically that of its Werewolf gameline then you kinda know what to expect from its story, its fairly straightforward and a little basic, but basic isn't necessarily bad.  If you are a newcomer then there will be a couple of headscratching moments where you don't know what is going on.  For example the Black Spiral Dancers, newcomers will probably be confused about why some wherewolves are working with the bad guys, but long time fans will understand.

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay: So this game tricks you into thinking its going to be a stealth game with some werewolf combat elements. The intro and the first mission force you to like stealth around and then shift gears into fighting hordes of enemies with potentially the best werewolf based combat in games. The contrast is hilarious because this game has the worst stealth game play in all of gaming In not sure if that is hyperbole. It may actually be the worst. THIS STUDIO MADE "Styx: Master of Shadows!?" Guess what though, the stealth game play inst just "optional." You flat out don't have to do it at all. You don't have to do it, and then fail to start fighting.  The second you're in a hostile area the game lets you "Press Q to Enrage" and yeah your basically playing a better version of the Venom portions of "Ultimate Spiderman" for the PS2. Some people might find it boring or repetitive, I am aware. I do wish there was more enemy variety, but I had a blast. Leveling up the skill tress and shifting between stances.  I love games like  "inFamous" "Marvel:Ultimate Alliance" "Batman: Arkham City" or "Spiderman:PS4" its fun to feel powerful, and enjoy your powers. This game does that. Seriously, your dodge and jumping animations have active hit boxes, so you can maintain juggling enemies and keep combos going by jumping or dodging into them. I think that's pretty cool! Reminds me of Devil may Cry kind of.Story: The story is cringe-worthy nonsense. Any story about werewolves where its not an infection but some bloodline nonsense will inevitably be trash and uninteresting. I'm sorry a bunch of grown adults referring to themselves as "pack" and "warriors of Gaia", is so lame and this games story takes itself seriously. The shear amount of times you will hear the words, "Wyrm," "Cairn," and "Gaia" used  un-ironically will make you want to stop. Now me personally I enjoyed the story because the way the dialogue is read in conjunction with the poorly animated cut scenes. I'm going to be honest in terms of story I think this game is "so bad its good." It actually made me laugh a few times, and I see that as a positive. Given the choice between laughing at something when its bad or rolling my eyes and groaning I'd choose the former.  Its all funnier when you realize they're using these very European folklore terms even the characters have odd Eurocentric names and this game takes place in the state of Colorado.Glitches and low quality areas: I'll start this section by saying I am aware this is not a full priced game. I do have to mention on one mission I loaded a checkpoint into a hard lock. I was stuck in an elevator and had to restart my mission progress to keep playing. I mentioned Arkham city earlier this game rips off the hit counter mechanic for how many consecutive hits your landing, doesn't do or mean anything. I was getting up past 100x hits as far as I can tell its just fluff. The lore stuff like the random readable pieces of paper and data logs? There is no Journal or anyway to read them later not that I cared that much but the whats the point though? All the cut-scenes are weird.. Also lots of re used animations and bosses. Oh and the games short witch is good and bad it doesn't over stay its welcome but I beat it in around 7 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Werewolf: The Apocalypse - Earthblood

_childDocuments_.review: If you're not dealing with lamentable voice-acting, a plot that's drier than the Caern of Southern Dakota, and cookie-cutter world hubs with meaningless side quests and no world-building, then you're dealing with janky combat, an AI whose sneak detection flip-flops between potato-brain and god-mode, a character that doesn't do what you tell him to, and glitches that prevent you from completing the combat encounter. If, by some miracle, you're not dealing with either of those, then you're sneaking through bland environments with seemingly random level design that are-- in some cases-- meant to force you to enter combat. The only redeemable quality of this game is the combat, which sucks because half the time, the combat is unrewarding, repetitive, and buggy.

_childDocuments_.review: You start the game with 15 minutes of lore dump via two cut scenes that doesn't tell you you could skip.Then, I got the crossbow and right clicking while covered blocked half my vision by clipping my camera into the object, so you can't really sneak/stealth behind obstacles intuitively. Breaks game immersion right off the get go.Another part that irked me was the voice acting. I usually don't really put too much attention to voice actors, but my god was it bad. Dude kills a packmate and goes "oh no what have i done" and I'm like, "not a very good job on the dub that's what you've done." I can't even find who did his voice on IMDB because Cahal isn't listed. I don't need you to be the best VA on the planet for every role, but I do need you to not make me question whether my 10 year old niece can do a better job than you.The initial lore dump was the worst part. The writer should have led with less fancy schmancy unexplained wyld/worm lore and more on Endron being an evil capitalist corporations that's hellbent on persecuting werewolves. I the player neither cared for the little girl nor the woman that died in the tutorial and nobody was memorable or stood out. Maybe there'll be a hook that catches my attention later, but you've already lost me if you can't convince me to like or care for your characters within the first couple minutes.I'd be excited to play this in maybe 2001. For a game released in 2022 by friggin' CYANIDE STUDIO this was a massive disappointment. Other games that Cyanide made include Styx: Master of Shadow and Shard of Darkness, both of which I loved. I had expected a similar experience for a stealth action game, but ultimately this game fell short whether it was the janky controls, the less than desirable voice acting, or the crawl-slow pace that it started off of. 20 minutes of this was all I could take. Praise steam refund.

_childDocuments_.review: I went into Werewolf Apocalypse Earthblood with no real high expectations. Most reviews already spot on said it all. If you're expecting a AAA game, this is not it. HOWEVER, that being said, I still had a lot of fun with it! For starters, it has the most wicked cool looking werewolves in it! I mean, heck.. it has WEREWOLVES in it. I am pretty sure, sadly, that this IS the only werewolf game out there. And for that, it's doing a fine job. The combat is wild and ferocious. The only thing that bugged the wolf outta me was, that quite often, the mouse wouldn't respond. Not enough so that it was a hindrance but rather, extremely annoying, especially in the heat of the battle. There are stealth aspects to this game. They are not greatly developed BUT they are there and do help thin out some of the enemies. Personally, as someone who sucks at stealth anyway, I very much appreciated that there were zero penalties for saying 'screw this' and going full Werewolf. The story was okay. Nothing fancy but interesting enough to keep you going throughout. All in all, it feels like it had excellent potential but got cut short. The graphics are mediocre, though the cinematics are pretty awesome! All in all - it's an enjoyable game. Not too long, but with so many huge, massive open world games out there, it's a nice little change of pace.

_childDocuments_.review: I would say that objectively, this is not a great game.  It's not great at stealth, and it's not great at combat.  The dialog choices aren't super interesting, and you can only play a male werewolf.  The story line is pretty meh and is all about eco-terrorists.  What does make this game great in my opinion is the lore.  The creators of this game paid very close attention into keeping the lore as close to Werewolf: The Apocalypse RPG as they could.  The Red Talons were perfect, having the wyrm and the formori were great.  It touched on the weaver, which was pretty cool.  Exploring the unchecked werewolf rage was good to see.  The downside to all of this is that none of this lore was explained well.  Some of it was in all the little text notes scattered about, but unless you actually know the RPG you're missing out on so much.All together, I would say this game is fun if you enjoy Werewolf: The Apocalypse RPG, just being a werewolf in general, or really like watching a werewolf put extra effort into keeping his eye patch when he shifts.  All the other werewolves don't keep their clothes when they shift, but  keeps his eye patch, like the boss he is.

_childDocuments_.review: Personally, I don't see why this game gets such a bad wrap. _childDocuments_.review: I feel sorry for anyone who paid more than 20 €/$/£ for this game. The trailer sure made it look very cool, but beneath the surface this is a very mediocre game.The good stuff:- It has werewolves. How many games are there about werewolves? If you're a werewolf fan, you're probably going to get this and enjoy this game for that aspect alone. The wolves are very cool and shifting and fighting is decent enough.The bad stuff:- Sometimes the graphics look okay, but generally, they are very outdated. The werewolf looks cool, but all the facial animations are stiff and sometimes bugged and would have looked okay some 20 years ago. Your model clips through surfaces constantly and walking through a water puddle is like walking on ice, with no water effects whatsoever.- You get two places in between missions, a forest, and a desert, but otherwise all you do is sneak around and fight in these compounds that all look alike. It gets boring and repetitive really fast.- The AI is poor. It doesn't see you if you are in a different room (different 'area') and jumping up and down, but the moment you step inside the other room, they can spot you. These days I think players are used to pretty decent AI and actually needing to take care of not being noticed when sneaking around.- The plot is super generic and not very exciting. You get some conversation options but they don't really matter at all.- The voice acting is wooden. The guy voicing Cahal was okay, but otherwise the characters sound kind of amateurish.- The enemies are a few different kinds of soldiers, a few werewolves and Wyrm-infected soldiers. That's it.It's too bad this setting wasn't used more effectively. Get it if you are a werewolf fan and can get it cheap, but definitely don't bother with the extra content. It doesn't make your super mediocre experience any better and you'll just be wasting your money. This game is worth 10 eur at best.

_childDocuments_.review: It would be a good game on paper.A stealth and hack&slash game centered around werewolves and an extensive lore. The best part is that you can choose if you want to stealth the game or go all claws swinging. Unlike some people say, the game does not force stealth on you and you are not deadmeat if you fail to stealth until the end. You can just smash your way across the levels as a werewolf if you want. I loved this freedom. It meant I could spice up the levels by stealthing one part and just smashing in skulls in the next.It was great.Now onto the bad part. You knew it was coming.As I said before, it would be a good game on paper but sadly it does not work with the current glitches and issues it is having.1. Saving is a nightmare. There is no manual save and the game only, strictly only saves at checkpoints. So, if you do some side missions, collect some stuff before a main mission and die before reaching a checkpoint... good luck collecting all the spirits, reading all the notes, and redoing your side missions again.2. Stealth is a glitchy mess. If as a lupus your tail sticks out from the mesh of a cover, the enemy will spot you for some reason. If you stealth kill someone, the body might glitch out and go crazy. Like, falling through walls right onto the path of a patrolling enemy, or flies around the floor like possessed by a demon and alerts the entire level of its presence. Yes, both happened to me multiple times.3. I would have no issues with graphics if it was properly optimized. I mean, it looks like a game from 2010 but requires a PC from 2030 to run it without issues.The only reason I am even daring to give it a thumbs up is that I enjoyed the gameplay, despite these issues and gave a nice 20 hours of entertainment. Ignore the 1,5 hours, though. That was due to me redoing side missions and collectibles because of the terrible saving system.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd already beaten this game on PS4 when it first released last year, but that didn't stop me from double dipping here. Werewolf is an enjoyable werewolf game (of which there are few, unfortunately) where you play as Cahal on a mission to defeat Endron, working for the Wyrm to destroy Gaia. The missions are pretty linear, but I enjoy it nonetheless, especially the side quests where you get in touch with the spirits. You use the wolf form for stealth and can bark to draw the attention of enemies. Werewolf wreaks destruction when your cover is blown or you feel like just giving everyone a bad day. Graphics wise, I think the game is just fine. They're not ungodly realistic like some games, but they're dx efinitely not potato either. Story definitely could've been a bit more fleshed out, but for what the game is, I really enjoyed it. Who wouldn't want to fight for Gaia? Music is pretty kickass when you're ripping enemies apart with your claws. Love werewolves? Definitely pick this up!

_childDocuments_.review: I find the critics harsh on the game. It is not a masterpiece but it's another solid game by Cyanide. Forced stealth seems to be a big complaint but it is barely the first hour or so of the game, you have a good 7 hours of mayhem if you wish so after that. Closer to 5 hours if you put it on easy, ignore stealth at all beside the early mandatory part, and have some mindless destructive fun. Ironically enough, I think there are more encounters in the whole game that force combat than stealth. I'm not sure if it is bad game design or people having too short attention span, I'm pretty sure you can finish the "tutorial" in the 2 hour Steam refund period and actually see what the game really is.Voice acting is not awful but bland, graphics even on maximum are rough for 2022 and gameplay remind you of old PS2 action-rpg but it is what I expected controlling a fearsome werewolf. The skill tree is simple and does not offer game changing skills but it allow you to focus on your favorite playstyle. The game is quite linear, mission based with very few sidequests and while you can have a couple different way to explore the areas it's pretty much a series of rooms. Open or Semi-Open World would probably have been too much for Cyanide but it would have been great for this game.My knowledge of the Werewolf part of the World of Darkness is on the low side so I can't say how faithful it is but I enjoyed the nature and spirit lore. Plants and other natural trinkets being your source of experience is a fun idea and does not penalise stealth since combat does not give experience at all.The only reason I would not recommend this game is because of Nacon and the one year Epic exclusivity. The game itself is fine if you buy it on sale because it is a solid 7/10 for me but too short for the full price.

_childDocuments_.review: A really fun hack and slasher which lets you take on the role of a big, furry killing machine. The best bit about the game is the combat in which you turn into a monstrous werewolf and rip and tear your way through rooms of humans, mechs, and later on sort of demonic possessed people. The game does an amazing job of making you feel powerful. When you transform you'll send civilians (mostly scientists) fleeing in terror and becoming catatonic whilst you rend their allies limb from limb. By the end of the game I had improved my fighting stances so much that even bosses didn't stand much of a chance - especially with the levelled fury\rage mechanic that heals you as you fight.There's some very simplistic stealth mechanics, but don't expect to go through this game without fighting. Hell, some areas demand you kill everyone. I found the stealth fun at first, but it quickly just got in the way; though I did enjoy turning into a normal wolf a lot due to increased movement speed rather than being sneaky.You can't do much in your human form, but you're constantly shifting back into it to talk on your radio, open doors, and collect spirits and stuff to gain spirit points so as to improve your abilities. Oh, you do have a crossbow, but I didn't use it after the first few missions, I enjoyed just going loud. lol.There's also some very, very minor RPG elements, but you'll have levelled up everything you wanted long before the game has ended. Story is kinda crappy and predictable. You are Cahal, a werewolf fighting for Gaia against cartoonishly evil mega-corporations. You could take this story, hell the whole werewolf setting, and put it into a cyberpunk world and nothing will have been lost. Cahal is a man doomed to play out a predictable story in which the events of the past happen again as he wages his nature themed cyberpunk anti-corpo campaign of terror. Be prepared to be hit over the head with themes of "mankind is bad!" and "businesses are so evil, guys!" and for it to really go no deeper than that because in the end they're all serving some evil apocalyptic entity named the Wyrm. Not too familiar with the source material so I have no clue if the themes in that are this shallow and silly; only played Vampire and Demon myself.Anyway, if you can pick it up during a sale and, like me, like the idea of rampaging around as a nigh unstoppable killing machine, then check this game out. I got it for roughly £2.50 during a sale. Game really isn't worth full price, in my opinion.
