_childDocuments_.name: Werewolf: The Apocalypse - Earthblood

_childDocuments_.review: First off I do not think this is a bad game and should not be that negatively reviewed. However, this game has many problems. Namely low detail on NPCs and other things in the environment is one. That is passable at least, but the combat and stealth need some work. Combat is good in my eyes, aside from maybe you dying too fast (I only died once in combat and that was from turrets) and enemies having some BS knockback attacks (The knockback animation sends you flying way too far). Stealth is completely optional (aside from one mission in the beginning so anyone complaining about that needs to play more) and it has many flaws that come with an underdeveloped stealth system. The flaws are enemies seeing through cover, wonky detection, crossbow being nearly useless in most areas, and takedowns being random in time and placement after it finishes causing you to get spotted from it.Now I think this game is good, but it is definitely a 40 dollar or less title. The character model for your character and the werewolves are great (aside from the goofy handlebar mustache on the MC). The story is shallow and it doesn't allow time to connect to characters at all. Yet the story is surprisingly long and the game will take a minute to complete (If you go for every spirit). All in all I recommend this game on sale, but it is highly repetitive and at times annoying so a possible avoid for most.
_childDocuments_.name: Werewolf: The Apocalypse - Earthblood

_childDocuments_.review: A very decent hack and slash/stealth game, although it's mechanics could have been better explored. There are very few combos, the stealth is really simple, and there are even some overlooked anoying details, like the fact the character always stands to aim with the crosbow, which makes you visible when crouching behind cover. Anyways, it's a fun game if you are into simple and direct action.That said, if you were into the lore of the pen and paper game, you will hardly be disapointed. There's no meaningless fan service here. The references and the lore work solidly in favour of the experience. Also, on a quick comment, the voice acting isn't as half as bad as most people think, the actors could have made some more effort, true, but all the voices are nicely cast and a match for how the characters look.A fun 7/10 game for fans of the pen and paper game, and perhaps 5/10 for others, but still fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Werewolf: The Apocalypse - Earthblood

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not worth the asking price. It's story is shoddy, it's voice acting is terrible, it's game-play is basic AF, and it's graphics are pathetic for the time it was made. Also the trailers are basically false advertisement, they basically just hype up this crappy game by showing a 4k cinematic and get your heart racing with heavy metal. The only thing that makes this game worth playing at all is the fact that this is the 1st World of Darkness game that is not a tabletop or book that goes into the story of the world's Lycanthropes. BTW still waiting on Bloodlines 2 to release, losing hope that it ever will.
_childDocuments_.name: Werewolf: The Apocalypse - Earthblood

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game at around the $15 price point.  Stealth is simple and the level layouts are spartan and artificial to accommodate that play style.  The fight sequences are solid and the Alien Weaponry soundtrack is outstanding.  Aside from that, the entire experience is far more bare bones that I expected going into a licensed title.  The models, animations, level scale, voice acting and every other aspect of this game are B-tier, not AAA.  More than  anything it reminds me of Bungie's 2001 third person action game Oni - fun to play through once and gets the job done, but nothing more.  It might merit a second play through stealth style and to collect and missed lore, but that's about it.  In conclusion, not a great game or novel use of the license but decent fun if you can find it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Werewolf: The Apocalypse - Earthblood

_childDocuments_.review: I can't shake the feeling that with just a little more effort put into it, a little more variety, more polished graphics and animations and a bit more depth to the story, this game could have become something memorable. Especially considering the vast World of Darkness lore (that I can not claim to be too familiar with).But the way it is now it's just kind of bland and repetetive. Like a remnant of the PS2 era rediscovered in 2021.Don't get me wrong, it's not a bad game in its own right. Voice acting is good, story is ok, gameplay is ok, the skill tree is ok, the graphics are... kind of ok I guess (aside from facial expressions and dialogue animations, obviously). Everything is neat but nothing is great. Except for the fact that you can turn into a nine foot werewolf, ripping your enemies to shreds. But that is probably the only thing that sets it apart from a bunch of other games that already covered all other aspects in a more fun and exciting way.The current Steam price however is fair and if you happen to get it on sale you can't really go wrong with it.Despite its obvious shortcomings I still had fun playing it and if you are down for a dark fantasy werewolf sneak/slasher game then it's the best you can get at the moment. If Splinter Cell had an edgy teenage furry child, it would be this.
_childDocuments_.name: Werewolf: The Apocalypse - Earthblood

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fun for what it is. It's not pushing a message at me, it doesn't punish me for not being stealthy, and the story while not fantastic also isn't horrible. I like that I can challenge myself by trying to clear an entire room without a single person seeing me, or just hulk out and whole sale slaughter everyone. The Crinos form FEELS powerful and I love that, it takes something of my own caliber to actually stand against me and thats fun. That being said there's the obvious issues like the graphics. The facial expressions are very robotic and things look like they're from 2010, not 2021. Spirit hunting, while fun at times, can get tiresome. They give you a crossbow, and talents to increase it, but theres so little ammo I never saw a reason to use it. One of the times I did use it two bolts hit an invisible wall and the third  disappeared. If you're going to get this I highly recommend waiting until its 10 to 15.

name: OUTRIDERS
detailed_description: OUTRIDERS COMPLETE EDITION OUTRIDERS COMPLETE EDITION includes all the released content for OUTRIDERS: OUTRIDERS WORLDSLAYER Expansion HELL'S RANGERS Content pack Five Exclusive Emotes OUTRIDERS is a brutal looter-shooter with unique classes, visceral gunplay and powers, set in an original dark universe. Play both the story and endgame modes in single-player or with up to two friends in seamless drop-in drop-out co-op. OUTRIDERS WORLDSLAYER EXPANSION The WORLDSLAYER EXPANSION allows owners of OUTRIDERS to dive straight into the new WORLDSLAYER game content. With new horrors to challenge you and new weapons, mods and gear to discover, you’ll be further developing your build through the new PAX hybrid branch class trees. Survive the campaign and you’ll face even greater horrors in the Trials of Tarya Grata, the brand new endgame. Which partnered with Ascension Points offers a new long term progression system for the most committed players. Finally, push hard through the new Apocalypse difficulty tiers, with each step up to level 40 increasing the chances of obtaining incredible Apocalypse gear and its game changing third mod slot. Reviews & Accolades 'Brutal and Unrelenting' - MMORPG Absolutely Incredible” - Gamers Heroes “THE SCI-FI RPG EPIC WE’VE BEEN WAITING FOR” - COGConnected “Grisly combo of gunplay and superpowers” - IGN “A bonafide hit” - Heavy About the Game OUTRIDERS is a 1-3 player co-op RPG shooter set in an original, dark and desperate sci-fi universe. As mankind bleeds out in the trenches of Enoch, you’ll create your own Outrider and embark on a journey across the hostile planet. With rich storytelling spanning a diverse world, you’ll leave behind the slums and shanty towns of the First City and traverse forests, mountains and desert in the pursuit of a mysterious signal. Combining intense gunplay with violent powers and an arsenal of increasingly twisted weaponry and gear-sets, OUTRIDERS offers countless hours of gameplay from one of the finest shooter developers in the industry – People Can Fly. A JOURNEY OF DEATH As mankind bleeds out in the trenches of Enoch, you must journey across the hostile alien planet in the pursuit of a mysterious signal that could save what’s left of humanity. Should you survive, the powerful Ereshkigal will be your ultimate test. FOUR UNIQUE CLASSES Choose from four distinct classes, each with its own unique abilities to define your personal playstyle. Assassinate your enemies as the Trickster, incinerate them as the Pyromancer, punish them up close as the Devastator, or engage them at range as the Technomancer, master of heavy ordinance. LOOK AND FEEL LEGENDARY Equip yourself with twisted guns and gear with unique savage sci-fi designs made from heavy, brutal metal and feral organic materials. And transmog your appearance effortlessly to any piece of gear you've collected. DEADLY BUILDCRAFTING Discover countless builds to crush your enemies in new and unique ways. Fine-tune your loadout with hundreds of mods across your guns and gear, multiple class-based skill trees, and attribute points. Once your build is perfected, you can turn up the heat by increasing the world tier to face harder enemies and receive better loot. APOCALYPTIC ENDGAME Put your skills to the test in Expeditions: 18 hand-crafted endgame levels featuring unique mechanics and challenges. And even greater horrors await in The Trial of Tarya Gratar, an intense dungeon crawl with brutal bosses.

_childDocuments_.review: So let me start off by saying it's normally good to read the negative reviews, but in this case be careful what you believe.  I've played this for a while now and am not stopping any time soon.  Reason being?  These devs KNEW what they were doing, and anyone who says otherwise clearly has a problem with challenges, paying attention to detail or learning from their experiences.  In this game, you will find that if you don't know what you are doing and can't pay attention to everything in the world around you, you'll die.  if you don't learn from that then you'll die again.  The game makes it so you can adjust to you're capability.  If you pushed too hard and got a world tier too high to handle, well then fix something.  What I mean by that is your gear is now too under leveled to handle that tier in one way or another.  Anyone who says that this game is unbalanced has not learned how to play this game.  One of the things about this game that I love is that it is TOTALLY solo capable or with a team, and either way you play it, it's challenging.  You can't just click buttons or sit there and watch things happen around you, and you can't get to a point where you'll one tap everything like in other poinless games. In a hostile world such as this you can't be just tank or just support.  Yes you have to do DPS in this game... but that doesn't make you not a tank or a support character.  I started as trickster and realized I had to be more than DPS to solo.  but tanking only means endgame takes too long to get as much loot, so I have to find that right balance that works for my play style. Each person is different but if you read the negative reviews, then you will get a false picture painted for this game.  Bottom lines are these:-Disconnect Issues: At the beginning of the game were an issue and have mostly been resolved... the ones that remain tend    to be the players connection (ISP) issues.  IF you have a bad service provider or a really bad bandwith, don't play it unless    you don't mind getting DC'd and having to reconnect.-Crashes: They have happened but rarely happen now, and no one can say ANY game doesn't have crashes especially at    the beginning of its launch (this game has been out 1 month and I may get a crash on ending the game but that's it)     People who 'say' they have a top tier computer either don;t have what they say or probably have an issue in software or    hardware that is causing crashes.  I have a good computer but not top tiers and I have rarely had ANY issues outside of    day 1-3 launch.-Balance of difficulty or classes?  If this is a complaint then you don't pay attention to details and/or don't know how to    adapt.  I have seen Devestators rip other classes to shreds in dmg and vice versa.  I've also tanked better as a trickster    than I have as my devestator... Learn more about the game by playing it and experiment with other ideas than you're    initial base thought.. then?  Stop complaining so that you can work through the problem and have a sense of    achievement in success.-Inventory loss: I have never seen this ever.  But the devs have literally said they are working on it and should have it fixed    soon.-I can admit that the story can be a bit depressing in how sh***y the world can be and how even worse humanity can be,    but that's more real than believing everything is glitter and rainbows.  If you don't like gritty then this game might not be    good for you.  If you like hard hitting gritty story telling then this is a solid one.-The need for connection during solo play:  I can say this shouldn't be necessary but maybe it is for a reason such as piracy    prevention.  In which it makes sense to protect your product.  Having to be connected can pose a problem for when they    bring down the servers for maintenance which may cause a DC while playing resulting in loss of loot or progression.  To    this end I agree that it's not a good thing, but this can't always be avoided like in any game... sometimes sh** happens.     But it would help to have a launcher or some kind of 'server is up' or 'down' signal to tell us why we cant reconnect/got    DC'd.-The so called "NERFS":  I love the complaints about these "NERFS"  People like to complain about things they don't understand.  They want to complain how the DPS build is the only build but when they 'FIX' (not nerf) the bullet abilities so that other abilities are as viable BECAUSE the calculations on the bullet abilities were going to obscene highs making it not challenging when the game is supposed to be challenging.  The legendary rewards were taken away from repeating missions because they were initially meant to be the first playthrough on a character rewards and not a spammable reward to be taken advantage of... again as to make things not too easy because its supposed to be challenging. ALL in ALL:  This is a Fantastically Great game with normal issues that are ACTIVELY being worked on and resolved at a great pace.  I rarely go out of my way to defend a game so much.  The devs seem very attentive to whats happening and are there to work not just twiddle their thumbs.  My only complaints are I wish that it was a little less bullet sponge and a little more skill based defeating and there needs to be more classes/expeditions/character slots.  I don't know why there are only 6 character slots but there needs to be more.  There definitely needs to be more expeditions because the grind from them would be less noticeable if it wasn't always  the same few over and over.

_childDocuments_.review: So, the company that made Bulletstorm made a looter shooter.  Cool.  They made a demo for it, and fixed it multiple times.  It ran well enough, and the loot hinted at in the demo that the game would evolve and play well, because they were willing to fix a demo with several fixes and updates to make it run smooth.I'm here to tell you that is not the case.  Server issues aside, they have decided to break most builds, through bugs that have not yet been addressed, or simply nerfing other viable builds while certain classes already suffer through a slog.  Sure there are some that can shred end game, but good luck getting there.It's a shame because you can see the game truly shine now and then as a fun single player or co-op experience.  But not enough. One thing that really annoyed me is they gated end game content in a bizarre way.  End game has it's own in game currency.  I figured that would be the case, but it 100% invalidates all other currencies in the game.  Sure titanium is still sorta worth it, but the others almost don't matter at all.  You trip over finding enough of them just breaking down the stuff you don't want.  Which is a lot of stuff.To make matters worse, they rewarded us that stuck with the game god rolled loot.  Hey cool, the whole reason you play a looter shooter is to get the top tier items.  Well, I got 'em. They gave them to me!  Now the whole reason for playing the game is gone!  Whose idea was that anyway? I mean seriously...One of three things happened to this game: This game got near zero QA, or it was released too early, or both.I really wanted to like this one, but I can't recommend it in the state it's in.Especially for the price they ask.

_childDocuments_.review: Outriders is an easy to recommend game. It stands out as being unique and fresh in many ways to me. There is a strong story and immersive world. The characters are charming, and I find myself drawn into the lore of the game quite easily. I feel the game-play and visuals are at the top of the genre. I have on a handful of occasions found myself in awe at the chaotic and engaging moment to moment of fights. This is supported very well by the large amount of diversity available in gear and skill choices and the combos of each. The outcome is a fresh feeling each time you step into a fight with a new build. The end game is repetitive, and a long grind, with random drops as an obstacle. This could be a pro or a con depending on your taste. I have found the most replay value in going back to try new classes or new builds as opposed to grinding a single character into the endgame.

Nobody is "going to get lost" if you remove the cutscene where you literally just open the door. Nobody is going to wonder where the boss came from with enough sound queues and notifications. _childDocuments_.review: Fun gun play, somewhere between Remnant and Gears of War (Speaking of Remnant, if you liked that you might end up loving this). The cover system could be better and farther utilized, sometimes it feels like it detracts from the game play. Much fun with friends in the same way Diablo is fun with friends. While the launch has been buggy and a bit of a shaky start, people can fly seem to be working hard at fixing problems and balancing things.      Fun builds that are interesting, Loot and build decisions matter, which is where outriders strikes out in the Looter shooter world very pleasantly to me, looter shooters really need to try and get more on par with top end arpg's and I think outriders takes a really damn good shot at that. This is one of the only Looter shooters where it doesn't feel like a race (gun wise) to get to the endgame, gun's start to get fun once you get blues (which have mods on them that can really impact on how they perform) I really applaud People can Fly on this, it's a rarity in the genre.As for the story, it's not great honestly, It could have been so much more, but it's decent enough where it didn't bother me. The level layouts all play fairly similar but lots of diversity in scenery, which is quite nice. nothing awe striking but interesting and pleasant enough where it doesn't feel boring to me.      While there is pretty good diversity in enemies There isn't anything that feels super new or thought provoking honestly, Outriders does enough with it's enemy roster where everything doesn't feel samey and on higher difficulties can make you consider your build, but I would like to see more added in either dlc or a sequel (Which I would love to see a sequel to outriders). Outriders to me is a bit of a flawed game with some wonderful nuances to it, show's great promise to grow as a series. I'm excited to see where this will go as time passes.

_childDocuments_.review: The scenery and the story are the highlights - both incredible (scenery) to great (story/plot).  The story flows and is interesting.  The world and world building they've created is alive and real.  When the game is working well, the gameplay is fun and addicting.  Hiding works sometimes, however, it's too sticky and many times you will die because you're doing the "hiding shuffle," which is pretty frustrating.  The guns mostly all feel real and you will get a plethora of them to choose from, though the Legendaries are lackluster in strength, but radiate in visual quality.  The other highlight is drop-in and out co-op.  It really makes the game fun playing with my friends and family.The low lights are that an entire class is FUBAR'ed and useless solo - the Devastator.  It is a completely broken class and when I play it, I utterly regret buying the game.  I hate it so much, I want to throw my computer out a 10 story building.  How could the devs screw up a class so f'ing bad?!  Have they even tried playing their class??!!  But when I play my main, Technomancer, with my wife and step-son, the game is semi-redeemed.  Some of the quests are broken, which is also frustrating and annoying and take a lot away from the game on the whole. The stats are mostly all broken - sometimes I have 48K armor and then I'll have 12K after unequipping some various items that have nothing to do with armor adjustments - lol.  Also, armor is broken.  There's another bug where my armor will just keep going up and up unequipping and requipping the same 2 items back and forth - I think I got it up to 2.5million, and then I died in 3 hits to an elite, so I know it was actually bugged.  Even if I have 48K real armor I can't stand toe to toe with anything, like a good tank should - I'll die with 3 hits compared to the Pyromancer who dies in 2 hits.  Devs - if you are going to make a melee / close ranged tank class, make sure they have the tools to do so.... duh.Overall, I am driven to finish the game due to the story and playing co-op.  Once we stopped going up in Tier's (read - difficulty setting), we really started to enjoy the game and oddly enough, I still recommend it because 51 is greater than 49 percent, so take my recommendation with a grain of salt.

_childDocuments_.review: --Review Edit 5/6/21--Since they restored my character, I can say that I do recommend this game. It seems like they've fixed a lot of stuff since my review, but we still have issues sometimes where one person will get left behind on an expedition. Luckily, the solution is just to rejoin now.This is a fun game if you like grinding for better gear. They definitely make you work for those Legendaries. But seeing how much damage you do and whatnot at the end of expeditions is really nice.--Original Review on 4/11/21--I currently cannot recommend the game. Why? I'm one of the players who's character got wiped. Because it's not just the inventory, but the character itself becomes unplayable. So there's no just getting a couple pieces of gear to get you through, you just lose complete access to that character. There's also the issue of disconnecting all the time (in multiplayer). We're doing end-game missions, have one enemy left, almost dead and I get an error and disconnected. THEN I can't even get back into the game without restarting my computer (this includes having to sit through the unskippable opening sequence every ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ time). It's a consistent enough problem that it happens at least once a day. We've spent 2-3 hours before trying to get all of us reconnected to a multiplayer game after having played together fine for a couple hours.Other than the stuff that makes it unplayable (literally), it's not a bad game. I liked the story and thought they added enough to make it interesting. It's very grind-stastic, but I think a lot of games are like that now.Once the major bugs are fixed, I'll update my review, but for now, it's not worth playing if you lose your character.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Play this if you love looters, but don't have the time to engage with a Games as Service style looter shooter. This game got review bombed pretty bad on launch day and so I felt like a review was warranted after investing time into the game. It is not stable. There have been some horrific technical elements of this launch. You have heard the horror stories. My experience was not that. I have a ROG Zephyrus with a AMD 9 Processor. I had around 6-8 crashes during my time with the game. They increased with the patch released during the week of April 12th. The Games as Service model has evolved in tandem with the looter genre and while I love the experience of grinding and working for that perfect piece of loot. I don't have the time to commit to maintaining active participation in a service model like Destiny. I have to compromise with my experience, when I play I know there are only so many things I can do because I don't have the time that so many GasS demand from the player base.This game respects your time so much. Everything you do in the loot loop contributes to the endgame, even from the beginning. The power fantasy that looters promise is that the end of the experience ebs and flows. You can scale difficulty, you can respect for free, the modification system gives a great deal of flexibility. In Destiny, a "God Roll" could be a gun you pursue all season until you get all of the right traits. In Outriders you have a lot leniency in making loot into a god roll. Finally, a things that bothered me about the criticism is the story. It is cohesive. It is has twists and turns. If you thought Anthem's setting and story had promise well People that Fly told the story that Bioware tried to tell better. My main jibe is that it is not a B-Movie plot. It is not a Scy-Fy original film. It's not that corny. You always know what you are doing in the game, but the stakes for why you are doing it are a little abstract at times.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay now lets do a solid review of Outriders.Now I am not a fanboy of any game at all. I see the games for what Developers said it would be, what they should be, and what they are. The truth does not set well with some people but it does not change the fact that it is still the truth.At first glance this game seems solid and really brings some new styles to the 3rd person shooter realm.... And in some ways this is true. BUT the game also brings very outdated systems as well. And these are things I for one, don't feel any game should ever have them in it. Now lets start off with the PROS of the game:A) The graphics are solid.B) The voice acting is damn good.C) The classes are nice and offer each person a different play style they can all like.D) The classes mix well and each one brings an amazing compliment to a multiplayer play style.E) The game sounds are not bad at all and really do help pull you a little into the world you are about to explore (For as much as you can explore in a railed game).Now on to the CONS of the game:A) SPAWNING ENEMIES: They appear right in front of you. This is poor design and not worthy of $59.99. This is cutting corners and simply cheesing out. They did not want to put the time into the game to make the A.I. a challenge. They chose to simply spawn everything around you. Pathetic, because this seems to have become the standard for piss poor game design in most games today.B) RESTRICTED COMBAT: If you start to get overrun at any point and you try and fall back to give yourself some space (Like in real combat) there is an invisible boundary that starts a timer while it reads "Don't lead enemies to your Allies". Then it counts down and loads you back to the start of the fight. It is already very much a rail game to begin with. But load boundaries are (again) pathetic. C) CUSTOMIZATION: Or should I say the lack there of? You have very little control over customizing your character look, colors, Weapons, Armors, and........ the list goes on. Even the color palettes seem to have been done by someone who is color blind. The vibrant color you choose turns out more like a really soft bland color. Black isn't even really black, it's gray. Gray is a slightly off white. Red looks Orange and Orange looks Yellow...... You get the point. No real thought into freedom of choice in a game that should really have brought that choice to the table, being that it is one thing that could make the game a little more likable.D) DISCONNECTIONS: The game has been riddled with issues but disconnections seems to be one of the bigger ones. Now we dealt with some disconnections when we played the Demo but NOTHING like after the game went live on April 1st.  Most of us battled issues when loading the game to crashing before the "Geforce RTX" window came up, freezes at logging in, servers not responding, crashing while loading into a multiplayer match and so on and so on.KIND OF A FIX BUT NOT REALLY: After days of crashing we all changed the DX12 to the DX11. The Demo played on DX11. DX12 is riddled with issues and this is a major reason why the game was crashing so much. After the switch we all still crashed but at much, much , much lower rate. (I hope this helps someone out)E) ANTI-CHEAT PROTECTION: This wonderful nightmare is another issue that crashes the game from time to time. Unfortunately there is not a way to shut it down without you getting banned.F) SERVERS: The servers have been an issue since launch. Crashing and/or rebooting without warning. People even lost hours of game play and items over this fuster cluck. The bright side is that the Developers have acknowledged this issue and are claiming "We are working on it".G) LOGGING IN TO PLAY SOLO: Well this brainfart has pissed off a lot of customers. Being that the servers have been less than reliable, people would just like to skip logging in and play offline. Well this is not an option with Outriders.H) The game has a solid story arch behind it but even with that, the play feels very dry. It is a rinse and repeat on all missions. You simply get bored playing after a short time. Now I like to complete a game and I will but I can guarantee I will be taking breaks often.Now I really wanted to give this game a rave review but alas I cannot do so. At this time in the game, we have had not one bug fix addressing these major issues. Even though some of these issues are game breaking. But I have hopes for the future. I am just sick and tired of putting money into games like this that release a turd and try and convince you that the issue is your $3500 PC.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're not like me and you don't buy EVERY game that looks even half-way decent that comes out, I suggest you hold off on buying this game (and probably never buy it).This game has really bad netcode, really poor optimization (graphically), poor servers with connectivity issues, an interesting story but poorly presented.The netcode: It's awful man, you rubber band CONSTANTLY when using skills, moving around near other players or monsters, even dodgeroll is glitchy in multiplayer. The terrible netcode makes the game's multiplayer feel like you're getting a ton of lag even though you aren't, even when you have great pings to the players you're playing with.Optimization: This isn't a beta, this is a full release. I'm using a 2080 RTX and I had to completely nerf my graphics, turn OFF DLSS, etc just to get the game to stop hitching frames. It really runs worse than ANY of the "full release" games i've played over the recent years.The servers drop people constantly, for no real reason there are CRAZY LONG load screens and waiting for connection screens - you spend half your time waiting on these, and if you're trying to "matchmake" you'll spend nearly 100% of the time looking at loading screens that are already at 100% bar but never loads up, ALT+F4 the game try again, even when matchmaking works you'll get massive lag and disconnects all the time. The way all of this is coded is seriously really bad, worse than Division 2 or Destiny 2 or any other similar genre game.Story : The story itself is actually pretty good - like if I were to spoil the whole story and tell you about it, it'd probably sound cool to you... however in-game it's represented TERRIBLY with bad actors, constantly cringy cutscenes made by a Polish company and I can only assume it's a lost-in-translation / cultural difference issue.. it's bad, and there are SO many un-needed cutscenes showing your character climb something, open a door, do down a rope etc for NO reason instead of just loading the next zone you get a pointless cutscene to watch and THEN a loading screen on top of that!All of this being said,The skill tree system for classes is very coolThe gear and itemization is handled BETTER than Destiny, BETTER than Division 2, and any other similar game!The way the World Tier system works, levels work, damage works, how difficult the game is, these things are all executed so well it's actually amazing. It's like the developers making this game REALLY KNOW how to make an amazing game! The problem is, the netcode totally ruins the experience.. just like we all feared when playing the demo and seeing how bad the netcode was.. they promised us the release would have better netcode.. but it's really ♥♥♥♥.The rubberbanding and "Not smooth feeling" gameplay in multiplayer is so bad it's hard to even compare it to another game because i've never seen a game of this genre do it this poorly.Also, while the game IS fun...The enemies you fight are not fun. Many times in this game - single or multiplayer - you will think to yourself, "WHAT THE ♥♥♥♥ JUST KILLED ME?!"There are marksman, trappers, and all kinds of random things that hit you from seemingly no where. (Especially captains and their anomaly abilities). MOST of their stupid abilities you will not see until you get hit by them.Part of this is because you are AIMING DOWN SIGHTS and this game has AoE warning circles on the ground beneath  you which you CANNOT SEE because you are aiming down sights (lol)   You could try hipfiring, but the inaccurate fire while hipfiring is so bad you'll probably not even hit enemies and you're not likely to hit their crit spots.The melee enemies are even worse, the bigger nasty ones, which the game throws a *lot* at you are almost totally immune to CC and resist everything, while constantly using anomaly magic samurai dash lunges at you which are extremely difficult to dodge unless you are only dealing with 1 or maybe 2 at a time. When there's 5+ of them, and there often are that many in multiplayer, - - combined with TERRIBLE NETCODE - - you will just die. You'll be running against invisible enemies, getting rubberbanded, all kinds of stupid stuff that shouldn't happen.I enjoy a challenge, I like "hard" games and I love difficult co-op games, and while this game has amazing potential, I don't recommend it to anyone that is expecting a "finished product" this is most certainly NOT a finished product. It's a buggy mess with awesome game design, but terrible netcode and terrible optimization and a LOT of frequent game-breaking bugs.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a dumpster fire, but for me the things wrong with it aren't things that are likely to be fixed.Alright, lets get one thing out of the way first, the gameplay (if you get that far. I have a solid pc, so I had minimal crashes, still more crashes than I had day 1 in cyberpunk 2077) is pretty solid. Gunplay is nice and the abilities are fun to use. I picked trickster, and the first 5 abilities you get as trickster are all fun to use. I have a sweeping sword attack that turns everyone into skeletons, a shield that slows time for everyone but you (looks amazing by the way. bullets entering the field or shot in the field start moving really slowly and you can see them), an ability that teleports you behind an enemy and slows them, an ability that loads your equipped weapon with void bullets that can explode people, and an ability that turns you into a beyblade (The animation is trash, you just T-pose, get particle effects and spin around really fast, but its really funny to look at). The weapons all feel pretty good. They have enough variants and perk rolls that they feel generally unique, and you can reroll perks on your weapons or switch variants using crafting materials. The gameplay loop is fun, even if everything looks kinda meh. Its a decent looter shooter.Now that the good is out of the way...Starting with the gameplay...Every mission turns into the same thing. Enter area, kill every enemy (sometimes there is a miniboss), the last enemy drops a key to get into the next area. Repeat. Killing every enemy is fun, its just I have played the game for 3 hours, done 8-9 quests, and they are all like that.Voice acting is flat and boring, and the writing is atrocious in all areas. Here is a summary of the story so far:Humans ♥♥♥♥♥♥ Earth...possibly. An apocalypse happened. Details on the largest event in human history are...vague.2 colony ships were built to go to 2 different systems to save the rest of humanity. There are cryopods and the ships are a couple of kilometers long each, so there would be a fair number of people. Maybe 2 million. This will become relevant later.The colony ship you are on arrives at a planet, and instead of scanning it from orbit, the first group of people land to begin exploring immediately. They then clear a camp about 1000 square feet to house everyone? Like the camp is initially about 1000 square feet with a cliff on each side. And they want to begin landing operations immediately.Anyway, after talking to your mentor, we know he's your mentor because it directly mentions this in the tutorial, in a cutscene that your character just stands there like a bored fridge for with 0 animation, you go off to find a probe that has been collecting data while lying on its side on a hill. You get to the probe and learn that there is another probe out there that is also transmitting, but you don't know why? There is only 1 colony ship in orbit. If you dropped 2 probes, you should know where they are.You and the other Outriders (apparently a separate group from regular colony security. I am long past it being relevant and I have no idea about their significance) go off to find the second probe. On the way, someone eats black goo and starts presumably dying. You continue alone to find out what the probe is doing. Its relaying a signal from another frequency. Your character writes the frequency on his hand...Anyway, a storm is brewing and you run back through it as red circles on the ground show where lightning is about to strike. You get back to the crew and all the outriders are just kinda getting evaporated. You jump into one of the vehicles with mentor, the only other 2 people to survive, and black goo man. The other 2 vehicles just ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ melt. Also the murder lightning hit you and gave you superpowers. I assume the reason is explained elsewhere why the 2 options here are literally float into the sky painfully evaporating from the feet up, or get superpowers. You get back to the camp and the person leading the colony doesn't want to let the people infected with an unknown disease and demands they be contained instead. For this common sense, your mentor screams at him, and everyone acts like not wanting an unknown number of important people to get a potentially fatal disease is unreasonable. So they kill mentor, and you shoot your way through everyone to get to the guy in charge and yell at him to stop the landing. Before he can, he explodes because a leaf landed on a car (I wish I was kidding). Next, you get put into a cryopod for unknown reasons. You aren't in any particularly critical condition. They just kinda shove you in without saying anything. No debrief on the probe you were the only witness to. No trying to give you basic medical attention. Just into the pod.You wake up some time later to find that you are in sci-fi WW1. A bunch of people with skull masks throw you into no mans land and expect you to die to a storm. Given that at this point, it is a known fact that there is a random chance for the storm to give you superpowers, this seems counterproductive. Now you get the ability tutorial. You fight your way through a brown muddy waste until you hit the other side of the trenches where a random guy appears to worship you for being an outrider and someone with superpowers, while Sephiroth without the iroth or the sword magnets ♥♥♥♥ into you then ♥♥♥♥♥ off. Look, his name is Seth, he has white hair and a long black leather coat. He gives off heavy Sephiroth vibes. Its the copy my work but don't make it obvious meme. Anyway, the guy who literally grovelled at your feet takes you to their side's general. Turns out, its one of your friends from way back when, who on learning that you are alive and have superpowers, wishes you had never woken up and would just go away, and it turns out you were asleep for 30 years. This is the end of the tutorial. It takes around an hour, and I unironically muted the voice acting for 10 minutes, then changed it to german and turned off subtitles. This improved the experience. Sci-fi writers should talk to some scientists to get things at least plausible. There are so many ways this could have been improved. Step 1: Start with a cutscene of Earth getting ♥♥♥♥♥♥ and an explanation of history.Step 2: Make the Outriders something other than just random dudes. Suggestion: The Outriders were people genetically enhanced to survive a potentially hostile and unknown planet. These genetic enhancements mean that when they get hit by the storm, they get superpowers.Step 3: Make the storm something everyone else dies to in horrible ways. No superpowers from the storm unless you are an outrider.Step 4: Humanity is not locked in a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ valley. This reduces the capacity for new cool things. Step 5: You are the only Outrider initially hit by the storm. It put you in critical condition which is why you get cryofrozen.Step 6: While you were in Cryosleep, factions emerged around different Outriders who ended up getiing caught in the storm and getting superpowers. Some stayed sane, others start believing they are gods, or turn into vigilantes. That gives you the option for potentially limitless factions based on Outriders and their children. You are woken up from cryosleep 60 years after landing (if you want to keep some of the original cast alive) either by your friends, Outriders who didn't go insane, or by other Outriders trying to get a leg up by recruiting another Outrider. Outrider picks you up, teaches you about abilities, then you decide you don't like him and escape to your friends, who, and this is very important, are happy to see you. In the end though, that would require a massive redesign of the game that is not doable. Get this one on sale and after the first few patches. Its fun. The games a dumpster fire, but at least marshmallows were provided.

_childDocuments_.review: So far I am deeply enjoying the game, with the story extending out over longer than i expected, and the game-play being good. For reasons i am unable to identify, I have run into none of the issues described by others. My game has not crashed once, and I have not been disconnected ever. I do consistently have the no HUD bug though, but a enter-main menu-enter fixes it immediately. I am using AMD 5700xt.The one enemy type though which I hate with a passion and is nearly unavoidable sometimes are the snipers, which instantly hit you if you peak in cover or move slightly into their line of site, and sometimes even when blind-firing, but that may be game design. Game looks beautiful, no re-use of assets, although enemies are mostly the same. For the love of god fix the mini-map, I need to find stuff by trial by error, because I have no idea where i am facing when looking at it, and the full map doesn't show it either.Modifying stuff can be a pita, because I need to remember what i want to modify then access the system, because the UI of modification is pretty bad.Bad stuff: modification UI, mini-map, potential enemy design.Honestly enjoy the game a lot, regardless of its issues, would recommend, but you may have more issues than me.EDIT:After finishing the campaign and running expeditions, I can say the online play is positively horrendous. Joining another's game makes your game feel like the enemies teleport at will and attack you; sometimes you instantly die because 3 of an enemy leap at you, but the game doesn't update until they have landed and dealt damage, which considering you are meant to roll to evade the attack is really stupid.The expeditions throw so many enemies at you that evading attacks is necessary to survive, but the second you join another's game, or someone joins yours the ability to evade goes out the window. You want me to play with others to finish this stuff but doing so makes the game unplayable, so you have to do everything solo. In addition, in high-level solo there is the same number of enemies, just lower health, and in certain expeditions the game spawns 3-4 boss-type enemies which can attack you through obstacles and/or freeze you, in most cases instantly killing, and there is nothing you can do.I still like the game, however the expeditions in their current form with networking issues are terrible beyond words, but I enjoy the game's mechanics so I will keep playing.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fairly fun to play though I can scale up the difficulty quickly.  But it's got so many issues... First, the netcode is terrible and you can't play Offline really.  This means the game regularly crashes on start up (apparently because of the 'anti-cheat' software).  You can't play co-op unless you're fairly close geographically.  And there are well documented issues of players loosing their gear because the game crashed while it was 'saving' (which it does all the time).  Second, the game is supposed to be a 'looter shooter' type game.  But loot is in short supply.  Add to this the fact that different gear can have widely varying stats and it's very difficult to setup a good build.  Though I will admit to not reaching 'end game' were I suppose things might change a bit.Third, Crafting doesn't allow you to 'make' anything.  You just modify the stuff that drops.  And it takes lots of resources which are in artificially short supply.  Forcing you to make do with crappy gear.  Unless you farm loot chests or rerun side quests.  Which is possible but painfully tedious and requires an outrageous amount of time.Forth, it's difficult to even report the issues you might be having.  Square Enix wants you to go through Steam.  Which causes a delay.  And even though I have a Square Enix account it's just difficult to get support.This is the bottom line:  I'd put up with all the short comings IF I could just play co-op with a friend.  See I live in Albuquerque, NM and he lives in Seattle, WA.  And due to the issues with the netcode it barely works.  But it crashes, disconnects, and generally fails to be moderately 'playable'.  By comparison we have no issues playing a variety of other games (think Destiny 2 or Borderlands 3 for instance).  So all this game has given me is lots of frustration!So they finally patched the game... This didn't really fix all the networking issues.  I'm still getting disconnected from the lead.  At the same time, my armor is now basically made of tissue paper.  Not sure what the Devs are thinking on this change.  So I'm done with this game.  Good Luck to anyone who chooses to play.  But that are other games I can play that are more fun.  So no need to waste time with something that was poorly designed and executed.

_childDocuments_.review: How to waste AAA game? Bugs + crappy end game + crappy coop = no players.I'll probably play it a bit longer after I've beat the main game with one character once.. I'll probably even buy DLC if it goes to a 90% discount (yet, DLC is way too expensive and game is so crap) to do it with another character and try few things it offers.. but I won't recommend to pay more than 20-25 EUR for game to anyone else.+ AAA game, nice vfx, sounds, animations, dialogues + voices;+ good performance;+ beautiful surroundings, various biomes, great art design;+ good story, interesting world settings, good lore;+ 4 classes, each with bunch of skills and class trees (+pax points and ascension with DLC);+ good combat: plenty of different enemies with different behaviors (aka AI);+ good gear and itemization, unlocking mods is fun, set bonuses are ok;+ different weapons, upgrade, mod customization, even sub-type change;+ difficulty balancing, world level, apocalypse level,+ despite levels are tunnel-like, there are hidden secrets to find: chests, ore deposites, lore...- lots of bugs;- no way to communicate in coop;- endgame is running expeditions (somewhat boring), feels grindy and not good rewarding, devs expect players to play hundereds of hours, there is another activity possible - resetting or doing in coop main quests, which is even less rewarding and overall feel pointless (poorly thought);- UI is also poor, worst is the map/minimap, it's VERY hard to navigate in this game,y lacking and limited stash, lack of hotkeys, many screen in screens, lack of description (e.g. buffs/debufs), timing mods cooldowns is impossible;- I dislike arenas design, basically I am approaching enemy defenses and can use outmost cover, but melee/charge enemy types force me to backpedal, unless my character is strong enough to survive/take them down.. this can lead to a VERY long backpedaling (sometime game doesn't allow it and my reset the fight after a countdown) and then forward to get another meaty enemy.. perhaps I should always play on world level 1 or what?- useless and annoying repeatable cut-scenes: when transitioning between levels and sub-levels, when using vendors, turning in quests;- some checkpoints are poorly thought, e.g. saving before loading a sub-level starting with long cut-scene before a boss fight.Biggest NO GO for me is a lack of communication in coop. I could easily spend hundreds of hours here, enjoying coop while farming gear, talking to players, sharing knowledge, making friends.. The devs were lazy to give anything to me, no server lists, no lookup, no filters by language, region, anything..Another thing which I couldn't master - is a controlling of character. It looks simple at first, but e.g. same key is used to dodge and to hop over obstacles, I often jump over the cover straight into bullets from enemies, instead of just quickly reaching the cover. Switching cover function (holding space) is a crappy idea in fast-paced action shooter, would be a good option in tactical turn-based shooter though.. I can't master switching to a right shoulder, there are always obstacles between my gun and enemy, but not between his gun and my face somehow.. Add to it bugs: the character may stuck in place, unable to run forward (due to a large collider of nearby item?) or refuse to use skill.I wish this game will be further developed. It has potential. It could be as fun as Deep Rock Galactic is (rather buy it, than this game). Removing bugs, adding or altering a thing or two. But I have feeling those devs are very greedy, look at price of their DLC (compared to a base game, which was reduced and that's why I bought it myself), which adds just a bit (compared to a base game).

_childDocuments_.review: So after playing through the entirety of the game and logging 53~ hours of playtime since release a few days ago, I can honestly say that this game has it's ups and downs but the issues are so prevalent that it makes enjoying the game for any decent period of time impossible. Here are my thoughts on what the game has to offer you: (TL:DR Below)** I will note that of the 53 hours I have logged, roughly 6< of them were being Disconnected and waiting to get back online. (being generous here it was very likely more than this if you include my co-op partner also disconnecting.) The game offers you a slightly decent story but nothing to write home about, challenging campaign experience for both solo and co-op play with gun play that encourages you to push into crowds of enemies and "kill them before they kill you". Hiding behind cover doesn't serve much a purpose other than waiting on ability cooldowns to come back up. The endgame is almost non existent when it comes to variety, but it does offer a fun experience to play through for a few days. This can be heavily extended if you enjoy playing multiple classes or builds.You can complete everything the game has to offer on a single character within 60 hours playtime. If that is worth 60$ to you, then feel free to buy it. I would suggest to simply wait until it goes on sale as the servers should be fixed by then.The ammo system and "On-kill" effects are my BIGGEST gripes about the game for co-op play. It feels absolutely amazing for these effects to work in solo, but when you are fighting for last hits on kills to restore your ammo in co-op it just becomes a miserable mess. Heavily reduces the amount of viable builds IMO and makes you feel like you are griefing yourself or your teammate by taking the killing blow on mobs. ** TLDR **Good:- Challenging Co-Op and solo experience. The game is definitely harder solo, but co-op is no joke either. - Gearing & Crafting system is great. Customization is numerous and you can make many builds and play styles.- Classes are well designed for the most part, many abilities and talent choices make your decisions matter.- Autoloot feature (Press H. to autoloot, auto loot rarity can be adjusted.)- Currencies aren't a complete grind to get- Gun play feels great when it works, which honestly is most of the time if solo. (Having infinite auto-shotgun ammo just feels really good.)Bad:- Terrible FOV for close-range classes. (Preference, really.)- While build diversity is there, it feels bad to experiment in this game due to the difficulty of the endgame & management of ammo + health/defenses.- Ammo is annoying to manage, especially in co-op play. "on kill" effects are prevalent and impactful. Does not play or function very well with Co-op.- Loot management for multiple gear-sets can be a chore as there is no way to mark or save personalized sets.- No Transmog, look like a circus clown all the time.- Progress is not shared between characters. (No mod sharing, No campaign skipping, hardly any level boosting if at all) You can however, trade loot between your characters VIA Stash.- Buggy mess. crash 10+ times a night to completely different things, auto-saving is trash, abilities bug out, mobs bug out, zones bug out, my character bugs out, can't rez, can't revive friend, friend can't revive me, monster op, monster immune, monster in air, monster fell through world. Bugged. Just really bugged.- Pretty bad balancing overall, but everything CAN clear all content. (Top end vs low end is a massive difference right now)The game was fun, I can say I enjoyed my time playing but I had a lot more patience than I normally would have. The servers were an absolute mess for 3 days on launch, and the crashes persist into day 4. I'd say this is a worthwhile buy, it's honestly got the making of a fantastic game. However I can't justify a 60$ price tag while the game is in its current state. I'd encourage anyone and everyone to wait till it's 30-40$ or balancing + tuning & stability updates come.

_childDocuments_.review: It's sad to see that there is so many negative reviews for the game when in reality it is a fantastic looter shooter. There is issues currently with the servers causing numerous disconnects but I don't think that means it deserves leaving a negative review when it will be fixed some time soon. This game genuinely makes you feel like a god only a few hours in as all of the powers and abilities are unique and fun to use, the way enemies just explode into mist or disintegrate depending on the class you are using truly makes you feel like a beast.The armor and weapons are also fantastic to use and collect as there is dozens of unique modifiers and abilities for you to collect with each upgrade to armor you get allowing you to essentially play a entirely different play style every few levels keeping things fresh and exciting. The crafting system also allows for some pretty deep customization to how you play your character as you are able to change one of the mods on any weapons or armor you are using into a different mod you have collected by dismantling older gear. For example with my devastator I crafted a set of armor and weapons that essentially allow me to life steal and regen health very quickly as I kill enemies allowing me to steam roll through the fodder and weaker enemies.The main downside I have with the game is that there is a lot of small loading screens when you go from one area to another that can get quite frustrating. There will be a cut scene that is 3 seconds long just showing your character jumping over a gap or opening a door that just seems not needed.Overall I am having a blast playing this game and I really think anyone who is on the fence about the game because of the mixed reviews should give it a shot and see for yourself if you enjoy it or not.

_childDocuments_.review: 50 hours under the belt (albeit some of it was just having game launched). Reached endgame, with Eye of the Storm left. Haven't touched multi yet.Generally, I'd give it 8/10 with possibility to put it notch higher if multi is bringing another hours of game.Pros:+ no BS. you really get what you pay for. Standalone, contained experience with no MTX, lootboxes, GAAS bloated skeleton of a game. This is fully executed product for 30-50 hours of gameplay you've paid for.+ builds, synergies, minmaxing, power fantasy. The general jist of looter shooters+ if Destiny 2 and Warframe had a violent threesome with Borderlands 3 while Division 2 was filming the whole thing and Deep Rock Galactic was peeping through the window - this is Outriders+ full support of devs. I just can't imagine frustration that they have due to Square Enix's faulty online infrastructure+ shooting feeling. Vital in game where you spend 90% of your time spewing bullets + performance. You can see that PCF put a lot of time into thinking this one through and optimizing the gorgeous Unreal engine 4 to make it work like a charm. Fast loadings (albeit frequent), no major bugs, visual clarity, sporadic audio cut-offs when there are 20938 sound channels overlapping, + a bit less obvious yet important thing - no grave imbalance between the classes. Cons:- servers, but frankly, for 50 hours straight I would say I had relatively unhindered experience.- enemies variety. This is a bit of lackluster, yet it might be fatigue due to long time already put into it.- frankly, I don't see much of the solo endgame at the moment. Eye of the storm and level 50 is my go to and then probably another character, however game would really benefit from like set items, more build defining uniques...- missing pvp which would be fun if PCF would change it's stance on GAAS and balance such mode properly Final thoughts. If you are in the market for looter shooter for foreseeable 50-100+ hours and got your index finger bored with Destiny & co., the Outriders might just scratch that itch. It is truly enjoyable game, occassionally (frequency might vary) hampered by repetitive encounters and server issues (which I'm certain it will be ironed out very soon). Ideas and concepts for future:* transmogrification is a must and despite game not having players' hub (since it's not GAAS) where you can flash out your sparkling new WMDs and robes, it would be nice to have outfit that you fully like rather than orange sneakers with predator skull helmet, tight spandex pants with a wet rag on your back. * Hunts, assassinations with more modifiers. Instances with affixed giving you bonuses, akin Borderlands 3 system. Increasing game longevity.* Environment interaction. Doubtly this can be implemented but as PCF worked wonders with environmental kills in BulletStorm, I thought we might have some of that in Outriders. * new biomes and enemies. At some point. Enjoy,DissTurbo

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT 2: After seeing the "fixes" that broke the game even more, I've abandoned this game, in which I put almost 100 hours for an experience that, ultimately, left a bitter taste in my mouth.The endgame isn't rewarding, armor not working makes it almost impossible to play solo, the abilities aren't balanced... What else can I say ? Ah, yes, the devs systematically fix the only bugs that make the game playable, while breaking it even more on other parts. This is an effin' disgrace.EDIT: RECOMMENDED, but DON'T BUY THIS GAME YET ! Elaborated a bit after playing for a few more hours.TL:DR - Good game, but servers are unstable.Progress at the moment: Level 21, World Tier 8Frankly, the game is good.I really enjoy playing it. The mechanics aren't bad at all, if you liked playing Gears of War you'll love it.It's a good mix between difficulty and bashing mindlessly through hordes of enemies, while mashing your abilities out of pure instinct. The passive tree isn't very elaborate, and the abilities aren't numerous, but it's just the right amount to enjoy it without spending hours theory-crafting your build. I don't know what the endgame looks like (yet), but it's promising.Also, the crafting mechanic is really nice and simple, relatively streamlined, and you'll be able to mix and match pretty much everything. For example, I'm playing the supposedly close-ranged focused class with a sniper, because there are really nice synergies and it's very versatile.But the servers are so unstable that I can't even play most of the time. I'm in France, and I can't play most of the evening because I can't even access the servers in the first place. And when I could, I was very likely to be ejected from my game if there were too many players at the time.Best example I have is from yesterday evening: I killed a boss, and it dropped an epic sniper rifle and about 50 titanium.I opened my inventory to check the gun, and couldn't read the stats, because I lost connection to the server.I reconnected, and to my absolute regret, the boss' drops weren't here anymore. No titanium, no epic sniper rifle, no rare ♥♥♥♥ to dismantle.I didn't run into a great deal of bugs, and can't exactly remember one in particular, except the occasional game crash, but this might be because I'm mostly playing solo at the moment. Unfortunately, so many players are experiencing game-breaking bugs that I feel the need to mention it. They're there, and depending on your setup and installation, you might run into a lot, or almost none. Please fix this; this could be a great game if it wasn't plagued with bugs and server instability.

_childDocuments_.review: Outriders manages to distinguish itself from its contemporaries by presenting a grim world full of bleak comedy and then pulls you in with a strong narrative hook, fast leading to excuses where you trade lead with the local fauna. The potential is immediately apparent, but that’s all it ever is, for it is plagued by a plethora of technical issues and questionable design.Armor and weapons lack variety and impact outside of the traits you can customize them with, many guns feel and sound the same, but at least armor provides visual distinction. Class trees, while impactful, are dull and only offers percent benefits.  Combat gets monotonous, a lack of diversity in enemy types leads to a lot of identical scenarios. At times environmental occlusion will not work, allowing the enemy to shoot you through walls.  The scaling is broken, meaning bullet sponges frequently appear, in one outrageous example an enemy required 9 minutes of sustained fire to bring down. Music commonly glitches out, the combat themes can get stuck in a loop or overlap with a duplicate track.	Given enough support by the developers, it might turn into something excellent one day.

_childDocuments_.review: There is a ton of stuff the game does great in the looter-shooter loot-loop genre. You can sense the devs are fans of the genre and where their inspiration(s) were drawn from. Or it could very well be our own experiences from games that came before it which makes me feel this way. Honestly I do not have a bunch of negative to say about it. Obviously it is not flawless and a lot has happened at launch & post launch which upset a lot of players. For me I will look past this and lean towards the Pros while including the Cons where i see them. I appreciate the time if you make it to the end of my perspective. I don't feel the need to over sell or underrate anything, we've played games of the genre before. And if you are new to this game style, maybe you may find something useful? First and foremost I really like the upgrading system. Love when you have freedom to mold as much as possible into your  character build. I am a tinkerer so being able to fondle my gear tickles my fancy. -Like Tony Stark building his prototype, Enhancing & Customizing. Stats & Synergy are a must which is definitely a strong suit here. 8/102. The momentum of the gameplay is a love/hate relationship. Pop into a zone with the highest gear possible, beat the ♥♥♥♥ out of everything reap the rewards and move onto the next. Rinse & Repeat. We also have the ability to increase difficulty for even more challenge. That is the process we all know and love but, there is a downside. I keep getting this bug that requires a LOOOAD SCREEN for everything lol. Everyone who has played it knows what I mean. And because of this, it simply slows down progress. The maps are honestly too small to justify a load screen for every enter/exit in my opinion. Loading in assets/enemies for areas that are small In combination with the wild goose chase map designs i.e the dead-ends, Outriders feels dated with the way these things are implemented. 6.5/103. I'm attracted to the beautiful locals - reminds of Monster Hunter: World in ways and the designs of the enemies feel barbaric. But the creatures give off a Remnant from the Ashes vibe to me. I don't feel the comparison hurts the game that much but it does feel too familiar to feel new.  One of the things I do wish that was different is the variety of mob types. Personally it feels dull (dated) mowing down the same style of enemies. Also their predictive paths and/or their spawn points hurt the combat but, that is just a peeve which is easily overlooked once you progress further into the anomaly. 9/10 4. The combat isn't much to talk about. It feels good, works good, animations & abilities look good.. What bothers me is a few things - 1. the way cooldowns work (soft lock) while waiting for enemies to fully spawn into frame. The rest of the environment can still be moving and attacking but will lock you out if a boss or a nest is spawning - 2. Waiting on cooldown & alt rotation just feels old. Maybe it feels like this to me because I've played games of this genre dozens of times.? Games like The Division share the same similar combat style. Nothing wrong with that per-say it works I'm just looking for something a bit more original.  Put that all to the side and the loot drops will make up for the dated combat. With a inventory that quickly fills, keeping you wanting to change and upgrade, the combat feels worth it in the end. 7/10And lastly; the post story content and how the story leads into it is pretty good. Having a ton of fun going beyond the anomaly and taking on expeditions which offer even greater difficulty then just World Tiers. Which also offers more equipment and a few other things that one would expect from endgame content. Getting to the endgame was a fun ride. I enjoyed the story and the characters each had their own personality. My only gripe was the personality of our character. It would have been nice to get a different tone besides the Take No Prisoners attitude. But, the world around you is unforgiving so it does fit the vibe of the game. Outriders isn't trying to be a hardcore rpg with heavy emphasis on story rich  dialogue options. It is a straight forward loot loop grind that is simple and effective. 8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: First off, if you like a game to be completely finished with no issues before giving it a go, then go look for another game. Its been a consistent trend for the last 5+ years for AAA companies to release games unfinished and this one is no exception. With that being said, if little things here and there dont bug you as long as the core gameplay experience is working correctly, then read on. This is not a live service game like Destiny 2, and as such I wont be comparing it to games like that. If I had to compare it to anything its got the gameplay experience of Borderlands with the rain of loot like Diablo. You've got your guns and your abilities. Your abilities arnt just there to supplement your gunplay like in Borderlands, they ARE your gameplay, just like Diablo. Anomaly (magic) builds will be spamming them off cooldown while more weapon-centric builds will still be using them fairly often. You cant win on just gameplay alone in other words. At launch there are 4 classes to play (In order from easiest to play to hardest): • Technomancer• Devastator• Pyromancer• TricksterTechno and Devastator are considered to be good solo classes while pyro and trick take a bit more setup. Overall the game has its faults, just like any other game from the last few years, but if you can get past those small issues and you enjoy the core gameplay loop that Borderlands and Diablo 3 gave rolled into a looter-shooter then you'll likely enjoy this game. For a much more detailed "review" of the game I'd recommend checking out Datto's recent video "Is Outriders worth $60?":

_childDocuments_.review: Devastator is a tank class that can't tank because there's no taunt or aggro control in this game.The core gameloop is speedrunning end-game content. That's it. Speed is all that matters. And yet, Devastator doesn't have an elemental ammo skill, so the only way it can complete the speedruns is to cheese gun-swapping with mods that have nothing to do with the class itself. And since the only thing that matters is speed, and there's always a mathematical fastest way to deal damage, even the other three classes have very defined build paths.If you want to enjoy this game, only pick one of the three dps classes, and follow the meta. Choice is an illusion, and replayability is limited. It feels like the devs didn't have a very clear idea of what to do with this game beyond the initial class-based shooter concept, sadly.Steam says I'm in the top 2.1% of achievement earners in this game (oof) so maybe my review is accurate. But the devs are updating it periodically, so maybe it'll be better by the time you read this. Hopefully.

_childDocuments_.review: I have enjoyed the hell out of this game. I waited about a week before getting it and by then the server issues that most people were complaining about were all but gone. I found the gameplay and story to be really engaging and it had my attention from start to finish. This is not a game as a service game. It's a play, beat it, optimize a build, enjoy the story and have a good time with it - but then it's done. Maybe chase all those in-game achievements if you want to... but the game wants to give you a fun experience without controlling your life. Just enjoy the time you spend with it and move on.Pro's: The loot system. As a veteran of many action rpg's this was a really fun system to play with, but the game has some wonderful features to help you manage the loot - and I hope future ARPG's take note and get influenced by this: I.E. they've raised the bar here.I personally enjoyed the story. It's not perfect, but I found it engaging and I couldn't wait to see where it was headed next.The gameplay is fun! It's a 3rd person Action RPG more akin to Diablo that focuses more on shooting stuff.  It doesn't re-make the wheel but it doesn't have to. I didn't find anything here that was a turnoff. Some cons: Online only. I don't understand why this is a thing with a game of this nature. Playing with other people and friends is fun, but it shouldn't be required if you want to enjoy it solo. It's also really confusing to players when the devs have stated it's not a games as a service game and yet the lobby and always online nature seem to contradict that statement.For a loot shooter, it's an odd choice to have to constantly toggle the compare option - it resets EVERY time you leave the character screen and it's really annoying. I hope this gets fixed because it does get frustrating after awhile.There are some sound balancing issues with the game around sound effects etc but these don't really affect the core gameplay mechanics. These will get fixed, but it doesn't hinder gameplay.Overall this game was well worth my time and I really enjoyed the journey. Look to spend roughly 30-40 hours in the game for the average person, maybe 60 or so for those who want to do all the things... but you will eventually get to a point where there's nothing left to do - and that's ok. That's the game the devs made. I personally got it at 60$ and felt it was worth the money, but I can also see it becoming more valuable to some as the price goes down.

_childDocuments_.review: Easily became one of my top 3 games. The story in this game is one of the best I have seen in a long long time. Highly recommend reading all the journal entries as they give the story more depth and emotion. Voice acting and dialogue is entertaining and does not become stagnant. Gets better further into the story.Fun to play both solo and with a party. The AI does get stronger the larger the party, so it does get a bit strategic at some areas. Check your gear, check your abilities, etc. from time to time.Controls are fluid and if you are familiar with all your abilities, weapons, etc. you can get really aggressive and creative in firefights.The world tier system setting loot rarity and gauging your skill/difficulty is solid. I was stuck at a tier for a while, but once I learned some of the other mechanics built into the game I was able to climb higher. Others I have played online with mention this game is a good cross between Destiny and Anthem.Most of the negative reviews I have seen both on Steam and online have to do with having to be online at all times to play. When this initially launched there were issues connecting to the servers and loosing loot. But now the servers are noticeably more stable and the fixed the loot issue in a recent update. I have not had a disconnect or could not connect to servers issue since April 03. I am hearing though it did vary in other regions though. That was weeks ago, have not heard about connection issues from others in a while now. I have seen some glitches and disconnects from a party, but simply just rejoin the game. Only downside is you loose maybe a minute or two trying to figure things out. What I have noticed is this game seems to be more stable with Nvidia cards than AMD. What I would recommend is lowing the graphics settings to medium or low (game will still look good) so performance is maximized. I am playing on high with anti-aliasing set to medium, because on Ultra or anti-aliasing set to high there were noticeable performance issues.

_childDocuments_.review: "It fails to even convince me that we are on an Alien planet"This is the quote i subscribe to, it has been ringing in my head for the entirety of play single player playtrough.Everything about this "alien" planet is so human that it might have wel been earth in another fluffed up dimension.TLDR: destiny 2 and the division lovechild pulling an Anthem.my issues with this game are numberous so il list them for the most part.*hitboxes of weapons, enemies and attacks.*the cover system randomly walking you everywhere.*enemies phasing trough terrain *enemy AI not activating when in combat.*enemies appearing out of thin air.*ragdolls blocking shots.*missions crashing the game when activiating dialog during certain events.*mission tracking not working when teleporting.*mission objectives not appearing.*minimap/large map being terrible to navigate.*no pauze option when playing solo.*no preview of class abilities when selecting your class.*cubical combat zonesThese are just the objective bad things this game has to offer. things that could get fixed but probably wont ever be adressed. now to the subjective list.*god aweful story.*weapon diversity limited to about 11 but most do the same thing.*Skills are mostly unimpactful or utterly useless.*game wants you to use skills but punishes you for ever being out in the open.*this is just earth 2.0 everything is so human from buildings to plantlife it fails to convince you that this is an alien planet.*terrible blood effects when killing enemies.*lack of information regarding what weapon mods do, (what is ash? why does it exist 3 times?!)*bullet spungy enemies that take forever to kill unless your constantly ontop of upgrading your weapons and armor.*spray n pray mentality of this game. you cant imploy tactics or strategy, just run and gun because anything with precision is pointless to use.*bigger clip = profit. *enemy design is rather dull, there is maybe a handful of enemy types like gunners, snipers, heavy weapons, shotgunners and run at your face for bonks. these are copy pasted everywhere with a different skin attached.*monsterous enemies numbers in the 5 to 7 maybe? they just have a different color occasionally.*voices not syncing with characters both in and out of cutscenes.Truth be told there would probably be more things to complain about. but i either forgot about it entirely or i hvnt encountered it enough to make a note of it.in the end of it all, its maybe worth 20 bucks or if you have gamepass. but for full price its far to unpolished and uninteresting. the 2,0 update added transmog which is fine but its not a selling point. especially with a lot being just recolors of existing weaponry and legendary equipment only appearing towards the extreme late game. as in after you finished the story to do repeatable expeditions. i hvnt bothered with that myself because i got burned out by the end of the game.
