_childDocuments_.review: If you're a casual gamer who just likes to run around and shoot things like me, this is hands-down the best looter-shooter currently on the market.  The gameplay is fast, fluid and unmatched, the visuals are pretty to look at, and the story shows a surprising amount of effort for a game that didn't even really have to have one.  Most of the complaints I see for this game fall into two broad categories: (1) Launch week technical woes, and (2) hyper-serious gamers who can't find a specific loot drop thingamabob they wanted.  Well, I just downloaded this game at the start of May and I have not experienced a single bug in 12 hours so I guess the technical complaints have been ironed out, and I really don't care anything about specific epic/legendary/BestEver loot; if the next gun up does more damage than the one I've current got that's plenty good enough for me, and so far there's always been a better gun.  And really, you can just drop some iron on a gun you've already got to boost it until you find something better anyway so the loot system isn't that big of a deal.Bottom line:  Serious hardcore gamers may want to wait or pass on Outriders right now because apparently those kind of gamers have a lot to complain about until the game gets tweaked some more.  If, like myself, you really just want to explore an alien world, see cool stuff, and feel like a sci-fi demigod, Outriders is definitely the game for you.  Just set the World Level on 3, don't ever give it another thought, and enjoy yourself.  I even payed full price and don't regret it one bit.  In fact, I'll be getting any DLCs for this game the day they come out!

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:StoryCharactersVoice actingAnimationsSkills and classesCombatCrafting system (limited as it is)Cons:Expedition TimersEnd game (Expedition Timers)This has been one of my favorite games thus far. The story was interesting and well done. The combat is a blast regardless of which class you play. The pace of the game felt great all the way to the end of the storyline. The problem with Outriders, is the Endgame. While story wise, the expeditions fit, However, the expedition timers remove the ability to play your character the way it has been played through the entire game up to that point. This is a cover shooter that removes the ability to use cover in the endgame. There are some awesome tank builds, that you CAN NOT use at endgame, not because they are not effective, because they are, but simply because they dont kill fast enough to get even a bronze in the expeditions, much less silver or Gold. This is not a case of "I'm complaining because I am not good enough" I gold every expedition on CT15 with my Devastator (in a group) or my Trickster. But if I want to play my Devastator the way I had him specced throughout the game, or a sniper, sitting in cover taking out the boss while my teamates wipe out the rest of the room? not at endgame.

_childDocuments_.review: Now that I’ve had time to fully blast my way through Outriders, it’s time for our final review – we appreciate your patience! Now, People Can Fly’s gritty, blood-and-guts take on the co-op looter-shooter RPG genre definitely delivers great action that’s kicked up a notch by impressive sci-fi super powers, some cool world design, and a pretty satisfying loot grind. At the same time, an occasionally clunky interface, some persistent bugs, and a messy story make it seem less like a big-budget science-fiction epic and more like a guilty pleasure Sy-Fy Channel™ original series.

_childDocuments_.review: Update after 40 hrs:The server problems at the beginning were shameful and quite frankly should not have happened. If you want to read more about them, you can read my day 2 review further below. After a couple of days we could start to play and it was quite enjoyable. There are some really weird decisions made by the devs that I personally won't ever understand. Why would you have a  cutscene to traverse any part of the map? You go through a door? Cutscene! Jump a bridge? Cutscene! Go through a tight space between two cars? Cutscene! The map portions between cutscenes are tiny and u can just skip them. It has become a running gag in my play group that everything has an overly useless cutscene. Then there were bugs all around. But all in all, the game was enjoyable. Then I entered the late game and went through expeditions. Those were challenging and enjoyable as well until I hit the jackpot of ♥♥♥♥. The dreaded inventory wipe accompanied with the server connection issue. Basically everything I have accumulated over 40 hours of gameplay has gone up in flames and disappeared. My gear is gone and every time I try to enter the game with my character, the server boots me out of the game and back to the title screen. If I don't want to start over with a lvl 1 character, the game is unplayable now.That kind of game breaking bug is more than unacceptable for a game that comes with a AAA price tag. It does not help a lot when the devs announce that they are investigating and hope they might be able to restore the lost items. But they might have other stats. After they said the last patch should made things better only to come back shortly after saying it seems the patch made things worse instead. Not a trust building measure at all.I will stay clear of this game and everything that Square Enix and People can fly touch. This is not quite a Cyberpunk 2077 ♥♥♥♥ up, but it is a close runner up.     Just a quick update on the inventory wipe. I hear the devs are investigating and testing. No solution in sight but they will let us know asap. After about 2 month into the issue (it was already present in the demo), this is a disgrace. To give insult to injury, they managed to implement another bug with the last patches that now gets people the pleasure to instantly die while receiving damage. Basically another way to completely make the game unplayable. Every time you think they can'T make things worse, they do.  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------Day 2 review:The demo looked fine and got me and my friends into buying the full version. Turns out the demo was a scam and the full version is unplayable. I get disconnected every 10-15 minutes and can't log in for about an hour. The graphics decide to turn to software rendered ♥♥♥♥ show randomly and there is bugs all over the place. I'D put up with all of it for the fun that is exploding dudes in a time shift bubble. But we weren't able to play together for longer than 10 minutes so far and that is a shame for a game that was created as a co-op experience.Too bad I tested long enough to not be able to refund it. I'd give it back in a heartbeat. Shame on this mess, it's Anthem all over.

_childDocuments_.review: I actually don't understand all the hate the game is receiving. 1-  I have the exact same performance as while playing the demo (it was a demo, not early access, so I didn't expect improvements anyway). 2- I got disconnected once during around 6 hours of gameplay (playing right after launch, still day 1), so it's expected. Yeah, you're playing alone, but the game is a lobby, it's not "solo game that requires to be connected" as most are saying, it's a online game, you're playing a lobby solo, but it's still an online game. If you have performance issues even after updating the drivers, try running DX11, seems to solve almost every performance issue (if you have a decent rig anyways).I can't say anything about the endgame, but I've seem a guy trashing the endgame with 0.7 hours of gameplay (How? The game is around 25 hours to beat). Up to the point I've played, the game is loads of fun. The gunplay is very similar to gears of war but a little less stiff. The wall cover mechanic needs a bit of work but it's not bad. The crafting system is very good, I don't feel like I'm wasting resources at lower levels, it makes me want to experiment.I've seem some people complaining about bugs with the HUD not showing and the crossplay between PC and Console being broken, haven't experienced any of it up to this point, but the game launched yesterday, not nearly enough time to leave a bad review just because of that.TLDR: It's an online game and people are leaving bad reviews with some unreasonable claims (for normal day 1 bugs and glitches) and some straight out lies. Game is not perfect, but it's still good and worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: I have just finished the first playthrough after 40-ish hours. I did not play the game at launch so my review is based on the current status of the game as when I wrote this review.Outriders is what it's advertised - a linear shooter & looter with RPG element. It is also not a live service game - meaning you paid for the total content and no features are locked behind microtransactions (at least up till now).The story is decent and interesting but it is not like something you've never seen before. There are good and bad cutscenes but overall experience is entertaining. The main character has somewhat laid back attitude and does not really give a ♥♥♥♥ on pulling the trigger - typical mercenary type. It is not necessarily good or bad, just the matter of preference. I don't take things too serious while gaming so I kinda dig the humor of the game. The character voices are well done as well.The gameplay is what worth mentioning for this type of games. The gunplay or combat is good, satisfied and responsive. Builds and mechanics are decent comparing to majority of the same type of games. It can get quite addictive if you are into shooter & looter.The visual and audio is very good. It is also running smooth on my GTX 1070 with a few graphics tweaks.There are still quite some flaws and bugs in the game which are minor annoyances. However, they are not game breaking in any way. There will be ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ moments when you would be screaming out loud because of a certain bugs, but in the end if you are just to enjoy like me, it is fine.Unless you overhyped the game yourself, I think Outriders actually delivered what it promised. I do recommend the game because I feel like it is worth it. Maybe get it while it is on sale if you are in doubt (due to the current review rating) or you can also try the free demo for yourself. Take it easy and you might end up enjoy playing the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Such a great game, just can't give this game a positive review in its current state.The game crashes way too frequently, the fact that I'm forced to play in DX11 and windowed mode to avoid crashes is just dumb.Just last night I experienced a crash right when we killed the last mob in an expedition and I missed out on both the loot and the drop pod resources, this crash really didn't help with my already horrible experience in this game.Might return whenever they actually push out updates.Performance is decent, could be way better, especially in the towns/hubs.Servers are completely garbage, it's now almost 2 weeks after release and they still suffer with inventory wipes, people can't join co-op and the ones that actually connect to each other experience latency issues. if they get to fix the massive amount of random crashes, this game is a no brainer if you like looter shooters, but for now the game is in a horrible state.They should honestly have delayed this game 6 months minimum to work out all these game breaking quirks that a lot of people seem to experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Outriders should be a Game of the Year contender, but it probably will not be because of launch day issues: server connectivity, graphics instability, inventory deleting and progress reset bugs, to name a few. But, the campaign is absolutely fantastic and quite memorable.I had frustrating moments, especially when an event or boss had two stages and failure in the second stage resulted in a reset to stage one…I know it’s an old common game mechanic, but it is still annoying.I liked the implementation of the side missions: even though they are sometimes directionally buggy or may not activate when you get to the right location. Going back to the game’s lobby and re-entering the campaign usually fixed the faulty GPS or in-game missing mission start button. The high reward giving Hunt missions were my favorite.Shooting Enoch’s native fauna and other modified humanoid was very satisfying. The visual and sonic feedback of enemies being dispatched was quite enjoyable.The Altered in Outriders is a modified human with powerful god-like abilities that would make even Zeus himself wish he had an Assault Rifle that can call down lightning.Outriders is at times frustrating, but it is also an epic story containing funny and spectacular moments set in environments that truly amaze.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is good.At its core, Outriders has good gameplay and an interesting premise. The gear upgrading system feels great, swapping weapon mods and creating the best character that you can is fun.Pro-   story   gameplay   skill tree   how abilities feel   craftingCon-   Server instability   DX12 issues   Losing my HUD for no reason   Online OnlyAt the end of the day, I wish that SQEX and People Can Fly had looked at their demo numbers and then anticipated at least triple the people in the real release. There are issues connecting to the game itself, this is a problem because you can't play offline, so if servers don't work, you can't even play single player. I assume online only was a choice made to prevent offline duping or something along those lines. I've experienced mild stutter issues as well that others have attributed to poor DX12 implementation. One of the most tilting issues I've had is loading in to find that I have no hud. Returning to lobby and restarting the game doesn't fix this. It's only solved by selecting a different story point, then reselecting the story point you were on. While these issues are annoying, it's not the worst launch I've ever experienced and after these issues are fixed, the game will be a banger. As of this review, I'm a level 18 trickster.

_childDocuments_.review: The game has the potential to be fun if you play with friends.Most of the time it won't because of technical issues like lagging in co-op or random crashes.But there are players who got hit with much worse problems, and the developers obviously don't have a focus on helping them. And don't even think about the matchmaking or crossplay, DirectX 12 still isn't working for me.The campaign is mediocre at best and feels like they were running out of time at the end just telling you the big story twist with scattered documents.But the worst part is the endgame. To progress AND to get at least a chance on good loot you have to run the same few missions again and again, with enemies one-hitting or stunlocking you, and a timer that's not forgiving any mistakes. So don't think you can just have some easy fun rounds with your friends; or play careful and tactical instead of just running in with blazing guns; or that you could step away for a minute or two.And even if you sit through all of that, drop chances are just ridiculously low, and without almost BiS gear you won't advance. So it gets really boring really fast and is not rewarding at all.And while those problems are known since launch and some even since beta, the developers are inept to handle them. Instead they are busy "balancing" and "fixing" stuff, usually in a way most players see as nerfing the few only viable builds instead of buffing the other options to make those playable too.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR - Wait until you can get it really cheap or for free with something...Outriders has it's moments. The combat is actually pretty fun (when it's working). The skills make you feel like a god and really do make dashing into combat as an utter wrecking ball extremely fun. The classes all have their own reasonably unique feel to them which makes each bring something a little different to the table. Similarly, the modding of gear is very much at the forefront, since as soon as you get something new you're going to go and mod it to suit your character. Even the story is passable. I actually enjoyed the player character just being, generally, an utter bastard and thought it was a refreshing change from the usual saint/saviour experience.However, the technical side of this game is a shambles. I've lost count of the number of crashes I've had over the two machines I've been playing on. Multiplayer lacks voice chat, so you can't communicate with your team in a *cooperative game*. There's not even a ping system to show that there's an ammo/loot box. My favourite bug of all though is the absence of sound for incoming damage, or the wild "one shot" deaths, where everything goes from peachy to death and there's sweet FA you can do about it. Oh, and that map... jesus christ, whose idea was that useless map?<EDIT> Ok, my new favourite bugs might be it: 1) robbing me of Legendary items redeemed as part of WT completions; and, 2) the weapons bugging out so their mods don't function. After being released for 2 days shy of 2 months, this game is still an utterly buggy mess. </EDIT>I'd be lying if i said that I didn't enjoy many sections of Outriders. But, I find myself constantly just dialing down the world tier to a lower level with little challenge because I'm tired of being one-shotted, or receiving a crash as I'm nearing a final area, only to have to do the whole thing again.As I said initially, get it when it's cheap with some mates, and play it through. The MP is pretty fun and the story isn't terrible. Hopefully they'll fix the countless bugs/issues by then...

_childDocuments_.review: Outriders is a quite simple concept, whereas it attempts to comes across as a  and  hybrid. The core mechanics of the game work and do not work at thesame time. I will elaborate some of these mechanics. The cover system is absolutely shoddy. Probably the shoddiest I have seen in alot of shooter games. It's wonky and rarely does whatever you want it to do. Want to go to the cover in front of you? Let's take a left and get swarmed by the enemy. Not to mention the mechanics of healing and the cover system. Two out of 4 classes need to be up close in order to heal from a kill. And I could keep going on like that, but I'd prefer to move on. Let's put it simple, the AI is not sophisticated or advanced. It's basic as it can be. This is the coding of the AI: Take cover -> Shoot -> Use a skill / rinse repeat.If the AI are a bunch of creatures it's simply swarming you until it gets so extremely chaotic, you will lose track of what you are doing. There is no input or audio that you are going to get attacked from behind, forcing you to spin around like a pinãta on a party infested with ADHD toddlers. There are four classes with each their own unique skillset. So far I have played the Devastator, so I can't go on and tell much about the others (they didn't seem interesting to me), so I will talk about the Devastator. While meant to be a tank-archetype, it doesn't feel like that. At all. You're down quicker then a bottle of whiskey at an AA-meeting. So I can only envision how other classes will be. The ratio of skills/damage/armor and HP are quite poorly balanced, especially when progressing world tiers.  Just don't.... it feels like a quickly coded, poorly envisioned game, that has been hashed out in the hope it can pick up on something 'unique' wich it clearly doesn't. It may be fun for a bit, but once grind and repetitive gameplay kicks in (Roughly after a few hours), you will feel this game is FAR from being worth the money being asked. I'd reccomend playing this with the gamepass and not spend a dollar/euro/rouble/shingle more on this game.

_childDocuments_.review: FPS veteran in general, and an enjoyer of Borderlands and Destiny 2.I really wanted to like this game but I just couldn't bring myself to do so. Note that this is just on the base game and not regarding the DLC which I purchased but was unmotivated to continue onto. I went through the game completely solo. I didn't want to feel like I was getting carried or anything so just went through solo. I went with the assassin class which felt like a relatively poor choice for solo. Most of the healing abilities relied on being close to enemies who could just blast AOE damage and kill in a couple of bullets. Maybe this was more of a factor of me always playing on the highest world level available (which the game has a setting to automatically upgrade), but who wants to play a looter shooter only to stay at a low level and not upgrade equipment?In the end the strategy for virtually every map became the same. Use a long range gun to target elites, kill close range enemies with close range gun and abilities, kite the boss enemy of the room. And the extremely disappointing part is that none of this was exciting because the enemies were really simple and basic. There's only a handful of enemy types that just get reskinned throughout the game and each one of them always acts in the same exact way. There's also more or less a standard mix of enemies so the story just becomes this repetitive slog through reskinned rooms of the same enemies you'd been fighting this whole time with no excitement.And in terms of the actual loot, the special effects that get added onto gear and equipment feels pretty monotonous. Just the same types of additional effects that you see over and over on a handful of weapon types. Not to mention most of the effects are not even applied to the weapons themselves but to your character's skills which just makes the actual shooter part take a backseat to trying to build around character skills. As I mentioned, maybe my class selection was really off the mark, but I spent a lot of time just shooting in this game. So the weapons being all more or less the same (all LMGs felt the same, etc) truly made the story mode a slog.IN CONCLUSION / TLDR: So please note, I played Outriders single player through the entire campaign and always playing on the hardest world level (enemy level) so that I could level up more and get stronger loot. The enemies felt too basic with little variety, the weapons equally as plain and simple. Again, I wanted to like it because I generally enjoy looter shooters but I think borderlands and destiny still beat it out.

_childDocuments_.review: This poor game has stellar mechanics, an intriguing story and seemingly deep lore. There are a litany of technical issues that are somewhat outside of the developer's control such as the publisher's server issues (which is unacceptable for SQUARE ENIX of all publishers) and graphical issues that seem to stem from the latest Nvidia driver update.The developers have been 100% up-front on what's going on, what they're doing to fix it, and putting a massive amount of resources into resolving everything they can while Square Enix tries to resolve server issues.It's completely understandable that people are annoyed. You pay a lot of money for a supposedly AAA game then it falls flat out of the gate. It SUCKS.However, I'm reviewing what I've been able to play of the game so far. Combat is snappy, the loot-shoot cycle is addicting, and I'm so invested in the world of Enoch. I know I'm going to sink a lot of time into this game once the technical issues are out of the way. It has all the makings of a master-class experience. However, hold off if you're easily incensed by Day One hiccups. Very few modern games--especially that aim for this kind of scope--release without a hitch. And before someone comments that old games didn't have these issues, you're right; they had completely different issues that could never be fixed and were also far less complex. You'd think that Cyberpunk would've taught a lot of consumers about not buying in right away if they're afraid to wait.As for people complaining about online-only when they're playing single-player... You're NOT playing single-player. You are playing solo in a private online match. I don't understand why this is so difficult to grasp.

_childDocuments_.review: Let's just get down to it.If the reason you are buying this game because it look and felt similar to destiny then no, don't buy the game. The game play itself is similar to games like gear of war. Wherein you are in a third person shooter that place emphasis on using cover to avoid taking damage and moving forward while mowing down enemy and getting to the goal. The game give you four playable classes. Each class has eight skills in total, starting with a single one and unlocking more as you level up. Each class also has three sub-classes you can spec out with the Class Trees, and you are free to change that at any time. Class trees are split into three branches made up of small and large nodes, granting bonuses to your character's attributes or greater percentage-based bonuses affecting other skills respectively. While each branch is unique for each class, they're essentially grouped into weapon damage, survival, or Anomaly power.The classes are as follows:-Devastator : Close range tanker play-style -Pyromancer : Medium range play-style -Technomancer : Long range play- style-Trickster : Hit and run play-styleIn my opinion out of this four classes the best to used would be technomancer. Since you are require to just deal damage to regain back your hp. Pyromancer regain hp by killing marked target. Devastator heals through all closed ranged kills. Lastly Trickster heals when killing enemy at a closed range. -Gameplay/customizationThe combat for the game is satisfying for the most part. Abilities felt impact full and rewarding for some of the classes. Customization for the character is pretty lackluster. The addition of transmog later on in the game atleast make my character didn't look like he just got robbed and put on any clothes that he find. The grind for the most part is alright, but it is understandable if everyone not down for it.  But if you are looking to farm legendary item would require to be in late game and at least the world level need to be higher. But if you are just playing casual , there are side mission that you are able to do to get better equipment and so on. Side note don't play this game more than 90 fov. If you feel it is not enough trust me its enough . If you play on +100 fov i respect you. I don't know how people able to play it without motion sickness, I tip my hats of to you sir. -Story-I am just gonna simplified it to not spoil for people that haven't play this yet. Basically, after earth literally can't be livable. Earth decide to build a spaceship and go to a distant planet that similar to earth. The game start as you the player called Outrider, Outrider are soldier that are send beforehand to new planet to scout if it is safe for the colonist. Long story short you found a distress call from a ship similar to yours. You try to find the source of the signal. You gain power from the mystical planet. Lastly you use the power you receive to pave the way. -Cons-I don't know why they choose to have the cinematic camera to be film like they getting chase by people. I am not getting the feel of the story, the only thing i got was motion sickness. The scaling for some of the bosses are pretty weird at one point they felt like pushover and another part they almost one shot you. Gears are pretty much randomize good luck with that, pray to the rng god that you get good loot.-End note-Is the game worth to buy ? Not really. Don't get me wrong it's fun and all but doesn't really pull you in from my perspectiveOnly buy this game if there is a promotion or sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Single player mode, while playing through the story isn't too bad. Once DX11 option was available, few crashes throughout the whole campaign. Coop is terrible right now, can read the cons below.Pros+ Decent graphics, worlds look nice+ Okay story+ Pretty good variety of armour, weapons, modsCons- Lots of bugs, fortunately (at least for me so far), none have been game breaking- Visual/audio glitches- Too many repetitive cutscenes, level layouts- Game balance: okay in story mode, non-existant in endgame (unless happen to have perfect gear/mods)- Coop is terrible: lag, very few viable builds (see point above, unless you're high DPS get kicked more often than not)- Replayability: if you want to try different classes, have to go through the whole story for each character (maybe this wouldn't be so bad if each class had a somewhat different approach with some variety in sidequests or something)- Endgame: boring and repetitive, right now DPS due to timers is only option, could've easily had:* variety of missions/objectives instead of one* incentives to play coop with variety of classes* more customization options (e.g., ability to switch out all mods, legendary having 3 mods etc.)- Nerfs: weird decisions by developer to nerf builds, sometimes without fully notifying players of exact changes, given it's a non-competitive PVE game, makes no sense, especially given the OP enemies and AIOverall, given the price they want for this game, it is NOT worth it at this time. There is nothing new gameplay wise that they bring to this title, the story is not that great, and at least right now endgame is not looking great.

_childDocuments_.review: I've tried well known titles such Borderlands 1/2 and Destiny 2, but neither of those hit me as hard as Outriders did. Maybe it's because I had no expectations, as I only learned about the game 1 day prior to its release. That said, it is easily my favorite looter shooter that I've played so far, to the point that I'm a bit sad that it isn't a live-service game, as I definitely want to see more content for it.Exploration is the downside of this game. As it is very linear, there isn't much to explore. At most, you might want to check every corners for the few journals that are hidden in each region(shared through all of your  characters), but that's it. The game focuses more on its story and gameplay elements.I found the story to be very enjoyable, although there is a lot of swears, which could be a deal breaker for some. You and your people are fighting against a planet that potentially wants to get rid of you while trying to survive through the various problems that comes along. As you progress through the story, there will be a lot of dumb and funny moments. I personally enjoyed every single character designed in this game.The encounters are a bit boring early on, but once you start getting more monster varieties, it starts becoming more fun. That said, the mob varieties are a bit lacking, but as the game encourages aggressive gameplay, you will still get plenty of action. At most, you shouldn't get bored of the game until after you're done with the story, which took me around 20-30 hours while playing on the highest difficulty(World Tiers) as they are unlocked.The overall character progression feels really good. While the Skill Tree takes a while to get running, Character Skills feels great to use and finding new mods is very exciting. You can salvage your loot to permanently unlock its mods for customizations which is unlocked down the road. However, only one mod slot per gear can be customized. You will also be able to change your guns' shooting behaviors to adapt to your playstyle(ie: Semi Auto, Burst, Full Auto). Iron and Leather are super easy to get, so don't be afraid to use them to customize your gear.Once you finish the story, you will unlock a new game mode, that lets you expand on the looting aspect of the game. Overall, the full product is very solid. However, if you only plan to play for the story without expanding on the looting aspect of the game, then the price tag might be a little bit heavy without a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, gather 'round, folks, it's time to chat about "Outriders" – the game that had me hopeful for a fix of that sweet, sweet looter shooter action. But did it deliver? Well, let's just say it's a bit of a mixed bag.First off, the story – meh. It's not terrible, but it's not exactly keeping me on the edge of my seat either. Just kind of... there. Same goes for the animations in the cutscenes – not exactly winning any awards in that department.But let's talk gameplay. When it's good, it's really good. I mean, who doesn't love mowing down enemies with all sorts of flashy powers and guns? It's like a symphony of destruction, and I'm the conductor. But here's the kicker – I ran into more bugs than a picnic in a swamp in the beginning. Not exactly the smoothest start.I managed to push through to early endgame, but then something just... fizzled out. I was hoping for that same addictive loop that kept me coming back for more in games like "The Division," but alas, it just wasn't there for me.Now, I've heard through the grapevine that "Outriders" has gotten a bit better since I last played. Maybe it's worth giving it another shot, but for now, it's just a fun game to hop into for a few hours here and there. A missed opportunity? Yeah, in my book. But hey, at least it's good for a few laughs and some decent shootin'.

_childDocuments_.review: Here's my honest review of this game with over 100 hours of play so far, this game like any other has it's good and not so good. I guess its all in the eye of the beholder to determine which category this game falls into more. I am in no way whining about the game and this is my opinion. Take from it what you will.The Good:-Graphics are really good-Gameplay is decent-Story is goodThe Not so good:-Co-op match making needs major improvement. I can't tell you how many times I have joined an expedition only to have players AFK at camp for god knows how long, leave and start the process all over, rinse and repeat. It gets really annoying and eats into your game time like no tomorrow.-Expeditions: Need a way to be able to pick from sort of list of a current expedition level running. Currently there's nothing for this and you also have no indication what team you are joining, all the game tells you is that it found a game. So it's a huge guess every single time.-Another point of topic as far as expeditions go, getting kicked at the end of the expedition before the pod opens or the game crashes right at the end sucks big time. You lose out on any of the loot that would have dropped for you and any pod resources. The devs really need to address this. The solution I can suggest here, skip the pod opening to get the loot, award the items to the player right at the end of expedition round no matter what. That way if the game crashes (which happens a lot) or you get kicked for no reason what so ever at least you get your rewards and don't feel like it's been a huge waste of time. -Legendary drop rates: This needs improvement as well. I realize that legendary items are supposed to be a grind for the game but the grind for gear is super obnoxious. Case in point is also what I just mentioned above, if you get kicked or the game decides its going to crash at the end, you are SOL.-Tiago: The major complaint I have here, why on earth is there no countdown for Legendary items he sells and why doesn't the stock rotate out? Looking at the same crap every time gets old, give us more variety with Legendaries he sells. We still have to grind for POD resources anyway in order to buy them. -Modding gear: Please give us a way to roll out a stat on a item (either weapon or armor) and by that I mean things like Max Health (which is useless). At least allow us to roll one stat out, it would allow us a little easier of a time making the build we want as opposed to checking every vendor, waiting for the shop to reset only to find there's absolutely nothing you want to buy and wait again. It gets old very quick. Plus if we did have a way to re-roll a stat, at least then we could make a nice looking build instead of having this mismatched crappy looking build until you find the right piece to replace.-One last note on gear, please give us transmogs for gear. That way we can make our gear look better then what it is now.Anyway, thank you for reading through this review. I like this game and still would suggest getting it, but the game could be a whole lot better. The devs are working through some of the bugs in the game and have addressed some of them, but they have a long way to go if they want to make the players happy and have a successful game. This game has a lot of potential and I really think it can get there, just as long as the devs don't give up on it. Happy gaming.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr Outrider's crafting is nothing groundbreaking, but it solves the problem I've had with so many other looter shooters and I can say that I am now hooked.----------------------------------------------------------------------------At first, I wasn't impressed. I played the demo for a day. Got to the max level. Graphics were decent enough but performance was a little meh. Gunplay was fun enough but it was "nothing special". Pretty much a standard looter shooter. So I bought it and waited. Played the first day unlocked the crafting and my whole perception shifted for the better. The 2 most important things for a "looter shooter" is the lootin' and the shootin'. What I have witnessed a lot of recent games in this genre is that they may get the shootin' right, but they fail at providing a lootin' experience that  compliments the shootin' and hooks the player into wanting to play for an extended period of time. These games tend to have a hard time keeping their players interested in their endgame. Outrider's crafting is nothing groundbreaking, but it solves the problem I've had with so many other looter shooters and I can say that I am now hooked. The crafting combined with the character progression has the potential to hold interest far into the endgame. The moment I knew I was hooked was when I was able to know exactly the type of character I wanted to build start building that character as soon as crafting was unlocked.You like a certain weapon? You can keep that weapon throughout the entire game by being able to level it up, mod it, and upgrade its rarity with the right amount of resources. The major problem other looter shooters has is  they force the player to rely too much on RNGesus in order to build themselves to the way they want to play. Then they artificially limit the best of RNGesus in order to arbitrarily extend playtimes. Not in Outriders. Build the way you want to play from the *beginning* and spend your time grinding towards making your style stronger instead of grinding towards *hoping* to get the right combinations of gear that will make your style possible.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fun, but it is infinitely more fun if you are playing with friends or using the 2-3 player co-op. The game thrives there where you're using your abilities (that the game is focused around) to help and support your teammates. I've played Technomancer, but mostly singleplayer. Singleplayer looks and plays great, but as soon as I hop into multiplayer, the connection is spotty in places and you'll infinitely run into connectivity issues or your game will crash. It is incredibly disappointing to have so much fun with the game, only to have the central attracting experience in the game (the co-op and multiplayer) tarnished by this poor multiplayer rollout. I have played the game on the Xbox One (ehh) and run into the exact same issues on multiplayer and it just doesn't run as well. _childDocuments_.review: World Slayer update: They fixed many of the issues. Story still sucks. Endgame is better. No more timed missions. Class skills feel stronger which means more build variety. Leaning in to class skills makes combat less reliant on the limp gunplay, but new mods make even gunplay feel a bit better. Level design has improved in content released after vanilla. Staggers aren't as deadly. Many of the bugs are fixed, although I do still experience the occasional glitch and  crash. Worldslayer itself is overpriced. Only buy this if you can get both vanilla and worldslayer for 60.00 or less. Outriders has a couple of good ideas that better games should steal so that we can all toss this in the trash where it belongs. I'll start with the positive. The design of some of these classes is truly inspired. The abilities are striking visually. That's it. Everything else is complete and utter garbage.Let's start with the story.  It feels like a late B+ SciFi movie from 2008. It unashamedly rolls through every single possible cliche like some kind of Katamari of mediocrity. The characters are two-dimensional at best. The lines are so awkward sometimes that I wonder if this dialogue is just badly translated. The rest of the time it feels like it was written by a teenager who just discovered how to swear. The story and dialogue are truly awful.But who cares about the story if the gameplay is good? Well, let's talk about that. The game is set up to be a third-person cover shooter. However, class and encounter design encourage you to avoid cover. It is not a good sign when the cover system in your cover shooter is best described as superfluous. In fact, the cover is so bad it will get you killed more often than it will save you. Once you figure out that the cover is bad, each encounter plays out the same. You run past cover and maul enemies with your weapons and skills then move on to the next arena to do the same. Arena design is largely irrelevant. To be fair, most looter shooters are fundamentally repetitious. You're just killing things over and over in every single one, but it's so much worse in this game. The arenas feel the same because the level design is largely just a series of corridors. The arena design is so bland that it sometimes feels like an asset flip. There was a point in the game where I was in an arena reminiscent of the wild west and it took me a few minutes to realize how ridiculous this was for a science fiction shooter because everything blends together.  There is approximately zero thought put into how encounters play out. Enemy composition is also relatively predictable and predictably obnoxious as you increase difficulty. You'll have a swath of weak enemies to deal with, and one or two "elite" bullet sponge enemies that will pose a problem with their superpowers. As you increase difficulty the stronger enemies become more numerous. The encounter design is just so boring and one-note. This would be fine if the gunplay were good. Destiny survived a bland launch thanks to great gunplay. The gunplay is not good in this game. The moment-to-moment process of shooting is basically Anthem but worse. There's so much unnecessary momentum that you feel like you're on ice. Guns have little impact beyond the numbers that cascade from their shots. There's no "oomph" like there is in Doom or Destiny. But it isn't just bland, it's also frustrating. Every so often your shooting is interrupted by an enemy stunning you. Snipers and nearly everything with a melee attack will knock you out of ADS (Aim Down Sights) and make you vulnerable for a second. This is the kind of game where if something coughs on you, you die. It also takes some time to reorient yourself after being stunned. At higher difficulties, this time is usually enough to get you killed. You have a dodge. It doesn't work. You'll dodge completely out of the way of an enemy attack and still be stunned by it. So on top of the structure being monotonous, the game is also infuriating.Oh, but it may be fun if there's a lot of build variety, right? Nope. Endgame events are timed. You get less loot in endgame if you don't finish encounters within a specific amount of time. This structure forces very specific builds. All of those cool skills you get? All but three will be meaningless. At first, the specialization tree seems interesting. You won't ever touch 2/3s of it. This means that there's no depth or interest in making your character the way you want to make them.The visuals also leave a lot to be desired. They initially overwhelm with bright colors, detail, and special effects. That would have been impressive in 2012, but recent years have put a real emphasis on art direction. And the art direction is lacking in this game. When you look past the sheen, a lot of stuff is bland and generic. I was eager for this game because I was looking for a break from Destiny. Now I have a newfound appreciation for it. Actually, this game gave me a greater appreciation for the quality of Anthem. I wrote in my Avengers review that it was a disappointing waste of money. Thanks to Outriders I am now playing and enjoying Avengers. Destiny, Borderlands, Anthem, Avengers, and the Division all feel better to play, have better writing and acting, better art direction, and are generally more well-thought-out experiences. Avengers isn't even a shooter! Yet you'd be better off in Avengers than this. You should only play Outriders if you have plumbed every ounce of fun out of those games first and if Outriders heavily discounted.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; I never went to college, but I know how to give an opinion. 10/10. Great read. The game is pretty good too.Once upon a time, I paid full price for this game that was supposed to be great. It was the new Destiny they said. It was going to revolutionize online shooters in a way you couldn't even comprehend. It was Gears of War but multiplayer. Then the beta dropped and it seemed pretty rote, but I was in. There was definitely more to it. This obviously opened up into something greater. The world was interesting, even if many of the characters were kind of dull. The abilities were cool, even if the mod system was kind of limiting. There was promise in this game.Cut to November 15, 2021. I'm hanging in my room, just chillin. You know - relaxin. Pop into Steam to see what the deal is, and lo and behold, Outriders is less than $20. I'm like, "Whatever, bruh! Game is over!" Then curiosity takes me. "What's going on?" I say, looking at the only piece of art in my entire house - a poster of the great Nostradamus that hangs squarely in the center of my bedroom wall, "Could they - nay - would they DARE release AN UPDATE!?!?" Nostradamus appears to nod back. I shift in my chair, eyebrows awrinkle. The air is hot, muggy, ALIVE. I click on the Outriders banner and time seems to slow. The back of my neck is cold and hot at the same time. As the page loads, I begin to hyperventilate. I try to scroll down, but my fingers are too slippery from sweat. I pound on my down arrow, but the contents of the store page seem to stretch on forever. But just when I have lost hope, a glimmer of light appears. It reads "Outriders Broadcast #6 - Coming November 15th." I stand up, "That's today!" I exclaim to no one. I shakily grasp the mouse in my clammy paw. I click the link.Then I black out.I awake hours later covered in a sticky substance, head pounding. Somewhere in the back of my mind I know that an update has been made. I hear voices that tell me 4 new expeditions will be added, and that the time limit will now be optional. Other memories begin to roil up, but just then a knock comes at the door. I bolt upright and spring clumsily forward, saliva spattering the hardwood. My fumbling digits grasp the doorknob and turn.On the other side, a boy no older than thirteen stands, nervously clutching a tattered baseball cap, covered in soot. He looks up, head tilted down, "Hey, mistuh," he says in a strangely anachronistic manner. I look to Nostradamus, who now appears to shrug. The boy tries for more words, "I jus wanted t- to tell yous dat... Um..." he freezes, seeing my red, bloated visage covered in it's own spittle."WHAT IS IT, BOY?!" I scream, jugular palpating, "SPIT IT OUT!"A sudden courage overtakes the lad. He puffs out his chest and shouts at me as though he is trying to ward off a hungry bear at his campsite, "Get gud, noob!" Then he plants his size 8 right in my two bits. As I fall, I hear him whisper, "Connectivity patches, skill balances, and a brand new transmog system," and just as mysteriously as he arrived, he is gone.I lean back against the wall. I guess this is it. A solitary tear rolls down my face as I realize that I have defecated. A violin can be heard played from somewhere far off. Nostradamus appears to have left. I'm well and truly alone now. I will do what must be done. I will reinstall Outriders.

But if the game is that badly written in terms of story, design, functionality, etc, then I don't see any point putting any effort into the review. So here you go, have my autistic rant :^DSPOILERS-----------^^^^^^^ORIGINAL REVIEW - Updates below--------------------------------------0/4 - Should be £$5 or less.Looks, feels and functions like a late PS3 game.It's like Path of Exile, Defiance, Remnant, Gears of War and Destiny had a "party". Monster Hunter shows up uninvited and they all have a "good time". Fast forward 9 months. Monster Hunter gives birth to a mutant and names it "Outriders". Turns out, MH and Remnant were blood related.Seriously though, it's just not a good game. Uninteresting story, cheesy characters (the bad kind), bad gunplay, bad voice acting, capes for some reason, no variety of enemies or weapons, "bosses" are mediocre, dodging is inconsistent, powers are samey. The melee lacks substance. You just put your hand out and things happen. Nothing connects.Menus are incomplete/buggy and the game crashes fairly often, for me at least. Cyberpunk crashed a few times in 168 hours but this games crashes at least 2 or 3 times an hour. Resource numbers appear half the time. Shards don't appear at all.It's nothing more than a Remnant alternative that's not much better. At the very least, it has some fancy weapon mods.I bought it so I'll finish it.I'll update this review when I'm done.UPDATE 1. Game complete - Technomancer-----------------------------------------------0/10 - Should be free.Easily one of the worst games I've ever played. Everything from the original review still stands. The UI is still buggy for me, the game still crashes randomly and more often than Cyberpunk ever did. The shards I talked about are accessed by hovering over the shards only to show that shards are actually split into each individual attribute, forcing you to mindlessly farm for one specific shard that you want or buy them. Speaking of which. shops are pointless as you can just dismantle everything for scrap and you get better weapons from just playing the game.The Devastator class is obsolete. It is the weakest out of all 4 classes. It does the least damage overall to the point that others will kick you from endgame parties because you're simply too weak to kill anything fast enough according to many sources on the magical world of the internet. Google it. I started as the Devastator and it took about 40+ hours to get halfway through the game solo. I started a new Technomancer and completed the game in under 20 hours using nothing but pistols and ordnance skills. Pistols have infinite ammo so why bother using anything else? Just upgrade some dual-pistols and slap on some chains, locusts or anything that does high damage over time. Just fire and forget. Or you can go for claymores and lightning whip. High damage and it refreshes within a few seconds so you can just keep firing.Pointless cutscenes. My most used keys in this game were ESC and Space. Every time you travel to a different area, your screen fades to black, loads a dumb segment of your character opening a door, rappelling down a cliff or simply jumping across a gap. I get that it has to load a new area, new instance, etc but why bother adding a cutscene? Just load the new area and save memory or simply make the transition during the jump or door being opened. We don't need a black screen or a loading screen. Apart from that time waster, I just started skipping through every cutscene in the game. It was genuinely boring and the bad voice acting didn't help. Your character is also a complete imbecile. They're supposed to be a legendary "OuTrIdEr" but starts panicking when a nuke is about to launch instead of keeping calm and trying to figure something out like an Outrider would. No wonder they're all dead, eh? After that's all over, they just go back to being a bumbling idiot with no emotional balance.The characters are forgettable. I actually had to look up the character's names mentioned in this review. The movie and TV references don't add anything to the game. It wasn't funny. Stop it.The animations are very similar to Fortnite which makes sense since People Can Fly are part of it. But at the very least, make something different. It just feels like the UE4 blueprint for 3rd person games which is not how your game should look or feel.Graphics are whatever. I don't care. Pixel, realistic, artistic, it doesn't matter. With this game, the art style is painfully generic. It looks ok but won't win any awards.Music was mediocre.ENDING SPOILERS--------------------^^^^^^^^^^^^^The ending was absolute garbage. Zahedi survived and said "I wish Jane was here to see this." even though HE got her killed by his own naive actions. He somehow believed that some grunt would keep his word if he let him go. The moment Zahedi looked away, BANG, Jane was shot and no one batted an eye. Then Zahedi thought he'd somehow save Jane who at this point has a hole straight through her THROAT, is choking on blood and can barely function.None of the big bad aliens or "aLtErEd" actually died so that's easily recyclable content, I guess. Also, they actually did it. Tiago just had to say something about friendship before the credits rolled. Yeah, we definitely found friendship didn't we? That was the real treasure.Endgame is boring and repetitive. All my loot is now scrap due to the broken loot system. World Tiers give you a boost to loot drops. WT15 gives you a 500% loot rarity modifier and a +425% Legendary drop rate modifier. So far, throughout the whole game, the only legendary loot I've gotten has been through quests and accolades. Not a single legendary has dropped from the endgame or the world. Legendary weapons aren't even that amazing. My Epic gear is still better than my Legendary gear. I just scrap em for mods and stick em on my Epic gear.I need to go.UPDATE 2 - Expeditions----------------------------------It somehow got worse.After about 100+ expeditions, I have received a grand total of 1 legendary drop. A crappy gas mask that has terrible stats and mods and looks generic.The whole point of the endgame is to get legendaries, right? So, where are they?Zahedi is still an idiot.UPDATE 3 - New Horizon-----------------------------------It's still ♥♥♥♥.There's still nothing to do.Wow, new content.. cool. Got a single legendary, was worse than my rare gear :^)♥♥♥♥ Zahedi.UPDATE 4 - Turdslayer or whatever it's called------------------------------------------------Really? Zahedi was about to get shot but no.. that traitorous fool was allowed to live. He quite literally got someone killed, has been sharing data with "the enemy" and he's still "important"? Come on.. I came up with better stories when I was playing with toy soldiers and stuff.The DLC is just more of the same. Grind for blues and purples with no sign of ever getting legendary stuff. _childDocuments_.review: At the time of writing, I have almost 40 hours spent in Outriders. TL;DR: It's a fun game, lots of loot and you don't feel like you are grinding for better gear. The story has humor in it to break up the otherwise 'end of the world for the second time' tone, through an ongoing war and hostile nature of Enoch the planet you are on. I'm not sure I'm halfway through the story, but I've done all side quests available so far. There's plenty to keep you playing.You can be forgiven for feeling like there is a generic story at the start. Things don't go as planned and quite soon you find factions have been fighting it out for decades as a battle for survival in a hostile alien world of Enoch, which doesn't seem to like the arrival of new travelers.The story gets better as you venture through and has left me wanting to continue playing to discover the secrets of Enoch. There is plenty of humor in the writing. No other video game has made me laugh at events or dialogue (mainly through the main quest) than any other video game I've played in the last 30 years. There is one side quest when you reach Trench Town, which had an absolutely hilarious ending.There is plenty to keep you going, at 40 hours I have all the available side quest completed, and maybe I'm around halfway through the story? An assumption based on where I am on the map.I'm now level 27 and just recently gained 3 legendary weapons to equip.The gunplay is very good, guns available range from Shotguns, to various types of assault rifles (inc. submachine guns) to sniper rifles. Now and then I miss not having any grenades, but that is where your anomaly powers come in.  Guns have mod slots applying status effects on enemies, increasing damage/critical shots, and applying additional damage from either just shooting an enemy to cause lightning to strike them from above, or getting kills on frozen enemies to cause them to explode damaging anyone around.You get to select 3 out of 8 anomaly powers (you unlock them as you level up). These skills vary depending on your class (I went for Trickster), and you would be best investing your skill points into a single tree path for best effect rather than trying to spread them around.Your armor allows for skill slots that have various effects on your skills (i.e. increasing duration of the effect of the skill, adding a second activation before cooldown, increasing your armor for rolling/being out or in cover, etc). You can change the skill in the mod slot to customize and cater and get the best out of the skills you like to use the most. Skills aren't a equip once and use forever, there have been many times where I needed to change up skills to deal with situations (usually with boss encounters).You will want to explore the areas of Enoch as much as you can. There are plenty of equipment crates scattered around which you could easily miss if you just follow the guide marker. At the start, you are rewarded quite well with these locations, but then they feel like they get less, where you will go around edges for nooks and crannies which feel like there should be a crate but there isn't.Same with the glowing blue rocks which you will want to mine to gain resources for upgrading your gear. Having said that, I have plenty of resources and you can always recycle unwanted equipment to make up for any lack.As you level up you also unlock world tiers. This is your difficulty level. At times you will find certain encounters more difficult than others. I found switch up weapons and skills is enough to overcome these hurdles. But, If you are really struggling you can lower the tier (at the expense of less quality loot) to keep your progression going.Its clear Outriders lack polish in certain aspects, mostly interaction events. You'll find yourself holding down the E key just for your character to wiggle as they trying to interact with a gate or to mine rock. You'll be tempted to try and adjust your position, it's best that you just interact again without moving your character. I've found no more than by the 3rd time the interaction will happen.Animations are off in places: scrunching up a wanted poster as it levitates a couple of meters off to your side, or suddenly jumping off location as you interact with a switch to open a gateThere are varying audio levels during the dialogue when characters are speaking over the radios. At times the audio will just increase quite noticeably.Others have reported more game-breaking bugs like lost inventory and multiple crashes. The game has only crashed on me twice in the 40 hours played. I have not come across the inventory wipe bug, but then I have not tried playing with others and have soloed the entire game so far.I've enjoyed what I've played so far and have not been bored. _childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately in it's current state I cannot recommend this tame.I was having no issue until I reached the "End Game" and now I"m experience near constant crashes, loss of progress, but thankfully no inventory loss.Edit: Decided to give it another go, still has texture popping and first NPC I talked to crashed the game. Still can't recommend it. Still buggy, not worth the bandwidth.Once these are patched and fixed, I would recommend this game. The loop is very entertaining and fun, the story is interesting enough to play through the entirety of the game just for that. The World Tier system is brilliant, allowing people take on  whatever challenge they want. However and of 4/13/21, this is a wait and see until it gets fixed situation.Edit: Having experienced more of the end game, I would have to change my stance on recommending at any point. The game was fun and enjoyable Up To Endgame. At which point, the End Game is a series of Soft Time Trial Elimination Missions.Levels suffer from very generic designs. Go to a room / hallway and kill all the enemies. Go to a Room and stand in a glowing circle, and kill all the enemies. Got to a room and Kill a Boss or 2, and all the other enemies. There is no variation to this what so ever.In it's current state there is also an issue with the Downscaling. Essentially if you have Tier 13 Gear and go down to Tier 3 for some simple farming or helping a friend your stats are Lowered. This is done to such an aggressive level that you are actively weaker wearing Tier 13 Gear in a Tier 3 Mission than wearing Tier 2 Gear into a Tier 3 Mission.There are also general control issues, that in the story mode I was more forgiving of, but the high DPS/Avoidance nature of the End Game has pushed them to be unforgivable. Sprint rarely works, regardless if i set to Toggle or Hold, the character will often ignore the input. Without double tapping or hitting the Roll button, my character will just roll. Apparently it counts as a double tap if you go from A to S quickly enough while strafing fire. These issues, have caused several unnecessary deaths, and since I have been avoiding online due to the wipe bug....this means restarting the Entire Run.In Group Play, you apparently get 1 Self Revive, but in Solo its back to the beginning no matter what. This seems to more strongly punish solo players, which is already more punishing as you get all the attention of every enemy on screen. And there can be a lot of enemies on screen. All doing a plethora of attacks, many of which will blanket the ground in red circles denoting AoE so that you have no safe zone to take a moment and re-group.You will get staggered, knocked backed, frozen, and once you do, you're as good as restarting at that point. It is a frustrating experience.In Essence, the End Game does not reflect the Campaign journey. One single game mode as the End Game, with broken loot, broken scaling, backwards decisions on co-op vs solo play, and even the always online for being a solo player.For a game claiming to be Anti-Live Service, it has at every step followed the exact same follies and foot steps as Live Service games like Anthem and Destiny.

_childDocuments_.review: Before I begin, forgive me. This is my first review of a game.I would say that I have played a good amount to get the idea of whether the game is good or not (for me or people like me). Straight up, for me, its amazing. I recommend it to anyone that is looking for a looter-shooter. (Loot drops are very similar to the Diablo-style drops, a bunch of gear all over the place). Basically if you like the style of Destiny, Anthem (RIP), Borderlands and Diablo. Then you may get a kick out of this game. While it shares similarities to them, it certainly is not the same game. So keep that in mind.Pros: - The shooting feels really good, except for the blighted rounds on the technomancer (WARNING: turn the audio down if you use this character/build) it is LOUD.- If you bought into the idea of Anthem (still RIP), it feels the closest to this game, only with actual working mechanics, decent boss/enemy fights, proper loot system, you can actually inspect and equip the gear you get when you get it and not have to go back to base...basically a well polished what we wished it would've been anthem. Just without the flying.- Loot for days! (ok so not as intense as Borderlands, but far better than my other suggested 'similar' games).- Actual weapon and armor editing or 'crafting' so you can have more opportunities to get 'God Roll' items. Or at least create them. While Legendary gear is more of a static stat drop. It does often drop with different armor ratings. - actually all the gear has a pool of armor points it can be. Example: lvl 50 helmet, i've seen range from 8k - 12k ish in armor. - Story line is ok, not fantastic, but it does the job of explaining the situation and pulls you in enough to make you want to keep playing. While it does have a frequent amount of cut scenes to tell the base story, there is also a good amount of books/items/etc to pick up that tells the stories a little deeper or at least provides a little context to some situations. Some you can read for deeper information while others when picked up has your character talking with the team about what happened.- A well thought out skill tree system. In which creates a decent amount of build opportunities, its NOT just a 'only build Firepower', while yes it does lean a bit towards building Anomoly power for most classes, you can still hit Gold tier in the end game with most of the other builds. Kind of look at it this way, each class has 3 skill tree options, 1. Higher firepower/weapon damage, 2. Survivability/Tank/Heals, 3. Anomoly power focused. But you aren't limited to just that tree, they do have some nodes that connect to the others so you can branch off of one tree and snag a few that apply to what you are looking to build.WOW - sorry I didn't realize it would be this long, and there's still more to say. Cons - As I mentioned above while they have some good, there is also some not so good.- Blighted rounds are extremely loud for some reason. - The infamous connection issues - while I personally have only had it a few times just casually playing. It does seem to happen a bit more when playing with others and majority of the time when playing with people on console.- Seems console received the worst of the connection and server issues. Yes they exist as they do in almost any game these days. But for me at least, it's not that bad of an experience to put me off from still recommending the game.- So they made a patch and fixed a lot of stuff. While also kind of breaking as some would call, a vital piece of the game. Survivability. More so, the damage resistance from your armor seems to have been bugged and you now take more damage. (its in the works to being patched).- they did have an issue where everyone lost all their gear/ character locked out. But that's currently being rectified. ** The biggest one for me: No in game chat/text to communicate with blueberries (other players), no inspecting other players gear to get all jealous of what they received from RN-Jesus.I suppose this is where I put in the TL;DR? ... I guess I should've just written that then and not this novel...but, where's the fun in that. :DTL;DR -If you enjoy a game that is a looter shooter with an emphasis on Loot (compared to recent looter shooter games), has crafting/editing gear, some dope abilities. 4 very different characters each with 3 skill trees. Provides about 25-50 hrs of game play. (pending side quests, difficulty setting and solo or with a team). Pretty reasonable AI enemies (they dont just sit there waiting to die most the time). Its ALL doable with friends or solo. Has a pretty decent end game loot farm. NOT a Live Service game. Again, not a live service game - no paying for currency packs to look cool, no battlepass, no extra fees associated with it. YET it can still give someone like me 170+ hours of fun..(sigh of relief). Then I think this game would be good for you. I will admit, I did get it 20% off using a popular site that's related to Green men. But I still would've been satisfied paying the full $60 for what I got and am still getting out of it. Yes there's some issues/bugs/etc. But overall, the game has good bones and the issues are able to and have been fixed with patches.* Lastly *I hope you enjoy the game if you decide to get it. At the very least, if you still question it but like the idea/concept of the game, wait for a sale. If you don't like these types of games, or are a salty rager that cant restart the game to fix a minor inconvenience and you've read this much... what're you doing? go play Fortnite or COD. Alright, there's my 2 cents.

_childDocuments_.review: Outriders has a lot of potential if the devs can sort out the bugs and other issues asap. It's a lot of fun, I love the progression system and the combat. It's a shame the whole cover fire is wasted, but that was a weird decision putting a cover system in a game where the endgame is time-trials. Nobody uses cover in the endgame expeditions. The game crashes have eased up a lot, although they do still occur on occasion. The loot sometimes drops for the wrong class spec, and you can even lose all your inventory items when you try and matchmake. But, these issues are a priority and updates on social media are keeping the player-base in touch. My biggest criticism of the game is that it's more a single player experience, rather than mult-player, You can party with 1-3 players (4 would have been better, to incorporate all the classes) but the matchmaking is ♥♥♥♥, and the netcode and servers are absolute garbage. It's a game of Russian roulette as to whether the map will rubber-band or lag out in party's, and if the "host" disconnects, the rest of the team crashes or DC's as well. I can only play with my Steam buddies, if I want to have a good time in group-play in Outriders.   I'm at the point now though, where there is nothing else to do. Once you've clocked the expeditions and timed them on gold, there is nothing left. And with Outriders not being a live service game with regular updates, story, or expedition missions, things are going to get stale very quickly.

_childDocuments_.review: You really want to love this game. The gun play is a lot of fun with an eclectic system of loot and mods. Unfortunately, that's where the game's value ends. While the story doesn't take itself too seriously, it's so run of the mill and boring, you'll be tapping space to skip any line of dialogue or cutscene only a few hours in. The visuals follow suit with the story. While it runs quite well on a decently specced machine, there is nothing here that stands out and is quite stuck in the early 2000's in terms of art design. The AI boils down to dumb hordes of creatures rushing you or gun equipped enemies that will continually flush you out with grenades/mortars from cover and never miss a shot while you're in the open. This leads to needing to take full advantage of your abilities and a good deal of skill to traverse each arena while maintaining each classes system of healing to survive.Which leads to the level design. You will literally be funneled down a corridor into an arena to fight a group of enemies in every single area/quest. There is little to no exploration or much variety from the first mission to the next despite a decent set of backdrops (war torn, snow, forest, etc.) It's all very sterile and outdated for any genre of shooter.The plethora of glitches, server issues, and matchmaking that is completely broken makes Outriders very hard to recommend even if you are a diehard looter shooter fan. It's not a bad game by any means but you'd do well to wait for a deep sale.

_childDocuments_.review: There is no point on judging a game based on game instability since that, for me at least, is mostly fixed. Let's look at the actual game itself.Gameplay is a lot a fun. I thoroughly enjoy tinkering with mods and attributes and some of the abilities (devastator :D) are lots of fun to use. If you're not doing mods, skills, class, weapon customisation, then you're only getting a fraction of the fun. Hitting a wall and reconfiguring your mods and skills until you get one that works is really nice and I often find myself swapping between builds depending on the situation. Voice acting is very well done especially dr Zahedi and surly Jakub. Story is pretty good with some unexpected events I did not foresee. Always nice to be surprised. And finally, playing this co-op with friends is huge fun, especially when you've got a challenging scenario and you're trying to find things that synergize well.This game is not a live service game a la Destiny or Warframe. But I definitely see myself getting a lot of hours of gameplay out of it.

_childDocuments_.review: A small intro,My experience with looter shooters is heavily influenced by Borderlands, Division 1/2 Shadow Warrior and Destiny/Warframe, Of them i see Shadow Warrior and Borderlands to be the ones all others are judged by.The good, the bad, and the broodmother......So the bad,1 Bugs bugs bugs, from audio to hud to bullets that dont show, invisible enemy bullets should be part of the hard mode, not a bug.2 Map and locating yourself on it, atrocious.3 The map made an auto guide needed(TAB by default) it bugs out and takes you anywhere but to your selected quest4 audio itself, bland isnt a word, its an accurate description, from the guns sounding every variation of meh at you, to the music making you want to mute it and put something on YT.5 the world, be it the same type of locations, namely a small arena, a corridor, a small arena, the changing decorations dont help it much.6 story, decent is good, but wont save your game.and lastly, the characters, "oi, the chick died, shame i didnt get to know her enough to care" sums it up.Now the good.The gun varierity and skills are two completing eachother well crafted aspects.The ability to mod improve and max your weapons cheaply(yes cheaply, compared to the competition and what could be) and ability to change even the mods themselves is something no competition did.Same for the on the fly changing of your skills and class tree.So far, 5/10 with a stretch 6/10with the potential to hit a 9

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty fun game, but it stutters and crashes with an annoying frequency. Would be nice if publishers and developers would stop releasing games that are not ready for release.Update at 70+ hours in game: Bottom line is that I still cannot recommend it. I obviously like the gameplay, but the bugs, errors, and crashes are still persistent. I don't think it has ever started first try. Additionally, I lost loot (including a legendary) following an expedition, which is an incredibly egregious problem in a looter shooter. I am sure the dev and publisher "are working hard" and all that, but the game is still in a sad state from a technical point of view.Final review at 140+ hours: In its current state, I can recommend Outriders without reservations. The game-play has remained consistently outstanding, and it seems that PCF has finally reined in the most egregious, damaging bugs (inventory wipes, namely). While Outriders has been compared to Diablo, I view it more in the vein of Borderlands with maybe a bit of Destiny 1 mixed in. The weapons are bizarre yet interesting and powerful. If you like customizing builds, carefully thinking through synergies, you will enjoy this game immensely. The power fantasy is well in place. This is not a 2000+ hour game like Destiny 2, but you can easily play it for 200+, particularly if you take your time with the campaign, side-missions, hunts, etc. The story is solid, although it is not without its weirdnesses and ironies.

_childDocuments_.review: 🟩 Campaign story is very good, also the lores were interesting as well🟩 Graphics and the environment looks really good🟩 Variety of guns available with mods and their stats can be highly tweaked🟩 Gameplay is solid🟩 Difficulty and rewards can be easily customized by changing World Tier🟩 Skills are cool, and the skill tree can be resetted freely anytime. This is such a good feature allowing you complete freedom to change to any build anytime🟩 Auto-Loot option is good, you can get all loots dropped together automatically and manage them later which I prefer🟥 Online-only game. If the server goes down in the future, you won't ever be able to play the game and all your hard-earned gear farming will be flushed down in the drain. They should've made it offline and online co-op like Borderlands which would've made it almost perfect🟥 Playerbase is not that big, which is a worrying issue for long-term sustainance as this is an online-only game. Crossplay kinda makes up for it but it's still surprising to see such a small playerbase compared to other games🟥 Due to it's online-only nature, if there's any connection hiccup on your end or the server, you'll be kicked out of the game and can't reconnect to your previous instance. This is a game-breaking issue they should fix and can be an extremely frustrating experience particularly if it occurs during end-game expeditions. Even while playing campaign, game disconnected twice for me even after having a good connection🟥 Bullet animations are pretty lackluster, and occasionally you won't know who's hitting/shooting at you🟥 No communication options during co-op. At least a chat box would've been sufficient but they decided to not include anything in the first place which is weird for a modern game🟥 Expeditions are clearly designed for co-op play and not for solo play. This can be a huge issue if you don't have friends and need to depend on random people. The small playerbase makes it difficult to find the right people if you're farming for higher tiers and need two more teammates. Solo expedition is really unfair, if you die once while soloing, you've to restart the whole expedition. Co-op has 1 free self-revives in each area and you can be revived by other players. Meanwhile soloing you get no checkpoints, no revives making it a punishing experience to solo🟥 Co-op also has frequent lag issues which can be annoying🟥 DLSS has really bad ghostingOverall, I did enjoy playing Outriders a lot but having no checkpoint in end-game expeditions ruined it for me as it's difficult to constantly solo higher tiers or find the right people. If you loved playing Borderlands and itching to play something like it, I can highly recommend it but do keep in mind this game has some big issues.

_childDocuments_.review: Outriders is a mix of looter-shooter, cover shooter, with a very well written story line and smooth game play.You are an Outrider, an Altered. Humans from a distant earth left a dying world behind. War, greed, and desperation are a way of life for humanity's survivors. Aboard a grand vessel built for space travel, humans have been promised a second chance after canvasing a distant planet hospitable and habitable by human life. An unexpected cataclysmic event arrived known only as the unexplainable Anomaly Storm, altering DNA, killing people, and granting a selected few powers beyond understanding. As expected, the human condition reared its ugly head, and the new Utopia has once again become a warzone, in a world where survival of the fittest, doesn't mean what it used to. There is no denying that this is the coop game we've been waiting for, for a long awhile.
