_childDocuments_.review: This game is an excellent looter-shooter, the classes have tons of options depending on what playstyle you're looking for, the looting aspect is well made as it's fairly easy to manage and dropped gear doesn't feel like a grind, and on top of that it has an interesting story, though it takes a while to get to the good parts. I've seen other looter-shooter failing miserably on these core aspects of the genre, outriders is not one of these.On the downside, it has bugs, some can really make a difference in battle, in a negative way, though luckily I've been able to overlook these because of all the good aspects of the game. If you're aware that you have little patients for bugs, I'd advise waiting a while, hopefully devs will fix most of these. An example to me has been not  being able to ress party members, which occurs almost every game, or abilities just not working as intended.Last note - this is a game meant to be played multiplayer. It shines at its best when you're playing with friends, especially if they're into this type of games. It can be played alone, though it can feel as if something is missing when played this way.I recommend it because the looter-shooter aspects are delivered in an excellent manner, everything else like bugs can be fixed over time, though gameplay mechanics and gameplay loop cannot, though luckily outriders does not have issues when it comes to these two aspects of the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: I am doing an early review because I am seeing tons of people with less than an hour played trying to bomb this game. First off, what game in the last 10+ years that is a live service game has released without issues... Hell, even games that have been in this business for years (WoW, FF14, Destiny, etc.) STILL to this day have issues on launch. So... Ignoring the privileged that think games should launch at an absolute perfect state with no room to grow... :)The game is fun as hell. From a purely gameplay perspective, it hooks you in almost immediately. It thrust you into the story from the tutorial and sets you up to push forward to figure out "what next...". Whether you jump in with friends and go on a warpath destroying everything in your path or go it alone facing the vast world and extremely challenging difficulty curve. Diving into the game's world immediately reminds you of some of your favorite games. I have heard, "It feels like gears... Looks like Mass Effect... Plays like Destiny... Fantasy Division...This reminds me of the good parts of Anthem..." the list goes on. You can clearly see that this game was inspired by so many games that came before it while maintaining its own unique identity in the lootershooter realm. For me the story feels a bit forced, but let's be real... most of us are not playing for the story anyways. We are just here to shoot, loot, and get epic gear.In terms of the visuals, the game is gorgeous. There are clipping issues, and some visual designs that I don't personally agree with, but I can tell the effort was put in to really polish specific areas of the game.The sound is the major sore thumb for me right now. I am noticing a lot of audio bugs (gun getting extremely loud when activating skills, voices in general, random sounds that don't belong...). It kind of ruins a bit of that immersive value, but I assume this will resolve as the game goes on (as it is a live service game). Bugs.... There are many, but this is the life of BRAND NEW GAME. Find the bugs, point them out. If it is game breaking or makes it so you can't progress or use something correctly, just report it to them so they can queue it up for fixing. WE are the ultimate playtesters/QA because if we can ride on a rocket into combat wearing the severed head of our enemy as a crown, we will. _childDocuments_.review: Outriders marries gameplay of the Division 2 and Remnant, adding RPG elements to the first person shooter genre.  If you like fast-paced, run and gun shooters with cooperative elements, you will like Outriders.  The main problem is that the game is "always on," and you must be able to connect to the internet while playing.  This internet-only feature has no basis in necessity.  Cheating is a non-issue because you can choose who you want to play with (the game allows you to play cooperatively with two others).  There is no competitive scoreboard, unwanted player interaction, or player vs. player content.  In other words, there is no reason to have the game be always on.  The main issue with the game's launch is server unavailability.  Players cannot play the game right now and communication from Square Enix has been inconsistent.  For example, SE tells players to go to  to see whether the game is available; this page appears to be a static screen showing that the status is green and available.  However, all game servers are down and no one is able to play.  There are some other issues, like stuttering/crashing even on high-end systems.  The new NVidia drivers cause significant performance problems with DX12, even on an RTX 3090 with AMD Ryzen 5800X.  The heads up display disappears randomly.  Cross-server matchmaking is disabled with no ETA on resolution.  These issues, particularly the game not being available, make me not recommend this game to you right now.  Hopefully, SE can resolve the problems quickly so that I can revise my review to include the awesome gameplay elements that we saw in the demo.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't often write reviews, except on these rare occasions when a game truly inspired me to do so.In this instance, I got the game on sale, and I had seen the reviews which were mostly positive, but the consensus on most threads was that the game wasn't exactly re-inventing the wheel either. So why should anyone give this game a try? Simply put, it's a fun experience, pretty well optimized, there is good solo content, and from what I've seen the multiplayer is quite fun too. But above all else, it's a good game, without ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. I don't get why or how people use arbitrary measuring sticks these days. Not every game has to be the skyrim or the witcher 3 to the current generation, and Outriders will not be the best game you've played in the last decade.So pros:-Interesting lore; I've been reading the various notes found through the game, and I'm just that kind of player, I love an immersive setting, and a compelling world, and the whole plot of the game is decently intriguing.-Fun/challenging gameplay; I thought the game was just too easy at first, but that's only until I understood how the very unique difficulty settings of this game worked. Once the difficulty cranked up, it kept me on my toes, and had to pay attention to my build.-Well optimized; I've seen some complaints on the internet, mostly related to blurry textures, but it's easily remedied, and for me the game was solid on Ultra & 4k resolution (Note: I do have a RTX 3080 with a solid CPU).-Good graphics; if that's an important factor for you, the game hasn't the most mind-blowing graphics out there, but I thought it was pretty good, and some vistas in the game are good eye-candy nonetheless. The only ofputting part, were some of the facial animations at some points, these could use some work, specifically those of the main character, but it's not exactly horrendous either.-And this may just be me, but whilst the quests are pretty minimalistic; ea. you have a 1 minute dialogue with an NPC, which send you off to a nearby map, you slaughter everything on site, then you have the quest objective resolution with a small dialogue, and report back. Basic, but it works. The part which left me quite pleasantly surprised, is the way most quests get resolved, "the plot twist" if you will. I can't explain without spoiling, but let's just say, quests don't end the way you've come to expect them to, and I say this as a gamer veteran with a preference for rpg's. I've done a great many quests in my time... too many... and some of these quests I'll remember fondly, despite the basic format.As for the downsides, I'd say the game is a little repetitive, but frankly it's like complaining that an ARPG is repetitive, you get the game you bought, and this is an action-oriented third-person shooter.This game is a refreshing blast, very enjoyable, and quite simply a good game which doesn't pull any marketing ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ on you. Give it a go, and give it a chance, and the next time you look at the your watch, 10 hours will have flown by.

_childDocuments_.review: Until the game is patched, avoid it. There is a solid base here, with good and satisfying combat and some interesting customization and synergy between weapons, mods, talents and powers.But, the game is wildly unbalanced and has major difficulty swings. The game barely rewards you with loot despite not being a "live" game, and you will hit massive upticks in difficulties in bosses (Bailey, Shaman etc) that then wipe out your tier progress and force you to die cheap deaths over and over again. Most bosses require you to cheese them a bit, or get lucky, or mostly disengage from the fun that makes up the rest of the game.I kept pushing and trying to enjoy this game, but these walls of difficulty are too common and too frustrating to continue. They've even said balancing can be done without patches, so do it. Right now, I just can't recommend trying to fit oneself into this weird box that Outriders wants to force you into.Edit 1: I should mention that many combat rooms and minibosses are fine, I enjoyed working out the best way to survive a room and study the enemy composition as a teleporting Trickster. I always kept my World Tier as high as possible as I enjoyed the challenge. The deaths usually felt fair.There are too many bosses though where the deaths don't feel fair, and force you to play the game in ways that isn't fun.Edit 2 (For New Horizon review): Balance is still terrible. Bosses feel easier, but there are still massive random difficulty spikes that feel impossible to get past solo.

_childDocuments_.review: I only recommend this game if you can purchase it for 10-15$ or less. I give them an A for effort, but a C- in execution.Don't bother playing co-op, too many issues with multiplayer, still unresolved as of 4/26/2022. Focus on the main campaign, take your time and do everything. That's how you'll get the most out of this game. It can be a fun game, and also challenging.The rant:The graphics are seriously outdated for a 2021 game using Unreal Engine 4. I'm playing on Ultra settings at 1080p with 200 resolution scale and it still looks like a game from 2010. There is too much blurry effect, even when I set the post-processing to Low. I feel the textures are lacking details; I can't play with a constant sharp image. It's as if the game changes the settings on its own depending on the scene / area. There appears to be a dynamic rending linked with vsync or the frame limiter which tunes down the resolution settings automatically; it's an extremely bad design and should be removed immediately. You can get rid of this problem by disabling vsync and the frame limiter within the game, and instead enabling it in your nvidia settings.The cutscenes are amateurish at best, very poorly executed. You need to start and end a cutscene the exact same way for ALL of your cutscenes, with a smooth fade-in/fade-out effect. In many cutscenes, the camera is very jerky at times (not talking about shaking), and ruins the cinematic experience. There is still a weird audio glitch whereby the sound skips or gets out of sync or something like that in all the cutscenes, but only in cutscenes. The dialogues of some cutscenes are also cut abruptly, i.e. the last word of someone's sentence gets cut too early. This is no professional work, by the stretch of any imagination. There are completely useless cutscenes when you jump over a ledge to another area, DON'T do that. Get rid of all those jumping cutscenes, they are ruining the game experience, my gosh. During cutscenes, all characters armor/cloth will constantly pop-in like the texture just has been loaded, giving the effect of a jumping cloth. This occurs every time the cutscene camera moves away and back to the character in question.Where are all the configurable graphic settings? Why are you hiding so many graphical settings? Give us the options to tweak the game how we want instead of having to edit an Engine.ini file.Skipping cutscenes: sometimes you have to press SPACE bar, sometimes you have to press ESC to skip a cutscene. WHY? WHY? WHY? MAKE IT THE SAME KEY!!!! $%()*?&%$)*$)$%*&^%$&Sometimes the cutscenes have 2 black widescreen bands, sometimes they don't. WHY? Keep it consistent, how hard can this truly be?Instead of having a screenshot of planet as the main welcome screen of the game, you'd think that an animated rotating planet with some clouds or something like that wouldn't have been such a difficult task to accomplish. All in all, i feel like many small details have been willingly ignored to cut on production time, but all those details add up and matter, and as whole their absence negatively impact the game.The Legendary Merchant at the Outriders camp allows you to reroll for its entire legendary stock at a hefty price, on T15 it's 96k pods per reroll. _childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot of good things going for it, Despite being a very generic looter shooter type game, it is ever so slightly different enough to be enjoyable and fun. The powers feel satisfying to use, the cover is pointless and feels better to run around in the heat of battle and the guns (some of them) feel very nice to use. However in the current state of things, with constant server disconnects and potentially shaky frame rates (Yesterday the game ran at 120fps on both DX11 and DX12, today it doesn't seem to want to go above 50 on either DX) It's probably best to hold off from buying this game, at least until these things are fixed. The issues that can't be fixed though should still be considered. These include but are not limited to Questionable VA and Facial expressions, An extremely forgettable story with characters that just don't have any impact and Cutscenes... So... so many cutscenes.... Why do I need one to jump over a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ crevice or open a door.. it just breaks things up in a very poor manner. Also, moving from locale to locale requires talking to an NPC, and each location is self contained. I assume to help with frame-rate but it's not enjoyable, especially since I can't use my mouse to select dialogue for whatever reason. Naturally I have more things to complain about than I do praise since I'm still early in the game, due to the server issues but some things I do like are the auto-loot system and the World Tiers, they feel like a nice quality of life thing to have.

_childDocuments_.review: Bugs aside, This Looter Shooter is a refreshing take on the genre.Borderlands really set the genre up over 10 years ago. Outriders has some humor but takes itself seriously. I very much have looked forward to this game and am glad to finally have sunk my teeth into it.The game is has a decent challenge and has a surprisingly long campaign for a game of it style. this is no 8 hr campaign (provided you're play some sides and leave the world tier difficulty system in place). _childDocuments_.review: After about ten hours between the demo and the game I was prepared to give this game a decent review until the frequent server disconnects prevented me from playing the game for more than a few minutes at a time. It's a fun C-Tier $25 looter shooter with a good difficulty mechanic, fun power system, basic but servicable story, decent characters and voice acting, and tight shooting mechanics, but due to technical difficulties and frequent server disconnects I can't justify purchasing it.Nothing is quite as frustrating as spending ten to fifteen minutes on higher difficulties wiping goons and mini-bosses in an area, finally feeling that ounce of hope that this run is going to be the one that goes all the way, only to have the server disconnect and to lose all progress.  This game is a firm reminder of why always online gameplay should be a red flag for consumers, particularly those looking to play alone.Beyond that the graphics are sub-par, even on ultra with a 3090 and 5800X, and looking through a scope honestly reminded me of some PS1 games.If the game existed as is for $30 and featured an offline mode for the campaign I would consider this a good buy, but as it stands I can't enjoy solo or multi-player without fear that all of my progress will be lost at any moment, because more often than not, it is.

_childDocuments_.review: Outriders is a 1-3 player co-op RPG shooter set in an original, dark and desperate sci-fi universe. As mankind bleeds out in the trenches of Enoch, you'll create your own Outrider and embark on a journey across the hostile planet. With rich storytelling spanning a diverse world, you'll leave behind the slums and shanty towns of the First City and traverse forests, mountains and desert in the pursuit of a mysterious signal. Combining intense gunplay with violent powers and an arsenal of increasingly twisted weaponry and gear-sets, Outriders offers countless hours of gameplay from one of the finest shooter developers in the industry People Can Fly.
